title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.5
description: Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the childhood pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself. Although such pastimes appear exactly like those of an ordinary child, they should be understood as various pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> vande caitanya-kṛṣṇasya
> bālya-līlāṁ mano-harām
> laukikīm api tām īśa-
> ceṣṭayā valitāntarām
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vande]]---I worship; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇasya]]---of Lord Caitanya, who is Kṛṣṇa Himself; [[synonyms:b:bālya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes of childhood; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:h:harām]]---which are so beautiful; [[synonyms:l:laukikīm]]---appearing ordinary; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:t:tām]]---those; [[synonyms:ī:īśa]]-[[synonyms:c:ceṣṭayā]]---by manifestation of supreme authority; [[synonyms:v:valita]]-[[synonyms:a:antarām]]---quite fit although appearing differently.
translation: Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the childhood pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself. Although such pastimes appear exactly like those of an ordinary child, they should be understood as various pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
purport:
In the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:11|(Bg. 9.11)]] this statement is confirmed as follows:

> avajānanti māṁ mūḍhā
> mānuṣīṁ tanum āśritam
> paraṁ bhāvam ajānanto
> mama bhūta-maheśvaram

"Fools deride Me when I descend in the human form. They do not know My transcendental nature and My supreme dominion over all that be." To execute His pastimes, the Supreme Personality of Godhead appears on this planet or within this universe like an ordinary human being or human child, yet He maintains His superiority as the Supreme Lord. Lord Kṛṣṇa appeared as a human child, but His uncommon activities, even in His childhood-like the killing of the demon Pūtanā or lifting of Govardana Hill-were not the engagements of an ordinary child. Similarly, although the pastimes of Lord Caitanya, as they will be described in this chapter, appear like the activities of a small boy, they are uncommon pastimes impossible for an ordinary human child to execute.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.50
description: Addressing the girls, the Lord would say, "Worship Me, and I shall give you good husbands or good benedictions. The Ganges and Goddess Durgā are My maidservants. What to speak of other demigods, even Lord Śiva is My servant."
text:
> kanyāre kahe,---āmā pūja, āmi diba vara
> gaṅgā-durgā---dāsī mora, maheśa---kiṅkara
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kanyāre]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---addressing the girls, the Lord would say; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]] [[synonyms:p:pūja]]---"Worship Me"; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:d:diba]]---shall give; [[synonyms:v:vara]]---nice husband; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]---the Ganges; [[synonyms:d:durgā]]---Goddess Durgā; [[synonyms:d:dāsī]]---maidservants; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:m:maheśa]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:k:kiṅkara]]---servant.
translation: Addressing the girls, the Lord would say, "Worship Me, and I shall give you good husbands or good benedictions. The Ganges and Goddess Durgā are My maidservants. What to speak of other demigods, even Lord Śiva is My servant."
purport:
There is a misconception about the Hindu religion among people who profess other religions, such as Christians and Muslims, who say that in the Hindu religion there are many Gods. Actually that is not a fact. God is one, but there are many other powerful living entities who are in charge of different departments of administration. They are called demigods. All the demigods are servants who carry out the orders of the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead. Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu disclosed this fact in His childhood. Out of ignorance, sometimes people worship the demigods to receive some particular boon, but actually, one who becomes a devotee and worshiper of the Supreme Personality of Godhead does not need to go to the demigods for any benediction because he obtains everything by the grace of the Supreme Lord. The //Bhagavad-gītā// ([[books:bg:7:20|7.20]], [[books:bg:7:28|28]]) therefore condemns such demigod worship:

> kāmais tais tair hṛta-jñānāḥ
> prapadyante 'nya-devatāḥ
> taṁ taṁ niyamam āsthāya
> prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā

"Only persons whose intelligence is lost and who are mad with lusty desires worship the demigods and follow the particular rules and regulations of worship according to their own natures."

> yeṣāṁ tv anta-gataṁ pāpaṁ
> janānāṁ puṇya-karmaṇām
> te dvandva-moha-nirmuktā
> bhajante māṁ dṛḍha-vratāḥ

"But persons who are freed from all sinful activities and the duality of delusion engage themselves in the worship of the Supreme Personality of Godhead with determination." Only the less intelligent worship the demigods for their various purposes. The most intelligent worship only the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa.

Sometimes we, the members of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, are accused of not approving of the worship of demigods. But how can we approve of this when it is condemned by Lord Caitanya and Lord Kṛṣṇa? How can we allow people to become foolish and //hṛta-jñāna,// bereft of intelligence? Our propaganda is simply meant to enable intelligent people to understand the distinction between matter and spirit and understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the whole spiritual identity. That is our mission. How could we mislead people into worshiping so-called gods in material bodies within this material world?

Our position of not allowing worship of the many hundreds of demigods is confirmed by Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu even in His childhood. Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura has sung in this connection:

> anya devāśraya nāi,     tomāre kahinu bhāi,
> ei bhakti parama karaṇa

"To become a staunch, pure devotee of the Supreme Personality of Godhead without deviation [//ananya-bhāk//], one should not divert his attention to the worship of the demigods. Such control is a symptom of pure devotional service."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.51
description: Without the permission of the girls, the Lord would take the sandalwood pulp and smear it on His own body, put the flower garlands on His neck, and snatch and eat all the offerings of sweetmeats, rice and bananas.
text:
> āpani candana pari' parena phula-mālā
> naivedya kāḍiyā khā'na---sandeśa, cāla, kalā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āpani]]---Himself; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---pulp of sandalwood; [[synonyms:p:pari']]---smearing over the body; [[synonyms:p:parena]]---takes; [[synonyms:p:phula]]-[[synonyms:m:mālā]]---the flower garlands; [[synonyms:n:naivedya]]---offering of food; [[synonyms:k:kādiyā]]---snatching; [[synonyms:k:khā'na]]---begins to eat; [[synonyms:s:sandeśa]]---the sweetmeats; [[synonyms:c:cāla]]---rice; [[synonyms:k:kalā]]---bananas.
translation: Without the permission of the girls, the Lord would take the sandalwood pulp and smear it on His own body, put the flower garlands on His neck, and snatch and eat all the offerings of sweetmeats, rice and bananas.
purport:
According to the system of worship, when something is offered to deities outside one's home, it is generally not cooked food but raw rice, bananas and sweetmeats. Out of His causeless mercy, the Lord would snatch the offerings from the girls and eat them, admonishing the girls not to worship the demigods but to worship Him. This worship of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is recommended in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.32):

> kṛṣṇa-varṇaṁ tviṣākṛṣnaṁ
> sāṅgopāṅgāstra-pārṣadam
> yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair
> yajanti hi su-medhasaḥ

"One should worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead who appears in this Age of Kali with His associates as the Pañca-tattva: the Lord Himself and His associates Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrī Advaita Prabhu, Śrī Gadādhara Prabhu and Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura. In this age an intelligent person worships the Pañca-tattva by the method of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// and, if possible, distributing //prasāda.//" Our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is introducing this bona fide method of worship in the Western world. Its members are going from village to village and town to town with Deities of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, teaching people how to worship the Lord by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra,// offering //prasāda// and distributing //prasāda// to people in general.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.55
description: "They will be learned, clever and young and possess abundant wealth and rice. Not only that, but you will each have seven sons, who will all live long lives and be very intelligent."
text:
> paṇḍita, vidagdha, yuvā, dhana-dhānyavān
> sāta sāta putra habe---cirāyu, matimān"
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---learned; [[synonyms:v:vidagdha]]---expert and humorous; [[synonyms:y:yuvā]]---young man; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]-[[synonyms:d:dhānyavān]]---very rich, possessing wealth and rice; [[synonyms:s:sāta]] [[synonyms:s:sāta]]---seven each; [[synonyms:p:putra]]---sons; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---you will have; [[synonyms:c:cirāyu]]---born with a long life; [[synonyms:m:matimān]]---and intelligent.
translation: "They will be learned, clever and young and possess abundant wealth and rice. Not only that, but you will each have seven sons, who will all live long lives and be very intelligent."
purport:
Generally it is the ambition of a young girl to have a very handsome husband who is learned, clever, young and rich. According to the Vedic culture, one is rich if he possesses a large stock of food grains and a very large number of animals. //Dhānyena dhanavān gavayā dhanavān:// one is rich if he possesses food grains, cows and bulls. A girl also desires to have many children, especially sons (//putra//) who are very intelligent and long-lived. Now because society has deteriorated there is propaganda to have one or two children and kill the rest by contraceptive methods. But the natural ambition of a girl is to possess not only more than one child but at least half a dozen.

In exchange for the paraphernalia of worship He usurped for Himself, Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to bless the girls to fulfill all their ambitions and desires. One can easily become happy and obtain the material benefits of a good husband, wealth, food grains and a number of nice children by worshiping Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted //sannyāsa// at an early age, it is not necessary for His devotees to follow Him by also taking //sannyāsa.// One can stay a householder, but one must be a devotee of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Then one will be happy, with all the material opulences of a good home, good children, good mate, good wealth and everything he desires. Therefore the //śāstras// advise, //yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair yajanti hi su-medhasaḥ// (//Bhāg.// 11.5.32). Every householder, therefore, who is actually intelligent should introduce the //saṅkīrtana// movement home to home and live peacefully in this life and go back to Godhead in the next.

purport: This double-dealing is natural for girls. When they are satisfied within, they externally show dissatisfaction. Such feminine dealings are very palatable to boys who try to make friendships with them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.58
description: "If you are miserly and do not give Me the offerings, every one of you will have an old husband with at least four co-wives."
text:
> yadi naivedya nā deha ha-iyā kṛpaṇī
> buḍā bhartā habe, āra cāri cāri satinī
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:n:naivedya]]---offering; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---do not; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---give Me; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:iyā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:k:kṛpaṇī]]---miser; [[synonyms:b:buḍā]]---old; [[synonyms:b:bhartā]]---husband; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---will have; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---four; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---four; [[synonyms:s:satinī]]---co-wives.
translation: "If you are miserly and do not give Me the offerings, every one of you will have an old husband with at least four co-wives."
purport:
In India in those days and even until fifty years ago, polygamy was freely allowed. Any man, especially of the higher castes---the //brāhmaṇas,// the //vaiśyas// and particularly the //kṣatriyas//-could marry more than one wife. In the //Mahābhārata,// or the old history of India, we see that //kṣatriya// kings especially used to marry many wives. According to Vedic civilization there was no restriction against this, and even a man more than fifty years old could marry. But to be married to a man who had many wives was not a very pleasing situation because the husband's love would be divided among his many wives. To punish the girls unwilling to offer Him the //naivedya,// Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu apparently wanted to curse them to be married to men who had at least four wives.

The social structure allowing a man to marry more than one wife can be supported in this way. Generally in every society the female population is greater in number than the male population. Therefore if it is a principle in the society that all girls should be married, unless polygamy is allowed it will not be possible. If all the girls are not married there is a good chance of adultery, and a society in which adultery is allowed cannot be very peaceful or pure. In our Kṛṣṇa consciousness society we have restricted illicit sex life. The practical difficulty is to find a husband for each and every girl. We are therefore in favor of polygamy, provided, of course, that the husband is able to maintain more than one wife.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.6
description: In His first childhood pastimes the Lord turned upside down while lying on His bed, and thus He showed His parents the marks of His lotus feet.
text:
> bālya-līlāya āge prabhura uttāna śayana
> pitā-mātāya dekhāila cihna caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bālya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlāya]]---in His pastimes as a child; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---first of all; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:u:uttāna]]---turning the body; [[synonyms:ś:śayana]]---lying down; [[synonyms:p:pitā]]-[[synonyms:m:mātāya]]---unto the parents; [[synonyms:d:dekhāila]]---showed; [[synonyms:c:cihna]]---marks; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---of the lotus feet.
translation: In His first childhood pastimes the Lord turned upside down while lying on His bed, and thus He showed His parents the marks of His lotus feet.
purport: The word //uttāna// is also used to mean "lying down on the bed face upwards" or "lying down flat on the bed." In some readings the word is //utthāna,// which means "standing up." In His childhood pastimes the Lord tried to catch the wall and stand up, but as an ordinary child falls down, so the Lord also fell down and again took to lying on His bed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.60
description: The girls then brought the offerings before the Lord, who ate them all and blessed the girls to their satisfaction.
text:
> āniyā naivedya tārā sammukhe dharila
> khāiyā naivedya tāre iṣṭa-vara dila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āniyā]]---bringing; [[synonyms:n:naivedya]]---offering; [[synonyms:t:tārā]]---all of them; [[synonyms:s:sammukhe]]---in front; [[synonyms:d:dharila]]---held; [[synonyms:k:khāiyā]]---eating; [[synonyms:n:naivedya]]---offering; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---them; [[synonyms:i:iṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:v:vara]]---desired benediction; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave.
translation: The girls then brought the offerings before the Lord, who ate them all and blessed the girls to their satisfaction.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.61
description: When this cunning behavior of the Lord with the girls became known to the people in general, it did not create misunderstandings among them. Rather, they enjoyed happiness in these dealings.
text:
> ei mata cāpalya saba lokere dekhāya
> duḥkha kāro mane nahe, sabe sukha pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eimata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:c:cāpalya]]---cunning behavior; [[synonyms:s:sabalokere]]---unto the people in general; [[synonyms:d:dekhāya]]---exhibits; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:k:kāro]]---distress; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---there is no such thing; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---everyone; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---enjoys.
translation: When this cunning behavior of the Lord with the girls became known to the people in general, it did not create misunderstandings among them. Rather, they enjoyed happiness in these dealings.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.62
description: One day a girl of the name Lakṣmī, the daughter of Vallabhācārya, came to the bank of the Ganges to take bath in the river and worship the demigods.
text:
> eka-dina vallabhācārya-kanyā 'lakṣmī' nāma
> devatā pūjite āila kari gaṅgā-snāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:v:vallabhācārya]]-[[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---the daughter of Vallabhācārya; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---Lakṣmī; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:d:devatā]]---demigods; [[synonyms:p:pūjite]]---to worship; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---taking; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bath in the Ganges.
translation: One day a girl of the name Lakṣmī, the daughter of Vallabhācārya, came to the bank of the Ganges to take bath in the river and worship the demigods.
purport: According to the //Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā,// verse 45, Lakṣmī was formerly Jānakī, the wife of Lord Rāmacandra, and Rukmiṇī, the wife of Lord Kṛṣṇa in Dvārakā. The same goddess of fortune descended as Lakṣmī to become the wife of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.63
description: Seeing Lakṣmīdevī, the Lord became attached to her, and Lakṣmī, upon seeing the Lord, felt great satisfaction within her mind.
text:
> tāṅre dekhi' prabhura ha-ila sābhilāṣa mana
> lakṣmī citte prīta pāila prabhura darśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing her; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:s:sa]]---her; [[synonyms:a:abhilāsa]]---attachment; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---Lakṣmī also; [[synonyms:c:citte]]---in the heart; [[synonyms:p:prīta]]---satisfaction; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---attained; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---meeting.
translation: Seeing Lakṣmīdevī, the Lord became attached to her, and Lakṣmī, upon seeing the Lord, felt great satisfaction within her mind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.64
description: Their natural love for one another awakened, and although it was covered by childhood emotions, it became apparent that they were mutually attracted.
text:
> sāhajika prīti duṅhāra karila udaya
> bālya-bhāvācchanna tabhu ha-ila niścaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sāhajika]]---natural; [[synonyms:p:prīti]]---affection; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]]---both of them; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---made; [[synonyms:u:udaya]]---appearance; [[synonyms:b:bālya]]---childhood; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācchanna]]---covered by emotion; [[synonyms:t:tabhu]]---still; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---it so became; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---fixed up.
translation: Their natural love for one another awakened, and although it was covered by childhood emotions, it became apparent that they were mutually attracted.
purport: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Lakṣmīdevī are eternal husband and wife. Therefore it was quite natural for their dormant love to awaken when they saw each other. Their natural feelings were immediately awakened by their meeting.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.65
description: They both enjoyed natural pleasure in seeing each nother, and under the pretext of demigod worship they manifested their feelings.
text:
> duṅhā dekhi' duṅhāra citte ha-ila ullāsa
> deva-pūjā chale kaila duṅhe parakāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:duṅhā]]---both of them; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]]---of both of them; [[synonyms:c:citte]]---in the minds; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:p:pūjā]]---worshiping the demigods; [[synonyms:c:chale]]---on the plea of; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---there was; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:p:parakāśa]]---manifestation.
translation: They both enjoyed natural pleasure in seeing each nother, and under the pretext of demigod worship they manifested their feelings.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.66
description: The Lord told Lakṣmī, "Just worship Me, for I am the Supreme Lord. If you worship Me, certainly you will get the benediction you desire."
text:
> prabhu kahe, 'āmā' pūja, āmi maheśvara
> āmāre pūjile pābe abhīpsita vara'
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:ā:āmā']] [[synonyms:p:pūja]]---just worship Me; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I am; [[synonyms:m:maheśvara]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:ā:āmāre]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:p:pūjile]]---if you worship; [[synonyms:p:pābe]]---you will get; [[synonyms:a:abhīpsita]]---desired; [[synonyms:v:vara]]---benediction.
translation: The Lord told Lakṣmī, "Just worship Me, for I am the Supreme Lord. If you worship Me, certainly you will get the benediction you desire."
purport:
This is the same philosophy declared by Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself:

> sarva-dharmān parityajya
> mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja
> ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo
> mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ

"Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reaction. Do not fear." [[books:bg:18:66|(Bg. 18.66)]] People do not understand this. They are accustomed to flatter or worship many demigods, human beings, or even cats and dogs, but when requested to worship the Supreme Lord, they refuse. This is called illusion. Factually, if one worships the Supreme Lord there is no need to worship anyone else. For example, in a village of a limited area one may use different wells for different purposes, but when one goes to a river where there is water constantly flowing in waves, that water can serve all his purposes. When there is a river, one can take drinking water, wash his clothes, bathe and so on, for that water will serve all purposes. Similarly, if one worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, all his goals will be achieved. //Kāmais tais tair hṛta-jñānāḥ prapadyante 'nya-devatāḥ:// only men who have lost their intelligence worship the various demigods to fulfill their desires [[books:bg:7:20|(Bg. 7.20)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.67
description: On hearing the order of the Supreme Lord, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Lakṣmī immediately worshiped Him, offering sandalwood pulp and flowers for His body, garlanding Him with mallikā flowers, and offering prayers.
text:
> lakṣmī tāṅra aṅge dila puṣpa-candana
> mallikāra mālā diyā karila vandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---Lakṣmīdevī; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---on the body; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]---flowers; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood pulp; [[synonyms:m:mallikāra]]---of the flower of the name //mallikā//; [[synonyms:m:mālā]]---garland; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---offered; [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---prayers.
translation: On hearing the order of the Supreme Lord, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Lakṣmī immediately worshiped Him, offering sandalwood pulp and flowers for His body, garlanding Him with mallikā flowers, and offering prayers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.68
description: Being worshiped by Lakṣmī, the Lord began to smile. He recited a verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and thus accepted the emotion she expressed.
text:
> prabhu tāṅra pūjā pāñā hāsite lāgilā
> śloka paḍi' tāṅra bhāva aṅgīkāra kailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---her; [[synonyms:p:pūjā]]---worship; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---receiving; [[synonyms:h:hāsite]]---to smile; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting one verse; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---her; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---emotion; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]] [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---accepted.
translation: Being worshiped by Lakṣmī, the Lord began to smile. He recited a verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and thus accepted the emotion she expressed.
purport: The verse quoted in this connection is the twenty-fifth verse of the Twenty-second Chapter, Tenth Canto, of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.// The //gopīs// worshiped the goddess Durgā, or Kātyāyanī, but their inner desire was to get Lord Kṛṣṇa as their husband. Kṛṣṇa, as Paramātmā, could realize the ardent desire of the //gopīs,// and therefore He enjoyed the pastime of //vastra-haraṇa.// When the //gopīs// went to bathe in the river Yamunā, they left their garments on the land and dipped into the water completely naked. Taking this opportunity, Kṛṣṇa stole all their garments and sat down in the top of a tree with them, desiring to see the girls naked just to become their husband. The //gopīs// desired to have Kṛṣṇa as their husband, and since it is only before her husband that a woman can be naked, to fulfill their desire Lord Kṛṣṇa accepted their prayers by this pastime of stealing their garments. When the //gopīs// received their garments back from Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa recited this verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.69
description: "My dear gopīs, I accept your desire to have Me as your husband and thus worship Me. I wish your desire to be fulfilled because it deserves to be so."
text:
> saṅkalpo viditaḥ sādhvyo
> bhavatīnāṁ mad-arcanam
> mayānumoditaḥ so 'sau
> satyo bhavitum arhati
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saṅkalpaḥ]]---desire; [[synonyms:v:viditaḥ]]---has been understood; [[synonyms:s:sādhvyaḥ]]---O all of you chaste ladies; [[synonyms:b:bhavatīnām]]---of all of you; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:a:arcanam]]---for worshiping Me; [[synonyms:m:mayā]]---by Me; [[synonyms:a:anumoditaḥ]]---accepted; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---that determination or desire; [[synonyms:s:satyaḥ]]---successful; [[synonyms:b:bhavitum]]---to become; [[synonyms:a:arhati]]---deserves.
translation: "My dear gopīs, I accept your desire to have Me as your husband and thus worship Me. I wish your desire to be fulfilled because it deserves to be so."
purport: The //gopīs,// the girlfriends of Kṛṣṇa, were almost of the same age as He. Within their minds they desired that Kṛṣṇa be their husband, but because of feminine bashfulness they could not express their desire. Therefore later on, after stealing their garments, Kṛṣṇa informed them, "I immediately understood your desire and approved of it. Because I have now stolen your garments, you have presented yourselves before Me completely naked, which means that I have accepted all of you as My wives." Sometimes foolish rascals, not knowing the purpose of the Lord or the purpose of the //gopīs,// unnecessarily criticize from their own angle of vision, but the real purpose of //vastra-haraṇa// is expressed by the Lord in this verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.7
description: When the Lord tried to walk, in His small footprints the specific marks of Lord Viṣṇu were visible, namely, the flag, thunderbolt, conchshell, disc and fish.
text:
> gṛhe dui jana dekhi laghupada-cihna
> tāhe śobhe dhvaja, vajra, śaṅkha, cakra, mīna
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---at home; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---the father and mother; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---seeing; [[synonyms:l:laghu]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:c:cihna]]---the marks of the lotus feet, which were very small at that time; [[synonyms:t:tāhe]]---in those; [[synonyms:ś:śobhe]]---which were beautifully visible; [[synonyms:d:dhvaja]]---flag; [[synonyms:v:vajra]]---thunderbolts; [[synonyms:ś:śaṅkha]]---conchshell; [[synonyms:c:cakra]]---disc; [[synonyms:m:mīna]]---fish.
translation: When the Lord tried to walk, in His small footprints the specific marks of Lord Viṣṇu were visible, namely, the flag, thunderbolt, conchshell, disc and fish.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.70
description: After thus expressing their feelings to each other, Lord Caitanya and Lakṣmī returned home. Who can understand the grave pastimes of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu?
text:
> ei-mata līlā kari' duṅhe gelā ghare
> gambhīra caitanya-līlā ke bujhite pāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---executing; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---returned; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---home; [[synonyms:g:gambhīra]]---very grave; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes of Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:k:ke]]---who; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand; [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---is able.
translation: After thus expressing their feelings to each other, Lord Caitanya and Lakṣmī returned home. Who can understand the grave pastimes of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.71
description: When the neighboring people saw the naughty behavior of Lord Caitanya, out of love for Him they lodged complaints with Śacīmātā and Jagannātha Miśra.
text:
> caitanya-cāpalya dekhi' preme sarva jana
> śacī-jagannāthe dekhi' dena olāhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:c:cāpalya]]---naughtiness; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---out of love; [[synonyms:s:sarva]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---all people; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]---before Śacīmātā; [[synonyms:j:jagannāthe]]---and Jagannātha Miśra; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing them; [[synonyms:d:dena]]---gave; [[synonyms:o:olāhana]]---a little rebuke.
translation: When the neighboring people saw the naughty behavior of Lord Caitanya, out of love for Him they lodged complaints with Śacīmātā and Jagannātha Miśra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.72
description: One day mother Śacī went to catch her son, wanting to rebuke Him, but He fled from the spot.
text:
> ekadina śacī-devī putrere bhartsiyā
> dharibāre gelā, putra gelā palāiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:d:devī]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:p:putrere]]---unto the son; [[synonyms:b:bhartsiyā]]---rebuking; [[synonyms:d:dharibāre]]---to catch Him; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:p:putra]]---the son; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:p:palāiyā]]---running away.
translation: One day mother Śacī went to catch her son, wanting to rebuke Him, but He fled from the spot.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.73
description: Although He is the maintainer of the entire universe, once the Lord sat upon some rejected pots in the pit where the remnants of food were thrown, after the pots had been used for cooking.
text:
> ucchiṣṭa-garte tyakta-hāṇḍīra upara
> basiyāchena sukhe prabhu deva-viśvambhara
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:ucchiṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:g:garte]]---in the pit where the remnants of food were thrown; [[synonyms:t:tyakta]]---rejected; [[synonyms:h:hāṇḍīra]]---pots; [[synonyms:u:upara]]---upon; [[synonyms:b:basiyāchena]]---sat down; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---very pleasingly; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:d:deva]]---the Supreme God; [[synonyms:v:viśvambhara]]---the maintainer of the universe.
translation: Although He is the maintainer of the entire universe, once the Lord sat upon some rejected pots in the pit where the remnants of food were thrown, after the pots had been used for cooking.
purport: Formerly it was the custom of //brāhmaṇas// to worship Lord Viṣṇu daily at home and cook food in new pots. This system is still going on in Jagannātha Purī. The food would be cooked in earthen pots, all fresh and new, and after cooking, the pots would be thrown away. By the side of the house there was generally a big pit where such pots were thrown. Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat down on the pots very pleasingly, just to give His mother a lesson.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.74
description: When mother Śacī saw her boy sitting on the rejected pots, she protested, "Why have You touched these untouchable pots? You have now become impure. Go and bathe in the Ganges."
text:
> śacī āsi' kahe,---kene aśuci chuṅilā
> gaṅgā-snāna kara yāi'---apavitra ha-ilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śacī]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---mother Śacī, coming there; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:a:aśuci]]---untouchable; [[synonyms:c:chuṅilā]]---You have touched; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing in the Ganges; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---do; [[synonyms:y:yāi']]---going there; [[synonyms:a:apavitra]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---You have become impure.
translation: When mother Śacī saw her boy sitting on the rejected pots, she protested, "Why have You touched these untouchable pots? You have now become impure. Go and bathe in the Ganges."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.75
description: Hearing this, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu taught His mother about absolute knowledge. Although amazed by this, His mother forced Him to take a bath.
text:
> ihā śuni' mātāke kahila brahma-jñāna
> vismitā ha-iyā mātā karāila snāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ihā]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:m:mātāke]]---unto His mother; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---explained; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---absolute knowledge; [[synonyms:v:vismitā]]---amazed; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:iyā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---the mother; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---forced; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing.
translation: Hearing this, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu taught His mother about absolute knowledge. Although amazed by this, His mother forced Him to take a bath.
purport: The absolute knowledge explained by the Lord to His mother is described by Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura in his //Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya// as follows: "The Lord said, 'Mother, that this is pure and that is impure is surely a worldly sentiment with no basis in fact. You have cooked food for Lord Viṣṇu within these pots and offered the food to Him. How then can these pots be untouchable? Everything in relationship with Viṣṇu is to be considered an expansion of Viṣṇu's energy. Viṣṇu, the Supersoul, is eternal and uncontaminated. How then may these pots be considered pure or impure?' Hearing this discourse on absolute knowledge, His mother was very much astonished and forced Him to take a bath."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.76
description: Sometimes, taking her son with her, mother Śacī would lie down on her bed, and she would see that denizens of the celestial world had come there, filling the entire house.
text:
> kabhu putra-saṅge śacī karilā śayana
> dekhe, divyaloka āsi' bharila bhavana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:p:putra]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---taking the boy; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:k:karilāśayana]]---took rest; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---celestial denizens; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming there; [[synonyms:b:bharila]]---filled up; [[synonyms:b:bhavana]]---the whole house.
translation: Sometimes, taking her son with her, mother Śacī would lie down on her bed, and she would see that denizens of the celestial world had come there, filling the entire house.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.77
description: Once mother Śacī told the Lord, "Please go call Your father." Receiving this order from His mother, the Lord went out to call him.
text:
> śacī bale,---yāha, putra, bolāha bāpere
> mātṛ-ājñā pāiyā prabhu calilā bāhire
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śacī]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---mother Śacī said; [[synonyms:y:yāha]]---go; [[synonyms:p:putra]]---my dear son; [[synonyms:b:bolāha]]---call; [[synonyms:b:bāpere]]---Your father; [[synonyms:m:mātṛ]]-[[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---the order of His mother; [[synonyms:p:paiyā]]---getting; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went; [[synonyms:b:bāhire]]---out.
translation: Once mother Śacī told the Lord, "Please go call Your father." Receiving this order from His mother, the Lord went out to call him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.78
description: When the child was going out, there was a tinkling of ankle bells from His lotus feet. Hearing this, His father and mother were struck with wonder.
text:
> calite caraṇe nūpura bāje jhanjhan
> śuni' camakita haila pitā-mātāra mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:calite]]---while going; [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---on the lotus feet; [[synonyms:n:nūpura]]---ankle bells; [[synonyms:b:bāje]]---sounded; [[synonyms:j:jhanjhan]]---tinkling; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:c:camakita]]---struck with wonder; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:p:pitā]]---of His father; [[synonyms:m:mātāra]]---and mother; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds.
translation: When the child was going out, there was a tinkling of ankle bells from His lotus feet. Hearing this, His father and mother were struck with wonder.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.79
description: Jagannātha Miśra said, "This is a very wonderful incident. Why is there a sound of ankle bells from the bare feet of my child?"
text:
> miśra kahe,---ei baḍa adbhuta kāhinī
> śiśura śūnya-pade kene nūpurera dhvani
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:miśra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Jagannātha Miśra said; [[synonyms:e:eibaḍa]]---this is very; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:k:kāhinī]]---incident; [[synonyms:ś:śiśura]]---of the child; [[synonyms:ś:śūnya]]-[[synonyms:p:pade]]---on the naked legs; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:n:nūpurera]]---of the ankle bells; [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---sound.
translation: Jagannātha Miśra said, "This is a very wonderful incident. Why is there a sound of ankle bells from the bare feet of my child?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.8
description: Seeing all these marks, neither His father nor His mother could understand whose footprints they were. Thus struck with wonder, they could not understand how those marks could be possible in their home.
text:
> dekhiyā doṅhāra citte janmila vismaya
> kāra pada-cihna ghare, nā pāya niścaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing all these marks; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]]---of the parents, Śacīmātā and Jagannātha Miśra; [[synonyms:c:citte]]---in their hearts; [[synonyms:j:janmila]]---there was; [[synonyms:v:vismaya]]---wonder; [[synonyms:k:kāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:c:cihna]]---footprints; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at home; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---get; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---certainty.
translation: Seeing all these marks, neither His father nor His mother could understand whose footprints they were. Thus struck with wonder, they could not understand how those marks could be possible in their home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.80
description: Mother Śacī said, "I also saw another wonder. People were coming down from the celestial kingdom and crowding the entire courtyard.
text:
> śacī kahe,---āra eka adbhuta dekhila
> divya divya loka āsi' aṅgana bharila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śacī]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---mother Śacī said; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---I saw; [[synonyms:d:divya]]---celestial; [[synonyms:d:divya]]---celestial; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming there; [[synonyms:a:aṅgana]]---courtyard; [[synonyms:b:bharila]]---filled up.
translation: Mother Śacī said, "I also saw another wonder. People were coming down from the celestial kingdom and crowding the entire courtyard.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.81
description: "They made noisy sounds I could not understand. I guess they were offering prayers to someone."
text:
> kibā kelāhala kare, bujhite nā pāri
> kāhāke vā stuti kare---anumāna kari
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---what; [[synonyms:k:kelāhala]]---rowdy sounds; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---they make; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---I am able; [[synonyms:k:kāhāke]]---to whom; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:s:stuti]]---prayer; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---they offer; [[synonyms:a:anumāna]]---guess; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I do.
translation: "They made noisy sounds I could not understand. I guess they were offering prayers to someone."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.82
description: Jagannātha Miśra replied, "Never mind what it is. There is no need to worry. Let there always be good fortune for Viśvambhara. This is all I want."
text:
> miśra bale,---kichu ha-uk, cintā kichu nāi
> viśvambharera kuśala ha-uk,---ei mātra cāi
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:miśra]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---Jagannātha Miśra replied; [[synonyms:k:kichu]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:u:uk]]---whatever it may be; [[synonyms:c:cintā]] [[synonyms:k:kichu]] [[synonyms:n:nāi]]---don't be worried; [[synonyms:v:viśvambharera]]---of Viśvambhara; [[synonyms:k:kuśala]]---auspiciousness; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:u:uk]]---let there be; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mātra]]---only; [[synonyms:c:cāi]]---I want.
translation: Jagannātha Miśra replied, "Never mind what it is. There is no need to worry. Let there always be good fortune for Viśvambhara. This is all I want."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.83
description: On another occasion, Jagannātha Miśra, seeing the mischievous acts of his son, gave Him lessons in morality after rebuking Him greatly.
text:
> eka-dina miśra putrera cāpalya dekhiyā
> dharma-śikṣā dila bahu bhartsanā kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:m:miśra]]---Jagannātha Miśra; [[synonyms:p:putrera]]---of his son; [[synonyms:c:cāpalya]]---the mischievous behavior; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:ś:śikṣā]]---religious teaching; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---much; [[synonyms:b:bhartsanā]]---rebuking; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---doing.
translation: On another occasion, Jagannātha Miśra, seeing the mischievous acts of his son, gave Him lessons in morality after rebuking Him greatly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.84
description: On that very night, Jagannātha Miśra dreamt that a brāhmaṇa had come before him speaking these words in great anger:
text:
> rātre svapna dekhe,---eka āsi' brahmaṇa
> miśrere kahaye kichu sa-roṣa vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rātre]]---at night; [[synonyms:s:svapnadekhe]]---he dreamt; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:b:brāhmana]]---//brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:m:miśrere]]---unto Jagannātha Miśra; [[synonyms:k:kahaye]]---spoke; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:r:roṣa]]---with anger; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---words.
translation: On that very night, Jagannātha Miśra dreamt that a brāhmaṇa had come before him speaking these words in great anger:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.85
description: "My dear Miśra, you do not know anything about your son. You think Him your son, and therefore you rebuke and chastise Him."
text:
> "miśra, tumi putrera tattva kichui nā jāna
> bhartsana-tāḍana kara,---putra kari' māna"
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:miśra]]---my dear Jagannātha Miśra; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:p:putrera]]---of your son; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]---truth; [[synonyms:k:kichui]]---something; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---do not; [[synonyms:j:jāna]]---know; [[synonyms:b:bhartsana]]---rebuking; [[synonyms:t:tāḍana]]---chastisement; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---you do; [[synonyms:p:putra]]---son; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making Him; [[synonyms:m:māna]]---you regard.
translation: "My dear Miśra, you do not know anything about your son. You think Him your son, and therefore you rebuke and chastise Him."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.86
description: Jagannātha Miśra replied, "This boy may be a demigod, a mystic yogī or a great saintly person. It doesn't matter what He is, for I think He is only my son.
text:
> miśra kahe,---deva, siddha, muni kene naya
> ye se baḍa ha-uk mātra āmāra tanaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:miśra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Jagannātha Miśra replied; [[synonyms:d:deva]]---demigod; [[synonyms:s:siddha]]---mystic //yogī//; [[synonyms:m:muni]]---great saintly person; [[synonyms:k:kenenaya]]---may be so or not; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:s:se]]---whatever; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---great; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:u:uk]]---He may be; [[synonyms:m:mātra]]---only; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---my; [[synonyms:t:tanaya]]---son.
translation: Jagannātha Miśra replied, "This boy may be a demigod, a mystic yogī or a great saintly person. It doesn't matter what He is, for I think He is only my son.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.87
description: "It is the duty of a father to educate his son in both religion and morality. If I do not give Him this education, how will He know of it?"
text:
> putrera lālana-śikṣā---pitāra sva-dharma
> āmi nā śikhāle kaiche janibe dharma-marma
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:putrera]]---of the son; [[synonyms:l:lālana]]---maintenance; [[synonyms:ś:śikṣā]]---education; [[synonyms:p:pitara]]---of the father; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---duty; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---if I; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---do not; [[synonyms:ś:śikhāle]]---give education; [[synonyms:k:kaiche]]---how; [[synonyms:j:janibe]]---He will know; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:m:marma]]---religion and morality.
translation: "It is the duty of a father to educate his son in both religion and morality. If I do not give Him this education, how will He know of it?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.88
description: The brāhmaṇa replied, "If your son is a transcendental mystic boy with self-effulgent perfect knowledge, what is the use of your education?"
text:
> vipra kahe,---putra yadi daiva-siddha haya
> svataḥ-siddha-jñāna, tabe śikṣā vyartha haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the //brāhmaṇa// replied; [[synonyms:p:putra]]---son; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:d:daiva]]---transcendental; [[synonyms:s:siddha]]---mystic; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---were; [[synonyms:s:svataḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:siddha]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---self-illuminated perfect knowledge; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:ś:śikṣā]]---education; [[synonyms:v:vyartha]]---futile; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes.
translation: The brāhmaṇa replied, "If your son is a transcendental mystic boy with self-effulgent perfect knowledge, what is the use of your education?"
purport: The //brāhmaṇa// Jagannātha Miśra saw in his dream told him that his son was not an ordinary human being. If He were a transcendental person, He would have self-effulgent knowledge, and thus there would be no need to educate Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.89
description: Jagannātha Miśra replied, "Even if my son is not a common man but Nārāyaṇa, still it is the duty of a father to instruct his son."
text:
> miśra kahe,---"putra kene nahe nārāyaṇa
> tathāpi pitāra dharma---putrera śikṣaṇa"
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:miśra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Jagannātha Miśra replied; [[synonyms:p:putra]]---my son; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---may be; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---why not; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:p:pitāra]]---of a father; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---the duty; [[synonyms:p:putrera]]---of the son; [[synonyms:ś:śikṣaṇa]]---instruction.
translation: Jagannātha Miśra replied, "Even if my son is not a common man but Nārāyaṇa, still it is the duty of a father to instruct his son."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.9
description: Jagannātha Miśra said, "Certainly child Kṛṣṇa is with the śālagrāma-śilā. Taking His childhood form, He is playing within the room."
text:
> miśra kahe,---bālagopāla āche śilā-saṅge
> teṅho mūrti hañā ghare khele, jāni, raṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:miśra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Jagannātha Miśra said; [[synonyms:b:bāla]]-[[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa as a child; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there is; [[synonyms:ś:śilā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---along with the //śālagrāma-śilā//; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:m:mūrtihañā]]---taking His transcendental form; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---within the room; [[synonyms:k:khele]]---plays; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I understand; [[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---in curiosity.
translation: Jagannātha Miśra said, "Certainly child Kṛṣṇa is with the śālagrāma-śilā. Taking His childhood form, He is playing within the room."
purport: When the form of the Lord is carved from wood, stone or any other element, it is to be understood that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is there. Even logically we can understand that all material elements are expansions of the energy of the Lord. Since the energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is nondifferent from His personal body, the Lord is always present in His energy, and He manifests Himself on account of the ardent desire of a devotee. Since the Lord is supremely powerful, it is logical that He can manifest Himself in His energy. Deity worship or worship of the //śālagrāma-śilā// is not idol worship. The Deity of the Lord in the house of a pure devotee can act exactly as He can in His original transcendental personality.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.90
description: In this way Jagannātha Miśra and the brāhmaṇa discussed the principles of religion in the dream, yet Jagannātha Miśra was absorbed in unalloyed parental mellow and did not want to know anything else.
text:
> ei-mate duṅhe karena dharmera vicāra
> viśuddha-vātsalya miśrera, nāhi jāne āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---in this way; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---do; [[synonyms:d:dharmera]]---of religion; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---consideration; [[synonyms:v:viśuddha]]---unalloyed; [[synonyms:v:vātsalya]]---parental affection; [[synonyms:m:miśrera]]---of Jagannātha Miśra; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---he knew; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---anything else.
translation: In this way Jagannātha Miśra and the brāhmaṇa discussed the principles of religion in the dream, yet Jagannātha Miśra was absorbed in unalloyed parental mellow and did not want to know anything else.
purport: In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.8.45) it is said: "Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is worshiped with exalted hymns by all the //Vedas// and //Upaniṣads// and by great personalities through //sāṅkhya-yoga// in the mode of goodness, was considered by mother Yaśodā and Nanda to be their own little son." Similarly, Jagannātha Miśra also considered Lord Caitanya Mahāprahhu his beloved little boy, although He is worshiped with all veneration by learned //brāhmaṇas// and saintly persons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.91
description: Being very much pleased, the brāhmaṇa left after talking with Jagannātha Miśra, and when Jagannātha Miśra awakened from his dream, he was very much astonished.
text:
> eta śuni' dvija gelā hañā ānandita
> miśra jāgiyā ha-ilā parama vismita
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---after hearing so much; [[synonyms:d:dvija]]---the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---returned; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very much pleased; [[synonyms:m:miśra]]---Jagannātha Miśra; [[synonyms:j:jāgiyā]]---being awakened; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---highly; [[synonyms:v:vismita]]---astonished.
translation: Being very much pleased, the brāhmaṇa left after talking with Jagannātha Miśra, and when Jagannātha Miśra awakened from his dream, he was very much astonished.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.92
description: He related the dream to his friends and relatives, and every one of them was very much astonished to hear of it.
text:
> bandhu-bāndhava-sthāne svapna kahila
> śuniyā sakala loka vismita ha-ila

translation: He related the dream to his friends and relatives, and every one of them was very much astonished to hear of it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.93
description: In this way Gaurahari performed His childhood pastimes and day after day increased the pleasure of His parents.
text:
> ei mata śiśu-līlā kare gauracandra
> dine dine pitā-mātāra bāḍāya ānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mata]]---like; [[synonyms:ś:śiśu]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---childhood pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:g:gauracandra]]---Śrī Gaurahari; [[synonyms:d:dine]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---day after day; [[synonyms:p:pitā]]-[[synonyms:m:mātāra]]---of His parents; [[synonyms:b:bāḍāya]]---He increases; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---the pleasure.
translation: In this way Gaurahari performed His childhood pastimes and day after day increased the pleasure of His parents.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.94
description: After some days Jagannātha Miśra inaugurated the primary education of his son by performing the hāte khaḍi ceremony. Within a very few days the Lord learned all the letters and combinations of letters.
text:
> kata dine miśra putrera hāte khaḍi dila
> alpa dine dvādaśa-phalā akṣara śikhila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kata]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---after some days; [[synonyms:m:miśra]]---Jagannātha Miśra; [[synonyms:p:putrera]]---of his son; [[synonyms:h:hāte]]---in the hand; [[synonyms:k:khaḍi]]---chalk; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:a:alpa]]---within a very few; [[synonyms:d:dine]]---days; [[synonyms:d:dvādaśa]]-[[synonyms:p:phalā]]---twelve combinations of letters; [[synonyms:a:akṣara]]---letters; [[synonyms:ś:śikhila]]---learned.
translation: After some days Jagannātha Miśra inaugurated the primary education of his son by performing the hāte khaḍi ceremony. Within a very few days the Lord learned all the letters and combinations of letters.
purport: The twelve //phalā,// or combinations of letters, are called //repha, mūrdhanya// (cerebral), //ṇa, dāntavya// (dental), //na, ma, ya, ra, la, va, ṛ, ṝ, ḷ// and //ḷ. Hāte khaḍi// is the primary educational beginning. At the age of four or five years, on an auspicious day called //vidyārambha// marking the beginning of primary education, there is a ceremony worshiping Lord Viṣṇu, and after that the teacher gives the child a long chalk pencil. Then, guiding the hand of the student, he instructs him how to write the letters of the alphabet (//a, ā, i,// etc.) by writing big letters on the floor. When the child is a little advanced in writing, he is given a slate for his primary education, which ends when he learns the two-letter combinations, which are called //phalā,// as mentioned above.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 14.95
description: This is a synopsis of the childhood pastimes of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, placed herewith in chronological order. Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has already elaborately explained these pastimes in his book Caitanya-bhāgavata.
text:
> bālyalīlā-sūtra ei kaila anukrama
> ihā vistāriyāchena dāsa-vṛndāvana

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 15.10
description: Mother Śacī said, "You have spoken very nicely. I shall not eat grains on Ekādaśī." From that day, she began to observe fasting on Ekādaśī.
text:
> śacī kahe,---nā khāiba, bhāla-i kahilā
> sei haite ekādaśī karite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śacī]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---mother Śacī said; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:khāiba]]---I shall not take; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]-[[synonyms:i:i]] [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---You have said very nicely; [[synonyms:s:seihaite]]---from that day; [[synonyms:e:ekādaśī]]---Ekādaśī day; [[synonyms:k:karitelāgilā]]---began to observe.
translation: Mother Śacī said, "You have spoken very nicely. I shall not eat grains on Ekādaśī." From that day, she began to observe fasting on Ekādaśī.
purport: It is a prejudice amongst //smārta-brāhmaṇas// that a widow must observe fasting on Ekādaśī but a woman who has her husband should not. It appears that before the request of Lord Caitanya Śacīmātā was not observing Ekādaśī because of her being //sa-dhava,// which means that her husband was living. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, however, introduced the system that a woman, even if not a widow, must observe the Ekādaśī day and must not touch any kind of grains, even those offered to the Deity of Viṣṇu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 15.12

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 15.14
description: "My dear mother and father," the Lord said, "it is very good that Viśvarūpa has accepted the sannyāsa order, for thus He has delivered both His father's family and His mother's family."
text:
> bhāla haila,---viśvarūpa sannyāsa karila
> pitṛ-kula, mātṛ-kula,---dui uddhārila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāla]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---it is very good; [[synonyms:v:viśvarūpa]]---of the name Viśvarūpa; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---has accepted; [[synonyms:p:pitṛ]]-[[synonyms:k:kula]]---father's family; [[synonyms:m:mātṛ]]-[[synonyms:k:kula]]---mother's family; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---both of them; [[synonyms:u:uddhārila]]---delivered.
translation: "My dear mother and father," the Lord said, "it is very good that Viśvarūpa has accepted the sannyāsa order, for thus He has delivered both His father's family and His mother's family."
purport:
It is sometimes said that Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not approve of the acceptance of the //sannyāsa// order in this Kali-yuga because in the //śāstra// it is said:

> aśvamedhaṁ gavālambhaṁ
> sannyāsaṁ pala-paitṛkam
> devareṇa sutotpattiṁ
> kalau pañca vivarjayet

"In this Kali-yuga the performance of the //aśvamedha-yajña// or //gomedha-yajña,// sacrifices in which a horse or cow is offered, should be avoided, as should the acceptance of //sannyāsa,// the renounced order of life." (//Brahma-vaivarta Purāṇa, Kṛṣṇa-janma-khaṇḍa// 185.180)

Nevertheless we see that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself accepted //sannyāsa// and approved of the //sannyāsa of// His elder brother, Viśvarūpa. It is clearly said here, //bhāla haila,---viśvarūpa sannyāsa karila pitṛ-kula, mātṛ-kula,---dui uddhārila.// Therefore, should it be thought that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu made statements that are contradictory? No, actually He did not. It is recommended that one accept //sannyāsa// to dedicate his life for the service of the Lord, and everyone must take that kind of //sannyāsa,// for by accepting such //sannyāsa// one renders the best service to both his paternal and maternal families. But one should not accept the //sannyāsa// order of the Māyāvāda school, which has practically no meaning. We find many Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// simply loitering in the street thinking themselves Brahman or Nārāyaṇa and spending all day and night begging so they can fill their hungry bellies. Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// have become so degraded that there is a section of them who eat everything, just like hogs and dogs. It is such degraded //sannyāsa// that is prohibited in this age. Actually, Śrīla Śaṅkarācārya's principles for the acceptance of //sannyāsa// were very strict, but later the so-called Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// became degraded because of their false philosophy, which propounds that by accepting //sannyāsa// one becomes Nārāyaṇa. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu rejected that kind of //sannyāsa.// But the acceptance of //sannyāsa// is one of the items of the //varṇāśrama-dharma.// How then can it be rejected?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 15.16
description: One day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ate betel nuts offered to the Deity, but they acted as an intoxicant, and He fell down on the ground unconscious.
text:
> eka-dina naivedya-tāmbūla khāiyā
> bhūmite paḍilā prabhu acetana hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:n:naivedya]]---food offered to the Deity; [[synonyms:t:tāmbūla]]---betel nut; [[synonyms:k:khāiyā]]---after eating; [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:padilā]]---fell; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:a:acetana]]---unconscious; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming.
translation: One day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ate betel nuts offered to the Deity, but they acted as an intoxicant, and He fell down on the ground unconscious.
purport: Betel nuts are an intoxicant, and therefore the regulative principles prohibit eating them. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastime of fainting after eating betel nuts is a solid instruction to all of us that one should not touch betel nuts, even those offered to Viṣṇu, just as one should not touch grains on the Ekādaśī day. Of course, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's fainting had a particular purpose. As the Supreme Personality of Godhead, He can do whatever He likes and eat whatever He wants, but we should not imitate His pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 15.22
description: In this way Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed various pastimes, but why He did so I cannot understand.
text:
> ei mata nānā līlā kare gaurahari
> ki kāraṇe līlā,---ihā bujhite nā pāri
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:k:kāraṇe]]---what is the reason; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---I am able.
translation: In this way Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed various pastimes, but why He did so I cannot understand.
purport: The Supreme Personality of Godhead and His devotees who come to this world are executing a mission, and therefore sometimes they act in a way that is very difficult to understand. It is said, therefore, //vaiṣṇavera kriyā-mudrā vijñeha nā bujhaya:// even if one is a very learned and intelligent scholar, he cannot understand the activities of a Vaiṣṇava. A Vaiṣṇava accepts anything favorable for executing his mission. But foolish persons, not knowing the purpose of such exalted Vaiṣṇavas, indulge in criticizing them. That is forbidden. Since no one can understand what a Vaiṣṇava does for the purpose of executing his mission, to criticize such a Vaiṣṇava is the offense called //sādhu-nindā.//
