title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.265
description: "I shall accept the sannyāsa order of life, for thus people will offer Me their obeisances, thinking of Me as a member of the renounced order.
text:
> ataeva avaśya āmi sannyāsa kariba
> sannyāsi-buddhye more praṇata ha-iba
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---shall accept; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsi]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhye]]---by thinking of Me as a //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:p:praṇata]]---bow down; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:iba]]---they shall do.
translation: "I shall accept the sannyāsa order of life, for thus people will offer Me their obeisances, thinking of Me as a member of the renounced order.
purport:
Among the members of the //varṇāśrama// institution's social orders (//brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya// and //śūdra//), the //brāhmaṇa// is considered the foremost, for he is the teacher and spiritual master of all the other //varṇas.// Similarly, among the spiritual orders (//brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha// and //sannyāsa//), the //sannyāsa// order is the most elevated. Therefore a //sannyāsī// is the spiritual master of all the //varṇas// and //āśramas,// and a //brāhmaṇa// is also expected to offer obeisances to a //sannyāsī.// Unfortunately, however, caste //brāhmaṇas// do not offer obeisances to a Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsī.// They are so proud that they do not offer obeisances even to Indian //sannyāsīs,// what to speak of European and American //sannyāsīs.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, however, expected that even the caste //brāhmaṇas// would offer respectful obeisances to a //sannyāsī// because five hundred years ago the social custom was to offer obeisances immediately to any //sannyāsī,// known or unknown.

The //sannyāsīs// of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement are bona fide. All the students of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement have undergone the regular process of initiation. As enjoined in the //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa// by Sanātana Gosvāmī, //tathā dīkṣā-vidhānena dvijatvaṁ jāyate nṛṇām:// by the regular process of initiation, any man can become a //brāhmaṇa.// Thus in the beginning the students of our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement agree to live with devotees, and gradually, having given up four prohibited activities-illicit sex, gambling, meat-eating and intoxication---they become advanced in the activities of spiritual life. When one is found to be regularly following these principles, he is given the first initiation (//hari-nāma//), and he regularly chants at least sixteen rounds a day. Then, after six months or a year, he is initiated for the second time and given the sacred thread with the regular sacrifice and rituals. After some time, when he advances still further and is willing to give up this material world, he is given the //sannyāsa// order. At that time he receives the title //svāmī or gosvāmī,// both of which mean "master of the senses." Unfortunately, debauched so-called //brāhmaṇas// in India neither offer them respect nor accept them as bona fide //sannyāsīs.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu expected the so-called //brāhmaṇas// to offer respect to such Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsīs.// Nevertheless, it does not matter whether they offer respect or whether they accept these //sannyāsīs// as bona fide, for the //śāstra// describes punishment for such disobedient so-called //brāhmaṇas.// The śāstric injuction declares:

> devatā-pratimāṁ dṛṣṭvā
> yatiṁ caiva tridaṇḍinam
> namaskāraṁ na kuryād yaḥ
> prāyaścittīyate naraḥ

"One who does not offer respect to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, to His Deity in the temple or to a //tridaṇḍī sannyāsī// must undergo //prāyaścitta// [atonement]." If one does not offer obeisances to such a //sannyāsī,// the prescribed //prāyaścitta// is to fast for one day.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.266
description: "Offering obeisances will relieve them of all the reactions to their offenses. Then, by My grace, devotional service [bhakti] will awaken in their pure hearts.
text:
> praṇatite habe ihāra aparādha kṣaya
> nirmala hṛdaye bhakti karāiba udaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:praṇatite]]---by offering obeisances; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of such offenders; [[synonyms:a:aparādha]]---the offenses; [[synonyms:k:kṣaya]]---destruction; [[synonyms:n:nirmala]]---pure; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---in the heart; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:k:karāiba]]---I shall cause; [[synonyms:u:udaya]]---the rising.
translation: "Offering obeisances will relieve them of all the reactions to their offenses. Then, by My grace, devotional service [bhakti] will awaken in their pure hearts.
purport: According to Vedic injunctions, only a //brāhmaṇa// may be offered //sannyāsa.// The Śaṅkara-sampradāya (//ekadaṇḍa-sannyāsa-sampradāya//) awards the //sannyāsa// order only to caste //brāhmaṇas,// or born //brāhmaṇas,// but in the Vaiṣṇava system even one not born in a //brāhmaṇa// family may be made a //brāhmaṇa// according to the direction of the //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa// (//tathā dīkṣā-vidhānena dvijatvaṁ jāyate nṛṇām//). Any person from any part of the world may be made a //brāhmaṇa// by the regular process of initiation, and when he follows brahminical behavior, observing the principle of abstaining from intoxication, illicit sex, meat-eating and gambling, he may be offered //sannyāsa.// All the //sannyāsīs// in the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, who are preaching all over the world, are regular //brāhmaṇa-sannyāsīs.// Thus the so-called caste //brāhmaṇas// should not object to offering them respectful obeisances. By offering such obeisances, as recommended by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they will diminish their offenses and automatically awaken to their natural position of devotional service. As it is said, //nitya-siddha kṛṣṇa-prema sādhya kabhu naya:kṛṣṇa-prema// can be awakened in a purified heart. The more we offer obeisances to //sannyāsīs,// especially Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsīs,// the more we diminish our offenses and purify our hearts. Only in a purified heart can //kṛṣṇa-prema// awaken. This is the process of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's cult, the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.267
description: "All the unfaithful rogues of this world can be delivered by this process. There is no alternative. This is the essence of the argument."

> āra kona upāya nāhi, ei yukti sāra

translation: "All the unfaithful rogues of this world can be delivered by this process. There is no alternative. This is the essence of the argument."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.268
description: After coming to this firm conclusion, the Lord continued to stay at home. In the meantime Keśava Bhāratī came to the town of Nadia.
text:
> ei dṛḍha yukti kari' prabhu āche ghare
> keśava bhāratī āilā nadīyā-nagare
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]]---firm; [[synonyms:y:yukti]]---consideration; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---was; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in His home; [[synonyms:k:keśava]] [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]]---of the name Keśava Bhāratī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:n:nadīyā]]-[[synonyms:n:nagare]]---to the town of Nadia.
translation: After coming to this firm conclusion, the Lord continued to stay at home. In the meantime Keśava Bhāratī came to the town of Nadia.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.269
description: The Lord offered him respectful obeisances and invited him to His house. After feeding him sumptuously, He submitted to him His petition.
text:
> prabhu tāṅre namaskari' kaila nimantraṇa
> bhikṣā karāiyā tāṅre kaila nivedana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to him; [[synonyms:n:namaskari']]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---alms; [[synonyms:k:karāiyā]]---giving; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to him; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---submitted; [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---His prayer.
translation: The Lord offered him respectful obeisances and invited him to His house. After feeding him sumptuously, He submitted to him His petition.
purport: According to the system of Vedic society, whenever an unknown //sannyāsī// comes to a village or town, someone must invite him to take //prasāda// in his home. //Sannyāsīs// generally take //prasāda// in the house of a //brāhmaṇa// because the //brāhmaṇa// worships the Lord Nārāyaṇa //śilā,// or //śālagrāma-śilā,// and therefore there is //prasāda// that the //sannyāsī// may take. Keśava Bhāratī accepted the invitation of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Thus the Lord had a good opportunity to explain His desire to take //sannyāsa// from him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.27
description: "A devotee engaged in chanting the holy name of the Lord should practice forbearance like that of a tree. Even if rebuked or chastised, he should not say anything to others to retaliate.
text:
> taru-sama sahiṣṇutā vaiṣṇava karibe
> bhartsana-tāḍane kāke kichu nā balibe
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:taru]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---like a tree; [[synonyms:s:sahiṣṇutā]]---forbearance; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotee; [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---should practice; [[synonyms:b:bhartsana]]---rebuking; [[synonyms:t:tāḍane]]---chastising; [[synonyms:k:kāke]]---unto anyone; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:b:balibe]]---will utter.
translation: "A devotee engaged in chanting the holy name of the Lord should practice forbearance like that of a tree. Even if rebuked or chastised, he should not say anything to others to retaliate.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.270
description: "Sir, you are directly Nārāyaṇa. Therefore please be merciful unto Me. Deliver Me from this material bondage."
text:
> tumi ta' īśvara baṭa,---sākṣāt nārāyaṇa
> kṛpā kari' kara mora saṁsāra mocana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:b:baṭa]]---are; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---the Supreme Lord, Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing mercy; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---please do; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]---material life; [[synonyms:m:mocana]]---deliverance.
translation: "Sir, you are directly Nārāyaṇa. Therefore please be merciful unto Me. Deliver Me from this material bondage."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.271
description: Keśava Bhāratī replied to the Lord, "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Supersoul. I must do whatever You cause me to do. I am not independent of You."
text:
> bhāratī kahena,---tumi īśvara, antaryāmī
> ye karāha, se kariba,---svatantra nahi āmi
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Keśava Bhāratī replied; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:antaryāmī]]---You know everything from within; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:k:karāha]]---You cause to do; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---I must do; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]]---independent; [[synonyms:n:nahi]]---not; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I.
translation: Keśava Bhāratī replied to the Lord, "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Supersoul. I must do whatever You cause me to do. I am not independent of You."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.272
description: After saying this, Keśava Bhāratī, the spiritual master, went back to his village, Katwa. Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu went there and accepted the renounced order of life [sannyāsa].
text:
> eta bali' bhāratī gosāñi kāṭoyāte gelā
> mahāprabhu tāhā yāi' sannyāsa karilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]]---Keśava Bhāratī; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---the spiritual master; [[synonyms:k:kāṭoyāte]]---to Katwa; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tahā]]---there; [[synonyms:y:yai']]---going; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---accepted.
translation: After saying this, Keśava Bhāratī, the spiritual master, went back to his village, Katwa. Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu went there and accepted the renounced order of life [sannyāsa].
purport:
At the end of His twenty-fourth year, at the end of the fortnight of the waxing moon, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu left Navadvīpa and crossed the river Ganges at a place known as Nidayāra-ghāṭa. Then He reached Kaṇṭaka-nagara, or Kāṭoyā (Katwa), where He accepted //ekadaṇḍa-sannyāsa// according to the Śaṅkarite system. Since Keśava Bhāratī belonged to the Śaṅkarite sect, he could not initiate Caitanya Mahāprabhu into the Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsa// order, whose members carry the //tridaṇḍa.//

Candraśekhara Ācārya assisted in the routine ceremonial work of the Lord's acceptance of //sannyāsa.// By the order of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, //kīrtana// was performed for the entire day, and at the end of the day the Lord shaved off His hair. On the next day He became a regular //sannyāsī,// with one rod (//ekadaṇḍa//). From that day on His name was Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. Before that, He was known as Nimāi Paṇḍita. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, in the //sannyāsa// order, traveled all over Rāḍha-deśa, the region where the Ganges River cannot be seen. Keśava Bhāratī accompanied Him for some distance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.273
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted sannyāsa, three personalities were with Him to perform all the necessary activities. They were Nityānanda Prabhu, Candraśekhara Ācārya and Mukunda Datta.
text:
> saṅge nityānanda, candraśekhara ācārya
> mukunda-datta,---ei tina kaila sarva kārya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in His company; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:c:candraśekhara]] [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Candraśekhara Ācārya; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]-[[synonyms:d:datta]]---Mukunda Datta; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:tina]]---these three; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kārya]]---necessary activities.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted sannyāsa, three personalities were with Him to perform all the necessary activities. They were Nityānanda Prabhu, Candraśekhara Ācārya and Mukunda Datta.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.274
description: Thus I have summarized the incidents of the ādi-līlā. Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has described them elaborately [in his Caitanya-bhāgavata].
text:
> ei ādi-līlāra kaila sūtra gaṇana
> vistāri varṇilā ihā dāsa vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:l:līlara]]---of the //ādi-līlā// (the first portion of Lord Caitanya's pastimes); [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:s:sūtra]]---synopsis; [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---enumeration; [[synonyms:v:vistāri]]---elaborately; [[synonyms:v:varṇilā]]---described; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]] [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura.
translation: Thus I have summarized the incidents of the ādi-līlā. Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has described them elaborately [in his Caitanya-bhāgavata].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.275
description: The same Supreme Personality of Godhead who appeared as the son of mother Yaśodā has now appeared as the son of mother Śacī, relishing four kinds of devotional activities.
text:
> yaśodā-nandana hailā śacīra nandana
> catur-vidha bhakta-bhāva kare āsvādana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yaśodā]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of mother Yaśodā; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:ś:śacīra]]---of mother Śacī; [[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]]---four kinds of; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---devotional humors; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasting.
translation: The same Supreme Personality of Godhead who appeared as the son of mother Yaśodā has now appeared as the son of mother Śacī, relishing four kinds of devotional activities.
purport: Servitude, friendship, parental affection and conjugal love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead are the basis of the four kinds of devotional activities. In //śānta,// the marginal stage of devotional service, there is no activity. But above the //śānta// humor are servitude, friendship, parental affection and conjugal love, which represent the gradual growth of devotional service to higher and higher platforms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.276
description: To taste the mellows of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's loving affairs in Her relationship with Kṛṣṇa, and to understand the reservoir of pleasure in Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Himself, as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, accepted the mood of Rādhārāṇī.
text:
> sva-mādhurya rādhā-prema-rasa āsvādite
> rādhā-bhāva aṅgī kariyāche bhāla-mate
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---His own conjugal love; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---the mellow of the loving affairs between Rādhārāṇī and Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādite]]---to taste; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the mood of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:a:aṅgī]] [[synonyms:k:kariyāche]]---He accepted; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---very well.
translation: To taste the mellows of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's loving affairs in Her relationship with Kṛṣṇa, and to understand the reservoir of pleasure in Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Himself, as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, accepted the mood of Rādhārāṇī.
purport:
In this connection Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura writes in his //Anubhāṣya,// "Śrī Gaurasundara is Kṛṣṇa Himself with the attitude of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu never gave up the attitude of the //gopīs.// He remained everlastingly predominated by Kṛṣṇa and never accepted the part of the predominator by imitating conjugal love with an ordinary woman, as //sahajiyās// generally do. He never placed Himself in the position of a debauchee. Lusty materialists like the members of the //sahajiyā-sampradāya// hanker after women, even others' wives. But when they try to ascribe the responsibility for their lusty activities to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they become offenders to Svarūpa Dāmodara and Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura. In //Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata, Ādi-khaṇḍa,// Chapter Fifteen, it is said:

> sabe para-strīra prati nāhi parihāsa
> strī dekhi' dūre prabhu hayena eka-pāśa

'Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu never even joked with others' wives. As soon as He saw a woman coming, He would immediately give her ample room to pass without talking.' He was extremely strict regarding the association of women. The //sahajiyās,// however, pose as followers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu although they indulge in lusty affairs with women. In His youth Lord Caitanya was very humorous with everyone, but He never joked with any woman, nor in this incarnation did He talk about women. The //gaurāṅga-nāgarī// party is not approved by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu or Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura. Even though one may offer all kinds of prayers to Caitanya Mahāprabhu, one should strictly avoid worshiping Him as the Gaurāṅga Nāgara. The personal behavior of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and the verses written by Śrī Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura have completely repudiated the lusty desires of the //gaurāṅga-nāgarīs.//"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.277
description: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the mood of the gopīs, who accept Vrajendranandana, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, as their lover.
text:
> gopī-bhāva yāte prabhu dhariyāche ekānta
> vrajendra-nandane māne āpanāra kānta
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the mood of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---in which; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dhariyāche]]---accepted; [[synonyms:e:ekānta]]---positively; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandane]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---they accept; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāra]]---own; [[synonyms:k:kānta]]---lover.
translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the mood of the gopīs, who accept Vrajendranandana, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, as their lover.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.278
description: It is firmly ascertained that the ecstatic mood of the gopīs is possible only before Kṛṣṇa, and no one else.
text:
> gopikā-bhāvera ei sudṛḍha niścaya
> vrajendra-nandana vinā anyatra nā haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopikā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of the ecstasy of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:sudṛḍha]]---firm; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---confirmation; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:a:anyatra]]---anyone else; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is possible.
translation: It is firmly ascertained that the ecstatic mood of the gopīs is possible only before Kṛṣṇa, and no one else.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.279
description: He has a bluish complexion, a peacock feather on His head, a guñjā garland and the decorations of a cowherd boy. His body is curved in three places, and He holds a flute to His mouth.
text:
> śyāmasundara, śikhipiccha-guñjā-vibhūṣaṇa
> gopa-veśa, tri-bhaṅgima, muralī-vadana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śyāma]]-[[synonyms:s:sundara]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa, who has a bluish color; [[synonyms:ś:śikhi]]-[[synonyms:p:piccha]]---with a peacock feather on the head; [[synonyms:g:guñjā]]---a garland of //guñjā// (small berries or conchshells); [[synonyms:v:vibhūṣaṇa]]---decorations; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:v:veśa]]---with the dress of a cowherd boy; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṅgima]]---curved in three places; [[synonyms:m:muralī]]-[[synonyms:v:vadana]]---holding a flute to His mouth.
translation: He has a bluish complexion, a peacock feather on His head, a guñjā garland and the decorations of a cowherd boy. His body is curved in three places, and He holds a flute to His mouth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.28
description: "For even if one cuts a tree, it never protests, and even if it is drying up and dying it does not ask anyone for water.
text:
> kāṭileha taru yena kichu nā bolaya
> śukāiyā mare, tabu jala nā māgaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāṭileha]]---even being cut; [[synonyms:t:taru]]---the tree; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:b:bolaya]]---says; [[synonyms:ś:śukāiyā]]---drying up; [[synonyms:m:mare]]---dies; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---water; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:m:māgaya]]---ask for.
translation: "For even if one cuts a tree, it never protests, and even if it is drying up and dying it does not ask anyone for water.
purport: This practice of forbearance (//tṛṇād api sunīcena//) is very difficult, but when one actually engages in chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra,// the quality of forbearance automatically develops. A person advanced in spiritual consciousness through the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// need not practice to develop it separately, for a devotee develops all good qualities simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// regularly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.280
description: If Lord Kṛṣṇa gives up this original form and assumes another Viṣṇu form, nearness to Him cannot invoke the ecstatic mood of the gopīs.
text:
> ihā chāḍi' kṛṣṇa yadi haya anyākāra
> gopikāra bhāva nāhi yāya nikaṭa tāhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---takes; [[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---another form; [[synonyms:g:gopikāra]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the ecstasy; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---does not; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---arise; [[synonyms:n:nikaṭa]]---near; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---that (form).
translation: If Lord Kṛṣṇa gives up this original form and assumes another Viṣṇu form, nearness to Him cannot invoke the ecstatic mood of the gopīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.281
description: "Once Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa playfully manifested Himself as Nārāyaṇa, with four victorious hands and a very beautiful form. When the gopīs saw this exalted form, however, their ecstatic feelings were crippledī. A learned scholar, therefore, cannot understand the gopīs' ecstatic feelings, which are firmly fixed upon the original form of Lord Kṛṣṇa as the son of Nanda Mahārāja. The wonderful feelings of the gopīs in ecstatic parama-rasa with Kṛṣṇa constitute the greatest mystery in spiritual life.""
text:
> gopīnāṁ paśupendra-nandana-juṣo bhāvasya kas tāṁ krtī
> vijñātuṁ kṣamate durūha-padavī-sañcāriṇaḥ prakriyām
> āviṣkurvati vaiṣṇavīm api tanuṁ tasmin bhujair jiṣṇubhir
> yāsāṁ hanta caturbhir adbhuta-ruciṁ rāgodayaḥ kuñcati
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnām]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:p:paśupa]]-[[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]-[[synonyms:j:juṣaḥ]]---of the service of the son of Vraja's King, Mahārāja Nanda; [[synonyms:b:bhāvasya]]---ecstatic; [[synonyms:k:kaḥ]]---what; [[synonyms:t:tām]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kṛtī]]---learned man; [[synonyms:v:vijñātum]]---to understand; [[synonyms:k:kṣamate]]---is able; [[synonyms:d:durūha]]---very difficult to understand; [[synonyms:p:padavī]]---the position; [[synonyms:s:sañcāriṇaḥ]]---which provokes; [[synonyms:p:prakriyām]]---activity; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣkurvati]]---He manifests; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavīm]]---of Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:a:api]]---certainly; [[synonyms:t:tanum]]---the body; [[synonyms:t:tasmin]]---in that; [[synonyms:b:bhujaiḥ]]---with arms; [[synonyms:j:jiṣṇubhiḥ]]---very beautiful; [[synonyms:y:yāsām]]---of whom (the //gopīs//); [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---alas; [[synonyms:c:caturbhiḥ]]---four; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderfully; [[synonyms:r:rucim]]---beautiful; [[synonyms:r:rāga]]-[[synonyms:u:udayaḥ]]---the evoking of ecstatic feelings; [[synonyms:k:kuñcati]]---cripples.
translation: "Once Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa playfully manifested Himself as Nārāyaṇa, with four victorious hands and a very beautiful form. When the gopīs saw this exalted form, however, their ecstatic feelings were crippledī. A learned scholar, therefore, cannot understand the gopīs' ecstatic feelings, which are firmly fixed upon the original form of Lord Kṛṣṇa as the son of Nanda Mahārāja. The wonderful feelings of the gopīs in ecstatic parama-rasa with Kṛṣṇa constitute the greatest mystery in spiritual life.""
purport: This is a quotation from the //Lalita-mādhava// (6.54), by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.282
description: During the season of springtime, when the rāsa dance was going on, suddenly Kṛṣṇa disappeared from the scene, indicating that He wanted to be alone with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
text:
> vasanta-kāle rāsa-līlā kare govardhane
> antardhāna kailā saṅketa kari' rādhā-sane
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vasanta]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---during the season of spring; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:g:govardhane]]---near the Govardhana Hill; [[synonyms:a:antardhāna]]---disappearance; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:s:saṅketa]]---indication; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with Rādhārāṇī.
translation: During the season of springtime, when the rāsa dance was going on, suddenly Kṛṣṇa disappeared from the scene, indicating that He wanted to be alone with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.283
description: Kṛṣṇa was sitting in a solitary bush, waiting for Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī to pass by. But while He was searching, the gopīs arrived there, like a phalanx of soldiers.
text:
> nibhṛta-nikuñje vasi' dekhe rādhāra bāṭa
> anveṣite āilā tāhāṅ gopikāra ṭhāṭa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nibhṛta]]---solitary; [[synonyms:n:nikuñje]]---in a bush; [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---waiting to see; [[synonyms:r:rādhāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:b:bāṭa]]---the passing; [[synonyms:a:anveṣite]]---while searching; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:g:gopikāra]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāṭa]]---the phalanx.
translation: Kṛṣṇa was sitting in a solitary bush, waiting for Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī to pass by. But while He was searching, the gopīs arrived there, like a phalanx of soldiers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.284
description: "Just see!" the gopīs said, seeing Kṛṣṇa from a distant place. "Here within a bush is Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja."
text:
> dūra haite kṛṣṇe dekhi' bale gopī-gaṇa
> "ei dekha kuñjera bhitara vrajendra-nandana"
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from a distance; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---said; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dekha]]---just see here; [[synonyms:k:kuñjera]]---the bush; [[synonyms:b:bhitara]]---within; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of Nanda Mahārāja.
translation: "Just see!" the gopīs said, seeing Kṛṣṇa from a distant place. "Here within a bush is Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.285
description: As soon as Kṛṣṇa saw all the gopīs, He was struck with emotion. Thus He could not hide Himself, and out of fear He became motionless.
text:
> gopī-gaṇa dekhi' kṛṣṇera ha-ila sādhvasa
> lukāite nārila, bhaye hailā vibaśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the //gopīs// combined together; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there were; [[synonyms:s:sādhvasa]]---some emotional feelings; [[synonyms:l:lukāite]]---to hide; [[synonyms:n:nārila]]---was unable; [[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---out of fear; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vibaśa]]---motionless.
translation: As soon as Kṛṣṇa saw all the gopīs, He was struck with emotion. Thus He could not hide Himself, and out of fear He became motionless.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.286
description: Kṛṣṇa assumed His four-armed Nārāyaṇa form and sat there. When all the gopīs came, they looked at Him and spoke as follows.
text:
> catur-bhuja mūrti dhari' āchena vasiyā
> kṛṣṇa dekhi' gopī kahe nikaṭe āsiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:catur]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---four-armed; [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---form; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:ā:āchena]]---was; [[synonyms:v:vasiyā]]---sitting; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---say; [[synonyms:n:nikaṭe]]---nearby; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming there.
translation: Kṛṣṇa assumed His four-armed Nārāyaṇa form and sat there. When all the gopīs came, they looked at Him and spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.287
description: "He is not Kṛṣṇa! He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa." After saying this, they offered obeisances and the following respectful prayers.
text:
> 'ihoṅ kṛṣṇa nahe, ihoṅ nārāyaṇa mūrti'
> eta bali' tāṅre sabhe kare nati-stuti
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ihoṅ]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---is not; [[synonyms:i:ihoṅ]]---this is; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---the form; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:s:sabhe]]---all the gopīs; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---make; [[synonyms:n:nati]]-[[synonyms:s:stuti]]---obeisances and prayers.
translation: "He is not Kṛṣṇa! He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa." After saying this, they offered obeisances and the following respectful prayers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.288
description: "O Lord Nārāyaṇa, we offer our respectful obeisances unto You. Kindly be merciful to us. Give us the association of Kṛṣṇa and thus vanquish our lamentation."
text:
> "namo nārāyaṇa, deva karaha prasāda
> kṛṣṇa-saṅga deha' mora ghucāha viṣāda"
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]] [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---all respects to Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:d:deva]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---kindly give; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---Your mercy; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---association with Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:deha']]---giving; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---our; [[synonyms:g:ghucāha]]---please diminish; [[synonyms:v:viṣāda]]---lamentation.
translation: "O Lord Nārāyaṇa, we offer our respectful obeisances unto You. Kindly be merciful to us. Give us the association of Kṛṣṇa and thus vanquish our lamentation."
purport: The //gopīs// were not made happy even by seeing the four-armed form of Nārāyaṇa. Yet they offered their respects to the Supreme Personality of Godhead and begged from Him the benediction of achieving the association of Kṛṣṇa. Such is the ecstatic feeling of the //gopīs.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.289
description: After saying this and offering obeisances, all the gopīs dispersed. Then Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī came and appeared before Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> eta bali namaskari' gelā gopī-gaṇa
> hena-kāle rādhā āsi' dilā daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali]]---saying this; [[synonyms:n:namaskari']]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went away; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming there; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---audience.
translation: After saying this and offering obeisances, all the gopīs dispersed. Then Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī came and appeared before Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.29
description: "Thus a Vaiṣṇava should not ask anything from anyone else. If someone gives him something without being asked, he should accept it, but if nothing comes, a Vaiṣṇava should be satisfied to eat whatever vegetables and fruits are easily available.
text:
> ei-mata vaiṣṇava kāre kichu nā māgiba
> ayācita-vṛtti, kiṁvā śāka-phala khāiba
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---a devotee; [[synonyms:k:kāre]]---from anyone; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---anything; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:m:māgiba]]---shall ask for; [[synonyms:a:ayācita]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛtti]]---the profession of not asking for anything; [[synonyms:k:kiṁvā]]---or; [[synonyms:ś:śāka]]---vegetables; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---fruits; [[synonyms:k:khāiba]]---shall eat.
translation: "Thus a Vaiṣṇava should not ask anything from anyone else. If someone gives him something without being asked, he should accept it, but if nothing comes, a Vaiṣṇava should be satisfied to eat whatever vegetables and fruits are easily available.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.290
description: When Lord Kṛṣṇa saw Rādhārāṇī, He wanted to maintain the four-armed form to joke with Her.
text:
> rādhā dekhi' kṛṣṇa tāṅre hāsya karite
> sei catur-bhuja mūrti cāhena rākhite
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Her; [[synonyms:h:hāsya]]---joking; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to do; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:c:catur]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---four-armed; [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---form; [[synonyms:c:cāhena]]---wanted; [[synonyms:r:rākhite]]---to keep.
translation: When Lord Kṛṣṇa saw Rādhārāṇī, He wanted to maintain the four-armed form to joke with Her.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.291
description: In front of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Śrī Kṛṣṇa had to hide the two extra arms. He tried His best to keep four arms before Her, but He was completely unable to do so.
text:
> lukāilā dui bhuja rādhāra agrete
> bahu yatna kailā kṛṣṇa, nārila rākhite
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lukāilā]]---He hid; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---arms; [[synonyms:r:rādhāra]]---of Srīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:a:agrete]]---in front; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---much; [[synonyms:y:yatna]]---endeavor; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nārila]]---was unable; [[synonyms:r:rākhite]]---to keep.
translation: In front of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Śrī Kṛṣṇa had to hide the two extra arms. He tried His best to keep four arms before Her, but He was completely unable to do so.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.292
description: The influence of Rādhārāṇī's pure ecstasy is so inconceivably great that it forced Kṛṣṇa to come to His original two-armed form.
text:
> rādhāra viśuddha-bhāvera acintya prabhāva
> ye kṛṣṇere karāilā dvi-bhuja-svabhāva
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rādhāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:v:viśuddha]]---purified; [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of the ecstasy; [[synonyms:a:acintya]]---inconceivable; [[synonyms:p:prabhāva]]---influence; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]]---unto Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:karāilā]]---forced; [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---two-armed; [[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---original form.
translation: The influence of Rādhārāṇī's pure ecstasy is so inconceivably great that it forced Kṛṣṇa to come to His original two-armed form.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.293
description: "Prior to the rāsa dance, Lord Kṛṣṇa hid Himself in a grove just to have fun. When the gopīs came, their eyes resembling those of deer, by His sharp intelligence He exhibited His beautiful four-armed form to hide Himself. But when Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī came there, Kṛṣṇa could not maintain His four arms in Her presence. This is the wonderful glory of Her love."
text:
> rāsārambha-vidhau nilīya vasatā kuñje mṛgākṣī-gaṇair
> dṛṣṭaṁ gopayituṁ svam uddhura-dhiyā yā suṣṭhu sandarśitā
> rādhāyāḥ praṇayasya hanta mahimā yasya śriyā rakṣituṁ
> sā śakyā prabhaviṣṇunāpi hariṇā nāsīc catur-bāhutā
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārambha]]-[[synonyms:v:vidhau]]---in the matter of beginning the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:n:nilīya]]---having hidden; [[synonyms:v:vasatā]]---sitting; [[synonyms:k:kuñje]]---in a grove; [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]-[[synonyms:a:akṣī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇaiḥ]]---by the //gopīs,// who had eyes resembling those of deer; [[synonyms:d:dṛṣṭam]]---being seen; [[synonyms:g:gopayitum]]---to hide; [[synonyms:s:svam]]---Himself; [[synonyms:u:uddhura]]-[[synonyms:d:dhiyā]]---by first-class intelligence; [[synonyms:y:yā]]---which; [[synonyms:s:suṣṭhu]]---perfectly; [[synonyms:s:sandarśitā]]---exhibited; [[synonyms:r:rādhāyāḥ]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:p:praṇayasya]]---of the love; [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---just see; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---the glory; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of which; [[synonyms:ś:śriyā]]---the opulence; [[synonyms:r:rakṣitum]]---to protect that; [[synonyms:s:sā]]---that; [[synonyms:ś:śakyā]]---able; [[synonyms:p:prabhaviṣṇunā]]---by Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:h:hariṇā]]---by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:ā:āsīt]]---was; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhutā]]---four-armed form.
translation: "Prior to the rāsa dance, Lord Kṛṣṇa hid Himself in a grove just to have fun. When the gopīs came, their eyes resembling those of deer, by His sharp intelligence He exhibited His beautiful four-armed form to hide Himself. But when Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī came there, Kṛṣṇa could not maintain His four arms in Her presence. This is the wonderful glory of Her love."
purport: This is a quotation from the //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi,// by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.294
description: Father Nanda, the King of Vrajabhūmi, is now Jagannātha Miśra, the father of Caitanya Mahāprabhu. And mother Yaśodā, the Queen of Vrajabhūmi, is now Śacīdevī, Lord Caitanya's mother.
text:
> sei vrajeśvara---ihaṅ jagannātha pitā
> sei vrajeśvarī---ihaṅ śacīdevī mātā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vrajeśvara]]---the King of Vraja; [[synonyms:i:ihaṅ]]---now; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Jagannātha Miśra; [[synonyms:p:pitā]]---the father of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vrajeśvarī]]---Queen of Vraja; [[synonyms:i:ihaṅ]]---now; [[synonyms:ś:śacīdevī]]---Śacīdevī; [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---the mother of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Father Nanda, the King of Vrajabhūmi, is now Jagannātha Miśra, the father of Caitanya Mahāprabhu. And mother Yaśodā, the Queen of Vrajabhūmi, is now Śacīdevī, Lord Caitanya's mother.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.295
description: The former son of Nanda Mahārāja is now Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the former Baladeva, Kṛṣṇa's brother, is now Nityānanda Prabhu, the brother of Lord Caitanya.
text:
> sei nanda-suta---ihaṅ caitanya-gosāñi
> sei baladeva---ihaṅ nityānanda bhāi
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:n:nanda]]-[[synonyms:s:suta]]---the same son of Nanda Mahārāja; [[synonyms:i:ihaṅ]]---now; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:b:baladeva]]---the selfsame Baladeva; [[synonyms:i:ihaṅ]]---now; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]] [[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---Nityānanda Prabhu, the brother of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: The former son of Nanda Mahārāja is now Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the former Baladeva, Kṛṣṇa's brother, is now Nityānanda Prabhu, the brother of Lord Caitanya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.296
description: Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu always feels the ecstatic emotions of paternity, servitude and friendship. He always assists Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in that way.
text:
> vātsalya, dāsya, sakhya---tina bhāvamaya
> sei nityānanda---kṛṣṇa-caitanya-sahāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vātsalya]]---paternity; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]---servitude; [[synonyms:s:sakhya]]---fraternity; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---emotional ecstasies; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sahāya]]---the assistant.
translation: Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu always feels the ecstatic emotions of paternity, servitude and friendship. He always assists Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in that way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.297
description: Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu overflooded the entire world by distributing transcendental loving service. No one can understand His character and activities.
text:
> prema-bhakti diyā teṅho bhāsā'la jagate
> tāṅra caritra loke nā pāre bujhite
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhāsā'la]]---overflooded; [[synonyms:j:jagate]]---in the world; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:c:caritra]]---character; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---people; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---able; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand.
translation: Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu overflooded the entire world by distributing transcendental loving service. No one can understand His character and activities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.298
description: Śrīla Advaita Ācārya Prabhu appeared as an incarnation of a devotee. He is in the category of Kṛṣṇa, but He descended to this earth to propagate devotional service.
text:
> advaita-ācārya-gosāñi bhakta-avatāra
> kṛṣṇa avatāriyā kailā bhaktira pracāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Śrī Advaita Prabhu; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---spiritual master; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the incarnation of a devotee; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:avatāriyā]]---descending; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:b:bhaktira]]---of devotional service; [[synonyms:p:pracāra]]---propagation.
translation: Śrīla Advaita Ācārya Prabhu appeared as an incarnation of a devotee. He is in the category of Kṛṣṇa, but He descended to this earth to propagate devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.299
description: His natural emotions were always on the platform of fraternity and servitude, but the Lord sometimes treated Him as His spiritual master.
text:
> sakhya, dāsya,---dui bhāva sahaja tāṅhāra
> kabhu prabhu karena tāṅre guru-vyavahāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakhya]]---fraternity; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]---servitude; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---ecstasies; [[synonyms:s:sahaja]]---natural; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---His; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to Him; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---of spiritual master; [[synonyms:v:vyavahāra]]---treatment.
translation: His natural emotions were always on the platform of fraternity and servitude, but the Lord sometimes treated Him as His spiritual master.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.3
description: I have already given a synopsis of the kaiśora-līlā of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Now let me enumerate His youthful pastimes in chronological order.
text:
> kaiśora-līlāra sūtra karila gaṇana
> yauvana-līlāra sūtra kari anukrama

translation: I have already given a synopsis of the kaiśora-līlā of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Now let me enumerate His youthful pastimes in chronological order.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.30
description: "One should strictly follow the principle of always chanting the holy name, and one should be satisfied with whatever he gets easily. Such devotional behavior solidly maintains one's devotional service.
text:
> sadā nāma la-iba, yathā-lābhete santoṣa
> eita ācāra kare bhakti-dharma-poṣa

translation: "One should strictly follow the principle of always chanting the holy name, and one should be satisfied with whatever he gets easily. Such devotional behavior solidly maintains one's devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.300
description: All the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, have their own emotional humors in which they render service unto Him.
text:
> śrīvāsādi yata mahāprabhura bhakta-gaṇa
> nija nija bhāve karena caitanya-sevana

translation: All the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, have their own emotional humors in which they render service unto Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.301
description: Personal associates like Gadādhara, Svarūpa Dāmodara, Rāmānanda Rāya, and the six Gosvāmīs (headed by Rūpa Gosvāmī) are all situated in their respective transcendental humors. Thus the Lord submits to various positions in various transcendental mellows.
text:
> paṇḍita-gosāñi ādi yāṅra yei rasa
> sei sei rase prabhu hana tāṅra vaśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Gadādhara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---transcendental mellow; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that respective; [[synonyms:r:rase]]---by the mellow; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:h:hana]]---is; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---under control.
translation: Personal associates like Gadādhara, Svarūpa Dāmodara, Rāmānanda Rāya, and the six Gosvāmīs (headed by Rūpa Gosvāmī) are all situated in their respective transcendental humors. Thus the Lord submits to various positions in various transcendental mellows.
purport:
In verses 296 through 301 the emotional devoted service of Śrī Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita Prabhu and others has been fully described. Describing such individual service, the //Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā,// verses 11 through 16, declares that although Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu appeared as a devotee, He is none other than the son of Nanda Mahārāja. Similarly, although Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu appeared as Lord Caitanya's assistant, He is none other than Baladeva, the carrier of the plow. Advaita Ācārya is the incarnation of Sadāśiva from the spiritual world. All the devotees headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura are His marginal energy, whereas the devotees headed by Gadādhara Paṇḍita are manifestations of His internal potency.

Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Advaita Prabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu all belong to the //viṣṇu-tattva// category. Because Lord Caitanya is an ocean of mercy, He is addressed as //mahāprabhu,// whereas Nityānanda and Advaita, being two great personalities who assist Lord Caitanya, are addressed as //prabhu.// Thus there are two //prabhus// and one //mahāprabhu.// Gadādhara Gosvāmī is a representative of a perfect //brāhmaṇa// spiritual master. Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura represents a perfect //brāhmaṇa// devotee. These five are known as the Pañca-tattva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.302
description: In kṛṣṇa-lilā the Lord's complexion is blackish. Holding a flute to His mouth, He enjoys as a cowherd boy. Now the selfsame person has appeared with a fair complexion, sometimes acting as a brāhmaṇa and sometimes accepting the renounced order of life.
text:
> tihaṅ śyāma,---vaṁśī-mukha, gopa-vilāsī
> ihaṅ gaura---kabhu dvija, kabhu ta' sannyāsī
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tihaṅ]]---in //kṛṣṇa-līlā//; [[synonyms:ś:śyāma]]---blackish color; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---a flute in the mouth; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsī]]---an enjoyer as a cowherd boy; [[synonyms:i:ihaṅ]]---now; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]---fair complexion; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:d:dvija]]---//brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---in the renounced order of life.
translation: In kṛṣṇa-lilā the Lord's complexion is blackish. Holding a flute to His mouth, He enjoys as a cowherd boy. Now the selfsame person has appeared with a fair complexion, sometimes acting as a brāhmaṇa and sometimes accepting the renounced order of life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.303
description: Therefore the Lord Himself, accepting the emotional ecstasy of the gopīs, now addresses the son of Nanda Mahārāja, "O master of My life! O My dear husband!"
text:
> ataeva āpane prabhu gopī-bhāva dhari'
> vrajendra-nandane kahe 'prāṇa-nātha' kari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the ecstasy of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandane]]---the son of Nanda Mahārāja; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---addresses; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nātha]]---O Lord of My life (husband); [[synonyms:k:kari']]---accepting.
translation: Therefore the Lord Himself, accepting the emotional ecstasy of the gopīs, now addresses the son of Nanda Mahārāja, "O master of My life! O My dear husband!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.304
description: He is Kṛṣṇa, yet He has accepted the mood of the gopīs. How is it so? It is the inconceivable character of the Lord, which is very difficult to understand.
text:
> sei kṛṣṇa, sei gopī,---parama virodha
> acintya caritra prabhura ati sudurbodha
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---that Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:g:gopī]]---that //gopī//; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:v:virodha]]---very much contradictory; [[synonyms:a:acintya]]---inconceivable; [[synonyms:c:caritra]]---character; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:a:ati]]---very much; [[synonyms:s:sudurbodha]]---difficult to understand.
translation: He is Kṛṣṇa, yet He has accepted the mood of the gopīs. How is it so? It is the inconceivable character of the Lord, which is very difficult to understand.
purport:
Kṛṣṇa's accepting the part of the //gopīs// is certainly contradictory according to any mundane calculations, but the Lord, by His inconceivable character, may act like the //gopīs// and feel separation from Kṛṣṇa, although He is Kṛṣṇa Himself. Such a contradiction can be reconciled only in the Supreme Personality of Godhead because He has energy that is inconceivable (//acintya//), which can make possible that which is impossible to do (//aghaṭa-ghaṭana-patīyasī//). Such contradictions are very difficult to understand unless a devotee strictly follows the Vaiṣṇava philosophy under the direction of the Gosvāmīs. Therefore Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī ends every chapter with this verse:

> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa

"Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate //Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta,// following in their footsteps."

In a song by Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura it is stated:

> rūpa-raghunātha-pade ha-ibe ākuti
> kabe hāma bujhaba se yugala-pīriti

The conjugal love between Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, which is called //yugala-pīriti,// is not understandable by mundane scholars, artists or poets. It is simply to be understood by devotees who strictly follow in the footsteps of the six Gosvāmīs. Sometimes so-called artists and poets try to understand the love affairs of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and they publish cheap books of poetry and pictures on the subject. Unfortunately, however, they do not understand the transcendental affairs of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa even to the smallest degree. They are simply meddling in a matter in which they are not fit even to enter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.305
description: One cannot understand the contradictions in Lord Caitanya's character by putting forward mundane logic and arguments. Consequently one should not maintain doubts in this connection. One should simply try to understand the inconceivable energy of Kṛṣṇa; otherwise one cannot understand how such contradictions are possible.
text:
> ithe tarka kari' keha nā kara saṁśaya
> kṛṣṇera acintya-śakti ei mata haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ithe]]---in this matter; [[synonyms:t:tarka]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making arguments; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---do not; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---make; [[synonyms:s:saṁśaya]]---doubts; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:acintya]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---inconceivable potency; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mata]]---the verdict; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is.
translation: One cannot understand the contradictions in Lord Caitanya's character by putting forward mundane logic and arguments. Consequently one should not maintain doubts in this connection. One should simply try to understand the inconceivable energy of Kṛṣṇa; otherwise one cannot understand how such contradictions are possible.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.306
description: The pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu are inconceivable and wonderful. His ecstasy is wonderful, His qualities are wonderful, and His behavior is wonderful.
text:
> acintya, adbhuta kṛṣṇa-caitanya-vihāra
> citra bhāva, citra guṇa, citra vyavahāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:acintya]]---inconceivable; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vihāra]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:c:citra]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---ecstasy; [[synonyms:c:citra]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---qualities; [[synonyms:c:citra]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:v:vyavahāra]]---behavior.
translation: The pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu are inconceivable and wonderful. His ecstasy is wonderful, His qualities are wonderful, and His behavior is wonderful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.307
description: If one simply adheres to mundane arguments and therefore does not accept this, he will boil in the hell of Kumbhīpāka. For him there is no deliverance.
text:
> tarke ihā nāhi māne yei durācāra
> kumbhīpāke pace, tāra nāhika nistāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tarke]]---by arguments; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---accepts; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:d:durācāra]]---debauchee; [[synonyms:k:kumbhī]]-[[synonyms:p:pāke]]---in the boiling oil of hell; [[synonyms:p:pace]]---boils; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---deliverance.
translation: If one simply adheres to mundane arguments and therefore does not accept this, he will boil in the hell of Kumbhīpāka. For him there is no deliverance.
purport: Kumbhīpāka, a type of hellish condition, is described in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:5:26:13|(5.26.13)]], wherein it is said that a person who cooks living birds and beasts to satisfy his tongue is brought before Yamarāja after death and punished in the Kumbhīpāka hell. There he is put into boiling oil called //kumbhī-pāka,// from which there is no deliverance. Kumbhīpāka is meant for persons who are unnecessarily envious. Those who are envious of the activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are punished in that hellish condition.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.308
description: "Anything transcendental to material nature is called inconceivable, whereas arguments are all mundane. Since mundane arguments cannot touch transcendental subject matters, one should not try to understand transcendental subjects through mundane arguments."
text:
> acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvā
> na tāṁs tarkeṇa yojayet
> prakṛtibhyaḥ paraṁ yac ca
> tad acintyasya lakṣaṇam
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:acintyāḥ]]---inconceivable; [[synonyms:k:khalu]]---certainly; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those; [[synonyms:b:bhāvaḥ]]---subject matters; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:t:tān]]---them; [[synonyms:t:tarkeṇa]]---by argument; [[synonyms:y:yojayet]]---one may understand; [[synonyms:p:prakṛtibhyaḥ]]---to material nature; [[synonyms:p:param]]---transcendental; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---that which; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:a:acintyasya]]---of the inconceivable; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇam]]---a symptom.
translation:
"Anything transcendental to material nature is called inconceivable, whereas arguments are all mundane. Since mundane arguments cannot touch transcendental subject matters, one should not try to understand transcendental subjects through mundane arguments."


This is a quote from the //Mahābhārata// (//Bhīṣma parva// 5.22) and is also quoted in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (2.5.93), by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.309
description: Only a person who has firm faith in the wonderful pastimes of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu can approach His lotus feet.
text:
> adbhuta caitanya-līlāya yāhāra viśvāsa
> sei jana yāya caitanyera pada pāśa

translation: Only a person who has firm faith in the wonderful pastimes of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu can approach His lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.31
description: "One who thinks himself lower than the grass, who is more tolerant than a tree, and who does not expect personal honor yet is always prepared to give all respect to others can very easily always chant the holy name of the Lord."
text:
> tṛṇād api su-nīcena
> taror iva sahiṣṇunā
> amāninā māna-dena
> kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tṛṇāt]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---than downtrodden grass; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:n:nīcena]]---being lower; [[synonyms:t:taroḥ]]---than a tree; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:s:sahiṣṇunā]]---with tolerance; [[synonyms:a:amāninā]]---without being puffed up by false pride; [[synonyms:m:māna]]-[[synonyms:d:dena]]---giving respect to all; [[synonyms:k:kīrtanīyaḥ]]---to be chanted; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---the holy name of the Lord.
translation: "One who thinks himself lower than the grass, who is more tolerant than a tree, and who does not expect personal honor yet is always prepared to give all respect to others can very easily always chant the holy name of the Lord."
purport: The grass is specifically mentioned in this verse because everyone tramples upon it yet the grass never protests. This example indicates that a spiritual master or leader should not be proud of his position; being always humbler than an ordinary common man, he should go on preaching the cult of Caitanya Mahāprabhu by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.310

translation: In this discourse I have explained the essence of the devotional conclusion. Anyone who hears this develops unalloyed devotional service to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.311

> likhita granthera yadi kari anuvāda

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.312
description: We can see in the scripture Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam the conduct of its author, Śrī Vyāsadeva. After speaking the narration, he repeats it again and again.

> dekhi granthe bhāgavate vyāsera ācāra

translation: We can see in the scripture Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam the conduct of its author, Śrī Vyāsadeva. After speaking the narration, he repeats it again and again.
purport: At the end of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// in the Twelfth Canto, the Twelfth Chapter contains forty-three verses in which Śrī Kṛṣṇa-dvaipāyana Vedavyāsa recapitulates //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam's// entire subject matter. Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī wants to follow in the footsteps of Śrī Vyāsadeva by recapitulating the seventeen chapters of //Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta's Ādi-līlā.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.313
description: Therefore I shall enumerate the chapters of the Ādi-līlā. In the First Chapter I offer obeisances to the spiritual master, for this is the beginning of auspicious writing.
text:
> tāte ādi-līlāra kari pariccheda gaṇana
> prathama paricchede kailuṅ 'maṅgalācaraṇa'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.314

> dvitīya paricchede 'caitanya-tattva-nirūpaṇa'
> svayaṁ bhagavān yei vrajendra-nandana

translation: The Second Chapter explains the truth of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Kṛṣṇa, the son of Mahārāja Nanda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.315
description: Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is Kṛṣṇa Himself, has now appeared as the son of mother Śacī. The Third Chapter describes the general cause of His appearance.
text:
> teṅho ta' caitanya-kṛṣṇa---śacīra nandana
> tṛtīya paricchede janmera 'sāmānya' kāraṇa

translation: Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is Kṛṣṇa Himself, has now appeared as the son of mother Śacī. The Third Chapter describes the general cause of His appearance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.316
description: The Third Chapter specifically describes the distribution of love of Godhead. It also describes the religion of the age, which is simply to distribute the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa and propagate the process of loving Him.
text:
> tahiṅ madhye prema-dāna---'viśeṣa' kāraṇa
> yuga-dharma---kṛṣṇa-nāma-prema-pracāraṇa

translation: The Third Chapter specifically describes the distribution of love of Godhead. It also describes the religion of the age, which is simply to distribute the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa and propagate the process of loving Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.317
description: The Fourth Chapter describes the main reason for His appearance, which is to taste the mellows of His own transcendental loving service and His own sweetness.
text:
> caturthe kahiluṅ janmera 'mūla' prayojana
> sva-mādhurya-premānanda-rasa-āsvādana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caturthe]]---in the Fourth Chapter; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have described; [[synonyms:j:janmera]]---of His birth; [[synonyms:m:mūla]]---the real; [[synonyms:p:prayojana]]---necessity; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---His own transcendental sweetness; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---of ecstatic joy from love; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---the mellows; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasting.
translation: The Fourth Chapter describes the main reason for His appearance, which is to taste the mellows of His own transcendental loving service and His own sweetness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.318
description: The Fifth Chapter describes the truth of Lord Nityānanda Prabhu, who is none other than Balarāma, the son of Rohiṇī.
text:
> pañcame 'śrī-nityānanda'-tattva nirūpaṇa
> nityānanda hailā rāma rohiṇī-nandana

translation: The Fifth Chapter describes the truth of Lord Nityānanda Prabhu, who is none other than Balarāma, the son of Rohiṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.319
description: The Sixth Chapter considers the truth of Advaita Ācārya. He is an incarnation of Mahā-Viṣṇu.
text:
> ṣaṣṭha paricchede 'advaita-tattve'ra vicāra
> advaita-ācārya---mahā-viṣṇu-avatāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṣṭha]] [[synonyms:p:paricchede]]---in the Sixth Chapter; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:t:tattvera]]---of the truth; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---consideration; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Prabhu; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnation of Mahā-Viṣṇu.
translation: The Sixth Chapter considers the truth of Advaita Ācārya. He is an incarnation of Mahā-Viṣṇu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.32
description: Raising my hands, I declare, "Everyone please hear me! String this verse on the thread of the holy name and wear it on your neck for continuous remembrance."
text:
> ūrdhva-bāhu kari' kahoṅ, śuna, sarva-loka
> nāma-sūtre gāṅthi' para kaṇṭhe ei śloka
synonyms: [[synonyms:ū:ūrdhva]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhu]]---raising my hands; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing so; [[synonyms:k:kahoṅ]]---I declare; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---all persons; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---of the holy name; [[synonyms:s:sūtre]]---on the thread; [[synonyms:g:gāṅthi]]---stringing; [[synonyms:p:para]]---get it; [[synonyms:k:kaṇṭhe]]---on the neck; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verse.
translation: Raising my hands, I declare, "Everyone please hear me! String this verse on the thread of the holy name and wear it on your neck for continuous remembrance."
purport: When chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra,// in the beginning one may commit many offenses, which are called //nāmābhāsa// and //nāma-aparādha.// In this stage there is no possibility of achieving perfect love of Kṛṣṇa by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// Therefore one must chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// according to the principles of the above verse, //tṛṇād api su-nīcena taror iva sahiṣṇunā.// One should note in this connection that chanting involves the activities of the upper and lower lips as well as the tongue. All three must be engaged in chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// The words "Hare Kṛṣṇa" should be very distinctly pronounced and heard. Sometimes one mechanically produces a hissing sound instead of chanting with the proper pronunciation with the help of the lips and tongue. Chanting is very simple, but one must practice it seriously. Therefore the author of //Caitanya-caritāmṛta,// Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī, advises everyone to keep this verse always strung about his neck.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.320
description: The Seventh Chapter describes the Pañca-tattva-Śrī Caitanya, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita, Gadādhara and Śrīvāsa. They all combined together to distribute love of Godhead everywhere.
text:
> saptama paricchede 'pañca-tattve'ra ākhyāna
> pañca-tattva mili' yaiche kailā prema-dāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saptama]] [[synonyms:p:paricchede]]---in the Seventh Chapter; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:t:tattvera]]---of the five //tattvas// (truths); [[synonyms:ā:ākhyāna]]---the elaboration; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]]---the five //tattvas//; [[synonyms:m:mili']]---combining together; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---in what way; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:d:dāna]]---distribution of love of Godhead.
translation: The Seventh Chapter describes the Pañca-tattva-Śrī Caitanya, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita, Gadādhara and Śrīvāsa. They all combined together to distribute love of Godhead everywhere.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.321
description: The Eighth Chapter gives the reason for describing Lord Caitanya's pastimes. It also describes the greatness of Lord Kṛṣṇa's holy name.
text:
> aṣṭame 'caitanya-līlā-varṇana'-kāraṇa
> eka kṛṣṇa-nāmera mahā-mahimā-kathana

translation: The Eighth Chapter gives the reason for describing Lord Caitanya's pastimes. It also describes the greatness of Lord Kṛṣṇa's holy name.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.322
description: The Ninth Chapter describes the desire tree of devotional service. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself is the gardener who planted it.
text:
> navamete 'bhakti-kalpa-vṛkṣera varṇana'
> śrī-caitanya-mālī kailā vṛkṣa āropaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:navamete]]---in the Ninth Chapter; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:k:kalpa]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛkṣera]]---of the desire tree of devotional service; [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---the description; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:m:mālī]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as the gardener; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]---the tree; [[synonyms:ā:āropaṇa]]---implantation.
translation: The Ninth Chapter describes the desire tree of devotional service. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself is the gardener who planted it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.323
description: The Tenth Chapter describes the branches and subbranches of the main trunk, and the distribution of their fruits.
text:
> daśamete mūla-skandhera 'śākhādi-gaṇana'
> sarva-śākhā-gaṇera yaiche phala-vitaraṇa

translation: The Tenth Chapter describes the branches and subbranches of the main trunk, and the distribution of their fruits.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.324
description: The Eleventh Chapter describes the branch called Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu. The Twelfth Chapter describes the branch called Śrī Advaita Prabhu.
text:
> ekādaśe 'nityānanda-śākhā-vivaraṇa'
> dvādaśe 'advaita-skandha śākhāra varṇana'

translation: The Eleventh Chapter describes the branch called Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu. The Twelfth Chapter describes the branch called Śrī Advaita Prabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.325
description: The Thirteenth Chapter describes the birth of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, which took place with the chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> trayodaśe mahāprabhura 'janma-vivaraṇa'
> kṛṣṇa-nāma-saha yaiche prabhura janama

translation: The Thirteenth Chapter describes the birth of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, which took place with the chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.326
description: The Fourteenth Chapter gives some description of the Lord's childhood pastimes. The Fifteenth briefly describes the Lord's boyhood pastimes.
text:
> caturdaśe 'bālya-līlāra' kichu vivaraṇa
> pañcadaśe 'paugaṇḍa-līlāra' saṅkṣepe kathana

translation: The Fourteenth Chapter gives some description of the Lord's childhood pastimes. The Fifteenth briefly describes the Lord's boyhood pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.327
description: In the Sixteenth Chapter I have indicated the pastimes of the kaiśora age [the age prior to youth]. In the Seventeenth Chapter I have specifically described His youthful pastimes.
text:
> ṣoḍaśa paricchede 'kaiśora-līlā' ra uddeśa

translation: In the Sixteenth Chapter I have indicated the pastimes of the kaiśora age [the age prior to youth]. In the Seventeenth Chapter I have specifically described His youthful pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.328
description: Thus there are seventeen varieties of subjects in the First Canto, which is known as the Ādi-līlā. Twelve of these constitute the preface of this scripture.
text:

translation: Thus there are seventeen varieties of subjects in the First Canto, which is known as the Ādi-līlā. Twelve of these constitute the preface of this scripture.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.329
description: After the chapters of the preface, I have described five transcendental mellows in five chapters. I have described them very briefly rather than expansively.
text:

> saṅkṣepe kahiluṅ ati,---nā kailuṅ vistṛta

translation: After the chapters of the preface, I have described five transcendental mellows in five chapters. I have described them very briefly rather than expansively.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.33
description: One must strictly follow the principles given by Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu in this verse. If one simply follows in the footsteps of Lord Caitanya and the Gosvāmīs, certainly he will achieve the ultimate goal of life, the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
text:

> avaśya pāibe tabe śrī-kṛṣṇa-caraṇa

translation: One must strictly follow the principles given by Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu in this verse. If one simply follows in the footsteps of Lord Caitanya and the Gosvāmīs, certainly he will achieve the ultimate goal of life, the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.330
description: By the order and strength of Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has elaborately described in his Caitanya-maṅgala all that I have not.
text:

> vistāri' varṇilā nityānanda-ājñā-bale
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---Ṭhākura Vṛndāvana dāsa; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:m:maṅgale]]---in his book //Caitanya-maṅgala//; [[synonyms:v:vistāri']]---expanding; [[synonyms:v:varṇilā]]---described; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---of Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---of the order; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---on the strength.
translation: By the order and strength of Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has elaborately described in his Caitanya-maṅgala all that I have not.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.331
description: The pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are wonderful and unlimited. Even personalities like Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and Śeṣa Nāga cannot find their end.
text:
> śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-līlā---adbhuta, ananta
> brahmā-śiva-śeṣa yāṅra nāhi pāya anta
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]---Lord Śeṣa Nāga; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of which; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---get; [[synonyms:a:anta]]---end.
translation: The pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are wonderful and unlimited. Even personalities like Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and Śeṣa Nāga cannot find their end.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.332
description: Anyone who describes or hears any part of this elaborate subject will very soon receive the causeless mercy of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> ye yei aṁśa kahe, śune sei dhanya
> acire milibe tāre śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya

translation: Anyone who describes or hears any part of this elaborate subject will very soon receive the causeless mercy of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.333
description: [Herein the author again describes the Pañca-tattva.] Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita, Gadādhara, Śrīvāsa and all the devotees of Lord Caitanya.
text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.334

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.335-336
description: I wish to place the lotus feet of the Gosvāmīs on my head. Their names are Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara, Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrī Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī and Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī. Placing their lotus feet on my head, always hoping to serve them, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-svarūpa-śrī-rūpa-śrī-sanātana
> śrī-raghunātha-dāsa, āra śrī-jīva-caraṇa
>
> śire dhari vandoṅ, nitya karoṅ tāṅra āśa

translation:
I wish to place the lotus feet of the Gosvāmīs on my head. Their names are Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara, Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrī Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī and Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī. Placing their lotus feet on my head, always hoping to serve them, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.

//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā,  Seventeenth Chapter, describing the pastimes of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu in His youth.//

END OF THE ĀDI-LĪLĀ

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.34

> rātre saṅkīrtana kaila eka saṁvatsara

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu regularly led congregational chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra in the house of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura every night for one full year.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.35
description: This ecstatic chanting was performed with the doors closed so that nonbelievers who came to make fun could not gain entrance.
text:
> kapāṭa diyā kīrtana kare parama āveśe
> pāṣaṇḍī hāsite āise, nā pāya praveśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kapāṭa]]---door; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---closing; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---chanting; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performed; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---very high; [[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in an ecstatic condition; [[synonyms:p:pāṣaṇḍī]]---nonbelievers; [[synonyms:h:hāsite]]---to laugh; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---come; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---get; [[synonyms:p:praveśe]]---entrance.
translation: This ecstatic chanting was performed with the doors closed so that nonbelievers who came to make fun could not gain entrance.
purport: Chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// is open to everyone, but sometimes nonbelievers come to disturb the ceremony of chanting. It is indicated herein that under such circumstances the temple doors should be closed. Only bona fide chanters should be admitted; others should not. But when there is large-scale congregational chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra,// we keep our temples for everyone to join, and by the grace of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu this policy has given good results.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.36
