translation: Śrī Advaita is the principal limb [aṅga] of Nārāyaṇa. Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam speaks of "limb" [aṅga] as "a plenary portion" [aṁśa] of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.23
description: "O Lord of lords, You are the seer of all creation. You are indeed everyone's dearest life. Are You not, therefore, my father, Nārāyaṇa? 'Nārāyaṇa' refers to one whose abode is in the water born from Nara [Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu ], and that Nārāyaṇa is Your plenary portion. All Your plenary portions are transcendental. They are absolute and are not creations of māyā."
text:
> nārāyaṇas tvaṁ na hi sarva-dehinām
> ātmāsy adhīśākhila-loka-sākṣī
> nārāyaṇo 'ṅgaṁ nara-bhū-jalāyanāt
> tac cāpi satyaṁ na tavaiva māyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇaḥ]]---Lord Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:t:tvam]]---You; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:d:dehinām]]---of the embodied beings; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the Supersoul; [[synonyms:a:asi]]---You are; [[synonyms:a:adhīśa]]---O Lord; [[synonyms:a:akhila]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---of all the worlds; [[synonyms:s:sākṣī]]---the witness; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇaḥ]]---known as Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:a:aṅgam]]---plenary portion; [[synonyms:n:nara]]---of Nara; [[synonyms:b:bhū]]---born; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---in the water; [[synonyms:a:ayanāt]]---due to the place of refuge; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:a:api]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:satyam]]---highest truth; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---at all; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---the illusory energy.
translation: "O Lord of lords, You are the seer of all creation. You are indeed everyone's dearest life. Are You not, therefore, my father, Nārāyaṇa? 'Nārāyaṇa' refers to one whose abode is in the water born from Nara [Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu ], and that Nārāyaṇa is Your plenary portion. All Your plenary portions are transcendental. They are absolute and are not creations of māyā."
purport: This text is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.14.14).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.24
description: This verse describes that the limbs and plenary portions of the Lord are all spiritual; they have no relationship with the material energy.
text:
> īśvarera 'aṅga' aṁśa---cid-ānanda-maya
> māyāra sambandha nāhi' ei śloke kaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iśvarera]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---limb; [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---part; [[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---all-spiritual; [[synonyms:m:māyāra]]---of the material energy; [[synonyms:s:sambandha]]---relationship; [[synonyms:n:nāhi']]---there is not; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloke]]---this verse; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---says.
translation: This verse describes that the limbs and plenary portions of the Lord are all spiritual; they have no relationship with the material energy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.25
description: Why has Śrī Advaita been called a limb and not a part? The reason is that "limb" implies greater intimacy.
text:
> 'aṁśa' nā kahiyā, kene kaha tāṅre 'aṅga'
> 'aṁśa' haite 'aṅga,' yāte haya antaraṅga
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---part; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kahiyā]]---not saying; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---you say; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---limb; [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---than a part; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---limb; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---because; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:a:antaraṅga]]---more.
translation: Why has Śrī Advaita been called a limb and not a part? The reason is that "limb" implies greater intimacy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.26
description: Śrī Advaita, who is a reservoir of virtues, is the main limb of Mahā-Viṣṇu. His full name is Advaita, for He is identical in all respects with that Lord.
text:
> mahā-viṣṇura aṁśa---advaita guṇa-dhāma
> īśvare abheda, teñi 'advaita' pūrṇa nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣṇura]]---of Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---part; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---reservoir of all attributes; [[synonyms:ī:īśvare]]---from the Lord; [[synonyms:a:abheda]]---nondifferent; [[synonyms:t:teñi]]---therefore; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---nondifferent; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---full name.
translation: Śrī Advaita, who is a reservoir of virtues, is the main limb of Mahā-Viṣṇu. His full name is Advaita, for He is identical in all respects with that Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.27
description: As He had formerly created all the universes, now He descended to introduce the path of bhakti.
text:
> pūrve yaiche kaila sarva-viśvera sṛjana
> avatari' kaila ebe bhakti-pravartana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---formerly; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:v:viśvera]]---of the universes; [[synonyms:s:sṛjana]]---creation; [[synonyms:a:avatari']]---taking incarnation; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:p:pravartana]]---inauguration of the //bhakti// cult.
translation: As He had formerly created all the universes, now He descended to introduce the path of bhakti.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.28
description: He delivered all living beings by offering the gift of kṛṣṇa-bhakti. He explained the Bhagavad-gītā and Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam in the light of devotional service.
text:
> jīva nistārila kṛṣṇa-bhakti kari' dāna
> gītā-bhāgavate kaila bhaktira vyākhyāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---the living entities; [[synonyms:n:nistārila]]---delivered; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:d:dāna]]---gift; [[synonyms:g:gītā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavate]]---in the //Bhagavad-gītā// and //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:b:bhaktira]] [[synonyms:v:vyākhyāna]]---explanation of devotional service.
translation: He delivered all living beings by offering the gift of kṛṣṇa-bhakti. He explained the Bhagavad-gītā and Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam in the light of devotional service.
purport: Although Śrī Advaita Prabhu is an incarnation of Viṣṇu, for the welfare of the conditioned souls He manifested Himself as a servitor of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and throughout all His activities He showed Himself to be an eternal servitor. Lord Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda also manifested the same principle, although They also belong to the category of Viṣṇu. If Lord Caitanya, Lord Nityānanda and Advaita Prabhu had exhibited Their all-powerful Viṣṇu potencies within this material world, people would have become greater impersonalists, monists and self-worshipers than they had already become under the spell of this age. Therefore the Personality of Godhead and His different incarnations and forms played the parts of devotees to instruct the conditioned souls how to approach the transcendental stage of devotional service. Advaita Ācārya especially intended to teach the conditioned souls about devotional service. The word //ācārya// means "teacher."The special function of such a teacher is to make people Kṛṣṇa conscious. A bona fide teacher following in the footsteps of Advaita Ācārya has no other business than to spread the principles of Kṛṣṇa consciousness all over the world. The real qualification of an //ācārya// is that he presents himself as a servant of the Supreme. Such a bona fide //ācārya// can never support the demoniac activities of atheistic men who present themselves as God. It is the main business of an //ācārya// to defy such imposters posing as God before the innocent public.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.29
description: Since He has no other occupation than to teach devotional service, His name is Advaita Ācārya.
text:
> bhakti-upadeśa vinu tāṅra nāhi kārya
> ataeva nāma haila 'advaita ācārya'
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:u:upadeśa]]---instruction of devotional service; [[synonyms:v:vinu]]---without; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:k:kārya]]---occupation; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:a:advaita]] [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---the supreme teacher (//ācārya//) Advaita Prabhu.
translation: Since He has no other occupation than to teach devotional service, His name is Advaita Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.3
description: In five verses I have described the principle of Lord Nityānanda. Then in the following two verses I describe the glories of Śrī Advaita Ācārya.
text:
> pañca śloke kahila śrī-nityānanda-tattva
> śloka-dvaye kahi advaitācāryera mahattva
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pañca]] [[synonyms:ś:śloke]]---in five verses; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---described; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]]---the truth of Śrī Nityānanda; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]-[[synonyms:d:dvaye]]---in two verses; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I describe; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]]---of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:m:mahattva]]---the glories.
translation: In five verses I have described the principle of Lord Nityānanda. Then in the following two verses I describe the glories of Śrī Advaita Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.30
description: He is the spiritual master of all devotees and is the most revered personality in the world. By a combination of these two names, His name is Advaita Ācārya.
text:
> vaiṣṇavera guru teṅho jagatera ārya
> dui-nāma-milane haila 'advaita-ācārya'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---spiritual master; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:j:jagatera]] [[synonyms:ā:ārya]]---the most respectable personality in the world; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:m:milane]]---by combining the two names; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---the name Advaita Ācārya.
translation: He is the spiritual master of all devotees and is the most revered personality in the world. By a combination of these two names, His name is Advaita Ācārya.
purport: Śrī Advaita Ācārya is the prime spiritual master of the Vaiṣṇavas, and He is worshipable by all Vaiṣṇavas. Vaiṣṇavas must follow in the footsteps of Advaita Ācārya, for by so doing one can actually engage in the devotional service of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.31
description: Since He is a limb or part of the lotus-eyed Supreme Lord, He also bears the name Kamalākṣa.
text:
> kamala-nayanera teṅho, yāte 'aṅga' 'aṁśa'
> 'kamalākṣa' kari dhare nāma avataṁsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kamala]]-[[synonyms:n:nayanera]]---of the lotus-eyed; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---since; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---limb; [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---part; [[synonyms:k:kamala]]-[[synonyms:a:akṣa]]---the lotus-eyed; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---accepting that; [[synonyms:d:dhare]]---takes; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name; [[synonyms:a:avataṁsa]]---partial expansion.
translation: Since He is a limb or part of the lotus-eyed Supreme Lord, He also bears the name Kamalākṣa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.32
description: His associates have the same bodily features as the Lord. They all have four arms and are dressed in yellow garments like Nārāyaṇa.
text:
> īśvara-sārūpya pāya pāriṣada-gaṇa
> catur-bhuja, pīta-vāsa, yaiche nārāyaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:s:sārūpya]]---the same bodily features as the Lord; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:p:pāriṣada]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the associates; [[synonyms:c:catur]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---four hands; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---yellow dress; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just as; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---Lord Nārāyaṇa.
translation: His associates have the same bodily features as the Lord. They all have four arms and are dressed in yellow garments like Nārāyaṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.33
description: Śrī Advaita Ācārya is the principal limb of the Supreme Lord. His truths, names and attributes are all wonderful.
text:
> advaita-ācārya---īśvarera aṁśa-varya
> tāṅra tattva-nāma-guṇa, sakali āścarya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya Prabhu; [[synonyms:ī:īśvarera]]---of the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]-[[synonyms:v:varya]]---principal part; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]---truths; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---names; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---attributes; [[synonyms:s:sakali]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:āścarya]]---wonderful.
translation: Śrī Advaita Ācārya is the principal limb of the Supreme Lord. His truths, names and attributes are all wonderful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.34
description: He worshiped Kṛṣṇa with tulasī leaves and water of the Ganges and called for Him in a loud voice. Thus Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu appeared on earth, accompanied by His personal associates.
text:
> yāṅhāra tulasī-jale, yāṅhāra huṅkāre
> sva-gaṇa sahite caitanyera avatāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāṅhāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]-[[synonyms:j:jale]]---by //tulasī// leaves and Ganges water; [[synonyms:y:yāṅhāra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:h:huṅkāre]]---by the loud voice; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---His personal associates; [[synonyms:s:sahite]]---accompanied by; [[synonyms:c:caitanyera]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:avatāre]]---in the incarnation.
translation: He worshiped Kṛṣṇa with tulasī leaves and water of the Ganges and called for Him in a loud voice. Thus Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu appeared on earth, accompanied by His personal associates.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.35
description: It is through Him [Advaita Ācārya] that Lord Caitanya spread the saṅkīrtana movement and through Him that He delivered the world.
text:
> yāṅra dvārā kaila prabhu kīrtana pracāra
> yāṅra dvārā kaija prabhu jagat nistāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]] [[synonyms:d:dvārā]]---by whom; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]] [[synonyms:p:pracāra]]---spreading of the //saṅkīrtana// movement; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]] [[synonyms:d:dvārā]]---by whom; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jagat]] [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---deliverance of the entire world.
translation: It is through Him [Advaita Ācārya] that Lord Caitanya spread the saṅkīrtana movement and through Him that He delivered the world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.36
description: The glory and attributes of Advaita Ācārya are unlimited. How can the insignificant living entities fathom them?
text:
> ācārya gosāñira guṇa-mahimā apāra
> jīva-kīṭa kothāya pāibeka tāra pāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---the glory of the attributes; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unfathomable; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:k:kīṭa]]---a living being who is just like a worm; [[synonyms:k:kothāya]]---where; [[synonyms:p:pāibeka]]---will get; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:p:pāra]]---the other side.
translation: The glory and attributes of Advaita Ācārya are unlimited. How can the insignificant living entities fathom them?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.37
description: Śrī Advaita Ācārya is a principal limb of Lord Caitanya. Another limb of the Lord is Nityānanda Prabhu.
text:
> ācārya gosāñi caitanyera mukhya aṅga
> āra eka aṅga tāṅra prabhu nityānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:c:caitanyera]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---primary; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---part; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---part; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda.
translation: Śrī Advaita Ācārya is a principal limb of Lord Caitanya. Another limb of the Lord is Nityānanda Prabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.38
description: The devotees headed by Śrīvāsa are His smaller limbs. They are like His hands, face and eyes and His disc and other weapons.
text:
> prabhura upāṅga---śrīvāsādi bhakta-gaṇa
> hasta-mukha-netra-aṅga cakrādy-astra-sama
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:u:upāṅga]]---Lord Caitanya's smaller parts; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by Śrīvāsa; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:h:hasta]]---hands; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---face; [[synonyms:n:netra]]---eyes; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---parts of the body; [[synonyms:c:cakra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the disc; [[synonyms:a:astra]]---weapons; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---like.
translation: The devotees headed by Śrīvāsa are His smaller limbs. They are like His hands, face and eyes and His disc and other weapons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.39
description: With all of them Lord Caitanya performed His pastimes, and with them He spread His mission.
text:
> e-saba la-iyā caitanya-prabhura vihāra
> e-saba la-iyā karena vāñchita pracāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all these; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iyā]]---taking; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vihāra]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of them; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iyā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:v:vāñchita]] [[synonyms:p:pracāra]]---spreading His mission.
translation: With all of them Lord Caitanya performed His pastimes, and with them He spread His mission.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.4
description: Lord Advaita Ācārya is the incarnation of Mahā-Viṣṇu, whose main function is to create the cosmic world through the actions of māyā.
text:
> mahā-viṣṇur jagat-kartā
> māyayā yaḥ sṛjaty adaḥ
> tasyāvatāra evāyam
> advaitācārya īśvaraḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣṇuḥ]]---of the name Mahā-Viṣṇu, the resting place of the efficient cause; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:k:kartā]]---the creator of the cosmic world; [[synonyms:m:māyayā]]---by the illusory energy; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:s:sṛjati]]---creates; [[synonyms:a:adaḥ]]---that universe; [[synonyms:t:tasya]]---His; [[synonyms:a:avatāraḥ]]---incarnation; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācāryaḥ]]---of the name Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ī:īśvaraḥ]]---the Supreme Lord, the resting place of the material cause.
translation: Lord Advaita Ācārya is the incarnation of Mahā-Viṣṇu, whose main function is to create the cosmic world through the actions of māyā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.40
description: Thinking "He [Śrī Advaita Ācārya] is a disciple of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī," Lord Caitanya obeys Him, respecting Him as His spiritual master.
text:
> mādhavendra-purīra iṅho śiṣya, ei jñāne
> ācārya-gosāñire prabhu guru kari' māne
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mādhavendra]]-[[synonyms:p:purīra]]---of Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:i:iṅho]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]---disciple; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---by this consideration; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñire]]---unto Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---spiritual master; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking as; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---obeys Him.
translation: Thinking "He [Śrī Advaita Ācārya] is a disciple of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī," Lord Caitanya obeys Him, respecting Him as His spiritual master.
purport: Śrī Mādhavendra Purī is one of the //ācāryas// in the disciplic succession from Madhvācārya. Mādhavendra Purī had two principal disciples, Īśvara Purī and Śrī Advaita Prabhu. Therefore the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava-sampradāya is a disciplic succession from Madhvācārya. This fact has been accepted in the authorized books known as //Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā// and //Prameya-ratnāvalī,// as well as by Gopāla Guru Gosvāmī. The //Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā// clearly states the disciplic succession of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas as follows: "Lord Brahmā is the direct disciple of Viṣṇu, the Lord of the spiritual sky. His disciple is Nārada, Nārada's disciple is Vyāsa, and Vyāsa's disciples are Śukadeva Gosvāmī and Madhvācārya. Padmanābha Ācārya is the disciple of Madhvācārya, and Narahari is the disciple of Padmanābha Ācārya. Mādhava is the disciple of Narahari, Akṣobhya is the direct disciple of Mādhava, and Jayatīrtha is the disciple of Akṣobhya. Jayatīrtha's disciple is Jñānasindhu, and his disciple is Mahānidhi. Vidyānidhi is the disciple of Mahānidhi, and Rājendra is the disciple of Vidyānidhi. Jayadharma is the disciple of Rājendra. Puruṣottama is the disciple of Jayadharma. Śrīmān Lakṣmīpati is the disciple of Vyāsatīrtha, who is the disciple of Puruṣottama. And Mādhavendra Purī is the disciple of Lakṣmīpati."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.41
description: To maintain the proper etiquette for the principles of religion, Lord Caitanya bows down at the lotus feet of Śrī Advaita Ācārya with reverential prayers and devotion.
text:
> laukika-līlāte dharma-maryādā-rakṣaṇa
> stuti-bhaktye karena tāṅra caraṇa vandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:laukika]]---popular; [[synonyms:l:līlāte]]---in pastimes; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:m:maryādā]]---etiquette of religious principles; [[synonyms:r:rakṣaṇa]]---observing; [[synonyms:s:stuti]]---prayers; [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---by devotion; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---He does; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---lotus feet; [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---worshiping.
translation: To maintain the proper etiquette for the principles of religion, Lord Caitanya bows down at the lotus feet of Śrī Advaita Ācārya with reverential prayers and devotion.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.42
description: Śrī Advaita Ācārya, however, considers Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu His master, and He thinks of Himself as a servant of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> caitanya-gosāñike ācārya kare 'prabhu'-jñāna
> āpanāke karena tāṅra 'dāsa'-abhimāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñike]]---unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---considering His master; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāke]]---unto Himself; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---as a servant; [[synonyms:a:abhimāna]]---conception.
translation: Śrī Advaita Ācārya, however, considers Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu His master, and He thinks of Himself as a servant of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
purport:
The //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// of Rūpa Gosvāmī explains the superexcellent quality of devotional service as follows:

> brahmānando bhaved eṣa
> cet parārdha-guṇī-kṛtaḥ
> naiti bhakti-sukhāmbhodheḥ
> paramāṇu-tulām api

"If multiplied billions of times, the transcendental pleasure derived from impersonal Brahman realization still could not compare to even an atomic portion of the ocean of //bhakti,// or transcendental service." (//Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// 1.1.38) Similarly, the //Bhāvārtha-dīpikā// states:

> tvat-kathāmṛta-pāthodhau
> viharanto mahā-mudaḥ
> kurvanti kṛtinaḥ kecic
> catur-vargaṁ tṛṇopamam

"For those who take pleasure in the transcendental topics of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the four progressive realizations of religiosity, economic development, sense gratification and liberation, all combined together, cannot compare, any more than a straw, to the happiness derived from hearing about the transcendental activities of the Lord." Those who engage in the transcendental service of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, being relieved of all material enjoyment, have no attraction to topics of impersonal monism. In the //Padma Purāṇa,// in connection with the glorification of the month of Kārttika, it is stated that devotees pray:

> varaṁ deva mokṣaṁ na mokṣāvadhiṁ vā
> na cānyaṁ vṛṇe 'haṁ vareśād apīha
> idaṁ te vapur nātha gopāla-bālaṁ
> sadā me manasy āvirāstāṁ kim anyaiḥ
>
> kuverātmajau baddha-mūrtyaiva yadvat
> tvayā mocitau bhakti-bhājau kṛtau ca
> tathā prema-bhaktiṁ svakāṁ me prayaccha
> na mokṣe graho me 'sti dāmodareha

"Dear Lord, always remembering Your childhood pastimes at Vṛndāvana is better for us than aspiring to merge into the impersonal Brahman. During Your childhood pastimes You liberated the two sons of Kuvera and made them great devotees of Your Lordship. Similarly, I wish that instead of giving me liberation You may award me such devotion unto You." In the //Hayaśīrṣīya-śrī-nārāyaṇa-vyūha-stava,// in the chapter called //Nārāyaṇa-stotra,// it is stated:

> na dharmaṁ kāmam arthaṁ vā
> mokṣaṁ vā vara-deśvara
> prārthaye tava pādābje
> dāsyam evābhikāmaye

"My dear Lord, I do not wish to become a man of religion or a master of economic development or sense gratification, nor do I wish for liberation. Although I can have all these from You, the supreme bestower of benedictions, I do not pray for all these. I simply pray that I may always be engaged as a servant of Your lotus feet." Nṛsiṁhadeva offered Prahlāda Mahārāja all kinds of benedictions, but Prahlāda Mahārāja did not accept any of them, for he simply wanted to engage in the service of the lotus feet of the Lord. Similarly, a pure devotee wishes to be blessed like Mahārāja Prahlāda by being thus endowed with devotional service. Devotees also offer their respects to Hanumān, who always remained a servant of Lord Rāma. The great devotee Hanumān prayed:

> bhava-bandha-cchide tasyai
> spṛhayāmi na muktaye
> bhavān prabhur ahaṁ dāsa
> iti yatra vilupyate

"I do not wish to take liberation or to merge in the Brahman effulgence, where the conception of being a servant of the Lord is completely lost." Similarly, in the //Nārada-pañcarātra// it is stated:

> dharmārtha-kāma-mokṣeṣu
> necchā mama kadācana
> tvat-pāda-paṅkajasyādho
> jīvitaṁ dīyatāṁ mama

"I do not want any one of the four desirable stations. I simply want to engage as a servant of the lotus feet of the Lord." King Kulaśekhara, in his very famous book //Mukunda-mālā-stotra,// prays:

> nāhaṁ vande tava caraṇayor dvandvam advandva-hetoḥ
> kumbhī-pākaṁ gurum api hare nārakaṁ nāpanetum
> ramyā-rāmā-mṛdu-tanu-latā-nandane nābhirantuṁ
> bhāve bhāve hṛdaya-bhavane bhāvayeyaṁ bhavantam

"My Lord, I do not worship You to be liberated from this material entanglement, nor do I wish to save myself from the hellish condition of material existence, nor do I ever pray for a beautiful wife to enjoy in a nice garden. I wish only that I may always be in full ecstasy with the pleasure of serving Your Lordship." (M.m.s. 4) In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// also there are many instances in the Third and Fourth cantos in which devotees pray to the Lord simply to be engaged in His service, and nothing else (//Bhāg.// [[books:sb:3:4:15|3.4.15]], [[books:sb:3:25:34|3.25.34]], [[books:sb:3:25:36|3.25.36]], [[books:sb:4:8:22|4.8.22]], [[books:sb:4:9:10|4.9.10]] and [[books:sb:4:20:24|4.20.24]]).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.43
description: He forgets Himself in the joy of that conception and teaches all living entities, "You are servants of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu."
text:
> sei abhimāna-sukhe āpanā pāsare
> 'kṛṣṇa-dāsa' hao---jīve upadeśa kare
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:a:abhimāna]]-[[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in the happiness of that conception; [[synonyms:ā:āpanā]]---Himself; [[synonyms:p:pāsare]]---He forgets; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]] [[synonyms:h:hao]]---You are servants of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:j:jīve]]---the living beings; [[synonyms:u:upadeśa]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---He instructs.
translation: He forgets Himself in the joy of that conception and teaches all living entities, "You are servants of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu."
purport: The transcendental devotional service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is so ecstatic that even the Lord Himself plays the part of a devotee. Forgetting Himself to be the Supreme, He personally teaches the whole world how to render service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.44
description: The conception of servitude to Śrī Kṛṣṇa generates such an ocean of joy in the soul that even the joy of oneness with the Absolute, if multiplied ten million times, could not compare to a drop of it.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-dāsa-abhimāne ye ānanda-sindhu
> koṭī-brahma-sukha nahe tāra eka bindu
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:a:abhimāne]]---under this impression of being a servant of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---that; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sindhu]]---ocean of transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:k:koṭī]]-[[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]---ten million times the transcendental bliss of becoming one with the Absolute; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of the ocean of transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:b:bindu]]---drop.
translation: The conception of servitude to Śrī Kṛṣṇa generates such an ocean of joy in the soul that even the joy of oneness with the Absolute, if multiplied ten million times, could not compare to a drop of it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.45
description: He says, "Nityānanda and I are servants of Lord Caitanya." Nowhere else is there such joy as that which is tasted in this emotion of servitude.
text:
> muñi ye caitanya-dāsa āra nityānanda
> dāsa-bhāva-sama nahe anyatra ānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---that; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---servant of Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---of Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the emotion of being a servant; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal to; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:a:anyatra]]---anywhere else; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---transcendental bliss.
translation: He says, "Nityānanda and I are servants of Lord Caitanya." Nowhere else is there such joy as that which is tasted in this emotion of servitude.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.46
description: The most beloved goddess of fortune resides on the chest of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, yet she too, earnestly praying, begs for the joy of service at His feet.
text:
> parama-preyasī lakṣmī hṛdaye vasati
> teṅho dāsya-sukha māge kariyā minati
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:p:preyasī]]---the most beloved; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---on the chest; [[synonyms:v:vasati]]---residence; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---she; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]---the happiness of being a maidservant; [[synonyms:m:māge]]---begs; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---offering; [[synonyms:m:minati]]---prayers.
translation: The most beloved goddess of fortune resides on the chest of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, yet she too, earnestly praying, begs for the joy of service at His feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.47
description: All the associates of Lord Kṛṣṇa, such as Brahmā, Śiva, Nārada, Śuka and Sanātana, are very much pleased in the sentiment of servitude.
text:
> dāsya-bhāve ānandita pāriṣada-gaṇa
> vidhi, bhava, nārada āra śuka, sanātana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in the conception of being a servant; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very pleased; [[synonyms:p:pāriṣada]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the associates; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:b:bhava]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:n:nārada]]---the great sage Nārada; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]---Śukadeva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---and Sanātana.
translation: All the associates of Lord Kṛṣṇa, such as Brahmā, Śiva, Nārada, Śuka and Sanātana, are very much pleased in the sentiment of servitude.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.48
description: Śrī Nityānanda, the wandering mendicant, is the foremost of all the associates of Lord Caitanya. He became mad in the ecstasy of service to Lord Caitanya.
text:
> nityānanda avadhūta sabāte āgala
> caitanyera dāsya-preme ha-ilā pāgala
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]] [[synonyms:a:avadhūta]]---the mendicant Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:s:sabāte]]---among all; [[synonyms:ā:āgala]]---foremost; [[synonyms:c:caitanyera]] [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]-[[synonyms:p:preme]]---in the emotional ecstatic love of being a servant of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]] [[synonyms:p:pāgala]]---became mad.
translation: Śrī Nityānanda, the wandering mendicant, is the foremost of all the associates of Lord Caitanya. He became mad in the ecstasy of service to Lord Caitanya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.49-50
description: Śrīvāsa, Haridāsa, Rāmadāsa, Gadādhara, Murāri, Mukunda, Candraśekhara and Vakreśvara are all glorious and are all learned scholars, but the sentiment of servitude to Lord Caitanya makes them mad in ecstasy.
text:
> śrīvāsa, haridāsa, rāmadāsa, gadādhara
> murāri, mukunda, candraśekhara, vakreśvara
>
> e-saba paṇḍita-loka parama-mahattva
> caitanyera dāsye sabāya karaye unmatta
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]---Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:r:rāmadāsa]]---Rāmadāsa; [[synonyms:g:gadādhara]]---Gadādhara; [[synonyms:m:murāri]]---Murāri; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:c:candraśekhara]]---Candraśekhara; [[synonyms:v:vakreśvara]]---Vakreśvara; [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of them; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---very learned scholars; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:m:mahattva]]---very much glorified; [[synonyms:c:caitanyera]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dāsye]]---the servitude; [[synonyms:s:sabāya]]---all of them; [[synonyms:k:karayeunmatta]]---makes mad.
translation: Śrīvāsa, Haridāsa, Rāmadāsa, Gadādhara, Murāri, Mukunda, Candraśekhara and Vakreśvara are all glorious and are all learned scholars, but the sentiment of servitude to Lord Caitanya makes them mad in ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.5
description: Because He is nondifferent from Hari, the Supreme Lord, He is called Advaita, and because He propagates the cult of devotion, He is called Ācārya. He is the Lord and the incarnation of the Lord's devotee. Therefore I take shelter of Him.
text:
> advaitaṁ hariṇādvaitād
> ācāryaṁ bhakti-śaṁsanāt
> bhaktāvatāram īśaṁ tam
> advaitācāryam āśraye
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaitam]]---known as Advaita; [[synonyms:h:hariṇā]]---with Lord Hari; [[synonyms:a:advaitāt]]---from being nondifferent; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryam]]---known as Ācārya; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaṁsanāt]]---from the propagation of devotional service to Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāram]]---the incarnation as a devotee; [[synonyms:ī:īśam]]---to the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---to Him; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācāryam]]---to Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āśraye]]---I surrender.
translation: Because He is nondifferent from Hari, the Supreme Lord, He is called Advaita, and because He propagates the cult of devotion, He is called Ācārya. He is the Lord and the incarnation of the Lord's devotee. Therefore I take shelter of Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.51
description: Thus they dance, sing and laugh like madmen, and they instruct everyone, "Just be loving servants of Lord Caitanya."
text:
> ei mata gāya, nāce, kare aṭṭahāsa
> loke upadeśe,---'hao caitanyera dāsa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chant; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:a:aṭṭa]]-[[synonyms:h:hāsa]]---laughing like madmen; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---unto the people in general; [[synonyms:u:upadeśe]]---instruct; [[synonyms:h:hao]]---just become; [[synonyms:c:caitanyera]] [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---servants of Śrī Caitanya.
translation: Thus they dance, sing and laugh like madmen, and they instruct everyone, "Just be loving servants of Lord Caitanya."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.52
description: Śrī Advaita Ācārya thinks, "Lord Caitanya considers Me His spiritual master, yet I feel Myself to be only His servant."
text:
> caitanya-gosāñi more kare guru jñāna
> tathāpiha mora haya dāsa-abhimāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:g:guru]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---consideration as a spiritual master; [[synonyms:t:tathāpiha]]---still; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:a:abhimāna]]---the conception of being His servant.
translation: Śrī Advaita Ācārya thinks, "Lord Caitanya considers Me His spiritual master, yet I feel Myself to be only His servant."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.53
description: Love for Kṛṣṇa has this one unique effect: it imbues superiors, equals and inferiors with the spirit of service to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-premera ei eka apūrva prabhāva
> guru-sama-laghuke karāya dāsya-bhāva
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:premera]]---of love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:a:apūrva]] [[synonyms:p:prabhāva]]---unprecedented influence; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---to those on the level of the spiritual master; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal level; [[synonyms:l:laghuke]]---unto the less important; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---makes; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the conception of being a servant.
translation: Love for Kṛṣṇa has this one unique effect: it imbues superiors, equals and inferiors with the spirit of service to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
purport: There are two kinds of devotional service: the way of //pāñcarātrika// regulative principles and the way of //bhāgavata// transcendental loving service. The love of Godhead of those engaged in //pāñcarātrika// regulative principles depends more or less on the opulent and reverential platform, but the worship of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa is purely on the platform of transcendental love. Even persons who play as the superiors of Kṛṣṇa also take the chance to offer transcendental loving service to the Lord. The service attitude of the devotees who play the parts of superiors of the Lord is very difficult to understand, but can be very plainly understood in connection with the superexcellence of their particular service to Lord Kṛṣṇa. A vivid example is the service of mother Yaśodā to Kṛṣṇa, which is distinct. In the feature of Nārāyaṇa, the Lord can accept services only from His associates who play parts in which they are equal to or less than Him, but in the feature of Lord Kṛṣṇa He accepts service very plainly from His fathers, teachers and other elders who are His superiors, as well as from His equals and His subordinates. This is very wonderful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.54
description: For evidence, please listen to the examples described in the revealed scriptures, which are also corroborated by the realization of great souls.
text:
> ihāra pramāṇa śuna---śāstrera vyākhyāna
> mahad-anubhava yāte sudṛḍha pramāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of this; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---evidence; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:ś:śāstrera]] [[synonyms:v:vyākhyāna]]---the description in the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:a:anubhava]]---the conception of great souls; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---by which; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]]---strong; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---evidence.
translation: For evidence, please listen to the examples described in the revealed scriptures, which are also corroborated by the realization of great souls.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.55-56
description: Although no one is a more respected elder for Kṛṣṇa than Nanda Mahārāja in Vraja, who in transcendental paternal love has no knowledge that his son is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, still ecstatic love makes him, what to speak of others, feel himself to be a servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> anyera kā kathā, vraje nanda mahāśaya
> tāra sama 'guru' kṛṣṇera āra keha naya
>
> śuddha-vātsalye īśvara-jñāna nāhi tāra
> tāhākei preme karāya dāsya-anukāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anyera]]---of others; [[synonyms:k:kā]]---what; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---to speak; [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:n:nanda]] [[synonyms:m:mahāśaya]]---Nanda Mahārāja; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:s:sama]]---like him; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---a superior; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:n:naya]]---not; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:v:vātsalye]]---in transcendental paternal love; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---conception of the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his; [[synonyms:t:tāhākei]]---unto him; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---ecstatic love; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---makes; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]-[[synonyms:a:anukāra]]---the conception of being a servant.
translation: Although no one is a more respected elder for Kṛṣṇa than Nanda Mahārāja in Vraja, who in transcendental paternal love has no knowledge that his son is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, still ecstatic love makes him, what to speak of others, feel himself to be a servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.57
description: He too prays for attachment and devotion to the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, as the words from his own mouth give evidence.
text:
> teṅho rati-mati māge kṛṣṇera caraṇe
> tāhāra śrī-mukha-vāṇī tāhāte pramāṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he also; [[synonyms:r:rati]]-[[synonyms:m:mati]]---affection and attraction; [[synonyms:m:māge]]---begs; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---unto the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---his; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]-[[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---words from his mouth; [[synonyms:t:tāhāte]]---in that; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇe]]---evidence.
translation: He too prays for attachment and devotion to the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, as the words from his own mouth give evidence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.58-59
description: "My dear Uddhava, please hear me. In truth Kṛṣṇa is my son, but even if you think that He is God, I would still bear toward Him my own feelings for my son. May my mind be attached to your Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> śuna uddhava, satya, kṛṣṇa---āmāra tanaya
> teṅho īśvara---hena yadi tomāra mane laya
> tathāpi tāṅhāte rahu mora mano-vṛtti
> tomāra īśvara-kṛṣṇe hauka mora mati
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuna]] [[synonyms:u:uddhava]]---my dear Uddhava, please hear me; [[synonyms:s:satya]]---the truth; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:t:tanaya]]---my son; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:hena]]---thus; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---the mind; [[synonyms:l:laya]]---takes; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāte]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:r:rahu]]---let there be; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vrtti]]---mental functions; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---to Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:h:hauka]]---let there be; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:m:mati]]---attention.
translation: "My dear Uddhava, please hear me. In truth Kṛṣṇa is my son, but even if you think that He is God, I would still bear toward Him my own feelings for my son. May my mind be attached to your Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.6
description: Śrī Advaita Ācārya is indeed directly the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. His glory is beyond the conception of ordinary living beings.
text:
> advaita-ācārya gosāñi sākṣāt īśvara
> yāṅhāra mahimā nahe jīvera gocara
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---of the name Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]] [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---directly the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:y:yāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---whose glories; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jīveragocara]]---within the reach of the understanding of ordinary living beings.
translation: Śrī Advaita Ācārya is indeed directly the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. His glory is beyond the conception of ordinary living beings.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.60
description: "May our minds be attached to the lotus feet of your Lord Kṛṣṇa, may our tongues chant His holy names, and may our bodies lie prostrate before Him.
text:
> manaso vṛttayo naḥ syuḥ
> kṛṣṇa-pādāmbujāśrayāḥ
> vāco 'bhidhāyinīr nāmnāṁ
> kāyas tat-prahvaṇādiṣu
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:manasaḥ]]---of the mind; [[synonyms:v:vṛttayaḥ]]---activities (thinking, feeling and willing); [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---of us; [[synonyms:s:syuḥ]]---let there be; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:a:ambuja]]---the lotus feet; [[synonyms:ā:āśrayāḥ]]---those sheltered by; [[synonyms:v:vācaḥ]]---the words; [[synonyms:a:abhidhāyinīḥ]]---speaking; [[synonyms:n:nāmnām]]---of His holy names; [[synonyms:k:kāyaḥ]]---the body; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---to Him; [[synonyms:p:prahvaṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādiṣu]]---bowing down to Him, etc.
translation: "May our minds be attached to the lotus feet of your Lord Kṛṣṇa, may our tongues chant His holy names, and may our bodies lie prostrate before Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.61
description: "Wherever we wander in the material universe under the influence of karma by the will of the Lord, may our auspicious activities cause our attraction to Lord Kṛṣṇa to increase."
text:
> karmabhir bhrāmyamāṇānāṁ
> yatra kvāpīśvarecchayā
> maṅgalācaritair dānai
> ratir naḥ kṛṣṇa īśvare
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:karmabhiḥ]]---by the activities; [[synonyms:b:bhrāmyamāṇānām]]---of those wandering within the material universe; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---wherever; [[synonyms:k:kva]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---anywhere; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:i:icchayā]]---by the supreme will of the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:m:maṅgala]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācaritaiḥ]]---by auspicious activities; [[synonyms:d:dānaiḥ]]---like charity and philanthropy; [[synonyms:r:ratiḥ]]---the attraction; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---our; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---in Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ī:īśvare]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: "Wherever we wander in the material universe under the influence of karma by the will of the Lord, may our auspicious activities cause our attraction to Lord Kṛṣṇa to increase."
purport: These verses from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.47.66-67) were spoken by the denizens of Vṛndāvana, headed by Mahārāja Nanda and his associates, to Uddhava, who had come from Mathurā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.62
description: Lord Kṛṣṇa's friends in Vṛndāvana, headed by Śrīdāmā, have pure fraternal affection for Lord Kṛṣṇa and have no idea of His opulences.
text:
> śrīdāmādi vraje yata sakhāra nicaya
> aiśvarya-jñāna-hīna, kevala-sakhya-maya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrīdāmā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---Kṛṣṇa's friends, headed by Śrīdāmā; [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:s:sakhāra]]---of the friends; [[synonyms:n:nicaya]]---the group; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---of opulence; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:h:hīna]]---without; [[synonyms:k:kevala]]---purely; [[synonyms:s:sakhya]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---fraternal affection.
translation: Lord Kṛṣṇa's friends in Vṛndāvana, headed by Śrīdāmā, have pure fraternal affection for Lord Kṛṣṇa and have no idea of His opulences.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.63
description: Although they fight with Him and climb upon His shoulders, they worship His lotus feet in a spirit of servitude.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-saṅge yuddha kare, skandhe ārohaṇa
> tārā dāsya-bhāve kare caraṇa-sevana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yuddha]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---fight; [[synonyms:s:skandhe]]---on His shoulders; [[synonyms:ā:ārohaṇa]]---getting up; [[synonyms:t:tārā]]---they; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in the conception of being Lord Kṛṣṇa's servants; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sevana]]---worship the lotus feet.
translation: Although they fight with Him and climb upon His shoulders, they worship His lotus feet in a spirit of servitude.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.64
description: "Some of the friends of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, massaged His feet, and others whose sinful reactions had been destroyed fanned Him with hand-held fans."
text:
> pāda-saṁvāhanaṁ cakruḥ
> kecit tasya mahātmanaḥ
> apare hata-pāpmāno
> vyajanaiḥ samavījayan
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:s:saṁvāhanam]]---massaging the feet; [[synonyms:c:cakruḥ]]---performed; [[synonyms:k:kecit]]---some of them; [[synonyms:t:tasya]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmanaḥ]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:apare]]---others; [[synonyms:h:hata]]---destroyed; [[synonyms:p:pāpmānaḥ]]---whose resultant actions of sinful life; [[synonyms:v:vyajanaiḥ]]---with hand-held fans; [[synonyms:s:samavījayan]]---fanned very pleasingly.
translation: "Some of the friends of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, massaged His feet, and others whose sinful reactions had been destroyed fanned Him with hand-held fans."
purport: This verse, quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.15.17), describes how Lord Kṛṣṇa and Lord Balarāma were playing with the cowherd boys after killing Dhenukāsura in Tālavana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.65-66
description: Even the beloved girlfriends of Lord Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana, the gopīs, the dust of whose feet was desired by Śrī Uddhava and beyond whom no one is more dear to Kṛṣṇa, regard themselves as Kṛṣṇa's maidservants.
text:
> kṛṣṇera preyasī vraje yata gopī-gaṇa
> yāṅra pada-dhūli kare uddhava prārthana
>
> yāṅ-sabāra upare kṛṣṇera priya nāhi āna
> tāṅhārā āpanāke kare dāsī-abhimāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:preyasī]]---the beloved girls; [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:d:dhūli]]---the dust of the feet; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:u:uddhava]]---of the name Uddhava; [[synonyms:p:prārthana]]---desiring; [[synonyms:y:yāṅ]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---all of them; [[synonyms:u:upare]]---beyond; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:priya]]---dear; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:ā:āna]]---anyone else; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhārā]]---all of them; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāke]]---to themselves; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:d:dāsī]]-[[synonyms:a:abhimāna]]---the conception of being maidservants.
translation: Even the beloved girlfriends of Lord Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana, the gopīs, the dust of whose feet was desired by Śrī Uddhava and beyond whom no one is more dear to Kṛṣṇa, regard themselves as Kṛṣṇa's maidservants.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.67
description: "O Lord, remover of the afflictions of the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana! O hero of all women! O Lord who destroy the pride of Your devotees by Your sweet, gentle smile! O friend! We are Your maidservants. Please fulfill our desires and show us Your attractive lotus face."
text:
> vraja-janārti-han vīra yoṣitāṁ
> nija-jana-smaya-dhvaṁsana-smita
> bhaja sakhe bhavat-kiṅkarīḥ sma no
> jala-ruhānanaṁ cāru darśaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārti]]-[[synonyms:h:han]]---O one who diminishes all the painful conditions of the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:v:vīra]]---O hero; [[synonyms:y:yoṣitām]]---of women; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---personal; [[synonyms:j:jana]]---of the associates; [[synonyms:s:smaya]]---the pride; [[synonyms:d:dhvaṁsana]]---destroying; [[synonyms:s:smita]]---whose smile; [[synonyms:b:bhaja]]---worship; [[synonyms:s:sakhe]]---O dear friend; [[synonyms:b:bhavat]]-[[synonyms:k:kiṅkarīḥ]]---Your servants; [[synonyms:s:sma]]---certainly; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---unto us; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:r:ruha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanam]]---a face exactly like a lotus flower; [[synonyms:c:cāru]]---attractive; [[synonyms:d:darśaya]]---please show.
translation: "O Lord, remover of the afflictions of the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana! O hero of all women! O Lord who destroy the pride of Your devotees by Your sweet, gentle smile! O friend! We are Your maidservants. Please fulfill our desires and show us Your attractive lotus face."
purport: This verse in connection with the //rāsa// dance of Kṛṣṇa with the //gopīs// is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.31.6). When Kṛṣṇa disappeared from His companions in the course of dancing, the //gopīs// sang like this in separation from Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.68
description: "O Uddhava! It is indeed regrettable that Kṛṣṇa resides in Mathurā. Does He remember His father's household affairs and His friends, the cowherd boys? O great soul! Does He ever talk about us, His maidservants? When will He lay on our heads His aguru-scented hand?"
text:
> api bata madhu-puryām ārya-putro 'dhunāste
> smarati sa pitṛ-gehān saumya bandhūṁś ca gopān
> kvacid api sa kathāṁ naḥ kiṅkariṇāṁ gṛṇīte
> bhujam aguru-sugandhaṁ mūrdhny adhāsyat kadā nu
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:api]]---certainly; [[synonyms:b:bata]]---regrettable; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:p:puryām]]---in the city of Mathurā; [[synonyms:ā:ārya]]-[[synonyms:p:putraḥ]]---the son of Nanda Mahārāja; [[synonyms:a:adhunā]]---now; [[synonyms:ā:āste]]---resides; [[synonyms:s:smarati]]---remembers; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:p:pitṛ]]-[[synonyms:g:gehān]]---the household affairs of His father; [[synonyms:s:saumya]]---O great soul (Uddhava); [[synonyms:b:bandhūn]]---His many friends; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:g:gopān]]---the cowherd boys; [[synonyms:k:kvacit]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:a:api]]---or; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:k:kathām]]---talks; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---of us; [[synonyms:k:kiṅkarīṇām]]---of the maidservants; [[synonyms:g:gṛṇīte]]---relates; [[synonyms:b:bhujam]]---hand; [[synonyms:a:aguru]]-[[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:g:gandham]]---having the fragrance of //aguru//; [[synonyms:m:mūrdhni]]---on the head; [[synonyms:a:adhāsyat]]---will keep; [[synonyms:k:kadā]]---when; [[synonyms:n:nu]]---may be.
translation: "O Uddhava! It is indeed regrettable that Kṛṣṇa resides in Mathurā. Does He remember His father's household affairs and His friends, the cowherd boys? O great soul! Does He ever talk about us, His maidservants? When will He lay on our heads His aguru-scented hand?"
purport: This verse appears in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.47.21) in the section known as the //Bhramara-gītā.// When Uddhava came to Vṛndāvana, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, in complete separation from Kṛṣṇa, sang like this.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.69-70
description: What to speak of the other gopīs, even Śrī Rādhikā, who in every respect is the most elevated of them all and who has bound Śrī Kṛṣṇa forever by Her loving attributes, serves His feet as His maidservant.
text:
> tāṅ-sabāra kathā rahu,---śrīmatī rādhikā
> sabā haite sakalāṁśe parama-adhikā
>
> teṅho yāṅra dāsī haiñā sevena caraṇa
> yāṅra prema-guṇe kṛṣṇa baddha anukṣaṇa

translation: What to speak of the other gopīs, even Śrī Rādhikā, who in every respect is the most elevated of them all and who has bound Śrī Kṛṣṇa forever by Her loving attributes, serves His feet as His maidservant.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.7
description: Mahā-Viṣṇu performs all the functions for the creation of the universes. Śrī Advaita Ācārya is His direct incarnation.
text:
> mahā-viṣṇu sṛṣṭi karena jagad-ādi kārya
> tāṅra avatāra sākṣāt advaita ācārya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---the original Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]---creation; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the material world; [[synonyms:k:kārya]]---the occupation; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnation; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:a:advaitaācārya]]---Prabhu Advaita Ācārya.
translation: Mahā-Viṣṇu performs all the functions for the creation of the universes. Śrī Advaita Ācārya is His direct incarnation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.71
description: "O My Lord, O My husband, O most dearly beloved! O mighty-armed Lord! Where are You? Where are You? O My friend, reveal Yourself to Your maidservant, who is very much aggrieved by Your absence."
text:
> hā nātha ramaṇa preṣṭha
> kvāsi kvāsi mahā-bhuja
> dāsyās te kṛpaṇāyā me
> sakhe darśaya sannidhim
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hā]]---O; [[synonyms:n:nātha]]---My Lord; [[synonyms:r:ramaṇa]]---O My husband; [[synonyms:p:preṣṭha]]---O My most dear one; [[synonyms:k:kva]] [[synonyms:a:asi]] [[synonyms:k:kva]] [[synonyms:a:asi]]---where are You, where are You; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---O mighty-armed one; [[synonyms:d:dāsyāḥ]]---of the maidservant; [[synonyms:t:te]]---You; [[synonyms:k:kṛpaṇāyāḥ]]---very much aggrieved by Your absence; [[synonyms:m:me]]---to Me; [[synonyms:s:sakhe]]---O My friend; [[synonyms:d:darśaya]]---show; [[synonyms:s:sannidhim]]---nearness to You.
translation: "O My Lord, O My husband, O most dearly beloved! O mighty-armed Lord! Where are You? Where are You? O My friend, reveal Yourself to Your maidservant, who is very much aggrieved by Your absence."
purport: This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.30.39). When the //rāsa// dance was going on in full swing, Kṛṣṇa left all the //gopīs// and took only Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī with Him. At that time all the //gopīs// lamented, and Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, being proud of Her position, requested Kṛṣṇa to carry Her wherever He liked. Then Kṛṣṇa immediately disappeared from the scene, and Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī began to lament.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.72
description: In Dvārakā-dhāma, all the queens, headed by Rukmiṇī, also consider themselves maidservants of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> dvārakāte rukmiṇy-ādi yateka mahiṣī
> tāṅhārāo āpanāke māne kṛṣṇa-dāsī
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dvārakāte]]---in Dvārakā-dhāma; [[synonyms:r:rukmiṇī]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by Rukmiṇī; [[synonyms:y:yateka]]---all of them; [[synonyms:m:mahiṣī]]---the queens; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhārāo]]---all of them also; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāke]]---themselves; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---consider; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsī]]---maidservants of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: In Dvārakā-dhāma, all the queens, headed by Rukmiṇī, also consider themselves maidservants of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.73
description: "When Jarāsandha and other kings, bows and arrows upraised, stood ready to deliver me in charity to Śiśupāla, He forcibly took me from their midst, as a lion takes its share of goats and sheep. The dust of His lotus feet is therefore the crown of unconquerable soldiers. May those lotus feet, which are the shelter of the goddess of fortune, be the object of my worship."
text:
> caidyāya mārpayitum udyata-kārmukeṣu
> rājasv ajeya-bhaṭa-śekharitāṅghri-reṇuḥ
> ninye mṛgendra iva bhāgam ajāvi-yūthāt
> tac chrī-niketa-caraṇo 'stu mamārcanāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caidyāya]]---unto Śiśupāla; [[synonyms:m:mā]]---me; [[synonyms:a:arpayitum]]---to deliver or to give in charity; [[synonyms:u:udyata]]---upraised; [[synonyms:k:kārmukeṣu]]---whose bows and arrows; [[synonyms:r:rājasu]]---among the kings headed by Jarāsandha; [[synonyms:a:ajeya]]---unconquerable; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭa]]---of the soldiers; [[synonyms:ś:śekharita]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅghri]]-[[synonyms:r:reṇuḥ]]---the dust of whose lotus feet is the crown; [[synonyms:n:ninye]]---forcibly took; [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]-[[synonyms:i:indraḥ]]---the lion; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:b:bhāgam]]---the share; [[synonyms:a:aja]]---of the goats; [[synonyms:a:avi]]---and sheep; [[synonyms:y:yūthāt]]---from the midst; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:n:niketana]]---of the shelter of the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:c:caraṇaḥ]]---the lotus feet; [[synonyms:a:astu]]---let there be; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---my; [[synonyms:a:arcanāya]]---for worshiping.
translation: "When Jarāsandha and other kings, bows and arrows upraised, stood ready to deliver me in charity to Śiśupāla, He forcibly took me from their midst, as a lion takes its share of goats and sheep. The dust of His lotus feet is therefore the crown of unconquerable soldiers. May those lotus feet, which are the shelter of the goddess of fortune, be the object of my worship."
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.83.8) was spoken by Queen Rukmiṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.74
description: "Knowing me to be performing austerities with the desire to touch His feet, He came with His friend Arjuna and accepted my hand. Yet I am but a maidservant engaged in sweeping the floor of the house of Śrī Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> tapaś carantīm ājñāya
> sva-pāda-sparśanāśayā
> sakhyopetyāgrahīt pāṇiṁ
> sāhaṁ tad-gṛha-mārjanī
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tapaḥ]]---austerity; [[synonyms:c:carantīm]]---performing; [[synonyms:ā:ājñāya]]---knowing; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:s:sparśana]]---of touching His feet; [[synonyms:ā:āśayā]]---with the desire; [[synonyms:s:sakhyā]]---with His friend Arjuna; [[synonyms:u:upetya]]---coming; [[synonyms:a:agrahīt]]---accepted; [[synonyms:p:pāṇim]]---my hand; [[synonyms:s:sā]]---that woman; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---His; [[synonyms:g:gṛha]]-[[synonyms:m:mārjanī]]---keeper of the home.
translation: "Knowing me to be performing austerities with the desire to touch His feet, He came with His friend Arjuna and accepted my hand. Yet I am but a maidservant engaged in sweeping the floor of the house of Śrī Kṛṣṇa."
purport: Like the previous verse, this verse appears in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.83.11) in connection with the meeting of the family ladies of the Kuru and Yadu dynasties at Samanta-pañcaka. At the time of that meeting, the queen of Kṛṣṇa named Kālindī spoke to Draupadī in this way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.75
description: "Through austerity and through renunciation of all attachments, we have become maidservants in the home of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is satisfied in Himself."
text:
> ātmārāmasya tasyemā
> vayaṁ vai gṛha-dāsikāḥ
> sarva-saṅga-nivṛttyāddhā
> tapasā ca babhūvima
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmasya]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is satisfied in Himself; [[synonyms:t:tasya]]---His; [[synonyms:i:imāḥ]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vayam]]---we; [[synonyms:v:vai]]---certainly; [[synonyms:g:gṛha]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsikāḥ]]---the maidservants of the home; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---association; [[synonyms:n:nivṛttyā]]---fully bereft of; [[synonyms:a:addhā]]---directly; [[synonyms:t:tapasā]]---on account of austerity; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:b:babhūvima]]---we have become.
translation: "Through austerity and through renunciation of all attachments, we have become maidservants in the home of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is satisfied in Himself."
purport: During the same incident, this verse, quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.83.39), was spoken to Draupadī by a queen of Kṛṣṇa's named Lakṣmaṇā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.76
description: What to speak of others, even Lord Baladeva, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is full of emotions like pure friendship and paternal love.
text:
> ānera ki kathā, baladeva mahāśaya
> yāṅra bhāva---śuddha-sakhya-vātsalyādi-maya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ānera]]---of others; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---what to speak; [[synonyms:b:baladeva]]---Lord Baladeva; [[synonyms:m:mahāśaya]]---the Supreme Personality; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---emotion; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:s:sakhya]]---pure friendship; [[synonyms:v:vātsalya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---with a touch of paternal love.
translation: What to speak of others, even Lord Baladeva, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is full of emotions like pure friendship and paternal love.
purport: Although Lord Baladeva appeared before the birth of Lord Kṛṣṇa and is therefore Kṛṣṇa's worshipable elder brother, He used to act as Kṛṣṇa's eternal servitor. In the spiritual sky all the Vaikuṇṭha planets are predominated by the quadruple expansions of Kṛṣṇa known as the //catur-vyūha.// They are direct expansions from Baladeva. It is the singularity of the Supreme Lord that everyone in the spiritual sky thinks himself a servitor of the Lord. According to social convention one may be superior to Kṛṣṇa, but factually everyone engages in His service. Therefore in the spiritual sky or the material sky, in all the different planets, no one is able to supersede Lord Kṛṣṇa or demand service from Him. On the contrary, everyone engages in the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa. As such, the more a person engages in the service of the Lord, the more he is important; and, conversely, the more one is bereft of the transcendental service of Kṛṣṇa, the more he invites the bad fortune of material contamination. In the material world, although materialists want to become one with God or compete with God, everyone directly or indirectly engages in the service of the Lord. The more one is forgetful of the service of Kṛṣṇa, the more he is considered to be dying. Therefore, when one develops pure Kṛṣṇa consciousness, he immediately develops his eternal servitorship to Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.77
description: He also considers Himself a servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Indeed, who is there who does not have this conception of being a servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa?
text:
> teṅho āpanāke karena dāsa-bhāvanā
> kṛṣṇa-dāsa-bhāva vinu āche kona janā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He also; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāke]]---Himself; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvanā]]---considering a servant; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the conception of being a servant of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vinu]]---without; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---is; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---what; [[synonyms:j:janā]]---person.
translation: He also considers Himself a servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Indeed, who is there who does not have this conception of being a servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.78
description: He who is Śeṣa, Saṅkarṣaṇa, with His thousands of mouths, serves Śrī Kṛṣṇa by assuming ten forms.
text:
> sahasra-vadane yeṅho śeṣa-saṅkarṣaṇa
> daśa deha dhari' kare kṛṣṇera sevana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]-[[synonyms:v:vadane]]---with thousands of mouths; [[synonyms:y:yeṅho]]---one who; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkarṣaṇa]]---Lord Śeṣa, the incarnation of Saṅkarṣaṇa; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]---ten; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---bodies; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---service.
translation: He who is Śeṣa, Saṅkarṣaṇa, with His thousands of mouths, serves Śrī Kṛṣṇa by assuming ten forms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.79
description: Rudra, who is an expansion of Sadāśiva and who appears in unlimited universes, is also a guṇāvatāra [qualitative incarnation] and is the ornament of all the demigods in the endless universes.
text:
> ananta brahmāṇḍe rudra---sadāśivera aṁśa
> guṇāvatāra teṅho, sarva-deva-avataṁsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍe]]---in the universes; [[synonyms:r:rudra]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:s:sadāśivera]] [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---part and parcel of Sadāśiva; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---an incarnation of a quality; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he also; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:a:avataṁsa]]---the ornament of all the demigods.
translation: Rudra, who is an expansion of Sadāśiva and who appears in unlimited universes, is also a guṇāvatāra [qualitative incarnation] and is the ornament of all the demigods in the endless universes.
purport: There are eleven expansions of Rudra, or Lord Śiva. They are as follows: Ajaikapāt, Ahibradhna, Virūpākṣa, Raivata, Hara, Bahurūpa, Devaśreṣṭha Tryambaka, Sāvitra, Jayanta, Pināki and Aparājita. Besides these expansions there are eight forms of Rudra called earth, water, fire, air, sky, the sun, the moon and //soma-yājī.// Generally all these Rudras have five faces, three eyes and ten arms. Sometimes it is found that Rudra is compared to Brahmā and considered a living entity. But when Rudra is explained to be a partial expansion of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he is compared to Śeṣa. Lord Śiva is therefore simultaneously an expansion of Lord Viṣṇu and, in his capacity for annihilating the creation, one of the living entities. As an expansion of Lord Viṣṇu he is called Hara, and he is transcendental to the material qualities, but when he is in touch with //tamo-guṇa// he appears contaminated by the material modes of nature. This is explained in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// and the //Brahma-saṁhitā.// In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// Tenth Canto, it is stated that Lord Rudra is always associated with the material nature when she is in the neutral, unmanifested stage, but when the modes of material nature are agitated he associates with material nature from a distance. In the //Brahma-saṁhitā// the relationship between Viṣṇu and Lord Śiva is compared to that of milk and yogurt. Milk is converted into yogurt by certain additives, but although milk and yogurt have the same ingredients, they have different functions. Similarly, Lord Śiva is an expansion of Lord Viṣṇu, yet because of his taking part in the annihilation of the cosmic manifestation, he is considered to be changed, like milk converted into yogurt. In the //Purāṇas// it is found that Durgā appears sometimes from the heads of Brahmā and sometimes from the heads of Viṣṇu. The annihilator, Rudra, is born from Saṅkarṣaṇa and the ultimate fire to burn the whole creation. In the //Vāyu Purāṇa// there is a description of Sadāśiva in one of the Vaikuṇṭha planets. That Sadāśiva is a direct expansion of Lord Kṛṣṇa's form for pastimes. It is said that Sadāśiva (Lord Śambhu) is an expansion from the Sadāśiva in the Vaikuṇṭha planets (Lord Viṣṇu) and that his consort, Mahāmāyā, is an expansion of Ramādevī, or Lakṣmī. Mahāmāyā is the origin or birthplace of material nature.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.8
description: That puruṣa creates and maintains with His external energy. He creates innumerable universes in His pastimes.
text:
> ye puruṣa sṛṣṭi-sthiti karena māyāya
> ananta brahmāṇḍa sṛṣṭi karena līlāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]---that personality who; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]-[[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---creation and maintenance; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---performs; [[synonyms:m:māyāya]]---through the external energy; [[synonyms:a:ananta]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]---unlimited universes; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]---creation; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:l:līlāya]]---by pastimes.
translation: That puruṣa creates and maintains with His external energy. He creates innumerable universes in His pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.80
description: He also desires only to be a servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Śrī Sadāśiva always says, "I am a servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> teṅho karena kṛṣṇera dāsya-pratyāśa
> nirantara kahe śiva, 'muñi kṛṣṇa-dāsa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]-[[synonyms:p:pratyāśa]]---expectation of being a servant; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---constantly; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---a servant of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: He also desires only to be a servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Śrī Sadāśiva always says, "I am a servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.81
description: Intoxicated by ecstatic love for Lord Kṛṣṇa, he becomes overwhelmed and incessantly dances without clothing and sings about Lord Kṛṣṇa's qualities and pastimes.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-preme unmatta, vihvala digambara
> kṛṣṇa-guṇa-līlā gāya, nāce nirantara
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:u:unmatta]]---almost mad; [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:d:digambara]]---without any dress; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---attributes; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chants; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---constantly.
translation: Intoxicated by ecstatic love for Lord Kṛṣṇa, he becomes overwhelmed and incessantly dances without clothing and sings about Lord Kṛṣṇa's qualities and pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.82
description: All the emotions, whether those of father, mother, teacher or friend, are full of sentiments of servitude. That is the nature of love of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> pitā-mātā-guru-sakhā-bhāva kene naya
> kṛṣṇa-premera svabhāve dāsya-bhāva se karaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pitā]]---father; [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---mother; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---superior teacher; [[synonyms:s:sakhā]]---friend; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the emotion; [[synonyms:k:kene]] [[synonyms:n:naya]]---let it be; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:premera]]---of love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:svabhāve]]---in a natural inclination; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]] [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the emotion of becoming a servant; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:k:karaya]]---does.
translation: All the emotions, whether those of father, mother, teacher or friend, are full of sentiments of servitude. That is the nature of love of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.83
description: Lord Kṛṣṇa, the one master and the Lord of the universe, is worthy of being served by everyone. Indeed, everyone is but a servant of His servants.
text:
> eka kṛṣṇa---sarva-sevya, jagat-īśvara
> āra yata saba,---tāṅra sevakānucara

translation: Lord Kṛṣṇa, the one master and the Lord of the universe, is worthy of being served by everyone. Indeed, everyone is but a servant of His servants.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.84
description: That same Lord Kṛṣṇa has descended as Lord Caitanya, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Everyone, therefore, is His servant.
text:
> sei kṛṣṇa avatīrṇa---caitanya-īśvara
> ataeva āra saba,---tāṅhāra kiṅkara
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:avatīrṇa]]---descended; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---Lord Caitanya, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---others; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:k:kiṅkara]]---His servants.
translation: That same Lord Kṛṣṇa has descended as Lord Caitanya, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Everyone, therefore, is His servant.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.85
description: Some accept Him whereas others do not, yet everyone is His servant. One who does not accept Him, however, will be ruined by his sinful activities.
text:
> keha māne, keha nā māne, saba tāṅra dāsa
> ye nā māne, tāra haya sei pāpe nāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kehamāne]]---someone accepts; [[synonyms:k:kehanāmāne]]---someone does not accept; [[synonyms:s:sabatāṅradāsa]]---all His servants; [[synonyms:y:yenāmāne]]---one who does not accept; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of him; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:p:pāpe]]---in sinful activity; [[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---annihilation.
translation: Some accept Him whereas others do not, yet everyone is His servant. One who does not accept Him, however, will be ruined by his sinful activities.
purport: When a living entity forgets his constitutional position, he prepares himself to be an enjoyer of the material resources. Sometimes he is also misguided by the thought that service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead is not absolute engagement. In other words, he thinks that there are many other engagements for a living entity besides the service of the Lord. Such a foolish person does not know that in any position he either directly or indirectly engages in activities of service to the Supreme Lord. Actually, if a person does not engage in the service of the Lord, all inauspicious activities encumber him because service to the Supreme Lord, Lord Caitanya, is the constitutional position of the infinitesimal living entities. Because the living entity is infinitesimal, the allurement of material enjoyment attracts him, and he tries to enjoy matter, forgetting his constitutional position. But when his dormant Kṛṣṇa consciousness is awakened, he no longer engages in the service of matter but engages in the service of the Lord. In other words, when one is forgetful of his constitutional position, he appears in the position of the lord of material nature. Even at that time he remains a servant of the Supreme Lord, but in an unqualified or contaminated state.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.86
description: "I am a servant of Lord Caitanya, a servant of Lord Caitanya. I am a servant of Lord Caitanya, and a servant of His servants."
text:

translation: "I am a servant of Lord Caitanya, a servant of Lord Caitanya. I am a servant of Lord Caitanya, and a servant of His servants."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.87
description: Saying this, Advaita Prabhu dances and loudly sings. Then at the next moment He quietly sits down.
text:
> eta bali' nāce, gāya, huṅkāra gambhīra

translation: Saying this, Advaita Prabhu dances and loudly sings. Then at the next moment He quietly sits down.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.88

text:

translation: The source of the sentiment of servitude is indeed Lord Balarāma. The plenary expansions who follow Him are all influenced by that ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.90

translation: Śeṣa Saṅkarṣaṇa, who holds all the planets on His head, expands Himself in different bodies to render service to Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 6.96
description: These are all incarnations of Lord Kṛṣṇa, yet we always find that they act as devotees.
text:
