translation: To describe the unlimited pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is not possible, but I now wish to relate the chief incidents and give a synopsis of those pastimes occurring at the end.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.100
description: The Lord had left Nityānanda's company and had gone alone to the Jagannātha temple, but later Nityānanda, Jagadānanda, Dāmodara and Mukunda came to see Him, and after seeing Him they were very pleased.
text:
> nityānanda, jagadānanda, dāmodara, mukunda
> pāche āsi' mili' sabe pāila ānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---of the name Nityānanda; [[synonyms:j:jagadānanda]]---of the name Jagadānanda; [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---of the name Dāmodara; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---of the name Mukunda; [[synonyms:p:pācheāsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:m:mili']]---meeting; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---pleasure
translation: The Lord had left Nityānanda's company and had gone alone to the Jagannātha temple, but later Nityānanda, Jagadānanda, Dāmodara and Mukunda came to see Him, and after seeing Him they were very pleased.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.101
description: After this incident, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His mercy upon Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya by showing him His original form as the Lord.
text:
> tabe sārvabhaume prabhu prasāda karila
> āpana-īśvara-mūrti tāṅre dekhāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhaume]]---unto Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prasādakarila]]---bestowed mercy; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]---His own; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---original form as the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:d:dekhāila]]---showed.
translation: After this incident, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His mercy upon Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya by showing him His original form as the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.102
description: After bestowing mercy upon Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, the Lord started for southern India. When He came to Kūrma-kṣetra, He delivered a person named Vāsudeva.
text:
> tabe ta' karilā prabhu dakṣiṇa gamana
> kūrma-kṣetre kaila vāsudeva vimocana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---thereafter; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]]---to southern India; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---traveling; [[synonyms:k:kūrma]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣetre]]---at the pilgrimage site known as Kūrma-kṣetra; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]---of the name Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:v:vimocana]]---deliverance.
translation: After bestowing mercy upon Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, the Lord started for southern India. When He came to Kūrma-kṣetra, He delivered a person named Vāsudeva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.103
description: After visiting Kūrma-kṣetra, the Lord visited the South Indian temple of Jiyaḍa-nṛsiṁha and offered His prayers to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva. On His way, He introduced the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra in every village.
text:
> jiyaḍa-nṛsiṁhe kaila nṛsiṁha-stavana
> pathe-pathe grāme-grāme nāma-pravartana
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jiyaḍa]]-[[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁhe]]---the place of pilgrimage known as Jiyaḍa-nṛsiṁha; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁha]]---to Nṛsiṁha; [[synonyms:s:stavana]]---praying; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way; [[synonyms:g:grāme]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---every village; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:p:pravartana]]---introduction of the holy name of the Lord.
translation: After visiting Kūrma-kṣetra, the Lord visited the South Indian temple of Jiyaḍa-nṛsiṁha and offered His prayers to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva. On His way, He introduced the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra in every village.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.104
description: Once the Lord mistook the forest on the bank of the river Godāvarī to be Vṛndāvana. In that place He happened to meet Rāmānanda Rāya.
text:
> godāvarī-tīra-vane vṛndāvana-bhrama
> rāmānanda rāya saha tāhāñi milana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:godāvarī]]-[[synonyms:t:tīra]]---on the bank of the river Godāvarī; [[synonyms:v:vane]]---in the forest; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhrama]]---mistook as Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:r:rāmānandarāya]]---of the name Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:t:tāhāñi]]---there; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting.
translation: Once the Lord mistook the forest on the bank of the river Godāvarī to be Vṛndāvana. In that place He happened to meet Rāmānanda Rāya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.105
description: He visited the place known as Trimalla, or Tirupati, and there He extensively preached the chanting of the Lord's holy name.
text:
> trimalla-tripadī-sthāna kaila daraśana
> sarvatra karila kṛṣṇa-nāma pracāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:trimalla]]---a place named Trimalla; [[synonyms:t:tripadī]]---or Tirupati; [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---the pace; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visit; [[synonyms:s:sarvatra]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pracāraṇa]]---preaching.
translation: He visited the place known as Trimalla, or Tirupati, and there He extensively preached the chanting of the Lord's holy name.
purport: This holy place is situated in the district of Tāñjor, South India. The temple of Tripadī is situated in the valley of Veṅkaṭācala (Veṅkaṭa Mountain) and contains a Deity of Lord Rāmacandra. On top of Veṅkaṭācala is the famous temple of Bālājī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.106
description: After visiting the temple of Trimalla, or Tripadī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had to subdue some atheists. He then visited the temple of Ahovala-nṛsiṁha.
text:
> tabe ta' pāṣaṇḍī-gaṇe karila dalana
> ahovala-nṛsiṁhādi kaila daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---thereafter; [[synonyms:p:pāṣaṇḍī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---unto the atheists; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:d:dalana]]---subduing; [[synonyms:a:ahovala]]-[[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---Nṛsiṁhadeva, named Ahovala or at Ahovala; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visit.
translation: After visiting the temple of Trimalla, or Tripadī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had to subdue some atheists. He then visited the temple of Ahovala-nṛsiṁha.
purport: This Ahovala temple is situated in Dākṣiṇātya, in the district of Karṇula, within the subdivision of Sārbela. Throughout the whole district this very famous temple is much appreciated by the people. There are eight other temples also, and all of them together are called the Nava-nṛsiṁha temples. There is much wonderful architecture and artistic engraving work in these temples. However, as stated in the local gazette, the //Karṇula Manual,// the work is not complete.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.107
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to the land of Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra, on the bank of the Kāverī, He visited the temple of Śrī Raṅganātha and was there overwhelmed in the ecstasy of love of Godhead.
text:
> śrī-raṅga-kṣetra āilā kāverīra tīra
> śrī-raṅga dekhiyā preme ha-ilā asthira
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅga]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣetra]]---to the place where the temple of Raṅganātha is situated; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:k:kāverīra]]---of the river Kāverī; [[synonyms:t:tīra]]---the bank; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅga]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---after seeing this temple; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in love of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:a:asthira]]---agitated.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to the land of Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra, on the bank of the Kāverī, He visited the temple of Śrī Raṅganātha and was there overwhelmed in the ecstasy of love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.108
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lived at the house of Trimalla Bhaṭṭa for the four months of the rainy season.
text:
> trimalla bhaṭṭera ghare kaila prabhu vāsa
> tāhāñi rahilā prabhu varṣā cāri māsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:trimalla]] [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭera]]---of Trimalla Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at the house; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---residence; [[synonyms:t:tāhāñi]]---there; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---lived; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:v:varṣā]]---the rainy season; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---four; [[synonyms:m:māsa]]---months.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lived at the house of Trimalla Bhaṭṭa for the four months of the rainy season.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.109
description: Śrī Trimalla Bhaṭṭa was both a member of the Śrī Vaiṣṇava community and a learned scholar; therefore when he saw Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who was both a great scholar and a great devotee of the Lord, he was very much astonished.
text:
> śrī-vaiṣṇava trimalla-bhaṭṭa---parama paṇḍita
> gosāñira pāṇḍitya-preme ha-ilā vismita
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:t:trimalla]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Trimalla Bhaṭṭa was a Śrī Vaiṣṇava; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---highly; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---learned scholar; [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pāṇḍitya]]---scholarship; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---as well as in the love of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---was; [[synonyms:v:vismita]]---astonished.
translation: Śrī Trimalla Bhaṭṭa was both a member of the Śrī Vaiṣṇava community and a learned scholar; therefore when he saw Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who was both a great scholar and a great devotee of the Lord, he was very much astonished.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.11-12
description: I shall describe only in synopsis that portion which Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has described very elaborately in his book Caitanya-maṅgala. Whatever incidents are outstanding, however, I shall later elaborate.
text:
> tāra madhye yei bhāga dāsa-vṛndāvana
> 'caitanya-maṅgale' vistāri' karilā varṇana
>
> sei bhāgera ihāṅ sūtra-mātra likhiba
> tāhāṅ ye viśeṣa kichu, ihāṅ vistāriba
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---amongst them; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---which; [[synonyms:b:bhāga]]---portion; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:m:maṅgale]]---in his book //Caitanya-maṅgala//; [[synonyms:v:vistāri']]---elaborating; [[synonyms:k:karilāvarṇana]]---has described; [[synonyms:s:seibhāgera]]---of that portion; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here in this book; [[synonyms:s:sūtra]]-[[synonyms:m:mātra]]---the synopsis only; [[synonyms:l:likhiba]]---I shall write; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:v:viśeṣa]]---special details; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅvistāriba]]---I shall describe elaborately.
translation: I shall describe only in synopsis that portion which Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has described very elaborately in his book Caitanya-maṅgala. Whatever incidents are outstanding, however, I shall later elaborate.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.110
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed the Cāturmāsya months with the Śrī Vaiṣṇavas, dancing and singing, and also chanting the holy name of the Lord.
text:
> cāturmāsya tāṅhā prabhu śrī-vaiṣṇavera sane
> goṅāila nṛtya-gīta-kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtane
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāturmāsya]]---observance of the four months ot the rainy season; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhā]]---there; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]] [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with the Śrī Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:g:goṅāila]]---passed; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:g:gīta]]---singing; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtane]]---in chanting the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed the Cāturmāsya months with the Śrī Vaiṣṇavas, dancing and singing, and also chanting the holy name of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.111
description: After the end of Cāturmāsya, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued traveling throughout South India. At that time He met Paramānanda Purī.
text:
> cāturmāsya-ante punaḥ dakṣiṇa gamana
> paramānanda-purī saha tāhāñi milana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāturmāsya]]-[[synonyms:a:ante]]---at the end of Cāturmāsya; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---traveling in South India; [[synonyms:p:paramānanda]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]---of the name Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:t:tāhāñi]]---there; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting.
translation: After the end of Cāturmāsya, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued traveling throughout South India. At that time He met Paramānanda Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.112
description: After this, Kṛṣṇadāsa, the servant of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, was delivered from the clutches of a Bhaṭṭathāri. Caitanya Mahāprabhu then preached that Lord Kṛṣṇa's name should also be chanted by brāhmaṇas who were accustomed to chanting Lord Rāma's name.
text:
> tabe bhaṭṭathāri haite kṛṣṇa-dāsera uddhāra
> rāma-japī vipra-mukhe kṛṣṇa-nāma pracāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---after this; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]-[[synonyms:t:thāri]]---a Bhaṭṭathāri; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsera]]---of Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:u:uddhāra]]---the deliverance; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:j:japī]]---chanters of the name of Lord Rāma; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---unto //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pracāra]]---preaching.
translation: After this, Kṛṣṇadāsa, the servant of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, was delivered from the clutches of a Bhaṭṭathāri. Caitanya Mahāprabhu then preached that Lord Kṛṣṇa's name should also be chanted by brāhmaṇas who were accustomed to chanting Lord Rāma's name.
purport: In the Mālābāra district, a section of the //brāhmaṇas// are known as Nambudari //brāhmaṇas,// and the Bhaṭṭathāris are their priests. Bhaṭṭathāris know many tantric black arts, such as the art of killing a person, of bringing him under submission, and of destroying or devastating him. They are very expert in these black arts, and one such Bhaṭṭathāri bewildered the personal servant of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu while the servant accompanied the Lord in His travels through South India. Somehow or other Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered this Kṛṣṇadāsa from the clutches of the Bhaṭṭathāri. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is well known as Patita-pāvana, the savior of all fallen souls, and He proved this in His behavior toward His personal servant, Kṛṣṇadāsa, whom He saved. Sometimes the word Bhaṭṭathāri is misspelled in Bengal as Bhaṭṭamāri.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.113
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then met Śrī Raṅgapurī and mitigated all the sufferings of a brāhmaṇa named Rāmadāsa.
text:
> śrī-raṅga-purī saha tāhāñi milana
> rāma-dāsa viprera kaila duḥkha-vimocana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅga]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]---of the name Śrī Raṅga-purī; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:t:tāhāñi]]---there; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---of the name Rāmadāsa; [[synonyms:v:viprera]]---of the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]-[[synonyms:v:vimocana]]---deliverance from all sufferings.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then met Śrī Raṅgapurī and mitigated all the sufferings of a brāhmaṇa named Rāmadāsa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.114
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu also had a discussion with the Tattvavādī community, and the Tattvavādīs felt themselves to be inferior Vaiṣṇavas.
text:
> tattva-vādī saha kaila tattvera vicāra
> āpanāke hīna-buddhi haila tāṅ-sabāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tattva]]-[[synonyms:v:vādī]]---a section of the Madhvācārya-sampradāya; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:t:tattvera]]---of the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---discussion; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāke]]---themselves; [[synonyms:h:hīna]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---consideration as inferior in quality; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:t:tāṅ]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all the opposing parties.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu also had a discussion with the Tattvavādī community, and the Tattvavādīs felt themselves to be inferior Vaiṣṇavas.
purport: The Tattvavādī sect belongs to Madhvācārya's Vaiṣṇava community, but its behavior differs from the strict Madhvācārya Vaiṣṇava principles. There is one monastery named Uttararāḍhī, and its commander is named Raghuvarya Tīrtha Madhvācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.115
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then visited the Viṣṇu temples of Anantadeva, Puruṣottama, Śrī Janārdana, Padmanābha and Vāsudeva.
text:
> ananta, puruṣottama, śrī-janārdana
> padmanābha, vāsudeva kaila daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---Anantadeva; [[synonyms:p:puruṣottama]]---of the name Puruṣottama; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:j:janārdana]]---of the name Śrī Janārdana; [[synonyms:p:padma]]-[[synonyms:n:nābha]]---of the name Padmanābha; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]---of the name Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visit.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then visited the Viṣṇu temples of Anantadeva, Puruṣottama, Śrī Janārdana, Padmanābha and Vāsudeva.
purport: A temple of Ananta Padmanābha Viṣṇu is situated in the Trivandrum district. This temple is very famous in those quarters. Another Viṣṇu temple, named Śrī Janārdana, is situated about twenty-six miles north of the Trivandrum district, near the railway station called Varkālā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.116
description: After that, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered the celebrated Sapta-tāla trees, took His bath at Setubandha Rāmeśvara and visited the temple of Lord Śiva known as Rāmeśvara.
text:
> tabe prabhu kaila sapta-tāla vimocana
> setubandhe snāna, rāmeśvara daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:sapta]]-[[synonyms:t:tāla]]-[[synonyms:v:vimocana]]---deliverance of the Sapta-tāla trees; [[synonyms:s:setubandhe]]---at Cape Comorin; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing; [[synonyms:r:rāmeśvara]]---temple of Rāmeśvara; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visit.
translation: After that, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered the celebrated Sapta-tāla trees, took His bath at Setubandha Rāmeśvara and visited the temple of Lord Śiva known as Rāmeśvara.
purport: It is said that the Sapta-tāla trees arevery old, massive palm trees. There was once a fight between Vāliand his brother Sugrīva, and Lord Rāmacandra took the side of Sugrīva and killed Vāli, keeping Himself behind one of these celebrated trees. When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu toured south India, He embraced these trees, which were delivered and directly promoted to Vaikuṇṭha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.117
description: At Rāmeśvara, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had a chance to read the Kūrma Purāṇa, in which He discovered that the form of Sītā kidnapped by Rāvaṇa was not that of the real Sītā but a mere shadow representation.
text:
> tāhāñi karila kūrma-purāṇa śravaṇa
> māyā-sītā nileka rāvaṇa, tāhāte likhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhāñi]]---there; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:k:kūrma]]-[[synonyms:p:purāṇa]]---of the //Kūrma Purāṇa//; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]---hearing; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:s:sītā]]---a false Sītā; [[synonyms:n:nileka]]---kidnapped; [[synonyms:r:rāvaṇa]]---by Rāvaṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāhāte]]---in that book; [[synonyms:l:likhana]]---it is stated.
translation: At Rāmeśvara, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had a chance to read the Kūrma Purāṇa, in which He discovered that the form of Sītā kidnapped by Rāvaṇa was not that of the real Sītā but a mere shadow representation.
purport: The //Kūrma Purāṇa// states that this shadowy Sītā was placed into a fire as a test of chastity. It was Māyā-sītā who entered the fire and the real Sītā who came out of the fire.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.118
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very glad to read about the false Sītā, and He remembered His meeting with Rāmadāsa Vipra, who was very sorry that mother Sītā had been kidnapped by Rāvaṇa.
text:
> śuniyā prabhura ānandita haila mana
> rāma-dāsa viprera kathā ha-ila smaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing this; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very happy; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---of the name Rāmadāsa; [[synonyms:v:viprera]]---with the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---of the conversation; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---was; [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---remembrance.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very glad to read about the false Sītā, and He remembered His meeting with Rāmadāsa Vipra, who was very sorry that mother Sītā had been kidnapped by Rāvaṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.119
description: Indeed, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu eagerly tore this page from the Kūrma Purāṇa, although the book was very old, and He later showed it to Rāmadāsa Vipra, whose unhappiness was mitigated.
text:
> sei purātana patra āgraha kari' nila
> rāmadāse dekhāiyā duḥkha khaṇḍāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:p:purātana]]---old; [[synonyms:p:patra]]---page; [[synonyms:ā:āgraha]]---with great enthusiasm; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:n:nila]]---took; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:d:dāse]]---to the //brāhmaṇa// Rāmadāsa; [[synonyms:d:dekhāiyā]]---showing; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍāila]]---mitigated.
translation: Indeed, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu eagerly tore this page from the Kūrma Purāṇa, although the book was very old, and He later showed it to Rāmadāsa Vipra, whose unhappiness was mitigated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.120
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also found two other books-namely, Brahma-saṁhitā and Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta. Knowing these books to be excellent, He took them to present to His devotees.
text:
> brahma-saṁhitā, karṇāmṛta, dui puṅthi pāñā
> dui pustaka lañā āilā uttama jāniñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṁhitā]]---the book named //Brahma-saṁhitā//; [[synonyms:k:karṇāmṛta]]---the book named //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta//; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:p:puṅthi]]---scriptures; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---obtaining; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:p:pustaka]]---books; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---carrying; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came back; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]---very good; [[synonyms:j:jāniñā]]---knowing.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also found two other books-namely, Brahma-saṁhitā and Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta. Knowing these books to be excellent, He took them to present to His devotees.
purport: In the olden days there were no presses, and all the important scriptures were handwritten and kept in large temples. Caitanya Mahāprabhu found //Brahma-saṁhitā// and //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta// in handwritten texts, and knowing them to be very authoritative, He took them with Him to present to His devotees. Of course, He obtained the permission of the temple commander. Now both //Brahma-saṁhitā// and //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta// are available in print with commentaries by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.121
description: After collecting these books, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to Jagannātha Purī. At that time, the bathing ceremony of Jagannātha was taking place, and He saw it.
text:
> punarapi nīlācale gamana karila
> bhakta-gaṇe meliyā snāna-yātrā dekhila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going back; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:m:meliyā]]---meeting; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---the bathing ceremony of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---saw.
translation: After collecting these books, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to Jagannātha Purī. At that time, the bathing ceremony of Jagannātha was taking place, and He saw it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.122
description: When Jagannātha was absent from the temple, Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who could not see Him, felt separation and left Jagannātha Purī to go to a place known as Ālālanātha.
text:
> anavasare jagannāthera nā pāñā daraśana
> virahe ālālanātha karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anavasare]]---during the absence; [[synonyms:j:jagannāthera]]---of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visit; [[synonyms:v:virahe]]---in separation; [[synonyms:ā:ālālanātha]]---of the place named Ālālanātha; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going.
translation: When Jagannātha was absent from the temple, Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who could not see Him, felt separation and left Jagannātha Purī to go to a place known as Ālālanātha.
purport:
Ālālanātha is also known as Brahmagiri. This place is about fourteen miles from Jagannātha Purī and is also on the beach. There is a temple of Jagannātha there. At the present moment a police station and post office are situated there because so many people come to see the temple.

The word //anavasara// is used when Śrī Jagannāthajī cannot be seen in the temple. After the bathing ceremony (//snāna-yātrā//), Lord Jagannātha apparently becomes sick. He is therefore removed to His private apartment, where no one can see Him. Actually, during this period renovations are made on the body of the Jagannātha Deity. This is called //nava-yauvana.// During the Ratha-yātrā ceremony, Lord Jagannātha once again comes before the public. Thus for fifteen days after the bathing ceremony, Lord Jagannātha is not visible to any visitors.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.123
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained for some days at Ālālanātha. In the meantime, Caitanya Mahāprabhu received news that all the devotees from Bengal were coming to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> bhakta-sane dina kata tāhāñi rahilā
> gauḍera bhakta āise, samācāra pāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with the devotees; [[synonyms:d:dina]] [[synonyms:k:kata]]---some days; [[synonyms:t:tāhāñi]]---there at Ālālanātha; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:g:gauḍera]]---of Bengal; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---come; [[synonyms:s:samācāra]]---news; [[synonyms:p:pāilā]]---He got.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained for some days at Ālālanātha. In the meantime, Caitanya Mahāprabhu received news that all the devotees from Bengal were coming to Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.124
description: When the devotees from Bengal arrived at Jagannātha Purī, both Nityānanda Prabhu and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya greatly endeavored to take Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu back to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> nityānanda-sārvabhauma āgraha kariñā
> nīlācale āilā mahāprabhuke la-iñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āgraha]] [[synonyms:k:kariñā]]---showing great eagerness; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhuke]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iñā]]---taking.
translation: When the devotees from Bengal arrived at Jagannātha Purī, both Nityānanda Prabhu and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya greatly endeavored to take Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu back to Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.125
description: When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally left Ālālanātha to return to Jagannātha Purī, He was overwhelmed both day and night due to separation from Jagannātha. His lamentation knew no bounds. During this time, all the devotees from different parts of Bengal, and especially from Navadvīpa, arrived in Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> virahe vihvala prabhu nā jāne rātri-dine
> hena-kāle āilā gauḍera bhakta-gaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:virahe]]---in separation; [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---knows; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---day and night; [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:g:gauḍera]]---of Bengal; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---all the devotees.
translation: When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally left Ālālanātha to return to Jagannātha Purī, He was overwhelmed both day and night due to separation from Jagannātha. His lamentation knew no bounds. During this time, all the devotees from different parts of Bengal, and especially from Navadvīpa, arrived in Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.126
description: After due consideration, all the devotees began chanting the holy name congregationally. Lord Caitanya's mind was thus pacified by the ecstasy of the chanting.
text:
> sabe mili' yukti kari' kīrtana ārambhila
> kīrtana-āveśe prabhura mana sthira haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabemili']]---meeting all together; [[synonyms:y:yuktikari']]---after due consideration; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---congregational chanting of the holy name; [[synonyms:ā:ārambhila]]---began; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in the ecstasy of //kīrtana//; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:s:sthira]]---pacified; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became.
translation: After due consideration, all the devotees began chanting the holy name congregationally. Lord Caitanya's mind was thus pacified by the ecstasy of the chanting.
purport: Being absolute, Lord Jagannātha is identical in person, form, picture, //kīrtana// and all other circumstances. Therefore when Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard the chanting of the holy name of the Lord, He was pacified. Previously, He had been feeling very morose due to separation from Jagannātha. The conclusion is that whenever a //kīrtana// of pure devotees takes place, the Lord is immediately present. By chanting the holy names of the Lord, we associate with the Lord personally.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.127
description: Previously, when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had been touring South India, He had met Rāmānanda Rāya on the banks of the Godāvarī. At that time it had been decided that Rāmānanda Rāya would resign from his post as governor and return to Jagannātha Purī to live with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> pūrve yabe prabhu rāmānandere mililā
> nīlācale āsibāre tāṅre ājñā dilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---before this; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---while; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:rāmānandere]]---Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āsibāre]]---to come; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:ā:ājñādilā]]---ordered.
translation: Previously, when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had been touring South India, He had met Rāmānanda Rāya on the banks of the Godāvarī. At that time it had been decided that Rāmānanda Rāya would resign from his post as governor and return to Jagannātha Purī to live with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.128
description: Upon the order of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya took leave of the King and returned to Jagannātha Purī. After he arrived, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very much enjoyed talking with him both day and night about Lord Kṛṣṇa and His pastimes.
text:
> rāja-ājñā lañā teṅho āilā kata dine
> rātri-dine kṛṣṇa-kathā rāmānanda-sane
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---the permission of the King, Pratāparudra; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---getting; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned; [[synonyms:k:katadine]]---in some days; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---day and night; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---talks of Lord Kṛṣṇa and His pastimes; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---in the company of Rāmānanda Rāya.
translation: Upon the order of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya took leave of the King and returned to Jagannātha Purī. After he arrived, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very much enjoyed talking with him both day and night about Lord Kṛṣṇa and His pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.129
description: After Rāmānanda Rāya's arrival, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His mercy upon Kāśī Miśra and met Pradyumna Miśra and others. At that time three personalities-Paramānanda Purī, Govinda and Kāśīśvara-came to see Lord Caitanya at Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> kāśī-miśre kṛpā, pradyumna miśrādi-milana
> paramānanda-purī-govinda-kāśīśvarāgamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāśī]]-[[synonyms:m:miśrekṛpā]]---His mercy to Kāśī Miśra; [[synonyms:p:pradyumnamiśra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting with Pradyumna Miśra and others; [[synonyms:p:paramānanda]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]---of the name Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---of the name Govinda; [[synonyms:k:kāśīśvara]]---of the name Kāśīśvara; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---coming.
translation: After Rāmānanda Rāya's arrival, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His mercy upon Kāśī Miśra and met Pradyumna Miśra and others. At that time three personalities-Paramānanda Purī, Govinda and Kāśīśvara-came to see Lord Caitanya at Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.13
description: Actually the authorized compiler of the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa, the incarnation of Vyāsadeva. Only upon his orders am I trying to chew the remnants of food that he has left.
text:
> caitanya-līlāra vyāsa---dāsa vṛndāvana
> tāṅra ājñāya karoṅ tāṅra ucchiṣṭa carvaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlāravyāsa]]---the Vyāsadeva, or compiler of the pastimes, of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dāsavṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of him; [[synonyms:ā:ājñāya]]---upon the order; [[synonyms:k:karoṅ]]---I do; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:u:ucchiṣṭa]]---of the remnants of food; [[synonyms:c:carvaṇa]]---chewing.
translation: Actually the authorized compiler of the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa, the incarnation of Vyāsadeva. Only upon his orders am I trying to chew the remnants of food that he has left.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.130
description: Eventually there was a meeting with Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, and the Lord became very greatly pleased. Then there was a meeting with Śikhi Māhiti and with Bhavānanda Rāya, the father of Rāmānanda Rāya.
text:
> dāmodara-svarūpa-milane parama ānanda
> śikhi-māhiti-milana, rāya bhavānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]-[[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:m:milane]]---in meeting; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---great; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:ś:śikhi]]-[[synonyms:m:māhiti]]---of the name Śikhi Māhiti; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting; [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:b:bhavānanda]]---Bhavānanda, the father of Rāmānanda Rāya.
translation: Eventually there was a meeting with Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, and the Lord became very greatly pleased. Then there was a meeting with Śikhi Māhiti and with Bhavānanda Rāya, the father of Rāmānanda Rāya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.131
description: All the devotees from Bengal gradually began arriving at Jagannātha Purī. At this time, the residents of Kulīna-grāma also came to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for the first time.
text:
> gauḍa ha-ite sarva vaiṣṇavera āgamana
> kulīna-grāma-vāsi-saṅge prathama milana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---from Bengal; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]]---of the Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---appearance; [[synonyms:k:kulīna]]-[[synonyms:g:grāma]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsi]]---the residents of Kulīna-grāma; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with them; [[synonyms:p:prathama]]---first; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting.
translation: All the devotees from Bengal gradually began arriving at Jagannātha Purī. At this time, the residents of Kulīna-grāma also came to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for the first time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.132
description: Eventually Narahari dāsa and other inhabitants of Khaṇḍa, along with Śivānanda Sena, all arrived, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu met them.
text:
> narahari dāsa ādi yata khaṇḍa-vāsī
> śivānanda-sena-saṅge mililā sabe āsi'
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:narahari]] [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---of the name Narahari dāsa; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---heading the list; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---devotees of the place known as Khaṇḍa; [[synonyms:ś:śivānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sena]]---of the name Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---He met; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming there.
translation: Eventually Narahari dāsa and other inhabitants of Khaṇḍa, along with Śivānanda Sena, all arrived, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu met them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.133
description: After seeing the bathing ceremony of Lord Jagannātha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu washed and cleaned Śrī Guṇḍicā temple with the assistance of many devotees.
text:
> snāna-yātrā dekhi' prabhu saṅge bhakta-gaṇa
> sabā lañā kailā prabhu guṇḍicā mārjana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:snāna]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---the bathing ceremony; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Him; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:guṇḍicā]] [[synonyms:m:mārjana]]---washing and cleaning the Guṇḍicā temple.
translation: After seeing the bathing ceremony of Lord Jagannātha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu washed and cleaned Śrī Guṇḍicā temple with the assistance of many devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.134
description: After this, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all the devotees saw the Ratha-yātrā, the car festival ceremony. Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself danced in front of the car, and after dancing He entered a garden.
text:
> sabā-saṅge ratha-yātrā kaila daraśana
> ratha-agre nṛtya kari' udyāne gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with all of them; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---the car festival; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:a:agre]]---in front of the car; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:u:udyāne]]---in the garden; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going.
translation: After this, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all the devotees saw the Ratha-yātrā, the car festival ceremony. Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself danced in front of the car, and after dancing He entered a garden.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.135
description: In that garden, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His mercy upon King Pratāparudra. Afterwards, when the Bengali devotees were about to return home, the Lord gave separate orders to almost every one of them.
text:
> pratāparudrere kṛpā kaila sei sthāne
> gauḍīyā-bhakte ājñā dila vidāyera dine
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pratāparudrere]]---unto King Pratāparudra; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:seisthāne]]---in that garden; [[synonyms:g:gauḍīyā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---to all the devotees of Bengal; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---the order; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:v:vidāyera]]---of departure; [[synonyms:d:dine]]---on the day.
translation: In that garden, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His mercy upon King Pratāparudra. Afterwards, when the Bengali devotees were about to return home, the Lord gave separate orders to almost every one of them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.136
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu desired to meet all the devotees of Bengal every year. Therefore He ordered them to come to see the Ratha-yātrā festival every year.
text:
> pratyabda āsibe ratha-yātrā-daraśane
> ei chale cāhe bhakta-gaṇera milane
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:a:abda]]---every year; [[synonyms:ā:āsibe]]---you should all come; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---the car festival; [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---to see; [[synonyms:e:eichale]]---under this plea; [[synonyms:c:cāhe]]---desires; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of all the devotees; [[synonyms:m:milane]]---the meeting.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu desired to meet all the devotees of Bengal every year. Therefore He ordered them to come to see the Ratha-yātrā festival every year.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.137
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was invited to dine at the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. While He was eating sumptuously, the son-in-law of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya [the husband of his daughter Ṣāṭhī] criticized Him. Because of this, Ṣāṭhī's mother cursed him by praying that Ṣāṭhī would become a widow. In other words, she cursed her son-in-law to die.
text:
> sārvabhauma-ghare prabhura bhikṣā-paripāṭī
> ṣāṭhīra mātā kahe, yāte rāṇḍī ha-uk ṣāṭhī
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]-[[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---eating; [[synonyms:p:paripāṭī]]---sumptuously; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣāṭhīra]] [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---the mother of Ṣāṭhī, who was the daughter of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---by which; [[synonyms:r:rāṇḍī]]---widow; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:u:uk]]---let her become; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣāṭhī]]---Ṣāṭhī, the daughter.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was invited to dine at the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. While He was eating sumptuously, the son-in-law of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya [the husband of his daughter Ṣāṭhī] criticized Him. Because of this, Ṣāṭhī's mother cursed him by praying that Ṣāṭhī would become a widow. In other words, she cursed her son-in-law to die.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.138
description: At the end of the year, all the devotees from Bengal, headed by Advaita Ācārya, again came to see the Lord. Indeed, there was a great rush of devotees to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> varṣāntare advaitādi bhaktera āgamana
> prabhure dekhite sabe karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:varṣa]]-[[synonyms:a:antare]]---at the end of the year; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:b:bhaktera]]---of all the devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---coming to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going to Jagannātha Purī.
translation: At the end of the year, all the devotees from Bengal, headed by Advaita Ācārya, again came to see the Lord. Indeed, there was a great rush of devotees to Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.139
description: When all the devotees from Bengal arrived, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu allotted them residential quarters, and Śivānanda Sena was put in charge of their maintenance.
text:
> ānande sabāre niyā dena vāsa-sthāna
> śivānanda sena kare sabāra pālana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in great pleasure; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:n:niyā]]---taking; [[synonyms:d:dena]]---gives; [[synonyms:v:vāsa]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---residential quarters; [[synonyms:ś:śivānandasena]]---of the name Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all; [[synonyms:p:pālana]]---maintenance.
translation: When all the devotees from Bengal arrived, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu allotted them residential quarters, and Śivānanda Sena was put in charge of their maintenance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.14
description: Placing his lotus feet upon my head in great devotion, I shall now describe in summary the Lord's final pastimes.
text:
> bhakti kari' śire dhari tāṅhāra caraṇa
> śeṣa-līlāra sūtra-gaṇa kariye varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---with great devotion; [[synonyms:ś:śire]]---on my head; [[synonyms:d:dhari]]---I hold; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---his; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---lotus feet; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlāra]]---of the pastimes at the end; [[synonyms:s:sūtra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the synopsis; [[synonyms:k:kariye]]---I do; [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---describe.
translation: Placing his lotus feet upon my head in great devotion, I shall now describe in summary the Lord's final pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.140
description: A dog accompanied Śivānanda Sena and the devotees, and that dog was so fortunate that after seeing the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, it was liberated and went back home, back to Godheand.
text:
> śivānandera saṅge āilā kukkura bhāgyavān
> prabhura caraṇa dekhi' kaila antardhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śivānanderasaṅge]]---with Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:k:kukkura]]---a dog; [[synonyms:b:bhāgyavān]]---fortunate; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:a:antardhāna]]---disappearing.
translation: A dog accompanied Śivānanda Sena and the devotees, and that dog was so fortunate that after seeing the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, it was liberated and went back home, back to Godheand.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.141
description: Everyone met Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya on his way to Vārāṇasī.
text:
> pathe sārvabhauma saha sabāra milana
> sārvabhauma bhaṭṭācāryera kāśīte gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhaumabhaṭṭācāryera]]---of the devotee named Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kāśīte]]---to Vārāṇasī; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going.
translation: Everyone met Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya on his way to Vārāṇasī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.142
description: After arriving at Jagannātha Purī, all the Vaiṣṇavas met with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Later, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sported in the water, taking all the devotees with Him.
text:
> prabhure mililā sarva vaiṣṇava āsiyā
> jala-krīḍā kaila prabhu sabāre la-iyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---arriving at Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:k:krīḍā]]---sporting in the water; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iyā]]---taking.
translation: After arriving at Jagannātha Purī, all the Vaiṣṇavas met with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Later, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sported in the water, taking all the devotees with Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.143
description: First the Lord washed the temple of Guṇḍicā very thoroughly. Then everyone saw the Ratha-yātrā festival and the Lord's dancing before the car.
text:
> sabā lañā kaila guṇḍicā-gṛha-sammārjana
> ratha-yātrā-daraśane prabhura nartana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabālañā]]---taking all of them; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:g:guṇḍicā]]-[[synonyms:g:gṛha]]-[[synonyms:s:sammārjana]]---washing of the Guṇḍicā temple; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---the car festival; [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---in seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dancing.
translation: First the Lord washed the temple of Guṇḍicā very thoroughly. Then everyone saw the Ratha-yātrā festival and the Lord's dancing before the car.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.144
description: In the garden along the road from the Jagannātha temple to Guṇḍicā, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed various pastimes. A brāhmaṇa named Kṛṣṇadāsa performed the bathing ceremony of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> upavane kaila prabhu vividha vilāsa
> prabhura abhiṣeka kaila vipra kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:upavane]]---in the garden by the road; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vividha]]---varieties of; [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:abhiṣeka]]---bathing; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---of the name Kṛṣṇadāsa.
translation: In the garden along the road from the Jagannātha temple to Guṇḍicā, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed various pastimes. A brāhmaṇa named Kṛṣṇadāsa performed the bathing ceremony of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.145
description: After dancing in the Guṇḍicā temple, the Lord sported in the water with His devotees, and on Herā-pañcamī day they all saw the activities of the goddess of fortune, Lakṣmīdevī.
text:
> guṇḍicāte nṛtya-ante kaila jala-keli
> herā-pañcamīte dekhila lakṣmī-devīra kelī
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:guṇḍicāte]]---in the neighborhood of the Guṇḍicā temple; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:a:ante]]---after dancing; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:k:keli]]---sporting in the water; [[synonyms:h:herā]]-[[synonyms:p:pañcamīte]]---on the day of Herā-pañcamī; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---saw; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]-[[synonyms:d:devīra]]---of the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:k:kelī]]---activities.
translation: After dancing in the Guṇḍicā temple, the Lord sported in the water with His devotees, and on Herā-pañcamī day they all saw the activities of the goddess of fortune, Lakṣmīdevī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.146
description: On Janmāṣṭamī, Lord Kṛṣṇa's birthday, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu dressed Himself as a cowherd boy. At that time He carried a balance with pots of yogurt and wheeled a rod about.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-janma-yātrāte prabhu gopa-veśa hailā
> dadhi-bhāra vahi' tabe laguḍa phirāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:j:janma]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrāte]]---on the birthday ceremony of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:v:veśa]]---dressed like a cowherd boy; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---was; [[synonyms:d:dadhi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāra]]---a balance for pots of yogurt; [[synonyms:v:vahi']]---carrying; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:l:laguḍa]]---a rod; [[synonyms:p:phirāilā]]---wheeled about.
translation: On Janmāṣṭamī, Lord Kṛṣṇa's birthday, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu dressed Himself as a cowherd boy. At that time He carried a balance with pots of yogurt and wheeled a rod about.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.147
description: After this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade farewell to all the devotees from Gauḍa-deśa [Bengal] and continued chanting with His intimate devotees who constantly remained with Him.
text:
> gauḍera bhakta-gaṇe tabe karila vidāya
> saṅgera bhakta lañā kare kīrtana sadāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍera]]---of Gauḍa-deśa (Bengal); [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---to the devotees; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---gave; [[synonyms:v:vidāya]]---farewell; [[synonyms:s:saṅgera]]---of constant companionship; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotees; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---congregational chanting; [[synonyms:s:sadāya]]---always.
translation: After this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade farewell to all the devotees from Gauḍa-deśa [Bengal] and continued chanting with His intimate devotees who constantly remained with Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.148
description: To visit Vṛndāvana, the Lord went to Gauḍa-deśa [Bengal]. On the way, King Pratāparudra performed a variety of service to please the Lord.
text:
> vṛndāvana yāite kaila gauḍere gamana
> pratāparudra kaila pathe vividha sevana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]] [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gauḍere]]---to Bengal; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going; [[synonyms:p:pratāparudra]]---King Pratāparudra; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the road; [[synonyms:v:vividha]]---various; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---services.
translation: To visit Vṛndāvana, the Lord went to Gauḍa-deśa [Bengal]. On the way, King Pratāparudra performed a variety of service to please the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.149
description: On the way to Vṛndāvana via Bengal, there was an incident wherein some cloth was exchanged with Purī Gosāñi. Śrī Rāmānada Rāya accompanied the Lord as far as the city of Bhadraka.
text:
> purī-gosāñi-saṅge vastra-pradāna-prasaṅga
> rāmānanda rāya āilā bhadraka paryanta
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Purī Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:v:vastra]]-[[synonyms:p:pradāna]]-[[synonyms:p:prasaṅga]]---incidents of exchanging cloth; [[synonyms:r:rāmānandarāya]]---of the name Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:b:bhadraka]]---a place of the name Bhadraka; [[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---as far as.
translation: On the way to Vṛndāvana via Bengal, there was an incident wherein some cloth was exchanged with Purī Gosāñi. Śrī Rāmānada Rāya accompanied the Lord as far as the city of Bhadraka.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.15
description: For twenty-four years, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained at home, and whatever pastimes He performed during that time are called the ādi-līlā.
text:
> cabbiśa vatsara prabhura gṛhe avasthāna
> tāhāṅ ye karilā līlā---'ādi-līlā' nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cabbiśa]] [[synonyms:v:vatsara]]---for twenty-four years; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---at home; [[synonyms:a:avasthāna]]---residing; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---He performed; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---are called //ādi-līlā.//
translation: For twenty-four years, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained at home, and whatever pastimes He performed during that time are called the ādi-līlā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.150
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu reached Vidyānagara, Bengal, on the way to Vṛndāvana, He stopped at the house of Vidyā-vācaspati, who was the brother of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu suddenly arrived at his house, great crowds of people gathered.
text:
> āsi' vidyā-vācaspatira gṛhete rahilā
> prabhure dekhite loka-saṅghaṭṭa ha-ilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming to Bengal; [[synonyms:v:vidyā]]-[[synonyms:v:vācaspatira]]---of Vidyā-vācaspati; [[synonyms:g:gṛhete]]---at the home; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅghaṭṭa]]---crowds of men; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---there were.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu reached Vidyānagara, Bengal, on the way to Vṛndāvana, He stopped at the house of Vidyā-vācaspati, who was the brother of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu suddenly arrived at his house, great crowds of people gathered.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.151
description: For five consecutive days all the people gathered to see the Lord, and still there was no rest. Out of fear of the crowd, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu left at night and went to the town of Kuliyā [present-day Navadvīpa].
text:
> pañca-dina dekhe loka nāhika viśrāma
> loka-bhaye rātre prabhu āilā kuliyā-grāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---continuously for five days; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---see; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:v:viśrāma]]---rest; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---on account of fearing the crowds of men; [[synonyms:r:rātre]]---at night; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---went; [[synonyms:k:kuliyā]]-[[synonyms:g:grāma]]---to the place known as Kuliyā.
translation: For five consecutive days all the people gathered to see the Lord, and still there was no rest. Out of fear of the crowd, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu left at night and went to the town of Kuliyā [present-day Navadvīpa].
purport: If one considers the statements of the //Caitanya-bhāgavata// along with the description by Locana dāsa Ṭhākura, it is clear that present-day Navadvīpa was formerly known as Kuliyā-grāma. While at Kuliyā-grāma, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His favor upon Devānanda Paṇḍita and delivered Gopāla Cāpala and many others who had previously committed offenses at His lotus feet. At that time, to go from Vidyānagara to Kuliyā-grāma one had to cross a branch of the Ganges. All of those old places still exist. Cināḍāṅgā was formerly situated in Kuliyā-grāma, which is now known as Kolera Gañja.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.152
description: Hearing of the Lord's arrival in Kuliyā-grāma, may hundreds and thousands of people came to see Him.
text:
> kuliyā-grāmete prabhura śuniyā āgamana
> koṭi koṭi loka āsi' kaila daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kuliyā]]-[[synonyms:g:grāmete]]---in that place known as Kuliyā-grāma; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---about the arrival; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]] [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---hundreds of thousands; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---of people; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---took; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---audience.
translation: Hearing of the Lord's arrival in Kuliyā-grāma, may hundreds and thousands of people came to see Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.153
description: The specific acts performed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu at this time were His showing favor to Devānanda Paṇḍita and excusing the brāhmaṇa known as Gopāla Cāpala from the offense he had committed at the lotus feet of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura.
text:
> kuliyā-grāme kaila devānandere prasāda
> gopāla-viprere kṣamāila śrīvāsāparādha
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kuliyā]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in that village known as Kuliyā-grāma; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---showed; [[synonyms:d:devānandere]] [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---mercy to Devānanda Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:v:viprere]]---and to the //brāhmaṇa// known as Gopāla Cāpala; [[synonyms:k:kṣamāila]]---excused; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]-[[synonyms:a:aparādha]]---the offense to the lotus feet of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura.
translation: The specific acts performed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu at this time were His showing favor to Devānanda Paṇḍita and excusing the brāhmaṇa known as Gopāla Cāpala from the offense he had committed at the lotus feet of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.154
description: Many atheists and blasphemers came and fell at the lotus feet of the Lord, and the Lord in return excused them and gave them love of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> pāṣaṇḍī nindaka āsi' paḍilā caraṇe
> aparādha kṣami' tāre dila kṛṣṇa-preme

translation: Many atheists and blasphemers came and fell at the lotus feet of the Lord, and the Lord in return excused them and gave them love of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.155
description: When Śrī Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī heard that Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu would go to Vṛndāvana, he became very pleased and mentally began decorating the way there.
text:
> vṛndāvana yābena prabhu śuni' nṛsiṁhānanda
> patha sājāila mane pāiyā ānanda

translation: When Śrī Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī heard that Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu would go to Vṛndāvana, he became very pleased and mentally began decorating the way there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.156
description: First Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī contemplated a broad road starting from the city of Kuliyā. He bedecked the road with jewels, upon which he then laid a bed of stemless flowers.
text:
> kuliyā nagara haite patha ratne bāndhāila
> nivṛnta puṣpa-śayyā upare pātila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kuliyā]] [[synonyms:n:nagara]]---the city of Kuliyā; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:p:patha]]---way; [[synonyms:r:ratne]]---with jewels; [[synonyms:b:bāndhāila]]---constructed; [[synonyms:n:nivṛnta]]---stemless; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śayyā]]---flower bed; [[synonyms:u:upare]]---on top; [[synonyms:p:pātila]]---laid down.
translation: First Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī contemplated a broad road starting from the city of Kuliyā. He bedecked the road with jewels, upon which he then laid a bed of stemless flowers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.157
description: He mentally decorated both sides of the road with bakula flower trees, and at intervals on both sides he placed lakes of a transcendental nature.
text:
> pathe dui dike puṣpa-bakulera śreṇī
> madhye madhye dui-pāśe divya puṣkariṇī

translation: He mentally decorated both sides of the road with bakula flower trees, and at intervals on both sides he placed lakes of a transcendental nature.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.158
description: These lakes had bathing places constructed with jewels, and they were filled with blossoming lotus flowers. There were various birds chirping, and the water was exactly like nectar.
text:
> ratna-bāṅdhā ghāṭa, tāhe praphulla kamala
> nānā pakṣi-kolāhala, sudhā-sama jala
