translation: These lakes had bathing places constructed with jewels, and they were filled with blossoming lotus flowers. There were various birds chirping, and the water was exactly like nectar.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.159
description: The entire road was surcharged with many cool breezes, which carried the fragrances from various flowers. He carried the construction of this road as far as Kānāi Nāṭaśālā.
text:
> śītala samīra vahe nānā gandha lañā
> 'kānāira nāṭaśālā' paryanta la-ila bāndhiñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śītala]]---very cool; [[synonyms:s:samīra]]---breezes; [[synonyms:v:vahe]]---blowing; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:g:gandha]]---fragrances; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---carrying; [[synonyms:k:kānāira]] [[synonyms:n:nāṭa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śālā]]---the place named Kānāi Nāṭaśālā; [[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---as far as; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---carried; [[synonyms:b:bāndhiñā]]---constructing.
translation: The entire road was surcharged with many cool breezes, which carried the fragrances from various flowers. He carried the construction of this road as far as Kānāi Nāṭaśālā.
purport: Kānāi Nāṭaśālā is about 202 miles from Calcutta on the Loop line of the Eastern Railway. The railway station is named Tālajhāḍi, and after one gets off at that station, he has to go about two miles to find Kānāi Nāṭaśālā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.16
description: At the end of His twenty-fourth year, in the month of Māgha, during the fortnight of the waxing moon, the Lord accepted the renounced order of life, sannyāsa.
text:
> cabbiśa vatsara śeṣe yei māgha-māsa
> tāra śukla-pakṣe prabhu karilā sannyāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cabbiśa]] [[synonyms:v:vatsara]]---of those twenty-four years; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---at the end; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---which; [[synonyms:m:māgha]]-[[synonyms:m:māsa]]---the month of Māgha (January-February); [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that month; [[synonyms:ś:śukla]]-[[synonyms:p:pakṣe]]---during the fortnight of the waxing moon; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---accepted; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---the renounced order of life.
translation: At the end of His twenty-fourth year, in the month of Māgha, during the fortnight of the waxing moon, the Lord accepted the renounced order of life, sannyāsa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.160
description: Within the mind of Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī, the road could not be constructed beyond Kānāi Nāṭaśālā. He could not understand why the road's construction could not be completed, and thus he was astonished.
text:
> āge mana nāhi cale, nā pāre bāndhite
> patha-bāndhā nā yāya, nṛsiṁha hailā vismite
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---beyond this; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---does not; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---go; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---is not; [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---able; [[synonyms:b:bāndhite]]---to construct the road; [[synonyms:p:patha]]-[[synonyms:b:bāndhā]]---construction of the road; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---is not possible; [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁha]]---Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vismite]]---astonished.
translation: Within the mind of Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī, the road could not be constructed beyond Kānāi Nāṭaśālā. He could not understand why the road's construction could not be completed, and thus he was astonished.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.161
description: With great assurance he then told the devotees that Lord Caitanya would not go to Vṛndāvana at that time.
text:
> niścaya kariyā kahi, śuna, bhakta-gaṇa
> ebāra nā yābena prabhu śrī-vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---assurance; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---making; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I say; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---my dear devotees; [[synonyms:e:ebāra]]---this time; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yābena]]---will go; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---to Vṛndāvana.
translation: With great assurance he then told the devotees that Lord Caitanya would not go to Vṛndāvana at that time.
purport:
Śrīla Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī was a great devotee of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; therefore when he heard that from Kuliyā Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was going to Vṛndāvana, although he had no material wealth he began to construct within his mind a very attractive path or road for Caitanya Mahāprabhu to traverse. Some of the description of this path is given above. But even mentally he could not construct the road beyond Kānāi Nāṭaśālā. Therefore he concluded that Caitanya Mahāprabhu would not go to Vṛndāvana at that time.

For a pure devotee, it is the same whether he materially constructs a path or constructs one within his mind. This is because the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Janārdana, is //bhāva-grāhī,// or appreciative of the sentiment. For Him a path made with actual jewels and a path made of mental jewels are the same. Though subtle, mind is also matter, so any path-indeed, anything for the service of the Lord, whether in gross matter or in subtle matter-is accepted equally by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Lord accepts the attitude of His devotee and sees how much he is prepared to serve Him. The devotee is at liberty to serve the Lord either in gross matter or in subtle matter. The important point is that the service be in relation with the Supreme Personality of Godheand. This is confirmed in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:26|(Bg. 9.26)]]:

> patraṁ puṣpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ
> yo me bhaktyā prayacchati
> tad ahaṁ bhakty-upahṛtam
> aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ

"If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I will accept it." The real ingredient is //bhakti// (devotion). Pure devotion is uncontaminated by the modes of material nature. //Ahaituky apratihatā:// unconditional devotional service cannot be checked by any material condition. This means that one does not have to be very rich to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Even the poorest man can equally serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead if he has pure devotion. If there is no ulterior motive, devotional service cannot be checked by any material condition.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.162
description: Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī said, "The Lord will go to Kānāi Nāṭaśālā and then will return. All of you will come to know of this later, but I now say this with great assurance."
text:
> 'kānāñira nāṭaśālā' haite āsiba phiriñā
> jānibe paścāt, kahilu niścaya kariñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kānāñira]] [[synonyms:n:nāṭa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śālā]]---the place of the name Kānāi Nāṭaśālā; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:ā:āsiba]]---will come; [[synonyms:p:phiriñā]]---returning; [[synonyms:j:jānibe]]---you will know; [[synonyms:p:paścāt]]---later; [[synonyms:k:kahilu]]---I say; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---assurance; [[synonyms:k:kariñā]]---making.
translation: Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī said, "The Lord will go to Kānāi Nāṭaśālā and then will return. All of you will come to know of this later, but I now say this with great assurance."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.163
description: When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to proceed from Kuliyā toward Vṛndāvana, thousands of men were with Him, and all of them were devotees.
text:
> gosāñi kuliyā haite calilā vṛndāvana
> saṅge sahasreka loka yata bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kuliyā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from Kuliyā; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---proceeded; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---toward Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Him; [[synonyms:s:sahasreka]]---thousands; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---of people; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees.
translation: When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to proceed from Kuliyā toward Vṛndāvana, thousands of men were with Him, and all of them were devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.164
description: Wherever the Lord visited, crowds of innumerable people came to see Him. When they saw Him, all their unhappiness and lamentation disappeared.
text:
> yāhāṅ yāya prabhu, tāhāṅ koṭi-saṅkhya loka
> dekhite āise, dekhi' khaṇḍe duḥkha-śoka
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkhya]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---an unlimited number of people; [[synonyms:d:dekhiteāise]]---come to see Him; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after seeing; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍe]]---removes; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:ś:śoka]]---lamentation.
translation: Wherever the Lord visited, crowds of innumerable people came to see Him. When they saw Him, all their unhappiness and lamentation disappeared.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.165
description: Wherever the Lord touched the ground with His lotus feet, people immediately came and gathered the dirt. Indeed, they gathered so much that many holes were created in the road.
text:
> yāhāṅ yāhāṅ prabhura caraṇa paḍaye calite
> se mṛttikā laya loka, garta haya pathe
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---lotus feet; [[synonyms:p:paḍaye]]---touch; [[synonyms:c:calite]]---while walking; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:m:mṛttikā]]---dirt; [[synonyms:l:laya]]---take; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people; [[synonyms:g:garta]]---a hole; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there becomes; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the road.
translation: Wherever the Lord touched the ground with His lotus feet, people immediately came and gathered the dirt. Indeed, they gathered so much that many holes were created in the road.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.166
description: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu eventually arrived at a village named Rāmakeli. This village is situated on the border of Bengal and is very exquisite.
text:
> aiche cali, āilā prabhu 'rāmakeli' grāma
> gauḍera nikaṭa grāma ati anupāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:c:cali]]---walking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:rāmakeli]] [[synonyms:g:grāma]]---to the village of the name Rāmakeli; [[synonyms:g:gauḍera]]---Bengal; [[synonyms:n:nikaṭa]]---near; [[synonyms:g:grāma]]---the village; [[synonyms:a:ati]]---very; [[synonyms:a:anupāma]]---exquisite.
translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu eventually arrived at a village named Rāmakeli. This village is situated on the border of Bengal and is very exquisite.
purport: Rāmakeli-grāma is situated on the banks of the Ganges on the border of Bengal. Śrīla Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmīs had their residences in this village.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.167
description: While performing saṅkīrtana in Rāmakeli-grāma, the Lord danced and sometimes lost consciousness due to love of God. While at Rāmakeli-grāma, an unlimited number of people came to see His lotus feet.
text:
> tāhāṅ nṛtya kare prabhu preme acetana
> koṭi koṭi loka āise dekhite caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performed; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in love of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:acetana]]---unconscious; [[synonyms:k:koṭikoṭi]]---innumerable; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---came; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---His lotus feet.
translation: While performing saṅkīrtana in Rāmakeli-grāma, the Lord danced and sometimes lost consciousness due to love of God. While at Rāmakeli-grāma, an unlimited number of people came to see His lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.168
description: When the Muslim King of Bengal heard of Caitanya Mahāprabhu's influence in attracting innumerable people, he became very astonished and began to speak as follows.
text:
> gauḍeśvara yavana-rājā prabhāva śuniñā
> kahite lāgila kichu vismita hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---King of Bengal; [[synonyms:y:yavana]]-[[synonyms:r:rājā]]---Muslim king; [[synonyms:p:prabhāva]]---influence; [[synonyms:ś:śuniñā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to say; [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:v:vismita]]---astonished; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming.
translation: When the Muslim King of Bengal heard of Caitanya Mahāprabhu's influence in attracting innumerable people, he became very astonished and began to speak as follows.
purport: At that time the Muslim king of Bengal was Nawab Hussain Shah Bādasāha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.169
description: "Such a person, who is followed by so many people without giving them charity, must be a prophet. I can surely understand this fact."
text:
> vinā dāne eta loka yāṅra pāche haya
> sei ta' gosāñā, ihā jāniha niścaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:d:dāne]]---charity; [[synonyms:e:eta]]---so many; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---persons; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whom; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---after; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---become; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---He certainly; [[synonyms:g:gosāñā]]---a prophet; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:j:jāniha]]---know; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---surely.
translation: "Such a person, who is followed by so many people without giving them charity, must be a prophet. I can surely understand this fact."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.17
description: After accepting sannyāsa, Lord Caitanya remained within this material world for another twenty-four years. Within this period, whatever pastimes He enacted are called the śeṣa-līlā, or pastimes occurring at the end.
text:
> sannyāsa kariyā cabbiśa vatsara avasthāna
> tāhāṅ yei līlā, tāra 'śeṣa-līlā' nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---after accepting the order of //sannyāsa//; [[synonyms:c:cabbiśa]] [[synonyms:v:vatsara]]---the twenty-four years; [[synonyms:a:avasthāna]]---remaining in this material world; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---in that portion; [[synonyms:y:yeilīlā]]---whatever pastimes (were performed); [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of those pastimes; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes at the end; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named.
translation: After accepting sannyāsa, Lord Caitanya remained within this material world for another twenty-four years. Within this period, whatever pastimes He enacted are called the śeṣa-līlā, or pastimes occurring at the end.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.170
description: The Muslim King ordered the magistrate, "Do not disturb this Hindu prophet out of jealousy. Let Him do His own will wherever He likes."
text:
> kājī, yavana ihāra nā kariha hiṁsana
> āpana-icchāya buluna, yāhāṅ uṅhāra mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kājī]]---magistrate; [[synonyms:y:yavana]]---Muslim; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of Him; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---do not; [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---make; [[synonyms:h:hiṁsana]]---jealousy; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:i:icchāya]]---at His own will; [[synonyms:b:buluna]]---let Him go; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:u:uṅhāra]]---of Him; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind.
translation: The Muslim King ordered the magistrate, "Do not disturb this Hindu prophet out of jealousy. Let Him do His own will wherever He likes."
purport: Even a Muslim king could understand Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's transcendental position as a prophet; therefore he ordered the local magistrate not to disturb Him but to let Him do whatever He liked.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.171
description: When the Muslim King asked his assistant, Keśava Chatrī, for news of the influence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Keśava Chatrī, although knowing everything about Caitanya Mahāprabhu, tried to avoid the conversation by not giving any importance to Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities.
text:
> keśava-chatrīre rājā vārtā puchila
> prabhura mahimā chatrī uḍāiyā dila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:keśava]]-[[synonyms:c:chatrīre]]---from the person named Keśava Chatrī; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:v:vārtā]]---news; [[synonyms:p:puchila]]---inquired; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---glories; [[synonyms:c:chatrī]]---Keśava Chatrī; [[synonyms:u:uḍāiyā]]---attaching no importance; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave.
translation: When the Muslim King asked his assistant, Keśava Chatrī, for news of the influence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Keśava Chatrī, although knowing everything about Caitanya Mahāprabhu, tried to avoid the conversation by not giving any importance to Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities.
purport: Keśava Chatrī became a diplomat when questioned about Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Although he knew everything about Him, he was afraid that the Muslim King might become His enemy. He gave no importance to the Lord's activities so that the Muslim King would take Him to be an ordinary man and would not give Him any trouble.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.172
description: Keśava Chatrī informed the Muslim King that Caitanya Mahāprabhu was a mendicant touring different places of pilgrimage and that, as such, only a few people came to see Him.
text:
> bhikhārī sannyāsī kare tīrtha paryaṭana
> tāṅre dekhibāre āise dui cāri jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhikhāri]]---beggar; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---mendicant; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]---of holy places; [[synonyms:p:paryaṭana]]---touring; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:d:dekhibṁre]]---to see; [[synonyms:ṁ:ṁise]]---come; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:c:cṁri]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---only a few people.
translation: Keśava Chatrī informed the Muslim King that Caitanya Mahāprabhu was a mendicant touring different places of pilgrimage and that, as such, only a few people came to see Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.173
description: Keśava Chatrī said, "Out of jealousy your Muslim servant plots against Him. I think that you should not be very interested in Him, for there is no profit in it. Rather, there is simply loss."
text:
> yavane tomāra ṭhāñi karaye lāgāni
> tāṅra hiṁsāya lābha nāhi, haya āra hāni
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yavane]]---your Muslim servant; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---place; [[synonyms:k:karaye]]---does; [[synonyms:l:lāgāni]]---instigation; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Him; [[synonyms:h:hiṁsāya]]---to become jealous; [[synonyms:l:lābha]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is no profit; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---rather; [[synonyms:h:hāni]]---loss.
translation: Keśava Chatrī said, "Out of jealousy your Muslim servant plots against Him. I think that you should not be very interested in Him, for there is no profit in it. Rather, there is simply loss."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.174
description: After pacifying the King in this way, Keśava Chatrī sent a brāhmaṇa messenger to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, requesting Him to leave without delay.
text:
> rājāre prabodhi' keśava brāhmaṇa pāṭhāñā
> calibāra tare prabhure pāṭhāila kahiñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājāre]]---unto the King; [[synonyms:p:prabodhi']]---pacifying; [[synonyms:k:keśava]]---of the name Keśava Chatrī; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---one //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāñā]]---sending there; [[synonyms:c:calibāra]] [[synonyms:t:tare]]---for the sake of leaving; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---unto the Lord; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāila]]---sent; [[synonyms:k:kahiñā]]---telling.
translation: After pacifying the King in this way, Keśava Chatrī sent a brāhmaṇa messenger to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, requesting Him to leave without delay.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.175
description: In private, the King inquired from Dabira Khāsa [Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī], who began to speak about the glories of the Lord.
text:
> dabira khāsere rājā puchila nibhṛte
> gosāñira mahimā teṅho lāgila kahite
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dabira]] [[synonyms:k:khāsere]]---of the name Dabira Khāsa (then the name of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī); [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:p:puchila]]---inquired; [[synonyms:n:nibhṛte]]---in privacy; [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---glories; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak.
translation: In private, the King inquired from Dabira Khāsa [Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī], who began to speak about the glories of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.176
description: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī said, "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who gave you this kingdom and whom you accept as a prophet, has taken birth in your country due to your good fortune.
text:
> ye tomāre rājya dila, ye tomāra gosāñā
> tomāra deśe tomāra bhāgye janmilā āsiñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]---that one who; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---unto you; [[synonyms:r:rājya]]---kingdom; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---the one who; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:g:gosāñā]]---prophet; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in your country; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:b:bhāgye]]---on account of your good fortune; [[synonyms:j:janmilā]]---took birth; [[synonyms:ā:āsiñā]]---coming.
translation: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī said, "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who gave you this kingdom and whom you accept as a prophet, has taken birth in your country due to your good fortune.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.177
description: "This prophet always desires your good fortune. By His grace, all your business is successful. By His blessings, you will attain victory everywhere.
text:
> tomāra maṅgala vāñche, kārya-siddhi haya
> ihāra āśīrvāde tomāra sarvatra-i jaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:m:maṅgala]]---good fortune; [[synonyms:v:vāñche]]---He desires; [[synonyms:k:kārya]]---of business; [[synonyms:s:siddhi]]---the perfection; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of Him; [[synonyms:ā:āśīrvāde]]---by the blessings; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:s:sarvatra]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---victory.
translation: "This prophet always desires your good fortune. By His grace, all your business is successful. By His blessings, you will attain victory everywhere.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.178
description: "Why are you questioning me? Better that you question your own mind. Because you are the King of the people, you are the representative of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore you can understand this better than I."
text:
> more kena pucha, tumi pucha āpana-mana
> tumi narādhipa hao viṣṇu-aṁśa sama
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto me; [[synonyms:k:kena]]---why; [[synonyms:p:pucha]]---you inquire; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:p:pucha]]---inquire; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---your own mind; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:n:nara]]-[[synonyms:a:adhipa]]---King of the people; [[synonyms:h:hao]]---you are; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁśa]] [[synonyms:s:sama]]---representative of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: "Why are you questioning me? Better that you question your own mind. Because you are the King of the people, you are the representative of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore you can understand this better than I."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.179
description: Thus Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī informed the King about his mind as a way of knowing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He assured the King that whatever occurred in his mind could be considered evidence.
text:
> tomāra citte caitanyere kaiche haya jñāna
> tomāra citte yei laya, sei ta' pramāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:c:citte]]---in your mind; [[synonyms:c:caitanyere]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaiche]]---how; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:c:citte]]---mind; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:l:laya]]---takes; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']] [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---that is evidence.
translation: Thus Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī informed the King about his mind as a way of knowing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He assured the King that whatever occurred in his mind could be considered evidence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.18
description: The final pastimes of the Lord, occurring in His last twenty-four years, are called madhya [middle] and antya [final]. All the devotees of the Lord refer to His pastimes according to these divisions.
text:
> śeṣa-līlāra 'madhya' 'antya',---dui nāma haya
> līlā-bhede vaiṣṇava saba nāma-bheda kaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlāra]]---of the //śeṣa-līlā,// or pastimes at the end; [[synonyms:m:madhya]]---the middle; [[synonyms:a:antya]]---the final; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---names; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhede]]---by the difference of pastimes; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---the devotees of the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:b:bheda]]---different names; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---say.
translation: The final pastimes of the Lord, occurring in His last twenty-four years, are called madhya [middle] and antya [final]. All the devotees of the Lord refer to His pastimes according to these divisions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.180
description: The King replied, "I consider Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to be the Supreme Personality of Godhead. There is no doubt about it."
text:
> rājā kahe, śuna, mora mane yei laya
> sākṣāt īśvara ihaṅ nāhika saṁśaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the King replied; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---mind; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---what; [[synonyms:l:laya]]---takes; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---personally; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Personality; [[synonyms:i:ihaṅ]]---He; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:s:saṁśaya]]---doubt.
translation: The King replied, "I consider Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to be the Supreme Personality of Godhead. There is no doubt about it."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.181
description: After having this conversation with Rūpa Gosvāmī, the King entered his private house. Rūpa Gosvāmī, then known as Dabira Khāsa, also returned to his residence.
text:
> eta kahi' rājā gelā nija abhyantare
> tabe dabira khāsa āilā āpanāra ghare
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---saying this; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---own; [[synonyms:a:abhyantare]]---to the private house; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:d:dabira]] [[synonyms:k:khāsa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāra]]---his own; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to the residence.
translation: After having this conversation with Rūpa Gosvāmī, the King entered his private house. Rūpa Gosvāmī, then known as Dabira Khāsa, also returned to his residence.
purport: A monarch is certainly a representative of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. As stated in the //Bhagavad-gītā, sarva-loka-maheśvaram:// the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the proprietor of all planetary systems. In each and every planet there must be some king, governmental head or executive. Such a person is supposed to be the representative of Lord Viṣṇu. On behalf of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he must see to the interests of all the people. Therefore Lord Viṣṇu, as Paramātmā, gives the king all intelligence to execute governmental affairs. Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī therefore asked the King what was in his mind concerning Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and indicated that whatever the King thought about Him was correct.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.182
description: After returning to his residence, Dabira Khāsa and his brother decided after much consideration to go see the Lord incognito.
text:
> ghare āsi' dui bhāi yukati kariñā
> prabhu dekhibāre cale veśa lukāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:ghareāsi']]---after returning home; [[synonyms:d:duibhāi]]---two brothers; [[synonyms:y:yukati]]---arguments; [[synonyms:k:kariñā]]---making; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhibāre]]---to see; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---go; [[synonyms:v:veśa]]---dress; [[synonyms:l:lukāñā]]---hiding.
translation: After returning to his residence, Dabira Khāsa and his brother decided after much consideration to go see the Lord incognito.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.183
description: Thus in the dead of night the two brothers, Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika, went to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu incognito. First they met Nityānanda Prabhu and Haridāsa Ṭhākura.
text:
> ardha-rātre dui bhāi āilā prabhu-sthāne
> prathame mililā nityānanda-haridāsa sane
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ardha]]-[[synonyms:r:rātre]]---in the dead of night; [[synonyms:d:duibhāi]]---the two brothers; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the place of Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:p:prathame]]---first; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]-[[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Lord Nityānanda and Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with.
translation: Thus in the dead of night the two brothers, Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika, went to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu incognito. First they met Nityānanda Prabhu and Haridāsa Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.184
description: Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu and Haridāsa Ṭhākura told Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu that two personalities-Śrī Rūpa and Sanātana-had come to see Him.
text:
> tāṅrā dui-jana jānāilā prabhura gocare
> rūpa, sākara-mallika āilā tomā' dekhibāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅrā]]---they; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons; [[synonyms:j:jānāilā]]---informed; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gocare]]---in the presence; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:sākara]]-[[synonyms:m:mallika]]---and Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---have come; [[synonyms:t:tomā']]---You; [[synonyms:d:dekhibāre]]---to see.
translation: Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu and Haridāsa Ṭhākura told Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu that two personalities-Śrī Rūpa and Sanātana-had come to see Him.
purport: Sākara Mallika was the name of Sanātana Gosvāmī, and Dabira Khāsa was the name of Rūpa Gosvāmī. They were recognized by these names in the service of the Muslim King; therefore these are Muslim names. As officials, the brothers adopted all kinds of Muslim customs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.185
description: In great humility, both brothers took bunches of straw between their teeth and, each binding a cloth around his neck, fell down like rods before the Lord.
text:
> dui guccha tṛṇa duṅhe daśane dhariñā
> gale vastra bāndhi' paḍe daṇḍavat hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:g:guccha]]---bunches; [[synonyms:t:tṛṇa]]---of straw; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:d:daśane]]---in the teeth; [[synonyms:d:dhariñā]]---catching; [[synonyms:g:gale]]---on the neck; [[synonyms:v:vastra]]---cloth; [[synonyms:b:bāndhi']]---binding; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fall; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]]---like rods; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming.
translation: In great humility, both brothers took bunches of straw between their teeth and, each binding a cloth around his neck, fell down like rods before the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.186
description: Upon seeing Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the two brothers were overwhelmed with joy, and out of humility they began to cry. Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked them to get up and assured them of all good fortune.
text:
> dainya rodana kare, ānande vihvala
> prabhu kahe,---uṭha, uṭha, ha-ila maṅgala
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dainya]]---humility; [[synonyms:r:rodana]]---crying; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:u:uṭha]] [[synonyms:u:uṭha]]---stand up, stand up; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]] [[synonyms:m:maṅgala]]---all auspiciousness unto you.
translation: Upon seeing Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the two brothers were overwhelmed with joy, and out of humility they began to cry. Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked them to get up and assured them of all good fortune.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.187
description: The two brothers got up, and again taking straw between their teeth, they humbly offered their prayers with folded hands.
text:
> uṭhi' dui bhāi tabe dante tṛṇa dhari'
> dainya kari' stuti kare karayoḍa kari
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---standing up; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---brothers; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:d:dante]]---in the teeth; [[synonyms:t:tṛṇa]]---straw; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---holding; [[synonyms:d:dainyakari']]---in all humbleness; [[synonyms:s:stutikare]]---offer prayers; [[synonyms:k:kara]]-[[synonyms:y:yoḍa]]---folded hands; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making.
translation: The two brothers got up, and again taking straw between their teeth, they humbly offered their prayers with folded hands.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.188
description: "All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the most merciful savior of the fallen souls! All glories to the Supreme Personality!
text:
> jaya jaya śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya dayā-maya
> patita-pāvana jaya, jaya mahāśaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jayajaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---the most merciful; [[synonyms:p:patita]]-[[synonyms:p:pāvana]]---the savior of the fallen souls; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---glories; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---glories; [[synonyms:m:mahāśaya]]---to the great personality.
translation: "All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the most merciful savior of the fallen souls! All glories to the Supreme Personality!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.189
description: "Sir, we belong to the lowest class of men, and our associates and employment are also of the lowest type. Therefore we cannot introduce ourselves to You. We feel very much ashamed, standing here before You.
text:
> nīca-jāti, nīca-saṅgī, kari nīca kāja
> tomāra agrete prabhu kahite vāsi lāja
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nīca]]-[[synonyms:j:jāti]]---classified among the fallen; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgī]]---associated with fallen souls; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---we perform; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]---abominable; [[synonyms:k:kāja]]---work; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of You; [[synonyms:a:agrete]]---in front; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---O Lord; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to say; [[synonyms:v:vāsi]]---we feel; [[synonyms:l:lāja]]---ashamed.
translation: "Sir, we belong to the lowest class of men, and our associates and employment are also of the lowest type. Therefore we cannot introduce ourselves to You. We feel very much ashamed, standing here before You.
purport: Although the two brothers, Rūpa and Sanātana (at that time Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika), presented themselves as being born in a low family, they nonetheless belonged to a most respectable //brāhmaṇa// family that was originally from Karṇāta. Thus they actually belonged to the //brāhmaṇa// caste. Unfortunately, because of being associated with the Muslim governmental service, their customs and behavior resembled those of the Muslims. Therefore they presented themselves as //nīca-jāti.// The word //jāti// means birth. According to //śāstra,// there are three kinds of birth. The first birth is from the womb of the mother, the second birth is the acceptance of the reformatory method, and the third birth is acceptance by the spiritual master (initiation). One becomes abominable by adopting an abominable profession or by associating with people who are naturally abominable. Rūpa and Sanātana, as Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika, associated with Muslims, who were naturally opposed to brahminical culture and cow protection. In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (Seventh Canto) it is stated that every person belongs to a certain classification. A person is identifiable by the special symptoms mentioned in the //śāstras.// By one's symptoms, one is known to belong to a certain caste. Both Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika belonged to the //brāhmaṇa// caste, but because they were employed by Muslims, their original habits degenerated into those of the Muslim community. Since the symptoms of brahminical culture were almost nil, they identified themselves with the lowest caste. In the //Bhakti-ratnākara// it is clearly stated that because Sākara Mallika and Dabira Khāsa associated with lower-class men, they introduced themselves as belonging to the lower classes. Actually, however, they had been born in respectable //brāhmaṇa// families.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.19
description: For six years of the last twenty-four, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu traveled all over India from Jagannātha Purī to Bengal and from Cape Comorin to Vṛndāvana.

> tāra madhye chaya vatsara---gamanāgamana
> nīlācala-gauḍa-setubandha-vṛndāvana

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.190
description: "Dear Lord, let us inform you that no one is more sinful than us, nor is there any offender like us. Even if we wanted to mention our sinful activities, we would immediately become ashamed. And what to speak of giving them up!"
text:
> mat-tulyo nāsti pāpātmā
> nāparādhī ca kaścana
> parihāre 'pi lajjā me
> kiṁ bruve puruṣottama

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.193
description: "The brothers Jagāi and Mādhāi belonged to the brāhmaṇa caste, and their residence was in the holy place of Navadvīpa. They never served low-class persons, nor were they instruments to abominable activities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.194
description: "Jagāi and Mādhāi had but one fault—they were addicted to sinful activity. However, volumes of sinful activity can be burned to ashes simply by a dim reflection of the chanting of Your holy name.
text:
> sabe eka doṣa tāra, haya pāpācāra
> pāpa-rāśi dahe nāmābhāsei tomāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---in all; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one only; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---fault; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of them; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---they are; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācāra]]---attached to sinful activities; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]-[[synonyms:r:rāśi]]---volumes of sinful activities; [[synonyms:d:dahe]]---become burned; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāsei]]---simply by the dim reflection of chanting the holy name; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of Your Lordship.
translation: "Jagāi and Mādhāi had but one fault---they were addicted to sinful activity. However, volumes of sinful activity can be burned to ashes simply by a dim reflection of the chanting of Your holy name.
purport: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and Sanātana Gosvāmī presented themselves as being lower than the two brothers Jagāi and Mādhāi, who were delivered by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. When Rūpa and Sanātana compared themselves to Jagāi and Mādhāi, they found themselves inferior because the Lord had no trouble in delivering two drunken brothers. This was so because, despite the fact that they were addicted to sinful activity, in other ways their life was brilliant. They belonged to the //brāhmaṇa// caste of Navadvīpa, and such //brāhmaṇas// were pious by nature. Although they had been addicted to some sinful activities due to bad association, those unwanted things could vanish simply because of the chanting of the holy name of the Lord. Another point for Jagāi and Mādhāi was that, as members of a //brāhmaṇa// family, they did not accept service under anyone. The //śāstras// strictly forbid a //brāhmaṇa// to accept service under anyone. The idea is that by accepting a master, one accepts the occupation of a dog. In other words, a dog cannot thrive without having a master, and for the sake of pleasing the master, dogs offend many people. They bark at innocent people just to please the master. Similarly, when one is a servant, he has to perform abominable activities according to the orders of the master. Therefore, when Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika compared their position to that of Jagāi and Mādhāi, they found Jagāi and Mādhāi's position far better. Jagāi and Mādhāi never accepted the service of a low-class person; nor were they forced to execute abominable activities under the order of a low-class master. Jagāi and Mādhāi chanted the name of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by way of blasphemy, but because they simply chanted His name, they immediately became free from the reactions of sinful activities. Thus later they were saved.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.195

translation: "Jagāi and Mādhāi uttered Your holy name by way of blaspheming You. Fortunately, that holy name became the cause of their deliverance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.196

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.197
description: "Actually we belong to the caste of meat-eaters because we are servants of meat-eaters. Indeed, our activities are exactly like those of the meat-eaters. Because we always associate with such people, we are inimical toward the cows and brāhmaṇas."
text:
> mleccha-jāti, mleccha-sevī, kari mleccha-karma
> go-brāhmaṇa-drohi-saṅge āmāra saṅgama
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:j:jāti]]---belonging to the meat-eater caste; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:s:sevī]]---servants of the meat-eaters; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---we execute; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:k:karma]]---the work of meat-eaters; [[synonyms:g:go]]---cows; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---//brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:d:drohi]]---those inimical to; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---our; [[synonyms:s:saṅgama]]---association.
translation: "Actually we belong to the caste of meat-eaters because we are servants of meat-eaters. Indeed, our activities are exactly like those of the meat-eaters. Because we always associate with such people, we are inimical toward the cows and brāhmaṇas."
purport: There are two kinds of meat-eaters-one who is born in a family of meat-eaters and one who has learned to associate with meat-eaters. From Śrīla Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmīs (formerly Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika) we can learn how one attains the character of a meat-eater simply by associating with meat-eaters. At the present moment in India the presidential offices are occupied by many so-called //brāhmaṇas,// but the state maintains slaughterhouses for killing cows and makes propaganda against Vedic civilization. The first principle of Vedic civilization is the avoidance of meat-eating and intoxication. Presently in India, intoxication and meat-eating are encouraged, and the so-called learned //brāhmaṇas// presiding over this state of affairs have certainly become degraded according to the standard given herein by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and Sanātana Gosvāmī. These so-called //brāhmaṇas// give sanction to slaughterhouses for the sake of a fat salary, and they do not protest these abominable activities. By deprecating the principles of Vedic civilization and supporting cow-killing, they are immediately degraded to the platform of //mlecchas// and //yavanas. A mleccha// is a meat-eater, and a //yavana// is one who has deviated from Vedic culture. Unfortunately, such //mlecchas// and //yavanas// are in executive power. How, then, can there be peace and prosperity in the state? The king or the president must be the representative of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. When Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira accepted the rule of Bhārata-varṣa (formerly this entire planet, including all the seas and land), he took sanction from authorities like Bhīṣmadeva and Lord Kṛṣṇa. He thus ruled the entire world according to religious principles. At the present moment, however, heads of state do not care for religious principles. If irreligious people vote on an issue, even though it be against the principles of the //śāstras,// the bills will be passed. The president and heads of state become sinful by agreeing to such abominable activities. Sanātana and Rūpa Gosvāmīs pleaded guilty to such activities; they therefore classified themselves among the //mlecchas,// although born in a //brāhmaṇa// family.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.198
description: The two brothers, Sākara Mallika and Dabira Khāsa, very humbly submitted that due to their abominable activities they were now bound by the neck and hands and had been thrown into a ditch filled with abominable stoollike objects of material sense enjoyment.
text:
> mora karma, mora hāte-galāya bāndhiyā
> ku-viṣaya-viṣṭhā-garte diyāche phelāiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mora]]---our; [[synonyms:k:karma]]---activities; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---our; [[synonyms:h:hāte]]---on the hand; [[synonyms:g:galāya]]---on the neck; [[synonyms:b:bāndhiyā]]---binding; [[synonyms:k:ku]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]---of abominable objects of sense gratification; [[synonyms:v:viṣṭhā]]---of the stool; [[synonyms:g:garte]]---in the ditch; [[synonyms:d:diyāche]] [[synonyms:p:phelāiyā]]---have been thrown.
translation: The two brothers, Sākara Mallika and Dabira Khāsa, very humbly submitted that due to their abominable activities they were now bound by the neck and hands and had been thrown into a ditch filled with abominable stoollike objects of material sense enjoyment.
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura has explained //ku-viṣaya garta// as follows: "Because of the activities of the senses, we become subjected to many sense gratificatory processes and are thus entangled by the laws of material nature. This entanglement is called //viṣaya.// When the sense gratificatory processes are executed by pious activity, they are called //su-viṣaya.// The word //su// means 'good,' and //viṣaya// means 'sense objects.' When the sense gratificatory activities are performed under sinful conditions, they are called //ku-viṣaya,// bad sense enjoyment. In either case, either //ku-viṣaya// or //su-viṣaya,// these are material activities. As such, they are compared to stool. In other words, such things are to be avoided. To become free from //su-viṣaya// and //ku-viṣaya,// one must engage himself in the transcendental loving service of Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The activities of devotional service are free from the contamination of material qualities. Therefore, to be free from the reactions of //su-viṣaya// and //ku-viṣaya,// one must take to Kṛṣṇa consciousness. In that way, one will save himself from contamination." In this connection, Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura has sung:

> karma-kāṇḍa, jñāna-kāṇḍa, kevala viṣera bhāṇḍa
> amṛta baliyā yeba khāya
> nānā yoni sadā phire, kadarya bhakṣaṇa kare
> tāra janma adhaḥ-pāte yāya

Su-viṣaya and //ku-viṣaya// both fall under the category of //karma-kāṇḍa.// There is another //kāṇḍa// (platform of activity), called //jñāna-kāṇḍa,// or philosophical speculation about the effects of //ku-viṣaya// and //su-viṣaya// with the intention to find out the means of deliverance from material entanglement. On the platform of //jñāna-kāṇḍa,// one may give up the objects of //ku-viṣaya// and //su-viṣaya.// But that is not the perfection of life. Perfection is transcendental to both //jñāna-kāṇḍa// and //karma-kāṇḍa;// it is on the platform of devotional service. If we do not take to devotional service in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, we have to remain within this material world and endure the repetition of birth and death due to the effects of //jñāna-kāṇḍa// and //karma-kāṇḍa.// Therefore Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says:

> nānā yoni sadā phire, kadarya bhakṣaṇa kare
> tāra janma adhaḥ-pāte yāya

"One travels throughout various species of life and eats all kinds of nonsense. Thus he spoils his existence." A man in material existence and attached to //ku-viṣaya// or //su-viṣaya// is in the same position as that of a worm in stool. After all, whether it be moist or dry, stool is stool. Similarly, material activities may be either pious or impious, but because they are all material, they are compared to stool. Worms cannot get out of stool by their own endeavor; similarly, those who are overly attached to material existence cannot get out of materialism and suddenly become Kṛṣṇa conscious. Attachment is there. As explained by Prahlāda Mahārāja in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:7:5:30|(7.5.30)]]:

> matir na kṛṣṇe parataḥ svato vā
> mitho 'bhipadyeta gṛha-vratānām
> adānta-gobhir viśatāṁ tamisraṁ
> punaḥ-punaś-carvita-carvaṇānām

"Those who have made up their minds to remain in this material world and enjoy sense gratification cannot become Kṛṣṇa conscious. Because of their attachment to material activity, they cannot attain liberation, either by the instructions of superior persons or by their own endeavor or by passing resolutions in big conferences. Because their senses are uncontrolled, they gradually descend to the darkest regions of material existence to repeat the same process of birth and death in desirable or undesirable species of life."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.199

translation: "No one within the three worlds is sufficiently powerful to deliver us. You are the only savior of the fallen souls; therefore there is no one but You.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.2
description: I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda, who are like the sun and moon. They have arisen simultaneously on the horizon of Gauḍa to dissipate the darkness of ignorance and thus wonderfully bestow benediction upon all.

> nityānandau sahoditau

translation: I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda, who are like the sun and moon. They have arisen simultaneously on the horizon of Gauḍa to dissipate the darkness of ignorance and thus wonderfully bestow benediction upon all.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.20

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.200
description: "If You simply deliver us by Your transcendental strength, then certainly Your name will be known as Patita-pāvana, the savior of the fallen souls.

> 'patita-pāvana' nāma tabe se saphala

translation: "If You simply deliver us by Your transcendental strength, then certainly Your name will be known as Patita-pāvana, the savior of the fallen souls.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.201
description: "Let us speak one word that is very true. Plainly hear us, O merciful one. There is no other object of mercy within the three worlds but us.

> satya eka bāta kahoṅ, śuna, dayā-maya
> mo-vinu dayāra pātra jagate nā haya

translation: "Let us speak one word that is very true. Plainly hear us, O merciful one. There is no other object of mercy within the three worlds but us.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.202

translation: "We are the most fallen; therefore by showing us Your mercy, Your mercy is most successful. Let the power of Your mercy be exhibited throughout the entire universe!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.203

> na mṛṣā paramārtham eva me

translation: “ 'Let us submit one piece of information before You, dear Lord. It is not at all false but is full of meaning. It is this: If You are not merciful upon us, then it will be very, very difficult to find more suitable candidates for Your mercy.'
purport: This verse is from the //Stotra-ratna// (47), by Śrī Yāmunācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.204

> āpane ayogya dekhi' mane pāṅ kṣobha

translation: "We are very depressed at being unfit candidates for Your mercy. Yet since we have heard of Your transcendental qualities, we are very much attracted to You.

translation: "Indeed, we are like a dwarf who wants to capture the moon. Although we are completely unfit, a desire to receive Your mercy is awakening within our minds.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.206
description: " 'By serving You constantly, one is freed from all material desires and is completely pacified. When shall I engage as Your permanent eternal servant and always feel joyful to have such a fitting master?' "
text:
> bhavantam evānucaran nirantaraḥ
> praśānta-niḥśeṣa-mano-rathāntaraḥ
> kadāham aikāntika-nitya-kiṅkaraḥ
> praharṣayiṣyāmi sanātha-jīvitam
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhavantam]]---You; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:anucaran]]---serving; [[synonyms:n:nirantaraḥ]]---always; [[synonyms:p:praśānta]]---pacified; [[synonyms:n:niḥśeṣa]]---all; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:r:ratha]]---desires; [[synonyms:a:antaraḥ]]---other; [[synonyms:k:kadā]]---when; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:a:aikāntika]]---exclusive; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---eternal; [[synonyms:k:kiṅkaraḥ]]---servant; [[synonyms:p:praharṣayiṣyāmi]]---I shall become joyful; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:n:nātha]]---with a fitting master; [[synonyms:j:jīvitam]]---living.
translation: “ 'By serving You constantly, one is freed from all material desires and is completely pacified. When shall I engage as Your permanent eternal servant and always feel joyful to have such a fitting master?' "
purport: In His teachings to Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has declared every living entity to be an eternal servitor of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is the constitutional position of all living entities. Just as a dog or servant is very satisfied to get a competent, perfect master, or as a child is completely satisfied to possess a competent father, so the living entity is satisfied by completely engaging in the service of the Supreme Lord. He thereby knows that he has a competent master to save him from all kinds of danger. Unless the living entity comes to the guaranteed protection of the Supreme Lord, He is full of anxiety. This life of anxiety is called material existence. To be completely satisfied and devoid of anxiety, one must come to the position of eternally rendering service to the Supreme Lord. This verse is also from the //Stotra-ratna// (43) by Śrī Yāmunācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.207
description: After hearing the prayer of Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My dear Dabira Khāsa, you two brothers are My old servants.
text:
> śuni' mahāprabhu kahe,---śuna, dabira-khāsa
> tumi dui bhāi---mora purātana dāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:d:dabirakhāsa]]---Dabira Khāsa; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---two brothers; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:p:purātana]]---old; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---servants.
translation: After hearing the prayer of Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My dear Dabira Khāsa, you two brothers are My old servants.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.208
description: "My dear Sākara Mallika, from this day your names will be changed to Śrīla Rūpa and Śrīla Sanātana. Now please abandon your humility, for My heart is breaking to see you so humble.
text:
> āji haite duṅhāra nāma 'rūpa' 'sanātana'
> dainya chāḍa, tomāra dainye phāṭe mora mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ājihaite]]---from this day; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]]---of both of you; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---these names; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrī Rūpa; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---Śrī Sanātana; [[synonyms:d:dainyachāḍa]]---give up your humility; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:d:dainye]]---humility; [[synonyms:p:phāṭe]]---breaks; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---heart.
translation: "My dear Sākara Mallika, from this day your names will be changed to Śrīla Rūpa and Śrīla Sanātana. Now please abandon your humility, for My heart is breaking to see you so humble.
purport:
Actually this is Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's initiation of Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika. They approached the Lord with all humility, and the Lord accepted them as old servants, as eternal servants, and He changed their names. It is to be understood from this that it is essential for a disciple to change his name after initiation.

> śaṅkha-cakrādy-ūrdhva-puṇḍra-
> dhāraṇādy-ātma-lakṣaṇam
> tan nāma-karaṇaṁ caiva
> vaiṣṇavatvam ihocyate

"After initiation, the disciple's name must be changed to indicate that he is a servant of Lord Viṣṇu. The disciple should also immediately begin marking his body with //tilaka// (//ūrdhva-puṇḍra//), especially his forehead. These are spiritual marks, symptoms of a perfect Vaiṣṇava." This is a verse from the //Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa.// A member of the //sahajiyā-sampradāya// does not change his name; therefore he cannot be accepted as a Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava. If a person does not change his name after initiation, it is to be understood that he will continue in his bodily conception of life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.218
description: When all of the devotees saw the mercy of the Lord upon the two brothers, they were very much gladdened, and they began to chant the holy name of the Lord, "Hari! Hari!"
text:
> dui jane prabhura kṛpā dekhi' bhakta-gaṇe
> 'hari' 'hari' bale sabe ānandita-mane
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:duijane]]---unto the two persons; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---the mercy; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:h:harihari]]---the holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---chant; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---cheerful; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind.
translation: When all of the devotees saw the mercy of the Lord upon the two brothers, they were very much gladdened, and they began to chant the holy name of the Lord, "Hari! Hari!"
purport: Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says, //chāḍiyā vaiṣṇava sevā nistāra pāyeche kebā:// unless one serves a Vaiṣṇava, he cannot be delivered. The spiritual master initiates the disciple to deliver him, and if the disciple executes the order of the spiritual master and does not offend other Vaiṣṇavas, his path is clear. Consequently Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested all the Vaiṣṇavas present to show mercy toward the two brothers, Rūpa and Sanātana, who had just been initiated by the Lord. When a Vaiṣṇava sees that another Vaiṣṇava is a recipient of the Lord's mercy, he becomes very happy. Vaiṣṇavas are not envious. If a Vaiṣṇava, by the mercy of the Lord, is empowered by Him to distribute the Lord's holy name all over the world, other Vaiṣṇavas become very joyful---that is, if they are truly Vaiṣṇavas. One who is envious of the success of a Vaiṣṇava is certainly not a Vaiṣṇava himself, but an ordinary mundane man. Envy and jealousy are manifested by mundane people, not by Vaiṣṇavas. Why should a Vaiṣṇava be envious of another Vaiṣṇava who is successful in spreading the holy name of the Lord? An actual Vaiṣṇava is very pleased to accept another Vaiṣṇava who is bestowing the Lord's mercy. A mundane person in the dress of a Vaiṣṇava should not be respected but rejected. This is enjoined in the //śāstra// (//upekṣā//). The word //upekṣā// means neglect. One should neglect an envious person. A preacher's duty is to love the Supreme Personality of Godhead, make friendships with Vaiṣṇavas, show mercy to the innocent and reject or neglect those who are envious or jealous. There are many jealous people in the dress of Vaiṣṇavas in this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, and they should be completely neglected. There is no need to serve a jealous person who is in the dress of a Vaiṣṇava. When Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says //chāḍiyā vaiṣṇava sevā nistāra payeche kebā,// he is indicating an actual Vaiṣṇava, not an envious or jealous person in the dress of a Vaiṣṇava.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.219
description: All the Vaiṣṇava associates of the Lord were present, including Nityānanda, Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Mukunda, Jagadānanda, Murāri and Vakreśvara.
text:
> nityānanda, haridāsa, śrīvāsa, gadādhara
> mukunda, jagadānanda, murāri, vakreśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]---Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:g:gadādhara]]---Gadādhara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:j:jagadānanda]]---Jagadānanda; [[synonyms:m:murāri]]---Murāri; [[synonyms:v:vakreśvara]]---Vakreśvara.
translation: All the Vaiṣṇava associates of the Lord were present, including Nityānanda, Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Mukunda, Jagadānanda, Murāri and Vakreśvara.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.22
description: For eighteen continuous years, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained at Jagannātha Purī and, through His personal behavior, instructed all living entities in the mode of devotional service.
text:
> aṣṭādaśa-varṣa kevala nīlācale sthiti
> āpani ācari' jīve śikhāilā bhakti
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aṣṭādaśa]]-[[synonyms:v:varṣa]]---for eighteen years; [[synonyms:k:kevala]]---only; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---in Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---staying; [[synonyms:ā:āpani]]---personally; [[synonyms:ā:ācari']]---behaving; [[synonyms:j:jīve]]---unto the living entities; [[synonyms:ś:śikhāilā]]---instructed; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service.
translation: For eighteen continuous years, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained at Jagannātha Purī and, through His personal behavior, instructed all living entities in the mode of devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.220
description: In accordance with the instructions of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the two brothers, Rūpa and Sanātana, immediately touched the lotus feet of these Vaiṣṇavas, who all became very happy and congratulated the two brothers for having received the mercy of the Lord.
text:
> sabāra caraṇe dhari, paḍe dui bhāi
> sabe bale,---dhanya tumi, pāile gosāñi
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---the lotus feet; [[synonyms:d:dhari]]---touching; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fall down; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---the two brothers; [[synonyms:s:sabebale]]---all the Vaiṣṇavas say; [[synonyms:d:dhanyatumi]]---you are so fortunate; [[synonyms:p:pāilegosāñi]]---you have gotten the shelter of the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: In accordance with the instructions of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the two brothers, Rūpa and Sanātana, immediately touched the lotus feet of these Vaiṣṇavas, who all became very happy and congratulated the two brothers for having received the mercy of the Lord.
purport: This behavior is indicative of real Vaiṣṇavas. When they saw that Rūpa and Sanātana were fortunate enough to receive the mercy of the Lord, they were so pleased that they all congratulated the two brothers. A jealous person in the dress of a Vaiṣṇava is not at all happy to see the success of another Vaiṣṇava in receiving the Lord's mercy. Unfortunately in this Age of Kali there are many mundane persons in the dress of Vaiṣṇavas, and Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has described them as disciples of Kali. He says, //kali-celā.// He indicates that there is another Vaiṣṇava, a pseudoVaiṣṇava with //tilaka// on his nose and //kaṇṭhī// beads around his neck. Such a pseudoVaiṣṇava associates with money and women and is jealous of successful Vaiṣṇavas. Although passing for a Vaiṣṇava, his only business is earning money in the dress of a Vaiṣṇava. Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura therefore says that such a pseudoVaiṣṇava is not a Vaiṣṇava at all but a disciple of Kali-yuga. A disciple of Kali cannot become an //ācārya// by the decision of some high court. Mundane votes have no jurisdiction to elect a Vaiṣṇava //ācārya.// A Vaiṣṇava //ācārya// is self-effulgent, and there is no need for any court judgment. A false //ācārya// may try to override a Vaiṣṇava by a high-court decision, but Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that he is nothing but a disciple of Kali-yuga.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.221
description: After begging the permission of all the Vaiṣṇavas present, the two brothers, at the time of their departure, humbly submitted something at the lotus feet of the Lord.
text:
> sabā-pāśa ājñā māgi' calana-samaya
> prabhu-pade kahe kichu kariyā vinaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all of them; [[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---from; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:m:māgi']]---taking; [[synonyms:c:calana]]-[[synonyms:s:samaya]]---at the time of departure; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---say; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---doing; [[synonyms:v:vinaya]]---submission.
translation: After begging the permission of all the Vaiṣṇavas present, the two brothers, at the time of their departure, humbly submitted something at the lotus feet of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.222
description: They said, "Dear Lord, although the King of Bengal, Nawab Hussain Shah, is very respectful toward You, You have no other business here. Kindly depart from this place.
text:
> ihāṅ haite cala, prabhu, ihāṅ nāhi kāya
> yadyapi tomāre bhakti kare gauḍa-rāja
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from this place; [[synonyms:c:cala]]---please depart; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---dear Lord; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---in this place; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:k:kāya]]---there is no other business; [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---unto You; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---respect; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---shows; [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]-[[synonyms:r:rāja]]---the King of Bengal.
translation: They said, "Dear Lord, although the King of Bengal, Nawab Hussain Shah, is very respectful toward You, You have no other business here. Kindly depart from this place.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.223
description: "Although the King is respectful toward You, he still belongs to the yavana class and should not be believed. We think that there is no need for such a great crowd to accompany You on Your pilgrimage to Vṛndāvana.
text:
> tathāpi yavana jāti, nā kari pratīti
> tīrtha-yātrāya eta saṅghaṭṭa bhāla nahe rīti
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:y:yavanajāti]]---by caste a Muslim; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---do; [[synonyms:p:pratīti]]---confidence; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrāya]]---in going for a pilgrimage; [[synonyms:e:eta]]---so; [[synonyms:s:saṅghaṭṭa]]---crowd; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]---good; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:r:rīti]]---etiquette.
translation: "Although the King is respectful toward You, he still belongs to the yavana class and should not be believed. We think that there is no need for such a great crowd to accompany You on Your pilgrimage to Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.224
description: "Dear Lord, You are going to Vṛndāvana with hundreds and thousands of people following You, and this is not a fitting way to go on a pilgrimage."
text:
> yāra saṅge cale ei loka lakṣa-koṭi
> vṛndāvana-yātrāra e nahe paripāṭī
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the company; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---follow; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---hundreds and thousands; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrāra]]---of going to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:e:e]]---this; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:p:paripāṭī]]---method.
translation: "Dear Lord, You are going to Vṛndāvana with hundreds and thousands of people following You, and this is not a fitting way to go on a pilgrimage."
purport: Sometimes, for business purposes, large crowds of men are taken to different places of pilgrimage, and money is collected from them. That is a very lucrative business, but Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmīs, expressing their opinion in the presence of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, disapproved of such crowded pilgrimages. Actually when Lord Caitanya visited Vṛndāvana, He visited it alone and accepted a servant only at His devotees' request. He never visited Vṛndāvana with crowds of people for a commercial purpose.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.225
description: Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself, the Supreme Lord, and was therefore not at all fearful, He still acted like a human being to teach neophytes how to act.
text:
> yadyapi vastutaḥ prabhura kichu nāhi bhaya
> tathāpi laukika-līlā, loka-ceṣṭā-maya
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:v:vastutaḥ]]---in fact; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---any; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:l:laukika]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---general pastimes; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:c:ceṣṭā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---consisting of popular behavior.
translation: Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself, the Supreme Lord, and was therefore not at all fearful, He still acted like a human being to teach neophytes how to act.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.226
description: Having spoken thus, the two brothers offered prayers to the lotus feet of the Lord and returned to their homes. Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu then desired to leave that village.
text:
> eta bali' caraṇa vandi' gelā dui-jana
> prabhura sei grāma haite calite haila mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandi']]---offering prayers to the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went back; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---the two brothers; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:g:grāma]]---village; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:c:calite]]---to go; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: Having spoken thus, the two brothers offered prayers to the lotus feet of the Lord and returned to their homes. Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu then desired to leave that village.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.227
description: In the morning, the Lord left and went to a place known as Kānāi Nāṭaśālā. While there, He saw may pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> prāte cali' āilā prabhu 'kānāira nāṭaśālā'
> dekhila sakala tāhāṅ kṛṣṇa-caritra-līlā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prāte]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---departing; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kānāira]] [[synonyms:n:nāṭaśālā]]---to the place of the name Kānāi Nāṭaśālā; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---saw; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caritra]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: In the morning, the Lord left and went to a place known as Kānāi Nāṭaśālā. While there, He saw may pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
purport: In those days in Bengal there were many places known as Kānāi Nāṭaśālā, where pictures of the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa were kept. People used to go there to see them. This is called //kṛṣṇa-caritra-līlā.// In Bengal there are still many places called //hari-sabhā,// which indicates a place where local people gather to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// and discuss the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. The word //kānāi// means "Lord Kṛṣṇa's," and //nāṭaśālā// indicates a place where pastimes are demonstrated. So those places which at the present moment are called //hari-sabhā// may previously have been known as Kānāi Nāṭaśālā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.228
description: That night the Lord considered Sanātana Gosvāmī's proposal that He should not go to Vṛndāvana followed by so many people.
text:
> sei rātre prabhu tāhāṅ cinte mane mana
> saṅge saṅghaṭṭa bhāla nahe, kaila sanātana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:r:rātre]]---that night; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:c:cinte]]---thinks; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---within His mind; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Him; [[synonyms:s:saṅghaṭṭa]]---crowds of men; [[synonyms:b:bhālanahe]]---is not good; [[synonyms:k:kailasanātana]]---Sanātana has so spoken.
translation: That night the Lord considered Sanātana Gosvāmī's proposal that He should not go to Vṛndāvana followed by so many people.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.229
description: The Lord thought, "If I go to Mathurā with such crowds behind Me, it would not be a very happy situation, for the atmosphere would be disturbed."
text:
> mathurā yāiba āmi eta loka saṅge
> kichu sukha nā pāiba, habe rasa-bhaṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mathurā]]---the holy place of the name Mathurā; [[synonyms:y:yāiba]]---shall go; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:e:eta]]---so many; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---any; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāiba]]---I shall get; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṅge]]---a disturbance in the atmosphere.
translation: The Lord thought, "If I go to Mathurā with such crowds behind Me, it would not be a very happy situation, for the atmosphere would be disturbed."
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu confirms that visiting a holy place like Vṛndāvana with so many people is simply disturbing. He would not find the happiness He desired by visiting such holy places in that way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.23
description: Of these eighteen years at Jagannātha Purī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu spent six years with His many devotees. By chanting and dancing, He introduced the loving service of the Lord.
text:
> tāra madhye chaya vatsara bhakta-gaṇa-saṅge
> prema-bhakti pravartāilā nṛtya-gīta-raṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that period; [[synonyms:c:chayavatsara]]---for six years; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with all the devotees; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---the loving service of the Lord; [[synonyms:p:pravartāilā]]---introduced; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---in the matter of chanting and dancing.
translation: Of these eighteen years at Jagannātha Purī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu spent six years with His many devotees. By chanting and dancing, He introduced the loving service of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.230
description: The Lord concluded that He would go alone to Vṛndāvana or, at most, would take only one person as His companion. In that way, going to Vṛndāvana would be very pleasant.
text:
> ekākī yāiba, kimvā saṅge eka jana
> tabe se śobhaye vṛndāvanere gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ekākī]]---alone; [[synonyms:y:yāiba]]---I shall go; [[synonyms:k:kimvā]]---or; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:j:jana]]---person; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then only; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:ś:śobhaye]]---becomes beautiful; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvanere]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going.
translation: The Lord concluded that He would go alone to Vṛndāvana or, at most, would take only one person as His companion. In that way, going to Vṛndāvana would be very pleasant.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.231
description: Thinking like this, the Lord took His morning bath in the Ganges and started for Nīlācala, saying "I shall go there."
text:
> eta cinti prātaḥ-kāle gaṅgā-snāna kari'
> 'nīlācale yāba' bali' calilā gaurahari
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:etacinti]]---thus thinking; [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing in the Ganges; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---performing; [[synonyms:n:nīlācaleyāba]]---I shall go to Nīlācala (Jagannātha Purī); [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---started; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Thinking like this, the Lord took His morning bath in the Ganges and started for Nīlācala, saying "I shall go there."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.232
description: Walking and walking, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at Śāntipura and remained at the house of Advaita Ācārya for five to seven days.
text:
> ei mata cali' cali' āilā śāntipure
> dina pāṅca-sāta rahilā ācāryera ghare
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:c:cali']] [[synonyms:c:cali']]---walking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:ś:śāntipure]]---to Śāntipura; [[synonyms:d:dina]] [[synonyms:p:pāṅca]]-[[synonyms:s:sāta]]---five or seven days; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryeraghare]]---at the house of Advaita Ācārya.
translation: Walking and walking, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at Śāntipura and remained at the house of Advaita Ācārya for five to seven days.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.233
description: Taking this opportunity, Śrī Advaita Ācārya Prabhu sent for mother Śacīdevī, and she remained at His house for seven days to prepare the meals for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> śacī-devī āni' tāṅre kaila namaskāra
> sāta dina tāṅra ṭhāñi bhikṣā-vyavahāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:d:devī]]---mother Śacīdevī; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---calling her; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:s:sātadina]]---seven days; [[synonyms:t:tāṅraṭhāñi]]---from Śacīdevī; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]-[[synonyms:v:vyavahāra]]---accepting meals.
translation: Taking this opportunity, Śrī Advaita Ācārya Prabhu sent for mother Śacīdevī, and she remained at His house for seven days to prepare the meals for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.234
description: Taking permission from His mother, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu started for Jagannātha Purī. When the devotees followed Him, He humbly begged them to remain and bade them all farewell.
text:
> tāṅra ājñā lañā punaḥ karilā gamane
> vinaya kariyā vidāya dila bhakta-gaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking the permission of mother Śacīdevī; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gamane]]---starting; [[synonyms:v:vinayakariyā]]---by submitting pleasing words; [[synonyms:v:vidāya]]---farewell; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---to all the devotees.
translation: Taking permission from His mother, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu started for Jagannātha Purī. When the devotees followed Him, He humbly begged them to remain and bade them all farewell.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.235
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, although requesting all the devotees to go back, allowed two people to follow Him. He requested all the devotees to come to Jagannātha Purī and meet Him during the car festival.
text:
> janā dui saṅge āmi yāba nīlācale
> āmāre milibā āsi' ratha-yātrā-kāle
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:janā]]---persons; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---shall go; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āmāre]]---Me; [[synonyms:m:milibā]]---will meet; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming there; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---during the time of the car festival.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, although requesting all the devotees to go back, allowed two people to follow Him. He requested all the devotees to come to Jagannātha Purī and meet Him during the car festival.
