title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.91
description: This is the first synopsis: After accepting the sannyāsa order, Caitanya Mahāprabhu proceeded toward Vṛndāvana.
text:
> prathama sūtra prabhura sannyāsa-karaṇa
> sannyāsa kari' calilā prabhu śrī-vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prathama]]---first; [[synonyms:s:sūtra]]---synopsis; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]-[[synonyms:k:karaṇa]]---accepting the //sannyāsa// order; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---after accepting the renounced order; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---toward Vṛndāvana.
translation: This is the first synopsis: After accepting the sannyāsa order, Caitanya Mahāprabhu proceeded toward Vṛndāvana.
purport: Clearly these statements are a real account of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's acceptance of the renounced order of life. His acceptance of this renounced order is not at all comparable to the acceptance of //sannyāsa// by Māyāvādīs. After accepting //sannyāsa,// Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to reach Vṛndāvana. He was unlike the Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs,// who desire to merge into the existence of the Absolute. For a Vaiṣṇava, acceptance of //sannyāsa// means getting relief from all material activities and completely devoting oneself to the transcendental loving service of the Lord. This is confirmed by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī (//Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// 1.2.255): //anāsaktasya viṣayān yathārham upayuñjataḥ nirbandhaḥ kṛṣṇa-sambandhe yuktaṁ vairāgyam ucyate.// For a Vaiṣṇava, the renounced order means completely giving up attachment for material things and engaging nonstop in the transcendental loving service of the Lord. The Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs,// however, do not know how to engage everything in the service of the Lord. Because they have no devotional training, they think material objects to be untouchable. //Brahma satyaṁ jagan mithyā// The Māyāvādīs think that the world is false, but the Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsīs// do not think like this. Vaiṣṇavas say, "Why should the world be false? It is reality, and it is meant for the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead." For a Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsī,// renunciation means not accepting anything for personal sense enjoyment. Devotional service means engaging everything for the satisfaction of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.92
description: When proceeding toward Vṛndāvana, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was overwhelmed with ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, and He lost all remembrance of the external world. In this way He traveled continuously for three days in Rāḍha-deśa, the country where the Ganges River does not flow.
text:
> premete vihvala bāhya nāhika smaraṇa
> rāḍha-deśe tina dina karilā bhramaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:premete]]---in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---external; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---remembrance; [[synonyms:r:rāḍha]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in the Rāḍha countries; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---three days; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:b:bhramaṇa]]---traveling.
translation: When proceeding toward Vṛndāvana, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was overwhelmed with ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, and He lost all remembrance of the external world. In this way He traveled continuously for three days in Rāḍha-deśa, the country where the Ganges River does not flow.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.93
description: First of all, Lord Nityānanda bewildered Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by bringing Him along the banks of the Ganges, saying that it was the river Yamunā.
text:
> nityānanda prabhu mahāprabhu bhulāiyā
> gaṅgā-tīre lañā āilā 'yamunā' baliyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhulāiyā]]---bewildering; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank of the Ganges; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---brought; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]---the river Yamunā; [[synonyms:b:baliyā]]---informing.
translation: First of all, Lord Nityānanda bewildered Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by bringing Him along the banks of the Ganges, saying that it was the river Yamunā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.94
description: After three days, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to the house of Advaita Ācārya at Śāntipura and accepted alms there. This was His first acceptance of alms. At night He performed congregational chanting there.
text:
> śāntipure ācāryera gṛhe āgamana
> prathama bhikṣā kaila tāhāṅ, rātre saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śāntipure]]---in the city of Śāntipura; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]]---of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---to the home; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---coming; [[synonyms:p:prathama]]---first; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---accepting alms; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:r:rātre]]---at night; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---performance of congregational chanting.
translation: After three days, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to the house of Advaita Ācārya at Śāntipura and accepted alms there. This was His first acceptance of alms. At night He performed congregational chanting there.
purport: It appears that in His transcendental ecstasy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu forgot to eat for three continuous days. He was then misled by Nityānanda Prabhu, who said that the river Ganges was the Yamunā. Because the Lord was in the ecstasy of going to Vṛndāvana, He was engladdened to see the Yamunā, although in actuality the river was the Ganges. In this way the Lord was brought to the house of Advaita Prabhu at Śāntipura after three days, and He accepted food there. As long as the Lord remained there, He saw His mother, Śacīdevī, and every night executed congregational chanting with all the devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.95
description: At the house of Advaita Prabhu, He met His mother as well as all the devotees from Māyāpura. He adjusted everything and then went to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> mātā bhakta-gaṇera tāhāṅ karila milana
> sarva samādhāna kari' kaila nīlādri-gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---the mother; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---in that place; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:s:samādhāna]]---adjustments; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---executing; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:n:nīlādri]]-[[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going to Jagannātha Purī.
translation: At the house of Advaita Prabhu, He met His mother as well as all the devotees from Māyāpura. He adjusted everything and then went to Jagannātha Purī.
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu knew very well that His acceptance of //sannyāsa// was a thunderbolt for His mother. He therefore called for His mother and the devotees from Māyāpura, and by the arrangement of Śrī Advaita Ācārya, He met them for the last time after His acceptance of //sannyāsa.// His mother was overwhelmed with grief when she saw that He was clean-shaven. There was no longer any beautiful hair on His head. Mother Śacī was pacified by all the devotees, and Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked her to cook for Him because He was very hungry, not having taken anything for three days. His mother immediately agreed, and forgetting everything else, she cooked for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu during all the days she was at the house of Śrī Advaita Prabhu. Then, after a few days, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested His mother's permission to go to Jagannātha Purī. At His mother's request, He made Jagannātha Purī His headquarters after His acceptance of //sannyāsa.// Thus everything was adjusted, and with His mother's permission Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu proceeded toward Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.96
description: On the way toward Jagannātha Purī, Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed many other pastimes. He visited various temples and heard the story about Mādhavendra Purī and the installation of Gopāla.
text:
> pathe nānā līlā-rasa, deva-daraśana
> mādhava-purīra kathā, gopāla-sthāpana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---transcendental pastimes; [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting the temples; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]-[[synonyms:p:purīra]]---of Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---incidents; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---of Gopāla; [[synonyms:s:sthāpana]]---the installation.
translation: On the way toward Jagannātha Purī, Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed many other pastimes. He visited various temples and heard the story about Mādhavendra Purī and the installation of Gopāla.
purport: This Mādhava Purī is Mādhavendra Purī. Another Mādhava Purī is Mādhavācārya, who was the spiritual master of a devotee in the line of Gadādhara Paṇḍita and who wrote a book known as //Śrī Maṅgala-bhāṣya.// Mādhavācārya, however, is different from Mādhavendra Purī, who is mentioned in this verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.97
description: From Nityānanda Prabhu, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard the story of Kṣīra-curī Gopinātha and of the witness Gopāla. Then Nityānanda Prabhu broke the sannyāsa rod belonging to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> kṣīra-curi-kathā, sākṣi-gopāla-vivaraṇa
> nityānanda kaila prabhura daṇḍa-bhañjana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]-[[synonyms:c:curi]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---the narration of the stealing of the condensed milk; [[synonyms:s:sākṣi]]-[[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---the description of witness Gopāla; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhañjana]]---breaking the //sannyāsa// rod.
translation: From Nityānanda Prabhu, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard the story of Kṣīra-curī Gopinātha and of the witness Gopāla. Then Nityānanda Prabhu broke the sannyāsa rod belonging to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
purport:
This Kṣīra-curī Gopinātha is situated about five miles away from the Bāleśvara station on the Northeastern Railway, formerly known as the Bengal Māyāpura Railway. This station is situated a few miles away from the famous Kargapura junction station. Sometimes the charge of the temple was given to Śyāmasundara Adhikārī from Gopīvallabhapura, which lies on the border of the district of Medinīpura. Śyāmasundara Adhikārī was a descendant of Rasikānanda Murāri, the chief disciple of Śyāmānanda Gosvāmī.

A few miles before the Jagannātha Purī station is a small station called Sākṣi-gopāla. Near this station is a village named Satyavādī, where the temple of Sākṣi-gopāla is situated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.98
description: After His sannyāsa rod was broken by Nityānanda Prabhu, Caitanya Mahāprabhu apparently became very angry and left His company to travel alone to the Jagannātha temple. When Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered the Jagannātha temple and saw Lord Jagannātha, He immediately lost His senses and fell down on the ground.
text:

> dekhiyā mūrcchita hañā paḍilā bhūmite
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kruddha]]---angry; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:e:ekā]]---alone; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---after seeing Jagannātha; [[synonyms:m:mūrcchita]]---senseless; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]]---on the ground.
translation: After His sannyāsa rod was broken by Nityānanda Prabhu, Caitanya Mahāprabhu apparently became very angry and left His company to travel alone to the Jagannātha temple. When Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered the Jagannātha temple and saw Lord Jagannātha, He immediately lost His senses and fell down on the ground.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 1.99
description: After Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw Lord Jagannātha in the temple and fell down unconscious, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya took Him to his home. The Lord remained unconscious until the afternoon, when He finally regained His consciousness.
text:
> sārvabhauma lañā gelā āpana-bhavana
> tṛtīya prahare prabhura ha-ila cetana

translation: After Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw Lord Jagannātha in the temple and fell down unconscious, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya took Him to his home. The Lord remained unconscious until the afternoon, when He finally regained His consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.1
description: I offer my respectful obeisances unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is compared to a cloud that pours water on fields of grain, which are like devotees suffering due to a shortage of rain. Separation from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is like a drought, but when the Lord returns, His presence is like a nectarean rain that falls on all the grains and saves them from perishing.
text:
> taṁ vande gaura-jaladaṁ
> svasya yo darśanāmṛtaiḥ
> vicchedāvagraha-mlāna-
> bhakta-śasyāny ajīvayat

translation: I offer my respectful obeisances unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is compared to a cloud that pours water on fields of grain, which are like devotees suffering due to a shortage of rain. Separation from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is like a drought, but when the Lord returns, His presence is like a nectarean rain that falls on all the grains and saves them from perishing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.10
description: The King asked, "Why has He left Jagannātha Purī?"
text:
> rājā kahe,-jagannātha chāḍi' kene gelā

translation:
The King asked, "Why has He left Jagannātha Purī?"


The Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "Such are the pastimes of a great personality.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.100

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.101

translation: There was a solitary room at Kāśī Miśra's house, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu gave it to Paramānanda Purī. He also gave him one servant.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.102
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara also arrived the next day. He was a very intimate friend of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and he was an ocean of transcendental mellows.

synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---next day; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]] [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:atyanta]]---very; [[synonyms:m:marmī]]---intimate friend; [[synonyms:r:rasera]]---of transcendental mellows; [[synonyms:s:sāgara]]---ocean.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara also arrived the next day. He was a very intimate friend of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and he was an ocean of transcendental mellows.
purport: "Svarūpa" is one of the names of a //brahmacārī// in Śaṅkarācārya's disciplic succession. In the Vedic discipline there are ten names for //sannyāsīs,// and it is customary for a //brahmacārī// assisting a //sannyāsī// of the designation Tīrtha or Āśrama to receive the title Svarūpa. Dāmodara Svarūpa was formerly a resident of Navadvīpa, and his name was Puruṣottama Ācārya. When he went to Vārāṇasī, he took //sannyāsa// from a //sannyāsī// designated Tīrtha. Although he received the title Svarūpa in his //brahmacārī// stage, he did not change his name when he took //sannyāsa.// Actually as a //sannyāsī// he should have been called Tīrtha, but he chose to retain his original //brahmacārī// title as Svarūpa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.103
description: When Svarūpa Dāmodara was residing at Navadvīpa under the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, his name was Puruṣottama Ācārya.
text:
> 'puruṣottama ācārya' tāṅra nāma pūrvāśrame
> navadvīpe chilā teṅha prabhura caraṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:puruṣottama]] [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Puruṣottama Ācārya; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---name; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśrame]]---in the previous //āśrama//; [[synonyms:n:navadvīpe]]---at Navadvīpa; [[synonyms:c:chilā]]---was; [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---he; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the feet.
translation: When Svarūpa Dāmodara was residing at Navadvīpa under the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, his name was Puruṣottama Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.104
description: After seeing that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the renounced order, Puruṣottama Ācārya became like a madman and immediately went to Vārāṇasī to take sannyāsa.
text:
> prabhura sannyāsa dekhi' unmatta hañā
> sannyāsa grahaṇa kaila vārāṇasī giyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---when he saw the //sannyāsa// order; [[synonyms:u:unmatta]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---he became just like a madman; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]] [[synonyms:g:grahaṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---he also accepted the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:v:vārāṇasī]]---to Vārāṇasī; [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---going.
translation: After seeing that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the renounced order, Puruṣottama Ācārya became like a madman and immediately went to Vārāṇasī to take sannyāsa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.105
description: At the conclusion of his sannyāsa, his spiritual master, Caitanyānanda Bhāratī, ordered him, "Read Vedānta-sūtra and teach it to all others."
text:
> 'caitanyānanda' guru tāṅra ājñā dilena tāṅre
> vedānta paḍiyā paḍāo samasta lokere
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---of the name Caitanyānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---spiritual master; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:d:dilena]]---gave; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to him; [[synonyms:v:vedānta]] [[synonyms:p:paḍiyā]]---reading the //Vedānta-sūtra//; [[synonyms:p:paḍāo]]---teach; [[synonyms:s:samasta]]---all; [[synonyms:l:lokere]]---people.
translation: At the conclusion of his sannyāsa, his spiritual master, Caitanyānanda Bhāratī, ordered him, "Read Vedānta-sūtra and teach it to all others."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.106
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara was a great renunciant as well as a great learned scholar. With heart and soul he took shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> parama virakta teṅha parama paṇḍita
> kāya-mane āśriyāche śrī-kṛṣṇa-carita
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:parama]]---very; [[synonyms:v:virakta]]---renounced; [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---he; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---great; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---learned scholar; [[synonyms:k:kāya]]-[[synonyms:m:mane]]---with body and mind; [[synonyms:ā:āśriyāche]]---took shelter of; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:carita]]---the Personality of Godhead Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara was a great renunciant as well as a great learned scholar. With heart and soul he took shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.107
description: He was very enthusiastic to worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa without disturbance, and therefore, almost in madness, he accepted the sannyāsa order.
text:
> 'niścinte kṛṣṇa bhajiba' ei ta' kāraṇe
> unmāde karila teṅha sannyāsa grahaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:niścinte]]---without disturbance; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhajiba]]---I shall worship; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---for this; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇe]]---reason; [[synonyms:u:unmāde]]---ecstatic; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---he; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:g:grahaṇe]]---taking.
translation: He was very enthusiastic to worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa without disturbance, and therefore, almost in madness, he accepted the sannyāsa order.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.108
description: Upon accepting sannyāsa, Puruṣottama Ācārya followed the regulative principles by giving up his tuft of hair and sacred thread, but he did not accept the saffron-colored dress. Also, he did not accept a sannyāsī title but remained as a naiṣṭhika-brahmacārī.
text:
> sannyāsa karilā śikhā-sūtra-tyāga-rūpa
> yoga-paṭṭa nā nila, nāma haila 'svarūpa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---accepted the //sannyāsa// order; [[synonyms:ś:śikhā]]---tuft of hair; [[synonyms:s:sūtra]]---sacred thread; [[synonyms:t:tyāga]]---giving up; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---in the form of; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]-[[synonyms:p:paṭṭa]]---saffron-colored dress; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:n:nila]]---did not accept; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---name; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa.
translation: Upon accepting sannyāsa, Puruṣottama Ācārya followed the regulative principles by giving up his tuft of hair and sacred thread, but he did not accept the saffron-colored dress. Also, he did not accept a sannyāsī title but remained as a naiṣṭhika-brahmacārī.
purport:
There are regulative principles governing the renounced order. One has to perform eight kinds of //śrāddha.// One must offer oblations to one's forefathers and perform the sacrifice of //virajā-homa// Then one must cut off the tuft of hair called a //śikhā// and also give up the sacred thread. These are preliminary processes in the acceptance of //sannyāsa,// and Svarūpa Dāmodara accepted all these. However, Puruṣottama Ācārya did not accept the saffron color, a //sannyāsī// name or a //daṇḍa,// and for this reason he retained his //brahmacārī// name. Actually Puruṣottama Ācārya did not accept the //sannyāsa// order formally, but he renounced worldly life. He did not want to be disturbed by the formality of the //sannyāsa// order. He simply wanted to worship Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa without disturbance; therefore with heart and soul he took up the renounced order but not the formalities accompanying it. Renunciation means not doing anything but serving the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. When one acts on this platform, trying to please the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one is both a //sannyāsī// and a //yogī.// This is confirmed in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:6:1|(Bg. 6.1)]]:

> śrī-bhagavān uvāca
> anāśritaḥ karma-phalaṁ
> kāryaṁ karma karoti yaḥ
> sa sannyāsī ca yogī ca
> na niragnir na cākriyaḥ

"The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: One who is unattached to the fruits of his work and who works as he is obligated is in the renounced order of life, and he is the true mystic, not he who lights no fire and performs no work."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.109
description: After taking permission from his sannyāsa-guru, Svarūpa Dāmodara went to Nīlācala and accepted the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Then all day and night, in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa, he enjoyed transcendental mellows in the loving service of the Lord.
text:
> guru-ṭhāñi ājñā māgi' āilā nīlācale
> rātri-dine kṛṣṇa-prema-ānanda-vihvale
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:guru]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---from his spiritual master; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:m:māgi']]---asking permission; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---day and night; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---by ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vihvale]]---overwhelmed.
translation: After taking permission from his sannyāsa-guru, Svarūpa Dāmodara went to Nīlācala and accepted the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Then all day and night, in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa, he enjoyed transcendental mellows in the loving service of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.11
description: "Great saints go to holy places of pilgrimage in order to purify them. For that reason Caitanya Mahāprabhu is visiting many tīrthas and delivering many, many conditioned souls.
text:
> tīrtha pavitra karite kare tīrtha-bhramaṇa
> sei chale nistāraye sāṁsārika jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]---holy places; [[synonyms:p:pavitra]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to purify; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhramaṇa]]---touring in places of pilgrimage; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:c:chale]]---on that plea; [[synonyms:n:nistāraye]]---delivers; [[synonyms:s:sāṁsārika]]---conditioned; [[synonyms:j:jana]]---souls.
translation: "Great saints go to holy places of pilgrimage in order to purify them. For that reason Caitanya Mahāprabhu is visiting many tīrthas and delivering many, many conditioned souls.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.110
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara was the limit of all learned scholarship, but he did not exchange words with anyone. He simply remained in a solitary place, and no one could understand where he was.
text:
> pāṇḍityera avadhi, vākya nāhi kāro sane
> nirjane rahaye, loka saba nāhi jāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāṇḍityera]] [[synonyms:a:avadhi]]---the limit of learned scholarship; [[synonyms:v:vākya]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---no word; [[synonyms:k:kāro]] [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with anyone; [[synonyms:n:nirjane]]---in a solitary place; [[synonyms:r:rahaye]]---stays; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people in general; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---do not know.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara was the limit of all learned scholarship, but he did not exchange words with anyone. He simply remained in a solitary place, and no one could understand where he was.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.111
description: Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara was the personification of ecstatic love, fully cognizant of the transcendental mellows in relationship with Kṛṣṇa. He directly represented Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as His second expansion.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-rasa-tattva-vettā, deha-prema-rūpa
> sākṣāt mahāprabhura dvitīya svarūpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---of transcendental mellows in relationship with Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]---of the truth; [[synonyms:v:vettā]]---cognizant; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---body; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---personified //prema//; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]]---second; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---representation.
translation: Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara was the personification of ecstatic love, fully cognizant of the transcendental mellows in relationship with Kṛṣṇa. He directly represented Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as His second expansion.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.112
description: If someone wrote a book or composed verses and songs and wanted to recite them before Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Svarūpa Dāmodara would first examine them and then correctly present them. Only then would Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu agree to listen.
text:
> grantha, śloka, gīta keha prabhu-pāśe āne
> svarūpa parīkṣā kaile, pāche prabhu śune
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:grantha]]---scriptures; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verses; [[synonyms:g:gīta]]---songs; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśe]]---to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āne]]---brings; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:p:parīkṣā]] [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---after he examined; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---later; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hears.
translation: If someone wrote a book or composed verses and songs and wanted to recite them before Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Svarūpa Dāmodara would first examine them and then correctly present them. Only then would Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu agree to listen.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.113
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was never pleased to hear books or verses opposed to the conclusive statements of devotional service. The Lord did not like hearing rasābhāsa, the overlapping of transcendental mellows.
text:
> bhakti-siddhānta-viruddha, āra rasābhāsa
> śunite nā haya prabhura cittera ullāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:s:siddhānta]]---conclusive statements about the science of devotional service; [[synonyms:v:viruddha]]---opposing; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāsa]]---overlapping of transcendental mellows; [[synonyms:ś:śunite]]---to hear; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cittera]]---of the heart; [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---jubilation.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was never pleased to hear books or verses opposed to the conclusive statements of devotional service. The Lord did not like hearing rasābhāsa, the overlapping of transcendental mellows.
purport: Bhakti-siddhānta-viruddha refers to that which is against the principle of unity in diversity, philosophically known as //acintya-bhedābheda//-simultaneous oneness and difference-while //rasābhāsa// is something that may appear to be a transcendental mellow but actually is not. Those who are pure Vaiṣṇavas should avoid both these things opposed to devotional service. These misconceptions practically parallel the Māyāvāda philosophy. If one indulges in Māyāvāda philosophy, he gradually falls down from the platform of devotional service. By overlapping mellows (//rasābhāsa//) one eventually becomes a //prākṛta-sahajiyā// and takes everything to be very easy. One may also become a member of the //bāula// community and gradually become attracted to material activities. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has therefore advised us to avoid //bhakti-siddhānta-viruddha// and //rasābhāsa.// In this way the devotee can remain pure and free from falldowns. Everyone should try to remain aloof from //bhakti-siddhānta-viruddha// and //rasābhāsa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.114
description: It was the practice of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī to examine all works of literature to find out whether their conclusions were correct. Only then would he allow them to be heard by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> ataeva svarūpa āge kare parīkṣaṇa
> śuddha haya yadi, prabhure karā'na śravaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---at first; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:p:parīkṣaṇa]]---examination; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]---pure; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karā'na]]---causes; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]---hearing.
translation: It was the practice of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī to examine all works of literature to find out whether their conclusions were correct. Only then would he allow them to be heard by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that if something impedes the execution of devotional service, it should be understood to be impure. Pure devotees of the Lord do not accept impure principles. Impure devotees accept //rasābhāsa,// or overlapping, contradictory mellows, and other principles opposed to the //bhakti// path. The followers of such impure principles are never accepted as pure devotees. There are many parties following the path of //rasābhāsa,// and the followers are sometimes adored by ordinary men. Those who adopt the conclusions of //rasābhāsa// and //bhakti-siddhānta-viruddha// are never accepted as devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī never approved such followers as Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas, nor did he allow them even to meet the Supreme Lord, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.115
description: Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara used to read the poems of Vidyāpati and Caṇḍīdāsa and Jayadeva Gosvāmī's Śrī Gīta-govinda. He used to make Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very happy by singing these songs.
text:
> vidyāpati, caṇḍīdāsa, śrī-gīta-govinda
> ei tina gīte karā'na prabhura ānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vidyāpati]]---an old Vaiṣṇava poet from the province of Mithilā; [[synonyms:c:caṇḍīdāsa]]---a Bengali Vaiṣṇava poet born in the village of Nānnura, in the Birbhum district; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]-[[synonyms:g:govinda]]---a celebrated poem by Jayadeva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:g:gīte]]---songs; [[synonyms:k:karā'na]]---cause; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---happiness.
translation: Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara used to read the poems of Vidyāpati and Caṇḍīdāsa and Jayadeva Gosvāmī's Śrī Gīta-govinda. He used to make Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very happy by singing these songs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.116
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara was as expert a musician as the Gandharvas, and in scriptural discussion he was just like Bṛhaspati, the priest of the heavenly gods. Therefore it is to be concluded that there was no great personality quite like Svarūpa Dāmodara.
text:
> saṅgīte-gandharva-sama, śāstre bṛhaspati
> dāmodara-sama āra nāhi mahā-mati
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saṅgīte]]---in music; [[synonyms:g:gandharva]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---just like the Gandharvas; [[synonyms:ś:śāstre]]---in discussions of the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:b:bṛhaspati]]---like Bṛhaspati, the priest of the heavenly demigods; [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal to Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---anyone else; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:m:mati]]---great personality.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara was as expert a musician as the Gandharvas, and in scriptural discussion he was just like Bṛhaspati, the priest of the heavenly gods. Therefore it is to be concluded that there was no great personality quite like Svarūpa Dāmodara.
purport: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī was very expert in music as well as the Vedic scriptures. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to call him Dāmodara because of his expert singing and musical skills. The name Dāmodara was given by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and added to the name given by his //sannyāsa-guru.// He was therefore known as Svarūpa Dāmodara, or Dāmodara Svarūpa. He compiled a book of music named //Saṅgīta-dāmodara.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.117
description: Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara was very dear to Advaita Ācārya and Nityānanda Prabhu, and he was the life and soul of all the devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura.
text:
> advaita-nityānandera parama priyatama
> śrīvāsādi bhakta-gaṇera haya prāṇa-sama
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:n:nityānandera]]---of Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---very; [[synonyms:p:priya]]-[[synonyms:t:tama]]---dear; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---beginning with Śrīvāsa; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---exactly like the life and soul.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.119
description: "O ocean of mercy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! Let there be an awakening of Your auspicious mercy, which easily drives away all kinds of material lamentation. By Your mercy, everything is made pure and blissful. It awakens transcendental bliss and covers all material pleasures. By Your auspicious mercy, quarrels and disagreements arising among different scriptures are vanquished. Your auspicious mercy causes the heart to jubilate by pouring forth transcendental mellows. Your mercy always stimulates devotional service, which is full of joy. You are always glorifying the conjugal love of God. May transcendental bliss be awakened within my heart by Your causeless mercy."
text:
> heloddhūnita-khedayā viśadayā pronmīlad-āmodayā
> śāmyac-chāstra-vivādayā rasa-dayā cittārpitonmādayā
> śaśvad-bhakti-vinodayā sa-madayā mādhurya-maryādayā
> śrī-caitanya dayā-nidhe tava dayā bhūyād amandodayā
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:helā]]---very easily; [[synonyms:u:uddhūnita]]---driven away; [[synonyms:k:khedayā]]---lamentation; [[synonyms:v:viśadayā]]---which purifies everything; [[synonyms:p:pronmīlat]]---awakening; [[synonyms:ā:āmodayā]]---transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:ś:śāmyat]]---mitigating; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---of revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:v:vivādayā]]---disagreements; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:d:dayā]]---distributing all transcendental mellows; [[synonyms:c:citta]]---in the heart; [[synonyms:a:arpita]]---fixed; [[synonyms:u:unmādayā]]---jubilation; [[synonyms:ś:śaśvat]]---always; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:v:vinodayā]]---stimulating; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:m:madayā]]---full of ecstasy; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---of conjugal love; [[synonyms:m:maryādayā]]---the limit; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---O Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]-[[synonyms:n:nidhe]]---ocean of mercy; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:b:bhūyāt]]---let it be; [[synonyms:a:amanda]]---of good fortune; [[synonyms:u:udayā]]---in which there is awakening.
translation: "O ocean of mercy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! Let there be an awakening of Your auspicious mercy, which easily drives away all kinds of material lamentation. By Your mercy, everything is made pure and blissful. It awakens transcendental bliss and covers all material pleasures. By Your auspicious mercy, quarrels and disagreements arising among different scriptures are vanquished. Your auspicious mercy causes the heart to jubilate by pouring forth transcendental mellows. Your mercy always stimulates devotional service, which is full of joy. You are always glorifying the conjugal love of God. May transcendental bliss be awakened within my heart by Your causeless mercy."
purport:
This important verse (//Śrī Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka// 8.10) specifically describes the Lord's causeless mercy. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura explains that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is the most magnanimous Personality of Godhead, distributes His causeless mercy in three ways to the conditioned soul. Every living entity is morose in the material world because he is always in want. He undergoes a great struggle for existence and tries to minimize his miserable condition by squeezing the utmost pleasure out of this world. But the living entity is never successful in this endeavor. While in a miserable condition, a person sometimes seeks the favor of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but this is very difficult for materialistic people to obtain. However, when one becomes Kṛṣṇa conscious by the grace of the Lord, the fragrance of the lotus feet of the Lord expands, and in this way a materialist may gain freedom from his miseries. Actually his mind is cleansed by his transcendental connection with the lotus feet of the Lord. At such a time one is enlightened by the loving service of the Lord.

There are many different kinds of scriptures, and by reading them one often becomes puzzled. But when one receives the mercy of the Lord, his confusion is mitigated. Not only are scriptural disparities resolved, but a kind of transcendental bliss is awakened, and in this way one is fully satisfied. The transcendental loving service of the Lord constantly engages the conditioned soul in serving the Lord's lotus feet. Through such fortunate engagement, one's transcendental love for Kṛṣṇa is increased. One's position is thus completely purified, and one is filled with transcendental bliss accompanied by the spirit soul's jubilation.

Thus the transcendental causeless mercy of Lord Kṛṣṇa is manifest in the heart of the devotee. At such a time, material needs no longer exist. The lamentation that invariably accompanies material desires also vanishes. By the grace of the Lord one is elevated to the transcendental position, and then the transcendental mellows of the spiritual world are manifest in him. One's devotional service then becomes firm, and one engages in the Lord's transcendental loving service with great determination. All these combine to fully awaken the devotee's heart with love of Kṛṣṇa.

In the beginning, a conditioned soul is bereft of Kṛṣṇa consciousness and is always morose in his material activities. Later, by associating with a pure devotee, one becomes inquisitive to know the Absolute Truth. In this way one begins to engage in the transcendental service of the Lord. Next, by the Lord's grace all misconceptions are vanquished and the heart is cleansed of all material dirt. It is only then that the pleasure of transcendental bliss is awakened. By the Lord's mercy one is completely convinced of the value of devotional service. When one can see the pastimes of the Lord everywhere, he is firmly situated in transcendental bliss. Such a devotee is relieved of all kinds of material desires, and he preaches the glories of the Lord all over the world. These Kṛṣṇa conscious activities separate him from material activities and the desire for liberation, for at every step the devotee feels himself connected with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although such a devotee may sometimes be involved in household life, he is untouched by material existence due to his constant engagement in devotional service. Thus everyone is advised to take shelter of devotional service to become happy and liberated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.13
description: "A Vaiṣṇava travels to places of pilgrimage to purify them and reclaim fallen conditioned souls. This is one of the duties of a Vaiṣṇava. Actually, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is not a living entity but the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. Consequently, He is a fully independent controller, yet in His position as a devotee, He carries out the activities of a devotee."
text:
> vaiṣṇavera ei haya eka svabhāva niścala
> teṅho jīva nahena, hana svatantra īśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]]---of great devotees; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---nature; [[synonyms:n:niścala]]---unflinching; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---conditioned soul; [[synonyms:n:nahena]]---is not; [[synonyms:h:hana]]---is; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]]---independent; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---controller.
translation: "A Vaiṣṇava travels to places of pilgrimage to purify them and reclaim fallen conditioned souls. This is one of the duties of a Vaiṣṇava. Actually, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is not a living entity but the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. Consequently, He is a fully independent controller, yet in His position as a devotee, He carries out the activities of a devotee."
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura points out that because there are many permanent residents in holy places who do not precisely follow the rules and regulations governing living in a sacred place, exalted devotees have to go to these places to reclaim such persons. This is the business of a Vaiṣṇava. A Vaiṣṇava is unhappy to see others materially enmeshed. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu taught these activities of a Vaiṣṇava although He is the worshipable Deity of all Vaiṣṇavas, the complete and independent Supreme Personality of Godhead. He is //pūrṇaḥ śuddho nitya-muktaḥ//-complete, completely uncontaminated and eternally liberated. He is //sanātana,// for He has no beginning or end.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.132
description: "I am the servant of Īśvara Purī. My name is Govinda, and following the orders of my spiritual master, I have come here.
text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.136
description: After hearing this, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya asked Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Why did Īśvara Purī keep a servant who comes from a śūdra family?"
text:
> eta śuni' sārvabhauma prabhure puchila
> purī-gosāñi śūdra-sevaka kāṅhe ta' rākhila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto the Lord; [[synonyms:p:puchila]]---inquired; [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Īśvara Purī; [[synonyms:ś:śūdra]]-[[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---a servant who is a //śūdra//; [[synonyms:k:kāṅhe]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---why; [[synonyms:r:rākhila]]---kept.
translation: After hearing this, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya asked Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Why did Īśvara Purī keep a servant who comes from a śūdra family?"
purport:
Both Kāśīśvara and Govinda were personal servants of Īśvara Purī. After Īśvara Purī's demise, Kāśīśvara went to visit all the holy places of India. Following the orders of his spiritual master, Govinda immediately went to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for shelter. Govinda came from a //śūdra// family, but because he was initiated by Īśvara Purī, he was certainly a //brāhmaṇa.// Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya here asked Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu why Īśvara Purī accepted a disciple from a //śūdra// family. According to the //smṛti-śāstra,// which gives directions for the management of the //varṇāśrama// institution, a //brāhmaṇa// cannot accept a disciple from the lower castes. In other words, a //kṣatriya, vaiśya// or //śūdra// cannot be accepted as a servant. If a spiritual master accepts such a person, he is contaminated. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya therefore asked why Īśvara Purī accepted a servant or disciple born of a //śūdra// family.

In answer to this question, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied that His spiritual master, Īśvara Purī, was so empowered that he was as good as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. As such, Īśvara Purī was the spiritual master of the whole world. He was not a servant of any mundane rule or regulation. An empowered spiritual master like Īśvara Purī can bestow his mercy upon anyone, irrespective of caste or creed. The conclusion is that a spiritual master who is authorized and empowered by Kṛṣṇa and his own //guru// should be considered as good as the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. That is the verdict of Viśvanātha Cakravartī: //sākṣād-dharitvenaśā.// An authorized spiritual master is as good as Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. As Hari is free to act as He likes, the empowered spiritual master is also free. As Hari is not subject to mundane rules and regulations, the spiritual master empowered by Him is also not subject. According to the //Caitanya-caritāmṛta// (//Antya-līlā// 7.11), //kṛṣṇa-śakti vinā nahe tāra pravartana.// An authorized spiritual master empowered by Kṛṣṇa can spread the glories of the holy name of the Lord, for he has power of attorney from the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In the mundane world, anyone possessing his master's power of attorney can act on behalf of his master. Similarly, a spiritual master empowered by Kṛṣṇa through his own bona fide spiritual master should be considered as good as the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. That is the meaning of //sākṣād-dharitvena.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu therefore describes the activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the bona fide spiritual master as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.137

text:

> īśvarera kṛpā nahe veda-paratantra

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Both the Supreme Personality of Godhead and My spiritual master, Īśvara Purī, are completely independent. Therefore neither the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead nor that of Īśvara Purī is subject to any Vedic rules or regulations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.138

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.139
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa's mercy is dependent only on affection. Being obliged only by affection, Lord Kṛṣṇa acts very independently.
text:
> sneha-leśāpekṣā mātra śrī-kṛṣṇa-kṛpāra
> sneha-vaśa hañā kare svatantra ācāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sneha]]---of affection; [[synonyms:l:leśa]]---on a trace; [[synonyms:a:apekṣā]]---reliance; [[synonyms:m:mātra]]---only; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛpāra]]---of the mercy; [[synonyms:s:sneha]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---obliged by affection; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]]---independent; [[synonyms:ā:ācāra]]---behavior.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa's mercy is dependent only on affection. Being obliged only by affection, Lord Kṛṣṇa acts very independently.
purport: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is merciful, but His mercy does not depend on mundane rules and regulations. He is dependent only on affection and nothing else. Service to Lord Kṛṣṇa can be rendered in two ways. One can serve the Lord in affection or in veneration. When service is rendered in affection, it is the Lord's special mercy. When service is rendered in veneration, it is doubtful whether Kṛṣṇa's mercy is actually involved. If Kṛṣṇa's mercy is there, it is not dependent on any prescribed caste or creed. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to inform Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya that Lord Kṛṣṇa is the spiritual master of everyone, and He does not care for mundane caste or creed. Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu cited the example of Lord Kṛṣṇa's accepting food at the house of Vidura, who was a //śūdra// by birth. By the same token, Īśvara Purī, an empowered spiritual master, could show mercy to anyone. As such, he accepted Govinda, although the boy was born in a //śūdra// family. When Govinda was initiated, he became a //brāhmaṇa// and was accepted as Īśvara Purī's personal servant. In the //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa,// Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī states that one who is initiated by a bona fide spiritual master immediately becomes a //brāhmaṇa.// A pseudo spiritual master cannot transform a person into a //brāhmaṇa,// but an authorized spiritual master can do so. This is the verdict of //śāstra,// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all the Gosvāmīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.14

translation: "As such, it is not befitting that the guru's servant should engage in My personal service. Yet My spiritual master has given this order. What shall I do?"
purport: A //guru's// servants or disciples are all Godbrothers to one another, and as such they should all respect one another as //prabhu,// or master. No one should disrespect his Godbrother or try to engage him as a servant. For this reason Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya what to do about Govinda. Govinda was the personal servant of Īśvara Purī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's spiritual master, and now Īśvara Purī had ordered Govinda to become Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's personal servant. So what was to be done? This was the inquiry Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu placed before Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, an experienced friend.

> tabe mahāprabhu tāṅre kaila aṅgīkāra
> āpana-śrī-aṅga-sevāya dila adhikāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---after that; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Govinda; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---acceptance; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]---personal; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---of the transcendental body; [[synonyms:s:sevāya]]---in the service; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:a:adhikāra]]---responsibility.
translation: After Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced Govinda and engaged him in the service of His personal body.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.148
description: Everyone respected Govinda as the dearest servant of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and Govinda served all the Vaiṣṇavas and saw to their needs.
text:
> prabhura priya bhṛtya kari' sabe kare māna
> sakala vaiṣṇavera govinda kare samādhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:priya]]---dear; [[synonyms:b:bhṛtya]]---servant; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---understanding; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:m:māna]]---respect; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]]---of devotees; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:s:samādhāna]]---service.
translation: Everyone respected Govinda as the dearest servant of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and Govinda served all the Vaiṣṇavas and saw to their needs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.149
description: Both Haridāsa senior and Haridāsa junior, who were musicians, as well as Rāmāi and Nandāi, used to stay with Govinda.
text:
> choṭa-baḍa-kīrtanīyā-dui haridāsa
> rāmāi, nandāi rahe govindera pāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:choṭa]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---junior and senior; [[synonyms:k:kīrtanīyā]]---musicians; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsas; [[synonyms:r:rāmāi]]---Rāmāi; [[synonyms:n:nandāi]]---Nandāi; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---stay; [[synonyms:g:govindera]] [[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---with Govinda.
translation: Both Haridāsa senior and Haridāsa junior, who were musicians, as well as Rāmāi and Nandāi, used to stay with Govinda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.15
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself and is completely independent. Being Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself, He is not dependent on anyone.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya kahe,-teṅho svayaṁ īśvara svatantra
> sākṣāt śrī-kṛṣṇa, teṅho nahe para-tantra
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sārvabhauma replied; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---personally; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]]---independent; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---is not; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:t:tantra]]---dependent on anyone.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself and is completely independent. Being Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself, He is not dependent on anyone.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.150
description: They all remained with Govinda to serve Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; therefore no one could estimate the good fortune of Govinda.
text:
> govindera saṅge kare prabhura sevana
> govindera bhāgya-sīmā nā yāya varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:govindera]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Govinda; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---service; [[synonyms:g:govindera]]---of Govinda; [[synonyms:b:bhāgya]]-[[synonyms:s:sīmā]]---the limit of good fortune; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāya]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---can be described.
translation: They all remained with Govinda to serve Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; therefore no one could estimate the good fortune of Govinda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.151
description: The next day Mukunda Datta informed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Brahmānanda Bhāratī has come to see You."
text:
> āra dine mukunda-datta kahe prabhura sthāne
> brahmānanda-bhāratī āilā tomāra daraśane
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---the next day; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]-[[synonyms:d:datta]]---Mukunda Datta; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---at the place; [[synonyms:b:brahmānanda]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāratī]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---has come; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---to see You.
translation: The next day Mukunda Datta informed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Brahmānanda Bhāratī has come to see You."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.152
description: Mukunda Datta then asked the Lord, "Shall I bring him here?"
text:
> ājñā deha' yadi tāṅre āniye ethāi
> prabhu kahe,-guru teṅha, yāba tāṅra ṭhāñi
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:deha']]---order; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:ā:āniye]]---I can bring; [[synonyms:e:ethāi]]---here; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:g:guru]] [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---he is My spiritual master; [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---I shall go; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---to his place.
translation:
Mukunda Datta then asked the Lord, "Shall I bring him here?"


Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Brahmānanda Bhāratī is like My spiritual master. It is better that I go to him."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.153
description: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His devotees came into the presence of Brahmānanda Bhāratī.
text:
> eta bali' mahāprabhu bhakta-gaṇa-saṅge
> cali' āilā brahmānanda-bhāratīra āge
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the devotees; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---walking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:b:brahmānanda]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāratīra]]---of Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in the presence.
translation: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His devotees came into the presence of Brahmānanda Bhāratī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.154
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His devotees approached him, they saw that he was covered with a deerskin. Seeing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very unhappy.
text:
> brahmānanda pariyāche mṛga-carmāmbara
> tāhā dekhi' prabhu duḥkha pāilā antara
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmānanda]]---Brahmānanda; [[synonyms:p:pariyāche]]---did wear; [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]-[[synonyms:c:carma]]-[[synonyms:a:ambara]]---a garment made of deerskin; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing that; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:p:pāilā]]---got; [[synonyms:a:antara]]---within Himself.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His devotees approached him, they saw that he was covered with a deerskin. Seeing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very unhappy.
purport: Brahmānanda Bhāratī belonged to the Śaṅkara-sampradāya. (The title //bhāratī// indicates a member of one of that //sampradāya's// ten classes of //sannyāsīs//.) It is customary for a person who has renounced the world to cover his body with a deerskin or the bark of a tree. This is enjoined by the //Manu-saṁhitā.// But if a //sannyāsī// who has renounced the world simply wears a deerskin and does not spiritually advance, he is bewildered by false prestige. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not like to see Brahmānanda Bhāratī wearing a deerskin.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.155
description: Seeing Brahmānanda Bhāratī wearing the deerskin, Caitanya Mahāprabhu pretended not to see him. Instead, He asked Mukunda Datta, "Where is Brahmānanda Bhāratī, My spiritual master?"
text:
> dekhiyā ta' chadma kaila yena dekhe nāñi
> mukundere puche,-kāhāṅ bhāratī-gosāñi
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:c:chadma]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---pretended; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:n:nāñi]]---not; [[synonyms:m:mukundere]] [[synonyms:p:puche]]---inquired from Mukunda; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī, my spiritual master.
translation: Seeing Brahmānanda Bhāratī wearing the deerskin, Caitanya Mahāprabhu pretended not to see him. Instead, He asked Mukunda Datta, "Where is Brahmānanda Bhāratī, My spiritual master?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.156
description: Mukunda Datta replied, "Here is Brahmānanda Bhāratī, in Your presence."
text:
> mukunda kahe,-ei āge dekha vidyamāna
> prabhu kahe,-teṅha nahena, tumi ageyāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukunda]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Mukunda said; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---here in front; [[synonyms:d:dekha]]---see; [[synonyms:v:vidyamāna]]---present; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied; [[synonyms:t:teṅha]] [[synonyms:n:nahena]]---he is not; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:a:ageyāna]]---you are incorrect.
translation:
Mukunda Datta replied, "Here is Brahmānanda Bhāratī, in Your presence."


The Lord replied, "You are incorrect. This is not Brahmānanda Bhāratī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.157
description: "You must be talking of someone else, for this is surely not Brahmānanda Bhāratī. You simply have no knowledge. Why should Brahmānanda Bhāratī wear a deerskin?"
text:
> anyere anya kaha, nāhi tomāra jñāna
> bhāratī-gosāñi kene paribena cāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anyere]]---another; [[synonyms:a:anya]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---you talk of someone else; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---My spiritual master; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:p:paribena]]---should wear; [[synonyms:c:cāma]]---skin.
translation: "You must be talking of someone else, for this is surely not Brahmānanda Bhāratī. You simply have no knowledge. Why should Brahmānanda Bhāratī wear a deerskin?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.158
description: When Brahmānanda Bhāratī heard this, he thought, "My deerskin is not approved by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu."
text:
> śuni' brahmānanda kare hṛdaye vicāre
> mora carmāmbara ei nā bhāya iṅhāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:b:brahmānanda]]---Brahmānanda; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---within himself; [[synonyms:v:vicāre]]---consideration; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:c:carma]]-[[synonyms:a:ambara]]---deerskin garment; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:b:bhāya]]---is approved; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāre]]---by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: When Brahmānanda Bhāratī heard this, he thought, "My deerskin is not approved by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.159
description: Thus admitting his mistake, Brahmānanda Bhāratī thought, "He spoke well. I put on this deerskin only for prestige. I cannot cross over the ocean of nescience simply by wearing a deerskin.
text:
> bhāla kahena,---carmāmbara dambha lāgi' pari
> carmāmbara-paridhāne saṁsāra nā tari
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]---well; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---He said; [[synonyms:c:carma]]-[[synonyms:a:ambara]]---the garment of deerskin; [[synonyms:d:dambha]]---prestige; [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for the matter of; [[synonyms:p:pari]]---I put on; [[synonyms:c:carma]]-[[synonyms:a:ambara]]-[[synonyms:p:paridhāne]]---by putting on a garment of skin; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]---the material world; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:t:tari]]---I cannot cross.
translation: Thus admitting his mistake, Brahmānanda Bhāratī thought, "He spoke well. I put on this deerskin only for prestige. I cannot cross over the ocean of nescience simply by wearing a deerskin.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.16
description: "Still, I endeavored very hard to keep Him here, but because He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead and completely independent, I was not successful."
text:
> tathāpi rākhite tāṅre bahu yatna kailuṅ
> īśvarera svatantra icchā, rākhite nāriluṅ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:r:rākhite]]---to keep; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---various; [[synonyms:y:yatna]]---endeavors; [[synonyms:k:kailuṅ]]---I made; [[synonyms:ī:īśvarera]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]]---independent; [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---desire; [[synonyms:r:rākhite]]---to keep; [[synonyms:n:nāriluṅ]]---I was unable.
translation: "Still, I endeavored very hard to keep Him here, but because He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead and completely independent, I was not successful."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.160
description: "From today on I shall not wear this deerskin." As soon as Brahmānanda Bhāratī decided this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, understanding his mind, immediately sent for the robes of a sannyāsī.
text:
> āji haite nā pariba ei carmāmbara
> prabhu bahirvāsa ānāilā jāniyā antara
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āji]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from today; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pariba]]---I shall not put on; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:c:carma]]-[[synonyms:a:ambara]]---deerskin garment; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bahirḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---the cloth of a //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:ā:ānāilā]]---had someone bring; [[synonyms:j:jāniyā]]---knowing; [[synonyms:a:antara]]---his contemplation.
translation: "From today on I shall not wear this deerskin." As soon as Brahmānanda Bhāratī decided this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, understanding his mind, immediately sent for the robes of a sannyāsī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.161
description: As soon as Brahmānanda Bhāratī gave up his deerskin and covered himself with sannyāsī robes, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came and offered His respects at his lotus feet.
text:
> carmāmbara chāḍi' brahmānanda parila vasana
> prabhu āsi' kaila tāṅra caraṇa vandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:carma]]-[[synonyms:a:ambara]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up the deerskin garment; [[synonyms:b:brahmānanda]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:p:parila]]---put on; [[synonyms:v:vasana]]---cloth garment; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---worshiping the feet.
translation: As soon as Brahmānanda Bhāratī gave up his deerskin and covered himself with sannyāsī robes, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came and offered His respects at his lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.162
description: Brahmānanda Bhāratī said, "You instruct the general populace by Your behavior. I will not do anything against Your wishes; otherwise You will not offer me respects but will neglect me. I am afraid of this.
text:
> bhāratī kahe,-tomāra ācāra loka śikhāite
> punaḥ nā karibe nati, bhaya pāṅa citte
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī said; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:ā:ācāra]]---behavior; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people in general; [[synonyms:ś:śikhāite]]---to teach; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---will do; [[synonyms:n:nati]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:p:pāṅa]]---I get; [[synonyms:c:citte]]---within the mind.
translation: Brahmānanda Bhāratī said, "You instruct the general populace by Your behavior. I will not do anything against Your wishes; otherwise You will not offer me respects but will neglect me. I am afraid of this.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.163
description: "At the present moment I see two Brahmans. One Brahman is Lord Jagannātha, who does not move, and the other Brahman, who is moving, is You. Lord Jagannātha is the arcā-vigraha, the worshipable Deity, and it is He who is the nonmoving Brahman. But You are Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and You are moving here and there. The two of You are the same Brahman, master of the material nature, but You are playing two parts-one moving and one not moving. In this way two Brahmans are now residing at Jagannātha Purī, Puruṣottama.
text:
> sāmpratika 'dui brahma' ihāṅ 'calācala'
> jagannātha-acala brahma, tumi ta' sacala
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sāmpratika]]---at the present moment; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---two Brahmans, or spiritual identities; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:c:cala]]-[[synonyms:a:acala]]---moving and not moving; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:a:acala]] [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---not moving Brahman; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---but; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:c:cala]]---moving Brahman.
translation: "At the present moment I see two Brahmans. One Brahman is Lord Jagannātha, who does not move, and the other Brahman, who is moving, is You. Lord Jagannātha is the arcā-vigraha, the worshipable Deity, and it is He who is the nonmoving Brahman. But You are Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and You are moving here and there. The two of You are the same Brahman, master of the material nature, but You are playing two parts-one moving and one not moving. In this way two Brahmans are now residing at Jagannātha Purī, Puruṣottama.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.164
description: "Of the two Brahmans, You are fair-complexioned, and the other, Lord Jagannātha, is blackish. Both of You are delivering the whole world."
text:
> tumi-gaura-varṇa, teṅha-śyāmala-varṇa
> dui brahme kaila saba jagat-tāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇa]]---having a golden or fair complexion; [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---He; [[synonyms:ś:śyāmala]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇa]]---having a blackish complexion; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:brahme]]---both Brahmans; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---of the whole world; [[synonyms:t:tāraṇa]]---deliverance.
translation: "Of the two Brahmans, You are fair-complexioned, and the other, Lord Jagannātha, is blackish. Both of You are delivering the whole world."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.165
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "Actually, to tell you the truth, due to your presence there are now two Brahmans at Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> prabhu kahe,-satya kahi, tomara āgamane
> dui brahma prakaṭila śrī-puruṣottame
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I speak the truth; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:ā:āgamane]]---by your presence; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---two Brahmans; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭila]]---appeared; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣottame]]---at Jagannātha Purī.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "Actually, to tell you the truth, due to your presence there are now two Brahmans at Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.166
description: "Both Brahmānanda and Gaurahari are moving, whereas the blackish Lord Jagannātha is sitting tight and immobile."
text:
> 'brahmānanda' nāma tumi-gaura-brahma 'cala'
> śyama-varṇa jagannātha vasiyāchena 'acala'
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmānanda]]---Brahmānanda; [[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---your name; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:brahma]]---the Brahman of the name Gaura; [[synonyms:c:cala]]---both of them are moving; [[synonyms:ś:śyāma]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇa]]---of blackish hue; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:v:vasiyāchena]]---is sitting; [[synonyms:a:acala]]---without movement.
translation: "Both Brahmānanda and Gaurahari are moving, whereas the blackish Lord Jagannātha is sitting tight and immobile."
purport: Brahmānanda Bhāratī wanted to prove that there is no difference between the Supreme Lord and the //jīva,// while Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to prove that He and Brahmānanda Bhāratī were //jīvas// and that although the //jīvas// are Brahman, they are many, but the Supreme Lord, the Supreme Brahman, is one. On the other hand, Brahmānanda Bhāratī also wanted to prove that Jagannātha and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are one, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but that to fulfill His mission Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu appeared to be moving whereas Lord Jagannātha appeared to be inert. Thus this jolly argument was going on. Finally, Brahmānanda Bhāratī referred the whole matter to Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya for a final decision.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.167
description: Brahmānanda Bhāratī said, "My dear Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, please become the mediator in this logical argument between Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and me."
text:
> bhāratī kahe,-sārvabhauma, madhyastha hañā
> iṅhāra sane āmāra 'nyāya' bujha' mana diyā

translation: Brahmānanda Bhāratī said, "My dear Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, please become the mediator in this logical argument between Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and me."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.168
description: Brahmānanda Bhāratī continued, "The living entity is localized, whereas the Supreme Brahman is all-pervading. That is the verdict of the revealed scriptures.
text:
> 'vyāpya' 'vyāpaka'-bhāve 'jīva'-'brahme' jāni
> jīva-vyāpya, brahma-vyāpaka, śāstrete vākhāni
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyāpya]]---localized; [[synonyms:v:vyāpaka]]---all-pervading; [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in this way; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---living entity; [[synonyms:b:brahme]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I know; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---the living entity; [[synonyms:v:vyāpya]]---localized; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:v:vyāpaka]]---all-pervading; [[synonyms:ś:śāstrete]]---in the revealed scripture; [[synonyms:v:vākhāni]]---description.
translation: Brahmānanda Bhāratī continued, "The living entity is localized, whereas the Supreme Brahman is all-pervading. That is the verdict of the revealed scriptures.
purport:
Brahmānanda Bhāratī drew Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's attention because he wanted him to judge the argument. He then stated that Brahman, the Supreme Lord, is all-pervading. This is confirmed by Lord Kṛṣṇa in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:13:3|(Bg. 13.3)]]:

> kṣetra-jñaṁ cāpi māṁ viddhi
> sarva-kṣetreṣu bhārata
> kṣetra-kṣetrajñayor jñānaṁ
> yat taj jñānaṁ mataṁ mama

"O scion of Bharata, you should understand that I am also the knower in all bodies, and to understand this body and its knower is called knowledge. That is My opinion."

The Supreme Personality of Godhead in His Paramātmā feature is expanded everywhere. The //Brahma-saṁhitā// says, //aṇḍāntara-stha-paramāṇu-cayāntara-stham:// by virtue of His all-pervasive nature, the Supreme Lord is within the universe as well as within all elements of the universe. He is even within the atom. In this way the Supreme Lord Govinda is all-pervasive. On the other hand, the living entities are very, very small. It is said that the living entity is one ten-thousandth of the tip of a hair. Therefore the living entity is localized. Living entities rest on the Brahman effulgence, the bodily rays of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.169
description: "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu purified me by taking away my deerskin. This is proof that He is all-pervasive and all-powerful and that I am subordinate to Him.
text:
> carma ghucāñā kaila āmāre śodhana
> doṅhāra vyāpya-vyāpakatve ei ta' kāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:carma]]---deerskin; [[synonyms:g:ghucāñā]]---taking away; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:āmāre]]---unto me; [[synonyms:ś:śodhana]]---purification; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]]---of both of us; [[synonyms:v:vyāpya]]---being localized; [[synonyms:v:vyāpakatve]]---being all-pervasive; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause.
translation: "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu purified me by taking away my deerskin. This is proof that He is all-pervasive and all-powerful and that I am subordinate to Him.
purport: Brahmānanda Bhāratī herein asserts that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the Supreme Brahman and that he is the subordinate Brahman. This is confirmed in the //Vedas:nityo nityānāṁ cetanaś cetanānām.// The Supreme Personality of Godhead is Brahman or Paraṁbrahman, the chief of all living entities. Both the Supreme Brahman, or the Personality of Godhead, and the living entities are persons, but the Supreme Brahman is the predominator, whereas the living entities are predominated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.17
description: The King said, "Bhaṭṭācārya, you are the most learned and experienced person I know. Therefore when you address Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as Lord Kṛṣṇa, I accept this as the truth.
text:
> rājā kahe,-bhaṭṭa tumi vijña-śiromaṇi
> tumi tāṅre 'kṛṣṇa' kaha, tāte satya māni
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the King said; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:v:vijña]]-[[synonyms:ś:śiromaṇi]]---the most experienced learned scholar; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---address as Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---your statement; [[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:m:māni]]---I accept as true.
translation: The King said, "Bhaṭṭācārya, you are the most learned and experienced person I know. Therefore when you address Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as Lord Kṛṣṇa, I accept this as the truth.
purport:
This is the way to advance in spiritual science. One must accept the words of an //ācārya,// a bona fide spiritual master, to clear the path for spiritual advancement. This is the secret of success. However, one's guide must be a spiritual master who is actually an unalloyed devotee strictly following the instructions of the previous //ācārya// without deviation. Whatever the spiritual master says must be accepted by the disciple. Only then is success certain. This is the Vedic system.

Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was a //brāhmaṇa// and a realized soul, whereas Pratāparudra was a //kṣatriya. Kṣatriya// kings used to obey very faithfully the orders of learned //brāhmaṇas// and saintly persons, and in this way they would rule their country. Similarly, //vaiśyas// used to follow the king's orders, and //śūdras// used to serve the three higher castes. In this way the //brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas// and //śūdras// used to live cooperatively, performing their respective duties. Consequently society was peaceful, and people were able to discharge the duties of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Thus they were happy in this life and able to return home, back to Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.170

Accepting the renounced order, the Lord is always equipoised. He is firmly fixed in His mission of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra, and He is firmly situated in His dualistic conclusion and in His peace.'

> sannyāsa-kṛc chamaḥ śānto

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.172
description: After hearing this, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya rendered his judgment, saying, "Brahmānanda Bhāratī, I see that you are victorious."

translation:
After hearing this, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya rendered his judgment, saying, "Brahmānanda Bhāratī, I see that you are victorious."


Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately said, "I accept whatever Brahmānanda Bhāratī has said. It is quite all right with Me."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.173
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus posed Himself as a disciple and accepted Brahmānanda Bhāratī as His spiritual master. He then said, "The disciple is certainly defeated in an argument with the spiritual master."

translation:
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus posed Himself as a disciple and accepted Brahmānanda Bhāratī as His spiritual master. He then said, "The disciple is certainly defeated in an argument with the spiritual master."


Brahmānanda Bhāratī immediately countered these words, saying, "This is not the cause of Your defeat. There is another cause.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.174
