title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.175
description: "I have been meditating on the impersonal Brahman since my birth, but since I have seen You, I have fully experienced Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> ājanma karinu muñi 'nirākāra'-dhyāna
> tomā dekhi' 'kṛṣṇa' haila mora vidyamāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ā]]-[[synonyms:j:janma]]---since my birth; [[synonyms:k:karinu]]---have done; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nirākāra]]-[[synonyms:d:dhyāna]]---meditation on impersonal Brahman; [[synonyms:t:tomā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---by seeing You; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:v:vidyamāna]]---experience.
translation: "I have been meditating on the impersonal Brahman since my birth, but since I have seen You, I have fully experienced Kṛṣṇa."
purport:
Brahmānanda Bhāratī admitted that when there is an argument between the spiritual master and the disciple, the spiritual master is naturally victorious, although the disciple may put forward a strong argument. In other words, it is customary that the words of the spiritual master are more worshipable than the words of a disciple. Under the circumstances, since Brahmānanda Bhāratī was in the position of a spiritual master, he emerged victorious over Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who considered Himself Brahmānanda Bhāratī's disciple. However, Brahmānanda Bhāratī reversed the argument and took the position of a devotee, admitting that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa. This means that the Lord was voluntarily defeated out of affection for His devotee. He was defeated voluntarily, because no one can defeat the Supreme Lord. Concerning this, the words of Bhīṣma in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:9:37|(1.9.37)]] are important:

> sva-nigamam apahāya mat-pratijñām
> ṛtam adhikartum avapluto ratha-sthaḥ
> dhṛta-ratha-caraṇo 'bhyayāc calad-gur
> harir iva hantum ibhaṁ gatottarīyaḥ

"Fulfilling my desire and sacrificing His own promise, He got down from the chariot, took up its wheel and ran toward me hurriedly, just as a lion goes to kill an elephant. He even dropped His outer garment on the way."

Kṛṣṇa promised not to fight in the Battle of Kurukṣetra, but in order to break Kṛṣṇa's promise, Bhīṣma attacked Arjuna in such a vigorous way that Kṛṣṇa was obliged to take up a chariot wheel and attack Bhīṣma. The Lord did this to show that His devotee was being maintained at the sacrifice of His own promise. Brahmānanda Bhāratī said, "Since the beginning of my life I was attached to impersonal Brahman realization, but as soon as I saw You, I became very much attached to the Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa." Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself, and thus Brahmānanda Bhāratī became His devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.176

I now want to chant the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Over and above this, within my heart I consider You to be Kṛṣṇa, and I am therefore very eager to serve You.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-nāma sphure mukhe, mane netre kṛṣṇa
> tomāke tad-rūpa dekhi' hṛdaya-satṛṣṇa

translation: Brahmānanda Bhāratī continued, "Since I have seen You, I have been feeling Lord Kṛṣṇa's presence in my mind and have been seeing Him before my eyes. I now want to chant the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Over and above this, within my heart I consider You to be Kṛṣṇa, and I am therefore very eager to serve You.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.177
description: "Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura abandoned his impersonal realization for the realization of the Personality of Godhead. I now see that my condition is similar to his, for it has already changed."
text:
> bilvamaṅgala kaila yaiche daśā āpanāra
> ihāṅ dekhi' sei daśā ha-ila āmāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bilvamaṅgala]]---Bilvamaṅgala; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---condition; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāra]]---his own; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---I see; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---that condition; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---mine.
translation: "Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura abandoned his impersonal realization for the realization of the Personality of Godhead. I now see that my condition is similar to his, for it has already changed."
purport:
In his early life, Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura was an impersonalistic monist, and he used to meditate upon the impersonal Brahman effulgence. Later he became a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa, and his explanation for this change is given in a verse (text 178) that is quoted in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu.// Sometimes a devotee gradually comes to the stage of Bhagavān realization, realization of the Supreme Person, after having attained the lower stages of realization-impersonal Brahman realization and localized Paramātmā realization. The condition of such a devotee is described in the //Caitanya-candrāmṛta// (5) by Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī:

> kaivalyaṁ narakāyate tri-daśa-pūr ākāśa-puṣpāyate
> durdāntendriya-kāla-sarpa-paṭalī protkhāta-daṁṣṭrāyate
> viśvaṁ pūrṇa-sukhāyate vidhi-mahendrādiś ca kīṭāyate
> yat-kāruṇya-kaṭākṣa-vaibhavavatāṁ taṁ gauram eva stumaḥ

Kaivalya, oneness in the effulgence of Brahman, appears hellish to the devotee. The heavenly planets, the abodes of the demigods, appear to a devotee like phantasmagoria. The //yogīs// meditate for sense control, but for the devotee the senses appear like serpents with broken teeth. The devotee doesn't have to control his senses, for his senses are already engaged in the Lord's service. Consequently there is no possibility that the senses will act like serpents. In the material condition, the senses are as strong as poisonous snakes. But when the senses are engaged in the Lord's service, they are like poisonous snakes with their fangs removed, and so they are no longer dangerous. The entire world is a replica of Vaikuṇṭha for the devotee because he has no anxiety. He sees that everything belongs to Kṛṣṇa, and he does not want to enjoy anything for himself. He does not even aspire for the position of Lord Brahmā or Indra. He simply wants to engage everything in the service of the Lord; therefore he has no problem. He stands in his original constitutional position. All this is possible when one receives Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's merciful glance.

In the //Caitanya-candrāmṛta// there are many more verses illustrating this same principle.

> dhik kurvanti ca brahma-yoga-viduṣas taṁ gauracandraṁ numaḥ
>
> tāvad brahma-kathā vimukta-padavī tāvan na tiktī-bhavet
> tāvac cāpi viśṛṅkhalatvam ayate no loka-veda-sthitiḥ
> tāvac chāstra-vidāṁ mithaḥ kala-kalo nānā-bahir-vartmasu
> śrī-caitanya-padāmbuja-priya-jano yāvan na dig-gocaraḥ
>
> gauraś cauraḥ sakalamaharat ko 'pi me tīvra-vīryaḥ

A discussion of the impersonal Brahman is not very palatable to a devotee. The so-called regulations of the //śāstras// also appear null and void to him. There are many people who argue over the //śāstras,// but for a devotee such discussions are but tumultuous roaring. By the influence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all these problems disappear.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.178
description: Brahmānanda Bhāratī concluded, " 'Although I was worshiped by those on the path of monism and initiated into self-realization through the yoga system, I have nonetheless been forcibly turned into a maidservant by some cunning boy who is always joking with the gopīs.' "
text:
> advaita-vīthī-pathikair upāsyāḥ
> svānanda-siṁhāsana-labdha-dīkṣāḥ
> śaṭhena kenāpi vayaṁ haṭhena
> dāsī-kṛtā gopa-vadhū-viṭena
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:v:vīthī]]---of the path of monism; [[synonyms:p:pathikaiḥ]]---by the wanderers; [[synonyms:u:upāsyāḥ]]---worshipable; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---of self-realization; [[synonyms:s:siṁha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsana]]---on the throne; [[synonyms:l:labdha]]-[[synonyms:d:dīkṣāḥ]]---being initiated; [[synonyms:ś:śaṭhena]]---by a cheater; [[synonyms:k:kena]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---some; [[synonyms:v:vayam]]---I; [[synonyms:h:haṭhena]]---by force; [[synonyms:d:dāsī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛtā]]---made into a maidservant; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:v:vadhū]]-[[synonyms:v:viṭena]]---by a boy engaged in joking with the //gopīs.//
translation: Brahmānanda Bhāratī concluded, " 'Although I was worshiped by those on the path of monism and initiated into self-realization through the yoga system, I have nonetheless been forcibly turned into a maidservant by some cunning boy who is always joking with the gopīs.' "
purport: This is a verse written by Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura. It is quoted in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (3.1.44).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.179
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "You have a deep ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa; therefore wherever you turn your eyes, you simply heighten your Kṛṣṇa consciousness."
text:
> prabhu kahe,-kṛṣṇe tomāra gāḍha premā haya
> yāhāṅ netra paḍe, tāhāṅ śrī-kṛṣṇa sphuraya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:g:gāḍha]]---deep; [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:n:netra]]---eyes; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fall; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sphuraya]]---becomes manifest.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "You have a deep ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa; therefore wherever you turn your eyes, you simply heighten your Kṛṣṇa consciousness."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.18
description: "When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returns again, I wish to see Him just once in order to make my eyes perfect."
text:
> punarapi ihāṅ tāṅra haile āgamana
> eka-bāra dekhi' kari saphala nayana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:h:haile]]---when there is; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---arrival; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---once; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I make; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]---fruitful; [[synonyms:n:nayana]]---my eyes.
translation: "When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returns again, I wish to see Him just once in order to make my eyes perfect."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.180
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "The statements of both of you are correct. Kṛṣṇa gives direct audience through His own mercy.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya kahe,-doṅhāra susatya vacana
> āge yadi kṛṣṇa dena sākṣāt daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]]---of both; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:s:satya]]---correct; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---statements; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---first; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dena]]---gives; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---direct; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---audience.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "The statements of both of you are correct. Kṛṣṇa gives direct audience through His own mercy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.181
description: "Without having ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, one cannot see Him directly. Therefore through the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Brahmānanda Bhāratī has acquired direct vision of the Lord."
text:
> prema vinā kabhu nahe tāṅra sākṣātkāra
> iṅhāra kṛpāte haya daraśana iṅhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]] [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without ecstatic love; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---there is never; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:s:sākṣātkāra]]---direct meeting; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpāte]]---by the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes possible; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visit; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]]---of Brahmānanda Bhāratī.
translation: "Without having ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, one cannot see Him directly. Therefore through the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Brahmānanda Bhāratī has acquired direct vision of the Lord."
purport:
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "You are Brahmānanda Bhāratī, an advanced devotee who ecstatically loves the Supreme Lord. Therefore you see Kṛṣṇa everywhere, and there is no doubt about it." Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was a mediator between Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Brahmānanda Bhāratī, and his judgment was that an advanced devotee like Brahmānanda Bhāratī was seeing Kṛṣṇa by Kṛṣṇa's mercy. Kṛṣṇa directly presents Himself before the vision of an advanced devotee. Since Brahmānanda Bhāratī was an advanced devotee, he saw Kṛṣṇa in the person of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. In the words of the //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.38):

> premāñjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena
> santaḥ sadaiva hṛdayeṣu vilokayanti
> yaṁ śyāmasundaram acintya-guṇa-svarūpaṁ
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi

"I worship the primeval, Lord Govinda, who is always seen by the devotee whose eyes are anointed with the pulp of love. He is seen in His eternal form of Śyāmasundara, situated within the heart of the devotee."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.182
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, what are you saying? Lord Viṣṇu, save Me! Such glorification is simply another form of blasphemy."
text:
> prabhu kahe,-'viṣṇu' 'viṣṇu', ki kaha sārvabhauma
> 'ati-stuti' haya ei nindāra lakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]] [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Lord Viṣṇu, Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---what are you speaking; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:a:ati]]-[[synonyms:s:stuti]]---overly glorifying; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:n:nindāra]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---symptom of blasphemy.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, what are you saying? Lord Viṣṇu, save Me! Such glorification is simply another form of blasphemy."
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was a little embarrassed by the Bhaṭṭācārya's statement; therefore He uttered the name Viṣṇu to save Himself. The Lord herein confirms that if one is overestimated, glorification is just another form of blasphemy. In this way He protests this so-called offensive statement.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.183
description: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took Brahmānanda Bhāratī with Him to His residence. From that time on, Brahmānanda Bhāratī remained with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> eta bali' bhāratīre lañā nija-vāsā āilā
> bhāratī-gosāñi prabhura nikaṭe rahilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:b:bhāratīre]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking with Him; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsā]] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned to His own residence; [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:n:nikaṭe]]---in the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained.
translation: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took Brahmānanda Bhāratī with Him to His residence. From that time on, Brahmānanda Bhāratī remained with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.184
description: Later, Rāmabhadra Ācārya and Bhagavān Ācārya also joined them and, giving up all other responsibilities, remained under Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's shelter.
text:
> rāmabhadrācārya, āra bhagavān ācārya
> prabhu-pade rahilā duṅhe chāḍi' sarva kārya
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāmabhadra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Rāmabhadra Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]] [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Bhagavān Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pade]]---under the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:s:sarva]] [[synonyms:k:kārya]]---all other responsibilities.
translation: Later, Rāmabhadra Ācārya and Bhagavān Ācārya also joined them and, giving up all other responsibilities, remained under Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's shelter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.185
description: The next day, Kāśīśvara Gosāñi also came and remained with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who received him with great respect.
text:
> kāśīśvara gosāñi āilā āra dine
> sammāna kariyā prabhu rākhilā nija sthāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāśīśvara]] [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Kāśīśvara Gosāñi, another devotee; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---the next day; [[synonyms:s:sammāna]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---giving all respect; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:rākhilā]]---kept; [[synonyms:n:nija]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---at His own place.
translation: The next day, Kāśīśvara Gosāñi also came and remained with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who received him with great respect.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.186
description: Kāśīśvara used to usher Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu into the Jagannātha temple. He would precede the Lord into the crowd and keep the people from touching Him.
text:
> prabhuke lañā karā'na īśvara daraśana
> āge loka-bhiḍa saba kari' nivāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:karā'na]]---helps in; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:b:bhiḍa]]---crowds of people; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:n:nivāraṇa]]---restraining.
translation: Kāśīśvara used to usher Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu into the Jagannātha temple. He would precede the Lord into the crowd and keep the people from touching Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.187
description: As all the rivers flow into the sea, all the devotees throughout the country finally came to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's shelter.
text:
> yata nada nadī yaiche samudre milaya
> aiche mahāprabhura bhakta yāhāṅ tāhāṅ haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:n:nada]] [[synonyms:n:nadī]]---rivers; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:s:samudre]]---in the sea; [[synonyms:m:milaya]]---meet; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---similarly; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotees; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---they were.
translation: As all the rivers flow into the sea, all the devotees throughout the country finally came to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's shelter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.188
description: Since all the devotees came to Him for shelter, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu showed them all mercy and kept them under His protection.
text:
> sabe āsi' mililā prabhura śrī-caraṇe
> prabhu kṛpā kari' sabāya rākhila nija sthāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---under the shelter; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing mercy; [[synonyms:s:sabāya]]---every one of them; [[synonyms:r:rākhila]]---kept; [[synonyms:n:nija]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---under His protection.
translation: Since all the devotees came to Him for shelter, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu showed them all mercy and kept them under His protection.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.189
description: Thus I have described the meeting of all the Vaiṣṇavas with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Whoever hears this description ultimately attains His shelter.
text:
> ei ta' kahila prabhura vaiṣṇava-milana
> ihā yei śune, pāya caitanya-caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---thus; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---I have described; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting with all the Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this narration; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hears; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Thus I have described the meeting of all the Vaiṣṇavas with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Whoever hears this description ultimately attains His shelter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.19
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "His Holiness Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will return very soon. I wish to have a nice place ready for Him, a place solitary and peaceful.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya kahe,-teṅho āsibe alpa-kāle
> rahite tāṅre eka sthāna cāhiye virale

translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "His Holiness Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will return very soon. I wish to have a nice place ready for Him, a place solitary and peaceful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.190
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation:
Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Tenth Chapter, describing the Lord's meeting the Vaiṣṇavas upon His return to Jagannātha Purī from South India.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.2
description: All glories to Lord Caitanya All glories to Nityānanda! All glories to Advaitacandra! And all glories to all the devotees of Lord Caitanya!
text:
> jaya jaya śrī-caitanya jaya nityānanda
> jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---to Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---to Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---to all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All glories to Lord Caitanya All glories to Nityānanda! All glories to Advaitacandra! And all glories to all the devotees of Lord Caitanya!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.20
description: "Lord Caitanya's residence should be very much secluded and also near the temple of Jagannātha. Please consider this proposal and give me a nice place for Him."
text:
> ṭhākurera nikaṭa, āra ha-ibe nirjane
> e-mata nirṇaya kari' deha' eka sthāne

translation: "Lord Caitanya's residence should be very much secluded and also near the temple of Jagannātha. Please consider this proposal and give me a nice place for Him."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.21
description: The King replied, "Kāśī Miśra's house is exactly what you require. It is near the temple and is very much secluded, calm and quiet."
text:
> rājā kahe,-aiche kāśī-miśrera bhavana
> ṭhākurera nikaṭa, haya parama nirjana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the King replied; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---exactly like that; [[synonyms:k:kāśī]]-[[synonyms:m:miśrera]] [[synonyms:b:bhavana]]---the house of Kāśī Miśra; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākurera]] [[synonyms:n:nikaṭa]]---near Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---very much; [[synonyms:n:nirjana]]---secluded.
translation: The King replied, "Kāśī Miśra's house is exactly what you require. It is near the temple and is very much secluded, calm and quiet."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.22
description: After saying this, the King became very anxious for the Lord to return. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then went to Kāśī Miśra to convey the King's desire.
text:
> eta kahi' rājā rahe utkaṇṭhita hañā
> bhaṭṭācārya kāśī-miśre kahila āsiyā

translation: After saying this, the King became very anxious for the Lord to return. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then went to Kāśī Miśra to convey the King's desire.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.23
description: When Kāśī Miśra heard the proposal, he said, "I am very fortunate that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord of all prabhus, will stay at my home."
text:
> kāśī-miśra kahe,-āmi baḍa bhāgyavān
> mora gṛhe 'prabhu-pādera' habe avasthāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāśī]]-[[synonyms:m:miśra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Kāśī Miśra said; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very much; [[synonyms:b:bhāgyavān]]---fortunate; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---in my home; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pādera]]---of the Lord of the //prabhus//; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:a:avasthāna]]---staying.
translation: When Kāśī Miśra heard the proposal, he said, "I am very fortunate that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord of all prabhus, will stay at my home."
purport:
In this verse the word //prabhupāda,// referring to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, is significant. Regarding this, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda comments, "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and all His servants address Him as Prabhupāda. This means that there are many //prabhus// taking shelter under His lotus feet." The pure Vaiṣṇava is addressed as //prabhu,// and this address is an etiquette observed between Vaiṣṇavas. When many //prabhus// remain under the shelter of the lotus feet of another //prabhu,// the address Prabhupāda is given. Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu and Śrī Advaita Prabhu are also addressed as Prabhupāda. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Śrī Advaita Prabhu and Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu are all //viṣṇu-tattva,// the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Viṣṇu. Therefore all living entities are under Their lotus feet. Lord Viṣṇu is the eternal Lord of everyone, and the representative of Lord Viṣṇu is the Lord's confidential servant. Such a person acts as the spiritual master for neophyte Vaiṣṇavas; therefore the spiritual master is as respectable as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya or Lord Viṣṇu Himself. For this reason the spiritual master is addressed as Oṁ Viṣṇupāda or Prabhupāda. The //ācārya,// the spiritual master, is generally respected by others as Śrīpāda, and the initiated Vaiṣṇavas are addressed as Prabhu. Prabhu, Prabhupāda and Viṣṇupāda are described in revealed scriptures like //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Caitanya-caritāmṛta// and //Caitanya-bhāgavata.// In this regard, these scriptures present evidence accepted by unalloyed devotees.

The //prākṛta-sahajiyās// are not even worthy of being called Vaiṣṇavas. They think that only caste //gosvāmīs// should be called Prabhupāda. Such ignorant //sahajiyās// call themselves //vaiṣṇava-dāsa-anudāsa,// which means the servant of the servant of the Vaiṣṇavas. However, they are opposed to addressing a pure Vaiṣṇava as Prabhupāda. In other words, they are envious of a bona fide spiritual master who is addressed as Prabhupāda, and they commit offenses by considering a bona fide spiritual master an ordinary human being or a member of a certain caste. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura describes such //sahajiyās// as most unfortunate. Because of their misconceptions, they fall into a hellish condition.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.24

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.26
description: Hearing of the Lord's return, everyone became very happy, and they all went to Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and spoke to him as follows.

> śuni' ānandita haila sabākāra mana

translation: Hearing of the Lord's return, everyone became very happy, and they all went to Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and spoke to him as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.27
description: "Please arrange our meeting with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. It is only by your mercy that we can attain the shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord."
text:
> prabhura sahita āmā-sabāra karāha milana

translation: "Please arrange our meeting with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. It is only by your mercy that we can attain the shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.28

text:
> bhaṭṭācārya kahe,-kāli kāśī-miśrera ghare

translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya replied to the people, "Tomorrow the Lord will be at the house of Kāśī Miśra. I shall arrange for you all to meet Him."

text:
> āra dina mahāprabhu bhaṭṭācāryera saṅge

translation: The next day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived and went with Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, with great enthusiasm, to see the temple of Lord Jagannātha.

translation: After seeing Lord Jagannātha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu left the temple. The Bhaṭṭācārya then took Him to the house of Kāśī Miśra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.40
description: "In Your absence all these people have been exactly like thirsty cātaka birds crying in disappointment. Kindly accept them."
text:
> tṛṣita cātaka yaiche kare hāhākāra
> taiche ei saba,-sabe kara aṅgīkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tṛṣita]]---thirsty; [[synonyms:c:cātaka]]---the //cātaka// bird; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just as; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:h:hāhā]]-[[synonyms:k:kāra]]---vibration of disappointment; [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---similarly; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of these; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---kindly accept.
translation: "In Your absence all these people have been exactly like thirsty cātaka birds crying in disappointment. Kindly accept them."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.41
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya first introduced Janārdana, saying, "Here is Janārdana, servant of Lord Jagannātha. He renders service to the Lord when it is time to renovate His transcendental body."
text:
> jagannātha-sevaka ei, nāma-janārdana
> anavasare kare prabhura śrī-aṅga-sevana
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---servitor of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:j:janārdana]]---Janārdana; [[synonyms:a:anavasare]]---during the time of renovation; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---of the transcendental body; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---service.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya first introduced Janārdana, saying, "Here is Janārdana, servant of Lord Jagannātha. He renders service to the Lord when it is time to renovate His transcendental body."
purport: During Anavasara, after the Snāna-yātrā ceremony, Lord Jagannātha is absent from the temple for fifteen days so He can be renovated. This occurs annually. Janārdana, who is here being introduced to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, was rendering this service at the time. The renovation of Lord Jagannātha is also known as Nava-yauvana, which indicates that the Jagannātha Deity is being fully restored to youth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.42
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya continued, "This is Kṛṣṇadāsa, who carries a golden cane, and here is Śikhi Māhiti, who is in charge of writing.
text:
> kṛṣṇadāsa-nāma ei suvarṇa-vetra-dhārī
> śikhi māhāti-nāma ei likhanādhikārī
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:suvarṇa]]---golden; [[synonyms:v:vetra]]-[[synonyms:d:dhārī]]---carrier of the cane; [[synonyms:ś:śikhi]] [[synonyms:m:māhāti]]---Śikhi Māhiti; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:l:likhana]]-[[synonyms:a:adhikārī]]---entrusted with writing.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya continued, "This is Kṛṣṇadāsa, who carries a golden cane, and here is Śikhi Māhiti, who is in charge of writing.
purport: The person in charge of writing is also called //deula-karaṇa-pada-prāpta karmacārī.// He is employed especially to write the calendar called //Mātalā-pāṅji.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.43
description: "This is Pradyumna Miśra, who is chief of all Vaiṣṇavas. He is a great servitor of Jagannātha, and his name is Dāsa.
text:
> pradyumna-miśra iṅha vaiṣṇava pradhāna
> jagannāthera mahā-soyāra iṅha 'dāsa' nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pradyumna]]-[[synonyms:m:miśra]]---Pradyumna Miśra; [[synonyms:i:iṅha]]---this person; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---chief of all the Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:j:jagannāthera]]---of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:s:soyāra]]---great servitor; [[synonyms:i:iṅha]]---this; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---designated as Dāsa.
translation: "This is Pradyumna Miśra, who is chief of all Vaiṣṇavas. He is a great servitor of Jagannātha, and his name is Dāsa.
purport: In Orissa most of the //brāhmaṇas// have the title Dāsa. Generally it is understood that the word //dāsa// refers to those other than the //brāhmaṇas,// but in Orissa the //brāhmaṇas// use the Dāsa title. This is confirmed by Culli Bhaṭṭa. Actually, everyone is //dāsa// because everyone is a servant of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In that sense, the bona fide //brāhmaṇa// has first claim to the appellation //dāsa.// Therefore in this case the designation //dāsa// is not incompatible.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.44
description: "This is Murāri Māhiti, the brother of Śikhi Māhiti. He has nothing other than Your lotus feet.
text:
> murāri māhāti iṅha-śikhi-māhātira bhāi
> tomāra caraṇa vinu āra gati nāi
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:murāri]] [[synonyms:m:māhāti]]---Murāri Māhiti; [[synonyms:i:iṅha]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śikhi]]-[[synonyms:m:māhātira]]---of Śikhi Māhiti; [[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---younger brother; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---lotus feet; [[synonyms:v:vinu]]---without; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---any other; [[synonyms:g:gati]]---destination; [[synonyms:n:nāi]]---he does not have.
translation: "This is Murāri Māhiti, the brother of Śikhi Māhiti. He has nothing other than Your lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.45
description: "Here are Candaneśvara, Siṁheśvara, Murāri Brāhmaṇa and Viṣṇudāsa. They are all constantly engaged in meditating on Your lotus feet.
text:
> candaneśvara, siṁheśvara, murāri brāhmaṇa
> viṣṇudāsa,-iṅha dhyāye tomāra caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:candaneśvara]]---Candaneśvara; [[synonyms:s:siṁheśvara]]---Siṁheśvara; [[synonyms:m:murāri]] [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---the //brāhmaṇa// named Murāri; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇudāsa]]---Viṣṇudāsa; [[synonyms:i:iṅha]]---all of them; [[synonyms:d:dhyāye]]---meditate; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---on the lotus feet.
translation: "Here are Candaneśvara, Siṁheśvara, Murāri Brāhmaṇa and Viṣṇudāsa. They are all constantly engaged in meditating on Your lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.46
description: "This is Paramānanda Prahararāja, who is also known as Mahāpātra. He is very, very intelligent.
text:
> prahararāja mahāpātra iṅha mahā-mati
> paramānanda mahāpātra iṅhāra saṁhati
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prahararāja]]---Prahararāja; [[synonyms:m:mahāpātra]]---Mahāpātra; [[synonyms:i:iṅha]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:m:mati]]---very intelligent; [[synonyms:p:paramānanda]] [[synonyms:m:mahāpātra]]---Paramānanda Mahāpātra; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]]---of him; [[synonyms:s:saṁhati]]---combination.
translation: "This is Paramānanda Prahararāja, who is also known as Mahāpātra. He is very, very intelligent.
purport: Prahararāja is a designation given to //brāhmaṇas// who represent the king when the throne is vacant. In Orissa, between the time of a king's death and the enthronement of another king, a representative must sit on the throne. This representative is called Prahararāja. The Prahararāja is generally selected from a family of priests close to the king. During the time of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Prahararāja was Paramānanda Prahararāja.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.47
description: "All these pure devotees serve as ornaments to Jagannātha Purī. They are always undeviatingly meditating upon Your lotus feet."
text:
> e-saba vaiṣṇava-ei kṣetrera bhūṣaṇa
> ekānta-bhāve cinte sabe tomāra caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---all these pure devotees; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:k:kṣetrera]]---of this holy place; [[synonyms:b:bhūṣaṇa]]---ornaments; [[synonyms:e:ekānta]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---without deviation; [[synonyms:c:cinte]]---meditate; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---on Your lotus feet.
translation: "All these pure devotees serve as ornaments to Jagannātha Purī. They are always undeviatingly meditating upon Your lotus feet."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.48

> sabā āliṅgilā prabhu prasāda kariyā

translation: After this introduction, everyone fell to the ground like rods. Being very merciful upon them all, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced each one of them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.49
description: At this time Bhavānanda Rāya appeared with four of his sons, and all of them fell down at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> hena-kāle āilā tathā bhavānanda rāya
> cāri-putra-saṅge paḍe mahāprabhura pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---there; [[synonyms:b:bhavānanda]] [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Bhavānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:p:putra]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with four of his sons; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fell down; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: At this time Bhavānanda Rāya appeared with four of his sons, and all of them fell down at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
purport: Bhavānanda Rāya had five sons, one of whom was the exalted personality known as Rāmānanda Rāya. Bhavānanda Rāya first met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu after His return from South India. At that time Rāmānanda Rāya was still serving at his government post; therefore when Bhavānanda Rāya went to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he went with his other four sons. They were named Vāṇīnātha, Gopīnātha, Kalānidhi and Sudhānidhi. A description of Bhavānanda Rāya and his five sons is given in the //Ādi-līlā// (10.133-34).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.5
description: The King said to the Bhaṭṭācārya, "I have heard that a great personality has come from Bengal and is staying at your home. I have also heard that He is very, very merciful.
text:
> śunilāṅa tomāra ghare eka mahāśaya
> gauḍa ha-ite āilā, teṅho mahā-kṛpāmaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śunilāṅa]]---I have heard; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at home; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:m:mahāśaya]]---great personality; [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---from Bengal; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---has come; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---very merciful.
translation: The King said to the Bhaṭṭācārya, "I have heard that a great personality has come from Bengal and is staying at your home. I have also heard that He is very, very merciful.

> sārvabhauma kahe,-ei rāya bhavānanda

translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya continued, "This is Bhavānanda Rāya, the father of Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya, who is his first son."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.51

text:
> tabe mahāprabhu tāṅre kaila āliṅgana
> stuti kari' kahe rāmānanda-vivaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereupon; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing; [[synonyms:s:stuti]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---praising very highly; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---of Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---description.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced Bhavānanda Rāya and with great respect spoke of his son Rāmānanda Rāya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.52
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu honored Bhavānanda Rāya by saying, "The glories of a person who has a jewel of a son like Rāmānanda Rāya cannot be described within this mortal world.
text:
> rāmānanda-hena ratna yāṅhāra tanaya
> tāṅhāra mahimā loke kahana nā yāya

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu honored Bhavānanda Rāya by saying, "The glories of a person who has a jewel of a son like Rāmānanda Rāya cannot be described within this mortal world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.53
description: "You are Mahārāja Pāṇḍu himself, and your wife is Kuntīdevī herself. All your highly intellectual sons are representatives of the five Pāṇḍavas."
text:
> sākṣāt pāṇḍu tumi, tomāra patnī kuntī
> pañca-pāṇḍava tomāra pañca-putra mahā-mati
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]] [[synonyms:p:pāṇḍu]]---directly Mahārāja Pāṇḍu; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:p:patnī]]---wife; [[synonyms:k:kuntī]]---like Kuntīdevī; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:p:pāṇḍava]]---five Pāṇḍavas; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:p:putra]]---five sons; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:m:mati]]---all highly intellectual.
translation: "You are Mahārāja Pāṇḍu himself, and your wife is Kuntīdevī herself. All your highly intellectual sons are representatives of the five Pāṇḍavas."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.54
description: After hearing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's praise, Bhavānanda Rāya submitted, "I am in the fourth class of the social order, and I engage in mundane affairs. Although I am very much fallen, You have still touched me. This is proof that You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead."
text:
> rāya kahe,-āmi śūdra, viṣayī, adhama
> tabu tumi sparśa,-ei īśvara-lakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Bhavānanda Rāya replied; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:ś:śūdra]]---I belong to the fourth class of the social divisions; [[synonyms:v:viṣayī]]---engaged in mundane affairs; [[synonyms:a:adhama]]---very much fallen; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:s:sparśa]]---touch; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---sign of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: After hearing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's praise, Bhavānanda Rāya submitted, "I am in the fourth class of the social order, and I engage in mundane affairs. Although I am very much fallen, You have still touched me. This is proof that You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead."
purport:
As stated in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:5:18|(Bg. 5.18)]]:

> vidyā-vinaya-sampanne
> brāhmaṇe gavi hastini
> śuni caiva śva-pāke ca
> paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ

"The humble sages, by virtue of true knowledge, see with equal vision a learned and gentle //brāhmaṇa,// a cow, an elephant, a dog and a dog-eater [outcaste]."

Those who are highly advanced in spiritual understanding do not care about a person's material condition. A spiritually advanced person sees the spiritual identity of every living being, and consequently he makes no distinction between a learned //brāhmaṇa,// a dog, a //caṇḍāla// or anyone else. He is not influenced by the material body but sees a person's spiritual identity. Consequently Bhavānanda Rāya appreciated Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's statement, which showed that the Lord did not consider the social position of Bhavānanda Rāya, who belonged to the //śūdra// caste engaged in mundane activities. Rather, the Lord considered the spiritual position of Bhavānanda Rāya, along with that of Rāmānanda Rāya and his brothers. The servant of the Lord is also similarly inclined. He gives shelter to any person-any living entity-regardless of whether he belongs to a //brāhmaṇa// family or a //caṇḍāla// family. The spiritual master reclaims all people and encourages everyone in spiritual life. By taking shelter of such a devotee, one can make his life successful. As confirmed in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:4:18|(2.4.18)]]:

> kirāta-hūṇāndhra-pulinda-pulkaśā
> ābhīra-śumbhā yavanāḥ khasādayaḥ
> ye 'nye ca pāpā yad-apāśrayāśrayāḥ
> śudhyanti tasmai prabhaviṣṇave namaḥ

"Members of the Kirāta, Hūṇa, Āndhra, Pulinda, Pulkaśa, Ābhīra, Śumbha, Yavana and Khasa races, and even others addicted to sinful acts, can be purified by taking shelter of the devotees of the Lord, due to His being the supreme power. I beg to offer my respectful obeisances unto Him."

Whoever takes shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead or His pure devotee is elevated to the spiritual order and purified from material contamination. This is also confirmed by Kṛṣṇa in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:32|(Bg. 9.32)]]:

> māṁ hi pārtha vyapāśritya
> ye 'pi syuḥ pāpa-yonayaḥ
> striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrās
> te 'pi yānti parāṁ gatim

"O son of Pṛthā, those who take shelter in Me, though they be of lower birth-women, //vaiśyas// [merchants] and //śūdras// [workers]---can attain the supreme destination."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.55
description: Appreciating Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's favor, Bhavānanda Rāya also said, "Along with my home, riches, servants and five sons, I surrender myself at Your lotus feet.
text:
> nija-gṛha-vitta-bhṛtya-pañca-putra-sane
> ātmā samarpiluṅ āmi tomāra caraṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]---own; [[synonyms:g:gṛha]]---house; [[synonyms:v:vitta]]---wealth; [[synonyms:b:bhṛtya]]---servants; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:p:putra]]---five sons; [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---self; [[synonyms:s:samarpiluṅ]]---surrender; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the lotus feet.
translation: Appreciating Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's favor, Bhavānanda Rāya also said, "Along with my home, riches, servants and five sons, I surrender myself at Your lotus feet.
purport:
This is the process of surrender. As Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura sings:

> mānasa, deha, geha, yo kichu mora
> arpiluṅ tuyā pade nanda-kiśora!

(//Śaraṇāgati//)

When one surrenders unto the lotus feet of the Lord, he does so with everything in his possession-his house, his body, his mind and whatever else he possesses. If there is any obstruction to this surrendering process, one should immediately give it up without attachment. If one can surrender with all his family members, there is no need to take //sannyāsa.// However, if the surrendering process is hampered by so-called family members, one should immediately give them up to complete the surrendering process.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.56
description: "This son Vāṇīnātha will remain at Your lotus feet to always immediately attend to Your orders and serve You.
text:
> ei vāṇīnātha rahibe tomara caraṇe
> yabe yei ājñā, tāhā karibe sevane

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.62

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My dear Bhaṭṭācārya, just consider this man's character. He went with Me to South India.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.64
description: "He left My company to associate with the Bhaṭṭathāris, but I rescued him from their company and brought him here.
text:
> bhaṭṭathāri-kāche gelā āmāre chāḍiyā
> bhaṭṭathāri haite iṅhāre āniluṅ uddhāriyā

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.65
description: "Now that I have brought him here, I am asking him to leave. Now he can go wherever he likes, for I am no longer responsible for him."
text:
> ebe āmi ihāṅ āni' karilāṅa vidāya
> yāhāṅ icchā, yāha, āmā-sane nāhi āra dāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:k:karilāṅa]] [[synonyms:v:vidāya]]---have asked to go away; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---wherever he likes; [[synonyms:y:yāha]]---go; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with Me; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---there is no more; [[synonyms:d:dāya]]---responsibility.
translation: "Now that I have brought him here, I am asking him to leave. Now he can go wherever he likes, for I am no longer responsible for him."
purport: Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa was influenced and allured by nomads or gypsies, who enticed him with women. //Māyā// is so strong that Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa left Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's company to join gypsy women. Even though a person may associate with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he can be allured by //māyā// and leave the Lord's company due to his slight independence. Only one who is overwhelmed by //māyā// can be so unfortunate as to leave Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's company, yet unless one is very conscientious, the influence of //māyā// can drag one away, even though he be the personal assistant of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. And what to speak of others? The Bhaṭṭathāris used to increase their numbers by using women to allure outsiders. This is factual evidence showing that it is possible at any time to fall down from the Lord's association. One need only misuse his little independence. Once fallen and separated from the Supreme Personality of Godhead's association, one becomes a candidate for suffering in the material world. Although rejected by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa was given another chance, as the following verses relate.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.66
description: Hearing the Lord reject him, Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa began to cry. However, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, not caring for him, immediately left to take His noon lunch.
text:
> eta śuni' kṛṣṇadāsa kāndite lāgila
> madhyāhna karite mahāprabhu cali' gela
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:k:kāndite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began to cry; [[synonyms:m:madhyāhna]]---noon lunch; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to execute; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cali']] [[synonyms:g:gela]]---left.
translation: Hearing the Lord reject him, Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa began to cry. However, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, not caring for him, immediately left to take His noon lunch.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.67
description: After this, the other devotees-headed by Nityānanda Prabhu, Jagadānanda, Mukunda and Dāmodara-began to consider a certain plan.
text:
> nityānanda, jagadānanda, mukunda, dāmodara
> cāri-jane yukti tabe karilā antara
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jagadānanda]]---Jagadānanda; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Dāmodara; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---four persons; [[synonyms:y:yukti]]---plan; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereupon; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:a:antara]]---within the mind.
translation: After this, the other devotees-headed by Nityānanda Prabhu, Jagadānanda, Mukunda and Dāmodara-began to consider a certain plan.
purport: Even though a person is rejected by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the devotees of the Lord do not reject him; therefore the Lord's devotees are more merciful than the Lord Himself. Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura thus sings, //chāḍiyā vaiṣṇava-sevā nistāra pāyeche kebā:// one cannot be relieved from the material clutches without engaging in the service of pure devotees. The Lord Himself may sometimes be very hard, but the devotees are always kind. Thus Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa received the mercy of the four devotees mentioned above.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.68

translation: The Lord's four devotees considered, "We want a person to go to Bengal just to inform Śacīmātā about Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's arrival at Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.69

text:
> advaita-śrīvāsādi yata bhakta-gaṇa
> sabei āsibe śuni' prabhura āgamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---Advaita Prabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and all the devotees like Śrīvāsa; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---devotees; [[synonyms:s:sabei]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:āsibe]]---will come; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---arrival.
translation: "After hearing news of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's arrival, devotees like Advaita and Śrīvāsa will certainly come to see Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.7
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "All that you have heard is true, but as far as an interview is concerned, it is very difficult to arrange.

translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "All that you have heard is true, but as far as an interview is concerned, it is very difficult to arrange.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.70
description: "Let us therefore send Kṛṣṇadāsa to Bengal." Saying this, they kept Kṛṣṇadāsa engaged in the service of the Lord and gave him assurance.
text:
> ei kṛṣṇadāse diba gauḍe pāṭhāñā
> eta kahi' tāre rākhilena āśvāsiyā

translation: "Let us therefore send Kṛṣṇadāsa to Bengal." Saying this, they kept Kṛṣṇadāsa engaged in the service of the Lord and gave him assurance.
purport: Because Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu rejected him, Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa became very, very sorry and began to cry. Therefore the Lord's devotees took compassion upon him, gave him assurance and encouraged him to continue to engage in the Lord's service.

synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---next day; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---before Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---submission; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:deha']]---please give permission; [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---to Bengal; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāi]]---we may send; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---one person.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.72

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.73

text:
> eka-jana yāi' kahuk śubha samācāra

synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---one person; [[synonyms:y:yāi']]---going; [[synonyms:k:kahuk]]---may inform; [[synonyms:ś:śubha]] [[synonyms:s:samācāra]]---this auspicious news; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord replied; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---do that; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---desire; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your.

"One person should go to Bengal and inform them about the auspicious news of Your return to Jagannātha Purī."


Upon hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "Do whatever you decide."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.74

> vaiṣṇava-sabāke dite mahā-prasāda dila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāse]]---Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:g:gauḍe]]---to Bengal; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāila]]---sent; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāke]]---to all the Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to deliver; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---the remnants of Jagannātha's food; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---they gave.
translation: In this way Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa was sent to Bengal, and he was given sufficient quantities of Lord Jagannātha's food remnants to distribute there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.75
description: Thus Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa went to Bengal, and he first went to Navadvīpa to see mother Śacī.
text:
> tabe gauḍa-deśe āilā kālā-kṛṣṇadāsa
> navadvīpe gela teṅha śacī-āi-pāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---to Bengal; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:k:kālā]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:n:navadvīpe]]---to Navadvīpa; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went; [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---he; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:ā:āi]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---before mother Śacī.
translation: Thus Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa went to Bengal, and he first went to Navadvīpa to see mother Śacī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.76
description: Upon reaching mother Śacī, Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa first offered his obeisances and delivered the food remnants [mahā-prasāda]. He then informed her of the good news that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had returned from His South Indian tour.
text:
> mahā-prasāda diyā tāṅre kaila namaskāra
> dakṣiṇa haite āilā prabhu,-kahe samācāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---delivering the //mahā-prasāda//; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Śacīmātā; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---he offered respects by bowing down; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the South India tour; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came back; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahe]] [[synonyms:s:samācāra]]---he delivered this news.
translation: Upon reaching mother Śacī, Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa first offered his obeisances and delivered the food remnants [mahā-prasāda]. He then informed her of the good news that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had returned from His South Indian tour.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.77
description: This good news gave much pleasure to mother Śacī, as well as to all the devotees of Navadvīpa, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura.
text:
> śuniyā ānandita haila śacīmātāra mana
> śrīvāsādi āra yata yata bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very happy; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:m:mātāra]]---of mother Śacī; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by Śrīvāsa; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and others; [[synonyms:y:yata]] [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---devotees.
translation: This good news gave much pleasure to mother Śacī, as well as to all the devotees of Navadvīpa, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.78
description: Hearing of Lord Caitanya's return to Purī, everyone became very glad. Kṛṣṇadāsa next went to the house of Advaita Ācārya.
text:
> śuniyā sabāra haila parama ullāsa
> advaita-ācārya-gṛhe gelā kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---supreme; [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---happiness; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---of Advaita Ācārya Prabhu; [[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---to the home; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Kṛṣṇadāsa.
translation: Hearing of Lord Caitanya's return to Purī, everyone became very glad. Kṛṣṇadāsa next went to the house of Advaita Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.79
description: After paying Him respectful obeisances, Kṛṣṇadāsa offered mahā-prasāda to Advaita Ācārya. He then informed Him of the news of Lord Caitanya in complete detail.
text:
> ācāryere prasāda diyā kari' namaskāra
> samyak kahila mahāprabhura samācāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryere]]---unto Śrī Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---the remnants of Jagannātha's food; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---delivering; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:s:samyak]]---completely; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---informed; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:samācāra]]---news.
translation: After paying Him respectful obeisances, Kṛṣṇadāsa offered mahā-prasāda to Advaita Ācārya. He then informed Him of the news of Lord Caitanya in complete detail.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.8
description: "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is in the renounced order and is very much detached from worldly affairs. He stays in solitary places, and even in dreams He does not grant interviews to a king.
text:
> virakta sannyāsī teṅho rahena nirjane
> svapneha nā karena teṅho rāja-daraśane
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:virakta]]---detached; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---in the renounced order; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:r:rahena]]---keeps Himself; [[synonyms:n:nirjane]]---in a solitary place; [[synonyms:s:svapneha]]---even in dreams; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---do; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---interview with a king.
translation: "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is in the renounced order and is very much detached from worldly affairs. He stays in solitary places, and even in dreams He does not grant interviews to a king.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.80
description: When Advaita Ācārya Gosvāmī heard of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's return, He became very much pleased. In His great ecstasy of love, He made a rumbling sound and danced and chanted for a long time.
text:
> śuni' ācārya-gosāñira ānanda ha-ila
> premāveśe huṅkāra bahu nṛtya-gīta kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of the spiritual master; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was much jubilation; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in great ecstasy; [[synonyms:h:huṅkāra]]---rumbling sound; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---various; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]---chanting and dancing; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed.
translation: When Advaita Ācārya Gosvāmī heard of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's return, He became very much pleased. In His great ecstasy of love, He made a rumbling sound and danced and chanted for a long time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.81
description: Also hearing this auspicious news, Haridāsa Ṭhākura became very much pleased. So also did Vāsudeva Datta, Murāri Gupta and Śivānanda Sena.
text:
> haridāsa ṭhākurera haila parama ānanda
> vāsudeva datta, gupta murāri, sena śivānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākurera]]---of Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---topmost; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---ecstasy; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]] [[synonyms:d:datta]]---Vāsudeva Datta; [[synonyms:g:gupta]] [[synonyms:m:murāri]]---Murāri Gupta; [[synonyms:s:sena]] [[synonyms:ś:śivānanda]]---Śivānanda Sena.
translation: Also hearing this auspicious news, Haridāsa Ṭhākura became very much pleased. So also did Vāsudeva Datta, Murāri Gupta and Śivānanda Sena.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.82
description: Ācāryaratna, Vakreśvara Paṇḍita, Ācāryanidhi and Gadādhara Paṇḍita were all very much pleased to hear this news.
text:
> ācāryaratna, āra paṇḍita vakreśvara
> ācāryanidhi, āra paṇḍita gadādhara
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryaratna]]---Ācāryaratna; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]] [[synonyms:v:vakreśvara]]---Vakreśvara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryanidhi]]---Ācāryanidhi; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]] [[synonyms:g:gadādhara]]---Gadādhara Paṇḍita.
translation: Ācāryaratna, Vakreśvara Paṇḍita, Ācāryanidhi and Gadādhara Paṇḍita were all very much pleased to hear this news.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.83
description: Śrīrāma Paṇḍita, Dāmodara Paṇḍita, Śrīmān Paṇḍita, Vijaya and Śrīdhara were also very much pleased to hear it.
text:
> śrīrāma paṇḍita āra paṇḍita dāmodara
> śrīmān paṇḍita, āra vijaya, śrīdhara
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rāma]] [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---Śrīrāma Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]] [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Dāmodara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:ś:śrīmān]] [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---Śrīmān Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:v:vijaya]]---Vijaya; [[synonyms:ś:śrīdhara]]---Śrīdhara.
translation: Śrīrāma Paṇḍita, Dāmodara Paṇḍita, Śrīmān Paṇḍita, Vijaya and Śrīdhara were also very much pleased to hear it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.84
description: Rāghava Paṇḍita, the son of Advaita Ācārya and all the devotees became very much satisfied. How many can I describe?
text:
> rāghava-paṇḍita, āra ācārya nandana
> kateka kahiba āra yata prabhura gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāghava]]-[[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---Rāghava Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:kateka]]---how many; [[synonyms:k:kahiba]]---shall I describe; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---other; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---associates of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Rāghava Paṇḍita, the son of Advaita Ācārya and all the devotees became very much satisfied. How many can I describe?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.85
description: Everyone was very much pleased, and they all gathered together at the house of Advaita Ācārya.
text:
> śuniyā sabāra haila parama ullāsa
> sabe meli' gelā śrī-advaitera pāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---great ecstasy; [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:m:meli']]---all together; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:a:advaitera]] [[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---to the house of Śrī Advaita Ācārya.
translation: Everyone was very much pleased, and they all gathered together at the house of Advaita Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.86
description: All the devotees offered respectful obeisances at the lotus feet of Advaita Ācārya, and in return Advaita Ācārya embraced them all.
text:
> ācāryera sabe kaila caraṇa vandana
> ācārya-gosāñi sabāre kaila āliṅgana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]]---of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---offering obeisances at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---to all; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing.
translation: All the devotees offered respectful obeisances at the lotus feet of Advaita Ācārya, and in return Advaita Ācārya embraced them all.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.87
description: Advaita Ācārya then held a festival that lasted two or three days. Thereafter, they all made a firm decision to go to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> dina dui-tina ācārya mahotsava kaila
> nīlācala yāite ācārya yukti dṛḍha kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dina]] [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:t:tina]]---for two or three days; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:m:mahotsava]]---festival; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:n:nīlācala]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:y:yukti]]---consideration; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]]---firm; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made.
translation: Advaita Ācārya then held a festival that lasted two or three days. Thereafter, they all made a firm decision to go to Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.88
description: All the devotees met together at Navadvīpa and, with mother Śacī's permission, departed for Nīlādri, Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> sabe meli' navadvīpe ekatra hañā
> nīlādri calila śacīmātāra ājñā lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:m:meli']]---meeting; [[synonyms:n:navadvīpe]]---at Navadvīpa; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being together; [[synonyms:n:nīlādri]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:c:calila]]---departed; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:m:mātāra]]---of mother Śacī; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---permission; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking.
translation: All the devotees met together at Navadvīpa and, with mother Śacī's permission, departed for Nīlādri, Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.89
description: The inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma-Satyarāja, Rāmānanda and all the other devotees there-came and joined Advaita Ācārya.
text:
> prabhura samācāra śuni' kulīna-grāma-vāsī
> satyarāja-rāmānanda mililā sabe āsi'
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:samācāra]]---news; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:k:kulīna]]-[[synonyms:g:grāma]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---the inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma; [[synonyms:s:satyarāja]]---Satyarāja; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming.
translation: The inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma-Satyarāja, Rāmānanda and all the other devotees there-came and joined Advaita Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.9
description: "Still, I would have tried to arrange your interview, but He has recently left to tour South India."
text:
> tathāpi prakāre tomā karāitāma daraśana
> samprati karilā teṅho dakṣiṇa gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---yet; [[synonyms:p:prakāre]]---somehow or other; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]---you; [[synonyms:k:karāitāma]]---I would have arranged; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---interview; [[synonyms:s:samprati]]---recently; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---has done; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]]---to the southern part of India; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---departure.
translation: "Still, I would have tried to arrange your interview, but He has recently left to tour South India."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.90
description: Mukunda, Narahari, Raghunandana and all the others came from Khaṇḍa to Advaita Ācārya's home to accompany Him to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> mukunda, narahari, raghunandana khaṇḍa haite
> ācāryera ṭhāñi āilā nīlācala yāite
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:n:narahari]]---Narahari; [[synonyms:r:raghunandana]]---Raghunandana; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the place known as Khaṇḍa; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---to Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:n:nīlācala]] [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go to Nīlācala (Jagannātha Purī).
translation: Mukunda, Narahari, Raghunandana and all the others came from Khaṇḍa to Advaita Ācārya's home to accompany Him to Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.91
description: At that time Paramānanda Purī came from South India. Traveling along the banks of the Ganges, he ultimately reached the town of Nadia.
text:
> se-kāle dakṣiṇa haite paramānanda-purī
> gaṅgā-tīre-tīre āilā nadīyā nagarī
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the South; [[synonyms:p:paramānanda]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---along the bank of the Ganges; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:n:nadīyā]] [[synonyms:n:nagarī]]---to the town of Nadia.
translation: At that time Paramānanda Purī came from South India. Traveling along the banks of the Ganges, he ultimately reached the town of Nadia.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.92
description: At Navadvīpa, Paramānanda Purī took his board and lodging at the house of Śacīmātā. She provided him with everything very respectfully.
text:
> āira mandire sukhe karilā viśrāma
> āi tāṅre bhikṣā dilā kariyā sammāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āira]] [[synonyms:m:mandire]]---at the house of Śacīmātā; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in happiness; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---took; [[synonyms:v:viśrāma]]---lodging; [[synonyms:ā:āi]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave boarding; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:s:sammāna]]---with great respect.
translation: At Navadvīpa, Paramānanda Purī took his board and lodging at the house of Śacīmātā. She provided him with everything very respectfully.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.93
description: While residing at the house of Śacīmātā, Paramānanda Purī heard the news of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's return to Jagannātha Purī. He therefore decided to go there as soon as possible.
text:
> prabhura āgamana teṅha tāhāṅi śunila
> śīghra nīlācala yāite tāṅra icchā haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhuraāgamana]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's return; [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---he; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅi]]---there; [[synonyms:ś:śunila]]---heard; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]]---very soon; [[synonyms:n:nīlācala]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---desire; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became.
translation: While residing at the house of Śacīmātā, Paramānanda Purī heard the news of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's return to Jagannātha Purī. He therefore decided to go there as soon as possible.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 10.94
description: There was a devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's named Dvija Kamalākānta, whom Paramānanda Purī took with him to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> prabhura eka bhakta-'dvija kamalākānta' nāma
> tāṅre lañā nīlācale karilā prayāṇa

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.10
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Although it is correct that the King is a great devotee, he is still to be considered a venomous snake. Similarly, even though a woman be made of wood, one becomes agitated simply by touching her form.
text:
> prabhu kahe,-tathāpi rājā kāla-sarpākāra
> kāṣṭha-nārī-sparśe yaiche upaje vikāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]-[[synonyms:s:sarpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---just like a venomous snake; [[synonyms:k:kāṣṭha]]-[[synonyms:n:nārī]]---a woman made of wood; [[synonyms:s:sparśe]]---by touching; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:u:upaje]]---arises; [[synonyms:v:vikāra]]---agitation.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Although it is correct that the King is a great devotee, he is still to be considered a venomous snake. Similarly, even though a woman be made of wood, one becomes agitated simply by touching her form.
purport:
Śrī Cāṇakya Paṇḍita in his moral instructions has stated: //tyaja durjana-saṁsargaṁ bhaja sādhu-samāgamam.// This means that one has to abandon the association of materialistic people and associate with spiritually advanced people. However qualified a materialist may be, he is no better than a venomous serpent. Everyone knows that a snake is dangerous and poisonous, and when its hood is decorated with jewels, it is no less poisonous or dangerous. However qualified a materialist may be, he is no better than a snake decorated with jewels. One should therefore be careful in dealing with such materialists, just as one would be careful in dealing with a bejeweled serpent.

Even though a woman be made of wood or stone, she becomes attractive when decorated. One becomes sexually agitated even by touching the form. Therefore one should not trust his mind, which is so fickle that it can give way to enemies at any moment. The mind is always accompanied by six enemies-namely, //kāma, krodha, mada, moha, mātsarya// and //bhaya//---that is, lust, anger, intoxication, illusion, envy and fear. Although the mind may be merged in spiritual consciousness, one should always be very careful in dealing with it, just as one is careful in dealing with a snake. One should never think that his mind is trained and that he can do whatever he likes. One interested in spiritual life should always engage his mind in the service of the Lord so that the enemies of the mind, who always accompany the mind, will be subdued. If the mind is not engaged in Kṛṣṇa consciousness at every moment, there is a chance that it will give way to its enemies. In this way we become victims of the mind.

Chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// engages the mind at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa constantly; thus the mind's enemies do not have a chance to strike. Following Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's example in these verses, we should be very careful in dealing with the mind, which should not be indulged in any circumstance. Once we indulge the mind, it can create havoc in this life, even though we may be spiritually advanced. The mind is specifically agitated through the association of materialistic men and women. Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, through His personal behavior, warns everyone to avoid meeting a materialistic person or a woman.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.102
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "A person who has received but a small fraction of mercy from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu can understand that He is Lord Kṛṣṇa. No one else can.
text:
> bhaṭṭa kahe,-tāṅra kṛpā-leśa haya yāṅre
> sei se tāṅhāre 'kṛṣṇa' kari' la-ite pāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---of Lord Caitanya's mercy; [[synonyms:l:leśa]]---even a fraction; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:y:yāṅre]]---unto whom; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:se]]---that person only; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāre]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---accepting as Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---can take up.
translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "A person who has received but a small fraction of mercy from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu can understand that He is Lord Kṛṣṇa. No one else can.
purport: The //saṅkīrtana// movement can be spread by a person who is especially favored by Lord Kṛṣṇa (//kṛṣṇa-śakti vinā nahe tāra pravartana//). Without first obtaining the mercy of the Lord, one cannot spread the holy name of the Lord. One who can spread the Lord's name is called //labdha-caitanya// in the words of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī. The //labdha-caitanya// is one who has actually awakened his original consciousness, Kṛṣṇa consciousness. The influence of the pure devotees in Kṛṣṇa consciousness is such that it can awaken others to become immediately Kṛṣṇa conscious and engage themselves in the transcendental loving service of Kṛṣṇa. In this way the descendants of pure devotees increase, and Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu takes much pleasure in seeing the increase of His devotees. The word //su-medhasaḥ// means "sharply intelligent." When one's intelligence is sharp, he can increase the interests of common men in loving Caitanya Mahāprabhu and through Him in loving Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. Those not interested in understanding Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are simply material in their attempts at professional chanting and dancing for money, despite their supposed artistry. If one does not have full faith in Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he cannot properly chant and dance in the //saṅkīrtana// movement. Artificial chanting and dancing may be due to sentiments or sentimental agitation, but this cannot help one advance in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.
