description: "If the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is not bestowed upon a person-regardless of how learned a scholar that person may be and regardless of his seeing or listening-he cannot accept Lord Caitanya as the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> tāṅra kṛpā nahe yāre, paṇḍita nahe kene
> dekhile śunileha tāṅre 'īśvara' nā māne
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---His mercy; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---there is not; [[synonyms:y:yāre]]---unto whom; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---learned scholar; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---even though; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---nevertheless; [[synonyms:d:dekhile]]---even by seeing; [[synonyms:ś:śunileha]]---even by listening; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---as the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:m:māne]]---does not accept.
translation: "If the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is not bestowed upon a person-regardless of how learned a scholar that person may be and regardless of his seeing or listening-he cannot accept Lord Caitanya as the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
purport: The same principles can be applied to demoniac persons, even though they be in the //sampradāya// of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Without receiving the Lord's special power, one cannot preach His glories all over the world. Even though one may celebrate himself as a learned follower of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and even though one may attempt to preach the holy name of the Lord all over the world, if he is not favored by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu he will find fault with the pure devotee and will not be able to understand how a preacher is empowered by Lord Caitanya. One must be considered bereft of the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu when he criticizes the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement now spreading all over the world or finds fault with this movement or the leader of the movement.

> prasāda lañā saṅge cale pāṅca-sāta
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the King said; [[synonyms:b:bhavānandera]] [[synonyms:p:putra]]---the son of Bhavānanda; [[synonyms:v:vāṇīnātha]]---Vāṇīnātha; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking //mahā-prasāda//; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---along; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---goes; [[synonyms:p:pāṅca]]-[[synonyms:s:sāta]]---five or seven men.
translation: The King said, "The son of Bhavānanda Rāya named Vāṇīnātha, along with five or seven other men, went there to obtain the remnants of Lord Jagannātha's food.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.109
description: "Indeed, Vāṇīnātha has already gone to the residence of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and has taken a huge quantity of mahā-prasāda. Please let me know the reason for this."
text:
> mahāprabhura ālaye karila gamana
> eta mahā-prasāda cāhi'-kaha ki kāraṇa

translation: "Indeed, Vāṇīnātha has already gone to the residence of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and has taken a huge quantity of mahā-prasāda. Please let me know the reason for this."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.11
description: " 'Just as one is immediately frightened upon seeing a live serpent or even the form of a serpent, one endeavoring for self-realization should similarly fear a materialistic person and a woman. Indeed, he should not even glance at their bodily features.'
text:
> ākārād api bhetavyaṁ
> strīṇāṁ viṣayiṇām api
> yathāher manasaḥ kṣobhas
> tathā tasyākṛter api
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ākārāt]]---from bodily features; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:b:bhetavyam]]---to be feared; [[synonyms:s:strīṇām]]---of women; [[synonyms:v:viṣayiṇām]]---of materialistic persons; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:a:aheḥ]]---from a serpent; [[synonyms:m:manasaḥ]]---of the mind; [[synonyms:k:kṣobhaḥ]]---agitation; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---so; [[synonyms:t:tasya]]---of it; [[synonyms:ā:ākṛteḥ]]---from the appearance; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even.
translation: “ 'Just as one is immediately frightened upon seeing a live serpent or even the form of a serpent, one endeavoring for self-realization should similarly fear a materialistic person and a woman. Indeed, he should not even glance at their bodily features.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrī Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka// (8.24).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.110
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Understanding that all the devotees have come, Lord Caitanya gave the sign, and therefore Vāṇīnātha and the others have brought such great quantities of mahā-prasāda."
text:
> bhaṭṭa kahe,-bhakta-gaṇa āila jāniñā
> prabhura iṅgite prasāda yāya tāṅrā lañā

translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Understanding that all the devotees have come, Lord Caitanya gave the sign, and therefore Vāṇīnātha and the others have brought such great quantities of mahā-prasāda."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.111
description: The King then asked the Bhaṭṭācārya, "Why have the devotees not observed the regulations for visiting the pilgrimage place, such as fasting, shaving and so on? Why have they first eaten prasāda?"
text:
> rājā kahe,-upavāsa, kṣaura-tīrthera vidhāna
> tāhā nā kariyā kene khāiba anna-pāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the King said; [[synonyms:u:upavāsa]]---fasting; [[synonyms:k:kṣaura]]---shaving; [[synonyms:t:tīrthera]] [[synonyms:v:vidhāna]]---this is the regulation for visiting a holy place; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---without performing; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:k:khāiba]]---they shall eat; [[synonyms:a:anna]]-[[synonyms:p:pāna]]---solid and liquid food.
translation: The King then asked the Bhaṭṭācārya, "Why have the devotees not observed the regulations for visiting the pilgrimage place, such as fasting, shaving and so on? Why have they first eaten prasāda?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.112
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya told the King, "What you have said is right according to the regulative principles governing the visiting of holy places, but there is another path, which is the path of spontaneous love. According to those principles, there are subtle intricacies involved in the execution of religious principles.
text:
> bhaṭṭa kahe,-tumi yei kaha, sei vidhi-dharma
> ei rāga-mārge āche sūkṣma-dharma-marma
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---whatever you say; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---that is a regulative principle; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:r:rāga]]-[[synonyms:m:mārge]]---in this spontaneous love; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there are; [[synonyms:s:sūkṣma]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:m:marma]]---subtle intricacies of the religious system.
translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya told the King, "What you have said is right according to the regulative principles governing the visiting of holy places, but there is another path, which is the path of spontaneous love. According to those principles, there are subtle intricacies involved in the execution of religious principles.
purport:
According to the Vedic regulative principles, one has to be celibate before entering a holy place of pilgrimage. Generally people are very much addicted to sense gratification, and unless they have sex at night, they cannot sleep. The regulative principles therefore enjoin that before a common man goes to a holy place of pilgrimage, he should observe complete celibacy. As soon as one enters a holy place, he must observe fasting for the day, and after shaving his head clean, he must take a bath in a river or ocean near the holy place. These methods are adopted to neutralize the effects of sinful activities. Visiting a holy place of pilgrimage means neutralizing the reactions of a sinful life. Those who go to holy places of pilgrimage actually unload the reactions of their sinful lives, and consequently holy places are overloaded with sinful activities left there by visitors.

When a saintly person or pure devotee visits such a holy place, he absorbs the sinful effects left by the common man and again purifies the holy place. //Tīrthī-kurvanti tīrthāni// [[books:sb:1:13:10|(Bhāg. 1.13.10)]]. Therefore a common man's visit to a holy place and an exalted saintly person's visit there are different. The common man leaves his sins in the holy place, and a saintly person or devotee cleanses these sins simply by his presence. The devotees of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu were not common men, and they could not be subjected to the rules and regulations governing the visiting of holy places. Rather, they exhibited their spontaneous love for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Immediately upon arrival at the holy place, they went to see Lord Caitanya, and by His order they took //mahā-prasāda// without following the regulations governing holy places.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.113
description: "The scriptural injunctions for shaving and fasting are indirect orders of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. However, when there is a direct order from the Lord to take prasāda, naturally the devotees take prasāda as their first duty.
text:
> īśvarera parokṣa ājñā-kṣaura, upoṣaṇa
> prabhura sākṣāt ājñā-prasāda-bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ī:īśvarera]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:p:parokṣa]]---indirect; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:k:kṣaura]]---shaving; [[synonyms:u:upoṣaṇa]]---fasting; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---direct; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]-[[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---to take the //prasāda.//
translation: "The scriptural injunctions for shaving and fasting are indirect orders of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. However, when there is a direct order from the Lord to take prasāda, naturally the devotees take prasāda as their first duty.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.114
description: "When mahā-prasāda is not available, there must be fasting, but when the Supreme Personality of Godhead directly orders one to take prasāda, neglecting such an opportunity is offensive.
text:
> tāhāṅ upavāsa, yāhāṅ nāhi mahā-prasāda
> prabhu-ājñā-prasāda-tyāge haya aparādha
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:u:upavāsa]]---fasting; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---remnants of food of the Lord; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---direct order of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---remnants of food; [[synonyms:t:tyāge]]---giving up; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:a:aparādha]]---offense.
translation: "When mahā-prasāda is not available, there must be fasting, but when the Supreme Personality of Godhead directly orders one to take prasāda, neglecting such an opportunity is offensive.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.115
description: "When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is distributing prasāda with His transcendental hand, who will neglect such an opportunity and accept the regulative principle of fasting?
text:
> viśeṣe śrī-haste prabhu kare pariveśana
> eta lābha chāḍi' kon kare upoṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viśeṣe]]---especially; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:h:haste]]---with His transcendental hands; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:p:pariveśana]]---distribution; [[synonyms:e:eta]]---so much; [[synonyms:l:lābha]]---profit; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:k:kon]]---who; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:u:upoṣaṇa]]---fasting.
translation: "When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is distributing prasāda with His transcendental hand, who will neglect such an opportunity and accept the regulative principle of fasting?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.116
description: "Previously the Lord gave me mahā-prasāda rice one morning, and I ate that just sitting on my bed, without having even washed my mouth.
text:
> pūrve prabhu more prasāda-anna āni' dila
> prāte śayyāya vasi' āmi se anna khāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---before this; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto me; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]-[[synonyms:a:anna]]---rice //mahā-prasāda//; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---delivered; [[synonyms:p:prāte]]---early in the morning; [[synonyms:ś:śayyāya]]---on my bed; [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---rice; [[synonyms:k:khāila]]---ate.
translation: "Previously the Lord gave me mahā-prasāda rice one morning, and I ate that just sitting on my bed, without having even washed my mouth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.117
description: "The man to whom the Lord shows His mercy by inspiring him within the heart takes shelter only of Lord Kṛṣṇa and abandons all Vedic and social customs.
text:
> yāṅre kṛpā kari' karena hṛdaye preraṇa
> kṛṣṇāśraya haya, chāḍe veda-loka-dharma
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāṅre]]---in whomever; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---bestowing; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---in the heart; [[synonyms:p:preraṇa]]---inspiration; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśraya]]---shelter of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:c:chāḍe]]---he gives up; [[synonyms:v:veda]]---Vedic principles; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---social etiquette.
translation: "The man to whom the Lord shows His mercy by inspiring him within the heart takes shelter only of Lord Kṛṣṇa and abandons all Vedic and social customs.
purport:
This is also the teaching of Lord Kṛṣṇa in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:18:66|(Bg. 18.66)]]:

> sarva-dharmān parityajya
> mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja
> ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo
> mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ

"Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear." Such firm faith in the Supreme Personality of Godhead is possible only by the mercy of the Lord. The Lord is sitting within everyone's heart, and when He personally inspires His devotee, the devotee does not stick to the Vedic principles or social customs but rather devotes himself to the transcendental loving service of the Lord. This is confirmed in the following verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:4:29:46|(4.29.46)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.118
description: " 'When one is inspired by the Lord, who is sitting in everyone's heart, he does not care for social custom or Vedic regulative principles.' "
text:
> yadā yam anugṛhṇāti
> bhagavān ātma-bhāvitaḥ
> sa jahāti matiṁ loke
> vede ca pariniṣṭhitām
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadā]]---when; [[synonyms:y:yam]]---to whom; [[synonyms:a:anugṛhṇāti]]---shows special favor; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvitaḥ]]---who is seated in everyone's heart; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that person; [[synonyms:j:jahāti]]---gives up; [[synonyms:m:matim]]---attention; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---to social behavior; [[synonyms:v:vede]]---to Vedic injunctions; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:p:pariniṣṭhitām]]---attached.
translation: “ 'When one is inspired by the Lord, who is sitting in everyone's heart, he does not care for social custom or Vedic regulative principles.' "
purport: This instruction [[books:sb:4:29:46|(Bhāg. 4.29.46)]] was given by Nārada Gosvāmī to King Prācīnabarhi in connection with the story of Purañjana. Here Nārada implies that without the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead one cannot extricate himself from the fruitive activities that are under the jurisdiction of the //Vedas.// In previous verses (//Bhāg.// 4.29.42-44) Nārada admits that even personalities like Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva, Manu, the Prajāpatis (headed by Dakṣa), the four Kumāras, Marīci, Atri, Aṅgira, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Bhṛgu, Vasiṣṭha and even Nārada himself could not properly receive the causeless mercy of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.119
description: After this, King Pratāparudra came down from the top of his palace to the ground and called for Kāśī Miśra and the inspector of the temple.
text:
> tabe rājā aṭṭālikā haite talete āilā
> kāśī-miśra, paḍichā-pātra, duṅhe ānāilā

translation: After this, King Pratāparudra came down from the top of his palace to the ground and called for Kāśī Miśra and the inspector of the temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.12
description: "Bhaṭṭācārya, if you continue to speak like this, you will never see Me here again. Therefore you should never let such a request come from your mouth."
text:
> aiche bāta punarapi mukhe nā ānibe
> kaha yadi, tabe āmāya ethā nā dekhibe
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aichebāta]]---such a request; [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the mouth; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---do not; [[synonyms:ā:ānibe]]---bring; [[synonyms:k:kaha]] [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if you speak; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:ā:āmāya]]---Me; [[synonyms:e:ethā]]---here; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:d:dekhibe]]---you will see.
translation: "Bhaṭṭācārya, if you continue to speak like this, you will never see Me here again. Therefore you should never let such a request come from your mouth."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.120-121
description: Mahārāja Pratāparudra then told both Kāśī Miśra and the temple inspector, "Provide all the devotees and associates of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with comfortable residences, convenient eating facilities for prasāda and convenient visiting arrangements at the temple so that there will not be any difficulty.
text:
> pratāparudra ājñā dila sei dui jane
> prabhu-sthāne āsiyāchena yata prabhura gaṇe
> sabāre svacchanda vāsā, svacchanda prasāda
> svacchanda darśana karāiha, nahe yena bādha
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pratāparudra]]---King Pratāparudra; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---ordered; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jane]]---to those two persons; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---at the place of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyāchena]]---have arrived; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all the devotees who; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---associates of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---to all of them; [[synonyms:s:svacchanda]]---convenient; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]]---residential places; [[synonyms:s:svacchanda]]---convenient; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---remnants of the food of Jagannātha; [[synonyms:s:svacchanda]] [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---convenient visit; [[synonyms:k:karāiha]]---arrange for; [[synonyms:n:nahe]] [[synonyms:y:yena]] [[synonyms:b:bādha]]---so that there will not be any difficulties.
translation: Mahārāja Pratāparudra then told both Kāśī Miśra and the temple inspector, "Provide all the devotees and associates of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with comfortable residences, convenient eating facilities for prasāda and convenient visiting arrangements at the temple so that there will not be any difficulty.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.122
description: "The orders of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu must be carefully carried out. Although the Lord may not give direct orders, you are still to carry out His desires simply by understanding His indications."
text:
> prabhura ājñā pāliha duṅhe sāvadhāna hañā
> ājñā nahe, tabu kariha, iṅgita bujhiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---the order; [[synonyms:p:pāliha]]---carry out; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of you; [[synonyms:s:sāvadhāna]]---careful; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---although there is no direct order; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do; [[synonyms:i:iṅgita]]---indication; [[synonyms:b:bujhiyā]]---understanding.
translation: "The orders of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu must be carefully carried out. Although the Lord may not give direct orders, you are still to carry out His desires simply by understanding His indications."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.123
description: Saying this, the King gave them permission to leave. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya also went to see the assembly of all the Vaiṣṇavas.
text:
> eta bali' vidāya dila sei dui-jane
> sārvabhauma dekhite āila vaiṣṇava-milane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:v:vidāya]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---granted permission to go; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---to those two persons; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:m:milane]]---in the meeting of all the Vaiṣṇavas.
translation: Saying this, the King gave them permission to leave. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya also went to see the assembly of all the Vaiṣṇavas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.124
description: From a distant place both Gopīnātha Ācārya and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya watched the meeting of all the Vaiṣṇavas with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> gopīnāthācārya bhaṭṭācārya sārvabhauma
> dūre rahi' dekhe prabhura vaiṣṇava-milana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]] [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:d:dūre]] [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---standing a little off; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---see; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting with the Vaiṣṇavas.
translation: From a distant place both Gopīnātha Ācārya and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya watched the meeting of all the Vaiṣṇavas with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.125
description: Beginning from the right side of the lion gate, or the main gate of the temple, all the Vaiṣṇavas began to proceed toward the house of Kāśī Miśra.
text:
> siṁha-dvāra ḍāhine chāḍi' saba vaiṣṇava-gaṇa
> kāśī-miśra-gṛha-pathe karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:siṁha]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāra]] [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍāhine]]---on the right side of the lion gate; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---leaving aside; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---devotees of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kāśī]]-[[synonyms:m:miśra]]-[[synonyms:g:gṛha]]---to the house of Kāśī Miśra; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---began to proceed.
translation: Beginning from the right side of the lion gate, or the main gate of the temple, all the Vaiṣṇavas began to proceed toward the house of Kāśī Miśra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.126
description: In the meantime, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, accompanied by His personal associates, met all the Vaiṣṇavas on the road with great jubilation.
text:
> hena-kāle mahāprabhu nija-gaṇa-saṅge
> vaiṣṇave mililā āsi' pathe bahu-raṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nila]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the association of His personal assistants; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇave]]---all the Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the road; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---in great jubilation.
translation: In the meantime, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, accompanied by His personal associates, met all the Vaiṣṇavas on the road with great jubilation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.127
description: First Advaita Ācārya offered prayers to the lotus feet of the Lord, and the Lord immediately embraced Him in ecstatic love.
text:
> advaita karila prabhura caraṇa vandana
> ācāryere kaila prabhu prema-āliṅgana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---worship; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryere]]---unto Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing in ecstatic love.
translation: First Advaita Ācārya offered prayers to the lotus feet of the Lord, and the Lord immediately embraced Him in ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.128
description: Indeed, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Advaita Ācārya displayed agitation due to ecstatic love. Seeing the time and circumstance, however, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained patient.
text:
> premānande hailā duṅhe parama asthira
> samaya dekhiyā prabhu hailā kichu dhīra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:a:asthira]]---greatly agitated; [[synonyms:s:samaya]]---the time; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---a little; [[synonyms:d:dhīra]]---patient.
translation: Indeed, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Advaita Ācārya displayed agitation due to ecstatic love. Seeing the time and circumstance, however, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained patient.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.129
description: After this, all the devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, offered prayers to the lotus feet of the Lord, and the Lord embraced each and every one of them in great love and ecstasy.
text:
> śrīvāsādi karila prabhura caraṇa vandana
> pratyeke karila prabhu prema-āliṅgana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---devotees headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---worshiping the lotus feet; [[synonyms:p:pratyeke]]---to everyone; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing in love.
translation: After this, all the devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, offered prayers to the lotus feet of the Lord, and the Lord embraced each and every one of them in great love and ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.13
description: Being afraid, Sārvabhauma returned home and began to meditate on the matter.
text:
> bhaya pāñā sārvabhauma nija ghare gelā
> vāsāya giyā bhaṭṭācārya cintita ha-ilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaya]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---being afraid; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---own; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to home; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---returned; [[synonyms:v:vāsāya]] [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---reaching his residential place; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---the Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:c:cintita]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became meditative.
translation: Being afraid, Sārvabhauma returned home and began to meditate on the matter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.130
description: The Lord addressed all the devotees one after another and took all of them with Him into the house.
text:
> eke eke sarva-bhakte kaila sambhāṣaṇa
> sabā lañā abhyantare karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ekeeke]]---one after another; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---to every devotee; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:sambhāṣaṇa]]---address; [[synonyms:s:sabā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking all of them; [[synonyms:a:abhyantare]]---inside; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---entered.
translation: The Lord addressed all the devotees one after another and took all of them with Him into the house.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.131
description: Since the residence of Kāśī Miśra was insufficient, all the assembled devotees were very much overcrowded.
text:
> miśrera āvāsa sei haya alpa sthāna
> asaṅkhya vaiṣṇava tāhāṅ haila parimāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:miśrera]] [[synonyms:ā:āvāsa]]---the residence of Kāśī Miśra; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:a:alpa]] [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---insufficient place; [[synonyms:a:asaṅkhya]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotees; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---were; [[synonyms:p:parimāṇa]]---overcrowded.
translation: Since the residence of Kāśī Miśra was insufficient, all the assembled devotees were very much overcrowded.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.132
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu made all the devotees sit at His side, and with His own hand He offered them garlands and sandalwood pulp.
text:
> āpana-nikaṭe prabhu sabā vasāilā
> āpani śrī-haste sabāre mālya-gandha dilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:n:nikaṭe]]---by His own side; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all of them; [[synonyms:v:vasāilā]]---made sit; [[synonyms:ā:āpani]]---personally Himself; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:h:haste]]---with His hand; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---unto everyone; [[synonyms:m:mālya]]---garland; [[synonyms:g:gandha]]---sandalwood pulp; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---offered.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu made all the devotees sit at His side, and with His own hand He offered them garlands and sandalwood pulp.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.133
description: After this, Gopīnātha Ācārya and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya met all the Vaiṣṇavas at the place of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in a befitting manner.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya, ācārya tabe mahāprabhura sthāne
> yathā-yogya mililā sabākāra sane
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---at the place of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]-[[synonyms:y:yogya]]---as it is befitting; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:s:sabākāra]] [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with all the Vaiṣṇavas assembled there.
translation: After this, Gopīnātha Ācārya and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya met all the Vaiṣṇavas at the place of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in a befitting manner.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.134
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu addressed Advaita Ācārya Prabhu, saying sweetly, "My dear Sir, today I have become perfect because of Your arrival."
text:
> advaitere kahena prabhu madhura vacane
> āji āmi pūrṇa ha-ilāṅa tomāra āgamane
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaitere]]---unto Advaita Ācārya Prabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---says; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:madhura]] [[synonyms:v:vacane]]---in sweet language; [[synonyms:ā:āji]]---today; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---perfect; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilāṅa]]---became; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:ā:āgamane]]---on arrival.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu addressed Advaita Ācārya Prabhu, saying sweetly, "My dear Sir, today I have become perfect because of Your arrival."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.135-136
description: Advaita Ācārya Prabhu replied, "This is a natural characteristic of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although He is personally complete and full of all opulences, He takes transcendental pleasure in the association of His devotees, with whom He has a variety of eternal pastimes."
text:
> advaita kahe,-īśvarera ei svabhāva haya
> yadyapi āpane pūrṇa, sarvaiśvarya-maya
>
> tathāpi bhakta-saṅge haya sukhollāsa
> bhakta-saṅge kare nitya vividha vilāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaitakahe]]---Advaita Ācārya Prabhu said; [[synonyms:ī:īśvarera]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---feature; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---Himself; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---all-perfect; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---full of all opulences; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the association of devotees; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---great jubilation; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with devotees; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---eternally; [[synonyms:v:vividha]]---various; [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---pastimes.
translation: Advaita Ācārya Prabhu replied, "This is a natural characteristic of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although He is personally complete and full of all opulences, He takes transcendental pleasure in the association of His devotees, with whom He has a variety of eternal pastimes."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.137
description: As soon as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw Vāsudeva Datta, the father of Mukunda Datta, He immediately became very happy and, placing His hand on his body, began to speak.
text:
> vāsudeva dekhi' prabhu ānandita hañā
> tāṅre kichu kahe tāṅra aṅge hasta diyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]---Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming very much pleased; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:kichu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says something; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---on his body; [[synonyms:h:hasta]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---placing His hand.
translation: As soon as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw Vāsudeva Datta, the father of Mukunda Datta, He immediately became very happy and, placing His hand on his body, began to speak.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.138
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Although Mukunda is My friend from childhood, I nonetheless take greater pleasure in seeing you than in seeing him."
text:
> yadyapi mukunda-āmā-saṅge śiśu haite
> tāṅhā haite adhika sukha tomāre dekhite
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Me; [[synonyms:ś:śiśu]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from childhood; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---than him; [[synonyms:a:adhika]]---still more; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]] [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see you.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Although Mukunda is My friend from childhood, I nonetheless take greater pleasure in seeing you than in seeing him."
purport: Vāsudeva Datta was the father of Mukunda Datta, who was the childhood friend of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. It is naturally a great pleasure to see a friend, but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu informed the father that although it was His pleasure to see His friend, His pleasure was increased by seeing the father.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.139
description: Vāsudeva replied, "Mukunda got Your association in the beginning. As such, he has taken shelter at Your lotus feet. That is his transcendental rebirth."
text:
> vāsu kahe,-mukunda ādau pāila tomāra saṅga
> tomāra caraṇa pāila sei punar-janma
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vāsukahe]]---Vāsudeva Datta said; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:ā:ādau]]---in the beginning; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---Your association; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---Your lotus feet; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]-[[synonyms:j:janma]]---transcendental rebirth.
translation: Vāsudeva replied, "Mukunda got Your association in the beginning. As such, he has taken shelter at Your lotus feet. That is his transcendental rebirth."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.14
description: At this time, Mahārāja Pratāparudra arrived at Jagannātha Purī, Puruṣottama, and, accompanied by his secretaries, ministers and military officers, went to visit the temple of Lord Jagannātha.
text:
> hena kāle pratāparudra puruṣottame āilā
> pātra-mitra-saṅge rājā daraśane calilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:henakāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:p:pratāparudra]]---King Pratāparudra; [[synonyms:p:puruṣottame]]---at Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:p:pātra]]-[[synonyms:m:mitra]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---accompanied by his secretaries, ministers, military officers and so on; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---to visit Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---departed.
translation: At this time, Mahārāja Pratāparudra arrived at Jagannātha Purī, Puruṣottama, and, accompanied by his secretaries, ministers and military officers, went to visit the temple of Lord Jagannātha.
purport: It appears that Mahārāja Pratāparudra used to live at Kaṭaka, his capital. Later he shifted his capital to Khurdā, a few miles from Jagannātha Purī. Presently there is a railway station there called Khurdā Road.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.140
description: Thus Vāsudeva Datta admitted his inferiority to Mukunda, his son. "Although Mukunda is my junior," he said, "he first received Your favor. Consequently he became transcendentally senior to me. Besides that, You very much favored Mukunda. Thus he is superior in all good qualities."
text:
> choṭa hañā mukunda ebe haila āmāra jyeṣṭha
> tomāra kṛpā-pātra tāte sarva-guṇe śreṣṭha
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:choṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being junior; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---has become; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---my; [[synonyms:j:jyeṣṭha]]---senior; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---favorite; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---in all good qualities; [[synonyms:ś:śreṣṭha]]---superior.
translation: Thus Vāsudeva Datta admitted his inferiority to Mukunda, his son. "Although Mukunda is my junior," he said, "he first received Your favor. Consequently he became transcendentally senior to me. Besides that, You very much favored Mukunda. Thus he is superior in all good qualities."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.141
description: The Lord said, "For your sake only, I have brought two books from South India.
text:
> punaḥ prabhu kahe-āmi tomāra nimitte
> dui pustaka āniyāchi 'dakṣiṇa' ha-ite
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:n:nimitte]]---for your sake; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:p:pustaka]]---books; [[synonyms:ā:āniyāchi]]---have brought; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---from South India.
translation: The Lord said, "For your sake only, I have brought two books from South India.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.142
description: "The books are kept with Svarūpa Dāmodara, and you can get them copied." Hearing this, Vāsudeva became very glad.
text:
> svarūpera ṭhāṅi āche, laha tā likhiyā
> vāsudeva ānandita pustaka pāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpera]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāṅi]]---in the possession of Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---they are; [[synonyms:l:laha]]---you take; [[synonyms:t:tā]]---them; [[synonyms:l:likhiyā]]---copying; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]---Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very glad; [[synonyms:p:pustaka]]---the books; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting.
translation: "The books are kept with Svarūpa Dāmodara, and you can get them copied." Hearing this, Vāsudeva became very glad.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.143
description: Indeed, each and every Vaiṣṇava copied the two books. By and by, the two books [the Brahma-saṁhitā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta] were broadcast all over India.
text:
> pratyeka vaiṣṇava sabe likhiyā la-ila
> krame krame dui grantha sarvatra vyāpila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pratyeka]]---each and every; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotee; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:l:likhiyā]]---copying; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---took; [[synonyms:k:krame]] [[synonyms:k:krame]]---by and by; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:g:grantha]]---the two books; [[synonyms:s:sarvatra]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:v:vyāpila]]---become broadcast.
translation: Indeed, each and every Vaiṣṇava copied the two books. By and by, the two books [the Brahma-saṁhitā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta] were broadcast all over India.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.144
description: The Lord addressed Śrīvāsa and his brothers with great love and affection, saying, "I am so obliged that I am purchased by you four brothers."
text:
> śrīvāsādye kahe prabhu kari' mahā-prīta
> tomāra cāri-bhāira āmi ha-inu vikrīta
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādye]]---unto Śrīvāsa and his three brothers; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---giving; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prīta]]---great love; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of you; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāira]]---of four brothers; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:inu]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vikrīta]]---purchased.
translation: The Lord addressed Śrīvāsa and his brothers with great love and affection, saying, "I am so obliged that I am purchased by you four brothers."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.145
description: Śrīvāsa then replied to the Lord, "Why are You speaking in a contradictory way? Rather, we four brothers have been purchased by Your mercy."
text:
> śrīvāsa kahena,-kene kaha viparīta
> kṛpā-mūlye cāri bhāi ha-i tomāra krīta

translation: Śrīvāsa then replied to the Lord, "Why are You speaking in a contradictory way? Rather, we four brothers have been purchased by Your mercy."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.146
description: After seeing Śaṅkara, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told Dāmodara, "My affection for you is on the platform of awe and reverence.
text:
> śaṅkare dekhiyā prabhu kahe dāmodare
> sagaurava-prīti āmāra tomāra upare
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śaṅkare]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing Śaṅkara; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:d:dāmodare]]---unto Dāmodara; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaurava]]-[[synonyms:p:prīti]]---affection with awe and reverence; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:u:upare]]---upon you.
translation: After seeing Śaṅkara, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told Dāmodara, "My affection for you is on the platform of awe and reverence.
purport: Here the Lord is addressing Dāmodara Paṇḍita, who is different from Svarūpa Dāmodara. Dāmodara Paṇḍita is the elder brother of Śaṅkara. Thus the Lord informed Dāmodara that His affection toward him was on the platform of awe and reverence. However, the Lord's affection toward his younger brother, Śaṅkara, was on the platform of pure love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.147
description: "Therefore keep your younger brother Śaṅkara with you because he is connected to Me by pure unalloyed love."
text:
> śuddha kevala-prema śaṅkara-upare
> ataeva tomāra saṅge rākhaha śaṅkare

translation: "Therefore keep your younger brother Śaṅkara with you because he is connected to Me by pure unalloyed love."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.148
description: Dāmodara Paṇḍita replied, "Śaṅkara is my younger brother, but from today he becomes my elder brother because of Your special mercy upon him."
text:
> dāmodara kahe,-śaṅkara choṭa āmā haite
> ebe āmāra baḍa bhāi tomāra kṛpāte

translation: Dāmodara Paṇḍita replied, "Śaṅkara is my younger brother, but from today he becomes my elder brother because of Your special mercy upon him."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.149
description: Then turning toward Śivānanda Sena, the Lord said, "I know that from the very beginning your affection for Me has been very great."
text:
> śivānande kahe prabhu,-tomāra āmāte
> gāḍha anurāga haya, jāni āge haite
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śivānande]]---unto Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:ā:āmāte]]---upon Me; [[synonyms:g:gāḍha]] [[synonyms:a:anurāga]]---deep affection; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I know; [[synonyms:ā:āge]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the very beginning.
translation: Then turning toward Śivānanda Sena, the Lord said, "I know that from the very beginning your affection for Me has been very great."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.15
description: When King Pratāparudra returned to Jagannātha Purī, Rāmānanda Rāya also came with him. Rāmānanda Rāya immediately went to meet Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with great pleasure.
text:
> rāmānanda rāya āilā gajapati-saṅge
> prathamei prabhure āsi' mililā bahu-raṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]] [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:g:gajapati]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the King; [[synonyms:p:prathamei]]---in the first instance; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---with great pleasure.
translation: When King Pratāparudra returned to Jagannātha Purī, Rāmānanda Rāya also came with him. Rāmānanda Rāya immediately went to meet Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with great pleasure.
purport: All Indian kings are given titles. Sometimes they are known as Chatrapati, sometimes as Narapati, sometimes as Aśvapati, and so on. The King of Orissa is addressed as Gajapati.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.150
description: Immediately upon hearing this, Śivānanda Sena became absorbed in ecstatic love and fell down on the ground, offering obeisances to the Lord. He then began to recite the following verse.
text:
> śuni' śivānanda-sena premāviṣṭa hañā
> daṇḍavat hañā paḍe śloka paḍiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:ś:śivānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sena]]---Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming absorbed in pure love; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---falls down; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---a verse; [[synonyms:p:paḍiyā]]---reciting.
translation: Immediately upon hearing this, Śivānanda Sena became absorbed in ecstatic love and fell down on the ground, offering obeisances to the Lord. He then began to recite the following verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.151
description: " 'O my Lord! O unlimited one! Although I was merged in the ocean of nescience, I have now, after a long time, attained You, just as one may attain the seashore. My dear Lord, by getting me, You have obtained the right person upon whom to bestow Your causeless mercy.' "
text:
> nimajjato 'nanta bhavārṇavāntaś
> cirāya me kūlam ivāsi labdhaḥ
> tvayāpi labdhaṁ bhagavann idānīm
> anuttamaṁ pātram idaṁ dayāyāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nimajjataḥ]]---being immersed; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---O unlimited one; [[synonyms:b:bhava]]-[[synonyms:a:arṇava]]-[[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]---within the ocean of nescience; [[synonyms:c:cirāya]]---after a long time; [[synonyms:m:me]]---of me; [[synonyms:k:kūlam]]---the shore; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:a:asi]]---You are; [[synonyms:l:labdhaḥ]]---obtained; [[synonyms:t:tvayā]]---by You; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:l:labdham]]---has been gained; [[synonyms:b:bhagavan]]---O my Lord; [[synonyms:i:idānīm]]---now; [[synonyms:a:anuttamam]]---the best; [[synonyms:p:pātram]]---candidate; [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this; [[synonyms:d:dayāyāḥ]]---for showing Your mercy.
translation: “ 'O my Lord! O unlimited one! Although I was merged in the ocean of nescience, I have now, after a long time, attained You, just as one may attain the seashore. My dear Lord, by getting me, You have obtained the right person upon whom to bestow Your causeless mercy.' "
purport:
This is a verse from the //Stotra-ratna// (21), composed by Ālabandāru Yāmunācārya. One's relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead may be reestablished even after one has fallen into the ocean of nescience, which is the ocean of material existence involving the repetition of birth, death, old age and disease, all arising out of the acceptance of the material body. There are 8,400,000 species of material life, but in the human body one attains a chance to get release from the repetition of birth and death. When one becomes the Lord's devotee, he is rescued from this dangerous ocean of birth and death. The Lord is always prepared to show His mercy to the fallen souls struggling against miserable material conditions. As Lord Kṛṣṇa states in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:15:7|(Bg. 15.7)]]:

> mamaivāṁśo jīva-loke
> jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ
> manaḥ-ṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi
> prakṛti-sthāni karṣati

"The living entities in this conditioned world are My eternal fragmental parts. Due to conditioned life, they are struggling very hard with the six senses, which include the mind."

Thus every living being is struggling hard in this material nature. Actually the living entity is part and parcel of the Supreme Lord, and when he surrenders unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he attains release from the ocean of birth and death. The Lord, being very kind to fallen souls, is always anxious to get the living entity out of the ocean of nescience. If the living entity understands his position and surrenders to the Lord, his life becomes successful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.152
description: Murāri Gupta at first did not meet the Lord but rather remained outside the door, falling down like a stick to offer obeisances.
text:
> prathame murāri-gupta prabhure nā miliyā
> bāhirete paḍi' āche daṇḍavat hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prathame]]---at first; [[synonyms:m:murāri]]-[[synonyms:g:gupta]]---Murāri Gupta; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---without; [[synonyms:m:miliyā]]---meeting; [[synonyms:b:bāhirete]]---outside; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---falling down; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---was there; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]]---falling flat like a stick; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming so.
translation: Murāri Gupta at first did not meet the Lord but rather remained outside the door, falling down like a stick to offer obeisances.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.153
description: When Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu could not see Murāri amongst the devotees, He inquired about him. Thereupon many people immediately went to Murāri, running to take him to the Lord.
text:
> murāri nā dekhiyā prabhu kare anveṣaṇa
> murāri la-ite dhāñā āilā bahu-jana

translation: When Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu could not see Murāri amongst the devotees, He inquired about him. Thereupon many people immediately went to Murāri, running to take him to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.154
description: Thus Murāri Gupta, catching two bunches of straw in his teeth, went before Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with humility and meekness.
text:
> tṛṇa dui-guccha murāri daśane dhariyā
> mahāprabhu āge gelā dainyādhīna hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tṛṇa]]---of straw; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:g:guccha]]---bunches; [[synonyms:m:murāri]]---Murāri; [[synonyms:d:daśane]]---in his teeth; [[synonyms:d:dhariyā]]---catching; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]-[[synonyms:a:adhīna]]---under obligation of meekness; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming.
translation: Thus Murāri Gupta, catching two bunches of straw in his teeth, went before Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with humility and meekness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.155
description: Upon seeing Murāri come to meet Him, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went up to him, but Murāri began to run away and speak as follows.
text:
> murāri dekhiyā prabhu āilā milite
> pāche bhāge murāri, lāgilā kahite
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:murāri]]---Murāri; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came out; [[synonyms:m:milite]]---to meet; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:b:bhāge]]---runs away; [[synonyms:m:murāri]]---Murāri; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak.
translation: Upon seeing Murāri come to meet Him, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went up to him, but Murāri began to run away and speak as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.156
description: "My Lord, please do not touch me. I am most abominable and am not fit for You to touch because my body is sinful."
text:
> more nā chuṅiha, prabhu, muñi ta' pāmara
> tomāra sparśa-yogya nahe pāpa kalevara
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:more]]---me; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:c:chuṅiha]]---do not touch; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---my Lord; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:p:pāmara]]---most abominable; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of You; [[synonyms:s:sparśa]]-[[synonyms:y:yogya]]---fit to be touched; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]---sinful; [[synonyms:k:kalevara]]---body.
translation: "My Lord, please do not touch me. I am most abominable and am not fit for You to touch because my body is sinful."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.157
description: The Lord said, "My dear Murāri, please restrain your unnecessary humility. My mind is disturbed to see your meekness."

translation: The Lord said, "My dear Murāri, please restrain your unnecessary humility. My mind is disturbed to see your meekness."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.158
description: Saying this, the Lord embraced Murāri and had him sit down by His side. The Lord then began to cleanse his body with His own hands.
text:
> eta bali' prabhu tāṅre kaila āliṅgana

translation: Saying this, the Lord embraced Murāri and had him sit down by His side. The Lord then began to cleanse his body with His own hands.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.159-160
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then again and again embraced all the devotees, including Ācāryaratna, Vidyānidhi, Paṇḍita Gadādhara, Gaṅgādāsa, Hari Bhaṭṭa and Ācārya Purandara. The Lord described their good qualities and glorified them again and again.
text:
> ācāryaratna, vidyānidhi, paṇḍita gadādhara
> gaṅgādāsa, hari-bhaṭṭa, ācārya purandara
>
> pratyeke sabāra prabhu kari' guṇa gāna
> punaḥ punaḥ āliṅgiyā karila sammāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryaratna]]---Ācāryaratna; [[synonyms:v:vidyānidhi]]---Vidyānidhi; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]] [[synonyms:g:gadādhara]]---Paṇḍita Gadādhara; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgādāsa]]---Gaṅgādāsa; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Hari Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:p:purandara]]---Ācārya Purandara; [[synonyms:p:pratyeke]]---each and every one of them; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:g:guṇa]] [[synonyms:g:gāna]]---glorifying the qualities; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]] [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again and again; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgiyā]]---embracing; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:sammāna]]---honor.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then again and again embraced all the devotees, including Ācāryaratna, Vidyānidhi, Paṇḍita Gadādhara, Gaṅgādāsa, Hari Bhaṭṭa and Ācārya Purandara. The Lord described their good qualities and glorified them again and again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.16
description: Upon meeting Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Rāmānanda Rāya offered his obeisances. The Lord embraced him, and both of them began to cry in the great ecstasy of love.
text:
> rāya praṇati kaila, prabhu kaila āliṅgana
> dui jane premāveśe karena krandana

translation: Upon meeting Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Rāmānanda Rāya offered his obeisances. The Lord embraced him, and both of them began to cry in the great ecstasy of love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.161
description: After thus offering respect to each and every devotee, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very jubilant. However, not seeing Haridāsa Ṭhākura, He inquired, "Where is Haridāsa?"
text:
> sabāre sammāni' prabhura ha-ila ullāsa
> haridāse nā dekhiyā kahe,-kāhāṅ haridāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabāre]] [[synonyms:s:sammāni']]---respecting everyone; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---jubilation; [[synonyms:h:haridāse]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---without seeing; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---where is Haridāsa.
translation: After thus offering respect to each and every devotee, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very jubilant. However, not seeing Haridāsa Ṭhākura, He inquired, "Where is Haridāsa?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.162
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then saw in the distance that Haridāsa Ṭhākura was lying down flat on the road offering obeisances.
text:
> dūra haite haridāsa gosāñe dekhiyā
> rājapatha-prānte paḍi' āche daṇḍavat hañā

description: Haridāsa Ṭhākura replied, "I cannot go near the temple because I am a low-caste, abominable person. I have no authority to go there."

translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura replied, "I cannot go near the temple because I am a low-caste, abominable person. I have no authority to go there."
purport: Although Haridāsa Ṭhākura was such a highly exalted Vaiṣṇava that he was addressed as Haridāsa Gosvāmī, he still did not like to disturb the common sense of the general populace. Haridāsa Ṭhākura was so exalted that he was addressed as //ṭhākura// and //gosāñi,// and these titles are offered to the most advanced Vaiṣṇavas. The spiritual master is generally called //gosāñi,// and //ṭhākura// is used to address the //paramahaṁsas,// those in the topmost rank of spirituality. Nonetheless, Haridāsa Ṭhākura did not want to go near the temple, although he was called there by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself. The Jagannātha temple still accepts only those Hindus who are in the //varṇāśrama// order. Other castes, especially those who are not Hindu, are not allowed to enter the temple. This is a long-standing regulation, and thus Haridāsa Ṭhākura, although certainly competent and qualified to enter the temple, did not want even to go near it. This is called Vaiṣṇava humility.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.176
description: "Please give that room to Me, for I have a need for it. Indeed, I shall remember the lotus feet of the Lord sitting in that solitary place."

> sei ghara āmāke deha'-āche prayojana
> nibhṛte vasiyā tāhāṅ kariba smaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:g:ghara]]---that room; [[synonyms:ā:āmāke]] [[synonyms:d:deha']]---please give to Me; [[synonyms:ā:āche]] [[synonyms:p:prayojana]]---there is necessity; [[synonyms:n:nibhṛte]]---in the solitary place; [[synonyms:v:vasiyā]]---sitting; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:k:kariba]] [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---I shall remember the lotus feet of the Lord.
translation: "Please give that room to Me, for I have a need for it. Indeed, I shall remember the lotus feet of the Lord sitting in that solitary place."
purport:
This statement of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is significant. //Nibhṛte vasiyā tāhāṅ kariba smaraṇa:// "I shall sit down there in that solitary place and remember the lotus feet of the Lord." Neophyte students are not to imitate sitting in a solitary place and remembering the lotus feet of the Lord by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// We should always remember that it was Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself who wanted such a place, either for Himself or Haridāsa Ṭhākura. No one can suddenly attain the level of Haridāsa Ṭhākura and sit down in a solitary place to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// and remember the lotus feet of the Lord. Only an exalted person like Haridāsa Ṭhākura or Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is personally exhibiting the proper behavior for an //ācārya,// can engage in such a practice.

At the present moment we see that some of the members of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness are tending to leave their preaching activities in order to sit in a solitary place. This is not a very good sign. It is a fact that Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura has condemned this process for neophytes. He has even stated in a song, //pratiṣṭhāra tare, nirjanera ghare, tava hari-nāma kevala kaitava:// "Sitting in a solitary place intending to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// is considered a cheating process." This practice is not possible for neophytes at all. The neophyte devotee must act and work very laboriously under the direction of the spiritual master, and he must thus preach the cult of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Only after maturing in devotion can he sit down in a solitary place to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself did. Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, He nonetheless traveled all over India continuously for six years and then retired at Jagannātha Purī to teach us a lesson. Even at Jagannātha Purī the Lord chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// in great meetings at the Jagannātha temple. The point is that one should not try to imitate Haridāsa Ṭhākura at the beginning of one's transcendental life. One must first become very mature in devotion and thus receive the approval of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Only at such a time may one actually sit down peacefully in a solitary place to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// and remember the lotus feet of the Lord. The senses are very strong, and if a neophyte devotee imitates Haridāsa Ṭhākura, his enemies (//kāma, krodha, lobha, moha, mada// and //mātsarya//) will disturb and fatigue him. Instead of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra,// the neophyte will simply sleep soundly. Preaching work is meant for advanced devotees, and when an advanced devotee is further elevated on the devotional scale, he may retire to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// in a solitary place. However, if one simply imitates advanced spiritual life, he will fall down, just like the //sahajiyās// in Vṛndāvana.

The King was very much pleased to give him relief, and thus Rāmānanda Rāya retired from service and received a pension from the government.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.187
description: Then both the Lord and His servant began to cry in ecstatic love. Indeed, the Lord was transformed by the quality of His servant, and the servant was transformed by the quality of his master.
text:
> dui-jane premāveśe karena krandane
> prabhu-guṇe bhṛtya vikala, prabhu bhṛtya-guṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---both of them; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in loving ecstasy; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:k:krandane]]---were crying; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---by the quality of the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhṛtya]]---servant; [[synonyms:v:vikala]]---transformed; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhṛtya]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---by the quality of the servant.
translation: Then both the Lord and His servant began to cry in ecstatic love. Indeed, the Lord was transformed by the quality of His servant, and the servant was transformed by the quality of his master.
purport:
The Māyāvādī philosophers say that the living entity and the Supreme Lord are nondifferent, and therefore they equate the transformation of the living entity with the transformation of the Lord. In other words, Māyāvādīs say that if the living entity is pleased, the Lord is also pleased, and if the living entity is displeased, the Lord is also displeased. By juggling words in this way, Māyāvādīs try to prove that there is no difference between the living entity and the Lord. This, however, is not a fact. In this verse Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī explains: //prabhu-guṇe bhṛtya vikala, prabhu bhṛtya-guṇe.// The Lord and the living entity are not equal, for the Lord is always the master, and the living entity is always the servant. Transformation takes place due to transcendental qualities, and it is thus said that the servant of the Lord is the heart of the Lord, and the Lord is the heart of the servant. This is also explained by Lord Kṛṣṇa in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:4:11|(Bg. 4.11)]]:

> ye yathā māṁ prapadyante
> tāṁs tathaiva bhajāmy aham
> mama vartmānuvartante
> manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ

"As all surrender unto Me, I reward them accordingly. Everyone follows My path in all respects, O son of Pṛthā."

The Lord is always eager to congratulate the servant because of the servant's transcendental quality. The servant pleasingly renders service unto the Lord, and the Lord also very pleasingly reciprocates, rendering even more service unto the servant.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.188
description: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "My dear Lord, please do not touch me, for I am most fallen and untouchable and am the lowest among men."
text:
> haridāsa kahe,-prabhu, nā chuṅio more
> muñi-nīca, aspṛśya, parama pāmare
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura said; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---my dear Lord; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:c:chuṅio]] [[synonyms:m:more]]---please do not touch me; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]---most fallen; [[synonyms:a:aspṛśya]]---untouchable; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:p:pāmare]]---the lowest of mankind.
translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "My dear Lord, please do not touch me, for I am most fallen and untouchable and am the lowest among men."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.189
description: The Lord said, "I wish to touch you just to be purified, for your purified activities do not exist in Me."
text:
> prabhu kahe,-tomā sparśi pavitra ha-ite
> tomāra pavitra dharma nāhika āmāte
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:t:tomā]] [[synonyms:s:sparśi]]---I touch you; [[synonyms:p:pavitra]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---just to become purified; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:p:pavitra]]---purified; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---occupation; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---is not; [[synonyms:ā:āmāte]]---in Me.
translation: The Lord said, "I wish to touch you just to be purified, for your purified activities do not exist in Me."
purport:
This is an example of the reciprocation of feelings between master and servant. The servant thinks that he is most impure and that the master should not touch him, and the master thinks that because He has become impure by associating with so many impure living entities, He should touch a pure devotee like Haridāsa Ṭhākura just to purify Himself. Actually both the servant and the master are already purified because neither of them is in touch with the impurities of material existence. They are already equal in quality because both of them are the purest. There is a difference in quantity, however, because the master is unlimited and the servant is limited. Consequently the servant always remains subordinate to the master, and this relationship is eternal and undisturbed. As soon as the servant feels like becoming the master, he falls into //māyā.// Thus it is by misuse of free will that one falls under the influence of //māyā.//

The Māyāvādī philosophers try to explain the equality of master and servant in terms of quantity, but they fail to explain why, if the master and servant are equal, the servant falls victim to //māyā.// They try to explain that when the servant, the living entity, is out of the clutches of //māyā,// he immediately becomes the so-called master again. Such an explanation is never satisfactory. Being unlimited, the master cannot become a victim of //māyā,// for in such a case His unlimitedness would be crippled or limited. Thus the Māyāvāda explanation is not correct. The fact is that the master is always master and unlimited, and the servant, being limited, is sometimes curtailed by the influence of //māyā. Māyā// is also the master's energy and is also unlimited; therefore the limited servant or limited living entity is forced to remain under the master or the master's potency, //māyā.// Being freed from //māyā's// influence, one can again become a pure servant and equal qualitatively to the Lord. The relationship between master and servant continues due to their being unlimited and limited respectively.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.19
description: "I said, 'Your Majesty, I am now not willing to engage in political activities. I desire only to stay at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Kindly give me permission.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.191

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.192
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then recited the following verse: " 'My dear Lord, one who always keeps Your holy name on his tongue becomes greater than an initiated brāhmaṇa. Although he may be born in a family of dog-eaters and therefore by material calculation may be the lowest among men, he is still glorious. This is the wonderful effect of chanting the holy name of the Lord. It is therefore concluded that one who chants the holy name of the Lord should be understood to have performed all kinds of austerities and great sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas. He has already taken his bath in all the holy places of pilgrimage. He has studied all the Vedas, and he is actually an Āryan.' "
text:
> aho bata śva-paco 'to garīyān
> yaj-jihvāgre vartate nāma tubhyam
> tepus tapas te juhuvuḥ sasnur āryā
> brahmānūcur nāma gṛṇanti ye te
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aho]] [[synonyms:b:bata]]---how wonderful it is; [[synonyms:ś:śva]]-[[synonyms:p:pacaḥ]]---dog-eaters; [[synonyms:a:ataḥ]]---than the initiated //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:g:garīyān]]---more glorious; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---of whom; [[synonyms:j:jihvā]]-[[synonyms:a:agre]]---on the tongue; [[synonyms:v:vartate]]---remains; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---holy name; [[synonyms:t:tubhyam]]---of You, my Lord; [[synonyms:t:tepuḥ]]---have performed; [[synonyms:t:tapaḥ]]---austerity; [[synonyms:t:te]]---they; [[synonyms:j:juhuvuḥ]]---have performed sacrifices; [[synonyms:s:sasnuḥ]]---have bathed in all holy places; [[synonyms:ā:āryāḥ]]---really belonging to the Āryan race; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---all the //Vedas//; [[synonyms:a:anūcuḥ]]---have studied; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---holy name; [[synonyms:g:gṛṇanti]]---chant; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---who; [[synonyms:t:te]]---they.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then recited the following verse: " 'My dear Lord, one who always keeps Your holy name on his tongue becomes greater than an initiated brāhmaṇa. Although he may be born in a family of dog-eaters and therefore by material calculation may be the lowest among men, he is still glorious. This is the wonderful effect of chanting the holy name of the Lord. It is therefore concluded that one who chants the holy name of the Lord should be understood to have performed all kinds of austerities and great sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas. He has already taken his bath in all the holy places of pilgrimage. He has studied all the Vedas, and he is actually an Āryan.' "
purport: The word Āryan means advanced. Unless one is spiritually advanced, he cannot be called an Āryan, and this is the difference between Āryan and non-Āryan. Non-Āryans are those who are not spiritually advanced. By following the Vedic culture, by performing great sacrifices and by becoming a strict follower of the Vedic instructions, one may become a //brāhmaṇa,// a //sannyāsī// or an Āryan. It is not possible to become a //brāhmaṇa, sannyāsī// or Āryan without being properly qualified. //Bhāgavata-dharma// never allows one to become a cheap //brāhmaṇa, sannyāsī// or Āryan. The qualities or qualifications described herein are quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:33:7|(3.33.7)]] and were spoken by Devahūti, the mother of Kapiladeva, when she understood the influence of devotional service (//bhakti-yoga//). In this way Devahūti praised the devotee, pointing out his greatness in all respects.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.193

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.194

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested Haridāsa Ṭhākura, "Remain here and chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra. I shall personally come here to meet you daily.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.195
description: "Remain here peacefully and look at the cakra on the top of the temple and offer obeisances. As far as your prasāda is concerned, I shall arrange to have that sent here."
text:
> mandirera cakra dekhi' kariha praṇāma
> ei ṭhāñi tomāra āsibe prasādānna
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mandirera]]---of the temple of Jagannātha; [[synonyms:c:cakra]]---the wheel on the top; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kariha]] [[synonyms:p:praṇāma]]---offer your obeisances; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---in this place; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:ā:āsibe]]---will come; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]-[[synonyms:a:anna]]---remnants of food of Jagannātha.
translation:
"Remain here peacefully and look at the cakra on the top of the temple and offer obeisances. As far as your prasāda is concerned, I shall arrange to have that sent here."


Since he was born in a Muslim family, Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura could not enter the temple of Jagannātha due to temple restrictions. Nonetheless, he was recognized by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as Nāmācārya Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Haridāsa Ṭhākura, however, considered himself unfit to enter the Jagannātha temple. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu could have personally taken Haridāsa Ṭhākura into the Jagannātha temple if He wished, but the Lord did not like to disturb a popular custom. Consequently the Lord asked His servant simply to look at the Viṣṇu wheel on top of the temple and offer obeisances (//namaskāra//). This means that if one is not allowed to enter the temple, or if he thinks himself unfit to enter the temple, he can look at the wheel from outside the temple, and that is as good as seeing the Deity within.

Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu promised to come daily to see Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura, and this indicates that Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura was so advanced in spiritual life that, although considered unfit to enter the temple, he was being personally visited by the Lord every day. Nor was there any need for his going outside his residence to collect food. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu assured Haridāsa Ṭhākura that the remnants of His food would be sent there. As the Lord states in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:22|(Bg. 9.22)]], //yoga-kṣemaṁ vahāmy aham:// "I arrange all life's necessities for My devotees."

A reference is made here for those who are very anxious to imitate the behavior of Ṭhākura Haridāsa in an unnatural way. One must receive the order of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu or His representative before adopting such a way of life. The duty of a pure devotee or a servant of the Lord is to carry out the order of the Lord. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked Nityānanda Prabhu to go to Bengal and preach, and He asked the Gosvāmīs, Rūpa and Sanātana, to go to Vṛndāvana and excavate the lost places of pilgrimage. In this case the Lord asked Haridāsa Ṭhākura to remain there at Jagannātha Purī and constantly chant the holy names of the Lord. Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu gave different persons different orders, and consequently one should not try to imitate the behavior of Haridāsa Ṭhākura without being ordered by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu or His representative. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura condemns such imitations in this way:

> duṣṭa mana! tumi kisera vaiṣṇava?
> pratiṣṭhāra tare, nirjanera ghare,
> tava hari-nāma kevala kaitava

"My dear mind, you are trying to imitate Haridāsa Ṭhākura and chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// in a secluded place, but you are not worth being called a Vaiṣṇava because what you want is cheap popularity and not the actual qualifications of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. If you try to imitate him you will fall down, for your neophyte position will cause you to think of women and money. Thus you will fall into the clutches of //māyā,// and your so-called chanting in a secluded place will bring about your downfall."
