> na me bhaktāś ca te janāḥ
> mad-bhaktānāṁ ca ye bhaktās
> te me bhakta-tamā matāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:j:janāḥ]]---devotees; [[synonyms:p:pārtha]]---O Pārtha; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:b:bhaktāḥ]]---devotees; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:t:te]]---those; [[synonyms:j:janāḥ]]---persons; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktānām]]---of My devotees; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---certainly; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:b:bhaktāḥ]]---devotees; [[synonyms:t:te]]---such persons; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:t:tamāḥ]]---most advanced devotees; [[synonyms:m:matāḥ]]---that is My opinion.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa told Arjuna, 'Those who are My direct devotees are actually not My devotees, but those who are the devotees of My servant are factually My devotees.'
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu quotes this verse from the //Ādi Purāṇa.// The verse is also included in the //Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta// (2.6).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.29-30
description: " 'My devotees take great care and respect in rendering Me service. They offer obeisances to Me with all their bodily limbs. They worship other devotees and find all living entities related to Me. For Me they engage the entire energy of their bodies. They engage the power of speech in the glorification of My qualities and form. They also dedicate their minds unto Me and try to give up all kinds of material desires. Thus My devotees are characterized.'
text:
> ādaraḥ paricaryāyāṁ
> sarvāṅgair abhivandanam
> mad-bhakta-pūjābhyadhikā
> sarva-bhūteṣu man-matiḥ
>
> mad-artheṣv aṅga-ceṣṭā ca
> vacasā mad-guṇeraṇam
> mayy arpaṇaṁ ca manasaḥ
> sarva-kāma-vivarjanam
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ādaraḥ]]---respect, care; [[synonyms:p:paricaryāyām]]---in service; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅgaiḥ]]---by all the parts of the body; [[synonyms:a:abhivandanam]]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---of My devotees; [[synonyms:p:pūjā]]---worshiping; [[synonyms:a:abhyadhikā]]---very high; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūteṣu]]---in all living entities; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:m:matiḥ]]---realization of having a relationship with Me; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:a:artheṣu]]---for the sake of My service; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:c:ceṣṭāḥ]]---engaging the bodily energy; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:v:vacasā]]---by words; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ī:īraṇam]]---describing My glories; [[synonyms:m:mayi]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:a:arpaṇam]]---dedicating; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:m:manasaḥ]]---of the mind; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāma]]---all material desires; [[synonyms:v:vivarjanam]]---giving up.
translation: “ 'My devotees take great care and respect in rendering Me service. They offer obeisances to Me with all their bodily limbs. They worship other devotees and find all living entities related to Me. For Me they engage the entire energy of their bodies. They engage the power of speech in the glorification of My qualities and form. They also dedicate their minds unto Me and try to give up all kinds of material desires. Thus My devotees are characterized.'
purport: These two verses are quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.19.21-22). They were spoken by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Kṛṣṇa, who was answering Uddhava's inquiry about devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.3
description: The next day Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya requested Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to give him permission to submit a statement without fear.
text:
> āra dina sārvabhauma kahe prabhu-sthāne
> abhaya-dāna deha' yadi, kari nivedane
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---the next day; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in the presence of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:abhaya]]-[[synonyms:d:dāna]]---the charity of fearlessness; [[synonyms:d:deha']]---You give; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I do; [[synonyms:n:nivedane]]---submission.
translation: The next day Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya requested Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to give him permission to submit a statement without fear.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.31
description: "Lord Śiva told the goddess Durgā, 'My dear Devī, although the Vedas recommend worship of demigods, the worship of Lord Viṣṇu is topmost. However, above the worship of Lord Viṣṇu is the rendering of service to Vaiṣṇavas, who are related to Lord Viṣṇu.'
text:
> ārādhanānāṁ sarveṣāṁ
> viṣṇor ārādhanaṁ param
> tasmāt parataraṁ devi
> tadīyānāṁ samarcanam
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ārādhanānām]]---of varieties of worship; [[synonyms:s:sarveṣām]]---all; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇoḥ]]---of Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:ā:ārādhanam]]---worship; [[synonyms:p:param]]---the most exalted; [[synonyms:t:tasmāt]]---and above such worship of Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:p:parataram]]---of greater value; [[synonyms:d:devi]]---O goddess; [[synonyms:t:tadīyānām]]---of persons in relationship with Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:s:samarcanam]]---rigid and firm worship.
translation: "Lord Śiva told the goddess Durgā, 'My dear Devī, although the Vedas recommend worship of demigods, the worship of Lord Viṣṇu is topmost. However, above the worship of Lord Viṣṇu is the rendering of service to Vaiṣṇavas, who are related to Lord Viṣṇu.'
purport:
The //Vedas// are divided into three divisions-//karma-kāṇḍa, jñāna-kāṇḍa// and //upāsanā-kāṇḍa.// These are activities dealing with fruitive work, empiric philosophical speculation and worship. There are recommendations in the //Vedas// for the worship of various demigods as well as Lord Viṣṇu. In this quotation from the //Padma Purāṇa,// Lord Śiva answers a question posed to him by the goddess Durgā. This verse is also included in the //Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta// (2.4), by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. The words //viṣṇor ārādhanam// refer to the worship of Lord Viṣṇu, or Kṛṣṇa. Thus the supreme form of worship is the satisfaction of the Supreme Personality of Godhead Śrī Kṛṣṇa. It is further concluded that the worshiper of Lord Viṣṇu renders better service by worshiping the devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa. There are different types of devotees---those in //śānta-rasa, dāsya-rasa, sakhya-rasa, vātsalya-rasa// and //mādhurya-rasa.// Although all the //rasas// are on the transcendental platform, //mādhurya-rasa// is the supreme transcendental mellow. Consequently it is concluded that the worship of devotees engaged in the Lord's service in //mādhurya-rasa// is the supreme spiritual activity. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His followers mainly worship Lord Kṛṣṇa in //mādhurya-rasa.// Other Vaiṣṇava //ācāryas// recommended worship up to //vātsalya-rasa.// Therefore Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī in his //Vidagdha-mādhava// (1.2) describes Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's cult as supreme:

> anarpita-carīṁ cirāt karuṇayāvatīrṇaḥ kalau
> samarpayitum unnatojjvala-rasāṁ sva-bhakti-śriyam

Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu appeared in this Age of Kali to exhibit the superexcellence of //mādhurya-rasa,// a gift never previously bestowed by any //ācārya// or incarnation. Consequently Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is accepted as the most magnanimous incarnation. It is He only who distributed love of Kṛṣṇa while exhibiting the superexcellence of loving Kṛṣṇa in the conjugal //rasa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.32
description: " 'Those whose austerity is meager can hardly obtain the service of the pure devotees progressing on the path back to the kingdom of Godhead, the Vaikuṇṭhas. Pure devotees engage one hundred percent in glorifying the Supreme Lord, who is the Lord of the demigods and the controller of all living entities.' "
text:
> durāpā hy alpa-tapasaḥ
> sevā vaikuṇṭha-vartmasu
> yatropagīyate nityaṁ
> deva-devo janārdanaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:durāpā]]---very difficult to achieve; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:alpa]]-[[synonyms:t:tapasaḥ]]---by a person not advanced in spiritual life; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---service; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]]-[[synonyms:v:vartmasu]]---unto persons on the path back home, back to Godhead; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---wherein; [[synonyms:u:upagīyate]]---is worshiped and glorified; [[synonyms:n:nityam]]---regularly; [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:d:devaḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:j:janārdanaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: “ 'Those whose austerity is meager can hardly obtain the service of the pure devotees progressing on the path back to the kingdom of Godhead, the Vaikuṇṭhas. Pure devotees engage one hundred percent in glorifying the Supreme Lord, who is the Lord of the demigods and the controller of all living entities.' "
purport: This verse is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:7:20|(3.7.20)]]. It was spoken by Vidura in his conversation with Maitreya Ṛṣi, a great devotee of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.33
description: Paramānanda Purī, Brahmānanda Bhāratī Gosāñi, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosāñi, Lord Nityānanda, Jagadānanda, Mukunda and others were present before the Lord at that time.
text:
> purī, bhāratī-gosāñi, svarūpa, nityānanda
> jagadānanda, mukundādi yata bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---on the level of the spiritual master; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jagadānanda]]---Jagadānanda; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and others; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Paramānanda Purī, Brahmānanda Bhāratī Gosāñi, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosāñi, Lord Nityānanda, Jagadānanda, Mukunda and others were present before the Lord at that time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.34
description: Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya therefore offered his obeisances to all the Lord's devotees, in particular to the four spiritual masters. Thus Rāmānanda Rāya suitably met all the devotees.
text:
> cāri gosāñira kaila rāya caraṇa vandana
> yathā-yogya saba bhaktera karila milana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of the four //gosāñis,// or spiritual masters; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---worshiping the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]-[[synonyms:y:yogya]]---as it is befitting; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhaktera]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting.
translation: Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya therefore offered his obeisances to all the Lord's devotees, in particular to the four spiritual masters. Thus Rāmānanda Rāya suitably met all the devotees.
purport: The four spiritual masters referred to in this verse are Paramānanda Purī, Brahmānanda Bhāratī, Svarūpa Dāmodara and Lord Nityānanda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.35
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu next asked Rāmānanda Rāya, "Have you already visited the temple of the lotus-eyed Lord Jagannātha?"
text:
> prabhu kahe,-rāya, dekhile kamala-nayana?
> rāya kahe-ebe yāi pāba daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---My dear Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:d:dekhile]]---have you seen; [[synonyms:k:kamala]]-[[synonyms:n:nayana]]---the lotus-eyed Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Rāmānanda Rāya replied; [[synonyms:e:ebe]] [[synonyms:y:yāi]]---now I shall go; [[synonyms:p:pāba]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---I shall visit the temple.
translation:
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu next asked Rāmānanda Rāya, "Have you already visited the temple of the lotus-eyed Lord Jagannātha?"


Rāmānanda Rāya replied, "I shall now go visit the temple."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.36
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "What have you done, My dear Rāya? Why did you not first see Lord Jagannātha and then come here? Why have you come here first?"
text:
> prabhu kahe,-rāya, tumi ki kārya karile?
> īśvare nā dekhi' kene āge ethā āile?
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---My dear Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:k:kārya]]---what; [[synonyms:k:karile]]---have done; [[synonyms:ī:īśvare]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---without seeing; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---first; [[synonyms:e:ethā]]---here; [[synonyms:ā:āile]]---you came.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "What have you done, My dear Rāya? Why did you not first see Lord Jagannātha and then come here? Why have you come here first?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.37
description: Rāmānanda Rāya said, "The legs are like the chariot, and the heart is like the charioteer. Wherever the heart takes the living entity, the living entity is obliged to go."
text:
> rāya kahe, caraṇa-ratha, hṛdaya-sārathi
> yāhāṅ lañā yāya, tāhāṅ yāya jīva-rathī
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāyakahe]]---Rāmānanda Rāya replied; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the legs; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]---chariot; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]---the heart; [[synonyms:s:sārathi]]---chariot driver; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:r:rathī]]---the living entity on the chariot.
translation: Rāmānanda Rāya said, "The legs are like the chariot, and the heart is like the charioteer. Wherever the heart takes the living entity, the living entity is obliged to go."
purport:
In the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:18:61|(Bg. 18.61)]] Lord Kṛṣṇa explains:

> īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ
> hṛd-deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati
> bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni
> yantrārūḍhāni māyayā

"The Supreme Lord is situated in everyone's heart, O Arjuna, and is directing the wanderings of all living entities, who are seated as on a machine made of material energy."

Thus the living entity wanders within this universe riding upon a chariot (the body) bestowed by material nature. A similar explanation is given in the //Kaṭha Upaniṣad// (1.3.3-4):

> ātmānaṁ rathinaṁ viddhi
> śarīraṁ ratham eva tu
> buddhiṁ tu sārathiṁ viddhi
> manaḥ pragraham eva ca
>
> indriyāṇi hayān āhur
> viṣayāṁs teṣu gocarān
> ātmendriya-mano-yuktaṁ
> bhoktety āhur manīṣiṇaḥ

Here it is said that the living entity is the passenger riding in the chariot of the body, which is offered by material nature. The intelligence is the charioteer, the mind is the reins controlling the horses, and the senses are the horses. Thus the living entity is the false enjoyer of the material world.

One who is advanced in Kṛṣṇa consciousness can control the mind and intelligence and in this way rein in the horses, the senses, even though they are very powerful. One who can control the senses by his mind and intelligence can very easily approach the Supreme Personality of Godhead, or Viṣṇu, who is the ultimate goal of life. //Tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṁ padaṁ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ.// Those who are actually advanced approach Lord Viṣṇu, their ultimate goal. Such people are never captivated by Lord Viṣṇu's external energy, the material world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.38
description: Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya continued, "What shall I do? My mind has brought me here. I could not consider going first to Lord Jagannātha's temple."
text:
> āmi ki kariba, mana ihāṅ lañā āila
> jagannātha-daraśane vicāra nā kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---shall do; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---my mind; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---arrived; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---to see Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---consideration; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---did not; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---make.
translation: Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya continued, "What shall I do? My mind has brought me here. I could not consider going first to Lord Jagannātha's temple."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.39
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu advised, "Immediately go to Lord Jagannātha's temple to see the Lord. Then go home and meet your family members."
text:
> prabhu kahe,-śīghra giyā kara daraśana
> aiche ghara yāi' kara kuṭumba milana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]] [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---going hastily; [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---see Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---similarly; [[synonyms:g:ghara]] [[synonyms:y:yāi']]---going home; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---just do; [[synonyms:k:kuṭumba]]---family; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu advised, "Immediately go to Lord Jagannātha's temple to see the Lord. Then go home and meet your family members."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.4
description: The Lord gave the Bhaṭṭācārya assurance that he could speak without fear, but added that if his statement were suitable He would accept it, and if it were not, He would reject it.
text:
> prabhu kahe,-kaha tumi, nāhi kichu bhaya
> yogya haile kariba, ayogya haile naya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:k:kaha]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---yes, you can speak; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---any; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:y:yogya]]---befitting; [[synonyms:h:haile]]---if it is; [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---I shall grant; [[synonyms:a:ayogya]]---not befitting; [[synonyms:h:haile]]---if it is; [[synonyms:n:naya]]---then I shall not.
translation: The Lord gave the Bhaṭṭācārya assurance that he could speak without fear, but added that if his statement were suitable He would accept it, and if it were not, He would reject it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.40
description: Having received Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's permission, Rāmānanda Rāya hastily went to the temple of Lord Jagannātha. Who can understand the devotional service of Rāya Rāmānanda?
text:
> prabhu ājñā pāñā rāya calilā daraśane
> rāyera prema-bhakti-rīti bujhe kon jane
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhuājñā]]---the Lord's permission; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---departed; [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---to see Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:r:rāyera]]---of Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rīti]]---process; [[synonyms:b:bujhe]]---understands; [[synonyms:k:kon]] [[synonyms:j:jane]]---what person.
translation: Having received Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's permission, Rāmānanda Rāya hastily went to the temple of Lord Jagannātha. Who can understand the devotional service of Rāya Rāmānanda?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.41
description: When King Pratāparudra returned to Jagannātha Purī, he called for Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. When the Bhaṭṭācārya went to see the King, the King offered him respects and made the following inquiries.
text:
> kṣetre āsi' rājā sārvabhaume bolāilā
> sārvabhaume namaskari' tāṅhāre puchilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṣetre]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhaume]]---for Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:b:bolāilā]]---called; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhaume]]---unto Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:n:namaskari']]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāre]] [[synonyms:p:puchilā]]---he asked him.
translation: When King Pratāparudra returned to Jagannātha Purī, he called for Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. When the Bhaṭṭācārya went to see the King, the King offered him respects and made the following inquiries.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.42
description: The King asked, "Have you submitted my petition to the Lord?"
text:
> mora lāgi' prabhu-pade kaile nivedana?
> sārvabhauma kahe,-kainu aneka yatana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:moralāgi']]---on my behalf; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kaile]] [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---did you submit my petition; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sārvabhauma replied; [[synonyms:k:kainu]]---I did; [[synonyms:a:aneka]] [[synonyms:y:yatana]]---much endeavor.
translation:
The King asked, "Have you submitted my petition to the Lord?"


Sārvabhauma replied, "Yes, with much endeavor I have tried my best.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.43
description: "Yet despite my great endeavor, the Lord would not agree to see a king. Indeed, He said that if He were asked again, He would quit Jagannātha Purī and go elsewhere."
text:
> tathāpi nā kare teṅha rāja-daraśana
> kṣetra chāḍi' yābena punaḥ yadi kari nivedana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---yet; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does not do; [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---He; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting a king; [[synonyms:k:kṣetra]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---leaving Jagannātha-kṣetra; [[synonyms:y:yābena]]---He will go away; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:k:kari]] [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---I request.
translation: "Yet despite my great endeavor, the Lord would not agree to see a king. Indeed, He said that if He were asked again, He would quit Jagannātha Purī and go elsewhere."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.44
description: Hearing this, the King became very unhappy and, greatly lamenting, began to speak as follows.
text:
> śuniyā rājāra mane duḥkha upajila
> viṣāda kariyā kichu kahite lāgila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:r:rājāra]]---of the King; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:u:upajila]]---arose; [[synonyms:v:viṣāda]]---lamentation; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---doing; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began.
translation: Hearing this, the King became very unhappy and, greatly lamenting, began to speak as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.45
description: The King said, "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has descended just to deliver all kinds of sinful, lowborn persons. Consequently He has delivered sinners like Jagāi and Mādhāi.
text:
> pāpī nīca uddhārite tāṅra avatāra
> jagāi mādhāi teṅha karilā uddhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāpī]]---sinful; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]---lowborn; [[synonyms:u:uddhārite]]---to deliver; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnation; [[synonyms:j:jagāi]]---Jagāi; [[synonyms:m:mādhāi]]---Mādhāi; [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---He; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:u:uddhāra]]---delivered.
translation: The King said, "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has descended just to deliver all kinds of sinful, lowborn persons. Consequently He has delivered sinners like Jagāi and Mādhāi.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.46
description: "Alas, has Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu incarnated to deliver all kinds of sinners with the exception of a king named Mahārāja Pratāparudra?
text:
> pratāparudra chāḍi' karibe jagat nistāra
> ei pratijñā kari' kariyāchena avatāra?
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pratāparudra]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---except for Pratāparudra; [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---He will do; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---of the whole universe; [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---deliverance; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:p:pratijñā]]---this promise; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchena]]---has made; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnation.
translation: "Alas, has Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu incarnated to deliver all kinds of sinners with the exception of a king named Mahārāja Pratāparudra?
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mission is thus described by Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura: //patita-pāvana-hetu tava avatāra mo-sama patita prabhu nā pāibe āra.// If Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu descended to reclaim sinners, then one who is the most sinful and lowborn is the first candidate for the Lord's consideration. Mahārāja Pratāparudra considered himself a most fallen soul because he had to deal with material things constantly and enjoy material profits. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's business was the deliverance of the most fallen. How, then, could He reject the King? The more fallen a person is, the more he has the right to be delivered by the Lord-provided, of course, he surrenders unto the Lord. Mahārāja Pratāparudra was a fully surrendered soul; therefore the Lord could not refuse him on the grounds that he was a worldly pounds-shillings man.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.47
description: " 'Alas, has Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu made His advent deciding that He will deliver all others with the exception of me? He bestows His merciful glance upon many lower-class men who are usually not even to be seen.' "
text:
> adarśanīyān api nīca-jātīn
> saṁvīkṣate hanta tathāpi no mām
> mad-eka-varjaṁ kṛpayiṣyatīti
> nirṇīya kiṁ so 'vatatāra devaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:adarśanīyān]]---upon those who are unfit to be seen; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]-[[synonyms:j:jātīn]]---the lower class of men; [[synonyms:s:saṁvīkṣate]]---puts His merciful glance; [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---alas; [[synonyms:t:tathā]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---still; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:u:u]]---not; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---upon me; [[synonyms:m:mat]]---myself; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---alone; [[synonyms:v:varjam]]---rejecting; [[synonyms:k:kṛpayiṣyati]]---He will bestow His mercy; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:n:nirṇīya]]---deciding; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---whether; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:avatatāra]]---has descended; [[synonyms:d:devaḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'Alas, has Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu made His advent deciding that He will deliver all others with the exception of me? He bestows His merciful glance upon many lower-class men who are usually not even to be seen.' "
purport: This verse is found in the //Śrī Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka// (8.28).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.48
description: Mahārāja Pratāparudra continued, "If Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is determined not to see me, then I am determined to give up my life if I do not see Him.
text:
> tāṅra pratijñā-more nā karibe daraśana
> mora pratijñā-tāṅhā vinā chāḍiba jīvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:p:pratijñā]]---His determination; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto me; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---will do; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:p:pratijñā]]---my promise; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhā]] [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without Him; [[synonyms:c:chāḍiba]]---I will give up; [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---life.
translation: Mahārāja Pratāparudra continued, "If Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is determined not to see me, then I am determined to give up my life if I do not see Him.
purport:
A devotee with Mahārāja Pratāparudra's determination will certainly be victorious in advancing in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Śrī Kṛṣṇa confirms this in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:14|(Bg. 9.14)]]:

> satataṁ kīrtayanto māṁ
> yatantaś ca dṛḍha-vratāḥ
> namasyantaś ca māṁ bhaktyā
> nitya-yuktā upāsate

"Always chanting My glories, endeavoring with great determination, bowing down before Me, these great souls perpetually worship Me with devotion."

These are the symptoms of a //mahātmā// engaged in the Lord's service in full Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Thus Mahārāja Pratāparudra's determination is very much exalted and is called //dṛḍha-vrata.// Because of this determination, he was finally able to receive Lord Caitanya's direct mercy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.49
description: "If I do not receive Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mercy, my body and my kingdom are certainly useless."
text:
> yadi sei mahāprabhura nā pāi kṛpā-dhana
> kibā rājya, kibā deha,-saba akāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāi]]---I get; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---the treasure of mercy; [[synonyms:k:kibā]] [[synonyms:r:rājya]]---what is the value of my kingdom; [[synonyms:k:kibā]] [[synonyms:d:deha]]---what is the value of this body; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:a:akāraṇa]]---everything useless.
translation: "If I do not receive Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mercy, my body and my kingdom are certainly useless."
purport: This is an excellent example of //dṛḍha-vrata,// determination. If one does not receive the Supreme Personality of Godhead's mercy, one's life is defeated. In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:5:5:5|(5.5.5)]] it is said: //parābhavas tāvad abodha-jāto yāvan na jijñāsata ātma-tattvam.// Unless one inquires into spiritual life, everything is useless. Without spiritual inquiry, our labor and the object of our labor are simply a waste of time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.5
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "There is a king named Pratāparudra Rāya. He is very anxious to meet You, and he wants Your permission."
text:
> sārvabhauma kahe-ei pratāparudra rāya
> utkaṇṭhā hañāche, tomā milibāre cāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:p:pratāparudra]] [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---King Pratāparudra of Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:u:utkaṇṭhā]] [[synonyms:h:hañāche]]---has been very anxious; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]---You; [[synonyms:m:milibāre]]---to meet; [[synonyms:c:cāya]]---he wants.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "There is a king named Pratāparudra Rāya. He is very anxious to meet You, and he wants Your permission."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.50
description: Hearing King Pratāparudra's determination, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya became thoughtful. Indeed, he was very much astonished to see the King's determination.
text:
> eta śuni' sārvabhauma ha-ilā cintita
> rājāra anurāga dekhi' ha-ilā vismita
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:c:cintita]]---very thoughtful; [[synonyms:r:rājāra]]---of the King; [[synonyms:a:anurāga]]---attachment; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vismita]]---astonished.
translation: Hearing King Pratāparudra's determination, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya became thoughtful. Indeed, he was very much astonished to see the King's determination.
purport: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was astonished because such determination is not possible for a worldly man attached to material enjoyment. The King certainly had ample opportunity for material enjoyment, but he was thinking that his kingdom and everything else was useless if he could not see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. This is certainly sufficient cause for astonishment. In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// it is stated that //bhakti,// devotional service, must be unconditional. No material impediments can actually check the advancement of devotional service, be it executed by a common man or a king. In any case, devotional service rendered to the Lord is always complete, despite the devotee's material position. Devotional service is so exalted that it can be executed by anyone in any position. One must simply be //dṛḍha-vrata,// firmly determined.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.51
description: Finally Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "My dear King, do not worry. Because of your firm determination, I am sure that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mercy will definitely be bestowed upon you."
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya kahe-deva nā kara viṣāda
> tomāre prabhura avaśya ha-ibe prasāda
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:d:deva]]---O King; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:v:viṣāda]]---do not be worried; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---unto you; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ibe]]---there must be; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---mercy.
translation: Finally Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "My dear King, do not worry. Because of your firm determination, I am sure that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mercy will definitely be bestowed upon you."
purport:
Due to King Pratāparudra's firm determination, the Bhaṭṭācārya predicted that the King would receive Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mercy without fail. As confirmed elsewhere in //Caitanya-caritāmṛta// [[books:cc:madhya:19:151|(Madhya 19.151)]], //guru-kṛṣṇa-prasāde pāya bhakti-latā-bīja:// "By the mercy of the spiritual master and Kṛṣṇa, one gets the seed of devotional service." The Bhaṭṭācārya was the spiritual master of King Pratāparudra, and he gave his blessings to the effect that the Lord would be merciful upon the King. The mercy of the spiritual master and Kṛṣṇa combine to grant success to a devotee engaged in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. This is confirmed by the //Vedas://

> yasya deve parā bhaktir
> yathā deve tathā gurau
> tasyaite kathitā hy arthāḥ
> prakāśante mahātmanaḥ

"Only unto those great souls who have implicit faith in both the Lord and the spiritual master are all the imports of Vedic knowledge automatically revealed." (//Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad// 6.23)

Mahārāja Pratāparudra had firm faith in the Bhaṭṭācārya, who declared Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to be the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Having firm faith in the Bhaṭṭācārya as his spiritual master, King Pratāparudra immediately accepted Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as the Supreme Lord. Thus he began worshiping Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in his mind. This is the process of devotional service. According to Lord Kṛṣṇa in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:34|(Bg. 9.34)]]:

> man-manā bhava mad-bhakto
> mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru
> mām evaiṣyasi yuktvaivam
> ātmānaṁ mat-parāyaṇaḥ

"Engage your mind always in thinking of Me, become My devotee, offer obeisances to Me and worship Me. Being completely absorbed in Me, surely you will come to Me."

This process is very simple. One need only be firmly convinced by the spiritual master that Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. If one decides this, he can make further progress by thinking of Kṛṣṇa, chanting of Kṛṣṇa and glorifying Him. There is then no doubt that such a fully surrendered devotee will receive the blessings of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Śrīla Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya explains this further.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.52
description: As soon as the Bhaṭṭācārya saw the King's firm determination, he declared, "The Supreme Lord is approached only by pure love. Your love for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is very, very deep; therefore without a doubt He will be merciful upon you."
text:
> teṅha-premādhīna, tomāra prema-gāḍhatara
> avaśya karibena kṛpā tomāra upara
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---He (Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu); [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:a:adhīna]]---under the control of love; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:p:prema]]---your love; [[synonyms:g:gāḍha]]-[[synonyms:t:tara]]---very deep; [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:k:karibena]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---He will bestow mercy; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:u:upara]]---upon you.
translation: As soon as the Bhaṭṭācārya saw the King's firm determination, he declared, "The Supreme Lord is approached only by pure love. Your love for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is very, very deep; therefore without a doubt He will be merciful upon you."
purport: Such determination is the first qualification. As confirmed by Rūpa Gosvāmī (//Upadeśāmṛta// 3): //utsāhān niścayād dhairyāt.// One must first have firm determination, firm faith. When one engages in devotional service, he must maintain this firm determination. Then Kṛṣṇa will be pleased with his service. The spiritual master can show the path of devotional service. If the disciple follows the principles rigidly and undeviatingly, he will certainly receive the mercy of Kṛṣṇa. This is confirmed by the //śāstras.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.53
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then suggested, "There is one means by which you can directly see Him.
text:
> tathāpi kahiye āmi eka upāya
> ei upāya kara' prabhu dekhibe yāhāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:k:kahiye]]---say; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---one means; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---this means; [[synonyms:k:kara']]---try to adopt; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhibe]]---will see you; [[synonyms:y:yāhāya]]---by that.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then suggested, "There is one means by which you can directly see Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.54
description: "On the day of the car festival, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will dance before the Deity in great ecstatic love.
text:
> ratha-yātrā-dine prabhu saba bhakta lañā
> ratha-āge nṛtya karibena premāviṣṭa hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---on the day of the car festival ceremony; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotees; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking with Him; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]---the chariot; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:karibena]]---will dance; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---in great ecstatic love.
translation: "On the day of the car festival, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will dance before the Deity in great ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.55
description: "On that Ratha-yātrā festival day, after dancing before the Lord, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will enter the Guṇḍicā garden. At that time you should go there alone, stripped of your royal dress.
text:
> premāveśe puṣpodyāne karibena praveśa
> sei-kāle ekale tumi chāḍi' rāja-veśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:u:udyāne]]---into the garden at Guṇḍicā where the Lord stays; [[synonyms:k:karibena]] [[synonyms:p:praveśa]]---will enter; [[synonyms:s:sei]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time; [[synonyms:e:ekale]]---alone; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:v:veśa]]---the royal dress.
translation: "On that Ratha-yātrā festival day, after dancing before the Lord, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will enter the Guṇḍicā garden. At that time you should go there alone, stripped of your royal dress.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.56
description: "When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu enters the Guṇḍicā, you should also go there and read the five chapters about Lord Kṛṣṇa's dancing with the gopīs. In this way you can catch hold of the Lord's lotus feet.
text:
> 'kṛṣṇa-rāsa-pañcādhyāya' karite paṭhana
> ekale yāi' mahāprabhura dharibe caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:a:adhyāya]]---the five chapters in the Tenth Canto of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// in which Lord Kṛṣṇa's pastimes of the //rāsa// dance are described; [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:p:paṭhana]]---to recite; [[synonyms:e:ekale]] [[synonyms:y:yāi']]---going alone; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dharibe]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---catch hold of the lotus feet.
translation: "When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu enters the Guṇḍicā, you should also go there and read the five chapters about Lord Kṛṣṇa's dancing with the gopīs. In this way you can catch hold of the Lord's lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.57
description: "Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will be in a mood of ecstatic love, without external consciousness. At that time, as you recite those chapters from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, He will embrace you, knowing you to be a pure Vaiṣṇava.
text:
> bāhya-jñāna nāhi, se-kāle kṛṣṇa-nāma śuni,
> āliṅgana karibena tomāya 'vaiṣṇava' jāni'
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---without external consciousness; [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---by hearing the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]] [[synonyms:k:karibena]]---He will embrace; [[synonyms:t:tomāya]]---you; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---taking you to be a Vaiṣṇava.
translation: "Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will be in a mood of ecstatic love, without external consciousness. At that time, as you recite those chapters from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, He will embrace you, knowing you to be a pure Vaiṣṇava.
purport: A Vaiṣṇava is always ready to help another Vaiṣṇava progress toward realization of the Absolute Truth. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya could understand the King's position as a pure Vaiṣṇava. The King was always thinking of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the Bhaṭṭācārya wanted to help him approach the Lord. A Vaiṣṇava is always compassionate, especially when he sees a prospective devotee very much determined (//dṛḍha-vrata//). Consequently the Bhaṭṭācārya was ready to help the King.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.58
description: "The Lord has already changed His mind due to Rāmānanda Rāya's description of your pure love for Him."
text:
> rāmānanda rāya, āji tomāra prema-guṇa
> prabhu-āge kahite prabhura phiri' gela mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]] [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:ā:āji]]---today; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---quality of love; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---when he described; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:phiri']] [[synonyms:g:gela]]---became changed; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: "The Lord has already changed His mind due to Rāmānanda Rāya's description of your pure love for Him."
purport:
At first the Lord did not want to see the King, but due to the Bhaṭṭācārya's and Rāmānanda Rāya's earnest endeavors, the Lord's mind was changed. The Lord already declared that Kṛṣṇa would be merciful upon the King due to the King's service to the devotees. This is the process by which one can advance in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. First there must be the devotee's mercy; then Kṛṣṇa's mercy will descend. //Yasya prasādād bhagavat-prasādo yasyāprasādān na gatiḥ kuto 'pi.// Our first duty, therefore, is to satisfy the spiritual master, who can arrange for the Lord's mercy. A common man must first begin to serve the spiritual master, or the devotee. Then, through the mercy of the devotee, the Lord will be satisfied. Unless one receives the dust of a devotee's lotus feet on one's head, there is no possibility of advancement. This is also confirmed by a statement of Prahlāda Mahārāja's in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:7:5:32|(7.5.32)]]:

> naiṣāṁ matis tāvad urukramāṅghriṁ
> spṛśaty anarthāpagamo yad-arthaḥ
> mahīyasāṁ pāda-rajo-'bhiṣekaṁ
> niṣkiñcanānāṁ na vṛṇīta yāvat

Unless one approaches a pure devotee, he cannot understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Mahārāja Pratāparudra worshiped both Rāmānanda Rāya and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. Thus he touched the lotus feet of pure devotees and was able thereby to approach Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.59
description: Mahārāja Pratāparudra took the Bhaṭṭācārya's advice and firmly decided to follow his instructions. Thus he felt transcendental happiness.
text:
> śuni' gajapatira mane sukha upajila
> prabhure milite ei mantraṇā dṛḍha kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:g:gajapatira]]---of King Pratāparudra; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:u:upajila]]---awakened; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:milite]]---to meet; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mantraṇā]]---instruction; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---decided to accept rigidly.
translation: Mahārāja Pratāparudra took the Bhaṭṭācārya's advice and firmly decided to follow his instructions. Thus he felt transcendental happiness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.6
description: As soon as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard this proposal, He immediately covered His ears with His hands and said, "My dear Sārvabhauma, why are you requesting such an undesirable thing from Me?
text:
> karṇe hasta diyā prabhu smare 'nārāyaṇa'
> sārvabhauma, kaha kena ayogya vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:karṇe]]---on the ears; [[synonyms:h:hasta]]---hands; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---placing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:smare]]---remembers; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---the holy name of Lord Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---My dear Sārvabhauma; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---you say; [[synonyms:k:kena]]---why; [[synonyms:a:ayogya]] [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---a request that is not suitable.
translation: As soon as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard this proposal, He immediately covered His ears with His hands and said, "My dear Sārvabhauma, why are you requesting such an undesirable thing from Me?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.60
description: When the King asked the Bhaṭṭācārya when the bathing ceremony [Snāna-yātrā] of Lord Jagannātha would take place, the Bhaṭṭācārya replied that there were only three days left before the ceremony.
text:
> snāna-yātrā kabe habe puchila bhaṭṭere
> bhaṭṭa kahe,-tina dina āchaye yātrāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:snāna]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---the bathing ceremony of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:k:kabe]]---when; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---will be; [[synonyms:p:puchila]]---he inquired; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭere]]---from the Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---three days; [[synonyms:ā:āchaye]]---there are still; [[synonyms:y:yātrāre]]---until the festival.
translation: When the King asked the Bhaṭṭācārya when the bathing ceremony [Snāna-yātrā] of Lord Jagannātha would take place, the Bhaṭṭācārya replied that there were only three days left before the ceremony.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.61
description: After thus encouraging the King, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya returned home. On the day of Lord Jagannātha's bathing ceremony, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very happy at heart.
text:
> rājāre prabodhiyā bhaṭṭa gelā nijālaya
> snāna-yātrā-dine prabhura ānanda hṛdaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājāre]]---the King; [[synonyms:p:prabodhiyā]]---encouraging; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---departed; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:ā:ālaya]]---to his own home; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---on the day of the bathing ceremony of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---full of happiness; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]---heart.
translation: After thus encouraging the King, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya returned home. On the day of Lord Jagannātha's bathing ceremony, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very happy at heart.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.62
description: Upon seeing the bathing ceremony of Lord Jagannātha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very happy. But when Lord Jagannātha retired after the ceremony, Lord Caitanya became very unhappy because He could not see Him.
text:
> snāna-yātrā dekhi' prabhura haila baḍa sukha
> īśvarera 'anavasare' pāila baḍa duḥkha
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:snāna]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---the bathing ceremony of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very much; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:ī:īśvarera]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:a:anavasare]]---during the pastime of retirement; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very much; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness.
translation: Upon seeing the bathing ceremony of Lord Jagannātha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very happy. But when Lord Jagannātha retired after the ceremony, Lord Caitanya became very unhappy because He could not see Him.
purport: After the bathing ceremony of Śrī Jagannātha, which takes place just a fortnight before the Ratha-yātrā ceremony, the body of the Lord Jagannātha Deity is repainted, and this takes just about a fortnight to complete. This period is called Anavasara. There are many who visit the temple to see Lord Jagannātha regularly every day, and for them His retirement after the bathing ceremony is unbearable. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu felt Lord Jagannātha's absence from the temple very much.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.63
description: Due to separation from Lord Jagannātha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu felt the same great anxiety the gopīs feel in separation from Kṛṣṇa. In this condition He gave up all association and went to Ālālanātha.
text:
> gopī-bhāve virahe prabhu vyākula hañā
> ālālanāthe gelā prabhu sabāre chāḍiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in the mood of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:v:virahe]]---in separation; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vyākula]]---agitated; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:ā:ālālanāthe]]---to Ālālanātha; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---all; [[synonyms:c:chāḍiyā]]---having given up.
translation: Due to separation from Lord Jagannātha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu felt the same great anxiety the gopīs feel in separation from Kṛṣṇa. In this condition He gave up all association and went to Ālālanātha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.64
description: The devotees who had followed the Lord came into His presence and requested Him to return to Purī. They submitted that the devotees from Bengal were coming to Puruṣottama-kṣetra.
text:
> pāche prabhura nikaṭa āilā bhakta-gaṇa
> gauḍa haite bhakta āise,-kaila nivedana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---behind; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nikaṭa]]---in the presence; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from Bengal; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---come; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---submitted.
translation: The devotees who had followed the Lord came into His presence and requested Him to return to Purī. They submitted that the devotees from Bengal were coming to Puruṣottama-kṣetra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.65
description: In this way Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya brought Lord Caitanya back to Jagannātha Purī. He then went to King Pratāparudra and informed him of the Lord's arrival.
text:
> sārvabhauma nīlācale āilā prabhu lañā
> prabhu āilā,-rājā-ṭhāñi kahilena giyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---to the King; [[synonyms:k:kahilena]]---said; [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---after going.
translation: In this way Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya brought Lord Caitanya back to Jagannātha Purī. He then went to King Pratāparudra and informed him of the Lord's arrival.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.66
description: At this time, Gopīnātha Ācārya came there while Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was with King Pratāparudra. Being a brāhmaṇa, he offered his benediction to the King and addressed Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya as follows.
text:
> hena-kāle āilā tathā gopīnāthācārya
> rājāke āśīrvāda kari' kahe,-śuna bhaṭṭācārya
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---during this time; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---there; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:r:rājāke]]---unto the King; [[synonyms:ā:āśīrvāda]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---offering a benediction; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]] [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---my dear Bhaṭṭācārya, kindly listen.
translation: At this time, Gopīnātha Ācārya came there while Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was with King Pratāparudra. Being a brāhmaṇa, he offered his benediction to the King and addressed Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.67
description: "About two hundred devotees are coming from Bengal. All of them are greatly advanced devotees and specifically devoted to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> gauḍa haite vaiṣṇava āsitechena dui-śata
> mahāprabhura bhakta saba-mahā-bhāgavata
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍahaite]]---from Bengal; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āsitechena]]---are coming; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:ś:śata]]---numbering about two hundred; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]---greatly advanced devotees.
translation: "About two hundred devotees are coming from Bengal. All of them are greatly advanced devotees and specifically devoted to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.68
description: "All of them have already arrived on the bank of Lake Narendra and are waiting there. I desire residential quarters and prasāda arrangements for them."
text:
> narendre āsiyā sabe haila vidyamāna
> tāṅ-sabāre cāhi vāsā prasāda-samādhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:narendre]]---on the bank of Lake Narendra; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:h:haila]] [[synonyms:v:vidyamāna]]---staying; [[synonyms:t:tāṅ]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---for all of them; [[synonyms:c:cāhi]]---I want; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]]---residential quarters; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---for distributing //prasāda//; [[synonyms:s:samādhāna]]---arrangement.
translation: "All of them have already arrived on the bank of Lake Narendra and are waiting there. I desire residential quarters and prasāda arrangements for them."
purport: Narendra is a small lake still existing in Jagannātha Purī, where the Candana-yātrā festival takes place. Up to the present date, all the Bengali devotees who visit the Jagannātha temple first take their bath in this lake. There they wash their hands and feet before entering the temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.69
description: The King replied, "I shall give orders to the attendant in the temple. He will arrange for everyone's residential quarters and prasāda, as you desire.
text:
> rājā kahe,-paḍichāke āmi ājñā diba
> vāsā ādi ye cāhiye,-paḍichā saba diba
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the King said; [[synonyms:p:paḍichāke]]---unto the attendant; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:diba]]---shall give orders; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]]---residential quarters; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and other arrangements; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:c:cāhiye]]---whatever you want; [[synonyms:p:paḍichā]]---the attendant; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---everything; [[synonyms:d:diba]]---will supply.
translation: The King replied, "I shall give orders to the attendant in the temple. He will arrange for everyone's residential quarters and prasāda, as you desire.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.7
description: "Since I am in the renounced order, it is as dangerous for Me to meet a king as to meet a woman. To meet either would be just like drinking poison."
text:
> virakta sannyāsī āmāra rāja-daraśana
> strī-daraśana-sama viṣera bhakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:virakta]]---unattached; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---person in the renounced order; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---meeting a king; [[synonyms:s:strī]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---meeting a woman; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---like; [[synonyms:v:viṣera]]---of poison; [[synonyms:b:bhakṣaṇa]]---drinking.
translation: "Since I am in the renounced order, it is as dangerous for Me to meet a king as to meet a woman. To meet either would be just like drinking poison."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.70
description: "Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, please show me, one after another, all of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's devotees who are coming from Bengal."
text:
> mahāprabhura gaṇa yata āila gauḍa haite
> bhaṭṭācārya, eke eke dekhāha āmāte
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---associates; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---who have come; [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from Bengal; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:e:eke]] [[synonyms:e:eke]]---one after another; [[synonyms:d:dekhāha]]---please show; [[synonyms:ā:āmāte]]---to me.
translation: "Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, please show me, one after another, all of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's devotees who are coming from Bengal."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.71
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya requested the King, "Go up on the roof of the palace. Gopīnātha Ācārya knows every one of the devotees. He will identify them for you.
text:
> bhaṭṭa kahe,-aṭṭālikāya kara ārohaṇa
> gopīnātha cine sabāre, karābe daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:a:aṭṭālikāya]]---on the roof of the palace; [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:ā:ārohaṇa]]---just go up; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:c:cine]]---knows; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---everyone; [[synonyms:k:karābe]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---he will show.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya requested the King, "Go up on the roof of the palace. Gopīnātha Ācārya knows every one of the devotees. He will identify them for you.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.72
description: "Actually I do not know any of them, although I have a desire to know them. Since Gopīnātha Ācārya knows them all, he will give you their names."
text:
> āmi kāho nāhi cini, cinite mana haya
> gopīnāthācārya sabāre karā'be paricaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kāho]]---anyone; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---do not; [[synonyms:c:cini]]---know; [[synonyms:c:cinite]] [[synonyms:m:mana]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---I desire to know; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---all of them; [[synonyms:k:karā'be]] [[synonyms:p:paricaya]]---will identify.
translation: "Actually I do not know any of them, although I have a desire to know them. Since Gopīnātha Ācārya knows them all, he will give you their names."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.73
description: After Sārvabhauma said this, he went up to the top of the palace with the King and Gopīnātha Ācārya. At this time all the Vaiṣṇava devotees from Bengal drew closer to the palace.
text:
> eta bali' tina jana aṭṭālikāya caḍila
> hena-kāle vaiṣṇava saba nikaṭe āila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---the three persons (namely, the King, Gopīnātha Ācārya and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya); [[synonyms:a:aṭṭālikāya]]---on the roof of the palace; [[synonyms:c:caḍila]]---went up; [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---the Vaiṣṇava devotees; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:n:nikaṭe]]---nearby; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came.
translation: After Sārvabhauma said this, he went up to the top of the palace with the King and Gopīnātha Ācārya. At this time all the Vaiṣṇava devotees from Bengal drew closer to the palace.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.74
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara and Govinda, taking the flower garlands and prasāda of Lord Jagannātha, proceeded to where all the Vaiṣṇavas were standing.
text:
> dāmodara-svarūpa, govinda,-dui jana
> mālā-prasāda lañā yāya, yāhāṅ vaiṣṇava-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]-[[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons; [[synonyms:m:mālā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---flower garlands and remnants of Lord Jagannātha's food; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---went; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the Vaiṣṇavas.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara and Govinda, taking the flower garlands and prasāda of Lord Jagannātha, proceeded to where all the Vaiṣṇavas were standing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.75
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu first sent them both in advance. The King inquired, "Who are these two? Please let me know their identities."
text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.8
description: Greatly lamenting, the Lord then informed Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, " 'Alas, for a person who is seriously desiring to cross the material ocean and engage in the transcendental loving service of the Lord without material motives, seeing a materialist engaged in sense gratification or seeing a woman who is similarly interested is more abominable than drinking poison willingly.' "

> niṣkiñcanaṣya bhagavad-bhajanonmukhasya

> sandarśanaṁ viṣayiṇām atha yoṣitāṁ ca
> hā hanta hanta viṣa-bhakṣaṇato 'py asādhu
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:niṣkiñcanasya]]---of a person who has completely detached himself from material enjoyment; [[synonyms:b:bhagavat]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---in serving; [[synonyms:u:unmukhasya]]---who is eager to be engaged; [[synonyms:p:pāram]]---to the other side; [[synonyms:p:param]]---distant; [[synonyms:j:jigamiṣoḥ]]---who is desiring to go; [[synonyms:b:bhava]]-[[synonyms:s:sāgarasya]]---of the ocean of material existence; [[synonyms:s:sandarśanam]]---the seeing (for some material purpose); [[synonyms:v:viṣayiṇām]]---of persons engaged in material activities; [[synonyms:a:atha]]---as well as; [[synonyms:y:yoṣitām]]---of women; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:h:hā]]---alas; [[synonyms:h:hanta]] [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---expression of great lamentation; [[synonyms:v:viṣa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakṣaṇataḥ]]---than the act of drinking poison; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:a:asādhu]]---more abominable.
translation: Greatly lamenting, the Lord then informed Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, " 'Alas, for a person who is seriously desiring to cross the material ocean and engage in the transcendental loving service of the Lord without material motives, seeing a materialist engaged in sense gratification or seeing a woman who is similarly interested is more abominable than drinking poison willingly.' "
purport:
This is a quotation from //Śrī Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka// (8.23). Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu enunciates the principles for a //sannyāsī// renouncing the material world for spiritual advancement. Spiritual advancement is not meant for magic shows and jugglery but for crossing the material world and being transferred to the spiritual world. //Pāraṁ paraṁ jigamiṣoḥ// means desiring to go to the other side of the material world. There is a river called Vaitaraṇī, and on one side of this river is the material world, and on the other side is the spiritual world. Since the Vaitaraṇī River is compared to a great ocean, it is named //bhava-sāgara,// the ocean of repeated birth and death. Spiritual life aims at stopping this repetition of birth and death and entering into the spiritual world, where one can live eternally cognizant and blissful.

Unfortunately, the general populace does not know anything about spiritual life or the spiritual world. The spiritual world is mentioned in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:8:20|(Bg. 8.20)]]:

> paras tasmāt tu bhāvo 'nyo
> 'vyakto 'vyaktāt sanātanaḥ
> yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu
> naśyatsu na vinaśyati

"Yet there is another unmanifest nature, which is eternal and is transcendental to this manifested and unmanifested matter. It is supreme and is never annihilated. When all in this world is annihilated, that part remains as it is."

Thus there is a spiritual nature beyond this material world, and that spiritual nature exists eternally. Spiritual advancement means stopping material activities and entering into spiritual activities. This is the process of //bhakti-yoga.// In the material world, the via media for sense gratification is mainly a woman. One who is seriously interested in spiritual life should strictly avoid women. A //sannyāsī// should never see a man or a woman for material benefit. In addition, talks with materialistic men and women are also dangerous, and they are compared to drinking poison. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very strict on this point. He therefore refused to see King Pratāparudra, who was naturally always engaged in political and economic affairs. The Lord even refused to see the King despite the request of a personality like Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, who was the Lord's intimate friend and devotee.

As far as Vāsudeva Ghoṣa is concerned, he composed many nice songs about Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and these are all authorized Vaiṣṇava songs, like the songs of Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura, Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, Locana dāsa Ṭhākura, Govinda dāsa Ṭhākura and other great Vaiṣṇavas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.89

> rāghava paṇḍita, iṅha ācārya nandana
> śrīmān paṇḍita ei, śrīkānta, nārāyaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāghava]] [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---Rāghava Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:i:iṅha]]---here; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:n:nandana]]---Ācārya Nandana; [[synonyms:ś:śrīmān]] [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---Śrīmān Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śrīkānta]]---Śrīkānta; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---and also Nārāyaṇa.
translation: "Here is Rāghava Paṇḍita, here is Ācārya Nandana, there is Śrīmān Paṇḍita, and here are Śrīkānta and Nārāyaṇa."
purport:
Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura, honoring the personal associates of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, has sung as follows (//Prārthanā// 13):

> gaurāṅgera saṅgi-gaṇe,     nitya-siddha kari' māne
> se yāya vrajendra-suta-pāśa

One who is intelligent understands that all the personal associates and devotees of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are ever liberated. This means that they do not belong to this material world because they are always engaged in the devotional service of the Lord. One who is engaged in the Lord's devotional service twenty-four hours daily and never forgets the Lord is called //nitya-siddha.// Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī confirms this statement:

> īhā yasya harer dāsye
> karmaṇā manasā girā
> nikhilāsv apy avasthāsu
> jīvan-muktaḥ sa ucyate

"A person acting in the service of Kṛṣṇa with body, mind, intelligence and words is a liberated person even within the material world, although he may be engaged in many so-called material activities." (//Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// 1.2.187)

A devotee is always thinking of how better to serve Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and how to broadcast His name, fame and qualities throughout the world. One who is //nitya-siddha// has no business other than broadcasting the glories of the Lord all over the world according to his ability. Such people are already associates of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Therefore Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says, //nitya-siddha kari' māne.// One should not think that because Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was personally present five hundred years ago, only His associates were liberated. Rather, Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says that anyone is a //nitya-siddha// if he acts on behalf of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by spreading the glories of the holy name of the Lord. We should respect those devotees preaching the glories of the Lord as //nitya-siddha// and should not consider them conditioned.

> māṁ ca yo 'vyabhicāreṇa
> bhakti-yogena sevate
> sa guṇān samatītyaitān
> brahma-bhūyāya kalpate

(Bg. 14.26)

One who has transcended the material modes of nature is said to be on the Brahman platform. That is also the platform of //nitya-siddha.// The //nitya-siddha// not only stays on the Brahman platform but also works on that platform. Simply by accepting the associates of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu as //nitya-siddha,// one can very easily go back home, back to Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.9

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.95
description: "Indeed, their effulgence is like the brilliance of a million suns. Nor have I ever heard the Lord's names chanted so melodiously.
text:
> koṭi-sūrya-sama saba-ujjvala-varaṇa
> kabhu nāhi śuni ei madhura kīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:s:sūrya]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal to the shining of millions of suns; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of them; [[synonyms:u:ujjvala]]-[[synonyms:v:varaṇa]]---very bright luster; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---I have never heard; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:madhura]] [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---such melodious performance of congregational chanting.
translation: "Indeed, their effulgence is like the brilliance of a million suns. Nor have I ever heard the Lord's names chanted so melodiously.
purport: Such are the symptoms of pure devotees when they are chanting. All the pure devotees are as bright as sunshine, and their bodily luster is very effulgent. In addition, their performance of //saṅkīrtana// is unparalleled. There are many professional chanters who can perform congregational chanting with various musical instruments in an artistic and musical way, but their chanting cannot be as attractive as the congregational chanting of pure devotees. If a devotee sticks strictly to the principles governing Vaiṣṇava behavior, his bodily luster will naturally be attractive, and his singing and chanting of the holy names of the Lord will be effective. People will appreciate such //kīrtana// without hesitation. Even dramas about the pastimes of Lord Caitanya or Śrī Kṛṣṇa should be played by devotees. Such dramas will immediately interest an audience and be full of potency. The students of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness should note these two points and try to apply these principles in their spreading of the Lord's glories.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.96
description: "I have never before seen such ecstatic love, nor heard the vibration of the holy name of the Lord chanted in such a way, nor seen such dancing during saṅkīrtana."
text:
> aiche prema, aiche nṛtya, aiche hari-dhvani
> kāhāṅ nāhi dekhi, aiche kāhāṅ nāhi śuni
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---ecstatic love; [[synonyms:a:aiche]] [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---such dancing; [[synonyms:a:aiche]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---such vibration of the chanting of the holy name; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---anywhere; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---I have never seen; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---anywhere; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---I never heard.
translation: "I have never before seen such ecstatic love, nor heard the vibration of the holy name of the Lord chanted in such a way, nor seen such dancing during saṅkīrtana."
purport: Because the temple of Lord Jagannātha is situated at Jagannātha Purī, many devotees from all parts of the world came to perform //saṅkīrtana// in glorification of the Lord. All these devotees were certainly seen and heard by Mahārāja Pratāparudra, but he herein admits that the //kīrtana// performed by the associates of the Lord was unique. He had never before heard such //saṅkīrtana// nor seen such attractive features manifest by the devotees. The members of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness should go to India during the birthday ceremony of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu at Māyāpura and perform //saṅkīrtana// congregationally. This will attract the attention of all the important personalities in India, just as the beauty, bodily luster and //saṅkīrtana// performance by the associates of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu attracted the attention of Mahārāja Pratāparudra. The associates of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were unlimited during the Lord's presence on this planet, but anyone who is pure in life and devoted to the mission of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is to be understood as a //nitya-siddha// associate of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 11.99
description: "Anyone who worships Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu by congregational chanting should be understood to be very intelligent. One who does not do so must be considered a victim of this age and bereft of all intelligence.
text:
> saṅkīrtana-yajñe tāṅre kare ārādhana
> sei ta' sumedhā, āra-kali-hata-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]-[[synonyms:y:yajñe]]---in the performance of congregational chanting; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ā:ārādhana]]---worship; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---such a person; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:medhā]]---sharply intelligent; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---others; [[synonyms:k:kali]]-[[synonyms:h:hata]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---victims of this Age of Kali.
translation: "Anyone who worships Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu by congregational chanting should be understood to be very intelligent. One who does not do so must be considered a victim of this age and bereft of all intelligence.
purport:
Rascals propose that anyone can invent his own religious process, and this proposition is condemned herein. If one actually wants to become religious, he must take up the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// The real meaning of religion is stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:6:3:19|(6.3.19-22)]].

> dharmaṁ tu sākṣād bhagavat-praṇītaṁ
> na vai vidur ṛṣayo nāpi devāḥ
> na siddha-mukhyā asurā manuṣyāḥ
> kuto nu vidyādhara-cāraṇādayaḥ
>
> svayambhūr nāradaḥ śambhuḥ
> kumāraḥ kapilo manuḥ
> prahlādo janako bhīṣmo
> balir vaiyāsakir vayam
>
> dvādaśaite vijānīmo
> dharmaṁ bhāgavataṁ bhaṭāḥ
> guhyaṁ viśuddhaṁ durbodhaṁ
> yaṁ jñātvāmṛtam aśnute
>
> etāvān eva loke 'smin
> puṁsāṁ dharmaḥ paraḥ smṛtaḥ
> bhakti-yogo bhagavati
> tan-nāma-grahaṇādibhiḥ

The purport of these verses is that //dharma,// or religion, cannot be manufactured by a human being. Religion is the law or code of the Lord. Consequently religion cannot be manufactured even by great saintly persons, demigods or //siddha-mukhyas,// and what to speak of //asuras,// human beings, Vidyādharas, Cāraṇas, and so on. The principles of //dharma,// religion, come down in the //paramparā// system beginning with twelve personalities-namely, Lord Brahmā; the great saint Nārada; Lord Śiva; the four Kumāras; Kapila, the son of Devahūti; Svāyambhuva Manu; Prahlāda Mahārāja; King Janaka; grandfather Bhīṣma; Bali Mahārāja; Śukadeva Gosvāmī; and Yamarāja. The principles of religion are known to these twelve personalities. //Dharma// refers to the religious principles by which one can understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead. //Dharma// is very confidential, uncontaminated by any material influence, and very difficult for ordinary men to understand. However, if one actually understands //dharma,// he immediately becomes liberated and is transferred to the kingdom of God. //Bhāgavata-dharma,// or the principle of religion enunciated by the //paramparā// system, is the supreme principle of religion. In other words, //dharma// refers to the science of //bhakti-yoga,// which begins by the novice's chanting the holy name of the Lord (//tan-nāma-grahaṇādibhiḥ//).

Therefore in this Age of Kali, as recommended here in the //Caitanya-caritāmṛta// [[books:cc:madhya:11:98|(text 98)]], //kali-kāle dharma-kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana:// the chanting of the holy name of the Lord is the method of religion approved by all Vedic scriptures. In the next text of the //Caitanya-caritāmṛta,// quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.32), this principle is further stressed.
