> nija-vastre kaila prabhu gṛha sammārjana
> mahāprabhu nija-vastre mājila siṁhāsana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:v:vastre]]---by His own garment; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gṛha]]---room; [[synonyms:s:sammārjana]]---mopping; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:v:vastre]]---by His own garment; [[synonyms:m:mājila]]---polished; [[synonyms:s:siṁhāsana]]---throne.
translation: The Lord mopped the rooms with His own clothes, and He polished the throne with them also.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.105
description: In this way all the rooms were cleansed with a hundred waterpots. After the rooms had been cleansed, the minds of the devotees were as clean as the rooms.
text:
> śata ghaṭa jale haila mandira mārjana
> mandira śodhiyā kaila-yena nija mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śata]]---one hundred; [[synonyms:g:ghaṭa]]---of waterpots; [[synonyms:j:jale]]---by the water; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mandira]]---the temple; [[synonyms:m:mārjana]]---cleansed; [[synonyms:m:mandira]]---the temple; [[synonyms:ś:śodhiyā]]---cleansing; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:n:nija]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---his own mind.
translation: In this way all the rooms were cleansed with a hundred waterpots. After the rooms had been cleansed, the minds of the devotees were as clean as the rooms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.106
description: When the temple was cleansed, it was purified, cool and pleasing, just as if the Lord's own pure mind had appeared.
text:
> nirmala, śītala, snigdha karila mandire
> āpana-hṛdaya yena dharila bāhire
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirmala]]---purified; [[synonyms:ś:śītala]]---cool; [[synonyms:s:snigdha]]---pleasing; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---made; [[synonyms:m:mandire]]---the temple; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]---own heart; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:d:dharila]]---kept; [[synonyms:b:bāhire]]---outside.
translation: When the temple was cleansed, it was purified, cool and pleasing, just as if the Lord's own pure mind had appeared.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.107
description: Since hundreds of men were engaged in bringing water from the lake, there was no place to stand on the banks. Consequently someone began to draw water from a well.
text:
> śata śata jana jala bhare sarovare
> ghāṭe sthāna nāhi, keha kūpe jala bhare
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---hundreds of men; [[synonyms:j:jala]] [[synonyms:b:bhare]]---draw water; [[synonyms:s:sarovare]]---from the lake; [[synonyms:g:ghāṭe]]---on the bank; [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---place; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:k:kūpe]]---from the well; [[synonyms:j:jala]] [[synonyms:b:bhare]]---draws the water.
translation: Since hundreds of men were engaged in bringing water from the lake, there was no place to stand on the banks. Consequently someone began to draw water from a well.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.108
description: Hundreds of devotees brought water in the pots, and hundreds took the empty pots away to fill them up again.
text:
> pūrṇa kumbha lañā āise śata bhakta-gaṇa
> śūnya ghaṭa lañā yāya āra śata jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kumbha]]---a filled waterpot; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---come; [[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---hundreds of devotees; [[synonyms:ś:śūnya]] [[synonyms:g:ghaṭa]]---an empty waterpot; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking back; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---go; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---hundreds of men.
translation: Hundreds of devotees brought water in the pots, and hundreds took the empty pots away to fill them up again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.109
description: With the exception of Nityānanda Prabhu, Advaita Ācārya, Svarūpa Dāmodara, Brahmānanda Bhāratī and Paramānanda Purī, everyone was engaged in filling the waterpots and bringing them there.
text:
> nityānanda, advaita, svarūpa, bhāratī, purī
> iṅhā vinu āra saba āne jala bhari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:i:iṅhā]]---these; [[synonyms:v:vinu]]---except; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---others; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:āne]]---bring; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---water; [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---filling up.
translation: With the exception of Nityānanda Prabhu, Advaita Ācārya, Svarūpa Dāmodara, Brahmānanda Bhāratī and Paramānanda Purī, everyone was engaged in filling the waterpots and bringing them there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.11
description: When the Bhaṭṭācārya received this letter, he became very anxious. He then took the letter and went to the devotees of the Lord.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya patrī dekhi' cintita hañā
> bhakta-gaṇa-pāśa gelā sei patrī lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:patrī]]---the letter; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:c:cintita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming very anxious; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---near; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:p:patrī]]---letter; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking.
translation: When the Bhaṭṭācārya received this letter, he became very anxious. He then took the letter and went to the devotees of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.110
description: Many of the waterpots were broken when people collided with one another, and hundreds of men had to bring new waterpots to fill.
text:
> ghaṭe ghaṭe ṭheki' kata ghaṭa bhāṅgi' gela
> śata śata ghaṭa loka tāhāṅ lañā āila
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:ghaṭe]] [[synonyms:g:ghaṭe]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭheki']]---when there was a collision between one pot and another; [[synonyms:k:kata]]---so many; [[synonyms:g:ghaṭa]]---pots; [[synonyms:b:bhāṅgi']] [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---became broken; [[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:ś:śata]]---hundreds of; [[synonyms:g:ghaṭa]]---pots; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---bringing; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came.
translation: Many of the waterpots were broken when people collided with one another, and hundreds of men had to bring new waterpots to fill.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.111
description: Some people were filling the pots, and others were washing the rooms, but everyone was engaged in chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and Hari.
text:
> jala bhare, ghara dhoya, kare hari-dhvani
> 'kṛṣṇa' 'hari' dhvani vinā āra nāhi śuni
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jala]] [[synonyms:b:bhare]]---they were drawing water; [[synonyms:g:ghara]] [[synonyms:d:dhoya]]---washing the rooms; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---chanting the holy name of Hari; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:hari]]---the holy name of Hari; [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---vibration; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---except; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---anything else; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there was not; [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---hearing.
translation: Some people were filling the pots, and others were washing the rooms, but everyone was engaged in chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and Hari.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.112
description: One person begged for a waterpot by chanting the holy names "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa," and another delivered a pot while chanting "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> 'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa' kahi' kare ghaṭera prārthana
> 'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa' kahi' kare ghaṭa samarpaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---while chanting "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa"; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:g:ghaṭera]]---for the waterpots; [[synonyms:p:prārthana]]---begging; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---chanting; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:g:ghaṭa]]---of the waterpots; [[synonyms:s:samarpaṇa]]---delivery.
translation: One person begged for a waterpot by chanting the holy names "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa," and another delivered a pot while chanting "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.113
description: Whenever anyone had to speak, he did so by uttering the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Consequently, the holy name of Kṛṣṇa became an indication for everyone who wanted something.
text:
> yei yei kahe, sei kahe kṛṣṇa-nāme
> kṛṣṇa-nāma ha-ila saṅketa saba-kāme
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---anyone who was speaking; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---he; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāme]]---by uttering the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---the holy name of Kṛṣṇa became; [[synonyms:s:saṅketa]]---indication; [[synonyms:s:saba]]-[[synonyms:k:kāme]]---for everyone who wanted something.
translation: Whenever anyone had to speak, he did so by uttering the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Consequently, the holy name of Kṛṣṇa became an indication for everyone who wanted something.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.114
description: As Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was vibrating the holy name of Kṛṣṇa in ecstatic love, He Himself was performing the work of hundreds of men.
text:
> premāveśe prabhu kahe 'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa'-nāma
> ekale premāveśe kare śata-janera kāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:e:ekale]]---alone; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ś:śata]]-[[synonyms:j:janera]] [[synonyms:k:kāma]]---the work of hundreds of men.
translation: As Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was vibrating the holy name of Kṛṣṇa in ecstatic love, He Himself was performing the work of hundreds of men.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.115
description: It appeared as though Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were cleansing and washing with a hundred hands. He approached every devotee just to teach him how to work.
text:
> śata-haste karena yena kṣālana-mārjana
> pratijana-pāśe yāi' karāna śikṣana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śata]]-[[synonyms:h:haste]]---with one hundred hands; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---He does; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:k:kṣālana]]-[[synonyms:m:mārjana]]---rinsing and washing; [[synonyms:p:pratijana]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśe]] [[synonyms:y:yāi']]---going to the side of everyone; [[synonyms:k:karāna]] [[synonyms:ś:śikṣaṇa]]---He was teaching them.
translation: It appeared as though Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were cleansing and washing with a hundred hands. He approached every devotee just to teach him how to work.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.116
description: When He saw someone doing nicely, the Lord praised him, but if He saw that someone was not working to His satisfaction, He immediately chastised that person, not bearing him any grudge.
text:
> bhāla karma dekhi' tāre kare prasaṁśana
> mane nā milile kare pavitra bhartsana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]---good; [[synonyms:k:karma]]---work; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---to him; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prasaṁśana]]---praising; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in His mind; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:m:milile]]---being approved; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---He does; [[synonyms:p:pavitra]]---purified, ungrudgingly; [[synonyms:b:bhartsana]]---chastisement.
translation: When He saw someone doing nicely, the Lord praised him, but if He saw that someone was not working to His satisfaction, He immediately chastised that person, not bearing him any grudge.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.117
description: The Lord would say, "You have done well. Please teach this to others so that they may act in the same way."
text:
> tumi bhāla kariyācha, śikhāha anyere
> ei-mata bhāla karma seho yena kare
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]] [[synonyms:k:kariyācha]]---have done well; [[synonyms:ś:śikhāha]] [[synonyms:a:anyere]]---teach others; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]] [[synonyms:k:karma]]---good work; [[synonyms:s:seho]]---he also; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---so that; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs.
translation: The Lord would say, "You have done well. Please teach this to others so that they may act in the same way."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.118
description: As soon as they heard Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu say this, everyone became ashamed. Thus the devotees began to work with great attention.
text:
> e-kathā śuniyā sabe saṅkucita hañā
> bhāla-mate karma kare sabe mana diyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]] [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing these words; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:s:saṅkucita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being ashamed; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---very well; [[synonyms:k:karma]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do work; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:m:mana]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---with attention.
translation: As soon as they heard Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu say this, everyone became ashamed. Thus the devotees began to work with great attention.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.119
description: They washed the Jagamohana area and then the place where food was kept. All other places were also washed.
text:
> tabe prakṣālana kaila śrī-jagamohana
> bhoga-mandira-ādi tabe kaila prakṣālana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:p:prakṣālana]]---washing; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:j:jagamohana]]---in front of the temple; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]-[[synonyms:m:mandira]]---the place where food is offered; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---all such places; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:p:prakṣālana]]---washed.
translation: They washed the Jagamohana area and then the place where food was kept. All other places were also washed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.12
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya met with all the devotees and described the King's wishes. Then he presented the letter to all of them for inspection.
text:
> sabāre miliyā kahila rāja-vivaraṇa
> piche sei patrī sabāre karāila daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---everyone; [[synonyms:m:miliyā]]---meeting; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---said; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---description of the King's desire; [[synonyms:p:piche]]---later; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:patrī]]---that letter; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---unto everyone; [[synonyms:k:karāila]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---showed.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya met with all the devotees and described the King's wishes. Then he presented the letter to all of them for inspection.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.120
description: In this way the meeting place was washed, the entire yard, the raised sitting places, the kitchen and every other room.
text:
> nāṭaśālā dhui' dhuila catvara-prāṅgaṇa
> pākaśālā-ādi kari' karila prakṣālana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nāṭa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śālā]]---the meeting place; [[synonyms:d:dhui']]---washing; [[synonyms:d:dhuila]]---washed; [[synonyms:c:catvara]]-[[synonyms:p:prāṅgaṇa]]---the yard and the raised sitting place; [[synonyms:p:pāka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śālā]]---the kitchen; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and so on; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:p:prakṣālana]]---washed.
translation: In this way the meeting place was washed, the entire yard, the raised sitting places, the kitchen and every other room.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.121
description: Thus all places around the temple were thoroughly washed within and without.
text:
> mandirera catur-dik prakṣālana kaila
> saba antaḥpura bhāla-mate dhoyāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mandirera]]---the temple; [[synonyms:c:caturḥ]]-[[synonyms:d:dik]]---all around; [[synonyms:p:prakṣālana]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---washed; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:a:antaḥpura]]---inside the rooms; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---with great care; [[synonyms:d:dhoyāila]]---washed.
translation: Thus all places around the temple were thoroughly washed within and without.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.122
description: After everything was thoroughly washed, a Vaiṣṇava from Bengal, who was very intelligent and simple, came and poured water on the lotus feet of the Lord.
text:
> hena-kāle gauḍīyā eka subuddhi sarala
> prabhura caraṇa-yuge dila ghaṭa-jala
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:g:gauḍīyā]]---Vaiṣṇava from Bengal; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---very intelligent; [[synonyms:s:sarala]]---simple; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:y:yuge]]---on the lotus feet of the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---poured; [[synonyms:g:ghaṭa]]-[[synonyms:j:jala]]---one potful of water.
translation: After everything was thoroughly washed, a Vaiṣṇava from Bengal, who was very intelligent and simple, came and poured water on the lotus feet of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.123
description: The Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava then took that water and drank it himself. Seeing that, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu felt a little unhappy and was also outwardly angry.
text:
> sei jala lañā āpane pāna kaila
> tāhā dekhi' prabhura mane duḥkha roṣa haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:j:jala]]---that water; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:p:pāna]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---drank; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing that; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:r:roṣa]]---anger; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was.
translation: The Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava then took that water and drank it himself. Seeing that, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu felt a little unhappy and was also outwardly angry.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.124
description: Although the Lord was certainly satisfied with him, He became angry externally in order to establish the etiquette of religious principles.
text:
> yadyapi gosāñi tāre hañāche santoṣa
> dharma-saṁsthāpana lāgi' bāhire mahā-roṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---with him; [[synonyms:h:hañāche]]---became; [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---satisfied; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṁsthāpana]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for establishing the etiquette of religious principles; [[synonyms:b:bāhire]]---externally; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:r:roṣa]]---very angry.
translation: Although the Lord was certainly satisfied with him, He became angry externally in order to establish the etiquette of religious principles.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.125
description: The Lord then called for Svarūpa Dāmodara and told him, "Just see the behavior of your Bengali Vaiṣṇava.
text:
> śikṣā lāgi' svarūpe ḍāki' kahila tāṅhāre
> ei dekha tomāra 'gauḍīyā'ra vyavahāre

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.126
description: "This person from Bengal has washed My feet within the temple of the Personality of Godhead. Not only that, but he has drunk the water himself.

> sei jala āpani lañā pāna kaila

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.127
description: "I now do not know what My destination is because of this offense. Indeed, your Bengali Vaiṣṇava has greatly implicated Me."
text:
> ei aparādhe mora kāhāṅ habe gati
> tomāra 'gauḍīyā' kare eteka phaijati!
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:a:aparādhe]]---by such an offense; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---of Me; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---will be; [[synonyms:g:gati]]---destination; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:g:gauḍīyā]]---your Bengali Vaiṣṇava; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:e:eteka]]---such; [[synonyms:p:phaijati]]---implication.
translation: "I now do not know what My destination is because of this offense. Indeed, your Bengali Vaiṣṇava has greatly implicated Me."
purport: It is significant that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī that the Bengali Vaiṣṇava was "your Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava." This means that all Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas who are followers of the Caitanya cult are subordinate to Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī. The //paramparā// system is very strictly observed by Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's personal secretary was Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī. The next group of devotees was the six Gosvāmīs, then Kavirāja Gosvāmī. It is necessary to observe the //paramparā// system of the Caitanya cult. There are many offenses one can commit while serving the Lord, and these are described in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, Hari-bhakti-vilāsa// and other books. According to the rules and regulations, no one should accept obeisances in the temple of the Lord before the Deity. Nor is it proper for a devotee to offer obeisances and touch the feet of the spiritual master before the Deity. This is considered an offense. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself was personally the Supreme Personality of Godhead; therefore it was not actually offensive to wash His lotus feet in the temple. However, because He was playing the part of an //ācārya,// the Lord considered Himself an ordinary human being. He also wanted to give instructions to ordinary human beings. The point is that even though one plays the part of a spiritual master, he should not accept obeisances or permit a disciple to wash his feet before the Deity. This is a matter of etiquette.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.135
description: Outside the gateway of the temple, all the roads were also cleansed, and no one could tell exactly how this was done.
text:
> ei-mata puradvāra-āge patha yata
> sakala śodhila, tāhā ke varṇibe kata
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:p:pura]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāra]]---of the gateway of the temple; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:p:patha]] [[synonyms:y:yata]]---as many avenues; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:ś:śodhila]]---were cleansed; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:ke]] [[synonyms:v:varṇibe]]---who can describe; [[synonyms:k:kata]]---how much.
translation: Outside the gateway of the temple, all the roads were also cleansed, and no one could tell exactly how this was done.
purport:
In commenting on the cleansing of the Guṇḍicā temple, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, as the world leader, was personally giving instructions on how one should receive Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, within one's cleansed and pacified heart. If one wants to see Kṛṣṇa seated in his heart, he must first cleanse the heart, as prescribed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in His //Śikṣāṣṭaka:ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanam.// In this age, everyone's heart is especially unclean, as confirmed in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam:hṛdy antaḥ-stho hy abhadrāṇi.// To wash away all dirty things accumulated within the heart, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu advised everyone to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra.// The first result will be that the heart is cleansed (//ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanam//). Similarly, //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:2:17|(1.2.17)]] confirms this statement:

> śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
> puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ
> hṛdy antaḥ-stho hy abhadrāṇi
> vidhunoti suhṛt satām

"Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramātmā [Supersoul] in everyone's heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who relishes His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted."

If a devotee at all wants to cleanse his heart, he must chant and hear the glories of the Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa (//śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ//). This is a simple process. Kṛṣṇa Himself will help cleanse the heart because He is already seated there. Kṛṣṇa wants to continue living within the heart, and the Lord wants to give directions, but one has to keep his heart as clean as Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu kept the Guṇḍicā temple. The devotee therefore has to cleanse his heart just as the Lord cleansed the Guṇḍicā temple. In this way one can be pacified and enriched in devotional service. If the heart is filled with straw, grains of sand, weeds or dust (in other words, //anyābhilāṣa-pūrṇa//), one cannot enthrone the Supreme Personality of Godhead there. The heart must be cleansed of all material motives brought about through fruitive work, speculative knowledge, the mystic //yoga// system and so many other forms of so-called meditation. The heart must be cleansed without ulterior motive. As Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī says: //anyābhilāṣitā-śūnyaṁ jñāna-karmādy-anāvṛtam.// In other words, there should not be any external motive. One should not attempt material upliftment, understanding the Supreme by speculative knowledge, fruitive activity, severe austerity and penance, and so on. All these activities are against the natural growth of spontaneous love of Godhead. As soon as these are present within the heart, the heart should be understood to be unclean and therefore unfit to serve as Kṛṣṇa's sitting place. We cannot perceive the Lord's presence in our hearts unless our hearts are cleansed.

A material desire is explained as a desire to enjoy the material world to its fullest extent. In modern language, this is called economic development. An inordinate desire for economic development is considered to be like straws and grains of sand within the heart. If one is overly engaged in material activity, the heart will always remain disturbed. As stated by Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura:

> saṁsāra viṣānale,     divā-niśi hiyā jvale,
> juḍāite nā kainu upāya

In other words, endeavor for material opulence is against the principle of devotional service. Material enjoyment includes activities such as great sacrifices for auspicious activity, charity, austerity, elevation to the higher planetary system, and even living happily within the material world.

Modernized material benefits are like the dust of material contamination. When this dust is agitated by the whirlwind of fruitive activity, it overcomes the heart. Thus the mirror of the heart is covered with dust. There are many desires for performing auspicious and inauspicious activities, but people do not know how life after life they are keeping their hearts unclean. One who cannot give up the desire for fruitive activity is understood to be covered by the dust of material contamination. //Karmīs// generally think that the interaction of fruitive activities can be counteracted by another //karma,// or fruitive activity. This is certainly a mistaken conception. If one is deluded by such a conception, he is cheated by his own activity. Such activities have been compared to an elephant's bathing. An elephant may bathe very thoroughly, but as soon as it comes out of the river, it immediately takes some sand from the land and throws it all over its body. If one suffers due to his past fruitive activities, he cannot counteract his suffering by performing auspicious activities. The sufferings of human society cannot be counteracted by material plans. The only way suffering can be mitigated is by Kṛṣṇa consciousness. When one takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness and engages himself in the devotional service of the Lord-beginning with chanting and hearing the glories of the Lord---the cleansing of the heart begins. When the heart is actually cleansed, one can clearly see the Lord sitting there without any disturbance. In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:9:4:68|(9.4.68)]] the Lord confirms that He sits within the heart of the pure devotee: //sādhavo hṛdayaṁ mahyaṁ sādhūnāṁ hṛdayaṁ tv aham.//

Impersonal speculation, monism (merging into the existence of the Supreme), speculative knowledge, mystic //yoga// and meditation are all compared to grains of sand. They simply cause irritation to the heart. No one can satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead by such activities, nor do we give the Lord a chance to sit in our hearts peacefully. Rather, the Lord is simply disturbed by them. Sometimes //yogīs// and //jñānīs// in the beginning take to the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// as a way to begin their various practices. But when they falsely think that they have attained release from the bondage of material existence, they give up chanting. They do not consider that the ultimate goal is the form of the Lord or the name of the Lord. Such unfortunate creatures are never favored by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for they do not know what devotional service is. Lord Kṛṣṇa describes them in the //Bhagavad-gītā// in this way:

> tān ahaṁ dviṣataḥ krūrān
> saṁsāreṣu narādhamān
> kṣipāmy ajasram aśubhān
> āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu

"Those who are envious and mischievous, who are the lowest among men, I perpetually cast into the ocean of material existence, into various demoniac species of life." [[books:bg:16:19|(Bg. 16.19)]]

By His practical example, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has shown us that all the grains of sand must be picked up thoroughly and thrown outside. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also cleansed the outside of the temple, fearing that the grains of sand would again come within. In this connection Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura explains that even though one may become free from the desire for fruitive activity, sometimes the subtle desire for fruitive activity again comes into being within the heart. One often thinks of conducting business to improve devotional activity. But the contamination is so strong that it may later develop into misunderstanding, described as //kuṭi-nāṭi// (faultfinding) and //pratiṣṭhāśā// (the desire for name and fame and for high position), //jīva-hiṁsā// (envy of other living entities), //niṣiddhācāra// (accepting things forbidden in the //śāstra//), //kāma// (desire for material gain) and //pūjā// (hankering for popularity). The word //kuṭi-nāṭi// means "duplicity." As an example of //pratiṣṭhāśā,// one may attempt to imitate Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura by living in a solitary place. One's real desire may be for name and fame-in other words, one thinks that fools will accept one to be as good as Haridāsa Ṭhākura just because one lives in a solitary place. These are all material desires. A neophyte devotee is certain to be attacked by other material desires as well, namely desires for women and money. In this way the heart is again filled with dirty things and becomes harder and harder, like that of a materialist. Gradually one desires to become a reputed devotee or an //avatāra// (incarnation).

The word //jīva-hiṁsā// (envy of other living entities) actually means stopping the preaching of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Preaching work is described as //paropakāra,// welfare activity for others. Those who are ignorant of the benefits of devotional service must be educated by preaching. If one stops preaching and simply sits down in a solitary place, he is engaging in material activity. If one desires to make a compromise with the Māyāvādīs, he is also engaged in material activity. A devotee should never make compromises with nondevotees. By acting as a professional //guru,// mystic //yogī// or miracle man, one may cheat and bluff the general public and gain fame as a wonderful mystic, but all this is considered to be dust, straw and grains of sand within the heart. In addition, one should follow the regulative principles and not desire illicit sex, gambling, intoxicants or meat.

To give us practical instructions, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu cleansed the temple twice. His second cleansing was more thorough. The idea was to throw away all the stumbling blocks on the path of devotional service. He cleansed the temple with firm conviction, as is evident from His using His own personal garments for cleaning. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to see personally that the temple was thoroughly cleansed to the standard of clean marble. Clean marble gives a cooling effect. Devotional service means attaining peace from all disturbances caused by material contamination. In other words, it is the process by which the mind is cooled. The mind can be peaceful and thoroughly cleansed when one no longer desires anything but devotional service.

Even though all dirty things may be cleansed away, sometimes subtle desires remain in the mind for impersonalism, monism, success and the four principles of religious activity (//dharma, artha, kāma// and //mokṣa//). All these are like spots on clean cloth. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also wanted to cleanse all these away.

By His practical activity, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu informed us how to cleanse our hearts. Once the heart is cleansed, we should invite Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa to sit down, and we should observe the festival by distributing //prasāda// and chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to teach every devotee by His personal behavior. Everyone who spreads the cult of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepts a similar responsibility. The Lord was personally chastising and praising individuals in the course of the cleaning, and those who are engaged as //ācāryas// must learn from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu how to train devotees by personal example. The Lord was very much pleased with those who could cleanse the temple by taking out undesirable things accumulated within. This is called //anartha-nivṛtti,// cleansing the heart of all unwanted things. Thus the cleansing of the Guṇḍicā-mandira was conducted by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to let us know how the heart should be cleansed and soothed to receive Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and enable Him to sit within the heart without disturbance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.136

synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁha]]-[[synonyms:m:mandira]]---the temple of Nṛsiṁhadeva; [[synonyms:b:bhitara]]---inside; [[synonyms:b:bāhira]]---outside; [[synonyms:ś:śodhila]]---cleansed; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇeka]]---for a few moments; [[synonyms:v:viśrāma]]---rest; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---after taking; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:ā:ārambhila]]---began.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also cleansed the Nṛsiṁha temple inside and outside. Finally, He rested a few minutes and then began dancing.
purport: The Nṛsiṁha temple is a nice temple just outside the Guṇḍicā temple. In this temple there is a great festival on the day of Nṛsiṁha-caturdaśī. There is also a Nṛsiṁha temple at Navadvīpa where the same festival is observed, as described by Murāri Gupta in his book //Caitanya-carita.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.137
description: All around Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu all the devotees performed congregational chanting. The Lord, just like a maddened lion, danced in the middle.
text:
> cāri-dike bhakta-gaṇa karena kīrtana
> madhye nṛtya karena prabhu matta-siṁha-sama
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---all around; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---devotees; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---performed; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---congregational chanting; [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in the middle; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:matta]]-[[synonyms:s:siṁha]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---just like a maddened lion.
translation: All around Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu all the devotees performed congregational chanting. The Lord, just like a maddened lion, danced in the middle.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.138
description: As usual, when Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced, there were perspiration, trembling, fading, tears, jubilation and roaring. Indeed, the tears from His eyes washed His body and those before Him.
text:
> sveda, kampa, vaivarṇyāśru pulaka, huṅkāra
> nija-aṅga dhui' āge cale aśru-dhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sveda]]---perspiration; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:v:vaivarṇya]]---fading; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]---jubilation; [[synonyms:h:huṅkāra]]---roaring; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---personal body; [[synonyms:d:dhui']]---washing; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---forward; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---goes; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---a flow of tears.
translation: As usual, when Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced, there were perspiration, trembling, fading, tears, jubilation and roaring. Indeed, the tears from His eyes washed His body and those before Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.139
description: In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu washed the bodies of all the devotees with the tears from His eyes. The tears poured like rains in the month of Śrāvaṇa.
text:
> cāri-dike bhakta-aṅga kaila prakṣālana
> śrāvaṇera megha yena kare variṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---all around; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the bodies of the devotees; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prakṣālana]]---washing; [[synonyms:ś:śrāvaṇera]] [[synonyms:m:megha]]---exactly like a cloud in the month of Śrāvaṇa (July-August); [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:v:variṣaṇa]]---pour.
translation: In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu washed the bodies of all the devotees with the tears from His eyes. The tears poured like rains in the month of Śrāvaṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.14
description: The devotees gave their opinion and said, "The Lord will never meet the King, and if we requested Him to do so, the Lord will surely feel very unhappy."
text:
> sabe kahe,-prabhu tāṅre kabhu nā milibe
> āmi-saba kahi yadi, duḥkha se mānibe
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabekahe]]---everyone said; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:m:milibe]]---would see; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of us; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---say; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:s:se]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mānibe]]---will feel.
translation: The devotees gave their opinion and said, "The Lord will never meet the King, and if we requested Him to do so, the Lord will surely feel very unhappy."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.140
description: The sky was filled with the great and loud chanting of saṅkīrtana, and the earth shook from the jumping and dancing of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> mahā-ucca-saṅkīrtane ākāśa bharila
> prabhura uddaṇḍa-nṛtye bhūmi-kampa haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:u:ucca]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtane]]---by a great and loud performance of chanting; [[synonyms:ā:ākāśa]]---the sky; [[synonyms:b:bharila]]---became filled; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:u:uddaṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:n:nṛtye]]---by dancing and jumping high; [[synonyms:b:bhūmi]]-[[synonyms:k:kampa]]---earthquake; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was.
translation: The sky was filled with the great and loud chanting of saṅkīrtana, and the earth shook from the jumping and dancing of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.141
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu always liked the loud chanting of Svarūpa Dāmodara. Therefore when Svarūpa Dāmodara sang, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced and jumped high in jubilation.
text:
> svarūpera ucca-gāna prabhure sadā bhāya
> ānande uddaṇḍa nṛtya kare gaurarāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpera]]---of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:u:ucca]]-[[synonyms:g:gāna]]---loud singing; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sadā]] [[synonyms:b:bhāya]]---always very pleasing; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in jubilation; [[synonyms:u:uddaṇḍa]] [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---jumping high and dancing; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:g:gaurarāya]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu always liked the loud chanting of Svarūpa Dāmodara. Therefore when Svarūpa Dāmodara sang, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced and jumped high in jubilation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.142
description: The Lord thus chanted and danced for some time. Finally, understanding the circumstances, He stopped.
text:
> ei-mata kata-kṣaṇa nṛtya ye kariyā
> viśrāma karilā prabhu samaya bujhiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:k:kata]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇa]]---for some time; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---after performing; [[synonyms:v:viśrāma]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---rested; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:samaya]] [[synonyms:b:bujhiyā]]---understanding the time.
translation: The Lord thus chanted and danced for some time. Finally, understanding the circumstances, He stopped.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.143
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then ordered Śrī Gopāla, the son of Advaita Ācārya, to dance.
text:
> ācārya-gosāñira putra śrī-gopāla-nāma
> nṛtya karite tāṅre ājñā dila gauradhāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Śrī Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:putra]]---son; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named Śrī Gopāla; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to dance; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:g:gauradhāma]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then ordered Śrī Gopāla, the son of Advaita Ācārya, to dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.144
description: While dancing in ecstatic love, Śrī Gopāla fainted and fell to the ground unconscious.
text:
> premāveśe nṛtya kari' ha-ilā mūrcchite
> acetana hañā teṅha paḍilā bhūmite
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---dancing; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]] [[synonyms:m:mūrcchite]]---fainted; [[synonyms:a:acetana]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being unconscious; [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---he; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell; [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]]---on the ground.
translation: While dancing in ecstatic love, Śrī Gopāla fainted and fell to the ground unconscious.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.145
description: When Śrī Gopāla fainted, Advaita Ācārya hastily took him upon His lap. Seeing that he was not breathing, He became very much agitated.
text:
> āste-vyaste ācārya tāṅre kaila kole
> śvāsa-rahita dekhi' ācārya hailā vikale
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āste]]-[[synonyms:v:vyaste]]---with great haste; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---took; [[synonyms:k:kole]]---on His lap; [[synonyms:ś:śvāsa]]-[[synonyms:r:rahita]]---without breathing; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vikale]]---agitated.
translation: When Śrī Gopāla fainted, Advaita Ācārya hastily took him upon His lap. Seeing that he was not breathing, He became very much agitated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.146
description: Advaita Ācārya and others began to chant the holy name of Lord Nṛsiṁha and sprinkle water. The roaring of the chant was so great that it seemed to shake the entire universe.
text:
> nṛsiṁhera mantra paḍi' māre jala-chāṅṭi
> huṅkārera śabde brahmāṇḍa yāya phāṭi'
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁhera]] [[synonyms:m:mantra]]---prayers to Nṛsiṁhadeva; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---chanting; [[synonyms:m:māre]]---throws; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:c:chāṅṭi]]---sprinkling of water; [[synonyms:h:huṅkārera]] [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the sound of roaring; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]---the whole universe; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:p:phāṭi']]---cracking.
translation: Advaita Ācārya and others began to chant the holy name of Lord Nṛsiṁha and sprinkle water. The roaring of the chant was so great that it seemed to shake the entire universe.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.147
description: When the boy did not regain consciousness after some time, Advaita Ācārya and the other devotees began to cry.
text:
> aneka karila, tabu nā haya cetana
> ācārya kāndena, kānde saba bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aneka]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---much endeavor was done; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there was not; [[synonyms:c:cetana]]---consciousness; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:k:kāndena]]---Advaita Ācārya began to cry; [[synonyms:k:kānde]]---cried; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the other devotees.
translation: When the boy did not regain consciousness after some time, Advaita Ācārya and the other devotees began to cry.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.148
description: Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu placed His hand on the chest of Śrī Gopāla and said loudly, "Gopāla, stand up."
text:
> tabe mahāprabhu tāṅra buke hasta dila
> 'uṭhaha gopāla' bali' uccaiḥsvare kahila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:b:buke]]---on his chest; [[synonyms:h:hasta]]---hand; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---placed; [[synonyms:u:uṭhaha]] [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---stand up, Gopāla; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying; [[synonyms:u:uccaiḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:svare]]---very loudly; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---said.
translation: Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu placed His hand on the chest of Śrī Gopāla and said loudly, "Gopāla, stand up."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.149
description: As soon as Gopāla heard the voice of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he immediately came to his senses. All the devotees then began to dance, chanting the holy name of Hari.
text:
> śunitei gopālera ha-ila cetana
> 'hari' bali' nṛtya kare sarva-bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śunitei]]---upon hearing; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of Śrī Gopāla; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:c:cetana]]---consciousness; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---chanting the holy name of Hari; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---danced; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees.
translation: As soon as Gopāla heard the voice of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he immediately came to his senses. All the devotees then began to dance, chanting the holy name of Hari.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.15
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then said, "We shall go once again to the Lord, but we shall not request Him to meet the King. Rather, we shall simply describe the good behavior of the King."
text:
> sārvabhauma kahe,-sabe cala' eka-bāra
> milite nā kahiba, kahiba rāja-vyavahāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhaumakahe]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:c:cala']]---let all of us go; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---once; [[synonyms:m:milite]]---to meet; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kahiba]]---we shall not request; [[synonyms:k:kahiba]]---we shall simply describe; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:v:vyavahāra]]---the behavior of the King.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then said, "We shall go once again to the Lord, but we shall not request Him to meet the King. Rather, we shall simply describe the good behavior of the King."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.150
description: This incident has been described in detail by Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura. Therefore I have described it only in brief.
text:
> ei līlā varṇiyāchena dāsa vṛndāvana
> ataeva saṅkṣepa kari' kariluṅ varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---this pastime; [[synonyms:v:varṇiyāchena]]---has described; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]] [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:s:saṅkṣepa]]---briefly; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:k:kariluṅ]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---I have described.
translation: This incident has been described in detail by Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura. Therefore I have described it only in brief.
purport: This is a matter of etiquette. If a previous //ācārya// has already written about something, there is no need to repeat it for personal sense gratification or to outdo the previous //ācārya.// Unless there is some definite improvement, one should not repeat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.151
description: After taking rest, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all the devotees departed to take their baths.
text:
> tabe mahāprabhu kṣaṇeka viśrāma kariyā
> snāna karibāre gelā bhakta-gaṇa lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇeka]]---for some time; [[synonyms:v:viśrāma]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---taking rest; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:karibāre]]---for bathing; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking all the devotees.
translation: After taking rest, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all the devotees departed to take their baths.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.152
description: After bathing, the Lord stood on the bank of the lake and put on dry garments. After offering obeisances to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, whose temple was nearby, the Lord entered a garden.
text:
> tīre uṭhi' parena prabhu śuṣka vasana
> nṛsiṁha-deve namaskari' gelā upavana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tīre]] [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---getting on the bank; [[synonyms:p:parena]]---puts on; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śuṣka]] [[synonyms:v:vasana]]---dry garments; [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁha]]-[[synonyms:d:deve]]---unto Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva; [[synonyms:n:namaskari']]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:g:gelā]] [[synonyms:u:upavana]]---entered a garden.
translation: After bathing, the Lord stood on the bank of the lake and put on dry garments. After offering obeisances to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, whose temple was nearby, the Lord entered a garden.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.153
description: In the garden, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat down with the other devotees. Vāṇīnātha Rāya then came and brought all kinds of mahā-prasāda.
text:
> udyāne vasilā prabhu bhakta-gaṇa lañā
> tabe vāṇīnātha āilā mahā-prasāda lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:udyāne]]---in the garden; [[synonyms:v:vasilā]]---sat down; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---with the devotees; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:v:vāṇīnātha]]---Vāṇīnātha Rāya; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---bringing all kinds of //mahā-prasāda.//
translation: In the garden, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat down with the other devotees. Vāṇīnātha Rāya then came and brought all kinds of mahā-prasāda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.154-155
description: Kāśī Miśra and Tulasī, the superintendent of the temple, brought as much prasāda as five hundred men could eat. Seeing the large quantity of prasāda, which consisted of rice, cakes, sweet rice and a variety of vegetables, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very much satisfied.
text:
> kāśī-miśra, tulasī-paḍichā-dui jana
> pañca-śata loka yata karaye bhojana
> tata anna-piṭhā-pānā saba pāṭhāila
> dekhi' mahāprabhura mane santoṣa ha-ila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāśī]]-[[synonyms:m:miśra]]---Kāśī Miśra; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]-[[synonyms:p:paḍichā]]---Tulasī, the superintendent of the temple; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---five hundred men; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---as much; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eat; [[synonyms:t:tata]]---so; [[synonyms:a:anna]]-[[synonyms:p:piṭhā]]-[[synonyms:p:pānā]]---rice, cakes and sweet rice; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāila]]---sent; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---satisfaction; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was.
translation: Kāśī Miśra and Tulasī, the superintendent of the temple, brought as much prasāda as five hundred men could eat. Seeing the large quantity of prasāda, which consisted of rice, cakes, sweet rice and a variety of vegetables, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very much satisfied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.156
description: Among the devotees present with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were Paramānanda Purī, Brahmānanda Bhāratī, Advaita Ācārya and Nityānanda Prabhu.
text:
> purī-gosāñi, mahāprabhu, bhāratī brahmānanda
> advaita-ācārya, āra prabhu-nityānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]] [[synonyms:b:brahmānanda]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Nityānanda Prabhu.
translation: Among the devotees present with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were Paramānanda Purī, Brahmānanda Bhāratī, Advaita Ācārya and Nityānanda Prabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.157
description: Ācāryaratna, Ācāryanidhi, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Śaṅkara, Nandanācārya, Rāghava Paṇḍita and Vakreśvara were also present.
text:
> ācāryaratna, ācāryanidhi, śrīvāsa, gadādhara
> śaṅkara, nandanācārya, āra rāghava, vakreśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryaratna]]---Candraśekhara; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryanidhi]]---Ācāryanidhi; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]---Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:g:gadādhara]]---Gadādhara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:ś:śaṅkara]]---Śaṅkara; [[synonyms:n:nandana]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Nandanācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:r:rāghava]]---Rāghava Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:v:vakreśvara]]---Vakreśvara.
translation: Ācāryaratna, Ācāryanidhi, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Śaṅkara, Nandanācārya, Rāghava Paṇḍita and Vakreśvara were also present.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.158
description: Receiving the permission of the Lord, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya sat down. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all His devotees sat on raised wooden seats.
text:
> prabhu-ājñā pāñā vaise āpane sārvabhauma
> piṇḍāra upare prabhu vaise lañā bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---the order of the Lord; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:v:vaise]]---sits down; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:piṇḍāra]] [[synonyms:u:upare]]---on raised platforms; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vaise]]---sits; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---along with; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees.
translation: Receiving the permission of the Lord, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya sat down. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all His devotees sat on raised wooden seats.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.159
description: In this way all the devotees sat down to take their lunch in consecutive lines, one beside the other.
text:
> tāra tale, tāra tale kari' anukrama
> udyāna bhari' vaise bhakta karite bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:t:tale]]---below them; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:t:tale]]---below them; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---in this way; [[synonyms:a:anukrama]]---consecutively; [[synonyms:u:udyāna]] [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---filling the entire garden; [[synonyms:v:vaise]]---sit; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---to take lunch.
translation: In this way all the devotees sat down to take their lunch in consecutive lines, one beside the other.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.16
description: Having thus reached a decision, they all went to the place of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. There, although ready to speak, they could not even utter a word.
text:
> eta bali' sabe gelā mahāprabhura sthāne
> kahite unmukha sabe, nā kahe vacane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---deciding like this; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the place; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:u:unmukha]]---ready; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---do not; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---say; [[synonyms:v:vacane]]---any word.
translation: Having thus reached a decision, they all went to the place of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. There, although ready to speak, they could not even utter a word.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.160
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was repeatedly calling, "Haridāsa, Haridāsa," and at that time Haridāsa, standing at a distance, spoke as follows.
text:
> 'haridāsa' bali' prabhu ḍāke ghane ghana
> dūre rahi' haridāsa kare nivedana
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---calling Haridāsa; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍāke]]---calls; [[synonyms:g:ghane]] [[synonyms:g:ghana]]---repeatedly; [[synonyms:d:dūre]] [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---standing at a distance; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Ṭhākura Haridāsa; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---submitted.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was repeatedly calling, "Haridāsa, Haridāsa," and at that time Haridāsa, standing at a distance, spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.161
description: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "Let Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu take His lunch with the devotees. Since I am abominable, I cannot sit down among you.
text:
> bhakta-saṅge prabhu karuna prasāda aṅgīkāra
> e-saṅge vasite yogya nahi muñi chāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---let Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sit down with the devotees; [[synonyms:k:karuna]]---let Him do; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---of remnants of food; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---accepting; [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with this batch; [[synonyms:v:vasite]]---to sit down; [[synonyms:y:yogya]]---befitting; [[synonyms:n:nahi]]---am not; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:c:chāra]]---most abominable.
translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "Let Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu take His lunch with the devotees. Since I am abominable, I cannot sit down among you.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.162
description: "Govinda will give me prasāda later, outside the door." Understanding his mind, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not call him again.
text:
> pāche more prasāda govinda dibe bahirdvāre
> mana jāni' prabhu punaḥ nā balila tāṅre
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---at last; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto me; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---remnants of food; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---the personal servant of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dibe]]---will deliver; [[synonyms:b:bahir]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---outside the door; [[synonyms:m:mana]] [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---understanding the mind; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:b:balila]]---called; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him.
translation: "Govinda will give me prasāda later, outside the door." Understanding his mind, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not call him again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.163-164
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Jagadānanda, Dāmodara Paṇḍita, Kāśīśvara, Gopīnātha, Vāṇīnātha and Śaṅkara distributed prasāda, and the devotees chanted the holy names at intervals.
text:
> svarūpa-gosāñi, jagadānanda, dāmodara
> kāśīśvara, gopīnātha, vāṇīnātha, śaṅkara
>
> pariveśana kare tāhāṅ ei sāta-jana
> madhye madhye hari-dhvani kare bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:j:jagadānanda]]---Jagadānanda; [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Dāmodara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:k:kāśīśvara]]---Kāśīśvara; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha,]] [[synonyms:v:vāṇīnātha,]] [[synonyms:ś:śaṅkara]]---Gopīnātha, Vāṇīnātha and Śaṅkara; [[synonyms:p:pariveśana]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---distribute; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:s:sāta]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---seven persons; [[synonyms:m:madhye]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---at intervals; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---resounding of the holy name of Hari; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Jagadānanda, Dāmodara Paṇḍita, Kāśīśvara, Gopīnātha, Vāṇīnātha and Śaṅkara distributed prasāda, and the devotees chanted the holy names at intervals.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.165
description: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa had previously taken His lunch in the forest, and that very pastime was remembered by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> pulina-bhojana kṛṣṇa pūrve yaiche kaila
> sei līlā mahāprabhura mane smṛti haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pulina]]---in the forest; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eating; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---formerly; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the same pastime; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:s:smṛti]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was remembrance.
translation: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa had previously taken His lunch in the forest, and that very pastime was remembered by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.166
description: Just by remembering the pastimes of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was agitated by ecstatic love. But considering the time and circumstance, He remained somewhat patient.
text:
> yadyapi premāveśe prabhu hailā asthira
> samaya bujhiyā prabhu hailā kichu dhīra
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:a:asthira]]---agitated; [[synonyms:s:samaya]] [[synonyms:b:bujhiyā]]---understanding the time and circumstances; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---somewhat; [[synonyms:d:dhīra]]---patient.
translation: Just by remembering the pastimes of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was agitated by ecstatic love. But considering the time and circumstance, He remained somewhat patient.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.167
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "You can give Me the ordinary vegetable known as lāphrā-vyañjana, and you may deliver to all the devotees better preparations like cakes, sweet rice and amṛta-guṭikā."
text:
> prabhu kahe,-more deha' lāphrā-vyañjane
> piṭhā-pānā, amṛta-guṭikā deha' bhakta-gaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:d:deha']]---give; [[synonyms:l:lāphrā]]-[[synonyms:v:vyañjane]]---ordinary vegetable; [[synonyms:p:piṭhā]]-[[synonyms:p:pānā]]---cakes and sweet rice; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:g:guṭikā]]---and the preparation named //amṛta-guṭikā//; [[synonyms:d:deha']]---deliver; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---to the devotees.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "You can give Me the ordinary vegetable known as lāphrā-vyañjana, and you may deliver to all the devotees better preparations like cakes, sweet rice and amṛta-guṭikā."
purport: //Lāphrā-vyañjana// is a combination of several green vegetables all mixed together. It is often mixed with rice and delivered to poor men. //Amṛta-guṭikā// is a preparation of thick //purī// mixed with condensed milk. It is also known as //amṛta-rasāvalī.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.168
description: Since Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is omniscient, He knew what type of preparation each person liked. He therefore had Svarūpa Dāmodara deliver these preparations to their full satisfaction.
text:
> sarvajña prabhu jānena yāṅre yei bhāya
> tāṅre tāṅre sei deoyāya svarūpa-dvārāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:j:jña]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the omniscient Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jānena]]---knows; [[synonyms:y:yāṅre]]---to whom; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:b:bhāya]]---appeals; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]] [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto each person; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:d:deoyāya]]---orders to administer; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:d:dvārāya]]---by Svarūpa Dāmodara.
translation: Since Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is omniscient, He knew what type of preparation each person liked. He therefore had Svarūpa Dāmodara deliver these preparations to their full satisfaction.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.169
description: Jagadānanda went to distribute prasāda, and suddenly he placed all the first-class preparations on the plate of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> jagadānanda beḍāya pariveśana karite
> prabhura pāte bhāla-dravya dena ācambite
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagadānanda]]---Jagadānanda; [[synonyms:b:beḍāya]]---walks; [[synonyms:p:pariveśana]]---distribution of //prasāda//; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to do; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:p:pāte]]---on the plate of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]-[[synonyms:d:dravya]]---the first-class preparations; [[synonyms:d:dena]]---puts; [[synonyms:ā:ācambite]]---suddenly.
translation: Jagadānanda went to distribute prasāda, and suddenly he placed all the first-class preparations on the plate of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.17
description: After they arrived at Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's place, the Lord, seeing them, said, "What have you all come here to say? I see that you want to say something, but you do not speak. What is the reason?"
text:
> prabhu kahe,-ki kahite sabāra āgamana
> dekhiye kahite cāha,-nā kaha, ki kāraṇa?
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of you; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---there is the presence here; [[synonyms:d:dekhiye]]---I see; [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:c:cāha]]---you want to speak; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---but do not speak; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---what is the reason.
translation: After they arrived at Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's place, the Lord, seeing them, said, "What have you all come here to say? I see that you want to say something, but you do not speak. What is the reason?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.170
description: When such nice prasāda was put on the plate of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord was outwardly very angry. Nonetheless, when the preparations were placed on His plate sometimes by tricks and sometimes by force, the Lord was satisfied.
text:
> yadyapi dile prabhu tāṅre karena roṣa
> bale-chale tabu dena, dile se santoṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:d:dile]]---by such deliverance; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:r:roṣa]]---anger; [[synonyms:b:bale]]-[[synonyms:c:chale]]---somehow or other (sometimes by tricks, sometimes by force); [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:d:dena]]---delivers; [[synonyms:d:dile]]---when he delivers; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very much pleased.
translation: When such nice prasāda was put on the plate of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord was outwardly very angry. Nonetheless, when the preparations were placed on His plate sometimes by tricks and sometimes by force, the Lord was satisfied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.171
description: When the food was thus delivered, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu looked at it for some time. Being afraid of Jagadānanda, He finally ate something.
text:
> punarapi sei dravya kare nirīkṣaṇa
> tāṅra bhaye prabhu kichu karena bhakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:dravya]]---that very thing; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:n:nirīkṣaṇa]]---sees carefully; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---out of fear of Jagadānanda; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:b:bhakṣaṇa]]---eating.
translation: When the food was thus delivered, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu looked at it for some time. Being afraid of Jagadānanda, He finally ate something.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.172
description: The Lord knew that if He did not eat the food offered by Jagadānanda, Jagadānanda would certainly fast. Being afraid of this, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ate some of the prasāda he offered.
text:
> nā khāile jagadānanda karibe upavāsa
> tāṅra āge kichu khā'na-mane ai trāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:khāile]]---if He did not eat; [[synonyms:j:jagadānanda]]---Jagadānanda; [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---will observe; [[synonyms:u:upavāsa]]---fasting; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---before him; [[synonyms:k:kichu]] [[synonyms:k:khā'na]]---eats something; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---within the mind; [[synonyms:a:ai]]---that; [[synonyms:t:trāsa]]---fear.
translation: The Lord knew that if He did not eat the food offered by Jagadānanda, Jagadānanda would certainly fast. Being afraid of this, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ate some of the prasāda he offered.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.173
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī then brought some excellent sweetmeats and, standing before the Lord, offered them to Him.
text:
> svarūpa-gosāñi bhāla miṣṭa-prasāda lañā
> prabhuke nivedana kare āge dāṇḍāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]---first-class; [[synonyms:m:miṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---sweetmeats; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---unto Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nivedana]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---offered; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of Him; [[synonyms:d:dāṇḍāñā]]---standing.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī then brought some excellent sweetmeats and, standing before the Lord, offered them to Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.174
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī then said, "Just take a little of this mahā-prasāda, and see how it is that Lord Jagannātha has accepted it."
text:
> ei mahā-prasāda alpa karaha āsvādana
> dekha, jagannātha kaiche karyāchena bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---this //mahā-prasāda//; [[synonyms:a:alpa]]---a little; [[synonyms:k:karahaāsvādana]]---You must taste; [[synonyms:d:dekha]]---just see; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:k:kaiche]]---how; [[synonyms:k:karyāchena]]---has done; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eating.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī then said, "Just take a little of this mahā-prasāda, and see how it is that Lord Jagannātha has accepted it."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.175
description: Upon saying this, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī placed some food before the Lord, and the Lord, out of affection, ate it.
text:
> eta bali' āge kichu kare samarpaṇa
> tāṅra snehe prabhu kichu karena bhojana

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.180
description: After serving the Bhaṭṭācārya with first-class prasāda, Gopīnātha Ācārya said, "Just consider what the Bhaṭṭācārya's previous mundane behavior was! Just consider how at present he is enjoying transcendental bliss!"
text:
> kāhāṅ bhaṭṭācāryera pūrva jaḍa-vyavahāra
> kāhāṅ ei paramānanda,-karaha vicāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]---previous; [[synonyms:j:jaḍa]]-[[synonyms:v:vyavahāra]]---material behavior; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---just try to consider.
translation: After serving the Bhaṭṭācārya with first-class prasāda, Gopīnātha Ācārya said, "Just consider what the Bhaṭṭācārya's previous mundane behavior was! Just consider how at present he is enjoying transcendental bliss!"
purport: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was previously a //smārta-brāhmaṇa//---that is, one who strictly follows the Vedic principles on the mundane platform. On the mundane platform one cannot believe that //prasāda// is transcendental, that Govinda is the original form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, or that a Vaiṣṇava is a liberated person. These transcendental considerations are out of the ordinary Vedic scholar's jurisdiction. Most Vedic scholars are called Vedāntists. These so-called followers of Vedānta philosophy consider the Absolute Truth to be impersonal. They also believe that a person born in a particular caste cannot change his caste until he dies and takes rebirth. The //smārta-brāhmaṇas// also reject the fact that //mahā-prasāda// (food offered to the Deity) is transcendental and materially uncontaminated. Originally, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was subjected to all the rules and regulations of the Vedic principles on the mundane platform. Now Gopīnātha Ācārya pointed out how Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya had been converted by the causeless mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Being converted, Sārvabhauma partook of //prasāda// with the Vaiṣṇavas. Indeed, he sat by the side of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "I was simply a less intelligent logician. But by your grace I have received this opulence of perfection.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 12.184
description: "Whereas I once associated with the disciples of logic, all nondevotees, I am now merged in the waves of the nectarean ocean of the association of devotees."
text:
> kāhāṅ bahirmukha tārkika-śiṣyagaṇa-saṅge
> kāhāṅ ei saṅga-sudhā-samudra-taraṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---whereas; [[synonyms:b:bahirḥ]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---nondevotees; [[synonyms:t:tārkika]]---of logic; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---disciples; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---now; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---association; [[synonyms:s:sudhā]]---of nectar; [[synonyms:s:samudra]]---of the ocean; [[synonyms:t:taraṅge]]---in the waves.
translation: "Whereas I once associated with the disciples of logic, all nondevotees, I am now merged in the waves of the nectarean ocean of the association of devotees."
purport:
As Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura explains, the word //bahirmukha// refers to a person who is very busy tasting material enjoyment. Such a person always poses himself as an enjoyer of the external energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Being attracted by external opulence, the nondevotee always forgets his intimate relationship with Kṛṣṇa. Such a person does not like the idea of becoming Kṛṣṇa conscious. This is explained by Śrīla Prahlāda Mahārāja in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:7:5:30|(7.5.30-31)]]:

> matir na kṛṣṇe parataḥ svato vā
> mitho 'bhipadyeta gṛha-vratānām
> adānta-gobhir viśatāṁ tamisraṁ
> punaḥ punaś carvita-carvaṇānām
>
> na te viduḥ svārtha-gatiṁ hi viṣṇuṁ
> durāśayā ye bahir-artha-māninaḥ
> andhā yathāndhair upanīyamānās
> te 'pīśa-tantryām uru-dāmni baddhāḥ

Materialists who are overly attracted to the material body, material world and material enjoyment, who cannot control their material senses, are carried to the darkest regions of material existence. Such people cannot become Kṛṣṇa conscious, either by themselves or by congregational effort. Such people do not understand that the goal of life for a human being is to understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu. A human life is especially meant for this purpose, and one has to go through all kinds of penances and austerities and set aside the propensity for sense gratification. Materialists always remain blind because they are always guided by blind rascals. A materialistic person considers himself free to act as he likes. He does not know that he is rigidly controlled by the stringent laws of nature, nor does he know that he has to transmigrate from one body to another and perpetually rot in material existence. Such rascals and foolish people are lured by the prayers of their foolish leaders for sense gratification, and they cannot understand what is meant by Kṛṣṇa consciousness. The material world exists outside the spiritual sky, and a foolish materialist cannot estimate the extent of this material sky. What, then, can he know of the spiritual sky? Materialists simply believe their imperfect senses and do not take instructions from the revealed scriptures. According to Vedic civilization, one has to see through the authority of the revealed scriptures. //Śāstra-cakṣuḥ:// one should see everything through the medium of the Vedic literature. In this way, one can distinguish between the spiritual world and material world. Those who ignore such instructions cannot be convinced of the existence of the spiritual world. Because they have forgotten their spiritual identity, such materialists take this material world as the all in all. They are therefore called //bahirmukha.//
