title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.136
description: "The gopīs spoke thus: 'Dear Lord, whose navel is just like a lotus flower, Your lotus feet are the only shelter for those who have fallen into the deep well of material existence. Your feet are worshiped and meditated upon by great mystic yogīs and highly learned philosophers. We wish that these lotus feet may also be awakened within our hearts, although we are only ordinary persons engaged in household affairs.' "
text:
> āhuś ca te nalina-nābha padāravindaṁ
> yogeśvarair hṛdi vicintyam agādha-bodhaiḥ
> saṁsāra-kūpa-patitottaraṇāvalambaṁ
> gehaṁ juṣām api manasy udiyāt sadā naḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āhuḥ]]---the //gopīs// said; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:t:te]]---Your; [[synonyms:n:nalina]]-[[synonyms:n:nābha]]---O Lord, whose navel is just like a lotus flower; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:a:aravindam]]---lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśvaraiḥ]]---by great mystic yogīs; [[synonyms:h:hṛdi]]---within the heart; [[synonyms:v:vicintyam]]---to be meditated upon; [[synonyms:a:agādha]]-[[synonyms:b:bodhaiḥ]]---who are highly learned philosophers; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]-[[synonyms:k:kūpa]]---in the dark well of material existence; [[synonyms:p:patita]]---of those fallen; [[synonyms:u:uttaraṇa]]---for deliverance; [[synonyms:a:avalambam]]---the only shelter; [[synonyms:g:geham]]---in family affairs; [[synonyms:j:juṣām]]---of those engaged; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:m:manasi]]---in the minds; [[synonyms:u:udiyāt]]---let be awakened; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---our.
translation: "The gopīs spoke thus: 'Dear Lord, whose navel is just like a lotus flower, Your lotus feet are the only shelter for those who have fallen into the deep well of material existence. Your feet are worshiped and meditated upon by great mystic yogīs and highly learned philosophers. We wish that these lotus feet may also be awakened within our hearts, although we are only ordinary persons engaged in household affairs.' "
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.82.48). The //gopīs// were never interested in //karma-yoga, jñāna-yoga,// or //dhyāna-yoga.// They were simply interested in //bhakti-yoga.// Unless they were forced, they never liked to meditate on the lotus feet of the Lord. Rather, they preferred to take the lotus feet of the Lord and place them on their breasts. Sometimes they regretted that their breasts were so hard, fearing that Kṛṣṇa might not be very pleased to keep His soft lotus feet there. When those lotus feet were pricked by the grains of sand in the Vṛndāvana pasturing ground, the //gopīs// were pained and began to cry. The //gopīs// wanted to keep Kṛṣṇa at home always, and in this way their minds were absorbed in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Such pure Kṛṣṇa consciousness can arise only in Vṛndāvana. Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to explain His own mind, which was saturated in the ecstasy of the //gopīs.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.137
description: Speaking in the mood of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, " 'For most people, the mind and heart are one, but because My mind is never separated from Vṛndāvana, I consider My mind and Vṛndāvana to be one. My mind is already Vṛndāvana, and since You like Vṛndāvana, will You please place Your lotus feet there? I would deem that Your full mercy.
text:
> anyera hṛda ya-mana, mora mana-vṛndāvana,
> 'mane' 'vane' eka kari' jāni
> tāhāṅ tomāra pada-dvaya, karāha yadi udaya,
> tabe tomāra pūrṇa kṛpā māni
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anyera]]---of others; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]---consciousness; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---My mind; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana consciousness; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---with the mind; [[synonyms:v:vane]]---with Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---as one and the same; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I know; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there, at Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:d:dvaya]]---two lotus feet; [[synonyms:k:karāha]]---You do; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:u:udaya]]---appearance; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---complete; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:m:māni]]---I accept.
translation: Speaking in the mood of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, " 'For most people, the mind and heart are one, but because My mind is never separated from Vṛndāvana, I consider My mind and Vṛndāvana to be one. My mind is already Vṛndāvana, and since You like Vṛndāvana, will You please place Your lotus feet there? I would deem that Your full mercy.
purport: Only when the mind is free from designations can one desire the association of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The mind must have some occupation. If a person is to be free of material things, his mind cannot be vacant; there must be subject matters for thinking, feeling and willing. Unless one's mind is filled with thoughts of Kṛṣṇa, feelings for Kṛṣṇa and a desire to serve Kṛṣṇa, the mind will be filled with material activities. Those who have given up all material activities and have ceased thinking of them should always retain the ambition to think of Kṛṣṇa. Without Kṛṣṇa, one cannot live, just as a person cannot live without some enjoyment for his mind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.138
description: " 'My dear Lord, kindly hear My true submission. My home is Vṛndāvana, and I wish Your association there. But if I do not get it, then it will be very difficult for Me to keep My life.
text:
> prāṇa-nātha, śuna mora satya nivedana
> vraja-āmāra sadana, tāhāṅ tomāra saṅgama,
> nā pāile nā rahe jīvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nātha]]---O My Lord, master of My life; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:s:satya]]---true; [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---submission; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]---Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:s:sadana]]---place; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:s:saṅgama]]---association; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāile]]---if I do not get; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---does remain; [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---life.
translation: “ 'My dear Lord, kindly hear My true submission. My home is Vṛndāvana, and I wish Your association there. But if I do not get it, then it will be very difficult for Me to keep My life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.139
description: " 'My dear Kṛṣṇa, formerly, when You were staying in Mathurā, You sent Uddhava to teach Me speculative knowledge and mystic yoga. Now You Yourself are speaking the same thing, but My mind doesn't accept it. There is no place in My mind for jñāna-yoga or dhyāna-yoga. Although You know Me very well, You are still instructing Me in jñāna-yoga and dhyāna-yoga. It is not right for You to do so.' "
text:
> pūrve uddhava-dvāre, ebe sākṣāt āmāre,
> yoga-jñāne kahilā upāya
> tumi-vidagdha, kṛpāmaya, jānaha āmāra hṛdaya,
> more aiche kahite nā yuyāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---previously; [[synonyms:u:uddhava]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---through Uddhava; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:ā:āmāre]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]---mystic yogic meditation; [[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---philosophical speculation; [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---You have said; [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---the means; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:v:vidagdha]]---very humorous; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---mercifu1; [[synonyms:j:jānaha]]---You know; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]---mind; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yuyāya]]---is not at all befitting.
translation: “ 'My dear Kṛṣṇa, formerly, when You were staying in Mathurā, You sent Uddhava to teach Me speculative knowledge and mystic yoga. Now You Yourself are speaking the same thing, but My mind doesn't accept it. There is no place in My mind for jñāna-yoga or dhyāna-yoga. Although You know Me very well, You are still instructing Me in jñāna-yoga and dhyāna-yoga. It is not right for You to do so.' "
purport: The process of mystic //yoga,// the speculative method for searching out the Supreme Absolute Truth, does not appeal to one who is always absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa. A devotee is not at all interested in speculative activities. Instead of cultivating speculative knowledge or practicing mystic //yoga,// a devotee should worship the Deity in the temple and continuously engage in the Lord's service. Temple Deity worship is realized by the devotees to be the same as direct service to the Lord. The Deity is known as //arcā-vigraha// or //arcā-avatāra,// an incarnation of the Supreme Lord in the form of a material manifestation (brass, stone or wood). Ultimately there is no difference between Kṛṣṇa manifest in matter or Kṛṣṇa manifest in spirit because both are His energies. For Kṛṣṇa, there is no distinction between matter and spirit. His manifestation in material form, therefore, is as good as His original form, //sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha.// A devotee constantly engaged in Deity worship according to the rules and regulations laid down in the //śāstras// and given by the spiritual master realizes gradually that he is in direct contact with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Thus he loses all interest in so-called meditation, //yoga// practice and mental speculation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.14
description: While the Lord was transported from the throne to the car, tumultuous sounds were made on various musical instruments. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was chanting "Maṇimā Maṇimā," but He could not be heard.
text:
> mahāprabhu 'maṇimā' 'maṇimā' kare dhvani
> nānā-vādya-kolāhale kichui nā śuni
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:maṇimā]]---Maṇimā; [[synonyms:m:maṇimā]]---Maṇimā; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---makes; [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---the sound; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:v:vādya]]---of musical instruments; [[synonyms:k:kolāhale]]---by the tumultuous sound; [[synonyms:k:kichui]]---anything; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---can hear.
translation: While the Lord was transported from the throne to the car, tumultuous sounds were made on various musical instruments. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was chanting "Maṇimā Maṇimā," but He could not be heard.
purport: The word //maṇimā// is used to address a respectable person in Orissa. Lord Jagannātha was being respectfully addressed by Śrī Caitanya in this way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.140
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued: " 'I would like to withdraw My consciousness from You and engage it in material activities, but even though I try, I cannot do so. I am naturally inclined to You only. Your instructions for Me to meditate on You are therefore simply ludicrous. In this way, You are killing Me. It is not very good for You to think of Me as a candidate for Your instructions.
text:
> citta kāḍhi' tomā haite, viṣaye cāhi lāgāite,
> yatna kari, nāri kāḍhibāre
> tāre dhyāna śikṣā karāha, loka hāsāñā māra,
> sthānāsthāna nā kara vicāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:citta]] [[synonyms:k:kāḍhi']]---withdrawing the consciousness; [[synonyms:t:tomā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from You; [[synonyms:v:viṣaye]]---in mundane subject matters; [[synonyms:c:cāhi]]---Iwant; [[synonyms:l:lāgāite]]---to engage; [[synonyms:y:yatna]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I endeavor; [[synonyms:n:nāri]] [[synonyms:k:kāḍhibāre]]---I cannot withdraw; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---to such a servant; [[synonyms:d:dhyāna]]---of meditation; [[synonyms:ś:śikṣā]]---instruction; [[synonyms:k:karāha]]---You give; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people in general; [[synonyms:h:hāsāñā]]---laugh; [[synonyms:m:māra]]---You kill; [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]-[[synonyms:a:asthāna]]---proper or improper place; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---You do not make; [[synonyms:v:vicāre]]---consideration.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued: " 'I would like to withdraw My consciousness from You and engage it in material activities, but even though I try, I cannot do so. I am naturally inclined to You only. Your instructions for Me to meditate on You are therefore simply ludicrous. In this way, You are killing Me. It is not very good for You to think of Me as a candidate for Your instructions.
purport:
Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī says in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.1.11):

> anyābhilāṣitā-śūnyaṁ
> jñāna-karmādy-anāvṛtam
> ānukūlyena kṛṣṇānu-
> śīlanaṁ bhaktir uttamā

For a pure devotee, there is no scope for indulgence in mystic //yoga// practice or the cultivation of speculative philosophy. It is indeed impossible for a pure devotee to engage his mind in such unwanted activities. Even if a pure devotee wanted to, his mind would not allow him to do so. That is a characteristic of a pure devotee-he is transcendental to all fruitive activity, speculative philosophy and mystic //yoga// meditation. The //gopīs// therefore expressed themselves as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.141
description: " 'The gopīs are not like the mystic yogīs. They will never be satisfied simply by meditating on Your lotus feet and imitating the so-called yogīs. Teaching the gopīs about meditation is another kind of duplicity. When they are instructed to undergo mystic yoga practice, they are not at all satisfied. On the contrary, they become more angry with You.' "
text:
> nahe gopī yogeśvara, pada-kamala tomāra,
> dhyāna kari' pāibe santoṣa
> tomāra vākya-paripāṭī, tāra madhye kuṭināṭī,
> śuni' gopīra āro bāḍhe roṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]---//gopīs//; [[synonyms:y:yogeśvara]]---masters of mystic yoga practice; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:k:kamala]] [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your lotus feet; [[synonyms:d:dhyāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---by meditation; [[synonyms:p:pāibe]] [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---we get satisfaction; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:v:vākya]]---words; [[synonyms:p:paripāṭī]]---very kindly composed; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that; [[synonyms:k:kuṭināṭī]]---duplicity; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:g:gopīra]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:ā:āro]]---more and more; [[synonyms:b:bāḍhe]]---increases; [[synonyms:r:roṣa]]---anger.
translation: “ 'The gopīs are not like the mystic yogīs. They will never be satisfied simply by meditating on Your lotus feet and imitating the so-called yogīs. Teaching the gopīs about meditation is another kind of duplicity. When they are instructed to undergo mystic yoga practice, they are not at all satisfied. On the contrary, they become more angry with You.' "
purport:
Śrīla Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī has stated (//Caitanya-candrāmṛta// 5):

> kaivalyaṁ narakāyate tri-daśa-pūr ākāśa-puṣpāyate
> durdāntendriya-kāla-sarpa-paṭalī protkhāta-daṁṣṭrāyate
> viśvaṁ pūrṇa-sukhāyate vidhi-mahendrādiś ca kīṭāyate
> yat kāruṇya-katākṣa-vaibhavavatāṁ taṁ gauram eva stumaḥ

For a pure devotee who has realized Kṛṣṇa consciousness through Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the monistic philosophy by which one becomes one with the Supreme appears hellish. The mystic //yoga// practice by which the mind is controlled and the senses subjugated also appears ludicrous to a pure devotee. The devotee's mind and senses are already engaged in the transcendental service of the Lord. In this way the poisonous effects of sense activities are removed. If one's mind is always engaged in the service of the Lord, there is no possibility that one will think, feel or act materially. Similarly, the fruitive workers' attempt to attain heavenly planets is nothing more than phantasmagoria for the devotee. After all, the heavenly planets are material, and in due course of time they will all be dissolved. Devotees do not care for such temporary things. They engage in transcendental devotional activities because they desire elevation to the spiritual world, where they can live eternally and peacefully and with full knowledge of Kṛṣṇa. In Vṛndāvana, the //gopīs,// cowherd boys and even the calves, cows, trees and water are fully conscious of Kṛṣṇa. They are never satisfied with anything but Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.142
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued: " 'The gopīs are fallen in the great ocean of separation, and they are being devoured by the timiṅgila fish, which represent their ambition to serve You. The gopīs are to be delivered from the mouths of these timiṅgila fish, for they are pure devotees. Since they have no material conception of life, why should they aspire for liberation? The gopīs do not want that liberation desired by yogīs and jñānīs, for they are already liberated from the ocean of material existence.
text:
> deha-smṛti nāhi yāra, saṁsāra-kūpa kāhāṅ tāra,
> tāhā haite nā cāhe uddhāra
> viraha-samudra-jale, kāma-timiṅgile gile,
> gopī-gaṇe neha' tāra pāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:deha]]-[[synonyms:s:smṛti]]---bodily concept of life; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---one whose; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]-[[synonyms:k:kūpa]]---blind well of material life; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where is; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from that; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:c:cāhe]]---want; [[synonyms:u:uddhāra]]---liberation; [[synonyms:v:viraha]]-[[synonyms:s:samudra]]-[[synonyms:j:jale]]---in the water of the ocean of separation; [[synonyms:k:kāma]]-[[synonyms:t:timiṅgile]]---the transcendental Cupid in the form of //timiṅgila// fish; [[synonyms:g:gile]]---swallow; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:n:neha']]---please take out; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:p:pāra]]---beyond that.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued: " 'The gopīs are fallen in the great ocean of separation, and they are being devoured by the timiṅgila fish, which represent their ambition to serve You. The gopīs are to be delivered from the mouths of these timiṅgila fish, for they are pure devotees. Since they have no material conception of life, why should they aspire for liberation? The gopīs do not want that liberation desired by yogīs and jñānīs, for they are already liberated from the ocean of material existence.
purport: The bodily conception is created by the desire for material enjoyment. This is called //vipada-smṛti,// which is the opposite of real life. The living entity is eternally the servant of Kṛṣṇa, but when he desires to enjoy the material world, he cannot progress in spiritual life. One can never be happy by advancing materially. This is also stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:7:5:30|(7.5.30)]]: //adānta-gobhir viśatāṁ tamisraṁ punaḥ-punaś-carvita-carvaṇānām.// Through the uncontrolled senses, one may advance one's hellish condition. He may continue to chew the chewed; that is, repeatedly accept birth and death. The conditioned souls use the duration of life between birth and death only to engage in the same hackneyed activities-eating, sleeping, mating and defending. In the lower animal species, we find the same activities. Since these activities are repeated, engaging in them is like chewing that which has already been chewed. If one can give up his ambition to engage in hackneyed material life and take to Kṛṣṇa consciousness instead, he will be liberated from the stringent laws of material nature. One does not need to make a separate attempt to become liberated. If one simply engages in the service of the Lord, he will be liberated automatically. As Śrīla Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura therefore says, //muktiḥ svayaṁ mukulitāñjali sevate 'smān:// "Liberation stands before me with folded hands, begging to serve me."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.143
description: " 'It is amazing that You have forgotten the land of Vṛndāvana. And how is it that You have forgotten Your father, mother and friends? How have You forgotten Govardhana Hill, the bank of the Yamunā, and the forest where You enjoyed the rāsa-līlā dance?
text:
> vṛndāvana, govardhana, yamunā-pulina, vana,
> sei kuñje rāsādika līlā
> sei vrajera vraja-jana, mātā, pitā, bandhu-gaṇa,
> baḍa citra, kemane pāsarilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---the transcendental land known as Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]---Govardhana Hill; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]-[[synonyms:p:pulina]]---the bank of the Yamunā; [[synonyms:v:vana]]---all the forests where the pastimes of the Lord took place; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kuñje]]---in the bushes in that forest; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādika]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes of the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vrajera]]---of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---inhabitants; [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---mother; [[synonyms:p:pitā]]---father; [[synonyms:b:bandhu]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---friends; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:c:citra]]---most wonderful; [[synonyms:k:kemane]] [[synonyms:p:pāsarilā]]---how have You forgotten.
translation: “ 'It is amazing that You have forgotten the land of Vṛndāvana. And how is it that You have forgotten Your father, mother and friends? How have You forgotten Govardhana Hill, the bank of the Yamunā, and the forest where You enjoyed the rāsa-līlā dance?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.144
description: " 'Kṛṣṇa, You are certainly a refined gentleman with all good qualities. You are well-behaved, softhearted and merciful. I know that there is not even a tinge of fault to be found in You, yet Your mind does not even remember the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana. This is only My misfortune, and nothing else.
text:
> vidagdha, mṛdu, sad-guṇa, suśīla, snigdha, karuṇa,
> tumi, tomāra nāhi doṣābhāsa
> tabe ye tomāra mana, nāhi smare vraja-jana,
> se-āmāra durdaiva-vilāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vidagdha]]---most refined; [[synonyms:m:mṛdu]]---gentle; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---endowed with all good qualities; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:ś:śīla]]---well-behaved; [[synonyms:s:snigdha]]---softhearted; [[synonyms:k:karuṇa]]---merciful; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāsa]]---even a tinge of fault; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---still; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---indeed; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---does not; [[synonyms:s:smare]]---remember; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:d:durdaiva]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---suffering of past misdeeds.
translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa, You are certainly a refined gentleman with all good qualities. You are well-behaved, softhearted and merciful. I know that there is not even a tinge of fault to be found in You, yet Your mind does not even remember the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana. This is only My misfortune, and nothing else.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.145
description: " 'I do not care for My personal unhappiness, but when I see the morose face of Your mother Yaśodā and the hearts of all the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana breaking because of You, I wonder whether You want to kill them all. Is it that You want to enliven them by coming there? Why is it You are simply keeping them alive in a state of suffering?
text:
> nā gaṇi āpana-duḥkha, dekhi' vrajeśvarī-mukha,
> vraja-janera hṛdaya vidare
> kibā māra' vraja-vāsī, kibā jīyāo vraje āsi',
> kena jīyāo duḥkha sahāibāre?
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇi]]---I do not care; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---My personal unhappiness; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:v:vrajeśvarī]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---the face of mother Yaśodā; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:j:janera]]---of all the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]] [[synonyms:v:vidare]]---the hearts break; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---whether; [[synonyms:m:māra']] [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---You want to kill the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---or; [[synonyms:j:jīyāo]]---You want to keep their lives; [[synonyms:v:vraje]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:k:kena]]---why; [[synonyms:j:jīyāo]]---You let them live; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]] [[synonyms:s:sahāibāre]]---just to cause to suffer unhappiness.
translation: “ 'I do not care for My personal unhappiness, but when I see the morose face of Your mother Yaśodā and the hearts of all the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana breaking because of You, I wonder whether You want to kill them all. Is it that You want to enliven them by coming there? Why is it You are simply keeping them alive in a state of suffering?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.146
description: " 'The inhabitants of Vṛndāvana do not want You dressed like a prince, nor do they want You to associate with great warriors in a different country. They cannot leave the land of Vṛndāvana, and without Your presence, they are all dying. What is their condition to be?
text:
> tomāra ye anya veśa, anya saṅga, anya deśa,
> vraja-jane kabhu nāhi bhāya
> vraja-bhūmi chāḍite nāre, tomā nā dekhile mare,
> vraja-janera ki habe upāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---that; [[synonyms:a:anya]] [[synonyms:v:veśa]]---different dress; [[synonyms:a:anya]] [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---other associates; [[synonyms:a:anya]] [[synonyms:d:deśa]]---other countries; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---to the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---does not; [[synonyms:b:bhāya]]---appeal; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūmi]]---the land of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:c:chāḍite]] [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---they do not like to leave; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]---You; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:d:dekhile]]---seeing; [[synonyms:m:mare]]---they die; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:j:janera]]---of the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---will be; [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---means.
translation: “ 'The inhabitants of Vṛndāvana do not want You dressed like a prince, nor do they want You to associate with great warriors in a different country. They cannot leave the land of Vṛndāvana, and without Your presence, they are all dying. What is their condition to be?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.147
description: " 'My dear Kṛṣṇa, You are the life and soul of Vṛndāvana-dhāma. You are especially the life of Nanda Mahārāja. You are the only opulence in the land of Vṛndāvana, and You are very merciful. Please come and let them all live. Kindly keep Your lotus feet again in Vṛndāvana.'
text:
> tumi-vrajera jīvana, vraja-rājera prāṇa-dhana,
> tumi vrajera sakala sampad
> kṛpārdra tomāra mana, āsi' jīyāo vraja-jana,
> vraje udaya karāo nija-pada
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:v:vrajera]] [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---the life and soul of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:r:rājera]]---and of the King of Vraja, Nanda Mahārāja; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---the only life; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:v:vrajera]]---of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:s:sakala]] [[synonyms:s:sampad]]---all opulence; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:a:ardra]]---melting with kindness; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---Your mind; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:j:jīyāo]]---give life; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---to all the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:u:udaya]] [[synonyms:k:karāo]]---cause to appear; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]---Your lotus feet.
translation: “ 'My dear Kṛṣṇa, You are the life and soul of Vṛndāvana-dhāma. You are especially the life of Nanda Mahārāja. You are the only opulence in the land of Vṛndāvana, and You are very merciful. Please come and let them all live. Kindly keep Your lotus feet again in Vṛndāvana.'
purport: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī did not express Her personal unhappiness at being separated from Kṛṣṇa. She wanted to evoke Kṛṣṇa's feelings for the condition of all others in Vṛndāvana-dhāma-mother Yaśodā, Mahārāja Nanda, the cowherd boys, the //gopīs,// the birds and bees on the banks of the Yamunā, the water of the Yamunā, the trees, forests and all other paraphernalia associated with Kṛṣṇa before He left Vṛndāvana for Mathurā. These feelings of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī were manifested by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and therefore He invited Lord Jagannātha, Kṛṣṇa, to return to Vṛndāvana. That is the purport of the Ratha-yātrā car's going from Jagannātha Purī to the Guṇḍicā temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.148
description: "After hearing Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's statements, Lord Kṛṣṇa's love for the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana was evoked, and His body and mind became very perturbed. After hearing of their love for Him, He immediately thought Himself to be always indebted to the residents of Vṛndāvana. Then Kṛṣṇa began to pacify Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī as follows.
text:
> śuniyā rādhikā-vāṇī, vraja-prema mane āni,
> bhāve vyākulita deha-mana
> vraja-lokera prema śuni', āpanāke 'ṛṇī' māni',
> kare kṛṣṇa tāṅre āśvāsana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---after hearing; [[synonyms:r:rādhikā]]-[[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---the statement of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]---the love of Vraja; [[synonyms:m:mane]] [[synonyms:ā:āni]]---remembering; [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in that ecstasy; [[synonyms:v:vyākulita]]---very much perturbed; [[synonyms:d:deha]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the body and mind; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:p:prema]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---after hearing of the loving affairs; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāke]]---Himself; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṇī]] [[synonyms:m:māni']]---considering very indebted; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Her; [[synonyms:ā:āśvāsana]]---pacification.
translation: "After hearing Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's statements, Lord Kṛṣṇa's love for the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana was evoked, and His body and mind became very perturbed. After hearing of their love for Him, He immediately thought Himself to be always indebted to the residents of Vṛndāvana. Then Kṛṣṇa began to pacify Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.149
description: " 'My dearest Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, please hear Me. I am speaking the truth. I cry day and night simply upon remembering all you inhabitants of Vṛndāvana. No one knows how unhappy this makes Me.'
text:
> prāṇa-priye, śuna, mora e-satya-vacana
> tomā-sabāra smaraṇe, jhuroṅ muñi rātri-dine,
> mora duḥkha nā jāne kona jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:priye]]---O My dearmost; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---of Me; [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:satya]]-[[synonyms:v:vacana]]---this true statement; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of you; [[synonyms:s:smaraṇe]]---by remembrance; [[synonyms:j:jhuroṅ]]---cry; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---both day and night; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---My distress; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---does not know; [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---anyone.
translation: “ 'My dearest Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, please hear Me. I am speaking the truth. I cry day and night simply upon remembering all you inhabitants of Vṛndāvana. No one knows how unhappy this makes Me.'
purport: It is said: //vṛndāvanaṁ parityajya padam ekaṁ na gacchati.// In one sense, Kṛṣṇa, the original Personality of Godhead (//īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ//), does not even take one step away from Vṛndāvana. However, in order to take care of various duties, Kṛṣṇa had to leave Vṛndāvana. He had to go to Mathurā to kill Kaṁsa, and then He was taken by His father to Dvārakā, where He was busy with state affairs and disturbances created by demons. Kṛṣṇa was away from Vṛndāvana, and He was not at all happy, as He plainly disclosed to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. She is the dearmost life and soul of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and He expressed His mind to Her as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.15
description: While the Lord was being carried from the throne to the car, King Pratāparudra personally engaged in the Lord's service by cleansing the road with a broom that had a golden handle.
text:
> tabe pratāparudra kare āpane sevana
> suvarṇa-mārjanī lañā kare patha sammārjana

translation: While the Lord was being carried from the throne to the car, King Pratāparudra personally engaged in the Lord's service by cleansing the road with a broom that had a golden handle.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.150
description: "Śrī Kṛṣṇa continued: 'All the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana-dhāma-My mother, father, cowherd boy friends and everything else-are like My life and soul. And among all the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana, the gopīs are My very life and soul. Among the gopīs, You, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, are the chief. Therefore You are the very life of My life.
text:
> vraja-vāsī yata jana, mātā, pitā, sakhā-gaṇa,
> sabe haya mora prāṇa-sama
> tāṅra madhye gopī-gaṇa, sākṣāt mora jīvana,
> tumi mora jīvanera jīvana

translation: "Śrī Kṛṣṇa continued: 'All the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana-dhāma-My mother, father, cowherd boy friends and everything else-are like My life and soul. And among all the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana, the gopīs are My very life and soul. Among the gopīs, You, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, are the chief. Therefore You are the very life of My life.
purport: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is the center of all Vṛndāvana's activities. In Vṛndāvana, Kṛṣṇa is the instrument of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; therefore all the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana still chant "Jaya Rādhe." From Kṛṣṇa's own statement given herein, it appears that Rādhārāṇī is the Queen of Vṛndāvana and that Kṛṣṇa is simply Her decoration. Kṛṣṇa is known as Madana-mohana, the enchanter of Cupid, but Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is the enchanter of Kṛṣṇa. Consequently Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is called Madana-mohana-mohinī, the enchanter of the enchanter of Cupid.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.151
description: " 'My dear Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, I am always subservient to the loving affairs of all of you. I am under your control only. My separation from you and residence in distant places have occurred due to My strong misfortune.
text:
> tomā-sabāra prema-rase, āmāke karila vaśe,
> āmi tomāra adhīna kevala
> tomā-sabā chāḍāñā, āmā dūra-deśe lañā,
> rākhiyāche durdaiva prabala

translation: “ 'My dear Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, I am always subservient to the loving affairs of all of you. I am under your control only. My separation from you and residence in distant places have occurred due to My strong misfortune.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.152
description: " 'When a woman is separated from the man she loves or a man is separated from his beloved woman, neither of them can live. It is a fact that they live only for one another, for if one dies and the other hears of it, he or she will die also.
text:
> priyā priya-saṅga-hīnā, priya priyā-saṅga vinā,
> nāhi jīye,-e satya pramāṇa
> mora daśā śone yabe, tāṅra ei daśā habe,
> ei bhaye duṅhe rākhe prāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:priyā]]---a woman beloved; [[synonyms:p:priya]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]-[[synonyms:h:hīnā]]---being separated from the man beloved; [[synonyms:p:priya]]---the man beloved; [[synonyms:p:priyā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]] [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---being separated from the woman beloved; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:j:jīye]]---cannot live; [[synonyms:e:e]] [[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---this is factual evidence; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---situation; [[synonyms:ś:śone]] [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when one hears; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---situation; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---out of this fear; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both; [[synonyms:r:rākhe]] [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]---keep their life.
translation: “ 'When a woman is separated from the man she loves or a man is separated from his beloved woman, neither of them can live. It is a fact that they live only for one another, for if one dies and the other hears of it, he or she will die also.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.153
description: " 'A loving, chaste wife and a loving husband who desire all welfare for each other in separation and do not care for personal happiness, desire only one another's well-being. Such a pair certainly meet again without delay.
text:
> sei satī premavatī, premavān sei pati,
> viyoge ye vāñche priya-hite
> nā gaṇe āpana-duḥkha, vāñche priyajana-sukha,
> sei dui mile acirāte
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:satī]]---that chaste wife; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:v:vatī]]---full of love; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:v:vān]]---loving; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:pati]]---that husband; [[synonyms:v:viyoge]]---in separation; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---who; [[synonyms:v:vāñche]]---desire; [[synonyms:p:priya]]-[[synonyms:h:hite]]---for the welfare of the other; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---and do not care; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---for personal unhappiness; [[synonyms:v:vāñche]]---desire; [[synonyms:p:priya]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]---the happiness of the dearmost beloved; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:m:mile]]---meet; [[synonyms:a:acirāte]]---without delay.
translation: “ 'A loving, chaste wife and a loving husband who desire all welfare for each other in separation and do not care for personal happiness, desire only one another's well-being. Such a pair certainly meet again without delay.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.154
description: " 'You are My most dear, and I know that in My absence You cannot live for a moment. Just to keep You living, I worship Lord Nārāyaṇa. By His merciful potency, I come to Vṛndāvana every day to enjoy pastimes with You. I then return to Dvārakā-dhāma. Thus You can always feel My presence here in Vṛndāvana.
text:
> rākhite tomāra jīvana, sevi āmi nārāyaṇa,
> tāṅra śaktye āsi niti-niti
> tomā-sane krīḍā kari', niti yāi yadu-purī,
> tāhā tumi mānaha mora sphūrti
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rākhite]]---just to keep; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---Your life; [[synonyms:s:sevi]] [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---I always worship Lord Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:ś:śaktye]]---by His potency; [[synonyms:ā:āsi]] [[synonyms:n:niti]]-[[synonyms:n:niti]]---I come to You daily; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with You; [[synonyms:k:krīḍā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---enjoying pastimes; [[synonyms:n:niti]]---daily; [[synonyms:y:yāi]] [[synonyms:y:yadu]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]---I return to Dvārakā-dhāma, known as Yadu-purī; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:m:mānaha]]---experience; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:s:sphūrti]]---manifestation.
translation: “ 'You are My most dear, and I know that in My absence You cannot live for a moment. Just to keep You living, I worship Lord Nārāyaṇa. By His merciful potency, I come to Vṛndāvana every day to enjoy pastimes with You. I then return to Dvārakā-dhāma. Thus You can always feel My presence here in Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.155
description: " 'Our love affair is more powerful because of My good fortune in receiving Nārāyaṇa's grace. This allows Me to come here unseen by others. I hope that very soon I will be visible to everyone.
text:
> mora bhāgya mo-viṣaye, tomāra ye prema haye,
> sei prema-parama prabala
> lukāñā āmā āne, saṅga karāya tomā-sane,
> prakaṭeha ānibe satvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:b:bhāgya]]---My fortune; [[synonyms:m:mo]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣaye]]---in relation with Me; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love; [[synonyms:h:haye]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:prema]]---that love; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:p:pra]]-[[synonyms:b:bala]]---very powerful; [[synonyms:l:lukāñā]]---secretly; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]] [[synonyms:ā:āne]]---brings Me; [[synonyms:s:saṅga]] [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---obliges Me to associate; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with You; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭeha]]---directly manifested; [[synonyms:ā:ānibe]]---will bring; [[synonyms:s:satvara]]---very soon.
translation: “ 'Our love affair is more powerful because of My good fortune in receiving Nārāyaṇa's grace. This allows Me to come here unseen by others. I hope that very soon I will be visible to everyone.
purport:
Kṛṣṇa has two kinds of presence-//prakaṭa// and //aprakaṭa,// manifest and unmanifest. Both are identical to the sincere devotee. Even if Kṛṣṇa is not physically present, the devotee's absorption in the affairs of Kṛṣṇa makes Him present. This is confirmed in the //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.38):

> premāñjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena
> santaḥ sadaiva hṛdayeṣu vilokayanti
> yaṁ śyāmasundaram acintya-guṇa-svarūpaṁ
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi

Due to his intense love, the pure devotee always sees Lord Kṛṣṇa present within his heart. All glories to Govinda, the primeval Personality of Godhead! When Kṛṣṇa is not manifest before the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana, they are always absorbed in thoughts of Him. Therefore even though Kṛṣṇa was living at that time at Dvārakā, He was simultaneously present before all the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana. This was His //aprakaṭa// presence. Devotees who are always absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa will soon see Kṛṣṇa face to face without a doubt. Devotees who are always engaged in Kṛṣṇa consciousness and are fully absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa certainly return home, back to Godhead. They then see Kṛṣṇa directly, face to face, take //prasāda// with Him and enjoy His company. This is confirmed in //Bhagavad-gītā:tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so 'rjuna// [[books:bg:4:9|(Bg. 4.9)]].

During his lifetime, a pure devotee is always speaking of Kṛṣṇa and engaging in His service, and as soon as he gives up his body, he immediately returns to Goloka Vṛndāvana, where Kṛṣṇa is personally present. He then meets Kṛṣṇa directly. This is successful human life. This is the meaning of //prakaṭeha ānibe satvara.// The pure devotee will soon see the personal manifestation of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.156
description: " 'I have already killed all the mischievous demons who are enemies of the Yadu dynasty, and I have also killed Kaṁsa and his allies. However, there are two or four demons still living. I want to kill them, and after doing so I shall very soon return to Vṛndāvana. Please know this for certain.
text:
> yādavera vipakṣa, yata duṣṭa kaṁsa-pakṣa,
> tāhā āmi kailuṅ saba kṣaya
> āche dui-cāri jana, tāhā māri' vṛndāvana,
> āilāma āmi, jāniha niścaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yādavera]] [[synonyms:v:vipakṣa]]---all the enemies of the Yadu dynasty; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:d:duṣṭa]]---mischievous; [[synonyms:k:kaṁsa]]-[[synonyms:p:pakṣa]]---the party of Kaṁsa; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---them; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kailuṅ]] [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:k:kṣaya]]---have annihilated all; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there are still; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---two or four demons; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:m:māri']]---after killing them; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:ā:āilāma]] [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I am coming very soon; [[synonyms:j:jāniha]] [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---please know it very well.
translation: “ 'I have already killed all the mischievous demons who are enemies of the Yadu dynasty, and I have also killed Kaṁsa and his allies. However, there are two or four demons still living. I want to kill them, and after doing so I shall very soon return to Vṛndāvana. Please know this for certain.
purport: Just as Kṛṣṇa does not take a step away from Vṛndāvana, Kṛṣṇa's devotee also does not like to leave Vṛndāvana. However, when he has to tend to Kṛṣṇa's business, he leaves Vṛndāvana. After finishing his mission, a pure devotee returns home, back to Vṛndāvana, back to Godhead. Kṛṣṇa assured Rādhārāṇī that after killing the demons outside Vṛndāvana, He would return. "I am coming back very soon," He promised, "as soon as I have killed the few remaining demons."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.157
description: " 'I wish to protect the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana from the attacks of My enemies. That is why I remain in My kingdom; otherwise I am indifferent to My royal position. Whatever wives, sons and wealth I maintain in the kingdom are only for the satisfaction of the Yadus.
text:
> sei śatru-gaṇa haite, vraja-jana rākhite,
> rahi rājye udāsīna hañā
> yebā strī-putra-dhane, kari rājya āvaraṇe,
> yadu-gaṇera santoṣa lāgiyā

translation: “ 'I wish to protect the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana from the attacks of My enemies. That is why I remain in My kingdom; otherwise I am indifferent to My royal position. Whatever wives, sons and wealth I maintain in the kingdom are only for the satisfaction of the Yadus.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.158
description: " 'Your loving qualities always attract Me to Vṛndāvana. Indeed, they will bring Me back within ten or twenty days, and when I return I shall enjoy both day and night with You and all the damsels of Vrajabhūmi.'
text:
> tomāra ye prema-guṇa, kare āmā ākarṣaṇa,
> ānibe āmā dina daśa biśe

translation: “ 'Your loving qualities always attract Me to Vṛndāvana. Indeed, they will bring Me back within ten or twenty days, and when I return I shall enjoy both day and night with You and all the damsels of Vrajabhūmi.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.159
description: "While speaking to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Kṛṣṇa became very anxious to return to Vṛndāvana. He made Her listen to a verse which banished all Her difficulties and which assured Her that She would again attain Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> eta tāṅre kahi kṛṣṇa, vraje yāite satṛṣṇa,
> eka śloka paḍi' śunāila
> sei śloka śuni' rādhā, khāṇḍila sakala bādhā,
> kṛṣṇa-prāptye pratīti ha-ila

translation: "While speaking to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Kṛṣṇa became very anxious to return to Vṛndāvana. He made Her listen to a verse which banished all Her difficulties and which assured Her that She would again attain Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.16
description: The King sprinkled the road with sandalwood-scented water. Although he was the owner of the royal throne, he engaged in menial service for the sake of Lord Jagannātha.
text:
> candana-jalete kare patha niṣecane
> tuccha sevā kare vasi' rāja-siṁhāsane

translation: The King sprinkled the road with sandalwood-scented water. Although he was the owner of the royal throne, he engaged in menial service for the sake of Lord Jagannātha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.160
description: "Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: 'Devotional service unto Me is the only way to attain Me. My dear gopīs, whatever love and affection you have attained for Me by good fortune is the only reason for My returning to you.' "
text:
> mayi bhaktir hi bhūtānām
> amṛtatvāya kalpate
> diṣṭyā yad āsīn mat-sneho
> bhavatīnāṁ mad-āpanaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mayi]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:b:bhaktiḥ]]---the nine kinds of devotional service, such as //śravaṇa, kīrtana// and //smaraṇa//; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:b:bhūtānām]]---of all living entities; [[synonyms:a:amṛtatvāya]]---for becoming eternal associates of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kalpate]]---is quite befitting; [[synonyms:d:diṣṭyā]]---by good fortune; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---whatever; [[synonyms:ā:āsīt]]---there was; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:s:snehaḥ]]---love and affection for Me; [[synonyms:b:bhavatīnām]]---of all you //gopīs//; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:ā:āpanaḥ]]---the cause for getting Me back.
translation: "Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: 'Devotional service unto Me is the only way to attain Me. My dear gopīs, whatever love and affection you have attained for Me by good fortune is the only reason for My returning to you.' "
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.82.44).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.161
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would sit in His room with Svarūpa Dāmodara and taste the topics of these verses day and night.
text:
> ei saba artha prabhu svarūpera sane
> rātri-dine ghare vasi' kare āsvādane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all these; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meanings; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:svarūpera]] [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---both day and night; [[synonyms:g:ghare]] [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting within His room; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādane]]---taste.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would sit in His room with Svarūpa Dāmodara and taste the topics of these verses day and night.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.162
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced completely absorbed in ecstatic emotion. While looking at the face of Lord Jagannātha, He danced and recited these verses.
text:
> nṛtya-kāle sei bhāve āviṣṭa hañā
> śloka paḍi' nāce jagannātha-mukha cāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---while dancing; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in such ecstasy; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---absorbed; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting these verses; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---the face of Jagannātha; [[synonyms:c:cāñā]]---looking upon.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced completely absorbed in ecstatic emotion. While looking at the face of Lord Jagannātha, He danced and recited these verses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.163
description: No one can describe the good fortune of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, for he is always absorbed in the service of the Lord with his body, mind and words.
text:
> svarūpa-gosāñira bhāgya nā yāya varṇana
> prabhute āviṣṭa yāṅra kāya, vākya, mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:b:bhāgya]]---the fortune; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāya]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---can be described; [[synonyms:p:prabhute]]---in the service of the Lord; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---fully absorbed; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:k:kāya]]---body; [[synonyms:v:vākya]]---words; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind.
translation: No one can describe the good fortune of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, for he is always absorbed in the service of the Lord with his body, mind and words.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.164
description: The senses of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were identical with the senses of Svarūpa. Therefore Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to become fully absorbed in tasting the singing of Svarūpa Dāmodara.
text:
> svarūpera indriye prabhura nijendriya-gaṇa
> āviṣṭa hañā kare gāna-āsvādana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpera]]---of Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:i:indriye]]---in the senses; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:i:indriya]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---own senses; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being fully absorbed; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:g:gāna]]---the singing; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasting.
translation: The senses of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were identical with the senses of Svarūpa. Therefore Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to become fully absorbed in tasting the singing of Svarūpa Dāmodara.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.165
description: In emotional ecstasy, Caitanya Mahāprabhu would sometimes sit on the ground and, looking down, would write on the ground with His finger.
text:
> bhāvera āveśe kabhu bhūmite vasiyā
> tarjanīte bhūme likhe adhomukha hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]] [[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---because of ecstatic emotion; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:v:vasiyā]]---sitting; [[synonyms:t:tarjanīte]]---with the ring finger; [[synonyms:b:bhūme]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:l:likhe]]---writes; [[synonyms:a:adhomukha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---looking down.
translation: In emotional ecstasy, Caitanya Mahāprabhu would sometimes sit on the ground and, looking down, would write on the ground with His finger.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.166
description: Feeling that the Lord would injure His finger by writing in this way, Svarūpa Dāmodara checked Him with his own hand.
text:
> aṅgulite kṣata habe jāni' dāmodara
> bhaye nija-kare nivāraye prabhu-kara
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aṅgulite]]---on the finger; [[synonyms:k:kṣata]]---injury; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---will take place; [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---knowing; [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---out of fear; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:k:kare]]---by his own hand; [[synonyms:n:nivāraye]]---checks; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:k:kara]]---the hand of the Lord.
translation: Feeling that the Lord would injure His finger by writing in this way, Svarūpa Dāmodara checked Him with his own hand.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.167
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara used to sing exactly according to the ecstatic emotion of the Lord. Whenever a particular mellow was being tasted by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Svarūpa Dāmodara would personify it by singing.
text:
> prabhura bhāvānurūpa svarūpera gāna
> yabe yei rasa tāhā kare mūrtimān
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:a:anurūpa]]---following the ecstatic emotions; [[synonyms:s:svarūpera]]---of Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:g:gāna]]---the singing; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---mellow; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---makes; [[synonyms:m:mūrtimān]]---personified.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara used to sing exactly according to the ecstatic emotion of the Lord. Whenever a particular mellow was being tasted by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Svarūpa Dāmodara would personify it by singing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.168
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu looked upon the beautiful lotuslike face and eyes of Lord Jagannātha.
text:
> śrī-jagannāthera dekhe śrī-mukha-kamala
> tāhāra upara sundara nayana-yugala
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:j:jagannāthera]]---of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]-[[synonyms:k:kamala]]---the lotuslike face; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]] [[synonyms:u:upara]]---upon this; [[synonyms:s:sundara]]---beautiful; [[synonyms:n:nayana]]-[[synonyms:y:yugala]]---a pair of eyes.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu looked upon the beautiful lotuslike face and eyes of Lord Jagannātha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.169
description: Lord Jagannātha was garlanded, dressed with nice garments and adorned with beautiful ornaments. His face was glittering from the rays of sunshine, and the entire atmosphere was fragrant.
text:
> sūryera kiraṇe mukha kare jhalamala
> mālya, vastra, divya alaṅkāra, parimala
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sūryera]]---of the sun; [[synonyms:k:kiraṇe]]---by the rays of sunshine; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---the face; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:j:jhalamala]]---glittering; [[synonyms:m:mālya]]---garland; [[synonyms:v:vastra]]---garments; [[synonyms:d:divya]] [[synonyms:a:alaṅkāra]]---beautiful ornaments; [[synonyms:p:parimala]]---surrounded by a fragrance.
translation: Lord Jagannātha was garlanded, dressed with nice garments and adorned with beautiful ornaments. His face was glittering from the rays of sunshine, and the entire atmosphere was fragrant.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.17
description: Although the King was the most exalted respectable person, still he accepted menial service for the Lord; he, therefore, became a suitable candidate for receiving the Lord's mercy.
text:
> uttama hañā rājā kare tuccha sevana
> ataeva jagannāthera kṛpāra bhājana
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uttama]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---although very respectable; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---accepts; [[synonyms:t:tuccha]]---menial; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---service; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:j:jagannāthera]]---of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:k:kṛpāra]]---in the matter of mercy; [[synonyms:b:bhājana]]---suitable candidate.
translation: Although the King was the most exalted respectable person, still he accepted menial service for the Lord; he, therefore, became a suitable candidate for receiving the Lord's mercy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.170
description: An ocean of transcendental bliss expanded in the heart of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and symptoms of madness immediately intensified like a hurricane.
text:
> prabhura hṛdaye ānanda-sindhu uthalila
> unmāda, jhañjhā-vāta tat-kṣaṇe uṭhila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---in the heart of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sindhu]]---the ocean of transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:u:uthalila]]---arose; [[synonyms:u:unmāda]]---madness; [[synonyms:j:jhañjhā]]-[[synonyms:v:vāta]]---hurricane; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---immediately; [[synonyms:u:uṭhila]]---intensified.
translation: An ocean of transcendental bliss expanded in the heart of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and symptoms of madness immediately intensified like a hurricane.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.171
description: The madness of transcendental bliss created waves of various emotions. The emotions appeared like opposing soldiers staging a fight.
text:
> ānandonmāde uṭhāya bhāvera taraṅga
> nānā-bhāva-sainye upajila yuddha-raṅga
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:u:unmāde]]---the madness of transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāya]]---causes to arise; [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of emotion; [[synonyms:t:taraṅga]]---waves; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---emotions; [[synonyms:s:sainye]]---among soldiers; [[synonyms:u:upajila]]---there appeared; [[synonyms:y:yuddha]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅga]]---fighting.
translation: The madness of transcendental bliss created waves of various emotions. The emotions appeared like opposing soldiers staging a fight.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.172
description: There was an increase in all the natural emotional symptoms. Thus there were awakening emotions, peacefulness, joined, mixed, transcendental and prevalent emotions, and impetuses for emotion.
text:
> bhāvodaya, bhāva-śānti, sandhi, śābalya
> sañcārī, sāttvika, sthāyī svabhāva-prābalya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]]---awakening of emotion; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śānti]]---emotions of peace; [[synonyms:s:sandhi]]---the junction of different emotions; [[synonyms:ś:śābalya]]---mixing of all emotions; [[synonyms:s:sañcārī]]---impetuses for all kinds of emotion; [[synonyms:s:sāttvika]]---transcendental; [[synonyms:s:sthāyī]]---prevalent; [[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---natural emotion; [[synonyms:p:prābalya]]---increase.
translation: There was an increase in all the natural emotional symptoms. Thus there were awakening emotions, peacefulness, joined, mixed, transcendental and prevalent emotions, and impetuses for emotion.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.173
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's body appeared like a transcendental Himalayan mountain bearing ecstatic emotional flower trees, all of them blooming.
text:
> prabhura śarīra yena śuddha-hemācala
> bhāva-puṣpa-druma tāhe puṣpita sakala
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śarīra]]---body; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]---transcendental; [[synonyms:h:hemācala]]---Himalayan mountain; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---emotional; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:d:druma]]---flower trees; [[synonyms:t:tāhe]]---in that situation; [[synonyms:p:puṣpita]]---blooming with flowers; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's body appeared like a transcendental Himalayan mountain bearing ecstatic emotional flower trees, all of them blooming.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.174
description: Upon seeing all these symptoms, everyone's mind and consciousness were attracted. Indeed, the Lord sprinkled everyone's mind with the nectar of transcendental love of Godhead.
text:
> dekhite ākarṣaye sabāra citta-mana
> premāmṛta-vṛṣṭye prabhu siñce sabāra mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---by seeing; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaye]]---attracts; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:c:citta]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind and consciousness; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛṣṭye]]---by pouring of the nectar of transcendental love for God; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:siñce]]---sprinkled; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---everyone's; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind.
translation: Upon seeing all these symptoms, everyone's mind and consciousness were attracted. Indeed, the Lord sprinkled everyone's mind with the nectar of transcendental love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.175
description: He sprinkled the minds of the servants of Lord Jagannātha, the government officers, the pilgrim visitors, the general populace and all the residents of Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> jagannātha-sevaka yata rāja-pātra-gaṇa
> yātrika loka, nīlācala-vāsī yata jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---the servants of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---and the government officers; [[synonyms:y:yātrika]]---pilgrim visitors; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people in general; [[synonyms:n:nīlācala]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---the residents of Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:y:yata]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---as many people as there were.
translation: He sprinkled the minds of the servants of Lord Jagannātha, the government officers, the pilgrim visitors, the general populace and all the residents of Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.176
description: After seeing the dancing and ecstatic love of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, everyone became astonished. In their hearts they became infatuated with love of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> prabhura nṛtya prema dekhi' haya camatkāra
> kṛṣṇa-prema uchalila hṛdaye sabāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---become; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonished; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]---love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:u:uchalila]]---infatuated; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---in the hearts; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone.
translation: After seeing the dancing and ecstatic love of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, everyone became astonished. In their hearts they became infatuated with love of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.177
description: Everyone danced and chanted in ecstatic love, and a great noise resounded. Everyone was overwhelmed with transcendental bliss just to see the dancing of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> preme nāce, gāya, loka, kare kolāhala
> prabhura nṛtya dekhi' sabe ānande vihvala
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chant; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people in general; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---make; [[synonyms:k:kolāhala]]---a great noise; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---everyone; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---overwhelmed.
translation: Everyone danced and chanted in ecstatic love, and a great noise resounded. Everyone was overwhelmed with transcendental bliss just to see the dancing of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.178
description: Apart from the others, even Lord Jagannātha and Lord Balarāma, with great happiness, began to move very slowly upon seeing the dancing of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> anyera ki kāya, jagannātha-haladhara
> prabhura nṛtya dekhi' sukhe calilā manthara
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anyera]] [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:k:kāya]]---apart from the actions of others; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:h:haladhara]]---Balarāma; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---the dancing; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in great happiness; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---moved; [[synonyms:m:manthara]]---slowly.
translation: Apart from the others, even Lord Jagannātha and Lord Balarāma, with great happiness, began to move very slowly upon seeing the dancing of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.179
description: Lord Jagannātha and Lord Balarāma sometimes stopped the car and happily observed Lord Caitanya's dancing. Anyone who was able to see Them stop and watch the dancing bore witness to Their pastimes.
text:
> kabhu sukhe nṛtya-raṅga dekhe ratha rākhi'
> se kautuka ye dekhila, sei tāra sākṣī
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in great happiness; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅga]]---amusement in dancing; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]---the car; [[synonyms:r:rākhi']]---stopping; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:k:kautuka]]---that amusement; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---saw; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---//he//; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:s:sākṣī]]---witness.
translation: Lord Jagannātha and Lord Balarāma sometimes stopped the car and happily observed Lord Caitanya's dancing. Anyone who was able to see Them stop and watch the dancing bore witness to Their pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.18
description: Upon seeing the King engaged in such menial service, Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very happy. Simply by rendering this service, the King received the mercy of the Lord.
text:
> mahāprabhu sukha pāila se-sevā dekhite
> mahāprabhura kṛpā haila se-sevā ha-ite
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sukha]] [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---felt very happy; [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]]---that kind of service; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---because of that service.
translation: Upon seeing the King engaged in such menial service, Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very happy. Simply by rendering this service, the King received the mercy of the Lord.
purport:
Unless one receives the mercy of the Lord, he cannot understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead or engage in His devotional service.

> athāpi te deva padāmbuja-dvaya-
> prasāda-leśānugṛhīta eva hi
> jānāti tattvaṁ bhagavan-mahimno
> na cānya eko 'pi ciraṁ vicinvan
> (//Bhāg.// 10.14.29)

Only a devotee who has received a small fraction of the mercy of the Lord can understand Him. Others may engage in theoretical speculation to understand the Lord, but they can not know anything about Him. Although Mahārāja Pratāparudra was very eager to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord refused to see him. However, when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the King engaged in menial service for Lord Jagannātha, He became very happy. Thus the King became eligible to receive Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mercy. If a devotee accepts Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as the universal //guru// and Lord Jagannātha as the Supreme Personality of Godhead Kṛṣṇa, he is benefited by the combined mercy of Kṛṣṇa and //guru.// That is stated by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in His instructions to Rūpa Gosvāmī. [[books:cc:madhya:19:151|(Cc. Madhya 19.151)]]

> brahmāṇḍa bhramite kona bhāgyavān jīva
> guru-kṛṣṇa-prasāde pāya bhakti-latā-bīja

The seed of devotional service fructifies and becomes a transcendental creeper. Finally it reaches the lotus feet of the Lord in the spiritual sky. This seed is obtained by the mercy of the Lord and the //guru.// By the Lord's mercy one gets the association of a bona fide //guru,// and by the mercy of the //guru,// one gets a chance to render devotional service. Devotional service, the science of //bhakti-yoga,// carries one from this material world to the spiritual world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.180

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.184
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had already been satisfied by the King's behavior, for the King had accepted the service of a sweeper for Lord Jagannātha. Therefore Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu actually desired to see the King.
text:
> yadyapi rājāra dekhi' hāḍira sevana
> prasanna hañāche tāṅre milibāre mana

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.185
description: However, just to warn His personal associates, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, externally expressed feelings of anger.
text:
> tathāpi āpana-gaṇe karite sāvadhāna
> bāhye kichu roṣābhāsa kailā bhagavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---to personal associates; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to do; [[synonyms:s:sāvadhāna]]---warning; [[synonyms:b:bāhye]]---externally; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:r:roṣa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāsa]]---apparent anger; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---showed; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: However, just to warn His personal associates, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, externally expressed feelings of anger.
purport:
When Mahārāja Pratāparudra asked to see the Lord, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately refused, saying:

> niṣkiñcanasya bhagavad-bhajanonmukhasya
> pāraṁ paraṁ jigamiṣor bhava-sāgarasya
> sandarśanaṁ viṣayiṇām atha yoṣitāṁ ca
> hā hanta hanta viṣa-bhakṣaṇato 'py asādhu

(Cc. Madhya 11.8)

The word //niṣkiñcanasya// refers to a person who has finished his material activities. Such a person can begin to execute his activities in Kṛṣṇa consciousness to cross over the ocean of nescience. It is very dangerous for such a person to have intimate relationships with mundane people or to become intimately related with women. This formality is to be observed by anyone who is serious about going back home, back to Godhead. To teach His personal associates these principles, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu expressed external anger when touched by the King. Since the Lord was very satisfied with the humble behavior of the King, He intentionally allowed the King to touch Him, but externally He expressed anger just to warn His personal associates.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.186
description: King Pratāparudra became frightened when Lord Caitanya showed external anger, but Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya told the King, "Don't worry."
text:
> prabhura vacane rājāra mane haila bhaya
> sārvabhauma kahe,-tumi nā kaya saṁśaya

translation: King Pratāparudra became frightened when Lord Caitanya showed external anger, but Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya told the King, "Don't worry."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.187
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya informed the King, "The Lord is very satisfied with you. By pointing you out, He was teaching His personal associates how to behave with mundane people."
text:
> tomāra upare prabhura suprasanna mana
> tomā lakṣya kari' śikhāyena nija gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:u:upare]]---upon you; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:p:prasanna]]---very satisfied; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]---you; [[synonyms:l:lakṣya]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---pointing out; [[synonyms:ś:śikhāyena]]---He teaches; [[synonyms:n:nija]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---His personal associates.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya informed the King, "The Lord is very satisfied with you. By pointing you out, He was teaching His personal associates how to behave with mundane people."
purport: Although outwardly the King was a mundane man interested in money and women, internally he was purified by devotional activities. He showed this by engaging as a street sweeper to please Lord Jagannātha. A person may appear to be a pounds-and-shillings man interested in money and women, but if he is actually very meek and humble and surrendered to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he is not mundane. Such a judgment can be made only by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His very confidential devotees. As a general principle, however, no devotee should intimately mix with mundane people interested in money and women.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.188
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya continued, "I shall submit your petition when there is an opportune moment. It will then be easy for you to come and meet the Lord."
text:
> avasara jāni' āmi kariba nivedana
> sei-kāle yāi' kariha prabhura milana

translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya continued, "I shall submit your petition when there is an opportune moment. It will then be easy for you to come and meet the Lord."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.189
description: After circumambulating Jagannātha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went behind the car and began pushing it with His head.
text:

> ratha-pāche yāi' ṭhele rathe māthā diyā

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.19
description: Everyone was astonished to see the decorations on the Ratha car. The car appeared to be newly made of gold, and it was as high as Mount Sumeru.
text:
> rathera sājani dekhi' loke camatkāra
> nava hemamaya ratha-sumeru-ākāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rathera]]---of the car; [[synonyms:s:sājani]]---decoration; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---by seeing; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---everyone; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonished; [[synonyms:n:nava]]---new; [[synonyms:h:hema]]-[[synonyms:m:ma]] [[synonyms:y:ya]]---golden; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]---chariot car; [[synonyms:s:sumeru]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---as high as the mountain Sumeru.
translation: Everyone was astonished to see the decorations on the Ratha car. The car appeared to be newly made of gold, and it was as high as Mount Sumeru.
purport: In the year 1973 there was a gorgeous Ratha-yātrā festival in London, England, and the car was brought to Trafalgar Square. The London daily newspaper the //Guardian// published a front-page photo caption: "ISKCON Ratha-yātrā is rival to the Nelson Column in Trafalgar Square." The Nelson Column is a very impressive statue of Lord Nelson and can be seen from a good distance. Just as the residents of Purī compared the Ratha-yātrā car to Mount Sumeru, the residents of London considered the car rival to the Nelson Monument.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.190
description: As soon as He pushed, the car immediately started to move, making a rattling noise. The people all around began to chant the holy name of the Lord, "Hari! Hari!"
text:

translation: As soon as He pushed, the car immediately started to move, making a rattling noise. The people all around began to chant the holy name of the Lord, "Hari! Hari!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.191
description: As the car began to move, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took His personal associates in front of the cars occupied by Lord Balarāma and Subhadrā, the goddess of fortune. Greatly inspired, He then began to dance in front of Them.
text:

text:
> tāhāṅ nṛtya kari' jagannātha āge āilā

translation: After finishing the dance before Lord Baladeva and Subhadrā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came before Lord Jagannātha's car. Upon seeing Lord Jagannātha, He began to dance again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.193
description: When they reached the place called Balagaṇḍi, Lord Jagannātha stopped His car and began to look left and right.
text:
> caliyā āila ratha 'balagaṇḍi'-sthāne
> jagannātha ratha rākhi' dekhe ḍāhine vāme
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caliyā]]---moving; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]---the car; [[synonyms:b:balagaṇḍi]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---at the place known as Balagaṇḍi; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]---car; [[synonyms:r:rākhi']]---after stopping; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍāhine]] [[synonyms:v:vāme]]---left and right.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.194
description: On the left side, Lord Jagannātha saw the neighborhood of brāhmaṇas known as vipra-śāsana and the coconut tree grove. On the right side, He saw nice flower gardens resembling those in the holy place Vṛndāvana.
text:
> vāme-'vipra-śāsana' nārikela-vana
> ḍāhine ta' puṣpodyāna yena vṛndāvana

translation: On the left side, Lord Jagannātha saw the neighborhood of brāhmaṇas known as vipra-śāsana and the coconut tree grove. On the right side, He saw nice flower gardens resembling those in the holy place Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.195
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His devotees were dancing in front of the car, and, having stopped the car, Lord Jagannātha watched the dancing.

description: It was customary that food be offered to the Lord at vipra-śāsana. Indeed, innumerable dishes of food were offered, and Lord Jagannātha tasted each one of them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.197
