title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.198
description: This included the King, his queens, his ministers and friends and all other big and small residents of Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> rājā, rāja-mahiṣī-vṛnda, pātra, mitra-gaṇa
> nīlācala-vāsī yata choṭa-baḍa jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:m:mahiṣī]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---the queens of the King; [[synonyms:p:pātra]]---ministers; [[synonyms:m:mitra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---friends; [[synonyms:n:nīlācala]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---all the residents of Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---as many; [[synonyms:c:choṭa]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---small and big; [[synonyms:j:jana]]---persons.
translation: This included the King, his queens, his ministers and friends and all other big and small residents of Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.199
description: All the visitors who had come from different countries to Jagannātha Purī, as well as the local devotees, offered their personally cooked food to the Lord.
text:
> nānā-deśera deśī yata yātrika jana
> nija-nija-bhoga tāhāṅ kare samarpaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:d:deśera]]---of various countries; [[synonyms:d:deśī]]---local; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all kinds of; [[synonyms:y:yātrika]]---visiting; [[synonyms:j:jana]]---people; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:n:nija]]---personally cooked; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---food; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:s:samarpaṇa]]---offering.
translation: All the visitors who had come from different countries to Jagannātha Purī, as well as the local devotees, offered their personally cooked food to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.2
description: All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Prabhu Nityānanda! All glories to Advaitacandra! And all glories to the devotees of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!
text:
> jaya jaya śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya nityānanda
> jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jayajaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---to Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---to Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---to Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---to the devotees of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Prabhu Nityānanda! All glories to Advaitacandra! And all glories to the devotees of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.20
description: The decorations included bright mirrors and hundreds and hundreds of cāmaras [white whisks made of yak tails]. On top of the car were a neat and clean canopy and very beautiful flag.
text:
> śata śata su-cāmara-darpaṇe ujjvala
> upare patākā śobhe cāṅdoyā nirmala
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:ś:śata]]---hundreds upon hundreds; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:c:cāmara]]---beautiful white whisks; [[synonyms:d:darpaṇe]]---with mirrors; [[synonyms:u:ujjvala]]---very bright; [[synonyms:u:upare]]---on the top; [[synonyms:p:patākā]]---flag; [[synonyms:ś:śobhe]]---looks beautiful; [[synonyms:c:cāṅdoyā]]---canopy; [[synonyms:n:nirmala]]---thoroughly cleansed.
translation: The decorations included bright mirrors and hundreds and hundreds of cāmaras [white whisks made of yak tails]. On top of the car were a neat and clean canopy and very beautiful flag.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.200
description: The devotees offered their foods everywhere, in front and behind the car, on the two sides and within the flower garden. Wherever possible, they made their offering to the Lord, for there were no hard-and-fast rules.
text:
> āge pāche, dui pārśve puṣpodyāna-vane
> yei yāhā pāya, lāgāya,-nāhika niyame
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āge]] [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---in front or at the end; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:p:pārśve]]---on two sides; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:u:udyāna]]-[[synonyms:v:vane]]---in the flower gardens; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---one who; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets the opportunity; [[synonyms:l:lāgāya]]---offers; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:n:niyame]]---there are no hard-and-fast rules.
translation: The devotees offered their foods everywhere, in front and behind the car, on the two sides and within the flower garden. Wherever possible, they made their offering to the Lord, for there were no hard-and-fast rules.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.201
description: While the food was being offered, a large crowd of people gathered. At that time Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stopped His dancing and went to a nearby garden.
text:
> bhogera samaya lokera mahā bhiḍa haila
> nṛtya chāḍi' mahāprabhu upavane gela
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhogera]] [[synonyms:s:samaya]]---at the time the food was offered; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of all the people; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]---great; [[synonyms:b:bhiḍa]]---crowd; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up His dancing; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:u:upavane]] [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went to a nearby garden.
translation: While the food was being offered, a large crowd of people gathered. At that time Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stopped His dancing and went to a nearby garden.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.202
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to the garden. Immersed in a great ecstatic emotion, He fell flat on a raised platform there.
text:

> puṣpodyāne gṛha-piṇḍāya rahilā paḍiyā

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to the garden. Immersed in a great ecstatic emotion, He fell flat on a raised platform there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.203
description: The Lord was very fatigued from the hard labor of dancing, and there was perspiration all over His body. He therefore enjoyed the fragrant, cool breeze of the garden.
text:
> nṛtya-pariśrame prabhura dehe ghana gharma
> sugandhi śītala-vāyu karena sevana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:p:pariśrame]]---by fatigue due to dancing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dehe]]---on the body; [[synonyms:g:ghana]] [[synonyms:g:gharma]]---much perspiration; [[synonyms:s:sugandhi]]---fragrant; [[synonyms:ś:śītala]]-[[synonyms:v:vāyu]]---cool breeze; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---enjoyed very much.
translation: The Lord was very fatigued from the hard labor of dancing, and there was perspiration all over His body. He therefore enjoyed the fragrant, cool breeze of the garden.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.204
description: All the devotees who were performing saṅkīrtana came there and took rest under each and every tree.

translation: All the devotees who were performing saṅkīrtana came there and took rest under each and every tree.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.205

translation: Thus I have described the great performance of congregational chanting by Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as He danced in front of Lord Jagannātha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.206
description: In his prayer known as the Caitanyāṣṭaka, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī has given a vivid description of the Lord's dancing before the car of Jagannātha.

synonyms: [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:a:agrete]]---in front of the car; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---performed; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dancing; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:a:aṣṭake]]---in the prayer named //Caitanyāṣṭaka//; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:k:karyāche]]---has done; [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---a vivid description.
translation: In his prayer known as the Caitanyāṣṭaka, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī has given a vivid description of the Lord's dancing before the car of Jagannātha.
purport: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī composed three prayers, each with the title //Caitanyāṣṭaka.// The verse next quoted is from the first of the //Caitanyāṣṭaka// prayers included in the book //Stava-mālā.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.207
description: "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced down the main road in great ecstasy before Lord Jagannātha, the master of Nīlācala, who was sitting on His car. Overwhelmed by the transcendental bliss of dancing and surrounded by Vaiṣṇavas who sang the holy names, He manifested waves of ecstatic love of Godhead. When will Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu again be visible to my vision?"
text:
> rathārūḍhasyārād adhipadavi nīlācala-pater
> adabhra-premormi-sphurita-naṭanollāsa-vivaśaḥ
> saharṣaṁ gāyadbhiḥ parivṛta-tanur vaiṣṇava-janaiḥ
> sa caitanyaḥ kiṁ me punar api dṛśor yāsyati padam

translation: "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced down the main road in great ecstasy before Lord Jagannātha, the master of Nīlācala, who was sitting on His car. Overwhelmed by the transcendental bliss of dancing and surrounded by Vaiṣṇavas who sang the holy names, He manifested waves of ecstatic love of Godhead. When will Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu again be visible to my vision?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.208
description: Anyone who hears this description of the car festival will attain Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He will also attain the elevated state by which he will have firm conviction in devotional service and love of Godhead.
text:

> sudṛḍha viśvāsa-saha prema-bhakti haya

translation: Anyone who hears this description of the car festival will attain Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He will also attain the elevated state by which he will have firm conviction in devotional service and love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.209
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation:
Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Thirteenth Chapter, describing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's ecstatic dancing at Lord Jagannātha's car festival.//

> ghāghara, kiṅkiṇī bāje, ghaṇṭāra kvaṇita

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.22

text:
> līlāya caḍila īśvara rathera upara
> āra dui rathe caḍe subhadrā, haladhara

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.23
description: For fifteen days the Lord had remained in a secluded place with the supreme goddess of fortune and had performed His pastimes with her.
text:
> pañca-daśa dina īśvara mahā-lakṣmī lañā
> tāṅra saṅge krīḍā kaila nibhṛte vasiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:d:daśa]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---fifteen days; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---the supreme goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---with; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in her company; [[synonyms:k:krīḍā]]---enjoyment; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:n:nibhṛte]]---in a solitary place; [[synonyms:v:vasiyā]]---sitting.
translation: For fifteen days the Lord had remained in a secluded place with the supreme goddess of fortune and had performed His pastimes with her.
purport: The fifteen-day period of //anavasara// is also called //nibhṛta,// in honor of the solitary place where the supreme goddess of fortune lives. After living there a fortnight, Lord Jagannātha took permission from the goddess of fortune to leave.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.24
description: Having taken permission from the goddess of fortune, the Lord came out to ride on the Ratha car and perform His pastimes for the pleasure of the devotees.
text:
> tāṅhāra sammati lañā bhakte sukha dite
> rathe caḍi' bāhira haila vihāra karite
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:s:sammati]]---her permission; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:s:sukha]] [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to please; [[synonyms:r:rathe]] [[synonyms:c:caḍi']]---riding on the car; [[synonyms:b:bāhira]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---came out; [[synonyms:v:vihāra]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to perform pastimes.
translation: Having taken permission from the goddess of fortune, the Lord came out to ride on the Ratha car and perform His pastimes for the pleasure of the devotees.
purport:
In this connection, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that as an ideal husband, Lord Jagannātha remained fifteen days in a secluded place with His wife, the supreme goddess of fortune. Nonetheless, the Lord wanted to come out of seclusion to give happiness to His devotees. The Lord enjoys Himself in two ways, known as //svakīya// and //parakīya.// The Lord's conjugal love in the //svakīya-rasa// relates to the regulative principles observed in Dvārakā. There the Lord has many married queens, but in Vṛndāvana the conjugal love of the Lord is not with His married wives but with His girl friends, the //gopīs.// Conjugal love with the //gopīs// is called //parakīya-rasa.// Lord Jagannātha leaves the secluded place where He enjoys the company of the supreme goddess of fortune in //svakīya-rasa,// and He goes to Vṛndāvana where He enjoys the //parakīya-rasa.// Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura therefore reminds us that the Lord's pleasure in //parakīya-rasa// is superior to His pleasure in //svakīya-rasa.//

In the material world, //parakīya-rasa,// or loving affairs with unmarried girl friends, is a most degraded relationship, but in the spiritual world this type of loving affair is considered the supreme enjoyment. In the material world everything is but a reflection of the spiritual world, and that reflection is perverted. We cannot understand the affairs of the spiritual world on the basis of our experience in the material world. The Lord's pastimes with the //gopīs// are therefore misunderstood by mundane scholars and word-wranglers. The //parakīya-rasa// of the spiritual world should not be discussed except by one who is very advanced in pure devotional service. The //parakīya-rasa// in the spiritual world and that in the material world are not comparable. The former is like gold, and the latter is like iron. Because the difference between the two is so great, they cannot actually be compared. However, one can easily distinguish the value of gold by seeing the value of iron. One who has the proper realization can easily distinguish the transcendental activities of the spiritual world from material activities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.25
description: The fine, white sand spread all over the path resembled the bank of the Yamunā, and the small gardens on both sides looked just like those in Vṛndāvana.
text:
> sūkṣma śveta-bālu pathe pulinera sama
> dui dike ṭoṭā, saba-yena vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sūkṣma]]---fine; [[synonyms:ś:śveta]]-[[synonyms:b:bālu]]---white sand; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the path; [[synonyms:p:pulinerasama]]---just like the bank of the Yamunā; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:d:dike]]---on two sides; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭoṭā]]---gardens; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---like; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---the holy place Vṛndāvana.
translation: The fine, white sand spread all over the path resembled the bank of the Yamunā, and the small gardens on both sides looked just like those in Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.26
description: As Lord Jagannātha rode in His car and saw the beauty on both sides, His mind was filled with pleasure.
text:
> rathe caḍi' jagannātha karilā gamana
> dui-pārśve dekhi' cale ānandita-mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rathecaḍi']]---riding on the car; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:k:karilāgamana]]---was passing; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:p:pārśve]]---on both sides; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---goes; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---full of pleasure; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind.
translation: As Lord Jagannātha rode in His car and saw the beauty on both sides, His mind was filled with pleasure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.27
description: The pullers of the car were known as gauḍas, and they pulled with great pleasure. However, the car sometimes went very fast and sometimes very slow.
text:
> 'gauḍa' saba ratha ṭāne kariyā ānanda
> kṣaṇe śīghra cale ratha, kṣaṇe cale manda
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]---the pullers of the car; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]---the car; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭāne]]---pull; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---feeling; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---happiness; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]] [[synonyms:c:cale]]---goes very fast; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]---the car; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---goes; [[synonyms:m:manda]]---very slow.
translation: The pullers of the car were known as gauḍas, and they pulled with great pleasure. However, the car sometimes went very fast and sometimes very slow.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.28
description: Sometimes the car would stand still and not move, even though it was pulled very vigorously. The chariot therefore moved by the will of the Lord, not by the strength of any ordinary person.
text:
> kṣaṇe sthira hañā rahe, ṭānileha nā cale
> īśvara-icchāya cale, nā cale kāro bale
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:s:sthira]]---still; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---stays; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭāṅileha]]---in spite of being pulled; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:c:cale]]---does not go; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:i:icchāya]]---by the will of the Lord; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---goes; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:c:cale]]---does not go; [[synonyms:k:kāro]]---of anyone; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---by the strength.
translation: Sometimes the car would stand still and not move, even though it was pulled very vigorously. The chariot therefore moved by the will of the Lord, not by the strength of any ordinary person.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.29
description: As the car stood still, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu gathered all His devotees and, with His own hand, decorated them with flower garlands and sandalwood pulp.
text:
> tabe mahāprabhu saba lañā bhakta-gaṇa
> svahaste parāila sabe mālya-candana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---devotees; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:h:haste]]---by His own hand; [[synonyms:p:parāila]]---decorated; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---everyone; [[synonyms:m:mālya]]-[[synonyms:c:candana]]---with flower garlands and pulp of sandalwood.
translation: As the car stood still, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu gathered all His devotees and, with His own hand, decorated them with flower garlands and sandalwood pulp.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.3
description: All glories to the listeners of Caitanya-caritāmṛta. Please hear the description of the dancing of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu at the Ratha-yātrā festival. His dancing is very enchanting. Please hear of it with great attention.
text:
> jaya śrotā-gaṇa, śuna, kari' eka mana
> ratha-yātrāya nṛtya prabhura parama mohana
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:ś:śrotā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---to the listeners; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---keeping yourself; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---in one attention; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrāya]]---in the car festival; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---extremely; [[synonyms:m:mohana]]---enchanting.
translation: All glories to the listeners of Caitanya-caritāmṛta. Please hear the description of the dancing of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu at the Ratha-yātrā festival. His dancing is very enchanting. Please hear of it with great attention.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.30
description: Paramānanda Purī and Brahmānanda Bhāratī were both personally given garlands and sandalwood pulp from the very hands of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. This increased their transcendental pleasure.
text:
> paramānanda purī, āra bhāratī brahmānanda
> śrī-haste candana pāñā bāḍila ānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paramānanda]] [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:b:bhāratībrahmānanda]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:h:haste]]---by the hand of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood pulp; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:b:bāḍila]]---increased; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---transcendental bliss.
translation: Paramānanda Purī and Brahmānanda Bhāratī were both personally given garlands and sandalwood pulp from the very hands of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. This increased their transcendental pleasure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.31
description: Similarly, when Advaita Ācārya and Nityānanda Prabhu felt the touch of the transcendental hand of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, They were both very pleased.
text:
> advaita-ācārya, āra prabhu-nityānanda
> śrī-hasta-sparśe duṅhāra ha-ila ānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:h:hasta]]-[[synonyms:s:sparśe]]---by the touch of the transcendental hand of Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]]---of both of Them; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---transcendental bliss.
translation: Similarly, when Advaita Ācārya and Nityānanda Prabhu felt the touch of the transcendental hand of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, They were both very pleased.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.32
description: The Lord also gave garlands and sandalwood pulp to the performers of saṅkīrtana. The chief two performers were Svarūpa Dāmodara and Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura.
text:
> kīrtanīyā-gaṇe dila mālya-candana
> svarūpa, śrīvāsa,-yāhāṅ mukhya dui-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kīrtanīyā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---unto the performers of //saṅkīrtana//; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:m:mālya]]-[[synonyms:c:candana]]---garlands and sandalwood pulp; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]---Śrīvāsa; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---principal; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons.
translation: The Lord also gave garlands and sandalwood pulp to the performers of saṅkīrtana. The chief two performers were Svarūpa Dāmodara and Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.33
description: There were altogether four parties of kīrtana performers, comprising twenty-four chanters. In each party there were also two mṛdaṅga players, making an additional eight persons.
text:
> cāri sampradāye haila cabbiśa gāyana
> dui dui mārdaṅgika haila aṣṭa jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:s:sampradāye]]---in the four parties; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there were; [[synonyms:c:cabbiśa]]---twenty-four; [[synonyms:g:gāyana]]---performers of //kīrtana//; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two in each party; [[synonyms:m:mārdaṅgika]]---players of //mṛdaṅga// drums; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there were; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---eight persons.
translation: There were altogether four parties of kīrtana performers, comprising twenty-four chanters. In each party there were also two mṛdaṅga players, making an additional eight persons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.34
description: When the four parties were formed, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, after some consideration, divided the chanters.
text:
> tabe mahāprabhu mane vicāra kariyā
> cāri sampradāya dila gāyana bāṅṭiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---after this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---considering; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:s:sampradāya]]---four parties; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:g:gāyana]] [[synonyms:b:bāṅṭiyā]]---dividing the singers.
translation: When the four parties were formed, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, after some consideration, divided the chanters.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.35
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered Nityānanda Prabhu, Advaita Ācārya, Haridāsa Ṭhākura and Vakreśvara Paṇḍita to dance in each of the four respective parties.
text:
> nityānanda, advaita, haridāsa, vakreśvare
> cāri jane ājñā dila nṛtya karibāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:v:vakreśvare]]---Vakreśvara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:j:jane]]---to these four persons; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---the Lord gave an order; [[synonyms:n:nṛtyakaribāre]]---to dance.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered Nityānanda Prabhu, Advaita Ācārya, Haridāsa Ṭhākura and Vakreśvara Paṇḍita to dance in each of the four respective parties.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.36
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara was chosen as the leader of the first party and was given five assistants to respond to his chanting.
text:
> prathama sampradāye kaila svarūpa-pradhāna
> āra pañca-jana dila tāṅra pāligāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prathamasampradāye]]---in the first party; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---fixed; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---as the chief; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---five persons; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:p:pāligāna]]---responders.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara was chosen as the leader of the first party and was given five assistants to respond to his chanting.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.37
description: The five who responded to the singing of Svarūpa Dāmodara were Dāmodara Paṇḍita, Nārāyaṇa, Govinda Datta, Rāghava Paṇḍita and Śrī Govindānanda.
text:
> dāmodara, nārāyaṇa, datta govinda
> rāghava paṇḍita, āra śrī-govindānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Dāmodara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:d:dattagovinda]]---Govinda Datta; [[synonyms:r:rāghava]] [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---Rāghava Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:g:govindānanda]]---Śrī Govindānanda.
translation: The five who responded to the singing of Svarūpa Dāmodara were Dāmodara Paṇḍita, Nārāyaṇa, Govinda Datta, Rāghava Paṇḍita and Śrī Govindānanda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.38
description: Advaita Ācārya Prabhu was ordered to dance in the first group. The Lord then formed another group with Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura as the chief man.
text:
> advaitere nṛtya karibāre ājñā dila
> śrīvāsa-pradhāna āra sampradāya kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaitere]]---unto Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:k:karibāre]]---for performing; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]---Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---chief; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:s:sampradāya]]---group; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---formed.
translation: Advaita Ācārya Prabhu was ordered to dance in the first group. The Lord then formed another group with Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura as the chief man.
purport: In the first group, Dāmodara Svarūpa was appointed chief singer, and the responding singers were Dāmodara Paṇḍita, Nārāyaṇa, Govinda Datta, Rāghava Paṇḍita and Govindānanda. Śrī Advaita Ācārya was appointed as a dancer. The next group was formed, and the chief singer was Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.39
description: The five singers who responded to the singing of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura were Gaṅgādāsa, Haridāsa, Śrīmān, Śubhānanda and Śrī Rāma Paṇḍita. Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu was appointed as a dancer.
text:
> gaṅgādāsa, haridāsa, śrīmān, śubhānanda
> śrī-rāma paṇḍita, tāhāṅ nāce nityānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gaṅgādāsa]]---Gaṅgādāsa; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa; [[synonyms:ś:śrīmān]]---Śrīmān; [[synonyms:ś:śubhānanda]]---Śubhānanda; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rāma]] [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---Śrī Rāma Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda.
translation: The five singers who responded to the singing of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura were Gaṅgādāsa, Haridāsa, Śrīmān, Śubhānanda and Śrī Rāma Paṇḍita. Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu was appointed as a dancer.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.4
description: The next day, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His personal associates got up in the dark and attentively took their early morning baths.
text:
> āra dina mahāprabhu hañā sāvadhāna
> rātre uṭhi' gaṇa-saṅge kaila prātaḥ-snāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---the next day; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:s:sāvadhāna]]---very careful; [[synonyms:r:rātre]] [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---getting up at night; [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with His personal devotees; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---took; [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing early in the morning.
translation: The next day, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His personal associates got up in the dark and attentively took their early morning baths.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.40
description: Another group was formed consisting of Vāsudeva, Gopīnātha, and Murāri. All these were responsive singers, and Mukunda was the chief singer.
text:
> vāsudeva, gopīnātha, murāri yāhāṅ gāya
> mukunda-pradhāna kaila āra sampradāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]---Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]---Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:m:murāri]]---Murāri; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sing; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---chief; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---formed; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:s:sampradāya]]---group.
translation: Another group was formed consisting of Vāsudeva, Gopīnātha, and Murāri. All these were responsive singers, and Mukunda was the chief singer.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.41
description: Another two persons, Śrīkānta and Vallabha Sena, joined as responsive singers. In this group, Haridāsa Ṭhākura [the senior] was the dancer.
text:
> śrīkānta, vallabha-sena āra dui jana
> haridāsa-ṭhākura tāhāṅ karena nartana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrīkānta,]] [[synonyms:v:vallabha]]-[[synonyms:s:sena]]---Śrīkānta and Vallabha Sena; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---performs; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dancing.
translation: Another two persons, Śrīkānta and Vallabha Sena, joined as responsive singers. In this group, Haridāsa Ṭhākura [the senior] was the dancer.
purport: In the third group, Mukunda was appointed the chief singer. This party was composed of Vāsudeva, Gopīnātha, Murāri, Śrīkānta and Vallabha Sena. The senior Haridāsa Ṭhākura was the dancer.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.42
description: The Lord formed another group, appointing Govinda Ghosh as leader. In this group the younger Haridāsa, Viṣṇudāsa and Rāghava were the responding singers.
text:
> govinda-ghoṣa-pradhāna kaila āra sampradāya
> haridāsa, viṣṇudāsa, rāghava, yāhāṅ gāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:g:ghoṣa]]---Govinda Ghosh; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---the chief; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---formed; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:s:sampradāya]]---group; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---the younger Haridāsa; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇudāsa]]---Viṣṇudāsa; [[synonyms:r:rāghava]]---Rāghava; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sing.
translation: The Lord formed another group, appointing Govinda Ghosh as leader. In this group the younger Haridāsa, Viṣṇudāsa and Rāghava were the responding singers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.43
description: Two brothers named Mādhava Ghosh and Vāsudeva Ghosh also joined this group as responsive singers. Vakreśvara Paṇḍita was the dancer.
text:
> mādhava, vāsudeva-ghoṣa,-dui sahodara
> nṛtya karena tāhāṅ paṇḍita-vakreśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]---Mādhava; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]-[[synonyms:g:ghoṣa]]---Vāsudeva Ghosh; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:s:sahodara]]---two brothers; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:karena]]---dances; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]-[[synonyms:v:vakreśvara]]---Vakreśvara Paṇḍita.
translation: Two brothers named Mādhava Ghosh and Vāsudeva Ghosh also joined this group as responsive singers. Vakreśvara Paṇḍita was the dancer.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.44
description: There was a saṅkīrtana party from the village known as Kulīna-grāma, and Rāmānanda and Satyarāja were appointed the dancers in this group.
text:
> kulīna-grāmera eka kīrtanīyā-samāja
> tāhāṅ nṛtya karena rāmānanda, satyarāja
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kulīna]]-[[synonyms:g:grāmera]]---of the village known as Kulīna-grāma; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:k:kīrtanīyā]]-[[synonyms:s:samāja]]---//saṅkīrtana// party; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:karena]]---dances; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda; [[synonyms:s:satyarāja]]---Satyarāja Khān.
translation: There was a saṅkīrtana party from the village known as Kulīna-grāma, and Rāmānanda and Satyarāja were appointed the dancers in this group.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.45
description: There was another party that came from Śāntipura and was formed by Advaita Ācārya. Acyutānanda was the dancer, and the rest of the men were singers.
text:
> śāntipurera ācāryera eka sampradāya
> acyutānanda nāce tathā, āra saba gāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śāntipurera]]---of Śāntipura; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]]---of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:s:sampradāya]]---group; [[synonyms:a:acyutānanda]]---the son of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---there; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---the rest; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---were singing.
translation: There was another party that came from Śāntipura and was formed by Advaita Ācārya. Acyutānanda was the dancer, and the rest of the men were singers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.46
description: Another party was formed by the people of Khaṇḍa. These people were singing in a different place. In that group, Narahari Prabhu and Raghunandana were dancing.
text:
> khaṇḍera sampradāya kare anyatra kīrtana
> narahari nāce tāhāṅ śrī-raghunandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍera]]---of the place named Khaṇḍa; [[synonyms:s:sampradāya]]---party; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:a:anyatra]]---in a different place; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---chanting; [[synonyms:n:narahari]]---Narahari; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:raghunandana]]---Raghunandana.
translation: Another party was formed by the people of Khaṇḍa. These people were singing in a different place. In that group, Narahari Prabhu and Raghunandana were dancing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.47
description: Four parties chanted and danced in front of Lord Jagannātha, and on both sides were two other parties. Another was at the rear.
text:
> jagannāthera āge cāri sampradāya gāya
> dui pāśe dui, pāche eka sampradāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannāthera]] [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of the Deity Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:s:sampradāya]] [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---four groups were chanting; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:p:pāśe]]---on two sides; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---another two groups; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---at the rear; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:s:sampradāya]]---another group.
translation: Four parties chanted and danced in front of Lord Jagannātha, and on both sides were two other parties. Another was at the rear.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.48
description: There were altogether seven parties of saṅkīrtana, and in each party two men were beating drums. Thus fourteen drums were being played at once. The sound was tumultuous, and all the devotees became mad.
text:
> sāta sampradāye bāje caudda mādala
> yāra dhvani śuni' vaiṣṇava haila pāgala
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sāta]] [[synonyms:s:sampradāye]]---in seven groups; [[synonyms:b:bāje]]---were beating; [[synonyms:c:caudda]]---fourteen; [[synonyms:m:mādala]]---drums; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---the sound; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:p:pāgala]]---mad.
translation: There were altogether seven parties of saṅkīrtana, and in each party two men were beating drums. Thus fourteen drums were being played at once. The sound was tumultuous, and all the devotees became mad.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.49
description: All the Vaiṣṇavas came together like an assembly of clouds. As the devotees chanted the holy names, tears fell in great ecstasy like rainfall from their eyes.
text:
> vaiṣṇavera megha-ghaṭāya ha-ila bādala
> kīrtanānande saba varṣe netra-jala
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:m:megha]]-[[synonyms:g:ghaṭāya]]---by the assembly of clouds; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:b:bādala]]---rainfall; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in the blissful situation of chanting; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of them; [[synonyms:v:varṣe]]---rain; [[synonyms:n:netra]]-[[synonyms:j:jala]]---tears from the eyes.
translation: All the Vaiṣṇavas came together like an assembly of clouds. As the devotees chanted the holy names, tears fell in great ecstasy like rainfall from their eyes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.5
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His personal associates then went to see the ceremony of Pāṇḍu-vijaya. During this ceremony, Lord Jagannātha leaves His throne and gets up onto the car.
text:
> pāṇḍu-vijaya dekhibāre karila gamana
> jagannātha yātrā kaila chāḍi' siṁhāsana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāṇḍu]]-[[synonyms:v:vijaya]]---the ceremony named Pāṇḍu-vijaya; [[synonyms:d:dekhibāre]]---for seeing; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---go; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---departure; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---leaving; [[synonyms:s:siṁhāsana]]---the throne.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His personal associates then went to see the ceremony of Pāṇḍu-vijaya. During this ceremony, Lord Jagannātha leaves His throne and gets up onto the car.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.50
description: When the saṅkīrtana resounded, it filled the three worlds. Indeed, no one could hear mundane sounds or musical instruments other than the saṅkīrtana.
text:
> tri-bhuvana bhari' uṭhe kīrtanera dhvani
> anya vādyādira dhvani kichui nā śuni
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvana]] [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---filling the three worlds; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---arose; [[synonyms:k:kīrtanera]] [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---vibration of saṅkīrtana; [[synonyms:a:anya]]---other; [[synonyms:v:vādya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādira]]---of musical instruments; [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---the sound; [[synonyms:k:kichui]]---anything; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---hears.
translation: When the saṅkīrtana resounded, it filled the three worlds. Indeed, no one could hear mundane sounds or musical instruments other than the saṅkīrtana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.51
description: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu wandered through all seven groups chanting the holy name, "Hari, Hari!" Raising His arms, He shouted, "All glories to Lord Jagannātha!"
text:
> sāta ṭhāñi bule prabhu 'hari' 'hari' bali'
> 'jaya jagannātha', balena hasta-yuga tuli'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sāta]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---in the seven places; [[synonyms:b:bule]]---wanders; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---chanting the holy names Hari, Hari; [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---all glories to Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:b:balena]]---says; [[synonyms:h:hasta]]-[[synonyms:y:yuga]]---His two arms; [[synonyms:t:tuli']]---raising.
translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu wandered through all seven groups chanting the holy name, "Hari, Hari!" Raising His arms, He shouted, "All glories to Lord Jagannātha!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.52
description: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu then exhibited another mystic power by performing pastimes simultaneously in all seven groups.
text:
> āra eka śakti prabhu karila prakāśa
> eka-kāle sāta ṭhāñi karila vilāsa

translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu then exhibited another mystic power by performing pastimes simultaneously in all seven groups.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.53
description: Everyone said, "Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu is present in my group. Indeed, He does not go anywhere else. He is bestowing His mercy upon us."
text:

> anya ṭhāñi nāhi yā'na āmāre dayāya

translation: Everyone said, "Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu is present in my group. Indeed, He does not go anywhere else. He is bestowing His mercy upon us."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.54
description: Actually, no one could see the inconceivable potency of the Lord. Only the most confidential devotees, those in pure, unalloyed devotional service, could understand.
text:

> antaraṅga-bhakta jāne, yāṅra śuddha-bhakti

translation: Actually, no one could see the inconceivable potency of the Lord. Only the most confidential devotees, those in pure, unalloyed devotional service, could understand.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.55
description: Lord Jagannātha was very pleased by the saṅkīrtana, and He brought His car to a standstill just to see the performance.
text:
> kīrtana dekhiyā jagannātha haraṣita
> saṅkīrtana dekhe ratha kariyā sthagita

translation: Lord Jagannātha was very pleased by the saṅkīrtana, and He brought His car to a standstill just to see the performance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.56
description: King Pratāparudra also was astonished to see the saṅkīrtana. He became inactive and was converted to ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa.
text:

translation: King Pratāparudra also was astonished to see the saṅkīrtana. He became inactive and was converted to ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.57
description: When the King informed Kāśī Miśra of the glories of the Lord, Kāśī Miśra replied, "O King, your fortune has no limit!"
text:
> kāśī-miśre kahe rājā prabhura mahimā
> kāśī-miśra kahe,-tomāra bhāgyera nāhi sīmā

translation: When the King informed Kāśī Miśra of the glories of the Lord, Kāśī Miśra replied, "O King, your fortune has no limit!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.58
description: The King and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya were both aware of the Lord's activities, but no one else could see the tricks of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

translation: The King and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya were both aware of the Lord's activities, but no one else could see the tricks of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.59
description: Only a person who has received the mercy of the Lord can understand. Without the Lord's mercy, even the demigods, headed by Lord Brahmā, cannot understand.

> yāre tāṅra kṛpā, sei jānibāre pāre
> kṛpā vinā brahmādika jānibāre nāre

translation: Only a person who has received the mercy of the Lord can understand. Without the Lord's mercy, even the demigods, headed by Lord Brahmā, cannot understand.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.6
description: King Pratāparudra in person, as well as his entourage, allowed the Pāṇḍu-vijaya ceremony to be seen by all the associates of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> āpani pratāparudra lañā pātra-gaṇa
> mahāprabhura gaṇe karāya vijaya-darśana

translation: King Pratāparudra in person, as well as his entourage, allowed the Pāṇḍu-vijaya ceremony to be seen by all the associates of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.60
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very satisfied to see the King accept the menial task of sweeping the street, and for this humility, the King received the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He could therefore observe the mystery of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities.
text:
> rājāra tuccha sevā dekhi' prabhura tuṣṭa mana
> sei ta' prasāde pāila 'rahasya-darśana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājāra]]---of the King; [[synonyms:t:tuccha]]---insignificant, menial; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---service; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tuṣṭa]]---satisfied; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:p:prasāde]]---by mercy; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got; [[synonyms:r:rahasya]]-[[synonyms:d:darśana]]---seeing of the mystery of the activities.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very satisfied to see the King accept the menial task of sweeping the street, and for this humility, the King received the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He could therefore observe the mystery of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities.
purport: The mystery of the Lord's activities is described by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura. Lord Jagannātha was astonished to see the transcendental dancing and chanting of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and He stopped His car just to see the dancing. Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu then danced in such a mystical way that He pleased Lord Jagannātha. The seer and the dancer were one and the same Supreme Person, but the Lord, being one and many at the same time, was exhibiting the variegatedness of His pastimes. This is the meaning behind His mysterious exhibition. By the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the King could understand how both of Them were enjoying each other's activities. Another mysterious exhibition was Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's simultaneous presence in seven groups. By the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the King could understand that also.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.61
description: Although the King was refused an interview, he was indirectly bestowed causeless mercy. Who can understand the internal potency of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu?
text:
> sākṣāte nā deya dekhā, parokṣe ta' dayā
> ke bujhite pāre caitanya-candrera māyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sākṣāte]]---directiy; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:d:deya]]---gives; [[synonyms:d:dekhā]]---interview; [[synonyms:p:parokṣe]]---indirectly; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]---there was mercy; [[synonyms:k:ke]]---who; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand; [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---is able; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:candrera]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---internal potency.
translation: Although the King was refused an interview, he was indirectly bestowed causeless mercy. Who can understand the internal potency of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu?
purport: As Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was playing the part of a world teacher, He did not agree to see the King because a king is a mundane person interested in money and women. Indeed, the very name "king" suggests one who is always surrounded by money and women. As a //sannyāsī,// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was afraid of both money and women. The very word "king" is repugnant to one who is in the renounced order of life. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu refused to see the King, but indirectly, by the Lord's causeless mercy, the King was able to understand the Lord's mysterious activities. Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities were exhibited sometimes to reveal Him as the Supreme Personality of Godhead and sometimes to show Him as a devotee. Both kinds of activity are mysterious and appreciated only by pure devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.62
description: When the two great personalities Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Kāśī Miśra saw Caitanya Mahāprabhu's causeless mercy upon the King, they were astonished.
text:
> sārvabhauma, kāśī-miśra,-dui mahāśaya
> rājāre prasāda dekhi' ha-ilā vismaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kāśī]]-[[synonyms:m:miśra]]---Kāśī Miśra; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:m:mahāśaya]]---two great personalities; [[synonyms:r:rājāre]]---unto the King; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---mercy; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vismaya]]---astonished.
translation: When the two great personalities Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Kāśī Miśra saw Caitanya Mahāprabhu's causeless mercy upon the King, they were astonished.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.63
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed His pastimes for some time in this way. He personally sang and induced His personal associates to dance.
text:
> ei-mata līlā prabhu kaila kata-kṣaṇa
> āpane gāyena, nācā'na nija-bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:k:kata]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇa]]---for some time; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]] [[synonyms:g:gāyena]]---personally sings; [[synonyms:n:nācā'na]]---made to dance; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---His own personal devotees.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed His pastimes for some time in this way. He personally sang and induced His personal associates to dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.64

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.65
description: Indeed, the Personality of Godhead forgot Himself in the course of His transcendental pastimes, but His internal potency [līlā-śakti], knowing the intentions of the Lord, made all arrangements.
text:
> līlāveśe prabhura nāhi nijānusandhāna
> icchā jāni 'līlā śakti' kare samādhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in the ecstasy of transcendental pastimes; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there was not; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:a:anusandhāna]]---understanding about His personal self; [[synonyms:i:icchā]] [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---knowing His desire; [[synonyms:l:līlā]] [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---the potency known as //līlā-śakti//; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:s:samādhāna]]---all arrangements.
translation: Indeed, the Personality of Godhead forgot Himself in the course of His transcendental pastimes, but His internal potency [līlā-śakti], knowing the intentions of the Lord, made all arrangements.
purport:
It is stated in the //Upaniṣads://

> parāsya śaktir vividhaiva śrūyate
> svābhāvikī jñāna-bala-kriyā ca

"The Supreme Lord has multi-potencies which act so perfectly that all consciousness, strength and activity are being directed solely by His will." (//Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad// 6.8)

Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu exhibited His mystic power in presenting Himself simultaneously in each and every //saṅkīrtana// group. Most people thought that He was one, but some saw that He was many. The internal devotees could understand that the Lord, although one, was exhibiting Himself as many in the different //saṅkīrtana// groups. When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced, He forgot Himself and was simply absorbed in ecstatic bliss. However, His internal potency arranged everything perfectly. This is the difference between the internal and external potency. In the material world, the external potency (material energy) can act only after one endeavors at great length, but when the Supreme Lord desires, everything is performed automatically by the internal potency. By His will, things happen so nicely and perfectly that they appear to be carried out automatically. Sometimes the activities of the internal potency are exhibited in the material world. In fact, all the activities of material nature are actually performed by the inconceivable energies of the Lord, but so-called scientists and students of material nature are unable to understand ultimately how things are happening. They evasively conclude that everything is being done by nature, but they do not know that behind nature is the potent Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is explained in //Bhagavad-gītā://

> mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ
> sūyate sa-carācaram
> hetunānena kaunteya
> jagad viparivartate

"This material nature is working under My direction, O son of Kuntī, and it is producing all moving and unmoving beings. By its rule this manifestation is created and annihilated again and again." [[books:bg:9:10|(Bg. 9.10)]]

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.67
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's dancing before the Ratha-yātrā car could be perceived only by pure devotees. Others could not understand. Descriptions of Lord Kṛṣṇa's uncommon dancing can be found in the revealed scripture Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.
text:
> bhakta-gaṇa anubhave, nāhi jāne āna
> śrī-bhāgavata-śāstra tāhāte pramāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all devotees; [[synonyms:a:anubhave]]---could perceive; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---do not know; [[synonyms:ā:āna]]---others; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---the revealed scripture //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:t:tāhāte]]---in that connection; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---evidence.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's dancing before the Ratha-yātrā car could be perceived only by pure devotees. Others could not understand. Descriptions of Lord Kṛṣṇa's uncommon dancing can be found in the revealed scripture Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.
purport: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa expanded Himself into many forms while engaged in the //rāsa-līlā// dance, and He also expanded Himself when He married 16,000 wives in Dvārakā. The same process was adopted by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu when He expanded Himself into seven forms to dance in each and every group of the //saṅkīrtana// party. These expansions were appreciated by pure devotees, including King Pratāparudra. Although for reasons of external formality Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu refused to see King Pratāparudra because he was a king, King Pratāparudra became one of the Lord's most confidential devotees by the Lord's special mercy upon Him. The King could see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu simultaneously present in all seven groups. As confirmed in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// one cannot see the expansions of the transcendental forms of the Lord unless one is a pure devotee of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.79
description: " 'Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is He who is known as jana-nivāsa, the ultimate resort of all living entities, and who is also known as Devakī-nandana or Yaśodā-nandana, the son of Devakī and Yaśodā. He is the guide of the Yadu dynasty, and with His mighty arms He kills everything inauspicious as well as every man who is impious. By His presence He destroys all things inauspicious for all living entities, moving and inert. His blissful smiling face always increases the lusty desires of the gopīs of Vṛndāvana. May He be all glorious and happy!'

synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jayati]]---eternally lives gloriously; [[synonyms:j:jana]]-[[synonyms:n:nivāsaḥ]]---He who lives among human beings like the members of the Yadu dynasty and is the ultimate resort of all living entities; [[synonyms:d:devakī]]-[[synonyms:j:janma]]-[[synonyms:v:vādaḥ]]---known as the son of Devakī (No one can actually become the father or mother of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore //devakī-janma-vāda// means that He is known as the son of Devakī. Similarly, He is also known as the son of mother Yaśodā, Vasudeva or Nanda Mahārāja.); [[synonyms:y:yadu]]-[[synonyms:v:vara]]-[[synonyms:p:pariṣat]]---served by the members of the Yadu dynasty or the cowherd men of Vṛndāvana (all of whom are constant associates of the Supreme Lord and are the Lord's eternal servants); [[synonyms:s:svaiḥ]] [[synonyms:d:dorbhiḥ]]---by His own arms, or by His devotees like Arjuna who are just like His own arms; [[synonyms:a:asyan]]---killing; [[synonyms:a:adharmam]]---demons or the impious; [[synonyms:s:sthira]]-[[synonyms:c:cara]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛjina]]-[[synonyms:g:ghnaḥ]]---the destroyer of all the ill fortune of all living entities, moving and not moving; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:s:smita]]---always smiling; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhena]]---by His beautiful face; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:p:pura]]-[[synonyms:v:vanitānām]]---of the damsels of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:v:vardhayan]]---increasing; [[synonyms:k:kāma]]-[[synonyms:d:devam]]---the lusty desires.
translation: “ 'Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is He who is known as jana-nivāsa, the ultimate resort of all living entities, and who is also known as Devakī-nandana or Yaśodā-nandana, the son of Devakī and Yaśodā. He is the guide of the Yadu dynasty, and with His mighty arms He kills everything inauspicious as well as every man who is impious. By His presence He destroys all things inauspicious for all living entities, moving and inert. His blissful smiling face always increases the lusty desires of the gopīs of Vṛndāvana. May He be all glorious and happy!'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.90.48).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.8
description: The very strongly built dayitās [carriers of the Jagannātha Deity] were as powerful as drunken elephants. They manually carried Lord Jagannātha from the throne to the car.
text:
> baliṣṭha dayitā' gaṇa-yena matta hātī
> jagannātha vijaya karāya kari' hātāhāti
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:baliṣṭha]] [[synonyms:d:dayitā']] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---very strong //dayitās,// or carriers of Jagannātha; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:m:matta]] [[synonyms:h:hātī]]---drunken elephants; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:v:vijaya]]---departure; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---cause; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---performing; [[synonyms:h:hātāhāti]]---hand to hand.
translation: The very strongly built dayitās [carriers of the Jagannātha Deity] were as powerful as drunken elephants. They manually carried Lord Jagannātha from the throne to the car.
purport: The word //dayitā// refers to one who has received the mercy of the Lord. Lord Jagannātha has a number of stalwart servants known as //dayitās.// These servants do not come from very high-caste families (//brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas// or //vaiśyas//), but because they are engaged in the service of the Lord, they have been elevated to a respected position. Thus they are known as //dayitās.// These servants of Lord Jagannātha take care of the Lord from the day of the Snāna-yātrā up to the time the Lord is carried from the throne to the Ratha car. In the //Kṣetra-māhātmya// these //dayitās// are said to come from the //śabaras,// a caste that keeps and sells pigs. However, among the //dayitās// there are also many who come from the //brāhmaṇa// caste. Those //dayitās// coming from the //brāhmaṇa// families are called //dayitā-patis,// or leaders of the //dayitās. The dayitā-patis// offer food such as sweetmeats to Lord Jagannātha during the //anavasara,// the resting period after Snāna-yātrā. They also make the early morning offering of sweetmeats daily, It is said that during the //anavasara// Lord Jagannātha suffers from fever and that the //dayitā-patis// offer Him an infusion of drugs represented by fruit juice. It is said that in the beginning Lord Jagannātha was worshiped by the //śabaras// and was known as the Deity Nīla Mādhava. Later, when the Deity was established in the temple, the Lord became known as Jagannātha. Because the Deities were taken from the //śabaras,// all the //śabara// devotees were elevated to the position of //dayitās.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.80
description: " 'I am not a brāhmaṇa, I am not a kṣatriya, I am not a vaiśya or a śūdra. Nor am I a brahmacārī, a householder, a vānaprastha or a sannyāsī. I identify Myself only as the servant of the servant of the servant of the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the maintainer of the gopīs. He is like an ocean of nectar, and He is the cause of universal transcendental bliss. He is always existing with brilliance.' "
text:
> nāhaṁ vipro na ca nara-patir nāpi vaiśyo na śūdro
> nāhaṁ varṇī na ca gṛha-patir no vanastho yatir vā
> kintu prodyan-nikhila-paramānanda-pūrnāmṛtābdher
> gopī-bhartuḥ pada-kamalayor dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:v:vipraḥ]]---a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:n:nara]]-[[synonyms:p:patiḥ]]---a king or //kṣatriya//; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:v:vaiśyaḥ]]---belonging to the mercantile class; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:ś:śūdraḥ]]---belonging to the worker class; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:v:varṇī]]---belonging to any caste, or //brahmacārī// (A //brahmacārī// may belong to any caste. Anyone can become a //brahmacārī// or lead a life of celibacy.); [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:g:gṛha]]-[[synonyms:p:patiḥ]]---householder; [[synonyms:n:no]]---not; [[synonyms:v:vana]]-[[synonyms:s:sthaḥ]]---//vānaprastha,// one who, after retirement from family life, goes to the forest to learn how to be detached from family life; [[synonyms:y:yatiḥ]]---mendicant or renunciant; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---either; [[synonyms:k:kintu]]---but; [[synonyms:p:prodyan]]---brilliant; [[synonyms:n:nikhila]]---universal; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---with transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---complete; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:abdheḥ]]---who is the ocean of nectar; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhartuḥ]]---of the Supreme Person, who is the maintainer of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:k:kamalayoḥ]]---of the two lotus feet; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---of the servant; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:a:anudāsaḥ]]---the servant of the servant.
translation: “ 'I am not a brāhmaṇa, I am not a kṣatriya, I am not a vaiśya or a śūdra. Nor am I a brahmacārī, a householder, a vānaprastha or a sannyāsī. I identify Myself only as the servant of the servant of the servant of the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the maintainer of the gopīs. He is like an ocean of nectar, and He is the cause of universal transcendental bliss. He is always existing with brilliance.' "
purport: This verse is found in the //Padyāvalī// (74).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.81
description: Having recited all these verses from scripture, the Lord again offered His obeisances, and all the devotees, with folded hands, also offered prayers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> eta paḍi' punarapi karila praṇāma
> yoḍa-hāte bhakta-gaṇa vande bhagavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting these; [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---the Lord offered; [[synonyms:p:praṇāma]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:y:yoḍa]]-[[synonyms:h:hāte]]---with folded hands; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:v:vande]]---offer prayer; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: Having recited all these verses from scripture, the Lord again offered His obeisances, and all the devotees, with folded hands, also offered prayers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.82
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced and jumped high, roaring like thunder and moving in a circle like a wheel, He appeared like a circling firebrand.
text:
> uddaṇḍa nṛtya prabhu kariyā huṅkāra
> cakra-bhrami bhrame yaiche alāta-ākāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uddaṇḍa]]---jumping; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---making; [[synonyms:h:huṅkāra]]---loud vibration; [[synonyms:c:cakra]]-[[synonyms:b:bhrami]]---making a circular movement like a wheel; [[synonyms:b:bhrame]]---moves; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as if; [[synonyms:a:alāta]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---circle of fire.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced and jumped high, roaring like thunder and moving in a circle like a wheel, He appeared like a circling firebrand.
purport: If a burning cinder of a firebrand is whirled about very swiftly, it gives the appearance of a circle of fire. This is called //alāta-ākāra,// or a firebrand circle. This whole circle is not actually made of fire but is a single fire in motion. Similarly, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is a single personality, but when He danced and jumped high in a circle, He appeared like the //alāta-cakra.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.83
description: Wherever Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stepped while dancing, the whole earth, with its hills and seas, appeared to tilt.
text:
> nṛtye prabhura yāhāṅ yāṅhā paḍe pada-tala
> sasāgara-śaila mahī kare ṭalamala

translation: Wherever Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stepped while dancing, the whole earth, with its hills and seas, appeared to tilt.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.84
description: When Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced, He displayed various blissful transcendental changes in His body. Sometimes He appeared as though stunned. Sometimes the hairs of His body stood on end. Sometimes He perspired, cried, trembled and changed color, and sometimes He exhibited symptoms of helplessness, pride, exuberance and humility.
text:
> stambha, sveda, pulaka, aśru, kampa, vaivarṇya
> nānā-bhāve vivaśatā, garva, harṣa, dainya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:stambha]]---being stunned; [[synonyms:s:sveda]]---perspiration; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]---jubilation; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:v:vaivarṇya]]---change of color; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in various ways; [[synonyms:v:vivaśatā]]---helplessness; [[synonyms:g:garva]]---pride; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---exuberation; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]---humility.
translation: When Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced, He displayed various blissful transcendental changes in His body. Sometimes He appeared as though stunned. Sometimes the hairs of His body stood on end. Sometimes He perspired, cried, trembled and changed color, and sometimes He exhibited symptoms of helplessness, pride, exuberance and humility.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.85
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell down with a crash while dancing, He would roll on the ground. At such times it appeared that a golden mountain was rolling on the ground.
text:
> āchāḍa khāñā paḍe bhūme gaḍi' yāya
> suvarṇa-parvata yaiche bhūmete loṭāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āchāḍa]] [[synonyms:k:khāñā]]---crashing; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---falls; [[synonyms:b:bhūme]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:g:gaḍi']]---rolling; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes; [[synonyms:s:suvarṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:parvata]]---a golden mountain; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as if; [[synonyms:b:bhūmete]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:l:loṭāya]]---rolls.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell down with a crash while dancing, He would roll on the ground. At such times it appeared that a golden mountain was rolling on the ground.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.86
description: Nityānanda Prabhu would stretch out His two hands and try to catch the Lord when He was running here and there.
text:

> prabhure dharite cāhe āśa-pāśa dhāñā

translation: Nityānanda Prabhu would stretch out His two hands and try to catch the Lord when He was running here and there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.87
description: Advaita Ācārya would walk behind the Lord and loudly chant "Hari bol! Hari bol!" again and again.
text:

translation: Advaita Ācārya would walk behind the Lord and loudly chant "Hari bol! Hari bol!" again and again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.88
description: Just to check the crowds from coming too near the Lord, they formed three circles. The first circle was guided by Nityānanda Prabhu, who is Balarāma Himself, the possessor of great strength.
text:

> prathama-maṇḍale nityānanda mahā-bala

translation: Just to check the crowds from coming too near the Lord, they formed three circles. The first circle was guided by Nityānanda Prabhu, who is Balarāma Himself, the possessor of great strength.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.89

text:

> hātāhāti kari' haila dvitīya āvaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāśīśvara]]---Kāśīśvara; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by Govinda; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---devotees; [[synonyms:h:hātāhāti]]---linked hand to hand; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]]---a second; [[synonyms:ā:āvaraṇa]]---covering circle.
translation: All the devotees headed by Kāśīśvara and Govinda linked hands and formed a second circle around the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.9
description: While carrying the Deity of Lord Jagannātha, some of the dayitās took hold of the shoulders of the Lord, and some caught His lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.90

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.91
description: With his hands on the shoulders of Haricandana, King Pratāparudra could see Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu dancing, and the King felt great ecstasy.
text:

translation: With his hands on the shoulders of Haricandana, King Pratāparudra could see Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu dancing, and the King felt great ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.92
description: While the King beheld the dancing, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, standing in front of him, became ecstatic as he saw the dancing of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

translation: While the King beheld the dancing, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, standing in front of him, became ecstatic as he saw the dancing of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 13.93
description: Seeing Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura standing before the King, Haricandana touched Śrīvāsa with his hand and requested him to step aside.
text:

> haste tāṅre sparśi' kahe,-hao eka-pāśa
