title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.156
description: "Kṛṣṇa is full of ecstatic love and always subordinate to the love of his devotees. The gopīs are very experienced in pure love and in the dealings of transcendental mellows.
text:
> premamaya-vapu kṛṣṇa bhakta-premādhīna
> śuddha-preme, rasa-guṇe, gopikā-pravīṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]-[[synonyms:v:vapu]]---body of love and ecstasy; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:a:adhīna]]---always subordinate to the loving feelings of His devotees; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:p:preme]]---in pure uncontaminated love; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---and in the qualities of transcendental mellows; [[synonyms:g:gopikā]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:p:pravīṇa]]---very experienced.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa is full of ecstatic love and always subordinate to the love of his devotees. The gopīs are very experienced in pure love and in the dealings of transcendental mellows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.157
description: "There is no flaw or adulteration in the love of the gopīs; therefore they give Kṛṣṇa the highest pleasure.
text:
> gopikāra preme nāhi rasābhāsa-doṣa
> ataeva kṛṣṇera kare parama santoṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopikāra]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in the loving affairs; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāsa]]---of an adulterated taste of mellow; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---fault; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---they do; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---highest satisfaction.
translation: "There is no flaw or adulteration in the love of the gopīs; therefore they give Kṛṣṇa the highest pleasure.
purport:
//Rasābhāsa// occurs when one's relationship with Kṛṣṇa is adulterated. There are different types of //rasābhāsa//-first-, second-and third-class. The word //rāsa// means "mellow," and //ābhāsa// means "a shadow." If one tastes one kind of mellow and something extra is imposed, that is //uparasa.// If something is derived from the original mellow, it is called //anurasa.// If something is appreciated that is far removed from the original mellow, it is called //aparasa. Uparasa, anurasa// and //aparasa// are, respectively, first-, second-and third-class //rasābhāsas.// As stated in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (4.9):

> pūrvam evānuśiṣṭena vikalā rasa-lakṣaṇā
> rasā eva rasābhāsā rasa-jñair anukīrtitāḥ
> syus tridhoparasāś cānurasāś cāparasāś ca te
> uttamā madhyamāḥ proktāḥ kaniṣṭhāś cety amī kramāt

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.158
description: " 'Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is the Absolute Truth, enjoyed His rāsa dance every night during the autumn season. He performed this dance in the moonlight and with full transcendental mellows. He used poetic words and surrounded Himself with women who were very much attracted to Him.'
text:
> evaṁ śaśaṅkāṁśu-virājitā niśāḥ
> sa satya-kāmo 'nuratābalā-gaṇaḥ
> siṣeva ātmany avaruddha-saurataḥ
> sarvāḥ śarat-kāvya-kathā-rasāśrayāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:evam]]---thus; [[synonyms:ś:śaśaṅka]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁśu]]---with rays of moonshine; [[synonyms:v:virājitāḥ]]---beautifully existing; [[synonyms:n:niśāḥ]]---nights; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:s:satya]]-[[synonyms:k:kāmaḥ]]---the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:a:anurata]]---to whom are attracted; [[synonyms:a:abalā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇaḥ]]---women; [[synonyms:s:siṣeva]]---performed; [[synonyms:ā:ātmani]]---in His own self; [[synonyms:a:avaruddha]]-[[synonyms:s:saurataḥ]]---His transcendental erotic love was checked; [[synonyms:s:sarvāḥ]]---all; [[synonyms:ś:śarat]]---in autumn; [[synonyms:k:kāvya]]---poetic; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---words; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśrayāḥ]]---full of all transcendental mellows.
translation: “ 'Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is the Absolute Truth, enjoyed His rāsa dance every night during the autumn season. He performed this dance in the moonlight and with full transcendental mellows. He used poetic words and surrounded Himself with women who were very much attracted to Him.'
purport: This verse is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.33.25). The //gopīs// are all transcendental spirit souls. One should never think that the //gopīs// and Kṛṣṇa have material bodies. Vṛndāvana-dhāma is also a spiritual abode, and there the days and nights, the trees, flowers, water and everything else are spiritual. There is not even a trace of material contamination. Kṛṣṇa, who is the Supreme Brahman and Supersoul, is not at all interested in anything material. His activities with the //gopīs// are all spiritual and take place within the spiritual world. They have nothing to do with the material world. Lord Kṛṣṇa's lusty desires and ail His dealings with the //gopīs// are on the spiritual platform. One has to be transcendentally realized before even considering relishing the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa with the //gopīs.// One who is on the mundane platform must first purify himself by following the regulative principles. Only then can he try to understand Kṛṣṇa and the //gopīs.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī are here talking about the relationship between Kṛṣṇa and the //gopīs:// therefore the subject matter is neither mundane nor erotic. Being a //sannyāsī,// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very strict in His dealings with women. Unless the //gopīs// were on the spiritual platform, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would have never even mentioned them to Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī. Therefore these descriptions do not at all pertain to material activity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.159
description: "The gopīs can be divided into a left wing and a right wing. Both wings induce Kṛṣṇa to taste transcendental mellows by various manifestations of ecstatic love.
text:
> 'vāmā' eka gopī-gaṇa, 'dakṣiṇā' eka gaṇa
> nānā-bhāve karāya kṛṣṇe rasa āsvādana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vāmā]]---left wing; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---party of //gopīs//; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇā]]---right wing; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---another; [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---party of //gopīs//; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in varieties of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---cause to do; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rasa]] [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasting of transcendental mellows.
translation: "The gopīs can be divided into a left wing and a right wing. Both wings induce Kṛṣṇa to taste transcendental mellows by various manifestations of ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.16
description: How powerful is the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! Without even inquiring about the King, the Lord made everything successful.
text:
> ei dekha,-caitanyera kṛpā-mahābala
> tāra anusandhāna vinā karāya saphala
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:d:dekha]]---just see; [[synonyms:c:caitanyera]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛpa]]-[[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bala]]---how greatly powerful is the mercy; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:a:anusandhāna]]---inquiring about him; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---He makes; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]---successful.
translation: How powerful is the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! Without even inquiring about the King, the Lord made everything successful.
purport:
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mercy is so powerful that it acts automatically. If a person renders loving service to Kṛṣṇa, it never goes in vain. It is recorded in a spiritual account, and in due time it will fructify. This is confirmed by the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:2:40|(Bg. 2.40)]]. //Svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt:// "In this endeavor there is no loss or diminution, and a little advancement on this path can protect one from the most dangerous type of fear."

Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has particularly bestowed upon all fallen souls in this age the most potent method of devotional service, and whoever takes to it through the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is immediately elevated to the transcendental position. //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// recommends: //yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair yajanti hi su-medhasaḥ// (//Bhāg.// 11.5.32).

A student of Kṛṣṇa consciousness must receive Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mercy; then his devotional service will quickly succeed. This was the case with King Pratāparudra. One has to be noticed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and a little service with sincere efforts will convince the Lord that one is a proper candidate for returning home, back to Godhead. Mahārāja Pratāparudra did not have a chance to meet Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, but when the Lord saw that the King was serving Lord Jagannātha as a menial sweeper, the Lord's mercy upon the King became a solid fact. When Mahārāja Pratāparudra, in the dress of a Vaiṣṇava, was serving the Lord, the Lord did not even inquire who he was. Rather, He had compassion upon him and began to embrace him.

Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī wants to point out that nothing could compare to the Lord's mercy toward Mahārāja Pratāparudra; therefore he uses the word //dekha// ("just see") and //caitanyera kṛpā-mahābala// ("how powerful is the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu"). This is also confirmed by Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī: //yat-kāruṇya-kaṭākṣa-vaibhava-vatām// (//Caitanya-candrāmṛta// 5). Even a little of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mercy serves as a great asset for spiritual advancement. Therefore the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement must be spread through the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. When Rūpa Gosvāmī experienced the mercy and magnanimity of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he said:

> namo mahā-vadānyāya
> kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāya te
> kṛṣṇāya kṛṣṇa-caitanya-
> nāmne gaura-tviṣe namaḥ

"I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya who is more magnanimous than any other //avatāra,// even Kṛṣṇa Himself, because He is bestowing freely what no one else has ever given-pure love of Kṛṣṇa." Śrīla Locana dāsa Ṭhākura has also sung, //parama karuṇa, pahuṅ dui jana, nitāi-gaura-candra:// "The two brothers Nitāi and Gaura are so kind that no one can compare to them." Similarly, Śrīla Narottama dāsa ṭhākura has sung:

> vrajendra-nandana yei,     śacī-suta haila sei,
> balarāma haila nitāi,
> dīna-hīna yata chila,     hari-nāme uddhārila,
> tā'ra sākṣī jagāi-mādhāi

Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's special mission is the deliverance of all fallen souls in Kali-yuga. Devotees of Kṛṣṇa must persistently seek the favor and mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to become fit to return home, back to Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.160
description: "Of all the gopīs, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is the chief. She is a jewel mine of ecstatic love and the source of all purified transcendental conjugal mellows.
text:
> gopī-gaṇa-madhye śreṣṭhā rādhā-ṭhākurāṇī
> nirmala-ujjvala-rasa-prema-ratna-khani
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---of all the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:ś:śreṣṭhā]]---the chief; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākurāṇī]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:n:nirmala]]---purified; [[synonyms:u:ujjvala]]---brilliant; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---in mellows; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:r:ratna]]-[[synonyms:k:khani]]---the jewel mine.
translation: "Of all the gopīs, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is the chief. She is a jewel mine of ecstatic love and the source of all purified transcendental conjugal mellows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.161
description: "Rādhārāṇī is grown up, and Her character is equipoised. She is always deeply absorbed in ecstatic love and always feeling in the mood of a left-wing gopī.
text:
> vayase 'madhyamā' teṅho svabhāvete 'samā'
> gāḍha prema-bhāve teṅho nirantara 'vāmā'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vayase]] [[synonyms:m:madhyamā]]---grown up; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvete]]---in character; [[synonyms:s:samā]]---equipoised; [[synonyms:g:gāḍha]]---deep; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---She; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---constantly; [[synonyms:v:vāmā]]---of the group of the left-wing //gopīs.//
translation: "Rādhārāṇī is grown up, and Her character is equipoised. She is always deeply absorbed in ecstatic love and always feeling in the mood of a left-wing gopī.
purport:
The left wing and right wing of the //gopīs// has been explained by Rūpa Gosvāmī in //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi.// The left wing is described in this way:

> mana-grahe sadodyuktā
> tac-chaithilye ca kopanā
> abhedyā nāyake prāyaḥ
> krūrā vāmeti kīrtyate

"A //gopī// who is always eager to be jealously angered, who is very enthusiastic for that position, who immediately becomes angry when defeated, who is never under the control of a hero and who always opposes Him is called //vāmā,// or a leftwing //gopī.//"

Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī describes the right-wing //gopīs// in this way:

> asahyā māna-nirbandhe
> nāyake yukta-vādinī
> sāmabhis tena bhedyā ca
> dakṣiṇā parikīrtitā

"A //gopī// who cannot tolerate womanly anger, who speaks suitable words to the hero and who is satisfied by His sweet words is called a //dakṣiṇā,// or a right-wing //gopi."//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.162
description: "Because She is a left-wing gopī, Her womanly anger is always awakening, but Kṛṣṇa derives transcendental bliss from Her activities.
text:
> vāmya-svabhāve māna uṭhe nirantara
> tāra madhye uṭhe kṛṣṇera ānanda-sāgara
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vāmya]]-[[synonyms:s:svabhāve]]---because of left-wing character; [[synonyms:m:māna]]---womanly anger; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---awakens; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---always; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in that dealing; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---is awakening; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sāgara]]---an ocean of transcendental bliss.
translation: "Because She is a left-wing gopī, Her womanly anger is always awakening, but Kṛṣṇa derives transcendental bliss from Her activities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.163
description: " 'The progress of loving affairs between young couples is by nature crooked, like the movement of a snake. Because of this, two types of anger arise between young couples-anger with a cause and anger without a cause.' "
text:
> aher iva gatiḥ premṇaḥ
>   svabhāva-kuṭilā bhavet
> ato hetor ahetoś ca
> yūnor māna udañcati
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aheḥ]]---of the snake; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:g:gatiḥ]]---the movement; [[synonyms:p:premṇaḥ]]---of the loving affairs; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---by nature; [[synonyms:k:kuṭilā]]---crooked; [[synonyms:b:bhavet]]---is; [[synonyms:a:ataḥ]]---therefore; [[synonyms:h:hetoḥ]]---from some cause; [[synonyms:a:ahetoḥ]]---from the absence of a cause; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:y:yūnoḥ]]---of the young couple; [[synonyms:m:mānaḥ]]---anger; [[synonyms:u:udañcati]]---appears.
translation: “ 'The progress of loving affairs between young couples is by nature crooked, like the movement of a snake. Because of this, two types of anger arise between young couples-anger with a cause and anger without a cause.' "
purport: This is a quotation from Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi// (//Śṛṅgāra-bheda-prakaraṇa// 102).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.164
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard these talks, His ocean of transcendental bliss increased. He therefore told Svarūpa Dāmodara, "Go on speaking, go on speaking." And thus Svarūpa Dāmodara continued.
text:
> eta śuni' bāḍe prabhura ānanda-sāgara
> 'kaha, kaha' kahe prabhu, bale dāmodara
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:b:bāḍe]]---increased; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sāgara]]---the ocean of transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:k:kaha]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---go on speaking; [[synonyms:k:kahe]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued to request; [[synonyms:b:bale]] [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Dāmodara Gosvāmī continued to reply.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard these talks, His ocean of transcendental bliss increased. He therefore told Svarūpa Dāmodara, "Go on speaking, go on speaking." And thus Svarūpa Dāmodara continued.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.165
description: "Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's love is a highly advanced ecstasy. All Her dealings are completely pure and devoid of material tinge. Indeed, Her dealings are ten times purer than gold.
text:
> 'adhirūḍha mahābhāva'-rādhikāra prema
> viśuddha, nirmala, yaiche daśa-vāṇa hema
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:adhirūḍha]] [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---highly elevated ecstatic love; [[synonyms:r:rādhikāra]] [[synonyms:p:prema]]---the loving affairs of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:v:viśuddha]]---completely uncontaminated; [[synonyms:n:nirmala]]---purified; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as if; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:v:vāṇa]]---ten times purified; [[synonyms:h:hema]]---gold.
translation: "Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's love is a highly advanced ecstasy. All Her dealings are completely pure and devoid of material tinge. Indeed, Her dealings are ten times purer than gold.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.166
description: "As soon as Rādhārāṇī gets a chance to see Kṛṣṇa, Her body is suddenly decorated with various ecstatic ornaments.
text:
> kṛṣṇera darśana yadi pāya ācambite
> nānā-bhāva-vibhūṣaṇe haya vibhūṣite
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---interview; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:ā:ācambite]]---all of a sudden; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---ecstatic; [[synonyms:v:vibhūṣaṇe]]---with ornaments; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:v:vibhūṣite]]---decorated.
translation: "As soon as Rādhārāṇī gets a chance to see Kṛṣṇa, Her body is suddenly decorated with various ecstatic ornaments.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.167
description: "The transcendental ornaments of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's body include the eight sāttvikas, or transcendental symptoms, the thirty-three vyabhicārībhāvas, beginning with harṣa, or jubilation in natural love, and the twenty bhāvas, or ecstatic emotional ornaments.
text:
> aṣṭa 'sāttvika', harṣādi 'vyabhicārī' yāṅra
> 'sahaja prema', viṁśati 'bhāva'-alaṅkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]]---eight; [[synonyms:s:sāttvika]]---transcendental symptoms; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---like jubilation; [[synonyms:v:vyabhicārī]]---distinctive features; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of whose; [[synonyms:s:sahaja]] [[synonyms:p:prema]]---natural love; [[synonyms:v:viṁśati]]---twenty; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---of ecstasy; [[synonyms:a:alaṅkāra]]---ornaments.
translation: "The transcendental ornaments of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's body include the eight sāttvikas, or transcendental symptoms, the thirty-three vyabhicārībhāvas, beginning with harṣa, or jubilation in natural love, and the twenty bhāvas, or ecstatic emotional ornaments.
purport: The thirty-three //vyabhicārī-bhāvas,// bodily symptoms manifest in ecstatic love, are as follows: (1) //nirveda,// indifference; (2) //viṣāda,// moroseness; (3) //dainya,// meekness; (4) //glāni,// a feeling that one is in a faulty position; (5) //śrama,// fatigue; (6) //mada,// madness; (7) //garva,// pride; (8) //śaṅkā,// doubt; (9) //trāsa,// shock; (10) //āvega,// intense emotion; (11) //unmāda,// craziness; (12) //apasmāra,// forgetfulness; (13) //vyādhi,// disease; (14) //moha,// bewilderment; (15) //mṛti,// death; (16) //ālasya,// laziness; (17) //jāḍya,// invalidity; (18) //vrīḍā,// shame; (19) //avahitthā,// concealment; (20) //smṛti,// remembrance; (21) //vitarka,// argument; (22) //cintā,// contemplation; (23) //mati,// attention; (24) //dhṛti,// forbearance; (25) //harṣa,// jubilation; (26) //autsukya,// eagerness; (27) //augrya,// violence; (28) //amarṣa,// anger; (29) //asūyā,// jealousy; (30) //cāpalya,// impudence; (31) //nidrā,// sleep; (32) //supti,// deep sleep and (33) //prabodha,// awakening.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.168
description: "Some of the symptoms critically explained in the following verses are kilakiñcita, kuṭṭamita, vilāsa, lalita, vivvoka, moṭṭāyita, maugdhya and cakita.
text:
> 'kila-kiñcita', 'kuṭṭamita', 'vilāsa', 'lalita'
> 'vivvoka', 'moṭṭāyita', āra 'maugdhya', 'cakita'
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kila]]-[[synonyms:k:kiñcita]]---a particular type of ornament at the time of seeing Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kuṭṭamita]]---the symptom explained in verse 197; [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---the symptom explained in verse 187; [[synonyms:l:lalita]]---the symptom explained in verse 192; [[synonyms:v:vivvoka]]---neglecting the presentation given by the hero; [[synonyms:m:moṭṭāyita]]---awakening of lusty desires by the remembrance and words of the hero; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:m:maugdhya]]---assuming the position of not knowing things although everything is known; [[synonyms:c:cakita]]---a position in which the heroine appears very afraid although she is not at all afraid.
translation: "Some of the symptoms critically explained in the following verses are kilakiñcita, kuṭṭamita, vilāsa, lalita, vivvoka, moṭṭāyita, maugdhya and cakita.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.169
description: "When Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's body manifests the ornaments of many ecstatic symptoms, the ocean of Kṛṣṇa's happiness immediately displays transcendental waves.
text:
> eta bhāva-bhūṣāya bhūṣita śrī-rādhāra aṅga
> dekhite uthale kṛṣṇa-sukhābdhi-taraṅga
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]]---so many; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūṣāya]]---with the ornaments of ecstasy; [[synonyms:b:bhūṣita]]---decorated; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rādhāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the body; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:u:uthale]]---awakens; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:a:abdhi]]---of the ocean of Kṛṣṇa's happiness; [[synonyms:t:taraṅga]]---waves.
translation: "When Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's body manifests the ornaments of many ecstatic symptoms, the ocean of Kṛṣṇa's happiness immediately displays transcendental waves.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.17
description: Finally Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Who are you? You have done so much for Me. All of a sudden you have come here and made Me drink the nectar of the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> prabhu bale,-ke tumi, karilā mora hita?
> ācambite āsi' piyāo kṛṣṇa-līlāmṛta?
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:k:ke]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---who are you; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---you have done; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:h:hita]]---welfare; [[synonyms:ā:ācambite]]---all of a sudden; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:p:piyāo]]---you make Me drink; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---the nectar of the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Finally Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Who are you? You have done so much for Me. All of a sudden you have come here and made Me drink the nectar of the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.170
description: "Now hear a description of different ecstasies, beginning with kila-kiñcita. With these ecstatic ornaments, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī enchants the mind of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> kila-kiñcitādi-bhāvera śuna vivaraṇa
> ye bhāva-bhūṣāya rādhā hare kṛṣṇa-mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kila]]-[[synonyms:k:kiñcita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---beginning with the ecstasy named //kila-kiñcita//; [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of ecstasies; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---the description; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūṣāya]]---with these ecstatic ornaments; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---enchants; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Now hear a description of different ecstasies, beginning with kila-kiñcita. With these ecstatic ornaments, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī enchants the mind of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.171
description: "When Śrī Kṛṣṇa sees Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and wants to touch Her body, He prohibits Her from going to the spot where one can cross the River Yamunā.
text:
> rādhā dekhi' kṛṣṇa yadi chuṅite kare mana
> dāna-ghāṭi-pathe yabe varjena gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after seeing; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:c:chuṅite]]---to touch; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---desires; [[synonyms:d:dāna]]-[[synonyms:g:ghāṭi]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way leading toward the spot from where one crosses the river to the other side; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:v:varjena]]---prohibits; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going.
translation: "When Śrī Kṛṣṇa sees Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and wants to touch Her body, He prohibits Her from going to the spot where one can cross the River Yamunā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.172
description: "Approaching Her, Kṛṣṇa prohibits Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī from picking flowers. He may also touch Her in front of Her friends.
text:
> yabe āsi' mānā kare puṣpa uṭhāite
> sakhī-āge cāhe yadi gāye hāta dite
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming nearby; [[synonyms:m:mānā]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---prohibits; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]] [[synonyms:u:uṭhāite]]---to pick up flowers; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of the friends of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:c:cāhe]]---wants; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:g:gāye]]---in the body; [[synonyms:h:hāta]] [[synonyms:d:dite]]---touch with the hand.
translation: "Approaching Her, Kṛṣṇa prohibits Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī from picking flowers. He may also touch Her in front of Her friends.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.173
description: "At such times, the ecstatic symptoms of kila-kiñcita are awakened. First there is jubilation in ecstatic love, which is the root cause of these symptoms.
text:
> ei-saba sthāne 'kila-kiñcita' udgama
> prathame 'harṣa' sañcārī-mūla kāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in such places; [[synonyms:k:kila]]-[[synonyms:k:kiñcita]]---of the symptom of the ecstasy known as //kila-kiñcita//; [[synonyms:u:udgama]]---awakening; [[synonyms:p:prathame]]---in the beginning; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---jubilation; [[synonyms:s:sañcārī]]---ecstatic emotion; [[synonyms:m:mūla]] [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the root cause.
translation: "At such times, the ecstatic symptoms of kila-kiñcita are awakened. First there is jubilation in ecstatic love, which is the root cause of these symptoms.
purport: Whenever Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī leaves Her house, She is always well-dressed and attractive. It is Her womanly nature to attract Śrī Kṛṣṇa's attention, and upon seeing Her so attractively dressed, Śrī Kṛṣṇa desires to touch Her body. The Lord then finds some fault in Her and prohibits Her from going to a river crossing and stops Her from picking flowers. Such are the pastimes between Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Being a cowherd girl, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī regularly carries a container of milk and often goes to sell it on the other side of the Yamunā. To cross the river, She has to pay the boatman, and the spot where the boatman collects his fares is called the //dāna-ghāṭi.// Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa stops Her from going, telling Her, "First You have to pay the fee; then You will be allowed to go." This pastime is called //dāna-keli-līlā.// Similarly, if Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī wants to pick a flower, Śrī Kṛṣṇa claims to be the garden's proprietor and prohibits Her. This pastime is called //kila-kiñcita.// Rādhārāṇī's shyness arises due to Śrī Kṛṣṇa's prohibitions, and ecstatic loving bodily symptoms called //kila-kiñcita-bhāva// are manifest at this time. These ecstatic symptoms are explained in the following verse, which is from Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi// (//Anubhāva-prakaraṇa// 44).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.174
description: " 'Pride, ambition, weeping, smiling, envy, fear and anger are the seven ecstatic loving symptoms manifest by a jubilant shrinking away, and these symptoms are called kila-kiñcita-bhāva.'
text:
> garvābhilāṣa-rudita-
> smitāsūyā-bhaya-krudhām
> saṅkarī-karaṇaṁ harṣād
> ucyate kila-kiñcitam
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:garva]]---pride; [[synonyms:a:abhilāṣa]]---ambition; [[synonyms:r:rudita]]---crying; [[synonyms:s:smita]]---smiling; [[synonyms:a:asūyā]]---envying; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fearing; [[synonyms:k:krudhām]]---anger; [[synonyms:s:saṅkarī]]-[[synonyms:k:karaṇam]]---the act of shrinking away; [[synonyms:h:harṣāt]]---because of jubilation; [[synonyms:u:ucyate]]---is called; [[synonyms:k:kila]]-[[synonyms:k:kiñcitam]]---ecstatic symptoms known as //kila-kiñcita.//
translation: “ 'Pride, ambition, weeping, smiling, envy, fear and anger are the seven ecstatic loving symptoms manifest by a jubilant shrinking away, and these symptoms are called kila-kiñcita-bhāva.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.175
description: "There are seven other transcendental ecstatic symptoms, and when they combine on the platform of jubilation, the combination is called mahābhāva.
text:
> āra sāta bhāva āsi' sahaje milaya
> asta-bhāva-sammilane 'mahābhāva' haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---other; [[synonyms:s:sāta]]---seven; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---ecstatic symptoms; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming together; [[synonyms:s:sahaje]]---naturally; [[synonyms:m:milaya]]---become mixed; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---of eight kinds of ecstatic emotional symptoms; [[synonyms:s:sammilane]]---by the combining; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is //mahābhāva.//
translation: "There are seven other transcendental ecstatic symptoms, and when they combine on the platform of jubilation, the combination is called mahābhāva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.176
description: "The seven combined ingredients of mahābhāva are pride, ambition, fear, dry artificial crying, anger, envy and mild smiling.
text:
> garva, abhilāṣa, bha ya, śuṣka-rudita
> krodha, asūyā haya, āra manda-smita
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:garva]]---pride; [[synonyms:a:abhilāṣa]]---ambition; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:ś:śuṣka]]-[[synonyms:r:rudita]]---dry, artificial crying; [[synonyms:k:krodha]]---anger; [[synonyms:a:asūyā]]---envy; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also; [[synonyms:m:manda]]-[[synonyms:s:smita]]---mild smiling.
translation: "The seven combined ingredients of mahābhāva are pride, ambition, fear, dry artificial crying, anger, envy and mild smiling.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.177
description: "There are eight symptoms of ecstatic love on the platform of transcendental jubilation, and when they are combined and tasted by Kṛṣṇa, the Lord's mind is completely satisfied.
text:
> nānā-svādu aṣṭa-bhāva ekatra milana
> yāhāra āsvāde tṛpta haya kṛṣṇa-mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:s:svādu]]---tasteful; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---eight kinds of ecstatic symptoms; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]]---at one place; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting; [[synonyms:y:yāhāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:ā:āsvāde]]---by the tasting; [[synonyms:t:tṛpta]]---satisfied; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "There are eight symptoms of ecstatic love on the platform of transcendental jubilation, and when they are combined and tasted by Kṛṣṇa, the Lord's mind is completely satisfied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.178
description: "Indeed, they are compared to a combination of yogurt, candy, ghee, honey, black pepper, camphor and cardamom, which, when mixed together, are very tasty and sweet.
text:
> dadhi, khaṇḍa, ghṛta, madhu, marīca, karpūra
> elāci-milane yaiche rasālā madhura
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dadhi]]---yogurt; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]]---candy; [[synonyms:g:ghṛta]]---ghee; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]---honey; [[synonyms:m:marīca]]---black pepper; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]---camphor; [[synonyms:e:elāci]]---cardamom; [[synonyms:m:milane]]---by combining together; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:r:rasālā]]---very tasteful; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---and sweet.
translation: "Indeed, they are compared to a combination of yogurt, candy, ghee, honey, black pepper, camphor and cardamom, which, when mixed together, are very tasty and sweet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.179
description: "Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is thousands upon thousands of times more satisfied when He sees Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's face light up from this combination of ecstatic love than He is by direct union with Her.
text:
> ei bhāva-yukta dekhi' rādhāsya-nayana
> saṅgama ha-ite sukha pāya koṭi-guṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eibhāva]]---with these ecstatic symptoms; [[synonyms:y:yukta]]---combined together; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:a:asya]]-[[synonyms:n:nayana]]---the face and eyes of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:s:saṅgama]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---than direct embracing; [[synonyms:s:sukha]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---enjoys happiness; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---millions of times more.
translation:
"Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is thousands upon thousands of times more satisfied when He sees Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's face light up from this combination of ecstatic love than He is by direct union with Her.


This is further explained in the following verse from the //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi// (//Anubhāva-prakaraṇa// 46) of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.18
description: The King replied, "My Lord, I am the most obedient servant of Your servants. It is my ambition that You will accept me as the servant of Your servants."
text:
> rājā kahe,-āmi tomāra dāsera anudāsa
> bhṛtyera bhṛtya kara,-ei mora āśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the King said; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:d:dāsera]] [[synonyms:a:anudāsa]]---most obedient servant of Your servant; [[synonyms:b:bhṛtyera]] [[synonyms:b:bhṛtya]]---servant of the servant; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---make (me); [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---my desire.
translation: The King replied, "My Lord, I am the most obedient servant of Your servants. It is my ambition that You will accept me as the servant of Your servants."
purport: The greatest achievement for a devotee is to become a servant of the servants. Actually no one should desire to become the direct servant of the Lord. That is not a very good idea. When Prahlāda Mahārāja was offered a benediction by Nṛsiṁhadeva, Prahlāda rejected all kinds of material benediction, but he prayed to become the servant of the servant of the Lord. When Dhruva Mahārāja was offered a benediction by Kuvera, the treasurer of the demigods, Dhruva could have asked for unlimited material opulence, but he simply asked for the benediction of becoming the servant of the servants of the Lord. Kholāvecā Śrīdhara was a very poor man, but when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to give him a benediction, he also prayed to the Lord to be allowed to remain a servant of the servants of the Lord. The conclusion is that being the servant of the servants of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the highest benediction one can desire.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.180
description: " 'May the sight of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's kila-kiñcita ecstasy, which is like a bouquet, bring good fortune to all. When Śrī Kṛṣṇa blocked Rādhārāṇī's way to the dāna-ghāṭi, there was laughter within Her heart. Her eyes grew bright, and fresh tears flowed from Her eyes, reddening them. Due to Her sweet relationship with Kṛṣṇa, Her eyes were enthusiastic, and when Her crying subsided, She appeared even more beautiful.'
text:
> antaḥ smeratayojjvalā jala-kaṇa-vyākīrṇa-pakṣmāṅkurā
> kiñcit pāṭalitāñcalā rasikatotsiktā puraḥ kuñcatī
> ruddhāyāḥ pathi mādhavena madhura-vyābhugna-torottarā
> rādhāyāḥ kila-kiñcita-stavakinī dṛṣṭiḥ śriyaṁ vaḥ kriyāt
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]---internally or not manifested; [[synonyms:s:smeratayā]] [[synonyms:u:ujjvala]]---brightened by mild smiling; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:k:kaṇa]]---with drops of water; [[synonyms:v:vyākīrṇa]]---scattered; [[synonyms:p:pakṣma]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅkurā]]---from the eyelashes; [[synonyms:k:kiñcit]]---very little; [[synonyms:p:pāṭalita]]-[[synonyms:a:añcalā]]---a tinge of redness, mixed with whiteness, on the borders of the eyes; [[synonyms:r:rasikata]]-[[synonyms:u:utsiktā]]---being merged in the cunning behavior of the Lord; [[synonyms:p:puraḥ]]---in the front; [[synonyms:k:kuñcatī]]---shrinks; [[synonyms:r:ruddhāyāḥ]]---having been blocked; [[synonyms:p:pathi]]---on the way; [[synonyms:m:mādhavena]]---by Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweet; [[synonyms:v:vyābhugna]]---curved; [[synonyms:t:torā]]-[[synonyms:u:uttarā]]---the eyes; [[synonyms:r:rādhāyāḥ]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:k:kila]]-[[synonyms:k:kiñcita]]---the ecstatic symptom named //kila-kiñcita//; [[synonyms:s:stavakinī]]---like a bouquet of flowers; [[synonyms:d:dṛṣṭiḥ]]---glance; [[synonyms:ś:śriyam]]---good fortune; [[synonyms:v:vaḥ]]---of all of you; [[synonyms:k:kriyāt]]---may perform.
translation: “ 'May the sight of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's kila-kiñcita ecstasy, which is like a bouquet, bring good fortune to all. When Śrī Kṛṣṇa blocked Rādhārāṇī's way to the dāna-ghāṭi, there was laughter within Her heart. Her eyes grew bright, and fresh tears flowed from Her eyes, reddening them. Due to Her sweet relationship with Kṛṣṇa, Her eyes were enthusiastic, and when Her crying subsided, She appeared even more beautiful.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.181
description: " 'Agitated by tears, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's eyes were tinged with red, just like the eastern horizon at sunrise. Her lips began to move with jubilation and lusty desire. Her eyebrows curved, and Her lotus-like face smiled mildly. Seeing Rādhārāṇī's face exhibit such emotion, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa felt a million times happier than when He embraced Her. Indeed, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa's happiness is not at all mundane.' "
text:
> bāṣpa-vyākulitāruṇāñcala-calan-netraṁ rasollāsitaṁ
> helollāsa-calādharaṁ kuṭilita-bhrū-yugmam udyat-smitam
> rādhāyāḥ kila-kiñcitāñcitam asau vīkṣyānanaṁ saṅgamād
> ānandaṁ tam avāpa koṭi-guṇitaṁ yo 'bhūn na gīr-gocaraḥ

translation: “ 'Agitated by tears, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's eyes were tinged with red, just like the eastern horizon at sunrise. Her lips began to move with jubilation and lusty desire. Her eyebrows curved, and Her lotus-like face smiled mildly. Seeing Rādhārāṇī's face exhibit such emotion, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa felt a million times happier than when He embraced Her. Indeed, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa's happiness is not at all mundane.' "
purport: This is a quotation from the //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (9.18).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.182
description: Upon hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very happy, and, being absorbed in this happiness, He embraced Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī.
text:
> eta śuni' prabhu hailā ānandita mana
> sukhāviṣṭa hañā svarūpe kailā āliṅgana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---very happy in His mind; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being absorbed in happiness; [[synonyms:s:svarūpe]]---unto Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing.
translation: Upon hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very happy, and, being absorbed in this happiness, He embraced Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.183
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then asked Svarūpa Dāmodara, "Please speak of the ecstatic ornaments decorating the body of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, by which She enchants the mind of Śrī Govinda."
text:
> 'vilāsādi'-bhāva-bhūṣāra kaha ta' lakṣaṇa
> yei bhāve rādhā hare govindera mana?
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---beginning with transcendental enjoyment; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---of ecstasy; [[synonyms:b:bhūṣāra]]---of the ornaments; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please speak; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the symptoms; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---by which symptoms; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---enchants; [[synonyms:g:govindera]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind of Śrī Govinda.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then asked Svarūpa Dāmodara, "Please speak of the ecstatic ornaments decorating the body of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, by which She enchants the mind of Śrī Govinda."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.184
description: Being thus requested, Svarūpa Dāmodara began to speak. All the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were very happy to hear him.
text:
> tabe ta' svarūpa-gosāñi kahite lāgilā
> śuni' prabhura bhakta-gaṇa mahā-sukha pāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to speak; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]] [[synonyms:p:pāilā]]---achieved great happiness.
translation: Being thus requested, Svarūpa Dāmodara began to speak. All the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were very happy to hear him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.185
description: "Sometimes when Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is sitting or when She is going to Vṛndāvana, She sometimes sees Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> rādhā vasi' āche, kibā vṛndāvane yāya
> tāhāṅ yadi ācambite kṛṣṇa-daraśana pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rādhā]] [[synonyms:v:vasi']] [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is sitting; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---or; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvane]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---is going to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:ā:ācambite]]---all of a sudden; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets the opportunity to see Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Sometimes when Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is sitting or when She is going to Vṛndāvana, She sometimes sees Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.186
description: "The symptoms of various ecstasies that become manifest at that time are called vilāsa.
text:
> dekhite nānā-bhāva haya vilakṣaṇa
> se vailakṣaṇyera nāma 'vilāsa'-bhūṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---while seeing; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---of various ecstasies; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:v:vilakṣaṇa]]---symptoms; [[synonyms:s:se]]---those; [[synonyms:v:vailakṣaṇyera]]---of different symptoms; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name; [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---//vilāsa//; [[synonyms:b:bhūṣaṇa]]---ornaments.
translation: "The symptoms of various ecstasies that become manifest at that time are called vilāsa.
purport: This is described in the following verse, taken from the //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi// (//Anubhāva-prakaraṇa// 31).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.187
description: " 'The various symptoms manifested in a woman's face, eyes, and the other parts of her body and the way she moves, stands or sits when she meets her beloved are called vilāsa.' "
text:
> gati-sthānāsanādīnāṁ
> mukha-netrādi-karmaṇām
> tātkālikaṁ tu vaiśiṣṭyaṁ
> vilāsaḥ priya-saṅgajam

translation: “ 'The various symptoms manifested in a woman's face, eyes, and the other parts of her body and the way she moves, stands or sits when she meets her beloved are called vilāsa.' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.188
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara said, "Timidity, jubilation, ambition, respect, fear and the characteristics of the left-wing gopīs were all ecstatic symptoms combined to agitate Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
text:
> lajjā, harṣa, abhilāṣa, sambhrama, vāmya, bhaya
> eta bhāva mili' rādhāya cañcala karaya

translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara said, "Timidity, jubilation, ambition, respect, fear and the characteristics of the left-wing gopīs were all ecstatic symptoms combined to agitate Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
purport: This is explained in the following verse found in the //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (9.11).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.189
description: " 'When Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī saw Lord Kṛṣṇa just before Her, Her progress stopped, and She assumed an attitude of opposition. Although Her face was slightly covered by a blue garment, Her two starry eyes were agitated, being wide and curved. Thus She was decorated with the ornaments of vilāsa, and Her beauty increased to give pleasure to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
text:
> puraḥ kṛṣṇālokāt sthagita-kuṭilāsyā gatir abhūt
> tiraścīnaṁ kṛṣṇāmbara-dara-vṛtaṁ śrī-mukham api
> calat-tāraṁ sphāraṁ nayana-yugam ābhugnam iti sā
> vilāsākhya-svālaṅkaraṇa-valitāsīt priya-mude

translation: “ 'When Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī saw Lord Kṛṣṇa just before Her, Her progress stopped, and She assumed an attitude of opposition. Although Her face was slightly covered by a blue garment, Her two starry eyes were agitated, being wide and curved. Thus She was decorated with the ornaments of vilāsa, and Her beauty increased to give pleasure to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.19
description: At that time, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu displayed some of His divine opulences to the King, and He forbade him to disclose this to anyone.
text:
> tabe mahāprabhu tāṅre aiśvarya dekhāila
> 'kāreha nā kahibe' ei niṣedha karila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to the King; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---divine power; [[synonyms:d:dekhāila]]---showed; [[synonyms:k:kāreha]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kahibe]]---do not speak to anyone; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:n:niṣedha]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---forbade.
translation: At that time, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu displayed some of His divine opulences to the King, and He forbade him to disclose this to anyone.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.190
description: "When Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī stands before Kṛṣṇa, She stands bent in three places-Her neck, waist and legs-and Her eyebrows dance.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-āge rādhā yadi rahe dāṇḍāñā
> tina-aṅga-bhaṅge rahe bhrū nācāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:d:dāṇḍāñā]]---standing; [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṅge]]---with three bends in the body; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:b:bhrū]]---eyebrows; [[synonyms:n:nācāñā]]---dancing.
translation: "When Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī stands before Kṛṣṇa, She stands bent in three places-Her neck, waist and legs-and Her eyebrows dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 14.191
description: "When there is an awakening of various ecstatic features on Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's face and in Her eyes, the lalita ornaments are manifest.
text:
> mukhe-netre haya nānā-bhāvera udgāra
> ei kāntā-bhāvera nāma 'lalita'-alaṅkāra
