translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then submitted that Paramānanda Purī Gosvāmī should accept a five-day invitation at his place. This was settled before the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.195
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Dāmodara Svarūpa is my intimate friend. He will come sometimes with You and sometimes alone.
text:
> dāmodara-svarūpa,---ei bāndhava āmāra
> kabhu tomāra saṅge yābe, kabhu ekeśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]-[[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:b:bāndhava]] [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---my very intimate friend; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with You; [[synonyms:y:yābe]]---will come; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:e:ekeśvara]]---alone.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Dāmodara Svarūpa is my intimate friend. He will come sometimes with You and sometimes alone.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.196
description: "The other eight sannyāsīs will accept invitations for two days each. In this way there will be engagements for each and every day during the entire month.
text:
> āra aṣṭa sannyāsīra bhikṣā dui dui divase
> eka eka-dina, eka eka jane pūrṇa ha-ila māse
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---other; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]]---eight; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]]---of //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---invitation for lunch; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:d:divase]]---two days each; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---on each day; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:j:jane]]---one person; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---filled; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---will be; [[synonyms:m:māse]]---the month.
translation: "The other eight sannyāsīs will accept invitations for two days each. In this way there will be engagements for each and every day during the entire month.
purport: For the entire month consisting of thirty days, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would visit five days, Paramānanda Purī Gosvāmī five days, Svarūpa Dāmodara four days, and the eight other //sannyāsīs// two days each. In this way the thirty days of the month were completed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.197
description: "If all the sannyāsīs come together, it would not be possible for me to pay them proper respects. Therefore I would be an offender.
text:
> bahuta sannyāsī yadi āise eka ṭhāñi
> sammāna karite nāri, aparādha pāi
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bahuta]] [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---many //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---come; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---together; [[synonyms:s:sammāna]] [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:n:nāri]]---I cannot receive them properly; [[synonyms:a:aparādha]] [[synonyms:p:pāi]]---I shall be an offender.
translation: "If all the sannyāsīs come together, it would not be possible for me to pay them proper respects. Therefore I would be an offender.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.198
description: "Sometimes You will come alone to my place, and sometimes You will be accompanied by Svarūpa Dāmodara."
text:
> tumiha nija-chāye āsibe mora ghara
> kabhu saṅge āsibena svarūpa-dāmodara
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumiha]]---You; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:c:chāye]]---alone; [[synonyms:ā:āsibe]]---will come; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:g:ghara]]---to my place; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with You; [[synonyms:ā:āsibena]]---will come; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī.
translation: "Sometimes You will come alone to my place, and sometimes You will be accompanied by Svarūpa Dāmodara."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.199
description: Having this arrangement confirmed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Bhaṭṭācārya became very glad and immediately invited the Lord to his house on that very day.
text:
> prabhura iṅgita pāñā ānandita mana
> sei dina mahāprabhura kaila nimantraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:i:iṅgita]]---acceptance; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---receiving; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very happy; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---on that day; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation.
translation: Having this arrangement confirmed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Bhaṭṭācārya became very glad and immediately invited the Lord to his house on that very day.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.2
description: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaitacandra! And all glories to all the devotees of Lord Caitanya!
text:
> jaya jaya śrī-caitanya jaya nityānanda
> jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jayajaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---unto Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---all glories to Advaita Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---to the devotees of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaitacandra! And all glories to all the devotees of Lord Caitanya!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.20
description: At that time, King Pratāparudra was also personally present with Kāśī Miśra, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Tulasī Paḍichāpātra.
text:
> āpane pratāparudra, āra miśra-kāśī
> sārvabhauma, āra paḍichā-pātra tulasī
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āpane]] [[synonyms:p:pratāparudra]]---personally King Pratāparudra; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:m:miśra]]-[[synonyms:k:kāśī]]---Kāśī Miśra; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:paḍichā]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]] [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]---Paḍichāpātra Tulasī, the temple superintendent.
translation: At that time, King Pratāparudra was also personally present with Kāśī Miśra, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Tulasī Paḍichāpātra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.200
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's wife was known as the mother of Ṣāṭhī. She was a great devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and she was affectionate like a mother.
text:
> 'ṣāṭhīra mātā' nāma, bhaṭṭācāryera gṛhiṇī
> prabhura mahā-bhakta teṅho, snehete jananī
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣāṭhīra]] [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---the mother of Ṣāṭhī; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]] [[synonyms:g:gṛhiṇī]]---the wife of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---a great devotee; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---she; [[synonyms:s:snehete]]---in affection; [[synonyms:j:jananī]]---just like a mother.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's wife was known as the mother of Ṣāṭhī. She was a great devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and she was affectionate like a mother.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.201
description: After returning to his home, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya gave orders to his wife, and his wife, known as Ṣāṭhīra Mātā, the mother of Ṣāṭhī, began cooking with great pleasure.
text:
> ghare āsi' bhaṭṭācārya tāṅre ājñā dila
> ānande ṣāṭhīra mātā pāka caḍāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:ghare]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming home; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---her; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---ordered; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---with great satisfaction; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣāṭhīra]] [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---the mother of Ṣāṭhī; [[synonyms:p:pāka]] [[synonyms:c:caḍāila]]---began cooking.
translation: After returning to his home, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya gave orders to his wife, and his wife, known as Ṣāṭhīra Mātā, the mother of Ṣāṭhī, began cooking with great pleasure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.202
description: At Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's house, there was always a full stock of food. Whatever spinach, vegetables, fruit and so on were required, he collected and brought back home.
text:
> bhaṭṭācāryera gṛhe saba dravya āche bhari'
> yebā śāka-phalādika, ānāila āhari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]] [[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---at the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:d:dravya]]---all kinds of ingredients; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there are; [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---filling; [[synonyms:y:yebā]]---whatever; [[synonyms:ś:śāka]]---spinach; [[synonyms:p:phala]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādika]]---fruits and so on; [[synonyms:ā:ānāila]]---he brought; [[synonyms:ā:āhari']]---collecting.
translation: At Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's house, there was always a full stock of food. Whatever spinach, vegetables, fruit and so on were required, he collected and brought back home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.203
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya personally began to help his wife cook. His wife, the mother of Ṣāṭhī, was very experienced, and she knew how to cook nicely.
text:
> āpani bhaṭṭācārya kare pākera saba karma
> ṣāṭhīra mātā---vicakṣaṇā, jāne pāka-marma
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āpani]]---personally; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---arranges; [[synonyms:p:pākera]]---of cooking; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:k:karma]]---all activities; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣāṭhīra]] [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---the mother of Ṣāṭhī; [[synonyms:v:vicakṣaṇā]]---very experienced; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---knows; [[synonyms:p:pāka]]-[[synonyms:m:marma]]---how to cook.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya personally began to help his wife cook. His wife, the mother of Ṣāṭhī, was very experienced, and she knew how to cook nicely.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.204
description: On the southern side of the kitchen were two rooms for offering food, and in one of them the food was offered to Śālagrāma Nārāyaṇa.
text:
> pāka-śālāra dakṣiṇe---dui bhogālaya
> eka-ghare śālagrāmera bhoga-sevā haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śālāra]] [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇe]]---on the southern side of the kitchen; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]-[[synonyms:ā:ālaya]]---two rooms for offering food; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in one room; [[synonyms:ś:śālagrāmera]]---of Lord Śālagrāma; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]]---offering of food; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is.
translation: On the southern side of the kitchen were two rooms for offering food, and in one of them the food was offered to Śālagrāma Nārāyaṇa.
purport: Among the followers of the Vedic way, //śālagrāma-śilā,// the //vigraha// of Nārāyaṇa, is worshiped in the form of a stone ball. In India, every //brāhmaṇa// still worships the //śālagrāma-śilā// in his home. The //vaiśyas// and //kṣatriyas// may also engage in this worship, but it is compulsory in the house of a //brāhmaṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.205
description: The other room was for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's lunch. The Lord's lunch room was very secluded, and it was newly constructed by Bhaṭṭācārya.
text:
> āra ghara mahāprabhura bhikṣāra lāgiyā
> nibhṛte kariyāche bhaṭṭa nūtana kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:g:ghara]]---the other room; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣāra]] [[synonyms:l:lāgiyā]]---for taking lunch; [[synonyms:n:nibhṛte]] [[synonyms:k:kariyāche]]---constructed in a solitary place; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:n:nūtana]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---newly done.
translation: The other room was for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's lunch. The Lord's lunch room was very secluded, and it was newly constructed by Bhaṭṭācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.206
description: The room was so constructed that there was only one door as an entrance from the outside for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. There was another door attached to the kitchen, and it was through this door that the food was brought.
text:
> bāhye eka dvāra tāra, prabhu praveśite
> pāka-śālāra eka dvāra anna pariveśite
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāhye]]---outside; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:d:dvāra]]---one door; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of this room; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:p:praveśite]]---for the entrance of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pāka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śālāra]]---of the kitchen; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:d:dvāra]]---another door; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food; [[synonyms:p:pariveśite]]---to serve.
translation: The room was so constructed that there was only one door as an entrance from the outside for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. There was another door attached to the kitchen, and it was through this door that the food was brought.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.207
description: First, three mānas of cooked rice-almost six pounds-was poured on a big banana leaf.
text:
> battiśā-āṭhiyā kalāra āṅgaṭiyā pāte
> tina-māna taṇḍulera ubhārila bhāte
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:battiśā]]-[[synonyms:ā:āṭhiyā]]---named //battiśā-āṭhiyā//; [[synonyms:k:kalāra]]---of the banana tree; [[synonyms:ā:āṅgaṭiyā]]---without being divided; [[synonyms:p:pāte]]---on a leaf; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:m:māna]]---//mānas// (a certain weight); [[synonyms:t:taṇḍulera]]---of rice; [[synonyms:u:ubhārila]]---poured; [[synonyms:b:bhāte]]---cooked rice.
translation: First, three mānas of cooked rice-almost six pounds-was poured on a big banana leaf.
purport: This is the beginning of a description of the food prepared for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. This description is given by Kavirāja Gosvāmī, who, it is assumed, was an expert cook who knew both how to prepare and how to serve food.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.208
description: Then, the whole stack of rice was mixed with so much yellowish and fragrant clarified butter that it began to overflow the leaf.
text:
> pīta-sugandhi-ghṛte anna sikta kaila
> cāri-dike pāte ghṛta vahiyā calila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pīta]]---yellowish; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:g:gandhi]]---fragrant; [[synonyms:g:ghṛte]]---with clarified butter; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---rice; [[synonyms:s:sikta]]---mixed; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---on all sides; [[synonyms:p:pāte]]---the leaf; [[synonyms:g:ghṛta]]---the clarified butter; [[synonyms:v:vahiyā]] [[synonyms:c:calila]]---began to flood.
translation: Then, the whole stack of rice was mixed with so much yellowish and fragrant clarified butter that it began to overflow the leaf.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.209
description: There were a number of pots made of the bark of banana trees and the leaves of the keyā plant. These pots were filled with various cooked vegetables and placed on all sides of the leaf.
text:
> keyāpatra-kalākholā-ḍoṅgā sāri sāri
> cāri-dike dhariyāche nānā vyañjana bhari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:keyā]]-[[synonyms:p:patra]]---the leaf of the //keyā// plant; [[synonyms:k:kalā]]-[[synonyms:k:kholā]]---the skin of the banana tree; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍoṅgā]]---pots; [[synonyms:s:sāri]] [[synonyms:s:sāri]]---one after another; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---on all sides; [[synonyms:d:dhariyāche]]---were holding; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---cooked vegetables; [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---filled.
translation: There were a number of pots made of the bark of banana trees and the leaves of the keyā plant. These pots were filled with various cooked vegetables and placed on all sides of the leaf.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.21
description: As usual, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced jubilantly. Everyone was covered with milk, yogurt and yellow turmeric water.
text:
> iṅhā-sabā lañā prabhu kare nṛtya-raṅga
> dadhi-dugdha haridrā-jale bhare sabāra aṅga
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṅhā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking all of them; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅga]]---performed dancing in jubilation; [[synonyms:d:dadhi]]---yogurt; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]---milk; [[synonyms:h:haridrā]]---turmeric; [[synonyms:j:jale]]---with water; [[synonyms:b:bhare]]---covered; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---bodies.
translation: As usual, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced jubilantly. Everyone was covered with milk, yogurt and yellow turmeric water.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.210
description: There were about ten kinds of spinach, a soup called sukhta, which was made with bitter nimba leaves, a pungent preparation made with black pepper, a mild cake made of fried curd, and buttermilk mixed with small fried pieces of dhal.
text:
> daśa-prakāra śāka, nimba-tikta-sukhta-jhola
> maricera jhāla, chānā-baḍā, baḍi ghola
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śāka]]---spinach of ten varieties; [[synonyms:n:nimba]]-[[synonyms:t:tikta]]-[[synonyms:s:sukhta]]-[[synonyms:j:jhola]]---a soup called //sukhta,// made with bitter //nimba// leaf; [[synonyms:m:maricera]] [[synonyms:j:jhāla]]---a pungent preparation made with black pepper; [[synonyms:c:chānā]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍā]]---a mild cake made of fried curd; [[synonyms:b:baḍi]] [[synonyms:g:ghola]]---buttermilk with small pieces of fried dhal.
translation: There were about ten kinds of spinach, a soup called sukhta, which was made with bitter nimba leaves, a pungent preparation made with black pepper, a mild cake made of fried curd, and buttermilk mixed with small fried pieces of dhal.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.211
description: There were preparations of dugdha-tumbī, dugdha-kuṣmāṇḍa, vesara, lāphrā, mocā-ghaṇṭa, mocā-bhājā and other vegetables.
text:
> dugdha-tumbī, dugdha-kuṣmāṇḍa, vesara, lāphrā
> mocā-ghaṇṭa, mocā-bhājā, vividha śākrā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]-[[synonyms:t:tumbī]]---squash cooked with milk; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṣmāṇḍa]]---pumpkin cooked with milk; [[synonyms:v:vesara]]---a preparation made from chick-pea flour; [[synonyms:l:lāphrā]]---a combination of several vegetables; [[synonyms:m:mocā]]-[[synonyms:g:ghaṇṭa]]---boiled banana flowers; [[synonyms:m:mocā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhājā]]---fried banana flowers; [[synonyms:v:vividha]]---various; [[synonyms:ś:śākrā]]---vegetables.
translation: There were preparations of dugdha-tumbī, dugdha-kuṣmāṇḍa, vesara, lāphrā, mocā-ghaṇṭa, mocā-bhājā and other vegetables.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.212
description: There were unlimited quantities of vṛddha-kuṣmāṇḍa-baḍī, phula-baḍī, fruits and various roots.
text:
> vṛddha-kuṣmāṇḍa-baḍīra vyañjana apāra
> phulabaḍī-phala-mūla vividha prakāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛddha]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṣmāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍīra]]---of small pieces of fried dhal mixed with ripe pumpkin; [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---vegetables; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:p:phula]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍī]]---small fried pieces of another kind of //dhal//; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---fruits; [[synonyms:m:mūla]]---roots; [[synonyms:v:vividha]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---of different varieties.
translation: There were unlimited quantities of vṛddha-kuṣmāṇḍa-baḍī, phula-baḍī, fruits and various roots.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.213
description: Other preparations included eggplant mixed with newly grown nimba leaves fried together, light baḍī, fried paṭola, and fried rounds of squash and pumpkin.
text:
> nava-nimbapatra-saha bhṛṣṭa-vārtākī
> phula-baḍi paṭola-bhājā, kuṣmāṇḍa-māna-cākī
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nava]]---newly grown; [[synonyms:n:nimba]]-[[synonyms:p:patra]]---nimba leaves; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---along with; [[synonyms:b:bhṛṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:v:vārtākī]]---fried eggplant; [[synonyms:p:phula]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍī]]---light baḍī; [[synonyms:p:paṭola]]-[[synonyms:b:bhājā]]---fried //paṭola// vegetable; [[synonyms:k:kuṣmāṇḍa]]---of pumpkin; [[synonyms:m:māna]]---of squash; [[synonyms:c:cākī]]---rounds.
translation: Other preparations included eggplant mixed with newly grown nimba leaves fried together, light baḍī, fried paṭola, and fried rounds of squash and pumpkin.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.214
description: There was a soup made with fried urad dhal and mung dhal, defeating nectar. There were also sweet chutney and five or six kinds of sour preparations, beginning with baḍāmla.
text:
> bhṛṣṭa-māṣa-mudga-sūpa amṛta nindaya
> madhurāmla, baḍāmlādi amla pāṅca chaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhṛṣṭa]]---fried; [[synonyms:m:māṣa]]---urd //dhal//; [[synonyms:m:mudga]]---mung //dhal//; [[synonyms:s:sūpa]]---soup; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---nectar; [[synonyms:n:nindaya]]---defeating; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]-[[synonyms:a:amla]]---sweet chutney; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]-[[synonyms:a:amla]]---sour preparation made with fried //dhal//; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and so on; [[synonyms:a:amla]]---sour; [[synonyms:p:pāṅca]] [[synonyms:c:chaya]]---five or six kinds.
translation: There was a soup made with fried urad dhal and mung dhal, defeating nectar. There were also sweet chutney and five or six kinds of sour preparations, beginning with baḍāmla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.215
description: There were bharats made of mung dhal, of urd dhal and of sweet bananas, and there was sweet rice cake, coconut cake and various other cakes.
text:
> mudga-baḍā, māṣa-baḍā, kalā-baḍā miṣṭa
> kṣīra-puli, nārikela-pulī āra yata piṣṭa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mudga]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍā]]---fried cakes made of mung //dhal//; [[synonyms:m:māṣa]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍā]]---fried cakes made of //urd dhal//; [[synonyms:k:kalā]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍā]]---fried cakes made of banana; [[synonyms:m:miṣṭa]]---very sweet; [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]-[[synonyms:p:puli]]---cakes made with sweet rice; [[synonyms:n:nārikela]]-[[synonyms:p:pulī]]---coconut cake; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---varieties of; [[synonyms:p:piṣṭa]]---cakes.
translation: There were bharats made of mung dhal, of urd dhal and of sweet bananas, and there was sweet rice cake, coconut cake and various other cakes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.216
description: There was kāṅji-baḍā, dugdha-ciḍā, dugdha-laklakī and various cakes, which I am unable to describe.
text:
> kāṅji-baḍā, dugdha-ciḍā, dugdha-laklakī
> āra yata piṭhā kaila, kahite nā śaki
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāṅji]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍā]]---cakes made with sour rice-water; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]-[[synonyms:c:ciḍā]]---sweet rice mixed with milk; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]-[[synonyms:l:laklakī]]---another preparation of milk and cakes to be licked up; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---various types of; [[synonyms:p:piṭhā]]---cakes; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to describe; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:ś:śaki]]---I am not able.
translation: There was kāṅji-baḍā, dugdha-ciḍā, dugdha-laklakī and various cakes, which I am unable to describe.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.217
description: Sweet rice mixed with ghee was poured into an earthen pot and mixed with cāṅpā-kalā, condensed milk and mango.
text:
> ghṛta-sikta paramānna, mṛt-kuṇḍikā bhari'
> cāṅpākalā-ghanadugdha-āmra tāhā dhari
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:ghṛta]]-[[synonyms:s:sikta]] [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:a:anna]]---sweet rice mixed with ghee; [[synonyms:m:mṛt]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṇḍikā]] [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---filling an earthen pot; [[synonyms:c:cāṅpā]]-[[synonyms:k:kalā]]---a kind of banana; [[synonyms:g:ghana]]-[[synonyms:d:dugdha]]---condensed milk; [[synonyms:ā:āmra]]---mango pulp; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:d:dhari]]---including.
translation: Sweet rice mixed with ghee was poured into an earthen pot and mixed with cāṅpā-kalā, condensed milk and mango.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.218
description: Other preparations included a very delicious churned curd and a variety of sandeśa sweetmeats. Indeed, all the various eatables available in Bengal and Orissa were prepared.
text:
> rasālā-mathita dadhi, sandeśa apāra
> gauḍe utkale yata bhakṣyera prakāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rasālā]]---delicious; [[synonyms:m:mathita]]---churned; [[synonyms:d:dadhi]]---curd; [[synonyms:s:sandeśa]]---a sweetmeat; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:g:gauḍe]]---in Bengal; [[synonyms:u:utkale]]---in Orissa; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhakṣyera]]---of eatables; [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---kinds.
translation: Other preparations included a very delicious churned curd and a variety of sandeśa sweetmeats. Indeed, all the various eatables available in Bengal and Orissa were prepared.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.219
description: Thus Bhaṭṭācārya prepared a great variety of food and spread a fine cloth over a white wooden platform.
text:
> śraddhā kari' bhaṭṭācārya saba karāila
> śubhra-pīṭhopari sūkṣma vasana pātila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---with great respect; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---had them all prepared; [[synonyms:ś:śubhra]]---white; [[synonyms:p:pīṭha]]---a wooden platform; [[synonyms:u:upari]]---over; [[synonyms:s:sūkṣma]]---fine; [[synonyms:v:vasana]]---cloth; [[synonyms:p:pātila]]---spread.
translation: Thus Bhaṭṭācārya prepared a great variety of food and spread a fine cloth over a white wooden platform.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.22
description: It was at this time that Śrīla Advaita Ācārya said, "Please do not be angry. I speak the truth. I shall know whether You are a cowherd boy only if You can wheel this rod about."
text:
> advaita kahe,---satya kahi, nā kariha kopa
> laguḍa phirāite pāra, tabe jāni gopa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaita]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Advaita Ācārya says; [[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I speak the truth; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kariha]] [[synonyms:k:kopa]]---please do not be angry; [[synonyms:l:laguḍa]]---stick, staff; [[synonyms:p:phirāite]] [[synonyms:p:pāra]]---if You can wheel around; [[synonyms:t:tabe]] [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---then I shall understand; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]---cowherd boy.
translation: It was at this time that Śrīla Advaita Ācārya said, "Please do not be angry. I speak the truth. I shall know whether You are a cowherd boy only if You can wheel this rod about."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.220
description: On two sides of the stack of food were pitchers filled with scented cold water. The flowers of the tulasī tree were placed above the mound of rice.
text:
> dui pāśe sugandhi śītala jala-jhārī
> anna-vyañjanopari dila tulasī-mañjarī
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:p:pāśe]]---on two sides; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:g:gandhi]]---nicely scented; [[synonyms:ś:śītala]]---cold; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:j:jhāri]]---pitchers of water; [[synonyms:a:anna]]-[[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]-[[synonyms:u:upari]]---over the rice and vegetables; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---placed; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]-[[synonyms:m:mañjarī]]---flowers of //tulasī.//
translation: On two sides of the stack of food were pitchers filled with scented cold water. The flowers of the tulasī tree were placed above the mound of rice.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.221
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya also included several types of food that had been offered to Lord Jagannātha. This included sweetballs known as amṛta-guṭikā, sweet rice and cakes. All these were kept separately.
text:
> amṛta-guṭikā, piṭhā-pānā ānāila
> jagannātha-prasāda saba pṛthak dharila
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:g:guṭikā]]---the sweet named //amṛta-guṭikā//; [[synonyms:p:piṭhā]]-[[synonyms:p:pānā]]---cakes and sweet rice; [[synonyms:ā:ānāila]]---brought; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---remnants of the food of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]] [[synonyms:d:dharila]]---kept separately.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya also included several types of food that had been offered to Lord Jagannātha. This included sweetballs known as amṛta-guṭikā, sweet rice and cakes. All these were kept separately.
purport: Although the remnants of food left by Jagannātha were brought into Bhaṭṭācārya's house, they were kept separate from the preparations he had made at his home. It sometimes happens that //prasāda// is mixed with a larger quantity of food and then distributed, but in this case we find that Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya kept the //jagannātha-prasāda// separate. He kept it aside particularly for the satisfaction of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.222
description: When everything was ready, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came there alone after finishing His midday duties. He knew the heart of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.
text:
> hena-kāle mahāprabhu madhyāhna kariyā
> ekale āila tāṅra hṛdaya jāniyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:madhyāhna]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---finishing His midday duties; [[synonyms:e:ekale]]---alone; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]---the heart; [[synonyms:j:jāniyā]]---knowing.
translation: When everything was ready, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came there alone after finishing His midday duties. He knew the heart of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.223
description: After Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya washed the Lord's feet, the Lord entered the room to take His lunch.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya kaila tabe pāda prakṣālana
> gharera bhitare gelā karite bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:p:pāda]] [[synonyms:p:prakṣālana]]---washing the feet; [[synonyms:g:gharera]] [[synonyms:b:bhitare]]---within the room; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---entered; [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---to take lunch.
translation: After Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya washed the Lord's feet, the Lord entered the room to take His lunch.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.224
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was a little astonished to see the gorgeous arrangement, and, gesturing, He spoke to Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.
text:
> annādi dekhiyā prabhu vismita hañā
> bhaṭṭācārye kahe kichu bhaṅgi kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anna]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing the arrangement of food; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vismita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being astonished; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārye]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said to Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:b:bhaṅgi]]---gesture; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---making.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was a little astonished to see the gorgeous arrangement, and, gesturing, He spoke to Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.225
description: "This is most uncommon! How was this arrangement of rice and vegetables finished within six hours?
text:
> alaukika ei saba anna-vyañjana
> dui prahara bhitare kaiche ha-ila randhana?
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:alaukika]]---uncommon; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:a:anna]]-[[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---rice and vegetables; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:p:prahara]] [[synonyms:b:bhitare]]---within six hours; [[synonyms:k:kaiche]]---how; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]] [[synonyms:r:randhana]]---cooking was finished.
translation: "This is most uncommon! How was this arrangement of rice and vegetables finished within six hours?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.226
description: "Even a hundred men cooking on a hundred ovens could not possibly finish all these preparations within so short a time.
text:
> śata culāya śata jana pāka yadi kare
> tabu śīghra eta dravya rāndhite nā pāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:c:culāya]]---in one hundred ovens; [[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---one hundred men; [[synonyms:p:pāka]] [[synonyms:y:yadi]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---if engaged in cooking; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]]---so soon; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:d:dravya]]---so many preparations; [[synonyms:r:rāndhite]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---could not cook.
translation: "Even a hundred men cooking on a hundred ovens could not possibly finish all these preparations within so short a time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.227
description: "I hope the food has already been offered to Kṛṣṇa, since I see there are tulasī flowers over the plates.
text:
> kṛṣṇera bhoga lāgāñācha,---anumāna kari
> upare dekhiye yāte tulasī-mañjarī
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:b:bhoga]] [[synonyms:l:lāgāñācha]]---you have offered to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:anumāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I hope; [[synonyms:u:upare]]---upon the food; [[synonyms:d:dekhiye]]---I see; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---since; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]-[[synonyms:m:mañjarī]]---flowers of the //tulasī// tree.
translation: "I hope the food has already been offered to Kṛṣṇa, since I see there are tulasī flowers over the plates.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.228
description: "You are most fortunate, and your endeavor is successful, for you have offered such wonderful food to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> bhāgyavān tumi, saphala tomāra udyoga
> rādhā-kṛṣṇe lāgāñācha etādṛśa bhoga
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāgyavān]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you are fortunate; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]---successful; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:u:udyoga]]---endeavor; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Their Lordships Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:lāgāñācha]]---you offered; [[synonyms:e:etādṛśa]]---such; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---food.
translation: "You are most fortunate, and your endeavor is successful, for you have offered such wonderful food to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.229
description: "The color of the rice is so attractive and its aroma so good that it appears Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa have directly taken it.
text:
> annera saurabhya, varṇa---ati manorama
> rādhā-kṛṣṇa sākṣāt ihāṅ kariyāchena bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:annera]] [[synonyms:s:saurabhya]]---the flavor of the cooked rice; [[synonyms:v:varṇa]]---color; [[synonyms:a:ati]] [[synonyms:m:manorama]]---very attractive; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa and Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---all this; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchena]] [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---have eaten.
translation: "The color of the rice is so attractive and its aroma so good that it appears Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa have directly taken it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.23
description: Accepting Advaita Ācārya's challenge, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took a big rod and began to wheel it around and around. Again and again He threw the rod into the sky and caught it when it fell.
text:
> tabe laguḍa lañā prabhu phirāite lāgilā
> bāra bāra ākāśe pheli' luphiyā dharilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:l:laguḍa]]---rod; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:phirāite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to wheel it around; [[synonyms:b:bāra]] [[synonyms:b:bāra]]---again and again; [[synonyms:ā:ākāśe]]---in the sky; [[synonyms:p:pheli']]---throwing; [[synonyms:l:luphiyā]]---tossing; [[synonyms:d:dharilā]]---He captured.
translation: Accepting Advaita Ācārya's challenge, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took a big rod and began to wheel it around and around. Again and again He threw the rod into the sky and caught it when it fell.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.230
description: "My dear Bhaṭṭācārya, your fortune is very great. How much shall I praise you? I also am very fortunate to be able to take the remnants of this food.
text:
> tomāra bahuta bhāgya kata praśaṁsiba
> āmi---bhāgyavān, ihāra avaśeṣa pāba
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:b:bahuta]]---great; [[synonyms:b:bhāgya]]---fortune; [[synonyms:k:kata]]---how much; [[synonyms:p:praśaṁsiba]]---shall I praise; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bhāgyavān]]---fortunate; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of this; [[synonyms:a:avaśeṣa]]---remnants; [[synonyms:p:pāba]]---shall get.
translation: "My dear Bhaṭṭācārya, your fortune is very great. How much shall I praise you? I also am very fortunate to be able to take the remnants of this food.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.231
description: "Take away Kṛṣṇa's sitting place and put it aside. Then give me prasāda on a different plate."
text:
> kṛṣṇera āsana-pīṭha rākhaha uṭhāñā
> more prasāda deha' bhinna pātrete kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āsana]]-[[synonyms:p:pīṭha]]---the sitting place; [[synonyms:r:rākhaha]]---keep aside; [[synonyms:u:uthāñā]]---raising; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---prasāda; [[synonyms:d:deha']]---give; [[synonyms:b:bhinna]]---separate; [[synonyms:p:pātrete]]---on a plate; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---putting.
translation: "Take away Kṛṣṇa's sitting place and put it aside. Then give me prasāda on a different plate."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.232
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "It is not so wonderful, my Lord. Everything has been made possible by the energy and mercy of He who will eat the food.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya bale---prabhu nā karaha vismaya
> yei khābe, tāṅhāra śaktye bhoga siddha haya

translation: "Now please sit in this place and take Your lunch." Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "This place is worshipable because it was used by Kṛṣṇa."
purport: According to etiquette, things used by Kṛṣṇa should not be used by anyone else. Similarly, things used by the spiritual master should also not be used by anyone else. That is etiquette. Whatever is used by Kṛṣṇa or the spiritual master is worshipable. In particular, their sitting or eating places should not be used by anyone else. A devotee must be very careful to observe this.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.237
description: " 'My dear Lord, the garlands, scented substances, garments, ornaments and other such things that have been offered to You may later be used by Your servants. By partaking of these things and eating the remnants of food You have left, we will be able to conquer the illusory energy.' "
text:
> tvayopayukta-srag-gandha-
> vāso 'laṅkāra-carcitāḥ
> ucchiṣṭa-bhojino dāsās
> tava māyāṁ jayema hi
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tvayā]]---by You; [[synonyms:u:upayukta]]---used; [[synonyms:s:srak]]---flower garlands; [[synonyms:g:gandha]]---scented substances like sandalwood pulp; [[synonyms:v:vāsaḥ]]---garments; [[synonyms:a:alaṅkāra]]---ornaments; [[synonyms:c:carcitāḥ]]---being decorated with; [[synonyms:u:ucchiṣṭa]]---remnants of food; [[synonyms:b:bhojinaḥ]]---eating; [[synonyms:d:dāsāḥ]]---servants; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:m:māyām]]---illusory energy; [[synonyms:j:jayema]]---can conquer over; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly.
translation: “ 'My dear Lord, the garlands, scented substances, garments, ornaments and other such things that have been offered to You may later be used by Your servants. By partaking of these things and eating the remnants of food You have left, we will be able to conquer the illusory energy.' "
purport:
This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.6.46). In the Hare Kṛṣṇa movement, the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra,// the dancing in ecstasy and the eating of the remnants of food offered to the Lord are very, very important. One may be illiterate or incapable of understanding the philosophy, but if he partakes of these three items, he will certainly be liberated without delay.

This verse was spoken by Uddhava to Lord Kṛṣṇa. This was during the time when the //Uddhava-gītā// was spoken. At that time there was some disturbance in Dvārakā, and Lord Kṛṣṇa had to leave the material world and enter the spiritual world. Uddhava could understand the situation, and he talked with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The verse quoted above is an excerpt from their conversations. Śrī Kṛṣṇa's pastimes in this material world are called //prakaṭa-līlā// (manifested pastimes), and His pastimes in the spiritual world are called //aprakaṭa-līlā// (unmanifested pastimes). By unmanifested we mean that they are not present before our eyes. It is not that Lord Kṛṣṇa's pastimes are unmanifest. They are going on exactly as the sun is going on perpetually, but when the sun is present before our eyes, we call it daytime (manifest), and when it is not present, we call it night (unmanifest). Those who are above the jurisdiction of night are always in the spiritual world, where the Lord's pastimes are constantly manifest to them. As the //Brahma-saṁhitā// confirms:

> ānanda-cinmaya-rasa-pratibhāvitābhis
> tābhir ya eva nija-rūpatayā kalābhiḥ
> goloka eva nivasaty akhilātma-bhūto
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
>
> premāñjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena
> santaḥ sadaiva hṛdayeṣu vilokayanti
> yaṁ śyāmasundaram acintya-guṇa-svarūpaṁ
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi

"I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who resides in His own realm, Goloka, with Rādhā, who resembles His own spiritual figure and who embodies the ecstatic potency [//hlādinī//]. Their companions are Her confidantes, who embody extensions of Her bodily form and who are imbued and permeated with everblissful spiritual //rasa.// I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who is Śyāmasundara, Kṛṣṇa Himself with inconceivable innumerable attributes, whom the pure devotees see in their heart of hearts with the eye of devotion tinged with the salve of love." (Bs. 5.37-38)

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.238

translation: "At Dvārakā, You keep sixteen thousand queens in sixteen thousand palaces. Also, there are eighteen mothers and numerous friends and relatives of the Yadu dynasty.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.241
description: "In Vṛndāvana You also have Your father's elder brothers, Your father's younger brothers, maternal uncles, husbands of Your father's sisters and many cowherd men. There are also cowherd boy friends, and You eat twice a day, morning and evening, in the house of each and every one.
text:
> vraje jyeṭhā, khuḍā, māmā, pisādi gopa-gaṇa
> sakhā-vṛnda sabāra ghare dvisandhyā-bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---at Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:j:jyeṭhā]]---the father's elder brothers; [[synonyms:k:khuḍā]]---the father's younger brothers; [[synonyms:m:māmā]]---the mother's brothers; [[synonyms:p:pisā]]---the husbands of aunts; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and so on; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---cowherd men; [[synonyms:s:sakhā]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---hundreds of friends; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in the houses; [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:s:sandhyā]]---twice a day; [[synonyms:b:bho]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---eating.
translation: "In Vṛndāvana You also have Your father's elder brothers, Your father's younger brothers, maternal uncles, husbands of Your father's sisters and many cowherd men. There are also cowherd boy friends, and You eat twice a day, morning and evening, in the house of each and every one.
purport: In Dvārakā, Lord Kṛṣṇa had eighteen mothers like Devakī, Rohiṇī and others. Besides these was. His foster mother Yaśodā in Vṛndāvana. Lord Kṛṣṇa also had two uncles, who were brothers of Nanda Mahārāja. As stated by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī in his //Śrī-kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, upanando 'bhinandaś ca pitṛvyau pūr-va-jau pituḥ:// "The elder brothers of Nanda Mahārāja were Upananda and Abhinanda." Similarly, in the same book the names of the younger brothers of Nanda Mahārāja are given. //Pitṛvyau tu kanīyāṁsau syātāṁ sannanda-nandanau:// "Sannanda and Nandana, or Sunanda and Pāṇḍava, were the younger brothers of Kṛṣṇa's father, Nanda Mahārāja." Śrī Kṛṣṇa's maternal uncles were also described there. //Yaśodhara-yaśodeva-sudevādyās tu mātulāḥ:// "Yaśodhara, Yaśodeva and Sudeva were the maternal uncles of Kṛṣṇa." Kṛṣṇa's uncles are also mentioned. //Mahānīlaḥ sunīlaś ca ramaṇāv etayoḥ kramāt:// "Mahānīla and Sunīla are the husbands of Kṛṣṇa's aunts."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.242
description: "Indeed," Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya continued, "at the Govardhana-pūjā ceremony You ate stacks of rice. In comparison to that, this small quantity is not even a morsel for You.
text:
> govardhana-yajñe anna khāilā rāśi rāśi
> tāra lekhāya ei anna nahe eka grāsī

translation: "Indeed," Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya continued, "at the Govardhana-pūjā ceremony You ate stacks of rice. In comparison to that, this small quantity is not even a morsel for You.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.243
description: "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whereas I am a most insignificant living being. Therefore You may accept a little quantity of food from my house."
text:
> tumi ta' īśvara, muñi---kṣudra jīva chāra
> eka-grāsa mādhukarī karaha aṅgīkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kṣudra]] [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---insignificant living being; [[synonyms:c:chāra]]---worthless; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:g:grāsa]]---one small quantity; [[synonyms:m:mādhu]]-[[synonyms:k:karī]]---as collected by the bees; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---please do; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---accept.
translation: "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whereas I am a most insignificant living being. Therefore You may accept a little quantity of food from my house."
purport: A //sannyāsī// is expected to collect a little food from each and every householder. That is to say, he should take whatever he requires to eat. This system is called //mādhukarī.// The word //mādhukarī// comes from the word //mādhukara// and means "honey-collecting bees." Bees collect a little honey from each flower, but all these small quantities of honey accumulate to become a beehive. //Sannyāsīs// should collect a little from each and every householder and should eat simply what is necessary to maintain the body. Being a //sannyāsī,// Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu could collect a little food from the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, and this was the Bhaṭṭācārya's request. Compared to the food eaten by the Lord on other occasions, Bhaṭṭācārya's feast was not even a morsel. This is what Bhaṭṭācārya is pointing out to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.244

translation: Hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu smiled and sat down to eat. Bhaṭṭācārya, with great pleasure, first offered Him the prasāda from the Jagannātha temple.

translation: At this time Bhaṭṭācārya had a son-in-law named Amogha, who was the husband of his daughter named Ṣāṭhī. Although born in an aristocratic brāhmaṇa family, this Amogha was a great faultfinder and blasphemer.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.246
description: Amogha wanted to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu eat, but he was not allowed to enter. Indeed, Bhaṭṭācārya guarded the threshold of his house with a stick in his hand.

translation: Amogha wanted to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu eat, but he was not allowed to enter. Indeed, Bhaṭṭācārya guarded the threshold of his house with a stick in his hand.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.247
description: However, as soon as Bhaṭṭācārya began distributing prasāda and was a little inattentive, Amogha came in. Seeing the quantity of food, he began to blaspheme.
text:
> teṅho yadi prasāda dite hailā āna-mana
> amogha āsi' anna dekhi' karaye nindana

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.261
description: "If the man who blasphemed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is killed, his sinful action may be atoned."
text:
> caitanya-gosāñira nindā śunila yāhā haite
> tāre vadha kaile haya pāpa-prāyaścitte
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nindā]]---blasphemy; [[synonyms:ś:śunila]]---I have heard; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from whom; [[synonyms:t:tāre]] [[synonyms:v:vadha]] [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---if he is killed; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]-[[synonyms:p:prāyaścitte]]---atonement for the sinful act.
translation: "If the man who blasphemed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is killed, his sinful action may be atoned."
purport:
The //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa// cites the following quotation from //Skanda Purāṇa// concerning the blaspheming of a Vaiṣṇava:

> yo hi bhāgavataṁ lokam
> upahāsaṁ nṛpottama
> karoti tasya naśyanti
> artha-dharma-yaśaḥ-sutāḥ
>
> nindāṁ kurvanti ye mūḍhā
> vaiṣṇavānāṁ mahātmanām
> patanti pitṛbhiḥ sārdhaṁ
> mahā-raurava-saṁjñite
>
> hanti nindati vai dveṣṭi
> vaiṣṇavān nābhinandati
> krudhyate yāti no harṣaṁ
> darśane patanāni ṣaṭ

In this conversation between Mārkaṇḍeya and Bhagīratha, it is said: "My dear King, if one derides an exalted devotee, he loses the results of his pious activities, his opulence, his reputation and his sons. Vaiṣṇavas are all great souls. Whoever blasphemes them falls down to the hell known as Mahāraurava. He is also accompanied by his forefathers. Whoever kills or blasphemes a Vaiṣṇava and whoever is envious of a Vaiṣṇava or angry with him, or whoever does not offer him obeisances or feel joy upon seeing a Vaiṣṇava, certainly falls into a hellish condition."

The //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa// (10.314) also gives the following quotation from //Dvārakā-māhātmya://

> kara-patraiś ca phālyante
> sutīvrair yama-śāsanaiḥ
> nindāṁ kurvanti ye pāpā
> vaiṣṇavānāṁ mahātmanām

In a conversation between Prahlāda Mahārāja and Bali Mahārāja, it is said, "Those sinful people who blaspheme Vaiṣṇavas, who are all great souls, are subjected very severely to the punishment offered by Yamarāja."

In the //Bhakti-sandarbha// (313) there is a statement concerning the blaspheming of Lord Viṣṇu.

> ye nindanti hṛṣīkeśaṁ
> tad-bhaktaṁ puṇya-rūpiṇam
> śata-janmārjitaṁ puṇyaṁ
> teṣāṁ naśyati niścitam
>
> te pacyante mahā-ghore
> kumbhīpāke bhayānake
> bhakṣitāḥ kīṭa-saṅghena
> yāvac candra-divākarau
> śrī-viṣṇor avamānanād
> gurutaraṁ śrī-vaiṣṇavollaṅghanam
>
> tadīya-dūṣaka-janān
> na paśyet puruṣādhamān
> taiḥ sārdhaṁ vañcaka-janaiḥ
> saha-vāsaṁ na kārayet

"One who criticizes Lord Viṣṇu and His devotees loses all the benefits accrued in a hundred pious births. Such a person rots in the Kumbhīpāka hell and is bitten by worms as long as the sun and moon exist. One should therefore not even see the face of a person who blasphemes Lord Viṣṇu and His devotees. Never try to associate with such persons."

In his //Bhakti-sandarbha// (265), Jīva Gosvāmī further quotes from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.74.40):

> nindāṁ bhagavataḥ śṛṇvan
> tat-parasya janasya vā
> tato nāpaiti yaḥ so 'pi
> yāty adhaḥ sukṛtāc cyutaḥ

"If one does not immediately leave upon hearing the Lord or the Lord's devotee blasphemed, he falls down from devotional service." Similarly, Lord Śiva's wife Satī states in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:4:4:17|(4.4.17)]]:

> karṇau pidhāya nirayād yad akalpa īśe
> dharmāvitary asṛṇibhir nṛbhir asyamāne
> chindyāt prasahya ruśatīm asatīṁ prabhuś cej
> jihvām asūn api tato visṛjet sa dharmaḥ

"If one hears an irresponsible person blaspheme the master and controller of religion, he should block his ears and go away if unable to punish him. But if one is able to kill, then one should by force cut out the blasphemer's tongue and kill the offender, and after that he should give up his own life."

description: "Instead, I shall never see the face of that blasphemer. I reject him and give up his relationship. I shall never even speak his name.

> parityāga kailuṅ, tāra nāma nā la-iba

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.264
description: "Inform my daughter Ṣāṭhī to abandon her relationship with her husband because he has fallen down. When the husband falls down, it is the wife's duty to relinquish the relationship.
text:
> ṣāṭhīre kaha---tāre chāḍuka, se ha-ila 'patita'
> 'patita' ha-ile bhartā tyajite ucita
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣāṭhīre]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---inform Ṣāṭhī; [[synonyms:t:tāre]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍuka]]---let her give him up; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---he has become; [[synonyms:p:patita]]---fallen; [[synonyms:p:patita]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ile]]---when one has fallen; [[synonyms:b:bhartā]]---such a husband; [[synonyms:t:tyajite]]---to give up; [[synonyms:u:ucita]]---is the duty.
translation: "Inform my daughter Ṣāṭhī to abandon her relationship with her husband because he has fallen down. When the husband falls down, it is the wife's duty to relinquish the relationship.
purport:
Śrīla Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya considered that if Amogha were killed, one would suffer sinful reactions for killing the body of a //brāhmaṇa.// For the same reason, it would have been undesirable for Bhaṭṭācārya to commit suicide because he also was a //brāhmaṇa.// Since neither course could be accepted, Bhaṭṭācārya decided to give up his relationship with Amogha and never see his face.

As far as killing the body of a //brāhmaṇa// is concerned, //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:7:53|(1.7.53)]] gives the following injunction:

> śrī-bhagavān uvāca
> brahma-bandhur na hantavya
> ātatāyī vadhār-haṇaḥ
> mayaivobhayam āmnātaṁ
> paripāhy anuśāsanam

"The Personality of Godhead Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: A friend of a //brāhmaṇa// is not to be killed, but if he is an aggressor, he must be killed. All these rulings are in the scriptures, and you should act accordingly."

Quoting from the //smṛti,// Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī comments on this quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam://

> ātatāyinam āyāntam
> api vedānta-pāragam
> jighāṁ-santaṁ jighāṁsīyān
> na tena brahmahā bhavet

"Even though an aggressor may be a very learned scholar of Vedānta, he should be killed because of his envy in killing others. In such a case, it is not sinful to kill a //brāhmaṇa."//

It is also stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:7:57|(1.7.57)]]:

> vapanaṁ draviṇādānaṁ
> sthānān niryāpaṇaṁ tathā
> eṣa hi brahma-bandhūnāṁ
> vadho nānyo 'sti daihikaḥ

"Cutting the hair from his head, depriving him of his wealth and driving him from his residence are the prescribed punishments for the relative of a //brāhmaṇa.// There is no injunction for killing the body."

Such punishment is sufficient for a //brahma-bandhu.// There is no need to personally kill his body. As far as Ṣāṭhī, the daughter of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, was concerned, she was advised to give up her relationship with her husband. Concerning this, //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:5:5:18|(5.5.18)]] states, //na patiś ca sa syān na mocayed yaḥ samupeta-mṛtyum:// "One cannot be a husband if he cannot liberate his dependents from inevitable death." If a person is not in Kṛṣṇa consciousness and is bereft of spiritual power, he cannot protect his wife from the path of repeated birth and death. Consequently such a person cannot be accepted as a husband. A wife should dedicate her life and everything to Kṛṣṇa for further advancement in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. If she gives up her connection with her husband, who abandons Kṛṣṇa consciousness, she follows in the footsteps of the //dvija-patnī,// the wives of the //brāhmaṇas// who were engaged in performing sacrifices. The wife is not to be condemned for cutting off such a relationship. In this regard, Śrī Kṛṣṇa states in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.23.31-32):

> patayo nābhyasūyeran
> pitṛ-bhrātṛ-sutādayaḥ
> lokāś ca vo mayopetā
> devā apy anumanvate
>
> na prītaye 'nurāgāya
> hy aṅga-saṅgo nṛṇām iha
> tan mano mayi yuñjānā
> acirān mām avāpsyatha

Such a separation is never condemned by the supreme will. No one should be envious of the order of Kṛṣṇa. Even demigods support such action. In this material world, one does not become beloved simply by maintaining a bodily relationship. However, one can attain complete perfection by associating in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.265
description: "When a husband is fallen, his relationship must be given up."
text: > patiṁ ca patitaṁ tyajet

translation: "When a husband is fallen, his relationship must be given up."
purport:
This is a quotation from //smṛti-śāstram.// As stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:7:11:28|(7.11.28)]]:

> santuṣṭālolupā dakṣā
> dharma-jñā priya-satya-vāk
> apramattā śuciḥ snigdhā
> patiṁ tv apatitaṁ bhajet

"A wife who is satisfied, who is not greedy, who is expert and knows religious principles, who speaks what is dear and truthful and is not bewildered, who is always clean and affectionate, should be very devoted to her husband who is not fallen."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.269
description: " 'What we have had to arrange with great endeavor by collecting elephants, horses, chariots and infantry soldiers has already been accomplished by the Gandharvas.'
text:
> mahatā hi prayatnena
> hasty-aśva-ratha-pattibhiḥ
> asmābhir yad anuṣṭheyaṁ
> gandharvais tad anuṣṭhitam
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahatā]]---very great; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:p:prayatnena]]---by endeavor; [[synonyms:h:hasti]]---elephants; [[synonyms:a:aśva]]---horses; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]---chariots; [[synonyms:p:pattibhiḥ]]---and by infantry soldiers; [[synonyms:a:asmābhiḥ]]---by ourselves; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---whatever; [[synonyms:a:anuṣṭheyaṁ]]---has to be arranged; [[synonyms:g:gandharvaiḥ]]---by the Gandharvas; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:a:anuṣṭhitam]]---done.
translation: “ 'What we have had to arrange with great endeavor by collecting elephants, horses, chariots and infantry soldiers has already been accomplished by the Gandharvas.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Mahābhārata// (//Vana-parva// 241.15). Bhīmasena made this statement when all the Pāṇḍavas were living incognito. At that time there was a fight between the Kauravas and the Gandharvas. The Kaurava soldiers were under the command of Karṇa, but the commander-in-chief of the Gandharvas was able to arrest all the Kauravas by virtue of superior military strength. At that time Duryodhana's ministers and commanders, who were living in the forest, requested Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira to help. After being thus petitioned, Bhīmasena spoke the verse given above, remembering Duryodhana's former nefarious and atrocious activities against them. Indeed, Bhīmasena felt it very fitting that Duryodhana and his company were arrested. This could have been accomplished by the Pāṇḍavas only with great endeavor.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.270
description: " 'When a person mistreats great souls, his life span, opulence, reputation, religion, possessions and good fortune are all destroyed.'
text:
> āyuḥ śriyaṁ yaśo dharmaṁ
> lokān āśiṣa eva ca
> hanti śreyāṁsi sarvāṇi
> puṁso mahad-atikramaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āyuḥ]]---duration of life; [[synonyms:ś:śriyam]]---opulence; [[synonyms:y:yaśaḥ]]---reputation; [[synonyms:d:dharmam]]---religion; [[synonyms:l:lokān]]---possessions; [[synonyms:ā:āśiṣaḥ]]---benedictions; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:h:hanti]]---destroys; [[synonyms:ś:śreyāṁsi]]---good fortune; [[synonyms:s:sarvāṇi]]---all; [[synonyms:p:puṁsaḥ]]---of a person; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]---of great souls; [[synonyms:a:atikramaḥ]]---violation.
translation: “ 'When a person mistreats great souls, his life span, opulence, reputation, religion, possessions and good fortune are all destroyed.'
purport:
This is a statement made by Śukadeva Gosvāmī, who was relating //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.4.46) to Mahārāja Parīkṣit. This quotation concerns the attempted killing of Kṛṣṇa's sister (Yogamāyā), who appeared before Kṛṣṇa's birth as the daughter of mother Yaśodā. This daughter Yogamāyā and Kṛṣṇa were born simultaneously, and Vasudeva replaced Kṛṣṇa by taking Yogamāyā away. When she was brought to Mathurā and Kaṁsa attempted to kill her, Yogamāyā slipped out of his hands. She could not be killed. She then informed Kaṁsa about the birth of his enemy, Kṛṣṇa, and being thus baffled, Kaṁsa consulted his associates, who were all demons. When this big conspiracy was taking place, this verse was spoken by Śukadeva Gosvāmī. He points out that a demon can lose everything because of his nefarious activities.

The word //mahad-atikramaḥ,// meaning "envy of Lord Viṣṇu and His devotees," is significant in this verse. The word //mahat// indicates a great personality, a devotee or the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. Being always engaged in the

Lord's service, the devotees themselves are as great as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The word //mahat// is also explained in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:13|(Bg. 9.13)]]:

> mahātmānas tu māṁ pārtha
> daivīṁ prakṛtim āśritāḥ
> bhajanty ananya-manaso
> jñātvā bhūtādim avyayam

"O son of Pṛthā, those who are not deluded, the great souls, are under the protection of the divine nature. They are fully engaged in devotional service because they know Me as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, original and inexhaustible."

Being envious of the Lord and His devotees is not at all auspicious for a demon. By such envy, a demon loses everything considered beneficial.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.277
description: "Therefore, Amogha, get up and chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra! If you do so, Kṛṣṇa will unfailingly bestow mercy upon you."
text:
> uṭhaha, amogha, tumi lao kṛṣṇa-nāma
> acire tomāre kṛpā karibe bhagavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uṭhaha]]---get up; [[synonyms:a:amogha]]---Amogha; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:l:lao]]---chant; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:acire]]---very soon; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---unto you; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---will bestow; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: "Therefore, Amogha, get up and chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra! If you do so, Kṛṣṇa will unfailingly bestow mercy upon you."
purport:
The Absolute Truth is realized in three phases-impersonal Brahman, Paramātmā and the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Bhagavān. All of these are one and the same truth, but Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān constitute three different features. Whoever understands Brahman is called a //brāhmaṇa,// and when a //brāhmaṇa// engages in the Lord's devotional service, he is called a Vaiṣṇava. Unless one comes to understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead, his realization of impersonal Brahman is imperfect. A //brāhmaṇa// can chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// on the platform of //nāmābhāsa,// but not on the platform of pure vibration. When a //brāhmaṇa// engages in the Lord's service, fully understanding his eternal relationship, his devotional service is called //abhidheya.// When one attains that stage, he is called a //bhāgavata// or a Vaiṣṇava. This indicates that he is free from contamination and material attachment. This is confirmed by //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:7:28|(Bg. 7.28)]]:

> yeṣāṁ tv anta-gataṁ pāpaṁ
> janānāṁ puṇya-karmaṇām
> te dvandva-moha-nirmuktā
> bhajante māṁ dṛḍha-vratāḥ

"Persons who have acted piously in previous lives and in this life, whose sinful actions are completely eradicated and who are freed from the duality of delusion, engage themselves in My service with determination."

A //brāhmaṇa// may be a very learned scholar, but this does not mean that he is free from material contamination. A //brāhmaṇa's// contamination, however, is in the mode of goodness. In the material world, the three modes are goodness, passion and ignorance, and all of these are simply different gradations of contamination. Unless a //brāhmaṇa// transcends such contamination and approaches the platform of unalloyed devotional service, he cannot be accepted as a Vaiṣṇava. An impersonalist may be aware of the impersonal Brahman feature of the Absolute Truth, but his activities are on the impersonal platform. Sometimes he imagines a form of the Lord (//saguṇa-upāsanā),// but such an attempt is never successful in helping one attain complete realization. The impersonalist may consider himself a //brāhmaṇa// and may be situated in the mode of goodness, but nonetheless he is conditioned by one of the modes of material nature. This means that he is not yet liberated, for liberation cannot be attained unless one is completely free from the modes. In any case, the Māyāvāda philosophy keeps one conditioned. If one becomes a Vaiṣṇava through proper initiation, he automatically becomes a //brāhmaṇa.// There is no doubt about it. The //Garuḍa Purāṇa// confirms this:

> brāhmaṇānāṁ sahasrebhyaḥ
> satra-yājī viśiṣyate
> satra-yāji-sahasrebhyaḥ
> sarva-vedānta-pāragaḥ
>
> sarva-vedānta-vit-koṭyā
> viṣṇu-bhakto viśiṣyate

"Out of many thousands of //brāhmaṇas,// one may become qualified to perform //yajña.// Out of many thousands of such qualified //brāhmaṇas,// one may be fully aware of the Vedānta philosophy. Out of many millions of learned Vedānta scholars, there may be one //viṣṇu-bhakta,// or devotee of Lord Viṣṇu. It is he who is most exalted."

Unless one is a fully qualified //brāhmaṇa,// he cannot advance in the spiritual science. A real //brāhmaṇa// is never envious of Vaiṣṇavas. If he is, he is considered an imperfect neophyte. Impersonalist //brāhmaṇas// are always opposed to Vaiṣṇava principles. They are envious of Vaiṣṇavas because they do not know the goal of life. //Na te viduḥ svārtha-gatiṁ hi viṣṇum.// However, when a //brāhmaṇa// becomes a Vaiṣṇava, there is no duality. If a //brāhmaṇa// does not become a Vaiṣṇava, he certainly falls down from the //brāhmaṇa// platform. This is confirmed by //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.3): //na bhajanty avajānanti sthānād bhraṣṭāḥ patanty adhaḥ.//

We can actually see that in this Age of Kali many so-called //brāhmaṇas// are envious of Vaiṣṇavas. The Kali-contaminated //brāhmaṇas// consider Deity worship to be imaginative: //arcye viṣṇau śilā-dhīr guruṣu nara-matir vaiṣṇave jāti-buddhiḥ.// Such a contaminated //brāhmaṇa// may superficially imagine a form of the Lord, but actually he considers the Deity in the temple to be made of stone or wood. Similarly, such a contaminated //brāhmaṇa// considers the //guru// to be an ordinary human being, and he objects when a Vaiṣṇava is created by the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. Many so-called //brāhmaṇas// attempt to fight us, saying, "How can you create a //brāhmaṇa// out of a European or American? A //brāhmaṇa// can be born only in a //brāhmaṇa// family." They do not consider that this is never stated in any revealed scripture. It is specifically stated in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:4:13|(Bg. 4.13)]]: //cātur-varṇyaṁ mayā sṛṣṭaṁ guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśaḥ.// "According to the three modes of material nature and the work ascribed to them, the four divisions of human society were created by Me."

Thus a //brāhmaṇa// is not a result of the caste system. He becomes a //brāhmaṇa// only by qualification. Similarly, a Vaiṣṇava does not belong to a particular caste; rather, his designation is determined by the rendering of devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.278
description: After hearing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and being touched by Him, Amogha, who was on his deathbed, immediately stood up and began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Thus he became mad with ecstatic love and began to dance emotionally.
text:
> śuni' 'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa' bali' amogha uṭhilā
> premonmāde matta hañā nācite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---speaking; [[synonyms:a:amogha]] [[synonyms:u:uṭhilā]]---Amogha stood up; [[synonyms:p:premonmāde]]---in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:matta]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming maddened; [[synonyms:n:nācite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to dance.
translation: After hearing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and being touched by Him, Amogha, who was on his deathbed, immediately stood up and began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Thus he became mad with ecstatic love and began to dance emotionally.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.279
description: While Amogha danced in ecstatic love, he manifested all the ecstatic symptoms-trembling, tears, jubilation, trance, perspiration and a faltering voice. Seeing these waves of ecstatic emotion, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to laugh.
text:
> kampa, aśru, pulaka, stambha, sveda, svara-bhaṅga
> prabhu hāse dekhi' tāra premera taraṅga
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]---jubilation; [[synonyms:s:stambha]]---being stunned; [[synonyms:s:sveda]]---perspiration; [[synonyms:s:svara]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṅga]]---faltering of the voice; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:h:hāse]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to laugh; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---Amogha's; [[synonyms:p:premera]] [[synonyms:t:taraṅga]]---waves of ecstatic love.
translation: While Amogha danced in ecstatic love, he manifested all the ecstatic symptoms-trembling, tears, jubilation, trance, perspiration and a faltering voice. Seeing these waves of ecstatic emotion, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to laugh.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.28
description: This valuable cloth was wrapped around the head of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The other devotees, headed by Advaita Ācārya, also had cloths wrapped about their heads.
text:
> bahu-mūlya vastra prabhu-mastake bāndhila
> ācāryādi prabhura gaṇere parāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:m:mūlya]]---very valuable; [[synonyms:v:vastra]]---cloth; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:m:mastake]]---on the head of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bāndhila]]---wrapped; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gaṇere]]---on the associates; [[synonyms:p:parāila]]---put.
translation: This valuable cloth was wrapped around the head of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The other devotees, headed by Advaita Ācārya, also had cloths wrapped about their heads.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.280
description: Amogha then fell before the Lord's lotus feet and submissively said, "O merciful Lord, please excuse my offense."
text:
> prabhura caraṇe dhari' karaye vinaya
> aparādha kṣama more, prabhu, dayāmaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching; [[synonyms:k:karaye]]---does; [[synonyms:v:vinaya]]---submission; [[synonyms:a:aparādha]]---offense; [[synonyms:k:kṣama]]---kindly excuse; [[synonyms:m:more]]---me; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---O Lord; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---merciful.
translation: Amogha then fell before the Lord's lotus feet and submissively said, "O merciful Lord, please excuse my offense."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.281
description: Not only did Amogha beg the Lord's pardon, but he also began slapping his own cheeks, saying, "By this mouth I have blasphemed You."
text:
> ei chāra mukhe tomāra karinu nindane
> eta bali' āpana gāle caḍāya āpane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:c:chāra]] [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in this abominable mouth; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:k:karinu]]---I did; [[synonyms:n:nindane]]---blaspheming; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]---his own; [[synonyms:g:gāle]]---cheeks; [[synonyms:c:caḍāya]]---he slapped; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---himself.
translation: Not only did Amogha beg the Lord's pardon, but he also began slapping his own cheeks, saying, "By this mouth I have blasphemed You."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.282
description: Indeed, Amogha continued slapping his face over and over until his cheeks were swollen. Finally Gopīnātha Ācārya stopped him by catching hold of his hands.
text:
> caḍāite caḍāite gāla phulāila
> hāte dhari' gopīnāthācārya niṣedhila
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caḍāite]] [[synonyms:c:caḍāite]]---slapping over and over again; [[synonyms:g:gāla]]---the cheeks; [[synonyms:p:phulāila]]---he made them swollen; [[synonyms:h:hāte]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching his hands; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:n:niṣedhila]]---forbade.
translation: Indeed, Amogha continued slapping his face over and over until his cheeks were swollen. Finally Gopīnātha Ācārya stopped him by catching hold of his hands.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.283
description: After this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu pacified Amogha by touching his body and saying, "You are the object of My affection because you are the son-in-law of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.
text:
> prabhu āśvāsana kare sparśi' tāra gātra
> sārvabhauma-sambandhe tumi mora sneha-pātra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āśvāsana]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---pacifies; [[synonyms:s:sparśi']]---touching; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his; [[synonyms:g:gātra]]---body; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]-[[synonyms:s:sambandhe]]---because of a relation to Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:s:sneha]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---object of affection.
translation: After this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu pacified Amogha by touching his body and saying, "You are the object of My affection because you are the son-in-law of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.284
description: "Everyone in Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's house is very dear to Me, including his maids and servants and even his dog. And what to speak of his relatives?
text:
> sārvabhauma-gṛhe dāsa-dāsī, ye kukkura
> seha mora priya, anya jana rahu dūra

translation: "Everyone in Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's house is very dear to Me, including his maids and servants and even his dog. And what to speak of his relatives?

description: "Amogha, always chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra and do not commit any further offenses." After giving Amogha this instruction, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Sārvabhauma's house."
text:

synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aparādha']] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---do not commit offenses; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:l:lao]]---chant; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra//; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---to the place of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.
translation: "Amogha, always chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra and do not commit any further offenses." After giving Amogha this instruction, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Sārvabhauma's house."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.286
description: Upon seeing the Lord, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya immediately caught hold of His lotus feet. The Lord also embraced him and sat down.
text:
> prabhu dekhi' sārvabhauma dharilā caraṇe
> prabhu tāṅre āliṅgiyā vasilā āsane
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:d:dharilā]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---caught hold of His feet; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgiyā]]---embracing; [[synonyms:v:vasilā]] [[synonyms:ā:āsane]]---sat down on the seat.

text:

> kene upavāsa kara, kene kara roṣa

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu pacified Sārvabhauma, saying, "After all, Amogha, your son-in-law, is a child. So what is his fault? Why are you fasting, and why are you angry?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.288
description: "Just get up and take your bath and go see the face of Lord Jagannātha. Then return here to eat your lunch. In this way I shall be happy.
text:
> uṭha, snāna kara, dekha jagannātha-mukha
> śīghra āsi, bhojana kara, tabe mora sukha
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uṭha]]---get up; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---take your bath; [[synonyms:d:dekha]]---see; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---Lord Jagannātha's face; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi]]---coming back very soon; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---take your lunch; [[synonyms:t:tabe]] [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---then I shall be very happy.

text:
> tāvat rahiba āmi ethāya vasiyā
> yāvat nā khāibe tumi prasāda āsiyā

translation: In ecstasy, Kānāñi Khuṭiyā, who was dressed as Nanda Mahārāja, and Jagannātha Māhāti, who was dressed as mother Yaśodā, distributed all the riches they had stocked at home.

translation: Catching hold of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's lotus feet, Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Why did You bring Amogha back to life? It would have been better had he died."

> ebe 'vaiṣṇava' haila, tāra gela 'aparādha'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.293
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, " Please go, my Lord, to see Lord Jagannātha. After taking my bath, I shall go there and then return."

> bhaṭṭa kahe,---cala, prabhu, īśvara-daraśane
> snāna kari' tāṅhā muñi āsichoṅ ekhane

translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, " Please go, my Lord, to see Lord Jagannātha. After taking my bath, I shall go there and then return."

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then told Gopīnātha, "Stay here and inform Me when Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya has taken his prasāda."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.295

translation: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to see Lord Jagannātha. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya completed his bath, went to see Lord Jagannātha and then returned to his house to accept food.

translation: Thereafter, Amogha became an unalloyed devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He danced in ecstasy and peacefully chanted the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.297

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.298
description: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu enjoyed eating in Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's house. Within that one pastime, many wonderful pastimes were manifest.

translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu enjoyed eating in Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's house. Within that one pastime, many wonderful pastimes were manifest.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.299
description: These are the peculiar characteristics of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastimes. Thus the Lord ate in Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's house, and in this way Sārvabhauma's love for the Lord has become very well known.
text:
> sārvabhauma-ghare ei bhojana-carita
> sārvabhauma-prema yāṅhā ha-ilā vidita
