translation: The Lord then with great respect extended an invitation to all the inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma, asking them to come every year and bring silken rope to carry Lord Jagannātha during the Ratha-yātrā festival.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 15.99
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "Guṇarāja Khān of Kulīna-grāma compiled a book named Śrī Kṛṣṇa-vijaya in which there is a sentence revealing the author's ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> guṇarāja-khāṅna kaila śrī-kṛṣṇa-vijaya
> tāhāṅ eka-vākya tāṅra āche premamaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:guṇarāja]]-[[synonyms:k:khāṅna]]---Guṇarāja Khān; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---compiled; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:vijaya]]---the book named //Śrī Kṛṣṇa-vijaya//; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:v:vākya]]---one sentence; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of it; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---is; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---full of love of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "Guṇarāja Khān of Kulīna-grāma compiled a book named Śrī Kṛṣṇa-vijaya in which there is a sentence revealing the author's ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa."
purport:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa-vijaya is a book of poems considered to be the first poetry book written in Bengal. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura states that this book was compiled in the year 1395 //śakābda// (A.D. 1474). After seven years, it was completed (1402 //śakābda//). This book was written in plain language, and even half-educated Bengalis and women could read it very clearly. Even ordinary men with little knowledge of the alphabet could read this book and understand it. Its language is not very ornamental, and sometimes the poetry is not very sweet to hear. Although according to the sonnet style each line should contain fourteen syllables, there are sometimes sixteen, twelve and thirteen syllables in his verse. Many words used in those days could be understood only by local inhabitants, yet this book is still so popular that no book store is complete without it. It is very valuable for those who are interested in advancing in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

Śrī Guṇarāja Khān was one of the topmost Vaiṣṇavas, and he has translated the Tenth and Eleventh Cantos of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// for the understanding of the common man. The book //Śrī Kṛṣṇa-vijaya// was highly praised by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and it is very valuable for all Vaiṣṇavas. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura gives a genealogical table and family history of Guṇarāja Khān. When a Bengali emperor named Ādiśūra first came from Kānyakubja, or Kānowj, he brought with him five //brāhmaṇas// and five //kāyasthas.// Since the king is supposed to be accompanied by his associates, the //brāhmaṇas// accompanied the King to help him in higher spiritual matters. The //kāyasthas// were to render other services. In the northern Indian high country, the //kāyasthas// are accepted as //śūdras,// but in Bengal the //kāyasthas// are considered among the higher castes. It is a fact that the //kāyasthas// came to Bengal from northern India, specifically from Kānyakubja, or Kānowj. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that the //kāyasthas// who came from Kānyakubja were high-class men. Of them, Daśaratha Vasu was a great personality, and the thirteenth generation of his family included Guṇarāja Khān.

His real name was Mālādhara Vasu, but the title Khān was given to him by the Emperor of Bengal. Thus he became known as Guṇarāja Khān. Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura gives the following genealogical table of Guṇarāja Khān: (1) Daśaratha Vasu; (2) Kuśala; (3) Śubhaśaṅkara; (4) Haṁsa; (5) Śaktirāma (Bāgāṇḍā), Muktirāma (Māinagara) and Alaṅkāra (Baṅgaja); (6) Dāmodara; (7) Anantarāma; (8) Guṇīnāyaka and Vīṇānāyaka. The twelfth generation included Bhagīratha, and the thirteenth Mālādhara Vasu, or Guṇarāja Khān. Śrī Guṇarāja Khān had fourteen sons, of whom the second son, Lakṣmīnāthavasu, received the title Satyarāja Khān. His son was Śrī Rāmānanda Vasu; therefore Rāmānanda Vasu belonged to the fifteenth generation. Guṇarāja Khān was a very well known and wealthy man. His palace, fort and temples are still existing, and from these we can deduce that the opulence of Guṇarāja Khān was certainly very great. Śrī Guṇarāja Khān never cared for the artificial aristocracy introduced by Ballāl Sena.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.1
description: By the nectar of His personal glance, the cloud known as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu poured water upon the garden of Gauḍa-deśa and revived the people, who were like creepers and plants burning in the forest fire of material existence.
text:
> gauḍodyānaṁ gaura-meghaḥ
> siñcan svālokanāmṛtaiḥ
> bhavāgni-dagdha-janatā-
> vīrudhaḥ samajīvayat
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]-[[synonyms:u:udyānam]]---upon the garden known as Gauḍa-deśa; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:m:meghaḥ]]---the cloud known as Gaura; [[synonyms:s:siñcan]]---pouring water; [[synonyms:s:sva]]---His own; [[synonyms:ā:ālokana]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛtaiḥ]]---with the nectar of the glance; [[synonyms:b:bhava]]-[[synonyms:a:agni]]---by the blazing fire of material existence; [[synonyms:d:dagdha]]---having been burnt; [[synonyms:j:janatā]]---the people in general; [[synonyms:v:vīrudhaḥ]]---who are like creepers and plants; [[synonyms:s:samajīvayat]]---revived.
translation: By the nectar of His personal glance, the cloud known as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu poured water upon the garden of Gauḍa-deśa and revived the people, who were like creepers and plants burning in the forest fire of material existence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.10
description: In this way they both presented many impediments, indirectly not granting the Lord permission to go to Vṛndāvana. They did this because they were afraid of separation from Him.
text:
> āji-kāli kari' uṭhāya vividha upāya
> yāite sammati nā deya vicchedera bhaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āji]]-[[synonyms:k:kāli]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---delaying today and tomorrow; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāya]]---they put forward; [[synonyms:v:vividha]] [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---many devices; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go; [[synonyms:s:sammati]]---permission; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:deya]]---did not give; [[synonyms:v:vicchedera]] [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---because of fearing separation.
translation: In this way they both presented many impediments, indirectly not granting the Lord permission to go to Vṛndāvana. They did this because they were afraid of separation from Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.100
description: After reaching the city of Kaṭaka, He saw the temple of Gopāla, and a brāhmaṇa there named Svapneśvara invited the Lord to eat.
text:
> 'kaṭake' āsiyā kaila 'gopāla' daraśana
> svapneśvara-vipra kaila prabhura nimantraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kaṭake]]---to the city of Kaṭaka; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:s:svapneśvara]]-[[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the brāhmaṇa named Svapneśvara; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation.
translation: After reaching the city of Kaṭaka, He saw the temple of Gopāla, and a brāhmaṇa there named Svapneśvara invited the Lord to eat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.101
description: Rāmānanda Rāya invited all the others for their meals, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu made His resting place in a garden outside the temple.
text:
> rāmānanda-rāya saba-gaṇe nimantrila
> bāhira udyāne āsi' prabhu vāsā kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:s:saba]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---all the followers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nimantrila]]---invited; [[synonyms:b:bāhira]] [[synonyms:u:udyāne]]---in an outside garden; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made His resting place.
translation: Rāmānanda Rāya invited all the others for their meals, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu made His resting place in a garden outside the temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.102
description: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was taking rest beneath a bakula tree, Rāmānanda Rāya immediately went to Mahārāja Pratāparudra.
text:
> bhikṣā kari' bakula-tale karilā viśrāma
> pratāparudra-ṭhāñi rāya karila payāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---after taking lunch; [[synonyms:b:bakula]]-[[synonyms:t:tale]]---underneath a //bakula// flower tree; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:v:viśrāma]]---took rest; [[synonyms:p:pratāparudra]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---to the presence of Mahārāja Pratāparudra; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:p:payāna]]---departed.
translation: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was taking rest beneath a bakula tree, Rāmānanda Rāya immediately went to Mahārāja Pratāparudra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.103
description: The King was very happy to hear the news, and he hastily went there. Upon seeing the Lord, he fell flat to offer Him obeisances.
text:
> śuni' ānandita rājā ati-śīghra āilā
> prabhu dekhi' daṇḍavat bhūmete padilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very pleased; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:a:ati]]-[[synonyms:ś:śīghra]]---hastily; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]]---obeisances offered falling flat; [[synonyms:b:bhūmete]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down. obeisances offered falling flat; [[synonyms:b:bhūmete]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down.
translation: The King was very happy to hear the news, and he hastily went there. Upon seeing the Lord, he fell flat to offer Him obeisances.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.104
description: Being overwhelmed with love, the King again and again got up and fell down. When he offered prayers, his whole body shivered, and tears fell from his eyes.
text:
> punaḥ uṭhe, punaḥ paḍe praṇaya-vihvala
> stuti kare, pulakāṅga, paḍe aśru-jala
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---he arose; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---he fell down; [[synonyms:p:praṇaya]]-[[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---overwhelmed with love; [[synonyms:s:stuti]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---offers prayers; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the entire body quivering in joy; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fell down; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]-[[synonyms:j:jala]]---tears.
translation: Being overwhelmed with love, the King again and again got up and fell down. When he offered prayers, his whole body shivered, and tears fell from his eyes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.105
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to see the King's devotion, and He therefore stood up and embraced him.
text:
> tāṅra bhakti dekhi' prabhura tuṣṭa haila mana
> uṭhi' mahāprabhu tāṅre kailā āliṅgana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---his devotion; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tuṣṭa]]---pleased; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---standing up; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embraced.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to see the King's devotion, and He therefore stood up and embraced him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.106
description: When the Lord embraced the King, the King again and again offered prayers and obeisances. In this way, the Lord's mercy brought tears from the King, and the Lord's body was bathed with these tears.
text:
> punaḥ stuti kari' rājā karaye praṇāma
> prabhu-kṛpā-aśrute tāṅra deha haila snāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:s:stuti]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---offering prayers; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:p:praṇāma]]---offered obeisances; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---of the mercy of the Lord; [[synonyms:a:aśrute]]---by the tears; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---the body; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathed.
translation: When the Lord embraced the King, the King again and again offered prayers and obeisances. In this way, the Lord's mercy brought tears from the King, and the Lord's body was bathed with these tears.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.107
description: Finally Rāmānanda Rāya pacified the King and made him sit down. The Lord also bestowed mercy upon him through His body, mind and words.
text:
> sustha kari, rāmānanda rājāre vasāilā
> kāya-mano-vākye prabhu tāṅre kṛpā kailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sustha]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---comforting him; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāya Rāmānanda; [[synonyms:r:rājāre]] [[synonyms:v:vasāilā]]---made the King sit down; [[synonyms:k:kāya]]-[[synonyms:m:mano]]-[[synonyms:v:vākye]]---with body, mind and words; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto the King; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---showed His mercy.
translation: Finally Rāmānanda Rāya pacified the King and made him sit down. The Lord also bestowed mercy upon him through His body, mind and words.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.108
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu showed such mercy to the King that from that day on the Lord became known as Pratāparudra-santrātā, the deliverer of Mahārāja Pratāparudra.
text:
> aiche tāṅhāre kṛpā kaila gaurarāya
> "pratāparudra-santrātā" nāma haila yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāre]]---unto the King; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---showed; [[synonyms:g:gaurarāya]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pratāparudra]]-[[synonyms:s:santrātā]]---the deliverer of Mahārāja Pratāparudra; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---by which.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu showed such mercy to the King that from that day on the Lord became known as Pratāparudra-santrātā, the deliverer of Mahārāja Pratāparudra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.109
description: All the governmental officers also paid their respects to the Lord, and finally the King and his men were bade farewell by the son of mother Śacī.
text:
> rāja-pātra-gaṇa kaila prabhura vandana
> rājāre vidāya dilā śacīra nandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the officers of the King; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---glorifying the Lord; [[synonyms:r:rājāre]]---unto the King; [[synonyms:v:vidāya]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---bade farewell; [[synonyms:ś:śacīra]] [[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of mother Śacī.
translation: All the governmental officers also paid their respects to the Lord, and finally the King and his men were bade farewell by the son of mother Śacī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.11
description: Although the Lord is completely independent and incapable of being checked by anyone, He still did not go without the permission of His devotees.
text:
> yadyapi svatantra prabhu nahe nivāraṇa
> bhakta-icchā vinā prabhu nā kare gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]]---fully independent; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nahe]] [[synonyms:n:nivāraṇa]]---there is no checking Him; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:i:icchā]] [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without the permission of devotees; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---does not go.
translation: Although the Lord is completely independent and incapable of being checked by anyone, He still did not go without the permission of His devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.110
description: The King then went outside and had orders written down and sent to the government servants within his kingdom.
text:
> bāhire āsi' rājā ājñā-patra lekhāila
> nija-rājye yata 'viṣayī', tāhāre pāṭhāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāhire]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming outside; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]-[[synonyms:p:patra]]---letters of command; [[synonyms:l:lekhāila]]---had written; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:r:rājye]]---in his own kingdom; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:v:viṣayī]]---government servants; [[synonyms:t:tāhāre]]---unto them; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāila]]---sent.
translation: The King then went outside and had orders written down and sent to the government servants within his kingdom.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.111
description: His orders read: "In every village you should construct new residences, and in five or seven new houses, you should store all kinds of food.
text:
> 'grāme-grāme' nūtana āvāsa karibā
> pāṅca-sāta navya-gṛhe sāmagrye bharibā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:grāme]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in every village; [[synonyms:n:nūtana]]---new; [[synonyms:ā:āvāsa]]---residential places; [[synonyms:k:karibā]]---you should construct; [[synonyms:p:pāṅca]]-[[synonyms:s:sāta]]---five to seven; [[synonyms:n:navya]]-[[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---in new houses; [[synonyms:s:sāmagrye]]---with food; [[synonyms:b:bharibā]]---you should fill.
translation: His orders read: "In every village you should construct new residences, and in five or seven new houses, you should store all kinds of food.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.112
description: "You should personally take the Lord to these newly constructed houses. Day and night you should engage in His service with a stick in your hands."
text:
> āpani prabhuke lañā tāhāṅ uttaribā
> rātri-dibā vetra-haste sevāya rahibā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āpani]]---personally, yourself; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:u:uttaribā]]---you should go there; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dibā]]---night and day; [[synonyms:v:vetra]]-[[synonyms:h:haste]]---with a cane in the hands; [[synonyms:s:sevāya]] [[synonyms:r:rahibā]]---should remain engaged in His service.
translation: "You should personally take the Lord to these newly constructed houses. Day and night you should engage in His service with a stick in your hands."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.113
description: The King ordered two respectable officers named Haricandana and Mardarāja to do whatever was necessary to carry out these orders.
text:
> dui mahā-pātra,---'haricandana', 'mardarāja'
> tāṅre ājñā dila rājā---'kariha sarva kāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---two respectable officers; [[synonyms:h:haricandana]]---Haricandana; [[synonyms:m:mardarāja]]---Mardarāja; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to them; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave orders; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do; [[synonyms:s:sarva]] [[synonyms:k:kāya]]---everything needed.
translation: The King ordered two respectable officers named Haricandana and Mardarāja to do whatever was necessary to carry out these orders.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.114-115
description: The King also ordered them to maintain a new boat on the banks of the river, and wherever Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took His bath or crossed to the other side of the river, they should establish a memorial column and make that place a great place of pilgrimage. "Indeed," said the King, "I will take my bath there. And let me also die there."
text:
> eka navya-naukā āni' rākhaha nadī-tīre
> yāhāṅ snāna kari' prabhu yā'na nadī-pāre
>
> tāhāṅ stambha ropaṇa kara 'mahā-tīrtha' kari'
> nitya snāna kariba tāhāṅ, tāhāṅ yena mari
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:n:navya]]---new; [[synonyms:n:naukā]]---boat; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:r:rākhaha]]---keep; [[synonyms:n:nadī]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank of the river; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking bath; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yā'na]]---goes; [[synonyms:n:nadī]]-[[synonyms:p:pāre]]---on the other bank of the river; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:s:stambha]]---a memorial column; [[synonyms:r:ropaṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---establish; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrtha]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making that place a great place of pilgrimage; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---daily; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---I shall bathe; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:y:yena]] [[synonyms:m:mari]]---let me die.
translation: The King also ordered them to maintain a new boat on the banks of the river, and wherever Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took His bath or crossed to the other side of the river, they should establish a memorial column and make that place a great place of pilgrimage. "Indeed," said the King, "I will take my bath there. And let me also die there."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.116
description: The King continued, "At Caturdvāra, please construct new residential quarters. Now, Rāmānanda, you can return to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu."
text:
> caturdvāre karaha uttama navya vāsa
> rāmānanda, yāha tumi mahāprabhu-pāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caturdvāre]]---at the place named Caturdvāra; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---make; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]---very nice; [[synonyms:n:navya]] [[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---new residential quarters; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:y:yāha]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you please go; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---near Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: The King continued, "At Caturdvāra, please construct new residential quarters. Now, Rāmānanda, you can return to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.117
description: When the King heard that the Lord was leaving that evening, he immediately made arrangements for some elephants with small tents on their backs to be brought there. Then all the ladies of the palace got on the elephants.
text:
> sandhyāte calibe prabhu,---nṛpati śunila
> hastī-upara tāmbu-gṛhe strī-gaṇe caḍāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sandhyāte]]---in the evening; [[synonyms:c:calibe]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord will start; [[synonyms:n:nṛpati]] [[synonyms:ś:śunila]]---the King heard; [[synonyms:h:hastī]]-[[synonyms:u:upara]]---upon the backs of elephants; [[synonyms:t:tāmbu]]-[[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---in tents; [[synonyms:s:strī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---all the ladies; [[synonyms:c:caḍāila]]---made get up.
translation: When the King heard that the Lord was leaving that evening, he immediately made arrangements for some elephants with small tents on their backs to be brought there. Then all the ladies of the palace got on the elephants.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.118
description: All these ladies went to the road the Lord was taking and remained there in a line. That evening, the Lord departed with His devotees.
text:
> prabhura calibāra pathe rahe sāri hañā
> sandhyāte calilā prabhu nija-gaṇa lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:c:calibāra]] [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the route of walking; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remained; [[synonyms:s:sāri]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being in a line; [[synonyms:s:sandhyāte]]---in the evening; [[synonyms:c:calilā]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord departed; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking His own men.
translation: All these ladies went to the road the Lord was taking and remained there in a line. That evening, the Lord departed with His devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.119
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to the bank of the River Citrotpalā to take His bath, all the queens and ladies of the palace offered their obeisances to Him.
text:
> 'citrotpalā-nadī' āsi' ghāṭe kaila snāna
> mahiṣī-sakala dekhi' karaye praṇāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:citrotpalā]]-[[synonyms:n:nadī]]---to the river named Citrotpalā; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:g:ghāṭe]]---on the bank; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---took a bath; [[synonyms:m:mahiṣī]]-[[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all the queens and ladies of the palace; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:p:praṇāma]]---offered their obeisances.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to the bank of the River Citrotpalā to take His bath, all the queens and ladies of the palace offered their obeisances to Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.12
description: Then, for the third year, all the devotees of Bengal wanted to return again to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> tṛtīya vatsare saba gauḍera bhakta-gaṇa
> nīlācale calite sabāra haila mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tṛtīya]] [[synonyms:v:vatsare]]---in the third year; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:g:gauḍera]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---devotees from Bengal; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:c:calite]]---to go; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: Then, for the third year, all the devotees of Bengal wanted to return again to Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.120
description: Upon seeing the Lord, they all felt themselves overwhelmed with love of Godhead, and, tears pouring from their eyes, they began to chant the holy name, "Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!"
text:
> prabhura daraśane sabe haila premamaya
> 'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa' kahe, netra aśru variṣaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---by seeing the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---overwhelmed with love; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---chanted the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:netra]]---the eyes; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:v:variṣaya]]---poured.
translation: Upon seeing the Lord, they all felt themselves overwhelmed with love of Godhead, and, tears pouring from their eyes, they began to chant the holy name, "Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.121
description: There is no one as merciful as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu within all three worlds. Simply by seeing Him from a distance, one is overwhelmed with love of Godhead.
text:
> emana kṛpālu nāhi śuni tribhuvane
> kṛṣṇa-premā haya yāṅra dūra daraśane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:emana]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpālu]]---such a merciful person; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---we hear; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvane]]---within the three worlds; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:premā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---one gets love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---by seeing from a distance.
translation: There is no one as merciful as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu within all three worlds. Simply by seeing Him from a distance, one is overwhelmed with love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.122
description: The Lord then got into a new boat and crossed the river. Walking in the full moonlight, He finally reached the town known as Caturdvāra.
text:
> naukāte caḍiyā prabhu haila nadī pāra
> jyotsnāvatī rātrye cali' āilā caturdvāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:naukāte]] [[synonyms:c:caḍiyā]]---getting on the boat; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:n:nadī]] [[synonyms:p:pāra]]---across the river; [[synonyms:j:jyotsnāvatī]]---lighted by the full moon; [[synonyms:r:rātrye]]---in the night; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---walking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:c:caturdvāra]]---to Caturdvāra.
translation: The Lord then got into a new boat and crossed the river. Walking in the full moonlight, He finally reached the town known as Caturdvāra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.123
description: The Lord spent the night there and in the morning took His bath. At that time, remnants of Lord Jagannātha's food arrived.
text:
> rātrye tathā rahi' prāte snāna-kṛtya kaila
> hena-kāle jagannāthera mahā-prasāda āila
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rātrye]]---on that night; [[synonyms:t:tathā]] [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---staying there; [[synonyms:p:prāte]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---took His bath; [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time; [[synonyms:j:jagannāthera]]---of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---remnants of food arrived.
translation: The Lord spent the night there and in the morning took His bath. At that time, remnants of Lord Jagannātha's food arrived.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.124
description: Following the King's orders, the superintendent of the temple sent large quantities of prasāda every day, and it was carried by many persons.
text:
> rājāra ājñāya paḍichā pāṭhāya dine-dine
> bahuta prasāda pāṭhāya diyā bahu-jane
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rājāra]] [[synonyms:ā:ājñāya]]---by the order of the King; [[synonyms:p:paḍichā]]---the superintendent of the temple; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāya]]---sent; [[synonyms:d:dine]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---day after day; [[synonyms:b:bahuta]] [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---a large quantity of food; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāya]]---he sent; [[synonyms:d:diyā]] [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---carried by many persons.
translation: Following the King's orders, the superintendent of the temple sent large quantities of prasāda every day, and it was carried by many persons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.125
description: After accepting the prasāda, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stood up and started to go, chanting the holy names, "Hari! Hari!"
text:
> svagaṇa-sahite prabhu prasāda aṅgīkari'
> uṭhiyā calilā prabhu bali' 'hari' 'hari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sahite]]---with His personal associates; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---the remnants of food; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:u:uṭhiyā]]---standing up; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---started; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---uttering; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---Hari, Hari.
translation: After accepting the prasāda, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stood up and started to go, chanting the holy names, "Hari! Hari!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.126
description: Rāmānanda Rāya, Mardarāja and Śrī Haricandana always went with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and rendered various services.
text:
> rāmānanda, mardarāja, śrī-haricandana
> saṅge sevā kari' cale ei tina jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda; [[synonyms:m:mardarāja]]---Mardarāja; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:h:haricandana]]---Śrī Haricandana; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in company; [[synonyms:s:sevā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---rendering service; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---went; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---these three gentlemen.
translation: Rāmānanda Rāya, Mardarāja and Śrī Haricandana always went with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and rendered various services.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.127-129
description: Paramānanda Purī Gosvāmī, Svarūpa Dāmodara, Jagadānanda, Mukunda, Govinda, Kāśīśvara, Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Vakreśvara Paṇḍita, Gopīnātha Ācārya, Dāmodara Paṇḍita, Rāmāi, Nandāi and many other devotees accompanied the Lord. I have mentioned only the chief devotees. No one can describe the total number.
text:
> prabhu-saṅge purī-gosāñi, svarūpa-dāmodara
> jagadānanda, mukunda, govinda, kāśīśvara
>
> haridāsa-ṭhākura, āra paṇḍita-vakreśvara
> gopīnāthācārya, āra paṇḍita-dāmodara
>
> rāmāi, nandāi, āra bahu bhakta-gaṇa
> pradhāna kahiluṅ, sabāra ke kare gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:j:jagadānanda]]---Jagadānanda; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:k:kāśīśvara]]---Kāśīśvara; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]-[[synonyms:v:vakreśvara]]---Paṇḍita Vakreśvara; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]-[[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Paṇḍita Dāmodara; [[synonyms:r:rāmāi]]---Rāmāi; [[synonyms:n:nandāi]]---Nandāi; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:b:bahu]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---many devotees; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---the chief; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have mentioned; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:k:ke]]---who; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---can make an account.
translation: Paramānanda Purī Gosvāmī, Svarūpa Dāmodara, Jagadānanda, Mukunda, Govinda, Kāśīśvara, Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Vakreśvara Paṇḍita, Gopīnātha Ācārya, Dāmodara Paṇḍita, Rāmāi, Nandāi and many other devotees accompanied the Lord. I have mentioned only the chief devotees. No one can describe the total number.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.13
description: All the Bengali devotees gathered around Advaita Ācārya, and in great jubilation Advaita Ācārya departed to Jagannātha Purī to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> sabe meli' gelā advaita ācāryera pāśe
> prabhu dekhite ācārya calilā ullāse
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---everyone; [[synonyms:m:meli']]---after assembling together; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---Advaita; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]]---of the leader of Navadvīpa; [[synonyms:p:pāśe]]---in the presence; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---departed; [[synonyms:u:ullāse]]---in great jubilation.
translation: All the Bengali devotees gathered around Advaita Ācārya, and in great jubilation Advaita Ācārya departed to Jagannātha Purī to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.130
description: When Gadādhara Paṇḍita started to go with the Lord, he was forbidden to come and was asked not to give up the vow of kṣetra-sannyāsa.
text:
> gadādhara-paṇḍita yabe saṅgete calilā
> 'kṣetra-sannyāsa nā chāḍiha'---prabhu niṣedhilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gadādhara]]-[[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---Gadādhara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:s:saṅgete]]---with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---started to go; [[synonyms:k:kṣetra]]-[[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---the renounced order of life at a holy place of pilgrimage; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍiha]]---do not give up; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:n:niṣedhilā]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu forbade.
translation: When Gadādhara Paṇḍita started to go with the Lord, he was forbidden to come and was asked not to give up the vow of kṣetra-sannyāsa.
purport: When one takes //kṣetra-sannyāsa,// he leaves his household life and goes to a place of pilgrimage devoted to Lord Viṣṇu. Such places include Puruṣottama (Jagannātha Purī), Navadvīpa-dhāma and Mathurā-dhāma. The //kṣetra-sannyāsī// lives in these places alone or with his family. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura considers //kṣetra-sannyāsa// to be the preferable //vānaprastha// situation in this Age of Kali. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya lived in this way, and he has been called a //kṣetra-sannyāsī---//that is, a //sannyāsī// living in Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.131
description: When he was requested to return to Jagannātha Purī, Gadādhara Paṇḍita told the Lord, "Wherever You are staying is Jagannātha Purī. Let my so-called kṣetra-sannyāsa go to hell."
text:
> paṇḍita kahe,---"yāhāṅ tumi, sei nīlācala
> kṣetra-sannyāsa mora yāuka rasātala"
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Gadādhara Paṇḍita said; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You are situated; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:n:nīlācala]]---Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:k:kṣetra]]-[[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---vow to remain in a holy place of pilgrimage; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:y:yāuka]]---let it go; [[synonyms:r:rasātala]]---to hell.
translation: When he was requested to return to Jagannātha Purī, Gadādhara Paṇḍita told the Lord, "Wherever You are staying is Jagannātha Purī. Let my so-called kṣetra-sannyāsa go to hell."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.132
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked Gadādhara Paṇḍita to remain at Jagannātha Purī and engage in Gopīnātha's service, Gadādhara Paṇḍita replied, "One renders service to Gopīnātha a million times simply by seeing Your lotus feet."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---"iṅhā kara gopīnātha sevana"
> paṇḍita kahe,---"koṭi-sevā tvat-pāda-darśana"
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:i:iṅhā]]---here; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---just do; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]] [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---worship of Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the //paṇḍita// said; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]]---millions of times the service; [[synonyms:t:tvat]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:d:darśana]]---seeing Your lotus feet.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked Gadādhara Paṇḍita to remain at Jagannātha Purī and engage in Gopīnātha's service, Gadādhara Paṇḍita replied, "One renders service to Gopīnātha a million times simply by seeing Your lotus feet."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.133
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "If you abandon His service, it will be My fault. It is better that you remain here and render service. That will be My satisfaction."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---"sevā chāḍibe, āmāya lāge doṣa
> iṅhā rahi' sevā kara,---āmāra santoṣa"
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:s:sevā]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍibe]]---you will give up the service; [[synonyms:ā:āmāya]]---to Me; [[synonyms:l:lāge]]---will attach; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---fault; [[synonyms:i:iṅhā]] [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---staying here; [[synonyms:s:sevā]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---just be engaged in service; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---satisfaction.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "If you abandon His service, it will be My fault. It is better that you remain here and render service. That will be My satisfaction."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.134
description: The Paṇḍita replied, "Do not worry. All the faults will be on my head. I shall not accompany You but shall go alone.
text:
> paṇḍita kahe,---"saba doṣa āmāra upara
> tomā-saṅge nā yāiba, yāiba ekeśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Paṇḍita said; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---fault; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:u:upara]]---upon me; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with You; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāiba]]---I shall not go; [[synonyms:y:yāiba]]---I shall go; [[synonyms:e:ekeśvara]]---alone.
translation: The Paṇḍita replied, "Do not worry. All the faults will be on my head. I shall not accompany You but shall go alone.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.135
description: "I shall go to see Śacīmātā, but I shall not go for Your sake. I shall be responsible for the abandoning of my vow and service to Gopīnātha."
text:
> āi'ke dekhite yāiba, nā yāiba tomā lāgi'
> 'pratijñā'-'sevā'-tyāga-doṣa, tāra āmi bhāgī"
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āi'ke]]---mother Śacīdevī; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:y:yāiba]]---I shall go; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāiba]]---I shall not go; [[synonyms:t:tomā]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for Your sake; [[synonyms:p:pratijñā]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]]---the vow and service to Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:t:tyāga]]-[[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---the fault of giving up; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---for that; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:b:bhāgī]]---I am responsible.
translation: "I shall go to see Śacīmātā, but I shall not go for Your sake. I shall be responsible for the abandoning of my vow and service to Gopīnātha."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.136
description: Thus Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī traveled alone, but when they all arrived at Kaṭaka, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu called him, and he went in the Lord's company.
text:
> eta bali' paṇḍita-gosāñi pṛthak calilā
> kaṭaka āsi' prabhu tāṅre saṅge ānāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Gadādhara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]] [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---proceeded separately; [[synonyms:k:kaṭaka]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---when He came to Kaṭaka; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Him; [[synonyms:ā:ānāilā]]---brought.
translation: Thus Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī traveled alone, but when they all arrived at Kaṭaka, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu called him, and he went in the Lord's company.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.137
description: No one can understand the loving intimacy between Gadādhara Paṇḍita and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Gadādhara Paṇḍita gave up his vow and service to Gopīnātha just as one gives up a piece of straw.
text:
> paṇḍitera gaurāṅga-prema bujhana nā yāya
> 'pratijñā', 'śrī-kṛṣṇa-sevā' chāḍila tṛṇa-prāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paṇḍitera]]---of Gadādhara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:g:gaurāṅga]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]---the love for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bujhana]]---understanding; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---is not possible; [[synonyms:p:pratijñā]]---a vow; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]]---the service of the Lord; [[synonyms:c:chāḍila]]---gave up; [[synonyms:t:tṛṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prāya]]---almost like straw.
translation: No one can understand the loving intimacy between Gadādhara Paṇḍita and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Gadādhara Paṇḍita gave up his vow and service to Gopīnātha just as one gives up a piece of straw.
purport: Just to get Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's association, Gadādhara Paṇḍita gave up his life's vow to engage in Gopīnātha's service. This kind of loving affection can be understood only by very confidential devotees. Ordinarily, no one can understand its purport.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.138
description: Gadādhara Paṇḍita's behavior was very pleasing to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's heart. Nevertheless, the Lord took his hand and spoke to him, displaying the anger of love.
text:
> tāṅhāra caritre prabhu antare santoṣa
> tāṅhāra hāte dhari' kahe kari' praṇaya-roṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:c:caritre]]---in his behavior; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---within His heart; [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---very satisfied; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:h:hāte]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching his hand; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---exhibiting; [[synonyms:p:praṇaya]]-[[synonyms:r:roṣa]]---anger in love.
translation: Gadādhara Paṇḍita's behavior was very pleasing to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's heart. Nevertheless, the Lord took his hand and spoke to him, displaying the anger of love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.139
description: "You have abandoned Gopīnātha's service and broken your vow to live in Purī. All that is now complete because you have come so far.
text:
> 'pratijñā', 'sevā' chāḍibe,---e tomāra 'uddeśa'
> se siddha ha-ila---chāḍi' āilā dūra deśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pratijñā]]---the vow; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---and service; [[synonyms:c:chāḍibe]]---will give up; [[synonyms:e:e]]---this; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:u:uddeśa]]---purpose; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:s:siddha]]---complete; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---has become; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---have come; [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:d:deśa]]---to a distant place.
translation: "You have abandoned Gopīnātha's service and broken your vow to live in Purī. All that is now complete because you have come so far.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.14-15
description: Although the Lord told Nityānanda Prabhu to stay in Bengal and spread ecstatic love of God, Nityānanda left to go see Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Who can understand Nityānanda Prabhu's ecstatic love?
text:
> yadyapi prabhura ājñā gauḍete rahite
> nityānanda-prabhuke prema-bhakti prakāśite
>
> tathāpi calilā mahāprabhure dekhite
> nityānandera prema-ceṣṭā ke pāre bujhite
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---the order; [[synonyms:g:gauḍete]] [[synonyms:r:rahite]]---to stay in Bengal; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---unto Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---ecstatic love of Godhead; [[synonyms:p:prakāśite]]---to preach; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---departed; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:n:nityānandera]]---of Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:c:ceṣṭā]]---the activities of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:k:ke]]---who; [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---is able; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand.
translation: Although the Lord told Nityānanda Prabhu to stay in Bengal and spread ecstatic love of God, Nityānanda left to go see Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Who can understand Nityānanda Prabhu's ecstatic love?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.140
description: "Your wanting to go with Me is simply a desire for sense gratification. In this way, you are breaking two religious principles, and because of this I am very unhappy.
text:
> āmāra saṅge rahite cāha,---vāñcha nija-sukha
> tomāra dui dharma yāya,---āmāra haya 'duḥkha'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Me; [[synonyms:r:rahite]]---to remain; [[synonyms:c:cāha]]---you want; [[synonyms:v:vāñcha]]---you desire; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]---your own sense gratification; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---two principles; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---go away; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---of Me; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness.
translation: "Your wanting to go with Me is simply a desire for sense gratification. In this way, you are breaking two religious principles, and because of this I am very unhappy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.141
description: "If you want My happiness, please return to Nīlācala. You will simply condemn Me if you say any more about this matter."
text:
> mora sukha cāha yadi, nīlācale cala
> āmāra śapatha, yadi āra kichu bala
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mora]]---of Me; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---the satisfaction; [[synonyms:c:cāha]]---you want; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]] [[synonyms:c:cala]]---go back to Jagannātha Purī (Nīlācala); [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śapatha]]---My condemnation; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---more; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:b:bala]]---you say.
translation: "If you want My happiness, please return to Nīlācala. You will simply condemn Me if you say any more about this matter."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.142
description: Saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu got into a boat, and Gadādhara Paṇḍita immediately fell down in an unconscious state.
text:
> eta bali' mahāprabhu naukāte caḍilā
> mūrcchita hañā paṇḍita tathāi paḍilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:naukāte]] [[synonyms:c:caḍilā]]---got on a boat; [[synonyms:m:mūrcchita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---fainting; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:t:tathāi]]---there; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down.
translation: Saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu got into a boat, and Gadādhara Paṇḍita immediately fell down in an unconscious state.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.143
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya to take Gadādhara Paṇḍita with him. The Bhaṭṭācārya told Gadādhara Paṇḍita, "Get up! Such are the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> paṇḍite lañā yāite sārvabhaume ājñā dilā
> bhaṭṭācārya kahe,---"uṭha, aiche prabhura līlā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paṇḍite]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking the Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---unto Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave an order; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:u:uṭha]]---please get up; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the way of the Lord's pastimes.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya to take Gadādhara Paṇḍita with him. The Bhaṭṭācārya told Gadādhara Paṇḍita, "Get up! Such are the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.144
description: "You should know that Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself violated His own promise just to keep the promise of Grandfather Bhīṣma.
text:
> tumi jāna, kṛṣṇa nija-pratijñā chāḍilā
> bhakta kṛpā-vaśe bhīṣmera pratijñā rākhilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:j:jāna]]---you know; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:p:pratijñā]]---His own promise; [[synonyms:c:chāḍilā]]---gave up; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśe]]---being obliged by the devotional service of a devotee; [[synonyms:b:bhīṣmera]]---of Grandfather Bhīṣma; [[synonyms:p:pratijñā]] [[synonyms:r:rākhilā]]---kept the promise.
translation: "You should know that Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself violated His own promise just to keep the promise of Grandfather Bhīṣma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.145
description: " 'Intending to make my promise true, Lord Kṛṣṇa broke His own promise not to take up a weapon at Kurukṣetra. With His outer garment falling off, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa jumped from His chariot, picked up a wheel and came running at me to kill me. Indeed, He rushed at me like a lion going to kill an elephant, and He caused the whole earth to tremble.'
text:
> svanigamam apahāya mat-pratijñām
> ṛtam adhikartum avapluto ratha-sthaḥ
> dhṛta-ratha-caraṇo 'bhyayāc caladgur
> harir iva hantum ibhaṁ gatottarīyaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:n:nigamam]]---His own promise not to take a weapon and fight on behalf of the Pāṇḍavas; [[synonyms:a:apahāya]]---giving up; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:p:pratijñām]]---my promise; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛtam]]---true; [[synonyms:a:adhikartum]]---to make more; [[synonyms:a:avaplutaḥ]]---having jumped down; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:s:sthaḥ]]---who was on the chariot (Lord Kṛṣṇa); [[synonyms:d:dhṛta]]---who took up; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇaḥ]]---the wheel of the chariot; [[synonyms:a:abhyayāt]]---ran forward; [[synonyms:c:calat]]-[[synonyms:g:guḥ]]---making the entire planet tremble; [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---a lion; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:h:hantum]]---to kill; [[synonyms:i:ibham]]---an elephant; [[synonyms:g:gata]]-[[synonyms:u:uttarīyaḥ]]---losing the outer garment.
translation: “ 'Intending to make my promise true, Lord Kṛṣṇa broke His own promise not to take up a weapon at Kurukṣetra. With His outer garment falling off, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa jumped from His chariot, picked up a wheel and came running at me to kill me. Indeed, He rushed at me like a lion going to kill an elephant, and He caused the whole earth to tremble.'
purport: Lord Kṛṣṇa promised not to fight in the battle of Kurukṣetra or even take up a weapon. But when Bhīṣma wanted to keep his own promise to break the promise of the Lord, the Lord immediately got down from the chariot, and to make Bhīṣma's promise true He picked up a chariot wheel and rushed forward to kill him. This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:9:37|(1.9.37)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.146
description: "Similarly, tolerating your separation, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has protected your vow with great endeavor."
text:
> ei-mata prabhu tomāra viccheda sahiyā
> tomāra pratijñā rakṣā kaila yatna kariyā"
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of you; [[synonyms:v:viccheda]] [[synonyms:s:sahiyā]]---tolerating the separation; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:p:pratijñā]]---your vow; [[synonyms:r:rakṣā]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---protected; [[synonyms:y:yatna]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---with great endeavor.
translation: "Similarly, tolerating your separation, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has protected your vow with great endeavor."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.147
description: In this way Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya revived Gadādhara Paṇḍita. Then both of them, very much grief-stricken, returned to Jagannātha Purī, Nīlācala.
text:
> ei-mata kahi' tāṅre prabodha karilā
> dui-jane śokākula nīlācale āilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---speaking; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:p:prabodha]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---awoke; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---the two persons; [[synonyms:ś:śoka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākula]]---overwhelmed with grief; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---went back.
translation: In this way Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya revived Gadādhara Paṇḍita. Then both of them, very much grief-stricken, returned to Jagannātha Purī, Nīlācala.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.148
description: All the devotees would abandon all kinds of duties for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's sake, yet the Lord did not like the devotees' giving up their promised duties.
text:
> prabhu lāgi' dharma-karma chāḍe bhakta-gaṇa
> bhakta-dharma-hāni prabhura nā haya sahana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for the sake of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:k:karma]]---all prescribed duties; [[synonyms:c:chāḍe]]---give up; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---of the duty of a devotee; [[synonyms:h:hāni]]---the abandonment; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is not; [[synonyms:s:sahana]]---tolerable.
translation: All the devotees would abandon all kinds of duties for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's sake, yet the Lord did not like the devotees' giving up their promised duties.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.149
description: All these are the misgivings of loving affairs. Whoever listens to these incidents gets Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's shelter very soon.
text:
> 'premera vivarta' ihā śune yei jana
> acire miliye tāṅre caitanya-caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:premera]] [[synonyms:v:vivarta]]---the misgivings of loving affairs; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---listens; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---any person who; [[synonyms:a:acire]]---very soon; [[synonyms:m:miliye]]---meet; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All these are the misgivings of loving affairs. Whoever listens to these incidents gets Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's shelter very soon.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.150
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His party arrived at Yājapura, the Lord asked the two government officers who had come with Him to return.
text:
> dui rāja-pātra yei prabhu-saṅge yāya
> 'yājapura' āsi' prabhu tāre dilena vidāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---the two government officers; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---who; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---go; [[synonyms:y:yājapura]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---when coming to Yājapura; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---unto them; [[synonyms:d:dilena]] [[synonyms:v:vidāya]]---bade farewell.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His party arrived at Yājapura, the Lord asked the two government officers who had come with Him to return.
purport:
The place called Yājapura is very well known in Orissa. It is a subdivision of the Kaṭaka district and is situated on the southern side of the Vaitaraṇī River. Formerly great sages performed sacrifices on the northern bank of the Vaitaraṇī River; consequently the place is known as Yājapura---"the place where sacrifices are performed." Some people say that this was one of the capital cities of King Yayāti and that from the name Yayāti-nagara the name Yājapura has come. As stated in //Mahābhārata (Vana-parva// Chapter 114):

> ete kaliṅgāḥ kaunteya
> yatra vaitaraṇī nadī
> yatrāyajata dharmo 'pi
> devān śaraṇam etya vai
> atra vai ṛṣayo 'nye ca
> purā kratubhir ījire

According to the //Mahābhārata,// great sages formerly performed sacrifices in this place. There are still many temples of demigods and incarnations there, and there is also a Deity of Śrī Varāhadeva. This Deity is especially important and is visited by many pilgrims. Those who worship the Supreme Lord's energy worship Vārāhī, Vaiṣṇavī and Indrāṇī, as well as many similar forms of Devī, the internal energy. There are many deities of Lord Śiva, and there are many places along the river known as Daśāśvamedha-ghāṭa. Sometimes Yājapura is also called Nābhi-gayā or Virajā-kṣetra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.151
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade farewell to the officers, and Rāya Rāmānanda continued on with the Lord. The Lord talked to Rāmānanda Rāya about Śrī Kṛṣṇa day and night.
text:
> prabhu vidāya dila, rāya yāya tāṅra sane
> kṛṣṇa-kathā rāmānanda-sane rātri-dine
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:v:vidāya]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---the Lord bade them farewell; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with Him; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---discussion of topics of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with Rāmānanda; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---day and night.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade farewell to the officers, and Rāya Rāmānanda continued on with the Lord. The Lord talked to Rāmānanda Rāya about Śrī Kṛṣṇa day and night.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.152
description: In each and every village, in compliance with the King's order, government officers constructed new houses and filled each of them with stocks of grains. Thus they served the Lord.
text:
> prati-grāme rāja-ājñāya rāja-bhṛtya-gaṇa
> navya gṛhe nānā-dravye karaye sevana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in each village; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:ā:ājñāya]]---by the order of the King; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:b:bhṛtya]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the government servants; [[synonyms:n:navya]] [[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---in newly constructed houses; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:d:dravye]]---with all kinds of food grains; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---rendered service.
translation: In each and every village, in compliance with the King's order, government officers constructed new houses and filled each of them with stocks of grains. Thus they served the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.153
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally arrived at Remuṇā, where He bade farewell to Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya.
text:
> ei-mata cali' prabhu 'remuṇā' āilā
> tathā haite rāmānanda-rāye vidāya dilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---walking; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:remuṇā]] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came to Remuṇā; [[synonyms:t:tathā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from there; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:r:rāye]]---unto Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:v:vidāya]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---bade farewell.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally arrived at Remuṇā, where He bade farewell to Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya.
purport: It was stated in the First Chapter of //Madhya-līlā,// verse 149, that Rāmānanda Rāya was bade farewell from Bhadraka. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura states that in those days the place called Remuṇā also included Bhadraka.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.154
description: When Rāmānanda Rāya fell to the ground and lost consciousness, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took him upon His lap and began to cry.
text:
> bhūmete paḍilā rāya nāhika cetana
> rāye kole kari' prabhu karaye krandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhūmete]] [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down on the ground; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:c:cetana]]---there was no consciousness; [[synonyms:r:rāye]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:k:kole]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking on the lap; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:k:krandana]]---began crying.
translation: When Rāmānanda Rāya fell to the ground and lost consciousness, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took him upon His lap and began to cry.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.155
description: Rāmānanda Rāya's separation from Caitanya Mahāprabhu is very difficult to describe. It is almost intolerable, and therefore I cannot describe it further.
text:
> rāyera vidāya-bhāva nā yāya sahana
> kahite nā pāri ei tāhāra varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāyera]] [[synonyms:v:vidāya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---feelings of separation from Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---not possible; [[synonyms:s:sahana]]---to tolerate; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---I am not able; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---a description.
translation: Rāmānanda Rāya's separation from Caitanya Mahāprabhu is very difficult to describe. It is almost intolerable, and therefore I cannot describe it further.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.156
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally arrived at the border of the state of Orissa, a government officer came there to meet Him.
text:
> tabe 'oḍhra-deśa-sīmā' prabhu cali' āilā
> tathā rāja-adhikārī prabhure mililā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:o:oḍhra]]-[[synonyms:d:deśa]]-[[synonyms:s:sīmā]]---the boundary of Orissa; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---traveling; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---reached; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---there; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:a:adhikārī]]---a government officer; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally arrived at the border of the state of Orissa, a government officer came there to meet Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.157
description: For two or four days, the government officer served the Lord. He also gave the Lord detailed information of what was ahead.
text:
> dina dui-cāri teṅho karila sevana
> āge calibāre sei kahe vivaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dina]] [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:c:cāri]]---two or four days; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---served the Lord; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---forward; [[synonyms:c:calibāre]]---for going; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that officer; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---spoke; [[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---detailed information.
translation: For two or four days, the government officer served the Lord. He also gave the Lord detailed information of what was ahead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.158
description: He informed the Lord that the territory ahead was ruled by a Moslem governor, who was a drunkard. Out of fear for this king, no one could walk the road freely.
text:
> madyapa yavana-rājāra āge adhikāra
> tāṅra bhaye pathe keha nāre calibāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madyapa]]---drunkard; [[synonyms:y:yavana]]---Mohammedan; [[synonyms:r:rājāra]]---of a king; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---ahead; [[synonyms:a:adhikāra]]---the government; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---being afraid of such a king; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the road; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---not able; [[synonyms:c:calibāra]]---to travel.
translation: He informed the Lord that the territory ahead was ruled by a Moslem governor, who was a drunkard. Out of fear for this king, no one could walk the road freely.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.159
description: The jurisdiction of the Mohammedan government extended up to Pichaladā. Due to fear of the Mohammedans, no one would cross the river.
text:
> pichaladā paryanta saba tāṅra adhikāra
> tāṅra bhaye nadī keha haite nāre pāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pichaladā]]---the place named Pichaladā; [[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---up to; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---everything; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of him; [[synonyms:a:adhikāra]]---under the authority; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---because of fear of him; [[synonyms:n:nadī]]---the river; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---to cross; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---not able; [[synonyms:p:pāra]]---to the other side.
translation: The jurisdiction of the Mohammedan government extended up to Pichaladā. Due to fear of the Mohammedans, no one would cross the river.
purport: During the old days, Pichaladā was part of Tamaluka and Bengal. Pichaladā is located about fourteen miles south of Tamaluka. The River Rūpa-nārāyaṇa is well known in Tamaluka, and Pichaladā was situated on the bank of the Rūpa-nārāyaṇa River.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.16-17
description: All the devotees of Navadvīpa departed, including Ācāryaratna, Vidyānidhi, Śrīvāsa, Rāmāi, Vāsudeva, Murāri, Govinda and his two brothers and Rāghava Paṇḍita, who took bags of assorted foods. The inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma, carrying silken ropes, also departed.
text:
> ācāryaratna, vidyānidhi, śrīvāsa, rāmāi
> vāsudeva, murāri, govindādi tina bhāi
> rāghava paṇḍita nija-jhāli sājāñā
> kulīna-grāma-vāsī cale paṭṭa-ḍorī lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryaratna]]---Ācāryaratna; [[synonyms:v:vidyānidhi]]---Vidyānidhi; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]---Śrīvāsa; [[synonyms:r:rāmāi]]---Rāmāi; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]---Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:m:murāri]]---Murāri; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---Govinda and his two brothers; [[synonyms:r:rāghava]] [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---Rāghava Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:j:jhāli]]---his own bags; [[synonyms:s:sājāñā]]---assorting; [[synonyms:k:kulīna]]-[[synonyms:g:grāma]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---the inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---went; [[synonyms:p:paṭṭa]]-[[synonyms:ḍ:ḍorī]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking silken ropes.
translation: All the devotees of Navadvīpa departed, including Ācāryaratna, Vidyānidhi, Śrīvāsa, Rāmāi, Vāsudeva, Murāri, Govinda and his two brothers and Rāghava Paṇḍita, who took bags of assorted foods. The inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma, carrying silken ropes, also departed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.160
description: Mahārāja Pratāparudra's government officer further informed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu that He should stay at the Orissa border for some days so that a peaceful agreement could be negotiated with the Mohammedan governor. In that way, the Lord would be able to cross the river peacefully in a boat.
text:
> dina kata raha---sandhi kari' tāṅra sane
> tabe sukhe naukāte karāiba gamane
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dina]] [[synonyms:k:kata]] [[synonyms:r:raha]]---stay here for a few days; [[synonyms:s:sandhi]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making peaceful negotiations; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with him; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in happiness; [[synonyms:n:naukāte]]---on the boat; [[synonyms:k:karāiba]] [[synonyms:g:gamane]]---I will help You start.
translation: Mahārāja Pratāparudra's government officer further informed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu that He should stay at the Orissa border for some days so that a peaceful agreement could be negotiated with the Mohammedan governor. In that way, the Lord would be able to cross the river peacefully in a boat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.161
description: At that time, a follower of the Mohammedan governor arrived at the Orissa encampment dressed in disguise.
text:
> sei kāle se yavanera eka anucara
> 'uḍiyā-kaṭake' āila kari' veśāntara
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:y:yavanera]]---of the Mohammedan governor; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:a:anucara]]---one follower; [[synonyms:u:uḍiyā]]-[[synonyms:k:kaṭake]]---to the camp of Orissan soldiers; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:v:veśa]]-[[synonyms:a:antara]]---changing the dress.
translation: At that time, a follower of the Mohammedan governor arrived at the Orissa encampment dressed in disguise.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.162-163
description: The Mohammedan spy saw the wonderful characteristics of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and when he returned to the Mohammedan governor, he told him, "A mendicant has come from Jagannātha Purī with many liberated persons.
text:
> prabhura sei adabhuta caritra dekhiyā
> hindu-cara kahe sei yavana-pāśa giyā
>
> 'eka sannyāsī āila jagannātha ha-ite
> aneka siddha-puruṣa haya tāṅhāra sahite
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:a:adabhutacaritra]]---wonderful characteristics; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:hindu]]-[[synonyms:c:cara]]---the Hindu spy; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:y:yavana]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśa]] [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---going to the Mohammedan king; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:s:sannyāsi]]---one mendicant; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---has come; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---from Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:a:aneka]]---many; [[synonyms:s:siddha]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]---liberated persons; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:s:sahite]]---with Him.
translation: The Mohammedan spy saw the wonderful characteristics of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and when he returned to the Mohammedan governor, he told him, "A mendicant has come from Jagannātha Purī with many liberated persons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.164
description: "All these saintly people incessantly chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, and they all laugh, dance, chant and cry.
text:
> nirantara kare sabe kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtana
> sabe hāse, nāce, gāya, karaye krandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---without stopping; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:h:hāse]]---laugh; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sing; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:k:krandana]]---and cry.
translation: "All these saintly people incessantly chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, and they all laugh, dance, chant and cry.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.165
description: "Many millions upon millions of people come to see Him, and after they see Him, they cannot return home.
text:
> lakṣa lakṣa loka āise tāhā dekhibāre
> tāṅre dekhi' punarapi yāite nāre ghare
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---millions upon millions; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---come; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:d:dekhibāre]]---to see; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after seeing Him; [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---are not able; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---home.
translation: "Many millions upon millions of people come to see Him, and after they see Him, they cannot return home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.166
description: "All these people become like madmen. They simply dance and chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Sometimes they even cry and roll on the ground.
text:
> sei saba loka haya bāulera prāya
> 'kṛṣṇa' kahi' nāce, kānde, gaḍāgaḍi yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all those persons; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:b:bāulera]] [[synonyms:p:prāya]]---almost like madmen; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---they dance; [[synonyms:k:kānde]]---they cry; [[synonyms:g:gaḍāgaḍi]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---they roll on the ground.
translation: "All these people become like madmen. They simply dance and chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Sometimes they even cry and roll on the ground.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.167
description: "Actually these things cannot even be described. One can understand them only by seeing. By His influence, I accept Him as the Supreme Personality of Godhead."
text:
> kahibāra kathā nahe---dekhile se jāni
> tāṅhāra prabhāve tāṅre 'īśvara' kari' māni'

translation: Upon hearing this proposal, the representative of the Orissan government, the mahā-pātra, was very astonished. He thought, "The Mohammedan governor is a drunkard. Who has changed his mind?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.175
description: "It must be Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself who has changed the Mohammedan's mind. Due to His presence and even due to His remembrance, the whole world is liberated."
text:
> āpane mahāprabhu tāṅra mana phirāila
> darśana-smaraṇe yāṅra jagat tārila'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:p:phirāila]]---changed; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---by a personal visit; [[synonyms:s:smaraṇe]]---by remembrance; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the whole world; [[synonyms:t:tārila]]---He has delivered.
translation: "It must be Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself who has changed the Mohammedan's mind. Due to His presence and even due to His remembrance, the whole world is liberated."
purport:
From this we can understand that the Mohammedan governor was a drunkard (//madyapa).// Ordinarily, there was no chance that he would change, but Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu could turn anyone's mind to Kṛṣṇa consciousness. One can be delivered from material existence simply by remembering Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's holy name or by visiting Him. This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is being spread throughout the world, but not even one //yavana// or //mleccha// addicted to drinking could have changed and accepted Kṛṣṇa consciousness without Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's grace. People are often astonished to see many thousands of Westerners converted to Vaiṣṇavism. Generally Westerners are addicted to meat-eating, drinking, gambling and illicit sex; therefore their taking up Kṛṣṇa consciousness is astonishing. In India, especially, there is much astonishment at this. The answer, however, is given here: //darśana-smaraṇe yāṅra jagat tārila.// This change is made possible simply by the remembrance of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The Western devotees are very sincerely chanting the holy names of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His associates: //śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya prabhu nityānanda śrī-advaita gadādhara śrīvāsādi-gaura-bhakta-vṛnda.// By the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His associates, people are being purified and their consciousness directed from //māyā// to Kṛṣṇa.

The word //viśvāsa// refers to a secretary. This title is generally found among the //kāyastha// caste in the Hindu community. In Bengal, the title //viśvāsa// is still used by the //kāyasthas.// The word //viśvāsa// means "faithful," and a //viśvāsī// is a person in whom one can place faith. Śrī Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura states that during the Mohammedan reign in Bengal, there was a secretariat entitled //viśvāsa-khānā.// The office of //viśvāsa-khānā// was a secretariat office in which only the most reliable people were employed. They were elected from the //kāyastha// community, a community that is still very expert in managing business and government affairs. The secretariat, or //viśvāsa-khānā,// is generally a very reliable and faithful servant. Whenever some confidential service was needed, these officers were employed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.176

translation: Upon seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu from a distant place, the Mohammedan governor fell to the ground and offered obeisances. Tears came to his eyes, and he was jubilant with ecstatic emotions.

description: The governor then submissively asked, "Why was I born in a Mohammedan family? This is considered a low birth. Why didn't supreme Providence grant me a birth in a Hindu family?
text:

"
