> śuniyā vaiṣṇava-mane bāḍila ānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sākṣi]]-[[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of the Deity known as Sākṣi-gopāla; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---the narration; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the minds of all the Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:b:bāḍila]]---increased; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---the transcendental bliss.
translation:
When Nityānanda Prabhu described all the activities of Sākṣi-gopāla, transcendental bliss increased in the minds of all the Vaiṣṇavas.


For these activities refer to //Madhya-līlā,// Chapter Five, verses 8-138.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.37
description: Everyone in the party was very anxious at heart to see Caitanya Mahāprabhu; therefore they hastily went on to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> prabhuke milite sabāra utkaṇṭhā antare
> śīghra kari' āilā sabe śrī-nīlācale
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]] [[synonyms:m:milite]]---to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:u:utkaṇṭhā]]---anxiety; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---within the heart; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making great haste; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---reached; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---Jagannātha Purī.
translation: Everyone in the party was very anxious at heart to see Caitanya Mahāprabhu; therefore they hastily went on to Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.38
description: When they all arrived at a bridge called Āṭhāranālā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, hearing the news of their arrival, sent two garlands with Govinda.
text:
> āṭhāranālāke āilā gosāñi śuniyā
> dui-mālā pāṭhāilā govinda-hāte diyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āṭhāranālāke]]---Āṭhāranālā; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---they have reached; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:m:mālā]]---two garlands; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāilā]]---sent; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:h:hāte]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---through the hands of Govinda.
translation: When they all arrived at a bridge called Āṭhāranālā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, hearing the news of their arrival, sent two garlands with Govinda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.39
description: Govinda offered the two garlands to Advaita Ācārya and Nityānanda Prabhu, and They both became very happy.
text:
> dui mālā govinda dui-jane parāila
> advaita, avadhūta-gosāñi baḍa sukha pāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:m:mālā]]---the two garlands; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]] [[synonyms:p:parāila]]---placed on the necks of two personalities; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:a:avadhūta]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:s:sukha]] [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---became very happy.
translation: Govinda offered the two garlands to Advaita Ācārya and Nityānanda Prabhu, and They both became very happy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.4
description: The King therefore called for Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Rāmānanda Rāya, and he spoke the following submissive words to them.
text:
> sārvabhauma, rāmānanda, āni' dui jana
> duṅhāke kahena rājā vinaya-vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---calling; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāke]]---unto both of them; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---said; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:v:vinaya]]-[[synonyms:v:vacana]]---submissive words.
translation: The King therefore called for Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Rāmānanda Rāya, and he spoke the following submissive words to them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.40
description: Indeed, They began chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa on that very spot, and, dancing and dancing, both Advaita Ācārya and Nityānanda Prabhu reached Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> tāhāñi ārambha kaila kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtana
> nācite nācite cali' āilā dui-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhāñi]]---on that very spot; [[synonyms:ā:ārambha]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---began; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nācite]] [[synonyms:n:nācite]]---dancing and dancing; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---going; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---reached; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---both of Them.
translation: Indeed, They began chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa on that very spot, and, dancing and dancing, both Advaita Ācārya and Nityānanda Prabhu reached Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.41
description: Then, for the second time, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sent garlands through Svarūpa Dāmodara and other personal associates. Thus they went forward, sent by the son of mother Śacī.
text:
> punaḥ mālā diyā svarūpādi nija-gaṇa
> āgu bāḍi' pāṭhāila śacīra nandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:m:mālā]]---garlands; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---offering; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and others; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---personal associates; [[synonyms:ā:āgu]] [[synonyms:b:bāḍi']]---going forward; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāila]]---sent; [[synonyms:ś:śacīra]] [[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of mother Śacī.
translation: Then, for the second time, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sent garlands through Svarūpa Dāmodara and other personal associates. Thus they went forward, sent by the son of mother Śacī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.42
description: When the devotees from Bengal reached Lake Narendra, Svarūpa Dāmodara and the others met them and offered them the garlands given by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> narendra āsiyā tāhāṅ sabāre mililā
> mahāprabhura datta mālā sabāre parāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:narendra]]---to the lake named Narendra; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---everyone; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:datta]]---given; [[synonyms:m:mālā]]---garlands; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]] [[synonyms:p:parāilā]]---offered to everyone.
translation: When the devotees from Bengal reached Lake Narendra, Svarūpa Dāmodara and the others met them and offered them the garlands given by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.43
description: When the devotees finally reached the lion gate, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard the news and personally went to meet them.
text:
> siṁha-dvāra-nikaṭe āilā śuni' gaurarāya
> āpane āsiyā prabhu mililā sabāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:siṁha]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāra]]---the lion gate; [[synonyms:n:nikaṭe]]---near; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:g:gaurarāya]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mililā]] [[synonyms:s:sabāya]]---met them all.
translation: When the devotees finally reached the lion gate, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard the news and personally went to meet them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.44
description: Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all His devotees visited Lord Jagannātha. Finally, accompanied by them all, He returned to His own residence.
text:
> sabā lañā kaila jagannātha-daraśana
> sabā lañā āilā punaḥ āpana-bhavana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking all of them; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:s:sabā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking them all; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---went back; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhavana]]---to His own residence.
translation: Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all His devotees visited Lord Jagannātha. Finally, accompanied by them all, He returned to His own residence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.45
description: Vāṇīnātha Rāya and Kāśī Miśra then brought a large quantity of prasāda, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu distributed it with His own hand and fed them all.
text:
> vāṇīnātha, kāśī-miśra prasāda ānila
> svahaste sabāre prabhu prasāda khāoyāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vāṇīnātha]]---Vāṇīnātha; [[synonyms:k:kāśī]]-[[synonyms:m:miśra]]---Kāśī Miśra; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:ā:ānila]]---brought all kinds of //prasāda//; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:h:haste]]---with His own hand; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---unto everyone; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---the remnants of the food of Jagannātha; [[synonyms:k:khāoyāila]]---fed.
translation: Vāṇīnātha Rāya and Kāśī Miśra then brought a large quantity of prasāda, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu distributed it with His own hand and fed them all.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.46
description: In the previous year, everyone had his own particular residence, and the same residences were again offered. Thus they all went to take rest.
text:
> pūrva vatsare yāṅra yei vāsā-sthāna
> tāhāṅ sabā pāṭhāñā karāila viśrāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]] [[synonyms:v:vatsare]]---in the previous year; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---wherever; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---place to stay; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all of them; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāñā]]---sending; [[synonyms:k:karāila]] [[synonyms:v:viśrāma]]---made them rest.
translation: In the previous year, everyone had his own particular residence, and the same residences were again offered. Thus they all went to take rest.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.47
description: For four continuous months all the devotees remained there and enjoyed chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> ei-mata bhakta-gaṇa rahilā cāri māsa
> prabhura sahita kare kīrtana-vilāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:m:māsa]]---for four months; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:s:sahita]]---with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performed; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---the pastimes of //saṅkīrtana.//
translation: For four continuous months all the devotees remained there and enjoyed chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.48
description: As in the previous year, they all washed the Guṇḍicā temple when the time for Ratha-yātrā arrived.
text:
> pūrvavat ratha-yātrā-kāla yābe āila
> sabā lañā guṇḍicā-mandira prakṣālila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---as in the previous year; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]-[[synonyms:k:kāla]]---the time for Ratha-yātrā festival; [[synonyms:y:yābe]]---when; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---arrived; [[synonyms:s:sabā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking all of them; [[synonyms:g:guṇḍicā]]-[[synonyms:m:mandira]]---the temple of Guṇḍicā; [[synonyms:p:prakṣālila]]---washed.
translation: As in the previous year, they all washed the Guṇḍicā temple when the time for Ratha-yātrā arrived.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.49
description: The inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma delivered silken ropes to Lord Jagannātha, and as previously they all danced before the Lord's car.
text:
> kulīna-grāmī paṭṭa-ḍorī jagannāthe dila
> pūrvavat ratha-agre nartana karila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kulīna]]-[[synonyms:g:grāmī]]---the residents of Kulīna-grāma; [[synonyms:p:paṭṭa]]-[[synonyms:ḍ:ḍorī]]---silken ropes; [[synonyms:j:jagannāthe]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---offered to Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---like the previous year; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:a:agre]]---in front of the car; [[synonyms:n:nartana]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---danced.
translation: The inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma delivered silken ropes to Lord Jagannātha, and as previously they all danced before the Lord's car.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.5
description: Pratāparudra Mahārāja said, "Please endeavor to keep Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu here at Jagannātha purī, for now He is thinking of going elsewhere.
text:
> nīlādri chāḍi' prabhura mana anyatra yāite
> tomarā karaha yatna tāṅhāre rākhite
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nīlādri]]---Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:a:anyatra]]---elsewhere; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go; [[synonyms:t:tomarā]]---both of you; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---make; [[synonyms:y:yatna]]---endeavor; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāre]]---Him; [[synonyms:r:rākhite]]---to keep.
translation: Pratāparudra Mahārāja said, "Please endeavor to keep Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu here at Jagannātha purī, for now He is thinking of going elsewhere.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.50
description: After dancing a great deal, they all went to a nearby garden and took rest beside a lake.
text:
> bahu nṛtya kari' punaḥ calila udyāne
> vāpī-tīre tāhāṅ yāi' karila viśrāme
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bahu]] [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---after dancing a great deal; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:c:calila]]---started for; [[synonyms:u:udyāne]]---the garden; [[synonyms:v:vāpī]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank of the lake; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:y:yāi']]---going there; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:v:viśrāme]]---took rest.
translation: After dancing a great deal, they all went to a nearby garden and took rest beside a lake.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.51
description: One brāhmaṇa named Kṛṣṇadāsa, who was a resident of Rāḍha-deśa and a servant of Lord Nityānanda's, was a very fortunate person.
text:
> rāḍhī eka vipra, teṅho---nityānanda dāsa
> mahā-bhāgyavān teṅho, nāma---kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāḍhī]] [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---one //brāhmaṇa// resident of Rāḍha-deśa (where the Ganges does not flow); [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]] [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---servant of Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgyavān]]---greatly fortunate; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Kṛṣṇadāsa.
translation: One brāhmaṇa named Kṛṣṇadāsa, who was a resident of Rāḍha-deśa and a servant of Lord Nityānanda's, was a very fortunate person.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.52
description: It was Kṛṣṇadāsa who filled a great waterpot and poured it over the Lord while He was taking His bath. The Lord was greatly satisfied by this.
text:
> ghaṭa bhari' prabhura teṅho abhiṣeka kaila
> tāṅra abhiṣeke prabhu mahā-tṛpta haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:ghaṭa]] [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---filling one waterpot; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:a:abhiṣeka]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed the bathing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:a:abhiṣeke]]---by the act of bathing the Lord; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:t:tṛpta]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became very satisfied.
translation: It was Kṛṣṇadāsa who filled a great waterpot and poured it over the Lord while He was taking His bath. The Lord was greatly satisfied by this.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.53
description: The remnants of food offered to the Lord at Balagaṇḍi then arrived in great quantity, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all His devotees ate it.
text:
> balagaṇḍi-bhogera bahu prasāda āila
> sabā saṅge mahāprabhu prasāda khāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:balagaṇḍi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhogera]]---of the food offered at Balagaṇḍi; [[synonyms:b:bahu]] [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---a great quantity of //prasāda//; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---arrived; [[synonyms:s:sabā]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with all the devotees; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---remnants of the food of Jagannātha; [[synonyms:k:khāila]]---ate.
translation: The remnants of food offered to the Lord at Balagaṇḍi then arrived in great quantity, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all His devotees ate it.
purport: In reference to Balagaṇḍi, see //Madhya-līlā// (13.193).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.54
description: As in the previous year, the Lord, with all the devotees, saw the Ratha-yātrā festival and the Herā-pañcamī festival as well.
text:
> pūrvavat ratha-yātrā kaila daraśana
> herā-pañcamī-yātrā dekhe lañā bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---as in the previous year; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---the car festival; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---saw; [[synonyms:h:herā]]-[[synonyms:p:pañcamī]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---the festival of Herā-pañcamī; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---He sees; [[synonyms:l:lañā]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---with all the devotees.
translation: As in the previous year, the Lord, with all the devotees, saw the Ratha-yātrā festival and the Herā-pañcamī festival as well.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.55
description: Advaita Ācārya then extended an invitation to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and there was a great rainstorm connected with that incident.
text:
> ācārya-gosāñi prabhura kaila nimantraṇa
> tāra madhye kaila yaiche jhaḍa-variṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that episode; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---occurred; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just as; [[synonyms:j:jhaḍa]]-[[synonyms:v:variṣaṇa]]---rainstorm.
translation: Advaita Ācārya then extended an invitation to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and there was a great rainstorm connected with that incident.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.56
description: All these episodes have been elaborately described by Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura. Then one day Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura extended an invitation to the Lord.
text:
> vistāri' varṇiyāchena dāsa-vṛndāvana
> śrīvāsa prabhure tabe kaila nimantraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vistāri']]---elaborating; [[synonyms:v:varṇiyāchena]]---has described; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]---Śrīvāsa; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---gave an invitation.
translation: All these episodes have been elaborately described by Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura. Then one day Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura extended an invitation to the Lord.
purport: Caitanya-bhāgavata (Antya-līlā, Chapter Eight) gives the following description. One day Śrīla Advaita Ācārya, having extended an invitation to Caitanya Mahāprabhu, thought that if the Lord came alone He would feed Him to His great satisfaction. It then so happened that when the other //sannyāsīs// were going to Advaita Ācārya's to take lunch, there was a big rainstorm, and they could not reach His house. Thus, according to Advaita Ācārya's desires, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came alone and accepted the //prasāda.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.64
description: "Do not come to Jagannātha Purī every year, but stay in Bengal and fulfill My desire."
text:
> prati-varṣa nīlācale tumi nā āsibā
> gauḍe rahi' mora icchā saphala karibā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:v:varṣa]]---every year; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:ā:āsibā]]---do not come; [[synonyms:g:gauḍe]] [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---staying in Bengal; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---My desire; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]] [[synonyms:k:karibā]]---make successful.
translation: "Do not come to Jagannātha Purī every year, but stay in Bengal and fulfill My desire."
purport:
The mission of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is to spread the only medicine effective in this fallen age of Kali---the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// Following the orders of His mother, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was residing at Jagannātha Purī, and the devotees were coming to see Him. However, the Lord felt that this message must be spread very elaborately in Bengal, and in His absence there was not a second person capable of doing it. Consequently the Lord requested Nityānanda Prabhu to stay there and broadcast the message of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. The Lord also entrusted a similar preaching responsibility to Rūpa and Sanātana. Nityānanda Prabhu was requested not to come every year to Jagannātha Purī, although seeing Lord Jagannātha greatly benefits everyone. Does this mean that the Lord was refusing Nityānanda Prabhu a fortunate opportunity? No. One who is a faithful servant of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu must execute His order, even if one has to sacrifice going to Jagannātha Purī to see Lord Jagannātha there. In other words, it is a greater fortune to carry out Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's order than to satisfy one's senses by seeing Lord Jagannātha.

Preaching Caitanya Mahāprabhu's cult throughout the world is more important than staying in Vṛndāvana or Jagannātha Purī for one's own personal satisfaction. Spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness is Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mission; therefore His sincere devotees must carry out His desire.

> pṛthivīte āche yata nagarādi grāma
> sarvatra pracāra haibe mora nāma

The devotees of Lord Caitanya must preach Kṛṣṇa consciousness in every village and town in the world. That will satisfy the Lord. It is not that one should act whimsically for his own personal satisfaction. This order comes down through the //paramparā// system, and the spiritual master presents these orders to the disciple so that he can spread the message of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. It is the duty of every disciple to carry out the order of the bona fide spiritual master and spread Lord Caitanya's message all over the world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.65
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "You can perform a task that even I cannot do. But for You, I cannot find anyone in Gauḍa-deśa who can fulfill My mission there."
text:
> tāhāṅ siddhi kare---hena anye nā dekhiye
> āmāra 'duṣkara' karma, tomā haite haye
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:s:siddhi]]---success; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---makes; [[synonyms:h:hena]]---such; [[synonyms:a:anye]]---other person; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:d:dekhiye]]---I see; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:d:duṣkara]]---difficult to perform; [[synonyms:k:karma]]---work; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]---You; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:h:haye]]---becomes successful.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "You can perform a task that even I cannot do. But for You, I cannot find anyone in Gauḍa-deśa who can fulfill My mission there."
purport:
Lord Caitanya's mission is to deliver the fallen souls of this age. In this Age of Kali, practically cent percent of the population is fallen. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu certainly delivered many fallen souls, but His disciples mainly came from the upper classes. For example, He delivered Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Sanātana Gosvāmī, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and many others who were socially elevated but fallen from the spiritual point of view. Śrīla Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmīs were situated in government service, and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was the topmost scholar of India. Similarly, Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī was a leader of many thousands of Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs.// It was Śrīla Nityānanda Prabhu, however, who delivered persons like Jagāi and Mādhāi. Therefore, Lord Caitanya says, //āmāra 'duṣkara' karma, tomā haite haye.// Jagāi and Mādhāi were delivered solely by Nityānanda Prabhu's mercy. When they injured Nityānanda Prabhu, Lord Caitanya became angry and decided to kill them with His Sudarśana //cakra,// but Nityānanda Prabhu saved them from the Lord's wrath and delivered them. In the incarnation of Gaura-Nitāi, the Lord is not supposed to kill demons but deliver them by preaching Kṛṣṇa consciousness. In the case of Jagāi and Mādhāi, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was so angry that He would have immediately killed them, but Nityānanda Prabhu was so kind that He not only saved them from death but elevated them to the transcendental position. Thus what was not possible for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was carried out by Nityānanda Prabhu.

Similarly, if one is true to Gaura-Nitāi's service in the disciplic succession, he can even excel Nityānanda Prabhu's service. This is the process of disciplic succession. Nityānanda Prabhu delivered Jagāi and Mādhāi, but a servant of Nityānanda Prabhu, by His grace, can deliver many thousands of Jagāi's and Mādhāi's. That is the special benediction of the disciplic succession. One who is situated in the disciplic succession can be understood by the result of his activities. This is always true as far as the activities of the Lord and His devotees are concerned. Therefore Lord Śiva says:

> ārādhanānāṁ sarveṣāṁ
> viṣṇor ārādhanaṁ paraṁ
> tasmāt parataraṁ devi
> tadīyānāṁ samarcanam

"Of all types of worship, worship of Lord Viṣṇu is best, and better than the worship of Lord Viṣṇu is the worship of His devotee, the Vaiṣṇava." (//Padma Purāṇa//)

By the grace of Viṣṇu, a Vaiṣṇava can render better service than Viṣṇu; that is the special prerogative of a Vaiṣṇava. The Lord actually wants to see His servants work more gloriously than Himself. For instance, on the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra, Śrī Kṛṣṇa provoked Arjuna to fight because all the warriors on the battlefield were to die by Kṛṣṇa's plan. Kṛṣṇa Himself did not want to take credit; rather, He wanted Arjuna to take credit. Therefore He asked him to fight and win fame.

> tasmāt tvam uttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva
> jitvā śatrūn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṁ samṛddham
> mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva
> nimitta-mātraṁ bhava savyasācin

"Therefore get up and prepare to fight. After conquering your enemies, you will enjoy a flourishing kingdom. They are already put to death by My arrangement, and you, O Savyasācin, can be but an instrument in the fight." [[books:bg:11:33|(Bg. 11.33)]]

Thus the Supreme Personality of Godhead gives credit to a devotee who performs any heavy task perfectly. Hanumānjī, or Vajrāṅgajī, the servant of Lord Rāmacandra, also serves as another example. It was Hanumānjī who jumped over the sea in one leap and reached the shore of Laṅkā from the shore of Bhārata-varṣa. When Lord Rāmacandra chose to go there, He paved the way with stones, although by His will the stones were able to float on the sea. If we simply follow Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's instructions and follow in the footsteps of Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement can advance, and even more difficult tasks can be performed by the preachers remaining faithful to the service of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.66
description: Nityānanda Prabhu replied, "O Lord, You are the life, and I am the body. There is no difference between the body and life itself, but life is more important than the body.
text:
> nityānanda kahe,---āmi 'deha' tumi 'prāṇa'
> 'deha' 'prāṇa' bhinna nahe,---ei ta pramāṇa

translation: Nityānanda Prabhu replied, "O Lord, You are the life, and I am the body. There is no difference between the body and life itself, but life is more important than the body.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.67
description: "By Your inconceivable energy, You can do whatever You like, and whatever You make Me do, I do without restriction."
text:
> acintya-śaktye kara tumi tāhāra ghaṭana
> ye karāha, sei kari, nāhika niyama
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:acintya]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaktye]]---by inconceivable energy; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---do; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---of that relationship; [[synonyms:g:ghaṭana]]---the operation; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:k:karāha]]---You make Me do; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I do; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:n:niyama]]---restriction.
translation: "By Your inconceivable energy, You can do whatever You like, and whatever You make Me do, I do without restriction."
purport:
As stated in the beginning of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam:tene brahma hṛdā ya ādi-kavaye.// Lord Brahmā is the first living creature within this universe, and he is also the creator of this universe. How is this possible? Although he is the first living entity, Lord Brahmā is not in the category of //viṣṇu-tattva.// Rather, he is part of the //jīva-tattva.// Nonetheless, by the grace of the Lord, who instructed him through the heart (//tene brahma hṛdā),// Lord Brahmā could create a huge universe. Those who are actually pure devotees of the Lord are instructed by the Lord through the heart, where the Lord is always situated. //Īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ hṛd-deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati// [[books:bg:18:61|(Bg. 18.61)]]. If he follows the instructions of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the living entity, even though an insignificant creature, can perform the most difficult tasks by the Lord's grace. This also is confirmed in //Bhagavad-gītā://

> teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ
> bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam
> dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ
> yena mām upayānti te

"To those who are constantly devoted and worship Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me," [[books:bg:10:10|(Bg. 10.10)]]

Everything is possible for a pure devotee because he acts under the instructions of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Through His inconceivable energy, a pure devotee can perform tasks that are supposed to be very, very difficult. He can perform tasks not even previously performed by the Lord Himself. Therefore Nityānanda Prabhu told Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, //ye karāha, sei kari, nāhika niyama:// "I do not know by what regulative principle I am carrying out this wonderful work, but I know for certain that I will do whatever You desire." Although the Lord wants to give all credit to His devotee, the devotee himself never takes credit, for he acts only under the Lord's direction. Consequently all credit goes to the Lord. This is the nature of the relationship between the Lord and His devotee. The Lord wants to give all credit to His servant, but the servant does not take any credit, for he knows that everything is carried out by the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.68

translation: In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced Nityānanda Prabhu and bade Him farewell. He then bade farewell to all the other devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.69

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.72
description: "A person who is always chanting the holy name of the Lord is to be considered a first-class Vaiṣṇava, and your duty is to serve his lotus feet."
text:
> "kṛṣṇa-nāma nirantara yāṅhāra vadane
> sei vaiṣṇava-śreṣṭha, bhaja tāṅhāra caraṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---incessantly; [[synonyms:y:yāṅhāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:v:vadane]]---in the mouth; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---such a person; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:ś:śreṣṭha]]---a first-class Vaiṣṇava; [[synonyms:b:bhaja]]---worship; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---his lotus feet.
translation: "A person who is always chanting the holy name of the Lord is to be considered a first-class Vaiṣṇava, and your duty is to serve his lotus feet."
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that any Vaiṣṇava who is constantly chanting the holy name of the Lord should be considered to have attained the second platform of Vaiṣṇavism. Such a devotee is superior to a neophyte Vaiṣṇava who has just learned to chant the holy name of the Lord. A neophyte devotee simply tries to chant the holy name, whereas the advanced devotee is accustomed to chanting and takes pleasure in it. Such an advanced devotee is called //madhyama-bhāgavata,// which indicates that he has attained the intermediate stage between the neophyte and the perfect devotee. Generally a devotee in the intermediate stage becomes a preacher. A neophyte devotee or an ordinary person should worship the //madhyama-bhāgavata,// who is a via medium.

In his //Upadeśāmṛta// Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī says: //praṇatibhiś ca bhajantam īśam.// This means that //madhyama-adhikārī// devotees should exchange obeisances between themselves.

The word //nirantara,// meaning "without cessation, continuously, constantly," is very important in this verse. The word //antara// means "interval." if one has desires other than a desire to perform devotional service-in other words, if one sometimes engages in devotional service and sometimes strives for sense gratification-his service will be interrupted. A pure devotee, therefore, should have no other desire than to serve Kṛṣṇa. He should be above fruitive activity and speculative knowledge. In his //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu,// Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī says:

> anyābhilāṣitā-śūnyaṁ
> jñāna-karmādy-anāvṛtam
> ānukūlyena kṛṣṇānu-
> śīlanaṁ bhaktir uttamā

This is the platform of pure devotional service. One should not be motivated by fruitive activity or mental speculation but should simply serve Kṛṣṇa favorably. That is first-class devotion.

Another meaning of //antara// is "this body." The body is an impediment to self-realization because it is always engaged in sense gratification. Similarly, //antara// means "money." If money is not used in Kṛṣṇa's service, it is also an impediment. //Antara// also means //janatā,// "people in general." The association of ordinary persons may destroy the principles of devotional service. Similarly, //antara// may mean "greed," greed to acquire more money or enjoy more sense gratification. Finally, the word //antara// may also mean "atheistic ideas" by which one considers the temple Deity to be made of stone, wood or gold. All of these are impediments. The Deity in the temple is not material-He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. Similarly, considering the spiritual master an ordinary human being (//guruṣu nara-matiḥ//) is also an impediment. Nor should one consider a Vaiṣṇava a member of a particular caste or nation. Nor should a Vaiṣṇava be considered material. //Caraṇāmṛta// should not be considered ordinary drinking water, and the holy name of the Lord should not be considered an ordinary sound vibration. Nor should one look on Lord Kṛṣṇa as an ordinary human being, for He is the origin of all //viṣṇu-tattvas;// nor should one regard the Supreme Lord as a demigod. Intermingling the spiritual with the material causes one to look on transcendence as material and the mundane as spiritual. This is all due to a poor fund of knowledge. One should not consider Lord Viṣṇu and things related to him as being different. All this is offensive.

In the //Bhakti-sandarbha// (265), Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī writes: //nāmaikaṁ yasya vāci smaraṇa-patha-gatam ityādau deha-draviṇādi-nimittaka-'pāṣaṇḍa'-śabdena ca daśa aparādhā lakṣyante, pāṣaṇḍamayatvāt teṣām.//

The Māyāvādīs look on Viṣṇu and Vaiṣṇavas imperfectly due to their poor fund of knowledge, and this is condemned. In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.2.46), the intermediate Vaiṣṇava is described as follows:

> īśvare tad-adhīneṣu
> bāliśeṣu dviṣatsu ca
> prema-maitrī-kṛpopekṣā
> yaḥ karoti sa madhyamaḥ

"The intermediate Vaiṣṇava has to love God, make friends with the devotees, instruct the innocent and reject jealous people." These are the four functions of the Vaiṣṇava in the intermediate stage. In //Caitanya-caritāmṛta// [[books:cc:madhya:22:64|(Madhya 22.64)]] Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī is taught:

> śraddhāvān jana haya bhakti-adhikārī
> 'uttama', 'madhyama', 'kaniṣṭha'---śraddhā-anusārī

"One who is faithful is a proper candidate for devotional service. In terms of one's degree of faith in devotional service, one is a first-class, second-class or neophyte Vaiṣṇava."

> śāstra-yukti nāhi jāne dṛḍha, śraddhāvān
> 'madhyama-adhikārī' sei mahā-bhāgyavān

"One who has attained the intermediate stage is not very advanced in śāstric knowledge, but he has firm faith in the Lord. Such a person is very fortunate to be situated on the intermediate platform." [[books:cc:madhya:22:67|(Cc. Madhya 22.67)]]

> rati-prema-tāratamye bhakta-tara-tama

"Attraction and love are the ultimate goal of devotional service. The degrees of such attraction and love for God distinguish the different stages of devotion-neophyte, intermediate and perfectional." [[books:cc:madhya:22:71|(Cc. Madhya 22.71)]] An intermediate devotee is greatly attracted to chanting the holy name, and by chanting he is elevated to the platform of love. If one chants the holy name of the Lord with great attachment, he can understand his position as an eternal servant of the spiritual master, other Vaiṣṇavas and Kṛṣṇa Himself. Thus the intermediate Vaiṣṇava considers himself //kṛṣṇa-dāsa,// Kṛṣṇa's servant. He therefore preaches Kṛṣṇa consciousness to innocent neophytes and stresses the importance of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// An intermediate devotee can identify the nondevotee or motivated devotee. The motivated devotee or the nondevotee are on the material platform, and they are called //prākṛta.// The intermediate devotee does not mix with such materialistic people. However, he understands that the Supreme Personality of Godhead and everything related to Him are on the same transcendental platform. Actually none of them are mundane.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.73

text:
> varṣāntare punaḥ tāṅrā aiche praśna kaila
> vaiṣṇavera tāratamya prabhu śikhāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:varṣāntare]]---after one year; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:t:tāṅrā]]---they (the inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma); [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:p:praśna]]---a question; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]]---of Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:t:tāratamya]]---upper and lower gradations; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śikhāila]]---taught.
translation: The following year, the inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma again asked the Lord the same question. Hearing this question, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu again taught them about the different types of Vaiṣṇavas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.74
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "A first-class Vaiṣṇava is he whose very presence makes others chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> yāṅhāra darśane mukhe āise kṛṣṇa-nāma
> tāṅhāre jāniha tumi 'vaiṣṇava-pradhāna'
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:d:darśane]]---by the sight of whom; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the mouth; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---automatically awakens; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāre]]---him; [[synonyms:j:jāniha]]---must know; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---the first-class Vaiṣṇava.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "A first-class Vaiṣṇava is he whose very presence makes others chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa."
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that if an observer immediately remembers the holy name of Kṛṣṇa upon seeing a Vaiṣṇava, that Vaiṣṇava should be considered a //mahā-bhāgavata,// a first-class devotee. Such a Vaiṣṇava is always aware of his Kṛṣṇa conscious duty, and he is enlightened in self-realization. He is always in love with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, and this love is without adulteration. Because of this love, he is always awake to transcendental realization. Because he knows that Kṛṣṇa consciousness is the basis of knowledge and action, he sees everything connected with Kṛṣṇa. Such a person is able to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa perfectly. Such a //mahā-bhāgavata// Vaiṣṇava has the transcendental eyes to see who is sleeping under the spell of //māyā,// and he engages himself in awakening sleeping conditioned beings by spreading the knowledge of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. He opens eyes that are closed by forgetfulness of Kṛṣṇa. Thus the living entity is liberated from the dullness of material energy and is engaged fully in the service of the Lord. The //madhyama-adhikārī// Vaiṣṇava can awaken others to Kṛṣṇa consciousness and engage them in duties whereby they can advance. It is therefore said in //Caitanya-caritāmṛta (Madhya-līlā,// Chapter Six, verse 279):

> lohāke yāvat sparśi' hema nāhi kare
> tāvat sparśa-maṇi keha cinite nā pāre

"One cannot understand the value of touchstone until it turns iron into gold." One should judge by action, not by promises. A //mahā-bhāgavata// can turn a living entity from abominable material life to the Lord's service. This is the test of a //mahā-bhāgavata.// Although preaching is not meant for a //mahā-bhāgavata,// a //mahā-bhāgavata// can descend to the platform of //madhyama-bhāgavata// just to convert others to Vaiṣṇavism. Actually a //mahā-bhāgavata// is fit to spread Kṛṣṇa consciousness, but he does not distinguish where Kṛṣṇa consciousness should be spread from where it should not. He thinks that everyone is competent to accept Kṛṣṇa consciousness if the chance is provided. A neophyte and intermediate devotee should always be anxious to hear the //mahā-bhāgavata// and serve him in every respect. The neophyte and intermediate devotees can gradually rise to the platform of //uttama-adhikārī// and become first-class devotees. Symptoms of a first-class devotee are given in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.2.45):

> sarva-bhūteṣu yaḥ paśyed
> bhagavad-bhāvam ātmanaḥ
> bhūtāni bhagavaty ātmany
> eṣa bhāgavatottamaḥ

When teaching Sanātana Gosvāmī, the Lord further said:

> śāstra-yuktye sunipuṇa, dṛḍha-śraddhā yāṅra
> 'uttama-adhikārī' se tāraye saṁsāra

"If one is expert in Vedic literature and has full faith in the Supreme Lord, then he is an //uttama-adhikārī,// a first-class Vaiṣṇava, a topmost Vaiṣṇava who can deliver the whole world and turn everyone to Kṛṣṇa consciousness." [[books:cc:madhya:22:65|(Cc. Madhya 22.65)]] With great love and affection, the //mahā-bhāgavata// observes the Supreme Personality of Godhead, devotional service and the devotee. He observes nothing beyond Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa consciousness and Kṛṣṇa's devotees. The //mahā-bhāgavata// knows that everyone is engaged in the Lord's service in different ways. He therefore descends to the middle platform to elevate everyone to the Kṛṣṇa conscious position.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.75
description: In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu instructed different types of Vaiṣṇavas—the Vaiṣṇava, Vaiṣṇavatara and Vaiṣṇavatama. He thus successively explained all the symptoms of a Vaiṣṇava to the inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma.
text:
> krama kari' kahe prabhu 'vaiṣṇava'-lakṣaṇa
> 'vaiṣṇava', 'vaiṣṇavatara', āra 'vaiṣṇavatama'

translation: In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu instructed different types of Vaiṣṇavas---the Vaiṣṇava, Vaiṣṇavatara and Vaiṣṇavatama. He thus successively explained all the symptoms of a Vaiṣṇava to the inhabitants of Kulīna-grāma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.76

translation: Finally all the Vaiṣṇavas returned to Bengal, but that year Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi remained at Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.77
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi had a friendly, intimate relationship, and as far as discussing topics about Kṛṣṇa, they were situated on the same platform.
text:
> svarūpa-sahita tāṅra haya sakhya-prīti
> dui-janāya kṛṣṇa-kathāya ekatra-i sthiti

translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi had a friendly, intimate relationship, and as far as discussing topics about Kṛṣṇa, they were situated on the same platform.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.78
description: Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi initiated Gadādhara Paṇḍita for the second time, and on the day of Oḍana-ṣaṣṭhī he saw the festival.
text:
> gadādhara-paṇḍite teṅho punaḥ mantra dila
> oḍana-ṣaṣṭhīra dine yātrā ye dekhila
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gadādhara]]-[[synonyms:p:paṇḍite]]---unto Gadādhara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again, the second; [[synonyms:m:mantra]]---initiation; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:o:oḍana]]-[[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṣṭhīra]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---on the day of performing the Oḍana-ṣaṣṭhī function; [[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---festival; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---indeed; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---he saw.
translation: Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi initiated Gadādhara Paṇḍita for the second time, and on the day of Oḍana-ṣaṣṭhī he saw the festival.
purport: At the beginning of winter, there is a ceremony known as the Oḍana-ṣaṣṭhī. This ceremony indicates that from that day forward, a winter covering should be given to Lord Jagannātha. That covering is directly purchased from a weaver. According to the //arcana-mārga,// a cloth should first be washed to remove all the starch, and then it can be used to cover the Lord. Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi saw that the priest neglected to wash the cloth before covering Lord Jagannātha. Since he wanted to find some fault in the devotees, he became indignant.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.79
description: When Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi saw that Lord Jagannātha was given a starched garment, he became a little hateful. In this way his mind was polluted.
text:
> jagannātha parena tathā 'māḍuyā' vasana
> dekhiyā saghṛṇa haila vidyānidhira mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:p:parena]]---puts on; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---there; [[synonyms:m:māḍuyā]] [[synonyms:v:vasana]]---cloth with starch; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:g:ghṛṇa]]---with hatred; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:v:vidyānidhira]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind of Vidyānidhi.
translation: When Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi saw that Lord Jagannātha was given a starched garment, he became a little hateful. In this way his mind was polluted.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.8
description: Rāmānanda Rāya and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya requested the Lord to observe first the Ratha-yātrā festival. Then when the month of Kārttika arrived, He could go to Vṛndāvana.
text:
> duṅhe kahe,---ratha-yātrā kara daraśana
> kārtika āile, tabe kariha gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---both of them said; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---the Ratha-yātrā festival; [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---please see; [[synonyms:k:kārtika]] [[synonyms:ā:āile]]---when the month of Kārttika arrives; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:k:kariha]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---You can go.
translation: Rāmānanda Rāya and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya requested the Lord to observe first the Ratha-yātrā festival. Then when the month of Kārttika arrived, He could go to Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.80
description: That night the brothers Lord Jagannātha and Balarāma came to Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi and, smiling, began to slap him.
text:
> sei rātrye jagannātha-balāi āsiyā
> dui-bhāi caḍā'na tāṅre hāsiyā hāsiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:r:rātrye]]---on that night; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:b:balāi]]---Lord Balarāma; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---both brothers; [[synonyms:c:caḍā'na]]---slapped; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:h:hāsiyā]] [[synonyms:h:hāsiyā]]---smiling.
translation: That night the brothers Lord Jagannātha and Balarāma came to Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi and, smiling, began to slap him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.81
description: Although his cheeks were swollen from the slapping, Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi was very happy within. This incident has been elaborately described by Ṭhākura Vṛndāvana dāsa.
text:
> gāla phulila, ācārya antare ullāsa
> vistāri' varṇiyāchena vṛndāvana-dāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gāla]]---the cheeks; [[synonyms:p:phulila]]---became swollen; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---within the heart; [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---very happy; [[synonyms:v:vistāri']]---elaborating; [[synonyms:v:varṇiyāchena]]---has narrated; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura.
translation: Although his cheeks were swollen from the slapping, Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi was very happy within. This incident has been elaborately described by Ṭhākura Vṛndāvana dāsa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.82
description: Every year the devotees of Bengal would come and stay with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to see the Ratha-yātrā festival.
text:
> ei-mata pratyabda āise gauḍera bhakta-gaṇa
> prabhu-saṅge rahi' kare yātrā-daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:a:abda]]---every year; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---come; [[synonyms:g:gauḍera]]---of Bengal; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Lord Śrī Caitanya Prabhu; [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---residing; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:y:yātrā]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---observing the Ratha-yātrā festival.
translation: Every year the devotees of Bengal would come and stay with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to see the Ratha-yātrā festival.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.83
description: Whatever happened during those years that is worth noting shall be described later.
text:
> tāra madhye ye ye varṣe āchaye viśeṣa
> vistāriyā āge tāhā kahiba niḥśeṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within those episodes; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:v:varṣe]]---in years; [[synonyms:ā:āchaye]]---there is; [[synonyms:v:viśeṣa]]---particular occurrence; [[synonyms:v:vistāriyā]]---elaborating; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---ahead; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kahiba]]---I shall say; [[synonyms:n:niḥśeṣa]]---completely.
translation: Whatever happened during those years that is worth noting shall be described later.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.84
description: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed four years. He spent the first two years on His tour in South India.
text:
> ei-mata mahāprabhura cāri vatsara gela
> dakṣiṇa yāñā āsite dui vatsara lāgila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---four; [[synonyms:v:vatsara]]---years; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---passed; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]] [[synonyms:y:yāñā]]---after touring southern India; [[synonyms:ā:āsite]]---to come back; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:v:vatsara]] [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---He took two years.
translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed four years. He spent the first two years on His tour in South India.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.85
description: The other two years, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to go to Vṛndāvana, but He could not leave Jagannātha Purī because of Rāmānanda Rāya's tricks.
text:
> āra dui vatsara cāhe vṛndāvana yāite
> rāmānanda-haṭhe prabhu nā pāre calite
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:v:vatsara]]---another two years; [[synonyms:c:cāhe]]---He wanted; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]] [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:h:haṭhe]]---by the tricks of Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---was not able; [[synonyms:c:calite]]---to go.
translation: The other two years, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to go to Vṛndāvana, but He could not leave Jagannātha Purī because of Rāmānanda Rāya's tricks.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.86
description: During the fifth year, the devotees from Bengal came to see the Ratha-yātrā festival. After seeing it, they did not stay but returned to Bengal.
text:
> pañcama vatsare gauḍera bhakta-gaṇa āilā
> ratha dekhi' nā rahilā, gauḍere calilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pañcama]] [[synonyms:v:vatsare]]---on the fifth year; [[synonyms:g:gauḍera]]---of Bengal; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:r:ratha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the Ratha-yātrā festival; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---did not stay; [[synonyms:g:gauḍere]] [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---returned to Bengal.
translation: During the fifth year, the devotees from Bengal came to see the Ratha-yātrā festival. After seeing it, they did not stay but returned to Bengal.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.87
description: Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu placed a proposal before Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Rāmānanda Rāya. He embraced them and spoke sweet words.
text:
> tabe prabhu sārvabhauma-rāmānanda-sthāne
> āliṅgana kari' kahe madhura vacane
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]-[[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---before Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---embracing; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:m:madhura]] [[synonyms:v:vacane]]---sweet words.
translation: Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu placed a proposal before Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Rāmānanda Rāya. He embraced them and spoke sweet words.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.88
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My desire to go to Vṛndāvana has very much increased. Because of your tricks, I have not been able to go there for the past two years.
text:
> bahuta utkaṇṭhā mora yāite vṛndāvana
> tomāra haṭhe dui vatsara nā kailuṅ gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bahuta]] [[synonyms:u:utkaṇṭhā]]---great anxiety; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:y:yāite]] [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---to go to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:h:haṭhe]]---by your tricks; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:v:vatsara]]---for two years; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kailuṅ]]---I did not do; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My desire to go to Vṛndāvana has very much increased. Because of your tricks, I have not been able to go there for the past two years.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.89
description: "This time I must go. Will you please give Me permission? Save for you two, I have no other resort.
text:
> avaśya caliba, duṅhe karaha sammati
> tomā-duṅhā vinā mora nāhi anya gati
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:c:caliba]]---I shall go; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of you; [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:s:sammati]]---kindly agree to this proposal; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:d:duṅhā]] [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---except you two; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:a:anya]] [[synonyms:g:gati]]---other resort.
translation: "This time I must go. Will you please give Me permission? Save for you two, I have no other resort.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.9
description: However, when the month of Kārttika came, they both told the Lord, "Now it is very cold. It is better that You wait to see the Dola-yātrā festival and then go. That will be very nice."
text:
> kārtika āile kahe---ebe mahā-śīta
> dola-yātrā dekhi' yāo---ei bhāla rīta
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kārtika]] [[synonyms:ā:āile]]---when the month of Kārttika arrived; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---both of them said; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śīta]]---very cold; [[synonyms:d:dola]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after seeing the Dola-yātrā ceremony; [[synonyms:y:yāo]]---You go; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]] [[synonyms:r:rīta]]---a very nice program.
translation: However, when the month of Kārttika came, they both told the Lord, "Now it is very cold. It is better that You wait to see the Dola-yātrā festival and then go. That will be very nice."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.90
description: "In Bengal I have two shelters-my mother and the River Ganges. Both of them are very merciful.
text:
> gauḍa-deśe haya mora 'dui samāśraya'
> 'jananī' jāhnavī',---ei dui dayāmaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in Bengal; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:s:samāśraya]]---shelters; [[synonyms:j:jananī]]---the mother; [[synonyms:j:jāhnavī]]---mother Ganges; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]]---these two; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---very merciful.
translation: "In Bengal I have two shelters-my mother and the River Ganges. Both of them are very merciful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.91
description: "I shall go to Vṛndāvana through Bengal and see both My mother and the River Ganges. Now would you two be pleased to give Me permission?"
text:
> gauḍa-deśa diyā yāba tāṅ-sabā dekhiyā
> tumi duṅhe ājñā deha' parasanna hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:deśa]]---the country known as Bengal; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---through; [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---I shall go; [[synonyms:t:tāṅ]]-[[synonyms:s:sabā]]---both of them; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of you; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:deha']]---give Me permission; [[synonyms:p:parasanna]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being very pleased.
translation: "I shall go to Vṛndāvana through Bengal and see both My mother and the River Ganges. Now would you two be pleased to give Me permission?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.92
description: When Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Rāmānanda Rāya heard these words, they began to consider that it was not at all good that they played so many tricks on the Lord.
text:
> śuniyā prabhura vāṇī mane vicāraya
> prabhu-sane ati haṭha kabhu bhāla naya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---the words; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in their minds; [[synonyms:v:vicāraya]]---considered; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:ati]]---very much; [[synonyms:h:haṭha]]---tricks; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]] [[synonyms:n:naya]]---s not very good.
translation: When Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Rāmānanda Rāya heard these words, they began to consider that it was not at all good that they played so many tricks on the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.93
description: They both said, "Now that the rainy season is here, it will be difficult for You to travel. It is better to wait for Vijayā-daśamī before departing for Vṛndāvana."
text:
> duṅhe kahe,---ebe varṣā, calite nāribā
> vijayā-daśamī āile avaśya calibā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---both of them said; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:v:varṣā]]---rainy season; [[synonyms:c:calite]] [[synonyms:n:nāribā]]---You will not be able to go; [[synonyms:v:vijayā]]-[[synonyms:d:daśamī]]---the Vijayā-daśamī day; [[synonyms:ā:āile]]---when it arrives; [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:c:calibā]]---You will go.
translation: They both said, "Now that the rainy season is here, it will be difficult for You to travel. It is better to wait for Vijayā-daśamī before departing for Vṛndāvana."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.94
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to thus receive their permission. He waited until the rainy season passed, and when the day of Vijayā-daśamī arrived, He departed for Vṛndāvana.
text:
> ānande mahāprabhu varṣā kaila samādhāna
> vijayā-daśamī-dine karila payāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in great pleasure; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:varṣā]]---the rainy season; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:s:samādhāna]]---passed; [[synonyms:v:vijayā]]-[[synonyms:d:daśamī]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---on Vijayā-daśamī, the day when the victory was won by Lord Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:p:payāna]]---He departed.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to thus receive their permission. He waited until the rainy season passed, and when the day of Vijayā-daśamī arrived, He departed for Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.95
description: The Lord collected whatever remnants of food were left by Lord Jagannātha. He also took remnants of the Lord's kaḍāra ointment, sandalwood and ropes with Him.
text:
> jagannāthera prasāda prabhu yata pāñāchila
> kaḍāra, candana, ḍora, saba saṅge laila
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannāthera]]---of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---the remnants of food; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:p:pāñāchila]]---had obtained; [[synonyms:k:kaḍāra]]---a kind of //tilaka//; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍora]]---ropes; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]] [[synonyms:l:laila]]---He took with Him.
translation: The Lord collected whatever remnants of food were left by Lord Jagannātha. He also took remnants of the Lord's kaḍāra ointment, sandalwood and ropes with Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.96
description: After taking Lord Jagannātha's permission early in the morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu departed, and all the devotees of Orissa began following Him.
text:
> jagannāthe ājñā māgi' prabhāte calilā
> uḍiyā-bhakta-gaṇa saṅge pāche cali' āilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannāthe]]---from Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:m:māgi']]---taking permission; [[synonyms:p:prabhāte]]---early in the morning; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---departed; [[synonyms:u:uḍiyā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees of Orissa; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Him; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---following; [[synonyms:c:cali']] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---went.
translation: After taking Lord Jagannātha's permission early in the morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu departed, and all the devotees of Orissa began following Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.97
description: It was with great care that Caitanya Mahāprabhu forbade the Orissa devotees to follow Him. Accompanied by personal associates, He first went to Bhavānīpura.
text:
> uḍiyā-bhakta-gaṇe prabhu yatne nivārilā
> nija-gaṇa-saṅge prabhu 'bhavānīpura, āilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uḍiyā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the devotees of Orissa; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yatne]]---with great care; [[synonyms:n:nivārilā]]---stopped; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with His personal associates; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhavānīpura]] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came to Bhavānīpura.
translation: It was with great care that Caitanya Mahāprabhu forbade the Orissa devotees to follow Him. Accompanied by personal associates, He first went to Bhavānīpura.
purport: One goes through Bhavānīpura before reaching a well-known place named Jānkādei-pura, or Jānakīdevī-pura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.98
description: After Lord Caitanya reached Bhavānīpura, Rāmānanda Rāya arrived on his palanquin, and Vāṇīnātha Rāya had a large quantity of prasāda sent to the Lord.
text:
> rāmānanda āilā pāche dolāya caḍiyā
> vāṇīnātha bahu prasāda dila pāṭhāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---behind; [[synonyms:d:dolāya]] [[synonyms:c:caḍiyā]]---riding on a palanquin; [[synonyms:v:vāṇīnātha]]---Vāṇīnātha Rāya; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---a large quantity of; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---remnants of the food of Jagannātha; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāñā]]---sending.
translation: After Lord Caitanya reached Bhavānīpura, Rāmānanda Rāya arrived on his palanquin, and Vāṇīnātha Rāya had a large quantity of prasāda sent to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 16.99
description: After taking prasāda, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained there for the night. Early in the morning, He began walking and finally reached Bhuvaneśvara.
text:
> prasāda bhojana kari' tathāya rahilā
> prātaḥ-kāle cali' prabhu'bhuvaneśvara' āilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:b:bhojana]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---after taking the prasāda; [[synonyms:t:tathāya]] [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---He stayed there; [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---early in the morning; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---walking; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhuvaneśvara]] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---reached the place known as Bhuvaneśvara.
translation: After taking prasāda, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained there for the night. Early in the morning, He began walking and finally reached Bhuvaneśvara.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.1

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.100

translation: Even though He had not made such a plan, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained for ten days at Vārāṇasī, being obligated by the requests of His two servants.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.101
description: At Vārāṇasī there was a Mahārāṣṭrīyan brāhmaṇa who used to come daily to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. This brāhmaṇa was simply astonished to see the Lord's personal beauty and ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> mahārāṣṭrīya vipra āise prabhu dekhibāre
> prabhura rūpa-prema dekhi' haya camatkāre

translation: At Vārāṇasī there was a Mahārāṣṭrīyan brāhmaṇa who used to come daily to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. This brāhmaṇa was simply astonished to see the Lord's personal beauty and ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.102
description: When the brāhmaṇas of Vārāṇasī would invite Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to lunch, the Lord would not accept their invitations. He would reply, "I have already been invited somewhere else."
text:
> vipra saba nimantraya, prabhu nāhi māne
> prabhu kahe,---'āji mora hañāche nimantraṇe'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the brāhmaṇas; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:n:nimantraya]]---invite; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:m:māne]]---does not accept; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord replies; [[synonyms:ā:āji]]---today; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:h:hañāche]]---has been; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇe]]---invitation.
translation: When the brāhmaṇas of Vārāṇasī would invite Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to lunch, the Lord would not accept their invitations. He would reply, "I have already been invited somewhere else."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.103
description: Every day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu refused their invitation because He feared associating with Māyāvādī sannyāsīs.
text:
> ei-mata prati-dina karena vañcana
> sannyāsīra saṅga-bhaye nā mānena nimantraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---daily; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:v:vañcana]]---denies other inviters; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]]---of the Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---from fear of the association; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:m:mānena]]---does not accept; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation.
translation: Every day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu refused their invitation because He feared associating with Māyāvādī sannyāsīs.
purport: A Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsī// never accepts an invitation from a party who considers Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// and Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsīs// to be one and the same. In other words, Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsīs// do not at all like to associate with Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs,// to say nothing of eating together. This principle must be followed by the //sannyāsīs// of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. That is the instruction of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu given by His personal behavior.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.104
description: There was a great Māyāvādī sannyāsī named Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī who used to teach Vedānta philosophy to a great assembly of followers.
text:
> prakāśānanda śrīpāda sabhāte vasiyā
> 'vedānta' paḍāna bahu śiṣya-gaṇa lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prakāśānanda]]---Prakāśānanda; [[synonyms:ś:śrīpāda]]---a great //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:s:sabhāte]]---in the assembly; [[synonyms:v:vasiyā]]---sitting down; [[synonyms:v:vedānta]]---Vedānta philosophy; [[synonyms:p:paḍāna]]---instructs; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---many; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---disciples; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking.
translation: There was a great Māyāvādī sannyāsī named Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī who used to teach Vedānta philosophy to a great assembly of followers.
purport:
Śrīpāda Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī was a Māyāvādī //sannyāsī,// and his characteristics have been described in //Caitanya-bhāgavata (Madhya-khaṇḍa// Chapter Three):

> 'hasta', 'pada', 'mukha' mora nāhika 'locana'
> veda more ei-mata kare viḍambana
>
> kāśīte paḍāya veṭā 'prakāśa-ānanda'
> sei veṭā kare mora aṅga khaṇḍa-khaṇḍa
>
> vākhānaye veda, mora vigraha nā māne
> sarvāṅge ha-ila kuṣṭha, tabu nāhi jāne
>
> sarva-yajñamaya mora ye-aṅga---pavitra
> 'aja', 'bhava' ādi gāya yāṅhāra caritra
>
> 'puṇya' pavitratā pāya ye-aṅga-paraśe
> tāhā 'mithyā' bale veṭā kemana sāhase

In the //Madhya-khaṇḍa,// Chapter Twenty, it is said:

> sannyāsī 'prakāśānanda' vasaye kāśīte
> more khaṇḍa-khaṇḍa veṭā kare bhāla-mate
>
> paḍāya 'vedānta', mora 'vigraha' nā māne
> kuṣṭha karāiluṅ aṅge, tabu nāhi jāne
>
> 'satya' mora 'līlā-karma', 'satya' mora 'sthāna'
> ihā 'mithyā' bale, more kare khān-khān

Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī used to explain impersonalism, the Absolute Truth, as being without hands, legs, mouths or eyes. In this way he used to cheat the people by denying the personal form of the Lord. Such a foolish person was Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī, whose only business was to sever the limbs of the Lord by proving the Lord impersonal. Although the Lord has form, Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī was attempting to cut off the hands and legs of the Lord. This is the business of demons. The //Vedas// state that people who do not accept the Lord's form are rascals. The form of the Lord is factual, for Kṛṣṇa states in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:15:15|(Bg. 15.15)]]: //vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ.// When Kṛṣṇa says //aham,// He says "I am," which means "I," the person. He adds the word //eva,// which is used for conclusive verification. It is by Vedānta philosophy that one has to know the Supreme Person. Whoever describes Vedic knowledge as impersonal is a demon. One becomes successful in life by worshiping the form of the Lord. The Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// deny the form of the Lord, which delivers all fallen souls. Indeed, this form is cut to pieces by Māyāvādī demons.

The Personality of Godhead is worshiped by exalted demigods like Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva. The original Māyāvādī //sannyāsī,// Śaṅkarācārya, also accepted the fact that the Lord's form is transcendental. //Nārāyaṇaḥ paro 'vyaktāt:// "Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is beyond the //avyakta,// the unmanifested material energy." //Avyaktād aṇḍa-sambhavaḥ:// "This material world is a creation of that unmanifested material energy." However, Nārāyaṇa has His own eternal form, which is not created by material energy. Simply by worshiping the form of the Lord, one is purified. However, Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// are impersonalist philosophers, and they describe the form of the Lord as //māyā,// or false. How can one be purified by worshiping something false? Māyāvādī philosophers have no sufficient reason for being impersonalists. They blindly follow a principle that cannot be supported by reason or argument. This was the situation with Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī, the chief Māyāvādī //sannyāsī// of Benares. He was supposed to teach Vedānta philosophy, but he would not accept the form of the Lord; therefore he was attacked with leprosy. Nonetheless, he continued to commit sins by describing the Absolute Truth as impersonal. The Absolute Truth, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, always displays pastimes and activities, but Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// claim that these activities are false.

Some people falsely claim that Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī later became known as Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī, but this is not a fact. Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī was the uncle and spiritual master of Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī. In his //gṛhastha// life, Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī was a resident of Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra, and he belonged to the Vaiṣṇava Rāmānuja-sampradāya. It is a mistake to consider Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī and Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī the same man.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.105

translation: The brāhmaṇa told Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī, "There is a sannyāsī who has come from Jagannātha Purī, and I cannot describe His wonderful influence and glories.

description: "Everything is wonderful about that sannyāsī. He has a very well built and luxurious body, and His complexion is like purified gold.
text:
> sakala dekhiye tāṅte adbhuta-kathana
> prakāṇḍa-śarīra, śuddha-kāñcana-varaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakala]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiye]]---I see everything; [[synonyms:t:tāṅte]]---in Him; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]-[[synonyms:k:kathana]]---wonderful description; [[synonyms:p:prakāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śarīra]]---very large body; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]---pure; [[synonyms:k:kāñcana]]---gold; [[synonyms:v:varaṇa]]---complexion.
translation: "Everything is wonderful about that sannyāsī. He has a very well built and luxurious body, and His complexion is like purified gold.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.108
description: "He has arms that extend to His knees, and His eyes are like the petals of a lotus. In His person are all the transcendental symptoms of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

> yata kichu īśvarera sarva sal-lakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ājānu]]-[[synonyms:l:lambita]]---reaching down to the knees; [[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---arms; [[synonyms:k:kamala]]-[[synonyms:n:nayana]]---eyes like the petals of a lotus flower; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---as many as; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---any; [[synonyms:ī:īśvarera]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---transcendental symptoms.
translation: "He has arms that extend to His knees, and His eyes are like the petals of a lotus. In His person are all the transcendental symptoms of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.109

text:

> yei tāṅre dekhe, kare kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing that; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---one comes to the conclusion; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa Himself; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "When one sees all these features, one takes Him to be Nārāyaṇa Himself. Whoever sees Him immediately begins to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.11

text:
> 'uttama brāhmaṇa' eka saṅge avaśya cāhi
> bhikṣā kari' bhikṣā dibe, yābe pātra vahi'

text:

> se-saba lakṣaṇa prakaṭa dekhiye tāṅhāte

> nāma, rūpa, guṇa tāṅra, saba---anupama
