title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.183
description: "Foolish people will blaspheme You, but I shall not tolerate the words of such mischievous people."
text:
> 'mūrkha'-loka karibeka tomāra nindana
> sahite nā pārimu sei 'duṣṭe'ra vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---foolish persons; [[synonyms:k:karibeka]]---will do; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:n:nindana]]---blaspheming You; [[synonyms:s:sahite]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pārimu]]---I shall not be able to tolerate; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:d:duṣṭera]] [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---words of mischievous persons.
translation: "Foolish people will blaspheme You, but I shall not tolerate the words of such mischievous people."
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura remarks that although the //brāhmaṇa// did not belong to a superior community, he fearlessly chastised so-called caste //brāhmaṇas// because he was situated on the platform of pure devotional service. There are people who are opposed to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's accepting a Vaiṣṇava belonging to a lower caste. Such people do not consider //mahā-prasāda// transcendental, and therefore they are described here as //mūrkha// (foolish) and //duṣṭa// (mischievous). A pure devotee has the power to challenge such high-caste people, and his brave statements are not to be considered proud or puffed up. On the contrary, he is to be considered straightforward. Such a person does not like to flatter high-class //brāhmaṇas// who belong to the non-Vaiṣṇava community.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.184
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "The Vedas, Purāṇas and great learned sages are not always in agreement with one another. Consequently there are different religious principles.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---śruti, smṛti, yata ṛṣi-gaṇa
> sabe 'eka'-mata nahe, bhinna bhinna dharma
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:ś:śruti]]---the Vedas; [[synonyms:s:smṛti]]---the //Purāṇas//; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣi]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---great sages; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---do not agree; [[synonyms:b:bhinna]] [[synonyms:b:bhinna]] [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---different grades of religious principles.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "The Vedas, Purāṇas and great learned sages are not always in agreement with one another. Consequently there are different religious principles.
purport:
Unless one comes to the Absolute Truth, there is no possibility of agreement. //Nāsav ṛṣir yasya mataṁ na bhinnam:// it is said that a great learned scholar or sage cannot be exalted unless he disagrees. On the material platform, there is no possibility of agreement; therefore there are different kinds of religious systems. However, the Absolute Truth is one, and when one is situated in the Absolute Truth, there is no disagreement. On that absolute platform the Supreme Personality of Godhead is worshipable. As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:18:55|(Bg. 18.55)]]: //bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaś cāsmi tattvataḥ.// On the absolute platform, the worshipful Deity is one, and the process of worship is also one. That process is //bhakti.//

There are many different religions throughout the world because they are not all on the absolute platform of devotional service. As confirmed in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:18:66|(Bg. 18.66)]]: //sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja.// The word //ekam// means "one," Kṛṣṇa. On this platform, there are no different religious systems. According to //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:1:2|(1.1.2)]]: //dharmaḥ projjhita-kaitavo 'tra.// On the material platform, religious systems are different. //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// describes them from the very beginning as //dharmaḥ kaitavaḥ,// cheating religions. None of these religions are actually genuine. The genuine religious system is that which enables one to become a lover of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In the words of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:2:6|(1.2.6)]]:

> sa vai puṁsāṁ paro dharmo
> yato bhaktir adhokṣaje
> ahaituky apratihatā
> yayātmā suprasīdati

"The supreme occupation [//dharma//] for all humanity is that by which men can attain to loving devotional service unto the transcendent Lord. Such devotional service must be unmotivated and uninterrupted in order to completely satisfy the self."

On this platform there is nothing but the service of the Lord. When a person has no ulterior motive, there is certainly oneness and agreement of principles. Since everyone has a different body and mind, different types of religions are needed. But when one is situated on the spiritual platform, there are no bodily and mental differences. Consequently on the absolute platform there is oneness in religion.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.185
description: "A devotee's behavior establishes the true purpose of religious principles. The behavior of Mādhavendra Purī Gosvāmī is the essence of such religious principles."
text:
> dharma-sthāpana-hetu sādhura vyavahāra
> purī-gosāñira ye ācaraṇa, sei dharma sāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāpana]]-[[synonyms:h:hetu]]---to establish the principles of religion; [[synonyms:s:sādhura]] [[synonyms:v:vyavahāra]]---behavior of a devotee; [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:ā:ācaraṇa]]---the behavior; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:d:dharma]] [[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the essence of all religion.
translation: "A devotee's behavior establishes the true purpose of religious principles. The behavior of Mādhavendra Purī Gosvāmī is the essence of such religious principles."
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura gives the following commentary on this passage. A //sādhu// or an honest man is called a //mahājana// or a //mahātmā.// The //mahātmā// is thus described in //Bhagavad-gītā://

> mahātmānas tu māṁ pārtha
> daivīṁ prakṛtim āśritāḥ
> bhajanty ananya-manaso
> jñātvā bhūtādim avyayam

"O son of Pṛthā, those who are not deluded, the great souls, are under the protection of the divine nature. They are fully engaged in devotional service because they know Me as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, original and inexhaustible." [[books:bg:9:13|(Bg. 9.13)]]

In the material world, the word //mahātmā// is understood in different ways by different religionists. Mundaners also come up with their different angles of vision. For the conditioned soul busy in sense gratification, a //mahājana// is recognized according to the proportion of sense gratification he offers. For instance, a businessman may consider a certain banker to be a //mahājana,// and //karmīs// desiring material enjoyment may consider philosophers like Jaimini to be //mahājanas.// There are many //yogīs// who want to control the senses, and for them Patañjali Rṣi is a //mahā-jana.// For the //jñānīs,// the atheist Kapila, Vaśiṣṭha, Durvāsā, Dattātreya and other impersonalist philosophers are //mahājanas.// For the demons, Hiraṇyākṣa, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Rāvaṇa, Rāvaṇa's son Meghanāda, Jarāsandha and others are accepted as //mahājanas.// For materialistic anthropologists speculating on the evolution of the body, a person like Darwin is a //mahājana.// The scientists who are bewildered by Kṛṣṇa's external energy have no relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, yet they are accepted by some as //mahājanas.// Similarly, philosophers, historians, literary men, public speakers and social and political leaders are sometimes accepted as //mahājanas.// Such //mahājanas// are respected by certain men who have been described in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:3:19|(2.3.19)]]:

> śva-viḍ-varāhoṣṭra-kharaiḥ
> saṁstutaḥ puruṣaḥ paśuḥ
> na yat-karṇa-pathopeto
> jātu nāma gadāgrajaḥ

"Men who are like dogs, hogs, camels and asses praise those men who never listen to the transcendental pastimes of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the deliverer from evils."

Thus on the material platform animalistic leaders are worshiped by animals. Sometimes physicians, psychiatrists and social workers try to mitigate bodily pain, distress and fear, but they have no knowledge of spiritual identity and are bereft of a relationship with God. Yet they are considered //mahājanas// by the illusioned. Self-deceived persons sometimes accept leaders or spiritual masters from a priestly order that has been officially appointed by the codes of material life. In this way, they are deceived by official priests. Sometimes people accept as //mahā-janas// those who have been designated by Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura as //ḍhaṅga-vipras// (imposter //brāhmaṇas).// Such imposters imitate the characteristics of Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura, and they envy Haridāsa Ṭhākura, who was certainly a //mahājana.// They make great artificial endeavors, advertising themselves as great devotees of the Lord or as mystic hypnotists knowledgeable in witchcraft, hypnotism and miracles. Sometimes people accept demons like Pūtanā, Tṛṇāvarta, Vatsa, Baka, Aghāsura and Dhenuka, Kālīya and Pralamba. Some people accept imitators and adversaries of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, such as Pauṇḍraka, Śṛgāla Vāsudeva, the spiritual master of the demons (Śukrācārya), or atheists like Cārvāka, King Vena, Sugata and Arhat. Such people have no faith in Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Rather, they accept godless cheaters who present themselves as incarnations of God and cheat foolish people within the material world by word jugglery. Thus many rascals are accepted as //mahājanas.//

In this material world a person may be famous as a //karma-vīra,// a successful fruitive worker, or one may be very successful in performing religious duties, or he may be known as a hero in mental speculation (//jñāna-vīra),// or he may be a very famous renunciant. In any case, //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:23:56|(3.23.56)]] gives the following opinion in this matter.

> neha yat karma dharmāya
> na virāgāya kalpate
> na tīrtha-pada-sevāyai
> jīvann api mṛto hi saḥ

"Anyone whose work is not meant to elevate him to religious life, anyone whose religious ritualistic performances do not raise him to renunciation, and anyone situated in renunciation that does not lead him to devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead must be considered dead, although he is breathing."

The conclusion is that all pious activity, fruitive activity, religious principles and renunciation must ultimately lead to devotional service. There are different types of processes for rendering service. One may serve his country, people, society, the //varṇāśrama-dharma,// the sick, the poor, the rich, women, demigods and so on. All this comes under the heading of sense gratification, or enjoyment in the material world. It is most unfortunate that people are more or less attracted by such material activity and that the leaders of these activities are accepted as //mahājanas,// great ideal leaders. Actually they are only misleaders, but an ordinary man cannot understand how he is being misled.

Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says: //sādhu-śāstra-guru-vākya, cittete kariyā aikya. A sādhu// is a great personality like Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The //śāstras// are the injunctions of revealed scriptures. Those who are devoid of devotional service sometimes mistake those who have mundane motives for //mahājanas.// The only motive must be //kṛṣṇa-bhakti,// devotional service to the Lord. Sometimes fruitive workers, dry philosophers, nondevotees, mystic //yogīs// and persons attached to material opulence, women and money are considered //mahājanas.// However, //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:6:3:25|(6.3.25)]] gives the following statements about such unauthorized //mahājanas://

> prāyeṇa veda tad idaṁ na mahājano 'yaṁ
> devyā vimohita-matir bata māyayālam
> trayyāṁ jaḍī-kṛta-matir madhu-puṣpitāyāṁ
> vaitānike mahati karmaṇi yujyamānaḥ

In this material world, //karmīs// (fruitive actors) are accepted as //mahājanas// by foolish people who do not know the value of devotional service. Their mundane intelligence and mental speculative methods are under the control of the three modes of material nature. Consequently they cannot understand unalloyed devotional service. They are attracted by material activities, and they become worshipers of material nature. Thus they are known as fruitive actors. They even become entangled in material activities disguised as spiritual activities. In //Bhagavad-gītā,// such people are described as //veda-vāda-ratā.// They do not understand the real purpose of the //Vedas,// yet they think of themselves as Vedic authorities. People versed in Vedic knowledge must know Kṛṣṇa as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. //Vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ.// [[books:bg:15:15|(Bg. 15.15)]]

A man covered by illusion cannot understand the proper way; therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu says: //dharma-sthāpana-hetu sādhura vyavahāra.// The behavior of a devotee is the criterion for all other behavior. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself followed the devotional principles and taught others to follow them. //Purī-gosāñira ye ācaraṇa, sei dharma sāra.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally followed the behavior of Mādhavendra Purī and advised others to follow his principles. Unfortunately, people have been attracted to the material body since time immemorial.

> yasyātma-buddhiḥ kuṇape tridhātuke
> sva-dhīḥ kalatrādiṣu bhauma ijya-dhīḥ
> yat-tīrtha-buddhiḥ salile na karhicij
> janeṣv abhijñeṣu sa eva go-kharaḥ

"A human being who identifies this body made of three elements with his self, who considers the by-products of the body to be his kinsmen, who considers the land of birth worshipable, and who goes to the place of pilgrimage simply to take a bath rather than meet men of transcendental knowledge there is to be considered like an ass or a cow." (//Bhāg.// 10.84.13) Those who accept the logic of //gaḍ-ḍalikā-pravāha// and follow in the footsteps of pseudo-//mahājanas// are carried away by the waves of //māyā.// Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura therefore warns:

> miche māyāra vaśe, yāccha bhese',
> khāccha hābuḍubu, bhāi
> jīva kṛṣṇa-dāsa, e viśvāsa,
> ka'rle ta' āra duḥkha nāi

"Don't be carried away by the waves of //māyā.// Just surrender to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, and all miseries will end." Those who follow social customs and behavior forget to follow the path chalked out by the //mahājanas;// thus they are offenders at the feet of the //mahājanas.// Sometimes they consider such //mahājanas// very conservative, or they create their own //mahājanas.// In this way they ignore the principles of the //paramparā// system. This is a great misfortune for everyone. If one does not follow in the footsteps of a real //mahājana,// one's plans for happiness will be frustrated. This is elaborately explained in //Madhya-līlā// (Chapter Twenty-five, verses 55, 56 and 58). It is there stated:

> parama kāraṇa īśvare keha nāhi māne
> sva-sva-mata sthāpe para-matera khaṇḍane
>
> tāte chaya darśana haite 'tattva' nāhi jāni
> 'mahājana' yei kahe, sei 'satya' māni
>
> śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-vāṇī---amṛtera dhāra
> tiṅho ye kahaye vastu, sei 'tattva'---sāra

People are so unfortunate that they do not accept the instructions of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Instead, they want to be supported by so-called //mahājanas,// authorities. //Tāte chaya darśana haite 'tattva' nāhi jāni:// we cannot ascertain the real truth simply by following speculators. We have to follow the footsteps of the //mahājanas// in the disciplic succession. Then our attempt will be successful. //Śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-vāṇī-amṛtera dhāra:// "Whatever is spoken by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is an incessant flow of nectar." Whoever accepts His words as reality can understand the essence of the Absolute Truth. No one can ascertain the Absolute Truth by following the philosophy of Sāṅkhya or Patañjali, for the followers of Sāṅkhya or Patañjali do not accept Lord Viṣṇu as the Supreme Personality of Godhead (//na te viduḥ svārtha-gatiṁ hi viṣṇum).// The ambition of such people is never fulfilled; therefore they are attracted by the external energy. Although mental speculators may be renowned all over the world as great authorities, actually they are not. Such leaders are themselves conservative and not at all liberal. However, if we preach this philosophy, people will consider Vaiṣṇavas very sectarian. Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī was a real //mahājana,// but misguided people cannot distinguish the real from the unreal. However, a person who is awakened to Kṛṣṇa consciousness can understand the real religious path chalked out by the Lord and His pure devotees. Śrī Mādhavendra Purī was a real //mahājana// because he understood the Absolute Truth properly and throughout his life behaved like a pure devotee. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu approved the method of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī. Therefore, although from the material viewpoint the Sanoḍiyā //brāhmaṇa// was on a lower platform, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu considered him situated on the highest platform of spiritual realization.

Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (6.3.20) states that there are twelve //mahājanas:// Brahmā, Nārada, Śambhu, Kumāra, Kapila, Manu, Prahlāda, Janaka, Bhīṣma, Bali, Śukadeva and Yamarāja.

To select our //mahājanas// in the Gauḍīya-sampradāya, we have to follow in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His representatives. His next representative is Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, and the next are the six Gosvāmīs-Śrī Rūpa, Śrī Sanātana, Bhaṭṭa Raghunātha, Śrī Jīva, Gopāla Bhaṭṭa and Dāsa Raghunātha. The follower of Viṣṇusvāmī was Śrīdhara Svāmī, the most well known commentator on //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.// He was also a //mahājana.// Similarly, Caṇḍīdāsa, Vidyāpati and Jayadeva were all //mahājanas.// One who tries to imitate the //mahājanas// just to become an imitative spiritual master is certainly far away from following in the footsteps of the //mahājanas.// Sometimes people cannot actually understand how a //mahājana// follows other //mahājanas.// In this way people are inclined to fall from devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.186
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued," 'Dry arguments are inconclusive. A great personality whose opinion does not differ from others is not considered a great sage. Simply by studying the Vedas, which are variegated, one cannot come to the right path by which religious principles are understood. The solid truth of religious principles is hidden in the heart of an unadulterated self-realized person. Consequently, as the śāstras confirm, one should accept whatever progressive path the mahājanas advocate.' "
text:
> tarko 'pratiṣṭhaḥ śrutayo vibhinnā
> nāsāv ṛṣir yasya mataṁ na bhinnam
> dharmasya tattvaṁ nihitaṁ guhāyāṁ
> mahājano yena gataḥ sa panthāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tarkaḥ]]---dry argument; [[synonyms:a:apratiṣṭhaḥ]]---not fixed; [[synonyms:ś:śrutayaḥ]]---//Vedas//; [[synonyms:v:vibhinnāḥ]]---possessing different departments; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---that; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣiḥ]]---great sage; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---whose; [[synonyms:m:matam]]---opinion; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:b:bhinnam]]---separate; [[synonyms:d:dharmasya]]---of religious principles; [[synonyms:t:tattvam]]---truth; [[synonyms:n:nihitam]]---placed; [[synonyms:g:guhāyām]]---in the heart of a realized person; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:j:janaḥ]]---self-realized predecessors; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---by which way; [[synonyms:g:gataḥ]]---acted; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:p:panthāḥ]]---the pure unadulterated path.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued," 'Dry arguments are inconclusive. A great personality whose opinion does not differ from others is not considered a great sage. Simply by studying the Vedas, which are variegated, one cannot come to the right path by which religious principles are understood. The solid truth of religious principles is hidden in the heart of an unadulterated self-realized person. Consequently, as the śāstras confirm, one should accept whatever progressive path the mahājanas advocate.' "
purport: This is a verse spoken by Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja in the //Mahābhārata, Vana-parva// (313.117).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.187
description: After this discussion, the brāhmaṇa gave lunch to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Then all the people residing in Mathurā came to see the Lord.
text:
> tabe sei vipra prabhuke bhikṣā karāila
> madhu-purīra loka saba prabhuke dekhite āila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---after that; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---gave lunch; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:p:purīra]]---of Mathurā; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people in general; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]] [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came to see.
translation: After this discussion, the brāhmaṇa gave lunch to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Then all the people residing in Mathurā came to see the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.188
description: People came by hundreds of thousands, and no one could count them. Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came out of the house to give audience to the people.
text:
> lakṣa-saṅkhya loka āise, nāhika gaṇana
> bāhira hañā prabhu dila daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkhya]]---numbering hundreds of thousands; [[synonyms:l:loka]] [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---people came; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---there is no counting; [[synonyms:b:bāhira]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---coming out; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dila]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---gave audience.
translation: People came by hundreds of thousands, and no one could count them. Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came out of the house to give audience to the people.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.189
description: When the people assembled, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu raised His arms and said very loudly, "Hari bol!" The people responded to the Lord and became ecstatic. As if mad, they began to dance and vibrate the transcendental sound, "Hari!"
text:
> bāhu tuli' bale prabhu 'hari-bola'-dhvani
> preme matta nāce loka kari' hari-dhvani
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāhu]] [[synonyms:t:tuli']]---raising the arms; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---says; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:b:bola]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---the transcendental sound vibration Hari bol; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:m:matta]]---maddened; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---making the transcendental vibration Hari.
translation: When the people assembled, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu raised His arms and said very loudly, "Hari bol!" The people responded to the Lord and became ecstatic. As if mad, they began to dance and vibrate the transcendental sound, "Hari!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.19
description: "The other brāhmaṇa can carry Your cloth and waterpot, and Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya will collect alms and cook for You."
text:
> sei vipra vahi' nibe vastrāmbu-bhājana
> bhaṭṭācārya bhikṣā dibe kari' bhikṣāṭana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the other //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:v:vahi']] [[synonyms:n:nibe]]---will carry; [[synonyms:v:vastra]]-[[synonyms:a:ambu]]-[[synonyms:b:bhājana]]---the cloth and waterpot; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:d:dibe]]---will arrange for cooking; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---performing; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]-[[synonyms:a:aṭana]]---collecting alms.
translation: "The other brāhmaṇa can carry Your cloth and waterpot, and Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya will collect alms and cook for You."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.190
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bathed in twenty-four ghats along the banks of the Yamunā, and the brāhmaṇa showed Him all the places of pilgrimage.
text:
> yamunāra 'cabbiśa ghāṭe' prabhu kaila snāna
> sei vipra prabhuke dekhāya tīrtha-sthāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yamunāra]]---of the River Yamunā; [[synonyms:c:cabbiśa]] [[synonyms:g:ghāṭe]]---in the twenty-four ghats, or bathing places; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhāya]]---shows; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---the holy places of pilgrimage.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bathed in twenty-four ghats along the banks of the Yamunā, and the brāhmaṇa showed Him all the places of pilgrimage.
purport: The twenty-four ghats (bathing places) along the Yamunā are (1) Avimukta, (2) Adhirūḍha, (3) Guhya-tīrtha, (4) Prayāga-tīrtha, (5) Kanakhala-tīrtha, (6) Tinduka, (7) Sūrya-tīrtha, (8) Vaṭasvāmī, (9) Dhruva-ghāṭa, (10) Ṛṣi-tīrtha, (11) Mokṣa-tīrtha, (12) Bodha-tīrtha, (13) Gokarṇa, (14) Kṛṣṇagaṅgā, (15) Vaikuṇṭha, (16) Asi-kuṇḍa, (17) Catuḥ-sāmudrika-kūpa, (18) Akrūra-tīrtha, (19) Yājñika-vipra-sthāna, (20) Kubjā-kūpa, (21) Raṅga-sthala, (22) Mañca-sthala, (23) Mallayuddha-sthāna and (24) Daśāśvamedha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.191
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited all the holy places on the banks of the Yamunā, including Svayambhu, Viśrāma-ghāṭa, Dīrgha Viṣṇu, Bhūteśvara, Mahāvidyā and Gokarṇa.
text:
> svayambhu, viśrāma, dīrgha-viṣṇu, bhūteśvara
> mahāvidyā, gokarṇādi dekhilā vistara

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited all the holy places on the banks of the Yamunā, including Svayambhu, Viśrāma-ghāṭa, Dīrgha Viṣṇu, Bhūteśvara, Mahāvidyā and Gokarṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.192
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to see the various forests of Vṛndāvana, He took the brāhmaṇa with Him.
text:
> 'vana' dekhibāre yadi prabhura mana haila
> sei ta brāhmaṇe prabhu saṅgete la-ila

translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to see the various forests of Vṛndāvana, He took the brāhmaṇa with Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.193
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the different forests, including Madhuvana, Tālavana, Kumudavana and Bahulāvana. Wherever He went, He took His bath with great ecstatic love.
text:

> tāhāṅ tāhāṅ snāna kari' premāviṣṭa hailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:v:vana]]---Madhuvana; [[synonyms:t:tāla]]---Tālavana; [[synonyms:k:kumuda]]---Kumudavana; [[synonyms:b:bahulā]]-[[synonyms:v:vana]]---Bahulāvana; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---He visited; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---here and there; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking bath; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became overwhelmed by ecstatic love.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the different forests, including Madhuvana, Tālavana, Kumudavana and Bahulāvana. Wherever He went, He took His bath with great ecstatic love.
purport: The word //vana// means "forest." Vṛndāvana is the name given to the forest where Śrīmatī Vṛndādevī (Tulasīdevī) grows profusely. Actually it is not a forest as we ordinarily consider a forest because it is very thick with green vegetation. There are twelve such //vanas// in Vṛndāvana. Some are located on the western side of the Yamunā and others on the eastern side. The forests situated on the eastern side are Bhadravana, Bilvavana, Lauhavana, Bhāṇḍīravana and Mahāvana. On the western side are Madhuvana, Tālavana, Kumudavana, Bahulāvana, Kāmyavana, Khadiravana and Vṛndāvana. These are the twelve forests of the Vṛndāvana area.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.194
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed through Vṛndāvana, herds of grazing cows saw Him pass and, immediately surrounding Him, began to moo very loudly.
text:
> pathe gābhī-ghaṭā care prabhure dekhiyā
> prabhuke beḍaya āsi' huṅkāra kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the road; [[synonyms:g:gābhī]]-[[synonyms:g:ghaṭā]]---groups of cows; [[synonyms:c:care]]---graze; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---after seeing Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]] [[synonyms:b:beḍaya]]---they surrounded the Lord; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:h:huṅ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāra]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---making a loud vibration.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed through Vṛndāvana, herds of grazing cows saw Him pass and, immediately surrounding Him, began to moo very loudly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.195
description: Seeing the herds approach Him, the Lord was stunned with ecstatic love. The cows then began to lick His body in great affection.
text:
> gābhī dekhi' stabdha prabhu premera taraṅge
> vātsalye gābhī prabhura cāṭe saba-aṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gābhī]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the cows; [[synonyms:s:stabdha]]---stunned; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:premera]] [[synonyms:t:taraṅge]]---in the waves of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:v:vātsalye]]---in great affection; [[synonyms:g:gābhī]]---all the cows; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cāṭe]]---licked; [[synonyms:s:saba]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---all over the body.
translation: Seeing the herds approach Him, the Lord was stunned with ecstatic love. The cows then began to lick His body in great affection.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.196
description: Becoming pacified, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to caress the cows, and the cows, being unable to give up His company, went with Him.
text:
> sustha hañā prabhu kare aṅga-kaṇḍūyana
> prabhu-saṅge cale, nāhi chāḍe dhenu-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sustha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming patient; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---of the body; [[synonyms:k:kaṇḍūyana]]---scratching; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---go; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍe]]---do not give up; [[synonyms:d:dhenu]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the cows.
translation: Becoming pacified, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to caress the cows, and the cows, being unable to give up His company, went with Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.197
description: It was with great difficulty that the cowherd men were able to keep the cows back. Then when the Lord chanted, all the deer heard His sweet voice and approached Him.
text:
> kaṣṭe-sṛṣṭye dhenu saba rākhila goyāla
> prabhu-kaṇṭha-dhvani śuni' āise mṛgī-pāla
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kaṣṭe]]-[[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭye]]---with great difficulty; [[synonyms:d:dhenu]]---the cows; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:r:rākhila]]---kept back; [[synonyms:g:goyāla]]---the cowherd men; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:k:kaṇṭha]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---the musical voice of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---came; [[synonyms:m:mṛgī]]-[[synonyms:p:pāla]]---flocks of deer.
translation: It was with great difficulty that the cowherd men were able to keep the cows back. Then when the Lord chanted, all the deer heard His sweet voice and approached Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.198
description: When the does and bucks came and saw the Lord's face, they began to lick His body. Not being at all afraid of Him, they accompanied Him along the path.
text:
> mṛga-mṛgī mukha dekhi' prabhu-aṅga cāṭe
> bhaya nāhi kare, saṅge yāya vāṭe-vāṭe
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]-[[synonyms:m:mṛgī]]---the deer, both male and female; [[synonyms:m:mukha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing His face; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]] [[synonyms:c:cāṭe]]---began to lick the body of the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---they were not at all afraid; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---go with Him; [[synonyms:v:vāṭe]]-[[synonyms:v:vāṭe]]---all along the road.
translation: When the does and bucks came and saw the Lord's face, they began to lick His body. Not being at all afraid of Him, they accompanied Him along the path.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.199
description: Bumblebees and birds like the parrot and cuckoo all began to sing loudly on the fifth note, and the peacocks began to dance in front of the Lord.
text:
> śuka, pika, bhṛṅga prabhure dekhi' 'pañcama' gāya
> śikhi-gaṇa nṛtya kari' prabhu-āge yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]---parrots; [[synonyms:p:pika]]---cuckoos; [[synonyms:b:bhṛṅga]]---bumblebees; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:pañcama]]---the fifth musical note; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sing; [[synonyms:ś:śikhi]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---peacocks; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---performing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---go.
translation: Bumblebees and birds like the parrot and cuckoo all began to sing loudly on the fifth note, and the peacocks began to dance in front of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.2
description: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda! All glories to Advaitacandra! All glories to all the devotees of the Lord!
text:
> jaya jaya gauracandra jaya nityānanda
> jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gauracandra]]---to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---to Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---to Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---to the devotees of Lord Caitanya.
translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda! All glories to Advaitacandra! All glories to all the devotees of the Lord!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.20
description: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the request of Svarūpa Dāmodara Paṇḍita and agreed to take Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya with Him.
text:
> tāṅhāra vacana prabhu aṅgīkāra kaila
> balabhadra-bhaṭṭācārye saṅge kari' nila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---his words; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---accepted; [[synonyms:b:balabhadra]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārye]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]] [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:n:nila]]---took with Him.
translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the request of Svarūpa Dāmodara Paṇḍita and agreed to take Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya with Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.200
description: Upon seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the trees and creepers of Vṛndāvana became jubilant. Their twigs stood up, and they began to shed tears of ecstasy in the form of honey.
text:
> prabhu dekhi' vṛndāvanera vṛkṣa-latā-gaṇe
> aṅkura pulaka, madhu-aśru variṣaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvane]]---of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:l:latā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the trees and creepers; [[synonyms:a:aṅkura]]---twigs; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]---jubilant; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears in the form of honey; [[synonyms:v:variṣaṇe]]---pour.
translation: Upon seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the trees and creepers of Vṛndāvana became jubilant. Their twigs stood up, and they began to shed tears of ecstasy in the form of honey.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.201
description: The trees and creepers, overloaded with fruits and flowers, fell down at the lotus feet of the Lord and greeted Him with various presentations as if they were friends.
text:
> phula-phala bhari' ḍāla paḍe prabhu-pāya
> bandhu dekhi' bandhu yena'bheṭa' lañā yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:phula]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]] [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---loaded with fruits and flowers; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍāla]]---the branches; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fall down; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pāya]]---at the lotus feet of the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bandhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing one friend; [[synonyms:b:bandhu]]---another friend; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:b:bheṭa]]---a presentation; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes.
translation: The trees and creepers, overloaded with fruits and flowers, fell down at the lotus feet of the Lord and greeted Him with various presentations as if they were friends.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.202
description: Thus all the moving and nonmoving living entities of Vṛndāvana became very jubilant to see the Lord. It was as if friends were made happy by seeing another friend.
text:
> prabhu dekhi' vṛndāvanera sthāvara-jaṅgama
> ānandita---bandhu yena dekhe bandhu-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the Lord; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvanera]]---of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:s:sthāvara]]-[[synonyms:j:jaṅgama]]---all living entities, moving and not moving; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very jubilant; [[synonyms:b:bandhu]]---friend; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---see; [[synonyms:b:bandhu]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---friends.
translation: Thus all the moving and nonmoving living entities of Vṛndāvana became very jubilant to see the Lord. It was as if friends were made happy by seeing another friend.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.203
description: Seeing their affection, the Lord was moved by ecstatic love. He began to sport with them exactly as a friend sports with another friend. Thus He voluntarily came under the control of His friends.
text:
> tā-sabāra prīti dekhi' prabhu bhāvāveśe
> sabā-sane krīḍā kare hañā tāra vaśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:p:prīti]]---affection; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:s:sabā]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with all of them; [[synonyms:k:krīḍā]]---sporting; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---their; [[synonyms:v:vaśe]]---under control.
translation: Seeing their affection, the Lord was moved by ecstatic love. He began to sport with them exactly as a friend sports with another friend. Thus He voluntarily came under the control of His friends.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.204
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to embrace each and every tree and creeper, and they began to offer their fruits and flowers as if in meditation.
text:
> prati vṛkṣa-latā prabhu karena āliṅgana
> puṣpādi dhyāne karena kṛṣṇe samarpaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prati]]---each and every; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:l:latā]]---tree and creeper; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embraced; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---all the flowers and fruits; [[synonyms:d:dhyāne]]---in meditation; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---do; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:samarpaṇa]]---offering.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to embrace each and every tree and creeper, and they began to offer their fruits and flowers as if in meditation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.205
description: The Lord's body was restless, and tears, trembling and jubilation were manifest. He said very loudly, "Chant Kṛṣṇa! Chant Kṛṣṇa!"
text:
> aśru-kampa-pulaka-preme śarīra asthire
> 'kṛṣṇa' bala, 'kṛṣṇa' bala---bale uccaiḥsvare
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]---jubilation; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:ś:śarīra]]---the whole body; [[synonyms:a:asthire]]---restless; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bala]]---say Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bala]]---say Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---the Lord says; [[synonyms:u:uccaiḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:svare]]---very loudly.
translation: The Lord's body was restless, and tears, trembling and jubilation were manifest. He said very loudly, "Chant Kṛṣṇa! Chant Kṛṣṇa!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.206
description: All moving and nonmoving creatures then began to vibrate the transcendental sound of Hare Kṛṣṇa, as if they were echoing the deep sound of Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> sthāvara-jaṅgama mili' kare kṛṣṇa-dhvani
> prabhura gambhīra-svare yena prati-dhvani
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sthāvara]]-[[synonyms:j:jaṅgama]]---all living entities, nonmoving and moving; [[synonyms:m:mili']]---meeting together; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---vibration of the sound Hare Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gambhīra]]-[[synonyms:s:svare]]---deep voice; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---responsive vibration.
translation: All moving and nonmoving creatures then began to vibrate the transcendental sound of Hare Kṛṣṇa, as if they were echoing the deep sound of Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.207
description: The Lord then clasped the necks of the deer and began to cry. There was jubilation manifest in the bodies of the deer, and tears were in their eyes.
text:
> mṛgera galā dhari' prabhu karena rodane
> mṛgera pulaka aṅge, aśru nayane
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mṛgera]]---of the deer; [[synonyms:g:galā]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching the necks; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:r:rodane]]---crying; [[synonyms:m:mṛgera]]---of the deer; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]] [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---jubilation; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:n:nayane]]---in the eyes.
translation: The Lord then clasped the necks of the deer and began to cry. There was jubilation manifest in the bodies of the deer, and tears were in their eyes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.208
description: When a male and female parrot appeared on the branches of a tree, the Lord saw them and wanted to hear them speak.
text:
> vṛkṣa-ḍāle śuka-śārī dila daraśana
> tāhā dekhi' prabhura kichu śunite haila mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:ḍ:ḍāle]]---on a branch of a tree; [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śārī]]---male and female parrots; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---appearance; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing that; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:ś:śunite]]---to hear; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind.
translation: When a male and female parrot appeared on the branches of a tree, the Lord saw them and wanted to hear them speak.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.209
description: Both parrots flew onto the hand of the Lord and began to chant the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, and the Lord listened to them.
text:
> śuka-śārikā prabhura hāte uḍi' paḍe
> prabhuke śunāñā kṛṣṇera guṇa-śloka paḍe
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śārikā]]---the parrots, male and female; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hāte]]---on the hand; [[synonyms:u:uḍi']]---flying; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fall; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śunāñā]]---causing to hear; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---chanted verses about the transcendental qualities.
translation: Both parrots flew onto the hand of the Lord and began to chant the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, and the Lord listened to them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.21
description: On the previous night, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had visited Lord Jagannātha and taken His permission. Now, near the end of night, the Lord got up and started immediately. He was not seen by others.
text:
> pūrva-rātrye jagannātha dekhi' 'ājñā' lañā
> śeṣa-rātre uṭhi' prabhu calilā lukāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:r:rātrye]]---on the previous night; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking permission; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]-[[synonyms:r:rātre]]---near the end of night; [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---rising; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---started; [[synonyms:l:lukāñā]]---without being seen.
translation: On the previous night, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had visited Lord Jagannātha and taken His permission. Now, near the end of night, the Lord got up and started immediately. He was not seen by others.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.210
description: The male parrot sang: "The glorification of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is beneficial to everyone in the universe. His beauty is victorious over the gopīs of Vṛndāvana, and it subdues their patience. His pastimes astound the goddess of fortune, and His bodily strength turns Govardhana Hill into a small toy like a ball. His spotless qualities are unlimited, and His behavior satisfies everyone. Lord Kṛṣṇa is attractive to everyone. Oh, may our Lord maintain the whole universe!"
text:
> saundaryaṁ lalanāli-dhairya-dalanaṁ līlā ramā-stambhinī
> vīryaṁ kandukitādri-varyam amalāḥ pāre-parārdhaṁ guṇāḥ
> śīlaṁ sarva-janānurañjanam aho yasyāyam asmat-prabhur
> viśvaṁ viśva-janīna-kīrtir avatāt kṛṣṇo jagan-mohanaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saundaryam]]---the bodily beauty; [[synonyms:l:lalanā]]-[[synonyms:ā:āli]]---of groups of //gopīs//; [[synonyms:d:dhairya]]---the patience; [[synonyms:d:dalanam]]---subduing; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:r:ramā]]---the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:s:stambhinī]]---astounding; [[synonyms:v:vīryam]]---strength; [[synonyms:k:kandukita]]---making like a small ball for throwing; [[synonyms:a:adri]]-[[synonyms:v:varyam]]---the great mountain; [[synonyms:a:amalāḥ]]---without a spot; [[synonyms:p:pāre]]-[[synonyms:p:parārdham]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:g:guṇāḥ]]---qualities; [[synonyms:ś:śīlam]]---behavior; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---all kinds of living entities; [[synonyms:a:anurañjanam]]---satisfying; [[synonyms:a:aho]]---oh; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---whose; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:a:asmat]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhuḥ]]---our Lord; [[synonyms:v:viśvam]]---the whole universe; [[synonyms:v:viśva]]-[[synonyms:j:janīna]]---for the benefit of everyone; [[synonyms:k:kīrtiḥ]]---whose glorification; [[synonyms:a:avatāt]]---may He maintain; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:m:mohanaḥ]]---the attractor of the whole world.
translation: The male parrot sang: "The glorification of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is beneficial to everyone in the universe. His beauty is victorious over the gopīs of Vṛndāvana, and it subdues their patience. His pastimes astound the goddess of fortune, and His bodily strength turns Govardhana Hill into a small toy like a ball. His spotless qualities are unlimited, and His behavior satisfies everyone. Lord Kṛṣṇa is attractive to everyone. Oh, may our Lord maintain the whole universe!"
purport: This verse is found in the //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (13.29).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.211
description: After hearing this description of Lord Kṛṣṇa from the male parrot, the female parrot began to recite a description of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
text:
> śuka-mukhe śuni' tabe kṛṣṇera varṇana
> śārikā paḍaye tabe rādhikā-varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the mouth of the male parrot; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---a description of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śārikā]]---female parrot; [[synonyms:p:paḍaye]]---recites; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:r:rādhikā]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---a description of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
translation: After hearing this description of Lord Kṛṣṇa from the male parrot, the female parrot began to recite a description of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.212
description: The female parrot said: "Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's affection, Her exquisite beauty and good behavior, Her artistic dancing and chanting and Her poetic compositions are all so attractive that they attract the mind of Kṛṣṇa, who attracts the mind of everyone in the universe."
text:
> śrī-rādhikāyāḥ priyatā surūpatā
> suśīlatā nartana-gāna-cāturī
> guṇāli-sampat kavitā ca rājate
> jagan-mano-mohana-citta-mohinī
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rādhikāyāḥ]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:p:priyatā]]---affection; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpatā]]---exquisite beauty; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:ś:śīlatā]]---good behavior; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]-[[synonyms:g:gāna]]---in chanting and dancing; [[synonyms:c:cāturī]]---artistry; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āli]]-[[synonyms:s:sampat]]---possession of such transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:k:kavitā]]---poetry; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:r:rājate]]---shine; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:m:mohana]]---of Kṛṣṇa, who attracts the mind of the whole universe; [[synonyms:c:citta]]-[[synonyms:m:mohinī]]---the attractor of the mind.
translation: The female parrot said: "Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's affection, Her exquisite beauty and good behavior, Her artistic dancing and chanting and Her poetic compositions are all so attractive that they attract the mind of Kṛṣṇa, who attracts the mind of everyone in the universe."
purport: This verse is found in the //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (13.30).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.213
description: Thereafter the male parrot said, "Kṛṣṇa is the enchanter of the mind of Cupid." He then began to recite another verse.
text:
> punaḥ śuka kahe,---kṛṣṇa 'madana-mohana'
> tabe āra śloka śuka karila paṭhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]---the male parrot; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mohana]]---Kṛṣṇa is the conqueror of the mind of Cupid; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verse; [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]---the male parrot; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:p:paṭhana]]---recited.
translation: Thereafter the male parrot said, "Kṛṣṇa is the enchanter of the mind of Cupid." He then began to recite another verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.214
description: The parrot then said, "My dear śārī [female parrot], Śrī Kṛṣṇa carries a flute and enchants the hearts of all women throughout the universe. He is specifically the enjoyer of beautiful gopīs, and He is the enchanter of Cupid also. Let Him be glorified!"
text:
> vamśī-dhārī jagan-nāri-
> citta-hārī sa śārike
> vihārī gopa-nārībhir
> jīyān madana-mohanaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:d:dhārī]]---the carrier of the flute; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:n:nārī]]---of all women of the universe; [[synonyms:c:citta]]-[[synonyms:h:hārī]]---the stealer of the hearts; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:ś:śārike]]---my dear //śārī//; [[synonyms:v:vihārī]]---enjoyer; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:n:nārībhiḥ]]---with the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:j:jīyāt]]---let Him be glorified; [[synonyms:m:madana]]---of Cupid; [[synonyms:m:mohanaḥ]]---the enchanter.
translation: The parrot then said, "My dear śārī [female parrot], Śrī Kṛṣṇa carries a flute and enchants the hearts of all women throughout the universe. He is specifically the enjoyer of beautiful gopīs, and He is the enchanter of Cupid also. Let Him be glorified!"
purport: This verse is also found in the //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (13.31).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.215
description: Then the female parrot began to speak jokingly to śuka, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was struck with wonderful ecstatic love to hear her speak.
text:
> punaḥ śārī kahe śuke kari' parihāsa
> tāhā śuni' prabhura haila vismaya-premollāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:ś:śārī]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the female parrot said; [[synonyms:ś:śuke]]---unto the male parrot; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:p:parihāsa]]---jokingly; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing that; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:v:vismaya]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---awakening of ecstatic love.
translation: Then the female parrot began to speak jokingly to śuka, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was struck with wonderful ecstatic love to hear her speak.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.216
description: The parrot śārī said, "When Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is with Rādhārāṇī, He is the enchanter of Cupid; otherwise, when He is alone, He Himself is enchanted by erotic feelings even though He enchants the whole universe."
text:
> rādhā-saṅge yadā bhāti
> tadā 'madana-mohanaḥ'
> anyathā viśva-moho 'pi
> svayaṁ 'madana-mohitaḥ'
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:y:yadā]]---when; [[synonyms:b:bhāti]]---shines; [[synonyms:t:tadā]]---at that time; [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mohanaḥ]]---the enchanter of the mind of Cupid; [[synonyms:a:anyathā]]---otherwise; [[synonyms:v:viśva]]-[[synonyms:m:mohaḥ]]---the enchanter of the whole universe; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even though; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---personally; [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mohitaḥ]]---enchanted by Cupid.
translation: The parrot śārī said, "When Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is with Rādhārāṇī, He is the enchanter of Cupid; otherwise, when He is alone, He Himself is enchanted by erotic feelings even though He enchants the whole universe."
purport: This is another verse from the //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (13.32).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.217
description: Both parrots then flew onto a tree branch, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to watch the dancing of peacocks with curiosity.
text:
> śuka-śārī uḍi' punaḥ gela vṛkṣa-ḍāle
> mayūrera nṛtya prabhu dekhe kutūhale
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śārī]]---the male and female parrots; [[synonyms:u:uḍi']]---flying; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:ḍ:ḍāle]]---to the branch of a tree; [[synonyms:m:mayūrera]]---of the peacocks; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:k:kutūhale]]---with curiosity.
translation: Both parrots then flew onto a tree branch, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to watch the dancing of peacocks with curiosity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.218
description: When the Lord saw the bluish necks of the peacocks, His remembrance of Kṛṣṇa immediately awakened, and He fell to the ground in ecstatic love.
text:
> mayūrera kaṇṭha dekhi' prabhura kṛṣṇa-smṛti haila
> premāveśe mahāprabhu bhūmite paḍila
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mayūrera]]---of the peacocks; [[synonyms:k:kaṇṭha]]---necks; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:smṛti]]---remembrance of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍila]]---fell down.
translation: When the Lord saw the bluish necks of the peacocks, His remembrance of Kṛṣṇa immediately awakened, and He fell to the ground in ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.219
description: When the brāhmaṇa saw that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was unconscious, he and Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya took care of Him.
text:
> prabhure mūrcchita dekhi' sei ta brāhmaṇa
> bhaṭṭācārya-saṅge kare prabhura santarpaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mūrcchita]]---unconscious; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:t:ta]] [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---indeed that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:santarpaṇa]]---taking care.
translation: When the brāhmaṇa saw that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was unconscious, he and Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya took care of Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.22
description: Because the Lord had departed, the devotees, unable to see Him early in the morning, began to search for Him with great anxiety.
text:
> prātaḥ-kāle bhakta-gaṇa prabhu nā dekhiyā
> anveṣaṇa kari' phire vyākula hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---early in the morning; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---not seeing; [[synonyms:a:anveṣaṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---searching; [[synonyms:p:phire]]---wander; [[synonyms:v:vyākula]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming very anxious.
translation: Because the Lord had departed, the devotees, unable to see Him early in the morning, began to search for Him with great anxiety.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.220
description: They hastily sprinkled water over the Lord's body. Then they took up His cloth and began to fan Him with it.
text:
> āste-vyaste mahāprabhura lañā bahirvāsa
> jala-seka kare aṅge, vastrera vātāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āste]]-[[synonyms:v:vyaste]]---with great haste; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:b:bahirvāsa]]---covering cloth; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:s:seka]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---sprinkle water; [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---on the body; [[synonyms:v:vastrera]] [[synonyms:v:vātāsa]]---fanning with the cloth.
translation: They hastily sprinkled water over the Lord's body. Then they took up His cloth and began to fan Him with it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.221
description: They then began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa into the Lord's ear. When the Lord regained consciousness, He began rolling on the ground.
text:
> prabhu-karṇe kṛṣṇa-nāma kahe ucca kari'
> cetana pāñā prabhu yā'na gaḍāgaḍi
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:k:karṇe]]---in the ear of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---chant; [[synonyms:u:ucca]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---loudly; [[synonyms:c:cetana]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---coming to consciousness; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yā'na]]---goes; [[synonyms:g:gaḍāgaḍi]]---rolling on the ground.
translation: They then began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa into the Lord's ear. When the Lord regained consciousness, He began rolling on the ground.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.222
description: When the Lord rolled on the ground, sharp thorns injured His body. Taking Him on his lap, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya pacified Him.
text:
> kaṇṭaka-durgama vane aṅga kṣata haila
> bhaṭṭācārya kole kari' prabhure sustha kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kaṇṭaka]]-[[synonyms:d:durgama]]---difficult to traverse because of thorns; [[synonyms:v:vane]]---in the forest; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the body; [[synonyms:k:kṣata]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became injured; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kole]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking Him on his lap; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sustha]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---pacified.
translation: When the Lord rolled on the ground, sharp thorns injured His body. Taking Him on his lap, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya pacified Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.223
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mind wandered in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa. He immediately stood up and said, "Chant! Chant!" Then He Himself began to dance.
text:
> kṛṣṇāveśe prabhura preme garagara mana
> 'bol' 'bol' kari' uṭhi' karena nartana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---by love; [[synonyms:g:garagara]]---disturbed; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:b:bol]] [[synonyms:b:bol]]---chant, chant; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---saying; [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---standing up; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---began to dance.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mind wandered in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa. He immediately stood up and said, "Chant! Chant!" Then He Himself began to dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.224
description: Being thus ordered by the Lord, both Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya and the brāhmaṇa began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Then the Lord, dancing and dancing, proceeded along the path.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya, sei vipra 'kṛṣṇa-nāma' gāya
> nācite nācite pathe prabhu cali' yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nācite]] [[synonyms:n:nācite]]---dancing and dancing; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the road; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cali']] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes forward.
translation: Being thus ordered by the Lord, both Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya and the brāhmaṇa began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Then the Lord, dancing and dancing, proceeded along the path.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.225
description: The brāhmaṇa was astounded to see the symptoms of ecstatic love exhibited by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He then became anxious to give the Lord protection.
text:
> prabhura premāveśa dekhi' brāhmaṇa---vismita
> prabhura rakṣā lāgi' vipra ha-ilā cintita
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---ecstatic love; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:v:vismita]]---astonished; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:rakṣā]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for the protection; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:c:cintita]]---very anxious.
translation: The brāhmaṇa was astounded to see the symptoms of ecstatic love exhibited by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He then became anxious to give the Lord protection.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.226
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mind was absorbed in ecstatic love at Jagannātha Purī, but when He passed along the road on the way to Vṛndāvana, that love increased a hundred times.
text:
> nīlācale chilā yaiche premāveśa mana
> vṛndāvana yāite pathe haila śata-guṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---at Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:c:chilā]]---was; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---always in a mentality of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---going; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the road; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:ś:śata]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---one hundred times.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mind was absorbed in ecstatic love at Jagannātha Purī, but when He passed along the road on the way to Vṛndāvana, that love increased a hundred times.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.227
description: The Lord's ecstatic love increased a thousand times when He visited Mathurā, but it increased a hundred thousand times when He wandered in the forests of Vṛndāvana.
text:
> sahasra-guṇa prema bāḍe mathurā daraśane
> lakṣa-guṇa prema bāḍe, bhramena yabe vane
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---one thousand times; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love; [[synonyms:b:bāḍe]]---increased; [[synonyms:m:mathurā]]---Mathurā; [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---upon seeing; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---a hundred thousand times; [[synonyms:p:prema]] [[synonyms:b:bāḍe]]---love increases; [[synonyms:b:bhramena]]---wanders; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:v:vane]]---in the forests of Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.31

text:

> 'kṛṣṇa kaha' bali' prabhu jala pheli' mārilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---bathed and was chanting the Gāyatrī //mantra// within the water; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:h:hastī]]---the elephants; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---chant Hare Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jala]] [[synonyms:p:pheli']]---throwing water; [[synonyms:m:mārilā]]---struck.
translation: While the Lord was bathing and murmuring the Gāyatrī mantra, the elephants came before Him. The Lord immediately splashed some water on the elephants and asked them to chant the name of Kṛṣṇa.
purport:
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was the Supreme personality of Godhead playing the part of a very great advanced devotee. On the //mahā-bhāgavata// platform, the devotee makes no distinction between friends and enemies. On that platform he sees everyone as a servant of Kṛṣṇa. As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā://

> vidyā-vinaya-sampanne
> brāhmaṇe gavi hastini
> śuni caiva śvapāke ca
> paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ

"The humble sage, by virtue of true knowledge, sees with equal vision a learned and gentle //brāhmaṇa,// a cow, an elephant, a dog, and a dog-eater [outcaste]." [[books:bg:5:18|(Bg. 5.18)]]

A //mahā-bhāgavata,// being learned and advanced in spiritual consciousness, sees no difference between a tiger, an elephant or a learned scholar. The test of advanced spiritual consciousness is that one becomes fearless. He envies no one, and he is always engaged in the Lord's service. He sees every living entity as an eternal part and parcel of the Lord, rendering service according to his capacity by the will of the Supreme Lord. As //Bhagavad-gītā// confirms:

> sarvasya cāhaṁ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo
> mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṁ ca

"I am seated in everyone's heart, and from Me come remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness." [[books:bg:15:15|(Bg. 15.15)]]

The //mahā-bhāgavata// knows that Kṛṣṇa is in everyone's heart. Kṛṣṇa is dictating, and the living entity is following His dictations. Kṛṣṇa is within the heart of the tiger, elephant and boar. Therefore Kṛṣṇa tells them, "Here is a //mahā-bhāgavata.// Please do not disturb him." Why, then, should the animals be envious of such a great personality? Those who are neophytes or even a little progressed in devotional service should not try to imitate the //mahā-bhāgavata.// Rather, they should only follow in their footsteps. The word //anukara// means "imitating," and //anusara// means "trying to follow in the footsteps." We should not try to imitate the activities of a //mahā-bhāgavata// or Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Our best efforts should be exerted in trying to follow them according to our ability. The //mahā-bhāgavata's// heart is completely freed from material contamination, and he can become very dear even to fierce animals like tigers and elephants. Indeed, the //mahā-bhāgavata// treats them as his very intimate friends. On this platform there is no question of envy. When the Lord was passing through the forest, He was in ecstasy, thinking the forest to be Vṛndāvana. He was simply searching for Kṛṣṇa.
