> keha bhūme paḍe, keha karaye citkāra
> dekhi' bhaṭṭācāryera mane haya camatkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:keha]]---some of them; [[synonyms:b:bhūme]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fall down; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---some of them; [[synonyms:k:karaye]]---perform; [[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:k:kāra]]---screaming; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there was; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonishment.
translation: Some of the elephants fell to the ground, and some screamed in ecstasy. Seeing this, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya was completely astonished.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.34
description: Sometimes Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu chanted very loudly while passing through the jungle. Hearing His sweet voice, all the does came near Him.
text:
> pathe yāite kare prabhu ucca saṅkīrtana
> madhura kaṇṭha-dhvani śuni' āise mṛgī-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pathe]] [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---while passing on the path; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:u:ucca]]---loud; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweet; [[synonyms:k:kaṇṭha]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---the voice from His throat; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---came; [[synonyms:m:mṛgī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---she-deer.
translation: Sometimes Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu chanted very loudly while passing through the jungle. Hearing His sweet voice, all the does came near Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.35
description: Hearing the Lord's great vibration, all the does followed Him left and right. While reciting a verse with great curiosity, the Lord patted them.
text:
> ḍāhine-vāme dhvani śuni' yāya prabhu-saṅge
> prabhu tāra aṅga muche, śloka paḍe raṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍāhine]]-[[synonyms:v:vāme]]---right and left; [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---vibration; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---they follow; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the Lord; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---their; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---bodies; [[synonyms:m:muche]]---pats; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verse; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---recites; [[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---in great curiosity.
translation: Hearing the Lord's great vibration, all the does followed Him left and right. While reciting a verse with great curiosity, the Lord patted them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.36
description: "Blessed are all these foolish deer because they have approached the son of Mahārāja Nanda, who is gorgeously dressed and is playing on His flute. Indeed, both the does and the bucks worship the Lord with looks of love and affection."
text:
> dhanyāḥ sma mūḍha-matayo 'pi hariṇya etā
> yā nanda-nandanam upātta-vicitra-veśam
> ākarṇya veṇu-raṇitaṁ saha-kṛṣṇa-sārāḥ
> pūjāṁ dadhur viracitāṁ praṇayāvalokaiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dhanyāḥ]]---fortunate, blessed; [[synonyms:s:sma]]---certainly; [[synonyms:m:mūḍha]]-[[synonyms:m:matayaḥ]]---foolish, without good sense; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:h:hariṇyaḥ]]---she-deer; [[synonyms:e:etāḥ]]---these; [[synonyms:y:yāḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:n:nanda]]-[[synonyms:n:nandanam]]---the son of Mahārāja Nanda; [[synonyms:u:upātta]]-[[synonyms:v:vicitra]]-[[synonyms:v:veśam]]---dressed very attractively; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṇya]]---hearing; [[synonyms:v:veṇu]]-[[synonyms:r:raṇitam]]---the sound of His flute; [[synonyms:s:saha]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sārāḥ]]---accompanied by the black deer (their husbands); [[synonyms:p:pūjām]] [[synonyms:d:dadhuḥ]]---they worshiped; [[synonyms:v:viracitām]]---performed; [[synonyms:p:praṇaya]]-[[synonyms:a:avalokaiḥ]]---by their affectionate glances.
translation: "Blessed are all these foolish deer because they have approached the son of Mahārāja Nanda, who is gorgeously dressed and is playing on His flute. Indeed, both the does and the bucks worship the Lord with looks of love and affection."
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.21.11) spoken by the //gopīs// of Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.37
description: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was passing through the jungle, five or seven tigers came. Joining the deer, the tigers began to follow the Lord.
text:
> hena-kāle vyāghra tathā āila pāṅca-sāta
> vyāghra-mṛgī mili' cale mahāprabhura sātha
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:v:vyāghra]]---tigers; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---there; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:p:pāṅca]]-[[synonyms:s:sāta]]---five to seven; [[synonyms:v:vyāghra]]-[[synonyms:m:mṛgī]]---the tigers and deer; [[synonyms:m:mili']]---coming together; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---go; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]] [[synonyms:s:sātha]]---with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was passing through the jungle, five or seven tigers came. Joining the deer, the tigers began to follow the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.38
description: Seeing the tigers and deer following Him, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately remembered the land of Vṛndāvana. He then began to recite a verse describing the transcendental quality of Vṛndāvana.
text:
> dekhi' mahāprabhura 'vṛndāvana'-smṛti haila
> vṛndāvana-guṇa-varṇana śloka paḍila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---of the holy land of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:s:smṛti]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was remembrance; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---of Śrī Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---of the qualities; [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---description; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verse; [[synonyms:p:paḍila]]---recited.
translation: Seeing the tigers and deer following Him, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately remembered the land of Vṛndāvana. He then began to recite a verse describing the transcendental quality of Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.39
description: "Vṛndāvana is the transcendental abode of the Lord. There is no hunger, anger or thirst there. Though naturally inimical, both human beings and fierce animals live together there in transcendental friendship."
text:
> yatra naisarga-durvairāḥ
> sahāsan nṛ-mṛgādayaḥ
> mitrāṇīvājitāvāsa-
> druta-ruṭ-tarṣaṇādikam
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---where; [[synonyms:n:naisarga]]---by nature; [[synonyms:d:durvairāḥ]]---living in enmity; [[synonyms:s:saha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsan]]---live together; [[synonyms:n:nṛ]]---human beings; [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādayaḥ]]---and animals; [[synonyms:m:mitrāṇi]]---friends; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:a:ajita]]---of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āvāsa]]---residence; [[synonyms:d:druta]]---gone away; [[synonyms:r:ruj]]---anger; [[synonyms:t:tarṣaṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādikam]]---thirst and so on.
translation: "Vṛndāvana is the transcendental abode of the Lord. There is no hunger, anger or thirst there. Though naturally inimical, both human beings and fierce animals live together there in transcendental friendship."
purport: This is a statement from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.13.60). After stealing the cowherd boys, calves and cows of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Lord Brahmā kept them asleep and hid them. After a moment, Brahmā returned to see Kṛṣṇa's condition. When he saw that Kṛṣṇa was still busy with His cowherd boyfriends and animals and was not disturbed, Lord Brahmā appreciated the transcendental opulence of Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.4
description: The Lord requested Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī to help Him go to Vṛndāvana.
text:
> "mora sahāya kara yadi, tumi-dui jana
> tabe āmi yāñā dekhi śrī-vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mora]]---of Me; [[synonyms:s:sahāya]]---help; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---you do; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:y:yāñā]]---going; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---shall see; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma.
translation: The Lord requested Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī to help Him go to Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.40
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Chant Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!" the tigers and deer began to dance and chant, "Kṛṣṇa!"
text:
> 'kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kaha' kari' prabhu yabe balila
> 'kṛṣṇa' kahi' vyāghra-mṛga nācite lāgila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---chant Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---in this way; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:b:balila]]---uttered; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vyāghra]]-[[synonyms:m:mṛga]]---the tigers and deer; [[synonyms:n:nācite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began to dance.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Chant Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!" the tigers and deer began to dance and chant, "Kṛṣṇa!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.41
description: When all the tigers and does danced and jumped, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya saw them and was struck with wonder.
text:
> nāce, kunde vyāghra-gaṇa mṛgī-gaṇa-saṅge
> balabhadra-bhaṭṭācārya dekhe apūrva-raṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:k:kunde]]---jump; [[synonyms:v:vyāghra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the tigers; [[synonyms:m:mṛgī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the does; [[synonyms:b:balabhadra]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:a:apūrva]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---with great wonder.
translation: When all the tigers and does danced and jumped, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya saw them and was struck with wonder.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.42
description: Indeed, the tigers and deer began to embrace one another, and, touching mouths, they began to kiss.
text:
> vyāghra-mṛga anyonye kare āliṅgana
> mukhe mukha diyā kare anyonye cumbana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyāghra]]-[[synonyms:m:mṛga]]---the tigers and deer; [[synonyms:a:anyonye]]---one another; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]] [[synonyms:m:mukha]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---touching one anothers' mouths; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:a:anyonye]] [[synonyms:c:cumbana]]---kissing one another.
translation: Indeed, the tigers and deer began to embrace one another, and, touching mouths, they began to kiss.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.43
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw all this fun, He began to smile. Finally He left the animals and continued on His way.
text:
> kautuka dekhiyā prabhu hāsite lāgilā
> tā-sabāke tāhāṅ chāḍi' āge cali' gelā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kautuka]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing this fun; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hāsite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to smile; [[synonyms:t:tā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāke]]---all of them; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---leaving there; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---forward; [[synonyms:c:cali']] [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---advanced.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw all this fun, He began to smile. Finally He left the animals and continued on His way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.44
description: Various birds, including the peacock, saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and began to follow Him, chanting and dancing. They were all maddened by the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> mayūrādi pakṣi-gaṇa prabhure dekhiyā
> saṅge cale, 'kṛṣṇa' bali' nāce matta hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mayūra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---beginning with peacocks; [[synonyms:p:pakṣi]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---different types of birds; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]] [[synonyms:c:cale]]---go with Him; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:m:matta]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming mad.
translation: Various birds, including the peacock, saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and began to follow Him, chanting and dancing. They were all maddened by the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.45
description: When the Lord loudly chanted "Hari bol!" the trees and creepers became jubilant to hear Him.
text:
> 'hari-bola' bali' prabhu kare ucca-dhvani
> vṛkṣa-latā---praphullita, sei dhvani śuni'
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:b:bola]]---the vibration of Hari-bol; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---chanting; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---makes; [[synonyms:u:ucca]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---a loud sound; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:l:latā]]---the trees and creepers; [[synonyms:p:praphullita]]---very jubilant; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---sound; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing.
translation: When the Lord loudly chanted "Hari bol!" the trees and creepers became jubilant to hear Him.
purport: The loud chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// is so powerful that it can even penetrate the ears of trees and creepers-what to speak of animals and human beings. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu once asked Haridāsa Ṭhākura how trees and plants could be delivered, and Haridāsa Ṭhākura replied that the loud chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// would benefit not only trees and plants but insects and all other living beings. One should therefore not be disturbed by the loud chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa, for it is beneficial not only to the chanter but to everyone who gets an opportunity to hear.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.46
description: Thus all living entities-some moving and some standing still in the forest of Jhārikhaṇḍa-became maddened by hearing the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa vibrated by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> 'jhārikhaṇḍe' sthāvara-jaṅgama āche yata
> kṛṣṇa-nāma diyā kaila premete unmatta
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jhārikhaṇḍe]]---in the place known as Jhārikhaṇḍa; [[synonyms:s:sthāvara]]-[[synonyms:j:jaṅgama]]---moving and not moving; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there are; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving them the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:p:premete]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:u:unmatta]]---mad.
translation: Thus all living entities-some moving and some standing still in the forest of Jhārikhaṇḍa-became maddened by hearing the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa vibrated by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
purport: The great forest of Jhārikhaṇḍa is a great tract of land including Āṭagaḍa, Ḍheṅkānala, Āṅgula, Lāhārā, Kiyañjhaḍa, Bāmaḍā, Bonāi, Gāṅgapura, Choṭa Nāgapura, Yaśapura and Saragujā. All these places, which are covered with mountains and jungles, are known as Jhārikhaṇḍa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.47
description: In all the villages through which the Lord passed and in all the places He rested on His journey, everyone was purified and awakened to ecstatic love of God.
text:
> yei grāma diyā yāna, yāhāṅ karena sthiti
> se-saba grāmera lokera haya 'prema-bhakti'
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:g:grāma]]---which villages; [[synonyms:d:diyā]] [[synonyms:y:yāna]]---the Lord goes through; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---takes; [[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---rest; [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all those; [[synonyms:g:grāmera]]---of the villages; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of the people; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is awakening of; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---ecstatic love of God.
translation: In all the villages through which the Lord passed and in all the places He rested on His journey, everyone was purified and awakened to ecstatic love of God.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.48-49
description: When someone heard the chanting of the holy name from the mouth of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and someone else heard this chanting from that second person, and someone again heard this chanting from the third person, everyone in all countries became a Vaiṣṇava through such disciplic succession. Thus everyone chanted the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and Hari, and they danced, cried and smiled.
text:
> keha yadi tāṅra mukhe śune kṛṣṇa-nāma
> tāṅra mukhe āna śune tāṅra mukhe āna
>
> sabe 'kṛṣṇa' 'hari' bali' nāce, kānde, hāse
> paramparāya 'vaiṣṇava' ha-ila sarva deśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---when; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---from His mouth; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hears; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra//; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---from the mouth of such chanters; [[synonyms:ā:āna]] [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---someone else hears; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---and from his mouth; [[synonyms:ā:āna]]---someone else; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa's holy name; [[synonyms:h:hari]]---another holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---chanting; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:k:kānde]]---cry; [[synonyms:h:hāse]]---smile; [[synonyms:p:paramparāya]]---by disciplic succession; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotees; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in all countries.
translation: When someone heard the chanting of the holy name from the mouth of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and someone else heard this chanting from that second person, and someone again heard this chanting from the third person, everyone in all countries became a Vaiṣṇava through such disciplic succession. Thus everyone chanted the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and Hari, and they danced, cried and smiled.
purport: The transcendental power or potency of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// is herein explained. First, the holy name is vibrated by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. When someone hears from Him directly, he is purified. When another person hears from that person, he also is purified. In this way the purification process is advanced among pure devotees. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and no one can claim His potency. Nonetheless, if one is a pure devotee, hundreds and thousands of men can be purified by his vibration. This potency is within every living being, provided he chants the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// offenselessly and without material motives. When a pure devotee chants offenselessly, another person will become a Vaiṣṇava, and from him another Vaiṣṇava will emerge. This is the //paramparā// system.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.5
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I shall leave early in the morning and go incognito, taking the road to the forest. I shall go alone and not take anyone with Me.
text:
> rātrye uṭhi' vana-pathe palāñā yāba
> ekākī yāiba, kāhoṅ saṅge nā la-iba
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rātrye]] [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---rising at night; [[synonyms:v:vana]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the road to the forest; [[synonyms:p:palāñā]] [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---I shall go away secretly; [[synonyms:e:ekākī]] [[synonyms:y:yāiba]]---I shall go alone; [[synonyms:k:kāhoṅ]]---anyone; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Me; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iba]]---I shall not take.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I shall leave early in the morning and go incognito, taking the road to the forest. I shall go alone and not take anyone with Me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.50
description: The Lord did not always manifest His ecstasy. Being afraid of a great assembly of people, the Lord kept His ecstasy concealed.
text:
> yadyapi prabhu loka-saṅghaṭṭera trāse
> prema 'gupta' karena, bāhire nā prakāśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅghaṭṭera]]---of crowds of people; [[synonyms:t:trāse]]---being afraid; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---ecstasy; [[synonyms:g:gupta]] [[synonyms:k:karena]]---keeps hidden; [[synonyms:b:bāhire]]---externally; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---manifest.
translation: The Lord did not always manifest His ecstasy. Being afraid of a great assembly of people, the Lord kept His ecstasy concealed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.51
description: Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not manifest His natural ecstatic love, everyone became a pure devotee simply by seeing and hearing Him.
text:
> tathāpi tāṅra darśana-śravaṇa-prabhāve
> sakala deśera loka ha-ila 'vaiṣṇave'
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---of seeing; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]---of hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhāve]]---by the potency; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:d:deśera]]---of countries; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇave]]---pure devotees of the Lord.
translation: Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not manifest His natural ecstatic love, everyone became a pure devotee simply by seeing and hearing Him.
purport: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī has described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as //mahā-vadānya-avatāra,// the most munificent incarnation. Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is not physically present now, simply by chanting His holy name (//śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya prabhu nityānanda śrī-advaita gadādhara śrīvāsādi-gaura-bhakta-vṛnda//) people throughout the world are becoming devotees. This is due to the ecstatic chanting of the holy name of the Lord. It is said that a pure devotee can see the Lord every moment, and because of this he is empowered by the Lord. This is confirmed in the //Brahma-saṁhitā:premāñjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena santaḥ sadaiva hṛdayeṣu vilokayanti.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu appeared five hundred years ago, but it cannot be said that now the potency of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// is less powerful than it was in His presence. By hearing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu through the //paramparā// system, one can be purified. Therefore in this verse it is said: //tathāpi tāṅra darśana-śravaṇa-prabhāve.// It is not that everyone is able to see Kṛṣṇa or Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu physically, but if one hears about Him through books like //Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta// and through the //paramparā// system of pure Vaiṣṇavas, there is no difficulty in becoming a pure Vaiṣṇava, free from mundane desires and personal motivations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.52
description: In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally toured Bengal, East Bengal, Orissa and the southern countries, and He delivered all kinds of people by spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness.
text:
> gauḍa, baṅga, utkala, dakṣiṇa-deśe giyā
> lokera nistāra kaila āpane bhramiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]---Bengal; [[synonyms:b:baṅga]]---East Bengal; [[synonyms:u:utkala]]---Orissa; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---southern India; [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---going; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of all the people; [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---liberation; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:b:bhramiyā]]---touring.
translation: In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally toured Bengal, East Bengal, Orissa and the southern countries, and He delivered all kinds of people by spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.53
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to Jhārikhaṇḍa on His way to Mathurā, He found that the people there were almost uncivilized and were devoid of God consciousness.
text:
> mathurā yāibāra chale āsena jhārikhaṇḍa
> bhilla-prāya loka tāhāṅ parama-pāṣaṇḍa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mathurā]]---to Mathurā; [[synonyms:y:yāibāra]]---of going; [[synonyms:c:chale]]---on the pretext; [[synonyms:ā:āsena]]---came; [[synonyms:j:jhārikhaṇḍa]]---to Jhārikhaṇḍa; [[synonyms:b:bhilla]]-[[synonyms:p:prāya]]---like the Bheels, a kind of low people; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:p:pāṣaṇḍa]]---without God consciousness.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to Jhārikhaṇḍa on His way to Mathurā, He found that the people there were almost uncivilized and were devoid of God consciousness.
purport: The word //bhilla// refers to a class of men belonging to the Bheels. The Bheels are like Black Africans, and they are lower than //śūdras.// Such people generally live in the jungle, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had to meet them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.54
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu gave even the Bheels an opportunity to chant the holy name and come to the platform of ecstatic love. Thus He delivered all of them. Who has the power to understand the transcendental pastimes of the Lord?
text:
> nāma-prema diyā kaila sabāra nistāra
> caitanyera gūḍha-līlā bujhite śakti kāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---bestowing upon them ecstatic love and the holy name; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]] [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---liberation of all of them; [[synonyms:c:caitanyera]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gūḍha]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---confidential pastimes; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---the power; [[synonyms:k:kāra]]---who has.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu gave even the Bheels an opportunity to chant the holy name and come to the platform of ecstatic love. Thus He delivered all of them. Who has the power to understand the transcendental pastimes of the Lord?
purport: As evidence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mercy, we are experiencing that the people of Africa are taking to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, chanting and dancing and taking //prasāda// like other Vaiṣṇavas. This is all due to the power of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Who can understand how His potency is working all over the world?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.55
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed through the Jhārikhaṇḍa forest, He took it for granted that it was Vṛndāvana. When He passed over the hills, He took it for granted that they were Govardhana.
text:
> vana dekhi' bhrama haya---ei 'vṛndāvana'
> śaila dekhi' mane haya---ei 'govardhana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vana]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the forest; [[synonyms:b:bhrama]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is illusion; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana forest; [[synonyms:ś:śaila]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing a hill; [[synonyms:m:mane]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---considers; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]---this is Govardhana Hill.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed through the Jhārikhaṇḍa forest, He took it for granted that it was Vṛndāvana. When He passed over the hills, He took it for granted that they were Govardhana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.56
description: Similarly, whenever Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw a river, He immediately accepted it as the River Yamunā. Thus while in the forest He was filled with great ecstatic love, and He danced and fell down crying.
text:
> yāhāṅ nadī dekhe tāhāṅ mānaye---'kālindī'
> mahā-premāveśe nāce prabhu paḍe kāndi'
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:n:nadī]]---river; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:m:mānaye]]---considers; [[synonyms:k:kālindī]]---the River Yamunā; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in great ecstatic love; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---falls down; [[synonyms:k:kāndi']]---crying.
translation: Similarly, whenever Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw a river, He immediately accepted it as the River Yamunā. Thus while in the forest He was filled with great ecstatic love, and He danced and fell down crying.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.57
description: Along the way, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya collected all kinds of spinach, roots and fruit whenever possible.
text:
> pathe yāite bhaṭṭācārya śāka-mūla-phala
> yāhāṅ yei pāyena tāhāṅ layena sakala
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pathe]] [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---while passing on the way; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ś:śāka]]---spinach; [[synonyms:m:mūla]]---roots; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---fruits; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:p:pāyena]]---he gets; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:l:layena]]---he takes; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all.
translation: Along the way, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya collected all kinds of spinach, roots and fruit whenever possible.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.58
description: Whenever Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited a village, a few brāhmaṇas-five or seven-would come and extend invitations to the Lord.
text:
> ye-grāme rahena prabhu, tathāya brāhmaṇa
> pāṅca-sāta jana āsi' kare nimantraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in whatever village; [[synonyms:r:rahena]]---stays; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tathāya]]---there; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---//brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:p:pāṅca]]-[[synonyms:s:sāta]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---five or seven persons; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation.
translation: Whenever Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited a village, a few brāhmaṇas-five or seven-would come and extend invitations to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.59
description: Some people would bring grains and deliver them to Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya. Others would bring milk and yogurt, and still others would bring ghee and sugar.
text:
> keha anna āni' deya bhaṭṭācārya-sthāne
> keha dugdha, dadhi, keha ghṛta, khaṇḍa āne
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---grains; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:d:deya]]---delivers; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---before Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]---milk; [[synonyms:d:dadhi]]---yogurt; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:g:ghṛta]]---ghee; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]]---sugar; [[synonyms:ā:āne]]---brings.
translation: Some people would bring grains and deliver them to Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya. Others would bring milk and yogurt, and still others would bring ghee and sugar.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.6
description: "If someone wants to follow Me, please stop him. I don't want anyone to go with Me.
text:
> keha yadi saṅga la-ite pāche uṭhi' dhāya
> sabāre rākhibā, yena keha nāhi yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:s:saṅga]] [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---to take company; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---behind; [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---getting up; [[synonyms:d:dhāya]]---runs; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---everyone; [[synonyms:r:rākhibā]]---please stop; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---so that; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---does not go.
translation: "If someone wants to follow Me, please stop him. I don't want anyone to go with Me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.60
description: In some villages there were no brāhmaṇas; nonetheless, devotees born in non-brāhmaṇa families came and extended invitations to Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya.
text:
> yāhāṅ vipra nāhi tāhāṅ 'śūdra-mahājana'
> āsi' sabe bhaṭṭācārye kare nimantraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---//brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:ś:śūdra]]-[[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---devotees born in families other than //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārye]]---to Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---make invitation.
translation: In some villages there were no brāhmaṇas; nonetheless, devotees born in non-brāhmaṇa families came and extended invitations to Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya.
purport: Actually a //sannyāsī// or a //brāhmaṇa// will not accept an invitation extended by a person born in a lower family. However, there are many devotees who are raised to the platform of //brāhmaṇa// by their initiation. These people are called //śūdra-mahājana.// This indicates that one who is born in a non-//brāhmaṇa// family has accepted the //brāhmaṇa// status by initiation. Such devotees extended invitations to Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya. A Māyāvādī //sannyāsī// will accept an invitation only from a //brāhmaṇa// family, but a Vaiṣṇava does not accept an invitation from a //brāhmaṇa// if he does not belong to the Vaiṣṇava sect. However, a Vaiṣṇava will accept an invitation from a //brāhmaṇa// or //śūdra-mahājana// if that person is an initiated Vaiṣṇava. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself accepted invitations from //śūdra-mahājanas,// and this confirms the fact that anyone initiated by a Vaiṣṇava //mantra// can be accepted as a //brāhmaṇa.// One can accept an invitation from such a person.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.61
description: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya used to cook all kinds of vegetables gathered from the forest, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to accept these preparations.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya pāka kare vanya-vyañjana
> vanya-vyañjane prabhura ānandita mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:pāka]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---cooks; [[synonyms:v:vanya]]-[[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---all varieties of forest vegetables; [[synonyms:v:vanya]]-[[synonyms:v:vyañjane]]---by such forest vegetables; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind is very happy.
translation: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya used to cook all kinds of vegetables gathered from the forest, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to accept these preparations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.62-63
description: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya used to keep a stock of food grains that would last from two to four days. Where there were no people, he would cook the grains and prepare vegetables, spinach, roots and fruits collected from the forest.
text:
> dui-cāri dinera anna rākhena saṁhati
> yāhāṅ śūnya vana, lokera nāhika vasati
>
> tāhāṅ sei anna bhaṭṭācārya kare pāka
> phala-mūle vyañjana kare, vanya nānā śāka
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:c:cāri]]---two to four; [[synonyms:d:dinera]]---of days; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food grains; [[synonyms:r:rākhena]]---keeps; [[synonyms:s:saṁhati]]---in stock; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:ś:śūnya]] [[synonyms:v:vana]]---the solitary forest; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of people; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:v:vasati]]---habitation; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food grains; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:p:pāka]]---cooks; [[synonyms:p:phala]]-[[synonyms:m:mūle]]---with roots and fruits; [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---he prepares vegetables; [[synonyms:v:vanya]]---from the forest; [[synonyms:n:nānā]] [[synonyms:ś:śāka]]---many kinds of spinach.
translation: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya used to keep a stock of food grains that would last from two to four days. Where there were no people, he would cook the grains and prepare vegetables, spinach, roots and fruits collected from the forest.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.64
description: The Lord was always very happy to eat these forest vegetables, and He was even happier when He had an opportunity to stay in a solitary place.
text:
> parama santoṣa prabhura vanya-bhojane
> mahā-sukha pāna, ye dina rahena nirjane
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:parama]]---very much; [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---satisfaction; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:v:vanya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhojane]]---in eating vegetables collected from the forest; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]] [[synonyms:p:pāna]]---gets great happiness; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---on which day; [[synonyms:r:rahena]]---stays; [[synonyms:n:nirjane]]---in a solitary place.
translation: The Lord was always very happy to eat these forest vegetables, and He was even happier when He had an opportunity to stay in a solitary place.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.65
description: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya was so affectionate to the Lord that he was rendering service just like a menial servant. His assistant brāhmaṇa carried the waterpot and garments.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya sevā kare, snehe yaiche 'dāsa'
> tāṅra vipra vahe jala-pātra-bahirvāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:s:sevā]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---renders service; [[synonyms:s:snehe]]---in great affection; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---exactly like; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---a servant; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---his //brāhmaṇa// assistant; [[synonyms:v:vahe]]---carries; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---the waterpot; [[synonyms:b:bahirvāsa]]---and garments.
translation: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya was so affectionate to the Lord that he was rendering service just like a menial servant. His assistant brāhmaṇa carried the waterpot and garments.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.66
description: The Lord used to bathe three times a day in the warm water of the waterfalls. He also used to heat Himself morning and evening with a fire made of the limitless wood.
text:
> nirjharete uṣṇodake snāna tina-bāra
> dui-sandhyā agni-tāpa kāṣṭhera apāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirjharete]]---in the waterfalls; [[synonyms:u:uṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:u:udake]]---in warm water; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bath; [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---thrice; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:s:sandhyā]]---morning and evening; [[synonyms:a:agni]]-[[synonyms:t:tāpa]]---heating by a fire; [[synonyms:k:kāṣṭhera]]---of wood; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---without limit.
translation: The Lord used to bathe three times a day in the warm water of the waterfalls. He also used to heat Himself morning and evening with a fire made of the limitless wood.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.67
description: While traveling in this secluded forest and feeling very happy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu made the following statement.
text:
> nirantara premāveśe nirjane gamana
> sukha anubhavi' prabhu kahena vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---always; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:n:nirjane]]---in a solitary place; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going; [[synonyms:s:sukha]] [[synonyms:a:anubhavi']]---feeling happiness; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---says; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---statement.
translation: While traveling in this secluded forest and feeling very happy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu made the following statement.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.68
description: "My dear Bhaṭṭācārya, I have traveled very far through the forest, and I have not even slightly received any trouble.
text:
> śuna, bhaṭṭācārya,---"āmi gelāṅa bahu-deśa
> vana-pathe duḥkhera kāhāṅ nāhi pāi leśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---My dear Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:g:gelāṅa]]---traveled; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:d:deśa]]---many countries; [[synonyms:v:vana]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---through the forest path; [[synonyms:d:duḥkhera]]---of unhappiness; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---anywhere; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:p:pāi]]---I do not get; [[synonyms:l:leśa]]---even a trace.
translation: "My dear Bhaṭṭācārya, I have traveled very far through the forest, and I have not even slightly received any trouble.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.69
description: "Kṛṣṇa is very merciful, especially to Me. He has shown His mercy by bringing Me on this path through the forest. Thus He has given Me great pleasure.
text:
> kṛṣṇa---kṛpālu, āmāya bahuta kṛpā kailā
> vana-pathe āni' āmāya baḍa sukha dilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛpālu]]---very kind; [[synonyms:ā:āmāya]]---upon Me; [[synonyms:b:bahuta]]---greatly; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---showed; [[synonyms:v:vana]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the path in the forest; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:ā:āmāya]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very much; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa is very merciful, especially to Me. He has shown His mercy by bringing Me on this path through the forest. Thus He has given Me great pleasure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.7
description: "Please give Me your permission with great pleasure and do not be unhappy. If you are happy, I shall be happy on My way to Vṛndāvana."
text:
> prasanna hañā ājñā dibā, nā mānibā 'duḥkha'
> tomā-sabāra 'sukhe' pathe habe mora 'sukha' "
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prasanna]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being pleased; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:dibā]]---give permission; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---do not; [[synonyms:m:mānibā]] [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---become unhappy; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of you; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---by the happiness; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the road; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness.
translation: "Please give Me your permission with great pleasure and do not be unhappy. If you are happy, I shall be happy on My way to Vṛndāvana."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.70
description: "Before this, I decided to go to Vṛndāvana and on the way see My mother, the River Ganges and other devotees once again.
text:
> pūrve vṛndāvana yāite karilāṅa vicāra
> mātā, gaṅgā, bhakta-gaṇe dekhiba eka-bāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---formerly; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---to the holy place of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go; [[synonyms:k:karilāṅa]]---I did; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---consideration; [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---mother; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]---the Ganges; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---and devotees; [[synonyms:d:dekhiba]]---I shall see; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---once.
translation: "Before this, I decided to go to Vṛndāvana and on the way see My mother, the River Ganges and other devotees once again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.71
description: "I thought that once again I would see and meet all the devotees and take them with Me to Vṛndāvana.
text:
> bhakta-gaṇa-saṅge avaśya kariba milana
> bhakta-gaṇe saṅge lañā yāba 'vṛndāvana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with all My devotees; [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---shall do; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---along with Me; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---I shall go; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---to Vṛndāvana-dhāma.
translation: "I thought that once again I would see and meet all the devotees and take them with Me to Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.72
description: "Thus I went to Bengal, and I was very happy to see My mother, the River Ganges and the devotees.
text:
> eta bhāvi' gauḍa-deśe kariluṅ gamana
> mātā, gaṅgā bhakte dekhi' sukhī haila mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bhāvi']]---thinking like this; [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---to Bengal; [[synonyms:k:kariluṅ]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---I went; [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---My mother; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]---the Ganges; [[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---devotees; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:sukhī]]---happy; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---My mind.
translation: "Thus I went to Bengal, and I was very happy to see My mother, the River Ganges and the devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.73
description: "However, when I started for Vṛndāvana, many thousands and millions of people gathered and began to go with Me.
text:
> bhakta-gaṇe lañā tabe calilāṅa raṅge
> lakṣa-koṭi loka tāhāṅ haila āmā-saṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:c:calilāṅa]] [[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---I started with great pleasure; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---many thousands and millions; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---My companions.
translation: "However, when I started for Vṛndāvana, many thousands and millions of people gathered and began to go with Me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.74
description: "Thus I was going to Vṛndāvana with a big crowd, but through the mouth of Sanātana, Kṛṣṇa taught Me a lesson. Thus by making some impediment, He has brought Me on a path through the forest to Vṛndāvana.
text:
> sanātana-mukhe kṛṣṇa āmā śikhāilā
> tāhā vighna kari' vana-pathe lañā āilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---from the mouth of Sanātana; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:ś:śikhāilā]]---gave instructions; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vighna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making a hindrance; [[synonyms:v:vana]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the path through the forest; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came.
translation: "Thus I was going to Vṛndāvana with a big crowd, but through the mouth of Sanātana, Kṛṣṇa taught Me a lesson. Thus by making some impediment, He has brought Me on a path through the forest to Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.75
description: "Kṛṣṇa is an ocean of mercy. He is especially merciful to the poor and fallen. Without His mercy, there is no possibility of happiness."
text:
> kṛpāra samudra, dīna-hīne dayāmaya
> kṛṣṇa-kṛpā vinā kona 'sukha' nāhi haya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛpāra]] [[synonyms:s:samudra]]---ocean of mercy; [[synonyms:d:dīna]]-[[synonyms:h:hīne]]---unto the poor and fallen; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---very merciful; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---the mercy of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---any; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is not.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa is an ocean of mercy. He is especially merciful to the poor and fallen. Without His mercy, there is no possibility of happiness."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.76
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then embraced Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya and told him, "It is only by your kindness that I am now so happy."
text:
> bhaṭṭācārye āliṅgiyā tāṅhāre kahila
> 'tomāra prasāde āmi eta sukha pāila'
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārye]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgiyā]]---embracing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---said; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:p:prasāde]]---by your kindness; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:e:eta]]---so much; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then embraced Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya and told him, "It is only by your kindness that I am now so happy."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.77
description: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "My dear Lord, You are Kṛṣṇa Himself, and therefore You are merciful. I am a fallen living entity, but You have bestowed a great favor upon me.
text:
> teṅho kahena,---"tumi 'kṛṣṇa', tumi 'dayāmaya'
> adhama jīva muñi, more ha-ilā sadaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:teṅho]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---You are Kṛṣṇa Himself; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---merciful; [[synonyms:a:adhama]]---the lowest of the low; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---living entity; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto me; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---You have been; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:d:daya]]---favorable.
translation: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "My dear Lord, You are Kṛṣṇa Himself, and therefore You are merciful. I am a fallen living entity, but You have bestowed a great favor upon me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.78
description: "Sir, I am most fallen, yet You have brought me with You. Showing great mercy, You have accepted food prepared by me.
text:
> muñi chāra, more tumi saṅge lañā āilā
> kṛpā kari' mora hāte 'prabhu' bhikṣā kailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:c:chāra]]---most fallen; [[synonyms:m:more]]---me; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---have come; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing great mercy; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:h:hāte]]---from my hand; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---my Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---You accepted food.
translation: "Sir, I am most fallen, yet You have brought me with You. Showing great mercy, You have accepted food prepared by me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.79
description: "You have made me Your carrier Garuḍa, although I am no better than a condemned crow. Thus You are the independent Personality of Godhead, the original Lord.
text:
> adhama-kākere kailā garuḍa-samāna
> 'svatantra īśvara' tumi---svayaṁ bhagavān"
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:adhama]]-[[synonyms:k:kākere]]---the most condemned crow; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---You have made; [[synonyms:g:garuḍa]]-[[synonyms:s:samāna]]---like Garuḍa; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]]---independent; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:s:svayam]] [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the original Personality of Godhead.
translation: "You have made me Your carrier Garuḍa, although I am no better than a condemned crow. Thus You are the independent Personality of Godhead, the original Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.8
description: Upon hearing this, Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī replied, "Dear Lord, You are completely independent. Since You are not dependent on anyone, You do whatever You desire.
text:
> dui-jana kahe,---'tumi īśvara 'svatantra'
> yei icchā, sei karibā, naha 'paratantra'
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the two persons replied; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]]---completely independent; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---whatever You desire; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:k:karibā]]---You will do; [[synonyms:n:naha]]---You are not; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:t:tantra]]---dependent on anyone.
translation: Upon hearing this, Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī replied, "Dear Lord, You are completely independent. Since You are not dependent on anyone, You do whatever You desire.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.80
description: " 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead has the form of sac-cid-ānanda vigraha, transcendental bliss, knowledge and eternity. I offer my respectful obeisances unto He who turns the dumb into eloquent speakers and enables the lame to cross mountains. Such is the mercy of the Lord.' "
text:
> mūkaṁ karoti vācālaṁ
> paṅguṁ laṅghayate girim
> yat-kṛpā tam ahaṁ vande
> paramānanda-mādhavam
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mūkam]]---a person who cannot speak; [[synonyms:k:karoti]]---makes; [[synonyms:v:vācālam]]---an eloquent speaker; [[synonyms:p:paṅgum]]---a person who cannot even walk; [[synonyms:l:laṅghayate]]---causes to cross over; [[synonyms:g:girim]]---the mountain; [[synonyms:y:yat]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---whose mercy; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:v:vande]]---offer obeisances; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---the transcendentally blissful; [[synonyms:m:mādhavam]]---Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead has the form of sac-cid-ānanda vigraha, transcendental bliss, knowledge and eternity. I offer my respectful obeisances unto He who turns the dumb into eloquent speakers and enables the lame to cross mountains. Such is the mercy of the Lord.' "
purport: This is a quotation from the //Bhāvārtha-dīpikā// commentary on //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:1:1|(1.1.1)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.81
description: In this way Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya offered his prayers to the Lord. By rendering service unto Him in ecstatic love, He pacified the Lord's mind.
text:
> ei-mata balabhadra karena stavana
> prema-sevā kari' tuṣṭa kaila prabhura mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:b:balabhadra]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---offers; [[synonyms:s:stavana]]---prayers; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---rendering service in love; [[synonyms:t:tuṣṭa]]---pacified; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: In this way Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya offered his prayers to the Lord. By rendering service unto Him in ecstatic love, He pacified the Lord's mind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.82
description: Finally the Lord with great happiness arrived at the holy place called Kāśī. There He took His bath in the bathing ghat known as Maṇikarṇikā.
text:
> ei-mata nānā-sukhe prabhu āilā 'kāśī'
> madhyāhna-snāna kaila maṇikarṇikāya āsi'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in great happiness; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:k:kāśī]]---to the holy place named Kāśī; [[synonyms:m:madhyāhna]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---afternoon bath; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---took; [[synonyms:m:maṇikarṇikāya]]---to the bathing place known as Maṇikarṇikā; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming.
translation: Finally the Lord with great happiness arrived at the holy place called Kāśī. There He took His bath in the bathing ghat known as Maṇikarṇikā.
purport: Kāśī is another name for Vārāṇasī (Benares). It has been a place of pilgrimage since time immemorial. Two rivers named Asiḥ and Varuṇā merge there. Maṇikarṇikā is famous because, according to the opinion of great personalities, a bejeweled earring fell there from the ear of Lord Viṣṇu. According to some, it fell from the ear of Lord Śiva. The word //maṇi// means "jewel," and //karṇika// means "from the ear." According to some, Lord Viśvanātha is the great physician who cures the disease of material existence by delivering a person through the ear, which receives the vibration of the holy name of Lord Rāma. Because of this, this holy place is called Maṇi-karṇikā. It is said that there is no better place than where the River Ganges flows, and the bathing ghat known as Maṇikarṇikā is especially sanctified because it is very dear to Lord Viśvanātha. In the //Kāśī-khaṇḍa// it is said: //saṁsāri-cintāmaṇir atra yasmāt tārakaṁ sajjana-karṇikāyām. śivo 'bhidhatte saha-sānta-kāle tad gīyate 'sau maṇi-karṇiketi. mukti-lakṣmī mahā-pīṭha-maṇis tac caraṇābjayoḥ. karṇikeyaṁ tataḥ prāhur yāṁ janā maṇi-karṇikām.// According to the //Kāśī-khaṇḍa,// if one gives up his body at Maṇikarṇikā, he is liberated simply by remembering Lord Śiva's name.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.83
description: At that time, Tapana Miśra was taking his bath in the Ganges, and he was astonished to see the Lord there.
text:
> sei-kāle tapana-miśra kare gaṅgā-snāna
> prabhu dekhi' haila tāṅra kichu vismaya jñāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time; [[synonyms:t:tapana]]-[[synonyms:m:miśra]]---a //brāhmaṇa// named Tapana Miśra; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---was taking his bath in the Ganges; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the Lord; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:v:vismaya]] [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---astonishment.
translation: At that time, Tapana Miśra was taking his bath in the Ganges, and he was astonished to see the Lord there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.84
description: Tapana Miśra then began to think, "I have heard that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has accepted the renounced order." Thinking this, Tapana Miśra became very jubilant within his heart.
text:
> 'pūrve śuniyāchi prabhu karyāchena sannyāsa'
> niścaya kariyā haila hṛdaye ullāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---formerly; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyāchi]]---I have heard; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karyāchena]] [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---has accepted the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---ascertaining that; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---within the heart; [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---great jubilation.
translation: Tapana Miśra then began to think, "I have heard that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has accepted the renounced order." Thinking this, Tapana Miśra became very jubilant within his heart.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.85
description: He then clasped the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and began to cry. The Lord raised him up and embraced him.
text:
> prabhura caraṇa dhari' karena rodana
> prabhu tāre uṭhāñā kaila āliṅgana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---lotus feet; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---touching; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:r:rodana]]---crying; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---him; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāñā]]---raising; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing.
translation: He then clasped the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and began to cry. The Lord raised him up and embraced him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.86
description: Tapana Miśra then took Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to visit the temple of Viśveśvara. Coming from there, they saw the lotus feet of Lord Bindu Mādhava.
text:
> prabhu lañā gelā viśveśvara-daraśane
> tabe āsi' dekhe bindu-mādhava-caraṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking the Lord; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---he went; [[synonyms:v:viśveśvara]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---to visit the temple of Viśveśvara; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---see; [[synonyms:b:bindu]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhava]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---the lotus feet of Bindu Mādhava.
translation: Tapana Miśra then took Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to visit the temple of Viśveśvara. Coming from there, they saw the lotus feet of Lord Bindu Mādhava.
purport:
This Bindu Mādhava is the oldest Viṣṇu temple in Vārāṇasī. Presently this temple is known as Veṇī Mādhava, and it is situated on the banks of the Ganges. Formerly five rivers converged there, and they were named Dhūtapāpā, Kiraṇā, Sarasvatī, Gaṅgā and Yamunā. Now only the River Ganges is visible. The old temple of Bindu Mādhava, which was visited by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, was later dismantled by Aurangzeb, the great Hindu-hating emperor of the Mogul dynasty. In the place of this temple, he constructed a big //majīda,// or mosque. Later, another temple was constructed by the side of the mosque, and this temple is still existing. In the temple of Bindu Mādhava there are Deities of four-handed Nārāyaṇa and the goddess Lakṣmī. In front of these Deities is a column of Śrī Garuḍa, and along the side are deities of Lord Rāma, Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa and Śrī Hanumānjī.

In the province of Mahārāṣṭra is a state known as Sātārā. During the time of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, the native prince belonged to the Vaiṣṇava cult. Being a //brāhmaṇa,// he took charge of worshiping the Deity. He was known as Śrīmanta Bālāsāheba Pantha Mahārāja. The state still bears the expenditure for temple maintenance. The first king in this dynasty to take charge of worship in the temple, two hundred years ago, was Mahārāja Jagatjīvana Rāo Sāheba.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.87
description: With great pleasure Tapana Miśra brought Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to his home and rendered service unto Him. Indeed, he began to dance, waving his cloth.
text:
> ghare lañā āilā prabhuke ānandita hañā
> sevā kari' nṛtya kare vastra uḍāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:ghare]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking to his home; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---in great happiness; [[synonyms:s:sevā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---rendering service; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---began to dance; [[synonyms:v:vastra]] [[synonyms:u:uḍāñā]]---waving his cloth.
translation: With great pleasure Tapana Miśra brought Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to his home and rendered service unto Him. Indeed, he began to dance, waving his cloth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.88
description: He washed the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and afterwards he and his whole family drank the wash water. He also worshiped Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya and showed him respect.
text:
> prabhura caraṇodaka savaṁśe kaila pāna
> bhaṭṭācāryera pūjā kaila kariyā sammāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:u:udaka]]---the water used to wash the lotus feet; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:v:vaṁśe]]---with his whole family; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:p:pāna]]---drank; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:pūjā]]---worship; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---showing; [[synonyms:s:sammāna]]---respect.
translation: He washed the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and afterwards he and his whole family drank the wash water. He also worshiped Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya and showed him respect.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.89
description: Tapana Miśra invited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to take lunch at his home, and he had Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya cook.
text:
> prabhure nimantraṇa kari' ghare bhikṣā dila
> balabhadra-bhaṭṭācārye pāka karāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhure]] [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---inviting the Lord; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at home; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave lunch; [[synonyms:b:balabhadra]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārye]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:pāka]] [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---he had cook.
translation: Tapana Miśra invited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to take lunch at his home, and he had Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya cook.
purport:
While at Vārāṇasī (Benares), Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stayed at the house of Tapana Miśra. Near Tapana Miśra's house was a bathing ghat known as Pañcanadī-ghāṭa. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to take His bath daily at this ghat, and He used to see the temple of Bindu Mādhava. Then He took His lunch at Tapana Miśra's house. Near the Bindu Mādhava temple is a big banyan tree, and it is said that after eating, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to rest beneath the tree. That banyan tree is still known today as Caitanya-vaṭa. Gradually, due to changes in language, the name became Yatana-vaṭa. The local people still call that place Yatana-vaṭa.

Presently, beside a lane there is a tomb of Vallabhācārya, but there is no sign that Caitanya Mahāprabhu ever lived there. Vallabhācārya was also known as Mahāprabhu among his disciples. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu probably lived at Yatana-vaṭa, but there is no sign of Candraśekhara's or Tapana Miśra's house, nor is there sign of the Māyāvādī //sannyāsī// Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī, with whom Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu discussed //Vedānta-sūtra.// A little distance from Yatana-vaṭa is a temple of Gaura-Nityānanda established by Śaśibhūṣaṇa Niyogī Mahāśaya of Calcutta. This temple is now managed by the mother-in-law of Śaśibhūṣaṇa and his brother-in-law Nārāyaṇa-candra Ghosh.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.9

translation: "Dear Lord, kindly hear our one petition. You have already said that You will derive happiness from our happiness. This is Your own statement.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.90

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.92
description: Candraśekhara happened to be a friend of Tapana Miśra's, and he was long known to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as His servant. He was a physician by caste, and by profession he was a clerk. At the time he was living in Vārāṇasī.
text:

> vaidya-jāti, likhana-vṛtti, vārāṇasī-vāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:miśrera]] [[synonyms:s:sakhā]]---friend of Tapana Miśra; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]] [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---former servant; [[synonyms:v:vaidya]]-[[synonyms:j:jāti]]---by caste a physician; [[synonyms:l:likhana]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛtti]]---by profession a clerk; [[synonyms:v:vārāṇasī]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---resident of Vārāṇasī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.93

text:

> prabhu uṭhi' tāṅre kṛpāya kaila āliṅgana

translation: When Candraśekhara came there, he fell down before the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and began to cry. The Lord, standing up, embraced him out of His causeless mercy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.94
description: Candraśekhara said, "My dear Lord, You bestowed Your causeless mercy upon me because I am Your old servant. Indeed, You have come here personally to give me Your audience.
text:
> candraśekhara kahe,---"prabhu, baḍa kṛpā kailā
> āpane āsiyā bhṛtye daraśana dilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:candraśekhara]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Candraśekhara said; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---my dear Lord; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---You have shown Your causeless mercy; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:b:bhṛtye]]---unto Your servant; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave Your audience.
translation: Candraśekhara said, "My dear Lord, You bestowed Your causeless mercy upon me because I am Your old servant. Indeed, You have come here personally to give me Your audience.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.95
description: "Due to my past deeds, I am residing at Vārāṇasī, but here I do not hear anything but the words māyā and Brahman."
text:
> āpana-prārabdhe vasi' vārāṇasī-sthāne
> 'māyā', 'brahma' śabda vinā nāhi śuni kāṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:p:prārabdhe]]---because of my past deeds; [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---staying; [[synonyms:v:vārāṇasī]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in the place known as Vārāṇasī; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---//māyā//; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---and //brahma//; [[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---the words; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---except; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---I do not hear; [[synonyms:k:kāṇe]]---in the ear.
translation: "Due to my past deeds, I am residing at Vārāṇasī, but here I do not hear anything but the words māyā and Brahman."
purport:
The word //prārabdhe// (past deeds) is important in this verse. Since Candraśekhara was a devotee, he was always eager to hear about Kṛṣṇa and His transcendental pastimes. Most of the inhabitants of Benares were and are impersonalists, worshipers of Lord Śiva and followers of the //pañcopāsanā// method. The impersonalists imagine some form of the impersonal Brahman, and to facilitate meditation they concentrate upon the forms of Viṣṇu, Śiva, Gaṇeśa, Sūrya and goddess Durgā. Actually these //pañcopāsakas// are not devotees of anyone. As it is said, to be a servant of everyone is to be the servant of no one. Vārāṇasī, or Kāśī, is the chief holy place of pilgrimage for impersonalists, and it is not at all suitable for devotees. A Vaiṣṇava likes to live in a //viṣṇu-tīrtha,// a place where Lord Viṣṇu's temples are present. In Vārāṇasī there are many hundreds and thousands of Lord Śiva's temples, or //pañcopāsaka// temples. Consequently Candraśekhara expressed great unhappiness as he informed Lord Caitanya that he was obliged to live at Benares due to his past misdeeds. In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// it is also said, //durjāty-ārambhakaṁ pāpaṁ yat syāt prārabdham eva tat.// "According to one's past misdeeds, one takes birth on a lower platform." In the //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.54) it is said: //karmāṇi nirdahati kintu ca bhakti-bhājām.// There is no //karma// attached to the past deeds or misdeeds of one in devotional service. A devotee is not subjected to //karma-phala,// the effect of fruitive activity. //Karma-phala// is applicable to //karmīs,// not //bhaktas.//

There are three kinds of devotees: those who are eternally on the transcendental platform (//nitya-siddha),// those elevated to the transcendental platform by the execution of devotional service (//sādhana-siddha),// and those who are neophytes advancing toward the perfectional platform (//sādhaka).// The //sādhakas// are gradually becoming free from fruitive reaction. //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.1.17) describes the symptoms of //bhakti-yoga// thus:

> kleśa-ghnī śubhadā mokṣa-
> laghutākṛt sudurlabhā
> sāndrānanda-viśeṣātmā
> śrī-kṛṣṇākarṣiṇī ca sā

Devotional service is //kleśa-ghnī// even for beginners. This means that it reduces or nullifies all kinds of suffering. The word //śubhadā// indicates that devotional service bestows all good fortune, and the words //kṛṣṇa-ākarṣiṇī// indicate that devotional service gradually attracts Kṛṣṇa toward the devotee. Consequently a devotee is not subject to any sinful reaction. In //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:18:66|(Bg. 18.66)]] Kṛṣṇa says:

> sarva-dharmān parityajya
> mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja
> ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo
> mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ

"Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reaction. Do not fear."

Thus a fully surrendered, sincere devotee immediately receives relief from all kinds of sinful reaction. There are three stages of fructification for sinful activity. At one stage, one commits the sinful act. Before that, the seed of this act exists, and before that there is ignorance whereby one commits the sin. Suffering is involved in all three stages. However, Kṛṣṇa is merciful to His devotee, and consequently He immediately nullifies all three stages---the sin, the seed of sin and the ignorance that leads one to sin. //Padma Purāṇa// confirms this:

> aprārabdha-phalaṁ pāpaṁ
> kūṭaṁ bījaṁ phalonmukham
> krameṇaiva pralīyeta
> viṣṇu-bhakti-ratātmanām

For a further explanation of this, //The Nectar of Devotion// should be consulted.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.96
description: Candraśekhara continued, "There is no talk at Vārāṇasī other than discussions on the six philosophical theses. Nonetheless, Tapana Miśra has been very kind to me, for he speaks about topics relating to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> ṣaḍ-darśana-vyākhyā vinā kathā nāhi ethā
> miśra kṛpā kari' more śunāna kṛṣṇa-kathā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṭ]]-[[synonyms:d:darśana]]---of six kinds of philosophical theses; [[synonyms:v:vyākhyā]]---explanation; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---except; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---talk; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:e:ethā]]---here; [[synonyms:m:miśra]]---Tapana Miśra; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---being very merciful; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto me; [[synonyms:ś:śunāna]]---explains; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---topics of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Candraśekhara continued, "There is no talk at Vārāṇasī other than discussions on the six philosophical theses. Nonetheless, Tapana Miśra has been very kind to me, for he speaks about topics relating to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
purport: The six philosophical treatises are: (1) //vaiśeṣika,// propounded by Kaṇāda Ṛṣi, (2) //nyāya,// propounded by Gautama Ṛṣi, (3) //yoga// or mysticism, propounded by Patañjali Ṛṣi, (4) the philosophy of //sāṅkhya,// propounded by Kapila Ṛṣi, (5) the philosophy of //karma-mīmāṁsā,// propounded by Jaimini Ṛṣi, and (6) the philosophy of //brahma-mīmāṁsā,// or Vedānta, the ultimate conclusion of the Absolute Truth (//janmādy asya yataḥ),// propounded by Vedavyāsa. Actually Vedānta philosophy is meant for the devotees because in //Bhagavad-gītā// Lord Kṛṣṇa says, //vedānta-kṛd veda-vid eva cāham:// "I am the compiler of Vedānta, and I am the knower of the //Vedas.//"[[books:bg:15:15|(Bg. 15.15)]] Vyāsadeva is an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa, and consequently Kṛṣṇa is the compiler of Vedānta philosophy. Therefore Kṛṣṇa clearly knows the purport of Vedānta philosophy. As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā,// whoever hears Vedānta philosophy from Kṛṣṇa is actually aware of the real meaning of Vedānta. The Māyāvādīs who have called themselves Vedāntists do not at all understand the purport of Vedānta philosophy. Not being properly educated, people in general think that Vedānta means the Śaṅkarite interpretation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.97
description: "My dear Lord, we two think of Your lotus feet incessantly. Although You are the omniscient Supreme Personality of Godhead, You have granted us Your audience.
text:
> nirantara duṅhe cinti tomāra caraṇa
> 'sarvajña īśvara' tumi dilā daraśana
