translation: "My dear Lord, we two think of Your lotus feet incessantly. Although You are the omniscient Supreme Personality of Godhead, You have granted us Your audience.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.98
description: "My Lord, I have heard that You are going to Vṛndāvana. After You stay here at Vārāṇasī for some days, please deliver us, for we are Your two servants."
text:
> śuni,---'mahāprabhu' yābena śrī-vṛndāvane
> dina kata rahi' tāra' bhṛtya dui-jane"
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---I hear; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yābena]]---will go; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndāvane]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:d:dina]] [[synonyms:k:kata]]---for some days; [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---staying; [[synonyms:t:tāra']]---please deliver; [[synonyms:b:bhṛtya]]---servants; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---two persons.
translation: "My Lord, I have heard that You are going to Vṛndāvana. After You stay here at Vārāṇasī for some days, please deliver us, for we are Your two servants."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.99
description: Tapana Miśra then said, "My dear Lord, as long as You stay at Vārāṇasī, please do not accept any invitation other than mine."
text:
> miśra kahe,---'prabhu, yāvat kāśīte rahibā
> mora nimantraṇa vinā anya nā mānibā'
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:miśra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Tapana Miśra said; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---my Lord; [[synonyms:y:yāvat]]---as long as; [[synonyms:k:kāśīte]] [[synonyms:r:rahibā]]---You will stay at Kāśī, Vārāṇasī; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---my invitation; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---besides; [[synonyms:a:anya]]---others; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:m:mānibā]]---do not accept.
translation: Tapana Miśra then said, "My dear Lord, as long as You stay at Vārāṇasī, please do not accept any invitation other than mine."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.1
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu traveled all over Vṛndāvana and pleased all living entities, moving and nonmoving, with His glances. The Lord took much personal pleasure in seeing everyone. In this way Lord Gaurāṅga traveled in Vṛndāvana.
text:
> vṛndāvane sthira-carān
> nandayan svāvalokanaiḥ
> ātmānaṁ ca tad-ālokād
> gaurāṅgaḥ parito 'bhramat
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvane]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:s:sthira]]-[[synonyms:c:carān]]---to the living entities, both moving and not moving; [[synonyms:n:nandayan]]---giving pleasure; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:a:avalokanaiḥ]]---by His personal glances; [[synonyms:ā:ātmānam]]---to Himself; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:ā:ālokāt]]---by seeing them; [[synonyms:g:gaurāṅgaḥ]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:paritaḥ]]---all around; [[synonyms:a:abhramat]]---traveled.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu traveled all over Vṛndāvana and pleased all living entities, moving and nonmoving, with His glances. The Lord took much personal pleasure in seeing everyone. In this way Lord Gaurāṅga traveled in Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.10
description: "Indeed, Lord Kṛṣṇa gives ecstatic love like that of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī to whoever bathes in that lake even once in his life.
text:
> sei kuṇḍe yei eka-bāra kare snāna
> tāṅre rādhā-sama 'prema' kṛṣṇa kare dāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kuṇḍe]]---in that lake; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---once; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---takes a bath; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---like Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---ecstatic love; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:d:dāna]]---gives as charity.
translation: "Indeed, Lord Kṛṣṇa gives ecstatic love like that of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī to whoever bathes in that lake even once in his life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.100
description: When Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya asked to see Kṛṣṇa at Kālīya-daha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu mercifully slapped him, saying, "You are a learned scholar, but you have become a fool influenced by the statements of other fools.
text:
> tabe tāṅre kahe prabhu cāpaḍa māriyā
> "mūrkhera vākye 'mūrkha' hailā paṇḍita hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cāpaḍa]] [[synonyms:m:māriyā]]---slapping; [[synonyms:m:mūrkhera]] [[synonyms:v:vākye]]---by the words of some rascals and fools; [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]] [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---you became a fool; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being a learned scholar.
translation: When Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya asked to see Kṛṣṇa at Kālīya-daha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu mercifully slapped him, saying, "You are a learned scholar, but you have become a fool influenced by the statements of other fools.
purport: Māyā is so strong that even a person like Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya, who was constantly staying with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, was influenced by the words of fools. He wanted to see Kṛṣṇa directly by going to Kālīya-daha, but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, being the original spiritual master, would not allow His servant to fall into such foolishness. He therefore chastised him, slapping him just to bring him to a real sense of Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.101
description: "Why will Kṛṣṇa appear in the Age of Kali? Foolish people who are mistaken are simply causing agitation and making a tumult.
text:
> kṛṣṇa kene daraśana dibe kali-kāle?
> nija-bhrame mūrkha-loka kare kolāhale
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---interview; [[synonyms:d:dibe]]---would give; [[synonyms:k:kali]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in this Age of Kali; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:b:bhrame]]---by their own mistake; [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---foolish persons; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:k:kolāhale]]---make a chaotic tumult.
translation: "Why will Kṛṣṇa appear in the Age of Kali? Foolish people who are mistaken are simply causing agitation and making a tumult.
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's first statement (//kṛṣṇa kene daraśana dibe kali-kāle//) refers to the scriptures. According to scripture, Kṛṣṇa appears in Dvāpara-yuga, but He never appears as Himself in Kali-yuga. Rather, He appears in Kali-yuga in a covered form. As stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.32): //kṛṣṇa-varṇaṁ tviṣākṛṣṇaṁ sāṅgopāṅgāstra-pārṣadam.// Kṛṣṇa appears in the Age of Kali in the garb of a devotee, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who always associates with His internal soldiers-Śrī Advaita Prabhu, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrīvāsa Prabhu and Gadādhara Prabhu. Although Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya was personally serving Lord Kṛṣṇa in His role as a devotee (Caitanya Mahāprabhu), he mistook Lord Kṛṣṇa for an ordinary man and an ordinary man for Lord Kṛṣṇa because he did not follow the rules set down by //śāstra// and //guru.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.102
description: "Do not become mad. Simply sit down here, and tomorrow night you will go see Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> 'vātula' nā ha-io, ghare rahata vasiyā
> 'kṛṣṇa' daraśana kariha kāli rātrye yāñā"
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vātula]]---mad; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:io]]---do not become; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at home; [[synonyms:r:rahata]]---keep; [[synonyms:v:vasiyā]]---sitting; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---you may do; [[synonyms:k:kāli]]---tomorrow; [[synonyms:r:rātrye]]---at night; [[synonyms:y:yāñā]]---going.
translation: "Do not become mad. Simply sit down here, and tomorrow night you will go see Kṛṣṇa."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.103
description: The next morning some respectable gentlemen came to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the Lord asked them, "Have you seen Kṛṣṇa?"
text:
> prātaḥ-kāle bhavya-loka prabhu-sthāne āilā
> 'kṛṣṇa dekhi' āilā?'---prabhu tāṅhāre puchilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---the next morning; [[synonyms:b:bhavya]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---respectable gentlemen; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---at the place of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---have you come; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāre]] [[synonyms:p:puchilā]]---inquired from them.
translation: The next morning some respectable gentlemen came to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the Lord asked them, "Have you seen Kṛṣṇa?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.104
description: These respectable gentlemen replied, "At night in the Kālīya Lake a fisherman lighting a torch in his boat catches many fish.
text:
> loka kahe,---rātrye kaivartya naukāte caḍiyā
> kālīya-dahe matsya māre, deuṭī jvāliyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:loka]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the sensible respectable persons said; [[synonyms:r:rātrye]]---at night; [[synonyms:k:kaivartya]]---a fisherman; [[synonyms:n:naukāte]]---on a boat; [[synonyms:c:caḍiyā]]---getting up; [[synonyms:k:kālīya]]-[[synonyms:d:dahe]]---in the lake of Kālīya; [[synonyms:m:matsya]] [[synonyms:m:māre]]---catches fish; [[synonyms:d:deuṭī]] [[synonyms:j:jvāliyā]]---lighting a torch.
translation: These respectable gentlemen replied, "At night in the Kālīya Lake a fisherman lighting a torch in his boat catches many fish.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.105
description: "From a distance, people mistakenly think that they are seeing Kṛṣṇa dancing on the body of the Kālīya serpent.
text:
> dūra haite tāhā dekhi' lokera haya 'bhrama'
> 'kālīyera śarīre kṛṣṇa kariche nartana'!
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from a distant place; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing that; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of people in general; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:b:bhrama]]---mistake; [[synonyms:k:kālīyera]]---of the snake Kālīya; [[synonyms:ś:śarīre]]---on the body; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kariche]] [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---is dancing.
translation: "From a distance, people mistakenly think that they are seeing Kṛṣṇa dancing on the body of the Kālīya serpent.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.106
description: "These fools think that the boat is the Kālīya serpent and the torchlight the jewels on his hoods. People also mistake the fisherman to be Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> naukāte kālīya-jñāna, dīpe ratna-jñāne!
> jāliyāre mūḍha-loka 'kṛṣṇa' kari' māne!
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:naukāte]]---on the boat; [[synonyms:k:kālīya]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge as the Kālīya snake; [[synonyms:d:dīpe]]---on the torch; [[synonyms:r:ratna]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---consideration as jewels; [[synonyms:j:jāliyāre]]---the fisherman; [[synonyms:m:mūḍha]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---foolish men; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:m:māne]]---accept as Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "These fools think that the boat is the Kālīya serpent and the torchlight the jewels on his hoods. People also mistake the fisherman to be Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.107
description: "Actually Lord Kṛṣṇa has again returned to Vṛndāvana. That also is a truth, and people have seen Him.
text:
> vṛndāvane 'kṛṣṇa' āilā,---sei 'satya' haya
> kṛṣṇere dekhila loka,---ihā 'mithyā' naya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvane]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---has come back; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is true; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---saw; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people; [[synonyms:i:ihā]] [[synonyms:m:mithyā]] [[synonyms:n:naya]]---this is not false.
translation: "Actually Lord Kṛṣṇa has again returned to Vṛndāvana. That also is a truth, and people have seen Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.108
description: "But where they are seeing Kṛṣṇa is their mistake. It is like considering a dry tree to be a person."
text:
> kintu kāhoṅ 'kṛṣṇa' dekhe, kāhoṅ 'bhrama' māne
> sthāṇu-puruṣe yaiche viparīta-jñāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kintu]]---but; [[synonyms:k:kāhoṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---one sees; [[synonyms:k:kāhoṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:b:bhrama]] [[synonyms:m:māne]]---mistakes; [[synonyms:s:sthāṇu]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣe]]---the dry tree and a person; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:v:viparīta]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---by understanding one to be the other.
translation: "But where they are seeing Kṛṣṇa is their mistake. It is like considering a dry tree to be a person."
purport: The word //sthāṇu// means "a dry tree without leaves." From a distance one may mistake such a tree for a person. This is called //sthāṇu-puruṣa.// Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was living in Vṛndāvana, the inhabitants considered Him an ordinary human being, and they mistook the fisherman to be Kṛṣṇa. Every human being is prone to make such mistakes. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was mistaken for an ordinary //sannyāsī,// the fisherman was mistaken for Kṛṣṇa, and the torchlight was mistaken for bright jewels on Kālīya's hoods.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.109
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then asked them, "Where have you seen Kṛṣṇa directly?" The people replied, "You are a sannyāsī, a renunciant; therefore You are a moving Nārāyaṇa [jaṅgama-nārāyaṇa]."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---'kāhāṅ pāilā 'kṛṣṇa daraśana?'
> loka kahe,---'sannyāsī tumi jaṅgama-nārāyaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu further inquired; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:p:pāilā]]---where have you gotten; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---sight of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:loka]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the respectable persons replied; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You are a //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:j:jaṅgama]]-[[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---moving Nārāyaṇa.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then asked them, "Where have you seen Kṛṣṇa directly?" The people replied, "You are a sannyāsī, a renunciant; therefore You are a moving Nārāyaṇa [jaṅgama-nārāyaṇa]."
purport:
This is the viewpoint of Māyāvāda philosophy. Māyāvāda philosophy supports the impersonalist view that Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, has no form. One can imagine impersonal Brahman in any form-as Viṣṇu, Lord Śiva, Vivasvān, Gaṇeśa or Devī Durgā. According to the Māyāvāda philosophy, when one becomes a //sannyāsi// he is to be considered a moving Nārāyaṇa. Māyāvāda philosophy holds that the real Nārāyaṇa does not move because, being impersonal, He has no legs. Thus according to Māyāvāda philosophy, whoever becomes a //sannyāsī// declares himself Nārāyaṇa. Foolish people accept such ordinary human beings as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is called //vivarta-vāda.//

In this regard, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that //jaṅgama-nārāyaṇa// means that the impersonal Brahman takes a shape and moves here and there in the form of a Māyāvādī //sannyāsī.// The Māyāvāda philosophy confirms this. //Daṇḍa-grahaṇa-mātreṇa naro nārāyaṇo bhavet:// "Simply by accepting the //daṇḍa// of the order of //sannyāsa,// one is immediately transformed into Nārāyaṇa." Therefore Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// address themselves by saying, //oṁ namo nārāyaṇāya.// In this way one Nārāyaṇa worships another Nārāyaṇa.

Actually an ordinary human being cannot become Nārāyaṇa. Even the chief Māyāvādī //sannyāsī,// Śrī Śaṅkarācārya, says, //nārāyaṇaḥ paro 'vyaktāt:// "Nārāyaṇa is not a creation of this material world. Nārāyaṇa is above the material creation." Due to their poor fund of knowledge, Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// think that Nārāyaṇa, the Absolute Truth, takes birth as a human being and that when He realizes this, He becomes Nārāyaṇa again. They never consider why Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, accepts an inferior position as a human being and then again becomes Nārāyaṇa when He is perfect. Why should Nārāyaṇa be imperfect? Why should He appear as a human being? Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very nicely explained these points while at Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.11
description: "The attraction of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is as sweet as that of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Similarly, the glories of the kuṇḍa [lake] are as glorious as Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
text:
> kuṇḍera 'mādhurī'---yena rādhāra 'madhurimā'
> kuṇḍera 'mahimā'---yena rādhāra 'mahimā'
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kuṇḍera]]---of the lake; [[synonyms:m:mādhurī]]---sweetness; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:r:rādhāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:m:madhurimā]]---sweetness; [[synonyms:k:kuṇḍera]]---of the lake; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---glories; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:r:rādhāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---glories.
translation: "The attraction of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is as sweet as that of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Similarly, the glories of the kuṇḍa [lake] are as glorious as Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.110
description: The people then said, "You have appeared in Vṛndāvana as an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa. Just by seeing You, everyone is now liberated."
text:
> vṛndāvane ha-ilā tumi kṛṣṇa-avatāra
> tomā dekhi' sarva-loka ha-ila nistāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvane]]---at Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnation of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tomā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---by seeing You; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---all people; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]] [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---become liberated.
translation: The people then said, "You have appeared in Vṛndāvana as an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa. Just by seeing You, everyone is now liberated."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.111
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately exclaimed, "Viṣṇu! Viṣṇu! Do not call Me the Supreme Personality of Godhead. A jīva cannot become Kṛṣṇa at any time. Do not even say such a thing!
text:
> prabhu kahe,---'viṣṇu' 'viṣṇu' ihā nā kahibā!
> jīvādhame 'kṛṣṇa'-jñāna kabhu nā karibā!
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]] [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---O Viṣṇu, Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kahibā]]---do not speak; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:a:adhame]]---fallen conditioned souls; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---accepting as Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---ever; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:karibā]]---do not do.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately exclaimed, "Viṣṇu! Viṣṇu! Do not call Me the Supreme Personality of Godhead. A jīva cannot become Kṛṣṇa at any time. Do not even say such a thing!
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately stated that a living being, however exalted he may be, should never be compared to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. All of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's preaching protests the monistic philosophy of the Māyāvāda school. The central point of Kṛṣṇa consciousness is that the //jīva,// the living entity, can never be accepted as Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu. This viewpoint is elaborated in the following verses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.112
description: "A sannyāsī in the renounced order is certainly part and parcel of the complete whole, just as a shining molecular particle of sunshine is part and parcel of the sun itself. Kṛṣṇa is like the sun, full of six opulences, but the living entity is only a fragment of the complete whole.
text:
> sannyāsī---cit-kaṇa jīva, kiraṇa-kaṇa-sama
> ṣaḍ-aiśvarya-pūrṇa kṛṣṇa haya sūryopama
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---a person in the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:k:kaṇa]] [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---a small fragmental living being; [[synonyms:k:kiraṇa]]---of sunshine; [[synonyms:k:kaṇa]]---small particle; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---like; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṭ]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]-[[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---full in six opulences; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:s:sūrya]]-[[synonyms:u:upama]]---compared to the sun.
translation: "A sannyāsī in the renounced order is certainly part and parcel of the complete whole, just as a shining molecular particle of sunshine is part and parcel of the sun itself. Kṛṣṇa is like the sun, full of six opulences, but the living entity is only a fragment of the complete whole.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.113
description: "A living entity and the Absolute Personality of Godhead are never to be considered equal, just as a fragmental spark can never be considered the original flame.
text:
> jīva, īśvara-tattva---kabhu nahe 'sama'
> jvalad-agni-rāśi yaiche sphuliṅgera 'kaṇa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---a living being; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]]---and the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal; [[synonyms:j:jvalat]]-[[synonyms:a:agni]]-[[synonyms:r:rāśi]]---large flame; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:s:sphuliṅgera]]---of a spark; [[synonyms:k:kaṇa]]---fragmental portion.
translation: "A living entity and the Absolute Personality of Godhead are never to be considered equal, just as a fragmental spark can never be considered the original flame.
purport: Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// consider themselves Brahman, and they superficially speak of themselves as Nārāyaṇa. The monistic disciples of the Māyāvāda school (known as //smārta-brāhmaṇas//) are generally householder //brāhmaṇas// who accept the Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// as Nārāyaṇa incarnate; therefore they offer their obeisances to them. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately protested this unauthorized system, specifically mentioning that a //sannyāsī// (//cit-kaṇa jīva//) is nothing but a fragmental portion of the Supreme. In other words, he is nothing more than an ordinary living being. He is never Nārāyaṇa, just as a molecular portion of sunshine is never the sun itself. The living entity is nothing but a fragmental part of the Absolute Truth; therefore at no stage of perfection can a living entity become the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This Māyāvāda viewpoint is always condemned by the Vaiṣṇava school. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself protested this philosophy. When the Māyāvādīs accept //sannyāsa// and consider themselves Nārāyaṇa, they become so puffed up that they do not even enter the temple of Nārāyaṇa to offer respects, for they falsely think themselves Nārāyaṇa Himself. Although Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// may offer respects to other //sannyāsīs// and address them as Nārāyaṇa, they do not go to a Nārāyaṇa temple and offer respects. These Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// are always condemned and are described as demons. The //Vedas// clearly state that living entities are subordinate parts and parcels of the supreme. //Eko bahūnāṁ yo vidadhāti kāmān:// the Supreme Being, Kṛṣṇa, maintains all living entities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.114
description: " 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, the supreme controller, is always full of transcendental bliss and is accompanied by the potencies known as hlādinī and samvit. The conditioned soul, however, is always covered by ignorance and embarrassed by the threefold miseries of life. Thus he is a treasure-house of all kinds of tribulations.'
text:
> hlādinyā saṁvid-āśliṣṭaḥ
> sac-cid-ānanda īśvaraḥ
> svāvidyā-saṁvṛto jīvaḥ
> saṅkleśa-nikarākaraḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hlādinyā]]---by the //hlādinī// potency; [[synonyms:s:saṁvit]]---by the //samvit// potency; [[synonyms:ā:āśliṣṭaḥ]]---surrounded; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānandaḥ]]---always transcendentally blissful; [[synonyms:ī:īśvaraḥ]]---the supreme controller; [[synonyms:s:sva]]---own; [[synonyms:a:avidyā]]---by ignorance; [[synonyms:s:saṁvṛtaḥ]]---surrounded; [[synonyms:j:jīvaḥ]]---the living entity; [[synonyms:s:saṅkleśa]]---of the threefold miseries; [[synonyms:n:nikara]]---of the multitude; [[synonyms:ā:ākaraḥ]]---the mine.
translation: “ 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, the supreme controller, is always full of transcendental bliss and is accompanied by the potencies known as hlādinī and samvit. The conditioned soul, however, is always covered by ignorance and embarrassed by the threefold miseries of life. Thus he is a treasure-house of all kinds of tribulations.'
purport: This quotation of Viṣṇusvāmī is cited in Śrīdhara Svāmī's //Bhāvārtha-dīpikā// commentary on //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:7:6|(1.7.6)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.115
description: "A foolish person who says that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the same as the living entity is an atheist, and he becomes subject to punishment by the superintendent of death, Yamarāja.
text:
> yei mūḍha kahe,---jīva īśvara haya 'sama'
> seita 'pāṣaṇḍī' haya, daṇḍe tāre yama
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:m:mūḍha]]---any foolish person who; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---the living entity; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the supreme controller; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal; [[synonyms:s:seita]]---he; [[synonyms:p:pāṣaṇḍī]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is a first-class atheist; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍe]]---punishes; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---him; [[synonyms:y:yama]]---the superintendent of death, Yamarāja.
translation: "A foolish person who says that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the same as the living entity is an atheist, and he becomes subject to punishment by the superintendent of death, Yamarāja.
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that the word //pāṣaṇḍī// refers to one who considers the living entity under the control of the illusory energy to be equal with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is transcendental to all material qualities. Another kind of //pāṣaṇḍī// is one who does not believe in the spirit soul, the superior potency of the Lord, and therefore does not distinguish between spirit and matter. While describing one of the offenses against chanting the holy names, an offense called //śruti-śāstra-nindana// (blaspheming the Vedic literature), Jīva Gosvāmī states in his //Bhakti-sandarbha:yathā pāṣaṇḍa-mārgeṇa dattātreyarṣabha-devopāsakānāṁ pāṣaṇḍīnām.// Worshipers of impersonalists like Dattātreya are also //pāṣaṇḍīs.// Concerning the offense of //ahaṁ-mama-buddhi,// or //dehātma-buddhi// (considering the body to be the self), Jīva Gosvāmī states: //deva-draviṇādi-nimittaka-'pāṣaṇḍa'-śabdena ca daśāparādhā eva lakṣyante, pāṣaṇḍamayatvāt teṣām.// "Those who are overly absorbed in the conception of the body and the bodily necessities are also called //pāṣaṇḍīs.//" lsewhere in //Bhakti-sandarbha// it is stated:

> uddiśya devatā eva
> juhoti ca dadāti ca
> sa pāṣaṇḍīti vijñeyaḥ
> svatantro vāpi karmasu

"A //pāṣaṇḍī// is one who considers the demigods and the Supreme Personality of Godhead to be one; therefore a //pāṣaṇḍī// worships any kind of demigod as the Supreme Personality of Godhead." One who disobeys the orders of the spiritual master is also considered a //pāṣaṇḍī.// The word //pāṣaṇḍī// has been described in many places in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// including 4.2.28, 30, 32; 5.6.9 and 12.2.13, 43.

On the whole, a //pāṣaṇḍī// is a nondevotee who does not accept the Vedic conclusions. In the //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa// (1.117) there is a verse quoted from //Padma Purāṇa// describing the //pāṣaṇḍī.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu quotes this verse as the following text.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.116
description: " 'A person who considers demigods like Brahmā and Śiva to be on an equal level with Nārāyaṇa is to be considered an offender and a pāṣaṇḍī.' "
text:
> yas tu nārāyaṇaṁ devaṁ
> brahma-rudrādi-daivataiḥ
> samatvenaiva vīkṣeta
> sa pāṣaṇḍī bhaved dhruvam
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---any person who; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---however; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇam]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the master of such demigods as Brahmā and Śiva; [[synonyms:d:devam]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:r:rudra]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and others; [[synonyms:d:daivataiḥ]]---with such demigods; [[synonyms:s:samatvena]]---on an equal level; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:v:vīkṣeta]]---observes; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---such a person; [[synonyms:p:pāṣaṇḍī]]---pāṣaṇḍī; [[synonyms:b:bhavet]]---must be; [[synonyms:d:dhruvam]]---certainly.
translation: “ 'A person who considers demigods like Brahmā and Śiva to be on an equal level with Nārāyaṇa is to be considered an offender and a pāṣaṇḍī.' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.117
description: After Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu explained the difference between an ordinary living being and the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the people said, "No one considers You an ordinary human being. You are like Kṛṣṇa in every respect, in both bodily features and characteristics.
text:
> loka kahe,---tomāte kabhu nahe jīva'-mati
> kṛṣṇera sadṛśa tomāra ākṛti-prakṛti
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:loka]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the people said; [[synonyms:t:tomāte]]---unto You; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---there is not; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:m:mati]]---considering an ordinary living being; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:s:sadṛśa]]---like Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:ā:ākṛti]]---bodily features; [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]]---characteristics.
translation: After Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu explained the difference between an ordinary living being and the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the people said, "No one considers You an ordinary human being. You are like Kṛṣṇa in every respect, in both bodily features and characteristics.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.118
description: "By Your bodily features we can see that You are none other than the son of Nanda Mahārāja, although the golden luster of Your body has covered Your original complexion.
text:
> 'ākṛtye' tomāre dekhi 'vrajendra-nandana'
> deha-kānti pītāmbara kaila ācchādana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ākṛtye]]---by bodily features; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---You; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---we see; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---directly the son of Mahārāja Nanda; [[synonyms:d:deha]]-[[synonyms:k:kānti]]---the luster of the body; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]-[[synonyms:a:ambara]]---golden covering; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:ā:ācchādana]]---covered.
translation: "By Your bodily features we can see that You are none other than the son of Nanda Mahārāja, although the golden luster of Your body has covered Your original complexion.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.119
description: "As the aroma of deer musk cannot be concealed by wrapping it in a cloth, Your characteristics as the Supreme Personality of Godhead cannot be concealed by any means.
text:
> mṛga-mada vastre bāndhe, tabu nā lukāya
> 'īśvara-svabhāva' tomāra ṭākā nāhi yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]-[[synonyms:m:mada]]---deer musk; [[synonyms:v:vastre]]---in cloth; [[synonyms:b:bāndhe]]---wraps; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:l:lukāya]]---is concealed; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---characteristics as the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of You; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭākā]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---are not concealed.
translation: "As the aroma of deer musk cannot be concealed by wrapping it in a cloth, Your characteristics as the Supreme Personality of Godhead cannot be concealed by any means.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.12
description: " 'Because of its wonderful transcendental qualities, Rādhā-kuṇḍa is as dear to Kṛṣṇa as Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. It was in that lake that the all-opulent Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa performed His pastimes with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī with great pleasure and transcendental bliss. Whoever bathes just once in Rādhā-kuṇḍa attains Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's loving attraction for Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Who within this world can describe the glories and sweetness of Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa?' "
text:
> śrī-rādheva hares tadīya-sarasī preṣṭhādbhutaiḥ svair guṇair
> yasyāṁ śrī-yuta-mādhavendur aniśaṁ prītyā tayā krīḍati
> premāsmin bata rādhikeva labhate yasyāṁ sakṛt snāna-kṛt
> tasyā vai mahimā tathā madhurimā kenāstu varṇyaḥ kṣitau
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]]---of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tadīya]]---Her; [[synonyms:s:sarasī]]---lake; [[synonyms:p:preṣṭhā]]---very dear; [[synonyms:a:adbhutaiḥ]]---by wonderful; [[synonyms:s:svaiḥ]]---own; [[synonyms:g:guṇaiḥ]]---transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:y:yasyām]]---in which; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:y:yuta]]---all-opulent; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]---Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:i:induḥ]]---like the moon; [[synonyms:a:aniśam]]---incessantly; [[synonyms:p:prītyā]]---with great affection; [[synonyms:t:tayā]]---in association with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:k:krīḍati]]---performs pastimes; [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love; [[synonyms:a:asmin]]---for Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bata]]---certainly; [[synonyms:r:rādhikā]] [[synonyms:i:iva]]---exactly like Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:l:labhate]]---obtains; [[synonyms:y:yasyām]]---in which; [[synonyms:s:sakṛt]]---once; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛt]]---one who takes a bath; [[synonyms:t:tasyāḥ]]---of the lake; [[synonyms:v:vai]]---certainly; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---glories; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---as well as; [[synonyms:m:madhurimā]]---sweetness; [[synonyms:k:kena]]---by whom; [[synonyms:a:astu]]---can be; [[synonyms:v:varṇyaḥ]]---described; [[synonyms:k:kṣitau]]---on this earth.
translation: “ 'Because of its wonderful transcendental qualities, Rādhā-kuṇḍa is as dear to Kṛṣṇa as Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. It was in that lake that the all-opulent Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa performed His pastimes with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī with great pleasure and transcendental bliss. Whoever bathes just once in Rādhā-kuṇḍa attains Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's loving attraction for Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Who within this world can describe the glories and sweetness of Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa?' "
purport: This verse is found in the //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (7.102).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.120
description: "Indeed, Your characteristics are uncommon and beyond the imagination of an ordinary living being. Simply by seeing You, the entire universe becomes mad with ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> alaukika 'prakṛti' tomāra---buddhi-agocara
> tomā dekhi' kṛṣṇa-preme jagat pāgala

translation: "Indeed, Your characteristics are uncommon and beyond the imagination of an ordinary living being. Simply by seeing You, the entire universe becomes mad with ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.121-122
description: "If even women, children, old men, meat-eaters or members of the lowest caste can see You even once, they immediately chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa, dance like madmen and become spiritual masters capable of delivering the whole world.

> strī-bāla-vṛddha, āra 'caṇḍāla, 'yavana'
> yei tomāra eka-bāra pāya daraśana

translation: "If even women, children, old men, meat-eaters or members of the lowest caste can see You even once, they immediately chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa, dance like madmen and become spiritual masters capable of delivering the whole world.

> sei kṛṣṇa-preme matta, tāre tribhuvane

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.124
description: "Simply by hearing Your holy name, dog-eaters become holy saints. Your uncommon potencies cannot be described in words.
text:

> alaukika śakti tomāra nā yāya kathana

translation: "Simply by hearing Your holy name, dog-eaters become holy saints. Your uncommon potencies cannot be described in words.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.125
description: " 'To say nothing of the spiritual advancement of persons who see the Supreme Person face to face, even a person born in a family of dog-eaters becomes immediately eligible to perform Vedic sacrifices if he once utters the holy name of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, or chants about Him, hears about His pastimes, offers Him obeisances or even remembers Him.'
text:
> yan-nāmadheya-śravaṇānukīrtanād
> yat-prahvaṇād yat-smaraṇād api kvacit
> śvādo 'pi sadyaḥ savanāya kalpate
> kutaḥ punas te bhagavan nu darśanāt
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yat]]---of whom; [[synonyms:n:nāmadheya]]---of the name; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]---from hearing; [[synonyms:a:anukīrtanāt]]---and thereafter from chanting; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---to whom; [[synonyms:p:prahvaṇāt]]---from offering respects; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---of whom; [[synonyms:s:smaraṇāt]]---from simply remembering; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:k:kvacit]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:ś:śva]]-[[synonyms:a:adaḥ]]---a dog-eater; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:s:sadyaḥ]]---immediately; [[synonyms:s:savanāya]]---for performing Vedic sacrifices; [[synonyms:k:kalpate]]---becomes eligible; [[synonyms:k:kutaḥ]]---what to speak; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:t:te]]---of You; [[synonyms:b:bhagavan]]---O Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:nu]]---certainly; [[synonyms:d:darśanāt]]---from seeing.
translation: “ 'To say nothing of the spiritual advancement of persons who see the Supreme Person face to face, even a person born in a family of dog-eaters becomes immediately eligible to perform Vedic sacrifices if he once utters the holy name of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, or chants about Him, hears about His pastimes, offers Him obeisances or even remembers Him.'
purport:
This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:33:6|(3.33.6)]]. According to this verse, it doesn't matter what position a person holds. One may be the lowest of the low-a //caṇḍāla,// or dog-eater---but if he takes to chanting and hearing the holy name of the Lord, he is immediately eligible to perform Vedic sacrifices. This is especially true in this Age of Kali.

> harer nāma harer nāma
> harer nāmaiva kevalam
> kalau nāsty eva nāsty eva
> nāsty eva gatir anyathā

(//Bṛhan-nāradīya Purāṇa// 38.126)

A person born in a //brāhmaṇa// family cannot perform Vedic sacrifices until he is properly purified and has attained his sacred thread. However, according to this verse, it is understood that even a lowborn person can immediately perform sacrifices if he sincerely chants and hears the holy name of the Lord. Sometimes envious people ask how Europeans and Americans in this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement can become //brāhmaṇas// and perform sacrifices. They do not know that the Europeans and Americans have already been purified by chanting the holy name of the Lord-Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare HareHare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare. This is the proof. //Śvādo 'pi sadyaḥ savanāya kalpate.// One may be born in a family of dog-eaters, but he can perform sacrifices simply by chanting the //mahā-mantra.//

Those who find fault in the Western Vaiṣṇavas should consider this statement from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// and the commentary on this verse by Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī. In this regard, Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī has stated that to become a //brāhmaṇa,// one has to wait for purification and undergo the sacred thread ceremony, but a chanter of the holy name does not have to wait for the sacred thread ceremony. We do not allow devotees to perform sacrifices until they are properly initiated in the sacred thread ceremony. Yet according to this verse, an offenseless chanter of the holy name is already fit to perform a fire ceremony, even though he is not doubly initiated by the sacred thread ceremony. This is the verdict given by Lord Kapiladeva in His instructions to His mother, Devahūti. It was Lord Kapiladeva who instructed Devahūti in pure Sāṅkhya philosophy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.126
description: "These glories of Yours are only marginal. Originally You are the son of Mahārāja Nanda."
text:
> eita' mahimā---tomāra 'taṭastha'-lakṣaṇa
> 'svarūpa'-lakṣaṇe tumi---'vrajendra-nandana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eita']]---all these; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---glories; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:t:taṭastha]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---marginal characteristics; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---original; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇe]]---by characteristics; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of Mahārāja Nanda.
translation: "These glories of Yours are only marginal. Originally You are the son of Mahārāja Nanda."
purport: The original characteristics of a substance are called //svarūpa,// and the subsequent corollaries are called //taṭastha-lakṣaṇa,// or marginal characteristics. The glories of the Lord's marginal characteristics prove Him to be the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, the son of Mahārāja Nanda. As soon as one understands this, one accepts Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.127
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then bestowed His causeless mercy upon all the people there, and everyone became ecstatic with love of God. Finally they all returned to their homes.
text:
> sei saba loke prabhu prasāda karila
> kṛṣṇa-preme matta loka nija-ghare gela

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then bestowed His causeless mercy upon all the people there, and everyone became ecstatic with love of God. Finally they all returned to their homes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.128
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained for some days in Akrūra-tīrtha. He delivered everyone there simply by distributing the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and ecstatic love for the Lord.

> ei-mata kata-dina 'akrūre' rahilā
> kṛṣṇa-nāma-prema diyā loka nistārilā

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained for some days in Akrūra-tīrtha. He delivered everyone there simply by distributing the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and ecstatic love for the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.129
description: The brāhmaṇa disciple of Mādhavendra Purī went from house to house in Mathurā and inspired other brāhmaṇas to invite Caitanya Mahāprabhu to their homes.
text:
> mādhava-purīra śiṣya seita brāhmaṇa
> mathurāra ghare-ghare karā'na nimantraṇa

translation: The brāhmaṇa disciple of Mādhavendra Purī went from house to house in Mathurā and inspired other brāhmaṇas to invite Caitanya Mahāprabhu to their homes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.13
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus offered prayers to Rādhā-kuṇḍa. Overwhelmed by ecstatic love, He danced on the bank, remembering the pastimes Lord Kṛṣṇa performed on the bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa.
text:
> ei-mata stuti kare premāviṣṭa hañā
> tīre nṛtya kare kuṇḍa-līlā saṅariyā

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus offered prayers to Rādhā-kuṇḍa. Overwhelmed by ecstatic love, He danced on the bank, remembering the pastimes Lord Kṛṣṇa performed on the bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.130
description: Thus all the respectable people of Mathurā, headed by the brāhmaṇas, came to Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya and extended invitations to the Lord.
text:
> mathurāra yata loka brāhmaṇa sajjana
> bhaṭṭācārya-sthāne āsi' kare nimantraṇa

translation: Thus all the respectable people of Mathurā, headed by the brāhmaṇas, came to Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya and extended invitations to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.131
description: In one day, ten to twenty invitations were received, but Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya would accept only one of them.
text:
> eka-dina 'daśa' 'biśa' āise nimantraṇa
> bhaṭṭācārya ekera mātra karena grahaṇa

translation: In one day, ten to twenty invitations were received, but Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya would accept only one of them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.132
description: Since everyone did not get an opportunity to offer invitations to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally, they requested the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa to ask the Lord to accept their invitations.

> avasara nā pāya loka nimantraṇa dite

translation: Since everyone did not get an opportunity to offer invitations to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally, they requested the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa to ask the Lord to accept their invitations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.133
description: The brāhmaṇas from different places, such as Kānyakubja and South India, who were all strict followers of the Vedic religion, offered invitations to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with great humility.
text:

> dainya kari, kare mahāprabhura nimantraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kānyakubja]]---brāhmaṇas from Kānyakubja; [[synonyms:d:dākṣiṇātyera]]---certain //brāhmaṇas// from South India; [[synonyms:v:vaidika]]---followers of the Vedic religion; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---//brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:d:dainya]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---with great humility; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation.
translation: The brāhmaṇas from different places, such as Kānyakubja and South India, who were all strict followers of the Vedic religion, offered invitations to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with great humility.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.134
description: In the morning they would come to Akrūra-tīrtha and cook food. After offering it to the śālagrāma-śilā, they offered it to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> prātaḥ-kāle akrūre āsi' randhana kariyā
> prabhure bhikṣā dena śālagrāme samarpiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:a:akrūre]]---to Akrūra-tīrtha; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:r:randhana]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---cooking; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:d:dena]]---offer lunch; [[synonyms:ś:śālagrāme]] [[synonyms:s:samarpiyā]]---after offering to the //śālagrāma-śilā.//
translation: In the morning they would come to Akrūra-tīrtha and cook food. After offering it to the śālagrāma-śilā, they offered it to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
purport: There are //brāhmaṇas// known as //pañca-gauḍa-brāhmaṇas// who come from five places in northern India, and there are //brāhmaṇas// known as //pañca-dākṣiṇātya-brāhmaṇas// who come from five places in southern India. In northern India the places are Kānyakubja, Sārasvata, Gauḍa, Maithila and Utkala. In southern India the places are Āndhra, Karṇāta, Gurjara, Drāviḍa and Mahārāṣṭra. The //brāhmaṇas// from these places are considered to be very strict followers of the Vedic principles, and they are accepted as pure //brāhmaṇas.// They strictly observe Vedic principles and are not polluted by tantric misdeeds. All of these //brāhmaṇas// respectfully invited Caitanya Mahāprabhu for lunch.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.135
description: One day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat at the bathing ghat of Akrūra-tīrtha and thought the following thoughts.
text:
> eka-dina sei akrūra-ghāṭera upare
> vasi' mahāprabhu kichu karena vicāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---once upon a time; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:a:akrūra]]-[[synonyms:g:ghāṭera]]---of the Akrūra bathing ghat; [[synonyms:u:upare]]---on the bank; [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:v:vicāre]]---consideration.
translation:
One day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat at the bathing ghat of Akrūra-tīrtha and thought the following thoughts.


Akrūra-tīrtha is located on the road between Vṛndāvana and Mathurā. When Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma were being taken to Mathurā by Akrūra, the Lord rested at this place and took His bath in the Yamunā. When Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma took Their baths, Akrūra saw the entire world of Vaikuṇṭha within the water. The inhabitants of Vṛndāvana also saw the Vaikuṇṭha planets within the water.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.136
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thought, "At this bathing place, Akrūra saw Vaikuṇṭha, the spiritual world, and all the inhabitants of Vraja saw Goloka Vṛndāvana."
text:
> ei ghāṭe akrūra vaikuṇṭha dekhila
> vrajavāsī loka 'goloka' darśana kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:g:ghāṭe]]---in this bathing place; [[synonyms:a:akrūra]]---Akrūra; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---saw the spiritual world; [[synonyms:v:vrajavāsī]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:g:goloka]] [[synonyms:d:darśana]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---saw Goloka.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thought, "At this bathing place, Akrūra saw Vaikuṇṭha, the spiritual world, and all the inhabitants of Vraja saw Goloka Vṛndāvana."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.137
description: While considering how Akrūra remained within the water, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately jumped in and stayed under water for some time.
text:
> eta bali' jhāṅpa dilā jalera upare
> ḍubiyā rahilā prabhu jalera bhitare
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:j:jhāṅpa]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---jumped; [[synonyms:j:jalera]] [[synonyms:u:upare]]---above the water; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍubiyā]]---sinking; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jalera]] [[synonyms:b:bhitare]]---within the water.
translation: While considering how Akrūra remained within the water, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately jumped in and stayed under water for some time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.138

> bhaṭṭācārya śīghra āsi' prabhure uṭhāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:k:kāndi']]---crying; [[synonyms:p:phu]]-[[synonyms:k:kāra]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---called loudly; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]]---hastily; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]] [[synonyms:u:uṭhāila]]---raised Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: When Kṛṣṇadāsa saw that Caitanya Mahāprabhu was drowning, he cried and shouted very loudly. Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya immediately came and pulled the Lord out.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.139

translation: After this, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya took the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa to a secluded place and consulted with him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.14
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then marked His body with tilaka made from the mud of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, and with the help of Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya, He collected some of the mud and took it with Him.

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then marked His body with tilaka made from the mud of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, and with the help of Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya, He collected some of the mud and took it with Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.140
description: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Since I was present today, it was possible for me to pull the Lord up. However, if He starts to drown at Vṛndāvana, who will help Him?

> āji āmi āchilāṅa uṭhāiluṅ prabhure
> vṛndāvane ḍubena yadi, ke uṭhābe tāṅre?

translation: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Since I was present today, it was possible for me to pull the Lord up. However, if He starts to drown at Vṛndāvana, who will help Him?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.141
description: "Now there is a crowd of people here, and these invitations are causing much disturbance. In addition, the Lord is always ecstatic and emotional. I do not find the situation here very good.
text:
> lokera saṅghaṭṭa, āra nimantraṇera jañjāla
> nirantara āveśa prabhura nā dekhiye bhāla

translation: "Now there is a crowd of people here, and these invitations are causing much disturbance. In addition, the Lord is always ecstatic and emotional. I do not find the situation here very good.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.142
description: "It would be good if we could get Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu out of Vṛndāvana. That is my final conclusion."
text:
> vṛndāvana haite yadi prabhure kāḍiye
> tabe maṅgala haya,---ei bhāla yukti haye

translation: "It would be good if we could get Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu out of Vṛndāvana. That is my final conclusion."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.143
description: The Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa said, "Let us take Him to Prayāga and go along the banks of the Ganges. It will be very pleasurable to go that way.
text:
> vipra kahe,---prayāge prabhu lañā yāi
> gaṅgā-tīra-pathe yāi, tabe sukha pāi

translation: The Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa said, "Let us take Him to Prayāga and go along the banks of the Ganges. It will be very pleasurable to go that way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.144
description: "After going to the holy place named Soro-kṣetra, and taking bath in the Ganges, let us take Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu that way and go.
text:
> 'soro-kṣetre, āge yāñā kari' gaṅgā-snāna
> sei pathe prabhu lañā kariye payāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:soro]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣetre]]---to the holy place named Soro-kṣetra; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---first, beyond; [[synonyms:y:yāñā]]---going; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---having taken bath in the Ganges; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---that way; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kariye]] [[synonyms:p:payāna]]---let us go.
translation: "After going to the holy place named Soro-kṣetra, and taking bath in the Ganges, let us take Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu that way and go.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.145
description: "It is now the beginning of the month of Māgha. If we go to Prayāga at this time, we shall have an opportunity to bathe for a few days during Makara-saṅkrānti."
text:
> māgha-māsa lāgila, ebe yadi yāiye
> makare prayāga-snāna kata dina pāiye
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māgha]]-[[synonyms:m:māsa]] [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---the month of Māgha has begun; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:y:yāiye]]---we go; [[synonyms:m:makare]]---during the Makara-saṅkrānti; [[synonyms:p:prayāga]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing at Prayāga; [[synonyms:k:kata]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---for a few days; [[synonyms:p:pāiye]]---we shall get.
translation: "It is now the beginning of the month of Māgha. If we go to Prayāga at this time, we shall have an opportunity to bathe for a few days during Makara-saṅkrānti."
purport:
Bathing during the month of Māgha at Māgha-melā still takes place. This has been a very old //melā// (assembly) from time immemorial. It is said that the Lord in the form of Mohinī took a bucket of nectar and kept it at Prayāga. Consequently Māgha-melā has been observed, and there is an assembly of holy men there every year. Every twelfth year there is a Kumbha-melā, a great festival, and all the holy men from all over India assemble there. The //brāhmaṇa// wanted to take advantage of the Māgha-melā and bathe there.

Bathing at the confluence of the Ganges and Yamunā near the fort at Allahabad, Prayāga, is mentioned in revealed scriptures:

> māghe māsi gamiṣyanti
> gaṅgā-yāmuna-saṅgamam
> gavāṁ śata-sahasrasya
> samyag dattaṁ ca yat-phalam

> prayāge māgha-māse vai
> tryahaṁ snātasya tat-phalam

"If one goes to Prayāga and bathes at the confluence of the Ganges and Yamunā in the month of Māgha, he attains the result of giving hundreds and thousands of cows in charity. Simply by bathing for three days there, he attains the results of such a pious activity." Because of this, the Sanoḍiyā //brāhmaṇa// was very eager to go to Prayāga and bathe. Generally //karmīs// (fruitive laborers) take advantage of bathing there during the month of Māgha, thinking that they will be rewarded in the future. Those who are situated in devotional service do not very strictly follow this //karma-kāṇḍīya// process.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.146
description: The Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa continued, "Kindly submit to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu the unhappiness you are feeling within yourself. Then propose that we all go to Prayāga on the full-moon day of the month of Māgha.
text:
> āpanāra duḥkha kichu kari' nivedana
> 'makara-paṅcasi prayāge' kariha sūcana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āpanāra]]---personal; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---submission; [[synonyms:m:makara]]-[[synonyms:p:paṅcasi]]---the full-moon day in the month of Māgha; [[synonyms:p:prayāge]]---to Prayāga; [[synonyms:k:kariha]] [[synonyms:s:sūcana]]---kindly inform.
translation: The Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa continued, "Kindly submit to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu the unhappiness you are feeling within yourself. Then propose that we all go to Prayāga on the full-moon day of the month of Māgha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.147
description: "Tell the Lord of the happiness you will feel in traveling via the banks of the Ganges." Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya therefore submitted this prayer to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> gaṅgā-tīra-pathe sukha jānāiha tāṅre
> bhaṭṭācārya āsi' tabe kahila prabhure
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:t:tīra]]---on the bank of the Ganges; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the path; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:j:jānāiha]]---kindly let know; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:k:kahila]] [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---informed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: "Tell the Lord of the happiness you will feel in traveling via the banks of the Ganges." Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya therefore submitted this prayer to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.148
description: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya told the Lord, "I can no longer tolerate the disturbance of the crowd. People are coming one after another to offer invitations.
text:
> "sahite nā pāri āmi lokera gaḍabaḍi
> nimantraṇa lāgi' loka kare huḍāhuḍi
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sahite]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---cannot tolerate; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of people; [[synonyms:g:gaḍabaḍi]]---disturbance; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitations; [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:h:huḍāhuḍi]]---hurrying.
translation: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya told the Lord, "I can no longer tolerate the disturbance of the crowd. People are coming one after another to offer invitations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.149
description: "Early in the morning people come here, and not seeing You present, they simply tax my brain.
text:
> prātaḥ-kāle āise loka, tomāre nā pāya
> tomāre nā pāñā loka mora māthā khāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---come; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---You; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---cannot see; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---not getting You; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:m:māthā]] [[synonyms:k:khāya]]---tax my brain.
translation: "Early in the morning people come here, and not seeing You present, they simply tax my brain.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.15
description: From Rādhā-kuṇḍa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Sumanaḥ Lake. When He saw Govardhana Hill from there, He was overwhelmed by joy.
text:
> tabe cali' āilā prabhu 'sumanaḥ-sarovara'
> tāhāṅ 'govardhana' dekhi' ha-ilā vihvala
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---traveling; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sumanaḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:sarovara]]---to the lake known as Sumanaḥ; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]---Govardhana Hill; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]] [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---became overwhelmed.
translation: From Rādhā-kuṇḍa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Sumanaḥ Lake. When He saw Govardhana Hill from there, He was overwhelmed by joy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.150
description: "I will be very happy if we all leave and take the path by the banks of the Ganges. Then we can have the opportunity to bathe in the Ganges in Prayāga during Makara-saṅkrānti.
text:
> tabe sukha haya yabe gaṅgā-pathe yāiye
> ebe yadi yāi, 'makare' gaṅgā-snāna pāiye
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:s:sukha]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---it will be great happiness for me; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the path of the Ganges; [[synonyms:y:yāiye]]---we go; [[synonyms:e:ebe]] [[synonyms:y:yadi]] [[synonyms:y:yāi]]---if we go just now; [[synonyms:m:makare]]---during Makara-saṅkrānti; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:p:pāiye]]---we can take bath in the Ganges.
translation: "I will be very happy if we all leave and take the path by the banks of the Ganges. Then we can have the opportunity to bathe in the Ganges in Prayāga during Makara-saṅkrānti.
purport: There are two great occasions for bathing in the Ganges during Māgha-melā. One is on the day of the dark moon, and the other is on the day of the full moon during the month of Māgha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.151
description: "My mind has become very agitated, and I cannot bear this anxiety. May everything rest on the permission of Your Lordship. I will accept whatever You want to do."
text:
> udvigna ha-ila prāṇa, sahite nā pāri
> prabhura ye ājñā haya, sei śire dhari"
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:udvigna]]---agitated; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---has become; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]---my mind; [[synonyms:s:sahite]]---to bear; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---I am unable; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---what; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ś:śire]] [[synonyms:d:dhari]]---I accept that.
translation: "My mind has become very agitated, and I cannot bear this anxiety. May everything rest on the permission of Your Lordship. I will accept whatever You want to do."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.152
description: Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had no desire to leave Vṛndāvana, He began to speak sweet words just to fulfill the desire of His devotee.
text:
> yadyapi vṛndāvana-tyāge nāhi prabhura mana
> bhakta-icchā pūrite kahe madhura vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:t:tyāge]]---to leave Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---was not the desire of the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---of the devotee; [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---desire; [[synonyms:p:pūrite]]---to fulfill; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:m:madhura]] [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---sweet words.
translation: Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had no desire to leave Vṛndāvana, He began to speak sweet words just to fulfill the desire of His devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.153
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "You have brought Me here to show Me Vṛndāvana. I am very much indebted to you, and I shall not be able to repay this debt.
text:
> "tumi āmāya āni' dekhāilā vṛndāvana
> ei 'ṛṇa' āmi nāriba karite śodhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:ā:āmāya]]---Me; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:d:dekhāilā]]---showed; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---the holy place named Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṇa]]---this debt; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:n:nāriba]]---I shall not be able; [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:ś:śodhana]]---to repay.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "You have brought Me here to show Me Vṛndāvana. I am very much indebted to you, and I shall not be able to repay this debt.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.154
description: "Whatever you desire, I must do. Wherever you take Me, I shall go."
text:
> ye tomāra icchā, āmi seita kariba
> yāhāṅ lañā yāha tumi, tāhāṅi yāiba"
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---whatever You like; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:s:seita]] [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---must act accordingly; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:l:lañā]] [[synonyms:y:yāha]]---take; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅi]] [[synonyms:y:yāiba]]---I shall go there.
translation: "Whatever you desire, I must do. Wherever you take Me, I shall go."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.155
description: The next morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu got up early. After taking His bath, He became ecstatic with love, knowing that He now had to leave Vṛndāvana.
text:
> prātaḥ-kāle mahāprabhu prātaḥ-snāna kaila
> 'vṛndāvana chāḍiba' jāni' premāveśa haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---took His morning bath; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍiba]]---I shall have to leave Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---knowing; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became ecstatic in love.
translation: The next morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu got up early. After taking His bath, He became ecstatic with love, knowing that He now had to leave Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.156
description: Although the Lord did not exhibit any external symptoms, His mind was filled with ecstatic love. At that time, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Let us go to Mahāvana [Gokula]."
text:
> bāhya vikāra nāhi, premāviṣṭa mana
> bhaṭṭācārya kahe,---cala, yāi mahāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---external; [[synonyms:v:vikāra]]---symptoms; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there were not; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind was full of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:c:cala]]---let us go; [[synonyms:y:yāi]] [[synonyms:m:mahāvana]]---let us go to Mahāvana.
translation: Although the Lord did not exhibit any external symptoms, His mind was filled with ecstatic love. At that time, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Let us go to Mahāvana [Gokula]."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.157
description: Saying this, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya made Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sit aboard a boat. After they crossed the river, he took the Lord with him.
text:
> eta bali' mahāprabhure naukāya vasāñā
> pāra kari' bhaṭṭācārya calilā lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:naukāya]]---on a boat; [[synonyms:v:vasāñā]]---making sit down; [[synonyms:p:pāra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---crossing the river; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking.
translation: Saying this, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya made Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sit aboard a boat. After they crossed the river, he took the Lord with him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.158
description: Both Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa and the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa knew the path along the Ganges bank very well.
text:
> premī kṛṣṇadāsa, āra seita brāhmaṇa
> gaṅgā-tīra-pathe yāibāra vijña dui-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:premī]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---the devotee Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:s:seita]] [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---that Sanoḍiyā //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:t:tīra]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the path by the bank of the Ganges; [[synonyms:y:yāibāra]]---to go; [[synonyms:v:vijña]]---experienced; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons.
translation: Both Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa and the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa knew the path along the Ganges bank very well.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.159
description: While walking, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, understanding that the others were fatigued, took them all beneath a tree and sat down.
text:
> yāite eka vṛkṣa-tale prabhu sabā lañā
> vasilā, sabāra patha-śrānti dekhiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---while passing; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:t:tale]]---underneath a tree; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sabā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking all of them; [[synonyms:v:vasilā]]---sat down; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:p:patha]]-[[synonyms:ś:śrānti]]---fatigue because of walking; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---understanding.
translation: While walking, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, understanding that the others were fatigued, took them all beneath a tree and sat down.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.16
description: When the Lord saw Govardhana Hill, He immediately offered obeisances, falling down on the ground like a rod. He embraced one piece of rock from Govardhana Hill and became mad.
text:
> govardhana dekhi' prabhu ha-ilā daṇḍavat
> 'eka śilā' āliṅgiyā ha-ilā unmatta
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:govardhana]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Govardhana Hill; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]] [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]]---offered obeisances like a straight rod; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:ś:śilā]]---one piece of stone; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgiyā]]---embracing; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:u:unmatta]]---maddened.
translation: When the Lord saw Govardhana Hill, He immediately offered obeisances, falling down on the ground like a rod. He embraced one piece of rock from Govardhana Hill and became mad.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.160
description: There were many cows grazing near that tree, and the Lord was very pleased to see them.
text:
> sei vṛkṣa-nikaṭe care bahu gābhī-gaṇa
> tāhā dekhi' mahāprabhura ullasita mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:n:nikaṭe]]---near the tree; [[synonyms:c:care]]---were grazing; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---many; [[synonyms:g:gābhī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---cows; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:u:ullasita]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind became very pleased.
translation: There were many cows grazing near that tree, and the Lord was very pleased to see them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.161
description: Suddenly a cowherd boy blew on his flute, and immediately the Lord was struck with ecstatic love.
text:
> ācambite eka gopa vaṁśī bājāila
> śuni' mahāprabhura mahā-premāveśa haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācambite]]---suddenly; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:g:gopa]]---one cowherd boy; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]---flute; [[synonyms:b:bājāila]]---blew; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---absorption in great ecstatic love; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was.
translation: Suddenly a cowherd boy blew on his flute, and immediately the Lord was struck with ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.162
description: Filled with ecstatic love, the Lord fell unconscious to the ground. He foamed about the mouth, and His breathing stopped.
text:
> acetana hañā prabhu bhūmite paḍilā
> mukhe phenā paḍe, nāsāya śvāsa ruddha hailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:acetana]]---unconscious; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]] [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell on the ground; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---at the mouth; [[synonyms:p:phenā]] [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---there was foam; [[synonyms:n:nāsāya]]---in the nostrils; [[synonyms:ś:śvāsa]]---breath; [[synonyms:r:ruddha]] [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---stopped.
translation: Filled with ecstatic love, the Lord fell unconscious to the ground. He foamed about the mouth, and His breathing stopped.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.163
description: While the Lord was unconscious, ten cavalry soldiers belonging to the Mohammedan Pāṭhāna military order rode up and dismounted.
text:
> hena-kāle tāhāṅ āśoyāra daśa āilā
> mleccha-pāṭhāna ghoḍā haite uttarilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---just at this time; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:ā:āśoyāra]]---soldiers; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]---ten; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]---Mohammedans; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāna]]---the race of Pāṭhānas; [[synonyms:g:ghoḍā]]---horses; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:u:uttarilā]]---got down.
translation: While the Lord was unconscious, ten cavalry soldiers belonging to the Mohammedan Pāṭhāna military order rode up and dismounted.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.164
description: Seeing the Lord unconscious, the soldiers thought, "This sannyāsī must have possessed a large quantity of gold.
text:
> prabhure dekhiyā mleccha karaye vicāra
> ei yati-pāśa chila suvarṇa apāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]---the Mohammedans; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---considered; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:y:yati]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---within the possession of this //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:c:chila]]---there was; [[synonyms:s:suvarṇa]] [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---a large quantity of gold.
translation: Seeing the Lord unconscious, the soldiers thought, "This sannyāsī must have possessed a large quantity of gold.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.165
description: "These four rogues here must have taken away that sannyāsī's riches after killing Him by making Him take the poison dhuturā."
text:
> ei cāri bāṭoyāra dhuturā khāoyāñā
> māri' ḍāriyāche, yatira saba dhana lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---four; [[synonyms:b:bāṭoyāra]]---rogues; [[synonyms:d:dhuturā]]---//dhuturā//; [[synonyms:k:khāoyāñā]]---making Him eat; [[synonyms:m:māri']] [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍāriyāche]]---killed; [[synonyms:y:yatira]]---of the //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---wealth; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking away.
translation: "These four rogues here must have taken away that sannyāsī's riches after killing Him by making Him take the poison dhuturā."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.166
description: Thinking this, the Pāṭhāna soldiers arrested the four persons and decided to kill them. Because of this, the two Bengalis began to tremble.
text:
> tabe sei pāṭhāna cāri-janere bāṅdhila
> kāṭite cāhe, gauḍiyā saba kāṅpite lāgila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāna]]---the Pāṭhāna soldiers; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:j:janere]]---the four persons; [[synonyms:b:bāṅdhila]]---arrested; [[synonyms:k:kāṭite]] [[synonyms:c:cāhe]]---wanted to kill them; [[synonyms:g:gauḍiyā]]---the Bengalis; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kāṅpite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began to tremble.
translation: Thinking this, the Pāṭhāna soldiers arrested the four persons and decided to kill them. Because of this, the two Bengalis began to tremble.
purport: The four persons were Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya, his assistant //brāhmaṇa,// Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa and the Sanoḍiyā //brāhmaṇa// devotee of Mādhavendra Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.167
description: The devotee Kṛṣṇadāsa, who belonged to the Rājaputa race, was very fearless. The Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa was also fearless, and he spoke very bravely.
text:
> kṛṣṇadāsa---rājaputa, nirbhaya se baḍa
> sei vipra---nirbhaya, se---mukhe baḍa daḍa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:r:rājaputa]]---belonging to the Rājaputa race; [[synonyms:n:nirbhaya]]---fearless; [[synonyms:s:se]]---he; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the Sanoḍiyā //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:n:nirbhaya]]---also fearless; [[synonyms:s:se]]---he; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the mouth; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:d:daḍa]]---very brave.
translation: The devotee Kṛṣṇadāsa, who belonged to the Rājaputa race, was very fearless. The Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa was also fearless, and he spoke very bravely.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.168
description: The brāhmaṇa said, "You Pāṭhāna soldiers are all under the protection of your king. Let us go to your commander and get his decision.
text:
> vipra kahe,---pāṭhāna, tomāra pātsāra dohāi
> cala tumi āmi sikdāra-pāśa yāi
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the //brāhmaṇa// said; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāna]]---you Pāṭhāna soldiers; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:p:pātsāra]]---king; [[synonyms:d:dohāi]]---under the protection of; [[synonyms:c:cala]]---let us go; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---we; [[synonyms:s:sikdāra]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---to the commander; [[synonyms:y:yāi]]---let us go.
translation: The brāhmaṇa said, "You Pāṭhāna soldiers are all under the protection of your king. Let us go to your commander and get his decision.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.169
description: "This sannyāsī is my spiritual master, and I am from Mathurā. I am a brāhmaṇa, and I know many people who are in the service of the Mohammedan king.
text:
> ei yati---āmāra guru, āmi---māthura brāhmaṇa
> pātsāra āge āche mora 'śata jana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:y:yati]]---this //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:g:guru]]---my spiritual master; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:m:māthura]] [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---a //brāhmaṇa// from Mathurā; [[synonyms:p:pātsāra]] [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in the service of the Mohammedan king; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there are; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---one hundred persons.
translation: "This sannyāsī is my spiritual master, and I am from Mathurā. I am a brāhmaṇa, and I know many people who are in the service of the Mohammedan king.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.17
description: Mad with ecstatic love, the Lord came to the village known as Govardhana. It was there that He saw the Deity Harideva and offered His obeisances unto Him.
text:
> preme matta cali' āilā govardhana-grāma
> 'harideva' dekhi' tāhāṅ ha-ilā praṇāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:m:matta]]---maddened; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---proceeding; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]-[[synonyms:g:grāma]]---to the village known as Govardhana; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:deva]]---the Deity named Harideva installed there; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]] [[synonyms:p:praṇāma]]---offered obeisances.
translation: Mad with ecstatic love, the Lord came to the village known as Govardhana. It was there that He saw the Deity Harideva and offered His obeisances unto Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.170
description: "This sannyāsī sometimes falls unconscious due to the influence of a disease. Please sit down here, and you will see that He will very soon regain consciousness and His normal condition.
text:
> ei yati vyādhite kabhu hayena mūrcchita
> abaṅhi cetana pāibe, ha-ibe samvita
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:y:yati]]---this //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:v:vyādhite]]---under the influence of disease; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:h:hayena]] [[synonyms:m:mūrcchita]]---becomes unconscious; [[synonyms:a:abaṅhi]]---very soon; [[synonyms:c:cetana]]---consciousness; [[synonyms:p:pāibe]]---will get back; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ibe]] [[synonyms:s:samvita]]---will come to His proper senses.
