translation: "This sannyāsī sometimes falls unconscious due to the influence of a disease. Please sit down here, and you will see that He will very soon regain consciousness and His normal condition.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.171
description: "Sit down here for a while and keep us all under arrest. When the sannyāsī regains his senses, you can question Him. Then, if you like, you can kill us all."
text:
> kṣaṇeka ihāṅ vaisa, bāndhi' rākhaha sabāre
> iṅhāke puchiyā, tabe māriha sabāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇeka]]---for some time; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]] [[synonyms:v:vaisa]]---sit down here; [[synonyms:b:bāndhi']]---arresting; [[synonyms:r:rākhaha]]---keep; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---all of us; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāke]] [[synonyms:p:puchiyā]]---after questioning Him; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:m:māriha]] [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---you can kill all of us.
translation: "Sit down here for a while and keep us all under arrest. When the sannyāsī regains his senses, you can question Him. Then, if you like, you can kill us all."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.172
description: The Pāṭhāna soldiers said, "You are all rogues. Two of you belong to the district of Mathurā, and the other two, who are trembling, belong to Bengal."
text:
> pāṭhāna kahe,---tumi paścimā māthura dui-jana
> 'gauḍiyā' ṭhak ei kāṅpe dui-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāna]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the soldiers said; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:p:paścimā]]---western Indians; [[synonyms:m:māthura]]---belonging to the district of Mathurā; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---two of you; [[synonyms:g:gauḍiyā]]---Bengalis; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhak]]---rogues; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:k:kāṅpe]]---are trembling; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons.
translation: The Pāṭhāna soldiers said, "You are all rogues. Two of you belong to the district of Mathurā, and the other two, who are trembling, belong to Bengal."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.173
description: Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa said, "I have my home here, and I also have about two hundred Turkish soldiers and about one hundred cannons.
text:
> kṛṣṇadāsa kahe,---āmāra ghara ei grāme
> dui-śata turkī āche, śateka kāmāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa said; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:g:ghara]]---my home; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in this village; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:t:turkī]]---two hundred Turks; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---I have; [[synonyms:ś:śateka]] [[synonyms:k:kāmāne]]---one hundred cannons.
translation: Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa said, "I have my home here, and I also have about two hundred Turkish soldiers and about one hundred cannons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.174
description: "If I call loudly, they will come immediately to kill you and plunder your horses and saddles.
text:
> ekhani āsibe saba, āmi yadi phukāri
> ghoḍā-piḍā luṭi' labe tomā-sabā māri'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ekhani]]---immediately; [[synonyms:ā:āsibe]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of them will come; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:p:phu]]-[[synonyms:k:kāri]]---call loudly; [[synonyms:g:ghoḍā]]-[[synonyms:p:piḍā]]---horses and their saddles; [[synonyms:l:luṭi']]---plundering; [[synonyms:l:labe]]---will take; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabā]] [[synonyms:m:māri']]---after killing all of you.
translation: "If I call loudly, they will come immediately to kill you and plunder your horses and saddles.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.175
description: "The Bengali pilgrims are not rogues. You are rogues, for you want to kill the pilgrims and plunder them."
text:
> gauḍiyā---'bāṭapāḍa' nahe, tumi---'bāṭapāḍa'
> tīrtha-vāsī luṭha', āra cāha' māribāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍiyā]]---the Bengalis; [[synonyms:b:bāṭapāḍa]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---are not rogues; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:b:bāṭapāḍa]]---rogues; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---persons visiting places of pilgrimage; [[synonyms:l:luṭha']]---you plunder; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:c:cāha']]---you want; [[synonyms:m:māribāra]]---to kill.
translation: "The Bengali pilgrims are not rogues. You are rogues, for you want to kill the pilgrims and plunder them."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.176
description: Upon hearing this challenge, the Pāṭhāna soldiers became hesitant. Then suddenly Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu regained consciousness.
text:
> śuniyā pāṭhāna mane saṅkoca ha-ila
> hena-kāle mahāprabhu 'caitanya' pāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāna]]---the Mohammedan soldiers; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:s:saṅkoca]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was a little hesitation; [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]] [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---came to his senses.
translation: Upon hearing this challenge, the Pāṭhāna soldiers became hesitant. Then suddenly Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu regained consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.177
description: Coming to His senses, the Lord very loudly began chanting the holy name, "Hari! Hari!" The Lord raised His arms upward and began to dance in ecstatic love.
text:
> huṅkāra kariyā uṭhe, bale 'hari' 'hari'
> premāveśe nṛtya kare ūrdhva-bāhu kari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:huṅ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāra]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---resounded very loudly; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---stands up; [[synonyms:b:bale]] [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---chants Hari, Hari; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---dances; [[synonyms:ū:ūrdhva]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhu]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---raising his arms upward.
translation: Coming to His senses, the Lord very loudly began chanting the holy name, "Hari! Hari!" The Lord raised His arms upward and began to dance in ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.178
description: When the Lord shouted very loudly in ecstatic love, it appeared to the Mohammedan soldiers that their hearts were struck by thunderbolts.
text:
> premāveśe prabhu yabe karena citkāra
> mlecchera hṛdaye yena lāge śeladhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:c:citkāra]]---loudly shouts; [[synonyms:m:mlecchera]] [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---in the hearts of the Mohammedan soldiers; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:l:lāge]]---strikes; [[synonyms:ś:śela]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---a thunderbolt.
translation: When the Lord shouted very loudly in ecstatic love, it appeared to the Mohammedan soldiers that their hearts were struck by thunderbolts.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.179
description: Seized by fear, all the Pāṭhāna soldiers immediately released the four persons. Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not see His personal associates arrested.
text:
> bhaya pāñā mleccha chāḍi' dila cāri-jana
> prabhu nā dekhila nija-gaṇera bandhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaya]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---being afraid; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]---the Mohammedans; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---released; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---the four persons; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---did not see; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of His personal associates; [[synonyms:b:bandhana]]---the arrest.
translation: Seized by fear, all the Pāṭhāna soldiers immediately released the four persons. Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not see His personal associates arrested.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.18
description: Harideva is an incarnation of Nārāyaṇa, and His residence is on the western petal of the lotus of Mathurā.
text:
> 'mathurā'-padmera paścima-dale yāṅra vāsa
> 'harideva' nārāyaṇa---ādi parakāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mathurā]]-[[synonyms:p:padmera]]---of the lotus flower of Mathurā; [[synonyms:p:paścima]]-[[synonyms:d:dale]]---on the western petal; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---residence; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:deva]]---Lord Harideva; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---incarnation of Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---original; [[synonyms:p:parakāśa]]---manifestation.
translation: Harideva is an incarnation of Nārāyaṇa, and His residence is on the western petal of the lotus of Mathurā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.180
description: At that time, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya went to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and made Him sit down. Seeing the Mohammedan soldiers, the Lord regained His normal senses.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya āsi' prabhure dhari' vasāila
> mleccha-gaṇa dekhi' mahāprabhura 'bāhya' haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---immediately coming near; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---taking; [[synonyms:v:vasāila]]---made to sit; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the Mohammedan soldiers; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---external consciousness; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was.
translation: At that time, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya went to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and made Him sit down. Seeing the Mohammedan soldiers, the Lord regained His normal senses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.181
description: All the Mohammedan soldiers then came before the Lord, worshiped His lotus feet and said, "Here are four rogues.
text:
> mleccha-gaṇa āsi' prabhura vandila caraṇa
> prabhu-āge kahe,---ei ṭhak cāri-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the Mohammedan soldiers; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---after coming there; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vandila]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---worshiped the lotus feet; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said before the Lord; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhak]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---these four persons are rogues.
translation: All the Mohammedan soldiers then came before the Lord, worshiped His lotus feet and said, "Here are four rogues.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.182
description: "These rogues have made You take dhuturā. Having made You mad, they have taken all Your possessions."
text:
> ei cāri mili' tomāya dhuturā khāoyāñā
> tomāra dhana laila tomāya pāgala kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:m:mili']]---four rogues together; [[synonyms:t:tomāya]]---You; [[synonyms:d:dhuturā]] [[synonyms:k:khāoyāñā]]---making to drink poison; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---wealth; [[synonyms:l:laila]]---took away; [[synonyms:t:tomāya]]---You; [[synonyms:p:pāgala]]---intoxicated; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---making.
translation: "These rogues have made You take dhuturā. Having made You mad, they have taken all Your possessions."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.183
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "These are not rogues. They are My associates. Being a sannyāsī beggar, I do not possess anything.
text:
> prabhu kahena,---ṭhak nahe, mora 'saṅgī' jana
> bhikṣuka sannyāsī, mora nāhi kichu dhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhak]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---they are not rogues; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:s:saṅgī]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---My associates; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣuka]]---beggar; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---//sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---are not; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---any; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---riches.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "These are not rogues. They are My associates. Being a sannyāsī beggar, I do not possess anything.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.184
description: "Due to epilepsy, I sometimes fall unconscious. Out of their mercy, these four men maintain Me."
text:
> mṛgī-vyādhite āmi kabhu ha-i acetana
> ei cāri dayā kari' karena pālana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mṛgī]]-[[synonyms:v:vyādhite]]---due to epilepsy; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---become; [[synonyms:a:acetana]]---unconscious; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---these four men; [[synonyms:d:dayā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---being merciful; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:p:pālana]]---maintain Me.
translation: "Due to epilepsy, I sometimes fall unconscious. Out of their mercy, these four men maintain Me."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.185
description: Among the Mohammedans was a grave person who was wearing a black dress. People called him a saintly person.
text:
> sei mleccha-madhye eka parama gambhīra
> kāla vastra pare sei,---loke kahe 'pīra'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---among those Mohammedans; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:g:gambhīra]]---very grave; [[synonyms:k:kāla]] [[synonyms:v:vastra]]---black garments; [[synonyms:p:pare]] [[synonyms:s:sei]]---he wears; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---people; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---call; [[synonyms:p:pīra]]---a saintly person.
translation: Among the Mohammedans was a grave person who was wearing a black dress. People called him a saintly person.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.186
description: The heart of that saintly person softened upon seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He wanted to talk to Him and establish impersonal Brahman on the basis of his own scripture, the Koran.
text:
> citta ārdra haila tāṅra prabhure dekhiyā
> 'nirviśeṣa-brahma' sthāpe svaśāstra uṭhāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:citta]]---heart; [[synonyms:ā:ārdra]]---softened; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nirviśeṣa]]-[[synonyms:b:brahma]]---impersonal Brahman; [[synonyms:s:sthāpe]]---wanted to establish; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstra]] [[synonyms:u:uṭhāñā]]---raising his scripture.
translation: The heart of that saintly person softened upon seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He wanted to talk to Him and establish impersonal Brahman on the basis of his own scripture, the Koran.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.187
description: When that person established the impersonal Brahman conception of the Absolute Truth on the basis of the Koran, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu refuted his argument.
text:
> 'advaita-brahma-vāda' sei karila sthāpana
> tāra śāstra-yuktye tāre prabhu kailā khaṇḍana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:v:vāda]]---the impersonal Brahman conception; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that saintly person; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:s:sthāpana]]---established; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:y:yuktye]]---on the logic of his scripture; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍana]]---refutation.
translation: When that person established the impersonal Brahman conception of the Absolute Truth on the basis of the Koran, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu refuted his argument.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.188
description: Whatever arguments he put forward, the Lord refuted them all. Finally the person became stunned and could not speak.
text:
> yei yei kahila, prabhu sakali khaṇḍila
> uttara nā āise mukhe, mahā-stabdha haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---whatever he spoke; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sakali]] [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍila]]---refuted everything; [[synonyms:u:uttara]]---answer; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---could not come; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in his mouth; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:s:stabdha]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---he became greatly stunned.
translation: Whatever arguments he put forward, the Lord refuted them all. Finally the person became stunned and could not speak.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.189
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "The Koran has certainly established impersonalism, but at the end it refutes that impersonalism and establishes the personal God.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---tomāra śāstra sthāpe 'nirviśeṣe'
> tāhā khaṇḍi' 'saviśeṣa' sthāpiyāche śeṣe
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued to speak; [[synonyms:t:tomāraśāstra]]---your scripture (the Koran); [[synonyms:s:sthāpe]]---establishes; [[synonyms:n:nirviśeṣe]]---impersonalism; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍi']]---refuting that; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:v:viśeṣa]]---personal God; [[synonyms:s:sthāpiyāche]]---established; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---at the end.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "The Koran has certainly established impersonalism, but at the end it refutes that impersonalism and establishes the personal God.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.19
description: Mad with ecstatic love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to dance before the Harideva Deity. Hearing of the Lord's wonderful activities, all the people came to see Him.
text:
> harideva-āge nāce preme matta hañā
> saba loka dekhite āila āścarya śuniyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of Harideva; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:m:matta]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming maddened; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:ā:āścarya]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing.
translation: Mad with ecstatic love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to dance before the Harideva Deity. Hearing of the Lord's wonderful activities, all the people came to see Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.190
description: "The Koran accepts the fact that ultimately there is only one God. He is full of opulence, and His bodily complexion is blackish.
text:
> tomāra śāstre kahe śeṣe 'eka-i īśvara'
> 'sarvaiśvarya-pūrṇa teṅho---śyāma-kalevara
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śāstre]]---in your scripture; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it says; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---at the end; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:i:i]] [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---there is one God; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]-[[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---full of all opulence; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:ś:śyāma]]-[[synonyms:k:kalevara]]---bodily complexion is blackish.
translation: "The Koran accepts the fact that ultimately there is only one God. He is full of opulence, and His bodily complexion is blackish.
purport: The revealed scripture of the Mohammedans is the Koran. There is one Mohammedan //sampradāya// known as the Sufis. The Sufis accept impersonalism, believing in the oneness of the living entity with the Absolute Truth. Their supreme slogan is //"analahak.//" he Sufi //sampradāya// was certainly derived from Śaṅkarācārya's impersonalists.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.191
description: "According to the Koran, the Lord has a supreme, blissful, transcendental body. He is the Absolute Truth, the all-pervading, omniscient and eternal being. He is the origin of everything.
text:
> sac-cid-ānanda-deha, pūrṇa-brahma-svarūpa
> 'sarvātmā', 'sarvajña', nitya sarvādi-svarūpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:d:deha]]---transcendental, blissful, spiritual body; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---the identification of the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---all-pervading; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:j:jña]]---omniscient; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---eternal; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the origin of everything; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---the real form of the Lord.
translation: "According to the Koran, the Lord has a supreme, blissful, transcendental body. He is the Absolute Truth, the all-pervading, omniscient and eternal being. He is the origin of everything.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.192
description: "Creation, maintenance and dissolution come from Him. He is the original shelter of all gross and subtle cosmic manifestations.
text:
> sṛṣṭi, sthiti, pralaya tāṅhā haite haya
> sthūla-sūkṣma-jagatera teṅho samāśraya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]---creation; [[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---maintenance; [[synonyms:p:pralaya]]---dissolution; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhā]]---Him; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes possible; [[synonyms:s:sthūla]]---gross; [[synonyms:s:sūkṣma]]---subtle; [[synonyms:j:jagatera]]---of the cosmic manifestation; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:s:samāśraya]]---the only shelter.
translation: "Creation, maintenance and dissolution come from Him. He is the original shelter of all gross and subtle cosmic manifestations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.193
description: "The Lord is the Supreme Truth worshipable by everyone. He is the cause of all causes. By engaging in His devotional service, the living entity is relieved from material existence.
text:
> sarva-śreṣṭha, sarvārādhya, kāraṇera kāraṇa
> tāṅra bhaktye haya jīvera saṁsāra-tāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śreṣṭha]]---the Supreme Truth; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārādhya]]---worshipable by everyone; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇera]] [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause of all causes; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:j:jīvera]]---of the living entity; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]-[[synonyms:t:tāraṇa]]---deliverance from material existence.
translation: "The Lord is the Supreme Truth worshipable by everyone. He is the cause of all causes. By engaging in His devotional service, the living entity is relieved from material existence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.194
description: "No conditioned soul can get out of material bondage without serving the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Love at His lotus feet is the ultimate goal of life.
text:
> tāṅra sevā vinā jīvera nā yāya 'saṁsāra'
> tāṅhāra caraṇe prīti---'puruṣārtha-sāra'
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---service; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:j:jīvera]]---of the conditioned soul; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---finishes; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]---material bondage; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---His; [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:p:prīti]]---love; [[synonyms:p:puruṣārtha]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the ultimate goal of life.
translation: "No conditioned soul can get out of material bondage without serving the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Love at His lotus feet is the ultimate goal of life.
purport: According to the Mohammedan scripture, without //evādat,// offering prayers at a mosque or elsewhere five times daily (//namāja//), one cannot be successful in life. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu pointed out that in the revealed scripture of the Mohammedans, love of Godhead is the ultimate goal. //Karma-yoga// and //jñāna-yoga// are certainly described in the Koran, but ultimately the Koran states that the ultimate goal is the offering of prayers to the Supreme Person (//evādat//).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.195
description: "The happiness of liberation, whereby one merges into the Lord's existence, cannot even be compared to a fragment of the transcendental bliss obtained by service unto the Lord's lotus feet.
text:
> mokṣādi ānanda yāra nahe eka 'kaṇa'
> pūrṇānanda-prāpti tāṅra caraṇa-sevana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mokṣa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---liberation and so on; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---even; [[synonyms:k:kaṇa]]---a fragment; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:p:prāpti]]---attainment of completely blissful life; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sevana]]---service to His lotus feet.
translation: "The happiness of liberation, whereby one merges into the Lord's existence, cannot even be compared to a fragment of the transcendental bliss obtained by service unto the Lord's lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.196
description: "In the Koran there are descriptions of fruitive activity, speculative knowledge, mystic power and union with the Supreme, but ultimately everything is refuted as the Lord's personal feature and His devotional service is established.
text:
> 'karma', jñāna', 'yoga' āge kariyā sthāpana
> saba khaṇḍi' sthāpe 'īśvara', 'tāṅhāra sevana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:karma]]---fruitive activities; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---speculative knowledge; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]---mystic power; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in the beginning; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:s:sthāpana]]---establishing; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍi']]---refuting everything; [[synonyms:s:sthāpe]]---establishes; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---His service.
translation: "In the Koran there are descriptions of fruitive activity, speculative knowledge, mystic power and union with the Supreme, but ultimately everything is refuted as the Lord's personal feature and His devotional service is established.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.197
description: "The scholars of the Koran are not very advanced in knowledge. Although there are many methods prescribed, they do not know that the ultimate conclusion should be considered the most powerful.
text:
> tomāra paṇḍita-sabāra nāhi śāstra-jñāna
> pūrvāpara-vidhi-madhye 'para'---balavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of the learned scholars of your community; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge of revealed scripture; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āpara]]---former and latter; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]---regulative principles; [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---among; [[synonyms:p:para]]---the conclusion at the end; [[synonyms:b:balavān]]---most powerful.
translation: "The scholars of the Koran are not very advanced in knowledge. Although there are many methods prescribed, they do not know that the ultimate conclusion should be considered the most powerful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.198
description: "Seeing your own Koran and deliberating over what is written there, what is your conclusion?"
text:
> nija-śāstra dekhi' tumi vicāra kariyā
> ki likhiyāche śeṣe kaha nirṇaya kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---your own scripture; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---deliberating; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:l:likhiyāche]]---what was written; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---at the end; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---say; [[synonyms:n:nirṇaya]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---ascertaining.
translation: "Seeing your own Koran and deliberating over what is written there, what is your conclusion?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.199
description: The saintly Mohammedan replied, "All that You have said is true. This has certainly been written in the Koran, but our scholars can neither understand nor accept it.
text:
> mleccha kahe,---yei kaha, sei 'satya' haya
> śāstre likhiyāche, keha la-ite nā pāraya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mleccha]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Mohammedan replied; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---what You say; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is true; [[synonyms:ś:śāstre]]---in the Koran; [[synonyms:l:likhiyāche]]---it has been written; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---to take; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāraya]]---is not able.
translation: The saintly Mohammedan replied, "All that You have said is true. This has certainly been written in the Koran, but our scholars can neither understand nor accept it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.2
description: All glories to Lord Gauracandra! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Prabhu! And all glories to the devotees of Lord Caitanya headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura!
text:
> jaya jaya gauracandra jaya nityānanda
> jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gauracandra]]---to Lord Gauracandra (Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu); [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---to Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---to Śrī Advaita Gosāñi; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---to the devotees of Lord Caitanya.
translation: All glories to Lord Gauracandra! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Prabhu! And all glories to the devotees of Lord Caitanya headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.20
description: The people were astonished when they saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's ecstatic love and personal beauty. The priests who served the Harideva Deity offered the Lord a good reception.
text:
> prabhu-prema-saundarya dekhi' loke camatkāra
> haridevera bhṛtya prabhura karila satkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:s:saundarya]]---ecstatic love and beauty; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---people; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonished; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:devera]]---of Lord Harideva; [[synonyms:b:bhṛtya]]---servants; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:s:satkāra]]---offered a good reception.
translation: The people were astonished when they saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's ecstatic love and personal beauty. The priests who served the Harideva Deity offered the Lord a good reception.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.200
description: "Usually they describe the Lord's impersonal aspect, but they hardly know that the Lord's personal feature is worshipable. They are undoubtedly lacking this knowledge.
text:
> 'nirviśeṣa-gosāñi' lañā karena vyākhyāna
> 'sākāra-gosāñi'---sevya, kāro nāhi jñāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirviśeṣa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead as impersonal; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:v:vyākhyāna]]---they describe; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---the personal feature of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sevya]]---worshipable; [[synonyms:k:kāro]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---no one has this knowledge.
translation: "Usually they describe the Lord's impersonal aspect, but they hardly know that the Lord's personal feature is worshipable. They are undoubtedly lacking this knowledge.
purport: The saintly Mohammedan admitted that those who were supposedly conversant in the teachings of the Koran could not ultimately understand the essence of the Koran. Because of this, they accepted only the Lord's impersonal feature. Generally they recite and explain this portion only. Although the transcendental body of the Lord is worshipable, most of them are unaware of this.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.201
description: "Since You are that very same Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself, please be merciful upon me. I am fallen and unfit.
text:
> seita 'gosāñi' tumi---sākṣāt 'īśvara'
> more kṛpā kara, muñi---ayogya pāmara
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:seita]]---that; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:m:more]]---upon me; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---kindly be merciful; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:a:ayogya]] [[synonyms:p:pāmara]]---very fallen and unfit.
translation: "Since You are that very same Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself, please be merciful upon me. I am fallen and unfit.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.202
description: "I have studied the Mohammedan scripture very extensively, but from it I cannot conclusively decide what the ultimate goal of life is or how I can approach it.
text:
> aneka dekhinu muñi mleccha-śāstra haite
> 'sādhya-sādhana-vastu' nāri nirdhārite
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aneka]]---many; [[synonyms:d:dekhinu]]---have studied; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---Mohammedan scripture; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:s:sādhya]]---the ultimate goal of life; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---how to approach it; [[synonyms:v:vastu]]---matter; [[synonyms:n:nāri]] [[synonyms:n:nirdhārite]]---I cannot decide conclusively.
translation: "I have studied the Mohammedan scripture very extensively, but from it I cannot conclusively decide what the ultimate goal of life is or how I can approach it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.203
description: "Now that I have seen You, my tongue is chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā mantra. The false prestige I felt from being a learned scholar is now gone."
text:
> tomā dekhi' jihvā mora bale 'kṛṣṇa-nāma'
> 'āmi---baḍa jñānī'---ei gela ābhimāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---by seeing You; [[synonyms:j:jihvā]]---tongue; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:b:bale]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---chants the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra//; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:j:jñānī]]---very learned scholar; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:g:gela]] [[synonyms:ā:ābhimāna]]---false prestige has gone away.
translation: "Now that I have seen You, my tongue is chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā mantra. The false prestige I felt from being a learned scholar is now gone."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.204
description: Saying this, the saintly Mohammedan fell at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and requested Him to speak of life's ultimate goal and the process by which it could be obtained.
text:
> kṛpā kari' bala more 'sādhya-sādhane'
> eta bali' paḍe mahāprabhura caraṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---by Your causeless mercy; [[synonyms:b:bala]]---speak; [[synonyms:m:more]]---to me; [[synonyms:s:sādhya]]-[[synonyms:s:sādhane]]---the ultimate object of life and the process to achieve it; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---falls down; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Saying this, the saintly Mohammedan fell at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and requested Him to speak of life's ultimate goal and the process by which it could be obtained.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.205
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Please get up. You have chanted the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; therefore the sinful reactions you have accrued for many millions of lives are now gone. You are now pure."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---uṭha, kṛṣṇa-nāma tumi la-ilā
> koṭi-janmera pāpa gela, 'pavitra' ha-ilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:u:uṭha]]---please get up; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---have taken; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:j:janmera]]---of many millions of births; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]] [[synonyms:g:gela]]---your sinful reactions have gone; [[synonyms:p:pavitra]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---you have become pure.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Please get up. You have chanted the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; therefore the sinful reactions you have accrued for many millions of lives are now gone. You are now pure."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.206
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then told all the Mohammedans there, "Chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa! Chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa!" As they all began to chant, they were overwhelmed by ecstatic love.
text:
> 'kṛṣṇa' kaha, 'kṛṣṇa' kaha,---kailā upadeśa
> sabe'kṛṣṇa' kahe, sabāra haila premāveśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---just chant "Kṛṣṇa"; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---just chant "Kṛṣṇa"; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:u:upadeśa]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu instructed; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---ecstatic love.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then told all the Mohammedans there, "Chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa! Chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa!" As they all began to chant, they were overwhelmed by ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.207
description: In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu indirectly initiated the saintly Mohammedan by advising him to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. The Mohammedan's name was changed to Rāmadāsa. There was also another Pāṭhāna Moslem present whose name was Vijulī Khān.
text:
> 'rāmadāsa' bali' prabhu tāṅra kaila nāma
> āra eka pāṭhāna, tāṅra nāma---'vijulī-khāṅna'
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāmadāsa]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---of the name Rāmadāsa; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---name; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāna]]---another Mohammedan; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---his name; [[synonyms:v:vijulī]]-[[synonyms:k:khāṅna]]---Vijulī Khān.
translation: In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu indirectly initiated the saintly Mohammedan by advising him to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. The Mohammedan's name was changed to Rāmadāsa. There was also another Pāṭhāna Moslem present whose name was Vijulī Khān.
purport: After being initiated, the devotees in the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement change their names. Whenever a person in the Western world becomes interested in this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, he is initiated by this process. In India we are falsely accused of converting //mlecchas// and //yavanas// into the Hindu religion. In India there are many Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// known as //jagad-guru,// although they have hardly visited the whole world. Some are not even sufficiently educated, yet they make accusations against our movement and accuse us of destroying the principles of the Hindu religion by accepting Mohammedans and //yavanas// as Vaiṣṇavas. Such people are simply envious. We are not spoiling the Hindu system of religion but are simply following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by traveling all over the world and accepting those who are interested in understanding Kṛṣṇa as Kṛṣṇadāsa or Rāmadāsa. By the process of a bona fide initiation, their names are changed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.208
description: Vijulī Khān was very young, and he was the son of the king. All the other Mohammedans, Pāṭhānas, headed by Rāmadāsa, were his servants.
text:
> alpa vayasa tāṅra, rājāra kumāra
> 'rāmadāsa' ādi pāṭhāna---cākara tāṅhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:alpa]] [[synonyms:v:vayasa]] [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his age is very young; [[synonyms:r:rājāra]] [[synonyms:k:kumāra]]---son of the king; [[synonyms:r:rāmadāsa]]---Rāmadāsa; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---heading the list; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāna]]---the Mohammedans; [[synonyms:c:cākara]] [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---servants of him.
translation: Vijulī Khān was very young, and he was the son of the king. All the other Mohammedans, Pāṭhānas, headed by Rāmadāsa, were his servants.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.209
description: Vijulī Khān also fell down at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the Lord placed His foot on his head.
text:
> 'kṛṣṇa' bali' paḍe sei mahāprabhura pāya
> prabhu śrī-caraṇa dila tāṅhāra māthāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---falls down; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that Vijulī Khān; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---placed His foot; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:m:māthāya]]---on his head.
translation: Vijulī Khān also fell down at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the Lord placed His foot on his head.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.21
description: At Brahma-kuṇḍa, Bhaṭṭācārya cooked food, and the Lord, after taking His bath at Brahma-kuṇḍa, accepted His lunch.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya 'brahma-kuṇḍe' pāka yāñā kaila
> brahma-kuṇḍe snāna kari' prabhu bhikṣā kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṇḍe]]---at the lake called Brahma-kuṇḍa; [[synonyms:p:pāka]]---cooking; [[synonyms:y:yāñā]]---going there; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---peformed; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṇḍe]]---at Brahma-kuṇḍa; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking a bath; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---accepted lunch.
translation: At Brahma-kuṇḍa, Bhaṭṭācārya cooked food, and the Lord, after taking His bath at Brahma-kuṇḍa, accepted His lunch.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.210
description: Bestowing His mercy upon them in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu left. All the Pāṭhāna Mohammedans then became mendicants.
text:
> tāṅ-sabāre kṛpā kari' prabhu ta' calilā
> seita pāṭhāna saba 'vairāgī' ha-ilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅ]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---to all of them; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---bestowing mercy; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---departed; [[synonyms:s:seita]]---they; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāna]]---the Mohammedans of the Pāṭhāna community; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vairāgī]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became mendicants.
translation: Bestowing His mercy upon them in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu left. All the Pāṭhāna Mohammedans then became mendicants.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.211
description: Later these very Pāṭhānas became celebrated as the Pāṭhāna Vaiṣṇavas. They toured all over the country and chanted the glorious activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> pāṭhāna-vaiṣṇava bali' haila tāṅra khyāti
> sarvatra gāhiyā bule mahāprabhura kīrti
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāna]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---known as Pāṭhāna Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---their; [[synonyms:k:khyāti]]---reputation; [[synonyms:s:sarvatra]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:g:gāhiyā]] [[synonyms:b:bule]]---travel while chanting; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kīrti]]---glorious activities.
translation: Later these very Pāṭhānas became celebrated as the Pāṭhāna Vaiṣṇavas. They toured all over the country and chanted the glorious activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.212
description: Vijulī Khān became a greatly advanced devotee, and his importance was celebrated at every holy place of pilgrimage.
text:
> sei vijulī-khāṅna haila 'mahā-bhāgavata'
> sarva-tīrthe haila tāṅra parama-mahattva
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vijulī]]-[[synonyms:k:khāṅna]]---Vijulī Khān; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]---most advanced devotee; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrthe]]---in all places of pilgrimage; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---great; [[synonyms:m:mahattva]]---importance.
translation: Vijulī Khān became a greatly advanced devotee, and his importance was celebrated at every holy place of pilgrimage.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.213
description: In this way Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed His pastimes. Coming to the western part of India, He bestowed good fortune upon the yavanas and mlecchas.
text:
> aiche līlā kare prabhu śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya
> 'paścime' āsiyā kaila yavanādi dhanya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performed; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:paścime]]---to the western part of India; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:y:yavana]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---meat-eaters and others; [[synonyms:d:dhanya]]---fortunate.
translation: In this way Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed His pastimes. Coming to the western part of India, He bestowed good fortune upon the yavanas and mlecchas.
purport: The word //yavana// means "meat-eater." Anyone from a meat-eating community is called a //yavana.// One who does not strictly observe the Vedic regulative principles is called a //mleccha.// These words do not refer to any particular man. Even if a person is born in a //brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya// or //śūdra// family, he is a //mleccha// or //yavana// if he does not strictly follow the regulative principles or if he eats meat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.214
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu next went to a holy place of pilgrimage called Soro-kṣetra. He took His bath in the Ganges there and started for Prayāga on the path along the banks of the Ganges.
text:
> soro-kṣetre āsi' prabhu kailā gaṅgā-snāna
> gaṅgā-tīra-pathe kailā prayāge prayāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:soro]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣetre]]---to Soro-kṣetra; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing in the Ganges; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:t:tīra]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the path on the bank of the Ganges; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prayāge]] [[synonyms:p:prayāṇa]]---departure for Prayāga.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu next went to a holy place of pilgrimage called Soro-kṣetra. He took His bath in the Ganges there and started for Prayāga on the path along the banks of the Ganges.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.215
description: At Soro-kṣetra, the Lord requested the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa and Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa to return home, but with folded hands they began to speak as follows.
text:
> sei vipre, kṛṣṇadāse, prabhu vidāya dilā
> yoḍa-hāte dui-jana kahite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipre]]---to the Sanoḍiyā //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāse]]---and the Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vidāya]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---asked to go back; [[synonyms:y:yoḍa]]-[[synonyms:h:hāte]]---with folded hands; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons; [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to say.
translation: At Soro-kṣetra, the Lord requested the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa and Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa to return home, but with folded hands they began to speak as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.216
description: They prayed, "Let us go to Prayāga with You. If we do not go, when shall we again get the association of Your lotus feet?
text:
> prayāga-paryanta duṅhe tomā-saṅge yāba
> tomāra caraṇa-saṅga punaḥ kāhāṅ pāba?
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prayāga]]-[[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---up to Prayāga; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of us; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with You; [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---shall go; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---association of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:p:pāba]]---shall we get.
translation: They prayed, "Let us go to Prayāga with You. If we do not go, when shall we again get the association of Your lotus feet?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.217
description: "This country is mainly occupied by Mohammedans. At any place someone can create a disturbance, and although Your companion Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya is a learned scholar, he does not know how to speak the local language."
text:
> mleccha-deśa, keha kāhāṅ karaye utpāta
> bhaṭṭācārya---paṇḍita, kahite nā jānena vāt
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:d:deśa]]---this is a country occupied by the Mohammedans; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---anywhere; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:u:utpāta]]---can create a disturbance; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---learned scholar; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:j:jānena]]---does not know; [[synonyms:v:vāt]]---language.
translation: "This country is mainly occupied by Mohammedans. At any place someone can create a disturbance, and although Your companion Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya is a learned scholar, he does not know how to speak the local language."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.218
description: Hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted their proposal by smiling mildly. Thus those two persons continued to accompany Him.
text:
> śuni' mahāprabhu īṣat hāsite lāgilā
> sei dui-jana prabhura saṅge cali' āilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ī:īṣat]]---mildly; [[synonyms:h:hāsite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to smile; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cali']] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came.
translation: Hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted their proposal by smiling mildly. Thus those two persons continued to accompany Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.219
description: Whoever got to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would feel himself overwhelmed with ecstatic love and would begin to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra.
text:
> yei yei jana prabhura pāila daraśana
> sei preme matta haya, kare kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:y:yei]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:j:jana]]---person; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pāila]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---got the sight; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that person; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---with ecstatic love; [[synonyms:m:matta]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes overwhelmed; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Whoever got to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would feel himself overwhelmed with ecstatic love and would begin to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.22
description: That night the Lord stayed at the temple of Harideva, and during the night He began to reflect.
text:
> se-rātri rahilā haridevera maṇḍire
> rātre mahāprabhu kare manete vicāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:r:rātri]]---that night; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:devera]]---of Harideva; [[synonyms:m:mandire]]---in the temple; [[synonyms:r:rātre]]---at night; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:m:manete]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:v:vicāre]]---consideration.
translation: That night the Lord stayed at the temple of Harideva, and during the night He began to reflect.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.220
description: Whoever met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became a Vaiṣṇava, and whoever met that Vaiṣṇava also became a Vaiṣṇava. In this way, all the towns and villages one after the other became Vaiṣṇava.
text:
> tāṅra saṅge anyonye, tāṅra saṅge āna
> ei-mata 'vaiṣṇava' kailā saba deśa-grāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Him; [[synonyms:a:anyonye]]---other; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---and with him; [[synonyms:ā:āna]]---another; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---Vaiṣṇava; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---made; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:d:deśa]]-[[synonyms:g:grāma]]---villages and towns.
translation: Whoever met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became a Vaiṣṇava, and whoever met that Vaiṣṇava also became a Vaiṣṇava. In this way, all the towns and villages one after the other became Vaiṣṇava.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.221
description: Just as the Lord inundated South India on His tour there, He also inundated the western part of the country with love of Godhead.
text:
> dakṣiṇa yāite yaiche śakti prakāśilā
> sei-mata paścima deśa, preme bhāsāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]] [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---while touring in the southern part of India; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśilā]]---manifested His spiritual energy; [[synonyms:s:sei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in that way; [[synonyms:p:paścima]] [[synonyms:d:deśa]]---the western part of India; [[synonyms:p:preme]] [[synonyms:b:bhāsāilā]]---inundated with love of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Just as the Lord inundated South India on His tour there, He also inundated the western part of the country with love of Godhead.
purport: According to some opinions, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited Kurukṣetra while going to Prayāga from Vṛndāvana. There is a temple of Bhadra-kālī in Kurukṣetra, and near that temple there is a temple containing the Deity of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.222
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally arrived at Prayāga and for ten successive days bathed in the confluence of the Rivers Yamunā and Ganges during the festival of Makara-saṅkrānti [Māgha-melā].
text:
> ei-mata cali' prabhu 'prayāga' āilā
> daśa-dina triveṇīte makara-snāna kailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---walking; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prayāga]]---the holy place named Prayāga; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---reached; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---ten days; [[synonyms:t:triveṇīte]]---at the confluence of the Rivers Ganges and Yamunā; [[synonyms:m:makara]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---bathed during the festival of Makara, or Māgha-melā.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally arrived at Prayāga and for ten successive days bathed in the confluence of the Rivers Yamunā and Ganges during the festival of Makara-saṅkrānti [Māgha-melā].
purport: Actually the word //triveṇī// indicates the confluence of three rivers-namely the Ganges, Yamunā and Sarasvatī. Presently the Sarasvatī River is not visible, but the River Ganges and the River Yamunā merge at Allahabad.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.223
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's visit to Vṛndāvana and His activities there are unlimited. Even Lord Śeṣa, who has thousands of hoods, cannot reach the end of His activities.
text:
> vṛndāvana-gamana, prabhu-caritra ananta
> 'sahasra-vadana' yāṅra nāhi pā'na anta
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:c:caritra]]---pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]-[[synonyms:v:vadana]]---Lord Śeṣa, who has thousands of hoods; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---does not; [[synonyms:p:pā'na]]---get; [[synonyms:a:anta]]---limit.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's visit to Vṛndāvana and His activities there are unlimited. Even Lord Śeṣa, who has thousands of hoods, cannot reach the end of His activities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.224
description: What ordinary living being can describe the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu? I have only indicated the general direction in the form of codes.
text:
> tāhā ke kahite pāre kṣudra jīva hañā
> dig-daraśana kailuṅ muñi sūtra kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:ke]] [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---who can describe; [[synonyms:k:kṣudra]]---very little; [[synonyms:j:jīva]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being a conditioned soul; [[synonyms:d:dik]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]] [[synonyms:k:kailuṅ]]---have simply made an indication; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:s:sūtra]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---in codes.
translation: What ordinary living being can describe the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu? I have only indicated the general direction in the form of codes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.225
description: The pastimes and methods of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are uncommon. Unfortunate is he who cannot believe even after hearing all these things.
text:
> alaukika-līlā prabhura alaukika-rīti
> śunileo bhāgya-hīnera nā haya pratīti
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:alaukika]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---uncommon pastimes; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:alaukika]]-[[synonyms:r:rīti]]---uncommon method; [[synonyms:ś:śunileo]]---even though one hears; [[synonyms:b:bhāgya]]-[[synonyms:h:hīnera]]---of one who is unfortunate; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]] [[synonyms:p:pratīti]]---there is no belief.
translation: The pastimes and methods of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are uncommon. Unfortunate is he who cannot believe even after hearing all these things.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.226
description: From beginning to end the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are uncommon. Just hear them with faith and accept them as true and correct.
text:
> ādyopānta caitanya-līlā---'alaukika' jāna'
> śraddhā kari' śuna ihā, 'satya' kari' māna'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ādya]]-[[synonyms:u:upānta]]---from beginning to end; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:alaukika]] [[synonyms:j:jāna']]---everyone should know as uncommon; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---with faith; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]] [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---hear this; [[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:m:māna']]---accepting it as true and correct.
translation: From beginning to end the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are uncommon. Just hear them with faith and accept them as true and correct.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.227
description: Whoever argues about this is a great fool. He intentionally and personally brings a thunderbolt down upon his head.
text:
> yei tarka kare ihāṅ, sei---'mūrkha-rāja'
> āpanāra muṇḍe se āpani pāḍe vāja
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:t:tarka]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---one who simply argues; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---in this matter; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that person; [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]]-[[synonyms:r:rāja]]---a great fool; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāra]] [[synonyms:m:muṇḍe]]---on his own head; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that person; [[synonyms:ā:āpani]]---himself; [[synonyms:p:pāḍe]] [[synonyms:v:vāja]]---strikes with a thunderbolt.
translation: Whoever argues about this is a great fool. He intentionally and personally brings a thunderbolt down upon his head.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.228
description: The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are an ocean of nectar. Even a drop of this ocean can inundate the whole world with transcendental bliss.
text:
> caitanya-caritra ei---'amṛtera sindhu'
> jagat ānande bhāsāya yāra eka-bindu
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritra]]---pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:a:amṛtera]] [[synonyms:s:sindhu]]---ocean of nectar; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the whole world; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---with bliss; [[synonyms:b:bhāsāya]]---inundates; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:b:bindu]]---one drop.
translation: The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are an ocean of nectar. Even a drop of this ocean can inundate the whole world with transcendental bliss.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.229
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation:
Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Eighteenth Chapter, describing the Lord's visit to Śrī Vṛndāvana and His conversion of the Mohammedan soldiers on the way to Prayāga.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.23
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thought, "Since I shall not at any time climb Govardhana Hill, how shall I be able to see Gopāla Rāya?"
text:
> 'govardhana-upare āmi kabhu nā caḍiba
> gopāla-rāyera daraśana kemane pāiba?'
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]-[[synonyms:u:upare]]---upon the hill known as Govardhana; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:c:caḍiba]]---shall climb; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:r:rāyera]]---of Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visit; [[synonyms:k:kemane]]---how; [[synonyms:p:pāiba]]---I shall get.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thought, "Since I shall not at any time climb Govardhana Hill, how shall I be able to see Gopāla Rāya?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.24
description: Thinking in this way, the Lord remained silent, and Lord Gopāla, knowing His contemplation, played a trick.
text:
> eta mane kari' prabhu mauna kari' rahilā
> jāniyā gopāla kichu bhaṅgī uṭhāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]]---so much; [[synonyms:m:mane]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---considering within the mind; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mauna]]---silent; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---becoming; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:j:jāniyā]]---knowing; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the Deity Gopāla; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:b:bhaṅgī]]---tricks; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāilā]]---raised.
translation: Thinking in this way, the Lord remained silent, and Lord Gopāla, knowing His contemplation, played a trick.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.25
description: Coming down from Govardhana Hill, Lord Gopāla granted an interview to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who was unwilling to climb the hill, thinking Himself a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> anārurukṣave śailaṁ
> svasmai bhaktābhimānine
> avaruhya gireḥ kṛṣṇo
> gaurāya svam adarśayat
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anārurukṣave]]---who was unwilling to climb up; [[synonyms:ś:śailam]]---the mountain; [[synonyms:s:svasmai]]---unto Himself; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:a:abhimānine]]---considering Himself a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:avaruhya]]---getting down; [[synonyms:g:gireḥ]]---from the hill; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gaurāya]]---unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:svam]]---Himself; [[synonyms:a:adarśayat]]---showed.
translation: Coming down from Govardhana Hill, Lord Gopāla granted an interview to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who was unwilling to climb the hill, thinking Himself a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.26
description: Gopāla stayed in a village called Annakūṭa-grāma on Govardhana Hill. The villagers who lived in that village were mainly from Rajasthan.
text:
> 'annakūṭa'-nāme grāme gopālera sthiti
> rāja-puta-lokera sei grāme vasati
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:annakūṭa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāme]]---by the name Annakūṭa; [[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in the village; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of Gopāla; [[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---residence; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:p:puta]]-[[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of people from Rajasthan; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in that village; [[synonyms:v:vasati]]---habitation.
translation: Gopāla stayed in a village called Annakūṭa-grāma on Govardhana Hill. The villagers who lived in that village were mainly from Rajasthan.
purport:
The village named Annakūṭa-grāma is referred to in //Bhakti-ratnākara// (Fifth Wave):

> gopa-gopī bhuñjāyena kautuka apāra
> ei hetu 'āniyora' nāma se ihāra
>
> annakūṭa-sthāna ei dekha śrīnivāsa
> e-sthāna darśane haya pūrṇa abhilāṣa

"It is here that all the //gopīs// and the //gopas// enjoyed wonderful pastimes with Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Therefore this place is also called Āniyora. The Annakūṭa ceremony was celebrated here. O Śrīnivāsa, whoever sees this place has all his desires fulfilled." It is also stated:

> kuṇḍera nikaṭa dekha niviḍa-kānana
> ethāi 'gopāla' chilā hañā saṅgopana

"Look at the dense forest near the //kuṇḍa.// It was there that Gopāla was concealed." Also, the //Stavāvalī// (8.75) by Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī states:

> vrajendra-varyārpita-bhogam uccair
> dhṛtvā bṛhat-kāyam aghārir utkaḥ
> vareṇa rādhāṁ chalayan vibhuṅkte
> yatrānna-kūṭaṁ tad ahaṁ prapadye

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.27
description: One person who came to the village informed the inhabitants, "The Turkish soldiers are now preparing to attack your village.
text:
> eka-jana āsi' rātre grāmīke balila
> 'tomāra grāma mārite turuka-dhārī sājila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---one person; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:r:rātre]]---at night; [[synonyms:g:grāmīke]]---to the inhabitants of the village; [[synonyms:b:balila]]---said; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:g:grāma]]---village; [[synonyms:m:mārite]]---to attack; [[synonyms:t:turuka]]-[[synonyms:d:dhārī]]---Turkish Mohammedan soldiers; [[synonyms:s:sājila]]---are prepared.
translation: One person who came to the village informed the inhabitants, "The Turkish soldiers are now preparing to attack your village.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.28
description: "Flee this village tonight, and do not allow one person to remain. Take the Deity with you and leave, for the Mohammedan soldiers will come tomorrow."
text:
> āji rātrye palāha, nā rahiha eka-jana
> ṭhākura lañā bhāga', āsibe kāli yavana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āji]] [[synonyms:r:rātrye]]---this night; [[synonyms:p:palāha]]---go away; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:r:rahiha]]---do not remain; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---one person; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---the Deity; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:b:bhāga']]---go away; [[synonyms:ā:āsibe]]---will come; [[synonyms:k:kāli]]---tomorrow; [[synonyms:y:yavana]]---the Mohammedan soldiers.
translation: "Flee this village tonight, and do not allow one person to remain. Take the Deity with you and leave, for the Mohammedan soldiers will come tomorrow."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.29
description: Hearing this, all the villagers became very anxious. They first took Gopāla and moved Him to a village known as Gāṅṭhuli.
text:
> śuniyā grāmera loka cintita ha-ila
> prathame gopāla lañā gāṅṭhuli-grāme khuila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:g:grāmera]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people in the village; [[synonyms:c:cintita]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became very anxious; [[synonyms:p:prathame]]---first; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking Gopāla; [[synonyms:g:gāṅṭhuli]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in the village known as Gāṅṭhuli; [[synonyms:k:khuila]]---kept Him hidden.
translation: Hearing this, all the villagers became very anxious. They first took Gopāla and moved Him to a village known as Gāṅṭhuli.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.3
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced in ecstasy, but when He arrived at Āriṭgrāma, His sense perception was awakened.
text:
> ei-mata mahāprabhu nācite nācite
> 'āriṭ'-grāme āsi' 'bāhya' haila ācambite
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nācite]] [[synonyms:n:nācite]]---dancing and dancing; [[synonyms:ā:āriṭ]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in the village known as Āriṭ-grāma; [[synonyms:ā:āsi]]---coming; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---sense perception; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:ā:ācambite]]---suddenly.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced in ecstasy, but when He arrived at Āriṭgrāma, His sense perception was awakened.
purport: Āriṭ-grāma is also called Ariṣṭa-grāma. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu understood that in that village, Ariṣṭāsura was killed by Śrī Kṛṣṇa. While there, He inquired about Rādhā-kuṇḍa, but no one could tell Him where it was. The //brāhmaṇa// accompanying Him could also not ascertain its whereabouts. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu could then understand that the holy places known as Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa were at that time lost to everyone's vision. He therefore discovered Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa, which were two reservoirs of water in two paddy fields. Although there was very little water, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was omniscient and could understand that formerly these two ponds were called Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa. In this way Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa were discovered.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.30
description: The Gopāla Deity was kept in the house of a brāhmaṇa, and His worship was conducted secretly. Everyone fled, and thus the village of Annakūṭa was deserted.
text:
> vipra-gṛhe gopālera nibhṛte sevana
> grāma ujāḍa haila, palāila sarva-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipra]]-[[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---in the house of a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:n:nibhṛte]]---very secretly; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---worship; [[synonyms:g:grāma]]---the village; [[synonyms:u:ujāḍa]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became deserted; [[synonyms:p:palāila]]---fled; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---all the people.
translation: The Gopāla Deity was kept in the house of a brāhmaṇa, and His worship was conducted secretly. Everyone fled, and thus the village of Annakūṭa was deserted.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.31
description: Due to fear of the Mohammedans, the Gopāla Deity was moved from one place to another again and again. Thus giving up His temple, Lord Gopāla would sometimes live in a bush and sometimes in one village after another.
text:
> aiche mleccha-bhaye gopāla bhāge bāre-bāre
> mandira chāḍi' kuñje rahe, kibā grāmāntare
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---because of fear of the Mohammedans; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the Deity of Gopāla Rāya; [[synonyms:b:bhāge]]---runs away; [[synonyms:b:bāre]]-[[synonyms:b:bāre]]---again and again; [[synonyms:m:mandira]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up the temple; [[synonyms:k:kuñje]]---in the bush; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---or; [[synonyms:g:grāma]]-[[synonyms:a:antare]]---in a different village.
translation: Due to fear of the Mohammedans, the Gopāla Deity was moved from one place to another again and again. Thus giving up His temple, Lord Gopāla would sometimes live in a bush and sometimes in one village after another.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.32
description: In the morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took His bath in a lake called Mānasa-gaṅgā. He then circumambulated Govardhana Hill.
text:
> prātaḥ-kāle prabhu 'mānasa-gaṅgā'ya kari' snāna
> govardhana-parikramāya karilā prayāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mānasa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṅgāya]]---in the lake named Mānasa-gaṅgā; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---performing; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing; [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]---Govardhana Hill; [[synonyms:p:parikramāya]]---in circumambulating; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prayāṇa]]---starting.
translation: In the morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took His bath in a lake called Mānasa-gaṅgā. He then circumambulated Govardhana Hill.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.33
description: Just by seeing Govardhana Hill, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became ecstatic with love of Kṛṣṇa. While dancing and dancing, He recited the following verse.
text:
> govardhana dekhi' prabhu premāviṣṭa hañā
> nācite nācite calilā śloka paḍiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:govardhana]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Govardhana Hill; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming ecstatic in love; [[synonyms:n:nācite]] [[synonyms:n:nācite]]---dancing and dancing; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---departed; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:p:paḍiyā]]---reciting the following verse.
translation: Just by seeing Govardhana Hill, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became ecstatic with love of Kṛṣṇa. While dancing and dancing, He recited the following verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.34
description: "Of all the devotees, this Govardhana Hill is the best! O My friends, this hill supplies Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, as well as Their calves, cows and cowherd friends, with all kinds of necessities-water for drinking, very soft grass, caves, fruits, flowers and vegetables. In this way the hill offers respect to the Lord. Being touched by the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, Govardhana Hill appears very jubilant. "
text:
> hantāyam adrir abalā haridāsa-varyo
> yad rāma-kṛṣṇa-caraṇa-sparaśa-pramodaḥ
> mānaṁ tanoti saha-go-gaṇayos tayor yat
> pānīya-sūyavasa-kandara-kanda-mūlaiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---oh; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:a:adriḥ]]---hill; [[synonyms:a:abalāḥ]]---O friends; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]-[[synonyms:v:varyaḥ]]---the best among the servants of the Lord; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---because; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---of the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma; [[synonyms:s:sparaśa]]---by the touch; [[synonyms:p:pramodaḥ]]---jubilant; [[synonyms:m:mānam]]---respects; [[synonyms:t:tanoti]]---offers; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:g:go]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇayoḥ]]---cows, calves and cowherd boys; [[synonyms:t:tayoḥ]]---to Them (Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma); [[synonyms:y:yat]]---because; [[synonyms:p:pānīya]]---drinking water; [[synonyms:s:sūyavasa]]---very soft grass; [[synonyms:k:kandara]]---caves; [[synonyms:k:kanda]]-[[synonyms:m:mūlaiḥ]]---and by roots.
translation: "Of all the devotees, this Govardhana Hill is the best! O My friends, this hill supplies Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, as well as Their calves, cows and cowherd friends, with all kinds of necessities-water for drinking, very soft grass, caves, fruits, flowers and vegetables. In this way the hill offers respect to the Lord. Being touched by the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, Govardhana Hill appears very jubilant. "
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.21.18). It was spoken by the //gopīs// when Lord Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma entered the forest in the autumn. The //gopīs// spoke among themselves and glorified Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma for Their pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.35
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then took His bath in a lake called Govinda-kuṇḍa, and while He was there, He heard that the Deity Gopāla had already gone to Gāṅṭhuli-grāma.
text:
> 'govinda-kuṇḍādi' tīrthe prabhu kailā snāna
> tāhāṅ śunilā---gopāla gela gāṅṭhuli grāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---Govinda-kuṇḍa and others; [[synonyms:t:tīrthe]]---in the holy places; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---performed bathing; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:ś:śunilā]]---heard; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the Gopāla Deity; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---has gone; [[synonyms:g:gāṅṭhuli]]---Gāṅṭhuli; [[synonyms:g:grāma]]---to the village.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then took His bath in a lake called Govinda-kuṇḍa, and while He was there, He heard that the Deity Gopāla had already gone to Gāṅṭhuli-grāma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.36
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then went to the village of Gāṅṭhuli-grāma and saw the Lord Gopāla Deity. Overwhelmed by ecstatic love, He began to chant and dance.
text:
> sei grāme giyā kaila gopāla-daraśana
> premāveśe prabhu kare kīrtana-nartana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:g:grāme]]---to that village; [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---going; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]-[[synonyms:n:nartana]]---chanting and dancing.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then went to the village of Gāṅṭhuli-grāma and saw the Lord Gopāla Deity. Overwhelmed by ecstatic love, He began to chant and dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 18.37
description: As soon as the Lord saw the beauty of the Gopāla Deity, He was immediately overwhelmed by ecstatic love, and He recited the following verse. He then chanted and danced until the day ended.
text:
> gopālera saundarya dekhi' prabhura āveśa
> ei śloka paḍi' nāce, haila dina-śeṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of Gopāla; [[synonyms:s:saundarya]]---beauty; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---ecstasy; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting the following verse; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:d:dina]]-[[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]---the end of the day.
translation: As soon as the Lord saw the beauty of the Gopāla Deity, He was immediately overwhelmed by ecstatic love, and He recited the following verse. He then chanted and danced until the day ended.
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura gives the following information about Govinda-kuṇḍa. There is a village named Āniyora on Govardhana Hill, a little distance from the village of Paiṭhā. Govinda-kuṇḍa is situated near here, and there are two temples to Govinda and Baladeva there. According to some, Queen Padmāvatī excavated this lake. In the //Bhakti-ratnākara// (Fifth Wave), the following statement is found:

> ei śrī-govinda-kuṇḍa-mahimā aneka
> ethā indra kaila govindera abhiṣeka

"Govinda-kuṇḍa is exalted for its many spiritual activities. It was here that Indra was defeated by Lord Kṛṣṇa, and Indra offered his prayers and bathed Lord Govinda." In the book //Stavāvalī// (//Vraja-vilāsa-stava// 74) the following verse is found:

> nīcaiḥ prauḍha-bhayāt svayaṁ surapatiḥ pādau vidhṛtyeha yaiḥ
> svar-gaṅgā-salilaiś cakāra surabhi-dvārābhiṣekotsavam
> govindasya navaṁ gavām adhipatā rājye sphuṭaṁ kautukāt
> tair yat prādurabhūt sadā sphuratu tad govinda-kuṇḍaṁ dṛśoḥ

In the //Mathurā-khaṇḍa// it is also stated:

> yatrābhiṣikto bhagavān
> maghonā yadu-vairiṇā
> govinda-kuṇḍaṁ taj-jātaṁ
> snāna-mātreṇa mokṣadam

"Simply by bathing in Govinda-kuṇḍa, one is awarded liberation. This lake was produced when Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa was bathed by Lord Indra."
