title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.228
description: "On the platform of paternal love, the devotee considers himself the Lord's maintainer. Thus the Lord is the object of maintenance, like a son, and therefore this mellow is full of the four qualities of śānta-rasa, dāsya-rasa, fraternity and parental love. This is more transcendental nectar.
text:
> āpanāre 'pālaka' jñāna, kṛṣṇe 'pālya'-jñāna
> 'cāri' guṇe vātsalya rasa---amṛta-samāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āpanāre]]---unto himself; [[synonyms:p:pālaka]] [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---the notion of a caretaker; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---in Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pālya]]---as object of protection; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---notion; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---four; [[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---in qualities; [[synonyms:v:vātsalya]] [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---the mellow of parental love; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:s:samāna]]---like nectar.
translation: "On the platform of paternal love, the devotee considers himself the Lord's maintainer. Thus the Lord is the object of maintenance, like a son, and therefore this mellow is full of the four qualities of śānta-rasa, dāsya-rasa, fraternity and parental love. This is more transcendental nectar.
purport: In his //Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya,// Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura gives us a short summary of this complicated description of the different //rasas.// He states that by becoming firmly fixed in the Lord's service, one is devoid of all material desires. There are two transcendental qualities on the //śānta-rasa// platform. In all the material elements, sound vibration is found. Similarly, //śānta-rasa// is spread over all the other transcendental mellows, which are known as //dāsya-rasa, sakhya-rasa, vātsalya-rasa// and //madhura-rasa.// Although there is attachment for Kṛṣṇa in awe and veneration in the //śānta-rasa// along with two valuable transcendental qualities -attachment for Kṛṣṇa and detachment from material desires-nonetheless the sense of intimacy is lacking. Therefore in the //śānta-rasa,// attachment for impersonal Brahman and localized Paramātmā is prominent. The sense of intimacy is lacking. By that intimacy one thinks of Kṛṣṇa as one's only shelter and only friend. In the //śānta-rasa// one accepts Kṛṣṇa as the impersonal Param Brahma or the localized Paramātmā. This is based on the speculative knowledge of the //jñānī.// However, when this knowledge is further developed, one is convinced that Paramātmā, the Supreme Lord, is master and that the living entity is His eternal servant. One then attains the platform of //dāsya-rasa.// In //dāsya-rasa// the Lord is accepted with awe and veneration. However, although in the //śānta-rasa// there is no active service, in the //dāsya-rasa// active service is prominent. Thus in the //dāsya-rasa,// the qualities of //śānta-rasa// and service are predominantly visible. Similarly, when this same //rasa// is developed into fraternity (//sakhya-rasa),// a friendly intimacy is added. There is no awe or veneration in the //sakhya-rasa//.The //sakhya-rasa// is invested with three qualities-//śānta, dāsya,// and //sakhya.// Similarly, on the platform of parental love, the qualities of //śānta-rasa// and //dāsya-rasa// are fully developed in another form---the sense of maintaining the Lord. Therefore on the platform of parental love there exists a combination of four transcendental qualities-//śānta, dāsya, sakhya,// and the qualities of paternity, which put the devotee in the position of a maintainer. Thus on the platform of parental love the four qualities of transcendental love are present.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.229

text:
> se amṛtānande bhakta saha ḍubena āpane
> 'kṛṣṇa---bhakta-vaśa' guṇa kahe aiśvarya-jñāni-gaṇe

translation: "The exchange of spiritual happiness between Kṛṣṇa and His devotee, in which Kṛṣṇa is controlled by His devotee, is compared to an ocean of nectar into which the devotee and Kṛṣṇa plunge. This is the verdict of learned scholars who appreciate Kṛṣṇa's opulence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.230
description: " 'Again let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead. O my Lord, I offer my obeisances hundreds and thousands of times with all affection because by Your personal pastimes You plunge the gopīs into an ocean of nectar. Appreciating Your opulence, devotees generally declare that You are always subjugated by their feelings.'
text:
> itīdṛk-svalīlābhir ānanda-kuṇḍe
> svaghoṣaṁ nimajjantam ākhyāpayantam
> tadīyeśita-jñeṣu bhaktair jitatvaṁ
> punaḥ prematās taṁ śatāvṛtti vande

translation: “ 'Again let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead. O my Lord, I offer my obeisances hundreds and thousands of times with all affection because by Your personal pastimes You plunge the gopīs into an ocean of nectar. Appreciating Your opulence, devotees generally declare that You are always subjugated by their feelings.'
purport: This verse is from the //Dāmodarāṣṭaka// in the //Padma Purāṇa.// Attachment for Kṛṣṇa in //śānta-rasa,// rendering service to the Lord in //dāsya-rasa,// rendering relaxed service in fraternity, and serving in parental love with feelings of maintenance all combine on the platform of conjugal love when the devotee wants to serve the Lord by offering Him his personal body. Thus the qualities of the other //rasas// combine to form the nectar of conjugal love. On this platform, all the different feelings of a devotee are amalgamated.

translation: "Later, you can go from Vṛndāvana to Jagannātha Purī through Bengal [Gauḍa-deśa]. There you will meet Me again."

translation: While Candraśekhara was waiting outside the city, he suddenly saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrive, and he fell down at the Lord's feet. Being very happy, he took the Lord to his home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.26
description: Sanātana Gosvāmī said, "You are the supreme ruler of Bengal and are completely independent. Whenever someone commits a fault, you punish him accordingly."

translation: Sanātana Gosvāmī said, "You are the supreme ruler of Bengal and are completely independent. Whenever someone commits a fault, you punish him accordingly."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.27
description: Hearing this, the Nawab of Bengal stood up and returned to his home. He ordered the arrest of Sanātana Gosvāmī so that he would not be able to leave.
text:
> eta śuni' gauḍeśvara uṭhi' ghare gelā
> palāiba bali' sanātanere bāndhilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Nawab of Bengal; [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---standing up; [[synonyms:g:ghare]] [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went back home; [[synonyms:p:palāiba]]---I shall run away; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---because of this; [[synonyms:s:sanātanere]] [[synonyms:b:bāndhilā]]---he arrested Sanātana.
translation: Hearing this, the Nawab of Bengal stood up and returned to his home. He ordered the arrest of Sanātana Gosvāmī so that he would not be able to leave.
purport: It is said that the relationship between the Nawab of Bengal and Sanātana Gosvāmī was very intimate. The Nawab used to consider Sanātana Gosvāmī his younger brother, and when Sanātana Gosvāmī showed a very strong intention to resign, the Nawab, feeling familial affection, essentially said, "I am your elder brother, but I do not look after the state management. My only business is attacking other states with my soldiers and fighting everywhere as a plunderer. Because I am a meat-eater [//yavana//], I am used to hunting all kinds of living beings. In this way I am destroying all kinds of living entities in Bengal. While engaged in this destructive business, I am hoping that you will tend to the administration of the state. Since I, your elder brother, am engaged in such a destructive business, you, being my younger brother, should look after the state management. If you do not, how will things continue?" This talk was based on a family relationship, and Sanātana Gosvāmī also replied in an intimate and joking way. Essentially he told the Nawab, "My dear brother, you are the independent ruler of Bengal. You can act in whatever way you like, and if someone commits fault, you can punish him accordingly." In other words, Sanātana Gosvāmī was saying that since the Nawab was accustomed to acting like a plunderer, he should go ahead and take action. Since Sanātana was not showing much enthusiasm in performing his duty, the Nawab should dismiss him from his service. The Nawab could understand the intention of Sanātana Gosvāmī's statement. He therefore left in an angry mood and ordered Sanātana Gosvāmī's arrest.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.28
description: At this time, the Nawab was going to attack the province of Orissa, and he told Sanātana Gosvāmī, "Come along with me."

> sanātane kahe,---tumi cala mora sāthe
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:u:uḍiyā]] [[synonyms:m:mārite]]---to attack the Orissa province; [[synonyms:s:sanātane]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---he said to Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:c:cala]]---you come; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:s:sāthe]]---along with me.
translation: At this time, the Nawab was going to attack the province of Orissa, and he told Sanātana Gosvāmī, "Come along with me."
purport: Hussain Shah attacked the province of Orissa in 1424 Śakābda Era. At that time he conquered the feudal princes of neighboring Orissa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.29
description: Sanātana Gosvāmī replied, "You are going to Orissa to give pain to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. For this reason I am powerless to go with you."
text:
> teṅho kahe,---yābe tumi devatāya duḥkha dite
> mora śakti nāhi, tomāra saṅge yāite
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:teṅho]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī replied; [[synonyms:y:yābe]]---will go; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:d:devatāya]]---to the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]] [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give unhappiness; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---my power; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in company with you; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go.
translation: Sanātana Gosvāmī replied, "You are going to Orissa to give pain to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. For this reason I am powerless to go with you."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.3
description: After meeting Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in the village of Rāmakeli, the brothers Rūpa and Sanātana returned to their homes.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-sanātana rahe rāmakeli-grāme
> prabhure miliyā gelā āpana-bhavane
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---the brothers named Rūpa and Sanātana; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---stayed; [[synonyms:r:rāmakeli]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in Rāmakeli; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:miliyā]]---meeting; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went back; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhavane]]---to their own homes.
translation: After meeting Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in the village of Rāmakeli, the brothers Rūpa and Sanātana returned to their homes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.30
description: The Nawab again arrested Sanātana Gosvāmī and kept him in prison. At this time, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu departed for Vṛndāvana from Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> tabe tāṅre bāndhi' rākhi' karilā gamana
> ethā nīlācala haite prabhu calilā vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:b:bāndhi']]---arresting; [[synonyms:r:rākhi']]---keeping; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---he went away; [[synonyms:e:ethā]]---at this time; [[synonyms:n:nīlācala]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:calilā]] [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---departed for Vṛndāvana.
translation: The Nawab again arrested Sanātana Gosvāmī and kept him in prison. At this time, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu departed for Vṛndāvana from Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.31
description: The two persons who went to Jagannātha Purī to inquire about the Lord's departure returned and informed Rūpa Gosvāmī that the Lord had already departed for Vṛndāvana.
text:
> tabe sei dui cara rūpa-ṭhāñi āila
> 'vṛndāvana calilā prabhu'---āsiyā kahila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:c:cara]]---messengers; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---to the presence of Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came back; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]] [[synonyms:c:calilā]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has departed for Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---they informed.
translation: The two persons who went to Jagannātha Purī to inquire about the Lord's departure returned and informed Rūpa Gosvāmī that the Lord had already departed for Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.32
description: Upon receiving this message from his two messengers, Rūpa Gosvāmī immediately wrote a letter to Sanātana Gosvāmī saying that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had departed for Vṛndāvana.
text:
> śuniyā śrī-rūpa likhila sanātana-ṭhāñi
> 'vṛndāvana calilā śrī-caitanya-gosāñi
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:l:likhila]]---wrote; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---to Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---has gone; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Upon receiving this message from his two messengers, Rūpa Gosvāmī immediately wrote a letter to Sanātana Gosvāmī saying that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had departed for Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.33
description: In his letter to Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī wrote, "We two brothers are starting out to go see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. You must also somehow or other get released and come meet us."
text:
> āmi-dui-bhāi calilāṅa tāṅhāre milite
> tumi yaiche taiche chuṭi' āisa tāhāṅ haite
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]-[[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---we two brothers; [[synonyms:c:calilāṅa]]---have gone; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāre]] [[synonyms:m:milite]]---to meet Him; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]] [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---somehow or other; [[synonyms:c:chuṭi']]---getting free; [[synonyms:ā:āisa]]---come; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from there.
translation: In his letter to Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī wrote, "We two brothers are starting out to go see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. You must also somehow or other get released and come meet us."
purport: The two brothers herein mentioned are Rūpa Gosvāmī and his younger brother, Anupama Mallika. Rūpa Gosvāmī was informing Sanātana Gosvāmī that he should join him and his younger brother.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.34
description: Rūpa Gosvāmī further informed Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī: "I have left a deposit of ten thousand coins with the grocer. Use that money to get out of prison.
text:
> daśa-sahasra mudrā tathā āche mudi-sthāne
> tāhā diyā kara śīghra ātma-vimocane
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:s:sahasra]] [[synonyms:m:mudrā]]---ten thousand coins; [[synonyms:t:tāthā]]---there; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there are; [[synonyms:m:mudi]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in the grocer's place; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---with this amount; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---get; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]]---as soon as possible; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:v:vimocane]]---release from the internment.
translation: Rūpa Gosvāmī further informed Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī: "I have left a deposit of ten thousand coins with the grocer. Use that money to get out of prison.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.35
description: "Somehow or other get yourself released and come to Vṛndāvana." After writing this, the two brothers [Rūpa Gosvāmī and Anupama] went to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> yaiche taiche chuṭi' tumi āisa vṛndāvana'
> eta likhi' dui-bhāi karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yaiche]] [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---somehow or other; [[synonyms:c:chuṭi']]---getting released; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:ā:āisa]]---come; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:l:likhi']]---writing this; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---the two brothers, namely Rūpa Gosvāmī and his younger brother Anupama; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---departed.
translation: "Somehow or other get yourself released and come to Vṛndāvana." After writing this, the two brothers [Rūpa Gosvāmī and Anupama] went to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.36
description: Rūpa Gosvāmī's younger brother was a great devotee whose actual name was Śrī Vallabha, but he was given the name Anupama Mallika.
text:
> anupama mallika, tāṅra nāma---'śrī-vallabha'
> rūpa-gosāñira choṭa-bhāi---parama-vaiṣṇava
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anupama]] [[synonyms:m:mallika]]---Anupama Mallika; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---his name; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vallabha]]---Śrī Vallabha; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:c:choṭa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---younger brother; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---great devotee.
translation: Rūpa Gosvāmī's younger brother was a great devotee whose actual name was Śrī Vallabha, but he was given the name Anupama Mallika.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.37
description: Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī and Anupama Mallika went to Prayāga, and they were very pleased to hear news that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was there.
text:
> tāṅhā lañā rūpa-gosāñi prayāge āilā
> mahāprabhu tāhāṅ śuni' ānandita hailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅhā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking him along; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pra]] [[synonyms:y:yāge]]---to Prayāga; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]] [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---were very much pleased.
translation: Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī and Anupama Mallika went to Prayāga, and they were very pleased to hear news that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.38
description: At Prayāga, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to see the temple of Bindu Mādhava, and many hundreds of thousands of people followed Him just to meet Him.
text:
> prabhu caliyāchena bindu-mādhava-daraśane
> lakṣa lakṣa loka āise prabhura milane
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:caliyāchena]]---was going; [[synonyms:b:bindu]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhava]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---to see Lord Bindu Mādhava; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---many hundreds of thousands of people; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:milane]]---for meeting.
translation: At Prayāga, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to see the temple of Bindu Mādhava, and many hundreds of thousands of people followed Him just to meet Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.39
description: Some of the people following the Lord were crying. Some were laughing, some dancing and some chanting. Indeed, some of them were rolling on the ground, exclaiming, "Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!"
text:
> keha kānde, keha hāse, keha nāce, gāya
> 'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa' bali' keha gaḍāgaḍi yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:k:kānde]]---some cried; [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:h:hāse]]---some laughed; [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---some danced; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chanted; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---some; [[synonyms:g:gaḍāgaḍi]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---rolled on the ground.
translation: Some of the people following the Lord were crying. Some were laughing, some dancing and some chanting. Indeed, some of them were rolling on the ground, exclaiming, "Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.4
description: The two brothers devised a means whereby they could give up their material activities. For this purpose, they appointed two brāhmaṇas and paid them a large amount of money.
text:
> dui-bhāi viṣaya-tyāgera upāya sṛjila
> bhau-dhana diyā dui brāhmaṇe varila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---the two brothers; [[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]-[[synonyms:t:tyāgera]]---of giving up material activities; [[synonyms:u:upāya]] [[synonyms:s:sṛjila]]---discovered a means; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---much money; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---paying; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇe]]---two //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:v:varila]]---appointed.
translation: The two brothers devised a means whereby they could give up their material activities. For this purpose, they appointed two brāhmaṇas and paid them a large amount of money.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.40
description: Prayāga is located at the confluence of two rivers—the Ganges and the Yamunā. Although these rivers were not able to flood Prayāga with water, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu inundated the whole area with waves of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> gaṅgā-yamunā prayāga nārila ḍubāite
> prabhu ḍubāila kṛṣṇa-premera vanyāte
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:y:yamunā]]---the River Ganges and River Yamunā; [[synonyms:p:prayāga]]---Prayāga; [[synonyms:n:nārila]]---were not able; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍubāite]]---to flood; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍubāila]]---flooded; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:premera]]---of ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vanyāte]]---in an inundation.
translation: Prayāga is located at the confluence of two rivers---the Ganges and the Yamunā. Although these rivers were not able to flood Prayāga with water, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu inundated the whole area with waves of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.41
description: Seeing the great crowd, the two brothers remained standing in a secluded place. They could see that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was ecstatic to see Lord Bindu Mādhava.
text:
> bhiḍa dekhi' dui bhāi rahilā nirjane
> prabhura āveśa haila mādhava-daraśane
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhiḍa]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the crowd; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---the two brothers; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:n:nirjane]]---in a secluded place; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---ecstasy; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---by seeing the Deity, Bindu Mādhava.
translation: Seeing the great crowd, the two brothers remained standing in a secluded place. They could see that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was ecstatic to see Lord Bindu Mādhava.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.42
description: The Lord was loudly chanting the holy name of Hari. Dancing in ecstatic love and raising His arms, He asked everyone to chant "Hari! Hari!"
text:
> premāveśe nāce prabhu hari-dhvani kari'
> ūrdhva bāhu kari' bale---bala 'hari' 'hari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---danced; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---vibrating the holy name of Hari; [[synonyms:ū:ūrdhva]]---raised; [[synonyms:b:bāhu]]---the arms; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---says; [[synonyms:b:bala]] [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---chant Hari, Hari.
translation: The Lord was loudly chanting the holy name of Hari. Dancing in ecstatic love and raising His arms, He asked everyone to chant "Hari! Hari!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.43
description: Everyone was astounded to see the greatness of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Indeed, I cannot properly describe the pastimes of the Lord at Prayāga.
text:
> prabhura mahimā dekhi' loke camatkāra
> prayāge prabhura līlā nāri varṇibāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---the greatness; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---in all people; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonishment; [[synonyms:p:prayāge]]---at Prayāga; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes; [[synonyms:n:nāri]]---I am not able; [[synonyms:v:varṇibāra]]---to describe.
translation: Everyone was astounded to see the greatness of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Indeed, I cannot properly describe the pastimes of the Lord at Prayāga.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.44
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had made an acquaintance with a brāhmaṇa from Deccan [in South India], and that brāhmaṇa invited Him for meals and took Him to his place.
text:
> dākṣiṇātya-vipra-sane āche paricaya
> sei vipra nimantriyā nila nijālaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dākṣiṇātya]]---Deccan; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:paricaya]]---acquaintance; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---//brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:n:nimantriyā]]---inviting; [[synonyms:n:nila]]---brought; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:ā:ālaya]]---to his own place.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had made an acquaintance with a brāhmaṇa from Deccan [in South India], and that brāhmaṇa invited Him for meals and took Him to his place.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.45
description: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was sitting in a solitary place in the home of that Deccan brāhmaṇa, Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrī Vallabha [Anupama Mallika] came to meet Him.
text:
> vipra-gṛhe āsi' prabhu nibhṛte vasilā
> śrī-rūpa-vallabha duṅhe āsiyā mililā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipra]]-[[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---to the house of that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nibhṛte]]---in a solitary place; [[synonyms:v:vasilā]]---sat down; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:v:vallabha]]---the two brothers Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrī Vallabha; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met Him.
translation: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was sitting in a solitary place in the home of that Deccan brāhmaṇa, Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrī Vallabha [Anupama Mallika] came to meet Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.46
description: Seeing the Lord from a distance, the two brothers put two clumps of straw between their teeth and immediately fell down on the ground like rods, offering Him obeisances.
text:
> dui-guccha tṛṇa duṅhe daśane dhariyā
> prabhu dekhi' dūre paḍe daṇḍavat hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:g:guccha]]---two bunches; [[synonyms:t:tṛṇa]]---straw; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:d:daśane]] [[synonyms:d:dhariyā]]---holding in the teeth; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dūre]]---in a distant place; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fell down; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---like rods; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming.
translation: Seeing the Lord from a distance, the two brothers put two clumps of straw between their teeth and immediately fell down on the ground like rods, offering Him obeisances.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.47
description: Both brothers were overwhelmed with ecstatic emotion, and reciting various Sanskrit verses, they stood up and fell down again and again.
text:
> nānā śloka paḍi' uṭhe, paḍe bāra bāra
> prabhu dekhi' premāveśa ha-ila duṅhara
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verses; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---stood up; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fell down; [[synonyms:b:bāra]] [[synonyms:b:bāra]]---again and again; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the Lord; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---ecstatic emotion; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]]---of both of them.
translation: Both brothers were overwhelmed with ecstatic emotion, and reciting various Sanskrit verses, they stood up and fell down again and again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.48
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to see Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, and He told him, "Stand up! Stand up! My dear Rūpa, come here."
text:
> śrī-rūpe dekhiyā prabhura prasanna haila mana
> 'uṭha, uṭha, rūpa, āisa', balilā vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prasanna]]---very pleased; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:u:uṭha]]---please stand up; [[synonyms:u:uṭha]]---please stand up; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---My dear Rūpa; [[synonyms:ā:āisa]]---come; [[synonyms:b:balilā]]---He said; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---the words.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to see Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, and He told him, "Stand up! Stand up! My dear Rūpa, come here."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.49
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "It is not possible to describe Kṛṣṇa's mercy, for He has delivered you both from the well of material enjoyment.
text:
> kṛṣṇera karuṇā kichu nā yāya varṇane
> viṣaya-kūpa haite kāḍila tomā dui-jane
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:karuṇā]]---the mercy; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---any; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---is possible; [[synonyms:v:varṇane]]---to describe; [[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]-[[synonyms:k:kūpa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the well of material enjoyment; [[synonyms:k:kāḍila]]---delivered; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]---you; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---both.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "It is not possible to describe Kṛṣṇa's mercy, for He has delivered you both from the well of material enjoyment.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.5
description: The brāhmaṇas performed religious ceremonies and chanted the holy name of Kṛṣṇa so that the two brothers might attain shelter at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very soon.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-mantre karāila dui puraścaraṇa
> acirāt pāibāre caitanya-caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mantre]]---in the holy //mantra// Hare Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---caused to perform; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:p:puraścaraṇa]]---religious ceremonies; [[synonyms:a:acirāt]]---without delay; [[synonyms:p:pāibāre]]---to get; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: The brāhmaṇas performed religious ceremonies and chanted the holy name of Kṛṣṇa so that the two brothers might attain shelter at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very soon.
purport: A //puraścaraṇa// is a ritualistic ceremony performed under the guidance of an expert spiritual master or a //brāhmaṇa.// It is performed for the fulfillment of certain desires. One rises early in the morning, chants the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra,// performs //arcana// by the //ārati// ceremony and worships the Deities. These activities are described in the Fifteenth Chapter, verse 108.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.50
description: " 'Even though a person is a very learned scholar of the Sanskrit Vedic literatures, he is not accepted as My devotee unless he is pure in devotional service. Even though a person is born in a family of dog-eaters, he is very dear to Me if he is a pure devotee who has no motive to enjoy fruitive activities or mental speculation. Indeed, all respects should be given to him, and whatever he offers should be accepted. Such devotees are as worshipable as I am.' "
text:
> na me 'bhaktaś catur-vedī
> mad-bhaktaḥ śvapacaḥ priyaḥ
> tasmai deyaṁ tato grāhyaṁ
> sa ca pūjyo yathā hy aham
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:a:abhaktaḥ]]---devoid of pure devotional service; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vedī]]---a scholar in the four Vedas; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktaḥ]]---My devotee; [[synonyms:ś:śva]]-[[synonyms:p:pacaḥ]]---even from a family of dog-eaters; [[synonyms:p:priyaḥ]]---very dear; [[synonyms:t:tasmai]]---to him (a pure devotee, even though born in a very low family); [[synonyms:d:deyam]]---should be given; [[synonyms:t:tataḥ]]---from him; [[synonyms:g:grāhyam]]---should be accepted (remnants of food); [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that person; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:p:pūjyaḥ]]---worshipable; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as much as; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I.
translation: “ 'Even though a person is a very learned scholar of the Sanskrit Vedic literatures, he is not accepted as My devotee unless he is pure in devotional service. Even though a person is born in a family of dog-eaters, he is very dear to Me if he is a pure devotee who has no motive to enjoy fruitive activities or mental speculation. Indeed, all respects should be given to him, and whatever he offers should be accepted. Such devotees are as worshipable as I am.' "
purport: This verse is included in the //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa// (10.127) compiled by Sanātana Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.51
description: After reciting this verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced both brothers, and out of His causeless mercy He placed His feet on their heads.
text:
> ei śloka paḍi' duṅhāre kailā āliṅgana
> kṛpāte duṅhāra māthāya dharilā caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---this verse; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāre]]---the two brothers; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embraced; [[synonyms:k:kṛpāte]]---out of causeless mercy; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]]---of both of them; [[synonyms:m:māthāya]]---on the heads; [[synonyms:d:dharilā]]---placed; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---His feet.
translation: After reciting this verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced both brothers, and out of His causeless mercy He placed His feet on their heads.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.52
description: After receiving the Lord's causeless mercy, the brothers folded their hands and in great humility offered the following prayers unto the Lord.
text:
> prabhu-kṛpā pāñā duṅhe dui hāta yuḍi'
> dīna hañā stuti kare vinaya ācari'

translation: After receiving the Lord's causeless mercy, the brothers folded their hands and in great humility offered the following prayers unto the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.53
description: "O most munificent incarnation! You are Kṛṣṇa Himself appearing as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu. You have assumed the golden color of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and You are widely distributing pure love of Kṛṣṇa. We offer our respectful obeisances unto You.
text:
> namo mahā-vadānyāya
> kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāya te
> kṛṣṇāya kṛṣṇa-caitanya-
> nāmne gaura-tviṣe namaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:v:vadānyāya]]---who is most munificent and charitably disposed; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]---love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pradāya]]---who can give; [[synonyms:t:te]]---unto You; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇāya]]---the original Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:n:nāmne]]---under the name Kṛṣṇa Caitanya; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:t:tviṣe]]---whose complexion is the golden complexion of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---obeisances.
translation: "O most munificent incarnation! You are Kṛṣṇa Himself appearing as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu. You have assumed the golden color of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and You are widely distributing pure love of Kṛṣṇa. We offer our respectful obeisances unto You.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.54
description: "We offer our respectful obeisances unto that merciful Supreme Personality of Godhead who has converted all three worlds, which were maddened by ignorance, and saved them from their diseased condition by making them mad with the nectar from the treasure-house of love of God. Let us take full shelter of that Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, whose activities are wonderful."
text:
> yo 'jñāna-mattaṁ bhuvanaṁ dayālur
> ullāghayann apy akarot pramattam
> sva-prema-sampat-sudhayādbhutehaṁ
> śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanyam amuṁ prapadye
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---that Personality of Godhead who; [[synonyms:a:ajñāna]]-[[synonyms:m:mattam]]---maddened by ignorance or foolishly passing time //in karma, jñāna, yoga// and Māyāvāda philosophy; [[synonyms:b:bhuvanam]]---the entire three worlds; [[synonyms:d:dayāluḥ]]---so merciful; [[synonyms:u:ullāghayan]]---subduing such processes as //karma, jñāna// and //yoga//; [[synonyms:a:api]]---despite; [[synonyms:a:akarot]]---made; [[synonyms:p:pra]]-[[synonyms:m:mattam]]---maddened; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:s:sampat]]-[[synonyms:s:sudhayā]]---by the nectar of His personal devotional service, which is an invaluable treasure of bliss; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]-[[synonyms:ī:īham]]---whose activities are wonderful; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanyam]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:amum]]---that; [[synonyms:p:prapadye]]---I surrender.
translation: "We offer our respectful obeisances unto that merciful Supreme Personality of Godhead who has converted all three worlds, which were maddened by ignorance, and saved them from their diseased condition by making them mad with the nectar from the treasure-house of love of God. Let us take full shelter of that Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, whose activities are wonderful."
purport: This verse is found in the //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (1.2).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.55

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.60

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu selected His residence beside the confluence of the Ganges and Yamunā at a place called Triveṇī. The two brothers-Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrī Vallabha-selected their residence near the Lord's.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.61
description: At that time, Śrī Vallabha Bhaṭṭa was staying at Āḍāila-grāma, and when he heard that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had arrived, he went to His place to see Him.
text:
> se-kāle vallabha-bhaṭṭa rahe āḍāila-grāme
> mahāprabhu āilā śuni' āila tāṅra sthāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time; [[synonyms:v:vallabha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Vallabha Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---resided; [[synonyms:ā:āḍāila]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in the village known as Āḍāila; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---has come; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to His place.
translation: At that time, Śrī Vallabha Bhaṭṭa was staying at Āḍāila-grāma, and when he heard that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had arrived, he went to His place to see Him.
purport:
Vallabha Bhaṭṭa was a great learned scholar of Vaiṣṇavism. In the beginning he was very much devoted to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, but since he thought that he could not receive proper respect from Him, he later joined the Viṣṇusvāmī sect and became //ācārya// of that sect. His sect is celebrated as the Vallabhācārya-sampradāya. This //sampradāya// has had great influence in Vṛndāvana near Gokula and in Bombay. Vallabha Bhaṭṭa wrote many books, including a commentary on //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// called //Subodhinī-ṭīkā,// and notes on the //Vedānta-sūtra,// in the form of an //Anubhāṣya.// He also wrote a combination of sixteen short works called //Ṣoḍaśa-grantha.// Āḍāila-grāma, where he was staying, was near the confluence of the Rivers Ganges and Yamunā on the other side of the Yamunā about one mile from the river. The village there is called Aḍelī-grāma, or Āḍāila-grāma. A temple of Lord Viṣṇu there still belongs to the Vallabha-sampradāya.

Vallabha Bhaṭṭa was originally from a place in southern India called Trailaṅga. There is a railway station there called Niḍāḍābhalu. Sixteen miles from that station is a village called Kāṅkaḍabāḍa, or Kākuṅrapāḍhu. A learned //brāhmaṇa// named Lakṣmaṇa Dīkṣita used to live there, and Vallabha Bhaṭṭa was his son. There are five sections of the //brāhmaṇa// community of Āndhra Pradesh known as //bella-nāṭī, vegī-nāṭī, muraki-nāṭi telagu-nāṭī// and //kāśala-nāṭī.// Out of these five brahminical communities, Vallabhācārya took his birth in the community of //bella-nāṭī// in the year 1400 Śakābda Era. According to some people, Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya's father took //sannyāsa// before Vallabha's birth, and he returned home to take Vallabhācārya as his son. According to the opinion of others, Vallabhācārya was born in 1400 Śakābda Era on the Ekādaśī day of the dark moon in the month of Caitra, and he took his birth in a //brāhmaṇa// family surnamed Khambhaṁpāṭībāru. According to this account, his father's name was Lakṣmaṇa Bhaṭṭa Dīkṣita, and he was born in Campakāraṇya. In someone else's opinion, Vallabhācārya appeared near the village named Cāṅpā-jhāra-grāma, which is near a railway station named Rājima in Madhya Pradesh.

After studying for eleven years at Vārāṇasī, Vallabhācārya returned home. On his return, he heard that his father had departed from the material world. Keeping his brother and mother at home, he went to the banks of the River Tuṅgabhadrā in a village called Vidyānagara, and it was there that he enlightened Kṛṣṇadeva, the grandson of King Bukkarāja. After that, he traveled throughout India thrice on trips lasting six years. Thus he passed eighteen years and became victorious in his discussions of revealed scripture. When he was thirty years old, he married Mahālakṣmī, who belonged to the same //brāhmaṇa// community. Near Govardhana Hill he established a Deity in the valley. Finally he came to Āḍāila, which is on the other side of Prayāga.

Vallabhācārya had two sons, Gopīnātha and Viṭhṭhaleśvara, and in his old age he accepted the renounced order. In 1452 Śakābda Era, he passed away from the material world at Vārāṇasī. His book known as //Ṣoḍaśa-grantha// and his commentaries on //Vedānta-sūtra (Anubhāṣya//) and //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Subodhinī//) are very famous. He has written many other books besides.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.62

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.63
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu felt great ecstatic love when they began discussing Kṛṣṇa, but the Lord checked His feelings because He felt shy before Vallabha Bhaṭṭa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.64

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.69
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Don't touch him, for he belongs to a very low caste. You are a follower of Vedic principles and are a well experienced performer of many sacrifices. You also belong to the aristocracy."
text:
> 'iṅho nā sparśiha, iṅho jāti ati-hīna!
> vaidika, yājñika tumi kulīna pravīṇa!'
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṅho]]---him; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:s:sparśiha]]---do not touch; [[synonyms:i:iṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:j:jāti]]---caste; [[synonyms:a:ati]]-[[synonyms:h:hīna]]---very low; [[synonyms:v:vaidika]]---a follower of Vedic principles; [[synonyms:y:yājñika]]---a performer of many sacrifices; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:k:kulīna]]---aristocratic //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:p:pravīṇa]]---an experienced person.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Don't touch him, for he belongs to a very low caste. You are a follower of Vedic principles and are a well experienced performer of many sacrifices. You also belong to the aristocracy."
purport:
Generally //brāhmaṇas// are puffed up with false prestige because they belong to the aristocracy and perform many Vedic sacrifices. In South India especially, this fastidious position is most prominent. At any rate, this was the case five hundred years ago. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu actually started a revolution against this brahminical system by inaugurating the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra.// By this chanting, one can be delivered regardless of caste, creed, color or social position. Whoever chants the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// is immediately purified due to the transcendental position of devotional service. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is here hinting to Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya that an exalted //brāhmaṇa// who makes sacrifices and follows Vedic principles should not neglect a person who is engaged in devotional service by chanting the holy name of the Lord.

Actually Rūpa Gosvāmī did not belong to a lower caste. He was from a highly aristocratic //brāhmaṇa// family, but due to his association with the Mohammedan Nawab, he was considered fallen and excommunicated from //brāhmaṇa// society. However, due to his advanced devotional service, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted him as a //gosvāmī.// Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya knew all this. One who is a devotee is above caste and creed, yet Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya felt himself prestigious.

The present head of the Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya //sampradāya// of Bombay is named Dīkṣita Mahārāja. He is very friendly to our movement, and whenever we meet him, this learned //brāhmaṇa// scholar highly praises the activities of the Hare Kṛṣṇa movement. He is a life member of our Society, and although he is a learned scholar in the brahminical caste tradition, he accepts our Society and considers its members bona fide devotees of Lord Viṣṇu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.7
description: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī divided the wealth that he brought back home. He gave fifty percent in charity to brāhmaṇas and Vaiṣṇavas and twenty-five percent to his relatives.
text:
> brāhmaṇa-vaiṣṇave dilā tāra ardha-dhane
> eka cauṭhi dhana dilā kuṭumba-bharaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇave]]---to the //brāhmaṇas// and Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave as charity; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of the riches; [[synonyms:a:ardha]]-[[synonyms:d:dhane]]---fifty percent; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:c:cauṭhi]] [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---one-fourth of the riches; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave; [[synonyms:k:kuṭumba]]-[[synonyms:b:bharaṇe]]---to satisfy the relatives.
translation: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī divided the wealth that he brought back home. He gave fifty percent in charity to brāhmaṇas and Vaiṣṇavas and twenty-five percent to his relatives.
purport: This is a practical example of how one should divide his money and retire from household life. Fifty percent of one's money should be distributed to qualified and pure devotees of the Lord. Twenty-five percent may be given to family members, and twenty-five percent may be kept for personal use in case of emergency.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.70
description: Hearing the holy name constantly vibrated by the two brothers, Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya could understand the hints of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> duṅhāra mukhe nirantara kṛṣṇa-nāma śuni'
> bhaṭṭa kahe, prabhura kichu iṅgita-bhaṅgī jāni'
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]] [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the mouths of both Rūpa Gosvāmī and his brother Vallabha; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---continuously; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing the chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:i:iṅgita]]---indications; [[synonyms:b:bhaṅgī]]---hints; [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---understanding.
translation: Hearing the holy name constantly vibrated by the two brothers, Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya could understand the hints of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.71
description: Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya admitted, "Since these two are constantly chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa, how can they be untouchable? On the contrary, they are most exalted."
text:
> 'duṅhāra mukhe kṛṣṇa-nāma kariche nartana
> ei-dui 'adhama' nahe, haya 'sarvottama'
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]] [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the mouths of both; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kariche]]---is doing; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dancing; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:d:dui]]---both of them; [[synonyms:a:adhama]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not fallen; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:u:uttama]]---the most exalted.
translation: Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya admitted, "Since these two are constantly chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa, how can they be untouchable? On the contrary, they are most exalted."
purport: Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya's admission of the brothers' exalted position should serve as a lesson to one who is falsely proud of his position as a //brāhmaṇa.// Sometimes so-called //brāhmaṇas// do not recognize our European and American disciples as devotees or //brāhmaṇas,// and some //brāhmaṇas// are so proud that they do not allow them to enter temples. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu herein gives a great lesson. Although Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya was a great authority on brahmanism and a learned scholar, he admitted that those who chant the Lord's holy name are bona fide //brāhmaṇas// and Vaiṣṇavas and are therefore exalted.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.72
description: Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya then recited the following verse: " 'My dear Lord, one who always keeps Your holy name on his tongue becomes greater than an initiated brāhmaṇa. Although he may be born in a family of dog-eaters and may therefore, by material calculation, be the lowest among men, he is still glorious. This is the wonderful effect of chanting the holy name of the Lord. It is therefore concluded that one who chants the holy name of the Lord should be understood to have performed all kinds of austerities and great sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas. He has already taken his bath in all the holy places of pilgrimage. He has studied all the Vedas, and he is actually an Āryan.' "
text:
> aho bata śva-paco 'to garīyān
> yaj-jihvāgre vartate nāma tubhyam
> tepus tapas te juhuvuḥ sasnur āryā

Although he may be born in a family of dog-eaters and may therefore, by material calculation, be the lowest among men, he is still glorious. This is the wonderful effect of chanting the holy name of the Lord. It is therefore concluded that one who chants the holy name of the Lord should be understood to have performed all kinds of austerities and great sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas. He has already taken his bath in all the holy places of pilgrimage. He has studied all the Vedas, and he is actually an Āryan.' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.73
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to hear Vallabha Bhaṭṭa quoting from śāstra about the position of a devotee. The Lord praised him personally, and, feeling ecstatic love of Godhead, began to quote many verses from śāstra.
text:
> śuni' mahāprabhu tāṅre bahu praśaṁśilā
> premāviṣṭa hañā śloka paḍite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---very much; [[synonyms:p:praśaṁśilā]]---praised; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming ecstatic in love of Godhead; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verses; [[synonyms:p:paḍite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to recite.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to hear Vallabha Bhaṭṭa quoting from śāstra about the position of a devotee. The Lord praised him personally, and, feeling ecstatic love of Godhead, began to quote many verses from śāstra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.74
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, " 'A person who has the pure characteristics of a brāhmaṇa due to devotional service, which is like a blazing fire burning to ashes all the sinful reactions of past lives, is certainly saved from the consequences of sinful acts, such as taking birth in a lower family. Even though he may be born in a family of dog-eaters, he is recognized by learned scholars. However, although a person may be a learned scholar in Vedic knowledge, he is not recognized if he is an atheist.
text:
> śuciḥ sad-bhakti-dīptāgni-
> dagdha-durjāti-kalmaṣaḥ
> śvapāko 'pi budhaiḥ ślāgyo
> na vedajño 'pi nāstikaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuciḥ]]---a //brāhmaṇa// purified internally and externally; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---of devotional service without motives; [[synonyms:d:dīpta]]-[[synonyms:a:agni]]---by the blazing fire; [[synonyms:d:dagdha]]---burnt to ashes; [[synonyms:d:durjāti]]---such as birth in a low family; [[synonyms:k:kalmaṣaḥ]]---whose sinful reactions; [[synonyms:ś:śva]]-[[synonyms:p:pākaḥ]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---even though born in a family of dog-eaters; [[synonyms:b:budhaiḥ]]---by learned scholars; [[synonyms:ś:ślāgyaḥ]]---recognized; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:j:jñaḥ]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---even though completely conversant in Vedic knowledge; [[synonyms:n:nāstikaḥ]]---an atheist.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, " 'A person who has the pure characteristics of a brāhmaṇa due to devotional service, which is like a blazing fire burning to ashes all the sinful reactions of past lives, is certainly saved from the consequences of sinful acts, such as taking birth in a lower family. Even though he may be born in a family of dog-eaters, he is recognized by learned scholars. However, although a person may be a learned scholar in Vedic knowledge, he is not recognized if he is an atheist.
purport: This verse and the next are quoted from the //Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya// (3.11,12), a transcendental literature extracted from the //Purāṇas.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.75
description: " 'For a person devoid of devotional service, birth in a great family or nation, knowledge of revealed scripture, performance of austerities and penance, and chanting of Vedic mantras are all like ornaments on a dead body. Such ornaments simply serve the concocted pleasures of the general populace.' "
text:
> bhagavad-bhakti-hīnasya
> jātiḥ śāstraṁ japas tapaḥ
> aprāṇasyeva dehasya
> maṇḍanaṁ loka-rañjanam
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhagavat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:h:hīnasya]]---of a person devoid of devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:j:jātiḥ]]---birth in a high caste; [[synonyms:ś:śāstram]]---knowledge in revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:j:japaḥ]]---pronunciation of //mantras//; [[synonyms:t:tapaḥ]]---austerities and penances; [[synonyms:a:aprāṇasya]]---which is dead; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:d:dehasya]]---of a body; [[synonyms:m:maṇḍanam]]---decoration; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---to the whims of people in general; [[synonyms:r:rañjanam]]---simply pleasing.
translation: “ 'For a person devoid of devotional service, birth in a great family or nation, knowledge of revealed scripture, performance of austerities and penance, and chanting of Vedic mantras are all like ornaments on a dead body. Such ornaments simply serve the concocted pleasures of the general populace.' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.76
description: When he saw the Lord's ecstatic love, Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya was certainly very astonished. He was also astonished by the Lord's knowledge of the essence of devotional service, as well as by His personal beauty and influence.
text:
> prabhura premāveśa, āra prabhāva bhakti-sāra
> saundaryādi dekhi' bhaṭṭera haila camatkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---ecstasy in love of Godhead; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:prabhāva]]---the influence; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the essence of devotional service; [[synonyms:s:saundarya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---personal beauty and other qualities; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭera]]---of Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonishment.
translation: When he saw the Lord's ecstatic love, Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya was certainly very astonished. He was also astonished by the Lord's knowledge of the essence of devotional service, as well as by His personal beauty and influence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.77
description: Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya then put Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His associates aboard a boat and took them to his own place to offer them lunch.
text:
> sagaṇe prabhure bhaṭṭa naukāte caḍāñā
> bhikṣā dite nija-ghare calilā lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---with His associates; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:n:naukāte]]---a boat; [[synonyms:c:caḍāñā]]---putting aboard; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to offer lunch; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to his own place; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---departed; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking.
translation: Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya then put Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His associates aboard a boat and took them to his own place to offer them lunch.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.78
description: While crossing the River Yamunā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the glossy black water and was immediately bewildered with ecstatic love.
text:
> yamunāra jala dekhi' cikkaṇa śyāmala
> premāveśe mahāprabhu ha-ilā vihvala
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yamunāra]]---of the River Yamunā; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---the water; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:c:cikkaṇa]]---glossy; [[synonyms:ś:śyāmala]]---blackish; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---bewildered.
translation: While crossing the River Yamunā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the glossy black water and was immediately bewildered with ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.79
description: Indeed, as soon as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the River Yamunā, He immediately made a great sound and jumped into the water. Everyone was filled with fear and trembling to see this.
text:
> huṅkāra kari' yamunāra jale dilā jhāṅpa
> prabhu dekhi' sabāra mane haila bhaya-kāṅpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:huṅkāra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making a loud sound; [[synonyms:y:yamunāra]] [[synonyms:j:jale]]---in the water of the River Yamunā; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave; [[synonyms:j:jhāṅpa]]---a plunge; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]-[[synonyms:k:kāṅpa]]---fear and trembling.
translation: Indeed, as soon as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the River Yamunā, He immediately made a great sound and jumped into the water. Everyone was filled with fear and trembling to see this.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.8
description: He kept one-fourth of his wealth with a respectable brāhmaṇa. He kept this for his personal safety because he was expecting some legal complications.
text:
> daṇḍa-bandha lāgi' cauṭhi sañcaya karilā
> bhāla-bhāla vipra-sthāne sthāpya rākhilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:b:bandha]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---in case of legal implications; [[synonyms:c:cauṭhi]]---one-fourth; [[synonyms:s:sañcaya]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---he collected; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāla]]---very respectable; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in the custody of a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:s:sthāpya]] [[synonyms:r:rākhilā]]---kept deposited.
translation: He kept one-fourth of his wealth with a respectable brāhmaṇa. He kept this for his personal safety because he was expecting some legal complications.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.80
description: They all hastily grabbed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and pulled Him out of the water. Once on the boat's platform, the Lord began to dance.
text:
> āste-vyaste sabe dhari' prabhure uṭhāila
> naukāra upare prabhu nācite lāgila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āste]]-[[synonyms:v:vyaste]]---with great haste; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāila]]---raised; [[synonyms:n:naukāra]]---of the boat; [[synonyms:u:upare]]---on top; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nācite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began to dance.
translation: They all hastily grabbed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and pulled Him out of the water. Once on the boat's platform, the Lord began to dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.81
description: Due to the Lord's heavy weight, the boat began to tilt. It began filling up with water and was on the verge of sinking.
text:
> mahāprabhura bhare naukā kare ṭalamala
> ḍubite lāgila naukā, jhalake bhare jala
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhare]]---because of the weight; [[synonyms:n:naukā]]---the boat; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭalamala]]---tilting; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍubite]]---to sink; [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began; [[synonyms:n:naukā]]---the boat; [[synonyms:j:jhalake]]---in gushes; [[synonyms:b:bhare]]---fills; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---water.
translation: Due to the Lord's heavy weight, the boat began to tilt. It began filling up with water and was on the verge of sinking.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.82
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu tried to restrain Himself as far as possible before Vallabhācārya, but although He tried to keep calm, His ecstatic love could not be checked.
text:
> yadyapi bhaṭṭera āge prabhura dhairya haila mana
> durvāra udbhaṭa prema nahe samvaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭera]]---of Vallabhācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dhairya]]---patient; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:d:durvāra]]---difficult to stop; [[synonyms:u:udbhaṭa]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---ecstatic love; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---there is not; [[synonyms:s:samvaraṇa]]---checking.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu tried to restrain Himself as far as possible before Vallabhācārya, but although He tried to keep calm, His ecstatic love could not be checked.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.83
description: Seeing the circumstances, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally became calm so that the boat was able to reach the shore of Āḍāila and land there.
text:
> deśa-pātra dekhi' mahāprabhu dhairya ha-ila
> āḍāilera ghāṭe naukā āsi' uttarila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:deśa]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the circumstances; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dhairya]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became calm; [[synonyms:ā:āḍāilera]] [[synonyms:g:ghāṭe]]---at the shore of the village Āḍāila; [[synonyms:n:naukā]]---the boat; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:u:uttarila]]---landed.
translation: Seeing the circumstances, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally became calm so that the boat was able to reach the shore of Āḍāila and land there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.84
description: Fearing for the Lord's welfare, Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya stayed in His association. After arranging for the Lord's bath, he took Him to his own house.
text:
> bhaye bhaṭṭa saṅge rahe, madhyāhna karāñā
> nija-gṛhe ānilā prabhure saṅgete lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---with fear; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's association; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:m:madhyāhna]] [[synonyms:k:karāñā]]---after arranging for His bath; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---to his own home; [[synonyms:ā:ānilā]]---brought; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:saṅgete]]---in company; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking.
translation: Fearing for the Lord's welfare, Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya stayed in His association. After arranging for the Lord's bath, he took Him to his own house.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.85
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at his home, Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya, being greatly pleased, offered the Lord a nice sitting place and personally washed His feet.
text:
> ānandita hañā bhaṭṭa dila divyāsana
> āpane karila prabhura pāda-prakṣālana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming pleased; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsana]]---a nice sitting place; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:prakṣālana]]---washing of the feet.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at his home, Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya, being greatly pleased, offered the Lord a nice sitting place and personally washed His feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.86
description: Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya and his whole family then sprinkled that water over their heads. They then offered the Lord new underwear and outer garments.
text:
> savaṁśe sei jala mastake dharila
> nūtana kaupīna-bahirvāsa parāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:v:vaṁśe]]---with all the family members; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---water; [[synonyms:m:mastake]]---on the head; [[synonyms:d:dharila]]---sprinkled; [[synonyms:n:nūtana]]---fresh; [[synonyms:k:kaupīna]]---underwear; [[synonyms:b:bahirvāsa]]---external covering; [[synonyms:p:parāila]]---put on.
translation: Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya and his whole family then sprinkled that water over their heads. They then offered the Lord new underwear and outer garments.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.87
description: Vallabhācārya worshiped the Lord with great pomp, offering scents, incense, flowers and lamps, and with great respect he induced Balabhadra Bhaṭṭa [the Lord's cook] to cook.
text:
> gandha-puṣpa-dhūpa-dīpe mahā-pūjā kaila
> bhaṭṭācārye mānya kari' pāka karāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gandha]]---scents; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]---flowers; [[synonyms:d:dhūpa]]---incense; [[synonyms:d:dīpe]]---by lamps; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:pūjā]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---he worshiped the Lord with great pomp; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārye]]---to Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:m:mānya]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---offering respect; [[synonyms:p:pāka]] [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---engaging in cooking.
translation: Vallabhācārya worshiped the Lord with great pomp, offering scents, incense, flowers and lamps, and with great respect he induced Balabhadra Bhaṭṭa [the Lord's cook] to cook.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.88
description: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was offered lunch with great care and affection. The brothers Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrī Vallabha were also offered food.
text:
> bhikṣā karāila prabhure sasneha yatane
> rūpa-gosāñi dui-bhāiye karāila bhojane
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---made take His lunch; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sasneha]]---with affection; [[synonyms:y:yatane]]---with great care; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāiye]]---the two brothers; [[synonyms:k:karāila]] [[synonyms:b:bhojane]]---made eat.
translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was offered lunch with great care and affection. The brothers Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrī Vallabha were also offered food.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.89
description: Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya first offered the remnants of the Lord's food to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and then to Kṛṣṇadāsa.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya śrī-rūpe deoyāila 'avaśeṣa'
> tabe sei prasāda kṛṣṇadāsa pāila śeṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:d:deoyāila]]---offered; [[synonyms:a:avaśeṣa]]---the remnants; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---remnants of food; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]---the balance.
translation: Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya first offered the remnants of the Lord's food to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and then to Kṛṣṇadāsa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.9
description: He deposited ten thousand coins, which were later spent by Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, in the custody of a local Bengali grocer.
text:
> gauḍe rākhila mudrā daśa-hājāre
> sanātana vyaya kare, rākhe mudi-ghare
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍe]]---in Bengal; [[synonyms:r:rākhila]]---kept; [[synonyms:m:mudrā]]---coins; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:h:hājāre]]---ten thousand; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---his elder brother; [[synonyms:v:vyaya]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---spent; [[synonyms:r:rākhe]]---deposited; [[synonyms:m:mudi]]-[[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in the place of a local grocer.
translation: He deposited ten thousand coins, which were later spent by Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, in the custody of a local Bengali grocer.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.90
description: The Lord was then given spices to purify His mouth. Afterwards He was made to rest, and Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya personally massaged His legs.
text:
> mukha-vāsa diyā prabhure karāila śayana
> āpane bhaṭṭa karena prabhura pāda-samvāhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukha]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---spices; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---offering; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---made to do; [[synonyms:ś:śayana]]---resting; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Śrīla Vallabha Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:s:samvāhana]]---massaging the leg.
translation: The Lord was then given spices to purify His mouth. Afterwards He was made to rest, and Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya personally massaged His legs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.91
description: While Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya was massaging Him, the Lord asked him to go take prasāda. After taking prasāda, he returned to the lotus feet of the Lord.
text:
> prabhu pāṭhāila tāṅre karite bhojane
> bhojana kari' āilā teṅho prabhura caraṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāila]]---sent; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him (Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya); [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:b:bhojane]]---to take his lunch; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---after taking lunch; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---to the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: While Vallabha Bhaṭṭācārya was massaging Him, the Lord asked him to go take prasāda. After taking prasāda, he returned to the lotus feet of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.92
description: At that time there arrived Raghupati Upādhyāya, who belonged to the Tiruhitā district. He was a very learned scholar, a great devotee and a respectable gentleman.
text:
> hena-kāle āilā raghupati upādhyāya
> tiruhitā paṇḍita, baḍa vaiṣṇava, mahāśaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:r:raghupati]] [[synonyms:u:upādhyāya]]---a //brāhmaṇa// named Raghupati Upādhyāya; [[synonyms:t:tiruhitā]]---belonging to the Tiruhitā state; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---a very learned scholar; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---great; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotee; [[synonyms:m:mahāśaya]]---respectable gentleman.
translation:
At that time there arrived Raghupati Upādhyāya, who belonged to the Tiruhitā district. He was a very learned scholar, a great devotee and a respectable gentleman.


Tiruhitā, or Tirhuṭiyā, is a combination of four districts in Behar: Sāraṇa, Campāraṇa, Majahphara-pura and Dvārabhāṅgā. The people of this state are called Tiruṭiyā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.93
description: Raghupati Upādhyāya first offered his respects to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the Lord gave him His blessings, saying, "Always stay in Kṛṣṇa consciousness."
text:
> āsi' teṅho kaila prabhura caraṇa vandana
> 'kṛṣṇe mati rahu' bali' prabhura vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---worshiping the lotus feet; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]] [[synonyms:m:mati]] [[synonyms:r:rahu]]---just remain always Kṛṣṇa conscious; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---the blessings of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Raghupati Upādhyāya first offered his respects to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the Lord gave him His blessings, saying, "Always stay in Kṛṣṇa consciousness."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.94
description: Raghupati Upādhyāya was very pleased to hear the Lord's blessings. The Lord then asked him to describe Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> śuni' ānandita haila upādhyāyera mana
> prabhu tāṅre kahila,---'kaha kṛṣṇera varṇana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very pleased; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:u:upādhyāyera]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind of Upādhyāya; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to him; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---spoke; [[synonyms:k:kaha]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---just try to describe Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Raghupati Upādhyāya was very pleased to hear the Lord's blessings. The Lord then asked him to describe Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.95
description: When Raghupati Upādhyāya was requested to describe Kṛṣṇa, he began to recite some verses he had personally composed about Kṛṣṇa's pastimes. Hearing those verses, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was overwhelmed with ecstatic love.
text:
> nija-kṛta kṛṣṇa-līlā-śloka paḍila
> śuni' mahāprabhura mahā premāveśa haila

translation: When Raghupati Upādhyāya was requested to describe Kṛṣṇa, he began to recite some verses he had personally composed about Kṛṣṇa's pastimes. Hearing those verses, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was overwhelmed with ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.96
description: Raghupati Upādhyāya recited: "Those who are afraid of material existence worship Vedic literature. Some worship smṛti, the corollaries to Vedic literature, and others worship the Mahābhārata. As far as I am concerned, I worship Mahārāja Nanda, the father of Kṛṣṇa, in whose courtyard the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Absolute Truth, is playing."
text:
> śrutim apare smṛtim itare
> bhāratam anye bhajantu bhava-bhītāḥ
> aham iha nandaṁ vande
> yasyālinde paraṁ brahma

translation: Raghupati Upādhyāya recited: "Those who are afraid of material existence worship Vedic literature. Some worship smṛti, the corollaries to Vedic literature, and others worship the Mahābhārata. As far as I am concerned, I worship Mahārāja Nanda, the father of Kṛṣṇa, in whose courtyard the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Absolute Truth, is playing."
purport: This verse recited by Raghupati Upādhyāya was later included in Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī's //Padyāvalī// (126).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.97
description: When Raghupati Upādhyāya was requested by the Lord to recite more, he immediately offered his respects to the Lord and granted His request.
text:
> 'āge kaha'---prabhu-vākye upādhyāya kahila
> raghupati upādhyāya namaskāra kaila

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 19.98
description: "To whom can I speak who will believe me when I say that Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is hunting the gopīs in the bushes by the banks of the River Yamunā? In this way the Lord demonstrates His pastimes."
text:
> kaṁ prati kathayitum īśe
> samprati ko vā pratītim āyātu
> go-pati-tanayā-kuñje
> gopa-vadhūṭī-viṭaṁ brahma
