translation: "If by chance such a moment comes when I can once again see Kṛṣṇa, then I shall worship those seconds, moments and hours with flower garlands and pulp of sandalwood and decorate them with all kinds of jewels and ornaments."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.39
description: In an instant, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu regained external consciousness and saw two persons before Him. Questioning them, He asked, "Am I conscious? What dreams have I been seeing? What craziness have I spoken? Have you heard some expressions of humility?''
text:
> kṣaṇe bāhya haila mana, āge dekhe dui jana,
> tāṅre puche,---āmi nā caitanya?
> svapna-prāya ki dekhinu, kibā āmi pralāpinu,
> tomarā kichu śuniyācha dainya?
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---in an instant; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---outside; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto them; [[synonyms:p:puche]]---inquires; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---conscious; [[synonyms:s:svapna]]-[[synonyms:p:prāya]]---almost dreaming; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:d:dekhinu]]---I have seen; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---what; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:p:pralāpinu]]---spoke in craziness; [[synonyms:t:tomarā]]---you; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyācha]]---have heard; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]---humility.
translation: In an instant, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu regained external consciousness and saw two persons before Him. Questioning them, He asked, "Am I conscious? What dreams have I been seeing? What craziness have I spoken? Have you heard some expressions of humility?''
purport: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus spoke in ecstasy, He saw two persons before Him. One was His secretary, Svarūpa Dāmodara, and the other was Rāya Rāmānanda. Coming to His external consciousness, He saw them both present, and although He was still talking in the ecstasy of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, He immediately began to question whether He was the same Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.4
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's state of mind, day and night, was practically identical to Rādhārāṇī's state of mind when Uddhava came to Vṛndāvana to see the gopīs.
text:
> śrī-rādhikāra ceṣṭā yena uddhava-darśane
> ei-mata daśā prabhura haya rātri-dine
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rādhikāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:c:ceṣṭā]]---the activities; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---just like; [[synonyms:u:uddhava]]-[[synonyms:d:darśane]]---in seeing Uddhava at Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---the condition; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---day and night.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's state of mind, day and night, was practically identical to Rādhārāṇī's state of mind when Uddhava came to Vṛndāvana to see the gopīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.40
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "My dear friends, you are all My life and soul; therefore I tell you that I possess no wealth of love for Kṛṣṇa. Consequently My life is poverty-stricken. My limbs and senses are useless."
text:
> śuna mora prāṇera bāndhava
> nāhi kṛṣṇa-prema-dhana, daridra mora jīvana,
> dehendriya vṛthā mora saba
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---kindly hear; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:p:prāṇera]]---of life; [[synonyms:b:bāndhava]]---friends; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is none; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---wealth of love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:daridra]]---poverty-stricken; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---life; [[synonyms:d:deha]]-[[synonyms:i:indriya]]---all the limbs and senses of My body; [[synonyms:v:vṛthā]]---fruitless; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "My dear friends, you are all My life and soul; therefore I tell you that I possess no wealth of love for Kṛṣṇa. Consequently My life is poverty-stricken. My limbs and senses are useless."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.41
description: Again He addressed both Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāya Rāmānanda, speaking despondently, "Alas! My friends, you can now know the certainty within My heart, and after knowing My heart you should judge whether I am correct or not. You can speak of this properly." Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then began to chant another verse.
text:
> punaḥ kahe,---hāya hāya, śuna, svarūpa-rāmarāya,
> ei mora hṛdaya-niścaya
> śuni karaha vicāra, haya, naya---kaha sāra,
> eta bali' śloka uccāraya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:h:hāya]] [[synonyms:h:hāya]]---alas; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---kindly hear; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:r:rāya]]---My dear Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]-[[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---the certainty in My heart; [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---hearing; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---just make; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---judgment; [[synonyms:h:haya,]] [[synonyms:n:naya]]---correct or not; [[synonyms:k:kaha]] [[synonyms:s:sāra]]---tell Me the essence; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---another verse; [[synonyms:u:uccāraya]]---recites.
translation: Again He addressed both Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāya Rāmānanda, speaking despondently, "Alas! My friends, you can now know the certainty within My heart, and after knowing My heart you should judge whether I am correct or not. You can speak of this properly." Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then began to chant another verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.42
description: " 'Love of Godhead, devoid of cheating propensities, is not possible within this material world. If there is such a love, there cannot be separation, for if there is separation, how can one live?'
text:
> ka-i-avarahi-aṁ pemmaṁ ṇa hi hoi māṇuse loe
> ja-i hoi kassa virahe hontammi ko jīa-i
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:ka]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]-[[synonyms:a:avarahi]]-[[synonyms:a:am]]---without any cheating propensity, without any motive concerning the four principles of material existence (namely, religiosity, economic development, sense gratification and liberation); [[synonyms:p:pemmam]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:ṇ:ṇa]]---never; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:h:hoi]]---becomes; [[synonyms:m:māṇuse]]---in human society; [[synonyms:l:loe]]---in this world; [[synonyms:j:ja]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---if; [[synonyms:h:hoi]]---there is; [[synonyms:k:kassa]]---whose; [[synonyms:v:virahe]]---in separation; [[synonyms:h:hontammi]]---is; [[synonyms:k:ko]]---who; [[synonyms:j:jīa]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---lives.
translation: “ 'Love of Godhead, devoid of cheating propensities, is not possible within this material world. If there is such a love, there cannot be separation, for if there is separation, how can one live?'
purport: This is a verse in a common language called //prākṛta,// and the exact Sanskrit transformation is //kaitava-rahitaṁ premā na hi bhavati mānuṣe loke yadi bhavati kasya viraho virahe saty api ko jīvati.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.43
description: "Pure love for Kṛṣṇa, just like gold from the Jāmbū River, does not exist in human society. If it existed, there could not be separation. If separation were there, one could not live."
text:
> akaitava kṛṣṇa-prema, yena jāmbūnada-hema,
> sei premā nṛloke nā haya
> yadi haya tāra yoga, nā haya tabe viyoga,
> viyoga haile keha nā jīyaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:akaitava]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]---unalloyed love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---like; [[synonyms:j:jāmbū]]-[[synonyms:n:nada]]-[[synonyms:h:hema]]---gold from the Jāmbū River; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:premā]]---that love of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:nṛ]]-[[synonyms:l:loke]]---in the material world; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is not possible; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---with it; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]---connection; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:v:viyoga]]---separation; [[synonyms:v:viyoga]]---separation; [[synonyms:h:haile]]---if there is; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:j:jīyaya]]---cannot live.
translation: "Pure love for Kṛṣṇa, just like gold from the Jāmbū River, does not exist in human society. If it existed, there could not be separation. If separation were there, one could not live."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.44
description: Thus speaking, the son of Śrīmatī Śacīmātā recited another wonderful verse, and Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara heard this verse with rapt attention. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I feel shameful to disclose the activities of My heart. Nonetheless, I shall be done with all formalities and speak from the heart. Please hear."
text:
> eta kahi' śacī-suta, śloka paḍe adbhuta,
> śune duṅhe eka-mana hañā
> āpana-hṛdaya-kāja, kahite vāsiye lāja,
> tabu kahi lāja-bīja khāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---thus saying; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:s:suta]]---the son of Śrīmatī Śacīmātā; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verse; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---recites; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hear; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---the two persons; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---with rapt attention; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]-[[synonyms:k:kāja]]---the activities of one's own heart; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:v:vāsiye]]---I feel; [[synonyms:l:lāja]]---shameful; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I speak; [[synonyms:l:lāja]]-[[synonyms:b:bīja]]---the seed of bashfulness; [[synonyms:k:khāñā]]---finishing.
translation: Thus speaking, the son of Śrīmatī Śacīmātā recited another wonderful verse, and Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara heard this verse with rapt attention. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I feel shameful to disclose the activities of My heart. Nonetheless, I shall be done with all formalities and speak from the heart. Please hear."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.45
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, " 'My dear friends, I have not the slightest tinge of love of Godhead within My heart. When you see Me crying in separation, I am just falsely exhibiting a demonstration of My great fortune. Indeed, not seeing the beautiful face of Kṛṣṇa playing His flute, I continue to live My life like an insect, without purpose.'
text:
> na prema-gandho 'sti darāpi me harau
> krandāmi saubhāgya-bharaṁ prakāśitum
> vaṁśī-vilāsy-ānana-lokanaṁ vinā
> bibharmi yat prāṇa-pataṅgakān vṛthā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---never; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:g:gandhaḥ]]---a scent of love of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:asti]]---there is; [[synonyms:d:darā]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---even in a slight proportion; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:h:harau]]---in the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:krandāmi]]---I cry; [[synonyms:s:saubhāgya]]-[[synonyms:b:bharam]]---the volume of My fortune; [[synonyms:p:prakāśitum]]---to exhibit; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsi]]---of the great flute-player; [[synonyms:ā:ānana]]---at the face; [[synonyms:l:lokanam]]---looking; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:b:bibharmi]]---I carry; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---because; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pataṅgakān]]---My insectlike life; [[synonyms:v:vṛthā]]---with no purpose.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, " 'My dear friends, I have not the slightest tinge of love of Godhead within My heart. When you see Me crying in separation, I am just falsely exhibiting a demonstration of My great fortune. Indeed, not seeing the beautiful face of Kṛṣṇa playing His flute, I continue to live My life like an insect, without purpose.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.46
description: "Actually, My love for Kṛṣṇa is far, far away. Whatever I do is actually false. When you see Me cry, I am simply exhibiting My great fortune. Please try to understand this beyond a doubt.
text:
> dūre śuddha-prema-gandha, kapaṭa premera bandha,
> seha mora nāhi kṛṣṇa-pāya
> tabe ye kari krandana, sva-saubhāgya prakhyāpana,
> kari, ihā jāniha niścaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dūre]]---far away; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:g:gandha]]---a scent of pure devotional love; [[synonyms:k:kapaṭa]]---false; [[synonyms:p:premera]]---of love of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bandha]]---binding; [[synonyms:s:seha]]---that; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pāya]]---at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---but; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I do; [[synonyms:k:krandana]]---crying; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:s:saubhāgya]]---My own fortune; [[synonyms:p:prakhyāpana]]---demonstration; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I do; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:j:jāniha]]---know; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---certainly.
translation: "Actually, My love for Kṛṣṇa is far, far away. Whatever I do is actually false. When you see Me cry, I am simply exhibiting My great fortune. Please try to understand this beyond a doubt.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.47
description: "Even though I do not see the moonlike face of Kṛṣṇa playing on His flute and although there is no possibility of My meeting Him, still I take care of My own body. That is the way of lust. In this way, I maintain My flylike life.
text:
> yāte vaṁśī-dhvani-sukha, nā dekhi' se cāṅda mukha,
> yadyapi nāhika 'ālambana'
> nija-dehe kari prīti, kevala kāmera rīti,
> prāṇa-kīṭera kariye dhāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---in which; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]---the happiness of hearing the playing of the flute; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---not seeing; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:c:cāṅda]] [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---moonlike face; [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:a:'ālambana']]---the meeting of the lover and beloved; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---own; [[synonyms:d:dehe]]---in the body; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I do; [[synonyms:p:prīti]]---affection; [[synonyms:k:kevala]]---only; [[synonyms:k:kāmera]]---of lust; [[synonyms:r:rīti]]---the way; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]---of life; [[synonyms:k:kīṭera]]---of the fly; [[synonyms:k:kariye]]---I do; [[synonyms:d:dhāraṇa]]---continuing.
translation: "Even though I do not see the moonlike face of Kṛṣṇa playing on His flute and although there is no possibility of My meeting Him, still I take care of My own body. That is the way of lust. In this way, I maintain My flylike life.
purport: In this connection, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that the lovable Supreme Lord is the supreme shelter. The Lord is the supreme subject, and the devotees are the object. The coming together of a subject and object is called //ālambana.// The object hears, and the subject plays the flute. That the object cannot see the moonlike face of Kṛṣṇa and has no eagerness to see Him is the sign of being without //ālambana.// Externally imagining such a thing simply satisfies one's lusty desires, and thus one lives without purpose.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.48
description: "Love for Lord Kṛṣṇa is very pure, just like the waters of the Ganges. That love is an ocean of nectar. That pure attachment to Kṛṣṇa does not conceal any spot, which would appear just like a spot of ink on a white cloth.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-premā sunirmala, yena śuddha-gaṅgā-jala,
> sei premā---amṛtera sindhu
> nirmala se anurāge, nā lukāya anya dāge,
> śukla-vastre yaiche masī-bindu
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:premā]]---love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:n:nirmala]]---without material contamination; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---exactly like; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:j:jala]]---the pure water of the Ganges; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:premā]]---that love; [[synonyms:a:amṛtera]] [[synonyms:s:sindhu]]---the ocean of nectar; [[synonyms:n:nirmala]]---pure; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:a:anurāge]]---attraction; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:l:lukāya]]---does not conceal; [[synonyms:a:anya]]---other; [[synonyms:d:dāge]]---spot; [[synonyms:ś:śukla]]-[[synonyms:v:vastre]]---on white cloth; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:m:masī]]-[[synonyms:b:bindu]]---a spot of ink.
translation: "Love for Lord Kṛṣṇa is very pure, just like the waters of the Ganges. That love is an ocean of nectar. That pure attachment to Kṛṣṇa does not conceal any spot, which would appear just like a spot of ink on a white cloth.
purport: Unalloyed love of Kṛṣṇa is just like a big sheet of white cloth. Absence of attachment is compared to a black spot on that white cloth. Just as the black spot is prominent, so the absence of love of Godhead is prominent on the platform of pure love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.49
description: "Unalloyed love of Kṛṣṇa is like an ocean of happiness. If someone gets one drop of it, the whole world can drown in that drop. It is not befitting to express such love of Godhead, yet a madman must speak. However, even though he speaks, no one believes him."
text:
> śuddha-prema-sukha-sindhu, pāi tāra eka bindu,
> sei bindu jagat ḍubāya
> kahibāra yogya naya, tathāpi bāule kaya,
> kahile vā kebā pātiyāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]---unalloyed love; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:s:sindhu]]---an ocean of happiness; [[synonyms:p:pāi]]---if I get; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:b:bindu]]---drop; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:b:bindu]]---that drop; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the whole world; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍubāya]]---drowns; [[synonyms:k:kahibāra]]---to speak; [[synonyms:y:yogya]] [[synonyms:n:naya]]---is not fit; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:b:bāule]]---a madman; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---speaks; [[synonyms:k:kahile]]---if spoken; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:k:kebā]] [[synonyms:p:pātiyāya]]---who believes.
translation: "Unalloyed love of Kṛṣṇa is like an ocean of happiness. If someone gets one drop of it, the whole world can drown in that drop. It is not befitting to express such love of Godhead, yet a madman must speak. However, even though he speaks, no one believes him."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.5
description: The Lord constantly exhibited a state of mind reflecting the madness of separation. All His activities were based on forgetfulness, and His talks were always based on madness.
text:
> nirantara haya prabhura viraha-unmāda
> bhrama-maya ceṣṭā sadā, pralāpa-maya vāda
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---constantly; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:v:viraha]]---of separation; [[synonyms:u:unmāda]]---the madness; [[synonyms:b:bhrama]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---forgetful; [[synonyms:c:ceṣṭā]]---activities; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:p:pralāpa]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---full of delirium; [[synonyms:v:vāda]]---talking.
translation: The Lord constantly exhibited a state of mind reflecting the madness of separation. All His activities were based on forgetfulness, and His talks were always based on madness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.50
description: In this way, Lord Caitanya used to revel in ecstasy day after day and exhibit these ecstasies before Svarūpa and Rāmānanda Rāya. Externally there appeared severe tribulation, as if He were suffering from poisonous effects, but internally He was experiencing bliss. This is characteristic of transcendental love of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> ei mata dine dine, svarūpa-rāmānanda-sane,
> nija-bhāva karena vidita
> bāhye viṣa-jvālā haya, bhitare ānanda-maya,
> kṛṣṇa-premāra adbhuta carita
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:d:dine]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---day after day; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---own; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---ecstasy; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---makes; [[synonyms:v:vidita]]---known; [[synonyms:b:bāhye]]---externally; [[synonyms:v:viṣa]]-[[synonyms:j:jvālā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is suffering from poisonous effects; [[synonyms:b:bhitare]]---within; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---transcendental ecstasy; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:premāra]]---of love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:c:carita]]---characteristic.
translation: In this way, Lord Caitanya used to revel in ecstasy day after day and exhibit these ecstasies before Svarūpa and Rāmānanda Rāya. Externally there appeared severe tribulation, as if He were suffering from poisonous effects, but internally He was experiencing bliss. This is characteristic of transcendental love of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.51
description: If one tastes such love of Godhead, he can compare it to hot sugarcane. When one chews hot sugarcane, his mouth burns, yet he cannot give it up. Similarly, if one has but a little love of Godhead, he can perceive its powerful effects. It can only be compared to poison and nectar mixed together.
text:
> ei premā-āsvādana, tapta-ikṣu-carvaṇa,
> mukha jvale, nā yāya tyajana
> sei premā yāṅra mane, tāra vikrama sei jāne,
> viṣāmṛte ekatra milana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasting; [[synonyms:t:tapta]]---hot; [[synonyms:i:ikṣu]]-[[synonyms:c:carvaṇa]]---chewing sugarcane; [[synonyms:m:mukha]] [[synonyms:j:jvale]]---the mouth burns; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]] [[synonyms:t:tyajana]]---still not possible to give up; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]] [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in someone's mind; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:v:vikrama]]---the power; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---he knows; [[synonyms:v:viṣa]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛte]]---poison and nectar; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]]---in oneness; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting.
translation: If one tastes such love of Godhead, he can compare it to hot sugarcane. When one chews hot sugarcane, his mouth burns, yet he cannot give it up. Similarly, if one has but a little love of Godhead, he can perceive its powerful effects. It can only be compared to poison and nectar mixed together.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.52
description: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu spoke, " 'My dear beautiful friend, if one develops love of Godhead, love of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja, all the bitter and sweet influences of this love will manifest in one's heart. Such love of Godhead acts in two ways. The poisonous effects of love of Godhead defeat the severe and fresh poison of the serpent. Yet there is simultaneously transcendental bliss, which pours down and defeats the pride of nectar and diminishes its value. In other words, love of Kṛṣṇa is so powerful that it simultaneously defeats the poisonous effects of a snake, as well as the happiness derived from pouring nectar on one's head. It is perceived as doubly effective, simultaneously poisonous and nectarean.' "
text:
> pīḍābhir nava-kāla-kūṭa-kaṭutā-garvasya nirvāsano
> nisyandena mudāṁ sudhā-madhurimāhaṅkāra-saṅkocanaḥ
> premā sundari nanda-nandana-paro jāgarti yasyāntare
> jñāyante sphuṭam asya vakra-madhurās tenaiva vikrāntayaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pīḍābhiḥ]]---by the sufferings; [[synonyms:n:nava]]---fresh; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]-[[synonyms:k:kūṭa]]---of poison; [[synonyms:k:kaṭutā]]---of the severity; [[synonyms:g:garvasya]]---of pride; [[synonyms:n:nirvāsanaḥ]]---banishment; [[synonyms:n:nisyandena]]---by pouring down; [[synonyms:m:mudām]]---happiness; [[synonyms:s:sudhā]]---of nectar; [[synonyms:m:madhurimā]]---of the sweetness; [[synonyms:a:ahaṅkāra]]---the pride; [[synonyms:s:saṅkocanaḥ]]---minimizing; [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love; [[synonyms:s:sundari]]---beautiful friend; [[synonyms:n:nanda]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]-[[synonyms:p:paraḥ]]---fixed upon the son of Mahārāja Nanda; [[synonyms:j:jāgarti]]---develops; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---in the heart; [[synonyms:j:jñāyante]]---are perceived; [[synonyms:s:sphuṭam]]---explicitly; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of that; [[synonyms:v:vakra]]---crooked; [[synonyms:m:madhurāḥ]]---and sweet; [[synonyms:t:tena]]---by him; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---alone; [[synonyms:v:vikrāntayaḥ]]---the influences.
translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu spoke, " 'My dear beautiful friend, if one develops love of Godhead, love of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja, all the bitter and sweet influences of this love will manifest in one's heart. Such love of Godhead acts in two ways. The poisonous effects of love of Godhead defeat the severe and fresh poison of the serpent. Yet there is simultaneously transcendental bliss, which pours down and defeats the pride of nectar and diminishes its value. In other words, love of Kṛṣṇa is so powerful that it simultaneously defeats the poisonous effects of a snake, as well as the happiness derived from pouring nectar on one's head. It is perceived as doubly effective, simultaneously poisonous and nectarean.' "
purport: This verse is spoken by Paurṇamāsī to Nāndīmukhī in the //Vidagdha-mādhava// (2.18), by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.53
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would see Jagannātha along with Balarāma and Subhadrā, He would immediately think that He had reached Kurukṣetra, where all of them had come. He would think that His life was successful because He had seen the lotus-eyed one, whom, if seen, pacifies the body, mind and eyes.
text:
> ye kāle dekhe jagannātha-śrīrāma-subhadrā-sātha,
> tabe jāne---āilāma kurukṣetra
> saphala haila jīvana, dekhiluṅ padma-locana,
> juḍāila tanu-mana-netra
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time when; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---He sees; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rāma]]---Balarāma; [[synonyms:s:subhadrā]]---Subhadrā; [[synonyms:s:sātha]]---with; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---knows; [[synonyms:ā:āilāma]]---I have come; [[synonyms:k:kurukṣetra]]---to the pilgrimage site known as Kurukṣetra; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]---successful; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---has become; [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---life; [[synonyms:d:dekhiluṅ]]---I have seen; [[synonyms:p:padma]]-[[synonyms:l:locana]]---the lotus eyes; [[synonyms:j:juḍāila]]---pacified; [[synonyms:t:tanu]]---body; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:n:netra]]---eyes.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would see Jagannātha along with Balarāma and Subhadrā, He would immediately think that He had reached Kurukṣetra, where all of them had come. He would think that His life was successful because He had seen the lotus-eyed one, whom, if seen, pacifies the body, mind and eyes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.54
description: Staying near the Garuḍa-stambha, the Lord would look upon Lord Jagannātha. What can be said about the strength of that love? On the ground beneath the column of the Garuḍa-stambha was a deep ditch, and that ditch was filled with the water of His tears.
text:
> garuḍera sannidhāne, rahi' kare daraśane,
> se ānandera ki kahiba ba'le
> garuḍa-stambhera tale, āche eka nimna khāle,
> se khāla bharila aśru-jale
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:garuḍera]]---Garuḍa; [[synonyms:s:sannidhāne]]---near; [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---staying; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:ā:ānandera]]---of that bliss; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:k:kahiba]]---I shall say; [[synonyms:b:ba'le]]---on the strength; [[synonyms:g:garuḍa]]---of the statue of Garuḍa; [[synonyms:s:stambhera]]---of the column; [[synonyms:t:tale]]---underneath; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there is; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:n:nimna]]---low; [[synonyms:k:khāle]]---ditch; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:k:khāla]]---that ditch; [[synonyms:b:bharila]]---became filled; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]-[[synonyms:j:jale]]---with the water of tears.
translation: Staying near the Garuḍa-stambha, the Lord would look upon Lord Jagannātha. What can be said about the strength of that love? On the ground beneath the column of the Garuḍa-stambha was a deep ditch, and that ditch was filled with the water of His tears.
purport: In front of the temple of Jagannātha is a column on which the statue of Garuḍa is situated. It is called the Garuḍa-stambha. At the base of that column is a ditch, and that ditch was filled with the tears of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.55
description: When coming from the Jagannātha temple to return to His house, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to sit on the ground and mark it with His nails. At such times He would be greatly morose and would cry, "Alas, where is Vṛndāvana? Where is Kṛṣṇa, the son of the King of the cowherd men? Where is that person who plays the flute?"
text:
> tāhāṅ haite ghare āsi', māṭīra upare vasi',
> nakhe kare pṛthivī likhana
> hā-hā kāhāṅ vṛndāvana, kāhāṅ gopendra-nandana,
> kāhāṅ sei vaṁśī-vadana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from there; [[synonyms:g:ghare]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming back home; [[synonyms:m:māṭīra]]---the ground; [[synonyms:u:upare]]---upon; [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting; [[synonyms:n:nakhe]]---by the nails; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:p:pṛthivī]]---on the surface of the earth; [[synonyms:l:likhana]]---marking; [[synonyms:h:hā]]-[[synonyms:h:hā]]---alas; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where is; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of the King of the cowherd men; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:v:vadana]]---the person with the flute.
translation: When coming from the Jagannātha temple to return to His house, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to sit on the ground and mark it with His nails. At such times He would be greatly morose and would cry, "Alas, where is Vṛndāvana? Where is Kṛṣṇa, the son of the King of the cowherd men? Where is that person who plays the flute?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.56
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to lament by saying, "Where is Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose form is curved in three places? Where is the sweet song of His flute, and where is the bank of the Yamunā? Where is the rāsa dance? Where is that dancing, singing, and laughing? Where is My Lord, Madana-mohana, the enchanter of Cupid?"
text:
> kāhāṅ se tri-bhaṅga-ṭhāma, kāhāṅ sei veṇu-gāna,
> kāhāṅ sei yamunā-pulina
> kāhāṅ se rāsa-vilāsa, kāhāṅ nṛtya-gīta-hāsa,
> kāhāṅ prabhu madana-mohana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṅga]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāma]]---figure curved in three places; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---//where//; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:veṇu]]-[[synonyms:g:gāna]]---sweet song of the flute; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]-[[synonyms:p:pulina]]---bank of the Yamunā River; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]-[[synonyms:h:hāsa]]---dancing, music and laughing; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---My Lord; [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mohana]]---the enchanter of Madana (Cupid).
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to lament by saying, "Where is Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose form is curved in three places? Where is the sweet song of His flute, and where is the bank of the Yamunā? Where is the rāsa dance? Where is that dancing, singing, and laughing? Where is My Lord, Madana-mohana, the enchanter of Cupid?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.57
description: In this way various ecstatic emotions evolved, and the Lord's mind filled with anxiety. He could not escape even for a moment. In this way, because of fierce feelings of separation, His patience began to totter, and He began to recite various verses.
text:
> uṭhila nānā bhāvāvega, mane haila udvega,
> kṣaṇa-mātra nāre goṅāite
> prabala virahānale, dhairya haila ṭalamale,
> nānā śloka lāgilā paḍite
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uṭhila]]---arose; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āvega]]---forces of emotion; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:u:udvega]]---anxiety; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mātra]]---even for a moment; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---not able; [[synonyms:g:goṅāite]]---to pass; [[synonyms:p:prabala]]---powerful; [[synonyms:v:viraha]]-[[synonyms:a:anale]]---in the fire of separation; [[synonyms:d:dhairya]]---patience; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭalamale]]---tottering; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verses; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began; [[synonyms:p:paḍite]]---to recite.
translation: In this way various ecstatic emotions evolved, and the Lord's mind filled with anxiety. He could not escape even for a moment. In this way, because of fierce feelings of separation, His patience began to totter, and He began to recite various verses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.58
description: " 'O My Lord, O Supreme Personality of Godhead, O friend of the helpless! You are the only ocean of mercy! Because I have not met You, My inauspicious days and nights have become unbearable. I do not know how I shall pass the time.'
text:
> amūny adhanyāni dināntarāṇi
> hare tvad-ālokanam antareṇa
> anātha-bandho karuṇaika-sindho
> hā hanta hā hanta kathaṁ nayāmi
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:amūni]]---all those; [[synonyms:a:adhanyāni]]---inauspicious; [[synonyms:d:dina]]-[[synonyms:a:antarāṇi]]---other days; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---O My Lord; [[synonyms:t:tvat]]---of You; [[synonyms:ā:ālokanam]]---seeing; [[synonyms:a:antareṇa]]---without; [[synonyms:a:anātha]]-[[synonyms:b:bandho]]---O friend of the helpless; [[synonyms:k:karuṇā]]-[[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:s:sindho]]---O only ocean of mercy; [[synonyms:h:hā]] [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---alas; [[synonyms:h:hā]] [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---alas; [[synonyms:k:katham]]---how; [[synonyms:n:nayāmi]]---shall I pass.
translation: “ 'O My Lord, O Supreme Personality of Godhead, O friend of the helpless! You are the only ocean of mercy! Because I have not met You, My inauspicious days and nights have become unbearable. I do not know how I shall pass the time.'
purport: This is a verse from //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta// (41), by Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.59
description: "All these inauspicious days and nights are not passing, for I have not met You. It is difficult to know how to pass all this time. But You are the friend of the helpless and an ocean of mercy. Kindly give Me Your audience, for I am in a precarious position."
text:
> tomāra darśana-vine, adhanya e rātri-dine,
> ei kāla nā yāya kāṭana
> tumi anāthera bandhu, apāra karuṇā-sindhu,
> kṛpā kari' deha daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---audience; [[synonyms:v:vine]]---without; [[synonyms:a:adhanya]]---inauspicious; [[synonyms:e:e]]---this; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---night and day; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:k:kāla]]---this time; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---does not go; [[synonyms:k:kāṭana]]---passing; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:a:anāthera]] [[synonyms:b:bandhu]]---friend of the helpless; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:k:karuṇā]]-[[synonyms:s:sindhu]]---ocean of mercy; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing mercy; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---kindly give; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---audience.
translation: "All these inauspicious days and nights are not passing, for I have not met You. It is difficult to know how to pass all this time. But You are the friend of the helpless and an ocean of mercy. Kindly give Me Your audience, for I am in a precarious position."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.6
description: Blood flowed from all the pores of His body, and all His teeth were loosened. At one moment His whole body became slender, and at another moment His whole body became fat.
text:
> roma-kūpe raktodgama, danta saba hāle
> kṣaṇe aṅga kṣīṇa haya, kṣaṇe aṅga phule
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:roma]]-[[synonyms:k:kūpe]]---the pores of the body; [[synonyms:r:rakta]]-[[synonyms:u:udgama]]---exuding blood; [[synonyms:d:danta]]---teeth; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:h:hāle]]---loosen; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---in one moment; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the whole body; [[synonyms:k:kṣīṇa]]---slender; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---in another moment; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the body; [[synonyms:p:phule]]---fattens.
translation: Blood flowed from all the pores of His body, and all His teeth were loosened. At one moment His whole body became slender, and at another moment His whole body became fat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.60
description: In this way, the Lord's restlessness was awakened by ecstatic feelings, and His mind became agitated. No one could understand what course such ecstasy would take. Because Lord Caitanya could not meet the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, His mind burned. He began to ask Kṛṣṇa of the means by which He could reach Him.
text:
> uṭhila bhāva-cāpala, mana ha-ila cañcala,
> bhāvera gati bujhana nā yāya
> adarśane poḍe mana, kemane pāba daraśana,
> kṛṣṇa-ṭhāñi puchena upāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uṭhila]]---arose; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:c:cāpala]]---restlessness of ecstatic emotion; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became; [[synonyms:c:cañcala]]---agitated; [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of ecstatic emotion; [[synonyms:g:gati]]---the course; [[synonyms:b:bujhana]]---understanding; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---not possible; [[synonyms:a:adarśane]]---without seeing; [[synonyms:p:poḍe]]---burns; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:k:kemane]]---how; [[synonyms:p:pāba]]---I shall get; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---audience; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---from Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:puchena]]---inquires; [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---the means.
translation: In this way, the Lord's restlessness was awakened by ecstatic feelings, and His mind became agitated. No one could understand what course such ecstasy would take. Because Lord Caitanya could not meet the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, His mind burned. He began to ask Kṛṣṇa of the means by which He could reach Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.61
description: " 'O Kṛṣṇa, O flute-player, the sweetness of Your early age is wonderful within these three worlds. You know My unsteadiness, and I know Yours. No one else knows about this. I want to see Your beautiful attractive face somewhere in a solitary place, but how can this be accomplished?'
text:
> tvac-chaiśavaṁ tri-bhuvanādbhutam ity avehi
> mac-cāpalaṁ ca tava vā mama vādhigamyam
> tat kiṁ karomi viralaṁ muralī-vilāsi
> mugdhaṁ mukhāmbujam udīkṣitum īkṣaṇābhyām
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tvat]]---Your; [[synonyms:ś:śaiśavam]]---early age; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvana]]---within the three worlds; [[synonyms:a:adbhutam]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:a:avehi]]---know; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:c:cāpalam]]---My unsteadiness; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---of You; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---of Me; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:a:adhigamyam]]---to be understood; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what; [[synonyms:k:karomi]]---I do; [[synonyms:v:viralam]]---in solitude; [[synonyms:m:muralī]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsi]]---O player of the flute; [[synonyms:m:mugdham]]---attractive; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]-[[synonyms:a:ambujam]]---lotuslike face; [[synonyms:u:udīkṣitum]]---to see sufficiently; [[synonyms:ī:īkṣaṇābhyām]]---by the eyes.
translation: “ 'O Kṛṣṇa, O flute-player, the sweetness of Your early age is wonderful within these three worlds. You know My unsteadiness, and I know Yours. No one else knows about this. I want to see Your beautiful attractive face somewhere in a solitary place, but how can this be accomplished?'
purport: This is another quote from the //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta// (32), of Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.62
description: "My dear Kṛṣṇa, only You and I know the strength of Your beautiful features and, because of them, My unsteadiness. Now, this is My position; I do not know what to do or where to go. Where can I find You? I am asking You to give directions."
text:
> tomāra mādhurī-bala, tāte mora cāpala,
> ei dui, tumi āmi jāni
> kāhāṅ karoṅ kāhāṅ yāṅ, kāhāṅ gele tomā pāṅ,
> tāhā more kaha ta' āpani
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:m:mādhurī]]-[[synonyms:b:bala]]---strength of sweetness; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in that; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:c:cāpala]]---impotence; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---know; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:k:karoṅ]]---I do; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:y:yāṅ]]---I go; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:g:gele]]---by going; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]---You; [[synonyms:p:pāṅ]]---I can get; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please speak; [[synonyms:t:ta']] [[synonyms:ā:āpani]]---You.
translation: "My dear Kṛṣṇa, only You and I know the strength of Your beautiful features and, because of them, My unsteadiness. Now, this is My position; I do not know what to do or where to go. Where can I find You? I am asking You to give directions."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.63
description: Because of the various kinds of ecstasy, contradictory states of mind occurred, and this resulted in a great fight between different types of ecstasy. Anxiety, impotence, humility, anger and impatience were all like soldiers fighting, and the madness of love of Godhead was the cause.
text:
> nānā-bhāvera prābalya, haila sandhi-śābalya,
> bhāve-bhāve haila mahā-raṇa
> autsukya, cāpalya, dainya, roṣāmarṣa ādi sainya,
> premonmāda---sabāra kāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of ecstasies; [[synonyms:p:prābalya]]---the force; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:s:sandhi]]---meeting; [[synonyms:ś:śābalya]]---contradiction; [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---between ecstasies; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:r:raṇa]]---a great fight; [[synonyms:a:autsukya]]---eagerness; [[synonyms:c:cāpalya]]---impotence; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]---humility; [[synonyms:r:roṣa]]-[[synonyms:a:amarṣa]]---anger and impatience; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---all these; [[synonyms:s:sainya]]---soldiers; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:u:unmāda]]---madness in love; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause.
translation: Because of the various kinds of ecstasy, contradictory states of mind occurred, and this resulted in a great fight between different types of ecstasy. Anxiety, impotence, humility, anger and impatience were all like soldiers fighting, and the madness of love of Godhead was the cause.
purport: In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// it is stated that when similar ecstasies from separate causes meet, they are called //svarūpa-sandhi.// When opposing elements meet, whether they arise from a common cause or different causes, their conjunction is called //bhinna-rūpa-sandhi,// the meeting of contradictory ecstasies. The simultaneous joining of different ecstasies-fear and happiness, regret and happiness-is called meeting (//sandhi//). The word //śābalya// refers to different types of ecstatic symptoms combined together, like pride, despondency, humility, remembrance, doubt, impatience caused by insult, fear, disappointment, patience and eagerness. The friction that occurs when these combine is called //śābalya.// Similarly, when the desire to see the object is very prominent, or when one is unable to tolerate any delay in seeing the desired object, the incapability is called //autsukya,// or eagerness. If such eagerness is present, one's mouth dries up and one becomes restless. One also becomes full of anxiety, and hard breathing and patience are observed. Similarly, the lightness of heart caused by strong attachment and strong agitation of the mind is called impotence (//cāpalya//). Failure of judgment, misuse of words, and obstinate activities devoid of anxiety are observed. Similarly, when one becomes too angry at the other party, offensive and abominable speech occurs, and this anger is called //roṣa.// When one becomes impatient due to being scolded or insulted, the resultant state of mind is called //amarṣa.// In this state of mind, one perspires, acquires a headache, fades in bodily color and experiences anxiety and an urge to search out the remedy. The bearing of a grudge, aversion and chastisement are all visible symptoms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.64
description: The body of the Lord was just like a field of sugarcane into which the mad elephants of ecstasy entered. There was a fight amongst the elephants, and in the process the entire field of sugarcane was destroyed. Thus transcendental madness was awakened in the body of the Lord, and He experienced despondency in mind and body. In this ecstatic condition, He began to speak as follows.
text:
> matta-gaja bhāva-gaṇa, prabhura deha---īkṣu-vana,
> gaja-yuddhe vanera dalana
> prabhura haila divyonmāda, tanu-manera avasāda,
> bhāvāveśe kare sambodhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:matta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaja]]---mad elephant; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---symptoms of ecstasy; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---body; [[synonyms:i:ikṣu]]-[[synonyms:v:vana]]---sugarcane forest; [[synonyms:g:gaja]]-[[synonyms:y:yuddhe]]---in the fight of the elephants; [[synonyms:v:vanera]]---of the forest; [[synonyms:d:dalana]]---trampling; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:u:unmāda]]---transcendental madness; [[synonyms:t:tanu]]-[[synonyms:m:manera]]---of the mind and body; [[synonyms:a:avasāda]]---despondency; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---on account of absorption in ecstasy; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:s:sambodhana]]---addressing.
translation: The body of the Lord was just like a field of sugarcane into which the mad elephants of ecstasy entered. There was a fight amongst the elephants, and in the process the entire field of sugarcane was destroyed. Thus transcendental madness was awakened in the body of the Lord, and He experienced despondency in mind and body. In this ecstatic condition, He began to speak as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.65

> he deva he dayita he bhuvanaika-bandho
> he kṛṣṇa he capala he karuṇaika-sindho

purport: This is text 40 of //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.66
description: The symptoms of madness served as an impetus for remembering Kṛṣṇa. The mood of ecstasy awoke love, disdain, defamation by words, pride, honor and indirect prayer. Thus Śrī Kṛṣṇa was sometimes blasphemed and sometimes honored.
text:
> unmādera lakṣaṇa, karāya kṛṣṇa-sphuraṇa,
> bhāvāveśe uṭhe praṇaya māna
> solluṇṭha-vacana-rīti, māna, garva, vyāja-stuti,
> kabhu nindā, kabhu vā sammāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:unmādera]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the symptoms of madness; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---causes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sphuraṇa]]---impetus; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in an ecstatic condition; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---awakens; [[synonyms:p:praṇaya]]---love; [[synonyms:m:māna]]---disdain; [[synonyms:s:solluṇṭha]]-[[synonyms:v:vacana]]---of disrespect by sweet words; [[synonyms:r:rīti]]---the way; [[synonyms:m:māna]]---honor; [[synonyms:g:garva]]---pride; [[synonyms:v:vyāja]]-[[synonyms:s:stuti]]---indirect prayer; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:n:nindā]]---blasphemy; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:s:sammāna]]---honor.
translation: The symptoms of madness served as an impetus for remembering Kṛṣṇa. The mood of ecstasy awoke love, disdain, defamation by words, pride, honor and indirect prayer. Thus Śrī Kṛṣṇa was sometimes blasphemed and sometimes honored.
purport: The word //unmāda// is explained in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// as extreme joy, misfortune and bewilderment in the heart due to separation. Symptoms of //unmāda// are laughing like a madman, dancing, singing, performing ineffectual activities, talking nonsense, running, shouting and sometimes working in contradictory ways. The word //praṇaya// is explained thus: When there is a possibility of receiving direct honor but it is avoided, that love is called //praṇaya.// Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, in his //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi,// explains the word //māna// thus: When the lover feels novel sweetness by exchanging hearty loving words but wishes to hide his feelings by crooked means, //māna// is experienced.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.7

purport: The word //vaidagdhya// means that one is very expert, learned, humorous, cunning, beautiful and expert in manifesting caricatures.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.72
description: There were different transformations of the body of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu: being stunned, trembling, perspiring, fading away of color, weeping, and choking of the voice. In this way His whole body was pervaded by transcendental joy. As a result, sometimes Caitanya Mahāprabhu would laugh, sometimes cry, sometimes dance and sometimes sing. Sometimes He would get up and run here and there, and sometimes fall on the ground and lose consciousness.
text:
> stambha, kampa, prasveda, vaivarṇya, aśru, svara-bheda,
> deha haila pulake vyāpita
> hāse, kānde, nāce, gāya, uṭhi' iti uti dhāya,
> kṣaṇe bhūme paḍiyā mūrcchita
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:stambha]]---being stunned; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:p:prasveda]]---perspiration; [[synonyms:v:vaivarṇya]]---fading away of the color; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:s:svara]]-[[synonyms:b:bheda]]---choking of the voice; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---body; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:p:pulake]]---in joy; [[synonyms:v:vyāpita]]---pervaded; [[synonyms:h:hāse]]---laughs; [[synonyms:k:kānde]]---cries; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sings; [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---getting up; [[synonyms:i:iti]] [[synonyms:u:uti]]---here and there; [[synonyms:d:dhāya]]---runs; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:b:bhūme]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍiyā]]---falling down; [[synonyms:m:mūrcchita]]---unconscious.
translation: There were different transformations of the body of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu: being stunned, trembling, perspiring, fading away of color, weeping, and choking of the voice. In this way His whole body was pervaded by transcendental joy. As a result, sometimes Caitanya Mahāprabhu would laugh, sometimes cry, sometimes dance and sometimes sing. Sometimes He would get up and run here and there, and sometimes fall on the ground and lose consciousness.
purport: In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu,// eight kinds of transcendental change taking place in the body are described. //Stambha,// being stunned, refers to the mind's becoming transcendentally absorbed. In that state, the peaceful mind is placed on the life air, and different bodily transformations are manifest. These symptoms are visible in the body of an advanced devotee. When life becomes almost inactive, it is called "stunned." The emotions resulting from this condition are joy, fear, astonishment, moroseness and anger. In this condition the power of speech is lost, and there is no movement in the hands and legs. Otherwise, being stunned is a mental condition. Many other symptoms are visible on the entire body in the beginning. These are very subtle, but gradually they become very apparent. When one cannot speak, naturally one's active senses are arrested, and the knowledge-acquiring senses are rendered inoperative. //Kampa,// trembling of the body, is mentioned in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// as a result of a special kind of fear, anger and joy. This is called //vepathu,// or //kampa.// When the body begins to perspire because of joy, fear and anger combined, this is called //sveda. Vaivarṇya// is described as a change in the bodily color. It is caused by a combination of moroseness, anger and fear. When these emotions are experienced, the complexion turns pale and the body becomes lean and thin. //Aśru// is explained in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// as a combination of joy, anger and moroseness that causes water to flow from the eyes without effort. When there is joy and there are tears in the eyes, the temperature of the tears is cold, but when there is anger, the tears are hot. In both cases, the eyes are restless, the eyeballs are red and there is itching. These are all symptoms of //aśru.// When there is a combination of moroseness, astonishment, anger, joy and fear, there is a choking in the voice. This choking is called //gadgada.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu refers to //gadgada-ruddhayā girā,// or "a faltering voice." In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, pulaka// is described as joy, encouragement and fear. When these combine, the hairs on the body stand on end, and this bodily state is called //pulaka.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.73
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was thus unconscious, He happened to meet the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Consequently He got up and immediately made a tumultuous sound, very loudly declaring, "Now Kṛṣṇa, the great personality, is present." In this way, because of Kṛṣṇa's sweet qualities, Caitanya Mahāprabhu made different types of mistakes in His mind. Thus by reciting the following verse, He ascertained the presence of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> mūrcchāya haila sākṣātkāra, uṭhi' kare huhuṅkāra,
> kahe---ei āilā mahāśaya
> kṛṣṇera mādhurī-guṇe, nānā bhrama haya mane,
> śloka paḍi' karaye niścaya

Consequently He got up and immediately made a tumultuous sound, very loudly declaring, "Now Kṛṣṇa, the great personality, is present." In this way, because of Kṛṣṇa's sweet qualities, Caitanya Mahāprabhu made different types of mistakes in His mind. Thus by reciting the following verse, He ascertained the presence of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.74
description: In the attitude of Rādhārāṇī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu addressed the gopīs, " 'My dear friends, where is that Kṛṣṇa, Cupid personified, who has the effulgence of a kadamba flower, who is sweetness itself, the nectar of My eyes and mind, He who loosens the hair of the gopīs, who is the supreme source of transcendental bliss and My life and soul? Has He come before My eyes again?' "

> māraḥ svayaṁ nu madhura-dyuti-maṇḍalaṁ nu
> mādhuryam eva nu mano-nayanāmṛtaṁ nu

Has He come before My eyes again?' "
purport: This is another verse from the //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta// (68).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.75
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then would begin to talk like this: "Is Cupid personified present with the effulgence and reflection of the kadamba tree? title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.76
description: As the spiritual master chastises the disciple and teaches him the art of devotional service, so all the ecstatic symptoms of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu-including despondency, moroseness, humility, restlessness, joy, endurance and anger-all instructed His body and mind. In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed His time.
text:
> guru---nānā bhāva-gaṇa, śiṣya---prabhura tanu-mana,
> nānā rīte satata nācāya
> nirveda, viṣāda, dainya, cāpalya, harṣa, dhairya, manyu,
> ei nṛtye prabhura kāla yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:guru]]---the teacher; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---ecstasies; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]---disciples; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:t:tanu]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---body and mind; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:r:rīte]]---in ways; [[synonyms:s:satata]]---always; [[synonyms:n:nācāya]]---causes to dance; [[synonyms:n:nirveda]]---despondency; [[synonyms:v:viṣāda]]---moroseness; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]---humility; [[synonyms:c:cāpalya]]---restlessness; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---joy; [[synonyms:d:dhairya]]---endurance; [[synonyms:m:manyu]]---anger; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:n:nṛtye]]---in dancing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]---time; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---passes.
translation: As the spiritual master chastises the disciple and teaches him the art of devotional service, so all the ecstatic symptoms of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu-including despondency, moroseness, humility, restlessness, joy, endurance and anger-all instructed His body and mind. In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed His time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.77
description: He also passed His time reading the books and singing the songs of Caṇḍīdāsa and Vidyāpati, and listening to quotations from the Jagannātha-vallabha-nāṭaka, Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta and Gīta-govinda. Thus in the association of Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāya Rāmānanda, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed His days and nights chanting and hearing with great pleasure.
text:
> caṇḍīdāsa, vidyāpati, rāyera nāṭaka-gīti,
> karṇāmṛta, śrī-gīta-govinda
> svarūpa-rāmānanda-sane, mahāprabhu rātri-dine,
> gāya, śune---parama ānanda

translation: He also passed His time reading the books and singing the songs of Caṇḍīdāsa and Vidyāpati, and listening to quotations from the Jagannātha-vallabha-nāṭaka, Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta and Gīta-govinda. Thus in the association of Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāya Rāmānanda, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed His days and nights chanting and hearing with great pleasure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.78
description: Among His associates, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu enjoyed paternal loving affection from Paramānanda Purī, friendly affection with Rāmānanda Rāya, unalloyed service from Govinda and others, and humors of conjugal love with Gadādhara, Jagadānanda and Svarūpa Dāmodara. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu enjoyed all these four mellows, and thus He remained obliged to His devotees.
text:
> purīra vātsalya mukhya, rāmānandera śuddha-sakhya,
> govindādyera śuddha-dāsya-rasa
> gadādhara, jagadānanda, svarūpera mukhya rasānanda,
> ei cāri bhāve prabhu vaśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purīra]]---of Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:v:vātsalya]]---paternal affection; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---chiefly; [[synonyms:r:rāmānandera]]---of Rāya Rāmānanda; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:s:sakhya]]---pure fraternity; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādyera]]---of Govinda and others; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsya]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---the pure and unalloyed mellow of service; [[synonyms:g:gadādhara]]---Gadādhara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:j:jagadānanda]]---Jagadānanda Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:s:svarūpera]]---of Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---chiefly; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---tasting the pleasure of conjugal love; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---in four; [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---ecstatic conditions; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---became obliged.
translation: Among His associates, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu enjoyed paternal loving affection from Paramānanda Purī, friendly affection with Rāmānanda Rāya, unalloyed service from Govinda and others, and humors of conjugal love with Gadādhara, Jagadānanda and Svarūpa Dāmodara. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu enjoyed all these four mellows, and thus He remained obliged to His devotees.
purport: Paramānanda Purī is said to have been Uddhava in Vṛndāvana. His affections with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were on the platform of paternal love. This was because Paramānanda Purī happened to be the Godbrother of the spiritual master of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Similarly, Rāmānanda Rāya, who is considered an incarnation of Arjuna and by some an incarnation of Viśākhādevī, enjoyed unalloyed fraternal love with the Lord. Unalloyed personal service was enjoyed by Govinda and others. In the presence of His most confidential devotees like Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Jagadānanda and Svarūpa Dāmodara, Caitanya Mahāprabhu enjoyed the ecstatic conditions of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī in Her conjugal relationship with Kṛṣṇa. Absorbed in these four transcendental mellows, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu resided in Jagannātha Purī, feeling very much obliged to His devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.79
description: Līlāśuka [Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura] was an ordinary human being, yet he developed many ecstatic symptoms in his body. What, then, is so astonishing about these symptoms' being manifest in the body of the Supreme Personality of Godhead? In the ecstatic mood of conjugal love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was on the highest platform; therefore, all the exuberant ecstasies were naturally visible in His body.
text:
> līlāśuka---martya-jana, tāṅra haya bhāvodgama,
> īśvare se---ki ihā vismaya
> tāhe mukhya-rasāśraya, ha-iyāchena mahāśaya,
> tāte haya sarva-bhāvodaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śuka]]---Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:m:martya]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---a person of this world; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of him; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:u:udgama]]---manifestation of different ecstasies; [[synonyms:ī:īśvare]]---in the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---here; [[synonyms:v:vismaya]]---astonishing; [[synonyms:t:tāhe]]---in that; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---chief; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśraya]]---mellows,; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:iyāchena]]---has become; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśaya]]---the great personality Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]]---a manifestation of all ecstasies.
translation: Līlāśuka [Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura] was an ordinary human being, yet he developed many ecstatic symptoms in his body. What, then, is so astonishing about these symptoms' being manifest in the body of the Supreme Personality of Godhead? In the ecstatic mood of conjugal love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was on the highest platform; therefore, all the exuberant ecstasies were naturally visible in His body.
purport: Līlāśuka is Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura Gosvāmī. He was a South Indian, a //brāhmaṇa,// and his former name was Śilhaṇa Miśra. When he was a householder, he became attracted to a prostitute named Cintāmaṇi, but eventually he took her advice and became renounced. Thus he wrote a book named //Śānti-śataka,// and later, by the mercy of Lord Kṛṣṇa and the Vaiṣṇavas, he became a great devotee. Thus he became famous as Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura Gosvāmī. On that elevated platform he wrote a book named //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta,// which is very famous amongst Vaiṣṇavas. Since he exhibited so many ecstatic symptoms, people used to call him Līlāśuka.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.8
description: Although the three doors of the house were always closed, the Lord would nonetheless go out and sometimes would be found at the Jagannātha Temple, before the gate known as Siṁha-dvāra. And sometimes the Lord would fall flat into the sea.
text:
> tina dvāre kapāṭa, prabhu yāyena bāhire
> kabhu siṁha-dvāre paḍe, kabhu sindhu-nīre
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---the three doors; [[synonyms:k:kapāṭa]]---completely closed; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:y:yāyena]]---goes; [[synonyms:b:bāhire]]---outside; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:s:siṁha]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---at the gate of the temple of Jagannātha, known as Siṁha-dvāra; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---falls flat; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:s:sindhu]]-[[synonyms:n:nīre]]---in the water of the sea.
translation: Although the three doors of the house were always closed, the Lord would nonetheless go out and sometimes would be found at the Jagannātha Temple, before the gate known as Siṁha-dvāra. And sometimes the Lord would fall flat into the sea.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.80
description: During His previous pastimes in Vṛndāvana, Lord Kṛṣṇa desired to enjoy the three different types of ecstasy, but despite great endeavor, He could not taste them. Such ecstasies are the monopoly of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Therefore, in order to taste them, Śrī Kṛṣṇa accepted the position of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī in the form of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> pūrve vraja-vilāse, yei tina abhilāṣe,
> yatneha āsvāda nā haila
> śrī-rādhāra bhāva-sāra, āpane kari' aṅgīkāra,
> sei tina vastu āsvādila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---formerly; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāse]]---in the pastimes of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:t:tina]]---those three; [[synonyms:a:abhilāṣe]]---in desires; [[synonyms:y:yatneha]]---by great endeavor; [[synonyms:ā:āsvāda]]---taste; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was not; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rādhāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the essence of the ecstasy; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---acceptance; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:v:vastu]]---three subjects; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādila]]---tasted.
translation: During His previous pastimes in Vṛndāvana, Lord Kṛṣṇa desired to enjoy the three different types of ecstasy, but despite great endeavor, He could not taste them. Such ecstasies are the monopoly of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Therefore, in order to taste them, Śrī Kṛṣṇa accepted the position of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī in the form of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.81
description: By personally tasting the mellows of love of Godhead, Caitanya Mahāprabhu taught His direct disciples the process. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is a wealthy capitalist possessing the touchstone of love of God. Not considering whether one is a proper or improper recipient, He gives His treasure to anyone and everyone. Thus He is the most munificent.
text:
> āpane kari' āsvādane, śikhāila bhakta-gaṇe,
> prema-cintāmaṇira prabhu dhanī
> nāhi jāne sthānāsthāna, yāre tāre kaila dāna,
> mahāprabhu---dātā-śiromaṇi
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādane]]---tasting; [[synonyms:ś:śikhāila]]---He taught; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---to His direct disciples; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:c:cintāmaṇira]]---of the touchstone of love of Godhead; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dhanī]]---capitalist; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---does not; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---know; [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]-[[synonyms:a:asthāna]]---the proper place or improper place; [[synonyms:y:yāre]]---to whomever; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---to him; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:d:dāna]]---charity; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dātā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śiromaṇi]]---the most munificent personality.
translation: By personally tasting the mellows of love of Godhead, Caitanya Mahāprabhu taught His direct disciples the process. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is a wealthy capitalist possessing the touchstone of love of God. Not considering whether one is a proper or improper recipient, He gives His treasure to anyone and everyone. Thus He is the most munificent.
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's capital is the touchstone of love of Godhead, and consequently He is a great owner of that transcendental treasure. After making unlimited amounts of gold, the touchstone remains the same. Similarly, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, although distributing love of Godhead unlimitedly, still remained the supreme owner of this transcendental opulence. His devotees, who learned it from Him, also had to distribute it munificently all over the world. This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His confidential devotees, is also trying to distribute love of Godhead all over the world through the chanting of the holy names of the Lord-Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 2.82
description: No one, not even Lord Brahmā, can ascertain or even taste a drop of this confidential ocean of ecstasy, but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, out of His causeless mercy, has distributed this love of Godhead all over the world. Thus there cannot be any incarnation more munificent than Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. There is no greater donor. Who can describe His transcendental qualities?
text:
> ei gupta bhāva-sindhu, brahmā nā pāya eka bindu,
> hena dhana vilāila saṁsāre
> aiche dayālu avatāra, aiche dātā nāhi āra,
> guṇa keha nāre varṇibāre
