title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.135
description: " 'However, if you dig up a small quantity of dirt on the eastern side, your hands will immediately touch the pot of treasure.'
text:
> pūrva-dike tāte māṭī alpa khudite
> dhanera jhāri paḍibeka tomāra hātete
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---on the eastern side; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---there; [[synonyms:m:māṭī]]---the dirt; [[synonyms:a:alpa]]---small quantity; [[synonyms:k:khudite]]---digging; [[synonyms:d:dhanera]]---of the treasure; [[synonyms:j:jhāri]]---the pot; [[synonyms:p:paḍibeka]]---you will get; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:h:hātete]]---in the hands.
translation: “ 'However, if you dig up a small quantity of dirt on the eastern side, your hands will immediately touch the pot of treasure.'
purport:
The Vedic literatures, including the //Purāṇas,// state that according to the position of the conditioned soul, there are different processes-//karma-kāṇḍa, jñāna-kāṇḍa,// the yogic process and the //bhakti-yoga// process. //Karma-kāṇḍa// is compared to wasps and drones that will simply bite if one takes shelter of them. //jñāna-kāṇḍa,// the speculative process, is simply like a ghost who creates mental disturbances. //Yoga,// the mystic process, is compared to a black snake that devours people by the impersonal cultivation of //kaivalya.// However, if one takes to //bhakti-yoga,// he becomes quickly successful. In other words, through //bhakti-yoga,// one's hands touch the hidden treasure without difficulty.

Therefore it is said in //Bhagavad-gītā:vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ.// One has to take to devotional service. Although the //Vedas// enjoin one to search out Kṛṣṇa and take shelter at His lotus feet, other Vedic processes will not help. According to //Bhagavad-gītā,// only the //bhakti// process is said to be definitive. //Bhaktyā mām abhijānāti.// This is the conclusive statement of the //Vedas,// and one has to accept this process if one is serious in searching for Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In this connection, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura gives the following statement. The eastern side represents devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa. The southern side represents the process of fruitive activity (//karma-kāṇḍa),// which ends in material gain. The western side represents //jñāna-kāṇḍa,// the process of mental speculation, sometimes called //siddhi-kāṇḍa.// The northern side represents the speculative method sometimes known as the mystic //yoga// system. It is only the eastern side, devotional service, that enables one to attain life's real goal. On the southern side, there are fruitive activities by which one is subject to the punishment of Yamarāja. When one follows the system of fruitive activity, his material desires remain prominent. Consequently the results of this process are compared to wasps and drones. The living entity is bitten by the wasps and drones of fruitive activity and thus suffers in material existence birth after birth. One cannot be free from material desires by following this process. The propensity for material enjoyment never ends. Therefore the cycle of birth and death continues, and the spirit soul suffers perpetually.

The mystic //yoga// process is compared to a black snake that devours the living entity and injects him with poison. The ultimate goal of the //yoga// system is to become one with the Absolute. This means finishing one's personal existence. However, the spiritual part and parcel of the Supreme Personality of Godhead has an eternal individual existence. //Bhagavad-gītā// confirms that the individual soul existed in the past, is existing in the present and will continue to exist as an individual in the future. Artificially trying to become one with the Absolute is suicidal. One cannot annihilate his natural condition.

A //yakṣa,// a protector of riches, will not allow anyone to take away riches for enjoyment. Such a demon will simply create disturbances. In other words, a devotee will not depend on his material resources but on the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who can give real protection. This is called //rakṣiṣyatīti viśvāsaḥ// or (in the Bengali poetry of Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura's //Śaraṇāgati), 'avaśya rakṣibe kṛṣṇa'-viśvāsa pālana.// The surrendered soul must accept the fact that his real protector is Kṛṣṇa, not his material acquisitions.

Considering all these points, devotional service to Kṛṣṇa is the real treasure house for the living entity. When one comes to the platform of devotional service, he always remains opulent in the association of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. One who is bereft of devotional service is swallowed by the black snake of the //yoga// system and bitten by the wasps and drones of fruitive activity, and he suffers consequent material miseries. Sometimes the living entity is misled into trying to merge into spiritual existence, thinking himself as good as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This means that when he comes to the spiritual platform, he will be disturbed and will again return to the material platform. According to //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:10:2:32|(10.2.32)]]:

> ye 'nye 'ravindākṣa vimukta-māninas
> tvayy asta-bhāvād aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ
> āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ
> patanty adho 'nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ

Such people may become //sannyāsīs,// but unless they take shelter of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, they will return to the material platform to perform philanthropic activities. In this way, one's spiritual life is lost. This is to be understood as being devoured by the black snake.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.136
description: "Revealed scriptures conclude that one should give up fruitive activity, speculative knowledge and the mystic yoga system and instead take to devotional service, by which Kṛṣṇa can be fully satisfied.
text:
> aiche śāstra kahe,---karma, jñāna, yoga tyaji'
> 'bhaktye' kṛṣṇa vaśa haya, bhaktye tāṅre bhaji
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Vedic literatures confirm; [[synonyms:k:karma]]---fruitive activities; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---speculative knowledge; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]---the mystic yoga system; [[synonyms:t:tyaji']]---giving up; [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---the Supreme Absolute Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:v:vaśa]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes satisfied; [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:b:bhaji]]---we worship.
translation: "Revealed scriptures conclude that one should give up fruitive activity, speculative knowledge and the mystic yoga system and instead take to devotional service, by which Kṛṣṇa can be fully satisfied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.137
description: [The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, said:] " 'My dear Uddhava, neither through aṣṭāṅga-yoga [the mystic yoga system to control the senses], nor through impersonal monism or an analytical study of the Absolute Truth, nor through study of the Vedas, nor through practice of austerities, nor through charity, nor through acceptance of sannyāsa can one satisfy Me as much as one can by developing unalloyed devotional service unto Me.'
text:
> na sādhayati māṁ yogo
> na sāṅkhyaṁ dharma uddhava
> na svādhyāyas tapas tyāgo
> yathā bhaktir mamorjitā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---never; [[synonyms:s:sādhayati]]---causes to remain satisfied; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---Me; [[synonyms:y:yogaḥ]]---the process of control; [[synonyms:n:na]]---nor; [[synonyms:s:sāṅkhyam]]---the process of gaining philosophical knowledge about the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:d:dharmaḥ]]---such an occupation; [[synonyms:u:uddhava]]---My dear Uddhava; [[synonyms:n:na]]---nor; [[synonyms:s:svādhyāyaḥ]]---study of the Vedas; [[synonyms:t:tapaḥ]]---austerities; [[synonyms:t:tyāgaḥ]]---renunciation, acceptance of sannyāsa, or charity; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as much as; [[synonyms:b:bhaktiḥ]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:ū:ūrjitā]]---developed.
translation: [The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, said:] " 'My dear Uddhava, neither through aṣṭāṅga-yoga [the mystic yoga system to control the senses], nor through impersonal monism or an analytical study of the Absolute Truth, nor through study of the Vedas, nor through practice of austerities, nor through charity, nor through acceptance of sannyāsa can one satisfy Me as much as one can by developing unalloyed devotional service unto Me.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.14.20). The explanation for this verse is given in //Ādi-līlā// (17.76).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.138
description: " 'Being very dear to the devotees and sādhus, I am attained through unflinching faith and devotional service. This bhakti-yoga system, which gradually increases attachment for Me, purifies even a human being born among dog-eaters. That is to say, everyone can be elevated to the spiritual platform by the process of bhakti-yoga.'
text:
> bhaktyāham ekayā grāhyaḥ
> śraddhayātmā priyaḥ satām
> bhaktiḥ punāti man-niṣṭhā
> śva-pākān api sambhavāt
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaktyā]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:e:ekayā]]---unflinching; [[synonyms:g:grāhyaḥ]]---obtainable; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhayā]]---by faith; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the most dear; [[synonyms:p:priyaḥ]]---to be served; [[synonyms:s:satām]]---by the devotees; [[synonyms:b:bhaktiḥ]]---the devotional service; [[synonyms:p:punāti]]---purifies; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:n:niṣṭhā]]---fixed only on Me; [[synonyms:ś:śva]]-[[synonyms:p:pākān]]---the lowest of human beings, who are accustomed to eat dogs; [[synonyms:a:api]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:sambhavāt]]---from all faults due to birth and other circumstances.
translation: “ 'Being very dear to the devotees and sādhus, I am attained through unflinching faith and devotional service. This bhakti-yoga system, which gradually increases attachment for Me, purifies even a human being born among dog-eaters. That is to say, everyone can be elevated to the spiritual platform by the process of bhakti-yoga.'
purport: This verse is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.14.21).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.139
description: "The conclusion is that devotional service is the only means to approach the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This system is therefore called abhidheya. This is the verdict of all revealed scriptures.
text:
> ataeva 'bhakti'---kṛṣṇa-prāptyera upāya
> 'abhidheya' bali' tāre sarva-śāstre gāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prāptyera]]---of achieving the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---the only means; [[synonyms:a:abhidheya]]---abhidheya; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---calling; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---this system; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstre]]---in all revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---is described.
translation: "The conclusion is that devotional service is the only means to approach the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This system is therefore called abhidheya. This is the verdict of all revealed scriptures.
purport:
As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:18:55|(Bg. 18.55)]].

> bhaktyā mām abhijānāti
> yāvān yaś cāsmi tattvataḥ
> tato māṁ tattvato jñātvā
> viśate tad-anantaram

"One can understand the Supreme Personality as He is only by devotional service. And when one is in full consciousness of the Supreme Lord by such devotion, he can enter the kingdom of God."

The aim of life is to get rid of the material conditioning and enter into spiritual existence. Although the //śāstras// prescribe different methods for different men, the Supreme Personality of Godhead says that one ultimately must accept the path of devotional service as the assured path of spiritual advancement. Devotional service to the Lord is the only process actually confirmed by the Lord. //Sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja// [[books:bg:18:66|(Bg. 18.66)]]. One must become a devotee if one wants to return home, back to Godhead, and become eternally blissful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.14
description: Sanātana Gosvāmī could see that the mind of the meat-eater was still not satisfied. He then stacked Seven thousand gold coins before him.

> tathāpi yavana-mana prasanna nā dekhilā
> sāta-hājāra mudrā tāra āge rāśi kailā

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.140
description: "When one actually becomes rich, he naturally enjoys all kinds of happiness. When one is actually in a happy mood, all distressful conditions go away by themselves. No extraneous endeavor is needed.
text:
> dhana pāile yaiche sukha-bhoga phala pāya
> sukha-bhoga haite duḥkha āpani palāya

translation: "When one actually becomes rich, he naturally enjoys all kinds of happiness. When one is actually in a happy mood, all distressful conditions go away by themselves. No extraneous endeavor is needed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.141
description: "Similarly, as a result of bhakti, one's dormant love for Kṛṣṇa awakens. When one is so situated that he can taste the association of Lord Kṛṣṇa, material existence, the repetition of birth and death, comes to an end.
text:
> taiche bhakti-phale kṛṣṇe prema upajaya
> preme kṛṣṇāsvāda haile bhava nāśa pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---similarly; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:p:phale]]---by the result of devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love; [[synonyms:u:upajaya]]---arises; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in devotional love; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsvāda]]---tasting the association of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haile]]---when there is; [[synonyms:b:bhava]]---the distress of the repetition of birth and death; [[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---annihilation; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---obtains.
translation: "Similarly, as a result of bhakti, one's dormant love for Kṛṣṇa awakens. When one is so situated that he can taste the association of Lord Kṛṣṇa, material existence, the repetition of birth and death, comes to an end.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.142
description: "The goal of love of Godhead is not to become materially rich or free from material bondage. The real goal is to be situated in devotional service to the Lord and to enjoy transcendental bliss.
text:
> dāridrya-nāśa, bha va-kṣa ya,---premera 'phala' naya
> prema-sukha-bhoga---mukhya prayojana haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dāridrya]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---the end of poverty-stricken life; [[synonyms:b:bhava]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaya]]---annihilation of material existence; [[synonyms:p:premera]]---of love of Godhead; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---the result; [[synonyms:n:naya]]---certainly is not; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---enjoyment of the happiness of love of God; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---chief; [[synonyms:p:prayojana]]---goal of life; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is.
translation: "The goal of love of Godhead is not to become materially rich or free from material bondage. The real goal is to be situated in devotional service to the Lord and to enjoy transcendental bliss.
purport: The results of devotional service are certainly not material benefits or liberation from material bondage. The goal of devotional service is to be eternally situated in the loving service of the Lord and to enjoy spiritual bliss from that service. One is said to be in a poverty-stricken condition when one forgets the Supreme Personality of Godhead. One has to end such a life of poverty in order to automatically end the miserable conditions of material existence. One is automatically liberated from material enjoyment when one tastes the service of Kṛṣṇa. One does not have to endeavor separately for opulence. Opulence automatically comes to the pure devotee, even though he does not desire material happiness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.143
description: "In Vedic literatures, Kṛṣṇa is the central point of attraction, and His service is our activity. To attain the platform of love of Kṛṣṇa is life's ultimate goal. Therefore Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa's service and love of Kṛṣṇa are the three great riches of life.
text:
> veda-śāstre kahe sambandha, abhidheya, prayojana
> kṛṣṇa, kṛṣṇa-bhakti, prema,---tina mahā-dhana

translation: "In Vedic literatures, Kṛṣṇa is the central point of attraction, and His service is our activity. To attain the platform of love of Kṛṣṇa is life's ultimate goal. Therefore Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa's service and love of Kṛṣṇa are the three great riches of life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.144
description: "In all revealed scriptures, beginning with the Vedas, the central point of attraction is Kṛṣṇa. When complete knowledge of Him is realized, the bondage of māyā, the illusory energy, is automatically broken.
text:
> vedādi sakala śāstre kṛṣṇa---mukhya sambandha
> tāṅra jñāne ānuṣaṅge yāya māyā-bandha
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---beginning with the Vedas; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:ś:śāstre]]---in the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---chief; [[synonyms:s:sambandha]]---central point or central attraction; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---by knowledge of Him; [[synonyms:ā:ānuṣaṅge]]---simultaneously; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes away; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:b:bandha]]---the bondage of material existence.
translation: "In all revealed scriptures, beginning with the Vedas, the central point of attraction is Kṛṣṇa. When complete knowledge of Him is realized, the bondage of māyā, the illusory energy, is automatically broken.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.145
description: " 'There are many types of Vedic literatures and supplementary Purāṇas. In each of them there are particular demigods who are spoken of as the chief demigods. This is just to create an illusion for moving and nonmoving living entities. Let them perpetually engage in such imaginations. However, when one analytically studies all these Vedic literatures collectively, he comes to the conclusion that Lord Viṣṇu is the one and only Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
text:
> vyāmohāya carācarasya jagatas te te purāṇāgamās
> tāṁ tām eva hi devatāṁ paramikāṁ jalpantu kalpāvadhi
> siddhānte punar eka eva bhagavān viṣṇuḥ samastāgama-
> vyāpāreṣu vivecana-vyatikaraṁ nīteṣu niścīyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyāmohāya]]---to increase the illusion and ignorance; [[synonyms:c:cara]]-[[synonyms:a:acarasya]]---of all living entities, moving and nonmoving; [[synonyms:j:jagataḥ]]---of the world; [[synonyms:t:te]] [[synonyms:t:te]]---those respective; [[synonyms:p:purāṇa]]---the supplementary Vedic literatures called the Purāṇas; [[synonyms:ā:āgamāḥ]]---and Vedas; [[synonyms:t:tām]] [[synonyms:t:tām]]---that respective; [[synonyms:e:eva]] [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:d:devatām]]---demigod; [[synonyms:p:paramikām]]---as supreme; [[synonyms:j:jalpantu]]---let them speak about; [[synonyms:k:kalpa]]-[[synonyms:a:avadhi]]---until the end of the millennium; [[synonyms:s:siddhānte]]---in conclusion; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---but; [[synonyms:e:ekaḥ]]---one; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---only; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇuḥ]]---Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:s:samasta]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:āgama]]---of the Vedas; [[synonyms:v:vyāpāreṣu]]---in the dealings; [[synonyms:v:vivecana]]-[[synonyms:v:vyatikaram]]---to collective consideration; [[synonyms:n:nīteṣu]]---when forcibly brought; [[synonyms:n:niścīyate]]---is established.
translation: “ 'There are many types of Vedic literatures and supplementary Purāṇas. In each of them there are particular demigods who are spoken of as the chief demigods. This is just to create an illusion for moving and nonmoving living entities. Let them perpetually engage in such imaginations. However, when one analytically studies all these Vedic literatures collectively, he comes to the conclusion that Lord Viṣṇu is the one and only Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
purport: This is a verse from the //Padma Purāṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.146
description: "When one accepts Vedic literature by interpretation or even by dictionary meaning, directly or indirectly the ultimate declaration of Vedic knowledge points to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> mukhya-gauṇa-vṛtti, kiṁvā anvaya-vyatireke
> vedera pratijñā kevala kahaye kṛṣṇake
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---chief; [[synonyms:g:gauṇa]]---secondary; [[synonyms:v:vṛtti]]---meaning; [[synonyms:k:kiṁvā]]---or; [[synonyms:a:anvaya]]-[[synonyms:v:vyatireke]]---directly or indirectly; [[synonyms:v:vedera]] [[synonyms:p:pratijñā]]---ultimate declaration of the Vedas; [[synonyms:k:kevala]]---only; [[synonyms:k:kahaye]]---speaks; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇake]]---about Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "When one accepts Vedic literature by interpretation or even by dictionary meaning, directly or indirectly the ultimate declaration of Vedic knowledge points to Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.147-148
description: " 'What is the direction of all Vedic literatures? On whom do they set focus? Who is the purpose of all speculation? Outside of Me no one knows these things. Now you should know that all these activities are aimed at ordaining and setting forth Me. The purpose of Vedic literature is to know Me by different speculations, either by indirect understanding or by dictionary understanding. Everyone is speculating about Me. The essence of all Vedic literatures is to distinguish Me from māyā. By considering the illusory energy, one comes to the platform of understanding Me. In this way one becomes free from speculation about the Vedas and comes to Me as the conclusion. Thus one is satisfied.'
text:
> kiṁ vidhatte kim ācaṣṭe
> kim anūdya vikalpayet
> ity asyā hṛdayaṁ loke
> nānyo mad veda kaścana
>
> māṁ vidhatte 'bhidhatte māṁ
> vikalpyāpohyate hy aham
> etāvān sarva-vedārthaḥ
> śabda āsthāya māṁ bhidām
> māyā-mātram anūdyānte
> pratiṣidhya prasīdati
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what; [[synonyms:v:vidhatte]]---direct; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what; [[synonyms:ā:ācaṣṭe]]---declare; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what; [[synonyms:a:anūdya]]---taking as the object; [[synonyms:v:vikalpayet]]---may conjecture; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:a:asyāḥ]]---of the Vedic literature; [[synonyms:h:hṛdayam]]---intention; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---in this world; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:anyaḥ]]---other; [[synonyms:m:mat]]---than Me; [[synonyms:v:veda]]---knows; [[synonyms:k:kaścana]]---anyone; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---Me; [[synonyms:v:vidhatte]]---they ordain; [[synonyms:a:abhidhatte]]---set forth; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---Me; [[synonyms:v:vikalpya]]---speculating; [[synonyms:a:aphyate]]---am fixed; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:e:etāvān]]---of such measures; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:a:arthaḥ]]---the purport of the Vedas; [[synonyms:ś:śabdaḥ]]---the Vedas; [[synonyms:ā:āsthāya]]---taking shelter of; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---Me; [[synonyms:b:bhidām]]---different; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---illusory energy; [[synonyms:m:mātram]]---only; [[synonyms:a:anūdya]]---saying; [[synonyms:a:ante]]---at the end; [[synonyms:p:pratiṣidhya]]---driving away; [[synonyms:p:prasīdati]]---gets satisfaction.
translation: “ 'What is the direction of all Vedic literatures? On whom do they set focus? Who is the purpose of all speculation? Outside of Me no one knows these things. Now you should know that all these activities are aimed at ordaining and setting forth Me. The purpose of Vedic literature is to know Me by different speculations, either by indirect understanding or by dictionary understanding. Everyone is speculating about Me. The essence of all Vedic literatures is to distinguish Me from māyā. By considering the illusory energy, one comes to the platform of understanding Me. In this way one becomes free from speculation about the Vedas and comes to Me as the conclusion. Thus one is satisfied.'
purport: These two verses are quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.21.42,43). When Uddhava asked Kṛṣṇa about the purpose of Vedic speculation, the Lord informed him of the process of understanding Vedic literature. The //Vedas// are composed of //karma-kāṇḍa, jñāna-kāṇḍa// and //upāsanā-kāṇḍa.// If one analytically studies the purpose of the //Vedas,// he understands that by //karma-kāṇḍa,// sacrificial activity, one comes to the conclusion of //jñāna-kāṇḍa,// speculative knowledge. After speculation, one comes to the conclusion that worship of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the ultimate. When one comes to this conclusion, he becomes fully satisfied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.149
description: "The transcendental form of Lord Kṛṣṇa is unlimited and also has unlimited opulence. He possesses the internal potency, external potency and marginal potency.
text:
> kṛṣṇera svarūpa---ananta, vaibhava---apāra
> cic-chakti, māyā-śakti, jīva-śakti āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the transcendental form of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimitedly expanded; [[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]---opulence; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---internal potency; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---external potency; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---marginal potency; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and.
translation: "The transcendental form of Lord Kṛṣṇa is unlimited and also has unlimited opulence. He possesses the internal potency, external potency and marginal potency.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.15
description: When the meat-eater saw the coins, he was attracted to them. He then agreed, and that night he cut Sanātana's shackles and let him cross the Ganges.
text:
> lobha ha-ila yavanera mudrā dekhiyā
> rātre gaṅgā-pāra kaila dāḍukā kāṭiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lobha]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was attraction for the money; [[synonyms:y:yavanera]]---of the meat-eater; [[synonyms:m:mudrā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing the golden coins; [[synonyms:r:rātre]]---at night; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:p:pāra]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---he got him across the Ganges; [[synonyms:d:dāḍukā]]---shackles; [[synonyms:k:kāṭiyā]]---breaking.
translation: When the meat-eater saw the coins, he was attracted to them. He then agreed, and that night he cut Sanātana's shackles and let him cross the Ganges.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.150
description: "Both the material and spiritual world are transformations of Kṛṣṇa's internal and external potencies. Therefore Kṛṣṇa is the original source of both material and spiritual manifestations.
text:
> vaikuṇṭha, brahmāṇḍa-gaṇa---śakti-kārya ha ya
> svarūpa-śakti śakti-kāryera---kṛṣṇa samāśraya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]]---the spiritual world; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---universes of the material world; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:k:kārya]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---they are all activities of Kṛṣṇa's potencies; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---of the internal potency; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:k:kāryera]]---of the activities of the external potency; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:samāśraya]]---the original source.
translation: "Both the material and spiritual world are transformations of Kṛṣṇa's internal and external potencies. Therefore Kṛṣṇa is the original source of both material and spiritual manifestations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.151
description: " 'The Tenth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam reveals the tenth object, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the shelter of all surrendered souls. He is known as Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and He is the ultimate source of all the universes. Let me offer my obeisances unto Him.'
text:
> daśame daśamaṁ lakṣyam
> āśritāśraya-vigraham
> śrī-kṛṣṇākhyaṁ paraṁ dhāma
> jagad-dhāma namāmi tat
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daśame]]---in the Tenth Canto; [[synonyms:d:daśamam]]---the tenth subject matter; [[synonyms:l:lakṣyam]]---to be seen; [[synonyms:ā:āśrita]]---of the sheltered; [[synonyms:ā:āśraya]]---of the shelter; [[synonyms:v:vigraham]]---who is the form; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākhyam]]---known as Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:param]]---supreme; [[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---abode; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---the abode of the universes; [[synonyms:n:namāmi]]---I offer my obeisances; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---to Him.
translation: “ 'The Tenth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam reveals the tenth object, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the shelter of all surrendered souls. He is known as Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and He is the ultimate source of all the universes. Let me offer my obeisances unto Him.'
purport:
This is a quotation from //Bhāvārtha-dīpikā,// Śrīdhara Svāmī's commentary on //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.1.1). In the Tenth Canto of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// there is a description of the //āśraya-tattva,// Śrī Kṛṣṇa. There are two //tattvas-āśraya-tattva// and //āśrita-tattva. Āśraya-tattva// is the objective, and //āśrita-tattva// is the subjective. Since the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa are the shelter of all devotees, Śrī Kṛṣṇa is called //paraṁ dhāma.// In //Bhagavad-gītā// it is stated: //paraṁ brahma paraṁ dhāma pavitraṁ paramaṁ bhavān.// Everything is resting under the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.14.58) it is stated:

> samāśritā ye pada-pallava-plavaṁ
> mahat-padaṁ puṇya-yaśo-murāreḥ

Under the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the entire //mahat-tattva// is existing. Since everything is under Śrī Kṛṣṇa's protection, Śrī Kṛṣṇa is called //āśraya-tattva.// Everything else is called //āśrita-tattva.// The material creation is also called //āśrita-tattva.// Liberation from material bondage and the attainment of the spiritual platform are also //āśrita-tattva.// Kṛṣṇa is the only //āśraya-tattva.// In the beginning of the creation there are Mahā-Viṣṇu, Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu. They are also //āśraya-tattva.// Kṛṣṇa is the cause of all causes (//sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam).// To understand Kṛṣṇa perfectly, one has to make an analytical study of //āśraya-tattva// and //āśrita-tattva.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.152
description: "O Sanātana, please hear about the eternal form of Lord Kṛṣṇa. He is the Absolute Truth, devoid of duality but present in Vṛndāvana as the son of Nanda Mahārāja.
text:
> kṛṣṇera svarūpa-vicāra śuna, sanātana
> advaya-jñāna-tattva, vraje vrajendra-nandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---consideration of the eternal form; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---My dear Sanātana; [[synonyms:a:advaya]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]]---the Absolute Truth without duality; [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of Nanda Mahārāja.
translation: "O Sanātana, please hear about the eternal form of Lord Kṛṣṇa. He is the Absolute Truth, devoid of duality but present in Vṛndāvana as the son of Nanda Mahārāja.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.153
description: "Kṛṣṇa is the original source of everything and the sum total of everything. He appears as the supreme youth, and His whole body is composed of spiritual bliss. He is the shelter of everything and master of everyone.
text:
> sarva-ādi, sarva-aṁśī, kiśora-śekhara
> cid-ānanda-deha, sarvāśraya, sarveśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---origin of everything; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁśī]]---sum total of all parts and parcels; [[synonyms:k:kiśora]]-[[synonyms:ś:śekhara]]---the supreme youth; [[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:d:deha]]---a body of spiritual blissfulness; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśraya]]---shelter of everyone; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---master of everyone.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa is the original source of everything and the sum total of everything. He appears as the supreme youth, and His whole body is composed of spiritual bliss. He is the shelter of everything and master of everyone.
purport: Kṛṣṇa is the origin of all //viṣṇu-tattvas,// including Mahā-Viṣṇu, Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu. He is the ultimate goal of Vaiṣṇava philosophy. Everything emanates from Him. His body is completely spiritual and is the source of all spiritual being. Although He is the source of everything, He Himself has no source. //Advaitam acyutam anādim ananta-rūpaṁ, ādyaṁ purāṇa-puruṣaṁ nava-yauvanaṁ ca.// Although He is the supreme source of everyone, He is still always a fresh youth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.154
description: " 'Kṛṣṇa, who is known as Govinda, is the supreme controller. He has an eternal, blissful, spiritual body. He is the origin of all. He has no other origin, for He is the prime cause of all causes.'
text:
> īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
> sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ
> anādir ādir govindaḥ
> sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam
synonyms: [[synonyms:ī:īśvaraḥ]]---the controller; [[synonyms:p:paramaḥ]]---supreme; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sat]]---eternal existence; [[synonyms:c:cit]]---absolute knowledge; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---absolute bliss; [[synonyms:v:vigrahaḥ]]---whose form; [[synonyms:a:anādiḥ]]---without beginning; [[synonyms:ā:ādiḥ]]---the origin; [[synonyms:g:govindaḥ]]---Lord Govinda; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kāraṇam]]---the cause of all causes.
translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa, who is known as Govinda, is the supreme controller. He has an eternal, blissful, spiritual body. He is the origin of all. He has no other origin, for He is the prime cause of all causes.'
purport: This is the first verse of the Fifth Chapter of //Brahma-saṁhitā.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.155
description: "The original Supreme Personality of Godhead is Kṛṣṇa. His original name is Govinda. He is full of all opulences, and His eternal abode is known as Goloka Vṛndāvana.
text:
> svayaṁ bhagavān kṛṣṇa, 'govinda' para nāma
> sarvaiśvarya-pūrṇa yāṅra goloka---nitya-dhāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sva]] [[synonyms:y:yam]]---personally; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:p:para]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---another name; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]-[[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---full of all opulences; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:g:goloka]]---Goloka Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---eternal abode.
translation: "The original Supreme Personality of Godhead is Kṛṣṇa. His original name is Govinda. He is full of all opulences, and His eternal abode is known as Goloka Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.156
description: " 'All these incarnations of Godhead are either plenary portions or parts of the plenary portions of the puruṣa-avatāras. But Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. In every age He protects the world through His different features when the world is disturbed by the enemies of Indra.'
text:
> ete cāṁśa-kalāḥ puṁsaḥ
> kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam
> indrāri-vyākulaṁ lokaṁ
> mṛḍayanti yuge yuge
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ete]]---these; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---plenary portions; [[synonyms:k:kalāḥ]]---parts of plenary portions; [[synonyms:p:puṁsaḥ]]---of the puruṣa-avatāras; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---Himself; [[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:a:ari]]---the enemies of Lord Indra; [[synonyms:v:vyākulam]]---full of; [[synonyms:l:lokam]]---the world; [[synonyms:m:mṛḍayanti]]---make happy; [[synonyms:y:yuge]] [[synonyms:y:yuge]]---at the right time in each age.
translation: “ 'All these incarnations of Godhead are either plenary portions or parts of the plenary portions of the puruṣa-avatāras. But Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. In every age He protects the world through His different features when the world is disturbed by the enemies of Indra.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:3:28|(1.3.28)]]. See also //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Two, verse 67.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.157
description: "There are three kinds of spiritual processes for understanding the Absolute Truth—the processes of speculative knowledge, mystic yoga and bhakti-yoga. According to these three processes, the Absolute Truth is manifested as Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān.
text:
> jñāna, yoga, bhakti,---tina sādhanera vaśe
> brahma, ātmā, bhagavān---trividha prakāśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]---mystic power; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:s:sādhanera]]---of the processes of spiritual life; [[synonyms:v:vaśe]]---under the control; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---impersonal Brahman; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---localized Paramātmā; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---three kinds of manifestation.
translation: "There are three kinds of spiritual processes for understanding the Absolute Truth---the processes of speculative knowledge, mystic yoga and bhakti-yoga. According to these three processes, the Absolute Truth is manifested as Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.158
description: " 'Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth call this nondual substance Brahman, Paramātmā or Bhagavān.'
text:
> vadanti tat tattva-vidas
> tattvaṁ yaj jñānam advayam
> brahmeti paramātmeti
> bhagavān iti śabdyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vadanti]]---they say; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]-[[synonyms:v:vidaḥ]]---learned souls; [[synonyms:t:tattvam]]---the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:j:jñānam]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:a:advayam]]---nondual; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---Brahman; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:p:paramātmā]]---Paramātmā; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---Bhagavān; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:ś:śabdyate]]---is known.
translation: “ 'Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth call this nondual substance Brahman, Paramātmā or Bhagavān.'
purport:
This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:2:11|(1.2.11)]]. For an explanation, see also //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Two, verse 11.

Those who are interested in the impersonal Brahman effulgence which is not different from the Supreme Personality of Godhead, can attain that goal by speculative knowledge. Those who are interested in practicing mystic //yoga// can attain the localized aspect of Paramātmā. As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā, īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ hṛd-deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati:// the Supreme Personality of Godhead is situated within the heart as Paramātmā. He witnesses the activities of the living entities and gives them permission to act.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.159
description: "The manifestation of the impersonal Brahman effulgence, which is without variety, is the rays of Kṛṣṇa's bodily effulgence. It is exactly like the sun. When the sun is seen by our ordinary eyes, it simply appears to consist of effulgence.
text:
> brahma---aṅga-kānti tāṅra, nirviśeṣa prakāśe
> sūrya yena carma-cakṣe jyotirmaya bhāse
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---the impersonal Brahman effulgence; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:k:kānti]]---the bodily rays; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Him; [[synonyms:n:nirviśeṣa]]---without varieties; [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---manifestation; [[synonyms:s:sūrya]] [[synonyms:y:yena]]---exactly like the sun; [[synonyms:c:carma]]-[[synonyms:c:cakṣe]]---with our ordinary material eyes; [[synonyms:j:jyotiḥ]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---simply effulgent; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---appears.
translation: "The manifestation of the impersonal Brahman effulgence, which is without variety, is the rays of Kṛṣṇa's bodily effulgence. It is exactly like the sun. When the sun is seen by our ordinary eyes, it simply appears to consist of effulgence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.16
description: In this way, Sanātana Gosvāmī was released. However, he was not able to walk along the path of the fortress. Walking day and night, he finally arrived at the hilly tract of land known as Pātaḍā.
text:
> gaḍa-dvāra-patha chāḍilā, nāre tāhāṅ yāite
> rātri-dina cali' āilā pātaḍā-parvate
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gaḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāra]]-[[synonyms:p:patha]]---the path of the fortress; [[synonyms:c:chāḍilā]]---gave up; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---not able; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---night and day; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---walking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:p:pātaḍā]]-[[synonyms:p:parvate]]---in the hilly tract of land known as Pātaḍā.
translation: In this way, Sanātana Gosvāmī was released. However, he was not able to walk along the path of the fortress. Walking day and night, he finally arrived at the hilly tract of land known as Pātaḍā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.160
description: " 'I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who is endowed with great power. The glowing effulgence of His transcendental form is the impersonal Brahman, which is absolute, complete and unlimited and which displays the varieties of countless planets, with their different opulences, in millions and millions of universes.'
text:
> yasya prabhā prabhavato jagad-aṇḍa-koṭi-
> koṭiṣv aśeṣa-vasudhādi-vibhūti-bhinnam
> tad brahma niṣkalam anantam aśeṣa-bhūtaṁ
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:p:prabhā]]---the effulgence; [[synonyms:p:prabhavataḥ]]---of one who excels in power; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:a:aṇḍa]]---of universes; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭiṣu]]---in millions and millions; [[synonyms:a:aśeṣa]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:v:vasudhā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---with planets and other manifestations; [[synonyms:v:vibhūti]]---with opulences; [[synonyms:b:bhinnam]]---becoming variegated; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---Brahman; [[synonyms:n:niṣkalam]]---without parts; [[synonyms:a:anantam]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:a:aśeṣa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūtam]]---being complete; [[synonyms:g:govindam]]---Lord Govinda; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣam]]---the original person; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---Him; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bhajāmi]]---worship.
translation: “ 'I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who is endowed with great power. The glowing effulgence of His transcendental form is the impersonal Brahman, which is absolute, complete and unlimited and which displays the varieties of countless planets, with their different opulences, in millions and millions of universes.'
purport: This verse is quoted from //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.40). For an explanation, refer to //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Two, verse 14.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.161
description: "The Paramātmā, the Supersoul feature, is the partial plenary portion of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the original source of all living entities. It is also Kṛṣṇa who is the original source of Paramātmā.
text:
> paramātmā yeṅho, teṅho kṛṣṇera eka aṁśa
> ātmāra 'ātmā' haya kṛṣṇa sarva-avataṁsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paramātmā]]---the Supersoul within the heart; [[synonyms:y:yeṅho]]---who; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---plenary portion; [[synonyms:ā:ātmāra]]---of the soul; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the soul; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---of everything; [[synonyms:a:avataṁsa]]---source.
translation: "The Paramātmā, the Supersoul feature, is the partial plenary portion of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the original source of all living entities. It is also Kṛṣṇa who is the original source of Paramātmā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.162
description: " 'You should know Kṛṣṇa as the original soul of all ātmās [living entities]. For the benefit of the whole universe, He has, out of His causeless mercy, appeared as an ordinary human being. He has done this with the strength of His own internal potency.'
text:
> kṛṣṇam enam avehi tvam
> ātmānam akhilātmanām
> jagad-dhitāya so 'py atra
> dehīvābhāti māyayā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇam]]---in the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:e:enam]]---this; [[synonyms:a:avehi]]---just try to understand; [[synonyms:t:tvam]]---you; [[synonyms:ā:ātmānam]]---the soul; [[synonyms:a:akhila]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmanām]]---of all living entities; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:h:hita]]-[[synonyms:y:ya]]---the benefit of the whole universe; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:a:api]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:atra]]---here; [[synonyms:d:dehī]]---a human being; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:ā:ābhāti]]---appears; [[synonyms:m:māyayā]]---by His internal potency.
translation: “ 'You should know Kṛṣṇa as the original soul of all ātmās [living entities]. For the benefit of the whole universe, He has, out of His causeless mercy, appeared as an ordinary human being. He has done this with the strength of His own internal potency.'
purport:
This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.14.55). Parīkṣit Mahārāja asked Śukadeva Gosvāmī why Kṛṣṇa was so beloved by the residents of Vṛndāvana, who loved Him even more than their own offspring or life itself. At that time Śukadeva Gosvāmī replied that everyone's //ātmā,// or soul, is very, very dear, especially to all living entities who have accepted material bodies. However, that //ātmā,// the spirit soul, is part and parcel of Kṛṣṇa. For this reason, Kṛṣṇa is very dear to every living entity. Everyone's body is very dear to oneself, and one wants to protect the body by all means because within the body the soul is living. Due to the intimate relationship between the soul and the body, the body is important and dear to everyone. Similarly, the soul, being part and parcel of Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, is very, very dear to all living entities. Unfortunately, the soul forgets his constitutional position and thinks he is only the body (//deha-ātma-bud-dhi).// Thus the soul is subjected to the rules and regulations of material nature. When a living entity, by his intelligence, reawakens his attraction for Kṛṣṇa, he can understand that he is not the body but part and parcel of Kṛṣṇa. Thus filled with knowledge, he no longer labors under attachment to the body and everything related to the body. //janasya moho 'yam aham mameti.// Material existence, wherein one thinks, "I am the body, and this belongs to me," is also illusory. One must redirect his attraction to Kṛṣṇa. //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:2:7|(1.2.7)]] states:

> vāsudeve bhagavati
> bhakti-yogaḥ prayojitaḥ
> janayaty āśu vairāgyaṁ
> jñānaṁ ca yad ahaitukam

"By rendering devotional service unto the Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, one immediately acquires causeless knowledge and detachment from the world."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.163
description: " 'But what need is there, Arjuna, for all this detailed knowledge? With a single fragment of Myself, I pervade and support this entire universe.'
text:
> athavā bahunaitena
> kiṁ jñātena tavārjuna
> viṣṭabhyāham idaṁ kṛtsnam
> ekāṁśena sthito jagat
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:athavā]]---or; [[synonyms:b:bahunā]]---much; [[synonyms:e:etena]]---with this; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what use; [[synonyms:j:jñātena]]---being known; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---by you; [[synonyms:a:arjuna]]---O Arjuna; [[synonyms:v:viṣṭabhya]]---pervading; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kṛtsnam]]---entire; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁśena]]---with one portion; [[synonyms:s:sthitaḥ]]---situated; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---universe.
translation: “ 'But what need is there, Arjuna, for all this detailed knowledge? With a single fragment of Myself, I pervade and support this entire universe.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:10:42|(Bg. 10.42)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.164
description: "Only by devotional activity can one understand the transcendental form of the Lord, which is perfect in all respects. Although His form is one, He can expand His form into unlimited numbers by His supreme will.
text:
> 'bhaktye' bhagavānera anubhava---pūrṇa-rūpa
> eka-i vigrahe tāṅra ananta svarūpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:b:bhagavānera]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:anubhava]]---perception; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---perfectly; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---one; [[synonyms:v:vigrahe]]---in the transcendental form; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---expansions of plenary portions.
translation: "Only by devotional activity can one understand the transcendental form of the Lord, which is perfect in all respects. Although His form is one, He can expand His form into unlimited numbers by His supreme will.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.165
description: "The Supreme Personality of Godhead exists in three principal forms-svayaṁ-rūpa, tad-ekātma-rūpa, and āveśa-rūpa.
text:
> sva yaṁ-rūpa, tad-ekātma-rūpa, āveśa---nāma
> prathamei tina-rūpe rahena bhagavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sva]] [[synonyms:y:yam]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the personal form; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:e:ekātma]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the same form, nondifferent from svayaṁ-rūpa; [[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---especially empowered; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:p:prathamei]]---in the beginning; [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in three forms; [[synonyms:r:rahena]]---remains; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: "The Supreme Personality of Godhead exists in three principal forms-svayaṁ-rūpa, tad-ekātma-rūpa, and āveśa-rūpa.
purport:
Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī has described //svayaṁ-rūpa// in his //Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta, pūrva-khaṇḍa,// verse 12, //ananyāpekṣi yad rūpaṁ svayaṁ-rūpaḥ sa ucyate:// the original form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead does not depend on other forms. The original form is called //svayaṁ-rūpa,// and it is described in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam:kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam// (1.3.28). Kṛṣṇa's original form as a cowherd boy in Vṛndāvana is called //svayaṁ-rūpa.// It is confirmed in the //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.1):

> īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
> sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ
> anādir ādir govindaḥ
> sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam

There is nothing superior to Govinda. He is the ultimate source and the cause of all causes. In //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:7:7|(Bg. 7.7)]] the Lord says, //mattaḥ parataraṁ nānyat:// "There is no truth superior to Me.

The //tad-ekātma-rūpa// is also described in the //Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta, Pūrva-khaṇḍa,// verse 14:

> yad rūpaṁ tad-abhedena
> svarūpeṇa virājate
> ākṛtyādibhir anyādṛk
> sa tad-ekātma-rūpakaḥ

The //tad-ekātma-rūpa// forms exist simultaneously with the //svayaṁ-rūpa// form and are nondifferent. At the same time, the bodily features and specific activities appear to be different. This //tad-ekātma-rūpa// is also divided into two categories-//svāṁśa// and //vilāsa.//

His //āveśa// form is also explained in the //Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta,// verse 18:

> jñāna-śaktyādi-kalayā
> yatrāviṣṭo janārdanaḥ
> ta āveśā nigadyante
> jīvā eva mahattamāḥ

A living entity who is specifically empowered by the Lord with knowledge or strength is technically called //āveśa-rūpa.// As stated in the //Caitanya-caritāmṛta// [[books:cc:antya:7:11|(Antya 7.11)]], //kṛṣṇa-śakti vinā nahe tāra pravartana:// unless a devotee is specifically empowered by the Lord, he cannot preach the holy name of the Lord all over the world. This is an explanation of the word //āveśa-rūpa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.166
description: "The original form of the Lord [svayaṁ-rūpa] is exhibited in two forms-svayaṁ-rūpa and svayaṁ-prakāśa. In His original form as svayaṁ-rūpa, Kṛṣṇa is observed as a cowherd boy in Vṛndāvana.
text:
> 'svayaṁ-rūpa' 's va yaṁ-prakāśa'---dui rūpe sphūrti
> svayaṁ-rūpe---eka 'kṛṣṇa' vraje gopa-mūrti
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sva]] [[synonyms:y:yam]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the original form of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sva]] [[synonyms:y:yam]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---the personal manifestation; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in two forms; [[synonyms:s:sphūrti]]---exhibition; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in the original form; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---the cowherd boy.
translation: "The original form of the Lord [svayaṁ-rūpa] is exhibited in two forms-svayaṁ-rūpa and svayaṁ-prakāśa. In His original form as svayaṁ-rūpa, Kṛṣṇa is observed as a cowherd boy in Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.167
description: "In His original form, Kṛṣṇa manifests Himself in two features-prābhava and vaibhava. He expands His one original form into many, as He did during the rāsa-līlā dance.
text:
> 'prābhava-vaibhava'-rūpe dvividha prakāśe
> eka-vapu bahu rūpa yaiche haila rāse
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prābhava]]---prābhava; [[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]---vaibhava; [[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in forms; [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:p:pra]]-[[synonyms:k:kāśe]]---twofold manifestations; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:v:vapu]]---the same original form; [[synonyms:b:bahu]] [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---expanded into unlimited numbers; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---like; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---it was; [[synonyms:r:rāse]]---while dancing in the rāsa dance with the gopīs.
translation: "In His original form, Kṛṣṇa manifests Himself in two features-prābhava and vaibhava. He expands His one original form into many, as He did during the rāsa-līlā dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.168
description: "When the Lord married 16,108 wives at Dvārakā, He expanded Himself into many forms. These expansions and the expansions at the rāsa dance are called prābhava-prakāśa, according to the directions of revealed scriptures.
text:
> mahiṣī-vivāhe haila bahu-vidha mūrti
> 'prābhava prakāśa'---ei śāstra-parasiddhi
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahiṣī]]-[[synonyms:v:vivāhe]]---in the matter of marrying 16,108 wives at Dvārakā; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there were; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---many forms; [[synonyms:p:prābhava]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---called //prābhava-prakāśa//; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:p:parasiddhi]]---determined by reference to the revealed scriptures.
translation: "When the Lord married 16,108 wives at Dvārakā, He expanded Himself into many forms. These expansions and the expansions at the rāsa dance are called prābhava-prakāśa, according to the directions of revealed scriptures.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.169
description: "The prābhava-prakāśa expansions of Lord Kṛṣṇa are not like the expansions of the sage Saubhari. Had they been so, Nārada would not have been astonished to see them.
text:
> saubhary-ādi-prāya sei kāya-vyūha naya
> kāya-vyūha haile nāradera vismaya nā haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saubhari]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---beginning with the sage named Saubhari; [[synonyms:p:prāya]]---like; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kāya]]-[[synonyms:v:vyūha]]---the expansion of one's body; [[synonyms:n:naya]]---is not; [[synonyms:k:kāya]]-[[synonyms:v:vyūha]]---expansions of the body; [[synonyms:h:haile]]---if there are; [[synonyms:n:nāradera]]---of Nārada Muni; [[synonyms:v:vismaya]]---the astonishment; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there cannot be.
translation: "The prābhava-prakāśa expansions of Lord Kṛṣṇa are not like the expansions of the sage Saubhari. Had they been so, Nārada would not have been astonished to see them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.17
description: After reaching Pātaḍā, he met a landholder and submissively requested him to get him across that hilly tract of land.
text:
> tathā eka bhaumika haya, tāra ṭhāñi gelā
> 'parvata pāra kara āmā'---vinati karilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---there; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:b:bhaumika]]---one landowner; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---unto him; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---he went; [[synonyms:p:parvata]]---the hilly tract; [[synonyms:p:pāra]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---cross over; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]---me; [[synonyms:v:vinati]]---submission; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---he made.
translation: After reaching Pātaḍā, he met a landholder and submissively requested him to get him across that hilly tract of land.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.170
description: " 'It is astounding that Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is one without a second, expanded Himself in sixteen thousand similar forms to marry sixteen thousand queens in their respective homes.'
text:
> citraṁ bataitad ekena
> vapuṣā yugapat pṛthak
> gṛheṣu dvy-aṣṭa-sāhasraṁ
> striya eka udāvahat
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:citram]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:b:bata]]---oh; [[synonyms:e:etat]]---this; [[synonyms:e:ekena]]---with one; [[synonyms:v:vapuṣā]]---form; [[synonyms:y:yugapat]]---simultaneously; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---separately; [[synonyms:g:gṛheṣu]]---in the houses; [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:a:asta]]-[[synonyms:s:sāhasram]]---sixteen thousand; [[synonyms:s:striyaḥ]]---all the queens; [[synonyms:e:ekaḥ]]---the one Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:u:udāvahat]]---married.
translation: “ 'It is astounding that Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is one without a second, expanded Himself in sixteen thousand similar forms to marry sixteen thousand queens in their respective homes.'
purport: This verse is spoken by Nārada Muni in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.69.2).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.171
description: "If one form or feature is differently manifested according to different emotional features, it is called vaibhava-prakāśa.
text:
> sei vapu, sei ākṛti pṛthak yadi bhāse
> bhāvāveśa-bhede nāma 'vaibhava-prakāśe'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vapu]]---that form; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ā:ākṛti]]---that feature; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---different; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---appears; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---of the ecstatic emotion; [[synonyms:b:bhede]]---according to varieties; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---vaibhava-prakāśa.
translation: "If one form or feature is differently manifested according to different emotional features, it is called vaibhava-prakāśa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.172
description: "When the Lord expands Himself in innumerable forms, there is no difference in the forms, but due to different features, bodily colors and weapons, the names are different.
text:
> ananta prakāśe kṛṣṇera nāhi mūrti-bheda
> ākāra-varṇa-astra-bhede nāma-vibheda
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---in innumerable manifestations; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]-[[synonyms:b:bheda]]---difference of form; [[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---of features; [[synonyms:v:varṇa]]---of color; [[synonyms:a:astra]]---of weapons; [[synonyms:b:bhede]]---according to differentiation; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:v:vibheda]]---difference of names.
translation: "When the Lord expands Himself in innumerable forms, there is no difference in the forms, but due to different features, bodily colors and weapons, the names are different.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.173
description: " 'In different Vedic scriptures, there are prescribed rules and regulative principles for worshiping different types of forms. When one is purified by these rules and regulations, he worships You, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although manifest in many forms, You are one.'
text:
> anye ca saṁskṛtātmāno
> vidhinābhihitena te
> yajanti tvan-mayās tvāṁ vai
> bahu-mūrtyeka-mūrtikam
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anye]]---different persons; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:s:saṁskṛta]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmānaḥ]]---persons who are purified; [[synonyms:v:vidhinā]]---by the regulative principles; [[synonyms:a:abhihitena]]---stated in the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:t:te]]---such persons; [[synonyms:y:yajanti]]---worship; [[synonyms:t:tvat]]-[[synonyms:m:mayāḥ]]---being absorbed in You; [[synonyms:t:tvām]]---You; [[synonyms:v:vai]]---certainly; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---having many forms; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrtikam]]---although one.
translation: “ 'In different Vedic scriptures, there are prescribed rules and regulative principles for worshiping different types of forms. When one is purified by these rules and regulations, he worships You, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although manifest in many forms, You are one.'
purport:
This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.40.7). In the //Vedas// it is stated that the one becomes many (//eko bahu syām).// The Supreme Personality of Godhead expands Himself in various forms-//viṣṇu-tattva, jīva-tattva// and //śakti-tattva.//

According to the Vedic literatures, there are different regulative principles for the worship of each of these forms. If one takes advantage of the Vedic literatures and purifies himself by following the rules and regulations, ultimately he worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa says in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:4:11|(Bg. 4.11)]]: //mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ.// Worship of the demigods is in a sense worship of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but such worship is said to be //avidhi-pūrvakam,// improper. Actually demigod worship is meant for unintelligent men. One who is intelligent considers the words of the Supreme Personality of Godhead: //sarva dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja.// One who worships demigods worships the Supreme Lord indirectly, but according to the revealed scriptures, there is no need to worship Him indirectly. One can worship Him directly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.174
description: "The first manifestation of the vaibhava feature of Kṛṣṇa is Śrī Balarāmajī. Śrī Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa have different bodily colors, but otherwise Śrī Balarāma is equal to Kṛṣṇa in all respects.
text:
> vaibhava-prakāśa kṛṣṇera---śrī-balarāma
> varṇa-mātra-bheda, saba---kṛṣṇera samāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---manifestation of the vaibhava feature; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:b:balarāma]]---Śrī Balarāma; [[synonyms:v:varṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mātra]]---color only; [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---difference; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---everything; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:s:samāna]]---equal to Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "The first manifestation of the vaibhava feature of Kṛṣṇa is Śrī Balarāmajī. Śrī Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa have different bodily colors, but otherwise Śrī Balarāma is equal to Kṛṣṇa in all respects.
purport: To understand the difference between //svayaṁ-rūpa, tad-ekātma-rūpa, āveśa, prābhava// and //vaibhava,// Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has given the following description. In the beginning, Kṛṣṇa has three bodily features: (1) //svayaṁ-rūpa,// as a cowherd boy in Vṛndāvana; (2) //tad-ekātma-rūpa,// which is divided into //svāṁśaka// and //vilāsa;// and (3) //āveśa-rūpa.// The //svāṁśaka,// or expansions of the personal potency, are (1) Kāraṇodakaśāyī, Garbhodakaśāyī, Kṣīrodakaśāyī and (2) incarnations such as the fish, tortoise, boar and Nṛsiṁha. The //vilāsa-rūpa// has a //prābhava// division, including Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. There is also a //vaibhava// division in which there are twenty-four forms, including the second Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. For each of these, there are three forms; therefore there are twelve forms altogether. These twelve forms constitute the predominant names for the twelve months of the year as well as the twelve //tilaka// marks on the body. Each of the four Personalities of Godhead expands into two other forms; thus there are eight forms, such as Puruṣottama, Acyuta, etc. The four forms (Vāsudeva, etc.), the twelve (Keśava, etc.), and the eight (Puruṣottama, etc.) all together constitute twenty-four forms. All the forms are differently named in accordance with the weapons They hold in Their four hands.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.175
description: "An example of vaibhava-prakāśa is the son of Devakī. He sometimes has two hands and sometimes four hands.
text:
> vaibhava-prakāśa yaiche devakī-tanuja
> dvibhuja-svarūpa kabhu, kabhu haya caturbhuja
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---the feature of //vaibhava-prakāśa//; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just as; [[synonyms:d:devakī]]-[[synonyms:t:tanuja]]---the son of Devakī; [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---two-handed; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---form; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---four-handed.
translation: "An example of vaibhava-prakāśa is the son of Devakī. He sometimes has two hands and sometimes four hands.
purport: When Lord Kṛṣṇa took His birth, He appeared outside the womb as four-handed Viṣṇu. Then Devakī and Vasudeva offered their prayers to Him and asked Him to assume His two-handed form. The Lord immediately assumed His two handed form and ordered that He be transferred to Gokula on the other side of the River Yamunā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.176
description: "When the Lord is two-handed, He is called vaibhava-prakāśa, and when He is four-handed He is called prābhava-prakāśa.
text:
> ye-kāle dvibhuja, nāma---vaibhava-prakāśa
> caturbhuja haile, nāma---prābhava-prakāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]] [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---when the Lord appears as two-handed; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---//vaibhava-prakāśa//; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]] [[synonyms:h:haile]]---when He becomes four-handed; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:p:prābhava]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---//prābhava-prakāśa.//
translation: "When the Lord is two-handed, He is called vaibhava-prakāśa, and when He is four-handed He is called prābhava-prakāśa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.177
description: "In His original form, the Lord dresses like a cowherd boy and thinks Himself one of them. When He appears as Vāsudeva, the son of Vasudeva and Devakī, His dress and consciousness are those of a kṣatriya, a warrior.
text:
> sva yaṁ-rūpera gopa-veśa, gopa-abhimāna
> vāsudevera kṣatriya-veśa, 'āmi---kṣatriya'-jñāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svayam]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpera]]---of the original form; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:v:veśa]]---the dress of a cowherd boy; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:a:abhimāna]]---thinking Himself a cowherd boy; [[synonyms:v:vāsudevera]]---of Vāsudeva, the son of Vasudeva and Devakī; [[synonyms:k:kṣatriya]]-[[synonyms:v:veśa]]---the dress is like that of a kṣatriya; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kṣatriya]]---a kṣatriya; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge.
translation: "In His original form, the Lord dresses like a cowherd boy and thinks Himself one of them. When He appears as Vāsudeva, the son of Vasudeva and Devakī, His dress and consciousness are those of a kṣatriya, a warrior.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.178
description: "When one compares the beauty, opulence, sweetness and intellectual pastimes of Vāsudeva, the warrior, to Kṛṣṇa, the cowherd boy, son of Nanda Mahārāja, one sees that Kṛṣṇa's attributes are more pleasant.
text:
> saundarya, aiśvarya, mādhurya, vaidagdhya-vilāsa
> vrajendra-nandane ihā adhika ullāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saundarya]]---the beauty; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---the opulence; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---the sweetness; [[synonyms:v:vaidagdhya]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---the intellectual pastimes; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandane]]---of the son of Nanda Mahārāja and Yaśodā; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---all these; [[synonyms:a:adhika]] [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---more jubilant.
translation: "When one compares the beauty, opulence, sweetness and intellectual pastimes of Vāsudeva, the warrior, to Kṛṣṇa, the cowherd boy, son of Nanda Mahārāja, one sees that Kṛṣṇa's attributes are more pleasant.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.179
description: "Indeed, Vāsudeva is agitated just to see the sweetness of Govinda, and a transcendental greed awakens in Him to enjoy that sweetness.
text:
> govindera mādhurī dekhi' vāsudevera kṣobha
> se mādhurī āsvādite upajaya lobha
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:govindera]]---of Lord Govinda; [[synonyms:m:mādhurī]]---the sweetness; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:v:vāsudevera]]---of Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:k:kṣobha]]---agitation; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:m:mādhurī]]---sweetness; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādite]]---to taste; [[synonyms:u:upajaya]]---awakens; [[synonyms:l:lobha]]---greed.
translation: "Indeed, Vāsudeva is agitated just to see the sweetness of Govinda, and a transcendental greed awakens in Him to enjoy that sweetness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.18
description: A man who was expert in palmistry was at that time staying with the landlord. Knowing about Sanātana, he whispered the following in the landlord's ear.
text:
> sei bhūñāra saṅge haya hāta-gaṇitā
> bhūñāra kāṇe kahe sei jāni' ei kathā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:b:bhūñāra]]---the landlord; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:h:hāta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇita]]---an expert in palmistry; [[synonyms:b:bhūñāra]]---of the landlord; [[synonyms:k:kāṇe]]---in the ear; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that man; [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---knowing; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---this statement.
translation: A man who was expert in palmistry was at that time staying with the landlord. Knowing about Sanātana, he whispered the following in the landlord's ear.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.180
description: " 'My dear friend, this dramatic actor appears like a second form of My own self. Like a picture, He displays My pastimes as a cowherd boy overflowing with wonderfully attractive sweetness and fragrance, which are so dear to the damsels of Vraja. When I see such a display, My heart becomes greatly excited. I long for such pastimes and desire a form exactly like the damsels of Vraja.'
text:
> udgīrṇādbhuta-mādhurī-parimalasyābhīra-līlasya me
> dvaitaṁ hanta samīkṣayan muhur asau citrīyate cāraṇaḥ
> cetaḥ keli-kutūhalottaralitaṁ satyaṁ sakhe māmakaṁ
> yasya prekṣya svarūpatāṁ vraja-vadhū-sārūpyam anvicchati
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:udgīrṇa]]---overflowing; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:m:mādhurī]]---sweetness; [[synonyms:p:parimalasya]]---whose fragrance; [[synonyms:ā:ābhīra]]---of a cowherd boy; [[synonyms:l:līlasya]]---who has pastimes; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:d:dvaitam]]---second form; [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---alas; [[synonyms:s:samīkṣayan]]---showing; [[synonyms:m:muhuḥ]]---again and again; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---that; [[synonyms:c:citrīyate]]---is acting like a picture; [[synonyms:c:cāraṇaḥ]]---dramatic actor; [[synonyms:c:cetaḥ]]---heart; [[synonyms:k:keli]]-[[synonyms:k:kutūhala]]---by longing for pastimes; [[synonyms:u:uttaralitam]]---greatly excited; [[synonyms:s:satyam]]---actually; [[synonyms:s:sakhe]]---O dear friend; [[synonyms:m:māmakam]]---My; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:p:prekṣya]]---by seeing; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpatām]]---similarity to My form; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:v:vadhū]]---of the damsels of Vrajabhūmi; [[synonyms:s:sārūpyam]]---a form like the forms; [[synonyms:a:anvicchati]]---desires.
translation: “ 'My dear friend, this dramatic actor appears like a second form of My own self. Like a picture, He displays My pastimes as a cowherd boy overflowing with wonderfully attractive sweetness and fragrance, which are so dear to the damsels of Vraja. When I see such a display, My heart becomes greatly excited. I long for such pastimes and desire a form exactly like the damsels of Vraja.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Lalita-mādhava// (4.19).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.181
description: "One instance of Vāsudeva's attraction to Kṛṣṇa occurred when Vāsudeva saw the Gandharva dance at Mathurā. Another instance occurred in Dvārakā when Vāsudeva was surprised to see a picture of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> mathurāya yaiche gandharva-nṛtya-daraśane
> punaḥ dvārakāte yaiche citra-vilokane
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mathurāya]]---at Mathurā; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just as; [[synonyms:g:gandharva]]-[[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---the dance of the Gandharvas; [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---by seeing; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:d:dvārakāte]]---at Dvārakā; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just as; [[synonyms:c:citra]]-[[synonyms:v:vilokane]]---by seeing a picture of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "One instance of Vāsudeva's attraction to Kṛṣṇa occurred when Vāsudeva saw the Gandharva dance at Mathurā. Another instance occurred in Dvārakā when Vāsudeva was surprised to see a picture of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.182
description: " 'Who manifests an abundance of sweetness greater than Mine, which has never been experienced before and which causes wonder to all? Alas, I Myself, My mind bewildered upon seeing this beauty, impetuously desire to enjoy it like Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.'
text:
> aparikalita-pūrvaḥ kaś camatkāra-kārī
> sphuratu mama garīyān eṣa mādhurya-pūraḥ
> ayam aham api hanta prekṣya yaṁ lubdha-cetāḥ
> sarabhasam upabhoktuṁ kāmaye rādhikeva
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aparikalita]]---not experienced; [[synonyms:p:pūrvaḥ]]---previously; [[synonyms:k:kaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]-[[synonyms:k:kārī]]---causing wonder; [[synonyms:s:sphuratu]]---manifests; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---My; [[synonyms:g:garīyān]]---more great; [[synonyms:e:eṣaḥ]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]-[[synonyms:p:pūraḥ]]---abundance of sweetness; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---alas; [[synonyms:p:prekṣya]]---seeing; [[synonyms:y:yam]]---which; [[synonyms:l:lubdha]]-[[synonyms:c:cetāḥ]]---My mind being bewildered; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:r:rabhasam]]---impetuously; [[synonyms:u:upabhoktum]]---to enjoy; [[synonyms:k:kāmaye]]---desire; [[synonyms:r:rādhikā]] [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
translation: “ 'Who manifests an abundance of sweetness greater than Mine, which has never been experienced before and which causes wonder to all? Alas, I Myself, My mind bewildered upon seeing this beauty, impetuously desire to enjoy it like Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.'
purport: This verse spoken by Vāsudeva in Dvārakā is recorded by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī in his //Lalita-mādhava// (8.34).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.183
description: "When that body is a little differently manifest and its features a little different in transcendental emotion and form, it is called tad-ekātma.
text:
> sei vapu bhinnābhāse kichu bhinnākāra
> bhāvāveśākṛti-bhede 'tad-ekātma' nāma tāṅra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vapu]]---that body; [[synonyms:b:bhinna]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāse]]---manifested differently; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:b:bhinna]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---bodily differences; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṛti]]---forms and transcendental emotions; [[synonyms:b:bhede]]---by different; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:e:ekātma]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name is //tad-ekātma//; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "When that body is a little differently manifest and its features a little different in transcendental emotion and form, it is called tad-ekātma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.184
description: "In the tad-ekātma-rūpa there are pastime expansions [vilāsa] and personal expansions [svāṁśa]. Consequently there are two divisions. According to pastime and personal expansion, there are various differences.
text:
> tad-ekātma-rūpe 'vilāsa', 'svāṁśa'---dui bheda
> vilāsa, svāṁśera bhede vividha vibheda
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:e:ekātma]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in the form of //tad-ekātma//; [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---pastime; [[synonyms:s:svāṁśa]]---personal expansion; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---two divisions; [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---of the pastime expansion; [[synonyms:s:svāṁśera]]---of the personal expansion; [[synonyms:b:bhede]]---by differences; [[synonyms:v:vividha]]---various; [[synonyms:v:vibheda]]---distinctions.
translation: "In the tad-ekātma-rūpa there are pastime expansions [vilāsa] and personal expansions [svāṁśa]. Consequently there are two divisions. According to pastime and personal expansion, there are various differences.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.185
description: "Again the vilāsa forms are divided into twofold categories-prābhava and vaibhava. Again the pastimes of these forms are of unlimited variety.
text:
> prābhava-vaibhava-bhede vilāsa---dvidhākāra
> vilāsera vilāsa-bheda---ananta prakāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prābhava]]-[[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]-[[synonyms:b:bhede]]---by the differences between //prābhava// and //vaibhava,//; [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---pastime expansion; [[synonyms:d:dvidhā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---twofold; [[synonyms:v:vilāsera]]---of pastime forms; [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]-[[synonyms:b:bheda]]---by the different pastimes; [[synonyms:a:ananta]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---unlimited varieties.
translation: "Again the vilāsa forms are divided into twofold categories-prābhava and vaibhava. Again the pastimes of these forms are of unlimited variety.
purport:
In the //Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta, Pūrva-khaṇḍa,// verse 17, it is stated:

> tādṛśo nyūna-śaktiṁ yo
> vyanakti svāṁśa īritaḥ
> saṅkarṣaṇādir matsyādir
> yathā tat-tat-svadhāmasu

When a form of Kṛṣṇa is nondifferent from the original form but is less important and exhibits less potency, it is called //svāṁśa.// Examples of the //svāṁśa// expansion can be found in the quadruple forms of the Lord residing in their respective places, beginning with Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha and including the //puruṣa-avatāras, līlā-avatāras, manvantara-avatāras// and //yuga-avatāras.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.186
description: "The chief quadruple expansions are named Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. These are called prābhava-vilāsa.
text:
> prābhava-vilāsa---vāsudeva, saṅkarṣaṇa
> pradyumna, aniruddha,---mukhya cāri-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prābhava]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---the //prābhava-vilāsa// forms; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]---Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:s:saṅkarṣaṇa]]---Saṅkarṣaṇa; [[synonyms:p:pradyumna]]---Pradyumna; [[synonyms:a:aniruddha]]---Aniruddha; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---the four chief expansions.
translation: "The chief quadruple expansions are named Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. These are called prābhava-vilāsa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.187
