description: "Balarāma, who has the same original form of Kṛṣṇa, is Himself a cowherd boy in Vṛndāvana, and He also considers Himself to belong to the kṣatriya race in Dvārakā. Thus His color and dress are different, and He is called a pastime form of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> vraje gopa-bhāva rāmera, pure kṣatriya-bhāvana
> varṇa-veśa-bheda, tāte 'vilāsa' tāṅra nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---emotion of a cowherd boy; [[synonyms:r:rāmera]]---of Balarāma; [[synonyms:p:pure]]---in Dvārakā; [[synonyms:k:kṣatriya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvana]]---the emotion of a kṣatriya; [[synonyms:v:varṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:veśa]]-[[synonyms:b:bheda]]---by differences of dress and color; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---pastime expansion; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---His name.
translation: "Balarāma, who has the same original form of Kṛṣṇa, is Himself a cowherd boy in Vṛndāvana, and He also considers Himself to belong to the kṣatriya race in Dvārakā. Thus His color and dress are different, and He is called a pastime form of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.188
description: "Śrī Balarāma is a vaibhava-prakāśa manifestation of Kṛṣṇa. He is also manifest in the original quadruple expansion of Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. These are prābhava-vilāsa expansions with different emotions.
text:
> vaibhava-prakāśe āra prābhava-vilāse
> eka-i mūrtye baladeva bhāva-bhede bhāse
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---in vaibhava manifestation; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:prābhava]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāse]]---in the prābhava pastime form; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:i:i]] [[synonyms:m:mūrtye]]---in one form; [[synonyms:b:baladeva]]---Lord Baladeva; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhede]]---according to different emotions; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---exists.
translation: "Śrī Balarāma is a vaibhava-prakāśa manifestation of Kṛṣṇa. He is also manifest in the original quadruple expansion of Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. These are prābhava-vilāsa expansions with different emotions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.189
description: "The first expansion of the caturvyūha, quadruple forms, is unique. There is nothing to compare with Them. These quadruple forms are the source of unlimited quadruple forms.
text:
> ādi-catur-vyūha---iṅhāra keha nāhi sama
> ananta caturvyūha-gaṇera prākaṭya-kāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vyūha]]---the original quadruple group; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]]---of this; [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---no one; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vyūha]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the quadruple expansions; [[synonyms:p:prākaṭya]]---of manifestation; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause.
translation: "The first expansion of the caturvyūha, quadruple forms, is unique. There is nothing to compare with Them. These quadruple forms are the source of unlimited quadruple forms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.19
description: The palmist said, "This man Sanātana possesses eight gold coins." Hearing this, the landlord was very pleased and spoke the following to Sanātana Gosvāmī.
text:
> 'iṅhāra ṭhāñi suvarṇera aṣṭa mohara haya'
> śuni' ānandita bhūñā sanātane kaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---in the possession of this man; [[synonyms:s:suvarṇera]]---of gold; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]]---eight; [[synonyms:m:mohara]]---coins; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---pleased; [[synonyms:b:bhūñā]]---the landlord; [[synonyms:s:sanātane]]---to Sanātana; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---says.
translation: The palmist said, "This man Sanātana possesses eight gold coins." Hearing this, the landlord was very pleased and spoke the following to Sanātana Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.190
description: "These four prābhava pastime forms of Lord Kṛṣṇa reside eternally in Dvārakā and Mathurā.
text:
> kṛṣṇera ei cāri prābhava-vilāsa
> dvārakā-mathurā-pure nitya iṅhāra vāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---four; [[synonyms:p:prābhava]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---//prābhava// pastime forms; [[synonyms:d:dvārakā]]-[[synonyms:m:mathurā]]-[[synonyms:p:pure]]---in the two cities Dvārakā and Mathurā; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---eternal; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]]---of Them; [[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---the residential quarters.
translation: "These four prābhava pastime forms of Lord Kṛṣṇa reside eternally in Dvārakā and Mathurā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.191
description: "From the original quadruple expansion, twenty-four forms are manifest. They differ according to the placement of weapons in Their four hands. They are called vaibhava-vilāsa.
text:
> ei cāri haite cabbiśa mūrti parakāśa
> astra-bhede nāma-bheda---vaibhava-vilāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from these four; [[synonyms:c:cabbiśa]]---twenty-four; [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---forms; [[synonyms:p:parakāśa]]---manifestation; [[synonyms:a:astra]]-[[synonyms:b:bhede]]---according to the different weapons; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:b:bheda]]---the difference of names; [[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---the //vaibhava// pastime expansions.
translation: "From the original quadruple expansion, twenty-four forms are manifest. They differ according to the placement of weapons in Their four hands. They are called vaibhava-vilāsa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.192
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa again expands, and within the paravyoma, the spiritual sky, He is situated in fullness as the four-handed Nārāyaṇa, accompanied by expansions of the original quadruple form.
text:
> punaḥ kṛṣṇa catur-vyūha lañā pūrva-rūpe
> paravyoma-madhye vaise nārāyaṇa-rūpe
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vyūha]]---the quadruple expansions; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---as previously; [[synonyms:p:paravyoma]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in the paravyoma area; [[synonyms:v:vaise]]---resides; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in the form of four-handed Nārāyaṇa.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa again expands, and within the paravyoma, the spiritual sky, He is situated in fullness as the four-handed Nārāyaṇa, accompanied by expansions of the original quadruple form.
purport: At the top of the //paravyoma,// the spiritual sky, there is Goloka Vṛndāvana, which is divided into three parts. Two of the parts, called Mathurā and Dvārakā, are the residences of Kṛṣṇa in His //prābhava-vilāsa// forms. Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa's //vaibhava-prakāśa,// is eternally situated in Gokula. From the quadruple //prābhava-vilāsa,// twenty-four forms of the //vaibhava-vilāsa// are expanded. Each has four hands holding weapons in different positions. The topmost planet in the spiritual sky is Goloka Vṛndāvana, and below that planet is the spiritual sky itself. In that spiritual sky, Kṛṣṇa Himself is four-handed and is situated as Nārāyaṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.193
description: "Thus the original quadruple forms again manifest Themselves in a second quadruple expansion. The residences of these second quadruple expansions cover the four directions.
text:
> tāṅhā haite punaḥ catur-vyūha-parakāśa
> āvaraṇa-rūpe cāri-dike yāṅra vāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from that original //catur-vyūha//; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vyūha]]-[[synonyms:p:parakāśa]]---manifestation of quadruple expansions; [[synonyms:ā:āvaraṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in the form of a covering; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---in four directions; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---residence.
translation: "Thus the original quadruple forms again manifest Themselves in a second quadruple expansion. The residences of these second quadruple expansions cover the four directions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.194
description: "Again these quadruple forms expand three times, beginning with Keśava. That is the fulfillment of the pastime forms.
text:
> cāri-janera punaḥ pṛthak tina tina mūrti
> keśavādi yāhā haite vilāsera pūrti
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:j:janera]]---of the original of the four expansions; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---separate; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three each; [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---forms; [[synonyms:k:keśava]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---beginning with Lord Keśava; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from which; [[synonyms:v:vilāsera]] [[synonyms:p:pūrti]]---the vilāsa expansions are fulfilled.
translation: "Again these quadruple forms expand three times, beginning with Keśava. That is the fulfillment of the pastime forms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.195
description: "Out of the catur-vyūha, there are three expansions of each and every form, and they are named differently according to the position of the weapons. The Vāsudeva expansions are Keśava, Nārāyaṇa and Mādhava.
text:
> cakrādi-dhāraṇa-bhede nāma-bheda saba
> vāsudevera mūrti---keśava, nārāyaṇa, mādhava
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cakra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---of the disc and other weapons; [[synonyms:d:dhāraṇa]]---of holding; [[synonyms:b:bhede]]---by differences; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---of names; [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---differences; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vāsudevera]] [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---the expansions of Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:k:keśava]]---Keśava; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]---Mādhava.
translation: "Out of the catur-vyūha, there are three expansions of each and every form, and they are named differently according to the position of the weapons. The Vāsudeva expansions are Keśava, Nārāyaṇa and Mādhava.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.196
description: "The expansions of Saṅkarṣaṇa are Govinda, Viṣṇu and Madhusūdana. This Govinda is different from the original Govinda, for He is not the son of Mahārāja Nanda.
text:
> saṅkarṣaṇera mūrti---govinda, viṣṇu, madhusūdana
> e anya govinda---nahe vrajendra-nandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saṅkarṣaṇera]] [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---the expansions of Saṅkarṣaṇa; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sūdana]]---Madhusūdana; [[synonyms:e:e]]---this; [[synonyms:a:anya]]---another; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:n:nahe]] [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---not the son of Nanda Mahārāja.
translation: "The expansions of Saṅkarṣaṇa are Govinda, Viṣṇu and Madhusūdana. This Govinda is different from the original Govinda, for He is not the son of Mahārāja Nanda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.197
description: "The expansions of Pradyumna are Trivikrama, Vāmana and Śrīdhara. The expansions of Aniruddha are Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha and Dāmodara.
text:
> pradyumnera mūrti---trivikrama, vāmana, śrīdhara
> aniruddhera mūrti---hṛṣīkeśa, padmanābha, dāmodara
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pradyumnera]] [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---expansions of the form of Pradyumna; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:v:vikrama]]---Trivikrama; [[synonyms:v:vāmana]]---Vāmana; [[synonyms:ś:śrīdhara]]---Śrīdhara; [[synonyms:a:aniruddhera]] [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---expansions of Aniruddha; [[synonyms:h:hṛṣīkeśa]]---Hṛṣīkeśa; [[synonyms:p:padmanābha]]---Padmanābha; [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Dāmodara.
translation: "The expansions of Pradyumna are Trivikrama, Vāmana and Śrīdhara. The expansions of Aniruddha are Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha and Dāmodara.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.198
description: "These twelve are the predominating Deities of the twelve months. Keśava is the predominating Deity of Agrahāyana, and Nārāyaṇa is the predominating Deity of Pauṣa.
text:
> dvādaśa-māsera devatā---ei-bāra jana
> mārga-śīrṣe---keśava, pauṣe---nārāyaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dvādaśa]]-[[synonyms:m:māsera]]---of the twelve months; [[synonyms:d:devatā]]---predominating Deities; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:b:bāra]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---twelve Personalities of Godhead; [[synonyms:m:mārga]]-[[synonyms:ś:śīrṣe]]---the month of Agrahāyana (November-December); [[synonyms:k:keśava]]---Keśava; [[synonyms:p:pauṣe]]---the month of Pauṣa (December-January); [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---Nārāyaṇa.
translation: "These twelve are the predominating Deities of the twelve months. Keśava is the predominating Deity of Agrahāyana, and Nārāyaṇa is the predominating Deity of Pauṣa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.199
description: "The predominating Deity for the month of Māgha is Mādhava, and the predominating Deity for the month of Phālguna is Govinda. Viṣṇu is the predominating Deity for Caitra, and Madhusūdana is the predominating Deity for Vaiśākha.
text:
> māghera devatā---mādhava, govinda---phālgune
> caitre---viṣṇu, vaiśākhe---śrī-madhusūdana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māghera]] [[synonyms:d:devatā]]---the predominating Deity of the month of Māgha (January-February); [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]---Mādhava; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:p:phālgune]]---in the month of Phālguna (February-March); [[synonyms:c:caitre]]---in the month of Caitra (March-April); [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:v:vaiśākhe]]---in the month of Vaiśākha (April-May); [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:m:madhusūdana]]---Madhusūdana.
translation: "The predominating Deity for the month of Māgha is Mādhava, and the predominating Deity for the month of Phālguna is Govinda. Viṣṇu is the predominating Deity for Caitra, and Madhusūdana is the predominating Deity for Vaiśākha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.2
description: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!
text:
> jaya jaya śrī-caitanya jaya nityānanda
> jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---to Nityānanda; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---to Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---to all devotees of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.20
description: The landlord said, "I shall get you across that hilly tract at night with my own men. Now just take your lunch and cook for yourself."
text:
> "rātrye parvata pāra kariba nija-loka diyā
> bhojana karaha tumi randhana kariyā"
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rātrye]]---at night; [[synonyms:p:parvata]]---the hilly tract; [[synonyms:p:pāra]] [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---I shall cross; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---with my own men; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]] [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---just take your meal; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:r:randhana]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---cooking.
translation: The landlord said, "I shall get you across that hilly tract at night with my own men. Now just take your lunch and cook for yourself."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.200
description: "In the month of Jyaiṣṭha, the predominating Deity is Trivikrama. In Āṣāḍha the Deity is Vāmana, in Śrāvaṇa the Deity is Śrīdhara, and in Bhādra the Deity is Hṛṣīkeśa.
text:
> jyaiṣṭhe---trivikrama, āṣāḍhe---vāmana deveśa
> śrāvaṇe---śrīdhara, bhādre---deva hṛṣīkeśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jyaiṣṭhe]]---in the month of Jyaiṣṭha (May-June); [[synonyms:t:trivikrama]]---Trivikrama; [[synonyms:ā:āṣāḍhe]]---in the month of Āṣāḍha (June-July); [[synonyms:v:vāmana]] [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśa]]---Lord Vāmana; [[synonyms:ś:śrāvaṇe]]---in the month of Śrāvaṇa (July-August); [[synonyms:ś:śrīdhara]]---Śrīdhara; [[synonyms:b:bhādre]]---in the month of Bhādra (August-September); [[synonyms:d:deva]] [[synonyms:h:hṛṣīkeśa]]---Lord Hṛṣīkeśa.
translation: "In the month of Jyaiṣṭha, the predominating Deity is Trivikrama. In Āṣāḍha the Deity is Vāmana, in Śrāvaṇa the Deity is Śrīdhara, and in Bhādra the Deity is Hṛṣīkeśa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.201
description: "In the month of Āśvina, the predominating Deity is Padmanābha, and in Kārttika it is Dāmodara. This Dāmodara is different from Rādhā-Dāmodara, the son of Nanda Mahārāja in Vṛndāvana.
text:
> āśvine---padmanābha, kārtike dāmodara
> 'rādhā-dāmodara' anya vrajendra-koṅara
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āśvine]]---in the month of Āśvina (September-October); [[synonyms:p:padma]]-[[synonyms:n:nābha]]---Padmanābha; [[synonyms:k:kārtike]]---in the month of Kārttika (October-November); [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Dāmodara; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---the Dāmodara of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:a:anya]]---another; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:k:koṅara]]---the son of Mahārāja Nanda.
translation: "In the month of Āśvina, the predominating Deity is Padmanābha, and in Kārttika it is Dāmodara. This Dāmodara is different from Rādhā-Dāmodara, the son of Nanda Mahārāja in Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.202
description: "When putting the twelve tilaka marks on the twelve places of the body, one has to chant the mantra consisting of these twelve Viṣṇu names. After daily worship, when one anoints the different parts of the body with water, these names should be chanted as one touches each part of the body.
text:
> dvādaśa-tilaka-mantra ei dvādaśa nāma
> ācamane ei nāme sparśi tat-tat-sthāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dvādaśa]]-[[synonyms:t:tilaka]]---for twelve marks of tilaka; [[synonyms:m:mantra]]---the mantra; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:d:dvādaśa]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---twelve names; [[synonyms:ā:ācamane]]---in washing with water; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:n:nāme]]---with these names; [[synonyms:s:sparśi]]---we touch; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---the respective places.
translation: "When putting the twelve tilaka marks on the twelve places of the body, one has to chant the mantra consisting of these twelve Viṣṇu names. After daily worship, when one anoints the different parts of the body with water, these names should be chanted as one touches each part of the body.
purport:
While marking the body with //tilaka,// one should chant the following //mantra,// which consists of the twelve names of Lord Viṣṇu.

> lalāṭe keśavaṁ dhyāyen
> nārāyaṇam athodare
> vakṣaḥ-sthale mādhavaṁ tu
> govindaṁ kaṇṭha-kūpake
>
> viṣṇuṁ ca dakṣiṇe kukṣau
> bāhau ca madhusūdanam
> trivikramaṁ kandhare tu
> vāmanaṁ vāma-pārśvake
>
> śrīdharaṁ vāma-bāhau tu
> hṛṣīkeśaṁ tu kandhare
> pṛṣṭhe ca padmanābhaṁ ca
> kaṭyāṁ dāmodaraṁ nyaset

"When one marks the forehead with //tilaka,// he must remember Keśava. When one marks the lower abdomen, he must remember Nārāyaṇa. For the chest, one should remember Mādhava, and when marking the hollow of the neck one should remember Govinda. Lord Viṣṇu should be remembered while marking the right side of the belly, and Madhusūdana should be remembered when marking the right arm. Trivikrama should be remembered when marking the right shoulder, and Vāmana should be remembered when marking the left side of the belly. Śrīdhara should be remembered while marking the left arm, and Hṛṣīkeśa should be remembered when marking the left shoulder. Padmanābha and Dāmodara should be remembered when marking the back."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.203
description: "From Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha, there are eight additional pastime expansions. O Sanātana, please hear Me as I mention Their names.
text:
> ei cāri-janera vilāsa-mūrti āra aṣṭa jana
> tāṅ sabāra nāma kahi, śuna sanātana

translation: "From Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha, there are eight additional pastime expansions. O Sanātana, please hear Me as I mention Their names.

> hari, kṛṣṇa, adhokṣaja, upendra,---aṣṭa-jana

translation: "The eight pastime expansions are Puruṣottama, Acyuta, Nṛsiṁha, Janārdana, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, Adhokṣaja and Upendra.

translation: "At Prayāga, the Lord is situated as Bindu Mādhava, and at Mandāra-parvata, the Lord is known as Madhusūdana. Vāsudeva, Padmanābha and Janārdana reside at Ānandāraṇya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.217
description: "At Viṣṇu-kāñcī there is Lord Viṣṇu, at Māyāpur Lord Hari, and throughout the universe a variety of other forms.
text:
> viṣṇu-kāñcīte viṣṇu, hari rahe, māyāpure
> aiche āra nānā mūrti brahmāṇḍa-bhitare
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:k:kāñcīte]]---at Viṣṇu-kāñcī; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:h:hari]]---Lord Hari; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:m:māyāpure]]---at Māyāpur; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---similarly; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---forms; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhitare]]---throughout the universe.
translation: "At Viṣṇu-kāñcī there is Lord Viṣṇu, at Māyāpur Lord Hari, and throughout the universe a variety of other forms.
purport:
All of these forms are //mūrti// forms, and They are worshiped in the temples. Their names are Keśava at Mathurā, Puruṣottama or Jagannātha at Nīlācala, Śrī Bindu Mādhava at Prayāga, Madhusūdana at Mandāra, and Vāsudeva, Padmanābha and Janārdana at Ānandāraṇya, which is situated in Kerala, South India. At Viṣṇu-kāñcī, which is situated in the Barada state, there is Lord Viṣṇu, and Hari is situated at Māyāpur, Lord Caitanya's birthsite. Thus in different places throughout the universe there are various Deities in temples bestowing Their causeless mercy upon the devotees. All these Deity forms are nondifferent from the //mūrtis// in the spiritual world of the Vaikuṇṭhas. Although the //arcā-mūrti,// the worshipable Deity form of the Lord, appears to be made of material elements, it is as good as the spiritual forms found in the spiritual Vaikuṇṭhalokas. The Deity in the temple, however, is visible to the material eyes of the devotee. It is not possible for one in material conditional life to see the spiritual form of the Lord. To bestow causeless mercy upon us, the Lord appears as //arcā-mūrti// so that we can see Him. It is forbidden to consider the //arcā-mūrti// to be made of stone or wood. In the //Padma Purāṇa// it is said:

> arcye viṣṇau śilā-dhīr guruṣu nara-matir vaiṣṇave jāti-buddhir
> viṣṇor vā vaiṣṇavānāṁ kali-mala-mathane pāda-tīrthe 'mbu-buddhiḥ
> śrī-viṣṇor nāmni mantre sakala-kaluṣa-he śabde-sāmānya-buddhir
> viṣṇau sarveśvareśe tad-itara-sama-dhīr yasya vā nārakī saḥ

No one should consider the Deity in the temple to be made of stone or wood, nor should one consider the spiritual master an ordinary human being. No one should consider a Vaiṣṇava to belong to a particular caste or creed, and no one should consider //caraṇāmṛta// or Ganges water to be like ordinary water. Nor should anyone consider the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// to be a material vibration. All these expansions of Kṛṣṇa in the material world are simply demonstrations of the Lord's mercy and willingness to give facility to His devotees who are engaged in His devotional service within the material world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.218
description: "Within the universe the Lord is situated in different spiritual manifestations. These are situated on seven islands in nine sections. Thus Their pastimes are going on.
text:
> ei-mata brahmāṇḍa-madhye sabāra 'parakāśa'
> sapta-dvīpe nava-khaṇḍe yāṅhāra vilāsa

translation: "Within the universe the Lord is situated in different spiritual manifestations. These are situated on seven islands in nine sections. Thus Their pastimes are going on.

The seven islands are mentioned in the //Siddhānta-śiromaṇi://

>
> śākaṁ tataḥ śālmala-matra kauśaṁ
> krauñcaṁ ca go-medaka-puṣkare ca
> dvayor dvayor antaram ekam ekaṁ
> samudrayor dvīpam udāharanti

The seven islands (//dvīpas//) are known as (1) Jambu, (2) Śāka, (3) Śālmalī, (4) Kuśa, (5) Krauñca, (6) Gomeda, or Plakṣa, and (7) Puṣkara. The planets are called //dvīpa.// Outer space is like an ocean of air. just as there are islands in the watery ocean, these planets in the ocean of space are called //dvīpas,// or islands in outer space. There are nine //khaṇḍas,// known as (1) Bhārata, (2) Kinnara, (3) Hari, (4) Kuru, (5) Hiraṇmaya, (6) Ramyaka, (7) Ilāvṛta, (8) Bhadrāśva and (9) Ketumāla. These are different parts of the Jambūdvīpa. A valley between two mountains is called a //khaṇḍa// or //varṣa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.219
description: "The Lord is situated in all the universes in different forms just to please His devotees. Thus the Lord destroys irreligious principles and establishes religious principles.
text:
> sarvatra prakāśa tāṅra---bhakte sukha dite
> jagatera adharma nāśi' dharma sthāpite
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarvatra]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---manifestations; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---to the devotees; [[synonyms:s:sukha]] [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give happiness; [[synonyms:j:jagatera]]---of the material world; [[synonyms:a:adharma]]---irreligious principles; [[synonyms:n:nāśi']]---destroying; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---religious principles; [[synonyms:s:sthāpite]]---to establish.
translation: "The Lord is situated in all the universes in different forms just to please His devotees. Thus the Lord destroys irreligious principles and establishes religious principles.
purport: In the material world the Lord is situated in different //arcā-mūrtis// (Deities) in the temples, just to decrease the material activities of the conditioned soul and increase his spiritual activities. Particularly in India there are many temples throughout the country. Devotees may take advantage of them and go see the Lord at Jagannātha Purī, Vṛndāvana, Prayāga, Mathurā, Hardwar and Viṣṇu-kāñcī. When the devotees travel to these places and see the Lord, they become very happy in devotional service.

translation: "Lord Adhokṣaja holds the lotus, club, conch and disc. Lord Upendra holds the conch, club, disc and lotus.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.237
description: "According to the Hayaśīrṣa-pañcarātra, there are sixteen personalities. I shall now describe that opinion of how They hold the weapons.

translation: "According to the Hayaśīrṣa-pañcarātra, there are sixteen personalities. I shall now describe that opinion of how They hold the weapons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.238

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.24

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.240
description: "Kṛṣṇa, the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, indicated as the son of Mahārāja Nanda, has two names. One is svayaṁ bhagavān, and the other is līlā-puruṣottama.
text:
> 'svayaṁ bhagavān' āra 'līlā-puruṣottama'
> ei dui nāma dhare vrajendra-nandana

translation: "Kṛṣṇa, the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, indicated as the son of Mahārāja Nanda, has two names. One is svayaṁ bhagavān, and the other is līlā-puruṣottama.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.241
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa personally surrounds Dvārakā Purī as its protector. In different parts of the Purī, in nine places, He expands in nine different forms.
text:
> purīra āvaraṇa-rūpe purīra nava-deśe
> nava-vyūha-rūpe nava-mūrti parakāśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purīra]]---of Dvārakā Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āvaraṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---as a covering for the four sides; [[synonyms:p:purīra]] [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in nine different parts of the city; [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:v:vyūha]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in nine Deities; [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---nine forms; [[synonyms:p:parakāśe]]---manifests.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa personally surrounds Dvārakā Purī as its protector. In different parts of the Purī, in nine places, He expands in nine different forms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.242
description: " 'The nine personalities mentioned are Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Nārāyaṇa, Nṛsiṁha, Hayagrīva, Varāha and Brahmā.'
text:
> catvāro vāsudevādyā
> nārāyaṇa-nṛsiṁhakau
> hayagrīvo mahākroḍo
> brahmā ceti navoditāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:catvāraḥ]]---four principal protectors; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādyāḥ]]---Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---including Lord Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁhakau]]---as well as Lord Nṛsiṁha; [[synonyms:h:hayagrīvaḥ]]---Lord Hayagrīva; [[synonyms:m:mahākroḍaḥ]]---Lord Varāha; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:u:uditāḥ]]---nine personalities.
translation: “ 'The nine personalities mentioned are Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Nārāyaṇa, Nṛsiṁha, Hayagrīva, Varāha and Brahmā.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta// (1.451). The Brahmā mentioned herein is not a living entity. Sometimes, when there is a scarcity of living entities to take charge of Brahmā's post, Mahā-Viṣṇu expands Himself as Lord Brahmā. This Brahmā is not considered to be a living entity; He is an expansion of Viṣṇu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.243
description: "I have already described the pastime and prakāśa forms. Now please hear about the different personal expansions.
text:
> prakāśa-vilāsera ei kailuṅ vivaraṇa
> svāṁśera bheda ebe śuna, sanātana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsera]]---of pastime forms and manifestations; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kailuṅ]]---I have made; [[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---description; [[synonyms:s:svāṁśera]]---of personal expansions; [[synonyms:b:bhede]]---the differences; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---O Sanātana Gosvāmī.
translation: "I have already described the pastime and prakāśa forms. Now please hear about the different personal expansions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.244
description: "The first personal expansion is Saṅkarṣaṇa, and the others are incarnations like the fish incarnation. Saṅkarṣaṇa is an expansion of the Puruṣa, or Viṣṇu. The incarnations such as Matsya, the fish incarnation, appear in different yugas for specific pastimes.
text:
> saṅkarṣaṇa, matsyādika,---dui bheda tāṅra
> saṅkarṣaṇa---puruṣāvatāra, līlāvatāra āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saṅkarṣaṇa]]---Saṅkarṣaṇa; [[synonyms:m:matsya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādika]]---and incarnations such as the fish; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---differentiations; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:s:saṅkarṣaṇa]]---Saṅkarṣaṇa; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations of Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---pastime incarnations; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and.
translation: "The first personal expansion is Saṅkarṣaṇa, and the others are incarnations like the fish incarnation. Saṅkarṣaṇa is an expansion of the Puruṣa, or Viṣṇu. The incarnations such as Matsya, the fish incarnation, appear in different yugas for specific pastimes.
purport:
The //puruṣa-avatāras// are the Lords of the universal creation. These are the Kāraṇodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu. There are also //līlā-avatāras,// and these include (1) Catuḥsana, (2) Nārada, (3) Varāha, (4) Matsya, (5) Yajña, (6) Nara-Nārāyaṇa, (7) Kārdami Kapila, (8) Dattātreya, (9) Hayaśīrṣā, (10) Haṁsa, (11) Dhruvapriya, or Pṛśnigarbha, (12) Ṛṣabha, (13) Pṛthu, (14) Nṛsiṁha, (15) Kūrma, (16) Dhanvantari, (17) Mohinī, (18) Vāmana, (19) Bhārgava Paraśurāma, (20) Rāghavendra, (21) Vyāsa, (22) Pralambāri Balarāma, (23) Kṛṣṇa, (24) Buddha and (25) Kalki.

These twenty-five Personalities of Godhead are known as //līlā-avatāras.// Because they appear in each day of Brahmā, or in each //kalpa// (millennium), they are sometimes known as //kalpa-avatāras.// Of these incarnations, Haṁsa and Mohinī are not very permanent or well known, but They are listed among the //prābhava-avatāras.// Kapila, Dattātreya, Ṛṣabha, Dhanvantari and Vyāsa are eternally situated and very widely known. They are also counted among the //prābhava// incarnations. Kūrma, Matsya, Nārāyaṇa, Varāha, Hayagrīva, Pṛśnigarbha, and Baladeva, the killer of Pralambāsura, are counted among the //vaibhava-avatāras.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.245
description: "There are six types of incarnations [avatāras] of Kṛṣṇa. One is the incarnations of Viṣṇu [puruṣa-avatāras], and another is the incarnations meant for the performance of pastimes [līlā-avatāras].
text:
> avatāra haya kṛṣṇera ṣaḍ-vidha prakāra
> puruṣāvatāra eka, līlāvatāra āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṭ]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---six kinds; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations of Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations for the execution of pastimes; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also.
translation: "There are six types of incarnations [avatāras] of Kṛṣṇa. One is the incarnations of Viṣṇu [puruṣa-avatāras], and another is the incarnations meant for the performance of pastimes [līlā-avatāras].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.246
description: "There are incarnations that control the material qualities [guṇa-avatāras], incarnations of the Manus [manvantara-avatāras], incarnations in different millenniums [yuga-avatāras] and incarnations of empowered living entities [śaktyāveśa-avatāras].
text:
> guṇāvatāra, āra manvantarāvatāra
> yugāvatāra, āra śaktyāveśāvatāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the incarnations to control the material qualities; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also; [[synonyms:m:manu]]-[[synonyms:a:antara]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the incarnations of the Manus; [[synonyms:y:yuga]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the incarnations according to different yugas; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---empowered incarnations.
translation: "There are incarnations that control the material qualities [guṇa-avatāras], incarnations of the Manus [manvantara-avatāras], incarnations in different millenniums [yuga-avatāras] and incarnations of empowered living entities [śaktyāveśa-avatāras].
purport:
The //guṇa-avatāras// are three-Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and Lord Viṣṇu (//Bhāg.// 10.88.3). The //avatāras// of Manu, or //manvantara-avatāras,// are listed as follows in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (8.1.5,13): (1) Yajña, (2) Vibhu, (3) Satyasena, (4) Hari, (5) Vaikuṇṭha, (6) Ajita, (7) Vāmana, (8) Sārvabhauma, (9) Ṛṣabha, (10) Viṣvaksena, (11) Dharmasetu, (12) Sudhāmā, (13) Yogeśvara and (14) Bṛhadbhānu. Altogether these are fourteen in number, and of these, both Yajña and Vāmana are also counted among the //līlā-avatāras.// All these Manu incarnations are sometimes called //vaibhava-avatāras.//

The four //yuga-avatāras// are (1) //śukla// (white) in the Satya-yuga (//Bhāg.// 11.5.21), (2) //rakta// (red) in the Tretā-yuga (//Bhāg.// 11.5.24), (3) //śyāma// (dark blue) in the Dvāpara-yuga (//Bhāg.// 11.5.27), and (4) generally //kṛṣṇa// (black) but in special cases //pīta// (yellow) as Caitanya Mahāprabhu in the Kali-yuga, (//Bhāg.// 11.5.32 and 10.8.13).

The //śaktyāveśa-avatāra// is categorized into (1) forms of divine absorption (//bhagavad-āveśa//) like Kapiladeva or Ṛṣabhadeva and (2) divinely empowered forms (//śaktyāveśa),// of whom there are seven: (1) Śeṣa Nāga in the Vaikuṇṭha world, empowered for the personal service of the Supreme Lord (//sva-sevana-śakti),// (2) Anantadeva, empowered to bear all the planets within the universe (//bhū-dhāraṇa-śakti),// (3) Lord Brahmā, empowered with the energy to create the cosmic manifestation (//sṛṣṭi-śakti),// (4) Catuḥsana, or the Kumāras, specifically empowered to distribute transcendental knowledge (//jñāna-śakti),// (5) Nārada Muni, empowered to distribute devotional service (//bhakti-śakti),// (6) Mahārāja Pṛthu, specifically empowered to rule and maintain the living entities (//pālana-śakti//) and (7) Paraśurāma, specifically empowered to cut down rogues and demons (//duṣṭa-damana-śakti).//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.247
description: "Childhood and boyhood are the typical ages of the Deity. Kṛṣṇa, the son of Mahārāja Nanda, performed His pastimes as a child and as a boy.
text:
> bālya, paugaṇḍa haya vigrahera dharma
> eta-rūpe līlā karena vrajendra-nandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bālya]]---childhood; [[synonyms:p:paugaṇḍa]]---boyhood; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:v:vigrahera]]---of the Deity; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---characteristics; [[synonyms:e:eta]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in so many forms; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---executes; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja.
translation: "Childhood and boyhood are the typical ages of the Deity. Kṛṣṇa, the son of Mahārāja Nanda, performed His pastimes as a child and as a boy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.248
description: "There are innumerable incarnations of Kṛṣṇa, and there is no possibility of counting them. We can simply indicate them by giving the example of the moon and the branches of a tree.
text:
> ananta avatāra kṛṣṇera, nāhika gaṇana
> śākhā-candra-nyāya kari dig-daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---there is no possibility of counting; [[synonyms:ś:śākhā]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]-[[synonyms:n:nyāya]]---by the analogy of the moon and the branches of a tree; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I make; [[synonyms:d:dik]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---a slight indication.
translation: "There are innumerable incarnations of Kṛṣṇa, and there is no possibility of counting them. We can simply indicate them by giving the example of the moon and the branches of a tree.
purport:
Although the moon appears to be located in the branches of a tree, it is actually situated very far away. Similarly, none of the //avatāras,// or incarnations, of Lord Kṛṣṇa are within this material world, but they are visible by the causeless mercy of the Lord. We should not consider them to belong to this material world. As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā://

> avajānanti māṁ mūḍhā
> mānuṣīṁ tanum āśritam
> paraṁ bhāvam ajānanto
> mama bhūta-maheśvaram

"Fools deride Me when I descend in the human form. They do not know My transcendental nature and My supreme dominion over all that be." [[books:bg:9:11|(Bg. 9.11)]]

//Avatāras// descend of their own free will, and although they may act like ordinary human beings, they do not belong to this material world. Lord Kṛṣṇa and His //avatāras// can be understood only by the grace of the Lord.

> nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo
> na medhayā na bahunā śrutena
> yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas
> tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṁ svām
> (//Kaṭha Upaniṣad// 1.2.23)
>
> athāpi te deva padāmbuja-dvaya-
> prasāda-leśānugṛhīta eva hi
> jānāti tattvaṁ bhagavan-mahimno
> na cānya eko 'pi ciraṁ vicinvan
> (//Bhāg.// 10.14.29)

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.249
description: " 'O learned brāhmaṇas, just as hundreds and thousands of small ponds issue from great reservoirs of water, innumerable incarnations flow from Śrī Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the reservoir of all power.'
text:
> avatārā hy asaṅkhyeyā
> hareḥ sattva-nidher dvijāḥ
> yathā 'vidāsinaḥ kulyāḥ
> sarasaḥ syuḥ sahasraśaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:avatārāḥ]]---all the incarnations; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:asaṅkhyeyāḥ]]---beyond counting; [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]]---from the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:sattva]]-[[synonyms:n:nidheḥ]]---who is the reservoir of spiritual energy; [[synonyms:d:dvijāḥ]]---O brāhmaṇas; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:a:avidāsinaḥ]]---containing a great reservoir of water; [[synonyms:k:kulyāḥ]]---small ponds; [[synonyms:s:sarasaḥ]]---from a lake; [[synonyms:s:syuḥ]]---must be; [[synonyms:s:sahasraśaḥ]]---by hundreds and thousands of times.
translation: “ 'O learned brāhmaṇas, just as hundreds and thousands of small ponds issue from great reservoirs of water, innumerable incarnations flow from Śrī Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the reservoir of all power.'
purport: This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:3:26|(1.3.26)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.25
description: Hearing this, Sanātana Gosvāmī chastised his servant, saying, "Why have you brought this death knell with you?"
text:
> śuni' sanātana tāre karilā bhartsana
> 'saṅge kene āniyācha ei kāla-yama?'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---him; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:b:bhartsana]]---chastised; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with you; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:ā:āniyācha]]---have you brought; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]-[[synonyms:y:yama]]---death knell.
translation: Hearing this, Sanātana Gosvāmī chastised his servant, saying, "Why have you brought this death knell with you?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.250
description: "In the beginning, Kṛṣṇa incarnates Himself as puruṣa-avatāras, or Viṣṇu incarnations. These are of three types.
text:
> prathamei kare kṛṣṇa 'puruṣāvatāra'
> seita puruṣa haya trividha prakāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prathamei]]---in the beginning; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the incarnation of the three Viṣṇus (Mahā-Viṣṇu, Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu); [[synonyms:s:seita]]---that; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]---Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:p:pra]]-[[synonyms:k:kāra]]---three different manifestations.
translation: "In the beginning, Kṛṣṇa incarnates Himself as puruṣa-avatāras, or Viṣṇu incarnations. These are of three types.
purport: Up to this verse, the many types of expansions have been described. Now the manifestations of the Lord's different potencies will be described.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.251
description: " 'Viṣṇu has three forms called puruṣas. The first, Mahā-Viṣṇu, is the creator of the total material energy [mahat], the second is Garbhodakaśāyī, who is situated within each universe, and the third is Kṣīrodakaśāyī, who lives in the heart of every living being. He who knows these three becomes liberated from the clutches of māyā.'
text:
> viṣṇos tu trīṇi rūpāṇi
> puruṣākhyāny atho viduḥ
> ekaṁ tu mahataḥ sraṣṭṛ
> dvitīyaṁ tv aṇḍa-saṁsthitam
> tṛtīyaṁ sarva-bhūta-sthaṁ
> tāni jñātvā vimucyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viṣṇoḥ]]---of Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---certainly; [[synonyms:t:trīṇi]]---three; [[synonyms:r:rūpāṇi]]---forms; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākhyāni]]---celebrated as the puruṣa; [[synonyms:a:atho]]---how; [[synonyms:v:viduḥ]]---they know; [[synonyms:e:ekam]]---one of them; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:m:mahataḥ]] [[synonyms:s:sraṣṭṛ]]---the creator of the total material energy; [[synonyms:d:dvitīyam]]---the second; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:a:aṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṁsthitam]]---situated within the universe; [[synonyms:t:tṛtīyam]]---the third; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūta]]-[[synonyms:s:stham]]---within the hearts of all living entities; [[synonyms:t:tāni]]---these three; [[synonyms:j:jñātvā]]---knowing; [[synonyms:v:vimucyate]]---one becomes liberated.
translation: “ 'Viṣṇu has three forms called puruṣas. The first, Mahā-Viṣṇu, is the creator of the total material energy [mahat], the second is Garbhodakaśāyī, who is situated within each universe, and the third is Kṣīrodakaśāyī, who lives in the heart of every living being. He who knows these three becomes liberated from the clutches of māyā.'
purport: This verse appears in the //Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta// (//Pūrva-khaṇḍa// 33), where it has been quoted from the //Sātvata-tantra.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.252
description: "Kṛṣṇa has unlimited potencies, out of which three are chief-willpower, the power of knowledge and the creative energy.
text:
> ananta-śakti-madhye kṛṣṇera tina śakti pradhāna
> 'icchā-śakti' 'jñāna-śakti' 'kriyā-śakti' nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---of unlimited potencies; [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in the midst; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---potencies; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---are chief; [[synonyms:i:icchā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---willpower; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---the power of knowledge; [[synonyms:k:kriyā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---the creative energy; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa has unlimited potencies, out of which three are chief-willpower, the power of knowledge and the creative energy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.253
description: "The predominator of the willing potency is Lord Kṛṣṇa, for by His supreme will everything comes into existence. In willing, there is a need for knowledge, and that knowledge is expressed through Vāsudeva.
text:
> icchā-śakti-pradhāna kṛṣṇa---icchāya sarva-kartā
> jñāna-śakti-pradhāna vāsudeva adhiṣṭhātā
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:icchā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---of willpower; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---predominator; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:i:icchāya]]---simply by willing; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kartā]]---the creator of everything; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---the predominator of the power of knowledge; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]---Lord Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:a:adhiṣṭhātā]]---reservoir.
translation: "The predominator of the willing potency is Lord Kṛṣṇa, for by His supreme will everything comes into existence. In willing, there is a need for knowledge, and that knowledge is expressed through Vāsudeva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.254
description: "There is no possibility of creation without thinking, feeling, willing, knowledge and activity. The combination of the supreme will, knowledge and action brings about the cosmic manifestation.
text:
> icchā-jñāna-kriyā vinā nā haya sṛjana
> tinera tina-śakti meli' prapañca-racana
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:icchā]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]-[[synonyms:k:kriyā]]---thinking, feeling, willing, knowledge and activity; [[synonyms:v:vina]]---without; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sṛjana]]---creation; [[synonyms:t:tinera]]---of the three; [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---three potencies; [[synonyms:m:meli']]---being amalgamated; [[synonyms:p:prapañca]]-[[synonyms:r:racana]]---there is the cosmic manifestation.
translation: "There is no possibility of creation without thinking, feeling, willing, knowledge and activity. The combination of the supreme will, knowledge and action brings about the cosmic manifestation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.255
description: "Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa is Lord Balarāma. Being the predominator of the creative energy, He creates both the material and spiritual worlds.
text:
> kriyā-śakti-pradhāna saṅkarṣaṇa balarāma
> prākṛtāprākṛta-sṛṣṭi karena nirmāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kriyā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---the predominator of the creative energy; [[synonyms:s:saṅkarṣaṇa]]---Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa; [[synonyms:b:balarāma]]---Lord Balarāma; [[synonyms:p:prākṛta]]---material; [[synonyms:a:aprākṛta]]---spiritual; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]---worlds; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:n:nirmāṇa]]---creation.
translation: "Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa is Lord Balarāma. Being the predominator of the creative energy, He creates both the material and spiritual worlds.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.256
description: "That original Saṅkarṣaṇa [Lord Balarāma] is the cause of both the material and spiritual creation. He is the predominating deity of egotism, and by the will of Kṛṣṇa and the power of the spiritual energy, He creates the spiritual world, which consists of the planet Goloka Vṛndāvana and the Vaikuṇṭha planets.
text:
> ahaṅkārera adhiṣṭhātā kṛṣṇera icchāya
> goloka, vaikuṇṭha sṛje cic-chakti-dvārāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ahaṅkārera]]---of egotism; [[synonyms:a:adhiṣṭhātā]]---the source or predominating Deity; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:i:icchāya]]---by the will; [[synonyms:g:goloka]]---the supreme spiritual planet, known as Goloka; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]]---other, lower planets, known as Vaikuṇṭhas; [[synonyms:s:sṛje]]---creates; [[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:d:dvārāya]]---by the spiritual energy.
translation: "That original Saṅkarṣaṇa [Lord Balarāma] is the cause of both the material and spiritual creation. He is the predominating deity of egotism, and by the will of Kṛṣṇa and the power of the spiritual energy, He creates the spiritual world, which consists of the planet Goloka Vṛndāvana and the Vaikuṇṭha planets.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.257
description: "Although there is no question of creation as far as the spiritual world is concerned, the spiritual world is nonetheless manifest by the supreme will of Saṅkarṣaṇa. The spiritual world is the abode of the pastimes of the eternal spiritual energy.
text:
> yadyapi asṛjya nitya cic-chakti-vilāsa
> tathāpi saṅkarṣaṇa-icchāya tāhāra prakāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:a:asṛjya]]---there is no question of creation; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---eternal; [[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---pastimes of the eternal spiritual energy; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:s:saṅkarṣaṇa]]-[[synonyms:i:icchāya]]---by the will of Saṅkarṣaṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---of the spiritual world; [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---manifestation.
translation: "Although there is no question of creation as far as the spiritual world is concerned, the spiritual world is nonetheless manifest by the supreme will of Saṅkarṣaṇa. The spiritual world is the abode of the pastimes of the eternal spiritual energy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.258
description: " 'Gokula, the supreme abode and planet, appears like a lotus flower that has a thousand petals. The whorl of that lotus is the abode of the Supreme Lord, Kṛṣṇa. This lotus-shaped supreme abode is created by the will of Lord Ananta.'
text:
> sahasra-patraṁ kamalaṁ
> gokulākhyaṁ mahat-padam
> tat-karṇikāraṁ tad-dhāma
> tad anantāṁśa-sambhavam
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]-[[synonyms:p:patram]]---with thousands of petals; [[synonyms:k:kamalam]]---resembling a lotus flower; [[synonyms:g:gokula]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākhyam]]---named Gokula; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:p:padam]]---the supreme abode; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:k:karṇikāram]]---the whorl of that lotus flower; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---the abode of the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---from the expansion of energy of Ananta; [[synonyms:s:sambhavam]]---creation.
translation: “ 'Gokula, the supreme abode and planet, appears like a lotus flower that has a thousand petals. The whorl of that lotus is the abode of the Supreme Lord, Kṛṣṇa. This lotus-shaped supreme abode is created by the will of Lord Ananta.'
purport: This verse is quoted from //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.2).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.259
description: "By the agency of the material energy, this same Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa creates all the universes. The dull material energy-known in modern language as nature-is not the cause of the material universe.
text:
> māyā-dvāre sṛje teṅho brahmāṇḍera gaṇa
> jaḍa-rūpā prakṛti nahe brahmāṇḍa-kāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---by the agency of the external energy; [[synonyms:s:sṛje]]---creates; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍera]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the groups of universes; [[synonyms:j:jaḍa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpā]]---appearing dull; [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]]---the material energy; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---is not; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause of the cosmic manifestation.
translation: "By the agency of the material energy, this same Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa creates all the universes. The dull material energy-known in modern language as nature-is not the cause of the material universe.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.26
description: Thereupon, Sanātana Gosvāmī took the seven gold coins in his hands and went to the landlord. Holding the gold coins before him, he spoke as follows.
text:
> tabe sei sāta mohara hastete kariyā
> bhūñāra kāche yāñā kahe mohara dhariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:sāta]] [[synonyms:m:mohara]]---these seven golden coins; [[synonyms:h:hastete]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---taking in the hands; [[synonyms:b:bhūñāra]] [[synonyms:k:kāche]]---to the landlord; [[synonyms:y:yāñā]]---going; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:m:mohara]] [[synonyms:d:dhariyā]]---holding the golden coins.
translation: Thereupon, Sanātana Gosvāmī took the seven gold coins in his hands and went to the landlord. Holding the gold coins before him, he spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.260
description: "Without the Supreme Personality of Godhead's energy, dull matter cannot create the cosmic manifestation. Its power does not arise from the material energy itself but is endowed by Saṅkarṣaṇa.
text:
> jaḍa haite sṛṣṭi nahe īśvara-śakti vine
> tāhātei saṅkarṣaṇa kare śaktira ādhāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaḍa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the dull material energy; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---the cosmic manifestation is not possible; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]] [[synonyms:v:vine]]---without the help of the energy of the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tāhātei]]---in the material energy; [[synonyms:s:saṅkarṣaṇa]]---Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ś:śaktira]]---of the spiritual energy; [[synonyms:ā:ādhāne]]---empowering.
translation: "Without the Supreme Personality of Godhead's energy, dull matter cannot create the cosmic manifestation. Its power does not arise from the material energy itself but is endowed by Saṅkarṣaṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.261
description: "Dull matter alone cannot create anything. The material energy produces the creation by the power of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Iron itself has no power to burn, but when iron is placed in fire, it is empowered to burn.
text:
> īśvarera śaktye sṛṣṭi karaye prakṛti
> lauha yena agni-śaktye pāya dāha-śakti
synonyms: [[synonyms:ī:īśvarera]] [[synonyms:ś:śaktye]]---by the energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]---creation; [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:y:ye]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]]---material energy; [[synonyms:l:lauha]]---iron; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as; [[synonyms:a:agni]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaktye]]---by the power of fire; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:d:dāha]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---the power to burn.
translation: "Dull matter alone cannot create anything. The material energy produces the creation by the power of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Iron itself has no power to burn, but when iron is placed in fire, it is empowered to burn.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.262
description: " 'Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa are the original efficient and material causes of the material world. As Mahā-Viṣṇu and the material energy, They enter into the material elements and create the diversities by multi-energies. Thus They are the cause of all causes.'
text:
> etau hi viśvasya ca bīja-yonī
> rāmo mukundaḥ puruṣaḥ pradhānam
> anvīya bhūteṣu vilakṣaṇasya
> jñānasya ceśāta imau purāṇau
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:etau]]---these two, namely Rāma and Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:v:viśvasya]]---of the universe; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:b:bīja]]-[[synonyms:y:yonī]]---both the cause and ingredient; [[synonyms:r:rāmaḥ]]---Balarāma; [[synonyms:m:mukundaḥ]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:puruṣaḥ]]---the original Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:p:pradhānam]]---material energy; [[synonyms:a:anvīya]]---after entering; [[synonyms:b:bhūteṣu]]---into the material elements; [[synonyms:v:vilakṣaṇasya]]---of varieties of manifestation; [[synonyms:j:jñānasya]]---of knowledge; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:ī:īśāte]]---are the controlling power; [[synonyms:i:imau]]---both of Them; [[synonyms:p:purāṇau]]---are the original cause.
translation: “ 'Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa are the original efficient and material causes of the material world. As Mahā-Viṣṇu and the material energy, They enter into the material elements and create the diversities by multi-energies. Thus They are the cause of all causes.'
purport: This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.46.31).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.263
description: "The form of the Lord that descends into the material world to create is called an avatāra, or incarnation.
text:
> sṛṣṭi-hetu yei mūrti prapañce avatare
> sei īśvara-mūrti 'avatāra' nāma dhare
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]-[[synonyms:h:hetu]]---for the purpose of creation; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---which form of the Lord; [[synonyms:p:prapañce]]---in the material world; [[synonyms:a:avatare]]---descends; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---form of the Lord; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnation; [[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:d:dhare]]---takes the name.
translation: "The form of the Lord that descends into the material world to create is called an avatāra, or incarnation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.264
description: "All the expansions of Lord Kṛṣṇa are actually residents of the spiritual world. However, when they descend into the material world, they are called incarnations [avatāras].
text:
> māyātīta paravyome sabāra avasthāna
> viśve avatari' dhare 'avatāra' nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:a:atīta]]---beyond the material nature; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:v:vyome]]---in the spiritual sky; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---all of them; [[synonyms:a:avasthāna]]---residence; [[synonyms:v:viśve]]---within the material universe; [[synonyms:a:avatari']]---coming down; [[synonyms:d:dhare]]---take; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name avatāra.
translation: "All the expansions of Lord Kṛṣṇa are actually residents of the spiritual world. However, when they descend into the material world, they are called incarnations [avatāras].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.265
description: "To glance over that material energy and empower her, Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa first incarnates as Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu.
text:
> sei māyā avalokite śrī-saṅkarṣaṇa
> puruṣa-rūpe avatīrṇa ha-ilā prathama
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---that material energy; [[synonyms:a:avalokite]]---just to glance over; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkarṣaṇa]]---Saṅkarṣaṇa; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in the original form of Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:a:avatīrṇa]]---incarnated; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:p:prathama]]---at first.
translation: "To glance over that material energy and empower her, Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa first incarnates as Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.266
description: " 'In the beginning of the creation, the Lord expanded Himself in the form of the puruṣa incarnation, accompanied by all the ingredients of material creation. First He created the sixteen principal energies suitable for creation. This was for the purpose of manifesting the material universes.'
text:
> jagṛhe pauruṣaṁ rūpaṁ
> bhagavān mahad-ādibhiḥ
> sambhūtaṁ ṣoḍaśa-kalam
> ādau loka-sisṛkṣayā
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagṛhe]]---accepted; [[synonyms:p:pauruṣam]] [[synonyms:r:rūpam]]---the form of the puruṣa incarnation; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādibhiḥ]]---with the material energy, etc.; [[synonyms:s:sambhūtam]]---created; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣoḍaśa]]---sixteen; [[synonyms:k:kalam]]---elements; [[synonyms:ā:ādau]]---in the beginning; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---of the material worlds; [[synonyms:s:sisṛkṣayā]]---with a desire for the creation.
translation: “ 'In the beginning of the creation, the Lord expanded Himself in the form of the puruṣa incarnation, accompanied by all the ingredients of material creation. First He created the sixteen principal energies suitable for creation. This was for the purpose of manifesting the material universes.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:3:1|(1.3.1)]]. For an explanation, refer to //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Five, verse 84.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.267
description: " 'Kāraṇābdhiśāyī Viṣṇu [Mahā-Viṣṇu] is the first incarnation of the Supreme Lord, and He is the master of eternal time, space, cause and effects, mind, elements, material ego, modes of nature, senses, the universal form of the Lord, Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, and the sum total of all living beings, both moving and nonmoving.'
text:
> ādyo 'vatāraḥ puruṣaḥ parasya
> kālaḥ svabhāvaḥ sad-asan-manaś ca
> dravyaṁ vikāro guṇa indriyāṇi
> virāṭ svarāṭ sthāsnu cariṣṇu bhūmnaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ādyaḥ]] [[synonyms:a:avatāraḥ]]---the original incarnation; [[synonyms:p:puruṣaḥ]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:p:parasya]]---of the Supreme; [[synonyms:k:kālaḥ]]---time; [[synonyms:s:svabhāvaḥ]]---nature; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:a:asat]]---cause and effect; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---as well as the mind; [[synonyms:d:dravyam]]---the five elements; [[synonyms:v:vikāraḥ]]---transformation or the false ego; [[synonyms:g:guṇaḥ]]---modes of nature; [[synonyms:i:indriyāṇi]]---senses; [[synonyms:v:virāṭ]]---the universal form; [[synonyms:s:svarāṭ]]---complete independence; [[synonyms:s:sthāsnu]]---immovable; [[synonyms:c:cariṣṇu]]---movable; [[synonyms:b:bhūmnaḥ]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'Kāraṇābdhiśāyī Viṣṇu [Mahā-Viṣṇu] is the first incarnation of the Supreme Lord, and He is the master of eternal time, space, cause and effects, mind, elements, material ego, modes of nature, senses, the universal form of the Lord, Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, and the sum total of all living beings, both moving and nonmoving.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:6:42|(2.6.42)]]. For an explanation, refer to //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Five, verse 83.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.268
description: "That original Personality of Godhead, named Saṅkarṣaṇa, first lies down in the river Virajā, which serves as a border between the material and spiritual worlds. As Kāraṇābdhiśāyī Viṣṇu, He is the original cause of the material creation.
text:
> sei puruṣa virajāte karena śayana
> 'kāraṇābdhiśāyī' nāma jagat-kāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:v:virajāte]]---on the border known as Virajā; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:ś:śayana]]---lies down; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:abdhi]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāyī]]---Kāraṇābdhiśāyī; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---is the original cause of material creation.
translation: "That original Personality of Godhead, named Saṅkarṣaṇa, first lies down in the river Virajā, which serves as a border between the material and spiritual worlds. As Kāraṇābdhiśāyī Viṣṇu, He is the original cause of the material creation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.269
description: "The Virajā, or Causal Ocean, is the border between the spiritual and material worlds. The material energy is situated on one shore of that ocean, and it cannot enter onto the other shore, which is the spiritual sky.
text:
> kāraṇābdhi-pāre māyāra nitya avasthiti
> virajāra pāre paravyome nāhi gati
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:abdhi]]-[[synonyms:p:pāre]]---on one bank of the Causal Ocean; [[synonyms:m:māyāra]]---of the material energy; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---eternal; [[synonyms:a:avasthiti]]---position; [[synonyms:v:virajāra]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---on the other bank of the Virajā, or the Causal Ocean; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:v:vyome]]---in the spiritual world or sky; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:g:gati]]---admission.
translation: "The Virajā, or Causal Ocean, is the border between the spiritual and material worlds. The material energy is situated on one shore of that ocean, and it cannot enter onto the other shore, which is the spiritual sky.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.27
description: "I have these seven gold coins with me. Please accept them, and from a religious point of view please get me across that hilly tract of land.
text:
> "ei sāta suvarṇa mohara āchila āmāra
> ihā lañā dharma dekhi' parvata kara pāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:sāta]]---these seven; [[synonyms:s:suvarṇa]] [[synonyms:m:mohara]]---golden coins; [[synonyms:ā:āchila]]---were; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---mine; [[synonyms:i:ihā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---accepting them; [[synonyms:d:dharma]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---observing religious principles; [[synonyms:p:parvata]]---the hilly tract of land; [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:p:pāra]]---kindly get me across.
translation: "I have these seven gold coins with me. Please accept them, and from a religious point of view please get me across that hilly tract of land.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.270
description: " 'In the spiritual world, there is neither the mode of passion, the mode of ignorance nor a mixture of both, nor is there adulterated goodness, nor the influence of time or māyā itself. Only the pure devotees of the Lord, who are worshiped both by demigods and by demons, reside in the spiritual world as the Lord's associates.'
text:
> pravartate yatra rajas tamas tayoḥ
> sattvaṁ ca miśraṁ na ca kāla-vikramaḥ
> na yatra māyā kim utāpare harer
> anuvratā yatra surāsurārcitāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pravartate]]---exists; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---where; [[synonyms:r:rajaḥ]]---the mode of passion; [[synonyms:t:tamaḥ]]---the mode of ignorance; [[synonyms:t:tayoḥ]]---of both of them; [[synonyms:s:sattvam]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and the mode of goodness; [[synonyms:m:miśram]]---mixture; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]-[[synonyms:v:vikramaḥ]]---the influence of time or annihilation; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---where; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---external energy; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what; [[synonyms:u:uta]]---to speak; [[synonyms:a:apare]]---others; [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:anuvratāḥ]]---strict followers; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---where; [[synonyms:s:sura]]---by demigods; [[synonyms:a:asura]]---and by demons; [[synonyms:a:arcitāḥ]]---being worshiped.
translation: “ 'In the spiritual world, there is neither the mode of passion, the mode of ignorance nor a mixture of both, nor is there adulterated goodness, nor the influence of time or māyā itself. Only the pure devotees of the Lord, who are worshiped both by demigods and by demons, reside in the spiritual world as the Lord's associates.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:9:10|(2.9.10)]] was spoken by Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī. He was answering the questions of Parīkṣit Mahārāja, who asked how the living entity falls down into the material world. Śukadeva Gosvāmī explained the cream of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// in four verses, which had been explained to Lord Brahmā at the end of the severe austerities he performed for one thousand celestial years. At that time, Brahmā was shown the spiritual world and its transcendental nature.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.271
description: "Māyā has two functions. One is called māyā, and the other is called pradhāna. Māyā refers to the efficient cause, and pradhāna refers to the ingredients that create the cosmic manifestation.
text:
> māyāra ye dui vṛtti---'māyā' āra 'pradhāna'
> 'māyā' nimitta-hetu, viśvera upādāna 'pradhāna'
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māyāra]]---of the material nature; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:v:vṛtti]]---functions; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---called māyā; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---ingredients; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---the word ma-ya; [[synonyms:n:nimitta]]-[[synonyms:h:hetu]]---the efficient cause; [[synonyms:v:viśvera]]---of the material universe; [[synonyms:u:upādāna]]---ingredients; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---is called pradhāna.
translation: "Māyā has two functions. One is called māyā, and the other is called pradhāna. Māyā refers to the efficient cause, and pradhāna refers to the ingredients that create the cosmic manifestation.
purport: For a further explanation, see //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Five, verse 58.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.272
description: "When the Supreme Personality of Godhead glances over the material energy, she becomes agitated. At that time, the Lord injects the original semina of the living entities.
text:
> sei puruṣa māyā-pāne kare avadhāna
> prakṛti kṣobhita kari' kare vīryera ādhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]---that Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:p:pāne]]---toward māyā; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:a:avadhāna]]---glances; [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]]---the material nature; [[synonyms:k:kṣobhita]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making agitated; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---impregnates; [[synonyms:v:vīryera]]---of the semina; [[synonyms:ā:ādhāna]]---injection.
translation: "When the Supreme Personality of Godhead glances over the material energy, she becomes agitated. At that time, the Lord injects the original semina of the living entities.
purport:
In //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:7:10|(Bg. 7.10)]], Kṛṣṇa says, //bījaṁ māṁ sarva-bhūtānām:// "I am the original seed of all existences." This is also confirmed in another verse in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:14:4|(Bg. 14.4)]]:

> sarva-yoniṣu kaunteya
> mūrtayaḥ sambhavanti yāḥ
> tāsāṁ brahma mahad-yonir
> ahaṁ bīja-pradaḥ pitā

"It should be understood that all species of life, O son of Kuntī, are made possible by birth in this material nature, and that I am the seed-giving father."

For a further explanation, one may refer to //Brahma-saṁhitā// (Chapter Five, verses 10-13). //Brahma-saṁhitā// also states (5.51):

> agnir mahī gaganam ambu marud diśaś ca
> kālas tathātma-manasīti jagat-trayāṇi
> yasmād bhavanti vibhavanti viśanti yaṁ ca
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi

All material elements, as well as the spiritual sparks (individual souls), are emanating from the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is also confirmed by the //Vedānta-sūtra// (1.1). //janmādy asya yataḥ:// "The Absolute Truth is He from whom everything emanates." He is the Supreme Truth: //satyaṁ paraṁ dhīmahi// [[books:sb:1:1:1|(Bhāg. 1.1.1)]]. The absolute ultimate truth is Kṛṣṇa. //Oṁ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya janmādy asya yato 'nvayād itarataś cārtheṣv abhijñaḥ sva-rāṭ:// "The Absolute Truth is a person who is directly and indirectly cognizant of the entire cosmic manifestation." [[books:sb:1:1:1|(Bhāg. 1.1.1)]]

The Absolute Truth, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, educated Lord Brahmā from the heart [[books:sb:1:1:1|(Bhāg. 1.1.1)]]: //tene brahma hṛdā ya ādi-kavaye.// Therefore the Absolute Truth cannot be dull matter; the Absolute Truth must be the Supreme Person Himself. //Sei puruṣa māyā-pāne kare avadhāna.// Simply by His glance, material nature is impregnated with all living entities. According to their //karma// and fruitive activity, they emerge in different bodies. That is the explanation given by //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:2:13|(Bg. 2.13)]]:

> dehino 'smin yathā dehe
> kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā
> tathā dehāntara-prāptir
> dhīras tatra na muhyati

"As the embodied soul continually passes, in this body, from boyhood to youth to old age, the soul similarly passes into another body at death. The self-realized soul is not bewildered by such a change."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.273
description: "To impregnate with the seeds of living entities, the Lord Himself does not directly touch the material energy, but by His specific functional expansion, He touches the material energy, and thus the living entities, who are His parts and parcels, are impregnated into material nature.
text:
> svāṅga-viśeṣābhāsa-rūpe prakṛti-sparśana
> jīva-rūpa 'bīja' tāte kailā samarpaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:v:viśeṣa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāsa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in the form of a specific shadow from His personal body; [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]]-[[synonyms:s:sparśana]]---the Lord glances over the material nature; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---having the form of the sparklike living entities, who are parts and parcels; [[synonyms:b:bīja]]---semina; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in that material nature; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:s:samarpaṇa]]---impregnated.
translation: "To impregnate with the seeds of living entities, the Lord Himself does not directly touch the material energy, but by His specific functional expansion, He touches the material energy, and thus the living entities, who are His parts and parcels, are impregnated into material nature.
purport:
According to //Bhagavad-gītā://

> mamaivāṁśo jīva-loke
> jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ
> manaḥ ṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi
> prakṛti-sthāni karṣati

"The living entities in this conditioned world are My eternal, fragmental parts. Due to conditioned life, they are struggling very hard with the six senses, which include the mind." [[books:bg:15:7|(Bg. 15.7)]]

The word //prakṛti-sparśana// is explained in //Caitanya-caritamṛta// in reference to the way the living entities come in contact with dull matter. The glancing is performed by Mahā-Viṣṇu: //sa aikṣata lokān nu sṛjā iti// (//Aitareya Upaniṣad// 1.1.1). In the conditional stage we impregnate according to the bodily conception---that is, by sexual intercourse---but the Supreme Lord does not need sexual intercourse to impregnate. The impregnation is performed simply by His glance. This is also explained in the //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.32):

> aṅgāni yasya sakalendriya-vṛttimanti
> paśyanti pānti kalayanti ciraṁ jaganti
> ānanda-cinmaya-sad-ujjvala-vigrahasya
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi

Govinda can impregnate simply by glancing. In other words, His eyes can work as His genitals. He does not need genitals to beget a child. Indeed, Kṛṣṇa can beget any one of the living entities with any part of His body.

The word //svāṅga-viśeṣābhāsa-rūpe,// the form by which the Lord begets living entities in the material world, is explained herein. He is Lord Śiva. In the //Brahma-saṁhitā// it is stated that Lord Śiva, who is another form of Mahā-Viṣṇu, is like yogurt. Yogurt is nothing but milk, yet it is not milk. Similarly, Lord Śiva is considered the father of this universe, and material nature is considered the mother. The father and mother are known as Lord Śiva and the goddess Durgā. Together, Lord Śiva's genitals and the vagina of goddess Durgā are worshiped as //śiva-liṅga.// This is the origin of the material creation. Thus Lord Śiva's position is between the living entity and the Supreme Lord. Lord Śiva is neither the Supreme Personality of Godhead nor the living entity. He is the form through which the Supreme Lord works to beget living entities within this material world. As yogurt is prepared when milk is mixed with a culture, the form of Lord Śiva expands when the Supreme Personality of Godhead is in touch with material nature. The impregnation of material nature by the father, Lord Śiva, is wonderful because at one time innumerable living entities are conceived. //Bhāgo jīvaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sa cānantyāya kalpate// (//Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad// 5.9). These living entities are very, very small.

> keśāgra-śata-bhāgasya
> śatāṁśa-sadṛśātmakaḥ
> jīvaḥ sūkṣma-svarūpo 'yam
> saṅkhyātīto hi cit-kaṇaḥ

"If we divide the tip of a hair into a hundred parts and then take one of these parts and divide it again into a hundred parts, that very fine division is the size of but one of the numberless living entities. They are all //cit-kaṇa,// particles of spirit, not matter."

The innumerable //brahmāṇḍas,// or universes, come from the pores of the Lord's body, and innumerable living entities also come from the pores of the transcendental body of the Lord. This is the process of material creation. Without the living entity, this material nature has no value. Both emanate from the pores of the transcendental body of Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu. They are different energies. That is explained in //Bhagavad-gītā://

> bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ
> khaṁ mano buddhir eva ca
> ahaṅkāra itīyaṁ me
> bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā

"Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intelligence and false ego-all together these eight comprise My separated material energies." [[books:bg:7:4|(Bg. 7.4)]] The material elements also come from the body of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and they are also a different type of energy. Although the living entities also come from the Lord's body, they are categorized as a superior energy.

> apareyam itas tv anyāṁ
> prakṛtiṁ viddhi me parām
> jīva-bhūtāṁ mahā-bāho
> yayedaṁ dhāryate jagat

"Besides this inferior nature, O mighty-armed Arjuna, there is a superior energy of Mine, which consists of all living entities who are struggling with material nature and are sustaining the universe." [[books:bg:7:5|(Bg. 7.5)]] The inferior energy, matter, cannot act without the superior energy. All these things are very clearly explained in the //Vedas.// The materialistic theory that life develops from matter is incorrect. Life and matter come from the supreme living entity; therefore, being the source of both, that supreme living entity, Kṛṣṇa, is described in //Vedānta-sūtra// as //janmādy asya yataḥ// (1.1), or the original source of everything, //sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam.// This is further explained in the following verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.274
description: " 'From time immemorial, after agitating the material nature into three qualities, the Supreme Personality of Godhead places the semina of innumerable living entities within the womb of that material nature. Thus material nature gives birth to the total material energy known as the hiraṇmaya-mahat-tattva, the original symbolic representation of the cosmic manifestation.'
text:
> daivāt kṣubhita-dharmiṇyāṁ
> svasyāṁ yonau paraḥ pumān
> ādhatta vīryaṁ sā 'sūta
> mahat-tattvaṁ hiraṇmayam
