synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daivāt]]---from time immemorial; [[synonyms:k:kṣubhita]]-[[synonyms:d:dharmiṇyām]]---the material nature, which is subjected to agitation; [[synonyms:s:svasyām]]---which belongs to the Supreme as one of His energies; [[synonyms:y:yonau]]---in the womb from which the living entity takes his birth; [[synonyms:p:paraḥ]] [[synonyms:p:pumān]]---the Supreme Brahman, the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ā:ādhatta]]---impregnated; [[synonyms:v:vīryam]]---semina; [[synonyms:s:sā]]---that material nature; [[synonyms:a:asūta]]---produced; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:t:tattvam]]---the total material energy; [[synonyms:h:hiraṇmayam]]---the original source for the emanation of varieties of material things.
translation: “ 'From time immemorial, after agitating the material nature into three qualities, the Supreme Personality of Godhead places the semina of innumerable living entities within the womb of that material nature. Thus material nature gives birth to the total material energy known as the hiraṇmaya-mahat-tattva, the original symbolic representation of the cosmic manifestation.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:26:19|(3.26.19)]]. Lord Kapila is explaining to His mother the relationship between the Supreme Personality of Godhead and material nature. He is informing her how the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the original cause of the living entities, who emanated from material nature. Over and above the twenty-eight elements of the material creation is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the cause of all causes. Life comes not from matter but from life itself. As explained in the //Vedas:nityo nityānāṁ cetanaś cetanānām (Kaṭha Upaniṣad// 2.2.13). The Supreme Lord is the original source of life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.275
description: " 'In due course of time, the Supreme Personality of Godhead [Mahā-Viṣṇu or Mahā-Vaikuṇṭhanātha], by the agency of a further expansion of His personal self, places the seed of the living entities within the womb of material nature.'
text:
> kāla-vṛttyā tu māyāyāṁ
> guṇamayyām adhokṣajaḥ
> puruṣeṇātma-bhūtena
> vīryam ādhatta vīryavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāla]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛttyā]]---in due course of time, as the immediate cause of creation; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:m:māyāyām]]---within the material nature; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mayyām]]---full of the three material modes of nature (sattva-guṇa, rajo-guṇa and tamo-guṇa); [[synonyms:a:adhokṣajaḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is beyond material conceptions; [[synonyms:p:puruṣeṇa]]---by the enjoyer of material nature; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūtena]]---who is an expansion of His personal self; [[synonyms:v:vīryam]]---semina; [[synonyms:ā:ādhatta]]---placed; [[synonyms:v:vīryavān]]---the omnipotent.
translation: “ 'In due course of time, the Supreme Personality of Godhead [Mahā-Viṣṇu or Mahā-Vaikuṇṭhanātha], by the agency of a further expansion of His personal self, places the seed of the living entities within the womb of material nature.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:5:26|(3.5.26)]]. This verse tells how the living entities come in contact with material nature. Just as a woman cannot beget children without uniting with a man, material nature cannot beget living entities without being in union with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. There is a history of how the Absolute Lord becomes the father of all living entities. In every system of religion, it is accepted that God is the supreme father of all living entities. According to Christianity, the supreme father, God, provides the living entities with all of life's necessities. Therefore they pray, "Give us this day our daily bread." Any religion that does not accept the Supreme Lord as the absolute father is called //kaitava-dharma,// or a cheating religion. Such religious systems are rejected in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:1:2|(1.1.2)]]: //dharmaḥ projjhita-kaitavo 'tra.// Only an atheist does not accept the omnipotent supreme father. If one accepts the omnipotent supreme father, he abides by His orders and becomes a religious person.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.276
description: "First the total material energy is manifest, and from this arise the three types of egotism, which are the original sources from which all demigods [controlling deities], senses and material elements expand.
text:
> tabe mahat-tattva haite trividha ahaṅkāra
> yāhā haite devatendriya-bhūtera pracāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the total material energy; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]]---three kinds of; [[synonyms:a:ahaṅkāra]]---egotism; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from which; [[synonyms:d:devatā]]---of predominating deities; [[synonyms:i:indriya]]---of the senses; [[synonyms:b:bhūtera]]---and of material elements; [[synonyms:p:pracāra]]---expansion.
translation: "First the total material energy is manifest, and from this arise the three types of egotism, which are the original sources from which all demigods [controlling deities], senses and material elements expand.
purport: The three types of egotism (//ahaṅkāra//) are technically known as //vaikārika, taijasa// and //tāmasa.// The //mahat-tattva// is situated within the heart, or //citta,// and the predominating Deity of the //mahat-tattva// is Lord Vāsudeva [[books:sb:3:26:21|(Bhāg. 3.26.21)]]. The //mahat-tattva// is transformed into three divisions: (1) //vaikārika,// egotism in goodness (//sāttvika-ahaṅkāra//), from which the eleventh sense organ, the mind, is manifest and whose predominating Deity is Aniruddha [[books:sb:3:26:27|(Bhāg. 3.26.27-28)]]; (2) //taijasa,// or egotism in passion (//rājasa-ahaṅkāra//), from which the senses and intelligence are manifest and whose predominating Deity is Lord Pradyumna [[books:sb:3.26.29|(Bhāg. 3.26.29-31)]]; (3) //tāmasa,// or egotism in ignorance, from which sound vibration (//śabda-tanmātra//) expands. From the sound vibration, the sky (//ākāśa//) is manifest and, the senses, beginning with the ear, are also manifest [[books:sb:3:26:32|(Bhāg. 3.26.32)]]. Of these three types of egotism, Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa is the predominating Deity. In the philosophical discourse known as the //Sāṅkhya-kārikā,// it is stated: //sāttvika ekādaśakaḥ pravartate vaikṛtād ahaṅkārāt-bhūtādes tan-mātraṁ tāmasa-taijasādy-ubhayam.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.277
description: "Combining all the different elements, the Supreme Lord created all the universes. Those universes are unlimited in number; there is no possibility of counting them.
text:
> sarva tattva mili' sṛjila brahmāṇḍera gaṇa
> ananta brahmāṇḍa, tāra nāhika gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]] [[synonyms:t:tattva]]---all different elements; [[synonyms:m:mili']]---combining; [[synonyms:s:sṛjila]]---created; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍera]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the universes; [[synonyms:a:ananta]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]---those universes are unlimited in number; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---there is no possibility of counting them.
translation: "Combining all the different elements, the Supreme Lord created all the universes. Those universes are unlimited in number; there is no possibility of counting them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.278
description: "The first form of Lord Viṣṇu is called Mahā-Viṣṇu. He is the original creator of the total material energy. The innumerable universes emanate from the pores of His body.
text:
> iṅho mahat-sraṣṭā puruṣa---'mahā-viṣṇu' nāma
> ananta brahmāṇḍa tāṅra loma-kūpe dhāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:s:sraṣṭā]]---the creator of the mahat-tattva, or total material energy; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]---the person; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---called Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]---universes; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of His body; [[synonyms:l:loma]]-[[synonyms:k:kūpe]]---within the hair holes; [[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---are situated.
translation: "The first form of Lord Viṣṇu is called Mahā-Viṣṇu. He is the original creator of the total material energy. The innumerable universes emanate from the pores of His body.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.279-280
description: "These universes are understood to be floating in air as the Mahā-Viṣṇu exhales. They are like atomic particles that float in sunshine and pass through the holes of a screen. All these universes are thus created by the exhalation of Mahā-Viṣṇu, and when Mahā-Viṣṇu inhales, they return to His body. The unlimited opulences of Mahā-Viṣṇu are completely beyond material conception.
text:
> gavākṣe uḍiyā yaiche reṇu āse yāya
> puruṣa-niśvāsa-saha brahmāṇḍa bāhirāya
>
> punarapi niśvāsa-saha yāya abhyantara
> ananta aiśvarya tāṅra, saba---māyā-pāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gavākṣe]]---from a hole at the top of a wall; [[synonyms:u:uḍiyā]]---floating; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:r:reṇu]]---atomic particles; [[synonyms:ā:āse]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---come and go; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:n:niśvāsa]]-[[synonyms:s:saha]]---with the exhaling of Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]---the universes; [[synonyms:b:bāhirāya]]---come outside; [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:n:niśvāsa]]-[[synonyms:s:saha]]---by His inhalation; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---go; [[synonyms:a:abhyantara]]---within; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---opulences; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Him; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---everything; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:p:pāra]]---beyond the material conception.
translation: "These universes are understood to be floating in air as the Mahā-Viṣṇu exhales. They are like atomic particles that float in sunshine and pass through the holes of a screen. All these universes are thus created by the exhalation of Mahā-Viṣṇu, and when Mahā-Viṣṇu inhales, they return to His body. The unlimited opulences of Mahā-Viṣṇu are completely beyond material conception.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.28
description: "I am a prisoner of the government, and I cannot go along the way of the ramparts. It will be very pious of you to take this money and kindly get me across this hilly tract of land."
text:
> rāja-bandī āmi, gada-dvāra yāite nā pāri
> puṇya habe, parvata āmā deha' pāra kari"
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:b:bandī]]---a prisoner of the government; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:g:gaḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāra]] [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go openly on the road by the ramparts; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---I am not able; [[synonyms:p:puṇya]]---pious activity; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:p:parvata]]---the hilly tract of land; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]---to me; [[synonyms:d:deha']]---give help; [[synonyms:p:pāra]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---by crossing over.
translation: "I am a prisoner of the government, and I cannot go along the way of the ramparts. It will be very pious of you to take this money and kindly get me across this hilly tract of land."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.281
description: " 'The Brahmās and other lords of the mundane worlds appear from the pores of the Mahā-Viṣṇu and remain alive for the duration of His one exhalation. I adore the primeval Lord, Govinda, for Mahā-Viṣṇu is a portion of His plenary portion.'
text:
> yasyaika-niśvasita-kālam athāvalambya
> jīvanti loma-vilajā jagad-aṇḍa-nāthāḥ
> viṣṇur mahān sa iha yasya kalā-viśeṣo
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---whose; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:n:niśvasita]]---of breath; [[synonyms:k:kālam]]---time; [[synonyms:a:atha]]---thus; [[synonyms:a:avalambya]]---taking shelter of; [[synonyms:j:jīvanti]]---live; [[synonyms:l:loma]]-[[synonyms:v:vilajāḥ]]---grown from the hair holes; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:a:aṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāthāḥ]]---the masters of the universes (the Brahmās); [[synonyms:v:viṣṇuḥ]] [[synonyms:m:mahān]]---the Supreme Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---here; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---whose; [[synonyms:k:kalā]]-[[synonyms:v:viśeṣaḥ]]---particular plenary portion or expansion; [[synonyms:g:govindam]]---Lord Govinda; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣam]]---the original person; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---Him; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bhajāmi]]---worship.
translation: “ 'The Brahmās and other lords of the mundane worlds appear from the pores of the Mahā-Viṣṇu and remain alive for the duration of His one exhalation. I adore the primeval Lord, Govinda, for Mahā-Viṣṇu is a portion of His plenary portion.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.48).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.282
description: "Mahā-Viṣṇu is the Supersoul of all the universes. Lying on the Causal Ocean, He is the master of all material worlds.
text:
> samasta brahmāṇḍa-gaṇera iṅho antaryāmī
> kāraṇābdhiśāyī---saba jagatera svāmī
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:samasta]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the aggregate of the brahmāṇḍas, or universes; [[synonyms:i:iṅho]]---that Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:a:antaryāmī]]---the Supersoul; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:abdhi]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāyī]]---Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu, lying on the Causal Ocean; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:j:jagatera]]---of all the universes; [[synonyms:s:svāmī]]---the Supreme Lord.
translation: "Mahā-Viṣṇu is the Supersoul of all the universes. Lying on the Causal Ocean, He is the master of all material worlds.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.283
description: "I have thus explained the truth of the first Personality of Godhead, Mahā Viṣṇu. I shall now explain the glories of the second Personality of Godhead.
text:
> eita kahiluṅ prathama puruṣera tattva
> dvitīya puruṣera ebe śunaha mahattva
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eita]]---thus; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have explained; [[synonyms:p:prathama]] [[synonyms:p:puruṣera]]---of the first incarnation of the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]---the truth; [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]] [[synonyms:p:puruṣera]]---of the second incarnation of the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:ś:śunaha]]---please hear; [[synonyms:m:mahattva]]---glories.
translation: "I have thus explained the truth of the first Personality of Godhead, Mahā Viṣṇu. I shall now explain the glories of the second Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.284
description: "After creating the total number of universes, which are unlimited, the Mahā-Viṣṇu expanded Himself into unlimited forms and entered into each of them.
text:
> sei puruṣa ananta-koṭi brahmāṇḍa sṛjiyā
> ekaika-mūrtye praveśilā bahu mūrti hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]---that Personality of Godhead, Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭi]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]---millions and trillions of brahmāṇḍas, or universes; [[synonyms:s:sṛjiyā]]---after creating; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:e:eka]]---in each one of them; [[synonyms:m:mūrtye]]---in a form; [[synonyms:p:praveśilā]]---entered; [[synonyms:b:bahu]] [[synonyms:m:mūrti]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming many forms.
translation: "After creating the total number of universes, which are unlimited, the Mahā-Viṣṇu expanded Himself into unlimited forms and entered into each of them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.285
description: "When Mahā-Viṣṇu entered each of the limitless universes, He saw that there was darkness all around and that there was no place to stay. He therefore began to consider the situation.
text:
> praveśa kariyā dekhe, saba---andhakāra
> rahite nāhika sthāna, karilā vicāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:praveśa]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---after entering; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---He sees; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:a:andhakāra]]---complete darkness; [[synonyms:r:rahite]]---to remain there; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---there was no place; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---then He considered.
translation: "When Mahā-Viṣṇu entered each of the limitless universes, He saw that there was darkness all around and that there was no place to stay. He therefore began to consider the situation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.286
description: "With the perspiration produced from His own body, the Lord filled half the universe with water. He then lay down on that water on the bed of Lord Śeṣa.
text:
> nijāṅga-sveda-jale brahmāṇḍārdha bharila
> sei jale śeṣa-śayyāya śayana karila
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---from His own personal body; [[synonyms:s:sveda]]-[[synonyms:j:jale]]---by emitting the water of perspiration; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:a:ardha]]---half of the universe; [[synonyms:b:bharila]]---filled; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:j:jale]]---on that water; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śayyāya]]---on the bed of Lord Śeṣa; [[synonyms:ś:śayana]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---lay down.
translation: "With the perspiration produced from His own body, the Lord filled half the universe with water. He then lay down on that water on the bed of Lord Śeṣa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.287
description: "A lotus flower then sprouted from the lotus navel of that Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu. That lotus flower became Lord Brahmā's birthplace.
text:
> tāṅra nābhi-padma haite uṭhila eka padma
> sei padme ha-ila brahmāra janma-sadma
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:n:nābhi]]-[[synonyms:p:padma]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from His lotus navel; [[synonyms:u:uṭhila]]---grew; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:p:padma]]---lotus flower; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:padme]]---on that lotus flower; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:b:brahmāra]]---of Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:j:janma]]-[[synonyms:s:sadma]]---the place of generation.
translation: "A lotus flower then sprouted from the lotus navel of that Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu. That lotus flower became Lord Brahmā's birthplace.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.288
description: "In the stem of that lotus flower the fourteen worlds were generated. Then He became Lord Brahmā and created the entire universe.
text:
> sei padma-nāle ha-ila caudda bhuvana
> teṅho 'brahmā' hañā sṛṣṭi karila sṛjana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:padma]]-[[synonyms:n:nāle]]---within the stem of that lotus; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became manifested; [[synonyms:c:caudda]]---fourteen; [[synonyms:b:bhuvana]]---planetary systems; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---having become; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]---the material creation; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:s:sṛjana]]---created.
translation: "In the stem of that lotus flower the fourteen worlds were generated. Then He became Lord Brahmā and created the entire universe.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.289
description: "In this way, the Supreme Personality of Godhead in His form of Viṣṇu maintains the entire material world. Since He is always beyond the material qualities, the material nature cannot touch Him.
text:
> 'viṣṇu'-rūpa hañā kare jagat pālane
> guṇātīta viṣṇu---sparśa nāhi māyā-sane
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa in His form as Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:j:jagat]] [[synonyms:p:pālane]]---maintenance of the material world; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:atīta]]---beyond the material qualities, transcendental; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:s:sparśa]]---touching; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with māyā, the material energy.
translation: "In this way, the Supreme Personality of Godhead in His form of Viṣṇu maintains the entire material world. Since He is always beyond the material qualities, the material nature cannot touch Him.
purport: The influence of the material energy cannot touch Lord Viṣṇu as she touches Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva. Therefore it is said that Lord Viṣṇu is transcendental to the material qualities. The incarnations of the material qualities-Lord Śiva and Lord Brahmā-are under the jurisdiction of the external energy. Lord Viṣṇu, however, is different. In the //mantras// of the //Ṛg Veda// it is said: //oṁ tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṁ padam (Ṛg Veda-saṁhitā// 1.22.20). The words //paramaṁ padam// indicate that He is transcendental to the material qualities. Because Lord Viṣṇu is not within the jurisdiction of the material qualities, He is always superior to the living entities who are controlled by material energy. This is one of the differences between the Supreme Lord and the living entities. Lord Brahmā is a very powerful living entity, and Lord Śiva is even more powerful. Therefore Lord Śiva is not accepted as a living entity, but at the same time is not considered to be on the level of Lord Viṣṇu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.29
description: Smiling, the landlord said, "Before you offered them, I already knew that there were eight gold coins in your servant's possession.
text:
> bhūñā hāsi' kahe,---"āmi jāniyāchi pahile
> asta mohara haya tomāra sevaka-āṅcale
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhūñā]]---the landlord; [[synonyms:h:hāsi']]---smiling; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:j:jāniyāchi]]---knew; [[synonyms:p:pahile]]---before this; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]] [[synonyms:m:mohara]]---eight golden coins; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:s:sevaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:āṅcale]]---in the pocket of the servant.
translation: Smiling, the landlord said, "Before you offered them, I already knew that there were eight gold coins in your servant's possession.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.290
description: "The Supreme Lord, and His form of Rudra [Lord Śiva], brings about the dissolution of this material creation. In other words, by His will only, there is creation, maintenance and dissolution of the whole cosmic manifestation.
text:
> 'rudra'-rūpa dhari kare jagat saṁhāra
> sṛṣṭi, sthiti, pralaya haya icchāya yāṅhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rudra]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]] [[synonyms:d:dhari]]---accepting the form of Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:j:jagat]] [[synonyms:s:saṁhāra]]---dissolution of the universal creation; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]---creation; [[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---maintenance; [[synonyms:p:pralaya]]---and dissolution; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---take place; [[synonyms:i:icchāya]]---by the will; [[synonyms:y:yāṅhāra]]---of whom.
translation: "The Supreme Lord, and His form of Rudra [Lord Śiva], brings about the dissolution of this material creation. In other words, by His will only, there is creation, maintenance and dissolution of the whole cosmic manifestation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.291
description: "Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva are His three incarnations of the material qualities. Creation, maintenance and destruction respectively are under the charge of these three personalities.
text:
> brahmā, viṣṇu, śiva---tāṅra guṇa-avatāra
> sṛṣṭi-sthiti-pralayera tinera adhikāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations of the material qualities; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]-[[synonyms:s:sthiti]]-[[synonyms:p:pralayera]]---of the three functions, namely creation, maintenance and dissolution; [[synonyms:t:tinera]] [[synonyms:a:adhikāra]]---there is control by the three deities (Lord Brahmā, Lord Viṣṇu and Lord Śiva).
translation: "Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva are His three incarnations of the material qualities. Creation, maintenance and destruction respectively are under the charge of these three personalities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.292
description: "Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, known within the universe as Hiraṇyagarbha and the antaryāmī, or Supersoul, is glorified in the Vedic hymns, beginning with the hymn that starts with the word sahasra-śīrṣā.
text:
> hiraṇyagarbha-antaryāmī---garbhodakaśāyī
> 'sahasra-śīrṣādi' kari' vede yāṅre gāi
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hiraṇyagarbha]]---named Hiraṇyagarbha; [[synonyms:a:antaryāmī]]---the Supersoul; [[synonyms:g:garbha]]-[[synonyms:u:udaka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāyī]]---Lord Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]-[[synonyms:ś:śīrṣā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---by the Vedic hymns beginning with sahasra-śīrṣā (//Ṛg Veda-saṁhitā// 10.90); [[synonyms:v:vede]] [[synonyms:y:yāṅre]] [[synonyms:g:ga]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---unto whom the Vedas pray.
translation: "Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, known within the universe as Hiraṇyagarbha and the antaryāmī, or Supersoul, is glorified in the Vedic hymns, beginning with the hymn that starts with the word sahasra-śīrṣā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.293
description: "This second Personality of Godhead, known as Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, is the master of each and every universe and the shelter of the external energy. Nonetheless, He remains beyond the touch of the external energy.
text:
> ei ta' dvitīya-puruṣa---brahmāṇḍera īśvara
> māyāra 'āśraya' haya, tabu māyā-pāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---in this way; [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]---the second Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍera]] [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the master of the universe; [[synonyms:m:māyāra]]---of the external, material energy; [[synonyms:ā:āśraya]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes the shelter; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:p:pāra]]---is beyond the touch of the material energy.
translation: "This second Personality of Godhead, known as Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, is the master of each and every universe and the shelter of the external energy. Nonetheless, He remains beyond the touch of the external energy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.294
description: "The third expansion of Viṣṇu is the Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, who is the incarnation of the quality of goodness. He is to be counted within the two types of incarnations [puruṣa-avatāras and guṇa-avatāras].
text:
> tṛtīya-puruṣa viṣṇu---'guṇa-avatāra'
> dui avatāra-bhitara gaṇanā tāṅhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tṛtīya]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]---the third Personality; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the incarnation of the material quality of goodness; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]-[[synonyms:b:bhitara]]---within the two incarnations; [[synonyms:g:gaṇanā]]-[[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---He is designated.
translation: "The third expansion of Viṣṇu is the Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, who is the incarnation of the quality of goodness. He is to be counted within the two types of incarnations [puruṣa-avatāras and guṇa-avatāras].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.295
description: "This Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu is the universal form of the Lord and is the Supersoul within every living entity. He is known as Kṣīrodakaśāyī, or the Lord who lies on the ocean of milk. He is the maintainer and master of the universe.
text:
> virāṭ vyaṣṭi-jīvera teṅho antaryāmī
> kṣīrodakaśāyī teṅho---pālana-kartā, svāmī
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:virāṭ]]---the universal form; [[synonyms:v:vyaṣṭi]]-[[synonyms:j:jīvera]]---of all other living entities; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:a:antaryāmī]]---the Supersoul; [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]-[[synonyms:u:udaka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāyī]]---Lord Viṣṇu who lies down in the ocean of milk; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:p:pālana]]-[[synonyms:k:kartā]]---the maintainer; [[synonyms:s:svāmī]]---the master.
translation: "This Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu is the universal form of the Lord and is the Supersoul within every living entity. He is known as Kṣīrodakaśāyī, or the Lord who lies on the ocean of milk. He is the maintainer and master of the universe.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.296
description: "O Sanātana, I have definitively described the three puruṣa-avatāras of Viṣṇu. Now please hear from Me about the pastime incarnations.
text:
> puruṣāvatārera ei kailuṅ nirūpaṇa
> līlāvatāra ebe śuna, sanātana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatārera]]---of all the puruṣa-avatāras; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kailuṅ]] [[synonyms:n:nirūpaṇa]]---I have described; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations for pastimes; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---O Sanātana.
translation: "O Sanātana, I have definitively described the three puruṣa-avatāras of Viṣṇu. Now please hear from Me about the pastime incarnations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.297
description: "No one can count the innumerable pastime incarnations of Lord Kṛṣṇa, but I shall describe the principal ones.
text:
> līlāvatāra kṛṣṇera nā yāya gaṇana
> pradhāna kariyā kahi dig-daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations for pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---are not countable; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---chiefly; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---let me describe; [[synonyms:d:dik]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---by a sample direction.
translation: "No one can count the innumerable pastime incarnations of Lord Kṛṣṇa, but I shall describe the principal ones.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.298
description: "Some of the pastime incarnations are the fish incarnation, the tortoise incarnation, Lord Rāmacandra, Lord Nṛsiṁha, Lord Vāmana, and Lord Varāha. There is no end to them.
text:
> matsya, kūrma, raghunātha, nṛsiṁha, vāmana
> varāhādi---lekhā yāṅra nā yāya gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:matsya]]---the fish incarnation; [[synonyms:k:kūrma]]---the tortoise incarnation; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Lord Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁha]]---the man-lion incarnation; [[synonyms:v:vāmana]]---the dwarf incarnation; [[synonyms:v:varāha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the hog incarnation and others; [[synonyms:l:lekhā]]---describing; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of which incarnations; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---cannot be counted.
translation: "Some of the pastime incarnations are the fish incarnation, the tortoise incarnation, Lord Rāmacandra, Lord Nṛsiṁha, Lord Vāmana, and Lord Varāha. There is no end to them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.299
description: " 'O Lord of the universe, best of the Yadu dynasty, we are offering our prayers unto You mainly to diminish the heavy burden of the universe. Indeed, You diminished this burden formerly by incarnating in the form of a fish, a horse [Hayagrīva], a tortoise, a lion [Lord Nṛsiṁha], a boar [Lord Varāha] and a swan. You also incarnated as Lord Rāmacandra, Paraśurāma and Vāmana the dwarf. You have always protected us demigods and the universe in this way. Now please continue.'
text:
> matsyāśva-kacchapa-nṛsiṁha-varāha-haṁsa-
> rājanya-vipra-vibudheṣu kṛtāvatāraḥ
> tvaṁ pāsi nas tribhuvanaṁ ca tathādhuneśa
> bhāraṁ bhuvo hara yadūttama vandanaṁ te
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:matsya]]---in the forms of a fish; [[synonyms:a:aśva]]---of a horse; [[synonyms:k:kacchapa]]---of a tortoise; [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁha]]---of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva; [[synonyms:v:varāha]]---of a boar; [[synonyms:h:haṁsa]]---of a swan; [[synonyms:r:rājanya]]---of Lord Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---of Lord Paraśurāma; [[synonyms:v:vibudheṣu]]---and of Vāmanadeva; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāraḥ]]---who have accepted incarnation; [[synonyms:t:tvam]]---You; [[synonyms:p:pāsi]]---please protect; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---us demigods; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvanam]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and the three worlds; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---as well; [[synonyms:a:adhunā]]---now; [[synonyms:ī:īśa]]---O Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhāram]]---the burden; [[synonyms:b:bhuvaḥ]]---of the universe; [[synonyms:h:hara]]---kindly take away; [[synonyms:y:yadu]]-[[synonyms:u:uttama]]---O best of the Yadu dynasty; [[synonyms:v:vandanam]] [[synonyms:t:te]]---to You we offer our prayers.
translation: “ 'O Lord of the universe, best of the Yadu dynasty, we are offering our prayers unto You mainly to diminish the heavy burden of the universe. Indeed, You diminished this burden formerly by incarnating in the form of a fish, a horse [Hayagrīva], a tortoise, a lion [Lord Nṛsiṁha], a boar [Lord Varāha] and a swan. You also incarnated as Lord Rāmacandra, Paraśurāma and Vāmana the dwarf. You have always protected us demigods and the universe in this way. Now please continue.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.2.40).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.3
description: While Sanātana Gosvāmī was imprisoned in Bengal, a letter arrived from Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.
text:
> ethā gauḍe sanātana āche bandi-śāle
> śrī-rūpa-gosāñīra patrī āila hena-kāle
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ethā]]---here; [[synonyms:g:gauḍe]]---in Bengal; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---was; [[synonyms:b:bandi]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāle]]---in prison; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñīra]]---of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:patrī]]---the letter; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time.
translation: While Sanātana Gosvāmī was imprisoned in Bengal, a letter arrived from Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura informs us that this letter from Rūpa Gosvāmī to Sanātana Gosvāmī is mentioned by the annotator of //Udbhaṭa-candrikā.// Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī wrote a note to Sanātana Gosvāmī from Bāklā. This note indicated that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was coming to Mathurā, and it stated:

> yadu-pateḥ kva gatā mathurā-purī
> raghu-pateḥ kva gatottara-kośalā
> iti vicintya kurusva manaḥ sthiraṁ
> na sad idaṁ jagad ity avadhāraya

"Where has the Mathurā Purī of Yadupati gone? Where has the northern Kośalā of Raghupati gone? By reflection, make the mind steady, thinking, 'This universe is not eternal.' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.30
description: "On this very night I would have killed you and taken your coins. It is very good that you have voluntarily offered them to me. I am now relieved from such a sinful activity.
text:
> tomā māri' mohara la-itāma ājikāra rātrye
> bhāla haila, kahilā tumi, chuṭilāṅa pāpa haite
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomā]] [[synonyms:m:māri']]---killing you; [[synonyms:m:mohara]]---golden coins; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:itāma]]---I would have taken; [[synonyms:ā:ājikāra]] [[synonyms:r:rātrye]]---on this night; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---it was very good; [[synonyms:k:kahilā]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you have spoken; [[synonyms:c:chuṭilāṅa]]---I am relieved; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from such a sin.
translation: "On this very night I would have killed you and taken your coins. It is very good that you have voluntarily offered them to me. I am now relieved from such a sinful activity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.300
description: "I have given a few examples of pastime incarnations. Now I will describe the guṇa-avatāras, the incarnations of the material qualities. Please listen.
text:
> līlāvatārera kailuṅ dig-daraśana
> guṇāvatārera ebe śuna vivarana
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:a:avatārera]]---of the incarnations of pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kailuṅ]]---I have done; [[synonyms:d:dik]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---indicating the direction only; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatārera]]---of incarnations of the material qualities; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]] [[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---hear the description.
translation: "I have given a few examples of pastime incarnations. Now I will describe the guṇa-avatāras, the incarnations of the material qualities. Please listen.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.301
description: "There are three functions within this material world. Everything here is created, everything is maintained for some time, and everything is finally dissolved. The Lord therefore incarnates Himself as the controllers of the three qualities-sattva-guṇa, rajo-guṇa and tamo-guṇa [goodness, passion and ignorance]. Thus the transactions of the material world take place.
text:
> brahmā, viṣṇu, śiva,---tina guṇa avatāra
> tri-guṇa aṅgīkari' kare sṛṣṭy-ādi-vyavahāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmā,]] [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu,]] [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]---Lord Brahmā, Lord Viṣṇu and Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]] [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the incarnations of the material qualities; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---the three qualities of material nature; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:v:vyavahāra]]---transactions in reference to the creation, maintenance and dissolution.
translation: "There are three functions within this material world. Everything here is created, everything is maintained for some time, and everything is finally dissolved. The Lord therefore incarnates Himself as the controllers of the three qualities-sattva-guṇa, rajo-guṇa and tamo-guṇa [goodness, passion and ignorance]. Thus the transactions of the material world take place.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.302
description: "Because of his past pious activities mixed with devotional service, the first-class living entity is influenced by the mode of passion within his mind.
text:
> bhakti-miśra-kṛta-puṇye kona jīvottama
> rajo-guṇe vibhāvita kari' tāṅra mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:m:miśra]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:p:puṇye]]---because of pious activities mixed with devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---someone; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:u:uttama]]---the best of the living entities; [[synonyms:r:rajaḥ]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---by the mode of passion; [[synonyms:v:vibhāvita]]---influenced; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind.
translation: "Because of his past pious activities mixed with devotional service, the first-class living entity is influenced by the mode of passion within his mind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.303
description: "Such a devotee is empowered by Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu. In this way, an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa in the form of Brahmā engineers the total creation of the universe.
text:
> garbhodakaśāyī-dvārā śakti sañcāri'
> vyaṣṭi sṛṣṭi kare kṛṣṇa brahmā-rūpa dhari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:garbha]]-[[synonyms:u:udaka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāyi]]-[[synonyms:d:dvārā]]---by Lord Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]] [[synonyms:s:sañcāri']]---giving him special powers; [[synonyms:v:vyaṣṭi]]---total; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]---creation; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---accepting the form of Lord Brahmā.
translation: "Such a devotee is empowered by Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu. In this way, an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa in the form of Brahmā engineers the total creation of the universe.
purport: The Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu //puruṣa-avatāra// expansion of Lord Viṣṇu accepts the material modes-//sattva-guṇa, rajo-guṇa// and //tamo-guṇa//-and thus incarnates as Lord Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Śiva. These are incarnations of the material qualities. Among the many superior living entities qualified with pious activities and devotional service, one, called Lord Brahmā, is infused with the quality of passion by the supreme will of Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu. Thus Lord Brahmā becomes the incarnation of the creative energy of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.304
description: " 'The sun manifests his brilliance in a gem, although it is stone. Similarly, the original Personality of Godhead, Govinda, manifests His special power in a pious living entity. Thus the living entity becomes Brahmā and manages the affairs of the universe. Let me worship Govinda, the original Personality of Godhead.'
text:
> bhāsvān yathāśma-sakaleṣu nijeṣu tejaḥ
> svīyaṁ kiyat prakaṭayaty api tadvad atra
> brahmā ya eṣa jagad-aṇḍa-vidhāna-kartā
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāsvān]]---the illuminating sun; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:a:aśma]]-[[synonyms:s:sakaleṣu]]---in various types of precious stones; [[synonyms:n:nijeṣu]]---his own; [[synonyms:t:tejaḥ]]---brilliance; [[synonyms:s:svīyam]]---his own; [[synonyms:k:kiyat]]---to some extent; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭayati]]---manifests; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:t:tadvat]]---similarly; [[synonyms:a:atra]]---here; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who is; [[synonyms:e:eṣaḥ]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:a:aṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:v:vidhāna]]-[[synonyms:k:kartā]]---becomes the chief of the universe; [[synonyms:g:govindam]] [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣam]]---Lord Govinda, the original Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---Him; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bhajāmi]]---worship.
translation: “ 'The sun manifests his brilliance in a gem, although it is stone. Similarly, the original Personality of Godhead, Govinda, manifests His special power in a pious living entity. Thus the living entity becomes Brahmā and manages the affairs of the universe. Let me worship Govinda, the original Personality of Godhead.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.49).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.305
description: "If in a kalpa a suitable living entity is not available to take charge of Brahmā's post, the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself personally expands and becomes Lord Brahmā.
text:
> kona kalpe yadi yogya jīva nāhi pāya
> āpane īśvara tabe aṁśe 'brahmā' haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:k:kalpe]]---in some lifetime of Brahmā; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:y:yogya]]---suitable; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---living entity; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---is available; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:a:aṁśe]]---by His plenary expansion; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes Lord Brahmā.
translation: "If in a kalpa a suitable living entity is not available to take charge of Brahmā's post, the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself personally expands and becomes Lord Brahmā.
purport: One day of Brahmā consists of the four //yugas// multiplied a thousand times-or, according to solar calculations, 4,320,000,000 years-and such also is the duration of his night. One year of Brahmā's life consists of 360 days and nights, and Brahmā lives for one hundred such years. Such is the life of a Brahmā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.306
description: " 'What is the value of a throne to Lord Kṛṣṇa? The masters of the various planetary systems accept the dust of His lotus feet on their crowned heads. That dust makes the holy places sacred, and even Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva, Lakṣmī and I myself, who are all portions of His plenary portion, eternally carry that dust on our heads.'
text:
> yasyāṅghri-paṅkaja-rajo 'khila-loka-pālair
> mauly-uttamair dhṛtam upāsita-tīrtha-tīrtham
> brahmā bhavo 'ham api yasya kalāḥ kalāyāḥ
> śrīś codvahema ciram asya nṛpāsanaṁ kva
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---whose; [[synonyms:a:aṅghri]]-[[synonyms:p:paṅkaja]]---lotuslike feet; [[synonyms:r:rajaḥ]]---the dust; [[synonyms:a:akhila]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---of the universal planetary systems; [[synonyms:p:pālaiḥ]]---by the masters; [[synonyms:m:mauli]]-[[synonyms:u:uttamaiḥ]]---with valuable turbans on their heads; [[synonyms:d:dhṛtam]]---accepted; [[synonyms:u:upāsita]]---worshiped; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrtham]]---the sanctifier of the holy places; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:b:bhavaḥ]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:a:aham]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---even I; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:k:kalāḥ]]---portions; [[synonyms:k:kalāyāḥ]]---of a plenary portion; [[synonyms:ś:śrīḥ]]---the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:u:udvahema]]---we carry; [[synonyms:c:ciram]]---eternally; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of Him; [[synonyms:n:nṛpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsanam]]---the throne of a king; [[synonyms:k:kva]]---where.
translation: “ 'What is the value of a throne to Lord Kṛṣṇa? The masters of the various planetary systems accept the dust of His lotus feet on their crowned heads. That dust makes the holy places sacred, and even Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva, Lakṣmī and I myself, who are all portions of His plenary portion, eternally carry that dust on our heads.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.68.37). When the Kauravas flattered Baladeva so that He would become their ally and spoke ill of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Lord Baladeva was angry and spoke this verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.307
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, expands a portion of His plenary portion and, accepting the association of the material mode of ignorance, assumes the form of Rudra to dissolve the cosmic manifestation.
text:
> nijāṁśa-kalāya kṛṣṇa tamo-guṇa aṅgīkari'
> saṁhārārthe māyā-saṅge rudra-rūpa dhari
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---of His personal plenary expansion; [[synonyms:k:kalāya]]---by an expansion known as kalā; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tamaḥ]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---the material mode of darkness; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:s:saṁhāra]]-[[synonyms:a:arthe]]---for the purpose of dissolution; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in association with the external energy; [[synonyms:r:rudra]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the form of Rudra; [[synonyms:d:dhari]]---assumes.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, expands a portion of His plenary portion and, accepting the association of the material mode of ignorance, assumes the form of Rudra to dissolve the cosmic manifestation.
purport: This is a description of the Rudra form, which is another expansion of Kṛṣṇa. Only //viṣṇu-mūrtis// are expansions of Kṛṣṇa's personal and plenary portions. Mahā Viṣṇu, who lies on the Causal Ocean, is an expansion of Saṅkarṣaṇa. When Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu accepts the material modes of nature for the purpose of dissolving the cosmic manifestation, His form is called Rudra. As already explained, Lord Viṣṇu is the controller of //māyā.// How, then, can He associate with //māyā//? The conclusion is that the incarnation of Lord Śiva or Lord Brahmā indicates the absence of the supreme power of Viṣṇu. When the supreme power is not there, it is possible to associate with //māyā,// the external energy. Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva are to be considered creations of //māyā.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.308
description: "Rudra, Lord Śiva, has various forms, which are transformations brought about by association with māyā. Although Rudra is not on a level with the jīva-tattvas, he still cannot be considered a personal expansion of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> māyā-saṅga-vikārī rudra---bhinnābhinna rūpa
> jīva-tattva nahe, nahe kṛṣṇera 'svarūpa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---by association with māyā; [[synonyms:v:vikārī]]---transformed; [[synonyms:r:rudra]]---the form of Rudra; [[synonyms:b:bhinna]]-[[synonyms:a:abhinna]] [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---having different types of forms; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---still he is not called jīva-tattva; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---nor; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---personal form.
translation: "Rudra, Lord Śiva, has various forms, which are transformations brought about by association with māyā. Although Rudra is not on a level with the jīva-tattvas, he still cannot be considered a personal expansion of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
purport: Rudra is simultaneously one with and different from the //viṣṇu-tattva.// Due to his association with //māyā,// he is different from the //viṣṇu-tattva,// but at the same time he is an expansion of Kṛṣṇa's personal form. This situation is called //bhedābheda-tattva,// or //acintya-bhedābheda-tattva,// simultaneously one and different.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.309
description: "Milk is transformed into yogurt when it associates with a yogurt culture. Thus yogurt is nothing but milk, but still it is not milk.
text:
> dugdha yena amla-yoge dadhi-rūpa dhare
> dugdhāntara vastu nahe, dugdha haite nāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]---milk; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as; [[synonyms:a:amla:yoge]]---in association with a sour substance; [[synonyms:d:dadhi]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the form of yogurt; [[synonyms:d:dhare]]---takes; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]-[[synonyms:a:antara]]---something other than milk; [[synonyms:v:vastu]]---substance; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---is not; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]---milk; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---to be; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---is not able.
translation: "Milk is transformed into yogurt when it associates with a yogurt culture. Thus yogurt is nothing but milk, but still it is not milk.
purport: Of the three deities supervising the creation, maintenance and dissolution of the universe, Lord Viṣṇu is never separate from the original Viṣṇu. However, Lord Śiva and Brahmā, due to their association with //māyā,// are different from Viṣṇu. Viṣṇu cannot be transformed into any form of material energy. Whenever there is association with //māyā,// the personality involved must be different from Lord Viṣṇu. Therefore Lord Śiva and Lord Brahmā are called //guṇa-avatāras,// for they associate with the material qualities. The conclusion is that Rudra is a transformation of Viṣṇu, but he is not exactly Lord Viṣṇu. Therefore, he does not come within the category of the //viṣṇu-tattvas.// Thus he is inconceivably one with Viṣṇu and different from Him. The example given in this verse is very clear. Milk is compared to Viṣṇu. As soon as milk touches a sour substance, it becomes yogurt, or Lord Śiva. Although yogurt is constitutionally milk it cannot be used in place of milk.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.31
description: "I am very satisfied with your behavior. I shall not accept these gold coins, but I shall get you across that hilly tract of land simply to perform a pious activity."
text:
> santuṣṭa ha-ilāṅa āmi, mohara nā la-iba
> puṇya lāgi' parvata tomā' pāra kari' diba"
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:santuṣṭa]]---satisfied; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilāṅa]]---have become; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:m:mohara]]---the golden coins; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iba]]---I shall not take; [[synonyms:p:puṇya]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---simply for pious activity; [[synonyms:p:parvata]]---the hilly tract of land; [[synonyms:t:tomā']]---you; [[synonyms:p:pāra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:d:diba]]---I shall get across.
translation: "I am very satisfied with your behavior. I shall not accept these gold coins, but I shall get you across that hilly tract of land simply to perform a pious activity."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.310
description: " 'Milk changes into yogurt when mixed with a yogurt culture, but actually it is constitutionally nothing but milk. Similarly, Govinda, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, assumes the form of Lord Śiva [Śambhu] for the special purpose of material transactions. I offer my obeisances at His lotus feet.'
text:
> kṣīraṁ yathā dadhi vikāra-viśeṣa-yogāt
> sañjāyate na tu tataḥ pṛthag asti hetoḥ
> yaḥ śambhutām api tathā samupaiti kāryād
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṣīram]]---milk; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:d:dadhi]]---yogurt; [[synonyms:v:vikāra]]-[[synonyms:v:viśeṣa]]---with a special transforming agent; [[synonyms:y:yogāt]]---by mixing; [[synonyms:s:sañjāyate]]---is transformed into; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:t:tataḥ]]---from the milk; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---separated; [[synonyms:a:asti]]---is; [[synonyms:h:hetoḥ]]---which is the cause; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:ś:śambhutām]]---the nature of Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even though; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---as; [[synonyms:s:samupaiti]]---accepts; [[synonyms:k:kāryāt]]---from the matter of some particular business; [[synonyms:g:govindam]]---unto Govinda, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣam]]---the original person; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bhajāmi]]---offer my respectful obeisances.
translation: “ 'Milk changes into yogurt when mixed with a yogurt culture, but actually it is constitutionally nothing but milk. Similarly, Govinda, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, assumes the form of Lord Śiva [Śambhu] for the special purpose of material transactions. I offer my obeisances at His lotus feet.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.45).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.311
description: "Lord Śiva is an associate of the external energy; therefore he is absorbed in the material quality of darkness. Lord Viṣṇu is transcendental to māyā and the qualities of māyā. Therefore He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> 'śiva'---māyā-śakti-saṅgī, tamo-guṇā veśa
> māyātīta, guṇātīta 'viṣṇu'---parameśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgī]]---an associate of the external energy; [[synonyms:t:tamaḥ]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---absorbed by the quality of ignorance; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:a:atīta]]---transcendental to the external energy; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:atīta]]---transcendental to the qualities of matter; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśa]]---the Supreme Lord.
translation: "Lord Śiva is an associate of the external energy; therefore he is absorbed in the material quality of darkness. Lord Viṣṇu is transcendental to māyā and the qualities of māyā. Therefore He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
purport: Viṣṇu is beyond the range of the material manifestation, and He is not within the control of the material energy. He is the supreme independent Personality of Godhead. This is even admitted by Śaṅkarācārya: //nārāyaṇaḥ paro 'vyaktāt (Gīta-bhāṣya).// In his constitutional form, Śiva is a //mahā-bhāgavata,// a supreme devotee of the Lord, but because he accepts //māyā's// association-especially the quality of ignorance-he is not free from //māyā's// influence. Such an intimate association is completely absent in the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu. Lord Śiva accepts //māyā,// but in the presence of Lord Viṣṇu, //māyā// does not exist. Consequently Lord Śiva has to be considered a product of //māyā.// When Lord Śiva is free from //māyā's// influence, he is in the position of a //mahā-bhāgavata,// a supreme devotee of Lord Viṣṇu. //Vaiṣṇavānāṁ yathā śambhuḥ.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.312
description: " 'The truth about Lord Śiva is that he is always covered with three material coverings-vaikārika, taijasa and tāmasa. Because of these three modes of material nature, he always associates with the external energy and egotism itself.'
text:
> śivaḥ śakti-yuktaḥ śaśvat
> triliṅgo guṇa-saṁvṛtaḥ
> vaikārikas taijasaś ca
> tāmasaś cety ahaṁ tridhā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śivaḥ]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:y:yuktaḥ]]---associated with material nature; [[synonyms:ś:śaśvat]]---eternally; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:l:liṅgaḥ]]---in three features; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṁvṛtaḥ]]---covered by the modes of nature; [[synonyms:v:vaikārikaḥ]]---one is called vaikārika; [[synonyms:t:taijasaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---another is called taijasa; [[synonyms:t:tāmasaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---as well as tāmasa; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---egotism; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:d:dhā]]---three kinds.
translation: “ 'The truth about Lord Śiva is that he is always covered with three material coverings-vaikārika, taijasa and tāmasa. Because of these three modes of material nature, he always associates with the external energy and egotism itself.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.88.3).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.313
description: " 'Śrī Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is situated beyond the range of material nature; therefore He is the supreme transcendental person. He can see everything inside and outside; therefore He is the supreme overseer of all living entities. If someone takes shelter at His lotus feet and worships Him, he also attains a transcendental position.'
text:
> harir hi nirguṇaḥ sākṣāt
> puruṣaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ
> sa sarva-dṛg upadraṣṭā
> taṁ bhajan nirguṇo bhavet
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:n:nirguṇaḥ]]---transcendental to all material qualities; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:p:puruṣaḥ]]---the supreme enjoyer; [[synonyms:p:prakṛteḥ]]---material nature; [[synonyms:p:paraḥ]]---beyond; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛk]]---the seer of everything; [[synonyms:u:upadraṣṭā]]---the overseer of everything; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---Him; [[synonyms:b:bhajan]]---by worshiping; [[synonyms:n:nirguṇaḥ]]---transcendental to material qualities; [[synonyms:b:bhavet]]---one becomes.
translation: “ 'Śrī Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is situated beyond the range of material nature; therefore He is the supreme transcendental person. He can see everything inside and outside; therefore He is the supreme overseer of all living entities. If someone takes shelter at His lotus feet and worships Him, he also attains a transcendental position.'
purport: This is also a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.88.5).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.314
description: "For the maintenance of the universe, Lord Kṛṣṇa descends as His personal plenary expansion in the form of Viṣṇu. He is the director of the mode of goodness; therefore He is transcendental to the material energy.
text:
> pālanārtha svāṁśa viṣṇu-rūpe avatāra
> sattva-guṇa draṣṭā, tāte guṇa-māyā-pāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pālana]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---for maintenance; [[synonyms:s:svāṁśa]]---personal plenary expansion; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in the form of Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnation; [[synonyms:s:sattva]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---of the mode of goodness; [[synonyms:d:draṣṭā]]---director; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:p:pāra]]---transcendental to the material modes of nature.
translation: "For the maintenance of the universe, Lord Kṛṣṇa descends as His personal plenary expansion in the form of Viṣṇu. He is the director of the mode of goodness; therefore He is transcendental to the material energy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.315
description: "Lord Viṣṇu is in the category of svāṁśa because He has opulences almost equal to Kṛṣṇa's. Kṛṣṇa is the original person, and Lord Viṣṇu is His personal expansion. This is the verdict of all Vedic literature.
text:
> svarūpa---aiśvarya-pūrṇa, kṛṣṇa-sama prāya
> kṛṣṇa aṁśī, teṅho aṁśa, vede hena gāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---personal expansion; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]-[[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---full of all opulences; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prāya]]---almost; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:a:aṁśī]]---Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---personal expansion; [[synonyms:v:vede]]---the Vedas; [[synonyms:h:hena]]---thus; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sing.
translation: "Lord Viṣṇu is in the category of svāṁśa because He has opulences almost equal to Kṛṣṇa's. Kṛṣṇa is the original person, and Lord Viṣṇu is His personal expansion. This is the verdict of all Vedic literature.
purport: Although an incarnation of the material energy, Lord Brahmā is nonetheless the director of the material mode of passion. Similarly, Lord Śiva, although simultaneously one with and different from Lord Kṛṣṇa, is still the incarnation of the mode of darkness. However, Lord Viṣṇu is Kṛṣṇa's personal expansion; therefore He is the director of the mode of goodness and is always transcendentally situated beyond the jurisdiction of the modes of material nature. Lord Viṣṇu is the original personal expansion of Kṛṣṇa, and Kṛṣṇa is the original source of all incarnations. As far as power is concerned, Lord Viṣṇu is as powerful as Lord Kṛṣṇa because He possesses all the opulences.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.316
description: " 'When the flame of one candle is expanded to another candle and placed in a different position, it burns separately, and its illumination is as powerful as the original candle. Similarly, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Govinda, expands Himself in different forms as Viṣṇu, who is equally luminous, powerful and opulent. Let me worship that Supreme Personality of Godhead, Govinda.'
text:
> dīpārcir eva hi daśāntaram abhyupetya
> dīpāyate vivṛta-hetu-samāna-dharmā
> yas tādṛg eva hi ca viṣṇutayā vibhāti
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
