translation: “ 'When the flame of one candle is expanded to another candle and placed in a different position, it burns separately, and its illumination is as powerful as the original candle. Similarly, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Govinda, expands Himself in different forms as Viṣṇu, who is equally luminous, powerful and opulent. Let me worship that Supreme Personality of Godhead, Govinda.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.46).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.317
description: "The conclusion is that Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva are simply devotee incarnations who carry out orders. However, Lord Viṣṇu, the maintainer, is the personal feature of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> brahmā, śiva---ājñā-kārī bhakta-avatāra
> pālanārthe viṣṇu---kṛṣṇera svarūpa-ākāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]-[[synonyms:k:kārī]]---order carriers; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations of devotees; [[synonyms:p:pālana]]-[[synonyms:a:arthe]]---for maintenance; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---in the form of a personal feature.
translation: "The conclusion is that Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva are simply devotee incarnations who carry out orders. However, Lord Viṣṇu, the maintainer, is the personal feature of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.318
description: " 'Lord Brahmā said, "I am engaged by the Supreme Personality of Godhead to create. Following His orders, Lord Śiva dissolves everything. The Supreme Personality of Godhead, in His form of Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, maintains all the affairs of material nature. Thus the supreme controller of the three modes of material nature is Lord Viṣṇu." '
text:
> sṛjāmi tan-niyukto 'ham-
> haro harati tad-vaśaḥ
> viśvaṁ puruṣa-rūpeṇa
> paripāti triśakti-dhṛk
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sṛjāmi]]---create; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:n:niyuktaḥ]]---engaged by Him; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:h:haraḥ]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:h:harati]]---annihilates; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśaḥ]]---under His control; [[synonyms:v:viśvam]]---the whole universe; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpeṇa]]---in the form of Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:p:paripāti]]---maintains; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:d:dhṛk]]---the controller of the three modes of material nature.
translation: “ 'Lord Brahmā said, "I am engaged by the Supreme Personality of Godhead to create. Following His orders, Lord Śiva dissolves everything. The Supreme Personality of Godhead, in His form of Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, maintains all the affairs of material nature. Thus the supreme controller of the three modes of material nature is Lord Viṣṇu." '
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:6:32|(2.6.32)]]. Lord Brahmā gave this information to Devarṣi Nārada when he was receiving instructions from Lord Brahmā to understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Paramātmā. After describing the universal form of the Lord, Lord Brahmā explained that his position and Lord Śiva's position are controlled by Lord Viṣṇu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.319
description: "O Sanātana, just hear about the Manu incarnations [manvantara-avatāras]. They are unlimited, and no one can count them. Just hear of their source.
text:
> manvantarāvatāra ebe śuna, sanātana
> asaṅkhya gaṇana tāṅra, śunaha kāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:manu]]-[[synonyms:a:antara]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the Manu incarnations; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---O Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:a:asaṅkhya]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---counting; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of them; [[synonyms:ś:śunaha]]---just hear; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause.
translation: "O Sanātana, just hear about the Manu incarnations [manvantara-avatāras]. They are unlimited, and no one can count them. Just hear of their source.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.32
description: Sanātana Gosvāmī replied, "If you do not accept these coins, someone else will kill me for them. It is better that you save me from the danger by accepting the coins."
text:
> gosāñi kahe,---"keha dravya la-ibe āmā māri'
> āmāra prāṇa rakṣā kara dravya aṅgīkari' "
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī said; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone else; [[synonyms:d:dravya]]---the valuable coins; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ibe]]---will take; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]] [[synonyms:m:māri']]---killing me; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---my; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]---life; [[synonyms:r:rakṣā]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---save; [[synonyms:d:dravya]] [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkari']]---by accepting these coins.
translation: Sanātana Gosvāmī replied, "If you do not accept these coins, someone else will kill me for them. It is better that you save me from the danger by accepting the coins."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.320
description: "In one day of Brahmā, there are fourteen changes of the Manus, and all those fourteen Manus are considered incarnations manifested by the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> brahmāra eka-dine haya caudda manvantara
> caudda avatāra tāhāṅ karena īśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmāra]] [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---in one day of Brahmā; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:c:caudda]]---14; [[synonyms:m:manu]]-[[synonyms:a:antara]]---changes of Manu; [[synonyms:c:caudda]]---14; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---in that time; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---manifests; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: "In one day of Brahmā, there are fourteen changes of the Manus, and all those fourteen Manus are considered incarnations manifested by the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
purport: In one day of Brahmā, there are 14 Manus, and all of them are considered to be //manvantara-avatāras// of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Thus in one month days) of Brahmā's life, there are 5,040 Manu incarnations. Thus for the one hundred years of Brahmā's life, there is a total of 504,000 //manvantara-avatāras.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.321
description: "There are 14 manvantara-avatāras in one day of Brahmā, 420 in one month, and 5,040 in one year.
text:
> caudda eka dine, māse cāri-śata biśa
> brahmāra vatsare pañca-sahasra calliśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caudda]]---14; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---in one day; [[synonyms:m:māse]]---in one month; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:b:biśa]]---420; [[synonyms:b:brahmāra]] [[synonyms:v:vatsare]]---in one year of Brahmā; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:s:sahasra]] [[synonyms:c:calliśa]]---5,040 avatāras.
translation: "There are 14 manvantara-avatāras in one day of Brahmā, 420 in one month, and 5,040 in one year.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.322
description: "During the hundred years of Brahmā's life, there are 504,000 manvantara-avatarās.
text:
> śateka vatsara haya jīvana' brahmāra
> pañca-lakṣa cāri-sahasra manvantarāvatāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śateka]] [[synonyms:v:vatsara]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are one hundred years; [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---the duration of life; [[synonyms:b:brahmāra]]---of Brahmā; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---500,000; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:s:sahasra]]---4,000; [[synonyms:m:manu]]-[[synonyms:a:antara]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations of Manu.
translation: "During the hundred years of Brahmā's life, there are 504,000 manvantara-avatarās.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.323
description: "The number of manvantara-avatāras for only one universe has been given. One can only imagine how many manvantara-avatāras exist in the innumerable universes. And all these universes and Brahmās exist only during one exhalation of Mahā-Viṣṇu.
text:
> ananta brahmāṇḍe aiche karaha gaṇana
> mahā-viṣṇu eka-śvāse brahmāra jīvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍe]]---in innumerable universes; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---just try to count; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śvāse]]---by one exhalation; [[synonyms:b:brahmāra]] [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---the duration of life of one Brahmā.
translation: "The number of manvantara-avatāras for only one universe has been given. One can only imagine how many manvantara-avatāras exist in the innumerable universes. And all these universes and Brahmās exist only during one exhalation of Mahā-Viṣṇu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.324
description: "There is no limit to the exhalations of Mahā-Viṣṇu. Just see how impossible it is to speak or write of even only the manvantara-avatāra.
text:
> mahā-viṣṇura niśvāsera nāhika paryanta
> eka manvantarāvatārera dekha lekhāra anta
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣṇura]]---of Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:n:niśvāsera]]---of the exhalations; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---there is no limit; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:m:manvantara]]-[[synonyms:a:avatārera]]---of only one feature of the Lord, namely the //manvantara-avatāra//; [[synonyms:d:dekha]]---just see; [[synonyms:l:lekhāra]] [[synonyms:a:anta]]---it is beyond the power of writing.
translation: "There is no limit to the exhalations of Mahā-Viṣṇu. Just see how impossible it is to speak or write of even only the manvantara-avatāra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.325
description: "In the Svāyambhuva-manvantara, the avatāra was named Yajña. In the Svārociṣa-manvantara, he was named Vibhu. In the Auttama-manvantara, he was named Satyasena, and in the Tāmasa-manvantara he was named Hari.
text:
> svāyaṁbhuve 'yajña', svārociṣe 'vibhu' nāma
> auttame 'satyasena', tāmase 'hari' abhidhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svāyaṁbhuve]]---in the Svāyambhuva-manvantara; [[synonyms:y:yajña]]---the avatāra named Yajña; [[synonyms:s:svārociṣe]]---in the Svārociṣa-manvantara; [[synonyms:v:vibhu]]---the avatāra Vibhu; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:a:auttame]]---in the Auttama-manvantara; [[synonyms:s:satyasena]]---the avatāra named Satyasena; [[synonyms:t:tāmase]]---in the Tāmasa-manvantara; [[synonyms:h:hari]]---Hari; [[synonyms:a:abhidhāna]]---named.
translation: "In the Svāyambhuva-manvantara, the avatāra was named Yajña. In the Svārociṣa-manvantara, he was named Vibhu. In the Auttama-manvantara, he was named Satyasena, and in the Tāmasa-manvantara he was named Hari.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.326
description: "In the Raivata-manvantara, the avatāra was named Vaikuṇṭha, and in the Cākṣuṣa-manvantara, he was named Ajita. In the Vaivasvata-manvantara, he was named Vāmana, and in the Sāvarṇya-manvantara, he was named Sārvabhauma. In the Dakṣa-sāvarṇya-manvantara, he was named Ṛṣabha.
text:
> raivate 'vaikuṇṭha' cākṣuṣe 'ajita', vaivasvate 'vāmana'
> sāvarṇye 'sārvabhauma', dakṣa-sāvarṇye 'ṛṣabha' gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:raivate]]---in the Raivata-manvantara; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]]---the avatāra named Vaikuṇṭha; [[synonyms:c:cākṣuṣe]]---in the Cākṣuṣa-manvantara; [[synonyms:a:ajita]]---the avatāra named Ajita; [[synonyms:v:vaivasvate]]---in the Vaivasvata-manvantara; [[synonyms:v:vāmana]]---the avatāra named Vāmana; [[synonyms:s:sāvarṇye]]---in the Sāvarṇya-manvantara; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---the avatāra named Sārvabhauma; [[synonyms:d:dakṣa]]-[[synonyms:s:sāvarṇye]]---in the Dakṣa-sāvarṇya-manvantara; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣabha]]---the avatāra Ṛṣabha; [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---named.
translation: "In the Raivata-manvantara, the avatāra was named Vaikuṇṭha, and in the Cākṣuṣa-manvantara, he was named Ajita. In the Vaivasvata-manvantara, he was named Vāmana, and in the Sāvarṇya-manvantara, he was named Sārvabhauma. In the Dakṣa-sāvarṇya-manvantara, he was named Ṛṣabha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.327
description: "In the Brahma-sāvarṇya-manvantara, the avatāra was named Viṣvaksena, and in the Dharma-sāvarṇya, he was named Dharmasetu. In the Rudra-sāvarṇya he was named Sudhāmā, and in the Deva-sāvarṇya, he was named Yogeśvara.
text:
> brahma-sāvarṇye 'viṣvaksena', 'dharmasetu' dharma-sāvarṇye
> rudra-sāvarṇye 'sudhāmā', 'yogeśvara' deva-sāvarṇye
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:s:sāvarṇye]]---in the Brahma-sāvarṇya-manvantara; [[synonyms:v:viṣvaksena]]---the avatāra named Viṣvaksena; [[synonyms:d:dharmasetu]]---the avatāra named Dharmasetu; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:s:sāvarṇye]]---in the Dharma-sāvarṇya-manvantara; [[synonyms:r:rudra]]-[[synonyms:s:sāvarṇye]]---in the Rudra-sāvarṇya-manvantara; [[synonyms:s:sudhāmā]]---the avatāra named Sudhāmā; [[synonyms:y:yogeśvara]]---the avatāra named Yogeśvara; [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:s:sāvarṇye]]---in the Deva-sāvarṇya-manvantara.
translation: "In the Brahma-sāvarṇya-manvantara, the avatāra was named Viṣvaksena, and in the Dharma-sāvarṇya, he was named Dharmasetu. In the Rudra-sāvarṇya he was named Sudhāmā, and in the Deva-sāvarṇya, he was named Yogeśvara.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.328
description: "In the Indra-sāvarṇya-manvantara, the avatāra was named Bṛhadbhānu. These are the names of the fourteen avatāras in the fourteen manvantaras.
text:
> indra-sāvarṇye 'bṛhadbhānu' abhidhāna
> ei caudda manvantare caudda 'avatāra' nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:s:sāvarṇye]]---in the Indra-sāvarṇya-manvantara; [[synonyms:b:bṛhadbhānu]]---the //avatāra// named Bṛhadbhānu; [[synonyms:a:abhidhāna]]---named; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:c:caudda]] [[synonyms:m:manvantare]]---in the fourteen manvantaras; [[synonyms:c:caudda]]---fourteen; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---of the incarnations; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---different names.
translation: "In the Indra-sāvarṇya-manvantara, the avatāra was named Bṛhadbhānu. These are the names of the fourteen avatāras in the fourteen manvantaras.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, in his //Anubhāṣya,// gives a list of Manus and their fathers' names: (1) Svāyambhuva Manu, the son of Lord Brahma; (2) Svārociṣa, the son of Svarociḥ, or Agni, the predominating deity of fire; (3) Uttama, the son of King Priyavrata; (4) Tāmasa, the brother of Uttama; (5) Raivata, the twin brother of Tāmasa; (6) Cākṣuṣa, the son of the demigod Cakṣu; (7) Vaivasvata, the son of Vivasvān, the sun-god (whose name is also mentioned in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:4:1|(Bg. 4.1)]]); (8) Sāvarṇi, a son born to the sun-god and wife named Chāyā; (9) Dakṣa-sāvarṇi, the son of the demigod Varuṇa; (10) Brahma-sāvarṇi, the son of Upaśloka; (11-14) Rudra-sāvarṇi, Dharma-sāvarṇi, Deva-sāvarṇi and Indra-sāvarṇi, the sons of Rudra, Ruci, Satyasahā and Bhūti respectively.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.329
description: "O Sanātana, now hear from Me about the yuga-avatāras, the incarnations for the millenniums. First of all, there are four yugas-Satya-yuga, Tretā-yuga, Dvāpara-yuga and Kali-yuga.
text:
> yugāvatāra ebe śuna, sanātana
> satya-tretā-dvāpara-kali-yugera gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yuga]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnation of millenniums; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---O Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:satya]]-[[synonyms:t:tretā]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāpara]]-[[synonyms:k:kali]]-[[synonyms:y:yugera]]---of the Satya-yuga, Tretā-yuga, Dvāpara-yuga and Kali-yuga; [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---the chronological order.
translation: "O Sanātana, now hear from Me about the yuga-avatāras, the incarnations for the millenniums. First of all, there are four yugas-Satya-yuga, Tretā-yuga, Dvāpara-yuga and Kali-yuga.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.33
description: After this settlement was made, the landlord gave Sanātana Gosvāmī four watchmen to accompany him. They went through the forest path for the whole night and thus brought him over the hilly tract of land.
text:
> tabe bhūñā gosāñira saṅge cāri pāika dila
> rātrye rātrye vana-pathe parvata pāra kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereupon; [[synonyms:b:bhūñā]]---the landlord; [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:p:pāika]]---four watchmen; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:r:rātrye]] [[synonyms:r:rātrye]]---during the whole night; [[synonyms:v:vana]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the jungle path; [[synonyms:p:parvata]]---the hilly tract of land; [[synonyms:p:pāra]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---took him across.
translation: After this settlement was made, the landlord gave Sanātana Gosvāmī four watchmen to accompany him. They went through the forest path for the whole night and thus brought him over the hilly tract of land.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.330
description: "In the four yugas-Satya, Tretā, Dvāpara and Kali—the Lord incarnates in four colors: white, red, black and yellow respectively. These are the colors of the incarnations in different millenniums.
text:
> śukla-rakta-kṛṣṇa-pīta---krame cāri varṇa
> cāri varṇa dhari' kṛṣṇa karena yuga-dharma
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śukla]]---white; [[synonyms:r:rakta]]---red; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---black; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]---yellow; [[synonyms:k:krame]]---one after another; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:v:varṇa]]---four colors; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:v:varṇa]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---accepting these four colors; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:y:yuga]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---manifests His pastimes in different millenniums.
translation: "In the four yugas-Satya, Tretā, Dvāpara and Kali---the Lord incarnates in four colors: white, red, black and yellow respectively. These are the colors of the incarnations in different millenniums.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.331
description: " 'This child formerly had three colors according to the prescribed color for different millenniums. Formerly He was white, red and yellow, and now He has assumed a blackish color.'
text:
> āsan varṇās trayo hy asya
> gṛhṇato 'nu-yugaṁ tanūḥ
> śuklo raktas tathā pīta
> idānīṁ kṛṣṇatāṁ gataḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āsan]]---there were; [[synonyms:v:varṇāḥ]]---colors; [[synonyms:t:trayaḥ]]---three; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of your son; [[synonyms:g:gṛhṇataḥ]]---accepting; [[synonyms:a:anu]]-[[synonyms:y:yugam]]---according to the millennium; [[synonyms:t:tanūḥ]]---body; [[synonyms:ś:śuklaḥ]]---white; [[synonyms:r:raktaḥ]]---red; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---as well as; [[synonyms:p:pītaḥ]]---yellow; [[synonyms:i:idānīm]]---just now; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇatām]] [[synonyms:g:gataḥ]]---He has assumed a blackish hue.
translation: “ 'This child formerly had three colors according to the prescribed color for different millenniums. Formerly He was white, red and yellow, and now He has assumed a blackish color.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.8.13) was spoken by Gargamuni when performing the name-giving ceremony for Kṛṣṇa at the house of Nanda Mahārāja. The following two verses are also from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.21,24).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.332
description: " 'In the Satya-yuga, the Lord appeared in a body colored white with four arms and matted hair. He wore tree bark and bore a black antelope skin. He wore a sacred thread and a garland of rudrākṣa beads. He carried a rod and a waterpot, and He was a brahmacārī.'
text:
> kṛte śuklaś catur-bāhur
> jaṭilo valkalāmbaraḥ
> kṛṣṇājinopavītākṣān
> bibhrad daṇḍa-kamaṇḍalū
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛte]]---in the Satya-yuga; [[synonyms:ś:śuklaḥ]]---having a white color and bearing the name Śukla; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhuḥ]]---having four arms; [[synonyms:j:jaṭilaḥ]]---with a bunch of hair; [[synonyms:v:valkala]]-[[synonyms:a:ambaraḥ]]---wearing a garment made of tree bark; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:ajina]]---black-colored antelope skin; [[synonyms:u:upavīta]]---sacred thread; [[synonyms:a:akṣān]]---a garland of beads for chanting; [[synonyms:b:bibhrat]]---carried; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:k:kamaṇḍalū]]---a rod and waterpot.
translation: “ 'In the Satya-yuga, the Lord appeared in a body colored white with four arms and matted hair. He wore tree bark and bore a black antelope skin. He wore a sacred thread and a garland of rudrākṣa beads. He carried a rod and a waterpot, and He was a brahmacārī.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.333
description: " 'In the Tretā-yuga, the Lord appeared in a body that had a reddish hue and four arms. There were three distinctive lines on His abdomen, and His hair was golden. His form manifested the Vedic knowledge, and He bore the symbols of a sacrificial spoon, ladle and so on.'
text:
> tretāyāṁ rakta-varṇo 'sau
> catur-bāhus trimekhalaḥ
> hiraṇya-keśas trayy-ātmā
> sruk-sruv-ādy-upalakṣaṇaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tretāyām]]---in the Tretā-yuga; [[synonyms:r:rakta]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇaḥ]]---of a reddish color; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---He; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhuḥ]]---with four arms; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:m:mekhalaḥ]]---having three circles on the abdomen; [[synonyms:h:hiraṇya]]-[[synonyms:k:keśaḥ]]---hair colored like gold; [[synonyms:t:trayī]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---whose form manifests the Vedas; [[synonyms:s:sruk]]-[[synonyms:s:sruv]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:u:upalakṣaṇaḥ]]---decorated with the sacrificial spoon, ladle and so on.
translation: “ 'In the Tretā-yuga, the Lord appeared in a body that had a reddish hue and four arms. There were three distinctive lines on His abdomen, and His hair was golden. His form manifested the Vedic knowledge, and He bore the symbols of a sacrificial spoon, ladle and so on.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.334
description: "As the white incarnation, the Lord taught religion and meditation. He offered benedictions to Kardama Muni, and in this way He showed His causeless mercy.
text:
> satya-yuge dharma-dhyāna karāya 'śukla'-mūrti dhari'
> kardamake vara dilā yeṅho kṛpā kari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:satya]]-[[synonyms:y:yuge]]---in the millennium of Satya-yuga; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:d:dhyāna]]---religious principles and meditation; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---induces; [[synonyms:ś:śukla]]---whitish; [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---form; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:k:kardamake]]---to Kardama Muni; [[synonyms:v:vara]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave benedictions; [[synonyms:y:yeṅho]]---who; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---out of causeless mercy.
translation: "As the white incarnation, the Lord taught religion and meditation. He offered benedictions to Kardama Muni, and in this way He showed His causeless mercy.
purport: Kardama Muni was one of the //prajāpatis.// He married Devahūti, the daughter of Manu, and their son was Kapiladeva. The Supreme Lord was very pleased with Kardama Muni's austerities, and He appeared before Kardama Muni in a whitish body. This happened in the Satya-yuga millennium, when people were accustomed to practicing meditation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.335
description: "In the Satya-yuga the people were generally advanced in spiritual knowledge and could meditate upon Kṛṣṇa very easily. The people's occupational duty in Tretā-yuga was to perform great sacrifices. This was induced by the Personality of Godhead in His reddish incarnation.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-'dhyāna' kare loka jñāna-adhikārī
> tretāra dharma 'yajña' karāya 'rakta'-varṇa dhari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dhyāna]]---meditation upon Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]-[[synonyms:a:adhikārī]]---who are advanced in spiritual knowledge; [[synonyms:t:tretāra]]---of the Tretā-yuga; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---the occupational duty; [[synonyms:y:yajña]]---performance of sacrifices; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---induces; [[synonyms:r:rakta]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇa]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---assuming a reddish color.
translation: "In the Satya-yuga the people were generally advanced in spiritual knowledge and could meditate upon Kṛṣṇa very easily. The people's occupational duty in Tretā-yuga was to perform great sacrifices. This was induced by the Personality of Godhead in His reddish incarnation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.336
description: "In Dvāpara-yuga the people's occupational duty was to worship the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore Lord Kṛṣṇa, appearing in a blackish body, personally induced people to worship Him.
text:
> 'kṛṣṇa-padārcana' haya dvāparera dharma
> 'kṛṣṇa'-varṇe karāya loke kṛṣṇārcana-karma
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:a:arcana]]---worshiping the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:d:dvāparera]]---of the Dvāpara millennium; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---the occupational duty; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇe]]---in a blackish color; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---induces; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---to the people; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:arcana]]-[[synonyms:k:karma]]---the activities of worshiping Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "In Dvāpara-yuga the people's occupational duty was to worship the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore Lord Kṛṣṇa, appearing in a blackish body, personally induced people to worship Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.337
description: " 'In the Dvāpara-yuga the Personality of Godhead appears in a blackish hue. He is dressed in yellow, He holds His own weapons, and He is decorated with the Kaustubha jewel and marks of Śrīvatsa. That is how His symptoms are described.'
text:
> dvāpare bhagavān śyāmaḥ
> pīta-vāsā nijāyudhaḥ
> śrī-vatsādibhir aṅkaiś ca
> lakṣaṇair upalakṣitaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dvāpare]]---in the Dvāpara-yuga; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ś:śyāmaḥ]]---blackish; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsāḥ]]---having yellow clothes; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---own; [[synonyms:ā:āyudhaḥ]]---having weapons; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vatsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādibhiḥ]]---such as Śrīvatsa; [[synonyms:a:aṅkaiḥ]]---by bodily markings; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇaiḥ]]---by external characteristics such as the Kaustubha jewel; [[synonyms:u:upalakṣitaḥ]]---characterized.
translation: “ 'In the Dvāpara-yuga the Personality of Godhead appears in a blackish hue. He is dressed in yellow, He holds His own weapons, and He is decorated with the Kaustubha jewel and marks of Śrīvatsa. That is how His symptoms are described.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.27). The //śyāma// color is not exactly blackish. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura compares it to the color of the //atasī// flower. It is not that Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself appears in a blackish color in all the Dvāpara-yugas. In other Dvāpara-yugas, previous to Lord Kṛṣṇa's appearance, the Supreme Lord appeared in a greenish body by His own personal expansion. This is mentioned in the //Viṣṇu Purāṇa, Hari-vaṁśa// and //Mahābhārata.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.338
description: " 'I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, expanded as Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha.'
text:
> namas te vāsudevāya
> namaḥ saṅkarṣaṇāya ca
> pradyumnāyāniruddhāya
> tubhyaṁ bhagavate namaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---let me offer my respectful obeisances; [[synonyms:t:te]]---unto You; [[synonyms:v:vāsudevāya]]---Lord Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---respectful obeisances; [[synonyms:s:saṅkarṣaṇāya]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also to Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa; [[synonyms:p:pradyumnāya]]---to Lord Pradyumna; [[synonyms:a:aniruddhāya]]---unto Aniruddha; [[synonyms:t:tubhyam]]---unto You; [[synonyms:b:bhagavate]]---unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---my respectful obeisances.
translation: “ 'I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, expanded as Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha.'
purport: This is a prayer from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.29) spoken by Karabhājana Muni when he was questioned by Mahārāja Nimi, the King of Videha, about the incarnations in specific //yugas// and their method of worship. Karabhājana Muni was one of the nine Yogendras, and he met the King to inform him about future incarnations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.339
description: "By this mantra, the people worship Lord Kṛṣṇa in the Dvāpara-yuga. In the Kali-yuga the occupational duty of the people is to chant congregationally the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> ei mantre dvāpare kare kṛṣṇārcana
> 'kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana'---kali-yugera dharma
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:m:mantre]]---by this mantra; [[synonyms:d:dvāpare]]---in the age of Dvāpara; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:arcana]]---the worship of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kali]]-[[synonyms:y:yugera]] [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---the occupational duty in the Age of Kali.
translation: "By this mantra, the people worship Lord Kṛṣṇa in the Dvāpara-yuga. In the Kali-yuga the occupational duty of the people is to chant congregationally the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.
purport:
As stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (12.3.51):

> kaler doṣa-nidhe rājann
> asti hy eko mahān guṇaḥ
> kīrtanād eva kṛṣṇasya
> mukta-saṅgaḥ paraṁ vrajet

In Kali-yuga one worships Lord Kṛṣṇa by chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare. To propagate this movement, Lord Kṛṣṇa personally appeared as Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu. That is described in the following verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.34
description: After crossing the hills, Sanātana Gosvāmī told his servant, "Īśāna, I think you still have some balance left from the gold coins."
text:
> tabe pāra hañā gosāñi puchilā īśāne
> 'jāni,---śeṣa dravya kichu āche tomā sthāne"
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:p:pāra]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---after crossing; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:puchilā]]---asked; [[synonyms:ī:īśāne]]---Īśāna; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I know; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]] [[synonyms:d:dravya]]---something valuable left; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there is; [[synonyms:t:tomā]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---with you.
translation: After crossing the hills, Sanātana Gosvāmī told his servant, "Īśāna, I think you still have some balance left from the gold coins."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.340
description: "Accompanied by His personal devotees, Lord Kṛṣṇa, assuming a golden color, introduces the hari-nāma-saṅkīrtana, the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra, in the Age of Kali. By this process, He delivers love for Kṛṣṇa to the general populace.
text:
> pita'-varṇa dhari' tabe kailā pravartana
> prema-bhakti dilā loke lañā bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pīta]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇa]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---assuming the color yellow; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:p:pravartana]]---introduced the saṅkīrtana movement; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---He distributed love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---to the people in general; [[synonyms:l:lañā]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---accompanied by His devotees.
translation: "Accompanied by His personal devotees, Lord Kṛṣṇa, assuming a golden color, introduces the hari-nāma-saṅkīrtana, the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra, in the Age of Kali. By this process, He delivers love for Kṛṣṇa to the general populace.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.341
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja, personally introduces the occupational duty of the Age of Kali. He personally chants and dances in ecstatic love, and thus the entire world chants congregationally.
text:
> dharma pravartana kare vrajendra-nandana
> preme gāya nāce loka kare saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dharma]] [[synonyms:p:pravartana]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---introduces a particular type of religious activity; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---Kṛṣṇa Himself; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in love; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chants; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all people; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---congregational chanting.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja, personally introduces the occupational duty of the Age of Kali. He personally chants and dances in ecstatic love, and thus the entire world chants congregationally.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.342
description: " 'In the Age of Kali, intelligent persons perform congregational chanting to worship the incarnation of Godhead who constantly sings the name of Kṛṣṇa. Although His complexion is not blackish, He is Kṛṣṇa Himself. He is accompanied by His associates, servants, weapons and confidential companions.'
text:
> kṛṣṇa-varṇaṁ tviṣākṛṣṇam-
> sāṅgopāṅgāstra-pārṣadam
> yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair
> yajanti hi su-medhasaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇam]]---repeating the syllables kṛṣ-ṇa; [[synonyms:t:tviṣā]]---with a luster; [[synonyms:a:akṛṣṇam]]---not black (golden); [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---with associates; [[synonyms:u:upāṅga]]---servitors; [[synonyms:a:astra]]---weapons; [[synonyms:p:pārṣadam]]---confidential companions; [[synonyms:y:yajñaiḥ]]---by sacrifice; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]-[[synonyms:p:prāyaiḥ]]---consisting chiefly of congregational chanting; [[synonyms:y:yajanti]]---they worship; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:medhasaḥ]]---intelligent persons.
translation: “ 'In the Age of Kali, intelligent persons perform congregational chanting to worship the incarnation of Godhead who constantly sings the name of Kṛṣṇa. Although His complexion is not blackish, He is Kṛṣṇa Himself. He is accompanied by His associates, servants, weapons and confidential companions.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.32). See also //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Three, text 52.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.343
description: "In the other three yugas-Satya, Tretā and Dvāpara-people perform different types of spiritual activities. Whatever results they achieve in that way, they can achieve in Kali-yuga simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra.
text:
> āra tina-yuge dhyānādite yei phala haya
> kali-yuge kṛṣṇa-nāme sei phala pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:y:yuge]]---in the three other yugas; [[synonyms:d:dhyāna]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādite]]---by processes beginning with meditation; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---result; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:k:kali]]-[[synonyms:y:yuge]]---in this Age of Kali; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāme]]---by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:phala]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---one gets the same achievement.
translation: "In the other three yugas-Satya, Tretā and Dvāpara-people perform different types of spiritual activities. Whatever results they achieve in that way, they can achieve in Kali-yuga simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.344
description: " 'My dear King, although Kali-yuga is full of faults, there is still one good quality about this age. It is that simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, one can become free from material bondage and be promoted to the transcendental kingdom.
text:
> kaler doṣa-nidhe rājann
> asti hy eko mahān guṇaḥ
> kīrtanād eva kṛṣṇasya
> mukta-bandhaḥ paraṁ vrajet
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kaleḥ]]---of the Age of Kali; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]-[[synonyms:n:nidhe]]---in the ocean of faults; [[synonyms:r:rājan]]---O King; [[synonyms:a:asti]]---there is; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:e:ekaḥ]]---one; [[synonyms:m:mahān]]---very great; [[synonyms:g:guṇaḥ]]---good quality; [[synonyms:k:kīrtanāt]]---by chanting; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇasya]]---of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mukta]]-[[synonyms:b:bandhaḥ]]---liberated from material bondage; [[synonyms:p:param]]---to the transcendental spiritual kingdom; [[synonyms:v:vrajet]]---one can go.
translation: “ 'My dear King, although Kali-yuga is full of faults, there is still one good quality about this age. It is that simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, one can become free from material bondage and be promoted to the transcendental kingdom.
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (12.3.51).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.345
description: " 'Whatever result was obtained in Satya-yuga by meditating on Viṣṇu, in Tretā-yuga by performing sacrifices and in Dvāpara-yuga by serving the Lord's lotus feet can also be obtained in Kali-yuga simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.'
text:
> kṛte yad dhyāyato viṣṇuṁ
> tretāyāṁ yajato makhaiḥ
> dvāpare paricaryāyāṁ
> kalau tad dhari-kīrtanāt
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛte]]---in the Satya-yuga; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:d:dhyāyataḥ]]---from meditation; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇum]]---on Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:t:tretāyām]]---in the Tretā-yuga; [[synonyms:y:yajataḥ]]---from worshiping; [[synonyms:m:makhaiḥ]]---by performing sacrifices; [[synonyms:d:dvāpare]]---in the age of Dvāpara; [[synonyms:p:paricaryāyām]]---by worshiping the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kalau]]---in the Age of Kali; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that same result (can be achieved); [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:k:kīrtanāt]]---simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.
translation: “ 'Whatever result was obtained in Satya-yuga by meditating on Viṣṇu, in Tretā-yuga by performing sacrifices and in Dvāpara-yuga by serving the Lord's lotus feet can also be obtained in Kali-yuga simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.'
purport:
This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (12.3.52). At the present moment in Kali-yuga there are many false meditators who concoct some imaginary form and try to meditate upon it. It has become fashionable to meditate, but people know nothing about the object of meditation. That is explained here. //Yad dhyāyato viṣṇum.// One has to meditate upon Lord Viṣṇu or Lord Kṛṣṇa. Without referring to the //śāstras,// so-called meditators aim at impersonal objects. Lord Kṛṣṇa has condemned them in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:12:5|(Bg. 12.5)]]:

> kleśo 'dhikataras teṣām
> avyaktāsakta-cetasām
> avyaktā hi gatir duḥkhaṁ
> dehavadbhir avāpyate

"For those whose minds are attached to the unmanifested, impersonal feature of the Supreme, advancement is very troublesome. To make progress in that discipline is always difficult for those who are embodied."

Not knowing how to meditate, foolish people simply suffer, and there is no benefit derived from their spiritual activities. The same reference can be found in the following verse from the //Viṣṇu Purāṇa// (6.2.17), //Padma Purāṇa// (//Uttara-khaṇḍa// 72.25) and //Bṛhan-nāradīya Purāṇa// (38.97).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.346
description: " 'Whatever is achieved by meditation in Satya-yuga, by the performance of yajña in Tretā-yuga or by the worship of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet in Dvāpara-yuga is also obtained in the Age of Kali simply by chanting and glorifying Lord Keśava.'
text:
> dhyāyan kṛte yajan yajñais
> tretāyāṁ dvāpare 'rcayan
> yad āpnoti tad āpnoti
> kalau saṅkīrtya keśavam
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dhyāyan]]---meditating; [[synonyms:k:kṛte]]---in the Satya-yuga; [[synonyms:y:yajan]]---worshiping; [[synonyms:y:yajñaiḥ]]---by the performance of great sacrifices; [[synonyms:t:tretāyām]]---in the Tretā-yuga; [[synonyms:d:dvāpare]]---in the Dvāpara-yuga; [[synonyms:a:arcayan]]---worshiping the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---whatever; [[synonyms:ā:āpnoti]]---is achieved; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:ā:āpnoti]]---is obtained; [[synonyms:k:kalau]]---in the Age of Kali; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtya]]---simply by chanting; [[synonyms:k:keśavam]]---the pastimes and qualities of Lord Keśava.
translation: “ 'Whatever is achieved by meditation in Satya-yuga, by the performance of yajña in Tretā-yuga or by the worship of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet in Dvāpara-yuga is also obtained in the Age of Kali simply by chanting and glorifying Lord Keśava.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.347
description: " 'Those who are advanced and highly qualified and are interested in the essence of life, know the good qualities of Kali-yuga. Such people worship the Age of Kali because in this age, simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra, one can advance in spiritual knowledge and attain life's goal.'
text:
> kaliṁ sabhājayanty āryā
> guṇa-jñāḥ sāra-bhāginaḥ
> yatra saṅkīrtanenaiva
> sarva-svārtho 'bhilabhyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kalim]]---the Kali-yuga; [[synonyms:s:sabhājayanti]]---worship; [[synonyms:ā:āryāḥ]]---advanced people; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāḥ]]---appreciating this good quality of Kali-yuga; [[synonyms:s:sāra]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāginaḥ]]---persons who accept the essence of life; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---in which age; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtanena]]---simply by performing saṅkīrtana-yajña, the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:a:arthaḥ]]---all interests of life; [[synonyms:a:abhilabhyate]]---are achieved.
translation: “ 'Those who are advanced and highly qualified and are interested in the essence of life, know the good qualities of Kali-yuga. Such people worship the Age of Kali because in this age, simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra, one can advance in spiritual knowledge and attain life's goal.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.36) spoken by the great sage Karabhājana Ṛṣi, one of the nine Yogendras. The sage was informing Mahārāja Nimi about the people's duty to worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead according to different processes in different //yugas.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.348
description: "As stated before when I described the incarnations of the material modes [guṇa-avatāras], one should consider that these incarnations also are unlimited and that no one can count them.
text:
> pūrvavat likhi yabe guṇāvatāra-gaṇa
> asaṅkhya saṅkhyā tāṅra, nā haya gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---as previously; [[synonyms:l:likhi]]---I write; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---incarnations of the material modes of nature; [[synonyms:a:asaṅkhya]]---innumerable; [[synonyms:s:saṅkhya]]---counting; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of them; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---not actually countable.
translation: "As stated before when I described the incarnations of the material modes [guṇa-avatāras], one should consider that these incarnations also are unlimited and that no one can count them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.349
description: "Thus I have given a description of the incarnations of the four different yugas." After hearing all this, Sanātana Gosvāmī gave an indirect hint to the Lord.
text:
> cāri-yugāvatāre ei ta' gaṇana
> śuni' bhaṅgi kari' tāṅre puche sanātana

translation: "Thus I have given a description of the incarnations of the four different yugas." After hearing all this, Sanātana Gosvāmī gave an indirect hint to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.35
description: Īśāna replied, "I still have one gold coin in my possession." Sanātana Gosvāmī then said, "Take the coin and return to your home."
text:
> īśāna kahe,---"eka mohara āche avaśeṣa"
> gosāñi kahe,---"mohara lañā yāha' tumi deśa"
