title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.350
description: Sanātana Gosvāmī had been a minister under Nawab Hussain Shah, and he was undoubtedly as intelligent as Bṛhaspati, the chief priest of the heavenly kingdom. Due to the Lord's unlimited mercy, Sanātana Gosvāmī questioned Him without hesitation.
text:
> rāja-mantrī sanātana---buddhye bṛhaspati
> prabhura kṛpāte puche asaṅkoca-mati
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:m:mantrī]] [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī was formerly an intelligent minister for Nawab Hussain Shah; [[synonyms:b:buddhye]]---in intelligence; [[synonyms:b:bṛhaspati]]---exactly like Bṛhaspati, the priest in the heavenly kingdom; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpāte]]---because of the unlimited mercy of the Lord; [[synonyms:p:puche]]---inquires; [[synonyms:a:asaṅkoca]]-[[synonyms:m:mati]]---without hesitation.
translation: Sanātana Gosvāmī had been a minister under Nawab Hussain Shah, and he was undoubtedly as intelligent as Bṛhaspati, the chief priest of the heavenly kingdom. Due to the Lord's unlimited mercy, Sanātana Gosvāmī questioned Him without hesitation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.351
description: Sanātana Gosvāmī said, "I am a very insignificant living entity. I am low and poorly behaved. How can I understand who is the incarnation for this Age of Kali?"
text:
> 'ati kṣudra jīva muñi nīca, nīcācāra
> kemane jāniba kalite kon avatāra?'
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ati]]---very; [[synonyms:k:kṣudra]]---unimportant, insignificant; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---living entity; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]---low; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācāra]]---having very abominable behavior; [[synonyms:k:kemane]]---how; [[synonyms:j:jāniba]]---shall i know; [[synonyms:k:kalite]]---in this age; [[synonyms:k:kon]] [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---who is the incarnation.
translation: Sanātana Gosvāmī said, "I am a very insignificant living entity. I am low and poorly behaved. How can I understand who is the incarnation for this Age of Kali?"
purport: This verse is very important in reference to the incarnations of God. At present there are especially many rascals prevalent in India who proclaim themselves incarnations of God or goddesses. Thus they are fooling and bluffing foolish people. On behalf of the general populace, Sanātana Gosvāmī presented himself as a foolish, lowborn, poorly behaved person, although he was a most exalted personality. Inferior people cannot accept the real God, yet they are very eager to accept an imitation God who can simply bluff foolish people. All this is going on in this Age of Kali. To guide these foolish people, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu answers the question as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.352
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "As in other ages an incarnation is accepted according to the directions of the śāstras, in this Age of Kali an incarnation of God should be accepted in that way.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---"anyāvatāra śāstra-dvāre jāni
> kalite avatāra taiche śāstra-vākye māni
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the incarnations in other yugas; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]] [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---one has to accept by reference to the śāstras; [[synonyms:k:kalite]]---in this Age of Kali; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnation; [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---similarly; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:v:vākye]] [[synonyms:m:māni]]---one has to accept according to the description of revealed scriptures.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "As in other ages an incarnation is accepted according to the directions of the śāstras, in this Age of Kali an incarnation of God should be accepted in that way.
purport: According to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, this is the way an incarnation should be accepted. Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says, //sādhu-śāstra-guru-vākya, cittete kariyā aikya.// One should accept a thing as genuine by studying the words of saintly people, the spiritual master and //śāstra.// The actual center is //śāstra,// the revealed scripture. If a spiritual master does not speak according to revealed scripture, he is not to be accepted. Similarly, if a saintly person does not speak according to the //śāstra,// he is not a saintly person. //Śāstra// is the center for all. Unfortunately, at the present moment, people do not refer to the //śāstras;// therefore they accept rascals as incarnations, and consequently they have made incarnations into a very cheap thing. Intelligent people who follow Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's instructions and the instructions of the //ācārya,// the bona fide spiritual master, will not accept a pretender as an incarnation of God. In Kali-yuga, the only incarnation is Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Imitation incarnations take advantage of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The Lord appeared within the past five hundred years, played as the son of a //brāhmaṇa// from Nadia and introduced the //saṅkīrtana// movement. Imitating Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and ignoring the //śāstra,// rascals present themselves as incarnations and introduce their rascaldom as a religious process. As we have repeatedly said, religion can be given only by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. From the discussions in //Caitanya-caritāmṛta,// we can understand that in different ages the Supreme Lord introduces different systems and different religious duties. In this Age of Kali, the only incarnation of Kṛṣṇa is Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and He introduced the religious duty of Kali-yuga, the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra:// Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare HareHare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.353
description: "The Vedic literatures composed by the omniscient Mahāmuni Vyāsadeva are evidence of all spiritual existence. Only through these revealed scriptures can all conditioned souls attain knowledge.
text:
> sarvajña munira vākya---śāstra-'paramāṇa'
> āmā-sabā jīvera haya śāstra-dvārā jñāna'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:j:jña]] [[synonyms:m:munira]] [[synonyms:v:vākya]]---the words of the omniscient muni (Vyāsadeva); [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:p:paramāṇa]]---evidence of revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all of us; [[synonyms:j:jīvera]]---of the conditioned souls; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:d:dvārā]]---through the medium of revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge.
translation: "The Vedic literatures composed by the omniscient Mahāmuni Vyāsadeva are evidence of all spiritual existence. Only through these revealed scriptures can all conditioned souls attain knowledge.
purport:
Foolish people try to concoct knowledge by manufacturing something in their brains. That is not the real way of knowledge. Knowledge is //śabda-pramāṇa,// evidence from Vedic literature. Śrīla Vyāsadeva is called Mahāmuni. He is also known as Vedavyāsa because he has compiled so many //śāstras.// He has divided the //Vedas// into four divisions-//Sāma, Ṛg, Yajur// and //Atharva.// He has expanded the //Vedas// into eighteen //Purāṇas// and has summarized Vedic knowledge in the //Vedānta-sūtra.// He also compiled the //Mahābhārata,// which is accepted as the fifth //Veda. Bhagavad-gītā// is contained within the //Mahābhārata.// Therefore //Bhagavad-gītā// is also Vedic literature (//smṛti).// Some of the Vedic literatures are called //śrutis,// and some are called //smṛtis.// Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī recommends in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.101):

> śruti-smṛti-purāṇādi-
> pañcarātra-vidhiṁ vinā
> aikāntikī harer bhaktir
> utpātāyaiva kalpate

Unless one refers to //śāstra (śruti, smṛti// and //purāṇādi),// one's spiritual activity simply disturbs society. There is no king or government to check people, and therefore society has fallen into a chaotic condition as far as spiritual understanding is concerned. Taking advantage of this chaotic condition, many rascals have appeared and proclaimed themselves incarnations of God. As a result, the entire population is indulging in sinful activities such as illicit sex, intoxication, gambling and meat-eating. Out of many sinful people, many incarnations of God are emerging. This is a very regrettable situation, especially in India.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.354
description: "An actual incarnation of God never says, 'I am God,' or 'I am an incarnation of God.' The great sage Vyāsadeva, knowing all, has already recorded the characteristics of the avatāras in the śāstras.
text:
> avatāra nāhi kahe---'āmi avatāra'
> muni saba jāni' kare lakṣaṇa-vicāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the actual incarnation of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---never; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---I am an incarnation; [[synonyms:m:muni]]---the great sage Mahāmuni Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---knowing all (past, present and future); [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---describes the symptoms of the avatāras.
translation: "An actual incarnation of God never says, 'I am God,' or 'I am an incarnation of God.' The great sage Vyāsadeva, knowing all, has already recorded the characteristics of the avatāras in the śāstras.
purport: In this verse it is clearly stated that a real incarnation of God never claims to be a real incarnation. According to the symptoms described in the //śāstra,// one can understand who is an //avatāra// and who is not.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.355
description: " 'The Lord does not have a material body, yet He descends among human beings in His transcendental body as an incarnation. Therefore it is very difficult for us to understand who is an incarnation. Only by His extraordinary prowess and uncommon activities, which are impossible for embodied living entities, can one partially understand the incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
text:
> yasyāvatārā jñāyante
> śarīriṣv aśarīriṇaḥ
> tais tair atulyātiśayair
> vīryair dehiṣv asaṅgataiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---whose; [[synonyms:a:avatārāḥ]]---incarnations; [[synonyms:j:jñāyante]]---can be known; [[synonyms:ś:śarīriṣu]]---among the living entities; [[synonyms:a:aśarīriṇaḥ]]---of the Lord, who has no material body; [[synonyms:t:taiḥ]] [[synonyms:t:taiḥ]]---all those; [[synonyms:a:atulya]]---incomparable; [[synonyms:a:atiśayaiḥ]]---extraordinary; [[synonyms:v:vīryaiḥ]]---by prowess; [[synonyms:d:dehiṣu]]---among the living entities; [[synonyms:a:asaṅgataiḥ]]---impossible.
translation: “ 'The Lord does not have a material body, yet He descends among human beings in His transcendental body as an incarnation. Therefore it is very difficult for us to understand who is an incarnation. Only by His extraordinary prowess and uncommon activities, which are impossible for embodied living entities, can one partially understand the incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.10.34).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.356
description: "By two symptoms-personal characteristics and marginal characteristics—the great sages can understand an object.
text:
> 'svarūpa'-lakṣaṇa, āra 'taṭastha-lakṣaṇa'
> ei dui lakṣaṇe 'vastu' jāne muni-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the personal characteristics; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:t:taṭastha]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the marginal characteristics; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇe]]---by these two symptoms; [[synonyms:v:vastu]]---an object; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---know; [[synonyms:m:muni]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the great sages.
translation: "By two symptoms-personal characteristics and marginal characteristics---the great sages can understand an object.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.357
description: "Bodily features, nature and form are the personal characteristics. Knowledge of His activities provides the marginal characteristic.
text:
> ākṛti, prakṛti, svarūpa,---svarūpa-lakṣaṇa
> kārya-dvārā jñāna,---ei taṭastha-lakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ākṛti]]---bodily features; [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]]---nature; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---form; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---personal symptoms; [[synonyms:k:kārya]]-[[synonyms:d:dvārā]]---by activities; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:t:taṭastha]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the marginal symptom.
translation: "Bodily features, nature and form are the personal characteristics. Knowledge of His activities provides the marginal characteristic.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.358
description: "In the auspicious invocation in the beginning of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Śrīla Vyāsadeva has described the Supreme Personality of Godhead by these symptoms.
text:
> bhāgavatārambhe vyāsa maṅgalācaraṇe
> 'parameśvara' nirūpila ei dui lakṣaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārambhe]]---in the beginning of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]---the great author Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:m:maṅgala]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācaraṇe]]---in the auspicious invocation; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:nirūpila]]---has described; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇe]]---by these two characteristics, namely svarūpa (personal) and taṭastha (marginal) symptoms.
translation: "In the auspicious invocation in the beginning of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Śrīla Vyāsadeva has described the Supreme Personality of Godhead by these symptoms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.359
description: " 'I offer my obeisances unto Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva, who is the supreme all-pervading Personality of Godhead. I meditate upon Him, the transcendent reality, who is the primeval cause of all causes, from whom all manifested universes arise, in whom they dwell and by whom they are destroyed. I meditate upon that eternally effulgent Lord who is directly and indirectly conscious of all manifestations and yet is beyond them. It is He only who first imparted Vedic knowledge unto the heart of Brahmā, the first created being. Through Him this world, like a mirage, appears real even to great sages and demigods. Because of Him, the material universes, created by the three modes of nature, appear factual, although they are unreal. I meditate, therefore, upon Him, the Absolute Truth, who is eternally existent in His transcendental abode and who is forever free of illusion.'
text:
> janmādy asya yato 'nvayād itarataś cārtheṣv abhijñaḥ svarāṭ
> tene brahma hṛdā ya ādi-kavaye muhyanti yat sūrayaḥ
> tejo-vāri-mṛdāṁ yathā vinimayo yatra tri-sargo 'mṛṣā
> dhāmnā svena sadā nirasta-kuhakaṁ satyaṁ paraṁ dhīmahi
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:janma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---creation, maintenance and dissolution; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of this (the universe); [[synonyms:y:yataḥ]]---from whom; [[synonyms:a:anvayāt]]---directly from the spiritual connection; [[synonyms:i:itarataḥ]]---indirectly from the lack of material contact; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:a:artheṣu]]---in all affairs; [[synonyms:a:abhijñaḥ]]---perfectly cognizant; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rāṭ]]---independent; [[synonyms:t:tene]]---imparted; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:h:hṛdā]]---through the heart; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:k:kavaye]]---unto Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:m:muhyanti]]---are bewildered; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---in whom; [[synonyms:s:sūrayaḥ]]---great personalities like Lord Brahmā and other demigods or great brāhmaṇas; [[synonyms:t:tejaḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vāri]]-[[synonyms:m:mṛdām]]---of fire, water and earth; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:v:vinimayaḥ]]---the exchange; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---in whom; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:s:sargaḥ]]---the material creation of three modes; [[synonyms:a:amṛṣā]]---factual; [[synonyms:d:dhāmnā]]---with the abode; [[synonyms:s:svena]]---His own personal; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:n:nirasta]]-[[synonyms:k:kuhakam]]---devoid of all illusion; [[synonyms:s:satyam]]---the truth; [[synonyms:p:param]]---absolute; [[synonyms:d:dhīmahi]]---let us meditate upon.
translation: “ 'I offer my obeisances unto Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva, who is the supreme all-pervading Personality of Godhead. I meditate upon Him, the transcendent reality, who is the primeval cause of all causes, from whom all manifested universes arise, in whom they dwell and by whom they are destroyed. I meditate upon that eternally effulgent Lord who is directly and indirectly conscious of all manifestations and yet is beyond them. It is He only who first imparted Vedic knowledge unto the heart of Brahmā, the first created being. Through Him this world, like a mirage, appears real even to great sages and demigods. Because of Him, the material universes, created by the three modes of nature, appear factual, although they are unreal. I meditate, therefore, upon Him, the Absolute Truth, who is eternally existent in His transcendental abode and who is forever free of illusion.'
purport: This verse, quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:1:1|(1.1.1)]], links //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// with the //Vedānta-sūtra// with the words //janmādy asya yataḥ.// It is stated that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vāsudeva, is the Absolute Truth beyond the material creation. This has been accepted by all //ācāryas.// Even Śaṅkarācārya, the most elevated impersonalist, says in the beginning of his commentary on //Bhagavad-gītā:nārāyaṇaḥ paro 'vyaktāt.// When this material creation is not yet manifested from the //mahat-tattva,// it is called //avyakta,// and when it is demonstrated from that total energy, it is called //vyakta.// Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is beyond this //vyakta-avyakta,// manifested and unmanifested material nature. This is the chief qualification of the Supreme Personality of Godhead when He assumes a particular incarnation. Kṛṣṇa tells Arjuna that they both took birth many, many times before. Kṛṣṇa remembers everything about His previous appearances, but Arjuna does not remember. Since Kṛṣṇa is beyond the cosmic creation, He is in the exalted position of being able to remember everything in the past. Everything within the cosmic creation has a material body, but Kṛṣṇa, being beyond the material cosmic creation, always has a spiritual body. He imparted Vedic knowledge into the heart of Brahmā. Although Brahmā is the most important and exalted personality within this universe, he could not remember what he did in his past life. Kṛṣṇa has to remind him through the heart. When Lord Brahmā was thus inspired, he was able to create the entire universe. Remembering everything about the past and inspiring Lord Brahmā to create are vivid examples of the characteristics called //svarūpa-lakṣaṇa// and //taṭastha-lakṣaṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.36
description: After departing from Īśāna, Sanātana Gosvāmī began traveling alone with a waterpot in his hand. Simply covered with a torn quilt, he thus lost all his anxiety.
text:
> tāre vidāya diyā gosāñi calilā ekalā
> hāte karoṅyā, chiṅḍā kānthā, nirbhaya ha-ilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāre]] [[synonyms:v:vidāya]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---bidding him farewell; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:c:calilā]] [[synonyms:e:ekalā]]---began to travel alone; [[synonyms:h:hāte]]---in the hand; [[synonyms:k:karoṅyā]]---a beggar's pot; [[synonyms:c:chiṅḍā]] [[synonyms:k:kānthā]]---a torn quilt; [[synonyms:n:nirbhaya]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---he became free from all anxiety.
translation: After departing from Īśāna, Sanātana Gosvāmī began traveling alone with a waterpot in his hand. Simply covered with a torn quilt, he thus lost all his anxiety.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.360
description: "In this invocation from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, the word param indicates Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and the word satyam indicates His personal characteristics.
text:
> ei śloke 'paraṁ'-śabde 'kṛṣṇa'-nirūpaṇa
> 'satyaṁ' śabde kahe tāṅra svarūpa-lakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloke]]---in this verse; [[synonyms:p:param]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word param, or supreme; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nirūpaṇa]]---there is an indication; [[synonyms:s:satyam]] [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word satyam, or Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---indicates; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---personal characteristics.
translation: "In this invocation from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, the word param indicates Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and the word satyam indicates His personal characteristics.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.361
description: "In that same verse it is stated that the Lord is the creator, maintainer and annihilator of the cosmic manifestation, and that He enabled Lord Brahmā to create the universe by infusing him with the knowledge of the Vedas. It is also stated that the Lord has full knowledge directly and indirectly, that He knows past, present and future and that His personal energy is separate from māyā, the illusory energy.
text:
> viśva-sṛṣṭy-ādi kaila, veda brahmāke paḍāila
> arthābhijñatā, svarūpa-śaktye māyā dūra kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viśva]]-[[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---creation, maintenance and dissolution of the cosmic manifestation; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:v:veda]]---the Vedic knowledge; [[synonyms:b:brahmāke]]---unto Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:p:paḍāila]]---instructed; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:a:abhijñatā]]---having full knowledge of past, present and future; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaktye]]---by His personal energy; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---the illusory energy; [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---separated.
translation: "In that same verse it is stated that the Lord is the creator, maintainer and annihilator of the cosmic manifestation, and that He enabled Lord Brahmā to create the universe by infusing him with the knowledge of the Vedas. It is also stated that the Lord has full knowledge directly and indirectly, that He knows past, present and future and that His personal energy is separate from māyā, the illusory energy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.362
description: "All these activities are His marginal characteristics. Great saintly persons understand the incarnations of the Supreme Personality of Godhead by the indications of the two characteristics known as svarūpa and taṭastha. All the incarnations of Kṛṣṇa should be understood in this way.
text:
> ei saba kārya---tāṅra taṭastha-lakṣaṇa
> anya avatāra aiche jāne muni-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:k:kārya]]---all these activities; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:t:taṭastha]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---marginal characteristics; [[synonyms:a:anya]] [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---another incarnation; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that same way; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---know; [[synonyms:m:muni]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the great saintly persons like Vyāsadeva.
translation: "All these activities are His marginal characteristics. Great saintly persons understand the incarnations of the Supreme Personality of Godhead by the indications of the two characteristics known as svarūpa and taṭastha. All the incarnations of Kṛṣṇa should be understood in this way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.363
description: "At the time of Their appearance, the incarnations of the Lord are known in the world because people can consult the śāstras to understand the incarnation's chief characteristics, known as svarūpa and taṭastha. In this way the incarnations become known to great saintly persons."
text:
> avatāra-kāle haya jagate gocara
> ei dui lakṣaṇe keha jānaye īśvara"
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at the time of incarnation; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:j:jagate]]---in the world; [[synonyms:g:gocara]]---information; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇe]]---by these two characteristics, namely svarūpa and taṭastha; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---some persons; [[synonyms:j:jānaye]]---know; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the incarnation of the Supreme Lord.
translation: "At the time of Their appearance, the incarnations of the Lord are known in the world because people can consult the śāstras to understand the incarnation's chief characteristics, known as svarūpa and taṭastha. In this way the incarnations become known to great saintly persons."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.364
description: Sanātana Gosvāmī, "The color of the personality in whom the characteristics of the Lord are found is yellowish. His activities include the distribution of love of Godhead and the chanting of the holy names of the Lord.
text:
> sanātana kahe,---"yāte īśvara-lakṣaṇa
> pīta-varṇa, kārya---prema-dāna-saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sanātana]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sanātana said; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---in whom; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the characteristics of the Lord are found; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇa]]---yellowish color; [[synonyms:k:kārya]]---activities; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:d:dāna]]---distributing love of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---and chanting congregationally the holy name of the Lord.
translation: Sanātana Gosvāmī, "The color of the personality in whom the characteristics of the Lord are found is yellowish. His activities include the distribution of love of Godhead and the chanting of the holy names of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.365
description: "The incarnation of Kṛṣṇa for this age is indicated by these symptoms. Please confirm this definitely so that all my doubts will go away."
text:
> kali-kāle sei 'kṛṣṇāvatāra' niścaya
> sudṛḍha kariyā kaha, yāuka saṁśaya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kali]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in the Age of Kali; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that personality; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the incarnation of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---firmly; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---kindly inform me; [[synonyms:y:yāuka]] [[synonyms:s:saṁśaya]]---so that all doubts may go away.
translation: "The incarnation of Kṛṣṇa for this age is indicated by these symptoms. Please confirm this definitely so that all my doubts will go away."
purport: Sanātana Gosvāmī wanted to confirm the fact that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the incarnation of Kṛṣṇa for this age. According to //śāstra,// in Kali-yuga the Lord would assume a golden or yellow color and would distribute love of Kṛṣṇa and the //saṅkīrtana// movement. In accordance with //śāstra// and saintly persons, these characteristics were vividly displayed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and it was therefore clear that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa. He was confirmed by the //śāstras,// and His characteristics were accepted by saintly people. Since Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu could not escape Sanātana Gosvāmī's argument, He remained silent on this point and thereby indirectly accepted Sanātana's statement. By this we can clearly understand that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was the direct incarnation of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.366
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "O Sanātana, you must give up your intelligent tricks. Just try to understand the meaning of the śaktyāveśa-avatāra.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---caturāli chāḍa, sanātana
> śaktyāveśāvatārera śuna vivarana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied; [[synonyms:c:caturāli]]---very intelligent argument; [[synonyms:c:chāḍa]]---give up; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---O Sanātana; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatārera]]---of the especially empowered incarnations; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---the description.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "O Sanātana, you must give up your intelligent tricks. Just try to understand the meaning of the śaktyāveśa-avatāra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.367
description: "There are unlimited śaktyāveśa-avatāras of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Let Me describe the chief among them.
text:
> śaktyāveśāvatāra kṛṣṇera asaṅkhya gaṇana
> dig-daraśana kari mukhya mukhya jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations especially empowered by the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:asaṅkhya]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---unlimited and innumerable; [[synonyms:d:dik]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---let Me describe some of them; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]] [[synonyms:m:mukhya]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---who are counted as the chief.
translation: "There are unlimited śaktyāveśa-avatāras of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Let Me describe the chief among them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.368
description: "Empowered incarnations are of two types-primary and secondary. The primary one is directly empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead and is called an incarnation. The secondary one is indirectly empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead and is called vibhūti.
text:
> śaktyāveśa dui-rūpa---'mukhya', 'gauṇa' dekhi
> sākṣāt-śaktye 'avatāra', ābhāse 'vibhūti' likhi
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---empowered incarnations; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---two categories; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---primary; [[synonyms:g:gauṇa]]---secondary; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---I see; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaktye]]---when there is direct power; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---they are called incarnations; [[synonyms:ā:ābhāse]]---when there is indication; [[synonyms:v:vibhūti]] [[synonyms:l:likhi]]---they are called vibhūti, or possessing special favor.
translation: "Empowered incarnations are of two types-primary and secondary. The primary one is directly empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead and is called an incarnation. The secondary one is indirectly empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead and is called vibhūti.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.369
description: "Some śaktyāveśa-avatāras are the four Kumāras, Nārada, Mahārāja Pṛthu and Paraśurāma. When a living being is empowered to act as Lord Brahmā, he is also considered a śaktyāveśa-avatāra.
text:
> 'sanakādi', 'nārada', 'pṛthu' 'paraśurāma'
> jīva-rūpa 'brahmāra' āveśāvatāra-nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sanaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the four Kumāras; [[synonyms:n:nārada]]---Nārada; [[synonyms:p:pṛthu]]---Mahārāja Pṛthu; [[synonyms:p:paraśurāma]]---Paraśurāma; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---as the living entity; [[synonyms:b:brahmāra]]---of Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---all of them are called empowered incarnations.
translation: "Some śaktyāveśa-avatāras are the four Kumāras, Nārada, Mahārāja Pṛthu and Paraśurāma. When a living being is empowered to act as Lord Brahmā, he is also considered a śaktyāveśa-avatāra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.37
description: Walking and walking, Sanātana Gosvāmī finally arrived at a place called Hājipura. That evening he sat down within a garden.
text:
> cali' cali' gosāñi tabe āilā hājipure
> sandhyā-kāle vasilā eka udyāna-bhitare
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cali']] [[synonyms:c:cali']]---walking and walking; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:h:hājipure]]---at Hājipura; [[synonyms:s:sandhyā]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in the evening; [[synonyms:v:vasilā]]---sat down; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:u:udyāna]]-[[synonyms:b:bhitare]]---within a garden.
translation: Walking and walking, Sanātana Gosvāmī finally arrived at a place called Hājipura. That evening he sat down within a garden.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.370
description: "Lord Śeṣa in the spiritual world of Vaikuṇṭha and, in the material world, Lord Ananta, who carries innumerable planets on His hood, are two primary empowered incarnations. There is no need to count the others, for they are unlimited.
text:
> vaikuṇṭhe 'śeṣa'---dharā dharaye 'ananta'
> ei mukhyāveśāvatāra---vistāre nāhi anta
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭhe]]---in the spiritual world; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]---Lord Śeṣa; [[synonyms:d:dharā]] [[synonyms:d:dharaye]]---carries innumerable planets; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---Ananta; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---primary directly empowered incarnations; [[synonyms:v:vistāre]]---in expanding them; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:a:anta]]---limit.
translation: "Lord Śeṣa in the spiritual world of Vaikuṇṭha and, in the material world, Lord Ananta, who carries innumerable planets on His hood, are two primary empowered incarnations. There is no need to count the others, for they are unlimited.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.371
description: "The power of knowledge was invested in the four Kumāras, and the power of devotional service was invested in Nārada. The power of creation was invested in Lord Brahmā, and the power to carry innumerable planets was invested in Lord Ananta.
text:
> sanakādye 'jñāna'-śakti, nārade śakti 'bhakti'
> brahmāya 'sṛṣṭi'-śakti, anante 'bhū-dhāraṇa'-śakti
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sanaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādye]]---in the four Kumāras; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---the power of knowledge; [[synonyms:n:nārade]]---in Nārada Muni; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---the power; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---of devotional service; [[synonyms:b:brahmāya]]---in Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---the power of creation; [[synonyms:a:anante]]---in Lord Ananta; [[synonyms:b:bhū]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāraṇa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---the power to carry the planets.
translation: "The power of knowledge was invested in the four Kumāras, and the power of devotional service was invested in Nārada. The power of creation was invested in Lord Brahmā, and the power to carry innumerable planets was invested in Lord Ananta.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.372
description: "The Supreme Personality of Godhead invested the power of personal service to Lord Śeṣa, and He invested the power to rule the earth in King Pṛthu. Lord Paraśurāma received the power to kill rogues and miscreants.
text:
> śeṣe 'sva-sevana'-śakti, pṛthute 'pālana'
> paraśurāme 'duṣṭa-nāśaka-vīrya-sañcāraṇa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---in Lord Śeṣa; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:s:sevana]] [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---the power to serve the Lord personally; [[synonyms:p:pṛthute]]---in King Pṛthu; [[synonyms:p:pālana]]---the power to rule; [[synonyms:p:paraśurāme]]---in Paraśurāma; [[synonyms:d:duṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśaka]]-[[synonyms:v:vīrya]]---the extraordinary power to kill rogues and miscreants; [[synonyms:s:sañcāraṇa]]---empowering.
translation: "The Supreme Personality of Godhead invested the power of personal service to Lord Śeṣa, and He invested the power to rule the earth in King Pṛthu. Lord Paraśurāma received the power to kill rogues and miscreants.
purport: Kṛṣṇa says in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:4:8|(Bg. 4.8)]]: //paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām.// Sometimes the Lord invests His power to rule in a king like Pṛthu and enables such a king to kill rogues and miscreants. He also invests His power in incarnations like Paraśurāma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.373
description: " 'Whenever the Lord is present in someone by portions of His various potencies, the living entity representing the Lord is called śaktyāveśa-avatāra—that is, an incarnation invested with special power.'
text:
> jñāna-śakty-ādi-kala yā
> yatrāviṣṭo janārdanaḥ
> ta āveśā nigadyante
> jīvā eva mahattamāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:k:kalayā]]---by portions of the potencies of knowledge, devotional service, creation, personal service, ruling over the material world, carrying the different planets, and killing the rogues and miscreants; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---wherever; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭaḥ]]---is entered; [[synonyms:j:janārdanaḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:t:te]]---they; [[synonyms:ā:āveśāḥ]]---empowered; [[synonyms:n:nigadyante]]---are called; [[synonyms:j:jīvāḥ]]---living entities; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---although; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:t:tamāḥ]]---most exalted devotees.
translation: “ 'Whenever the Lord is present in someone by portions of His various potencies, the living entity representing the Lord is called śaktyāveśa-avatāra---that is, an incarnation invested with special power.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta// (1.18).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.374
description: "As explained in the Eleventh Chapter of Bhagavad-gītā, Kṛṣṇa has spread Himself all over the universe in many personalities through specific powers, known as vibhūti.
text:
> 'vibhūti' kahiye yaiche gītā-ekādaśe
> jagat vyāpila kṛṣṇa-śakty-ābhāsāveśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vibhūti]]---specific power; [[synonyms:k:kahiye]]---we say; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just like; [[synonyms:g:gītā]]---of Bhagavad-gītā; [[synonyms:e:ekādaśe]]---in the Eleventh Chapter; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---throughout the whole universe; [[synonyms:v:vyāpila]]---He expanded; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---by the reflection of His power.
translation: "As explained in the Eleventh Chapter of Bhagavad-gītā, Kṛṣṇa has spread Himself all over the universe in many personalities through specific powers, known as vibhūti.
purport: The expansion of specific //māyā// powers is explained in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:7:39|(2.7.39)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.375
description: " 'Know that all beautiful, glorious and mighty creations spring but from a spark of My splendor.
text:
> yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṁ
> śrīmad ūrjitam eva vā
> tat tad evāvagaccha tvaṁ
> mama tejo 'ṁśa-sambhavam
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yat]] [[synonyms:y:yat]]---whatever and wherever; [[synonyms:v:vibhūtimat]]---extraordinarily opulent; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:t:tvam]]---living entity; [[synonyms:ś:śrīmat]]---full of wealth; [[synonyms:ū:ūrjitam]]---full of power; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:t:tat]] [[synonyms:t:tat]]---there; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:avagaccha]]---should know; [[synonyms:t:tvam]]---you; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---of Me; [[synonyms:t:tejaḥ]]---of power; [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---of a part; [[synonyms:s:sambhavam]]---exhibition.
translation: “ 'Know that all beautiful, glorious and mighty creations spring but from a spark of My splendor.
purport: This is a statement made by Kṛṣṇa in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:10:41|(Bg. 10.41)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.376
description: " 'But what need is there, Arjuna, for all this detailed knowledge? With a single fragment of Myself I pervade and support this entire universe.'
text:
> athavā bahunaitena
> kiṁ jñātena tavārjuna
> viṣṭabhyāham idaṁ kṛtsnam
> ekāṁśena sthito jagat
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:athavā]]---or; [[synonyms:b:bahunā]]---much; [[synonyms:e:etena]]---with this; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what use; [[synonyms:j:jñātena]]---being known; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---by you; [[synonyms:a:arjuna]]---O Arjuna; [[synonyms:v:viṣṭabhya]]---pervading; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kṛtsnam]]---entire; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁśena]]---with one portion; [[synonyms:s:sthitaḥ]]---situated; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---universe.
translation: “ 'But what need is there, Arjuna, for all this detailed knowledge? With a single fragment of Myself I pervade and support this entire universe.'
purport: This is also a statement made by Kṛṣṇa in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:10:42|(Bg. 10.42)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.377
description: "Thus I have explained specifically empowered incarnations. Now please hear about the characteristics of Lord Kṛṣṇa's childhood, boyhood and youth.
text:
> eita kahiluṅ śakty-āveśa-avatāra
> bālya-paugaṇḍa-dharmera śunaha vicāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eita]]---thus; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have explained; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---the incarnations specifically empowered; [[synonyms:b:bālya]]---in childhood; [[synonyms:p:paugaṇḍa]]---in boyhood; [[synonyms:d:dharmera]]---of the characteristics; [[synonyms:ś:śunaha]]---now hear; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---the consideration.
translation: "Thus I have explained specifically empowered incarnations. Now please hear about the characteristics of Lord Kṛṣṇa's childhood, boyhood and youth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.378
description: "As the son of Mahārāja Nanda, Lord Kṛṣṇa is by nature the paragon of kiśora [youth]. He chooses to exhibit His pastimes at that age.
text:
> kiśora-śekhara-dharmī vrajendra-nandana
> prakaṭa-līlā karibāre yabe kare mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kiśora]]-[[synonyms:ś:śekhara]]---topmost of youth; [[synonyms:d:dharmī]]---whose natural position; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of Mahārāja Nanda; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---manifested pastimes; [[synonyms:k:karibāre]]---to perform; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---makes; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind.
translation: "As the son of Mahārāja Nanda, Lord Kṛṣṇa is by nature the paragon of kiśora [youth]. He chooses to exhibit His pastimes at that age.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.379
description: "Before His personal appearance, the Lord causes some of His devotees to appear as His mother, father and intimate associates. He then appears later as if He were taking birth and growing from a baby to a child and gradually into a youth.
text:
> ādau prakaṭa karāya mātā-pita---bhakta-gaṇe
> pāche prakaṭa haya janmādika-līlā-krame
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ādau]]---first; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭa]]---manifest; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---He makes; [[synonyms:m:mātā]]-[[synonyms:p:pitā]]---His mother and father; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---similar devotees; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---after that; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭa]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes manifest; [[synonyms:j:janma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādika]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:k:krame]]---such pastimes as birth, in order.
translation: "Before His personal appearance, the Lord causes some of His devotees to appear as His mother, father and intimate associates. He then appears later as if He were taking birth and growing from a baby to a child and gradually into a youth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.38
description: In Hājipura there was a gentlemen named Śrīkānta, who happened to be the husband of Sanātana Gosvāmī's sister. He was engaged there in government service.
text:
> sei hājipure rahe---śrīkānta tāra nāma
> gosāñira bhaginī-pati, kare rāja-kāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:h:hājipure]]---in Hājipura; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---there is; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kānta]]---Śrīkānta; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---name; [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:b:bhaginī]]-[[synonyms:p:pati]]---sister's husband; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---executes; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:k:kāma]]---government service.
translation: In Hājipura there was a gentlemen named Śrīkānta, who happened to be the husband of Sanātana Gosvāmī's sister. He was engaged there in government service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.380
description: " 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead is eternally enjoying Himself, and He is the shelter of all kinds of devotional service. Although His ages are various, His age known as kiśora [pre-youth] is best of all.'
text:
> vayaso vividhatve 'pi
> sarva-bhakti-rasāśrayaḥ
> dharmī kiśora evātra
> nitya-līlā-vilāsa vān
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vayasaḥ]]---of age; [[synonyms:v:vividhatve]]---in varieties; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---of all kinds; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśrayaḥ]]---the shelter of devotional service; [[synonyms:d:dharmī]]---whose constitutional nature; [[synonyms:k:kiśoraḥ]]---in the age before youth; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:atra]]---in this; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---of eternal pastimes; [[synonyms:v:vilāsavān]]---the supreme enjoyer.
translation: “ 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead is eternally enjoying Himself, and He is the shelter of all kinds of devotional service. Although His ages are various, His age known as kiśora [pre-youth] is best of all.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (2.1.63).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.381
description: "When Lord Kṛṣṇa appears, from moment to moment He exhibits His different pastimes, beginning with the killing of Pūtanā. All these pastimes are eternally being demonstrated one after another.
text:
> pūtanā-vadhādi yata līlā kṣaṇe kṣaṇe
> saba līlā nitya prakaṭa kare anukrame
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūtanā]]-[[synonyms:v:vadha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---killing of the demons like Pūtanā; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]] [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---one moment after another; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---all these pastimes; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---eternally; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭa]]---manifesting; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:a:anukrame]]---one after another.
translation: "When Lord Kṛṣṇa appears, from moment to moment He exhibits His different pastimes, beginning with the killing of Pūtanā. All these pastimes are eternally being demonstrated one after another.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.382
description: "The consecutive pastimes of Kṛṣṇa are manifest in one of the innumerable universes moment after moment. There is no possibility of counting the universes, but in any case some pastime of the Lord is being manifest at every moment in one universe or another.
text:
> ananta brahmāṇḍa, tāra nāhika gaṇana
> kona līlā kona brahmāṇḍe haya prakaṭana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]---innumerable universes; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---there is no counting; [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---some pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍe]]---in some universe; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭana]]---manifestation.
translation: "The consecutive pastimes of Kṛṣṇa are manifest in one of the innumerable universes moment after moment. There is no possibility of counting the universes, but in any case some pastime of the Lord is being manifest at every moment in one universe or another.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.383
description: "Thus the Lord's pastimes are like flowing Ganges water. In this way all the pastimes are manifested by the son of Nanda Mahārāja.
text:
> ei-mata saba līlā---yena gaṅgā-dhāra
> se-se līlā prakaṭa kare vrajendra-kumāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---all pastimes; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---like; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---the flowing of the water of the Ganges; [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:s:se]]---those; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭa]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---demonstrates; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:k:kumāra]]---the son of Mahārāja Nanda.
translation: "Thus the Lord's pastimes are like flowing Ganges water. In this way all the pastimes are manifested by the son of Nanda Mahārāja.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.384
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa exhibits His pastimes of childhood, boyhood and pre-youth. When He reaches pre-youth, He continues to exist eternally to perform His rāsa dance and other pastimes.
text:
> krame bālya-paugaṇḍa-kaiśoratā-prāpti
> rāsa-ādi līlā kare, kaiśore nitya-sthiti
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:krame]]---gradually; [[synonyms:b:bālya]]---childhood; [[synonyms:p:paugaṇḍa]]---boyhood; [[synonyms:k:kaiśoratā]]---youth; [[synonyms:p:prāpti]]---development; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]---dancing with the gopīs; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and others; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:k:kaiśore]]---in His age of pre-youth; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]-[[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---eternally existing.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa exhibits His pastimes of childhood, boyhood and pre-youth. When He reaches pre-youth, He continues to exist eternally to perform His rāsa dance and other pastimes.
purport:
The comparison made here is very interesting. Kṛṣṇa does not grow like an ordinary human being, even though He exhibits His pastimes of childhood, boyhood and pre-youth. When He reaches the age of pre-youth, //kaiśora,// He does not grow any older. He simply remains in His //kaiśora// age. He is therefore described in the //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.33) as //nava-yauvana.//

> advaitam acyutam anādim ananta-rūpam
> ādyaṁ purāṇa-puruṣaṁ nava-yauvanaṁ ca
> vedeṣu durlabham adurlabham ātma-bhaktau
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi

This //nava-yauvana,// or pre-youth, is the eternal transcendental form of Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa never grows older than //nava-yauvana.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.385
description: "Descriptions of Kṛṣṇa's eternal pastimes are in all revealed scriptures. But one cannot understand how they are continuing eternally.
text:
> 'nitya-līlā' kṛṣṇera sarva-śāstre kaya
> bujhite nā pāre līlā kemane 'nitya' haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nitya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---eternal pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstre]] [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---described in every śāstra; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---not able to understand; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kemane]]---how; [[synonyms:n:nitya]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are eternal.
translation: "Descriptions of Kṛṣṇa's eternal pastimes are in all revealed scriptures. But one cannot understand how they are continuing eternally.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.386
description: "Let me give an example by which people may understand Lord Kṛṣṇa's eternal pastimes. An example can be found in the zodiac.
text:
> dṛṣṭānta diyā kahi tabe loka yadi jāne
> kṛṣṇa-līlā---nitya, jyotiścakra-pramāṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dṛṣṭānta]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving an example; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---let Me say; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---can understand; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---eternal; [[synonyms:j:jyotiḥ]]-[[synonyms:c:cakra]]---of the zodiac; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇe]]---by evidence.
translation: "Let me give an example by which people may understand Lord Kṛṣṇa's eternal pastimes. An example can be found in the zodiac.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.387
description: "The sun moves across the zodiac day and night and crosses the oceans between the seven islands one after the other.
text:
> jyotiścakre sūrya yena phire rātri-dine
> sapta-dvīpāmbudhi laṅghi' phire krame krame
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jyotiḥ]]-[[synonyms:c:cakre]]---in the zodiac; [[synonyms:s:sūrya]]---of the sun; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as; [[synonyms:p:phire]]---moves; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---the day and night; [[synonyms:s:sapta]]-[[synonyms:d:dvīpa]]-[[synonyms:a:ambudhi]]---the oceans of the islands; [[synonyms:l:laṅghi']]---crossing; [[synonyms:p:phire]]---rotates; [[synonyms:k:krame]] [[synonyms:k:krame]]---one after another.
translation: "The sun moves across the zodiac day and night and crosses the oceans between the seven islands one after the other.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.388
description: "According to Vedic astronomical calculations, the rotation of the sun consists of sixty daṇḍas, and it is divided into thirty-six hundred palas.
text:
> rātri-dine haya ṣaṣṭi-daṇḍa-parimāṇa
> tina-sahasra chaya-śata 'pala' tāra māna
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---during the whole day and night; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṣṭi]]-[[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---of sixty daṇḍas (a measure of time); [[synonyms:p:parimāṇa]]---duration; [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:s:sahasra]]---three thousand; [[synonyms:c:chaya]]-[[synonyms:ś:śata]]---six hundred; [[synonyms:p:pala]]---palas; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:m:māna]]---measurement.
translation: "According to Vedic astronomical calculations, the rotation of the sun consists of sixty daṇḍas, and it is divided into thirty-six hundred palas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.389
description: "The sun rises in steps consisting of sixty palas. Sixty palas equal one daṇḍa, and eight daṇḍas comprise one prahara.
text:
> sūryodaya haite ṣaṣṭi-pala-kramodaya
> sei eka daṇḍa, aṣṭa daṇḍe 'prahara' haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sūrya]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---beginning from the sunrise; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṣṭi]]-[[synonyms:p:pala]]---sixty palas; [[synonyms:k:krama]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]]---gradually rising higher and higher; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---one daṇḍa; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]] [[synonyms:d:daṇḍe]]---in eight daṇḍas; [[synonyms:p:prahara]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is a prahara.
translation: "The sun rises in steps consisting of sixty palas. Sixty palas equal one daṇḍa, and eight daṇḍas comprise one prahara.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.39
description: Śrīkānta had 300,000 gold coins with him, which had been given to him by the emperor for the purchase of horses. Thus Śrīkānta was buying horses and dispatching them to the emperor.
text:
> tina lakṣa mudrā rājā diyāche tāra sthāne
> ghoḍā mūlya lañā pāṭhāya pātsāra sthāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---300,000; [[synonyms:m:mudrā]]---golden coins; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the king or nawab; [[synonyms:d:diyāche]]---has given; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in his custody; [[synonyms:g:ghoḍā]]---of horses; [[synonyms:m:mūlya]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking the price; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāya]]---sends; [[synonyms:p:pātsāra]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the care of the emperor.
translation: Śrīkānta had 300,000 gold coins with him, which had been given to him by the emperor for the purchase of horses. Thus Śrīkānta was buying horses and dispatching them to the emperor.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.390
description: "Day and night are divided into eight praharas-four belonging to the day and four belonging to the night. After eight praharas, the sun rises again.
text:
> eka-dui-tina-cāri prahare asta haya
> cāri-prahara rātri gele punaḥ sūryodaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:c:cāri]]---one, two, three, four; [[synonyms:p:prahare]]---in praharas; [[synonyms:a:asta]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---the sun sets in the evening; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:p:prahara]]---generally after four praharas; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]---the night; [[synonyms:g:gele]]---when it passes; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:s:sūryodaya]]---the sun rises.
translation: "Day and night are divided into eight praharas-four belonging to the day and four belonging to the night. After eight praharas, the sun rises again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.391
description: "Just like the sun, there is an orbit to Kṛṣṇa's pastimes, which are manifest one after the other. During the lifetime of fourteen Manus, this orbit expands through all the universes, and gradually it returns. Thus Kṛṣṇa moves with His pastimes through all the universes, one after another.
text:
> aiche kṛṣṇera līlā-maṇḍala caudda-manvantare
> brahmāṇḍa-maṇḍala vyāpi' krame krame phire
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in the same way; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇḍala]]---groups of different pastimes; [[synonyms:c:caudda]]-[[synonyms:m:manvantare]]---in the duration of fourteen Manus; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇḍala]]---all of the universes; [[synonyms:v:vyāpi']]---spreading through; [[synonyms:k:krame]] [[synonyms:k:krame]]---gradually; [[synonyms:p:phire]]---return.
translation: "Just like the sun, there is an orbit to Kṛṣṇa's pastimes, which are manifest one after the other. During the lifetime of fourteen Manus, this orbit expands through all the universes, and gradually it returns. Thus Kṛṣṇa moves with His pastimes through all the universes, one after another.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.392
description: "Kṛṣṇa remains within a universe for 125 years, and He enjoys His pastimes both in Vṛndāvana and Dvārakā.
text:
> saoyāśata vatsara kṛṣṇera prakaṭa-prakāśa
> tāhā yaiche vraja-pure karilā vilāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saoyāśata]]---125; [[synonyms:v:vatsara]]---years; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭa]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---manifestation of the appearance; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---like; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:p:pure]]---in Vṛndāvana and Dvārakā; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---enjoys the pastimes.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa remains within a universe for 125 years, and He enjoys His pastimes both in Vṛndāvana and Dvārakā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.393
description: "The cycle of His pastimes turns like a wheel of fire. Thus Kṛṣṇa exhibits His pastimes one after the other in every universe.
text:
> alāta-cakra-prāya sei līlā-cakra phire
> saba līlā saba brahmāṇḍe krame udaya kare
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:alāta]]-[[synonyms:c:cakra]]-[[synonyms:p:prāya]]---exactly like a wheel of fire; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:c:cakra]]---the cycle of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes; [[synonyms:p:phire]]---turns; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---all these pastimes; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍe]]---in all the universes; [[synonyms:k:krame]]---one after another; [[synonyms:u:udaya]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---become manifest.
translation: "The cycle of His pastimes turns like a wheel of fire. Thus Kṛṣṇa exhibits His pastimes one after the other in every universe.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.394
description: "Kṛṣṇa's pastimes-appearance, childhood, boyhood and youth-are all manifest, beginning with the killing of Pūtanā and extending to the end of mauṣala-līlā, the annihilation of the Yadu dynasty. All of these pastimes are rotating in every universe.
text:
> janma, bālya, paugaṇḍa, kaiśora prakāśa
> pūtanā-vadhādi kari' mauṣalānta vilāsa

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.397
description: "The eternal pastimes of Kṛṣṇa are continuously taking place in the original Goloka Vṛndāvana planet. These same pastimes are gradually manifest within the material world, in each and every brahmāṇḍa.
text:
> ataeva goloka-sthāne nitya vihāra
> brahmāṇḍa-gaṇe krame prākaṭya tāhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:g:goloka]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in the original Goloka Vṛndāvana planet; [[synonyms:n:nitya]] [[synonyms:v:vihāra]]---eternal pastimes; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---within the material universes; [[synonyms:k:krame]]---gradually; [[synonyms:p:prākaṭya]]---manifestation; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---of them.
translation: "The eternal pastimes of Kṛṣṇa are continuously taking place in the original Goloka Vṛndāvana planet. These same pastimes are gradually manifest within the material world, in each and every brahmāṇḍa.
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura elucidates this complicated explanation of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes. Kṛṣṇa's pastimes are always present in the material world in one of the many universes. These pastimes appear in the universes one after the other, just as the sun moves across the sky and measures the time. Kṛṣṇa's appearance may be manifest in this universe at one moment, and immediately after His birth, this pastime is manifest in the next universe. After His killing of Pūtanā is manifest in this universe, it is next manifest in another universe. Thus all the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa are eternally existing both in the original Goloka Vṛndāvana planet and in the material universes. The 125 years calculated in our solar system to be Kṛṣṇa's lifetime equal one moment for Kṛṣṇa. One moment these pastimes are manifest in one universe, and the next moment they are manifest in the next universe. There are unlimited universes, and Kṛṣṇa's pastimes are manifest one moment after the other in all of them. This rotation is explained through the example of the sun's moving across the sky. Kṛṣṇa appears and disappears in innumerable universes, just as the sun appears and disappears during the day. Although the sun appears to rise and set, it is continuously shining somewhere on the earth. Although Kṛṣṇa's pastimes seem to appear and disappear, they are continuously existing in one //brahmāṇḍa// (universe) or another. Thus all of Kṛṣṇa's //līlās// are present simultaneously throughout the innumerable universes. By our limited senses we cannot appreciate this; therefore Kṛṣṇa's eternal pastimes are very difficult for us to understand. One should try to understand how they are taking place by understanding the allegory of the sun. Although the Lord is appearing constantly in the material universes, His pastimes are eternally present in the original Goloka Vṛndāvana. Therefore these pastimes are called //nitya-līlā// (eternally present pastimes). Because we cannot see what is going on in other universes, it is a little difficult for us to understand how Kṛṣṇa is eternally manifesting His pastimes. There are fourteen Manus in one day of Brahmā, and this time calculation is also taking place in other universes. Kṛṣṇa's pastimes are manifest before fourteen Manus expire. Although it is a little difficult to understand the eternal pastimes of Kṛṣṇa in this way, we must accept the verdict of Vedic literatures.

There are two types of devotees---the //sādhaka,// who is preparing for perfection, and the //siddha,// who is already perfect. As far as those who are already perfect are concerned, //Bhagavad-gītā// says, //tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so 'rjuna:// "After giving up this material body, such a devotee comes to Me." After leaving the material body, the perfect devotee takes birth in the womb of a //gopī// on a planet where Kṛṣṇa's pastimes are going on. This may be in this universe or another universe. This statement is found in the //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi,// which is commented upon by Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura. When a devotee becomes perfect, he is transferred to the universe where Kṛṣṇa's pastimes are taking place. Kṛṣṇa's eternal associates go wherever Kṛṣṇa manifests His pastimes. As stated before, first the father and mother of Kṛṣṇa appear, then the other associates. Quitting his material body, the perfect devotee also goes to associate with Kṛṣṇa and His other associates.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.398

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.400

When all the qualities are manifest, but not fully, He is called more complete. When He manifests all His qualities in fullness, He is called most complete. This is the version of all learned scholars in the devotional science.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.57
description: " 'Saints of your caliber are themselves places of pilgrimage. Because of their purity, they are constant companions of the Lord, and therefore they can purify even the places of pilgrimage.'
text:
> bhavad-vidhā bhāgavatās
> tīrtha-bhūtāḥ svayaṁ prabho
> tīrthī-kurvanti tīrthāni
> svāntaḥ-sthena gadā-bhṛtā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhavat]]-[[synonyms:v:vidhāḥ]]---like you; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavatāḥ]]---advanced devotees; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūtāḥ]]---personified holy places of pilgrimage; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---personally; [[synonyms:p:prabho]]---my lord; [[synonyms:t:tīrthī]]-[[synonyms:k:kurvanti]]---make into holy places; [[synonyms:t:tīrthāni]]---all the holy places of pilgrimage; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:sthena]]---situated within their hearts; [[synonyms:g:gadā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhṛtā]]---by Lord Viṣṇu, who carries a club.
translation: “ 'Saints of your caliber are themselves places of pilgrimage. Because of their purity, they are constant companions of the Lord, and therefore they can purify even the places of pilgrimage.'
purport:
This verse was spoken by Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira to Vidura in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:13:10|(1.13.10)]]. Vidura was returning home after visiting sacred places of pilgrimage, and Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira was receiving his saintly uncle. In essence, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira was saying, "My dear Lord Vidura, you yourself are a holy place because you are an advanced devotee. People like you always carry Lord Viṣṇu in their hearts. You can revitalize all holy places after they have been polluted by the pilgrimages of sinners."

A sinful person goes to a holy place of pilgrimage to be purified. In a holy place, there are many saintly people and temples of Lord Viṣṇu; however, the holy place becomes infected with the sins of many visitors. When an advanced devotee goes to a holy place, he counteracts all the sins of the pilgrims. Therefore Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira addressed Vidura in this way.

Since an advanced devotee carries Lord Viṣṇu within his heart, he is a moving temple and a moving Viṣṇu. An advanced devotee does not need to go to holy places, for wherever he stays is a holy place. In this connection, Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura states, //tīrtha-yātrā pariśrama, kevala manera bhrama:// visiting holy places is simply another type of bewilderment. Since an advanced devotee does not need to go to a holy place, why does he go? The answer is that he goes simply to purify the place.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.58
description: " 'Even though a person is a very learned scholar of the Sanskrit Vedic literatures, he is not accepted as My devotee unless he is pure in devotional service. However, even though a person is born in a family of dog-eaters, he is very dear to Me if he is a pure devotee who has no motive to enjoy fruitive activity or mental speculation. Indeed, all respects should be given to him, and whatever he offers should be accepted. Such devotees are as worshipable as I am.'

translation: “ 'Even though a person is a very learned scholar of the Sanskrit Vedic literatures, he is not accepted as My devotee unless he is pure in devotional service. However, even though a person is born in a family of dog-eaters, he is very dear to Me if he is a pure devotee who has no motive to enjoy fruitive activity or mental speculation. Indeed, all respects should be given to him, and whatever he offers should be accepted. Such devotees are as worshipable as I am.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.59
description: " 'One may be born in a brāhmaṇa family and have all twelve brahminical qualities, but if he is not devoted to the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, who has a navel shaped like a lotus, he is not as good as a caṇḍāla who has dedicated his mind, words, activities, wealth and life to the service of the Lord. Simply to take birth in a brāhmaṇa family or to have brahminical qualities is not sufficient. One must become a pure devotee of the Lord. If a śva-paca or caṇḍāla is a devotee, he delivers not only himself but his whole family, whereas a brāhmaṇa who is not a devotee but simply has brahminical qualifications cannot even purify himself, not to speak of his family.' "
text:

translation: “ 'One may be born in a brāhmaṇa family and have all twelve brahminical qualities, but if he is not devoted to the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, who has a navel shaped like a lotus, he is not as good as a caṇḍāla who has dedicated his mind, words, activities, wealth and life to the service of the Lord. Simply to take birth in a brāhmaṇa family or to have brahminical qualities is not sufficient. One must become a pure devotee of the Lord. If a śva-paca or caṇḍāla is a devotee, he delivers not only himself but his whole family, whereas a brāhmaṇa who is not a devotee but simply has brahminical qualifications cannot even purify himself, not to speak of his family.' "
purport:
This verse is spoken by Prahlāda Mahārāja in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:7:9:10|(7.9.10)]]. A //brāhmaṇa// is supposed to be qualified with twelve qualities. As stated in the //Mahābhārata://

> dharmaś ca satyaṁ ca damas tapaś ca
> amātsaryaṁ hrīs titikṣānasūyā
> yajñaś ca dānaṁ ca dhṛtiḥ śrutaṁ ca
> vratāni vai dvādaśa brāhmaṇasya

"A //brāhmaṇa// must be perfectly religious. He must be truthful, and he must be able to control his senses. He must execute severe austerities, and he must be detached, humble and tolerant. He must not envy anyone, and he must be expert in performing sacrifices and giving whatever he has in charity. He must be fixed in devotional service and expert in the knowledge of the //Vedas.// These are the twelve qualifications for a //brāhmaṇa."//

Bhagavad-gītā describes the brahminical qualities in this way:

> śamo damas tapaḥ śaucam
> kṣāntir ārjavam eva ca
> jñānaṁ vijñānam āstikyaṁ
> brahma-karma svabhāva-jam

"Peacefulness, self-control, austerity, purity, tolerance, honesty, wisdom, knowledge, and religiousness---these are the qualities by which the //brāhmaṇas// work." [[books:bg:18:42|(Bg. 18.42)]]

In the //Muktāphala-ṭīkā,// it is said:

> śamo damas tapaḥ śaucaṁ
> kṣānty-ārjava-virakta yaḥ
> jñāna-vijñāna-santoṣāḥ
> satyāstikye dviṣaḍ guṇāḥ

"Mental equilibrium, sense control, austerity, cleanliness, tolerance, simplicity, detachment, theoretical and practical knowledge, satisfaction, truthfulness and firm faith in the //Vedas// are the twelve qualities of a //brāhmaṇa."//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.6
description: "If one releases a conditioned soul or imprisoned person according to religious principles, he himself is also released from material bondage by the Supreme Personality of Godhead."
text:
> eka bandī chāḍe yadi nija-dharma dekhiyā
> saṁsāra ha-ite tāre mukta karena gosāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:b:bandī]]---one imprisoned person; [[synonyms:c:chāḍe]]---one releases; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---one's own religion; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---consulting; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---from material bondage; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---him; [[synonyms:m:mukta]] [[synonyms:k:karena]]---releases; [[synonyms:g:gosāñā]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: "If one releases a conditioned soul or imprisoned person according to religious principles, he himself is also released from material bondage by the Supreme Personality of Godhead."
purport:
It appears from this statement that Sanātana Gosvāmī, who was formerly a minister of the Nawab, was trying to cheat the Mohammedan superintendent. A jail superintendent had only an ordinary education, or practically no education, and he was certainly not supposed to be very advanced in spiritual knowledge. However, just to satisfy him, Sanātana Gosvāmī praised him as a very learned scholar of the scriptures. The jailkeeper could not deny that he was a learned scholar because when one is elevated to an exalted position, one thinks oneself fit for that position. Sanātana Gosvāmī was correctly explaining the effects of spiritual activity, and the jailkeeper connected his statement with his release from jail. There are innumerable conditioned souls rotting in the material world, imprisoned by //māyā// under the spell of sense gratification. The living entity is so entranced by the spell of //māyā// that in conditioned life even a pig feels satisfied.

There are two kinds of covering powers exhibited by //māyā.// One is called //prakṣepātmikā,// and the other is called //āvaraṇātmikā.// When one is determined to get out of material bondage, the //prakṣepātmikā-śakti,// the spell of diversion, impels one to remain in conditioned life fully satisfied by sense gratification. Due to the other power (//āvaraṇātmikā),// a conditioned soul feels satisfied even if he is rotting in the body of a pig or a worm in stool. To release a conditioned soul from material bondage is very difficult because the spell of //māyā// is so strong. Even when the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself descends to deliver conditioned souls, asking them to surrender unto Him, the conditioned souls do not agree to the Lord's proposals. Therefore Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī said, "Somehow or other, if one helps another gain release from the bondage of //māyā,// he is certainly recognized immediately by the Supreme Personality of Godhead." As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:18:69|(Bg. 18.69)]]:

> na ca tasmān manuṣyeṣu
> kaścin me priya-kṛttamaḥ
> bhavitā na ca me tasmād
> anyaḥ priyataro bhuvi

The greatest service one can render to the Lord is to try to infuse devotional service into the heart of the conditioned soul so that the conditioned soul may be released from conditional life. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has said that a Vaiṣṇava is recognized by his preaching work---that is, by convincing the conditioned soul about his eternal position, which is explained here as //nija-dharma.// It is the living entity's eternal position to serve the Lord; therefore to help one get release from material bondage is to awaken one to the dormant understanding that he is the eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa. //jīvera 'svarūpa' haya-kṛṣṇera 'nitya-dāsa'.// This will be further explained by the Lord Himself to Sanātana Gosvāmī.

purport: This is confirmed in the following verse from the //Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya// (13.2).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.61
description: " 'My dear Vaiṣṇava, seeing a person like you is the perfection of one's eyesight. Touching your lotus feet is the perfection of the sense of touch. Glorifying your good qualities is the tongue's real activity, for in the material world it is very difficult to find a pure devotee of the Lord.' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.63
description: "My dear Sanātana, Kṛṣṇa has saved you from Mahāraurava, life's deepest hell. He is an ocean of mercy, and His activities are very grave."
text:
> mahā-raurava haite tomā karilā uddhāra
> kṛpāra samudra kṛṣṇa gambhīra apāra"
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:r:raurava]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the deepest hellish condition of life; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]---you; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:u:uddhāra]]---has delivered; [[synonyms:k:kṛpāra]] [[synonyms:s:samudra]]---the ocean of mercy; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gambhīra]]---very grave; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimitedly.
translation: "My dear Sanātana, Kṛṣṇa has saved you from Mahāraurava, life's deepest hell. He is an ocean of mercy, and His activities are very grave."
purport: As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā, īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ hṛd-deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati.// Staying within everyone's heart, Lord Kṛṣṇa works very gravely. No one can understand how He is working, but as soon as the Lord understands the sincere activity of a person in devotional service, He helps him in such a way that the devotee cannot understand how things are happening. If the devotee is determined to serve the Lord, the Lord is always prepared to help him (//dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ yena mām upayānti te).// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is telling Sanātana Gosvāmī how merciful the Lord is. Sanātana Gosvāmī was a minister in the service of Nawab Hussain Shah. He was always mixing with people materially inclined, particularly with Mohammedans, meat-eaters. Although he was in intimate touch with them, by Kṛṣṇa's mercy he came to find such association distasteful. Therefore he left them. As stated by Śrīnivāsa Ācārya: //tyaktvā tūrṇam aśeṣa-man-dala-pati-śreṇīṁ sadā tuccha-vat.// Kṛṣṇa enlightened Sanātana Gosvāmī in such a way that he was able to give up his exalted post as minister. Thinking his material position insignificant, Sanātana was prepared to become a mendicant. Appreciating the activities of Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu praised his action and thanked Kṛṣṇa for His mercy upon him.

translation: Sanātana replied, "I do not know who Kṛṣṇa is. As far as I am concerned, I have been released from prison only by Your mercy."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.70
description: Candraśekhara then made Sanātana Gosvāmī look like a gentleman. He took him to bathe in the Ganges, and afterwards he brought him a new set of clothes.
text:

> śekhara āniyā tāṅre nūtana vastra dila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhadra]] [[synonyms:k:karāñā]]---making gentle; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing in the Ganges; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---caused to do; [[synonyms:ś:śekhara]]---Candraśekhara; [[synonyms:ā:āniyā]]---bringing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to him; [[synonyms:n:nūtana]]---new; [[synonyms:v:vastra]]---clothing; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---delivered.
translation: Candraśekhara then made Sanātana Gosvāmī look like a gentleman. He took him to bathe in the Ganges, and afterwards he brought him a new set of clothes.
purport: The words //bhadra karāñā// are significant in this verse. Due to his long hair, moustache and beard, Sanātana Gosvāmī looked like a //daraveśa,// or hippie. Since Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not like Sanātana Gosvāmī's hippie features, he immediately asked Candraśekhara to get him shaved clean. If anyone with long hair or a beard wants to join this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement and live with us, he must similarly shave himself clean. The followers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu consider long hair objectionable. Sanātana Gosvāmī was saved from a hellish condition (Mahāraurava) by the grace of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Mahāraurava is a hell wherein animal killers are placed. In this regard, refer to //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (5.26.10-12).
