title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.81
description: Sanātana replied, "I shall practice the process of mādhukarī. Why should I accept full meals in the house of a brāhmaṇa?"
text:
> sanātana kahe,---"āmi mādhukarī kariba
> brāhmaṇera ghare kene ekatra bhikṣā laba?"
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sanātana]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sanātana replied; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:m:mādhukarī]] [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---shall practice acceptance of food by mādhukarī means; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇera]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in the house of a brāhmaṇa; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]]---in one place; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:l:laba]]---I should accept lunch.
translation: Sanātana replied, "I shall practice the process of mādhukarī. Why should I accept full meals in the house of a brāhmaṇa?"
purport:
The word //mādhukarī// comes from the word //madhukara,// which refers to bees collecting honey from flower to flower. A //mādhukarī// is a saintly person or a mendicant who does not accept a full meal at one house but begs from door to door, taking a little food from each householder's place. In this way he does not overeat or give householders unnecessary trouble. A person in the renounced order may beg but not cook. His begging should not be a burden for the householders. The //mādhukarī// process is strictly to be followed by a //bābājī,// that is, one who has attained the //paramahaṁsa// stage. This practice is still current in Vṛndāvana, and there are many places where alms are offered. Unfortunately, there are many beggars who have come to Vṛndāvana to accept alms but not follow the principles of Sanātana Gosvāmī. People try to imitate him and lead an idle life by practicing //mādhukarī.// It is almost impossible to strictly follow Sanātana Gosvāmī or Rūpa Gosvāmī. It is better to accept food offered to Kṛṣṇa in the temple than to try to imitate Sanātana Gosvāmī and Rūpa Gosvāmī.

> yuktāhāra-vihārasya
> yukta-ceṣṭasya karmasu
> yukta-svapnāvabodhasya
> yogo bhavati duḥkha-hā

"He who is temperate in his habits of eating, sleeping, working and recreation can mitigate all material pains by practicing the //yoga// system." [[books:bg:6:17|(Bg. 6.17)]]

The ideal //sannyāsī// strictly follows the ways practiced by the Gosvāmīs.

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "I have already deliberately considered this matter. Since Lord Kṛṣṇa is very merciful, He has nullified your attachment for material things. Why should Kṛṣṇa allow you to maintain a last bit of material attachment? After vanquishing a disease, a good physician does not allow any of the disease to remain.

translation: "It is contradictory to practice mādhukarī and at the same time wear a valuable blanket. One loses his spiritual strength by doing this, and one will also become an object for jokes."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.93

> gosāñi kahe,---'ye khaṇḍila kuviṣaya-bhoga

translation: Sanātana Gosvāmī replied, "The Supreme Personality of Godhead has saved me from the sinful life of material existence. By His desire, my last piece of material attraction is now gone."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.97
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, personally told Sanātana Gosvāmī about Lord Kṛṣṇa's real identity. He also told him about the Lord's conjugal love, His personal opulence and the mellows of devotional service. All these truths were explained to Sanātana Gosvāmī by the Lord Himself out of His causeless mercy.

> kṛṣṇa-svarūpa-mādhuryaiś-

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 20.99
description: Sanātana Gosvāmī said, "I was born in a low family, and my associates are all low-class men. I myself am fallen and am the lowest of men. Indeed, I have passed my whole life fallen in the well of sinful materialism.
text:
> "nīca jāti, nīca-saṅgī, patita adhama
> kuviṣaya-kūpe paḍi' goṅāinu janama!
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nīca]] [[synonyms:j:jāti]]---born of a low family; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgī]]---associated with low men; [[synonyms:p:patita]]---fallen; [[synonyms:a:adhama]]---the lowest; [[synonyms:k:ku]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]-[[synonyms:k:kūpe]]---in a well of material enjoyment; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---having fallen down; [[synonyms:g:goṅāinu]]---I have passed; [[synonyms:j:janama]]---my life.
translation: Sanātana Gosvāmī said, "I was born in a low family, and my associates are all low-class men. I myself am fallen and am the lowest of men. Indeed, I have passed my whole life fallen in the well of sinful materialism.
purport: Actually Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī belonged to a //brāhmaṇa// family because he belonged to the Sārasvata division of the //brāhmaṇas// and was well cultured and well educated. Somehow or other he accepted a ministership in the Muslim government; therefore he had to associate with meat-eaters, drunkards and gross materialists. Sanātana Gosvāmī considered himself fallen, for in the association of such men, he also fell victim to material enjoyment. Having passed his life in that way, he considered that he had wasted his valuable time. This statement about how one can become fallen in this material world is made by the greatest authority in the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava-sampradāya. Actually the whole world is presently fallen into material existence. Everyone is a meat-eater, drunkard, woman hunter, gambler and whatnot. People are enjoying material life by committing the four basic sins. Although they are fallen, if they simply submit themselves at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they will be saved from sinful reactions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.1
description: Offering my obeisances unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, let me describe a particle of His opulence and sweetness. He is most valuable for a fallen conditioned soul bereft of spiritual knowledge, and He is the only shelter for those who do not know the real goal of life.
text:
> agaty-eka-gatiṁ natvā
> hīnārthādhika-sādhakam
> śrī-caitanyaṁ likhāmy asya
> mādhuryaiśvarya-śīkaram
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:agati]]-[[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:g:gatim]]---to the only shelter for the conditioned souls who do not know the goal of life; [[synonyms:n:natvā]]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:h:hīna]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---of the necessities of the conditioned souls, who are poor in spiritual knowledge; [[synonyms:a:adhika]]---increase; [[synonyms:s:sādhakam]]---bringing about; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanyam]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:likhāmi]]---I am writing; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of Him; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---of the sweetness and opulence; [[synonyms:ś:śīkaram]]---a small portion.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.10
description: "The spiritual qualities of Kṛṣṇa are also unlimited. Great personalities like Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and the four Kumāras cannot estimate the spiritual qualities of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.100
description: " 'To exhibit the strength of His own spiritual potency, Lord Kṛṣṇa manifested a suitable form just for His pastimes in the material world. This form was wonderful even for Him and was the supreme abode of the wealth of good fortune. Its limbs were so beautiful that they increased the beauty of the ornaments worn on different parts of His body.'

> yan martya-līlaupayikaṁ svayoga-

translation: “ 'To exhibit the strength of His own spiritual potency, Lord Kṛṣṇa manifested a suitable form just for His pastimes in the material world. This form was wonderful even for Him and was the supreme abode of the wealth of good fortune. Its limbs were so beautiful that they increased the beauty of the ornaments worn on different parts of His body.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:2:12|(3.2.12)]] is stated in a conversation between Vidura and Uddhava. Uddhava thus begins his description of the pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa in His form exhibited by //yogamāyā.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.101

He carries a flute in His hand, and His youth is new. He is also an expert dancer. All this is just suitable for His pastimes as a human being.
text:
> kṛṣṇera yateka khelā, sarvottama nara-līlā,

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.102

text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.103
description: "The transcendental form of Kṛṣṇa is shown to the world by Lord Kṛṣṇa's internal spiritual energy, which is a transformation of pure goodness. This jewellike form is the most confidential treasure of the devotees. This form is manifest from Kṛṣṇa's eternal pastimes.

> yogamāyā cic-chakti, viśuddha-sattva-pariṇati,

translation: "The transcendental form of Kṛṣṇa is shown to the world by Lord Kṛṣṇa's internal spiritual energy, which is a transformation of pure goodness. This jewellike form is the most confidential treasure of the devotees. This form is manifest from Kṛṣṇa's eternal pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.104
description: "The wonder of Kṛṣṇa in His personal feature is so great that it attracts even Kṛṣṇa to taste His own association. Thus Kṛṣṇa becomes very eager to taste that wonder. Total beauty, knowledge, wealth, strength, fame and renunciation are the six opulences of Kṛṣṇa. He is eternally situated in His opulences.
text:
> rūpa dekhi' āpanāra, kṛṣṇera haila camatkāra,
> āsvādite mane uṭhe kāma
> 'svasaubhāgya' yāṅra nāma, saundaryādi-guṇa-grāma,
> ei-rūpa nitya tāra dhāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rūpa]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---by seeing the form; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāra]]---His own; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---wonder; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādite]]---to taste; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---arises; [[synonyms:k:kāma]]---a desire; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:s:saubhāgya]]---one's own good fortune; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of which; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name; [[synonyms:s:saundarya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:grāma]]---the transcendental qualities, headed by beauty; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---this form; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---eternal; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of them; [[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---the abode.
translation: "The wonder of Kṛṣṇa in His personal feature is so great that it attracts even Kṛṣṇa to taste His own association. Thus Kṛṣṇa becomes very eager to taste that wonder. Total beauty, knowledge, wealth, strength, fame and renunciation are the six opulences of Kṛṣṇa. He is eternally situated in His opulences.
purport:
Kṛṣṇa has many pastimes, of which His pastimes in Goloka Vṛndāvana (the //gokula-līlā//) are supreme. He also has pastimes in the Vaikuṇṭhas, the spiritual world, as Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. In His pastimes in the spiritual sky, He lies down in the Causal Ocean as Kāraṇārṇavaśāyī, the //puruṣa-avatāra.// His incarnations as a fish, tortoise and so on are called His causal incarnations. He incarnates in the modes of nature as Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and Lord Viṣṇu. He also incarnates as empowered living entities like Pṛthu and Vyāsa. The Supersoul is His localized incarnation, and His all-pervasive aspect is the impersonal Brahman.

When we consider impartially all the unlimited pastimes of the Lord, we find that His pastimes as a human being on this planet-wherein He sports as a cowherd boy with a flute in His hands and appears youthful and fresh like a ballet dancer-are pastimes and features that are never subjected to material laws and inebrieties. The wonderful beauty of Kṛṣṇa is presented in the supreme planet, Gokula (Goloka Vṛndāvana). Inferior to that is His representation in the spiritual sky, and inferior to that is His representation in the external energy (Devī-dhāma). A mere drop of Kṛṣṇa's sweetness can drown these three worlds-Goloka Vṛndāvana, Hari-dhāma (Vaikuṇṭhaloka), and Devī-dhāma (the material world). Everywhere, Kṛṣṇa's beauty merges everyone in the ecstasy of transcendental bliss. Actually the activities of //yogamāyā// are absent in the spiritual sky and the Vaikuṇṭha planets. She simply works in the supreme planet, Goloka Vṛndāvana, and she works to manifest the activities of Kṛṣṇa when He descends to the material universe to please His innumerable devotees within the material world. Thus a replica of the Goloka Vṛndāvana planet and the pastimes there are manifest on this planet on a specific tract of land-Bhauma Vṛndāvana, the Vṛndāvana-dhāma on this planet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.105
description: "Ornaments caress that body, but the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa is so beautiful that it beautifies the ornaments He wears. Therefore Kṛṣṇa's body is said to be the ornament of ornaments. Despite the wonderful beauty of Kṛṣṇa, there is His three-curved style of standing, which beautifies that form. Above all these beautiful features, Kṛṣṇa's eyes dance and move obliquely, acting like arrows to pierce the minds of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and the gopīs. When the arrow succeeds in hitting its target, their minds become agitated.
text:
> bhūṣaṇera bhūṣaṇa aṅga, tāheṅ lalita tribhaṅga,
> tāhāra upara bhrūdhanu-nartana
> terache netrānta bāṇa, tāra dṛḍha sandhāna,
> vindhe rādhā-gopī-gaṇa-mana

Therefore Kṛṣṇa's body is said to be the ornament of ornaments. Despite the wonderful beauty of Kṛṣṇa, there is His three-curved style of standing, which beautifies that form. Above all these beautiful features, Kṛṣṇa's eyes dance and move obliquely, acting like arrows to pierce the minds of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and the gopīs. When the arrow succeeds in hitting its target, their minds become agitated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.106
description: "The beauty of Kṛṣṇa's body is so attractive that it attracts not only the demigods and other living entities within this material world but the personalities of the spiritual sky as well, including the Nārāyaṇas, who are expansions of Kṛṣṇa's personality. The minds of the Nārāyaṇas are thus attracted by the beauty of Kṛṣṇa's body. In addition, the goddesses of fortune [Lakṣmīs]—who are wives of the Nārāyaṇas and are the women described in the Vedas as most chaste-are also attracted by the wonderful beauty of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> brahmāṇḍopari paravyoma, tāhāṅ ye svarūpa-gaṇa,
> tāṅ-sabāra bale hare mana
> pati-vratā-śiromaṇi, yāṅre kahe veda-vāṇī,
> ākarṣaye sei lakṣmī-gaṇa

The minds of the Nārāyaṇas are thus attracted by the beauty of Kṛṣṇa's body. In addition, the goddesses of fortune [Lakṣmīs]---who are wives of the Nārāyaṇas and are the women described in the Vedas as most chaste-are also attracted by the wonderful beauty of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.107
description: "Favoring them, Kṛṣṇa rides on the chariot of the minds of the gopīs, and just to receive loving service from them, He attracts their minds like Cupid. Therefore He is also called Madana-mohana, the attractor of Cupid. Cupid has five arrows, representing form, taste, smell, sound and touch. Kṛṣṇa is the owner of these five arrows, and with His Cupid-like beauty, He conquers the minds of the gopīs, though they are very proud of their superexcellent beauty. Becoming a new Cupid, Kṛṣṇa attracts their minds and engages in the rāsa dance.
text:
> caḍi' gopī-manorathe, manmathera mana mathe,
> nāma dhare 'madana-mohana'
> jini' pañcaśara-darpa, svayaṁ nava-kandarpa,
> rāsa kare lañā gopī-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caḍi']]---riding; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:r:rathe]]---on the chariot of the minds of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:m:manmathera]]---of Cupid; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:m:mathe]]---churns; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name; [[synonyms:d:dhare]]---accepts; [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mohana]]---Madana-mohana, the deluder of Cupid; [[synonyms:j:jini']]---conquering; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:ś:śara]]---of Cupid, the master of the five arrows of the senses; [[synonyms:d:darpa]]---the pride; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---personally; [[synonyms:n:nava]]---new; [[synonyms:k:kandarpa]]---Cupid; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]---//rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---with; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the //gopīs.//

Therefore He is also called Madana-mohana, the attractor of Cupid. Cupid has five arrows, representing form, taste, smell, sound and touch. Kṛṣṇa is the owner of these five arrows, and with His Cupid-like beauty, He conquers the minds of the gopīs, though they are very proud of their superexcellent beauty. Becoming a new Cupid, Kṛṣṇa attracts their minds and engages in the rāsa dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.108
description: "When Lord Kṛṣṇa wanders in the forest of Vṛndāvana with His friends on an equal level, there are innumerable cows grazing. This is another of the Lord's blissful enjoyments. When He plays on His flute, all living entities-including trees, plants, animals and human beings-tremble and are saturated with jubilation. Tears flow constantly from their eyes.
text:
> nija-sama sakhā-saṅge, go-gaṇa-cāraṇa raṅge,
> vṛndāvane svacchanda vihāra
> yāṅra veṇu-dhvani śuni' sthāvara-jaṅgama prāṇī,
> pulaka, kampa, aśru vahe dhāra

translation: "When Lord Kṛṣṇa wanders in the forest of Vṛndāvana with His friends on an equal level, there are innumerable cows grazing. This is another of the Lord's blissful enjoyments. When He plays on His flute, all living entities-including trees, plants, animals and human beings-tremble and are saturated with jubilation. Tears flow constantly from their eyes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.109
description: "Kṛṣṇa wears a pearl necklace that appears like a chain of white ducks around His neck. The peacock feather in His hair appears like a rainbow, and His yellow garments appear like lightning in the sky. Kṛṣṇa appears like a newly risen cloud, and the gopīs appear like newly grown grains in the field. Constant rains of nectarean pastimes fall upon these newly grown grains, and it seems that the gopīs are receiving beams of life from Kṛṣṇa, exactly as grains receive life from the rains.
text:
> muktā-hāra---baka-pāṅti, indra-dhanu-piñcha tati,
> pītāmbara---vijurī-sañcāra
> kṛṣṇa nava-jaladhara, jagat-śasya-upara,
> variṣaye līlāmṛta-dhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muktā]]-[[synonyms:h:hāra]]---a necklace of pearls; [[synonyms:b:baka]]-[[synonyms:p:pāṅti]]---like a row of white ducks; [[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:d:dhanu]]---like a rainbow; [[synonyms:p:piñcha]]---a peacock feather; [[synonyms:t:tati]]---there; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]-[[synonyms:a:ambara]]---yellow garments; [[synonyms:v:vijurī]]-[[synonyms:s:sañcāra]]---like the appearance of lightning in the sky; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nava]]---new; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:d:dhara]]---cloud carrying water; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the universe; [[synonyms:ś:śasya]]---like crops of grains; [[synonyms:u:upara]]---upon; [[synonyms:v:variṣaye]]---rains; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---like a shower.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa wears a pearl necklace that appears like a chain of white ducks around His neck. The peacock feather in His hair appears like a rainbow, and His yellow garments appear like lightning in the sky. Kṛṣṇa appears like a newly risen cloud, and the gopīs appear like newly grown grains in the field. Constant rains of nectarean pastimes fall upon these newly grown grains, and it seems that the gopīs are receiving beams of life from Kṛṣṇa, exactly as grains receive life from the rains.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.11
description: " 'In time, great scientists may be able to count all the atoms of the universe, all the stars and planets in the sky, and all the particles of snow, but who among them can count the unlimited transcendental qualities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead? He descends on the surface of the globe for the benefit of all living entities.'
text:
> guṇātmanas te 'pi guṇān vimātuṁ
> hitāvatīrṇasya ka īśire 'sya
> kālena yair vā vimitāḥ sukalpair
> bhū-pāṁśavaḥ khe mihikā dyubhāsaḥ

translation: “ 'In time, great scientists may be able to count all the atoms of the universe, all the stars and planets in the sky, and all the particles of snow, but who among them can count the unlimited transcendental qualities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead? He descends on the surface of the globe for the benefit of all living entities.'
purport: This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.14.7).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.110
description: "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, is full in all six opulences, including His attractive beauty, which engages Him in conjugal love with the gopīs. Such sweetness is the quintessence of His qualities. Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the son of Vyāsadeva, has described these pastimes of Kṛṣṇa throughout Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. Hearing the descriptions, the devotees become mad with love of God."
text:
> mādhurya bhagavattā-sāra, vraje kaila paracāra,
> tāhā śuka---vyāsera nandana
> sthāne sthāne bhāgavate, varṇiyāche jānāite,
> tāhā śuni' māte bhakta-gaṇa

Hearing the descriptions, the devotees become mad with love of God."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.111
description: Just as the women of Mathurā ecstatically described the fortune of the gopīs of Vṛndāvana and the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu described the different mellows of Kṛṣṇa and became overwhelmed with ecstatic love. Grasping the hand of Sanātana Gosvāmī, He recited the following verse.
text:
> kahite kṛṣṇera rase, śloka paḍe premāveśe,
> preme sanātana-hāta dhari'
> gopī-bhāgya, kṛṣṇa guṇa, ye karila varṇana,
> bhāvāveśe mathurā-nāgarī

Grasping the hand of Sanātana Gosvāmī, He recited the following verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.112
description: " 'What austerities must the gopīs have performed? With their eyes they always drink the nectar of the face of Lord Kṛṣṇa, which is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equaled or surpassed. That loveliness is the only abode of beauty, fame and opulence. It is self-perfect, ever fresh and unique.'
text:
> gopyas tapaḥ kim acaran yad amuṣya rūpaṁ
> lāvaṇya-sāram asamordhvam ananya-siddham
> dṛgbhiḥ pibanty anusavābhinavaṁ durāpam
> ekānta-dhāma yaśasaḥ śriya aiśvarasya

translation: “ 'What austerities must the gopīs have performed? With their eyes they always drink the nectar of the face of Lord Kṛṣṇa, which is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equaled or surpassed. That loveliness is the only abode of beauty, fame and opulence. It is self-perfect, ever fresh and unique.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.44.14) was spoken by the women of Mathurā when they saw Kṛṣṇa in the wrestling arena.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.113
description: "The bodily beauty of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is like a wave in the ocean of eternal youth. In that great ocean is the whirlpool of the awakening of ecstatic love. The vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute is like a whirlwind, and the flickering minds of the gopīs are like straws and dry leaves. After they fall down in the whirlwind, they never rise again but remain eternally at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> tāruṇyāmṛta---pārāvāra, taraṅga---lāvaṇya-sāra,
> tāte se āvarta bhāvodgama
> vaṁśī-dhvani---cakravāta, nārīra mana---tṛṇa-pāta,
> tāhā ḍubāya nā haya udgama
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāruṇya]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---eternal youth; [[synonyms:p:pārāvāra]]---like a great ocean; [[synonyms:t:taraṅga]]---waves; [[synonyms:l:lāvaṇya]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the essence of bodily beauty; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in that ocean; [[synonyms:s:se]]---//that//; [[synonyms:ā:āvarta]]---like a whirlpool; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:u:udgama]]---awakening of different ecstatic emotions; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---the vibration of the flute; [[synonyms:c:cakravāta]]---a whirlwind; [[synonyms:n:nārīra]]---of the women; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds; [[synonyms:t:tṛṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pāta]]---leaves of grass; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍubāya]]---plunge down; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]] [[synonyms:u:udgama]]---never to come up again.
translation: "The bodily beauty of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is like a wave in the ocean of eternal youth. In that great ocean is the whirlpool of the awakening of ecstatic love. The vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute is like a whirlwind, and the flickering minds of the gopīs are like straws and dry leaves. After they fall down in the whirlwind, they never rise again but remain eternally at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.114
description: "O my dear friend, what severe austerities have the gopīs performed to drink His transcendental beauty and sweetness through their eyes in complete fulfillment? Thus they glorify their births, bodies and minds.
text:
> sakhī he, kon tapa kaila gopī-gaṇa
> kṛṣṇa-rūpa-sumādhurī, pibi' pibi' netra bhari',
> ślāghya kare janma-tanu-mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakhī]] [[synonyms:h:he]]---My dear friend; [[synonyms:k:kon]]---what; [[synonyms:t:tapa]]---austerity; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---have executed; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---of the beauty of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhurī]]---the essence of all sweetness; [[synonyms:p:pibi']] [[synonyms:p:pibi']]---drinking and drinking; [[synonyms:n:netra]] [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---filling the eyes; [[synonyms:ś:ślāghya]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---they glorify; [[synonyms:j:janma]]-[[synonyms:t:tanu]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---their births, bodies and minds.
translation: "O my dear friend, what severe austerities have the gopīs performed to drink His transcendental beauty and sweetness through their eyes in complete fulfillment? Thus they glorify their births, bodies and minds.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.115
description: "The sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's beauty enjoyed by the gopīs is unparalleled. Nothing is equal to or greater than such ecstatic sweetness. Even the predominating Deities of the Vaikuṇṭha planets, the Nārāyaṇas, do not possess such sweetness. Indeed, none of the incarnations of Kṛṣṇa up to Nārāyaṇa possess such transcendental beauty.
text:
> ye mādhurīra ūrdhva āna, nāhi yāra samāna,
> paravyome svarūpera gaṇe
> yeṅho saba-avatārī, paravyoma-adhikārī,
> e mādhurya nāhi nārāyaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:m:mādhurīra]]---that sweetness; [[synonyms:ū:ūrdhva]]---higher; [[synonyms:ā:āna]]---another; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:y:yāra]] [[synonyms:s:samāna]]---equal to which; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:v:vyome]]---the spiritual sky; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpera]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---among the expansions of Kṛṣṇa's personality; [[synonyms:y:yeṅho]]---who; [[synonyms:s:saba]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāri]]---the source of all the incarnations; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:v:vyoma]]-[[synonyms:a:adhikārī]]---the predominating Deity of the Vaikuṇṭha planets; [[synonyms:e:e]] [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---this ecstatic sweetness; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---is not; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇe]]---even in Lord Nārāyaṇa.
translation: "The sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's beauty enjoyed by the gopīs is unparalleled. Nothing is equal to or greater than such ecstatic sweetness. Even the predominating Deities of the Vaikuṇṭha planets, the Nārāyaṇas, do not possess such sweetness. Indeed, none of the incarnations of Kṛṣṇa up to Nārāyaṇa possess such transcendental beauty.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.116
description: "Even the dearest consort of Nārāyaṇa, the goddess of fortune, who is worshiped by all chaste women, is captivated by the unparalleled sweetness of Kṛṣṇa. She even gave up everything in her desire to enjoy Kṛṣṇa, and taking a great vow, she underwent severe austerities.
text:
> tāte sākṣī sei ramā, nārāyaṇera priyatamā,
> pativratā-gaṇera upāsyā
> tiṅho ye mādhurya-lobhe, chāḍi' saba kāma-bhoge,
> vrata kari' karilā tapasyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in this regard; [[synonyms:s:sākṣī]]---the evidence; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:r:ramā]]---that goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇera]] [[synonyms:p:priya]]-[[synonyms:t:tamā]]---the most dear consort of Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:p:pati]]-[[synonyms:v:vratā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of all chaste women; [[synonyms:u:upāsyā]]---worshipable; [[synonyms:t:tiṅho]]---she; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---that; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]-[[synonyms:l:lobhe]]---being attracted by the same sweetness; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kāma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhoge]]---to enjoy with Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vrata]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking a vow; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:t:tapasyā]]---executed austerities.
translation: "Even the dearest consort of Nārāyaṇa, the goddess of fortune, who is worshiped by all chaste women, is captivated by the unparalleled sweetness of Kṛṣṇa. She even gave up everything in her desire to enjoy Kṛṣṇa, and taking a great vow, she underwent severe austerities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.117
description: "The quintessence of Kṛṣṇa's sweet bodily luster is so perfect that there is no perfection above it. He is the immutable mine of all transcendental qualities. In His other manifestations and personal expansions, there is only a partial exhibition of such qualities. We understand all His personal expansions in this way.
text:
> sei ta' mādhurya-sāra, anya-siddhi nāhi tāra,
> tiṅho---mādhuryādi-guṇa-khani
> āra saba prakāśe, tāṅra datta guṇa bhāse,
> yāhāṅ yata prakāśe kārya jāni
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']] [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---that is the quintessence of sweetness; [[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:s:siddhi]]---perfection due to anything else; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:t:tiṅho]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:khani]]---the mine of transcendental mellows, headed by sweetness; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all other; [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---in manifestations; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:d:datta]]---given; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---are exhibited; [[synonyms:y:yāhaṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---as much as; [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---in that manifestation; [[synonyms:k:kārya]]---to be done; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I understand.
translation: "The quintessence of Kṛṣṇa's sweet bodily luster is so perfect that there is no perfection above it. He is the immutable mine of all transcendental qualities. In His other manifestations and personal expansions, there is only a partial exhibition of such qualities. We understand all His personal expansions in this way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.118
description: "Both the gopīs and Kṛṣṇa are complete. The gopīs' ecstatic love is like a mirror that becomes newer and newer at every moment and reflects Kṛṣṇa's bodily luster and sweetness. Thus competition increases. Since neither give up, their pastimes become newer and newer, and both sides constantly increase.
text:
> gopī-bhāva-darapaṇa, nava nava kṣaṇe kṣaṇa,
> tāra āge kṛṣṇera mādhurya
> doṅhe kare huḍāhuḍi, bāḍe, mukha nāhi muḍi,
> nava nava doṅhāra prācurya
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:d:darapaṇa]]---the //gopīs'// ecstasy is like a mirror; [[synonyms:n:nava]] [[synonyms:n:nava]] [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]] [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇa]]---newer and newer at every moment; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of that; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's beauty; [[synonyms:d:doṅhe]]---both; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:h:huḍāhuḍi]]---struggling together; [[synonyms:b:bāḍe]]---increases; [[synonyms:m:mukha]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:m:muḍi]]---never turning away the faces; [[synonyms:n:nava]] [[synonyms:n:nava]]---newer and newer; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]]---of both of them; [[synonyms:p:prācurya]]---abundance.
translation: "Both the gopīs and Kṛṣṇa are complete. The gopīs' ecstatic love is like a mirror that becomes newer and newer at every moment and reflects Kṛṣṇa's bodily luster and sweetness. Thus competition increases. Since neither give up, their pastimes become newer and newer, and both sides constantly increase.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.119
description: "The transcendental mellows generated from the dealings between the gopīs and Kṛṣṇa cannot be tasted by fruitive activity, yogic austerities, speculative knowledge, regulative devotional service, mantra-yoga or meditation. This sweetness can be tasted only through the spontaneous love of liberated persons who chant the holy names with great ecstatic love.
text:
> karma, tapa, yoga, jñāna, vidhi-bhakti, japa, dhyāna,
> ihā haite mādhurya durlabha
> kevala ye rāga-mārge, bhaje kṛṣṇe anurāge,
> tāre kṛṣṇa-mādhurya sulabha
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:karma]]---fruitive activities; [[synonyms:t:tapa]]---austerities; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]---the practice of mystic //yoga//; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---speculative cultivation of knowledge; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---regulative principles in devotional service; [[synonyms:j:japa]]---chanting; [[synonyms:d:dhyāna]]---meditation; [[synonyms:i:ihā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from these things; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:durlabha]]---very difficult to perceive; [[synonyms:k:kevala]]---only; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---one; [[synonyms:r:rāga]]-[[synonyms:m:mārge]]---by the path of spontaneous ecstatic love; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---worships; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:anurāge]]---with transcendental feeling; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's; [[synonyms:s:sulabha]]---very easily appreciated.
translation: "The transcendental mellows generated from the dealings between the gopīs and Kṛṣṇa cannot be tasted by fruitive activity, yogic austerities, speculative knowledge, regulative devotional service, mantra-yoga or meditation. This sweetness can be tasted only through the spontaneous love of liberated persons who chant the holy names with great ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.12
description: "To say nothing of Lord Brahmā, even Lord Ananta, who has thousands of heads, could not reach the end of the Lord's transcendental qualities, even though He is continuously chanting their praises.
text:
> brahmādi rahu---sahasra-vadane 'ananta'
> nirantara gāya mukhe, nā pāya guṇera anta
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:r:rahu]]---leave aside Lord Brahmā and others; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]-[[synonyms:v:vadane]]---in thousands of mouths; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---Lord Ananta; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---continuously; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chants; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the mouths; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---does not obtain; [[synonyms:g:guṇera]]---of qualities of the Lord; [[synonyms:a:anta]]---the end.
translation: "To say nothing of Lord Brahmā, even Lord Ananta, who has thousands of heads, could not reach the end of the Lord's transcendental qualities, even though He is continuously chanting their praises.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.120
description: "Such ecstatic transactions between Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs are only possible in Vṛndāvana, which is full of the opulences of transcendental love. The form of Kṛṣṇa is the original source of all transcendental qualities. It is like a mine of gems. The opulences belonging to all the personal expansions of Kṛṣṇa are to be understood to be bestowed by Kṛṣṇa; therefore Kṛṣṇa is the original source and shelter of everyone.
text:
> sei-rūpa vrajāśraya, aiśvarya-mādhuryamaya,
> divya-guṇa-gaṇa-ratnālaya
> ānera vaibhava-sattā, kṛṣṇa-datta bhagavattā,
> kṛṣṇa---sarva-aṁśī, sarvāśraya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---that supernatural beauty; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśraya]]---whose abode is in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---full of opulence and the sweetness of love; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---of transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:r:ratna]]-[[synonyms:ā:ālaya]]---the source of all the gems; [[synonyms:ā:ānera]]---of others; [[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]-[[synonyms:s:sattā]]---the presence of opulences; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:datta]]---all bestowed by Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhagavattā]]---qualities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁśī]]---the original source of all of them; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśraya]]---the shelter of all of them.
translation: "Such ecstatic transactions between Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs are only possible in Vṛndāvana, which is full of the opulences of transcendental love. The form of Kṛṣṇa is the original source of all transcendental qualities. It is like a mine of gems. The opulences belonging to all the personal expansions of Kṛṣṇa are to be understood to be bestowed by Kṛṣṇa; therefore Kṛṣṇa is the original source and shelter of everyone.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.121
description: "Beauty, humility, mercy, merit, patience and expert intelligence are all manifest in Kṛṣṇa. But besides these, Kṛṣṇa has other qualities like good behavior, mildness and magnanimity. He also performs welfare activities for the whole world. All these qualities are not visible in expansions like Nārāyaṇa.
text:
> śrī, lajjā, dayā, kīrti, dhairya, vaiśāradī mati,
> ei saba kṛṣṇe pratiṣṭhita
> suśīla, mṛdu, vadānya, kṛṣṇa-sama nāhi anya,
> kṛṣṇa kare jagatera hita
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]---beauty; [[synonyms:l:lajjā]]---humility; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:k:kīrti]]---merit; [[synonyms:d:dhairya]]---patience; [[synonyms:v:vaiśāradī]]---very expert; [[synonyms:m:mati]]---intelligence; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all these; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---in Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pratiṣṭhita]]---situated; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:ś:śīla]]---well behaved; [[synonyms:m:mṛdu]]---mild; [[synonyms:v:vadānya]]---magnanimous; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---like Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is no one; [[synonyms:a:anya]]---else; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:j:jagatera]]---of the world; [[synonyms:h:hita]]---welfare.
translation: "Beauty, humility, mercy, merit, patience and expert intelligence are all manifest in Kṛṣṇa. But besides these, Kṛṣṇa has other qualities like good behavior, mildness and magnanimity. He also performs welfare activities for the whole world. All these qualities are not visible in expansions like Nārāyaṇa.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura mentions that the qualities of beauty, humility, mercy, merit, patience and expert intelligence are brilliant qualities, and when they are exhibited in the person of Nārāyaṇa, one should know that they are bestowed upon Nārāyaṇa by Kṛṣṇa. Good behavior, mildness and magnanimity are found only in Kṛṣṇa. Only Kṛṣṇa performs welfare activities for the whole world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.122
description: "After seeing Kṛṣṇa, various people criticize the blinking of their eyes. In Vṛndāvana, especially, all the gopīs criticize Lord Brahmā because of this defect in the eyes." Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited some verses from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and explained them vividly, thus enjoying the taste of transcendental sweetness with great happiness.
text:
> kṛṣṇa dekhi' nānā jana, kaila nimiṣe nindana,
> vraje vidhi ninde gopī-gaṇa
> sei saba śloka paḍi', mahāprabhu artha kari',
> sukhe mādhurya kare āsvādana

translation: "After seeing Kṛṣṇa, various people criticize the blinking of their eyes. In Vṛndāvana, especially, all the gopīs criticize Lord Brahmā because of this defect in the eyes." Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited some verses from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and explained them vividly, thus enjoying the taste of transcendental sweetness with great happiness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.123
description: " 'All men and women were accustomed to enjoying the beauty of the shining face of Lord Kṛṣṇa, as well as His sharklike earrings swinging on His ears. His beautiful features, His cheeks and His playful smiles all combined to form a constant festival for the eyes, and the blinking of the eyes became obstacles that impeded one from seeing that beauty. For this reason, men and women became very angry at the creator [Lord Brahmā].'
text:
> yasyānanaṁ makara-kuṇḍala-cāru-karṇa-
> bhrājat-kapola-subhagaṁ savilāsa-hāsam
> nityotsavaṁ na tatṛpur dṛśibhiḥ pibantyo
> nāryo narāś ca muditāḥ kupitā nimeś ca
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:ānanam]]---face; [[synonyms:m:makara]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṇḍala]]---by earrings resembling sharks; [[synonyms:c:cāru]]---beautified; [[synonyms:k:karṇa]]---the ears; [[synonyms:b:bhrājat]]---shining; [[synonyms:k:kapola]]---cheeks; [[synonyms:s:subhagam]]---delicate; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]-[[synonyms:h:hāsam]]---smiling with an enjoying spirit; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]-[[synonyms:u:utsavam]]---in which there are eternal festivities of joy; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:t:tatṛpuḥ]]---satisfied; [[synonyms:d:dṛśibhiḥ]]---by the eyes; [[synonyms:p:pibantyaḥ]]---drinking; [[synonyms:n:nāryaḥ]]---all the women; [[synonyms:n:narāḥ]]---the men; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:m:muditāḥ]]---very pleased; [[synonyms:k:kupitāḥ]]---very angry; [[synonyms:n:nimeḥ]]---at the creator of the blinking of the eyes; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also.
translation: “ 'All men and women were accustomed to enjoying the beauty of the shining face of Lord Kṛṣṇa, as well as His sharklike earrings swinging on His ears. His beautiful features, His cheeks and His playful smiles all combined to form a constant festival for the eyes, and the blinking of the eyes became obstacles that impeded one from seeing that beauty. For this reason, men and women became very angry at the creator [Lord Brahmā].'
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:9:24:65|(9.24.65)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.124
description: " 'O Kṛṣṇa, when You go to the forest during the day and we do not see Your sweet face, which is surrounded by beautiful, curling hair, half a second becomes as long as an entire age for us. And we consider the creator, who has put eyelids on the eyes we use for seeing You, to be simply a fool.'
text:
> aṭati yad bhavān ahni kānanaṁ
> truṭir yugāyate tvām apaśyatām
> kuṭila-kuntalaṁ śrī-mukhaṁ ca te
> jaḍa udīkṣatāṁ pakṣma-kṛd dṛśām
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aṭati]]---goes; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---when; [[synonyms:b:bhavān]]---Your Lordship; [[synonyms:a:ahni]]---in the day; [[synonyms:k:kānanam]]---to the forest; [[synonyms:t:truṭiḥ]]---half a second; [[synonyms:y:yugāyate]]---appears like a //yuga//; [[synonyms:t:tvām]]---You; [[synonyms:a:apaśyatām]]---of those not seeing; [[synonyms:k:kuṭila]]-[[synonyms:k:kuntalam]]---adorned with curled hair; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:m:mukham]]---beautiful face; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:t:te]]---Your; [[synonyms:j:jaḍaḥ]]---stupid; [[synonyms:u:udīkṣatām]]---looking at; [[synonyms:p:pakṣma]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛt]]---the maker of eyelashes; [[synonyms:d:dṛśām]]---of the eyes.
translation: “ 'O Kṛṣṇa, when You go to the forest during the day and we do not see Your sweet face, which is surrounded by beautiful, curling hair, half a second becomes as long as an entire age for us. And we consider the creator, who has put eyelids on the eyes we use for seeing You, to be simply a fool.'
purport: This verse is spoken by the //gopīs// in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.31.15).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.125
description: "Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is identical with the Vedic hymn known as the kāma-gāyatrī, which is composed of twenty-four and a half syllables. Those syllables are compared to moons that arise in Kṛṣṇa. Thus all three worlds are filled with desire.
text:
> kāma-gāyatrī-mantra-rūpa, haya kṛṣṇera svarūpa,
> sārdha-cabbiśa akṣara tāra haya
> se akṣara 'candra' haya, kṛṣṇe kari' udaya,
> trijagat kailā kāmamaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāma]]-[[synonyms:g:gāyatrī]]-[[synonyms:m:mantra]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the hymn known as //kāma-gāyatrī//; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---identical with Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sārdha]]-[[synonyms:c:cabbiśa]]---twenty-four and a half; [[synonyms:a:akṣara]]---syllables; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:a:akṣara]]---these syllables; [[synonyms:c:candra]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are like the moon; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:u:udaya]]---awakening; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the three worlds; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---made; [[synonyms:k:kāma]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---full of desire.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is identical with the Vedic hymn known as the kāma-gāyatrī, which is composed of twenty-four and a half syllables. Those syllables are compared to moons that arise in Kṛṣṇa. Thus all three worlds are filled with desire.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.126
description: "The face of Kṛṣṇa is the king of all moons, and the body of Kṛṣṇa is the throne. Thus the king governs a society of moons.
text:
> sakhī he, kṛṣṇa-mukha---dvija-rāja-rāja
> kṛṣṇa-vapu-siṁhāsane, vasi' rājya-śāsane,
> kare saṅge candrera samāja
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakhī]] [[synonyms:h:he]]---O dear friend; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---the face of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dvija]]-[[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:r:rāja]]---the king of moons; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:vapu]]---of the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:siṁhāsane]]---on the throne; [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting; [[synonyms:r:rājya]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāsane]]---ruling of the kingdom; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the company of; [[synonyms:c:candrera]] [[synonyms:s:samāja]]---the society of moons.
translation: "The face of Kṛṣṇa is the king of all moons, and the body of Kṛṣṇa is the throne. Thus the king governs a society of moons.
purport: The entire face is called the king of moons. The mouth is another moon, the left cheek is a moon, and the right cheek is a moon. The spots of sandalwood pulp on Kṛṣṇa's face are also considered different moons, and His fingernails and toenails are also different moons. His forehead is considered a half moon, His face is considered the king of moons, and His body is considered the throne. All the other //candras// (moons) are considered to be subordinate moons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.127
description: "Kṛṣṇa has two cheeks that shine like glowing gems. Both are considered full moons. His forehead is considered a half moon, and His spots of sandalwood are considered full moons.
text:
> dui gaṇḍa sucikkaṇa, jini' maṇi-sudarpaṇa,
> sei dui pūrṇa-candra jāni
> lalāṭe aṣṭamī-indu, tāhāte candana-bindu,
> sei eka pūrṇa-candra māni
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:g:gaṇḍa]]---cheeks; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:c:cikkaṇa]]---very shiny; [[synonyms:j:jini']]---conquering; [[synonyms:m:maṇi]]-[[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:d:darpaṇa]]---glowing gems; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]]---those two; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---full moons; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I consider; [[synonyms:l:lalāṭe]]---on the forehead; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭamī]]-[[synonyms:i:indu]]---eighth-day moon (half moon); [[synonyms:t:tāhāte]]---on that; [[synonyms:c:candana]]-[[synonyms:b:bindu]]---the drop of sandalwood pulp; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---full moon; [[synonyms:m:māni]]---I consider.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa has two cheeks that shine like glowing gems. Both are considered full moons. His forehead is considered a half moon, and His spots of sandalwood are considered full moons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.128
description: "His fingernails are many full moons, and they dance on the flute on His hands. Their song is the melody of that flute. His toenails are also many full moons, and they dance on the ground. Their song is the jingling of His ankle bells.
text:
> kara-nakha-cāndera hāṭa, vaṁśī-upara kare nāṭa,
> tāra gīta muralīra tāna
> pada-nakha-candra-gaṇa, tale kare nartana,
> nūpurera dhvani yāra gāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kara]]-[[synonyms:n:nakha]]---of the nails on the hands; [[synonyms:c:cāndera]]---of the full moons; [[synonyms:h:hāṭa]]---the bazaar; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]---the flute; [[synonyms:u:upara]]---on; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:n:nāṭa]]---dancing; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of them; [[synonyms:g:gīta]]---the song; [[synonyms:m:muralīra]] [[synonyms:t:tāna]]---the melody of the flute; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:n:nakha]]---of the nails on the toes; [[synonyms:c:candra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the different full moons; [[synonyms:t:tale]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dancing; [[synonyms:n:nūpurera]]---of the ankle bells; [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---the sound; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:g:gāna]]---musical song.
translation: "His fingernails are many full moons, and they dance on the flute on His hands. Their song is the melody of that flute. His toenails are also many full moons, and they dance on the ground. Their song is the jingling of His ankle bells.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.129
description: "Kṛṣṇa's face is the enjoyer king. That full-moon face makes His shark-shaped earrings and lotus eyes dance. His eyebrows are like bows, and His eyes are like arrows. His ears are fixed on the string of that bow, and when His eyes spread to His ears, He pierces the hearts of the gopīs.
text:
> nāce makara-kuṇḍala, netra---līlā-kamala,
> vilāsī rājā satata nācāya
> bhrū---dhanu, netra---bāṇa, dhanur-guṇa---dui kāṇa,
> nārī-mana-lakṣya vindhe tāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:m:makara]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṇḍala]]---the earrings shaped like sharks; [[synonyms:n:netra]]---the eyes; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---for play; [[synonyms:k:kamala]]---like lotus flowers; [[synonyms:v:vilāsī]]---the enjoyer; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the king; [[synonyms:s:satata]] [[synonyms:n:nācāya]]---always causes to dance; [[synonyms:b:bhrū]]---two eyebrows; [[synonyms:d:dhanu]]---just like bows; [[synonyms:n:netra]]---the eyes; [[synonyms:b:bāṇa]]---just like arrows; [[synonyms:d:dhanuḥ]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---the string of the bow; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:k:kāṇa]]---the two ears; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:l:lakṣya]]---the target; [[synonyms:v:vindhe]]---pierces; [[synonyms:t:tāya]]---there.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa's face is the enjoyer king. That full-moon face makes His shark-shaped earrings and lotus eyes dance. His eyebrows are like bows, and His eyes are like arrows. His ears are fixed on the string of that bow, and when His eyes spread to His ears, He pierces the hearts of the gopīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.13
description: " 'If I, Lord Brahmā, and your elder brothers, the great saints and sages, cannot understand the limits of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is full of various energies, who else can understand them? Although constantly chanting about His transcendental qualities, the thousand-hooded Lord Śeṣa has not yet reached the end of the Lord's activities.'
text:
> nāntaṁ vidāmy aham amī munayo 'grajās te
> māyā-balasya puruṣasya kuto 'varā ye
> gāyan guṇān daśa-śatānana ādi-devaḥ
> śeṣo 'dhunāpi samavasyati nāsya pāram
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:a:antam]]---no limit; [[synonyms:v:vidāmi]]---know; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:a:amī]]---those; [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]]---great saintly persons; [[synonyms:a:agrajāḥ]]---brothers; [[synonyms:t:te]]---of you; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:b:balasya]]---who has multi-energies; [[synonyms:p:puruṣasya]]---of the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:kutaḥ]]---how; [[synonyms:a:avarāḥ]]---less intelligent; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:g:gāyan]]---chanting; [[synonyms:g:guṇān]]---the qualities; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śata]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanaḥ]]---who has a thousand hoods; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:d:devaḥ]]---the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣaḥ]]---Ananta Śeṣa; [[synonyms:a:adhunā]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---even until now; [[synonyms:s:samavasyati]]---reaches; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:p:pāram]]---limit.
translation: “ 'If I, Lord Brahmā, and your elder brothers, the great saints and sages, cannot understand the limits of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is full of various energies, who else can understand them? Although constantly chanting about His transcendental qualities, the thousand-hooded Lord Śeṣa has not yet reached the end of the Lord's activities.'
purport: This verse, spoken to Nārada Muni, is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:7:41|(2.7.41)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.130
description: "The dancing features of His face surpass all other full moons and expand the marketplace of full moons. Although priceless, the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's face is distributed to everyone. Some purchase the moonrays of His sweet smiles, and others purchase the nectar of His lips. Thus He pleases everyone.
text:
> ei cāndera baḍa nāṭa, pasāri' cāndera hāṭa,
> vinimūle vilāya nijāmṛta
> kāhoṅ smita-jyotsnāmṛte, kāṅhāre adharāmṛte,
> saba loka kare āpyāyita
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:c:cāndera]]---of this moon of the face; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---big; [[synonyms:n:nāṭa]]---dancing; [[synonyms:p:pasāri']]---expanding; [[synonyms:c:cāndera]] [[synonyms:h:hāṭa]]---the marketplace of full moons; [[synonyms:v:vinimūle]]---without a price; [[synonyms:v:vilāya]]---distributes; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---its personal nectar; [[synonyms:k:kāhoṅ]]---to some; [[synonyms:s:smita]]-[[synonyms:j:jyotsnā]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛte]]---by the nectar of the sweetly smiling moonrays; [[synonyms:k:kāṅhāre]]---to someone; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛte]]---by the nectar of the lips; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all people; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:ā:āpyāyita]]---pleases.
translation: "The dancing features of His face surpass all other full moons and expand the marketplace of full moons. Although priceless, the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's face is distributed to everyone. Some purchase the moonrays of His sweet smiles, and others purchase the nectar of His lips. Thus He pleases everyone.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.131
description: "Kṛṣṇa has two reddish, widely spread eyes. These are ministers of the king, and they subdue the pride of Cupid, who also has beautiful eyes. That face of Govinda, which is full of happiness, is the home of the pastimes of beauty, and it is very pleasing to everyone's eyes.
text:
> vipulāyatāruṇa, madana-mada-ghūrṇana,
> mantrī yāra e dui nayana
> lāvaṇya-keli-sadana, jana-netra-rasāyana,
> sukhamaya govinda-vadana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipula]]-[[synonyms:ā:āyata]]---broad and spread; [[synonyms:a:aruṇa]]---reddish; [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mada]]---the pride of Cupid; [[synonyms:g:ghūrṇana]]---bewildering; [[synonyms:m:mantrī]]---ministers; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:e:e]]---these; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:n:nayana]]---eyes; [[synonyms:l:lāvaṇya]]-[[synonyms:k:keli]]---of pastimes of beauty; [[synonyms:s:sadana]]---home; [[synonyms:j:jana]]-[[synonyms:n:netra]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āyana]]---very pleasing to the eyes of everyone; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---full of happiness; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:v:vadana]]---the face of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa has two reddish, widely spread eyes. These are ministers of the king, and they subdue the pride of Cupid, who also has beautiful eyes. That face of Govinda, which is full of happiness, is the home of the pastimes of beauty, and it is very pleasing to everyone's eyes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.132
description: "If by devotional service one gets the results of pious activities and sees Lord Kṛṣṇa's face, he can relish the Lord with his eyes. His greed and thirst then increase twofold by seeing the nectarean face of Kṛṣṇa. Due to one's inability to sufficiently drink that nectar, one becomes very unhappy and criticizes the creator for not having given more than two eyes.
text:
> yāṅra puṇya-puñja-phale, se-mukha-darśana mile,
> dui āṅkhi ki karibe pāne?
> dviguṇa bāḍe tṛṣṇā-lobha, pite nāre---manaḥ-kṣobha,
> duḥkhe kare vidhira nindane
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:p:puṇya]]-[[synonyms:p:puñja]]-[[synonyms:p:phale]]---by the result of many pious activities; [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---of that face; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---seeing; [[synonyms:m:mile]]---if one gets to do; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:ā:āṅkhi]]---two eyes; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---how; [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---will do; [[synonyms:p:pāne]]---drinking; [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---twice; [[synonyms:b:bāḍe]]---increases; [[synonyms:t:tṛṣṇā]]-[[synonyms:l:lobha]]---greed and thirst; [[synonyms:p:pite]]---to drink; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---not able; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣobha]]---agitation of the mind; [[synonyms:d:duḥkhe]]---in great distress; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:v:vidhira]]---of the creator; [[synonyms:n:nindane]]---criticizing.
translation: "If by devotional service one gets the results of pious activities and sees Lord Kṛṣṇa's face, he can relish the Lord with his eyes. His greed and thirst then increase twofold by seeing the nectarean face of Kṛṣṇa. Due to one's inability to sufficiently drink that nectar, one becomes very unhappy and criticizes the creator for not having given more than two eyes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.133
description: "When the onlooker of Kṛṣṇa's face becomes dissatisfied in this way, he thinks, 'Why didn't the creator give me thousands and millions of eyes? Why has he given me only two? Even these two eyes are disturbed by blinking, which keeps me from continuously seeing Kṛṣṇa's face.' Thus one accuses the creator of being dry and tasteless due to engaging in severe austerities. 'The creator is only a dry manufacturer. He does not know how to create and set things in their proper places.
text:
> nā dileka lakṣa-koṭi, sabe dilā āṅkhi duṭi,
> tāte dilā nimiṣa-ācchādana
> vidhi---jaḍa tapodhana, rasa-śūnya tāra mana,
> nāhi jāne yogya sṛjana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dileka]]---did not award; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---thousands and millions; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---only; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave; [[synonyms:ā:āṅkhi]] [[synonyms:d:duṭi]]---two eyes; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in them; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave; [[synonyms:n:nimiṣa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācchādana]]---covering of the eyelids; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]---creator; [[synonyms:j:jaḍa]]---dull; [[synonyms:t:tapaḥ]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---assets of austerities; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śūnya]]---without juice; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---does not know; [[synonyms:y:yogya]]---suitable; [[synonyms:s:sṛjana]]---creating.
translation: "When the onlooker of Kṛṣṇa's face becomes dissatisfied in this way, he thinks, 'Why didn't the creator give me thousands and millions of eyes? Why has he given me only two? Even these two eyes are disturbed by blinking, which keeps me from continuously seeing Kṛṣṇa's face.' Thus one accuses the creator of being dry and tasteless due to engaging in severe austerities. 'The creator is only a dry manufacturer. He does not know how to create and set things in their proper places.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.134
description: " 'The creator says, "Let those who will see Kṛṣṇa's beautiful face have two eyes." Just see the lack of consideration exhibited by this person posing as a creator. If the creator took my advice, he would give millions of eyes to the person who intends to see Śrī Kṛṣṇa's face. If the creator will accept this advice, then I would say that he is competent in his work.'
text:
> ye dekhibe kṛṣṇānana, tāra kare dvi-nayana,
> vidhi hañā hena avicāra
> mora yadi bola dhare, koṭi āṅkhi tāra kare,
> tabe jāni yogya sṛṣṭi tāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:d:dekhibe]]---will see; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānana]]---the face of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of him; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---make; [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:n:nayana]]---two eyes; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]---an authority in creation; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:h:hena]]---such; [[synonyms:a:avicāra]]---lack of consideration; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:b:bola]]---instruction; [[synonyms:d:dhare]]---accepts; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]] [[synonyms:ā:āṅkhi]]---millions of eyes; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of him; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---would create; [[synonyms:t:tabe]] [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---then I would understand; [[synonyms:y:yogya]]---suitable; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]---creation; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his.
translation: “ 'The creator says, "Let those who will see Kṛṣṇa's beautiful face have two eyes." Just see the lack of consideration exhibited by this person posing as a creator. If the creator took my advice, he would give millions of eyes to the person who intends to see Śrī Kṛṣṇa's face. If the creator will accept this advice, then I would say that he is competent in his work.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.135
description: "The transcendental form of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is compared to an ocean. A particularly extraordinary vision is the moon above that ocean, and another vision is His smile, which is sweeter than sweet and is like shining beams of moonlight." While speaking of these things with Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to remember one thing after another. Moving His hands in ecstasy, He recited a verse.
text:
> kṛṣṇāṅga-mādhurya---sindhu, sumadhura mukha---indu,
> ati-madhu smita---sukiraṇe
> e-tine lāgila mana, lobhe kare āsvādana,
> śloka paḍe svahasta-cālane
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---of the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---of sweetness; [[synonyms:s:sindhu]]---the ocean; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:madhura]]---very sweet; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---face; [[synonyms:i:indu]]---like the full moon; [[synonyms:a:ati]]-[[synonyms:m:madhu]]---extraordinarily sweet; [[synonyms:s:smita]]---smiling; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:k:kiraṇe]]---beam of moonlight; [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:t:tine]]---these three; [[synonyms:l:lāgila]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---attracted the mind; [[synonyms:l:lobhe]]---with more and more greed; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---relished; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---recites a verse; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:h:hasta]]-[[synonyms:c:cālane]]---moving His own hand.
translation: "The transcendental form of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is compared to an ocean. A particularly extraordinary vision is the moon above that ocean, and another vision is His smile, which is sweeter than sweet and is like shining beams of moonlight." While speaking of these things with Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to remember one thing after another. Moving His hands in ecstasy, He recited a verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.136
description: " 'O my Lord, the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa is very sweet, and His face is even sweeter than His body. The soft smile on His face, which is like the fragrance of honey, is sweeter still.'
text:
> madhuraṁ madhuraṁ vapur asya vibhor
> madhuraṁ madhuraṁ vadanaṁ madhuram
> madhu-gandhi mṛdu-smitam etad aho
> madhuraṁ madhuraṁ madhuraṁ madhuram

translation: “ 'O my Lord, the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa is very sweet, and His face is even sweeter than His body. The soft smile on His face, which is like the fragrance of honey, is sweeter still.'
purport: This is a verse quoted from //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta// by Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.137
description: "My dear Sanātana, the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's personality is just like an ocean of ambrosia. Although My mind is now afflicted by convulsive diseases and I wish to drink that entire ocean, the repressive physician does not allow Me to drink even one drop.
text:
> sanātana, kṛṣṇa-mādhurya---amṛtera sindhu
> mora mana---sannipāti, saba pite kare mati,
> durdaiva-vaidya nā deya eka bindu
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---O My dear Sanātana; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---the sweetness of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:amṛtera]] [[synonyms:s:sindhu]]---an ocean of ambrosia; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---my mind; [[synonyms:s:sannipāti]]---a disease of convulsions; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:p:pite]]---to drink; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:m:mati]]---desire; [[synonyms:d:durdaiva]]-[[synonyms:v:vaidya]]---a physician who suppresses; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:d:deya]]---gives; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:b:bindu]]---drop.
translation: "My dear Sanātana, the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's personality is just like an ocean of ambrosia. Although My mind is now afflicted by convulsive diseases and I wish to drink that entire ocean, the repressive physician does not allow Me to drink even one drop.
purport: When there is a combination of //kapha, pitta// and //vāyu,// the three bodily elements, there occurs //sannipāti,// or a convulsive disease. "This disease is caused by the personal features of Lord Kṛṣṇa. The three elements are the beauty of Kṛṣṇa's body, the beauty of His face, and the beauty of His smile. Stricken by these three beauties, My mind goes into convulsions. It wishes to drink the ocean of Kṛṣṇa's beauty, but because I am undergoing convulsions, My physician, who is Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself, does not even allow Me to take a drop of water from that ocean." Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was ecstatic in this way because He was presenting Himself in the mood of the //gopīs.// The //gopīs// wanted to drink the ocean of sweetness arising from the bodily features of Kṛṣṇa, but Kṛṣṇa did not allow them to come near. Consequently their desire to meet Kṛṣṇa increased, and being unable to drink the ambrosia of Kṛṣṇa's bodily features, they became very unhappy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.138
description: "Kṛṣṇa's body is a city of attractive features, and it is sweeter than sweet. His face, which is like the moon, is sweeter still, and the gentle smile on that moonlike face is like rays of moonshine.
text:
> kṛṣṇāṅga---lāvaṇya-pūra, madhura haite sumadhura,
> tāte yei mukha sudhākara
> madhura haite sumadhura, tāhā ha-ite sumadhura,
> tāra yei smita jyotsnā-bhara
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the bodily features of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:lāvaṇya]]-[[synonyms:p:pūra]]---the city of attractive beauty; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweetness; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---than; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:madhura]]---still more sweet; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in that body; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---that; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---face; [[synonyms:s:sudhākara]]---like the moon; [[synonyms:m:madhura]] [[synonyms:h:haite]] [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweeter than sweetness; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---than that; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:madhura]]---still more sweet; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---that; [[synonyms:s:smita]]---smiling; [[synonyms:j:jyotsnā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhara]]---like the moonshine.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa's body is a city of attractive features, and it is sweeter than sweet. His face, which is like the moon, is sweeter still, and the gentle smile on that moonlike face is like rays of moonshine.
purport: The smile on Kṛṣṇa's face is just like the smiling of the moon, which generates greater and greater happiness for the //gopīs.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.139
description: "The beauty of Kṛṣṇa's smile is the sweetest feature of all. His smile is like a full moon that spreads its rays throughout the three worlds-Goloka Vṛndāvana, the spiritual sky of the Vaikuṇṭhas, and Devī-dhāma, the material world. Thus Kṛṣṇa's shining beauty spreads in all ten directions.
text:
> madhura haite sumadhura, tāhā haite sumadhura,
> tāhā haite ati sumadhura
> āpanāra eka kaṇe, vyāpe saba tribhuvane,
> daśa-dik vyāpe yāra pūra
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhura]] [[synonyms:h:haite]] [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweeter than sweet; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---than that; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:madhura]]---still sweeter; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---than that; [[synonyms:a:ati]] [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:madhura]]---still much more sweet; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāra]]---of Himself; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:k:kaṇe]]---by one particle; [[synonyms:v:vyāpe]]---spreads; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvane]]---throughout the three worlds; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:d:dik]]---ten directions; [[synonyms:v:vyāpe]]---spreads; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:p:pūra]]---the city of Kṛṣṇa's beauty.
translation: "The beauty of Kṛṣṇa's smile is the sweetest feature of all. His smile is like a full moon that spreads its rays throughout the three worlds-Goloka Vṛndāvana, the spiritual sky of the Vaikuṇṭhas, and Devī-dhāma, the material world. Thus Kṛṣṇa's shining beauty spreads in all ten directions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.14
description: "To say nothing of Anantadeva, even Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself cannot find an end to His transcendental qualities. Indeed, He Himself is always eager to know them.
text:
> seho rahu---sarvajña-śiromaṇi śrī-kṛṣṇa
> nija-guṇera anta nā pāñā hayena satṛṣṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:seho]] [[synonyms:r:rahu]]---let Him (Ananta) alone; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:j:jña]]---the omniscient; [[synonyms:ś:śiromaṇi]]---the topmost; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇera]]---of His personal qualities; [[synonyms:a:anta]]---limit; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:h:hayena]]---becomes; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:t:tṛṣṇa]]---very inquisitive.
translation: "To say nothing of Anantadeva, even Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself cannot find an end to His transcendental qualities. Indeed, He Himself is always eager to know them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.140
description: "His slight smiling and fragrant illumination are compared to camphor, which enters the sweetness of the lips. That sweetness is transformed and enters into space as vibrations from the holes of His flute.
text:
> smita-kiraṇa-sukarpūre, paiśe adhara-madhure,
> sei madhu mātāya tribhuvane
> vaṁśī-chidra ākāśe, tāra guṇa śabde paiśe,
> dhvani-rūpe pāñā pariṇāme
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:smita]]-[[synonyms:k:kiraṇa]]---the shining of Kṛṣṇa's smile; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:k:karpūre]]---compared to camphor; [[synonyms:p:paiśe]]---enters; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:m:madhure]]---within the sweetness of the lips; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:m:madhu]]---that ambrosia; [[synonyms:m:mātāya]]---maddens; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvane]]---the three worlds; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:c:chidra]]---of the holes in the flute; [[synonyms:ā:ākāśe]]---in the space; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---the quality of that sweetness; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---in sound vibration; [[synonyms:p:paiśe]]---enters; [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---the form of sound vibration; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---obtaining; [[synonyms:p:pariṇāme]]---by transformation.
translation: "His slight smiling and fragrant illumination are compared to camphor, which enters the sweetness of the lips. That sweetness is transformed and enters into space as vibrations from the holes of His flute.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.141
description: "The sound of Kṛṣṇa's flute spreads in four directions. Even though Kṛṣṇa vibrates His flute within this universe, its sound pierces the universal covering and goes to the spiritual sky. Thus the vibration enters the ears of all inhabitants. It especially enters Goloka Vṛndāvana-dhāma and attracts the minds of the young damsels of Vrajabhūmi, bringing them forcibly to where Kṛṣṇa is present.
text:
> se dhvani caudike dhāya, aṇḍa bhedi' vaikuṇṭhe yāya,
> bale paiśe jagatera kāṇe
> sabā mātoyāla kari', balātkāre āne dhari',
> viśeṣataḥ yuvatīra gaṇe

translation: "The sound of Kṛṣṇa's flute spreads in four directions. Even though Kṛṣṇa vibrates His flute within this universe, its sound pierces the universal covering and goes to the spiritual sky. Thus the vibration enters the ears of all inhabitants. It especially enters Goloka Vṛndāvana-dhāma and attracts the minds of the young damsels of Vrajabhūmi, bringing them forcibly to where Kṛṣṇa is present.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.142
description: "The vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute is very aggressive, and it breaks the vows of all chaste women. Indeed, its vibration takes them forcibly from the laps of their husbands. The vibration of His flute attracts even the goddesses of fortune in the Vaikuṇṭha planets, to say nothing of the poor damsels of Vṛndāvana.
text:
> dhvani---baḍa uddhata, pativratāra bhāṅge vrata,
> pati-kola haite ṭāni' āne
> vaikuṇṭhera lakṣmī-gaṇe, yei kare ākarṣaṇe,
> tāra āge kebā gopī-gaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---vibration; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very much; [[synonyms:u:uddhata]]---aggressive; [[synonyms:p:pati]]-[[synonyms:v:vratāra]]---of chaste wives; [[synonyms:b:bhāṅge]]---breaks; [[synonyms:v:vrata]]---the vow; [[synonyms:p:pati]]---of the husband; [[synonyms:k:kola]]---the lap; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭāni']]---taking; [[synonyms:ā:āne]]---brings; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭhera]]---of the Vaikuṇṭha planets; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---all the goddesses of fortune; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---that which; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaṇe]]---attracts; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:k:kebā]]---what to speak of; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the //gopīs// of Vṛndāvana.
translation: "The vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute is very aggressive, and it breaks the vows of all chaste women. Indeed, its vibration takes them forcibly from the laps of their husbands. The vibration of His flute attracts even the goddesses of fortune in the Vaikuṇṭha planets, to say nothing of the poor damsels of Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.143
description: "The vibration of His flute slackens the knots of their underwear even in front of their husbands. Thus the gopīs are forced to abandon their household duties and come before Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way all social etiquette, shame and fear are vanquished. The vibration of His flute causes all women to dance.
text:
> nīvi khasāya pati-āge, gṛha-dharma karāya tyāge,
> bale dhari' āne kṛṣṇa-sthāne
> loka-dharma, lajjā, bhaya, saba jñāna lupta haya,
> aiche nācāya saba nārī-gaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nīvi]]---the knots of the underwear; [[synonyms:k:khasāya]]---loosens; [[synonyms:p:pati]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---even in front of the husbands; [[synonyms:g:gṛha]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---household duties; [[synonyms:k:karāya]] [[synonyms:t:tyāge]]---causes to give up; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---by force; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching; [[synonyms:ā:āne]]---brings; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---before Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---social etiquette; [[synonyms:l:lajjā]]---shame; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---such knowledge; [[synonyms:l:lupta]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes hidden; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:n:nācāya]]---causes to dance; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the women.
translation: "The vibration of His flute slackens the knots of their underwear even in front of their husbands. Thus the gopīs are forced to abandon their household duties and come before Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way all social etiquette, shame and fear are vanquished. The vibration of His flute causes all women to dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.144
description: "The vibration of His flute is just like a bird that creates a nest within the ears of the gopīs and always remains prominent there, not allowing any other sound to enter their ears. Indeed, the gopīs cannot hear anything else, nor are they able to concentrate on anything else, not even to give a suitable reply. Such are the effects of the vibration of Lord Kṛṣṇa's flute."
text:
> kāṇera bhitara vāsā kare, āpane tāṅhā sadā sphure,
> anya śabda nā deya praveśite
> āna kathā nā śune kāṇa, āna balite bolaya āna,
> ei kṛṣṇera vaṁśīra carite
