> eka kṛṣṇa-deha haite sabāra prakāśe
> kṣaṇeke sabāi sei śarīre praveśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:deha]]---transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---the manifestation; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇeke]]---in a second; [[synonyms:s:sabāi]]---every one of Them; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ś:śarīre]]---in that body of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:praveśe]]---enter.
translation: "All these transcendental bodies emanated from the body of Kṛṣṇa, and within a second They all entered again into His body.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.24
description: "When the Lord Brahmā from this universe saw this pastime, he was astonished and struck with wonder. After offering his prayers, he gave the following conclusion.
text:
> ihā dekhi' brahmā hailā mohita, vismita
> stuti kari' ei pāche karilā niścita
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ihā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing this; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mohita]]---astonished; [[synonyms:v:vismita]]---struck with wonder; [[synonyms:s:stuti]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---offering prayers; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---at the end; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---made; [[synonyms:n:niścita]]---conclusion.
translation: "When the Lord Brahmā from this universe saw this pastime, he was astonished and struck with wonder. After offering his prayers, he gave the following conclusion.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.25
description: "Lord Brahmā said, 'If someone says that he knows everything about Kṛṣṇa's opulence, let him think that way. However, as far as I am concerned, with my body and mind I consider it in this way.
text:
> "ye kahe---'kṛṣṇera vaibhava muñi saba jānoṅ'
> se jānuka,---kāya-mane muñi ei mānoṅ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---if anyone says; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]---opulences; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:j:jānoṅ]]---know; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:j:jānuka]]---let him know; [[synonyms:k:kāya]]-[[synonyms:m:mane]]---by my body and mind; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---myself; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mānoṅ]]---accept.
translation: "Lord Brahmā said, 'If someone says that he knows everything about Kṛṣṇa's opulence, let him think that way. However, as far as I am concerned, with my body and mind I consider it in this way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.26
description: " 'My Lord, Your opulence is like an unlimited ocean of nectar, and it is verbally and mentally impossible for me to realize even a drop of that ocean.
text:
> ei ye tomāra ananta vaibhavāmṛta-sindhu
> mora vāṅ-mano-gamya nahe eka bindu
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:y:ye]]---all this; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:s:sindhu]]---ocean of the nectar of Your opulence; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:v:vāk]]-[[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:g:gamya]]---within the reach of words and mind; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:b:bindu]]---even a drop.
translation: “ 'My Lord, Your opulence is like an unlimited ocean of nectar, and it is verbally and mentally impossible for me to realize even a drop of that ocean.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.27
description: " 'There are people who say, "I know everything about Kṛṣṇa." Let them think that way. As far as I am concerned, I do not wish to speak very much about this matter. O my Lord, let me say this much. As far as Your opulences are concerned, they are all beyond the reach of my mind, body and words.'
text:
> jānanta eva jānantu
> kiṁ bahūktyā na me prabho
> manaso vapuṣo vāco
> vaibhavaṁ tava gocaraḥ"
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jānantaḥ]]---persons who think they are aware of Your unlimited potency; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:j:jānantu]]---let them think like that; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what is the use; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:u:uktyā]]---with many words; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:m:me]]---my; [[synonyms:p:prabho]]---O Lord; [[synonyms:m:manasaḥ]]---of the mind; [[synonyms:v:vapuṣaḥ]]---of the body; [[synonyms:v:vācaḥ]]---of the words; [[synonyms:v:vaibhavam]]---opulences; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:g:gocaraḥ]]---within the range.
translation: “ 'There are people who say, "I know everything about Kṛṣṇa." Let them think that way. As far as I am concerned, I do not wish to speak very much about this matter. O my Lord, let me say this much. As far as Your opulences are concerned, they are all beyond the reach of my mind, body and words.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.14.38), spoken by Lord Brahmā after he had stolen Lord Kṛṣṇa's cows, calves and cowherd boys and Kṛṣṇa had exhibited His transcendental opulence by re-creating all the stolen cows, calves and cowherd boys by His //viṣṇu-mūrti// expansions. After he had seen this, Brahmā offered the above prayer.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.28
description: "Let the glories of Lord Kṛṣṇa be! Who could be aware of all of them? His abode, Vṛndāvana, has many wonderful opulences. Just try to see them all.
text:
> kṛṣṇera mahimā rahu---kebā tāra jñātā
> vṛndāvana-sthānera dekha āścarya vibhutā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---glories; [[synonyms:r:rahu]]---let be; [[synonyms:k:kebā]]---//who//; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of those; [[synonyms:j:jñātā]]---a knower; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:s:sthānera]]---of the abode of Kṛṣṇa, Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:d:dekha]]---just see; [[synonyms:ā:āścarya]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:v:vibhutā]]---opulences.
translation: "Let the glories of Lord Kṛṣṇa be! Who could be aware of all of them? His abode, Vṛndāvana, has many wonderful opulences. Just try to see them all.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.29
description: "According to the revelations of revealed scripture, Vṛndāvana extends only sixteen krośas [thirty-two miles]. Nonetheless, all the Vaikuṇṭha planets and innumerable universes are located in one corner of this tract.
text:
> ṣola-krośa vṛndāvana,---śāstrera prakāśe
> tāra eka-deśe vaikuṇṭhājāṇḍa-gaṇa bhāse
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣola]]-[[synonyms:k:krośa]]---measuring sixteen //krośas// (thirty-two miles); [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana-dhāma; [[synonyms:ś:śāstrera]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---according to the revelation of revealed scripture; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in one corner; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]]---all the Vaikuṇṭha planets; [[synonyms:a:ajāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the innumerable universes; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---are situated.
translation: "According to the revelations of revealed scripture, Vṛndāvana extends only sixteen krośas [thirty-two miles]. Nonetheless, all the Vaikuṇṭha planets and innumerable universes are located in one corner of this tract.
purport: In Vraja, the land is divided into various //vanas,// or forests. The forests total twelve, and their extension is estimated to be eighty-four //krośas.// Of these, the special forest known as Vṛndāvana is located from the present municipal city of Vṛndāvana to the village called Nanda-grāma. This distance is sixteen //krośas// (thirty-two miles).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.3
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "All the transcendental forms of the Lord are situated in the spiritual sky. They preside over spiritual planets in that abode, but there is no counting those Vaikuṇṭha planets.
text:
> sarva svarūpera dhāma---paravyoma-dhāme
> pṛthak pṛthak vaikuṇṭha saba, nāhika gaṇane
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:s:svarūpera]]---of the personal forms; [[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---abode; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:v:vyoma]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāme]]---in the spiritual sky; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]] [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---separate; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]]---Vaikuṇṭha planets; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇane]]---there is no counting.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "All the transcendental forms of the Lord are situated in the spiritual sky. They preside over spiritual planets in that abode, but there is no counting those Vaikuṇṭha planets.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.30
description: "No one can estimate the opulence of Kṛṣṇa. That is unlimited. However, just as one sees the moon through the branches of a tree, I wish to give a little indication."
text:
> apāra aiśvarya kṛṣṇera---nāhika gaṇana
> śākhā-candra-nyāye kari dig-daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---opulence; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---there is no estimation; [[synonyms:ś:śākhā]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]-[[synonyms:n:nyāye]]---according to the logic of seeing the moon through the branches of a tree; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I make; [[synonyms:d:dik]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---an indication only.
translation: "No one can estimate the opulence of Kṛṣṇa. That is unlimited. However, just as one sees the moon through the branches of a tree, I wish to give a little indication."
purport: First a child is shown the branches of a tree, and then he is shown the moon through the branches. This is called //śākhā-candra-nyāya.// The idea is that first one must be given a simpler example. Then the more difficult background is explained.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.31
description: While describing the transcendental opulences of Kṛṣṇa, the ocean of opulence manifested in the mind of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and His mind and senses were immersed in this ocean. Thus He was perplexed.
text:
> aiśvarya kahite sphurila aiśvarya-sāgara
> manendriya ḍubilā, prabhu ha-ilā phāṅpara
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---opulence; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to describe; [[synonyms:s:sphurila]]---there manifested; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]-[[synonyms:s:sāgara]]---an ocean of opulence; [[synonyms:m:mana]]-[[synonyms:i:indriya]]---the chief sense, namely the mind; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍubilā]]---immersed; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:p:phāṅpara]]---perplexed.
translation: While describing the transcendental opulences of Kṛṣṇa, the ocean of opulence manifested in the mind of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and His mind and senses were immersed in this ocean. Thus He was perplexed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.32
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally recited the following verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and to relish the meaning, He began to explain it Himself.
text:
> bhāgavatera ei śloka paḍilā āpane
> artha āsvādite sukhe karena vyākhyāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāgavatera]]---of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verse; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---recited; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meaning; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādite]]---to taste; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in happiness; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:v:vyākhyāne]]---describes the meaning.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally recited the following verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and to relish the meaning, He began to explain it Himself.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.33
description: " 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, is the master of the three worlds and the three principal demigods [Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva]. No one is equal to or greater than Him. By His spiritual potency, known as svārājya-lakṣmī, all His desires are fulfilled. While offering their dues and presents in worship, the predominating deities of all the planets touch the lotus feet of the Lord with their helmets. Thus they offer prayers to the Lord.'
text:
> svayaṁ tv asāmyātiśayas tryadhīśaḥ
> svārājya-lakṣmy-āpta-samasta-kāmaḥ
> baliṁ haradbhiś cira-loka-pālaiḥ
> kirīṭa-koṭīḍita-pāda-pīṭhaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---personally the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:a:asāmya]]-[[synonyms:a:atiśayaḥ]]---who has no equal nor superior; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:a:adhīśaḥ]]---the master of three places, namely Goloka Vṛndāvana, Vaikuṇṭhaloka and the material world, or the master of Mahā-Viṣṇu, Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, or the master of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara, or the master of the three worlds (the higher, lower and middle planetary systems); [[synonyms:s:svārājya]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---by His personal spiritual potency; [[synonyms:ā:āpta]]---already achieved; [[synonyms:s:samasta]]-[[synonyms:k:kāmaḥ]]---all desirable objects; [[synonyms:b:balim]]---a presentation or taxation; [[synonyms:h:haradbhiḥ]]---who are offering; [[synonyms:c:cira]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:p:pālaiḥ]]---by the predominating deities of different planets; [[synonyms:k:kirīṭa]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---by millions of helmets; [[synonyms:ī:īḍita]]---being worshiped; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:pīṭhaḥ]]---whose lotus feet.
translation: “ 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, is the master of the three worlds and the three principal demigods [Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva]. No one is equal to or greater than Him. By His spiritual potency, known as svārājya-lakṣmī, all His desires are fulfilled. While offering their dues and presents in worship, the predominating deities of all the planets touch the lotus feet of the Lord with their helmets. Thus they offer prayers to the Lord.'
purport: This quotation is verse 21 of the Second Chapter, Third Canto of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.34
description: "Kṛṣṇa is the original Supreme Personality of Godhead; therefore He is the greatest of all. No one is equal to Him, nor is anyone greater than Him.
text:
> parama īśvara kṛṣṇa svayaṁ bhagavān
> tāte baḍa, tāṅra sama keha nāhi āna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:parama]]---supreme; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---controller; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---personally; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the original Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---most exalted; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:ā:āna]]---else.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa is the original Supreme Personality of Godhead; therefore He is the greatest of all. No one is equal to Him, nor is anyone greater than Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.35
description: " 'Kṛṣṇa, known as Govinda, is the supreme controller. He has an eternal, blissful, spiritual body. He is the origin of all. He has no other origin, for He is the prime cause of all causes.'
text:
> īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
> sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ
> anādir ādir govindaḥ
> sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam
synonyms: [[synonyms:ī:īśvaraḥ]]---the controller; [[synonyms:p:paramaḥ]]---supreme; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sat]]---eternal existence; [[synonyms:c:cit]]---absolute knowledge; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---absolute bliss; [[synonyms:v:vigrahaḥ]]---whose form; [[synonyms:a:anādiḥ]]---without beginning; [[synonyms:ā:ādiḥ]]---the origin; [[synonyms:g:govindaḥ]]---Lord Govinda; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kāraṇam]]---the cause of all causes.
translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa, known as Govinda, is the supreme controller. He has an eternal, blissful, spiritual body. He is the origin of all. He has no other origin, for He is the prime cause of all causes.'
purport: This is the first verse of the Fifth Chapter of //Brahma-saṁhitā.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.36
description: "The primary predominating deities of this material creation are Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and Lord Viṣṇu. Nonetheless, they simply carry out the orders of Lord Kṛṣṇa, who is master of them all.
text:
> brahmā, viṣṇu, hara,---ei sṛṣṭyādi-īśvara
> tine ājñākārī kṛṣṇera, kṛṣṇa---adhīśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:h:hara]]---and Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---they; [[synonyms:s:sṛṣṭi]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the masters of material creation, maintenance and dissolution; [[synonyms:t:tine]]---all three of them; [[synonyms:ā:ājñākārī]]---order carriers; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:adhīśvara]]---their master.
translation: "The primary predominating deities of this material creation are Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and Lord Viṣṇu. Nonetheless, they simply carry out the orders of Lord Kṛṣṇa, who is master of them all.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.37
description: "Lord Brahmā said, 'Following the will of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, I create, Lord Śiva destroys, and He Himself in the form of Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu maintains all the affairs of material nature. Thus the supreme controller of the three modes of material nature is Lord Viṣṇu.'
text:
> sṛjāmi tan-niyukto 'haṁ
> haro harati tad-vaśaḥ
> viśvaṁ puruṣa-rūpeṇa
> paripāti triśakti-dhṛk
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sṛjāmi]]---create; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:n:niyuktaḥ]]---engaged by Him; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:h:haraḥ]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:h:harati]]---annihilates; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśaḥ]]---under His control; [[synonyms:v:viśvam]]---the whole universe; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpeṇa]]---in the form of Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:p:paripāti]]---maintains; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:d:dhṛk]]---the controller of the three modes of material nature.
translation: "Lord Brahmā said, 'Following the will of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, I create, Lord Śiva destroys, and He Himself in the form of Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu maintains all the affairs of material nature. Thus the supreme controller of the three modes of material nature is Lord Viṣṇu.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:6:32|(2.6.32)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.38
description: "This is only a general description. Please try to understand another meaning of tryadhīśa. The three puruṣa incarnations of Viṣṇu are the original cause of the material creation.
text:
> e sāmānya, tryadhīśvarera śuna artha āra
> jagat-kāraṇa tina puruṣāvatāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:e]] [[synonyms:s:sāmānya]]---this is a general description; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:a:adhīśvarera]]---of the master of the three worlds; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause of the material creation; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---//puruṣa// incarnations of Viṣṇu.
translation: "This is only a general description. Please try to understand another meaning of tryadhīśa. The three puruṣa incarnations of Viṣṇu are the original cause of the material creation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.39
description: "Mahā-Viṣṇu, Padmanābha and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu are the Supersouls of all subtle and gross existences.
text:
> mahā-viṣṇu, padmanābha, kṣīrodaka-svāmī
> ei tina---sthūla-sūkṣma-sarva-antaryāmī
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:p:padmanābha]]---Padmanābha (Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu); [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]-[[synonyms:u:udaka]]-[[synonyms:s:svāmī]]---Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:tina]]---all these three; [[synonyms:s:sthūla]]-[[synonyms:s:sūkṣma]]---gross and subtle; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---of all; [[synonyms:a:antaryāmī]]---the Supersoul.
translation: "Mahā-Viṣṇu, Padmanābha and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu are the Supersouls of all subtle and gross existences.
purport: Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu is known as Kāraṇodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, the Supersoul of everything. Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, from whose lotus navel Brahmā was created, is also called Hiraṇyagarbha and is the total Supersoul and the subtle Supersoul. Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu is the universal form and the gross Supersoul.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.4
description: "The breadth of each Vaikuṇṭha planet is described as eight miles multiplied by one hundred, by one thousand, by ten thousand, by one hundred thousand, and by ten million. In other words, each Vaikuṇṭha planet is expanded beyond our ability to measure.
text:
> śata, sahasra, ayuta, lakṣa, koṭī-yojana
> eka eka vaikuṇṭhera vistāra varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śata]]---a hundred; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]---a thousand; [[synonyms:a:ayuta]]---ten thousand; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---a hundred thousand; [[synonyms:k:koṭī]]---ten million; [[synonyms:y:yojana]]---a distance of eight miles; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:e:eka]]---each and every one; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭhera]]---of the spiritual planets; [[synonyms:v:vistāra]]---the breadth; [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---description.
translation: "The breadth of each Vaikuṇṭha planet is described as eight miles multiplied by one hundred, by one thousand, by ten thousand, by one hundred thousand, and by ten million. In other words, each Vaikuṇṭha planet is expanded beyond our ability to measure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.40
description: "Although Mahā-Viṣṇu, Padmanābha and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu are all shelters and controllers of the entire universe, They are nonetheless but plenary portions or portions of the plenary portions of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore He is the original Personality of Godhead.
text:
> ei tina---sarvāśraya, jagat-īśvara
> eho saba kalā-aṁśa, kṛṣṇa---adhīśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:tina]]---these three; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśraya]]---the shelter of the whole material creation; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---supreme controllers of the universe; [[synonyms:e:eho]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of Them; [[synonyms:k:kalā]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---plenary portions, or portions of the plenary portions; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:adhīśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: "Although Mahā-Viṣṇu, Padmanābha and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu are all shelters and controllers of the entire universe, They are nonetheless but plenary portions or portions of the plenary portions of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore He is the original Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.41
description: " 'The Brahmās and other lords of the mundane worlds appear from the pores of the Mahā-Viṣṇu and remain alive for the duration of His one exhalation. I adore the primeval Lord, Govinda, for Mahā-Viṣṇu is a portion of His plenary portion.'
text:
> yasyaika-niśvasita-kālam athāvalambya
> jīvanti loma-vilajā jagad-aṇḍa-nāthāḥ
> viṣṇur mahān sa iha yasya kalā-viśeṣo
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---whose; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:n:niśvasita]]---of breath; [[synonyms:k:kālam]]---time; [[synonyms:a:atha]]---thus; [[synonyms:a:avalambya]]---taking shelter of; [[synonyms:j:jīvanti]]---live; [[synonyms:l:loma]]-[[synonyms:v:vilajāḥ]]---grown from the hair holes; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:a:aṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāthāḥ]]---the masters of the universes (the Brahmās); [[synonyms:v:viṣṇuḥ]] [[synonyms:m:mahān]]---the Supreme Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---here; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---whose; [[synonyms:k:kalā]]-[[synonyms:v:viśeṣaḥ]]---particular plenary portion or expansion; [[synonyms:g:govindam]]---Lord Govinda; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣam]]---the original person; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---Him; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bhajāmi]]---worship.
translation: “ 'The Brahmās and other lords of the mundane worlds appear from the pores of the Mahā-Viṣṇu and remain alive for the duration of His one exhalation. I adore the primeval Lord, Govinda, for Mahā-Viṣṇu is a portion of His plenary portion.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.48). See also //Ādi-līlā// (5.71).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.42
description: "This is the middle meaning. Now please hear the confidential meaning. Lord Kṛṣṇa has three places of residence, which are well known from revealed scriptures.
text:
> ei artha---madhyama, śuna 'gūḍha' artha āra
> tina āvāsa-sthāna kṛṣṇera śāstre khyāti yāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---this explanation; [[synonyms:m:madhyama]]---middle; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:g:gūḍha]]---confidential; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:ā:āvāsa]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---residential places; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śāstre]]---in the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:k:khyāti]]---fame; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which.
translation: "This is the middle meaning. Now please hear the confidential meaning. Lord Kṛṣṇa has three places of residence, which are well known from revealed scriptures.
purport: Kṛṣṇa has three abodes-His internal abode (Goloka Vṛndāvana), His intermediate abode (the spiritual sky), and His external abode (this material world).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.43
description: "The internal abode is called Goloka Vṛndāvana. It is there that Lord Kṛṣṇa's personal friends, associates, father and mother live.
text:
> 'antaḥpura'---goloka-śrī-vṛndāvana
> yāhāṅ nitya-sthiti mātā-pitā-bandhu-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]-[[synonyms:p:pura]]---the internal abode; [[synonyms:g:goloka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Goloka Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]-[[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---eternal residence; [[synonyms:m:mātā]]-[[synonyms:p:pitā]]---mother and father; [[synonyms:b:bandhu]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---and friends.
translation: "The internal abode is called Goloka Vṛndāvana. It is there that Lord Kṛṣṇa's personal friends, associates, father and mother live.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.44
description: "Vṛndāvana is the storehouse of Kṛṣṇa's mercy and the sweet opulences of conjugal love. That is where the spiritual energy, working as a maidservant, exhibits the rāsa dance, the quintessence of all pastimes.
text:
> madhuraiśvarya-mādhurya-kṛpādi-bhāṇḍāra
> yogamāyā dāsī yāhāṅ rāsādi līlā-sāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhura]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---of sweetness and opulence; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---of conjugal love; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and of mercy and so on; [[synonyms:b:bhāṇḍāra]]---storehouse; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]-[[synonyms:m:māyā]]---the spiritual energy; [[synonyms:d:dāsī]]---maidservant; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the //rāsa// dance and other pastimes; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the quintessence of all pastimes.
translation: "Vṛndāvana is the storehouse of Kṛṣṇa's mercy and the sweet opulences of conjugal love. That is where the spiritual energy, working as a maidservant, exhibits the rāsa dance, the quintessence of all pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.45
description: "Vṛndāvana-dhāma is very soft due to the mercy of the Supreme Lord, and it is especially opulent due to conjugal love. The transcendental glories of the son of Mahārāja Nanda are exhibited here. Under the circumstances, not the least anxiety is awakened within us.
text:
> karuṇā-nikuramba-komale
> madhuraiśvarya-viśeṣa-śālini
> jayati vraja-rāja-nandane
> na hi cintā-kaṇikābhyudeti naḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:karuṇā]]-[[synonyms:n:nikuramba]]-[[synonyms:k:komale]]---who is very soft because of great mercy; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]-[[synonyms:v:viśeṣa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śalini]]---especially by the opulence of conjugal love; [[synonyms:j:jayati]]---all glories; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:n:nandane]]---to the son of Mahārāja Nanda; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:c:cintā]]---of anxiety; [[synonyms:k:kaṇika]]---even a particle; [[synonyms:a:abhyudeti]]---awakens; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---of us.
translation: "Vṛndāvana-dhāma is very soft due to the mercy of the Supreme Lord, and it is especially opulent due to conjugal love. The transcendental glories of the son of Mahārāja Nanda are exhibited here. Under the circumstances, not the least anxiety is awakened within us.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.46
description: "Below the Vṛndāvana planet is the spiritual sky, which is known as Viṣṇuloka. In Viṣṇuloka there are innumerable Vaikuṇṭha planets controlled by Nārāyaṇa and other innumerable expansions of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> tāra tale paravyoma---'viṣṇuloka'-nāma
> nārāyaṇa-ādi ananta svarūpera dhāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:t:tale]]---below Vṛndāvana-dhāma; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:v:vyoma]]---the spiritual sky; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---known as Viṣṇuloka; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---Nārāyaṇa and others; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpera]]---of personal expansions; [[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---the place.
translation: "Below the Vṛndāvana planet is the spiritual sky, which is known as Viṣṇuloka. In Viṣṇuloka there are innumerable Vaikuṇṭha planets controlled by Nārāyaṇa and other innumerable expansions of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.47
description: "The spiritual sky, which is full in all six opulences, is the interim residence of Lord Kṛṣṇa. It is there that an unlimited number of forms of Kṛṣṇa enjoy Their pastimes.
text:
> 'madhyama-āvāsa' kṛṣṇera---ṣaḍ-aiśvarya-bhāṇḍāra
> ananta svarūpe yāhāṅ karena vihāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhyama]]-[[synonyms:ā:āvāsa]]---the middle residence; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṭ]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāṇḍāra]]---the storehouse of six opulences; [[synonyms:a:ananta]] [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in unlimited forms; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:v:vihāra]]---enjoys His pastimes.
translation: "The spiritual sky, which is full in all six opulences, is the interim residence of Lord Kṛṣṇa. It is there that an unlimited number of forms of Kṛṣṇa enjoy Their pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.48
description: "Innumerable Vaikuṇṭha planets, which are just like different rooms of a treasure-house, are all there, filled with all opulences. Those unlimited planets house the Lord's eternal associates, who are also enriched with the six opulences."
text:
> ananta vaikuṇṭha yāhāṅ bhāṇḍāra-koṭhari
> pāriṣada-gaṇe ṣaḍ-aiśvarye āche bhari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]]---Vaikuṇṭha planets; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:b:bhāṇḍāra]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭhari]]---like rooms of a treasure-house; [[synonyms:p:pāriṣada]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---eternal associates; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṭ]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarye]]---with the six opulences; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---are; [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---filling.
translation: "Innumerable Vaikuṇṭha planets, which are just like different rooms of a treasure-house, are all there, filled with all opulences. Those unlimited planets house the Lord's eternal associates, who are also enriched with the six opulences."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.49
description: " 'Below the planet named Goloka Vṛndāvana are the planets known as Devī-dhāma, Maheśa-dhāma and Hari-dhāma. These are opulent in different ways. They are managed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Govinda, the original Lord. I offer my obeisances unto Him.'
text:
> goloka-nāmni nija-dhāmni tale ca tasya
> devī-maheśa-hari-dhāmasu teṣu teṣu
> te te prabhāva-nicayā vihitāś ca yena
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:goloka]]-[[synonyms:n:nāmni]] [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāmni]]---in the planet known as Goloka Vṛndāvana, the personal abode of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tale]]---in the part underneath; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:t:tasya]]---of that; [[synonyms:d:devī]]---of the goddess Durgā; [[synonyms:m:maheśa]]---of Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:h:hari]]---of Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:d:dhāmasu]]---in the planets; [[synonyms:t:teṣu]] [[synonyms:t:teṣu]]---in each of them; [[synonyms:t:te]] [[synonyms:t:te]]---those respective; [[synonyms:p:prabhāva]]-[[synonyms:n:nicayāḥ]]---opulences; [[synonyms:v:vihitāḥ]]---established; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---by whom; [[synonyms:g:govindam]]---unto that Govinda; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣam]]---the original Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bhajāmi]]---offer my obeisances.
translation: “ 'Below the planet named Goloka Vṛndāvana are the planets known as Devī-dhāma, Maheśa-dhāma and Hari-dhāma. These are opulent in different ways. They are managed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Govinda, the original Lord. I offer my obeisances unto Him.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.43).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.5
description: "Each Vaikuṇṭha planet is very large, and each is made of spiritual bliss. The inhabitants are all associates of the Supreme Lord, and they have full opulence like the Lord Himself. Thus they are all situated.
text:
> saba vaikuṇṭha---vyāpaka, ānanda-cinmaya
> pāriṣada-ṣaḍaiśvarya-pūrṇa saba haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]]---the spiritual planets; [[synonyms:v:vyāpaka]]---vast; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---made of spiritual bliss; [[synonyms:p:pāriṣada]]---associates; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṭ]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---six kinds of opulence; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---in full; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are.
translation: "Each Vaikuṇṭha planet is very large, and each is made of spiritual bliss. The inhabitants are all associates of the Supreme Lord, and they have full opulence like the Lord Himself. Thus they are all situated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.50
description: " 'Between the spiritual and material worlds is a body of water known as the river Virajā. This water is generated from the bodily perspiration of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is known as Vedāṅga. Thus the river flows.'
text:
> pradhāna-parama-vyomnor
> antare virajā nadī
> vedāṅga-sveda-janitais
> toyaiḥ prasrāvitā śubhā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]-[[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:v:vyomnoḥ]] [[synonyms:a:antare]]---between the material world and spiritual world; [[synonyms:v:virajā]] [[synonyms:n:nadī]]---is a river known as Virajā; [[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---of the transcendental body of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:sveda]]-[[synonyms:j:janitaiḥ]]---produced from the perspiration; [[synonyms:t:toyaiḥ]]---with water; [[synonyms:p:prasrāvitā]]---flowing; [[synonyms:ś:śubhā]]---all-auspicious.
translation: “ 'Between the spiritual and material worlds is a body of water known as the river Virajā. This water is generated from the bodily perspiration of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is known as Vedāṅga. Thus the river flows.'
purport: This verse and the following verse are from the //Padma Purāṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.51
description: " 'Beyond the river Virajā is a spiritual nature, which is indestructible, eternal, inexhaustible and unlimited. It is the supreme abode consisting of three fourths of the Lord's opulences. It is known as paravyoma, the spiritual sky.'
text:
> tasyāḥ pāre paravyoma
> tripād-bhūtaṁ sanātanam
> amṛtaṁ śāśvataṁ nityam
> anantaṁ paramaṁ padam
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tasyāḥ]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---on the other bank of the Virajā River; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:v:vyoma]]---the spiritual sky; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:p:pād]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūtam]]---existing as three fourths of the opulence of the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:s:sanātanam]]---eternal; [[synonyms:a:amṛtam]]---without deterioration; [[synonyms:ś:śāśvatam]]---without being subjected to the control of time; [[synonyms:n:nityam]]---constantly existing; [[synonyms:a:anantam]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:p:paramam]]---supreme; [[synonyms:p:padam]]---abode.
translation: “ 'Beyond the river Virajā is a spiritual nature, which is indestructible, eternal, inexhaustible and unlimited. It is the supreme abode consisting of three fourths of the Lord's opulences. It is known as paravyoma, the spiritual sky.'
purport: In the spiritual sky there is neither anxiety nor fear. It is eternally existing, and it consists of three fourths of the Lord's energy. The material world is an exhibition of only one fourth of the Lord's energy. Therefore it is called //eka-pāda-vibhūti.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.52
description: "On the other side of the river Virajā is the external abode, which is full of unlimited universes, each containing unlimited atmospheres.
text:
> tāra tale 'bāhyāvāsa' virajāra pāra
> ananta brahmāṇḍa yāhāṅ koṭhari apāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:t:tale]]---below the spiritual world; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]-[[synonyms:ā:āvāsa]]---external abode; [[synonyms:v:virajāra]] [[synonyms:p:pāra]]---on the other side of the river Virajā; [[synonyms:a:ananta]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]---unlimited number of universes; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:k:koṭhari]]---apartments; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimited.
translation: "On the other side of the river Virajā is the external abode, which is full of unlimited universes, each containing unlimited atmospheres.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.53
description: "The abode of the external energy is called Devī-dhāma, and its inhabitants are conditioned souls. It is there that the material energy, Durgā, resides with many opulent maidservants.
text:
> 'devī-dhāma' nāma tāra, jīva yāra vāsī
> jagal-lakṣmī rākhi' rahe yāhāṅ māyā dāsī
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:devī]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---the place of the external energy; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---its; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---the conditioned living entities; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---the inhabitants; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---the material energy; [[synonyms:r:rākhi']]---keeping them; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---exists; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherein; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---the external energy; [[synonyms:d:dāsī]]---maidservant.
translation: "The abode of the external energy is called Devī-dhāma, and its inhabitants are conditioned souls. It is there that the material energy, Durgā, resides with many opulent maidservants.
purport: Because he wants to enjoy the material energy, the conditioned soul is allowed to reside in Devī-dhāma, the external energy, where the goddess Durgā carries out the orders of the Supreme Lord as His maidservant. The material energy is called //jagal-lakṣmī// because she protects the bewildered conditioned souls. The goddess Durgā is therefore known as the mother, and Lord Śiva, her husband, is known as the father. Lord Śiva and goddess Durgā are therefore known as the material father and mother. Goddess Durgā is so named because this material world is like a big fort where the conditioned soul is placed under her care. For material facilities, the conditioned soul tries to please the goddess Durgā, and mother Durgā supplies all kinds of material facilities. Because of this, the conditioned souls are allured and do not wish to leave the external energy. Consequently they are continuously making plans to live here peacefully and happily. Such is the material world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.54
description: "Kṛṣṇa is the supreme proprietor of all dhāmas, including Goloka-dhāma, Vaikuṇṭha-dhāma and Devī-dhāma. The paravyoma and Goloka-dhāma are beyond Devī-dhāma, this material world.
text:
> ei tina dhāmera haya kṛṣṇa adhīśvara
> goloka-paravyoma---prakṛtira para
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:d:dhāmera]]---of these three //dhāmas,// or residential places, namely Goloka Vṛndāvana-dhāma, Vaikuṇṭha-dhāma (Hari-dhāma) and Devī-dhāma (the material world); [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:adhīśvara]]---the supreme master; [[synonyms:g:goloka]]-[[synonyms:p:paravyoma]]---the spiritual planet Goloka and the spiritual sky; [[synonyms:p:prakṛtira]] [[synonyms:p:para]]---beyond this material energy.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa is the supreme proprietor of all dhāmas, including Goloka-dhāma, Vaikuṇṭha-dhāma and Devī-dhāma. The paravyoma and Goloka-dhāma are beyond Devī-dhāma, this material world.
purport: When a living entity is liberated from Devī-dhāma but does not know of the opulence of Hari-dhāma, he is placed in Maheśa-dhāma, which is between the other two //dhāmas.// The liberated soul does not get an opportunity to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead there; therefore although this Maheśa-dhāma is Lord Śiva's //dhāma// and above the Devī-dhāma, it is not the spiritual world. The spiritual world begins with Hari-dhāma, or Vaikuṇṭhaloka.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.55
description: "The spiritual world is considered to be three fourths of the energy and opulence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whereas this material world is only one fourth of that energy. That is our understanding.
text:
> cic-chakti-vibhūti-dhāma---tripād-aiśvarya-nāma
> māyika vibhūti---eka-pāda abhidhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---of the spiritual energy; [[synonyms:v:vibhūti]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---opulent abode; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:p:pād]]---three fourths; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---opulence; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:m:māyika]] [[synonyms:v:vibhūti]]---material opulence; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]---one fourth; [[synonyms:a:abhidhāna]]---known.
translation: "The spiritual world is considered to be three fourths of the energy and opulence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whereas this material world is only one fourth of that energy. That is our understanding.
purport: Hari-dhāma (//paravyoma//) and Goloka Vṛndāvana are beyond the material cosmic manifestation. They are celebrated as three fourths of the Lord's energy. The material world, conducted by the Supreme Lord's external energy, is called Devī-dhāma and is a manifestation of one fourth of His energy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.56
description: " 'Because it consists of three fourths of the Lord's energy, the spiritual world is called tripād-bhūta. Being a manifestation of one fourth of the Lord's energy, the material world is called eka-pāda.'
text:
> tripād-vibhūter dhāmatvāt
> tripād-bhūtaṁ hi tat padam
> vibhūtir māyikī sarvā
> proktā pādātmikā yataḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:p:pād]]-[[synonyms:v:vibhūteḥ]]---of the three fourths of the energy; [[synonyms:d:dhāmatvāt]]---because of being the abode; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:p:pād]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūtam]]---consisting of three fourths of the energy; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:t:tat]] [[synonyms:p:padam]]---that abode; [[synonyms:v:vibhūtiḥ]]---the energy or potency; [[synonyms:m:māyikī]]---material; [[synonyms:s:sarvā]]---all; [[synonyms:p:proktā]]---said; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmikā]]---only one fourth; [[synonyms:y:yataḥ]]---therefore.
translation: “ 'Because it consists of three fourths of the Lord's energy, the spiritual world is called tripād-bhūta. Being a manifestation of one fourth of the Lord's energy, the material world is called eka-pāda.'
purport: This verse is found in //Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta// (1.5.286).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.57
description: "The three-fourths part of Lord Kṛṣṇa's energy is beyond our speaking power. Let us therefore hear elaborately about the remaining one fourth of His energy.
text:
> tripāda-vibhūti kṛṣṇera---vākya-agocara
> eka-pāda vibhūtira śunaha vistāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:v:vibhūti]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---three fourths of the energy of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vākya]]-[[synonyms:a:agocara]]---beyond words; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]] [[synonyms:v:vibhūtira]]---of one fourth of the energy; [[synonyms:ś:śunaha]]---please hear; [[synonyms:v:vistāra]]---breadth.
translation: "The three-fourths part of Lord Kṛṣṇa's energy is beyond our speaking power. Let us therefore hear elaborately about the remaining one fourth of His energy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.58
description: "Actually it is very difficult to ascertain the number of universes. Every universe has its separate Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva, who are known as permanent governors. Therefore there is also no counting of them.
text:
> ananta brahmāṇḍera yata brahmā-rudra-gaṇa
> cira-loka-pāla-śabde tāhāra gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍera]]---of the universes; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---//all//; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmās; [[synonyms:r:rudra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---and Lord Śivas; [[synonyms:c:cira]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:p:pāla]]---permanent governors of the worlds; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---of them; [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---counting.
translation: "Actually it is very difficult to ascertain the number of universes. Every universe has its separate Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva, who are known as permanent governors. Therefore there is also no counting of them.
purport: Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva are called //cira-loka-pāla,// permanent governors. This means that they govern the affairs of the universe from the beginning of the creation to the end. In the next creation, the same living entities may not be present, but because Brahmā and Śiva are existing from the beginning to the end, they are called //cira-loka-pāla,// permanent governors. //Loka-pāla// means "predominating deities." There are eight predominating deities of the prominent heavenly planets, and they are Indra, Agni, Yama, Varuṇa, Nirṛti, Vāyu, Kuvera and Śiva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.59
description: "Once, when Kṛṣṇa was ruling Dvārakā, Lord Brahmā came to see Him, and the doorman immediately informed Lord Kṛṣṇa of Brahmā's arrival.
text:
> eka-dina dvārakāte kṛṣṇa dekhibāre
> brahmā āilā,---dvāra-pāla jānāila kṛṣṇere
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:d:dvārakāte]]---in Dvārakā; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:d:dekhibāre]]---to see Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---Lord Brahmā came; [[synonyms:d:dvāra]]-[[synonyms:p:pāla]]---the doorman; [[synonyms:j:jānāila]]---informed; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Once, when Kṛṣṇa was ruling Dvārakā, Lord Brahmā came to see Him, and the doorman immediately informed Lord Kṛṣṇa of Brahmā's arrival.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.6
description: "Since all the Vaikuṇṭha planets are located in a certain corner of the spiritual sky, who can measure the spiritual sky?
text:
> ananta vaikuṇṭha eka eka deśe yāra
> sei paravyoma-dhāmera ke karu vistāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]] [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]]---unlimited Vaikuṇṭha planets; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:e:eka]]---certain; [[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in a place; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:v:vyoma]]---of the spiritual sky; [[synonyms:d:dhāmera]]---of the abode; [[synonyms:k:ke]] [[synonyms:k:karu]] [[synonyms:v:vistāra]]---who can understand the breadth.
translation: "Since all the Vaikuṇṭha planets are located in a certain corner of the spiritual sky, who can measure the spiritual sky?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.60
description: "When Kṛṣṇa was so informed, He immediately asked the doorman, 'Which Brahmā? What is his name?' The doorman therefore returned and questioned Lord Brahmā.
text:
> kṛṣṇa kahena---'kon brahmā, ki nāma tāhāra?'
> dvārī āsi' brahmāre puche āra bāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Kṛṣṇa said; [[synonyms:k:kon]] [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---which Brahmā; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---what is his name; [[synonyms:d:dvārī]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---the doorman, coming back; [[synonyms:b:brahmāre]]---to Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:p:puche]]---inquires; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:b:bāra]]---again.
translation: "When Kṛṣṇa was so informed, He immediately asked the doorman, 'Which Brahmā? What is his name?' The doorman therefore returned and questioned Lord Brahmā.
purport: From this verse we can understand that Brahmā is the name of the post and that the person occupying the post has a particular name also. From //Bhagavad-gītā:imaṁ vivasvate yogam.// Vivasvān is the name of the present predominating deity of the sun. He is generally called Sūrya, the sun-god, but he also has his own particular name. The governor of the state is generally called //rāja-pāla,// but he also has his own individual name. Since there are hundreds and thousands of Brahmās with different names, Kṛṣṇa wanted to know which of them had come to see Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.61
description: "When the doorman asked, 'Which Brahmā?' Lord Brahmā was surprised. He told the doorman, 'Please go inform Lord Kṛṣṇa that I am the four-headed Brahmā who is the father of the four Kumāras.'
text:
> vismita hañā brahmā dvārīke kahilā
> 'kaha giyā sanaka-pitā caturmukha āilā'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vismita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming surprised; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:d:dvārīke]]---unto the doorman; [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---replied; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---inform; [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---going; [[synonyms:s:sanaka]]-[[synonyms:p:pitā]]---the father of the four Kumāras; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---four-headed; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---has come.
translation: "When the doorman asked, 'Which Brahmā?' Lord Brahmā was surprised. He told the doorman, 'Please go inform Lord Kṛṣṇa that I am the four-headed Brahmā who is the father of the four Kumāras.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.62
description: "The doorman then informed Lord Kṛṣṇa of Lord Brahmā's description, and Lord Kṛṣṇa gave him permission to enter. The doorman escorted Lord Brahmā in, and as soon as Brahmā saw Lord Kṛṣṇa, he offered obeisances at His lotus feet.
text:
> kṛṣṇe jānāñā dvārī brahmāre lañā gelā
> kṛṣṇera caraṇe brahmā daṇḍavat kailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]] [[synonyms:j:jānāñā]]---informing Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dvārī]]---the doorman; [[synonyms:b:brahmāre]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]] [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---offered obeisances.
translation: "The doorman then informed Lord Kṛṣṇa of Lord Brahmā's description, and Lord Kṛṣṇa gave him permission to enter. The doorman escorted Lord Brahmā in, and as soon as Brahmā saw Lord Kṛṣṇa, he offered obeisances at His lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.63
description: "After being worshiped by Lord Brahmā, Lord Kṛṣṇa also honored him with suitable words. Then Lord Kṛṣṇa asked him, 'Why have you come here?'
text:
> kṛṣṇa mānya-pūjā kari' tāṅre praśna kaila
> 'ki lāgi' tomāra ihāṅ āgamana haila?'
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mānya]]-[[synonyms:p:pūjā]]---respect and worship; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to him; [[synonyms:p:praśna]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---put a question; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for what reason; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was arrival.
translation: "After being worshiped by Lord Brahmā, Lord Kṛṣṇa also honored him with suitable words. Then Lord Kṛṣṇa asked him, 'Why have you come here?'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.64
description: "Being questioned, Lord Brahmā immediately replied, 'I shall later tell You why I have come. First of all there is a doubt in my mind which I wish You would kindly dissipate.
text:
> brahmā kahe,---'tāhā pāche kariba nivedana
> eka saṁśaya mane haya, karaha chedana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Brahmā said; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---later; [[synonyms:k:kariba]] [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---I shall submit unto You; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:s:saṁśaya]]---doubt; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:c:chedana]]---kindly dissipate it.
translation: "Being questioned, Lord Brahmā immediately replied, 'I shall later tell You why I have come. First of all there is a doubt in my mind which I wish You would kindly dissipate.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.65
description: " 'Why did you inquire which Brahmā had come to see You? What is the purpose of such an inquiry? Is there any other Brahmā besides me within this universe?'
text:
> 'kon brahmā?' puchile tumi kon abhiprāye?
> āmā ba-i jagate āra kon brahmā haye?'
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kon]] [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---which Brahmā; [[synonyms:p:puchile]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You inquired; [[synonyms:k:kon]] [[synonyms:a:abhiprāye]]---by what intention; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]] [[synonyms:b:ba]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---except me; [[synonyms:j:jagate]]---within this universe; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---other; [[synonyms:k:kon]]---which; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:h:haye]]---is there.
translation: “ 'Why did you inquire which Brahmā had come to see You? What is the purpose of such an inquiry? Is there any other Brahmā besides me within this universe?'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.66
description: "Upon hearing this, Śrī Kṛṣṇa smiled and immediately meditated. Unlimited Brahmās arrived instantly.
text:
> śuni' hāsi' kṛṣṇa tabe karilena dhyāne
> asaṅkhya brahmāra gaṇa āilā tata-kṣaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:h:hāsi']]---smilingly; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:karilena]]---did; [[synonyms:d:dhyāne]]---meditation; [[synonyms:a:asaṅkhya]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:b:brahmāra]]---of Lord Brahmās; [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the group; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:t:tata]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---at that time.
translation: "Upon hearing this, Śrī Kṛṣṇa smiled and immediately meditated. Unlimited Brahmās arrived instantly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.67
description: "These Brahmās had different numbers of heads. Some had ten heads, some twenty, some a hundred, some a thousand, some ten thousand, some a hundred thousand, some ten million and others a hundred million. No one can count the number of faces they had.
text:
> daśa-biśa-śata-sahasra-ayuta-lakṣa-vadana
> koṭy-arbuda mukha kāro, nā yāya gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daśa]]---ten; [[synonyms:b:biśa]]---twenty; [[synonyms:ś:śata]]---hundred; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]---thousand; [[synonyms:a:ayuta]]---ten thousand; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---a hundred thousand; [[synonyms:v:vadana]]---faces; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---ten million; [[synonyms:a:arbuda]]---a hundred million; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---faces; [[synonyms:k:kāro]]---of some of them; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---not possible to count.
translation: "These Brahmās had different numbers of heads. Some had ten heads, some twenty, some a hundred, some a thousand, some ten thousand, some a hundred thousand, some ten million and others a hundred million. No one can count the number of faces they had.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.68
description: "There also arrived many Lord Śivas with various heads numbering one hundred thousand and ten million. Many Indras also arrived, and they had hundreds of thousands of eyes all over their bodies.
text:
> rudra-gaṇa āilā lakṣa koṭi-vadana
> indra-gaṇa āilā lakṣa koṭi-nayana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rudra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the Śivas; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]] [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:v:vadana]]---possessing a hundred thousand and ten million faces; [[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the Indras; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---a hundred thousand; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---ten million; [[synonyms:n:nayana]]---eyes.
translation: "There also arrived many Lord Śivas with various heads numbering one hundred thousand and ten million. Many Indras also arrived, and they had hundreds of thousands of eyes all over their bodies.
purport: It is said that Indra, the King of heaven, is very lusty. Once he tactfully had sexual intercourse with the wife of a great sage, and when the sage learned about this, he cursed the lusty Indra with a curse that put vaginas all over his body. Being very ashamed, Indra fell down at the lotus feet of the great sage and begged his pardon. Being compassionate, the sage turned the vaginas into eyes; therefore Indra possesses hundreds and thousands of eyes all over his body. Just as Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva have many faces, the King of heaven, Indra, has many eyes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.69
description: "When the four-headed Brahmā of this universe saw all these opulences of Kṛṣṇa, he became very bewildered and considered himself a rabbit among many elephants.
text:
> dekhi' caturmukha brahmā phāṅpara ha-ilā
> hasti-gaṇa-madhye yena śaśaka rahilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]] [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---the four-faced Lord Brahmā of this universe; [[synonyms:p:phāṅpara]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became bewildered; [[synonyms:h:hasti]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in the midst of many elephants; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---like; [[synonyms:ś:śaśaka]]---a rabbit; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained.
translation: "When the four-headed Brahmā of this universe saw all these opulences of Kṛṣṇa, he became very bewildered and considered himself a rabbit among many elephants.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.7
description: "The shape of the spiritual sky is compared to a lotus flower. The topmost region of that flower is called the whorl, and within that whorl is Kṛṣṇa's abode. The petals of the spiritual lotus flower consist of many Vaikuṇṭha planets.
text:
> ananta vaikuṇṭha-paravyoma yāra dala-śreṇī
> sarvopari kṛṣṇaloka 'karṇikāra' gaṇi
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]]---Vaikuṇṭha planets; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:v:vyoma]]---the spiritual sky; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:d:dala]]-[[synonyms:ś:śreṇī]]---the bunches of outlying petals; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:u:upari]]---in the topmost portion of the spiritual sky; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---the abode of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:karṇikāra]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇi]]---we consider the whorl of the lotus flower.
translation: "The shape of the spiritual sky is compared to a lotus flower. The topmost region of that flower is called the whorl, and within that whorl is Kṛṣṇa's abode. The petals of the spiritual lotus flower consist of many Vaikuṇṭha planets.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.70
description: "All the Brahmās who came to see Kṛṣṇa offered their respects at His lotus feet, and when they did this, their helmets touched His lotus feet.
text:
> āsi' saba brahmā kṛṣṇa-pāda-pīṭha-āge
> daṇḍavat karite mukuṭa pāda-pīṭhe lāge
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---all the Brahmās; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:pīṭha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---before the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---offering their obeisances; [[synonyms:m:mukuṭa]]---helmets; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:pīṭhe]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:l:lāge]]---touched.
translation: "All the Brahmās who came to see Kṛṣṇa offered their respects at His lotus feet, and when they did this, their helmets touched His lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.71
description: "No one can estimate the inconceivable potency of Kṛṣṇa. All the Brahmās who were there were resting in the one body of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> kṛṣṇera acintya-śakti lakhite keha nāre
> yata brahmā, tata mūrti eka-i śarīre
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:acintya]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---inconceivable potencies; [[synonyms:l:lakhite]]---to observe; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---not able; [[synonyms:y:yata]] [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---all Brahmās; [[synonyms:t:tata]] [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---so many forms; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:i:i]] [[synonyms:ś:śarīre]]---in the same body.
translation: "No one can estimate the inconceivable potency of Kṛṣṇa. All the Brahmās who were there were resting in the one body of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.72
description: "When all the helmets struck together at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, there was a tumultuous sound. It appeared that the helmets themselves were offering prayers unto Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet.
text:
> pāda-pīṭa-mukuṭāgra-saṅghaṭṭe uṭhe dhvani
> pāda-pīṭhe stuti kare mukuṭa hena jāni'
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:pīṭa]]---at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet; [[synonyms:m:mukuṭa]]-[[synonyms:a:agra]]---of the tops of the helmets; [[synonyms:s:saṅghaṭṭe]]---in the crowding together; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]] [[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---there arose a sound; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:pīṭhe]] [[synonyms:s:stuti]]---offering prayers unto the lotus feet; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:m:mukuṭa]]---the helmets; [[synonyms:h:hena]] [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---appearing as such.
translation: "When all the helmets struck together at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, there was a tumultuous sound. It appeared that the helmets themselves were offering prayers unto Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.73
description: "With folded hands, all the Brahmās and Śivas began to offer prayers unto Lord Kṛṣṇa, saying, 'O Lord, You have shown me a great favor. I have been able to see Your lotus feet.'
text:
> yoḍa-hāte brahmā-rudrādi karaye stavana
> "baḍa kṛpā karilā prabhu, dekhāilā caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yoḍa]]-[[synonyms:h:hāte]]---with folded hands; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---the Lord Brahmās; [[synonyms:r:rudra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the Lord Śivas and others; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:s:stavana]]---offered their prayers; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---great mercy; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---You have shown; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---O Lord; [[synonyms:d:dekhāilā]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---You have shown Your lotus feet.
translation: "With folded hands, all the Brahmās and Śivas began to offer prayers unto Lord Kṛṣṇa, saying, 'O Lord, You have shown me a great favor. I have been able to see Your lotus feet.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.74
description: "All of them then said, 'It is my great fortune, Lord, that You have called me, thinking of me as Your servant. Now let me know what Your order is so that I may carry it on my heads.'
text:
> bhāgya, more bolāilā 'dāsa' aṅgīkari'
> kon ājñā haya, tāhā kari śire dhari' "
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāgya]]---great fortune; [[synonyms:m:more]]---me; [[synonyms:b:bolāilā]]---You have called; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---as a servant; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:k:kon]] [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---what is Your order; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---let me accept; [[synonyms:ś:śire]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---holding it on my head.
translation: "All of them then said, 'It is my great fortune, Lord, that You have called me, thinking of me as Your servant. Now let me know what Your order is so that I may carry it on my heads.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.75
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa replied, 'Since I wanted to see all of you together, I have called all of you here.
text:
> kṛṣṇa kahe,---tomā-sabā dekhite citta haila
> tāhā lāgi' eka ṭhāñi sabā bolāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa said; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all of you; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:c:citta]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was a desire; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for that reason; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---in one place; [[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all of you; [[synonyms:b:bolāila]]---I called for.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa replied, 'Since I wanted to see all of you together, I have called all of you here.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.76
description: " 'All of you should be happy. Is there any fear from the demons?' They replied, 'By Your mercy, we are victorious everywhere.
text:
> sukhī hao sabe, kichu nāhi daitya-bhaya?
> tārā kahe,---'tomāra prasāde sarvatra-i jaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sukhī]] [[synonyms:h:hao]]---be happy; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of you; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---//some//; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:d:daitya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear of the demons; [[synonyms:t:tārā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---all of them replied; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:p:prasāde]]---by Your mercy; [[synonyms:s:sarvatra]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---victorious.
translation: “ 'All of you should be happy. Is there any fear from the demons?' They replied, 'By Your mercy, we are victorious everywhere.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.77
description: " 'Whatever burden was upon the earth You have taken away by descending on that planet.'
text:
> samprati pṛthivīte yebā haiyāchila bhāra
> avatīrṇa hañā tāhā karilā saṁhāra'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:samprati]]---presently; [[synonyms:p:pṛthivīte]]---upon the earth; [[synonyms:y:yebā]]---whatever; [[synonyms:h:haiyāchila]]---there was; [[synonyms:b:bhāra]]---burden; [[synonyms:a:avatīrṇa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---descending; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:s:saṁhāra]]---You have taken away.
translation: “ 'Whatever burden was upon the earth You have taken away by descending on that planet.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.78
description: "This is the proof of Dvārakā's opulence: all the Brahmās thought, 'Kṛṣṇa is now staying in my jurisdiction.'
text:
> dvārakādi---vibhu, tāra ei ta pramāṇa
> 'āmāra-i brahmāṇḍe kṛṣṇa' sabāra haila jñāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dvārakā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---Dvārakā-dhāma and other abodes; [[synonyms:v:vibhu]]---transcendental abode; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta]] [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---this is the evidence of that; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]-[[synonyms:i:i]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍe]]---in my //brahmāṇḍa//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa is now present; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:h:haila]] [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---there was this knowledge.
translation: "This is the proof of Dvārakā's opulence: all the Brahmās thought, 'Kṛṣṇa is now staying in my jurisdiction.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.79
description: "Thus the opulence of Dvārakā was perceived by each and every one of them. Although they were all assembled together, no one could see anyone but himself.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-saha dvārakā-vaibhava anubhava haila
> ekatra milane keha kāho nā dekhila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saha]]---with Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dvārakā]]-[[synonyms:v:vaibhava]]---the opulence of Dvārakā; [[synonyms:a:anubhava]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was perception; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]] [[synonyms:m:milane]]---although they came together; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:k:kāho]]---anyone else; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---did not see.
translation: "Thus the opulence of Dvārakā was perceived by each and every one of them. Although they were all assembled together, no one could see anyone but himself.
purport: The four-headed Brahmā perceived the opulence of Dvārakā-dhāma where Kṛṣṇa was staying, and although there were Brahmās present having ten to ten million heads, and also many Lord Śivas were also assembled, only the four-headed Brahmā of this universe could see all of them. By the inconceivable potency of Kṛṣṇa, the others could not see one another. Although all the Brahmās and Śivas were assembled together, due to Kṛṣṇa's energy, they could not meet or talk among themselves individually.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.8
description: "Each Vaikuṇṭha planet is full of spiritual bliss, complete opulence and space, and each is inhabited by incarnations. If Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva cannot estimate the length and breadth of the spiritual sky and the Vaikuṇṭha planets, how can ordinary living entities begin to imagine them?
text:
> ei-mata ṣaḍ-aiśvarya, sthāna, avatāra
> brahmā, śiva anta nā pāya---jīva kon chāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---such; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṭ]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---six opulences; [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---abode; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnations; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:a:anta]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---cannot find the limit; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---a living entity; [[synonyms:k:kon]]---what of; [[synonyms:c:chāra]]---worthless.
translation: "Each Vaikuṇṭha planet is full of spiritual bliss, complete opulence and space, and each is inhabited by incarnations. If Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva cannot estimate the length and breadth of the spiritual sky and the Vaikuṇṭha planets, how can ordinary living entities begin to imagine them?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.80
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa then bade farewell to all the Brahmās there, and after offering their obeisances, they all returned to their respective homes.
text:
> tabe kṛṣṇa sarva-brahmā-gaṇe vidāya dilā
> daṇḍavat hañā sabe nija ghare gelā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:b:brahmā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---unto all the Brahmās; [[synonyms:v:vidāya]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---bade farewell; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:n:nija]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]] [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---returned to their respective homes.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa then bade farewell to all the Brahmās there, and after offering their obeisances, they all returned to their respective homes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.81
description: "After observing all these opulences, the four-headed Brahmā of this universe was astonished. He again came before the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and offered Him obeisances.
text:
> dekhi' caturmukha brahmāra haila camatkāra
> kṛṣṇera caraṇe āsi' kailā namaskāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāra]]---of the four-headed Brahmā of this universe; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonishment; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming to the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---offered his respects.
translation: "After observing all these opulences, the four-headed Brahmā of this universe was astonished. He again came before the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and offered Him obeisances.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.82
description: "Brahmā then said, 'Whatever I formerly decided about my knowledge, I have just now had personally verified.'
text:
> brahmā bale,---pūrve āmi ye niścaya kariluṅ
> tāra udāharaṇa āmi āji ta' dekhiluṅ
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmā]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---Brahmā said; [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---formerly; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]] [[synonyms:k:kariluṅ]]---decided; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:u:udāharaṇa]]---the example; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:ā:āji]]---today; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:d:dekhiluṅ]]---have seen.
translation: "Brahmā then said, 'Whatever I formerly decided about my knowledge, I have just now had personally verified.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.83
description: " 'There are people who say, "I know everything about Kṛṣṇa." Let them think in that way. As far as I am concerned, I do not wish to speak very much about this matter. O my Lord, let me say this much. As far as your opulences are concerned, they are all beyond the reach of my mind, body and words.'
text:
> jānanta eva jānantu
> kiṁ bahūktyā na me prabho
> manaso vapuṣo vāco
> vaibhavaṁ tava gocaraḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jānantaḥ]]---persons who think they are aware of Your unlimited potency; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:j:jānantu]]---let them think like that; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what is the use; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:u:uktyā]]---with many words; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:m:me]]---my; [[synonyms:p:prabho]]---O my Lord; [[synonyms:m:manasaḥ]]---of the mind; [[synonyms:v:vapuṣaḥ]]---of the body; [[synonyms:v:vācaḥ]]---of the words; [[synonyms:v:vaibhavam]]---opulences; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:g:gocaraḥ]]---within the range.
translation: “ 'There are people who say, "I know everything about Kṛṣṇa." Let them think in that way. As far as I am concerned, I do not wish to speak very much about this matter. O my Lord, let me say this much. As far as your opulences are concerned, they are all beyond the reach of my mind, body and words.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.14.38), spoken by Lord Brahmā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.84
description: "Kṛṣṇa said, 'Your particular universe extends four billion miles; therefore it is the smallest of all the universes. Consequently you have only four heads.
text:
> kṛṣṇa kahe, "ei brahmāṇḍa pañcāśat koṭi yojana
> ati kṣudra, tāte tomāra cāri vadana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Kṛṣṇa said; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]---this universe; [[synonyms:p:pañcāśat]] [[synonyms:k:koṭi]] [[synonyms:y:yojana]]---four billion miles; [[synonyms:a:ati]] [[synonyms:k:kṣudra]]---very small; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:v:vadana]]---four faces.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa said, 'Your particular universe extends four billion miles; therefore it is the smallest of all the universes. Consequently you have only four heads.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, one of the greatest astrologers of his time, gives information from //Siddhānta-śiromaṇi// that this universe measures 18,712,069,200,000,000 x 8 miles. This is the circumference of this universe. According to some, this is only half the circumference.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.85
description: " 'Some of the universes are one billion yojanas, some one trillion, some ten trillion and some one hundred trillion yojanas. Thus they are almost unlimited in area.
text:
> kona brahmāṇḍa śata-koṭi, kona lakṣa-koṭi
> kona niyuta-koṭi, kona koṭi-koṭi
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]---some universes; [[synonyms:ś:śata]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---one billion //yojanas//; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---some; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---one trillion //yojanas//; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---some; [[synonyms:n:niyuta]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---ten trillion; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---some; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---one hundred trillion.
translation: “ 'Some of the universes are one billion yojanas, some one trillion, some ten trillion and some one hundred trillion yojanas. Thus they are almost unlimited in area.
purport: A //yojana// equals eight miles.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.86
description: " 'According to the size of the universe, there are so many heads on the body of Brahmā. In this way I maintain innumerable universes [brahmāṇḍas].
text:
> brahmāṇḍānurūpa brahmāra śarīra-vadana
> ei-rūpe pāli āmi brahmāṇḍera gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:a:anurūpa]]---according to the size of a universe; [[synonyms:b:brahmāra]]---of Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:ś:śarīra]]-[[synonyms:v:vadana]]---heads on the body; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in this way; [[synonyms:p:pāli]] [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I maintain; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍera]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the innumerable groups of universes.
translation: “ 'According to the size of the universe, there are so many heads on the body of Brahmā. In this way I maintain innumerable universes [brahmāṇḍas].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.87
description: " 'No one can measure the length and breadth of one fourth of My energy. Who can measure the three fourths that is manifested in the spiritual world?'
text:
> 'eka-pāda vibhūti' ihāra nāhi parimāṇa
> 'tripāda vibhūti'ra kebā kare parimāṇa"
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]] [[synonyms:v:vibhūti]]---a one-fourth manifestation of My opulence; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of this; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:p:parimāṇa]]---measurement; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]] [[synonyms:v:vibhūtira]]---of the spiritual world, having three fourths of My energy; [[synonyms:k:kebā]]---who; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---can do; [[synonyms:p:parimāṇa]]---measurement.
translation: “ 'No one can measure the length and breadth of one fourth of My energy. Who can measure the three fourths that is manifested in the spiritual world?'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.88
description: " 'Beyond the river Virajā is a spiritual nature, which is indestructible, eternal, inexhaustible and unlimited. It is the supreme abode consisting of three fourths of the Lord's opulences. It is known as paravyoma, the spiritual sky.'
text:
> tasyāḥ pāre paravyoma
> tripād-bhūtaṁ sanātanam
> amṛtaṁ śāśvataṁ nityam
> anantaṁ paramaṁ padam
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tasyāḥ]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---on the other bank of the Virajā River; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:v:vyoma]]---the spiritual sky; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:p:pād]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūtam]]---existing as three fourths of the opulence of the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:s:sanātanam]]---eternal; [[synonyms:a:amṛtam]]---without deterioration; [[synonyms:ś:śāśvatam]]---without being subjected to the control of time; [[synonyms:n:nityam]]---constantly existing; [[synonyms:a:anantam]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:p:paramam]]---supreme; [[synonyms:p:padam]]---abode.
translation: “ 'Beyond the river Virajā is a spiritual nature, which is indestructible, eternal, inexhaustible and unlimited. It is the supreme abode consisting of three fourths of the Lord's opulences. It is known as paravyoma, the spiritual sky.'
purport: This is a verse from the //Padma Purāṇa,// recited here by Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 21.89
description: "In this way Lord Kṛṣṇa bade farewell to the four-headed Brahmā of this universe. We may thus understand that no one can calculate the extent of Kṛṣṇa's energies.
text:
> tabe kṛṣṇa brahmāre dilena vidāya
> kṛṣṇera vibhūti-svarūpa jānāna nā yāya
