title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.14-15
description: "In this way the conditioned soul becomes the servant of lusty desires, and when these are not fulfilled, he becomes a servant of anger and continues to be kicked by the external energy, māyā. Wandering and wandering throughout the universe, he may by chance get the association of a devotee physician, whose instructions and hymns make the witch of external energy flee. The conditioned soul thus gets into touch with the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa, and in this way he can approach nearer and nearer to the Lord.
text:
> kāma-krodhera dāsa hañā tāra lāthi khāya
> bhramite bhramite yadi sādhu-vaidya pāya
>
> tāṅra upadeśa-mantre piśācī palāya
> kṛṣṇa-bhakti pāya, tabe kṛṣṇa-nikaṭa yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāma]]---of lusty desires; [[synonyms:k:krodhera]]---and of anger; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---the servant; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---by them; [[synonyms:l:lāthi]] [[synonyms:k:khāya]]---is kicked; [[synonyms:b:bhramitebhramite]]---wandering and wandering; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]---a devotee; [[synonyms:v:vaidya]]---physician; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---he gets; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:u:upadeśa]]-[[synonyms:m:mantre]]---by instruction and hymns; [[synonyms:p:piśācī]]---the witch (the external energy); [[synonyms:p:palāya]]---flees; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---obtains; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---in this way; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nikaṭa]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---he goes to Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "In this way the conditioned soul becomes the servant of lusty desires, and when these are not fulfilled, he becomes a servant of anger and continues to be kicked by the external energy, māyā. Wandering and wandering throughout the universe, he may by chance get the association of a devotee physician, whose instructions and hymns make the witch of external energy flee. The conditioned soul thus gets into touch with the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa, and in this way he can approach nearer and nearer to the Lord.
purport:
An explanation of verses 8 through 15 is given by Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura in his //Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya.// The Lord is spread throughout the creation in His quadruple expansions and incarnations. Kṛṣṇa is fully represented with all potencies in each and every personal extension, but the living entities, although separated expansions, are also considered one of the Lord's energies. The living entities are divided into two categories---the eternally liberated and eternally conditioned. Those who are ever-liberated never come in contact with //māyā,// the external energy. The ever-conditioned are always under the clutches of the external energy. This is described in //Bhagavad-gītā://

> daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī
> mama māyā duratyayā

"This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome." [[books:bg:7:14|(Bg. 7.14)]]

The //nitya-baddhas// are always conditioned by the external energy, and the //nitya-muktas// never come in contact with the external energy. Sometimes an ever-liberated personal associate of the Supreme Personality of Godhead descends into this universe just as the Lord descends. Although working for the liberation of conditioned souls, the messenger of the Supreme Lord remains untouched by the material energy. Generally ever-liberated personalities live in the spiritual world as associates of Lord Kṛṣṇa, and they are known as //kṛṣṇa-pāriṣada,// associates of the Lord. Their only business is enjoying Lord Kṛṣṇa's company, and even though such eternally liberated persons come within this material world to serve the Lord's purpose, they enjoy Lord Kṛṣṇa's company without stoppage. The ever-liberated person who works on Kṛṣṇa's behalf enjoys Lord Kṛṣṇa's company through his engagement. The ever-conditioned soul, provoked by lusty desires to enjoy the material world, is subjected to transmigrate from one body to another. Sometimes he is elevated to higher planetary systems, and sometimes he is degraded to hellish planets and subjected to the tribulations of the external energy.

Due to being conditioned by the external energy, the conditioned soul within this material world gets two kinds of bodies-a gross material body and a subtle body composed of mind, intelligence and ego. Due to the gross and subtle bodies, he is subjected to the threefold miseries (//ādhyātmika, ādhibhautika// and //ādhidaivika),// miseries arising from the body and mind, other living entities, and natural disturbances caused by demigods from higher planetary systems. The conditioned soul subjected to the threefold material miseries is ceaselessly kicked by //māyā,// and this is his disease. If by chance he meets a saintly person who works on Kṛṣṇa's behalf to deliver conditioned souls, and if he agrees to abide by his order, he can gradually approach the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.140
description: "If a person gives up all material desires and completely engages in the transcendental loving service of Kṛṣṇa, as enjoined in revealed scriptures, he is never indebted to demigods, sages or forefathers.
text:
> kāma tyaji' kṛṣṇa bhaje śāstra-ājñā māni'
> deva-ṛṣi-pitrādikera kabhu nahe ṛṇī
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāma]]---material desires; [[synonyms:t:tyaji']]---giving up; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---worships; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---the direction of the revealed scripture; [[synonyms:m:māni']]---accepting; [[synonyms:d:deva]]---demigods; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣi]]---great sages; [[synonyms:p:pitṛ]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādikera]]---of the forefathers and so on; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṇī]]---a debtor.
translation: "If a person gives up all material desires and completely engages in the transcendental loving service of Kṛṣṇa, as enjoined in revealed scriptures, he is never indebted to demigods, sages or forefathers.
purport: After birth, every man is indebted in so many ways. He is indebted to the demigods for their supplying necessities like air, light and water. When one takes advantage of Vedic literatures, one becomes indebted to great sages like Vyāsadeva, Nārada, Devala and Asita. When one takes birth in a particular family, he becomes indebted to his forefathers. We are even indebted to common living entities like cows, from whom we take milk. Because we accept service from so many animals, we become indebted. However, if one is completely engaged in the Lord's devotional service, he is absolved of all debts. This is confirmed in the following verse, quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.41).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.141
description: " 'One who has given up all material duties and taken full shelter at the lotus feet of Mukunda, who gives shelter to all, is not indebted to the demigods, great sages, ordinary living beings, relatives, friends, mankind or even one's forefathers who have passed away.'
text:
> devarṣi-bhūtāpta-nṛṇāṁ pitṝṇāṁ
> na kiṅkaro nāyam ṛṇī ca rājan
> sarvātmanā yaḥ śaraṇaṁ śaraṇyaṁ
> gato mukundaṁ parihṛtya kartam
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:deva]]---of the demigods; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣi]]---of the sages; [[synonyms:b:bhūta]]---of ordinary living entities; [[synonyms:ā:āpta]]---of friends and relatives; [[synonyms:n:nṛṇām]]---of ordinary men; [[synonyms:p:pitṝṇām]]---of the forefathers; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:k:kiṅkaraḥ]]---the servant; [[synonyms:n:na]]---nor; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this one; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṇī]]---//debtor//; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:r:rājan]]---O King; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmanā]]---with his whole being; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---a person who; [[synonyms:ś:śaraṇam]]---shelter; [[synonyms:ś:śaraṇyam]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who affords shelter to all; [[synonyms:g:gataḥ]]---approached; [[synonyms:m:mukundam]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:p:parihṛtya]]---giving up; [[synonyms:k:kartam]]---duties.
translation: “ 'One who has given up all material duties and taken full shelter at the lotus feet of Mukunda, who gives shelter to all, is not indebted to the demigods, great sages, ordinary living beings, relatives, friends, mankind or even one's forefathers who have passed away.'
purport:
It is said:

> adhyāpanaṁ brahma-yajñaḥ
> pitṛ-yajñas tu tarpaṇam
> homo daivo balir bhauto
> nṛ-yajño 'tithi-pūjanam

"By performing oblations with ghee, the demigods are satisfied. By studying the //Vedas, brahma-yajña// is performed, and by this the great sages are satisfied. Offering libations of water before one's forefathers is called //pitṛ-yajña.// By offering tribute, //bhūta-yajña// is performed. By properly receiving guests, //nṛ-yajña// is performed." There are five //yajñas// and five kinds of indebtedness-indebtedness to the demigods, great sages, forefathers, living entities and common men. Therefore one has to perform five kinds of //yajñas,// but when one takes to //saṅkīrtana-yajña// (the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra//) one doesn't have to perform any other //yajña.// In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// Nārada Muni made a statement about the systematic performance of //bhāgavata-dharma// in connection with statements previously made by the nine Yogendras before Mahārāja Nimi. The sage Karabhājana Ṛṣi explained the four incarnations of the four //yugas,// and at the end, in this verse (text 141), he explained the position of Kṛṣṇa's pure devotee and how he is absolved of all debts.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.142
description: "Although the pure devotee does not follow all the regulative principles of varṇāśrama, he worships the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore he naturally has no tendency to commit sin.
text:
> vidhi-dharma chāḍi' bhaje kṛṣṇera caraṇa
> niṣiddha pāpācāre tāra kabhu nahe mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up all regulative principles of the //varṇa// and //āśrama// institution; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---worships; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:niṣiddha]]---forbidden; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācāre]]---in sinful activities; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: "Although the pure devotee does not follow all the regulative principles of varṇāśrama, he worships the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore he naturally has no tendency to commit sin.
purport:
The //varṇāśrama// institution is planned in such a way that one will not commit sinful activities. Material existence continues due to sinful activity. When one acts sinfully in this life, he gets a suitable body for the next life. When one again acts sinfully, he takes on another material body. In this way one is continuously under the influence of material nature.

> puruṣaḥ prakṛti-stho hi
> bhuṅkte prakṛti-jān guṇān
> kāraṇaṁ guṇa-saṅgo 'sya
> sad-asad-yoni-janmasu

"The living entity in material nature thus follows the ways of life, enjoying the three modes of material nature. This is due to his association with that material nature. Thus he meets with good and evil among various species." [[books:bg:13:22|(Bg. 13.22)]]

Due to our association with the modes of material nature, we get different types of bodies-good and bad. One cannot be liberated from the cycle of birth and death, known as transmigration of the soul, unless one is completely freed from all sinful activities. The best process, therefore, is to take to Kṛṣṇa consciousness. One cannot take to Kṛṣṇa consciousness without being freed from all sinful activities. Naturally one who is very serious about Kṛṣṇa consciousness is freed from all sinful activity. Consequently a devotee is never inclined to commit sins. If one is pressured by the law or obligations to give up sinful activity, one cannot do so. However, if one takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, he can very easily give up all sinful activity. This is confirmed herein.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.143
description: "If, however, a devotee accidentally becomes involved in a sinful activity, Kṛṣṇa purifies him. He does not have to undergo the regulative form of atonement.
text:
> ajñāne vā haya yadi 'pāpa' upasthita
> kṛṣṇa tāṅre śuddha kare, nā karāya prāyaścitta
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ajñāne]]---by ignorance; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]---sinful activities; [[synonyms:u:upasthita]]---present; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him (the devotee); [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---purifies; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---does not cause; [[synonyms:p:prāyaścitta]]---atonement.
translation: "If, however, a devotee accidentally becomes involved in a sinful activity, Kṛṣṇa purifies him. He does not have to undergo the regulative form of atonement.
purport: Kṛṣṇa purifies from within as //caitya-guru,// the spiritual master within the heart. This is described in the following verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.42).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.144
description: " 'One who has given up everything and taken full shelter at the lotus feet of Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is very dear to Kṛṣṇa. If he is involved in some sinful activity by accident, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is seated within everyone's heart, removes his sins without difficulty.'
text:
> svapāda-mūlaṁ bhajataḥ priyasya
> tyaktānya-bhāvasya hariḥ pareśaḥ
>
> vikarma yac cotpatitaṁ kathañcit
> dhunoti sarvaṁ hṛdi sanniviṣṭaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:m:mūlam]]---the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, the shelter of the devotees; [[synonyms:b:bhajataḥ]]---who is engaged in worshiping; [[synonyms:p:priyasya]]---who is very dear to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tyakta]]---given up; [[synonyms:a:anya]]---for others; [[synonyms:b:bhāvasya]]---of one whose disposition or inclination; [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśaḥ]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:v:vikarma]]---sinful activities; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---whatever; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:u:utpatitam]]---occurred; [[synonyms:k:kathañcit]]---somehow; [[synonyms:d:dhunoti]]---removes; [[synonyms:s:sarvam]]---everything; [[synonyms:h:hṛdi]]---in the heart; [[synonyms:s:sanniviṣṭaḥ]]---entered.
translation: “ 'One who has given up everything and taken full shelter at the lotus feet of Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is very dear to Kṛṣṇa. If he is involved in some sinful activity by accident, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is seated within everyone's heart, removes his sins without difficulty.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.145
description: "The path of speculative knowledge and renunciation is not very essential for devotional service. Indeed, good qualities such as nonviolence and mind and sense control automatically accompany a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> jñāna-vairāgyādi---bhaktira kabhu nahe 'aṅga'
> ahiṁsā-yama-niyamādi bule kṛṣṇa-bhakta-saṅga
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---the path of knowledge; [[synonyms:v:vairāgya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the path of renunciation and so on; [[synonyms:b:bhaktira]]---of devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---a part; [[synonyms:a:ahiṁsā]]---nonviolence; [[synonyms:y:yama]]---controlling the senses and the mind; [[synonyms:n:niyama]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---restrictions and so on; [[synonyms:b:bule]]---roam; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---in the association of a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "The path of speculative knowledge and renunciation is not very essential for devotional service. Indeed, good qualities such as nonviolence and mind and sense control automatically accompany a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
purport: Sometimes a neophyte devotee or ordinary person thinks highly of speculative knowledge, austerity, penances and renunciation, thinking them the only path for advancement in devotional service. Actually this is not a fact. The path of knowledge, mystic //yoga// and renunciation has nothing to do with the pure soul. When one is temporarily in the material world, such processes may help a little, but they are not necessary for a pure devotee of Kṛṣṇa. In the material world, such activities end in material enjoyment or merging into the effulgence of the Supreme. They have nothing to do with the eternal loving service of the Lord. If one abandons speculative knowledge and simply engages in devotional service, he has attained his perfection. The devotee has no need for speculative knowledge, pious activity or mystic //yoga.// All these are automatically present when one renders the Lord transcendental loving service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.146
description: " 'For one who is fully engaged in My devotional service, whose mind is fixed on Me in bhakti-yoga, the path of speculative knowledge and dry renunciation is not very beneficial.'
text:
> tasmān mad-bhakti-yuktasya
> yogino vai mad-ātmanaḥ
> na jñānaṁ na ca vairāgyaṁ
> prāyaḥ śreyo bhaved iha
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tasmāt]]---therefore; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---in My devotional service; [[synonyms:y:yuktasya]]---of one who is engaged; [[synonyms:y:yoginaḥ]]---the first-class //yogī// or mystic; [[synonyms:v:vai]]---certainly; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmanaḥ]]---whose mind is always engaged in Me; [[synonyms:n:na]]---//not//; [[synonyms:j:jñānam]]---speculative knowledge; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:v:vairāgyam]]---dry renunciation; [[synonyms:p:prāyaḥ]]---for the most part; [[synonyms:ś:śreyaḥ]]---beneficial; [[synonyms:b:bhavet]]---would be; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---in this world.
translation: “ 'For one who is fully engaged in My devotional service, whose mind is fixed on Me in bhakti-yoga, the path of speculative knowledge and dry renunciation is not very beneficial.'
purport: The path of devotional service is always independent of other activity. The path of speculative knowledge or mystic //yoga// may be a little beneficial in the beginning, but it cannot be considered part of devotional service. This verse (//Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// 11.20.31) was spoken by Lord Kṛṣṇa when He was speaking to Uddhava before His departure from this material world. These are important instructions given directly by Lord Kṛṣṇa. Śrī Uddhava asked the Lord about the two kinds of instructions given in the //Vedas.// One instruction is called //pravṛtti-mārga,// and the other is called //nivṛtti-mārga.// These are directions for enjoying the material world according to regulative principles and then giving up the material world for higher spiritual understanding. Sometimes one does not know whether to practice speculative knowledge or mystic //yoga// for advancement in spiritual knowledge. Kṛṣṇa explains to Uddhava that the mechanical process of speculative knowledge and //yoga// is not necessary for advancing in devotional service. Devotional service is completely spiritual; it has nothing to do with material things. It is awakened by hearing and chanting in the association of devotees. Because devotional service is always transcendental, it has nothing to do with material activity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.147
description: " 'O hunter, good qualities like nonviolence, which you have developed, are not very astonishing, for those who are engaged in the Lord's devotional service are never inclined to give pain to others because of envy.'
text:
> ete na hy adbhutā vyādha
> tavāhiṁsādayo guṇāḥ
> hari-bhaktau pravṛttā ye
> na te syuḥ paratāpinaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ete]]---all these; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:adbhutāḥ]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---O hunter; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---your; [[synonyms:a:ahiṁsā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādayaḥ]]---nonviolence and others; [[synonyms:g:guṇāḥ]]---qualities; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktau]]---in devotional service; [[synonyms:p:pravṛttāḥ]]---engaged; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:t:te]]---they; [[synonyms:s:syuḥ]]---are; [[synonyms:p:paratāpinaḥ]]---envious of other living entities.
translation: “ 'O hunter, good qualities like nonviolence, which you have developed, are not very astonishing, for those who are engaged in the Lord's devotional service are never inclined to give pain to others because of envy.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Skanda Purāṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.148
description: "My dear Sanātana, I have now in detail described devotional service according to the regulative principles. Now hear from Me about spontaneous devotional service and its characteristics.
text:
> vaidhī-bhakti-sādhanera kahiluṅ vivaraṇa
> rāgānugā-bhaktira lakṣaṇa śuna, sanātana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaidhī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---of devotional service according to the regulative principles; [[synonyms:s:sādhanera]]---of the execution; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have made; [[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---description; [[synonyms:r:rāgānugā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktira]]---of spontaneous devotional service; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the symptoms; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---O Sanātana.
translation: "My dear Sanātana, I have now in detail described devotional service according to the regulative principles. Now hear from Me about spontaneous devotional service and its characteristics.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.149
description: "The original inhabitants of Vṛndāvana are attached to Kṛṣṇa spontaneously in devotional service. Nothing can compare to such spontaneous devotional service, which is called rāgātmikā bhakti. When a devotee follows in the footsteps of the devotees of Vṛndāvana, his devotional service is called rāgānugā bhakti.
text:
> rāgātmikā-bhakti---'mukhyā' vraja-vāsi-jane
> tāra anugata bhaktira 'rāgānugā'-nāme
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāgātmikā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---spontaneous devotional service; [[synonyms:m:mukhyā]]---preeminent; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsi]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---in the inhabitants of Vraja, or Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---that; [[synonyms:a:anugata]]---following; [[synonyms:b:bhaktira]]---of devotional service; [[synonyms:r:rāgānugā]]-[[synonyms:n:nāme]]---named //rāgānugā// or following after spontaneous devotional service.
translation: "The original inhabitants of Vṛndāvana are attached to Kṛṣṇa spontaneously in devotional service. Nothing can compare to such spontaneous devotional service, which is called rāgātmikā bhakti. When a devotee follows in the footsteps of the devotees of Vṛndāvana, his devotional service is called rāgānugā bhakti.
purport:
In his //Bhakti-sandarbha,// Jīva Gosvāmī states:

tad evaṁ tat-tad-abhimāna-lakṣaṇa-bhāva-viśeṣveṇa svābhāvika-rāgasya vaiśiṣṭye sati tat-tad-rāga-prayuktā śravaṇa-kīrtana-smaraṇa-pāda-sevana-vandanātma-nivedana-prāyā bhaktis teṣāṁ rāgātmikā bhaktir ity ucyate.... tatas tadīyaṁ rāgaṁ rucyānugacchantī sā rāgānugā.

When a pure devotee follows the footsteps of a devotee in Vṛndāvana, he develops //rāgānugā bhakti.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.150
description: " 'When one becomes attached to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, his natural inclination to love is fully absorbed in thoughts of the Lord. That is called transcendental attachment, and devotional service according to that attachment is called rāgātmikā, or spontaneous devotional service.'
text:
> iṣṭe svārasikī rāgaḥ
> paramāviṣṭatā bhavet
> tanmayī yā bhaved bhaktiḥ
> sātra rāgātmikoditā
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṣṭe]]---unto the desired object of life; [[synonyms:s:svārasikī]]---appropriate for one's own original aptitude of love; [[synonyms:r:rāgaḥ]]---attachment; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭatā]]---absorption in the service of the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhavet]]---is; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:m:mayī]]---consisting of that transcendental attachment; [[synonyms:y:yā]]---which; [[synonyms:b:bhavet]]---is; [[synonyms:b:bhaktiḥ]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:s:sā]]---that; [[synonyms:a:atra]]---here; [[synonyms:r:rāgātmikā]]-[[synonyms:u:uditā]]---called //rāgātmikā,// or spontaneous devotional service.
translation: “ 'When one becomes attached to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, his natural inclination to love is fully absorbed in thoughts of the Lord. That is called transcendental attachment, and devotional service according to that attachment is called rāgātmikā, or spontaneous devotional service.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.272).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.151
description: "The primary characteristic of spontaneous love is deep attachment for the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Absorption in Him is a marginal characteristic.
text:
> iṣṭe 'gāḍha-tṛṣṇā'---rāgera svarūpa-lakṣaṇa
> iṣṭe 'āviṣṭatā'---ei taṭastha-lakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṣṭe]]---in the desired object, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:g:gāḍha]]-[[synonyms:t:tṛṣṇā]]---deep attachment; [[synonyms:r:rāgera]]---of spontaneous love; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the primary symptom; [[synonyms:i:iṣṭe]]---unto the Supreme; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭatā]]---absorption; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:t:taṭastha]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the marginal symptom.
translation: "The primary characteristic of spontaneous love is deep attachment for the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Absorption in Him is a marginal characteristic.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.152
description: "Thus devotional service which consists of rāga [deep attachment] is called rāgātmikā, spontaneous loving service. If a devotee covets such a position, he is considered to be most fortunate.
text:
> rāgamayī-bhaktira haya 'rāgātmikā' nāma
> ta-hā śuni' lubdha haya kona bhāgyavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāga]]-[[synonyms:m:mayī]]---consisting of attachment; [[synonyms:b:bhaktira]]---of devotional service; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:r:rāgātmikā]]---spontaneous love; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:l:lubdha]]---covetous; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:b:bhāgyavān]]---some fortunate person.
translation: "Thus devotional service which consists of rāga [deep attachment] is called rāgātmikā, spontaneous loving service. If a devotee covets such a position, he is considered to be most fortunate.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.153
description: "If one follows in the footsteps of the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana out of such transcendental covetousness, he does not care for the injunctions or reasonings of śāstra. That is the way of spontaneous love.
text:
> lobhe vraja-vāsīra bhāve kare anugati
> śāstra-yukti nāhi māne---rāgānugāra prakṛti
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lobhe]]---in such covetousness; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsīra]] [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in the moods of the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana, Vraja; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:a:anugati]]---follows; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:y:yukti]]---injunctions or reasonings of the //śāstras//; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:m:māne]]---does not abide by; [[synonyms:r:rāgānugāra]]---of spontaneous love; [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]]---the nature.
translation: "If one follows in the footsteps of the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana out of such transcendental covetousness, he does not care for the injunctions or reasonings of śāstra. That is the way of spontaneous love.
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that a devotee is attracted by the service of the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana-namely the cowherd men, Mahārāja Nanda, mother Yaśodā, Rādhārāṇī, the //gopīs,// and the cows and calves. An advanced devotee is attracted by the service rendered by an eternal servitor of the Lord. This attraction is called spontaneous attraction. Technically it is called //svarūpa-upalabdhi.// This stage is not achieved in the beginning. In the beginning one has to render service strictly according to the regulative principles set forth by the revealed scriptures and spiritual master. By continuously rendering service through the process of //vaidhī bhakti,// one's natural inclination is gradually awakened. That is called spontaneous attraction, or //rāgānugā bhakti.//

An advanced devotee situated on the platform of spontaneity is already very expert in śāstric instruction, logic and argument. When he comes to the point of eternal love for Kṛṣṇa, no one can deviate him from that position, neither by argument nor by śāstric evidence. An advanced devotee has realized his eternal relationship with the Lord, and consequently he does not accept the logic and arguments of others. Such an advanced devotee has nothing to do with the //sahajiyās,// who manufacture their own way and commit sins by indulging in illicit sex, intoxication and gambling, if not meat-eating. Sometimes the //sahajiyās// imitate advanced devotees and live in their own whimsical way, avoiding the principles set down in the revealed scriptures. Unless one follows the six Gosvāmīs-Śrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Śrī Jīva, Gopāla Bhaṭṭa and Raghunātha dāsa-one cannot be a bona fide spontaneous lover of Kṛṣṇa. In this connection, Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says: //rūpa-raghunātha-pade haibe ākuti kabe hāma bujhabase yugala pirīti.// The //sahajiyās'// understanding of the love affairs between Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa is not bona fide because they do not follow the principles laid down by the six Gosvāmīs. Their illicit connection and their imitation of the dress of Rūpa Gosvāmī as well as their avoidance of the prescribed methods of revealed scriptures will lead them to the lowest regions of hell. These imitative //sahajiyās// are cheated and unfortunate. They are not equal to advanced devotees (//paramahaṁsas//). Debauchees and //paramahaṁsas// are not on the same level.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.154
description: " 'Devotional service in spontaneous love is vividly expressed and manifested by the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana. Devotional service that accords with their devotional service is called rāgānugā bhakti, or devotional service following in the wake of spontaneous loving service.'
text:
> virājantīm abhivyaktāṁ
> vraja-vāsi-janādiṣu
> rāgātmikām anusṛtā
> yā sā rāgānugocyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:virājantīm]]---shining intensely; [[synonyms:a:abhivyaktām]]---fully expressed; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsi]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādiṣu]]---among the eternal inhabitants of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:r:rāgātmikā]]---devotional service consisting of spontaneous love; [[synonyms:a:anusṛtā]]---following; [[synonyms:y:yā]]---which; [[synonyms:s:sā]]---that; [[synonyms:r:rāgānugā]]---devotional service following in the wake of spontaneous love; [[synonyms:u:ucyate]]---is said.
translation: “ 'Devotional service in spontaneous love is vividly expressed and manifested by the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana. Devotional service that accords with their devotional service is called rāgānugā bhakti, or devotional service following in the wake of spontaneous loving service.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.270).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.155
description: " 'When an advanced realized devotee hears about the affairs of the devotees of Vṛndāvana-in the mellows of śānta, dāsya, sakhya, vātsalya and mādhurya-he becomes inclined in that way, and his intelligence becomes attracted. Indeed, he begins to covet that particular type of devotion. When such covetousness is awakened, one's intelligence no longer depends on the instruction of śāstra, revealed scripture, logic or argument.'
text:
> tat-tad-bhā' vādi-mādhurye
> śrute dhīr yad apekṣate
> nātra śāstraṁ na yuktiṁ ca
> tal lobhotpatti-lakṣaṇam

translation: “ 'When an advanced realized devotee hears about the affairs of the devotees of Vṛndāvana-in the mellows of śānta, dāsya, sakhya, vātsalya and mādhurya-he becomes inclined in that way, and his intelligence becomes attracted. Indeed, he begins to covet that particular type of devotion. When such covetousness is awakened, one's intelligence no longer depends on the instruction of śāstra, revealed scripture, logic or argument.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.292).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.156-157
description: "There are two processes by which one may execute this rāgānugā bhakti—external and internal. When self-realized, the advanced devotee externally remains like a neophyte and executes all the śāstric injunctions, especially hearing and chanting. However, within his mind, in his original purified self-realized position, he serves Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana in his particular way. He serves Kṛṣṇa twenty-four hours, all day and night.
text:
> bāhya, antara,---ihāra dui ta' sādhana
> 'bāhye' sādhaka-dehe kare śravaṇa-kīrtana
>
> 'mane' nija-siddha-deha kariyā bhāvana
> rātri-dine kare vraje kṛṣṇera sevana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---externally; [[synonyms:a:antara]]---internally; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of this spontaneous love of Godhead; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---such processes of execution; [[synonyms:b:bāhye]]---externally; [[synonyms:s:sādhaka]]-[[synonyms:d:dehe]]---with the body of an advanced devotee; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---hearing and chanting; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---the mind; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---own; [[synonyms:s:siddha]]-[[synonyms:d:deha]]---eternal body or self-realized position; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:b:bhāvana]]---thinking of; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---night and day; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---executes; [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---service.
translation: "There are two processes by which one may execute this rāgānugā bhakti---external and internal. When self-realized, the advanced devotee externally remains like a neophyte and executes all the śāstric injunctions, especially hearing and chanting. However, within his mind, in his original purified self-realized position, he serves Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana in his particular way. He serves Kṛṣṇa twenty-four hours, all day and night.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.158
description: " 'The advanced devotee who is inclined to spontaneous loving service should follow the activities of a particular associate of Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana. He should execute service externally as a regulative devotee as well as internally from his self-realized position. Thus he should perform devotional service both externally and internally.'
text:
> sevā sādhaka-rūpeṇa
> siddha-rūpeṇa cātra hi
> tad-bhāva-lipsunā kāryā
> vraja-lokānusārataḥ

He should execute service externally as a regulative devotee as well as internally from his self-realized position. Thus he should perform devotional service both externally and internally.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.295).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.159
description: "Actually the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana are very dear to Kṛṣṇa. If one wants to engage in spontaneous loving service, he must follow the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana and constantly engage in devotional service within his mind.
text:
> nijābhīṣṭa kṛṣṇa-preṣṭha pācheta' lāgiyā
> nirantara sevā kare antarmanā hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:a:abhīṣṭa]]---one's own choice; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:preṣṭha]]---the servitor of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pācheta']] [[synonyms:l:lāgiyā]]---following; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---twenty-four hours a day; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---service; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---executes; [[synonyms:a:antarmanā]]---within the mind; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being.
translation: "Actually the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana are very dear to Kṛṣṇa. If one wants to engage in spontaneous loving service, he must follow the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana and constantly engage in devotional service within his mind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.16
description: " 'O my Lord, there is no limit to the unwanted orders of lusty desires. Although I have rendered them so much service, they have not shown any mercy to me. I have not been ashamed to serve them, nor have I even desired to give them up. O my Lord, O head of the Yadu dynasty, recently, however, my intelligence has been awakened, and now I am giving them up. Due to transcendental intelligence, I now refuse to obey the unwanted orders of these desires, and I now come to You to surrender myself at Your fearless lotus feet. Kindly engage me in Your personal service and save me.'
text:
> kāmādīnāṁ kati na katidhā pālitā durnideśās
> teṣāṁ jātā mayi na karuṇā na trapā nopaśāntiḥ
> utsṛjyaitān atha yadu-pate sāmprataṁ labdha-buddhis
> tvām āyātaḥ śaraṇam abhayaṁ māṁ niyuṅkṣvātma-dāsye
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādīnām]]---of my masters such as lust, anger, greed, illusion and envy; [[synonyms:k:kati]]---how many; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:k:katidhā]]---in how many ways; [[synonyms:p:pālitāḥ]]---obeyed; [[synonyms:d:durnideśāḥ]]---undesirable orders; [[synonyms:t:teṣām]]---of them; [[synonyms:j:jātā]]---generated; [[synonyms:m:mayi]]---unto me; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:k:karuṇā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:t:trapā]]---shame; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:u:upaśāntiḥ]]---desire to cease; [[synonyms:u:utsṛjya]]---giving up; [[synonyms:e:etān]]---all these; [[synonyms:a:atha]]---herewith; [[synonyms:y:yadu]]-[[synonyms:p:pate]]---O best of the Yadu dynasty; [[synonyms:s:sāmpratam]]---now; [[synonyms:l:labdha]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhiḥ]]---having awakened intelligence; [[synonyms:t:tvām]]---You; [[synonyms:ā:āyātaḥ]]---approached; [[synonyms:ś:śaraṇam]]---who are the shelter; [[synonyms:a:abhayam]]---fearless; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---me; [[synonyms:n:niyuṅkṣva]]---please engage; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsye]]---in Your personal service.
translation: “ 'O my Lord, there is no limit to the unwanted orders of lusty desires. Although I have rendered them so much service, they have not shown any mercy to me. I have not been ashamed to serve them, nor have I even desired to give them up. O my Lord, O head of the Yadu dynasty, recently, however, my intelligence has been awakened, and now I am giving them up. Due to transcendental intelligence, I now refuse to obey the unwanted orders of these desires, and I now come to You to surrender myself at Your fearless lotus feet. Kindly engage me in Your personal service and save me.'
purport: This verse is also quoted in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (3.2.35). When we chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// we are saying, "Hare! O energy of the Lord! O my Lord Kṛṣṇa!" In this way we are simply addressing the Lord and His spiritual potency represented as Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, Sītā-Rāma, or Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa. The devotee always prays to the Lord and His internal energy (consort) so that he may engage in Their transcendental loving service. When the conditioned soul attains his real spiritual energy and fully surrenders unto the Lord's lotus feet, he tries to engage in the Lord's service. This is the real constitutional position of the living entity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.160
description: " 'The devotee should always think of Kṛṣṇa within himself, and one should choose a very dear devotee who is a servitor of Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana. One should constantly engage in topics about that servitor and his loving relationship to Kṛṣṇa, and one should live in Vṛndāvana. However, if one is physically unable to go to Vṛndāvana, he should mentally live there.'
text:
> kṛṣṇaṁ smaran janaṁ cāsya
> preṣṭhaṁ nija-samīhitam
> tat-tat-kathā-rataś cāsau
> kuryād vāsaṁ vraje sadā

translation: “ 'The devotee should always think of Kṛṣṇa within himself, and one should choose a very dear devotee who is a servitor of Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana. One should constantly engage in topics about that servitor and his loving relationship to Kṛṣṇa, and one should live in Vṛndāvana. However, if one is physically unable to go to Vṛndāvana, he should mentally live there.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.294).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.161
description: "Kṛṣṇa has many types of devotees-some are servants, some are friends, some are parents, and some are conjugal lovers. Those who are situated in one of these attitudes of spontaneous love according to their choice are considered to be on the path of spontaneous loving service.
text:
> dāsa-sakhā-pitrādi-preyasīra gaṇa
> rāga-mārge nija-nija-bhāvera gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---servants; [[synonyms:s:sakhā]]---friends; [[synonyms:p:pitṛ]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---parents; [[synonyms:p:preyasīra]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---conjugal lovers; [[synonyms:r:rāga]]-[[synonyms:m:mārge]]---on the path of spontaneous loving service; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:n:nija]]---of one's own choice; [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of the ecstasy; [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---counting.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa has many types of devotees-some are servants, some are friends, some are parents, and some are conjugal lovers. Those who are situated in one of these attitudes of spontaneous love according to their choice are considered to be on the path of spontaneous loving service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.162
description: " 'My dear mother, Devahūti! O emblem of peace! My weapon, the disc of time, never vanquishes those for whom I am very dear, for whom I am the Supersoul, the son, friend, spiritual master, well-wisher, worshipable Deity and desired goal. Since the devotees are always attached to Me, they are never vanquished by the agents of time.'
text:
> na karhicin mat-parāḥ śānta-rūpe
> naṅkṣyanti no me 'nimiṣo leḍhi hetiḥ
> yeṣām ahaṁ priya ātmā sutaś ca
> sakhā guruḥ suhṛdo daivam iṣṭam
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:k:karhicit]]---at any time; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:p:parāḥ]]---devotees of Me; [[synonyms:ś:śānta]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---O mother, the symbol of peacefulness; [[synonyms:n:naṅkṣyanti]]---will perish; [[synonyms:n:no]]---nor; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:a:animiṣaḥ]]---time; [[synonyms:l:leḍhi]]---licks up (destroys); [[synonyms:h:hetiḥ]]---weapon; [[synonyms:y:yeṣām]]---of whom; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:p:priyaḥ]]---dear; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the Supersoul; [[synonyms:s:sutaḥ]]---the son; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:s:sakhā]]---friend; [[synonyms:g:guruḥ]]---spiritual master; [[synonyms:s:suhṛdaḥ]]---well-wisher; [[synonyms:d:daivam]]---the Deity; [[synonyms:i:iṣṭam]]---chosen.
translation: “ 'My dear mother, Devahūti! O emblem of peace! My weapon, the disc of time, never vanquishes those for whom I am very dear, for whom I am the Supersoul, the son, friend, spiritual master, well-wisher, worshipable Deity and desired goal. Since the devotees are always attached to Me, they are never vanquished by the agents of time.'
purport: This was spoken by Kapiladeva to His mother Devahūti and is recorded in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:25:38|(3.25.38)]]. Kapiladeva instructed His mother in //sāṅkhya-yoga,// but the importance of //bhakti-yoga// is mentioned here. Later //sāṅhkya-yoga// was imitated by atheists, whose system was founded by a different Kapiladeva, Ṛṣi Kapiladeva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.163
description: " 'Let me offer my respectful obeisances again and again to those who always eagerly meditate upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead as a husband, son, friend, brother, father or intimate friend.'
text:
> pati-putra-suhṛd-bhrātṛ-
> pitṛvan mitravad dharim
> ye dhyāyanti sadodyuktās
> tebhyo 'pīha namo namaḥ

translation: “ 'Let me offer my respectful obeisances again and again to those who always eagerly meditate upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead as a husband, son, friend, brother, father or intimate friend.'
purport: This verse appears in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.308).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.164
description: "If one engages in spontaneous loving service to the Lord, his affection at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa gradually increases.
text:
> ei mata kare yebā rāgānugā-bhakti
> kṛṣṇera caraṇe tāṅra upajaya 'prīti'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---executes; [[synonyms:y:yebā]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:r:rāgānugā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---spontaneous devotional service to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:u:upajaya]]---awakens; [[synonyms:p:prīti]]---affection.
translation: "If one engages in spontaneous loving service to the Lord, his affection at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa gradually increases.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.165
description: "In the seed of affection, there is attachment which goes by two names, rati and bhāva. The Supreme Personality of Godhead comes under the control of such attachment.
text:
> prīty-aṅkure 'rati', 'bhāva'---haya dui nāma
> yāhā haite vaśa hana śrī-bhagavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prīti]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅkure]]---in the seed of affection; [[synonyms:r:rati]]---attachment; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---emotion; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---two names; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from which; [[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---controlled; [[synonyms:h:hana]]---is; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: "In the seed of affection, there is attachment which goes by two names, rati and bhāva. The Supreme Personality of Godhead comes under the control of such attachment.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments on this verse. Externally a devotee performs all the items of devotional service-//śravaṇa// and //kīrtana-//in nine different ways, and within his mind he always thinks of his eternal relationship with Kṛṣṇa and follows in the footsteps of the devotees of Vṛndāvana. If one engages himself in the service of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in this way, he can transcend the regulative principles enjoined in the //śāstras// and, through his spiritual master, fully engage in rendering spontaneous love to Kṛṣṇa. In this way, he attains affection at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa actually comes under the control of such spontaneous feelings, and ultimately one can attain association with the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.166
description: "That by which one can attain loving service to the Lord I have described in detail as the execution of devotional service called abhidheya.
text:
> yāhā haite pāi kṛṣṇera prema-sevana
> eita' kahiluṅ 'abhidheya'-vivaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from which; [[synonyms:p:pāi]]---I can get; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:s:sevana]]---affectionate service; [[synonyms:e:eita']]---this; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have done; [[synonyms:a:abhidheya]]-[[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---description of the means (devotional service) in detail.
translation: "That by which one can attain loving service to the Lord I have described in detail as the execution of devotional service called abhidheya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.167
description: "My dear Sanātana, I have briefly described the process of devotional service in practice, which is the means for obtaining love of Kṛṣṇa. It cannot be described broadly."
text:
> abhidheya, sādhana-bhakti ebe kahiluṅ sanātana
> saṅkṣepe kahiluṅ, vistāra nā yāya varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:abhidheya]]---the means of obtaining the desired object; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service performed by means of the body and senses; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have described; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---My dear Sanātana; [[synonyms:s:saṅkṣepe]]---in short; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have described; [[synonyms:v:vistāra]]---expansion; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---is not possible; [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---describing.
translation: "My dear Sanātana, I have briefly described the process of devotional service in practice, which is the means for obtaining love of Kṛṣṇa. It cannot be described broadly."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.168
description: Whoever hears the process of practical devotional service very soon attains shelter at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa in love and affection.
text:
> abhidheya sādhana-bhakti śune yei jana
> acirāt pāya sei kṛṣṇa-prema-dhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:abhidheya]]---necessary duty; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service in practice; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hears; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:a:acirāt]]---very soon; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that person; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---the treasure of love of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Whoever hears the process of practical devotional service very soon attains shelter at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa in love and affection.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.169
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation:
Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Twenty-second Chapter, describing the execution of devotional service.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.17
description: "Devotional service to Kṛṣṇa is the chief function of the living entity. There are different methods for the liberation of the conditioned soul-karma, jñāna, yoga and bhakti—but all are dependent on bhakti.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-bhakti haya abhidheya-pradhāna
> bhakti-mukha-nirīkṣaka karma-yoga-jñāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:a:abhidheya]]-[[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---the chief function of the living entity; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---of the face of devotional service; [[synonyms:n:nirīkṣaka]]---observers; [[synonyms:k:karma]]-[[synonyms:y:yoga]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---fruitive activities, mystic yoga and speculative knowledge.
translation: "Devotional service to Kṛṣṇa is the chief function of the living entity. There are different methods for the liberation of the conditioned soul-karma, jñāna, yoga and bhakti---but all are dependent on bhakti.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.18
description: "But for devotional service, all other methods for spiritual self-realization are weak and insignificant. Unless one comes to the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa, jñāna and yoga cannot give the desired results.
text:
> ei saba sādhanera ati tuccha bala
> kṛṣṇa-bhakti vinā tāhā dite nāre phala
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all these; [[synonyms:s:sādhanera]]---of methods of spiritual activities; [[synonyms:a:ati]]---very; [[synonyms:t:tuccha]]---insignificant; [[synonyms:b:bala]]---strength; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---all these; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to deliver; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---are not able; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---the desired result.
translation: "But for devotional service, all other methods for spiritual self-realization are weak and insignificant. Unless one comes to the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa, jñāna and yoga cannot give the desired results.
purport:
In Vedic scriptures, stress is sometimes given to fruitive activity, speculative knowledge and the mystic //yoga// system. Although people are inclined to practice these processes, they cannot attain the desired results without being touched by //kṛṣṇa-bhakti,// devotional service. In other words, the real desired result is to invoke dormant love for Kṛṣṇa. //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:2:6|(1.2.6)]] states:

> sa vai puṁsāṁ paro dharmo
> yato bhaktir adhokṣaje
> ahaituky apratihatā
> yayātmā suprasīdati

//Karma, jñāna// and //yoga// cannot actually awaken love of Godhead. One has to take to the Lord's devotional service, and the more one is inclined to devotional service, the more he loses interest in other so-called achievements. Dhruva Mahārāja went to practice mystic //yoga// to see the Lord personally face to face, but when he developed an interest in devotional service, he saw that he was not being benefited by //karma, jñāna// and //yoga.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.19
description: " 'When pure knowledge is beyond all material affinity but is not dedicated to the Supreme PersonaIity of Godhead [Kṛṣṇa], it does not appear very beautiful, although it is knowledge without a material tinge. What, then, is the use of fruitive activities-which are naturally painful from the beginning and transient by nature-if they are not utilized for the devotional service of the Lord? How can they be very attractive?'
text:
> naiṣkarmyam apy acyuta-bhāva-varjitaṁ
> na śobhate jñānam alaṁ nirañjanam
> kutaḥ punaḥ śaśvad abhadram īśvare
> na cārpitaṁ karma yad apy akāraṇam
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:naiṣkarmyam]]---which does not produce enjoyment of the resultant action; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:a:acyuta]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---of devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:v:varjitam]]---devoid; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:ś:śobhate]]---looks beautiful; [[synonyms:j:jñānam]]---speculative knowledge; [[synonyms:a:alam]]---exceedingly; [[synonyms:n:nirañjanam]]---which is without material contamination; [[synonyms:k:kutaḥ]]---how much less; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:ś:śaśvat]]---always (at the time of practicing and at the time of achieving the goal); [[synonyms:a:abhadram]]---inauspicious; [[synonyms:ī:īśvare]]---to the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:a:arpitam]]---dedicated; [[synonyms:k:karma]]---activities; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:a:akāraṇam]]---causeless.
translation: “ 'When pure knowledge is beyond all material affinity but is not dedicated to the Supreme PersonaIity of Godhead [Kṛṣṇa], it does not appear very beautiful, although it is knowledge without a material tinge. What, then, is the use of fruitive activities-which are naturally painful from the beginning and transient by nature-if they are not utilized for the devotional service of the Lord? How can they be very attractive?'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:5:12|(1.5.12)]]. Even after writing many Vedic literatures, Vyāsadeva felt very morose. Therefore his spiritual master, Nāradadeva, told him that he could be happy by writing about the activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Up to that time, Śrīla Vyāsadeva had written the //karma-kāṇḍa// and //jñāna-kāṇḍa// sections of the //Vedas,// but he had not written about //upāsanā-kāṇḍa,// or //bhakti.// Thus his spiritual master, Nārada, chastised him and advised him to write about the activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore Vyāsadeva began writing //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.2
description: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaitacandra! All glories to all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!
text:
> jaya jaya śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya nityānanda
> jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]] [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---to Advaita Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---to the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaitacandra! All glories to all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.20
description: " 'Those who perform severe austerities and penances, those who give away all their possessions out of charity, those who are very famous for their auspicious activity, those who are engaged in meditation and mental speculation, and even those who are very expert in reciting the Vedic mantras, are not able to obtain any auspicious results, although they are engaged in auspicious activities, if they do not dedicate their activities to the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. I therefore repeatedly offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose glories are always auspicious.'
text:
> tapasvino dāna-parā yaśasvino
> manasvino mantra-vidaḥ sumaṅgalāḥ
> kṣemaṁ na vindanti vinā yad-arpaṇaṁ
> tasmai subhadra-śravase namo namaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tapasvinaḥ]]---those engaged in severe austerities and penances; [[synonyms:d:dāna]]-[[synonyms:p:parāḥ]]---those engaged in giving his possessions as charity; [[synonyms:y:yaśasvinaḥ]]---those famous in society; [[synonyms:m:manasvinaḥ]]---experts in mental speculation or meditation; [[synonyms:m:mantra]]-[[synonyms:v:vidaḥ]]---experts in reciting the Vedic hymns; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:maṅgalāḥ]]---very auspicious; [[synonyms:k:kṣemam]]---real, eternal auspiciousness; [[synonyms:n:na]]---never; [[synonyms:v:vindanti]]---obtain; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:y:yat]]-[[synonyms:a:arpaṇam]]---dedicating unto whom (the Supreme Personality of Godhead); [[synonyms:t:tasmai]]---unto that Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:b:bhadra]] [[synonyms:ś:śravase]]---whose glory is very auspicious; [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]] [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---I offer my repeated respectful obeisances.
translation: “ 'Those who perform severe austerities and penances, those who give away all their possessions out of charity, those who are very famous for their auspicious activity, those who are engaged in meditation and mental speculation, and even those who are very expert in reciting the Vedic mantras, are not able to obtain any auspicious results, although they are engaged in auspicious activities, if they do not dedicate their activities to the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. I therefore repeatedly offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose glories are always auspicious.'
purport: This is also a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:4:17|(2.4.17)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.21
description: "Speculative knowledge alone, without devotional service, is not able to give liberation. On the other hand, even without knowledge one can obtain liberation if one engages in the Lord's devotional service.
text:
> kevala jñāna'mukti' dite nāre bhakti vine
> kṛṣṇonmukhe sei mukti haya vinā jñāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kevala]]---only; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---speculative knowledge; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to deliver; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---is not able; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:v:vine]]---without devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:u:unmukhe]]---if one is attached to the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---that liberation; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---appears; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---knowledge.
translation: "Speculative knowledge alone, without devotional service, is not able to give liberation. On the other hand, even without knowledge one can obtain liberation if one engages in the Lord's devotional service.
purport:
One cannot attain liberation simply by speculative knowledge. Even though one may be able to distinguish between Brahman and matter, one's liberation will be hampered if one is misled into thinking that the living entity is as good as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Indeed, one falls down again onto the material platform because considering oneself the Supreme Person, the Supreme Absolute Truth, is offensive. When such a person comes in contact with a pure devotee, he can actually become liberated from material bondage and engage in the Lord's service. A prayer by Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura is relevant here:

> bhaktis tvayi sthiratarā bhagavan yadi syād
> daivena naḥ phalati divya-kiśora-mūrtiḥ
> muktiḥ svayaṁ mukulitāñjali sevate 'smān
> dharmārtha-kāma-gatayaḥ samaya-pratīkṣāḥ

"O my Lord, if one engages in Your pure devotional service with determination, You become visible in Your original transcendental youthful form as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. As far as liberation is concerned, she stands before the devotee with folded hands waiting to render service. Religion, economic development and sense gratification are all automatically attained without separate endeavor."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.22
description: " 'My dear Lord, devotional service unto You is the only auspicious path. If one gives it up simply for speculative knowledge or the understanding that these living beings are spirit souls and the material world is false, he undergoes a great deal of trouble. He only gains troublesome and inauspicious activities. His endeavors are like beating a husk that is already devoid of rice. One's labor becomes fruitless.'
text:
> śreyaḥ-sṛtiṁ bhaktim udasya te vibho
> kliśyanti ye kevala-bodha-labdhaye
> teṣām asau kleśala eva śiṣyate
> nānyad yathā sthūla-tuṣāvaghātinām
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śreyaḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:sṛtim]]---the auspicious path of liberation; [[synonyms:b:bhaktim]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:u:udasya]]---giving up; [[synonyms:t:te]]---of You; [[synonyms:v:vibho]]---O my Lord; [[synonyms:k:kliśyanti]]---accept increased difficulties; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---all those persons who; [[synonyms:k:kevala]]---only; [[synonyms:b:bodha]]-[[synonyms:l:labdhaye]]---for obtaining knowledge; [[synonyms:t:teṣām]]---for them; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kleśalaḥ]]---trouble; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---only; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣyate]]---remains; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:anyat]]---anything else; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as much as; [[synonyms:s:sthūla]]---bulky; [[synonyms:t:tuṣa]]---husks of rice; [[synonyms:a:avaghātinām]]---of those beating.
translation: “ 'My dear Lord, devotional service unto You is the only auspicious path. If one gives it up simply for speculative knowledge or the understanding that these living beings are spirit souls and the material world is false, he undergoes a great deal of trouble. He only gains troublesome and inauspicious activities. His endeavors are like beating a husk that is already devoid of rice. One's labor becomes fruitless.'
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.14.4).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.23
description: " 'This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.'
text:
> daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī
> mama māyā duratyayā
> mām eva ye prapadyante
> māyām etaṁ taranti te
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daivī]]---belonging to the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:e:eṣā]]---this; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mayī]]---made of the three modes; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---My; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---external energy; [[synonyms:d:duratyayā]]---very difficult to surpass; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:p:prapadyante]]---surrender fully; [[synonyms:m:māyām]]---illusory energy; [[synonyms:e:etām]]---this; [[synonyms:t:taranti]]---cross over; [[synonyms:t:te]]---they.
translation: “ 'This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:7:14|(Bg. 7.14)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.24
description: "The living entity is bound around the neck by the chain of māyā because he has forgotten that he is eternally a servant of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> 'kṛṣṇa-nitya-dāsa'---jīva tāhā bhuli' gela
> ei doṣe māyā tāra galāya bāndhila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nitya]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---the living entity; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:b:bhuli']]---forgetting; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:doṣe]]---for this fault; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---the material energy; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his; [[synonyms:g:galāya]]---on the neck; [[synonyms:b:bāndhila]]---has bound.
translation: "The living entity is bound around the neck by the chain of māyā because he has forgotten that he is eternally a servant of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.25
description: "If the conditioned soul engages in the service of the Lord and simultaneously carries out the orders of his spiritual master and serves him, he can get out of the clutches of māyā and become eligible for shelter at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet.
text:
> tāte kṛṣṇa bhaje, kare gurura sevana
> māyā-jāla chuṭe, pāya kṛṣṇera caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---if one worships Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:g:gurura]] [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---service to his spiritual master; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:j:jāla]] [[synonyms:c:chuṭe]]---gets free from the binding net of //māyā//; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---shelter at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "If the conditioned soul engages in the service of the Lord and simultaneously carries out the orders of his spiritual master and serves him, he can get out of the clutches of māyā and become eligible for shelter at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet.
purport: It is a fact that every living entity is eternally a servant of Kṛṣṇa. This is forgotten due to the influence of //māyā,// which induces one to believe in material happiness. Being illusioned by //māyā,// one thinks that material happiness is the only desirable object. This material consciousness is like a chain around the neck of the conditioned soul. As long as he is bound to that conception, he cannot get out of //māyā's// clutches. However, if by Kṛṣṇa's mercy he gets in touch with a bona fide spiritual master, abides by his order and serves him, engaging other conditioned souls in the Lord's service, he then attains liberation and Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa's shelter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.26
description: "The followers of the varṇāśrama institution accept the regulative principles of the four social orders [brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya and śūdra] and four spiritual orders [brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha and sannyāsa]. However, if one carries out the regulative principles of these orders but does not render transcendental service to Kṛṣṇa, he falls into the hellish condition of material life.
text:
> cāri varṇāśramī yadi kṛṣṇa nāhi bhaje
> svakarma karite se raurave paḍi' maje
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:v:varṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśramī]]---followers of the four social and spiritual orders of life; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---serve; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:k:karma]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---performing his duty in life; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that person; [[synonyms:r:raurave]]---in a hellish condition; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---falling down; [[synonyms:m:maje]]---becomes immersed.
translation: "The followers of the varṇāśrama institution accept the regulative principles of the four social orders [brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya and śūdra] and four spiritual orders [brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha and sannyāsa]. However, if one carries out the regulative principles of these orders but does not render transcendental service to Kṛṣṇa, he falls into the hellish condition of material life.
purport: One may be a //brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya// or //śūdra,// or one may perfectly follow the spiritual principles of //brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha// and //sannyāsa,// but ultimately one falls down into a hellish condition unless one becomes a devotee. Without developing one's dormant Kṛṣṇa consciousness, one cannot be factually elevated. The regulative principles of //varṇāśrama-dharma// in themselves are insufficient for attainment of the highest perfection. That is confirmed in the following two quotations from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.2-3).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.27
description: " 'From the mouth of Brahmā, the brahminical order has come into existence. Similarly, from his arms the kṣatriyas have come, from his waist the vaiśyas have come, and from his legs the śūdras have come. These four orders and their spiritual counterparts [brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha and sannyāsa] combine to make human society complete.
text:
> mukha-bāhūru-pādebhyaḥ
> puruṣasyāśramaiḥ saha
> catvāro jajñire varṇā
> guṇair viprādayaḥ pṛthak
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---the mouth; [[synonyms:b:bāhu]]---the arms; [[synonyms:ū:ūru]]---the waist; [[synonyms:p:pādebhyaḥ]]---from the legs; [[synonyms:p:puruṣasya]]---of the Supreme Person; [[synonyms:ā:āśramaiḥ]]---the different spiritual orders; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:c:catvāraḥ]]---the four; [[synonyms:j:jajñire]]---appeared; [[synonyms:v:varṇāḥ]]---social orders; [[synonyms:g:guṇaiḥ]]---with particular qualifications; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādayaḥ]]---//brāhmaṇas// and so on; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---separately.
translation: “ 'From the mouth of Brahmā, the brahminical order has come into existence. Similarly, from his arms the kṣatriyas have come, from his waist the vaiśyas have come, and from his legs the śūdras have come. These four orders and their spiritual counterparts [brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha and sannyāsa] combine to make human society complete.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.28
description: " 'If one simply maintains an official position in the four varṇas and āśramas but does not worship the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu, he falls down from his puffed-up position into a heIlish condition.'
text:
> ya eṣāṁ puruṣaṁ sākṣād-
> ātma-prabhavam īśvaram
> na bhajanty avajānanti
> sthānād bhraṣṭāḥ patanty adhaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:e:eṣām]]---of those divisions of social and spiritual orders; [[synonyms:p:puruṣam]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhavam]]---the source of everyone; [[synonyms:ī:īśvaram]]---the supreme controller; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:b:bhajanti]]---worship; [[synonyms:a:avajānanti]]---or who neglect; [[synonyms:s:sthānāt]]---from their proper place; [[synonyms:b:bhraṣṭāḥ]]---being fallen; [[synonyms:p:patanti]]---fall; [[synonyms:a:adhaḥ]]---downward into hellish conditions.
translation: “ 'If one simply maintains an official position in the four varṇas and āśramas but does not worship the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu, he falls down from his puffed-up position into a heIlish condition.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.29
description: "There are many philosophical speculators [jñānīs] belonging to the Māyāvāda school who consider themselves liberated and call themselves Nārāyaṇa. However, their intelligence is not purified unless they engage in Kṛṣṇa's devotional service.
text:
> jñānī jīvan-mukta-daśā pāinu kari, māne
> vastutaḥ buddhi 'śuddha' nahe kṛṣṇa-bhakti vine
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jñānī]]---the speculative philosophers; [[synonyms:j:jīvan]]-[[synonyms:m:mukta]]-[[synonyms:d:daśā]]---the stage of liberation even while in this body; [[synonyms:p:pāinu]]---I have gotten; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---considers; [[synonyms:v:vastutaḥ]]---factually; [[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---intelligence; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]---purified; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:v:vine]]---without devotional service to Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "There are many philosophical speculators [jñānīs] belonging to the Māyāvāda school who consider themselves liberated and call themselves Nārāyaṇa. However, their intelligence is not purified unless they engage in Kṛṣṇa's devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.3
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I have described one's relation with Kṛṣṇa in various ways. This is the subject matter of all the Vedas. Kṛṣṇa is the center of all activities.
text:
> eita kahiluṅ sambandha-tattvera vicāra
> veda-śāstre upadeśe, kṛṣṇa---eka sāra

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I have described one's relation with Kṛṣṇa in various ways. This is the subject matter of all the Vedas. Kṛṣṇa is the center of all activities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.30
description: " 'O lotus-eyed one, those who think they are liberated in this life but do not render devotional service to You must be of impure intelligence. Although they accept severe austerities and penances and rise to the spiritual position, to impersonal Brahman realization, they fall down again because they neglect to worship Your lotus feet.'
text:
> ye 'nye 'ravindākṣa vimukta-māninas
> tvayy asta-bhāvād aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ
> āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ
> patanty adho 'nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]---all those who; [[synonyms:a:anye]]---others (nondevotees); [[synonyms:a:aravinda]]-[[synonyms:a:akṣa]]---O lotus-eyed one; [[synonyms:v:vimukta]]-[[synonyms:m:māninaḥ]]---who consider themselves liberated; [[synonyms:t:tvayi]]---unto You; [[synonyms:a:asta]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvāt]]---without devotion; [[synonyms:a:aviśuddha]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhayaḥ]]---whose intelligence is not purified; [[synonyms:ā:āruhya]]---having ascended; [[synonyms:k:kṛcchreṇa]]---by severe austerities and penances; [[synonyms:p:param]] [[synonyms:p:padam]]---to the supreme position; [[synonyms:t:tataḥ]]---from there; [[synonyms:p:patanti]]---fall; [[synonyms:a:adhaḥ]]---down; [[synonyms:a:anādṛta]]---without respecting; [[synonyms:y:yuṣmat]]---Your; [[synonyms:a:aṅghrayaḥ]]---lotus feet.
translation: “ 'O lotus-eyed one, those who think they are liberated in this life but do not render devotional service to You must be of impure intelligence. Although they accept severe austerities and penances and rise to the spiritual position, to impersonal Brahman realization, they fall down again because they neglect to worship Your lotus feet.'
purport: This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:10:2:32|(10.2.32)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.31
description: "Kṛṣṇa is compared to sunshine, and māyā is compared to darkness. Wherever there is sunshine, there cannot be darkness. As soon as one takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, the darkness of illusion (the influence of the external energy) will immediately vanish.
text:
> kṛṣṇa---sūrya-sama; māyā haya andhakāra
> yāhāṅ kṛṣṇa, tāhāṅ nāhi māyāra adhikāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:sūrya]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---like the sun planet; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---the illusory energy; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:a:andhakāra]]---darkness; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---wherever there is Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:m:māyāra]]---of //māyā,// or the darkness of illusion; [[synonyms:a:adhikāra]]---the jurisdiction.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa is compared to sunshine, and māyā is compared to darkness. Wherever there is sunshine, there cannot be darkness. As soon as one takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, the darkness of illusion (the influence of the external energy) will immediately vanish.
purport:
In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:9:34|(2.9.34)]] it is stated:

> ṛte 'rthaṁ yat pratīyeta
> na pratīyeta cātmani
> tad vidyād ātmano māyāṁ
> yathābhāso yathā tamaḥ

Wherever there is light, there cannot be darkness. When a living entity becomes Kṛṣṇa conscious, he is immediately relieved of all material lusty desires. Lusty desires and greed are associated with //rajas// and //tamas,// darkness and passion. When one becomes Kṛṣṇa conscious, the modes of darkness and passion immediately vanish, and the remaining mode, //sattva-guṇa// (goodness), remains. When one is situated in the mode of goodness, he can make spiritual advancement and understand things clearly. This position is not possible for everyone. When a person is Kṛṣṇa conscious, he continuously hears about Kṛṣṇa, thinks about Him, worships Him and serves Him as a devotee. If he remains in Kṛṣṇa consciousness in this way, the darkness of //māyā// certainly will not be able to touch him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.32
description: " 'The external illusory energy of Kṛṣṇa, known as māyā, is always ashamed to stand in front of Kṛṣṇa, just as darkness is ashamed to remain before the sunshine. However, that māyā bewilders unfortunate people who have no intelligence. Thus they simply boast that this material world is theirs and that they are its enjoyers.'
text:
> vilajjamānayā yasya
> sthātum īkṣā-pathe 'muyā
> vimohitā vikatthante
> mamāham iti durdhiyaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vilajjamānaya]]---being ashamed; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:s:sthātum]]---to remain; [[synonyms:ī:īkṣā]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---in the line of sight; [[synonyms:a:amuyā]]---by that (māyā); [[synonyms:v:vimohitāḥ]]---bewildered; [[synonyms:v:vikatthante]]---boast; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---my; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:d:durdhiyaḥ]]---having poor intelligence.
translation: “ 'The external illusory energy of Kṛṣṇa, known as māyā, is always ashamed to stand in front of Kṛṣṇa, just as darkness is ashamed to remain before the sunshine. However, that māyā bewilders unfortunate people who have no intelligence. Thus they simply boast that this material world is theirs and that they are its enjoyers.'
purport:
The entire world is bewildered because people are thinking, "This is my land," "America is mine," "India is mine." Not knowing the real value of life, people think that the material body and the land where it is produced are all in all. This is the basic principle behind nationalism, socialism and communism.
