Such thinking, which simply bewilders the living being, is nothing but rascalism. It is due to the darkness of //māyā,// but as soon as one becomes Kṛṣṇa conscious, he is immediately relieved from such misconceptions. This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:5:13|(2.5.13)]]. There is also another appropriate verse in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:7:47|(2.7.47)]]:

> śaśvat praśāntam abhayaṁ pratibodha-mātraṁ
> śuddhaṁ samaṁ sad-asataḥ paramātma-tattvam
> śabdo na yatra puru-kārakavān kriyārtho
> māyā paraity abhimukhe ca vilajjamānā
> tad vai padaṁ bhagavataḥ paramasya puṁso
> brahmeti yad vidur ajasra-sukhaṁ viśokam

"What is realized as the Absolute Brahman is full of unlimited bliss without grief. That is certainly the ultimate phase of the supreme enjoyer, the Personality of Godhead. He is eternally void of all disturbances, fearless, completely conscious as opposed to matter, uncontaminated and without distinctions. He is the principal, primeval cause of all causes and effects, in whom there is no sacrifice for fruitive activities and in whom the illusory energy does not stand."

This verse was spoken by Lord Brahmā when he was questioned by the great sage Nārada. Nārada was surprised to see the creator of the universe meditating, for he was doubting whether there was someone greater than Lord Brahmā. While answering the great sage Nārada, Lord Brahmā described the position of //māyā// and the bewildered living entities. This verse was spoken in that connection.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.33
description: "One is immediately freed from the clutches of māyā if he seriously and sincerely says, 'My dear Lord Kṛṣṇa, although I have forgotten You for so many long years in the material world, today I am surrendering unto You. I am Your sincere and serious servant. Please engage me in Your service.'
text:
> 'kṛṣṇa, tomāra haṅa' yadi bale eka-bāra
> māyā-bandha haite kṛṣṇa tāre kare pāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---O my Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:h:haṅa]]---I am Yours; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---someone says; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---once; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:b:bandha]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the bondage of conditional life; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---him; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:p:pāra]]---releases.
translation: "One is immediately freed from the clutches of māyā if he seriously and sincerely says, 'My dear Lord Kṛṣṇa, although I have forgotten You for so many long years in the material world, today I am surrendering unto You. I am Your sincere and serious servant. Please engage me in Your service.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.34
description: " 'It is My vow that if one only once seriously surrenders unto Me, saying, "My dear Lord, from this day I am Yours," and prays to Me for courage, I shall immediately award courage to that person, and he will always remain safe from that time on.'
text:
> sakṛd eva prapanno yas
> tavāsmīti ca yācate
> abhayaṁ sarvadā tasmai
> dadāmy etad vrataṁ mama
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakṛt]]---once only; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:p:prapannaḥ]]---surrendered; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Yours; [[synonyms:a:asmi]]---I am; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:y:yācate]]---prays; [[synonyms:a:abhayam]]---fearlessness; [[synonyms:s:sarvadā]]---always; [[synonyms:t:tasmai]]---unto him; [[synonyms:d:dadāmi]]---I give; [[synonyms:e:etat]]---this; [[synonyms:v:vratam]]---vow; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---My.
translation: “ 'It is My vow that if one only once seriously surrenders unto Me, saying, "My dear Lord, from this day I am Yours," and prays to Me for courage, I shall immediately award courage to that person, and he will always remain safe from that time on.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Rāmāyaṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.35
description: "Due to bad association, the living entity desires material happiness, liberation or merging into the impersonal aspect of the Lord, or he engages in mystic yoga for material power. If such a person actually becomes intelligent, he takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness by engaging himself in intense devotional service to Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> bhukti-mukti-siddhi-kāmī 'subuddhi' yadi haya
> gāḍha-bhakti-yoge tabe kṛṣṇere bhajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhukti]]---of material enjoyment; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---of impersonal liberation; [[synonyms:s:siddhi]]---of achieving mystic power; [[synonyms:k:kāmī]]---desirous; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---actually intelligent; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---he is; [[synonyms:g:gāḍha]]---deep; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:y:yoge]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]] [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---worships Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Due to bad association, the living entity desires material happiness, liberation or merging into the impersonal aspect of the Lord, or he engages in mystic yoga for material power. If such a person actually becomes intelligent, he takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness by engaging himself in intense devotional service to Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.36
description: " 'Whether one desires everything or nothing, or whether he desires to merge into the existence of the Lord, he is intelligent only if he worships Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by rendering transcendental Ioving service.'
text:
> akāmaḥ sarva-kāmo vā
> mokṣa-kāma udāra-dhīḥ
> tīvreṇa bhakti-yogena
> yajeta puruṣaṁ param
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:akāmaḥ]]---a pure devotee with no desire for material enjoyment; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāmaḥ]]---one who has no end to his desires for material enjoyment; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:m:mokṣa]]-[[synonyms:k:kāmaḥ]]---one who desires to merge into the existence of Brahman; [[synonyms:u:udāra]]-[[synonyms:d:dhīḥ]]---being very intelligent; [[synonyms:t:tīvreṇa]]---firm; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:y:yogena]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:y:yajeta]]---should worship; [[synonyms:p:puruṣam]]---the person; [[synonyms:p:param]]---supreme.
translation: “ 'Whether one desires everything or nothing, or whether he desires to merge into the existence of the Lord, he is intelligent only if he worships Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by rendering transcendental Ioving service.'
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:3:10|(2.3.10)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.37
description: "If those who desire material enjoyment or merging into the existence of the Absolute Truth engage in the Lord's transcendental loving service, they will immediately attain shelter at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, although they did not ask for it. Kṛṣṇa is therefore very merciful.
text:
> anya-kāmī yadi kare kṛṣṇera bhajana
> nā māgiteha kṛṣṇa tāre dena sva-caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:k:kāmī]]---one who desires many other things; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---he performs; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:m:māgiteha]]---although not asking; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---to him; [[synonyms:d:dena]]---gives; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the shelter of His lotus feet.
translation: "If those who desire material enjoyment or merging into the existence of the Absolute Truth engage in the Lord's transcendental loving service, they will immediately attain shelter at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, although they did not ask for it. Kṛṣṇa is therefore very merciful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.38
description: "Kṛṣṇa says, 'If one engages in My transcendental loving service but at the same time wants the opulence of material enjoyment, he is very, very foolish. Indeed, he is just like a person who gives up ambrosia to drink poison.
text:
> kṛṣṇa kahe,---'āmā bhaje, māge viṣaya-sukha
> amṛta chāḍi' viṣa māge,---ei baḍa mūrkha
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Kṛṣṇa says; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]] [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---he worships Me; [[synonyms:m:māge]]---but requests; [[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]---material happiness; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up the nectar; [[synonyms:v:viṣa]] [[synonyms:m:māge]]---he begs for poison; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]]---he is a great fool.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa says, 'If one engages in My transcendental loving service but at the same time wants the opulence of material enjoyment, he is very, very foolish. Indeed, he is just like a person who gives up ambrosia to drink poison.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.39
description: " 'Since I am very intelligent, why should I give this fool material prosperity? Instead I shall induce him to take the nectar of the shelter of My lotus feet and make him forget illusory material enjoyment.'
text:
> āmi---vijña, ei mūrkhe 'viṣaya' kene diba?
> sva-caraṇāmṛta diyā 'viṣaya' bhulāiba
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:v:vijña]]---all-intelligent; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:m:mūrkhe]]---unto this foolish person; [[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]---material enjoyment; [[synonyms:k:kene]] [[synonyms:d:diba]]---why should I give; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---the nectar of shelter at My lotus feet; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving; [[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]---the idea of material enjoyment; [[synonyms:b:bhulāiba]]---I shall make him forget.
translation: “ 'Since I am very intelligent, why should I give this fool material prosperity? Instead I shall induce him to take the nectar of the shelter of My lotus feet and make him forget illusory material enjoyment.'
purport: Those who are interested in material enjoyment are known as //bhukti.// One who is interested in merging into the effulgence of Brahman or perfecting the mystic //yoga// system is not a devotee at all. Devotees do not have such desires. However, if a //karmī, jñānī// or //yogī// somehow contacts a devotee and renders devotional service, Kṛṣṇa immediately awards him love of God and gives him shelter at His lotus feet, although he may have no idea how to develop love of Kṛṣṇa. If a person wants material profit from devotional service, Kṛṣṇa condemns such materialistic desires. To desire material opulence while engaging in devotional service is foolish. Although the person may be foolish, Kṛṣṇa, being all-intelligent, engages him in His devotional service in such a way that he gradually forgets material opulence. The point is that we should not try to exchange loving service for material prosperity. If we are actually surrendered to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, our only desire should be to satisfy Kṛṣṇa. That is pure Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Surrender does not mean that we demand something from the Lord but that we completely depend on His mercy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.4
description: "Now I shall speak about the characteristics of devotional service, by which one can attain the shelter of Kṛṣṇa and His loving transcendental service.
text:
> ebe kahi, śuna, abhidheya-lakṣaṇa
> yāhā haite pāi---kṛṣṇa, kṛṣṇa-prema-dhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I shall explain; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:a:abhidheya]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---one's prime business (devotional service); [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from which; [[synonyms:p:pāi]]---one can get; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---and the wealth of transcendental love for Him.
translation: "Now I shall speak about the characteristics of devotional service, by which one can attain the shelter of Kṛṣṇa and His loving transcendental service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.40
description: " 'Whenever Kṛṣṇa is requested to fulfill one's desire, He undoubtedly does so, but He does not award anything which, after being enjoyed, will cause someone to petition Him again and again to fulfill further desires. When one has other desires but engages in the Lord's service, Kṛṣṇa forcibly gives one shelter at His lotus feet, where one will forget all other desires.'
text:
> satyaṁ diśaty arthitam arthito nṛṇāṁ
> naivārthado yat punar arthitā yataḥ
> svayaṁ vidhatte bhajatām anicchatām
> icchā-pidhānaṁ nija-pāda-pallavam
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:satyam]]---it is true; [[synonyms:d:diśati]]---He awards; [[synonyms:a:arthitam]]---that which is desired; [[synonyms:a:arthitaḥ]]---being requested; [[synonyms:n:nṛṇām]]---by human beings; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:d:daḥ]]---giving desired things; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:a:arthitā]]---request; [[synonyms:y:yataḥ]]---from which; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---Himself; [[synonyms:v:vidhatte]]---He gives; [[synonyms:b:bhajatām]]---of those engaged in devotional service; [[synonyms:a:anicchatām]]---even though not desiring; [[synonyms:i:icchā]]-[[synonyms:p:pidhānam]]---covering all other desires; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:pallavam]]---the shelter of His own lotus feet.
translation: “ 'Whenever Kṛṣṇa is requested to fulfill one's desire, He undoubtedly does so, but He does not award anything which, after being enjoyed, will cause someone to petition Him again and again to fulfill further desires. When one has other desires but engages in the Lord's service, Kṛṣṇa forcibly gives one shelter at His lotus feet, where one will forget all other desires.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:5:19:27|(5.19.27)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.41
description: "When someone engages in Lord Kṛṣṇa's devotional service for the satisfaction of the senses and instead acquires a taste to serve Kṛṣṇa, he gives up his material desires and willingly offers himself as an eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> kāma lāgi' kṛṣṇe bhaje, pāya kṛṣṇa-rase
> kāma chāḍi' 'dāsa' haite haya abhilāṣe
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāma]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for fulfillment of one's material desires; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]] [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---one engages in the transcendental service of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---he gets; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rase]]---a taste of the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kāma]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up all desires for material enjoyment; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---to be an eternal servant of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:a:abhilāṣe]]---aspiration.
translation: "When someone engages in Lord Kṛṣṇa's devotional service for the satisfaction of the senses and instead acquires a taste to serve Kṛṣṇa, he gives up his material desires and willingly offers himself as an eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.42
description: [When he was being benedicted by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Dhruva Mahārāja said] " 'O my Lord, because I was seeking an opulent material position, I was performing severe types of penance and austerity. Now I have gotten You, who are very difficult for the great demigods, saintly persons and kings to attain. I was searching after a piece of glass, but instead I have found a most valuable jewel. Therefore I am so satisfied that I do not wish to ask any benediction from You.'
text:
> sthānābhilāṣī tapasi sthito 'haṁ
> tvāṁ prāptavān deva-munīndra-guhyam
> kācaṁ vicinvann api divya-ratnaṁ
> svāmin kṛtārtho 'smi varaṁ na yāce
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]-[[synonyms:a:abhilāṣī]]---desiring a very high position in the material world; [[synonyms:t:tapasi]]---in severe austerities and penances; [[synonyms:s:sthitaḥ]]---situated; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tvām]]---You; [[synonyms:p:prāptavān]]---have obtained; [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:m:muni]]-[[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:g:guhyam]]---difficult to achieve even for great demigods, saintly persons and kings; [[synonyms:k:kācam]]---a piece of glass; [[synonyms:v:vicinvan]]---searching for; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:r:ratnam]]---a transcendental gem; [[synonyms:s:svāmin]]---O my Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:arthaḥ]] [[synonyms:a:asmi]]---I am fully satisfied; [[synonyms:v:varam]]---any benediction; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:y:yāce]]---I do not ask.
translation: [When he was being benedicted by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Dhruva Mahārāja said] " 'O my Lord, because I was seeking an opulent material position, I was performing severe types of penance and austerity. Now I have gotten You, who are very difficult for the great demigods, saintly persons and kings to attain. I was searching after a piece of glass, but instead I have found a most valuable jewel. Therefore I am so satisfied that I do not wish to ask any benediction from You.'
purport: This verse is from the //Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya// (7.28).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.43
description: "There are unlimited conditioned souls who are bereft of Lord Kṛṣṇa's service. Not knowing how to cross the ocean of nescience, they are scattered by waves, time and tide. However, some are fortunate to contact devotees, and by this contact they are deIivered from the ocean of nescience, just as a log, floating down a river, accidentally washes upon the bank.
text:
> saṁsāra bhramite kona bhāgye keha tare
> nadīra pravāhe yena kāṣṭha lāge tīre
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]] [[synonyms:b:bhramite]]---wandering throughout the universe; [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:b:bhāgye]]---by some good fortune; [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:t:tare]]---someone crosses the ocean of nescience; [[synonyms:n:nadīra]] [[synonyms:p:pravāhe]]---in the flow of the river; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---just as; [[synonyms:k:kāṣṭha]]---wood; [[synonyms:l:lāge]]---sticks; [[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank.
translation: "There are unlimited conditioned souls who are bereft of Lord Kṛṣṇa's service. Not knowing how to cross the ocean of nescience, they are scattered by waves, time and tide. However, some are fortunate to contact devotees, and by this contact they are deIivered from the ocean of nescience, just as a log, floating down a river, accidentally washes upon the bank.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.44
description: "Because I am so fallen, I shall never get a chance to see the Supreme Personality of Godhead." This was my false apprehension. Rather, by chance a person as fallen as I am may get to see the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although one is being carried away by the waves of the river of time, one may eventually reach the shore.'
text:
> maivaṁ mamādhamasyāpi
> syād evācyuta-darśanam
> hriyamāṇaḥ kāla-nadyā
> kvacit tarati kaścana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mā]]---not; [[synonyms:e:evam]]---thus; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---of me; [[synonyms:a:adhamasya]]---who is the most fallen; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:s:syāt]]---there may be; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:acyuta]]-[[synonyms:d:darśanam]]---seeing of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:hriyamāṇaḥ]]---being carried; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]-[[synonyms:n:nadyā]]---by the stream of time; [[synonyms:k:kvacit]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:t:tarati]]---crosses over; [[synonyms:k:kaścana]]---someone.
translation: "Because I am so fallen, I shall never get a chance to see the Supreme Personality of Godhead." This was my false apprehension. Rather, by chance a person as fallen as I am may get to see the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although one is being carried away by the waves of the river of time, one may eventually reach the shore.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.38.5).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.45
description: "By good fortune, one becomes eligible to cross the ocean of nescience, and when one's term of material existence decreases, one may get an opportunity to associate with pure devotees. By such association, one's attraction to Kṛṣṇa is awakened.
text:
> kona bhāgye kāro saṁsāra kṣayonmukha haya
> sādhu-saṅge tabe kṛṣṇe rati upajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:b:bhāgye]]---by fortune; [[synonyms:k:kāro]]---of someone; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]---conditioned life; [[synonyms:k:kṣaya]]-[[synonyms:u:unmukha]]---on the point of destruction; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---by association with devotees; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---to Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rati]]---attraction; [[synonyms:u:upa]]-[[synonyms:j:jaya]]---awakens.
translation: "By good fortune, one becomes eligible to cross the ocean of nescience, and when one's term of material existence decreases, one may get an opportunity to associate with pure devotees. By such association, one's attraction to Kṛṣṇa is awakened.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains this point. Is this //bhāgya// (fortune) the result of an accident or something else? In the scriptures, devotional service and pious activity are considered fortunate. Pious activities can be divided into three categories-pious activities that awaken one's dormant Kṛṣṇa consciousness are called //bhakty-unmukhī sukṛti.// Pious activities that bestow material opulence are called //bhogonmukhī,// and pious activities that enable the living entity to merge into the existence of the Supreme are called //mokṣonmukhī.// These last two awards of pious activity are not actually fortunate. Pious activities are fortunate when they help one become Kṛṣṇa conscious. The good fortune of //bhakty-unmukhī// is attainable only when one comes in contact with a devotee. By associating with a devotee willingly or unwillingly, one advances in devotional service, and thus one's dormant Kṛṣṇa consciousness is awakened.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.46
description: " 'O my Lord! O infallible Supreme Person! When a person wandering throughout the universes becomes eligible for liberation from material existence, he gets an opportunity to associate with devotees. When he associates with devotees, his attraction for You is awakened. You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the highest goal of the supreme devotees and the Lord of the universe.'
text:
> bhavāpavargo bhramato yadā bhavej
> janasya tarhy acyuta sat-samāgamaḥ
> sat-saṅgamo yarhi tadaiva sad-gatau
> parāvareśe tvayi jāyate ratiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhava]]-[[synonyms:a:apavargaḥ]]---liberation from the nescience of material existence; [[synonyms:b:bhramataḥ]]---wandering; [[synonyms:y:yadā]]---when; [[synonyms:b:bhavet]]---should be; [[synonyms:j:janasya]]---of a person; [[synonyms:t:tarhi]]---at that time; [[synonyms:a:acyuta]]---O Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:s:samāgamaḥ]]---association with devotees; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgamaḥ]]---association with devotees; [[synonyms:y:yarhi]]---when; [[synonyms:t:tadā]]---at that time; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---only; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:g:gatau]]---the highest goal of life; [[synonyms:p:parāvareśe]]---the Lord of the universe; [[synonyms:t:tvayi]]---to You; [[synonyms:j:jāyate]]---appears; [[synonyms:r:ratiḥ]]---attraction.
translation: “ 'O my Lord! O infallible Supreme Person! When a person wandering throughout the universes becomes eligible for liberation from material existence, he gets an opportunity to associate with devotees. When he associates with devotees, his attraction for You is awakened. You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the highest goal of the supreme devotees and the Lord of the universe.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.51.53).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.47
description: "Kṛṣṇa is situated in everyone's heart as caitya-guru, the spiritual master within. When He is kind to some fortunate conditioned soul, He personally gives one lessons to progress in devotional service, instructing the person as the Supersoul within and the spiritual master without.
text:
> kṛṣṇa yadi kṛpā kare kona bhāgyavāne
> guru-antaryāmi-rūpe śikhāya āpane
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---shows His mercy; [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:b:bhāgyavāne]]---to some fortunate person; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---of the spiritual master; [[synonyms:a:antaryāmi]]---of the Supersoul; [[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in the form; [[synonyms:ś:śikhāya]]---teaches; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa is situated in everyone's heart as caitya-guru, the spiritual master within. When He is kind to some fortunate conditioned soul, He personally gives one lessons to progress in devotional service, instructing the person as the Supersoul within and the spiritual master without.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.48
description: " 'O my Lord! Transcendental poets and experts in spiritual science could not fully express their indebtedness to You, even if they were endowed with the prolonged lifetime of Brahmā, for You appear in two features-externally as the ācārya and internally as the Supersoul-to deliver the embodied living being by directing him how to come to You.'
text:
> naivopayanty apacitiṁ kavayas taveśa
> brahmāyuṣāpi kṛtam ṛddha-mudaḥ smarantaḥ
> yo 'ntar bahis tanu-bhṛtām aśubhaṁ vidhunvann
> ācārya-caittya-vapuṣā sva-gatiṁ vyanakti
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:e:eva]]---not at all; [[synonyms:u:upayanti]]---are able to express; [[synonyms:a:apacitim]]---their gratitude; [[synonyms:k:kavayaḥ]]---learned devotees; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:ī:īśa]]---O Lord; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:ā:āyuṣā]]---with a lifetime equal to Lord Brahmā's; [[synonyms:a:api]]---in spite of; [[synonyms:k:kṛtam]]---magnanimous work; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛddha]]---increased; [[synonyms:m:mudaḥ]]---joy; [[synonyms:s:smarantaḥ]]---remembering; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---//who//; [[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]---within; [[synonyms:b:bahiḥ]]---outside; [[synonyms:t:tanu]]-[[synonyms:b:bhṛtām]]---of those who are embodied; [[synonyms:a:aśubham]]---misfortune; [[synonyms:v:vidhunvan]]---dissipating; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---of the spiritual master; [[synonyms:c:caittya]]---of the Supersoul; [[synonyms:v:vapuṣā]]---by the forms; [[synonyms:s:sva]]---own; [[synonyms:g:gatim]]---path; [[synonyms:v:vyanakti]]---shows.
translation: “ 'O my Lord! Transcendental poets and experts in spiritual science could not fully express their indebtedness to You, even if they were endowed with the prolonged lifetime of Brahmā, for You appear in two features-externally as the ācārya and internally as the Supersoul-to deliver the embodied living being by directing him how to come to You.'
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.29.6). It was spoken by Uddhava after he had been instructed in //yoga// by Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.49
description: "By associating with a devotee, one awakens his faith in devotional service to Kṛṣṇa. Because of devotional service, one's dormant love for Kṛṣṇa awakens, and thus one's material, conditional existence comes to an end.
text:
> sādhu-saṅge kṛṣṇa-bhaktye śraddhā yadi haya
> bhakti-phala 'prema' haya, saṁsāra yāya kṣaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---by the association of devotees; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---in discharging devotional service to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]]---faith; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]---the result of devotional service to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---awakens; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]---the conditioned life in material existence; [[synonyms:y:yāya]] [[synonyms:k:kṣaya]]---becomes vanquished.
translation: "By associating with a devotee, one awakens his faith in devotional service to Kṛṣṇa. Because of devotional service, one's dormant love for Kṛṣṇa awakens, and thus one's material, conditional existence comes to an end.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.5
description: "A human being's activities should be centered only about devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa. That is the verdict of all Vedic literatures, and all saintly people have ascertained this.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-bhakti---abhidheya, sarva-śāstre kaya
> ataeva muni-gaṇa kariyāche niścaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:abhidheya]]---the real activity of life; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstre]]---all Vedic literatures; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---say; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:m:muni]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all saintly persons; [[synonyms:k:kariyāche]]---have made; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---ascertainment.
translation: "A human being's activities should be centered only about devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa. That is the verdict of all Vedic literatures, and all saintly people have ascertained this.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.50
description: " 'Somehow or other, if one is attracted to talks about Me and has faith in the instructions I have set forth in Bhagavad-gītā, and if one is actually detached from material things and material existence, his dormant love for Me will be awakened by devotional service.'
text:
> yadṛcchayā mat-kathādau
> jāta-śraddhas tu yaḥ pumān
> na nirviṇṇo nātisakto
> bhakti-yogo 'sya siddhidaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadṛcchayā]]---by some good fortune; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādau]]---in talk about Me; [[synonyms:j:jāta]]-[[synonyms:ś:śraddhaḥ]]---has awakened his attraction; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]] [[synonyms:p:pumān]]---a person who; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:n:nirviṇṇaḥ]]---not falsely detached; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:a:atisaktaḥ]]---not attached to material existence; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:y:yogaḥ]]---the process of devotional service; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---for such a person; [[synonyms:s:siddhi]]-[[synonyms:d:daḥ]]---bestowing perfection.
translation: “ 'Somehow or other, if one is attracted to talks about Me and has faith in the instructions I have set forth in Bhagavad-gītā, and if one is actually detached from material things and material existence, his dormant love for Me will be awakened by devotional service.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.20.8) was spoken by Kṛṣṇa at the time of His departure from this material world. It was spoken to Uddhava.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.51
description: "Unless one is favored by a pure devotee, he cannot attain the platform of devotional service. To say nothing of kṛṣṇa-bhakti, one cannot even be relieved from the bondage of material existence.
text:
> mahat-kṛpā vinā kona karme 'bhakti' naya
> kṛṣṇa-bhakti dūre rahu, saṁsāra nahe kṣaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---the mercy of great devotees; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:k:karme]]---by some other activity; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:n:naya]]---there is not devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---love of Kṛṣṇa or devotional service to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dūre]] [[synonyms:r:rahu]]---leaving aside; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]---the bondage of material existence; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---there is not; [[synonyms:k:kṣaya]]---destruction.
translation: "Unless one is favored by a pure devotee, he cannot attain the platform of devotional service. To say nothing of kṛṣṇa-bhakti, one cannot even be relieved from the bondage of material existence.
purport:
Pious activities bring about material opulence, but one cannot acquire devotional service by any amount of material pious activity, not by giving charity, opening big hospitals and schools or working philanthropically. Devotional service can be attained only by the mercy of a pure devotee. Without a pure devotee's mercy, one cannot even escape the bondage of material existence. The word //mahat// in this verse means "a pure devotee." As confirmed in //Bhagavad-gītā://

> mahātmānas tu māṁ pārtha
> daivīṁ prakṛtim āśritāḥ
> bhajanty ananya-manaso
> jñātvā bhūtādim avyayam

"O son of Pṛthā, those who are not deluded, the great souls, are under the protection of the divine nature. They are fully engaged in devotional service because they know Me as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, original and inexhaustible." [[books:bg:9:13|(Bg. 9.13)]]

One also has to associate with such a //mahātmā// who has accepted Kṛṣṇa as the supreme source of the entire creation. Without being a //mahātmā,// one cannot understand Kṛṣṇa's absolute position. A //mahātmā// is rare and transcendental, and he is a pure devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Foolish people consider Kṛṣṇa a human being, and they consider Lord Kṛṣṇa's pure devotee an ordinary human being also. Whatever one may be, one must take shelter at the lotus feet of a devotee //mahātmā// and treat him as the most exalted well-wisher of all human society. We should take shelter of such a //mahātmā// and ask for his causeless mercy. Only by his benediction can one be relieved from attachment to a materialistic way of life. When one is thus relieved, he can engage in the Lord's transcendental loving service through the mercy of the //mahātmā.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.52
description: " 'O King Rahūgaṇa, without taking upon one's head the dust from the lotus feet of a pure devotee [a mahājana or mahātmā], one cannot attain devotional service. Devotional service is not possible to attain simply by undergoing severe austerities and penances, by gorgeously worshiping the Deity, or by strictly following the rules and regulations of the sannyāsa or gṛhastha order, nor by studying the Vedas, submerging oneself in water, or exposing oneself to fire or scorching sunlight.'
text:
> rahūgaṇaitat tapasā na yāti
> na cejyayā nirvapaṇād gṛhād vā
> na cchandasā naiva jalāgni-sūryair
> vinā mahat-pāda-rajo-'bhiṣekam
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rahūgaṇa]]---O King Rahūgaṇa; [[synonyms:e:etat]]---this; [[synonyms:t:tapasā]]---by severe austerities and penances; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:y:yāti]]---one does not obtain; [[synonyms:n:na]]---neither; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:i:ijyayā]]---by gorgeous worship; [[synonyms:n:nirvapaṇāt]]---by renounced order of life; [[synonyms:g:gṛhāt]]---by sacrifices while living in the home; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:c:chandasā]]---nor by scholarly study of the //Vedas//; [[synonyms:n:na]]---nor; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:a:agni]]-[[synonyms:s:sūryaiḥ]]---by those who worship water, fire or scorching sunshine; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:r:rajaḥ]]---of the dust of the lotus feet of a //mahātmā//; [[synonyms:a:abhiṣekam]]---the sprinkling.
translation: “ 'O King Rahūgaṇa, without taking upon one's head the dust from the lotus feet of a pure devotee [a mahājana or mahātmā], one cannot attain devotional service. Devotional service is not possible to attain simply by undergoing severe austerities and penances, by gorgeously worshiping the Deity, or by strictly following the rules and regulations of the sannyāsa or gṛhastha order, nor by studying the Vedas, submerging oneself in water, or exposing oneself to fire or scorching sunlight.'
purport: This verse appears in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:5:12:12|(5.12.12)]]. Jaḍa Bharata herein tells King Rahūgaṇa how he attained the //paramahaṁsa// stage. Mahārāja Rahūgaṇa, the King of Sindhu-sauvīra, had asked Jaḍa Bharata how he had attained the //paramahaṁsa// stage. The King had called him to carry his palanquin, but when the King heard from //paramahaṁsa// Jaḍa Bharata about the supreme philosophy, he expressed surprise and asked Jaḍa Bharata how he had attained such great liberation. At that time Jaḍa Bharata informed the King how to become detached from material attraction.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.53
description: " 'Unless human society accepts the dust of the lotus feet of great mahātmās-devotees who have nothing to do with material possessions-mankind cannot turn its attention to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. Those lotus feet vanquish all the unwanted miserable conditions of material life.'
text:
> naiṣāṁ matis tāvad urukramāṅghriṁ
> spṛśaty anarthāpagamo yad-arthaḥ
> mahīyasāṁ pāda-rajo-'bhiṣekaṁ
> niṣkiñcanānāṁ na vṛṇīta yāvat
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:e:eṣām]]---of those who are attached to household life; [[synonyms:m:matiḥ]]---the interest; [[synonyms:t:tāvat]]---that long; [[synonyms:u:urukrama]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅghrim]]---the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is credited with uncommon activities; [[synonyms:s:spṛśati]]---touches; [[synonyms:a:anartha]]---of unwanted things; [[synonyms:a:apagamaḥ]]---vanquishing; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---of which; [[synonyms:a:arthaḥ]]---result; [[synonyms:m:mahīyasām]]---of the great personalities, devotees; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:r:rajaḥ]]---of the dust of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:a:abhiṣekam]]---sprinkling on the head; [[synonyms:n:niṣkiñcanānām]]---who are completely detached from material possessions; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:v:vṛṇīta]]---does not do; [[synonyms:y:yāvat]]---as long as.
translation: “ 'Unless human society accepts the dust of the lotus feet of great mahātmās-devotees who have nothing to do with material possessions-mankind cannot turn its attention to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. Those lotus feet vanquish all the unwanted miserable conditions of material life.'
purport: This verse appears in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:7:5:32|(7.5.32)]]. When the great sage Nārada was giving instructions to Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, he narrated the activities of Prahlāda Mahārāja. This verse was spoken by Prahlāda Mahārāja to his father, Hiraṇyakaśipu, the king of demons. Prahlāda Mahārāja informed his father of the nine basic processes of //bhakti-yoga.// Whoever takes to these processes is to be considered a highly learned scholar. Hiraṇyakaśipu, however, did not like his son to talk about devotional service; therefore he immediately called his teacher, Ṣaṇḍāmarka. The teacher explained that he did not teach devotional service to Prahlāda but that the boy was naturally inclined that way. At that time Hiraṇyakaśipu became very angry and asked Prahlāda why he had become a Vaiṣṇava. In answer to this question, Prahlāda Mahārāja recited this verse to the effect that one cannot become the Lord's devotee without receiving the mercy and blessings of another devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.54
description: "The verdict of all revealed scriptures is that by even a moment's association with a pure devotee, one can attain all success.
text:
> 'sādhu-saṅga', 'sādhu-saṅga'---sarva-śāstre kaya
> lava-mātra sādhu-saṅge sarva-siddhi haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]] [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---association with pure devotees; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstre]]---all the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---say; [[synonyms:l:lava]]-[[synonyms:m:mātra]]---even for a moment; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---by association with a devotee; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:s:siddhi]]---all success; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is.
translation: "The verdict of all revealed scriptures is that by even a moment's association with a pure devotee, one can attain all success.
purport: According to astronomical calculations, //lava// is one eleventh of one second.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.55
description: " 'The value of a moment's association with a devotee of the Lord cannot even be compared to the attainment of heavenly planets or liberation from matter, and what to speak of worldly benedictions in the form of material prosperity, which is for those who are meant for death.'
text:
> tulayāma lavenāpi
> na svargaṁ nāpunar-bhavam
> bhagavat-saṅgi-saṅgasya
> martyānāṁ kimutāśiṣaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tulayāma]]---we make equal; [[synonyms:l:lavena]]---with one instant; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:s:svargam]]---heavenly planets; [[synonyms:n:na]]---nor; [[synonyms:a:apunaḥ]]-[[synonyms:b:bhavam]]---merging into the existence of the Supreme; [[synonyms:b:bhagavat]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgi]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgasya]]---of the association of devotees who are always associated with the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:m:martyānām]]---of persons destined to die; [[synonyms:k:kim]] [[synonyms:u:uta]]---what; [[synonyms:ā:āśiṣaḥ]]---the blessings.
translation: “ 'The value of a moment's association with a devotee of the Lord cannot even be compared to the attainment of heavenly planets or liberation from matter, and what to speak of worldly benedictions in the form of material prosperity, which is for those who are meant for death.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:18:13|(1.18.13)]]. This verse concerns the Vedic rites and sacrifices performed by the great sages of Naimiṣāraṇya, headed by Śaunaka Ṛṣi. The sages pointed out that association with a devotee for even less than a second is beyond comparison to a thousand Vedic rituals and sacrifices, elevation to heavenly planets or merging into the existence of the Supreme.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.56
description: "Kṛṣṇa is so merciful that simply by aiming His instructions at Arjuna, He has given protection to the whole world.
text:
> kṛṣṇa kṛpālu arjunere lakṣya kariyā
> jagatere rākhiyāchena upadeśa diyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛpālu]]---merciful; [[synonyms:a:arjunere]]---Arjuna; [[synonyms:l:lakṣya]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---aiming at; [[synonyms:j:jagatere]]---the whole world; [[synonyms:r:rākhiyāchena]]---has protected; [[synonyms:u:upadeśa]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving instructions.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa is so merciful that simply by aiming His instructions at Arjuna, He has given protection to the whole world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.57-58
description: " 'Because you are My very dear friend, I am speaking to you the most confidential part of knowledge. Hear this from Me, for it is for your benefit. Always think of Me and become My devotee, worship Me and offer obeisances unto Me. Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend.'
text:
> sarva-guhyatamaṁ bhūyaḥ
> śṛṇu me paramaṁ vacaḥ
> iṣṭo 'si me dṛḍham iti
> tato vakṣyāmi te hitam
>
> man-manā bhava mad-bhakto
> mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru
> mām evaiṣyasi satyaṁ te
> pratijāne priyo 'si me
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:g:guhya]]-[[synonyms:t:tamam]]---most confidential of all; [[synonyms:b:bhūyaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:ś:śṛṇu]]---hear; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:p:paramam]] [[synonyms:v:vacaḥ]]---supreme instruction; [[synonyms:i:iṣṭaḥ]]---beloved; [[synonyms:a:asi]]---you are; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍham]] [[synonyms:i:iti]]---very firmly; [[synonyms:t:tataḥ]]---therefore; [[synonyms:v:vakṣyāmi]]---I shall speak; [[synonyms:t:te]]---to you; [[synonyms:h:hitam]]---words of benediction; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:m:manāḥ]]---whose mind is always on Me; [[synonyms:b:bhava]]---become; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktaḥ]]---My devotee; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:y:yājī]]---My worshiper; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:n:namaskuru]]---offer obeisances; [[synonyms:m:mām]] [[synonyms:e:eva]]---to Me only; [[synonyms:e:eṣyasi]]---you will come; [[synonyms:s:satyam]]---truly; [[synonyms:t:te]]---to you; [[synonyms:p:pratijāne]]---I promise; [[synonyms:p:priyaḥ]] [[synonyms:a:asi]]---you are dear; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My.
translation: “ 'Because you are My very dear friend, I am speaking to you the most confidential part of knowledge. Hear this from Me, for it is for your benefit. Always think of Me and become My devotee, worship Me and offer obeisances unto Me. Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Bhagavad-gītā// (18.64-65).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.59
description: "Although Kṛṣṇa has previously explained the proficiency of executing Vedic rituals, performing fruitive activity as enjoined in the Vedas, practicing yoga and cultivating jñāna, these last instructions are most powerful and stand above all the others.
text:
> pūrva ājñā,---veda-dharma, karma, yoga, jñāna
> saba sādhi' śeṣe ei ājñā---balavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]] [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---previous orders; [[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---performance of Vedic ritualistic ceremonies; [[synonyms:k:karma]]---fruitive activities; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]---mystic yoga practice; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---speculative knowledge; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:s:sādhi']]---executing all these processes; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---at the end; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---this order; [[synonyms:b:balavān]]---powerful.
translation: "Although Kṛṣṇa has previously explained the proficiency of executing Vedic rituals, performing fruitive activity as enjoined in the Vedas, practicing yoga and cultivating jñāna, these last instructions are most powerful and stand above all the others.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.6
description: " 'When the mother Vedas [śruti] is questioned as to whom to worship, she says that You are the only Lord and worshipable object. Similarly, the corollaries of the śruti-śāstras, the smṛti-śāstras, give the same instructions, just like sisters. The Purāṇas, which are like brothers, follow in the footsteps of their mother. O enemy of the demon Mura, the conclusion is that You are the only shelter. Now I have understood this in truth.'
text:
> śrutir mātā pṛṣṭā diśati bhavad-ārādhana-vidhiṁ
> yathā mātur vāṇī smṛtir api tathā vakti bhaginī
> purāṇādyā ye vā sahaja-nivahās te tad-anugā
> ataḥ satyaṁ jñātaṁ murahara bhavān eva śaraṇam
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrutiḥ]]---Vedic knowledge; [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---like a mother who is affectionate to her children; [[synonyms:p:pṛṣṭā]]---when questioned; [[synonyms:d:diśati]]---she directs; [[synonyms:b:bhavat]]---of You; [[synonyms:ā:ārādhana]]---worship; [[synonyms:v:vidhim]]---the process; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---just as; [[synonyms:m:mātuḥ]] [[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---the instructions of the mother; [[synonyms:s:smṛtiḥ]]---//smṛti-śāstras,// which explain the Vedic literatures; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---similarly; [[synonyms:v:vakti]]---express; [[synonyms:b:bhaginī]]---like a sister; [[synonyms:p:purāṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādyāḥ]]---headed by the //Purāṇas//; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:s:sahaja]]-[[synonyms:n:nivahāḥ]]---like brothers; [[synonyms:t:te]]---all of them; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---of the mother; [[synonyms:a:anugāḥ]]---followers; [[synonyms:a:ataḥ]]---therefore; [[synonyms:s:satyam]]---the truth; [[synonyms:j:jñātam]]---known; [[synonyms:m:mura]]-[[synonyms:h:hara]]---O killer of the demon Mura; [[synonyms:b:bhavān]]---Your Lordship; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---only; [[synonyms:ś:śaraṇam]]---the shelter.
translation: “ 'When the mother Vedas [śruti] is questioned as to whom to worship, she says that You are the only Lord and worshipable object. Similarly, the corollaries of the śruti-śāstras, the smṛti-śāstras, give the same instructions, just like sisters. The Purāṇas, which are like brothers, follow in the footsteps of their mother. O enemy of the demon Mura, the conclusion is that You are the only shelter. Now I have understood this in truth.'
purport: This quotation from the Vedic literature was spoken by great sages.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.60
description: "If the devotee has faith in the strength of this order, he worships Lord Kṛṣṇa and gives up all other activities.
text:
> ei ājñā-bale bhaktera 'śraddhā' yadi haya
> sarva-karma tyāga kari' se kṛṣṇa bhajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]-[[synonyms:b:bale]]---on the strength of this supreme order of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhaktera]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]]---faith; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:karma]]---all other activities, material and spiritual; [[synonyms:t:tyāga]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---leaving aside; [[synonyms:s:se]]---he; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---serves Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "If the devotee has faith in the strength of this order, he worships Lord Kṛṣṇa and gives up all other activities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.61
description: " 'As long as one is not satiated by fruitive activity and has not awakened his taste for devotional service by śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoh, one has to act according to the regulative principles of the Vedic injunctions.'
text:
> tāvat karmāṇi kurvīta
> na nirvidyeta yāvatā
> mat-kathā-śravaṇādau vā
> śraddhā yāvan na jāyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāvat]]---up to that time; [[synonyms:k:karmāṇi]]---fruitive activities; [[synonyms:k:kurvīta]]---one should execute; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:n:nirvidyeta]]---is not satiated; [[synonyms:y:yāvatā]]---as long as; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---of discourses about Me; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādau]]---in the matter of //śravaṇam, kīrtanam,// and so on; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]]---faith; [[synonyms:y:yāvat]]---as long as; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jāyate]]---is awakened.
translation: “ 'As long as one is not satiated by fruitive activity and has not awakened his taste for devotional service by śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoh, one has to act according to the regulative principles of the Vedic injunctions.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.20.9).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.62
description: "By rendering transcendental loving service to Kṛṣṇa, one automatically performs all subsidiary activities. This confident, firm faith, favorable to the discharge of devotional service, is called śraddhā.
text:
> 'śraddhā'-śabde---viśvāsa kahe sudṛḍha niścaya
> kṛṣṇe bhakti kaile sarva-karma kṛta haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //śraddhā//; [[synonyms:v:viśvāsa]]---faith; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---is said; [[synonyms:s:sudṛḍha]]---firm; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---certain; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---by executing; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:karma]]---all activities; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]---completed; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are.
translation: "By rendering transcendental loving service to Kṛṣṇa, one automatically performs all subsidiary activities. This confident, firm faith, favorable to the discharge of devotional service, is called śraddhā.
purport: Firm faith and confidence are called //śraddhā.// When one engages in the Lord's devotional service, he is to be understood to have performed all his responsibilities in the material world. He has satisfied his forefathers, ordinary living entities, and demigods and is free from all responsibility. Such a person does not need to meet his responsibilities separately. It is automatically done. Fruitive activity (//karma//) is meant to satisfy the senses of the conditioned soul. However, when one awakens to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, he does not have to work separately for pious activity. The best achievement of all fruitive activity is detachment from material life, and this detachment is spontaneously enjoyed by the devotee firmly engaged in the Lord's service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.63
description: " 'By pouring water on the root of a tree, one automatically satisfies the trunk, branches and twigs. Similarly, by supplying food to the stomach, where it nourishes the life air, one satisfies all the senses. In the same way, by worshiping Kṛṣṇa and rendering Him service, one automatically satisfies all the demigods.'
text:
> yathā taror mūla-niṣecanena
> tṛpyanti tat-skandha-bhujopaśākhāḥ
> prāṇopahārāc ca yathendriyāṇāṁ
> tathaiva sarvārhaṇam acyutejyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:t:taroḥ]]---of a tree; [[synonyms:m:mūla]]---on the root; [[synonyms:n:niṣecanena]]---by pouring water; [[synonyms:t:tṛpyanti]]---are satisfied; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---of the tree; [[synonyms:s:skandha]]---trunk; [[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---branches; [[synonyms:u:upaśākhāḥ]]---sub-branches; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]---to the living force; [[synonyms:u:upahārāt]]---from offering food; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:i:indriyāṇām]]---of all the senses; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---similarly; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---indeed; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---of all; [[synonyms:a:arhaṇam]]---worship; [[synonyms:a:acyuta]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:i:ijyā]]---worship.
translation: “ 'By pouring water on the root of a tree, one automatically satisfies the trunk, branches and twigs. Similarly, by supplying food to the stomach, where it nourishes the life air, one satisfies all the senses. In the same way, by worshiping Kṛṣṇa and rendering Him service, one automatically satisfies all the demigods.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:4:31:14|(4.31.14)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.64
description: "A faithful devotee is a truly eligible candidate for the loving service of the Lord. According to one's faith, one is classified as a topmost devotee, an intermediate devotee or an inferior devotee.
text:
> śraddhāvān jana haya bhakti-adhikārī
> 'uttama', 'madhyama', 'kaniṣṭha'---śraddhā-anusārī
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śraddhāvān]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---a person with faith; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:a:adhikārī]]---eligible for discharging transcendental loving service to the Lord; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]---first class; [[synonyms:m:madhyama]]---intermediate; [[synonyms:k:kaniṣṭha]]---the lowest class; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]]-[[synonyms:a:anusārī]]---according to the proportion of faith.
translation: "A faithful devotee is a truly eligible candidate for the loving service of the Lord. According to one's faith, one is classified as a topmost devotee, an intermediate devotee or an inferior devotee.
purport: The word //śraddhāvān// (faithful) means understanding Kṛṣṇa to be the //summum bonum,// the eternal truth and absolute transcendence. If one has full faith in Kṛṣṇa and confidence in Him, one becomes eligible to discharge devotional service confidentially. According to one's faith, one is a topmost, intermediate or inferior devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.65
description: "One who is expert in logic, argument and the revealed scriptures and who has firm faith in Kṛṣṇa is classified as a topmost devotee. He can deliver the whole world.
text:
> śāstra-yuktye sunipuṇa, dṛḍha-śraddhā yāṅra
> 'uttama-adhikārī' sei tāraye saṁsāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:y:yuktye]]---in argument and logic; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:n:nipuṇa]]---very expert; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]]-[[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]]---firm faith and confidence in Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]-[[synonyms:a:adhikārī]]---the topmost devotee; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---he; [[synonyms:t:tāraye]] [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]---can deliver the whole world.
translation: "One who is expert in logic, argument and the revealed scriptures and who has firm faith in Kṛṣṇa is classified as a topmost devotee. He can deliver the whole world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.66
description: " 'One who is expert in logic and understanding of revealed scriptures, and who always has firm conviction and deep faith that is not blind, is to be considered a topmost devotee in devotional service.'
text:
> śāstre yuktau ca nipuṇaḥ
> sarvathā dṛḍha-niścayaḥ
> prauḍha-śraddho 'dhikārī yaḥ
> sa bhaktāv uttamo mataḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śāstre]]---in the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:y:yuktau]]---in logic; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:n:nipuṇaḥ]]---expert; [[synonyms:s:sarvathā]]---in all respects; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]]-[[synonyms:n:niścayaḥ]]---who is firmly convinced; [[synonyms:p:prauḍha]]---deep; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhaḥ]]---who has faith; [[synonyms:a:adhikārī]]---eligible; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---he; [[synonyms:b:bhaktau]]---in devotional service; [[synonyms:u:uttamaḥ]]---highest; [[synonyms:m:mataḥ]]---is considered.
translation: “ 'One who is expert in logic and understanding of revealed scriptures, and who always has firm conviction and deep faith that is not blind, is to be considered a topmost devotee in devotional service.'
purport: This verse appears in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.17) by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.67
description: "One who is not very expert in argument and logic based on revealed scriptures but who has firm faith is considered a second-class devotee. He also must be considered most fortunate.
text:
> śāstra-yukti nāhi jāne dṛḍha, śraddhāvān
> 'madhyama-adhikārī' sei mahā-bhāgyavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:y:yukti]]---logical arguments on the basis of revealed scripture; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---knows; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]]---firmly; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhāvān]]---faithful; [[synonyms:m:madhyama]]-[[synonyms:a:adhikārī]]---second-class devotee; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---he; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgyavān]]---very fortunate.
translation: "One who is not very expert in argument and logic based on revealed scriptures but who has firm faith is considered a second-class devotee. He also must be considered most fortunate.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.68
description: " 'He who does not know scriptural argument very well but who has firm faith is called an intermediate or second-class devotee.'
text:
> yaḥ śāstrādiṣv anipuṇaḥ
> śraddhāvān sa tu madhyamaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādiṣu]]---in the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:a:anipuṇaḥ]]---not very expert; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhāvān]]---full of faith; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---he; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---certainly; [[synonyms:m:madhyamaḥ]]---second-class or middle-class devotee.
translation: “ 'He who does not know scriptural argument very well but who has firm faith is called an intermediate or second-class devotee.'
purport: This verse appears in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.18).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.69
description: "One whose faith is soft and pliable is called a neophyte, but by gradually following the process, he will rise to the platform of a first-class devotee.
text:
> yāhāra komala śraddhā, se 'kaniṣṭha' jana
> krame krame teṅho bhakta ha-ibe 'uttama'
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāhāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:k:komala]] [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]]---soft faith; [[synonyms:s:se]]---such a person; [[synonyms:k:kaniṣṭha]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---a neophyte devotee; [[synonyms:k:krame]] [[synonyms:k:krame]]---by a gradual progression; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotee; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ibe]]---will become; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]---first class.
translation: "One whose faith is soft and pliable is called a neophyte, but by gradually following the process, he will rise to the platform of a first-class devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.7
description: "Kṛṣṇa is the nondual Absolute Truth, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although He is one, He maintains different personal expansions and energies for His pastimes.
text:
> advaya-jñāna-tattva kṛṣṇa---svayaṁ bhagavān
> 'svarūpa-śakti' rūpe tāṅra haya avasthāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaya]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---of nondual knowledge; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]---the principle; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:svayam]] [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---Himself the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---personal expansions; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---of potencies; [[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in the form; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:a:avasthāna]]---existence.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa is the nondual Absolute Truth, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although He is one, He maintains different personal expansions and energies for His pastimes.
purport: The Lord has many potencies, and He is nondifferent from all these potencies. Because the potencies and the potent cannot be separated, they are identical. Kṛṣṇa is described as the source of all potencies, and He is also identified with the external potency, the material energy. Kṛṣṇa also has internal potencies, or spiritual potencies, which are always engaged in His personal service. His internal potency is different from His external potency. Kṛṣṇa's internal potency and Kṛṣṇa Himself, who is the potent, are always identical.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.70
description: " 'One whose faith is not very strong, who is just beginning, should be considered a neophyte devotee.'
text:
> yo bhavet komala-śraddhaḥ
> sa kaniṣṭho nigadyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:b:bhavet]]---may be; [[synonyms:k:komala]]---soft; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhaḥ]]---having faith; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---such a person; [[synonyms:k:kaniṣṭhaḥ]]---neophyte devotee; [[synonyms:n:nigadyate]]---is said to be.
translation: “ 'One whose faith is not very strong, who is just beginning, should be considered a neophyte devotee.'
purport: This verse also appears in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.19).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.71
description: "A devotee is considered superlative and superior according to his attachment and love. In the Eleventh Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, the following symptoms have been ascertained.
text:
> rati-prema-tāratamye bhakta---tara-tama
> ekādaśa skandhe tāra kariyāche lakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rati]]---of attachment; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---and love; [[synonyms:t:tāratamye]]---by comparison; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotee; [[synonyms:t:tara]]-[[synonyms:t:tama]]---superior and superlative; [[synonyms:e:ekādaśa]] [[synonyms:s:skandhe]]---in the Eleventh Canto of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of him; [[synonyms:k:kariyāche]]---has made; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---symptoms.
translation: "A devotee is considered superlative and superior according to his attachment and love. In the Eleventh Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, the following symptoms have been ascertained.
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has stated that if one has developed faith in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, he is to be considered an eligible candidate for further advancement in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Those who have faith are divided into three categories-//uttama, madhyama// and //kaniṣṭha// (first-class, second-class and neophyte). A first-class devotee has firm conviction in the revealed scriptures and is expert in arguing according to the //śāstras.// He is firmly convinced of the science of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. The //madhyama-adhikārī,// or second-class devotee, has firm conviction in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, but he cannot support his conviction by citing śāstric references. The neophyte devotee does not yet have firm faith. In this way the devotees are typed.

The standard of devotion is also categorized in the same way. A neophyte believes that only love of Kṛṣṇa or Kṛṣṇa consciousness is very good, but he may not know the basis of pure Kṛṣṇa consciousness or how one can become a perfect devotee. Sometimes in the heart of a neophyte there is attraction for //karma, jñāna// or //yoga.// When he is free and transcendental to mixed devotional activity, he becomes a second-class devotee. When he becomes expert in logic and can refer to the //śāstras,// he becomes a first-class devotee. The devotees are also described as positive, comparative and superlative, in terms of their love and attachment for Kṛṣṇa.

It should be understood that a //madhyama-adhikārī,// a second-class devotee, is fully convinced of Kṛṣṇa consciousness but cannot support his convictions with śāstric reference. A neophyte may fall down by associating with nondevotees because he is not firmly convinced and strongly situated. The second-class devotee, even though he cannot support his position with śāstric reference, can gradually become a first-class devotee by studying the //śāstras// and associating with a first-class devotee. However, if the second-class devotee does not advance himself by associating with a first-class devotee, he makes no progress. There is no possibility that a first-class devotee will fall down, even though he may mix with nondevotees to preach. Conviction and faith gradually increase to make one an //uttama-adhikārī,// a first-class devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.72
description: " 'A person advanced in devotional service sees within everything the soul of souls, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Consequently he always sees the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead as the cause of all causes and understands that all things are situated in Him.
text:
> sarva-bhūteṣu yaḥ paśyed
> bhagavad-bhāvam ātmanaḥ
> bhūtāni bhagavaty ātmany
> eṣa bhāgavatottamaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūteṣu]]---in all objects (in matter, spirit, and combinations of matter and spirit); [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:p:paśyet]]---sees; [[synonyms:b:bhagavat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvam]]---the ability to be engaged in the service of the Lord; [[synonyms:ā:ātmanaḥ]]---of the supreme spirit soul or the transcendence beyond the material conception of life; [[synonyms:b:bhūtāni]]---all beings; [[synonyms:b:bhagavati]]---in the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ā:ātmani]]---the basic principle of all existence; [[synonyms:e:eṣaḥ]]---this; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]-[[synonyms:u:uttamaḥ]]---a person advanced in devotional service.
translation: “ 'A person advanced in devotional service sees within everything the soul of souls, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Consequently he always sees the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead as the cause of all causes and understands that all things are situated in Him.
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.2.45).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.73
description: " 'An intermediate, second-class devotee shows love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is friendly to all devotees and is very merciful to neophytes and ignorant people. The intermediate devotee neglects those who are envious of devotional service.
text:
> īśvare tad-adhīneṣu
> bāliśeṣu dviṣatsu ca
> prema-maitrī-kṛpopekṣā
> yaḥ karoti sa madhyamaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ī:īśvare]]---unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:a:adhīneṣu]]---to persons who have taken fully to Kṛṣṇa consciousness; [[synonyms:b:bāliśeṣu]]---unto the neophytes or the ignorant; [[synonyms:d:dviṣatsu]]---to persons envious of Kṛṣṇa and the devotees of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love; [[synonyms:m:maitrī]]---friendship; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:u:upekṣā]]---negligence; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:k:karoti]]---does; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---he; [[synonyms:m:madhyamaḥ]]---a second-class devotee.
translation: “ 'An intermediate, second-class devotee shows love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is friendly to all devotees and is very merciful to neophytes and ignorant people. The intermediate devotee neglects those who are envious of devotional service.
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.2.46). This statement was made by the great sage Nārada while he was speaking to Vasudeva about devotional service. This subject was originally discussed between Nimi, the King of Videha, and the nine Yogendras.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.74
description: " 'A prākṛta, or materialistic devotee does not purposefully study the śāstra and try to understand the actual standard of pure devotional service. Consequently he does not show proper respect to advanced devotees. He may, however, follow the regulative principles learned from his spiritual master or from his family who worships the Deity. He is to be considered on the material platform, although he is trying to advance in devotional service. Such a person is a bhakta-prāya [neophyte devotee], or bhaktābhāsa, for he is a little enlightened by Vaiṣṇava philosophy.'
text:
> arcāyām eva haraye
> pūjāṁ yaḥ śraddhayehate
> na tad-bhakteṣu cānyeṣu
> sa bhaktaḥ prākṛtaḥ smṛtaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:arcāyām]]---in the temple worship; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:h:haraye]]---for the pleasure of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:p:pūjām]]---worship; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhayā]]---with faith and love; [[synonyms:ī:īhate]]---executes; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakteṣu]]---to the devotees of the Lord; [[synonyms:c:ca]] [[synonyms:a:anyeṣu]]---and to others; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---he; [[synonyms:b:bhaktaḥ]]---a devotee; [[synonyms:p:prākṛtaḥ]]---materialistic; [[synonyms:s:smṛtaḥ]]---is considered.
translation: “ 'A prākṛta, or materialistic devotee does not purposefully study the śāstra and try to understand the actual standard of pure devotional service. Consequently he does not show proper respect to advanced devotees. He may, however, follow the regulative principles learned from his spiritual master or from his family who worships the Deity. He is to be considered on the material platform, although he is trying to advance in devotional service. Such a person is a bhakta-prāya [neophyte devotee], or bhaktābhāsa, for he is a little enlightened by Vaiṣṇava philosophy.'
purport: This verse is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.2.47). Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that one who has full love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead and who maintains a good friendship with the Lord's devotees is always callous to those who envy Kṛṣṇa and Kṛṣṇa's devotees. Such a person is to be considered an intermediate devotee. He becomes a first-class devotee when, in the course of advancing in devotional service, he feels an intimate relationship with all living entities, seeing them as part and parcel of the Supreme Person.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.75
description: "A Vaiṣṇava is one who has developed all good transcendental qualities. All the good qualities of Kṛṣṇa gradually develop in Kṛṣṇa's devotee.
text:
> sarva mahā-guṇa-gaṇa vaiṣṇava-śarīre
> kṛṣṇa-bhakte kṛṣṇera guṇa sakali sañcāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]---great; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:ś:śarīre]]---in the bodies of Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---in the devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---the qualities; [[synonyms:s:sakali]]---all; [[synonyms:s:sañcāre]]---appear.
translation: "A Vaiṣṇava is one who has developed all good transcendental qualities. All the good qualities of Kṛṣṇa gradually develop in Kṛṣṇa's devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.76
description: " 'In one who has unflinching devotional faith in Kṛṣṇa, all the good qualities of Kṛṣṇa and the demigods are consistently manifest. However, he who has no devotion to the Supreme Personality of Godhead has no good qualifications because he is engaged by mental concoction in material existence, which is the external feature of the Lord.'
text:
> yasyāsti bhaktir bhagavaty akiñcanā
> sarvair guṇais tatra samāsate surāḥ
> harāv abhaktasya kuto mahad-guṇā
> mano-rathenāsati dhāvato bahiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:a:asti]]---there is; [[synonyms:b:bhaktiḥ]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:b:bhagavati]]---unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:akiñcanā]]---without material desires; [[synonyms:s:sarvaiḥ]]---all; [[synonyms:g:guṇaiḥ]]---with good qualities; [[synonyms:t:tatra]]---there; [[synonyms:s:samāsate]]---live; [[synonyms:s:surāḥ]]---the demigods; [[synonyms:h:harau]]---unto the Lord; [[synonyms:a:abhaktasya]]---of the nondevotee; [[synonyms:k:kutaḥ]]---where; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇāḥ]]---the high qualities; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:r:rathena]]---by mental concoction; [[synonyms:a:asati]]---to temporary material happiness; [[synonyms:d:dhāvataḥ]]---running; [[synonyms:b:bahiḥ]]---externally.
translation: “ 'In one who has unflinching devotional faith in Kṛṣṇa, all the good qualities of Kṛṣṇa and the demigods are consistently manifest. However, he who has no devotion to the Supreme Personality of Godhead has no good qualifications because he is engaged by mental concoction in material existence, which is the external feature of the Lord.'
purport: This was spoken by Bhadraśravā and his followers, who were offering prayers to Nṛsiṁhadeva [[books:sb:5:18:12|(Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 5.18.12)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.77
description: "All these transcendental qualities are the characteristics of pure Vaiṣṇavas, and they cannot be fully explained, but I shall try to point out some of the important qualities.
text:
> sei saba guṇa haya vaiṣṇava-lakṣaṇa
> saba kahā nā yāya, kari dig-daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---all those transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the symptoms of a Vaiṣṇava; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kahā]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---cannot be explained; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I shall do; [[synonyms:d:dik]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---a general review.
translation: "All these transcendental qualities are the characteristics of pure Vaiṣṇavas, and they cannot be fully explained, but I shall try to point out some of the important qualities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 22.78-80
description: "Devotees are always merciful, humble, truthful, equal to all, faultless, magnanimous, mild and clean. They are without material possessions, and they perform welfare work for everyone. They are peaceful, surrendered to Kṛṣṇa and desireless. They are indifferent to material acquisitions and are fixed in devotional service. They completely control the six bad qualities-lust, anger, greed and so forth. They eat only as much as required, and they are not inebriated. They are respectful, grave, compassionate and without false prestige. They are friendly, poetic, expert and silent.
text:
> kṛpālu, akṛta-droha, satya-sāra sama
> nidoṣa, vadānya, mṛdu, śuci, akiñcana
>
> sarvopakāraka, śānta, kṛṣṇaika-śaraṇa
> akāma, anīha, sthira, vijita-ṣaḍ-guṇa
>
> mita-bhuk, apramatta, mānada, amānī
> gambhīra, karuṇa, maitra, kavi, dakṣa, maunī
