title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.21
description: " 'O brāhmaṇas, just accept me as a completely surrendered soul, and let mother Ganges, the representative of the Lord, also accept me in that way, for I have already taken the lotus feet of the Lord into my heart. Let the snakebird-or whatever magical thing the brāhmaṇa created-bite me at once. I only desire that you all continue singing the deeds of Lord Viṣṇu.'
text:
> taṁ mopayātaṁ pratiyantu viprā
> gaṅgā ca devī dhṛta-cittam īśe
> dvijopasṛṣṭaḥ kuhakas takṣako vā
> daśatv alaṁ gāyata viṣṇu-gāthāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tam]]---him; [[synonyms:m:mā]]---me; [[synonyms:u:upayātam]]---surrendered; [[synonyms:p:pratiyantu]]---you may know; [[synonyms:v:viprāḥ]]---O //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]---mother Ganges; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:d:devī]]---the demigoddess; [[synonyms:d:dhṛta]]---offered; [[synonyms:c:cittam]]---whose mind; [[synonyms:ī:īśe]]---unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:d:dvija]]-[[synonyms:u:upasṛṣṭaḥ]]---created by the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kuhakaḥ]]---some trickery; [[synonyms:t:takṣakaḥ]]---snake-bird; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:d:daśatu]]---let it bite; [[synonyms:a:alam]]---never mind; [[synonyms:g:gāyata]]---chant; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:g:gāthāḥ]]---the holy names of Lord Viṣṇu.'
translation: “ 'O brāhmaṇas, just accept me as a completely surrendered soul, and let mother Ganges, the representative of the Lord, also accept me in that way, for I have already taken the lotus feet of the Lord into my heart. Let the snakebird-or whatever magical thing the brāhmaṇa created-bite me at once. I only desire that you all continue singing the deeds of Lord Viṣṇu.'
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:19:15|(1.19.15)]] spoken by Mahārāja Parīkṣit while he was sitting on the bank of the Ganges expecting to be bitten by a snakebird summoned by the curse of a //brāhmaṇa// boy named Śṛṅgi, who was the son of a great sage named Śamīka. News of the curse was conveyed to the King, who prepared for his imminent death. Many great saintly persons, sages, //brāhmaṇas,// kings and demigods came to see him in his last days. Mahārāja Parīkṣit, however, was not at all afraid of being bitten by the snake-bird. Indeed, he requested all the great personalities assembled to continue chanting the holy name of Lord Viṣṇu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.22
description: "Not a moment should be lost. Every moment should be utilized for Kṛṣṇa or connected with Him.
text: > kṛṣṇa-sambandha vinā kāla vyartha nāhi yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sambandha]] [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without a connection with Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]---time; [[synonyms:v:vyartha]]---useless; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---does not become.
translation:
"Not a moment should be lost. Every moment should be utilized for Kṛṣṇa or connected with Him.


PUPORT

Mahārāja Parīkṣit's expression of anxiety is explained in this verse. He says, "Let whatever is destined to happen take place. It doesn't matter. Just let me see that not a moment of my time is wasted without a relationship with Kṛṣṇa." One has to tolerate all obstacles on the path of Kṛṣṇa consciousness, and one has to see that not a moment of his life is wasted outside of Kṛṣṇa's service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.23

Despite all these activities, they are still not satisfied. This is the nature of pure devotees. Shedding tears from their eyes, they dedicate their whole lives to the Lord's service.'

text: > bhukti, siddhi, indriyārtha tāre nāhi bhāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhukti]]---material enjoyment; [[synonyms:s:siddhi]]---mystic power; [[synonyms:i:indriya]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---the objects of the senses; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:b:bhāya]]---do not appeal.
translation: "In the material field, people are interested in material enjoyment, mystic power and sense gratification. However, these things do not appeal to the devotee at all.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.25
description: " 'King Bharata was very eager to attain the association of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, who is called uttama-śloka because poems and prayers are offered to Him for His favor. In his youth, King Bharata gave up his attractive wife and children, as well as his beloved friends and opulent kingdom, just as one gives up stool after passing it.'
text:
> yo dustyajān dāra-sutān
> suḥrd-rājyaṁ hṛdi spṛśaḥ
> jahau yuvaiva malavad
> uttamaḥśloka-lālasaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who (Bharata Mahārāja); [[synonyms:d:dustyajān]]---difficult to give up; [[synonyms:d:dāra]]-[[synonyms:s:sutān]]---wife and children; [[synonyms:s:suḥrt]]---friends; [[synonyms:r:rājyam]]---kingdom; [[synonyms:h:hṛdi]] [[synonyms:s:spṛśaḥ]]---dear to the core of the heart; [[synonyms:j:jahau]]---gave up; [[synonyms:y:yuvā]]---youthful; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---at that time; [[synonyms:m:malavat]]---like stool; [[synonyms:u:uttamaḥ]]-[[synonyms:ś:śloka]]-[[synonyms:l:lālasaḥ]]---being captivated by the transcendental qualities, pastimes and association of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'King Bharata was very eager to attain the association of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, who is called uttama-śloka because poems and prayers are offered to Him for His favor. In his youth, King Bharata gave up his attractive wife and children, as well as his beloved friends and opulent kingdom, just as one gives up stool after passing it.'
purport: These are the signs of //virakti// (detachment) found in a person who has developed //bhāva,// the preliminary stage of love of Godhead; This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:5:14:43|(5.14.43)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.26
description: "Although a pure devotee's standard is above all, he still considers himself to be in the lowest stage of life.
text: > 'sarvottama' āpanāke 'hīna' kari māne
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:u:uttama]]---although standing above all; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāke]]---himself; [[synonyms:h:hīna]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---as the lowest; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---considers.
translation: "Although a pure devotee's standard is above all, he still considers himself to be in the lowest stage of life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.27
description: " 'Bharata Mahārāja always carried affection for Kṛṣṇa within his heart. Although Bharata Mahārāja was the crown jewel of kings, he was still wandering about and begging alms in the city of his enemies. He was even offering respects to caṇḍālas, low-class men who eat dogs.'
text:
> harau ratiṁ vahann eṣa
> narendrāṇāṁ śikhāmaṇiḥ
> bhikṣām aṭann ari-pure
> śva-pākam api vandate
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:harau]]---toward the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:r:ratim]]---affection; [[synonyms:v:vahan]]---carrying; [[synonyms:e:eṣaḥ]]---this one; [[synonyms:n:nara]]-[[synonyms:i:indrāṇām]]---of all the kings; [[synonyms:ś:śikhā]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇiḥ]]---brilliant crown jewel; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣām]]---begging alms; [[synonyms:a:aṭan]]---wandering for; [[synonyms:a:ari]]-[[synonyms:p:pure]]---even in the city of enemies; [[synonyms:ś:śva]]-[[synonyms:p:pākam]]---the fifth-grade //caṇḍālas//; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:v:vandate]]---worships.
translation: “ 'Bharata Mahārāja always carried affection for Kṛṣṇa within his heart. Although Bharata Mahārāja was the crown jewel of kings, he was still wandering about and begging alms in the city of his enemies. He was even offering respects to caṇḍālas, low-class men who eat dogs.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Padma Purāṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.28
description: "A fully surrendered devotee always hopes that Lord Kṛṣṇa will be kind to him. This hope is very firm in him.
text: > 'kṛṣṇa kṛpā karibena'---dṛḍha kari' jāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:karibena]]---will show His mercy; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making firm; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---he believes.
translation: "A fully surrendered devotee always hopes that Lord Kṛṣṇa will be kind to him. This hope is very firm in him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.29
description: " 'O my Lord, I do not have any love for You, nor am I qualified for discharging devotional service by chanting and hearing. Nor do I possess the mystic power of a Vaiṣṇava, knowledge or pious activities. Nor do I belong to a very high-caste family. On the whole, I do not possess anything. Still, O beloved of the gopīs, because You bestow Your mercy on the most fallen, I have an unbreakable hope that is constantly in my heart. That hope is always giving me pain.'
text:
> na premā śravaṇādi-bhaktir api vā yogo 'thavā vaiṣṇavo
> jñānaṁ vā śubha-karma vā kiyad aho saj-jātir apy asti vā
> hīnārthādhika-sādhake tvayi tathāpy acchedya-mūlā satī
> he gopī-jana-vallabha vyathayate hā hā mad-āśaiva mām
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---consisting of chanting, hearing and so on; [[synonyms:b:bhaktiḥ]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:y:yogaḥ]]---the power of mystic //yoga//; [[synonyms:a:athavā]]---or; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavaḥ]]---befitting a devotee; [[synonyms:j:jñānam]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:ś:śubha]]-[[synonyms:k:karma]]---pious activities; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:k:kiyat]]---a little; [[synonyms:a:aho]]---O my Lord; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:j:jātiḥ]]---birth in a good family; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:a:asti]]---there is; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:h:hīna]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:a:adhika]]-[[synonyms:s:sādhake]]---who bestows greater benedictions upon one who is fallen and possesses no good qualities; [[synonyms:t:tvayi]]---unto You; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:a:acchedya]]-[[synonyms:m:mūlā]]---whose root is uncuttable; [[synonyms:s:satī]]---being; [[synonyms:h:he]]---O; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]-[[synonyms:v:vallabha]]---most dear friend of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:v:vyathayate]]---gives pain; [[synonyms:h:hā]] [[synonyms:h:hā]]---alas; [[synonyms:m:mat]]---my; [[synonyms:ā:āśā]]---hope; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---to me.
translation: “ 'O my Lord, I do not have any love for You, nor am I qualified for discharging devotional service by chanting and hearing. Nor do I possess the mystic power of a Vaiṣṇava, knowledge or pious activities. Nor do I belong to a very high-caste family. On the whole, I do not possess anything. Still, O beloved of the gopīs, because You bestow Your mercy on the most fallen, I have an unbreakable hope that is constantly in my heart. That hope is always giving me pain.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.3.35).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.3
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "Now hear, O Sanātana, about the result of devotional service, which is love of Godhead, life's ultimate goal. If one hears this description, he will be enlightened in the transcendental mellows of devotional service.
text:
> ebe śuna bhakti-phala 'prema'-prayojana
> yāhāra śravaṇe haya bhakti-rasa-jñāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ebe]] [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---now hear; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]---the result of practice of devotional service; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:p:prayojana]]---the ultimate goal of life; [[synonyms:y:yāhāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇe]]---by hearing of which; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---transcendental knowledge of the mellows of devotional service.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "Now hear, O Sanātana, about the result of devotional service, which is love of Godhead, life's ultimate goal. If one hears this description, he will be enlightened in the transcendental mellows of devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.30
description: "This eagerness is chiefly characterized by an ardent desire to associate with the Lord.
text: > samutkaṇṭhā haya sadā lālasā-pradhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:samutkaṇṭhā]]---eagerness; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:l:lālasā]]---ardent desire; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---chiefly characterized by.
translation: "This eagerness is chiefly characterized by an ardent desire to associate with the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.31
description: " 'O Kṛṣṇa, O flute player, the sweetness of Your early age is wonderful within these three worlds. You know My unsteadiness, and I know Yours. No one else knows about this. I want to see Your beautiful, attractive face somewhere in a solitary place, but how can this be accomplished?'
text:
> tvac-chaiśavaṁ tri-bhuvanādbhutam ity avehi
> mac-cāpalaṁ ca tava vā mama vādhigamyam
> tat kiṁ karomi viralaṁ muralī-vilāsi
> mugdhaṁ mukhāmbujam udīkṣitum īkṣaṇābhyām
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tvat]]---Your; [[synonyms:ś:śaiśavam]]---early age; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvana]]---within the three worlds; [[synonyms:a:adbhutam]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:a:avehi]]---know; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:c:cāpalam]]---My unsteadiness; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---of You; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---of Me; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:a:adhigamyam]]---to bu understood; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what; [[synonyms:k:karomi]]---I do; [[synonyms:v:viralam]]---in solitude; [[synonyms:m:muralī]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsi]]---O player of the flute; [[synonyms:m:mugdham]]---attractive; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]-[[synonyms:a:ambujam]]---lotuslike face; [[synonyms:u:udīkṣitum]]---to see sufficiently; [[synonyms:ī:īkṣaṇābhyām]]---by the eyes.
translation: “ 'O Kṛṣṇa, O flute player, the sweetness of Your early age is wonderful within these three worlds. You know My unsteadiness, and I know Yours. No one else knows about this. I want to see Your beautiful, attractive face somewhere in a solitary place, but how can this be accomplished?'
purport: This is a verse from //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta// (32).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.32
description: "Due to having great relish for the holy name, one is inclined to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra constantly.
text: > nāma-gāne sadā ruci, laya kṛṣṇa-nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:g:gāne]]---in chanting the holy names; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---constantly; [[synonyms:r:ruci]]---taste,relish; [[synonyms:l:laya]]---takes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra.//
translation: "Due to having great relish for the holy name, one is inclined to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra constantly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.33
description: " 'O Govinda, this youthful girl named Rādhikā is today constantly pouring forth tears like nectar falling from flowers. She is also singing Your holy name in a sweet voice.'
text:
> rodana-bindu-maranda-syandi-
> dṛg-indīvarādya govinda
> tava madhura-svara-kaṇṭhī
> gāyati nāmāvalīṁ bālā
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rodana]]-[[synonyms:b:bindu]]---with teardrops; [[synonyms:m:maranda]]---like the nectar or juice of flowers; [[synonyms:s:syandi]]---pouring; [[synonyms:d:dṛk]]-[[synonyms:i:indīvarā]]---whose lotus eyes; [[synonyms:ā:ādya]]---today; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---O my Lord Govinda; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]-[[synonyms:s:svara]]-[[synonyms:k:kaṇṭhī]]---who has a very sweet voice; [[synonyms:g:gāyati]]---sings; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:āvalīm]]---holy names; [[synonyms:b:bālā]]---this young girl (Rādhikā).
translation: “ 'O Govinda, this youthful girl named Rādhikā is today constantly pouring forth tears like nectar falling from flowers. She is also singing Your holy name in a sweet voice.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.3.38).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.34
description: "At this stage of bhāva, a devotee has awakened the tendency to chant and describe the transcendental qualities of the Lord. He has attachment for this process.
text: > kṛṣṇa-guṇākhyāne haya sarvadā āsakti
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākhyāne]]---in describing the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sarvadā]]---always; [[synonyms:ā:āsakti]]---attachment.
translation: "At this stage of bhāva, a devotee has awakened the tendency to chant and describe the transcendental qualities of the Lord. He has attachment for this process.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.35
description: " 'O my Lord, the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa is very sweet, and His face is even sweeter than His body. The soft smile on His face, which is like the fragrance of honey, is sweeter still.'
text:
> madhuraṁ madhuraṁ vapur asya vibhor
> madhuraṁ madhuraṁ vadanaṁ madhuram
> madhu-gandhi mṛḍu-smitam etad aho
> madhuraṁ madhuraṁ madhuraṁ madhuram
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhuram]]---sweet; [[synonyms:m:madhuram]]---sweet; [[synonyms:v:vapuḥ]]---the transcendental form; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---His; [[synonyms:v:vibhoḥ]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:m:madhuram]]---sweet; [[synonyms:m:madhuram]]---sweet; [[synonyms:v:vadanam]]---face; [[synonyms:m:madhuram]]---more sweet; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:g:gandhi]]---the fragrance of honey; [[synonyms:m:mṛḍu]]-[[synonyms:s:smitam]]---soft smiling; [[synonyms:e:etat]]---this; [[synonyms:a:aho]]---oh; [[synonyms:m:madhuram]]---sweet; [[synonyms:m:madhuram]]---sweet; [[synonyms:m:madhuram]]---sweet; [[synonyms:m:madhuram]]---still more sweet.
translation: “ 'O my Lord, the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa is very sweet, and His face is even sweeter than His body. The soft smile on His face, which is like the fragrance of honey, is sweeter still.'
purport: This is a verse quoted from Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura's //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta// (92).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.36
description: "A devotee absorbed in ecstatic emotion for Kṛṣṇa always resides in a place where Kṛṣṇa's pastimes were performed.
text: > kṛṣṇa-līlā-sthāne kare sarvadā vasati
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in the place where Kṛṣṇa has His pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---makes; [[synonyms:s:sarvadā]]---always; [[synonyms:v:vasati]]---abode.
translation: "A devotee absorbed in ecstatic emotion for Kṛṣṇa always resides in a place where Kṛṣṇa's pastimes were performed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.37
description: " 'O Lord Puṇḍarīkākṣa, while chanting Your holy name with tears in my eyes, when shall I dance in ecstasy on the bank of the Yamunā?'
text:
> kadāhaṁ yamunā-tīre
> nāmāni tava kīrtayan
> udbāṣpaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣa
> racayiṣyāmi tāṇḍavam
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kadā]]---when; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank of the Yamunā; [[synonyms:n:nāmāni]]---holy names; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:k:kīrtayan]]---chanting; [[synonyms:u:udbāṣpaḥ]]---full of tears; [[synonyms:p:puṇḍarīka]]-[[synonyms:a:akṣa]]---O lotus-eyed one; [[synonyms:r:racayiṣyāmi]]---I shall create; [[synonyms:t:tāṇḍavam]]---dancing like a madman.
translation: “ 'O Lord Puṇḍarīkākṣa, while chanting Your holy name with tears in my eyes, when shall I dance in ecstasy on the bank of the Yamunā?'
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.156).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.38
description: "These are the symptoms of a person who has developed attraction [bhāva] for Kṛṣṇa. Now let me describe the symptoms of a person who is actually elevated to love of Kṛṣṇa. O Sanātana, please hear this from Me.
text:
> kṛṣṇe 'ratira' cihna ei kailuṅ vivaraṇa
> 'kṛṣṇa-premera' cihna ebe śuna sanātana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---for Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:ratira]]---of attraction; [[synonyms:c:cihna]]---the symptoms; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---all these; [[synonyms:k:kailuṅ]] [[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---I have described; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:premera]]---of love for Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:c:cihna]]---the symptoms; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]] [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---please hear, Sanātana.
translation: "These are the symptoms of a person who has developed attraction [bhāva] for Kṛṣṇa. Now let me describe the symptoms of a person who is actually elevated to love of Kṛṣṇa. O Sanātana, please hear this from Me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.39
description: "Even the most learned man cannot understand the words, activities and symptoms of a person situated in love of Godhead.
text:
> yāṅra citte kṛṣṇa-premā karaye udaya
> tāṅra vākya, kriyā, mudrā vijñeha nā bujhaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]] [[synonyms:c:citte]]---in whose heart; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:premā]]---love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:u:udaya]]---awakens; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:v:vākya]]---words; [[synonyms:k:kriyā]]---activities; [[synonyms:m:mudrā]]---symptoms; [[synonyms:v:vijñeha]]---even a learned scholar; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:b:bujhaya]]---does not understand.
translation: "Even the most learned man cannot understand the words, activities and symptoms of a person situated in love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.4
description: "When affection for Kṛṣṇa becomes deeper, one attains love of Godhead in devotional service. Such a position is called sthāyi-bhāva, permanent enjoyment of the mellows of devotional service to Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> kṛṣṇe rati gāḍha haile 'prema'-abhidhāna
> kṛṣṇa-bhakti-rasera ei 'sthāyi-bhāva'-nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rati]]---affection; [[synonyms:g:gāḍha]]---deep; [[synonyms:h:haile]]---when it becomes; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:a:abhidhāna]]---called love of God; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:r:rasera]]---of the mellows of devotional service to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:sthāyi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---called //sthāyi-bhāva.//
translation: "When affection for Kṛṣṇa becomes deeper, one attains love of Godhead in devotional service. Such a position is called sthāyi-bhāva, permanent enjoyment of the mellows of devotional service to Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.40
description: " 'Even a most learned scholar cannot understand the activities and symptoms of an exalted personality in whose heart love of Godhead has awakened.'
text:
> dhanyasyāyaṁ nava-premā
> yasyonmīlati cetasi
> antarvāṇibhir apy asya
> mudrā suṣṭhu sudurgamā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dhanyasya]]---of a most fortunate person; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:n:navaḥ]]---new; [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:u:unmīlati]]---manifests; [[synonyms:c:cetasi]]---in the heart; [[synonyms:a:antarvāṇibhiḥ]]---by persons well versed in //śāstras//; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of him; [[synonyms:m:mudrā]]---symptoms; [[synonyms:s:suṣṭhu]]---exceedingly; [[synonyms:s:sudurgamā]]---difficult to understand.
translation: “ 'Even a most learned scholar cannot understand the activities and symptoms of an exalted personality in whose heart love of Godhead has awakened.'
purport: This verse is also found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.4.17).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.41
description: " 'When a person is actually advanced and takes pleasure in chanting the holy name of the Lord, who is very dear to him, he is agitated and loudly chants the holy name. He also laughs, cries, becomes agitated and chants just like a madman, not caring for outsiders.'
text:
> evaṁvrataḥ sva-priya-nāma-kīrtyā
> jātānurāgo druta-citta uccaiḥ
> hasaty atho roditi rauti gāyaty
> unmādavan nṛtyati loka-bāhyaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:evam]]-[[synonyms:v:vrataḥ]]---when one thus engages in a vow to chant and dance; [[synonyms:s:sva]]---own; [[synonyms:p:priya]]---very dear; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name; [[synonyms:k:kīrtyā]]---by chanting; [[synonyms:j:jāta]]---in this way develops; [[synonyms:a:anurāgaḥ]]---attachment; [[synonyms:d:druta]]-[[synonyms:c:cittaḥ]]---very eagerly; [[synonyms:u:uccaiḥ]]---loudly; [[synonyms:h:hasati]]---laughs; [[synonyms:a:atho]]---also; [[synonyms:r:roditi]]---cries; [[synonyms:r:rauti]]---becomes agitated; [[synonyms:g:gāyati]]---chants; [[synonyms:u:unmāda]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---like a madman; [[synonyms:n:nṛtyati]]---dances; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhyaḥ]]---not caring for outsiders.
translation: “ 'When a person is actually advanced and takes pleasure in chanting the holy name of the Lord, who is very dear to him, he is agitated and loudly chants the holy name. He also laughs, cries, becomes agitated and chants just like a madman, not caring for outsiders.'
purport: This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.2.40).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.42
description: "Love of Godhead increases and is manifest as affection, counter-love, love, attachment, subattachment, ecstasy and sublime ecstasy.
text:
> premā krame bāḍi' haya---sneha, māna, praṇaya
> rāga, anurāga, bhāva, mahābhāva haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love of God; [[synonyms:k:krame]]---gradually; [[synonyms:b:bāḍi']]---increasing; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:s:sneha]]---affection; [[synonyms:m:māna]]---indignation due to affection; [[synonyms:p:praṇaya]]---love; [[synonyms:r:rāga]]---attachment; [[synonyms:a:anurāga]]---subattachment; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---ecstasy; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---exalted ecstasy; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is.
translation: "Love of Godhead increases and is manifest as affection, counter-love, love, attachment, subattachment, ecstasy and sublime ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.43
description: "This development is compared to sugarcane seeds, sugarcane plants, sugarcane juice, molasses, crude sugar, refined sugar, sugar candy and rock candy.
text:
> bīja, ikṣu, rasa, guḍa tabe khaṇḍa-sāra
> śarkarā, sitā-michari, śuddha-michari āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bīja]]---seeds; [[synonyms:i:ikṣu]]---sugarcane plants; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---juice; [[synonyms:g:guḍa]]---molasses; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---crude sugar; [[synonyms:ś:śarkarā]]---sugar; [[synonyms:s:sitā]]-[[synonyms:m:michari]]---sugar candy; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:m:michari]]---rock candy; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also.
translation: "This development is compared to sugarcane seeds, sugarcane plants, sugarcane juice, molasses, crude sugar, refined sugar, sugar candy and rock candy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.44
description: "Just as the taste of sugar increases as it is gradually purified, one should understand that when love of Godhead increases from rati, which is compared to the beginning seed, its taste increases.
text:
> ihā yaiche krame nirmala, krame bāḍe svāda
> rati-premādira taiche bāḍaye āsvāda
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---like; [[synonyms:k:krame]]---by succession; [[synonyms:n:nirmala]]---pure; [[synonyms:k:krame]]---gradually; [[synonyms:b:bāḍe]]---increases; [[synonyms:s:svāda]]---taste; [[synonyms:r:rati]]---from attachment; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādira]]---of love of Godhead and so on; [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:b:bāḍaye]]---increases; [[synonyms:ā:āsvāda]]---taste.
translation: "Just as the taste of sugar increases as it is gradually purified, one should understand that when love of Godhead increases from rati, which is compared to the beginning seed, its taste increases.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.45
description: "According to the candidate possessing these transcendental qualities [sneha, māna and so on], there are five transcendental mellows-neutrality, servitorship, friendship, parental love and conjugal love.
text:
> adhikāri-bhede rati---pañca parakāra
> śānta, dāsya, sakhya, vātsalya, madhura āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:adhikāri]]---of possessor; [[synonyms:b:bhede]]---according to differences; [[synonyms:r:rati]]---attachment; [[synonyms:p:pañca]] [[synonyms:p:parakāra]]---five varieties; [[synonyms:ś:śānta]]---neutral; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]---servitude; [[synonyms:s:sakhya]]---friendship; [[synonyms:v:vātsalya]]---paternal love; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---conjugal love; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also.
translation:
"According to the candidate possessing these transcendental qualities [sneha, māna and so on], there are five transcendental mellows-neutrality, servitorship, friendship, parental love and conjugal love.


In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, rati// (attraction) is thus described:

> vyaktaṁ masṛṇitevāntar-
> lakṣyate rati-lakṣaṇam
> mumukṣu-prabhṛtīnaṁ ced
> bhaved eṣā ratir na hi
>
> kintu bāla-camatkāra-
> kārī tac-cihna-vīkṣayā
> abhijñena subodho 'yaṁ
> raty-ābhāsaḥ prakīrtitaḥ

The real symptoms of the fructification of the seed of love (//rati//) are manifest because the heart is melted. When such symptoms are found among speculators and fruitive actors, they cannot be accepted as real symptoms of attachment. Foolish people without knowledge of devotional service praise such symptoms of attachment even when they are based on something other than a desire to serve Kṛṣṇa. However, one who is expert in devotional service calls such symptoms //rati-ābhāsa,// a mere glimpse of attachment.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.46
description: "These five transcendental mellows exist permanently. The devotee may be attracted to one of these mellows, and thus he becomes happy. Kṛṣṇa also becomes inclined toward such a devotee and comes under his control.
text:
> ei pañca sthāyī bhāva haya pañca 'rasa'
> ye-rase bhakta 'sukhī', kṛṣṇa haya 'vaśa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:p:pañca]]---these five kinds of transcendental mellow; [[synonyms:s:sthāyī]] [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---permanent ecstatic moods; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---become; [[synonyms:p:pañca]] [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---five kinds of transcendental mellow; [[synonyms:y:ye]]-[[synonyms:r:rase]]---in a particular mellow; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]] [[synonyms:s:sukhī]]---a devotee becomes happy; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---under the control.
translation: "These five transcendental mellows exist permanently. The devotee may be attracted to one of these mellows, and thus he becomes happy. Kṛṣṇa also becomes inclined toward such a devotee and comes under his control.
purport:
In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, sthāyi-bhāva,// permanent ecstasy, is thus described:

> aviruddhān viruddhāṁś ca
> bhāvān yo vaśatāṁ nayan
> su-rājeva virājeta
> sa sthāyī bhāva ucyate
> sthāyī bhāvo 'tra sa proktaḥ
> śrī-kṛṣṇa-viṣayā ratiḥ

These moods (//bhāvas//) bring under control the favorable ecstasies (such as laughing) and unfavorable ecstasies (such as anger). When these continue to remain as kings, they are called //sthāyi-bhāva,// or permanent ecstasies. Continuous ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa is called permanent ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.47
description: "When the permanent ecstasies [neutrality, servitorship and so on] are mixed with other ingredients, devotional service in love of Godhead is transformed and becomes composed of transcendental mellows.
text:
> premādika sthāyi-bhāva sāmagrī-milane
> kṛṣṇa-bhakti rasa-rūpe pāya pariṇāme
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādika]]---love of Godhead, beginning with //śānta, dāsya// and so on; [[synonyms:s:sthāyi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the permanent ecstasies; [[synonyms:s:sāmagrī]]-[[synonyms:m:milane]]---by mixing with other ingredients; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---composed of transcendental mellows; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:p:pariṇāme]]---by transformation.
translation: "When the permanent ecstasies [neutrality, servitorship and so on] are mixed with other ingredients, devotional service in love of Godhead is transformed and becomes composed of transcendental mellows.
purport:
In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu,// the following definition is given:

> athāsyāḥ keśava-rater
> lakṣitāyā nigadyate
> sāmagrī-paripoṣena
> paramā rasa-rūpatā
>
> vibhāvair anubhāvaiś ca
> sāttvikair vyabhicāribhiḥ
> svādyatvaṁ hṛdi bhaktānām
> ānītā śravaṇādibhiḥ
> eṣā kṛṣṇa-ratiḥ sthāyī
> bhāvo bhakti-raso bhavet

Love for Kṛṣṇa, Keśava, as previously described, reaches the supreme state of being composed of mellows when its ingredients are fulfilled. By means of //vibhāva, anubhāva, sāttvika// and //vyabhicārī,// hearing and chanting are activated, and the devotee is able to taste love for Kṛṣṇa. Then attachment for Kṛṣṇa, or permanent ecstasy (//sthāyi-bhāva//), becomes the mellow of devotional service (//bhakti-rasa//).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.48
description: "The permanent ecstasy becomes a more and more tasteful transcendental mellow through the mixture of special ecstasy, subordinate ecstasy, natural ecstasy and transitory ecstasy.
text:
> vibhāva, anubhāva, sāttvika, vyabhicārī
> sthāyi-bhāva 'rasa' haya ei cāri mili'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vibhāva]]---special ecstasy; [[synonyms:a:anubhāva]]---subordinate ecstasy; [[synonyms:s:sāttvika]]---natural ecstasy; [[synonyms:v:vyabhicārī]]---transitory ecstasy; [[synonyms:s:sthāyi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---permanent ecstasy; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---mellow; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---these four; [[synonyms:m:mili']]---meeting.
translation: "The permanent ecstasy becomes a more and more tasteful transcendental mellow through the mixture of special ecstasy, subordinate ecstasy, natural ecstasy and transitory ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.49
description: "Yogurt mixed with sugar candy, black pepper and camphor is very palatable and tasty. Similarly, when permanent ecstasy mixes with other ecstatic symptoms, it becomes unprecedentedly tasty.
text:
> dadhi yena khaṇḍa-marica-karpūra-milane
> 'rasālākhya' rasa haya apūrvāsvādane
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dadhi]]---yogurt; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]]---sugar candy; [[synonyms:m:marica]]---black pepper; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]---camphor; [[synonyms:m:milane]]---being mixed; [[synonyms:r:rasāla]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākhya]]---known os delicious; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---mellow; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:a:apūrva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsvādane]]---by an unprecedented taste.
translation: "Yogurt mixed with sugar candy, black pepper and camphor is very palatable and tasty. Similarly, when permanent ecstasy mixes with other ecstatic symptoms, it becomes unprecedentedly tasty.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.5
description: " 'When devotional service is situated on the transcendental platform of pure goodness, it is like a ray of the sunlight of love for Kṛṣṇa. At such a time, devotional service causes the heart to be softened by various tastes, and it is called bhāva [emotion].'
text:
> śuddha-sattva-viśeṣātmā
> prema-sūryāṁśu-sāmya-bhāk
> rucibhiś citta-masṛṇya-
> kṛd asau bhāva ucyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:s:sattva]]---by unadultered goodness; [[synonyms:v:viśeṣa]]---distinguished; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---whose nature; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---of love of God; [[synonyms:s:sūrya]]---like the sun; [[synonyms:a:aṁśu]]---a ray; [[synonyms:s:sāmya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāk]]---which is similar to; [[synonyms:r:rucibhiḥ]]---by different tastes; [[synonyms:c:citta]]---of the heart; [[synonyms:m:masṛṇya]]---softness; [[synonyms:k:kṛt]]---which causes; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---that softness; [[synonyms:b:bhāvaḥ]]---emotion; [[synonyms:u:ucyate]]---is called.
translation: “ 'When devotional service is situated on the transcendental platform of pure goodness, it is like a ray of the sunlight of love for Kṛṣṇa. At such a time, devotional service causes the heart to be softened by various tastes, and it is called bhāva [emotion].'
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.3.1).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.50
description: "There are two kinds of particular ecstasies [vibhāva]. One is called the support, and the other is called the awakening. The vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute is an example of the awakening, and Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself is an example of the support.
text:
> dvividha 'vibhāva',---ālambana, uddīpana
> vaṁśī-svarādi---'uddīpana', kṛṣṇādi---'ālambana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]]---two kinds; [[synonyms:v:vibhāva]]---particular ecstasy; [[synonyms:ā:ālambana]]---the support; [[synonyms:u:uddīpana]]---awakening; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:s:svara]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---such as the vibration of the flute; [[synonyms:u:uddīpana]]---exciting; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---Kṛṣṇa and others; [[synonyms:ā:ālambana]]---the support.
translation: "There are two kinds of particular ecstasies [vibhāva]. One is called the support, and the other is called the awakening. The vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute is an example of the awakening, and Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself is an example of the support.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.51
description: "The subordinate ecstasies are smiling, dancing and singing, as well as different manifestations in the body. The natural ecstasies, such as being stunned, are considered among the subordinate ecstasies [anubhāva].
text:
> 'anubhāva'---smita, nṛtya, gītādi udbhāsvara
> stambhādi---'sāttvika' anubhāvera bhitara
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anubhāva]]---subordinate ecstasy; [[synonyms:s:smita]]---smiling; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:g:gīta]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---songs and so on; [[synonyms:u:udbhāsvara]]---symptoms of bodily manifestation; [[synonyms:s:stambha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---being stunned and others; [[synonyms:s:sāttvika]]---natural; [[synonyms:a:anubhāvera]] [[synonyms:b:bhitara]]---within the category of subordinate ecstasies.
translation: "The subordinate ecstasies are smiling, dancing and singing, as well as different manifestations in the body. The natural ecstasies, such as being stunned, are considered among the subordinate ecstasies [anubhāva].
purport:
In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, vibhāva// is described as follows:

> tatra jñeyā vibhāvās tu
> raty-āsvādana-hetavaḥ
> te dvidhālambanā eke
> tathaivoddīpanāḥ pare

"The cause bringing about the tasting of love for Kṛṣṇa is called //vibhāva. Vibhāva// is divided into two categories---//ālambana// (support) and //uddīpana// (awakening)."

In the //Agni Purāṇa// it is stated:

> vibhāvyate hi raty-ādir
> yatra yena vibhāvyate
> vibhāvo nāma sa dvedhā-
> lambanoddīpanātmakaḥ

"That which causes love for Kṛṣṇa to appear is called //vibhāva.// That has two divisions---//ālambana// [in which love appears] and //uddīpana// [by which love appears]."

In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu,// the following is stated about //ālambana://

> kṛṣṇaś ca kṛṣṇa-bhaktāś ca
> budhair ālambanā matāḥ
> raty-āder viṣayatvena
> tathādhāratayāpi ca

"The object of love is Kṛṣṇa, and the container of that love is the devotee of Kṛṣṇa. Both of them are called by the learned scholars //ālambana//---the foundations." Similarly, //uddīpana// is described:

> uddīpanās tu te proktā
> bhāvam uddīpayanti ye

"Those things which awaken ecstatic love are called //uddīpana.//"

> te tu śrī-kṛṣṇa-candrasya
> guṇāś ceṣṭāḥ prasādhanam

Mainly this awakening is made possible by the qualities and activities of Kṛṣṇa, as well as by His mode of decoration and the way His hair is arranged.

> smitāṅga-saurabhe vaṁśa-
> śṛṅga-nūpura-kambavaḥ
> padāṅka-kṣetra-tulasī-
> bhakta-tad-vāsarādayaḥ

"Kṛṣṇa's smile, the fragrance of His transcendental body, His flute, bugle, ankle bells, conchshell, the marks on His feet, His place of residence, His favorite plant [//tulasī//], His devotees, and the observance of fasts and vows connected to His devotion all awaken the symptoms of ecstatic love."

In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, anubhāva// is described as follows:

> anubhāvās tu citta-stha-
> bhāvānām avabodhakāḥ
> te bahir vikriyā prāyāḥ
> proktā udbhāsvarākhyayā

The many external ecstatic symptoms or bodily transformations which indicate ecstatic emotions in the mind, and which are also called //udbhāsvara,// are the //anubhāvas,// or subordinate ecstatic expressions of love. Some of these are dancing, falling down and rolling on the ground, singing and crying very loudly, bodily contortions, loud vibrations, yawning, deep breathing, disregard for others, the frothing of saliva, mad laughter, spitting, hiccups and other similar symptoms. All these symptoms are divided into two divisions-//śīta// and //kṣepaṇa.// Singing, yawning and so on are called //śīta.// Dancing and bodily contortions are called //kṣepaṇa.//

The //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// describes //udbhāsvara// as follows:

> udbhāsante svadhāmnīti
> proktā udbhāsvarā budhaiḥ
> nīvyuttarīya-dhammilla-
> sraṁsanaṁ gātra-moṭanam
> jṛmbhā ghrāṇasya phullatvaṁ
> niśvāsādyāś ca te matāḥ

The ecstatic symptoms manifest in the external body of a person in ecstatic love are called by learned scholars //udbhāsvara.// Some of these are a slackening of the belt and a dropping of clothes and hair. Others are bodily contortions, yawning, a trembling of the front portion of the nostrils, heavy breathing, hiccupping and falling down and rolling on the ground. These are the external manifestations of emotional love. //Stambha// and other symptoms are described in //Madhya-līlā// (14.167).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.52
description: "There are other ingredients beginning with complete despondency and jubilation. Altogether there are thirty-three varieties, and when these combine, the mellow becomes very wonderful.
text:
> nirveda-harṣādi---tetriśa 'vyabhicārī'
> saba mili' 'rasa' haya camatkārakārī
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirveda]]-[[synonyms:h:harṣa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---complete despondency, jubilation and so on; [[synonyms:t:tetriśa]]---thirty-three; [[synonyms:v:vyabhicārī]]---transitory elements; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:m:mili']]---all meeting together; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---the mellows; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:c:camatkārakārī]]---a cause of wonder.
translation: "There are other ingredients beginning with complete despondency and jubilation. Altogether there are thirty-three varieties, and when these combine, the mellow becomes very wonderful.
purport:
Nirveda, harṣa, and other symptoms are explained in //Madhya-līlā// (14.167). The transitory elements (//vyabhicārī//) are described in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// as follows:

> athocyante trayas triṁśad-
> bhāvā ye vyabhicāriṇaḥ
> viśeṣeṇābhimukhyena
> caranti sthāyinaṁ prati
> vāg-aṅga-sattva-sūcyā ye
> jñeyās te vyabhicāriṇaḥ
>
> sañcārayanti bhāvasya
> gatiṁ sañcāriṇo 'pi te
> unmajjanti nimajjanti
> stāyiny-amṛta-vāridhau
> ūrmivad vardhayanty enaṁ
> yānti tad-rūpatāṁ ca te

There are thirty-three transitory elements known as //vyabhicārī//-ecstatic emotions. They especially wander about the permanent sentiments as assistants. They are to be known by words, by different symptoms seen in the limbs and in other parts of the body, and by the peculiar conditions of the heart. Because they set in motion the progress of the permanent sentiments, they are specifically called //sañcārī,// or impelling principles. These impelling principles rise up and fall back in the permanent sentiments of ecstatic love like waves in an ocean of ecstasy. Consequently they are called //vyabhicāri.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.53
description: "There are five transcendental mellows-neutrality, servitorship, friendship, paternal affection and conjugal love, which is also known as the mellow of sweetness. Conjugal love excels all others.
text:
> pañca-vidha rasa---śānta, dāsya, sakhya, vātsalya
> madhura-nāma śṛṅgāra-rasa---sabāte prābalya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---five kinds of mellows; [[synonyms:ś:śānta]]---neutrality; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]---servitorship; [[synonyms:s:sakhya]]---friendship; [[synonyms:v:vātsalya]]---paternal affection; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweet; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:ś:śṛṅgāra]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---the conjugal mellow; [[synonyms:s:sabāte]]---among all of them; [[synonyms:p:prābalya]]---predominant.
translation: "There are five transcendental mellows-neutrality, servitorship, friendship, paternal affection and conjugal love, which is also known as the mellow of sweetness. Conjugal love excels all others.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.54
description: "The position of neutrality increases up to the point where one can appreciate love of Godhead. The mellow of servitorship gradually increases to the point of spontaneous love of Godhead.
text:
> śānta-rase śānti-rati 'prema' paryanta haya
> dāsya-rati 'rāga' paryanta krameta bāḍaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śānta]]-[[synonyms:r:rase]]---in the mellow of neutrality; [[synonyms:ś:śānti]]-[[synonyms:r:rati]]---spiritual attachment in peacefulness; [[synonyms:p:prema]] [[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---up to love of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]-[[synonyms:r:rati]]---attachment in servitude; [[synonyms:r:rāga]]---spontaneous love; [[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---up to; [[synonyms:k:krameta]]---gradually; [[synonyms:b:bāḍaya]]---increases.
translation: "The position of neutrality increases up to the point where one can appreciate love of Godhead. The mellow of servitorship gradually increases to the point of spontaneous love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.55
description: "After the mellow of servitorship, there are the mellows of friendship and paternal love, which increase to subordinate spontaneous love. The greatness of the love found in friends like Subala extends to the standard of ecstatic love of Godhead.
text:
> sakhya-vātsalya-rati pāya 'anurāga'-sīmā
> subalādyera 'bhāva' paryanta premera mahimā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakhya]]---in friendship; [[synonyms:v:vātsalya]]---in paternal affection; [[synonyms:r:rati]]---affection; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---obtains; [[synonyms:a:anurāga]]-[[synonyms:s:sīmā]]---up to the limit of subordinate spontaneous love; [[synonyms:s:subala]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādyera]]---of friends like Subala and others; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---ecstatic love; [[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---up to; [[synonyms:p:premera]] [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---the glory of the love of Godhead.
translation: "After the mellow of servitorship, there are the mellows of friendship and paternal love, which increase to subordinate spontaneous love. The greatness of the love found in friends like Subala extends to the standard of ecstatic love of Godhead.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that the mellow of neutrality increases to simple love of Godhead. In the mellow of servitorship, love of Godhead increases beyond that to affection, counter-love (anger based on love), love and attachment. Similarly, the mellow of friendship increases to affection, counter-love, love, attachment and subattachment. It is the same with the mellow of paternal affection. The special feature of the mellow of friendship exhibited by personalities like Subala is that it increases from fraternal affection to counter-love, to spontaneous attachment, to subordinate attachment, and finally to the ecstasy where all the ecstatic symptoms continuously exist.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.56
description: "There are two divisions of each of the five mellows-yoga [connection] and viyoga [separation]. Among the mellows of friendship and parental affection, there are many divisions of connection and separation.
text:
> śānta-ādi rasera 'yoga', 'viyoga'---dui bheda
> sakhya-vātsalye yogādira aneka vibheda
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śānta]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:r:rasera]]---of the mellows beginning from neutrality; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]---connection; [[synonyms:v:viyoga]]---separation; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---two divisions; [[synonyms:s:sakhya]]---in the mellow of friendship; [[synonyms:v:vātsalye]]---in paternal affection; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādira]]---of connection and separation; [[synonyms:a:aneka]] [[synonyms:v:vibheda]]---many varieties.
translation: "There are two divisions of each of the five mellows-yoga [connection] and viyoga [separation]. Among the mellows of friendship and parental affection, there are many divisions of connection and separation.
purport:
In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu,// these divisions are described:

> ayoga-yogāvetasya
> prabhedau kathitāv ubhau

In the mellows of //bhakti-yoga,// there are two stages-//ayoga// and //yoga. Ayoga// is described in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu://

> saṅgābhāvo harer dhīrair
> ayoga iti kathyate
> ayoge tvan-manaskatvaṁ
> tad-guṇādy-anusandhayaḥ
> tat-prāpty-upāya-cintādyāḥ
> sarveṣāṁ kathitāḥ kriyāḥ

Learned scholars in the science of //bhakti-yoga// say that when there is an absence of association with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, separation takes place. In the stage of //ayoga// (separation), the mind is filled with Kṛṣṇa consciousness and is fully absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa. In that stage, the devotee searches out the transcendental qualities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. It is said that in that stage of separation, all the devotees in the different mellows are always active in thinking of ways to attain Kṛṣṇa's association.

The word //yoga// (connection) is thus described:

> kṛṣṇena saṅgamo yas tu
> sa yoga iti kīrtyate

"When one meets Kṛṣṇa directly, that is called //yoga."//

In the transcendental mellows of neutrality and servitorship, there are similar divisions of //yoga// and //viyoga,// but they are not variegated. The divisions of //yoga// and //viyoga// are always existing in the five mellows. However, in the transcendental mellows of friendship and paternal affection, there are many varieties of //yoga// and //viyoga.// The varieties of //yoga// are thus described:

> yogo 'pi kathitaḥ siddhis
> tuṣṭiḥ sthitir iti tridhā

Yoga (connection) is of three types-success, satisfaction and permanence. The divisions of //ayoga// (separation) are thus described:

> utkaṇṭhitaṁ viyogaś cety
> ayogo 'pi dvidhocyate

Thus //ayoga// has two divisions-longing and separation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.57
description: "Only in the conjugal mellow are there two ecstatic symptoms called rūḍha [advanced] and adhirūḍha [highly advanced]. The advanced ecstasy is found among the queens of Dvārakā, and the highly advanced ecstasies are found among the gopīs.
text:
> 'rūḍha', 'adhirūḍha' bhāva---kevala 'madhure'
> mahiṣī-gaṇera 'rūḍha', 'adhirūḍha' gopikā-nikare
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rūḍha]]---advanced; [[synonyms:a:adhirūḍha]]---highly advanced; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---ecstasy; [[synonyms:k:kevala]]---only; [[synonyms:m:madhure]]---in the transcendental mellow of conjugal love; [[synonyms:m:mahiṣī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the queens of Dvārakā; [[synonyms:r:rūḍha]]---advanced; [[synonyms:a:adhirūḍha]]---highly advanced; [[synonyms:g:gopikā]]-[[synonyms:n:nikare]]---among the //gopīs.//
translation: "Only in the conjugal mellow are there two ecstatic symptoms called rūḍha [advanced] and adhirūḍha [highly advanced]. The advanced ecstasy is found among the queens of Dvārakā, and the highly advanced ecstasies are found among the gopīs.
purport:
The //adhirūḍha// ecstasies are explained in the //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi://

> rūḍhoktebhyo 'nubhāvebhyaḥ
> kām apy āptā viśiṣṭatām
> yatrānubhāvā dṛśyante
> so 'dhirūḍho nigadyate

The very sweet attraction of conjugal love increases through affection, counter-love, love, attachment, subattachment, ecstasy and highly advanced ecstasy (//mahābhāva//). The platform of //mahābhāva// includes //rūḍha// and //adhirūḍha.// These platforms are possible only in conjugal love. Advanced ecstasy is found in Dvārakā, whereas highly advanced ecstasy is found among the //gopīs.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.58
description: "Highly advanced ecstasy is divided into two categories-mādana and mohana. Meeting together is called mādana, and separation is called mohana.
text:
> adhirūḍha-mahābhāva---dui ta' prakāra
> sambhoge 'mādana', virahe 'mohana' nāma tāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:adhirūḍha]]-[[synonyms:m:mahābhāva]]---highly advanced ecstasy; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:t:ta']] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---two varieties; [[synonyms:s:sambhoge]]---in actually meeting; [[synonyms:m:mādana]]---//mādana//; [[synonyms:v:virahe]]---in separation; [[synonyms:m:mohana]]---//mohana//; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the names; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of them.
translation: "Highly advanced ecstasy is divided into two categories-mādana and mohana. Meeting together is called mādana, and separation is called mohana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.59
description: "On the mādana platform there are kissing and many other symptoms, which are unlimited. In the mohana stage, there are two divisions-udghūrṇā [unsteadiness] and citra-jalpa [varieties of mad emotional talks].
text:
> 'mādane' cumbanādi haya ananta vibheda
> 'udghūrṇā', 'citra-jalpa' 'mohane' dui bheda
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mādane]]---in the stage of //mādana//; [[synonyms:c:cumbana]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---kissing and similar activities; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:a:ananta]] [[synonyms:v:vibheda]]---unlimited divisions; [[synonyms:u:udghūrṇā]]---unsteadiness; [[synonyms:c:citra]]-[[synonyms:j:jalpa]]---various mad talks; [[synonyms:m:mohane]]---the stage of //mohana//; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---two divisions.
translation: "On the mādana platform there are kissing and many other symptoms, which are unlimited. In the mohana stage, there are two divisions-udghūrṇā [unsteadiness] and citra-jalpa [varieties of mad emotional talks].
purport: For further information, see //Madhya-līlā// (1.87).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.6
description: "Bhāva [emotion] has two different symptoms-constitutional and marginal. Now, My dear Sanātana, listen to the symptoms of love.
text:
> e dui,---bhāvera 'svarūpa', 'taṭastha' lakṣaṇa
> premera lakṣaṇa ebe śuna, sanātana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]]---these two; [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of emotion; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---constitutional; [[synonyms:t:taṭastha]]---marginal; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---symptoms; [[synonyms:p:premera]]---of love; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the symptoms; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---O Sanātana.
translation: "Bhāva [emotion] has two different symptoms-constitutional and marginal. Now, My dear Sanātana, listen to the symptoms of love.
purport: The word //śuddha-sattva-viśeṣātmā// means "situated on the transcendental platform of pure goodness." In this way the soul is purified of all material contamination, and this position is called //svarūpa-lakṣaṇa,// the constitutional symptom of //bhāva,// emotion. By various tastes, one's heart is softened, and there is an awakening of one's loving propensity to render spontaneous service to the Lord. This is called //taṭastha-lakṣaṇa,// the marginal symptom of //bhāva.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.60
description: "Mad emotional talks include ten divisions, called prajalpa and other names. An example of this is the ten verses spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī called 'song to the bumblebee.'
text:
> citra-jalpera daśa aṅga---prajalpādi-nāma
> 'bhramara-gītā'ra daśa śloka tāhāte pramāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:citra]]-[[synonyms:j:jalpera]]---of the mad talks; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]---ten; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---parts; [[synonyms:p:prajalpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named //prajalpa// and so on; [[synonyms:b:bhramara]]-[[synonyms:g:gītāra]]---of Rādhārāṇī's talks with the bumblebee (//Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// Canto Ten, Chapter Forty-seven); [[synonyms:d:daśa]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---ten verses; [[synonyms:t:tāhāte]]---in that matter; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---the evidence.
translation: "Mad emotional talks include ten divisions, called prajalpa and other names. An example of this is the ten verses spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī called 'song to the bumblebee.'
purport: Imaginative mad talks known as //citra-jalpa// can be divided into ten categories-//prajalpa, parijalpa, vijalpa, ujjalpa, sañjalpa, avajalpa, abhijalpa, ājalpa, pratijalpa// and //sujalpa.// There are no English equivalents for these different features of //jalpa// (imaginative talk).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.61
description: "Udghūrṇā [unsteadiness] and vivaśa-ceṣṭā [boastful activities] are aspects of transcendental madness. In separation from Kṛṣṇa, one experiences the manifestation of Kṛṣṇa, and one thinks oneself to be Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> udghūrṇā, vivaśa-ceṣṭā---divyonmāda-nāma
> virahe kṛṣṇa-sphūrti, āpanāke 'kṛṣṇa'-jñāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:udghūrṇā]]---unsteadiness; [[synonyms:v:vivaśa]]-[[synonyms:c:ceṣṭā]]---boastful activities; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:u:unmāda]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named transcendental madness; [[synonyms:v:virahe]]---in separation; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sphūrti]]---manifestation of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāke]]---oneself; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---thinking as Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Udghūrṇā [unsteadiness] and vivaśa-ceṣṭā [boastful activities] are aspects of transcendental madness. In separation from Kṛṣṇa, one experiences the manifestation of Kṛṣṇa, and one thinks oneself to be Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.62
description: "In conjugal love [śṛṅgāra] there are two departments-meeting and separation. On the platform of meeting, there are unlimited varieties that are beyond description.
text:
> 'sambhoga'-'vipralambha'-bhede dvividha śṛṅgāra
> sambhogera ananta aṅga, nāhi anta tāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sambhoga]]---of meeting (enjoyment together); [[synonyms:v:vipralambha]]---of separation; [[synonyms:b:bhede]]---in two divisions; [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:ś:śṛṅgāra]]---two kinds of conjugal love; [[synonyms:s:sambhogera]]---of the stage of //sambhoga,// or meeting; [[synonyms:a:ananta]] [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---unlimited parts; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:a:anta]]---an end; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that.
translation: "In conjugal love [śṛṅgāra] there are two departments-meeting and separation. On the platform of meeting, there are unlimited varieties that are beyond description.
purport:
//Vipralambha// is described in the //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi://

> yūnor ayuktayor bhāvo
> yuktayor vātha yo mithaḥ
> abhīṣṭāliṅganādīnām
> anavāptau prakṛṣyate
> sa vipralambho vijñeyaḥ
> sambhogonnatikārakaḥ
>
> na vinā vipralambhena
> sambhogaḥ puṣṭim aśnute

When the lover and the beloved meet, they are called //yukta// (connected). Previous to their meeting, they are called //ayukta// (not connected). Whether connected or not connected, the ecstatic emotion arising due to not being able to embrace and kiss each other as desired is called //vipralambha.// This //vipralambha// helps nourish emotions at the time of meeting. Similarly, //sambhoga// is thus described:

> darśanāliṅganādīnām
> ānukūlyān niṣevayā
> yūnor ullāsam ārohan
> bhāvaḥ sambhoga īryate

"Meeting each other and embracing each other are aimed at bringing about the happiness of both the lover and the beloved. When this stage becomes increasingly jubilant, the resultant ecstatic emotion is called //sambhoga.//" hen awakened, //sambhoga// is divided into four categories:

(1) //pūrva-rāga-anantara-//after //pūrva-rāga// (attachment prior to meeting), //sambhoga// is called brief (//saṅkṣipta//);

(2) //māna-anantara-//after //māna// (anger based on love), //sambhoga// is called encroached (//saṅkīrṇa//);

(3) //kiñcid-dūra-pravāsa-anantara-//after being a little distance away for some time, //sambhoga// is called accomplished (//sampanna//);

(4) //sudūra-pravāsa-anantara-//after being far away, //sambhoga// is called perfection (//samṛddhimān//).

The meetings of the lovers that take place in dreams also have these four divisions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.63
description: "Vipralambha has four divisions-pūrva-rāga, māna, pravāsa, and prema-vaicittya.
text:
> 'vipralambha' catur-vidha---pūrva-rāga, māna
> pravāsākhya, āra prema-vaicittya-ākhyāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipralambha]]---separation; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]]---four divisions; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:r:rāga]]---//pūrva-rāga//; [[synonyms:m:māna]]---//māna//; [[synonyms:p:pravāsākhya]]---known as //pravāsa//; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:v:vaicittya]]---//prema-vaicittya//; [[synonyms:ā:ākhyāna]]---calling.
translation: "Vipralambha has four divisions-pūrva-rāga, māna, pravāsa, and prema-vaicittya.
purport:
//Pūrva-rāga// is described in //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi://

> ratir yā saṅgamāt pūrvaṁ
> darśana-śravaṇādi-jā
> tayor unmīlati prājñaiḥ
> pūrva-rāgaḥ sa ucyate

When attachment produced in both the lover and beloved before their meeting by seeing, hearing and so on becomes very palatable by the mixture of four ingredients, such as //vibhāva// and //anubhāva,// this is called //pūrva-rāga.//

The word //māna// is also described:

> dampatyor bhāva ekatra
> sator apy anuraktayoḥ
> svābhīṣṭāśleṣa-vīkṣādi-
> nirodhī māna ucyate

Māna is a word used to indicate the mood of the lover and the beloved experienced whether they are in one place or in different places. This mood obstructs their looking at one another and embracing one another, despite the fact that they are attached to one another.

Pravāsa is also explained as follows:

> pūrva-saṅga-tayor yūnor
> bhaved deśāntarādibhiḥ
> vyavadhānaṁ tu yat prājñaiḥ
> sa pravāsa itīryate

Pravāsa is a word used to indicate the separation of lovers who were previously intimately associated. This separation is due to their being in different places.

Similarly, //prema-vaicittya// is explained:

> priyasya sannikarṣe 'pi
> premotkarṣa-svabhāvataḥ
> yā viśeṣa-dhiyārtis tat
> prema-vaicittyam ucyate

Prema-vaicittya is a word used to indicate an abundance of love that brings about grief from fear of separation, although the lover is present.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.64
description: "Of the four kinds of separation, three [pūrva-rāga, pravāsa and māna] are celebrated in Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and the gopīs. In Dvārakā, among the queens, feelings of prema-vaicittya are very prominent.
text:
> rādhikādye 'pūrva-rāga' prasiddha 'pravāsa', 'māne'
> 'prema-vaicittya' śrī-daśame mahiṣī-gaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rādhikādye]]---in Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and the other //gopīs//; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:r:rāga]]---feelings before union; [[synonyms:p:prasiddha]]---celebrated; [[synonyms:p:pravāsa]] [[synonyms:m:māne]]---also //pravāsa// and //māna//; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:v:vaicittya]]---feelings of fear of separation; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:d:daśame]]---in the Tenth Canto; [[synonyms:m:mahiṣī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---among the queens.
translation: "Of the four kinds of separation, three [pūrva-rāga, pravāsa and māna] are celebrated in Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and the gopīs. In Dvārakā, among the queens, feelings of prema-vaicittya are very prominent.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.65
description: " 'My dear friend kurarī, it is now night, and Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is sleeping. You yourself are not asleep or resting but are lamenting. Should I presume that you, like us, are affected by the smiling, liberal, playful glances of the lotus eyed Kṛṣṇa? If so, your heart is deeply pierced. Is that why you are showing these signs of sleepless lamentation?'
text:
> kurari vilapasi tvaṁ vīta-nidrā na śeṣe
> svapiti jagati rātryām īśvaro gupta-bodhaḥ
> vayam iva sakhī kaccid gāḍha-nirviddha-cetā
> nalina-nayana-hāsodāra-līlekṣitena
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kurari]]---O female osprey; [[synonyms:v:vilapasi]]---are lamenting; [[synonyms:t:tvam]]---you; [[synonyms:v:vīta]]-[[synonyms:n:nidrā]]---without sleep; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---rest; [[synonyms:s:svapiti]]---sleeps; [[synonyms:j:jagati]]---in the world; [[synonyms:r:rātryām]]---at night; [[synonyms:ī:īśvaraḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gupta]]-[[synonyms:b:bodhaḥ]]---whose consciousness is hidden; [[synonyms:v:vayam]]---we; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]---O dear friend; [[synonyms:k:kaccid]]---whether; [[synonyms:g:gāḍha]]---deeply; [[synonyms:n:nirviddha]]-[[synonyms:c:cetā]]---pierced in the heart; [[synonyms:n:nalina]]-[[synonyms:n:nayana]]---of the lotus-eyed Lord; [[synonyms:h:hāsa]]---smiling; [[synonyms:u:udāra]]---liberal; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:ī:īkṣitena]]---by the playful glancing.
translation: “ 'My dear friend kurarī, it is now night, and Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is sleeping. You yourself are not asleep or resting but are lamenting. Should I presume that you, like us, are affected by the smiling, liberal, playful glances of the lotus eyed Kṛṣṇa? If so, your heart is deeply pierced. Is that why you are showing these signs of sleepless lamentation?'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.90.15). Although the queens were with Kṛṣṇa, they were still thinking of losing His company.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.66
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead who appeared as the son of Nanda Mahārāja, is the supreme hero in all dealings. Similarly, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is the topmost heroine in all dealings.
text:
> vrajendra-nandana kṛṣṇa---nāyaka-śiromaṇi
> nāyikāra śiromaṇi---rādhā-ṭhākurāṇī
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa, the son of Mahārāja Nanda; [[synonyms:n:nāyaka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śiromaṇi]]---best of all heroes; [[synonyms:n:nāyikāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śiromaṇi]]---the best of all heroines; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākurāṇī]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead who appeared as the son of Nanda Mahārāja, is the supreme hero in all dealings. Similarly, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is the topmost heroine in all dealings.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.67
description: " 'Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself, and He is the crown jewel of all heroes. In Kṛṣṇa, all transcendental good qualities are permanently situated.'
text:
> nāyakānāṁ śiroratnaṁ
> kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam
> yatra nityatayā sarve
> virājante mahā-guṇāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nāyakānām]]---of all heroes; [[synonyms:ś:śiroratnam]]---the crown jewel; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]] [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---in whom; [[synonyms:n:nityatayā]]---with permanence; [[synonyms:s:sarve]]---all; [[synonyms:v:virājante]]---exist; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇāḥ]]---transcendental qualities.
translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself, and He is the crown jewel of all heroes. In Kṛṣṇa, all transcendental good qualities are permanently situated.'
purport: This verse is also found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (2.1.17).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.68
description: " 'The transcendental goddess Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is the direct counterpart of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa. She is the central figure for all the goddesses of fortune. She possesses all the attraction to attract the all-attractive Personality of Godhead. She is the primeval internal potency of the Lord.'
text:
> devī kṛṣṇamayī proktā
> rādhikā para-devatā
> sarva-lakṣmīmayī sarva-
> kāntiḥ sammohinī parā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:devī]]---who shines brilliantly; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mayī]]---nondifferent from Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:proktā]]---called; [[synonyms:r:rādhikā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:d:devatā]]---;most worshipable; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]-[[synonyms:m:mayī]]---presiding over all the goddesses of fortune; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāntiḥ]]---in whom all splendor exists; [[synonyms:s:sammohinī]]---whose character completely bewilders Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:parā]]---the superior energy.
translation: “ 'The transcendental goddess Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is the direct counterpart of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa. She is the central figure for all the goddesses of fortune. She possesses all the attraction to attract the all-attractive Personality of Godhead. She is the primeval internal potency of the Lord.'
purport: This text is found in the //Bṛhad-gautamīya-tantra.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.69
description: "The transcendental qualities of Lord Kṛṣṇa are unlimited. Out of these, sixty-four are considered prominent. The ears of the devotees are satisfied simply by hearing all these qualities one after the other.
text:
> ananta kṛṣṇera guṇa, cauṣaṭṭi---pradhāna
> eka eka guṇa śuni' juḍāya bhakta-kāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---qualities; [[synonyms:c:cauṣaṭṭi]]---sixty-four; [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---chief ones; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one by one; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---qualities; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:j:juḍāya]]---satisfies; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:k:kāṇa]]---the ears of the devotees.
translation: "The transcendental qualities of Lord Kṛṣṇa are unlimited. Out of these, sixty-four are considered prominent. The ears of the devotees are satisfied simply by hearing all these qualities one after the other.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.7
description: " 'When that bhāva softens the heart completely, becomes endowed with a great feeling of possessiveness in relation to the Lord and becomes very much condensed and intensified, it is called prema [love of Godhead] by learned scholars.
text:
> samyaṅ masṛṇita-svānto
> mamatvātiśayāṅkitaḥ
> bhāvaḥ sa eva sāndrātmā
> budhaiḥ premā nigadyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:samyak]]---completely; [[synonyms:m:masṛṇita]]-[[synonyms:s:svāntaḥ]]---which makes the heart soft; [[synonyms:m:mamatva]]---of a sense of ownership; [[synonyms:a:atiśaya]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅkitaḥ]]---marked with an abundance; [[synonyms:b:bhāvaḥ]]---emotion; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:sāndra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---whose nature is very condensed; [[synonyms:b:budhaiḥ]]---by learned persons; [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:nigadyate]]---is described.
translation: “ 'When that bhāva softens the heart completely, becomes endowed with a great feeling of possessiveness in relation to the Lord and becomes very much condensed and intensified, it is called prema [love of Godhead] by learned scholars.
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.4.1).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.70
description: " 'Kṛṣṇa, the supreme hero, has the most beautiful transcendental body. This body possesses all good features. It is radiant and very pleasing to the eyes. His body is powerful, strong and youthful.
text:
> ayaṁ netā suramyāṅgaḥ
> sarva-sal-lakṣaṇānvitaḥ
> ruciras tejasā yukto
> balīyān vayasānvitaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this (Kṛṣṇa); [[synonyms:n:netā]]---supreme hero; [[synonyms:s:suramya]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅgaḥ]]---having the most beautiful transcendental body; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---all-auspicious bodily marks; [[synonyms:a:anvitaḥ]]---endowed with; [[synonyms:r:ruciraḥ]]---possessing radiance very pleasing to the eyes; [[synonyms:t:tejasā]]---with all power; [[synonyms:y:yuktaḥ]]---bestowed; [[synonyms:b:balīyān]]---very strong; [[synonyms:v:vayasa]]-[[synonyms:a:anvitaḥ]]---having a youthful age.
translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa, the supreme hero, has the most beautiful transcendental body. This body possesses all good features. It is radiant and very pleasing to the eyes. His body is powerful, strong and youthful.
purport: This verse and the following six verses are also found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (2.1.23-29).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.71
description: " 'Kṛṣṇa is the linguist of all wonderful languages. He is a truthful and very pleasing speaker. He is expert in speaking, and He is a very wise, learned scholar and a genius.
text:
> vividhādbhuta-bhāṣā-vit
> satya-vākyaḥ priyaṁ vadaḥ
> vāvadūkaḥ supāṇḍityo
> buddhimān pratibhānvitaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vividha]]---various; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:b:bhāṣā]]-[[synonyms:v:vit]]---knower of languages; [[synonyms:s:satya]]-[[synonyms:v:vākyaḥ]]---whose words are truthful; [[synonyms:p:priyam]] [[synonyms:v:vadaḥ]]---who speaks very pleasingly; [[synonyms:v:vāvadūkaḥ]]---expert in speaking; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:p:pāṇḍityaḥ]]---very learned; [[synonyms:b:buddhimān]]---very wise; [[synonyms:p:pratibhā]]-[[synonyms:a:anvitaḥ]]---genius.
translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa is the linguist of all wonderful languages. He is a truthful and very pleasing speaker. He is expert in speaking, and He is a very wise, learned scholar and a genius.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.72
description: " 'Kṛṣṇa is very expert in artistic enjoyment. He is highly cunning, expert, grateful and firmly determined in His vows. He knows how to deal according to time, person and country, and He sees through the scriptures and authoritative books. He is very clean and self-controlled.
text:
> vidagdhaś caturo dakṣaḥ
> kṛtajñaḥ sudṛḍha-vrataḥ
> deśa-kāla-supātrajñaḥ
> śāstra-cakṣuḥ śucir vaśī
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vidagdhaḥ]]---expert in artistic enjoyment; [[synonyms:c:caturaḥ]]---cunning; [[synonyms:d:dakṣaḥ]]---expert; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:j:jñaḥ]]---grateful; [[synonyms:s:sudṛḍha]]-[[synonyms:v:vrataḥ]]---firmly determined; [[synonyms:d:deśa]]---of country; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]---time; [[synonyms:s:supātra]]---of fitness; [[synonyms:j:jñaḥ]]---a knower; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:c:cakṣuḥ]]---expert in the authoritative scriptures; [[synonyms:ś:śuciḥ]]---very clean and neat; [[synonyms:v:vaśī]]---serf-controlled.
translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa is very expert in artistic enjoyment. He is highly cunning, expert, grateful and firmly determined in His vows. He knows how to deal according to time, person and country, and He sees through the scriptures and authoritative books. He is very clean and self-controlled.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.73
description: " 'Lord Kṛṣṇa is steady, His senses are controlled, and He is forgiving, grave and calm. He is also equal to all. Moreover, He is magnanimous, religious, chivalrous and kind. He is always respectful to respectable people.
text:
> sthiro dāntaḥ kṣamā-śīlo
> gambhīro dhṛtimān samaḥ
> vadānyo dhārmikaḥ śūraḥ
> karuṇo mānya-mānakṛt
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sthiraḥ]]---steady; [[synonyms:d:dāntaḥ]]---having controlled senses; [[synonyms:k:kṣamā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śīlaḥ]]---forgiving; [[synonyms:g:gambhīraḥ]]---grave; [[synonyms:d:dhṛtimān]]---calm, never bereft of intelligence; [[synonyms:s:samaḥ]]---equal; [[synonyms:v:vadānyaḥ]]---magnanimous; [[synonyms:d:dhārmikaḥ]]---religious; [[synonyms:ś:śūraḥ]]---chivalrous; [[synonyms:k:karuṇaḥ]]---kind; [[synonyms:m:mānya]]-[[synonyms:m:mānakṛt]]---respectful to the respectable.
translation: “ 'Lord Kṛṣṇa is steady, His senses are controlled, and He is forgiving, grave and calm. He is also equal to all. Moreover, He is magnanimous, religious, chivalrous and kind. He is always respectful to respectable people.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.74
description: " 'Kṛṣṇa is very simple and liberal, He is humble and bashful, and He is the protector of the surrendered soul. He is very happy, and He is always the well-wisher of His devotee. He is all-auspicious, and He is submissive to love.
text:
> dakṣiṇo vinayī hrīmān
> śaraṇāgata-pālakaḥ
> sukhī bhakta-suhṛt prema-
> vaśyaḥ sarva-śubhaṅkaraḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇaḥ]]---simple and liberal; [[synonyms:v:vinayī]]---humble; [[synonyms:h:hrīmān]]---bashful when glorified; [[synonyms:ś:śaraṇāgata]]-[[synonyms:p:pālakaḥ]]---protector of the surrendered soul; [[synonyms:s:sukhī]]---//always// happy; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:s:suhṛt]]---well-wisher of the devotees; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśyaḥ]]---submissive to love; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śubhaṅkaraḥ]]---all-auspicious.
translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa is very simple and liberal, He is humble and bashful, and He is the protector of the surrendered soul. He is very happy, and He is always the well-wisher of His devotee. He is all-auspicious, and He is submissive to love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.75
description: " 'Kṛṣṇa is very influential and famous, and He is the object of attachment for everyone. He is the shelter of the good and the virtuous. He is attractive to the minds of women, and He is worshiped by everyone. He is very, very rich.
text:
> pratāpī kīrtimān rakta-
> lokaḥ sādhu-samāśrayaḥ
> nārīgaṇa-manohārī
> sarvārādhyaḥ samṛddhimān
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pratāpī]]---very influential; [[synonyms:k:kīrtimān]]---famous for good works; [[synonyms:r:rakta]]-[[synonyms:l:lokaḥ]]---who is the object of the attachment of all people; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśrayaḥ]]---the shelter of the good and virtuous; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---to women; [[synonyms:m:manohārī]]---attractive; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārādhyaḥ]]---worshipable by everyone; [[synonyms:s:samṛddhimān]]---very rich.
translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa is very influential and famous, and He is the object of attachment for everyone. He is the shelter of the good and the virtuous. He is attractive to the minds of women, and He is worshiped by everyone. He is very, very rich.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.76
description: " 'Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme, and He is always glorified as the Supreme Lord and controller. Thus all the previously mentioned transcendental qualities are in Him. The fifty qualities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead above mentioned are as deep as an ocean. In other words, they are difficult to fully comprehend.
text:
> varīyān īśvaraś ceti
> guṇās tasyānukīrtitāḥ
> samudrā iva pañcāśad
> durvigāhā harer amī
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:varīyān]]---the best; [[synonyms:ī:īśvaraḥ]]---the supreme controller; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:g:guṇāḥ]]---the transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:t:tasya]]---of Him; [[synonyms:a:anukīrtitāḥ]]---described; [[synonyms:s:samudrāḥ]]---oceans; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:p:pañcāśat]]---fifty; [[synonyms:d:durvigāhāḥ]]---difficult to penetrate fully; [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:amī]]---all these.
translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme, and He is always glorified as the Supreme Lord and controller. Thus all the previously mentioned transcendental qualities are in Him. The fifty qualities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead above mentioned are as deep as an ocean. In other words, they are difficult to fully comprehend.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.77
description: " 'These qualities are sometimes very minutely exhibited in living beings, but they are fully manifest in the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
text:
> jīveṣu ete vasanto 'pi
> bindu-bindutayā kvacit
> paripūrṇatayā bhānti
> tatraiva puruṣottame
