synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jīveṣu]]---in the living entities; [[synonyms:e:ete]]---these; [[synonyms:v:vasantaḥ]]---are residing; [[synonyms:a:api]]---though; [[synonyms:b:bindu]]-[[synonyms:b:bindutayā]]---with a very minute quantity; [[synonyms:k:kvacit]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:p:paripūrṇatayā]]---with fullness; [[synonyms:b:bhānti]]---are manifest; [[synonyms:t:tatra]]---in Him; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:u:uttame]]---in the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'These qualities are sometimes very minutely exhibited in living beings, but they are fully manifest in the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
purport:
This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (2.1.30). Living entities are parts and parcels of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā://

> mamaivāṁśo jīva-loke
> jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ
> manaḥ ṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi
> prakṛti-sthāni karṣati

"The living entities in this conditioned world are My eternal, fragmental parts. Due to conditioned life, they are struggling very hard with the six senses, which include the mind." [[books:bg:15:7|(Bg. 15.7)]]

The qualities of Kṛṣṇa are present in the living entity in minute, atomic quantities. A small portion of gold is certainly gold, but it cannot be equal to a gold mine. Similarly, the living entities have all the characteristics of the Supreme Personality of Godhead in minute quantity, but the living entity is never equal to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. God is therefore described as the Supreme Being, and the living entity is described as a //jīva.// God is the Supreme Being, the chief of all living beings-//eko bahūnāṁ yo vidadhāti kāmān.// The Māyāvādīs maintain that everyone is God, but even if this philosophy is accepted, no one can maintain that everyone is equal to the Supreme Godhead. Only unintelligent men maintain that everyone is equal to God or that everyone is God.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.78
description: " 'Apart from these fifty qualities, there are five other qualities found in the Supreme Personality of Godhead that are partially present in demigods like Śiva.
text:
> atha pañca-guṇā ye syur
> aṁśena giriśādiṣu
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:atha]]---now(over and above these); [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇāḥ]]---five qualities; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:s:syuḥ]]---may exist; [[synonyms:a:aṁśena]]---by part; [[synonyms:g:giriśa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādiṣu]]---in demigods like Lord Śiva.
translation: “ 'Apart from these fifty qualities, there are five other qualities found in the Supreme Personality of Godhead that are partially present in demigods like Śiva.
purport: This verse and the following seven verses are also found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (2.1.37-44).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.79-81
description: " 'These qualities are (1) the Lord is always situated in His original position, (2) He is omniscient, (3) He is always fresh and youthful, (4) He is the concentrated form of eternity, knowledge and bliss, and (5) He is the possessor of all mystic perfection. There are another five qualities, which exist in the Vaikuṇṭha planets in Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Lakṣmī. These qualities are also present in Kṛṣṇa, but they are not present in demigods like Lord Śiva or in other living entities. These are (1) inconceivable supreme power, (2) generating innumerable universes from the body, (3) being the original source of all incarnations, (4) bestowing salvation upon enemies killed, and (5) the ability to attract exalted persons who are satisfied in themselves. Although these qualities are present in Nārāyaṇa, the dominating Deity of the Vaikuṇṭha planets, they are even more wonderfully present in Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> sadā svarūpa-saṁprāptaḥ
> sarva-jño nity-nūtanaḥ
> sac-cid-ānanda-sāndrāṅgaḥ
> sarva-siddhi-niṣevitaḥ
>
> athocyante guṇāḥ pañca
> ye lakṣmīśādi-vartinaḥ
> avicintya-mahā-śaktiḥ
> koṭi-brahmāṇḍa-vigrahaḥ
>
> avatārāvalī-bījaṁ
> hatāri-gati-dāyakaḥ
> ātmārāma-gaṇākarṣīty
> amī kṛṣṇe kilādbhutāḥ

translation: “ 'These qualities are (1) the Lord is always situated in His original position, (2) He is omniscient, (3) He is always fresh and youthful, (4) He is the concentrated form of eternity, knowledge and bliss, and (5) He is the possessor of all mystic perfection. There are another five qualities, which exist in the Vaikuṇṭha planets in Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Lakṣmī. These qualities are also present in Kṛṣṇa, but they are not present in demigods like Lord Śiva or in other living entities. These are (1) inconceivable supreme power, (2) generating innumerable universes from the body, (3) being the original source of all incarnations, (4) bestowing salvation upon enemies killed, and (5) the ability to attract exalted persons who are satisfied in themselves. Although these qualities are present in Nārāyaṇa, the dominating Deity of the Vaikuṇṭha planets, they are even more wonderfully present in Kṛṣṇa.

purport: This verse, quoted from the //Nārada-pañcarātra,// is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.4.2).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.82-83
description: " 'Apart from these sixty transcendental qualities, Kṛṣṇa has an additional four transcendental qualities, which are not manifest even in the personality of Nārāyaṇa. These are: (1) Kṛṣṇa is like an ocean filled with waves of pastimes that evoke wonder within everyone in the three worlds. (2) In His activities of conjugal love, He is always surrounded by His dear devotees who possess unequaled love for Him. (3) He attracts the minds of all three worlds by the melodious vibration of His flute. (4) His personal beauty and opulence are beyond compare. No one is equal to Him, and no one is greater than Him. Thus the Personality of Godhead astonishes all living entities, both moving and nonmoving, within the three worlds. He is so beautiful that He is called Kṛṣṇa.

These are: (1) Kṛṣṇa is like an ocean filled with waves of pastimes that evoke wonder within everyone in the three worlds. (2) In His activities of conjugal love, He is always surrounded by His dear devotees who possess unequaled love for Him. (3) He attracts the minds of all three worlds by the melodious vibration of His flute. (4) His personal beauty and opulence are beyond compare. No one is equal to Him, and no one is greater than Him. Thus the Personality of Godhead astonishes all living entities, both moving and nonmoving, within the three worlds. He is so beautiful that He is called Kṛṣṇa.
purport: Māyāvādī philosophers, who have a poor fund of knowledge, simply dismiss the subject by explaining that Kṛṣṇa means black. Not understanding the qualities of Kṛṣṇa, these atheistic rascals do not accept Him as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although the Lord is described and accepted by great personalities, //ācāryas// and sages, the Māyāvādīs still do not appreciate Him. Unfortunately at the present moment human society is so degraded that people cannot even provide themselves with life's daily necessities, yet they are captivated by Māyāvādī philosophers and are being misled. According to //Bhagavad-gītā,// simply by understanding Kṛṣṇa one can get free from the cycle of birth and death. //Tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so 'rjuna.// Unfortunately this great science of Kṛṣṇa consciousness has been impeded by Māyāvādī philosophers who are opposed to the personality of Kṛṣṇa. Those who are preaching this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement must try to understand Kṛṣṇa from the statements given in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (//The NectarofDevotion//).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.84-85
description: " 'Above Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa has four specific transcendental qualities-His wonderful pastimes, an abundance of wonderful associates who are very dear to Him [like the gopīs], His wonderful beauty and the wonderful vibration of His flute. Lord Kṛṣṇa is more exalted than ordinary living beings and demigods like Lord Śiva. He is even more exalted than His personal expansion Nārāyaṇa. In all, the Supreme Personality of Godhead has sixty-four transcendental qualities in full.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.87-91
description: " 'Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's twenty-five chief transcendental qualities are: (1) She is very sweet. (2) She is always freshly youthful. (3) Her eyes are restless. (4) She smiles brightly. (5) She has beautiful, auspicious lines. (6) She makes Kṛṣṇa happy with Her bodily aroma. (7) She is very expert in singing. (8) Her speech is charming. (9) She is very expert in joking and speaking pleasantly. (10) She is very humble and meek. (11) She is always full of mercy. (12) She is cunning. (13) She is expert in executing Her duties. (14) She is shy. (15) She is always respectful. (16) She is always calm. (17) She is always grave. (18) She is expert in enjoying life. (19) She is situated at the topmost level of ecstatic love. (20) She is the reservoir of loving affairs in Gokula. (21) She is the most famous of submissive devotees. (22) She is very affectionate to elderly people. (23) She is very submissive to the love of Her friends. (24) She is the chief gopī. (25) She always keeps Kṛṣṇa under Her control. In short, She possesses unlimited transcendental qualities, just as Lord Kṛṣṇa does.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.93
description: "Just as Lord Kṛṣṇa and Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī are the object and shelter of the mellow of conjugal love, so, in the mellow of servitorship, Kṛṣṇa, the son of Mahārāja Nanda, is the object, and servants like Citraka, Raktaka and Patraka are the shelter. Similarly, in the transcendental mellow of friendship, Lord Kṛṣṇa is the object, and friends like Śrīdāmā, Sudāmā and Subala are the shelter. In the transcendental mellow of paternal affection, Kṛṣṇa is the object, and mother Yaśodā and Mahārāja Nanda are the shelter.

Similarly, in the transcendental mellow of friendship, Lord Kṛṣṇa is the object, and friends like Śrīdāmā, Sudāmā and Subala are the shelter. In the transcendental mellow of paternal affection, Kṛṣṇa is the object, and mother Yaśodā and Mahārāja Nanda are the shelter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.95-98
description: " 'Those who are completely washed of all material contamination by pure devotional service, who are always satisfied and brightly enlightened in the heart, who are always attached to understanding the transcendental meaning of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, who are always eager to associate with advanced devotees, whose happiness in the service of the lotus feet of Govinda is their very life, who always discharge the confidential activities of love-for such advanced devotees, who are by nature situated in bliss, the seed of love [rati] is expanded in the heart by previous and current reformatory processes. Thus the mixture of ecstatic ingredients becomes tasty and, being within the perception of the devotee, reaches the highest platform of wonder and deep bliss.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 23.99
description: "The exchange between Kṛṣṇa and different devotees situated in different transcendental mellows is not to be experienced by nondevotees. Advanced devotees can understand and appreciate the different varieties of devotional service reciprocated with the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

translation: "The exchange between Kṛṣṇa and different devotees situated in different transcendental mellows is not to be experienced by nondevotees. Advanced devotees can understand and appreciate the different varieties of devotional service reciprocated with the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.1
description: May Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu be glorified. It was He who acted as the eastern horizon where the sun of the ātmārāma verse rises and manifests its rays in the form of different meanings and thus eradicates the darkness of the material world. May He protect the universe.
text:
> ātmārāmeti padyārkasy-
> ārthāṁśūn yaḥ prakāśayan
> jagat-tamo jahārāvyāt
> sa caitanyodayācalaḥ

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.10

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.100
description: " 'The great scripture Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, compiled by Mahāmuni Vyāsadeva from four original verses, describes the most elevated and kindhearted devotees and completely rejects the cheating ways of materially motivated religiosity. It propounds the highest principle of eternal religion, which can factually mitigate the threefold miseries of a living being and award the highest benediction of full prosperity and knowledge. Those willing to hear the message of this scripture in a submissive attitude of service can at once capture the Supreme Lord in their hearts. Therefore there is no need for any scripture other than Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.'
text:
> dharmaḥ projjhita-kaitavo 'tra paramo nirmatsarāṇāṁ satāṁ
> vedyaṁ vāstavam atra vastu śivadaṁ tāpa-trayonmūlanam
> śrīmad-bhāgavate mahāmuni-kṛte kiṁ vā parair īśvaraḥ
> sadyo hṛdy avarudhyate 'tra kṛtibhiḥ śuśrūṣubhis tat-kṣaṇāt

translation: “ 'The great scripture Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, compiled by Mahāmuni Vyāsadeva from four original verses, describes the most elevated and kindhearted devotees and completely rejects the cheating ways of materially motivated religiosity. It propounds the highest principle of eternal religion, which can factually mitigate the threefold miseries of a living being and award the highest benediction of full prosperity and knowledge. Those willing to hear the message of this scripture in a submissive attitude of service can at once capture the Supreme Lord in their hearts. Therefore there is no need for any scripture other than Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:1:2|(1.1.2)]]. For an explanation see also //Ādi-līlā// (1.91).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.102
description: "When the merciful Lord Kṛṣṇa understands a devotee's foolish desire for material prosperity, He gratefully gives him the shelter of His lotus feet. In this way, the Lord covers his undesirable ambitions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.103
description: " 'Whenever Kṛṣṇa is requested to fulfill one's desire, He undoubtedly does so, but He does not award anything which, after being enjoyed, will cause someone to petition Him again and again to fulfill further desires. When one has other desires but engages in the Lord's service, Kṛṣṇa forcibly gives one shelter at His lotus feet, where one will forget all other desires.'
text:
> satyaṁ diśaty arthitam arthito nṛṇāṁ
> naivārthado yat punar arthitā yataḥ
> svayaṁ vidhatte bhajatām anicchatām
> icchā-pidhānaṁ nija-pāda-pallavam

translation: “ 'Whenever Kṛṣṇa is requested to fulfill one's desire, He undoubtedly does so, but He does not award anything which, after being enjoyed, will cause someone to petition Him again and again to fulfill further desires. When one has other desires but engages in the Lord's service, Kṛṣṇa forcibly gives one shelter at His lotus feet, where one will forget all other desires.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:5:19:27|(5.19.27)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.104
description: "Association with a devotee, the mercy of Kṛṣṇa, and the nature of devotional service help one to give up all undesirable association and gradually attain elevation to the platform of love of Godhead.
text:
> sādhu-saṅga, kṛṣṇa-kṛpā, bhaktira svabhāva
> e tine saba chāḍāya, kare kṛṣṇe 'bhāva'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---the association of devotees; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---the mercy of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhaktira]]---of devotional service; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---nature; [[synonyms:e:e]] [[synonyms:t:tine]]---these three; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍāya]]---cause one to give up everything else; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the loving affairs.
translation: "Association with a devotee, the mercy of Kṛṣṇa, and the nature of devotional service help one to give up all undesirable association and gradually attain elevation to the platform of love of Godhead.
purport:
This verse refers to the association of pure devotees, the mercy of Kṛṣṇa and the rendering of devotional service. All these help one give up the association of nondevotees and the material opulence awarded by the external energy, //māyā.// A pure devotee is never attracted by material opulence, for he understands that wasting time to acquire material opulence is a misuse of the gift of human life. In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// it is said: //śrama eva hi kevalam.// In the eyes of a devotee, politicians, social workers, philanthropists, philosophers and humanitarians are simply wasting their time, for human society is not freed from the cycle of birth and death by their activity and propaganda. These so-called philanthropists, politicians and philosophers have no knowledge because they do not know that there is life after death. Understanding that there is life after death is the beginning of spiritual knowledge. A person can understand himself and what he is simply by understanding the first lessons of //Bhagavad-gītā.//

> dehino 'smin yathā dehe
> kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā
> tathā dehāntara-prāptir
> dhīras tatra na muhyati

"As the embodied soul continuously passes, in this body, from boyhood to youth to old age, the soul similarly passes into another body at death. The self-realized soul is not bewildered by such a change." [[books:bg:2:13|(Bg. 2.13)]]

Not knowing the real science of life one engages in the temporary activities of this life and thus becomes further entangled in the cycle of birth and death. Thus one always desires material opulence, which can be attained by //karma, jñāna// and //yoga.// However, when one is actually elevated to the devotional platform, he gives up all these desires. This is called //anyābhilāṣitā-śūnya.// Then one becomes a pure devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.105
description: "In this way I shall progressively explain all the words in the verse. It should be understood that all these words are meant to enable one to taste the transcendental quality of Kṛṣṇa.
text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.107
description: "There are two kinds of worshipers on the path of philosophical speculation-one is brahma-upāsaka, a worshiper of the impersonal Brahman, and the other is called mokṣākāṅkṣī, one who desires liberation.
text:
> jñāna-mārge upāsaka---duita' prakāra
> kevala brahmopāsaka, mokṣākāṅkṣī āra

translation: "There are two kinds of worshipers on the path of philosophical speculation-one is brahma-upāsaka, a worshiper of the impersonal Brahman, and the other is called mokṣākāṅkṣī, one who desires liberation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.108
description: "There are three types of people who worship the impersonal Brahman. The first is the beginner, the second is one whose thoughts are absorbed in Brahman, and the third is one who is actually merged in the impersonal Brahman.
text:
> kevala brahmopāsaka tina bheda haya
> sādhaka, brahmamaya, āra prāpta-brahma-laya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kevala]] [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:u:upāsaka]]---the worshiper of only the impersonal Brahman; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:b:bheda]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are three different groups; [[synonyms:s:sādhaka]]---the beginner; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---absorbed in thought of Brahman; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:prāpta]]-[[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:l:laya]]---actually merged into the Brahman effulgence.
translation: "There are three types of people who worship the impersonal Brahman. The first is the beginner, the second is one whose thoughts are absorbed in Brahman, and the third is one who is actually merged in the impersonal Brahman.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.109
description: "One cannot attain liberation simply through philosophical speculation devoid of devotional service. However, if one renders devotional service, he is automatically on the Brahman platform.
text:
> bhakti vinā kevala jñāne 'mukti' nāhi haya
> bhakti sādhana kare yei 'prāpta-brahma-laya'
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:k:kevala]]---only; [[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---by philosophical speculation; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is not; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---practice; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:p:prāpta]]-[[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:l:laya]]---as good as merging into the impersonal Brahman.
translation: "One cannot attain liberation simply through philosophical speculation devoid of devotional service. However, if one renders devotional service, he is automatically on the Brahman platform.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.11
description: "The seven different meanings of the word ātmā are the Absolute Truth, the body, the mind, endeavor, firmness, intelligence and nature.
text:
> 'ātmā'-śabde brahma, deha, mana, yatna, dhṛti
> buddhi, svabhāva,---ei sāta artha-prāpti
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ātmā//; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---the body; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:y:yatna]]---endeavor; [[synonyms:d:dhṛti]]---firmness; [[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---intelligence; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---nature; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:sāta]]---these seven; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:p:prāpti]]---obtainment of meanings.
translation: "The seven different meanings of the word ātmā are the Absolute Truth, the body, the mind, endeavor, firmness, intelligence and nature.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.110
description: "Characteristically, one in devotional service is attracted away from the impersonal Brahman platform. Be is offered a transcendental body to engage in Lord Kṛṣṇa's service.
text:
> bhaktira svabhāva,---brahma haite kare ākarṣaṇa
> divya deha diyā karāya kṛṣṇera bhajana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaktira]]---of devotional service; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---nature; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---impersonal Brahman realization; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaṇa]]---attracting; [[synonyms:d:divya]]---transcendental; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---body; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---offering; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---causes to perform; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Characteristically, one in devotional service is attracted away from the impersonal Brahman platform. Be is offered a transcendental body to engage in Lord Kṛṣṇa's service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.111
description: "When one gets a devotee's spiritual body, he can remember the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa. Simply by being attracted to Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities, one becomes a pure devotee engaged in His service.
text:
> bhakta-deha pāile haya guṇera smaraṇa
> guṇākṛṣṭa hañā kare nirmala bhajana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:d:deha]]---the body of a devotee; [[synonyms:p:pāile]]---when one gets; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:g:guṇera]] [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---remembrance of the transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being attracted by the transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:n:nirmala]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---pure devotional service.
translation: "When one gets a devotee's spiritual body, he can remember the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa. Simply by being attracted to Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities, one becomes a pure devotee engaged in His service.
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has given the following summary of verses 107-111. Transcendentalists on the path of philosophical speculation can be divided into two categories---the pure worshiper of impersonal Brahman and he who wishes to merge into the existence of impersonal Brahman. When one is fully absorbed in the thought that one is not different from the Supreme Absolute Truth, one is said to be a worshiper of the impersonal Brahman. The impersonal worshipers of Brahman can again be divided into three categories-(1) //sādhaka,// those who are nearing perfect execution of the process of Brahman realization; (2) those who are fully absorbed in meditation on Brahman; and (3) those who are on the //brahma-bhūta// platform and have no relationship with material existence. Even though the worshiper of impersonal Brahman can be highly advanced, he cannot attain liberation without discharging devotional service. Anyone who has realized himself as spirit soul can engage in devotional service. This is the verdict of //Bhagavad-gītā://

> brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā
> na śocati na kāṅkṣati
> samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu
> mad-bhaktiṁ labhate parām

"One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and is fully joyful. He never laments nor desires to have anything; he is equally disposed to every living entity. In that state he attains pure devotional service unto Me." [[books:bg:18:54|(Bg. 18.54)]]

To attain the platform of pure devotional service, one has to become spiritually pure and attain the //brahma-bhūta// platform, which is beyond material anxiety and material discrimination. When one approaches pure devotional service after realizing Brahman, one becomes attracted by pure devotional service. At such a time, by rendering devotional service, one gets a spiritual body with purified senses.

> sarvopādhi-vinirmuktaṁ
> tatparatvena nirmalam
> hṛṣīkeṇa hṛṣīkeśa-
> sevanaṁ bhaktir ucyate

When one's senses are pure, one can render loving devotional service to Kṛṣṇa. A pure devotee can only remember Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities. Remembering them, he fully engages in the loving service of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.112
description: " 'Even a liberated soul merged in the impersonal Brahman effulgence is attracted to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. He thus installs a Deity and renders the Lord service.'
text:
> "muktā api līlayā vigrahaṁ
> kṛtvā bhagavantaṁ bhajante"
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muktāḥ]]---liberated; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:l:līlayā]]---by pastimes; [[synonyms:v:vigraham]]---the form of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛtvā]]---having installed; [[synonyms:b:bhagavantam]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhajante]]---worship.
translation: “ 'Even a liberated soul merged in the impersonal Brahman effulgence is attracted to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. He thus installs a Deity and renders the Lord service.'
purport: Highly elevated Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// sometimes worship the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa Deity and discuss the pastimes of the Lord, but their purpose is not elevation to Goloka Vṛndāvana. They want to merge into the Lord's effulgence. This statement is quoted from Śaṅkarācārya's commentary on the //Upaniṣad// known as //Nṛsiṁha-tāpanī.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.113
description: "Although Śukadeva Gosvāmī and the four Kumāras were always absorbed in the thought of impersonal Brahman and were thus Brahmavādīs, they were nonetheless attracted by the transcendental pastimes and qualities of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore they later became devotees of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> janma haite śuka-sanakādi 'brahmamaya'
> kṛṣṇa-guṇākṛṣṭa hañā kṛṣṇere bhajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:janma]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from birth; [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]---Śukadeva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:sanaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the four Kumāras; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---absorbed in the thought of impersonal Brahman; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]]---attracted by the transcendental pastimes of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]] [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---worshiped Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Although Śukadeva Gosvāmī and the four Kumāras were always absorbed in the thought of impersonal Brahman and were thus Brahmavādīs, they were nonetheless attracted by the transcendental pastimes and qualities of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore they later became devotees of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.114
description: "The minds of the four Kumāras were attracted by the aroma of the flowers offered to Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet. Being thus attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, they engaged in pure devotional service.
text:
> sanakādyera kṛṣṇa-kṛpāya saurabhe hare mana
> guṇākṛṣṭa hañā kare nirmala bhajana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sanaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādyera]]---of the four Kumāras, headed by Sanaka; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpāya]]---by the mercy of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:saurabhe]]---the fragrance; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---took away; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---thus being attracted by the qualities of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform; [[synonyms:n:nirmala]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---pure devotional service.
translation: "The minds of the four Kumāras were attracted by the aroma of the flowers offered to Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet. Being thus attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, they engaged in pure devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.115
description: " 'When the breeze carrying the aroma of tulasī leaves and saffron from the lotus feet of the lotus-eyed Personality of Godhead entered through the nostrils into the hearts of those sages [the Kumāras], they experienced a change in both body and mind, even though they were attached to impersonal Brahman understanding.'
text:
> tasyāravinda-nayanasya padāravinda-
> kiñjalka-miśra-tulasī-makaranda-vāyuḥ
> antargataḥ svavivareṇa cakāra teṣāṁ
> saṅkṣobham akṣara-juṣām api citta-tanvoḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tasya]]---of Him; [[synonyms:a:aravinda]]-[[synonyms:n:nayanasya]]---of the lotus-eyed Lord; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:a:aravinda]]---of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:k:kiñjalka]]---with the toes; [[synonyms:m:miśra]]---mixed; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]---the //tulasī// leaves; [[synonyms:m:makaranda]]---fragrance; [[synonyms:v:vāyuḥ]]---breeze; [[synonyms:a:antargataḥ]]---entered within; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:v:vivareṇa]]---through their nostrils; [[synonyms:c:cakāra]]---made; [[synonyms:t:teṣām]]---of the Kumāras; [[synonyms:s:saṅkṣobham]]---agitation for change; [[synonyms:a:akṣara]]-[[synonyms:j:juṣām]]---attached to impersonal Brahman realization; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even though; [[synonyms:c:citta]]-[[synonyms:t:tanvoḥ]]---in both mind and body.
translation: “ 'When the breeze carrying the aroma of tulasī leaves and saffron from the lotus feet of the lotus-eyed Personality of Godhead entered through the nostrils into the hearts of those sages [the Kumāras], they experienced a change in both body and mind, even though they were attached to impersonal Brahman understanding.'
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:15:43|(3.15.43)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.116
description: "By the mercy of Śrīla Vyāsadeva, Śukadeva Gosvāmī was attracted by the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Being thus attracted by Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities, he also became a devotee and engaged in His service.
text:
> vyāsa-kṛpāya śukadevera līlādi-smaraṇa
> kṛṣṇa-guṇākṛṣṭa hañā karena bhajana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpāya]]---by the mercy of Śrīla Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:ś:śukadevera]]---of Śukadeva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---remembrance of the transcendental pastimes of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]]---attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---performed; [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---loving service.
translation: "By the mercy of Śrīla Vyāsadeva, Śukadeva Gosvāmī was attracted by the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Being thus attracted by Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities, he also became a devotee and engaged in His service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.117
description: " 'Being very much attracted by the transcendental pastimes of the Lord, the mind of Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī was agitated by Kṛṣṇa consciousness. He therefore began to study Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam by the grace of his father.'
text:
> harer guṇākṣipta-matir
> bhagavān bādarāyaṇiḥ
> adhyagān mahad-ākhyānaṁ
> nityaṁ viṣṇu-jana-priyaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṣipta]]-[[synonyms:m:matiḥ]]---whose mind was agitated by the qualities; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the most powerful transcendentalist; [[synonyms:b:bādarāyaṇiḥ]]---Śukadeva, son of Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:a:adhyagāt]]---studied; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākhyānam]]---the great epic description; [[synonyms:n:nityam]]---eternally; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]-[[synonyms:p:priyaḥ]]---who is very dear to the Vaiṣṇavas, devotees of Lord Viṣṇu.
translation: “ 'Being very much attracted by the transcendental pastimes of the Lord, the mind of Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī was agitated by Kṛṣṇa consciousness. He therefore began to study Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam by the grace of his father.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:7:11|(1.7.11)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.118
description: "From their very births, the nine great mystic yogīs [Yogendras] were impersonal philosophers of the Absolute Truth. However, because they heard about Lord Kṛṣṇa's qualities from Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and the great sage Nārada, they also became Kṛṣṇa's devotees.
text:
> nava-yogīśvara janma haite 'sādhaka' jñānī
> vidhi-śiva-nārada-mukhe kṛṣṇa-guṇa śuni'
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nava]]---nine; [[synonyms:y:yogi]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---great saintly //yogīs//; [[synonyms:j:janma]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the very birth; [[synonyms:s:sādhaka]]---practicers; [[synonyms:j:jñānī]]---well versed in transcendental knowledge; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:n:nārada]]---the great sage Nārada; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in their mouths; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "From their very births, the nine great mystic yogīs [Yogendras] were impersonal philosophers of the Absolute Truth. However, because they heard about Lord Kṛṣṇa's qualities from Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and the great sage Nārada, they also became Kṛṣṇa's devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.119
description: "In the Eleventh Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam there is a full description of the devotional service of the nine Yogendras, who rendered devotional service because they were attracted by the Lord's transcendental qualities.
text:
> guṇākṛṣṭa hañā kare kṛṣṇera bhajana
> ekādaśa-skandhe tāṅra bhakti-vivaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being attracted by the transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---engaged in; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---the devotional service of the Lord; [[synonyms:e:ekādaśa]]-[[synonyms:s:skandhe]]---in the Eleventh Canto of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of them; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---description of the devotional service.
translation: "In the Eleventh Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam there is a full description of the devotional service of the nine Yogendras, who rendered devotional service because they were attracted by the Lord's transcendental qualities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.12
description: " 'The following are synonyms of the word ātmā: the body, mind, Absolute Truth, natural characteristics, firmness, intelligence and endeavor.'
text:
> "ātmā deha-mano-brahma-svabhāva-dhṛti-buddhiṣu
> prayatne ca" iti   xxx
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the word //ātmā//; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---the body; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]---the mind; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---nature; [[synonyms:d:dhṛti]]---firmness; [[synonyms:b:buddhiṣu]]---in the sense of intelligence; [[synonyms:p:prayatne]]---in endeavor; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus.
translation: “ 'The following are synonyms of the word ātmā: the body, mind, Absolute Truth, natural characteristics, firmness, intelligence and endeavor.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.120
description: " 'The nine Yogendras entered Lord Brahmā's association and heard from him the real meaning of the topmost Vedic literatures—the Upaniṣads. Although they were already conversant in Vedic knowledge, they became very jubilant in Kṛṣṇa consciousness just by listening to Brahmā. Thus they wanted to enter Dvārakā, the abode of Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way they finally achieved the place known as Raṅga-kṣetra.'
text:
> akleśāṁ kamala-bhuvaḥ praviśya goṣṭhīṁ
> kurvantaḥ śruti-śirasāṁ śrutiṁ śrutajñāḥ
> uttuṅgaṁ yadu-pura-saṅgamāya raṅgaṁ
> yogīndrāḥ pulaka-bhṛto navāpy avāpuḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:akleśām]]---without material trouble; [[synonyms:k:kamala]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvaḥ]]---of Lord Brahmā, who took his birth from the lotus flower; [[synonyms:p:praviśya]]---entering; [[synonyms:g:goṣṭhīm]]---the association; [[synonyms:k:kurvantaḥ]]---continuously performing; [[synonyms:ś:śruti]]-[[synonyms:ś:śirasām]]---of the topmost Vedic knowledge; [[synonyms:ś:śrutim]]---hearing; [[synonyms:ś:śruta]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāḥ]]---who are expert in Vedic knowledge; [[synonyms:u:uttuṅgam]]---very high; [[synonyms:y:yadu]]-[[synonyms:p:pura]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgamāya]]---for going back home, back to Godhead, to Dvārakā; [[synonyms:r:raṅgam]]---to Raṅga-kṣetra; [[synonyms:y:yogīndrāḥ]]---great saintly persons; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]-[[synonyms:b:bhṛtaḥ]]---being spiritually pleased; [[synonyms:n:nava]]---nine; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:a:avāpuḥ]]---achieved.
translation: “ 'The nine Yogendras entered Lord Brahmā's association and heard from him the real meaning of the topmost Vedic literatures---the Upaniṣads. Although they were already conversant in Vedic knowledge, they became very jubilant in Kṛṣṇa consciousness just by listening to Brahmā. Thus they wanted to enter Dvārakā, the abode of Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way they finally achieved the place known as Raṅga-kṣetra.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Mahā Upaniṣad.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.121
description: "Those who wish to merge into the impersonal Brahman are also divided into three categories—those desiring to be liberated, those already liberated and those who have realized Brahman.
text:
> mokṣākāṅkṣī jñānī haya tina-prakāra
> mumukṣu, jīvan-mukta, prāpta-svarūpa āra

translation: "Those who wish to merge into the impersonal Brahman are also divided into three categories---those desiring to be liberated, those already liberated and those who have realized Brahman.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.122
description: "There are many people within this material world who desire liberation, and for this purpose they render devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> 'mumukṣu' jagate aneka saṁsārī jana
> 'mukti' lāgi' bhaktye kare kṛṣṇera bhajana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mumukṣu]]---desiring to be liberated; [[synonyms:j:jagate]]---in this world; [[synonyms:a:aneka]]---many; [[synonyms:s:saṁsārī]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---engaged in material activities; [[synonyms:m:mukti]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for the sake of liberation; [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---in devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---the worship of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "There are many people within this material world who desire liberation, and for this purpose they render devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.123
description: " 'Those who want to be relieved from the material clutches give up the worship of the various demigods, who have fearful bodily features. Such peaceful devotees, who are not envious of the demigods, worship the different forms of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa.'
text:
> mumukṣavo ghora-rūpān
> hitvā bhūta-patīn atha
> nārāyaṇa-kalāḥ śāntā
> bhajanti hy anasūyavaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mumukṣavaḥ]]---those who are perfectly learned, who desire the highest perfection, and who, unlike demons and nondevotees, are never envious of anyone; [[synonyms:g:ghora]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpān]]---demigods with fearful bodily features; [[synonyms:h:hitvā]]---giving up; [[synonyms:b:bhūta]]-[[synonyms:p:patīn]]---the forefathers (//prajāpatis//); [[synonyms:a:atha]]---therefore; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kalāḥ]]---the plenary expansions of Lord Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śāntāḥ]]---very peaceful; [[synonyms:b:bhajanti]]---they worship; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:anasūyavaḥ]]---nonenvious.
translation: “ 'Those who want to be relieved from the material clutches give up the worship of the various demigods, who have fearful bodily features. Such peaceful devotees, who are not envious of the demigods, worship the different forms of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:2:26|(1.2.26)]]. Those who actually want the highest perfection worship Lord Viṣṇu in His different incarnations. Those who are attracted to the materialistic way of life and who are always agitated and full of anxiety worship demigods who appear fierce, demigods like goddess Kālī and Kāla-bhairava (Rudra). The devotees of Kṛṣṇa, however, do not envy the demigods or their worshipers but peacefully render devotional service to the incarnations of Nārāyaṇa instead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.124
description: "If those who are attached to demigod worship fortunately associate with the devotees, their dormant devotional service and appreciation of the Lord's qualities gradually awaken. In this way they also engage in Kṛṣṇa's devotional service and give up the desire for liberation and the desire to merge into the existence of impersonal Brahman.
text:
> sei sabera sādhu-saṅge guṇa sphurāya
> kṛṣṇa-bhajana karāya, 'mumukṣā' chāḍāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:sabera]]---of all those worshipers of different demigods; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---the contact of real devotees; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]] [[synonyms:s:sphurāya]]---awakens the appreciation of transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhajana]] [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---engages in the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mumukṣā]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍāya]]---and causes to give up the desire to be liberated or merge into the impersonal feature of the Lord.
translation: "If those who are attached to demigod worship fortunately associate with the devotees, their dormant devotional service and appreciation of the Lord's qualities gradually awaken. In this way they also engage in Kṛṣṇa's devotional service and give up the desire for liberation and the desire to merge into the existence of impersonal Brahman.
purport: The four Kumāras (Catuḥ-sana), Śukadeva Gosvāmī and the nine Yogendras were absorbed in Brahman realization, and how they became devotees is described herein. There are three kinds of impersonalists---the //mumukṣu// (those desiring liberation), the //jīvan-muktas// (those liberated in this life) and the //prāpta-svarūpas// (those merged in Brahman realization). All three types of //jñānīs// are called //mokṣākāṅkṣīs,// those desiring liberation. By associating with devotees, such people give up the //mumukṣu// principle and render devotional service. The real cause for this change is the association of devotees. This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is meant to attract all types of men, even those who desire things other than the Lord's devotional service. Through the association of devotees, they gradually begin to render devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.125
description: " 'O great learned devotee, although there are many faults in this material world, there is one good opportunity—the association with devotees. Such association brings about great happiness. Due to this good quality, our strong desire to achieve liberation by merging into the Brahman effulgence has become weakened.'
text:
> aho mahātman bahu-doṣa-duṣṭo
> 'py ekena bhāty eṣa bhavo guṇena
> sat-saṅgamākhyena sukhāvahena
> kṛtādya no yena kṛśā mumukṣā
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aho]] [[synonyms:m:mahātman]]---O great devotee; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:d:doṣa]]-[[synonyms:d:duṣṭaḥ]]---infected with varieties of material disease or attachment; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:e:ekena]]---with one; [[synonyms:b:bhāti]]---shines; [[synonyms:e:eṣaḥ]]---this; [[synonyms:b:bhavaḥ]]---birth in this material world; [[synonyms:g:guṇena]]---with a good quality; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgama]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākhyena]]---known as association with devotees; [[synonyms:s:sukhā]]-[[synonyms:ā:āvahena]]---which brings about happiness; [[synonyms:k:kṛtā]]---made; [[synonyms:a:adya]]---now; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---our; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---by which; [[synonyms:k:kṛśā]]---insignificant; [[synonyms:m:mumukṣā]]---the desire for liberation.
translation: “ 'O great learned devotee, although there are many faults in this material world, there is one good opportunity---the association with devotees. Such association brings about great happiness. Due to this good quality, our strong desire to achieve liberation by merging into the Brahman effulgence has become weakened.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.126
description: "By associating with the great saint Nārada, the great sages like Śaunaka and others gave up the desire for liberation and engaged in Kṛṣṇa's devotional service.
text:
> nāradera saṅge śaunakādi muni-gaṇa
> mumukṣā chāḍiyā kailā kṛṣṇera bhajana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nāradera]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---by the association of the great saintly person Nārada; [[synonyms:ś:śaunaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:m:muni]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the great sages headed by Śaunaka Muni; [[synonyms:m:mumukṣā]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍiyā]]---giving up the desire for liberation; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---performed; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---devotional service to Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "By associating with the great saint Nārada, the great sages like Śaunaka and others gave up the desire for liberation and engaged in Kṛṣṇa's devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.127
description: "Simply by meeting Kṛṣṇa or receiving Kṛṣṇa's special favor, one can give up the desire for liberation. Being attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, one can engage in His service.
text:
> kṛṣṇera darśane, kāro kṛṣṇera kṛpāya
> mumukṣā chāḍiyā guṇe bhaje tāṅra pā'ya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:d:darśane]]---simply by meeting Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kāro]]---someone; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpāya]]---by the favor of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mumukṣā]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍiyā]]---giving up the desire for liberation; [[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---being attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---engages in service; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:p:pā'ya]]---at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Simply by meeting Kṛṣṇa or receiving Kṛṣṇa's special favor, one can give up the desire for liberation. Being attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, one can engage in His service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.128
description: " 'In this Dvārakā-dhāma, I am being attracted by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, who is personified spiritual bliss. Simply by seeing Him, I am feeling great happiness. Oh, I have wasted so much time trying to become self-realized through impersonal cultivation. This is a cause for lamentation!'
text:
> asmin sukha-ghana-mūrtau param-
> ātmani vṛṣṇi-pattane sphurati
> ātmārāmatayā me vṛthā
> gato bata ciraṁ kālaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:asmin]]---when this; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:g:ghana]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrtau]]---form of complete happiness; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmani]]---the Supreme Person; [[synonyms:v:vṛṣṇi]]-[[synonyms:p:pattane]]---in Dvārakā-dhāma; [[synonyms:s:sphurati]]---exists; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmatayā]]---by the process of cultivating Brahman realization; [[synonyms:m:me]]---my; [[synonyms:v:vṛthā]]---uselessly; [[synonyms:g:gataḥ]]---wasted; [[synonyms:b:bata]]---alas, what can I say; [[synonyms:c:ciram]]---for a long time; [[synonyms:k:kālaḥ]]---time.
translation: “ 'In this Dvārakā-dhāma, I am being attracted by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, who is personified spiritual bliss. Simply by seeing Him, I am feeling great happiness. Oh, I have wasted so much time trying to become self-realized through impersonal cultivation. This is a cause for lamentation!'
purport: This verse is also found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (3.1.34).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.129
description: "There are many people who are liberated even in this lifetime. Some are liberated by discharging devotional service, and others are liberated through the philosophical speculative process.
text:
> jīvan-mukta' aneka, sei dui bheda jāni
> 'bhaktye jīvan-mukta', jñāne jīvan-mukta' māni
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jīvat]]-[[synonyms:m:mukta]]---liberated in this life; [[synonyms:a:aneka]]---there are many; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---all of them; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---two divisions; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---we consider; [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]] [[synonyms:j:jīvat]]-[[synonyms:m:mukta]]---one liberated in this life by pursuing the process of devotional service; [[synonyms:j:jñāne]] [[synonyms:j:jīvat]]-[[synonyms:m:mukta]]---a person liberated in this life by following the process of philosophical speculation; [[synonyms:m:māni]]---we can understand.
translation: "There are many people who are liberated even in this lifetime. Some are liberated by discharging devotional service, and others are liberated through the philosophical speculative process.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.13
description: "The word ātmārāma refers to one who enjoys these seven items [the Absolute Truth, body, mind, and so on]. Later, I shall enumerate the ātmārāmas.
text:
> ei sāte rame yei, sei ātmārāma-gaṇa
> ātmārāma-gaṇera āge kariba gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:sāte]]---in these seven items; [[synonyms:r:rame]]---enjoy; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---those who; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---they; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---//ātmārāmas//; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the //ātmārāmas//; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---later; [[synonyms:k:kariba]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---shall make a count.
translation: "The word ātmārāma refers to one who enjoys these seven items [the Absolute Truth, body, mind, and so on]. Later, I shall enumerate the ātmārāmas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.130
description: "Those who are liberated by devotional service become more and more attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa. Thus they engage in His service. Those who are liberated by the speculative process eventually fall down again due to offensive activity.
text:
> 'bhaktye jīvan-mukta' guṇākṛṣṭa hañā kṛṣṇa bhaje
> śuṣka-jñāne jīvan-mukta aparādhe adho maje
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]] [[synonyms:j:jīvat]]-[[synonyms:m:mukta]]---persons liberated in this life by discharging devotional service; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---engage in the devotional service of the Lord; [[synonyms:ś:śuṣka]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāne]] [[synonyms:j:jīvat]]-[[synonyms:m:mukta]]---so-called liberated in this life by dry, speculative knowledge; [[synonyms:a:aparādhe]]---by offenses; [[synonyms:a:adho]] [[synonyms:m:maje]]---fall down.
translation: "Those who are liberated by devotional service become more and more attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa. Thus they engage in His service. Those who are liberated by the speculative process eventually fall down again due to offensive activity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.131
description: " 'O lotus-eyed one, those who think they are liberated in this life but are without devotional service to You are of impure intelligence. Although they accept severe austerities and penances and rise to the spiritual position, to impersonal Brahman realization, they fall down again because they neglect to worship Your lotus feet.'
text:
> ye 'nye 'ravindākṣa vimukta-māninas
> tvayy asta-bhāvād aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ
> āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ
> patanty adho 'nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]---all those who; [[synonyms:a:anye]]---others (nondevotees); [[synonyms:a:aravinda]]-[[synonyms:a:akṣa]]---O lotus-eyed one; [[synonyms:v:vimukta]]-[[synonyms:m:māninaḥ]]---who consider themselves liberated; [[synonyms:t:tvayi]]---unto You; [[synonyms:a:asta]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvāt]]---without devotion; [[synonyms:a:aviśuddha]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhayaḥ]]---whose intelligence is not purified; [[synonyms:ā:āruhya]]---having ascended; [[synonyms:k:kṛcchreṇa]]---by severe austerities and penances; [[synonyms:p:param]] [[synonyms:p:padam]]---to the supreme position; [[synonyms:t:tataḥ]]---from there; [[synonyms:p:patanti]]---fall; [[synonyms:a:adhaḥ]]---down; [[synonyms:a:anādṛta]]---without respecting; [[synonyms:y:yuṣmat]]---Your; [[synonyms:a:aṅghrayaḥ]]---lotus feet.
translation: “ 'O lotus-eyed one, those who think they are liberated in this life but are without devotional service to You are of impure intelligence. Although they accept severe austerities and penances and rise to the spiritual position, to impersonal Brahman realization, they fall down again because they neglect to worship Your lotus feet.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:10:2:32|(10.2.32)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.132
description: " 'One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and is fully joyful. Be never laments nor desires to have anything; he is equally disposed to every living entity. In that state he attains pure devotional service unto Me.'
text:
> brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā
> na śocati na kāṅkṣati
> samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu
> mad-bhaktiṁ labhate parām
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūtaḥ]]---being one with the Absolute; [[synonyms:p:prasanna]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---fully joyful; [[synonyms:n:na]]---never; [[synonyms:ś:śocati]]---laments; [[synonyms:n:na]]---never; [[synonyms:k:kāṅkṣati]]---desires; [[synonyms:s:samaḥ]]---equally disposed; [[synonyms:s:sarveṣu]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhūteṣu]]---to living entities; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktim]]---My devotional service; [[synonyms:l:labhate]]---gains; [[synonyms:p:parām]]---transcendental.
translation: “ 'One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and is fully joyful. Be never laments nor desires to have anything; he is equally disposed to every living entity. In that state he attains pure devotional service unto Me.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:18:54|(Bg. 18.54)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.133
description: " 'Although I was worshiped by those on the path of monism and initiated into self-realization through the yoga system, I am nonetheless forcibly turned into a maidservant by some cunning boy who is always joking with the gopīs.'
text:
> advaita-vīthī-pathikair upāsyāḥ
> svānanda-siṁhāsana-labdha-dīkṣāḥ
> śaṭhena kenāpi vayaṁ haṭhena
> dāsī-kṛtā gopa-vadhū-viṭena
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:v:vīthī]]---of the path of monism; [[synonyms:p:pathikaiḥ]]---by the wanderers; [[synonyms:u:upāsyāḥ]]---worshipable; [[synonyms:s:svānanda]]---of self-realization; [[synonyms:s:siṁhāsana]]---on the throne; [[synonyms:l:labdha]]-[[synonyms:d:dīkṣāḥ]]---being initiated; [[synonyms:ś:śaṭhena]]---by a cheater; [[synonyms:k:kenāpi]]---some; [[synonyms:v:vayam]]---I; [[synonyms:h:haṭhena]]---by force; [[synonyms:d:dāsī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛtā]]---made into a maidservant; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:v:vadhū]]-[[synonyms:v:viṭena]]---engaged in joking with the //gopīs.//
translation: “ 'Although I was worshiped by those on the path of monism and initiated into self-realization through the yoga system, I am nonetheless forcibly turned into a maidservant by some cunning boy who is always joking with the gopīs.'
purport: This is a verse written by Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.134
description: "One who has attained his constitutional position by the strength of devotional service attains a transcendental body even in this lifetime. Being attracted by Lord Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities, one fully engages in service at His lotus feet.
text:
> bhakti-bale 'prāpta-svarūpa' divya-deha pāya
> kṛṣṇa-guṇākṛṣṭa hañā bhaje kṛṣṇa-pā'ya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:b:bale]]---by the strength of devotional service; [[synonyms:p:prāpta]]-[[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---attaining his original status; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:d:deha]]---a transcendental body; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---one gets; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]]---attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---takes to devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pā'ya]]---at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet.
translation: "One who has attained his constitutional position by the strength of devotional service attains a transcendental body even in this lifetime. Being attracted by Lord Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities, one fully engages in service at His lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.135
description: " 'The living entities and other potencies merge in the Mahā-Viṣṇu as the Lord lies down and winds up [destroys] the cosmic manifestation. Liberation means being situated in one's eternal original form, which he attains after giving up the changeable gross and subtle bodies.'
text:
> nirodho 'syānu śayanam
> ātmanaḥ saha śaktibhiḥ
> muktir hitvānyathā-rūpaṁ
> svarūpeṇa vyavasthitiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirodhaḥ]]---winding up; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of this; [[synonyms:a:anu]]---after; [[synonyms:ś:śayanam]]---lying down; [[synonyms:ā:ātmanaḥ]]---of the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:ś:śaktibhiḥ]]---the energies (marginal and external); [[synonyms:m:muktiḥ]]---liberation; [[synonyms:h:hitvā]]---giving up; [[synonyms:a:anyathā]]---other; [[synonyms:r:rūpam]]---form; [[synonyms:s:svarūpeṇa]]---with one's own eternal form; [[synonyms:v:vyavasthitiḥ]]---staying.
translation: “ 'The living entities and other potencies merge in the Mahā-Viṣṇu as the Lord lies down and winds up [destroys] the cosmic manifestation. Liberation means being situated in one's eternal original form, which he attains after giving up the changeable gross and subtle bodies.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:10:6|(2.10.6)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.136
description: "By opposing Kṛṣṇa consciousness, one again becomes conditioned and fearful due to the influence of māyā. By executing devotional service faithfully, one is liberated from māyā.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-bahirmukha-doṣe māyā haite bhaya
> kṛṣṇonmukha bhakti haite māyā-mukta haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bahiḥ]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---of going against Kṛṣṇa consciousness; [[synonyms:d:doṣe]]---by the fault; [[synonyms:m:māyā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the illusory energy; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:u:unmukha]]---in favor of Kṛṣṇa consciousness; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:m:mukta]]---liberated from //māyā//; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---one becomes.
translation: "By opposing Kṛṣṇa consciousness, one again becomes conditioned and fearful due to the influence of māyā. By executing devotional service faithfully, one is liberated from māyā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.137
description: " 'When the living entity is attracted by the material energy that is separate from Kṛṣṇa, he is overpowered by fear. Because he is separated from the Supreme Personality of Godhead by the material energy, his conception of life is reversed. In other words, instead of being the eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa, he becomes Kṛṣṇa's competitor. This is called viparyayaḥ asmṛtiḥ. To nullify this mistake, one who is actually learned and advanced worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead as his spiritual master, worshipful Deity and source of life. Be thus worships the Lord by the process of unalloyed devotional service.'
text:
> bhayaṁ dvitīyābhiniveśataḥ syād
> īśād apetasya viparyayo 'smṛtiḥ
> tan-māyayāto budha ābhajet taṁ
> bhaktyaikayeśaṁ guru-devatātmā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhayam]]---fear; [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]]-[[synonyms:a:abhiniveśataḥ]]---from the misconception of being a product of material energy; [[synonyms:s:syāt]]---arises; [[synonyms:ī:īśāt]]---from the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:apetasya]]---of one who has withdrawn (the conditioned soul); [[synonyms:v:viparyayaḥ]]---reversal of position; [[synonyms:a:asmṛtiḥ]]---no conception of his relationship with the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:m:māyayā]]---because of the illusory energy of the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:a:ataḥ]]---therefore; [[synonyms:b:budhaḥ]]---one who is wise; [[synonyms:ā:ābhajet]]---must worship; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---Him; [[synonyms:b:bhaktyā]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:e:ekayā]]---undiverted to //karma// and //jñāna//; [[synonyms:ī:īśam]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---as the spiritual master; [[synonyms:d:devatā]]---worshipable Lord; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---Supersoul.
translation: “ 'When the living entity is attracted by the material energy that is separate from Kṛṣṇa, he is overpowered by fear. Because he is separated from the Supreme Personality of Godhead by the material energy, his conception of life is reversed. In other words, instead of being the eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa, he becomes Kṛṣṇa's competitor. This is called viparyayaḥ asmṛtiḥ. To nullify this mistake, one who is actually learned and advanced worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead as his spiritual master, worshipful Deity and source of life. Be thus worships the Lord by the process of unalloyed devotional service.'
purport: This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.2.37).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.138
description: " 'This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.'
text:
> daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī
> mama māyā duratyayā
> mām eva ye prapadyante
> māyām etāṁ taranti te
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daivī]]---belonging to the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:e:eṣā]]---this; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mayī]]---made of the three modes; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---My; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---external energy; [[synonyms:d:duratyayā]]---very difficult to surpass; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:p:prapadyante]]---surrender fully; [[synonyms:m:māyām]]---the illusory energy; [[synonyms:e:etām]]---this; [[synonyms:t:taranti]]---cross over; [[synonyms:t:te]]---they.
translation: “ 'This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:7:14|(Bg. 7.14)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.139
description: "One does not attain liberation without rendering devotional service. Liberation is only attained by devotional service.
text: > bhakti vinu mukti nāhi, bhaktye mukti haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:v:vinu]]---without; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---actually by devotional service; [[synonyms:m:mukti]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---liberation is attained.
translation: "One does not attain liberation without rendering devotional service. Liberation is only attained by devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.14
description: "My dear Sanātana, first hear the meanings of the other words, beginning with the word muni. I shall first explain their separate meanings, then combine them.
text:
> 'muni'-ādi śabdera artha śuna, sanātana
> pṛthak pṛthak artha pāche kariba milana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muni]]---the word //muni//; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and the other; [[synonyms:ś:śabdera]]---of the words; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meaning; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---My dear Sanātana; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]] [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---separately; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---after; [[synonyms:k:kariba]] [[synonyms:m:milana]]---I shall combine.
translation: "My dear Sanātana, first hear the meanings of the other words, beginning with the word muni. I shall first explain their separate meanings, then combine them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.140
description: " 'My dear Lord, devotional service unto You is the only auspicious path. If one gives it up simply for speculative knowledge or the understanding that these living beings are spirit souls and the material world is false, he undergoes a great deal of trouble. Be only gains troublesome and inauspicious activities. His actions are like beating a husk that is already devoid of rice. One's labor becomes fruitless.'
text:
> śreyaḥ-sṛtiṁ bhaktim udasya te vibho
> kliśyanti ye kevala-bodha-labdhaye
> teṣām asau kleśala eva śiṣyate
> nānyad yathā sthūla-tuṣāvaghātinām
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śreyaḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:sṛtim]]---the auspicious path of liberation; [[synonyms:b:bhaktim]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:u:udasya]]---giving up; [[synonyms:t:te]]---of You; [[synonyms:v:vibho]]---O my Lord; [[synonyms:k:kliśyanti]]---accept increased difficulties; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---all those persons who; [[synonyms:k:kevala]]---only; [[synonyms:b:bodha]]-[[synonyms:l:labdhaye]]---for obtaining knowledge; [[synonyms:t:teṣām]]---for them; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kleśalaḥ]]---trouble; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---only; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣyate]]---remains; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:anyat]]---anything else; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as much as; [[synonyms:s:sthūla]]---bulky; [[synonyms:t:tuṣa]]---husks of rice; [[synonyms:a:avaghātinām]]---of those beating.
translation: “ 'My dear Lord, devotional service unto You is the only auspicious path. If one gives it up simply for speculative knowledge or the understanding that these living beings are spirit souls and the material world is false, he undergoes a great deal of trouble. Be only gains troublesome and inauspicious activities. His actions are like beating a husk that is already devoid of rice. One's labor becomes fruitless.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.14.4).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.141
description: " 'O lotus-eyed one, those who think they are liberated in this life but are without devotional service to You are of impure intelligence. Although they accept severe austerities and penances and rise to the spiritual position, to impersonal Brahman realization, they fall down again because they neglect to worship Your lotus feet.'
text:
> ye 'nye 'ravindākṣa vimukta-māninas
> tvayy asta-bhāvād aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ
> āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ
> patanty adho 'nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]---all those who; [[synonyms:a:anye]]---others (nondevotees); [[synonyms:a:aravinda]]-[[synonyms:a:akṣa]]---O lotus-eyed one; [[synonyms:v:vimukta]]-[[synonyms:m:māninaḥ]]---who consider themselves liberated; [[synonyms:t:tvayi]]---unto You; [[synonyms:a:asta]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvāt]]---without devotion; [[synonyms:a:aviśuddha]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhayaḥ]]---whose intelligence is not purified; [[synonyms:ā:āruhya]]---having ascended; [[synonyms:k:kṛcchreṇa]]---by severe austerities and penances; [[synonyms:p:param]] [[synonyms:p:padam]]---to the supreme position; [[synonyms:t:tataḥ]]---from there; [[synonyms:p:patanti]]---fall; [[synonyms:a:adhaḥ]]---down; [[synonyms:a:anādṛta]]---without respecting; [[synonyms:y:yuṣmat]]---Your; [[synonyms:a:aṅghrayaḥ]]---lotus feet.
translation: “ 'O lotus-eyed one, those who think they are liberated in this life but are without devotional service to You are of impure intelligence. Although they accept severe austerities and penances and rise to the spiritual position, to impersonal Brahman realization, they fall down again because they neglect to worship Your lotus feet.'
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:10:2:32|(10.2.32)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.142
description: " 'If one simply maintains an official position in the four varṇas and āśramas but does not worship the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu, he falls down from his puffed up position into a hellish condition.'
text:
> ya eṣāṁ puruṣaṁ sākṣād
> ātma-prabhavam īśvaram
> na bhajanty avajānanti
> sthānād bhraṣṭāḥ patanty adhaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:e:eṣām]]---of those divisions of social and spiritual orders; [[synonyms:p:puruṣam]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhavam]]---the source of everyone; [[synonyms:ī:īśvaram]]---the supreme controller; [[synonyms:n:na]]---do not; [[synonyms:b:bhajanti]]---worship; [[synonyms:a:avajānanti]]---or who neglect; [[synonyms:s:sthānāt]]---from their proper place; [[synonyms:b:bhraṣṭāḥ]]---being fallen; [[synonyms:p:patanti]]---fall; [[synonyms:a:adhaḥ]]---downward into hellish conditions.
translation: “ 'If one simply maintains an official position in the four varṇas and āśramas but does not worship the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu, he falls down from his puffed up position into a hellish condition.'
purport: This is also a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.3).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.143
description: "When one is actually liberated by executing devotional service, he always engages in the transcendental loving service of the Lord.
text: > bhaktye mukti pāileha avaśya kṛṣṇere bhajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:p:pāileha]]---if one gets; [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]]---unto Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---renders service.
translation: "When one is actually liberated by executing devotional service, he always engages in the transcendental loving service of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.144
description: " 'Even a liberated soul merged in the impersonal Brahman effulgence is attracted to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. Be thus installs a Deity and renders the Lord service.'
text:
> "muktā api līlayā vigrahaṁ
> kṛtvā bhagavantaṁ bhajante"
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muktāḥ]]---liberated; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:l:līlayā]]---by the pastimes; [[synonyms:v:vigraham]]---the form of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛtvā]]---having installed; [[synonyms:b:bhagavantam]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhajante]]---worship.
translation: “ 'Even a liberated soul merged in the impersonal Brahman effulgence is attracted to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. Be thus installs a Deity and renders the Lord service.'
purport: This is a quotation from Śaṅkarācārya's commentary on the //Nṛsiṁha-tāpanī Upaniṣad.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.145
description: "These six kinds of ātmārāmas engage in the loving service of Kṛṣṇa. The varieties of service are indicated by adding ca, and they also bear the meaning of api, 'indeed.'
text:
> ei chaya ātmārāma kṛṣṇere bhajaya
> pṛthak pṛthak ca-kāre ihā 'api'ra artha kaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:c:chaya]]---all these six; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---transcendentalists; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]] [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---render service to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]] [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---separately; [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:k:kāre]]---in the use of the word //ca//; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---here; [[synonyms:a:'api'ra]]---of the word //api//; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---says.
translation: "These six kinds of ātmārāmas engage in the loving service of Kṛṣṇa. The varieties of service are indicated by adding ca, and they also bear the meaning of api, 'indeed.'
purport: There are six kinds of //ātmārāmas:// the neophyte (//sādhaka//) student who is absorbed in Brahman realization (//brahmamaya//), one who has already attained the Brahman position (//prāpta-brahma-laya//), one who desires to be liberated (//mumukṣu//), one who is liberated even in this life (//jīvan-mukta//), and one who is self-realized (//prāpta-svarūpa//).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.146
description: "The six kinds of ātmārāmas render devotional service to Kṛṣṇa without ulterior motives. The words munayaḥ and santaḥ indicate those who are very attached to meditating upon Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> "ātmārāmāś ca api" kare kṛṣṇe ahaitukī bhakti
> "munayaḥ santaḥ" iti kṛṣṇa-manane āsakti
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---self-realized persons also; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:ahaitukī]] [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---unmotivated devotional service; [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]] [[synonyms:s:santaḥ]]---great saintly persons and transcendentalists; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:manane]]---in meditation on Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āsakti]]---attraction.
translation: "The six kinds of ātmārāmas render devotional service to Kṛṣṇa without ulterior motives. The words munayaḥ and santaḥ indicate those who are very attached to meditating upon Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.147
description: "The word nirgranthāḥ means 'without ignorance' and 'devoid of rules and regulations.' Whichever meaning fits may be applied.
text:
> "nirgranthāḥ"---avidyā-hīna, keha---vidhi-hīna
> yāhāṅ yei yukta, sei arthera adhīna
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirgranthāḥ]]---//nirgranthāḥ//; [[synonyms:a:avidyā]]-[[synonyms:h:hīna]]---without ignorance; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---some of them; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]-[[synonyms:h:hīna]]---without following any regulative principles; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---which; [[synonyms:y:yukta]]---appropriate; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:a:arthera]] [[synonyms:a:adhīna]]---comes under that different import.
translation: "The word nirgranthāḥ means 'without ignorance' and 'devoid of rules and regulations.' Whichever meaning fits may be applied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.148
description: "By using the word ca in different places, there are different meanings. Over and above them, there is another meaning that is very important.
text:
> ca-śabde kari yadi'itaretara' artha
> āra eka artha kahe parama samartha
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ca//; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I do; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:i:itaretara]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---different and separate meanings; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---is said; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:s:samartha]]---highly suitable.
translation: "By using the word ca in different places, there are different meanings. Over and above them, there is another meaning that is very important.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.149
description: "Although the words ātmārāmāś ca would be repeated six times, simply by adding the word ca, five ātmārāmas are deleted.
text:
> "ātmārāmāś ca ātmārāmāś ca" kari' bāra chaya
> pañca ātmārāma chaya ca-kāre lupta haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]] [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---repeating the words //ātmārāmāḥ// and //ca//; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:b:bāra]] [[synonyms:c:chaya]]---six times; [[synonyms:p:pañca]] [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---five kinds of //ātmārāmas//; [[synonyms:c:chaya]]---six; [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:k:kāre]]---by the word //ca//; [[synonyms:l:lupta]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---become unpronounced.
translation: "Although the words ātmārāmāś ca would be repeated six times, simply by adding the word ca, five ātmārāmas are deleted.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.15
description: "The word muni refers to one who is thoughtful, one who is grave or silent, an ascetic, one who keeps great vows, one in the renounced order, a saint. These are the different meanings of the word muni.
text:
> 'muni'-śabde manana-śīla, āra kahe maunī
> tapasvī vratī, yati, āra ṛṣi, muni
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muni]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //muni//; [[synonyms:m:manana]]-[[synonyms:ś:śīla]]---who is thoughtful; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it means; [[synonyms:m:maunī]]---one who is silent; [[synonyms:t:tapasvī]]---an ascetic; [[synonyms:v:vratī]]---one who keeps great vows; [[synonyms:y:yati]]---one in the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣi]]---a saintly person; [[synonyms:m:muni]]---they are called //muni.//
translation: "The word muni refers to one who is thoughtful, one who is grave or silent, an ascetic, one who keeps great vows, one in the renounced order, a saint. These are the different meanings of the word muni.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.150
description: "Therefore there is no need to repeat the word ātmārāma. One is sufficient, and that one word indicates six persons.
text:
> eka 'ātmārāma'-śabda avaśeṣa rahe
> eka 'ātmārāma'-śabde chaya-jana kahe
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---//ātmārāma//; [[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---vibration; [[synonyms:a:avaśeṣa]] [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains at last; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---one //ātmārāma//; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by vibrating; [[synonyms:c:chaya]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---six persons; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---are indicated.
translation: "Therefore there is no need to repeat the word ātmārāma. One is sufficient, and that one word indicates six persons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.151
description: " 'Of words having the same form and case termination, the last one is the only one retained. For example, the word rāmaḥ is used to stand for rāmaś ca, rāmaś ca, rāmaś ca, etc.'
text:
> "sarūpāṇām eka-śeṣa eka-vibhaktau"
> uktārthānām aprayogaḥ
> rāmaś ca rāmaś ca rāmaś ca rāmā itivat
