synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpāṇām]]---of words of the same form; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śeṣaḥ]]---only the last; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:v:vibhaktau]]---in the same case; [[synonyms:u:ukta]]-[[synonyms:a:arthānām]]---of the previously spoken meanings; [[synonyms:a:aprayogaḥ]]---nonapplication; [[synonyms:r:rāmaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and Rāma; [[synonyms:r:rāmaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and Rāma; [[synonyms:r:rāmaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and Rāma; [[synonyms:r:rāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:i:itivat]]---in this way, by one //rāma,// many //rāmas// are indicated.
translation: “ 'Of words having the same form and case termination, the last one is the only one retained. For example, the word rāmaḥ is used to stand for rāmaś ca, rāmaś ca, rāmaś ca, etc.'
purport: This is a quotation from Pāṇini's //sūtras// (1.2.64).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.152
description: "By the aggregate use of the word ca, it is indicated that all the ātmārāmas and saints serve and worship Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> tabe ye ca-kāra, sei 'samuccaya' kaya
> "ātmārāmāś ca munayaś ca" kṛṣṇere bhajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---that; [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:k:kāra]]---syllable //ca//; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:s:samuccaya]]---aggregation; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---is said; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---all those who enjoy in the self; [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---all saintly persons; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]] [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---worship Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "By the aggregate use of the word ca, it is indicated that all the ātmārāmas and saints serve and worship Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.153
description: "Api added to the word nirgranthāḥ is used for exposition. Thus I have tried to clarify the seven types of meaning.
text:
> "nirgranthā api"ra ei 'api'---sambhāvane
> ei sāta artha prathame kariluṅ vyākhyāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirgranthāḥ]] [[synonyms:a:apira]]---of the words //nirgranthāḥ// api; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:a:api]]---//api//; [[synonyms:s:sambhāvane]]---in the matter of exposition; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:sāta]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---these seven different meanings; [[synonyms:p:prathame]]---in the beginning; [[synonyms:k:kariluṅ]]---I have done; [[synonyms:v:vyākhyāne]]---in explanation.
translation: "Api added to the word nirgranthāḥ is used for exposition. Thus I have tried to clarify the seven types of meaning.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.154
description: "The yogī who worships the Supersoul within himself is also called ātmārāma. There are two types of ātmārāma-yogīs.
text:
> antaryāmi-upāsaka 'ātmārāma' kaya
> sei ātmārāma yogīra dui bheda haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:antaryāmi]]---of the Supersoul; [[synonyms:u:upāsaka]]---worshiper; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]] [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---is also said to be an //ātmārāma//; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---that //ātmārāma//; [[synonyms:y:yogīra]]---of the mystic //yogī//; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bheda]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are two kinds.
translation: "The yogī who worships the Supersoul within himself is also called ātmārāma. There are two types of ātmārāma-yogīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.155
description: "The two ātmārāma-yogīs are called sagarbha and nigarbha. Each of these is divided into three; therefore there are six types of worshipers of the Supersoul.
text:
> sagarbha, nigarbha,---ei haya dui bheda
> eka eka tina bhede chaya vibheda
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sagarbha]]---//sagarbha//; [[synonyms:n:nigarbha]]---//nigarbha//; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---thus; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---different varieties; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:e:eka]]---each one; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:b:bhede]]---in three varieties; [[synonyms:c:chaya]] [[synonyms:v:vibheda]]---therefore there are six varieties.
translation: "The two ātmārāma-yogīs are called sagarbha and nigarbha. Each of these is divided into three; therefore there are six types of worshipers of the Supersoul.
purport: The word //sagarbha-yogī// refers to a //yogī// who worships the Supersoul in the Viṣṇu form. The //nigarbha-yogī// worships the Supersoul without form. The //sagarbha// and //nigarbha yogīs// are further categorized: (1) //sagarbha-yogārurukṣu,// (2) //nigarbha-yogārurukṣu,// (3) //sagarbha-yogārūḍha,// (4) //nigarbha-yogārūḍha,// (5) //sagarbha-prāpta-siddhi// and (6) //nigarbha-prāpta-siddhi.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.156
description: " 'Some yogīs think of the Lord within their hearts as measuring about six inches. The Lord has four hands, in which He holds a conchshell, club, disc and lotus flower. Those who worship this form of Viṣṇu within the heart are called sagarbha-yogīs.'
text:
> kecit svadehāntar hṛdayāvakāśe
> prādeśa-mātraṁ puruṣaṁ vasantam
> catur-bhujaṁ kañja-rathāṅga-śaṅkha-
> gadā-dharaṁ dhāraṇayā smaranti
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kecit]]---some of them; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:d:deha]]-[[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]---within one's own body; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]-[[synonyms:a:avakāśe]]---in the cavity of the heart; [[synonyms:p:prādeśa]]-[[synonyms:m:mātram]]---with the measurement of six inches; [[synonyms:p:puruṣam]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:v:vasantam]]---residing; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:b:bhujam]]---with four hands; [[synonyms:k:kañja]]---a lotus flower; [[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---a disc like the wheel of a chariot; [[synonyms:ś:śaṅkha]]---a conchshell; [[synonyms:g:gadā]]-[[synonyms:d:dharam]]---holding the club; [[synonyms:d:dhāraṇayā]]---by such contemplation; [[synonyms:s:smaranti]]---they remember.
translation: “ 'Some yogīs think of the Lord within their hearts as measuring about six inches. The Lord has four hands, in which He holds a conchshell, club, disc and lotus flower. Those who worship this form of Viṣṇu within the heart are called sagarbha-yogīs.'
purport: This verse is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:2:8|(2.2.8)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.157
description: " 'When one is in ecstatic love with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one's heart is melted by bhakti-yoga, and one feels transcendental bliss. There are bodily symptoms manifest, and, due to eagerness, there are tears in the eyes. Thus one is subjected to spiritual bliss. When the heart is overly afflicted, the meditative mind, like a fishing hook, is gradually separated from the object of meditation.'
text:
> evaṁ harau bhagavati pratilabdha-bhāvo
> bhaktyā dravad-dhṛdaya utpulakaḥ pramodāt
> autkaṇṭhya-bāṣpa-kalayā muhur ardyamānas
> tac cāpi citta-baḍiśaṁ śanakair viyuṅkte
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:evam]]---thus; [[synonyms:h:harau]]---unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhagavati]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:p:pratilabdha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvaḥ]]---one who has awakened a sense of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:b:bhaktyā]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:d:dravat]]---melting; [[synonyms:h:hṛdayaḥ]]---the heart; [[synonyms:u:utpulakaḥ]]---very pleased; [[synonyms:p:pramodāt]]---because of happiness; [[synonyms:a:autkaṇṭhya]]---with eagerness; [[synonyms:b:bāṣpa]]-[[synonyms:k:kalayā]]---with tears in the eyes; [[synonyms:m:muhuḥ]]---always; [[synonyms:a:ardyamānaḥ]]---merged in spiritual bliss; [[synonyms:t:tat]] [[synonyms:c:ca]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---that also; [[synonyms:c:citta]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍiśam]]---with the heart like a fishing hook; [[synonyms:ś:śanakaiḥ]]---gradually; [[synonyms:v:viyuṅkte]]---separates.
translation: “ 'When one is in ecstatic love with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one's heart is melted by bhakti-yoga, and one feels transcendental bliss. There are bodily symptoms manifest, and, due to eagerness, there are tears in the eyes. Thus one is subjected to spiritual bliss. When the heart is overly afflicted, the meditative mind, like a fishing hook, is gradually separated from the object of meditation.'
purport: This is also a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:28:34|(3.28.34)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.158
description: "By these three divisions of advancement in yoga-yogārurukṣu, yogārūḍha and prāpta-siddhi—there are six kinds of mystic yogīs.
text:
> 'yogārurukṣu', 'yogārūḍha' 'prāpta-siddhi' āra
> ei tina bhede haya chaya prakāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yoga]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārurukṣu]]---persons desiring elevation to the platform of yogic perfection; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārūḍha]]---persons already elevated to that position; [[synonyms:p:prāpta]]-[[synonyms:s:siddhi]]---persons who have achieved the success; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:tina]]---these three; [[synonyms:b:bhede]]---by varieties; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:c:chaya]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---six kinds.
translation: "By these three divisions of advancement in yoga-yogārurukṣu, yogārūḍha and prāpta-siddhi---there are six kinds of mystic yogīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.159
description: " 'Those who wish to rise to the platform of yogic perfection practice the yoga system and strictly follow its regulative principles. They practice the yoga postures, āsanas and breathing exercises. Those who are already elevated to this platform practice meditation and keep their minds on the Supreme Lord. They reject all material activity and keep their minds in an equipoised condition [śama].
text:
> ārurukṣor muner yogaṁ
> karma kāraṇam ucyate
> yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva
> śamaḥ kāraṇam ucyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ārurukṣoḥ]]---of a person desiring to rise to the platform of yogic perfection; [[synonyms:m:muneḥ]]---of a saintly person; [[synonyms:y:yogam]]---spiritual knowledge; [[synonyms:k:karma]]---work; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇam]]---the cause; [[synonyms:u:ucyate]]---is said; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārūḍhasya]]---of one who has attained such perfect knowledge; [[synonyms:t:tasya]]---for him; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:ś:śamaḥ]]---controlling the mind without being disturbed; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇam]]---cause; [[synonyms:u:ucyate]]---is said.
translation: “ 'Those who wish to rise to the platform of yogic perfection practice the yoga system and strictly follow its regulative principles. They practice the yoga postures, āsanas and breathing exercises. Those who are already elevated to this platform practice meditation and keep their minds on the Supreme Lord. They reject all material activity and keep their minds in an equipoised condition [śama].
purport: Texts 159 and 160 are from //Bhagavad-gītā// (6.3-4).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.16
description: "The word nirgrantha refers to one who is liberated from the material knots of ignorance. It also refers to one who is devoid of all regulative principles enjoined in the Vedic literature. It also refers to one who does not have knowledge.
text:
> 'nirgrantha'-śabde kahe, avidyā-granthi-hīna
> vidhi-niṣedha-veda-śāstra-jñānādi-vihīna
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirgrantha]]---nirgrantha; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---one means; [[synonyms:a:avidyā]]---of ignorance; [[synonyms:g:granthi]]-[[synonyms:h:hīna]]---without any knot; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]-[[synonyms:n:niṣedha]]---regulative principles of rules and restrictions; [[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---the Vedic literature; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---knowledge, and so on; [[synonyms:v:vihīna]]---without.
translation: "The word nirgrantha refers to one who is liberated from the material knots of ignorance. It also refers to one who is devoid of all regulative principles enjoined in the Vedic literature. It also refers to one who does not have knowledge.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.160
description: " 'When a person is no longer interested in acting for sense gratification and when he renounces all material desires, he is said to be situated in perfect yoga [yogārūḍha].'
text:
> yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu
> na karmasv anuṣajjate
> sarva-saṅkalpa-sannyāsī
> yogārūḍhas tadocyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadā]]---when; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:i:indriya]]-[[synonyms:a:artheṣu]]---sense gratification; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:k:karmasu]]---in activities; [[synonyms:a:anuṣajjate]]---one becomes engaged; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all kinds of; [[synonyms:s:saṅkalpa]]---desires; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---renouncing; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārūḍhaḥ]]---one who has actually attained perfection in the yoga system; [[synonyms:t:tadā]]---at that time; [[synonyms:u:ucyate]]---is said.
translation: “ 'When a person is no longer interested in acting for sense gratification and when he renounces all material desires, he is said to be situated in perfect yoga [yogārūḍha].'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.161
description: "When a purified yogī associates with devotees, he engages in Lord Kṛṣṇa's devotional service, being attracted by the Lord's transcendental qualities.
text:
> ei chaya yogī sādhu-saṅgādi-hetu pāñā
> kṛṣṇa bhaje kṛṣṇa-guṇe ākṛṣṭa hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:c:chaya]]---six; [[synonyms:y:yogī]]---mystics; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]---of devotees; [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the association; [[synonyms:h:hetu]]---because of; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---render service to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]]---attracted; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming.
translation: "When a purified yogī associates with devotees, he engages in Lord Kṛṣṇa's devotional service, being attracted by the Lord's transcendental qualities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.162
description: "The meanings of the words ca and api can be applied here. The meanings of the words muni and nirgrantha are the same as before.
text:
> ca-śabde 'api'ra artha ihāṅo kahaya
> 'muni', 'nirgrantha'-śabdera pūrvavat artha haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ca//; [[synonyms:a:'api'ra]]---of the word //api//; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meaning; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅo]]---here also; [[synonyms:k:kahaya]]---is applicable; [[synonyms:m:muni]]---a saintly person; [[synonyms:n:nirgrantha]]---fully liberated; [[synonyms:ś:śabdera]]---of the words; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---as mentioned above; [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are the meanings.
translation: "The meanings of the words ca and api can be applied here. The meanings of the words muni and nirgrantha are the same as before.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.163
description: "The word ahaitukī is always applicable to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Urukrama. In this way I have described the import of all these things in thirteen complete varieties.
text:
> urukrame ahaitukī kāhāṅ kona artha
> ei tera artha kahiluṅ parama samartha
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:urukrame]]---unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who acts uncommonly; [[synonyms:a:ahaitukī]]---without motives; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---some; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---import; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---in this way; [[synonyms:t:tera]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---thirteen imports; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have explained; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---supremely; [[synonyms:s:samartha]]---complete.
translation: "The word ahaitukī is always applicable to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Urukrama. In this way I have described the import of all these things in thirteen complete varieties.
purport: The thirteen varieties mentioned are (1) //sādhaka,// the neophyte performer; (2) //brahmamaya,// one absorbed in the thought of impersonal Brahman; (3) //prāpta-brahma-laya,// one who has actually attained Brahman perfection; (4) //mumukṣu,// the desirer of liberation; (5) //jīvan-mukta,// one who is liberated in this life; (6) //prāpta-svarūpa,// one who has attained one's original constitutional position; (7) //nirgrantha-muni,// a completely liberated saint; (8) //sagarbha-yogārurukṣu,// a //yogī// meditating upon the four-handed Viṣṇu form or desiring yogic perfection; (9) //nigarbha-yogārurukṣu,// one who has attained perfection in impersonal meditation; (10) //sagarbha-yogārūḍha,// already elevated to the //yoga// perfection platform; (11) //nigarbha-yogārūḍha,// similarly impersonal //yogi;// (12) //sagarbha-prāpta-siddhi,// one who has already attained the perfectional stage; (13) //nigarbha-prāpta-siddhi,// one who has attained perfection by impersonal meditation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.164
description: "These thirteen types of yogīs and munis are called śānta-bhaktas, for they render transcendental loving service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead in the neutral stage.
text:
> ei saba śānta yabe bhaje bhagavān
> 'śānta' bhakta kari' tabe kahi tāṅra nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all these; [[synonyms:ś:śānta]]---neutral; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---worship; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ś:śānta]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotees in the neutral stage of devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---describing as; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---that time; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I speak; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---their; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---name.
translation: "These thirteen types of yogīs and munis are called śānta-bhaktas, for they render transcendental loving service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead in the neutral stage.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.165
description: "The word ātmā sometimes means 'the mind.' In this case, the word ātmārāma means 'a person who is satisfied by mental speculation.' When such a person associates with a pure devotee, he takes to devotional service at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> 'ātmā' śabde 'mana' kaha---mane yei rame
> sādhu-saṅge seha bhaje śrī-kṛṣṇa-caraṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---ātmā; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---if you say; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---within the mind; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:r:rame]]---one who is satisfied by speculation; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---by the association of devotees; [[synonyms:s:seha]]---he also; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---takes to devotional service; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "The word ātmā sometimes means 'the mind.' In this case, the word ātmārāma means 'a person who is satisfied by mental speculation.' When such a person associates with a pure devotee, he takes to devotional service at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.166
description: " 'Those who follow the path of great, saintly mystic yogīs take to the yogic gymnastic process and begin worshiping from the abdomen, where it is said that Brahman is located. Such people are called śārkarākṣa, which means that they are situated in the gross bodily conception. There are also followers of the ṛṣi known as Āruṇa. Following that path, they observe the activities of the arteries. Thus they gradually rise to the heart, where subtle Brahman, Paramātmā, is situated. They then worship Him. O unlimited Ananta! Better than these persons are the mystic yogīs who worship You from the top of their heads. Beginning with the abdomen and proceeding through the heart, they reach the top of the head and pass through the brahma-randhra, the hole at the top of the skull. Thus yogīs attain the perfectional platform and do not enter the cycle of birth and death again.'
text:
> udaram upāsate ya ṛṣi-vartmasu kūrpa-dṛśaḥ
> parisara-paddhatiṁ hṛdayam āruṇayo daharam
> tata udagād ananta tava dhāma śiraḥ paramaṁ
> punar iha yat sametya na patanti kṛtānta-mukhe
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:udaram]]---the abdomen*; [[synonyms:u:upāsate]]---worship; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣi]]-[[synonyms:v:vartmasu]]---on the path marked out by the great saintly persons; [[synonyms:k:kūrpa]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛśaḥ]]---whose vision is grossly situated in the bodily conception of life; [[synonyms:p:parisara]]-[[synonyms:p:paddhatim]]---from which the system of the arteries comes; [[synonyms:h:hṛdayam]]---the heart; [[synonyms:ā:āruṇayaḥ]]---saintly persons headed by Āruṇa Ṛṣi; [[synonyms:d:daharam]]---the sky within the heart, the subtle conception of the Supersoul within the heart; [[synonyms:t:tataḥ]]---from that; [[synonyms:u:udagāt]]---went up; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---O unlimited one; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---place; [[synonyms:ś:śiraḥ]]---the top of the head; [[synonyms:p:paramam]]---supreme; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---in this material world; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:s:sametya]]---having achieved; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:p:patanti]]---fall down; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:anta]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the repetition of birth and death.
translation: “ 'Those who follow the path of great, saintly mystic yogīs take to the yogic gymnastic process and begin worshiping from the abdomen, where it is said that Brahman is located. Such people are called śārkarākṣa, which means that they are situated in the gross bodily conception. There are also followers of the ṛṣi known as Āruṇa. Following that path, they observe the activities of the arteries. Thus they gradually rise to the heart, where subtle Brahman, Paramātmā, is situated. They then worship Him. O unlimited Ananta! Better than these persons are the mystic yogīs who worship You from the top of their heads. Beginning with the abdomen and proceeding through the heart, they reach the top of the head and pass through the brahma-randhra, the hole at the top of the skull. Thus yogīs attain the perfectional platform and do not enter the cycle of birth and death again.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.87.18).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.167
description: "Being attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, yogīs become great saints. At that time, not being hampered by the yogic process, they engage in unalloyed devotional service.
text:
> eho kṛṣṇa-guṇākṛṣṭa mahā-muni hañā
> ahaitukī bhakti kare nirgrantha hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eho]]---such //yogīs//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]]---attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:m:muni]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming great saintly persons; [[synonyms:a:ahaitukī]] [[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---they perform causeless devotional service; [[synonyms:n:nirgrantha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming indifferent to the mystic //yoga// process.
translation: "Being attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, yogīs become great saints. At that time, not being hampered by the yogic process, they engage in unalloyed devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.168
description: "Ātmā also means 'endeavor.' Being attracted by Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities, some saints make a great endeavor to come to the point of rendering service to Him.
text:
> 'ātmā'-śabde 'yatna' kahe---yatna kariyā
> "munayo 'pi" kṛṣṇa bhaje guṇākṛṣṭa hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ātmā//; [[synonyms:y:yatna]]---endeavor; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---one means; [[synonyms:y:yatna]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---by great endeavor; [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---even great saintly persons; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---take to the devotional service of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being attracted by His transcendental qualities.
translation: "Ātmā also means 'endeavor.' Being attracted by Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities, some saints make a great endeavor to come to the point of rendering service to Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.169
description: " 'The transcendental position cannot be attained by wandering up and down from Brahmaloka and Satyaloka to Pātālaloka. If one is actually intelligent and learned, he should endeavor for that rare transcendental position. Whatever material happiness is available within the fourteen worlds is attained by the force of time, just as one attains distress in due course of time. Since these are not attained by spiritual consciousness, one should not try for them.'
text:
> tasyaiva hetoḥ prayateta kovido
> na labhyate yad bhramatām upary adhaḥ
> tal labhyate duḥkhavad anyataḥ sukhaṁ
> kālena sarvatra gabhīra-raṁhasā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tasya]] [[synonyms:e:eva]]---for that; [[synonyms:h:hetoḥ]]---reason; [[synonyms:p:prayateta]]---should endeavor; [[synonyms:k:kovidaḥ]]---one who is learned and intelligent; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:l:labhyate]]---is achieved; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---that which; [[synonyms:b:bhramatām]]---of those wandering; [[synonyms:u:upari]] [[synonyms:a:adhaḥ]]---up and down; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:l:labhyate]]---is achieved; [[synonyms:d:duḥkhavat]]---exactly like unhappiness or distress; [[synonyms:a:anyataḥ]]---from other reasons (one's past actions); [[synonyms:s:sukham]]---happiness; [[synonyms:k:kālena]]---by time; [[synonyms:s:sarvatra]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:g:gabhīra]]---insurmountable; [[synonyms:r:raṁhasā]]---having force.
translation: “ 'The transcendental position cannot be attained by wandering up and down from Brahmaloka and Satyaloka to Pātālaloka. If one is actually intelligent and learned, he should endeavor for that rare transcendental position. Whatever material happiness is available within the fourteen worlds is attained by the force of time, just as one attains distress in due course of time. Since these are not attained by spiritual consciousness, one should not try for them.'
purport: This verse was spoken by Nārada Muni in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:5:18|(1.5.18)]]. Nārada Muni was speaking to Vyāsadeva, who was morose even after he had compiled all Vedic literatures. In this connection, Nārada Muni advised Śrīla Vyāsadeva to attain devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.17
description: "Nirgrantha also refers to one who is illiterate, lowborn, misbehaved, unregulated and devoid of respect for Vedic literature. The word also refers to one who is a capitalist and to one who has no riches.
text:
> mūrkha, nīca, mleccha ādi śāstra-rikta-gaṇa
> dhana-sañcayī---nirgrantha, āra ye nirdhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]]---foolish, illiterate persons; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]---lowborn; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]---unclean persons with no principles; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and others; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:r:rikta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---persons devoid of all regulative principles stated in //śāstra//; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]-[[synonyms:s:sañcayī]]---capitalist (one who gathers wealth); [[synonyms:n:nirgrantha]]---called //nirgrantha//; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:n:nirdhana]]---without riches.
translation: "Nirgrantha also refers to one who is illiterate, lowborn, misbehaved, unregulated and devoid of respect for Vedic literature. The word also refers to one who is a capitalist and to one who has no riches.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.170
description: " 'Those who are anxious to awaken their spiritual consciousness, who have unflinching intelligence and who are not deviated, certainly attain the desired goal of life.'
text:
> sad-dharmasyāvabodhāya
> yeṣāṁ nirbandhinī matiḥ
> acirād eva sarvārthaḥ
> sidhyaty eṣām abhīpsitaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:d:dharmasya]]---of the path of progressive devotional service; [[synonyms:a:avabodhāya]]---for understanding; [[synonyms:y:yeṣām]]---those whose; [[synonyms:n:nirbandhinī]]---unflinching; [[synonyms:m:matiḥ]]---intelligence; [[synonyms:a:acirāt]]---very soon; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:a:arthaḥ]]---the goal of life; [[synonyms:s:sidhyati]]---becomes fulfilled; [[synonyms:e:eṣām]]---of these persons; [[synonyms:a:abhīpsitaḥ]]---desired.
translation: “ 'Those who are anxious to awaken their spiritual consciousness, who have unflinching intelligence and who are not deviated, certainly attain the desired goal of life.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Nāradīya Purāṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.171
description: "The word ca may be used in place of api, which gives emphasis to something. Thus it means that without sincere endeavor in devotional service, one cannot attain love of Godhead.
text:
> ca-śabda api-arthe, 'api'---avadhāraṇe
> yatnāgraha vinā bhakti nā janmāya preme
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---the word //ca//; [[synonyms:a:api]]---of the word //api//; [[synonyms:a:arthe]]---in the meaning; [[synonyms:a:api]] [[synonyms:a:avadhāraṇe]]---this //api// is used in sense of emphasis; [[synonyms:y:yatna]]-[[synonyms:ā:āgraha]] [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without sincere endeavor; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:j:janmāya]]---begets; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---love of Godhead.
translation: "The word ca may be used in place of api, which gives emphasis to something. Thus it means that without sincere endeavor in devotional service, one cannot attain love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.172
description: " 'Devotional perfection is very difficult to attain for two reasons. First, unless one is attached to Kṛṣṇa, he cannot attain devotional perfection even if he renders devotional service for a long time. Second, Kṛṣṇa does not easily deliver perfection in devotional service.'
text:
> sādhanaughair anāsaṅgair
> alabhyā sucirād api
> hariṇā cāśv adeyeti
> dvidhā sā syāt sudurlabhā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---activities of devotional service; [[synonyms:a:aughaiḥ]]---by masses of; [[synonyms:a:anāsaṅgaiḥ]]---without attachment; [[synonyms:a:alabhyā]]---very difficult to achieve; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:c:cirāt]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---even after a considerable duration of time; [[synonyms:h:hariṇā]]---by the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:ā:āśu]]---very soon; [[synonyms:a:adeyā]]---not to be delivered; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:d:dvidhā]]---two ways; [[synonyms:s:sā]]---that; [[synonyms:s:syāt]]---is; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:d:durlabhā]]---very difficult to obtain.
translation: “ 'Devotional perfection is very difficult to attain for two reasons. First, unless one is attached to Kṛṣṇa, he cannot attain devotional perfection even if he renders devotional service for a long time. Second, Kṛṣṇa does not easily deliver perfection in devotional service.'
purport: As stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:5:6:18|(5.6.18)]]: //muktiṁ dadāti karhicit.// Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī told Mahārāja Parīkṣit that Kṛṣṇa readily grants liberation but does not very readily grant perfection in devotional service. This means that Kṛṣṇa wants to see that a devotee is actually sincere and serious and that he does not have ulterior motives. If this is the case, devotional service can very easily be successful; otherwise it is very difficult to obtain from the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This verse appears in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.1.35).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.173
description: " 'To those who are constantly devoted and worship Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.'
text:
> teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ
> bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam
> dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ
> yena mām upayānti te
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:teṣām]]---to them; [[synonyms:s:satata]]-[[synonyms:y:yuktānām]]---always engaged; [[synonyms:b:bhajatām]]---in devotional service; [[synonyms:p:prīti]]-[[synonyms:p:pūrvakam]]---in loving ecstasy; [[synonyms:d:dadāmi]]---I give; [[synonyms:b:buddhi]]-[[synonyms:y:yogam]]---real intelligence; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---that; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---by which; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:u:upayānti]]---come; [[synonyms:t:te]]---they.
translation: “ 'To those who are constantly devoted and worship Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:10:10|(Bg. 10.10)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.174
description: "Another meaning of ātmā is dhṛti, or endurance. A person who endeavors with endurance is ātmārāma. With endurance, such a person engages in devotional service.
text:
> 'ātmā'-śabde 'dhṛti' kahe,---dhairye yei rame
> dhairyavanta eva hañā karaya bhajane
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ātmā//; [[synonyms:d:dhṛti]]---perseverance; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it is said; [[synonyms:d:dhairye]]---with perseverance; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:r:rame]]---anyone who endeavors; [[synonyms:d:dhairyavanta]]---such persons with endurance; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:k:karaya]]---perform; [[synonyms:b:bhajane]]---devotional service.
translation: "Another meaning of ātmā is dhṛti, or endurance. A person who endeavors with endurance is ātmārāma. With endurance, such a person engages in devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.175
description: "The word muni also means 'bird,' and 'bumblebee.' The word nirgrantha refers to foolish people. By the mercy of Kṛṣṇa, such creatures contact a sādhu [spiritual master] and thus engage in devotional service.
text:
> 'muni'-śabde---pakṣī, bhṛṅga; 'nirgranthe'---mūrkha-jana
> kṛṣṇa-kṛpāya sādhu-kṛpāya doṅhāra bhajana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muni]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //muni//; [[synonyms:p:pakṣī]]---bird; [[synonyms:b:bhṛṅga]]---bumblebee; [[synonyms:n:nirgranthe]]---in the word //nirgrantha//; [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---foolish people; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpāya]]---by the mercy of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpāya]]---by the mercy of a devotee; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---engages in devotional service of both (Kṛṣṇa and his spiritual master or the //sādhu//).
translation: "The word muni also means 'bird,' and 'bumblebee.' The word nirgrantha refers to foolish people. By the mercy of Kṛṣṇa, such creatures contact a sādhu [spiritual master] and thus engage in devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.176
description: " 'My dear mother, in this forest, all the birds, after rising on the beautiful branches of the trees, are closing their eyes and, not being attracted by any other sound, are simply listening to the vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute. Such birds and bees must be on the same level as great saints.'
text:
> prāyo batāmba munayo vihagā vane 'smin
> kṛṣṇekṣitaṁ tad-uditaṁ kala-veṇu-gītam
> āruhya ye druma-bhujān rucira-prabālān
> śṛṇvanti mīlita-dṛśo vigatānya-vācaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prāyaḥ]]---almost; [[synonyms:b:bata]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:amba]]---O mother; [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]]---great sages; [[synonyms:v:vihagāḥ]]---the birds; [[synonyms:v:vane]]---in the forest; [[synonyms:a:asmin]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ī:īkṣitam]]---seeing the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:u:uditam]]---created by Him; [[synonyms:k:kala]]-[[synonyms:v:veṇu]]-[[synonyms:g:gītam]]---sweet vibrations made by playing the flute; [[synonyms:ā:āruhya]]---rising; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---all of them; [[synonyms:d:druma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhujān]]---to the branches of the trees; [[synonyms:r:rucira]]-[[synonyms:p:prabālān]]---having beautiful creepers and twigs; [[synonyms:ś:śṛṇvanti]]---hear; [[synonyms:m:mīlita]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛśaḥ]]---closing their eyes; [[synonyms:v:vigata]]-[[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:v:vācaḥ]]---stopping all other sounds.
translation: “ 'My dear mother, in this forest, all the birds, after rising on the beautiful branches of the trees, are closing their eyes and, not being attracted by any other sound, are simply listening to the vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute. Such birds and bees must be on the same level as great saints.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.21.14). This statement was made by the //gopīs,// who were lamenting in separation from Kṛṣṇa and studying how the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana were enjoying life like saintly persons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.177
description: " 'O good fortune personified! O original Personality of Godhead, all these bees are chanting about Your transcendental fame, which will purify the entire universe. Indeed, they are following Your path in the forest and are worshiping You. Actually they are all saintly persons, but now they have taken the form of bees. Although You are playing like a human being, they could not forget that You are their worshipable Deity.'
text:
> ete 'linas tava yaśo 'khila-loka-tīrthaṁ
> gāyanta ādi-puruṣānupathaṁ bhajante
> prāyo amī muni-gaṇā bhavadīya-mukhyā
> gūḍhaṁ vane 'pi na jahaty anaghātma-daivam
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ete]]---all these; [[synonyms:a:alinaḥ]]---bees; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:y:yaśaḥ]]---reputation; [[synonyms:a:akhila]]---all; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrtham]]---auspicious for the planets; [[synonyms:g:gāyante]]---are singing; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]---O original person; [[synonyms:a:anupatham]]---along the path; [[synonyms:b:bhajante]]---they are engaged in transcendental loving service; [[synonyms:p:prāyaḥ]]---almost; [[synonyms:a:amī]]---these; [[synonyms:m:muni]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇāḥ]]---great saintly persons; [[synonyms:b:bhavadīya]]---in relation with You; [[synonyms:m:mukhyāḥ]]---very advanced devotees; [[synonyms:g:gūḍham]]---unknown; [[synonyms:v:vane]]---in the forest; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jahati]]---give up; [[synonyms:a:anagha]]---O personality of transcendental goodness; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:d:daivam]]---their worshipable Deity.
translation: “ 'O good fortune personified! O original Personality of Godhead, all these bees are chanting about Your transcendental fame, which will purify the entire universe. Indeed, they are following Your path in the forest and are worshiping You. Actually they are all saintly persons, but now they have taken the form of bees. Although You are playing like a human being, they could not forget that You are their worshipable Deity.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.15.6). Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma were just on the verge of boyhood and were entering the forest of Vṛndāvana when Kṛṣṇa began to offer prayers to please Balarāma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.178
description: " 'All the cranes and swans in the water are being enchanted by the melodious song of Kṛṣṇa's flute. They have approached and are worshiping the Supreme Personality of Godhead with full attention. Alas, they are closing their eyes and are becoming completely silent.'
text:
> sarasi sārasa-haṁsa-vihaṅgāś
> cāru-gīta-hṛta-cetasa etya
> harim upāsata te yata-cittā
> hanta mīlita-dṛśo dhṛta-maunāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarasi]]---in the water; [[synonyms:s:sārasa]]---cranes; [[synonyms:h:haṁsa]]---swans; [[synonyms:v:vihaṅgāḥ]]---birds; [[synonyms:c:cāru]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]---by the melodious song of Kṛṣṇa's flute; [[synonyms:h:hṛta]]-[[synonyms:c:cetasaḥ]]---devoid of material consciousness; [[synonyms:e:etya]]---coming near; [[synonyms:h:harim]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:u:upāsata]]---worshiped; [[synonyms:t:te]]---all of them; [[synonyms:y:yata]]-[[synonyms:c:cittāḥ]]---with full attention; [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---alas; [[synonyms:m:mīlita]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛśaḥ]]---closing their eyes; [[synonyms:d:dhṛta]]-[[synonyms:m:maunāḥ]]---completely silent.
translation: “ 'All the cranes and swans in the water are being enchanted by the melodious song of Kṛṣṇa's flute. They have approached and are worshiping the Supreme Personality of Godhead with full attention. Alas, they are closing their eyes and are becoming completely silent.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.35.11). In the day, Kṛṣṇa went to the forest of Vṛndāvana, and at that time, the //gopīs,// being morose due to separation from Him, were lamenting in this way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.179
description: " 'Kirāta, Hūna, Āndhra, Pulinda, Pulkaśa, Ābhīra, Śumbha, Yavana and the Khaśa races and even others who are addicted to sinful acts can be purified by taking shelter of the devotees of the Lord due to His being the supreme power. I beg to offer my respectful obeisances unto Him.'
text:
> kirāta-hūnāndhra-pulinda-pulkaśā
> ābhīra-śumbhā yavanāḥ khaśādayaḥ
> ye 'nye ca pāpā yad-upāśrayāśrayāḥ
> śudhyanti tasmai prabhaviṣṇave namaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kirāta]]---the aborigines named Kirātas; [[synonyms:h:hūna]]---the Hūnas; [[synonyms:ā:āndhra]]---Āndhras; [[synonyms:p:pulinda]]---Pulindas; [[synonyms:p:pulkaśāḥ]]---Pulkaśas; [[synonyms:ā:ābhīra]]---Ābhīras; [[synonyms:ś:śumbhāḥ]]---Śumbhas; [[synonyms:y:yavanāḥ]]---persons who do not follow the Vedic injunctions and who eat cow's flesh; [[synonyms:k:khaśa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādayaḥ]]---Khaśas and others; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:a:anye]]---similar others; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:p:pāpāḥ]]---sinful persons; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:u:upāśraya]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āśrayāḥ]]---taking shelter; [[synonyms:ś:śudhyanti]]---become purified; [[synonyms:t:tasmai]]---unto Him, Lord Viṣṇu, because of whom they become purified; [[synonyms:p:prabhaviṣṇave]]---to Lord Viṣṇu, the most powerful; [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---respectful obeisances.
translation: “ 'Kirāta, Hūna, Āndhra, Pulinda, Pulkaśa, Ābhīra, Śumbha, Yavana and the Khaśa races and even others who are addicted to sinful acts can be purified by taking shelter of the devotees of the Lord due to His being the supreme power. I beg to offer my respectful obeisances unto Him.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:4:18|(2.4.18)]]. This verse was spoken by Śukadeva Gosvāmī when Parīkṣit Mahārāja asked him for a description of the creation. While offering obeisances to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śukadeva Gosvāmī described the unlimited potencies of Lord Viṣṇu, who can purify the lowborn creatures mentioned herein.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.18
description: " 'The prefix niḥ may be used for a sense of ascertainment, gradation, construction or forbidding. The word grantha means riches, thesis and composition.'
text:
> nir niścaye niṣ kramārthe
> nir nirmāṇa-niṣedhayoḥ
> grantho dhane 'tha sandarbhe
> varṇa-saṅgrathane 'pi ca
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:niḥ]]---the prefix //niḥ//; [[synonyms:n:niścaye]]---in the sense of ascertainment; [[synonyms:n:niḥ]]---the prefix //niḥ//; [[synonyms:k:krama]]-[[synonyms:a:arthe]]---in the meaning of succession; [[synonyms:n:niḥ]]---the prefix //niḥ//; [[synonyms:n:nirmāṇa]]---in the sense of forming; [[synonyms:n:niṣedhayoḥ]]---in the sense of forbidding; [[synonyms:g:granthaḥ]]---the word //grantha//; [[synonyms:d:dhane]]---in the sense of wealth; [[synonyms:a:atha]]---also; [[synonyms:s:sandarbhe]]---thesis; [[synonyms:v:varṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgrathane]]---in the sense of tying together words; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and.
translation: “ 'The prefix niḥ may be used for a sense of ascertainment, gradation, construction or forbidding. The word grantha means riches, thesis and composition.'
purport: This is another quotation from the //Viśva-prakāśa// dictionary.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.180
description: "The word dhṛti is also used when one is fully perfect in knowledge. When due to having obtained the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he has no material miseries, he attains mahā-pūrṇa, the highest level of perfection.
text:
> kiṁvā'dhṛti'-śabde nija-pūrṇatādi-jñāna kaya
> duḥkhābhāve uttama-prāptye mahā-pūrṇa haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kiṁvā]]---or; [[synonyms:d:dhṛti]]---//dhṛti//; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by this word; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---own; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇatā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---perfection and so on; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---says; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]-[[synonyms:a:abhāve]]---in the absence of all material miseries; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]---the best; [[synonyms:p:prāptye]]---by obtaining; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes perfectly perfect.
translation: "The word dhṛti is also used when one is fully perfect in knowledge. When due to having obtained the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he has no material miseries, he attains mahā-pūrṇa, the highest level of perfection.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.181
description: " 'Dhṛti is the fullness felt by the absence of misery and brought about by receiving knowledge of the Supreme Lord and by obtaining pure love for Him. The lamentation that accrues from not obtaining a goal or by loss of something already attained does not affect this completeness.'
text:
> dhṛtiḥ syāt pūrṇatā jñāna-
> duḥkhābhāvottamāptibhiḥ
> aprāptātīta-naṣṭārthā-
> nabhisaṁśocanādikṛt
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dhṛtiḥ]]---endurance; [[synonyms:s:syāt]]---may become; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇatā]]---fullness; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]-[[synonyms:a:abhāva]]---the absence of misery; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]-[[synonyms:ā:āptibhiḥ]]---by attainment of the highest platform of perfection; [[synonyms:a:aprāpta]]---not obtained; [[synonyms:a:atīta]]---gone; [[synonyms:n:naṣṭa]]---destroyed; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---object, goal; [[synonyms:a:anabhisaṁ]]-[[synonyms:ś:śocana]]---absence of lamentation; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and so on; [[synonyms:k:kṛt]]---doing.
translation: “ 'Dhṛti is the fullness felt by the absence of misery and brought about by receiving knowledge of the Supreme Lord and by obtaining pure love for Him. The lamentation that accrues from not obtaining a goal or by loss of something already attained does not affect this completeness.'
purport: This verse is found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (2.4.144).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.182
description: "A devotee of Kṛṣṇa is never in a miserable condition, nor does he have any desire other than to serve Kṛṣṇa. He is experienced and advanced. He feels the transcendental bliss of love of Kṛṣṇa and always engages in His service fully protected.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-bhakta---duḥkha-hīna, vāñchāntara-hīna
> kṛṣṇa-prema-sevā-pūrṇānanda-pravīṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]-[[synonyms:h:hīna]]---not under miserable material conditions; [[synonyms:v:vāñchā]]-[[synonyms:a:antara]]-[[synonyms:h:hīna]]---he has no other desire than to serve Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]---love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---service; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---full in transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:p:pravīṇa]]---and very expert or experienced in all subject matters.
translation: "A devotee of Kṛṣṇa is never in a miserable condition, nor does he have any desire other than to serve Kṛṣṇa. He is experienced and advanced. He feels the transcendental bliss of love of Kṛṣṇa and always engages in His service fully protected.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.183
description: " 'My devotees, having fulfilled their desires by serving Me, do not accept the four kinds of salvation that are easily earned by such service. Why then should they accept any pleasures that are lost in the course of time?'
text:
> mat-sevayā pratītaṁ te
> sālokyādi-catuṣṭayam
> necchanti sevayā pūrṇāḥ
> kuto 'nyat kāla-viplutam
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mat]]---of Me; [[synonyms:s:sevayā]]---by service; [[synonyms:p:pratītam]]---obtained; [[synonyms:t:te]]---they; [[synonyms:s:sālokya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---liberation, beginning with //sālokya//; [[synonyms:c:catuṣṭayam]]---the four kinds of; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:i:icchanti]]---do not desire; [[synonyms:s:sevayā]]---by service; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇāḥ]]---complete; [[synonyms:k:kutaḥ]]---where; [[synonyms:a:anyat]]---other things; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]-[[synonyms:v:viplutam]]---which are lost in time.
translation: “ 'My devotees, having fulfilled their desires by serving Me, do not accept the four kinds of salvation that are easily earned by such service. Why then should they accept any pleasures that are lost in the course of time?'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:9:4:67|(9.4.67)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.184
description: "In this material world, all living entities are disturbed due to their flickering position. A devotee, however, is fixed in the service of the lotus feet of the Lord, the master of the senses. Such a person is to be considered situated in endurance and patience.
text:
> hṛṣīkeśe hṛṣīkāṇi
> yasya sthairya-gatāni hi
> sa eva dhairyam āpnoti
> saṁsāre jīva-cañcale
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hṛṣīkeśe]]---to the master of the senses; [[synonyms:h:hṛṣīkāṇi]]---all the senses; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---whose; [[synonyms:s:sthairya]]-[[synonyms:g:gatāni]]---fixed; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that person; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---of course; [[synonyms:d:dhairyam]] [[synonyms:ā:āpnoti]]---attains the position of //dhairya,// endurance; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāre]]---in the material world; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:c:cañcale]]---where everyone is disturbed.
translation: "In this material world, all living entities are disturbed due to their flickering position. A devotee, however, is fixed in the service of the lotus feet of the Lord, the master of the senses. Such a person is to be considered situated in endurance and patience.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.185
description: "The word ca is for emphasis, and the word api is used as an aggregate. It is to be understood that even dull creatures [birds and illiterates] can also be situated in endurance and engage in Kṛṣṇa's devotional service.
text:
> 'ca'---avadhāraṇe, ihā 'api'---samuccaye
> dhṛtimanta hañā bhaje pakṣi-mūrkha-caye
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ca]]---the word //ca//; [[synonyms:a:avadhāraṇe]]---in emphasis; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---here; [[synonyms:a:api]]---the word //api//; [[synonyms:s:samuccaye]]---in the sense of an aggregate; [[synonyms:d:dhṛtimanta]]---fully saturated; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---worship; [[synonyms:p:pakṣi]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrkha]]-[[synonyms:c:caye]]---dull creatures like the birds, the most foolish.
translation: "The word ca is for emphasis, and the word api is used as an aggregate. It is to be understood that even dull creatures [birds and illiterates] can also be situated in endurance and engage in Kṛṣṇa's devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.186
description: "The word ātmā is also used for a particular type of intelligence. Since all living entities generally have some intelligence, more or less, they are included.
text:
> 'ātmā'-śabde 'buddhi' kahe buddhi-viśeṣa
> sāmānya-buddhi-yukta yata jīva avaśeṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ātmā//; [[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---intelligence; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it is said; [[synonyms:b:buddhi]]-[[synonyms:v:viśeṣa]]---a particular type of intelligence; [[synonyms:s:sāmānya]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhi]]-[[synonyms:y:yukta]]---endowed with common intelligence; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---living entities; [[synonyms:a:avaśeṣa]]---the rest.
translation: "The word ātmā is also used for a particular type of intelligence. Since all living entities generally have some intelligence, more or less, they are included.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.187
description: "Everyone has some kind of intelligence, and one who utilizes his intelligence is called ātmārāma. There are two types of ātmārāma. One is a learned scholar and a philosopher, and the other is an uneducated, illiterate and foolish person.
text:
> buddhye rame ātmārāma---dui ta' prakāra
> 'paṇḍita' muni-gaṇa, nirgrantha 'mūrkha' āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:buddhye]]---in intelligence; [[synonyms:r:rame]]---who enjoys; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---is //ātmārāma//; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:t:ta']] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---two varieties; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---learned; [[synonyms:m:muni]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---philosophers; [[synonyms:n:nirgrantha]]---without education; [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]]---foolish; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also.
translation: "Everyone has some kind of intelligence, and one who utilizes his intelligence is called ātmārāma. There are two types of ātmārāma. One is a learned scholar and a philosopher, and the other is an uneducated, illiterate and foolish person.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.188
description: "By the mercy of Kṛṣṇa and by the association of devotees, one increases his attraction to and intelligence for pure devotional service; therefore one gives up everything and engages himself at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and His pure devotees.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-kṛpāya sādhu-saṅge rati-buddhi pāya
> saba chāḍi' śuddha-bhakti kare kṛṣṇa-pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpāya]]---by the mercy of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the association of devotees; [[synonyms:r:rati]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---devotional attraction and intelligence; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---one obtains; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up everything; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---pure devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pāya]]---at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "By the mercy of Kṛṣṇa and by the association of devotees, one increases his attraction to and intelligence for pure devotional service; therefore one gives up everything and engages himself at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and His pure devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.189
description: " 'I [Kṛṣṇa] am the original source of everything. Everything emanates from Me. The wise who perfectly know this engage in My service with love and devotion.'
text:
> ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo
> mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate
> iti matvā bhajante māṁ
> budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I, Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sarvasya]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:p:prabhavaḥ]]---the original source; [[synonyms:m:mattaḥ]]---from Me; [[synonyms:s:sarvam]]---everything; [[synonyms:p:pravartate]]---emanates; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:m:matvā]]---understanding; [[synonyms:b:bhajante]]---they engage in devotional service; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---to Me; [[synonyms:b:budhāḥ]]---those who are learned; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:s:samanvitāḥ]]---with love and devotion.
translation: “ 'I [Kṛṣṇa] am the original source of everything. Everything emanates from Me. The wise who perfectly know this engage in My service with love and devotion.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:10:8|(Bg. 10.8)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.19
description: "The word urukrama refers to one whose krama [step] is great. The word krama means 'throwing the foot forward,' that is, 'step.'
text:
> 'urukrama'-śabde kahe, baḍa yāṅra krama
> 'krama'-śabde kahe ei pāda-vikṣepaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:urukrama]]---urukrama; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by this word; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---one means; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---great; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:k:krama]]---step; [[synonyms:k:krama]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---in this word //krama//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---one means; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:v:vikṣepaṇa]]---throwing forth of the foot.
translation: "The word urukrama refers to one whose krama [step] is great. The word krama means 'throwing the foot forward,' that is, 'step.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.190
description: " 'Women, fourth-class men, uncivilized hill tribes, hunters and many others born of low families, as well as birds and beasts, can engage in the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead-who acts very wonderfully-and follow the path of the devotees and take lessons from them. Although the ocean of nescience is vast, they can still cross over it. What, then, is the difficulty for those who are advanced in Vedic knowledge?'
text:
> te vai vidanty atitaranti ca deva-māyāṁ
> strī-śūdra-hūna-śabarā api pāpa-jīvāḥ
> yady adbhuta-krama-parāyaṇa-śīla-śikṣās
> tiryag-janā api kimu śruta-dhāraṇā ye
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:te]]---all of them; [[synonyms:v:vai]]---certainly; [[synonyms:v:vidanti]]---understand; [[synonyms:a:atitaranti]]---cross over; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:m:māyām]]---the influence of the external illusory energy; [[synonyms:s:strī]]---women; [[synonyms:ś:śūdra]]---fourth-class men; [[synonyms:h:hūna]]---uncivilized hill tribes; [[synonyms:ś:śabarāḥ]]---and hunters; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]-[[synonyms:j:jīvāḥ]]---sinful creatures; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]-[[synonyms:k:krama]]---of the performer of wonderful activities; [[synonyms:p:parāyaṇa]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:ś:śīla]]-[[synonyms:ś:śikṣāḥ]]---characteristics and education; [[synonyms:t:tiryak]]-[[synonyms:j:janāḥ]]---birds and beasts; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:k:kimu]]---what to speak of; [[synonyms:ś:śruta]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāraṇāḥ]] [[synonyms:y:ye]]---persons advanced in the education of Vedic knowledge.
translation: “ 'Women, fourth-class men, uncivilized hill tribes, hunters and many others born of low families, as well as birds and beasts, can engage in the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead-who acts very wonderfully-and follow the path of the devotees and take lessons from them. Although the ocean of nescience is vast, they can still cross over it. What, then, is the difficulty for those who are advanced in Vedic knowledge?'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:7:46|(2.7.46)]]. Lord Brahmā said this when speaking to his disciple Nārada about the wonderful characteristics of Lord Viṣṇu. Simply by chanting the glories of Lord Viṣṇu, one can cross the ocean of nescience, even though one may be lowborn.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.191
description: "Considering all these points, when one engages in the service of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, Kṛṣṇa gives one the intelligence by which he can gradually progress toward perfection in service to the Lord.
text:
> vicāra kariyā yabe bhaje kṛṣṇa-pāya
> sei buddhi dena tāṅre, yāte kṛṣṇa pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---consideration; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---doing; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---one worships; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pāya]]---at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---that intelligence; [[synonyms:d:dena]]---gives; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to him; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---by which; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---one gets the shelter of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Considering all these points, when one engages in the service of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, Kṛṣṇa gives one the intelligence by which he can gradually progress toward perfection in service to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.192
description: " 'To those who are constantly devoted and worship Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.'
text:
> teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ
> bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam
> dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ
> yena mām upayānti te
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:teṣām]]---to them; [[synonyms:s:satata]]-[[synonyms:y:yuktānām]]---always engaged; [[synonyms:b:bhajatām]]---in devotional service; [[synonyms:p:prīti]]-[[synonyms:p:pūrvakam]]---in loving ecstasy; [[synonyms:d:dadāmi]]---I give; [[synonyms:b:buddhi]]-[[synonyms:y:yogam]]---real intelligence; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---that; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---by which; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:u:upayānti]]---come; [[synonyms:t:te]]---they.
translation: “ 'To those who are constantly devoted and worship Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:10:10|(Bg. 10.10)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.193
description: "To be elevated to the platform of devotional service, the following five items should be observed: association with devotees, engagement in the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the reading of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, the chanting of the holy names and residence at Vṛndāvana or Mathurā.
text:
> sat-saṅga, kṛṣṇa-sevā, bhāgavata, nāma
> vraje vāsa,---ei pañca sādhana pradhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---association with devotees; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]]---engagement in the service of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]---devotees and the book known as //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the chanting of the holy name; [[synonyms:v:vraje]] [[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---residence in Vṛndāvana or Mathurā; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]---five; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]] [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---the chief processes of devotion.
translation: "To be elevated to the platform of devotional service, the following five items should be observed: association with devotees, engagement in the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the reading of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, the chanting of the holy names and residence at Vṛndāvana or Mathurā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.194
description: "One's dormant love for Kṛṣṇa gradually awakens if one is a little advanced in one of these five items and is intelligent.
text:
> ei-pañca-madhye eka 'svalpa' yadi haya
> subuddhi janera haya kṛṣṇa-premodaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---out of the five; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---of only one; [[synonyms:s:svalpa]]---a small quantity; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---intelligent; [[synonyms:j:janera]]---of the person; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]]---awakening of dormant love for Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "One's dormant love for Kṛṣṇa gradually awakens if one is a little advanced in one of these five items and is intelligent.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.195
description: " 'The power of these five principles is very wonderful and difficult to reconcile. Even without faith in them, a person who is offenseless can experience dormant love of Kṛṣṇa simply by being a little connected with them.'
text:
> durūhādbhuta-vīrye 'smin
> śraddhā dūre 'stu pañcake
> yatra svalpo 'pi sambandhaḥ
> saddhiyāṁ bhāva-janmane
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:durūha]]---difficult to be reconciled; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:v:vīrye]]---in the power; [[synonyms:a:asmin]]---in this; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]]---faith; [[synonyms:d:dūre]]---far away; [[synonyms:a:astu]]---let it be; [[synonyms:p:pañcake]]---in the above-mentioned five principles; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---in which; [[synonyms:s:svalpaḥ]]---a little; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:s:sambandhaḥ]]---connection; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:d:dhiyām]]---of those who are intelligent and offenseless; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:j:janmane]]---to awaken one's dormant love for Kṛṣṇa.
translation: “ 'The power of these five principles is very wonderful and difficult to reconcile. Even without faith in them, a person who is offenseless can experience dormant love of Kṛṣṇa simply by being a little connected with them.'
purport: This verse is also found in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.238).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.196
description: "If a person is actually liberal and intelligent, he can advance and become perfect in devotional service even if he has material desires and serves the Lord with some motive.
text:
> udāra mahatī yāṅra sarvottamā buddhi
> nānā kāme bhaje, tabu pāya bhakti-siddhi
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:udāra]]---liberal; [[synonyms:m:mahatī]]---great; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:u:uttamā]]---first-class; [[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---intelligence; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:k:kāme]]---with desires; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---engages in devotional service; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:s:siddhi]]---perfection in devotional service.
translation: "If a person is actually liberal and intelligent, he can advance and become perfect in devotional service even if he has material desires and serves the Lord with some motive.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.197
description: " 'Whether one desires everything or nothing, or whether he desires to merge into the existence of the Lord, he is intelligent only if he worships Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by rendering transcendental loving service.'
text:
> akāmaḥ sarva-kāmo vā
> mokṣa-kāma udāra-dhīḥ
> tīvreṇa bhakti-yogena
> yajeta puruṣaṁ param
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:akāmaḥ]]---without material desires; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāmaḥ]]---full of all material desires; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:m:mokṣa]]-[[synonyms:k:kāmaḥ]]---desiring liberation; [[synonyms:u:udāra]]-[[synonyms:d:dhīḥ]]---sincere and advanced in devotional service; [[synonyms:t:tīvreṇa]]---firm; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:y:yogena]]---by the practice of //bhakti-yoga//; [[synonyms:y:yajeta]]---should worship; [[synonyms:p:puruṣam]] [[synonyms:p:param]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'Whether one desires everything or nothing, or whether he desires to merge into the existence of the Lord, he is intelligent only if he worships Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by rendering transcendental loving service.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:3:10|(2.3.10)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.198
description: "Devotional service is so strong that when one engages in it, he gradually gives up all material desires and becomes fully attracted to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. All this is brought about by attraction for the transcendental qualities of the Lord.
text:
> bhakti-prabhāva,---sei kāma chāḍāñā
> kṛṣṇa-pade bhakti karāya guṇe ākarṣiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhāva]]---the influence of devotional service; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kāma]]---material desire; [[synonyms:c:chāḍāñā]]---causing to give up; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pade]]---unto the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---engages in devotional service; [[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---by transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣiyā]]---attracting.
translation: "Devotional service is so strong that when one engages in it, he gradually gives up all material desires and becomes fully attracted to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. All this is brought about by attraction for the transcendental qualities of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.199
description: " 'Whenever Kṛṣṇa is requested to fulfill one's desire, He undoubtedly does so, but He does not award anything which, after being enjoyed, will cause someone to petition Him again and again to fulfill further desires. When one has other desires but engages in the Lord's service, Kṛṣṇa forcibly gives one shelter at His lotus feet, where one will forget all other desires.'
text:
> satyaṁ diśaty arthitam arthito nṛṇāṁ
> naivārthado yat punar arthitā yataḥ
> svayaṁ vidhatte bhajatām anicchatām
> icchā-pidhānaṁ nija-pāda-pallavam
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:satyam]]---it is true; [[synonyms:d:diśati]]---He awards; [[synonyms:a:arthitam]]---that which is desired; [[synonyms:a:arthitaḥ]]---being requested; [[synonyms:n:nṛṇām]]---by human beings; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:d:daḥ]]---giving desired things; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:a:arthitā]]---request; [[synonyms:y:yataḥ]]---from which; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---Himself; [[synonyms:v:vidhatte]]---He gives; [[synonyms:b:bhajatām]]---of those engaged in devotional service; [[synonyms:a:anicchatām]]---even though not desiring; [[synonyms:i:icchā]]-[[synonyms:p:pidhānam]]---covering all other desires; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:pallavam]]---the shelter of His own lotus feet.
translation: “ 'Whenever Kṛṣṇa is requested to fulfill one's desire, He undoubtedly does so, but He does not award anything which, after being enjoyed, will cause someone to petition Him again and again to fulfill further desires. When one has other desires but engages in the Lord's service, Kṛṣṇa forcibly gives one shelter at His lotus feet, where one will forget all other desires.'
purport: This verse is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:5:19:27|(5.19.27)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.2
description: All glories to Lord Caitanya! All glories to Lord Nityānanda! All glories to Advaitacandra! And all glories to all the devotees of Lord Caitanya!
text:
> jaya jaya śrī-caitanya jaya nityānanda
> jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---to Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---to Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---to all the devotees of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All glories to Lord Caitanya! All glories to Lord Nityānanda! All glories to Advaitacandra! And all glories to all the devotees of Lord Caitanya!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.20
description: "Krama also means power, trembling, a systematic method, argument, and a forcible attack by stepping forward. Thus Vāmana caused the three worlds to tremble.
text:
> śakti, kampa, paripāṭī, yukti, śaktye ākramaṇa
> caraṇa-cālane kāṅpāila tribhuvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---power; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:p:paripāṭī]]---method; [[synonyms:y:yukti]]---argument; [[synonyms:ś:śaktye]]---with great force; [[synonyms:ā:ākramaṇa]]---attacking; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:cālane]]---by moving the foot; [[synonyms:k:kāṅpāila]]---caused to tremble; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvana]]---the three worlds.
translation: "Krama also means power, trembling, a systematic method, argument, and a forcible attack by stepping forward. Thus Vāmana caused the three worlds to tremble.
purport: //Uru// means very great, and //krama// means step. When Lord Vāmanadeva was offered three steps of land, He expanded His three steps by covering the entire universe. In this way the three worlds trembled, and therefore Śrī Vāmanadeva, the incarnation of Lord Viṣṇu, is referred to as Urukrama.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.200
description: "Another meaning of the word ātmā is 'one's characteristic nature.' Whoever enjoys his particular type of nature is called ātmārāma. Therefore, all living entities-be they moving or nonmoving-are also called ātmārāma.
text:
> 'ātmā'-śabde 'svabhāva' kahe, tāte yei rame
> ātmārāma jīva yata sthāvara-jaṅgame
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ātmā//; [[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---nature; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---is sometimes said; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in that; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:r:rame]]---one who takes pleasure; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---called //ātmārāma//; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---the living entities; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all of them; [[synonyms:s:sthāvara]]-[[synonyms:j:jaṅgame]]---the moving and nonmoving.
translation: "Another meaning of the word ātmā is 'one's characteristic nature.' Whoever enjoys his particular type of nature is called ātmārāma. Therefore, all living entities-be they moving or nonmoving-are also called ātmārāma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.201
description: "The original nature of every living entity is to consider himself the eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa. However, under the influence of māyā, he thinks himself to be the body, and thus his original consciousness is covered.
text:
> jīvera svabhāva---kṛṣṇa-'dāsa'-abhimāna
> dehe ātma-jñāne ācchādita sei 'jñāna'
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jīvera]] [[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---the original characteristic of all living entities; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---servant of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:abhimāna]]---the conception; [[synonyms:d:dehe]]---in the material body; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---by the conception of the self; [[synonyms:ā:ācchādita]]---covered; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---that original consciousness.
translation: "The original nature of every living entity is to consider himself the eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa. However, under the influence of māyā, he thinks himself to be the body, and thus his original consciousness is covered.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.202
description: "In that case, by the word ca, the word eva is meant. The word api can be taken in the sense of aggregation. Thus the verse would read ātmārāmā eva; that is, 'even all kinds of living beings worship Kṛṣṇa.'
text:
> ca-śabde 'eva', 'api'-śabda samuccaye
> 'ātmārāmā eva' hañā śrī-kṛṣṇa bhajaye
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ca//; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---the word //eva//; [[synonyms:a:api]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---the word //api//; [[synonyms:s:samuccaye]]---in the sense of aggregation; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:e:eva]]---all the //ātmārāmas// (all kinds of living entities); [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bhajaye]]---become engaged in the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "In that case, by the word ca, the word eva is meant. The word api can be taken in the sense of aggregation. Thus the verse would read ātmārāmā eva; that is, 'even all kinds of living beings worship Kṛṣṇa.'
purport: It is here mentioned that every living entity is //ātmārāma.// Temporarily covered by the influence of //māyā,// the living entity serves his senses, which are represented as //kāma-krodha-lobha-moha-mada-mātsarya.// In the material condition, all living entities are engaged in sense gratification, but when they associate with devotees who follow the regulative principles, they become purified and awakened to their original consciousness. They then attempt to satisfy the senses of Lord Kṛṣṇa and engage in His devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.203
description: "Living entities include great personalities like the four Kumāras, low-class foolish people, trees, plants, birds and beasts.
text:
> ei jīva---sanakādi saba muni-jana
> 'nirgrantha'---mūrkha, nīca, sthāvara-paśu-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---these living entities; [[synonyms:s:sanaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:m:muni]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---all the great personalities, such as Sanaka and Sanātana; [[synonyms:n:nirgrantha]]---down to the illiterate; [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]]---foolish person; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]---lowborn; [[synonyms:s:sthāvara]]---the trees and plants; [[synonyms:p:paśu]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the beasts and birds.
translation: "Living entities include great personalities like the four Kumāras, low-class foolish people, trees, plants, birds and beasts.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.204
description: "The devotional service of Vyāsa, Śuka and the four Kumāras has already been well celebrated. Now let Me explain how immovable living entities like trees and plants engage in the Lord's devotional service.
text:
> vyāsa-śuka-sanakādira prasiddha bhajana
> 'nirgrantha' sthāvarādira śuna vivaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]---of Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]---of Śukadeva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:sanaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādira]]---of the four Kumāras; [[synonyms:p:prasiddha]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---the devotional service is celebrated; [[synonyms:n:nirgrantha]]---foolish, uneducated; [[synonyms:s:sthāvara]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādira]]---of the immovable elements; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]] [[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---hear the description.
translation: "The devotional service of Vyāsa, Śuka and the four Kumāras has already been well celebrated. Now let Me explain how immovable living entities like trees and plants engage in the Lord's devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.205
description: "Everyone is eligible to receive Kṛṣṇa's mercy-including Vyāsadeva, the four Kumāras, Śukadeva Gosvāmī, lowborn creatures, trees, plants and beasts. By Kṛṣṇa's mercy they are elevated and engaged in His service.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-kṛpādi-hetu haite sabāra udaya
> kṛṣṇa-guṇākṛṣṭa hañā tāṅhāre bhajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:h:hetu]]---the reason of Kṛṣṇa's mercy; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]] [[synonyms:u:udaya]]---anyone becomes a devotee; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāre]]---Him; [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---worship.
translation: "Everyone is eligible to receive Kṛṣṇa's mercy-including Vyāsadeva, the four Kumāras, Śukadeva Gosvāmī, lowborn creatures, trees, plants and beasts. By Kṛṣṇa's mercy they are elevated and engaged in His service.
purport:
This is also confirmed in //Bhagavad-gītā// wherein the Lord says:

> māṁ hi pārtha vyapāśritya
> ye 'pi syuḥ pāpa-yonayaḥ
> striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrās
> te 'pi yānti parāṁ gatim

"O son of Pṛthā, those who take shelter in Me, though they be of lower birth-women, //vaiśyas// [merchants], as well as //śūdras// [workers]---can approach the supreme destination." (9.32)

Everyone is eligible to become Kṛṣṇa's devotee. One simply has to be trained according to the approved process. It is the work of Kṛṣṇa's confidential devotees to turn everyone into a Kṛṣṇa //bhakta.// If the confidential devotees do not take up the task of elevating everyone to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, then who will do it? Those who claim to be devotees but do not engage in Kṛṣṇa's service to elevate all living creatures to Kṛṣṇa consciousness are to be considered //kaniṣṭha-adhikārīs// (people in the lowest stage of devotional service). When one rises to the second platform of devotional service, his business is to propagate Kṛṣṇa consciousness all over the world. Those who are active in the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement should not remain in the neophyte stage but should rise to the platform of preachers, the second platform of devotional service. Devotional service is so enchanting that even the first-class devotees (//uttama-adhikārīs//) also come down to the second platform to preach and render service to the Lord for the benefit of the whole world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.206
description: " 'This land Vṛndāvana [Vrajabhūmi] is glorified today. Your lotus feet have touched the earth and grass. Your fingers have touched the trees and creepers, and Your merciful eyes have glanced upon rivers, hills, birds and beasts. The gopīs have been embraced by Your arms, and even the goddess of fortune desires this. Now all of these are glorified.'
text:
