> dhanyeyam adya dharaṇī tṛṇa-vīrudhas tvat-
> pāda-spṛśo druma-latāḥ karajābhimṛṣṭāḥ
> nadyo 'drayaḥ khaga-mṛgāḥ sadayāvalokair
> gopyo 'ntareṇa bhujayor api yat-spṛhā śrīḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dhanyā]]---glorified; [[synonyms:i:iyam]]---this; [[synonyms:a:adya]]---today; [[synonyms:d:dharaṇī]]---the surface of the globe; [[synonyms:t:tṛṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:vīrudhaḥ]]---the grass and herbs; [[synonyms:t:tvat]]---Your; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:s:spṛśaḥ]]---from the touch of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:d:druma]]-[[synonyms:l:latāḥ]]---the creepers and trees; [[synonyms:k:karaja]]-[[synonyms:a:abhimṛṣṭāḥ]]---touched by Your nails; [[synonyms:n:nadyaḥ]]---the rivers; [[synonyms:a:adrayaḥ]]---the hills; [[synonyms:k:khaga]]-[[synonyms:m:mṛgāḥ]]---the birds and forest animals; [[synonyms:s:sadaya]]-[[synonyms:a:avalokaiḥ]]---because of Your merciful glances; [[synonyms:g:gopyaḥ]]---the //gopīs,// the damsels of Vraja; [[synonyms:a:antareṇa]]---by the region between; [[synonyms:b:bhujayoḥ]]---Your two arms; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---for which; [[synonyms:s:spṛhā]]---desirous; [[synonyms:ś:śrīḥ]]---the goddess of fortune.
translation: “ 'This land Vṛndāvana [Vrajabhūmi] is glorified today. Your lotus feet have touched the earth and grass. Your fingers have touched the trees and creepers, and Your merciful eyes have glanced upon rivers, hills, birds and beasts. The gopīs have been embraced by Your arms, and even the goddess of fortune desires this. Now all of these are glorified.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.15.8) is spoken by Lord Kṛṣṇa to Śrī Balarāma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.207
description: " 'My dear friend, both Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma are passing through the forest leading Their cows with Their cowherd boy friends. They both carry ropes with which, at the time of milking, They bind the rear legs of the cows. When They play on Their flutes, all moving living entities are stunned, and nonmoving living entities experience ecstatic jubilation by Their sweet music. All these things are certainly very wonderful.'
text:
> gā gopakair anuvanaṁ nayator udāra-
> veṇu-svanaiḥ kala-padais tanu-bhṛtsu sakhyaḥ
> aspandanaṁ gatimatāṁ pulakas tarūṇāṁ
> niryoga-pāśa-kṛta-lakṣaṇayor vicitram
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gāḥ]]---the cows; [[synonyms:g:gopakaiḥ]]---with the cowherd boys; [[synonyms:a:anuvanam]]---to each forest; [[synonyms:n:nayatoḥ]]---leading; [[synonyms:u:udāra]]---very liberal; [[synonyms:v:veṇu]]-[[synonyms:s:svanaiḥ]]---by the vibrations of the flutes; [[synonyms:k:kala]]-[[synonyms:p:padaiḥ]]---having sweet tones; [[synonyms:t:tanu]]-[[synonyms:b:bhṛtsu]]---among the living entities; [[synonyms:s:sakhyaḥ]]---O friends; [[synonyms:a:aspandanam]]---the lack of movement; [[synonyms:g:gatimatām]]---of those living entities that can move; [[synonyms:p:pulakaḥ]]---the ecstatic jubilation; [[synonyms:t:tarūṇām]]---of the otherwise nonmoving trees; [[synonyms:n:niryoga]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---the ropes for binding the rear legs of the cows; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇayoḥ]]---of those two (Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma), who are characterized by; [[synonyms:v:vicitram]]---wonderful.
translation: “ 'My dear friend, both Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma are passing through the forest leading Their cows with Their cowherd boy friends. They both carry ropes with which, at the time of milking, They bind the rear legs of the cows. When They play on Their flutes, all moving living entities are stunned, and nonmoving living entities experience ecstatic jubilation by Their sweet music. All these things are certainly very wonderful.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.21.19). All the //gopīs// were very attracted to Kṛṣṇa when they saw Him wandering in the forest with Baladeva. They thus praised the Lord's activities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.208
description: " 'The plants, creepers and trees were full of fruits and flowers due to ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa. Indeed, being so full, they were bowing down. They were inspired by such deep love for Kṛṣṇa that they were constantly pouring showers of honey. In this way the gopīs saw all the forest of Vṛndāvana.'
text:
> vana-latās tarava ātmani viṣṇuṁ
> vyañjayantya iva puṣpa-phalāḍhyāḥ
> praṇata-bhāra-viṭapā madhu-dhārāḥ
> prema-hṛṣṭa-tanavo vavṛṣuḥ sma
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vana]]-[[synonyms:l:latāḥ]]---the herbs and plants; [[synonyms:t:taravaḥ]]---the trees; [[synonyms:ā:ātmani]]---in the Supreme Soul; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇum]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:v:vyañjayantyaḥ]]---manifesting; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]-[[synonyms:ā:āḍhyāḥ]]---filled with luxuriant fruits and flowers; [[synonyms:p:praṇata]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāra]]---bowed down because of loads; [[synonyms:v:viṭapāḥ]]---the trees; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:d:dhārāḥ]]---showers; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:h:hṛṣṭa]]---inspired by love of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tanavaḥ]]---whose bodies; [[synonyms:v:vavṛṣuḥ]]---constantly rained; [[synonyms:s:sma]]---certainly.
translation: “ 'The plants, creepers and trees were full of fruits and flowers due to ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa. Indeed, being so full, they were bowing down. They were inspired by such deep love for Kṛṣṇa that they were constantly pouring showers of honey. In this way the gopīs saw all the forest of Vṛndāvana.'
purport: This verse is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.35.9).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.209
description: " 'Kirāta, Hūna, Āndhra, Pulinda, Pulkaśa, Ābhīra, Śumbha, Yavana and the Khaśa races and even others who are addicted to sinful acts can be purified by taking shelter of the devotees of the Lord due to His being the supreme power. I beg to offer my respectful obeisances unto Him.'
text:
> kirāta-hūnāndhra-pulinda-pulkaśā
> ābhīra-śumbhā yavanāḥ khaśādayaḥ
> ye 'nye ca pāpā yad-upāśrayāśrayāḥ
> śudhyanti tasmai prabhaviṣṇave namaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kirāta]]---the aborigines named Kirātas; [[synonyms:h:hūna]]---the Hūnas; [[synonyms:ā:āndhra]]---Āndhras; [[synonyms:p:pulinda]]---Pulindas; [[synonyms:p:pulkaśāḥ]]---Pulkaśas; [[synonyms:ā:ābhīra]]---Ābhīras; [[synonyms:ś:śumbhāḥ]]---Śumbhas; [[synonyms:y:yavanāḥ]]---persons who do not follow the Vedic injunctions and who eat cow's flesh; [[synonyms:k:khaśa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādayaḥ]]---Khaśas and others; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:a:anye]]---similar others; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:p:pāpāḥ]]---sinful persons; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:u:upāśraya]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āśrayāḥ]]---taking shelter; [[synonyms:ś:śudhyanti]]---become purified; [[synonyms:t:tasmai]]---unto Him, Lord Viṣṇu, because of whom they become purified; [[synonyms:p:prabhaviṣṇave]]---to Lord Viṣṇu, the most powerful; [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---respectful obeisances.
translation: “ 'Kirāta, Hūna, Āndhra, Pulinda, Pulkaśa, Ābhīra, Śumbha, Yavana and the Khaśa races and even others who are addicted to sinful acts can be purified by taking shelter of the devotees of the Lord due to His being the supreme power. I beg to offer my respectful obeisances unto Him.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.21
description: " 'Even if a learned man is able to count all the minute atoms in this material world, he still cannot count the potencies of Lord Viṣṇu. In the form of the Vāmana incarnation, Lord Viṣṇu, without hindrance, captured all the planets, beginning from the root of the material world up to Satyaloka. Indeed, He caused every planetary system to tremble by the force of His steps.'
text:
> viṣṇor nu vīrya-gaṇanāṁ katamo 'rhatīha
> yaḥ pārthivāny api kavir vimame rajāṁsi
> caskambha yaḥ sva-raṁhasāskhalatā tripṛṣṭhaṁ
> yasmāt trisāmya-sadanād urukampayānam
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viṣṇoḥ]]---of Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:n:nu]]---certainly; [[synonyms:v:vīrya]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇanām]]---a counting of the different potencies; [[synonyms:k:katamaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:a:arhati]]---is able to do; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---in this world; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:p:pārthivāni]]---of the element earth; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:k:kaviḥ]]---a learned person; [[synonyms:v:vimame]]---has counted; [[synonyms:r:rajāṁsi]]---the atoms; [[synonyms:c:caskambha]]---captured; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:s:sva]]---His own; [[synonyms:r:raṁhasā]]---by potency; [[synonyms:a:askhalatā]]---without hindrances; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:p:pṛṣṭham]]---the topmost planet (Satyaloka); [[synonyms:y:yasmāt]]---from some cause; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:s:sāmya]]---where there is equilibrium of the three //guṇas//; [[synonyms:s:sadanāt]]---from the place (from the root of the material world); [[synonyms:u:urukampayānam]]---trembling greatly.
translation: “ 'Even if a learned man is able to count all the minute atoms in this material world, he still cannot count the potencies of Lord Viṣṇu. In the form of the Vāmana incarnation, Lord Viṣṇu, without hindrance, captured all the planets, beginning from the root of the material world up to Satyaloka. Indeed, He caused every planetary system to tremble by the force of His steps.'
purport:
This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:7:40|(2.7.40)]]. In the //Ṛg Veda mantra// (1.2.154.1), it is said:

> oṁ viṣṇor nu vīryāṇi kaṁ prāvocaṁ
> yaḥ pārthivāni vimame rajāṁsi
> yo 'skambhayad uttaraṁ sadhasthaṁ
> vicakramāṇas tredhorugāyaḥ

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.210
description: "I have already spoken about the thirteen kinds of meaning. Now there are six more. Combined, these make nineteen.
text:
> āge 'tera' artha kariluṅ, āra 'chaya' ei
> ūnaviṁśati artha ha-ila mili' ei dui
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---previously; [[synonyms:t:tera]]---thirteen; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meanings; [[synonyms:k:kariluṅ]]---I have done; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:c:chaya]]---six; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:ū:ūnaviṁśati]]---altogether nineteen; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meanings; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there were; [[synonyms:m:mili']]---including; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]]---these two.
translation: "I have already spoken about the thirteen kinds of meaning. Now there are six more. Combined, these make nineteen.
purport: The six different meanings are (1) mental speculators (vide verse 165), (2) those engaged in different types of endeavor (vide verse 168), (3) those who are patient and sober (vide verse 174), (4) those who are intelligent and learned scholars (vide verse 187), (5) those who are intelligent but illiterate and foolish (vide verse 187), and (6) those who are conscious of eternal servitorship to Kṛṣṇa (vide verse 201).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.211
description: "I have already explained nineteen different meanings. Now please hear further meanings. The word ātma also refers to the body, and this can be taken in four ways.
text:
> ei ūniśa artha karilu, āge śuna āra
> 'ātma'-śabde 'deha' kahe,---cāri artha tāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:ū:ūniśa]]---nineteen; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meanings; [[synonyms:k:karilu]]---I have done; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---ahead; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---more; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ātma//; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---the body; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---is understood; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---four meanings; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that.
translation: "I have already explained nineteen different meanings. Now please hear further meanings. The word ātma also refers to the body, and this can be taken in four ways.
purport: The four divisions are (1) //aupādika-brahma-deha,// the material body considered as Brahman with designations (vide verse 212), (2) //karma-niṣṭha yājñikera karma-deha,// the body engaged in ritualistic ceremonies of the Vedic injunctions (vide verse 214), (3) //tapo-deha,// the body engaged in austerities and penances (vide verse 216), and (4) //sarva-kāma-deha,// the body engaged for the satisfaction of all kinds of material desires (vide verse 218).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.212
description: "One in the bodily conception worships his own body as Brahman, but when he comes in contact with the devotee, he gives up this mistaken idea and engages himself in the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> dehārāmī dehe bhaje 'dehopādhi brahma'
> sat-saṅge seha kare kṛṣṇera bhajana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dehārāmī]]---persons who have accepted this body as the self and are interested only in sense gratification; [[synonyms:d:dehe]]---in the body; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---worships; [[synonyms:d:deha]]-[[synonyms:u:upādhi]] [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---Brahman having the body as a designation; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the association of devotees; [[synonyms:s:seha]]---such a person; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---service to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "One in the bodily conception worships his own body as Brahman, but when he comes in contact with the devotee, he gives up this mistaken idea and engages himself in the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.213
description: " 'Those who follow the path of great, saintly mystic yogīs take to the yogic gymnastic process and begin worshiping from the abdomen, where it is said that Brahman is located. Such people are called śārk, which means that they are situated in the gross bodily conception. There are also followers of the ṛṣi known as Āruṇa. Following that path, they observe the activities of the arteries. Thus they gradually rise to the heart, where subtle Brahman, Paramātmā, is situated. They then worship Him. O, unlimited Ananta! Better than these persons are the mystic yogīs who worship You from the top of their heads. Beginning with the abdomen and proceeding through the heart, they reach the top of the head and pass through the brahma-randra, the hole at the top of the skull. Thus yogīs attain the perfectional platform and do not enter the cycle of birth and death again.'
text:
> udaram upāsate ya ṛṣi-vartmasu kūrpa-dṛśaḥ
> parisara-paddhatiṁ hṛdayam āruṇayo daharam
> tata udagād ananta tava dhāma śiraḥ paramaṁ
> punar iha yat sametya na patanti kṛtānta-mukhe
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:udaram]]---the abdomen; [[synonyms:u:upāsate]]---worship; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣi]]-[[synonyms:v:vartmasu]]---on the path marked out by the great saintly persons; [[synonyms:k:kūrpa]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛśaḥ]]---whose vision is grossly situated in the bodily conception of life; [[synonyms:p:parisara]]-[[synonyms:p:paddhatim]]---from which the system of the arteries comes; [[synonyms:h:hṛdayam]]---the heart; [[synonyms:ā:āruṇayaḥ]]---saintly persons headed by Āruṇa Ṛṣi; [[synonyms:d:daharam]]---the sky within the heart, the subtle conception of the Supersoul within the heart; [[synonyms:t:tataḥ]]---from that; [[synonyms:u:udagāt]]---went up; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---O unlimited one; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---place; [[synonyms:ś:śiraḥ]]---the top of the head; [[synonyms:p:paramam]]---supreme; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---in this material world; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:s:sametya]]---having achieved; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:p:patanti]]---fall down; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:anta]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the repetition of birth and death.
translation: “ 'Those who follow the path of great, saintly mystic yogīs take to the yogic gymnastic process and begin worshiping from the abdomen, where it is said that Brahman is located. Such people are called śārk, which means that they are situated in the gross bodily conception. There are also followers of the ṛṣi known as Āruṇa. Following that path, they observe the activities of the arteries. Thus they gradually rise to the heart, where subtle Brahman, Paramātmā, is situated. They then worship Him. O, unlimited Ananta! Better than these persons are the mystic yogīs who worship You from the top of their heads. Beginning with the abdomen and proceeding through the heart, they reach the top of the head and pass through the brahma-randra, the hole at the top of the skull. Thus yogīs attain the perfectional platform and do not enter the cycle of birth and death again.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.87.18).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.214
description: "Those who are in the bodily conception mainly engage in fruitive activity. Those who perform yajñas and ritualistic ceremonies are also considered in the same category. However, when they are all in contact with the pure devotee, they give up their fruitive activity and fully engage in the service of the Lord.
text:
> dehārāmī karma-niṣṭha---yājñikādi jana
> sat-saṅge 'karma' tyaji' karaya bhajana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dehārāmī]]---those in the bodily concept of life; [[synonyms:k:karma]]-[[synonyms:n:niṣṭha]]---attracted to fruitive activities; [[synonyms:y:yājñika]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---persons who perform ritualistic ceremonies for a better standard of life; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in contact with devotees; [[synonyms:k:karma]] [[synonyms:t:tyaji']]---giving up such fruitive activities; [[synonyms:k:karaya]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---engages in the devotional service of the Lord.
translation: "Those who are in the bodily conception mainly engage in fruitive activity. Those who perform yajñas and ritualistic ceremonies are also considered in the same category. However, when they are all in contact with the pure devotee, they give up their fruitive activity and fully engage in the service of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.215
description: " 'We have just begun performing this fruitive activity, a sacrificial fire, but due to the many imperfections in our action, we are not certain of its result. Our bodies have become black from the smoke, but we are factually pleased by the nectar of the lotus feet of the Personality of Godhead, Govinda, which you are distributing.'
text:
> karmaṇy asminn anāśvāse
> dhūma-dhūmrātmanāṁ bhavān
> āpāyayati govinda-
> pāda-padmāsavaṁ madhu
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:karmaṇi]]---in fruitive activity; [[synonyms:a:asmin]]---in this; [[synonyms:a:anāśvāse]]---although not positive in result; [[synonyms:d:dhūma]]-[[synonyms:d:dhūmra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmanām]]---whose bodies are simply becoming blackish because of smoke; [[synonyms:b:bhavān]]---you; [[synonyms:ā:āpāyayati]]---give a chance to drink; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:padma]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsavam]]---the nectarean beverage flowing from the lotus feet of Govinda; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]---sweet.
translation: “ 'We have just begun performing this fruitive activity, a sacrificial fire, but due to the many imperfections in our action, we are not certain of its result. Our bodies have become black from the smoke, but we are factually pleased by the nectar of the lotus feet of the Personality of Godhead, Govinda, which you are distributing.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:18:12|(1.18.12)]] was spoken to Sūta Gosvāmī at the meeting of great sages at Naimiṣāraṇya. The great sages were headed by Śaunaka, and Sūta Gosvāmī spoke of the glorious activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead at that meeting. At that time, all the //ṛṣis// assembled there neglected to complete the ritualistic ceremonies because there was no positive assurance of the results. All the performers were coated with black ash due to the large amount of smoke coming from the fire.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.216
description: "The tapasvīs, those who undergo severe austerities and penances to elevate themselves to the higher planetary systems, are also in the same category. When such persons come in contact with a devotee, they give up all those practices and engage in Lord Kṛṣṇa's service.
text:
> 'tapasvī' prabhṛti yata dehārāmī haya
> sādhu-saṅge tapa chāḍi' śrī-kṛṣṇa bhajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tapasvī]]---persons who undergo severe penances; [[synonyms:p:prabhṛti]]---and so on; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:d:dehārāmī]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are within the category of the bodily concept of life; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the association of devotees; [[synonyms:t:tapa]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up all such processes of penance and austerity; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---engage themselves in the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "The tapasvīs, those who undergo severe austerities and penances to elevate themselves to the higher planetary systems, are also in the same category. When such persons come in contact with a devotee, they give up all those practices and engage in Lord Kṛṣṇa's service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.217
description: " 'The taste for loving service is like the water of the River Ganges, which flows from the feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Every day that taste diminishes the results of sinful activities acquired over a period of many births by those who perform austerities.'
text:
> yat-pāda-sevābhirucis tapasvinām
> aśeṣa-janmopacitaṁ malaṁ dhiyaḥ
> sadyaḥ kṣiṇoty anvaham edhatī satī
> yathā padāṅguṣṭha-viniḥsṛtā sarit
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yat]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]]-[[synonyms:a:abhiruciḥ]]---the taste for serving the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tapasvinām]]---of persons undergoing severe penances; [[synonyms:a:aśeṣa]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:j:janma]]-[[synonyms:u:upacitam]]---contracted from life after life; [[synonyms:m:malam]]---dirt; [[synonyms:d:dhiyaḥ]]---of the intelligence; [[synonyms:s:sadyaḥ]]---immediately; [[synonyms:k:kṣiṇoti]]---vanquishes; [[synonyms:a:anvaham]]---every day; [[synonyms:e:edhatī]]---increasing; [[synonyms:s:satī]]---being in the mode of goodness; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅguṣṭha]]-[[synonyms:v:viniḥsṛtā]]---emanating from the toe of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sarit]]---the River Ganges.
translation: “ 'The taste for loving service is like the water of the River Ganges, which flows from the feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Every day that taste diminishes the results of sinful activities acquired over a period of many births by those who perform austerities.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:4:21:31|(4.21.31)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.218
description: "As long as one labors under the bodily conception, he must fulfill volumes and volumes of material desires. Thus a person is called ātmārāma. When such an ātmārāma is favored by the mercy of Kṛṣṇa, he gives up his so-called self-satisfaction and engages in the transcendental loving service of the Lord.
text:
> dehārāmī, sarva-kāma---saba ātmārāma
> kṛṣṇa-kṛpāya kṛṣṇa bhaje chāḍi' saba kāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dehārāmī]]---persons who are in the bodily concept of life; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāma]]---full of all material desires; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---enjoying self-satisfaction; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpāya]]---by the mercy of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---become engaged in the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']] [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:k:kāma]]---giving up all sorts of material desire.
translation: "As long as one labors under the bodily conception, he must fulfill volumes and volumes of material desires. Thus a person is called ātmārāma. When such an ātmārāma is favored by the mercy of Kṛṣṇa, he gives up his so-called self-satisfaction and engages in the transcendental loving service of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.219
description: [When he was being benedicted by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Dhruva Mahārāja said], " 'O my Lord, because I was seeking an opulent material position, I was performing severe types of penance and austerity. Now I have gotten You, who are very difficult for the great demigods, saintly persons and kings to attain. I was searching after a piece of glass, but instead I have found a most valuable jewel. Therefore I am so satisfied that I do not wish to ask any benediction from You.'
text:
> sthānābhilāṣī tapasi sthito 'haṁ
> tvāṁ prāptavān deva-munīndra-guhyam
> kācaṁ vicinvann api divya-ratnaṁ
> svāmin kṛtārtho 'smi varaṁ na yāce
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]-[[synonyms:a:abhilāṣī]]---desiring a very high position in the material world; [[synonyms:t:tapasi]]---in severe austerities and penances; [[synonyms:s:sthitaḥ]]---situated; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tvām]]---You; [[synonyms:p:prāptavān]]---have obtained; [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:m:muni]]-[[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:g:guhyam]]---difficult to achieve even for great demigods, saintly persons and kings; [[synonyms:k:kācam]]---a piece of glass; [[synonyms:v:vicinvan]]---searching for; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:r:ratnam]]---a transcendental gem; [[synonyms:s:svāmin]]---O my Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:arthaḥ]] [[synonyms:a:asmi]]---I am fully satisfied; [[synonyms:v:varam]]---any benediction; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:y:yāce]]---I do not ask.
translation: [When he was being benedicted by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Dhruva Mahārāja said], " 'O my Lord, because I was seeking an opulent material position, I was performing severe types of penance and austerity. Now I have gotten You, who are very difficult for the great demigods, saintly persons and kings to attain. I was searching after a piece of glass, but instead I have found a most valuable jewel. Therefore I am so satisfied that I do not wish to ask any benediction from You.'
purport: This verse is from the //Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya// (7.28).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.22
description: "Through His all-pervasive feature, the Supreme Personality of Godhead expanded the entire creation. He is holding and maintaining this creation by His extraordinary potency. By His conjugal potency, He maintains the planetary system known as Goloka Vṛndāvana. Through His six opulences, He maintains many Vaikuṇṭha planets.
text:
> vibhu-rūpe vyāpe, śaktye dhāraṇa-poṣaṇa
> mādhurya-śaktye goloka, aiśvarye paravyoma
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vibhu]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in His all-pervasive feature; [[synonyms:v:vyāpe]]---expands; [[synonyms:ś:śaktye]]---by His potency; [[synonyms:d:dhāraṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:poṣaṇa]]---maintaining and nourishing; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaktye]]---by His potency of conjugal love; [[synonyms:g:goloka]]---the planetary system Goloka Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarye]]---and by opulence; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:v:vyoma]]---the spiritual world.
translation: "Through His all-pervasive feature, the Supreme Personality of Godhead expanded the entire creation. He is holding and maintaining this creation by His extraordinary potency. By His conjugal potency, He maintains the planetary system known as Goloka Vṛndāvana. Through His six opulences, He maintains many Vaikuṇṭha planets.
purport: In His gigantic form, Lord Kṛṣṇa has covered the creation. He holds all the planetary systems and maintains them by His inconceivable potencies. Similarly, He is maintaining His personal abode, Goloka Vṛndāvana, through His conjugal love, and He is maintaining the spiritual world containing the Vaikuṇṭha planets by His opulences.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.220
description: "In addition to the nineteen other meanings, this ātmārāma meaning [including those laboring under the bodily conception] makes four meanings altogether and brings the total to twenty-three meanings. Now hear of another three meanings, which are very suitable.
text:
> ei cāri artha saha ha-ila 'teiśa' artha
> āra tina artha śuna parama samartha
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---four; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meanings; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there were; [[synonyms:t:teiśa]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---twenty-three different varieties of imports; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---another three imports; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:s:samartha]]---very strong.
translation: "In addition to the nineteen other meanings, this ātmārāma meaning [including those laboring under the bodily conception] makes four meanings altogether and brings the total to twenty-three meanings. Now hear of another three meanings, which are very suitable.
purport: The three different meanings are (1) the word //ca// meaning "in due course' " (2) the words //ca// meaning //eva,// and //api// meaning "censure," and (3) //nirgrantha,// meaning "one who is very poor, without money."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.221
description: "As mentioned above, the word ca has been used to mean 'aggregate.' According to this meaning, all the ātmārāmas and the munis engage in Kṛṣṇa's service. Besides 'aggregate,' there is another meaning of the word ca.
text:
> ca-śabde 'samuccaye', āra artha kaya
> 'ātmārāmāś ca munayaś ca' kṛṣṇere bhajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ca//; [[synonyms:s:samuccaye]]---in aggregation; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---import; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---is meant; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]] [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---all the //ātmārāmas// and //munis//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]] [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---worship Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "As mentioned above, the word ca has been used to mean 'aggregate.' According to this meaning, all the ātmārāmas and the munis engage in Kṛṣṇa's service. Besides 'aggregate,' there is another meaning of the word ca.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.222
description: "The word nirgranthāḥ is used as an adjective, and api is used in the sense of certainty. For instance, rāmaś ca kṛṣṇaś ca means that both Rāma and Kṛṣṇa enjoy walking in the forest.
text:
> 'nirgranthāḥ' hañā ihāṅ 'api'---nirdhāraṇe
> 'rāmaś ca kṛṣṇaś ca' yathā viharaye vane
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirgranthāḥ]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being liberated saintly persons; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:a:api]]---the word //api//; [[synonyms:n:nirdhāraṇe]]---in the sense of certainty; [[synonyms:r:rāmaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---both Rāma and Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:v:viharaye]]---enjoy walking; [[synonyms:v:vane]]---in the forest.
translation:
"The word nirgranthāḥ is used as an adjective, and api is used in the sense of certainty. For instance, rāmaś ca kṛṣṇaś ca means that both Rāma and Kṛṣṇa enjoy walking in the forest.


Because it is said that both Rāma and Kṛṣṇa enjoy wandering in the forest, it is understood that both of Them are enjoying Their tour within the forest.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.223
description: "The word ca also means anvācaye, which means to present a secondary thing to be done at the same time. This is the way of understanding the word anvācaye. An example is: 'O brahmacārī, go out to collect alms and at the same time bring in the cows.'
text:
> ca-śabde 'anvācaye' artha kahe āra
> 'baṭo, bhikṣām aṭa, gāṁ cānaya' yaiche prakāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ca//; [[synonyms:a:anvācaye]]---in presenting an action of secondary importance; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:b:baṭo]]---O //brahmacārī//; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣām]] [[synonyms:a:aṭa]]---just bring some alms; [[synonyms:g:gām]] [[synonyms:c:ca]] [[synonyms:ā:ānaya]]---also, at the same time, bring the cows; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---in this way.
translation: "The word ca also means anvācaye, which means to present a secondary thing to be done at the same time. This is the way of understanding the word anvācaye. An example is: 'O brahmacārī, go out to collect alms and at the same time bring in the cows.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.224
description: "Saintly persons who are always meditating upon Kṛṣṇa are engaged in the devotional service of the Lord. The ātmārāmas are also engaged in the Lord's service. That is the indirect import.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-manane muni kṛṣṇe sarvadā bhajaya
> 'ātmārāmā api' bhaje,---gauṇa artha kaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:manane]]---in meditating on Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:muni]]---saintly persons; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sarvadā]]---always; [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---perform devotional service; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---also those who are //ātmārāmas//; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---engage themselves in devotional service; [[synonyms:g:gauṇa]] [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---this is also another secondary import.
translation: "Saintly persons who are always meditating upon Kṛṣṇa are engaged in the devotional service of the Lord. The ātmārāmas are also engaged in the Lord's service. That is the indirect import.
purport: The //anvācaye// meaning of the word //ca// indicates that between the two words compounded by the word //ca,// one is given more importance, and the other is considered subordinate. For example: "O //brahmacārī,// please go out and collect alms and at the same time bring in the cows." In this statement, the collection of alms is of first importance, and the second business of collecting the cows is subordinate. Similarly, one who always meditates upon Kṛṣṇa is mainly a devotee of Kṛṣṇa engaged in His devotional service. Other //ātmārāmas// are subordinate in devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.225
description: "The word ca is also used to indicate the certainty that only saintly persons are engaged in rendering devotional service to Kṛṣṇa. In the combination ātmārāmā api, api is used in the sense of censure.
text:
> 'ca' evārthe---'munayaḥ eva' kṛṣṇere bhajaya
> "ātmārāmā api"---'api' 'garhā'-artha kaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ca]]---the word //ca//; [[synonyms:e:eva]]-[[synonyms:a:arthe]]---in the sense of //eva//; [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]] [[synonyms:e:eva]]---just the saintly persons; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]] [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---engage themselves in the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---also in this combination, //ātmārāmā api//; [[synonyms:a:api]]---the word //api//; [[synonyms:g:garhā]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---in the sense of censure.
translation: "The word ca is also used to indicate the certainty that only saintly persons are engaged in rendering devotional service to Kṛṣṇa. In the combination ātmārāmā api, api is used in the sense of censure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.226
description: "The word nirgrantha is taken as an adjective modifying muni and ātmārāma. There is another meaning, which you may hear from Me, indicating association with a devotee. Now I shall explain how it is that through the association of devotees, even a nirgrantha can become a devotee.
text:
> 'nirgrantha hañā'---ei duṅhāra 'viśeṣaṇa'
> āra artha śuna, yaiche sādhura saṅgama
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirgrantha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming //nirgrantha//; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]]---of both; [[synonyms:v:viśeṣaṇa]]---the adjective; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---another import; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---in which; [[synonyms:s:sādhura]] [[synonyms:s:saṅgama]]---there is association with devotees.
translation: "The word nirgrantha is taken as an adjective modifying muni and ātmārāma. There is another meaning, which you may hear from Me, indicating association with a devotee. Now I shall explain how it is that through the association of devotees, even a nirgrantha can become a devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.227
description: "The word nirgrantha-when combined with api, used in the sense of certainty-indicates a person who is a hunter by profession or who is very poor. Nonetheless, when such a person associates with a great saint like Nārada, he engages in Lord Kṛṣṇa's devotional service.
text:
> nirgrantha-śabde kahe tabe 'vyādha', 'nirdhana'
> sādhu-saṅge seha kare śrī-kṛṣṇa-bhajana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirgrantha]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //nirgrantha//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---is said; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---therefore; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---a hunter; [[synonyms:n:nirdhana]]---without any riches; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---by the association of a saintly person; [[synonyms:s:seha]]---he also; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---engages himself; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---in the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "The word nirgrantha-when combined with api, used in the sense of certainty-indicates a person who is a hunter by profession or who is very poor. Nonetheless, when such a person associates with a great saint like Nārada, he engages in Lord Kṛṣṇa's devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.228
description: "The words kṛṣṇārāmaś ca refer to one who takes pleasure in thinking of Kṛṣṇa. Even though such a person may be a hunter, he is still worshipable and is the best of devotees.
text:
> 'kṛṣṇārāmāś ca' eva---haya kṛṣṇa-manana
> vyādha hañā haya pūjya bhāgavatottama
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---one who takes pleasure in Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:manana]]---meditation on Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being a hunter; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:p:pūjya]]---worshipable; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]-[[synonyms:u:uttama]]---the best of the devotees.
translation: "The words kṛṣṇārāmaś ca refer to one who takes pleasure in thinking of Kṛṣṇa. Even though such a person may be a hunter, he is still worshipable and is the best of devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.229
description: "I shall now narrate the story of how the hunter became a great devotee by the association of such an exalted personality as Nārada Muni. From this story, one can understand the greatness of association with pure devotees.
text:
> eka bhakta-vyādhera kathā śuna sāvadhāne
> yāhā haite haya sat-saṅga-mahimāra jñāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vyādhera]]---one devotee who was a hunter; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---narration; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:s:sāvadhāne]]---with attention; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from which; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]-[[synonyms:m:mahimāra]] [[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---knowledge of the greatness of association with a great devotee.
translation: "I shall now narrate the story of how the hunter became a great devotee by the association of such an exalted personality as Nārada Muni. From this story, one can understand the greatness of association with pure devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.23
description: "The word urukrama indicates the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who, by His external potency, has perfectly created innumerable universes.
text:
> māyā-śaktye brahmāṇḍādi-paripāṭī-sṛjana
> 'urukrama'-śabdera ei artha nirūpaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaktye]]---by His external potency; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---of material universes and so on; [[synonyms:p:paripāṭī]]---an orderly arrangement; [[synonyms:s:sṛjana]]---creating; [[synonyms:u:urukrama]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabdera]]---of the word //urukrama//; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---of the meaning; [[synonyms:n:nirūpaṇa]]---ascertainment.
translation: "The word urukrama indicates the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who, by His external potency, has perfectly created innumerable universes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.230
description: "Once upon a time the great saint Nārada, after visiting Lord Nārāyaṇa in the Vaikuṇṭhas, went to Prayāga to bathe at the confluence of three rivers—the Ganges, Yamunā and Sarasvatī.
text:
> eka dina śrī-nārada dekhi' nārāyaṇa
> triveṇī-snāne prayāga karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:n:nārada]]---the great saintly person Nārada; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']] [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---after visiting Lord Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:v:veṇī]]-[[synonyms:s:snāne]]---to bathe at the confluence of the Ganges, Yamunā and Sarasvatī rivers; [[synonyms:p:prayāga]]---to Prayāga; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---went.
translation: "Once upon a time the great saint Nārada, after visiting Lord Nārāyaṇa in the Vaikuṇṭhas, went to Prayāga to bathe at the confluence of three rivers---the Ganges, Yamunā and Sarasvatī.
purport: The great saint Nārada is so liberated that he can go to the Vaikuṇṭha planets to see Nārāyaṇa and then immediately come to this planet in the material world and go to Prayāga to bathe in the confluence of three rivers. The word //tri-veṇī// refers to a confluence of three rivers. This confluence is still visited by many hundreds of thousands of people who go there to bathe, especially during the month of January (Māgha-melā). A liberated person who has no material body can go anywhere and everywhere; therefore a living entity is called //sarva-ga,// which indicates that he can go anywhere and everywhere. Presently scientists are trying to go to other planets, but due to their material bodies, they are not free to move at will. However, when one is situated in his original spiritual body, he can move anywhere and everywhere without difficulty. Within this material world there is a planet called Siddhaloka, whose inhabitants can go from one planet to another without the aid of a machine or space rocket. In the material world every planet has a specific advantage (//vibhūti-bhinna//). In the spiritual world, however, all the planets and their inhabitants are composed of spiritual energy. Because there are no material impediments, it is said that everything in the spiritual world is one.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.231
description: "Nārada Muni saw that a deer was lying on the path through the forest and that it was pierced by an arrow. It had broken legs and was twisting due to much pain.
text:
> vana-pathe dekhe mṛga āche bhūme paḍi'
> bāṇa-viddha bhagna-pāda kare dhaḍ-phaḍi
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vana]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the forest path; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---saw; [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]---deer; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there was; [[synonyms:b:bhūme]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---lying on the ground; [[synonyms:b:bāṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:viddha]]---pierced by an arrow; [[synonyms:b:bhagna]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]---broken legs; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:d:dhaḍ]]-[[synonyms:p:phaḍi]]---twisting with pain.
translation: "Nārada Muni saw that a deer was lying on the path through the forest and that it was pierced by an arrow. It had broken legs and was twisting due to much pain.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.232
description: "Farther ahead, Nārada Muni saw a boar pierced by an arrow. Its legs were also broken, and it was twisting in pain.
text:
> āra kata-dūre eka dekhena śūkara
> taiche viddha bhagna-pāda kare dhaḍ-phaḍa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:k:kata]]-[[synonyms:d:dūre]]---still farther along; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:d:dekhena]]---sees; [[synonyms:ś:śūkara]]---a boar; [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---similarly; [[synonyms:v:viddha]]---pierced; [[synonyms:b:bhagna]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]---broken legs; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:d:dhaḍ]]-[[synonyms:p:phaḍa]]---twists in pain.
translation: "Farther ahead, Nārada Muni saw a boar pierced by an arrow. Its legs were also broken, and it was twisting in pain.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.233
description: "When he went farther, he saw a rabbit that was also suffering. Nārada Muni was greatly pained at heart to see living entities suffer so.
text:
> aiche eka śaśaka dekhe āra kata-dūre
> jīvera duḥkha dekhi' nārada vyākula-antare
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---similarly; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:ś:śaśaka]]---one rabbit; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---he sees; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:k:kata]]-[[synonyms:d:dūre]]---still farther ahead; [[synonyms:j:jīvera]]---of the living entity; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing such horrible miseries; [[synonyms:n:nārada]]---the great saintly person; [[synonyms:v:vyākula]]-[[synonyms:a:antare]]---very pained within himself.
translation: "When he went farther, he saw a rabbit that was also suffering. Nārada Muni was greatly pained at heart to see living entities suffer so.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.234
description: "When Nārada Muni advanced farther, he saw a hunter behind a tree. This hunter was holding arrows, and he was ready to kill more animals.
text:
> kata-dūre dekhe vyādha vṛkṣe oṅta hañā
> mṛga māribāre āche bāṇa yuḍiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kata]]-[[synonyms:d:dūre]]---somewhat farther; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---Nārada Muni saw; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---the hunter; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣe]] [[synonyms:o:oṅta]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---hiding behind a tree; [[synonyms:m:mṛga]] [[synonyms:m:māribāre]]---to kill the animals; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---was there; [[synonyms:b:bāṇa]] [[synonyms:y:yuḍiyā]]---with arrows in the hand.
translation: "When Nārada Muni advanced farther, he saw a hunter behind a tree. This hunter was holding arrows, and he was ready to kill more animals.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.235
description: "The hunter's body was blackish. He had reddish eyes, and he appeared fierce. It was as if the superintendent of death, Yamarāja, was standing there with bows and arrows in his hands.
text:
> śyāma-varṇa rakta-netra mahā-bhayaṅkara
> dhanur-bāṇa haste,---yena yama daṇḍa-dhara
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śyāma]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇa]]---blackish color; [[synonyms:r:rakta]]-[[synonyms:n:netra]]---reddish eyes; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhayaṅkara]]---very fearful bodily features; [[synonyms:d:dhanuḥ]]-[[synonyms:b:bāṇa]] [[synonyms:h:haste]]---with arrows and bow in hand; [[synonyms:y:yena]] [[synonyms:y:yama]] [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:dhara]]---exactly like the superintendent of death, Yamarāja.
translation: "The hunter's body was blackish. He had reddish eyes, and he appeared fierce. It was as if the superintendent of death, Yamarāja, was standing there with bows and arrows in his hands.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.236
description: "When Nārada Muni left the forest path and went to the hunter, all the animals immediately saw him and fled.
text:
> patha chāḍi' nārada tāra nikaṭe calila
> nārade dekhi' mṛga saba palāñā gela
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:patha]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---leaving aside the path; [[synonyms:n:nārada]]---the saintly person Nārada; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:n:nikaṭe]]---near him; [[synonyms:c:calila]]---went; [[synonyms:n:nārade]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Nārada; [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]---the animals; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:p:palāñā]] [[synonyms:g:gela]]---left, running away.
translation: "When Nārada Muni left the forest path and went to the hunter, all the animals immediately saw him and fled.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.237
description: "When all the animals fled, the hunter wanted to chastise Nārada with abusive language, but due to Nārada's presence, he could not utter anything abusive.
text:
> kruddha hañā vyādha tāṅre gāli dite cāya
> nārada-prabhāve mukhe gāli nāhi āya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kruddha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being very angry; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---the hunter; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:g:gāli]] [[synonyms:d:dite]] [[synonyms:c:cāya]]---wanted to abuse; [[synonyms:n:nārada]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhāve]]---by the influence of Nārada; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the mouth; [[synonyms:g:gāli]]---abusive language; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:ā:āya]]---did not come.
translation: "When all the animals fled, the hunter wanted to chastise Nārada with abusive language, but due to Nārada's presence, he could not utter anything abusive.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.238

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.249
description: "Nārada Muni replied, 'If you leave the animals half-dead, you are purposefully giving them pain. Therefore you will have to suffer in retaliation.'
text:
> nārada kahe,---"ardha mārile jīva pāya vyathā
> jīve duḥkha ditecha, tomāra ha-ibe aiche avasthā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nārada]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Nārada Muni replied; [[synonyms:a:ardha]] [[synonyms:m:mārile]]---by half-killing the animals; [[synonyms:j:jīva]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]] [[synonyms:v:vyathā]]---the living beings suffer too much pain; [[synonyms:j:jīve]] [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]] [[synonyms:d:ditecha]]---you are giving troubles to the living beings; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ibe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:a:aiche]] [[synonyms:a:avasthā]]---the same suffering in retaliation.
translation: "Nārada Muni replied, 'If you leave the animals half-dead, you are purposefully giving them pain. Therefore you will have to suffer in retaliation.'
purport:
This is an authoritative statement given by the greatest authority, Nārada Muni. If one gives another living entity unnecessary pain, one will certainly be punished by the laws of nature by a similar pain. Although the hunter Mṛgāri was uncivilized, he still had to suffer the results of his sinful activities. However, if a civilized man kills animals regularly in a slaughterhouse to maintain his so-called civilization, using scientific methods and machines to kill animals, one cannot even estimate the suffering awaiting him. So-called civilized people consider themselves very advanced in education, but they do not know about the stringent laws of nature. According to nature's law, it is a life for a life. We can hardly imagine the sufferings of one who maintains a slaughterhouse. He endures suffering not only in this life, but in his next life also. It is said that a hunter, murderer or killer is advised not to live and not to die. If he lives, he accumulates even more sins, which bring about more suffering in a future life. He is advised not to die because his dying means that he immediately begins to endure more suffering. Therefore he is advised not to live and not to die.

As followers of the Vedic principles, we accept the statements of Nārada Muni in this regard. It is our duty to see that no one suffers due to sinful activities. Foolish rascals are described in //Bhagavad-gītā// as //māyayāpahṛta-jñānāḥ,// which indicates that although they are superficially educated, //māyā// has taken their real knowledge away. Such people are presently leading human society. In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// they are also described as //andhā yathāndhair upanīyamānāḥ.// These rascals are themselves blind, and yet they are leading others who are blind. When people follow such leaders, they suffer unlimited pains in the future. Despite so-called advancement, all this is happening. Who is safe? Who is happy? Who is without anxiety?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.25
description: "The word kurvanti, which means 'they do something for others,' is a form of the verb 'things done for others.' It is used in connection with devotional service, which must be executed for the satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa. That is the purport of the word kurvanti.
text:
> 'kurvanti'-pada ei parasmaipada haya
> kṛṣṇa-sukha-nimitta bhajane tātparya kahaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kurvanti]]---they do (for others); [[synonyms:p:pada]]---the word; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:p:parasmaipada]]---a verb form indicating things done for others; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:n:nimitta]]---to satisfy Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhajane]]---in devotional service; [[synonyms:t:tātparya]]---the purport; [[synonyms:k:kahaya]]---is said.
translation: "The word kurvanti, which means 'they do something for others,' is a form of the verb 'things done for others.' It is used in connection with devotional service, which must be executed for the satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa. That is the purport of the word kurvanti.
purport: In Sanskrit the verb "to do" has two forms, technically called //parasmaipada// and //ātmanepada.// When things are done for one's personal satisfaction, the form is called //ātmanepada.// In that case, the word "do" in English is //kurvante// in Sanskrit. When things are done for others, the verb form changes to //kurvanti.// Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu informed Sanātana Gosvāmī that in the //ātmārāma// verse the verb //kurvanti// means that things should be done only for the satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa. This is supported by the grammarian Pāṇini. The verb is formed as //ātmanepada// when the work is to be done for one's own benefit, and when it is done for others, it is called //parasmaipada.// Thus the verb is formed according to whether something is done for one's self-satisfaction or for another's satisfaction.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.250
description: "Nārada Muni continued, 'My dear hunter, your business is killing animals. That is a slight offense on your part, but when you consciously give them unnecessary pain by leaving them half-dead, you incur very great sins.'
text:
> vyādha tumi, jīva māra---'alpa' aparādha tomāra
> kadarthanā diyā māra'---e pāpa 'apāra'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyādha]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you are a hunter; [[synonyms:j:jīva]] [[synonyms:m:māra]]---your occupation is to kill animals; [[synonyms:a:alpa]]---slight; [[synonyms:a:aparādha]]---offense; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:k:kadarthanā]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---unnecessarily giving them pain; [[synonyms:m:māra']]---when you kill; [[synonyms:e:e]] [[synonyms:p:pāpa]] [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---this sinful activity is unlimited.
translation: "Nārada Muni continued, 'My dear hunter, your business is killing animals. That is a slight offense on your part, but when you consciously give them unnecessary pain by leaving them half-dead, you incur very great sins.'
purport:
This is another good instruction to animal killers. There are always animal killers and animal eaters in human society because less civilized people are accustomed to eating meat. In Vedic civilization, meat-eaters are advised to kill an animal for the goddess Kālī or a similar demigod. This is in order not to give the animal unnecessary pain, as slaughterhouses do. In the //balidāna// sacrifice to a demigod, it is recommended to cut the throat of an animal with one slice. This should be done on a dark-moon night, and the painful noises expressed by the animal at the time of being slaughtered are not to be heard by anyone. There are also many other restrictions. Slaughter is only allowed once a month, and the killer of the animal has to suffer similar pains in his next life. At the present moment, so-called civilized men do not sacrifice animals to a deity in a religious or ritualistic way. They openly kill animals daily by the thousands for no purpose other than the satisfaction of the tongue. Because of this the entire world is suffering in so many ways. Politicians are unnecessarily declaring war, and, according to the stringent laws of material nature, massacres are taking place between nations.

> prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni
> guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ
> ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā
> kartāham iti manyate

"The bewildered spirit soul, under the influence of the three modes of material nature, thinks himself to be the doer of activities, which are in actuality carried out by nature." [[books:bg:3:27|(Bg. 3.27)]] The laws of //prakṛti// (nature) are very stringent. No one should think that he has the freedom to kill animals and not suffer the consequences. One cannot be safe by doing this. Nārada Muni herein says that animal killing is offensive, especially when animals are given unnecessary pain. Meat-eaters and animal killers are advised not to purchase meat from the slaughterhouse. They can worship Kālī once a month, kill some unimportant animal and eat it. Even by following this method, one is still an offender.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.251
description: "Nārada Muni continued, 'All the animals that you have killed and given unnecessary pain will kill you one after the other in your next life and in life after life.'
text:
> kadarthiyā tumi yata mārilā jīvere
> tārā taiche tomā māribe janma-janmāntare"

translation: "Nārada Muni continued, 'All the animals that you have killed and given unnecessary pain will kill you one after the other in your next life and in life after life.'
purport: This is another authoritative statement made by the great sage Nārada. Those who kill animals and give them unnecessary pain-as people do in slaughterhouses-will be killed in a similar way in the next life and in many lives to come. One can never be excused from such an offense. If one kills many thousands of animals in a professional way so that other people can purchase the meat to eat, one must be ready to be killed in a similar way in his next life and in life after life. There are many rascals who violate their own religious principles. According to Judeo-Christian scriptures, it is clearly said, "Thou shalt not kill." Nonetheless, giving all kinds of excuses, even the heads of religions indulge in killing animals while trying to pass as saintly persons. This mockery and hypocrisy in human society bring about unlimited calamities; therefore occasionally there are great wars. Masses of such people go out onto battlefields and kill themselves. Presently they have discovered the atomic bomb, which is simply awaiting wholesale destruction. If people want to be saved from the killing business life after life, they must take to Kṛṣṇa consciousness and cease sinful activity. The International Society for Krishna Consciousness recommends that everyone abandon meat-eating, illicit sex, intoxication and gambling. When one gives up these sinful activities, he can understand Kṛṣṇa and take to this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. We therefore request everyone to abandon sinful activity and chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra.// In this way people can save themselves from repeated birth and death.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.252
description: "In this way, through the association of the great sage Nārada Muni, the hunter was a little convinced of his sinful activity. He therefore became somewhat afraid due to his offenses.
text:
> nārada-saṅge vyādhera mana parasanna ha-ila
> tāṅra vākya śuni' mane bhaya upajila
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nārada]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the association of the great sage Nārada Muni; [[synonyms:v:vyādhera]]---of the hunter; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:p:parasanna]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became cleansed and satisfied; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:v:vākya]]---words; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]] [[synonyms:u:upajila]]---some fear arose.
translation: "In this way, through the association of the great sage Nārada Muni, the hunter was a little convinced of his sinful activity. He therefore became somewhat afraid due to his offenses.
purport:
This is the effect of associating with a pure devotee. Our preachers who are preaching Kṛṣṇa consciousness all over the world should follow in the footsteps of Nārada Muni and become purified by following the four principles and chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// This will make them fit to become Vaiṣṇavas. Then, when they speak to sinful people about the teachings of this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, people will be affected and take the instructions. We receive instructions in devotional service through the disciplic succession. Nārada Muni is our original //guru// because he is the spiritual master of Vyāsadeva. Vyāsadeva is the spiritual master of our disciplic succession; therefore we should follow in the footsteps of Nārada Muni and become pure Vaiṣṇavas. A pure Vaiṣṇava is one who has no ulterior motive. He has totally dedicated himself to the service of the Lord. He does not have material desires, and he is not interested in so-called learning and philanthropic work. The so-called learned scholars and philanthropists are actually //karmīs// and //jñānīs,// and some are actually misers engaged in sinful activity. All are condemned because they are not devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

This is a chance to become purified by associating with this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement and strictly following the rules and regulations. By chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra,// one can become free from all contamination, especially contamination brought about by the killing of animals. Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself requested:

> sarva-dharmān parityajya
> mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja
> ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo
> mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ

"Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reaction. Do not fear." [[books:bg:18:66|(Bg. 18.66)]]

We should take this instruction from Kṛṣṇa and follow in the footsteps of Nārada Muni in the disciplic succession. If we simply surrender unto Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet and take this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement seriously, we can be freed from the //karma// incurred by sin. If we are intelligent enough, we shall engage in the loving service of the Lord. Then our lives will be successful, and we shall not have to suffer like the hunter life after life. By killing animals, not only will we be bereft of the human form but we will have to take an animal form and somehow or other be killed by the same type of animal we have killed. This is the law of nature. The Sanskrit word //māṁsa// means "meat." It is said: //māṁ saḥ khadati iti māṁsaḥ.// That is, "I am now eating the flesh of an animal who will some day in the future be eating my flesh."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.253
description: "The hunter then admitted that he was convinced of his sinful activity, and he said, 'I have been taught this business from my very childhood. Now I am wondering how I can become freed from these unlimited volumes of sinful activity.'
text:
> vyādha kahe,---"bālya haite ei āmāra karma
> kemane tarimu muñi pāmara adhama?
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyādha]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the hunter said; [[synonyms:b:bālya]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the very beginning of my childhood; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:k:karma]]---I have been taught this business (half-killing animals); [[synonyms:k:kemane]]---how; [[synonyms:t:tarimu]]---shall become free from these sinful activities; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:p:pāmara]] [[synonyms:a:adhama]]---sinful and misled.
translation:
"The hunter then admitted that he was convinced of his sinful activity, and he said, 'I have been taught this business from my very childhood. Now I am wondering how I can become freed from these unlimited volumes of sinful activity.'


This kind of admission is very beneficial as long as one does not again commit sin. Cheating and hypocrisy are not tolerated by higher authorities. If one understands what sin is, he should give it up with sincerity and regret and surrender unto the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead through His agent, the pure devotee. In this way, one can be freed from the reactions of sin and make progress in devotional service. However, if one continues committing sins after making some atonement, he will not be saved. In the //śāstras,// such atonement is compared to an elephant's bathing. An elephant takes a very good bath and cleanses its body very nicely, but as soon as it comes out of the water, it picks up some dust on the shore and throws it all over its body. Atonement may be carried out very nicely, but it will not help a person if he continues committing sins. Therefore the hunter first admitted his sinful activity before the saintly person Nārada and then asked how he could be saved.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.254
description: "The hunter continued, 'My dear sir, please tell me how I can be relieved from the reactions of my sinful life. Now I fully surrender unto you and fall down at your lotus feet. Please deliver me from sinful reactions.'
text:
> ei pāpa yāya mora, kemana upāye?
> nistāra karaha more, paḍoṅ tomāra pāye"
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]] [[synonyms:m:mora]]---sinful reaction of my life can be washed off; [[synonyms:k:kemana]] [[synonyms:u:upāye]]---by what means; [[synonyms:n:nistāra]] [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:m:more]]---kindly deliver me; [[synonyms:p:paḍoṅ]]---I fall down; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:p:pāye]]---at your lotus feet.
translation: "The hunter continued, 'My dear sir, please tell me how I can be relieved from the reactions of my sinful life. Now I fully surrender unto you and fall down at your lotus feet. Please deliver me from sinful reactions.'
purport: By the grace of Nārada Muni, the hunter came to his good senses and immediately surrendered unto the saint's lotus feet. This is the process. By associating with a saintly person, one is able to understand the reactions of his sinful life. When one voluntarily surrenders to a saintly person who is a representative of Kṛṣṇa and follows his instructions, one can become freed from sinful reaction. Kṛṣṇa demands the surrender of a sinful man, and Kṛṣṇa's representative gives the same instructions. The representative of Kṛṣṇa never tells his disciple, "Surrender unto me." Rather he says, "Surrender unto Kṛṣṇa." If the disciple accepts this principle and surrenders himself through the representative of Kṛṣṇa, his life is saved.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.255
description: "Nārada Muni assured the hunter, 'If you listen to my instructions, I shall find the way you can be liberated.'
text:
> nārada kahe,---'yadi dhara āmāra vacana
> tabe se karite pāri tomāra mocana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nārada]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Nārada Muni replied; [[synonyms:y:yadi]] [[synonyms:d:dhara]]---if you accept; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---my instruction; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:s:se]]---this; [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---I can do; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:m:mocana]]---liberation.
translation: "Nārada Muni assured the hunter, 'If you listen to my instructions, I shall find the way you can be liberated.'
purport: Gaurāṅgera bhakta-gaṇe jane jane śakti dhare. The purport of this song is that the devotees of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are very powerful, and each and every one of them can deliver the whole world. What, then, to speak of Nārada Muni? If one follows the instructions of Nārada Muni, one can be delivered from any amount of sinful reactions. This is the process. One must follow the instructions of a spiritual master; then one will certainly be delivered from all sinful reaction. This is the secret of success. //Yasya deve parā bhaktir yathā deve tathā gurau.// If one has unflinching faith in Kṛṣṇa and the spiritual master, the result is //tasyaite kathitā hy arthāḥ prakāśante mahātmanaḥ:// all the conclusions of revealed scriptures will be open to such a person. A pure devotee of Kṛṣṇa can make the same demands that Nārada Muni is making. He says, "If you follow my instructions, I shall take responsibility for your liberation." A pure devotee like Nārada can give assurance to any sinful man because by the grace of the Lord such a devotee is empowered to deliver any sinful person if that person follows the principles set forth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.256
description: "The hunter then said, 'My dear sir, whatever you say I shall do.' Nārada immediately ordered him, 'First of all, break your bow. Then I shall tell you what is to be done.'
text:
> vyādha kahe,---'yei kaha, sei ta' kariba'
> nārada kahe,---'dhanuka bhāṅga, tabe se kahiba'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyādha]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the hunter replied; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---whatever you say; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']] [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---that I shall do; [[synonyms:n:nārada]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Nārada Muni replied; [[synonyms:d:dhanuka]] [[synonyms:b:bhāṅga]]---break your bow; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:k:kahiba]]---I shall speak to you.
translation: "The hunter then said, 'My dear sir, whatever you say I shall do.' Nārada immediately ordered him, 'First of all, break your bow. Then I shall tell you what is to be done.'
purport: This is the process of initiation. The disciple must admit that he will no longer commit sinful activity-namely illicit sex, meat-eating, gambling and intoxication. He promises to execute the order of the spiritual master. Then the spiritual master takes care of him and elevates him to spiritual emancipation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.257
description: "The hunter replied, 'If I break my bow, how shall I maintain myself?' Nārada Muni replied, 'Do not worry. I shall supply all your food every day.'
text:
> vyādha kahe,---'dhanuka bhāṅgile vartiba kemane?'
> nārada kahe,---'āmi anna diba prati-dine'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyādha]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the hunter replied; [[synonyms:d:dhanuka]] [[synonyms:b:bhāṅgile]]---if I break my bow; [[synonyms:v:vartiba]] [[synonyms:k:kemane]]---what will be the source of my maintenance; [[synonyms:n:nārada]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Nārada Muni replied; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food; [[synonyms:d:diba]]---shall supply; [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---every day.
translation: "The hunter replied, 'If I break my bow, how shall I maintain myself?' Nārada Muni replied, 'Do not worry. I shall supply all your food every day.'
purport: The source of our income is not actually the source of our maintenance. Every living being-from the great Brahmā down to an insignificant ant-is being maintained by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. //Eko bahūnāṁ yo vidadhāti kāmān.// The one Supreme Being, Kṛṣṇa, maintains everyone. Our so-called source of income is our own choice only. If I wish to be a hunter, it will appear that hunting is the source of my income. If I become a //brāhmaṇa// and completely depend on Kṛṣṇa, I do not conduct a business, but nonetheless my maintenance is supplied by Kṛṣṇa. The hunter was disturbed about breaking his bow because he was worried about his income. Nārada Muni assured the hunter because he knew that the hunter was not being maintained by the bow but by Kṛṣṇa. Being the agent of Kṛṣṇa, Nārada Muni knew very well that the hunter would not suffer by breaking the bow. There was no doubt that Kṛṣṇa would supply him food.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.258
description: "Being thus assured by the great sage Nārada Muni, the hunter broke his bow, immediately fell down at the saint's lotus feet and fully surrendered. After this, Nārada Muni raised him with his hand and gave him instructions for spiritual advancement.
text:
> dhanuka bhāṅgi' vyādha tāṅra caraṇe paḍila
> tāre uṭhāñā nārada upadeśa kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dhanuka]] [[synonyms:b:bhāṅgi']]---breaking the bow; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---the hunter; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his (Nārada Muni's); [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:p:paḍila]]---surrendered; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---him; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāñā]]---raising; [[synonyms:n:nārada]]---the great saint Nārada Muni; [[synonyms:u:upadeśa]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---gave instruction.
translation: "Being thus assured by the great sage Nārada Muni, the hunter broke his bow, immediately fell down at the saint's lotus feet and fully surrendered. After this, Nārada Muni raised him with his hand and gave him instructions for spiritual advancement.
purport: This is the process of initiation. The disciple must surrender to the spiritual master, the representative of Kṛṣṇa. The spiritual master, being in the disciplic succession stemming from Nārada Muni, is in the same category with Nārada Muni. A person can be relieved from his sinful activity if he surrenders to the lotus feet of a person who actually represents Nārada Muni. Nārada Muni gave instructions to the hunter after the hunter surrendered.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.259
description: "Nārada Muni then advised the hunter, 'Return home and distribute whatever riches you have to the pure brāhmaṇas who know the Absolute Truth. After distributing all your riches to the brāhmaṇas, both you and your wife should leave home, taking only one cloth to wear.'
text:
> "ghare giyā brāhmaṇe deha' yata āche dhana
> eka eka vastra pari' bāhira hao dui-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:ghare]] [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---returning home; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇe]]---to the //brāhmaṇas,// the most intelligent men in spiritual understanding; [[synonyms:d:deha']]---give; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---whatever; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---you have; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---riches; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:e:eka]]---each of you; [[synonyms:v:vastra]] [[synonyms:p:pari']]---just one cloth; [[synonyms:b:bāhira]] [[synonyms:h:hao]]---leave home; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---both of you.
translation: "Nārada Muni then advised the hunter, 'Return home and distribute whatever riches you have to the pure brāhmaṇas who know the Absolute Truth. After distributing all your riches to the brāhmaṇas, both you and your wife should leave home, taking only one cloth to wear.'
purport: This is the process of renunciation at the stage of //vānaprastha.// After enjoying householder life for some time, the husband and wife must leave home and distribute their riches to //brāhmaṇas// and Vaiṣṇavas. One can keep his wife as an assistant in the //vānaprastha// stage. The idea is that the wife will assist the husband in spiritual advancement. Therefore Nārada Muni advised the hunter to adopt the //vānaprastha// stage and leave home. It is not that a //gṛhastha// should live at home until he dies. //Vānaprastha// is preliminary to //sannyāsa.// In the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement there are many young couples engaged in the Lord's service. Eventually they are supposed to take //vānaprastha,// and after the //vānaprastha// stage the husband may take //sannyāsa// in order to preach. The wife may then remain alone and serve the Deity or engage in other activities within the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.26
description: " 'The terminations of the ātmanepada are employed when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent of verbs having an indicatory ñ or a svarita accent.'
text: > "svaritañitaḥ kartrabhiprāye kriyā-phale"
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarita]]-[[synonyms:ñ:ñitaḥ]]---of verbs having an indicatory //ñ// or a //svarita// accent; [[synonyms:k:kartṛ]]-[[synonyms:a:abhiprāye]]---is meant for the agent; [[synonyms:k:kriyā]]-[[synonyms:p:phale]]---when the fruit of the action.
translation: “ 'The terminations of the ātmanepada are employed when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent of verbs having an indicatory ñ or a svarita accent.'
purport: This is a quotation from Pāṇini's //sūtras// (1.3.72).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.260
description: "Nārada Muni continued, 'Leave your home and go to the river. There you should construct a small cottage, and in front of the cottage you should grow a tulasī plant on a raised platform.
text:
> nadī-tīre eka-khāni kuṭīra kariyā
> tāra āge eka-piṇḍi tulasī ropiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nadī]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank of the river; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:k:khāni]]---just one; [[synonyms:k:kuṭīra]]---a cottage; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---constructing; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---just in front of the cottage; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:p:piṇḍi]]---one raised platform; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]---a tulasī plant; [[synonyms:r:ropiyā]]---growing.
translation: "Nārada Muni continued, 'Leave your home and go to the river. There you should construct a small cottage, and in front of the cottage you should grow a tulasī plant on a raised platform.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.261
description: " 'After planting the tulasī tree before your house, you should daily circumambulate that tulasī plant, serve her by giving her water and other things, and continuously chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.'
text:
> tulasī-parikramā kara, tulasī-sevana
> nirantara kṛṣṇa-nāma kariha kīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]-[[synonyms:p:parikramā]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---circumambulate the tulasī plant; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]-[[synonyms:s:sevana]]---just supply water to the root of tulasī-devī; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---continuously; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---just perform; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---chanting.
translation: “ 'After planting the tulasī tree before your house, you should daily circumambulate that tulasī plant, serve her by giving her water and other things, and continuously chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.'
purport: This is the beginning of spiritual life. After leaving householder life, one may go to a holy place, such as the bank of the Ganges or Yamunā, and erect a small cottage. A small cottage can be constructed without any expenditure. Four logs serving as pillars can be secured by any man from the forest. The roof can be covered with leaves, and one can cleanse the inside. Thus one can live very peacefully. In any condition, any man can live in a small cottage, plant a //tulasī// tree, water it in the morning, offer it prayers, and continuously chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// Thus one can make vigorous spiritual advancement. This is not at all difficult. One simply has to follow the instructions of the spiritual master strictly. Then everything will be successful in due course of time. As far as eating is concerned, there is no problem. If Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, supplies everyone with eatables, why should He not supply His devotee? Sometimes a devotee will not even bother to construct a cottage. He will simply go to live in a mountain cave. One may live in a cave, in a cottage beside a river, in a palace or in a big city like New York or London. In any case, a devotee can follow the instructions of his spiritual master and engage in devotional service by watering the //tulasī// plant and chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra.// Taking the advice of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and our spiritual master, Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Mahārāja, one can go to any part of the world and instruct people to become devotees of the Lord by following the regulative principles, worshiping the //tulasī// plant and continuously chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.262
description: "Nārada Muni continued, 'I shall send sufficient food to you both every day. You can take as much food as you want.'
text:
> āmi tomāya bahu anna pāṭhāimu dine
> sei anna labe, yata khāo dui-jane"
