synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tomāya]]---for you; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---much; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāimu]]---shall send; [[synonyms:d:dine]]---every day; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food; [[synonyms:l:labe]]---you shall take; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---whatever; [[synonyms:k:khāo]]---you can eat; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---both of you.
translation: "Nārada Muni continued, 'I shall send sufficient food to you both every day. You can take as much food as you want.'
purport:
When a person takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, there is no need to care for material necessities. Kṛṣṇa says that He personally carries all the necessities to His devotees.

> ananyāś cintayanto māṁ
> ye janāḥ paryupāsate
> teṣāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ
> yoga-kṣemaṁ vahāmy aham

"Those who worship Me with love and devotion, meditating on My transcendental form-to them I carry what they lack and preserve what they have." [[books:bg:9:22|(Bg. 9.22)]] Why should one be anxious about the necessities of life? The principle should be that one should not want more than what is absolutely necessary. Nārada Muni advises the hunter to accept only what is absolutely necessary for him and his wife. The devotee should always be alert to consume only those things that he absolutely requires and not create unnecessary needs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.263
description: "The three animals that were half-killed were then brought to their consciousness by the sage Nārada. Indeed, the animals got up and swiftly fled.
text:
> tabe sei mṛgādi tine nārada sustha kaila
> sustha hañā mṛgādi tine dhāñā palāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---animals, beginning with the deer; [[synonyms:t:tine]]---three; [[synonyms:n:nārada]]---the sage Nārada; [[synonyms:s:sustha]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---brought to their senses; [[synonyms:s:sustha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---coming to consciousness; [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the pierced animals; [[synonyms:t:tine]]---three; [[synonyms:d:dhāñā]] [[synonyms:p:palāila]]---very swiftly fled away from that place.
translation: "The three animals that were half-killed were then brought to their consciousness by the sage Nārada. Indeed, the animals got up and swiftly fled.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.264
description: "When the hunter saw the half-killed animals flee, he was certainly struck with wonder. He then offered his respectful obeisances to the sage Nārada and returned home.
text:
> dekhiyā vyādhera mane haila camatkāra
> ghare gela vyādha, guruke kari' namaskāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:v:vyādhera]]---of the hunter; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---wonder; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---home; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---the hunter; [[synonyms:g:guruke]]---to the spiritual master; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---offering obeisances.
translation: "When the hunter saw the half-killed animals flee, he was certainly struck with wonder. He then offered his respectful obeisances to the sage Nārada and returned home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.265
description: "After all this, Nārada Muni went to his destination. After the hunter returned home, he exactly followed the instructions of his spiritual master, Nārada.
text:
> yathā-sthāne nārada gelā, vyādha ghare āila
> nāradera upadeśe sakala karila
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yathā]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the proper destination; [[synonyms:n:nārada]]---sage Nārada; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---the hunter; [[synonyms:g:ghare]] [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came back to his house; [[synonyms:n:nāradera]] [[synonyms:u:upadeśe]]---under the instruction of the sage Nārada; [[synonyms:s:sakala]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---he executed everything.
translation: "After all this, Nārada Muni went to his destination. After the hunter returned home, he exactly followed the instructions of his spiritual master, Nārada.
purport: For spiritual advancement one must have a bona fide spiritual master and follow his instructions in order to be assured of advancement.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.266
description: "The news that the hunter had become a Vaiṣṇava spread all over the village. Indeed, all the villagers brought alms and presented them to the Vaiṣṇava who was formerly a hunter.
text:
> grāme dhvani haila,---vyādha 'vaiṣṇava' ha-ila
> grāmera loka saba anna ānite lāgila
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in the village; [[synonyms:d:dhvani]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was news; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---the hunter; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---has become a Vaiṣṇava, a lover and servitor of Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:g:grāmera]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the villagers; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all kinds of; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food; [[synonyms:ā:ānite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began to bring.
translation: "The news that the hunter had become a Vaiṣṇava spread all over the village. Indeed, all the villagers brought alms and presented them to the Vaiṣṇava who was formerly a hunter.
purport: It is the duty of the public to present a gift to a saintly person, Vaiṣṇava or //brāhmaṇa// when going to see him. Every Vaiṣṇava is dependent on Kṛṣṇa, and Kṛṣṇa is ready to supply all of life's necessities, provided a Vaiṣṇava follows the principles set forth by the spiritual master. There are certainly many householders in our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. They join the movement and live in the society's centers, but if they take advantage of this opportunity and do not work but live at the expense of the movement, eating //prasāda// and simply sleeping, they place themselves in a very dangerous position. It is therefore advised that //gṛhasthas// should not live in the temple. They must live outside the temple and maintain themselves. Of course, if the //gṛhasthas// are fully engaged in the Lord's service according to the directions of the authorities, there is no harm in their living in a temple. In any case, a temple should not be a place to eat and sleep. A temple manager should be very careful about these things.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.267
description: "In one day enough food was brought for ten or twenty people, but the hunter and his wife would accept only as much as they could eat.
text:
> eka-dina anna āne daśa-biśa jane
> dine tata laya, yata khāya dui jane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---in one day; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food; [[synonyms:ā:āne]]---brought; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:b:biśa]] [[synonyms:j:jane]]---enough for ten to twenty men; [[synonyms:d:dine]]---in a day; [[synonyms:t:tata]] [[synonyms:l:laya]]---would accept only as much; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---as; [[synonyms:k:khāya]] [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jane]]---the two of them required to eat.
translation: "In one day enough food was brought for ten or twenty people, but the hunter and his wife would accept only as much as they could eat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.268
description: "One day, while speaking to his friend Parvata Muni, Nārada Muni requested him to go with him to see his disciple the hunter.
text:
> eka-dina nārada kahe,---"śunaha, parvate
> āmāra eka śiṣya āche, calaha dekhite"
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:n:nārada]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Nārada Muni said; [[synonyms:ś:śunaha]]---please hear; [[synonyms:p:parvate]]---my dear Parvata; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---my; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]---disciple; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there is; [[synonyms:c:calaha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---let us go see.
translation: "One day, while speaking to his friend Parvata Muni, Nārada Muni requested him to go with him to see his disciple the hunter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.269
description: "When the saintly sages came to the hunter's place, the hunter could see them coming from a distance.
text:
> tabe dui ṛṣi āilā sei vyādha-sthāne
> dūra haite vyādha pāila gurura daraśane
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣi]]---two saintly persons; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the place of that hunter; [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from a distant place; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---the hunter; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got; [[synonyms:g:gurura]] [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---vision of his spiritual master.
translation: "When the saintly sages came to the hunter's place, the hunter could see them coming from a distance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.27
description: "The word hetu [cause] means that a thing is done for some motive. There can be three motives. One may act to enjoy the result personally, to achieve some material perfection, or to act in such a way that one may be liberated.
text:
> 'hetu'-śabde kahe---bhukti-ādi vāñchāntare
> bhukti, siddhi, mukti---mukhya ei tina prakāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hetu]]---cause; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it is said; [[synonyms:b:bhukti]]---enjoying the result by oneself; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and so on; [[synonyms:v:vāñchā]]-[[synonyms:a:antare]]---because of a different ambition; [[synonyms:b:bhukti]]---enjoying the result of action; [[synonyms:s:siddhi]]---the perfection of doing something; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---chief; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:p:prakāre]]---in three ways.
translation: "The word hetu [cause] means that a thing is done for some motive. There can be three motives. One may act to enjoy the result personally, to achieve some material perfection, or to act in such a way that one may be liberated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.270
description: "With great alacrity the hunter began to run toward his spiritual master, but he could not fall down and offer obeisances because ants were running hither and thither around his feet.
text:
> āste-vyaste dhāñā āse, patha nāhi pāya
> pathera pipīlikā iti-uti dhare pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āste]]-[[synonyms:v:vyaste]]---with great alacrity; [[synonyms:d:dhāñā]]---running; [[synonyms:ā:āse]]---came; [[synonyms:p:patha]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---does not get the path; [[synonyms:p:pathera]]---on the path; [[synonyms:p:pipīlikā]]---ants; [[synonyms:i:iti]]-[[synonyms:u:uti]]---here and there; [[synonyms:d:dhare]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---touch the foot.
translation: "With great alacrity the hunter began to run toward his spiritual master, but he could not fall down and offer obeisances because ants were running hither and thither around his feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.271
description: "Seeing the ants, the hunter whisked them away with a piece of cloth. After thus clearing the ants from the ground, he fell down flat to offer his obeisances.
text:
> daṇḍavat-sthāne pipīlikāre dekhiyā
> vastre sthāna jhāḍi' paḍe daṇḍavat hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in the place where he wanted to offer his obeisances; [[synonyms:p:pipīlikāre]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing the ants; [[synonyms:v:vastre]]---by the cloth; [[synonyms:s:sthāna]] [[synonyms:j:jhāḍi']]---cleansing the place; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]] [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---falls down flat like a rod.
translation: "Seeing the ants, the hunter whisked them away with a piece of cloth. After thus clearing the ants from the ground, he fell down flat to offer his obeisances.
purport: The word //daṇḍa// means "rod," and //vat// means "like." To offer obeisances to the spiritual master, one must fall flat exactly as a rod falls on the ground. This is the meaning of the word //daṇḍavat.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.272
description: "Nārada Muni said, 'My dear hunter, such behavior is not at all astonishing. A man in devotional service is automatically nonviolent. He is the best of gentlemen.
text:
> nārada kahe,---"vyādha, ei nā haya āścarya
> hari-bhaktye hiṁsā-śūnya haya sādhu-varya
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nārada]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Nārada Muni said; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---my dear hunter; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:ā:āścarya]]---this is not wonderful for you; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---by advancement in devotional service; [[synonyms:h:hiṁsā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śūnya]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---one becomes nonviolent and nonenvious; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:v:varya]]---thus one becomes the best of honest gentlemen.
translation: "Nārada Muni said, 'My dear hunter, such behavior is not at all astonishing. A man in devotional service is automatically nonviolent. He is the best of gentlemen.
purport: In this verse the word //sādhu-varya// means "the best of gentlemen." At the present moment there are many so-called gentlemen who are expert in killing animals and birds. Nonetheless, these so-called gentlemen profess a type of religion that strictly prohibits killing. According to Nārada Muni and Vedic culture, animal killers are not even gentlemen, to say nothing of being religious men. A religious person, a devotee of the Lord, must be nonviolent. Such is the nature of a religious person. It is contradictory to be violent and at the same time call oneself a religious person. Such hypocrisy is not approved by Nārada Muni and the disciplic succession.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.273
description: " 'O hunter, good qualities like nonviolence, which you have developed, are not very astonishing, for those engaged in the Lord's devotional service are never inclined to give pain to others because of envy.'
text:
> ete na hy adbhutā vyādha
> tavāhiṁsādayo guṇāḥ
> hari-bhaktau pravṛttā ye
> na te syuḥ paratāpinaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ete]]---all these; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:adbhutāḥ]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---O hunter; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---your; [[synonyms:a:ahiṁsā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādayaḥ]]---nonviolence and others; [[synonyms:g:guṇāḥ]]---qualities; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktau]]---in devotional service; [[synonyms:p:pravṛttāḥ]]---engaged; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---those who; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:t:te]]---they; [[synonyms:s:syuḥ]]---are; [[synonyms:p:paratāpinaḥ]]---envious of other living entities.
translation: “ 'O hunter, good qualities like nonviolence, which you have developed, are not very astonishing, for those engaged in the Lord's devotional service are never inclined to give pain to others because of envy.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Skanda Purāṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.274
description: "The hunter then received both the great sages in the courtyard of his house. He spread out a straw mat for them to sit upon, and with great devotion he begged them to sit down.
text:
> tabe sei vyādha doṅhāre aṅgane ānila
> kuśāsana āni' doṅhāre bhaktye vasāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]]---hunter; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāre]]---both Nārada Muni and Parvata; [[synonyms:a:aṅgane]] [[synonyms:ā:ānila]]---brought in the courtyard of his house; [[synonyms:k:kuśa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsana]] [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing straw mats for sitting; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāre]]---both of them; [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---with great devotion; [[synonyms:v:vasāila]]---made to sit down.
translation: "The hunter then received both the great sages in the courtyard of his house. He spread out a straw mat for them to sit upon, and with great devotion he begged them to sit down.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.275
description: "He then fetched water and washed the sages' feet with great devotion. Then both husband and wife drank that water and sprinkled it on their heads.
text:
> jala āni' bhaktye doṅhāra pāda prakṣālila
> sei jala strī-puruṣe piyā śire la-ila
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jala]] [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing water; [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---with great devotion; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]]---of both of them; [[synonyms:p:pāda]] [[synonyms:p:prakṣālila]]---washed the feet; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:j:jala]]---that water; [[synonyms:s:strī]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣe]]---husband and wife; [[synonyms:p:piyā]]---drinking; [[synonyms:ś:śire]] [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---put on their heads.
translation: "He then fetched water and washed the sages' feet with great devotion. Then both husband and wife drank that water and sprinkled it on their heads.
purport: This is the process one should follow when receiving the spiritual master or someone on the level of the spiritual master. When the spiritual master comes to the residence of his disciples, the disciples should follow in the footsteps of the former hunter. It doesn't matter what one was before initiation. After initiation, one must learn the etiquette mentioned herein.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.276
description: "When the hunter chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra before his spiritual master, his body trembled, and tears welled in his eyes. Filled with ecstatic love, he raised his hands and began to dance, waving his garments up and down.
text:
> kampa-pulakāśru haila kṛṣṇa-nāma gāñā
> ūrdhva bāhu nṛtya kare vastra uḍāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]-[[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears and jubilation; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there were; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:g:gāñā]]---chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra//; [[synonyms:ū:ūrdhva]] [[synonyms:b:bāhu]]---raising the arms; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---began to dance; [[synonyms:v:vastra]] [[synonyms:u:uḍāñā]]---waving his garments up and down.
translation: "When the hunter chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra before his spiritual master, his body trembled, and tears welled in his eyes. Filled with ecstatic love, he raised his hands and began to dance, waving his garments up and down.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.277
description: "When Parvata Muni saw the ecstatic loving symptoms of the hunter, he told Nārada, 'Certainly you are a touchstone.'
text:
> dekhiyā vyādhera prema parvata-mahāmuni
> nāradere kahe,---tumi hao sparśa-maṇi
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:v:vyādhera]]---of the hunter; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---the ecstatic love; [[synonyms:p:parvata]]-[[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:m:muni]]---the great sage Parvata Muni; [[synonyms:n:nāradere]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---spoke to Nārada Muni; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:h:hao]] [[synonyms:s:sparśa]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇi]]---you are certainly a touchstone.
translation: "When Parvata Muni saw the ecstatic loving symptoms of the hunter, he told Nārada, 'Certainly you are a touchstone.'
purport:
When a touchstone touches iron, it turns the iron to gold. Parvata Muni called Nārada Muni a touchstone because by his touch the hunter, who was lowest among men, became an elevated and perfect Vaiṣṇava. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura said that the position of a Vaiṣṇava can be tested by seeing how good a touchstone he is---that is, by seeing how many Vaiṣṇavas he has made during his life. A Vaiṣṇava should be a touchstone so that he can convert others to Vaiṣṇavism by his preaching, even though people may be fallen like the hunter. There are many so-called advanced devotees who sit in a secluded place for their personal benefit. They do not go out to preach and convert others into Vaiṣṇavas, and therefore they certainly cannot be called //sparśa-maṇi,// advanced devotees. //Kaniṣṭha-adhikārī// devotees cannot turn others into Vaiṣṇavas, but a //madhyama-adhikārī// Vaiṣṇava can do so by preaching. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu advised His followers to increase the numbers of Vaiṣṇavas.

> yāre dekha, tāre kaha 'kṛṣṇa'-upadeśa
> āmāra ājñāya guru hañā tāra' ei deśa

(Cc. Madhya 7.128)

It is Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's wish that everyone should become a Vaiṣṇava and //guru.// Following the instructions of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His disciplic succession, one can become a spiritual master, for the process is very easy. One can go everywhere and anywhere to preach the instructions of Kṛṣṇa. //Bhagavad-gītā// is Kṛṣṇa's instructions; therefore the duty of every Vaiṣṇava is to travel and preach //Bhagavad-gītā,// either in his country or a foreign country. This is the test of //sparśa-maṇi,// following in the footsteps of Nārada Muni.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.278
description: "Parvata Muni continued, 'My dear friend Nārada Muni, you are glorified as the sage among the demigods. By your mercy, even a lowborn person like this hunter can immediately become attached to Lord Kṛṣṇa.'
text:
> "aho dhanyo 'si devarṣe
> kṛpayā yasya tat-kṣaṇāt
> nīco 'py utpulako lebhe
> lubdhako ratim acyute"
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aho]]---oh; [[synonyms:d:dhanyaḥ]]---glorified; [[synonyms:a:asi]]---you are; [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣe]]---O sage among the demigods; [[synonyms:k:kṛpayā]]---by the mercy; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇāt]]---immediately; [[synonyms:n:nīcaḥ]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---even though one is the lowest of men; [[synonyms:u:utpulakaḥ]]---becoming agitated in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:l:lebhe]]---gets; [[synonyms:l:lubdhakaḥ]]---a hunter; [[synonyms:r:ratim]]---attraction; [[synonyms:a:acyute]]---unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: "Parvata Muni continued, 'My dear friend Nārada Muni, you are glorified as the sage among the demigods. By your mercy, even a lowborn person like this hunter can immediately become attached to Lord Kṛṣṇa.'
purport: A pure Vaiṣṇava believes in the statements of the //śāstras.// This verse is quoted from Vedic literature, the //Skanda Purāṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.279
description: "Nārada Muni then asked the hunter, 'My dear Vaiṣṇava, do you have some income for your maintenance?' The hunter replied, 'My dear spiritual master, whoever you send gives me something when he comes to see me.'
text:
> nārada kahe,---'vaiṣṇava, tomāra anna kichu āya?'
> vyādha kahe, "yāre pāṭhāo, sei diyā yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nārada]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Nārada Muni said; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---O Vaiṣṇava; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food; [[synonyms:k:kichu]] [[synonyms:ā:āya]]---does any come; [[synonyms:v:vyādha]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the hunter replied; [[synonyms:y:yāre]] [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāo]]---whoever you send; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that person; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving something; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes.
translation: "Nārada Muni then asked the hunter, 'My dear Vaiṣṇava, do you have some income for your maintenance?' The hunter replied, 'My dear spiritual master, whoever you send gives me something when he comes to see me.'
purport: This confirms the statement in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:22|(Bg. 9.22)]] to the effect that the Lord carries all necessities to His Vaiṣṇava devotee. Nārada Muni asked the former hunter how he was being maintained, and he replied that everyone who came to see him brought him something for his maintenance. Kṛṣṇa, who is situated in everyone's heart, says, "I personally carry all necessities to a Vaiṣṇava." He can order anyone to execute this. Everyone is ready to give something to a Vaiṣṇava, and if a Vaiṣṇava is completely engaged in devotional service, he need not be anxious for his maintenance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.28
description: "First we take the word bhukti [material enjoyment], which is of unlimited variety. We may also take the word siddhi [perfection], which has eighteen varieties. Similarly, the word mukti has five varieties.
text:
> eka bhukti kahe, bhoga---ananta-prakāra
> siddhi---aṣṭādaśa, mukti---pañca-vidhākāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]---first; [[synonyms:b:bhukti]]---material enjoyment by doing something; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---is known; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---enjoyment; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---unlimited varieties; [[synonyms:s:siddhi]]---the yogic perfections; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭādaśa]]---eighteen in number; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:v:vidhā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---five varieties.
translation: "First we take the word bhukti [material enjoyment], which is of unlimited variety. We may also take the word siddhi [perfection], which has eighteen varieties. Similarly, the word mukti has five varieties.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.280
description: "The former hunter said, 'Please do not send so may grains. Only send what is sufficient for two people, no more.'
text:
> eta anna nā pāṭhāo, kichu kārya nāi
> sabe dui-janāra yogya bhakṣya-mātra cāi"
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:a:anna]]---so much food; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāo]]---you do not need to send; [[synonyms:k:kichu]] [[synonyms:k:kārya]] [[synonyms:n:nāi]]---there is no such need; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---only; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:janāra]]---for two persons; [[synonyms:y:yogya]]---requisite; [[synonyms:b:bhakṣya]]-[[synonyms:m:mātra]]---eatables; [[synonyms:c:cāi]]---we want.
translation: "The former hunter said, 'Please do not send so may grains. Only send what is sufficient for two people, no more.'
purport: The former hunter only wanted enough for two people to eat, no more. It is not necessary for a Vaiṣṇava to keep a stock of food for the next day. He should receive only sufficient grains to last one day. The next day, he must again depend on the Lord's mercy. This is the instruction of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. When His personal servant Govinda sometimes kept a stock of //harītakī// (myrobalan), Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu chastised him, saying, "Why did you keep a stock for the next day?" Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and others were begging daily from door to door for their sustenance, and they never attempted to stock their //āśrama// with food for the next day. We should not materially calculate, thinking, "It is better to stock food for a week. Why give the Lord trouble by having Him bring food daily?" One should be convinced that the Lord will provide daily. There is no need to stock food for the next day.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.281
description: "Nārada Muni approved his not wanting more than a daily supply of food, and he blessed him, saying, 'You are fortunate.' Nārada Muni and Parvata Muni then disappeared from that place.
text:
> nārada kahe,---'aiche raha, tumi bhāgyavān'
> eta bali' dui-jana ha-ilā antardhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nārada]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Nārada Muni said; [[synonyms:a:aiche]] [[synonyms:r:raha]]---live like that; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:b:bhāgyavān]]---certainly you are very fortunate; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---both Nārada Muni and Parvata Muni; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]] [[synonyms:a:antardhāna]]---disappeared.
translation: "Nārada Muni approved his not wanting more than a daily supply of food, and he blessed him, saying, 'You are fortunate.' Nārada Muni and Parvata Muni then disappeared from that place.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.282
description: "So far I have narrated the incident of the hunter. By hearing this narration, one can understand the influence derived by associating with devotees.
text:
> ei ta' kahiluṅ tomāya vyādhera ākhyāna
> yā śunile haya sādhu-saṅga-prabhāva-jñāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']] [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---thus I have narrated; [[synonyms:t:tomāya]]---unto you; [[synonyms:v:vyādhera]] [[synonyms:ā:ākhyāna]]---the story of the hunter; [[synonyms:y:yā]] [[synonyms:ś:śunile]]---hearing which; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---of the association of devotees; [[synonyms:p:prabhāva]]---of the influence; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge.
translation: "So far I have narrated the incident of the hunter. By hearing this narration, one can understand the influence derived by associating with devotees.
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to stress that even a hunter, the lowest of men, could become a topmost Vaiṣṇava simply by associating with Nārada Muni or a devotee in his bona fide disciplic succession.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.283
description: "In this way we have found three more meanings. Combine these with the other meanings, and the total number of meanings add up to twenty-six in all.
text:
> ei āra tina artha gaṇanāte pāila
> ei dui artha mili' 'chābbiśa' artha haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this example; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---three imports; [[synonyms:g:gaṇanāte]]---in calculating; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---we have obtained; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:m:mili']]---by adding these two imports; [[synonyms:c:chābbiśa]]---twenty-six; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---imports; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there have been.
translation: "In this way we have found three more meanings. Combine these with the other meanings, and the total number of meanings add up to twenty-six in all.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.284
description: "There is yet another meaning, which is full of a variety of imports. Actually there are two gross meanings and thirty-two subtle meanings.
text:
> āra artha śuna, yāhā---arthera bhāṇḍāra
> sthūle 'dui' artha, sūkṣme 'batriśa' prakāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---import; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]]---which; [[synonyms:a:arthera]] [[synonyms:b:bhāṇḍāra]]---storehouse of knowledge; [[synonyms:s:sthūle]]---grossly; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---two meanings; [[synonyms:s:sūkṣme]]---by a subtle import; [[synonyms:b:batriśa]]---thirty-two; [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---varieties.
translation: "There is yet another meaning, which is full of a variety of imports. Actually there are two gross meanings and thirty-two subtle meanings.
purport: The two gross meanings refer to regulative devotional service and spontaneous devotional service. There are also thirty-two subtle meanings. Under the heading of regulative devotional service, there are sixteen meanings: (1) a servant of the Lord as His personal associate, (2) a personal friend, (3) personal parents or similar superiors, (4) a personal beloved, (5) a servant elevated by spiritual cultivation, (6) a friend by spiritual cultivation, (7) parents and superior devotees by cultivation of devotional service, (8) a beloved wife or female friend by cultivation of devotional service, (9) a mature devotee as a servant, (10) a mature devotee as a friend, (11) a mature devotee as a parent and superior, (12) a mature devotee as wife and beloved, (13) an immature devotee as servant, (14) an immature devotee as a friend, (15) an immature devotee as father and superior, and (16) an immature devotee as a beloved. Similarly, under the heading of spontaneous devotion there are also sixteen various associates. Therefore the total number of devotees under the headings of regular devotees and spontaneous devotees is thirty-two.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.285
description: "The word ātmā refers to all the different expansions of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. One of them is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself, Kṛṣṇa, and the others are different incarnations or expansions of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> 'ātmā'-śabde kahe---sarva-vidha bhagavān
> eka 'svayaṁ bhagavān', āra 'bhagavān'-ākhyāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ātmā//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it is said; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---all types of Personalities of Godhead; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:s:svayam]] [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākhyāna]]---the Personality of Godhead by an expansive designation.
translation:
"The word ātmā refers to all the different expansions of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. One of them is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself, Kṛṣṇa, and the others are different incarnations or expansions of Kṛṣṇa.


The word //ātmā// also includes all kinds of Bhagavān, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This means that Kṛṣṇa has unlimited expansions. This is described in //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.46):

> dīpārcir eva hi daśāntaram abhyupetya
> dīpāyate vivṛta-hetu-samāna-dharmā
> yas tādṛg eva hi ca viṣṇutayā vibhāti
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi

These expansions are thus compared to candles that have been lit from an original candle. All the secondary candles are equally powerful, but the original candle is that from which all the others have been lit. Kṛṣṇa is the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, and He is expanded as Balarāma, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Aniruddha, Pradyumna and Vāsudeva. In this way there are innumerable incarnations and expansions who are also called Bhagavān, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.286
description: "One who always engages in the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is called ātmārāma. There are two types of ātmārāma. One is an ātmārāma engaged in regulative devotional service, and the other is an ātmārāma engaged in spontaneous devotional service.
text:
> tāṅte rame yei, sei saba---'ātmārāma'
> 'vidhi-bhakta', 'rāga-bhakta',---dui-vidha nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅte]]---in all those Supreme Personalities of Godhead; [[synonyms:r:rame]]---takes pleasure in devotional service; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---those persons who; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of them; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---are also known as //ātmārāma//; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotees following the regulative principles; [[synonyms:r:rāga]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotees following spontaneous love; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---two different varieties.
translation: "One who always engages in the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is called ātmārāma. There are two types of ātmārāma. One is an ātmārāma engaged in regulative devotional service, and the other is an ātmārāma engaged in spontaneous devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.287
description: "The ātmārāmas engaged in regulative and spontaneous devotional service are further categorized into four groups. There are the eternal associates, the associates who have become perfect by devotional service, and those who are engaged in devotional service and are called sādhaka.
text:
> dui-vidha bhakta haya cāri cāri prakāra
> pāriṣada, sādhana-siddha, sādhaka-gaṇa āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---these two varieties of //ātmārāma// devotees; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---each of four different categories; [[synonyms:p:pāriṣada]]---personal associate; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]-[[synonyms:s:siddha]]---liberated to the position of associates by perfection in devotional service; [[synonyms:s:sādhaka]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]] [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and devotees already engaged in the devotional service of the Lord.
translation: "The ātmārāmas engaged in regulative and spontaneous devotional service are further categorized into four groups. There are the eternal associates, the associates who have become perfect by devotional service, and those who are engaged in devotional service and are called sādhaka.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.288
description: "Those who are practicing devotional service are either mature or immature. Therefore the sādhakas are of two types. Since the devotees execute either regulative devotional service or spontaneous devotional service and there are four groups within these two divisions, altogether there are eight varieties.
text:
> jāta-ajāta-rati-bhede sādhaka dui bheda
> vidhi-rāga-mārge cāri cāri---aṣṭa bheda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jāta]]-[[synonyms:a:ajāta]]-[[synonyms:r:rati]]-[[synonyms:b:bhede]]---by distinction of mature love and immature love; [[synonyms:s:sādhaka]] [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---those practicing are of two varieties; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]---regulative devotion; [[synonyms:r:rāga]]---spontaneous devotion; [[synonyms:m:mārge]]---on both the paths; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---there are four different varieties; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]] [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---a total of eight kinds.
translation: "Those who are practicing devotional service are either mature or immature. Therefore the sādhakas are of two types. Since the devotees execute either regulative devotional service or spontaneous devotional service and there are four groups within these two divisions, altogether there are eight varieties.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that the original Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and His expansions are also called the Personality of Godhead. However, Kṛṣṇa is the original Supreme Personality of Godhead. Speculative philosophers and mystic //yogīs// also meditate upon the form of Kṛṣṇa, but this form is not the form of the original Supreme Personality of Godhead. Such a Bhagavān is but a partial representation of the Lord's full potency. Nonetheless, He has to be understood to be the Supreme Personality of Godhead. To clarify this matter, one should simply understand that Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja in Vṛndāvana, the friend of the cowherd boys and lover of the //gopīs,// is actually the original Supreme Personality of Godhead. He is attained by spontaneous love. Although His expansions are also called the Supreme Personality of Godhead, They are attained only by the execution of regulative devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.289
description: "By executing regulative devotional service, one is elevated to the platform of an eternally perfect associate-such as a servant, friend, superior or beloved woman. These are of four varieties.
text:
> vidhi-bhaktye nitya-siddha pāriṣada---'dāsa'
> 'sakhā' 'guru' 'kāntā-gaṇa',---cāri-vidha prakāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---by regulative devotional service; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]-[[synonyms:s:siddha]] [[synonyms:p:pāriṣada]]---eternally perfect associate; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---the servant; [[synonyms:s:sakhā]] [[synonyms:g:guru]] [[synonyms:k:kāntā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---friends, superiors and beloved damsels; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---they are manifested in four varieties.
translation: "By executing regulative devotional service, one is elevated to the platform of an eternally perfect associate-such as a servant, friend, superior or beloved woman. These are of four varieties.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.29
description: "Causeless devotional service is unmotivated by sense enjoyment, perfection or liberation. When one is freed from all these contaminations, he can bring Lord Kṛṣṇa, who is very funny, under control.
text:
> ei yāṅhā nāhi, tāhā bhakti---'ahaitukī'
> yāhā haite vaśa haya śrī-kṛṣṇa kautukī
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:y:yāṅhā]]---where; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not existing; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---the platform of devotional service; [[synonyms:a:ahaitukī]]---unmotivated; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---by which; [[synonyms:v:vaśa]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---comes under control; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kautukī]]---the most funny.
translation: "Causeless devotional service is unmotivated by sense enjoyment, perfection or liberation. When one is freed from all these contaminations, he can bring Lord Kṛṣṇa, who is very funny, under control.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.290
description: "Among those who have perfected themselves by devotional service, there are servants, friends, superiors and beloved damsels. Similarly, there are four types of mature devotees.
text:
> sādhana-siddha---dāsa, sakhā, guru, kānta-gaṇa
> jāta-rati sādhaka-bhakta---cāri-vidha jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]-[[synonyms:s:siddha]]---those who have perfected themselves by devotional service; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---servants; [[synonyms:s:sakhā]]---friends; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---superiors; [[synonyms:k:kāntā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---beloved damsels; [[synonyms:j:jāta]]-[[synonyms:r:rati]] [[synonyms:s:sādhaka]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotees who have become mature by devotional service; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---they are also of four varieties.
translation: "Among those who have perfected themselves by devotional service, there are servants, friends, superiors and beloved damsels. Similarly, there are four types of mature devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.291
description: "Within the category of regulative devotional service, there are also immature devotees. These are also of four varieties. Thus in regulative devotional service there are altogether sixteen varieties.
text:
> ajāta-rati sādhaka-bhakta,---e cāri prakāra
> vidhi-mārge bhakte ṣoḍaśa bheda pracāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ajāta]]-[[synonyms:r:rati]] [[synonyms:s:sādhaka]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---immature devotees engaged in devotional service; [[synonyms:e:e]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---there are also the same four varieties; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]-[[synonyms:m:mārge]]---on the path of regulative devotional service; [[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---devotees; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣoḍaśa]] [[synonyms:b:bheda]] [[synonyms:p:pracāra]]---there are sixteen varieties.
translation: "Within the category of regulative devotional service, there are also immature devotees. These are also of four varieties. Thus in regulative devotional service there are altogether sixteen varieties.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.292
description: "On the path of spontaneous devotional service, there are also sixteen categories of devotees. Thus there are thirty-two types of ātmārāmas enjoying the Supreme Lord on these two paths.
text:
> rāga-mārge aiche bhakte ṣoḍaśa vibheda
> dui mārge ātmārāmera batriśa vibheda
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāga]]-[[synonyms:m:mārge]]---on the path of spontaneous loving service; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in the same way; [[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣoḍaśa]] [[synonyms:v:vibheda]]---divided into sixteen varieties; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:m:mārge]]---on the two paths, namely regulative devotional service and spontaneous devotional service; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmera]]---of persons enjoying with the Supreme Self; [[synonyms:b:batriśa]] [[synonyms:v:vibheda]]---there are thirty-two varieties of devotees.
translation: "On the path of spontaneous devotional service, there are also sixteen categories of devotees. Thus there are thirty-two types of ātmārāmas enjoying the Supreme Lord on these two paths.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.293
description: "When these thirty-two types of devotees are qualified with the words muni nirgrantha ca api, they can be increased in different ways and very soundly elaborated upon.
text:
> 'muni', 'nirgrantha', 'ca' 'api',---cāri śabdera artha
> yāhāṅ yei lāge, tāhā kariye samartha
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muni]]---the sage; [[synonyms:n:nirgrantha]]---either learned or foolish; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:a:api]]---in spite of; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:ś:śabdera]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meanings of these four words; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:l:lāge]]---they apply; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:k:kariye]] [[synonyms:s:samartha]]---make them sound.
translation: "When these thirty-two types of devotees are qualified with the words muni nirgrantha ca api, they can be increased in different ways and very soundly elaborated upon.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.294
description: "When we add the twenty-six types of devotees to these thirty-two, they altogether number fifty-eight. You may now hear from Me of manifestations with different meanings.
text:
> batriśe chābbiśe mili, aṣṭa-pañcāśa
> āra eka bheda śuna arthera prakāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:batriśe]]---these thirty-two varieties; [[synonyms:c:chābbiśe]]---the formerly described twenty-six varieties; [[synonyms:m:mili']]---added together; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:p:pañcāśa]]---they become fifty-eight; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---different; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:a:arthera]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---manifestation of import.
translation: "When we add the twenty-six types of devotees to these thirty-two, they altogether number fifty-eight. You may now hear from Me of manifestations with different meanings.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.295
description: "In this way, as I add the word ca to one word after another, I make a compound. Thus the different names of ātmārāmas can be taken fifty-eight times.
text:
> itaretara 'ca' diyā samāsa kariye
> 'āṭānna' bāra ātmārāma nāma la-iye
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:itaretara]]---in different varieties; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---the word //ca//; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---adding; [[synonyms:s:samāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kariye]]---make a compound word; [[synonyms:ā:āṭānna]] [[synonyms:b:bāra]]---fifty-eight times; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---the //ātmārāma// devotees; [[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iye]]---I take their different names.
translation: "In this way, as I add the word ca to one word after another, I make a compound. Thus the different names of ātmārāmas can be taken fifty-eight times.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.296
description: "In this way, one can repeat the word ātmārāmāḥ with ca for each of the fifty-eight meanings. By following the rule previously stated and rejecting all but the last, we retain that which represents all the meanings.
text:
> 'ātmārāmāś ca ātmārāmāś ca' āṭānna-bāra
> śeṣe saba lopa kari' rākhi eka-bāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]] [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---repeating //ātmārāmāḥ//; [[synonyms:ā:āṭānna]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---fifty-eight times; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---at the end; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:lopa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---rejecting all; [[synonyms:r:rākhi]]---we keep; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---only one.
translation: "In this way, one can repeat the word ātmārāmāḥ with ca for each of the fifty-eight meanings. By following the rule previously stated and rejecting all but the last, we retain that which represents all the meanings.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.297
description: " 'Of words having the same form and case termination, the last one is the only one retained.'
text:
> sarūpāṇām eka-śeṣa eka-vibhaktau,
> uktārthānām aprayoga iti
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpāṇām]]---of words of the same form; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śeṣaḥ]]---only the last; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:v:vibhaktau]]---in the same case; [[synonyms:u:ukta]]-[[synonyms:a:arthānām]]---of the previously spoken meanings; [[synonyms:a:aprayogaḥ]]---nonapplication; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus.
translation: “ 'Of words having the same form and case termination, the last one is the only one retained.'
purport: This is a quotation from Pāṇini's //sūtras// (1.2.64).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.298
description: "When all the ca-kāra, or additions to the word ca, are taken away, fifty-eight different meanings can still be understood by the one word ātmārāma.
text:
> āṭānna ca-kārera saba lopa haya
> eka ātmārāma-śabde āṭānna artha kaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āṭānna]]---fifty-eight; [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:k:kārera]]---of the additions of the word //ca//; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:lopa]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---all of them are rejected; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---//ātmārāma//; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word; [[synonyms:ā:āṭānna]] [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---fifty-eight imports are automatically derived.
translation: "When all the ca-kāra, or additions to the word ca, are taken away, fifty-eight different meanings can still be understood by the one word ātmārāma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.299
description: " 'By the plural word vṛkṣāḥ [trees], all trees, such as banyan trees, fig trees, kapittha trees and mango trees, are indicated.'
text: > aśvattha-vṛkṣāś ca baṭa-vṛkṣāś ca kapittha-vṛkṣāś ca āmra-vṛkṣāś ca vṛkṣāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aśvattha]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛkṣāḥ]]---banyan trees; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:b:baṭa]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛkṣāḥ]]---fig trees; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:k:kapittha]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛkṣāḥ]]---a type of tree named kapittha; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:ā:āmra]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛkṣāḥ]]---mango trees; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣāḥ]]---all indicated by the word "trees."
translation: “ 'By the plural word vṛkṣāḥ [trees], all trees, such as banyan trees, fig trees, kapittha trees and mango trees, are indicated.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.3
description: Thereafter, Sanātana Gosvāmī clasped the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and humbly submitted the following petition.
text:
> tabe sanātana prabhura caraṇe dhariyā
> punarapi kahe kichu vinaya kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]] [[synonyms:d:dhariyā]]---catching the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:v:vinaya]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---with great humility.
translation: Thereafter, Sanātana Gosvāmī clasped the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and humbly submitted the following petition.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.30
description: "There are ten meanings to the word bhakti, devotional service. One is execution of devotional service according to the regulative principles, and the other, called prema-bhakti [ecstatic love] has nine varieties.
text:
> 'bhakti'-śabdera artha haya daśa-vidhākāra
> eka---'sādhana', 'prema-bhakti'---nava prakāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---bhakti; [[synonyms:ś:śabdera]]---of this word; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meanings; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:v:vidhā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---ten varieties; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---the execution of regulative devotional service; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---ecstatic love; [[synonyms:n:nava]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---nine kinds.
translation: "There are ten meanings to the word bhakti, devotional service. One is execution of devotional service according to the regulative principles, and the other, called prema-bhakti [ecstatic love] has nine varieties.
purport: The nine varieties are //rati, prema, sneha, māna, praṇaya, rāga, anurāga, bhāva// and //mahābhāva-//attraction, love, affection, adverse feelings, intimacy, attachment, subattachment, ecstatic love and sublime ecstatic love. For the execution of devotional service according to regulative principles, there is only one meaning.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.300
description: "This ātmārāma verse is like the sentence, 'In this forest many different trees bear fruit.' All ātmārāmas render devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> "asmin vane vṛkṣāḥ phalanti" yaiche haya
> taiche saba ātmārāma kṛṣṇe bhakti karaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:asmin]] [[synonyms:v:vane]]---in this forest; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣāḥ]] [[synonyms:p:phalanti]]---different varieties of trees bear fruit; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---just as in this sentence; [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---similarly; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---self-realized souls; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]] [[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:k:karaya]]---engage themselves in loving devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "This ātmārāma verse is like the sentence, 'In this forest many different trees bear fruit.' All ātmārāmas render devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.301
description: "After fifty-eight times uttering the word ātmārāmāḥ and taking ca in a sense of aggregation, one may add the word munayaḥ. That will mean that they also render devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way there are fifty-nine meanings.
text:
> 'ātmārāmāś ca' samuccaye kahiye ca-kāra
> 'munayaś ca' bhakti kare,---ei artha tāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---similarly the word //ātmārāmāḥ// with the word //ca// added; [[synonyms:s:samuccaye]]---in aggregation; [[synonyms:k:kahiye]]---means; [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:k:kāra]]---the word //ca//; [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---the word //munayaḥ// with the word //ca// added; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---all of them engage in devotional service; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---this is the perfect meaning of the verse.
translation: "After fifty-eight times uttering the word ātmārāmāḥ and taking ca in a sense of aggregation, one may add the word munayaḥ. That will mean that they also render devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way there are fifty-nine meanings.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.302
description: "Then taking the word nirgranthā and considering api in the sense of sustenance, I have tried to explain fifty-nine meanings of the word.
text:
> 'nirgranthā eva' hañā, 'api'---nirdhāraṇe
> ei 'ūnaṣaṣṭi' prakāra artha kariluṅ vyākhyāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirgranthā]]---the word //nirgranthā//; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---also the word //eva//; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:a:api]]---the word //api//; [[synonyms:n:nirdhāraṇe]]---in fixation; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ū:ūnaṣaṣṭi]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---in this way fifty-nine imports; [[synonyms:k:kariluṅ]] [[synonyms:v:vyākhyāne]]---I have described.
translation: "Then taking the word nirgranthā and considering api in the sense of sustenance, I have tried to explain fifty-nine meanings of the word.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.303
description: "Taking all the words together, there is another meaning. Whether one is an ātmārāma, a great sage, or nirgrantha, everyone must engage in the service of the Lord.
text:
> sarva-samuccaye āra eka artha haya
> 'ātmārāmāś ca munayaś ca nirgranthāś ca' bhajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:s:samuccaye]]---taking all of them together; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---import; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]] [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]] [[synonyms:n:nirgranthāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]] [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---the //ātmārāmas,// great sages and //nirgranthas// (the learned and the fools) are all eligible to engage in the transcendental loving service of the Lord.
translation: "Taking all the words together, there is another meaning. Whether one is an ātmārāma, a great sage, or nirgrantha, everyone must engage in the service of the Lord.
purport: The word //sarva-samuccaye// is significant here. It includes all classes of men-//ātmārāma, muni// and //nirgrantha.// Everyone engages in the service of the Lord. Taking the word //api// in the sense of ascertainment, there are, all together, sixty different meanings.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.304
description: "The word api is then used in the sense of ascertainment, and then four times with four words the word eva can be uttered.
text:
> 'api'-śabda---avadhāraṇe, seha cāri bāra
> cāri-śabda-saṅge evera karibe uccāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:api]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---the word //api//; [[synonyms:a:avadhāraṇe]]---in the matter of ascertaining; [[synonyms:s:seha]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:b:bāra]]---those four times; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---four words; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:e:evera]]---of the word //eva//; [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---one can do; [[synonyms:u:uccāra]]---pronouncing.
translation: "The word api is then used in the sense of ascertainment, and then four times with four words the word eva can be uttered.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.305
description: "The words urukrama, bhakti, ahaitukī and kurvanti are added to the word eva again and again. Thus another meaning is explained.
text: > "urukrame eva bhaktim eva ahaitukīm eva kurvanty eva"
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:urukrame]]---unto the most powerful; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---only; [[synonyms:b:bhaktim]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---only; [[synonyms:a:ahaitukīm]]---without motives; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---only; [[synonyms:k:kurvanti]]---they perform; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---only.
translation: "The words urukrama, bhakti, ahaitukī and kurvanti are added to the word eva again and again. Thus another meaning is explained.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.306
description: "Now I have given sixty different meanings to the verse, and yet there is another meaning which is also very strongly evident.
text:
> ei ta' kahiluṅ ślokera 'ṣaṣṭi' saṅkhyaka artha
> āra eka artha śuna pramāṇe samartha
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---thus; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have explained; [[synonyms:ś:ślokera]]---of the verse; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṣṭi]]---sixty; [[synonyms:s:saṅkhyaka]]---numbering; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---imports; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---import; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇe]] [[synonyms:s:samartha]]---quite fit for giving evidence.
translation: "Now I have given sixty different meanings to the verse, and yet there is another meaning which is also very strongly evident.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.307
description: "The word ātmā also refers to the living entity who knows about his body. That is another symptom. From Lord Brahmā down to the insignificant ant, everyone is counted as the marginal potency of the Lord.
text:
> 'ātmā'-śabde kahe 'kṣetrajña jīva'-lakṣaṇa
> brahmādi kīṭa-paryanta---tāṅra śaktite gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //ātmā//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it is said; [[synonyms:k:kṣetra]]-[[synonyms:j:jña]] [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---the living entity who knows about his body; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---symptom; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---beginning from Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:k:kīṭa]]-[[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---down to the insignificant ant; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:ś:śaktite]]---as the marginal potency; [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---counting.
translation: "The word ātmā also refers to the living entity who knows about his body. That is another symptom. From Lord Brahmā down to the insignificant ant, everyone is counted as the marginal potency of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.308
description: " 'The potency of Lord Viṣṇu is summarized in three categories-namely the spiritual potency, the living entities and ignorance. The spiritual potency is full of knowledge; the living entities, although belonging to the spiritual potency, are subject to bewilderment; and the third energy, which is full of ignorance, is always visible in fruitive activities.'
text:
> viṣṇu-śaktiḥ parā proktā
> kṣetrajñākhyā tathā parā
> avidyā-karma-saṁjñānyā
> tṛtīyā śaktir iṣyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaktiḥ]]---the potency of Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:p:parā]]---spiritual; [[synonyms:p:proktā]]---it is said; [[synonyms:k:kṣetra]]-[[synonyms:j:jña]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākhyā]]---the potency known as //kṣetrajña//; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---as well as; [[synonyms:p:parā]]---spiritual; [[synonyms:a:avidyā]]---ignorance; [[synonyms:k:karma]]---fruitive activities; [[synonyms:s:saṁjñā]]---known as; [[synonyms:a:anyā]]---other; [[synonyms:t:tṛtīyā]]---third; [[synonyms:ś:śaktiḥ]]---potency; [[synonyms:i:iṣyate]]---known thus.
translation: “ 'The potency of Lord Viṣṇu is summarized in three categories-namely the spiritual potency, the living entities and ignorance. The spiritual potency is full of knowledge; the living entities, although belonging to the spiritual potency, are subject to bewilderment; and the third energy, which is full of ignorance, is always visible in fruitive activities.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Viṣṇu Purāṇa.// For an explanation, see //Ādi-līlā// (7.119).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.309
description: " 'The word kṣetrajña refers to the living entity, the enjoyer, the chief and material nature.'
text:
> "kṣetrajña ātmā puruṣaḥ
> pradhānaṁ prakṛtiḥ striyām"
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṣetra]]-[[synonyms:j:jñaḥ]]---the word //kṣetrajña//; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the living entity; [[synonyms:p:puruṣaḥ]]---the enjoyer; [[synonyms:p:pradhānam]]---the chief; [[synonyms:p:prakṛtiḥ]]---the material nature; [[synonyms:s:striyām]]---in the feminine gender.
translation: “ 'The word kṣetrajña refers to the living entity, the enjoyer, the chief and material nature.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Svarga-varga// (7) of the //Amara-kośa// dictionary.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.31
description: "Next are explained the symptoms of love of Godhead, which can be divided into nine varieties, beginning with attraction up to ecstatic love and finally up to the topmost ecstatic love [mahābhāva].
text:
> 'rati'-lakṣaṇā, 'prema'-lakṣaṇā, ityādi pracāra
> bhāva-rūpā, mahābhāva-lakṣaṇa-rūpā āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rati]]---of attraction; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇā]]---the symptoms; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---of love; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇā]]---the symptoms; [[synonyms:i:iti]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and so on; [[synonyms:p:pracāra]]---are known; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpā]]---in the form of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---of higher ecstatic love; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpā]]---there are many symptoms; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---other.
translation: "Next are explained the symptoms of love of Godhead, which can be divided into nine varieties, beginning with attraction up to ecstatic love and finally up to the topmost ecstatic love [mahābhāva].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.310
description: "The living entities are wandering in different species of life on different planets, but if by chance they get the association of a pure devotee [sādhu] they give up all other engagements and engage in the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> bhramite bhramite yadi sādhu-saṅga pāya
> saba tyaji' tabe tiṅho kṛṣṇere bhajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhramite]] [[synonyms:b:bhramite]]---wandering in different forms in different manners; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---one obtains the association of devotees; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:t:tyaji']]---giving up everything; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:t:tiṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]] [[synonyms:b:bhajaya]]---engages himself in the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "The living entities are wandering in different species of life on different planets, but if by chance they get the association of a pure devotee [sādhu] they give up all other engagements and engage in the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.311
description: "I have thus explained sixty different meanings, and all of them aim at the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa. After giving so many examples, that is the only meaning.
text:
> ṣāṭi artha kahiluṅ, saba---kṛṣṇera bhajane
> sei artha haya ei saba udāharaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣāṭi]]---sixty; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---imports; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I explained; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:b:bhajane]]---aiming at rendering transcendental loving service to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---that is the only meaning; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all these; [[synonyms:u:udāharaṇe]]---examples.
translation: "I have thus explained sixty different meanings, and all of them aim at the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa. After giving so many examples, that is the only meaning.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.312
description: "Now, due to your association, another meaning has awakened. It is due to your devotional service that these waves of meaning are arising.
text:
> 'eka-ṣaṣṭi' artha ebe sphurila tomā-saṅge
> tomāra bhakti-vaśe uṭhe arthera taraṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṣṭi]]---sixty-one; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---imports; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:s:sphurila]]---has awakened; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---because of your association; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśe]]---by dint of devotional service; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---there arises; [[synonyms:a:arthera]]---of imports; [[synonyms:t:taraṅge]]---waves.
translation: "Now, due to your association, another meaning has awakened. It is due to your devotional service that these waves of meaning are arising.
purport: The word //ātmā// refers to the living entity. From Lord Brahmā down to an insignificant ant, everyone is considered a living entity. Living entities are considered part of the Lord's marginal potency. All of them are //kṣetrajña,// knowers of the body. When they become //nirgrantha,// or free, saintly persons, they engage in Lord Kṛṣṇa's service. That is the sixty-first meaning of the verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.313
description: "[Lord Śiva said,] 'I may know; Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the son of Vyāsadeva, may know; and Vyāsadeva may know or may not know the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam. On the whole, Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, the spotless Purāṇa, can be learned only through devotional service, not by material intelligence, speculative methods or imaginary commentaries.' "
text:
> ahaṁ vedmi śuko vetti
> vyāso vetti na vetti vā
> bhaktyā bhāgavataṁ grāhyaṁ
> na buddhyā na ca ṭīkayā
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I (Lord Śiva); [[synonyms:v:vedmi]]---know; [[synonyms:ś:śukaḥ]]---Śukadeva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:v:vetti]]---knows; [[synonyms:v:vyāsaḥ]]---Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:v:vetti]]---knows; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:v:vetti]] [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or may not know; [[synonyms:b:bhaktyā]]---by devotional service (executed in nine different processes); [[synonyms:b:bhāgavatam]]---the //Bhāgavata Purāṇa// (called //Paramahaṁsa-saṁhitā,// the text or treatise readable by the topmost transcendentalists); [[synonyms:g:grāhyam]]---to be accepted; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:b:buddhyā]]---by so-called intelligence or experimental knowledge; [[synonyms:n:na]]---nor; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭīkayā]]---by imaginary commentary.
translation: "[Lord Śiva said,] 'I may know; Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the son of Vyāsadeva, may know; and Vyāsadeva may know or may not know the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam. On the whole, Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, the spotless Purāṇa, can be learned only through devotional service, not by material intelligence, speculative methods or imaginary commentaries.' "
purport: Devotional service includes nine processes, beginning with hearing, chanting and remembering the activities of Lord Viṣṇu. Only one who has taken to devotional service can understand //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// which is the spotless //Purāṇa// for a transcendentalist (//paramahaṁsa//). So-called commentaries are useless for this purpose. According to the Vedic injunction: //yasya deve parā bhaktir yathā deve tathā gurau.// All Vedic literatures maintain that //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// has to be learned from the person //bhāgavata,// and to understand it one has to engage in pure devotional service. //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// cannot be understood by so-called erudite scholars or grammarians. One who has developed pure Kṛṣṇa consciousness and has served the pure devotee, the spiritual master, can understand //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.// Others cannot.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.314
description: After hearing all the explanations of all the different meanings of the ātmārāma verse, Sanātana Gosvāmī was struck with wonder. He fell down at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and began to offer prayers.
text:
> artha śuni' sanātana vismita hañā
> stuti kare mahāprabhura caraṇe dhariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---by hearing the meaning (of the //ātmārāma// verse); [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:v:vismita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming struck with wonder; [[synonyms:s:stuti]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---offers prayers; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]] [[synonyms:d:dhariyā]]---touching the lotus feet.
translation: After hearing all the explanations of all the different meanings of the ātmārāma verse, Sanātana Gosvāmī was struck with wonder. He fell down at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and began to offer prayers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.315
description: Sanātana Gosvāmī said, "My dear Lord, You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, the son of Mahārāja Nanda. All the Vedic literatures are vibrated through Your breathing.
text:
> "sākṣāt īśvara tumi vrajendra-nandana

purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:1:23|(1.1.23)]] was a question raised by all the sages, who were headed by Śaunaka. This question put before the great devotee Sūta Gosvāmī is the foremost of the six questions raised. The answer to this important question is given in the next verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:3:43|(1.3.43)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.323
description: "If one becomes a madman like Me, he may also understand the meaning of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam by this process."
text:
> āmā-hena yebā keha 'vātula' haya
> ei-dṛṣṭe bhāgavatera artha jānaya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]-[[synonyms:h:hena]]---exactly like Me; [[synonyms:y:yebā]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---a person; [[synonyms:v:vātula]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes a madman; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛṣṭe]]---according to this process; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavatera]]---of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---import; [[synonyms:j:jānaya]]---he can understand.
translation: "If one becomes a madman like Me, he may also understand the meaning of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam by this process."
purport:
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu plainly explains that //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// cannot be understood by those who are materially situated. In other words, one has to become a madman like Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Apart from being the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is an //ācārya// who exhibited love of God like a madman. According to His own written verse: //yugāyitaṁ nimeṣeṇa.// He says that for Him, "a moment seems to last twelve years." //Cakṣuṣā prāvṛṣāyitam:// "My tears are flowing like torrents of rain." //Śūnyāyitaṁ jagat sarvam:// "I feel as if the entire universe were vacant." Why? //Govinda-viraheṇa me:// "Due to My being separated from Govinda, Kṛṣṇa."

One can understand //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// only by following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who was mad for Kṛṣṇa. We cannot, of course, imitate Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. It is not possible. However, unless one is very serious about understanding Kṛṣṇa, he cannot understand //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// gives the full narration of Kṛṣṇa's transcendental activities. The first nine cantos explain who Kṛṣṇa is, and the Lord's birth and activities are narrated in the Tenth Canto. In //Bhagavad-gītā// it is stated: //janma karma ca me divyam.// Kṛṣṇa's appearance and disappearance are transcendental, not mundane. A person is eligible to return home, back to Godhead, if he perfectly understands Kṛṣṇa and His appearance and disappearance. This is verified by //Bhagavad-gītā: tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so 'rjuna.//

It is therefore concluded that one has to learn about Kṛṣṇa from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// and //Bhagavad-gītā,// and one has to follow in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Those who do not follow Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu cannot understand //Bhagavad-gītā// and //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.325
description: "I am a most lowborn person. I have no knowledge of good behavior. How is it possible for me to write authorized directions about Vaiṣṇava activities?"
text:
> muñi---nīca-jāti, kichu nā jānoṅ ācāra
> mo-haite kaiche haya smṛti-paracāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]-[[synonyms:j:jāti]]---belong to a lower caste; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---anything; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jānoṅ]]---I know; [[synonyms:ā:ācāra]]---about proper behavior; [[synonyms:m:mo]]-[[synonyms:h:haite]]---from me; [[synonyms:k:kaiche]]---how; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:smṛti]]-[[synonyms:p:paracāra]]---propagation of the directions of Vaiṣṇava behavior.
translation: "I am a most lowborn person. I have no knowledge of good behavior. How is it possible for me to write authorized directions about Vaiṣṇava activities?"
purport: Actually Sanātana Gosvāmī belonged to a very respectable //brāhmaṇa// family. Nonetheless, he submitted himself as a fallen, lowborn person because he had served in the Mohammedan government. A //brāhmaṇa// is never supposed to be engaged for anyone's service. Accepting service for a livelihood (//paricaryātmakaṁ karma//) is the business of //śūdras.// The //brāhmaṇa// is always independent and busy studying //śāstra// and preaching //śāstra// to subordinate social members such as //kṣatriyas// and //vaiśyas.// Sanātana Gosvāmī felt unfit to write Vaiṣṇava //smṛti// about the behavior of Vaiṣṇavas because he had fallen from the brahminical position. Thus Sanātana Gosvāmī clearly admits that the brahminical culture should be standardized. Presently in India, so-called //brāhmaṇas// are almost all engaged in some mundane service, and they do not understand the import of the Vedic //śāstras.// Nonetheless, they are passing themselves off as //brāhmaṇas// on the basis of birth. In this connection, Sanātana Gosvāmī declares that a //brāhmaṇa// cannot be engaged in anyone's service if he wants to take a leading part in society. In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// Nārada Muni states that even if a //brāhmaṇa// is in a difficult position, he should not accept the occupation of a //śūdra.// This means that he should not be engaged in service for another, for this is the business of dogs. Under the circumstances, Sanātana Gosvāmī felt very low because he had accepted the service of the Muslim government. The conclusion is that no one should claim to be a //brāhmaṇa// simply by birthright while engaging in someone else's service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.326
description: Sanātana Gosvāmī then requested the Lord, "Please personally tell me how I can write this difficult book about Vaiṣṇava behavior. Please manifest Yourself in my heart.
text:
> sūtra kari' diśā yadi karaha upadeśa
> āpane karaha yadi hṛdaye praveśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sūtra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making a synopsis; [[synonyms:d:diśā]]---direction; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:u:upadeśa]]---You kindly instruct; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---You do; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]] [[synonyms:p:praveśa]]---entering into me or manifesting in my heart.
translation: Sanātana Gosvāmī then requested the Lord, "Please personally tell me how I can write this difficult book about Vaiṣṇava behavior. Please manifest Yourself in my heart.
purport: The writing of Vaiṣṇava literatures is not a function for ordinary men. Vaiṣṇava literatures are not mental concoctions. They are all authorized literature meant to guide those who are going to be Vaiṣṇavas. Under these circumstances, an ordinary man cannot give his own opinion. His opinion must always correspond with the conclusion of the //Vedas.// Unless one is fully qualified in Vaiṣṇava behavior and authorized by superior authority (the Supreme Personality of Godhead), one cannot write Vaiṣṇava literatures or purports and commentaries on //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// and //Bhagavad-gītā.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.327

> tabe tāra diśā sphure mo-nīcera hṛdaya

translation: "If You would please manifest Yourself within my heart and personally direct me in writing this book, then, although I am lowborn, I may hope to be able to write it. You can do this because You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead Yourself, and whatever You direct is perfect."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.328
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "Whatever you want to do you will be able to do correctly by Lord Kṛṣṇa's favor. He will manifest the real purport.

> prabhu kahe,---"ye karite karibā tumi mana
> kṛṣṇa sei sei tomā karābe sphuraṇa

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "Whatever you want to do you will be able to do correctly by Lord Kṛṣṇa's favor. He will manifest the real purport.
purport: Sanātana Gosvāmī was a pure devotee of Kṛṣṇa. A pure devotee has no business other than serving Kṛṣṇa; consequently Kṛṣṇa is always ready to help him. This benediction was given by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to Sanātana Gosvāmī, who was authorized to write Vaiṣṇava //smṛti.// Sanātana Gosvāmī was a pure devotee of the Lord, and through the blessings of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu he was able to write the book perfectly.

> pitṛ-mātṛ-sneha ādi 'anurāga'-anta
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakhā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the friends; [[synonyms:r:rati]]---the attraction; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:a:anurāga]] [[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---up to subecstatic love; [[synonyms:p:pitṛ]]-[[synonyms:m:mātṛ]]-[[synonyms:s:sneha]]---paternal love; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and so on; [[synonyms:a:anurāga]]-[[synonyms:a:anta]]---up to the end of subecstatic love.
translation: "Devotees in Vṛndāvana who are friends of the Lord can increase their ecstatic love to the point of anurāga. Paternal affectionate lovers, Kṛṣṇa's father and mother, can increase their love of Godhead up to the anurāga point also.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.330
description: "In your book there should be the characteristics of the bona fide guru and the bona fide disciple. Then, before accepting a spiritual master, one can be assured of the spiritual master's position. Similarly, the spiritual master can also be assured of the disciple's position. The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, should be described as the worshipable object, and you should consider the bīja-mantra for the worship of Kṛṣṇa, Rāma or any other expansion of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> guru-lakṣaṇa, śiṣya-lakṣaṇa, doṅhāra parīkṣaṇa
> sevya---bhagavān, sarva-mantra-vicāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:guru]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the symptoms of a bona fide spiritual master; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the symptoms of a bona fide disciple; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]]---of both; [[synonyms:p:parīkṣaṇa]]---the testing; [[synonyms:s:sevya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead is worshipable; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:m:mantra]]-[[synonyms:v:vicāraṇa]]---consideration of the different types of //mantras.//
