> svasukha-nibhṛta-cetās tad-vyudastānya-bhāvo
> 'py ajita-rucira-līlākṛṣṭa-sāras tadīyam
> vyatanuta kṛpayā yas tattva-dīpaṁ purāṇaṁ
> tam akhila-vṛjina-ghnaṁ vyāsa-sūnuṁ nato 'smi
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:n:nirbhṛta]]-[[synonyms:c:cetāḥ]]---whose mind was always fully absorbed in the happiness of self-realization; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---by that; [[synonyms:v:vyudasta]]-[[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvaḥ]]---being freed from all other attractions; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:a:ajita]]-[[synonyms:r:rucira]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---by the most attractive pastimes of Ajita, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ā:ākṛṣṭa]]---attracted; [[synonyms:s:sāraḥ]]---whose heart; [[synonyms:t:tadīyam]]---in relation to the Lord; [[synonyms:v:vyatanuta]]---described and spread; [[synonyms:k:kṛpayā]]---out of mercy; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---he who; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]-[[synonyms:d:dīpam]]---which is the light of the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:p:purāṇam]]---the supplementary Vedic literature //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---to him; [[synonyms:a:akhila]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛjina]]-[[synonyms:g:ghnam]]---who can destroy all kinds of material misery; [[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]-[[synonyms:s:sūnum]]---Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the son of Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:n:nataḥ]] [[synonyms:a:asmi]]---I offer my respectful obeisances.
translation: “ 'I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the son of Vyāsadeva. He is the destroyer of all sinful reactions and is full in self-realization and bliss. Because of this, he has no other desire. Still, he was attracted by the transcendental pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and out of compassion for the people, he described the transcendental historical literature called Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. This is compared to the light of the Absolute Truth.'
purport: This verse is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (12.12.68).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.49
description: "Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa attracts the minds of all the gopīs with His beautiful transcendental bodily features.
text: > śrī-aṅga-rūpe hare gopikāra mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---of His transcendental body; [[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---by the beauty; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:g:gopikāra]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds of the //gopīs.//
translation: "Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa attracts the minds of all the gopīs with His beautiful transcendental bodily features.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.5
description: " 'Those who are self-satisfied and unattracted by external material desires are also attracted to the loving service of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose qualities are transcendental and whose activities are wonderful. Hari, the Personality of Godhead, is called Kṛṣṇa because He has such transcendentally attractive features.'
text:
> ātmārāmāś ca munayo
> nirgranthā apy urukrame
> kurvanty ahaitukīṁ bhaktim
> ittham-bhūta-guṇo hariḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārāmāḥ]]---persons who take pleasure in being transcendentally situated in the service of the Lord; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]]---great saintly persons who have completely rejected material aspirations, fruitive activities and so forth; [[synonyms:n:nirgranthāḥ]]---without interest in any material desire; [[synonyms:a:api]]---certainly; [[synonyms:u:urukrame]]---unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, whose activities are wonderful; [[synonyms:k:kurvanti]]---do; [[synonyms:a:ahaitukīm]]---causeless, or without material desires; [[synonyms:b:bhaktim]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:i:ittham]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūta]]---so wonderful as to attract the attention of the self-satisfied; [[synonyms:g:guṇaḥ]]---who has transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'Those who are self-satisfied and unattracted by external material desires are also attracted to the loving service of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose qualities are transcendental and whose activities are wonderful. Hari, the Personality of Godhead, is called Kṛṣṇa because He has such transcendentally attractive features.'
purport: This is the famous //ātmārāma// verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:7:10|(1.7.10)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.50
description: " 'Dear Kṛṣṇa, we have simply surrendered ourselves as Your maidservants, for we have seen Your beautiful face decorated with tresses of hair, Your earrings falling upon Your cheeks and the nectar of Your lips. We have also seen the beauty of Your smile and have been embraced by Your arms, which give us courage. Because we have seen Your chest, which is beautiful and broad, we have surrendered ourselves.'
text:
> vīkṣyālakāvṛta-mukhaṁ tava kuṇḍala-śrī-
> gaṇḍa-sthalādhara-sudhaṁ hasitāvalokam
> dattābhayaṁ ca bhuja-daṇḍa-yugaṁ vilokya
> vakṣaḥ śriyaika-ramaṇaṁ ca bhavāma dāsyaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vīkṣya]]---seeing; [[synonyms:a:alaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:āvṛta]]-[[synonyms:m:mukham]]---face decorated with curling tresses of hair; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:k:kuṇḍala]]-[[synonyms:ś:śrī]]---beauty of earrings; [[synonyms:g:gaṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:s:sthala]]---falling on Your cheeks; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:s:sudham]]---and the nectar from Your lips; [[synonyms:h:hasita]]-[[synonyms:a:avalokam]]---Your smiling glance; [[synonyms:d:datta]]-[[synonyms:a:abhayam]]---which assure fearlessness; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:b:bhuja]]-[[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:y:yugam]]---the two arms; [[synonyms:v:vilokya]]---by seeing; [[synonyms:v:vakṣaḥ]]---chest; [[synonyms:ś:śriyā]]---by the beauty; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:r:ramaṇam]]---chiefly producing conjugal attraction; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:b:bhavāma]]---we have become; [[synonyms:d:dāsyaḥ]]---Your maidservants.
translation: “ 'Dear Kṛṣṇa, we have simply surrendered ourselves as Your maidservants, for we have seen Your beautiful face decorated with tresses of hair, Your earrings falling upon Your cheeks and the nectar of Your lips. We have also seen the beauty of Your smile and have been embraced by Your arms, which give us courage. Because we have seen Your chest, which is beautiful and broad, we have surrendered ourselves.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.29.39) was spoken by the //gopīs// when they arrived near Kṛṣṇa for the //rāsa// dance on a full moonlit night. The attracted //gopīs// were awestruck, and they began to speak about how they came to Kṛṣṇa to enjoy the //rāsa// dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.51
description: "The queens in Dvārakā, who are headed by Rukmiṇī, are also attracted to Kṛṣṇa simply by hearing about His transcendental beauty and qualities.
text: > rūpa-guṇa-śravaṇe rukmiṇy-ādira ākarṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---beauty; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---qualities; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇe]]---by hearing; [[synonyms:r:rukmiṇī]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādira]]---of the queens, headed by Rukmiṇī; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaṇa]]---attracting.
translation: "The queens in Dvārakā, who are headed by Rukmiṇī, are also attracted to Kṛṣṇa simply by hearing about His transcendental beauty and qualities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.52
description: " 'O most beautiful Kṛṣṇa, I have heard about Your transcendental qualities from others, and therefore all my bodily miseries are relieved. If one sees Your transcendental beauty, his eyes have attained everything profitable in life. O infallible one, I have become shameless after hearing of Your qualities, and I have become attracted to You.'
text:
> śrutvā guṇān bhuvana-sundara śṛṇvatāṁ te
> nirviśya karṇa-vivarair harato 'ṅga-tāpam
> rūpaṁ dṛśāṁ dṛśimatām akhilārtha-lābhaṁ
> tvayy acyutāviśati cittam apatrapaṁ me
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrutvā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:g:guṇān]]---the transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:b:bhuvana]]-[[synonyms:s:sundara]]---O most beautiful in the whole creation; [[synonyms:ś:śṛṇvatām]]---of those hearing; [[synonyms:t:te]]---Your; [[synonyms:n:nirviśya]]---entering; [[synonyms:k:karṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:vivaraiḥ]]---by the holes of the ears; [[synonyms:h:harataḥ]] [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:t:tāpam]]---decreasing all the miserable conditions of the body; [[synonyms:r:rūpam]]---the beauty; [[synonyms:d:dṛśām]]---of the eyes; [[synonyms:d:dṛśimatām]]---of those who can see; [[synonyms:a:akhila]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:l:lābham]]---the achievement of all kinds of gains; [[synonyms:t:tvayi]]---unto You; [[synonyms:a:acyuta]]---O infallible one; [[synonyms:ā:āviśati]]---enters; [[synonyms:c:cittam]]---the consciousness; [[synonyms:a:apatrapam]]---without shame; [[synonyms:m:me]]---my.
translation: “ 'O most beautiful Kṛṣṇa, I have heard about Your transcendental qualities from others, and therefore all my bodily miseries are relieved. If one sees Your transcendental beauty, his eyes have attained everything profitable in life. O infallible one, I have become shameless after hearing of Your qualities, and I have become attracted to You.'
purport: This verse (//Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// 10.52.37) was written by Rukmiṇīdevī in a letter to Kṛṣṇa inviting Him to kidnap her. Śukadeva Gosvāmī described this to Mahārāja Parīkṣit when the King asked him how Rukmiṇī had been kidnapped. Rukmiṇī had heard about Kṛṣṇa's qualities from different people, and after she heard about them, she decided to accept Kṛṣṇa as her husband. Everything had been arranged for her marriage to Śiśupāla; therefore she wrote a letter to Kṛṣṇa, which she sent through a //brāhmaṇa,// and invited Him to kidnap her.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.53
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa even attracts the mind of the goddess of fortune simply by vibrating His transcendental flute.
text: > vaṁśī-gīte hare kṛṣṇa lakṣmy-ādira mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:g:gīte]]---by the vibration of His flute; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:laksmī]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādira]]---of the goddess of fortune and others; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa even attracts the mind of the goddess of fortune simply by vibrating His transcendental flute.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.54
description: " 'O Lord, we do not know how the serpent Kāliya attained such an opportunity to be touched by the dust of Your lotus feet. For this end, the goddess of fortune performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows. Indeed, we do not know how this serpent Kāliya got such an opportunity.'
text:
> kasyānubhāvo 'sya na deva vidmahe
> tavāṅghri-reṇu-sparaśādhikāraḥ
> yad-vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo
> vihāya kāmān suciraṁ dhṛta-vratā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kasya]]---of what; [[synonyms:a:anubhāvaḥ]]---a result; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of the serpent (Kāliya); [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:d:deva]]---O Lord; [[synonyms:v:vidmahe]]---we know; [[synonyms:t:tava]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅghri]]---of Your lotus feet; [[synonyms:r:reṇu]]---of the dust; [[synonyms:s:sparaśa]]---for touching; [[synonyms:a:adhikāraḥ]]---qualification; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:v:vāñchayā]]---by desiring; [[synonyms:ś:śrīḥ]]---the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:l:lalanā]]---the topmost woman; [[synonyms:a:acarat]]---performed; [[synonyms:t:tapaḥ]]---austerity; [[synonyms:v:vihāya]]---giving up; [[synonyms:k:kāmān]]---all desires; [[synonyms:s:suciram]]---for a long time; [[synonyms:d:dhṛta]]---a law upheld; [[synonyms:v:vratā]]---as a vow.
translation: “ 'O Lord, we do not know how the serpent Kāliya attained such an opportunity to be touched by the dust of Your lotus feet. For this end, the goddess of fortune performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows. Indeed, we do not know how this serpent Kāliya got such an opportunity.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.16.36) was spoken by the wives of the Kāliya demon.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.55
description: "Kṛṣṇa attracts not only the minds of the gopīs and the goddesses of fortune but the minds of all the young girls in the three worlds as well.
text: > yogya-bhāve jagate yata yuvatīra gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yogya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---by proper behavior; [[synonyms:j:jagate]]---within the three worlds; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:y:yuvatīra]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the groups of young girls.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa attracts not only the minds of the gopīs and the goddesses of fortune but the minds of all the young girls in the three worlds as well.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.56
description: " 'My dear Lord Kṛṣṇa, where is that woman within the three worlds who cannot be captivated by the rhythms of the sweet songs coming from Your wonderful flute? Who cannot fall down from the path of chastity in this way? Your beauty is the most sublime within the three worlds. Upon seeing Your beauty, even cows, birds, animals and trees in the forest are stunned in jubilation.'
text:
> kā stry aṅga te kala-padāmṛta-veṇu-gīta-
> sammohitārya-caritān na calet trilokyām
> trailokya-saubhagam idaṁ ca nirīkṣya rūpaṁ
> yad go-dvija-druma-mṛgāḥ pulakāny abibhran
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kā]] [[synonyms:s:strī]]---who is that woman; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---O Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:te]]---of You; [[synonyms:k:kala]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]---by the rhythms; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:v:veṇu]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]---and sweet songs of Your flute; [[synonyms:s:sammohitā]]---being captivated; [[synonyms:ā:ārya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāt]]---from the path of chastity according to Vedic civilization; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:c:calet]]---would wander; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:l:lokyām]]---within the three worlds; [[synonyms:t:trailokya]]-[[synonyms:s:saubhagam]]---which is the fortune of the three worlds; [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:n:nirīkṣya]]---by observing; [[synonyms:r:rūpam]]---the beauty; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:g:go]]---the cows; [[synonyms:d:dvija]]---the birds; [[synonyms:d:druma]]---the trees; [[synonyms:m:mṛgāḥ]]---forest animals like the deer; [[synonyms:p:pulakāni]]---transcendental jubilation; [[synonyms:a:abibhran]]---manifested.
translation: “ 'My dear Lord Kṛṣṇa, where is that woman within the three worlds who cannot be captivated by the rhythms of the sweet songs coming from Your wonderful flute? Who cannot fall down from the path of chastity in this way? Your beauty is the most sublime within the three worlds. Upon seeing Your beauty, even cows, birds, animals and trees in the forest are stunned in jubilation.'
purport: This verse is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.29.40).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.57
description: "The women of Vṛndāvana, who are on the level of superior guardians, are attracted maternally. The men of Vṛndāvana are attracted as servants, friends and fathers to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> guru-tulya strī-gaṇera vātsalye ākarṣaṇa
> dāsya-sakhyādi-bhāve puruṣādi gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:guru]]-[[synonyms:t:tulya]]---on the level of a superior guardian; [[synonyms:s:strī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the ladies of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:v:vātsalye]]---in parental affection; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaṇa]]---attracting; [[synonyms:d:dāsya]]-[[synonyms:s:sakhya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---servants, friends, and others; [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in the mode of; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the males of Vṛndāvana.
translation: "The women of Vṛndāvana, who are on the level of superior guardians, are attracted maternally. The men of Vṛndāvana are attracted as servants, friends and fathers to Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.58
description: "The qualities of Kṛṣṇa captivate and attract everything, living and dead. Even birds, animals and trees are attracted to Kṛṣṇa's qualities.
text:
> pakṣī, mṛga, vṛkṣa, latā, cetanācetana
> preme matta kari' ākarṣaye kṛṣṇa-guṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pakṣī]]---birds; [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]---animals; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]---trees; [[synonyms:l:latā]]---creepers; [[synonyms:c:cetana]]-[[synonyms:a:acetana]]---living entities and even the stones and wood; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:m:matta]]---captivated; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaye]]---attract; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---the qualities of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "The qualities of Kṛṣṇa captivate and attract everything, living and dead. Even birds, animals and trees are attracted to Kṛṣṇa's qualities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.59
description: "Although the word hari has many different meanings, two of them are foremost. One meaning is that the Lord takes away all inauspicious things from His devotee, and the second meaning is that He attracts the mind by ecstatic love for God.
text:
> 'hariḥ'-śabde nānārtha, dui mukhyatama
> sarva amaṅgala hare, prema diyā hare mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---hari; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by this word; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---different imports; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]-[[synonyms:t:tama]]---chief; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:a:amaṅgala]]---inauspiciousness; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---takes away; [[synonyms:p:prema]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---by ecstatic love; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: "Although the word hari has many different meanings, two of them are foremost. One meaning is that the Lord takes away all inauspicious things from His devotee, and the second meaning is that He attracts the mind by ecstatic love for God.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.6
description: "I have heard this wonderful story and am therefore very inquisitive to hear it again. If You would kindly repeat it, I would be very pleased to hear."
text:
> āścarya śuniyā mora utkaṇṭhita mana
> kṛpā kari' kaha yadi, juḍāya śravaṇa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āścarya]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:u:utkaṇṭhita]]---desirous; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing Your causeless mercy; [[synonyms:k:kaha]] [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if You speak; [[synonyms:j:juḍāya]]---pleases; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]---the ear.
translation: "I have heard this wonderful story and am therefore very inquisitive to hear it again. If You would kindly repeat it, I would be very pleased to hear."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.60
description: "When the devotee somehow or other always remembers the Supreme Personality of Godhead anywhere and everywhere, Lord Hari takes away life's four miserable conditions.
text:
> yaiche taiche yohi kohi karaye smaraṇa
> cāri-vidha tāpa tāra kare saṁharaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yaiche]] [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---somehow or other; [[synonyms:y:yohi]] [[synonyms:k:kohi]]---anywhere and everywhere; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---remembers; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]]---the four kinds; [[synonyms:t:tāpa]]---miserable conditions of life; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of the devotee; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:s:saṁharaṇa]]---He takes away.
translation: "When the devotee somehow or other always remembers the Supreme Personality of Godhead anywhere and everywhere, Lord Hari takes away life's four miserable conditions.
purport: The four miserable conditions are due to the four kinds of sinful activities, known as (1) //pātaka,// (2) //urupātaka,// (3) //mahā-pātaka// and (4) //atipātaka-//preliminary sin, very great sin, greater sin and topmost sin. However, Kṛṣṇa assures the devotee, //ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ:// "I will protect you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear." The word //sarva-pāpebhyaḥ// indicates four kinds of sinful activity. As soon as the devotee surrenders unto Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, he is certainly relieved from all sinful activities and their results. The four basic sinful activities are summarized as illicit sex, intoxication, gambling and meat-eating.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.61
description: " 'As all fuel is burned to ashes by a full-fledged fire, all sinful activities are totally erased when one engages in devotional service to Me.'
text:
> yathāgniḥ susamṛddhārciḥ
> karoty edhāṁsi bhasmasāt
> tathā mad-viṣayā bhaktir
> uddhavaināṁsi kṛtsnaśaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:a:agniḥ]]---a fire; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:s:samṛddha]]-[[synonyms:a:arciḥ]]---having a full flame; [[synonyms:k:karoti]]---makes; [[synonyms:e:edhāṁsi]]---fuel; [[synonyms:b:bhasmasāt]]---into ashes; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---similarly; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣayā]] [[synonyms:b:bhaktiḥ]]---devotional service in relation to Me; [[synonyms:u:uddhava]]---O Uddhava; [[synonyms:e:enāṁsi]]---all kinds of sinful activity; [[synonyms:k:kṛtsnaśaḥ]]---totally.
translation: “ 'As all fuel is burned to ashes by a full-fledged fire, all sinful activities are totally erased when one engages in devotional service to Me.'
purport: This verse is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.14.19).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.62
description: "In this way, when all sinful activities are vanquished by the grace of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one gradually vanquishes all kinds of impediments on the path of devotional service, as well as the ignorance resulting from these impediments. After this, one totally manifests his original love of Godhead through devotional service in nine different ways-hearing, chanting and so forth.
text:
> tabe kare bhakti-bādhaka karma, avidyā nāśa
> śravaṇādyera phala 'premā' karaye prakāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:b:bādhaka]]---impediments on the path of devotional service; [[synonyms:k:karma]]---activities; [[synonyms:a:avidyā]]---ignorance; [[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---vanquishing; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādyera]]---of hearing, chanting and so forth; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---the result; [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---causes a manifestation of.
translation: "In this way, when all sinful activities are vanquished by the grace of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one gradually vanquishes all kinds of impediments on the path of devotional service, as well as the ignorance resulting from these impediments. After this, one totally manifests his original love of Godhead through devotional service in nine different ways-hearing, chanting and so forth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.63
description: "When the devotee is freed from all sinful material activities, Kṛṣṇa attracts his body, mind and senses to His service. Thus Kṛṣṇa is very merciful, and His transcendental qualities are very attractive.
text:
> nija-guṇe tabe hare dehendriya-mana
> aiche kṛpālu kṛṣṇa, aiche tāṅra guṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---by transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:d:deha]]-[[synonyms:i:indriya]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the body, senses and mind; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:k:kṛpālu]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---merciful Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---transcendental qualities.
translation: "When the devotee is freed from all sinful material activities, Kṛṣṇa attracts his body, mind and senses to His service. Thus Kṛṣṇa is very merciful, and His transcendental qualities are very attractive.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.64
description: "When one's mind, senses and body are attracted to the transcendental qualities of Hari, one gives up the four principles of material success. Thus I have explained the chief meanings of the word hari.
text:
> cāri puruṣārtha chāḍāya, guṇe hare sabāra mana
> 'hari'-śabdera ei mukhya kahiluṅ lakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---the four kinds of so-called goals of life; [[synonyms:c:chāḍāya]]---causes to give up; [[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---by the transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---everyone's mind; [[synonyms:h:hari]]---//hari//; [[synonyms:ś:śabdera]]---of the word; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---chief; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have explained; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the symptoms.
translation: "When one's mind, senses and body are attracted to the transcendental qualities of Hari, one gives up the four principles of material success. Thus I have explained the chief meanings of the word hari.
purport: The four principles of material success are (1) religious performance, (2) economic development, (3) sense gratification and (4) liberation, or merging in the impersonal effulgence of Brahman. These things do not interest the devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.65
description: "When the conjunction ca [and] and the adverb api [although] are added to this verse, the verse can assume whatever meaning one wants to give it.
text:
> 'ca' 'api', dui śabda tāte 'avyaya' haya
> yei artha lāgāiye, sei artha haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ca]]---//ca//; [[synonyms:a:api]]---//api//; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---words; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in that way; [[synonyms:a:avyaya]]---indeclinable words; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:l:lāgāiye]]---they want to use; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---can be used.
translation: "When the conjunction ca [and] and the adverb api [although] are added to this verse, the verse can assume whatever meaning one wants to give it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.66
description: "The word ca can be explained in seven ways.
text: > tathāpi ca-kārera kahe mukhya artha sāta
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:k:kārera]]---of the word //ca//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it is said; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---chief; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meanings; [[synonyms:s:sāta]]---seven.
translation: "The word ca can be explained in seven ways.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.67
description: " 'The word ca [and] is used to connect a word or sentence with a previous word or sentence, to give the sense of aggregation, to assist the meaning, to give a collective understanding, to suggest another effort or exertion, or to fulfill the meter of a verse. It is also used in the sense of certainty.'
text:
> cānvācaye samāhāre
> 'nyo 'nyārthe ca samuccaye
> yatnāntare tathā pāda-
> pūraṇe 'py avadhāraṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ca]]---this word //ca//; [[synonyms:a:anvācaye]]---in connecting one with another; [[synonyms:s:samāhāre]]---in the sense of aggregation; [[synonyms:a:anyo]] [[synonyms:n:'nya]]-[[synonyms:a:arthe]]---to help one another in the imports; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---the word //ca//; [[synonyms:s:samuccaye]]---in aggregate understanding; [[synonyms:y:yatna]]-[[synonyms:a:antare]]---in another effort; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---as well as; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:pūraṇe]]---in completing the verse; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:a:avadhāraṇe]]---in the sense of certainty.
translation: “ 'The word ca [and] is used to connect a word or sentence with a previous word or sentence, to give the sense of aggregation, to assist the meaning, to give a collective understanding, to suggest another effort or exertion, or to fulfill the meter of a verse. It is also used in the sense of certainty.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Viśva-prakāśa// dictionary.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.68
description: "There are seven chief meanings of the word api. They are as follows.
text: > api-śabde mukhya artha sāta vikhyāta
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:api]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //api//; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]---chief; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meanings; [[synonyms:s:sāta]]---seven; [[synonyms:v:vikhyāta]]---celebrated.
translation: "There are seven chief meanings of the word api. They are as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.69
description: " 'The word api is used in the sense of possibility, question, doubt, censure, aggregation, appropriate application of things, and extravagance.'
text:
> api sambhāvanā-praśna-
> śaṅkā-garhā-samuccaye
> tathā yukta-padārtheṣu
> kāma-cāra-kriyāsu ca
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:api]]---the word //api//; [[synonyms:s:sambhāvanā]]---possibility; [[synonyms:p:praśna]]---question; [[synonyms:ś:śaṅkā]]---doubt; [[synonyms:g:garhā]]---censure or abuse; [[synonyms:s:samuccaye]]---aggregation; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---as well as; [[synonyms:y:yukta]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:a:artheṣu]]---the appropriate application of things; [[synonyms:k:kāma]]-[[synonyms:c:cāra]]-[[synonyms:k:kriyāsu]]---of extravagance; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and.
translation: “ 'The word api is used in the sense of possibility, question, doubt, censure, aggregation, appropriate application of things, and extravagance.'
purport: This is another quotation from the //Viśva-prakāśa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.7
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "I am one madman, and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya is another. Therefore he took My words to be the truth.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---"āmi vātula, āmāra vacane
> sārvabhauma vātula tāhā satya kari' māne
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:v:vātula]]---a madman; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:v:vacane]]---in My words; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:v:vātula]]---another madman; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that (My explanation); [[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:m:māne]]---took as truth.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "I am one madman, and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya is another. Therefore he took My words to be the truth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.70
description: "I have now described the different meanings of the eleven separate words. Now let Me give the complete meaning of the śloka, as it is applied in different places.
text:
> ei ta' ekādaśa padera artha-nirṇaya
> ebe ślokārtha kari, yathā ye lāgaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---this; [[synonyms:e:ekādaśa]]---eleven; [[synonyms:p:padera]]---of the words; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:n:nirṇaya]]---demonstration of import; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---the total meaning of the verse; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---let Me do; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as much as; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:l:lāgaya]]---applicable.
translation: "I have now described the different meanings of the eleven separate words. Now let Me give the complete meaning of the śloka, as it is applied in different places.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.71
description: "The word brahma indicates the summum bonum, the Absolute Truth, which is greater than all other truths. It is the original identity, and there can be no truth equal to that Absolute Truth.
text:
> 'brahma' śabdera artha---tattva sarva-bṛhattama
> svarūpa aiśvarya kari' nāhi yāṅra sama
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---brahma; [[synonyms:ś:śabdera]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meaning of the word; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]---the truth; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:b:bṛhat]]-[[synonyms:t:tama]]---summum bonum among the relative truths; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the original identity; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]---opulence; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal.
translation: "The word brahma indicates the summum bonum, the Absolute Truth, which is greater than all other truths. It is the original identity, and there can be no truth equal to that Absolute Truth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.72
description: " 'I offer my respectful obeisances to the Absolute Truth, the summum bonum. He is the all-pervasive, all-increasing subject matter for the great yogīs. He is changeless, and He is the soul of all.'
text:
> bṛhattvād bṛṁhaṇatvāc ca
> tad brahma paramaṁ viduḥ
> tasmai namas te sarvātman
> yogi-cintyāvikāravat
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bṛhattvāt]]---because of being all-pervasive; [[synonyms:b:bṛṁhaṇatvāt]]---because of increasing unlimitedly; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:p:paramam]]---the ultimate; [[synonyms:v:viduḥ]]---they know; [[synonyms:t:tasmai]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:t:te]]---unto You; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātman]]---the Supreme Soul; [[synonyms:y:yogi]]-[[synonyms:c:cintya]]---appreciable by great //yogīs//; [[synonyms:a:avikāra]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---without change.
translation: “ 'I offer my respectful obeisances to the Absolute Truth, the summum bonum. He is the all-pervasive, all-increasing subject matter for the great yogīs. He is changeless, and He is the soul of all.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Viṣṇu Purāṇa// (1.12.57).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.73
description: "The proper meaning of the word brahma is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is one without a second and without whom nothing exists.
text:
> sei brahma-śabde kahe svayaṁ-bhagavān
> advitīya-jñāna, yāṅhā vinā nāhi āna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---//brahma//; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it is said; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]-[[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:advitīya]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---the supreme one, without duality; [[synonyms:y:yāṅhā]]---which; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:ā:āna]]---there is nothing else.
translation: "The proper meaning of the word brahma is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is one without a second and without whom nothing exists.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.74
description: " 'Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth say that it is nondual knowledge and is called impersonal Brahman, localized Paramātmā and the Personality of Godhead.'
text:
> vadanti tat tattva-vidas
> tattvaṁ yaj jñānam advayam
> brahmeti paramātmeti
> bhagavān iti śabdyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vadanti]]---they say; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]-[[synonyms:v:vidaḥ]]---learned souls; [[synonyms:t:tattvam]]---the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:j:jñānam]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:a:advayam]]---nondual; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---Brahman; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:p:paramātmā]]---Paramātmā; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---Bhagavān; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:ś:śabdyate]]---is known.
translation: “ 'Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth say that it is nondual knowledge and is called impersonal Brahman, localized Paramātmā and the Personality of Godhead.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.75
description: "That Absolute Truth without a second is Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He is the supreme truth in the past, present and future. That is the evidence of all revealed scriptures.
text:
> sei advaya-tattva kṛṣṇa---svayaṁ-bhagavān
> tina-kāle satya tiṅho---śāstra-pramāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:a:advaya]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]]---Absolute Truth without a second; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]-[[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in three phases of time (past, present and future); [[synonyms:s:satya]]---truth; [[synonyms:t:tiṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---the verdict of all Vedic literature.
translation: "That Absolute Truth without a second is Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He is the supreme truth in the past, present and future. That is the evidence of all revealed scriptures.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.76
description: " 'Prior to the cosmic creation, only I exist, and no phenomena exist, either gross, subtle or primordial. After creation, only I exist in everything, and after annihilation only I remain eternally.'
text:
> aham evāsam evāgre
> nānyad yat sad-asat-param
> paścād ahaṁ yad etac ca
> yo 'vaśiṣyeta so 'smy aham
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I, the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:ā:āsam]]---existed; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---only; [[synonyms:a:agre]]---before the creation; [[synonyms:n:na]]---never; [[synonyms:a:anyat]]---anything else; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:s:sat]]---the effect; [[synonyms:a:asat]]---the cause; [[synonyms:p:param]]---the supreme; [[synonyms:p:paścāt]]---after; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I, the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:e:etat]]---this creation; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:a:avaśiṣyeta]]---remains; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:a:asmi]]---am; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I, the Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'Prior to the cosmic creation, only I exist, and no phenomena exist, either gross, subtle or primordial. After creation, only I exist in everything, and after annihilation only I remain eternally.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:9:33|(2.9.33)]]. For an explanation see //Ādi-līlā// (1.53).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.77
description: "The word ātmā [self] indicates the highest truth, Kṛṣṇa. He is the all-pervasive witness of all, and He is the supreme form.
text:
> 'ātma'-śabde kahe kṛṣṇa bṛhattva-svarūpa
> sarva-vyāpaka, sarva-sākṣī, parama-svarūpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]---ātmā; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it is said; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bṛhattva]]---the greatest of all; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---identity; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:v:vyāpaka]]---all pervasive; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:s:sākṣī]]---the witness of all; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---the supreme form.
translation: "The word ātmā [self] indicates the highest truth, Kṛṣṇa. He is the all-pervasive witness of all, and He is the supreme form.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.78
description: " 'Hari, the Personality of Godhead, is the all-pervasive original source of everything; He is therefore the Supersoul of everything.'
text:
> ātatatvāc ca mātṛtvād
> ātmā hi paramo hariḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātatatvāt]]---due to being all-pervading; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:m:mātṛtvāt]]---due to being the progenitor; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the soul; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:p:paramaḥ]]---supreme; [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'Hari, the Personality of Godhead, is the all-pervasive original source of everything; He is therefore the Supersoul of everything.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Bhāvārtha-dīpikā,// Śrīdhara Svāmī's commentary on //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.79
description: "There are three ways to attain the lotus feet of the Absolute Truth, Kṛṣṇa. There is the process of philosophical speculation, the practice of mystic yoga and the execution of devotional service. Each of these has its different characteristics.
text:
> sei kṛṣṇa-prāpti-hetu trividha 'sādhana'
> jñāna, yoga, bhakti,---tinera pṛthak lakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prāpti]]---of achieving the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:hetu]]---causes; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---the three kinds of execution; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]---mystic yoga practice; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---and devotional service; [[synonyms:t:tinera]]---of these three; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the symptoms are different.
translation: "There are three ways to attain the lotus feet of the Absolute Truth, Kṛṣṇa. There is the process of philosophical speculation, the practice of mystic yoga and the execution of devotional service. Each of these has its different characteristics.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.8
description: "I do not recall what I spoke in that connection, but if something comes to My mind due to association with you, I shall explain it.
text:
> kibā pralāpilāṅa, kichu nāhika smaraṇe
> tomāra saṅga-bale yadi kichu haya mane
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---what; [[synonyms:p:pralāpilāṅa]]---I have said; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---anything; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:s:smaraṇe]]---in memory; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of you; [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]-[[synonyms:b:bale]]---by the strength of association; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in My mind.
translation: "I do not recall what I spoke in that connection, but if something comes to My mind due to association with you, I shall explain it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.80
description: "The Absolute Truth is the same, but according to the process by which one understands Him, He appears in three forms-as Brahman, Paramātmā, and Bhagavān, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> tina sādhane bhagavān tina svarūpe bhāse
> brahma, paramātmā, bhagavattā,---trividha prakāśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:s:sādhane]]---by these three different processes; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in identities; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---appears; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---the impersonal feature; [[synonyms:p:paramātmā]]---the localized feature; [[synonyms:b:bhagavattā]]---and the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:trividha]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---three manifestations.
translation: "The Absolute Truth is the same, but according to the process by which one understands Him, He appears in three forms-as Brahman, Paramātmā, and Bhagavān, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.81
description: " 'Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth say that it is nondual knowledge and is called impersonal Brahman, localized Paramātmā and the Personality of Godhead.'
text:
> vadanti tat tattva-vidas
> tattvaṁ yaj jñānam advayam
> brahmeti paramātmeti
> bhagavān iti śabdyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vadanti]]---they say; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]-[[synonyms:v:vidaḥ]]---learned souls; [[synonyms:t:tattvam]]---the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:j:jñānam]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:a:advayam]]---nondual; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---Brahman; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:p:paramātmā]]---Paramātmā; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---Bhagavān; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:ś:śabdyate]]---is known.
translation: “ 'Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth say that it is nondual knowledge and is called impersonal Brahman, localized Paramātmā and the Personality of Godhead.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.82
description: "Although the words brahma and ātmā indicate Kṛṣṇa, their direct meaning refers only to the impersonal Brahman and the Supersoul.
text:
> 'brahma-ātmā'-śabde yadi kṛṣṇere kahaya
> 'rūḍhi-vṛttye' nirviśeṣa antaryāmī kaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---brahma and //ātmā//; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by these words; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]] [[synonyms:k:kahaya]]---Kṛṣṇa is indicated; [[synonyms:r:rūḍhi]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛttye]]---by the direct meaning; [[synonyms:n:nirviśeṣa]]---impersonal; [[synonyms:a:antaryāmī]]---the Supersoul; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---is said.
translation: "Although the words brahma and ātmā indicate Kṛṣṇa, their direct meaning refers only to the impersonal Brahman and the Supersoul.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.83
description: "If one follows the path of philosophical speculation, the Absolute Truth manifests Himself as impersonal Brahman, and if one follows the path of mystic yoga, He manifests Himself as the Supersoul.
text:
> jñāna-mārge---nirviśeṣa-brahma prakāśe
> yoga-mārge---antaryāmi-svarūpete bhāse
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]-[[synonyms:m:mārge]]---the process of philosophical speculation; [[synonyms:n:nirviśeṣa]]-[[synonyms:b:brahma]]---the impersonal Brahman effulgence; [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---becomes manifest; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]-[[synonyms:m:mārge]]---by practicing mystic //yoga//; [[synonyms:a:antaryāmi]]-[[synonyms:s:svarūpete]]---in the localized aspect, Supersoul; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---appears.
translation: "If one follows the path of philosophical speculation, the Absolute Truth manifests Himself as impersonal Brahman, and if one follows the path of mystic yoga, He manifests Himself as the Supersoul.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.84
description: "There are two kinds of devotional activity-spontaneous and regulative. By spontaneous devotional service, one attains the original Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, and by the regulative process one attains the expansion of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> rāga-bhakti-vidhi-bhakti haya dui-rūpa
> 'svayaṁ-bhagavattve', bhagavattve---prakāśa dvi-rūpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāga]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---spontaneous devotional service; [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---regulative devotional service; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the two kinds of devotional service; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]-[[synonyms:b:bhagavattve]]---in the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhagavattve]]---and in His personal expansion; [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]] [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the two kinds of manifestation.
translation: "There are two kinds of devotional activity-spontaneous and regulative. By spontaneous devotional service, one attains the original Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, and by the regulative process one attains the expansion of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.85
description: "By executing spontaneous devotional service in Vṛndāvana, one attains the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa.
text: > rāga-bhaktye vraje svayaṁ-bhagavāne pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāga]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---by the discharge of spontaneous devotional service; [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---Himself; [[synonyms:b:bhagavāne]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---one gets.
translation: "By executing spontaneous devotional service in Vṛndāvana, one attains the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.86
description: " 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, the son of mother Yaśodā, is accessible to those devotees engaged in spontaneous loving service, but He is not as easily accessible to mental speculators, to those striving for self-realization by severe austerities and penances, or to those who consider the body the same as the self.'
text:
> nāyaṁ sukhāpo bhagavān
> dehināṁ gopikā-sutaḥ
> jñānināṁ cātma-bhūtānāṁ
> yathā bhaktimatām iha
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āpaḥ]]---easily available; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:d:dehinām]]---for materialistic persons who have accepted the body as the self; [[synonyms:g:gopikā]]-[[synonyms:s:sutaḥ]]---the son of mother Yaśodā; [[synonyms:j:jñāninām]]---for persons addicted to mental speculation; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūtānām]]---for persons performing severe austerities and penances; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:m:matām]]---for persons engaged in spontaneous devotional service; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---in this world.
translation: “ 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, the son of mother Yaśodā, is accessible to those devotees engaged in spontaneous loving service, but He is not as easily accessible to mental speculators, to those striving for self-realization by severe austerities and penances, or to those who consider the body the same as the self.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.9.21) is spoken by Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī. It concerns the statement about Kṛṣṇa's being subjugated by the //gopīs// and thus glorifying them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.87
description: "By executing regulative devotional service, one becomes an associate of Nārāyaṇa and attains the Vaikuṇṭhalokas, the spiritual planets in the spiritual sky.
text: > vidhi-bhaktye pārṣada-dehe vaikuṇṭhete yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vidhi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---by executing regulative devotional service; [[synonyms:p:pārṣada]]-[[synonyms:d:dehe]]---in the form of an associate of the Lord; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭhete]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---one achieves the Vaikuṇṭha planets.
translation: "By executing regulative devotional service, one becomes an associate of Nārāyaṇa and attains the Vaikuṇṭhalokas, the spiritual planets in the spiritual sky.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.88
description: " 'Those who discuss the activities of Lord Kṛṣṇa are on the highest platform of devotional life, and they evince the symptoms of tears in the eyes and bodily jubilation. Such persons discharge devotional service to Kṛṣṇa without practicing the rules and regulations of the mystic yoga system. They possess all spiritual qualities, and they are elevated to the Vaikuṇṭha planets, which exist above us.'
text:
> yac ca vrajanty animiṣām ṛṣabhānuvṛttyā
> dūre-yamā hy upari naḥ spṛhaṇīya-śīlāḥ
> bhartur mithaḥ suyaśasaḥ kathanānurāga-
> vaiklavya-bāṣpa-kalayā pulakīkṛtāṅgāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:v:vrajanti]]---go; [[synonyms:a:animiṣām]]---of the demigods; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣabha]]-[[synonyms:a:anuvṛttyā]]---by practicing the best means of spiritual life; [[synonyms:d:dūre]]---keeping at a distance; [[synonyms:y:yamāḥ]]---the regulative principles; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:u:upari]]---above; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---our; [[synonyms:s:spṛhaṇīya]]-[[synonyms:ś:śīlāḥ]]---decorated with desirable qualities; [[synonyms:b:bhartuḥ]]---of the master; [[synonyms:m:mithaḥ]]---mutually; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:y:yaśasaḥ]]---who has all transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:k:kathana]]-[[synonyms:a:anurāga]]---attracted to discussions; [[synonyms:v:vaiklavya]]---transformation; [[synonyms:b:bāṣpa]]-[[synonyms:k:kalayā]]---with tears in the eyes; [[synonyms:p:pulakīkṛta]]---jubilation; [[synonyms:a:aṅgāḥ]]---bodily limbs.
translation: “ 'Those who discuss the activities of Lord Kṛṣṇa are on the highest platform of devotional life, and they evince the symptoms of tears in the eyes and bodily jubilation. Such persons discharge devotional service to Kṛṣṇa without practicing the rules and regulations of the mystic yoga system. They possess all spiritual qualities, and they are elevated to the Vaikuṇṭha planets, which exist above us.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:15:25|(3.15.25)]]. In this verse Lord Brahmā is speaking to all the demigods, who feared the two //asuras// in Diti's womb. Lord Brahmā described the Kumāras' visit to Vaikuṇṭha, and this was again explained by Maitreya, the friend of Vyāsadeva, when he gave instructions to Vidura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.89
description: "The devotees are divided into three categories-akāma [desireless], mokṣa-kāma [desiring liberation], and sarva-kāma [desiring material perfection].
text:
> sei upāsaka haya trividha prakāra
> akāma, mokṣa-kāma, sarva-kāma āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:u:upāsaka]]---those devotees; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---three varieties; [[synonyms:a:akāma]]---without material desires; [[synonyms:m:mokṣa]]-[[synonyms:k:kāma]]---desiring to become liberated; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāma]]---filled with all material desires; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and.
translation: "The devotees are divided into three categories-akāma [desireless], mokṣa-kāma [desiring liberation], and sarva-kāma [desiring material perfection].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.9
description: "Generally by Myself I cannot give an explanation, but by the strength of your association something may manifest itself.
text:
> sahaje āmāra kichu artha nāhi bhāse
> tomā-sabāra saṅga-bale ye kichu prakāśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sahaje]]---generally; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---any; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---does not manifest; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]-[[synonyms:b:bale]]---by the strength of your association; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---manifests.
translation: "Generally by Myself I cannot give an explanation, but by the strength of your association something may manifest itself.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.90
description: " 'One who is actually intelligent, although he may be a devotee free from material desires, a karmī desiring all kinds of material facilities, or a jñānī desiring liberation, should seriously engage in bhakti-yoga for the satisfaction of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
text:
> akāmaḥ sarva-kāmo vā
> mokṣa-kāma udāra-dhīḥ
> tīvreṇa bhakti-yogena
> yajeta puruṣaṁ param
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:akāmaḥ]]---without material desires; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāmaḥ]]---full of all material desires; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:m:mokṣa]]-[[synonyms:k:kāmaḥ]]---desiring liberation; [[synonyms:u:udāra]]-[[synonyms:d:dhīḥ]]---sincere and advanced in devotional service; [[synonyms:t:tīvreṇa]]---firm; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:y:yogena]]---by the practice of //bhakti-yoga//; [[synonyms:y:yajeta]]---should worship; [[synonyms:p:puruṣam]] [[synonyms:p:param]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'One who is actually intelligent, although he may be a devotee free from material desires, a karmī desiring all kinds of material facilities, or a jñānī desiring liberation, should seriously engage in bhakti-yoga for the satisfaction of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:3:10|(2.3.10)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.91
description: "The meaning of the word udāra-dhīḥ is buddhimān-intelligent or considerate. Because of this, even for one's own sense gratification one engages in the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> buddhimān-arthe---yadi 'vicāra-jña' haya
> nija-kāma lāgiha tabe kṛṣṇere bhajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:buddhimān]]-[[synonyms:a:arthe]]---by the meaning of intelligent; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]-[[synonyms:j:jña]]---expert in scrutinizing things; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:k:kāma]] [[synonyms:l:lāgiha]]---even for sense gratification; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇere]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---worships Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "The meaning of the word udāra-dhīḥ is buddhimān-intelligent or considerate. Because of this, even for one's own sense gratification one engages in the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.92
description: "The other processes cannot yield results unless they are associated with devotional service. Devotional service, however, is so strong and independent that it can give one all the desired results.
text:
> bhakti vinu kona sādhana dite nāre phala
> saba phala deya bhakti svatantra prabala
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:v:vinu]]---without devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---some; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---practice for perfection; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---not able; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---any result; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:p:phala]]---all the results of different processes; [[synonyms:d:deya]]---give; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]]---independent; [[synonyms:p:prabala]]---and powerful.
translation: "The other processes cannot yield results unless they are associated with devotional service. Devotional service, however, is so strong and independent that it can give one all the desired results.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.93
description: "With the exception of devotional service, all the methods of self-realization are like nipples on the neck of a goat. An intelligent person adopts only devotional service, giving up all other processes of self-realization.
text:
> ajā-gala-stana-nyāya anya sādhana
> ataeva hari bhaje buddhimān jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ajā]]-[[synonyms:g:gala]]-[[synonyms:s:stana]]-[[synonyms:n:nyāya]]---like the nipples on the neck of a goat; [[synonyms:a:anya]]---other; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---execution of spiritual life; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:h:hari]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---one worships; [[synonyms:b:buddhimān]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---the intelligent person.
translation: "With the exception of devotional service, all the methods of self-realization are like nipples on the neck of a goat. An intelligent person adopts only devotional service, giving up all other processes of self-realization.
purport: Without devotional service, other methods for self-realization and spiritual life are useless. Other methods cannot produce good results at any time, and therefore they are compared to the nipples on the neck of a goat. These nipples cannot produce milk, although it may appear that they can. An unintelligent person cannot understand that only devotional service can elevate one to the transcendental position.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.94
description: " 'O best among the Bharatas [Arjuna], four kinds of pious men render devotional service unto Me—the distressed, the desirer of wealth, the inquisitive, and he who is searching for knowledge of the Absolute.'
text:
> catur-vidhā bhajante māṁ
> janāḥ sukṛtino 'rjuna
> ārto jijñāsur arthārthī
> jñānī ca bharatarṣabha
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vidhāḥ]]---four kinds; [[synonyms:b:bhajante]]---worship; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---Me; [[synonyms:j:janāḥ]]---persons; [[synonyms:s:sukṛtinaḥ]]---who have obeyed the principles of human life or the regulative principles of //varṇa// and //āśrama//; [[synonyms:a:arjuna]]---O Arjuna; [[synonyms:ā:ārtaḥ]]---the distressed; [[synonyms:j:jijñāsuḥ]]---the inquisitive; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:a:arthī]]---one in need of money; [[synonyms:j:jñānī]]---one pursuing knowledge; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:b:bharata]]-[[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣabha]]---O best of the Bharata dynasty.
translation: “ 'O best among the Bharatas [Arjuna], four kinds of pious men render devotional service unto Me---the distressed, the desirer of wealth, the inquisitive, and he who is searching for knowledge of the Absolute.'
purport:
This is a quotation from //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:7:16|(Bg. 7.16)]]. The word //sukṛtinaḥ// is very important in this verse. //Su// means "auspicious," and //kṛtī// means "meritorious" or "regulated." Unless one follows the regulative principles of religious life, human life is no different from animal life. Religious life means following the principles of //varṇa// and //āśrama.// In the //Viṣṇu Purāṇa// it is said:

> varṇāśramācāra-vatā
> puruṣeṇa paraḥ pumān
> viṣṇur ārādhyate panthā
> nānyat tat-toṣa-kāraṇam

According to religious life, society is divided into four social divisions-//brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya// and //śūdra-//and four spiritual divisions-//brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha// and //sannyāsa.// One needs to be trained to become a //brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya// or //śūdra,// just as one is trained to become an engineer, doctor or lawyer. Those who are properly trained can be considered human beings; if one is not trained socially and spiritually---that is, if one is uneducated and unregulated-his life is on the animal platform. Among animals there is no question of spiritual advancement. Spiritual life can be attained by proper training-either by following the principles of //varṇa// and //āśrama// or by being directly trained in the //bhakti// school by the methods of //śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoḥ smaraṇaṁ pāda-sevanamarcanaṁ vandanaṁ dāsyaṁ sakhyam ātma-nivedanam.// Without being trained, one cannot be //sukṛtī,// auspicious. In this verse Kṛṣṇa says that people approach Him when in distress, in need of money or when actually inquisitive to understand the Supreme Being or the original source of everything. Some people approach Him in the pursuit of knowledge of the Absolute Truth, and others approach Him when they are distressed, like the devotee Gajendra. Others are inquisitive, like the great sages headed by Sanaka, and others need money, like Dhruva Mahārāja. Śukadeva Gosvāmī approached the Lord when he pursued knowledge. All these great personalities thus took to the devotional service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.95
description: "Materialistic devotees take to devotional service and worship Kṛṣṇa when they are distressed or in need of money. Those who are actually inquisitive to understand the supreme source of everything and those who are in search of knowledge are called transcendentalists, for they desire liberation from all material contamination.
text:
> ārta, arthārthī,---dui sakāma-bhitare gaṇi
> jijñāsu, jñānī,---dui mokṣa-kāma māni
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ārta]]---distressed; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:a:arthī]]---desirous of money; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two persons; [[synonyms:s:sakāma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhitare]]---in the division of material activities; [[synonyms:g:gaṇi]]---we consider; [[synonyms:j:jijñāsu]]---inquisitive; [[synonyms:j:jñānī]]---pursuing knowledge; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:m:mokṣa]]-[[synonyms:k:kāma]]---transcendentalists pursuing spiritual knowledge for liberation; [[synonyms:m:māni]]---I consider.
translation: "Materialistic devotees take to devotional service and worship Kṛṣṇa when they are distressed or in need of money. Those who are actually inquisitive to understand the supreme source of everything and those who are in search of knowledge are called transcendentalists, for they desire liberation from all material contamination.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.96
description: "Because they have a pious background, all four types of people are to be considered greatly fortunate. Such people gradually give up material desires and become pure devotees.
text:
> ei cāri sukṛti haya mahā-bhāgyavān
> tat-tat-kāmādi chāḍi' haya śuddha-bhaktimān
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---these four persons; [[synonyms:s:sukṛti]]---pious men; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgyavān]]---highly fortunate; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:t:tat]]---those respective; [[synonyms:k:kāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---aspirations; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---become; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktimān]]---pure devotees.
translation: "Because they have a pious background, all four types of people are to be considered greatly fortunate. Such people gradually give up material desires and become pure devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.97
description: "One is elevated to the platform of devotional life by the mercy of a Vaiṣṇava, the bona fide spiritual master, and by the special mercy of Kṛṣṇa. On that platform, one gives up all material desires and the association of unwanted people. Thus one is elevated to the platform of pure devotional service.
text:
> sādhu-saṅga-kṛpā kimvā kṛṣṇera kṛpāya
> kāmādi 'duḥsaṅga' chāḍi' śuddha-bhakti pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---by the mercy of association with devotees; [[synonyms:k:kimvā]]---or; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpāya]]---by the mercy of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---material desires and so on; [[synonyms:d:duḥsaṅga]]---unwanted association; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---one obtains the platform of pure devotional life.
translation: "One is elevated to the platform of devotional life by the mercy of a Vaiṣṇava, the bona fide spiritual master, and by the special mercy of Kṛṣṇa. On that platform, one gives up all material desires and the association of unwanted people. Thus one is elevated to the platform of pure devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 24.98
description: " 'The intelligent, who have understood the Supreme Lord in the association of pure devotees and have become free from bad materialistic association, can never avoid hearing the glories of the Lord, even though they have heard them only once.'
text:
> sat-saṅgān mukta-duḥsaṅgo
> hātuṁ notsahate budhaḥ
> kīrtyamānaṁ yaśo yasya
> sakṛd ākarṇya rocanam
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgāt]]---by the association of pure devotees; [[synonyms:m:mukta]]---freed; [[synonyms:d:duḥsaṅgaḥ]]---the association of materialistic persons; [[synonyms:h:hātum]]---to give up; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:u:utsahate]]---is able; [[synonyms:b:budhaḥ]]---one who is actually learned; [[synonyms:k:kīrtyamānam]]---being glorified; [[synonyms:y:yaśaḥ]]---the glories; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom (the Supreme Personality of Godhead); [[synonyms:s:sakṛt]]---once; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṇya]]---hearing; [[synonyms:r:rocanam]]---very pleasing.
translation: “ 'The intelligent, who have understood the Supreme Lord in the association of pure devotees and have become free from bad materialistic association, can never avoid hearing the glories of the Lord, even though they have heard them only once.'
purport:
This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:10:11|(1.10.11)]]. All the members of the Kuru dynasty offered respects when Kṛṣṇa was leaving Hastināpura after the Battle of Kurukṣetra. Kṛṣṇa was going to His own kingdom, and all the members of the Kuru dynasty were overwhelmed by His departure. This verse was spoken in that connection by Śukadeva Gosvāmī. A pure devotee becomes attached to Kṛṣṇa by hearing the Lord's glories. The Lord's glories and the Lord Himself are identical. One has to be qualified to understand this Absolute Truth; therefore one should be given a chance to associate with a pure devotee. Our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is meant for this purpose. We want to create pure devotees so that other people will benefit by their association. In this way the number of pure devotees increases. Professional preachers cannot create pure devotees. There are many professional preachers of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// who read this work to earn their livelihood. However, they cannot convert materialistic people to devotional service. Only a pure devotee can convert others to pure devotional service. It is therefore important for all the preachers in our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement to first become pure devotees and follow the regulative principles, refraining from illicit sex, meat-eating, gambling and intoxication. They should regularly chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// on their beads, follow the devotional process, rise early in the morning, attend //maṅgala-ārati// and recite //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// and //Bhagavad-gītā// regularly. In this way, one can become purified and free from all material contamination.

> sarvopādhi-vinirmuktaṁ
> tat-paratvena nirmalam
> hṛṣīkeṇa hṛṣīkeśa-
> sevanaṁ bhaktir ucyate

(//Nārada-pañcarātra//)

To make a show of devotional service will not help one. One must be a pure devotee following the devotional process; then one can convert others to devotional service. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu practiced devotional service and preached (//āpani ācari' bhakti karila pracāra//). If a preacher behaves properly in devotional service, he will be able to convert others. Otherwise, his preaching will have no effect.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.101
description: " 'Everything animate or inanimate that is within the universe is controlled and owned by the Lord. One should therefore accept only those things for himself that are set aside as his quota, and one should not accept other things, knowing well to whom they belong.'
text:
> ātmāvāsyam idaṁ viśvaṁ
> yat kiñcij jagatyāṁ jagat
> tena tyaktena bhuñjīthā
> mā gṛdhaḥ kasyasvid dhanam
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:ā:āvāsyam]]---the expansion of the energy of the Supreme Soul, the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this; [[synonyms:v:viśvam]]---universe; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---whatever; [[synonyms:k:kiñcit]]---something; [[synonyms:j:jagatyām]]---within the universe; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---all that is animate or inanimate; [[synonyms:t:tena]]---by Him; [[synonyms:t:tyaktena]]---by things allotted to every person; [[synonyms:b:bhuñjīthā]]---you should accept for your maintenance; [[synonyms:m:mā]]---never; [[synonyms:g:gṛdhaḥ]]---encroach; [[synonyms:k:kasyasvit]]---someone else's; [[synonyms:d:dhanam]]---property.
translation: “ 'Everything animate or inanimate that is within the universe is controlled and owned by the Lord. One should therefore accept only those things for himself that are set aside as his quota, and one should not accept other things, knowing well to whom they belong.'
purport:
This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:8:1:10|(8.1.10)]]. Communists and socialists are trying to propagate the philosophy that everything belongs to the mass of people or to the state. Such an idea is not perfect. When this idea is expanded, we can see that everything belongs to God. That will be the perfection of the communistic idea. The purpose of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// is here very nicely explained. Every one of us must be satisfied with those things the Supreme Personality of Godhead has allotted us. We should not encroach upon the possessions of others. This simple idea can be expanded in our daily lives. Everyone should have a piece of land given by the government, and everyone should possess a few cows. Both of these should be utilized for one's daily bread. Above that, if something is manufactured in a factory, it should be considered the property of the Supreme Personality of Godhead because the ingredients belong to the Supreme Lord. Actually, there is no need to manufacture such things artificially, but if it is done, one should consider that the goods produced belong to the Supreme Lord. Spiritual communism recognizes the supreme proprietorship of the Supreme Lord. As explained in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:5:29|(Bg. 5.29)]]:

> bhoktāraṁ yajña-tapasāṁ
> sarva-loka-maheśvaram
> suhṛdaṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ
> jñātvā māṁ śāntim ṛcchati

"The sages, knowing Me as the ultimate purpose of all sacrifices and austerities, the Supreme Lord of all planets and demigods and the benefactor and well-wisher of all living entities, attain peace from the pangs of material miseries."

It is further explained in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// that no one should claim anything as his property. Whatever property one claims to be his actually belongs to Kṛṣṇa.

One should be satisfied with whatever has been allotted by the Supreme Lord and should not encroach upon the property of others. This will lead to peace in the whole world.

translation: "The essence of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam-our relationship with the Supreme Lord, our activities in that connection and the goal of life-is manifest in the four verses of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam known as the catuḥ-ślokī. Everything is explained in those verses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.103
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa says, 'I am the center of all relationships. Knowledge of Me and the practical application of that knowledge is actual knowledge. Approaching Me for devotional service is called abhidheya.
text:
> "āmi-'sambandha'-tattva, āmāra jñāna-vijñāna
> āmā pāite sādhana-bhakti 'abhidheya'-nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:s:sambandha]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]]---the center of all relationships; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---of Me; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:v:vijñāna]]---practical application of that knowledge; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]] [[synonyms:p:pāite]]---to obtain Me; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---the practice of devotional service; [[synonyms:a:abhidheya]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---is called activities in that relationship.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa says, 'I am the center of all relationships. Knowledge of Me and the practical application of that knowledge is actual knowledge. Approaching Me for devotional service is called abhidheya.
purport: Spiritual knowledge means fully understanding the Absolute Truth in three features-impersonal Brahman, localized Paramātmā and the all-powerful Supreme Personality of Godhead. Ultimately when one takes shelter at the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and engages in the Lord's service, the resultant knowledge is called //vijñāna,// special knowledge, or the practical application of spiritual knowledge. One should be engaged in the Lord's devotional service to achieve the aim of life, called //prayojana.// The practice of devotional service to attain that goal of life is called //abhidheya.//

translation: “ 'Prior to the cosmic manifestation, only I exist, and no phenomena exist, either gross, subtle or primordial. After creation, only I exist in everything, and after annihilation, only I remain eternally.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.116

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.118
description: " 'When one is transcendentally situated, he can perceive Me. This perception is the basis of one's relationship with the Supreme Lord. Now let Me further explain this subject matter.
text:
> māyātīta haile haya āmāra 'anubhava'
> ei 'sambandha'-tattva kahiluṅ, śuna āra saba
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:a:atīta]] [[synonyms:h:haile]]---when one becomes transcendentally situated above this external energy; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:a:anubhava]]---perception of Me; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:sambandha]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]] [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---this has been explained as the principle of a relationship with Me; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all the rest.
translation: “ 'When one is transcendentally situated, he can perceive Me. This perception is the basis of one's relationship with the Supreme Lord. Now let Me further explain this subject matter.
purport: Real spiritual knowledge has to be received from revealed scriptures. After this knowledge is attained, one can begin to perceive his actual spiritual life. Any knowledge achieved by speculation is imperfect. One must receive knowledge from the //paramparā// system and from the //guru,// otherwise one will be bewildered, and will ultimately become an impersonalist. When one very scrutinizingly deliberates, he can realize the personal feature of the Absolute Truth. The Supreme Personality of Godhead is always transcendental to this material creation. //Nārāyaṇaḥ paro 'vyaktāt:// Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is always transcendental. He is not a creation of this material world. Without realizing spiritual knowledge, one cannot understand that the transcendental form of the Lord is always beyond the creative energy. The example of the sun and sunshine is given. The sunshine is not the sun, but still the sunshine is not separate from the sun. The philosophy of //acintya-bhedābheda-tattva// (simultaneously one and different) cannot be understood by one who is fully under the influence of the external energy. Consequently a person under the influence of the material energy cannot understand the nature and form of the Personality of the Absolute Truth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.119

> ṛte 'rthaṁ yat pratīyeta
> na pratīyeta cātmani
> tad vidyād ātmano māyāṁ
> yathābhāso yathā tamaḥ

> duḥkha pāñā prabhu-pade kailā nivedana
