title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.120
description: " 'Now please hear from Me about the process of devotional service, which is applicable in any country, for any person, at all times and in all circumstances.
text:
> 'abhidheya' sādhana-bhaktira śunaha vicāra
> sarva-jana-deśa-kāla-daśāte vyāpti yāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:abhidheya]]---the means to obtain an end; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktira]]---of the process of executing devotional service; [[synonyms:ś:śunaha]] [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---please hear the procedure; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:j:jana]]---people; [[synonyms:d:deśa]]---countries; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]---times; [[synonyms:d:daśāte]]---and in circumstances; [[synonyms:v:vyāpti]] [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---which is all-pervasive.
translation: “ 'Now please hear from Me about the process of devotional service, which is applicable in any country, for any person, at all times and in all circumstances.
purport: The cult of //bhāgavata-dharma// can be spread in all circumstances, among all people and in all countries. Many envious people accuse this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement of spoiling the rigidity of so-called Hinduism. That is not actually the fact. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu confirms that devotional service to the Lord---the cult of //bhāgavata-dharma,// which is now being spread as the Hare Kṛṣṇa movement-can be spread in every country, for every person, in any condition of life, and in all circumstances. //Bhāgavata-dharma// does not restrict pure devotees to the Hindu community. A pure devotee is above a //brāhmaṇa;// therefore it is not incompatible to offer the sacred thread to devotees in Europe, America, Australia, Japan, Canada, and so on. Sometimes these pure devotees, who have been accepted by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, are not allowed to enter certain temples in India. Some high-caste //brāhmaṇas// and //gosvāmīs// refuse to take //prasāda// in the temples of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. Actually this is against the instruction of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Devotees can come from any country, and they can belong to any creed or race. On the strength of this verse, those who are actually devotees and followers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu must accept devotees from all parts of the world as pure Vaiṣṇavas. They should be accepted not artificially but factually. One should see how they are advanced in Kṛṣṇa consciousness and how they are conducting Deity worship, //saṅkīrtana// and Ratha-yātrā. Considering all these points, an envious person should refrain from malicious atrocities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.121
description: " 'As far as religious principles are concerned, there is a consideration of the person, the country, the time and the circumstance. In devotional service, however, there are no such considerations. Devotional service is transcendental to all considerations.
text:
> 'dharmādi' viṣaye yaiche e 'cāri, vicāra
> sādhana-bhakti-ei cāri vicārera pāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---of religious activities and so on; [[synonyms:v:viṣaye]]---in the subject matter; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just as; [[synonyms:e:e]] [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---there is a consideration of four principles, namely the person, country, time and atmosphere; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---of devotional service; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---four; [[synonyms:v:vicārera]]---to the considerations; [[synonyms:p:pāra]]---transcendental.
translation: “ 'As far as religious principles are concerned, there is a consideration of the person, the country, the time and the circumstance. In devotional service, however, there are no such considerations. Devotional service is transcendental to all considerations.
purport:
When we are on the material platform, there are different types of religions-Hinduism, Christianity, Mohammedanism, Buddhism, and so on. These are instituted for a particular time, a particular country or a particular person. Consequently there are differences. Christian principles are different from Hindu principles, and Hindu principles are different from Mohammedan and Buddhist principles. These may be considered on the material platform, but when we come to the platform of transcendental devotional service, there are no such considerations. The transcendental service of the Lord (//sādhana-bhakti//) is above these principles. The world is anxious for religious unity, and that common platform can be achieved in transcendental devotional service. This is the verdict of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. When one becomes a Vaiṣṇava, he becomes transcendental to all these limited considerations. This is also confirmed in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:14:26|(Bg. 14.26)]]:

> māṁ ca yo 'vyabhicāreṇa
> bhakti-yogena sevate
> sa guṇān samatītyaitān
> brahma-bhūyāya kalpate

"One who engages in full devotional service, who does not fall down in any circumstance, at once transcends the modes of material nature and thus comes to the level of Brahman."

The devotional activities of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement are completely transcendental to material considerations. As far as different faiths are concerned, religions may be of different types, but on the spiritual platform, everyone has an equal right to execute devotional service. That is the platform of oneness and the basis for a classless society. In his //Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya,// Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura confirms that one has to learn from a bona fide spiritual master about religious principles, economic development, sense gratification and ultimately liberation. These are the four divisions of regulated life, but they are subjected to the material platform. On the spiritual platform, the four principles are //jñāna, vijñāna, tad-aṅga// and //tad-rahasya.// Rules, regulations and restrictions are on the material platform, but on the spiritual platform one has to be equipped with transcendental knowledge, which is above the principles of religious rituals. Mundane religious activity is known as //smārta-viddhi,// but transcendental devotional service is called //Gosvāmī-viddhi.// Unfortunately many so-called //gosvāmīs// are on the platform of //smārta-viddhi,// yet they try to pass as //Gosvāmī-viddhi,// and thus the people are cheated. //Gosvāmī-viddhi// is strictly explained in Sanātana Gosvāmī's //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa,// wherein it is stated:

> yathā kāñcanatāṁ yāti
> kāṁsyaṁ rasa-vidhānataḥ
> tathā dīṣkā-vidhānena
> dvijatvaṁ jāyate nṛṇām

The conclusion is that devotional service is open for everyone, regardless of caste, creed, time and country. This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is functioning according to this principle.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.122

translation: “ 'It is therefore the duty of every man-in every country, in every circumstance and at all times-to approach the bona fide spiritual master, question him about devotional service and listen to him explain the process.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.124
description: " 'Supreme affection for Me is called love of Godhead, and that is the ultimate goal of life. Let Me explain by practical example the natural characteristics of such love.
text:
> āmāte ye 'prīti', sei 'prema'-'prayojana'
> kārya-dvāre kahi tāra 'svarūpa'-lakṣaṇa

translation: “ 'Supreme affection for Me is called love of Godhead, and that is the ultimate goal of life. Let Me explain by practical example the natural characteristics of such love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.125
description: " 'The five material elements are existing inside and outside of every living entity. Similarly, I, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, am manifest within the heart of the devotee as well as outside his body.
text:
> pañca-bhūta yaiche bhūtera bhitare-bāhire
> bhakta-gaṇe sphuri āmi bāhire-antare
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūta]]---the five material elements; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just as; [[synonyms:b:bhūtera]]---of the living entities; [[synonyms:b:bhitare]]---inside; [[synonyms:b:bāhire]]---and outside; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---unto the devotees; [[synonyms:s:sphuri]]---becoming manifest; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bāhire]]-[[synonyms:a:antare]]---externally and internally.
translation: “ 'The five material elements are existing inside and outside of every living entity. Similarly, I, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, am manifest within the heart of the devotee as well as outside his body.
purport: The pure devotee knows that he is a servant of Kṛṣṇa eternally. He knows that everything can be used in the service of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.126
description: " 'As the material elements enter the bodies of all living beings and yet remain outside them all, I exist within all material creations and yet am not within them.
text:
> yathā mahānti bhūtāni
> bhūteṣūccāvaceṣv anu
> praviṣṭāny apraviṣṭāni
> tathā teṣu na teṣv aham
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:m:mahānti]]---the universal; [[synonyms:b:bhūtāni]]---elements; [[synonyms:b:bhūteṣu]]---in the living entities; [[synonyms:u:ucca]]-[[synonyms:a:avaceṣu]]---both gigantic and minute; [[synonyms:a:anu]]---after; [[synonyms:p:praviṣṭāni]]---situated internally; [[synonyms:a:apraviṣṭāni]]---situated externally; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---so; [[synonyms:t:teṣu]]---in them; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:t:teṣu]]---in them; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I.
translation: “ 'As the material elements enter the bodies of all living beings and yet remain outside them all, I exist within all material creations and yet am not within them.
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:9:35|(2.9.35)]]. It is also the third verse of the //catuḥ-ślokī.// For an explanation see //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter One, text 55.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.127

text:
> bhakta āmā preme bāndhiyāche hṛdaya-bhitare
> yāhāṅ netra paḍe tāhāṅ dekhaye āmāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---a devotee; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]---Me; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---by love; [[synonyms:b:bāndhiyāche]]---has bound; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhitare]]---within his heart; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:n:netra]]---the eyes; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fall; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:d:dekhaye]]---he sees; [[synonyms:ā:āmāre]]---Me.
translation: “ 'A highly elevated devotee can bind Me, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in his heart by love. Wherever he looks, he sees Me and nothing else.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.128
description: " 'Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who destroys everything inauspicious for His devotees, does not leave the hearts of His devotees even if they remember Him and chant about Him inattentively. This is because the rope of love always binds the Lord within the devotees' hearts. Such devotees should be accepted as most elevated.
text:
> visṛjati hṛdayaṁ na yasya sākṣād
> dharir avaśābhihito 'py aghaugha-nāśaḥ
> praṇaya-rasanayā dhṛtāṅghri-padmaḥ
> sa bhavati bhāgavata-pradhāna uktaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:visṛjati]]---gives up; [[synonyms:h:hṛdayam]]---the heart; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---whose; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:avaśa]]-[[synonyms:a:abhihitaḥ]]---who is automatically glorified; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:a:aghaugha]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśaḥ]]---who annihilates all kinds of inauspicious offenses for a devotee; [[synonyms:p:praṇaya]]-[[synonyms:r:rasanayā]]---with the rope of love; [[synonyms:d:dhṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅghri]]-[[synonyms:p:padmaḥ]]---whose lotus feet are bound; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---such a devotee; [[synonyms:b:bhavati]]---is; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]-[[synonyms:p:pradhānaḥ]]---the most elevated devotee; [[synonyms:u:uktaḥ]]---is said.
translation: “ 'Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who destroys everything inauspicious for His devotees, does not leave the hearts of His devotees even if they remember Him and chant about Him inattentively. This is because the rope of love always binds the Lord within the devotees' hearts. Such devotees should be accepted as most elevated.
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.2.55).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.129
description: " 'A person advanced in devotional service sees within everything the soul of souls, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Consequently he always sees the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead as the cause of all causes and understands that all things are situated in Him.
text:
> sarva-bhūteṣu yaḥ paśyed
> bhagavad-bhāvam ātmanaḥ
> bhūtāni bhagavaty ātmany
> eṣa bhāgavatottamaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūteṣu]]---in all objects (in matter, spirit, or combinations of matter and spirit); [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:p:paśyet]]---sees; [[synonyms:b:bhagavat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvam]]---the capacity to be engaged in the service of the Lord; [[synonyms:ā:ātmanaḥ]]---of the Supreme Spirit Soul, or the transcendence beyond the material conception of life; [[synonyms:b:bhūtāni]]---all beings; [[synonyms:b:bhagavati]]---in the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ā:ātmani]]---the basic principle of all existence; [[synonyms:e:eṣaḥ]]---this; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]-[[synonyms:u:uttamaḥ]]---a person advanced in devotional service.
translation: “ 'A person advanced in devotional service sees within everything the soul of souls, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Consequently he always sees the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead as the cause of all causes and understands that all things are situated in Him.
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.2.45).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.13
description: They submitted their request, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, seeing His devotees' unhappiness, decided to turn the minds of the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs.
text:
> bhakta-duḥkha dekhi' prabhu manete cintila
> sannyāsīra mana phirāite mana ha-ila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:d:duḥkha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the unhappiness of the devotees; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:manete]] [[synonyms:c:cintila]]---considered within His mind; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds of the Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:p:phirāite]]---to turn; [[synonyms:m:mana]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu decided.
translation: They submitted their request, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, seeing His devotees' unhappiness, decided to turn the minds of the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.130
description: " 'All the gopīs assembled to chant the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa very loudly, and they began to wander from one forest to another like madwomen. They began to inquire about the Lord, who is situated in all living entities internally and externally. Indeed, they even asked all the plants and vegetables about Him, the Supreme Person.' "
text:
> gāyanta uccair amum eva saṁhatāḥ
> vicikyur unmattakavad vanād vanam
> papracchur ākāśavad antaraṁ bahir
> bhūteṣu santaṁ puruṣaṁ vanaspatīn
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gāyantaḥ]]---continuously singing; [[synonyms:u:uccaiḥ]]---very loudly; [[synonyms:a:amum]]---that one (Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa); [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:saṁhatāḥ]]---being assembled together; [[synonyms:v:vicikyuḥ]]---searched; [[synonyms:u:unmattaka]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---like those who have become mad; [[synonyms:v:vanāt]]---from one forest; [[synonyms:v:vanam]]---to another forest; [[synonyms:p:papracchuḥ]]---asked about; [[synonyms:ā:ākāśa]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---like the sky; [[synonyms:a:antaram]]---within; [[synonyms:b:bahiḥ]]---outside; [[synonyms:b:bhūteṣu]]---in all living entities; [[synonyms:s:santam]]---existing; [[synonyms:p:puruṣam]]---the Supreme Person; [[synonyms:v:vanaspatīn]]---all the trees and plants.
translation: “ 'All the gopīs assembled to chant the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa very loudly, and they began to wander from one forest to another like madwomen. They began to inquire about the Lord, who is situated in all living entities internally and externally. Indeed, they even asked all the plants and vegetables about Him, the Supreme Person.' "
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.30.4). The //gopīs// almost went mad due to Kṛṣṇa's suddenly leaving the //rāsa// dance. Because the //gopīs// were fully absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa, they were imitating His different postures and pastimes. They became very saddened because of His absence, and this incident is explained by Śukadeva Gosvāmī to Mahārāja Parīkṣit.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.131
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "One's relationship with the Lord, activities and devotional service, and the attainment of the highest goal of life, love of Godhead, are the subject matters of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.
text:
> ataeva bhāgavate ei 'tina' kaya
> sambandha-abhidheya-prayojana-maya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavate]]---in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:tina]]---these three principles; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---are explained; [[synonyms:s:sambandha]]-[[synonyms:a:abhidheya]]-[[synonyms:p:prayojana]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---first one's relationship, then activities in devotional service, and then achieving the highest goal of life, love of Godhead.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "One's relationship with the Lord, activities and devotional service, and the attainment of the highest goal of life, love of Godhead, are the subject matters of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.132
description: " 'The Absolute Truth is known by the self-realized souls as a unified identity known by different names-impersonal Brahman, localized Paramātmā, and Bhagavān, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
text:
> vadanti tat tattva-vidas
> tattvaṁ yaj jñānam advayam
> brahmeti paramātmeti
> bhagavān iti śabdyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vadanti]]---they say; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]-[[synonyms:v:vidaḥ]]---those who know the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:t:tattvam]]---the ultimate goal; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:j:jñānam]] [[synonyms:a:advayam]]---identical knowledge; [[synonyms:b:brahma]] [[synonyms:i:iti]]---as the impersonal Brahman; [[synonyms:p:paramātmā]] [[synonyms:i:iti]]---as the Supersoul; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]] [[synonyms:i:iti]]---as the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ś:śabdyate]]---it is described.
translation: “ 'The Absolute Truth is known by the self-realized souls as a unified identity known by different names-impersonal Brahman, localized Paramātmā, and Bhagavān, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:2:11|(1.2.11)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.133
description: " 'Before the cosmic manifestation was created, the creative propensity was merged in His person. At that time all potencies and manifestations were preserved in the personality of the Supreme Lord. The Lord is the cause of all causes, and He is the all-pervading, self-sufficient person. Before the creation, He existed with His spiritual potency in the spiritual world, wherein various Vaikuṇṭha planets are manifest.'
text:
> bhagavān eka āsedam
> agra ātmātmanāṁ vibhuḥ
> ātmecchānugatāv ātmā
> anānāmaty-upalakṣaṇaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:e:ekaḥ]]---only; [[synonyms:ā:āsa]]---was; [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this universe; [[synonyms:a:agre]]---before (before the creation of this cosmic manifestation); [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the living force; [[synonyms:ā:ātmanām]]---of all the living entities; [[synonyms:v:vibhuḥ]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]---of the Supreme; [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---the will; [[synonyms:a:anugatau]]---according to; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the Supersoul; [[synonyms:a:anānāmati]]-[[synonyms:u:upalakṣaṇaḥ]]---who is not realized by persons having many angles of vision.
translation: “ 'Before the cosmic manifestation was created, the creative propensity was merged in His person. At that time all potencies and manifestations were preserved in the personality of the Supreme Lord. The Lord is the cause of all causes, and He is the all-pervading, self-sufficient person. Before the creation, He existed with His spiritual potency in the spiritual world, wherein various Vaikuṇṭha planets are manifest.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:5:23|(3.5.23)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.134
description: " 'All these incarnations of Godhead are either plenary portions or parts of the plenary portions of the puruṣa-avatāras. But Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. In every age He protects the world through His different features when the world is disturbed by the enemies of Indra.'
text:
> ete cāṁśa-kalāḥ puṁsaḥ
> kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam
> indrāri-vyākulaṁ lokaṁ
> mṛḍayanti yuge yuge
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ete]]---these; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---plenary portions; [[synonyms:k:kalāḥ]]---parts of plenary portions; [[synonyms:p:puṁsaḥ]]---of the //puruṣa-avatāras//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---Himself; [[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:a:ari]]---the enemies of Lord Indra; [[synonyms:v:vyākulam]]---full of; [[synonyms:l:lokam]]---the world; [[synonyms:m:mṛḍayanti]]---make happy; [[synonyms:y:yuge]] [[synonyms:y:yuge]]---at the right time in each age.
translation: “ 'All these incarnations of Godhead are either plenary portions or parts of the plenary portions of the puruṣa-avatāras. But Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. In every age He protects the world through His different features when the world is disturbed by the enemies of Indra.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:3:28|(1.3.28)]]. For an explanation, see //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Two, text 67.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.135
description: "This is one's eternal relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Now please hear about the execution of devotional service. This principle pervades practically all the verses of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.
text:
> eita' 'sambandha', śuna 'abhidheya' bhakti
> bhāgavate prati-śloke vyāpe yāra sthiti
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eita']]---this; [[synonyms:s:sambandha]]---relationship; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:a:abhidheya]]---the function; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---known as devotional service; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavate]]---in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:ś:śloke]]---in each and every verse; [[synonyms:v:vyāpe]]---pervades; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---the situation.
translation: "This is one's eternal relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Now please hear about the execution of devotional service. This principle pervades practically all the verses of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.136
description: " 'Being very dear to the devotees and sādhus, I am attained through unflinching faith and devotional service. This bhakti-yoga system, which gradually increases attachment for Me, purifies even a human being born among dog-eaters. That is to say, everyone can be elevated to the spiritual platform by the process of bhakti-yoga.'
text:
> bhaktyāham ekayā grāhyaḥ
> śraddhayātmā priyaḥ satām
> bhaktiḥ punāti man-niṣṭhā
> śva-pākān api sambhavāt
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaktyā]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:e:ekayā]]---unflinching; [[synonyms:g:grāhyaḥ]]---obtainable; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhayā]]---by faith; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the most dear; [[synonyms:p:priyaḥ]]---to be served; [[synonyms:s:satām]]---by the devotees; [[synonyms:b:bhaktiḥ]]---the devotional service; [[synonyms:p:punāti]]---purifies; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:n:niṣṭhā]]---fixed only on Me; [[synonyms:ś:śva]]-[[synonyms:p:pākān]]---the lowest grade of human beings, who are accustomed to eating dogs; [[synonyms:a:api]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:sambhavāt]]---from all faults due to birth and so on.
translation: “ 'Being very dear to the devotees and sādhus, I am attained through unflinching faith and devotional service. This bhakti-yoga system, which gradually increases attachment for Me, purifies even a human being born among dog-eaters. That is to say, everyone can be elevated to the spiritual platform by the process of bhakti-yoga.'
purport: This verse is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.14.21).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.137
description: " 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, said: "My dear Uddhava, neither through aṣṭāṅga-yoga [the mystic yoga system to control the senses], nor through impersonalism or an analytical study of the Absolute Truth, nor through study of the Vedas, nor through practice of austerities, nor through charity, nor through acceptance of sannyāsa, can one satisfy Me as much as one can by developing unalloyed devotional service unto Me.' "
text:
> na sādhayati māṁ yogo
> na sāṅkhyaṁ dharma uddhava
> na svādhyāyas tapas tyāgo
> yathā bhaktir mamorjitā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---never; [[synonyms:s:sādhayati]]---causes to remain satisfied; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---Me; [[synonyms:y:yogaḥ]]---the process of control; [[synonyms:n:na]]---nor; [[synonyms:s:sāṅkhyam]]---the process of gaining philosophical knowledge about the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:d:dharmaḥ]]---such an occupation; [[synonyms:u:uddhava]]---My dear Uddhava; [[synonyms:n:na]]---nor; [[synonyms:s:svādhyāyaḥ]]---study of the //Vedas//; [[synonyms:t:tapaḥ]]---austerities; [[synonyms:t:tyāgaḥ]]---renunciation, acceptance of //sannyāsa,// or charity; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as much as; [[synonyms:b:bhaktiḥ]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:ū:ūrjitā]]---developed.
translation: “ 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, said: "My dear Uddhava, neither through aṣṭāṅga-yoga [the mystic yoga system to control the senses], nor through impersonalism or an analytical study of the Absolute Truth, nor through study of the Vedas, nor through practice of austerities, nor through charity, nor through acceptance of sannyāsa, can one satisfy Me as much as one can by developing unalloyed devotional service unto Me.' "
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.14.20). For an explanation see //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Seventeen, text 76.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.138
description: " 'When the living entity is attracted by the material energy, which is separate from Kṛṣṇa, he is overpowered by fear. Because he is separated from the Supreme Personality of Godhead by the material energy, his conception of life is reversed. In other words, instead of being the eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa, he becomes Kṛṣṇa's competitor. This is called viparyayo 'smṛtiḥ. To nullify this mistake, one who is actually learned and advanced worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead as his spiritual master, worshipful Deity and source of life. He thus worships the Lord by the process of unalloyed devotional service.'
text:
> bhayaṁ dvitīyābhiniveśataḥ syād
> īśād apetasya viparyayo 'smṛtiḥ
> tan-māyayāto budha ābhajet taṁ
> bhaktyaikayeśaṁ guru-devatātmā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhayam]]---fear; [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]]-[[synonyms:a:abhiniveśataḥ]]---from the misconception of being a product of material energy; [[synonyms:s:syāt]]---arises; [[synonyms:ī:īśāt]]---from the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:apetasya]]---of one who has withdrawn (the conditioned soul); [[synonyms:v:viparyayaḥ]]---reversal of position; [[synonyms:a:asmṛtiḥ]]---no conception of his relationship with the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:m:māyayā]]---because of the illusory energy of the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:a:ataḥ]]---therefore; [[synonyms:b:budhaḥ]]---one who is wise; [[synonyms:ā:ābhajet]]---must worship; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---Him; [[synonyms:b:bhaktyā]]---by devotional service; [[synonyms:e:ekayā]]---undiverted to //karma// and //jñāna//; [[synonyms:ī:īśam]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---as the spiritual master; [[synonyms:d:devatā]]---worshipable Lord; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---Supersoul.
translation: “ 'When the living entity is attracted by the material energy, which is separate from Kṛṣṇa, he is overpowered by fear. Because he is separated from the Supreme Personality of Godhead by the material energy, his conception of life is reversed. In other words, instead of being the eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa, he becomes Kṛṣṇa's competitor. This is called viparyayo 'smṛtiḥ. To nullify this mistake, one who is actually learned and advanced worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead as his spiritual master, worshipful Deity and source of life. He thus worships the Lord by the process of unalloyed devotional service.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.2.37).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.139
description: "Now hear from Me what actual love of Godhead is. It is the prime object of life and is symptomized by bodily trembling, tears in the eyes, chanting and dancing.
text:
> ebe śuna, prema, yei-mūla 'prayojana'
> pulakāśru-nṛtya-gīta-yāhāra lakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ebe]] [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---now hear; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---which; [[synonyms:m:mūla]] [[synonyms:p:prayojana]]---the chief objective; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]-[[synonyms:a:aśru]]-[[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]---trembling of the body, tears in the eyes, dancing and chanting; [[synonyms:y:yāhāra]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---the symptoms of which.
translation: "Now hear from Me what actual love of Godhead is. It is the prime object of life and is symptomized by bodily trembling, tears in the eyes, chanting and dancing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.14
description: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was seriously considering meeting with the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs, the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa approached Him and extended an invitation. The brāhmaṇa submitted his invitation with great humility, and he touched the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> hena-kāle vipra āsi' karila nimantraṇa
> aneka dainyādi kari' dharila caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the Mahārāṣṭrian //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:aneka]]---various; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---submissions; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:d:dharila]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---touched His lotus feet.
translation: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was seriously considering meeting with the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs, the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa approached Him and extended an invitation. The brāhmaṇa submitted his invitation with great humility, and he touched the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.140
description: " 'Pure devotees develop a spiritual body and symptoms of ecstatic love simply by remembering and reminding others of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, who takes away everything inauspicious from the devotee. This position is attained by rendering devotional service according to the regulative principles and then rising to the platform of spontaneous love.'
text:
> smarantaḥ smārayaś ca
> mitho 'ghaugha-haraṁ harim
> bhaktyā sañjātayā bhaktyā
> bibhraty utpulakāṁ tanum
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:smarantaḥ]]---remembering; [[synonyms:s:smārayaḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and reminding; [[synonyms:m:mithaḥ]]---one another; [[synonyms:a:aghaugha]]-[[synonyms:h:haram]]---who takes away everything inauspicious from the devotee; [[synonyms:h:harim]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhaktyā]]---by devotion; [[synonyms:s:sañjātayā]]---awakened; [[synonyms:b:bhaktyā]]---by devotion; [[synonyms:b:bibhrati]]---possess; [[synonyms:u:utpulakām]]---agitated by ecstasy; [[synonyms:t:tanum]]---body.
translation: “ 'Pure devotees develop a spiritual body and symptoms of ecstatic love simply by remembering and reminding others of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, who takes away everything inauspicious from the devotee. This position is attained by rendering devotional service according to the regulative principles and then rising to the platform of spontaneous love.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.3.31).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.141
description: " 'When a person is actually advanced and takes pleasure in chanting the holy name of the Lord, who is very dear to him, he is agitated and loudly chants the holy name. He also laughs, cries, becomes agitated and chants like a madman, not caring for outsiders.'
text:
> evaṁ-vrataḥ sva-priya-nāma-kīrtyā
> jātānurāgo druta-citta uccaiḥ
> hastay atho roditi rauti gāyaty
> unmādavan nṛtyati loka-bāhyaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:evam]]-[[synonyms:v:vrataḥ]]---when one thus engages in a vow to chant and dance; [[synonyms:s:sva]]---own; [[synonyms:p:priya]]---very dear; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---holy name; [[synonyms:k:kīrtyā]]---by chanting; [[synonyms:j:jāta]]---in this way develops; [[synonyms:a:anurāgaḥ]]---attachment; [[synonyms:d:druta]]-[[synonyms:c:cittaḥ]]---very eagerly; [[synonyms:u:uccaiḥ]]---loudly; [[synonyms:h:hasati]]---laughs; [[synonyms:a:atho]]---also; [[synonyms:r:roditi]]---cries; [[synonyms:r:rauti]]---becomes agitated; [[synonyms:g:gāyati]]---chants; [[synonyms:u:unmāda]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---like a madman; [[synonyms:n:nṛtyati]]---dances; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhyaḥ]]---without caring for outsiders.
translation: “ 'When a person is actually advanced and takes pleasure in chanting the holy name of the Lord, who is very dear to him, he is agitated and loudly chants the holy name. He also laughs, cries, becomes agitated and chants like a madman, not caring for outsiders.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.2.40).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.142
description: "Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam gives the actual meaning of the Vedānta-sūtra. The author of the Vedānta-sūtra is Vyāsadeva, and he himself has explained those codes in the form of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.
text:
> ataeva bhāgavata-sūtrera 'artha'-rūpa
> nija-kṛta sūtrera nija-'bhāṣya'-svarūpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]---//Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:s:sūtrera]]---of the //Brahma-sūtra//; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---of the meaning; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the form; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛta]]---made by himself; [[synonyms:s:sūtrera]]---of the //Vedānta-sūtra//; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāṣya]]---of his own commentary; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---the original form.
translation: "Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam gives the actual meaning of the Vedānta-sūtra. The author of the Vedānta-sūtra is Vyāsadeva, and he himself has explained those codes in the form of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.143-144
description: " 'The meaning of the Vedānta-sūtra is present in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. The full purport of the Mahābhārata is also there. The commentary of the Brahma-gāyatrī is also there and fully expanded with all Vedic knowledge. Śrīmad Bhāgavatam is the supreme Purāṇa, and it was compiled by the Supreme Personality of Godhead in His incarnation as Vyāsadeva. There are twelve cantos, 335 chapters and eighteen thousand verses.'
text:
> artho 'yaṁ brahma-sūtrāṇāṁ
> bhāratārtha-vinirṇayaḥ
> gāyatrī-bhāṣya-rūpo 'sau
> vedārtha-paribṛṁhitaḥ
>
> purāṇānāṁ sāma-rūpaḥ
> sākṣād-bhagavatoditaḥ
> dvādaśa-skandha-yukto 'yaṁ
> śata-viccheda-saṁyutaḥ
> grantho 'ṣṭādaśa-sāhasraḥ
> śrīmad-bhāgavatābhidhaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:artaḥ]] [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this is the meaning; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:s:sūtrāṇām]]---of the codes of //Vedānta-sūtra//; [[synonyms:b:bhārata]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:v:vinirṇayaḥ]]---the ascertainment of the //Mahābhārata//; [[synonyms:g:gāyatrī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāṣya]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpaḥ]]---the purport of Brahma-gāyatrī, the mother of the Vedic literatures; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---that; [[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:p:paribṛṁhitaḥ]]---expanded by the meanings of all the //Vedas//; [[synonyms:p:purāṇānām]]---of the //Purāṇas//; [[synonyms:s:sāma]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpaḥ]]---the best (like the //Sāma// among the //Vedas//); [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:b:bhagavatā]] [[synonyms:u:uditaḥ]]---spoken by Vyāsadeva, an incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:d:dvādaśa]]-[[synonyms:s:skanda]]-[[synonyms:y:yuktaḥ]]---having twelve cantos; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śata]]-[[synonyms:v:viccheda]]-[[synonyms:s:saṁyutaḥ]]---having 355 chapters; [[synonyms:g:granthaḥ]]---this great literature; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭādaśa]]-[[synonyms:s:sāhasraḥ]]---having 18,000 verses; [[synonyms:ś:śrīmad]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]-[[synonyms:a:abhidhaḥ]]---named //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.//
translation: “ 'The meaning of the Vedānta-sūtra is present in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. The full purport of the Mahābhārata is also there. The commentary of the Brahma-gāyatrī is also there and fully expanded with all Vedic knowledge. Śrīmad Bhāgavatam is the supreme Purāṇa, and it was compiled by the Supreme Personality of Godhead in His incarnation as Vyāsadeva. There are twelve cantos, 335 chapters and eighteen thousand verses.'
purport: This is a quotation from the //Garuda Purāṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.145
description: " 'The essence of all Vedic literature and all histories has been collected in this Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.'
text:
> sarva-vedetihāsānāṁ
> sāraṁ sāraṁ samuddhṛtam
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:v:veda]]---of all Vedic literature; [[synonyms:i:itihāsānām]]---of historical literature; [[synonyms:s:sāram]] [[synonyms:s:sāram]]---the essence of the essence; [[synonyms:s:samuddhṛtam]]---is collected (in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//).
translation: “ 'The essence of all Vedic literature and all histories has been collected in this Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.'
purport: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam was collected by the incarnation of God, Vyāsadeva, and it was later taught to his son, Śukadeva Gosvāmī. This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:3:42|(1.3.42)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.146
description: " 'Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is accepted as the essence of all Vedic literature and Vedānta philosophy. Whoever tastes the transcendental mellow of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam is never attracted to any other literature.'
text:
> sarva-vedānta-sāraṁ hi
> śrīmad-bhāgavatam iṣyate
> tad-rasāmṛta-tṛptasya
> nānyatra syād ratiḥ kvacit
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:v:vedānta]]-[[synonyms:s:sāram]]---the best part of all the Vedānta; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:ś:śrīmad]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavatam]]---the great literature about Bhagavān; [[synonyms:i:iṣyate]]---is accepted; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---by the transcendental mellow derived from that great literature; [[synonyms:t:tṛp]]-[[synonyms:t:tasya]]---of one who is satisfied; [[synonyms:n:na]]---never; [[synonyms:a:anyatra]]---anywhere else; [[synonyms:s:syāt]]---is; [[synonyms:r:ratiḥ]]---attraction; [[synonyms:k:kvacit]]---at any time.
translation: “ 'Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is accepted as the essence of all Vedic literature and Vedānta philosophy. Whoever tastes the transcendental mellow of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam is never attracted to any other literature.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (12.13.15).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.147
description: "In the beginning of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam there is an explanation of the Brahma-gāyatrī mantra. 'The Absolute Truth [satyaṁ param]' indicates the relationship, and 'we meditate [dhīmahi] on Him' indicates the execution of devotional service and the ultimate goal of life.
text:
> gāyatrīra arthe ei grantha-ārambhana
> "satyaṁ paraṁ"-sambandha, "dhīmahi"-sādhana-prayojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gāyatrīra]] [[synonyms:a:arthe]]---with the meaning of Brahma-gāyatrī; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:g:grantha]]---of the great literature; [[synonyms:ā:ārambhana]]---the beginning; [[synonyms:s:satyam]] [[synonyms:p:param]]---the supreme Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:s:sambandha]]---shows a relationship; [[synonyms:d:dhīmahi]]---we meditate (the end of the Gāyatrī //mantra//); [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]-[[synonyms:p:prayojana]]---the execution of service and the achievement of the ultimate goal.
translation: "In the beginning of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam there is an explanation of the Brahma-gāyatrī mantra. 'The Absolute Truth [satyaṁ param]' indicates the relationship, and 'we meditate [dhīmahi] on Him' indicates the execution of devotional service and the ultimate goal of life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.148
description: " 'I offer my obeisances unto Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva, who is the supreme all-pervading Personality of Godhead. I meditate upon Him, the transcendent reality, who is the primeval cause of all causes, from whom all manifested universes arise, in whom they dwell and by whom they are destroyed. I meditate upon that eternally effulgent Lord who is directly and indirectly conscious of all manifestations and yet is beyond them. It is He only who first imparted Vedic knowledge unto the heart of Brahmā, the first created being. Through Him this world, like a mirage, appears real even to great sages and demigods. Because of Him, the material universes, created by the three modes of nature, appear to be factual, although they are unreal. I meditate therefore upon Him, the Absolute Truth, who is eternally existent in His transcendental abode, and who is forever free of illusion.
text:
> janmādy asya yato 'nvayād itarataś cārtheṣv abhijñaḥ svarāṭ
> tene brahma hṛdā ya ādi-kavaye muhyanti yat sūrayaḥ
> tejo-vāri-mṛdāṁ yathā vinimayo yatra tri-sargo 'mṛṣā
> dhāmnā svena sadā nirasta-kuhakaṁ satyaṁ paraṁ dhīmahi
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:janma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---creation, maintenance and dissolution; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of this (the universe); [[synonyms:y:yataḥ]]---from whom; [[synonyms:a:anvayāt]]---directly from the spiritual connection; [[synonyms:i:itarataḥ]]---indirectly from the lack of material contact; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:a:artheṣu]]---in all affairs; [[synonyms:a:abhijñaḥ]]---perfectly cognizant; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rāṭ]]---independent; [[synonyms:t:tene]]---imparted; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:h:hṛdā]]---through the heart; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:k:kavaye]]---unto Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:m:muhyanti]]---are bewildered; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---in whom; [[synonyms:s:sūrayaḥ]]---great personalities like Lord Brahmā and other demigods or great //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:t:tejaḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vāri]]-[[synonyms:m:mṛdām]]---of fire, water and earth; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:v:vinimayaḥ]]---the exchange; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---in whom; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:s:sargaḥ]]---the material creation of three modes; [[synonyms:a:amṛṣā]]---factual; [[synonyms:d:dhāmnā]]---with the abode; [[synonyms:s:svena]]---His own personal; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:n:nirasta]]-[[synonyms:k:kuhakam]]---devoid of all illusion; [[synonyms:s:satyam]]---the truth; [[synonyms:p:param]]---absolute; [[synonyms:d:dhīmahi]]---let us meditate upon.
translation: “ 'I offer my obeisances unto Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva, who is the supreme all-pervading Personality of Godhead. I meditate upon Him, the transcendent reality, who is the primeval cause of all causes, from whom all manifested universes arise, in whom they dwell and by whom they are destroyed. I meditate upon that eternally effulgent Lord who is directly and indirectly conscious of all manifestations and yet is beyond them. It is He only who first imparted Vedic knowledge unto the heart of Brahmā, the first created being. Through Him this world, like a mirage, appears real even to great sages and demigods. Because of Him, the material universes, created by the three modes of nature, appear to be factual, although they are unreal. I meditate therefore upon Him, the Absolute Truth, who is eternally existent in His transcendental abode, and who is forever free of illusion.
purport: This is the opening invocation of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:1:1|(1.1.1)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.149
description: " 'Completely rejecting all religious activities which are materially motivated, this Bhāgavata Purāṇa propounds the highest truth, which is understandable by those devotees who are pure in heart. The highest truth is reality distinguished from illusion for the welfare of all. Such truth uproots the threefold miseries. This beautiful Bhāgavatam, compiled by the great sage Śrī Vyāsadeva, is sufficient in itself for God realization. As soon as one attentively and submissively hears the message of Bhāgavatam, he becomes attached to the Supreme Lord.'
text:
> dharmaḥ projjhita-kaitavo 'tra paramo nirmatsarāṇāṁ satāṁ
> vedyaṁ vāstavam atra vastu śivadaṁ tāpa-trayonmūlanam
> śrīmad-bhāgavate mahāmuni-kṛte kiṁ vā parair īśvaraḥ
> sadyo hṛdy avarudhyate 'tra kṛtibhiḥ śuśrūṣubhis tat-kṣaṇāt
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dharmaḥ]]---religiosity; [[synonyms:p:projjhita]]---completely rejected; [[synonyms:k:kaitavaḥ]]---in which there is fruitive intention; [[synonyms:a:atra]]---herein; [[synonyms:p:paramaḥ]]---the highest; [[synonyms:n:nirmatsarāṇām]]---of the one hundred percent pure in heart; [[synonyms:s:satām]]---devotees; [[synonyms:v:vedyam]]---to be understood; [[synonyms:v:vāstavam]]---factual; [[synonyms:a:atra]]---herein; [[synonyms:v:vastu]]---substance; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]-[[synonyms:d:dam]]---giving well-being; [[synonyms:t:tāpa]]-[[synonyms:t:traya]]---of the threefold miseries; [[synonyms:u:unmūlanam]]---causing uprooting; [[synonyms:ś:śrīmat]]---beautiful; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavate]]---in the //Bhāgavata Purāṇa//; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:m:muni]]---by the great sage (Vyāsadeva); [[synonyms:k:kṛte]]---compiled; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---indeed; [[synonyms:p:paraiḥ]]---with others; [[synonyms:ī:īśvaraḥ]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:s:sadyaḥ]]---at once; [[synonyms:h:hṛdi]]---within the heart; [[synonyms:a:avarudhyate]]---becomes confined; [[synonyms:a:atra]]---herein; [[synonyms:k:kṛtibhiḥ]]---by pious men; [[synonyms:ś:śuśrūṣubhiḥ]]---desiring to hear; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇāt]]---without delay.
translation: “ 'Completely rejecting all religious activities which are materially motivated, this Bhāgavata Purāṇa propounds the highest truth, which is understandable by those devotees who are pure in heart. The highest truth is reality distinguished from illusion for the welfare of all. Such truth uproots the threefold miseries. This beautiful Bhāgavatam, compiled by the great sage Śrī Vyāsadeva, is sufficient in itself for God realization. As soon as one attentively and submissively hears the message of Bhāgavatam, he becomes attached to the Supreme Lord.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:1:2|(1.1.2)]]. See also //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter One, text 91.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.15
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted his invitation, and the next day, after finishing His noontime activities, He went to the brāhmaṇa's house.
text:
> tabe mahāprabhu tāṅra nimantraṇa mānilā
> āra dina madhyāhna kari' tāṅra ghare gelā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---after this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation; [[synonyms:m:mānilā]]---accepted; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---the next day; [[synonyms:m:madhyāhna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---after finishing His //madhyāhna// activities (taking bath and murmuring //mantras//); [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]] [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---He went to the house of the Mahārāṣṭrian //brāhmaṇa.//
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted his invitation, and the next day, after finishing His noontime activities, He went to the brāhmaṇa's house.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.150
description: "Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam gives direct information of the mellow derived from service to Kṛṣṇa. Therefore Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is above all other Vedic literatures.
text:
> 'kṛṣṇa-bhakti-rasa-svarūpa' śrī-bhāgavata
> tāte veda-śāstra haite parama mahattva
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---of devotional service to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---of the transcendental mellow; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---the very form; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]---//Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---the Vedic literature; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---than; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:m:mahattva]]---has greater utility and value.
translation: "Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam gives direct information of the mellow derived from service to Kṛṣṇa. Therefore Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is above all other Vedic literatures.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.151
description: " 'Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is the essence of all Vedic literatures, and it is considered the ripened fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree of Vedic knowledge. It has been sweetened by emanating from the mouth of Śukadeva Gosvāmī. You who are thoughtful and who relish mellows should always try to taste this ripened fruit. O thoughtful devotees, as long as you are not absorbed in transcendental bliss, you should continue tasting this Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and when you are fully absorbed in bliss, you should go on tasting its mellows forever.'
text:
> nigama-kalpa-taror galitaṁ phalaṁ
> śuka-mukhād amṛta-drava-saṁyutam
> pibata bhāgavataṁ rasam ālayaṁ
> muhur aho rasikā bhuvi bhāvukāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nigama]]-[[synonyms:k:kalpa]]-[[synonyms:t:taroḥ]]---of the Vedic literature which is like a desire tree; [[synonyms:g:galitam]]---completely ripened; [[synonyms:p:phalam]]---fruit (which has come down without being distorted); [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhāt]]---from the mouth of Śukadeva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---which is like nectar; [[synonyms:d:drava]]-[[synonyms:s:saṁyutam]]---mixed with juice; [[synonyms:p:pibata]]---just drink; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavatam]]---//Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:r:rasam]] [[synonyms:ā:ālayam]]---the reservoir of all mellows; [[synonyms:m:muhuḥ]]---constantly; [[synonyms:a:aho]]---O; [[synonyms:r:rasikāḥ]]---intelligent and humorous devotees; [[synonyms:b:bhuvi]]---in this world; [[synonyms:b:bhāvukāḥ]]---thoughtful.
translation: “ 'Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is the essence of all Vedic literatures, and it is considered the ripened fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree of Vedic knowledge. It has been sweetened by emanating from the mouth of Śukadeva Gosvāmī. You who are thoughtful and who relish mellows should always try to taste this ripened fruit. O thoughtful devotees, as long as you are not absorbed in transcendental bliss, you should continue tasting this Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and when you are fully absorbed in bliss, you should go on tasting its mellows forever.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:1:3|(1.1.3)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.152
description: " 'We never tire of hearing the transcendental pastimes of the Personality of Godhead, who is glorified by hymns and prayers. Those who enjoy association with Him relish hearing His pastimes at every moment.' "
text:
> vayaṁ tu na vitṛpyāma
> uttamaḥśloka-vikrame
> yac chṛṇvatāṁ rasa-jñānāṁ
> svādu svādu pade pade
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vayam]] [[synonyms:t:tu]]---we of course; [[synonyms:n:na]]---never; [[synonyms:v:vitṛpyāmaḥ]]---are satisfied; [[synonyms:u:uttamaḥ]]-[[synonyms:ś:śloka]]-[[synonyms:v:vikrame]]---in the activities and pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:ś:śṛṇvatām]]---of those hearing; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:j:jñānām]]---who know the taste of mellows; [[synonyms:s:svādu]] [[synonyms:s:svādu]]---more palatable; [[synonyms:p:pade]] [[synonyms:p:pade]]---in every step.
translation: “ 'We never tire of hearing the transcendental pastimes of the Personality of Godhead, who is glorified by hymns and prayers. Those who enjoy association with Him relish hearing His pastimes at every moment.' "
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:1:19|(1.1.19)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.153
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu advised Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī, "Study Śrīmad Bhāgavatam very scrutinizingly. Then you will understand the actual meaning of Brahma-sūtra"
text:
> ataeva bhāgavata karaha vicāra
> ihā haite pābe sūtra-śrutira artha-sāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]---//Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---try to understand scrutinizingly; [[synonyms:i:ihā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from this; [[synonyms:p:pābe]]---you will get; [[synonyms:s:sūtra]]-[[synonyms:ś:śrutira]]---of the Vedic philosophy, the //Brahma-sūtra//; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the actual meaning.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu advised Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī, "Study Śrīmad Bhāgavatam very scrutinizingly. Then you will understand the actual meaning of Brahma-sūtra"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.154
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "Always discuss Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and constantly chant the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way you will be able to attain liberation very easily, and you will be elevated to the enjoyment of love of Godhead.
text:
> nirantara kara kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana
> helāya mukti pābe, pābe prema-dhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirantara]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---constantly perform; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---the chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:helāya]]---very easily; [[synonyms:m:mukti]] [[synonyms:p:pābe]]---you will get liberation; [[synonyms:p:pābe]] [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---you will achieve the highest goal, ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "Always discuss Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and constantly chant the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way you will be able to attain liberation very easily, and you will be elevated to the enjoyment of love of Godhead.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura states that without studying //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// one cannot understand the purport of //Brahma-sūtra// (//Vedānta-sūtra//) or the //Upaniṣads.// If one tries to understand Vedānta philosophy and the //Upaniṣads// without studying //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// he will be bewildered and, construing a different meaning will gradually become an atheist or an impersonalist.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.155
description: " 'One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and becomes fully joyful. He never laments nor desires to have anything; he is equally disposed to every living entity. In that state he attains pure devotional service unto Me.'
text:
> brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā
> na śocati na kāṅkṣati
> samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu
> mad-bhaktiṁ labhate parām
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūtaḥ]]---freed from material conceptions of life but attached to an impersonal situation; [[synonyms:p:prasanna]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---fully joyful; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:ś:śocati]]---he does not lament; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:k:kāṅkṣati]]---he does not hanker; [[synonyms:s:samaḥ]]---equally disposed; [[synonyms:s:sarveṣu]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhūteṣu]]---to the living entities; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktim]]---My devotional service; [[synonyms:l:labhate]]---achieves; [[synonyms:p:parām]]---transcendental.
translation: “ 'One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and becomes fully joyful. He never laments nor desires to have anything; he is equally disposed to every living entity. In that state he attains pure devotional service unto Me.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.156
description: " 'Even a liberated soul merged in the impersonal Brahman effulgence is attracted to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. He thus installs a Deity and renders the Lord service.'
text:
> "muktā api līlayā vigrahaṁ
> kṛtvā bhagavantaṁ bhajante"
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muktāḥ]]---liberated; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:l:līlayā]]---by pastimes; [[synonyms:v:vigraham]]---the form of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛtvā]]---having installed; [[synonyms:b:bhagavantam]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhajante]]---worship.
translation: “ 'Even a liberated soul merged in the impersonal Brahman effulgence is attracted to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. He thus installs a Deity and renders the Lord service.'
purport: This is a quotation from Śaṅkarācārya's commentary on the //Nṛsiṁha-tāpanī.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.157
description: " 'Śukadeva Gosvāmī addressed Parīkṣit Mahārāja, "My dear King, although I was fully situated in the transcendental position, I was nonetheless attracted to the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Therefore I studied Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam from my father.' "
text:
> pariniṣṭhito 'pi nairguṇye
> uttamaḥśloka-līlayā
> gṛhīta-cetā rājarṣe
> ākhyānaṁ yad adhītavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pariniṣṭhitaḥ]]---situated; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:n:nairguṇye]]---in the transcendental position, freed from the material modes of nature; [[synonyms:u:uttamaḥ]]-[[synonyms:ś:śloka]]-[[synonyms:l:līlayā]]---by the pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Uttamaḥśloka; [[synonyms:g:gṛhīta]]-[[synonyms:c:cetā]]---the mind became fully taken over; [[synonyms:r:rājarṣe]]---O great King; [[synonyms:ā:ākhyānam]]---the narration; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:a:adhītavān]]---studied.
translation: “ 'Śukadeva Gosvāmī addressed Parīkṣit Mahārāja, "My dear King, although I was fully situated in the transcendental position, I was nonetheless attracted to the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Therefore I studied Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam from my father.' "
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:1:9|(2.1.9)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.158
description: " 'When the breeze carrying the aroma of tulasī leaves and saffron from the lotus feet of the lotus-eyed Personality of Godhead entered through the nostrils into the hearts of those sages [the Kumāras], they experienced a change in both body and mind, even though they were attached to impersonal Brahman understanding.'
text:
> tasyāravinda-nayanasya padāravinda-
> kiñjalka-miśra-tulasī-makaranda-vāyuḥ
> antargataḥ svavivareṇa cakāra teṣāṁ
> saṅkṣobham akṣara-juṣām api citta-tanvoḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tasya]]---of Him; [[synonyms:a:aravinda]]-[[synonyms:n:nayanasya]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose eyes are like the petals of a lotus flower; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:a:aravinda]]---of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:k:kiñjalka]]---with saffron; [[synonyms:m:miśra]]---mixed; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]---of //tulasī// leaves; [[synonyms:m:makaranda]]---with the aroma; [[synonyms:v:vāyuḥ]]---the air; [[synonyms:a:antargataḥ]]---entered; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:v:vivareṇa]]---through the nostrils; [[synonyms:c:cakāra]]---created; [[synonyms:t:teṣām]]---of them; [[synonyms:s:saṅkṣobham]]---strong agitation; [[synonyms:a:akṣara]]-[[synonyms:j:juṣām]]---of the impersonally self-realized (Kumāras); [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:c:citta]]-[[synonyms:t:tanvoḥ]]---of the mind and the body.
translation: “ 'When the breeze carrying the aroma of tulasī leaves and saffron from the lotus feet of the lotus-eyed Personality of Godhead entered through the nostrils into the hearts of those sages [the Kumāras], they experienced a change in both body and mind, even though they were attached to impersonal Brahman understanding.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:15:43|(3.15.43)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.159
description: " 'Those who are self-satisfied and unattracted by external material desires are also attracted to the loving service of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose qualities are transcendental and whose activities are wonderful. Hari, the Personality of Godhead, is called Kṛṣṇa because He has such transcendentally attractive features.' "
text:
> ātmārāmāś ca munayo
> nirgranthā apy urukrame
> kurvanty ahaitukīṁ bhaktim
> ittham-bhūta-guṇo hariḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārāmāḥ]]---persons who take pleasure in being transcendentally situated in the service of the Lord; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]]---great saintly persons who have completely rejected material aspirations, fruitive activities, and so forth; [[synonyms:n:nirgranthāḥ]]---without interest in any material desire; [[synonyms:a:api]]---certainly; [[synonyms:u:urukrame]]---unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, whose activities are wonderful; [[synonyms:k:kurvanti]]---do; [[synonyms:a:ahaitukīm]]---causeless, or without material desires; [[synonyms:b:bhaktim]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:i:ittham]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūta]]---so wonderful as to attract the attention of the self-satisfied; [[synonyms:g:guṇaḥ]]---who has transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'Those who are self-satisfied and unattracted by external material desires are also attracted to the loving service of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose qualities are transcendental and whose activities are wonderful. Hari, the Personality of Godhead, is called Kṛṣṇa because He has such transcendentally attractive features.' "
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:7:10|(1.7.10)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.16
description: I have already described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's deliverance of the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs in the Seventh Chapter when I described the glories of the Pañca-tattva-Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Advaita Prabhu, Gadādhara Prabhu and Śrīvāsa.
text:
> tāhāṅ yaiche kailā prabhu sannyāsīra nistāra
> pañca-tattvākhyāne tāhā kariyāchi vistāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---how; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---performed; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]]---of the Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---deliverance; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākhyāne]]---in describing the glories of the Pañca-tattva (Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita, Gadādhara and Śrīvāsa); [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that subject matter; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchi]] [[synonyms:v:vistāra]]---have described elaborately.
translation: I have already described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's deliverance of the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs in the Seventh Chapter when I described the glories of the Pañca-tattva-Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Advaita Prabhu, Gadādhara Prabhu and Śrīvāsa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.160
description: At this time the brāhmaṇa from the province of Mahārāṣṭra mentioned Lord Caitanya's explanation of the ātmārāma verse.
text:
> hena-kāle sei mahārāṣṭrīya brāhmaṇa
> sabhāte kahila sei śloka-vivaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:m:mahārāṣṭrīya]] [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---the //brāhmaṇa// of Mahārāṣṭra province; [[synonyms:s:sabhāte]]---in the meeting; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---declared; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]-[[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---the description of the //ātmārāma-śloka// explained by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: At this time the brāhmaṇa from the province of Mahārāṣṭra mentioned Lord Caitanya's explanation of the ātmārāma verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.161
description: The Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa stated that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had already explained that verse in sixty-one ways. Everyone was astonished to hear this.
text:
> ei ślokera artha prabhu 'ekaṣaṣṭi' prakāra
> kariyāchena, yāhā śuni' loke camatkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:ślokera]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meanings of this verse; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṣṭi]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---sixty-one varieties; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchena]]---has done; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing which; [[synonyms:l:loke]] [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---everyone is astonished.
translation: The Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa stated that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had already explained that verse in sixty-one ways. Everyone was astonished to hear this.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.162
description: When all the people gathered there expressed the desire to hear again the sixty-one different meanings of the ātmārāma-śloka, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu again explained them.
text:
> tabe saba loka śunite āgraha karila
> 'ekaṣaṣṭi' artha prabhu vivari' kahila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people gathered there; [[synonyms:ś:śunite]]---to hear; [[synonyms:ā:āgraha]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---expressed their eagerness; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṣṭi]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---sixty-one different meanings of the verse; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vivari']]---elaborately; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---explained.
translation: When all the people gathered there expressed the desire to hear again the sixty-one different meanings of the ātmārāma-śloka, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu again explained them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.163
description: When everyone heard Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's explanation of the ātmārāma-śloka, everyone was astonished and struck with wonder. They concluded that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was none other than Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself.
text:
> śuniyā lokera baḍa camatkāra haila
> caitanya-gosāñi-'śrī-kṛṣṇa', nirdhārila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of all the people; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very great; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---wonder; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---personally Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nirdhārila]]---they concluded.
translation: When everyone heard Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's explanation of the ātmārāma-śloka, everyone was astonished and struck with wonder. They concluded that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was none other than Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.164
description: After giving those explanations again, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arose and took His leave. All the people there offered their obeisances unto Him and chanted the mahā-mantra.
text:
> eta kahi' uṭhiyā calilā gaurahari
> namaskāra kare loka hari-dhvani kari
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---after speaking that; [[synonyms:u:uṭhiyā]]---standing; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---began to walk; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Śrī Gaurasundara, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]] [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people offered their obeisances; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---loudly chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.//
translation: After giving those explanations again, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arose and took His leave. All the people there offered their obeisances unto Him and chanted the mahā-mantra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.165
description: All the inhabitants of Kāśī [Vārāṇasī] began chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra in ecstatic love. Sometimes they laughed, sometimes they cried, sometimes they chanted, and sometimes they danced.
text:
> saba kāśī-vāsī kare nāma-saṅkīrtana
> preme hāse, kāṅde, gāya, karaye nartana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:k:kāśī]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---all the inhabitants of Kāśī (Vārāṇasī); [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performed; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra//; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstatic love of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:hāse]]---they laughed; [[synonyms:k:kāṅde]]---they cried; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chanted; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---and danced.
translation: All the inhabitants of Kāśī [Vārāṇasī] began chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra in ecstatic love. Sometimes they laughed, sometimes they cried, sometimes they chanted, and sometimes they danced.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.166
description: After this, all the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs and learned scholars at Vārāṇasī began discussing Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered them.
text:
> sannyāsī paṇḍita kare bhāgavata vicāra
> vārāṇasī-pura prabhu karilā nistāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---the Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---the learned scholars; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]] [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---discussion on //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:v:vārāṇasī]]-[[synonyms:p:pura]]---the city known as Vārāṇasī; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---delivered.
translation: After this, all the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs and learned scholars at Vārāṇasī began discussing Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.167
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then returned to His residence with His personal associates. Thus He turned the whole city of Vārāṇasī into another Navadvīpa [Nadīyā-nagara].
text:
> nija-loka lañā prabhu āilā vāsāghara
> vārāṇasī haila dvitīya nadīyā-nagara
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---with His personal associates; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]] [[synonyms:v:vāsa]]-[[synonyms:a:aghara]]---came to His residential place; [[synonyms:v:vārāṇasī]]---the city of Vārāṇasī; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]]---second; [[synonyms:n:nadīyā]]-[[synonyms:n:nagara]]---Navadvīpa (Nadia).
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then returned to His residence with His personal associates. Thus He turned the whole city of Vārāṇasī into another Navadvīpa [Nadīyā-nagara].
purport: Both Navadvīpa and Vārāṇasī were celebrated for their highly educational activities. At the present time these cities are still inhabited by great, learned scholars, but Vārāṇasī is especially a center for Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// who are learned scholars. However, unlike Navadvīpa, there are hardly any devotees in Vārāṇasī. Consequently a discussion of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// was very rare in Vārāṇasī. In Navadvīpa, such a discussion was quite ordinary. After Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited Vārāṇasī and turned Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī and his disciples into Vaiṣṇavas, Vārāṇasī became like Navadvīpa because so many devotees began discussing //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.// Even at the present moment one can hear many discussions on //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// taking place on the banks of the Ganges. Many scholars and //sannyāsīs// gather there to hear //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// and perform //saṅkīrtana.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.168
description: Among His own associates, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu laughingly said, "I came here to sell My emotional ecstatic love.
text:
> nija-gaṇa lañā prabhu kahe hāsya kari'
> kāśīte āmi āilāṅa vecite bhāvakāli
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---with His personal associates; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:h:hāsya]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---laughingly; [[synonyms:k:kāśīte]]---in Kāśī; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:ā:āilāṅa]]---I came; [[synonyms:v:vecite]]---to sell; [[synonyms:b:bhāvakāli]]---emotional ecstatic love.
translation: Among His own associates, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu laughingly said, "I came here to sell My emotional ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.169
description: "Although I came to Vārāṇasī to sell My goods, there were no customers, and it appeared necessary for Me to carry them back to My own country.
text:
> kāśīte grāhaka nāhi, vastu nā vikāya
> punarapi deśe vahi' laoyā nāhi yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāśīte]]---in Kāśī (Benares); [[synonyms:g:grāhaka]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there was no customer; [[synonyms:v:vastu]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:v:vikāya]]---it was not selling; [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:d:deśe]]---to My own country; [[synonyms:v:vahi']]---carrying (it); [[synonyms:l:laoyā]]---to take; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---was not possible.
translation: "Although I came to Vārāṇasī to sell My goods, there were no customers, and it appeared necessary for Me to carry them back to My own country.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.17
description: Since I have already described this incident very elaborately in the Seventh Chapter of Ādi-līlā, I do not wish to increase the size of this book by giving another description. However, I shall try to include in this chapter whatever was not described there.
text:
> grantha bāḍe, punarukti haya ta' kathana
> tāhāṅ ye nā likhiluṅ, tāhā kariye likhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:grantha]]---the size of the book; [[synonyms:b:bāḍe]]---increases; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]-[[synonyms:u:ukti]]---repetition; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---would be; [[synonyms:t:ta']] [[synonyms:k:kathana]]---of subject matters once described; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there (in the Seventh Chapter); [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:l:likhiluṅ]]---I have not described; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kariye]] [[synonyms:l:likhana]]---I am writing.
translation: Since I have already described this incident very elaborately in the Seventh Chapter of Ādi-līlā, I do not wish to increase the size of this book by giving another description. However, I shall try to include in this chapter whatever was not described there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.170
description: "All of you were feeling unhappy that no one was purchasing My goods and that I would have to carry them away. Therefore, by your will only, I have distributed them without charging."
text:
> āmi bojhā vahimu, tomā-sabāra duḥkha haila
> tomā-sabāra icchāya vinā-mūlye bilāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bojhā]]---burden; [[synonyms:v:vahimu]]---shall carry; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]] [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---all of you became very unhappy; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]] [[synonyms:i:icchāya]]---only by your will; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]-[[synonyms:m:mūlye]] [[synonyms:b:bilāila]]---I distributed without a price.
translation: "All of you were feeling unhappy that no one was purchasing My goods and that I would have to carry them away. Therefore, by your will only, I have distributed them without charging."
purport: When we began distributing the message of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in the Western countries, a similar thing happened. In the beginning we were very disappointed for at least one year because no one came forth to help this movement, but by the grace of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, some young boys joined this movement in 1966. Of course we distributed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's message of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// without bargaining or selling. As a result, this movement has spread all over the world, with the assistance of European and American boys and girls. We therefore pray for all the blessings of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu upon all the devotees in the Western world who are spreading this movement.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.171
description: All the Lord's devotees then said, "You have incarnated to deliver fallen souls. You have delivered them in the east and in the south, and now you are delivering them in the west.
text:
> sabe kahe,-loka tārite tomāra avatāra
> 'pūrva' 'dakṣiṇa' 'paścima' karilā nistāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---everyone says; [[synonyms:l:loka]] [[synonyms:t:tārite]]---to deliver the fallen souls; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---Your incarnation; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]---east; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]]---south; [[synonyms:p:paścima]]---west; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---You have delivered.
translation: All the Lord's devotees then said, "You have incarnated to deliver fallen souls. You have delivered them in the east and in the south, and now you are delivering them in the west.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.172
description: "Only Vārāṇasī was left because the people there were against Your missionary activities. Now You have delivered them, and we are all very happy."
text:
> 'eka' vārāṇasī chila tomāte vimukha
> tāhā nistāriyā kailā āmā-sabāra sukha
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:v:vārāṇasī]]---the city of Vārāṇasī; [[synonyms:c:chila]]---remained; [[synonyms:t:tomāte]] [[synonyms:v:vimukha]]---against Your missionary activities; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:n:nistāriyā]]---delivering; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---have done; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of us; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---awakening of happiness.
translation: "Only Vārāṇasī was left because the people there were against Your missionary activities. Now You have delivered them, and we are all very happy."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.173
description: After the news of these events was broadcast, everyone from the surrounding neighborhoods began to pour in to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> vārāṇasī-grāme yadi kolāhala haila
> śuni' grāmī deśī loka āsite lāgila
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vārāṇasī]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in the city of Vārāṇasī; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---when; [[synonyms:k:kolāhala]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was broadcasting of this news; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:g:grāmī]]---from the villages; [[synonyms:d:deśī]]---from the towns; [[synonyms:l:loka]] [[synonyms:ā:āsite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---people began to pour in.
translation: After the news of these events was broadcast, everyone from the surrounding neighborhoods began to pour in to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.174
description: Hundreds and thousands of people came to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. There was no counting the number. Because the Lord's residence was very small, not everyone could see Him.
text:
> lakṣa koṭi loka āise, nāhika gaṇana
> saṅkīrṇa-sthāne prabhura nā pāya daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]] [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---hundreds and thousands; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---come; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---there was no counting; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in a small place; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---could not get an audience.
