translation: I have thus given a summary of the Madhya-līlā, which is a special description of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's travels to and from Jagannātha Purī. Indeed, the Lord traveled to and fro continuously for six years.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.241
description: After taking sannyāsa at the age of twenty-four, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lived another twenty-four years. For six of these years, He traveled extensively throughout India, sometimes going to Jagannātha Purī and sometimes leaving. After traveling for six years, the Lord fixed His residence at Jagannātha Purī and stayed there for the eighteen remaining years of His life. During these eighteen years He mainly chanted Hare Kṛṣṇa with His devotees.
text:
> śeṣa aṣṭādaśa vatsara nīlācale vāsa
> bhakta-gaṇa-saṅge kare kīrtana-vilāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]] [[synonyms:a:aṣṭādaśa]] [[synonyms:v:vatsara]]---the remaining eighteen years; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]] [[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---residence at Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with devotees; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---the pastimes of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra.//
translation: After taking sannyāsa at the age of twenty-four, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lived another twenty-four years. For six of these years, He traveled extensively throughout India, sometimes going to Jagannātha Purī and sometimes leaving. After traveling for six years, the Lord fixed His residence at Jagannātha Purī and stayed there for the eighteen remaining years of His life. During these eighteen years He mainly chanted Hare Kṛṣṇa with His devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.242
description: I shall now chronologically reassess the chapters of Madhya-līlā so that one can relish the transcendental features of these topics.
text:
> madhya-līlāra krama ebe kari anuvāda
> anuvāda kaile haya kathāra āsvāda
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlāra]] [[synonyms:k:krama]]---a chronological list of the pastimes described in the //Madhya-līlā// of //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I may do; [[synonyms:a:anuvāda]]---assessment; [[synonyms:a:anuvāda]] [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---by assessing in that way; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:k:kathāra]] [[synonyms:ā:āsvāda]]---tasting of all the topics.
translation: I shall now chronologically reassess the chapters of Madhya-līlā so that one can relish the transcendental features of these topics.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.243
description: In the First Chapter I have given a synopsis of the last pastimes [Antya-līlā]. Within this chapter is a vivid description of some of the pastimes of the Lord that took place toward the end of His life.
text:
> prathama paricchede-śeṣa-līlāra sūtra-gaṇa
> tathi-madhye kona bhāgera vistāra varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prathama]] [[synonyms:p:paricchede]]---in the First Chapter; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlāra]] [[synonyms:s:sūtra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the codes of the //Antya-līlā,// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastimes at the end; [[synonyms:t:tathi]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that; [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:b:bhāgera]]---of some portion of the book; [[synonyms:v:vistāra]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---a vivid description.
translation: In the First Chapter I have given a synopsis of the last pastimes [Antya-līlā]. Within this chapter is a vivid description of some of the pastimes of the Lord that took place toward the end of His life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.244
description: In the Second Chapter I have described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's talking like a crazy man. Within this chapter it is indicated how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu manifested His different emotional moods.
text:
> dvitīya paricchede-prabhura pralāpa-varṇana
> tathi-madhye nānā-bhāvera dig-daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]] [[synonyms:p:paricchede]]---in the Second Chapter; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pralāpa]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---a description of His behaving like a crazy man; [[synonyms:t:tathi]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of different emotional ecstasies; [[synonyms:d:dik]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---indication.
translation: In the Second Chapter I have described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's talking like a crazy man. Within this chapter it is indicated how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu manifested His different emotional moods.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.245
description: In the Third Chapter I have described the Lord's acceptance of the renounced order and how He enjoyed His pastimes in the house of Advaita Ācārya.
text:
> tṛtīya paricchede-prabhura kahiluṅ sannyāsa
> ācāryera ghare yaiche karilā vilāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tṛtīya]] [[synonyms:p:paricchede]]---in the Third Chapter; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have described; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---acceptance of the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at the house of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---how; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---enjoyed His pastimes.
translation: In the Third Chapter I have described the Lord's acceptance of the renounced order and how He enjoyed His pastimes in the house of Advaita Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.246
description: In the Fourth Chapter I have described Mādhavendra Purī's installation of the Gopāla Deity as well as Gopīnātha's stealing a pot of condensed milk at Remuṇā.
text:
> caturthe-mādhava purīra caritra-āsvādana
> gopāla sthāpana, kṣīra-curira varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caturthe]]---in the Fourth Chapter; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]] [[synonyms:p:purīra]]---of Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:c:caritra]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---relishing the characteristics; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]] [[synonyms:s:sthāpana]]---the installation of Gopāla; [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]-[[synonyms:c:curira]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---a description of Gopīnātha's stealing condensed milk at Remuṇā.
translation: In the Fourth Chapter I have described Mādhavendra Purī's installation of the Gopāla Deity as well as Gopīnātha's stealing a pot of condensed milk at Remuṇā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.247
description: In the Fifth Chapter I have narrated the story of Sākṣi-gopāla. Lord Nityānanda Prabhu narrated this while Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu listened.
text:
> pañcame-sākṣi-gopāla-caritra-varṇana
> nityānanda kahe, prabhu karena āsvādana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pañcame]]---in the Fifth Chapter; [[synonyms:s:sākṣi]]-[[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Sākṣi-gopāla; [[synonyms:c:caritra]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---a description of the characteristics; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Nityānanda described this; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasted it.
translation: In the Fifth Chapter I have narrated the story of Sākṣi-gopāla. Lord Nityānanda Prabhu narrated this while Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu listened.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.248
description: In the Sixth Chapter I have told how Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was delivered, and in the Seventh Chapter I have described the Lord's tour of different holy places and His deliverance of Vāsudeva.
text:
> ṣaṣṭhe-sārvabhaumera karilā uddhāra
> saptame-tīrtha-yātrā, vāsudeva nistāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṣṭhe]]---in the Sixth Chapter; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhaumera]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:u:uddhāra]]---the Lord delivered; [[synonyms:s:saptame]]---in the Seventh Chapter; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---going to different holy places; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]] [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---delivering Vāsudeva.
translation: In the Sixth Chapter I have told how Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was delivered, and in the Seventh Chapter I have described the Lord's tour of different holy places and His deliverance of Vāsudeva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.249
description: In the Eighth Chapter I have recorded the Lord's elaborate discussion with Rāmānanda Rāya. The Lord personally listened as Rāmānanda gave the conclusive essence of all Vedic literatures.
text:
> aṣṭame-rāmānanda-saṁvāda vistāra
> āpane śunilā 'sarva-siddhāntera sāra'
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aṣṭame]]---in the Eighth Chapter; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:saṁvāda]] [[synonyms:v:vistāra]]---an elaborate discussion with Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:ś:śunilā]]---listened; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:s:siddhāntera]]---of conclusions; [[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the essence.
translation: In the Eighth Chapter I have recorded the Lord's elaborate discussion with Rāmānanda Rāya. The Lord personally listened as Rāmānanda gave the conclusive essence of all Vedic literatures.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.25
description: "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu explains the direct meaning of the Upaniṣads. When all learned scholars hear this, their minds and ears are satisfied.
text:
> upaniṣadera karena mukhyārtha vyākhyāna
> śuniyā paṇḍita-lokera juḍāya mana-kāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:upaniṣadera]]---of the Vedic version known as the //Upaniṣads//; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---He does; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---the original meaning; [[synonyms:v:vyākhyāna]]---explanation; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]-[[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of the learned scholars; [[synonyms:j:juḍāya]]---satisfies; [[synonyms:m:mana]]-[[synonyms:k:kāṇa]]---the minds and ears.
translation: "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu explains the direct meaning of the Upaniṣads. When all learned scholars hear this, their minds and ears are satisfied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.250
description: In the Ninth Chapter I have described the Lord's tour of South India and the different places of pilgrimage. In the Tenth Chapter I have described the meeting of all the devotees of the Lord.
text:
> navame-kahiluṅ dakṣiṇa-tīrtha-bhramaṇa
> daśame-kahiluṅ sarva-vaiṣṇava-milana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:navame]]---in the Ninth Chapter; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have described; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhramaṇa]]---going on pilgrimage in South India; [[synonyms:d:daśame]]---in the Tenth Chapter; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have described; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting of all kinds of devotees.
translation: In the Ninth Chapter I have described the Lord's tour of South India and the different places of pilgrimage. In the Tenth Chapter I have described the meeting of all the devotees of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.251
description: In the Eleventh Chapter I have described the great chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra that surrounded the Lord. In the Twelfth Chapter I have given a narration of the cleansing and washing of the Guṇḍicā temple.
text:
> ekādaśe-śrī-mandire 'beḍā-saṅkīrtana'
> dvādaśe-guṇḍicā-mandira-mārjana-kṣālana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ekādaśe]]---in the Eleventh Chapter; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:m:mandire]]---in the Jagannātha temple; [[synonyms:b:beḍā]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// all around; [[synonyms:d:dvādaśe]]---in the Twelfth Chapter; [[synonyms:g:guṇḍicā]]-[[synonyms:m:mandira]]---of the temple known as Guṇḍicā; [[synonyms:m:mārjana]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣālana]]---cleansing and washing.
translation: In the Eleventh Chapter I have described the great chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra that surrounded the Lord. In the Twelfth Chapter I have given a narration of the cleansing and washing of the Guṇḍicā temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.252
description: In the Thirteenth Chapter I have described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's dancing before the chariot of Jagannātha. In the Fourteenth Chapter, there is an account of the Herā-pañcamī function.
text:
> trayodaśe-ratha-āge prabhura nartana
> caturdaśe-'herā-pañcamī'-yātrā-daraśana

translation: In the Twenty-third Chapter there is a description of the mellows of transcendental loving service, and in the Twenty-fourth Chapter the Lord analyzes the ātmārāma verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.261

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.262

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.264
description: To deliver all fallen souls, the Lord traveled from country to country. He personally tasted the transcendental pleasure of devotional service, and He simultaneously spread the cult of devotion everywhere.
text:
> jīva nistārite prabhu bhramilā deśe-deśe
> āpane āsvādi' bhakti karilā prakāśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jīva]] [[synonyms:n:nistārite]]---to deliver all the fallen souls; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhramilā]]---traveled; [[synonyms:d:deśe]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in various countries; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādi']]---tasting; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---broadcasting.
translation: To deliver all fallen souls, the Lord traveled from country to country. He personally tasted the transcendental pleasure of devotional service, and He simultaneously spread the cult of devotion everywhere.
purport:
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally traveled to different regions of India to spread the //bhakti// cult throughout the country. He also personally relished transcendental activities. By His personal behavior He has given an example for devotees to follow. That is, one should broadcast the cult of devotional service. He specifically instructed His devotees to enjoin all Indians to broadcast this message throughout the world because at that time the Lord could not personally travel to other parts of the world. In this regard, He has left two instructions:

> bhārata-bhūmite haila manuṣya-janma yāra
> janma sārthaka kari' kara para-upakāra

"All Indians should seriously take up the cult of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and should perfect their lives by adopting the process of devotional service. After perfecting their lives, they should broadcast this message all over the world for the welfare of all human beings [//para-upakāra//]." [[books:cc:adi:9:41|(Cc. Ādi 9.41)]] A Vaiṣṇava is especially interested in //para-upakāra,// doing good to others. Prahlāda Mahārāja was also interested in this. He did not want to be delivered alone; rather, he wanted to deliver all fallen souls, who are bereft of knowledge of //bhakti// and who misuse their intelligence for the temporary benefit of the material body. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also wanted His mission spread all over the world.

> pṛthivīte āche yata nagarādi grāma
> sarvatra pracāra haibe mora nāma

"In every town and village, the chanting of My name will be heard."

Following in His footsteps, we are trying to broadcast His message throughout the world. By His mercy, people are taking this movement very seriously. Indeed, our books are extensively distributed in the Western countries, especially in America and Europe. Even the ecclesiastical orders in these countries are appreciating the value of this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement and are ready to unite for the highest benefit of human society. The followers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu may therefore take this movement seriously and broadcast it throughout the world, from village to village and from town to town, just as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself did.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.265
description: Kṛṣṇa consciousness means understanding the truth of Kṛṣṇa, the truth of devotional service, the truth of love of Godhead, the truth of emotional ecstasy, the truth of transcendental mellow and the truth of the pastimes of the Lord.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-tattva, bhakti-tattva, prema-tattva sāra
> bhāva-tattva, rasa-tattva, līlā-tattva āra

translation: Kṛṣṇa consciousness means understanding the truth of Kṛṣṇa, the truth of devotional service, the truth of love of Godhead, the truth of emotional ecstasy, the truth of transcendental mellow and the truth of the pastimes of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.266
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has personally preached the transcendental truths and mellows of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and the Supreme Personality of Godhead are identical, for Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is the sound incarnation of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> śrī-bhāgavata-tattva-rasa karilā pracāre
> kṛṣṇa-tulya bhāgavata, jānāilā saṁsāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---the truth and transcendental taste of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:p:pracāre]]---Caitanya Mahāprabhu preached elaborately; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:t:tulya]]---identical with Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]---//Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:j:jānāilā]] [[synonyms:s:saṁsāre]]---has preached within this world.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has personally preached the transcendental truths and mellows of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and the Supreme Personality of Godhead are identical, for Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is the sound incarnation of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.267
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu broadcast the purpose of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. He sometimes spoke for the benefit of His devotees and sometimes empowered one of His devotees to speak while He listened.
text:
> bhakta lāgi' vistārilā āpana-vadane
> kāhāṅ bhakta-mukhe kahāi śunilā āpane
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---especially for the purpose of His devotees; [[synonyms:v:vistārilā]]---expansively described; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:v:vadane]]---personally, with His own mouth; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---through the mouth of His devotees; [[synonyms:k:kahāi]]---making describe; [[synonyms:ś:śunilā]] [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---listened Himself.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu broadcast the purpose of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. He sometimes spoke for the benefit of His devotees and sometimes empowered one of His devotees to speak while He listened.
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, as an ideal teacher, or //ācārya,// explained //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// very elaborately Himself. He sometimes also empowered His devotees to speak while He listened. This is the way an //ācārya// should train His disciples. Not only should he describe the //bhāgavata// cult personally, but he should also train his disciples to speak on this sublime subject.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.268
description: All sane men within these three worlds certainly accept the conclusion that no one is more merciful and magnanimous than Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and that no one is as kind to His devotees.
text:
> śrī-caitanya-sama āra kṛpālu vadānya
> bhakta-vatsala nā dekhi trijagate anya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---anyone else; [[synonyms:k:kṛpālu]]---merciful; [[synonyms:v:vadānya]]---magnanimous; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vatsala]]---very kind to the devotees; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---I do not see; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:j:jagate]]---in these three worlds; [[synonyms:a:anya]]---anyone else.
translation: All sane men within these three worlds certainly accept the conclusion that no one is more merciful and magnanimous than Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and that no one is as kind to His devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.269
description: All devotees should hear about Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastimes with faith and love. By the grace of the Lord, one can thus attain shelter at His lotus feet.
text:
> śraddhā kari' ei līlā śuna, bhakta-gaṇa
> ihāra prasāde pāibā caitanya-caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---having faith and love; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---these pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---O devotees; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]] [[synonyms:p:prasāde]]---by the grace of this transcendental hearing; [[synonyms:p:pāibā]]---you will get; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All devotees should hear about Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastimes with faith and love. By the grace of the Lord, one can thus attain shelter at His lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.27
description: "All the interpretations of Śaṅkarācārya are imaginary. Such imaginary interpretations are verbally accepted by learned scholars, but they do not appeal to the heart.
text:
> ācārya-kalpita artha ye paṇḍita śune
> mukhe 'haya' 'haya' kare, hṛdaya nā māne
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:k:kalpita]]---imagined by Śaṅkarācārya; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]] [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---any learned person who hears; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---only in the mouth; [[synonyms:h:haya]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---yes it is, yes it is; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]---his heart; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:m:māne]]---does not accept.
translation: "All the interpretations of Śaṅkarācārya are imaginary. Such imaginary interpretations are verbally accepted by learned scholars, but they do not appeal to the heart.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.270
description: By understanding the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, one can understand the truth about Kṛṣṇa. By understanding Kṛṣṇa, one can understand the limit of all knowledge described in various revealed scriptures.
text:
> ihāra prasāde pāibā kṛṣṇa-tattva-sāra
> sarva-śāstra-siddhāntera ihāṅ pāibā pāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ihāra]] [[synonyms:p:prasāde]]---by hearing these teachings of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pāibā]]---you will get; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the essence of the truth of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---of all revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:s:siddhāntera]]---of conclusions; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:p:pāibā]]---you will get; [[synonyms:p:pāra]]---the ultimate limit.
translation: By understanding the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, one can understand the truth about Kṛṣṇa. By understanding Kṛṣṇa, one can understand the limit of all knowledge described in various revealed scriptures.
purport:
As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:7:3|(Bg. 7.3)]]:

> manuṣyāṇāṁ sahasreṣu
> kaścid yatati siddhaye
> yatatām api siddhānāṁ
> kaścin māṁ vetti tattvataḥ

"Out of many thousands among men, one may endeavor for perfection, and of those who have achieved perfection, hardly one knows Me in truth."

It is very difficult to understand Kṛṣṇa, but if one tries to understand //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// through Caitanya Mahāprabhu's //bhakti// cult, one will undoubtedly understand Kṛṣṇa very easily. If somehow or other one understands Kṛṣṇa, his life will be successful. Again, as stated in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:4:9|(Bg. 4.9)]]:

> janma karma ca me divyam
> evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ
> tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma
> naiti mām eti so 'rjuna

"One who knows the transcendental nature of My appearance and activities does not, upon leaving the body, take his birth again in this material world, but attains My eternal abode, O Arjuna."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.271
description: The pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa are the essence of all nectar. They flow in hundreds of rivulets and in all directions. The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are an eternal reservoir, and one is advised to let his mind swim like a swan on this transcendental lake.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-līlā amṛta-sāra, tāra śata śata dhāra,
> daśa-dike vahe yāhā haite
> se caitanya-līlā haya, sarovara akṣaya,
> mano-haṁsa carāha' tāhāte
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]] [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa are the essence of all eternal bliss; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:ś:śata]] [[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---the flow of that eternal bliss is running in hundreds of branches; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---in all the ten directions; [[synonyms:v:vahe]]---flows; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from which; [[synonyms:s:se]]---those; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:s:sarovara]] [[synonyms:a:akṣaya]]---a transcendental eternal lake; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:h:haṁsa]]---my mind, which is like a swan; [[synonyms:c:carāha']]---please wander; [[synonyms:t:tāhāte]]---in that lake.
translation: The pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa are the essence of all nectar. They flow in hundreds of rivulets and in all directions. The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are an eternal reservoir, and one is advised to let his mind swim like a swan on this transcendental lake.
purport: The essence of spiritual knowledge is found in the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, which are identical with the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. This is the essence of knowledge. If knowledge does not include the understanding of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Kṛṣṇa, it is simply superfluous. By Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's grace, the nectar of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa's pastimes is flowing in different directions in hundreds and thousands of rivers. One should not think that the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are different from Kṛṣṇa's pastimes. It is said: //śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya, rādhā-kṛṣṇa nahe anya.// Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu is a combination of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and without understanding His pastimes, one cannot understand Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura therefore sings: //rūpa-raghunātha-pade haibe ākuti kabe hāma bujhaba se yugala pirīti.// "When shall I become very eager to study the books left by the six Gosvāmīs? Then I shall be able to understand the conjugal pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa." Caitanya Mahāprabhu directly empowered Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī. Following in their footsteps, the other six Gosvāmīs understood Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His mission. One should understand Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa from the Gosvāmīs in the //paramparā// system. This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is following as strictly as possible in the footsteps of the Gosvāmīs. Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says, //eichaya gosāñi yāra, mui tāra dāsa:// "I am the servant of the six Gosvāmīs." The philosophy of Kṛṣṇa consciousness is to become the servant of the servant of the servant of the Lord. Whoever wants to understand the difficult subject matter of //kṛṣṇa-kathā// should accept the disciplic succession. If one is somehow or other able to understand Kṛṣṇa, his life will be successful. //Tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so 'rjuna.// A perfect devotee is able to understand Kṛṣṇa through the disciplic succession, and his entrance into the kingdom of God is thereby certainly opened. When one understands Kṛṣṇa, there is no difficulty in transferring oneself to the spiritual kingdom.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.272
description: With all humility, I submit myself to the lotus feet of all of you devotees, taking the dust from your feet as my bodily ornaments. Now, my dear devotees, please hear one thing more from me.
text:
> bhakta-gaṇa, śuna mora dainya-vacana
> tomā-sabāra pada-dhūli, aṅge vibhūṣaṇa kari',
> kichu muñi karoṅ nivedana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---O devotees; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]-[[synonyms:v:vacana]]---humble submission; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of you; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:d:dhūli]]---the dust of the feet; [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---on my body; [[synonyms:v:vibhūṣaṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking as ornaments; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:karoṅ]] [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---wish to submit.
translation: With all humility, I submit myself to the lotus feet of all of you devotees, taking the dust from your feet as my bodily ornaments. Now, my dear devotees, please hear one thing more from me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.273
description: Devotional service to Kṛṣṇa is exactly like a pleasing, jubilant forest of lotus flowers wherein there is ample honey. I request everyone to taste this honey. If all the mental speculators bring the bees of their minds into this forest of lotus flowers and jubilantly enjoy ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa day and night, their mental speculation will be completely transcendentally satisfied.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-bhakti-siddhānta-gaṇa, yāte praphulla padma-vana,
> tāra madhu kari' āsvādana
> prema-rasa-kumuda-vane, praphullita rātri-dine,
> tāte carāo mano-bhṛṅga-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:s:siddhānta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the conclusive understanding of devotional service to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---by which; [[synonyms:p:praphulla]]---enlivened; [[synonyms:p:padma]]-[[synonyms:v:vana]]---the forest of lotus flowers; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhu]]---the honey collected from those lotus flowers; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---relishing; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---of transcendental love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kumuda]]-[[synonyms:v:vane]]---in the forest of //kumuda// flowers (a type of lotus); [[synonyms:p:praphullita]]---being jubilant; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---day and night; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in that forest of lotus flowers; [[synonyms:c:carāo]]---make wander; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:b:bhṛṅga]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the bumblebees of your minds.
translation: Devotional service to Kṛṣṇa is exactly like a pleasing, jubilant forest of lotus flowers wherein there is ample honey. I request everyone to taste this honey. If all the mental speculators bring the bees of their minds into this forest of lotus flowers and jubilantly enjoy ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa day and night, their mental speculation will be completely transcendentally satisfied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.274
description: The devotees who have a relationship with Kṛṣṇa are like the swans and cakravāka birds that play in the forest of lotus flowers. The buds of those lotus flowers are the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, and they are edibles for the swanlike devotees. Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is always engaged in His transcendental pastimes; therefore the devotees, following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, can always eat those lotus buds, for they are the pastimes of the Lord.
text:
> nānā-bhāvera bhakta-jana, haṁsa-cakravāka-gaṇa,
> yāte sabe' karena vihāra
> kṛṣṇa-keli sumṛṇāla, yāhā pāi sarva-kāla,
> bhakta-haṁsa karaye āhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvera]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---devotees relishing relationships with Kṛṣṇa in different ecstasies; [[synonyms:h:haṁsa]]-[[synonyms:c:cakravāka]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---compared to swans and //cakravāka// birds; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---in that place; [[synonyms:s:sabe']]---all; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:v:vihāra]]---enjoy life; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:keli]]---the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:mṛṇāla]]---sweet buds; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:p:pāi]]---which one can get; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāla]]---eternally; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:h:haṁsa]]---the devotees, who are just like swans; [[synonyms:k:karaye]]---do; [[synonyms:ā:āhāra]]---eating.
translation: The devotees who have a relationship with Kṛṣṇa are like the swans and cakravāka birds that play in the forest of lotus flowers. The buds of those lotus flowers are the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, and they are edibles for the swanlike devotees. Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is always engaged in His transcendental pastimes; therefore the devotees, following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, can always eat those lotus buds, for they are the pastimes of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.275
description: All the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu should go to that lake and, remaining always under the shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, become swans and cakravāka birds in those celestial waters. They should go on rendering service to Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and enjoy life perpetually. In this way all miseries will be diminished, the devotees will attain great happiness, and there will be jubilant love of God.
text:
> sei sarovare giyā, haṁsa-cakravāka hañā,
> sadā tāhāṅ karaha vilāsa
> khaṇḍibe sakala duḥkha, pāibā parama sukha,
> anāyāse habe premollāsa

translation: All the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu should go to that lake and, remaining always under the shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, become swans and cakravāka birds in those celestial waters. They should go on rendering service to Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and enjoy life perpetually. In this way all miseries will be diminished, the devotees will attain great happiness, and there will be jubilant love of God.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.276
description: The devotees who have taken shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu take the responsibility for distributing nectarean devotional service all over the world. They are like clouds pouring water on the ground that nourishes the fruit of love of Godhead in this world. The devotees eat that fruit to their hearts' content, and whatever remnants they leave are eaten by the general populace. Thus they live happily.
text:
> ei amṛta anukṣaṇa, sādhu mahānta-megha-gaṇa,
> viśvodyāne kare variṣaṇa
> tāte phale amṛta-phala, bhakta khāya nirantara,
> tāra śeṣe jīye jaga-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---this nectar; [[synonyms:a:anukṣaṇa]]---continuously; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]] [[synonyms:m:mahānta]]-[[synonyms:m:megha]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---pure devotees and saintly persons, who are compared to clouds; [[synonyms:v:viśva]]-[[synonyms:u:udyāne]]---in the garden of the universe; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:v:variṣaṇa]]---rain down these nectarean pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---because of that; [[synonyms:p:phale]]---grows; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]---the fruit of nectar; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]] [[synonyms:k:khāya]] [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---and the devotees eat such fruit continuously; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---after their eating; [[synonyms:j:jīye]] [[synonyms:j:jaga]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---the living entities all over the world live peacefully.
translation: The devotees who have taken shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu take the responsibility for distributing nectarean devotional service all over the world. They are like clouds pouring water on the ground that nourishes the fruit of love of Godhead in this world. The devotees eat that fruit to their hearts' content, and whatever remnants they leave are eaten by the general populace. Thus they live happily.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.277
description: The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are full of nectar, and the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa are like camphor. When one mixes these, they taste very sweet. By the mercy of the pure devotees, whoever tastes them can understand the depths of that sweetness.
text:
> caitanya-līlā-amṛta-pūra, kṛṣṇa-līlā-sukarpūra,
> duhe mili' haya sumādhurya
> sādhu-guru-prasāde, tāhā yei āsvāde,
> sei jāne mādhurya-prācurya

translation: The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are full of nectar, and the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa are like camphor. When one mixes these, they taste very sweet. By the mercy of the pure devotees, whoever tastes them can understand the depths of that sweetness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.278
description: Men become strong and stout by eating sufficient grains, but the devotee who simply eats ordinary grains but does not taste the transcendental pastimes of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Kṛṣṇa gradually becomes weak and falls down from the transcendental position. However, if one drinks but a drop of the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes, his body and mind begin to bloom, and he begins to laugh, sing and dance.
text:
> ye līlā-amṛta vine, khāya yadi anna-pāne,
> tabe bhaktera durbala jīvana
> yāra eka-bindu-pāne, utphullita tanu-mane,
> hāse, gāya, karaye nartana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]---he who; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---of the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa and Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]] [[synonyms:v:vine]]---without nectar; [[synonyms:k:khāya]] [[synonyms:y:yadi]] [[synonyms:a:anna]]-[[synonyms:p:pāne]]---if one eats only ordinary food grains; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:b:bhaktera]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:d:durbala]] [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---life becomes weakened; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:b:bindu]]-[[synonyms:p:pāne]]---if one drinks one drop; [[synonyms:u:utphullita]] [[synonyms:t:tanu]]-[[synonyms:m:mane]]---the body and mind become jubilant; [[synonyms:h:hāse]]---laughs; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chants; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dances.
translation: Men become strong and stout by eating sufficient grains, but the devotee who simply eats ordinary grains but does not taste the transcendental pastimes of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Kṛṣṇa gradually becomes weak and falls down from the transcendental position. However, if one drinks but a drop of the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes, his body and mind begin to bloom, and he begins to laugh, sing and dance.
purport: All the devotees connected with this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement must read all the books that have been translated (//Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Bhagavad-gītā// and others); otherwise, after some time, they will simply eat, sleep and fall down from their position. Thus they will miss the opportunity to attain an eternal, blissful life of transcendental pleasure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.279
description: The readers should relish this wonderful nectar because nothing compares to it. Keeping their faith firmly fixed within their minds, they should be careful not to fall into the pit of false arguments or the whirlpools of unfortunate situations. If one falls into such positions, he is finished.
text:
> e amṛta kara pāna, yāra sama nāhi āna,
> citte kari' sudṛḍha viśvāsa
> nā paḍa' kutarka-garte, amedhya karkaśa āvarte,
> yāte paḍile haya sarva-nāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:e]] [[synonyms:a:amṛta]] [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:p:pāna]]---all of you must drink this nectar; [[synonyms:y:yāra]] [[synonyms:s:sama]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:ā:āna]]---there is no comparison to this nectar; [[synonyms:c:citte]]---within the mind; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:s:sudṛḍha]] [[synonyms:v:viśvāsa]]---having firm faith in this conclusion; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:paḍa']] [[synonyms:k:kutarka]] [[synonyms:g:garte]]---do not fall down into the pit of false arguments; [[synonyms:a:amedhya]] [[synonyms:k:karkaśa]] [[synonyms:ā:āvarte]]---in the untouchable, harsh whirlpool; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---in which; [[synonyms:p:paḍile]]---if one falls down; [[synonyms:h:haya]] [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---the purpose of life will be spoiled.
translation: The readers should relish this wonderful nectar because nothing compares to it. Keeping their faith firmly fixed within their minds, they should be careful not to fall into the pit of false arguments or the whirlpools of unfortunate situations. If one falls into such positions, he is finished.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.28
description: "The words of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu are firm and convincing, and I accept them as true. In this Age of Kali, one cannot be delivered from material clutches simply by formally accepting the renounced order.
text:
> śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-vākya dṛḍha satya māni
> kali-kāle sannyāse 'saṁsāra' nāhi jini
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:v:vākya]]---the words of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]]---very firm and convincing; [[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:m:māni]]---I admit as truth; [[synonyms:k:kali]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in this Age of Kali; [[synonyms:s:sannyāse]]---simply by accepting the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:j:jini]]---one cannot escape the material clutches.
translation: "The words of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu are firm and convincing, and I accept them as true. In this Age of Kali, one cannot be delivered from material clutches simply by formally accepting the renounced order.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.280
description: In conclusion, I submit to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Nityānanda Prabhu, Advaita Prabhu, and all the other devotees and readers that I accept your lotus feet as the helmet on my head. In this way, all my purposes will be served.
text:
> śrī-caitanya, nityānanda, advaitādi bhakta-vṛnda,
> āra yata śrotā bhakta-gaṇa
> tomā-sabāra śrī-caraṇa, kari śire vibhūṣaṇa,
> yāhā haite abhīṣṭa-pūraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]] [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---as well as the devotees like Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:y:yata]] [[synonyms:ś:śrotā]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees who listen; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of all of you; [[synonyms:k:kari]] [[synonyms:ś:śire]] [[synonyms:v:vibhūṣaṇa]]---I keep on my head as a helmet; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from which; [[synonyms:a:abhīṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:p:pūraṇa]]---all my purposes will be served.
translation: In conclusion, I submit to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Nityānanda Prabhu, Advaita Prabhu, and all the other devotees and readers that I accept your lotus feet as the helmet on my head. In this way, all my purposes will be served.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.281
description: Taking the feet of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī and Jīva Gosvāmī on my head, I always desire their mercy. Thus I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, humbly try to describe the nectar of the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, which are mixed with the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-sanātana-raghunātha-jīva-caraṇa,
> śire dhari,-yāra karoṅ āśa
> kṛṣṇa, līlāmṛtānvita, caitanya-caritāmṛta,
> kahe kichu dīna kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and of Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]-[[synonyms:j:jīva]]---of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī and Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet; [[synonyms:ś:śire]] [[synonyms:d:dhari]]---taking on my head; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:k:karoṅ]] [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---I always desire; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:anvita]]---mixed with the nectar of //kṛṣṇa-līlā//; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---is trying to speak; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:d:dīna]]---most humble; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation: Taking the feet of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī and Jīva Gosvāmī on my head, I always desire their mercy. Thus I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, humbly try to describe the nectar of the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, which are mixed with the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.282
description: For the satisfaction of Śrī Madana-gopāla and Govindadeva, we pray that this book, Caitanya-caritāmṛta, may be offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> śrīman-madana-gopāla-
> govindadeva-tuṣṭaye
> caitanyārpitam astv etac
> caitanya-caritāmṛtam
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrīman]]-[[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---of the Deity named Śrīman Madana-gopāla; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:d:deva]]---of the Deity named Govindadeva; [[synonyms:t:tuṣṭaye]]---for the satisfaction; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:a:arpitam]]---offered unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:astu]]---let it be; [[synonyms:e:etat]]---this; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛtam]]---the book known as //Caitanya-caritāmṛta.//
translation: For the satisfaction of Śrī Madana-gopāla and Govindadeva, we pray that this book, Caitanya-caritāmṛta, may be offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.283
description: The Caitanya-caritāmṛta pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu constitute a very secret literature. It is the life and soul of all devotees. Those who are not fit to relish this literature, who are envious like hogs and pigs, will certainly not adore it. However, this will not harm my attempt. These pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will certainly please all saintly people who have clear hearts. They will certainly enjoy it. We wish that this will enhance their enjoyment more and more.
text:
> tad idam ati-rahasyaṁ gaura-līlāmṛtaṁ yat
> khala-samudaya-kolair nādṛtaṁ tair alabhyam
> kṣatir iyam iha kā me svāditaṁ yat samantāt
> sahṛdaya-sumanobhir modam eṣāṁ tanoti
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that (//Caitanya-caritāmṛta//); [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this; [[synonyms:a:ati]]-[[synonyms:r:rahasyam]]---full of spiritual mysteries; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛtam]]---the nectar of the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:k:khala]]-[[synonyms:s:samudaya]]---envious rascals; [[synonyms:k:kolaiḥ]]---by pigs; [[synonyms:n:na]]---never; [[synonyms:ā:ādṛtam]]---praised; [[synonyms:t:taiḥ]]---by them; [[synonyms:a:alabhyam]]---not obtainable; [[synonyms:k:kṣatiḥ]] [[synonyms:i:iyam]] [[synonyms:i:iha]] [[synonyms:k:kā]]---what is the loss in this connection; [[synonyms:m:me]]---of me; [[synonyms:s:svāditam]]---tasted; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:s:samantāt]]---completely; [[synonyms:s:sahṛdaya]]-[[synonyms:s:sumanobhiḥ]]---by those who are friendly and whose minds are very clean; [[synonyms:m:modam]]---enjoyment; [[synonyms:e:eṣām]]---of them; [[synonyms:t:tanoti]]---expands.
translation:
The Caitanya-caritāmṛta pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu constitute a very secret literature. It is the life and soul of all devotees. Those who are not fit to relish this literature, who are envious like hogs and pigs, will certainly not adore it. However, this will not harm my attempt. These pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will certainly please all saintly people who have clear hearts. They will certainly enjoy it. We wish that this will enhance their enjoyment more and more.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Twenty-fifth Chapter, describing how the inhabitants of Vārāṇasī were converted to Vaiṣṇavism.//

Note: \\
The author of //Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta,// Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī, has condemned all his enemies by comparing them to envious hogs and pigs. This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, which is spreading throughout the world, is being appreciated by sincere people, although they have never previously heard of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Kṛṣṇa's pastimes. Now even the higher, priestly circles are appreciating this movement. They have concluded that this movement is very nice and that they have something to learn from it. Nonetheless, in India there are some people who say that they belong to this cult but who are actually very envious of the //ācārya.// They have tried to suppress our activities in many ways, but as far as we are concerned, we follow in the footsteps of Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī and take them as envious pigs and hogs. We simply wish to present the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to the best of our ability so that those who are really honest can cleanse their hearts. We hope that they enjoy this literature and bestow their blessings upon us. It appears that even such a great personality as Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī met with some envious obstacles; what, then, to speak of us, who are only insignificant creatures in this universe. We are simply trying to execute the orders of our spiritual master to the best of our ability.

END OF THE MADHYA-LĪLĀ

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.29

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.30
description: "In this Age of Kali, one cannot attain liberation without taking to the devotional service of the Lord. In this age, even if one does not chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa perfectly, he still attains liberation very easily.
text:
> bhakti vinā mukti nahe, bhāgavate kaya
> kali-kāle nāmābhāse sukhe mukti haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without devotional service; [[synonyms:m:mukti]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---there is no question of liberation; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavate]] [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---it is said in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:k:kali]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in this Age of Kali; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāse]]---even by a slight appreciation of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra//; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---without difficulty; [[synonyms:m:mukti]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---one can get liberation.
translation: "In this Age of Kali, one cannot attain liberation without taking to the devotional service of the Lord. In this age, even if one does not chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa perfectly, he still attains liberation very easily.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.31
description: " 'My dear Lord, devotional service unto You is the only auspicious path. If one gives it up simply for speculative knowledge or the understanding that these living beings are spirit soul and the material world is false, he undergoes a great deal of trouble. He only gains troublesome and inauspicious activities. His actions are like beating a husk that is already devoid of rice. One's labor becomes fruitless.'
text:
> śreyaḥ-sṛtiṁ bhaktim udasya te vibho
> kliśyanti ye kevala-bodha-labdhaye
> teṣām asau kleśala eva śiṣyate
> nānyad yathā sthūla-tuṣāvaghātinām

translation: “ 'My dear Lord, devotional service unto You is the only auspicious path. If one gives it up simply for speculative knowledge or the understanding that these living beings are spirit soul and the material world is false, he undergoes a great deal of trouble. He only gains troublesome and inauspicious activities. His actions are like beating a husk that is already devoid of rice. One's labor becomes fruitless.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.14.4).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.32
description: " 'O lotus-eyed one, those who think they are liberated in this life but who are devoid of devotional service to You are of impure intelligence. Although they accept severe austerities and penances and rise to the spiritual position, to impersonal Brahman realization, they fall down again because they neglect to worship Your lotus feet.'
text:
> ye 'nye 'ravindākṣa vimukta-māninas
> tvayy asta-bhāvād aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ
> āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ
> patanty adho 'nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ

translation: “ 'O lotus-eyed one, those who think they are liberated in this life but who are devoid of devotional service to You are of impure intelligence. Although they accept severe austerities and penances and rise to the spiritual position, to impersonal Brahman realization, they fall down again because they neglect to worship Your lotus feet.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.33
description: "The word Brahman means 'the greatest.' This means that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is full in all six opulences. However, if we take the one-sided impersonalist view, His fullness is diminished.
text:
> 'brahma'-śabde kahe 'ṣaḍ-aiśvarya-pūrṇa bhagavān'
> tāṅre 'nirviśeṣa' sthāpi, 'pūrṇatā' haya hāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //brahma//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---is meant; [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṭ]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]-[[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead, full in all six opulences; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:n:nirviśeṣa]] [[synonyms:s:sthāpi]]---if we make impersonal; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇatā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]] [[synonyms:h:hāna]]---His completeness becomes damaged.
translation: "The word Brahman means 'the greatest.' This means that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is full in all six opulences. However, if we take the one-sided impersonalist view, His fullness is diminished.
purport:
The Supreme Personality of Godhead is originally the Supreme Person. The Lord says in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:4|(Bg. 9.4)]]:

> mayā tatam idaṁ sarvaṁ
> jagad avyakta-mūrtinā
> mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni
> na cāhaṁ teṣv avasthitaḥ

"By Me, in My unmanifested form, this entire universe is pervaded. All beings are in Me, but I am not in them."

The potency of Kṛṣṇa that is spread everywhere is impersonal. The sunlight is the impersonal expansion of the sun globe and the sun-god. If we simply take one side of the Supreme Personality of Godhead-His impersonal effulgence---that one side does not fully explain the Absolute Truth. Impersonal appreciation of the Absolute Truth is one-sided and incomplete. One should also accept the other side, the personal side-Bhagavān. //Brahmeti paramātmeti bhagavān iti śabdyate.// One should not be satisfied simply by understanding the Brahman feature of the Personality of Godhead. One must also know the Lord's personal feature. That is complete understanding of the Absolute Truth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.34
description: "Vedic literatures, the Upaniṣads, the Brahma-sūtra and the Purāṇas all describe the activities of the spiritual potency of the Lord. If one cannot accept the personal activities of the Lord, he jokes foolishly and gives an impersonal description.
text:
> śruti-purāṇa kahe-kṛṣṇera cic-chakti-vilāsa
> tāhā nāhi māni, paṇḍita kare upahāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śruti]]-[[synonyms:p:purāṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Vedic literatures and the //Purāṇas// confirm; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---activities of spiritual potencies; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:m:māni]]---not accepting that; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]] [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:u:upahāsa]]---so-called scholars play jokes without perfect understanding.
translation: "Vedic literatures, the Upaniṣads, the Brahma-sūtra and the Purāṇas all describe the activities of the spiritual potency of the Lord. If one cannot accept the personal activities of the Lord, he jokes foolishly and gives an impersonal description.
purport: In the Vedic literatures, including the //Purāṇas,// there are full descriptions of the spiritual potency of Kṛṣṇa. All the pastimes of the Lord are eternal, blissful and full of knowledge, just as the form of Kṛṣṇa Himself is eternal, blissful and full of knowledge (//sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha).// Unintelligent people with a poor fund of knowledge compare their temporary bodies to the spiritual body of Kṛṣṇa, and by such foolishness they try to understand Kṛṣṇa as one of them. //Avajānanti māṁ mūḍhā mānuṣīṁ tanum āśritam. Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:11|(Bg. 9.11)]] points out that foolish people think of Kṛṣṇa as one of them. Not understanding His spiritual potency, they simply decry the personal form of the Absolute Truth, foolishly thinking of themselves as //jñānīs// cognizant of the complete truth. They cannot understand that just as the material energy of the Lord has a variety of activities, the spiritual energy has variety also. They consider activities in devotional service the same as activities in material consciousness. Under such a wrong impression, they sometimes dare joke about the spiritual activities of the Lord and His devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.35
description: "The Māyāvādīs do not recognize the personal form of the Lord as spiritual and full of bliss. This is a great sin. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's statements are actually factual.
text:
> cid-ānanda kṛṣṇa-vigraha 'māyika' kari' māni
> ei baḍa 'pāpa',-satya caitanyera vāṇī
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:vigraha]]---the transcendental form of Kṛṣṇa, which is completely spiritual; [[synonyms:m:māyika]] [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:m:māni]]---accept as made of the external energy, //māyā//; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]---this is a great act of sin; [[synonyms:s:satya]]---true; [[synonyms:c:caitanyera]] [[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---the words of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: "The Māyāvādīs do not recognize the personal form of the Lord as spiritual and full of bliss. This is a great sin. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's statements are actually factual.
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's movement especially aims at defeating the Māyāvāda conclusion about the Absolute Truth. Since the members of the Māyāvāda school cannot understand the spiritual form of the Lord, they incorrectly think the Lord's form is also made of material energy. They think that He is covered by a material body just like other living beings. Due to this offensive understanding, they cannot recognize that Śrī Kṛṣṇa's personal form is transcendental, not material. Their conclusion is a great offense at the lotus feet of the Lord. As explained by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Śrī Kṛṣṇa has His eternal, blissful form that is full of knowledge, and all Vaiṣṇava //ācāryas// accept this. That is the proper understanding of the Absolute Truth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.36
description: " 'O supreme one, the transcendental form I am now seeing is full of transcendental bliss. It is not contaminated by the external energy. It is full of effulgence. My Lord, there is no better understanding of You than this. You are the Supreme Soul and the creator of this material world, but You are not connected with this material world. You are completely different from created form and variety. I sincerely take shelter of that form of Yours which I am now seeing. This form is the original source of all living beings and their senses.'
text:
> nātaḥ paraṁ parama yad bhavataḥ svarūpam
> ānanda-mātram avikalpam aviddha-varcaḥ
> paśyāmi viśva-sṛjam ekam aviśvam ātman
> bhūtendriyātmakam adas ta upāśrito 'smi
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:ataḥ]]---than this; [[synonyms:p:param]]---more supreme; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---O supreme one; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:b:bhavataḥ]]---of Your Lordship; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpam]]---the personal form; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---of transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:m:mātram]]---only; [[synonyms:a:avikalpam]]---where there is no creation; [[synonyms:a:aviddha]]---without contamination; [[synonyms:v:varcaḥ]]---having an effulgence; [[synonyms:p:paśyāmi]]---I see; [[synonyms:v:viśva]]-[[synonyms:s:sṛjam]] [[synonyms:e:ekam]]---who alone has created this universe; [[synonyms:a:aviśvam]]---not belonging to the destructible material world; [[synonyms:ā:ātman]]---O Supreme Soul; [[synonyms:b:bhūta]]-[[synonyms:i:indriya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmakam]]---the original cause of the senses and the living beings; [[synonyms:a:adaḥ]]---transcendental; [[synonyms:t:te]]---unto You; [[synonyms:u:upāśritaḥ]] [[synonyms:a:asmi]]---I take full shelter.
translation: “ 'O supreme one, the transcendental form I am now seeing is full of transcendental bliss. It is not contaminated by the external energy. It is full of effulgence. My Lord, there is no better understanding of You than this. You are the Supreme Soul and the creator of this material world, but You are not connected with this material world. You are completely different from created form and variety. I sincerely take shelter of that form of Yours which I am now seeing. This form is the original source of all living beings and their senses.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:9:3|(3.9.3)]]. This verse was spoken by Lord Brahmā, who perfectly realized the Supreme Personality of Godhead after meditating upon the Lord within the water of the Garbhodhaka Ocean. Brahmā realized that the form of the Lord is completely spiritual. This is certainly a better understanding of the Absolute Truth than impersonal understanding.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.37
description: " 'Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is the cause of all causes. He is past, present and future, and He is the movable and immovable. He is the greatest and the smallest, and He is visible and directly experienced. He is celebrated in Vedic literature. Everything is Kṛṣṇa, and without Him there is no existence. He is the root of all understanding, and He is that which is understood by all words.'
text:
> dṛṣṭaṁ śrutaṁ bhūta-bhavad-bhaviṣyat
> sthāsnuś cariṣṇur mahad alpakaṁ vā
> vinācyutād vastu-tarāṁ na vācyaṁ
> sa eva sarvaṁ paramātma-bhūtaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dṛṣṭam]]---experienced by direct perception; [[synonyms:ś:śrutam]]---experienced by hearing; [[synonyms:b:bhūta]]---past; [[synonyms:b:bhavat]]---present; [[synonyms:b:bhaviṣyat]]---which will be in the future; [[synonyms:s:sthāsnuḥ]]---immovable; [[synonyms:c:cariṣṇuḥ]]---movable; [[synonyms:m:mahat]]---the greatest; [[synonyms:a:alpakam]]---the smallest; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---except; [[synonyms:a:acyutāt]]---the infallible Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:v:vastu]]-[[synonyms:t:tarām]]---anything else; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:v:vācyam]]---not to be spoken; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:sarvam]]---everything; [[synonyms:p:paramātma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūtaḥ]]---the origin of all causes.
translation: “ 'Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is the cause of all causes. He is past, present and future, and He is the movable and immovable. He is the greatest and the smallest, and He is visible and directly experienced. He is celebrated in Vedic literature. Everything is Kṛṣṇa, and without Him there is no existence. He is the root of all understanding, and He is that which is understood by all words.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.46.43) was spoken by Uddhava when he came to pacify all the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana during Kṛṣṇa's absence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.38
description: " 'O most auspicious one! For our benefit You are worshiped by us. You manifest Your transcendental form, which You show to us in our meditation. We offer our respectful obeisances unto You, the Supreme Person, and we worship You whom impersonalists do not accept due to their poor fund of knowledge. Thus they are liable to descend into a hellish condition.'
text:
> tad vā idaṁ bhuvana-maṅgala maṅgalāya
> dhyāne sma no daraśitaṁ ta upāsakānām
> tasmai namo bhagavate 'nuvidhema tubhyaṁ
> yo 'nādṛto naraka-bhāgbhir asat-prasaṅgaiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this; [[synonyms:b:bhuvana]]-[[synonyms:m:maṅgala]]---O most auspicious of the entire world; [[synonyms:m:maṅgalāya]]---for the benefit; [[synonyms:d:dhyāne]]---in meditation; [[synonyms:s:sma]]---certainly; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---of us; [[synonyms:d:daraśitam]]---manifested; [[synonyms:t:te]]---by You; [[synonyms:u:upāsakānām]]---of devotees engaged in devotional service; [[synonyms:t:tasmai]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---all obeisances; [[synonyms:b:bhagavate]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:anuvidhema]]---we offer obeisances, following in the footsteps of the //ācāryas//; [[synonyms:t:tubhyam]]---unto You; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who is; [[synonyms:a:anādṛtaḥ]]---not much appreciated; [[synonyms:n:naraka]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgbhiḥ]]---by persons who are destined to go to a hellish condition of life; [[synonyms:a:asat]]-[[synonyms:p:prasaṅgaiḥ]]---who discuss the Supreme Personality of Godhead illogically.
translation: “ 'O most auspicious one! For our benefit You are worshiped by us. You manifest Your transcendental form, which You show to us in our meditation. We offer our respectful obeisances unto You, the Supreme Person, and we worship You whom impersonalists do not accept due to their poor fund of knowledge. Thus they are liable to descend into a hellish condition.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:9:4|(3.9.4)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.39
description: " 'Fools disrespect Me because I appear like a human being. They do not know My supreme position as the cause of all causes, the creator of the material energy.'
text:
> avajānanti māṁ mūḍhā
> mānuṣīṁ tanum āśritam
> paraṁ bhāvam ajānanto
> mama bhūta-maheśvaram
