translation: “ 'Fools disrespect Me because I appear like a human being. They do not know My supreme position as the cause of all causes, the creator of the material energy.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:11|(Bg. 9.11)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.4
description: For as long as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was in Vārāṇasī, Paramānanda Kīrtanīyā, who was a friend of Candraśekhara's, chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra and other songs to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in a very humorous way.
text:
> 'paramānanda kīrtanīyā'-śekharera saṅgī
> prabhure kīrtana śunāya, ati baḍa raṅgī
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paramānanda]] [[synonyms:k:kīrtanīyā]]---Paramānanda Kīrtanīyā; [[synonyms:ś:śekharera]] [[synonyms:s:saṅgī]]---a friend of Candraśekhara's; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]] [[synonyms:ś:śunāya]]---sings and chants; [[synonyms:a:ati]] [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:r:raṅgī]]---very humorous.
translation: For as long as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was in Vārāṇasī, Paramānanda Kīrtanīyā, who was a friend of Candraśekhara's, chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra and other songs to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in a very humorous way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.40
description: " 'Those who are envious of My form, who are cruel and mischievous and lowest among men, are perpetually cast by Me into hellish existence in various demoniac species of life.'
text:
> tān ahaṁ dviṣataḥ krūrān
> saṁsāreṣu narādhamān
> kṣipāmy ajasram aśubhān
> āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tān]]---all of them; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:d:dviṣataḥ]]---those who are envious; [[synonyms:k:krūrān]]---always willing to do harm; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāreṣu]]---in this material world; [[synonyms:n:nara]]-[[synonyms:a:adhamān]]---the lowest of men; [[synonyms:k:kṣipāmi]]---throw; [[synonyms:a:ajasram]]---again and again; [[synonyms:a:aśubhān]]---engaged in inauspicious acts; [[synonyms:ā:āsurīṣu]]---demoniac; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:y:yoniṣu]]---in families.
translation: “ 'Those who are envious of My form, who are cruel and mischievous and lowest among men, are perpetually cast by Me into hellish existence in various demoniac species of life.'
purport: This is also a quotation from //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:16:19|(Bg. 16.19)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.41
description: "Not accepting the transformation of energy, Śrīpād Śaṅkarācārya has tried to establish the theory of illusion under the plea that Vyāsadeva has made a mistake.
text:
> sūtrera pariṇāma-vāda, tāhā nā māniyā
> 'vivarta-vāda' sthāpe, 'vyāsa bhrānta' baliyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sūtrera]]---of the codes of the //Vedānta-sūtra//; [[synonyms:p:pariṇāma]]-[[synonyms:v:vāda]]---the transformation of energy; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:m:māniyā]]---not accepting this fact; [[synonyms:v:vivarta]]-[[synonyms:v:vāda]]---the theory of illusion; [[synonyms:s:sthāpe]]---establishes; [[synonyms:v:vyāsa]] [[synonyms:b:bhrānta]] [[synonyms:b:baliyā]]---accusing Vyāsadeva to be mistaken.
translation: "Not accepting the transformation of energy, Śrīpād Śaṅkarācārya has tried to establish the theory of illusion under the plea that Vyāsadeva has made a mistake.
purport: For a further explanation of this verse, one may refer to Chapter Seven (verses 121-126).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.42
description: "Śrīpād Śaṅkarācārya has given his interpretation and imaginary meaning. It does not actually appeal to the mind of any sane man. He has done this to convince the atheists and bring them under his control.
text:
> ei ta' kalpita artha mane nāhi bhāya
> śāstra chāḍi' kukalpanā pāṣaṇḍe bujhāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---this; [[synonyms:k:kalpita]]---imaginary; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---to the mind; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---does not; [[synonyms:b:bhāya]]---appeal; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---the authoritative scriptures; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:k:ku]]-[[synonyms:k:kalpanā]]---mischievous imagination; [[synonyms:p:pāṣaṇḍe]]---to the atheistic class of men; [[synonyms:b:bujhāya]]---teaches.
translation: "Śrīpād Śaṅkarācārya has given his interpretation and imaginary meaning. It does not actually appeal to the mind of any sane man. He has done this to convince the atheists and bring them under his control.
purport: Śrīpād Śaṅkarācārya's propaganda opposed the atheistic philosophy of Buddha. Lord Buddha's intention was to stop atheists from committing the sin of killing animals. Atheists cannot understand God; therefore Lord Buddha appeared and spread the philosophy of nonviolence to keep the atheists from killing animals. Unless one is free from the sin of animal killing, he cannot understand religion or God. Although Lord Buddha was an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa, he did not speak about God, for the people were unable to understand. He simply wanted to stop animal killing. Śrīpād Śaṅkarācārya wanted to establish the predominance of one's spiritual identity; therefore he wanted to convert the atheists through an imaginary interpretation of Vedic literatures. These are the secrets of the //ācāryas.// Sometimes they conceal the real purpose of the //Vedas// and explain the //Vedas// in a different way. Sometimes they enunciate a different theory just to bring the atheists under their control. Thus it is said that Śaṅkara's philosophy is for //pāṣaṇḍas,// atheists.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.43
description: "The atheists, headed by the Māyāvādī philosophers, do not care for liberation or Kṛṣṇa's mercy. They simply continue to put forward false arguments and counter—theories to atheistic philosophy, not considering or engaging in spiritual matters.
text:
> paramārtha-vicāra gela, kari mātra 'vāda'
> kāhāṅ mukti pāba, kāhāṅ kṛṣṇera prasāda
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---discussion on spiritual matters; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---has gone; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---we do; [[synonyms:m:mātra]] [[synonyms:v:vāda]]---only argument and word jugglery; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:p:pāba]]---we shall get; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "The atheists, headed by the Māyāvādī philosophers, do not care for liberation or Kṛṣṇa's mercy. They simply continue to put forward false arguments and counter---theories to atheistic philosophy, not considering or engaging in spiritual matters.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.44
description: "The conclusion is that the import of the Vedānta-sūtra is covered by the imaginary explanation of Śaṅkarācārya. Whatever Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu has said is perfectly true.
text:
> vyāsa-sūtrera artha ācārya kariyāche ācchādana
> ei haya satya śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]-[[synonyms:s:sūtrera]]---of the codes of the Vedānta known as //Vyāsa-sūtra//; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meanings; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Śaṅkarācārya; [[synonyms:k:kariyāche]] [[synonyms:ā:ācchādana]]---has purposely covered; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:s:satya]]---the truth; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:v:vacana]]---the words and explanation given by Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: "The conclusion is that the import of the Vedānta-sūtra is covered by the imaginary explanation of Śaṅkarācārya. Whatever Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu has said is perfectly true.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.45
description: "Whatever meaning Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu gives is perfect. Any other interpretation is only a distortion."
text:
> caitanya-gosāñi yei kahe, sei mata sāra
> āra yata mata, sei saba chārakhāra"
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---whatever He has said; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:m:mata]] [[synonyms:s:sāra]]---that explanation is actually the essence of Vedic knowledge; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:y:yata]] [[synonyms:m:mata]]---any other opinion not in collaboration with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's statement; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---these; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:c:chārakhāra]]---all distortions.
translation: "Whatever meaning Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu gives is perfect. Any other interpretation is only a distortion."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.46
description: After saying this, the disciple of Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Hearing this, Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī made the following statement.
text:
> eta kahi' sei kare kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtana
> śuni' prakāśānanda kichu kahena vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---speaking so much; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---the disciple of Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performed; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---the chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prakāśānanda]]---the //guru,// Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---says; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---words.
translation: After saying this, the disciple of Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Hearing this, Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī made the following statement.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.47
description: Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī said, "Śaṅkarācārya was very eager to establish the philosophy of monism. Therefore he explained Vedānta-sūtra, or Vedānta philosophy, in a different way to support monistic philosophy.
text:
> ācāryera āgraha-'advaita-vāda' sthāpite
> tāte sūtrārtha vyākhyā kare anya rīte
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]]---of Śaṅkarācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āgraha]]---the eagerness; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:v:vāda]]---monism; [[synonyms:s:sthāpite]]---to establish; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---for that reason; [[synonyms:s:sūtra]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meaning of the //Brahma-sūtra,// or Vedānta philosophy; [[synonyms:v:vyākhyā]]---explanation; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:a:anya]] [[synonyms:r:rīte]]---in a different way.
translation: Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī said, "Śaṅkarācārya was very eager to establish the philosophy of monism. Therefore he explained Vedānta-sūtra, or Vedānta philosophy, in a different way to support monistic philosophy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.48
description: "If one accepts the Personality of Godhead, the philosophy that maintains that God and the living entity are one cannot be established. Therefore Śaṅkarācārya argued against and refuted all kinds of revealed scriptures.
text:
> 'bhagavattā' mānile 'advaita' nā yāya sthāpana
> ataeva saba śāstra karaye khaṇḍana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhagavattā]]---the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:m:mānile]]---if one accepts; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---monism or nondualism; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---is possible; [[synonyms:s:sthāpana]]---establishing; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:k:karaye]]---does; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍana]]---refutation.
translation: "If one accepts the Personality of Godhead, the philosophy that maintains that God and the living entity are one cannot be established. Therefore Śaṅkarācārya argued against and refuted all kinds of revealed scriptures.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.49
description: "Anyone who wants to establish his own opinion or philosophy certainly cannot explain any scripture according to the principle of direct interpretation.
text:
> yei grantha-kartā cāhe sva-mata sthāpite
> śāstrera sahaja artha nahe tāṅhā haite
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yei]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:g:grantha]]-[[synonyms:k:kartā]]---author; [[synonyms:c:cāhe]]---wants; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]] [[synonyms:s:sthāpite]]---to establish his own opinion; [[synonyms:ś:śāstrera]]---of the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:s:sahaja]]---the direct; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---is not; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from such an author.
translation: "Anyone who wants to establish his own opinion or philosophy certainly cannot explain any scripture according to the principle of direct interpretation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.5
description: When the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs at Vārāṇasī criticized Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord's devotees became very depressed. To satisfy them, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu showed His mercy to the sannyāsīs.
text:
> sannyāsīra gaṇa prabhure yadi upekṣila
> bhakta-duḥkha khaṇḍāite tāre kṛpā kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---when; [[synonyms:u:upekṣila]]---criticized; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---the unhappiness of the devotees; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍāite]]---to drive away; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---to them; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---showed His mercy.
translation: When the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs at Vārāṇasī criticized Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord's devotees became very depressed. To satisfy them, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu showed His mercy to the sannyāsīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.50
description: "The Mīmāṁsaka philosophers conclude that if there is a God, He is subjected to our fruitive activities. Similarly, the Sāṅkhya philosophers who analyze the cosmic manifestation say that the cause of the cosmos is material nature.
text:
> 'mīmāṁsaka' kahe,-'īśvara haya karmera aṅga'
> 'sāṅkhya' kahe,-jagatera prakṛti kāraṇa-prasaṅga'
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mīmāṁsaka]]---the Mīmāṁsaka philosophers; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---say; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:k:karmera]] [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---subject to fruitive activities; [[synonyms:s:sāṅkhya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the atheistic Sāṅkhya philosophers say; [[synonyms:j:jagatera]]---of the cosmic manifestation; [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]]---nature; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause; [[synonyms:p:prasaṅga]]---thesis.
translation: "The Mīmāṁsaka philosophers conclude that if there is a God, He is subjected to our fruitive activities. Similarly, the Sāṅkhya philosophers who analyze the cosmic manifestation say that the cause of the cosmos is material nature.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.51
description: "The followers of nyāya, the philosophy of logic, maintain that the atom is the cause of the cosmic manifestation, and the Māyāvādī philosophers maintain that the impersonal Brahman effulgence is the cause of the cosmic manifestation.
text:
> 'nyāya' kahe,-'paramāṇu haite viśva haya'
> 'māyāvādī' nirviśeṣa-brahme 'hetu' kaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nyāya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the philosophers following logic say; [[synonyms:p:paramāṇu]]---the atom; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:v:viśva]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---the cosmic manifestation has come; [[synonyms:m:māyāvādī]]---the Māyāvādī philosophers, impersonalists; [[synonyms:n:nirviśeṣa]]-[[synonyms:b:brahme]]---in the impersonal Brahman effulgence; [[synonyms:h:hetu]]---the cause; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---say.
translation: "The followers of nyāya, the philosophy of logic, maintain that the atom is the cause of the cosmic manifestation, and the Māyāvādī philosophers maintain that the impersonal Brahman effulgence is the cause of the cosmic manifestation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.52
description: "The Pātañjala philosophers say that when one is self-realized, he understands the Lord. Similarly, according to the Vedas and Vedic principles, the original cause is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> 'pātañjala' kahe,-'īśvara haya svarūpa-jñāna'
> veda-mate kahe tāṅre 'svayaṁ-bhagavān'
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pātañjala]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Pātañjala philosophers say; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---the Supreme Lord is; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---self-realization; [[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---in the Vedic version; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---they say; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to Him; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]-[[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: "The Pātañjala philosophers say that when one is self-realized, he understands the Lord. Similarly, according to the Vedas and Vedic principles, the original cause is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.53
description: "After studying the six philosophical theses, Vyāsadeva completely summarized them all in the codes of Vedānta philosophy.
text:
> chayera chaya mata vyāsa kailā āvartana
> sei saba sūtra lañā 'vedānta'-varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:chayera]]---of the six philosophers; [[synonyms:c:chaya]] [[synonyms:m:mata]]---six different theses; [[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]---Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:ā:āvartana]]---analyzed fully; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:s:sūtra]]---the codes; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:v:vedānta]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---explaining the Vedānta philosophy.
translation: "After studying the six philosophical theses, Vyāsadeva completely summarized them all in the codes of Vedānta philosophy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.54
description: "According to Vedānta philosophy, the Absolute Truth is a person. When the word nirguṇa [without qualities] is used, it is to be understood that the Lord has attributes that are totally spiritual.
text:
> 'vedānta'-mate,-brahma 'sākāra' nirūpaṇa
> 'nirguṇa' vyatireke tiṅho haya ta' 'saguṇa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vedānta]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---according to Vedānta philosophy; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]] [[synonyms:n:nirūpaṇa]]---established as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, a person; [[synonyms:n:nirguṇa]]---without material qualifications; [[synonyms:v:vyatireke]]---by indirect explanations; [[synonyms:t:tiṅho]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---fully qualified with spiritual attributes.
translation: "According to Vedānta philosophy, the Absolute Truth is a person. When the word nirguṇa [without qualities] is used, it is to be understood that the Lord has attributes that are totally spiritual.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.55
description: "Of the philosophers mentioned, none really cares for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the cause of all causes. They are always busy refuting the philosophical theories of others and establishing their own.
text:
> parama kāraṇa īśvara keha nāhi māne
> sva-sva-mata sthāpe para-matera khaṇḍane
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the supreme cause, the cause of all causes; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:m:māne]]---none of the above-mentioned philosophers accept; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---their own personal opinions; [[synonyms:s:sthāpe]]---they establish; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:m:matera]] [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍane]]---busy in refuting the opinions of others.
translation: "Of the philosophers mentioned, none really cares for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the cause of all causes. They are always busy refuting the philosophical theories of others and establishing their own.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.56
description: "By studying the six philosophical theories, one cannot reach the Absolute Truth. It is therefore our duty to follow the path of the mahājanas, the authorities. Whatever they say should be accepted as the supreme truth.
text:
> tāte chaya darśana haite 'tattva' nāhi jāni
> 'mahājana' yei kahe, sei 'satya' māni
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:c:chaya]] [[synonyms:d:darśana]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the six philosophical principles; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:t:tva]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---we cannot understand the actual truth; [[synonyms:m:mahājana]]---the great authorities; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---whatever they say; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:m:māni]]---we can accept as truth.
translation: "By studying the six philosophical theories, one cannot reach the Absolute Truth. It is therefore our duty to follow the path of the mahājanas, the authorities. Whatever they say should be accepted as the supreme truth.
purport:
In his //Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya,// Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura gives the following summary of the six philosophical processes. Prakāśānanda admitted that Śrīpād Śaṅkarācārya, being very eager to establish his philosophy of monism, took shelter of the Vedānta philosophy and tried to explain it in his own way. The fact is, however, that if one accepts the existence of God, he certainly cannot establish the theory of monism. For this reason Śaṅkarācārya refuted all kinds of Vedic literature that establishes the supremacy of the Personality of Godhead. In various ways, Śaṅkarācārya has tried to refute Vedic literature. Throughout the world, ninety-nine percent of the philosophers following in the footsteps of Śaṅkarācārya refuse to accept the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Instead they try to establish their own opinions. It is typical of mundane philosophers to want to establish their own opinions and refute those of others. Therefore: (1) The Mīmāṁsaka philosophers, following the principles of Jaimini, stress fruitive activity and say that if there is a God, He must be under the laws of fruitive activity. In other words, if one performs his duties very nicely in the material world, God is obliged to give one the desired result. According to these philosophers, there is no need to become a devotee of God. If one strictly follows moral principles, one will be recognized by the Lord, who will give the desired reward. Such philosophers do not accept the Vedic principle of //bhakti-yoga.// Instead, they give stress to following one's prescribed duty. (2) Atheistic Sāṅkhya philosophers like Kapila analyze the material elements very scrutinizingly and thereby come to the conclusion that material nature is the cause of everything. They do not accept the Supreme Personality of Godhead as the cause of all causes. (3) Nyāya philosophers like Gautama and Kaṇāda have accepted a combination of atoms as the original cause of the creation. (4) Māyāvādī philosophers say that everything is an illusion. Headed by philosophers like Aṣṭāvakra, they stress the impersonal Brahman effulgence as the cause of everything. (5) Philosophers following the precepts of Patañjali practice //rāja-yoga.// They imagine a form of the Absolute Truth within many forms. That is their process of self-realization.

All five of these philosophies completely reject the predominance of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and strive to establish their own philosophical theories. However, Śrīla Vyāsadeva wrote the //Vedānta-sūtra// and, taking the essence of all Vedic literature, established the supremacy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. All five of the philosophers mentioned above understand that impersonal Brahman is without material qualities, and they believe that when the Personality of Godhead appears, He is contaminated and covered by the material qualities. The technical term used is //saguṇa.// They say, //"saguṇa// Brahman" and //"nirguṇa// Brahman." //Nirguṇa// Brahman means impersonal, and //saguṇa// Brahman means "accepting material contamination." More or less, this kind of philosophical speculation is called Māyāvāda philosophy. The fact is, however, that the Absolute Truth has nothing to do with material qualities because He is transcendental. He is always complete with full spiritual qualities. The five philosophers mentioned above do not accept Lord Viṣṇu as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but they are very busy refuting the philosophy of other schools. There are six kinds of philosophical processes in India. Because Vyāsadeva is the Vedic authority, he is known as Vedavyāsa. His philosophical explanation of the //Vedānta-sūtra// is accepted by the devotees. As Kṛṣṇa confirms in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:15:15|(Bg. 15.15)]]:

> sarvasya cāhaṁ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo
> mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṁ ca
> vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyo
> vedānta-kṛd veda-vid eva cāham

"I am seated in everyone's heart, and from Me come remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness. By all the //Vedas,// I am to be known; indeed, I am the compiler of Vedānta, and I am the knower of the //Vedas."//

The ultimate goal of studying all Vedic literature is the acceptance of Kṛṣṇa as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is propagating the philosophical conclusion of Śrīla Vyāsadeva and following other great //ācāryas// like Rāmānujācārya, Madhvācārya, Viṣṇusvāmī, Nimbārka and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.57
description: " 'Dry arguments are inconclusive. A great personality whose opinion does not differ from others is not considered a great sage. Simply by studying the Vedas, which are variegated, one cannot come to the right path by which religious principles are understood. The solid truth of religious principles is hidden in the heart of an unadulterated self-realized person. Consequently, as the śāstras confirm, one should accept whatever progressive path the mahājanas advocate.'
text:
> tarko 'pratiṣṭhaḥ śrutayo vibhinnā
> nāsāv ṛṣir yasya mataṁ na bhinnam
> dharmasya tattvaṁ nihitaṁ guhāyāṁ
> mahājano yena gataḥ sa panthāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tarkaḥ]]---dry argument; [[synonyms:a:apratiṣṭhaḥ]]---not fixed; [[synonyms:ś:śrutayaḥ]]---//Vedas//; [[synonyms:v:vibhinnāḥ]]---possessing different departments; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---that; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣiḥ]]---great sage; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---whose; [[synonyms:m:matam]]---opinion; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:b:bhinnam]]---separate; [[synonyms:d:dharmasya]]---of religious principles; [[synonyms:t:tattvam]]---truth; [[synonyms:n:nihitam]]---placed; [[synonyms:g:guhāyām]]---in the heart of a realized person; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:j:janaḥ]]---self-realized predecessors; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---by which way; [[synonyms:g:gataḥ]]---//acted//; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:p:panthāḥ]]---the pure, unadulterated path.
translation: “ 'Dry arguments are inconclusive. A great personality whose opinion does not differ from others is not considered a great sage. Simply by studying the Vedas, which are variegated, one cannot come to the right path by which religious principles are understood. The solid truth of religious principles is hidden in the heart of an unadulterated self-realized person. Consequently, as the śāstras confirm, one should accept whatever progressive path the mahājanas advocate.'
purport: This is a verse spoken by Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja in the //Mahābhārata, Vana-parva// (313.117).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.58
description: "The words of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are a shower of nectar. Whatever He concludes to be the ultimate truth is indeed the summum bonum of all spiritual knowledge."
text:
> śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-vāṇī-amṛtera dhāra
> tiṅho ye kahaye vastu, sei 'tattva'-sāra"
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---the message of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:amṛtera]] [[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---a continuous shower of nectar; [[synonyms:t:tiṅho]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:k:kahaye]] [[synonyms:v:vastu]]---whatever He says to be the ultimate truth, the //summum bonum//; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:t:tattva]] [[synonyms:s:sāra]]---that is the essence of all spiritual knowledge.
translation: "The words of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are a shower of nectar. Whatever He concludes to be the ultimate truth is indeed the summum bonum of all spiritual knowledge."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.59
description: After hearing all these statements, the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa very jubilantly went to inform Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> e saba vṛttānta śuni' mahārāṣṭrīya brāhmaṇa
> prabhure kahite sukhe karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:e]] [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:v:vṛttānta]]---all these descriptions; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:m:mahārāṣṭrīya]] [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---the Mahārāṣṭrian //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to inform; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---very happily; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---went.
translation: After hearing all these statements, the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa very jubilantly went to inform Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.6
description: In the Seventh Chapter of Ādi-līlā I have already elaborately described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's deliverance of the sannyāsīs at Vārāṇasī, but I shall briefly repeat it in this chapter.
text:
> sannyāsīre kṛpā pūrve likhiyāchoṅ vistāriyā
> uddeśe kahiye ihāṅ saṅkṣepa kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīre]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy upon the //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---before this; [[synonyms:l:likhiyāchoṅ]]---I have described; [[synonyms:v:vistāriyā]]---elaborately; [[synonyms:u:uddeśe]]---in reference to that; [[synonyms:k:kahiye]]---let me speak; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:s:saṅkṣepa]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---in brief.
translation: In the Seventh Chapter of Ādi-līlā I have already elaborately described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's deliverance of the sannyāsīs at Vārāṇasī, but I shall briefly repeat it in this chapter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.60
description: When the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa went to see Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord was going to the temple of Bindu Mādhava after bathing in the waters of Pañca-nada.
text:
> hena-kāle mahāprabhu pañca-nade snāna kari'
> dekhite caliyāchena 'bindu-mādhava hari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:n:nade]] [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking His bath in the Ganges, called the Pañca-nada; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]] [[synonyms:c:caliyāchena]]---was going to see; [[synonyms:b:bindu]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhava]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---the Deity known as Lord Bindu Mādhava.
translation: When the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa went to see Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord was going to the temple of Bindu Mādhava after bathing in the waters of Pañca-nada.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.61
description: While the Lord was on His way, the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa informed Him about the incident that took place in the camp of Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī. Hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu smiled happily.
text:
> pathe sei vipra saba vṛttānta kahila
> śuni' mahāprabhu sukhe īṣat hāsila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:v:vṛttānta]] [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---explained the whole incident; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in happiness; [[synonyms:ī:īṣat]]---mildly; [[synonyms:h:hāsila]]---smiled.
translation: While the Lord was on His way, the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa informed Him about the incident that took place in the camp of Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī. Hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu smiled happily.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.62
description: Upon reaching the temple of Bindu Mādhava, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, seeing the beauty of Lord Bindu Mādhava, became overwhelmed in ecstatic love. He then began to dance in the courtyard of the temple.
text:
> mādhava-saundarya dekhi' āviṣṭa ha-ilā
> aṅganete āsi' preme nācite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]-[[synonyms:s:saundarya]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after seeing the beauty of Lord Bindu Mādhava; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became ecstatic in love; [[synonyms:a:aṅganete]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming to the courtyard; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in great love; [[synonyms:n:nācite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to dance.
translation: Upon reaching the temple of Bindu Mādhava, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, seeing the beauty of Lord Bindu Mādhava, became overwhelmed in ecstatic love. He then began to dance in the courtyard of the temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.63
description: There were four people accompanying Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and these were Candraśekhara, Paramānanda Purī, Tapana Miśra and Sanātana Gosvāmī. They were all chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra in the following way.
text:
> śekhara, paramānanda, tapana, sanātana
> cāri-jana mili' kare nāma-saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śekhara]]---Candraśekhara; [[synonyms:p:paramānanda]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:t:tapana]]---Tapana Miśra; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]] [[synonyms:m:mili']]---all four of them; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra.//
translation: There were four people accompanying Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and these were Candraśekhara, Paramānanda Purī, Tapana Miśra and Sanātana Gosvāmī. They were all chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra in the following way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.64
description: They chanted, "Haraye namaḥ kṛṣṇa yādavāya namaḥ gopāla govinda rāma śrī-madhusūdana."
text:
> "haraye namaḥ kṛṣṇa yādavāya namaḥ
> gopāla govinda rāma śrī-madhusūdana"
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haraye]]---unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yādavāya]]---to the descendant of the Yadu family; [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Gopāla; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]---Rāma; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:m:madhusūdana]]---Śrī Madhusūdana.
translation: They chanted, "Haraye namaḥ kṛṣṇa yādavāya namaḥ gopāla govinda rāma śrī-madhusūdana."
purport: This is another way of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// The meaning is: "I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa. He is the descendant of the Yadu family. Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto Gopāla, Govinda, Rāma and Śrī Madhusūdana."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.65
description: In all directions, hundreds and thousands of people began to chant "Hari! Hari!" Thus there arose a tumultuous and auspicious sound filling the entire universe.
text:
> caudikete lakṣa loka bale 'hari' 'hari'
> uṭhila maṅgala-dhvani svarga-martya bhari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cau]]-[[synonyms:d:dikete]]---all around; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---hundreds of thousands; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---chant; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---O Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari; [[synonyms:u:uṭhila]]---there arose; [[synonyms:m:maṅgala]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---an auspicious sound; [[synonyms:s:svarga]]-[[synonyms:m:martya]] [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---overwhelming all the universe.
translation: In all directions, hundreds and thousands of people began to chant "Hari! Hari!" Thus there arose a tumultuous and auspicious sound filling the entire universe.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.66
description: When Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī, who was staying nearby, heard this tumultuous chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, he and his disciples immediately came to see the Lord.
text:
> nikaṭe hari-dhvani śuni' parakāśānanda
> dekhite kautuke āilā lañā śiṣya-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nikaṭe]]---nearby; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---after hearing the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra; [[synonyms:p:parakāśānanda]]---Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:k:kautuke]]---in great eagerness; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---all the disciples.
translation: When Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī, who was staying nearby, heard this tumultuous chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, he and his disciples immediately came to see the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.67
description: When Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī saw the Lord, he and his disciples also joined the chanting with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī was charmed by the Lord's dancing and ecstatic love and by the transcendental beauty of His body.
text:
> dekhiyā prabhura nṛtya, prema, dehera mādhurī
> śisya-gaṇa-saṅge sei bale 'hari' 'hari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---the dancing of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---ecstatic love; [[synonyms:d:dehera]] [[synonyms:m:mādhurī]]---the transcendental beauty of His body; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with his disciples; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---chants; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---Lord Hari's name.
translation: When Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī saw the Lord, he and his disciples also joined the chanting with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī was charmed by the Lord's dancing and ecstatic love and by the transcendental beauty of His body.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.68
description: Ecstatic spiritual transformations began to take place in the Lord's body. His body trembled, and His voice faltered. He perspired, turned pale and wept a constant flow of tears, which wet all the people standing there. The eruptions on the Lord's body appeared like kadamba flowers.
text:
> kampa, svara-bhaṅga, sveda, vaivarṇya, stambha
> aśru-dhārāya bhije loka, pulaka-kadamba
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:s:svara]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṅga]]---faltering voice; [[synonyms:s:sveda]]---perspiration; [[synonyms:v:vaivarṇya]]---fading of bodily color; [[synonyms:s:stambha]]---becoming stunned; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]-[[synonyms:d:dhārāya]]---with showers of tears from the eyes; [[synonyms:b:bhije]]---wet; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]-[[synonyms:k:kadamba]]---eruptions on the body like //kadamba// flowers.
translation: Ecstatic spiritual transformations began to take place in the Lord's body. His body trembled, and His voice faltered. He perspired, turned pale and wept a constant flow of tears, which wet all the people standing there. The eruptions on the Lord's body appeared like kadamba flowers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.69
description: All the people were astonished to see the Lord's jubilation and humility and to hear Him talk in ecstasy. Indeed, all the residents of Benares [Kāśī] saw the bodily transformations and were astonished.
text:
> harṣa, dainya, cāpalyādi 'sañcārī' vikāra
> dekhi' kāśī-vāsī lokera haila camatkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---jubilation; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]---humility; [[synonyms:c:cāpalya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---talking in ecstasy and so on; [[synonyms:s:sañcārī]] [[synonyms:v:vikāra]]---the transient transformations; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kāśī]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---the inhabitants of Benares; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of all the people; [[synonyms:h:haila]] [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---there was astonishment.
translation: All the people were astonished to see the Lord's jubilation and humility and to hear Him talk in ecstasy. Indeed, all the residents of Benares [Kāśī] saw the bodily transformations and were astonished.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.7
description: When the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs were criticizing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu anywhere and everywhere in Vārāṇasī, the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa, hearing this blasphemy, began to think about this unhappily.
text:
> yāhāṅ tāhāṅ prabhura nindā kare sannyāsīra gaṇa
> śuni' duḥkhe mahārāṣṭrīya vipra karaye cintana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---anywhere and everywhere; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:n:nindā]]---criticism of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:d:duḥkhe]]---in great unhappiness; [[synonyms:m:mahārāṣṭrīya]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the //brāhmaṇa// of Mahārāṣṭra province; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:c:cintana]]---was contemplating.
translation: When the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs were criticizing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu anywhere and everywhere in Vārāṇasī, the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa, hearing this blasphemy, began to think about this unhappily.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.70
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu regained His external consciousness, He saw that many Māyāvādī sannyāsīs and other people were gathered there. He therefore suspended His dancing for the time being.
text:
> loka-saṅghaṭṭa dekhi' prabhura 'bāhya' yabe haila
> sannyāsīra gaṇa dekhi' nṛtya saṁvarila
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅghaṭṭa]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---by seeing the great crowd of people; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---external consciousness; [[synonyms:y:yabe]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---when there was; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the groups of Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs,// headed by Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:s:saṁvarila]]---suspended His dancing.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu regained His external consciousness, He saw that many Māyāvādī sannyāsīs and other people were gathered there. He therefore suspended His dancing for the time being.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.71
description: After stopping the kīrtana, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is a great example of humility, offered prayers unto the feet of Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī. At this, Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī immediately came forward and clasped the Lord's lotus feet.
text:
> prakāśānandera prabhu vandilā caraṇa
> prakāśānanda āsi' tāṅra dharila caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prakāśānandera]]---of Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vandilā]]---prayed; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---at the feet; [[synonyms:p:prakāśānanda]]---Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:d:dharila]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---immediately caught the lotus feet.
translation: After stopping the kīrtana, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is a great example of humility, offered prayers unto the feet of Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī. At this, Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī immediately came forward and clasped the Lord's lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.72
description: When Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī caught hold of the Lord's lotus feet, the Lord said, "My dear sir, you are the spiritual master of the whole world; therefore you are most worshipable. As far as I am concerned, I am not even on the level of the disciple of your disciple."
text:
> prabhu kahe,-'tumi jagad-guru pūjyatama
> āmi tomāra nā ha-i 'śiṣyera śiṣya' sama
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued to speak; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:g:guru]]---the spiritual master of the whole world; [[synonyms:p:pūjya]]-[[synonyms:t:tama]]---the most worshipable; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---am not; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣyera]] [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]] [[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal to the disciple of the disciple.
translation: When Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī caught hold of the Lord's lotus feet, the Lord said, "My dear sir, you are the spiritual master of the whole world; therefore you are most worshipable. As far as I am concerned, I am not even on the level of the disciple of your disciple."
purport: Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// generally call themselves //jagad-guru,// the spiritual master of the whole world. Many consider themselves worshipable by everyone, although they do not even go outside India or their own district. Out of His great magnanimity and humility, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu presented Himself as a subordinate disciple of Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.73
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "You are a great, spiritually advanced personality, and therefore you cannot worship a person like Me. I am far inferior. If you do so, My spiritual power will be diminished, for you are as good as the impersonal Brahman.
text:
> śreṣṭha hañā kene kara hīnera vandana
> āmāra sarva-nāśa haya, tumi brahma-sama
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śreṣṭha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being a more honorable person; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---you do; [[synonyms:h:hīnera]]---of an inferior person; [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---worship; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśa]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---I become minimized in My strength; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---you are equal with the impersonal Brahman.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "You are a great, spiritually advanced personality, and therefore you cannot worship a person like Me. I am far inferior. If you do so, My spiritual power will be diminished, for you are as good as the impersonal Brahman.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.74
description: "My dear sir, for you everyone is on the level of impersonal Brahman, but for the enlightenment of people in general you should not behave in that way."
text:
> yadyapi tomāre saba brahma-sama bhāse
> loka-śikṣā lāgi' aiche karite nā āise'
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---for you; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---everyone; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal to the impersonal Brahman; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---appears; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śikṣā]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for the enlightenment of people in general; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in such a way; [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---you should not present yourself.
translation: "My dear sir, for you everyone is on the level of impersonal Brahman, but for the enlightenment of people in general you should not behave in that way."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.75
description: Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī replied, "Formerly I have committed many offenses against You by blaspheming You, but now the effects of my offenses are counteracted by my touching Your lotus feet.
text:
> teṅho kahe, 'tomāra pūrve nindā-aparādha ye karila
> tomāra caraṇa-sparśe, saba kṣaya gela
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:teṅho]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---he replied; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of You; [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---formerly; [[synonyms:n:nindā]]-[[synonyms:a:aparādha]]---offenses and blasphemy; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---whatever I have done; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sparśe]]---by touching Your lotus feet; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:k:kṣaya]] [[synonyms:g:gela]]---the effects of all those offenses have been destroyed.
translation: Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī replied, "Formerly I have committed many offenses against You by blaspheming You, but now the effects of my offenses are counteracted by my touching Your lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.76
description: " 'If a person considered liberated in this life commits offenses against the reservoir of inconceivable potencies, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he will again fall down and desire the material atmosphere for material enjoyment.'
text:
> jīvan-muktā api punar
> yānti saṁsāra-vāsanām
> yady acintya-mahā-śaktau
> bhagavaty aparādhinaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jīvat]]-[[synonyms:m:muktāḥ]]---persons liberated during this life; [[synonyms:a:api]]---//also//; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:y:yānti]]---go; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsanām]]---to desire material enjoyment; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:a:acintya]]-[[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaktau]]---to the possessor of inconceivable spiritual potency; [[synonyms:b:bhagavati]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:a:aparādhinaḥ]]---offenders.
translation: “ 'If a person considered liberated in this life commits offenses against the reservoir of inconceivable potencies, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he will again fall down and desire the material atmosphere for material enjoyment.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.77
description: " 'Being touched by the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, that serpent was immediately freed from the reactions of his sinful life. Thus the serpent gave up his body and assumed the body of a beautiful Vidyādhara demigod.' "
text:
> sa vai bhagavataḥ śrīmat-
> pāda-sparśa-hatāśubhaḥ
> bheje sarpa-vapur hitvā
> rūpaṁ vidyādharārcitam
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---he (the serpent); [[synonyms:v:vai]]---indeed; [[synonyms:b:bhagavataḥ]]---of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śrīmat]]-[[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:s:sparśa]]---by the touch of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:h:hata]]-[[synonyms:a:aśubhaḥ]]---relieved from all reactions of sinful life; [[synonyms:b:bheje]]---achieved; [[synonyms:s:sarpa]]-[[synonyms:v:vapuḥ]]---the body of a snake; [[synonyms:h:hitvā]]---giving up; [[synonyms:r:rūpam]]---beauty; [[synonyms:v:vidyādhara]]-[[synonyms:a:arcitam]]---suitable for a person of Vidyādhara-loka.
translation: “ 'Being touched by the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, that serpent was immediately freed from the reactions of his sinful life. Thus the serpent gave up his body and assumed the body of a beautiful Vidyādhara demigod.' "
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.34.9). The inhabitants of Vṛndāvana, under the leadership of Nanda Mahārāja, once wanted to go to the bank of the Sarasvatī on a pilgrimage. Nanda Mahārāja was fasting, and he lay down near the forest. At that time a serpent, who was formerly cursed by Āṅgirasa Ṛṣi, appeared. This serpent had formerly been named Sudarśana, and he had belonged to the Gandharvaloka planet. However, because he joked with the //ṛṣi,// he was condemned to take on the body of a big snake. When this serpent attacked Nanda Mahārāja, Nanda Mahārāja began to call, "Kṛṣṇa! Help!" Kṛṣṇa immediately appeared and began to kick the serpent with His lotus feet. Due to being touched by the Lord's lotus feet, the serpent was immediately freed from the reactions of his sinful life. Being freed, he again assumed his original form of Sudarśana, the Gandharva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.78
description: When Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī supported himself by quoting the verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately protested by uttering the holy name of Lord Viṣṇu. The Lord then presented Himself as a most fallen living entity, and He said, "If someone accepts a fallen conditioned soul as Viṣṇu, Bhagavān, or an incarnation, he commits a great offense."
text:
> prabhu kahe,-'viṣṇu' 'viṣṇu', āmi kṣudra jīva hīna
> jīve 'viṣṇu' māni-ei aparādha-cihna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]] [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---the holy name of Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kṣudra]]---infinitesimal; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---a living entity; [[synonyms:h:hīna]]---bereft of all good qualities; [[synonyms:j:jīve]]---such a low-grade living entity; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]] [[synonyms:m:māni]]---accepting as Lord Viṣṇu or the Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:a:aparādha]]-[[synonyms:c:cihna]]---this is a great offense.
translation: When Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī supported himself by quoting the verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately protested by uttering the holy name of Lord Viṣṇu. The Lord then presented Himself as a most fallen living entity, and He said, "If someone accepts a fallen conditioned soul as Viṣṇu, Bhagavān, or an incarnation, he commits a great offense."
purport: Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was Viṣṇu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, He nonetheless, to teach us a lesson, denied belonging to the Viṣṇu category. Unfortunately, there are many so-called Viṣṇu incarnations in this Age of Kali. People do not know that posing oneself as an incarnation is most offensive. People should not accept an ordinary man as an incarnation of God, for this also is a very great offense.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.79
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "To say nothing of ordinary living entities, even Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva cannot be considered on the level of Viṣṇu or Nārāyaṇa. If one considers them as such, he is immediately considered an offender and atheist.
text:
> jīve 'viṣṇu' buddhi dūre-yei brahma-rudra-sama
> nārāyaṇe māne tāre 'pāṣaṇḍīte' gaṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jīve]]---an ordinary living being; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---as Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---acceptance; [[synonyms:d:dūre]]---let alone; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:r:rudra]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal to personalities like Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇe]]---Lord Nārāyaṇa, Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---accepts; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---such a person; [[synonyms:p:pāṣaṇḍīte]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇana]]---is grouped among the //pāṣaṇḍīs,// atheistic offenders.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "To say nothing of ordinary living entities, even Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva cannot be considered on the level of Viṣṇu or Nārāyaṇa. If one considers them as such, he is immediately considered an offender and atheist.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.8
description: The Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa thought, "Whoever closely sees the characteristics of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately realizes His personality and accepts Him as the Supreme Lord.
text:
> "prabhura svabhāva,-yebā dekhe sannidhāne
> 'svarūpa' anubhavi' tāṅre 'īśvara' kari' māne
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the characteristics of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yebā]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:s:sannidhāne]]---nearby; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---His personality; [[synonyms:a:anubhavi']]---realizing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---as the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---accepts.
translation: The Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa thought, "Whoever closely sees the characteristics of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately realizes His personality and accepts Him as the Supreme Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.80
description: " 'A person who considers demigods like Brahmā and Śiva to be on an equal level with Nārāyaṇa is to be considered an offender, a pāṣaṇḍī.' "
text:
> yas tu nārāyaṇaṁ devaṁ

> samatvenaiva vīkṣeta

translation: “ 'A person who considers demigods like Brahmā and Śiva to be on an equal level with Nārāyaṇa is to be considered an offender, a pāṣaṇḍī.' "

translation: Prakāśānanda replied, "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa Himself. Nonetheless, You are considering Yourself His eternal servant.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.82
description: "My dear Lord, You are the Supreme Lord, and although You consider Yourself the Lord's servant, You are nonetheless worshipable. You are much greater than I am; therefore all my spiritual achievements have been lost because I have blasphemed You.
text:

> sarva-nāśa haya mora tomāra nindāte

translation: "My dear Lord, You are the Supreme Lord, and although You consider Yourself the Lord's servant, You are nonetheless worshipable. You are much greater than I am; therefore all my spiritual achievements have been lost because I have blasphemed You.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.83
description: " 'O great sage, out of many millions of materially liberated people who are free from ignorance, and out of many millions of siddhas who have nearly attained perfection, there is hardly one pure devotee of Nārāyaṇa. Only such a devotee is actually completely satisfied and peaceful.'
text:
> muktānām api siddhānāṁ
> nārāyaṇa-parāyaṇaḥ
> sudurlabhaḥ praśāntātmā
> koṭiṣv api mahā-mune

translation: “ 'O great sage, out of many millions of materially liberated people who are free from ignorance, and out of many millions of siddhas who have nearly attained perfection, there is hardly one pure devotee of Nārāyaṇa. Only such a devotee is actually completely satisfied and peaceful.'
purport: This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:6:14:5|(6.14.5)]].

text:

purport: This is a statement made by Śukadeva Gosvāmī, who was relating //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.4.46) to Mahārāja Parīkṣit.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.85

text:

> spṛśaty anarthāpagamo yad-arthaḥ
> mahīyasāṁ pāda-rajo-'bhiṣekaṁ
> niṣkiñcanānāṁ na vṛṇīta yāvat

translation: “ 'Unless human society accepts the dust of the lotus feet of great mahātmās-devotees who have nothing to do with material possessions-mankind cannot turn its attention to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. Those lotus feet vanquish all the unwanted miserable conditions of material life.'
purport: This verse appears in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:7:5:32|(7.5.32)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.86

text:
> ebe tomāra pādābje upajibe bhakti

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.9
description: "If by some means I can assemble all the sannyāsīs together, they will certainly become His devotees after seeing His personal characteristics.
text:
> kona prakāre pāroṅ yadi ekatra karite
> ihā dekhi' sannyāsi-gaṇa habe iṅhāra bhakte
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kona]] [[synonyms:p:prakāre]]---by some means; [[synonyms:p:pāroṅ]]---I am able; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to assemble; [[synonyms:i:ihā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---by seeing this (Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's personal characteristics); [[synonyms:s:sannyāsi]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// of Vārāṇasī; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---will become; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]] [[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---His devotees.
translation: "If by some means I can assemble all the sannyāsīs together, they will certainly become His devotees after seeing His personal characteristics.
purport:
If one saw the personal characteristics and activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, one would certainly be convinced that He was the Supreme Personality of Godhead. One can ascertain this by following in the footsteps of the śāstric injunctions. This sincere study and appreciation of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is also applicable to His authorized devotees, and it is clearly stated in the //Caitanya-caritāmṛta// [[books:cc:antya:7:11|(Antya 7.11)]]:

> kali-kālera dharma---kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana
> kṛṣṇa-śakti vinā nāhe tāra pravartana

In this Age of Kali, real religious propaganda should induce people to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// This is possible for someone who is especially empowered by Kṛṣṇa. No one can do this without being especially favored by Kṛṣṇa. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments in this regard in his //Anubhāṣya,// wherein he quotes a verse from //Nārāyaṇa-saṁhitā://

> dvāparīyair janair viṣṇuḥ
> pañcarātrais tu kevalaiḥ
> kalau tu nāma-mātreṇa
> pūjyate bhagavān hariḥ

"In Dvāpara-yuga, devotees of Lord Viṣṇu and Kṛṣṇa rendered devotional service according to the principles of //pāñcarātrika.// In this Age of Kali, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is worshiped simply by the chanting of His holy names." Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura then comments: "Without being empowered by the direct potency of Lord Kṛṣṇa to fulfill His desire and without being specifically favored by the Lord, no human being can become the spiritual master of the whole world. He certainly cannot succeed by mental concoction, which is not meant for devotees or religious people. Only an empowered personality can distribute the holy name of the Lord and enjoin all fallen souls to worship Kṛṣṇa. By distributing the holy name of the Lord, he cleanses the hearts of the most fallen people; therefore he extinguishes the blazing fire of the material world. Not only that, he broadcasts the shining brightness of Kṛṣṇa's effulgence throughout the world. Such an //ācārya,// or spiritual master, should be considered nondifferent from Kṛṣṇa---that is, he should be considered the incarnation of Lord Kṛṣṇa's potency. Such a personality is //kṛṣṇāliṅgita-vigraha---//that is, he is always embraced by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa. Such a person is above the considerations of the //varṇāśrama// institution. He is the //guru// or spiritual master for the entire world, a devotee on the topmost platform, the //mahā-bhāgavata// stage, and a //paramahaṁsa-ṭhākura,// a spiritual form only fit to be addressed as //paramahaṁsa// or //ṭhākura."//

Nonetheless, there are many people who are just like owls but never open their eyes to see the sunshine. These owlish personalities are inferior to the Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// who cannot see the brilliance of Kṛṣṇa's favor. They are prepared to criticize the person engaged in distributing the holy name all over the world and following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who wanted Kṛṣṇa consciousness preached in every town and city.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.90
description: "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and therefore You have inconceivable energies. I wish to hear from You briefly about the Brahma-sūtra."
text:
> tumi ta' īśvara, tomāra āche sarva-śakti
> saṅkṣepa-rūpe kaha tumi śunite haya mati
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed You are; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of You; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there are; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---all potencies; [[synonyms:s:saṅkṣepa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---briefly; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please explain; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:ś:śunite]] [[synonyms:h:haya]] [[synonyms:m:mati]]---I wish to hear.
translation: "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and therefore You have inconceivable energies. I wish to hear from You briefly about the Brahma-sūtra."
purport: Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī said that he had already understood Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's explanation of the direct import of //Brahma-sūtra.// Nonetheless, he was requesting the Lord to briefly give the purpose and purport of the //Brahma-sūtra,// the //Vedānta-sūtra.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.91
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "I am an ordinary living being, and therefore my knowledge is very insignificant. However, the meaning of the Brahma-sūtra is very grave because its author, Vyāsadeva, is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself.
text:
> prabhu kahe,-"āmi jīva', ati tuccha-jñāna!
> vyāsa-sūtrera gambhīra artha, vyāsa-bhagavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---I am an insignificant living being; [[synonyms:a:ati]] [[synonyms:t:tuccha]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---My knowledge is very meager; [[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]-[[synonyms:s:sūtrera]]---of the //Vedānta-sūtra,// written by Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:g:gambhīra]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---very grave meaning; [[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]---Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "I am an ordinary living being, and therefore my knowledge is very insignificant. However, the meaning of the Brahma-sūtra is very grave because its author, Vyāsadeva, is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself.
purport: An ordinary living being cannot actually understand the purpose of the //Vedānta-sūtra.// One can understand the purpose if he hears it from the authority, Vyāsadeva himself. For this reason, Vyāsadeva gave a commentary on the //Brahma-sūtra// in the form of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.// He had been instructed to do this by his spiritual master, Nārada. Of course, Śaṅkarācārya distorted the purpose of the //Brahma-sūtra// because he had a motive to serve. He wanted to establish Vedic knowledge in place of the atheistic knowledge spread by Lord Buddha. All these necessities are there according to time and circumstances. Neither Lord Buddha nor Śaṅkarācārya is to be blamed. The time required such an explanation for the understanding of various types of atheists. The conclusion is that one cannot understand the purpose of the //Vedānta-sūtra// without going through //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// and rendering devotional service. Caitanya Mahāprabhu therefore further explains the matter in the following verses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.92

translation: "The purpose of the Vedānta-sūtra is very difficult for an ordinary person to understand, but Vyāsadeva, out of his causeless mercy, has personally explained the meaning.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.93
