title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.94
description: "The meaning of the sound vibration oṁkāra is present in the Gāyatrī mantra. The same is elaborately explained in the four ślokas of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam known as catuḥ-ślokī.
text:
> praṇavera yei artha, gāyatrīte sei haya
> sei artha catuḥ-ślokīte vivariyā kaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:praṇavera]]---of the sound vibration, //oṁkāra//; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:g:gāyatrīte]]---in the Gāyatrī //mantra//; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---that same meaning; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:ś:ślokīte]]---in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// summarized in four //ślokas//; [[synonyms:v:vivariyā]]---describing elaborately; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---has said.
translation: "The meaning of the sound vibration oṁkāra is present in the Gāyatrī mantra. The same is elaborately explained in the four ślokas of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam known as catuḥ-ślokī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.95
description: "Whatever was spoken by the Supreme Personality of Godhead to Lord Brahmā in the four verses of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, was also explained to Nārada by Lord Brahmā.
text:
> brahmāre īśvara catuḥ-ślokī ye kahilā
> brahmā nārade sei upadeśa kailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmāre]]---to Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:ś:ślokī]]---the four famous verses known as //catuḥ-ślokī//; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---whatever was explained; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:n:nārade]]---to Nārada Muni; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:u:upadeśa]] [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---instructed.
translation: "Whatever was spoken by the Supreme Personality of Godhead to Lord Brahmā in the four verses of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, was also explained to Nārada by Lord Brahmā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.96
description: "Whatever Lord Brahmā told Nārada Muni was again explained by Nārada Muni to Vyāsadeva. Vyāsadeva later considered these instructions in his mind.
text:
> nārada sei artha vyāsere kahilā
> śuni' veda-vyāsa mane vicāra karilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nārada]]---the great sage Nārada; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the same purpose; [[synonyms:v:vyāsere]] [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---explained to Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]---Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---within the mind; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---considered very carefully.
translation: "Whatever Lord Brahmā told Nārada Muni was again explained by Nārada Muni to Vyāsadeva. Vyāsadeva later considered these instructions in his mind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.97
description: "Śrīla Vyāsadeva considered that whatever he had received from Nārada Muni as an explanation of oṁkāra he would elaborately explain in his book Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam as a commentary on Brahma-sūtra.
text:
> "ei artha-āmāra sūtrera vyākhyānurūpa
> 'bhāgavata' kariba sūtrera bhāṣya-svarūpa"
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---this explanation; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---my; [[synonyms:s:sūtrera]]---of //Brahma-sūtra//; [[synonyms:v:vyākhyā]]-[[synonyms:a:anurūpa]]---a suitable explanation; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]---//Śrīmad-Bhāgavata Purāṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---I shall make; [[synonyms:s:sūtrera]]---of the //Brahma-sūtra//; [[synonyms:b:bhāṣya]]-[[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---as the original commentary.
translation: "Śrīla Vyāsadeva considered that whatever he had received from Nārada Muni as an explanation of oṁkāra he would elaborately explain in his book Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam as a commentary on Brahma-sūtra.
purport: The sound vibration //oṁkāra// is the root of Vedic knowledge. This //oṁkāra// is known as //mahā-vākya,// or the supreme sound. Whatever meaning is in the supreme sound //oṁkāra// is further understood in the Gāyatrī //mantra.// Again, this same meaning is explained in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// in the four //ślokas// known as //catuḥ-ślokī,// which begin with the words //ahaṁ evāsam evāgre.// The Lord says, "Only I existed before the creation." From this verse, four //ślokas// have been composed, and these are known as the //catuḥ-ślokī.// In this way the Supreme Personality of Godhead informed Lord Brahmā about the purpose of the //catuḥ-ślokī.// Again, Lord Brahmā explained this to Nārada Muni, and Nārada Muni explained it to Śrīla Vyāsadeva. This is the //paramparā// system, the disciplic succession. The import of Vedic knowledge, the original word //praṇava,// has been explained in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.// The conclusion is that the //Brahma-sūtra// is explained in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.98
description: "Vyāsadeva collected whatever Vedic conclusions were in the four Vedas and 108 Upaniṣads and placed them in the codes of the Vedānta-sūtra.
text:
> cāri-veda-upaniṣade yata kichu haya
> tāra artha lañā vyāsa karilā sañcaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:v:veda]]---the four divisions of the //Vedas// (//Sāma, Yajur, Ṛg// and //Atharva//); [[synonyms:u:upaniṣade]]---and in 108 //Upaniṣads//; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---whatever; [[synonyms:k:kichu]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is there; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meanings of those Vedic literatures; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking together; [[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]---Vyāsadeva; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:s:sañcaya]]---collected.
translation: "Vyāsadeva collected whatever Vedic conclusions were in the four Vedas and 108 Upaniṣads and placed them in the codes of the Vedānta-sūtra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 25.99
description: "In Vedānta-sūtra, the purpose of all Vedic knowledge is explained, and in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam the same purpose has been explained in eighteen thousand verses.
text:
> yei sūtre yei ṛk-viṣaya-vacana
> bhāgavate sei ṛk śloke nibandhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:s:sūtre]]---in the codes of //Vedānta-sūtra//; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛk]]---Vedic //mantra//; [[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]-[[synonyms:v:vacana]]---subject matter to be explained; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavate]]---in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛk]]---that same Vedic //mantra//; [[synonyms:ś:śloke]]---in eighteen thousand verses; [[synonyms:n:nibandhana]]---compiling.
translation: "In Vedānta-sūtra, the purpose of all Vedic knowledge is explained, and in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam the same purpose has been explained in eighteen thousand verses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.1
description: After accepting the sannyāsa order of life, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, out of intense love for Kṛṣṇa, wanted to go to Vṛndāvana, but apparently by mistake He wandered in the Rāḍha-deśa. Later He arrived at Śāntipura and enjoyed Himself there with His devotees. I offer my respectful obeisances to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> nyāsaṁ vidhāyotpraṇayo 'tha gauro
> vṛndāvanaṁ gantu-manā bhramād yaḥ
> rāḍhe bhraman śānti-purīm ayitvā
> lalāsa bhaktair iha taṁ nato 'smi
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nyāsam]]---the regular ritualistic ceremonies of the //sannyāsa// order; [[synonyms:v:vidhāya]]---after accepting; [[synonyms:u:utpraṇayaḥ]]---arousal of intense love for Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:atha]]---thus; [[synonyms:g:gauraḥ]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvanam]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:g:gantu]]-[[synonyms:m:manāḥ]]---thinking of going; [[synonyms:b:bhramāt]]---apparently by mistake; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:r:rāḍhe]]---in the tract of land known as Rāḍha; [[synonyms:b:bhraman]]---wandering; [[synonyms:ś:śānti]]-[[synonyms:p:purīm]]---to Śāntipura; [[synonyms:a:ayitvā]]---going; [[synonyms:l:lalāsa]]---enjoyed; [[synonyms:b:bhaktaiḥ]]---with the devotees; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---here; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:n:nataḥ]] [[synonyms:a:asmi]]---I offer my respectful obeisances.
translation: After accepting the sannyāsa order of life, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, out of intense love for Kṛṣṇa, wanted to go to Vṛndāvana, but apparently by mistake He wandered in the Rāḍha-deśa. Later He arrived at Śāntipura and enjoyed Himself there with His devotees. I offer my respectful obeisances to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.10
description: As Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was enroute to Vṛndāvana, all the ecstatic symptoms became manifest, and He did not know in which direction He was going, nor did He know whether it was day or night.
text:
> eta bali' cale prabhu, premonmādera cihna
> dik-vidik-jñāna nāhi, kibā rātri-dina
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:etabali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:c:cale]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord began to proceed; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:u:unmādera]] [[synonyms:c:cihna]]---the symptoms of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:d:dik]]-[[synonyms:v:vidik]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge of the right direction or wrong direction; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---whether; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---night or day.
translation: As Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was enroute to Vṛndāvana, all the ecstatic symptoms became manifest, and He did not know in which direction He was going, nor did He know whether it was day or night.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.100
description: Śrīla Nityānanda Prabhu continued, "If you invite at least one hundred sannyāsīs to Your home and feed them sumptuously, Your offense will be nullified."
text:
> śateka sannyāsī yadi karāha bhojana
> tabe ei aparādha ha-ibe khaṇḍana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śateka]] [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---one hundred //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:k:karāha]]---You make; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---the eating; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:a:aparādha]]---offense; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ibe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍana]]---nullification.
translation: Śrīla Nityānanda Prabhu continued, "If you invite at least one hundred sannyāsīs to Your home and feed them sumptuously, Your offense will be nullified."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.101
description: Advaita Ācārya replied, "I shall never again invite another sannyāsī, for it is a sannyāsī who has spoiled all My brahminical smṛti regulations."
text:
> ācārya kahe---nā kariba sannyāsi-nimantraṇa
> sannyāsī nāśila mora saba smṛti-dharma
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryakahe]]---Advaita Ācārya said; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---I shall never do; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsi]]-[[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation to the //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---a //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:n:nāśila]]---has spoiled; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:s:smṛti]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---regulative principles of the //smṛti-śāstra.//
translation: Advaita Ācārya replied, "I shall never again invite another sannyāsī, for it is a sannyāsī who has spoiled all My brahminical smṛti regulations."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.102
description: After this, Advaita Ācārya made the Lords wash Their hands and mouths. He then took Them to a nice bed and made Them lie down to take rest.
text:
> eta bali' dui jane karāila ācamana
> uttama śayyāte la-iyā karāila śayana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:etabali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jane]]---unto the two personalities; [[synonyms:k:karāila]] [[synonyms:ā:ācamana]]---washed Their hands and mouth; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]---very nice; [[synonyms:ś:śayyāte]]---on a bed; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iyā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---made Them do; [[synonyms:ś:śayana]]---lying down.
translation: After this, Advaita Ācārya made the Lords wash Their hands and mouths. He then took Them to a nice bed and made Them lie down to take rest.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.103
description: Śrī Advaita Ācārya fed the two Lords cloves and cardamom mixed with tulasī flowers. Thus there was a good flavor within Their mouths.
text:
> lavaṅga elācī-bīja---uttama rasa-vāsa
> tulasī-mañjarī saha dila mukha-vāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lavaṅga]]---cloves; [[synonyms:e:elācī]]---cardamom; [[synonyms:b:bīja]]---seeds; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]---very nice; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---tasteful spices; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]-[[synonyms:m:mañjarī]]---the flowers of //tulasī//; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---perfume of the mouth.
translation: Śrī Advaita Ācārya fed the two Lords cloves and cardamom mixed with tulasī flowers. Thus there was a good flavor within Their mouths.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.104
description: Śrī Advaita Ācārya then smeared the bodies of the Lords with sandalwood pulp and then placed very fragrant flower garlands on Their chests.
text:
> sugandhi candane lipta kaila kalevara
> sugandhi puṣpa-mālā āni' dila hṛdaya-upara
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:g:gandhi]]---fragrant; [[synonyms:c:candane]]---in sandalwood; [[synonyms:l:lipta]]---smeared; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:k:kalevara]]---the bodies; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:g:gandhi]]---very fragrant; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:m:mālā]]---flower garlands; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]-[[synonyms:u:upara]]---on the chests.
translation: Śrī Advaita Ācārya then smeared the bodies of the Lords with sandalwood pulp and then placed very fragrant flower garlands on Their chests.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.105
description: When the Lord lay down on the bed, Advaita Ācārya waited to massage His legs, but the Lord was very hesitant and spoke as follows to Advaita Ācārya.
text:
> ācārya karite cāhe pāda-saṁvāhana
> saṅkucita hañā prabhu balena vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to do; [[synonyms:c:cāhe]]---wants; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:s:saṁvāhana]]---massaging the feet; [[synonyms:s:saṅkucita]]---hesitant; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:b:balena]]---says; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---the words.
translation: When the Lord lay down on the bed, Advaita Ācārya waited to massage His legs, but the Lord was very hesitant and spoke as follows to Advaita Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.106
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Advaita Ācārya, You have made Me dance in various ways. Now give up this practice. Go with Mukunda and Haridāsa and accept Your lunch."
text:
> bahuta nācāile tumi, chāḍa nācāna
> mukunda-haridāsa la-iyā karaha bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bahuta]]---in various ways; [[synonyms:n:nācāile]]---have made Me dance; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:c:chāḍa]]---give up; [[synonyms:n:nācāna]]---dancing; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iyā]]---with; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---do; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eating.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Advaita Ācārya, You have made Me dance in various ways. Now give up this practice. Go with Mukunda and Haridāsa and accept Your lunch."
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is here telling Advaita Ācārya that it is not befitting for a //sannyāsī// to accept nice beds to lie on or to chew cloves and cardamom and have his body smeared with sandalwood pulp. Nor is it befitting for him to accept fragrant garlands and have his legs massaged by a pure Vaiṣṇava. "You have already made Me dance according to Your vow," Caitanya Mahāprabhu said. "Now please stop it. You can go and take Your lunch with Mukunda and Haridāsa."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.107
description: Thereupon Advaita Ācārya took prasāda with Mukunda and Haridāsa, and they all wholeheartedly ate as much as they desired.
text:
> tabe ta' ācārya saṅge lañā dui jane
> karila icchāya bhojana, ye āchila mane
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabeta']]---thereafter; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jane]]---the two persons, namely Mukunda and Haridāsa; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:i:icchāya]]---according to desire; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eating; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:ā:āchila]] [[synonyms:m:mane]]---whatever there was in mind.
translation: Thereupon Advaita Ācārya took prasāda with Mukunda and Haridāsa, and they all wholeheartedly ate as much as they desired.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.108
description: When the people of Śāntipura heard that Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was staying there, they all immediately came to see His lotus feet.
text:
> śāntipurera loka śuni' prabhura āgamana
> dekhite āilā loka prabhura caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śāntipurera]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people of Śāntipura; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---the arrival of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came to see; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of the Lord.
translation: When the people of Śāntipura heard that Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was staying there, they all immediately came to see His lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.109
description: Being very pleased, all the people loudly began to shout the holy name of the Lord, "Hari! Hari!" Indeed, they became struck with wonder upon seeing the beauty of the Lord.
text:
> 'hari' 'hari' bale loka ānandita hañā
> camatkāra pāila prabhura saundarya dekhiñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:harihari]]---the holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---say; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---pleased; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---wonder; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:saundarya]]---the beauty; [[synonyms:d:dekhiñā]]---by seeing.
translation: Being very pleased, all the people loudly began to shout the holy name of the Lord, "Hari! Hari!" Indeed, they became struck with wonder upon seeing the beauty of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.11
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went toward Vṛndāvana, Nityānanda Prabhu, Candraśekhara and Prabhu Mukunda followed Him.
text:
> nityānanda, ācāryaratna, mukunda, tina jana
> prabhu-pāche-pāche tine karena gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryaratna]]---Candraśekhara; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---and Mukunda; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---three persons; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pāche]]-[[synonyms:p:pāche]]---following the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tine]]---all three of them; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---go.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went toward Vṛndāvana, Nityānanda Prabhu, Candraśekhara and Prabhu Mukunda followed Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.110
description: They saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's very fair-complexioned body and its bright luster, which conquered the brilliance of the sun. Over and above this was the beauty of the saffron garments that glittered upon His body.
text:
> gaura-deha-kānti sūrya jiniyā ujjvala
> aruṇa-vastra-kānti tāhe kare jhala-mala
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gaura]]---fair-complexioned; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---of the body; [[synonyms:k:kānti]]---the luster; [[synonyms:s:sūrya]]---the sun; [[synonyms:j:jiniyā]]---conquering; [[synonyms:u:ujjvala]]---bright; [[synonyms:a:aruṇa]]---reddish; [[synonyms:v:vastra]]-[[synonyms:k:kānti]]---the beauty of the garments; [[synonyms:t:tāhe]]---in that; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:j:jhala]]-[[synonyms:m:mala]]---glittering.
translation: They saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's very fair-complexioned body and its bright luster, which conquered the brilliance of the sun. Over and above this was the beauty of the saffron garments that glittered upon His body.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.111
description: People came and went with great pleasure. There was no calculating how many people assembled there before the day was over.
text:
> āise yāya loka harṣe, nāhi samādhāna
> lokera saṅghaṭṭe dina haila avasāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---come; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---go; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all people; [[synonyms:h:harṣe]]---in great pleasure; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:s:samādhāna]]---calculation; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of the people; [[synonyms:s:saṅghaṭṭe]]---in crowds; [[synonyms:d:dina]]---the day; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:a:avasāna]]---the end.
translation: People came and went with great pleasure. There was no calculating how many people assembled there before the day was over.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.112
description: As soon as it was evening, Advaita Ācārya began the congregational chanting. He even began to dance Himself, and the Lord saw the performance.
text:
> sandhyāte ācārya ārambhila saṅkīrtana
> ācārya nācena, prabhu karena darśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sandhyāte]]---in the evening; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:ārambhila]]---began; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---congregational chanting; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:n:nācena]]---dances; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---seeing.
translation: As soon as it was evening, Advaita Ācārya began the congregational chanting. He even began to dance Himself, and the Lord saw the performance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.113
description: When Advaita Ācārya began to dance, Nityānanda Prabhu began dancing behind Him. Haridāsa Ṭhākura, being very pleased, also began dancing behind Him.
text:
> nityānanda gosāñi bule ācārya dhariñā
> haridāsa pāche nāce haraṣita hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānandagosāñi]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:b:bule]]---began to move, dancing; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:d:dhariñā]]---following Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---behind; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:h:haraṣita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being pleased.
translation: When Advaita Ācārya began to dance, Nityānanda Prabhu began dancing behind Him. Haridāsa Ṭhākura, being very pleased, also began dancing behind Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.114
description: Advaita Ācārya said, " 'My dear friends, what shall I say? Today I have received the highest transcendental pleasure. After many, many days, Lord Kṛṣṇa is in My house.' "
text:
> ki kahiba re sakhī ājuka ānanda ora
> cira-dine mādhava mandire mora
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:k:kahiba]]---shall I say; [[synonyms:r:re]]---O; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]---My dear friends; [[synonyms:ā:ājuka]]---today; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:o:ora]]---the limit; [[synonyms:c:cira]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---after many days; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mandire]]---in the temple; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My.
translation: Advaita Ācārya said, " 'My dear friends, what shall I say? Today I have received the highest transcendental pleasure. After many, many days, Lord Kṛṣṇa is in My house.' "
purport: This is a song composed by Vidyāpati. Sometimes the word //mādhava// is misunderstood to refer to Mādhavendra Purī. Advaita Ācārya was a disciple of Mādhavendra Purī, and consequently some people think that He was referring to Mādhavendra Purī by using the word //mādhava.// But actually this is not the fact. This song was composed to commemorate the separation of Kṛṣṇa from Rādhārāṇī during Kṛṣṇa's absence in Mathurā. It is thought that this song was sung by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī when Kṛṣṇa returned. It is technically called //Mathurā-viraha.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.115
description: Advaita Ācārya led the saṅkīrtana party, and with great pleasure He sang this verse. There was a manifestation of ecstatic perspiration, shivering, raised hairs, tears in the eyes and sometimes thundering and bellowing.
text:
> ei pada gāoyāiyā harṣe karena nartana
> sveda-kampa-pulakāśru-huṅkāra-garjana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:p:pada]]---this verse; [[synonyms:g:gāoyāiyā]]---causing to be sung; [[synonyms:h:harṣe]]---in pleasure; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dancing; [[synonyms:s:sveda]]---perspiration; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---shivering; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]---standing of hairs; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears on account of pleasure; [[synonyms:h:huṅkāra]]---thundering; [[synonyms:g:garjana]]---bellowing.
translation: Advaita Ācārya led the saṅkīrtana party, and with great pleasure He sang this verse. There was a manifestation of ecstatic perspiration, shivering, raised hairs, tears in the eyes and sometimes thundering and bellowing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.116
description: While dancing, Advaita Ācārya would sometimes turn around and around and catch the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Advaita Ācārya would then speak to Him as follows.
text:
> phiri' phiri' kabhu prabhura dharena caraṇa
> caraṇe dhariyā prabhure balena vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:phiri']] [[synonyms:p:phiri']]---turning and turning; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dharena]]---catches; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet; [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]] [[synonyms:d:dhariyā]]---catching the lotus feet; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto the Lord; [[synonyms:b:balena]]---says; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---words.
translation: While dancing, Advaita Ācārya would sometimes turn around and around and catch the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Advaita Ācārya would then speak to Him as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.117
description: Śrī Advaita Ācārya would say, "Many days You escaped Me by bluffing. Now I have You in My home, and I will keep You bound up."
text:
> aneka dina tumi more beḍāile bhāṇḍiyā
> gharete pāñāchi, ebe rākhiba bāndhiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anekadina]]---many days; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:m:more]]---Me; [[synonyms:b:beḍāile]]---escaped; [[synonyms:b:bhāṇḍiyā]]---cheating or bluffing; [[synonyms:g:gharete]]---at My home; [[synonyms:p:pāñāchi]]---I have gotten; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:r:rākhiba]]---I shall keep; [[synonyms:b:bāndhiyā]]---binding up.
translation: Śrī Advaita Ācārya would say, "Many days You escaped Me by bluffing. Now I have You in My home, and I will keep You bound up."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.118
description: So speaking, Advaita Ācārya performed congregational chanting with great pleasure for three hours that night and danced all the time.
text:
> eta bali' ācārya ānande karena nartana
> prahareka-rātri ācārya kaila saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in pleasure; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dancing; [[synonyms:p:prahareka]]---about three hours; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]---at night; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Śrī Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---performed //saṅkīrtana,// or congregational chanting.
translation: So speaking, Advaita Ācārya performed congregational chanting with great pleasure for three hours that night and danced all the time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.119
description: When Advaita Ācārya danced in that way, Lord Caitanya felt ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, and because of His separation, the waves and flames of love increased.
text:
> premera utkaṇṭhā,---prabhura nāhi kṛṣṇa-saṅga
> virahe bāḍila prema-jvālāra taraṅga
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:premerautkaṇṭhā]]---the ecstasy of the love; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---meeting with Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:virahe]]---in separation; [[synonyms:b:bāḍila]]---increased; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:j:jvālāra]]---of flames of love; [[synonyms:t:taraṅga]]---waves.
translation: When Advaita Ācārya danced in that way, Lord Caitanya felt ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, and because of His separation, the waves and flames of love increased.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.12
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed through Rāḍha-deśa, whoever saw Him in ecstasy exclaimed, "Hari! Hari!" As they chanted this with the Lord, all the unhappiness of material existence diminished.
text:
> yei yei prabhu dekhe, sei sei loka
> premāveśe 'hari' bale, khaṇḍe duḥkha-śoka
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yeiyei]]---whoever; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---those persons; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in the ecstasy of love; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---exclaim "Hari"; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍe]]---pass over; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]-[[synonyms:ś:śoka]]---all kinds of material unhappiness and lamentation.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed through Rāḍha-deśa, whoever saw Him in ecstasy exclaimed, "Hari! Hari!" As they chanted this with the Lord, all the unhappiness of material existence diminished.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.120
description: Being agitated by the ecstasy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu suddenly fell to the ground. Seeing this, Advaita Ācārya stopped dancing.
text:
> vyākula hañā prabhu bhūmite paḍilā
> gosāñi dekhiyā ācārya nṛtya sambarilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyākulahañā]]---being too much agitated; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]]---to the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---the dancing; [[synonyms:s:sambarilā]]---checked.
translation: Being agitated by the ecstasy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu suddenly fell to the ground. Seeing this, Advaita Ācārya stopped dancing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.121
description: When Mukunda saw the ecstasy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he understood the feelings of the Lord and began to sing many stanzas augmenting the force of the Lord's ecstasy.
text:
> prabhura antara mukunda jāne bhāla-mate
> bhāvera sadṛśa pada lāgilā gāite
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:a:antara]]---the heart; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---knows; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---very well; [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---to the ecstatic mood; [[synonyms:s:sadṛśa]]---suitable; [[synonyms:p:pada]]---verses; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]] [[synonyms:g:gāite]]---began to sing.
translation: When Mukunda saw the ecstasy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he understood the feelings of the Lord and began to sing many stanzas augmenting the force of the Lord's ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.122
description: Advaita Ācārya raised the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to help Him dance, but the Lord, after hearing the stanzas sung by Mukunda, could not be held due to His bodily symptoms.
text:
> ācārya uṭhāila prabhuke karite nartana
> pada śuni' prabhura aṅga nā yāya dhāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāila]]---raised; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to do; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dancing; [[synonyms:p:pada]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---by hearing the stanzas; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the body; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---possible; [[synonyms:d:dhāraṇa]]---to hold.
translation: Advaita Ācārya raised the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to help Him dance, but the Lord, after hearing the stanzas sung by Mukunda, could not be held due to His bodily symptoms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.123
description: Tears fell from His eyes, and His whole body trembled. His hair stood on end, He perspired heavily, and His words faltered. Sometimes He stood, and sometimes He fell. And sometimes He cried.
text:
> aśru, kampa, pulaka, sveda, gadgada vacana
> kṣaṇe uṭhe, kṣaṇe paḍe, kṣaṇeka rodana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]---standing of bodily hairs in ecstasy; [[synonyms:s:sveda]]---perspiration; [[synonyms:g:gadgada]]---faltering; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---words; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---stands; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---falls down; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇeka]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:r:rodana]]---crying.
translation: Tears fell from His eyes, and His whole body trembled. His hair stood on end, He perspired heavily, and His words faltered. Sometimes He stood, and sometimes He fell. And sometimes He cried.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.124
description: Mukunda sang, " 'My dear intimate friend! What has not happened to me! Due to the effects of the poison of love for Kṛṣṇa, my body and mind have been severely afflicted.
text:
> hā hā prāṇa-priya-sakhī, ki nā haila more
> kānu-prema-viṣe mora tanu-mana jare
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hāhā]]---O; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:priya]]-[[synonyms:s:sakhī]]---my dear friend; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haila]] [[synonyms:m:more]]---what has not happened to me; [[synonyms:k:kānu]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣe]]---the poison of love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:t:tanu]]---body; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:j:jare]]---afflicts.
translation: Mukunda sang, " 'My dear intimate friend! What has not happened to me! Due to the effects of the poison of love for Kṛṣṇa, my body and mind have been severely afflicted.
purport: When Mukunda saw that Caitanya Mahāprabhu was feeling ecstatic pain and manifesting ecstatic bodily symptoms, all due to feelings of separation from Kṛṣṇa, he sang songs about meeting with Kṛṣṇa. Advaita Ācārya also stopped dancing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.125
description: " 'My feeling is like this: My mind burns day and night, and I can get no rest. If there were someplace I could go to meet Kṛṣṇa, I would immediately fly there.' "
text:
> rātri-dine poḍe mana soyāsti nā pāṅ
> yāhāṅ gele kānu pāṅ, tāhāṅ uḍi' yāṅ
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---day and night; [[synonyms:p:poḍe]]---burns; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:s:soyāsti]]---rest; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāṅ]]---I get; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:g:gele]]---if going; [[synonyms:k:kānu]] [[synonyms:p:pāṅ]]---I can get Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:u:uḍi']]---flying; [[synonyms:y:yāṅ]]---I go.
translation: “ 'My feeling is like this: My mind burns day and night, and I can get no rest. If there were someplace I could go to meet Kṛṣṇa, I would immediately fly there.' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.126
description: This stanza was sung by Mukunda in a very sweet voice, but as soon as Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard this stanza, His mind went to pieces.
text:
> ei pada gāya mukunda madhura susvare
> śuniyā prabhura citta antare vidare
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:p:pada]]---this stanza; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sings; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweet; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:s:svare]]---in a voice; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:c:citta]]---mind; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---within; [[synonyms:v:vidare]]---splits into pieces.
translation: This stanza was sung by Mukunda in a very sweet voice, but as soon as Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard this stanza, His mind went to pieces.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.127
description: The transcendental ecstatic symptoms of disappointment, moroseness, pleasure, restlessness, pride and humility all began to fight like soldiers within the Lord.
text:
> nirveda, viṣāda, harṣa, cāpalya, garva, dainya
> prabhura sahita yuddha kare bhāva-sainya
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirveda]]---disappointment; [[synonyms:v:viṣāda]]---moroseness; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:c:cāpalya]]---restlessness; [[synonyms:g:garva]]---pride; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]---humility; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sahita]]---with; [[synonyms:y:yuddha]]---fight; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---of ecstatic feelings; [[synonyms:s:sainya]]---soldiers.
translation: The transcendental ecstatic symptoms of disappointment, moroseness, pleasure, restlessness, pride and humility all began to fight like soldiers within the Lord.
purport: Harṣa is described in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu. Harṣa// is experienced when one finally attains the desired goal of life and consequently becomes very glad. When //harṣa// is present, the body shivers, and one's bodily hairs stand on end. There are perspiration, tears and an outburst of passion and madness. The mouth becomes swollen, and one experiences inertia and illusion. When a person attains his desired object and feels very fortunate, the luster of his body increases. Because of his own qualities and feelings of greatness, he does not care for anyone else, and this is called //garva,// or pride. In this condition one utters prayers and does not reply to others' inquiries. Seeing one's own body, concealing one's desires and not heeding the words of others are symptoms visible in the ecstasy of //garva.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.128
description: The entire body of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to totter due to the onslaught of various ecstatic symptoms. As a result, He immediately fell on the ground, and His breathing almost stopped.
text:
> jara-jara haila prabhu bhāvera prahāre
> bhūmite paḍila, śvāsa nāhika śarīre
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jara]]-[[synonyms:j:jara]]---tottering; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of the ecstatic moods; [[synonyms:p:prahāre]]---in the onslaught; [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍila]]---fell; [[synonyms:ś:śvāsa]]---breathing; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there was not; [[synonyms:ś:śarīre]]---in the body.
translation: The entire body of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to totter due to the onslaught of various ecstatic symptoms. As a result, He immediately fell on the ground, and His breathing almost stopped.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.129
description: Upon seeing the condition of the Lord, all the devotees became very anxious. Then, suddenly, the Lord got up and began to make thundering sounds.
text:
> dekhiyā cintita hailā yata bhakta-gaṇa
> ācambite uṭhe prabhu kariyā garjana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:c:cintita]]---anxious; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---devotees; [[synonyms:ā:ācambite]]---all of a sudden; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---rises; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---making; [[synonyms:g:garjana]]---thundering.
translation: Upon seeing the condition of the Lord, all the devotees became very anxious. Then, suddenly, the Lord got up and began to make thundering sounds.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.13
description: All the cowherd boys who saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passing joined with Him and began to shout loudly, "Hari! Hari!"
text:
> gopa-bālaka saba prabhuke dekhiyā
> 'hari' 'hari' bali' ḍāke ucca kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:b:bālaka]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all the cowherd boys; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing the Lord; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---vibrating the sounds "Hari Hari"; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍāke]]---shout; [[synonyms:u:ucca]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---loudly.
translation: All the cowherd boys who saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passing joined with Him and began to shout loudly, "Hari! Hari!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.130
description: Upon standing up, the Lord said, "Go on speaking! Go on speaking!" Thus He began to dance, overwhelmed with pleasure. No one could understand the strong waves of this ecstasy.
text:
> 'bal' 'bal' bale, nāce, ānande vihvala
> bujhana nā yāya bhāva-taraṅga prabala
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bal]] [[synonyms:b:bal]]---speak, speak; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---the Lord says; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in pleasure; [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:b:bujhana]]---understanding; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---not possible; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:t:taraṅga]]---the waves of ecstasy; [[synonyms:p:prabala]]---powerful.
translation: Upon standing up, the Lord said, "Go on speaking! Go on speaking!" Thus He began to dance, overwhelmed with pleasure. No one could understand the strong waves of this ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.131
description: Lord Nityānanda began to walk with Caitanya Mahāprabhu to see that He would not fall, and Advaita Ācārya and Haridāsa Ṭhākura followed Them, dancing.
text:
> nityānanda saṅge bule prabhuke dhariñā
> ācārya, haridāsa bule pāche ta', nāciñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:b:bule]]---walks; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dhariñā]]---catching; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Ṭhākura Haridāsa; [[synonyms:b:bule]]---walk; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---behind; [[synonyms:t:ta]]---certainly; [[synonyms:n:nāciñā]]---dancing.
translation: Lord Nityānanda began to walk with Caitanya Mahāprabhu to see that He would not fall, and Advaita Ācārya and Haridāsa Ṭhākura followed Them, dancing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.132
description: In this way the Lord danced for at least three hours. Sometimes the symptoms of ecstasy were visible, including pleasure, moroseness and many other waves of ecstatic emotional love.
text:
> ei mata prahareka nāce prabhu raṅge
> kabhu harṣa, kabhu viṣāda, bhāvera taraṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:p:prahareka]]---for about three hours; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---in great ecstasy; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:v:viṣāda]]---moroseness; [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of ecstasy; [[synonyms:t:taraṅge]]---in the waves.
translation: In this way the Lord danced for at least three hours. Sometimes the symptoms of ecstasy were visible, including pleasure, moroseness and many other waves of ecstatic emotional love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.133
description: The Lord had been fasting for three days, and after that period He took eatables sumptuously. Thus when He danced and jumped high, He became a little fatigued.
text:
> tina dina upavāse kariyā bhojana
> uddaṇḍa-nṛtyete prabhura haila pariśrama
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tinadina]]---three days; [[synonyms:u:upavāse]]---in fasting; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---doing; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eating; [[synonyms:u:uddaṇḍa]]---jumping high; [[synonyms:n:nṛtyete]]---in dancing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:pariśrama]]---fatigue.
translation: The Lord had been fasting for three days, and after that period He took eatables sumptuously. Thus when He danced and jumped high, He became a little fatigued.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.134
description: Being fully absorbed in love of Godhead, He would not understand His fatigue. But Nityānanda Prabhu, catching Him, stopped His dancing.
text:
> tabu ta' nā jāne śrama premāviṣṭa hañā
> nityānanda mahāprabhuke rākhila dhariñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---does not know; [[synonyms:ś:śrama]]---fatigue; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---absorbed in love; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhuke]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:rākhila]]---stopped; [[synonyms:d:dhariñā]]---catching.
translation: Being fully absorbed in love of Godhead, He would not understand His fatigue. But Nityānanda Prabhu, catching Him, stopped His dancing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.135
description: Although the Lord was fatigued, Nityānanda Prabhu kept Him steady by holding Him. At that time Advaita Ācārya suspended the chanting and, by rendering various services to the Lord, made Him lie down to take rest.
text:
> ācārya-gosāñi tabe rākhila kīrtana
> nānā sevā kari' prabhuke karāila śayana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:r:rākhila]]---suspended; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---the chanting; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---services; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---performing; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---unto the Lord; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---made to do; [[synonyms:ś:śayana]]---lying down.
translation: Although the Lord was fatigued, Nityānanda Prabhu kept Him steady by holding Him. At that time Advaita Ācārya suspended the chanting and, by rendering various services to the Lord, made Him lie down to take rest.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.136
description: For ten continuous days Advaita Ācārya held feasting and chanting in the evening. He served the Lord in this way without any change.
text:
> ei-mata daśa-dina bhojana-kīrtana
> eka-rūpe kari' kare prabhura sevana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---continuously for ten days; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]-[[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---eating and chanting; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---without change; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---service.
translation: For ten continuous days Advaita Ācārya held feasting and chanting in the evening. He served the Lord in this way without any change.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.137
description: In the morning Candraśekhara brought Śacīmātā from her house with many devotees, and he seated her in a palanquin.
text:
> prabhāte ācāryaratna dolāya caḍāñā
> bhakta-gaṇa-saṅge āilā śacīmātā lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhāte]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryaratna]]---Candraśekhara; [[synonyms:d:dolāya]]---in a palanquin; [[synonyms:c:caḍāñā]]---seating; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:m:mātā]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---bringing.
translation: In the morning Candraśekhara brought Śacīmātā from her house with many devotees, and he seated her in a palanquin.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.138
description: In this way, all the people of the town of Nadia-including all women, boys and old men-came there. Thus the crowd increased.
text:
> nadīyā-nagarera loka---strī-bālaka-vṛddha
> saba loka āilā, haila saṅghaṭṭa samṛddha
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nadīyā]]---known as Nadia; [[synonyms:n:nagarera]]---of the city; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people; [[synonyms:s:strī]]---women; [[synonyms:b:bālaka]]---boys; [[synonyms:v:vṛddha]]---old men; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all people; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:s:saṅghaṭṭa]]---crowd; [[synonyms:s:samṛddha]]---increased.
translation: In this way, all the people of the town of Nadia-including all women, boys and old men-came there. Thus the crowd increased.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.139
description: In the morning, after regular duties were completed and the Lord was chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, the people accompanied Śacīmātā to the house of Advaita Ācārya.
text:
> prātaḥ-kṛtya kari' kare nāma-saṅkīrtana
> śacīmātā lañā āilā advaita-bhavana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛtya]]---the morning duties; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---finishing; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra//; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:m:mātā]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---with; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:b:bhavana]]---at the house of Advaita Ācārya.
translation: In the morning, after regular duties were completed and the Lord was chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, the people accompanied Śacīmātā to the house of Advaita Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.14
description: When He heard all the cowherd boys also chanting "Hari! Hari!" Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased. He approached them, put His hand on their heads and said, "Go on chanting like that."
text:
> śuni' tā-sabāra nikaṭa gelā gaurahari
> 'bala' 'bala' bale sabāra śire hasta dhari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:t:tā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:n:nikaṭa]]---near; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bala]] [[synonyms:b:bala]]---go on speaking, go on speaking; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---He said; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:ś:śire]] [[synonyms:h:hasta]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---keeping His hand on their heads.
translation: When He heard all the cowherd boys also chanting "Hari! Hari!" Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased. He approached them, put His hand on their heads and said, "Go on chanting like that."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.140
description: As soon as mother Śacī appeared on the scene, Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell before her like a stick. Mother Śacī began to cry, taking the Lord on her lap.
text:
> śacī-āge paḍilā prabhu daṇḍavat hañā
> kāndite lāgilā śacī kole uṭhāiñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of mother Śacī; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---like a stick; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:k:kāndite]]---to cry; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:k:kole]]---on the lap; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāiñā]]---taking.
translation: As soon as mother Śacī appeared on the scene, Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell before her like a stick. Mother Śacī began to cry, taking the Lord on her lap.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.141
description: Upon seeing each other, they both became overwhelmed. Seeing the Lord's head without hair, mother Śacī became greatly agitated.
text:
> doṅhāra darśane duṅhe ha-ilā vihvala
> keśa nā dekhiyā śacī ha-ilā vikala
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]] [[synonyms:d:darśane]]---in seeing one another; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:k:keśa]]---hair; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vikala]]---agitated.
translation: Upon seeing each other, they both became overwhelmed. Seeing the Lord's head without hair, mother Śacī became greatly agitated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.142
description: Out of love she began to caress the body of the Lord. Sometimes she kissed His face and tried to observe Him carefully, but because her eyes were filled with tears, she could not see.
text:
> aṅga muche, mukha cumbe, kare nirīkṣaṇa
> dekhite nā pāya,---aśru bharila nayana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the body; [[synonyms:m:muche]]---caresses; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---face; [[synonyms:c:cumbe]]---kisses; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:n:nirīkṣaṇa]]---observing; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---not able; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:b:bharila]]---filled; [[synonyms:n:nayana]]---the eyes.
translation: Out of love she began to caress the body of the Lord. Sometimes she kissed His face and tried to observe Him carefully, but because her eyes were filled with tears, she could not see.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.143
description: Understanding that Lord Caitanya had accepted the renounced order of life, Śacīmātā, crying, said to the Lord, "My darling Nimāi, do not be cruel like Viśvarūpa, Your elder brother."
text:
> kāndiyā kahena śacī, bāchāre nimāñi
> viśvarūpa-sama nā kariha niṭhurāi
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāndiyā]]---crying; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---says; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:b:bāchāre]]---my darling; [[synonyms:n:nimāñi]]---O Nimāi; [[synonyms:v:viśvarūpa]]---Viśvarūpa; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---like; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do not do; [[synonyms:n:niṭhurāi]]---cruelty.
translation: Understanding that Lord Caitanya had accepted the renounced order of life, Śacīmātā, crying, said to the Lord, "My darling Nimāi, do not be cruel like Viśvarūpa, Your elder brother."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.144
description: Mother Śacī continued, "After accepting the renounced order, Viśvarūpa never again gave me audience. If You do like Him, that will certainly be the death of me."
text:
> sannyāsī ha-iyā punaḥ nā dila daraśana
> tumi taiche kaile mora ha-ibe maraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---a member of the renounced order; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:iyā]]---after becoming; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visit; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---like that; [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---if doing; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ibe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:m:maraṇa]]---death.
translation: Mother Śacī continued, "After accepting the renounced order, Viśvarūpa never again gave me audience. If You do like Him, that will certainly be the death of me."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.145
description: The Lord replied, "My dear mother, please hear. This body belongs to you. I do not possess anything.
text:
> kāndiyā balena prabhu---śuna, mora āi
> tomāra śarīra ei, mora kichu nāi
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāndiyā]]---crying; [[synonyms:b:balena]]---says; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:ā:āi]]---mother; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:ś:śarīra]]---body; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---anything; [[synonyms:n:nāi]]---is not.
translation: The Lord replied, "My dear mother, please hear. This body belongs to you. I do not possess anything.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.146
description: "This body was raised by you, and it comes from you. I cannot repay this debt even in millions of births.
text:
> tomāra pālita deha, janma tomā haite
> koṭi janme tomāra ṛṇa nā pāri śodhite
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:p:pālita]]---raised; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---body; [[synonyms:j:janma]]---birth; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]---you; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---millions; [[synonyms:j:janme]]---in births; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṇa]]---debt; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---I am able; [[synonyms:ś:śodhite]]---to repay.
translation: "This body was raised by you, and it comes from you. I cannot repay this debt even in millions of births.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.147
description: "Knowingly or unknowingly I have accepted this renounced order. Still, I shall never be indifferent to you.
text:
> jāni' vā nā jāni' kaila yadyapi sannyāsa
> tathāpi tomāre kabhu nahiba udāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---knowing; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---knowing; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---accepted; [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---the renounced order; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---unto you; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:n:nahiba]]---shall not become; [[synonyms:u:udāsa]]---indifferent.
translation: "Knowingly or unknowingly I have accepted this renounced order. Still, I shall never be indifferent to you.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.148
description: "My dear mother, wherever you ask Me to stay I shall stay, and whatever you order I shall execute."
text:
> tumi yāhāṅ kaha, āmi tāhāṅi rahiba
> tumi yei ājñā kara, sei ta' kariba
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---ask; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅi]]---there; [[synonyms:r:rahiba]]---shall stay; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---give; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---I shall execute.
translation: "My dear mother, wherever you ask Me to stay I shall stay, and whatever you order I shall execute."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.149
description: Saying this, the Lord offered obeisances to His mother again and again, and mother Śacī, being pleased, took Him again and again on her lap.
text:
> eta bali' punaḥ punaḥ kare namaskāra
> tuṣṭa hañā āi kole kare bāra bāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]] [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again and again; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---offers; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:t:tuṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being pleased; [[synonyms:ā:āi]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:k:kole]]---on the lap; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---takes; [[synonyms:b:bāra]] [[synonyms:b:bāra]]---again and again.
translation: Saying this, the Lord offered obeisances to His mother again and again, and mother Śacī, being pleased, took Him again and again on her lap.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.15
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus blessed them all, saying that they were all fortunate. In this way He praised them, and He felt very successful because they chanted the holy name of Lord Hari.
text:
> tā'-sabāra stuti kare,---tomarā bhāgyavān
> kṛtārtha karile more śunāñā hari-nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tā']]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:s:stuti]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu praised the behavior; [[synonyms:t:tomarā]]---you; [[synonyms:b:bhāgyavān]]---fortunate; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---successful; [[synonyms:k:karile]]---you have made; [[synonyms:m:more]]---to Me; [[synonyms:ś:śunāñā]]---by chanting; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Hari.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus blessed them all, saying that they were all fortunate. In this way He praised them, and He felt very successful because they chanted the holy name of Lord Hari.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.150
description: Then Advaita Ācārya took mother Śacī within the house. The Lord was immediately ready to meet all the devotees.
text:
> tabe āi lañā ācārya gelā abhyantara
> bhakta-gaṇa milite prabhu ha-ilā satvara

translation: Then Advaita Ācārya took mother Śacī within the house. The Lord was immediately ready to meet all the devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.151
description: The Lord met all the devotees one after the other, and looking at everyone's face individually, He embraced them tightly.
text:
> eke eke milila prabhu saba bhakta-gaṇa
> sabāra mukha dekhi' kare dṛḍha āliṅgana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ekeeke]]---one after another; [[synonyms:m:milila]]---met; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---face; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]]---tightly; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing.
translation: The Lord met all the devotees one after the other, and looking at everyone's face individually, He embraced them tightly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.152

translation: Although the devotees were unhappy at not seeing the Lord's hair, they nonetheless derived great happiness from seeing His beauty.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.153-155
description: Śrīvāsa, Rāmāi, Vidyānidhi, Gadādhara, Gaṅgādāsa, Vakreśvara, Murāri, Śuklāmbara, Buddhimanta Khāṅ, Nandana, Śrīdhara, Vijaya, Vāsudeva, Dāmodara, Mukunda, Sañjaya and all the others, however many I can mention-indeed, all the inhabitants of Navadvīpa-arrived there, and the Lord met them with smiles and glances of mercy.

> gaṅgādāsa, vakreśvara, murāri, śuklāmbara
>
> buddhimanta khāṅ, nandana, śrīdhara, vijaya

> kata nāma la-iba yata navadvīpa-vāsī

synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]---Śrīvāsa; [[synonyms:r:rāmāi]]---Rāmāi; [[synonyms:v:vidyānidhi]]---Vidyānidhi; [[synonyms:g:gadādhara]]---Gadādhara; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgādāsa]]---Gaṅgādāsa; [[synonyms:v:vakreśvara]]---Vakreśvara; [[synonyms:m:murāri]]---Murāri; [[synonyms:ś:śuklāmbara]]---Śuklāmbara; [[synonyms:b:buddhimanta]] [[synonyms:k:khāṅ]]---Buddhimanta Khāṅ; [[synonyms:n:nandana]]---Nandana; [[synonyms:ś:śrīdhara]]---Śrīdhara; [[synonyms:v:vijaya]]---Vijaya; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]---Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Dāmodara; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:s:sañjaya]]---Sañjaya; [[synonyms:k:kata]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---how many names; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iba]]---I shall mention; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:n:navadvīpa]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---the inhabitants of Navadvīpa; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---all of them; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛṣṭye]]---with merciful glances; [[synonyms:h:hāsi']]---smiling.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.156

text:

translation: Everyone was chanting the holy names of Hari and dancing. In this way the domicile of Advaita Ācārya was converted into Śrī Vaikuṇṭha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.157

text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.158
description: To everyone who came to see the Lord from villages nearby, especially from Navadvīpa, Advaita Ācārya gave residential quarters, as well as all kinds of eatables, for many days. Indeed, He properly adjusted everything.
text:
> sabākāre vāsā dila---bhakṣya, anna-pāna
> bahu-dina ācārya-gosāñi kaila samādhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabākāre]]---to all of them; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave residential quarters; [[synonyms:b:bhakṣya]]---eatables; [[synonyms:a:anna]]-[[synonyms:p:pāna]]---food and drink; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---for many days; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:samādhāna]]---adjustment.
translation: To everyone who came to see the Lord from villages nearby, especially from Navadvīpa, Advaita Ācārya gave residential quarters, as well as all kinds of eatables, for many days. Indeed, He properly adjusted everything.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.162
description: When the Lord performed kīrtana, He manifested all kinds of transcendental symptoms. He appeared stunned and trembling, His hair stood on end, and His voice faltered. There were tears and devastation.
text:
> kīrtana karite prabhura sarva-bhāvodaya
> stambha, kampa, pulakāśru, gadgada, pralaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kīrtanakarite]]---while performing chanting; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]]---manifestations of ecstatic symptoms; [[synonyms:s:stambha]]---being stunned; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]---standing of the hair; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:g:gadgada]]---faltering of the voice; [[synonyms:p:pralaya]]---devastation.
translation: When the Lord performed kīrtana, He manifested all kinds of transcendental symptoms. He appeared stunned and trembling, His hair stood on end, and His voice faltered. There were tears and devastation.
purport: Devastation is described in the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// as a combination of happiness and distress that becomes conspicuous by an absence of any sense of them. In this condition, a devotee falls to the ground, and the subsequent symptoms in the body ensue. These symptoms are mentioned above, and when they become prominent in the body, a state called //pralaya// (devastation) is manifest.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.163

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.166

translation: "Whenever Nimāi falls to the surface of the earth, please do not let Him feel any pain."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.167
description: When mother Śacī was thus overwhelmed in parental love for Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, she became transformed with happiness, fear and humility, as well as bodily symptoms.
text:
> ei-mata śacīdevī vātsalye vihvala
> harṣa-bhaya-dainya-bhāve ha-ila vikala
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:d:devī]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:v:vātsalye]]---in parental affection; [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---happiness; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---and in humility; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vikala]]---transformed.
translation: When mother Śacī was thus overwhelmed in parental love for Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, she became transformed with happiness, fear and humility, as well as bodily symptoms.
purport:
These verses indicate that mother Śacī, born in the family of Nīlāmbara Cakravartī, used to worship Lord Viṣṇu even before her marriage. As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:6:41|(6.41)]]:

> prāpya puṇya-kṛtāṁ lokān
> uṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
> śucīnāṁ śrīmatāṁ gehe
> yoga-bhraṣṭo 'bhijāyate

"The unsuccessful //yogī,// after many, many years of enjoyment on the planets of the pious living entities, is born into a family of righteous people, or into a family of rich aristocracy." Mother Śacī, a //nitya-siddha// living entity, is an incarnation of mother Yaśodā. She appeared in the house of Nīlāmbara Cakravartī and was everlastingly engaged in the service of Lord Viṣṇu. Later she directly had as her child Lord Viṣṇu, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and she served Him from the day of His appearance. This is the position of //nitya-siddha// associates. Śrī Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura therefore sings: 

> gaurāṅgera saṅgi-gaṇe nitya-siddha kari māne. Every devotee should know that all the associates of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu-His family members, friends and other associates-were all //nitya-siddhas. A nitya-siddha// never forgets the service of the Lord. He is always engaged, even from childhood, in worshiping the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.168
description: Since Advaita Ācārya was giving alms and food to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the other devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, also desired to give Him alms and invite Him for lunch.
text:
> śrīvāsādi yata prabhura vipra bhakta-gaṇa
> prabhuke bhikṣā dite haila sabākāra mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---especially the //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---devotees; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---unto the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---lunch; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:s:sabākāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: Since Advaita Ācārya was giving alms and food to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the other devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, also desired to give Him alms and invite Him for lunch.
purport: It is the duty of all //gṛhasthas// to invite a //sannyāsī// to their homes if he happens to be in the neighborhood or village. This very system is still current in India. If a //sannyāsī// is in the neighborhood of a village, he is inv ted by all householders, one after another. As long as a //sannyāsī// remains in the village, he enlightens the inhabitants in spiritual understanding. In other words, a //sannyāsī// has no housing or food problems even when he travels extensively. Even though Advaita Ācārya was supplying Caitanya Mahāprabhu with //prasāda,// the other devotees from Navadvīpa and Śāntipura also desired to offer Him //prasāda.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.169
description: Hearing these proposals made by other devotees of the Lord, mother Śacī said to the devotees, "How many times shall I get the chance to see Nimāi again?"
text:
> śuni' śacī sabākāre karila minati
> nimāñira daraśana āra muñi pāba kati
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing of this; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:s:sabākāre]]---unto all of them; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---made; [[synonyms:m:minati]]---submission; [[synonyms:n:nimāñira]]---of Nimāi, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visit; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---any more; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:p:pāba]]---shall get; [[synonyms:k:kati]]---where or how many times.
translation: Hearing these proposals made by other devotees of the Lord, mother Śacī said to the devotees, "How many times shall I get the chance to see Nimāi again?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.17
description: "If Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asks you about the path to Vṛndāvana, please show Him the path on the bank of the Ganges instead."
text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.181

text:
> teṅho yadi ihāṅ rahe, tabe mora sukha
> tāṅ'ra nindā haya yadi, seha mora duḥkha
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---stays; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:t:tāṅ'ra]] [[synonyms:n:nindā]]---blasphemy of Him; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:s:seha]]---that also; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness.
translation: Śacīmātā said, "It will be a great happiness for me if Nimāi, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, stays here. But at the same time, if someone blames Him, it will be my great unhappiness."
purport:
It is a great happiness for a mother if her son does not leave home to search out Kṛṣṇa but remains with her. At the same time, if a son does not search after Kṛṣṇa but simply remains at home, he is certainly blamed by experienced saintly persons. Such blame certainly causes great unhappiness for a mother. If a real mother wants her son to progress spiritually, she had better allow him to go out searching for Kṛṣṇa. The mother naturally desires the welfare of the son. If a mother does not allow her son to search for Kṛṣṇa, she is called //mā,// which indicates //māyā.// By allowing her son to go as a //sannyāsī// and search for Kṛṣṇa, Śacīmātā instructs all mothers of the world. She indicates that all sons should become real devotees of Kṛṣṇa and should not stay at home under the care of an affectionate mother. This is supported by //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:5:5:18|(5.5.18)]]:

> gurur na sa syāt sva-jano na sa syāt
> pitā na sa syāj jananī na sā syāt
> daivaṁ na tat syān na patiś ca sa syān
> na mocayed yaḥ samupeta-mṛtyum

"No one should become a spiritual master-nor a relative, father, mother, worshipable Deity or husband-if he cannot help a person escape the imminent path of death." Every living entity is wandering within the universe, subjected to the law of //karma// and transmigrating from one body to another and from one planet to another. Therefore the whole Vedic process is meant to save the wandering living entities from the clutches of //māyā//-birth, death, disease and old age. This means stopping the cycle of birth and death. This cycle can be stopped only if one worships Kṛṣṇa. As the Lord says in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:4:9|(Bg. 4.9)]]:

> janma karma ca me divyam
> evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ
> tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma
> naiti mām eti so 'rjuna

"One who knows the transcendental nature of My appearance and activities does not, upon leaving the body, take his birth again in this material world, but attains My eternal abode, O Arjuna."

To stop the cycle of birth and death, one has to understand Kṛṣṇa as He is. Simply by knowing Kṛṣṇa, one can stop the process of rebirth into this material world. By acting in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, one can return to Godhead. The highest perfection of life is for a father, mother, spiritual master, husband or any other family member to help others return home, back to Godhead. That is the most preferred welfare activity for the benefit of relatives. Therefore, Śacīmātā, although the mother of Nimāi Paṇḍita, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, considered all the facts and decided to allow her son to go out and search for Kṛṣṇa. At the same time, she made some arrangements in order that she might get news of all the activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

translation: All the devotees informed Lord Caitanya of Śacīmātā's decision. Hearing it, the Lord became very pleased.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.188
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered respects to all the devotees present from Navadvīpa and other towns, speaking to them as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.189
description: "My dear friends, you are all My intimate friends. Now I am begging a favor of you. Please give it to Me."
text:
> tumi-saba loka---mora parama bāndhava

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.190
description: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested them all to return home and begin chanting the holy name congregationally. He also requested them to worship Kṛṣṇa, chant His holy name and discuss His holy pastimes.
text:
> ghare yāñā kara sadā kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtana
> kṛṣṇa-nāma, kṛṣṇa-kathā, kṛṣṇa ārādhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:ghareyāñā]]---returning home; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---kindly do; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---discussion of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:ārādhana]]---worshiping.
translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested them all to return home and begin chanting the holy name congregationally. He also requested them to worship Kṛṣṇa, chant His holy name and discuss His holy pastimes.
purport: The cult of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Hare Kṛṣṇa movement, is very nicely explained by Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu authoritatively. It is not that everyone has to take //sannyāsa// like Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Everyone can execute the cult of Kṛṣṇa consciousness at home, as ordered by the Lord. Everyone can congregationally chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa, the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// One can also discuss the subject matter of the //Bhagavad-gītā// and //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// and install Deities of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa or Gaura-Nitāi or both and worship them very carefully in one's own home. It is not that we have to open different centers all over the world. Whoever cares for the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement can install Deities at home and, under superior guidance, worship the Deity regularly, chanting the //mahā-mantra// and discussing the //Bhagavad-gītā// and //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.// We are actually teaching in our classes how to go about this. One who feels that he is not yet ready to live in a temple or undergo strict regulative principles in the temple-especially householders who live with a wife and children-can start a center at home by installing the Deity, worshiping the Lord morning and evening, chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa and discussing the //Bhagavad-gītā// and //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.// Anyone can do this at home without difficulty, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested all the devotees present there to do so.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.191
description: After thus instructing the devotees, the Lord asked their permission to go to Jagannātha Purī. He assured them that at intervals He would come there and meet them again and again.
text:
> ājñā deha nīlācale kariye gamana
> madhye madhye āsi' tomāya diba daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:deha]]---give permission; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:k:kariye]]---I do; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going; [[synonyms:m:madhye]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming here; [[synonyms:t:tomāya]]---to all of you; [[synonyms:d:diba]]---I shall give; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---audience.
translation: After thus instructing the devotees, the Lord asked their permission to go to Jagannātha Purī. He assured them that at intervals He would come there and meet them again and again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.192
description: In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, offering due respects to all the devotees and smiling very mildly, bid them farewell.

> eta bali' sabākāre īṣat hāsiñā

translation: In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, offering due respects to all the devotees and smiling very mildly, bid them farewell.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.193
description: After requesting all the devotees to return home, the Lord decided to go to Jagannātha Purī. At that time Haridāsa Ṭhākura began to cry and speak some pathetic words.

translation: After requesting all the devotees to return home, the Lord decided to go to Jagannātha Purī. At that time Haridāsa Ṭhākura began to cry and speak some pathetic words.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.194
description: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "You are going to Jagannātha Purī, and that is all right, but what will be my destination? I am not able to go to Jagannātha Purī."
text:
> nīlācale yābe tumi, mora kon gati
> nīlācale yāite mora nāhika śakati
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]] [[synonyms:y:yābe]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You will go to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:k:kon]]---what; [[synonyms:g:gati]]---destination; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to go; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:ś:śakati]]---strength.
translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "You are going to Jagannātha Purī, and that is all right, but what will be my destination? I am not able to go to Jagannātha Purī."
purport: Although Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura was born in a Muslim family, he was accepted as a properly initiated //brāhmaṇa.// As such, he had every right to enter the temple of Jagannātha Purī, but because there were some rules and regulations stipulating that only //brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas// and //śūdras// (members of the //varṇāśrama-dharma// system) could enter, Haridāsa Ṭhākura, out of his great humility, did not want to violate these existing rules. He therefore said that he did not have the strength to enter into the temple, and he pointed out that if Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lived within the temple, there would be no way for Haridāsa Ṭhākura to see Him. Later, when Haridāsa Ṭhākura went to Jagannātha Purī, he lived outside the temple on the beach by the sea. A monastery has now been erected there, known as Siddhabakula Maṭha. people go there to see the place of worship (bhajana-kuṭīra) of Haridāsa Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.195
description: "Because I am the lowest among men, I shall not be able to see You. How shall I maintain my sinful life?"
