translation: "Because I am the lowest among men, I shall not be able to see You. How shall I maintain my sinful life?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.196

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.199

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.203
description: In this way all the opulences of Advaita Ācārya-His faith, devotion, home, riches and everything else-were successfully utilized in the worship of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> ācāryera śraddhā-bhakti-gṛha-sampada-dhane
> sakala saphala haila prabhura ārādhane
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]]---of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]]---faith; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotion; [[synonyms:g:gṛha]]---home; [[synonyms:s:sampada]]---opulence; [[synonyms:d:dhane]]---the wealth; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:s:saphala]]---successful; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ārādhane]]---in the worship.
translation: In this way all the opulences of Advaita Ācārya-His faith, devotion, home, riches and everything else-were successfully utilized in the worship of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
purport: Advaita Ācārya set an ideal example for all householder devotees in His receiving of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His devotees and in His execution of a daily festival at His home. If one has the proper means and wealth, he should occasionally invite the devotees of Lord Caitanya, who are engaged in preaching all over the world, and hold a festival at home simply by distributing //prasāda// and talking about Kṛṣṇa during the day and holding congregational chanting for at least three hours in the evening. This procedure must be adopted in all centers of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. Thus they will daily perform //saṅkīrtana-yajña.// In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.32) the daily performance of //saṅkīrtana-yajña// is recommended for this age (//yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair yajanti hi su-medhasaḥ//). One should worship Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His four associates, the Pañca-tattva, by distributing //prasāda// and holding congregational chanting. Indeed, that //yajña// or sacrifice is most recommended in this Age of Kali. In this age, other //yajñas// are not possible to perform, but this //yajña// can be performed everywhere and anywhere without difficulty.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.204

> bhojana karāñā pūrṇa kaila nija-sukha

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.209-210

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.211

translation: When everything was arranged, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu circumambulated His mother and then started for Jagannātha Purī. In the house of Advaita Ācārya there arose tumultuous crying.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.212
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was unaffected. He left swiftly, and Advaita Ācārya followed Him weeping.
text:
> nirapekṣa hañā prabhu śīghra calilā
> kāndite kāndite ācārya paścāt calilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirapekṣa]]---indifferent; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]]---very quickly; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went; [[synonyms:k:kāndite]] [[synonyms:k:kāndite]]---crying and crying; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:paścāt]]---behind; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was unaffected. He left swiftly, and Advaita Ācārya followed Him weeping.
purport: As Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura explains, the word //nirapekṣa// means not being affected by anything material and remaining fixed in the service of the Lord. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not very much care for the roaring tumult and cry at the house of Advaita Ācārya, which He heard when starting for Jagannātha Purī. Worldly moralists may criticize Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for being very cruel, but the Lord did not care for such criticism. As the world teacher of this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, He actually showed that a person seriously engaged in Kṛṣṇa consciousness should not be affected by worldly affection. The best course is to engage in rendering service to the Lord and to become callous to material objectives. Externally everyone is attached to material things, but if one becomes entangled in such things, he cannot make progress in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Therefore those who are engaged in Kṛṣṇa consciousness should not care for the so-called morality of the material world if that morality opposes the service of the Lord. As Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu has personally shown, one cannot properly execute Kṛṣṇa consciousness without being neutral.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.213
description: After He had followed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for some distance, Advaita Ācārya was petitioned by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with folded hands. The Lord spoke the following sweet words.
text:

> ācārye prabodhi' kahe kichu miṣṭa bāta

translation: After He had followed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for some distance, Advaita Ācārya was petitioned by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with folded hands. The Lord spoke the following sweet words.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.214
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Please pacify all the devotees and My mother. If You become agitated, no one will be able to continue to exist."

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Please pacify all the devotees and My mother. If You become agitated, no one will be able to continue to exist."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.215
description: Saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced Advaita Ācārya and stopped Him from following any further. Then, without anxiety, He proceeded to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> eta bali' prabhu tāṅre kari' āliṅgana
> nivṛtti kariyā kaila svacchanda gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing; [[synonyms:n:nivṛtti]]---stop; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---making; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:svacchanda]]---without anxiety; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going toward Jagannātha Purī.
translation: Saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced Advaita Ācārya and stopped Him from following any further. Then, without anxiety, He proceeded to Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.216
description: The Lord, with the other four persons, went along the banks of the Ganges through the path of Chatrabhoga toward Nīlādri, Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> gaṅgā-tīre-tīre prabhu cāri-jana-sāthe
> nīlādri calilā prabhu chatrabhoga-pathe
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the banks of the Ganges; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]-[[synonyms:s:sāthe]]---with the other four persons; [[synonyms:n:nīlādri]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---proceeded; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:c:chatrabhoga]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the path of Chatrabhoga.
translation: The Lord, with the other four persons, went along the banks of the Ganges through the path of Chatrabhoga toward Nīlādri, Jagannātha Purī.
purport: In the southern section of the eastern railway, in the district of twenty-four //pargaṇās,// is a station named Magrāhāṭa. If one goes to the southeastern side of that station for some fourteen miles, there is a place called Jayanagara. About six miles south of this Jayanagara station is a village named Chatrabhoga. Sometimes this village is called Khāḍi. In this village is a Deity of Lord Śiva known as Vaijurkānātha. A festival takes place there every year during the months of March and April. The festival is known as Nandā-melā. At the present moment the Ganges does not flow there. On the same railway line is another station, known as Bāruipura, and near this station is another place, called Āṭisārā. Formerly this village was also situated on the banks of the Ganges. One can go from this village to Pāṇihāṭī and from there to Varāha-nagara, north of Calcutta. In those days the Ganges flowed to the south of Calcutta through Kālī-ghāṭa, which is still known as Ādi-gaṅgā. From Bāruipura, the Ganges branched out and flowed through Diamond Harbor near the Mathurāpura police station. It is to be noted that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed through all these places on His way to Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.217
description: In his book known as Caitanya-maṅgala [Caitanya-bhāgavata], Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has elaborately described the Lord's passage to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> 'caitanya-maṅgale' prabhura nīlādri-gamana
> vistāri varṇiyāchena dāsa-vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:m:maṅgale]]---in the book named //Caitanya-maṅgala//; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:n:nīlādri]]-[[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:v:vistāri]]---elaborating; [[synonyms:v:varṇiyāchena]]---has described; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura.
translation: In his book known as Caitanya-maṅgala [Caitanya-bhāgavata], Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has elaborately described the Lord's passage to Jagannātha Purī.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura states that while Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed through Bengal, He passed through Āṭisārā-grāma, Varāha-grāma and Chatrabhoga. He then reached the Orissa province, where He passed through Prayāga-ghāṭa, Suvarṇarekhā, Remuṇā, Yājapura, Vaitaraṇī, Daśāśvamedha-ghāṭa, Kaṭaka, Mahānadī, Bhuvaneśvara (where there is a big lake known as Bindu-sarovara), Kamalapura and Āthāranālā. In this way, passing through all these and other places, He reached Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.218

translation: If one hears the activities of the Lord at the house of Advaita Ācārya, he will certainly very soon attain the riches of love of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.219
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation:
Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Third Chapter, describing Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's stay at the house of Advaita Ācārya, His acceptance of the sannyāsa order and observation of daily festivals at Advaita Ācārya's house, His congregationally chanting the holy name of the Lord and His feasting with all the devotees.//

text:

> śrīpāda kahe, tomāra saṅge yāba vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---the Lord inquired; [[synonyms:ś:śrīpāda]]---sir; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of You; [[synonyms:k:kothāke]]---where; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going; [[synonyms:ś:śrīpāda]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Nityānanda Prabhu replied; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---You; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---I shall go; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---toward Vṛndāvana.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was in ecstasy, and He asked where Nityānanda Prabhu was going. Nityānanda replied that He was going with Him toward Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.25
description: When the Lord asked Nityānanda Prabhu how far it was to Vṛndāvana, Nityānanda replied, "Just see! Here is the river Yamunā."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---kata dūre āche vṛndāvana
> teṅho kahena,---kara ei yamunā daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---the Lord replied; [[synonyms:k:kata]] [[synonyms:d:dūre]]---how far; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there is; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana-dhāma; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---He replied; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---just do; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]---Yamunā River; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing.
translation: When the Lord asked Nityānanda Prabhu how far it was to Vṛndāvana, Nityānanda replied, "Just see! Here is the river Yamunā."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.26
description: Saying this, Nityānanda Prabhu took Caitanya Mahāprabhu near the Ganges, and the Lord, in His ecstasy, accepted the river Ganges as the river Yamunā.
text:
> eta bali' ānila tāṅre gaṅgā-sannidhāne
> āveśe prabhura haila gaṅgāre yamunā-jñāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:etabali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:ā:ānila]]---He brought; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:sannidhāne]]---near the Ganges; [[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgāre]]---of the river Ganges; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---acceptance as the river Yamunā.
translation: Saying this, Nityānanda Prabhu took Caitanya Mahāprabhu near the Ganges, and the Lord, in His ecstasy, accepted the river Ganges as the river Yamunā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.27
description: The Lord said, "Oh, what good fortune! Now I have seen the river Yamunā." Thus thinking the Ganges to be the river Yamunā, Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to offer prayers to it.
text:
> aho bhāgya, yamunāre pāiluṅ daraśana
> eta bali' yamunāra karena stavana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ahobhāgya]]---oh, My great fortune; [[synonyms:y:yamunāre]]---of the river Yamunā; [[synonyms:p:pāiluṅ]]---I have gotten; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---vision; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---after saying this; [[synonyms:y:yamunāra]]---of the river Yamunā; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:s:stavana]]---praising.
translation: The Lord said, "Oh, what good fortune! Now I have seen the river Yamunā." Thus thinking the Ganges to be the river Yamunā, Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to offer prayers to it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.28
description: "O river Yamunā, you are the blissful spiritual water that gives love to the son of Nanda Mahārāja. You are the same as the water of the spiritual world, for you can vanquish all our offenses and the sinful reactions incurred in life. You are the creator of all auspicious things for the world. O daughter of the sun-god, kindly purify us by your pious activities."
text:
> cid-ānanda-bhānoḥ sadā nanda-sūnoḥ
> para-prema-pātrī drava-brahma-gātrī
> aghānāṁ lavitrī jagat-kṣema-dhātrī
> pavitrī-kriyān no vapur mitra-putrī
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cit]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:b:bhānoḥ]]---of the direct manifestation of spiritual energy and bliss; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:n:nanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sūnoḥ]]---of the son of Mahārāja Nanda; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:p:pātrī]]---the giver of the highest love; [[synonyms:d:drava]]-[[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:g:gātrī]]---composed of the water of the spiritual world; [[synonyms:a:aghānām]]---of all sins and offenses; [[synonyms:l:lavitrī]]---the destroyer; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣema]]-[[synonyms:d:dhātrī]]---the performer of everything auspicious for the world; [[synonyms:p:pavitrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kriyāt]]---kindly purify; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---our; [[synonyms:v:vapuḥ]]---existence; [[synonyms:m:mitra]]-[[synonyms:p:putrī]]---the daughter of the sun-god.
translation: "O river Yamunā, you are the blissful spiritual water that gives love to the son of Nanda Mahārāja. You are the same as the water of the spiritual world, for you can vanquish all our offenses and the sinful reactions incurred in life. You are the creator of all auspicious things for the world. O daughter of the sun-god, kindly purify us by your pious activities."
purport: This verse is recorded in the //Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka// (5.35), by Kavi-karṇapura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.29
description: After reciting this mantra, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered obeisances and took His bath in the Ganges. At that time He had on only one piece of underwear, for there was no second garment.
text:
> eta bali' namaskari' kaila gaṅgā-snāna
> eka kaupīna, nāhi dvitīya paridhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:etabali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:n:namaskari']]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing in the Ganges; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:k:kaupīna]]---only one piece of underwear; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there was not; [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]]---second; [[synonyms:p:paridhāna]]---garment.
translation: After reciting this mantra, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered obeisances and took His bath in the Ganges. At that time He had on only one piece of underwear, for there was no second garment.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.3
description: At the end of His twenty-fourth year, in the month of Māgha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the sannyāsa order during the waxing period of the moon.
text:
> cabbiśa vatsara-śeṣa yei māgha-māsa
> tāra śukla-pakṣe prabhu karilā sannyāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cabbiśa]]---twenty-fourth; [[synonyms:v:vatsara]]---of the year; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]---at the end; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---that; [[synonyms:m:māgha]]-[[synonyms:m:māsa]]---the month of Māgha (January and February); [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:ś:śukla]]-[[synonyms:p:pakṣe]]---in the waxing period of the moon; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---accepted; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---the //sannyāsa// order of life.
translation: At the end of His twenty-fourth year, in the month of Māgha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the sannyāsa order during the waxing period of the moon.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.30
description: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was standing there without a second garment, Śrī Advaita Ācārya arrived in a boat, bringing with Him new underwear and external garments.
text:
> hena kāle ācārya-gosāñi naukāte caḍiñā
> āila nūtana kaupīna-bahirvāsa lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:henakāle]]---at that time; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Advaita Ācārya Prabhu; [[synonyms:n:naukāte]] [[synonyms:c:caḍiñā]]---on board a boat; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---reached there; [[synonyms:n:nūtana]]---new; [[synonyms:k:kaupīna]]---underwear; [[synonyms:b:bahiḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---outer garments; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---bringing.
translation: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was standing there without a second garment, Śrī Advaita Ācārya arrived in a boat, bringing with Him new underwear and external garments.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.31
description: When Advaita Ācārya arrived, He stood before the Lord and offered His obeisances. After seeing Him, the Lord began to wonder about the entire situation.
text:
> āge ācārya āsi' rahilā namaskāra kari'
> ācārya dekhi' bale prabhu mane saṁśaya kari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---stood; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making obeisances; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---says; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---within His mind; [[synonyms:s:saṁśaya]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doubting.
translation: When Advaita Ācārya arrived, He stood before the Lord and offered His obeisances. After seeing Him, the Lord began to wonder about the entire situation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.32
description: Still in His ecstasy, the Lord asked Advaita Ācārya, "Why did You come here? How did You know that I was in Vṛndāvana?"
text:
> tumi ta' ācārya-gosāñi, ethā kene āilā
> āmi vṛndāvane, tumi ke-mate jānilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You are; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:e:ethā]]---here; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---You have come; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvane]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:k:ke]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---how; [[synonyms:j:jānilā]]---knew.
translation: Still in His ecstasy, the Lord asked Advaita Ācārya, "Why did You come here? How did You know that I was in Vṛndāvana?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.33
description: Advaita Ācārya disclosed the whole situation, telling Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Wherever You are, that is Vṛndāvana. Now it is My great fortune that You have come to the bank of the Ganges."
text:
> ācārya kahe---tumi yāhāṅ, sei vṛndāvana
> mora bhāgye gaṅgā-tīre tomāra āgamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryakahe]]---Ācārya replied; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever You are; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:b:bhāgye]]---by My great fortune; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank of the Ganges; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---Your appearance.
translation: Advaita Ācārya disclosed the whole situation, telling Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Wherever You are, that is Vṛndāvana. Now it is My great fortune that You have come to the bank of the Ganges."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.34
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "Nityānanda has cheated Me. He has brought Me to the bank of the Ganges and told Me that it was the Yamunā."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---nityānanda āmāre vañcilā
> gaṅgāke āniyā more yamunā kahilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---the Lord replied; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:ā:āmāre]]---Me; [[synonyms:v:vañcilā]]---has cheated; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgāke]]---to the bank of the Ganges; [[synonyms:ā:āniyā]]---bringing; [[synonyms:m:more]]---Me; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]---the river Yamunā; [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---informed.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "Nityānanda has cheated Me. He has brought Me to the bank of the Ganges and told Me that it was the Yamunā."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.35
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accused Nityānanda of cheating Him, Śrīla Advaita Ācārya said, "Whatever Nityānanda Prabhu has told You is not false. You have indeed just now taken Your bath in the river Yamunā."
text:
> ācārya kahe, mithyā nahe śrīpāda-vacana
> yamunāte snāna tumi karilā ekhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryakahe]]---Advaita Ācārya replied; [[synonyms:m:mithyā]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---this is not untrue; [[synonyms:ś:śrīpāda]]-[[synonyms:v:vacana]]---the words of Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:y:yamunāte]]---in the river Yamunā; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:e:ekhana]]---just now.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accused Nityānanda of cheating Him, Śrīla Advaita Ācārya said, "Whatever Nityānanda Prabhu has told You is not false. You have indeed just now taken Your bath in the river Yamunā."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.36
description: Advaita Ācārya then explained that at that spot both the Ganges and Yamunā flow together. On the western side was the Yamunā, and on the eastern side was the Ganges.
text:
> gaṅgāya yamunā vahe hañā eka-dhāra
> paścime yamunā vahe, pūrve gaṅgā-dhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gaṅgāya]]---with the river Ganges; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]---the river Yamunā; [[synonyms:v:vahe]]---flows; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---one stream; [[synonyms:p:paścime]]---on the western side; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]---the river Yamunā; [[synonyms:v:vahe]]---flows; [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---on the eastern side; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---the flow of the Ganges.
translation: Advaita Ācārya then explained that at that spot both the Ganges and Yamunā flow together. On the western side was the Yamunā, and on the eastern side was the Ganges.
purport: The Ganges and Yamunā mix at the confluence at Allahabad (Prayāga). The Yamunā flows from the western side and the Ganges from the eastern, and they merge. Since Caitanya Mahāprabhu bathed on the western side, He actually took His bath in the river Yamunā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.37
description: Advaita Ācārya then suggested that since Caitanya Mahāprabhu had taken His bath in the river Yamunā and His underwear was now wet, the Lord should change His underwear for dry garments.
text:
> paścima-dhāre yamunā vahe, tāhāṅ kaile snāna
> ārdra kaupīna chāḍi' śuṣka kara paridhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paścima]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāre]]---in the western flow; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]---the river Yamunā; [[synonyms:v:vahe]]---flows; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---You did; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing; [[synonyms:ā:ārdra]]---wet; [[synonyms:k:kaupīna]]---underwear; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:ś:śuṣka]]---dry; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---do; [[synonyms:p:paridhāna]]---putting on.
translation: Advaita Ācārya then suggested that since Caitanya Mahāprabhu had taken His bath in the river Yamunā and His underwear was now wet, the Lord should change His underwear for dry garments.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.38
description: Advaita Ācārya said, "You have been fasting continuously for three days in Your ecstasy of love for Kṛṣṇa. I therefore invite You to My home, where You may kindly take Your alms. Come with Me to My residence."
text:
> premāveśe tina dina ācha upavāsa
> āji mora ghare bhikṣā, cala mora vāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in the ecstasy of love; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---three days; [[synonyms:ā:ācha]]---You are; [[synonyms:u:upavāsa]]---fasting; [[synonyms:ā:āji]]---today; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at the house; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---alms; [[synonyms:c:cala]]---kindly come; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---to My residence.
translation: Advaita Ācārya said, "You have been fasting continuously for three days in Your ecstasy of love for Kṛṣṇa. I therefore invite You to My home, where You may kindly take Your alms. Come with Me to My residence."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.39
description: Advaita Prabhu continued, "At My home I have just cooked one palmful of rice. The vegetables are always very simple. There is no luxurious cooking-simply a little liquid vegetable and spinach."
text:
> eka-muṣṭi anna muñi kariyāchoṅ pāka
> śukhārukhā vyañjana kailuṅ, sūpa āra śāka
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:m:muṣṭi]]---one palmful; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---rice; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchoṅ]]---have done; [[synonyms:p:pāka]]---cooking; [[synonyms:ś:śukhā]]-[[synonyms:r:rukhā]]---not very luxurious; [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---vegetables; [[synonyms:k:kailuṅ]]---I have done; [[synonyms:s:sūpa]]---liquid vegetables; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:ś:śāka]]---spinach.
translation: Advaita Prabhu continued, "At My home I have just cooked one palmful of rice. The vegetables are always very simple. There is no luxurious cooking-simply a little liquid vegetable and spinach."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.4
description: After accepting the sannyāsa order, Caitanya Mahāprabhu, out of intense love for Kṛṣṇa, started for Vṛndāvana. However, He mistakenly wandered about in a trance continuously for three days in the tract of land known as Rāḍha-deśa.
text:
> sannyāsa kari' premāveśe calilā vṛndāvana
> rāḍha-deśe tina dina karilā bhramaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sannyāsakari']]---after accepting the //sannyāsa// order; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in intense love for Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---proceeded; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---toward Vṛndāvana-dhāma; [[synonyms:r:rāḍha]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in the tract of land known as Rāḍha; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---continuously for three days; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:b:bhramaṇa]]---wandering.
translation: After accepting the sannyāsa order, Caitanya Mahāprabhu, out of intense love for Kṛṣṇa, started for Vṛndāvana. However, He mistakenly wandered about in a trance continuously for three days in the tract of land known as Rāḍha-deśa.
purport: The word Rāḍha-deśa comes from the word //rāṣṭra,// or "state." From //rāṣṭra// the perverted word //rāḍha// has come. The part of Bengal on the western side of the Ganges is known as Rāḍha-deśa. Another name is Pauṇḍra-deśa or Peṅḍo-deśa. The word //peṅḍo// is a perverted form of the word //pauṇḍra.// It appears that the capital of Rāṣṭra-deśa was situated in that part of Bengal.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.40
description: Saying this, Śrī Advaita Ācārya took the Lord into the boat and brought the Lord to His residence. There Advaita Ācārya washed the feet of the Lord and was consequently very happy within.
text:
> eta bali' naukāya caḍāñā nila nija-ghara
> pāda-prakṣālana kaila ānanda-antara
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:n:naukāya]] [[synonyms:c:caḍāñā]]---making Him board the small boat; [[synonyms:n:nila]]---took; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:ghara]]---to His own residence; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:prakṣālana]]---washing the feet; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:a:antara]]---very happy within Himself.
translation: Saying this, Śrī Advaita Ācārya took the Lord into the boat and brought the Lord to His residence. There Advaita Ācārya washed the feet of the Lord and was consequently very happy within.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.41
description: All the eatables were first cooked by the wife of Advaita Ācārya. Then Śrīla Advaita Ācārya personally offered everything to Lord Viṣṇu.
text:
> prathame pāka kariyāchena ācāryāṇī
> viṣṇu-samarpaṇa kaila ācārya āpani
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prathame]]---first; [[synonyms:p:pāka]]---cooking; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchena]]---performed; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryāṇī]]---the wife of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:s:samarpaṇa]]---offering to Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āpani]]---Himself.
translation: All the eatables were first cooked by the wife of Advaita Ācārya. Then Śrīla Advaita Ācārya personally offered everything to Lord Viṣṇu.
purport: This is the ideal householder's life. The husband and wife live together, and the husband works very hard to secure paraphernalia for worshiping Lord Viṣṇu. The wife at home cooks a variety of foods for Lord Viṣṇu, and the husband offers it to the Deity. After that, //ārati// is performed, and the //prasāda// is distributed amongst family members and guests. According to the Vedic principles, there must always be a guest in a householder's house. In my childhood I have actually seen my father receive not less than four guests every day, and in those days my father's income was not very great. Nonetheless, there was no difficulty in offering //prasāda// to at least four guests every day. According to Vedic principles, a householder, before taking lunch, should go outside and shout very loudly to see if there is anyone without food. In this way he invites people to take //prasāda.// If someone comes, the householder offers him //prasāda,// and if there is not much left, he should offer his own portion to the guest. If no one responds to his call, the householder can accept his own lunch. Thus the householder's life is also a kind of austerity. Because of this, the householder's life is called the //gṛhastha-āśrama.// Although a person may live with his wife and children happily in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, he also observes the regulative principles followed in any temple. If there is no Kṛṣṇa consciousness, the householder's abode is called a //gṛhamedhī's// house. Householders in Kṛṣṇa consciousness are actually //gṛhasthas//---that is, those living in the //āśrama// with their families and children. Śrī Advaita Prabhu was an ideal //gṛhastha,// and His house was the ideal //gṛhastha-āśrama.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.42
description: All the prepared food was divided into three equal parts. One part was arranged on a metal plate for offering to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> tina ṭhāñi bhoga bāḍāila sama kari'
> kṛṣṇera bhoga bāḍāila dhātu-pātropari
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---in three places; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---cooked food; [[synonyms:b:bāḍāila]]---distributed; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---the food offered to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bāḍāila]]---was arranged; [[synonyms:d:dhātu]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]] [[synonyms:u:upari]]---on a metal plate.
translation: All the prepared food was divided into three equal parts. One part was arranged on a metal plate for offering to Lord Kṛṣṇa.
purport: The word //bāḍāila,// meaning "increased," is very significant in this verse. It is a sophisticated word used by the //gṛhasthas// in Bengal. Whenever food is prepared and we take away a portion, the food is actually decreased. But here it is the system to say //bāḍāila,// or "increased." If food is prepared for Kṛṣṇa and offered to Him and the Vaiṣṇavas, the stock is increased, never decreased.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.43
description: Of the three divisions, one was arranged on a metal plate, and the other two were arranged on plantain leaves. These leaves were not bifurcated, and they were taken from a banana tree that held at least thirty-two bunches of bananas. The two plates were filled very nicely with the kinds of food described below.
text:
> battiśā-āṭhiyā-kalāra āṅgaṭiyā pāte
> dui ṭhāñi bhoga bāḍāila bhāla mate
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:battiśā]]-[[synonyms:ā:āṭhiyā]]---producing thirty-two bunches; [[synonyms:k:kalāra]]---of a banana tree; [[synonyms:ā:āṅgaṭiyā]]---undivided; [[synonyms:p:pāte]]---on leaves; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---in two places; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---the eatables; [[synonyms:b:bāḍāila]]---arranged; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]] [[synonyms:m:mate]]---very nicely.
translation: Of the three divisions, one was arranged on a metal plate, and the other two were arranged on plantain leaves. These leaves were not bifurcated, and they were taken from a banana tree that held at least thirty-two bunches of bananas. The two plates were filled very nicely with the kinds of food described below.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.44
description: The cooked rice was a stack of very fine grains nicely cooked, and in the middle was yellow clarified butter from the milk of cows. Surrounding the stack of rice were pots made of the skins of banana trees, and in these pots were varieties of vegetables and mung dāl.
text:
> madhye pīta-ghṛta-sikta śāly-annera stūpa
> cāri-dike vyañjana-ḍoṅgā, āra mudga-sūpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in the middle; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]---yellow; [[synonyms:g:ghṛta]]-[[synonyms:s:sikta]]---wet with clarified butter; [[synonyms:ś:śāli]]-[[synonyms:a:annera]]---of very fine cooked rice; [[synonyms:s:stūpa]]---a mound; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---surrounding the mound of rice; [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]-[[synonyms:ḍ:ḍoṅgā]]---vegetable pots; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:m:mudga]]-[[synonyms:s:sūpa]]---//dāl// made of split mung.
translation: The cooked rice was a stack of very fine grains nicely cooked, and in the middle was yellow clarified butter from the milk of cows. Surrounding the stack of rice were pots made of the skins of banana trees, and in these pots were varieties of vegetables and mung dāl.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.45
description: Among the cooked vegetables were paṭolas, squash, mānakacu and a salad made with pieces of ginger and various types of spinach.
text:
> sārdraka, vāstuka-śāka vividha prakāra
> paṭola, kuṣmāṇḍa-baḍi, mānakacu āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārdraka]]---pots with ginger dishes; [[synonyms:v:vāstuka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāka]]---spinach; [[synonyms:v:vividha]]---various; [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---kinds; [[synonyms:p:paṭola]]---a kind of vegetable; [[synonyms:k:kuṣmāṇḍa]]---squash; [[synonyms:b:baḍi]]---with split //dāl//; [[synonyms:m:mānakacu]]---the root of a vegetable tree called //kacu//; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and.
translation: Among the cooked vegetables were paṭolas, squash, mānakacu and a salad made with pieces of ginger and various types of spinach.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.46
description: There was sukhta, bitter melon mixed with all kinds of vegetables, defying the taste of nectar. There were five types of bitter and pungent sukhtas.
text:
> ca-i-marica-sukhta diyā saba phala-mūle
> amṛta-nindaka pañca-vidha tikta-jhāle
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]-[[synonyms:m:marica]]---with black pepper and //ca-i// (a kind of spice); [[synonyms:s:sukhta]]---vegetables made bitter; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:p:phala]]-[[synonyms:m:mūle]]---various kinds of fruits and roots; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:n:nindaka]]---defying nectar; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]]---five kinds of; [[synonyms:t:tikta]]---bitter; [[synonyms:j:jhāle]]---and pungent.
translation: There was sukhta, bitter melon mixed with all kinds of vegetables, defying the taste of nectar. There were five types of bitter and pungent sukhtas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.47
description: Amongst the various vegetables were newly grown leaves of nimba trees fried with eggplant. The fruit known as paṭola was fried with phulabaḍi, a kind of dāl preparation first mashed and then dried in the sun. There was also a preparation known as kuṣmāṇḍa-mānacāki.
text:
> komala nimba-patra saha bhājā vārtākī
> paṭola-phula-baḍi-bhājā, kuṣmāṇḍa-mānacāki
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:komala]]---newly grown; [[synonyms:n:nimba]]-[[synonyms:p:patra]]---//nimba// leaves; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:b:bhājā]]---fried; [[synonyms:v:vārtākī]]---eggplant; [[synonyms:p:paṭola]]---with //paṭola// fruit; [[synonyms:p:phula]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍi]]---a preparation of //dāl//; [[synonyms:b:bhājā]]---fried; [[synonyms:k:kuṣmāṇḍa]]---squashes; [[synonyms:m:mānacāki]]---the food called //mānacāki.//
translation: Amongst the various vegetables were newly grown leaves of nimba trees fried with eggplant. The fruit known as paṭola was fried with phulabaḍi, a kind of dāl preparation first mashed and then dried in the sun. There was also a preparation known as kuṣmāṇḍa-mānacāki.
purport: We request our editors of cook books to add all these nice preparations described by the experienced author Śrīla Kavirāja Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.48
description: The preparation made with coconut pulp mixed with curd and rock candy was very sweet. There was a curry made of banana flowers and squash boiled in milk, all in great quantity.
text:
> nārikela-śasya, chānā, śarkarā madhura
> mochā-ghaṇṭa, dugdha-kuṣmāṇḍa, sakala pracura
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nārikela]]-[[synonyms:ś:śasya]]---the pulp of coconut; [[synonyms:c:chānā]]---curd; [[synonyms:ś:śarkarā]]---fruit sugar; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---very sweet; [[synonyms:m:mochā]]-[[synonyms:g:ghaṇṭa]]---a semisolid preparation made with banana flowers; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṣmāṇḍa]]---newly grown squash cut into pieces and boiled in milk; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:p:pracura]]---plentiful.
translation: The preparation made with coconut pulp mixed with curd and rock candy was very sweet. There was a curry made of banana flowers and squash boiled in milk, all in great quantity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.49
description: There were small cakes in sweet and sour sauce and five or six kinds of sour preparations. All the vegetables were so made that everyone present could take prasāda.
text:
> madhurāmla-baḍā, amlādi pāṅca-chaya
> sakala vyañjana kaila loke yata haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhura]]-[[synonyms:a:amla]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍā]]---sweet and sour cakes; [[synonyms:a:amla]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---sour preparations; [[synonyms:p:pāṅca]]-[[synonyms:c:chaya]]---five or six; [[synonyms:s:sakala]] [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---all vegetables; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---for the people; [[synonyms:y:yata]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---as many as there were.
translation: There were small cakes in sweet and sour sauce and five or six kinds of sour preparations. All the vegetables were so made that everyone present could take prasāda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.5
description: Passing through the tract of land known as Rāḍha-deśa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited the following verse in ecstasy.
text:
> ei śloka paḍi' prabhu bhāvera āveśe
> bhramite pavitra kaila saba rāḍha-deśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eiśloka]]---this verse; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhāvera]]---of ecstasy; [[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in a condition; [[synonyms:b:bhramite]]---wandering; [[synonyms:p:pavitra]]---purified; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:r:rāḍha]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---all of the tract of land known as Rāḍha-deśa.
translation: Passing through the tract of land known as Rāḍha-deśa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited the following verse in ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.50
description: There were soft cakes made with mung dāl, soft cakes made with ripe bananas, and soft cakes made with urad dāl. There were various kinds of sweetmeats, condensed milk mixed with rice cakes, a coconut preparation and every kind of cake desirable.
text:
> mudga-baḍā, kalā-baḍā, māṣa-baḍā, miṣṭa
> kṣīra-pulī, nārikela, yata piṭhā iṣṭa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mudga]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍā]]---soft cake made with mung; [[synonyms:k:kalā]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍā]]---soft cake made with fried banana; [[synonyms:m:māṣa]]-[[synonyms:b:baḍā]]---soft cake made with //uraddāl//; [[synonyms:m:miṣṭa]]---various kinds of sweets; [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]-[[synonyms:p:pulī]]---condensed milk mixed with rice cakes; [[synonyms:n:nārikela]]---a preparation of coconut; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all kinds of; [[synonyms:p:piṭhā]]---cakes; [[synonyms:i:iṣṭa]]---desirable.
translation: There were soft cakes made with mung dāl, soft cakes made with ripe bananas, and soft cakes made with urad dāl. There were various kinds of sweetmeats, condensed milk mixed with rice cakes, a coconut preparation and every kind of cake desirable.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.51
description: All the vegetables were served in pots made of banana leaves taken from trees producing at least thirty-two bunches of bananas. These pots were very strong and big and did not tilt or totter.
text:
> battiśā-āṭhiyā kalāra ḍoṅgā baḍa baḍa
> cale hāle nāhi,---ḍoṅgā ati baḍa daḍa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:battiśā]]-[[synonyms:ā:āṭhiyā]]---producing thirty-two bunches of bananas; [[synonyms:k:kalāra]]---of the banana tree; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍoṅgā]]---pots made of leaves; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---big; [[synonyms:c:cale]] [[synonyms:h:hāle]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---they did not tilt or totter; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍoṅgā]]---pots; [[synonyms:a:ati]]---very; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---big; [[synonyms:d:daḍa]]---strong.
translation: All the vegetables were served in pots made of banana leaves taken from trees producing at least thirty-two bunches of bananas. These pots were very strong and big and did not tilt or totter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.52
description: All around the three eating places were a hundred pots filled with various kinds of vegetables.
text:
> pañcāśa pañcāśa ḍoṅgā vyañjane pūriñā
> tina bhogera āśe pāśe rākhila dhariñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pañcāśa]] [[synonyms:p:pañcāśa]]---fifty and fifty; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍoṅgā]]---pots; [[synonyms:v:vyañjane]]---with vegetables; [[synonyms:p:pūriñā]]---filling; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:b:bhogera]]---of eating places; [[synonyms:ā:āśe]] [[synonyms:p:pāśe]]---all around; [[synonyms:r:rākhila]]---kept; [[synonyms:d:dhariñā]]---fixing.
translation: All around the three eating places were a hundred pots filled with various kinds of vegetables.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.53
description: Along with the various vegetables was sweet rice mixed with ghee. This was kept in new earthen pots. Earthen pots filled with highly condensed milk were placed in three places.
text:
> saghṛta-pāyasa nava-mṛt-kuṇḍikā bhariñā
> tina pātre ghanāvarta-dugdha rākheta dhariñā

translation: Along with the various vegetables was sweet rice mixed with ghee. This was kept in new earthen pots. Earthen pots filled with highly condensed milk were placed in three places.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.54
description: Besides the other preparations, there were chipped rice made with milk and mixed with bananas, and also white squash boiled in milk. Indeed, it is not possible to describe all the preparations that were made.
text:
> dugdha-ciḍā-kalā āra dugdha-laklakī
> yateka karila' tāhā kahite nā śaki

translation: Besides the other preparations, there were chipped rice made with milk and mixed with bananas, and also white squash boiled in milk. Indeed, it is not possible to describe all the preparations that were made.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.55
description: In two places there were earthen pots filled with another preparation made with yogurt, sandeśa [a sweetmeat made with curd] and banana. I am unable to describe it all.
text:
> dui pāśe dharila saba mṛt-kuṇḍikā bhari'
> cāṅpākalā-dadhi-sandeśa kahite nā pāri

translation: In two places there were earthen pots filled with another preparation made with yogurt, sandeśa [a sweetmeat made with curd] and banana. I am unable to describe it all.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.56
description: Upon the stack of boiled rice and all the vegetables were flowers of the tulasī trees. There were also pots filled with scented rosewater.
text:
> anna-vyañjana-upari dila tulasī-mañjarī
> tina jala-pātre suvāsita jala bhari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anna]]-[[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]-[[synonyms:u:upari]]---on top of the boiled rice and vegetables; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---placed; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]-[[synonyms:m:mañjarī]]---flowers of //tulasī//; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:p:pātre]]---waterpots; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsita]]---scented; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---water; [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---filling.
translation: Upon the stack of boiled rice and all the vegetables were flowers of the tulasī trees. There were also pots filled with scented rosewater.

description: There were three sitting places where soft cloths were placed. Thus Lord Kṛṣṇa was offered all the food, and the Lord took it very pleasantly.
text:
> tina śubhra-pīṭha, tāra upari vasana
> ei-rūpe sākṣāt kṛṣṇe karāila bhojana

translation: There were three sitting places where soft cloths were placed. Thus Lord Kṛṣṇa was offered all the food, and the Lord took it very pleasantly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.58
description: It is the system, after offering food, to perform bhoga-ārati. Advaita Prabhu asked the two brothers, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu, to come see the ārati. The two Lords and all others present went to see the ārati ceremony.
text:

> prabhu-saṅge sabe āsi' ārati dekhila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āratirakāle]]---during the time of //ārati//; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Nityānanda and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bolāila]]---He called; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the Lords; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all other people; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming there; [[synonyms:ā:ārati]]---the //ārati// ceremony; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---observed.
translation: It is the system, after offering food, to perform bhoga-ārati. Advaita Prabhu asked the two brothers, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu, to come see the ārati. The two Lords and all others present went to see the ārati ceremony.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.59
description: After ārati was performed for the Deities in the temple, Lord Kṛṣṇa was made to lie down to rest. Advaita Ācārya then came out to submit something to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> ārati kariyā kṛṣṇe karā'la śayana
> ācārya āsi' prabhure tabe kailā nivedana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āratikariyā]]---after finishing the //ārati//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:karā'la]]---made to do; [[synonyms:ś:śayana]]---lying down to rest; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---made; [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---submission.
translation: After ārati was performed for the Deities in the temple, Lord Kṛṣṇa was made to lie down to rest. Advaita Ācārya then came out to submit something to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.6
description: "[As a brāhmaṇa from Avantī-deśa said:] 'I shall cross over the insurmountable ocean of nescience by being firmly fixed in the service of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. This was approved by the previous ācāryas, who were fixed in firm devotion to the Lord, Paramātmā, the Supreme Personality of Godhead."
text:
> etāṁ sa āsthāya parātma-niṣṭhām
> adhyāsitāṁ pūrvatamair mahadbhiḥ
> ahaṁ tariṣyāmi duranta-pāraṁ
> tamo mukundāṅghri-niṣevayaiva
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:etām]]---this; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---such; [[synonyms:ā:āsthāya]]---being completely fixed in; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:n:niṣṭhām]]---devotion to the Supreme Person, Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:adhyāsitām]]---worshiped; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:t:tamaiḥ]]---by previous; [[synonyms:m:mahadbhiḥ]]---//ācāryas//; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tariṣyāmi]]---shall cross over; [[synonyms:d:duranta]]-[[synonyms:p:pāram]]---the insurmountable; [[synonyms:t:tamaḥ]]---the ocean of nescience; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅghri]]---of the lotus feet of Mukunda; [[synonyms:n:niṣevayā]]---by worship; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly.
translation: "[As a brāhmaṇa from Avantī-deśa said:] 'I shall cross over the insurmountable ocean of nescience by being firmly fixed in the service of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. This was approved by the previous ācāryas, who were fixed in firm devotion to the Lord, Paramātmā, the Supreme Personality of Godhead."
purport:
In connection with this verse, which is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.23.57), Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that of the sixty-four items required for rendering devotional service, acceptance of the symbolic marks of //sannyāsa// is a regulative principle. If one accepts the //sannyāsa// order, his main business is to devote his life completely to the service of Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa. If one does not completely devote his mind and body to the service of the Lord, he does not actually become a //sannyāsī.// It is not simply a matter of changing dress. In //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:6:1|(Bg. 6.1)]] it is also stated, //anāśritaḥ karma-phalaṁ kāryaṁ karma karoti yaḥ sa sannyāsī ca yogī ca:// one who works devotedly for the satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa is a //sannyāsī.// The dress is not //sannyāsa,// but the attitude of service to Kṛṣṇa is.

The word //parātma-niṣṭhā// means being a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa. //Parātmā,// the Supreme Person, is Kṛṣṇa. //Īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ.// Those who are completely dedicated to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa in service are actually //sannyāsīs.// As a matter of formality, the devotee accepts the //sannyāsa// dress as previous //ācāryas// did. He also accepts the three //daṇḍas.// Later Viṣṇusvāmī considered that accepting the dress of a //tridaṇḍī// was //parātma-niṣṭhā.// Therefore sincere devotees add another //daṇḍa,// the //jīva-daṇḍa,// to the three existing //daṇḍas.// The Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsī// is known as a //tridaṇḍi-sannyāsī.// The Māyāvādī //sannyāsī// accepts only one //daṇḍa,// not understanding the purpose of //tri-daṇḍa.// Later, many persons in the community of Śiva Svāmī gave up the //ātma-niṣṭhā// (devotional service) of the Lord and followed the path of Śaṅkarācārya. Instead of accepting 108 names, those in the Śiva Svāmī //sampradāya// follow the path of Śaṅkarācārya and accept the ten names of //sannyāsa.// Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the then-existing order of //sannyāsa// (namely //eka-daṇḍa//), He still recited a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// about the //tridaṇḍa-sannyāsa// accepted by the //brāhmaṇa// of Avantīpura. Indirectly He declared that within that //eka-daṇḍa,// one //daṇḍa,// four //daṇḍas// existed as one. Accepting //ekadaṇḍa-sannyāsa// without //parātma-niṣṭhā// (devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa) is not acceptable to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. In addition, according to the exact regulative principles, one should add the //jīva-daṇḍa// to the //tri-daṇḍa.// These four //daṇḍas,// bound together as one, are symbolic of unalloyed devotional service to the Lord. Because the //ekadaṇḍi-sannyāsīs// of the Māyāvāda school are not devoted to the service of Kṛṣṇa, they try to merge into the Brahman effulgence, which is a marginal position between material and spiritual existence. They accept this impersonal position as liberation. Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs,// not knowing that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was a //tridaṇḍī,// think of Caitanya Mahāprabhu as an //ekadaṇḍi-sannyāsī.// This is due to their //vivarta,// bewilderment. In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// there is no such thing as an //ekadaṇḍi-sannyāsī;// indeed, the //tridandi-sannyāsī// is accepted as the symbolic representation of the //sannyāsa// order. By citing this verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the //sannyāsa// order recommended in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.// The Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs,// who are enamored of the external energy of the Lord, cannot understand the mind of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

To date, all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, following in His footsteps, accept the //sannyāsa// order and keep the sacred thread and tuft of unshaved hair. The //ekadaṇḍi-sannyāsīs// of the Māyāvādī school give up the sacred thread and do not keep any tuft of hair. Therefore they are unable to understand the purport of //tridaṇḍa-sannyāsa,// and as such they are not inclined to dedicate their lives to the service of Mukunda. They simply think of merging into the existence of Brahman because of their disgust with material existence. The //ācāryas// who advocate the //daiva-varṇāśrama// (the social order of //cātur-varṇyam// mentioned in the //Bhagavad-gītā//) do not accept the proposition of //āsura-varṇāśrama,// which maintains that the social order of //varṇa// is indicated by birth.

The most intimate devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, namely Gadādhara Paṇḍita, accepted //tridaṇḍa-sannyāsa// and also accepted Mādhava Upādhyāya as his //tridaṇḍi-sannyāsī// disciple. It is said that from this Mādhavācārya the //sampradāya// known in western India as the Vallabhācārya //sampradāya// has begun. Śrīla Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, who is known as a //smṛty-ācārya// in the Gauḍīya-Vaiṣṇava-sampradāya, later accepted the //tridaṇḍa-sannyāsa// order from Tridaṇḍipāda Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī. Although acceptance of //tridaṇḍa-sannyāsa// is not distinctly mentioned in the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava literature, the first verse of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's //Upadeśāmṛta// advocates that one should accept the //tridaṇḍa-sannyāsa// order by controlling the six forces:

> vāco vegaṁ manasaḥ krodha-vegaṁ
> jihvā-vegam udaropastha-vegam
> etān vegān yo viṣaheta dhīraḥ
> sarvām apīmāṁ pṛthivīṁ sa śiṣyāt

"One who can control the forces of speech, mind, anger, belly, tongue and genitals is known as a //gosvāmī// and is competent to accept disciples all over the world." The followers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu never accepted the Māyāvāda order of //sannyāsa,// and for this they cannot be blamed. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted Śrīdhara Svāmī, who was a //tridaṇḍi-sannyāsī,// but the Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs,// not understanding Śrīdhara Svāmī, sometimes think that Śrīdhara Svāmī belonged to the Māyāvāda //ekadaṇḍa-sannyāsa// community. Actually this was not the case.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.60
description: Śrī Advaita Prabhu said, "My dear Lords, kindly enter this room." The two brothers, Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu, then came forward to take the prasāda.
text:
> gṛhera bhitare prabhu karuna gamana
> dui bhāi āilā tabe karite bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gṛherabhitare]]---within the room; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karuna]]---kindly do; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---entering; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---the two brothers, Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---to partake of the //prasāda.//
translation: Śrī Advaita Prabhu said, "My dear Lords, kindly enter this room." The two brothers, Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu, then came forward to take the prasāda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.61
description: When Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu went to accept the prasāda, They both called Mukunda and Haridāsa to come with Them. However, Mukunda and Haridāsa, both with folded hands, spoke as follows.
text:
> mukunda, haridāsa,---dui prabhu bolāila
> yoḍa-hāte dui-jana kahite lāgila
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the two Lords; [[synonyms:b:bolāila]]---called for; [[synonyms:y:yoḍa]]-[[synonyms:h:hāte]]---with folded hands; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons; [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began to say.
translation: When Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu went to accept the prasāda, They both called Mukunda and Haridāsa to come with Them. However, Mukunda and Haridāsa, both with folded hands, spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.62
description: When Mukunda was called for, he submitted, "My dear sir, I have something to do that is not yet finished. Later I shall accept the prasāda, so You two Prabhus should now please enter the room."
text:
> mukunda kahe---mora kichu kṛtya nāhi sare
> pāche muñi prasāda pāmu, tumi yāha ghare
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukundakahe]]---Mukunda said; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---of me; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:k:kṛtya]]---to perform; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:s:sare]]---not yet finished; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---later; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---//prasāda//; [[synonyms:p:pāmu]]---shall accept; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:y:yāha]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---You both kindly enter the room.
translation: When Mukunda was called for, he submitted, "My dear sir, I have something to do that is not yet finished. Later I shall accept the prasāda, so You two Prabhus should now please enter the room."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.63
description: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "I am the most sinful and lowest among men. Later I shall eat one palmful of prasāda while waiting outside."
text:
> haridāsa kahe---muñi pāpiṣṭha adhama
> bāhire eka muṣṭi pāche karimu bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Haridāsa said; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:p:pāpiṣṭha]]---sinful; [[synonyms:a:adhama]]---the lowest of men; [[synonyms:b:bāhire]]---outside; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:m:muṣṭi]]---palmful; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---later; [[synonyms:k:karimu]]---I shall do; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eating.
translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "I am the most sinful and lowest among men. Later I shall eat one palmful of prasāda while waiting outside."
purport: Although the Hindus and Muslims lived together in a very friendly manner, still there were distinctions between them. The Muslims were considered //yavanas,// or low-born, and whenever a Muslim was invited, he would be fed outside of the house. Although personally called by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu to take //prasāda// with Them, still, out of great humility, Haridāsa Ṭhākura submitted, "I shall take the //prasāda// outside of the house." Although Haridāsa Ṭhākura was an exalted Vaiṣṇava accepted by Advaita Ācārya, Nityānanda Prabhu and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, nonetheless, in order not to disturb social tranquillity, he humbly kept himself in the position of a Muslim, outside the jurisdiction of the Hindu community. Therefore he proposed to take //prasāda// outside the house. Although he was in an exalted position and equal to other great Vaiṣṇavas, he considered himself a //pāpiṣṭha,// a most sinful man, and //adhama,// the lowest among men. Although a Vaiṣṇava may be very much advanced spiritually, he keeps himself externally humble and submissive.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.64
description: Advaita Ācārya took Lord Nityānanda Prabhu and Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu within the room, and the two Lords saw the arrangement of the prasāda. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was especially very much pleased.
text:
> dui prabhu lañā ācārya gelā bhitara ghare
> prasāda dekhiyā prabhura ānanda antare
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:duiprabhu]]---the two //prabhus// (Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu); [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---with; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:b:bhitara]]---within; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---the room; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---the //prasāda//; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]] [[synonyms:a:antare]]---was very pleased within Himself.
translation: Advaita Ācārya took Lord Nityānanda Prabhu and Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu within the room, and the two Lords saw the arrangement of the prasāda. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was especially very much pleased.
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was pleased because He saw how nicely so many varieties of food were prepared for Kṛṣṇa. Actually all kinds of //prasāda// are prepared for Kṛṣṇa, not for the people, but the devotees partake of //prasāda// with great pleasure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.65
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu approved of all the methods employed in cooking and offering food to Kṛṣṇa. Indeed, He was so pleased that He said, "Frankly, I will personally take the lotus feet of anyone who can offer Kṛṣṇa such nice food and place those lotus feet on My head birth after birth."
text:
> aiche anna ye kṛṣṇake karāya bhojana
> janme janme śire dharoṅ tāṅhāra caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in this way; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---the eatables; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇake]]---unto Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---made to do; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eating; [[synonyms:j:janme]] [[synonyms:j:janme]]---birth after birth; [[synonyms:ś:śire]]---on My head; [[synonyms:d:dharoṅ]]---I keep; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---his; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---lotus feet.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu approved of all the methods employed in cooking and offering food to Kṛṣṇa. Indeed, He was so pleased that He said, "Frankly, I will personally take the lotus feet of anyone who can offer Kṛṣṇa such nice food and place those lotus feet on My head birth after birth."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.66
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered the room, He saw three divisions of food, and He knew that all of these were meant for Kṛṣṇa. However, He did not understand the intentions of Advaita Ācārya.
text:
> prabhu jāne tina bhoga---kṛṣṇera naivedya
> ācāryera manaḥ-kathā nahe prabhura vedya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhujāne]]---the Lord knows; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---three divisions of //bhoga//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:n:naivedya]]---offerings to Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]]---of Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---the intentions; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---to the Lord; [[synonyms:v:vedya]]---understandable.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered the room, He saw three divisions of food, and He knew that all of these were meant for Kṛṣṇa. However, He did not understand the intentions of Advaita Ācārya.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura states that one of these servings was offered in a metal dish and was meant for Kṛṣṇa, whereas the other two were placed on big banana leaves. The offering on the metal plate was personally offered by Advaita Ācārya to Kṛṣṇa. The other two servings, on banana leaves, were to be accepted by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Lord Nityānanda. That was Advaita Ācārya's intention, but He did not disclose this to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Thus when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the food offered in three places, He thought that all of it was meant for Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.67
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Let Us sit down in these three places, and We shall take prasāda." However, Advaita Ācārya said, "I shall distribute the prasāda."
text:
> prabhu bale---vaisa tine kariye bhojana
> ācārya kahe---āmi kariba pariveśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhubale]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:v:vaisa]]---sit down; [[synonyms:t:tine]]---in the three places; [[synonyms:k:kariye]]---do; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eating; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Advaita Ācārya replied; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:k:kariba]] [[synonyms:p:pariveśana]]---I shall distribute.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Let Us sit down in these three places, and We shall take prasāda." However, Advaita Ācārya said, "I shall distribute the prasāda."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.68
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thought that all three servings were meant for distribution; therefore He asked for another two banana leaves, saying, "Let Us have a very little quantity of vegetable and rice."
text:
> kon sthāne vasiba, āra āna dui pāta
> alpa kari' āni' tāhe deha vyañjana bhāta
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kon]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]] [[synonyms:v:vasiba]]---where shall We sit down; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---other; [[synonyms:ā:āna]]---bring; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:p:pāta]]---two leaves; [[synonyms:a:alpa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making a small quantity; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:t:tāhe]]---on that; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---give; [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---vegetables; [[synonyms:b:bhāta]]---and boiled rice.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thought that all three servings were meant for distribution; therefore He asked for another two banana leaves, saying, "Let Us have a very little quantity of vegetable and rice."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.69
description: Advaita Ācārya said, "Just sit down here on these seats." Catching Their hands, He sat Them both down.
text:
> ācārya kahe---vaisa doṅhe piṅḍira upare
> eta bali' hāte dhari' vasāila duṅhāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryakahe]]---Advaita Ācārya said; [[synonyms:v:vaisa]]---sit down; [[synonyms:d:doṅhe]]---You two; [[synonyms:p:piṅḍira]] [[synonyms:u:upare]]---on the planks of wood; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:h:hāte]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching Their hands; [[synonyms:v:vasāila]] [[synonyms:d:duṅhāre]]---sat the two Lords down.
translation: Advaita Ācārya said, "Just sit down here on these seats." Catching Their hands, He sat Them both down.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.7
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu approved the purport of this verse on account of the determination of the mendicant devotee to engage in the service of Lord Mukunda. He gave His approval of this verse, indicating that it was very good.
text:
> prabhu kahe---sādhu ei bhikṣura vacana
> mukunda sevana-vrata kaila nirdhāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]---very much purified; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣura]]---of the mendicant; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---words; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]-[[synonyms:v:vrata]]---decision to serve; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:n:nirdhāraṇa]]---indication.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu approved the purport of this verse on account of the determination of the mendicant devotee to engage in the service of Lord Mukunda. He gave His approval of this verse, indicating that it was very good.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.70
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "It is not proper for a sannyāsī to eat such a variety of foods. If he does, how can he control his senses?"
text:
> prabhu kahe---sannyāsīra bhakṣya nahe upakaraṇa
> ihā khāile kaiche haya indriya vāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]]---by a //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:b:bhakṣya]]---to be eaten; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---this is not; [[synonyms:u:upakaraṇa]]---varieties of food; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:k:khāile]]---if eating; [[synonyms:k:kaiche]]---how; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:i:indriya]]---senses; [[synonyms:v:vāraṇa]]---controlling.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "It is not proper for a sannyāsī to eat such a variety of foods. If he does, how can he control his senses?"
purport: The word //upakaraṇa// indicates a variety of foods, such as //dāl,// vegetables and other varieties of possible dishes that one can eat very nicely with rice. It is not proper, however, for a //sannyāsī// to eat such palatable dishes. If he did so, he would not be able to control his senses. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not encourage //sannyāsīs// to eat very palatable dishes, for the whole Vaiṣṇava cult is //vairāgya-vidyā,// as renounced as possible. Caitanya Mahāprabhu also advised Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī not to eat very palatable dishes, wear very nice garments or talk on mundane subjects. These things are all prohibited for those in the renounced order. A devotee does not accept anything to eat that is not first offered to Kṛṣṇa. All the rich foods offered to Kṛṣṇa are given to the //gṛhasthas,// the householders. There are many nice things offered to Kṛṣṇa-garlands, bedsteads, nice ornaments, nice food and even nicely prepared pan, betel nuts---but a humble Vaiṣṇava, thinking his body material and nasty, does not accept such preparations for himself. He thinks that by accepting such things he will offend the lotus feet of the Lord. Those who are //sahajiyās// cannot understand what Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu meant when He asked Advaita Ācārya to bring two separate leaves and give a small quantity of the //prasāda// to Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.71
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not accept the food that had already been served, Advaita Ācārya said, "Please give up Your concealment. I know what You are, and I know the confidential meaning of Your accepting the sannyāsa order."

translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not accept the food that had already been served, Advaita Ācārya said, "Please give up Your concealment. I know what You are, and I know the confidential meaning of Your accepting the sannyāsa order."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.74
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I will not be able to eat so much food, and it is not the duty of a sannyāsī to leave remnants."

> prabhu bale---eta anna nāriba khāite
> sannyāsīra dharma nahe ucchiṣṭa rākhite
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhubale]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:e:eta]]---so much; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---eatables; [[synonyms:n:nāriba]]---I will not be able; [[synonyms:k:khāite]]---to eat; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]]---of a //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:d:dharma]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---it is not the duty; [[synonyms:u:ucchiṣṭa]]---remnants of food; [[synonyms:r:rākhite]]---to keep.
translation:
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I will not be able to eat so much food, and it is not the duty of a sannyāsī to leave remnants."


According to //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.18.19):

> bahir jalāśayaṁ gatvā
> tatopaspṛśya vāg-yataḥ
> vibhajya pāvitaṁ śeṣaṁ
> bhuñjītāśeṣam āhṛtam

"A //sannyāsī// should take whatever edibles he gets from a householder's house, outside near some lake or river, and after offering the food to Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the sun (three divisions), he should eat the entire offering and not leave anything for others to eat."

translation: In this connection Advaita Ācārya referred to Caitanya Mahāprabhu's eating at Jagannātha Purī. Lord Jagannātha and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are identical. Advaita Ācārya pointed out that at Jagannātha Purī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ate fifty-four times a day, and each time He ate many hundreds of pots of food.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.8
description: The real purpose of accepting sannyāsa is to dedicate oneself to the service of Mukunda. By serving Mukunda, one can actually be liberated from the bondage of material existence.
text:
> parātma-niṣṭhā-mātra veṣa-dhāraṇa
> mukunda-sevāya haya saṁsāra-tāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:n:niṣṭhā]]-[[synonyms:m:mātra]]---only for the determination to serve Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:veṣa]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāraṇa]]---changing the dress; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]-[[synonyms:s:sevāya]]---by serving Mukunda; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]-[[synonyms:t:tāraṇa]]---liberation from this materiai bondage.
translation: The real purpose of accepting sannyāsa is to dedicate oneself to the service of Mukunda. By serving Mukunda, one can actually be liberated from the bondage of material existence.
purport: In this connection, Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the //sannyāsa// order and recommended the determination of the Avantīpura //bhikṣu// to engage in the service of Mukunda. He accepted the //brāhmaṇa's// version due to his determination to serve Mukunda. The //sannyāsī// dress is actually an attraction for material formality. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not like such formality, but He wanted the essence of it-service to Mukunda. Such determination in any condition is //parātma-niṣṭhā.// That is required. The conclusion is that the //sannyāsa// order depends not on the dress but the determination to serve Mukunda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 3.85
description: Advaita Ācārya said, "You are a reject paramahaṁsa, and You have accepted the renounced order of life just to fill up Your belly. I can understand that Your business is to give trouble to brāhmaṇas."
text:
> bhraṣṭa avadhūta tumi, udara bharite
> sannyāsa la-iyācha, bujhi, brāhmaṇa daṇḍite
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhraṣṭa]] [[synonyms:a:avadhūta]]---reject //paramahaṁsa//; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:u:udara]] [[synonyms:b:bharite]]---to fill Your belly; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]] [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iyācha]]---You have accepted the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:b:bujhi]]---I understand; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]] [[synonyms:d:daṇḍite]]---to give trouble to a //brāhmaṇa.//
translation: Advaita Ācārya said, "You are a reject paramahaṁsa, and You have accepted the renounced order of life just to fill up Your belly. I can understand that Your business is to give trouble to brāhmaṇas."
purport:
There is always a difference of opinion between a //smārta-brāhmaṇa// and a Vaiṣṇava //gosvāmī.// There are even //smārta// opinions and Vaiṣṇava //gosvāmī// opinions available in astrological and astronomical calculations. By calling Nityānanda Prabhu a //bhraṣṭa avadhūta// (a rejected //paramahaṁsa//), Advaita Ācārya Prabhu in a sense accepted Nityānanda Prabhu as a //paramahaṁsa.// In other words, Nityānanda Prabhu had nothing to do with the rules governing //smārta-brāhmaṇas.// Thus under pretense of condemning Him, Advaita Ācārya was actually praising Him. In the //avadhūta// stage, the //paramahaṁsa// stage, which is the supermost stage, one may appear to be //viṣayī,// on the platform of sense gratification, but in actuality he has nothing to do with sense gratification. At that stage, a person sometimes accepts the symptoms and dress of a //sannyāsī// and sometimes does not. Sometimes he dresses like a householder. We should know, however, that these are all joking words between Advaita Ācārya and Nityānanda Prabhu. They are not to be taken as insults.

In Khaḍadaha, sometimes people misunderstood Nityānanda Prabhu to belong to the //śākta-sampradāya,// whose philosophy is //antaḥ śāktaḥ bahiḥ śaivaḥ sabhāyāṁ vaiṣṇavo mataḥ.// According to the //śākta-sampradāya,// a person called //kaulāvadhūta// thinks materially while externally appearing to be a great devotee of Lord Śiva. When such a person is in an assembly of Vaiṣṇavas, he appears like a Vaiṣṇava. Actually Nityānanda Prabhu did not belong to such a community. Nityānanda Prabhu was always a //brahmacārī// of a //sannyāsī// of the //vaidika// order. Actually He was a //paramahaṁsa.// Sometimes He is accepted to be a disciple of Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha. If He is so accepted, Nityānanda Prabhu belonged to the Madhva-sampradāya. He did not belong to the //tāntrika-sampradāya// of Bengal.
