translation: Even though one may not like it, reputation, as ordained by providence, comes to him. Indeed, one's transcendental reputation is known throughout the entire world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.147
description: Being afraid of his reputation [pratiṣṭhā], Mādhavendra Purī fled from Remuṇā. But the reputation brought by love of Godhead is so sublime that it goes along with the devotee, as if following him.
text:
> pratiṣṭhāra bhaye purī gelā palāñā
> kṛṣṇa-preme pratiṣṭhā cale saṅge gaḍāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pratiṣṭhāra]] [[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---in fear of reputation; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went away; [[synonyms:p:palāñā]]---fleeing; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:preme]]---in love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pratiṣṭhā]]---reputation; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---goes; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---simultaneously; [[synonyms:g:gaḍāñā]]---gliding down.
translation: Being afraid of his reputation [pratiṣṭhā], Mādhavendra Purī fled from Remuṇā. But the reputation brought by love of Godhead is so sublime that it goes along with the devotee, as if following him.
purport: Almost all the conditioned souls within the material world are envious. Jealous people generally turn against one who automatically attains some reputation. This is natural for jealous people. Consequently, when a devotee is fit to receive worldly reputation, he is envied by many people. This is quite natural. When a person, out of humility, does not desire fame, people generally think him quite humble and consequently give him all kinds of fame. Actually a Vaiṣṇava does not hanker after fame or a great reputation. Mādhavendra Purī, the king of Vaiṣṇavas, bore his reputation, but he wanted to keep himself outside of the vision of the general populace. He wanted to cover his real identity as a great devotee of the Lord, but when people saw him overwhelmed in the ecstasy of love of Godhead, they naturally gave credit to him. Actually a first-class reputation is due Mādhavendra Purī because he was a most confidential devotee of the Lord. Sometimes a //sahajiyā// presents himself as being void of desires for reputation (//pratiṣṭhā//) in order to become famous as a humble man. Such people cannot actually attain the platform of celebrated Vaiṣṇavas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.148
description: Mādhavendra Purī wanted to leave Jagannātha Purī because the people were honoring him as a great devotee; however, this threatened to hinder his collecting sandalwood for the Gopāla Deity.
text:
> yadyapi udvega haila palāite mana
> ṭhākurera candana-sādhana ha-ila bandhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:u:udvega]]---anxiety; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:palāite]]---to go away; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākurera]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---of the sandalwood; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---the collecting; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:b:bandhana]]---bondage.
translation: Mādhavendra Purī wanted to leave Jagannātha Purī because the people were honoring him as a great devotee; however, this threatened to hinder his collecting sandalwood for the Gopāla Deity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.149
description: Śrī Mādhavendra Purī told all the servants of Lord Jagannātha and all the great devotees there the story of the appearance of Śrī Gopāla.
text:
> jagannāthera sevaka yata, yateka mahānta
> sabāke kahila purī gopāla-vṛttānta
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannāthera]] [[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---the servants of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:y:yateka]] [[synonyms:m:mahānta]]---all respectable devotees; [[synonyms:s:sabāke]]---unto everyone; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---told; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛttānta]]---the narration of Gopāla.
translation: Śrī Mādhavendra Purī told all the servants of Lord Jagannātha and all the great devotees there the story of the appearance of Śrī Gopāla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.15
description: When the Deity's helmet fell upon His head, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very pleased, and thus He chanted and danced in various ways with His devotees.
text:
> cūḍā pāñā mahāprabhura ānandita mana
> bahu nṛtya-gīta kaila lañā bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cūḍāpāñā]]---getting the helmet; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---pleased; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---various kinds; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]---dancing and chanting; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---with; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees.
translation: When the Deity's helmet fell upon His head, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very pleased, and thus He chanted and danced in various ways with His devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.150
description: When all the devotees at Jagannātha Purī heard that the Gopāla Deity wanted sandalwood, in great pleasure they all endeavored to collect it.
text:
> gopāla candana māge,---śuni' bhakta-gaṇa
> ānande candana lāgi' karila yatana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Lord Gopāla at Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood; [[synonyms:m:māge]]---wants; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in great pleasure; [[synonyms:c:candana]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for sandalwood; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---made; [[synonyms:y:yatana]]---endeavor.
translation: When all the devotees at Jagannātha Purī heard that the Gopāla Deity wanted sandalwood, in great pleasure they all endeavored to collect it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.151
description: Those who were acquainted with government officers met with them and begged for camphor and sandalwood, which they collected.
text:
> rāja-pātra-sane yāra yāra paricaya
> tāre māgi' karpūra-candana karilā sañcaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---government officers; [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with; [[synonyms:y:yāra]] [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whoever; [[synonyms:p:paricaya]]---had acquaintance; [[synonyms:t:tāre]] [[synonyms:m:māgi']]---begging them; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]-[[synonyms:c:candana]]---camphor and sandalwood; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---made; [[synonyms:s:sañcaya]]---collection.
translation: Those who were acquainted with government officers met with them and begged for camphor and sandalwood, which they collected.
purport: It appears that //malayaja-candana// (sandalwood) and camphor were used for the Jagannātha Deity. The camphor was used in His //ārātrika,// and the sandalwood was used to smear His body. Both these items were under government control; therefore the devotees had to meet with the government officials. Informing them of all the details, they attained permission to take the sandalwood and camphor outside Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.152
description: One brāhmaṇa and one servant were given to Mādhavendra Purī just to carry the sandalwood. He was also given the necessary traveling expenses.
text:
> eka vipra, eka sevaka, candana vahite
> purī-gosāñira saṅge dila sambala-sahite
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ekavipra]]---one //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---one servant; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---the sandalwood; [[synonyms:v:vahite]]---to carry; [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:s:sambala]]-[[synonyms:s:sahite]]---with the necessary expenditure.
translation: One brāhmaṇa and one servant were given to Mādhavendra Purī just to carry the sandalwood. He was also given the necessary traveling expenses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.153
description: To get past the toll collectors along the way, Mādhavendra Purī was supplied with the necessary release papers from government officers. The papers were placed in his hand.
text:
> ghāṭī-dānī chāḍāite rāja-pātra dvāre
> rāja-lekhā kari' dila purī-gosāñira kare
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:ghāṭī]]-[[synonyms:d:dānī]]---from the toll collectors; [[synonyms:c:chāḍāite]]---to get release; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---papers showing governmental sanction; [[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---at the gates; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:l:lekhā]]---governmental permission; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---delivered; [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Purī Gosāñi, Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---into the hand.
translation: To get past the toll collectors along the way, Mādhavendra Purī was supplied with the necessary release papers from government officers. The papers were placed in his hand.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.154
description: In this way Mādhavendra Purī started for Vṛndāvana with the burden of sandalwood, and after some days he again reached the village of Remuṇā and the Gopīnātha temple there.
text:
> calila mādhava-purī candana lañā
> kata-dine remuṇāte uttarila giyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:calila]]---proceeded; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:c:candana]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking the sandalwood; [[synonyms:k:kata]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---after some days; [[synonyms:r:remuṇāte]]---at the same temple of Remuṇā; [[synonyms:u:uttarila]]---reached; [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---going.
translation: In this way Mādhavendra Purī started for Vṛndāvana with the burden of sandalwood, and after some days he again reached the village of Remuṇā and the Gopīnātha temple there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.155
description: When Mādhavendra Purī reached the temple of Gopīnātha, he offered his respectful obeisances many times at the lotus feet of the Lord. In the ecstasy of love, he began to dance and sing without cessation.
text:
> gopīnātha-caraṇe kaila bahu namaskāra
> premāveśe nṛtya-gīta karilā apāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the lotus feet of Lord Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---many; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in the ecstasy of love; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]---dancing and chanting; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---performed; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimitedly.
translation: When Mādhavendra Purī reached the temple of Gopīnātha, he offered his respectful obeisances many times at the lotus feet of the Lord. In the ecstasy of love, he began to dance and sing without cessation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.156
description: When the priest of Gopīnātha saw Mādhavendra Purī again, he offered all respects to him and, giving him the sweet rice prasāda, made him eat.
text:
> purī dekhi' sevaka saba sammāna karila
> kṣīra-prasāda diyā tāṅre bhikṣā karāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purī]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---by seeing Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---the priest or servant; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:s:sammāna]]---all respects; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---offered; [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---sweet rice //prasāda//; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---offering; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---made to eat.
translation: When the priest of Gopīnātha saw Mādhavendra Purī again, he offered all respects to him and, giving him the sweet rice prasāda, made him eat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.157
description: Mādhavendra Purī took rest that night in the temple, but toward the end of the night he had another dream.
text:
> sei rātre devālaye karila śayana
> śeṣa-rātri haile purī dekhila svapana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:r:rātre]]---on that night; [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ālaye]]---in the temple; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:ś:śayana]]---sleeping; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]-[[synonyms:r:rātri]]---at the end of the night; [[synonyms:h:haile]]---when it was; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---saw; [[synonyms:s:svapana]]---a dream.
translation: Mādhavendra Purī took rest that night in the temple, but toward the end of the night he had another dream.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.158
description: Mādhavendra Purī dreamed that Gopāla came before him and said, "O Mādhavendra Purī, I have already received all the sandalwood and camphor.
text:
> gopāla āsiyā kahe,---śuna he mādhava
> karpūra-candana āmi pāilāma saba
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the Deity of Gopāla; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:h:he]]---O; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]-[[synonyms:c:candana]]---the camphor and sandalwood; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:p:pāilāma]]---have received; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all.
translation: Mādhavendra Purī dreamed that Gopāla came before him and said, "O Mādhavendra Purī, I have already received all the sandalwood and camphor.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.159
description: "Now just grind all the sandalwood together with the camphor and then smear the pulp on the body of Gopīnātha daily until it is finished.
text:
> karpūra-sahita ghaṣi' e-saba candana
> gopīnāthera aṅge nitya karaha lepana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]-[[synonyms:s:sahita]]---with the camphor; [[synonyms:g:ghaṣi']]---grinding; [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all this; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood; [[synonyms:g:gopīnāthera]]---of Śrī Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---on the body; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---daily; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---do; [[synonyms:l:lepana]]---smearing.
translation: "Now just grind all the sandalwood together with the camphor and then smear the pulp on the body of Gopīnātha daily until it is finished.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.16
description: All the servants of the Deity were struck with wonder due to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's intense love, His exquisite beauty and His transcendental qualities.
text:
> prabhura prabhāva dekhi' prema-rūpa-guṇa
> vismita ha-ilā gopīnāthera dāsa-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:p:prabhāva]]---the influence; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---His beauty; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---and His qualities; [[synonyms:v:vismita]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became struck with wonder; [[synonyms:g:gopīnāthera]]---of the Gopīnātha Deity; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the servants.
translation: All the servants of the Deity were struck with wonder due to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's intense love, His exquisite beauty and His transcendental qualities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.160
description: "There is no difference between My body and Gopīnātha's body. They are one and the same. Therefore if you smear the sandalwood pulp on the body of Gopīnātha, you will naturally also smear it on My body. Thus the temperature of My body will be reduced.
text:
> gopīnātha āmāra se eka-i aṅga haya
> iṅhāke candana dile habe mora tāpa-kṣaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]---Lord Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---one; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---body; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāke]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:c:candana]] [[synonyms:d:dile]]---in offering this //candana//; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:t:tāpa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaya]]---reduction of temperature.
translation: "There is no difference between My body and Gopīnātha's body. They are one and the same. Therefore if you smear the sandalwood pulp on the body of Gopīnātha, you will naturally also smear it on My body. Thus the temperature of My body will be reduced.
purport: Gopāla was situated in Vṛndāvana, which was far from Remuṇā. In those days, one had to pass through provinces governed by the Muslims, who sometimes hindered travelers. Considering the trouble of His devotee, Lord Gopāla, the greatest well-wisher of His devotees, ordered Mādhavendra Purī to smear the sandalwood pulp on the body of Gopīnātha, which was nondifferent from the body of Gopāla. In this way the Lord relieved Mādhavendra Purī from trouble and inconvenience.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.161
description: "You should not hesitate to act according to My order. Believing in Me, just do what is needed."
text:
> dvidhā nā bhāviha, nā kariha kichu mane
> viśvāsa kari' candana deha āmāra vacane
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dvidhā]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:b:bhāviha]]---do not hesitate; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do not do; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---anything; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:v:viśvāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---believing Me; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---offer; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:v:vacane]]---under My order.
translation: "You should not hesitate to act according to My order. Believing in Me, just do what is needed."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.162
description: After giving these instructions, Gopāla disappeared, and Mādhavendra Purī awoke. He immediately called for all the servants of Gopīnātha, and they came before him.
text:
> eta bali' gopāla gela, gosāñi jāgilā
> gopīnāthera sevaka-gaṇe ḍākiyā ānilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the Deity of Gopāla; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---disappeared; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]] [[synonyms:j:jāgilā]]---Mādhavendra Purī awoke; [[synonyms:g:gopīnāthera]]---of Lord Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:s:sevaka]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---to the servitors; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍākiyā]]---calling; [[synonyms:ā:ānilā]]---brought them.
translation: After giving these instructions, Gopāla disappeared, and Mādhavendra Purī awoke. He immediately called for all the servants of Gopīnātha, and they came before him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.163
description: Mādhavendra Purī said, "Smear the body of Gopīnātha with this camphor and sandalwood I have brought for Gopāla in Vṛndāvana. Do this regularly every day.
text:
> prabhura ājñā haila,---ei karpūra-candana
> gopīnāthera aṅge nitya karaha lepana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was an order of the Lord; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]---camphor; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---and sandalwood; [[synonyms:g:gopīnāthera]] [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---on the body of Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]---daily; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---do; [[synonyms:l:lepana]]---smearing.
translation: Mādhavendra Purī said, "Smear the body of Gopīnātha with this camphor and sandalwood I have brought for Gopāla in Vṛndāvana. Do this regularly every day.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.164
description: "If the sandalwood pulp is smeared over the body of Gopīnātha, then Gopāla will be cooled. After all, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is completely independent; His order is all-powerful."
text:
> iṅhāke candana dile, gopāla ha-ibe śītala
> svatantra īśvara---tāṅra ājñā se prabala
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṅhāke]]---unto Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:c:candana]] [[synonyms:d:dile]]---when sandalwood will be given; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Lord Gopāla in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ibe]]---will become; [[synonyms:ś:śītala]]---cool; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]] [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the most independent Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:p:prabala]]---powerful.
translation: "If the sandalwood pulp is smeared over the body of Gopīnātha, then Gopāla will be cooled. After all, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is completely independent; His order is all-powerful."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.165
description: The servants of Gopīnātha became very pleased to hear that in the summer all the sandalwood pulp would be used to anoint the body of Gopīnātha.
text:
> grīṣma-kāle gopīnātha paribe candana
> śuni' ānandita haila sevakera mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:grīṣma]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in the summer; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]---Lord Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:p:paribe]]---will put on; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood pulp; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---pleased; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:s:sevakera]]---of the servants; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds.
translation: The servants of Gopīnātha became very pleased to hear that in the summer all the sandalwood pulp would be used to anoint the body of Gopīnātha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.166
description: Mādhavendra Purī said, "These two assistants will regularly grind the sandalwood, and you should also get two other people to help. I shall pay their salary."
text:
> purī kahe,---ei dui ghaṣibe candana
> āra janā-dui deha, diba ye vetana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purī]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Mādhavendra Purī said; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]]---these two assistants; [[synonyms:g:ghaṣibe]]---will grind; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---the sandalwood; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:j:janā]]-[[synonyms:d:dui]]---two men; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---apply; [[synonyms:d:diba]]---I shall pay; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vetana]]---salary.
translation: Mādhavendra Purī said, "These two assistants will regularly grind the sandalwood, and you should also get two other people to help. I shall pay their salary."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.167
description: In this way Gopīnāthajī was supplied ground sandalwood pulp daily. The servants of Gopīnātha were very pleased with this.
text:
> ei mata candana deya pratyaha ghaṣiyā
> parāya sevaka saba ānanda kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood; [[synonyms:d:deya]]---gives; [[synonyms:p:pratyaha]]---daily; [[synonyms:g:ghaṣiyā]]---grinding; [[synonyms:p:parāya]]---caused to put on; [[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---servants; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of it; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---feeling.
translation: In this way Gopīnāthajī was supplied ground sandalwood pulp daily. The servants of Gopīnātha were very pleased with this.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.168
description: In this way the sandalwood pulp was smeared over the body of Gopīnātha until the whole stock was finished. Mādhavendra Purī stayed there until that time.

> pratyaha candana parāya, yāvat haila anta
> tathāya rahila purī tāvat paryanta
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pratyaha]]---daily; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood pulp; [[synonyms:p:parāya]]---smears over the body; [[synonyms:y:yāvat]]---until; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:a:anta]]---an end; [[synonyms:t:tathāya]]---there; [[synonyms:r:rahila]]---remained; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:t:tāvat]]---that time; [[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---until.
translation: In this way the sandalwood pulp was smeared over the body of Gopīnātha until the whole stock was finished. Mādhavendra Purī stayed there until that time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.169
description: At the end of summer Mādhavendra Purī returned to Jagannātha Purī, where he remained with great pleasure during the whole period of Cāturmāsya.
text:
> grīṣma-kāla-ante punaḥ nīlācale gelā
> nīlācale cāturmāsya ānande rahilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:grīṣma]]-[[synonyms:k:kāla]]---of the summer season; [[synonyms:a:ante]]---at the end; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---in Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:c:cātur]]-[[synonyms:m:māsya]]---the four months for vows; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in great pleasure; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained.
translation: At the end of summer Mādhavendra Purī returned to Jagannātha Purī, where he remained with great pleasure during the whole period of Cāturmāsya.
purport: The Cāturmāsya period begins in the month of Āṣāḍha (June-July) from the day of Ekādaśī called Śayanā-ekādaśī, in the fortnight of the waxing moon. The period ends in the month of Kārtika (October-November) on the Ekādaśī day known as Utthānā-ekādaśī, in the fortnight of the waxing moon. This four-month period is known as Cāturmāsya. Some Vaiṣṇavas also observe it from the full-moon day of Āṣāḍha until the full-moon day of Kārtika. That is also a period of four months. This period, calculated by the lunar months, is called Cāturmāsya, but others also observe Cāturmāsya according to the solar month from Śrāvaṇa to Kārtika. The whole period, either lunar or solar, takes place during the rainy season. Cāturmāsya should be observed by all sections of the population. It does not matter whether one is a //gṛhastha// or a //sannyāsī.// The observance is obligatory for all //āśramas.// The real purpose behind the vow taken during these four months is to minimize the quantity of sense gratification. This is not very difficult. In the month of Śrāvaṇa one should not eat spinach, in the month of Bhādra one should not eat yogurt, and in the month of Āśvina one should not drink milk. One should not eat fish or other nonvegetarian food during the month of Kārtika. A nonvegetarian diet means fish and meat. Similarly, //masūradāl// and //uraddāl// are also considered nonvegetarian. These two //dāl//s contain a great amount of protein, and food rich in protein is considered nonvegetarian. On the whole, during the four-month period of Cāturmāsya one should practice giving up all food intended for sense enjoyment.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.17
description: Because of their love for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they served Him in many ways, and that night the Lord stayed at the temple of Gopīnātha.
text:
> nānā-rūpe prītye kaila prabhura sevana
> sei rātri tāhāṅ prabhu karilā vañcana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in various ways; [[synonyms:p:prītye]]---on account of love; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---service; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:r:rātri]]---that night; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:v:vañcana]]---passing.
translation: Because of their love for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they served Him in many ways, and that night the Lord stayed at the temple of Gopīnātha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.170
description: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally praised the nectarean characteristics of Mādhavendra Purī, and while He related all this to the devotees, He personally relished it.
text:
> śrī-mukhe mādhava-purīra amṛta-carita
> bhakta-gaṇe śunāñā prabhu kare āsvādita
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---from the mouth of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]-[[synonyms:p:purīra]]---of Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:c:carita]]---nectarean characteristics; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:ś:śunāñā]]---making hear; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādita]]---relished.
translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally praised the nectarean characteristics of Mādhavendra Purī, and while He related all this to the devotees, He personally relished it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.171
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked Nityānanda Prabhu to judge whether there was anyone within the world as fortunate as Mādhavendra Purī.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---nityānanda, karaha vicāra
> purī-sama bhāgyavān jagate nāhi āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---just consider; [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---like Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:b:bhāgyavān]]---fortunate; [[synonyms:j:jagate]]---in the world; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---anyone else.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked Nityānanda Prabhu to judge whether there was anyone within the world as fortunate as Mādhavendra Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.172
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Mādhavendra Purī was so fortunate that Kṛṣṇa personally appeared before him on the plea of delivering milk. Three times the Lord gave orders to Mādhavendra Purī in dreams.
text:
> dugdha-dāna-chale kṛṣṇa yāṅre dekhā dila
> tina-bāre svapne āsi' yāṅre ājñā kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]-[[synonyms:d:dāna]]-[[synonyms:c:chale]]---on the plea of delivering milk; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yāṅre]]---unto whom; [[synonyms:d:dekhā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---made His appearance; [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:b:bāre]]---three times; [[synonyms:s:svapne]]---in dreams; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:y:yāṅre]]---unto whom; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---gave.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Mādhavendra Purī was so fortunate that Kṛṣṇa personally appeared before him on the plea of delivering milk. Three times the Lord gave orders to Mādhavendra Purī in dreams.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.173
description: "Being obliged because of the loving affairs of Mādhavendra Purī, Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself appeared as the Gopāla Deity, and, accepting his service, He liberated the whole world.
text:
> yāṅra preme vaśa hañā prakaṭa ha-ilā
> sevā aṅgīkāra kari' jagata tārilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---by love of Godhead; [[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---obliged; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭa]]---manifest; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---service; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---acceptance; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:j:jagata]]---the whole world; [[synonyms:t:tārilā]]---delivered.
translation: "Being obliged because of the loving affairs of Mādhavendra Purī, Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself appeared as the Gopāla Deity, and, accepting his service, He liberated the whole world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.174
description: "On account of Mādhavendra Purī, Lord Gopīnātha stole the pot of sweet rice. Thus He became famous as Kṣīra-corā [the thief who stole the sweet rice].
text:
> yāṅra lāgi' gopīnātha kṣīra kaila curi
> ataeva nāma haila 'kṣīra-corā' kari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whom; [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---on account of; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]---Lord Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]---sweet rice; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:c:curi]]---steal; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]-[[synonyms:c:corā]]---the thief of sweet rice; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making.
translation: "On account of Mādhavendra Purī, Lord Gopīnātha stole the pot of sweet rice. Thus He became famous as Kṣīra-corā [the thief who stole the sweet rice].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.175
description: "Mādhavendra Purī smeared the sandalwood pulp over the body of Gopīnātha, and in this way he was overpowered with love of Godhead.
text:
> karpūra-candana yāṅra aṅge caḍāila
> ānande purī-gosāñira prema uthalila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]-[[synonyms:c:candana]]---camphor and sandalwood; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]] [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---on whose body; [[synonyms:c:caḍāila]]---put; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in great pieasure; [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:u:uthalila]]---welled up.
translation: "Mādhavendra Purī smeared the sandalwood pulp over the body of Gopīnātha, and in this way he was overpowered with love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.176
description: "In the provinces of India governed by the Muslims, there was much inconvenience in traveling with sandalwood and camphor. Because of this, Mādhavendra Purī might have gotten into trouble. This became known to the Gopāla Deity.
text:
> mleccha-deśe karpūra-candana ānite jañjāla
> purī duḥkha pābe ihā jāniyā gopāla
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---through the countries where Muslims ruled; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]-[[synonyms:c:candana]]---camphor and sandalwood; [[synonyms:ā:ānite]]---to bring; [[synonyms:j:jañjāla]]---inconvenience; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:p:pābe]]---will get; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:j:jāniyā]]---knowing; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Gopāla.
translation: "In the provinces of India governed by the Muslims, there was much inconvenience in traveling with sandalwood and camphor. Because of this, Mādhavendra Purī might have gotten into trouble. This became known to the Gopāla Deity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.177
description: "The Lord is very merciful and attached to His devotees, so when Gopīnātha was covered with sandalwood pulp, Mādhavendra Purī's labor became successful."
text:
> mahā-dayā-maya prabhu---bhakata-vatsala
> candana pari' bhakta-śrama karila saphala
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]---very; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---merciful; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhakata]]-[[synonyms:v:vatsala]]---very attached to His devotees; [[synonyms:c:candana]] [[synonyms:p:pari']]---putting on the sandalwood; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:ś:śrama]]---the trouble of the devotee; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---made; [[synonyms:s:saphala]]---successful.
translation: "The Lord is very merciful and attached to His devotees, so when Gopīnātha was covered with sandalwood pulp, Mādhavendra Purī's labor became successful."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.178
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu placed the standard of Mādhavendra Purī's intense love before Nityānanda Prabhu for judgment. "All his loving activities are uncommon," Caitanya Mahāprabhu said. "Indeed, one is struck with wonder to hear of his activities."
text:
> purīra prema-parākāṣṭhā karaha vicāra
> alaukika prema citte lāge camatkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purīra]]---of Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:p:parā]]-[[synonyms:k:kāṣṭhā]]---the standard of intense love of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---just make; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---judgment; [[synonyms:a:alaukika]]---uncommon; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:c:citte]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:l:lāge]]---strikes; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---wonder.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu placed the standard of Mādhavendra Purī's intense love before Nityānanda Prabhu for judgment. "All his loving activities are uncommon," Caitanya Mahāprabhu said. "Indeed, one is struck with wonder to hear of his activities."
purport: When the living entity feels spiritual separation from Kṛṣṇa (//kṛṣṇa-viraha//), he has achieved the prime success of life. When one becomes disinterested in material things, he is simply experiencing the other side of attraction for material things. However, feeling separation from Kṛṣṇa and engaging in the service of the Lord to fulfill His mission constitute the best example of love of Kṛṣṇa. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to point out this intense love of Kṛṣṇa exhibited by Mādhavendra Purī. All Caitanya Mahāprabhu's devotees later followed in the footsteps of Mādhavendra Purī, serving the Lord without personal considerations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.179
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "Śrī Mādhavendra Purī used to remain alone. He was completely renounced and always very silent. He was uninterested in everything material, and for fear of talking about mundane things, he always lived without a companion.
text:
> parama virakta, maunī, sarvatra udāsīna
> grāmya-vārtā-bhaye dvitīya-saṅga-hīna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paramavirakta]]---totally renounced or unattached; [[synonyms:m:maunī]]---silent; [[synonyms:s:sarvatra]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:u:udāsīna]]---uninterested; [[synonyms:g:grāmya]]-[[synonyms:v:vārtā]]---of mundane topics; [[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---in fear; [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]]---second; [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---associate; [[synonyms:h:hīna]]---without.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "Śrī Mādhavendra Purī used to remain alone. He was completely renounced and always very silent. He was uninterested in everything material, and for fear of talking about mundane things, he always lived without a companion.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.18
description: The Lord remained there because He was very eager to receive the remnants of sweet rice offered to the Gopīnātha Deity, having heard a narration from His spiritual master, Īśvara Purī, of what had once happened there.
text:
> mahāprasāda-kṣīra-lobhe rahilā prabhu tathā
> pūrve īśvara-purī tāṅre kahiyāchena kathā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---for the remnants of food; [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]---sweet rice; [[synonyms:l:lobhe]]---in eagerness; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---there; [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---before that; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]---Īśvara Purī, His spiritual master; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:k:kahiyāchena]]---told; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---a narration.
translation: The Lord remained there because He was very eager to receive the remnants of sweet rice offered to the Gopīnātha Deity, having heard a narration from His spiritual master, Īśvara Purī, of what had once happened there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.180
description: "After receiving the transcendental orders of Gopāla, this great personality traveled thousands of miles just to collect sandalwood by begging.
text:
> hena-jana gopālera ājñāmṛta pāñā
> sahasra krośa āsi' bule candana māgiñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---such a personality; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of the Gopāla Deity; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---the nectarean order; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]---a thousand; [[synonyms:k:krośa]]---a distance of two miles; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:b:bule]]---walks; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood; [[synonyms:m:māgiñā]]---begging.
translation: "After receiving the transcendental orders of Gopāla, this great personality traveled thousands of miles just to collect sandalwood by begging.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.181
description: "Although Mādhavendra Purī was hungry, he would not beg food to eat. This renounced person carried a load of sandalwood for the sake of Śrī Gopāla.
text:
> bhoke rahe, tabu anna māgiñā nā khāya
> hena-jana candana-bhāra vahi' lañā yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhoke]]---hungry; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food; [[synonyms:m:māgiñā]]---begging; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:k:khāya]]---eat; [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---such a person; [[synonyms:c:candana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāra]]---the load of sandalwood; [[synonyms:v:vahi']]---carrying; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes.
translation: "Although Mādhavendra Purī was hungry, he would not beg food to eat. This renounced person carried a load of sandalwood for the sake of Śrī Gopāla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.182
description: "Without considering his personal comforts, Mādhavendra Purī carried one māna [about eighty-two pounds] of sandalwood and twenty tolās [about eight ounces] of camphor to smear over the body of Gopāla. This transcendental pleasure was sufficient for him.
text:
> 'maṇeka candana, tolā-viśeka karpūra
> gopāle parāiba'---ei ānanda pracura
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:maṇeka]] [[synonyms:c:candana]]---one //māna// of sandalwood; [[synonyms:t:tolā]]---a measurement of weight; [[synonyms:v:viśeka]]---twenty; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]---camphor; [[synonyms:g:gopāle]]---on Gopāla; [[synonyms:p:parāiba]]---I shall smear; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:p:pracura]]---sufficient.
translation: "Without considering his personal comforts, Mādhavendra Purī carried one māna [about eighty-two pounds] of sandalwood and twenty tolās [about eight ounces] of camphor to smear over the body of Gopāla. This transcendental pleasure was sufficient for him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.183
description: "Since there were restrictions against taking the sandalwood out of the Orissa province, the toll official confiscated the stock, but Mādhavendra Purī showed him the release papers given by the government and consequently escaped difficulties.
text:
> utkalera dānī rākhe candana dekhiñā
> tāhāṅ eḍāila rāja-patra dekhāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:utkalera]]---of Orissa; [[synonyms:d:dānī]]---toll officer; [[synonyms:r:rākhe]]---takes; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood; [[synonyms:d:dekhiñā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:e:eḍāila]]---escaped; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:p:patra]]---governmental release; [[synonyms:d:dekhāñā]]---by showing.
translation: "Since there were restrictions against taking the sandalwood out of the Orissa province, the toll official confiscated the stock, but Mādhavendra Purī showed him the release papers given by the government and consequently escaped difficulties.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.184
description: "Mādhavendra Purī was not at all anxious during the long journey to Vṛndāvana through the provinces governed by the Muslims and filled with unlimited numbers of watchmen.
text:
> mleccha-deśa dūra patha, jagāti apāra
> ke-mate candana niba---nāhi e vicāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:d:deśa]]---the countries governed by Muslims; [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:p:patha]]---long journey; [[synonyms:j:jagāti]]---watchmen; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:k:ke]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---how; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---the sandalwood; [[synonyms:n:niba]]---I shall take; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there was not; [[synonyms:e:e]]---this; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---consideration.
translation: "Mādhavendra Purī was not at all anxious during the long journey to Vṛndāvana through the provinces governed by the Muslims and filled with unlimited numbers of watchmen.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.185
description: "Although Mādhavendra Purī did not have a farthing with him, he was not afraid to pass by the toll officers. His only enjoyment was in carrying the load of sandalwood to Vṛndāvana for Gopāla.
text:
> saṅge eka vaṭa nāhi ghāṭī-dāna dite
> tathāpi utsāha baḍa candana lañā yāite

translation: "Although Mādhavendra Purī did not have a farthing with him, he was not afraid to pass by the toll officers. His only enjoyment was in carrying the load of sandalwood to Vṛndāvana for Gopāla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.186
description: "This is the natural result of intense love of Godhead. The devotee does not consider personal inconveniences or impediments. In all circumstances he wants to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> pragāḍha-premera ei svabhāva-ācāra
> nija-duḥkha-vighnādira nā kare vicāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pragāḍha]]---intense; [[synonyms:p:premera]]---of love of Godhead; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---natural; [[synonyms:ā:ācāra]]---behavior; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---personal; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---inconvenience; [[synonyms:v:vighna]]---impediments; [[synonyms:ā:ādira]]---and so on; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---consideration.
translation: "This is the natural result of intense love of Godhead. The devotee does not consider personal inconveniences or impediments. In all circumstances he wants to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
purport: It is natural for those who have developed intense love for Kṛṣṇa not to care for personal inconvenience and impediments. Such devotees are simply determined to execute the order of the Supreme Personality of Godhead or His representative, the spiritual master. In all circumstances, even amidst the greatest dangers, they undeviatingly carry on with the greatest determination. This definitely proves the intense love of the servitor. As stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.14.8), //tat te 'nukampāṁ su-samīkṣamāṇaḥ:// those who seriously desire to get free from the clutches of material existence, who have developed intense love for Kṛṣṇa, are worthy candidates for going back home, back to Godhead. An intense lover of Kṛṣṇa does not care for any number of material discomforts, scarcity, impediments or unhappiness. It is said that when one sees apparent unhappiness or distress in a perfect Vaiṣṇava, it is not at all unhappiness for him; rather, it is transcendental bliss. In the //Śikṣāṣṭaka// (8), Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has also instructed: //āśliṣya vā pāda-ratāṁ pinaṣṭu mām.// The intense lover of Kṛṣṇa is never deviated from his service, despite all difficulties and impediments brought before him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.197
description: "O My Lord! O most merciful master! O master of Mathurā! When shall I see You again? Because of My not seeing You, My agitated heart has become unsteady. O most beloved one, what shall I do now?"
text:
> ayi dīna-dayārdra nātha he
> mathurā-nātha kadāvalokyase
> hṛdayaṁ tvad-aloka-kātaraṁ
> dayita bhrāmyati kiṁ karomy aham
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ayi]]---O My Lord; [[synonyms:d:dīna]]---on the poor; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārdra]]---compassionate; [[synonyms:n:nātha]]---O master; [[synonyms:h:he]]---O; [[synonyms:m:mathurā]]-[[synonyms:n:nātha]]---the master of Mathurā; [[synonyms:k:kadā]]---when; [[synonyms:a:avalokyase]]---I shall see You; [[synonyms:h:hṛdayam]]---My heart; [[synonyms:t:tvat]]---of You; [[synonyms:a:aloka]]---without seeing; [[synonyms:k:kātaram]]---very much aggrieved; [[synonyms:d:dayita]]---O most beloved; [[synonyms:b:bhrāmyati]]---becomes overwhelmed; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what; [[synonyms:k:karomi]]---shall do; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I.
translation: "O My Lord! O most merciful master! O master of Mathurā! When shall I see You again? Because of My not seeing You, My agitated heart has become unsteady. O most beloved one, what shall I do now?"
purport:
The uncontaminated devotees who strictly depend on the Vedānta philosophy are divided into four //sampradāyas,// or transcendental parties. Out of the four //sampradāyas,// the Śrī Madhvācārya-sampradāya was accepted by Mādhavendra Purī. Thus he took //sannyāsa// according to //paramparā,// the disciplic succession. Beginning from Madhvācārya down to the spiritual master of Mādhavendra Purī, the //ācārya// named Lakṣmīpati, there was no realization of devotional service in conjugal love. Śrī Mādhavendra Purī introduced the conception of conjugal love for the first time in the Madhvācārya-sampradāya, and this conclusion of the Madhvācārya-sampradāya was revealed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu when He toured southern India and met the Tattvavādīs, who supposedly belonged to the Madhvācārya-sampradāya.

When Śrī Kṛṣṇa left Vṛndāvana and accepted the kingdom of Mathurā, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, out of ecstatic feelings of separation, expressed how Kṛṣṇa can be loved in separation. Thus devotional service in separation is central to this verse. Worship in separation is considered by the //Gauḍīya-Mādhva sampradāya// to be the topmost level of devotional service. According to this conception, the devotee thinks of himself as very poor and neglected by the Lord. Thus he addresses the Lord as //dīna-dayārdra nātha,// as did Mādhavendra Purī. Such an ecstatic feeling is the highest form of devotional service. Because Kṛṣṇa had gone to Mathurā, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī was very much affected, and She expressed Herself thus: "My dear Lord, because of Your separation My mind has become overly agitated. Now tell Me, what can I do? I am very poor and You are very merciful, so kindly have compassion upon Me and let Me know when I shall see You." Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was always expressing the ecstatic emotions of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī that She exhibited when She saw Uddhava at Vṛndāvana. Similar feelings, experienced by Mādhavendra Purī, are expressed in this verse. Therefore, Vaiṣṇavas in the //Gauḍīya-Mādhva sampradāya// say that the ecstatic feelings experienced by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu during His appearance came from Śrī Mādhavendra Purī through Īśvara Purī. All the devotees in the line of the //Gauḍīya-Mādhva sampradāya// accept these principles of devotional service.
