title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.200
description: Exhibiting ecstatic emotions, the Lord began to run here and there, making resounding noises. Sometimes He laughed, and sometimes He cried, and sometimes He danced and sang.
text:
> premonmāda haila, uṭhi' iti-uti dhāya
> huṅkāra karaye, hāse, kānde, nāce, gāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:u:unmāda]]---the madness of love; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---getting up; [[synonyms:i:iti]]-[[synonyms:u:uti]] [[synonyms:d:dhāya]]---runs here and there; [[synonyms:h:huṅkāra]]---resounding; [[synonyms:k:karaye]]---does; [[synonyms:h:hāse]]---laughs; [[synonyms:k:kānde]]---cries; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---and sings.
translation: Exhibiting ecstatic emotions, the Lord began to run here and there, making resounding noises. Sometimes He laughed, and sometimes He cried, and sometimes He danced and sang.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.201
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu could not recite the whole verse. He simply said, "Ayi dīna, ayi dīna," repeatedly. Thus He could not speak, and profuse tears were in His eyes.
text:
> 'ayi dīna, 'ayi dīna' bale bāra-bāra
> kaṇṭhe nā niḥsare vāṇī, netre aśru-dhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ayi]] [[synonyms:d:dīna]]---O My Lord, master of the poor; [[synonyms:a:ayi]] [[synonyms:d:dīna]]---O My Lord, master of the poor; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---says; [[synonyms:b:bāra]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---repeatedly; [[synonyms:k:kaṇṭhe]]---in the throat; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:n:niḥsare]]---comes out; [[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---the voice; [[synonyms:n:netre]]---in the eyes; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---torrents of tears.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu could not recite the whole verse. He simply said, "Ayi dīna, ayi dīna," repeatedly. Thus He could not speak, and profuse tears were in His eyes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.202
description: Trembling, perspiration, jubilant tears, shock, fading of the bodily luster, disappointment, moroseness, loss of memory, pride, joy and humility were all visible in Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's body.
text:
> kampa, sveda, pulakāśru, stambha, vaivarṇya
> nirveda, viṣāda, jāḍya, garva, harṣa, dainya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:s:sveda]]---perspiration; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]-[[synonyms:a:aśru]]---jubilation and tears; [[synonyms:s:stambha]]---shock; [[synonyms:v:vaivarṇya]]---loss of color; [[synonyms:n:nirveda]]---disappointment; [[synonyms:v:viṣāda]]---moroseness; [[synonyms:j:jāḍya]]---loss of memory; [[synonyms:g:garva]]---pride; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---joy; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]---humility.
translation: Trembling, perspiration, jubilant tears, shock, fading of the bodily luster, disappointment, moroseness, loss of memory, pride, joy and humility were all visible in Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's body.
purport: In the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, jāḍya// is explained as loss of memory brought about by severe shock due to separation from the beloved. In that state of mind, one loses all concern for loss and gain, hearing and seeing, as well as all other considerations. This marks the preliminary appearance of illusion.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.203
description: This verse uncovered the door of ecstatic love, and when it was exhibited, all the servants of Gopīnātha saw Caitanya Mahāprabhu dance in ecstasy.
text:
> ei śloke ughāḍilā premera kapāṭa
> gopīnātha-sevaka dekhe prabhura prema-nāṭa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloke]]---this verse; [[synonyms:u:ughāḍilā]]---uncovered; [[synonyms:p:premera]]---of conjugal love; [[synonyms:k:kapāṭa]]---the door; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---the servants of the Gopīnātha Deity; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---see; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:n:nāṭa]]---the dance in ecstatic love.
translation: This verse uncovered the door of ecstatic love, and when it was exhibited, all the servants of Gopīnātha saw Caitanya Mahāprabhu dance in ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.204
description: When many people crowded around Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, He regained His external senses. In the meantime, the offering to the Deity had been finished, and there was a resounding ārati performance.
text:
> lokera saṅghaṭṭa dekhi' prabhura bāhya haila
> ṭhākurera bhoga sari' ārati bājila
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of people; [[synonyms:s:saṅghaṭṭa]]---a crowd; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---external consciousness; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---appeared; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākurera]]---of the Deity; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---offering; [[synonyms:s:sari']]---finishing; [[synonyms:ā:ārati]]---performance of //ārati//; [[synonyms:b:bājila]]---resounded.
translation: When many people crowded around Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, He regained His external senses. In the meantime, the offering to the Deity had been finished, and there was a resounding ārati performance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.205
description: When the Deities were laid down to rest, the priest came out of the temple and offered all twelve pots of sweet rice to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> ṭhākure śayana karāñā pūjārī haila bāhira
> prabhura āge āni' dila prasāda bāra kṣīra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākure]]---the Deity; [[synonyms:ś:śayana]]---lying down; [[synonyms:k:karāñā]]---causing to do; [[synonyms:p:pūjārī]]---the priest; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:b:bāhira]]---out of the temple; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---offered; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---the remnants of food; [[synonyms:b:bāra]]---twelve; [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]---pots of sweet rice.
translation: When the Deities were laid down to rest, the priest came out of the temple and offered all twelve pots of sweet rice to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.206
description: When all the pots of sweet rice, remnants left by Gopīnātha, were placed before Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, He became very pleased. In order to feed the devotees, He accepted five of them.
text:
> kṣīra dekhi' mahāprabhura ānanda bāḍila
> bhakta-gaṇe khāoyāite pañca kṣīra laila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]---the sweet rice; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---the pleasure; [[synonyms:b:bāḍila]]---increased; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:k:khāoyaīte]]---to feed them; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]---five pots; [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]---sweet rice; [[synonyms:l:laila]]---accepted.
translation: When all the pots of sweet rice, remnants left by Gopīnātha, were placed before Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, He became very pleased. In order to feed the devotees, He accepted five of them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.207
description: The seven remaining pots were pushed forward and delivered to the priest. Then the five pots of sweet rice the Lord had accepted were distributed among the five devotees, and they ate the prasāda.
text:
> sāta kṣīra pūjārīke bāhuḍiyā dila
> pañca-kṣīra pañca-jane vāṅṭiyā khāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sāta]] [[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]---seven pots of sweet rice; [[synonyms:p:pūjārīke]]---toward the //pūjārī//; [[synonyms:b:bāhuḍiyā]]---pushing forward; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣīra]]---five pots of sweet rice; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---to five men; [[synonyms:v:vāṅṭiyā]]---distributing; [[synonyms:k:khāila]]---ate.
translation: The seven remaining pots were pushed forward and delivered to the priest. Then the five pots of sweet rice the Lord had accepted were distributed among the five devotees, and they ate the prasāda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.208
description: Being identical with the Gopīnātha Deity, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had already tasted and eaten the pots of sweet rice. Yet just to manifest devotional service, He again ate the pots of sweet rice as a devotee.
text:
> gopīnātha-rūpe yadi kariyāchena bhojana
> bhakti dekhāite kaila prasāda bhakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in His //arcā// incarnation as Gopīnātha; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---although; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchena]]---has done; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eating; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:d:dekhāite]]---to exhibit; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:b:bhakṣaṇa]]---eating.
translation: Being identical with the Gopīnātha Deity, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had already tasted and eaten the pots of sweet rice. Yet just to manifest devotional service, He again ate the pots of sweet rice as a devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.209
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed that night at the temple engaged in congregational chanting. In the morning, after seeing the maṅgala-ārati performance, He departed.
text:
> nāma-saṅkīrtane sei rātri goṅāilā
> maṅgala-ārati dekhi' prabhāte calilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtane]]---in congregational chanting; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]---night; [[synonyms:g:goṅāilā]]---passed; [[synonyms:m:maṅgala]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārati]]---the early //ārati//; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhāte]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---departed.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed that night at the temple engaged in congregational chanting. In the morning, after seeing the maṅgala-ārati performance, He departed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.21
description: Once, Śrī Mādhavendra Purī traveled to Vṛndāvana, where he came upon the hill known as Govardhana.
text:
> pūrve śrī-mādhava-purī āilā vṛndāvana
> bhramite, bhramite gelā giri govardhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---formerly; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhava]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]---Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:b:bhramite]] [[synonyms:b:bhramite]]---while traveling; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:g:giri]] [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]---to the hill known as Govardhana.
translation: Once, Śrī Mādhavendra Purī traveled to Vṛndāvana, where he came upon the hill known as Govardhana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.210
description: In this way, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally tasted with His own mouth the transcendental qualities of Gopālajī, Gopīnātha and Śrī Mādhavendra Purī.
text:
> gopāla-gopīnātha-purī-gosāñira guṇa
> bhakta-saṅge śrī-mukhe prabhu kailā āsvādana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---of the Gopāla Deity; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]---of the Gopīnātha Deity; [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---the qualities; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the devotees; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in His own mouth; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasting.
translation: In this way, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally tasted with His own mouth the transcendental qualities of Gopālajī, Gopīnātha and Śrī Mādhavendra Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.211
description: Thus I have described both the transcendental glories of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's affection for His devotees and the highest limit of ecstatic love of God.
text:
> ei ta' ākhyāne kahilā doṅhāra mahimā
> prabhura bhakta-vātsalya, āra bhakta-prema-sīmā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---thus; [[synonyms:ā:ākhyāne]]---in the narration; [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---described; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]]---of the two; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---the glories; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vātsalya]]---attachment for His devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:s:sīmā]]---the highest limit of ecstatic love by the devotee.
translation: Thus I have described both the transcendental glories of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's affection for His devotees and the highest limit of ecstatic love of God.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.212
description: One who hears this narration with faith and devotion attains the treasure of love of Godhead at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> śraddhā-yukta hañā ihā śune yei jana
> śrī-kṛṣṇa-caraṇe sei pāya prema-dhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]]-[[synonyms:y:yukta]]---possessed of faith; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hears; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---that; [[synonyms:j:jana]]---person; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that person; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---the treasure of love of Godhead.
translation: One who hears this narration with faith and devotion attains the treasure of love of Godhead at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.213
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation:
Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Fourth Chapter, describing Śrī Mādhavendra Purī's devotional service.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.22
description: Mādhavendra Purī was almost mad in his ecstasy of love of Godhead, and he did not know whether it was day or night. Sometimes he stood up, and sometimes he fell to the ground. He could not discriminate whether he was in a proper place or not.
text:
> preme matta,---nāhi tāṅra rātri-dina-jñāna
> kṣaṇe uṭhe, kṣaṇe paḍe, nāhi sthānāsthāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:premematta]]---maddened in the ecstasy of love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there was not; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of him; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---knowledge of day and night; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---stands; [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]] [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---sometimes falls; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there was no sense; [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]-[[synonyms:a:asthāna]]---a proper place or not.
translation: Mādhavendra Purī was almost mad in his ecstasy of love of Godhead, and he did not know whether it was day or night. Sometimes he stood up, and sometimes he fell to the ground. He could not discriminate whether he was in a proper place or not.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.23
description: After circumambulating the hill, Mādhavendra Purī went to Govinda-kuṇḍa and took his bath. He then sat beneath a tree to take his evening rest.
text:
> śaila parikramā kari' govinda-kuṇḍe āsi'
> snāna kari, vṛkṣa-tale āche sandhyāya vasi'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śaila]]---the hill; [[synonyms:p:parikramā]]---circumambulation; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---finishing; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṇḍe]]---to the bank of the Govinda-kuṇḍa; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming there; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---taking a bath; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:t:tale]]---under the shade of a tree; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---is; [[synonyms:s:sandhyāya]]---in the evening; [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---resting.
translation: After circumambulating the hill, Mādhavendra Purī went to Govinda-kuṇḍa and took his bath. He then sat beneath a tree to take his evening rest.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.24
description: While he was sitting beneath a tree, an unknown cowherd boy came with a pot of milk, placed it before Mādhavendra Purī and, smiling, addressed him as follows.
text:
> gopāla-bālaka eka dugdha-bhāṇḍa lañā
> āsi' āge dhari' kichu balila hāsiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:b:bālaka]]---cowherd boy; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāṇḍa]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking a pot of milk; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:ā:āge]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---holding it in front; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:b:balila]]---said; [[synonyms:h:hāsiyā]]---smiling.
translation: While he was sitting beneath a tree, an unknown cowherd boy came with a pot of milk, placed it before Mādhavendra Purī and, smiling, addressed him as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.25
description: "O Mādhavendra Purī, please drink the milk I have brought. Why don't you beg some food to eat? What kind of meditation are you undergoing?"
text:
> purī, ei dugdha lañā kara tumi pāna
> māgi' kene nāhi khāo, kibā kara dhyāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purī]]---O Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dugdha]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking this milk; [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:p:pāna]]---drink it; [[synonyms:m:māgi']]---by begging; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:k:khāo]]---you eat; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---what; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---do; [[synonyms:d:dhyāna]]---meditation.
translation: "O Mādhavendra Purī, please drink the milk I have brought. Why don't you beg some food to eat? What kind of meditation are you undergoing?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.26
description: When he saw the beauty of that boy, Mādhavendra Purī became very satisfied. Hearing His sweet words, he forgot all hunger and thirst.
text:
> bālakera saundarye purīra ha-ila santoṣa
> tāhāra madhura-vākye gela bhoka-śoṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bālakera]]---of the boy; [[synonyms:s:saundarye]]---in the beauty; [[synonyms:p:purīra]]---of Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---was; [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---very much satisfaction; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---of Him; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]-[[synonyms:v:vākye]]---by the sweet words; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---forgot; [[synonyms:b:bhoka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śoṣa]]---all hunger and thirst.
translation: When he saw the beauty of that boy, Mādhavendra Purī became very satisfied. Hearing His sweet words, he forgot all hunger and thirst.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.27
description: Mādhavendra Purī said, "Who are You ? Where do You reside? And how did You know that I was fasting?"
text:
> purī kahe,---ke tumi, kāhāṅ tomāra vāsa
> ke-mate jānile, āmi kari upavāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purī]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Mādhavendra Purī inquired from the boy; [[synonyms:k:ke]] [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---who are You; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---where do You reside; [[synonyms:k:ke]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---how; [[synonyms:j:jānile]]---You know; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:k:kari]] [[synonyms:u:upavāsa]]---I am fasting.
translation: Mādhavendra Purī said, "Who are You ? Where do You reside? And how did You know that I was fasting?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.28
description: The boy replied, "Sir, I am a cowherd boy, and I reside in this village. In My village, no one fasts.
text:
> bālaka kahe,---gopa āmi, ei grāme vasi
> āmāra grāmete keha nā rahe upavāsī
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bālaka]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the boy said; [[synonyms:g:gopa]] [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I am a cowherd boy; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:g:grāme]] [[synonyms:v:vasi]]---I reside in this village; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:g:grāmete]]---in My village; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:u:upavāsī]]---without food.
translation: The boy replied, "Sir, I am a cowherd boy, and I reside in this village. In My village, no one fasts.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.29
description: "In this village a person can beg food from others and thus eat. Some people drink only milk, but if a person does not ask anyone for food, I supply him all his eatables.
text:
> keha anna māgi' khāya, keha dugdhāhāra
> ayācaka-jane āmi diye ta' āhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food; [[synonyms:m:māgi']]---begging; [[synonyms:k:khāya]]---eats; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āhāra]]---drinks milk; [[synonyms:a:ayācaka]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---a person who does not beg; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:d:diye]]---supply; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:ā:āhāra]]---eatables.
translation: "In this village a person can beg food from others and thus eat. Some people drink only milk, but if a person does not ask anyone for food, I supply him all his eatables.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.3-4
description: The Lord went to Jagannātha Purī and visited Lord Jagannātha's temple. He also met with Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. All these pastimes have been very elaborately explained by Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura in his book Caitanya-bhāgavata.
text:
> nīlādri-gamana, jagannātha-daraśana
> sārvabhauma bhaṭṭācārya-prabhura milana
> e saba līlā prabhura dāsa vṛndāvana
> vistāri' kariyāchena uttama varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nīlādri]]-[[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting the temple of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]] [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---with Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting; [[synonyms:e:e]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all these; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]] [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:v:vistāri']]---elaborating; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchena]]---has done; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]---very nice; [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---description.
translation: The Lord went to Jagannātha Purī and visited Lord Jagannātha's temple. He also met with Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. All these pastimes have been very elaborately explained by Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura in his book Caitanya-bhāgavata.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.30
description: "The women who come here to take water saw you, and they supplied Me with this milk and sent Me to you."
text:
> jala nite strī-gaṇa tomāre dekhi' gela
> strī-saba dugdha diyā āmāre pāṭhāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jala]] [[synonyms:n:nite]]---for bringing water; [[synonyms:s:strī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the women; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---you; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']] [[synonyms:g:gela]]---saw you and went; [[synonyms:s:strī]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all the women; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]---milk; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving; [[synonyms:ā:āmāre]]---Me; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāila]]---have sent.
translation: "The women who come here to take water saw you, and they supplied Me with this milk and sent Me to you."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.31
description: The boy continued, "I must go very soon to milk the cows, but I shall return and take back this milk pot from you."
text:
> go-dohana karite cāhi, śīghra āmi yāba
> āra-bāra āsi āmi ei bhāṇḍa la-iba
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:go]]-[[synonyms:d:dohana]] [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:c:cāhi]]---I want to milk the cows; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]]---very soon; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---I must go; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---again; [[synonyms:ā:āsi]]---coming back; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:b:bhāṇḍa]]---pot; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iba]]---will take it back.
translation: The boy continued, "I must go very soon to milk the cows, but I shall return and take back this milk pot from you."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.32
description: Saying this, the boy left the place. Indeed, He suddenly could be seen no more, and Mādhavendra Purī's heart was filled with wonder.
text:
> eta bali' gelā bālaka nā dekhiye āra
> mādhava-purīra citte ha-ila camatkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:b:bālaka]]---the boy; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:d:dekhiye]]---could be seen; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---any more; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]-[[synonyms:p:purīra]]---of Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:c:citte]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---wonder.
translation: Saying this, the boy left the place. Indeed, He suddenly could be seen no more, and Mādhavendra Purī's heart was filled with wonder.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.33
description: After drinking the milk, Mādhavendra Purī washed the pot and put it aside. He looked toward the path, but the boy never returned.
text:
> dugdha pāna kari' bhāṇḍa dhuñā rākhila
> bāṭa dekhe, se bālaka punaḥ nā āila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]---milk; [[synonyms:p:pāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---drinking; [[synonyms:b:bhāṇḍa]]---the pot; [[synonyms:d:dhuñā]]---washing; [[synonyms:r:rākhila]]---kept aside; [[synonyms:b:bāṭa]] [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---looks at the path; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:b:bālaka]]---the boy; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---did not come back.
translation: After drinking the milk, Mādhavendra Purī washed the pot and put it aside. He looked toward the path, but the boy never returned.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.34
description: Mādhavendra Purī could not sleep. He sat and chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, and at the end of the night he dozed a little, and his external activities stopped.
text:
> vasi' nāma laya purī, nidrā nāhi haya
> śeṣa-rātre tandrā haila,---bāhya-vṛtti-laya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting there; [[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:l:laya]]---chants the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra//; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:n:nidrā]]---sleep; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there was not; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]-[[synonyms:r:rātre]]---at the end of the night; [[synonyms:t:tandrā]]---dozing; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛtti]]---of external activities; [[synonyms:l:laya]]---stop.
translation: Mādhavendra Purī could not sleep. He sat and chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, and at the end of the night he dozed a little, and his external activities stopped.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.35
description: In a dream Mādhavendra Purī saw the very same boy. The boy came before him and, holding his hand, took him to a bush in the jungle.
text:
> svapne dekhe, sei bālaka sammukhe āsiñā
> eka kuñje lañā gela hātete dhariñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svapne]]---in a dream; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---he saw; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:b:bālaka]]---the very same boy; [[synonyms:s:sammukhe]]---in front; [[synonyms:ā:āsiñā]]---coming; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:k:kuñje]]---in one of the bushes; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking him; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went; [[synonyms:h:hātete]] [[synonyms:d:dhariñā]]---holding him by the hand.
translation: In a dream Mādhavendra Purī saw the very same boy. The boy came before him and, holding his hand, took him to a bush in the jungle.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.36
description: The boy showed Mādhavendra Purī the bush and said, "I reside in this bush, and because of this I suffer very much from severe cold, rain showers, winds and scorching heat.
text:
> kuñja dekhāñā kahe,---āmi ei kuñje ra-i
> śīta-vṛṣṭi-vātāgnite mahā-duḥkha pāi
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kuñja]] [[synonyms:d:dekhāñā]]---while showing him the bush; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---He says; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kuñje]]---in the bush; [[synonyms:r:ra]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---reside; [[synonyms:ś:śīta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛṣṭi]]---in chilly cold and in showering rain; [[synonyms:v:vāta]]---in severe wind; [[synonyms:a:agnite]]---and in scorching heat; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:d:duḥkha]] [[synonyms:p:pāi]]---I am experiencing great pain.
translation: The boy showed Mādhavendra Purī the bush and said, "I reside in this bush, and because of this I suffer very much from severe cold, rain showers, winds and scorching heat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.37
description: "Please bring the people of the village and get them to take Me out of this bush. Then have them situate Me nicely on top of the hill.
text:
> grāmera loka āni' āmā kāḍha' kuñja haite
> parvata-upari lañā rākha bhāla-mate
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:grāmera]]---of the village; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]---Me; [[synonyms:k:kāḍha']]---take out; [[synonyms:k:kuñja]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from this bush; [[synonyms:p:parvata]]-[[synonyms:u:upari]]---on the top of the hill; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking Me; [[synonyms:r:rākha]]---keep Me; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---very nicely.
translation: "Please bring the people of the village and get them to take Me out of this bush. Then have them situate Me nicely on top of the hill.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.38
description: "Please construct a temple on top of that hill," the boy continued, "and install Me in that temple. After this, wash Me with large quantities of cold water so that My body may be cleansed.
text:
> eka maṭha kari' tāhāṅ karaha sthāpana
> bahu śītala jale kara śrī-aṅga mārjana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:m:maṭha]]---temple; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---constructing; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---do; [[synonyms:s:sthāpana]]---installment; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---much; [[synonyms:ś:śītala]]---cold; [[synonyms:j:jale]]---in water; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---do; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---My transcendental body; [[synonyms:m:mārjana]]---washing.
translation: "Please construct a temple on top of that hill," the boy continued, "and install Me in that temple. After this, wash Me with large quantities of cold water so that My body may be cleansed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.39
description: "For many days I have been observing you, and I have been wondering, 'When will Mādhavendra Purī come here to serve Me?'
text:
> bahu-dina tomāra patha kari nirīkṣaṇa
> kabe āsi' mādhava āmā karibe sevana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---many days; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of you; [[synonyms:p:patha]]---the path; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I do; [[synonyms:n:nirīkṣaṇa]]---observing; [[synonyms:k:kabe]]---when; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]---Me; [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---he will do; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---serving.
translation: "For many days I have been observing you, and I have been wondering, 'When will Mādhavendra Purī come here to serve Me?'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.40
description: "I have accepted your service due to your ecstatic love for Me. Thus I shall appear, and by My audience all fallen souls will be delivered.
text:
> tomāra prema-vaśe kari' sevā aṅgīkāra
> darśana diyā nistāriba sakala saṁsāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśe]]---by being subjugated by the love; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---of service; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---acceptance; [[synonyms:d:darśana]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving audience; [[synonyms:n:nistāriba]]---I shall deliver; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]---the material world.
translation: "I have accepted your service due to your ecstatic love for Me. Thus I shall appear, and by My audience all fallen souls will be delivered.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.41
description: "My name is Gopāla. I am the lifter of Govardhana Hill. I was installed by Vajra, and here I am the authority.
text:
> 'śrī-gopāla' nāma mora,---govardhana-dhārī
> vajrera sthāpita, āmi ihāṅ adhikārī
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:g:gopāla]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name Śrī Gopāla; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]-[[synonyms:d:dhārī]]---the lifter of Govardhana Hill; [[synonyms:v:vajrera]]---by Vajra, the grandson of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sthāpita]]---installed; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:a:adhikārī]]---the authority.
translation: "My name is Gopāla. I am the lifter of Govardhana Hill. I was installed by Vajra, and here I am the authority.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.42
description: "When the Muslims attacked, the priest who was serving Me hid Me in this bush in the jungle. Then he ran away out of fear of the attack.
text:
> śaila-upari haite āmā kuñje lukāñā
> mleccha-bhaye sevaka mora gela palāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śaila]]-[[synonyms:u:upari]]---the top of the hill; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]---Me; [[synonyms:k:kuñje]]---in the bushes; [[synonyms:l:lukāñā]]---concealing; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---from fear of the Muslims; [[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---servant; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went; [[synonyms:p:palāñā]]---running away.
translation: "When the Muslims attacked, the priest who was serving Me hid Me in this bush in the jungle. Then he ran away out of fear of the attack.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.43
description: "Since the priest went away, I have been staying in this bush. It is very good that you have come here. Now just remove Me with care."
text:
> sei haite rahi āmi ei kuñja-sthāne
> bhāla haila āilā āmā kāḍha sāvadhāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from that time; [[synonyms:r:rahi]]---reside; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kuñja]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in the bush; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---it was very good; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---you have come; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]---Me; [[synonyms:k:kāḍha]]---take out; [[synonyms:s:sāvadhāne]]---with care.
translation: "Since the priest went away, I have been staying in this bush. It is very good that you have come here. Now just remove Me with care."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.44
description: After saying this, the boy disappeared. Then Mādhavendra Purī woke up and began to consider his dream.
text:
> eta bali' se-bālaka antardhāna kaila
> jāgiyā mādhava-purī vicāra karila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:b:bālaka]]---that very boy; [[synonyms:a:antardhāna]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---disappeared; [[synonyms:j:jāgiyā]]---awakening; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---consideration; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---made.
translation: After saying this, the boy disappeared. Then Mādhavendra Purī woke up and began to consider his dream.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.45
description: Mādhavendra Purī began to lament, "I saw Lord Kṛṣṇa directly, but I could not recognize Him!" Thus he fell down on the ground in ecstatic love.
text:
> śrī-kṛṣṇake dekhinu muñi nārinu cinite
> eta bali' premāveśe paḍilā bhūmite
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇake]] [[synonyms:d:dekhinu]]---saw Lord Kṛṣṇa personally; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nārinu]]---was unable; [[synonyms:c:cinite]]---to identify; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in the ecstasy of love; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]]---on the ground.
translation: Mādhavendra Purī began to lament, "I saw Lord Kṛṣṇa directly, but I could not recognize Him!" Thus he fell down on the ground in ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.46
description: Mādhavendra Purī cried for some time, but then he fixed his mind on executing the order of Gopāla. Thus he became tranquil.
text:
> kṣaṇeka rodana kari, mana kaila dhīra
> ājñā-pālana lāgi' ha-ilā susthira
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇeka]]---for some time; [[synonyms:r:rodana]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---crying; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:d:dhīra]]---pacified; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---the order; [[synonyms:p:pālana]]---of executing; [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for the matter; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:s:sthira]]---silent.
translation: Mādhavendra Purī cried for some time, but then he fixed his mind on executing the order of Gopāla. Thus he became tranquil.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.47
description: After taking his morning bath, Mādhavendra Purī entered the village and assembled all the people. Then he spoke as follows.
text:
> prātaḥ-snāna kari' purī grāma-madhye gelā
> saba loka ekatra kari' kahite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---morning bath; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---finishing; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:g:grāma]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within the village; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---entered; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---assembling; [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to speak.
translation: After taking his morning bath, Mādhavendra Purī entered the village and assembled all the people. Then he spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.48
description: "The proprietor of this village, Govardhana-dhārī, is lying in the bushes. Let us go there and rescue Him from that place.
text:
> grāmera īśvara tomāra---govardhana-dhārī
> kuñje āche, cala, tāṅre bāhira ye kari
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:grāmera]]---of the village; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the proprietor; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]-[[synonyms:d:dhārī]]---the lifter of Govardhana Hill; [[synonyms:k:kuñje]] [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---in the bushes in the jungle; [[synonyms:c:cala]]---let us go; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:b:bāhira]] [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---take out.
translation: "The proprietor of this village, Govardhana-dhārī, is lying in the bushes. Let us go there and rescue Him from that place.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.49
description: "The bushes are very dense, and we will not be able to enter the jungle. Therefore take choppers and spades to clear the way."
text:
> atyanta niviḍa kuñja,---nāri praveśite
> kuṭhāri kodāli laha dvāra karite
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:atyanta]]---very much; [[synonyms:n:niviḍa]]---dense; [[synonyms:k:kuñja]]---bushes; [[synonyms:n:nāri]]---we are not able; [[synonyms:p:praveśite]]---to enter; [[synonyms:k:kuṭhāri]]---choppers; [[synonyms:k:kodāli]]---spades; [[synonyms:l:laha]]---take; [[synonyms:d:dvāra]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to make a way.
translation: "The bushes are very dense, and we will not be able to enter the jungle. Therefore take choppers and spades to clear the way."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.5
description: By nature all the activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are very wonderful and sweet, and when they are described by Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, they become like a shower of nectar.
text:
> sahaje vicitra madhura caitanya-vihāra
> vṛndāvana-dāsa-mukhe amṛtera dhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sahaje]]---naturally; [[synonyms:v:vicitra]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweet; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vihāra]]---the activities; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---from the mouth; [[synonyms:a:amṛtera]]---of nectar; [[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---shower.
translation: By nature all the activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are very wonderful and sweet, and when they are described by Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, they become like a shower of nectar.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.50
description: After hearing this, all the people accompanied Mādhavendra Purī with great pleasure. According to his directions, they cut down bushes, cleared a path and entered the jungle.
text:
> śuni' loka tāṅra saṅge calilā hariṣe
> kuñja kāṭi' dvāra kari' karilā praveśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---him; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went; [[synonyms:h:hariṣe]]---with great pleasure; [[synonyms:k:kuñja]] [[synonyms:k:kāṭi']]---cutting the bushes; [[synonyms:d:dvāra]]---a way; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:p:praveśe]]---entered.
translation: After hearing this, all the people accompanied Mādhavendra Purī with great pleasure. According to his directions, they cut down bushes, cleared a path and entered the jungle.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.51
description: When they saw the Deity covered with dirt and grass, they were all struck with wonder and pleasure.
text:
> ṭhākura dekhila māṭī-tṛṇe ācchādita
> dekhi' saba loka haila ānande vismita
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---the Deity; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---they saw; [[synonyms:m:māṭī]]---with dirt; [[synonyms:t:tṛṇe]]---and grass; [[synonyms:ā:ācchādita]]---covered; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---with pleasure; [[synonyms:v:vismita]]---amazed.
translation: When they saw the Deity covered with dirt and grass, they were all struck with wonder and pleasure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.52
description: After they cleansed the body of the Deity, some of them said, "The Deity is very heavy. No one person can move Him."
text:
> āvaraṇa dūra kari' karila vidite
> mahā-bhārī ṭhākura---keha nāre cālāite
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āvaraṇa]]---the covering; [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---clearing away; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:v:vidite]]---declared; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhārī]]---very heavy; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---the Deity; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---not able; [[synonyms:c:cālāite]]---to cause to move.
translation: After they cleansed the body of the Deity, some of them said, "The Deity is very heavy. No one person can move Him."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.53
description: Since the Deity was very heavy, some of the stronger men assembled to carry Him to the top of the hill. Mādhavendra Purī also went there.
text:
> mahā-mahā-baliṣṭha loka ekatra kariñā
> parvata-upari gela purī ṭhākura lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:baliṣṭha]]---who are very strong; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---persons; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]] [[synonyms:k:kariñā]]---assembling; [[synonyms:p:parvata]]-[[synonyms:u:upari]]---to the top of the hill; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking the Deity.
translation: Since the Deity was very heavy, some of the stronger men assembled to carry Him to the top of the hill. Mādhavendra Purī also went there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.54
description: A big stone was made into a throne, and the Deity was installed upon it. Another big stone was placed behind the Deity for support.
text:
> pātharera siṁhāsane ṭhākura vasāila
> baḍa eka pāthara pṛṣṭhe avalamba dila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pātharera]]---of stone; [[synonyms:s:siṁha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsane]]---on a throne; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---the Deity; [[synonyms:v:vasāila]]---installed; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---big; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:p:pāthara]]---stone; [[synonyms:p:pṛṣṭhe]]---at the back; [[synonyms:a:avalamba]]---support; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave.
translation: A big stone was made into a throne, and the Deity was installed upon it. Another big stone was placed behind the Deity for support.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.55
description: All the brāhmaṇa priests of the village gathered together with nine waterpots, and water from Govinda-kuṇḍa lake was brought there and filtered.
text:
> grāmera brāhmaṇa saba nava ghaṭa lañā
> govinda-kuṇḍera jala ānila chāniñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:grāmera]]---of the village; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---//brāhmaṇa// priests; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:n:nava]]---nine; [[synonyms:g:ghaṭa]]---waterpots; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---bringing; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṇḍera]]---of the lake known as Govinda-kuṇḍa; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---the water; [[synonyms:ā:ānila]]---brought; [[synonyms:c:chāniñā]]---filtering.
translation: All the brāhmaṇa priests of the village gathered together with nine waterpots, and water from Govinda-kuṇḍa lake was brought there and filtered.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.56
description: When the Deity was being installed, nine hundred pots of water were brought from Govinda-kuṇḍa. There were musical sounds of bugles and drums and the singing of women.
text:
> nava śata-ghaṭa jala kaila upanīta
> nānā vādya-bherī bāje, strī-gaṇa gāya gīta
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nava]]---nine; [[synonyms:ś:śata]]-[[synonyms:g:ghaṭa]]---hundreds of waterpots; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---water; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:u:upanīta]]---brought; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:v:vādya]]---musical sounds; [[synonyms:b:bherī]]---bugles; [[synonyms:b:bāje]]---vibrate; [[synonyms:s:strī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the women; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chant; [[synonyms:g:gīta]]---various songs.
translation: When the Deity was being installed, nine hundred pots of water were brought from Govinda-kuṇḍa. There were musical sounds of bugles and drums and the singing of women.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.57
description: During the festival at the installation ceremony, some people sang and some danced. All the milk, yogurt and clarified butter in the village was brought to the festival.
text:
> keha gāya, keha nāce, mahotsava haila
> dadhi, dugdha, ghṛta āila grāme yata chila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---some sing; [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---some dance; [[synonyms:m:mahotsava]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was a festival; [[synonyms:d:dadhi]]---yogurt; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]---milk; [[synonyms:g:ghṛta]]---clarified butter; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---was brought; [[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in the village; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---as much; [[synonyms:c:chila]]---as there was.
translation: During the festival at the installation ceremony, some people sang and some danced. All the milk, yogurt and clarified butter in the village was brought to the festival.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.58
description: Various foods and sweetmeats, as well as other kinds of presentations, were brought there. I am unable to describe all these.
text:
> bhoga-sāmagrī āila sandeśādi yata
> nānā upahāra, tāhā kahite pāri kata
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]-[[synonyms:s:sāmagrī]]---ingredients for eatables to be offered; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---brought in; [[synonyms:s:sandeśa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---sweetmeats; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all kinds of; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:u:upahāra]]---presentations; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to say; [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---I am able; [[synonyms:k:kata]]---how much.
translation: Various foods and sweetmeats, as well as other kinds of presentations, were brought there. I am unable to describe all these.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.59
description: The villagers brought a large quantity of tulasī leaves, flowers, and various kinds of garments. Then Śrī Mādhavendra Purī personally began the abhiṣeka [bathing ceremony].
text:
> tulasī ādi, puṣpa, vastra āila aneka
> āpane mādhava-purī kaila abhiṣeka
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]---//tulasī// leaves; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and others; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]---flowers; [[synonyms:v:vastra]]---garments; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---arrived; [[synonyms:a:aneka]]---in great quantity; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:m:mādhava]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]---Śrī Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---executed; [[synonyms:a:abhiṣeka]]---the bathing of the Deity at the beginning of the installation ceremony.
translation: The villagers brought a large quantity of tulasī leaves, flowers, and various kinds of garments. Then Śrī Mādhavendra Purī personally began the abhiṣeka [bathing ceremony].
purport: In the //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa// (sixth //vilāsa,// verse 30) it is stated that the Deity should be bathed in water mixed with yogurt and milk, accompanied by the sounds of conchshells, bells and other instruments and the chanting of the //mantra oṁbhagavate vāsudevāya namaḥ,// as well as the chanting of the //Brahma-saṁhitā// verses beginning //cintāmaṇi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-vṛkṣa-lakṣāvṛteṣu surabhīr abhipālayantam.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.6
description: Therefore I very humbly submit that since these incidents have already been nicely described by Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, I would be very proud to repeat the same thing, and this would not be very good. I do not have such powers.
text:
> ataeva tāhā varṇile haya punarukti
> dambha kari' varṇi yadi taiche nāhi śakti
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---such activities; [[synonyms:v:varṇile]]---if describing; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:p:punarukti]]---repetition; [[synonyms:d:dambha]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---being proud; [[synonyms:v:varṇi]]---I describe; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---such; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---power.
translation: Therefore I very humbly submit that since these incidents have already been nicely described by Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, I would be very proud to repeat the same thing, and this would not be very good. I do not have such powers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.60
description: After all inauspicious things were driven away by the chanting of the mantra, the Deity's bathing ceremony started. First the Deity was massaged with a large quantity of oil, so that His body became very glossy.
text:
> amaṅgalā dūra kari' karāila snāna
> bahu taila diyā kaila śrī-aṅga cikkaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:amaṅgalā]]---all inauspiciousness; [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---driving away; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---caused; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---a great quantity; [[synonyms:t:taila]]---oil; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---applying; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the body; [[synonyms:c:cikkaṇa]]---glossy.
translation: After all inauspicious things were driven away by the chanting of the mantra, the Deity's bathing ceremony started. First the Deity was massaged with a large quantity of oil, so that His body became very glossy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.61
description: After the first bathing, further bathings were conducted with pañca-gavya and then with pañcāmṛta. Then the mahā-snāna was performed with ghee and water, which had been brought in one hundred pots.
text:
> pañca-gavya, pañcāmṛte snāna karāñā
> mahā-snāna karāila śata ghaṭa diñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:g:gavya]]---in five kinds of products from the cow; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛte]]---in a preparation made with five palatable foods; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bath; [[synonyms:k:karāñā]]---finishing; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---a vast bath with ghee and water; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---performed; [[synonyms:ś:śata]]---one hundred; [[synonyms:g:ghaṭa]]---waterpots; [[synonyms:d:diñā]]---with.
translation: After the first bathing, further bathings were conducted with pañca-gavya and then with pañcāmṛta. Then the mahā-snāna was performed with ghee and water, which had been brought in one hundred pots.
purport: The ingredients of //pañca-gavya// are milk, yogurt, ghee (clarified butter), cow urine and cow dung. All these items come from the cow; therefore we can just imagine how important the cow is, since its urine and stool are required for bathing the Deity. The //pañcāmṛta// consists of five kinds of nectar-yogurt, milk, ghee, honey and sugar. The major portion of this preparation also comes from the cow. To make it more palatable, sugar and honey are added.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.62
description: After the mahā-snāna was finished, the Deity was again massaged with scented oil and His body made glossy. Then the last bathing ceremony was performed with scented water kept within a conchshell.
text:
> punaḥ taila diya kaila śrī-aṅga cikkaṇa
> śaṅkha-gandhodake kaila snāna samādhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:t:taila]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---with oil; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the body of the Deity; [[synonyms:c:cikkaṇa]]---shiny; [[synonyms:ś:śaṅkha]]-[[synonyms:g:gandha]]-[[synonyms:u:udake]]---in water scented with flowers and sandalwood pulp and kept within a conchshell; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bath; [[synonyms:s:samādhāna]]---execution.
translation: After the mahā-snāna was finished, the Deity was again massaged with scented oil and His body made glossy. Then the last bathing ceremony was performed with scented water kept within a conchshell.
purport: In his commentary on this occasion, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura quotes from the //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa.// Barley powder, wheat powder, vermilion powder, //urad dāl// powder and another powder preparation called //āvāṭā// (made by mixing banana powder and ground rice) are applied to the Deity's body with a brush made from the hair at the end of a cow's tail. This produces a nice finish. The oil smeared over the body of the Deity should be scented. To perform the //mahā-snāna,// at least two and a half //mānas// (about twenty-four gallons) of water are needed to pour over the body of the Deity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.63
description: After the body of the Deity was cleansed, He was dressed very nicely with new garments. Then sandalwood pulp, tulasī garlands and other fragrant flower garlands were placed upon the body of the Deity.
text:
> śrī-aṅga mārjana kari' vastra parāila
> candana, tulasī, puṣpa-mālā aṅge dila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the transcendental body of the Deity; [[synonyms:m:mārjana]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---cleansing; [[synonyms:v:vastra]]---garments; [[synonyms:p:parāila]]---were put on; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood pulp; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]---//tulasī// leaves; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:m:mālā]]---garlands of flowers; [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---on the body; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---were placed.
translation: After the body of the Deity was cleansed, He was dressed very nicely with new garments. Then sandalwood pulp, tulasī garlands and other fragrant flower garlands were placed upon the body of the Deity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.64
description: After the bathing ceremony was finished, incense and lamps were burned and all kinds of food offered before the Deity. These foods included yogurt, milk and as many sweetmeats as were received.
text:
> dhūpa, dīpa, kari' nānā bhoga lāgāila
> dadhi-dugdha-sandeśādi yata kichu āila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dhūpa]]---incense; [[synonyms:d:dīpa]]---lamp; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---burning; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---foods; [[synonyms:l:lāgāila]]---were offered; [[synonyms:d:dadhi]]---yogurt; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]---milk; [[synonyms:s:sandeśa]]---sweetmeats; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and others; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---as much as; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---received.
translation: After the bathing ceremony was finished, incense and lamps were burned and all kinds of food offered before the Deity. These foods included yogurt, milk and as many sweetmeats as were received.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.65
description: The Deity was first offered many varieties of food, then scented drinking water in new pots, and then water for washing the mouth. Finally pan mixed with a variety of spices was offered.
text:
> suvāsita jala nava-pātre samarpila
> ācamana diyā se tāmbūla nivedila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:suvāsita]] [[synonyms:j:jala]]---scented water; [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:p:pātre]]---in new pots; [[synonyms:s:samarpila]]---were offered; [[synonyms:ā:ācamana]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---when offering //ācamana// (water for washing the feet and mouth); [[synonyms:s:se]]---he; [[synonyms:t:tāmbūla]]---pan and spices; [[synonyms:n:nivedila]]---offered.
translation: The Deity was first offered many varieties of food, then scented drinking water in new pots, and then water for washing the mouth. Finally pan mixed with a variety of spices was offered.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.66
description: After the last offering of tāmbūla and pan, bhoga-ārātrika was performed. Finally everyone offered various prayers and then obeisances, falling flat before the Deity in full surrender.
text:
> ārātrika kari' kaila bahuta stavana
> daṇḍavat kari' kaila ātma-samarpaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ārātrika]]---the performance of //ārātrika//; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---finishing; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---chanted; [[synonyms:b:bahuta]]---varieties; [[synonyms:s:stavana]]---of prayers; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---offering; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:s:samarpaṇa]]---self-surrender.
translation: After the last offering of tāmbūla and pan, bhoga-ārātrika was performed. Finally everyone offered various prayers and then obeisances, falling flat before the Deity in full surrender.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.67
description: As soon as the people of the village had understood that the Deity was going to be installed, they had brought their entire stocks of rice, dāl and wheat flour. They brought such large quantities that the entire surface of the top of the hill was filled.
text:
> grāmera yateka taṇḍula, dāli godhūma-cūrṇa
> sakala āniyā dila parvata haila pūrṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:grāmera]]---of the village; [[synonyms:y:yateka]]---all; [[synonyms:t:taṇḍula]]---the rice; [[synonyms:d:dāli]]---//dāl//; [[synonyms:g:godhūma]]-[[synonyms:c:cūrṇa]]---wheat flour; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:ā:āniyā]]---bringing; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---offered; [[synonyms:p:parvata]]---the top of the hill; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---filled.
translation: As soon as the people of the village had understood that the Deity was going to be installed, they had brought their entire stocks of rice, dāl and wheat flour. They brought such large quantities that the entire surface of the top of the hill was filled.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.68
description: When the villagers brought their stock of rice, dāl and flour, the potters of the village brought all kinds of cooking pots, and in the morning the cooking began.
text:
> kumbhakāra ghare chila ye mṛd-bhājana
> saba ānāila prāte, caḍila randhana

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.77
description: Although Śrī Gopāla ate everything offered, still, by the touch of His transcendental hand, everything remained as before.
text:
> yadyapi gopāla saba anna-vyañjana khāila
> tāṅra hasta-sparśe punaḥ temani ha-ila
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:a:anna]]-[[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---//dāl,// rice and vegetables; [[synonyms:k:khāila]]---ate; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:h:hasta]]---of the hands; [[synonyms:s:sparśe]]---by the touch; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:t:temani]]---exactly as before; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became.
translation: Although Śrī Gopāla ate everything offered, still, by the touch of His transcendental hand, everything remained as before.
purport:
The atheists cannot understand how the Supreme Personality of Godhead, appearing in the form of the Deity, can eat all the food offered by His devotees. In the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:26|(Bg. 9.26)]] Kṛṣṇa says:

> patraṁ puṣpaṁ phalaṁ
> toyaṁ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati
> tad ahaṁ bhakty-upahṛtam
> aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ

"If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I will accept it." [[books:bg:9:26|(Bg. 9.26)]] The Lord is //pūrṇa,// complete, and therefore He eats everything offered by His devotees. However, by the touch of His transcendental hand, all the food remains exactly as before. It is the quality that is changed. Before the food was offered, it was something else, but after it is offered the food acquires a transcendental quality. Because the Lord is //pūrṇa,// He remains the same even after eating. //Pūrṇasya pūrṇam ādāya pūrṇam evāvaśiṣyate.// The food offered to Kṛṣṇa is qualitatively as good as Kṛṣṇa; just as Kṛṣṇa is //avyaya,// indestructible, the food eaten by Kṛṣṇa, being identical with Him, remains as before.

Apart from this, Kṛṣṇa can eat the food with any one of His transcendental senses. He can eat by seeing the food or by touching it. Nor should one think that it is necessary for Kṛṣṇa to eat. He does not become hungry like an ordinary human being; nonetheless, He presents Himself as being hungry, and as such, He can eat everything and anything, regardless of quantity. The philosophy underlying Kṛṣṇa's eating is understandable by our transcendental senses. When our senses are purified by constantly being engaged in the devotional service of the Lord, we can understand Kṛṣṇa's activities, names, forms, qualities, pastimes and entourage.

> ataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāmādi
> na bhaved grāhyam indriyaiḥ
> sevonmukhe hi jihvādau
> svayam eva sphuraty adaḥ

"No one can understand Kṛṣṇa by the blunt material senses. But He reveals Himself to the devotees, being pleased with them for their transcendental loving service unto Him." (//Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// 1.2.234) The devotees understand Kṛṣṇa through revelation. It is not possible for a mundane scholar to understand Kṛṣṇa and His pastimes through research work on the nondevotional platform.

translation: How Gopāla ate everything while the food remained the same was transcendentally perceived by Mādhavendra Purī Gosvāmī; nothing remains a secret to the devotees of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.79
description: The wonderful festival and installation of Śrī Gopālajī was arranged in one day. Certainly all this was accomplished by the potency of Gopāla. No one but a devotee can understand this.
text:
> eka-dinera udyoge aiche mahotsava kaila
> gopāla-prabhāve haya, anye nā jānila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dinera]] [[synonyms:u:udyoge]]---by one day's attempt; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:m:mahotsava]]---festival; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---of Gopāla; [[synonyms:p:prabhāve]]---by the potency; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is possible; [[synonyms:a:anye]]---others; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jānila]]---know.
translation: The wonderful festival and installation of Śrī Gopālajī was arranged in one day. Certainly all this was accomplished by the potency of Gopāla. No one but a devotee can understand this.
purport:
The Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement has spread all over the world within a very short time (within five years), and mundane people are very astonished at this. However, by the grace of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, we understand that everything is possible by the grace of Kṛṣṇa. Why does Kṛṣṇa have to take five years? In five days He can spread His name and fame all over the world like wildfire. Those who have faith in and devotion to Kṛṣṇa can understand that these things happen so wonderfully by the grace of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. We are simply the instruments. In the fierce Battle of Kurukṣetra, Arjuna was victorious within eighteen days simply because Kṛṣṇa's grace was on his side.

> yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo
> yatra pārtho dhanur-dharaḥ
> tatra śrīr vijayo bhūtir
> dhruvā nītir matir mama

"Wherever there is Kṛṣṇa, the master of all mystics, and wherever there is Arjuna, the supreme archer, there will also certainly be opulence, victory, extraordinary power and morality. That is my opinion." [[books:bg:18:78|(Bg. 18.78)]]

If the preachers in our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement are sincere devotees of Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa will always be with them because He is very kind and favorable to all His devotees. Just as Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa were victorious in the Battle of Kurukṣetra, this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement will surely emerge victorious if we but remain sincere devotees of the Lord and serve the Lord according to the advice of predecessors (the six Gosvāmīs and other devotees of the Lord). As Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura has stated: //tāṅdera caraṇa sevi bhakta-sane vāsa, janame janame haya ei abhilāṣa.// The Kṛṣṇa consciousness devotees must always desire to remain in the society of devotees. //Bhakta-sane vāsa:// they cannot go outside the Kṛṣṇa conscious society or the movement. Within the society we must try to serve the predecessors by preaching Caitanya Mahāprabhu's cult and spreading His name and fame all over the world. If we attempt this seriously within the society, it will be successfully done. There is no question of estimating how this will happen in the mundane sense. But without a doubt, it happens by the grace of Kṛṣṇa.

> sabe vasi' krame krame bhojana karila
> brāhmaṇa-brāhmaṇī-gaṇe āge khāoyāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting; [[synonyms:k:krame]] [[synonyms:k:krame]]---by and by; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---honored //prasāda// and ate it; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the //brāhmaṇas// and their wives; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---first; [[synonyms:k:khāoyāila]]---were fed.
translation: All the people gathered there sat down to honor the prasāda, and by and by they took food. All the brāhmaṇas and their wives were fed first.
purport: According to the //varṇāśrama// system, the //brāhmaṇas// are always honored first. Thus at the festival, the //brāhmaṇas// and their wives were first offered the remnants of food, and then the others (//kṣatriyas, vaiśyas// and //śūdras//). This has always been the system, and it is still prevalent in India, even though the caste //brāhmaṇas// are not qualified. The system is still current due to the //varṇāśrama// institutional rules and regulations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.85
description: Not only did the people of Govardhana village take prasāda, but also those who came from other villages. They also saw the Deity of Gopāla and were offered prasāda to eat.
text:
> anya grāmera loka yata dekhite āila
> gopāla dekhiyā saba prasāda khāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anya]]---other; [[synonyms:g:grāmera]]---of the villages; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---remnants of food; [[synonyms:k:khāila]]---partook.
translation: Not only did the people of Govardhana village take prasāda, but also those who came from other villages. They also saw the Deity of Gopāla and were offered prasāda to eat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.86
description: Seeing the influence of Mādhavendra Purī, all the people gathered there were struck with wonder. They saw that the Annakūṭa ceremony, which had been performed before during the time of Kṛṣṇa, was now taking place again by the mercy of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī.
text:
> dekhiyā purīra prabhāva loke camatkāra
> pūrva annakūṭa yena haila sākṣātkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---by seeing; [[synonyms:p:purīra]]---of Mādhavendra Purī; [[synonyms:p:prabhāva]]---the influence; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---all the people; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---struck with wonder; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]---formerly; [[synonyms:a:anna]]-[[synonyms:k:kūṭa]]---the Annakūṭa ceremony during the time of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:s:sākṣātkāra]]---directly manifest.
translation: Seeing the influence of Mādhavendra Purī, all the people gathered there were struck with wonder. They saw that the Annakūṭa ceremony, which had been performed before during the time of Kṛṣṇa, was now taking place again by the mercy of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī.
purport:
Formerly, at the end of Dvāpara-yuga, all the cowherd men of Vṛndāvana had arranged to worship King Indra, but they gave this worship up, following the advice of Kṛṣṇa. Instead, they performed a ceremony whereby they worshiped the cows, //brāhmaṇas// and Govardhana Hill. At that time Kṛṣṇa expanded Himself and declared, "I am Govardhana Hill." In this way He accepted all the paraphernalia and food offered to Govardhana Hill. It is stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.24.26, 31-33):

> pacyantāṁ vividhāḥ pākāḥ
> sūpāntāḥ pāyasādayaḥ
> saṁyāvā-pūpa-śaṣkulyaḥ
> sarva-dohaś ca gṛhyatām

> kālātmanā bhagavatā
> śakra-darpaṁ jighāṁsatā
> proktaṁ niśamya nandādyāḥ
> sādhv agṛhṇanta tad-vacaḥ
>
> tathā ca vyadadhuḥ sarvaṁ
> yathāha madhusūdanaḥ
> vācayitvā svasty-ayanaṁ
> tad-dravyeṇa giri-dvijān
>
> upahṛtya balīn sarvān
> ādṛtā yavasaṁ gavām
> go-dhanāni puras-kṛtya
> giriṁ cakruḥ pradakṣiṇam

“ 'Prepare very nice foods of all descriptions from the grains and ghee collected for the //yajña.// Prepare rice, //dāl,// then halavah, //pākorā, purī// and all kinds of milk preparations like sweet rice, sweetballs, //sandeśa, rasagullā// and //lāḍḍu.//'

"The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, therefore advised the cowherd men to stop the Indra-yajña and begin the Govardhana-pūjā to chastise Indra, who was very much puffed up at being the supreme controller of the heavenly planets. The honest and simple cowherd men, headed by Nanda Mahārāja, accepted Kṛṣṇa's proposal and executed in detail everything He advised. They performed Govardhana worship and circumambulation of the hill. According to the instruction of Lord Kṛṣṇa, Nanda Mahārāja and the cowherd men called in learned //brāhmaṇas// and began to worship Govardhana Hill by chanting Vedic hymns and offering //prasāda.// The inhabitants of Vṛndāvana assembled together, decorated their cows and gave them grass. Keeping the cows in front, they began to circumambulate Govardhana Hill."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.87
description: All the brāhmaṇas present on that occasion were initiated by Mādhavendra Purī into the Vaiṣṇava cult, and Mādhavendra Purī engaged them in different types of service.
text:
> sakala brāhmaṇe purī vaiṣṇava karila
> sei sei sevā-madhye sabā niyojila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakala]] [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇe]]---all the //brāhmaṇas// who were present there; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Mādhavendra Purī Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---elevated to the position of Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:sei]]---under different divisions; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in rendering service; [[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all of them; [[synonyms:n:niyojila]]---were engaged.
translation: All the brāhmaṇas present on that occasion were initiated by Mādhavendra Purī into the Vaiṣṇava cult, and Mādhavendra Purī engaged them in different types of service.
purport:
In the scriptures it is stated: //ṣaṭ-karma-nipuṇo vipro mantra-tantra-viśāradaḥ.// A qualified //brāhmaṇa// must be expert in the occupational duties of a //brāhmaṇa.// His duties are mentioned as six brahminical engagements. //Paṭhana// means that a //brāhmaṇa// must be conversant with the Vedic scriptures. He must also be able to teach others to study the Vedic scriptures. This is //pāṭhana.// He must also be expert in worshiping different deities and in performing the Vedic rituals (//yajana//). On account of this //yajana,// the //brāhmaṇa,// being the head of society, performs all the Vedic rituals for //kṣatriyas, vaiśyas,// and //śūdras.// This is called //yājana,// assisting others in performing ceremonies. The remaining two items are //dāna// and //pratigraha.// The //brāhmaṇa// accepts all kinds of contributions (//pratigraha//) from his followers (namely, the //kṣatriyas, vaiśyas// and //śūdras//). But he does not keep all the money. He keeps only as much as required and gives the balance to others in charity (//dāna//).

In order for such a qualified //brāhmaṇa// to worship the Deity, he must be a Vaiṣṇava. Thus the Vaiṣṇava's position is superior to that of the //brāhmaṇa.// This example given by Mādhavendra Purī confirms that even though a //brāhmaṇa// may be very expert, he cannot become a priest or servitor of the //viṣṇu-mūrti// unless he is initiated in //vaiṣṇava-mantra.// After installing the Deity of Gopāla, Mādhavendra Purī initiated all the //brāhmaṇas// into Vaiṣṇavism. He then allotted the //brāhmaṇas// different types of service to the Deity. From four in the morning until ten at night (from //maṅgala-ārātrika// to //śayana-ārātrika//), there must be at least five or six //brāhmaṇas// to take care of the Deity. Six //ārātrikas// are performed in the temple, and food is frequently offered to the Deity and the //prasāda// distributed. This is the method of worshiping the Deity according to the rules and regulations set by predecessors. Our //sampradāya// belongs to the disciplic succession of Mādhavendra Purī, who belonged to the Madhva-sampradāya. We are in the disciplic succession of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who was initiated by Śrī Īśvara Purī, a disciple of Mādhavendra Purī's. Our //sampradāya// is therefore called the Madhva-Gauḍīya-sampradāya. As such, we must carefully follow in the footsteps of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī and observe how he installed the Gopāla Deity on top of Govardhana Hill, how he arranged and performed the Annakūṭa ceremony in only one day, and so forth. Our installation of Deities in America and in the wealthy countries of Europe should be carried out in terms of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī's activities. All the servitors of the Deity must be strictly qualified as //brāhmaṇas// and, specifically, must engage in the Vaiṣṇava custom of offering as much //prasāda// as possible and distributing it to the devotees who visit the temple to see the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.88
description: After taking rest, the Deity must be awakened at the end of the day, and immediately some food and some water must be offered to Him.
text:
> punaḥ dina-śeṣe prabhura karāila utthāna
> kichu bhoga lāgāila karāila jala-pāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:d:dina]]-[[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---at the end of the day; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---caused to do; [[synonyms:u:utthāna]]---rising; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---food; [[synonyms:l:lāgāila]]---offered; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---caused to do; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---water; [[synonyms:p:pāna]]---drinking.
translation: After taking rest, the Deity must be awakened at the end of the day, and immediately some food and some water must be offered to Him.
purport: This offering is called //vaikāli-bhoga,// food offered at the end of the day.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.89
description: When it was advertised throughout the country that Lord Gopāla had appeared atop Govardhana Hill, all the people from neighboring villages came to see the Deity.
text:
> gopāla prakaṭa haila,---deśe śabda haila
> āśa-pāśa grāmera loka dekhite āila
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭa]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---has appeared; [[synonyms:d:deśe]]---throughout the country; [[synonyms:ś:śabda]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---the news spread; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---neighboring; [[synonyms:g:grāmera]]---of the villages; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]] [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came to see.
translation: When it was advertised throughout the country that Lord Gopāla had appeared atop Govardhana Hill, all the people from neighboring villages came to see the Deity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.9
description: I thus offer my respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura. I hope that I will not offend his lotus feet by this action.
text:
> ataeva tāṅra pāye kari namaskāra
> tāṅra pāya aparādha nā ha-uk āmāra

translation: I thus offer my respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura. I hope that I will not offend his lotus feet by this action.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.90
description: One village after another was pleased to beg Mādhavendra Purī to allot them one day to perform the Annakūṭa ceremony. Thus, day after day, the Annakūṭa ceremony was performed for some time.
text:
> ekeka dina ekeka grāme la-ila māgiñā
> anna-kūṭa kare sabe haraṣita hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ekekadina]]---one day after another; [[synonyms:e:ekeka]] [[synonyms:g:grāme]]---one village after another; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---took permission; [[synonyms:m:māgiñā]]---begging; [[synonyms:a:anna]]-[[synonyms:k:kūṭa]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform the Annakūṭa ceremony; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:h:haraṣita]]---pleased; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming.
translation: One village after another was pleased to beg Mādhavendra Purī to allot them one day to perform the Annakūṭa ceremony. Thus, day after day, the Annakūṭa ceremony was performed for some time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.91
description: Śrī Mādhavendra Purī did not eat anything throughout the day, but at night, after laying the Deity down to rest, he took a milk preparation.
text:
> rātri-kāle ṭhākurere karāiyā śayana
> purī-gosāñi kaila kichu gavya bhojana

translation: Śrī Mādhavendra Purī did not eat anything throughout the day, but at night, after laying the Deity down to rest, he took a milk preparation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.92
description: The next morning, the rendering of service to the Deity began again, and people from one village arrived with all kinds of food grains.
text:
> prātaḥ-kāle punaḥ taiche karila sevana
> anna lañā eka-grāmera āila loka-gaṇa
