translation: The next morning, the rendering of service to the Deity began again, and people from one village arrived with all kinds of food grains.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.93
description: The inhabitants of the village brought to the Deity of Gopāla as much food grains, ghee, yogurt and milk as they had in their village.
text:
> anna, ghṛta, dadhi, dugdha,---grāme yata chila
> gopālera āge loka āniyā dharila
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food grain; [[synonyms:g:ghṛta]]---ghee, or clarified butter; [[synonyms:d:dadhi]]---yogurt; [[synonyms:d:dugdha]]---milk; [[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in the village; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---as much; [[synonyms:c:chila]]---as there was; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]] [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---before the Deity Gopāla; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all people; [[synonyms:ā:āniyā]]---bringing; [[synonyms:d:dharila]]---placed.
translation: The inhabitants of the village brought to the Deity of Gopāla as much food grains, ghee, yogurt and milk as they had in their village.
purport:
Anna, ghṛta, dadhi and //dugdha// are food grains, ghee, yogurt and milk. Actually these are the basis of all food. Vegetables and fruits are subsidiary. Hundreds and thousands of preparations can be made out of grains, vegetables, ghee, milk and yogurt. The food offered to Gopāla in the Annakūṭa ceremony contained only these five ingredients. Only demoniac people are attracted to other types of food, which we will not even mention in this connection. We should understand that in order to prepare nutritious food, we require only grains, ghee, yogurt and milk. We cannot offer anything else to the Deity. The Vaiṣṇava, the perfect human being, does not accept anything not offered to the Deity. People are often frustrated with national food policies, but from the Vedic scriptures we find that if there are sufficient cows and grains, the entire food problem is solved. The //vaiśyas// (people engaged in agriculture and commerce) are therefore recommended in the //Bhagavad-gītā// to produce grains and give protection to cows. Cows are the most important animal because they produce the miracle food, milk, from which we can prepare ghee and yogurt.

The perfection of human civilization depends on Kṛṣṇa consciousness, which recommends Deity worship. Preparations made from vegetables, grains, milk, ghee and yogurt are offered to the Deity and then distributed. Here we can see the difference between the East and the West. The people who came to see the Deity of Gopāla brought all kinds of food to offer the Deity. They brought all the food they had in stock, and they came before the Deity not only to accept //prasāda// for themselves but to distribute it to others. The Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement vigorously approves this practice of preparing food, offering it to the Deity and distributing it to the general population. This activity should be extended universally to stop sinful eating habits as well as other behavior befitting only demons. A demoniac civilization will never bring peace within the world. Since eating is the first necessity in human society, those engaged in solving the problems of preparing and distributing food should take lessons from Mādhavendra Purī and execute the Annakūṭa ceremony. When the people take to eating only //prasāda// offered to the Deity, all the demons will be turned into Vaiṣṇavas. When the people are Kṛṣṇa conscious, naturally the government will be so also. A Kṛṣṇa conscious man is always a very liberal well-wisher of everyone. When such men head the government, the people will certainly be sinless. They will no longer be disturbing demons. It is then and then only that a peaceful condition can prevail in society.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.94
description: The next day, almost like before, there was an Annakūṭa ceremony. All the brāhmaṇas prepared foods and Gopāla accepted them.
text:
> pūrva-dina-prāya vipra karila randhana
> taiche anna-kūṭa gopāla karila bhojana

translation: The next day, almost like before, there was an Annakūṭa ceremony. All the brāhmaṇas prepared foods and Gopāla accepted them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.95
description: The ideal place to execute Kṛṣṇa consciousness is Vrajabhūmi, or Vṛndāvana, where the people are naturally inclined to love Kṛṣṇa and Kṛṣṇa is naturally inclined to love them.
text:
> vraja-vāsī lokera kṛṣṇe sahaja pirīti
> gopālera sahaja-prīti vraja-vāsi-prati
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana (Vrajabhūmi); [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of the people; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sahaja]]---natural; [[synonyms:p:pirīti]]---love; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:s:sahaja]]---natural; [[synonyms:p:prīti]]---love; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsi]]-[[synonyms:p:prati]]---toward the inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi.
translation: The ideal place to execute Kṛṣṇa consciousness is Vrajabhūmi, or Vṛndāvana, where the people are naturally inclined to love Kṛṣṇa and Kṛṣṇa is naturally inclined to love them.
purport:
In the //Bhagavad-gītā// it is said: //ye yathā māṁ prapadyante tāṁs tathaiva bhajāmy aham.// There is a responsive cooperation between the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa and His devotees. The more a devotee sincerely loves Kṛṣṇa, the more Kṛṣṇa reciprocates, so much so that a highly advanced devotee can talk with Kṛṣṇa face to face. Kṛṣṇa confirms this in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:10:10|(Bg. 10.10)]]:

> teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ
> bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam
> dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ
> yena mām upayānti te

"To those who are constantly devoted to worshiping Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me." The actual mission of human life is to understand Kṛṣṇa and return home, back to Godhead. Therefore one who is sincerely engaged in the service of the Lord with love and faith can talk with Kṛṣṇa and receive instructions by which he can speedily return home, back to Godhead. Today many scholars defend the science of religion, and they have some conception of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but religion without practical experience of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is no religion at all. //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// describes this as a form of cheating. Religion means abiding by the orders of Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. If one is not qualified to talk with Him and take lessons from Him, how can one understand the principles of religion? Thus talks of religion or religious experience without Kṛṣṇa consciousness are a useless waste of time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.96
description: Throngs of people came from different villages to see the Deity of Gopāla, and they took mahā-prasāda sumptuously. When they saw the superexcellent form of Lord Gopāla, all their lamentation and unhappiness disappeared.
text:
> mahā-prasāda khāila āsiyā saba loka
> gopāla dekhiyā sabāra khaṇḍe duḥkha-śoka
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---spiritualized foods offered to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:khāila]]---ate; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the Deity of Śrī Gopāla; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍe]]---disappears; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]-[[synonyms:ś:śoka]]---all lamentation and unhappiness.
translation: Throngs of people came from different villages to see the Deity of Gopāla, and they took mahā-prasāda sumptuously. When they saw the superexcellent form of Lord Gopāla, all their lamentation and unhappiness disappeared.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.97
description: All the villages in neighboring Vrajabhūmi [Vṛndāvana] became aware of the appearance of Gopāla, and all the people from these villages came to see Him. Day after day they all performed the Annakūṭa ceremony.
text:
> āśa-pāśa vraja-bhūmera yata grāma saba
> eka eka dina sabe kare mahotsava
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---neighboring; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūmera]]---of Vrajabhūmi; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:g:grāma]]---villages; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one after another; [[synonyms:d:dina]]---days; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:u:utsava]]---festivals.
translation: All the villages in neighboring Vrajabhūmi [Vṛndāvana] became aware of the appearance of Gopāla, and all the people from these villages came to see Him. Day after day they all performed the Annakūṭa ceremony.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.98
description: In this way not only the neighboring villages but all the other provinces came to know of Gopāla's appearance. Thus people came from all over, bringing a variety of presentations.
text:
> gopāla-prakaṭa śuni' nānā deśa haite
> nānā dravya lañā loka lāgila āsite
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---of the Deity of Gopāla; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭa]]---appearance; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:d:deśa]]---countries; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:d:dravya]]---things; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---bringing; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began; [[synonyms:ā:āsite]]---to come.
translation: In this way not only the neighboring villages but all the other provinces came to know of Gopāla's appearance. Thus people came from all over, bringing a variety of presentations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 4.99
description: The people of Mathurā, who are very big capitalists, also brought various presentations and offered them before the Deity in devotional service.
text:
> mathurāra loka saba baḍa baḍa dhanī
> bhakti kari' nānā dravya bheṭa deya āni'
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mathurāra]]---of the city of Mathurā; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very big; [[synonyms:d:dhanī]]---capitalists; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---out of devotion; [[synonyms:n:nānā]] [[synonyms:d:dravya]]---various kinds of things; [[synonyms:b:bheṭa]]---presents; [[synonyms:d:deya]]---gave; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing.
translation: The people of Mathurā, who are very big capitalists, also brought various presentations and offered them before the Deity in devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.1
description: I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of God [brahmaṇya-deva], who appeared as Sākṣi-gopāla to benefit a brāhmaṇa. For one hundred days He traveled through the country, walking on His own legs. Thus His activities are wonderful.
text:
> padbhyāṁ calan yaḥ pratimā-svarūpo
> brahmaṇya-devo hi śatāha-gamyam
> deśaṁ yayau vipra-kṛte 'dbhutehaṁ
> taṁ sākṣi-gopālam ahaṁ nato 'smi
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:padbhyām]]---by the two legs; [[synonyms:c:calan]]---walking; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---one who; [[synonyms:p:pratimā]]---of the Deity; [[synonyms:s:svarūpaḥ]]---in the form; [[synonyms:b:brahmaṇya]]-[[synonyms:d:devaḥ]]---the Supreme Lord of brahminical culture; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:ś:śata]]-[[synonyms:ā:āha]]---in one hundred days; [[synonyms:g:gamyam]]---to be passed over; [[synonyms:d:deśam]]---the country; [[synonyms:y:yayau]]---went; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛte]]---for the benefit of a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---most wonderful; [[synonyms:ī:īham]]---activity; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---unto that; [[synonyms:s:sākṣi]]-[[synonyms:g:gopālam]]---the Gopāla known as the witness Gopāla; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nataḥ]] [[synonyms:a:asmi]]---offer respectful obeisances.
translation: I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of God [brahmaṇya-deva], who appeared as Sākṣi-gopāla to benefit a brāhmaṇa. For one hundred days He traveled through the country, walking on His own legs. Thus His activities are wonderful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.10
description: Formerly at Vidyānagara in South India there were two brāhmaṇas who made a long tour to see different places of pilgrimage.
text:
> pūrve vidyānagarera dui ta' brāhmaṇa
> tīrtha karibāre duṅhe karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---previously; [[synonyms:v:vidyānagarera]]---of the town known as Vidyānagara; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---//brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]] [[synonyms:k:karibāre]]---to tour places of pilgrimage; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---began; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---journey.
translation: Formerly at Vidyānagara in South India there were two brāhmaṇas who made a long tour to see different places of pilgrimage.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.100
description: "Cook one kilogram of rice daily and offer it. I shall eat that rice and follow behind you."
text:
> eka-sera anna rāndhi' kariha samarpaṇa
> tāhā khāñā tomāra saṅge kariba gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:s:sera]]---one kilogram; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---of rice; [[synonyms:r:rāndhi']]---cooking; [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do; [[synonyms:s:samarpaṇa]]---offering; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:khāñā]]---eating; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of you; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the company; [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---I shall do; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---walking.
translation: "Cook one kilogram of rice daily and offer it. I shall eat that rice and follow behind you."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.101
description: The next day, the brāhmaṇa begged permission from Gopāla and started for his country. Gopāla followed him, step by step.
text:
> āra dina ājñā māgi' calilā brāhmaṇa
> tāra pāche pāche gopāla karilā gamana

translation: The next day, the brāhmaṇa begged permission from Gopāla and started for his country. Gopāla followed him, step by step.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.102
description: While Gopāla followed the young brāhmaṇa, the tinkling sound of His ankle bells could be heard. The brāhmaṇa became very pleased, and he cooked first-class rice for Gopāla to eat.
text:
> nūpurera dhvani śuni' ānandita mana
> uttamānna pāka kari' karāya bhojana

translation: While Gopāla followed the young brāhmaṇa, the tinkling sound of His ankle bells could be heard. The brāhmaṇa became very pleased, and he cooked first-class rice for Gopāla to eat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.103
description: The young brāhmaṇa walked and walked in this way until he eventually arrived in his own country. When he neared his own village, he began to think as follows.
text:
> ei-mate cali' vipra nija-deśe āilā
> grāmera nikaṭa āsi' manete cintilā

translation: The young brāhmaṇa walked and walked in this way until he eventually arrived in his own country. When he neared his own village, he began to think as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.104
description: "I have now come to my village, and I shall go to my home and tell all the people that the witness has arrived."
text:

translation: "I have now come to my village, and I shall go to my home and tell all the people that the witness has arrived."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.105
description: The brāhmaṇa then began to think that if the people didn't directly see the Gopāla Deity, they would not believe that He had arrived. "But even if Gopāla stays here," he thought, "there is still nothing to fear."
text:

translation: The brāhmaṇa then began to think that if the people didn't directly see the Gopāla Deity, they would not believe that He had arrived. "But even if Gopāla stays here," he thought, "there is still nothing to fear."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.106

translation: Thinking this, the brāhmaṇa turned to look back, and He saw that Gopāla, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, was standing there smiling.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.107

translation: The young brāhmaṇa then went to the town and informed all the people about Gopāla's arrival. Hearing this, the people were struck with wonder.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.109

translation: All the townspeople went to see the witness Gopāla, and when they saw the Lord actually standing there, they all offered their respectful obeisances.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.11
description: First of all they visited Gayā, then Kāśī, then Prayāga. Finally, with great pleasure, they came to Mathurā.

> gayā, vārāṇasī, prayāga---sakala kariyā

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.110
description: When the people arrived, they were very pleased to see the beauty of Gopāla, and when they heard that He had actually walked there, they were all surprised.

translation: When the people arrived, they were very pleased to see the beauty of Gopāla, and when they heard that He had actually walked there, they were all surprised.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.111

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.112

text:
> sakala lokera āge gopāla sākṣī dila
> baḍa-vipra choṭa-vipre kanyā-dāna kaila

translation: Thus in the presence of all the townspeople, Lord Gopāla bore witness that the elderly brāhmaṇa had offered his daughter in charity to the young brāhmaṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.113
description: After the marriage ceremony was performed, the Lord informed both brāhmaṇas, "You two brāhmaṇas are My eternal servants, birth after birth."
text:
> tabe sei dui vipre kahila īśvara
> "tumi-dui---janme-janme āmāra kiṅkara
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:v:vipre]]---unto the //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---spoke; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]-[[synonyms:d:dui]]---both of you; [[synonyms:j:janme]]-[[synonyms:j:janme]]---birth after birth; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:k:kiṅkara]]---servants.
translation: After the marriage ceremony was performed, the Lord informed both brāhmaṇas, "You two brāhmaṇas are My eternal servants, birth after birth."
purport:
Like these two //brāhmaṇas// of Vidyānagara, there are many devotees who are eternal servants of the Lord. They are specifically known as //nitya-siddha,// eternally perfect. Although the //nitya-siddhas// appear in the material world and seem to be common members of the world, they never forget the Supreme Personality of Godhead in any condition. This is the symptom of a //nitya-siddha.//

There are two kinds of living entities-//nitya-siddha// and //nitya-baddha.// The //nitya-siddha// never forgets his relationship with the Supreme Personality, whereas the //nitya-baddha// is always conditioned, even before the creation. He always forgets his relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Here the Lord informs the two //brāhmaṇas// that they are His servants birth after birth. The phrase birth after birth refers to the material world because in the spiritual world there is no birth, death, old age or disease. By the order of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the //nitya-siddha// remains within this material world like an ordinary man, but the only business of the //nitya-siddha// is to broadcast the glories of the Lord. This incident appears to be an ordinary story about a marriage transaction involving two ordinary people. However, Kṛṣṇa accepted the two //brāhmaṇas// as His eternal servants. Both //brāhmaṇas// took much trouble in these negotiations, just like mundane people, yet they were acting as eternal servants of the Lord. All //nitya-siddhas// within this material world may appear to toil like ordinary men, but they never forget their position as servants of the Lord.

Another point: The elderly //brāhmaṇa// belonged to an aristocratic family and was learned and wealthy. The young //brāhmaṇa// belonged to an ordinary family and was uneducated. But these mundane qualifications do not concern a //nitya-siddha// engaged in the service of the Lord. We have to accept the fact that the //nitya-siddhas// are completely distinct from the //nitya-baddhas,// who are ordinary human beings. Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura confirms this statement:

> gaurāṅgera saṅgi-gaṇe,    nitya-siddha kari' māne,
> se yāya vrajendra-suta-pāśa
> śrī-gauḍa-maṇḍala-bhūmi, yebā jāne cintāmaṇi,
> tāra haya vraja-bhūme vāsa

One who accepts the associates of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu as //nitya-siddhas// is certain to be elevated to the spiritual kingdom to become an associate of the Supreme Lord. One should also know that Gauḍa-maṇḍala-bhūmi---those places in Bengal where Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stayed-are equal to Vrajabhūmi, or Vṛndāvana. There is no difference between the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana and those of Gauḍa-maṇḍala-bhūmi, or Śrīdhāma Māyāpura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.114
description: The Lord continued, "I have become very pleased by the truthfulness of you both. Now you can ask for a benediction." Thus with great pleasure the two brāhmaṇas begged for a benediction.
text:
> duṅhāra satye tuṣṭa ha-ilāṅ, duṅhe māga' vara"
> dui-vipra vara māge ānanda-antara
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]] [[synonyms:s:satye]]---in the truthfulness of both of you; [[synonyms:t:tuṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilāṅ]]---I have be come satisfied; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of you; [[synonyms:m:māga']]---ask; [[synonyms:v:vara]]---some benediction; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:v:vipra]]---both the //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:v:vara]]---a benediction; [[synonyms:m:māge]]---beg; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---pleased; [[synonyms:a:antara]]---within.
translation: The Lord continued, "I have become very pleased by the truthfulness of you both. Now you can ask for a benediction." Thus with great pleasure the two brāhmaṇas begged for a benediction.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.115
description: The brāhmaṇas said, "Please remain here so that people all over the world will know how merciful You are to Your servants."
text:
> "yadi vara dibe, tabe raha ei sthāne
> kiṅkarere dayā tava sarva-loke jāne"
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:v:vara]]---benediction; [[synonyms:d:dibe]]---You will offer; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:r:raha]]---stay; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in this quarter; [[synonyms:k:kiṅkarere]]---to Your servants; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:l:loke]]---all people; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---may know.
translation: The brāhmaṇas said, "Please remain here so that people all over the world will know how merciful You are to Your servants."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.116
description: Lord Gopāla stayed, and the two brāhmaṇas engaged in His service. After hearing of the incident, many people from different countries began to come to see Gopāla.
text:
> gopāla rahilā, duṅhe karena sevana
> dekhite āilā saba deśera loka-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---stayed; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---do; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---service; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:d:deśera]]---of the countries; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---the people.
translation: Lord Gopāla stayed, and the two brāhmaṇas engaged in His service. After hearing of the incident, many people from different countries began to come to see Gopāla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.117
description: Eventually the King of that country heard of this wonderful story, and he also came to see Gopāla and thus became very satisfied.
text:
> se deśera rājā āila āścarya śuniñā
> parama santoṣa pāila gopāle dekhiñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:d:deśera]]---of that country; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:ā:āścarya]]---about the wonder; [[synonyms:ś:śuniñā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---great; [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---satisfaction; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---achieved; [[synonyms:g:gopāle]]---Gopāla; [[synonyms:d:dekhiñā]]---by seeing.
translation: Eventually the King of that country heard of this wonderful story, and he also came to see Gopāla and thus became very satisfied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.118
description: The King constructed a nice temple, and regular service was executed. Gopāla became very famous under the name of Sākṣi-gopāla [the witness Gopāla].
text:
> mandira kariyā rājā sevā cālāila
> 'sākṣi-gopāla' bali' tāṅra nāma khyāti haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mandira]]---a temple; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---constructing; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---service; [[synonyms:c:cālāila]]---regularly carried on; [[synonyms:s:sākṣi]]-[[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---by the name Sākṣi-gopāla; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---known as; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---name; [[synonyms:k:khyāti]]---celebrated; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was.
translation: The King constructed a nice temple, and regular service was executed. Gopāla became very famous under the name of Sākṣi-gopāla [the witness Gopāla].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.119
description: Thus Sākṣi-gopāla stayed in Vidyānagara and accepted service for a very long time.
text:
> ei mata vidyānagare sākṣi-gopāla
> sevā aṅgīkāra kari' āchena cira-kāla
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:v:vidyānagare]]---in the town of Vidyānagara; [[synonyms:s:sākṣi]]-[[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the witness Gopāla; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---service; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---acceptance; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:ā:āchena]]---remains; [[synonyms:c:cira]]-[[synonyms:k:kāla]]---a long time.
translation: Thus Sākṣi-gopāla stayed in Vidyānagara and accepted service for a very long time.
purport: This city of Vidyānagara is situated in Trailaṅga-deśa, South India, on the bank of the river Godāvarī. The place where the Godāvarī flows into the Bay of Bengal is called Koṭadeśa. The Orissa kingdom was very powerful, and this Koṭadeśa was the capital of Orissa. It was then known as Vidyānagara. Formerly this city was situated on the southern side of the river Godāvarī. At that time King Puruṣottama-deva managed to control Orissa and appoint a government. The present city of Vidyānagara is on the southeast side of the river, only twenty to twenty-five miles from Rājamahendrī. During the time of Mahārāja Pratāparudra, Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya was the governor there. Vijaya-nagara is not identical with Vidyānagara.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.12
description: After reaching Mathurā, they started visiting the different forests of Vṛndāvana and came to Govardhana Hill. They visited all twelve forests [vanas] and at last came to the town of Vṛndāvana.
text:
> vana-yātrāya vana dekhi' dekhe govardhana
> dvādaśa-vana dekhi' śeṣe gelā vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vana]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrāya]]---in touring the different forests; [[synonyms:v:vana]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---while seeing the forests; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---they see; [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]---Govardhana Hill; [[synonyms:d:dvādaśa]]-[[synonyms:v:vana]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---visiting the twelve forests in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---at last; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---reached; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana.
translation: After reaching Mathurā, they started visiting the different forests of Vṛndāvana and came to Govardhana Hill. They visited all twelve forests [vanas] and at last came to the town of Vṛndāvana.
purport: The five forests situated on the eastern side of the river Yamunā are Bhadra, Bilva, Loha, Bhāṇḍīra and Mahāvana. The seven forests situated on the western side of the Yamunā are Madhu, Tāla, Kumuda, Bahulā, Kāmya, Khadira and Vṛndāvana. After visiting all these forests, these pilgrims went to a place known as Pañcakrośī Vṛndāvana. Out of the twelve forests, the Vṛndāvana forest extends from the town of Vṛndāvana up to Nanda-grāma and Varṣāṇa, a distance of thirty-two miles, within which the Pañcakrośī Vṛndāvana town is situated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.120
description: Later there was a fight, and this country was conquered by King Puruṣottama-deva of Orissa.
text:
> utkalera rājā puruṣottama-deva nāma
> sei deśa jini' nila kariyā saṅgrāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:utkalera]]---of Orissa; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]---the King; [[synonyms:p:puruṣottama]]-[[synonyms:d:deva]]---Puruṣottama-deva; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:deśa]]---this country; [[synonyms:j:jini']]---conquering; [[synonyms:n:nila]]---took; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---executing; [[synonyms:s:saṅgrāma]]---fight.
translation: Later there was a fight, and this country was conquered by King Puruṣottama-deva of Orissa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.121
description: That King was victorious over the King of Vidyānagara, and he took possession of his throne, the Māṇikya-siṁhāsana, which was bedecked with many jewels.
text:
> sei rājā jini' nila tāṅra siṁhāsana
> 'māṇikya-siṁhāsana' nāma aneka ratana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:seirājā]]---that King (Mahārāja Puruṣottama-deva); [[synonyms:j:jini']]---conquering; [[synonyms:n:nila]]---took; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:s:siṁha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsana]]---the throne; [[synonyms:m:māṇikya]]-[[synonyms:s:siṁhāsana]]---the throne known as Māṇikya-siṁhāsana; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:a:aneka]]---various; [[synonyms:r:ratana]]---bedecked with jewels.
translation: That King was victorious over the King of Vidyānagara, and he took possession of his throne, the Māṇikya-siṁhāsana, which was bedecked with many jewels.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.122
description: King Puruṣottama-deva was a great devotee and was advanced in the civilization of the Āryans. He begged at the lotus feet of Gopāla, "Please come to my kingdom."
text:
> puruṣottama-deva sei baḍa bhakta ārya
> gopāla-caraṇe māge,---'cala mora rājya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:puruṣottama]]-[[synonyms:d:deva]]---King Puruṣottama-deva; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very great; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotee; [[synonyms:ā:ārya]]---Āryan; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the lotus feet of Gopāla; [[synonyms:m:māge]]---begs; [[synonyms:c:cala]]---please come; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:r:rājya]]---to the kingdom.
translation: King Puruṣottama-deva was a great devotee and was advanced in the civilization of the Āryans. He begged at the lotus feet of Gopāla, "Please come to my kingdom."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.123
description: When the King begged Him to come to his kingdom, Gopāla, who was already obliged for his devotional service, accepted his prayer. Thus the King took the Gopāla Deity and went back to Kaṭaka.
text:
> tāṅra bhakti-vaśe gopāla tāṅre ājñā dila
> gopāla la-iyā sei kaṭake āila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśe]]---under the obligation of the devotional service; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave the order; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the Gopāla Deity; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:iyā]]---taking; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that King; [[synonyms:k:kaṭake]]---to the city of Kaṭaka; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---returned.
translation: When the King begged Him to come to his kingdom, Gopāla, who was already obliged for his devotional service, accepted his prayer. Thus the King took the Gopāla Deity and went back to Kaṭaka.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.124
description: After winning the Māṇikya throne, King Puruṣottama-deva took it to Jagannātha Purī and presented it to Lord Jagannātha. In the meantime, he also established regular worship of the Gopāla Deity at Kaṭaka.
text:
> jagannāthe āni' dila māṇikya-siṁhāsana
> kaṭake gopāla-sevā karila sthāpana
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannāthe]]---unto Jagannātha; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---presented; [[synonyms:m:māṇikya]]-[[synonyms:s:siṁhāsana]]---the throne of the name Māṇikya-siṁhāsana; [[synonyms:k:kaṭake]]---at Kaṭaka; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]]---the service of the Gopāla Deity; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:s:sthāpana]]---established.
translation: After winning the Māṇikya throne, King Puruṣottama-deva took it to Jagannātha Purī and presented it to Lord Jagannātha. In the meantime, he also established regular worship of the Gopāla Deity at Kaṭaka.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.125
description: When the Gopāla Deity was installed at Kaṭaka, the Queen of Puruṣottama-deva went to see Him and, with great devotion, presented various kinds of ornaments.
text:
> tāṅhāra mahiṣī āilā gopāla-darśane
> bhakti kari' bahu alaṅkāra kaila samarpaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāramahiṣī]]---his Queen; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:d:darśane]]---to see the Gopāla Deity; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---in great devotion; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---various; [[synonyms:a:alaṅkāra]]---of ornaments; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:s:samarpaṇe]]---presentation.
translation: When the Gopāla Deity was installed at Kaṭaka, the Queen of Puruṣottama-deva went to see Him and, with great devotion, presented various kinds of ornaments.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.126
description: The Queen had a very valuable pearl, which she wore on her nose, and she wished to give it to Gopāla. She then began to think as follows.
text:
> tāṅhāra nāsāte bahu-mūlya muktā haya
> tāhā dite icchā haila, manete cintaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāranāsāte]]---on the nostril of the Queen; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:m:mūlya]]---very valuable; [[synonyms:m:muktā]]---pearl; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there was; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give; [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---the desire; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:m:manete]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:c:cintaya]]---thinks.
translation: The Queen had a very valuable pearl, which she wore on her nose, and she wished to give it to Gopāla. She then began to think as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.127
description: "If there were a hole in the Deity's nose, I could transfer the pearl to Him."
text:
> ṭhākurera nāsāte yadi chidra thākita
> tabe ei dāsī muktā nāsāya parāita
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākurera]] [[synonyms:n:nāsāte]]---in the nose of the Deity; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:c:chidra]]---a hole; [[synonyms:t:thākita]]---there were; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:d:dāsī]]---maidservant; [[synonyms:m:muktā]]---pearl; [[synonyms:n:nāsāya]]---on the nose; [[synonyms:p:parāita]]---could put on.
translation: "If there were a hole in the Deity's nose, I could transfer the pearl to Him."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.128
description: Considering this, the Queen offered her obeisances to Gopāla and returned to her palace. That night she dreamed that Gopāla appeared and began to speak to her as follows.
text:
> eta cinti' namaskari' gelā sva-bhavane
> rātri-śeṣe gopāla tāṅre kahena svapane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:c:cinti']]---thinking like that; [[synonyms:n:namaskari']]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhavane]]---to the palace of the King; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---at the end of night; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the Gopāla Deity; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto her; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---says; [[synonyms:s:svapane]]---in a dream.
translation: Considering this, the Queen offered her obeisances to Gopāla and returned to her palace. That night she dreamed that Gopāla appeared and began to speak to her as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.129
description: "During My childhood My mother made a hole in My nose and with great endeavor set a pearl there.
text:
> "bālya-kāle mātā mora nāsā chidra kari'
> muktā parāñāchila bahu yatna kari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bālya]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in My childhood; [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---mother; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:n:nāsā]]---nose; [[synonyms:c:chidra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making a hole; [[synonyms:m:muktā]]---a pearl; [[synonyms:p:parāñāchila]]---was put on it; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---much; [[synonyms:y:yatna]]---endeavor; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking.
translation: "During My childhood My mother made a hole in My nose and with great endeavor set a pearl there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.13
description: In the village of Pañcakrośī Vṛndāvana, at the site where the Govinda temple is now situated, there was a great temple where gorgeous worship of Gopāla was performed.
text:
> vṛndāvane govinda-sthāne mahā-devālaya
> se mandire gopālera mahā-sevā haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvane]]---within Pañcakrośī Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---at the place where the present Govinda temple is situated; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ālaya]]---a great temple; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:m:mandire]]---in that temple; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of the Deity of Gopāla; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]]---gorgeous worship; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is.
translation: In the village of Pañcakrośī Vṛndāvana, at the site where the Govinda temple is now situated, there was a great temple where gorgeous worship of Gopāla was performed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.130
description: "That very hole is still there, and you can use it to set the pearl you desired to give Me."
text:
> sei chidra adyāpiha āchaye nāsāte
> sei muktā parāha, yāhā cāhiyācha dite"
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:c:chidra]]---that hole; [[synonyms:a:adyāpiha]]---still, until now; [[synonyms:ā:āchaye]]---is; [[synonyms:n:nāsāte]]---in the nose; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:m:muktā]]---pearl; [[synonyms:p:parāha]]---put on; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]]---which; [[synonyms:c:cāhiyācha]]---you desired; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give to Me.
translation: "That very hole is still there, and you can use it to set the pearl you desired to give Me."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.131
description: After dreaming this, the Queen explained it to her husband, the King. Both the King and the Queen then went to the temple with the pearl.
text:
> svapne dekhi' sei rāṇī rājāke kahila
> rājā-saha muktā lañā mandire āila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svapne]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the dream; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:r:rāṇī]]---the Queen; [[synonyms:r:rājāke]]---unto the King; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---spoke; [[synonyms:r:rājā]]-[[synonyms:s:saha]]---with the King; [[synonyms:m:muktā]]---the pearl; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:m:mandire]]---to the temple; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---they went.
translation: After dreaming this, the Queen explained it to her husband, the King. Both the King and the Queen then went to the temple with the pearl.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.132
description: Seeing the hole in the nose of the Deity, they set the pearl there and, being very pleased, held a great festival.
text:
> parāila muktā nāsāya chidra dekhiñā
> mahā-mahotsava kaila ānandita hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:parāila]]---set; [[synonyms:m:muktā]]---the pearl; [[synonyms:n:nāsāya]]---on the nose; [[synonyms:c:chidra]]---the hole; [[synonyms:d:dekhiñā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:m:mahotsava]]---a great festival; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---pleased; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being.
translation: Seeing the hole in the nose of the Deity, they set the pearl there and, being very pleased, held a great festival.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.133
description: Since then, Gopāla has been situated in the city of Kaṭaka [Cuttak], and He has been known ever since as Sākṣi-gopāla.
text:
> sei haite gopālera kaṭakete sthiti
> ei lāgi 'sākṣi-gopāla' nāma haila khyāti
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:seihaite]]---since that time; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of Gopāla; [[synonyms:k:kaṭakete]]---in the town of Kaṭaka; [[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---the establishment; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi]]---for this reason; [[synonyms:s:sākṣi]]-[[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the witness Gopāla; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:k:khyāti]]---celebrated.
translation: Since then, Gopāla has been situated in the city of Kaṭaka [Cuttak], and He has been known ever since as Sākṣi-gopāla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.134

translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard the narration of Gopāla's activities. Both He and His personal devotees became very pleased.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.135

> duṅhe---raktāmbara, duṅhāra svabhāva---gambhīra

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.137

translation: The devotees saw that both Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Gopāla were brilliantly effulgent and had eyes like lotuses. They were both absorbed in ecstasy, and Their faces resembled full moons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.138
description: When Nityānanda saw both the Gopāla Deity and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in that way, He began to exchange remarks with the devotees, all of whom were smiling.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.139

> ei-mata mahā-raṅge se rātri vañciyā
> prabhāte calilā maṅgala-ārati dekhiñā

translation: Thus with great pleasure Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed that night in the temple. After seeing the maṅgala-ārati ceremony in the morning, He started on His journey.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.14
description: After taking baths at different bathing places along the river Yamunā, such as Keśī-ghāṭa and Kāliya-ghāṭa, the pilgrims visited the temple of Gopāla. Afterwards, they took rest in that temple.

> keśī-tīrtha, kālīya-hradādike kaila snāna
> śrī-gopāla dekhi' tāhāṅ karilā viśrāma

translation: After taking baths at different bathing places along the river Yamunā, such as Keśī-ghāṭa and Kāliya-ghāṭa, the pilgrims visited the temple of Gopāla. Afterwards, they took rest in that temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.140
description: [In his book Caitanya-bhāgavata] Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has very vividly described the places visited by the Lord on the way to Bhuvaneśvara.
text:
> bhuvaneśvara-pathe yaiche kaila daraśana
> vistāri' varṇiyāchena dāsa-vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhuvaneśvara]]-[[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way to Bhuvaneśvara; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---He did; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting; [[synonyms:v:vistāri']]---vividly; [[synonyms:v:varṇiyāchena]]---has described; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura.
translation: [In his book Caitanya-bhāgavata] Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has very vividly described the places visited by the Lord on the way to Bhuvaneśvara.
purport: In his book //Caitanya-bhāgavata, Antya-khaṇḍa,// Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has very nicely described the Lord's journey en route to Kaṭaka (Cuttak). On that journey, the Lord visited a place known as Bālihastā, or Bālakāṭīcaṭi. He then visited the city of Bhuvaneśvara, where Lord Śiva's temple is located. The temple of Bhuvaneśvara is situated about five to six miles from Bālakāṭīcaṭi. The temple of Lord Śiva is mentioned in the //Skanda Purāṇa// in the narration about the Lord's garden and the one mango tree. A king named Kāśirāja wanted to fight with Lord Kṛṣṇa, and consequently he took shelter of Lord Śiva to acquire the power to fight the Lord. Being pleased with his worship, Lord Śiva helped him fight Kṛṣṇa. Lord Śiva's name is Āśutoṣa, which indicates that he is very easily satisfied when one worships him, regardless of the purpose, and he gives his devotee whatever benediction the devotee wants. Therefore, people are generally very fond of worshiping Lord Śiva. Thus Kāśirāja was helped by Lord Śiva, but in the fight with Lord Kṛṣṇa he was not only defeated but killed. In this way the weapon known as Pāśupata-astra was baffled, and Kṛṣṇa set fire to the city of Kāśī. Later Lord Śiva became conscious of his mistake in helping Kāśirāja, and he begged Lord Kṛṣṇa's forgiveness. As a benediction from Lord Kṛṣṇa, he received a place known as Ekāmra-kānana. Later, the kings of the Keśarī dynasty established their capital there, and for many hundreds of years they reigned over the state of Orissa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.141
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at Kamalapura, He took His bath in the Bhārgīnadī River and left His sannyāsa staff in the hands of Lord Nityānanda.
text:
> kamalapure āsi bhārgīnadī-snāna kaila
> nityānanda-hāte prabhu daṇḍa dharila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kamala]]-[[synonyms:p:pure]]---to the place known as Kamalapura; [[synonyms:ā:āsi]]---coming; [[synonyms:b:bhārgī]]-[[synonyms:n:nadī]]---in the small river of the name Bhārgīnadī; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---took a bath; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]-[[synonyms:h:hāte]]---in the hands of Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---the //sannyāsa// staff; [[synonyms:d:dharila]]---left.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at Kamalapura, He took His bath in the Bhārgīnadī River and left His sannyāsa staff in the hands of Lord Nityānanda.
purport: In the //Caitanya-bhāgavata// (//Antya-khaṇḍa,// Chapter Two) it is said that when Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at Śrī Bhuvaneśvara, He visited the temple of Lord Śiva known as Gupta-kāśī (the concealed Vārāṇasī). Lord Śiva established this as a place of pilgrimage by bringing water from all holy places and creating the lake known as Bindu-sarovara. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took His bath in this lake, feeling a great regard for Lord Śiva. From the spiritual point of view, people still go to take a bath in this lake. Actually, by taking a bath there, one becomes very healthy even from the material viewpoint. Taking a bath and drinking the water of this lake can cure any disease of the stomach. Regular bathing certainly cures indigestion. The river Bhārgī or Bhārgīnadī is now known as Daṇḍa-bhāṅgā-nadī. It is situated six miles north of Jagannātha Purī. The reason for the change in names is given as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.142-143
description: When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to the temple of Lord Śiva known as Kapoteśvara, Nityānanda Prabhu, who was keeping His sannyāsa staff in custody, broke the staff in three parts and threw it into the river Bhārgīnadī. Later this river became known as Daṇḍa-bhāṅgā-nadī.
text:
> kapoteśvara dekhite gelā bhakta-gaṇa saṅge
> ethā nityānanda-prabhu kaila daṇḍa-bhaṅge
>
> tina khaṇḍa kari' daṇḍa dila bhāsāñā
> bhakta-saṅge āilā prabhu maheśa dekhiñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kapoteśvara]]---the Śiva temple of the name Kapoteśvara; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the devotees; [[synonyms:e:ethā]]---here; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---of the //sannyāsa// staff; [[synonyms:b:bhaṅge]]---breaking; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]]---three parts; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---the staff; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---threw in; [[synonyms:b:bhāsāñā]]---washing away; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:maheśa]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiñā]]---having seen the temple of Lord Śiva.
translation: When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to the temple of Lord Śiva known as Kapoteśvara, Nityānanda Prabhu, who was keeping His sannyāsa staff in custody, broke the staff in three parts and threw it into the river Bhārgīnadī. Later this river became known as Daṇḍa-bhāṅgā-nadī.
purport:
The mystery of the //sannyāsa-daṇḍa// (staff) of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has been explained by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the order of //sannyāsa// from a Māyāvādī //sannyāsī.// The Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// generally carry one staff, or //daṇḍa.// Taking advantage of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's absence, Śrīla Nityānanda Prabhu broke the staff into three parts and threw it into the river now known as the Daṇḍa-bhāṅgā-nadī. In the //sannyāsa// order there are four divisions-//kuṭīcaka, bahūdaka, haṁsa// and //paramahaṁsa.// Only when the //sannyāsī// remains on the //kuṭīcaka// and //bahūdaka// platforms can he carry a staff. However, when one is elevated to the status of //haṁsa// or //paramahaṁsa,// after touring and preaching the //bhakti// cult, he must give up the //sannyāsa// staff.

Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. It is therefore said, //śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya, rādhā-kṛṣṇa nahe anya:// "Two personalities-Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and Śrī Kṛṣṇa-are combined in the incarnation of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu." Therefore, considering Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to be an extraordinary person, Lord Nityānanda Prabhu did not wait for the //paramahaṁsa// stage. He reasoned that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is automatically on the //paramahaṁsa// stage; therefore He does not need to carry the //sannyāsa-daṇḍa.//

This is the reason Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu broke the staff into three pieces and threw it into the water.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.144
description: After seeing the temple of Jagannātha from a distant place, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately became ecstatic. After offering obeisances to the temple, He began to dance in the ecstasy of love of God.
text:
> jagannāthera deula dekhi' āviṣṭa hailā
> daṇḍavat kari preme nācite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannāthera]]---of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:d:deula]]---the temple; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---ecstatic; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in the ecstasy of love of God; [[synonyms:n:nācite]]---to dance; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began.
translation: After seeing the temple of Jagannātha from a distant place, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately became ecstatic. After offering obeisances to the temple, He began to dance in the ecstasy of love of God.
purport: The word //deula// refers to the temple where the Supreme Personality of Godhead is situated. The present temple of Jagannātha Purī was constructed by King Anaṅga-bhīma. Historians say this temple must have been constructed at least two thousand years ago. During the time of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the small buildings surrounding the original temple had not been constructed. Nor was the high platform in front of the temple present during the time of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.145
description: All the devotees became ecstatic in the association of Lord Caitanya, and thus absorbed in love of God, they were dancing and singing while going along the main road.
text:
> bhakta-gaṇa āviṣṭa hañā, sabe nāce gāya
> premāveśe prabhu-saṅge rāja-mārge yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---ecstatic; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sing; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---absorbed in love of God; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:m:mārge]]---on the pathway; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---going.
translation: All the devotees became ecstatic in the association of Lord Caitanya, and thus absorbed in love of God, they were dancing and singing while going along the main road.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.146
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu laughed, cried, danced and made many ecstatic vibrations and sounds. Although the temple was only six miles away, to Him the distance seemed thousands of miles.
text:
> hāse, kānde, nāce prabhu huṅkāra garjana
> tina-krośa patha haila---sahasra yojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hāse]]---laughs; [[synonyms:k:kānde]]---cries; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:huṅkāra]]---ecstatic vibrations; [[synonyms:g:garjana]]---resonations; [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:k:krośa]]---six miles; [[synonyms:p:patha]]---the way; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]] [[synonyms:y:yojana]]---thousands of miles.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu laughed, cried, danced and made many ecstatic vibrations and sounds. Although the temple was only six miles away, to Him the distance seemed thousands of miles.
purport: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was in ecstasy, He considered one moment to last as long as twelve years. After seeing the Jagannātha temple from a distant place, the Lord became so ecstatic that He considered the six-mile path many thousands of miles long.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.147
description: Thus walking and walking, the Lord eventually arrived at the place known as Āṭhāranālā. Arriving there, He expressed His external consciousness, speaking to Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu.
text:
> calite calite prabhu āilā 'āṭhāranālā'
> tāhāṅ āsi' prabhu kichu bāhya prakāśilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:calitecalite]]---walking in this way; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:ā:āṭhāranālā]]---at a place known as Āṭhāranālā; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---external consciousness; [[synonyms:p:prakāśilā]]---expressed.
translation: Thus walking and walking, the Lord eventually arrived at the place known as Āṭhāranālā. Arriving there, He expressed His external consciousness, speaking to Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu.
purport: At the entrance to Jagannātha Purī is a bridge with eighteen arches called Āṭhāranālā. (//Āṭhāra// means eighteen.)

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.148
description: When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu had thus regained external consciousness, He asked Lord Nityānanda Prabhu, "Please return My staff." Nityānanda Prabhu then replied, "It has been broken into three parts."
text:
> nityānande kahe prabhu,---deha mora daṇḍa
> nityānanda bale,---daṇḍa haila tina khaṇḍa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānande]]---to Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---asks; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---give; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---//sannyāsa// staff; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---Śrī Nityānanda replies; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---Your //sannyāsa// staff; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]]---divided into three parts.
translation: When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu had thus regained external consciousness, He asked Lord Nityānanda Prabhu, "Please return My staff." Nityānanda Prabhu then replied, "It has been broken into three parts."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.149
description: Nityānanda Prabhu said, "When You fell down in ecstasy, I caught You, but both of Us together fell upon the staff.
text:
> premāveśe paḍilā tumi, tomāre dharinu
> tomā-saha sei daṇḍa-upare paḍinu
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in an ecstatic condition; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---You; [[synonyms:d:dharinu]]---I caught; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:saha]]---with You; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:u:upare]]---upon that staff; [[synonyms:p:paḍinu]]---I fell down.
translation: Nityānanda Prabhu said, "When You fell down in ecstasy, I caught You, but both of Us together fell upon the staff.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.15
description: The beauty of the Gopāla Deity stole away their minds, and feeling great happiness, they remained there for two or four days.
text:
> gopāla-saundarya duṅhāra mana nila hari'
> sukha pāñā rahe tāhāṅ dina dui-cāri

translation: The beauty of the Gopāla Deity stole away their minds, and feeling great happiness, they remained there for two or four days.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.150
description: "Thus the staff broke under Our weight. Where the pieces have gone, I cannot say.
text:
> dui-janāra bhare daṇḍa khaṇḍa khaṇḍa haila
> sei khaṇḍa kāṅhā paḍila, kichu nā jānila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:janāra]]---of Us two; [[synonyms:b:bhare]]---by the weight; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---the staff; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]] [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]]---broken to pieces; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]]---pieces; [[synonyms:k:kāṅhā]] [[synonyms:p:paḍila]]---where they fell; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---anything; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:j:jānila]]---is not known.
translation: "Thus the staff broke under Our weight. Where the pieces have gone, I cannot say.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.151
description: "It is certainly because of My offense that Your staff was broken. Now You can punish Me on this account as You think proper."
text:
> mora aparādhe tomāra daṇḍa ha-ila khaṇḍa
> ye ucita haya, mora kara tāra daṇḍa"
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:a:aparādhe]]---by the offense; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---//sannyāsa// staff; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]]---broken; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:u:ucita]]---fitting; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---to Me; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---do; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---for that; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---punishment.
translation: "It is certainly because of My offense that Your staff was broken. Now You can punish Me on this account as You think proper."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.152
description: After hearing the story about how His staff had been broken, the Lord expressed a little sadness and, displaying a bit of anger, began to speak as follows.
text:
> śuni' kichu mahāprabhu duḥkha prakāśilā
> īṣat krodha kari' kichu kahite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:p:prakāśilā]]---expressed; [[synonyms:ī:īṣat]]---little; [[synonyms:k:krodha]]---anger; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began.
translation: After hearing the story about how His staff had been broken, the Lord expressed a little sadness and, displaying a bit of anger, began to speak as follows.
purport: Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu considered Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's acceptance of //sannyāsa// to be useless. He therefore relieved the Lord of the trouble of carrying the staff. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu expressed anger because He wanted to teach all other //sannyāsīs// that they should not give up the staff before attaining the platform of //paramahaṁsa.// Seeing that the regulative principles could be slackened by such action, Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to carry the staff personally. However, Nityānanda broke it. For this reason Caitanya Mahāprabhu displayed a little anger. It is said in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:3:21|(Bg. 3.21)]], //yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ:// Whatever great people do, others follow. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to follow the Vedic principles strictly in order to save inexperienced neophytes who try to imitate //paramahaṁsas.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.153
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "You have all benefited Me by bringing Me to Nīlācala. However, My only possession was that one staff, and you have not kept it.
text:
> nīlācale āni' mora sabe hita kailā
> sabe daṇḍa-dhana chila, tāhā nā rākhilā

translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "You have all benefited Me by bringing Me to Nīlācala. However, My only possession was that one staff, and you have not kept it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.154
description: "So all of you should go before or behind Me to see Lord Jagannātha. I shall not go with you."
text:
> tumi-saba āge yāha īśvara dekhite
> kibā āmi āge yāi, nā yāba sahite
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of you; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---ahead; [[synonyms:y:yāha]]---go; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]] [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see Jagannātha; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---or; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---ahead; [[synonyms:y:yāi]]---go; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---I shall go; [[synonyms:s:sahite]]---with you.
translation: "So all of you should go before or behind Me to see Lord Jagannātha. I shall not go with you."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.155
description: Mukunda Datta told Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "My Lord, You should go ahead and allow all the others to follow. We shall not go with You."
text:
> mukunda datta kahe,---prabhu, tumi yāha āge
> āmi-saba pāche yāba, nā yāba tomāra saṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukunda]] [[synonyms:d:datta]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the devotee named Mukunda Datta said; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---my Lord; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:y:yāha]]---go; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of us; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---behind; [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---shall go; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---shall go; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with You.
translation: Mukunda Datta told Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "My Lord, You should go ahead and allow all the others to follow. We shall not go with You."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.156
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then began to walk very swiftly before all the other devotees. No one could understand the real purpose of the two Lords, Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu.
text:
> eta śuni' prabhu āge calilā śīghra-gati
> bujhite nā pāre keha dui prabhura mati
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of the other devotees; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---began to go; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]]-[[synonyms:g:gati]]---very swiftly; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---able; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lords; [[synonyms:m:mati]]---intentions.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then began to walk very swiftly before all the other devotees. No one could understand the real purpose of the two Lords, Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.157
description: The devotees could not understand why Nityānanda Prabhu broke the staff, why Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu permitted Him to do so, or why, after permitting Him, Caitanya Mahāprabhu became angry.
text:
> iṅho kene daṇḍa bhāṅge, teṅho kene bhāṅgāya
> bhāṅgāñā krodhe teṅho iṅhāke doṣāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṅho]]---Nityānanda; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---the staff; [[synonyms:b:bhāṅge]]---breaks; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:b:bhāṅgāya]]---allows to break it; [[synonyms:b:bhāṅgāñā]]---after allowing to break it; [[synonyms:k:krodhe]]---in anger; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāke]]---Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:d:doṣāya]]---accuses.
translation: The devotees could not understand why Nityānanda Prabhu broke the staff, why Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu permitted Him to do so, or why, after permitting Him, Caitanya Mahāprabhu became angry.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.158
description: The pastime of the breaking of the staff is very deep. Only one whose devotion is fixed upon the lotus feet of the two Lords can understand it.
text:
> daṇḍa-bhaṅga-līlā ei---parama gambhīra
> sei bujhe, duṅhāra pade yāṅra bhakti dhīra
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṅga]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastime of breaking the staff; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---very; [[synonyms:g:gambhīra]]---grave; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:b:bujhe]]---one can understand; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]]---of both of Them; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---to the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:d:dhīra]]---fixed.
translation: The pastime of the breaking of the staff is very deep. Only one whose devotion is fixed upon the lotus feet of the two Lords can understand it.
purport: One who understands Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu in reality can understand Their identity as well as the breaking of the staff. All the previous //ācāryas,// being induced to engage themselves fully in the service of the Lord, gave up attachment for material life and thus accepted the staff, which signifies full engagement of the mind, speech and body in the service of the Lord. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the regulative principles of the renounced order of life. That is completely clear. However, in the //paramahaṁsa// stage there is no need to accept a //daṇḍa// (staff), and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was certainly in the //paramahaṁsa// stage. Nonetheless, to indicate that everyone should take //sannyāsa// at the end of life in order to engage fully in the service of the Lord, even //paramahaṁsas// like Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His confidential devotees follow the regulative principles unfailingly. Indeed, that was His purpose. Nityānanda Prabhu, who was His eternal servitor, believed that there was no need for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to carry the staff, and to declare to the world that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was above all regulations, He broke it into three pieces. The pastime known as //daṇḍa-bhaṅga-līlā// is thus explained by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.159
description: The glories of Lord Gopāla, who is merciful to brāhmaṇas, are very great. The narration of Sākṣi-gopāla was spoken by Nityānanda Prabhu and heard by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> brahmaṇya-deva-gopālera mahimā ei dhanya
> nityānanda---vaktā yāra, śrotā---śrī-caitanya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahmaṇya]]-[[synonyms:d:deva]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is merciful to the //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of Gopāla; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---glories; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:d:dhanya]]---glorified; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:v:vaktā]]---the speaker; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of the narration; [[synonyms:ś:śrotā]]---the hearer; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: The glories of Lord Gopāla, who is merciful to brāhmaṇas, are very great. The narration of Sākṣi-gopāla was spoken by Nityānanda Prabhu and heard by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
purport: There are four points of instruction one should consider in the story of Sākṣi-gopāla. First, the Deity (//arcā-vigraha//) of Śrī Gopāla is eternally //sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha,// the transcendental form of the Lord. Second, the Deity surpasses material regulative principles and extends the reality of transcendental principles. Third, one can be situated in a transcendental position after becoming a //brāhmaṇa,// but as a //brāhmaṇa,// one has to follow the regulative principles very strictly. Lastly, //brahmaṇya-deva// indicates Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself, who is worshiped thus: //namo brahmaṇya-devāya go-brāhmaṇa-hitāya ca jagad-dhitāya kṛṣṇāya govindāya namo namaḥ.// This indicates that a devotee who is under the protection of Kṛṣṇa is automatically situated as a //brāhmaṇa,// and such a //brāhmaṇa// is not illusioned. This is factual.

translation: One who hears this narration of Lord Gopāla with faith and love very soon attains the lotus feet of Lord Gopāla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.161
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.

> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named Caitanya-caritāmṛta; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation:
Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Fifth Chapter, describing the activities of Sākṣi-gopāla.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.17
description: Indeed, the young brāhmaṇa always rendered service to the older one, and the old man, being very satisfied with his service, was pleased with him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.2

translation: All glories to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Śrī Advaita Prabhu! And all glories to the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.20
description: "If I do not show you any respect, I will be ungrateful. Therefore, I promise to give you my daughter in charity."

> kṛta-ghnatā haya tomāya nā kaile sammāna
> ataeva tomāya āmi diba kanyā-dāna

translation: "If I do not show you any respect, I will be ungrateful. Therefore, I promise to give you my daughter in charity."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.22
description: "You are a most aristocratic family man, well educated and very rich. I am not at all aristocratic, and I am without a decent education and have no wealth.
text:
> mahā-kulīna tumi---vidyā-dhanādi-pravīṇa
> āmi akulīna, āra dhana-vidyā-hīna
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:k:kulīna]]---highly aristocratic; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:v:vidyā]]---education; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---riches; [[synonyms:p:pravīṇa]]---enriched; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:a:akulīna]]---not aristocratic; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]-[[synonyms:v:vidyā]]-[[synonyms:h:hīna]]---without any wealth and education.
translation: "You are a most aristocratic family man, well educated and very rich. I am not at all aristocratic, and I am without a decent education and have no wealth.
purport: Due to pious activities, one can be enriched by four opulences: one may obtain birth in an aristocratic family, become highly educated, become very beautiful or get a sufficient quantity of riches. These are symptoms of pious activities performed in one's past life. In India it is still current for an aristocratic family never to consider a marriage with a common family. Though the caste may be the same, to maintain the aristocracy such marriages are rejected. No poor man will dare marry the daughter of a rich man. Because of this, when the elderly //brāhmaṇa// offered the young //brāhmaṇa// his daughter, the young //brāhmaṇa// did not believe that it would be possible to marry her. Therefore he asked the elderly //brāhmaṇa// why he was proposing something unprecedented (//asambhava//). It was unheard of for an aristocratic person to offer his daughter to a person who was both uneducated and poor.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.23
description: "Sir, I am not a suitable bridegroom for your daughter. I render service to you only for the satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> kanyā-dāna-pātra āmi nā ha-i tomāra
> kṛṣṇa-prītye kari tomāra sevā-vyavahāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]-[[synonyms:d:dāna]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---a bridegroom suitable for one's daughter; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---am; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of you; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prītye]]---only for satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I do; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of you; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---of service; [[synonyms:v:vyavahāra]]---activities.
translation: "Sir, I am not a suitable bridegroom for your daughter. I render service to you only for the satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa.
purport: Both //brāhmaṇas// were pure Vaiṣṇavas. The younger man took special care of the older one simply to please Kṛṣṇa. In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.19.21) Kṛṣṇa says, //mad-bhakta-pūjābhyadhikā:// "It is better to render service to My devotee." Thus, according to the Gauḍīya-Vaiṣṇava philosophy of Caitanya Mahāprabhu, it is better to be a servant of the servant of God. One should not try to serve Kṛṣṇa directly. A pure Vaiṣṇava serves a servant of Kṛṣṇa and identifies himself as a servant of a servant of Kṛṣṇa. This is pleasing to Lord Kṛṣṇa. Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura confirms this philosophy: //chāḍiyā vaiṣṇava-sevā nistāra pāyeche kebā.// Unless one serves a liberated Vaiṣṇava, he cannot attain liberation by directly serving Kṛṣṇa. He must serve the servant of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.24
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa is very pleased by service rendered to brāhmaṇas, and when the Lord is pleased, the opulence of one's devotional service increases."
text:
> brāhmaṇa-sevāya kṛṣṇera prīti baḍa haya
> tāṅhāra santoṣe bhakti-sampad bāḍaya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sevāya]]---by rendering service to a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prīti]]---the satisfaction; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very great; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:s:santoṣe]]---by pleasing the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---of devotional service; [[synonyms:s:sampad]]---the opulence; [[synonyms:b:bāḍaya]]---increases.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa is very pleased by service rendered to brāhmaṇas, and when the Lord is pleased, the opulence of one's devotional service increases."
purport: In this regard, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that the younger //brāhmaṇa// rendered service to the older one with the purpose of pleasing Kṛṣṇa. It was not a matter of ordinary worldly dealings. Kṛṣṇa is pleased when a Vaiṣṇava is rendered service. Because the younger //brāhmaṇa// served the older one, Lord Gopāla agreed to become a witness of the marriage negotiation in order to maintain the prestige of both devotees. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would certainly not have liked to hear about marital dealings unless such dealings were exchanged between two Vaiṣṇavas. Marriage arrangements and ceremonies belong to ordinary material //karma-kāṇḍa// sections of the scriptures. The Vaiṣṇavas, however, are not interested in any kind of //karma-kāṇḍa// dealings. Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says: //karma-kāṇḍa jñāna-kāṇḍa kevala viṣera bhāṇḍa.// For a Vaiṣṇava, the //karma-kāṇḍa// and //jñāna-kāṇḍa// sections of the //Vedas// are unnecessary. Indeed, a real Vaiṣṇava takes these sections as a poison pot (//viṣera bhāṇḍa//). Sometimes we take part in a marriage ceremony for our disciples, but this does not mean that we are interested in //karma-kāṇḍa// activities. Sometimes, not knowing the Vaiṣṇava philosophy, an outsider criticizes such activity, maintaining that a //sannyāsī// should not take part in a marriage ceremony between a young boy and a young girl. However, this is not a //karma-kāṇḍa// activity, because our purpose is to spread the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. We are giving all facility to the general populace to take to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, and in order to fix the devotees in concentration on the service of the Lord, marriage is sometimes allowed. We have experienced that such married couples actually render very important service to the mission. Therefore, one should not misunderstand when a //sannyāsī// takes part in a marriage ceremony. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu took great pleasure in hearing about the marriage ceremony between the young //brāhmaṇa// and the daughter of the elderly //brāhmaṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.28
description: "King Bhīṣmaka wanted to give his daughter, Rukmiṇī, in charity to Kṛṣṇa, but Rukmī, his eldest son, objected. Therefore he could not carry out his decision."
text:
> bhīṣmakera icchā,---kṛṣṇe kanyā samarpite
> putrera virodhe kanyā nārila arpite"
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhīṣmakera]]---of King Bhīṣmaka; [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---the desire; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---daughter; [[synonyms:s:samarpite]]---to give; [[synonyms:p:putrera]]---of his son; [[synonyms:v:virodhe]]---by the objection; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---daughter; [[synonyms:n:nārila]]---was unable; [[synonyms:a:arpite]]---to offer.
translation: "King Bhīṣmaka wanted to give his daughter, Rukmiṇī, in charity to Kṛṣṇa, but Rukmī, his eldest son, objected. Therefore he could not carry out his decision."
purport:
As stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.52.25):

> bandhūnām icchatāṁ dātuṁ
> kṛṣṇāya bhaginīṁ nṛpa
> tato nivārya kṛṣṇa-dviḍ
> rukmī caidyam amanyata

King Bhīṣmaka of Vidarbha wanted to offer Kṛṣṇa his daughter, Rukmiṇī, but Rukmī, the eldest of his five sons, objected. Therefore he withdrew his decision and decided to offer Rukmiṇī to the King of Cedi, Śiśupāla, who was a cousin of Kṛṣṇa's. However, Rukmiṇī conceived of a trick: she sent a letter to Kṛṣṇa asking Him to kidnap her. Thus in order to please Rukmiṇī, who was His great devotee, Kṛṣṇa kidnapped her. There ensued a great fight between Kṛṣṇa and the opposing party, headed by Rukmiṇī's brother Rukmī. Rukmī was defeated and, because of his harsh words against Kṛṣṇa, was about to be killed, but he was saved at the request of Rukmiṇī. However, Kṛṣṇa shaved off all of Rukmī's hair with His sword. Śrī Balarāma did not like this, and so to please Rukmiṇī, Balarāma rebuked Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.31
