title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.32
description: Coming before Gopāla, the elderly brāhmaṇa said, "My dear Lord, please witness that I have given my daughter to this boy."
text:
> gopālera āge vipra kahite lāgila
> 'tumi jāna, nija-kanyā ihāre āmi dila'
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopālera]] [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of the Gopāla Deity; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the elderly //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:j:jāna]]---my Lord, please know; [[synonyms:n:nila]]-[[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---my own daughter; [[synonyms:i:ihāre]]---to this boy; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---have given in charity.
translation: Coming before Gopāla, the elderly brāhmaṇa said, "My dear Lord, please witness that I have given my daughter to this boy."
purport:
In India it is still the custom for a daughter to be offered to someone simply by word. This is called //vāg-datta.// This means that the father, brother or guardian of a girl has given his word that she will be married to a certain man. Consequently, that daughter cannot be married to anyone else. She is reserved by virtue of the honest words of the father or guardian. There are many instances in which the parents of a female child have given someone a verbal promise that their daughter will be married to his son. Both parties agree to wait until the boy and girl are grown up, and then the marriage takes place. Following this custom, which is very old in India, the elderly //brāhmaṇa// promised to give his daughter to the younger //brāhmaṇa// in charity, and he promised this before the Gopāla Deity. In India the custom is to honor any promise made before the Deity. Such a promise cannot be canceled. In Indian villages, whenever there is a quarrel between two parties, they go to a temple to settle the quarrel. Whatever is spoken in front of the Deity is taken to be true, for no one would dare lie before the Deity. This same principle was followed in the Battle of Kurukṣetra. Therefore in the very beginning of the //Bhagavad-gītā// it is stated: //dharma-kṣetre kuru-kṣetre.//

By not becoming God conscious, human society is deteriorating to the lowest standard of animal life. This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is very essential to reviving God consciousness among the general populace. If people actually become God conscious, all quarrels can be settled outside of court, as happened in the case of the two //brāhmaṇas// whose disagreement was settled by the witness Gopāla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.33

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.34

> guru-buddhye choṭa-vipra bahu sevā kare
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---speaking this; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---both the //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went; [[synonyms:d:deśere]]---toward their own country; [[synonyms:g:guru]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhye]]---accepting the elderly //brāhmaṇa// as //guru//; [[synonyms:c:choṭa]]-[[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the young //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---various; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]---services; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---renders.
translation: After these talks, the two brāhmaṇas started for home. As usual, the young brāhmaṇa accompanied the elderly brāhmaṇa as if the older brāhmaṇa were a guru [spiritual master] and rendered him service in various ways.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.35
description: After returning to Vidyānagara, each brāhmaṇa went to his respective home. After some time, the elderly brāhmaṇa became very anxious.
text:
> deśe āsi' dui-jane gelā nija-ghare
> kata dine baḍa-vipra cintita antare
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:deśe]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---after returning to their own country; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---both of them; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to their respective homes; [[synonyms:k:kata]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---after some time; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]-[[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the elderly //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:c:cintita]]---very anxious; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---within.
translation: After returning to Vidyānagara, each brāhmaṇa went to his respective home. After some time, the elderly brāhmaṇa became very anxious.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.36
description: He began to think, "I have given my word to a brāhmaṇa in a holy place, and what I promised will certainly come to pass. I must now disclose this to my wife, sons, other relatives and friends."
text:
> tīrthe vipre vākya diluṅ,---kemate satya haya
> strī, putra, jñāti, bandhu jānibe niścaya

translation: He began to think, "I have given my word to a brāhmaṇa in a holy place, and what I promised will certainly come to pass. I must now disclose this to my wife, sons, other relatives and friends."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.37
description: Thus one day the elderly brāhmaṇa called for a meeting of all his relatives and friends, and before them all he narrated what had taken place in front of Gopāla.
text:
> eka-dina nija-loka ekatra karila
> tā-sabāra āge saba vṛttānta kahila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---all his relatives; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]]---in one place; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---assembled; [[synonyms:t:tā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vṛttānta]]---narration; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---spoke.
translation: Thus one day the elderly brāhmaṇa called for a meeting of all his relatives and friends, and before them all he narrated what had taken place in front of Gopāla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.38
description: When those who belonged to the family circle heard the narration of the old brāhmaṇa, they made exclamations showing their disappointment. They all requested that he not make such a proposal again.
text:
> śuni' saba goṣṭhī tāra kare hāhā-kāra
> 'aiche bāt mukhe tumi nā ānibe āra

translation: When those who belonged to the family circle heard the narration of the old brāhmaṇa, they made exclamations showing their disappointment. They all requested that he not make such a proposal again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.39
description: They unanimously agreed, "If you offer your daughter to a degraded family, your aristocracy will be lost. When people hear of this, they will make jokes and laugh at you."
text:
> nīce kanyā dile kula yāibeka nāśa
> śuniñā sakala loka karibe upahāsa'

translation: They unanimously agreed, "If you offer your daughter to a degraded family, your aristocracy will be lost. When people hear of this, they will make jokes and laugh at you."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.4
description: In the temple of Varāhadeva, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu engaged in chanting and dancing and offered prayers. He passed that night in the temple.

> nṛtya-gīta kaila preme bahuta stavana
> yājapure se rātri karilā yāpana

translation: In the temple of Varāhadeva, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu engaged in chanting and dancing and offered prayers. He passed that night in the temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.40

text:
> vipra bale,---"tīrtha-vākya kemane kari āna
> ye ha-uk, se ha-uka, āmi diba kanyā-dāna"
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipra]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---the //brāhmaṇa// says; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]-[[synonyms:v:vākya]]---the promise made on the pilgrimage; [[synonyms:k:kemane]]---how; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I shall do; [[synonyms:ā:āna]]---otherwise; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:u:uk]]---whatever may be; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:u:uka]]---let it take place; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:d:diba]]---shall give; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]-[[synonyms:d:dāna]]---my daughter in charity.
translation: The elderly brāhmaṇa said, "How can I undo the promise I made in a holy place while on pilgrimage? Whatever may happen, I must give him my daughter in charity."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.41
description: The relatives unanimously said, "If you give your daughter to that boy, we shall give up all connection with you." Indeed, his wife and sons declared, "If such a thing happens, we shall take poison and die."
text:
> jñāti loka kahe,---'morā tomāke chāḍiba'
> strī-putra kahe,---'viṣa khāiyā mariba'
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jñāti]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the relatives; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---answer; [[synonyms:m:morā]]---we all; [[synonyms:t:tomāke]]---you; [[synonyms:c:chāḍiba]]---will give up; [[synonyms:s:strī]]---wife; [[synonyms:p:putra]]---sons; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---say; [[synonyms:v:viṣa]]---poison; [[synonyms:k:khāiyā]]---drinking; [[synonyms:m:mariba]]---we shall die.
translation: The relatives unanimously said, "If you give your daughter to that boy, we shall give up all connection with you." Indeed, his wife and sons declared, "If such a thing happens, we shall take poison and die."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.42
description: The elderly brāhmaṇa said, "If I do not give my daughter to the young brāhmaṇa, he will call Śrī Gopālajī as a witness. Thus he will take my daughter by force, and in that case my religious principles will become meaningless."
text:
> vipra bale,---"sākṣī bolāñā karibeka nyāya
> jiti' kanyā labe, mora vyartha dharma haya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viprabale]]---the //brāhmaṇa// says; [[synonyms:s:sākṣī]]---a witness; [[synonyms:b:bolāñā]]---calling for; [[synonyms:k:karibeka]]---there will be; [[synonyms:n:nyāya]]---justice; [[synonyms:j:jiti']]---winning; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---the daughter; [[synonyms:l:labe]]---he will take; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:v:vyartha]]---meaningless; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---religious principles; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---will be.
translation: The elderly brāhmaṇa said, "If I do not give my daughter to the young brāhmaṇa, he will call Śrī Gopālajī as a witness. Thus he will take my daughter by force, and in that case my religious principles will become meaningless."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.43
description: His son replied, "The Deity may be a witness, but He is in a distant country. How can He come to bear witness against you? Why are you so anxious over this?
text:
> putra bale,---"pratimā sākṣī, seha dūra deśe
> ke tomāra sākṣī dibe, cintā kara kise
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:putra]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---his son says; [[synonyms:p:pratimā]]---the Deity; [[synonyms:s:sākṣī]]---witness; [[synonyms:s:seha]]---He also; [[synonyms:d:dūra]]---distant; [[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in country; [[synonyms:k:ke]]---who; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---of you; [[synonyms:s:sākṣī]]---witness; [[synonyms:d:dibe]]---will give; [[synonyms:c:cintā]]---anxiety; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---you do; [[synonyms:k:kise]]---why.
translation: His son replied, "The Deity may be a witness, but He is in a distant country. How can He come to bear witness against you? Why are you so anxious over this?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.44
description: "You do not have to flatly deny that you spoke such a thing. There is no need to make a false statement. Simply say that you do not remember what you said.
text:
> nāhi kahi---nā kahio e mithyā-vacana
> sabe kahibe---'mora kichu nāhika smaraṇa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nāhikahi]]---I did not say; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kahio]]---do not say; [[synonyms:e:e]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mithyā]]-[[synonyms:v:vacana]]---false statement; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---only; [[synonyms:k:kahibe]]---you shall say; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---anything; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---not; [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---remembrance.
translation: "You do not have to flatly deny that you spoke such a thing. There is no need to make a false statement. Simply say that you do not remember what you said.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.45
description: "If you simply say, 'I do not remember,' I shall take care of the rest. By argument, I shall defeat the young brāhmaṇa."
text:
> tumi yadi kaha,---'āmi kichui nā jāni'
> tabe āmi nyāya kari' brāhmaṇere jini"
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---say; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:k:kichui]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I do not remember anything; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---in that case; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nyāya]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---arguing; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇere]]---the younger //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:j:jini]]---shall conquer.
translation: "If you simply say, 'I do not remember,' I shall take care of the rest. By argument, I shall defeat the young brāhmaṇa."
purport: The son of the elderly //brāhmaṇa// was an atheist and a follower of the Raghunātha-smṛti. He was very expert in dealing with pounds-shillings-pence, but he was fool number one. Consequently, he did not believe in the spiritual position of the Deity, nor did he have any faith in the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore, as a typical idol worshiper, he considered the form of the Lord to be made of stone or wood. Thus he assured his father that the witness was only a stone Deity and was not capable of speaking. Besides that, he assured his father that the Deity was situated far away and consequently could not come to bear witness. In essence, he was saying: "Have no anxiety. You do not have to lie directly, but you should speak like a diplomat, like King Yudhiṣṭhira when he spoke to Droṇācārya-//aśvatthāmā hata iti gajaḥ.// Following this principle, simply say that you do not remember anything and are completely unaware of the statements given by the young //brāhmaṇa.// If you make the background like that, I shall know how to fill in the argument and defeat him by word jugglery. Thus I shall save you from having to give your daughter to him. In this way, our aristocracy will be saved. You have nothing to worry about."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.46
description: When the elderly brāhmaṇa heard this, his mind became very agitated. Feeling helpless, he simply turned his attention to the lotus feet of Gopāla.
text:
> eta śuni' viprera cintita haila mana
> ekānta-bhāve cinte vipra gopāla-caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:v:viprera]]---of the old //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:c:cintita]]---agitated; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:e:ekānta]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---with single-minded attention; [[synonyms:c:cinte]]---thinks; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---of the lotus feet of Śrī Gopālajī.
translation: When the elderly brāhmaṇa heard this, his mind became very agitated. Feeling helpless, he simply turned his attention to the lotus feet of Gopāla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.47
description: The elderly brāhmaṇa prayed, "My dear Lord Gopāla, I have taken shelter of Your lotus feet, and therefore I request You to please protect my religious principles from disturbance and at the same time save my kinsmen from dying."
text:
> 'mora dharma rakṣā pāya, nā mare nija-jana
> dui rakṣā kara, gopāla, lainu śaraṇa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---religious principles; [[synonyms:r:rakṣā]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---spared; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:m:mare]]---die; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---own kinsmen; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:r:rakṣā]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---You kindly protect; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---my Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:l:lainu]]---I have taken; [[synonyms:ś:śaraṇa]]---shelter under Your lotus feet.
translation: The elderly brāhmaṇa prayed, "My dear Lord Gopāla, I have taken shelter of Your lotus feet, and therefore I request You to please protect my religious principles from disturbance and at the same time save my kinsmen from dying."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.48
description: The next day, the elderly brāhmaṇa was thinking deeply about this matter when the young brāhmaṇa came to his house.
text:
> ei-mata vipra citte cintite lāgila
> āra dina laghu-vipra tāṅra ghare āila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the elderly //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:c:citte]]---within the mind; [[synonyms:c:cintite]]---to think; [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---the next day; [[synonyms:l:laghu]]-[[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the young //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to the home; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came.
translation: The next day, the elderly brāhmaṇa was thinking deeply about this matter when the young brāhmaṇa came to his house.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.49
description: The young brāhmaṇa came to him and offered respectful obeisances. Then, very humbly folding his hands, he spoke as follows.
text:
> āsiñā parama-bhaktye namaskāra kari'
> vinaya kariñā kahe kara dui yuḍi'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āsiñā]]---coming; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---in great devotion; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:v:vinaya]] [[synonyms:k:kariñā]]---with great humility; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---hands; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:y:yuḍi']]---folding.
translation: The young brāhmaṇa came to him and offered respectful obeisances. Then, very humbly folding his hands, he spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.5
description: Afterwards, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to the town of Kaṭaka to see the temple of the witness Gopāla. When He saw the Deity of Gopāla, He was very much pleased with His beauty.
text:
> kaṭake āilā sākṣi-gopāla dekhite
> gopāla-saundarya dekhi' hailā ānandite
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kaṭake]]---in the town of Kaṭaka (Cuttak); [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:s:sākṣi]]-[[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the witness Gopāla; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---of the Deity of Gopāla; [[synonyms:s:saundarya]]---the beauty; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:ā:ānandite]]---very pleased.
translation: Afterwards, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to the town of Kaṭaka to see the temple of the witness Gopāla. When He saw the Deity of Gopāla, He was very much pleased with His beauty.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.50
description: "You have promised to give your daughter in charity to me. Now you do not say anything. What is your conclusion?"
text:
> 'tumi more kanyā dite karyācha aṅgīkāra
> ebe kichu nāhi kaha, ki tomāra vicāra'
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:m:more]]---to me; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---your daughter; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give in charity; [[synonyms:k:karyācha]]---have made; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---a promise; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---you say; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---conclusion.
translation: "You have promised to give your daughter in charity to me. Now you do not say anything. What is your conclusion?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.51
description: After the young brāhmaṇa submitted this statement, the elderly brāhmaṇa remained silent. Taking this opportunity, his son immediately came out with a stick to strike the younger man.
text:
> eta śuni' sei vipra rahe mauna dhari'
> tāṅra putra mārite āila hāte ṭheṅgā kari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the elderly //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:m:mauna]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---holding silence; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:p:putra]]---son; [[synonyms:m:mārite]]---to strike; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came out; [[synonyms:h:hāte]]---in hand; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭheṅgā]]---stick; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking.
translation: After the young brāhmaṇa submitted this statement, the elderly brāhmaṇa remained silent. Taking this opportunity, his son immediately came out with a stick to strike the younger man.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.52
description: The son said, "Oh, you are most degraded! You want to marry my sister, just like a dwarf who wants to catch the moon!"
text:
> 'āre adhama! mora bhagnī cāha vivāhite
> vāmana hañā cāṅda yena cāha ta' dharite'

translation: The son said, "Oh, you are most degraded! You want to marry my sister, just like a dwarf who wants to catch the moon!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.53
description: Seeing a stick in the hand of the son, the younger brāhmaṇa fled. The next day, however, he gathered together all the people of the village.
text:
> ṭheñā dekhi' sei vipra palāñā gela
> āra dina grāmera loka ekatra karila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭheñā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the stick in his hand; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the young //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:p:palāñā]] [[synonyms:g:gela]]---fled from that place; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---the next day; [[synonyms:g:grāmera]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the inhabitants of the village; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---gathered in one place.
translation: Seeing a stick in the hand of the son, the younger brāhmaṇa fled. The next day, however, he gathered together all the people of the village.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.54
description: All the people of the village then called for the elderly brāhmaṇa and brought him to their meeting place. The young brāhmaṇa then began to speak before them as follows.
text:
> saba loka baḍa-vipre ḍākiyā ānila
> tabe sei laghu-vipra kahite lāgila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the village inhabitants; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]-[[synonyms:v:vipre]]---to the senior //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍākiyā]]---calling; [[synonyms:ā:ānila]]---brought; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:l:laghu]]-[[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the junior //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---began to speak.
translation: All the people of the village then called for the elderly brāhmaṇa and brought him to their meeting place. The young brāhmaṇa then began to speak before them as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.55
description: "This gentleman has promised to hand over his daughter to me, yet now he does not follow his promise. Please ask him about his behavior."
text:
> 'iṅha more kanyā dite karyāche aṅgīkāra
> ebe ye nā dena, pucha iṅhāra vyavahāra'
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṅha]]---this gentleman; [[synonyms:m:more]]---to me; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---his daughter; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give in charity; [[synonyms:k:karyāche]]---has made; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---promise; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---indeed; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:d:dena]]---he gives; [[synonyms:p:pucha]]---kindly ask; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]]---of him; [[synonyms:v:vyavahāra]]---the behavior.
translation: "This gentleman has promised to hand over his daughter to me, yet now he does not follow his promise. Please ask him about his behavior."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.56
description: All the people gathered there asked the elderly brāhmaṇa, "If you have already promised to give him your daughter in charity, why are you not fulfilling your promise? You have given your word of honor."
text:
> tabe sei viprere puchila sarva-jana
> 'kanyā kene nā deha, yadi diyācha vacana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:viprere]]---//brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:p:puchila]]---asked; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---all the people; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---daughter; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:deha]]---you do not give in charity; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:d:diyācha]]---have given; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---word of honor.
translation: All the people gathered there asked the elderly brāhmaṇa, "If you have already promised to give him your daughter in charity, why are you not fulfilling your promise? You have given your word of honor."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.57
description: The elderly brāhmaṇa said, "My dear friends, please hear what I have to submit. I do not exactly remember making a promise like that."
text:
> vipra kahe,---'śuna, loka, mora nivedana
> kabe ki baliyāchi, mora nāhika smaraṇa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the senior //brāhmaṇa// replied; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all people; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---submission; [[synonyms:k:kabe]]---when; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:b:baliyāchi]]---I have said; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---remembrance.
translation: The elderly brāhmaṇa said, "My dear friends, please hear what I have to submit. I do not exactly remember making a promise like that."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.58
description: When the elderly brāhmaṇa's son heard this, he took the opportunity to juggle some words. Becoming very impudent, he stood before the assembly and spoke as follows.
text:
> eta śuni' tāṅra putra vākya-cchala pāñā
> pragalbha ha-iyā kahe sammukhe āsiñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:p:putra]]---his son; [[synonyms:v:vākya]]-[[synonyms:c:cchala]]---for jugglery of words; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting a chance; [[synonyms:p:pragalbha]]---impudent; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:iyā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:s:sammukhe]]---in the front; [[synonyms:ā:āsiñā]]---coming.
translation: When the elderly brāhmaṇa's son heard this, he took the opportunity to juggle some words. Becoming very impudent, he stood before the assembly and spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.59
description: "While touring various holy places of pilgrimage, my father carried much money. Seeing the money, this rogue decided to take it away.
text:
> 'tīrtha-yātrāya pitāra saṅge chila bahu dhana
> dhana dekhi ei duṣṭera laite haila mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrāya]]---when touring the holy places; [[synonyms:p:pitāra]]---my father; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:c:chila]]---there was; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---much; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---money; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---money; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---seeing; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:d:duṣṭera]]---of the rogue; [[synonyms:l:laite]]---to take; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---it was; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the intention.
translation: "While touring various holy places of pilgrimage, my father carried much money. Seeing the money, this rogue decided to take it away.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.6
description: While there, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu engaged in chanting and dancing for some time, and being overwhelmed, He offered many prayers to Gopāla.
text:
> premāveśe nṛtya-gīta kaila kata-kṣaṇa
> āviṣṭa hañā kaila gopāla stavana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in the ecstasy of love of God; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]---dancing and chanting; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed; [[synonyms:k:kata]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇa]]---for some time; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being overwhelmed; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---offered; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]] [[synonyms:s:stavana]]---prayers to Gopāla.
translation: While there, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu engaged in chanting and dancing for some time, and being overwhelmed, He offered many prayers to Gopāla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.60
description: "There was no one besides this man with my father. Giving him an intoxicant known as dhuturā to eat, this rogue made my father mad.
text:
> āra keha saṅge nāhi, ei saṅge ekala
> dhuturā khāoyāñā bāpe karila pāgala
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---anyone; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---else; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in company; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there was not; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in company; [[synonyms:e:ekala]]---alone; [[synonyms:d:dhuturā]]---an intoxicant; [[synonyms:k:khāoyāñā]]---making him eat; [[synonyms:b:bāpe]]---my father; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---made; [[synonyms:p:pāgala]]---mad.
translation: "There was no one besides this man with my father. Giving him an intoxicant known as dhuturā to eat, this rogue made my father mad.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.61
description: "Having taken all my father's money, this rogue claimed that it was taken by some thief. Now he is claiming that my father has promised to give him his daughter in charity.
text:
> saba dhana lañā kahe---'core la-ila dhana'
> 'kanyā dite cāhiyāche'---uṭhāila vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---money; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:c:core]]---a thief; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---took; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---all the money; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---the daughter; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give in charity; [[synonyms:c:cāhiyāche]]---has promised; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāila]]---has raised; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---a slogan.
translation: "Having taken all my father's money, this rogue claimed that it was taken by some thief. Now he is claiming that my father has promised to give him his daughter in charity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.62
description: "All of you assembled here are gentlemen. Please judge whether it is befitting to offer this poor brāhmaṇa my father's daughter."
text:
> tomarā sakala loka karaha vicāre
> 'mora pitāra kanyā dite yogya ki ihāre'
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomarā]]---you; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---just make; [[synonyms:v:vicāre]]---judgment; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:p:pitāra]]---of the father; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---the daughter; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give in charity; [[synonyms:y:yogya]]---befitting; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---is it; [[synonyms:i:ihāre]]---to him.
translation: "All of you assembled here are gentlemen. Please judge whether it is befitting to offer this poor brāhmaṇa my father's daughter."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.63
description: Hearing all these statements, all the people gathered there became a little doubtful. They thought it quite possible that because of attraction for riches one might give up his religious principles.
text:
> eta śuni' lokera mane ha-ila saṁśaya
> 'sambhave,---dhana-lobhe loka chāḍe dharma-bhaya'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing all this; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of all the people; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the minds; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:s:saṁśaya]]---doubt; [[synonyms:s:sambhave]]---possible; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]-[[synonyms:l:lobhe]]---by greed for money; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---some man; [[synonyms:c:chāḍe]]---gives up; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---religious principles.
translation: Hearing all these statements, all the people gathered there became a little doubtful. They thought it quite possible that because of attraction for riches one might give up his religious principles.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.64
description: At that time the young brāhmaṇa said, "My dear gentlemen, please hear. Just to gain victory in an argument, this man is lying.
text:
> tabe choṭa-vipra kahe, "śuna, mahājana
> nyāya jinibāre kahe asatya-vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:c:choṭa]]-[[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the young //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---all gentlemen; [[synonyms:n:nyāya]]---the argument; [[synonyms:j:jinibāre]]---to win; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---he says; [[synonyms:a:asatya]]-[[synonyms:v:vacana]]---untruthful statements.
translation: At that time the young brāhmaṇa said, "My dear gentlemen, please hear. Just to gain victory in an argument, this man is lying.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.65
description: "Being very satisfied with my service, this brāhmaṇa said to me of his own accord, 'I promise to hand over my daughter to you.'
text:
> ei vipra mora sevāya tuṣṭa yabe hailā
> 'tore āmi kanyā diba' āpane kahilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---this //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:s:sevāya]]---by the service; [[synonyms:t:tuṣṭa]]---fully satisfied; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---he was; [[synonyms:t:tore]]---to you; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---daughter; [[synonyms:d:diba]]---shall give; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---of his own accord; [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---promised.
translation: "Being very satisfied with my service, this brāhmaṇa said to me of his own accord, 'I promise to hand over my daughter to you.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.66
description: "At that time I forbade him to do this, telling him, 'O best of the brāhmaṇas, I am not a fit husband for your daughter.
text:
> tabe muñi niṣedhinu,---śuna, dvija-vara
> tomāra kanyāra yogya nahi muñi vara
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:niṣedhinu]]---forbade; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:d:dvija]]-[[synonyms:v:vara]]---O best of the //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:k:kanyāra]]---for the daughter; [[synonyms:y:yogya]]---suitable; [[synonyms:n:nahi]]---not; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:v:vara]]---husband.
translation: "At that time I forbade him to do this, telling him, 'O best of the brāhmaṇas, I am not a fit husband for your daughter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.67
description: " 'Whereas you are a learned scholar, a rich man belonging to an aristocratic family, I am a poor man, uneducated and with no claim to aristocracy.'
text:
> kāhāṅ tumi paṇḍita, dhanī, parama kulīna
> kāhāṅ muñi daridra, mūrkha, nīca, kula-hīna
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---whereas; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---learned scholar; [[synonyms:d:dhanī]]---rich man; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---first class; [[synonyms:k:kulīna]]---aristocracy; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---whereas; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:d:daridra]]---poor man; [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]]---not educated; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]---fallen; [[synonyms:k:kula]]-[[synonyms:h:hīna]]---without aristocracy.
translation: “ 'Whereas you are a learned scholar, a rich man belonging to an aristocratic family, I am a poor man, uneducated and with no claim to aristocracy.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.68
description: "Still this brāhmaṇa insisted. Again and again he asked me to accept his proposal, saying, 'I have given you my daughter. Please accept her.'
text:
> tabu ei vipra more kahe bāra bāra
> tore kanyā diluṅ, tumi karaha svīkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---//brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:m:more]]---to me; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:b:bāra]] [[synonyms:b:bāra]]---again and again; [[synonyms:t:tore]]---to you; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---my daughter; [[synonyms:d:diluṅ]]---I have given in charity; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---make; [[synonyms:s:svīkāra]]---acceptance.
translation: "Still this brāhmaṇa insisted. Again and again he asked me to accept his proposal, saying, 'I have given you my daughter. Please accept her.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.69
description: "I then said, 'Please hear. You are a learned brāhmaṇa. Your wife, friends and relatives will never agree to this proposal.
text:
> tabe āmi kahilāṅ---śuna, mahā-mati
> tomāra strī-putra-jñātira nā habe sammati
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kahilāṅ]]---said; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:m:mati]]---O intelligent //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:s:strī]]-[[synonyms:p:putra]]---wife and children; [[synonyms:j:jñātira]]---kinsmen; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:habe]] [[synonyms:s:sammati]]---will not agree.
translation: "I then said, 'Please hear. You are a learned brāhmaṇa. Your wife, friends and relatives will never agree to this proposal.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.7
description: That night Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stayed in the temple of Gopāla, and along with all the devotees, He heard the narration of the witness Gopāla with great pleasure.
text:
> sei rātri tāhāṅ rahi' bhakta-gaṇa-saṅge
> gopālera pūrva-kathā śune bahu raṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:r:rātri]]---that night; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---remaining; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the other devotees; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---previous narration; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hears; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---much; [[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---in pleasure.
translation: That night Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stayed in the temple of Gopāla, and along with all the devotees, He heard the narration of the witness Gopāla with great pleasure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.70
description: " 'My dear sir, you will not be able to fulfill your promise. Your promise will be broken.' Yet, again and again the brāhmaṇa emphasized his promise.
text:
> kanyā dite nāribe, habe asatya-vacana
> punarapi kahe vipra kariyā yatana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---daughter; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give; [[synonyms:n:nāribe]]---you will not be able; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---it will become; [[synonyms:a:asatya]]-[[synonyms:v:vacana]]---a false statement; [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---he says; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:y:yatana]]---with great attention.
translation: “ 'My dear sir, you will not be able to fulfill your promise. Your promise will be broken.' Yet, again and again the brāhmaṇa emphasized his promise.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.71
description: " 'I have offered you my daughter. Do not hesitate. She is my daughter, and I shall give her to you. Who can forbid me?'
text:
> kanyā tore diluṅ, dvidhā nā kariha cite
> ātma-kanyā diba, kebā pāre niṣedhite
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---the daughter; [[synonyms:t:tore]]---to you; [[synonyms:d:diluṅ]]---I have given; [[synonyms:d:dvidhā]]---hesitation; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---do not; [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do; [[synonyms:c:cite]]---within your mind; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---my own daughter; [[synonyms:d:diba]]---I shall give; [[synonyms:k:kebā]]---who; [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---is able; [[synonyms:n:niṣedhite]]---to forbid.
translation: “ 'I have offered you my daughter. Do not hesitate. She is my daughter, and I shall give her to you. Who can forbid me?'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.72
description: "At that time I concentrated my mind and requested the brāhmaṇa to make the promise before the Gopāla Deity.
text:
> tabe āmi kahilāṅ dṛḍha kari' mana
> gopālera āge kaha e-satya vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kahilāṅ]]---said; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]] [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---fixing my mind; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]] [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of the Gopāla Deity; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---speak; [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---this truthful statement.
translation: "At that time I concentrated my mind and requested the brāhmaṇa to make the promise before the Gopāla Deity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.73
description: "Then this gentleman said in front of the Gopāla Deity, 'My dear Lord, please bear witness. I have offered my daughter to this brāhmaṇa in charity.'
text:
> tabe iṅho gopālera āgete kahila
> tumi jāna, ei vipre kanyā āmi dila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:i:iṅho]]---this gentleman; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of the Gopāla Deity; [[synonyms:ā:āgete]]---in front; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---he said; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:j:jāna]]---my Lord, please know; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:v:vipre]]---unto this young //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]---my daughter; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---have offered.
translation: "Then this gentleman said in front of the Gopāla Deity, 'My dear Lord, please bear witness. I have offered my daughter to this brāhmaṇa in charity.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.74
description: "Accepting the Gopāla Deity as my witness, I then submitted the following at His lotus feet.
text:
> tabe āmi gopālere sākṣī kariñā
> kahilāṅ tāṅra pade minati kariñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:g:gopālere]]---to the Gopāla Deity; [[synonyms:s:sākṣī]]---the witness; [[synonyms:k:kariñā]]---making; [[synonyms:k:kahilāṅ]]---said; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at His lotus feet; [[synonyms:m:minati]]---humility; [[synonyms:k:kariñā]]---making.
translation: "Accepting the Gopāla Deity as my witness, I then submitted the following at His lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.75
description: " 'If this brāhmaṇa later hesitates to give me his daughter, my dear Lord, I shall call on You as a witness. Please note this with care and attention.'
text:
> yadi ei vipra more nā dibe kanyā-dāna
> sākṣī bolāimu tomāya, ha-io sāvadhāna

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.76
description: "Thus I have called upon a great personality in this transaction. I have asked the Supreme Godhead to be my witness. The entire world accepts the words of the Supreme Personality of Godhead."
text:
> ei vākye sākṣī mora āche mahājana
> yāṅra vākya satya kari māne tribhuvana"
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:v:vākye]]---in this statement; [[synonyms:s:sākṣī]]---witness; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there is; [[synonyms:m:mahājana]]---a great personality; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:v:vākya]]---words; [[synonyms:s:satya]]---true; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---taking as; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---accepts; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvana]]---the whole world.
translation: "Thus I have called upon a great personality in this transaction. I have asked the Supreme Godhead to be my witness. The entire world accepts the words of the Supreme Personality of Godhead."
purport: Although the young //brāhmaṇa// described himself as having no claims to aristocracy and being an uneducated common man, still he had one good qualification: he believed that the Supreme Personality of Godhead was the topmost authority, he accepted the words of Lord Kṛṣṇa without hesitation, and he had firm faith in the Lord's consistency. According to Prahlāda Mahārāja, another authority on the Supreme Personality of Godhead, such a staunch and faithful devotee of the Lord must be understood to be a most learned scholar: //tan manye 'dhītam uttamam// [[books:sb:7:5:24|(Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 7.5.24)]]. A pure devotee who has firm faith in the words of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is to be considered a most learned scholar, the topmost aristocrat and the richest man in the whole world. All godly qualities automatically exist in such a devotee. In the preaching work of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, we, as the servant of the servant of the servant of the servant of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, fully believe in the words of Kṛṣṇa and His servants, the disciplic succession. In this way we are presenting the words of Kṛṣṇa throughout the world. Even though we are neither a rich man nor a very learned scholar, and even though we do not belong to any aristocracy, this movement is still being welcomed and is very easily spreading all over the world. Although we are very poor and have no professional source of income, Kṛṣṇa supplies money whenever we need it. Whenever we need some men, Kṛṣṇa supplies them. Thus it is stated in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:6:20-23|(Bg. 6.22)]]: //yaṁ labdhvā cāparaṁ lābhaṁ manyate nādhikaṁ tataḥ.// Actually, if we can attain the favor of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, we do not need anything else. We certainly do not need those things which a mundane person considers to be material assets.

translation: Taking this opportunity, the elderly brāhmaṇa immediately confirmed that this was really true. He said, "If Gopāla personally comes here to serve as a witness, I shall surely give my daughter to the young brāhmaṇa." The elderly brāhmaṇa's son immediately confirmed this, saying, "Yes, this is a very nice settlement."
purport: As the Supersoul within the heart of all living entities, Kṛṣṇa knows everyone's desire, everyone's request and everyone's prayer. Although all these may be contradictory, the Lord has to create a situation in which everyone will be pleased. This is an instance of a marriage negotiation between an elderly //brāhmaṇa// and a youthful one. The elderly //brāhmaṇa// was certainly willing to give his daughter in charity to the young //brāhmaṇa,// but his son and relatives became impediments to this transaction. The elderly //brāhmaṇa// considered how to get out of this situation and still offer his daughter to the young //brāhmaṇa.// His son, an atheist and a very cunning fellow, was thinking of how to stop the marriage. The father and son were thinking in a contradictory way, yet Kṛṣṇa created a situation wherein they both agreed. They both agreed that if the Gopāla Deity would come and serve as a witness, the daughter would be given to the young //brāhmaṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.89
description: "My dear Lord, I am not thinking to become happy by getting the daughter as a bride. I am simply thinking that the brāhmaṇa has broken his promise, and that is giving me great pain."
text:
> kanyā pāba,---mora mane ihā nāhi sukha
> brāhmaṇera pratijñā yāya---ei baḍa duḥkha
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kanyā]] [[synonyms:p:pāba]]---I shall get the daughter; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---is not; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇera]]---of a pure //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:p:pratijñā]]---the promise; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---becomes lost; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very much; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness.
translation: "My dear Lord, I am not thinking to become happy by getting the daughter as a bride. I am simply thinking that the brāhmaṇa has broken his promise, and that is giving me great pain."
purport: It was not at all the intention of the young //brāhmaṇa// to get the daughter of the elderly //brāhmaṇa// in marriage and thus enjoy material happiness and sense gratification. It was not for that reason that the young //brāhmaṇa// went to Vṛndāvana to ask the Supreme Personality of Godhead to act as a witness. His only concern was that the elderly //brāhmaṇa// had promised something, and if Gopāla did not bear witness to that transaction, then the older //brāhmaṇa// would incur a spiritual blemish. Therefore, the young //brāhmaṇa// wanted protection and help from the Deity. The young //brāhmaṇa// was thus a pure Vaiṣṇava, and he had no desire for sense gratification. He wanted only to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the older //brāhmaṇa,// who was also a Vaiṣṇava and very devoted to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.9

text:
> sākṣi-gopālera kathā śuni, loka-mukhe
> sei kathā kahena, prabhu śune mahā-sukhe
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sākṣi]]-[[synonyms:g:gopālera]]---of the witness Gopāla; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---the narration; [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---hearing; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---from the people; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---that narration; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Nityānanda Prabhu narrates; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hears; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in great pleasure.
translation: At that time, Nityānanda Prabhu had heard the story of Sākṣi-gopāla from the townspeople. He now recited this again, and Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard the narration with great pleasure.
purport: The Sākṣi-gopāla temple is situated between the Khurdā Road junction railway station and the Jagannātha Purī station. The Deity is not presently situated in Kaṭaka, but when Nityānanda Prabhu traveled there, the Deity was present. Kaṭaka is a town in Orissa situated on the Mahānadī River. When Sākṣi-gopāla was brought from Vidyānagara in southern India, He stayed for some time at Kaṭaka. Thereafter, He was situated for some time in the Jagannātha temple. It seems that in the temple of Jagannātha there was some disagreement between Jagannātha and Sākṣi-gopāla, a disagreement called //prema-kalaha,// a quarrel of love. In order to settle this love quarrel, the King of Orissa constructed a village about six miles from Jagannātha Purī. The village was called Satyavādī, and Gopāla was stationed there. Thereafter, a new temple was constructed. Now there is a Sākṣi-gopāla station, and people go there to see the witness Gopāla.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.90
description: The young brāhmaṇa continued, "My dear sir, You are very merciful and You know everything. Therefore, kindly be a witness in this case. A person who knows things as they are and still does not bear witness becomes involved in sinful activities."
text:
> eta jāni' tumi sākṣī deha, dayā-maya
> jāni' sākṣī nāhi deya, tāra pāpa haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---knowing this; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:s:sākṣī]]---witness; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---please give; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---O most merciful one; [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---knowing; [[synonyms:s:sākṣī]]---witness; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:d:deya]]---does not give; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---for him; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]---sin; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is.
translation: The young brāhmaṇa continued, "My dear sir, You are very merciful and You know everything. Therefore, kindly be a witness in this case. A person who knows things as they are and still does not bear witness becomes involved in sinful activities."
purport: The dealings between a devotee and the Lord are very simple. The young //brāhmaṇa// said to the Lord, "You know everything, but if You do not bear witness, You will be involved in sinful activities." There is no possibility, however, of the Lord's being involved in sinful activities. A pure devotee, even though he knows everything of the Supreme Lord, can speak with the Lord exactly as if He were a common man. Although the dealings between the Lord and His devotee are always very simple and open, there is formality. All these things happen because of the connection between the Lord and the devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.91
description: Lord Kṛṣṇa replied, "My dear brāhmaṇa, go back to your home and call a meeting of all the men. In that meeting, just try to remember Me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 5.97
description: Śrī Gopālajī then smiled and said, "My dear brāhmaṇa, just listen to Me. I shall walk behind you, and in this way I shall go with you."
text:
> hāsiñā gopāla kahe,---"śunaha, brāhmaṇa
> tomāra pāche pāche āmi kariba gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hāsiñā]]---smiling; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---the Lord Gopāla; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:ś:śunaha]]---just hear; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---O My dear //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---you; [[synonyms:p:pāche]] [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---behind; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---shall do; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---walking.
translation: Śrī Gopālajī then smiled and said, "My dear brāhmaṇa, just listen to Me. I shall walk behind you, and in this way I shall go with you."
purport:
The conversation between Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and the //brāhmaṇa// is proof that the Lord in His //arcā-mūrti,// or form made of material elements, is not material, for those elements, although separated from the Lord, are also a part of the Lord's energy, as stated in the //Bhagavad-gītā.// Because the elements are the Lord's own energy and because there is no difference between the energy and the energetic, the Lord can appear through any element. Just as the sun can act through the sunshine and thus distribute its heat and light, so Kṛṣṇa, by His inconceivable power, can appear in His original spiritual form in any material element, including stone, wood, paint, gold, silver and jewels, because the material elements are all His energy. The //śāstras// warn, //arcye viṣṇau śilā-dhīḥ .// .// . nārakī saḥ:// one should never think of the //arcā-mūrti,// the Deity within the temple, as stone, wood or any other material element. Because of his advanced devotional position, the younger //brāhmaṇa// knew that although the Deity of Gopāla appeared to be stone, He was not stone. He was the son of Nanda Mahārāja, Vrajendra-nandana Himself.

As such, the Deity can act exactly as the Lord did in His original form as Kṛṣṇa. Lord Kṛṣṇa was talking to the young //brāhmaṇa// just to test his knowledge about the //arcā-vigraha.// In other words, those who have understood the science of Kṛṣṇa-Kṛṣṇa's name, form, quality and so forth-can also talk with the Deity. To an ordinary person, however, the Deity will appear to be made of stone, wood or some other material. In the higher sense, since all material elements ultimately emanate from the supreme spiritual entity, nothing is really material. Being omnipotent, omnipresent and omniscient, Kṛṣṇa can deal with His devotees in any form without difficulty. By the mercy of the Lord, the devotee knows perfectly well about the Lord's dealings. Indeed, he can talk face to face with the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.101
description: " 'In the past, your son has had bodies of three different colors, according to the age. These colors were white, red and yellow. In this age [Dvāpara-yuga] He has accepted a blackish body.'
text:
> āsan varṇās trayo hy asya
> gṛhṇato 'nu-yugaṁ tanūḥ
> śuklo raktas tathā pīta
> idānīṁ kṛṣṇatāṁ gataḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āsan]]---there were; [[synonyms:v:varṇāḥ]]---colors; [[synonyms:t:trayaḥ]]---three; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---indeed; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of Him; [[synonyms:g:gṛhṇataḥ]]---accepting; [[synonyms:a:anu]]-[[synonyms:y:yugam]]---according to the age; [[synonyms:t:tanūḥ]]---bodies; [[synonyms:ś:śuklaḥ]]---white; [[synonyms:r:raktaḥ]]---red; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---also; [[synonyms:p:pītaḥ]]---yellow; [[synonyms:i:idānīm]]---at the present moment; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇatām]]---blackish; [[synonyms:g:gataḥ]]---has accepted.
translation: “ 'In the past, your son has had bodies of three different colors, according to the age. These colors were white, red and yellow. In this age [Dvāpara-yuga] He has accepted a blackish body.'
purport: This verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.8.13) was spoken by Garga Muni when he was performing the rituals at Lord Kṛṣṇa's name-giving ceremony. He states that the incarnations of the Lord in other ages had been white, red and yellow. This yellow color refers to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, whose bodily complexion was yellowish. This confirms that in the past Kali-yugas, the Lord also had incarnated in a body that was yellow in hue. It is understood that the Lord incarnates in different colors for the different //yugas// (Satya, Tretā, Dvāpara and Kali). Accepting the color yellow (//pīta//), as well as other characteristics, the Lord incarnated as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. This is the verdict of all Vedic authorities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.103
description: " 'In this Age of Kali, those who are intelligent perform the congregational chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, worshiping the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who appears in this age always describing the glories of Kṛṣṇa. That incarnation is yellowish in hue and is always associated with His plenary expansions [such as Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu] and personal expansions [such as Gadādhara], as well as His devotees and associates [such as Svarūpa Dāmodara].'

That incarnation is yellowish in hue and is always associated with His plenary expansions [such as Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu] and personal expansions [such as Gadādhara], as well as His devotees and associates [such as Svarūpa Dāmodara].'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.104

He will be distinguished from Māyāvādī sannyāsīs in that He will be fixed in devotional service and will spread the saṅkīrtana movement.' "

translation: “ 'The Lord [in the incarnation of Gaurasundara] has a golden complexion. Indeed, His entire body, which is very nicely constituted, is like molten gold. Sandalwood pulp is smeared all over His body. He will take the fourth order of spiritual life [sannyāsa] and will be very self-controlled. title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.106
description: "When the Lord will be pleased with you, you will also understand these conclusions and will quote from the śāstras.
text:
> tomāra upare tāṅra kṛpā yabe habe
> e-saba siddhānta tabe tumiha kahibe
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāraupare]]---upon you; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---the Lord's; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all these; [[synonyms:s:siddhānta]]---conclusions; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:t:tumiha]]---you also; [[synonyms:k:kahibe]]---will quote.
translation: "When the Lord will be pleased with you, you will also understand these conclusions and will quote from the śāstras.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.107
description: "The false arguments and philosophical word jugglery of your disciples are not faults of theirs. They have simply received the benediction of Māyāvāda philosophy.
text:
> tomāra ye śiṣya kahe kutarka, nānā-vāda
> ihāra ki doṣa---ei māyāra prasāda
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]---disciples; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---say; [[synonyms:k:ku]]-[[synonyms:t:tarka]]---false arguments; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:v:vāda]]---jugglery of philosophy; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---their; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---fault; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:māyāra]]---of illusion; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---benediction.
translation: "The false arguments and philosophical word jugglery of your disciples are not faults of theirs. They have simply received the benediction of Māyāvāda philosophy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.108
description: " 'I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is full of unlimited qualities and whose different potencies bring about agreement and disagreement between disputants. Thus the illusory energy again and again covers the self-realization of both disputants.'
text:
> yac-chaktayo vadatāṁ vādināṁ vai
> vivāda-saṁvāda-bhuvo bhavanti
> kurvanti caiṣāṁ muhur ātma-mohaṁ
> tasmai namo 'nanta-guṇāya bhūmne
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yat]]---whose; [[synonyms:ś:śaktayaḥ]]---potencies; [[synonyms:v:vadatām]]---contending; [[synonyms:v:vādinām]]---of the opposing disputants; [[synonyms:v:vai]]---indeed; [[synonyms:v:vivāda]]---of opposition; [[synonyms:s:saṁvāda]]---of agreement; [[synonyms:b:bhuvaḥ]]---objects; [[synonyms:b:bhavanti]]---become; [[synonyms:k:kurvanti]]---do; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:e:eṣām]]---of them; [[synonyms:m:muhuḥ]]---always; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:m:moham]]---illusion of the self; [[synonyms:t:tasmai]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:g:guṇāya]]---who has qualities; [[synonyms:b:bhūmne]]---the Supreme.
translation: “ 'I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is full of unlimited qualities and whose different potencies bring about agreement and disagreement between disputants. Thus the illusory energy again and again covers the self-realization of both disputants.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:6:4:31|(6.4.31)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.109
description: " 'In almost all cases, whatever learned brāhmaṇas speak becomes accepted; nothing is impossible for one who takes shelter of My illusory energy and speaks under her influence.' "
text:
> yuktaṁ ca santi sarvatra
> bhāṣante brāhmaṇā yathā
> māyāṁ madīyām udgṛhya
> vadatāṁ kiṁ nu durghaṭam
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yuktam]]---quite befitting; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:s:santi]]---are; [[synonyms:s:sarvatra]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:b:bhāṣante]]---speak; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇāḥ]]---the learned; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as much; [[synonyms:m:māyām]]---illusion; [[synonyms:m:madīyām]]---of Me; [[synonyms:u:udgṛhya]]---accepting; [[synonyms:v:vadatām]]---of the speculators; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what; [[synonyms:n:nu]]---certainly; [[synonyms:d:durghaṭam]]---impossible.
translation: “ 'In almost all cases, whatever learned brāhmaṇas speak becomes accepted; nothing is impossible for one who takes shelter of My illusory energy and speaks under her influence.' "
purport: In this verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.22.4), the Supreme Personality of Godhead explains that His illusory energy can perform the impossible; such is the power of the illusory energy. In many cases philosophical speculators have covered the real truth and have boldly set forth false theories. In ancient times philosophers like Kapila, Gautama, Jaimini, Kaṇāda and similar //brāhmaṇas// propounded useless philosophical theories, and in modern days so-called scientists are setting forth many false theories about the creation, backed up by seemingly logical arguments. This is all due to the influence of the Supreme Lord's illusory energy. The illusory energy, therefore, sometimes appears correct because it is emanating from the Supreme Correct. To avoid the very bewildering illusory influence, one must accept the words of the Supreme Personality of Godhead as they are. Only then can one escape the influence of the illusory energy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.11
description: Sitting beside Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he thought, "This is a transcendental ecstatic transformation brought about by love of Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> vasi' bhaṭṭācārya mane karena vicāra
> ei kṛṣṇa-mahāpremera sāttvika vikāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting down; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in his mind; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]]---consideration; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:premera]]---of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sāttvika]]---transcendental; [[synonyms:v:vikāra]]---transformation.
translation: Sitting beside Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he thought, "This is a transcendental ecstatic transformation brought about by love of Kṛṣṇa."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.110
description: After hearing this from Gopīnātha Ācārya, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "First go to the place where Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is staying and invite Him here with His associates. Ask Him on my account.
text:
> tabe bhaṭṭācārya kahe, yāha gosāñira sthane
> āmāra nāme gaṇa-sahita kara nimantraṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:y:yāha]]---please go; [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]] [[synonyms:s:sthane]]---to the place of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:n:nāme]]---in my name; [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sahita]]---with His associates; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---make; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇe]]---invitation.
translation: After hearing this from Gopīnātha Ācārya, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "First go to the place where Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is staying and invite Him here with His associates. Ask Him on my account.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.111
description: "Take jagannātha-prasāda and first give it to Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His associates. After that, come back here and teach me well."
text:
> prasāda āni' tāṅre karāha āge bhikṣā
> paścāt āsi' āmāre karāiha śikṣā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing //jagannātha-prasāda//; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:k:karāha]]---make; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---first; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---acceptance; [[synonyms:p:paścāt]]---afterwards; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming here; [[synonyms:ā:āmāre]]---unto me; [[synonyms:k:karāiha]]---cause; [[synonyms:ś:śikṣā]]---teaching.
translation: "Take jagannātha-prasāda and first give it to Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His associates. After that, come back here and teach me well."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.112
description: Gopīnātha Ācārya was the brother-in-law of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; therefore their relationship was very sweet and intimate. Under the circumstances, Gopīnātha Ācārya taught him by sometimes blaspheming him, sometimes praising him and sometimes laughing at him. This had been going on for some time.
text:
> ācārya---bhaginī-pati, śyālaka---bhaṭṭācārya
> nindā-stuti-hāsye śikṣā karā'na ācārya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:b:bhaginī]]-[[synonyms:p:pati]]---sister's husband; [[synonyms:ś:śyālaka]]---wife's brother; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:n:nindā]]---sometimes blaspheming; [[synonyms:s:stuti]]---sometimes by praising; [[synonyms:h:hāsye]]---sometimes by laughing; [[synonyms:ś:śikṣā]]---instruction; [[synonyms:k:karā'na]]---causes; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya.
translation: Gopīnātha Ācārya was the brother-in-law of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; therefore their relationship was very sweet and intimate. Under the circumstances, Gopīnātha Ācārya taught him by sometimes blaspheming him, sometimes praising him and sometimes laughing at him. This had been going on for some time.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.113
description: Śrīla Mukunda Datta felt very satisfied to hear the conclusive statements of Gopīnātha Ācārya, but he became very unhappy and angry to hear the statements put forward by Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.
text:
> ācāryera siddhānte mukundera haila santoṣa
> bhaṭṭācāryera vākya mane haila duḥkha-roṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]]---of Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:s:siddhānte]]---with the conclusions; [[synonyms:m:mukundera]]---of Mukunda Datta; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---satisfaction; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:v:vākye]]---by the words; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:r:roṣa]]---and anger.
translation: Śrīla Mukunda Datta felt very satisfied to hear the conclusive statements of Gopīnātha Ācārya, but he became very unhappy and angry to hear the statements put forward by Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.114
description: According to the instructions of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Gopīnātha Ācārya went to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and invited Him on the Bhaṭṭācārya's behalf.
text:
> gosāñira sthāne ācārya kaila āgamana
> bhaṭṭācāryera nāme tāṅre kaila nimantraṇa

translation: According to the instructions of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Gopīnātha Ācārya went to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and invited Him on the Bhaṭṭācārya's behalf.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.115
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya's statements were discussed before Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Gopīnātha Ācārya and Mukunda Datta disapproved of the Bhaṭṭācārya's statements because they caused mental pain.
text:

> bhaṭṭācāryera nindā kare, mane pāñā vyathā

translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya's statements were discussed before Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Gopīnātha Ācārya and Mukunda Datta disapproved of the Bhaṭṭācārya's statements because they caused mental pain.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.116
description: Hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Do not speak like that. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya has shown great affection and mercy toward Me.
text:
> śuni mahāprabhu kahe aiche mat kaha
> āmā prati bhaṭṭācāryera haya anugraha
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---hearing them; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:m:mat]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---do not speak; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]] [[synonyms:p:prati]]---toward Me; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:a:anugraha]]---mercy.
translation: Hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Do not speak like that. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya has shown great affection and mercy toward Me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.117
description: "Out of paternal affection for Me, he wants to protect Me and see that I follow the regulative principles of a sannyāsī. What fault is there in this?"
text:
> āmāra sannyāsa-dharma cāhena rākhite
> vātsalye karuṇā karena, ki doṣa ihāte
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---regulative principles of //sannyāsa//; [[synonyms:c:cāhena]]---he wants; [[synonyms:r:rākhite]]---to keep; [[synonyms:v:vātsalye]]---out of paternal affection; [[synonyms:k:karuṇā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---fault; [[synonyms:i:ihāte]]---in this connection.
translation: "Out of paternal affection for Me, he wants to protect Me and see that I follow the regulative principles of a sannyāsī. What fault is there in this?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.118
description: The next morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya together visited the temple of Lord Jagannātha. Both of them were in a very pleasant mood.
text:
> āra dina mahāprabhu bhaṭṭācārya-sane
> ānande karilā jagannātha daraśane
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āradina]]---the next day; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---along with Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in great pleasure; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---to Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---visit.
translation: The next morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya together visited the temple of Lord Jagannātha. Both of them were in a very pleasant mood.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.119
description: When they entered the temple, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya offered Caitanya Mahāprabhu a seat, while he himself sat down on the floor out of due respect for a sannyāsī.
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya-saṅge tāṅra mandire āilā
> prabhure āsana diyā āpane vasilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---along with Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His (Lord Jagannātha's); [[synonyms:m:mandire]]---to the temple; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āsana]]---sitting place; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:v:vasilā]]---sat down.
translation: When they entered the temple, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya offered Caitanya Mahāprabhu a seat, while he himself sat down on the floor out of due respect for a sannyāsī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.12
description: Upon seeing the sign of sūddīpta-sāttvika, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya could immediately understand the transcendental ecstatic transformation in the body of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Such a sign takes place only in the bodies of eternally liberated devotees.
text:
> 'sūddīpta sāttvika' ei nāma ye 'pralaya'
> nitya-siddha bhakte se 'sūddīpta bhāva' haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:u:uddīpta]] [[synonyms:s:sāttvika]]---of the name //sūddīpta-sāttvika//; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:p:pralaya]]---devastation; [[synonyms:n:nitya]]-[[synonyms:s:siddha]]---eternally perfected; [[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---in the devotee; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:u:uddīpta]] [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---ecstasy known as //sūddīpta//; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes manifest.
translation: Upon seeing the sign of sūddīpta-sāttvika, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya could immediately understand the transcendental ecstatic transformation in the body of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Such a sign takes place only in the bodies of eternally liberated devotees.
purport: The word //sūddīpta-sāttvika// is explained as follows by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura: "The //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// mentions eight kinds of transcendental transformations in the bodies of advanced devotees. These are sometimes checked by the devotee, and there are two stages of such checking, technically known as //dhūmāyitā// and //jvalitā.// The //dhūmāyitā// (smoking) stage is exhibited when only one or two transformations are slightly present and it is possible to conceal them. When more than two or three transcendental transformations are manifest and it is still possible to conceal them, although with great difficulty, that stage is called //jvalitā// (lighted). When four or five symptoms are exhibited, the //dīpta// (blazing) stage has been reached. When five, six or all eight symptoms are simultaneously manifest, that position is called //uddīpta// (inflamed). And when all eight symptoms are multiplied a thousand times and are all visible at once, the devotee is in the //sūddīpta// (intensely inflamed) stage. //Nitya-siddha-bhakta// indicates the eternally liberated associates of the Lord. Such devotees enjoy the company of the Lord in four relationships-as servant, friend, parent or conjugal lover."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.120
description: He then began to instruct Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu on Vedānta philosophy, and out of affection and devotion, he spoke to the Lord as follows.
text:
> vedānta paḍāite tabe ārambha karilā
> sneha-bhakti kari' kichu prabhure kahilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vedānta]]---Vedānta philosophy; [[synonyms:p:paḍāite]]---to instruct; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:ā:ārambha]]---beginning; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---made; [[synonyms:s:sneha]]---affection; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---and devotion; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---said.
translation: He then began to instruct Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu on Vedānta philosophy, and out of affection and devotion, he spoke to the Lord as follows.
purport: The //Vedānta-// or //Brahma-sūtra,// written by Śrīla Vyāsadeva, is a book studied by all advanced spiritual students, especially by the //sannyāsīs// of all religious communities (//sampradāyas//). The //sannyāsīs// must read the //Vedānta-sūtra// to establish their final conclusions concerning Vedic knowledge. Here, of course, the //Vedānta// mentioned is the commentary of Śaṅkarācārya, known as //Śārīraka-bhāṣya.// Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya intended to convert Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who was a Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsī,// into a Māyāvādī //sannyāsī.// He therefore made this arrangement to instruct Him in the //Vedānta-sūtra// according to the //Śārīraka// commentary of Śaṅkarācārya. All the //sannyāsīs// of the Śaṅkara-sampradāya enjoy seriously studying the //Vedānta-sūtra// with the //Śārīraka-bhāṣya// commentary. It is said, //vedānta-vākyeṣu sadā ramantaḥ:// "One should always enjoy the studies of the //Vedānta-sūtra.//"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.121
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Hearing Vedānta philosophy is a sannyāsī's main business. Therefore without hesitation You should study Vedānta philosophy, hearing it without cessation from a superior person."
text:
> vedānta-śravaṇa,---ei sannyāsīra dharma
> nirantara kara tumi vedānta śravaṇa

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.127
description: "Only for the sake of executing the duties of the renounced order of sannyāsa do I listen. Unfortunately, I cannot in the least understand the meaning you are presenting."
text:
> sannyāsīra dharma lāgi' śravaṇa mātra kari
> tumi yei artha kara, bujhite nā pāri"
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]]---of one in the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---the occupation; [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for the matter of; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]---hearing; [[synonyms:m:mātra]]---only; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I do; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---present; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---I am able.
translation: "Only for the sake of executing the duties of the renounced order of sannyāsa do I listen. Unfortunately, I cannot in the least understand the meaning you are presenting."
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu presented Himself as if He were a //sannyāsī// in name only or, in other words, a number-one fool. Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// in India are very accustomed to declaring themselves //jagad-gurus,// teachers of the world, although they have no information of the outside world and are limited in their experience to a small town or village, or perhaps to the country of India. Nor do such //sannyāsīs// have sufficient education. Unfortunately, at the present moment there are many foolish //sannyāsīs,// both in India and elsewhere, who simply read and study Vedic literature without understanding the purports. When Caitanya Mahāprabhu was having His discussion with the Chand Kazi, the Muslim magistrate of Navadvīpa, He recited a verse from Vedic literature to the effect that the order of //sannyāsa// is prohibited in this Age of Kali. Only those who are very serious and who follow the regulative principles and study Vedic literature should accept //sannyāsa.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu approved of a //sannyāsī's// reading the //Vedānta-sūtra,// or //Brahma-sūtra,// but He did not approve the //Śārīraka// commentary of Śaṅkarācārya. Indeed, He said elsewhere, //māyāvādi-bhāṣya śunile haya sarva-nāśa:// "If one hears the //Śārīraka-bhāṣya// of Śaṅkarācārya, he is doomed." Thus a //sannyāsī,// a transcendentalist, must read the //Vedānta-sūtra// regularly, but he should not read the //Śārīraka-bhāṣya.// This is the conclusion of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The real commentary on the //Vedānta-sūtra// is //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. Artho 'yaṁ brahma-sūtrānām:Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// is the original commentary on the //Vedānta-sūtra// written by the author himself, Śrīla Vyāsadeva.
