translation: The Lord replied, "First let Me hear your explanation. After that, I shall try to explain what little I know."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.189
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then began to explain the ātmārāma verse, and according to the principles of logic, he put forward various propositions.
text:
> śuni' bhaṭṭācārya śloka karila vyākhyāna
> tarka-śāstra-mata uṭhāya vividha vidhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---of the verse; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:v:vyākhyāna]]---explanation; [[synonyms:t:tarka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---scriptures dealing with logic; [[synonyms:m:mata]]---according to; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāya]]---raises; [[synonyms:v:vividha]]---various; [[synonyms:v:vidhāna]]---propositions.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then began to explain the ātmārāma verse, and according to the principles of logic, he put forward various propositions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.19
description: Gopīnātha Ācārya had previously been acquainted with Mukunda Datta, and when the Ācārya saw him at Jagannātha Purī, he was very much astonished.
text:
> mukunda-sahita pūrve āche paricaya
> mukunda dekhiyā tāṅra ha-ila vismaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]-[[synonyms:s:sahita]]---with Mukunda Datta; [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---previously; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:paricaya]]---acquaintance; [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda Datta; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of him (Gopīnātha Ācārya); [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:v:vismaya]]---astonishment.
translation: Gopīnātha Ācārya had previously been acquainted with Mukunda Datta, and when the Ācārya saw him at Jagannātha Purī, he was very much astonished.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.190
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya explained the ātmārāma verse in nine different ways on the basis of scripture. After hearing his explanation, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, smiling a little, began to speak.
text:
> nava-vidha artha kaila śāstra-mata lañā
> śuni' prabhu kahe kichu īṣat hāsiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]]---nine kinds; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meanings; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---the principles of authorized scriptures; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---after hearing that; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---began to speak; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:ī:īṣat]]---slightly; [[synonyms:h:hāsiyā]]---smiling.
translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya explained the ātmārāma verse in nine different ways on the basis of scripture. After hearing his explanation, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, smiling a little, began to speak.
purport: The //ātmārāma// verse was discussed at Naimiṣāraṇya at a meeting of many great sages, headed by Śaunaka Ṛṣi. They questioned Śrīla Sūta Gosvāmī, who presided at the meeting, about why Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī, a //paramahaṁsa// already in the transcendental position, was attracted to a discussion of the qualities of Kṛṣṇa. In other words, they wanted to know why Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī engaged in the study of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.191
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My dear Bhaṭṭācārya, you are exactly like Bṛhaspati, the priest of the heavenly kingdom. Indeed, no one within this world has the power to explain the scriptures in such a way.
text:
> 'bhaṭṭācārya', jāni---tumi sākṣāt bṛhaspati
> śāstra-vyākhyā karite aiche kāro nāhi śakti
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---My dear Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I know; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:b:bṛhaspati]]---the learned priest of the demigods named Bṛhaspati; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:v:vyākhyā]]---explanation of the scriptures; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to do; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:k:kāro]]---of anyone else; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---power.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My dear Bhaṭṭācārya, you are exactly like Bṛhaspati, the priest of the heavenly kingdom. Indeed, no one within this world has the power to explain the scriptures in such a way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.192
description: "My dear Bhaṭṭācārya, you have certainly explained this verse by the prowess of your vast learning, but you should know that, besides this scholarly explanation, there is another purport to this verse."
text:
> kintu tumi artha kaile pāṇḍitya-pratibhāya
> ihā va-i ślokera āche āro abhiprāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kintu]]---but; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---have shown; [[synonyms:p:pāṇḍitya]]---scholarly; [[synonyms:p:pratibhāya]]---with prowess; [[synonyms:i:ihā]] [[synonyms:v:va]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---besides this; [[synonyms:ś:ślokera]]---of the verse; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there is; [[synonyms:ā:āro]]---another; [[synonyms:a:abhiprāya]]---purport.
translation: "My dear Bhaṭṭācārya, you have certainly explained this verse by the prowess of your vast learning, but you should know that, besides this scholarly explanation, there is another purport to this verse."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.193
description: Upon the request of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to explain the verse, without touching upon the nine explanations given by the Bhaṭṭācārya.
text:
> bhaṭṭācāryera prārthanāte prabhu vyākhyā kaila
> tāṅra nava artha-madhye eka nā chuṅila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:prārthanāte]]---on the request; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vyākhyā]]---explanation; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:n:nava]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---of the nine different types of explanations; [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in the midst; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:c:chuṅila]]---touched.
translation: Upon the request of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to explain the verse, without touching upon the nine explanations given by the Bhaṭṭācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.194
description: There are eleven words in the ātmārāma verse, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu explained each word, one after the other.
text:
> ātmārāmāś ca-śloke 'ekādaśa' pada haya
> pṛthak pṛthak kaila padera artha niścaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāmāś]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---known as such; [[synonyms:ś:śloke]]---in the verse; [[synonyms:e:ekādaśa]]---eleven; [[synonyms:p:pada]]---words; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]] [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---separately one after another; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:p:padera]]---of the words; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meaning; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---certainty.
translation: There are eleven words in the ātmārāma verse, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu explained each word, one after the other.
purport: The words in the //ātmārāma// verse are //ātmārāmāḥ, ca, munayaḥ, nirgranthāḥ, api, urukrame, kurvanti, ahaitukīm, bhaktim, ittham-bhūta-guṇaḥ// and //hariḥ.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.195
description: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu took each word specifically and combined it with the word "ātmārāma." He thus explained the word "ātmārāma" in eighteen different ways.
text:
> tat-tat-pada-prādhānye 'ātmārāma' milāñā
> aṣṭādaśa artha kaila abhiprāya lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]---all those items; [[synonyms:p:prādhānye]]---principally; [[synonyms:ā:ātmārāma]]---the word //ātmārāma//; [[synonyms:m:milāñā]]---causing to meet; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭādaśa]]---eighteen; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meanings; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:a:abhiprāya]]---purpose; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---accepting.
translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu took each word specifically and combined it with the word "ātmārāma." He thus explained the word "ātmārāma" in eighteen different ways.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.196
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, His different potencies and His transcendental qualities all have inconceivable prowess. It is not possible to explain them fully.
text:
> bhagavān, tāṅra śakti, tāṅra guṇa-gaṇa
> acintya prabhāva tinera nā yāya kathana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---His potencies; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---His transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:a:acintya]]---inconceivable; [[synonyms:p:prabhāva]]---the influence; [[synonyms:t:tinera]]---of the three; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---possible; [[synonyms:k:kathana]]---to speak.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, His different potencies and His transcendental qualities all have inconceivable prowess. It is not possible to explain them fully.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.197
description: "These three items attract the mind of a perfect student engaged in spiritual activities and overcome all other processes of spiritual activity."
text:
> anya yata sādhya-sādhana kari' ācchādana
> ei tine hare siddha-sādhakera mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anya]]---other; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:s:sādhya]]-[[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---objectives and transcendental practices; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:ā:ācchādana]]---covering; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:tine]]---these three; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---take away; [[synonyms:s:siddha]]---successful; [[synonyms:s:sādhakera]]---of the student engaged in spiritual activities; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: "These three items attract the mind of a perfect student engaged in spiritual activities and overcome all other processes of spiritual activity."
purport: Spiritual activities other than //bhakti-yoga// are divided into three categories-speculative activity conducted by the //jñāna-sampradāya// (learned scholars), fruitive activity conducted by the general populace according to Vedic regulations, and the activities of transcendentalists not engaged in devotional service. There are many different branches of these categories, but the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by His inconceivable potencies and transcendental qualities, attracts the mind of the student engaged in the activities of //karma, jñāna, yoga,// and so forth. The Supreme Lord is full of inconceivable potencies, which are related to His person, His energies and His transcendental qualities. All of these are very attractive to the serious student. Consequently the Lord is known as Kṛṣṇa, the all-attractive one.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.198
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu explained the meaning of the verse by giving evidence concerning Śukadeva Gosvāmī and the four ṛṣis Sanaka, Sanat-kumāra, Sanātana and Sanandana. Thus the Lord gave various meanings and explanations.
text:
> sanakādi-śukadeva tāhāte pramāṇa
> ei-mata nānā artha karena vyākhyāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sanaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the four //Sanas//; [[synonyms:ś:śukadeva]]---and Śukadeva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:t:tāhāte]]---in that; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---the evidence; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---varieties; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:v:vyākhyāna]]---explanation.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu explained the meaning of the verse by giving evidence concerning Śukadeva Gosvāmī and the four ṛṣis Sanaka, Sanat-kumāra, Sanātana and Sanandana. Thus the Lord gave various meanings and explanations.
purport: That Kṛṣṇa is all-attractive is verified by the activities of the four //ṛṣis// and Śukadeva Gosvāmī. All of them were liberated persons, yet they were attracted by the qualities and pastimes of the Lord. It is therefore said: //muktā api līlayā vigrahaṁ kṛtvā bhagavantaṁ bhajante.// [[books:cc:madhya:24:112|(Cc. Madhya 24.112)]] Even liberated persons are attracted by the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa and thus engage in devotional service. From the very beginning of their lives, Śukadeva Gosvāmī and the four Kumāras, known as //catuḥ-sana,// were liberated and self-realized on the Brahman platform. Nonetheless, they were attracted by the qualities of Kṛṣṇa, and they engaged in His service. The four Kumāras were attracted by the aroma of the flowers offered at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, and in this way they became devotees. Śukadeva Gosvāmī heard //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// by the mercy of his father, Vyāsadeva, and he was consequently attracted to Kṛṣṇa and became a great devotee. The conclusion is that the transcendental bliss experienced in the service of the Lord must be superior to //brahmānanda,// the bliss derived from realizing the impersonal Brahman.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.199
description: Upon hearing Caitanya Mahāprabhu's explanation of the ātmārāma verse, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was struck with wonder. He then understood Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to be Kṛṣṇa in person, and he thus condemned himself in the following words.
text:
> śuni' bhaṭṭācāryera mane haila camatkāra
> prabhuke kṛṣṇa jāni' kare āpanā dhikkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---wonder; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---accepting as; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ā:āpanā]]---himself; [[synonyms:d:dhikkāra]]---condemnation.
translation: Upon hearing Caitanya Mahāprabhu's explanation of the ātmārāma verse, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was struck with wonder. He then understood Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to be Kṛṣṇa in person, and he thus condemned himself in the following words.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.2
description: All glories to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to the devotees of Lord Caitanya!
text:
> jaya jaya gauracandra jaya nityānanda
> jayādvaitacandra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:g:gauracandra]]---all glories to Lord Gaurahari; [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---all glories to Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---all glories to Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---all glories to the devotees of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All glories to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to the devotees of Lord Caitanya!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.20
description: Mukunda Datta offered obeisances unto Gopīnātha Ācārya upon meeting him. Then the Ācārya embraced Mukunda Datta and inquired about news of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> mukunda tāṅhāre dekhi' kaila namaskāra
> teṅho āliṅgiyā puche prabhura samācāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukunda]]---Mukunda Datta; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāre]]---him; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---offered; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgiyā]]---embracing; [[synonyms:p:puche]]---inquires; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:samācāra]]---news.
translation: Mukunda Datta offered obeisances unto Gopīnātha Ācārya upon meeting him. Then the Ācārya embraced Mukunda Datta and inquired about news of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.200
description: "Caitanya Mahāprabhu is certainly Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself. Because I could not understand Him and was very proud of my own learning, I have committed many offenses."
text:
> 'iṅho ta' sākṣāt kṛṣṇa,---muñi nā jāniyā
> mahā-aparādha kainu garvita ha-iyā'
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṅho]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jāniyā]]---knowing; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:a:aparādha]]---a great offense; [[synonyms:k:kainu]]---did; [[synonyms:g:garvita]]---proud; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:iyā]]---being.
translation: "Caitanya Mahāprabhu is certainly Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself. Because I could not understand Him and was very proud of my own learning, I have committed many offenses."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.201
description: When Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya denounced himself as an offender and took shelter of the Lord, the Lord desired to show him mercy.
text:
> ātma-nindā kari' laila prabhura śaraṇa
> kṛpā karibāre tabe prabhura haila mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:n:nindā]]---self-indictment; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:l:laila]]---took; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:ś:śaraṇa]]---shelter; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:k:karibāre]]---to do; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---it was; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: When Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya denounced himself as an offender and took shelter of the Lord, the Lord desired to show him mercy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.202
description: To show him mercy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu allowed him to see His Viṣṇu form. Thus He immediately assumed four hands.
text:
> nija-rūpa prabhu tāṅre karāila darśana
> catur-bhuja-rūpa prabhu hā-ilā takhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---personal form; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---made; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---seeing; [[synonyms:c:catuḥ]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---four-handed; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---form; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:t:takhana]]---at that time.
translation: To show him mercy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu allowed him to see His Viṣṇu form. Thus He immediately assumed four hands.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.203
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu first showed him the four-handed form and then appeared before him in His original form of Kṛṣṇa, with a blackish complexion and a flute to His lips.
text:
> dekhāila tāṅre āge catur-bhuja-rūpa
> pāche śyāma-vaṁśī-mukha svakīya svarūpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhāila]]---showed; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---at first; [[synonyms:c:catur]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---the form with four hands; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---afterwards; [[synonyms:ś:śyāma]]---blackish; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---with a flute to the mouth; [[synonyms:s:svakīya]]---personal; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---form.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu first showed him the four-handed form and then appeared before him in His original form of Kṛṣṇa, with a blackish complexion and a flute to His lips.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.204
description: When Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya saw the form of Lord Kṛṣṇa manifested in Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he immediately fell down flat to offer Him obeisances. Then he stood up and with folded hands began to offer prayers.
text:
> dekhi' sārvabhauma daṇḍavat kari' paḍi'
> punaḥ uṭhi' stuti kare dui kara yuḍi'
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing that; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---falling flat; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---standing up; [[synonyms:s:stuti]]---prayer; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---hands; [[synonyms:y:yuḍi']]---folding.
translation: When Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya saw the form of Lord Kṛṣṇa manifested in Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he immediately fell down flat to offer Him obeisances. Then he stood up and with folded hands began to offer prayers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.205
description: By the mercy of the Lord, all truths were revealed to Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, and he could understand the importance of chanting the holy name and distributing love of Godhead everywhere.
text:
> prabhura kṛpāya tāṅra sphurila saba tattva
> nāma-prema-dāna-ādi varṇena mahattva
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛpāya]]---by the mercy; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---to him; [[synonyms:s:sphurila]]---manifested; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]---truths; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:d:dāna]]---distribution of love of Godhead; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and so on; [[synonyms:v:varṇena]]---describes; [[synonyms:m:mahattva]]---the importance.
translation: By the mercy of the Lord, all truths were revealed to Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, and he could understand the importance of chanting the holy name and distributing love of Godhead everywhere.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.206
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya composed one hundred verses in a very short time. Indeed, not even Bṛhaspati, the priest of the heavenly planets, could compose verses as quickly.
text:
> śata śloka kaila eka daṇḍa nā yāite
> bṛhaspati taiche śloka nā pāre karite
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śata]]---one hundred; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verses; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---composed; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---a duration of twenty-four minutes; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---passing; [[synonyms:b:bṛhaspati]]---Bṛhaspati, the priest of the heavenly planets; [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---such; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verses; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---able; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to compose.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya composed one hundred verses in a very short time. Indeed, not even Bṛhaspati, the priest of the heavenly planets, could compose verses as quickly.
purport: The name of the book of one hundred beautiful verses composed by Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya is //Suśloka-śataka.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.207
description: After hearing the one hundred verses, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu happily embraced Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, who was immediately overwhelmed in ecstatic love of Godhead and fell unconscious.
text:
> śuni' sukhe prabhu tāṅre kaila āliṅgana
> bhaṭṭācārya premāveśe haila acetana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in happiness; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in the ecstasy of love of God; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:a:acetana]]---unconscious.
translation: After hearing the one hundred verses, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu happily embraced Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, who was immediately overwhelmed in ecstatic love of Godhead and fell unconscious.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.208
description: Out of ecstatic love of God, the Bhaṭṭācārya shed tears, and his body was stunned. He exhibited an ecstatic mood, and he perspired, shook and trembled. He sometimes danced, sometimes chanted, sometimes cried and sometimes fell down to touch the lotus feet of the Lord.
text:
> aśru, stambha, pulaka, sveda, kampa tharahari
> nāce, gāya, kānde, paḍe prabhu-pada dhari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:s:stambha]]---a stunned condition; [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]---standing of hair; [[synonyms:s:sveda]]---perspiration; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:t:tharahari]]---with great shaking; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dances; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sings; [[synonyms:k:kānde]]---cries; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---falls down; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]---the lotus feet of the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching.
translation: Out of ecstatic love of God, the Bhaṭṭācārya shed tears, and his body was stunned. He exhibited an ecstatic mood, and he perspired, shook and trembled. He sometimes danced, sometimes chanted, sometimes cried and sometimes fell down to touch the lotus feet of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.209
description: While Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was in this ecstasy. Gopīnātha Ācārya was very pleased, The associates of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu all laughed to see the Bhaṭṭācārya dance so.
text:
> dekhi' gopīnāthācārya haraṣita-mana
> bhaṭṭācāryera nṛtya dekhi' hāse prabhura gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing this; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:h:haraṣita]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---a pleased mind; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:hāse]]---laughs; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the associates of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: While Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was in this ecstasy. Gopīnātha Ācārya was very pleased, The associates of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu all laughed to see the Bhaṭṭācārya dance so.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.21
description: Mukunda Datta replied, "The Lord has already arrived here. We have come with Him."
text:
> mukunda kahe,---prabhura ihāṅ haila āgamane
> āmi-saba āsiyāchi mahāprabhura sane
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukundakahe]]---Mukunda replies; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:ā:āgamane]]---coming; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of us; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyāchi]]---have come; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with.
translation: Mukunda Datta replied, "The Lord has already arrived here. We have come with Him."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.210
description: Gopīnātha Ācārya told Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Sir, You have brought all this upon Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya."
text:
> gopīnāthācārya kahe mahāprabhura prati
> 'sei bhaṭṭācāryera prabhu kaile ei gati'
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---of the name Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prati]]---to; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of that Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---my Lord; [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---You have made; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:g:gati]]---such a situation.
translation: Gopīnātha Ācārya told Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Sir, You have brought all this upon Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.211
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "You are a devotee. Because of your association, Lord Jagannātha has shown him mercy."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---'tumi bhakta, tomāra saṅga haite
> jagannātha iṅhāre kṛpā kaila bhāla-mate'
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---you are a devotee; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅga]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---on account of your association; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---showed; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---very well.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "You are a devotee. Because of your association, Lord Jagannātha has shown him mercy."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.212
description: After this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu pacified the Bhaṭṭācārya, and when he was quieted, he offered many prayers to the Lord.
text:
> tabe bhaṭṭācārye prabhu susthira karila
> sthira hañā bhaṭṭācārya bahu stuti kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārye]]---unto Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:s:sthira]]---pacification; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:sthira]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being pacified; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---many; [[synonyms:s:stuti]]---prayers; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---offered.
translation: After this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu pacified the Bhaṭṭācārya, and when he was quieted, he offered many prayers to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.213
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "My dear Sir, You have delivered the entire world, but that is not a very great task. However, You have also delivered me, and that is certainly the work of very wonderful powers.
text:
> 'jagat nistārile tumi,---seha alpa-kārya
> āmā uddhārile tumi,---e śakti āścarya
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the whole world; [[synonyms:n:nistārile]]---have delivered; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:s:seha]]---that; [[synonyms:a:alpa]]-[[synonyms:k:kārya]]---minor activity; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]---me; [[synonyms:u:uddhārile]]---have delivered; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:e:e]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---power; [[synonyms:ā:āścarya]]---wonderful.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "My dear Sir, You have delivered the entire world, but that is not a very great task. However, You have also delivered me, and that is certainly the work of very wonderful powers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.214
description: "I had become dull-headed due to reading too many books on logic. Consequently I had become like an iron bar. Nonetheless, You have melted me, and therefore Your influence is very great."
text:
> tarka-śāstre jaḍa āmi, yaiche lauha-piṇḍa
> āmā dravāile tumi, pratāpa pracaṇḍa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tarka]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstre]]---due to logical scriptures; [[synonyms:j:jaḍa]]---dull; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just like; [[synonyms:l:lauha]]-[[synonyms:p:piṇḍa]]---an iron bar; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]---me; [[synonyms:d:dravāile]]---melted; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:p:pratāpa]]---power; [[synonyms:p:pracaṇḍa]]---very great.
translation: "I had become dull-headed due to reading too many books on logic. Consequently I had become like an iron bar. Nonetheless, You have melted me, and therefore Your influence is very great."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.215
description: After hearing the prayers offered by Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to His residence, and the Bhaṭṭācārya, through Gopīnātha Ācārya, induced the Lord to accept lunch there.
text:
> stuti śuni' mahāprabhu nija vāsā āilā
> bhaṭṭācārya ācārya-dvāre bhikṣā karāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:stuti]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---after hearing the prayers; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---own; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]]---to the residence; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---through Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---luncheon; [[synonyms:k:karāilā]]---induced to take.
translation: After hearing the prayers offered by Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to His residence, and the Bhaṭṭācārya, through Gopīnātha Ācārya, induced the Lord to accept lunch there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.216
description: Early the following morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to see Lord Jagannātha in the temple, and He saw the Lord rise from His bed.
text:
> āra dina prabhu gelā jagannātha-daraśane
> darśana karilā jagannātha-śayyotthāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---the next day; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---to see Jagannātha in the temple; [[synonyms:d:darśana]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---saw; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:ś:śayya]]-[[synonyms:u:utthāne]]---the Lord's rising from bed early in the morning.
translation: Early the following morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to see Lord Jagannātha in the temple, and He saw the Lord rise from His bed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.217
description: The priest there presented Him with garlands and prasāda that had been offered to Lord Jagannātha. This pleased Caitanya Mahāprabhu very much.
text:
> pūjārī āniyā mālā-prasādānna dilā
> prasādānna-mālā pāñā prabhu harṣa hailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūjārī]]---the priest; [[synonyms:ā:āniyā]]---bringing; [[synonyms:m:mālā]]---garlands; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]-[[synonyms:a:anna]]---remnants of food; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---offered; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]-[[synonyms:a:anna]]---the //prasāda//; [[synonyms:m:mālā]]---and garlands; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---pleased; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became.
translation: The priest there presented Him with garlands and prasāda that had been offered to Lord Jagannātha. This pleased Caitanya Mahāprabhu very much.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.218
description: Carefully tying the prasāda and garlands in a cloth, Caitanya Mahāprabhu hastened to the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.
text:
> sei prasādānna-mālā añcale bāndhiyā
> bhaṭṭācāryera ghare āilā tvarāyukta hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]-[[synonyms:a:anna]]---those remnants of food; [[synonyms:m:mālā]]---and garlands; [[synonyms:a:añcale]]---in the end of His cloth; [[synonyms:b:bāndhiyā]]---binding; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to the house; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---went; [[synonyms:t:tvarā]]-[[synonyms:y:yukta]]---hasty; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being.
translation: Carefully tying the prasāda and garlands in a cloth, Caitanya Mahāprabhu hastened to the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.219
description: He arrived at the Bhaṭṭācārya's house a little before sunrise, just when the Bhaṭṭācārya was arising from bed.
text:
> aruṇodaya-kāle haila prabhura āgamana
> sei-kāle bhaṭṭācāryera haila jāgaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aruṇa]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]]---before sunrise; [[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at the time; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---the coming; [[synonyms:s:sei]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:j:jāgaraṇa]]---arising from bed.
translation: He arrived at the Bhaṭṭācārya's house a little before sunrise, just when the Bhaṭṭācārya was arising from bed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.22
description: As soon as Gopīnātha Ācārya saw Nityānanda Prabhu, he offered his obeisances unto Him. In this way, meeting all the devotees, he asked about news of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu again and again.
text:
> nityānanda-gosāñike ācārya kaila namaskāra
> sabe meli' puche prabhura vārtā bāra bāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñike]]---unto Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---offered obeisances; [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:m:meli']]---meeting them all; [[synonyms:p:puche]]---inquires; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vārtā]]---news; [[synonyms:b:bāra]] [[synonyms:b:bāra]]---again and again.
translation: As soon as Gopīnātha Ācārya saw Nityānanda Prabhu, he offered his obeisances unto Him. In this way, meeting all the devotees, he asked about news of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu again and again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.220
description: As Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya arose from bed, he distinctly chanted, "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa." Lord Caitanya was very pleased to hear him chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> 'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa' sphuṭa kahi' bhaṭṭācārya jāgilā
> kṛṣṇa-nāma śuni' prabhura ānanda bāḍilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---chanting the name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sphuṭa]]---distinctly; [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---saying; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:j:jāgilā]]---got up from the bed; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:b:bāḍilā]]---increased.
translation: As Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya arose from bed, he distinctly chanted, "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa." Lord Caitanya was very pleased to hear him chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.221
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya noticed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu outside, and with great haste he went to Him and offered prayers unto His lotus feet.
text:
> bāhire prabhura teṅho pāila daraśana
> āste-vyaste āsi' kaila caraṇa vandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāhire]]---outside the house; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---sight; [[synonyms:ā:āste]]-[[synonyms:v:vyaste]]---with great haste; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming there; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---worshiping the lotus feet.
translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya noticed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu outside, and with great haste he went to Him and offered prayers unto His lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.222
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya offered a carpet for the Lord to sit upon, and both of them sat there. Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu opened the prasāda and placed it in the hands of the Bhaṭṭācārya.
text:
> vasite āsana diyā duṅheta vasilā
> prasādānna khuli' prabhu tāṅra hāte dilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vasite]]---to sit; [[synonyms:ā:āsana]]---carpet; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---offering; [[synonyms:d:duṅheta]]---both of them; [[synonyms:v:vasilā]]---sat down; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]-[[synonyms:a:anna]]---the //prasāda//; [[synonyms:k:khuli']]---opening; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:h:hāte]]---in the hand; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---offered.
translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya offered a carpet for the Lord to sit upon, and both of them sat there. Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu opened the prasāda and placed it in the hands of the Bhaṭṭācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.223
description: At that time the Bhaṭṭācārya had not even washed his mouth, nor had he taken his bath or finished his morning duties. Nonetheless, he was very pleased to receive the prasāda of Lord Jagannātha.
text:
> prasādānna pāñā bhaṭṭācāryera ānanda haila
> snāna, sandhyā, danta-dhāvana yadyapi nā kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]-[[synonyms:a:anna]]---the remnants of food; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing; [[synonyms:s:sandhyā]]---morning duties; [[synonyms:d:danta]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāvana]]---washing the teeth; [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---finished.
translation: At that time the Bhaṭṭācārya had not even washed his mouth, nor had he taken his bath or finished his morning duties. Nonetheless, he was very pleased to receive the prasāda of Lord Jagannātha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.224
description: By the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all the dullness in the mind of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was eradicated. After reciting the following two verses, he ate the prasāda offered to him.
text:
> caitanya-prasāde manera saba jāḍya gela
> ei śloka paḍi' anna bhakṣaṇa karila
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāde]]---by the mercy of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:manera]]---of the mind; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:j:jāḍya]]---dullness; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went away; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---these verses; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---remnants of food; [[synonyms:b:bhakṣaṇa]]---eating; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did.
translation: By the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all the dullness in the mind of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was eradicated. After reciting the following two verses, he ate the prasāda offered to him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.225
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya said, " 'One should eat the mahā-prasāda of the Lord immediately upon receiving it, even though it is dried up, stale or brought from a distant country. One should consider neither time nor place.
text:
> śuṣkaṁ paryuṣitaṁ vāpi
> nītaṁ vā dūra-deśataḥ
> prāpti-mātreṇa bhoktavyaṁ
> nātra kāla-vicāraṇā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuṣkam]]---dry; [[synonyms:p:paryuṣitam]]---stale; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:n:nītam]]---brought; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:d:dūra]]-[[synonyms:d:deśataḥ]]---from a distant country; [[synonyms:p:prāpti]]-[[synonyms:m:mātreṇa]]---only with the receiving; [[synonyms:b:bhoktavyam]]---to be eaten; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:atra]]---in this; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]-[[synonyms:v:vicāraṇā]]---consideration of time or place.
translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya said, " 'One should eat the mahā-prasāda of the Lord immediately upon receiving it, even though it is dried up, stale or brought from a distant country. One should consider neither time nor place.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.226
description: " 'The prasāda of Lord Kṛṣṇa is to be eaten by gentlemen as soon as it is received; there should be no hesitation. There are no regulative principles concerning time and place. This is the order of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.' "
text:
> na deśa-niyamas tatra
> na kāla-niyamas tathā
> prāptam annaṁ drutaṁ śiṣṭair
> bhoktavyaṁ harir abravīt
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:d:deśa]]---of the country; [[synonyms:n:niyamaḥ]]---regulation; [[synonyms:t:tatra]]---in that; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]---of time; [[synonyms:n:niyamaḥ]]---regulation; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---so also; [[synonyms:p:prāptam]]---received; [[synonyms:a:annam]]---//prasāda//; [[synonyms:d:drutam]]---hastily; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣṭaiḥ]]---by gentlemen; [[synonyms:b:bhoktavyam]]---to be eaten; [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:a:abravīt]]---has said.
translation: “ 'The prasāda of Lord Kṛṣṇa is to be eaten by gentlemen as soon as it is received; there should be no hesitation. There are no regulative principles concerning time and place. This is the order of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.' "
purport: These verses are quoted from the //Padma Purāṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.227
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to see this. He became ecstatic in love of Godhead and embraced Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.
text:
> dekhi' ānandita haila mahāprabhura mana
> premāviṣṭa hañā prabhu kailā āliṅgana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing this; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very much pleased; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---absorbed in the ecstasy of love of God; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very pleased to see this. He became ecstatic in love of Godhead and embraced Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.228
description: The Lord and the servant embraced each other and began to dance. Simply by touching each other, they became ecstatic.
text:
> dui-jane dhari' duṅhe karena nartana
> prabhu-bhṛtya duṅhā sparśe, doṅhāra phule mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---both of them; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---embracing; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---do; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dancing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:b:bhṛtya]]---the master and the servant; [[synonyms:d:duṅhā]]---both; [[synonyms:s:sparśe]]---by touching each other; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]]---of both of them; [[synonyms:p:phule]]---were excited; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---minds.
translation: The Lord and the servant embraced each other and began to dance. Simply by touching each other, they became ecstatic.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.229
description: As they danced and embraced, spiritual symptoms manifested in their bodies. They perspired, trembled and shed tears, and the Lord began to speak in His ecstasy.
text:
> sveda-kampa-aśru duṅhe ānande bhāsilā
> premāviṣṭa hañā prabhu kahite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sveda]]---perspiration; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:b:bhāsilā]]---floated; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---absorbed in ecstatic love of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began.
translation: As they danced and embraced, spiritual symptoms manifested in their bodies. They perspired, trembled and shed tears, and the Lord began to speak in His ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.23
description: Mukunda Datta continued, "After accepting the sannyāsa order, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu has come to Jagannātha Purī and has brought all of us with Him.
text:
> mukunda kahe,---'mahāprabhu sannyāsa kariyā
> nīlācale āilā saṅge āmā-sabā lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukunda]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Mukunda Datta replies; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---after accepting the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---has come; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Him; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all of us; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking.
translation: Mukunda Datta continued, "After accepting the sannyāsa order, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu has come to Jagannātha Purī and has brought all of us with Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.230
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Today I have conquered the three worlds very easily. Today I have ascended to the spiritual world."
text:
> "āji muñi anāyāse jininu tribhuvana
> āji muñi karinu vaikuṇṭha ārohaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āji]]---today; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:a:anāyāse]]---very easily; [[synonyms:j:jininu]]---conquered; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvana]]---the three worlds; [[synonyms:ā:āji]]---today; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:karinu]]---did; [[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭha]]---to the spiritual world; [[synonyms:ā:ārohaṇa]]---ascending.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Today I have conquered the three worlds very easily. Today I have ascended to the spiritual world."
purport: The goal of human perfection is stated here in brief. One has to surpass all the planetary systems of the material universe, pierce through the covering of the universe and reach the spiritual world, known as Vaikuṇṭhaloka. The Vaikuṇṭhalokas are variegated spiritual planets situated in the Lord's impersonal bodily effulgence, known as the //brahmajyoti.// One may aspire to elevate himself to a heavenly planet within the material world, such as the moon, the sun or Venus, but if one is spiritually advanced in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, he does not wish to remain within the material universe, even in a higher planetary system. Rather, he prefers to penetrate the covering of the universe and attain the spiritual world. He can then be situated in one of the Vaikuṇṭha planets there. However, the devotees under the guidance of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu aspire to reach the topmost spiritual planet, known as Goloka Vṛndāvana, the residence of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and His eternal associates.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.235
description: " 'When a person unreservedly takes shelter of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the unlimited, merciful Lord bestows His causeless mercy upon him. Thus he can pass over the insurmountable ocean of nescience. Those whose intelligence is fixed in the bodily conception, who think, "I am this body," are fit food for dogs and jackals. The Supreme Lord never bestows His mercy upon such people.' "
text:
> yeṣāṁ sa eṣa bhagavān dayayed anantaḥ
> sarvātmanāśrita-pado yadi nirvyalīkam
> te dustarām atitaranti ca deva-māyāṁ
> naiṣāṁ mamāham iti dhīḥ śva-śṛgāla-bhakṣye
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yeṣām]]---unto those who are fully surrendered souls; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:e:eṣaḥ]]---this; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:d:dayayet]]---may show mercy; [[synonyms:a:anantaḥ]]---the unlimited; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmanā]]---fully, without reservation; [[synonyms:ā:āśrita]]-[[synonyms:p:padaḥ]]---those who have taken shelter of the Lord; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:n:nirvyalīkam]]---without duplicity; [[synonyms:t:te]]---such persons; [[synonyms:d:dustarām]]---insurmountable; [[synonyms:a:atitaranti]]---surpass; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:m:māyām]]---the illusory material energy; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:e:eṣām]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mama]] [[synonyms:a:aham]]---"my" and "I"; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---such; [[synonyms:d:dhīḥ]]---intelligence; [[synonyms:ś:śva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śṛgāla]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakṣye]]---in the body, which is to be eaten by dogs and jackals.
translation: “ 'When a person unreservedly takes shelter of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the unlimited, merciful Lord bestows His causeless mercy upon him. Thus he can pass over the insurmountable ocean of nescience. Those whose intelligence is fixed in the bodily conception, who think, "I am this body," are fit food for dogs and jackals. The Supreme Lord never bestows His mercy upon such people.' "
purport:
The Supreme Lord never bestows His benediction upon those fixed in the bodily conception. As Kṛṣṇa clearly states in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:18:66|(Bg. 18.66)]]:

> sarva-dharmān parityajya
> mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja
> ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo
> mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ

"Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear."

In this verse that Caitanya Mahāprabhu has quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:7:42|(2.7.42)]], the meaning of Śrī Kṛṣṇa's statement is explained. Kṛṣṇa bestowed His causeless mercy upon Arjuna just to get him out of the bodily conception. This was done at the very beginning of the Second Chapter of the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:2:13|(Bg. 2.13)]], where Kṛṣṇa says, //dehino 'smin yathā dehe kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā.// In this body, there is an owner, and one should not consider the body to be the self. This is the first instruction to be assimilated by a devotee. If one is under the bodily conception, he is unable to realize his true identity and engage in the loving devotional service of the Lord. Unless one comes to the transcendental position, he cannot expect the causeless mercy of the Supreme Lord, nor can he cross over the vast ocean of material nescience. This is also confirmed in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:7:14|(Bg. 7.14)]]: //mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṁ taranti te.// Without surrendering unto the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, one cannot expect release from the clutches of //māyā,// the illusory energy. According to //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:10:2:32|(10.2.32)]], Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// who falsely think of themselves as liberated from the clutches of //māyā// are called //vimukta-māninaḥ.// Actually, they are not liberated, but they think that they have become liberated and have become Nārāyaṇa Himself. Although they have apparently realized that they are not the material body but spirit soul, they nonetheless neglect the duty of the spirit soul, which is to render service to the Supreme Soul. Therefore their intelligence remains unsanctified. Unless one's intelligence is sanctified, one cannot apply it to understanding devotional service. Devotional service begins when the mind, intelligence and ego are completely purified. Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// do not purify their intelligence, mind and ego, and consequently they cannot engage in the service of the Lord or expect the causeless mercy of the Lord. Although they rise to a very high position by executing severe austerities and penances, they still hover in the material world without the benediction of the lotus feet of the Lord. Sometimes they rise to the Brahman effulgence, but because their minds are not completely purified, they must return to material existence.

The //karmīs// are fully under the bodily conception of life, and the //jñānīs,// although theoretically understanding that they are not the body, also have no information about the lotus feet of the Lord because they overly stress impersonalism. Consequently both //karmīs// and //jñānīs// are unfit for receiving the mercy of the Lord and becoming devotees. Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura therefore says, //karma-kāṇḍa jñāna-kāṇḍa, kevala viṣera bhāṇḍa:// those who have taken to the process of //karma-kāṇḍa// (fruitive activity) and //jñāna-kāṇḍa// (speculation on the science of transcendence) have simply eaten from poisoned pots. They are condemned to remain in material existence life after life until they take shelter of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. This is confirmed in //Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā// (7.19):

> bahūnāṁ janmanām ante
> jñānavān māṁ prapadyate
> vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti
> sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ

"After many births and deaths, he who is actually in knowledge surrenders unto Me, knowing Me to be the cause of all causes and all that is. Such a great soul is very rare."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.241
description: Then the Bhaṭṭācārya asked Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Which item is most important in the execution of devotional service?" The Lord replied that the most important item was the chanting of the holy name of the Lord.
text:
> bhakti-sādhana-śreṣṭha śunite haila mana
> prabhu upadeśa kaila nāma-saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---in the execution of devotional service; [[synonyms:ś:śreṣṭha]]---the most important item; [[synonyms:ś:śunite]]---to hear; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---it was; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:u:upadeśa]]---advice; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---gave; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the holy name of the Lord.
translation: Then the Bhaṭṭācārya asked Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Which item is most important in the execution of devotional service?" The Lord replied that the most important item was the chanting of the holy name of the Lord.
purport:
There are nine items to be executed in devotional service. These are enumerated in the following verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:7:5:23|(7.5.23)]]:

> śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoḥ
> smaraṇaṁ pāda-sevanam
> arcanaṁ vandanaṁ dāsyaṁ
> sakhyam ātma-nivedanam

Hearing the glories of the Lord, chanting, remembering, serving the lotus feet of the Lord, offering worship in the temple, offering prayers, becoming a servant of the Lord, becoming the Lord's friend, and //sarvātma-nivedana,// offering oneself fully at the lotus feet of the Lord---these are the nine devotional processes. In //The Nectar of Devotion,// When Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya asked the Lord which item was most important, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately answered that the most important item is the chanting of the holy names of the Lord-Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare. He then quoted the following verse from the //Bṛhan-nāradīya Purāṇa// (Thirty-eighth Chapter, verse 126) to confirm His statement.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.242
description: " 'In this age of quarrel and hypocrisy, the only means of deliverence is the chanting of the holy names of the Lord. There is no other way. There is no other way. There is no other way.' "
text:
> harer nāma harer nāma
> harer nāmaiva kevalam
> kalau nāsty eva nāsty eva
> nāsty eva gatir anyathā
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of the Lord Hari; [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of the Lord Hari; [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:k:kevalam]]---only; [[synonyms:k:kalau]]---in this Age of Kali; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:a:asti]]---there is not; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:a:asti]]---there is not; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:a:asti]]---there is not; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:g:gatiḥ]]---means; [[synonyms:a:anyathā]]---other.
translation: “ 'In this age of quarrel and hypocrisy, the only means of deliverence is the chanting of the holy names of the Lord. There is no other way. There is no other way. There is no other way.' "
purport:
Because the people of this age are so fallen, they can simply chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// In this way they can rid themselves of the bodily conception of life and become eligible to engage in the Lord's devotional service. One cannot engage in the devotional service of the Lord without being purified of all contamination. This is confirmed in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:7:28|(Bg. 7.28)]]:

> yeṣāṁ tv anta-gataṁ pāpaṁ
> janānāṁ puṇya-karmaṇām
> te dvandva-moha-nirmuktā
> bhajante māṁ dṛḍha-vratāḥ

"Persons who have acted piously in previous lives and in this life and whose sinful actions are completely eradicated are freed from the dualities of delusion, and they engage themselves in My service with determination." Sometimes people are surprised to see young men and women take so seriously to the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. By giving up sinful activity-illicit sex, meat-eating, intoxication and gambling-and strictly following the injunctions given by the spiritual master, they have become purified of all contamination. They can therefore fully engage in the devotional service of the Lord.

In this Age of Kali, //hari-kīrtana// is very, very important. The importance of chanting the holy name of the Lord is stated in the following verses from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (12.3.51-52):

> kaler doṣa-nidhe rājann
> asti hy eko mahān guṇaḥ
> kīrtanād eva kṛṣṇasya
> mukta-saṅgaḥ paraṁ vrajet

> kṛte yad dhyāyato viṣṇuṁ
> tretāyāṁ yajato makhaiḥ
> dvāpare paricaryāyāṁ
> kalau tad dhari-kīrtanāt

"The most important factor in this Age of Kali, which is an ocean of faults, is that one can be free from all contamination and become eligible to enter the kingdom of God simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra.// The self-realization that was achieved in the Satya millennium by meditation, in the Tretā millennium by the performance of different sacrifices, and in the Dvāpara millennium by worship of Lord Kṛṣṇa can be achieved in the Age of Kali simply by chanting the holy names, Hare Kṛṣṇa." ()

description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very elaborately explained the harer nāma verse of the Bṛhan-nāradīya Purāṇa, and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was struck with wonder to hear His explanation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.244
description: Gopīnātha Ācārya reminded Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, "My dear Bhaṭṭācārya, what I foretold to you has now taken place."
text:
> gopīnāthācārya bale,---'āmi pūrve ye kahila
> śuna, bhaṭṭācārya, tomāra sei ta' ha-ila'
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---of the name Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---says; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---previously; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---what; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---said; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---my dear Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---has happened.
translation: Gopīnātha Ācārya reminded Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, "My dear Bhaṭṭācārya, what I foretold to you has now taken place."
purport: Previously Gopīnātha Ācārya had informed Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya that when he would be blessed by the Lord he would thoroughly understand the transcendental process of devotional service. This prediction was now fulfilled. The Bhaṭṭācārya was fully converted to the cult of Vaiṣṇavism, and he was following the principles automatically, without being pressured. in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:2:40|(Bg. 2.40)]] it is therefore said, //svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt:// "Simply by performing a little devotional service, one can escape the greatest danger." Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya had been in the greatest danger because he had adhered to Māyāvāda philosophy. Somehow or other he came into contact with Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and became a perfect devotee. In this way he was saved from the great falldown of impersonalism.

He has descended because He is an ocean of transcendental mercy. Let me surrender unto His lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.255
description: "Let my consciousness, which is like a honeybee, take shelter of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has just now appeared as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu to teach the ancient system of devotional service to Himself. This system had almost been lost due to the influence of time."

> prāduṣkartuṁ kṛṣṇa-caitanya-nāmā

> gāḍhaṁ gāḍhaṁ līyatāṁ citta-bhṛṅgaḥ

translation: "Let my consciousness, which is like a honeybee, take shelter of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has just now appeared as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu to teach the ancient system of devotional service to Himself. This system had almost been lost due to the influence of time."
purport:
As stated in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:4:7|(Bg. 4.7)]]:

> yadā yadā hi dharmasya
> glānir bhavati bhārata
> abhyutthānam adharmasya
> tadātmānaṁ sṛjāmy aham

"Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice, O descendant of Bharata, and a predominant rise of irreligion-at that time I descend Myself." [[books:bg:4:7|(Bg. 4.7)]]

This is also the case with Caitanya Mahāprabhu's appearance. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu appeared in this world as a disguised incarnation of Kṛṣṇa, but His appearance is confirmed in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// the //Mahābhārata// and other Vedic scriptures. He appeared in order to teach the fallen souls in this material world, for in this Age of Kali almost everyone has become attached to fruitive and ritualistic activities and mental speculation. Consequently there was a great need to revive the system of devotional service. The Lord Himself personally came down disguised as a devotee so that the fallen populace might take advantage of the Lord's example.

At the conclusion of the //Bhagavad-gītā,// Lord Kṛṣṇa advised complete surrender unto Him, promising all protection to His devotee. Unfortunately, people are so fallen that they cannot accept the instructions of Lord Kṛṣṇa; therefore Kṛṣṇa returned with the same mission, but He executed it in a different way. As Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, He ordered us to surrender unto Himself, but as Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, He taught us how to surrender to Kṛṣṇa. Therefore He is praised by the Gosvāmīs: //namo mahā-vadānyāya kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāye te.// Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is certainly the Personality of Godhead, but He is not as magnanimous as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Lord Kṛṣṇa simply gave orders for one to become His devotee (//man-manā bhava mad-bhaktaḥ//), but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu actually taught the process of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. If one wants to become a devotee of Kṛṣṇa, he must first take shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, following in the footsteps of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and other exalted devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.257
description: Indeed, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya became an unalloyed devotee of Caitanya Mahāprabhu; he did not know anything but the service of the Lord.
text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.261
description: [The verse read:] "One who seeks Your compassion and thus tolerates all kinds of adverse conditions due to the karma of his past deeds, who engages always in Your devotional service with his mind, words and body, and who always offers obeisances unto You is certainly a bona fide candidate for becoming Your unalloyed devotee."
text:
> tat te 'nukampāṁ su-samīkṣamāṇo
> bhuñjāna evātma-kṛtaṁ vipākam
> hṛd-vāg-vapurbhir vidadhan namas te
> jīveta yo bhakti-pade sa dāya-bhāk

translation: [The verse read:] "One who seeks Your compassion and thus tolerates all kinds of adverse conditions due to the karma of his past deeds, who engages always in Your devotional service with his mind, words and body, and who always offers obeisances unto You is certainly a bona fide candidate for becoming Your unalloyed devotee."
purport: When reading this verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.14.8), Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya changed the original reading from //mukti-pade// to //bhakti-pade. Mukti// means liberation and merging into the impersonal Brahman effulgence. //Bhakti// means rendering transcendental service unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Because of having developed pure devotional service, the Bhaṭṭācārya did not like the word //mukti-pade,// which refers to the impersonal Brahman feature of the Lord. However, he was not authorized to change a word in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will explain. Although the Bhaṭṭācārya changed the word in his devotional ecstasy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not approve of it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.262

> 'bhakti-pade' kene paḍa, ki tomāra āśaya

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.263
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "The awakening of pure love of Godhead, which is the result of devotional service, far surpasses liberation from material bondage. For those averse to devotional service, merging into the Brahman effulgence is a kind of punishment."
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya kahe,---'bhakti'-sama nahe mukti-phala
> bhagavad-bhakti-vimukhera haya daṇḍa kevala
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal to; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---of liberation; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---the result; [[synonyms:b:bhagavat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---to the devotional service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:v:vimukhera]]---of one who is averse to; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---it is; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---the punishment; [[synonyms:k:kevala]]---only.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "The awakening of pure love of Godhead, which is the result of devotional service, far surpasses liberation from material bondage. For those averse to devotional service, merging into the Brahman effulgence is a kind of punishment."
purport:
In the //Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa// it is said:

> siddha-lokas tu tamasaḥ
> pāre yatra vasanti hi
> siddhā brahma-sukhe magnā
> daityāś ca hariṇā hatāḥ

"In Siddhaloka [Brahmaloka] there live two kinds of living entities---those who are killed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead due to their having been demons in their previous lives and those who are very fond of enjoying the impersonal effulgence of the Lord." The word //tamasaḥ// means "the coverings of the universe." Layers of material elements cover the universe, and outside these coverings is the impersonal Brahman effulgence. If one is destined to remain in the Lord's impersonal effulgence, he misses the opportunity to render service to the Personality of Godhead. Therefore devotees consider remaining in the impersonal Brahman effulgence a kind of punishment. Sometimes devotees think of merging into the Brahman effulgence, and consequently they are promoted to Siddhaloka. Because of their impersonal understanding, they are actually punished. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya continues to explain the distinction between //mukti-pada// and //bhakti-pada// in the following verses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.264-265
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya continued, "The impersonalists, who do not accept the transcendental form of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and the demons, who are always engaged in blaspheming and fighting with Him, are punished by being merged into the Brahman effulgence. But that does not happen to the person engaged in the devotional service of the Lord.

> yei nindā-yuddhādika kare tāṅra sane
>
> sei duira daṇḍa haya---'brahma-sāyujya-mukti'

But that does not happen to the person engaged in the devotional service of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.266
description: "There are five kinds of liberation: sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya, sārṣṭi and sāyujya.
text:
> yadyapi se mukti haya pañca-parakāra
> sālokya-sāmīpya-sārūpya-sārṣṭi-sāyujya āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:p:parakāra]]---of five different varieties; [[synonyms:s:sālokya]]---of the name //sālokya//; [[synonyms:s:sāmīpya]]---of the name //sāmīpya//; [[synonyms:s:sārūpya]]---of the name //sārūpya//; [[synonyms:s:sārṣṭi]]---of the name //sārṣṭi//; [[synonyms:s:sāyujya]]---of the name //sāyujya//; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and.
translation: "There are five kinds of liberation: sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya, sārṣṭi and sāyujya.
purport: Sālokya means that after material liberation one is promoted to the planet where the Supreme Personality of Godhead resides. //Sāmīpya// means remaining an associate of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. //Sārūpya// means attaining a four-handed form exactly like that of the Lord. //Sārṣṭi// means attaining opulences like those of the Supreme Lord, and //sāyujya// means merging into the Brahman effulgence of the Lord. These are the five types of liberation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.267
description: "If there is a chance to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead, a pure devotee sometimes accepts the sālokya, sārūpya, sāmīpya or sārṣṭi forms of liberation, but never sāyujya.
text:
> 'sālokyādi' cāri yadi haya sevā-dvāra
> tabu kadācit bhakta kare aṅgīkāra

translation: "If there is a chance to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead, a pure devotee sometimes accepts the sālokya, sārūpya, sāmīpya or sārṣṭi forms of liberation, but never sāyujya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.268
description: "A pure devotee does not like even to hear about sāyujya-mukti, which inspires him with fear and hatred. Indeed, the pure devotee would rather go to hell than merge into the effulgence of the Lord."
text:
> 'sāyujya' śunite bhaktera haya ghṛṇā-bhaya
> naraka vāñchaye, tabu sāyujya nā laya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sāyujya]]---liberation by merging into the effulgence; [[synonyms:ś:śunite]]---even to hear; [[synonyms:b:bhaktera]]---of the devotee; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:g:ghṛṇā]]---hatred; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:n:naraka]]---a hellish condition of life; [[synonyms:v:vāñchaye]]---he desires; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:s:sāyujya]]---merging into the effulgence of the Lord; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:l:laya]]---never accepts.
translation: "A pure devotee does not like even to hear about sāyujya-mukti, which inspires him with fear and hatred. Indeed, the pure devotee would rather go to hell than merge into the effulgence of the Lord."
purport: Śrīla Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī has sung: //kaivalyaṁ narakāyate.// The impersonalist's conception of becoming one with the effulgence of the Lord is exactly like hell. Therefore, of the five types of liberation, the first four (//sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya// and //sārṣṭi//) are not so undesirable because they can be avenues of service to the Lord. Nonetheless, a pure devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa rejects even these types of liberation; he aspires only to serve Kṛṣṇa birth after birth. He is not very interested in stopping the repetition of birth, for he simply desires to serve the Lord, even in hellish circumstances. Consequently the pure devotee hates and fears //sāyujya-mukti,// merging into the effulgence of the Lord. This merging is due to an offense committed against the transcendental loving service of the Lord, and therefore it is not at all desirable for a pure devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.269
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya continued, "There are two kinds of sāyujya-mukti: merging into the Brahman effulgence and merging into the personal body of the Lord. Merging into the Lord's body is even more abominable than merging into His effulgence."
text:
> brahme, īśvare sāyujya dui ta' prakāra
> brahma-sāyujya haite īśvara-sāyujya dhikkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahme]]---in the Brahman effulgence; [[synonyms:ī:īśvare]]---in the body of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sāyujya]]---merging; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---varieties; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:s:sāyujya]]---merging into the Brahman effulgence; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---than; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:s:sāyujya]]---merging into the body of the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dhikkāra]]---more abominable.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya continued, "There are two kinds of sāyujya-mukti: merging into the Brahman effulgence and merging into the personal body of the Lord. Merging into the Lord's body is even more abominable than merging into His effulgence."
purport:
According to the opinion of the Māyāvādī Vedāntists, the living entity's ultimate success is to merge into the impersonal Brahman. The impersonal Brahman, or bodily effulgence of the Supreme Lord, is known as Brahmaloka or Siddhaloka. According to the //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.40), //yasya prabhā prabhavato jagad-aṇḍa-koṭi:// the material universes are generated from the bodily rays of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. //Yogīs// who follow the principles of Patañjali accept the personality of the Absolute Truth, but they want to merge into the transcendental body of the Supreme Lord. That is their desire. Being the greatest authority, the Supreme Lord can easily allow many millions of living entities to merge into His body. The origin of everything is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Bhagavān, and His bodily effulgence is known as the //brahmajyoti,// Brahmaloka or Siddhaloka. Thus Brahmaloka or Siddhaloka is a place where many sparklike living entities, parts and parcels of the Supreme Lord, are assembled. Because these living entities do not wish to keep their individual existences, they are combined and allowed to remain in Brahmaloka like so many atomic particles of sunshine emanating from the sun.

The word //siddha// is very significant. //Siddha// refers to one who has realized the Brahman effulgence and who has complete knowledge that the living entity is not a material atom but a spiritual spark. This understanding is described in the //Bhagavad-gītā// as //brahma-bhūta.// In the conditioned state, the living entity is known as //jīva-bhūta,// or "the living force within matter." //Brahma-bhūta// living entities are allowed to stay in Brahmaloka or Siddhaloka, but unfortunately they sometimes again fall into the material world because they are not engaged in devotional service. This is supported by //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:10:2:32|(10.2.32)]]: //ye 'nye 'ravindākṣa.// These semi-liberated souls falsely claim to be liberated, but unless one engages in devotional service to the Lord, he is still materially contaminated. Therefore these living entities have been described as //vimukta-māninaḥ,// meaning that they falsely consider themselves liberated although their intelligence is not yet purified. Although these living entities undergo severe austerities to rise to the platform of Siddhaloka, they cannot remain there perpetually, for they are bereft of //ānanda// (bliss). Even though these living entities attain the //brahma-bhūta// stage and realize the Supreme Personality of Godhead through His bodily effulgence, they nonetheless fall down due to neglecting the Lord's service. They do not properly utilize whatever little knowledge they have of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Not attaining //ānanda,// or bliss, they come down to the material world to enjoy. This is certainly a falldown for one who is actually liberated. The //bhaktas// consider such a falldown equal to achieving a place in hell.

The followers of the Patañjali //yoga// system actually want to merge into the body of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This indicates that they do not want to engage in His service despite their knowledge of Him, and thus their position is even more abominable than that of those who want to merge into the Lord's effulgence. These //yogīs// meditate on the four-handed Viṣṇu form of the Lord in order to merge into His body. The Patañjali system describes the form of the Lord as //kleśa-karma-vipākāśayair aparāmṛṣṭaḥ puruṣa-viśeṣa īśvaraḥ:// "The Supreme Personality of Godhead is a person who does not partake of a miserable material life." The //yogīs// accept the eternity of the Supreme Person in one of their //mantras-sa pūrveṣām api guruḥ kālānavac-chedāt:// "Such a person is always supreme and is not influenced by the element of time." The followers of the Patañjali system therefore accept the eternity of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, yet, according to them: //puruṣārtha-śūnyānāṁ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṁ svarūpa-pratiṣṭhā vā citi-śaktir iti.// They believe that in the perfectional stage, the conception of //puruṣa// is vanquished. According to their description: //citi-śaktir iti.// They believe that when one becomes perfect, he cannot remain a person. This //yoga// system is therefore abominable because its final conception is impersonal. In the beginning, these //yogīs// accept the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but they ultimately give up this idea in order to become impersonal. They are most unfortunate because although they have a personal conception of the Absolute Truth, they neglect to render devotional service to the Lord and thus fall down again into the material world. This is supported by //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:10:2:32|(10.2.32)]]. //Āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ patanty adho 'nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ:// due to neglecting the lotus feet of the Lord, these //yogīs// again fall down into the material existence (//patanty adhaḥ//). Consequently this path of //yoga// is more abominable than the impersonalists' path. This conclusion is also supported by Lord Kapiladeva in the following verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:29:13|(3.29.13)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.27
description: "Just as I was thinking of meeting you, by chance we have actually met.
text:
> tomāra milane yabe āmāra haila mana
> daive sei kṣaṇe pāiluṅ tomāra daraśana
