translation: "Just as I was thinking of meeting you, by chance we have actually met.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.270
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya concluded, " 'Even though he is offered all kinds of liberation, the pure devotee does not accept them. He is fully satisfied engaging in the service of the Lord.' "
text:
> sālokya-sārṣṭi-sāmīpya-
> sārūpyaikatvam apy uta
> dīyamānaṁ na gṛhṇanti
> vinā mat-sevanaṁ janāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sālokya]]---the liberation of living in the same planet as the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sārṣṭi]]---to have opulence exactly like that of the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sāmīpya]]---to associate always with the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sārūpya]]---to achieve a body like that of the Lord; [[synonyms:e:ekatvam]]---to merge into the body of the Lord; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:u:uta]]---it is said; [[synonyms:d:dīyamānam]]---being offered; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:g:gṛhṇanti]]---do accept; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:m:mat]]---My; [[synonyms:s:sevanam]]---service; [[synonyms:j:janāḥ]]---the pure devotees.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya concluded, " 'Even though he is offered all kinds of liberation, the pure devotee does not accept them. He is fully satisfied engaging in the service of the Lord.' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.271
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "The word 'mukti-pade' has another meaning. Mukti-pada directly refers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---'mukti-pade'ra āra artha haya
> mukti-pada-śabde 'sākṣāt īśvara' kahaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]-[[synonyms:p:padera]]---of the term //mukti-pade//; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word //mukti-pada//; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:kahaya]]---is said.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "The word 'mukti-pade' has another meaning. Mukti-pada directly refers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.272
description: "All kinds of liberation exist under the feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; therefore He is known as mukti-pada. According to another meaning, mukti is the ninth subject, and the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the shelter of liberation.
text:
> mukti pade yāṅra, sei 'mukti-pada' haya
> kimvā navama padārtha 'muktira' samāśraya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---such a person; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is known as //mukti-pada//; [[synonyms:k:kimvā]]---or; [[synonyms:n:navama]]---ninth; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---subject matter; [[synonyms:m:muktira]]---of liberation; [[synonyms:s:samāśraya]]---shelter.
translation: "All kinds of liberation exist under the feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; therefore He is known as mukti-pada. According to another meaning, mukti is the ninth subject, and the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the shelter of liberation.
purport: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is also known as Mukunda, or He who gives transcendental bliss by offering all kinds of //mukti. Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// is divided into twelve cantos, and in the Ninth Canto different kinds of //mukti// are described. But the Tenth Canto is the actual center of all discussions of //mukti// because the Personality of Godhead Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is the tenth subject discussed in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// is the exclusive subject of the Tenth Canto. Since all types of //muktis// reside at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, He may be called //mukti-pada.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.273
description: "Since I can understand Kṛṣṇa according to these two meanings," Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "what point is there in changing the verse?" Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "I was not able to give that reading to the verse.
text:
> dui-arthe 'kṛṣṇa' kahi, kene pāṭha phiri
> sārvabhauma kahe,---o-pāṭha kahite nā pāri
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:a:arthe]]---by two interpretations; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I accept; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:p:pāṭha]]---reading; [[synonyms:p:phiri]]---changing; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sārvabhauma replied; [[synonyms:o:o]]-[[synonyms:p:pāṭha]]---such a reading; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to say; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---am able.
translation: "Since I can understand Kṛṣṇa according to these two meanings," Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "what point is there in changing the verse?" Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "I was not able to give that reading to the verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.274
description: "Although Your explanation is correct, it should not be used because there is ambiguity in the word 'mukti-pada.'
text:
> yadyapi tomāra artha ei śabde kaya
> tathāpi 'āśliṣya-doṣe' kahana nā yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---by the word; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---is said; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:ā:āśliṣya]]-[[synonyms:d:doṣe]]---by the fault of ambiguity; [[synonyms:k:kahana]]---to say; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---possible.
translation: "Although Your explanation is correct, it should not be used because there is ambiguity in the word 'mukti-pada.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.275
description: "The word 'mukti' refers to five kinds of liberation. Usually its direct meaning conveys the idea of becoming one with the Lord.
text:
> yadyapi 'mukti'-śabdera haya pañca vṛtti
> rūḍhi-vṛttye kahe tabu 'sāyujye' pratīti
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:ś:śabdera]]---of the word; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:p:pañca]] [[synonyms:v:vṛtti]]---five meanings; [[synonyms:r:rūḍhi]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛttye]]---by the chief or direct meaning; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it says; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:s:sāyujye]]---to become one with the Supreme; [[synonyms:p:pratīti]]---the conception.
translation: "The word 'mukti' refers to five kinds of liberation. Usually its direct meaning conveys the idea of becoming one with the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.276
description: "The very sound of the word 'mukti' immediately induces hate and fear, but when we say the word 'bhakti,' we naturally feel transcendental bliss within the mind."
text:
> mukti-śabda kahite mane haya ghṛṇā-trāsa
> bhakti-śabda kahite mane haya ta' ullāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukti]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---the word //mukti//; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---by pronouncing; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:g:ghṛṇā]]---hatred; [[synonyms:t:trāsa]]---and fear; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---the word //bhakti//; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---indeed; [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---transcendental joy.
translation: "The very sound of the word 'mukti' immediately induces hate and fear, but when we say the word 'bhakti,' we naturally feel transcendental bliss within the mind."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.277
description: Upon hearing this explanation, the Lord began to laugh and, with great pleasure, immediately embraced Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya very firmly.
text:
> śuniyā hāsena prabhu ānandita-mane
> bhaṭṭācārya kaila prabhu dṛḍha āliṅgane
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing this explanation; [[synonyms:h:hāsena]]---laughs; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]-[[synonyms:m:mane]]---with great pleasure in His mind; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---unto Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]]---firm; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgane]]---embracing.
translation: Upon hearing this explanation, the Lord began to laugh and, with great pleasure, immediately embraced Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya very firmly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.278
description: Indeed, that very person who was accustomed to reading and teaching Māyāvāda philosophy was now even hating the word "mukti." This was possible only by the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> yei bhaṭṭācārya pade paḍāya māyāvāde
> tāṅra aiche vākya sphure caitanya-prasāde
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yei]]---that; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---reads; [[synonyms:p:paḍāya]]---teaches; [[synonyms:m:māyāvāde]]---the philosophy of Māyāvāda impersonalism; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:v:vākya]]---explanation; [[synonyms:s:sphure]]---manifested; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāde]]---by the mercy of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Indeed, that very person who was accustomed to reading and teaching Māyāvāda philosophy was now even hating the word "mukti." This was possible only by the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.279

text:

> tāvat sparśa-maṇi keha cinite nā pāre

translation: As long as it does not turn iron into gold by its touch, no one can recognize an unknown stone to be a touchstone.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.28

text:
> cala, sabe yāi sārvabhaumera bhavana

translation: "First let us all go to the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and see Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Later we shall come to see Lord Jagannātha."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.280
description: Upon seeing transcendental Vaiṣṇavism in Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, everyone could understand that Lord Caitanya was none other than Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja.
text:
> bhaṭṭācāryera vaiṣṇavatā dekhi' sarva-jana
> prabhuke jānila---'sākṣāt vrajendra-nandana'

translation: Upon seeing transcendental Vaiṣṇavism in Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, everyone could understand that Lord Caitanya was none other than Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.281
description: After this incident, all the inhabitants of Jagannātha Purī, headed by Kāśī Miśra, came to take shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord.
text:
> kāśī-miśra-ādi yata nīlācala-vāsī
> śaraṇa la-ila sabe prabhu-pade āsi'

translation: After this incident, all the inhabitants of Jagannātha Purī, headed by Kāśī Miśra, came to take shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.282

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.283
description: I shall also describe in full detail how Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya perfectly rendered service to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by offering Him alms.

translation: I shall also describe in full detail how Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya perfectly rendered service to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by offering Him alms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.284-285
description: If one hears with faith and love these pastimes concerning Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's meeting with Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, he very soon is freed from the net of speculation and fruitive activity and attains the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's lotus feet.
text:
> ei mahāprabhura līlā---sārvabhauma-milana
> ihā yei śraddhā kari' karaye śravaṇa
>
> jñāna-karma-pāśa haite haya vimocana
> acire milaye tāṅre caitanya-caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastime; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]-[[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting with Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]]---faith; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---having; [[synonyms:k:karaye]]---does; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]---hearing; [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]-[[synonyms:k:karma]]---of speculation and fruitive activities; [[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---the net; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:v:vimocana]]---liberation; [[synonyms:a:acire]]---very soon; [[synonyms:m:milaye]]---meets; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---such a devotee; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya.
translation: If one hears with faith and love these pastimes concerning Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's meeting with Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, he very soon is freed from the net of speculation and fruitive activity and attains the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.286
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.

> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa

translation:
Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Sixth Chapter, describing the liberation of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.29
description: Hearing this and feeling very pleased, Gopīnātha Ācārya immediately took all the devotees with him and approached the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.

translation: Hearing this and feeling very pleased, Gopīnātha Ācārya immediately took all the devotees with him and approached the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.3
description: In ecstasy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went from Āṭhāranālā to the temple of Jagannātha. After seeing Lord Jagannātha, He became very restless due to love of Godhead.
text:
> āveśe calilā prabhu jagannātha-mandire
> jagannātha dekhi' preme ha-ilā asthire
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:m:mandire]]---to the temple of Jagannātha; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the Jagannātha Deity; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:a:asthire]]---restless.
translation: In ecstasy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went from Āṭhāranālā to the temple of Jagannātha. After seeing Lord Jagannātha, He became very restless due to love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.30
description: Arriving at the home of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, everyone saw the Lord lying unconscious. Seeing Him in this condition, Gopīnātha Ācārya became very unhappy, but at the same time he was happy just to see the Lord.
text:
> sārvabhauma-sthāne giyā prabhuke dekhila
> prabhu dekhi' ācāryera duḥkha-harṣa haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the place of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---going there; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---all of them saw; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the Lord; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]]---of Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---happiness; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was.
translation: Arriving at the home of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, everyone saw the Lord lying unconscious. Seeing Him in this condition, Gopīnātha Ācārya became very unhappy, but at the same time he was happy just to see the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.31
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya permitted all the devotees to enter his house, and upon seeing Nityānanda Prabhu, the Bhaṭṭācārya offered Him obeisances.
text:
> sārvabhaume jānāñā sabā nila abhyantare
> nityānanda-gosāñire teṅho kaila namaskāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhaume]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:j:jānāñā]]---informing and taking permission; [[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:n:nila]]---took; [[synonyms:a:abhyantare]]---within the house; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñire]]---unto Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---offered; [[synonyms:n:namaskāre]]---obeisances.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya permitted all the devotees to enter his house, and upon seeing Nityānanda Prabhu, the Bhaṭṭācārya offered Him obeisances.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.32
description: Sārvabhauma met with all the devotees and offered them a proper welcome. They were all pleased to see Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> sabā sahita yathā-yogya karila milana
> prabhu dekhi' sabāra haila haraṣita mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabā]] [[synonyms:s:sahita]]---with all of them; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]-[[synonyms:y:yogya]]---as it was befitting; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:h:haraṣita]]---pleased; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds.
translation: Sārvabhauma met with all the devotees and offered them a proper welcome. They were all pleased to see Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.33
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya then sent them all back to see Lord Jagannātha, and he asked his own son Candaneśvara to accompany them as a guide.
text:
> sārvabhauma pāṭhāila sabā darśana karite
> 'candaneśvara' nija-putra dila sabāra sāthe
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāila]]---sent them; [[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all; [[synonyms:d:darśana]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to see Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:c:candana]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---of the name Candaneśvara; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:p:putra]]---his son; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]] [[synonyms:s:sāthe]]---with all of them.
translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya then sent them all back to see Lord Jagannātha, and he asked his own son Candaneśvara to accompany them as a guide.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.34
description: Everyone was then very pleased to see the Deity of Lord Jagannātha. Lord Nityānanda in particular was overwhelmed with ecstasy.
text:
> jagannātha dekhi' sabāra ha-ila ānanda
> bhāvete āviṣṭa hailā prabhu nityānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:b:bhāvete]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda.
translation: Everyone was then very pleased to see the Deity of Lord Jagannātha. Lord Nityānanda in particular was overwhelmed with ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.35
description: When Lord Nityānanda Prabhu nearly fainted, all the devotees caught Him and steadied Him. At that time, the priest of Lord Jagannātha brought a garland that had been offered to the Deity and offered it to Nityānanda Prabhu.
text:
> sabe meli' dhari tāṅre susthira karila
> īśvara-sevaka mālā-prasāda āni' dila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:m:meli']]---meeting all together; [[synonyms:d:dhari]]---caught; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:s:sthira]]---steady; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---made; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---the priest of the Deity; [[synonyms:m:mālā]]---garland; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---offering; [[synonyms:ā:āni]]---bringing; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave.
translation: When Lord Nityānanda Prabhu nearly fainted, all the devotees caught Him and steadied Him. At that time, the priest of Lord Jagannātha brought a garland that had been offered to the Deity and offered it to Nityānanda Prabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.36
description: Everyone was pleased to receive this garland worn by Lord Jagannātha. Afterwards they all returned to the place where Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was staying.
text:
> prasāda pāñā sabe hailā ānandita mane
> punarapi āilā sabe mahāprabhura sthāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting this honor of the garland; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]] [[synonyms:m:mane]]---pleased in the mind; [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came back; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the place where Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was staying.
translation: Everyone was pleased to receive this garland worn by Lord Jagannātha. Afterwards they all returned to the place where Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was staying.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.37
description: All of the devotees then began to loudly chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra. Just before noon the Lord regained His consciousness.
text:
> ucca kari' kare sabe nāma-saṅkīrtana
> tṛtīya prahare haila prabhura cetana
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:ucca]]---very loudly; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---began; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra//; [[synonyms:t:tṛtīya]] [[synonyms:p:prahare]]---in the forenoon; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:c:cetana]]---consciousness.
translation: All of the devotees then began to loudly chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra. Just before noon the Lord regained His consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.38
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu got up and very loudly chanted, "Hari! Hari!" Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was very pleased to see the Lord regain consciousness, and he took the dust of the Lord's lotus feet.
text:
> huṅkāra kariyā uṭhe 'hari' 'hari' bali'
> ānande sārvabhauma tāṅra laila pada-dhūli
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:huṅkāra]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---making a loud sound; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---got up; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---chanting Hari, Hari; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in pleasure; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:l:laila]]---took; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:d:dhūli]]---the dust of the feet.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu got up and very loudly chanted, "Hari! Hari!" Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was very pleased to see the Lord regain consciousness, and he took the dust of the Lord's lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.39
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya informed all of them, "Please take your midday baths immediately. Today I shall offer you mahā-prasāda, the remnants of food offered to Lord Jagannātha."
text:
> sārvabhauma kahe,---śīghra karaha madhyāhna
> muñi bhikṣā dimu āji mahā-prasādānna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---//says//; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]]---very soon; [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---do; [[synonyms:m:madhya]]-[[synonyms:a:ahna]]---midday duties; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---alms; [[synonyms:d:dimu]]---shall offer; [[synonyms:ā:āji]]---today; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]]-[[synonyms:a:anna]]---remnants of food offered to Lord Jagannātha.
translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya informed all of them, "Please take your midday baths immediately. Today I shall offer you mahā-prasāda, the remnants of food offered to Lord Jagannātha."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.4
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went swiftly to embrace Lord Jagannātha, but when He entered the temple, He was so overwhelmed with love of Godhead that He fainted on the floor.
text:
> jagannātha āliṅgite calilā dhāñā
> mandire paḍilā preme āviṣṭa hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgite]]---to embrace; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went; [[synonyms:d:dhāñā]]---very swiftly; [[synonyms:m:mandire]]---in the temple; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went swiftly to embrace Lord Jagannātha, but when He entered the temple, He was so overwhelmed with love of Godhead that He fainted on the floor.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.40
description: After bathing in the sea, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His devotees returned very soon. The Lord then washed His feet and sat down on a carpet to take lunch.
text:
> samudra-snāna kari' mahāprabhu śīghra āilā
> caraṇa pākhāli' prabhu āsane vasilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:samudra]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---a bath in the sea; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]]---very soon; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---feet; [[synonyms:p:pākhāli']]---washing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āsane]]---on a seat; [[synonyms:v:vasilā]]---sat.
translation: After bathing in the sea, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His devotees returned very soon. The Lord then washed His feet and sat down on a carpet to take lunch.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.41
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya made arrangements to bring various kinds of mahā-prasāda from the Jagannātha temple. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then accepted lunch with great happiness.
text:
> bahuta prasāda sārvabhauma ānāila
> tabe mahāprabhu sukhe bhojana karila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bahuta]] [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---varieties of food offered to Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:ā:ānāila]]---caused to bring them; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in happiness; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---lunch; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---accepted.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya made arrangements to bring various kinds of mahā-prasāda from the Jagannātha temple. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then accepted lunch with great happiness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.42
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu was offered special rice and first-class vegetables on golden plates. He thus took lunch in the company of His devotees.
text:
> suvarṇa-thālīra anna uttama vyañjana
> bhakta-gaṇa-saṅge prabhu karena bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:suvarṇa]]-[[synonyms:t:thālīra]]---on golden plates; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---rice; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]---first-class; [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---vegetables; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---accepts; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---lunch.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu was offered special rice and first-class vegetables on golden plates. He thus took lunch in the company of His devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.43
description: While Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya personally distributed the prasāda, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested him, "Please give Me only boiled vegetables.
text:
> sārvabhauma pariveśana karena āpane
> prabhu kahe,---more deha lāphrā-vyañjane
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:p:pariveśana]]---distribution; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---please give; [[synonyms:l:lāphrā]]-[[synonyms:v:vyañjane]]---boiled vegetables.
translation: While Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya personally distributed the prasāda, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested him, "Please give Me only boiled vegetables.
purport: //Lāphrā-vyañjana// is a preparation in which many vegetables are boiled together, and then a //cheṅkā// is added, consisting of spices like cumin, black pepper and mustard seed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.44
description: "You can offer the cakes and other preparations made with condensed milk to all the devotees." Hearing this, the Bhaṭṭācārya folded his hands and spoke as follows.
text:
> pīṭhā-pānā deha tumi iṅhā-sabākāre
> tabe bhaṭṭācārya kahe yuḍi' dui kare
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pīṭhā]]-[[synonyms:p:pānā]]---cakes and condensed milk; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---give; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:i:iṅhā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabākāre]]---to all these devotees; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:y:yuḍi']]---folding; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---two hands.
translation: "You can offer the cakes and other preparations made with condensed milk to all the devotees." Hearing this, the Bhaṭṭācārya folded his hands and spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.45
description: "Today, all of you please try to taste the lunch just as Lord Jagannātha accepted it."
text:
> jagannātha kaiche kariyāchena bhojana
> āji saba mahāprasāda kara āsvādana
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:k:kaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchena]]---has accepted; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---lunch; [[synonyms:ā:āji]]---today; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of you; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---the remnants of food offered to the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---do; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasting.
translation: "Today, all of you please try to taste the lunch just as Lord Jagannātha accepted it."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.46
description: After saying this, he made them all eat the various cakes and condensed-milk preparations. After feeding them, he offered them water to wash their hands, feet and mouths.
text:
> eta bali' pīṭhā-pānā saba khāoyāilā
> bhikṣā karāñā ācamana karāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:p:pīṭhā]]-[[synonyms:p:pānā]]---many kinds of cakes and condensed-milk preparations; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:k:khāoyāilā]]---made to eat; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:k:karāñā]]---after offering //prasāda//; [[synonyms:ā:ācamana]] [[synonyms:k:karāilā]]---made them wash their hands, feet and mouths.
translation: After saying this, he made them all eat the various cakes and condensed-milk preparations. After feeding them, he offered them water to wash their hands, feet and mouths.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.47
description: Begging permission from Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His devotees, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then went with Gopīnātha Ācārya to take lunch. After finishing their lunch, they returned to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> ājñā māgi' gelā gopīnātha ācāryake lañā
> prabhura nikaṭa āilā bhojana kariñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:m:māgi']]---taking permission; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]] [[synonyms:ā:ācāryake]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nikaṭa]]---near; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---went; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]] [[synonyms:k:kariñā]]---after taking lunch.
translation: Begging permission from Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His devotees, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then went with Gopīnātha Ācārya to take lunch. After finishing their lunch, they returned to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.48
description: Offering his obeisances to Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Namo nārāyaṇāya" ["I offer my obeisances to Nārāyaṇa"]." In return, Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Kṛṣṇe matir astu" ["Let your attention be on Kṛṣṇa"]."
text:
> 'namo nārāyaṇāya' bali' namaskāra kaila
> 'kṛṣṇe matir astu' bali' gosāñi kahila
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:namaḥ]] [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇāya]]---I offer my respects to Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---offered respects to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:matiḥ]] [[synonyms:a:astu]]---let there be attraction; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---spoke.
translation: Offering his obeisances to Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Namo nārāyaṇāya" ["I offer my obeisances to Nārāyaṇa"]." In return, Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Kṛṣṇe matir astu" ["Let your attention be on Kṛṣṇa"]."
purport: It is the etiquette among //sannyāsīs,// those on the fourth platform of spiritual life, to offer respects by saying //oṁ namo nārāyaṇāya// ("I offer my respectful obeisances unto Nārāyaṇa"). This greeting is used especially by Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs.// According to the //smṛti// scriptures, a //sannyāsī// should not expect anything from anyone, nor should he consider himself identical with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsīs// never think of themselves as being one with the Lord; they always consider themselves eternal servants of Kṛṣṇa, and they want to see everyone in the world become Kṛṣṇa conscious. For this reason, a Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsī// always offers his blessings to everyone, saying //kṛṣṇe matir astu// ("May you become Kṛṣṇa conscious").

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.49
description: Hearing these words, Sārvabhauma understood Lord Caitanya to be a Vaiṣṇava sannyāsī.
text:
> śuni' sārvabhauma mane vicāra karila
> vaiṣṇava-sannyāsī iṅho, vacane jānila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---within the mind; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---considered; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---Vaiṣṇava //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:i:iṅho]]---this person; [[synonyms:v:vacane]]---by words; [[synonyms:j:jānila]]---understood.
translation: Hearing these words, Sārvabhauma understood Lord Caitanya to be a Vaiṣṇava sannyāsī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.5
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell down, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya happened to see Him. When the watchman threatened to beat the Lord, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya immediately forbade him.
text:
> daive sārvabhauma tāṅhāke kare daraśana
> paḍichā mārite teṅho kaila nivāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daive]]---by chance; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāke]]---Him; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:paḍichā]]---the watchman in the temple; [[synonyms:m:mārite]]---to beat; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:n:nivāraṇa]]---forbidding.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell down, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya happened to see Him. When the watchman threatened to beat the Lord, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya immediately forbade him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.50
description: Sārvabhauma then said to Gopīnātha Ācārya, "I want to know Caitanya Mahāprabhu's previous situation."
text:
> gopīnātha ācāryere kahe sārvabhauma
> gosāñira jānite cāhi kāhāṅ pūrvāśrama
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]] [[synonyms:ā:ācāryere]]---to Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jānite]]---to know; [[synonyms:c:cāhi]]---I want; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---what; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśrama]]---previous situation.
translation: Sārvabhauma then said to Gopīnātha Ācārya, "I want to know Caitanya Mahāprabhu's previous situation."
purport: The word //pūrvāśrama// refers to one's previous situation in life. Sometimes a person will accept the renounced order from householder life, and sometimes even from student (//brahmacārī//) life. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya wanted to know of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's previous situation as a householder.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.51
description: Gopīnātha Ācārya replied, "There was a man named Jagannātha, who was a resident of Navadvīpa, and whose surname was Miśra Purandara.
text:
> gopīnāthācārya kahe,---navadvīpe ghara
> 'jagannātha'---nāma, padavī---'miśra purandara'
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya replied; [[synonyms:n:navadvīpe]]---in Navadvīpa; [[synonyms:g:ghara]]---residence; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---of the name Jagannātha; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:p:padavī]]---the surname; [[synonyms:m:miśra]] [[synonyms:p:purandara]]---Miśra Purandara.
translation: Gopīnātha Ācārya replied, "There was a man named Jagannātha, who was a resident of Navadvīpa, and whose surname was Miśra Purandara.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.52
description: "Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the son of that Jagannātha Miśra, and His former name was Viśvambhara Miśra. He also happens to be the grandson of Nīlāmbara Cakravartī."
text:
> 'viśvambhara'---nāma iṅhāra, tāṅra iṅho putra
> nīlāmbara cakravartīra hayena dauhitra
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viśvambhara]]---of the name Viśvambhara; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]]---His; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Jagannātha Miśra; [[synonyms:i:iṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:p:putra]]---son; [[synonyms:n:nīlāmbara]] [[synonyms:c:cakravartīra]]---of Nīlāmbara Cakravartī; [[synonyms:h:hayena]]---is; [[synonyms:d:dauhitra]]---grandson (daughter's son).
translation: "Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the son of that Jagannātha Miśra, and His former name was Viśvambhara Miśra. He also happens to be the grandson of Nīlāmbara Cakravartī."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.53
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Nīlāmbara Cakravartī was a classmate of my father, Maheśvara Viśārada. I knew him as such.
text:
> sārvabhauma kahe,---nīlāmbara cakravartī
> viśāradera samādhyāyī,---ei tāṅra khyāti
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sārvabhauma said; [[synonyms:n:nīlāmbara]] [[synonyms:c:cakravartī]]---the gentleman named Nīlāmbara Cakravartī; [[synonyms:v:viśāradera]]---of Maheśvara Viśārada (Sārvabhauma's father); [[synonyms:s:samādhyāyī]]---class friend; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of him; [[synonyms:k:khyāti]]---acquaintance.
translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Nīlāmbara Cakravartī was a classmate of my father, Maheśvara Viśārada. I knew him as such.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.54
description: "Jagannātha Miśra Purandara was respected by my father. Thus because of their relationship with my father, I respect both Jagannātha Miśra and Nīlāmbara Cakravartī."
text:
> 'miśra purandara' tāṅra mānya, hena jāni
> pitāra sambandhe doṅhāke pūjya kari' māni
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:miśra]] [[synonyms:p:purandara]]---Jagannātha Miśra Purandara; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:m:mānya]]---respectable; [[synonyms:h:hena]]---thus; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I know; [[synonyms:p:pitāra]] [[synonyms:s:sambandhe]]---in relationship to my father; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāke]]---both of them (Nīlāmbara Cakravartī and Jagannātha Miśra); [[synonyms:p:pūjya]]---respectable; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---thinking; [[synonyms:m:māni]]---I accept.
translation: "Jagannātha Miśra Purandara was respected by my father. Thus because of their relationship with my father, I respect both Jagannātha Miśra and Nīlāmbara Cakravartī."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.55
description: Hearing that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu belonged to the Nadīyā district, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya became very pleased and addressed the Lord as follows.
text:
> nadīyā-sambandhe sārvabhauma hṛṣṭa hailā
> prīta hañā gosāñire kahite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nadīyā]]-[[synonyms:s:sambandhe]]---in connection with Nadīyā; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:h:hṛṣṭa]]---pleased; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:p:prīta]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---thus being pleased; [[synonyms:g:gosāñire]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to speak.
translation: Hearing that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu belonged to the Nadīyā district, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya became very pleased and addressed the Lord as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.56
description: "You are naturally respectable. Besides, You are a sannyāsī; thus I wish to become Your personal servant."
text:
> 'sahajei pūjya tumi, āre ta' sannyāsa
> ataeva haṅ tomāra āmi nija-dāsa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sahajei]]---naturally; [[synonyms:p:pūjya]]---respectable; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:ā:āre]]---over and above this; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:h:haṅ]]---am; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---personal servant.
translation: "You are naturally respectable. Besides, You are a sannyāsī; thus I wish to become Your personal servant."
purport: A //sannyāsī// is always to be worshiped and offered all kinds of respect by the //gṛhasthas// (householders). Although Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was older than Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Sārvabhauma respected Him as a //sannyāsī// and as one who had attained the topmost platform of spiritual ecstasy. Thus the Bhaṭṭācārya certainly accepted Him as his master.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.57
description: As soon as Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard this from the Bhaṭṭācārya, He immediately remembered Lord Viṣṇu and began to speak humbly to him as follows.
text:
> śuni' mahāprabhu kaila śrī-viṣṇu smaraṇa
> bhaṭṭācārye kahe kichu vinaya vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]] [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---remembering Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārye]]---to Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---speaks; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:v:vinaya]] [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---very humble statements.
translation: As soon as Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard this from the Bhaṭṭācārya, He immediately remembered Lord Viṣṇu and began to speak humbly to him as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.58
description: "Because you are a teacher of Vedānta philosophy, you are the master of all the people in the world and their well-wisher as well. You are also the benefactor of all kinds of sannyāsīs.
text:
> "tumi jagad-guru---sarvaloka-hita-kartā
> vedānta paḍāo, sannyāsīra upakartā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:g:guru]]---you are the master of all people; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]---of all people; [[synonyms:h:hita]]-[[synonyms:k:kartā]]---the well-wisher; [[synonyms:v:vedānta]] [[synonyms:p:paḍāo]]---you teach Vedānta philosophy; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]]---of the mendicants in the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:u:upakartā]]---the benefactor.
translation: "Because you are a teacher of Vedānta philosophy, you are the master of all the people in the world and their well-wisher as well. You are also the benefactor of all kinds of sannyāsīs.
purport: Because the Māyāvādī //sannyāsīs// teach Vedānta philosophy to their students or disciples, they are customarily called //jagad-guru.// This indicates that they are the benefactors of all people. Although Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was not a //sannyāsī// but a householder, he used to invite all the //sannyāsīs// to his home and offer them //prasāda.// Thus he was accepted as the best well-wisher and friend of all the //sannyāsīs.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.59
description: "I am a young sannyāsī, and I actually have no knowledge of what is good and what is bad. Therefore I am taking shelter of you and accepting you as My spiritual master.
text:
> āmi bālaka-sannyāsī---bhānda-manda nāhi jāni
> tomāra āśraya niluṅ, guru kari' māni
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bālaka]]-[[synonyms:s:sannyāsī]]---a young //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:b:bhānda]]-[[synonyms:m:manda]]---good and bad; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---know; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:ā:āśraya]]---shelter; [[synonyms:n:niluṅ]]---have taken; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---spiritual master; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking as; [[synonyms:m:māni]]---I accept.
translation: "I am a young sannyāsī, and I actually have no knowledge of what is good and what is bad. Therefore I am taking shelter of you and accepting you as My spiritual master.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.6
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was very much surprised to see the personal beauty of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu as well as the transcendental transformations wrought on His body due to love of Godhead.
text:
> prabhura saundarya āra premera vikāra
> dekhi' sārvabhauma hailā vismita apāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:saundarya]]---the beauty; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:premera]] [[synonyms:v:vikāra]]---ecstatic transformations; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vismita]]---surprised; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---very much.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was very much surprised to see the personal beauty of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu as well as the transcendental transformations wrought on His body due to love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.60
description: "I have come here only to associate with you, and I am now taking shelter of you. Will you kindly maintain Me in all respects?
text:
> tomāra saṅga lāgi' mora ihāṅ āgamana
> sarva-prakāre karibe āmāya pālana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---association; [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for the sake of; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---arrival; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāre]]---in all respects; [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---you will do; [[synonyms:ā:āmāya]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:p:pālana]]---maintaining.
translation: "I have come here only to associate with you, and I am now taking shelter of you. Will you kindly maintain Me in all respects?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.61
description: "The incident that happened today was a great obstacle for Me, but you have kindly relieved Me of it."
text:
> āji ye haila āmāra baḍa-i vipatti
> tāhā haite kaile tumi āmāra avyāhati"
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āji]]---today; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---that which; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---happened; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---very great; [[synonyms:v:vipatti]]---obstacle; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that danger; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---did; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:a:avyāhati]]---relief.
translation: "The incident that happened today was a great obstacle for Me, but you have kindly relieved Me of it."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.62
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "Do not go alone to see the Deity at the Jagannātha temple. It is better that You go with me or my men."
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya kahe,---ekale tumi nā yāiha darśane
> āmāra saṅge yābe, kimvā āmāra loka-sane
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Bhaṭṭācārya said; [[synonyms:e:ekale]]---alone; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāiha]]---go; [[synonyms:d:darśane]]---to see the Deity; [[synonyms:ā:āmārasaṅge]]---with me; [[synonyms:y:yābe]]---You should go; [[synonyms:k:kimvā]]---or; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with my men.
translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya replied, "Do not go alone to see the Deity at the Jagannātha temple. It is better that You go with me or my men."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.63
description: The Lord said, "I shall never enter the temple but shall always view the Lord from the side of the Garuḍa-stambha."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---'mandira bhitare nā yāiba
> garuḍera pāśe rahi' darśana kariba'
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya replied; [[synonyms:m:mandira]]---the temple; [[synonyms:b:bhitare]]---inside; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---never; [[synonyms:y:yāiba]]---I shall go; [[synonyms:g:garuḍera]]---of the column known as the Garuḍa-stambha; [[synonyms:p:pāśe]]---by the side; [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---staying; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kariba]]---I shall do.
translation: The Lord said, "I shall never enter the temple but shall always view the Lord from the side of the Garuḍa-stambha."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.64
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then told Gopīnātha Ācārya, "Take Gosvāmījī and show Him Lord Jagannātha.
text:
> gopīnāthācāryake kahe sārvabhauma
> 'tumi gosāñire lañā karāiha daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācāryake]]---to Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:g:gosāñire]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:karāiha]]---make Him do; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing of Lord Jagannātha.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya then told Gopīnātha Ācārya, "Take Gosvāmījī and show Him Lord Jagannātha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.65
description: "Also, the apartment belonging to my maternal aunt is in a very solitary place. Make all arrangements for Him to stay there."
text:
> āmāra mātṛ-svasā-gṛha---nirjana sthāna
> tāhāṅ vāsā deha, kara sarva samādhāna'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---my; [[synonyms:m:mātṛ]]-[[synonyms:s:svasā]]---of the aunt; [[synonyms:g:gṛha]]---the home; [[synonyms:n:nirjana]] [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---very solitary place; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]]---an apartment; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---give; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---make; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:s:samādhāna]]---arrangements.
translation: "Also, the apartment belonging to my maternal aunt is in a very solitary place. Make all arrangements for Him to stay there."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.66
description: Thus Gopīnātha Ācārya took Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu to the residential quarters and showed Him where to find water, tubs and waterpots. Indeed, he arranged everything.
text:
> gopīnātha prabhu lañā tāhāṅ vāsā dila
> jala, jala-pātrādika sarva sāmādhāna kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]]---apartment; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---water; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādika]]---waterpots and other vessels; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:s:sāmādhāna]]---arrangements; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made.
translation: Thus Gopīnātha Ācārya took Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu to the residential quarters and showed Him where to find water, tubs and waterpots. Indeed, he arranged everything.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.67
description: The next day Gopīnātha Ācārya took Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu to see the early rising of Lord Jagannātha.
text:
> āra dina gopīnātha prabhu sthāne giyā
> śayyotthāna daraśana karāila lañā

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.69
description: "The sannyāsī is very meek and humble by nature, and His person is very beautiful to see. Consequently my affection for Him increases.
text:
> 'prakṛti-vinīta, sannyāsī dekhite sundara
> āmāra bahu-prīti bāḍe iṅhāra upara

translation: "The sannyāsī is very meek and humble by nature, and His person is very beautiful to see. Consequently my affection for Him increases.
purport: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya considered Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu a very humble and meek person because although Caitanya Mahāprabhu was a //sannyāsī,// He still retained His //brahmacārī// name. The Lord took //sannyāsa// from Keśava Bhāratī in the Bhāratī //sampradāya,// in which the //brahmacārīs// (the assistants of the //sannyāsīs//) are named "Caitanya." Even after accepting //sannyāsa,// Caitanya Mahāprabhu retained the name "Caitanya," meaning a humble servant of a //sannyāsī.// Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya appreciated this very much.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.7
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained unconscious for a long time. Meanwhile, the time for offering prasāda to Lord Jagannātha came, and the Bhaṭṭācārya tried to think of a remedy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.71

> gopīnātha kahe,---nāma śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya
> guru iṅhāra keśava-bhāratī mahā-dhanya

translation: Gopīnātha Ācārya replied, "The Lord's name is Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, and His sannyāsa preceptor is the greatly fortunate Keśava Bhāratī."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.72
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, " 'Śrī Kṛṣṇa' is a very good name, but He belongs to the Bhāratī community. Therefore He is a second-class sannyāsī."
text:
> sārvabhauma kahe,---'iṅhāra nāma sarvottama
> bhāratī-sampradāya iṅho---hayena madhyama'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya replied; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]]---His; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---name; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:u:uttama]]---first-class; [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]]-[[synonyms:s:sampradāya]]---the community of the Bhāratī //sannyāsīs//; [[synonyms:i:iṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:h:hayena]]---becomes; [[synonyms:m:madhyama]]---middle-class.
translation: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said, " 'Śrī Kṛṣṇa' is a very good name, but He belongs to the Bhāratī community. Therefore He is a second-class sannyāsī."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.73
description: Gopīnātha Ācārya replied, "Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu does not rely on any external formality. There is no need for Him to accept the sannyāsa order from a superior sampradāya."
text:
> gopīnātha kahe,---iṅhāra nāhi bāhyāpekṣā
> ataeva baḍa sampradāyera nāhika apekṣā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya replied; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]-[[synonyms:a:apekṣā]]---dependence on any external formality; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---big; [[synonyms:s:sampradāyera]]---of a community; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:a:apekṣā]]---necessity.
translation: Gopīnātha Ācārya replied, "Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu does not rely on any external formality. There is no need for Him to accept the sannyāsa order from a superior sampradāya."
purport:
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted //sannyāsa// from the Bhāratī //sampradāya// (community), which belongs to the disciplic succession of Śaṅkarācārya. Śaṅkarācārya introduced names for his //sannyāsa// disciples, and these are ten in number. Out of these, the surnames Tīrtha, Āśrama and Sarasvatī are considered topmost. In the monastery at Śṛṅgerī, the surname Sarasvatī is considered first class, Bhāratī second class and Purī third class. A //sannyāsī// who has very nicely understood the slogan //tat tvam asi// and who takes his bath at the confluence of the rivers Ganges, Yamunā and Sarasvatī is called a Tīrtha. A person who is very eager to accept //sannyāsa,// who is detached from worldly activities, who has no desire for any kind of material facilities, and who is thus saved from repeated birth and death is known as Āśrama. When a //sannyāsī// lives in a beautiful, solitary place in the forest and is freed from all material desires, he is called Vana. A //sannyāsī// who always lives in the forest and renounces all connection with the world in order to be elevated to the heavenly planets, where he can live in the Nandana-kānana, is called Araṇya. One who prefers living in the mountains engaging in the study of the //Bhagavad-gītā// and whose intelligence is fixed is called Giri. One who prefers living in great mountains, even among ferocious animals, to attain the summit of philosophical speculation (understanding that the essence of this material world is useless) is called Parvata. A //sannyāsī// who has dipped into the ocean of the Absolute Truth and collected some valuable stones of knowledge from that ocean, who never falls from the regulative principles of a //sannyāsī,// is called Sāgara. One who has learned the classical art of music, who engages in its culture, and who has become expert and completely aloof from material attachment is called Sarasvatī. Sarasvatī is the goddess of music and learning, and in one hand she holds a musical instrument called a //vīṇā. A sannyāsī// who is always engaged in music for spiritual elevation is called Sarasvatī. One who has become completely educated and is freed from all kinds of ignorance and who is never unhappy, even in a distressed condition, is called Bhāratī. One who has become very expert in absolute knowledge, who is situated in the Absolute Truth, and who always discusses the Absolute Truth is called Purī.

All these //sannyāsīs// are assisted by //brahmacārīs,// who are described as follows: One who knows his real identity and is fixed in his particular occupational duty, who is always happy in spiritual understanding, is called Svarūpa-brahmacārī. One who completely knows the Brahman effulgence and is always engaged in the practice of //yoga// is called Prakāśa-brahmacārī. One who has acquired absolute knowledge and who always meditates on the Absolute Truth, knowledge, the unlimited and the Brahman effulgence, thus keeping himself in transcendental bliss, is called Ānanda-brahmacārī. One who is able to distinguish between matter and spirit, who is never disturbed by material transformations, and who meditates on the unlimited, inexhaustible, auspicious Brahman effulgence is a first-class, learned //brahmacārī// and is named Caitanya.

When Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was talking with Gopīnātha Ācārya about Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's //sannyāsa// community, he appreciated the first name, "Śrī Kṛṣṇa," but did not like the surname, "Caitanya," which is the name for a //brahmacārī// belonging to the Bhāratī community. He therefore suggested that the Lord be elevated to the Sarasvatī community. However, Gopīnātha Ācārya pointed out that the Lord does not depend on any external formality. Gopīnātha Ācārya was firmly convinced that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was Kṛṣṇa Himself and therefore independent of any external ritual or formality. If one wants to engage in pure devotional service, he does not require titular superiority as a Bhāratī or a Sarasvatī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 6.74
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya inquired, "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is in His full-fledged youthful life. How can He keep the principles of sannyāsa?
text:
> bhaṭṭācārya kahe,---'iṅhāra prauḍha yauvana
> kemate sannyāsa-dharma ha-ibe rakṣaṇa
