title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.135
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu left, the brāhmaṇa Kūrma followed Him a great distance, but eventually Lord Caitanya took care to send him back home.
text:
> prabhura anuvraji' kūrma bahu dūra āilā
> prabhu tāṅre yatna kari' ghare pāṭhāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:anuvraji']]---following behind; [[synonyms:k:kūrma]]---the brāhmaṇa named Kūrma; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---much; [[synonyms:d:dūra]]---distance; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:y:yatna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking much care; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to his home; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāilā]]---sent.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu left, the brāhmaṇa Kūrma followed Him a great distance, but eventually Lord Caitanya took care to send him back home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.136
description: There was also a brāhmaṇa named Vāsudeva, who was a great person but was suffering from leprosy. Indeed, his body was filled with living worms.
text:
> 'vāsudeva'-nāma eka dvija mahāśaya
> sarvāṅge galita kuṣṭha, tāte kīḍā-maya
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---of the name Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:d:dvija]]---one //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:m:mahāśaya]]---a great person; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---all over his body; [[synonyms:g:galita]]---acute; [[synonyms:k:kuṣṭha]]---leprosy; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in that; [[synonyms:k:kīḍā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---full of living worms.
translation: There was also a brāhmaṇa named Vāsudeva, who was a great person but was suffering from leprosy. Indeed, his body was filled with living worms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.137
description: Although suffering from leprosy, the brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva was enlightened. As soon as one worm fell from his body, he would pick it up and place it back again in the same location.
text:
> aṅga haite yei kīḍā khasiyā paḍaya
> uṭhāñā sei kīḍā rākhe sei ṭhāña
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aṅga]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from his body; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---which; [[synonyms:k:kīḍā]]---a worm; [[synonyms:k:khasiyā]]---drops; [[synonyms:p:paḍaya]]---falling off; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāñā]]---picking up; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kīḍā]]---worm; [[synonyms:r:rākhe]]---places; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāña]]---in the same place.
translation: Although suffering from leprosy, the brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva was enlightened. As soon as one worm fell from his body, he would pick it up and place it back again in the same location.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.138
description: Then one night Vāsudeva heard of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's arrival, and in the morning he came to see the Lord at the house of Kūrma.
text:
> rātrite śunilā teṅho gosāñira āgamana
> dekhibāre āilā prabhāte kūrmera bhavana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rātrite]]---at night; [[synonyms:ś:śunilā]]---heard; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---the arrival; [[synonyms:d:dekhibāre]]---to see Him; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---he came; [[synonyms:p:prabhāte]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:k:kūrmera]]---of the //brāhmaṇa// named Kūrma; [[synonyms:b:bhavana]]---to the house.
translation: Then one night Vāsudeva heard of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's arrival, and in the morning he came to see the Lord at the house of Kūrma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.139
description: When the leper Vāsudeva came to Kūrma's house to see Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he was informed that the Lord had already left. The leper then fell to the ground unconscious.
text:
> prabhura gamana kūrma-mukhete śuniñā
> bhūmite paḍilā duḥkhe mūrcchita hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---the going; [[synonyms:k:kūrma]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhete]]---from the mouth of the //brāhmaṇa// Kūrma; [[synonyms:ś:śuniñā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:d:duḥkhe]]---in great distress; [[synonyms:m:mūrcchita]]---unconsciousness; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming.
translation: When the leper Vāsudeva came to Kūrma's house to see Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he was informed that the Lord had already left. The leper then fell to the ground unconscious.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.14
description: Upon hearing this message from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all the devotees became very unhappy and remained silent with sullen faces.
text:
> śuniyā sabāra mane haila mahā-duḥkha
> niḥśabda ha-ilā, sabāra śukāila mukha
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing this; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all the devotees; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the minds; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---great unhappiness; [[synonyms:n:niḥśabda]]---silent; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:ś:śukāila]]---dried up; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---the faces.
translation: Upon hearing this message from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all the devotees became very unhappy and remained silent with sullen faces.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.140
description: When Vāsudeva, the leper brāhmaṇa, was lamenting due to not being able to see Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord immediately returned to that spot and embraced him.
text:
> aneka prakāra vilāpa karite lāgilā
> sei-kṣaṇe āsi' prabhu tāṅre āliṅgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aneka]] [[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---various kinds; [[synonyms:v:vilāpa]]---lamentation; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to do; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began; [[synonyms:s:sei]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---immediately; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming back; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgilā]]---embraced.
translation: When Vāsudeva, the leper brāhmaṇa, was lamenting due to not being able to see Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord immediately returned to that spot and embraced him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.141
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu touched him, both the leprosy and his distress went to a distant place. Indeed, Vāsudeva's body became very beautiful, to his great happiness.
text:
> prabhu-sparśe duḥkha-saṅge kuṣṭha dūre gela
> ānanda sahite aṅga sundara ha-ila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sparśe]]---by the touch of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---along with his unhappiness; [[synonyms:k:kuṣṭha]]---the infection of leprosy; [[synonyms:d:dūre]]---to a distant place; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]] [[synonyms:s:sahite]]---with great pleasure; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---whole body; [[synonyms:s:sundara]]---beautiful; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu touched him, both the leprosy and his distress went to a distant place. Indeed, Vāsudeva's body became very beautiful, to his great happiness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.142
description: The brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva was astonished to behold the wonderful mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and he began to recite a verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, touching the Lord's lotus feet.
text:
> prabhura kṛpā dekhi' tāṅra vismaya haila mana
> śloka paḍi' pāye dhari, karaye stavana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---the mercy; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of the //brāhmaṇa// Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:v:vismaya]] [[synonyms:h:haila]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---there was astonishment in his mind; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting a verse; [[synonyms:p:pāye]] [[synonyms:d:dhari]]---touching His lotus feet; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:s:stavana]]---offers prayers.
translation: The brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva was astonished to behold the wonderful mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and he began to recite a verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, touching the Lord's lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.143
description: He said, " 'Who am I? A sinful, poor friend of a brāhmaṇa. And who is Kṛṣṇa? The Supreme Personality of Godhead, full in six opulences. Nonetheless, He has embraced me with His two arms.' "
text:
> kvāhaṁ daridraḥ pāpīyān
> kva kṛṣṇaḥ śrī-niketanaḥ
> brahma-bandhur iti smāhaṁ
> bāhubhyāṁ parirambhitaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kva]]---who; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:d:daridraḥ]]---poor; [[synonyms:p:pāpīyān]]---sinful; [[synonyms:k:kva]]---who; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:n:niketanaḥ]]---the transcendental form of all opulence; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:b:bandhuḥ]]---the friend of a //brāhmaṇa,// not fit even to be called a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:s:sma]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:b:bāhubhyām]]---by the arms; [[synonyms:p:parirambhitaḥ]]---embraced.
translation: He said, " 'Who am I? A sinful, poor friend of a brāhmaṇa. And who is Kṛṣṇa? The Supreme Personality of Godhead, full in six opulences. Nonetheless, He has embraced me with His two arms.' "
purport: This verse was spoken by Sudāmā Brāhmaṇa in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.81.16), in connection with his meeting Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.144-145
description: The brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva continued, "O my merciful Lord, such mercy is not possible for ordinary living entities. Such mercy can be found only in You. Upon seeing me, even a sinful person goes away due to my bad bodily odor. Yet You have touched me. Such is the independent behavior of the Supreme Personality of Godhead."
text:
> bahu stuti kari' kahe,---śuna, dayā-maya
> jīve ei guṇa nāhi, tomāte ei haya
>
> more dekhi' mora gandhe palāya pāmara
> hena-more sparśa' tumi,---svatantra īśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---many; [[synonyms:s:stuti]]---prayers; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---presenting; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---kindly hear; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---O greatly merciful Lord; [[synonyms:j:jīve]]---in the living entity; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---quality; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:t:tomāte]]---in You; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:m:more]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---by seeing me; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:g:gandhe]]---from smelling my body; [[synonyms:p:palāya]]---runs away; [[synonyms:p:pāmara]]---even a sinful man; [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:m:more]]---such a person as me; [[synonyms:s:sparśa']]---touch; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]]---fully independent; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: The brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva continued, "O my merciful Lord, such mercy is not possible for ordinary living entities. Such mercy can be found only in You. Upon seeing me, even a sinful person goes away due to my bad bodily odor. Yet You have touched me. Such is the independent behavior of the Supreme Personality of Godhead."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.146
description: Being meek and humble, the brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva worried that he would become proud after being cured by the grace of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> kintu āchilāṅ bhāla adhama hañā
> ebe ahaṅkāra mora janmibe āsiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kintu]]---but; [[synonyms:ā:āchilāṅ]]---I was; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]---all right; [[synonyms:a:adhama]]---the lowest of mankind; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:a:ahaṅkāra]]---pride; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:j:janmibe]]---will appear; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming.
translation: Being meek and humble, the brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva worried that he would become proud after being cured by the grace of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.147
description: To protect the brāhmaṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu advised him to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra incessantly. By doing so, he would never become unnecessarily proud.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---"kabhu tomāra nā habe abhimāna
> nirantara kaha tumi 'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa' nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:a:abhimāna]]---pride; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---incessantly; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---chant; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: To protect the brāhmaṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu advised him to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra incessantly. By doing so, he would never become unnecessarily proud.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.148
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also advised Vāsudeva to preach about Kṛṣṇa and thus liberate living entities. As a result, Kṛṣṇa would very soon accept him as His devotee.
text:
> kṛṣṇa upadeśi' kara jīvera nistāra
> acirāte kṛṣṇa tomā karibena aṅgīkāra"
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:u:upadeśi']]---instructing about Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---just do; [[synonyms:j:jīvera]]---of all living entities; [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---the liberation; [[synonyms:a:acirāte]]---very soon; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tomā]]---you; [[synonyms:k:karibena]]---will make; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---acceptance.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also advised Vāsudeva to preach about Kṛṣṇa and thus liberate living entities. As a result, Kṛṣṇa would very soon accept him as His devotee.
purport: Although Vāsudeva Vipra was a leper and had suffered greatly, still Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu cured him. The only return the Lord wanted was that Vāsudeva preach the instructions of Kṛṣṇa and liberate all human beings. That is the process of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. Each and every member of this Society was rescued from a very abominable condition, but now they are engaged in preaching the cult of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. They are not only cured of the disease called materialism but are also living a very happy life. Everyone accepts them as great devotees of Kṛṣṇa, and their qualities are manifest in their very faces. If one wants to be recognized as a devotee by Kṛṣṇa, he should take to preaching work, following the advice of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Then one will undoubtedly attain the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself, without delay.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.149
description: After instructing the brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva in that way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu disappeared from that place. Then the two brāhmaṇas, Kūrma and Vāsudeva, embraced each other and began to cry, remembering the transcendental qualities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> eteka kahiyā prabhu kaila antardhāne
> dui vipra galāgali kānde prabhura guṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eteka]]---so much; [[synonyms:k:kahiyā]]---speaking; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:a:antardhāne]]---disappearance; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the two //brāhmaṇas,// Kūrma and Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:g:galāgali]]---embracing one another; [[synonyms:k:kānde]]---cry; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---due to the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: After instructing the brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva in that way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu disappeared from that place. Then the two brāhmaṇas, Kūrma and Vāsudeva, embraced each other and began to cry, remembering the transcendental qualities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.15
description: Nityānanda Prabhu then said, "How is it possible for You to go alone? Who can tolerate this?
text:
> nityānanda-prabhu kahe,---"aiche kaiche haya
> ekākī yāibe tumi, ke ihā sahaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu replied; [[synonyms:a:aiche]] [[synonyms:k:kaiche]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---how is this possible; [[synonyms:e:ekākī]]---alone; [[synonyms:y:yāibe]]---shall go; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:k:ke]]---who; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:s:sahaya]]---can tolerate.
translation: Nityānanda Prabhu then said, "How is it possible for You to go alone? Who can tolerate this?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.150
description: Thus I have described how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu reclaimed the leper Vāsudeva and so received the name Vāsudevāmṛta-prada.
text:
> 'vāsudevoddhāra' ei kahila ākhyāna
> 'vāsudevāmṛta-prada' haila prabhura nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]-[[synonyms:u:uddhāra]]---giving liberation to Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---is described; [[synonyms:ā:ākhyāna]]---narration; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:p:prada]]---the giver of nectar to Vāsudeva; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's holy name.
translation: Thus I have described how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu reclaimed the leper Vāsudeva and so received the name Vāsudevāmṛta-prada.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.151
description: Thus I end my description of the first tour of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, His visiting the temple of Kūrma and His liberating the leper brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva.
text:
> ei ta' kahila prabhura prathama gamana
> kūrma-daraśana, vāsudeva-vimocana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']] [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---thus I have described; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prathama]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---the first tour; [[synonyms:k:kūrma]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting the temple of Kūrma; [[synonyms:v:vāsudeva]]-[[synonyms:v:vimocana]]---and liberating the leper //brāhmaṇa// of the name Vāsudeva.
translation: Thus I end my description of the first tour of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, His visiting the temple of Kūrma and His liberating the leper brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.152
description: One who hears these pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with great faith will surely very soon attain the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> śraddhā kari' ei līlā ye kare śravaṇa
> acirāte milaye tāre caitanya-caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---with great faith; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---this pastime; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---anyone; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]---hearing; [[synonyms:a:acirāte]]---very soon; [[synonyms:m:milaye]]---meets; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---him; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: One who hears these pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with great faith will surely very soon attain the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.153
description: I admit that I do not know the beginning or the end of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastimes. However, whatever I have written I have heard from the mouths of great personalities.
text:
> caitanya-līlāra ādi-anta nāhi jāni
> sei likhi, yei mahāntera mukhe śuni
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlāra]]---of the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---beginning; [[synonyms:a:anta]]---and end; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I know; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:l:likhi]]---I write; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---which; [[synonyms:m:mahāntera]]---of the great personalities; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---from the mouths; [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---I hear.
translation: I admit that I do not know the beginning or the end of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastimes. However, whatever I have written I have heard from the mouths of great personalities.
purport: The name Vāsudevāmṛta-prada is mentioned in the verses composed by Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. When a person actually revives his consciousness with thoughts of Kṛṣṇa by the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he revives his spiritual life and becomes addicted to the service of the Lord. Only then can he act as an //ācārya.// In other words, everyone should engage in preaching, following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. In this way one will be very much appreciated by Lord Kṛṣṇa and will quickly be recognized by Him. Actually a devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu must engage in preaching in order to increase the followers of the Lord. By thus preaching actual Vedic knowledge all over the world, one will benefit all mankind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.154
description: O devotees, please do not consider my offenses in this regard. Your lotus feet are my only shelter.
text:
> ithe aparādha mora nā la-io, bhakta-gaṇa
> tomā-sabāra caraṇa---mora ekānta śaraṇa

translation: O devotees, please do not consider my offenses in this regard. Your lotus feet are my only shelter.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.155
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation:
Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Seventh Chapter, describing the liberation of the brāhmaṇa Vāsudeva and the Lord's tour of South India.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.16
description: "Let one or two of us go with You; otherwise You may fall into the clutches of thieves and rogues along the way. They may be whomever You like, but two persons should go with You.
text:
> dui-eka saṅge caluka, nā paḍa haṭha-raṅge
> yāre kaha sei dui caluk tomāra saṅge

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.17
description: "Indeed, I know all the paths to the different places of pilgrimage in South India. Just order Me, and I shall go with You."
text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.18

translation: The Lord replied, "I am simply a dancer, and You are the wire-puller. However You pull the wires to make Me dance, I shall dance in that way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.19

translation: "After accepting the sannyāsa order, I decided to go to Vṛndāvana, but You took Me instead to the house of Advaita Prabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.2

> jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda

translation: All glories to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to the devotees of Lord Caitanya!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.20

translation: "According to Dāmodara, I am still a neophyte as far as social etiquette is concerned; therefore he does not like My independent nature.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.27
description: "Dāmodara Paṇḍita and others are more advanced in receiving the mercy of Lord Kṛṣṇa; therefore they are independent of public opinion. As such, they want Me to enjoy sense gratification, even though it be unethical. But since I am a poor sannyāsī, I cannot abandon the duties of the renounced order, and therefore I follow them strictly.
text:
> lokāpekṣā nāhi iṅhāra kṛṣṇa-kṛpā haite
> āmi lokāpekṣā kabhu nā pāri chāḍite
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:a:apekṣā]]---care for society; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is none; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]]---of Dāmodara; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---the mercy of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:a:apekṣā]]---dependence on public opinion; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---able; [[synonyms:c:chāḍite]]---to give up.
translation: "Dāmodara Paṇḍita and others are more advanced in receiving the mercy of Lord Kṛṣṇa; therefore they are independent of public opinion. As such, they want Me to enjoy sense gratification, even though it be unethical. But since I am a poor sannyāsī, I cannot abandon the duties of the renounced order, and therefore I follow them strictly.
purport: A //brahmacārī// is supposed to assist a //sannyāsī;// therefore a //brahmacārī// should not try to instruct a //sannyāsī.// That is the etiquette. Consequently Dāmodara should not have advised Caitanya Mahāprabhu of His duty.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.28
description: "You should all therefore remain here in Nīlācala for some days while I tour the sacred places of pilgrimage alone."
text:
> ataeva tumi saba raha nīlācale
> dina kata āmi tīrtha bhramiba ekale"

translation: "You should all therefore remain here in Nīlācala for some days while I tour the sacred places of pilgrimage alone."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.29
description: Actually the Lord was controlled by the good qualities of all His devotees. On the pretense of attributing faults, He tasted all these qualities.
text:
> iṅhā-sabāra vaśa prabhu haye ye ye guṇe
> doṣāropa-cchale kare guṇa āsvādane
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṅhā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all the devotees; [[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---controlled; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:h:haye]]---is; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---by the qualities; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āropa]]-[[synonyms:c:chale]]---on the plea of attributing faults; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---high qualities; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādane]]---tasting.
translation: Actually the Lord was controlled by the good qualities of all His devotees. On the pretense of attributing faults, He tasted all these qualities.
purport: All the accusations made by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu against His beloved devotees actually showed His great appreciation of their intense love for Him. Yet He mentioned these faults one after another as if He were offended by their intense affection. The personal associates of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sometimes behaved contrary to regulative principles out of intense love for the Lord, and because of their love Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself sometimes violated the regulative principles of a //sannyāsī.// In the eyes of the public, such violations are not good, but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was so controlled by His devotees' love that He was obliged to break some of the rules. Although accusing them, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was indirectly indicating that He was very satisfied with their behavior in pure love of Godhead. Therefore in verse 27 He mentions that His devotees and associates place more importance on love of Kṛṣṇa than on social etiquette. There are many instances of devotional service rendered by previous //ācāryas// who did not care about social behavior when intensely absorbed in love for Kṛṣṇa. Unfortunately, as long as we are within this material world, we must observe social customs to avoid criticism by the general populace. This is Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's desire.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.3
description: After delivering Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, the Lord desired to go to South India to preach.
text:
> ei-mate sārvabhaumera nistāra karila
> dakṣiṇa-gamane prabhura icchā upajila

translation: After delivering Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, the Lord desired to go to South India to preach.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.30
description: No one can properly describe Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's affection for His devotees. He always tolerated all kinds of personal unhappiness resulting from His acceptance of the renounced order of life.
text:
> caitanyera bhakta-vātsalya---akathya-kathana
> āpane vairāgya-duḥkha karena sahana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanyera]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vātsalya]]---the love for His devotees; [[synonyms:a:akathya]]-[[synonyms:k:kathana]]---indescribable by words; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:v:vairāgya]]---of the renounced order; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:s:sahana]]---toleration.
translation: No one can properly describe Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's affection for His devotees. He always tolerated all kinds of personal unhappiness resulting from His acceptance of the renounced order of life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.31
description: The regulative principles observed by Caitanya Mahāprabhu were sometimes intolerable, and all the devotees became greatly affected by them. Although strictly observing the regulative principles, Caitanya Mahāprabhu could not tolerate the unhappiness felt by His devotees.
text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.37
description: "Since Your two hands will always be engaged in chanting and counting the holy names, how will You be able to carry the waterpot and external garments?

> tomāra dui hasta baddha nāma-gaṇane

synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:h:hasta]]---hands; [[synonyms:b:baddha]]---engaged; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name; [[synonyms:g:gaṇane]]---in counting; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---waterpot; [[synonyms:b:bahir]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsa]]---external garments; [[synonyms:v:vahibe]]---will carry; [[synonyms:k:kemane]]---how.
translation: "Since Your two hands will always be engaged in chanting and counting the holy names, how will You be able to carry the waterpot and external garments?
purport:
From this verse it is clear that Caitanya Mahāprabhu was chanting the holy names a fixed number of times daily. The Gosvāmīs used to follow in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and Haridāsa Ṭhākura also followed this principle. Concerning the Gosvāmīs-Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrīla Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, Śrīla Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī and Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī-Śrīnivāsa Ācārya confirms: //saṅkhyā-pūrvaka-nāma-gāna-natibhiḥ.// (//Ṣaḍ-gosvāmy-aṣṭaka// 6) In addition to other duties, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu introduced the system of chanting the holy name of the Lord a fixed number of times daily, as confirmed in this verse (//tomāra dui hasta baddha nāma-gaṇane//). Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to count on His fingers. While one hand was engaged in chanting, the other hand kept the number of rounds. This is corroborated in the //Caitanya-candrāmṛta// and also in Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's //Stava-mālā://

> badhnan prema-bhara-prakampita-karo granthīn kaṭī-dorakaiḥ
> saṅkhyātuṁ nija-loka-maṅgala-hare-kṛṣṇeti nāmnāṁ japan

(//Caitanya-candrāmṛta// 16)

> hare kṛṣṇety uccaiḥ sphurita-rasano nāma-gaṇanā-
> kṛta-granthi-śreṇī-subhaga-kaṭi-sūtrojjvala-karaḥ

(//Prathama-Caitanyāṣṭaka// 5)

Therefore devotees in the line of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu must chant at least sixteen rounds daily, and this is the number prescribed by the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. Haridāsa Ṭhākura daily chanted 300,000 names. Sixteen rounds is about 28,000 names. There is no need to imitate Haridāsa Ṭhākura or the other Gosvāmīs, but chanting the holy name a fixed number of times daily is essential for every devotee.

purport: This Kṛṣṇadāsa, known as Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa, is not the Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa mentioned in the Eleventh Chapter, verse 37, of the //Ādi-līlā.// The Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa mentioned in the Eleventh Chapter is one of the twelve //gopālas// (cowherd boys) who appeared to substantiate the pastimes of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He is known as a great devotee of Lord Nityānanda Prabhu. The //brāhmaṇa// named Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa who went with Śrī Caitanya to South India and later to Bengal is mentioned in the //Madhya-līlā,// Tenth Chapter, verses 62-79. One should not take these two to be the same person.

translation: At the end of the month of Phālguna, He witnessed the Dola-yātrā ceremony, and in His usual ecstatic love of God, He chanted and danced in various ways on the occasion.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.50

translation: Upon hearing Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's request, Caitanya Mahāprabhu relented. He stayed a few days longer and did not depart.

translation: The Bhaṭṭācārya eagerly invited Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu to his home and fed Him very nicely.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.52

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.62

> adhikārī hayena teṅho vidyānagare

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.63
description: "Please do not neglect him, thinking he belongs to a śūdra family engaged in material activities. It is my request that You meet him without fail."
text:
> śūdra viṣayi-jñāne upekṣā nā karibe
> āmāra vacane tāṅre avaśya milibe
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śūdra]]---the fourth social division; [[synonyms:v:viṣayi]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---by the impression of being a worldly man; [[synonyms:u:upekṣā]]---negligence; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---should not do; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---my; [[synonyms:v:vacane]]---on the request; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:m:milibe]]---You shouid meet.
translation: "Please do not neglect him, thinking he belongs to a śūdra family engaged in material activities. It is my request that You meet him without fail."
purport:
In the //varṇāśrama-dharma,// the //śūdra// is the fourth division in the social status. //Paricaryātmakaṁ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāva-jam// [[books:bg:18:44|(Bg. 18.44)]]. //Śūdras// are meant to engage in the service of the three higher classes-//brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas// and //vaiśyas.// Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya belonged to the //karaṇa// class, which is the equivalent of the //kāyastha// class in Bengal. This class is regarded all over India as //śūdra.// It is said that the Bengali //kāyasthas// were originally engaged as servants of //brāhmaṇas// who came from North India to Bengal. Later, the clerical class became the //kāyasthas// in Bengal. Now there are many mixed classes known as //kāyastha.// Sometimes it is said in Bengal that those who cannot claim any particular class belong to the //kāyastha// class. Although these //kāyasthas// or //karaṇas// are considered //śūdras,// they are very intelligent and highly educated. Most of them are professionals such as lawyers or politicians. Thus in Bengal the //kāyasthas// are sometimes considered //kṣatriyas.// In Orissa, however, the //kāyastha// class, which includes the //karaṇas,// is considered in the //śūdra// category. Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya belonged to this //karaṇa// class; therefore he was considered a //śūdra.// He was also the governor of South India under the regime of Mahārāja Pratāparudra of Orissa. In other words, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya informed Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu that Rāmānanda Rāya, although belonging to the //śūdra// class, was a highly responsible government officer. As far as spiritual advancement is concerned, materialists, politicians and //śūdras// are generally disqualified. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya therefore requested that Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu not neglect Rāmānanda Rāya, who was highly advanced spiritually although he was born a //śūdra// and a materialist.

A //viṣayī// is one who is attached to family life and is interested only in wife, children and worldly sense gratification. The senses can be engaged either in worldly enjoyment or in the service of the Lord. Those who are not engaged in the service of the Lord and are interested only in material sense gratification are called //viṣayī.// Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya was engaged in government service, and he belonged to the //karaṇa// class. He was certainly not a //sannyāsī// in saffron cloth, yet he was in the transcendental position of a //paramahaṁsa// householder. Before becoming Caitanya Mahāprabhu's disciple, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya considered Rāmānanda Rāya an ordinary //viṣayī// because he was a householder engaged in government service. However, when the Bhaṭṭācārya was actually enlightened in Vaiṣṇava philosophy, he could understand the exalted transcendental position of Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya; therefore he referred to him as //adhikārī.// An //adhikārī// is one who knows the transcendental science of Kṛṣṇa and is engaged in His service; therefore all //gṛhastha// devotees are designated as //dāsa adhikārī.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.64
description: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya continued, "Rāmānanda Rāya is a fit person to associate with You; no other devotee can compare with him in knowledge of the transcendental mellows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.66
description: "I could not realize when I first spoke with Rāmānanda Rāya that his topics and endeavors were all transcendentally uncommon. I made fun of him simply because he was a Vaiṣṇava."
text:
> alaukika vākya ceṣṭā tāṅra nā bujhiyā
> parihāsa kariyāchi tāṅre 'vaiṣṇava' baliyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:alaukika]]---uncommon; [[synonyms:v:vākya]]---words; [[synonyms:c:ceṣṭā]]---endeavor; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---without; [[synonyms:b:bujhiyā]]---understanding; [[synonyms:p:parihāsa]]---joking; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchi]]---I have done; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---a devotee of the Lord; [[synonyms:b:baliyā]]---as.
translation: "I could not realize when I first spoke with Rāmānanda Rāya that his topics and endeavors were all transcendentally uncommon. I made fun of him simply because he was a Vaiṣṇava."
purport:
Anyone who is a not a Vaiṣṇava, or an unalloyed devotee of the Supreme Lord, must be a materialist. A Vaiṣṇava living according to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's injunctions is certainly not on the materialistic platform. Caitanya means "spiritual force." All of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities were carried out on the platform of spiritual understanding; therefore only those who are on the spiritual platform are able to understand the activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Materialistic persons who cannot are generally known as //karmīs// or //jñānīs.// The //jñānīs// are mental speculators who simply try to understand what is spirit and what is soul. Their process is //neti neti:// "This is not spirit, this is not Brahman." The //jñānīs// are a little more advanced than the dull-headed //karmīs,// who are simply interested in sense gratification. Before becoming a Vaiṣṇava, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was a mental speculator (//jñānī//), and being such, he always cut jokes with Vaiṣṇavas. A Vaiṣṇava never agrees with the speculative system of the //jñānīs.// Both the //jñānīs// and //karmīs// depend on direct sense perception for their imperfect knowledge. The //karmīs// never agree to accept anything not directly perceived, and the //jñānīs// put forth only hypotheses. However, the Vaiṣṇavas, the unalloyed devotees of the Lord, do not follow the process of acquiring knowledge by direct sense perception or mental speculation. Because they are servants of the Supreme Lord, devotees receive knowledge directly from the Supreme Personality of Godhead as He speaks it in the //Bhagavad-gītā,// or sometimes as He imparts it from within as the //caitya-guru.// As stated in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:10:10|(Bg. 10.10)]]:

> teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ
> bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam
> dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ
> yena mām upayānti te

"To those who are constantly devoted to serving Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me." [[books:bg:10:10|(Bg. 10.10)]]

The //Vedas// are considered to have been spoken by the Supreme Lord. They were first realized by Brahmā, who is the first created being within the universe (//tene brahma hṛdā ya ādi-kavaye//). Our process is to receive knowledge through the //paramparā// system, from Kṛṣṇa to Brahmā, to Nārada, Vyāsa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and the six Gosvāmīs. By disciplic succession, Lord Brahmā was enlightened from within by the original person, Kṛṣṇa. Our knowledge is fully perfect due to being handed from master to disciple. A Vaiṣṇava is always engaged in the transcendental loving service of the Lord, and thus neither //karmīs// nor //jñānīs// can understand the activities of a Vaiṣṇava. It is said, //vaiṣṇavera kriyā-mudrā vijñeha nā bujhaya:// even the most learned man depending on direct perception of knowledge cannot understand the activities of a Vaiṣṇava. After being initiated into Vaiṣṇavism by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Bhaṭṭācārya realized what a mistake he had made in trying to understand Rāmānanda Rāya, who was very learned and whose endeavors were all directed to rendering transcendental loving service to the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.67
description: The Bhaṭṭācārya said, "By Your mercy I can now understand the truth about Rāmānanda Rāya. In talking with him, You also will acknowledge his greatness."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.69
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked the Bhaṭṭācārya to bless Him while he engaged in the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa at home, so that by Sārvabhauma's mercy the Lord could return to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> "ghare kṛṣṇa bhaji' more kariha āśīrvāde
> nīlācale āsi' yena tomāra prasāde"
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at home; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhaji']]---worshiping; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do; [[synonyms:ā:āśīrvāde]]---blessing; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---at Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---returning; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---so that; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:p:prasāde]]---by the mercy.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked the Bhaṭṭācārya to bless Him while he engaged in the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa at home, so that by Sārvabhauma's mercy the Lord could return to Jagannātha Purī.
purport: The word //kariha āśīrvāde// means "continue to bestow your blessings upon Me." Being a //sannyāsī,// Caitanya Mahāprabhu was on the highest platform of respect and adoration, whereas Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, as a householder, was on the second platform. Therefore a //sannyāsī// is supposed to offer blessings to a //gṛhastha.// Now Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by His practical behavior requested the blessings of a //gṛhastha.// This is the special significance of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's preaching. He gave equal status to everyone, regardless of material considerations. His movement is thoroughly spiritual. Although apparently a //gṛhastha// (householder), Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was unlike the so-called //karmīs// interested in sense gratification. After being initiated by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Bhaṭṭācārya was perfectly situated in the spiritual order; therefore it was quite possible for him to offer blessings even to a //sannyāsī.// He was always engaged in the service of the Lord even at home. In our disciplic line we have the example of a perfect householder //paramahaṁsa//-Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura. In his book //Śaraṇāgati,// Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura stated: //ye-dina gṛhe, bhajana dekhi', gṛhete goloka bhāya// (//Śaraṇāgati// 31.6). Whenever a householder glorifies the Supreme Lord in his home, his activities are immediately transformed into the activities of Goloka Vṛndāvana, spiritual activities taking place in the Goloka Vṛndāvana planet of Kṛṣṇa. Activities exhibited by Kṛṣṇa Himself at Bhauma Vṛndāvana, the Vṛndāvana-dhāma existing on this planet, are not different from His activities on the planet Goloka Vṛndāvana. This is proper realization of Vṛndāvana anywhere. In our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement we inaugurated the New Vṛndāvana activities, wherein devotees are always engaged in the transcendental loving service of the Lord, and this is not different from Goloka Vṛndāvana. The conclusion is that one who acts strictly in the line of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is competent to offer blessings to //sannyāsīs,// even though he be a //gṛhastha// householder. Although he is in an exalted position, a //sannyāsī// yet must elevate himself to the transcendental platform by rendering service to the Lord. By his actual behavior, Caitanya Mahāprabhu begged the blessings of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. He set the example of how one should expect blessings from a Vaiṣṇava, regardless of his social position.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.7-8
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu called all His devotees together and, holding them by the hand, humbly informed them, "You are all more dear to Me than My life. I can give up My life, but to give up you is difficult for Me.
text:
> nija-gaṇa āni' kahe vinaya kariyā
> āliṅgana kari' sabāya śrī-haste dhariyā
> tomā-sabā jāni āmi prāṇādhika kari'
> prāṇa chāḍā yāya, tomā-sabā chāḍite nā pāri

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu called all His devotees together and, holding them by the hand, humbly informed them, "You are all more dear to Me than My life. I can give up My life, but to give up you is difficult for Me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.70
description: Saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu departed on His tour, and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya immediately fainted and fell to the ground.

> mūrcchita hañā tāhāṅ paḍilā sārvabhauma
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---made; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---departure; [[synonyms:m:mūrcchita]]---fainted; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.
translation: Saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu departed on His tour, and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya immediately fainted and fell to the ground.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.71
description: Although Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya fainted, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not take notice of him. Rather, He left quickly. Who can understand the mind and intention of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu?
text:
> tāṅre upekṣiyā kaila śīghra gamana
> ke bujhite pāre mahāprabhura citta-mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:u:upekṣiyā]]---not paying serious attention; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]]---very fast; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---walking; [[synonyms:k:ke]]---who; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand; [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---is able; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:citta]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind and intention.
translation: Although Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya fainted, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not take notice of him. Rather, He left quickly. Who can understand the mind and intention of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu?
purport: It was naturally expected that when Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya fainted and fell to the ground Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would have taken care of him and waited for him to regain consciousness, but He did not do so. Rather, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately started on His tour. It is therefore very difficult to understand the activities of a transcendental person. Sometimes they may seem rather odd, but a transcendental personality remains in his position, unaffected by material considerations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.72
description: This is the nature of the mind of an uncommon personality. Sometimes it is soft like a flower, but sometimes it is as hard as a thunderbolt.
text:

> puṣpa-sama komala, kaṭhina vajra-maya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:a:anubhāvera]]---of a great personality; [[synonyms:c:cittera]]---of the mind; [[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---the nature; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---this is; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---like a flower; [[synonyms:k:komala]]---soft; [[synonyms:k:kaṭhina]]---hard; [[synonyms:v:vajra]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---like a thunderbolt.
translation: This is the nature of the mind of an uncommon personality. Sometimes it is soft like a flower, but sometimes it is as hard as a thunderbolt.
purport: The softness of a flower and the hardness of a thunderbolt are reconciled in the behavior of a great personality. The following quotation from //Uttara-rāma-carita// (2.7) explains this behavior. One may also consult //Madhya-līlā,// Third Chapter, verse 212.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.73

> mṛdūni kusumād api
> lokottarāṇāṁ cetāṁsi
> ko nu vijñātum īśvaraḥ

translation: "The hearts of those above common behavior are sometimes harder than a thunderbolt and sometimes softer than a flower. How can one accommodate such contradictions in great personalities?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.79
description: The body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was naturally very beautiful. It was like molten gold dressed in saffron cloth. Indeed, He was most beautiful for being ornamented with the ecstatic symptoms, which caused His hair to stand on end, tears to well in His eyes, and His body to tremble and perspire all over.

Indeed, He was most beautiful for being ornamented with the ecstatic symptoms, which caused His hair to stand on end, tears to well in His eyes, and His body to tremble and perspire all over.
