> dekhiyā lokera mane haila camatkāra
> yata loka āise, keha nāhi yāya ghara
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing all this; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of the people; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the minds; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonishment; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---came there; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes; [[synonyms:g:ghara]]---home.
translation: Everyone present was astonished to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's dancing and His bodily transformations. Whoever came did not want to return home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.81
description: Everyone-including children, old men and women-began to dance and chant the holy names of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Gopāla. In this way they all floated in the ocean of love of Godhead.
text:
> keha nāce, keha gāya, 'śrī-kṛṣṇa' 'gopāla'
> premete bhāsila loka,---strī-vṛddha-ābāla
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---someone dances; [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---someone chants; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa's name; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Gopāla's name; [[synonyms:p:premete]]---in love of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhāsila]]---floated; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people; [[synonyms:s:strī]]---women; [[synonyms:v:vṛddha]]---old men; [[synonyms:ā:ā]]-[[synonyms:b:bāla]]---from the children.
translation: Everyone-including children, old men and women-began to dance and chant the holy names of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Gopāla. In this way they all floated in the ocean of love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.82
description: Upon seeing the chanting and dancing of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Lord Nityānanda predicted that later there would be dancing and chanting in every village.
text:
> dekhi' nityānanda prabhu kahe bhakta-gaṇe
> ei-rūpe nṛtya āge habe grāme-grāme
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing this; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---unto the devotees; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in this way; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---ahead; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:g:grāme]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in every village.
translation: Upon seeing the chanting and dancing of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Lord Nityānanda predicted that later there would be dancing and chanting in every village.
purport: This prediction of Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu is applicable not only in India but also all over the world. That is now happening by His grace. The members of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness are now traveling from one village to another in the Western countries and are even carrying the Deity with them. These devotees distribute various scriptures all over the world. We hope that these devotees who are preaching the message of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will very seriously follow strictly in His footsteps. If they follow the rules and regulations and chant sixteen rounds daily, their endeavor to preach the cult of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu will certainly be successful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.83
description: Seeing that it was already getting late, Lord Nityānanda Prabhu, the spiritual master, invented a means to disperse the crowd.
text:
> atikāla haila, loka chāḍiyā nā yāya
> tabe nityānanda-gosāñi sṛjilā upāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:atikāla]]---very late; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---it was; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people in general; [[synonyms:c:chāḍiyā]]---giving up; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---do not go; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Śrīla Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---the spiritual master; [[synonyms:s:sṛjilā]]---invented; [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---a means.
translation: Seeing that it was already getting late, Lord Nityānanda Prabhu, the spiritual master, invented a means to disperse the crowd.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.84
description: When Lord Nityānanda Prabhu took Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for lunch at noon, everyone came running around Them.
text:
> madhyāhna karite gelā prabhuke lañā
> tāhā dekhi' loka āise caudike dhāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhyāhna]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to take lunch at noon; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing that; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people in general; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---came; [[synonyms:c:caudike]]---all around; [[synonyms:d:dhāñā]]---running.
translation: When Lord Nityānanda Prabhu took Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for lunch at noon, everyone came running around Them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.85
description: After finishing Their baths, They returned at noon to the temple. Admitting His own men, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu closed the outside door.
text:
> madhyāhna kariyā āilā devatā-mandire
> nija-gaṇa praveśi' kapāṭa dila bahir-dvāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhyāhna]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---performing bathing, etc; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came back; [[synonyms:d:devatā]]-[[synonyms:m:mandire]]---to the temple of the Lord; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]] [[synonyms:p:praveśi']]---allowing His own men; [[synonyms:k:kapāṭa]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---shut; [[synonyms:b:bahir]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---the outside door.
translation: After finishing Their baths, They returned at noon to the temple. Admitting His own men, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu closed the outside door.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.86
description: Gopīnātha Ācārya then brought prasāda for the two Lords to eat, and after They had eaten, the remnants of the food were distributed to all the devotees.
text:
> tabe gopīnātha dui-prabhure bhikṣā karāila
> prabhura śeṣa prasādānna sabe bāṅṭi' khāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereupon; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]---Gopīnātha Ācārya; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto the two Lords Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---gave prasāda to eat; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]---the remnants; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]-[[synonyms:a:anna]]---food; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:b:bāṅṭi']]---sharing; [[synonyms:k:kbāila]]---ate.
translation: Gopīnātha Ācārya then brought prasāda for the two Lords to eat, and after They had eaten, the remnants of the food were distributed to all the devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.87
description: Hearing about this, everyone there came to the outside door and began chanting the holy name, "Hari! Hari!" Thus there was a tumultuous sound.
text:
> śuni' śuni' loka-saba āsi' bahir-dvāre
> 'hari' 'hari' bali' loka kolāhala kare
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all the people; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming there; [[synonyms:b:bahir]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---to the outside door; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---the holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---chanting; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people; [[synonyms:k:kolāhala]]---tumultuous sound; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---made.
translation: Hearing about this, everyone there came to the outside door and began chanting the holy name, "Hari! Hari!" Thus there was a tumultuous sound.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.88
description: After lunch, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu made them open the door. In this way everyone received His audience with great pleasure.
text:
> tabe mahāprabhu dvāra karāila mocana
> ānande āsiyā loka pāila daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereupon; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dvāra]]---the door; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---made; [[synonyms:m:mocana]]---opening; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in great pleasure; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---sight.
translation: After lunch, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu made them open the door. In this way everyone received His audience with great pleasure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.89
description: The people came and went until evening, and all of them became Vaiṣṇava devotees and began to chant and dance.
text:
> ei-mata sandhyā paryanta loka āse, yāya
> 'vaiṣṇava' ha-ila loka, sabe nāce, gāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:s:sandhyā]] [[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---until evening; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:ā:āse]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---come and go; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotees; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---and chant.
translation: The people came and went until evening, and all of them became Vaiṣṇava devotees and began to chant and dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.9
description: "You are all My friends, and you have properly executed the duties of friends by bringing Me here to Jagannātha Purī and giving Me the chance to see Lord Jagannātha in the temple.
text:
> tumi-saba bandhu mora bandhu-kṛtya kaile
> ihāṅ āni' more jagannātha dekhāile
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of you; [[synonyms:b:bandhu]]---friends; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:b:bandhu]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛtya]]---duties of a friend; [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---you have executed; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:m:more]]---to Me; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:d:dekhāile]]---you have shown.
translation: "You are all My friends, and you have properly executed the duties of friends by bringing Me here to Jagannātha Purī and giving Me the chance to see Lord Jagannātha in the temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.90
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then passed the night there and discussed the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa with His devotees with great pleasure.
text:
> ei-rūpe sei ṭhāñi bhakta-gaṇa-saṅge
> sei rātri goṅāilā kṛṣṇa-kathā-raṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in this way; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---in that place; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the devotees; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:r:rātri]]---that night; [[synonyms:g:goṅāilā]]---passed; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---in great pleasure discussing Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then passed the night there and discussed the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa with His devotees with great pleasure.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.91
description: The next morning, after taking His bath, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu started on His South Indian tour. He bade farewell to the devotees by embracing them.
text:
> prātaḥ-kāle snāna kari' karilā gamana
> bhakta-gaṇe vidāya dilā kari' āliṅgana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bath; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---after taking; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---started; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---tour; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---to all the devotees; [[synonyms:v:vidāya]]---farewell; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing.
translation: The next morning, after taking His bath, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu started on His South Indian tour. He bade farewell to the devotees by embracing them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.92
description: Although they all fell to the ground unconscious, the Lord did not turn to see them but proceeded onward.
text:
> mūrcchita hañā sabe bhūmite paḍilā
> tāṅhā-sabā pāne prabhu phiri' nā cāhilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mūrcchita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming unconscious; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]]---to the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all of them; [[synonyms:p:pāne]]---toward; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:phiri']]---turning; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:c:cāhilā]]---saw.
translation: Although they all fell to the ground unconscious, the Lord did not turn to see them but proceeded onward.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.93
description: In separation, the Lord became very perturbed and walked on unhappily. His servant, Kṛṣṇadāsa, who was carrying His waterpot, followed behind.
text:
> vicchede vyākula prabhu calilā duḥkhī hañā
> pāche kṛṣṇadāsa yāya jala-pātra lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vicchede]]---in separation; [[synonyms:v:vyākula]]---perturbed; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went on; [[synonyms:d:duḥkhī]]---unhappy; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---just behind; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---His servant Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---went; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---the waterpot; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking.
translation: In separation, the Lord became very perturbed and walked on unhappily. His servant, Kṛṣṇadāsa, who was carrying His waterpot, followed behind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.94
description: All the devotees remained there and fasted, but the next day they all unhappily returned to Jagannātha Purī.
text:
> bhakta-gaṇa upavāsī tāhāṅi rahilā
> āra dine duḥkhī hañā nīlācale āilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:u:upavāsī]]---fasting; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅi]]---there; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---on the next day; [[synonyms:d:duḥkhī]]---unhappy; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned.
translation: All the devotees remained there and fasted, but the next day they all unhappily returned to Jagannātha Purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.95
description: Almost like a mad lion, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went on His tour filled with ecstatic love and performing saṅkīrtana, chanting Kṛṣṇa's names as follows.
text:
> matta-siṁha-prāya prabhu karilā gamana
> premāveśe yāya kari' nāma-saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:matta]]-[[synonyms:s:siṁha]]---a mad lion; [[synonyms:p:prāya]]---almost like; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---touring; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---performing; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting Kṛṣṇa's name.
translation: Almost like a mad lion, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went on His tour filled with ecstatic love and performing saṅkīrtana, chanting Kṛṣṇa's names as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.96
description: The Lord chanted:
text:
> kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! he
> kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! he
> kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! rakṣa mām
> kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa! pāhi mām
> rāma! rāghava! rāma! rāghava! rāma! rāghava! rakṣa mām
> kṛṣṇa! keśava! kṛṣṇa! keśava! kṛṣṇa! keśava! pāhi mām
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:he]]---O; [[synonyms:r:rakṣa]]---please protect; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---Me; [[synonyms:p:pāhi]]---please maintain; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]---Lord Rāma; [[synonyms:r:rāghava]]---descendant of King Raghu; [[synonyms:k:keśava]]---killer of the Keśī demon.
translation:
The Lord chanted:

Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! he \\
Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! he \\
Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Rakṣa mām \\
Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa! Pāhi mām

That is, "O Lord Kṛṣṇa, please protect Me and maintain Me." He also chanted:

Rāma! Rāghava! Rāma! Rāghava! Rāma! Rāghava! Rakṣa mām \\
Kṛṣṇa! Keśava! Kṛṣṇa! Keśava! Kṛṣṇa! Keśava! pāhi mām

That is, "O Lord Rāma, descendant of King Raghu, please protect Me. O Kṛṣṇa, O Keśava, killer of the Keśī demon, please maintain Me."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.97
description: Chanting this verse, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, known as Gaurahari, went on His way. As soon as He saw someone, He would request him to chant "Hari! Hari!"
text:
> ei śloka paḍi' pathe calilā gaurahari
> loka dekhi' pathe kahe,---bala 'hari' 'hari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting this verse //kṛṣṇa! kṛṣṇa!//; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:loka]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing other people; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---He says; [[synonyms:b:bala]]---say; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---the holy name of Lord Hari.
translation: Chanting this verse, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, known as Gaurahari, went on His way. As soon as He saw someone, He would request him to chant "Hari! Hari!"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.98
description: Whoever heard Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu chant "Hari, Hari," also chanted the holy name of Lord Hari and Kṛṣṇa. In this way they all followed the Lord, very eager to see Him.
text:
> sei loka prema-matta hañā bale 'hari' 'kṛṣṇa'
> prabhura pāche saṅge yāya darśana-satṛṣṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---that person; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:m:matta]]---maddened in love of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---says; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---the holy name of Lord Hari and Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---behind the Lord; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Him; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]-[[synonyms:s:satṛṣṇa]]---being very eager to see Him.
translation: Whoever heard Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu chant "Hari, Hari," also chanted the holy name of Lord Hari and Kṛṣṇa. In this way they all followed the Lord, very eager to see Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 7.99
description: After some time the Lord would embrace these people and bid them to return home, having investing them with spiritual potency.
text:
> kata-kṣaṇe rahi' prabhu tāre āliṅgiyā
> vidāya karila tāre śakti sañcāriyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kata]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]] [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---after remaining for some time; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---them; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgiyā]]---embracing; [[synonyms:v:vidāya]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---bade farewell; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---in them; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---spiritual potency; [[synonyms:s:sañcāriyā]]---investing.
translation: After some time the Lord would embrace these people and bid them to return home, having investing them with spiritual potency.
purport: In his //Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya,// Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains that this spiritual potency is the essence of the pleasure potency and the knowledge potency. By these two potencies, one is empowered with devotional service. Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself or His representative, the unalloyed devotee, can mercifully bestow these combined potencies upon any man. Being thus endowed with such potencies, one can become an unalloyed devotee of the Lord. Anyone favored by Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was empowered with this //bhakti-śakti.// Thus the Lord's followers were able to preach Kṛṣṇa consciousness by divine grace.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.1
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is known as Gaurāṅga, is the ocean of all conclusive knowledge in devotional service. He empowered Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya, who may be likened to a cloud of devotional service. This cloud was filled with the water of all the conclusive purports of devotional service and was empowered by the ocean to spread this water over the ocean of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself. Thus the ocean of Caitanya Mahāprabhu became filled with the jewels of the knowledge of pure devotional service.
text:
> sañcārya rāmābhidha-bhakta-meghe
> sva-bhakti-siddhānta-cayāmṛtāni
> gaurābdhir etair amunā vitīrṇais
> taj-jñatva-ratnālayatāṁ prayāti
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sañcārya]]---by empowering; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:a:abhidha]]---of the name Rāma; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:m:meghe]]---in the cloudlike devotee; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---of His own devotional service; [[synonyms:s:siddhānta]]---of conclusions; [[synonyms:c:caya]]---all collections; [[synonyms:a:amṛtāni]]---nectar; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:a:abdhiḥ]]---the ocean known as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:e:etaiḥ]]---by these; [[synonyms:a:amunā]]---by the cloud known as Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:v:vitīrṇaiḥ]]---distributed; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:j:jñatva]]---of knowledge of devotional service; [[synonyms:r:ratna]]-[[synonyms:ā:ālayatām]]---the quality of being an ocean containing valuable jewels; [[synonyms:p:prayāti]]---achieved.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is known as Gaurāṅga, is the ocean of all conclusive knowledge in devotional service. He empowered Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya, who may be likened to a cloud of devotional service. This cloud was filled with the water of all the conclusive purports of devotional service and was empowered by the ocean to spread this water over the ocean of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself. Thus the ocean of Caitanya Mahāprabhu became filled with the jewels of the knowledge of pure devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.10
description: As previously, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu converted to Vaiṣṇavism many people He met on the road. After some days, the Lord reached the banks of the River Godāvarī.
text:
> pūrvavat 'vaiṣṇava' kari' sarva loka-gaṇe
> godāvarī-tīre prabhu āilā kata-dine
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---as previously; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotees; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---all; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the people; [[synonyms:g:godāvarī]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank of the river Godāvarī; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:k:kata]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---after some days.
translation: As previously, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu converted to Vaiṣṇavism many people He met on the road. After some days, the Lord reached the banks of the River Godāvarī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.100
description: "When the gopīs began to talk among themselves, they said, 'Dear friends, the gopī who has been taken away by Kṛṣṇa to a secluded place must have worshiped the Lord more than anyone else.' "
text:
> anayārādhito nūnaṁ
> bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ
> yan no vihāya govindaḥ
> prīto yām anayad rahaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anayā]]---by Her; [[synonyms:ā:ārādhitaḥ]]---worshiped; [[synonyms:n:nūnam]]---indeed; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ī:īśvaraḥ]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---from which; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---us; [[synonyms:v:vihāya]]---rejecting; [[synonyms:g:govindaḥ]]---Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prītaḥ]]---satisfied; [[synonyms:y:yām]]---whom; [[synonyms:a:anayat]]---brought; [[synonyms:r:rahaḥ]]---a secluded place.
translation: "When the gopīs began to talk among themselves, they said, 'Dear friends, the gopī who has been taken away by Kṛṣṇa to a secluded place must have worshiped the Lord more than anyone else.' "
purport: The name Rādhā is derived from this verse (//Bhāg.// 10.30.28), from the words //anayārādhitaḥ,// meaning "by Her the Lord is worshiped." Sometimes the critics of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// find it difficult to find Rādhārāṇī's holy name, but the secret is disclosed here in the word //ārādhitaḥ,// from which the name //Rādhā// has come. Of course, the name of Rādhārāṇī is directly mentioned in other //Purāṇas.// This //gopī's// worship of Kṛṣṇa is topmost, and therefore Her name is Rādhā, or the topmost worshiper.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.101
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Please speak on. I am very happy to hear you because a river of unprecedented nectar is flowing from your mouth.
text:
> prabhu kahe---āge kaha, śunite pāi sukhe
> apūrvāmṛta-nadī vahe tomāra mukhe
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---ahead; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please speak; [[synonyms:ś:śunite]]---to hear; [[synonyms:p:pāi]]---I get; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---happiness; [[synonyms:a:apūrva]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---of unprecedented nectar; [[synonyms:n:nadī]]---a river; [[synonyms:v:vahe]]---flows; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---from your mouth.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Please speak on. I am very happy to hear you because a river of unprecedented nectar is flowing from your mouth.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.102
description: "During the rāsa dance Śrī Kṛṣṇa did not exchange loving affairs with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī due to the presence of the other gopīs. Because of the dependence of the others, the intensity of love between Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa was not manifest. Therefore He stole Her away.
text:
> curi kari' rādhāke nila gopī-gaṇera ḍare
> anyāpekṣā haile premera gāḍhatā nā sphure
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:curi]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---stealing; [[synonyms:r:rādhāke]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:n:nila]]---took away; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍare]]---out of fear; [[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:a:apekṣā]]---dependence on others; [[synonyms:h:haile]]---if there is; [[synonyms:p:premera]]---of love; [[synonyms:g:gāḍhatā]]---the intensity; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:s:sphure]]---manifests.
translation: "During the rāsa dance Śrī Kṛṣṇa did not exchange loving affairs with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī due to the presence of the other gopīs. Because of the dependence of the others, the intensity of love between Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa was not manifest. Therefore He stole Her away.
purport: Out of fear of the other //gopīs,// Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa took Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī to a secluded place. In this regard, the verse //kaṁsārir api// (verse 106 in this chapter) will be quoted from the //Gīta-govinda// of Jayadeva Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.103
description: "If Lord Kṛṣṇa rejected the company of the other gopīs for Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, we can understand that Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa has intense affection for Her."
text:
> rādhā lāgi' gopīre yadi sākṣāt kare tyāga
> tabe jāni,---rādhāya kṛṣṇera gāḍha-anurāga
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rādhā]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for the sake of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:g:gopīre]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:t:tyāga]]---rejection; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---we can understand; [[synonyms:r:rādhāya]]---in Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gāḍha]]---intense; [[synonyms:a:anurāga]]---affection.
translation: "If Lord Kṛṣṇa rejected the company of the other gopīs for Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, we can understand that Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa has intense affection for Her."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.104
description: Rāmānanda Rāya continued, "Please therefore hear from me about the glories of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's loving affairs. They are beyond compare within these three worlds.
text:
> rāya kahe,---tabe śuna premera mahimā
> tri-jagate rādhā-premera nāhika upamā
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Rāmānanda Rāya replied; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:p:premera]]---of that love; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---the glories; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:j:jagate]]---within the three worlds; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:p:premera]]---of the loving affairs of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there is not; [[synonyms:u:upamā]]---comparison.
translation: Rāmānanda Rāya continued, "Please therefore hear from me about the glories of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's loving affairs. They are beyond compare within these three worlds.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.105
description: "Finding Herself treated equally with all the other gopīs, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī displayed Her tricky behavior and left the circle of the rāsa dance. Missing Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's presence, Kṛṣṇa became very unhappy and began to lament and wander throughout the forest to search Her out.
text:
> gopī-gaṇera rāsa-nṛtya-maṇḍalī chāḍiyā
> rādhā cāhi' vane phire vilāpa kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---of //rāsa// dancing; [[synonyms:m:maṇḍalī]]---the circle; [[synonyms:c:chāḍiyā]]---rejecting; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:c:cāhi']]---desiring; [[synonyms:v:vane]]---in the forest; [[synonyms:p:phire]]---wanders; [[synonyms:v:vilāpa]]---lamentation; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---doing.
translation: "Finding Herself treated equally with all the other gopīs, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī displayed Her tricky behavior and left the circle of the rāsa dance. Missing Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's presence, Kṛṣṇa became very unhappy and began to lament and wander throughout the forest to search Her out.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.106
description: " 'Lord Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Kaṁsa, took Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī within His heart, for He desired to dance with Her. Thus He left the arena of the rāsa dance and the company of all the other beautiful damsels of Vraja.'
text:
> kaṁsārir api saṁsāra-
> vāsanā-baddha-śṛṅkhalām
> rādhām ādhāya hṛdaye
> tatyāja vraja-sundarīḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kaṁsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āriḥ]]---the enemy of Kaṁsa; [[synonyms:a:api]]---moreover; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsanā]]---desirous of the essence of enjoyment (//rāsa-līlā//); [[synonyms:b:baddha]]-[[synonyms:ś:śṛṅkhalām]]---being perfectly attracted to such activities; [[synonyms:r:rādhām]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:ā:ādhāya]]---taking; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---within the heart; [[synonyms:t:tatyāja]]---left aside; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:s:sundarīḥ]]---the other beautiful //gopīs.//
translation: “ 'Lord Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Kaṁsa, took Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī within His heart, for He desired to dance with Her. Thus He left the arena of the rāsa dance and the company of all the other beautiful damsels of Vraja.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.107
description: " 'Being afflicted by the arrow of Cupid and unhappily regretting His mistreating Rādhārāṇī, Mādhava, Lord Kṛṣṇa, began to search for Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī along the banks of the Yamunā River. When He failed to find Her, He entered the bushes of Vṛndāvana and began to lament.'
text:
> itas tatas tām anusṛtya rādhikām
> anaṅga-bāṇa-vraṇa-khinna-mānasaḥ
> kṛtānutāpaḥ sa kalinda-nandinī
> taṭānta-kuñje viṣasāda mādhavaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:itaḥ]] [[synonyms:t:tataḥ]]---hither and thither; [[synonyms:t:tām]]---Her; [[synonyms:a:anusṛtya]]---searching out; [[synonyms:r:rādhikām]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:a:anaṅga]]---of Cupid; [[synonyms:b:bāṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:vraṇa]]---by a wound from the arrow; [[synonyms:k:khinna]]-[[synonyms:m:mānasaḥ]]---whose heart is injured; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:anutāpaḥ]]---repentant for misbehavior; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He (Lord Kṛṣṇa); [[synonyms:k:kalinda]]-[[synonyms:n:nandinī]]---of the river Yamunā; [[synonyms:t:taṭa]]-[[synonyms:a:anta]]---on the edge of the bank; [[synonyms:k:kuñje]]---in the bushes; [[synonyms:v:viṣasāda]]---lamented; [[synonyms:m:mādhavaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: “ 'Being afflicted by the arrow of Cupid and unhappily regretting His mistreating Rādhārāṇī, Mādhava, Lord Kṛṣṇa, began to search for Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī along the banks of the Yamunā River. When He failed to find Her, He entered the bushes of Vṛndāvana and began to lament.'
purport: These two verses are from the //Gīta-govinda// (3.1, 2), written by Jayadeva Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.108
description: "Simply by considering these two verses one can understand what nectar there is in such dealings. It is exactly like freeing a mine of nectar.
text:
> ei dui-ślokera artha vicārile jāni
> vicārite uṭhe yena amṛtera khani
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:ś:ślokera]]---of the verses; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meanings; [[synonyms:v:vicārile]]---if considering; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I can understand; [[synonyms:v:vicārite]]---while considering; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---arises; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---like; [[synonyms:a:amṛtera]]---of nectar; [[synonyms:k:khani]]---a mine.
translation: "Simply by considering these two verses one can understand what nectar there is in such dealings. It is exactly like freeing a mine of nectar.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.109
description: "Although Kṛṣṇa was in the midst of hundreds of thousands of gopīs during the rāsa dance, He still kept Himself in one of His transcendental forms by the side of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
text:
> śata-koṭi gopī-saṅge rāsa-vilāsa
> tāra madhye eka-mūrtye rahe rādhā-pāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śata]]-[[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---hundreds of thousands; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---dancing in the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---among them; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrtye]]---by one of His transcendental forms; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---by the side of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
translation: "Although Kṛṣṇa was in the midst of hundreds of thousands of gopīs during the rāsa dance, He still kept Himself in one of His transcendental forms by the side of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.11
description: When He saw the River Godāvarī, the Lord remembered the River Yamunā, and when He saw the forest on the banks of the river, He remembered Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma.
text:
> godāvarī dekhi' ha-ila 'yamunā'-smaraṇa
> tīre vana dekhi' smṛti haila vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:godāvarī]]---the River Godāvarī; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]] [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---remembrance of the River Yamunā; [[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the banks; [[synonyms:v:vana]]---the forests; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:smṛti]]---remembrance; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Śrī Vṛndāvana.
translation: When He saw the River Godāvarī, the Lord remembered the River Yamunā, and when He saw the forest on the banks of the river, He remembered Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.110
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa is equal to everyone in His general dealings, but due to the conflicting ecstatic love of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, there were opposing elements.
text:
> sādhāraṇa-preme dekhi sarvatra 'samatā'
> rādhāra kuṭila-preme ha-ila 'vāmatā'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sādhāraṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:preme]]---in general love of Godhead; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---we see; [[synonyms:s:sarvatra]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:s:samatā]]---equality; [[synonyms:r:rādhāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:k:kuṭila]]-[[synonyms:p:preme]]---in the crooked love of Godhead; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:v:vāmatā]]---opposition.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa is equal to everyone in His general dealings, but due to the conflicting ecstatic love of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, there were opposing elements.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.111
description: " 'The progress of loving affairs between a young boy and a young girl is like the movement of a snake. On account of this, two types of anger arise between a young boy and girl-anger with cause and anger without cause.'
text:
> aher iva gatiḥ premṇaḥ
> svabhāva-kuṭilā bhavet
> ato hetor ahetoś ca
> yūnor māna udañcati
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aheḥ]]---of the snake; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:g:gatiḥ]]---the movement; [[synonyms:p:premṇaḥ]]---of the loving affairs; [[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---by nature; [[synonyms:k:kuṭilā]]---crooked; [[synonyms:b:bhavet]]---is; [[synonyms:a:ataḥ]]---therefore; [[synonyms:h:hetoḥ]]---from some cause; [[synonyms:a:ahetoḥ]]---from the absence of a cause; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:y:yūnoḥ]]---of the young couple; [[synonyms:m:mānaḥ]]---anger; [[synonyms:u:udañcati]]---appears.
translation: “ 'The progress of loving affairs between a young boy and a young girl is like the movement of a snake. On account of this, two types of anger arise between a young boy and girl-anger with cause and anger without cause.'
purport: During the //rāsa// dance, one form of Kṛṣṇa was between every two //gopīs.// But by the side of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī there was only one Kṛṣṇa. Although this was the case, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī still manifested disagreement with Kṛṣṇa. This verse is from the //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi// (//Śṛṅgāra-bheda-kathana// 102), written by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.112
description: "When Rādhārāṇī left the rāsa dance out of anger and resentment, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa became very anxious because He could not see Her.
text:
> krodha kari' rāsa chāḍi' gelā māna kari'
> tāṅre nā dekhiyā vyākula haila śrī-hari

translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "After hearing about your glories, I have come to your place. But you are offering Me words of praise out of respect for a sannyāsī, one in the renounced order of life.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura explains that a mundane person, being enriched by mundane opulences, must always know that the transcendental opulences of the advanced devotees are far more important than the materialistic opulences of a person like himself. A materialistic person with material opulences should not be very proud or puffed up before a transcendental devotee. If one approaches a transcendental devotee on the strength of one's material heritage, opulence, education and beauty and does not offer respect to the advanced devotee of the Lord, the Vaiṣṇava devotee may offer formal respects to such a materially puffed-up person, but he may not deliver transcendental knowledge to him. Indeed, the devotee sees him as a non-//brāhmaṇa// or //śūdra.// Such a puffed-up person cannot understand the science of Kṛṣṇa. A proud person is deceived in transcendental life and, despite having attained a human form, will again glide into hellish conditions. By His personal example, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu explains how one should be submissive and humble before a Vaiṣṇava, even though one may be situated on a high platform. Such is the teaching of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as the //ācārya// of the world, the supreme spiritual master and teacher.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.128
description: "Whether one is a brāhmaṇa, a sannyāsī or a śūdra-regardless of what he is-he can become a spiritual master if he knows the science of Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> kibā vipra, kibā nyāsī, śūdra kene naya
> yei kṛṣṇa-tattva-vettā, sei 'guru' haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---whether; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---whether; [[synonyms:n:nyāsī]]---a //sannyāsī//; [[synonyms:ś:śūdra]]---a //śūdra//; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:n:naya]]---not; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:t:tattva]]-[[synonyms:v:vettā]]---a knower of the science of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that person; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---the spiritual master; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is.
translation: "Whether one is a brāhmaṇa, a sannyāsī or a śūdra-regardless of what he is-he can become a spiritual master if he knows the science of Kṛṣṇa."
purport:
This verse is very important to the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. In his //Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya,// Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains that one should not think that because Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was born a //brāhmaṇa// and was situated in the topmost spiritual order as a //sannyāsī,// it was improper for Him to receive instructions from Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya, who belonged to the //śūdra// caste. To clarify this matter, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu informed Rāmānanda Rāya that knowledge of Kṛṣṇa consciousness is more important than caste. In the system of //varṇāśrama-dharma// there are various duties for the //brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas// and //śūdras.// Actually the //brāhmaṇa// is supposed to be the spiritual master of all other //varṇas,// or sects, but as far as Kṛṣṇa consciousness is concerned, everyone is capable of becoming a spiritual master because knowledge in Kṛṣṇa consciousness is on the platform of the spirit soul. To spread Kṛṣṇa consciousness, one need only be cognizant of the science of the spirit soul. It does not matter whether one is a //brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya, śūdra, sannyāsī, gṛhastha// or whatever. If one simply understands this science, he can become a spiritual master.

It is stated in the //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa// that one should not accept initiation from a person who is not in the brahminical order if there is a fit person in the brahminical order present. This instruction is meant for those who are overly dependent on the mundane social order and is suitable for those who want to remain in mundane life. If one understands the truth of Kṛṣṇa consciousness and seriously desires to attain transcendental knowledge for the perfection of life, he can accept a spiritual master from any social status, provided the spiritual master is fully conversant with the science of Kṛṣṇa. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura also states that although one is situated as a //brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya, śūdra, brahmacārī, vānaprastha, gṛhastha// or //sannyāsī,// if he is conversant in the science of Kṛṣṇa he can become a spiritual master as //vartma-pradarśaka-guru, dīkṣā-guru// or //śikṣā-guru.// The spiritual master who first gives information about spiritual life is called the //vartma-pradarśaka-guru,// the spiritual master who initiates according to the regulations of the //śāstras// is called the //dīkṣā-guru,// and the spiritual master who gives instructions for elevation is called the //śikṣā-guru.// Factually the qualifications of a spiritual master depend on his knowledge of the science of Kṛṣṇa. It does not matter whether he is a //brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, sannyāsī// or //śūdra.// This injunction given by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is not at all against the injunctions of the //śāstras.// In the //Padma Purāṇa// it is said:

> na śūdrāḥ bhagavad-bhaktās
> te 'pi bhāgavatottamāḥ
> sarva-varṇeṣu te śūdrā
> ye na bhaktā janārdane

One who is actually advanced in spiritual knowledge of Kṛṣṇa is never a //śūdra,// even though he may have been born in a //śūdra// family. However, even if a //vipra,// or //brāhmaṇa,// is very expert in the six brahminical activities (//paṭhana, pāṭhana, yajana, yājana, dāna, pratigraha//) and is also well versed in the Vedic hymns, he cannot become a spiritual master unless he is a Vaiṣṇava. But if one is born in the family of //caṇḍālas// yet is well versed in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, he can become a //guru.// These are the śāstric injunctions, and strictly following these injunctions, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, as a //gṛhastha// named Śrī Viśvambhara, was initiated by a //sannyāsī-guru// named Īśvara Purī. Similarly, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu was initiated by Mādhavendra Purī, a //sannyāsī.// According to others, however, He was initiated by Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha. Advaita Ācārya, although a //gṛhastha,// was initiated by Mādhavendra Purī, and Śrī Rasikānanda, although born in a //brāhmaṇa// family, was initiated by Śrī Śyāmānanda Prabhu, who was not born in a caste //brāhmaṇa// family. There are many instances in which a born //brāhmaṇa// took initiation from a person who was not born in a //brāhmaṇa// family. The brahminical symptoms are explained in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:7:11:35|(7.11.35)]], wherein it is stated:

> yasya yal-lakṣaṇaṁ proktaṁ
> puṁso varṇābhivyañjakam
> yad anyatrāpi dṛśyeta
> tat tenaiva vinirdiśet

If a person is born in a //śūdra// family but has all the qualities of a spiritual master, he should be accepted not only as a //brāhmaṇa// but as a qualified spiritual master also. This is also the instruction of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura therefore introduced the sacred thread ceremony for all Vaiṣṇavas according to the rules and regulations.

Sometimes a Vaiṣṇava who is a //bhajanānandī// does not take the //sāvitra-saṁskāra// (sacred thread initiation), but this does not mean that this system should be used for preaching work. There are two kinds of Vaiṣṇavas-//bhajanānandī// and //goṣṭhy-ānandī. A bhajanānandī// is not interested in preaching work, but a //goṣṭhy-ānandī// is interested in spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness to benefit the people and increase the number of Vaiṣṇavas. A Vaiṣṇava is understood to be above the position of a //brāhmaṇa.// As a preacher, he should be recognized as a //brāhmaṇa;// otherwise there may be a misunderstanding of his position as a Vaiṣṇava. However, a Vaiṣṇava //brāhmaṇa// is not selected on the basis of his birth but according to his qualities. Unfortunately, those who are unintelligent do not know the difference between a //brāhmaṇa// and a Vaiṣṇava. They are under the impression that unless one is a //brāhmaṇa// he cannot be a spiritual master. For this reason only, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu makes the statement in this verse:

> kibā vipra, kibā nyāsī, śūdra kene naya
> yei kṛṣṇa-tattva-vettā, sei 'guru' haya

If one becomes a //guru,// he is automatically a //brāhmaṇa.// Sometimes a caste //guru// says that //ye kṛṣṇa-tattva-vettā, sei guru haya// means that one who is not a //brāhmaṇa// may become a //śikṣā-guru// or a //vartma-pradarśaka-guru// but not an initiator //guru.// According to such caste //gurus,// birth and family ties are considered foremost. However, the hereditary consideration is not acceptable to Vaiṣṇavas. The word //guru// is equally applicable to the //vartma-pradarśaka-guru, śikṣā-guru// and //dīkṣā-guru.// Unless we accept the principle enunciated by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement cannot spread all over the world. According to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's intentions: //pṛthivīte āche yata nagarādi-grāma sarvatra pracāra haibe mora nāma.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's cult must be preached all over the world. This does not mean that people should take to His teachings and remain //śūdras// or //caṇḍālas.// As soon as one is trained as a pure Vaiṣṇava, he must be accepted as a bona fide //brāhmaṇa.// This is the essence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's instructions in this verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.129

> 'sannyāsī' baliyā more nā kariha vañcana
> kṛṣṇa-rādhā-tattva kahi' pūrṇa kara mana

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.13

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.130-131
description: Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya was a great devotee of the Lord and a lover of God, and although his mind could not be covered by Kṛṣṇa's illusory energy, and although he could understand the mind of the Lord, which was very strong and intense, Rāmānanda's mind became a little agitated.
text:
> yadyapi rāya---premī, mahā-bhāgavate
> tāṅra mana kṛṣṇa-māyā nāre ācchādite
>
> tathāpi prabhura icchā---parama prabala
> jānileha rāyera mana haila ṭalamala
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:p:premī]]---a great lover of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavate]]---a topmost devotee; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:māyā]]---the illusory energy of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---not able; [[synonyms:ā:ācchādite]]---to cover; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---the Lord's desire; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:p:prabala]]---very intense; [[synonyms:j:jānileha]]---even though it was known; [[synonyms:r:rāyera]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind of Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭalamala]]---agitation.
translation: Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya was a great devotee of the Lord and a lover of God, and although his mind could not be covered by Kṛṣṇa's illusory energy, and although he could understand the mind of the Lord, which was very strong and intense, Rāmānanda's mind became a little agitated.
purport: The perfect devotee always acts according to the desires of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. But a materialistic man is carried away by the waves of the material energy. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has said, //māyāra vaśe, yāccha bhese', khāccha hābuḍubu, bhāi.//  A person under the grip of the material energy is carried away by the waves of that illusory energy. In other words, a person in the material world is a servant of //māyā.// However, a person in the spiritual energy is a servant of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although Rāmānanda Rāya knew that nothing was unknown to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he nonetheless began to speak further on the subject because the Lord desired it.
