title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.92
description: "In Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam [10.32.22] it is said that Lord Kṛṣṇa cannot proportionately reciprocate devotional service in the mādhurya-rasa; therefore He always remains a debtor to such devotees.
text:
> ei 'preme'ra anurūpa nā pāre bhajite
> ataeva 'ṛṇī' haya---kahe bhāgavate
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:p:premera]]---of love of God; [[synonyms:a:anurūpa]]---exactly to the proportion; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---is able; [[synonyms:b:bhajite]]---to reciprocate; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṇī]]---debtor; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---is stated; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavate]]---in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.//
translation: "In Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam [10.32.22] it is said that Lord Kṛṣṇa cannot proportionately reciprocate devotional service in the mādhurya-rasa; therefore He always remains a debtor to such devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.93
description: "When the gopīs were overwhelmed with dissatisfaction due to Lord Kṛṣṇa's absence from the rāsa-līlā, Kṛṣṇa returned to them and told them, 'My dear gopīs, our meeting is certainly free from all material contamination. I must admit that in many lives it would be impossible for Me to repay My debt to you because you have cut off the bondage of family life just to search for Me. Consequently I am unable to repay you. Therefore please be satisfied with your honest activities in this regard.'
text:
> na pāraye 'haṁ niravadya-saṁyujāṁ
> sva-sādhu-kṛtyaṁ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ
> yā mābhajan durjara-geha-śṛṅkhalāḥ
> saṁvṛścya tad vaḥ pratiyātu sādhunā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāraye]]---am able; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:n:niravadya]]---without duplicity; [[synonyms:s:saṁyujām]]---meeting; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛtyam]]---your own honest activities; [[synonyms:v:vibudha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āyuṣā]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---even with a duration of life like that of the demigods; [[synonyms:v:vaḥ]]---you; [[synonyms:y:yā]]---who; [[synonyms:m:mā]]---Me; [[synonyms:a:abhajan]]---have worshiped; [[synonyms:d:durjara]]---difficult to surmount; [[synonyms:g:geha]]---of household life; [[synonyms:ś:śṛṅkhalāḥ]]---the chains; [[synonyms:s:saṁvṛścya]]---cutting off; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vaḥ]]---your; [[synonyms:p:pratiyātu]]---let there be a return; [[synonyms:s:sādhunā]]---by pious activities.
translation: "When the gopīs were overwhelmed with dissatisfaction due to Lord Kṛṣṇa's absence from the rāsa-līlā, Kṛṣṇa returned to them and told them, 'My dear gopīs, our meeting is certainly free from all material contamination. I must admit that in many lives it would be impossible for Me to repay My debt to you because you have cut off the bondage of family life just to search for Me. Consequently I am unable to repay you. Therefore please be satisfied with your honest activities in this regard.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.94
description: "Although Kṛṣṇa's unparalleled beauty is the topmost sweetness of love of Godhead, His sweetness increases unlimitedly when He is in the company of the gopīs. Consequently Kṛṣṇa's exchange of love with the gopīs is the topmost perfection of love of Godhead.
text:
> yadyapi kṛṣṇa-saundarya---mādhuryera dhurya
> vraja-devīra saṅge tāṅra bāḍaye mādhurya
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saundarya]]---the beauty of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mādhuryera]]---of sweetness; [[synonyms:d:dhurya]]---the supermost; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:d:devīra]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in company with; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:b:bāḍaye]]---increases; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---the sweetness.
translation: "Although Kṛṣṇa's unparalleled beauty is the topmost sweetness of love of Godhead, His sweetness increases unlimitedly when He is in the company of the gopīs. Consequently Kṛṣṇa's exchange of love with the gopīs is the topmost perfection of love of Godhead.
purport: Kṛṣṇa and His devotees become perfectly intimate in conjugal love of Godhead. In other mellows, the Lord and the devotees do not enjoy transcendental bliss as perfectly. The next verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.33.6) will illustrate this verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.95
description: " 'Although the son of Devakī, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is also the reservoir of all kinds of beauty, when He is among the gopīs He nonetheless becomes more beautiful, for He resembles a mārakata jewel surrounded by gold and other jewels.' "
text:
> tatrātiśuśubhe tābhir
> bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ
> madhye maṇīnāṁ haimānāṁ
> mahā-marakato yathā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tatra]]---there; [[synonyms:a:ati]]-[[synonyms:ś:śuśubhe]]---was very beautiful; [[synonyms:t:tābhiḥ]]---by them; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:d:devakī]]-[[synonyms:s:sutaḥ]]---son of Devakī; [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in the midst; [[synonyms:m:maṇīnām]]---of valuable jewels; [[synonyms:h:haimānām]]---lined with gold; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:m:marakataḥ]]---the jewel of the name //marakata//; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as.
translation: “ 'Although the son of Devakī, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is also the reservoir of all kinds of beauty, when He is among the gopīs He nonetheless becomes more beautiful, for He resembles a mārakata jewel surrounded by gold and other jewels.' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.96
description: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "This is certainly the limit of perfection, but please be merciful to Me and speak more if there is more."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---ei 'sādhyāvadhi' suniścaya
> kṛpā kari' kaha, yadi āge kichu haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:sādhya]]-[[synonyms:a:avadhi]]---the highest limit of perfection; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---being merciful to Me; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please speak; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---further; [[synonyms:k:kichu]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is something.
translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "This is certainly the limit of perfection, but please be merciful to Me and speak more if there is more."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.97
description: Rāya Rāmānanda replied, "Until this day I did not know anyone within this material world who could inquire beyond this perfectional stage of devotional service.
text:
> rāya kahe,---īhāra āge puche hena jane
> eta-dina nāhi jāni, āchaye bhuvane
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Rāmānanda Rāya replied; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]] [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---beyond this point; [[synonyms:p:puche]]---inquires; [[synonyms:h:hena]]---such; [[synonyms:j:jane]]---a person; [[synonyms:e:eta]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---until this day; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I did not know; [[synonyms:ā:āchaye]]---there is; [[synonyms:b:bhuvane]]---within this material world.
translation: Rāya Rāmānanda replied, "Until this day I did not know anyone within this material world who could inquire beyond this perfectional stage of devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.98
description: "Among the loving affairs of the gopīs," Rāmānanda Rāya continued, "Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's love for Śrī Kṛṣṇa is topmost. Indeed, the glories of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī are highly esteemed in all revealed scriptures.
text:
> iṅhāra madhye rādhāra prema---'sādhya-śiromaṇi'
> yāṅhāra mahimā sarva-śāstrete vākhāni
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---among the loving affairs of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:r:rādhāra]] [[synonyms:p:prema]]---the love of Godhead of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:s:sādhya]]-[[synonyms:ś:śiromaṇi]]---the topmost perfection; [[synonyms:y:yāṅhāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---the glorification; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstrete]]---in every scripture; [[synonyms:v:vākhāni]]---description.
translation: "Among the loving affairs of the gopīs," Rāmānanda Rāya continued, "Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's love for Śrī Kṛṣṇa is topmost. Indeed, the glories of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī are highly esteemed in all revealed scriptures.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.99
description: " 'Just as Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is most dear to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Her bathing place known [Rādhā-kuṇḍa] is also dear to Him. Among all the gopīs, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is supermost and very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa.'
text:
> yathā rādhā priyā viṣṇos
> tasyāḥ kuṇḍaṁ priyaṁ tathā
> sarva-gopīṣu saivaikā
> viṣṇor atyanta-vallabhā
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---just as; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:p:priyā]]---very dear; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇoḥ]]---to Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tasyāḥ]]---Her; [[synonyms:k:kuṇḍam]]---bathing place; [[synonyms:p:priyam]]---very dear; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---so also; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:g:gopīṣu]]---among all the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:s:sā]]---She; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:e:ekā]]---alone; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇoḥ]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:atyanta]]-[[synonyms:v:vallabhā]]---very dear.
translation: “ 'Just as Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is most dear to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Her bathing place known [Rādhā-kuṇḍa] is also dear to Him. Among all the gopīs, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is supermost and very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa.'
purport: This verse is from the //Padma Purāṇa// and is included in the //Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta// (2.1.45), by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. It also appears in //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Four, verse 215, and again in //Madhya-līlā,// Chapter Eighteen, verse 8.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.1
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu converted the inhabitants of South India. These people were as strong as elephants, but they were in the clutches of the crocodiles of various philosophies, such as the Buddhist, Jain and Māyāvāda philosophies. With His disc of mercy the Lord delivered them all by converting them into Vaiṣṇavas, devotees of the Lord.
text:
> nānā-mata-grāha-grastān
> dākṣiṇātya-jana-dvipān
> kṛpāriṇā vimucyaitān
> gauraś cakre sa vaiṣṇavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---by various philosophies; [[synonyms:g:grāha]]---like crocodiles; [[synonyms:g:grastān]]---captured; [[synonyms:d:dākṣiṇātya]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---the inhabitants of South India; [[synonyms:d:dvipān]]---like elephants; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:a:ariṇā]]---by His disc of mercy; [[synonyms:v:vimucya]]---liberating; [[synonyms:e:etān]]---all these; [[synonyms:g:gauraḥ]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cakre]]---converted; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavān]]---to the Vaiṣṇava cult.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu converted the inhabitants of South India. These people were as strong as elephants, but they were in the clutches of the crocodiles of various philosophies, such as the Buddhist, Jain and Māyāvāda philosophies. With His disc of mercy the Lord delivered them all by converting them into Vaiṣṇavas, devotees of the Lord.
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's converting the people of South India into Vaiṣṇavas is compared herein to Lord Viṣṇu's delivering Gajendra the elephant from the attack of a crocodile. When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited southern India, almost all the residents were within the jaws of the crocodiles of Buddhist, Jain and Māyāvāda philosophy. Here Kavirāja Gosvāmī states that although these people were as strong as elephants, they were almost in the clutches of death because they were being attacked by the crocodiles of various philosophies. However, as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in the form of Viṣṇu mercifully saved the elephant Gajendra from the clutches of a crocodile, so He saved all the people of South India from the clutches of various philosophies by converting them into Vaiṣṇavas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.10
description: By the influence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all these people abandoned their own opinions and became Vaiṣṇavas, devotees of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> sei saba loka prabhura darśana-prabhāve
> nija-nija-mata chāḍi' ha-ila vaiṣṇave
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all those people; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhāve]]---by the influence of His visit; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:n:nija]]---their own; [[synonyms:m:mata]]---opinion; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇave]]---devotees.
translation: By the influence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all these people abandoned their own opinions and became Vaiṣṇavas, devotees of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.100
description: "While seeing Lord Kṛṣṇa sitting in a chariot and instructing Arjuna, I am filled with ecstatic happiness.
text:
> arjunere kahitechena hita-upadeśa
> tāṅre dekhi' haya mora ānanda-āveśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:arjunere]]---unto Arjuna; [[synonyms:k:kahitechena]]---He is speaking; [[synonyms:h:hita]]-[[synonyms:u:upadeśa]]---good instruction; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---transcendental happiness; [[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---ecstasy.
translation: "While seeing Lord Kṛṣṇa sitting in a chariot and instructing Arjuna, I am filled with ecstatic happiness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.101
description: "As long as I read the Bhagavad-gītā, I simply see the Lord's beautiful features. It is for this reason that I am reading the Bhagavad-gītā, and my mind cannot be distracted from this."
text:
> yāvat paḍoṅ, tāvat pāṅa tāṅra daraśana
> ei lāgi' gītā-pāṭha nā chāḍe mora mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāvat]]---as long as; [[synonyms:p:paḍoṅ]]---I read; [[synonyms:t:tāvat]]---so long; [[synonyms:p:pāṅa]]---I get; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---audience; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for this reason; [[synonyms:g:gītā]]-[[synonyms:p:pāṭha]]---reading the //Bhagavad-gītā//; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍe]]---does not quit; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---my mind.
translation: "As long as I read the Bhagavad-gītā, I simply see the Lord's beautiful features. It is for this reason that I am reading the Bhagavad-gītā, and my mind cannot be distracted from this."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.102
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told the brāhmaṇa, "Indeed, you are an authority in the reading of the Bhagavad-gītā. Whatever you know constitutes the real purport of the Bhagavad-gītā."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---gītā-pāṭhe tomārā-i adhikāra
> tumi se jānaha ei gītāra artha-sāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord replied; [[synonyms:g:gītā]]-[[synonyms:p:pāṭhe]]---in reading the //Bhagavad-gītā//; [[synonyms:t:tomārāi]] [[synonyms:a:adhikāra]]---you have the proper authority; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:j:jānaha]]---know; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:g:gītāra]]---of the //Bhagavad-gītā//; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the real purport.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told the brāhmaṇa, "Indeed, you are an authority in the reading of the Bhagavad-gītā. Whatever you know constitutes the real purport of the Bhagavad-gītā."
purport:
According to the //śāstras:bhaktyā bhāgavataṁ grāhyaṁ na buddhyā na ca ṭīkayā.// One should understand the //Bhagavad-gītā// and //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// by hearing them from a real devotee. One cannot understand them simply by erudite scholarship or sharp intelligence. It is also said:

> gītādhītā ca yenāpi
> bhakti-bhāvena cetasā
> veda-śāstra-purāṇāni
> tenādhītāni sarvaśaḥ

To one who reads the //Bhagavad-gītā// with faith and devotion, the essence of Vedic knowledge is revealed. And according to the //Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad// (6.23):

> yasya deve parā bhaktir
> yathā deve tathā gurau
> tasyaite kathitā hy arthāḥ
> prakāśante mahātmanaḥ

All Vedic scriptures are to be understood with faith and devotion, not by mundane scholarship. We therefore present the //Bhagavad-gītā As It Is.// There are many so-called scholars and philosophers who read the //Bhagavad-gītā// in a scholarly way. They simply waste their time and mislead those who read their commentaries.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.103
description: After saying this, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced the brāhmaṇa, and the brāhmaṇa, catching the lotus feet of the Lord, began to cry.
text:
> eta bali' sei vipre kaila āliṅgana
> prabhu-pada dhari' vipra karena rodana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipre]]---that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---He embraced; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]---the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:r:rodana]]---crying.
translation: After saying this, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced the brāhmaṇa, and the brāhmaṇa, catching the lotus feet of the Lord, began to cry.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.104
description: The brāhmaṇa said, "Upon seeing You, my happiness is doubled. I take it that You are the same Lord Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> tomā dekhi' tāhā haite dvi-guṇa sukha haya
> sei kṛṣṇa tumi,---hena mora mane laya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---by seeing You; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---than the vision of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---twice as much; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---that Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You are; [[synonyms:h:hena]]---such; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:l:laya]]---takes.
translation: The brāhmaṇa said, "Upon seeing You, my happiness is doubled. I take it that You are the same Lord Kṛṣṇa."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.105
description: The mind of the brāhmaṇa was purified by the revelation of Lord Kṛṣṇa, and therefore he could understand the truth of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in all details.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-sphūrtye tāṅra mana hañāche nirmala
> ataeva prabhura tattva jānila sakala
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sphūrtye]]---by revelation of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:h:hañāche]]---did become; [[synonyms:n:nirmala]]---purified; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]---truth; [[synonyms:j:jānila]]---could understand; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all.
translation: The mind of the brāhmaṇa was purified by the revelation of Lord Kṛṣṇa, and therefore he could understand the truth of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in all details.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.106
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then taught the brāhmaṇa very thoroughly and requested him not to disclose the fact that He was Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself.
text:
> tabe mahāprabhu tāṅre karāila śikṣaṇa
> ei bāt kāhāṅ nā kariha prakāśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---made; [[synonyms:ś:śikṣaṇa]]---instruction; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:b:bāt]]---this version; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---anywhere; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---do not; [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do; [[synonyms:p:prakāśana]]---revelation.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then taught the brāhmaṇa very thoroughly and requested him not to disclose the fact that He was Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.107
description: That brāhmaṇa became a great devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and for four continuous months he did not give up the Lord's company.
text:
> sei vipra mahāprabhura baḍa bhakta haila
> cāri māsa prabhu-saṅga kabhu nā chāḍila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:seivipra]]---that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---big; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotee; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:m:māsa]]---for four months; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---association of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---at any time; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---did not; [[synonyms:c:chāḍila]]---give up.
translation: That brāhmaṇa became a great devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and for four continuous months he did not give up the Lord's company.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.108
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained at the house of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa and constantly talked with him about Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way He was very happy.
text:
> ei-mata bhaṭṭa-gṛhe rahe gauracandra
> nirantara bhaṭṭa-saṅge kṛṣṇa-kathānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]-[[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---in the house of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remained; [[synonyms:g:gauracandra]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---constantly; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---the transcendental bliss of talking about Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained at the house of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa and constantly talked with him about Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way He was very happy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.109
description: Being a Vaiṣṇava in the Rāmānuja-sampradāya, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa worshiped the Deities of Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa. Seeing his pure devotion, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very much satisfied.
text:
> śrī-vaiṣṇava' bhaṭṭa seve lakṣmī-nārāyaṇa
> tāṅra bhakti dekhi' prabhura tuṣṭa haila mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---a devotee of the Rāmānuja-sampradāya; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:s:seve]]---used to worship; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]-[[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---the Deities of Lord Nārāyaṇa and the goddess of fortune, Lakṣmī; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotion; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tuṣṭa]]---happy; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: Being a Vaiṣṇava in the Rāmānuja-sampradāya, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa worshiped the Deities of Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa. Seeing his pure devotion, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very much satisfied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.11
description: At the time, all the South Indian Vaiṣṇavas were worshipers of Lord Rāmacandra. Some were Tattvavādīs, and some were followers of Rāmānujācārya.
text:
> vaiṣṇavera madhye rāma-upāsaka saba
> keha 'tattvavādī', keha haya 'śrī-vaiṣṇava'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---amongst Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:u:upāsaka]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all worshipers of Lord Śrī Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]-[[synonyms:v:vādī]]---followers of Madhvācārya; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotees following the disciplic succession of Śrī Rāmānujācārya
translation: At the time, all the South Indian Vaiṣṇavas were worshipers of Lord Rāmacandra. Some were Tattvavādīs, and some were followers of Rāmānujācārya.
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura points out that the word "Tattvavādī" refers to the followers of Śrīla Madhvācārya. To distinguish his disciplic succession from the Māyāvādī followers of Śaṅkarācārya, Śrīla Madhvācārya named his party the Tattvavādīs. Impersonal monists are always attacked by these Tattvavādīs, who attempt to defeat their philosophy of impersonalism. Generally, they establish the supremacy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Actually the disciplic succession of Madhvācārya is known as the Brahmā Vaiṣṇava sect; that is the sect coming down from Lord Brahmā. Consequently the Tattvavādīs, or followers of Madhvācārya, do not accept the incident of Lord Brahmā's illusion, which is recorded in the Tenth Canto of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.// Śrīla Madhvācārya has purposefully avoided commenting on that portion of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// in which //brahma-mohana,// the illusion of Lord Brahmā, is mentioned. Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī was one of the //ācāryas// in the Tattvavāda disciplic succession, and he established the ultimate goal of transcendentalism to be attainment of pure devotional service, love of Godhead. Those Vaiṣṇavas belonging to the Gauḍīya-sampradāya, the disciplic succession following Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, are distinct from the Tattvavādīs, although they belong to the same Tattvavāda-sampradāya. The followers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are therefore known as the Madhva-Gauḍīya-sampradāya.

The word //pāṣaṇḍī// refers to those who are opposed to pure devotional service. In particular, these are the Māyāvādīs, the impersonalists. A definition of //pāṣaṇḍī// is given in the //Hari-bhakti-vilāsa// (1.73), wherein it is stated:

> yas tu nārāyaṇaṁ devaṁ
> brahma-rudrādi-daivataiḥ
> samatvenaiva vīkṣeta
> sa pāṣaṇḍī bhaved dhruvam

A //pāṣaṇḍī// is one who thinks that the Supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa, the Personality of Godhead, is on the same level with the demigods, headed by Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva. The devotee never considers Lord Nārāyaṇa to be on the same platform with Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva. The Madhvācārya-sampradāya and Rāmānuja-sampradāya are mainly worshipers of Lord Rāmacandra, although the Śrī Vaiṣṇavas are supposed to be worshipers of Lord Nārāyaṇa and Lakṣmī and the Tattvavādīs are supposed to be worshipers of Lord Kṛṣṇa. At present, in most of the monasteries belonging to the Madhva-sampradāya, Lord Rāmacandra is worshiped.

In the book known as //Adhyātma-rāmāyaṇa,// there are statements in Chapters Twelve to Fifteen about the worship of the Deities Śrī Rāmacandra and Sītā. There it is stated that during Lord Rāmacandra's time there was a //brāhmaṇa// who took a vow to fast until he saw Lord Rāmacandra. Sometimes, due to business, Lord Rāmacandra was absent from His capital for a full week and could not be seen by citizens during that time. Because of his vow, the //brāhmaṇa// could not take even a drop of water during that week. Later, after eight or nine days, when the //brāhmaṇa// could see Lord Rāmacandra personally, he would break his fast. Upon observing the //brāhmaṇa's// rigid vow, Lord Śrī Rāmacandra ordered His younger brother Lakṣmaṇa to deliver a pair of Sītā-Rāma Deities to the //brāhmaṇa.// The //brāhmaṇa// received the Deities from Śrī Lakṣmaṇajī and worshiped Them faithfully as long as he lived. At the time of his death, he delivered the Deities to Śrī Hanumānjī, who, for many years, hung Them around his neck and served Them with all devotion. After many years, when Hanumānjī departed on the hill known as Gandha-mādana, he delivered the Deities to Bhīmasena, one of the Pāṇḍavas, and Bhīmasena brought Them to his palace, where he kept Them very carefully. The last king of the Pāṇḍavas, Kṣemakānta, worshiped the Deities in that palace. Later, the same Deities were kept in the custody of the kings of Orissa known as Gajapatis. One of the //ācāryas,// known as Narahari Tīrtha, who was in the disciplic succession of Madhvācārya, received these Deities from the King of Orissa.

It may be noted that these particular Deities of Rāma and Sītā have been worshiped from the time of King Ikṣvāku. Indeed, they were worshiped by the royal princes even before the appearance of Lord Rāmacandra. Later, during Lord Rāmacandra's presence, the Deities were worshiped by Lakṣmaṇa. It is said that just three months before his disappearance, Śrī Madhvācārya received these Deities and installed them in the Uḍupī temple. Since then the Deities have been worshiped by the Madhvācārya-sampradāya at that monastery. As far as the Śrī Vaiṣṇavas are concerned, beginning with Rāmānujācārya, they also worshiped Deities of Sītā-Rāma. Sītā-Rāma Deities are also being worshiped in Tirupati and other places. From the Śrī Rāmānuja-sampradāya there is another branch known as Rāmānandī or Rāmāt, and the followers of that branch also worship Deities of Sītā-Rāma very rigidly. The Rāmānuja-sampradāya Vaiṣṇavas prefer the worship of Lord Rāmacandra to that of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.110
description: Constantly associating with each other, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa gradually developed a friendly relationship. Indeed, sometimes they laughed and joked together.
text:
> nirantara tāṅra saṅge haila sakhya-bhāva
> hāsya-parihāse duṅhe sakhyera svabhāva
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---constantly; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---being associated with him; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:s:sakhya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---a friendly relationship; [[synonyms:h:hāsya]]---laughing; [[synonyms:p:parihāse]]---joking; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:s:sakhyera]]---of fraternity; [[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---nature.
translation: Constantly associating with each other, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa gradually developed a friendly relationship. Indeed, sometimes they laughed and joked together.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.111
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told the Bhaṭṭācārya, "Your worshipable goddess of fortune, Lakṣmī, always remains on the chest of Nārāyaṇa, and she is certainly the most chaste woman in the creation.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---bhaṭṭa, tomāra lakṣmī-ṭhākurāṇī
> kānta-vakṣaḥ-sthitā, pativratā-śiromaṇi
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---My dear Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākurāṇī]]---goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:k:kānta]]---of her husband, Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:v:vakṣaḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:sthitā]]---situated on the chest; [[synonyms:p:pati]]-[[synonyms:v:vratā]]---chaste woman; [[synonyms:ś:śiromaṇi]]---the topmost.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told the Bhaṭṭācārya, "Your worshipable goddess of fortune, Lakṣmī, always remains on the chest of Nārāyaṇa, and she is certainly the most chaste woman in the creation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.112
description: "However, my Lord is Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, a cowherd boy who is engaged in tending cows. Why is it that Lakṣmī, being such a chaste wife, wants to associate with My Lord?
text:
> āmāra ṭhākura kṛṣṇa---gopa, go-cāraka
> sādhvī hañā kene cāhe tāṅhāra saṅgama
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---My worshipable Deity; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]---cowherd; [[synonyms:g:go]]-[[synonyms:c:cāraka]]---a tender of cows; [[synonyms:s:sādhvī]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being so chaste; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:c:cāhe]]---wants; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---His; [[synonyms:s:saṅgama]]---association.
translation: "However, my Lord is Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, a cowherd boy who is engaged in tending cows. Why is it that Lakṣmī, being such a chaste wife, wants to associate with My Lord?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.113
description: "Just to associate with Kṛṣṇa, Lakṣmī abandoned all transcendental happiness in Vaikuṇṭha and for a long time accepted vows and regulative principles and performed unlimited austerities."
text:
> ei lāgi' sukha-bhoga chāḍi' cira-kāla
> vrata-niyama kari' tapa karila apāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for this reason; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---the enjoyment of Vaikuṇṭha; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:c:cira]]-[[synonyms:k:kāla]]---for a long time; [[synonyms:v:vrata]]-[[synonyms:n:niyama]]---vows and regulative principles; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:t:tapa]]---austerity; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---performed unlimitedly.
translation: "Just to associate with Kṛṣṇa, Lakṣmī abandoned all transcendental happiness in Vaikuṇṭha and for a long time accepted vows and regulative principles and performed unlimited austerities."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.114
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, " 'O Lord, we do not know how the serpent Kāliya attained such an opportunity to be touched by the dust of Your lotus feet. Even the goddess of fortune, for this end, performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and observing austere vows. Indeed, we do not know how the serpent Kāliya got such an opportunity."'
text:
> kasyānubhāvo 'sya na deva vidmahe
> tavāṅghri-reṇu-sparaśādhikāraḥ
> yad-vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo
> vihāya kāmān su-ciraṁ dhṛta-vratā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kasya]]---of what; [[synonyms:a:anubhāvaḥ]]---a result; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of the serpent (Kāliya); [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:d:deva]]---O Lord; [[synonyms:v:vidmahe]]---we know; [[synonyms:t:tava]] [[synonyms:a:aṅghri]]---of Your lotus feet; [[synonyms:r:reṇu]]---of the dust; [[synonyms:s:sparaśa]]---for touching; [[synonyms:a:adhikāraḥ]]---qualification; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:v:vāñchayā]]---by desiring; [[synonyms:ś:śrīḥ]]---the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:l:lalanā]]---the topmost woman; [[synonyms:a:acarat]]---performed; [[synonyms:t:tapaḥ]]---austerity; [[synonyms:v:vihāya]]---giving up; [[synonyms:k:kāmān]]---all desires; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:c:ciram]]---for a long time; [[synonyms:d:dhṛta]]---a law upheld; [[synonyms:v:vratā]]---as a vow.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, " 'O Lord, we do not know how the serpent Kāliya attained such an opportunity to be touched by the dust of Your lotus feet. Even the goddess of fortune, for this end, performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and observing austere vows. Indeed, we do not know how the serpent Kāliya got such an opportunity."'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.16.36); it was spoken by the wives of the Kāliya serpent.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.115
description: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa then said, "Lord Kṛṣṇa and Lord Nārāyaṇa are one and the same, but the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa are more relishable due to their sportive nature.
text:
> bhaṭṭa kahe, kṛṣṇa-nārāyaṇa---eka-i svarūpa
> kṛṣṇete adhika līlā-vaidagdhyādi-rūpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa said; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:i:i]] [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---one and the same; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇete]]---in Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:adhika]]---more; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:v:vaidagdhya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---sportive nature.
translation: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa then said, "Lord Kṛṣṇa and Lord Nārāyaṇa are one and the same, but the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa are more relishable due to their sportive nature.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.116
description: "Since Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa are the same personality, Lakṣmī's association with Kṛṣṇa does not break her vow of chastity. Rather, it was in great fun that the goddess of fortune wanted to associate with Lord Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> tāra sparśe nāhi yāya pativratā-dharma
> kautuke lakṣmī cāhena kṛṣṇera saṅgama
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:s:sparśe]]---by the touching of Kṛṣṇa by Lakṣmī; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---does not; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---disappear; [[synonyms:p:pati]]-[[synonyms:v:vratā]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---the vow of chastity; [[synonyms:k:kautuke]]---in great fun; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:c:cāhena]]---wants; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:saṅgama]]---association.
translation: "Since Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa are the same personality, Lakṣmī's association with Kṛṣṇa does not break her vow of chastity. Rather, it was in great fun that the goddess of fortune wanted to associate with Lord Kṛṣṇa."
purport: This is an answer to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's question, and from this we can understand that Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa knew the truth. He told Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu that Nārāyaṇa is a form of Kṛṣṇa associated with transcendental opulence. Although Kṛṣṇa is two-armed and Nārāyaṇa four-armed, there is no difference in the person. They are one and the same. Nārāyaṇa is as beautiful as Kṛṣṇa, but Kṛṣṇa's pastimes are more sportive. It is not that the sportive pastimes of Kṛṣṇa make Him different from Nārāyaṇa. Lakṣmī's desiring to associate with Kṛṣṇa was perfectly natural. In other words, it is understandable that a chaste woman wants to associate with her husband in all his different dresses. Therefore one should not criticize Lakṣmī for wanting to associate with Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.117
description: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa continued, " 'According to transcendental realization, there is no difference between the forms of Nārāyaṇa and Kṛṣṇa. Yet in Kṛṣṇa there is a special transcendental attraction due to the conjugal mellow, and consequently He surpasses Nārāyaṇa. This is the conclusion of transcendental mellows.'
text:
> siddhāntatas tv abhede 'pi
> śrīśa-kṛṣṇa-svarūpayoḥ
> rasenotkṛṣyate kṛṣṇa-
> rūpam eṣā rasa-sthitiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:siddhāntataḥ]]---in reality; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:a:abhede]]---no difference; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśa]]---of the husband of Lakṣmī, Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:svarūpayoḥ]]---between the forms; [[synonyms:r:rasena]]---by transcendental mellows; [[synonyms:u:utkṛṣyate]]---is superior; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpam]]---the form of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:e:eṣā]]---this; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:s:sthitiḥ]]---reservoir of pleasure.
translation: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa continued, " 'According to transcendental realization, there is no difference between the forms of Nārāyaṇa and Kṛṣṇa. Yet in Kṛṣṇa there is a special transcendental attraction due to the conjugal mellow, and consequently He surpasses Nārāyaṇa. This is the conclusion of transcendental mellows.'
purport: This verse quoted by Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa is also found in //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.59).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.118
description: "The goddess of fortune considered that her vow of chastity would not be damaged by her relationship with Kṛṣṇa. Rather, by associating with Kṛṣṇa she could enjoy the benefit of the rāsa dance."
text:
> kṛṣṇa-saṅge pativratā-dharma nahe nāśa
> adhika lābha pāiye, āra rāsa-vilāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the association of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pati]]-[[synonyms:v:vratā]]---of chastity; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---vow; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---is not; [[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---lost; [[synonyms:a:adhika]]---more; [[synonyms:l:lābha]]---profit; [[synonyms:p:pāiye]]---I get; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---the enjoyment in the //rāsa// dance.
translation: "The goddess of fortune considered that her vow of chastity would not be damaged by her relationship with Kṛṣṇa. Rather, by associating with Kṛṣṇa she could enjoy the benefit of the rāsa dance."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.119
description: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa further explained, "Mother Lakṣmī, the goddess of fortune, is also an enjoyer of transcendental bliss; therefore if she wanted to enjoy herself with Kṛṣṇa, what fault is there? Why are You joking so about this?"
text:
> vinodinī lakṣmīra haya kṛṣṇe abhilāṣa
> ihāte ki doṣa, kene kara parihāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vinodinī]]---the enjoyer; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmīra]]---of the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---for Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:abhilāṣa]]---desire; [[synonyms:i:ihāte]]---in this; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---fault; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---You do; [[synonyms:p:parihāsa]]---joking.
translation: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa further explained, "Mother Lakṣmī, the goddess of fortune, is also an enjoyer of transcendental bliss; therefore if she wanted to enjoy herself with Kṛṣṇa, what fault is there? Why are You joking so about this?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.12
description: After meeting Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all those different Vaiṣṇavas became devotees of Kṛṣṇa and began chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.
text:
> sei saba vaiṣṇava mahāprabhura darśane
> kṛṣṇa-upāsaka haila, laya kṛṣṇa-nāme
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all those; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotees; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:darśane]]---by seeing; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:u:upāsaka]]---devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:l:laya]]---took; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāme]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: After meeting Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all those different Vaiṣṇavas became devotees of Kṛṣṇa and began chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.120
description: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "I know that there is no fault on the part of the goddess of fortune, but still she could not enter into the rāsa dance. We hear this from revealed scriptures.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---doṣa nāhi, ihā āmi jāni
> rāsa nā pāila lakṣmī, śāstre ihā śuni
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhukahe]]---the Lord replied; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is no fault; [[synonyms:i:ihā]] [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---this I know; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāila]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---Lakṣmī, the goddess of fortune, could not join the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:ś:śāstre]] [[synonyms:i:ihā]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---we get this information from revealed scriptures.
translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "I know that there is no fault on the part of the goddess of fortune, but still she could not enter into the rāsa dance. We hear this from revealed scriptures.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.121
description: " 'When Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa was dancing with the gopīs in the rāsa-līlā, He put His arms around their necks and embraced them. This transcendental favor was never bestowed upon the goddess of fortune or the other consorts in the spiritual world. Nor was such a thing ever imagined by the most beautiful girls in the heavenly planets, girls whose bodily luster and aroma exactly resemble the lotus flower. And what to speak of worldly women, who may be very, very beautiful according to material estimation?'
text:
> nāyaṁ śriyo 'ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ
> svar-yoṣitāṁ nalina-gandha-rucāṁ kuto 'nyāḥ
> rāsotsave 'sya bhuja-daṇḍa-gṛhīta-kaṇṭha-
> labdhāśiṣāṁ ya udagād vraja-sundarīṇām
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śriyaḥ]]---of the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---on the chest; [[synonyms:u:u]]---alas; [[synonyms:n:nitānta]]-[[synonyms:r:rateḥ]]---one who is very intimately related; [[synonyms:p:prasādaḥ]]---the favor; [[synonyms:s:svaḥ]]---of the heavenly planets; [[synonyms:y:yoṣitām]]---of women; [[synonyms:n:nalina]]---of the lotus flower; [[synonyms:g:gandha]]---having the aroma; [[synonyms:r:rucām]]---and bodily luster; [[synonyms:k:kutaḥ]]---much less; [[synonyms:a:anyāḥ]]---others; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:u:utsave]]---in the festival of the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhuja]]-[[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---by the arms; [[synonyms:g:gṛhīta]]---embraced; [[synonyms:k:kaṇṭha]]---their necks; [[synonyms:l:labdha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśiṣām]]---who achieved such a blessing; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---which; [[synonyms:u:udagāt]]---became manifest; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:s:sundarīṇām]]---of the beautiful //gopīs,// the transcendental girls of Vrajabhūmi.
translation: “ 'When Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa was dancing with the gopīs in the rāsa-līlā, He put His arms around their necks and embraced them. This transcendental favor was never bestowed upon the goddess of fortune or the other consorts in the spiritual world. Nor was such a thing ever imagined by the most beautiful girls in the heavenly planets, girls whose bodily luster and aroma exactly resemble the lotus flower. And what to speak of worldly women, who may be very, very beautiful according to material estimation?'
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.47.60).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.122
description: "But can you tell Me why the goddess of fortune, Lakṣmī, could not enter the rāsa dance? The authorities of Vedic knowledge could enter the dance and associate with Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> lakṣmī kene nā pāila, ihāra ki kāraṇa
> tapa kari' kaiche kṛṣṇa pāila śruti-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---did not; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---get; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of this; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---cause; [[synonyms:t:tapa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---undergoing severe austerities; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---how; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---attained; [[synonyms:ś:śruti]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---Vedic authorities.
translation: "But can you tell Me why the goddess of fortune, Lakṣmī, could not enter the rāsa dance? The authorities of Vedic knowledge could enter the dance and associate with Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.123
description: " 'Great sages conquer the mind and senses by practicing the mystic yoga system and controlling the breath. Thus engaging in mystic yoga, they see the Supersoul within their hearts and ultimately enter into impersonal Brahman. But even the enemies of the Supreme Personality of Godhead attain that position simply by thinking of the Supreme Lord. However, the damsels of Vraja, the gopīs, being attracted by the beauty of Kṛṣṇa, simply wanted to embrace Him and His arms, which are like serpents. Thus the gopīs ultimately tasted the nectar of the lotus feet of the Lord. Similarly, we Upaniṣads can also taste the nectar of His lotus feet by following in the footsteps of the gopīs.' "
text:
> nibhṛta-marun-mano-'kṣa-dṛḍha-yoga-yujo hṛdi yan-
> munaya upāsate tad arayo 'pi yayuḥ smaraṇāt
> striya uragendra-bhoga-bhuja-daṇḍa-viṣakta-dhiyo
> vayam api te samāḥ samadṛśo 'ṅghri-saroja-sudhāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nibhṛta]]---controlled; [[synonyms:m:marut]]---the life air; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]---the mind; [[synonyms:a:akṣa]]---the senses; [[synonyms:d:dṛḍha]]---strong; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]---in the mystic //yoga// process; [[synonyms:y:yujaḥ]]---who are engaged; [[synonyms:h:hṛdi]]---within the heart; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---who; [[synonyms:m:munayaḥ]]---the great sages; [[synonyms:u:upāsate]]---worship; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:a:arayaḥ]]---the enemies; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:y:yayuḥ]]---obtain; [[synonyms:s:smaraṇāt]]---from remembering; [[synonyms:s:striyaḥ]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:u:uraga]]-[[synonyms:i:indra]]---of serpents; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---like the bodies; [[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---the arms; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---like rods; [[synonyms:v:viṣakta]]---fastened to; [[synonyms:d:dhiyaḥ]]---whose minds; [[synonyms:v:vayam]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---we also; [[synonyms:t:te]]---Your; [[synonyms:s:samāḥ]]---equal to them; [[synonyms:s:sama]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛśaḥ]]---having the same ecstatic emotions; [[synonyms:a:aṅghri]]-[[synonyms:s:saroja]]---of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:s:sudhāḥ]]---the nectar.
translation: “ 'Great sages conquer the mind and senses by practicing the mystic yoga system and controlling the breath. Thus engaging in mystic yoga, they see the Supersoul within their hearts and ultimately enter into impersonal Brahman. But even the enemies of the Supreme Personality of Godhead attain that position simply by thinking of the Supreme Lord. However, the damsels of Vraja, the gopīs, being attracted by the beauty of Kṛṣṇa, simply wanted to embrace Him and His arms, which are like serpents. Thus the gopīs ultimately tasted the nectar of the lotus feet of the Lord. Similarly, we Upaniṣads can also taste the nectar of His lotus feet by following in the footsteps of the gopīs.' "
purport: This verse is from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.87.23).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.124
description: Having been asked by Caitanya Mahāprabhu why the goddess of fortune could not enter into the rāsa dance whereas the authorities on Vedic knowledge could, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa replied, "I cannot enter into the mysteries of this behavior."
text:
> śruti pāya, lakṣmī nā pāya, ithe ki kāraṇa
> bhaṭṭa kahe,---ihā praveśite nāre mora mana

translation: Having been asked by Caitanya Mahāprabhu why the goddess of fortune could not enter into the rāsa dance whereas the authorities on Vedic knowledge could, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa replied, "I cannot enter into the mysteries of this behavior."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.125
description: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa then admitted, "I am an ordinary human being. Since my intelligence is very much limited and I am easily agitated, my mind cannot enter within the deep ocean of the pastimes of the Lord.
text:
> āmi jīva,---kṣudra-buddhi, sahaje asthira
> īśvarera līlā---koṭi-samudra-gambhīra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---I am an ordinary living being; [[synonyms:k:kṣudra]]-[[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---possessing limited intelligence; [[synonyms:s:sahaje]] [[synonyms:a:asthira]]---very easily agitated; [[synonyms:ī:īśvarera]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:s:samudra]]---as millions of oceans; [[synonyms:g:gambhīra]]---as deep.
translation: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa then admitted, "I am an ordinary human being. Since my intelligence is very much limited and I am easily agitated, my mind cannot enter within the deep ocean of the pastimes of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.126
description: "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead Kṛṣṇa Himself. You know the purpose of Your activities, and the person whom You enlighten can also understand Your pastimes."
text:
> tumi sākṣāt sei kṛṣṇa, jāna nija-karma
> yāre jānāha, sei jāne tomāra līlā-marma
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:j:jāna]]---You know; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:k:karma]]---Your activities; [[synonyms:y:yāre]] [[synonyms:j:jānāha]]---and unto whom You make it known; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that person; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---knows; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:m:marma]]---the purport of the pastimes.
translation: "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead Kṛṣṇa Himself. You know the purpose of Your activities, and the person whom You enlighten can also understand Your pastimes."
purport: The Supreme Personality of Godhead Kṛṣṇa and His pastimes cannot be understood by blunt material senses. One has to purify the senses by rendering transcendental loving service unto the Lord. When the Lord is pleased and reveals Himself, one can understand the transcendental form, name, qualities and pastimes of the Lord. This is confirmed in the //Kaṭha Upaniṣad// (2.23) and in the //Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad// (3.2.3): //yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṁ svām.// "Anyone who is favored by the Supreme Personality of Godhead can understand His transcendental name, qualities, form and pastimes."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.127
description: The Lord replied, "Lord Kṛṣṇa has a special characteristic: He attracts everyone's heart by the mellow of His personal conjugal love.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---kṛṣṇera eka svabhāva vilakṣaṇa
> sva-mādhurye sarva citta kare ākarṣaṇa

translation: The Lord replied, "Lord Kṛṣṇa has a special characteristic: He attracts everyone's heart by the mellow of His personal conjugal love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.128
description: "By following in the footsteps of the inhabitants of the planet known as Vrajaloka or Goloka Vṛndāvana one can attain the shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. However, in that planet the inhabitants do not know that Lord Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> vraja-lokera bhāve pāiye tāṅhāra caraṇa
> tāṅre īśvara kari' nāhi jāne vraja-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of the inhabitants of Goloka Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in the ecstasy; [[synonyms:p:pāiye]]---one gets; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa's; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---lotus feet; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Person; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---do not; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---know; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---the inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi.
translation: "By following in the footsteps of the inhabitants of the planet known as Vrajaloka or Goloka Vṛndāvana one can attain the shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. However, in that planet the inhabitants do not know that Lord Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.129
description: "There someone may accept Him as a son and sometimes bind Him to a grinding mortar. Someone else may accept Him as an intimate friend and, attaining victory over Him, playfully mount His shoulders.
text:
> keha tāṅre putra-jñāne udukhale bāndhe
> keha sakhā-jñāne jini' caḍe tāṅra kāndhe
