translation: "There someone may accept Him as a son and sometimes bind Him to a grinding mortar. Someone else may accept Him as an intimate friend and, attaining victory over Him, playfully mount His shoulders.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.13
description: " 'O Lord Rāmacandra, descendant of Mahārāja Raghu, kindly protect me! O Lord Kṛṣṇa, killer of the Keśī demon, kindly protect me!' "
text:
> rāma! rāghava! rāma! rāghava! rāma! rāghava! pāhi mām
> kṛṣṇa! keśava! kṛṣṇa! keśava! kṛṣṇa! keśava! rakṣa mām
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāma]]---O Rāma; [[synonyms:r:rāghava]]---O descendant of Raghu; [[synonyms:p:pāhi]]---please protect; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---me; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---O Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:keśava]]---O killer of Keśī; [[synonyms:r:rakṣa]]---protect; [[synonyms:m:mām]]---me.
translation: “ 'O Lord Rāmacandra, descendant of Mahārāja Raghu, kindly protect me! O Lord Kṛṣṇa, killer of the Keśī demon, kindly protect me!' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.130
description: "The inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi know Kṛṣṇa as the son of Mahārāja Nanda, the King of Vrajabhūmi, and they consider that they can have no relationship with the Lord in the rasa of opulence.
text:
> 'vrajendra-nandana' bali' tāṅre jāne vraja-jana
> aiśvarya-jñāne nāhi kona sambandha-mānana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of Nanda Mahārāja, the King of Vrajabhūmi; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---as; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---know; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---the inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi; [[synonyms:a:aiśvarya]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---in opulence; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---any; [[synonyms:s:sambandha]]---relationship; [[synonyms:m:mānana]]---regarding.
translation: "The inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi know Kṛṣṇa as the son of Mahārāja Nanda, the King of Vrajabhūmi, and they consider that they can have no relationship with the Lord in the rasa of opulence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.131
description: "One who worships the Lord by following in the footsteps of the inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi attains Him in the transcendental planet of Vraja, where He is known as the son of Mahārāja Nanda."
text:
> vraja-lokera bhāve yei karaye bhajana
> sei jana pāya vraje vrajendra-nandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of the inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi; [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in the ecstasy; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:k:karaye]]---does; [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---worship; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---that person; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---attains; [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vraja; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa, the son of Mahārāja Nanda.
translation: "One who worships the Lord by following in the footsteps of the inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi attains Him in the transcendental planet of Vraja, where He is known as the son of Mahārāja Nanda."
purport: The inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi, or Goloka Vṛndāvana, know Kṛṣṇa as the son of Mahārāja Nanda. They do not accept Him as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, as people in general do. The Lord is the supreme maintainer of everyone and the chief personality among all personalities. In Vrajabhūmi Kṛṣṇa is certainly the central point of love, but no one knows Him there as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Rather, a person may know Him as a friend, son, lover or master. In any case, the center is Kṛṣṇa. The inhabitants of Vrajabhūmi are related to the Lord in servitude, friendship, parental love and conjugal love. A person engaged in devotional service may accept any one of these transcendental relationships, which are known as mellows. When such a person reaches the perfectional stage, he returns home, back to Kṛṣṇa, in his pure spiritual identity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.132
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu then quoted, " 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, the son of mother Yaśodā, is accessible to those devotees engaged in spontaneous loving service, but He is not as easily accessible to mental speculators, to those striving for self-realization by severe austerities and penances, or to those who consider the body the same as the self.'
text:
> nāyaṁ sukhāpo bhagavān
> dehināṁ gopikā-sutaḥ
> jñānināṁ cātma-bhūtānāṁ
> yathā bhakti-matām iha
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āpaḥ]]---easily available; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:d:dehinām]]---for materialistic persons who have accepted the body as the self; [[synonyms:g:gopikā]]-[[synonyms:s:sutaḥ]]---the son of mother Yaśodā; [[synonyms:j:jñāninām]]---for persons addicted to mental speculation; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūtānām]]---for persons performing severe austerities and penances; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:m:matām]]---for persons engaged in spontaneous devotional service; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---in this world.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu then quoted, " 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, the son of mother Yaśodā, is accessible to those devotees engaged in spontaneous loving service, but He is not as easily accessible to mental speculators, to those striving for self-realization by severe austerities and penances, or to those who consider the body the same as the self.'
purport: This verse, also given in //Madhya-līlā// 8.227, is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.9.21).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.133
description: "The authorities in the Vedic literature who are known as the śruti-gaṇa worshiped Lord Kṛṣṇa in the ecstasy of the gopīs and followed in their footsteps.
text:
> śruti-gaṇa gopī-gaṇera anugata hañā
> vrajeśvarī-suta bhaje gopī-bhāva lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śruti]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the authorities of Vedic hymns; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:a:anugata]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---following in the footsteps; [[synonyms:v:vrajeśvarī]]-[[synonyms:s:suta]]---the son of mother Yaśodā; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---worship; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the ecstasy of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---accepting.
translation: "The authorities in the Vedic literature who are known as the śruti-gaṇa worshiped Lord Kṛṣṇa in the ecstasy of the gopīs and followed in their footsteps.
purport: The authorities in the Vedic literature known as the //śruti-gaṇa// desired to enter into Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa's //rāsa// dance; therefore they began to worship the Lord in the ecstasy of the //gopīs.// In the beginning, however, they were unsuccessful. When they could not enter the dance simply by thinking of Kṛṣṇa in the ecstasy of the //gopīs,// they actually accepted bodies like those of the //gopīs.// They even took birth in Vrajabhūmi just like the //gopīs// and consequently became engrossed in the ecstasy of the //gopīs'// love. In this way they were allowed to enter into the //rāsa-līlā// dance of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.134
description: "The personified authorities on the Vedic hymns acquired bodies like those of the gopīs and took birth in Vrajabhūmi. In those bodies they were allowed to enter into the Lord's rāsa-līlā dance.
text:
> bāhyāntare gopī-deha vraje yabe pāila
> sei dehe kṛṣṇa-saṅge rāsa-krīḍā kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]-[[synonyms:a:antare]]---externally and internally; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:d:deha]]---the body of a //gopī//; [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vrajabhūmi; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---they got; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:dehe]]---in that body; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:k:krīḍā]]---pastimes of the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---performed.
translation: "The personified authorities on the Vedic hymns acquired bodies like those of the gopīs and took birth in Vrajabhūmi. In those bodies they were allowed to enter into the Lord's rāsa-līlā dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.135
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa belongs to the cowherd community, and the gopīs are the dearmost lovers of Kṛṣṇa. Although the wives of the denizens of the heavenly planets are most opulent within the material world, neither they nor any other women in the material universe can acquire Kṛṣṇa's association.
text:
> gopa-jāti kṛṣṇa, gopī---preyasī tāṅhāra
> devī vā anya strī kṛṣṇa nā kare aṅgīkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:j:jāti]]---belonging to the cowherd community; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]---the damsels of Vrajabhūmi, the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:p:preyasī]]---dearmost; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---His; [[synonyms:d:devī]]---the wives of the demigods; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:a:anya]]---other; [[synonyms:s:strī]]---women; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---acceptance.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa belongs to the cowherd community, and the gopīs are the dearmost lovers of Kṛṣṇa. Although the wives of the denizens of the heavenly planets are most opulent within the material world, neither they nor any other women in the material universe can acquire Kṛṣṇa's association.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.136
description: "The goddess of fortune, Lakṣmī, wanted to enjoy Kṛṣṇa and at the same time retain her spiritual body in the form of Lakṣmī. However, she did not follow in the footsteps of the gopīs in her worship of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> lakṣmī cāhe sei dehe kṛṣṇera saṅgama
> gopikā-anugā hañā nā kaila bhajana
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:c:cāhe]]---wants; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:d:dehe]]---in the body; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:s:saṅgama]]---the association of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gopikā]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:a:anugā]]---follower; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---did not; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---perform; [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---worship.
translation: "The goddess of fortune, Lakṣmī, wanted to enjoy Kṛṣṇa and at the same time retain her spiritual body in the form of Lakṣmī. However, she did not follow in the footsteps of the gopīs in her worship of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.137
description: "Vyāsadeva, the supreme authority on Vedic literature, composed the verse beginning 'nāyaṁ sukhāpo bhagavān' because no one can enter into the rāsa-līlā dance in any body other than that of a gopī."
text:
> anya dehe nā pāiye rāsa-vilāsa
> ataeva 'nāyaṁ' śloka kahe veda-vyāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anya]] [[synonyms:d:dehe]]---in a body other than those of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāiye]]---one gets; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]---the pastimes of the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:n:nāyam]]---beginning with the word //nāyam//; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---the Sanskrit verse; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]---Dvaipāyana Vedavyāsa.
translation: "Vyāsadeva, the supreme authority on Vedic literature, composed the verse beginning 'nāyaṁ sukhāpo bhagavān' because no one can enter into the rāsa-līlā dance in any body other than that of a gopī."
purport:
This verse confirms a verse of the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:25|(Bg. 9.25)]]:

> yānti deva-vratā devān
> pitṝn yānti pitṛ-vratāḥ
> bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā
> yānti mad-yājino 'pi mām

"[Lord Kṛṣṇa said:] 'Those who worship the demigods will take birth among the demigods; those who worship the ancestors go the ancestors; those who worship ghosts and spirits will take birth among such beings; and those who worship Me will live with Me.' "

In the material world, every conditioned soul changes his material body again and again, but when the spirit soul is purified of all material coverings, there is no longer a chance of his accepting a material body. Such a soul then remains in his original, spiritual identity, a state that is possible to achieve only by understanding Kṛṣṇa in truth through the practice of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. As Kṛṣṇa says in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:4:9|(Bg. 4.9)]],

> janma karma ca me divyam
> evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ
> tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma
> naiti mām eti so 'rjuna

"One who knows the transcendental nature of My appearance and activities does not, upon leaving the body, take his birth again in this material world, but attains My eternal abode, O Arjuna."

Only when one regains his original spiritual body can he enter into the spiritual kingdom. As far as the //rāsa-līlā// pastimes of the Lord are concerned, it is futile for one who is within the material world to attempt to imitate the Lord's dances.. One has to attain a spiritual body like that of a //gopī// to enter into the pastimes of the //rāsa-līlā.//  In the //nāyaṁ sukhāpo// verse, the devotees are referred to as //bhaktimat,// that is, fully engaged in devotional service and devoid of material contamination. One cannot enter into Kṛṣṇa's //rāsa-līlā// dance simply by artificially imitating it or artificially thinking oneself a //sakhī// and dressing up like one. Kṛṣṇa's //rāsa-līlā// dance is completely spiritual. It has nothing to do with material contamination; therefore no one can enter into this pastime by artificial, material means. That is the instruction of the //nāyaṁ sukhāpo// verse, and it must be strictly understood.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.138
description: Before this explanation was given by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa thought that Śrī Nārāyaṇa was the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> pūrve bhaṭṭera mane eka chila abhimāna
> 'śrī-nārāyaṇa' hayena svayaṁ-bhagavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---before this; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭera]]---of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:c:chila]]---there was; [[synonyms:a:abhimāna]]---an impression; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---the form of the Lord as Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:h:hayena]]---is; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---personally; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: Before this explanation was given by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa thought that Śrī Nārāyaṇa was the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.139
description: Thinking in this way, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa believed that worship of Nārāyaṇa was the supreme form of worship, superior to all other processes of devotional service, for it was followed by the Śrī Vaiṣṇava disciples of Rāmānujācārya.
text:
> tāṅhāra bhajana sarvopari-kakṣā haya
> śrī-vaiṣṇave'ra bhajana ei sarvopari haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---worship of Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:u:upari]]---topmost; [[synonyms:k:kakṣā]]---department; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]]---of the followers of Rāmānujācārya; [[synonyms:b:bhajana]]---worship; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:u:upari]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is the topmost.
translation: Thinking in this way, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa believed that worship of Nārāyaṇa was the supreme form of worship, superior to all other processes of devotional service, for it was followed by the Śrī Vaiṣṇava disciples of Rāmānujācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.14
description: While walking on the road, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to chant this Rāma Rāghava mantra. Chanting in this way, He arrived at the banks of the Gautamī-gaṅgā and took His bath there.
text:
> ei śloka pathe paḍi' karilā prayāṇa
> gautamī-gaṅgāya yāi' kaila gaṅgā-snāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---this Sanskrit verse; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prayāṇa]]---going; [[synonyms:g:gautamī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṅgāya]]---to the bank of the Gautamī-gaṅgā; [[synonyms:y:yāi']]---going; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing in the Ganges.
translation: While walking on the road, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to chant this Rāma Rāghava mantra. Chanting in this way, He arrived at the banks of the Gautamī-gaṅgā and took His bath there.
purport:
The Gautamī-gaṅgā is another branch of the river Godāvarī. Formerly a great sage named Gautama Ṛṣi used to live on the bank of this river opposite the city of Rājamahendri, and consequently this branch was called the Gautamī-gaṅgā.

Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that Śrīla Kavirāja Gosvāmī has recorded the names of the holy places visited by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu but that there is no chronological order of the places visited. However, there is a notebook of Govinda dāsa's containing a chronological order and references to geographical positions. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura requests the readers to refer to that book. According to Govinda dāsa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Trimanda from the Gautamī-gaṅgā. From there He went to Ḍhuṇḍirāma-tīrtha, another place of pilgrimage. According to this book, after visiting the Gautamī-gaṅgā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Mallikārjuna-tīrtha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.140
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had understood this misconception of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa's, and to correct it the Lord talked so much in a joking way.
text:
> ei tāṅra garva prabhu karite khaṇḍana
> parihāsa-dvāre uṭhāya eteka vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his (Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa's); [[synonyms:g:garva]]---pride; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍana]]---to curb; [[synonyms:p:parihāsa]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---by joking; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāya]]---raises; [[synonyms:e:eteka]]---so many; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---words.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had understood this misconception of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa's, and to correct it the Lord talked so much in a joking way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.141
description: The Lord then continued, "My dear Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa, please do not continue doubting. Lord Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and this is the conclusion of the Vedic literature.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---bhaṭṭa, tumi nā kariha saṁśaya
> 'svayaṁ-bhagavān' kṛṣṇa ei ta' niścaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---My dear Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do not do; [[synonyms:s:saṁśaya]]---doubt; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]-[[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---is Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']] [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---this is the conclusion.
translation: The Lord then continued, "My dear Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa, please do not continue doubting. Lord Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and this is the conclusion of the Vedic literature.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.142
description: "Lord Nārāyaṇa, the opulent form of Kṛṣṇa, attracts the minds of the goddess of fortune and her followers.
text:
> kṛṣṇera vilāsa-mūrti---śrī-nārāyaṇa
> ataeva lakṣmī-ādyera hare teṅha mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vilāsa]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---form for enjoyment; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---Lord Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādyera]]---of the goddess of fortune and her followers; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:t:teṅha]]---He (Lord Nārāyaṇa); [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: "Lord Nārāyaṇa, the opulent form of Kṛṣṇa, attracts the minds of the goddess of fortune and her followers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.143
description: " 'All these incarnations of Godhead are either plenary portions or parts of the plenary portions of the puruṣa-avatāras. But Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. In every age He protects the world through His different features when the world is disturbed by the enemies of Indra.'
text:
> ete cāṁśa-kalāḥ puṁsaḥ
> kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam
> indrāri-vyākulaṁ lokaṁ
> mṛḍayanti yuge yuge
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ete]]---these; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---plenary portions; [[synonyms:k:kalāḥ]]---parts of plenary portions; [[synonyms:p:puṁsaḥ]]---of the //puruṣa-avatāras//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---Himself; [[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:a:ari]]---the enemies of Lord Indra; [[synonyms:v:vyākulam]]---full of; [[synonyms:l:lokam]]---the world; [[synonyms:m:mṛḍayanti]]---make happy; [[synonyms:y:yuge]] [[synonyms:y:yuge]]---at the right time in each age.
translation: “ 'All these incarnations of Godhead are either plenary portions or parts of the plenary portions of the puruṣa-avatāras. But Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. In every age He protects the world through His different features when the world is disturbed by the enemies of Indra.'
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:3:28|(1.3.28)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.144
description: "Because Kṛṣṇa has four extraordinary qualities not possessed by Lord Nārāyaṇa, the goddess of fortune, Lakṣmī, always desires His company.
text:
> nārāyaṇa haite kṛṣṇera asādhāraṇa guṇa
> ataeva lakṣmīra kṛṣṇe tṛṣṇā anukṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---over and above Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:asādhāraṇa]] [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---uncommon qualities; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmīra]]---of the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tṛṣṇā]]---desire; [[synonyms:a:anukṣaṇa]]---always.
translation: "Because Kṛṣṇa has four extraordinary qualities not possessed by Lord Nārāyaṇa, the goddess of fortune, Lakṣmī, always desires His company.
purport: Lord Nārāyaṇa has sixty transcendental qualities. Over and above these, Kṛṣṇa has four extraordinary transcendental qualities absent in Lord Nārāyaṇa. These four qualities are: (1) His wonderful pastimes, which are compared to an ocean; (2) His association in the circle of the supreme devotees in conjugal love (the //gopīs//); (3) His playing on the flute, whose vibration attracts the three worlds; and (4) His extraordinary beauty, which surpasses the beauty of the three worlds. Lord Kṛṣṇa's beauty is unequaled and unsurpassed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.145
description: "You have recited the śloka beginning with 'siddhāntatas tv abhede 'pi.' That very verse is evidence that Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> tumi ye paḍilā śloka, se haya pramāṇa
> sei śloke āise 'kṛṣṇa---svayaṁ bhagavān'
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---have recited; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verse; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---evidence; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloke]]---in that verse; [[synonyms:ā:āise]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa is; [[synonyms:s:svayam]] [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: "You have recited the śloka beginning with 'siddhāntatas tv abhede 'pi.' That very verse is evidence that Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.146
description: " 'According to transcendental realization, there is no difference between the forms of Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa. Yet in Kṛṣṇa there is a special transcendental attraction due to the conjugal mellow, and consequently He surpasses Nārāyaṇa. This is the conclusion of transcendental mellows.'
text:
> siddhāntatas tv abhede 'pi
> śrīśa-kṛṣṇa-svarūpayoḥ
> rasenotkṛṣyate kṛṣṇa-
> rūpam eṣā rasa-sthitiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:siddhāntataḥ]]---in reality; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:a:abhede]]---no difference; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:ī:īśa]]---of the husband of Lakṣmī, Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:svarūpayoḥ]]---between the forms; [[synonyms:r:rasena]]---by transcendental mellows; [[synonyms:u:utkṛṣyate]]---is superior; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpam]]---the form of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:e:eṣā]]---this; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:s:sthitiḥ]]---the reservoir of pleasure.
translation: “ 'According to transcendental realization, there is no difference between the forms of Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa. Yet in Kṛṣṇa there is a special transcendental attraction due to the conjugal mellow, and consequently He surpasses Nārāyaṇa. This is the conclusion of transcendental mellows.'
purport: This is a verse from the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.2.59). Here Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja says that Lord Caitanya spoke the verse to Veṅkata Bhaṭṭa, and earlier he said that Veṅkata Bhaṭṭa spoke it to the Lord. But since their conversation took place long, long before the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// was composed, the question my be raised as to how either of them quoted the verse. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains that this verse and many others like it were current among devotees long before the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// was composed. Thus devotees would always quote them and explain their purport in ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.147
description: "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, attracts the mind of the goddess of fortune, but Lord Nārāyaṇa cannot attract the minds of the gopīs. This proves the superexcellence of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> svayaṁ bhagavān 'kṛṣṇa' hare lakṣmīra mana
> gopikāra mana harite nāre 'nārāyaṇa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svayam]] [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---is Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmīra]]---of the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:g:gopikāra]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds; [[synonyms:h:harite]]---to attract; [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---is not able; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---Lord Nārāyaṇa.
translation: "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, attracts the mind of the goddess of fortune, but Lord Nārāyaṇa cannot attract the minds of the gopīs. This proves the superexcellence of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.148
description: "To say nothing of Lord Nārāyaṇa personally, Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself appeared as Nārāyaṇa just to play a joke on the gopīs.
text:
> nārāyaṇera kā kathā, śrī-kṛṣṇa āpane
> gopikāre hāsya karāite haya 'nārāyaṇe'
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇera]]---of Lord Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:k:kā]] [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---what to speak; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---Himself; [[synonyms:g:gopikāre]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:h:hāsya]] [[synonyms:k:karāite]]---to make them jubilant; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇe]]---in the form of Nārāyaṇa.
translation: "To say nothing of Lord Nārāyaṇa personally, Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself appeared as Nārāyaṇa just to play a joke on the gopīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.149
description: "Although Kṛṣṇa assumed the four-armed form of Nārāyaṇa, He could not attract the serious attention of the gopīs in ecstatic love.
text:
> 'catur-bhuja-mūrti' dekhāya gopī-gaṇera āge
> sei 'kṛṣṇe' gopikāra nahe anurāge
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:catur]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---four-handed form; [[synonyms:d:dekhāya]]---exhibits; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto that Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gopikāra]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:a:anurāge]]---attraction.
translation: "Although Kṛṣṇa assumed the four-armed form of Nārāyaṇa, He could not attract the serious attention of the gopīs in ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.15
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then went to Mallikārjuna-tīrtha and saw the deity of Lord Śiva there. He also induced all the people to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.
text:
> mallikārjuna-tīrthe yāi' maheśa dekhila
> tāhāṅ saba loke kṛṣṇa-nāma laoyāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mallikārjuna]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrthe]]---to the holy place known as Mallikārjuna; [[synonyms:y:yāi']]---going; [[synonyms:m:maheśa]]---the deity of Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---He saw; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:l:loke]]---all the people; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa's holy name; [[synonyms:l:laoyāila]]---He induced to chant.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then went to Mallikārjuna-tīrtha and saw the deity of Lord Śiva there. He also induced all the people to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.
purport: Mallikārjuna is also known as Śrī Saila. It is situated about seventy miles south of Karṇula on the right bank of the Kṛṣṇā River. There are great walls all around the village, and within the walls resides the deity known as Mallikārjuna. It is a deity of Lord Śiva and is one of the Jyotirliṅgas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.150
description: " 'Once Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa playfully manifested Himself as Nārāyaṇa, with four victorious hands and a very beautiful form. When the gopīs saw this exalted form, however, their ecstatic feelings were crippled. A learned scholar, therefore, cannot understand the gopīs' ecstatic feelings, which are firmly fixed upon the original form of Lord Kṛṣṇa as the son of Nanda Mahārāja. The wonderful feelings of the gopīs in ecstatic parama-rasa with Kṛṣṇa constitute the greatest mystery in spiritual life.' "
text:
> gopīnāṁ paśupendra-nandana-juṣo bhāvasya kas tāṁ kṛtī
> vijñātuṁ kṣamate durūha-padavī-sañcāriṇaḥ prakriyām
> āviṣkurvati vaiṣṇavīm api tanuṁ tasmin bhujair jiṣṇubhir
> yāsāṁ hanta caturbhir adbhuta-ruciṁ rāgodayaḥ kuñcati
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopīnām]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:p:paśupa]]-[[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]-[[synonyms:j:juṣaḥ]]---of the service of the son of Vraja's King, Mahārāja Nanda; [[synonyms:b:bhāvasya]]---ecstatic; [[synonyms:k:kaḥ]]---what; [[synonyms:t:tām]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kṛtī]]---learned man; [[synonyms:v:vijñātum]]---to understand; [[synonyms:k:kṣamate]]---is able; [[synonyms:d:durūha]]---very difficult to understand; [[synonyms:p:padavī]]---the position; [[synonyms:s:sañcāriṇaḥ]]---which provokes; [[synonyms:p:prakriyām]]---activity; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣkurvati]]---He manifests; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavīm]]---of Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:a:api]]---certainly; [[synonyms:t:tanum]]---the body; [[synonyms:t:tasmin]]---in that; [[synonyms:b:bhujaiḥ]]---with arms; [[synonyms:j:jiṣṇubhiḥ]]---very beautiful; [[synonyms:y:yāsām]]---of whom (the //gopīs//); [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---alas; [[synonyms:c:caturbhiḥ]]---four; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderfully; [[synonyms:r:rucim]]---beautiful; [[synonyms:r:rāga]]-[[synonyms:u:udayaḥ]]---the evoking of ecstatic feelings; [[synonyms:k:kuñcati]]---cripples.
translation: “ 'Once Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa playfully manifested Himself as Nārāyaṇa, with four victorious hands and a very beautiful form. When the gopīs saw this exalted form, however, their ecstatic feelings were crippled. A learned scholar, therefore, cannot understand the gopīs' ecstatic feelings, which are firmly fixed upon the original form of Lord Kṛṣṇa as the son of Nanda Mahārāja. The wonderful feelings of the gopīs in ecstatic parama-rasa with Kṛṣṇa constitute the greatest mystery in spiritual life.' "
purport: This is a verse spoken by Nārada Muni in the //Lalita-mādhava-nāṭaka// (6.14), a drama written by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.151
description: In this way Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu deflated the pride of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa, but just to make him happy again, He spoke as follows.
text:
> eta kahi' prabhu tāṅra garva cūrṇa kariyā
> tāṅre sukha dite kahe siddhānta phirāiyā

translation: In this way Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu deflated the pride of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa, but just to make him happy again, He spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.152
description: The Lord pacified Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa by saying, "Actually whatever I have said is by way of jest. Now you can hear from Me the conclusion of the śāstras, in which every Vaiṣṇava devotee has firm faith.
text:
> duḥkha nā bhāviha, bhaṭṭa, kailuṅ parihāsa
> śāstra-siddhānta śuna, yāte vaiṣṇava-viśvāsa

translation: The Lord pacified Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa by saying, "Actually whatever I have said is by way of jest. Now you can hear from Me the conclusion of the śāstras, in which every Vaiṣṇava devotee has firm faith.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.153
description: "There is no difference between Lord Kṛṣṇa and Lord Nārāyaṇa, for They are of the same form. Similarly, there is no difference between the gopīs and the goddess of fortune, for they also are of the same form.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-nārāyaṇa, yaiche eka-i svarūpa
> gopī-lakṣmī-bheda nāhi haya eka-rūpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa and Lord Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---one; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---form; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---difference; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---one form.
translation: "There is no difference between Lord Kṛṣṇa and Lord Nārāyaṇa, for They are of the same form. Similarly, there is no difference between the gopīs and the goddess of fortune, for they also are of the same form.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.154
description: "The goddess of fortune enjoys the association of Kṛṣṇa through the gopīs. One should not see a difference between the forms of the Lord, for such a conception is offensive.
text:
> gopī-dvāre lakṣmī kare kṛṣṇa-saṅgāsvāda
> īśvaratve bheda mānile haya aparādha
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---through the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅga]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsvāda]]---tasting the sweetness of the association of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ī:īśvaratve]]---in the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bheda]]---difference; [[synonyms:m:mānile]]---if one considers; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:a:aparādha]]---offense.
translation: "The goddess of fortune enjoys the association of Kṛṣṇa through the gopīs. One should not see a difference between the forms of the Lord, for such a conception is offensive.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.155
description: "There is no difference between the transcendental forms of the Lord. Different forms are manifest due to different attachments of different devotees. Actually the Lord is one, but He appears in different forms just to satisfy His devotees.
text:
> eka īśvara---bhaktera dhyāna-anurūpa
> eka-i vigrahe kare nānākāra rūpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Lord is one; [[synonyms:b:bhaktera]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:d:dhyāna]]---meditation; [[synonyms:a:anurūpa]]---according to; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---one; [[synonyms:v:vigrahe]]---in form; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---exhibits; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---different; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---forms.
translation: "There is no difference between the transcendental forms of the Lord. Different forms are manifest due to different attachments of different devotees. Actually the Lord is one, but He appears in different forms just to satisfy His devotees.
purport:
In the //Brahma-saṁhitā// (5.33) it is stated:

> advaitam acyutam anādim ananta-rūpam
> ādyaṁ purāṇa-puruṣaṁ nava-yauvanaṁ ca

The Lord is //advaita,// without differentiation. There is no difference between the forms of Kṛṣṇa, Rāma, Nārāyaṇa and Viṣṇu. All of them are one. Sometimes foolish people ask whether when we chant "Rāma" in the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// we refer to Lord Rāmacandra or Lord Balarāma. If a devotee says that the name Rāma in the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// refers to Balarāma, a foolish person may become angry because to him the name Rāma refers to Lord Rāmacandra. Actually there is no difference between Balarāma and Lord Rāma. It does not matter if one chants Hare Rāma referring to Balarāma or Lord Rāmacandra, for there is no difference between Them. However, it is offensive to think that Balarāma is superior to Lord Rāmacandra or vice versa. Neophyte devotees do not understand this śāstric conclusion, and consequently they unnecessarily create an offensive situation. In text 154 Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu clarified this in a very lucid way: //īśvaratve bheda mānile haya aparādha.// "It is offensive for one to differentiate between the forms of the Lord." On the other hand, one should not think that the forms of the Lord are the same as the forms of the demigods. This is certainly offensive, as confirmed by the //Vaiṣṇava-tantra://

> yas tu nārāyaṇaṁ devaṁ
> brahmā-rudrādi-daivataiḥ
> samatvenaiva vīkṣeta
> sa pāṣaṇḍī bhaved dhruvam

"A //pāṣaṇḍī// is one who considers the great demigods such as Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva equal to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa." (//Hari-bhakti-vilāsa// 7.117)

The conclusion is that we should neither differentiate between the forms of the Lord nor equate the forms of the Lord with the forms of demigods or human beings. For instance, sometimes foolish //sannyāsīs,// thinking the body of the Lord to be material, equate //daridra-nārāyaṇa// with Nārāyaṇa, and this is certainly offensive. Unless one is instructed by a bona fide spiritual master, he cannot perfectly understand these different forms. The //Brahma-saṁhitā// confirms, //vedeṣu durlabham adurlabham ātma-bhaktau.// One cannot understand the differences between the forms of the Lord simply by academic study or by reading Vedic literature. One must learn from a realized devotee. Only then can one learn how to distinguish between one form of the Lord and another. The conclusion is that there is no difference between the forms of the Lord, but there is a difference between His forms and those of the demigods.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.156
description: " 'When the jewel known as vaidūrya touches various other materials, it appears to be separated into different colors, and consequently its forms also appear different. Similarly, according to the meditational ecstasy of the devotee, the Lord, who is known as Acyuta [infallible], appears in different forms, although He is essentially one.' "
text:
> maṇir yathā vibhāgena
> nīla-pītādibhir yutaḥ
> rūpa-bhedam avāpnoti
> dhyāna-bhedāt tathācyutaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:maṇiḥ]]---jewel, specifically the jewel known as //vaidūrya//; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as; [[synonyms:v:vibhāgena]]---separately; [[synonyms:n:nīla]]---blue; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]---yellow; [[synonyms:ā:ādibhiḥ]]---and with other colors; [[synonyms:y:yutaḥ]]---joined; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhedam]]---difference of form; [[synonyms:a:avāpnoti]]---gets; [[synonyms:d:dhyāna]]-[[synonyms:b:bhedāt]]---by different types of meditation; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---similarly; [[synonyms:a:acyutaḥ]]---the infallible Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: “ 'When the jewel known as vaidūrya touches various other materials, it appears to be separated into different colors, and consequently its forms also appear different. Similarly, according to the meditational ecstasy of the devotee, the Lord, who is known as Acyuta [infallible], appears in different forms, although He is essentially one.' "
purport: This is a verse quoted from //Śrī Nārada-pañcarātra.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.157
description: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa then said, "I am an ordinary fallen living entity, but You are Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself.
text:
> bhaṭṭa kahe,---kāhāṅ āmi jīva pāmara
> kāhāṅ tumi sei kṛṣṇa,---sākṣāt īśvara
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa said; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---whereas; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---an ordinary living being; [[synonyms:p:pāmara]]---fallen; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---whereas; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---the same Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]] [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---directly the Lord.
translation: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa then said, "I am an ordinary fallen living entity, but You are Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.158
description: "The transcendental pastimes of the Lord are unfathomable, and I do not know anything about them. Whatever You say I accept as the truth.
text:
> agādha īśvara-līlā kichui nā jāni
> tumi yei kaha, sei satya kari' māni
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:agādha]]---unfathomable; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kichui]]---anything; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I do not know; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---say; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:satya]]---that is right; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:m:māni]]---I accept.
translation: "The transcendental pastimes of the Lord are unfathomable, and I do not know anything about them. Whatever You say I accept as the truth.
purport:
This is the way to understand the truth about the Supreme Personality of Godhead. After hearing the //Bhagavad-gītā,// Arjuna said very much the same thing:

> sarvam etad ṛtaṁ manye
> yan māṁ vadasi keśava
> na hi te bhagavan vyaktiṁ
> vidur devā na dānavāḥ

"O Kṛṣṇa, I totally accept as truth all that You have told me. Neither the demigods nor the demons, O Lord, can understand Your personality." [[books:bg:10:14|(Bg. 10.14)]]

It is not possible to understand the truth about the pastimes of the Lord simply by using our own logic, argument and academic education. We must receive bona fide information from the Supreme Personality of Godhead, just as Arjuna received information when Kṛṣṇa spoke the //Bhagavad-gītā.// We have to accept the //Bhagavad-gītā// or any other Vedic literature in good faith. These Vedic scriptures are the only source of knowledge about the Lord. We must understand that we cannot comprehend the Absolute Truth by the speculative process.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.159
description: "I have been engaged in the service of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, and it is due to Their mercy that I have been able to see Your lotus feet.
text:
> more pūrṇa kṛpā kaila lakṣmī-nārāyaṇa
> tāṅra kṛpāya pāinu tomāra caraṇa-daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto me; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]---complete; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]-[[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---the Deity of mother goddess of fortune and Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpāya]]---by Their mercy; [[synonyms:p:pāinu]]---I have gotten; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---vision of the lotus feet.
translation: "I have been engaged in the service of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, and it is due to Their mercy that I have been able to see Your lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.16
description: There he saw Lord Mahādeva [Śiva], the servant of Lord Rāma. He then went to Ahovala-nṛsiṁha.
text:
> rāmadāsa mahādeve karila daraśana
> ahovala-nṛsiṁhere karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---Rāmadāsa; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:d:deve]]---of Mahādeva; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---did; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing; [[synonyms:a:ahovala]]-[[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁhere]]---to Ahovala-nṛsiṁha; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---going.
translation: There he saw Lord Mahādeva [Śiva], the servant of Lord Rāma. He then went to Ahovala-nṛsiṁha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.160
description: "Out of Your causeless mercy You have told me of the glories of Lord Kṛṣṇa. No one can reach the end of the opulence, qualities and forms of the Lord.
text:
> kṛpā kari' kahile more kṛṣṇera mahimā
> yāṅra rūpa-guṇaiśvaryera keha nā pāya sīmā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing causeless mercy; [[synonyms:k:kahile]]---You have spoken; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto me; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---the glories; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:aiśvaryera]]---of forms, qualities and opulence; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:s:sīmā]]---the limit.
translation: "Out of Your causeless mercy You have told me of the glories of Lord Kṛṣṇa. No one can reach the end of the opulence, qualities and forms of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.161
description: "I can now understand that devotional service unto Lord Kṛṣṇa is the supreme form of worship. Out of Your causeless mercy You have made my life successful simply by explaining the facts."
text:
> ebe se jāninu kṛṣṇa-bhakti sarvopari
> kṛtārtha karile, more kahile kṛpā kari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:j:jāninu]]---I understand; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:u:upari]]---above all; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---successful; [[synonyms:k:karile]]---You have made; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto me; [[synonyms:k:kahile]]---You have spoken; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---by Your causeless mercy.
translation: "I can now understand that devotional service unto Lord Kṛṣṇa is the supreme form of worship. Out of Your causeless mercy You have made my life successful simply by explaining the facts."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.162
description: After saying this, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa fell down before the lotus feet of the Lord, and the Lord, out of His causeless mercy, embraced him.
text:
> eta bali' bhaṭṭa paḍilā prabhura caraṇe
> kṛpā kari' prabhu tāṅre kailā āliṅgane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the lotus feet of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing him mercy; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgane]]---embracing.
translation: After saying this, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa fell down before the lotus feet of the Lord, and the Lord, out of His causeless mercy, embraced him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.163
description: When the period of Cāturmāsya was completed, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took permission to leave Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa, and after visiting Śrī Raṅga He proceeded further toward southern India.
text:
> cāturmāsya pūrṇa haila, bhaṭṭa-ājñā lañā
> dakṣiṇa calilā prabhu śrī-raṅga dekhiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāturmāsya]]---the period of Cāturmāsya; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became completed; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking permission from Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]]---south; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---proceeded; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅga]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---visiting Śrī Raṅga.
translation: When the period of Cāturmāsya was completed, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took permission to leave Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa, and after visiting Śrī Raṅga He proceeded further toward southern India.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.164
description: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa did not want to return home but also wanted to go with the Lord. It was with great endeavor that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade him farewell.
text:
> saṅgete calilā bhaṭṭa, nā yāya bhavane
> tāṅre vidāya dilā prabhu aneka yatane
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saṅgete]]---along with Him; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---began to go; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]] [[synonyms:b:bhavane]]---does not return to his home; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:v:vidāya]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---gave farewell; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:aneka]] [[synonyms:y:yatane]]---with great endeavor.
translation: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa did not want to return home but also wanted to go with the Lord. It was with great endeavor that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade him farewell.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.165
description: When He did so, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa fell down unconscious. Such are the pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the son of mother Śacī, at Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra.
text:
> prabhura viyoge bhaṭṭa haila acetana
> ei raṅga-līlā kare śacīra nandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:v:viyoge]]---on account of separation from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:a:acetana]]---unconscious; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:r:raṅga]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastime at Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ś:śacīra]] [[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of mother Śacī.
translation: When He did so, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa fell down unconscious. Such are the pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the son of mother Śacī, at Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.166
description: When the Lord arrived at Ṛṣabha Hill, He saw the temple of Lord Nārāyaṇa and offered obeisances and various prayers.
text:
> ṛṣabha-parvate cali' āilā gaurahari
> nārāyaṇa dekhilā tāṅhā nati-stuti kari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛṣabha]]-[[synonyms:p:parvate]]---to the Ṛṣabha Hill; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---walking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---the Deity of Lord Nārāyaṇa; [[synonyms:d:dekhilā]]---saw; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhā]]---there; [[synonyms:n:nati]]-[[synonyms:s:stuti]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---offering obeisances and prayers.
translation: When the Lord arrived at Ṛṣabha Hill, He saw the temple of Lord Nārāyaṇa and offered obeisances and various prayers.
purport: Ṛṣabha Hill is in southern Karṇāṭa, in the district of Madurai. Twelve miles north of Madurai City is a place called Ānāgaḍa-malaya-parvata, which is situated within the forest of Kuṭakācala. Within this forest Lord Ṛṣabhadeva burned Himself to ashes. Now this place is known as Palni Hill.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.167
description: Paramānanda Purī was staying at Ṛṣabha Hill during the four months of the rainy season, and when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard this, He immediately went to see him.
text:
> paramānanda-purī tāhāṅ rahe catur-māsa
> śuni' mahāprabhu gelā purī-gosāñira pāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paramānanda]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remained; [[synonyms:c:catur]]-[[synonyms:m:māsa]]---four months; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---the spiritual master; [[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---near.
translation: Paramānanda Purī was staying at Ṛṣabha Hill during the four months of the rainy season, and when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard this, He immediately went to see him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.168
description: Upon meeting Paramānanda Purī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered him all respects, touching his lotus feet, and Paramānanda Purī embraced the Lord in ecstasy.
text:
> purī-gosāñira prabhu kaila caraṇa vandana
> preme purī gosāñi tāṅre kaila āliṅgana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---worship of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:p:purī]] [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing.
translation: Upon meeting Paramānanda Purī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered him all respects, touching his lotus feet, and Paramānanda Purī embraced the Lord in ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.169
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stayed with Paramānanda Purī in the brāhmaṇa's house where he was residing. The two of them passed three days there discussing topics of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> tina-dina preme doṅhe kṛṣṇa-kathā-raṅge
> sei vipra-ghare doṅhe rahe eka-saṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---three days; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:d:doṅhe]]---both; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---discussing topics of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---in jubilation; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]-[[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in the home of a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:d:doṅhe]]---both of them; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---stayed; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---together.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stayed with Paramānanda Purī in the brāhmaṇa's house where he was residing. The two of them passed three days there discussing topics of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.17
description: After seeing the Ahovala-nṛsiṁha Deity, Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered many prayers unto the Lord. He then went to Siddhavaṭa, where He saw the Deity of Rāmacandra, the Lord of Sītādevī.
text:
> nṛsiṁha dekhiyā tāṅre kaila nati-stuti
> siddhavaṭa gelā yāhāṅ mūrti sītāpati
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---after seeing the Lord Nṛsiṁha Deity; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:n:nati]]-[[synonyms:s:stuti]]---offering of various prayers; [[synonyms:s:siddhavaṭa]]---to Siddhavaṭa; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---He went; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---the Deity; [[synonyms:s:sītā]]-[[synonyms:p:pati]]---Lord Rāmacandra.
translation: After seeing the Ahovala-nṛsiṁha Deity, Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered many prayers unto the Lord. He then went to Siddhavaṭa, where He saw the Deity of Rāmacandra, the Lord of Sītādevī.
purport: Siddhavaṭa, also known as Sidhauṭa, is ten miles east of the village Kuḍāpā. Previously this place was also known as southern Benares. There is a great banyan tree there, and it is therefore known as Siddhavaṭa. //Vaṭa// means banyan tree.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.170
description: Paramānanda Purī informed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu that he was going to see Puruṣottama at Jagannātha Purī. After seeing Lord Jagannātha there, he would go to Bengal to bathe in the Ganges.
text:
> purī-gosāñi bale,---āmi yāba puruṣottame
> puruṣottama dekhi' gauḍe yāba gaṅgā-snāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---said; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---shall go; [[synonyms:p:puruṣottame]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:p:puruṣottama]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after visiting Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:g:gauḍe]] [[synonyms:y:yāba]]---I shall go to Bengal; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]-[[synonyms:s:snāne]]---for bathing in the Ganges.
translation: Paramānanda Purī informed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu that he was going to see Puruṣottama at Jagannātha Purī. After seeing Lord Jagannātha there, he would go to Bengal to bathe in the Ganges.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.171
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then told him, "Please return to Jagannātha Purī, for I will return there very soon from Rāmeśvara [Setubandha].
text:
> prabhu kahe,---tumi punaḥ āisa nīlācale
> āmi setubandha haite āsiba alpa-kāle
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the Lord said; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:ā:āisa]]---come; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:s:setubandha]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from Rāmeśvara; [[synonyms:ā:āsiba]]---shall return; [[synonyms:a:alpa]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---very soon.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then told him, "Please return to Jagannātha Purī, for I will return there very soon from Rāmeśvara [Setubandha].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.172
description: "It is My desire to stay with you, and therefore if you would return to Jagannātha Purī, you would show great mercy to Me."
text:
> tomāra nikaṭe rahi,---hena vāñchā haya
> nīlācale āsibe more hañā sadaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:n:nikaṭe]]---with you; [[synonyms:r:rahi]]---I may stay; [[synonyms:h:hena]]---such; [[synonyms:v:vāñchā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is My desire; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:ā:āsibe]]---please come; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:d:daya]]---merciful.
translation: "It is My desire to stay with you, and therefore if you would return to Jagannātha Purī, you would show great mercy to Me."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.173
description: After talking in this way with Paramānanda Purī, the Lord took his permission to leave and, very much pleased, departed for southern India.
text:
> eta bali' tāṅra ṭhāñi ei ājñā lañā
> dakṣiṇe calilā prabhu haraṣita hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---from him; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking permission; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇe]] [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---departed for southern India; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:haraṣita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being very much pleased.
translation: After talking in this way with Paramānanda Purī, the Lord took his permission to leave and, very much pleased, departed for southern India.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.174
description: Thus Paramānanda Purī started for Jagannātha Purī, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began walking toward Śrī Śaila.
text:
> paramānanda purī tabe calilā nīlācale
> mahāprabhu cali cali āilā śrī-śaile
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paramānanda]] [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:c:calilā]] [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---departed for Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cali]] [[synonyms:c:cali]]---walking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaile]]---to Śrī Śaila.
translation: Thus Paramānanda Purī started for Jagannātha Purī, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began walking toward Śrī Śaila.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura remarks, "Which Śrī Śaila is being indicated by Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī is not clearly understood. There is no temple of Mallikārjuna in this area because the Śrī Śaila located in the district of Dhārwād cannot possibly be there. That Śrī Śaila is on the southern side of Belgaumā, and the Śiva temple of Mallikārjuna is located there. (Refer to text fifteen of this chapter.) It is said that on that hill Lord Śiva lived with Devī. Also, Lord Brahmā lived there with all the demigods."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.175
description: It was in Śrī Śaila that Lord Śiva and his wife Durgā lived in the dress of brāhmaṇas, and when they saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they became very much pleased.
text:
> śiva-durgā rahe tāhāṅ brāhmaṇera veśe
> mahāprabhu dekhi' doṅhāra ha-ila ullāse
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]-[[synonyms:d:durgā]]---Lord Śiva and his wife, Durgā; [[synonyms:r:rahe]] [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---stayed there; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇera]] [[synonyms:v:veśe]]---in the dress of //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]]---of both of them; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:u:ullāse]]---great pleasure.
translation: It was in Śrī Śaila that Lord Śiva and his wife Durgā lived in the dress of brāhmaṇas, and when they saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they became very much pleased.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.176
description: Lord Śiva, dressed like a brāhmaṇa, gave alms to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and invited Him to spend three days in a solitary place. Sitting there together, they talked very confidentially.
text:
> tina dina bhikṣā dila kari' nimantraṇa
> nibhṛte vasi' gupta-vārtā kahe dui jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---for three days; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---offered alms; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---inviting Him; [[synonyms:n:nibhṛte]]---in a solitary place; [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting together; [[synonyms:g:gupta]]-[[synonyms:v:vārtā]]---confidential talks; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---speak; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---both of them.
translation: Lord Śiva, dressed like a brāhmaṇa, gave alms to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and invited Him to spend three days in a solitary place. Sitting there together, they talked very confidentially.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.177
description: After talking with Lord Śiva, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took his permission to leave and went to Kāmakoṣṭhī-purī.
text:
> tāṅra saṅge mahāprabhu kari iṣṭagoṣṭhī
> tāṅra ājñā lañā āilā purī kāmakoṣṭhī
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with him; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kari]] [[synonyms:i:iṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:g:goṣṭhī]]---discussing spiritual subject matter; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:purī]] [[synonyms:k:kāmakoṣṭhī]]---to Kāmakoṣṭhī-purī.
translation: After talking with Lord Śiva, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took his permission to leave and went to Kāmakoṣṭhī-purī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.178
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at southern Mathurā from Kāmakoṣṭhī, He met a brāhmaṇa.
text:
> dakṣiṇa-mathurā āilā kāmakoṣṭhī haite
> tāhāṅ dekhā haila eka brāhmaṇa-sahite
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mathurā]]---at southern Mathurā; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:k:kāmakoṣṭhī]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from Kāmakoṣṭhī; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:d:dekhā]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---He met; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sahite]]---with a //brāhmaṇa.//
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at southern Mathurā from Kāmakoṣṭhī, He met a brāhmaṇa.
purport: Southern Madurai, presently known as Mādurā, is situated on the banks of the Bhāgāi River. This place of pilgrimage is specifically meant for the devotees of Lord Śiva; therefore it is called Śaiva-kṣetra, that is, the place where Lord Śiva is worshiped. In this area there are mountains and forests. There are also two Śiva temples, one known as Rāmeśvara and the other known as Sundareśvara. There is also a temple to Devī called the Mīnākṣī-devī temple, which displays very great architectural craftsmanship. It was built under the supervision of the kings of the Pāṇḍya Dynasty, and when the Muslims attacked this temple, as well as the temple of Sundareśvara, great damage was done. In the Christian year 1372, a king named Kampanna Udaiyara reigned on the throne of Mādurā. Long ago, Emperor Kulaśekhara ruled this area, and during his reign he established a colony of //brāhmaṇas.// A well-known king named Anantaguṇa Pāṇḍya is an eleventh-generation descendant of Emperor Kulaśekhara.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.179
description: The brāhmaṇa who met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu invited the Lord to his home. This brāhmaṇa was a great devotee and an authority on Lord Śrī Rāmacandra. He was always detached from material activities.
text:
> sei vipra mahāprabhuke kaila nimantraṇa
> rāma-bhakta sei vipra---virakta mahājana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhuke]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotee of Lord Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---//brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:v:virakta]]---very much detached; [[synonyms:m:mahājana]]---a great devotee and authority.
translation: The brāhmaṇa who met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu invited the Lord to his home. This brāhmaṇa was a great devotee and an authority on Lord Śrī Rāmacandra. He was always detached from material activities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.18
description: After seeing the Deity of Lord Rāmacandra, the descendant of King Raghu, the Lord offered His prayers and obeisances. Then a brāhmaṇa invited the Lord to take lunch.
text:
> raghunātha dekhi' kaila praṇati stavana
> tāhāṅ eka vipra prabhura kaila nimantraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:raghu]]-[[synonyms:n:nātha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after seeing Lord Rāmacandra, the descendant of Mahārāja Raghu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---offered; [[synonyms:p:praṇati]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:s:stavana]]---prayers; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---//brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation.
translation: After seeing the Deity of Lord Rāmacandra, the descendant of King Raghu, the Lord offered His prayers and obeisances. Then a brāhmaṇa invited the Lord to take lunch.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.180
description: After bathing in the river Kṛtamālā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to the brāhmaṇa's house to take lunch, but He saw that the food was unprepared because the brāhmaṇa had not cooked it.
text:
> kṛtamālāya snāna kari' āilā tāṅra ghare
> bhikṣā ki dibena vipra,---pāka nāhi kare
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛtamālāya]]---in the Kṛtamālā River; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---bathing; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to the home; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---offering of alms; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:d:dibena]]---what shall give; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:p:pāka]]---cooking; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---did not do.
translation: After bathing in the river Kṛtamālā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to the brāhmaṇa's house to take lunch, but He saw that the food was unprepared because the brāhmaṇa had not cooked it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.181
description: Seeing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My dear sir, please tell Me why you have not cooked. It is already noon."
text:
> mahāprabhu kahe tāṅre,---śuna mahāśaya
> madhyāhna haila, kene pāka nāhi haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]] [[synonyms:m:mahāśaya]]---please hear, My dear sir; [[synonyms:m:madhya]]-[[synonyms:a:ahna]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---it is already noon; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:p:pāka]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---you did not cook.
translation: Seeing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My dear sir, please tell Me why you have not cooked. It is already noon."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.182
description: The brāhmaṇa replied, "My dear Lord, we are living in the forest. For the time being we cannot get all the ingredients for cooking.
text:
> vipra kahe,---prabhu, mora araṇye vasati
> pākera sāmagrī vane nā mile samprati

translation: The brāhmaṇa replied, "My dear Lord, we are living in the forest. For the time being we cannot get all the ingredients for cooking.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.183
description: "When Lakṣmaṇa brings all the vegetables, fruits and roots from the forest, Sītā will do the necessary cooking."
text:
> vanya śāka-phala-mūla ānibe lakṣmaṇa
> tabe sītā karibena pāka-prayojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vanya]]---of the forest; [[synonyms:ś:śāka]]---vegetables; [[synonyms:p:phala]]-[[synonyms:m:mūla]]---fruits and roots; [[synonyms:ā:ānibe]]---will bring; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmaṇa]]---Lakṣmaṇa; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---that time; [[synonyms:s:sītā]]---mother Sītā; [[synonyms:k:karibena]]---will do; [[synonyms:p:pāka]]-[[synonyms:p:prayojana]]---the necessary cooking.
translation: "When Lakṣmaṇa brings all the vegetables, fruits and roots from the forest, Sītā will do the necessary cooking."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.184

synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:u:upāsanā]]---method of worship; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tuṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---was very much pleased; [[synonyms:ā:āste]]-[[synonyms:v:vyaste]]---with great haste; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---//brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:r:randhana]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---began to cook.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very much satisfied to hear about the brāhmaṇa's method of worship. Finally the brāhmaṇa hastily made arrangements for cooking.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.185

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "Please do not think this way any longer. You are a learned paṇḍita. Why don't you consider the case?"

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "Sītādevī, the dearmost wife of the Supreme Lord Rāmacandra, certainly has a spiritual form full of bliss. No one can see her with material eyes, for no materialist has such power.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.193
