translation: "As soon as Rāvaṇa arrived before Sītā, she disappeared. Then just to cheat Rāvaṇa she sent an illusory, material form.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.194
description: "Spiritual substance is never within the jurisdiction of the material conception. This is always the verdict of the Vedas and Purāṇas."
text:
> aprākṛta vastu nahe prākṛta-gocara
> veda-purāṇete ei kahe nirantara
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aprākṛta]]---spiritual; [[synonyms:v:vastu]]---substance; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:p:prākṛta]]---of matter; [[synonyms:g:gocara]]---within the jurisdiction; [[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:p:purāṇete]]---the //Vedas// and the //Purāṇas//; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---say; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---always.
translation: "Spiritual substance is never within the jurisdiction of the material conception. This is always the verdict of the Vedas and Purāṇas."
purport:
As stated in the //Kaṭha Upaniṣad// (2.3.9, 12):

> na saṁdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpam asya
> na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam
> hṛdā manīṣā manasābhikḷpto
> ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
>
> naiva vācā na manasā
> prāptuṁ śakyo na cakṣuṣā

"Spirit is not within the jurisdiction of material eyes, words or mind."

Similarly, //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.84.13) states:

> yasyātma-buddhiḥ kuṇape tri-dhātuke
> sva-dhīḥ kalatrādiṣu bhauma ijya-dhīḥ
> yat-tīrtha-buddhiḥ salile na karhicij
> janeṣv abhijñeṣu sa eva go-kharaḥ

"A human being who identifies his body made of three elements with his self, who considers the by-products of his body to be his kinsmen, who considers the land of his birth worshipable, and who goes to a place of pilgrimage simply to take a bath rather than to meet men of transcendental knowledge there, is to be considered like an ass or a cow."

These are some Vedic statements about spiritual substance. Spiritual substance cannot be seen by the unintelligent, because they do not have the eyes or the mentality to see the spirit soul. Consequently they think that there is no such thing as spirit. But the followers of the Vedic injunctions take their information from Vedic statements, such as the verses from the //Kaṭha Upaniṣad// and //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// quoted above.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.195
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then assured the brāhmaṇa, "Have faith in My words and do not burden your mind any longer with this misconception."
text:
> viśvāsa karaha tumi āmāra vacane
> punarapi ku-bhāvanā nā kariha mane
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viśvāsa]] [[synonyms:k:karaha]]---believe; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:v:vacane]]---in the words; [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:k:ku]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvanā]]---misconception; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do not do; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then assured the brāhmaṇa, "Have faith in My words and do not burden your mind any longer with this misconception."
purport: This is the process of spiritual understanding. //Acintyā khalu ye bhāvā na tāṁs tarkeṇa yojayet:// "We should not try to understand things beyond our material conception by argument and counterargument." //Mahā-jano yena gataḥ sa panthāḥ:// "We have to follow in the footsteps of great authorities coming down in the //paramparā// system." If we approach a bona fide //ācārya// and keep faith in his words, spiritual realization will be easy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.196
description: Although the brāhmaṇa was fasting, he had faith in the words of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and accepted food. In this way his life was saved.
text:
> prabhura vacane viprera ha-ila viśvāsa
> bhojana karila, haila jīvanera āśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:v:vacane]]---in the words of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:viprera]]---of the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---was; [[synonyms:v:viśvāsa]]---faith; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---he took his lunch; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:j:jīvanera]]---for living; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---hope.
translation: Although the brāhmaṇa was fasting, he had faith in the words of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and accepted food. In this way his life was saved.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.197
description: After thus assuring the brāhmaṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu proceeded further into southern India and finally arrived at Durvaśana, where He bathed in the river Kṛtamālā.
text:
> tāṅre āśvāsiyā prabhu karilā gamana
> kṛtamālāya snāna kari āilā durvaśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]] [[synonyms:ā:āśvāsiyā]]---assuring him; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---departed; [[synonyms:k:kṛtamālāya]]---in the river known as Kṛtamālā; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---bathing; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:d:durvaśana]]---to Durvaśana.
translation: After thus assuring the brāhmaṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu proceeded further into southern India and finally arrived at Durvaśana, where He bathed in the river Kṛtamālā.
purport: Presently the Kṛtamālā River is known as the river Bhāgāi. This river has three tributaries, named Surulī, Varāha-nadī and Baṭṭilla-guṇḍu. The river Kṛtamālā is also mentioned in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.39) by the sage Karabhājana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.198
description: At Durvaśana Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Lord Rāmacandra, and on the hill known as Mahendra-śaila He saw Lord Paraśurāma.
text:
> durvaśane raghunāthe kaila daraśana
> mahendra-śaile paraśurāmera kaila vandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:durvaśane]]---at Durvaśana; [[synonyms:r:raghunāthe]]---Lord Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited; [[synonyms:m:mahendra]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaile]]---on Mahendra-śaila; [[synonyms:p:paraśu]]-[[synonyms:r:rāmera]]---to Lord Paraśurāma; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---offered prayers.
translation: At Durvaśana Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Lord Rāmacandra, and on the hill known as Mahendra-śaila He saw Lord Paraśurāma.
purport: In Durvaśana, or Darbhaśayana, seven miles east of Ramnad, there is a temple of Lord Rāmacandra overlooking the ocean. The hill known as Mahendra-śaila is near Tirunelveli, and at the end of this hill is a city known as Tiruchendurḍ. West of Mahendra-śaila is the territory of Tribāṅkura. There is mention of Mahendra-śaila in the //Rāmāyaṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.199
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then went to Setubandha [Rāmeśvara], where He took His bath at the place called Dhanustīrtha. From there He visited the Rāmeśvara temple and then took rest.
text:
> setubandhe āsi' kaila dhanustīrthe snāna
> rāmeśvara dekhi' tāhāṅ karila viśrāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:setubandhe]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming to Setubandha; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:d:dhanuḥ]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrthe]] [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing at the holy place known as Dhanustīrtha; [[synonyms:r:rāmeśvara]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---visiting the holy place Rāmeśvara; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:v:viśrāma]]---took rest.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then went to Setubandha [Rāmeśvara], where He took His bath at the place called Dhanustīrtha. From there He visited the Rāmeśvara temple and then took rest.
purport:
The path through the ocean to the islands known as Mandṇḍapam and Pambam consists partly of sand and partly of water. The island of Pambam is about eleven miles long and six miles wide. On this island, four miles north of Pambam Harbor, is Setubandha, where the temple of Rāmeśvara is located. This is a temple of Lord Śiva, and the name Rāmeśvara indicates that he is a great personality whose worshipable Deity is Lord Rāma. Thus the Lord Śiva found in the temple of Rāmeśvara is a great devotee of Lord Rāmacandra. It is said, //devī-pattanam ārabhya gaccheyuḥ setu-bandhanam:// "After visiting the temple of the goddess Durgā, one should go to the temple of Rāmeśvara." \\
 \\

In this area there are twenty-four different holy places, one of which is Dhanustīrtha, located about twelve miles southeast of Rāmeśvara. It is near the last station of the South Indian Railway, a station called Ramnadā. It is said that here, on the request of Rāvaṇa's younger brother Vibhīṣaṇa, Lord Rāmacandra destroyed the bridge to Laṅkā with His bow while returning to His capital. It is also said that one who visits Dhanustīrtha is liberated from the cycle of birth and death, and that one who bathes there gets all the fruitive results of performing the //yajña// known as //agniṣṭoma.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.2
description: All glories to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Śrī Advaita Prabhu! And all glories to the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!
text:
> jaya jaya śrī-caitanya jaya nityānanda
> jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---unto Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jayaadvaita]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---all glories to Advaita Prabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---to the devotees of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All glories to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Śrī Advaita Prabhu! And all glories to the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.20
description: That day, Lord Caitanya remained there and accepted prasāda at his house. After bestowing mercy upon him in this way, the Lord proceeded ahead.
text:
> sei dina tāṅra ghare rahi' bhikṣā kari'
> tāṅre kṛpā kari' āge calilā gaurahari
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:seidina]]---on that day; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---the house of that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---staying; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---accepting //prasāda//; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing mercy; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---ahead; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---departed; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:h:hari]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: That day, Lord Caitanya remained there and accepted prasāda at his house. After bestowing mercy upon him in this way, the Lord proceeded ahead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.200
description: There, among the brāhmaṇas, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu listened to the Kūrma Purāṇa, wherein was mentioned the chaste woman's narration.
text:
> vipra-sabhāya śune tāṅhā kūrma-purāṇa
> tāra madhye āilā pativratā-upākhyāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipra]]-[[synonyms:s:sabhāya]]---among the assembly of //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hears; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhā]]---there; [[synonyms:k:kūrma]]-[[synonyms:p:purāṇa]]---the //Kūrma Purāṇa//; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that book; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:pati]]-[[synonyms:v:vratā]]---of the chaste woman; [[synonyms:u:upākhyāna]]---narration.
translation: There, among the brāhmaṇas, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu listened to the Kūrma Purāṇa, wherein was mentioned the chaste woman's narration.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura remarks that only two //khaṇḍas// of the //Kūrma Purāṇa// are now available, namely the //Pūrva-khaṇḍa// and //Uttara-khaṇḍa.// Sometimes it is said that the //Kūrma Purāṇa// contains six thousand verses, but originally the //Kūrma Purāṇa// contained seventeen thousand verses. According to //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// there are seventeen thousand verses in the //Kūrma Purāṇa,// which is one of the eighteen //Mahā-purāṇas.// The //Kūrma Purāṇa// is considered the fifteenth of these //Mahā-purāṇas.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.201
description: Śrīmatī Sītādevī is the mother of the three worlds and the wife of Lord Rāmacandra. Among chaste women she is supreme, and she is the daughter of King Janaka.
text:
> pativratā-śiromaṇi janaka-nandinī
> jagatera mātā sītā---rāmera gṛhiṇī
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pati]]-[[synonyms:v:vratā]]---chaste woman; [[synonyms:ś:śiromaṇi]]---the topmost; [[synonyms:j:janaka]]-[[synonyms:n:nandinī]]---is the daughter of King Janaka; [[synonyms:j:jagatera]]---of all the three worlds; [[synonyms:m:mātā]]---the mother; [[synonyms:s:sītā]]---Sītā; [[synonyms:r:rāmera]]---of Lord Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:g:gṛhiṇī]]---wife.
translation: Śrīmatī Sītādevī is the mother of the three worlds and the wife of Lord Rāmacandra. Among chaste women she is supreme, and she is the daughter of King Janaka.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.202
description: When Rāvaṇa came to kidnap mother Sītā and she saw him, she took shelter of the fire-god, Agni. The fire-god covered the body of mother Sītā, and in this way she was protected from the hands of Rāvaṇa.
text:
> rāvaṇa dekhiyā sītā laila agnira śaraṇa
> rāvaṇa haite agni kaila sītāke āvaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāvaṇa]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---after seeing Rāvaṇa; [[synonyms:s:sītā]]---mother Sītā; [[synonyms:l:laila]]---took; [[synonyms:a:agnira]]---of fire; [[synonyms:ś:śaraṇa]]---shelter; [[synonyms:r:rāvaṇa]]---Rāvaṇa; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:a:agni]]---fire; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:sītāke]]---unto mother Sītā; [[synonyms:ā:āvaraṇa]]---covering.
translation: When Rāvaṇa came to kidnap mother Sītā and she saw him, she took shelter of the fire-god, Agni. The fire-god covered the body of mother Sītā, and in this way she was protected from the hands of Rāvaṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.203
description: Upon hearing from the Kūrma Purāṇa how Rāvaṇa had kidnapped a false form of mother Sītā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very much satisfied.
text:
> 'māyā-sītā' rāvaṇa nila, śunilā ākhyāne
> śuni' mahāprabhu haila ānandita mane
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:s:sītā]]---false, illusory Sītā; [[synonyms:r:rāvaṇa]]---the demon Rāvaṇa; [[synonyms:n:nila]]---took; [[synonyms:ś:śunilā]]---heard; [[synonyms:ā:ākhyāne]]---in the narration of the //Kūrma Purāṇa//; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very happy; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---within the mind.
translation: Upon hearing from the Kūrma Purāṇa how Rāvaṇa had kidnapped a false form of mother Sītā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very much satisfied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.204
description: The fire-god, Agni, took away the real Sītā and brought her to the place of Pārvatī, goddess Durgā. An illusory form of mother Sītā was then delivered to Rāvaṇa, and in this way Rāvaṇa was cheated.
text:
> sītā lañā rākhilena pārvatīra sthāne
> 'māyā-sītā' diyā agni vañcilā rāvaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sītā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking away mother Sītā; [[synonyms:r:rākhilena]]---kept; [[synonyms:p:pārvatīra]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---with mother Pārvatī, or goddess Durgā; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:s:sītā]]---the false, illusory form of Sītā; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---delivering; [[synonyms:a:agni]]---fire-god; [[synonyms:v:vañcilā]]---cheated; [[synonyms:r:rāvaṇe]]---the demon Rāvaṇa.
translation: The fire-god, Agni, took away the real Sītā and brought her to the place of Pārvatī, goddess Durgā. An illusory form of mother Sītā was then delivered to Rāvaṇa, and in this way Rāvaṇa was cheated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.205
description: After Rāvaṇa was killed by Lord Rāmacandra, Sītādevī was brought before the fire and tested.
text:
> raghunātha āsi' yabe rāvaṇe mārila
> agni-parīkṣā dite yabe sītāre ānila
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Lord Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:r:rāvaṇe]]---Rāvaṇa; [[synonyms:m:mārila]]---killed; [[synonyms:a:agni]]-[[synonyms:p:parīkṣā]]---test by fire; [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:s:sītāre]]---Sītā; [[synonyms:ā:ānila]]---brought.
translation: After Rāvaṇa was killed by Lord Rāmacandra, Sītādevī was brought before the fire and tested.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.206
description: When the illusory Sītā was brought before the fire by Lord Rāmacandra, the fire-god made the illusory form disappear and delivered the real Sītā to Lord Rāmacandra.
text:
> tabe māyā-sītā agni kari antardhāna
> satya-sītā āni' dila rāma-vidyamāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:s:sītā]]---the illusory form of Sītā; [[synonyms:a:agni]]---the fire-god; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---doing; [[synonyms:a:antardhāna]]---disappearing; [[synonyms:s:satya]]-[[synonyms:s:sītā]]---real Sītā; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---delivered; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]---of Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:v:vidyamāna]]---in the presence.
translation: When the illusory Sītā was brought before the fire by Lord Rāmacandra, the fire-god made the illusory form disappear and delivered the real Sītā to Lord Rāmacandra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.207
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard this story, He was very much pleased, and He remembered the words of Rāmadāsa Vipra.
text:
> śuniñā prabhura ānandita haila mana
> rāmadāsa-viprera kathā ha-ila smaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniñā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very much pleased; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:r:rāmadāsa]]-[[synonyms:v:viprera]]---of the //brāhmaṇa// known as Rāmadāsa; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---words; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]] [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---He remembered.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard this story, He was very much pleased, and He remembered the words of Rāmadāsa Vipra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.208
description: Indeed, when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard these conclusive statements from the Kūrma Purāṇa, He felt great happiness. After asking the brāhmaṇas' permission, He took possession of those manuscript leaves.
text:
> e-saba siddhānta śuni' prabhura ānanda haila
> brāhmaṇera sthāne māgi' sei patra nila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:s:siddhānta]]---all these conclusive statements; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---happiness; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇera]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---from the //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:m:māgi']]---asking; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:p:patra]]---leaves; [[synonyms:n:nila]]---took.
translation: Indeed, when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard these conclusive statements from the Kūrma Purāṇa, He felt great happiness. After asking the brāhmaṇas' permission, He took possession of those manuscript leaves.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.209
description: Since the Kūrma Purāṇa was very old, the manuscript was also very old. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took possession of the original leaves in order to have direct evidence. The text was copied onto new leaves in order that the Purāṇa be replaced.
text:
> nūtana patra lekhāñā pustake deoyāila
> pratīti lāgi' purātana patra māgi' nila
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nūtana]]---new; [[synonyms:p:patra]]---leaves; [[synonyms:l:lekhāñā]]---getting written; [[synonyms:p:pustake]]---the book; [[synonyms:d:deoyāila]]---He gave; [[synonyms:p:pratīti]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for direct evidence; [[synonyms:p:purātana]]---the old; [[synonyms:p:patra]]---leaves; [[synonyms:m:māgi']]---requesting; [[synonyms:n:nila]]---He took.
translation: Since the Kūrma Purāṇa was very old, the manuscript was also very old. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took possession of the original leaves in order to have direct evidence. The text was copied onto new leaves in order that the Purāṇa be replaced.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.21
description: At the holy place known as Skanda-kṣetra, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Skanda. From there He went to Trimaṭha, where He saw the Viṣṇu Deity Trivikrama.
text:
> skanda-kṣetra-tīrthe kaila skanda daraśana
> trimaṭha āilā, tāhāṅ dekhi' trivikrama
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:skanda]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣetra]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrthe]]---in the holy place known as Skanda-kṣetra; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:skanda]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting Lord Skanda (Kārttikeya, son of Lord Śiva); [[synonyms:t:trimaṭha]]---at Trimaṭha; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:trivikrama]]---a form of Lord Viṣṇu, Trivikrama.
translation: At the holy place known as Skanda-kṣetra, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Skanda. From there He went to Trimaṭha, where He saw the Viṣṇu Deity Trivikrama.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.210
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to southern Mathurā [Madurai] and delivered the original manuscript of the Kūrma Purāṇa to Rāmadāsa Vipra.
text:
> patra lañā punaḥ dakṣiṇa-mathurā āilā
> rāmadāsa vipre sei patra āni dilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:patra]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking those leaves; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mathurā]]---to southern Mathurā; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:r:rāmadāsa]] [[synonyms:v:vipre]]---unto the //brāhmaṇa// known as Rāmadāsa; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:patra]]---those leaves; [[synonyms:ā:āni]]---bringing back; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---delivered.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to southern Mathurā [Madurai] and delivered the original manuscript of the Kūrma Purāṇa to Rāmadāsa Vipra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.211-212
description: "When he was petitioned by mother Sītā, the fire-god, Agni, brought forth an illusory form of Sītā, and Rāvaṇa, who had ten heads, kidnapped the false Sītā. The original Sītā then went to the abode of the fire-god. When Lord Rāmacandra tested the body of Sītā, it was the false, illusory Sītā that entered the fire. At that time the fire-god brought the original Sītā from his abode and delivered her to Lord Rāmacandra."
text:
> sītayārādhito vahniś
> chāyā-sītām ajījanat
> tāṁ jahāra daśa-grīvaḥ
> sītā vahni-puraṁ gatā
>
> parīkṣā-samaye vahniṁ
> chāyā-sītā viveśa sā
> vahniḥ sītāṁ samānīya
> tat-purastād anīnayat
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sītayā]]---by mother Sītā; [[synonyms:ā:ārādhitaḥ]]---being called for; [[synonyms:v:vahniḥ]]---the fire-god; [[synonyms:c:chāyā]]-[[synonyms:s:sītām]]---the illusory form of mother Sītā; [[synonyms:a:ajījanat]]---created; [[synonyms:t:tām]]---her; [[synonyms:j:jahāra]]---kidnapped; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:g:grīvaḥ]]---the ten-faced Rāvaṇa; [[synonyms:s:sītā]]---mother Sītā; [[synonyms:v:vahni]]-[[synonyms:p:puram]]---to the abode of the fire-god; [[synonyms:g:gatā]]---departed; [[synonyms:p:parīkṣā]]-[[synonyms:s:samaye]]---at the time of testing; [[synonyms:v:vahnim]]---the fire; [[synonyms:c:chāyā]]-[[synonyms:s:sītā]]---the illusory form of Sītā; [[synonyms:v:viveśa]]---entered; [[synonyms:s:sā]]---she; [[synonyms:v:vahniḥ]]---the fire-god; [[synonyms:s:sītām]]---the original mother Sītā; [[synonyms:s:samānīya]]---bringing back; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:p:purastāt]]---in His presence; [[synonyms:a:anīnayat]]---brought back.
translation: "When he was petitioned by mother Sītā, the fire-god, Agni, brought forth an illusory form of Sītā, and Rāvaṇa, who had ten heads, kidnapped the false Sītā. The original Sītā then went to the abode of the fire-god. When Lord Rāmacandra tested the body of Sītā, it was the false, illusory Sītā that entered the fire. At that time the fire-god brought the original Sītā from his abode and delivered her to Lord Rāmacandra."
purport: These two verses are taken from the //Kūrma Purāṇa.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.213
description: Rāmadāsa Vipra was very much pleased to receive the original leaf manuscript of the Kūrma Purāṇa, and he immediately fell down before the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and began to cry.
text:
> patra pāñā viprera haila ānandita mana
> prabhura caraṇe dhari' karaye krandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:patra]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting the leaves; [[synonyms:v:viprera]]---of the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---pleased; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---taking; [[synonyms:k:karaye]]---does; [[synonyms:k:krandana]]---crying.
translation: Rāmadāsa Vipra was very much pleased to receive the original leaf manuscript of the Kūrma Purāṇa, and he immediately fell down before the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and began to cry.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.214
description: After receiving the manuscript, the brāhmaṇa, being very much pleased, said, "Sir, You are Lord Rāmacandra Himself and have come in the dress of a sannyāsī to give me audience.
text:
> vipra kahe,---tumi sākṣāt śrī-raghunandana
> sannyāsīra veṣe more dilā daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the //brāhmaṇa// said; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:raghunandana]]---Lord Śrī Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsīra]] [[synonyms:v:veṣe]]---in the dress of a mendicant; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto me; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---You gave; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---audience.
translation: After receiving the manuscript, the brāhmaṇa, being very much pleased, said, "Sir, You are Lord Rāmacandra Himself and have come in the dress of a sannyāsī to give me audience.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.215
description: "My dear Sir, You have delivered me from a very unhappy condition. I request that You take Your lunch at my place. Please accept this invitation.
text:
> mahā-duḥkha ha-ite more karilā nistāra
> āji mora ghare bhikṣā kara aṅgīkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---great unhappiness; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ite]]---from; [[synonyms:m:more]]---me; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---You delivered; [[synonyms:ā:āji]]---today; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at home; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---lunch; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---do; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]]---accept.
translation: "My dear Sir, You have delivered me from a very unhappy condition. I request that You take Your lunch at my place. Please accept this invitation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.216
description: "Due to my mental distress I could not give You a very nice lunch the other day. Now, by good fortune, You have come again to my home."
text:
> mano-duḥkhe bhāla bhikṣā nā dila sei dine
> mora bhāgye punarapi pāiluṅ daraśane
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mano]]-[[synonyms:d:duḥkhe]]---out of great mental distress; [[synonyms:b:bhāla]] [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---good lunch; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---could not give You; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---that day; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:b:bhāgye]]---because of my good fortune; [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:p:pāiluṅ]]---I have gotten; [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---visit.
translation: "Due to my mental distress I could not give You a very nice lunch the other day. Now, by good fortune, You have come again to my home."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.217
description: Saying this, the brāhmaṇa very happily cooked food, and a first-class dinner was offered to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> eta bali' sei vipra sukhe pāka kaila
> uttama prakāre prabhuke bhikṣā karāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in great happiness; [[synonyms:p:pāka]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---cooked; [[synonyms:u:uttama]] [[synonyms:p:prakāre]]---very nicely; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]---lunch; [[synonyms:k:karāila]]---gave.
translation: Saying this, the brāhmaṇa very happily cooked food, and a first-class dinner was offered to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.218
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed that night in the house of the brāhmaṇa. Then, after showing him mercy, the Lord started toward Tāmraparṇī in Pāṇḍya-deśa.
text:
> sei rātri tāhāṅ rahi' tāṅre kṛpā kari'
> pāṇḍya-deśe tāmraparṇī gelā gaurahari
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:r:rātri]]---that night; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---staying; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing mercy; [[synonyms:p:pāṇḍya]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in the country known as Pāṇḍyadeśa; [[synonyms:t:tāmraparṇī]]---to the place named Tāmraparṇī; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed that night in the house of the brāhmaṇa. Then, after showing him mercy, the Lord started toward Tāmraparṇī in Pāṇḍya-deśa.
purport: Pāṇḍya-deśa is situated in the southern part of India known as Kerala and Cola. In all these areas there were many kings with the title Pāṇḍya who ruled over Madurai and Rāmeśvara. In the //Rāmāyaṇa// the name of Tāmraparṇī is mentioned. Tāmraparṇī is also known as Puruṇai and is situated on the bank of the Tinebheli River. This river flows into the Bay of Bengal. Tāmraparṇī is also mentioned in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.39) Popup

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.219
description: There was also a temple of Lord Viṣṇu at Naya-tripati on the bank of the river Tāmraparṇī, and after bathing in the river, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the Deity with great curiosity and wandered on.
text:
> tāmraparṇī snāna kari' tāmraparṇī-tīre
> naya tripati dekhi' bule kutūhale
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāmraparṇī]]---in the Tāmraparṇī River; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---taking a bath; [[synonyms:t:tāmraparṇī]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank of the Tāmraparṇī River; [[synonyms:n:naya]] [[synonyms:t:tripati]]---the Deity named Naya-tripati; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after seeing; [[synonyms:b:bule]]---wandered on; [[synonyms:k:kutūhale]]---in great curiosity.
translation: There was also a temple of Lord Viṣṇu at Naya-tripati on the bank of the river Tāmraparṇī, and after bathing in the river, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the Deity with great curiosity and wandered on.
purport: This Naya-tripati is also called Alwar Tirunagarai. It is a town about seventeen miles southeast of Tirunelveli. There are nine temples there of Śrīpati, or Viṣṇu. All the Deities of the temples assemble together during a yearly festival in the town.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.22
description: After visiting the temple of Trivikrama, the Lord returned to Siddhavaṭa, where He again visited the house of the brāhmaṇa, who was now constantly chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.
text:
> punaḥ siddhavaṭa āilā sei vipra-ghare
> sei vipra kṛṣṇa-nāma laya nirantare
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:s:siddha]]-[[synonyms:v:vaṭa]]---to the place known as Siddhavaṭa; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]-[[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in the house of the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---that //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:laya]]---chants; [[synonyms:n:nirantare]]---constantly.
translation: After visiting the temple of Trivikrama, the Lord returned to Siddhavaṭa, where He again visited the house of the brāhmaṇa, who was now constantly chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.220
description: After this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to a holy place known as Ciyaḍatalā, where He saw the Deities of the two brothers Lord Rāmacandra and Lakṣmaṇa. He then proceeded to Tila-kāñcī, where He saw the temple of Lord Śiva.
text:
> ciyaḍatalā tīrthe dekhi' śrī-rāma-lakṣmaṇa
> tila-kāñcī āsi' kaila śiva daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:ciyaḍatalā]]---named Ciyaḍatalā; [[synonyms:t:tīrthe]]---at the holy place; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣmaṇa]]---the Deity of Lord Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa; [[synonyms:t:tila]]-[[synonyms:k:kāñcī]]---to Tila-kāñcī; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting the temple of Lord Śiva.
translation: After this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to a holy place known as Ciyaḍatalā, where He saw the Deities of the two brothers Lord Rāmacandra and Lakṣmaṇa. He then proceeded to Tila-kāñcī, where He saw the temple of Lord Śiva.
purport: Ciyaḍatalā is sometimes known as Cheratalā. It is near the city of Kaila, and there is a temple there dedicated to Lord Śrī Rāmacandra and His brother Lakṣmaṇa. Tila-kāñcī is about thirty miles northeast of the city of Tirunelveli.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.221
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then visited the holy place named Gajendra-mokṣaṇa, where He went to a temple of Lord Viṣṇu. He then came to Pānāgaḍi, a holy place where He saw the Deities of Lord Rāmacandra and Sītā.
text:
> gajendra-mokṣaṇa-tīrthe dekhi viṣṇu-mūrti
> pānāgaḍi-tīrthe āsi' dekhila sītāpati
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gajendra]]-[[synonyms:m:mokṣaṇa]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrthe]]---at the holy place named Gajendra-mokṣaṇa; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---seeing; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---the Deity of Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:p:pānāgaḍi]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrthe]]---to the holy place Pānāgaḍi; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---saw; [[synonyms:s:sītā]]-[[synonyms:p:pati]]---Lord Śrī Rāmacandra and Sītādevī.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then visited the holy place named Gajendra-mokṣaṇa, where He went to a temple of Lord Viṣṇu. He then came to Pānāgaḍi, a holy place where He saw the Deities of Lord Rāmacandra and Sītā.
purport: The Gajendra-mokṣaṇa temple is sometimes mistaken for a temple of Lord Śiva. It is about two miles south of the city of Kaivera. Actually the Deity is not of Lord Śiva but of Viṣṇu. Pānāgaḍi is about thirty miles south of Tirunelveli. Formerly the temple there contained the Deity of Śrī Rāmacandra, but later the devotees of Lord Śiva replaced Lord Rāmacandra with a deity of Lord Śiva named Rāmeśvara or Rāma-liṅga Śiva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.222
description: Later the Lord went to Cāmtāpura, where He saw the Deities of Lord Rāmacandra and Lakṣmaṇa. He then went to Śrī Vaikuṇṭha and saw the temple of Lord Viṣṇu there.
text:
> cāmtāpure āsi' dekhi' śrī-rāma-lakṣmaṇa
> śrī-vaikuṇṭhe āsi' kaila viṣṇu daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāmtāpure]]---to Cāmtāpura; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣmaṇa]]---Lord Rāmacandra and Lakṣmaṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vaikuṇṭhe]] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming to Śrī Vaikuṇṭha; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing the temple of Lord Viṣṇu.
translation: Later the Lord went to Cāmtāpura, where He saw the Deities of Lord Rāmacandra and Lakṣmaṇa. He then went to Śrī Vaikuṇṭha and saw the temple of Lord Viṣṇu there.
purport: Cāmtāpura is sometimes called Ceṅgānura and is located in the state of Tribāṅkura. A temple of Lord Rāmacandra and Lakṣmaṇa is located there. Śrī Vaikuṇṭha-about four miles north of Alwar Tirunagarai and sixteen miles southeast of Tirunelveli-is situated on the bank of the Tāmraparṇī River.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.223
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then went to Malaya-parvata and offered prayers to Agastya Muni. He then visited Kanyā-kumārī [Cape Comorin].
text:
> malaya-parvate kaila agastya-vandana
> kanyā-kumārī tāṅhāṅ kaila daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:malaya]]-[[synonyms:p:parvate]]---in the Malaya Hills; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:a:agastya]]-[[synonyms:v:vandana]]---obeisances to Agastya Muni; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]-[[synonyms:k:kumārī]]---Kanyā-kumārī; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visited.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then went to Malaya-parvata and offered prayers to Agastya Muni. He then visited Kanyā-kumārī [Cape Comorin].
purport: The range of mountains in South India beginning at Kerala and extending to Cape Comorin is called Malaya-parvata. Concerning Agastya, there are four opinions: (1) There is a temple of Agastya Muni in the village of Agastyampallī in the district of Tanjoreāñ. (2) There is a temple of Lord Skanda on a hill known as Śiva-giri, and it is supposed to have been established by Agastya Muni. (3) Some say that near Cape Comorin there is a hill known as Paṭhiyā, which was supposed to have served as Agastya Muni's residence. (4) There is a place known as Agastya-malaya, which is a range of hills on both sides of the Tāmraparṇī River. Cape Comorin itself is known as Kanyā-kumārī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.224
description: After visiting Kanyā-kumārī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to Āmlitalā, where He saw the Deity of Śrī Rāmacandra. Thereafter He went to a place known as Mallāra-deśa, where a community of Bhaṭṭathāris lived.
text:
> āmlitalāya dekhi' śrī-rāma gaurahari
> mallāra-deśete āilā yathā bhaṭṭathāri
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmlitalāya]]---at Āmlitalā; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rāma]]---the Deity of Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mallāra]]-[[synonyms:d:deśete]]---to Mallāra-deśa; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---where; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭathāri]]---the Bhaṭṭathāri community.
translation: After visiting Kanyā-kumārī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to Āmlitalā, where He saw the Deity of Śrī Rāmacandra. Thereafter He went to a place known as Mallāra-deśa, where a community of Bhaṭṭathāris lived.
purport: North of Mallāra-deśa is South Kanaraḍā. To the east is Coorg and Mysoreīśū, to the south is Cochin, and to the west is the Arabian Sea. As far as the Bhaṭṭathāris are concerned, they are a nomadic community. They camp wherever they like and have no fixed place of residence. Outwardly they take up the dress of //sannyāsīs,// but their real business is stealing and cheating. They allure others to supply women for their camp, and they cheat many women and keep them within their community. In this way they increase their population. In Bengal also there is a similar community. Actually, all over the world there are nomadic communities whose business is simply to allure, cheat and steal innocent women.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.225
description: After visiting Mallāra-deśa, Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Tamāla-kārtika and then to Vetāpani. There He saw the temple of Raghunātha, Lord Rāmacandra, and passed the night.
text:
> tamāla-kārtika dekhi' āila vetāpani
> raghunātha dekhi' tāhāṅ vañcilā rajanī
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tamāla]]-[[synonyms:k:kārtika]]---the place named Tamāla-kārtika; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:v:vetāpani]]---to Vetāpani; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the temple of Lord Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:v:vañcilā]] [[synonyms:r:rajanī]]---passed the night.
translation: After visiting Mallāra-deśa, Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Tamāla-kārtika and then to Vetāpani. There He saw the temple of Raghunātha, Lord Rāmacandra, and passed the night.
purport: Tamāla-kārtika is forty-four miles south of Tirunelveli and two miles south of Aramavallī Mountain. It is located within the jurisdiction of Tovalai. At Tamāla-kārtika is a temple of Subrahmaṇya, or Lord Kārtika, the son of Lord Śiva. Vetāpani, or Vātāpāṇī, is north of Kaila in the Trivandrum district. It is also known as Bhūtapaṇḍi and is within the jurisdiction of the Tobala district. It is understood that formerly there was a Deity of Lord Rāmacandra there. Later the Deity was replaced with a deity of Lord Śiva known as Rāmeśvara or Bhūtanātha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.226
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was accompanied by His servant, Kṛṣṇadāsa. He was a brāhmaṇa, but he met with the Bhaṭṭathāris there.
text:
> gosāñira saṅge rahe kṛṣṇadāsa brāhmaṇa
> bhaṭṭathāri-saha tāhāṅ haila daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---there was; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]] [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---a //brāhmaṇa// servant named Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭathāri]]-[[synonyms:s:saha]]---with the Bhaṭṭathāris; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---a meeting.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was accompanied by His servant, Kṛṣṇadāsa. He was a brāhmaṇa, but he met with the Bhaṭṭathāris there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.227
description: With women the Bhaṭṭathāris allured the brāhmaṇa Kṛṣṇadāsa, who was simple and gentle. By virtue of their bad association, they polluted his intelligence.
text:
> strī-dhana dekhāñā tāṅra lobha janmāila
> ārya sarala viprera buddhi-nāśa kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:strī]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---women; [[synonyms:d:dekhāñā]]---showing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:l:lobha]]---attraction; [[synonyms:j:janmāila]]---they created; [[synonyms:ā:ārya]]---gentleman; [[synonyms:s:sarala]]---simple; [[synonyms:v:viprera]]---of the //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:b:buddhi]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---loss of intelligence; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---they made.
translation: With women the Bhaṭṭathāris allured the brāhmaṇa Kṛṣṇadāsa, who was simple and gentle. By virtue of their bad association, they polluted his intelligence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.228
description: Allured by the Bhaṭṭathāris, Kṛṣṇadāsa went to their place early in the morning. The Lord also went there very quickly just to find him out.
text:
> prāte uṭhi' āilā vipra bhaṭṭathāri-ghare
> tāhāra uddeśe prabhu āilā satvare
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prāte]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---rising from bed; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:v:vipra]]---the //brāhmaṇa// Kṛṣṇadāsa; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭathāri]]-[[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to the place of the Bhaṭṭathāris; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]] [[synonyms:u:uddeśe]]---for him; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:s:satvare]]---very soon.
translation: Allured by the Bhaṭṭathāris, Kṛṣṇadāsa went to their place early in the morning. The Lord also went there very quickly just to find him out.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.229
description: Upon reaching their community, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked the Bhaṭṭathāris, "Why are you keeping My brāhmaṇa assistant?
text:

translation: Upon reaching their community, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked the Bhaṭṭathāris, "Why are you keeping My brāhmaṇa assistant?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.23
description: After finishing His lunch there, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked the brāhmaṇa, "My dear friend, kindly tell Me what your position is now.
text:
> bhikṣā kari' mahāprabhu tāṅre praśna kaila
> ''kaha vipra, ei tomāra kon daśā haila

translation: After finishing His lunch there, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked the brāhmaṇa, "My dear friend, kindly tell Me what your position is now.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.230
description: "I am in the renounced order of life, and so are you. Yet you are purposefully giving Me pain, and I do not see any good logic in this."
text:
> āmiha sannyāsī dekha, tumiha sannyāsī
> more duḥkha deha,---tomāra 'nyāya' nāhi vāsi

translation: "I am in the renounced order of life, and so are you. Yet you are purposefully giving Me pain, and I do not see any good logic in this."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.231
description: Upon hearing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all the Bhaṭṭathāris came running from all sides with weapons in their hands, desiring to hurt the Lord.
text:
> suna' saba bhaṭṭathāri uṭhe astra lañā
> māribāre āila sabe cāri-dike dhāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:suna']]---hearing; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭathāri]]---nomads; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---rise up; [[synonyms:a:astra]]---weapons; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:m:māribāre]]---to kill; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---all around; [[synonyms:d:dhāñā]]---running.
translation: Upon hearing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all the Bhaṭṭathāris came running from all sides with weapons in their hands, desiring to hurt the Lord.

> khaṇḍa khaṇḍa haila bhaṭṭathāri palāya cāri bhite

translation: However, their weapons fell from their hands and struck their own bodies. When some of the Bhaṭṭathāris were thus cut to pieces, the others ran away in the four directions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.233

translation: While there was much roaring and crying at the Bhaṭṭathāri community, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu grabbed Kṛṣṇadāsa by the hair and took him away.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.234
description: That very night, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His assistant Kṛṣṇadāsa arrived at the bank of the Payasvinī River. They took their bath and then went to see the temple of Ādi-keśava.

> snāna kari' gelā ādi-keśava-mandire

translation: That very night, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His assistant Kṛṣṇadāsa arrived at the bank of the Payasvinī River. They took their bath and then went to see the temple of Ādi-keśava.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.235
description: When the Lord saw the Ādi-keśava temple, He was immediately overwhelmed with ecstasy. Offering various obeisances and prayers, He chanted and danced.

translation: When the Lord saw the Ādi-keśava temple, He was immediately overwhelmed with ecstasy. Offering various obeisances and prayers, He chanted and danced.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.236

translation: All the people there were greatly astonished to see the ecstatic pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. They all received the Lord very well.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.237

> kampāśru-sveda-stambha-pulaka vikāra

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.239-240
description: There is no scripture equal to the Brahma-saṁhitā as far as the final spiritual conclusion is concerned. Indeed, that scripture is the supreme revelation of the glories of Lord Govinda, for it reveals the topmost knowledge about Him. Since all conclusions are briefly presented in the Brahma-saṁhitā, it is essential among all the Vaiṣṇava scriptures.
text:
> siddhānta-śāstra nāhi 'brahma-saṁhitā'ra sama
> govinda-mahimā jñānera parama kāraṇa
>
> alpākṣare kahe siddhānta apāra
> sakala-vaiṣṇava-śāstra-madhye ati sāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:siddhānta]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---conclusive scripture; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṁhitāra]] [[synonyms:s:sama]]---like the scripture //Brahma-saṁhitā//; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---of the glories of Lord Govinda; [[synonyms:j:jñānera]]---of knowledge; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---final; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---cause; [[synonyms:a:alpa]]-[[synonyms:a:akṣare]]---briefly; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---expresses; [[synonyms:s:siddhānta]]---conclusion; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---devotional scriptures; [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---among; [[synonyms:a:atisāra]]---very essential.
translation: There is no scripture equal to the Brahma-saṁhitā as far as the final spiritual conclusion is concerned. Indeed, that scripture is the supreme revelation of the glories of Lord Govinda, for it reveals the topmost knowledge about Him. Since all conclusions are briefly presented in the Brahma-saṁhitā, it is essential among all the Vaiṣṇava scriptures.
purport: The //Brahma-saṁhitā// is a very important scripture. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu acquired the Fifth Chapter from the Ādi-keśava temple. In that Fifth Chapter, the philosophical conclusion of //acintya-bhedābheda-tattva// (simultaneous oneness and difference) is presented. The chapter also presents methods of devotional service; the eighteen-syllable Vedic hymn; discourses on the soul, the Supersoul and fruitive activity; an explanation of Kāma-gāyatrī, //kāma-bīja// and the original Mahā-Viṣṇu; and a detailed description of the spiritual world, specifically Goloka Vṛndāvana. //Brahma-saṁhitā// also explains the demigod Gaṇeśa; Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu; the origin of the Gāyatrī //mantra;// the form of Govinda and His transcendental position and abode; the living entities; the highest goal; the goddess Durgā; the meaning of austerity; the five gross elements; love of Godhead; impersonal Brahman; the initiation of Lord Brahmā; and the vision of transcendental love enabling one to see the Lord. The steps of devotional service are also explained. The mind; //yoga-nidrā;// the goddess of fortune; devotional service in spontaneous ecstasy; incarnations beginning with Lord Rāmacandra; Deities; the conditioned soul and its duties; the truth about Lord Viṣṇu; prayers; Vedic hymns; Lord Śiva; the Vedic literature; personalism and impersonalism; good behavior; and many other subjects are also discussed. There is also a description of the sun and the universal form of the Lord. All these subjects are conclusively explained in a nutshell in the //Brahma-saṁhitā.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.24
description: "Formerly you were constantly chanting the holy name of Lord Rāma. Why are you now constantly chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa?"
text:
> pūrve tumi nirantara laite rāma-nāma
> ebe kene nirantara lao kṛṣṇa-nāma''

translation: "Formerly you were constantly chanting the holy name of Lord Rāma. Why are you now constantly chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.241
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu copied the Brahma-saṁhitā and afterwards, with great pleasure, went to a place known as Ananta Padmanābha.
text:

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu copied the Brahma-saṁhitā and afterwards, with great pleasure, went to a place known as Ananta Padmanābha.
purport: Concerning Ananta Padmanābha, one should refer to //Madhya-līlā,// Chapter One, text 115.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.242
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained for two or three days at Ananta Padmanābha and visited the temple there. Then, in great ecstasy He went to see the temple of Śrī Janārdana.

> ānande dekhite āilā śrī-janārdana

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained for two or three days at Ananta Padmanābha and visited the temple there. Then, in great ecstasy He went to see the temple of Śrī Janārdana.
purport: The temple of Śrī Janārdana is situated twenty-six miles north of Trivandrum, near the Varkāla railway station.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.243
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu chanted and danced at Śrī Janārdana for two days. He then went to the bank of the Payasvinī River and visited the temple of Śaṅkara-nārāyaṇa.
text:

> payasvinī āsiyā dekhe śaṅkara nārāyaṇa
