title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.60
description: "By this method your spiritual master will regain his consciousness." Following Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's advice, all the Buddhist disciples began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa congregationally.
text:
> tomā-sabāra 'guru' tabe pāibe cetana
> saba bauddha mili' kare kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---all of you; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---the spiritual master; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:p:pāibe]]---will get; [[synonyms:c:cetana]]---consciousness; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:b:bauddha]]---all the Buddhist disciples; [[synonyms:m:mili']]---coming together; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra.//
translation: "By this method your spiritual master will regain his consciousness." Following Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's advice, all the Buddhist disciples began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa congregationally.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.61
description: When all the disciples chanted the holy names Kṛṣṇa, Rāma and Hari, the Buddhist teacher regained consciousness and immediately began to chant the holy name of Lord Hari.
text:
> guru-karṇe kahe sabe 'kṛṣṇa' 'rāma' 'hari'
> cetana pāñā ācārya bale 'hari' 'hari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:guru]]-[[synonyms:k:karṇe]]---into the ear of the spiritual master; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---they said; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all together; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:r:rāma]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---the holy names of the Lord, namely Kṛṣṇa, Rāma and Hari; [[synonyms:c:cetana]]---consciousness; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---the teacher; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---chanted; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---the name of Lord Hari.
translation: When all the disciples chanted the holy names Kṛṣṇa, Rāma and Hari, the Buddhist teacher regained consciousness and immediately began to chant the holy name of Lord Hari.
purport:
Śrī Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that all the Buddhist disciples were actually initiated by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu into the chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa, and when they chanted, they actually became different persons. At that time they were not Buddhists or atheists but Vaiṣṇavas. Consequently they immediately accepted Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's order. Their original Kṛṣṇa consciousness was revived, and they were immediately able to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa and begin worshiping the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu.

It is the spiritual master who delivers the disciple from the clutches of //māyā// by initiating him into the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.//  In this way a sleeping human being can revive his consciousness by chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare. In other words, the spiritual master awakens the sleeping living entity to his original consciousness so that he can worship Lord Viṣṇu. This is the purpose of //dīkṣā,// or initiation. Initiation means receiving the pure knowledge of spiritual consciousness.

One point to note in this regard is that the spiritual master of the Buddhists did not initiate his disciples. Rather, his disciples were initiated by Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and they in turn were able to initiate their so-called spiritual master. This is the //paramparā// system. The so-called spiritual master of the Buddhists was actually in the position of a disciple, and after his disciples were initiated by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they acted as his spiritual masters. This was possible only because the disciples of the Buddhist //ācārya// received the mercy of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Unless one is favored by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in the disciplic succession, one cannot act as a spiritual master. We should take the instructions of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the spiritual master of the whole universe, to understand how one becomes a spiritual master and a disciple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.62
description: When the spiritual master of the Buddhists began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and submitted to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all the people who were gathered there were astonished.
text:
> kṛṣṇa bali' ācārya prabhure karena vinaya
> dekhiyā sakala loka ha-ila vismaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---the so-called spiritual master of the Buddhists; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:v:vinaya]]---submission; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing this; [[synonyms:s:sakala]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all the people; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became; [[synonyms:v:vismaya]]---astonished.
translation: When the spiritual master of the Buddhists began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and submitted to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all the people who were gathered there were astonished.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.63
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the son of Śacīdevī, then suddenly and humorously disappeared from everyone's sight, and it was impossible for anyone to find Him.
text:
> ei-rūpe kautuka kari' śacīra nandana
> antardhāna kaila, keha nā pāya darśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in this way; [[synonyms:k:kautuka]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making fun; [[synonyms:ś:śacīra]] [[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of mother Śacī; [[synonyms:a:antardhāna]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---disappeared; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---get; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---audience.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the son of Śacīdevī, then suddenly and humorously disappeared from everyone's sight, and it was impossible for anyone to find Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.64
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu next arrived at Tirupati and Tirumala, where He saw a four-handed Deity. Then He next proceeded toward Veṅkaṭa Hill.
text:
> mahāprabhu cali' āilā tripati-trimalle
> catur-bhuja mūrti dekhi' vyeṅkaṭādrye cale
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cali']] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---arrived by walking; [[synonyms:t:tripati]]-[[synonyms:t:trimalle]]---at the holy places named Tirupati and Tirumala; [[synonyms:c:catur]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---fourhanded; [[synonyms:m:mūrti]]---Deity; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:v:vyeṅkaṭa]]-[[synonyms:a:adrye]]---to the holy place Veṅkaṭa Hill; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---began to proceed.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu next arrived at Tirupati and Tirumala, where He saw a four-handed Deity. Then He next proceeded toward Veṅkaṭa Hill.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura has actually described the chronological order of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's visit. The Tirupati temple is sometimes called Tirupaṭura. It is situated on the northern side of Arcot in the district of Candragiri. It is a famous holy place of pilgrimage. In pursuance of His name, Veṅkaṭeśvara, the four-handed Lord Viṣṇu, the Deity of Bālājī, with His potencies named Śrī and Bhū, is located on Veṅkaṭa Hill, about eight miles from Tirupati. This Veṅkaṭeśvara Deity is in the form of Lord Viṣṇu, and the place where He is situated is known as Veṅkaṭa-kṣetra. There are many temples in southern India, but this Bālājī temple is especially opulent. A great fair is held there in the months of September and October. There is a railway station called Tirupati on the Southern Railway. Nimna-tirupati is located in the valley of the Veṅkaṭa Hill. There are several temples there also, among which are those of Govindarāja and Lord Rāmacandra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.65
description: After arriving at Tirupati, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Lord Rāmacandra. He offered His prayers and obeisances before Rāmacandra, the descendant of King Raghu.
text:
> tripati āsiyā kaila śrī-rāma daraśana
> raghunātha-āge kaila praṇāma stavana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tripati]] [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming to Tirupati; [[synonyms:k:kaila]] [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rāma]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visited the temple of Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---before Lord Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:praṇāma]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:s:stavana]]---offering prayers.
translation: After arriving at Tirupati, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Lord Rāmacandra. He offered His prayers and obeisances before Rāmacandra, the descendant of King Raghu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.66
description: Everywhere Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went, His influence astonished everyone. He next arrived at the temple of Pānā-nṛsiṁha. The Lord is so merciful.
text:
> sva-prabhāve loka-sabāra karāñā vismaya
> pānā-nṛsiṁhe āilā prabhu dayā-maya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhāve]]---by His own influence; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all the people; [[synonyms:k:karāñā]]---inducing; [[synonyms:v:vismaya]]---astonishment; [[synonyms:p:pānā]]-[[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁhe]]---to the Lord named Pānā-nṛsiṁha; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dayā]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]---the most merciful.
translation: Everywhere Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went, His influence astonished everyone. He next arrived at the temple of Pānā-nṛsiṁha. The Lord is so merciful.
purport: Pānā-nṛsiṁha, or Pānākal-narasiṁha, is located in the district of Krishnā in the hills known as Maṅgalagiri, about seven miles from a city known as Vijayawada. One must climb six hundred steps to reach the temple. It is said that when the Lord is offered food with syrup here, He does not take more than half. Within this temple is a conchshell presented by the late king of Tanjor, and it is said that this shell was used by Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself. During the month of March, a great fair takes place in this temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.67
description: In great ecstatic love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered obeisances and prayers unto Lord Nṛsiṁha. The people were astonished to see Lord Caitanya's influence.
text:
> nṛsiṁhe praṇati-stuti premāveśe kaila
> prabhura prabhāve loka camatkāra haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁhe]]---unto Lord Nṛsiṁha; [[synonyms:p:praṇati]]-[[synonyms:s:stuti]]---obeisances and prayers; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---offered; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of the Lord; [[synonyms:p:prabhāve]]---by the influence; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---were astonished.
translation: In great ecstatic love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered obeisances and prayers unto Lord Nṛsiṁha. The people were astonished to see Lord Caitanya's influence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.68
description: Arriving at Śiva-kāñcī, Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the deity of Lord Śiva. By His influence, He converted all the devotees of Lord Śiva into Vaiṣṇavas.
text:
> śiva-kāñcī āsiyā kaila śiva daraśana
> prabhāve 'vaiṣṇava' kaila saba śaiva-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāñcī]]---to the holy place named Śiva-kāñcī; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting the temple of Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:p:prabhāve]]---by His influence; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---turned into Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:ś:śaiva]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees of Lord Śiva.
translation: Arriving at Śiva-kāñcī, Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the deity of Lord Śiva. By His influence, He converted all the devotees of Lord Śiva into Vaiṣṇavas.
purport: Śiva-kāñcī is also known as Kañjīvaramā, or the Benares of southern India. In Śiva-kāñcī there are hundreds of temples containing symbolic representations of Lord Śiva, and one of these temples is said to be very, very old.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.69
description: The Lord then visited a holy place known as Viṣṇu-kāñcī. There He saw Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa Deities, and He offered His respects and many prayers to please Them.
text:
> viṣṇu-kāñcī āsi' dekhila lakṣmī-nārāyaṇa
> praṇāma kariyā kaila bahuta stavana
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]-[[synonyms:k:kāñcī]]---to the holy place named Viṣṇu-kāñcī; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---the Lord saw; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]-[[synonyms:n:nārāyaṇa]]---the Deity of Lord Nārāyaṇa with mother Lakṣmī, the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:p:praṇāma]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---after offering obeisances; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:b:bahutastavana]]---many prayers.
translation: The Lord then visited a holy place known as Viṣṇu-kāñcī. There He saw Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa Deities, and He offered His respects and many prayers to please Them.
purport: Viṣṇu-kāñcī is situated about five miles away from Kañjīvaramā. It is here that Lord Varadarāja, another form of Lord Viṣṇu, resides. There is also a big lake known as Ananta-sarovara.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.7-8
description: As previously stated, all the residents of the villages visited by Lord Caitanya became Vaiṣṇavas and began to chant "Hari" and "Kṛṣṇa." In this way, in all the villages visited by the Lord, everyone became a Vaiṣṇava, a devotee.
text:
> pūrvavat pathe yāite ye pāya daraśana
> yei grāme yāya, se grāmera yata jana
>
> sabei vaiṣṇava haya, kahe 'kṛṣṇa' 'hari'
> anya grāma nistāraye sei 'vaiṣṇava' kari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---as done previously; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---while going; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---audience; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---which; [[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in the village; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu goes; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:g:grāmera]]---of the village; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:j:jana]]---people; [[synonyms:s:sabei]]---all of them; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---become devotees; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---say; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---the holy names of Lord Kṛṣṇa and Hari; [[synonyms:a:anya]] [[synonyms:g:grāma]]---other villages; [[synonyms:n:nistāraye]]---delivers; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---He; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotees; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making.
translation: As previously stated, all the residents of the villages visited by Lord Caitanya became Vaiṣṇavas and began to chant "Hari" and "Kṛṣṇa." In this way, in all the villages visited by the Lord, everyone became a Vaiṣṇava, a devotee.
purport: The holy names of Kṛṣṇa and Hari, or the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra,// are so spiritually powerful that even today, as our preachers go to remote parts of the world, people immediately begin chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. There cannot be anyone who can compare to Him or His potencies. However, because we are following in His footsteps and are also chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra,// the effect is almost as potent as during the time of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Our preachers mainly belong to European and American countries, yet by the grace of Lord Caitanya they have tremendous success wherever they go to open branches. Indeed, everywhere people are very seriously chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.70
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stayed at Viṣṇu-kāñcī for two days, He danced and performed kīrtana in ecstasy. When all the people saw Him, they were converted into devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> premāveśe nṛtya-gīta bahuta karila
> dina-dui rahi' loke 'kṛṣṇa-bhakta' kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]---dancing and chanting; [[synonyms:b:bahuta]]---much; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---performed; [[synonyms:d:dina]]-[[synonyms:d:dui]]---for two days; [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---staying; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---the people in general; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stayed at Viṣṇu-kāñcī for two days, He danced and performed kīrtana in ecstasy. When all the people saw Him, they were converted into devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.71
description: After visiting Trimalaya, Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to see Trikāla-hasti. There He saw Lord Śiva and offered him all respects and obeisances.
text:
> trimalaya dekhi' gelā trikāla-hasti-sthāne
> mahādeva dekhi' tāṅre karila praṇāme
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:trimalaya]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after seeing Trimalaya; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:t:trikāla]]-[[synonyms:h:hasti]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the place named Trikāla-hasti; [[synonyms:m:mahādeva]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:p:praṇāme]]---offered obeisances.
translation: After visiting Trimalaya, Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to see Trikāla-hasti. There He saw Lord Śiva and offered him all respects and obeisances.
purport: Trikāla-hasti is situated about twenty-two miles northeast of Tirupati. On its northern side is a river known as Suvarṇa-mukhī. The temple of Trikāla-hasti is located on the southern side of the river. The place is generally known as Śrī Kālahasti or Kālahasti and is famous for its temple of Lord Śiva. There he is called Vāyu-liṅga Śiva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.72
description: At Pakṣi-tīrtha, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Lord Śiva. Then He went to the Vṛddhakola place of pilgrimage.
text:
> pakṣi-tīrtha dekhi' kaila śiva daraśana
> vṛddhakola-tīrthe tabe karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pakṣi]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrtha]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after visiting the place known as Pakṣi-tīrtha; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting the temple of Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:v:vṛddhakola]]-[[synonyms:t:tīrthe]]---to the holy place known as Vṛddhakola; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---went.
translation: At Pakṣi-tīrtha, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Lord Śiva. Then He went to the Vṛddhakola place of pilgrimage.
purport: Pakṣi-tīrtha, also called Tirukāḍi-kuṇḍam, is located nine miles southeast of Ciṁlipaṭ. It has a five-hundred-foot elevation and is situated in a chain of hills known as Vedagiri or Vedācalam. There is a temple of Lord Śiva there, and the deity is known as Vedagirīśvara. Two birds come there daily to receive food from the temple priest, and it is claimed that they have been coming since time immemorial.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.73
description: At Vṛddhakola, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Śveta-varāha, the white boar incarnation. After offering Him respects, the Lord visited the temple of Lord Śiva, wherein the deity is dressed with yellow garments.
text:
> śveta-varāha dekhi, tāṅre namaskari'
> pītāmbara-śiva-sthāne gelā gaurahari
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śveta]]-[[synonyms:v:varāha]]---the white boar incarnation; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:n:namaskari']]---offering respect; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]-[[synonyms:a:ambara]]---dressed with yellow garments; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the temple of Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: At Vṛddhakola, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Śveta-varāha, the white boar incarnation. After offering Him respects, the Lord visited the temple of Lord Śiva, wherein the deity is dressed with yellow garments.
purport: The temple of the white boar incarnation is situated at Vṛddhakola. The temple is made of stone and is located about one mile south of an oasis known as Balipīṭham. There is a Deity of the white boar incarnation, above whose head Śeṣa Nāga serves as an umbrella. The deity of Lord Śiva is known as Pītāmbara and also as Cidāmbaram. This temple is located twenty-six miles south of Cuddaloreḍā, and the deity there is also known as Ākāśa-liṅga. The deity is in the form of Lord Śiva. This temple is situated on about thirty-nine acres of land, and all this land is surrounded by a wall sixty feet high.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.74
description: After visiting the temple of Śiyālī-bhairavī [another form of the goddess Durgā], Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the son of mother Śacī, went to the bank of the river Kāverī.
text:
> śiyālī bhairavī devī kari' daraśana
> kāverīra tīre āilā śacīra nandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śiyālī]] [[synonyms:b:bhairavī]]---Śiyālī-bhairavī; [[synonyms:d:devī]]---goddess; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting; [[synonyms:k:kāverīra]] [[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank of the river Kāverī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:ś:śacīra]] [[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of mother Śacī.
translation: After visiting the temple of Śiyālī-bhairavī [another form of the goddess Durgā], Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the son of mother Śacī, went to the bank of the river Kāverī.
purport: Śiyālī-bhairavī is located in the Tanjoreāñ district, about forty-eight miles northeast of Tanjoreāñ City. There is a very much celebrated temple of Lord Śiva there and also a very large lake. It is said that once a small boy who was a devotee of Lord Śiva came to that temple and the goddess Durgā, known as Bhairavī, gave him her breast to suck. After visiting this temple, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to the bank of the river Kāverī via the district of Tiruchchirāpalli. The Kāverī is mentioned in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.40) as a very pious river.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.75
description: The Lord then visited a place known as Go-samāja, where He saw Lord Śiva's temple. He then arrived at Vedāvana, where He saw another deity of Lord Śiva and offered him prayers.
text:
> go-samāje śiva dekhi' āilā vedāvana
> mahādeva dekhi' tāṅre karilā vandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:go]]-[[synonyms:s:samāje]]---at the place named Go-samāja; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the deity of Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]] [[synonyms:v:vedāvana]]---He arrived at Vedāvana; [[synonyms:m:mahādeva]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---offered prayers.
translation: The Lord then visited a place known as Go-samāja, where He saw Lord Śiva's temple. He then arrived at Vedāvana, where He saw another deity of Lord Śiva and offered him prayers.
purport: Go-samāja is a place of pilgrimage for the devotees of Lord Śiva. It is very important and is located next to Vedāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.76
description: Seeing the Śiva deity named Amṛta-liṅga, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered His obeisances. Thus He visited all the temples of Lord Śiva and converted the devotees of Lord Śiva into Vaiṣṇavas.
text:
> amṛtaliṅga-śiva dekhi' vandana karila
> saba śivālaye śaiva 'vaiṣṇava' ha-ila
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:l:liṅga]]-[[synonyms:ś:śiva]]---the Lord Śiva deity named Amṛta-liṅga; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:v:vandana]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---offered obeisances; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]-[[synonyms:ā:ālaye]]---in all the temples of Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:ś:śaiva]]---devotees of Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Seeing the Śiva deity named Amṛta-liṅga, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered His obeisances. Thus He visited all the temples of Lord Śiva and converted the devotees of Lord Śiva into Vaiṣṇavas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.77
description: At Devasthāna, Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Lord Viṣṇu, and there He talked with the Vaiṣṇavas in the disciplic succession of Rāmānujācārya. These Vaiṣṇavas are known as Śrī Vaiṣṇavas.
text:
> deva-sthāne āsi' kaila viṣṇu daraśana
> śrī-vaiṣṇavera saṅge tāhāṅ goṣṭhī anukṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the place known as Devasthāna; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting the temple of Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the Vaiṣṇavas in the disciplic succession of Rāmānuja; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:g:goṣṭhī]]---discussion; [[synonyms:a:anukṣaṇa]]---always.
translation: At Devasthāna, Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the temple of Lord Viṣṇu, and there He talked with the Vaiṣṇavas in the disciplic succession of Rāmānujācārya. These Vaiṣṇavas are known as Śrī Vaiṣṇavas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.78
description: At Kumbhakarṇa-kapāla, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw a great lake and then the holy place named Śiva-kṣetra, where a temple of Lord Śiva is located.
text:
> kumbhakarṇa-kapāle dekhi' sarovara
> śiva-kṣetre śiva dekhe gaurāṅga-sundara
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kumbhakarṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kapāle]]---at Kumbhakarṇa-kapāla; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---after seeing; [[synonyms:s:sarovara]]---the lake; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣetre]]---at Śiva-kṣetra; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:g:gaurāṅga]]-[[synonyms:s:sundara]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: At Kumbhakarṇa-kapāla, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw a great lake and then the holy place named Śiva-kṣetra, where a temple of Lord Śiva is located.
purport: Kumbhakarṇa is the name of the brother of Rāvaṇa. At the present moment the city of Kumbhakarṇa-kapāla is known as Kumbhakonṇam; it is situated twenty miles northeast of the city of Tanjoreāñ. There are twelve temples of Lord Śiva located at Kumbhakonṇam, as well as four Viṣṇu temples and one temple to Lord Brahmā. Śiva-kṣetra, within the city of Tanjoreāñ, is situated near a big lake known as Śiva-gaṅgā. At this place is a large temple of Lord Śiva known as Bṛhatīśvara-śiva-mandira.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.79
description: After visiting the holy place named Śiva-kṣetra, Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at Pāpanāśana and there saw the temple of Lord Viṣṇu. Then He finally reached Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra.
text:
> pāpa-nāśane viṣṇu kaila daraśana
> śrī-raṅga-kṣetre tabe karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśane]]---at the place named Pāpanāśana; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇu]]---Lord Viṣṇu; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅga]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣetre]]---to the holy place named Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---departure.
translation: After visiting the holy place named Śiva-kṣetra, Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at Pāpanāśana and there saw the temple of Lord Viṣṇu. Then He finally reached Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra.
purport:
According to some, the place known as Pāpanāśana was located eight miles southwest of Kumbhakonṇam. Others say that in the district of Tinebheli there is a city known as Pālamakoṭā and that Twenty miles west of there is the holy place known as Pāpanāśana, near the river Tāmraparṇī. Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra is a very famous place. Near Tiruchchirāpalli is a river named Kāverī, or Kolirana. A city known as Śrī Raṅgam is located on this river in the district of Tanjoreāñ, about ten miles west of Kumbhakonṇam. The Śrī Raṅga temple is the largest in India, and there are seven walls surrounding it. There are also seven roads leading to Śrī Raṅga. The ancient names of these roads are the road of Dharma, the road of Rājamahendra, the road of Kulaśekhara, the road of Ālināḍana, the road of Tiruvikrama, the Tirubiḍi road of Māḍamāḍi-gāisa, and the road of Aḍa-iyāvala-indāna. The temple was founded before the reign of Dharmavarma, who reigned before Rājamahendra. Many celebrated kings like Kulaśekhara, and others such as Ālabandāru, resided in the temple of Śrī Raṅgam. Yāmunācārya, Śrī Rāmānuja, Sudarśanācārya and others also supervised this temple.

The incarnation of the goddess of fortune known as Godādevī, who was one of the twelve liberated persons known as //divya-sūris,// was married to the Deity, Lord Śrī Raṅganātha. Later she entered into the body of the Lord. An incarnation of Kārmuka, Tirumaṅga (one of the Alwars), acquired some money by stealing and built the fourth boundary wall of Śrī Raṅgam. It is said that in the year 289 of the Age of Kali, the Alwar of the name Toṇḍaraḍippaḍi was born. While engaged in devotional service, he fell victim to a prostitute, and Śrī Raṅganātha, seeing His devotee so degraded, sent one of His servants with a golden plate to that prostitute. When the golden plate was discovered missing from the temple, there was a search, and it was found in the prostitute's house. When the devotee saw Raṅganātha's mercy upon this prostitute, his mistake was rectified. He then prepared the third boundary wall of the Raṅganātha temple and cultivated a //tulasī// garden there.

There was also a celebrated disciple of Rāmānujācārya's known as Kūreśa. Śrī Rāmapillā was the son of Kūreśa, and his son was Vāgvijaya Bhaṭṭa, whose son was Vedavyāsa Bhaṭṭa, or Śrī Sudarśanācārya. When Sudarśanācārya was an old man, the Mohammedans attacked the temple of Raṅganātha and killed about twelve hundred Śrī Vaiṣṇavas. At that time the Deity of Raṅganātha was transferred to the temple of Tirupati in the kingdom of Vijaya-nagara. The governor of Gingeeṅ, Goppaṇārya, brought Śrī Raṅganātha from the temple of Tirupati to a place known as Siṁha-brahma, where the Lord was situated for three years. In the year 1293 Śaka (A.D. 1372) the Deity was reinstalled in the Raṅganātha temple. On the eastern wall of the Raṅganātha temple is an inscription written by Vedānta-deśika relating how Raṅganātha was returned to the temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.80
description: After bathing in the river Kāverī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the temple of Raṅganātha and offered His ardent prayers and obeisances. Thus He felt Himself successful.
text:
> kāverīte snāna kari' dekhi' raṅganātha
> stuti-praṇati kari' mānilā kṛtārtha
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāverīte]]---in the river known as Kāverī; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---after bathing; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---visiting; [[synonyms:r:raṅga]]-[[synonyms:n:nātha]]---the Raṅganātha temple; [[synonyms:s:stuti]]---prayers; [[synonyms:p:praṇati]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---offering; [[synonyms:m:mānilā]]---thought Himself; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---very successful.
translation: After bathing in the river Kāverī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the temple of Raṅganātha and offered His ardent prayers and obeisances. Thus He felt Himself successful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.81
description: In the temple of Raṅganātha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu chanted and danced in ecstatic love of Godhead. Seeing His performance, everyone was struck with wonder.
text:
> premāveśe kaila bahuta gāna nartana
> dekhi' camatkāra haila saba lokera mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in the ecstasy of love; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:b:bahuta]]---various; [[synonyms:g:gāna]]---songs; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dancing; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing which; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonished; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---were; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of persons; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---minds.
translation: In the temple of Raṅganātha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu chanted and danced in ecstatic love of Godhead. Seeing His performance, everyone was struck with wonder.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.82
description: One Vaiṣṇava known as Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa then invited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to his home with great respect.
text:
> śrī-vaiṣṇava eka,---'vyeṅkaṭa bhaṭṭa' nāma
> prabhure nimantraṇa kaila kariyā sammāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:e:eka]]---a devotee belonging to the Rāmānuja-sampradāya; [[synonyms:v:vyeṅkaṭa]] [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---offering; [[synonyms:s:sammāna]]---great respect.
translation: One Vaiṣṇava known as Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa then invited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to his home with great respect.
purport: Śrī Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa was a Vaiṣṇava //brāhmaṇa// and an inhabitant of Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra. He belonged to the disciplic succession of Śrī Rāmānujācārya. Śrī Raṅga is one of the places of pilgrimage in the province of Tāmil Naduś. The inhabitants of that province do not retain the name Veṅkaṭa. It is therefore supposed that Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa did not belong to that province, although he may have been residing there for a very long time. Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa was in a branch of the Rāmānuja-sampradāya known as Baḍagala-i. He had a brother in the Rāmānuja-sampradāya known as Śrīpāda Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī. The son of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa was later known in the Gauḍīya-sampradāya as Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, and he established the Rādhāramaṇa temple in Vṛndāvana. More information about him may be found in a book known as //Bhakti-ratnākara,// by Narahari Cakravartī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.83
description: Śrī Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa took Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to his home. After he washed the Lord's feet, all the members of his family drank the water.
text:
> nija-ghare lañā kaila pāda-prakṣālana
> sei jala lañā kaila sa-vaṁśe bhakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to his own home; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---bringing; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:p:prakṣālana]]---washing of the feet; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:j:jala]]---that water; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:v:vaṁśe]]---with all the family members; [[synonyms:b:bhakṣaṇa]]---drinking.
translation: Śrī Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa took Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to his home. After he washed the Lord's feet, all the members of his family drank the water.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.84
description: After offering lunch to the Lord, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa submitted that the period of Cāturmāsya had already arrived.
text:
> bhikṣā karāñā kichu kaila nivedana
> cāturmāsya āsi' prabhu, haila upasanna
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:k:karāñā]]---after offering lunch; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---submission; [[synonyms:c:cāturmāsya]]---the period of Cāturmāsya; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---my Lord; [[synonyms:h:haila]] [[synonyms:u:upasanna]]---has already arrived.
translation: After offering lunch to the Lord, Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa submitted that the period of Cāturmāsya had already arrived.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.85
description: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa said, "Please be merciful to me and stay at my house during Cāturmāsya. Speak about Lord Kṛṣṇa's pastimes and kindly deliver me by Your mercy."
text:
> cāturmāsye kṛpā kari' raha mora ghare
> kṛṣṇa-kathā kahi' kṛpāya uddhāra' āmāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāturmāsye]]---during this period of Cāturmāsya; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---being merciful; [[synonyms:r:raha]]---please stay; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at my place; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---topics of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---speaking; [[synonyms:k:kṛpāya]]---by Your mercy; [[synonyms:u:uddhāra']] [[synonyms:ā:āmāre]]---kindly deliver me.
translation: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa said, "Please be merciful to me and stay at my house during Cāturmāsya. Speak about Lord Kṛṣṇa's pastimes and kindly deliver me by Your mercy."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.86
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained at the house of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa for four continuous months. The Lord passed His days in great happiness, enjoying the transcendental mellow of discussing Lord Kṛṣṇa's pastimes.
text:
> tāṅra ghare rahilā prabhu kṛṣṇa-kathā-rase
> bhaṭṭa-saṅge goṅāila sukhe cāri māse
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in his home; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---stayed; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]-[[synonyms:r:rase]]---enjoying the transcendental mellow of discussing Lord Kṛṣṇa's pastimes; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:g:goṅāila]]---passed; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in happiness; [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:m:māse]]---four months.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained at the house of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa for four continuous months. The Lord passed His days in great happiness, enjoying the transcendental mellow of discussing Lord Kṛṣṇa's pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.87
description: While there, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took His bath in the river Kāverī and visited the temple of Śrī Raṅga. Every day the Lord also danced in ecstasy.
text:
> kāverīte snāna kari' śrī-raṅga darśana
> pratidina premāveśe karena nartana

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.96
description: While reading the book, the brāhmaṇa experienced transcendental bodily transformations. His hair stood on end, tears welled in his eyes, and his body trembled and perspired as he read. Seeing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very happy.
text:
> pulakāśru, kampa, sveda,---yāvat paṭhana
> dekhi' ānandita haila mahāprabhura mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pulaka]]---standing of the hairs of the body; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---trembling; [[synonyms:s:sveda]]---perspiration; [[synonyms:y:yāvat]]---during; [[synonyms:p:paṭhana]]---the reading of the book; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing this; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very happy; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: While reading the book, the brāhmaṇa experienced transcendental bodily transformations. His hair stood on end, tears welled in his eyes, and his body trembled and perspired as he read. Seeing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very happy.
purport:
Although the //brāhmaṇa// could not pronounce the words very well due to illiteracy, he still experienced ecstatic symptoms while reading the //Bhagavad-gītā.// Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very much pleased to observe these symptoms, and this indicates that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is pleased by devotion, not by erudite scholarship. Even though the words were imperfectly pronounced, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself, did not think this very serious. Rather, the Lord was pleased by the //bhāva// (devotion). In //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:5:11|(1.5.11)]] this is confirmed:

> tad-vāg-visargo janatāgha-viplavo
> yasmin prati-ślokam abaddhavaty api
> nāmāny anantasya yaśo-'ṅkitāni yat
> śṛṇvanti gāyanti gṛṇanti sādhavaḥ

"On the other hand, that literature which is full of descriptions of the transcendental glories of the name, fame, forms and pastimes of the unlimited Supreme Lord is a different creation, full of transcendental words directed toward bringing about a revolution in the impious lives of this world's misdirected civilization. Such transcendental literature, even though imperfectly composed, is heard, sung and accepted by purified men who are thoroughly honest."

The purport to this verse may be considered for further information on this subject.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 9.98
description: The brāhmaṇa replied, "I am illiterate and therefore do not know the meaning of the words. Sometimes I read the Bhagavad-gītā correctly and sometimes incorrectly, but in any case I am doing this in compliance with the orders of my spiritual master."
text:
> vipra kahe,---mūrkha āmi, śabdārtha nā jāni
> śuddhāśuddha gītā paḍi, guru-ājñā māni'
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the //brāhmaṇa// replied; [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]] [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I am illiterate; [[synonyms:ś:śabda]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meaning of the words; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I do not know; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:a:aśuddha]]---sometimes correct and sometimes not correct; [[synonyms:g:gītā]]---the //Bhagavad-gītā//; [[synonyms:p:paḍi]]---I read; [[synonyms:g:guru]]-[[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---the order of my spiritual master; [[synonyms:m:māni']]---accepting.
translation: The brāhmaṇa replied, "I am illiterate and therefore do not know the meaning of the words. Sometimes I read the Bhagavad-gītā correctly and sometimes incorrectly, but in any case I am doing this in compliance with the orders of my spiritual master."
purport:
This is a good example of a person who had become so successful that he was able to capture the attention of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu even while reading the //Bhagavad-gītā// incorrectly. His spiritual activities did not depend on material things such as correct pronunciation. Rather, his success depended on strictly following the instructions of his spiritual master.

> yasya deve parā bhaktir
> yathā deve tathā gurau
> tasyaite kathitā hy arthāḥ
> prakāśante mahātmanaḥ

"Only unto those great souls who have implicit faith in both the Lord and the spiritual master are all the imports of Vedic knowledge automatically revealed."(//Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad// 6.23)

Actually the meaning of the words of the //Bhagavad-gītā// or //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// are revealed to one strictly following the orders of the spiritual master. They are also revealed to one who has equal faith in the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In other words, being faithful to both Kṛṣṇa and the spiritual master is the secret of success in spiritual life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.101
description: One has to learn about the beauty and transcendental position of the holy name of the Lord by hearing the revealed scriptures from the mouths of devotees. Nowhere else can we hear of the sweetness of the Lord's holy name.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-nāmera mahimā śāstra-sādhu-mukhe jāni
> nāmera mādhurī aiche kāhāṅ nāhi śuni
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāmera]] [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---the glories of the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---of the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the mouth; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---we can understand; [[synonyms:n:nāmera]] [[synonyms:m:mādhurī]]---the sweetness of the holy name; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---anywhere else; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---we do not hear.
translation: One has to learn about the beauty and transcendental position of the holy name of the Lord by hearing the revealed scriptures from the mouths of devotees. Nowhere else can we hear of the sweetness of the Lord's holy name.
purport:
It is said in the P//adma Purāṇa, ataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāmādi na bhaved grāhyam indriyaiḥ.// Chanting and hearing of the transcendental holy name of the Lord cannot be performed by the ordinary senses. The transcendental vibration of the Lord's holy name is completely spiritual. Thus it must be received from spiritual sources and must be chanted after having been heard from a spiritual master. One who hears the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// must receive it from the spiritual master by aural reception. Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī has forbidden us to hear the holy name of Kṛṣṇa chanted by non-Vaiṣṇavas, such as professional actors and singers, for it will have no effect. It is like milk touched by the lips of a serpent, as stated in the //padma purāṇa://

> avaiṣṇava-mukhodgīrṇaṁ
> pūtaṁ hari-kathāmṛtam
> śravaṇaṁ naiva kartavyaṁ
> sarpocchiṣṭaṁ yathā payaḥ

As far as possible, therefore, the devotees in the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement gather to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa in public so that both the chanters and the listeners may benefit.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.102
description: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced both Haridāsa and Rūpa Gosvāmī and left for the seaside to perform His noontime duties.
text:
> tabe mahāprabhu duṅhe kari' āliṅgana
> madhyāhna karite samudre karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---unto both Rūpa Gosvāmī and Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:ā:āliṅgana]]---embracing; [[synonyms:m:madhya]]-[[synonyms:a:ahna]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to perform His noontime duties; [[synonyms:s:samudre]]---o the seaside; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---went.
translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced both Haridāsa and Rūpa Gosvāmī and left for the seaside to perform His noontime duties.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.103-104
description: On the next day, after visiting the temple of Jagannātha as usual, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu met Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara. They all went together to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, and on the way the Lord greatly praised his qualities.
text:
> āra dina mahāprabhu dekhi' jagannātha
> sārvabhauma-rāmānanda-svarūpādi-sātha
> sabe mili' cali āilā śrī-rūpe milite
> pathe tāṅra guṇa sabāre lāgilā kahite
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---he next day; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha in the temple; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:sātha]]---along with; [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:m:mili']]---meeting all together; [[synonyms:c:cali]] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came there; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]] [[synonyms:m:milite]]---to meet Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---all the good qualities; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---unto all the personal associates; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]] [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---began to speak.
translation: On the next day, after visiting the temple of Jagannātha as usual, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu met Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara. They all went together to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, and on the way the Lord greatly praised his qualities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.105
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited the two important verses, He felt great pleasure; thus, as if He had five mouths, He began to praise His devotee.
text:
> dui śloka kahi' prabhura haila mahā-sukha
> nija-bhaktera guna kahe hañā pañca-mukha
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---reciting two verses; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]---great pleasure; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaktera]]---of His own devotee; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---the qualities; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---as if becoming; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:m:mukha]]---five-mouthed.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited the two important verses, He felt great pleasure; thus, as if He had five mouths, He began to praise His devotee.
purport: The two verses referred to are those beginning with //priyaḥ so 'yam// (79) and //tuṇḍe tāṇḍavinī// (99).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.106
description: Just to examine Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Rāmānanda Rāya, the Lord began to praise the transcendental qualities of Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī before them.
text:
> sārvabhauma-rāmānande parīkṣā karite
> śrī-rūpera guṇa duṅhāre lāgilā kahite
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]-[[synonyms:r:rāmānande]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:p:parīkṣā]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to examine; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpera]] [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---the transcendental qualities of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāre]]---unto both of them; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]] [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---He began to praise.
translation: Just to examine Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Rāmānanda Rāya, the Lord began to praise the transcendental qualities of Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī before them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.107
description: Characteristically, the Supreme Personality of Godhead does not take seriously an offense committed by a pure devotee. The Lord accepts whatever small service a devotee renders as being such a great service that He is prepared to give even Himself, not to speak of other benedictions.
text:
> 'īśvara-svabhāva'---bhaktera nā laya aparādha
> alpa-sevā bahu māne ātma-paryanta prasāda
synonyms: [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]-[[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---the characteristic of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhaktera]]---of the pure devotee; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:l:laya]]---does not take; [[synonyms:a:aparādha]]---any offense; [[synonyms:a:alpa]]-[[synonyms:s:sevā]]---very small service; [[synonyms:b:bahu]] [[synonyms:m:māne]]---the Lord accepts as very great; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---giving Himself; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---mercy.
translation: Characteristically, the Supreme Personality of Godhead does not take seriously an offense committed by a pure devotee. The Lord accepts whatever small service a devotee renders as being such a great service that He is prepared to give even Himself, not to speak of other benedictions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.108
description: "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is known as Puruṣottama, the greatest of all persons, has a pure mind. He is so gentle that even if His servant is implicated in a great offense, He does not take it very seriously. Indeed, if His servant renders some small service, the Lord accepts it as being very great. Even if an envious person blasphemes the Lord, the Lord never manifests anger against him. Such are His great qualities."
text:
> bhṛtyasya paśyati gurūn api nāparādhān
> sevāṁ manāg api kṛtāṁ bahudhābhyupaiti
> āviṣkaroti piśuneṣv api nābhyasūyāṁ
> śīlena nirmala-matiḥ puruṣottamo 'yam
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhṛtyasya]]---of the servant; [[synonyms:p:paśyati]]---He sees; [[synonyms:g:gurūn]]---very great; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:aparādhān]]---the offenses; [[synonyms:s:sevām]]---service; [[synonyms:m:manāk]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---however small; [[synonyms:k:kṛtām]]---performed; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:d:dhā]]---as great; [[synonyms:a:abhyupaiti]]---accepts,; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣkaroti]]---manifests; [[synonyms:p:piśuneṣu]]---on the enemies; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:abhyasūyām]]---envy; [[synonyms:ś:śīlena]]---by gentle behavior; [[synonyms:n:nirmala]]-[[synonyms:m:matiḥ]]---naturally clean-minded; [[synonyms:p:puruṣottamaḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the best of all personalities; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this.
translation: "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is known as Puruṣottama, the greatest of all persons, has a pure mind. He is so gentle that even if His servant is implicated in a great offense, He does not take it very seriously. Indeed, if His servant renders some small service, the Lord accepts it as being very great. Even if an envious person blasphemes the Lord, the Lord never manifests anger against him. Such are His great qualities."
purport: This verse is from the //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (2.1.138) by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.109
description: When Haridāsa Ṭhākura and Rūpa Gosvāmī saw that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had come with His intimate devotees, they both immediately fell down like logs and offered prayers to their lotus feet.
text:
> bhakta-saṅge prabhu āilā, dekhi' dui jana
> daṇḍavat hañā kailā caraṇa vandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---accompanied by other devotee associates; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing this; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---Rūpa Gosvāmī and Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍavat]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---falling flat like logs; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---prayers to their lotus feet.
translation: When Haridāsa Ṭhākura and Rūpa Gosvāmī saw that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had come with His intimate devotees, they both immediately fell down like logs and offered prayers to their lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.11
description: I am now almost an invalid because of old age, and I know that at any moment I may die. Therefore I have already described some portions of the antya-līlā.
text:
> āmi jarā-grasta, nikaṭe jāniyā maraṇa
> antya kono kono līlā kariyāchi varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]] [[synonyms:j:jarā]]-[[synonyms:g:grasta]]---I am invalid because of old age; [[synonyms:n:nikaṭe]]---very near; [[synonyms:j:jāniyā]]---knowing; [[synonyms:m:maraṇa]]---death; [[synonyms:a:antya]]---final; [[synonyms:k:kono]] [[synonyms:k:kono]]---some; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchi]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---I have described
translation: I am now almost an invalid because of old age, and I know that at any moment I may die. Therefore I have already described some portions of the antya-līlā.
purport: Following in the footsteps of Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī, I am trying to translate //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// as quickly as possible. However, knowing myself to be an old man and almost an invalid because of rheumatism, I have already translated the essence of all literatures, the Tenth Canto of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// as a summary study in English. I started the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement at the age of seventy. Now I am seventy-eight, and so my death is imminent. I am trying to finish the translation of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// as soon as possible, but before finishing it, I have given my readers the book //Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead,// so that if I die before finishing the whole task they may enjoy this book, which is the essence of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.110
description: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His personal devotees met Rūpa Gosvāmī and Haridāsa Ṭhākura. The Lord then sat down in an elevated place with His devotees.
text:
> bhakta-saṅge kailā prabhu duṅhāre milana
> piṇḍāte vasilā prabhu lañā bhakta-gaṇa

translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His personal devotees met Rūpa Gosvāmī and Haridāsa Ṭhākura. The Lord then sat down in an elevated place with His devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.111
description: Rūpa Gosvāmī and Haridāsa Ṭhākura sat at the foot of the elevated place where Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was sitting. Although everyone asked them to sit on the same level as the Lord and His associates, they did not do so.
text:
> rūpa haridāsa duṅhe vasilā piṇḍā-tale
> sabāra āgrahe nā uṭhilā piṅḍāra upare

translation: Rūpa Gosvāmī and Haridāsa Ṭhākura sat at the foot of the elevated place where Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was sitting. Although everyone asked them to sit on the same level as the Lord and His associates, they did not do so.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.112
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered Rūpa Gosvāmī to read the verse they had previously heard, Rūpa Gosvāmī, because of great shyness, did not read it but instead remained silent.
text:
> 'pūrva-śloka paḍa, rūpa' prabhu ājñā kailā
> lajjāte nā paḍe rūpa mauna dharilā

translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered Rūpa Gosvāmī to read the verse they had previously heard, Rūpa Gosvāmī, because of great shyness, did not read it but instead remained silent.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.113
description: Then Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī recited the verse, and when all the devotees heard it, their minds were struck with wonder.
text:
> svarūpa-gosāñi tabe sei śloka paḍila
> śuni' sabākāra citte camatkāra haila

translation: Then Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī recited the verse, and when all the devotees heard it, their minds were struck with wonder.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.114
description: "My dear friend, now I have met My very old and dear friend Kṛṣṇa on this field of Kurukṣetra. I am the same Rādhārāṇī, and now We are meeting together. It is very pleasant, but I would still like to go to the bank of the Yamunā beneath the trees of the forest there. I wish to hear the vibration of His sweet flute playing the fifth note within that forest of Vṛndāvana."
text:
> priyaḥ so 'yaṁ kṛṣṇaḥ saha-cari kuru-kṣetra-militas
> tathāhaṁ sā rādhā tad idam ubhayoḥ saṅgama-sukham
> tathāpy antaḥ-khelan-madhura-muralī-pañcama-juṣe
> mano me kālindī-pulina-vipināya spṛhayati
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:priyaḥ]]---very dear; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:saha]]-[[synonyms:c:cari]]---O My dear friend; [[synonyms:k:kuru]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣetra]]-[[synonyms:m:militaḥ]]---who is met on the field of Kurukṣetra; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---also; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:s:sā]]---that; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that; [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this; [[synonyms:u:ubhayoḥ]]---of both of Us; [[synonyms:s:saṅgama]]-[[synonyms:s:sukham]]---the happiness of meeting; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]---within; [[synonyms:k:khelan]]---playing; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweet; [[synonyms:m:muralī]]---of the flute; [[synonyms:p:pañcama]]---the fifth note; [[synonyms:j:juṣe]]---which delights in; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]---the mind; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:k:kālindī]]---of the River Yamunā; [[synonyms:p:pulina]]---on the ban k; [[synonyms:v:vipināya]]---the trees; [[synonyms:s:spṛhayati]]---desires.
translation: "My dear friend, now I have met My very old and dear friend Kṛṣṇa on this field of Kurukṣetra. I am the same Rādhārāṇī, and now We are meeting together. It is very pleasant, but I would still like to go to the bank of the Yamunā beneath the trees of the forest there. I wish to hear the vibration of His sweet flute playing the fifth note within that forest of Vṛndāvana."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.115
description: After hearing this verse, both Rāmānanda Rāya and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said to Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Without Your special mercy, how could this Rūpa Gosvāmī have understood Your mind?"
text:
> rāya, bhaṭṭācārya bale,---"tomāra prasāda vine
> tomāra hṛdaya ei jānila kemane
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---say; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:v:vine]]---without Your special mercy; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]---Your mind; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:j:jānila]]---understood; [[synonyms:k:kemane]]---how.
translation: After hearing this verse, both Rāmānanda Rāya and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya said to Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Without Your special mercy, how could this Rūpa Gosvāmī have understood Your mind?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.116
description: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya admitted that previously Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had empowered his heart so that he could express elevated and conclusive statements to which even Lord Brahmā has no access.
text:
> āmāte sañcāri' pūrve kahilā siddhānta
> ye saba siddhānte brahmā nāhi pāya anta
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmāte]]---within me; [[synonyms:s:sañcāri']]---creating all logical truths; [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---previously; [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---You express; [[synonyms:s:siddhānta]]---conclusive statements; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of; [[synonyms:s:siddhānte]]---conclusive statements; [[synonyms:b:brahmā]]---even Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]] [[synonyms:a:anta]]---cannot understand the limit.
translation: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya admitted that previously Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had empowered his heart so that he could express elevated and conclusive statements to which even Lord Brahmā has no access.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.117
description: "Had you not previously bestowed Your mercy on him," they said, "it would not have been possible for him to express Your internal feelings."
text:
> tāte jāni---pūrve tomāra pāñāche prasāda
> tāhā vinā nahe tomāra hṛdayānuvāda"
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in such instances; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I can understand; [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---previously; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:p:pāñāche]] [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---he has obtained special mercy; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without that; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---there is not; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]-[[synonyms:a:anuvāda]]---expression of feelings.
translation: "Had you not previously bestowed Your mercy on him," they said, "it would not have been possible for him to express Your internal feelings."
purport:
Devotees acknowledge Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's special mercy upon Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī in the following words:

> śrī-caitanya-mano 'bhīṣṭaṁ-
> sthāpitaṁ yena bhū-tale
> svayaṁ rūpaḥ kadā mahyaṁ
> dadāti sva-padāntikam

"When will Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī Prabhupāda, who has established within this material world the mission to fulfill the desire of Lord Caitanya, give me shelter under his lotus feet?"

The special function of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī is to establish the feelings of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. These feelings are His desires that His special mercy be spread throughout the world in this Kali-yuga.

> pṛthivīte āche yata nagarādi-grāma
> sarvatra pracāra haibe mora nāma

His desire is that all over the world everyone, in every village and every town, know of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His //saṅkīrtana// movement. These are the inner feelings of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī committed to writing all these feelings of the Lord. Now again, by the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the same feelings are being spread all over the world by the servants of the Gosvāmīs, and devotees who are pure and simple will appreciate this attempt. As concluded by Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī, however, those who are on the level of hogs and dogs will never appreciate such a great attempt. Yet this does not matter to the preachers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's cult, for all over the world they will continue to perform this responsible work, even though persons who are like cats and dogs do not appreciate them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.118
description: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My dear Rūpa, please recite that verse from your drama which, upon being heard, makes all people's unhappiness and lamentation go away."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---"kaha rūpa, nāṭakera śloka
> ye śloka śunile lokera yāya duḥkha-śoka
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please recite; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---My dear Rūpa; [[synonyms:n:nāṭakera]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---the verse of your drama; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verse; [[synonyms:ś:śunile]]---hearing; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of all people; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---go away; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]-[[synonyms:ś:śoka]]---the unhappiness and lamentation.
translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My dear Rūpa, please recite that verse from your drama which, upon being heard, makes all people's unhappiness and lamentation go away."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.119
description: When the Lord persisted in asking this again and again, Rūpa Gosvāmī recited that verse [as follows].
text:
> bāra bāra prabhu yadi tāre ājñā dila
> tabe sei śloka rūpa-gosāñi kahila
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāra]] [[synonyms:b:bāra]]---again and again; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---when; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---him; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---ordered; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---that particular verse; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---of the name Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---recited.
translation: When the Lord persisted in asking this again and again, Rūpa Gosvāmī recited that verse [as follows].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.12
description: In accordance with the synopsis previously written, I shall describe in detail whatever I have not mentioned.
text:
> pūrva-likhita grantha-sūtra-anusāre
> yei nāhi likhi, tāhā likhiye vistāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:l:likhita]]---previously mentioned; [[synonyms:g:grantha]]-[[synonyms:s:sūtra]]---the synopsis of the pastimes; [[synonyms:a:anusāre]]---according to; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:l:likhi]]---I have not mentioned; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---hat; [[synonyms:l:likhiye]]---I shall write; [[synonyms:v:vistāre]]---elaborately.
translation: In accordance with the synopsis previously written, I shall describe in detail whatever I have not mentioned.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.120
description: "I do not know how much nectar the two syllables 'Kṛṣ-ṇa' have produced. When the holy name of Kṛṣṇa is chanted, it appears to dance within the mouth. We then desire many, many mouths. When that name enters the holes of the ears, we desire many millions of ears. And when the holy name dances in the courtyard of the heart, it conquers the activities of the mind, and therefore all the senses become inert."
text:
> tuṇḍe tāṇḍavinī ratiṁ vitanute tuṇḍāvalī-labdhaye
> karṇa-kroḍa-kaḍambinī ghaṭayate karṇārbudebhyaḥ spṛhām
> cetaḥ-prāṅgaṇa-saṅginī vijayate sarvendriyāṇāṁ kṛtiṁ
> no jāne janitā kiyadbhir amṛtaiḥ kṛṣṇeti varṇa-dvayī
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tuṇḍe]]---in the mouth; [[synonyms:t:tāṇḍavinī]]---dancing; [[synonyms:r:ratim]]---the inspiration; [[synonyms:v:vitanute]]---expands; [[synonyms:t:tuṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āvalī]]-[[synonyms:l:labdhaye]]---to achieve many mouths; [[synonyms:k:karṇa]]---of the ear; [[synonyms:k:kroḍa]]---in the hole; [[synonyms:k:kaḍambinī]]---sprouting; [[synonyms:g:ghaṭayate]]---causes to appear; [[synonyms:k:karṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:arbudebhyaḥ]] [[synonyms:s:spṛhām]]---the desire for millions of ears; [[synonyms:c:cetaḥ]]-[[synonyms:p:prāṅgaṇa]]---in the courtyard of the heart; [[synonyms:s:saṅginī]]---being a companion; [[synonyms:v:vijayate]]---conquers; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:i:indriyāṇām]]---of all the senses; [[synonyms:k:kṛtim]]---the activity; [[synonyms:n:no]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---I know; [[synonyms:j:janitā]]---produced; [[synonyms:k:kiyadbhiḥ]]---of what measures by; [[synonyms:a:amṛtaiḥ]]---by nectar; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---the name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:v:varṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dvayī]]---the two syllables.
translation: "I do not know how much nectar the two syllables 'Kṛṣ-ṇa' have produced. When the holy name of Kṛṣṇa is chanted, it appears to dance within the mouth. We then desire many, many mouths. When that name enters the holes of the ears, we desire many millions of ears. And when the holy name dances in the courtyard of the heart, it conquers the activities of the mind, and therefore all the senses become inert."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.121
description: When all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, especially Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya, heard this verse, they were all filled with transcendental bliss and were struck with wonder.
text:
> yata bhakta-vṛnda āra rāmānanda rāya
> śloka śuni' sabāra ha-ila ānanda-vismaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yata]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---all the personal devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]] [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---of the name Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this verse; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:v:vismaya]]---transcendental bliss and astonishment.
translation: When all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, especially Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya, heard this verse, they were all filled with transcendental bliss and were struck with wonder.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.122
description: Everyone admitted that although they had heard many statements glorifying the holy name of the Lord, they had never heard such sweet descriptions as those of Rūpa Gosvāmī.
text:
> sabe bale,---'nāma-mahimā śuniyāchi apāra
> emana mādhurya keha nāhi varṇe āra'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---every one of them said; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---the glories of chanting the holy name; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyāchi]]---we have heard; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---many times; [[synonyms:e:emana]]---this kind of; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---sweetness; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:v:varṇe]]---describes; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---else.
translation: Everyone admitted that although they had heard many statements glorifying the holy name of the Lord, they had never heard such sweet descriptions as those of Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.123
description: Rāmānanda Rāya inquired, "What kind of drama are you writing? We ca understand that it is a mine of conclusive statements."
text:
> rāya kahe,---"kon grantha kara hena jāni?
> yāhāra bhitare ei siddhāntera khani?"
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Rāmānanda Rāya inquired; [[synonyms:k:kon]]---what; [[synonyms:g:grantha]]---dramatic literature; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---you are writing; [[synonyms:h:hena]]---such; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I can understand; [[synonyms:y:yāhāra]] [[synonyms:b:bhitare]]---within which; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:s:siddhāntera]] [[synonyms:k:khani]]---a mine of conclusive statements.
translation: Rāmānanda Rāya inquired, "What kind of drama are you writing? We ca understand that it is a mine of conclusive statements."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.124
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara replied for Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī: "He wanted to compose a drama about the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. He planned to describe in one book both the pastimes of Vṛndāvana and those of Dvārakā and Mathurā.
text:
> svarūpa kahe,---"kṛṣṇa-līlāra nāṭaka karite
> vraja-līlā-pura-līlā ekatra varṇite
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara replied on behalf of Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlāra]]---of the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nāṭaka]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---composing a drama; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:p:pura]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---His pastimes in Vṛndāvana and His pastimes in Mathurā and Dvārakā; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]]---in one book; [[synonyms:v:varṇite]]---to describe.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara replied for Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī: "He wanted to compose a drama about the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. He planned to describe in one book both the pastimes of Vṛndāvana and those of Dvārakā and Mathurā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.125
description: "He began it in that way, but now, following the order of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he has divided it in two and is writing two plays, one concerning the pastimes of Mathurā and Dvārakā and the other concerning the pastimes of Vṛndāvana.
text:
> ārambhiyāchilā, ebe prabhu-ājñā pāñā
> dui nāṭaka kariteche vibhāga kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ārambhiyāchilā]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī began; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting the order of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:n:nāṭaka]]---two different dramas; [[synonyms:k:kariteche]]---he is compiling; [[synonyms:v:vibhāga]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---dividing the original idea.
translation: "He began it in that way, but now, following the order of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he has divided it in two and is writing two plays, one concerning the pastimes of Mathurā and Dvārakā and the other concerning the pastimes of Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.126
description: "The two plays are called Vidagdha-mādhava and Lalita-mādhava. Both of them wonderfully describe ecstatic emotional love of God."
text:
> vidagdha-mādhava āra lalita-mādhava
> dui nāṭake prema-rasa adabhuta saba"
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vidagdha]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhava]]---one is named //Vidagdha-mādhava//; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:l:lalita]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhava]]---named Lalita-mādhava; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:n:nāṭake]]---in two plays; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---ecstatic mellows of emotional love for Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:adabhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all.
translation: "The two plays are called Vidagdha-mādhava and Lalita-mādhava. Both of them wonderfully describe ecstatic emotional love of God."
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura informs us in this connection that Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī composed the drama known as //Vidagdha-mādhava// in the year Śakābda 1454, and he finished //Lalita-mādhava// in Śakābda 1459. The discussion between Rāmānanda Rāya and Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī at Jagannātha Purī took place in Śakābda 1437.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.127

text:
> rāya kahe,---"nāndī-śloka paḍa dekhi, śuni?"

translation: Rāmānanda Rāya said, "PIease recite the introductory verse of Vidagdhamādhava so that I can hear and examine it." Thus Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī, being ordered by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, recited the verse (1.1).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.128
description: "May the pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa reduce the miseries existing in the material world and nullify all unwanted desires. The pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are like śikhariṇī, a blend of yogurt and sugar candy. They overpower the pride of even the nectar produced on the moon, for they distribute the sweet fragrance of the concentrated loving affairs of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and the gopīs."
text:
> sudhānāṁ cāndrīṇām api madhurimonmāda-damanī
> dadhānā rādhādi-praṇaya-ghana-sāraiḥ surabhitām
> samantāt santāpodgama-viṣama-saṁsāra-saraṇī-
> praṇītāṁ te tṛṣṇāṁ haratu hari-līlā-śikhariṇī
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sudhānām]]---of the nectar; [[synonyms:c:cāndrīṇām]]---produced on the moon; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:m:madhurimā]]---the sweetness; [[synonyms:u:unmāda]]-[[synonyms:d:damanī]]---overpowering the pride; [[synonyms:d:dadhānā]]---distributing; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and Her companions; [[synonyms:p:praṇaya]]-[[synonyms:g:ghana]]---of the concentrated loving affairs; [[synonyms:s:sāraiḥ]]---by the essence; [[synonyms:s:surabhitām]]---a good fragrance; [[synonyms:s:samantāt]]---everywhere; [[synonyms:s:santāpa]]---miserable conditions; [[synonyms:u:udgama]]---generating; [[synonyms:v:viṣama]]---very dangerous; [[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]-[[synonyms:s:saraṇī]]---on the path of material existence; [[synonyms:p:praṇītām]]---created; [[synonyms:t:te]]---your; [[synonyms:t:tṛṣṇām]]---desires; [[synonyms:h:haratu]]---let it take away; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śikhariṇī]]---exactly like a combination of yogurt and sugar candy.
translation: "May the pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa reduce the miseries existing in the material world and nullify all unwanted desires. The pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are like śikhariṇī, a blend of yogurt and sugar candy. They overpower the pride of even the nectar produced on the moon, for they distribute the sweet fragrance of the concentrated loving affairs of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and the gopīs."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.129
description: Rāmānanda Rāya said, "Now please recite the description of the glories of your worshipable Deity." Rūpa Gosvāmī, however, hesitated due to embarrassment because Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was present.
text:
> rāya kahe,---'kaha iṣṭa-devera varṇana'
> prabhura saṅkoce rūpa nā kare paṭhana

translation: Rāmānanda Rāya said, "Now please recite the description of the glories of your worshipable Deity." Rūpa Gosvāmī, however, hesitated due to embarrassment because Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was present.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.13
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to Jagannātha Purī from Vṛndāvana, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosāñi immediately sent news of the Lord's arrival to the devotees in Bengal.
text:
> vṛndāvana haite prabhu nīlācale āilā
> svarūpa-gosāñi gauḍe vārtā pāṭhāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned to Jagannātha Purī, Nīlācala; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:g:gauḍe]]---to Bengal; [[synonyms:v:vārtā]] [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāilā]]---sent news.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to Jagannātha Purī from Vṛndāvana, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosāñi immediately sent news of the Lord's arrival to the devotees in Bengal.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.130
description: The Lord, however, encouraged Rūpa Gosvāmī, saying, "Why are you embarrassed? You should recite it so the devotees can hear the good fruit of your writing."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---"kaha, kene kara saṅkoca-lāje?
> granthera phala śunāibā vaiṣṇava samāje?"
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu says; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---speak up; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---you do; [[synonyms:s:saṅkoca]]-[[synonyms:l:lāje]]---in shame and embarrassment; [[synonyms:g:granthera]]---of the book; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---the fruit; [[synonyms:ś:śunāibā]]---you should make heard; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:s:samāje]]---in the society of pure devotees.
translation: The Lord, however, encouraged Rūpa Gosvāmī, saying, "Why are you embarrassed? You should recite it so the devotees can hear the good fruit of your writing."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.131
description: When Rūpa Gosvāmī thus recited his verse, Caitanya Mahāprabhu disapproved of it because it described His personal glories. He expressed the opinion that it was an exaggerated explanation.
text:
> tabe rūpa-gosāñi yadi śloka paḍila
> śuni' prabhu kahe,---'ei ati stuti haila'
