translation: When Rūpa Gosvāmī thus recited his verse, Caitanya Mahāprabhu disapproved of it because it described His personal glories. He expressed the opinion that it was an exaggerated explanation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.132
description: "May the Supreme Lord, who is known as the son of Śrīmatī Śacīdevī, be transcendentally situated in the innermost core of your heart. Resplendent with the radiance of molten gold, He has descended in the Age of Kali by His causeless mercy to bestow what no incarnation has ever offered before: the most elevated mellow of devotional service, the mellow of conjugal love."
text:
> anarpita-carīṁ cirāt karuṇayāvatīrṇaḥ kalau
> samarpayitum unnatojjvala-rasāṁ sva-bhakti-śriyam
> hariḥ puraṭa-sundara-dyuti-kadamba-sandīpitaḥ
> sadā hṛdaya-kandare sphuratu vaḥ śacī-nandanaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anarpita]]---not bestowed; [[synonyms:c:carīm]]---having been formerly; [[synonyms:c:cirāt]]---for a long time; [[synonyms:k:karuṇayā]]---by causeless mercy; [[synonyms:a:avatīrṇaḥ]]---descended; [[synonyms:k:kalau]]---in the Age of Kali; [[synonyms:s:samarpayitum]]---to bestow; [[synonyms:u:unnata]]---elevated; [[synonyms:u:ujjvala]]-[[synonyms:r:rasām]]---the conjugal mellow; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---of His own service; [[synonyms:ś:śriyam]]---the treasure; [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:p:puraṭa]]---than gold; [[synonyms:s:sundara]]---more beautiful; [[synonyms:d:dyuti]]---of splendor; [[synonyms:k:kadamba]]---with a multitude; [[synonyms:s:sandīpitaḥ]]---illuminated; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]-[[synonyms:k:kandare]]---in the cavity of the heart; [[synonyms:s:sphuratu]]---let Him be manifest; [[synonyms:v:vaḥ]]---your; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:n:nandanaḥ]]---the son of mother Śacī.
translation: "May the Supreme Lord, who is known as the son of Śrīmatī Śacīdevī, be transcendentally situated in the innermost core of your heart. Resplendent with the radiance of molten gold, He has descended in the Age of Kali by His causeless mercy to bestow what no incarnation has ever offered before: the most elevated mellow of devotional service, the mellow of conjugal love."
purport: This verse (//Vidagdha-mādhava// 1.2) also appears in //Ādi-līlā// (1.4 and 3.4). In his commentary on //Vidagdha-mādhava,// Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī  Ṭhākura remarks: //mahā-prabhoḥ sphūrtiṁ vinā hari-līlā-rasāsvādanānupapatter iti bhāvaḥ.// Without the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, one cannot describe the pastimes of the Supreme personality of Godhead. Therefore Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī said, //vaḥ yuṣmākaṁ hṛdaya-rūpa-guhā yāṁ śacī-nandano hariḥ, pakṣe, siṁhaḥ sphuratu:// "May Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is exactly like a lion that kills all the elephants of desire, be awakened within everyone's heart, for by His merciful blessings one can understand the transcendental pastimes of Kṛṣṇa."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.133
description: All the devotees present so greatly appreciated this verse that they expressed their gratitude to Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī for his transcendental recitation.
text:
> saba bhakta-gaṇa kahe śloka śuniyā
> kṛtārtha karilā sabāya śloka śunāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees present there; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---say; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing this verse; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---you have obliged; [[synonyms:s:sabāya]]---everyone; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:ś:śunāñā]]---by reciting this verse.
translation: All the devotees present so greatly appreciated this verse that they expressed their gratitude to Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī for his transcendental recitation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.134
description: Rāmānanda Rāya inquired, "How have you introduced the assembly of the players?" Rūpa Gosvāmī replied, "The players assemble at a suitable time under the heading of pravartaka.
text:
> rāya kahe,---"kon āmukhe pātra-sannidhāna?"
> rūpa kahe,---"kāla-sāmye 'pravartaka' nāma"
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Rāmānanda Rāya says; [[synonyms:k:kon]]---what; [[synonyms:ā:āmukhe]]---by introduction; [[synonyms:p:pātra]]-[[synonyms:s:sannidhāna]]---presence of the players; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī replies; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]-[[synonyms:s:sāmye]]---in agreement of time; [[synonyms:p:pravartaka]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the introduction called //pravartaka.//
translation: Rāmānanda Rāya inquired, "How have you introduced the assembly of the players?" Rūpa Gosvāmī replied, "The players assemble at a suitable time under the heading of pravartaka.
purport:
In a drama all the actors are called //pātra,// or players. This is stated by Viśvanātha Kavirāja in the //Sāhitya-darpaṇa// (6.283):

> divya-martye sa tad-rūpo
> miśram anyataras tayoḥ
> sūcayed vastu-bījaṁ vā-
> mukhaṁ pātram athāpi vā

The meaning of //āmukha// is stated by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī in the //Nāṭaka-candrikā://

> sūtra-dhāro naṭī brūte
> sva-kāryaṁ pratiyuktitaḥ
> prastutākṣepicitroktyā
> yat tad āmukham īritam

When Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya inquired about the arrangement for introducing the assembly of players in the drama, Rūpa Gosvāmī replied that when the players first enter the stage in response to the time, the introduction is technically called //pravartaka.// For an example one may consult the //Antya-līlā,// First Chapter, verse 17. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that the introduction, which is technically called //āmukha,// may be of five different kinds, according to the //Sāhitya-darpaṇa// (6.288):

> udghātyakaḥ kathodghātaḥ
> prayogātiśayas tathā
> pravartakāvalagite
> pañca prastāvanā-bhidāḥ

Introductions may be classified as follows: (1) //udghātyaka,// (2) //kathodghāta,// (3) //prayogātiśaya,// (4) //pravartaka// and (5) //avalagita.// These five kinds of introduction are called //āmukha.// Thus Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya asked which of the five introductions had been employed, and Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī replied that he had used the introduction called the //pravartaka.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.135
description: 'When the entrance of the actors is set in motion by the arrival of a suitable time, the entrance is called pravartaka.'
text:
> ākṣiptaḥ kāla-sāmyena
> praveśaḥ syāt pravartakaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ākṣiptaḥ]]---set in motion; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]-[[synonyms:s:sāmyena]]---by a suitable time; [[synonyms:p:praveśaḥ]]---the entrance; [[synonyms:s:syāt]]---should be; [[synonyms:p:pravartakaḥ]]---named //pravartaka.//
translation: 'When the entrance of the actors is set in motion by the arrival of a suitable time, the entrance is called pravartaka.'
purport: This verse is from //Nāṭaka-candrikā// (12) by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.136
description: 'Springtime had arrived, and the fuIl moon of that season inspired the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is complete in everything, with new attraction to meet the beautiful Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī at night to increase the beauty of Their pastimes.' "
text:
> so 'yaṁ vasanta-samayaḥ samiyāya yasmin
> pūrṇaṁ tam īśvaram upoḍha-navānurāgam
> gūḍha-grahā rucirayā saha rādhayāsau
> raṅgāya saṅgamayitā niśi paurṇamāsī
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:v:vasanta]]-[[synonyms:s:samayaḥ]]---springtime; [[synonyms:s:samiyāya]]---had arrived; [[synonyms:y:yasmin]]---in which; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇam]]---the complete; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---Him; [[synonyms:ī:īśvaram]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:u:upoḍha]]---obtained; [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:a:anurāgam]]---new attachment; [[synonyms:g:gūḍha]]-[[synonyms:g:grahā]]---which covered the stars; [[synonyms:r:rucirayā]]---very beautiful; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:r:rādhayā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---that full-moon night; [[synonyms:r:raṅgāya]]---for increasing the beauty; [[synonyms:s:saṅgamayitā]]---caused to meet; [[synonyms:n:niśi]]---at night; [[synonyms:p:paurṇamāsī]]---the full-moon night.
translation: 'Springtime had arrived, and the fuIl moon of that season inspired the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is complete in everything, with new attraction to meet the beautiful Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī at night to increase the beauty of Their pastimes.' "
purport: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura interprets this verse (//Vidagdha-mādhava// 1.10) in two ways, for Lord Kṛṣṇa and for Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. When interpreted for Kṛṣṇa, the night is understood to have been a dark moon night, and when interpreted for Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, it is considered to have been a full moon night.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.137
description: Rāmānanda Rāya said, "Please recite the prarocanā portion so that I may hear and examine it." Śrī Rūpa replied, "I think that the desire to hear of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is prarocanā.
text:
> rāya kahe,---"prarocanādi kaha dekhi, śuni?"
> rūpa kahe,---"mahāprabhura śravaṇecchā jāni"
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya says; [[synonyms:p:prarocanādi]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please recite the //prarocanā//; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---I shall see; [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---and hear; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosāñi replies; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]-[[synonyms:i:icchā]]---desired to hear; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I think.
translation: Rāmānanda Rāya said, "Please recite the prarocanā portion so that I may hear and examine it." Śrī Rūpa replied, "I think that the desire to hear of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is prarocanā.
purport:
The method of inducing the audience to become more and more eager to hear by praising the time and place, the hero and the audience is called //prarocanā.// This is the statement regarding //prarocanā// in the //Nāṭaka-candrikā://

> deśa-kāla-kathā-vastu-
> sabhyādīnāṁ praśaṁsayā
> śrotṝṇām unmukhī-kāraḥ
> kathiteyaṁ prarocanā

Similarly the //Sāhitya-darpaṇa// (6.286) says:

> tasyāḥ prarocanā vīthī
> tathā prahasanā-mukhe
> aṅgānyatronmukhī-kāraḥ
> praśaṁsātaḥ prarocanā

Any literature presented in Sanskrit must follow the rules and regulations mentioned in the authoritative reference books. The technical inquiries by Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya and the replies of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī indicate that both of them were expert and fully conversant with the techniques of writing drama.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.138
description: 'The devotees now present are constantly thinking of the Supreme Lord and are therefore highly advanced. This work named Vidagdha-mādhava depicts the characteristic pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa with decorations of poetic ornaments. And the inner grounds of the forest of Vṛndāvana provide a suitable platform for the dancing of Kṛṣṇa with the gopīs. Therefore I think that the pious activities of persons like us, who have tried to advance in devotional service, have now attained maturity.'
text:
> bhaktānām udagād anargala-dhiyāṁ vargo nisargojjvalaḥ
> śīlaiḥ pallavitaḥ sa ballava-vadhū-bandho prabandho 'py asau
> lebhe catvaratāṁ ca tāṇḍava-vidher vṛndāṭavī-garbha-bhūr
> manye mad-vidha-puṇya-maṇḍala-parīpāko 'yam unmīlati
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhaktānām]]---of devotees; [[synonyms:u:udagāt]]---has appeared; [[synonyms:a:anargala]]-[[synonyms:d:dhiyām]]---constantly thinking of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vargaḥ]]---the assembly; [[synonyms:n:nisarga]]-[[synonyms:u:ujjvalaḥ]]---naturally very advanced; [[synonyms:ś:śīlaiḥ]]---with natural poetic decorations; [[synonyms:p:pallavitaḥ]]---spread like the leaves of a tree; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:b:ballava]]-[[synonyms:v:vadhū]]-[[synonyms:b:bandhaḥ]]---of the friend of the //gopīs,// Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prabandhaḥ]]---a literary composition; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---that; [[synonyms:l:lebhe]]---has achieved; [[synonyms:c:catvaratām]]---the quality of a quadrangular place with level ground; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:t:tāṇḍava]]-[[synonyms:v:vidheḥ]]---for dancing; [[synonyms:v:vṛndā]]-[[synonyms:a:aṭavī]]---of the forest of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:g:garbha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūḥ]]---the inner grounds; [[synonyms:m:manye]]---I consider; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:v:vidha]]---of persons like me; [[synonyms:p:puṇya]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇḍala]]---of groups of pious activities; [[synonyms:p:parīpākaḥ]]---the full development; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:u:unmīlati]]---appears.
translation: 'The devotees now present are constantly thinking of the Supreme Lord and are therefore highly advanced. This work named Vidagdha-mādhava depicts the characteristic pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa with decorations of poetic ornaments. And the inner grounds of the forest of Vṛndāvana provide a suitable platform for the dancing of Kṛṣṇa with the gopīs. Therefore I think that the pious activities of persons like us, who have tried to advance in devotional service, have now attained maturity.'
purport: This is verse eight of the First Act of //Vidagdha-mādhava.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.139
description: "O learned devotees, I am by nature ignorant and low, yet even though it is from me that Vidagdha-mādhava has come, it is filled with descriptions of the transcendental attributes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore, wiIl not such literature bring about the attainment of the highest goal of life? Although its wood may be ignited by a low-class ma, fire can nevertheless purify gold. Although I am very low by nature, this book may help cleanse the dirt from within the hearts of the golden devotees.' "
text:
> abhivyaktā mattaḥ prakṛti-laghu-rūpād api budhā
> vidhātrī siddhārthān hari-guṇa-mayī vaḥ kṛtir iyam
> pulindenāpy agniḥ kimu samidham-unmathya janito
> hiraṇya-śreṇīnām apaharati nāntaḥ-kaluṣatām
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:abhivyaktā]]---manifested; [[synonyms:m:mattaḥ]]---from me; [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]]---by nature; [[synonyms:l:laghu]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpāt]]---situated in a lower position; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:b:budhāḥ]]---O learned devotees; [[synonyms:v:vidhātrī]]---which may bring about; [[synonyms:s:siddha]]-[[synonyms:a:arthān]]---all the objects of perfection; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mayī]]---whose subject matter is the attributes of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vaḥ]]---of you; [[synonyms:k:kṛtiḥ]]---the poetic play known as //Vidagdha-mādhava//; [[synonyms:i:iyam]]---this; [[synonyms:p:pulindena]]---by the lowest class of men; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:a:agniḥ]]---a fire; [[synonyms:k:kimu]]---whether; [[synonyms:s:samidham]]---the wood; [[synonyms:u:unmathya]]---rubbing; [[synonyms:j:janitaḥ]]---produced; [[synonyms:h:hiraṇya]]---of gold; [[synonyms:ś:śreṇīnām]]---of quantities; [[synonyms:a:apaharati]]---vanquishes; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]---inner; [[synonyms:k:kaluṣatām]]---dirty things.
translation: "O learned devotees, I am by nature ignorant and low, yet even though it is from me that Vidagdha-mādhava has come, it is filled with descriptions of the transcendental attributes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore, wiIl not such literature bring about the attainment of the highest goal of life? Although its wood may be ignited by a low-class ma, fire can nevertheless purify gold. Although I am very low by nature, this book may help cleanse the dirt from within the hearts of the golden devotees.' "
purport: This verse is also from //Vidagdha-mādhava// (1.6).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.14
description: Upon hearing this news, mother Śacī and all the other devotees of Navadvīpa were very joyful, and they all departed together for Nīlācala [Jagannātha Purī].
text:
> śuni' śacī ānandita, saba bhakta-gaṇa
> sabe mili' nīlācale karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]---mother Śacī; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very pleased; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---as well as all the other devotees of Navadvīpa; [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:m:mili']]---meeting together; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---to Jagannātha Purī, Nīlācala; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---departed.
translation: Upon hearing this news, mother Śacī and all the other devotees of Navadvīpa were very joyful, and they all departed together for Nīlācala [Jagannātha Purī].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.140
description: Then Rāmānanda Rāya inquired from Rūpa Gosvāmī about the causes of the loving affairs between Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs, such as previous attachment, transformations of love, endeavors for love, and exchanges of letters disclosing the gopīs' awakening love for Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> rāya kahe,---"kaha dekhi premotpatti-kāraṇa?
> pūrva-rāga, vikāra, ceṣṭā, kāma-likhana?"
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya further inquires; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please recite; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---so that I may know; [[synonyms:p:prema.]] [[synonyms:u:utpatti]]-[[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the causes of awakening the loving propensity; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:r:rāga]]---previous attachment; [[synonyms:v:vikāra]]---transformation; [[synonyms:c:ceṣṭā]]---endeavor; [[synonyms:k:kāma]]-[[synonyms:l:likhana]]---writing of letters disclosing the //gopīs'// attachment for Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Then Rāmānanda Rāya inquired from Rūpa Gosvāmī about the causes of the loving affairs between Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs, such as previous attachment, transformations of love, endeavors for love, and exchanges of letters disclosing the gopīs' awakening love for Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.141
description: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī gradually informed Rāmānanda Rāya about everything he asked. Hearing his explanations, all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were struck with wonder.
text:
> krame śrī-rūpa-gosāñi sakali kahila
> śuni' prabhura bhakta-gaṇera camatkāra haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:krame]]---gradually; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:sakali]] [[synonyms:k:kahila]]---explained everything; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the devotees; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonishment; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was.
translation: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī gradually informed Rāmānanda Rāya about everything he asked. Hearing his explanations, all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were struck with wonder.
purport:
Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī has explained //kāma-likhana// in his book //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi// (//Vipralambha-prakaraṇa// 26):

> sa lekhaḥ kāma-lekhaḥ syāt
> yaḥ sva-prema-prakāśakaḥ
> yuvatyā yūni yūnā ca
> yuvatyāṁ saṁprahīyate

"Exchanges of letters between a young boy and young girl concerning their awakening of attachment for one another are called //kāma-lekha.//"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.142
description: Experiencing previous attachment to Kṛṣṇa [pūrva-rāga], Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī thought: "Since I have heard the name of a person called Kṛṣṇa, I have practically lost My good sense. Then, there is another person who plays His flute in such a way that after I hear the vibration, intense madness arises in My heart. And again there is still another person to whom My mind becomes attached when I see His beautiful lightning effulgence in His picture. Therefore I think that I am greatly condemned, for I have become simultaneously attached to three persons. It would be better for Me to die because of this."
text:
> ekasya śrutam eva lumpati matiṁ kṛṣṇeti nāmākṣaraṁ
> sāndronmāda-paramparām upanayaty anyas ya vaṁśī-kalaḥ
> eṣa snigdha-ghana-dyutir manasi me lagnaḥ paṭe vīkṣaṇāt
> kaṣṭaṁ dhik puruṣa-traye ratir abhūn manye mṛtiḥ śreyasī
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ekasya]]---of one person; [[synonyms:ś:śrutam]]---heard; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:l:lumpati]]---take away; [[synonyms:m:matim]]---the mind; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:i:iti]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:a:akṣaram]]---the letters of the name; [[synonyms:s:sāndra]]-[[synonyms:u:unmāda]]---of intense madness; [[synonyms:p:paramparām]]---a shower; [[synonyms:u:upanayati]]---brings; [[synonyms:a:anyasya]]---of another; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:k:kalaḥ]]---the sound vibration of the flute; [[synonyms:e:eṣaḥ]]---this third one; [[synonyms:s:snigdha]]---giving love; [[synonyms:g:ghana]]-[[synonyms:d:dyutiḥ]]---lightninglike effulgence; [[synonyms:m:manasi]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:l:lagnaḥ]]---attachment; [[synonyms:p:paṭe]]---in the picture; [[synonyms:v:vīkṣaṇāt]]---by seeing; [[synonyms:k:kaṣṭam]] [[synonyms:d:dhik]]---oh, shame upon Me; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:t:traye]]---to three persons; [[synonyms:r:ratiḥ]]---attachment; [[synonyms:a:abhūt]]---has appeared; [[synonyms:m:manye]]---I think; [[synonyms:m:mṛtiḥ]]---death; [[synonyms:ś:śreyasī]]---better.
translation: Experiencing previous attachment to Kṛṣṇa [pūrva-rāga], Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī thought: "Since I have heard the name of a person called Kṛṣṇa, I have practically lost My good sense. Then, there is another person who plays His flute in such a way that after I hear the vibration, intense madness arises in My heart. And again there is still another person to whom My mind becomes attached when I see His beautiful lightning effulgence in His picture. Therefore I think that I am greatly condemned, for I have become simultaneously attached to three persons. It would be better for Me to die because of this."
purport: This verse is from //Vidagdha-mādhava// (2.9).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.143
description: "My dear friend, these palpitations of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's heart are extremely difficult to cure. Even if one applied some medical treatment, it would only end in defamation."
text:
> iyam sakhi suduḥsādhyā
> rādhā hṛdaya-vedanā
> kṛtā yatra cikitsāpi
> kutsāyāṁ paryavasyati
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iyam]]---this; [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---my dear friend; [[synonyms:s:suduḥsādhyā]]---incurable; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaya]]-[[synonyms:v:vedanā]]---palpitation of the heart; [[synonyms:k:kṛtā]]---done; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---in which; [[synonyms:c:cikitsā]]---treatment; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:k:kutsāyām]]---in defamation; [[synonyms:p:paryavasyati]]---ends in.
translation: "My dear friend, these palpitations of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's heart are extremely difficult to cure. Even if one applied some medical treatment, it would only end in defamation."
purport: This verse ( //Vidagdha-mādhava// 2.8) is spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī Herself.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.144
description: "O dearly beautiful, the artistic loveliness of Your picture is now impressed within My mind. Since You are now living within My mind, wherever I wish to run because I am agitated by impressions of You, I find that You, O My friend, are blocking My way."
text:
> dhari-a paḍicchanda-guṇaṁ
> sundara maha mandire tumaṁ vasasi
> taha taha rundhasi bali-aṁ
> jaha jaha ca-idā palāemhi
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dhari]]-[[synonyms:a:a]]---capturing; [[synonyms:p:paḍicchanda]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇam]]---the quality of an artistic picture; [[synonyms:s:sundara]]---O most beautiful one; [[synonyms:m:maha]]---my; [[synonyms:m:mandire]]---within the heart; [[synonyms:t:tumam]]---You; [[synonyms:v:vasasi]]---reside; [[synonyms:t:taha]] [[synonyms:t:taha]]---that much; [[synonyms:r:rundhasi]]---You block; [[synonyms:b:bali]]-[[synonyms:a:am]]---by force; [[synonyms:j:jaha]] [[synonyms:j:jaha]]---as much as; [[synonyms:c:ca]]-[[synonyms:i:idā]]---being disturbed; [[synonyms:p:palāemhi]]---I try to escape.
translation: "O dearly beautiful, the artistic loveliness of Your picture is now impressed within My mind. Since You are now living within My mind, wherever I wish to run because I am agitated by impressions of You, I find that You, O My friend, are blocking My way."
purport:
This verse (//Vidagdha-mādhava// 2.33) is written in the Prākṛta language, not in Sanskrit. When transformed into Sanskrit, it reads as follows:

> dhṛtvā praticchanda-guṇaṁ sundara mama mandire tvaṁ vasasi
> tathā tathā ruṇatsi balitaṁ yathā yathā cakitā palāye

The meaning is the same, but the native language is different. It //was// spoken by Madhumaṅgala to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.145
description: "Upon seeing peacock feathers in front of Her, this girl suddenly begins trembling. When She sometimes sees a necklace of guñjā [small conchshells], She sheds tears and cries Ioudly. I do not know what kind of new ecstatic influence has entered the heart of this poor girl. It has imbued Her with the dancing attitude of a player creating wonderful, unprecedented dances on a stage."
text:
> agre vīkṣya śikhaṇḍa-khaṇḍam acirād utkampam ālambate
> guñjānāṁ ca vilokanān muhur asau sāsraṁ parikrośati
> no jāne janayann apūrva-naṭana-krīḍā-camatkāritāṁ
> bālāyāḥ kila citta-bhūmim aviśat ko 'yaṁ navīna-grahaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:agre]]---in front; [[synonyms:v:vīkṣya]]---seeing; [[synonyms:ś:śikhaṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:k:khaṇḍam]]---some peacock feathers; [[synonyms:a:acirāt]]---all of a sudden; [[synonyms:u:utkampam]]---trembling of the heart and body; [[synonyms:ā:ālambate]]---takes to; [[synonyms:g:guñjānām]]---of a garland of //guñjā// (small conchshells); [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:v:vilokanāt]]---by seeing; [[synonyms:m:muhuḥ]]---constantly; [[synonyms:a:asau]]---She; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:a:asram]]---with tears; [[synonyms:p:parikrośati]]---goes around crying; [[synonyms:n:no]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---I know; [[synonyms:j:janayan]]---awakening; [[synonyms:a:apūrva]]-[[synonyms:n:naṭana]]---like unheard-of dramatic dancing; [[synonyms:k:krīḍā]]---of activities; [[synonyms:c:camatkāritām]]---the madness; [[synonyms:b:bālāyāḥ]]---of this poor girl; [[synonyms:k:kila]]---certainly; [[synonyms:c:citta]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūmim]]---within the heart; [[synonyms:a:aviśat]]---has entered; [[synonyms:k:kaḥ]]---what; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:n:navīna]]-[[synonyms:g:grahaḥ]]---new ecstatic influence.
translation: "Upon seeing peacock feathers in front of Her, this girl suddenly begins trembling. When She sometimes sees a necklace of guñjā [small conchshells], She sheds tears and cries Ioudly. I do not know what kind of new ecstatic influence has entered the heart of this poor girl. It has imbued Her with the dancing attitude of a player creating wonderful, unprecedented dances on a stage."
purport: This verse (//Vidagdha-mādhava// 2.15) is spoken by Mukharā, Lord Kṛṣṇa's grandmother, in a conversation with the grandmother of Rādhārāṇī, Paurṇamāsī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.146
description: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī said to Her constant companion Viśākhā: "My dear friend, if Kṛṣṇa is unkind to Me, there will be no need for you to cry, for it wiIl not be due to any fault of yours. I shall then have to die, but afterwards please do one thing for Me: to observe My funeral ceremony, place My body with its arms embracing a tamāla tree like creepers so that I may remain forever in Vṛndāvana undisturbed. That is My last request."(Vidagdha-mādhava 2.47)
text:
> akāruṇyaḥ kṛṣṇo yadi mayi tavāgaḥ katham idaṁ
> mudhā mā rodīr me kuru param imām uttara-kṛtim
> tamālasya skandhe vinihita-bhuja-vallarir iyaṁ
> yathā vṛndāraṇye ciram avicalā tiṣṭhati tanuḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:akāruṇyaḥ]]---very cruel; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:m:mayi]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---your; [[synonyms:ā:āgaḥ]]---offense; [[synonyms:k:katham]]---how; [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mudhā]]---uselessly; [[synonyms:m:mā]] [[synonyms:r:rodīḥ]]---do not cry; [[synonyms:m:me]]---for Me; [[synonyms:k:kuru]]---do; [[synonyms:p:param]]---but afterwards; [[synonyms:i:imām]]---this; [[synonyms:u:uttara]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛtim]]---final act; [[synonyms:t:tamālasya]]---of a //tamāla// tree; [[synonyms:s:skandhe]]---the trunk; [[synonyms:v:vinihita]]---fixed upon; [[synonyms:b:bhuja]]-[[synonyms:v:vallariḥ]]---arms like creepers; [[synonyms:i:iyam]]---this; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---as far //as// possible; [[synonyms:v:vṛndā]]-[[synonyms:a:araṇye]]---in the forest of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:c:ciram]]---forever; [[synonyms:a:avicalā]]---without being disturbed; [[synonyms:t:tiṣṭhati]]---remains; [[synonyms:t:tanuḥ]]---the body.
translation: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī said to Her constant companion Viśākhā: "My dear friend, if Kṛṣṇa is unkind to Me, there will be no need for you to cry, for it wiIl not be due to any fault of yours. I shall then have to die, but afterwards please do one thing for Me: to observe My funeral ceremony, place My body with its arms embracing a tamāla tree like creepers so that I may remain forever in Vṛndāvana undisturbed. That is My last request."(Vidagdha-mādhava 2.47)

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.147
description: Rāmānanda Rāya inquired, "What are the characteristics of emotional love?" Rūpa Gosvāmī replied, "This is the nature of emotional love for Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> rāya kahe,---"kaha dekhi bhāvera svabhāva?"
> rūpa kahe,---"aiche haya kṛṣṇa-viṣayaka 'bhāva"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.148
description: 'My dear beautiful friend, if one develops love of Godhead, love of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja, all the bitter and sweet influences of this love will manifest in one's heart. Such love of Godhead acts in two ways. The poisonous effects of love of Godhead defeat the severe and fresh poison of the serpent. Yet there is simultaneously transcendental bliss, which pours down and defeats the poisonous effects of a snake, as well as the happiness derived from pouring nectar on one's head. It is perceived as doubly effective, simultaneously poisonous and nectarean.' "
text:
> pīḍābhir nava-kāla-kūṭa-kaṭutā-garvasya nirvāsano
> nisyandena mudāṁ sudhā-madhurimāhaṅkāra-saṅkocanaḥ
> premā sundari nanda-nandana-paro jāgarti yasyāntare
>  jñāyante sphuṭam asya vakra-madhurās tenaiva vikrāntayaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pīḍābhiḥ]]---by the sufferings; [[synonyms:n:nava]]---fresh; [[synonyms:k:kāla]]-[[synonyms:k:kūṭa]]---of poison; [[synonyms:k:kaṭutā]]---of the severity; [[synonyms:g:garvasya]]---of pride; [[synonyms:n:nirvāsanaḥ]]---banishment; [[synonyms:n:nisyandena]]---by pouring down; [[synonyms:m:mudām]]---happiness; [[synonyms:s:sudhā]]---of nectar; [[synonyms:m:madhurimā]]---of the sweetness; [[synonyms:a:ahaṅkāra]]---the pride; [[synonyms:s:saṅkocanaḥ]]---minimizing; [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love; [[synonyms:s:sundari]]---beautiful friend; [[synonyms:n:nanda]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]-[[synonyms:p:paraḥ]]---fixed upon the son of Mahārāja Nanda; [[synonyms:j:jāgarti]]---develops; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---in the heart; [[synonyms:j:jñāyante]]---are perceived; [[synonyms:s:sphuṭam]]---explicitly; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of that; [[synonyms:v:vakra]]---crooked; [[synonyms:m:madhurāḥ]]---and sweet; [[synonyms:t:tena]]---by him; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---alone; [[synonyms:v:vikrāntayaḥ]]---the influences.
translation: 'My dear beautiful friend, if one develops love of Godhead, love of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja, all the bitter and sweet influences of this love will manifest in one's heart. Such love of Godhead acts in two ways. The poisonous effects of love of Godhead defeat the severe and fresh poison of the serpent. Yet there is simultaneously transcendental bliss, which pours down and defeats the poisonous effects of a snake, as well as the happiness derived from pouring nectar on one's head. It is perceived as doubly effective, simultaneously poisonous and nectarean.' "
purport: This verse is from the //Vidagdha-mādhava// (2.18). It also appears in //Madhya-līlā,// Chapter Two, verse 52. It is spoken by Paurṇamāsī.

> rūpa-gosāñi kahe,---"sāhajika prema-dharma"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.15
description: Thus all the devotees of Kulīna-grāma and Śrī Khaṇḍa, as well as Advaita Ācārya, came together to meet Śivānanda Sena.
text:
> kulīna-grāmī bhakta āra yata khaṇḍa-vāsī
> ācārya śivānanda sane mililā sabe āsi'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.150
description: 'When one hears praise from his beloved, he outwardIy remains neutral but feels pain within his heart. When he hears his beloved making accusations about him, he takes them to be jokes and enjoys pleasure. When he finds faults in his beloved, they do not diminish his love, nor do the beloved's good qualities increase his spontaneous affection. Thus spontaneous love continues under all circumstances. That is how spontaneous love of Godhead acts within the heart.'
text:
> stotraṁ yatra taṭa-sthatāṁ prakaṭayac cittasya dhatte vyathāṁ
> nindāpi pramadaṁ prayacchati parīhāsa-śriyaṁ bibhratī
> doṣeṇa kṣayitām guṇena gurutāṁ kenāpy anātanvatī
> premṇaḥ svārasikasya kasyacid iyaṁ vikrīḍati prakriyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:stotram]]---praising; [[synonyms:y:yatra]]---in which; [[synonyms:t:taṭa]]-[[synonyms:s:sthatām]]---neutrality; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭayat]]---manifesting; [[synonyms:c:cittasya]]---to the heart; [[synonyms:d:dhatte]]---gives; [[synonyms:v:vyathām]]---painful reaction; [[synonyms:n:nindā]]---blaspheming; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:p:pramadam]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:p:prayacchati]]---delivers; [[synonyms:p:parīhāsa]]---of joking; [[synonyms:ś:śriyam]]---the beauty; [[synonyms:b:bibhratī]]---bringing forth; [[synonyms:d:doṣeṇa]]---by accusation; [[synonyms:k:kṣayitām]]---the quality of diminishing; [[synonyms:g:guṇena]]---by good qualities; [[synonyms:g:gurutām]]---the importance; [[synonyms:k:kena]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---by any; [[synonyms:a:anātanvatī]]---not increasing; [[synonyms:p:premṇaḥ]]---of love of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:svārasikasya]]---spontaneous; [[synonyms:k:kasyacit]]---of any; [[synonyms:i:iyam]]---this; [[synonyms:v:vikrīḍati]]---acts within the heart; [[synonyms:p:prakriyā]]---the manner of action.
translation: 'When one hears praise from his beloved, he outwardIy remains neutral but feels pain within his heart. When he hears his beloved making accusations about him, he takes them to be jokes and enjoys pleasure. When he finds faults in his beloved, they do not diminish his love, nor do the beloved's good qualities increase his spontaneous affection. Thus spontaneous love continues under all circumstances. That is how spontaneous love of Godhead acts within the heart.'
purport: This verse from //Vidagdha-mādhava// (5.4) is spoken by Paurṇamāsī, the grandmother of Rādhārāṇī and mother of Sāndīpani Muni.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.151
description: 'Upon hearing of My cruelty, moon-faced Rādhārāṇī may establish some kind of tolerance in Her aggrieved heart. But then She might turn against Me. Or, indeed, being fearful of the lusty desires invoked by the bow of formidable Cupid, She might even give up Her life. Alas! I have foolishly uprooted the soft creeper of Her desire just when it was ready to bear fruit.'
text:
> śrutvā niṣṭhuratāṁ mamendu-vadanā premāṅkuraṁ bhindatī
> svānte śānti-dhurāṁ vidhāya vidhure prāyaḥ parāñciṣyati
> kiṁvā pāmara-kāma-kārmuka-paritrastā vimokṣyaty asūn
> hā maugdhyāt phalinī manoratha-latā mṛdvī mayonmūlitā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrutvā]]---by hearing; [[synonyms:n:niṣṭhuratām]]---cruelty; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---My; [[synonyms:i:indu]]-[[synonyms:v:vadanā]]---moonfaced; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅkuram]]---the seed of love; [[synonyms:b:bhindatī]]---splitting; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:a:ante]]---within Her heart; [[synonyms:ś:śānti]]-[[synonyms:d:dhurām]]---great toleration; [[synonyms:v:vidhāya]]---taking; [[synonyms:v:vidhure]]---aggrieved; [[synonyms:p:prāyaḥ]]---almost; [[synonyms:p:parāñciṣyati]]---may turn against; [[synonyms:k:kiṁvā]]---or; [[synonyms:p:pāmara]]---most formidable; [[synonyms:k:kāma]]---of lusty desires or Cupid; [[synonyms:k:kārmuka]]---of the bow; [[synonyms:p:paritrastā]]---frightened; [[synonyms:v:vimokṣyati]]---will give up; [[synonyms:a:asūn]]---life; [[synonyms:h:hā]]---alas; [[synonyms:m:maugdhyāt]]---on account of bewilderment; [[synonyms:p:phalinī]]---almost fruitful; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:r:ratha]]-[[synonyms:l:latā]]---the creeper of growing love; [[synonyms:m:mṛdvī]]---very soft; [[synonyms:m:mayā]]---by Me; [[synonyms:u:unmūlita]]---uprooted.
translation: 'Upon hearing of My cruelty, moon-faced Rādhārāṇī may establish some kind of tolerance in Her aggrieved heart. But then She might turn against Me. Or, indeed, being fearful of the lusty desires invoked by the bow of formidable Cupid, She might even give up Her life. Alas! I have foolishly uprooted the soft creeper of Her desire just when it was ready to bear fruit.'
purport: Having been very cruel to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Kṛṣṇa is repenting in this way ( //Vidagdha-mādhava// 2.40).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.152
description: 'Desiring the happiness of His association and embraces, My dear friend, I disregarded even My superiors and relaxed My shyness and gravity before them. Furthermore, although you are My best friend, more dear to Me than My own life, I have given you so much trouble. Indeed, I even put aside the vow of dedication to My husband, a vow kept by the most elevated women. Oh, alas! Although He is now neglecting Me, I am so sinful that I am still living. Therefore I must condemn My so-called patience.'
text:
> yasyotsaṅga-sukhāśayā śithilitā gurvī gurubhyas trapā
> prāṇebhyo 'pi suhṛt-tamāḥ sakhi tathā yūyaṁ parikleśitāḥ
> dharmaḥ so 'pi mahān mayā na gaṇitaḥ sādhvībhir adhyāsito
> dhig dhairyaṁ tad-upekṣitāpi yad ahaṁ jīvāmi pāpīyasī
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:u:utsaṅga]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśayā]]---by the desire for the happiness of the association; [[synonyms:ś:śithilitā]]---slackened; [[synonyms:g:gurvī]]---very great; [[synonyms:g:gurubhyaḥ]]---unto the superiors; [[synonyms:t:trapā]]---bashfulness; [[synonyms:p:prāṇebhyaḥ]]---than My life; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:s:suhṛt]]-[[synonyms:t:tamāḥ]]---more dear; [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---O My dear friend; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---similarly; [[synonyms:y:yūyam]]---you; [[synonyms:p:parikleśitāḥ]]---so much troubled; [[synonyms:d:dharmaḥ]]---duties to My husband; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:m:mahān]]---very great; [[synonyms:m:mayā]]---by Me; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:g:gaṇitaḥ]]---cared for; [[synonyms:s:sādhvībhiḥ]]---by the most chaste women; [[synonyms:a:adhyāsitaḥ]]---practiced; [[synonyms:d:dhik]] [[synonyms:d:dhairyam]]---to hell with patience; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---by Him; [[synonyms:u:upekṣitā]]---neglected; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:j:jīvāmi]]---am living; [[synonyms:p:pāpīyasī]]---the most sinful.
translation: 'Desiring the happiness of His association and embraces, My dear friend, I disregarded even My superiors and relaxed My shyness and gravity before them. Furthermore, although you are My best friend, more dear to Me than My own life, I have given you so much trouble. Indeed, I even put aside the vow of dedication to My husband, a vow kept by the most elevated women. Oh, alas! Although He is now neglecting Me, I am so sinful that I am still living. Therefore I must condemn My so-called patience.'
purport: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is speaking this verse (//Vidagdha-mādhava// 2.41) to Her intimate friend Viśākhādevī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.153
description: 'I was engaged in My own playful activities in My home, and because of My childish innocence I did not know right from wrong. Therefore, is it good for You to have forced us into being so much attracted to You and then to have neglected us? Now You are indifferent to us. Do You think that is right?'
text:
> gṛhāntaḥ-khelantyo nija-sahaja-bālyasya balanād
> abhadraṁ bhadraṁ vā kim api hi na jānīmahi manāk
> vayaṁ netuṁ yuktāḥ katham aśaraṇāṁ kā api daśāṁ
> kathaṁ vā nyāyyā te prathayitum udāsīna-padavī
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gṛha]]-[[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:khelantyaḥ]]---who were engaged in childish play within the house; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---one's own; [[synonyms:s:sahaja]]---simple; [[synonyms:b:bālyasya]]---of childhood; [[synonyms:b:balanāt]]---on account of influence; [[synonyms:a:abhadram]]---bad; [[synonyms:b:bhadram]]---good; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:k:kim]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---what; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jānīmahi]]---we did know; [[synonyms:m:manāk]]---even slightly; [[synonyms:v:vayam]]---we; [[synonyms:n:netum]]---to lead; [[synonyms:y:yuktāḥ]]---suitable; [[synonyms:k:katham]]---how; [[synonyms:a:aśaraṇām]]---without surrender; [[synonyms:k:kām]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---such as this; [[synonyms:d:daśām]]---to the condition; [[synonyms:k:katham]]---how; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:n:nyāyyā]]---correct; [[synonyms:t:te]]---of You; [[synonyms:p:prathayitum]]---to manifest; [[synonyms:u:udāsīna]]---of carelessness; [[synonyms:p:padavī]]---the position.
translation: 'I was engaged in My own playful activities in My home, and because of My childish innocence I did not know right from wrong. Therefore, is it good for You to have forced us into being so much attracted to You and then to have neglected us? Now You are indifferent to us. Do You think that is right?'
purport: This verse ( //Vidagdha-mādhava// 2.46) is spoken to Kṛṣṇa by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.154
description: 'Our hearts are so polluted by miserable conditions that we are certainly going to Pluto's kingdom. Nevertheless, Kṛṣṇa does not give up His beautiful loving smiling, which is full of cheating tricks. O Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, You are very intelligent. How could You have developed such great loving affection for this deceitful debauchee from the neighborhood of the cowherds?'
text:
> antaḥ-kleśa-kalaṅkitāḥ kila vayaṁ yāmo 'dya yāmyāṁ purīṁ
> nāyaṁ vañcana-sañcaya-praṇayinaṁ hāsaṁ tathāpy ujjhati
> asmin sampuṭite gabhīra-kapaṭair ābhīra-pallī-viṭe
> hā medhāvini rādhike tava kathaṁ premā garīyān abhūt
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kleśa]]-[[synonyms:k:kalaṅkitāḥ]]---polluted by inner miserable conditions that continue even after death; [[synonyms:k:kila]]---certainly; [[synonyms:v:vayam]]---all of us; [[synonyms:y:yāmaḥ]]---are going; [[synonyms:a:adya]]---now; [[synonyms:y:yāmyām]]---of Yamarāja; [[synonyms:p:purīm]]---to the abode; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:v:vañcana]]-[[synonyms:s:sañcaya]]---cheating activities; [[synonyms:p:praṇayinam]]---aiming at; [[synonyms:h:hāsam]]---smiling; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:u:ujjhati]]---gives up; [[synonyms:a:asmin]]---in this; [[synonyms:s:sampuṭite]]---filled; [[synonyms:g:gabhīra]]---deep; [[synonyms:k:kapaṭaiḥ]]---with deceit; [[synonyms:ā:ābhīra]]-[[synonyms:p:pallī]]---from the village of the cowherd men; [[synonyms:v:viṭe]]---in a debauchee; [[synonyms:h:hā]]---alas; [[synonyms:m:medhāvini]]---O intelligent one; [[synonyms:r:rādhike]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:k:katham]]---how; [[synonyms:p:premā]]---love; [[synonyms:g:garīyān]]---so great; [[synonyms:a:abhūt]]---became.
translation: 'Our hearts are so polluted by miserable conditions that we are certainly going to Pluto's kingdom. Nevertheless, Kṛṣṇa does not give up His beautiful loving smiling, which is full of cheating tricks. O Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, You are very intelligent. How could You have developed such great loving affection for this deceitful debauchee from the neighborhood of the cowherds?'
purport: This verse ( //Vidagdha-mādhava// 2.37) is spoken to Rādhārāṇī by Lalitā-sakhī, another confidential friend.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.155
description: 'O Lord Kṛṣṇa, You are just like an ocean. The river of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī has reached You from a long distance-leaving far behind the tree of Her husband, breaking through the bridge of social convention, and forcibly crossing the hills of elder relatives. Coming here because of fresh feelings of love for You, that river has now received Your shelter, but now You are trying to turn Her back by the waves of unfavorable words. How is it that You are spreading this attitude?' "
text:
> hitvā dūre pathi dhava-taror antikaṁ dharā-setor
> bhaṅgodagrā guru-śikhariṇaṁ raṁhasā laṅghayantī
> lebhe kṛṣṇārṇava nava-rasā rādhikā-vāhinī tvāṁ
> vāg-vīcibhiḥ kim iva vimukhī-bhāvam asyās tanoṣi
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hitvā]]---giving up; [[synonyms:d:dūre]]---far away; [[synonyms:p:pathi]]---on the road; [[synonyms:d:dhava]]-[[synonyms:t:taroḥ]]---of the tree of the husband; [[synonyms:a:antikam]]---the vicinity; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:s:setoḥ]]---the bridge of religion; [[synonyms:b:bhaṅga]]-[[synonyms:u:udagrā]]---being strong enough for breaking; [[synonyms:g:guru]]-[[synonyms:ś:śikhariṇam]]---the hill of the superior relatives; [[synonyms:r:raṁhasā]]---with great force; [[synonyms:l:laṅghayantī]]---crossing over; [[synonyms:l:lebhe]]---has obtained; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:arṇava]]---O ocean of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:r:rasā]]---being influenced by new ecstatic love; [[synonyms:r:rādhikā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:v:vāhinī]]---like a river; [[synonyms:t:tvām]]---You; [[synonyms:v:vāk]]-[[synonyms:v:vīcibhiḥ]]---only by the waves of words; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---how; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like this; [[synonyms:v:vimukhī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāvam]]---indifference; [[synonyms:a:asyāḥ]]---toward Her; [[synonyms:t:tanoṣi]]---You are spreading.
translation: 'O Lord Kṛṣṇa, You are just like an ocean. The river of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī has reached You from a long distance-leaving far behind the tree of Her husband, breaking through the bridge of social convention, and forcibly crossing the hills of elder relatives. Coming here because of fresh feelings of love for You, that river has now received Your shelter, but now You are trying to turn Her back by the waves of unfavorable words. How is it that You are spreading this attitude?' "
purport: This verse from //Vidagdha-mādhava// (3.9) is spoken to Lord Kṛṣṇa by paurṇamāsī, the grandmother of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.156
description: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya further inquired: "How have you described Vṛndāvana, the vibration of the transcendental flute, and the relationship between Kṛṣṇa and Rādhikā?
text:
> rāya kahe,---"vṛndāvana, muralī-niḥsvana
> kṛṣṇa, rādhikāra kaiche kariyācha varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Rāmānanda Rāya says; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---the place named Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:m:muralī]]-[[synonyms:n:niḥsvana]]---the vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rādhikāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:k:kaiche]]---how; [[synonyms:k:kariyācha]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---you have described.
translation: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya further inquired: "How have you described Vṛndāvana, the vibration of the transcendental flute, and the relationship between Kṛṣṇa and Rādhikā?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.157
description: "Please tell me all this, for your poetic ability is wonderful." After offering obeisances to Rāmānanda Rāya, Rūpa Gosvāmī gradually began answering his inquiries.
text:
> kaha, tomāra kavitva śuni' haya camatkāra"
> krame rūpa-gosāñi kahe kari' namaskāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---kindly let me know; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:k:kavitva]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---by hearing your poetic ability; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---much astonishment; [[synonyms:k:krame]]---gradually; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---continues to speak; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---offering obeisances.
translation: "Please tell me all this, for your poetic ability is wonderful." After offering obeisances to Rāmānanda Rāya, Rūpa Gosvāmī gradually began answering his inquiries.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.158
description: 'The sweet, fragrant honey oozing from newly grown mango buds is again and again attracting groups of bumblebees, and this forest is trembling in the softly moving breezes from the Malaya Hills, which are full of sandalwood trees. Thus the forest of Vṛndāvana is increasing My transcendental pleasure.'
text:
> sugandhau mākanda-prakara-makarandasya madhure
> vinisyande vandī-kṛta-madhupa-vṛndaṁ muhur idam
> kṛtāndolaṁ mandonnatibhir anilaiś candana-girer
> mamānandaṁ vṛndā-vipinam atulaṁ tundilayati
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:g:gandhau]]---in the fragrance; [[synonyms:m:mākanda]]-[[synonyms:p:prakara]]---of the bunches of mango buds; [[synonyms:m:makarandasya]]---of the honey; [[synonyms:m:madhure]]---sweet; [[synonyms:v:vinisyande]]---in the oozing; [[synonyms:v:vandī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛta]]---grouped together; [[synonyms:m:madhupa]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndam]]---bumblebees; [[synonyms:m:muhuḥ]]---again and again; [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:andolam]]---agitated; [[synonyms:m:manda]]-[[synonyms:u:unnatibhiḥ]]---moving softly; [[synonyms:a:anilaiḥ]]---by the breezes; [[synonyms:c:candana]]-[[synonyms:g:gireḥ]]---from the Malaya Hills; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---My; [[synonyms:ā:ānandam]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:v:vṛndā]]-[[synonyms:v:vipinam]]---the forest of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:a:atulam]]---very much; [[synonyms:t:tundilayati]]---increases more and more.
translation: 'The sweet, fragrant honey oozing from newly grown mango buds is again and again attracting groups of bumblebees, and this forest is trembling in the softly moving breezes from the Malaya Hills, which are full of sandalwood trees. Thus the forest of Vṛndāvana is increasing My transcendental pleasure.'
purport: This verse from //Vidagdha-mādhava// (1.23) is spoken by Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.159
description: 'My dear friend, see how this forest of Vṛndāvana is full of transcendental creepers and trees. The tops of the creepers are full of flowers, and intoxicated bumblebees are buzzing around them, humming songs that please the ear and surpass even the Vedic hymns.'
text:
> vṛndāvanaṁ divya-latā-parītaṁ
> latāś ca puṣpa-sphuritāgra-bhājaḥ
> puṣpāṇi ca sphīta-madhu-vratāni
> madhu-vratāś ca śruti-hāri-gītāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvanam]]---the forest of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:l:latā]]-[[synonyms:p:parītam]]---surrounded by transcendental creepers; [[synonyms:l:latāḥ]] [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and the creepers; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]---by flowers; [[synonyms:s:sphurita]]---distinguished; [[synonyms:a:agra]]-[[synonyms:b:bhājaḥ]]---possessing ends; [[synonyms:p:puṣpāṇi]]---the flowers; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:s:sphīta]]-[[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:v:vratāni]]---having many maddened bumblebees; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:v:vratāḥ]]---the bumblebees; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:ś:śruti]]-[[synonyms:h:hāri]]-[[synonyms:g:gītāḥ]]---whose songs defeat the Vedic hymns and are pleasing to the ear.
translation: 'My dear friend, see how this forest of Vṛndāvana is full of transcendental creepers and trees. The tops of the creepers are full of flowers, and intoxicated bumblebees are buzzing around them, humming songs that please the ear and surpass even the Vedic hymns.'
purport: This verse from //Vidagdha-mādhava// (1.24) is spoken by Lord Balarāma to His friend Śrīdāmā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.16
description: Śivānanda Sena arranged for the journey. He maintained everyone and provided residential quarters.
text:
> śivānanda kare sabāra ghāṭi samādhāna
> sabāre pālana kare, deya vāsā-sthāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śivānanda]]---of the name Śivānanda; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:g:ghāṭi]]---the camp; [[synonyms:s:samādhāna]]---arrangement; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:p:pālana]]---maintenance; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:d:deya]]---gives; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---residential quarters.
translation: Śivānanda Sena arranged for the journey. He maintained everyone and provided residential quarters.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.160
description: 'My dear friend, this forest of Vṛndāvana is giving great pleasure to our senses in various ways. Somewhere bumblebees are singing in groups, and in some places mild breezes are cooling the entire atmosphere. Somewhere the creepers and tree twigs are dancing, the mallikā flowers are expanding their fragrance, and an overabundance of juice is constantly flowing in showers from pomegranate fruits.'
text:
> kvacid bhṛṅgī-gītaṁ kvacid anila-bhaṅgī-śiśiratā
> kvacid vallī-lāsyaṁ kvacid amala-mallī-parimalaḥ
> kvacid dhārā-śālī karaka-phala-pālī-rasa-bharo
> hṛṣīkāṇāṁ vṛndaṁ pramadayati vṛndāvanam idam
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kvacit]]---somewhere; [[synonyms:b:bhṛṅgī]]-[[synonyms:g:gītam]]---the humming songs of the bumblebees; [[synonyms:k:kvacit]]---somewhere; [[synonyms:a:anila]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṅgī]]-[[synonyms:ś:śiśiratā]]---coolness from the waves of the mild breezes; [[synonyms:k:kvacit]]---somewhere; [[synonyms:v:vallī]]-[[synonyms:l:lāsyam]]---the dancing of the creepers; [[synonyms:k:kvacit]]---somewhere; [[synonyms:a:amala]]-[[synonyms:m:mallī]]-[[synonyms:p:parimalaḥ]]---the pure fragrance of the //mallikā// flowers; [[synonyms:k:kvacit]]---somewhere; [[synonyms:d:dhārā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śālī]]---abounding in showers; [[synonyms:k:karaka]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]-[[synonyms:p:pālī]]---of pomegranate fruits; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:b:bharaḥ]]---overabundance of juice; [[synonyms:h:hṛṣīkāṇām]]---of the senses; [[synonyms:v:vṛndam]]---to the group; [[synonyms:p:pramadayati]]---is giving pleasure; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvanam]]---the forest of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:i:idam]]---this.
translation: 'My dear friend, this forest of Vṛndāvana is giving great pleasure to our senses in various ways. Somewhere bumblebees are singing in groups, and in some places mild breezes are cooling the entire atmosphere. Somewhere the creepers and tree twigs are dancing, the mallikā flowers are expanding their fragrance, and an overabundance of juice is constantly flowing in showers from pomegranate fruits.'
purport: This verse from //Vidagdha-mādhava// (1.31) is spoken by Lord Kṛṣṇa to His cowherd friend Madhumaṅgala.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.161
description: The flute of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes measures three fingers in length, and it is bedecked with indra-nīla gems. At the ends of the flute are aruṇa gems [rubies], glittering beautifully, and in between the flute is plated with gold, set ablaze by diamonds. This auspicious flute, pleasing to Kṛṣṇa, is glittering in His hand with transcendental brilliance.'
text:
> parāmṛṣṭāṅguṣṭha-trayam asita-ratnair ubhayato
> vahantī saṅkīrṇau maṇibhir aruṇais tat-parisarau
> tayor madhye hīrojjvala-vimala-jāmbūnada-mayī
> kare kalyāṇīyaṁ viharati hareḥ keli-muralī
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:parāmṛṣṭā]]---measured; [[synonyms:a:anguṣṭha]]-[[synonyms:t:trayam]]---a length of three fingers; [[synonyms:a:asita]]-[[synonyms:r:ratnaiḥ]]---with valuable //indra-nīla// jewels; [[synonyms:u:ubhayataḥ]]---from both ends; [[synonyms:v:vahantī]]---having; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrṇau]]---bedecked; [[synonyms:m:maṇibhiḥ]]---by gems; [[synonyms:a:aruṇaiḥ]]---rubies; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:p:parisarau]]---the two ends of the flute; [[synonyms:t:tayoḥ]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---between them; [[synonyms:h:hīra]]---with diamonds; [[synonyms:u:ujjvala]]---blazing; [[synonyms:v:vimala]]---pure; [[synonyms:j:jāmbūnada]]-[[synonyms:m:mayī]]---covered with gold plate; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---in the hand; [[synonyms:k:kalyāṇī]]---very auspicious; [[synonyms:i:iyam]]---this; [[synonyms:v:viharati]]---glitters; [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]]---of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:keli]]-[[synonyms:m:muralī]]---the pastime flute.
translation: The flute of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes measures three fingers in length, and it is bedecked with indra-nīla gems. At the ends of the flute are aruṇa gems [rubies], glittering beautifully, and in between the flute is plated with gold, set ablaze by diamonds. This auspicious flute, pleasing to Kṛṣṇa, is glittering in His hand with transcendental brilliance.'
purport: This verse from //Vidagdha-mādhava// (3.1) is spoken to Lalitādevī by Paurṇamāsī, the grandmother of Rādhārāṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.162
description: My dear friend the flute, it appears that you have been born of a very good family, for your residence is in the hands of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. By birth you are simple and are not at all crooked. Why then have you taken initiation into this dangerous mantra that enchants the assembled gopīs?'
text:
> sad-vaṁśatas tava janiḥ puruṣottamasya
> pāṇau sthitir muralike saralāsi jātyā
> kasmāt tvayā sakhi guror viṣamā gṛhītā
> gopāṅganā-gaṇa-vimohana-man tra-dīkṣā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:v:vaṁśataḥ]]---very respectable families; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---your; [[synonyms:j:janiḥ]]---birth; [[synonyms:p:puruṣottamasya]]---of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pāṇau]]---in the hands; [[synonyms:s:sthitiḥ]]---residence; [[synonyms:m:muralike]]---O good flute; [[synonyms:s:saralā]]---simple; [[synonyms:a:asi]]---you are; [[synonyms:j:jātyā]]---by birth; [[synonyms:k:kasmāt]]---why; [[synonyms:t:tvayā]]---by you; [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---O my dear friend; [[synonyms:g:guroḥ]]---from the spiritual master; [[synonyms:v:viṣamā]]---dangerous; [[synonyms:g:gṛhītā]]---taken; [[synonyms:g:gopā]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅganā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:vimohana]]---for bewildering the groups of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:m:mantra]]-[[synonyms:d:dīkṣā]]---initiation in the //mantra.//
translation: My dear friend the flute, it appears that you have been born of a very good family, for your residence is in the hands of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. By birth you are simple and are not at all crooked. Why then have you taken initiation into this dangerous mantra that enchants the assembled gopīs?'
purport: This verse (//Vidagdha-mādhava// 5.17) is spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.163
description: My dear friend the flute, you are actually full of many holes or faults. You are light, hard, juiceless and full of knots. But what kind of pious activities have engaged you in the service of being kissed by the Lord and embraced by His hands?'
text:
> sakhi murali viśāla-cchidra-jalena pūrṇā
> laghur atikaṭhinā tvaṁ granthilā nīrasāsi
> tad api bhajasi śvaśvac cumbanānanda-sāndraṁ
> hari-kara-parirambhaṁ kena puṇyodayena
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakhi]] [[synonyms:m:murali]]---O dear friend the flute; [[synonyms:v:viśāla]]-[[synonyms:c:chidra]]-[[synonyms:j:jālena]]---with so many big holes in your body (in other words, full of //chidra,// which also means "faults"); [[synonyms:p:pūrṇā]]---full; [[synonyms:l:laghuḥ]]---very light; [[synonyms:a:atikaṭhinā]]---very hard in constitution; [[synonyms:t:tvam]]---you; [[synonyms:g:granthilā]]---full of knots; [[synonyms:n:nīrasā]]---without juice; [[synonyms:a:asi]]---are; [[synonyms:t:tat]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---therefore; [[synonyms:b:bhajasi]]---you obtain through service; [[synonyms:ś:śvaśvat]]---continuously; [[synonyms:c:cumbana]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---the transcendental bliss of kissing by the Lord; [[synonyms:s:sāndram]]---intense; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:k:kara]]-[[synonyms:p:parirambham]]---embracing by the hands of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kena]]---by what; [[synonyms:p:puṇya]]-[[synonyms:u:udayena]]---means of pious activities.
translation: My dear friend the flute, you are actually full of many holes or faults. You are light, hard, juiceless and full of knots. But what kind of pious activities have engaged you in the service of being kissed by the Lord and embraced by His hands?'
purport: This verse ( //Vidagdha-mādhava// 4.7) is spoken by Candrāvalī-sakhī, the //gopī// competitor of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.164
description: 'The transcendental vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute blocked the movements of the rain clouds, struck the Gandharvas full of wonder, and agitated the meditation of great saintly persons like Sanaka and Sanandana. It created wonder in Lord Brahmā, wrought intense curiosity that agitated the mind of Bali Mahārāja, who was otherwise firmly fixed, made Mahārāja Ananta, the carrier of the planets, whirl around, and penetrated the strong coverings of the universe. Thus the sound of the flute in the hands of Kṛṣṇa created a wonderful situation.'
text:
> rundhann ambu-bhṛtaś camatkṛti-paraṁ kurvan muhus tumburuṁ
> dhyānād antarayan sanandana-mukhān vismāpayan vedhasam
> autsukyāvalibhir baliṁ caṭulayan bhogīndram āghūrṇayan
> bhindann aṇḍa-kaṭāha-bhittim abhito babhrāma vaṁśī-dhvaniḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rundhan]]---blocking; [[synonyms:a:ambu]]-[[synonyms:b:bhṛtaḥ]]---the clouds bearing rain; [[synonyms:c:camatkṛti]]-[[synonyms:p:param]]---full of wonder; [[synonyms:k:kurvan]]---making; [[synonyms:m:muhuḥ]]---at every moment; [[synonyms:t:tumburum]]---the King of the Gandharvas, Tumburu; [[synonyms:d:dhyānāt]]---from meditation; [[synonyms:a:antarayan]]---disturbing; [[synonyms:s:sanandana]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhān]]---the great saintly persons headed by Sanandana; [[synonyms:v:vismāpayan]]---causing wonder; [[synonyms:v:vedhasam]]---even to Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:a:autsukya]]-[[synonyms:ā:āvalibhiḥ]]---with thoughts of curiosity; [[synonyms:b:balim]]---King Bali; [[synonyms:c:caṭulayan]]---agitating; [[synonyms:b:bhogī]]-[[synonyms:i:indram]]---the King of the Nāgas; [[synonyms:ā:āghūrṇayan]]---whirling around; [[synonyms:b:bhindan]]---penetrating; [[synonyms:a:aṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:k:kaṭāha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhittim]]---the strong coverings of the universe; [[synonyms:a:abhitaḥ]]---all around; [[synonyms:b:babhrāma]]---circulated; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvaniḥ]]---the transcendental vibration of the flute.
translation: 'The transcendental vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute blocked the movements of the rain clouds, struck the Gandharvas full of wonder, and agitated the meditation of great saintly persons like Sanaka and Sanandana. It created wonder in Lord Brahmā, wrought intense curiosity that agitated the mind of Bali Mahārāja, who was otherwise firmly fixed, made Mahārāja Ananta, the carrier of the planets, whirl around, and penetrated the strong coverings of the universe. Thus the sound of the flute in the hands of Kṛṣṇa created a wonderful situation.'
purport: This verse (//Vidagdha-mādhava// 1.27) is spoken by Madhumaṅgala, a cowherd friend of Kṛṣṇa's.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.165
description: 'The beauty of Kṛṣṇa's eyes surpasses the beauty of white lotus flowers, His yellow garments surpass the brilliance of fresh decorations of kuṅkuma, His ornaments of selected forest flowers surpass the hankering for the best of garments, and His bodily beauty possesses mind-attracting splendor greater than the jewels known as marakata-maṇi [emeralds].'
text:
> ayaṁ nayana-daṇḍita-pra vara-puṇḍarīka-prabhaḥ
> prabhāti nava-jāguḍa-dyuti-viḍambi-pītāmbaraḥ
> araṇyaja-pariṣkriyā-damita-divya-veśādaro
> harin-maṇi-manohara-dyutibhir ujjvalāṅgo hariḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:n:nayana]]---by whose beautiful eyes; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍita]]---defeated; [[synonyms:p:pravara]]---best; [[synonyms:p:puṇḍarīka]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhaḥ]]---the luster of the white lotus flower; [[synonyms:p:prabhāti]]---looks beautiful; [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:j:jāguḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:dyuti]]---the brilliance of newly painted //viḍambi//; [[synonyms:v:viḍambi]]---deriding; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]-[[synonyms:a:ambaraḥ]]---whose yellow dress; [[synonyms:a:araṇya]]-[[synonyms:j:ja]]---picked up from the forest; [[synonyms:p:pariṣkriyā]]---by whose ornaments; [[synonyms:d:damita]]---subdued; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:v:veśa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādaraḥ]]---the hankering for first-class dress; [[synonyms:h:harin]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇi]]---of emeralds; [[synonyms:m:manohara]]---mind-attracting; [[synonyms:d:dyutibhiḥ]]---with splendor; [[synonyms:u:ujjvala]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅgaḥ]]---whose beautiful body; [[synonyms:h:hariḥ]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: 'The beauty of Kṛṣṇa's eyes surpasses the beauty of white lotus flowers, His yellow garments surpass the brilliance of fresh decorations of kuṅkuma, His ornaments of selected forest flowers surpass the hankering for the best of garments, and His bodily beauty possesses mind-attracting splendor greater than the jewels known as marakata-maṇi [emeralds].'
purport: This verse from //Vidagdha-mādhava// (1.17) is spoken by paurṇamāsī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.166
description: 'O most beautiful friend, please accept the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is standing before you full of transcendental bliss. The borders of His eyes roam from side to side, and His eyebrows move slowly like bumblebees on His lotuslike face. Standing with His right foot placed below the knee of His left leg, the middle of His body curved in three places, and His neck gracefully tilted to the side, He takes His flute to His pursed lips and moves His fingers upon it here and there.'
text:
> jaṅghādhas-taṭa-saṅgi-dakṣiṇa-padaṁ kiñcid vibhugna-trikam-
> sāci-stambhita-kandharaṁ sakhi tiraḥ-sañcāri-netrāñcalam
> vaṁśīṁ kuṭmalite dadhānam adhare lolāṅgulī-saṅgatāṁ
> riṅgad-bhrū-bhramaraṁ varāṅgi paramānandaṁ puraḥ svīkuru
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaṅghā]]---of the shin; [[synonyms:a:adhaḥ]]-[[synonyms:t:taṭa]]---at the lower border; [[synonyms:s:saṅgi]]---connected; [[synonyms:d:dakṣiṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:padam]]---the right foot; [[synonyms:k:kiñcit]]---slightly; [[synonyms:v:vibhugna]]-[[synonyms:t:trikam]]---the middle of the body bent in three places; [[synonyms:s:sāci]]-[[synonyms:s:stumbhita]]-[[synonyms:k:kandharam]]---whose neck is fixed in a curve to the side; [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---O friend; [[synonyms:t:tiraḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:sañcāri]]---roaming sideways; [[synonyms:n:netra]]-[[synonyms:a:añcalam]]---whose borders of the eyes; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśīm]]---flute; [[synonyms:k:kuṭmalite]]---shut like a flower bud; [[synonyms:d:dadhānam]]---placing; [[synonyms:a:adhare]]---on the lips; [[synonyms:l:lolā]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅgulī]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgatām]]---joined with fingers moving here and there; [[synonyms:r:riṅgat]]-[[synonyms:b:bhrū]]---whose slowly moving eyebrows; [[synonyms:b:bhramaram]]---like bumblebees; [[synonyms:v:varāṅgi]]---O most beautiful one; [[synonyms:p:paramānandam]]---the personality of bliss; [[synonyms:p:puraḥ]]---situated in front; [[synonyms:s:svī]]-[[synonyms:k:kuru]]---just accept.
translation: 'O most beautiful friend, please accept the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is standing before you full of transcendental bliss. The borders of His eyes roam from side to side, and His eyebrows move slowly like bumblebees on His lotuslike face. Standing with His right foot placed below the knee of His left leg, the middle of His body curved in three places, and His neck gracefully tilted to the side, He takes His flute to His pursed lips and moves His fingers upon it here and there.'
purport: This verse is from the //Lalita-mādhava-nāṭaka// (4.27), a ten-act play by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. The speaker here is Lalitādevī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.167
description: 'O beautiful-faced one, who is this creative person standing before us? With the sharp chisels of His loving glances, He is splitting the hard stones of many women's devotion to their husbands. And with the luster of His body, surpassing the brilliance of countless emeralds, He is simultaneously constructing private meeting places for His pastimes.'
text:
> kula-varatanu-dharma-grāva-vṛndāni bhindan
> sumukhi niśita-dīrghāpāṅga-ṭaṅka-cchaṭābhiḥ
> yugapad ayam apūrvaḥ kaḥ puro viśva-karmā
> marakata-maṇi-lakṣair goṣṭha-kakṣāṁ cinoti
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kula]]-[[synonyms:v:varatanu]]---of the family women; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---in the form of dedication to the husband, etc.; [[synonyms:g:grāva]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndāni]]---the stones; [[synonyms:b:bhindan]]---splitting; [[synonyms:s:sumukhi]]---O beautiful-faced one; [[synonyms:n:niśita]]---sharp; [[synonyms:d:dīrgha]]-[[synonyms:a:apāṅga]]---in the form of long outer corners of the eyes; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭaṅka]]-[[synonyms:c:chaṭābhiḥ]]---by chisels; [[synonyms:y:yugapat]]---simultaneously; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:a:apūrvaḥ]]---unprecedented; [[synonyms:k:kaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:p:puraḥ]]---in front; [[synonyms:v:viśva]]-[[synonyms:k:karmā]]---creative person; [[synonyms:m:marakata]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇi]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣaiḥ]]---with countless emeralds; [[synonyms:g:goṣṭha]]-[[synonyms:k:kakṣām]]---a private room for meeting; [[synonyms:c:cinoti]]---He is constructing.
translation: 'O beautiful-faced one, who is this creative person standing before us? With the sharp chisels of His loving glances, He is splitting the hard stones of many women's devotion to their husbands. And with the luster of His body, surpassing the brilliance of countless emeralds, He is simultaneously constructing private meeting places for His pastimes.'
purport: This verse (//Lalita-mādhava// 1.52) is spoken by Rādhārāṇī to Lalitādevī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.168
description: My dear friend, this newly youthful Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the moon in the family of Nanda Mahārāja, is so beautiful that He defies the beauty of clusters of valuable jewels. All glories to the vibration of His flute, for it is cunningly breaking the patience of chaste ladies by loosening their belts and tight dresses.'
text:
> mahendra-maṇi-maṇḍalī-mada-viḍambi-deha-dyutir
> vrajendra-kula-candramāḥ sphurati ko 'pi navyo yuvā
> sakhi sthira-kulāṅganā-nikara-nīvi-bandhārgala-
> cchidākaraṇa-kautukī jayati yasya vaṁśī-dhvaniḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahendra]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇi]]---of jewels of the name //mahendra-maṇi//; [[synonyms:m:maṇḍalī]]---of masses; [[synonyms:m:mada]]-[[synonyms:v:viḍambi]]---defeating the pride; [[synonyms:d:deha]]-[[synonyms:d:dyutiḥ]]---one whose bodily luster; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:k:kula]]-[[synonyms:c:candramāḥ]]---the moon of the family of Vrajarāja (Nanda Mahārāja); [[synonyms:s:sphurati]]---manifests; [[synonyms:k:kaḥ]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---some; [[synonyms:n:navyaḥ]] [[synonyms:y:yuvā]]---newly youthful person; [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---O my dear friend; [[synonyms:s:sthira]]---steady; [[synonyms:k:kula]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅganā]]---of family ladies; [[synonyms:n:nikara]]---of groups; [[synonyms:n:nīvi]]-[[synonyms:b:bandha]]-[[synonyms:a:argala]]---of the impediments such as tightened dresses and belts; [[synonyms:c:cchidā]]-[[synonyms:k:karaṇa]]---in causing the cutting; [[synonyms:k:kautukī]]---very cunning; [[synonyms:j:jayati]]---all glories; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:v:vaṁśī]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvaniḥ]]---to the vibration of the flute.
translation: My dear friend, this newly youthful Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the moon in the family of Nanda Mahārāja, is so beautiful that He defies the beauty of clusters of valuable jewels. All glories to the vibration of His flute, for it is cunningly breaking the patience of chaste ladies by loosening their belts and tight dresses.'
purport: This verse from //Lalita-mādhava// (1.49) is spoken by Lalitādevī to Rādhārāṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.169
description: The beauty of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's eyes forcibly devours the beauty of newly grown blue lotus flowers, and the beauty of Her face surpasses that of an entire forest of fully blossomed lotuses. Her bodily luster seems to place even gold in a painful situation. Thus the wonderful, unprecedented beauty of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is awakening in Vṛndāvana.'
text:
> balād akṣṇor lakṣmīḥ kavalayati navyaṁ kuvalayaṁ
> mukhollāsaḥ phullaṁ kamala-vanam ullaṅghayati ca
> daśāṁ kaṣṭām aṣṭā-padam api nayaty āṅgika-rucir
> vicitraṁ rādhāyāḥ kim api kila rūpaṁ vilasati
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:balāt]]---by force; [[synonyms:a:akṣṇoḥ]]---of the two eyes; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmīḥ]]---the beauty; [[synonyms:k:kavalayati]]---devours; [[synonyms:n:navyam]]---newly awakened; [[synonyms:k:kuvalayam]]---lotus flower; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]-[[synonyms:u:ullāsaḥ]]---the beauty of the face; [[synonyms:p:phullam]]---fructified; [[synonyms:k:kamala]]-[[synonyms:v:vanam]]---a forest of lotus flowers; [[synonyms:u:ullaṅghayati]]---surpasses; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:d:daśām]]---to a situation; [[synonyms:k:kaṣṭām]]---painful; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭā]]-[[synonyms:p:padam]]---gold; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:n:nayati]]---brings; [[synonyms:ā:āṅgika]]-[[synonyms:r:ruciḥ]]---the luster of the body; [[synonyms:v:vicitram]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:r:rādhāyāḥ]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:k:kim]] [[synonyms:a:api]]---some; [[synonyms:k:kila]]---certainly; [[synonyms:r:rūpam]]---the beauty; [[synonyms:v:vilasati]]---manifests.
translation: The beauty of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's eyes forcibly devours the beauty of newly grown blue lotus flowers, and the beauty of Her face surpasses that of an entire forest of fully blossomed lotuses. Her bodily luster seems to place even gold in a painful situation. Thus the wonderful, unprecedented beauty of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is awakening in Vṛndāvana.'
purport: This verse is from //Vidagdha-mādhava// (1.32). It is spoken by Paurṇamāsī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.17
description: While going to Jagannātha Purī, Śivānanda Sena allowed a dog to go with him. He supplied it food to eat and maintained it.
text:
> eka kukkura cale śivānanda-sane
> bhakṣya diyā lañā cale kariyā pālane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:k:kukkura]]---dog; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---goes; [[synonyms:ś:śivānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:b:bhakṣya]]---food; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:c:cale]]---goes; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:p:pālane]]---maintaining the dog.
translation: While going to Jagannātha Purī, Śivānanda Sena allowed a dog to go with him. He supplied it food to eat and maintained it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.170
description: Although the effulgence of the moon is brilliant initially at night, in the daytime it fades away. Similarly, although the lotus is beautiful during the daytime, at night it closes. But, O My friend, the face of My most dear Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is always bright and beautiful, both day and night. Therefore, to what can Her face be compared?'
text:
> vidhur eti divā virūpatāṁ
> śata-patraṁ bata śarvarī-mukhe
> iti kena sadā śriyojjvalaṁ
> tulanām arhati mat-priyānanam
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vidhuḥ]]---the moon; [[synonyms:e:eti]]---becomes; [[synonyms:d:divā]]---by daytime; [[synonyms:v:virūpatām]]---faded away; [[synonyms:ś:śata]]-[[synonyms:p:patram]]---he lotus flower; [[synonyms:b:bata]]---alas; [[synonyms:ś:śarvarī]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---in the beginning of evening; [[synonyms:i:iti]]---thus; [[synonyms:k:kena]]---with what; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:ś:śriyā]]-[[synonyms:u:ujjvalam]]---brilliant with beauty; [[synonyms:t:tulanām]]---comparison; [[synonyms:a:arhati]]---deserves; [[synonyms:m:mat]]---of Me; [[synonyms:p:priyā]]---of the dear one; [[synonyms:ā:ānanam]]---the face.
translation: Although the effulgence of the moon is brilliant initially at night, in the daytime it fades away. Similarly, although the lotus is beautiful during the daytime, at night it closes. But, O My friend, the face of My most dear Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is always bright and beautiful, both day and night. Therefore, to what can Her face be compared?'
purport: This verse (//Vidagdha-mādhava// 5.20) is spoken by Śrī Kṛṣṇa to Madhumaṅgala.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.171
description: When Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī smiles, waves of joy overtake Her cheeks, and Her arched eyebrows dance like the bow of Cupid. Her glance is so enchanting that it is like a dancing bumblebee, moving unsteadily due to intoxication. That bee has bitten the whorl of My heart.' "
text:
> pramada-rasa-taraṅga-smera-gaṇḍa-sthalāyāḥ
> smara-dhanur anubandhi-bhrū-latā-lāsya-bhājaḥ
> mada-kala-cala-bhṛṅgī-bhrānti-bhaṅgīṁ dadhāno
> hṛdayam idam adāṅkṣīt pakṣmalākṣyāḥ kaṭākṣaḥ
