title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.185
description: "This introduction is technically called udghātyaka, and the whole scene is called vīthī. You are so expert in dramatic expression that each of my statements before you is like a wave from an ocean of impudence.
text:
> 'udghātyaka' nāma ei 'āmukha'---'vīthī' aṅga
> tomāra āge kahi---ihā dhārṣṭyera taraṅga
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:'udghātyaka']] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---a dancing appearance of the player, technically known //as udghātyaka//; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ā:āmukha]]---this is the introduction; [[synonyms:v:vīthī]] [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the part is called //vīthī//; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---before you; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I say; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:d:dhārṣṭyera]] [[synonyms:t:taraṅga]]---a wave of impudence.
translation: "This introduction is technically called udghātyaka, and the whole scene is called vīthī. You are so expert in dramatic expression that each of my statements before you is like a wave from an ocean of impudence.
purport:
In this connection Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura again quotes the following verse from the //Sāhitya-darpaṇa// (6.288):

> udghātyakaḥ kathodghātaḥ
> prayogātiśayas tathā
> pravartakāvalagite
> pañca prastāvanā-bhidāḥ

Thus the technical names for the five kinds of introductory scenes of the drama are listed as //udghātyaka, kathodghāta, prayogātiśaya, pravartaka// and //avalagita.// When Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya inquired which of these five Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī had used to accomplish the technical introduction to his drama //Lalita-mādhava,// Rūpa Gosvāmī replied that he had used the introduction technically called //udghātyaka.// According to //Bhāratī-vṛtti,// three technical terms used are //prarocanā, vīthī// and //prahasanā.// Thus Rūpa Gosvāmī also mentioned //vīthī,// which is a technical term for a certain type of expression. According to the //Sāhitya-darpaṇa// (6.520):

> vīthyām eko bhaved aṅkaḥ
> kaścid eko 'tra kalpyate
> ākāśa-bhāṣitair uktaiś
> citrāṁ pratyuktim āśritaḥ

The //vīthī// beginning of a drama consists of only one scene. In that scene, one of the heroes enters the stage, and by means of opposing statements uttered by a voice from the sky (offstage), he introduces the abundant conjugal mellow and other mellows to some degree. In the course of the introduction, all the seeds of the play are planted. This introduction is called //udghātyaka// because the player dances on the stage. This term also indicates that the full moon enters the stage. In this case, when the word //naṭatā// ("dancing on the stage") is linked with the moon, its meaning is obscure, but because the meaning becomes very clear when the word //naṭatā// is linked with Kṛṣṇa, this type of introduction is called //udghātyaka.//

Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya used highly technical terms when he discussed this with Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. Rūpa Gosvāmī admitted that Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya was a greatly learned scholar of bona fide dramatic composition. Thus although Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī was quite fit to answer Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya's questions, due to his Vaiṣṇava humility he admitted that his words were impudent. Actually both Rūpa Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya were scholarly experts in composing poetry and presenting it strictly according to the //Sāhitya-darpaṇa// and other Vedic literatures.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.186

> yojayanti padair anyaiḥ
> sa udghātyaka ucyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:padāni]]---words; [[synonyms:t:tu]]---but; [[synonyms:a:agata]]-[[synonyms:a:arthāni]]---having an unclear meaning; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---that,; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:g:gataye]]---to understand the meaning; [[synonyms:n:narāḥ]]---men; [[synonyms:y:yojayanti]]---join; [[synonyms:p:padaiḥ]]---with words; [[synonyms:a:anyaiḥ]]---other; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:u:udghātyakaḥ]]---udghātyaka; [[synonyms:u:ucyate]]---is called.
translation: To explain an unclear word, men generally join it with other words. Such an attempt is called udghātyaka.' "
purport: This verse is quoted from the //Sāhitya-darpaṇa// (6.289).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.187
description: When Rāmānanda Rāya requested Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī to speak further about various portions of the play, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī briefly quoted his Lalita-mādhava.
text:
> rāya kahe,---"kaha āge aṅgera viśeṣa"
> śrī-rūpa kahena kichu saṅkṣepa-uddeśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya says; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please tell me; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---further; [[synonyms:a:aṅgera]] [[synonyms:v:viśeṣa]]---particular portions; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī says; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:s:saṅkṣepa]]---in brief; [[synonyms:u:uddeśa]]---reference.
translation: When Rāmānanda Rāya requested Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī to speak further about various portions of the play, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī briefly quoted his Lalita-mādhava.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.188
description: The dust from cows and calves on the road creates a kind of darkness indicating that Kṛṣṇa is returning home from the pasture. Also, the darkness of evening provokes the gopīs to meet Kṛṣṇa. Thus the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs are covered by a kind of transcendental darkness and are therefore impossible for ordinary scholars of the Vedas to see.'
text:
> harim uddiśate rajo-bharaḥ
> purataḥ saṅgamayaty amuṁ tamaḥ
> vrajavāma-dṛśāṁ na paddhatiḥ
> prakaṭā sarva-dṛśaḥ śruter api
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:harim]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:u:uddiśate]]---it indicates; [[synonyms:r:rajaḥ]]-[[synonyms:b:bharaḥ]]---dust from the cows,; [[synonyms:p:purataḥ]]---in front; [[synonyms:s:saṅgamayati]]---causes to meet; [[synonyms:a:amum]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tamaḥ]]---the darkness; [[synonyms:v:vrajavāma]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛśām]]---of the damsels of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:n:na]]---not; [[synonyms:p:paddhatiḥ]]---the course of activities; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭā]]---manifested; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:d:dṛśaḥ]]---who know everything; [[synonyms:ś:śruteḥ]]---of the //Vedas//; [[synonyms:a:api]]---as well as.
translation: The dust from cows and calves on the road creates a kind of darkness indicating that Kṛṣṇa is returning home from the pasture. Also, the darkness of evening provokes the gopīs to meet Kṛṣṇa. Thus the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs are covered by a kind of transcendental darkness and are therefore impossible for ordinary scholars of the Vedas to see.'
purport:
This verse from the //Lalita-mādhava// (1.23) is spoken by Paurṇamāsī in a conversation with Gārgī.

Kṛṣṇa stated in the //Bhagavad-gītā, traiguṇya-viṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna.// Thus He advised Arjuna to rise above the modes of material nature, for the entire Vedic system is filled with descriptions involving //sattva-guṇa, rajo-guṇa// and //tamo-guṇa.// People are generally covered by the quality of //rajo-guṇa// and are therefore unable to understand the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa with the //gopīs// of Vraja. Moreover, the quality of //tamo-guṇa// further disturbs their understanding. In Vṛndāvana, however, although Kṛṣṇa is covered by the hazy darkness of the dust, the //gopīs// can nevertheless understand that within the dust storm is Kṛṣṇa. Because they are His topmost devotees, they can perceive His hand in everything. Thus even in the dark or in a hazy storm of dust, devotees can understand what Kṛṣṇa is doing. The purport of this verse is that Kṛṣṇa is never lost, under any circumstances, to the vision of exalted devotees like the //gopīs.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.189
description: May the sweet sound of Lord Kṛṣṇa's flute, His authorized messenger, be glorified, for it expertly releases Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī from Her shyness and attracts Her from Her home to the forest.'
text:
> hriyam avagṛhya gṛhebhyaḥ karṣati
> rādhāṁ vanāya yā nipuṇā
> sā jayati nisṛṣṭārthā
> vara-vaṁśaja-kākalī dūtī
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hriyam]]---bashfulness; [[synonyms:a:avagṛhya]]---impeding; [[synonyms:g:gṛhebhyaḥ]]---from private houses; [[synonyms:k:karṣati]]---attracts; [[synonyms:r:rādhām]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:v:vanāya]]---to the forest; [[synonyms:y:yā]]---which; [[synonyms:n:nipuṇā]]---being expert; [[synonyms:s:sā]]---that; [[synonyms:j:jayati]]---let it be glorified; [[synonyms:n:nisṛṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:a:arthā]]---authorized; [[synonyms:v:vara]]-[[synonyms:v:vaṁśaja]]---of the bamboo flute; [[synonyms:k:kākalī]]---the sweet tone; [[synonyms:d:dūtī]]---the messenger.
translation: May the sweet sound of Lord Kṛṣṇa's flute, His authorized messenger, be glorified, for it expertly releases Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī from Her shyness and attracts Her from Her home to the forest.'
purport: This verse from //Lalita-mādhava// (1.24) is spoken by Gārgī, the daughter of Gargamuni.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.19
description: Śivānanda Sena, unhappy that the dog had to stay behind, paid the boatman ten paṇa of conchshells to take the dog across the river.
text:
> kukkura rahilā,---śivānanda duḥkhī hailā
> daśa paṇa kaḍi diyā kukkure pāra kailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kukkura]] [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---the dog remained; [[synonyms:ś:śivānanda]] [[synonyms:d:duḥkhī]] [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---Śivānanda became very unhappy; [[synonyms:d:daśa]] [[synonyms:p:paṇa]]---ten //paṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kaḍi]]---small conchshells; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---paying; [[synonyms:k:kukkure]]---the dog; [[synonyms:p:pāra]] [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---crossed to the other side of the river.
translation: Śivānanda Sena, unhappy that the dog had to stay behind, paid the boatman ten paṇa of conchshells to take the dog across the river.
purport: One //paṇa// is eighty //kaḍis,// or small conchshells. Formerly, even fifty or sixty years ago, there was no paper currency in India. Coins were generally made not of base metal but of gold, silver and copper. In other words, the medium of exchange was really something valuable. Four pieces of //kaḍi// made one //gaṇḍā,// and twenty such //gaṇḍās// equaled one //paṇa.// This //kaḍi// was also used as a medium of exchange; therefore Śivānanda Sena paid for the dog with //daśa paṇa,// or eighty times ten pieces of //kaḍi.// In those days one paisa was also subdivided into small conchshells, but at the present moment the prices for commodities have gone so high that there is nothing one can get in exchange for only one paisa. With one paisa in those days, however, one could purchase sufficient vegetables to provide for a whole family. Even thirty years ago, vegetables were occasionally so inexpensive that one paisa's worth could provide for a whole family for a day.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.190
description: My dear friend, who is this fearless young man? He is as bright as a lightning cloud, and He wanders in His pastimes like a maddened elephant. From where has He come to Vṛndāvana? Alas, by His restless movements and attractive glances He is plundering from the vault of My heart the treasure of My patience.'
text:
> sahacari nirātaṅkaḥ ko 'yaṁ yuvā mudira-dyutir
> vraja-bhuvi kutaḥ prāpto mādyan mataṅgaja-vibhramaḥ
> ahaha caṭulair utsarpadbhir dṛg-añcala-taskarair
> mama dhṛti-dhanaṁ cetaḥ-koṣād viluṇṭhayatīha yaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saha]]-[[synonyms:c:cari]]---O My dear friend; [[synonyms:n:nirātaṅkaḥ]]---without fear; [[synonyms:k:kaḥ]]---who; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:y:yuvā]]---young man; [[synonyms:m:mudira]]-[[synonyms:d:dyutiḥ]]---as effulgent as a lightning cloud; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvi]]---in the land of Vraja, Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:k:kutaḥ]]---from where; [[synonyms:p:prāptaḥ]]---obtained; [[synonyms:m:mādyan]]---being intoxicated; [[synonyms:m:mataṅgaja]]---like an elephant; [[synonyms:v:vibhramaḥ]]---whose pastimes; [[synonyms:a:ahaha]]---alas; [[synonyms:c:caṭulaiḥ]]---very unsteady; [[synonyms:u:utsarpadbhiḥ]]---with wanderings in all directions; [[synonyms:d:dṛk]]-[[synonyms:a:añcala]]-[[synonyms:t:taskaraiḥ]]---by the glances of His eyes like thieves; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---My; [[synonyms:d:dhṛti]]-[[synonyms:d:dhanam]]---the treasure of My patience; [[synonyms:c:cetaḥ]]---of the heart; [[synonyms:k:koṣāt]]---from the core; [[synonyms:v:viluṇṭhayati]]---plunders; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---here in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---he person who.
translation: My dear friend, who is this fearless young man? He is as bright as a lightning cloud, and He wanders in His pastimes like a maddened elephant. From where has He come to Vṛndāvana? Alas, by His restless movements and attractive glances He is plundering from the vault of My heart the treasure of My patience.'
purport: This verse (//Lalita-mādhava// 2.11) is spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī to Her friend Lalitādevī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.191
description: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is the Ganges in which the elephant of My mind enjoys pastimes. She is the shining of the full autumn moon for the cakora birds of My eyes. She is the dazzling ornament, the bright and beautiful arrangement of stars, on the border of the sky of My chest. Now today I have gained Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī because of the highly elevated state of My mind.' "
text:
> vihāra-sura-dīrghikā mama manaḥ-karīndrasya yā
> vilocana-cakorayoḥ śarad-amanda-candra-prabhā
> uro 'mbara-taṭasya cābharaṇa-cāru-tārāvalī
> mayonnata-manorathair iyam alambhi sā rādhikā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vihāra]]-[[synonyms:s:sura]]-[[synonyms:d:dīrghikā]]---the Ganges flowing in the heavenly planets; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---My; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kari]]-[[synonyms:i:indrasya]]---of the elephant-like mind; [[synonyms:y:yā]]---She who; [[synonyms:v:vilocana]]---glancing; [[synonyms:c:cakorayoḥ]]---of My two eyes, which are like //cakora// birds; [[synonyms:ś:śarat]]-[[synonyms:a:amanda]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhā]]---like the shine of the full moon in the autumn; [[synonyms:u:uraḥ]]---of My chest; [[synonyms:a:ambara]]---like the sky; [[synonyms:t:taṭasya]]---on the edge; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also; [[synonyms:ā:ābharaṇa]]---ornaments; [[synonyms:c:cāru]]---beautiful; [[synonyms:t:tārā]]-[[synonyms:ā:āvalī]]---like the stars; [[synonyms:m:mayā]]---by Me; [[synonyms:u:unnata]]---highly elevated; [[synonyms:m:manorathaiḥ]]---by mental desires; [[synonyms:i:iyam]]---this; [[synonyms:a:alambhi]]---attained; [[synonyms:s:sā]]---She; [[synonyms:r:rādhikā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
translation: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is the Ganges in which the elephant of My mind enjoys pastimes. She is the shining of the full autumn moon for the cakora birds of My eyes. She is the dazzling ornament, the bright and beautiful arrangement of stars, on the border of the sky of My chest. Now today I have gained Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī because of the highly elevated state of My mind.' "
purport: This verse from //Lalita-mādhava// (2.10) expresses the thoughts of Lord Kṛṣṇa in relation with Rādhārāṇī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.192
description: After hearing this, Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya submitted at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu the superexcellence of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's poetic expression and began to praise it as if he had thousands of mouths.
text:
> eta śuni' rāya kahe prabhura caraṇe
> rūpera kavitva praśaṁsi' sahasra-vadane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:rūpera]]---of Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:k:kavitva]]---poetic art; [[synonyms:p:praśaṁsi']]---glorifying; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]-[[synonyms:v:vadane]]---as if with a thousand mouths.
translation: After hearing this, Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya submitted at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu the superexcellence of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's poetic expression and began to praise it as if he had thousands of mouths.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.193
description: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya said, "This is not a poetic presentation; it is a continuous shower of nectar. Indeed, it is the essence of all ultimate realizations, appearing in the form of plays.
text:
> "kavitva nā haya ei amṛtera dhāra
> nāṭaka-lakṣaṇa saba siddhāntera sāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kavitva]]---poetic art; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is not; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:a:amṛtera]] [[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---constant shower of nectar; [[synonyms:n:nāṭaka]]---a drama; [[synonyms:l:lakṣaṇa]]---appearing as; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:s:siddhāntera]] [[synonyms:s:sāra]]---essences of ultimate realization.
translation: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya said, "This is not a poetic presentation; it is a continuous shower of nectar. Indeed, it is the essence of all ultimate realizations, appearing in the form of plays.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.194
description: The wonderful descriptions of Rūpa Gosvāmī are superb arrangements to express loving affairs. Hearing them will plunge the heart and ears of everyone into a whirlpool of transcendental bliss.
text:
> prema-paripāṭī ei adbhuta varṇana
> śuni' citta-karṇera haya ānanda-ghūrṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:p:paripāṭī]]---a first-class arrangement to express loving affairs; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---wonderful description; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:c:citta]]-[[synonyms:k:karṇera]]---of the heart and the ear; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:g:ghūrṇana]]---a whirlpool of transcendental bliss.
translation: The wonderful descriptions of Rūpa Gosvāmī are superb arrangements to express loving affairs. Hearing them will plunge the heart and ears of everyone into a whirlpool of transcendental bliss.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.195
description: What is the use of a bowman's arrow or a poet's poetry if they penetrate the heart but do not cause the head to spin?'
text:
> kiṁ kāvyena kaves tasya
> kiṁ kāṇḍena dhanuṣ-mataḥ
> parasya hṛdaye lagnaṁ
> na ghūrṇayati yac chiraḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what use; [[synonyms:k:kāvyena]]---with poetry; [[synonyms:k:kaveḥ]]---of the poet; [[synonyms:t:tasya]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what use; [[synonyms:k:kāṇḍena]]---with the arrow; [[synonyms:d:dhanuḥ]]-[[synonyms:m:mataḥ]]---of the bowman; [[synonyms:p:parasya]]---of another; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---in the heart; [[synonyms:l:lagnam]]---penetrating; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:g:ghūrṇayati]]---does not cause to roll about; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---which; [[synonyms:ś:śiraḥ]]---the head.
translation: What is the use of a bowman's arrow or a poet's poetry if they penetrate the heart but do not cause the head to spin?'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.196
description: Without Your mercy such poetic expressions would be impossible for an ordinary living being to write. My guess is that You have given him the power."
text:
> tomāra śakti vinā jīvera nahe ei vāṇī
> tumi śakti diyā kahāo,---hena anumāni"
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śakti]] [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without Your special power; [[synonyms:j:jīvera]]---of an ordinary living being; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---there is not; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---these words; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving power; [[synonyms:k:kahāo]]---make him say; [[synonyms:h:hena]]---such; [[synonyms:a:anumāni]]---I guess.
translation: Without Your mercy such poetic expressions would be impossible for an ordinary living being to write. My guess is that You have given him the power."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.197
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "I met Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī at Prayāga. He attracted and satisfied Me because of his qualities."
text:
> prabhu kahe,---"prayāge ihāra ha-ila milana
> ihāra guṇe ihāte āmāra tuṣṭa haila mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu says; [[synonyms:p:pra]] [[synonyms:y:yāge]]---at Prayāga; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of him; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]] [[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---by his transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:i:ihāte]]---in him; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---of Me; [[synonyms:t:tuṣṭa]]---satisfied; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "I met Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī at Prayāga. He attracted and satisfied Me because of his qualities."
purport:
The Supreme personality of Godhead is not partial to some and neutral to others. One can actually draw the attention of the Supreme Personality of Godhead by service. Then one is further empowered by the Lord to act in such a way that everyone can appreciate his service. This is confirmed in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:4:11|(Bg. 4.11)]]: //ye yathā māṁ prapadyante tāṁs tathaiva bhajāmy aham.// Kṛṣṇa is responsive. If one tries to render his best service to the Lord, the Lord gives him the power to do so. Kṛṣṇa also says in the //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:10:10|(Bg. 10.10)]]:

> teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ
> bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam
> dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ
> yena mām upayānti te

"To those who are constantly devoted and worship Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me." Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His special favor upon Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī because Rūpa Gosvāmī wanted to serve the Lord to the best of his ability. Such is the reciprocation between the devotee and the Lord in the discharge of devotional duties.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.198
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu praised the metaphors and other literary ornaments of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's transcendental poetry. Without such poetic attributes, He said, there is no possibility of preaching transcendental mellows.
text:
> madhura prasanna ihāra kāvya sālaṅkāra
> aiche kavitva vinu nahe rasera pracāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweet; [[synonyms:p:prasanna]]---pleasing; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---his; [[synonyms:k:kāvya]]---poetry; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:a:alaṅkāra]]---with metaphors and other ornaments; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such as that; [[synonyms:k:kavitva]]---poetic qualifications; [[synonyms:v:vinu]]---without; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---there is not; [[synonyms:r:rasera]]---of mellows; [[synonyms:p:pracāra]]---preaching.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu praised the metaphors and other literary ornaments of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's transcendental poetry. Without such poetic attributes, He said, there is no possibility of preaching transcendental mellows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.199
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested all His personal associates to bless Rūpa Gosvāmī so that he might continuously describe the pastimes of Vṛndāvana, which are full of emotional love of Godhead.
text:
> sabe kṛpā kari' iṅhāre deha' ei vara
> vraja-līlā-prema-rasa yena varṇe nirantara
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of you; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing your mercy; [[synonyms:i:iṅhāre]]---unto Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:d:deha']]---give; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:v:vara]]---this benediction; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---transcendental mellows of the pastimes of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---so that; [[synonyms:v:varṇe]]---he can describe; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---without cessation.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested all His personal associates to bless Rūpa Gosvāmī so that he might continuously describe the pastimes of Vṛndāvana, which are full of emotional love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.2
description: My path is very difficult. I am blind, and my feet are slipping again and again. Therefore, may the saints help me by granting me the stick of their mercy as my support.
text:
> durgame pathi me 'ndhasya
> skhalat-pāda-gater muhuḥ
> sva-kṛpā-yaṣṭi-dānena
> santaḥ santv avalambanam
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:durgame]]---very difficult; [[synonyms:p:pathi]]---on the path; [[synonyms:m:me]]---of me; [[synonyms:a:andhasya]]---one who is blind; [[synonyms:s:skhalat]]---slipping; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]---on feet; [[synonyms:g:gateḥ]]---whose manner of moving; [[synonyms:m:muhuḥ]]---again and again; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---of their own mercy; [[synonyms:y:yaṣṭi]]---the stick; [[synonyms:d:dānena]]---by giving; [[synonyms:s:santaḥ]]---those saintly persons; [[synonyms:s:santu]]---let that become; [[synonyms:a:avalambanam]]---my support.
translation: My path is very difficult. I am blind, and my feet are slipping again and again. Therefore, may the saints help me by granting me the stick of their mercy as my support.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.20
description: One day while Śivānanda was detained by a tollman, his servant forgot to give the dog its cooked rice.

> kukkurake bhāta dite sevaka pāsarilā

translation: One day while Śivānanda was detained by a tollman, his servant forgot to give the dog its cooked rice.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.200
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's elder brother, whose name is Sanātana Gosvāmī, is such a wise and learned scholar that no one is equal to him."
text:
> iṅhāra ye jyeṣṭha-bhrātā, nāma---'sanātana'
> pṛthivīte vijña-vara nāhi tāṅra sama
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṅhāra]]---of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---who; [[synonyms:j:jyeṣṭha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhrātā]]---the elder brother; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pṛthivīte]]---on the surface of the world; [[synonyms:v:vijña]]-[[synonyms:v:vara]]---most learned; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is none; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:sama]]---equal to him.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's elder brother, whose name is Sanātana Gosvāmī, is such a wise and learned scholar that no one is equal to him."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.201
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told Rāmānanda Rāya, "Sanātana Gosvāmī's renunciation of material connections is just like yours. Humility, renunciation and excellent learning exist in him simultaneously.
text:
> tomāra yaiche viṣaya-tyāga, taiche tāṅra rīti
> dainya-vairāgya-pāṇḍityera tāṅhātei sthiti
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just as; [[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]-[[synonyms:t:tyāga]]---renunciation of material connections; [[synonyms:t:taiche]]---similarly; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:r:rīti]]---his manner of activity; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]---humbleness; [[synonyms:v:vairāgya]]---renunciation; [[synonyms:p:pāṇḍityera]]---of learned scholarship; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhātei]]---in him; [[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---existing.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told Rāmānanda Rāya, "Sanātana Gosvāmī's renunciation of material connections is just like yours. Humility, renunciation and excellent learning exist in him simultaneously.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.202
description: I empowered both of these brothers to go to Vṛndāvana to expand the literature of bhakti."
text:
> ei dui bhāiye āmi pāṭhāiluṅ vṛndāvane
> śakti diyā bhakti-śāstra karite pravartane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:b:bhāiye]]---brothers; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāiluṅ]]---sent; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvane]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---empowering them; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]---transcendental literature regarding devotional service; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to do; [[synonyms:p:pravartane]]---establishing.
translation: I empowered both of these brothers to go to Vṛndāvana to expand the literature of bhakti."
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu informed Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya that he and Sanātana Gosvāmī had engaged equally in devotional service after giving up all relationships with material activity. Such renunciation is a symptom of an unalloyed devotee engaged in the service of the Lord with no tinge of material contamination. According to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, this is the position of //tṛṇād api sunīcena taror api sahiṣṇunā.// A pure devotee, free from the reactions of the material modes of nature, executes devotional service with tolerance like that of a tree. He also feels humbler than the grass. Such a devotee, who is called //niṣkiñcana// or free from all material possessions, is always absorbed in emotional love of Godhead. He is reluctant to perform any kind of sense gratification. In other words, such a devotee is free from all material bondage, but he engages in Kṛṣṇa conscious activities. Such expert devotional service is performed without hypocrisy. Humility, renunciation and learned scholarship were combined in Sanātana Gosvāmī, the ideal pure devotee, who was on the same level of understanding as Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya. Like Rāmānanda Rāya, Sanātana Gosvāmī was a fully cognizant expert in the conclusions of devotional service and was therefore able to describe such transcendental knowledge.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.203
description: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya replied to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "My Lord, You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead. If You like, You can cause even a wooden doll to dance.

> rāya kahe,---"īśvara tumi ye cāha karite

translation: Śrīla Rāmānanda Rāya replied to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "My Lord, You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead. If You like, You can cause even a wooden doll to dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.204
description: "I see that the truths regarding transcendental mellow that You have expounded through my mouth are all explained in the writings of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.
text:
> mora mukhe ye saba rasa karilā pracāraṇe
> sei rasa dekhi ei ihāra likhane
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---through my mouth; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---all such transcendental mellows; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---You did; [[synonyms:p:pracāraṇe]]---preaching; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---those same transcendental mellows; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---I see; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]] [[synonyms:l:likhane]]---in the writing of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.
translation: "I see that the truths regarding transcendental mellow that You have expounded through my mouth are all explained in the writings of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.205
description: "Because of Your causeless mercy toward Your devotees, You want to describe the transcendental pastimes in Vṛndāvana. Anyone empowered to do this can bring the entire world under Your influence."
text:
> bhakte kṛpā-hetu prakāśite cāha vraja-rasa
> yāre karāo, sei karibe jagat tomāra vaśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---unto the devotees; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:h:hetu]]---because of mercy; [[synonyms:p:prakāśite]]---to show; [[synonyms:c:cāha]]---You want; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---the transcendental mellows in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:y:yāre]]---whomever; [[synonyms:k:karāo]]---You may empower; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---he; [[synonyms:k:karibe]]---will make; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the whole world; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---under Your control.
translation: "Because of Your causeless mercy toward Your devotees, You want to describe the transcendental pastimes in Vṛndāvana. Anyone empowered to do this can bring the entire world under Your influence."
purport: This passage parallels the statement k//ṛṣṇa-śakti vinā nahe tāra pravartana,// which means that unless empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, one cannot spread the holy name of the Lord throughout the entire world [[books:cc:antya:7:11|(Cc. Antya 7.11)]]. Under the protection of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, a pure devotee can preach the holy name of the Lord so that everyone may take advantage of this facility and thus become Kṛṣṇa conscious.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.206
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then embraced Rūpa Gosvāmī and asked him to offer prayers at the lotus feet of all the devotees present.

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then embraced Rūpa Gosvāmī and asked him to offer prayers at the lotus feet of all the devotees present.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.208

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.211
description: Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī said, "I do not know anything. The only transcendental words I can utter are those which Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu makes me speak.
text:
> śrī-rūpa kahena,---āmi kichui nā jāni
> yei mahāprabhu kahāna, sei kahi vāṇī
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī replies; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kichui]]---anything; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:j:jani]]---do not know; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahāna]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu makes me say or write; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---hat; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I speak; [[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---transcendental words.
translation: Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī said, "I do not know anything. The only transcendental words I can utter are those which Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu makes me speak.
purport:
The poet or writer dealing with transcendental subject matters is not an ordinary writer or translator. Because he is empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whatever he writes becomes very effective. The principle of being empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead is essential. A materialistic poet who describes in his poetry the material activities of man and woman cannot describe the transcendental pastimes of the Lord or the transcendental conclusions of devotional service. Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī has therefore warned all neophyte devotees that one should not hear from the mouth of a non-Vaiṣṇava.

> avaiṣṇava-mukhodgīrṇaṁ
> pūtaṁ hari-kathāmṛtam
> śravaṇaṁ naiva kartavyaṁ
> sarpocchiṣṭaṁ yathā payaḥ

(//Padma Purāṇa//)

Unless one is a fully unalloyed devotee of the Lord, one should not try to describe the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa in poetry, for it will be only mundane. There are many descriptions of Kṛṣṇa's //Bhagavad-gītā// written by persons whose consciousness is mundane and who are not qualified by pure devotion. Although they attempted to write transcendental literature, they could not fully engage even a single devotee in Kṛṣṇa's service. Such literature is mundane, and therefore, as warned by Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, one should not touch it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.212
description: 'Although I am the lowest of men and have no knowledge, the Lord has mercifully bestowed upon me the inspiration to write transcendental literature about devotional service. Therefore I offer my obeisances at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has given me the chance to write these books.' "
text:
> hṛdi yasya preraṇayā
> pravartito 'haṁ varāka-rūpo 'pi
> tasya hareḥ pada-kamalaṁ
> vande caitanya-devasya
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hṛdi]]---within the heart; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom (the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who gives His pure devotees the intelligence to spread the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement); [[synonyms:p:preraṇayā]]---by the inspiration; [[synonyms:p:pravartitaḥ]]---engaged; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:v:varāka]]---insignificant and low; [[synonyms:r:rūpaḥ]]---Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:a:api]]---although; [[synonyms:t:tasya]]---of Him; [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]]---of Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:k:kamalam]]---to the lotus feet; [[synonyms:v:vande]]---let me offer my prayers; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:d:devasya]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: 'Although I am the lowest of men and have no knowledge, the Lord has mercifully bestowed upon me the inspiration to write transcendental literature about devotional service. Therefore I offer my obeisances at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has given me the chance to write these books.' "
purport: This verse is from //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.1.2).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.213
description: In this way Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī passed his time in close association with Haridāsa Ṭhākura by discussing the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa in great happiness.
text:
> ei-mata dui-jana kṛṣṇa-kathā-raṅge
> sukhe kāla goṅāya rūpa haridāsa-saṅge

translation: In this way Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī passed his time in close association with Haridāsa Ṭhākura by discussing the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa in great happiness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.214
description: All the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus spent four months with Him. Then the Lord bade them farewell, and they returned to Bengal.
text:
> cāri māsa rahi' saba prabhura bhakta-gaṇa
> gosāñi vidāya dilā, gauḍe karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cāri]] [[synonyms:m:māsa]]---four months; [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---staying; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vidāyadilā]]---bade farewell; [[synonyms:g:gauḍe]]---to Bengal; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---they returned.
translation: All the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus spent four months with Him. Then the Lord bade them farewell, and they returned to Bengal.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.215
description: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, however, stayed at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and when the Dola-yātrā festival took place, he saw it in great happiness with the Lord.
text:
> śrī-rūpa prabhu-pade nīlācale rahilā
> dola-yātrā prabhu-saṅge ānande dekhilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---at Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:d:dola]]-[[synonyms:y:yātrā]]---the festival of Dola-yātrā; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ānande]]---in great happiness; [[synonyms:d:dekhilā]]---saw.
translation: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, however, stayed at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and when the Dola-yātrā festival took place, he saw it in great happiness with the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.216
description: After the Dola-yātrā festival ended, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade farewell to Rūpa Gosvāmī also. The Lord empowered him and bestowed upon him all kinds of mercy.

translation: After the Dola-yātrā festival ended, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade farewell to Rūpa Gosvāmī also. The Lord empowered him and bestowed upon him all kinds of mercy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.217

translation: "Establish the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa and preach the mellows of Lord Kṛṣṇa's devotional service. I shall also go to Vṛndāvana once more."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.223
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.

Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.23
description: When the men returned without success, Śivānanda Sena became very unhappy and fasted for the night.
text:
> cāhiyā nā pāila kukkura, loka saba āilā
> duḥkhī hañā śivānanda upavāsa kailā

translation: When the men returned without success, Śivānanda Sena became very unhappy and fasted for the night.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.24
description: In the morning they looked for the dog, but it could not be found anywhere. All the Vaiṣṇavas were astonished.
text:
> prabhāte kukkura cāhi' kāṅhā nā pāila
> sakala vaiṣṇavera mane camatkāra haila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhāte]]---in the morning; [[synonyms:k:kukkura]]---the dog; [[synonyms:c:cāhi']]---looking for; [[synonyms:k:kāṅhā]]---anywhere; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---not found; [[synonyms:s:sakala]] [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]]---of all the Vaiṣṇavas present; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the minds; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was great astonishment.
translation: In the morning they looked for the dog, but it could not be found anywhere. All the Vaiṣṇavas were astonished.
purport:
Śivānanda Sena's attachment to the dog was a great boon for that animal. The dog appears to have been a street dog. Since it naturally began to follow Śivānanda Sena while he was going to Jagannātha Purī with his party, he accepted it into his party and maintained it the same way he was maintaining the other devotees. It appears that although on one occasion the dog was not allowed aboard a boat, Śivānanda did not leave the dog behind but paid more money just to induce the boatman to take the dog across the river. Then when the servant forgot to feed the dog and the dog disappeared, Śivānanda, being very anxious, sent ten men to find it. When they could not find it, Śivānanda observed a fast. Thus it appears that somehow or other Śivānanda had become attached to the dog.

As will be evident from the following verses, the dog got the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and was immediately promoted to Vaikuṇṭha to become an eternal devotee. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has therefore sung, //tumi ta' ṭhākura, tomāra kukkura, baliyā jānaha more// (//Śaraṇāgati// 19). He thus offers to become the dog of a Vaiṣṇava. There are many other instances in which the pet animal of a Vaiṣṇava was delivered back home to Vaikuṇṭhaloka, back to Godhead. Such is the benefit of somehow or other becoming the favorite of a Vaiṣṇava. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has also sung, //kīṭa-janma ha-u yathā tuyā dāsa// (//Śaraṇāgati// 11). There is no harm in taking birth again and again. Our only desire should be to take birth under the care of a Vaiṣṇava. Fortunately we had the opportunity to be born of a Vaiṣṇava father who took care of us very nicely. He prayed to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī that in the future we would become a servant of the eternal consort of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Thus somehow or other we are now engaged in that service. We may conclude that even as dogs we must take shelter of a Vaiṣṇava. The benefit will be the same as that which accrues to an advanced devotee under a Vaiṣṇava's care.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.25

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went with them to see the Lord in the temple, and on that day He also took lunch in the company of all those devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.3-4
description: I pray to the lotus feet of the six Gosvāmīs-Śrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Bhaṭṭa Raghunātha, Śrī Jīva, Gopāla Bhaṭṭa and Dāsa Raghunātha-so that all impediments to my writing this literature will be annihilated and my real desire will be fulfilled.
text:
> śrī-rūpa, sanātana bhaṭṭa-raghunātha
> śrī-jīva, gopāla-bhaṭṭa, dāsa-raghunātha
>
> ei chaya gurura karoṅ caraṇa vandana
> yāhā haite vighna-nāśa, abhīṣṭa-pūraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---of the name Śrī Rūpa; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---of the name Sanātana; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]-[[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---of the name Bhaṭṭa Raghunātha; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:j:jīva]]---of the name Śrī Jīva; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---of the name Gopāla Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---of the name Dāsa Raghunātha; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these six; [[synonyms:g:gurura]]---of spiritual masters; [[synonyms:k:karoṅ]]---I offer; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---prayers to the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]]---from which; [[synonyms:v:vighna]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---destruction of all impediments; [[synonyms:a:abhīṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:p:pūraṇa]]---fulfillment of desires.
translation: I pray to the lotus feet of the six Gosvāmīs-Śrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Bhaṭṭa Raghunātha, Śrī Jīva, Gopāla Bhaṭṭa and Dāsa Raghunātha-so that all impediments to my writing this literature will be annihilated and my real desire will be fulfilled.
purport: If one wants to benefit the entire world, he will certainly find persons like hogs and pigs who will put forward many impediments. That is natural. But if a devotee seeks shelter at the lotus feet of the six Gosvāmīs, the merciful Gosvāmīs will certainly give the Lord's servitor all protection. It is not astonishing that impediments are placed before those who are spreading the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement all over the world. Nevertheless, if we adhere to the lotus feet of the six Gosvāmīs and pray for their mercy, all impediments will be annihilated, and the transcendental devotional desire to serve the Supreme Lord will be fulfilled.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 1.30
description: Seeing the dog eating the green coconut pulp and chanting "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa" again and again, all the devotees present were very much surprised.
text:
