synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---the personal servant of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āste]]-[[synonyms:v:vyaste]]---with great haste; [[synonyms:s:strīke]]---the woman; [[synonyms:v:varjilā]]---got down; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---her; [[synonyms:n:nāmāite]]---to get down; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:govinde]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:n:niṣedhilā]]---forbade.
translation: When he saw this, Caitanya Mahāprabhu's personal secretary, Govinda, hastily got her down from her position. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, however, chastised him for this.
purport: Because Garuḍa is the carrier of Lord Viṣṇu, he is the supreme Vaiṣṇava. Therefore to touch his body with one's feet or to climb the column of Garuḍa is certainly a //vaiṣṇava-aparādha,// an offense to a Vaiṣṇava. The woman was also offensive to Kṛṣṇa by putting her foot on the shoulder of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Seeing all these offenses, Govinda very hastily made her get down.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.26
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said to Govinda, "O ādi-vasyā [uncivilized man], do not forbid this woman to climb the Garuḍa-stambha. Let her see Lord Jagannātha to her satisfaction."
text:
> 'ādi-vasyā' ei strīre nā kara varjana
> karuka yatheṣṭa jagannātha daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:v:vasyā]]---uncivilized; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:strīre]]---woman; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:v:varjana]]---do not forbid; [[synonyms:k:karuka]]---let her do; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]-[[synonyms:i:iṣṭa]]---as desired; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing Lord Jagannātha.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said to Govinda, "O ādi-vasyā [uncivilized man], do not forbid this woman to climb the Garuḍa-stambha. Let her see Lord Jagannātha to her satisfaction."
purport: For an explanation of the word //ādi-vasyā,// refer to //Antya-līlā,// Chapter Ten, verse 116.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.27
description: When the woman came to her senses, however, she quickly climbed back down to the ground and, seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, immediately begged at His lotus feet for forgiveness.
text:
> āste-vyaste sei nārī bhūmete nāmilā
> mahāprabhure dekhi' tāṅra caraṇa vandilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āste]]-[[synonyms:v:vyaste]]---in great haste; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:n:nārī]]---that woman; [[synonyms:b:bhūmete]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:n:nāmilā]]---got down; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhure]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandilā]]---begged pardon at the lotus feet.
translation: When the woman came to her senses, however, she quickly climbed back down to the ground and, seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, immediately begged at His lotus feet for forgiveness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.28
description: Seeing the woman's eagerness, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Lord Jagannātha has not bestowed so much eagerness upon Me.
text:
> tāra ārti dekhi' prabhu kahite lāgilā
> "eta ārti jagannātha more nāhi dilā!
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---her; [[synonyms:ā:ārti]]---eagerness; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to speak; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ā:ārti]]---so much eagerness; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---did not bestow.
translation: Seeing the woman's eagerness, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Lord Jagannātha has not bestowed so much eagerness upon Me.
purport: The woman was so eager to see Lord Jagannātha that she forgot she was offending the feet of a Vaiṣṇava by climbing the column of Garuḍa. She also neglected to consider that by putting her foot on the shoulder of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, she offended the Supreme Personality of Godhead. These are both grievous offenses that displease the Supreme Lord and Vaiṣṇavas. She was so eager to see Lord Jagannātha, however, that she committed all these offenses obliviously. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu praised her eagerness; He regretted that Lord Jagannātha had not bestowed such great eagerness upon Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.29
description: "She has fully absorbed her body, mind and life in Lord Jagannātha. Therefore she was unaware that she was putting her foot on My shoulder.
text:
> jagannāthe āviṣṭa ihāra tanu-mana-prāṇe
> mora skandhe pada diyāche, tāho nāhi jāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannāthe]]---in Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---fully absorbed; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of this woman; [[synonyms:t:tanu]]---body; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:p:prāṇe]]---life; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:s:skandhe]]---upon My shoulder; [[synonyms:p:pada]]---foot; [[synonyms:d:diyāche]]---has put; [[synonyms:t:tāho]]---she; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---did not understand.
translation: "She has fully absorbed her body, mind and life in Lord Jagannātha. Therefore she was unaware that she was putting her foot on My shoulder.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.3
description: All glories to Lord Nityānanda, who is Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's very life. And all glories to Advaita Ācārya, who is extremely dear to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> jaya jaya nityānanda caitanya-jīvana
> jayādvaitācārya jaya gaura-priyatama
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---to Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---the life of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---to Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:p:priya]]-[[synonyms:t:tama]]---very, very dear to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All glories to Lord Nityānanda, who is Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's very life. And all glories to Advaita Ācārya, who is extremely dear to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.30
description: "Alas! How fortunate this woman is! I pray at her feet that she favor Me with her great eagerness to see Lord Jagannātha."
text:
> aho bhāgyavatī ei, vandi ihāra pāya
> ihāra prasāde aiche ārti āmāra vā haya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aho]]---alas; [[synonyms:b:bhāgyavatī]]---very, very fortunate; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---she; [[synonyms:v:vandi]]---let Me offer prayers; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---at her feet; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]] [[synonyms:p:prasāde]]---by her favor; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:ā:ārti]]---eagerness; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:v:vā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---may be Mine.
translation: "Alas! How fortunate this woman is! I pray at her feet that she favor Me with her great eagerness to see Lord Jagannātha."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.31
description: Just previously, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had been seeing Lord Jagannātha as the son of Mahārāja Nanda, Kṛṣṇa, in person.
text:
> pūrve āsi' yabe kailā jagannātha daraśana
> jagannāthe dekhe---sākṣāt vrajendra-nandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrve]]---before this; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---executed; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:j:jagannāthe]] [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]] [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---personally the son of Mahārāja Nanda.
translation: Just previously, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had been seeing Lord Jagannātha as the son of Mahārāja Nanda, Kṛṣṇa, in person.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.32
description: Becoming fully absorbed in that vision, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had assumed the mood of the gopīs, so much so that everywhere He looked He saw Kṛṣṇa standing with His flute to His lips.
text:
> svapnera darśanāveśe tad-rūpa haila mana
> yāhāṅ tāhāṅ dekhe sarvatra muralī-vadana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svapnera]]---of the dream; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---by being fully absorbed in the vision; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---like that; [[synonyms:h:haila]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind became; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---anywhere and everywhere; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:s:sarvatra]]---all around; [[synonyms:m:muralī]]-[[synonyms:v:vadana]]---Kṛṣṇa with His flute to His mouth.
translation: Becoming fully absorbed in that vision, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had assumed the mood of the gopīs, so much so that everywhere He looked He saw Kṛṣṇa standing with His flute to His lips.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.33
description: After seeing the woman, the Lord's external consciousness returned, and He saw the original Deity forms of Lord Jagannātha, Subhadrā and Lord Balarāma.
text:
> ebe yadi strīre dekhi' prabhura bāhya haila
> jagannātha-subhadrā-balarāmera svarūpa dekhila
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---when; [[synonyms:s:strīre]]---the woman; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was external consciousness; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:s:subhadrā]]---His sister, Subhadrā; [[synonyms:b:balarāmera]]---and of His elder brother, Balarāma; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---forms; [[synonyms:d:dekhila]]---saw.
translation: After seeing the woman, the Lord's external consciousness returned, and He saw the original Deity forms of Lord Jagannātha, Subhadrā and Lord Balarāma.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.34
description: When He saw the Deities, Lord Caitanya thought He was seeing Kṛṣṇa in Kurukṣetra. He wondered, "Have I come to Kurukṣetra? Where is Vṛndāvana?"
text:
> kurukṣetre dekhi' kṛṣṇe aiche haila mana
> 'kāhāṅ kurukṣetre āilāṅa, kāhāṅ vṛndāvana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kurukṣetre]]---in Kurukṣetra; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:h:haila]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---became His mind; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:k:kurukṣetre]] [[synonyms:ā:āilāṅa]]---I have come to Kurukṣetra; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---Vṛndāvana.
translation: When He saw the Deities, Lord Caitanya thought He was seeing Kṛṣṇa in Kurukṣetra. He wondered, "Have I come to Kurukṣetra? Where is Vṛndāvana?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.35
description: Lord Caitanya grew very agitated, like a person who has just lost a recently acquired jewel. Then He became very morose and returned home.
text:
> prāpta-ratna hārāñā aiche vyagra ha-ilā
> viṣaṇṇa hañā prabhu nija-vāsā āilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prāpta]]-[[synonyms:r:ratna]]---the achieved jewel; [[synonyms:h:hārāñā]]---having lost; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:v:vyagra]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became very agitated; [[synonyms:v:viṣaṇṇa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being morose; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nija]]---own; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]]---to His residential place; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned.
translation: Lord Caitanya grew very agitated, like a person who has just lost a recently acquired jewel. Then He became very morose and returned home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.36
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat down on the ground and began to mark it with His nails. He was blinded by tears, which flowed from His eyes like the Ganges.
text:
> bhūmira upara vasi' nija-nakhe bhūmi likhe
> aśru-gaṅgā netre vahe, kichui nā dekhe
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhūmira]] [[synonyms:u:upara]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting down; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:n:nakhe]]---with His nails; [[synonyms:b:bhūmi]] [[synonyms:l:likhe]]---marked the ground; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]---a flow of tears like the Ganges; [[synonyms:n:netre]]---in the eyes; [[synonyms:v:vahe]]---flows; [[synonyms:k:kichui]]---anything; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---could not see.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat down on the ground and began to mark it with His nails. He was blinded by tears, which flowed from His eyes like the Ganges.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.37
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I found Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Vṛndāvana, but I have lost Him again. Who has taken My Kṛṣṇa? Where have I come?"
text:
> 'pāiluṅ vṛndāvana-nātha, punaḥ hārāiluṅ
> ke mora nileka kṛṣṇa? kāhāṅ mui āinu'?
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pāiluṅ]]---I got; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:n:nātha]]---the Supreme Lord of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:h:hārāiluṅ]]---I have lost; [[synonyms:k:ke]]---who; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:n:nileka]]---took away; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:m:mui]] [[synonyms:ā:āinu]]---have I come.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I found Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Vṛndāvana, but I have lost Him again. Who has taken My Kṛṣṇa? Where have I come?"
purport:
These are the feelings of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. First Lord Caitanya felt that He had been taken to Vṛndāvana, where He saw Kṛṣṇa's //rāsa// dance with the //gopīs.// Then He was brought to Kurukṣetra to see Lord Jagannātha, His sister (Subhadrā) and Lord Balarāma. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lost Vṛndāvana and Kṛṣṇa, the master of Vṛndāvana. At this time, Caitanya Mahāprabhu experienced //divyonmāda,// transcendental madness in separation from Kṛṣṇa. At Kurukṣetra, Kṛṣṇa displays His opulence, whereas in Vṛndāvana He is in His original position. Kṛṣṇa never goes even a step away from Vṛndāvana; therefore Kurukṣetra is less important for the //gopīs// than Vṛndāvana.

Although devotees who worship Kṛṣṇa in opulence (His Vaikuṇṭha aspect) may prefer to see Lord Kṛṣṇa at Kurukṣetra along with Subhadrā and Balarāma, the //gopīs// want to see Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana, performing the //rāsa// dance with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu showed by practical example how one can cultivate the mood of Rādhārāṇī and the other //gopīs// in separation from Kṛṣṇa. Devotees absorbed in this mood do not like to see Kṛṣṇa anywhere else but Vṛndāvana. Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lamented, "I found Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana, and now I have again lost Him and come to Kurukṣetra." Unless one is a very highly advanced devotee, he cannot understand these intricate feelings. The author of //Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta,// however, has tried to explain this //divyonmāda// as far as possible, and it is our duty simply to appreciate it as far as possible. Therefore the author has made the following request in verse 11:

> tāte viśvāsa kari' śuna bhāvera varṇana
> ha-ibe bhāvera jñāna, pāibā prema-dhana

"My dear readers, simply try to hear this description with faith and love. That will help you to understand transcendental ecstasy, and at last you will achieve love of Godhead very easily."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.38
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu dreamed of the rāsa dance, He was fully absorbed in transcendental bliss, but when His dream broke, He thought He had lost a precious jewel.
text:
> svapnāveśe preme prabhura gara gara mana
> bāhya haile haya---yena hārāila dhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svapna]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---when absorbed in dreams; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gara]] [[synonyms:g:gara]]---fully absorbed; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]] [[synonyms:h:haile]]---when He awakens; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---it is; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:h:hārāila]]---He has lost; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---something very precious.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu dreamed of the rāsa dance, He was fully absorbed in transcendental bliss, but when His dream broke, He thought He had lost a precious jewel.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.39
description: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would chant and dance, always absorbed in the bliss of transcendental madness. He carried out the necessities of the body, such as eating and bathing, merely out of habit.
text:
> unmattera prāya prabhu karena gāna-nṛtya
> dehera svabhāve karena snāna-bhojana-kṛtya
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:unmattera]] [[synonyms:p:prāya]]---as if mad; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---performs; [[synonyms:g:gāna]]-[[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---singing and dancing; [[synonyms:d:dehera]]---of the body; [[synonyms:s:svabhāve]]---by nature; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---carries out; [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eating; [[synonyms:k:kṛtya]]---duties.
translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would chant and dance, always absorbed in the bliss of transcendental madness. He carried out the necessities of the body, such as eating and bathing, merely out of habit.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.4
description: All glories to Svarūpa Dāmodara and the devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura. Please give me the strength to describe the character of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> jaya svarūpa, śrīvāsādi prabhu-bhakta-gaṇa
> śakti deha',---kari yena caitanya-varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---to Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---to the devotees of the Lord; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]] [[synonyms:d:deha']]---please give strength; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I can make; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---so that; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---description of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: All glories to Svarūpa Dāmodara and the devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura. Please give me the strength to describe the character of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.40
description: At night, Lord Caitanya would reveal to Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya the ecstatic feelings of His mind.
text:
> rātri haile svarūpa-rāmānande lañā
> āpana manera bhāva kahe ughāḍiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rātri]] [[synonyms:h:haile]]---when there was night; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:rāmānande]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking together; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]] [[synonyms:m:manera]]---of His own mind; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the ecstatic feelings; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---speaks; [[synonyms:u:ughāḍiyā]]---revealing.
translation: At night, Lord Caitanya would reveal to Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya the ecstatic feelings of His mind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.41
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "At first My mind somehow achieved the treasure of Kṛṣṇa, but it again lost Him. Therefore it gave up My body and home because of lamentation and accepted the religious principles of a kāpālika-yogī. Then My mind went to Vṛndāvana with its disciples, My senses.,"
text:
> prāpta-praṇaṣṭācyuta-vitta ātmā
> yayau viṣādojjhita-deha-gehaḥ
> gṛhīta-kāpālika-dharmako me
> vṛndāvanaṁ sendriya-śiṣya-vṛndaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prāpta]]---achieved; [[synonyms:p:praṇaṣṭa]]---lost; [[synonyms:a:acyuta]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vittaḥ]]---the treasure; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---mind; [[synonyms:y:yayau]]---went; [[synonyms:v:viṣāda]]---by lamentation; [[synonyms:u:ujjhita]]---given up; [[synonyms:d:deha]]-[[synonyms:g:gehaḥ]]---body and home; [[synonyms:g:gṛhīta]]---accepted; [[synonyms:k:kāpālika]]-[[synonyms:d:dharmakaḥ]]---the religious principles of a //kāpālika-yogī,// a kind of mendicant; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvanam]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:s:sa]]---with; [[synonyms:i:indriya]]---senses; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛndaḥ]]---disciples.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "At first My mind somehow achieved the treasure of Kṛṣṇa, but it again lost Him. Therefore it gave up My body and home because of lamentation and accepted the religious principles of a kāpālika-yogī. Then My mind went to Vṛndāvana with its disciples, My senses.,"
purport: This verse is clearly metaphorical.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.42
description: Having lost His acquired gem, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became overwhelmed with lamentation by remembering its attributes. Then, grasping the necks of Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, He cried, "Alas, where is My Lord Hari? Where is Hari?" Finally He became restless and lost all patience.
text:
> prāpta-ratna hārāñā, tāra guṇa saṅariyā,
> mahāprabhu santāpe vihvala
> rāya-svarūpera kaṇṭha dhari', kahe 'hāhā hari hari',
> dhairya gela, ha-ilā capala
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prāpta]]---acquired; [[synonyms:r:ratna]]---gem; [[synonyms:h:hārāñā]]---having lost; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of it; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---attributes; [[synonyms:s:saṅariyā]]---remembering; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:santāpe]]---in lamentation; [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---of Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:s:svarūpera]]---of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:k:kaṇṭha]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching the necks; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:h:hāhā]] [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---alas, where is Hari, where is Hari; [[synonyms:d:dhairya]]---patience; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---lost; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]] [[synonyms:c:capala]]---became restless.
translation: Having lost His acquired gem, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became overwhelmed with lamentation by remembering its attributes. Then, grasping the necks of Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, He cried, "Alas, where is My Lord Hari? Where is Hari?" Finally He became restless and lost all patience.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.43
description: "My dear friends," He said, "please hear of Kṛṣṇa's sweetness. Because of a great desire for that sweetness, My mind has given up all social and Vedic religious principles and taken to the profession of begging, exactly like a mystic yogī.
text:
> "śuna, bāndhava, kṛṣṇera mādhurī
> yāra lobhe mora mana, chāḍi' loka-veda-dharma,
> yogī hañā ha-ila bhikhārī
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:b:bāndhava]]---My friends; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:m:mādhurī]]---the sweetness of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---for which; [[synonyms:l:lobhe]]---by the greed; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---My mind; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:v:veda]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---social and Vedic religious principles; [[synonyms:y:yogī]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---having become a //yogī//; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]] [[synonyms:b:bhikhārī]]---has become a beggar.
translation: "My dear friends," He said, "please hear of Kṛṣṇa's sweetness. Because of a great desire for that sweetness, My mind has given up all social and Vedic religious principles and taken to the profession of begging, exactly like a mystic yogī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.44
description: "The ring of Kṛṣṇa's rāsa-līlā, manufactured by Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the most auspicious craftsman, is as pure as an earring made from a conchshell. The yogī of My mind is wearing that earring upon his ear. From a gourd he has carved out the bowl of My aspirations, and he has taken the bag of My expectations on his shoulder.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-līlā-maṇḍala, śuddha śaṅkha-kuṇḍala,
> gaḍiyāche śuka kārikara
> sei kuṇḍala kāṇe pari', tṛṣṇā-lāu-thālī dhari',
> āśā-jhuli kāndhera upara
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇḍala]]---the ring of the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]---pure; [[synonyms:ś:śaṅkha]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṇḍala]]---an earring of conchshell; [[synonyms:g:gaḍiyāche]]---has manufactured; [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]---Śukadeva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:k:kārikara]]---craftsman; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kuṇḍala]]---that earring; [[synonyms:k:kāṇe]] [[synonyms:p:pari]]---putting on the ear; [[synonyms:t:tṛṣṇā]]---aspiration; [[synonyms:l:lāu]]---of squash or gourd; [[synonyms:t:thālī]]---the bowl; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---taking; [[synonyms:ā:āśā]]---expectation; [[synonyms:j:jhuli]]---bag; [[synonyms:k:kāndhera]] [[synonyms:u:upara]]---on the shoulder.
translation: "The ring of Kṛṣṇa's rāsa-līlā, manufactured by Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the most auspicious craftsman, is as pure as an earring made from a conchshell. The yogī of My mind is wearing that earring upon his ear. From a gourd he has carved out the bowl of My aspirations, and he has taken the bag of My expectations on his shoulder.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.45
description: "The yogī of My mind wears the torn quilt of anxiety on his dirty body, which is covered with dust and ashes. His only words are,'Alas! Kṛṣṇa!' He wears twelve bangles of distress on his wrist and a turban of greed on his head. Because he has not eaten anything, he is very thin.
text:
> cintā-kānthā uḍhi gāya, dhūli-vibhūti-malina-kāya,
> 'hāhā kṛṣṇa' pralāpa-uttara
> udvega dvādaśa hāte, lobhera jhulani māthe,
> bhikṣābhāve kṣīṇa kalevara
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cintā]]---of anxiety; [[synonyms:k:kānthā]]---the torn quilt; [[synonyms:u:uḍhi]]---covering; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---on the body; [[synonyms:d:dhūli]]---dust; [[synonyms:v:vibhūti]]---ashes; [[synonyms:m:malina]]-[[synonyms:k:kāya]]---dirty body; [[synonyms:h:hāhā]]---alas; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pralāpa]]-[[synonyms:u:uttara]]---crazy replies; [[synonyms:u:udvega]]---distress; [[synonyms:d:dvādaśa]]---twelve (bangles); [[synonyms:h:hāte]]---on the wrist; [[synonyms:l:lobhera]]---of greed; [[synonyms:j:jhulani]]---turban; [[synonyms:m:māthe]]---on the head; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]-[[synonyms:a:abhāve]]---in the absence of alms; [[synonyms:k:kṣīṇa]]---skinny; [[synonyms:k:kalevara]]---body.
translation: "The yogī of My mind wears the torn quilt of anxiety on his dirty body, which is covered with dust and ashes. His only words are,'Alas! Kṛṣṇa!' He wears twelve bangles of distress on his wrist and a turban of greed on his head. Because he has not eaten anything, he is very thin.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.46
description: "The great yogī of My mind always studies the poetry and discussions of Lord Kṛṣṇa's Vṛndāvana pastimes. In the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and other scriptures, great saintly yogīs like Vyāsadeva and Śukadeva Gosvāmī have described Lord Kṛṣṇa as the Supersoul, beyond all material contamination.
text:
> vyāsa, śukādi yogi-gaṇa, kṛṣṇa ātmā nirañjana,
> vraje tāṅra yata līlā-gaṇa
> bhāgavatādi śāstra-gaṇe, kariyāche varṇane,
> sei tarjā paḍe anukṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vyāsa]]---Dvaipāyana Vyāsa; [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and other sages, such as Śukadeva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:y:yogi]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---great mystic //yogīs//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the Supersoul; [[synonyms:n:nirañjana]]---without material contamination; [[synonyms:v:vraje]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---His; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---//Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// and others; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---in revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:k:kariyāche]] [[synonyms:v:varṇane]]---have described; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:t:tarjā]]---that competition of poetry between two parties; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---reads; [[synonyms:a:anukṣaṇa]]---every moment.
translation: "The great yogī of My mind always studies the poetry and discussions of Lord Kṛṣṇa's Vṛndāvana pastimes. In the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and other scriptures, great saintly yogīs like Vyāsadeva and Śukadeva Gosvāmī have described Lord Kṛṣṇa as the Supersoul, beyond all material contamination.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.47
description: "The mystic yogī of My mind has assumed the name Mahābāula and made disciples of My ten senses. Thus My mind has gone to Vṛndāvana, leaving aside the home of My body and the great treasure of material enjoyment.
text:
> daśendriye śiṣya kari', 'mahā-bāula' nāma dhari',
> śiṣya lañā karila gamana
> mora deha sva-sadana, viṣaya-bhoga mahā-dhana,
> saba chāḍi' gelā vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:i:indriye]]---the ten senses; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making disciples; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bāula]]---of a great mendicant; [[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---taking the name; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking disciples; [[synonyms:k:karila]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---has gone; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:d:deha]]---body; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:s:sadana]]---own home; [[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---material enjoyment; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---great treasure; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---leaving aside everything; [[synonyms:g:gelā]] [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---has gone to Vṛndāvana.
translation: "The mystic yogī of My mind has assumed the name Mahābāula and made disciples of My ten senses. Thus My mind has gone to Vṛndāvana, leaving aside the home of My body and the great treasure of material enjoyment.
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu compares His mind to one of the mystic //yogīs// known as //bāula,// who makes at least ten disciples.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.48
description: "In Vṛndāvana, he goes from door to door begging alms with all his disciples. He begs from both the moving and the inert inhabitants—the citizens, the trees and the creepers. In this way he lives on fruits, roots and leaves.
text:
> vṛndāvane prajā-gaṇa, yata sthāvara-jaṅgama,
> vṛkṣa-latā gṛhastha-āśrame
> tāra ghare bhikṣāṭana, phala-mūla-patrāśana,
> ei vṛtti kare śiṣya-sane
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvane]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:p:prajā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the citizens; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:s:sthāvara]]-[[synonyms:j:jaṅgama]]---nonmoving and moving; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:l:latā]]---the trees and creepers; [[synonyms:g:gṛhastha]]-[[synonyms:ā:āśrame]]---in household life; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at his house; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]-[[synonyms:ā:āṭana]]---begging from door to door; [[synonyms:p:phala]]-[[synonyms:m:mūla]]-[[synonyms:p:patra]]---fruits, roots and leaves; [[synonyms:a:aśana]]---eating; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:v:vṛtti]]---this business; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performs; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with the disciples.
translation: "In Vṛndāvana, he goes from door to door begging alms with all his disciples. He begs from both the moving and the inert inhabitants---the citizens, the trees and the creepers. In this way he lives on fruits, roots and leaves.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.49
description: "The gopīs of Vrajabhūmi always taste the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's attributes, His beauty, His sweetness, His aroma, the sound of His flute and the touch of His body. My mind's five disciples, the senses of perception, gather the remnants of that nectar from the gopīs and bring them to the yogī of My mind. The senses maintain their lives by eating those remnants.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-guṇa-rūpa-rasa, gandha, śabda, paraśa,
> se sudhā āsvāde gopī-gaṇa
> tā-sabāra grāsa-śeṣe, āni' pañcendriya śiṣye,
> se bhikṣāya rākhena jīvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---attributes, beauty and sweetness; [[synonyms:g:gandha]] [[synonyms:ś:śabda]] [[synonyms:p:paraśa]]---aroma, sound and touch; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:s:sudhā]]---that nectar; [[synonyms:ā:āsvāde]]---taste; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:t:tā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:g:grāsa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---remnants of food; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:i:indriya]]---five senses; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣye]]---the disciples; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:b:bhikṣāya]]---by such alms; [[synonyms:r:rākhena]]---maintain; [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---life.
translation: "The gopīs of Vrajabhūmi always taste the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's attributes, His beauty, His sweetness, His aroma, the sound of His flute and the touch of His body. My mind's five disciples, the senses of perception, gather the remnants of that nectar from the gopīs and bring them to the yogī of My mind. The senses maintain their lives by eating those remnants.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.5
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's emotion of transcendental madness in separation from Kṛṣṇa is very deep and mysterious. Even though one is very advanced and learned, he cannot understand it.
text:
> prabhura virahonmāda-bhāva gambhīra
> bujhite nā pāre keha, yadyapi haya 'dhīra'
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:viraha]]-[[synonyms:u:unmāda]]---of the transcendental madness of separation from Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---emotion; [[synonyms:g:gambhīra]]---very deep and mysterious; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]] [[synonyms:k:keha]]---no one is able; [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:d:dhīra]]---a very learned and gentle scholar.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's emotion of transcendental madness in separation from Kṛṣṇa is very deep and mysterious. Even though one is very advanced and learned, he cannot understand it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.50
description: "There is a solitary garden where Kṛṣṇa enjoys His pastimes, and in one corner of a pavilion in that garden, the yogī of My mind, along with his disciples, practices mystic yoga. Wanting to see Kṛṣṇa directly, this yogī remains awake throughout the night, meditating on Kṛṣṇa who is the Supersoul, uncontaminated by the three modes of nature.
text:
> śūnya-kuñja-maṇḍapa-koṇe, yogābhyāsa kṛṣṇa-dhyāne,
> tāhāṅ rahe lañā śiṣya-gaṇa
> kṛṣṇa ātmā nirañjana, sākṣāt dekhite mana,
> dhyāne rātri kare jāgaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śūnya]]-[[synonyms:k:kuñja]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇḍapa]]-[[synonyms:k:koṇe]]---in the corner of a pavilion in a solitary garden; [[synonyms:y:yoga]]-[[synonyms:a:abhyāsa]]---practice of mystic //yoga//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dhyāne]]---by meditating on Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣya]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---disciples; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:ātmā]]---the Supersoul; [[synonyms:n:nirañjana]]---without material contamination; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---directly; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---to see; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:d:dhyāne]]---in meditation; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]---at night; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:j:jāgaraṇa]]---keeps awake.
translation: "There is a solitary garden where Kṛṣṇa enjoys His pastimes, and in one corner of a pavilion in that garden, the yogī of My mind, along with his disciples, practices mystic yoga. Wanting to see Kṛṣṇa directly, this yogī remains awake throughout the night, meditating on Kṛṣṇa who is the Supersoul, uncontaminated by the three modes of nature.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.51
description: "When My mind lost the association of Kṛṣṇa and could no longer see Him, he became depressed and took up mystic yoga. In the void of separation from Kṛṣṇa, he experienced ten transcendental transformations. Agitated by these transformations, My mind fled, leaving My body, his place of residence, empty. Thus I am completely in trance."
text:
> mana kṛṣṇa-viyogī, duḥkhe mana haila yogī,
> se viyoge daśa daśā haya
> se daśāya vyākula hañā, mana gela palāñā,
> śūnya mora śarīra ālaya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:viyogī]]---bereft of Kṛṣṇa's association; [[synonyms:d:duḥkhe]]---in unhappiness; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:y:yogī]]---a mystic //yogī//; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:v:viyoge]]---by that feeling of separation; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]---ten; [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---transcendental transformations; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:d:daśāya]]---by those transcendental transformations; [[synonyms:v:vyākula]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being very agitated; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went away; [[synonyms:p:palāñā]]---fleeing; [[synonyms:ś:śūnya]]---void; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:ś:śarīra]]---body; [[synonyms:ā:ālaya]]---place of residence.
translation: "When My mind lost the association of Kṛṣṇa and could no longer see Him, he became depressed and took up mystic yoga. In the void of separation from Kṛṣṇa, he experienced ten transcendental transformations. Agitated by these transformations, My mind fled, leaving My body, his place of residence, empty. Thus I am completely in trance."
purport: In this verse, the outward activities of the //kāpālika// mendicants have been described, but not their actual life. The //kāpālika// mendicants are tantric materialists who carry skulls in their hands. They are not Vaiṣṇavas and have nothing to do with spiritual life. Therefore they are untouchable. Only an outward comparison has been made between the mind and their activities, but their behavior should never be imitated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.52
description: When the gopīs felt separation from Kṛṣṇa, they experienced ten kinds of bodily transformations. These same symptoms appeared on the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> kṛṣṇera viyoge gopīra daśa daśā haya
> sei daśa daśā haya prabhura udaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:v:viyoge]]---by separation from Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gopīra]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:d:daśa]] [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---ten kinds of transcendental transformations of the body; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:d:daśa]] [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---ten kinds of transcendental transformations; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:u:udaya]]---visible in the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: When the gopīs felt separation from Kṛṣṇa, they experienced ten kinds of bodily transformations. These same symptoms appeared on the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.53
description: "The ten bodily transformations resulting from separation from Kṛṣṇa are anxiety, wakefulness, mental agitation, thinness, uncleanliness, talking like a madman, disease, madness, illusion and death."
text:
> cintātra jāgarodvegau
> tānavaṁ malināṅgatā
> pralāpo vyādhir unmādo
> moho mṛtyur daśā daśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cintā]]---anxiety; [[synonyms:a:atra]]---here (because of separation from Kṛṣṇa); [[synonyms:j:jāgara]]---wakefulness; [[synonyms:u:udvegau]]---and mental agitation; [[synonyms:t:tānavam]]---thinness; [[synonyms:m:malina]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅgatā]]---an unclean, almost dirty state of the body; [[synonyms:p:pralāpaḥ]]---talking like a madman; [[synonyms:v:vyādhiḥ]]---disease; [[synonyms:u:unmādaḥ]]---madness; [[synonyms:m:mohaḥ]]---illusion; [[synonyms:m:mṛtyuḥ]]---death; [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---conditions; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]---ten.
translation: "The ten bodily transformations resulting from separation from Kṛṣṇa are anxiety, wakefulness, mental agitation, thinness, uncleanliness, talking like a madman, disease, madness, illusion and death."
purport:
This verse is part of a description of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's different traits from //Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi// by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. In this book, he elaborately explains the ten symptoms as follows.

Cintā. As stated in the //Haṁsadūta://

> yadā yāto gopī-hṛdaya-madano nanda-sadanān
> mukundo gāndinyās tanayam anurundhan madhu-purīm
> tadāmāṅkṣīc cintā-sariti ghana-ghūrṇāparicayair
> agādhāyāṁ vādhāmaya-payasi rādhā virahiṇī

"At the request of Akrūra, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma left the house of Nanda Mahārāja for Mathurā. At that time, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's mind was disrupted, and She became almost mad because of extreme separation from Kṛṣṇa. She experienced great mental pain and agitation, which caused Her to drown in mental speculation in the river of anxiety. She thought, 'Now I am going to die, and when I die, Kṛṣṇa will surely come back to see Me again. But when He hears of My death from the people of Vṛndāvana, He will certainly be very unhappy. Therefore I shall not die.' " This is the explanation of the word //cintā.//

Jāgara. As stated in the //Padyāvalī://

> yāḥ paśyanti priyaṁ svapne
> dhanyāstāḥ sakhi yoṣitaḥ
> asmākaṁ tu gate kṛṣṇe
> gatā nidrāpi vairiṇī

Thinking Herself very unfortunate, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī addressed Her very dear friend Viśākhā, "My dear friend, if I could see Kṛṣṇa in My dreams, I would certainly be glorified for My great fortune. But what can I do? Sleep also plays mischievously with Me. Indeed, it has become My enemy. Therefore I have not slept since the departure of Kṛṣṇa."

Udvega. This word is also explained in the //Haṁsadūta// as follows:

> mano me hā kaṣṭaṁ jvalati kim ahaṁ hanta karavai
> na pāraṁ nāvāraṁ sumukhi kalayām yasya jaladheḥ
> iyaṁ vande mūrdhnā sapadi tam upāyaṁ kathaya me
> parāmṛśye yasmād dhṛti-kaṇikayāpi kṣaṇi-kayā

Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī addressed Lalitā, "My dear beautiful-faced Lalitā, I cannot express how My heart is burning. It is a great, unfathomable ocean of anxiety. Still, I wish to offer My obeisances at your lotus feet. What shall I do? Please consider My condition and advise Me how I can become peaceful. That is My desire."
> Tānava is described as follows:

> udañcad-vaktrāmbhoruha-vikṛtir antaḥ-kulaṣitā
> sadāhārābhāva-glapita-kucakokā yadu-pate
> viśuṣyanti rādhā tava viraha-tāpād anudinaṁ
> nidāghe kuly eva kraśima-paripākaṁ prathayati

When Uddhava returned to Mathurā after visiting Vṛndāvana, Lord Kṛṣṇa inquired from him about Rādhārāṇī and Viśākhā. Uddhava replied as follows: "Consider the condition of the //gopīs!// Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī especially is in a very painful condition because of separation from You. She has grown skinny, and Her bodily luster is almost gone. Her heart is immersed in pain, and because She has given up eating, Her breast has become black, as if diseased. Because of separation from You, all the //gopīs,// especially Rādhārāṇī, appear like dried-up water holes under the scorching heat of the sun."

Malina-aṅgatā is described as follows:

> hima-visara-viśīrṇāmbhoja-tulyānana-śrīḥ
> khara-marud-aparajyad-bandhu-jīvopamauṣṭhī
> agha-hara śarad-arkottāpitendīvarākṣī
> tava viraha-vipatti-mlāpitāsīd viśākhā

Uddhava said to Kṛṣṇa, "O most auspicious Kṛṣṇa, please hear me. The tribulation caused by Your absence has made Viśākhā languid. Her lips tremble like trees in a strong wind. Her beautiful face is like a lotus flower that has withered under the snow, and Her eyes are like lotus petals scorched by the heat of the autumn sun."

Pralāpa is explained in //Lalita-mādhava// as follows:

> kva nanda-kula-candramāḥ kva śikhi-candra-kālaṅkṛtiḥ
> kva manda-muralī-ravaḥ kva nu surendra-nīla-dyutiḥ
> kva rāsa-rasa-tāṇḍavī kva sakhi jīva-rakṣauṣadhir
> nidhir mama suhṛttamaḥ kva tava hanta hā dhig-vidhiḥ

This is Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's lamentation for Her beloved Kṛṣṇa, who was away from home. A woman whose husband has left home and gone to a foreign land is called //proṣita-bhartṛkā.// Lamenting for Kṛṣṇa in the same way as such a woman laments for her husband, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī said, "My dear friend, where is the glory of the family of Mahārāja Nanda, who wears a half-moon ornament on His head? Where is Kṛṣṇa, whose hue is like that of the //indranīla// jewel and who plays so nicely on His flute? Where is your friend, the best of all men, so expert in dancing in the circle of the //rāsa// dance? Where is He who is the real medicine to save Me from dying of heart disease? I must condemn Providence, for he has caused Me so many tribulations by separating Me from Kṛṣṇa."

Vyādhi is also described in //Lalita-mādhava://

> uttāpī puṭa-pākato 'pi garala-grāmād api kṣobhaṇo
> dambholer api duḥsahaḥ kaṭur alaṁ hṛn-magna-śūlyād api
> tīvraḥ prauḍha-visūcikāni-cayato 'py uccair mamāyaṁ balī
> marmāṇy adya bhinatti gokula-pater viśleṣa-janmā jvaraḥ

Being greatly afflicted by the pain of separation from Kṛṣṇa, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī said, "My dear Lalitā, kindly hear Me. I cannot bear suffering the fever of separation from Kṛṣṇa, nor can I explain it to you. It is something like gold melting in an earthen box. This fever produces more distress than poison, and it is more piercing than a thunderbolt. I suffer exactly like someone almost dead from cholera. To be giving Me so much pain, this fever must be very strong indeed."

Unmāda is explained as follows:

> bhramati bhavana-garbhe nirnimittaṁ hasantī
> prathayati tava vārtāṁ cetanācetaneṣu
> lutḥati ca bhuvi rādhā kampitāṅgī murāre
> viṣama-viraha-khedodgāri-vibhrānta-cittā

Uddhava said to Kṛṣṇa, "My dear Kṛṣṇa, all the //gopīs// are so afflicted by Your absence that they have become almost mad. O Murāri, at home Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī laughs unnecessarily and, like a madwoman, inquires about You from every entity without distinction, even from the stones. She rolls on the ground, unable to bear the agony of Your absence."

Moha is explained as follows:

> nirundhe dainyābdhiṁ harati guru-cintā paribhavaṁ
> vilumpaty unmādaṁ sthagayati balād bāṣpa-laharīm
> idānīṁ kaṁsāre kuvalaya-dṛśaḥ kevalam idaṁ
> vidhatte sācivyaṁ tava viraha-mūrcchā-sahacarī

Lalitā wrote Kṛṣṇa the following letter on Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's behalf: "My dear Kṛṣṇa, separation from You has greatly agitated Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's mind, and She has fallen unconscious on the ground. O enemy of Kaṁsa, You have now become a first-class politician, and therefore You can supposedly give relief to everyone. Therefore please consider the plight of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, or very soon You will hear of Her death. Maybe at that time You will lament, although now You are jubilant."

Mṛtyu is explained in the //Haṁsadūta://

> aye rāsa-krīḍā-rasika mama sakhyaṁ nava-navā
> purā baddhā yena praṇaya-laharī hanta gahanā
> sa cen muktāpekṣas tvam asi dhig imāṁ tūlaśakalaṁ
> yad etasyā nāsā-nihitam idam adyāpi calati

In the following letter, Lalitā chastised Kṛṣṇa for staying in Mathurā: "Simply by dancing in the circle of the //rāsa// dance, You attracted Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's love. Why are You now so indifferent to my dear friend Rādhārāṇī? She is lying nearly unconscious, thinking of Your pastimes. I shall determine whether She is alive by putting a cotton swab under Her nostrils, and if She is still living, I shall chastise Her."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.54
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was overwhelmed night and day by these ten ecstatic conditions. Whenever such symptoms arose, His mind became unsteady.
text:
> ei daśa-daśāya prabhu vyākula rātri-dine
> kabhu kona daśā uṭhe, sthira nahe mane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:d:daśa]]-[[synonyms:d:daśāya]]---by ten conditions; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vyākula]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---night and day; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---some; [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---condition; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---arises; [[synonyms:s:sthira]]---steady; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---is not; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---the mind.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was overwhelmed night and day by these ten ecstatic conditions. Whenever such symptoms arose, His mind became unsteady.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.55
description: After speaking in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell silent. Then Rāma-nanda Rāya began to recite various verses.
text:
> eta kahi' mahāprabhu mauna karilā
> rāmānanda-rāya śloka paḍite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---speaking this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mauna]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---became silent; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verses; [[synonyms:p:paḍite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to recite.
translation: After speaking in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell silent. Then Rāma-nanda Rāya began to recite various verses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.56
description: Rāmānanda Rāya recited verses from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī sang of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes. In this way, they brought Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to external consciousness.
text:
> svarūpa-gosāñi kare kṛṣṇa-līlā gāna
> dui jane kichu kailā prabhura bāhya jñāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosāñi; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---of the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gāna]]---singing; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:j:jane]]---both of them; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---revived; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]] [[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---external consciousness.
translation: Rāmānanda Rāya recited verses from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī sang of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes. In this way, they brought Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to external consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.57
description: After half the night had passed in this way, Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī made Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lie down on His bed in the inner room.
text:
> ei-mata ardha-rātri kailā niryāpaṇa
> bhitara-prakoṣṭhe prabhure karāilā śayana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:a:ardha]]-[[synonyms:r:rātri]]---half the night; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:n:niryāpaṇa]]---passed; [[synonyms:b:bhitara]]-[[synonyms:p:prakoṣṭhe]]---in the inner room; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karāilā]] [[synonyms:ś:śayana]]---they made to lie down.
translation: After half the night had passed in this way, Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī made Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lie down on His bed in the inner room.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.58
description: Then Rāmānanda Rāya returned home, and Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, along with Govinda, lay down in front of the door to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's room.
text:
> rāmānanda-rāya tabe gelā nija ghare
> svarūpa-govinda duṅhe śuilena dvāre

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.59
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained awake throughout the entire night, chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra very loudly.
text:
> saba rātri mahāprabhu kare jāgaraṇa
> ucca kari' kahe kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:r:rātri]]---all night; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:j:jāgaraṇa]]---remaining without sleep; [[synonyms:u:ucca]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---very loudly; [[synonyms:k:kahe]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chants the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained awake throughout the entire night, chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra very loudly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.6
description: How can one describe unfathomable subject matters? It is possible only if Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu gives him the capability.
text:
> bujhite nā pāri yāhā, varṇite ke pāre?
> sei bujhe, varṇe, caitanya śakti dena yāṅre
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---not being able; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]]---subject which; [[synonyms:v:varṇite]] [[synonyms:k:ke]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---who can describe; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:b:bujhe]]---he can understand; [[synonyms:v:varṇe]]---can describe; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---capacity; [[synonyms:d:dena]]---gives; [[synonyms:y:yāṅre]]---to whom.
translation: How can one describe unfathomable subject matters? It is possible only if Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu gives him the capability.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.60
description: After some time, Svarūpa Dāmodara could no longer hear Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu chanting. When he entered the room, he found the three doors locked, but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had gone.
text:
> śabda nā pāñā svarūpa kapāṭa kailā dūre
> tina-dvāra deoyā āche, prabhu nāhi ghare!
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---sound; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:k:kapāṭa]]---the door; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:d:dūre]]---opened; [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāra]]---three doors; [[synonyms:d:deoyā]] [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---were locked; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---was not within the room.
translation: After some time, Svarūpa Dāmodara could no longer hear Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu chanting. When he entered the room, he found the three doors locked, but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had gone.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.61
description: All the devotees were very anxious when they saw that the Lord was not in His room. They wandered about searching for Him with a warning lamp.
text:
> cintita ha-ila sabe prabhure nā dekhiyā
> prabhu cāhi' bule sabe deuṭī jvāliyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cintita]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became very anxious; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---not seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:cāhi']]---searching for; [[synonyms:b:bule]]---wander; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:d:deuṭī]]---lamp; [[synonyms:j:jvāliyā]]---lighting.
translation: All the devotees were very anxious when they saw that the Lord was not in His room. They wandered about searching for Him with a warning lamp.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.62
description: After searching for some time, they came upon Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lying in a corner by the northern side of the Siṁha-dvāra gate.
text:
> siṁha-dvārera uttara-diśāya āche eka ṭhāñi
> tāra madhye paḍi' āchena caitanya-gosāñi
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:siṁha]]-[[synonyms:d:dvārera]]---of the gate known as Siṁha-dvāra; [[synonyms:u:uttara]]-[[synonyms:d:diśāya]]---on the northern side; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there is; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---a place; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that place; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---lying down; [[synonyms:ā:āchena]]---was; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: After searching for some time, they came upon Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lying in a corner by the northern side of the Siṁha-dvāra gate.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.63
description: At first they were overjoyed to see Him, but when they saw His condition, all the devotees, headed by Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, were very anxious.
text:
> dekhi' svarūpa-gosāñi-ādi ānandita hailā
> prabhura daśā dekhi' punaḥ cintite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---all the devotees, headed by Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]] [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became very glad; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---the condition; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:c:cintite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---they began to feel anxiety.
translation: At first they were overjoyed to see Him, but when they saw His condition, all the devotees, headed by Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, were very anxious.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.64
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was lying unconscious, and His body had become elongated to five or six cubits [eight or nine feet]. There was no breath from His nostrils.
text:
> prabhu paḍi' āchena dīrgha hāta pāṅca-chaya
> acetana deha, nāsāya śvāsa nāhi vaya

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was lying unconscious, and His body had become elongated to five or six cubits [eight or nine feet]. There was no breath from His nostrils.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.65-66
description: Each of His arms and legs had become three cubits long; only skin connected the separated joints. The Lord's body temperature, indicating life, was very low. All the joints in His arms, legs, neck and waist were separated by at least six inches.
text:
> eka eka hasta-pāda---dīrgha tina tina-hāta
> asthi-granthi bhinna, carma āche mātra tāta
>

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.7
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī recorded all these transcendental activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in their notebooks.

> ei duira kaḍacāte e-līlā prakāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:duira]]---of these two; [[synonyms:k:kaḍacāte]]---in the notebooks; [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---these pastimes; [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---described.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī recorded all these transcendental activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in their notebooks.
purport:
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's transcendental feelings of separation from Kṛṣṇa and His consequent madness are not at all understandable by a person on the material platform. Nonetheless, a so-called party of devotees named //nadīyā-nāgarī// has sprung up and introduced the worship of Viṣṇupriyā. This certainly indicates their ignorance concerning Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastimes. In the opinion of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, such worship is a product of the imagination. Many other methods of worshiping Caitanya Mahāprabhu have also been introduced, but they have all been rejected by stalwart devotees like Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura. The groups practicing such unauthorized worship have been listed by Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura:

> āula, bāula, kartābhajā, neḍā, daraveśa, sāṅi
> sahajiyā, sakhībhekī, smārta, jāta-gosāñi
> ativāḍī, cūḍādhārī, gaurāṅga-nāgarī

Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī witnessed Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities firsthand, and they recorded them in two notebooks. Therefore, without reference to these notebooks, one cannot understand the activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Anyone inventing some new method for worshiping Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is certainly unable to understand the Lord's pastimes, for he is bereft of the real process of approaching the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.73
description: "Sometimes Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would go to the house of Kāśī Miśra. There He would be greatly aggrieved, feeling separation from Kṛṣṇa. The joints of His transcendental body would slacken, and His arms and legs would become elongated. Rolling on the ground, the Lord would cry out in distress in a faltering voice and weep very sorrowfully. The appearance of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, awakening in my heart, maddens me."

> kvacin miśrāvāse vraja-pati-sutasyoru-virahāt
> ślathac chrī-sandhitvād dadhad-adhika-dairghyaṁ bhuja-padoḥ

translation: "Sometimes Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would go to the house of Kāśī Miśra. There He would be greatly aggrieved, feeling separation from Kṛṣṇa. The joints of His transcendental body would slacken, and His arms and legs would become elongated. Rolling on the ground, the Lord would cry out in distress in a faltering voice and weep very sorrowfully. The appearance of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, awakening in my heart, maddens me."

It is a most unfortunate situation for human society that none of these notebooks are still extant.

> śāstra-lokātīta yei yei bhāva haya
> itara-lokera tāte nā haya niścaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:a:atīta]]---beyond the conception of people and the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---emotional ecstasies; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:i:itara]]-[[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of common men; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in that; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is not; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---belief.
translation: These ecstasies are not described in the śāstras, and they are inconceivable to common men. Therefore people in general do not believe in them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.83
description: Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī lived continuously with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. I am simply recording whatever I have heard from him. Although common men do not believe in these pastimes, I believe in them totally.
text:
> raghunātha-dāsera sadā prabhu-saṅge sthiti
> tāṅra mukhe śuni' likhi kariyā pratīti
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsera]]---of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---living; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---from his mouth; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:l:likhi]]---I write; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:p:pratīti]]---accepting in total.
translation: Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī lived continuously with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. I am simply recording whatever I have heard from him. Although common men do not believe in these pastimes, I believe in them totally.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.84
description: One day, while Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was going to the sea to bathe, He suddenly saw a sand dune named Caṭaka-parvata.
text:
> eka-dina mahāprabhu samudre yāite
> 'caṭaka'-parvata dekhilena ācambite
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:samudre]] [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---while going to the sea; [[synonyms:c:caṭaka]]-[[synonyms:p:parvata]]---the Caṭaka-parvata sand hill; [[synonyms:d:dekhilena]]---saw; [[synonyms:ā:ācambite]]---suddenly.
translation: One day, while Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was going to the sea to bathe, He suddenly saw a sand dune named Caṭaka-parvata.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.85
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu mistook the sand dune for Govardhana Hill and ran toward it.
text:
> govardhana-śaila-jñāne āviṣṭa ha-ilā
> parvata-diśāte prabhu dhāñā calilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaila]]---Govardhana Hill; [[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---by the understanding; [[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became overwhelmed; [[synonyms:p:parvata]]-[[synonyms:d:diśāte]]---in the direction of the sand hill; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dhāñā]] [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---began to run.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu mistook the sand dune for Govardhana Hill and ran toward it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.86
description: "Of all the devotees, this Govardhana Hill is the best! O My friends, this hill supplies Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, as well as Their calves, cows and cowherd friends, with all kinds of necessities-water for drinking, very soft grass, caves, fruits, flowers and vegetables. In this way the hill offers respect to the Lord. Being touched by the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, Govardhana Hill appears very jubilant."
text:
> hantāyam adrir abalā hari-dāsa-varyo
> yad rāma-kṛṣṇa-caraṇa-sparaśa-pramodaḥ
> mānaṁ tanoti saha-go-gaṇayos tayor yat
> pānīya-sūyavasa-kandara-kanda-mūlaiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hanta]]---oh; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:a:adriḥ]]---hill; [[synonyms:a:abalāḥ]]---O friends; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]-[[synonyms:v:varyaḥ]]---the best among the servants of the Lord; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---because; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---of the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma; [[synonyms:s:sparaśa]]---by the touch; [[synonyms:p:pramodaḥ]]---jubilant; [[synonyms:m:mānam]]---respects; [[synonyms:t:tanoti]]---offers; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:g:go]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇayoḥ]]---cows, calves and cowherd boys; [[synonyms:t:tayoḥ]]---to Them (Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma); [[synonyms:y:yat]]---because; [[synonyms:p:pānīya]]---drinking water; [[synonyms:s:sūyavasa]]---very soft grass; [[synonyms:k:kandara]]---caves; [[synonyms:k:kanda]]-[[synonyms:m:mūlaiḥ]]---and by roots.
translation: "Of all the devotees, this Govardhana Hill is the best! O My friends, this hill supplies Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, as well as Their calves, cows and cowherd friends, with all kinds of necessities-water for drinking, very soft grass, caves, fruits, flowers and vegetables. In this way the hill offers respect to the Lord. Being touched by the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, Govardhana Hill appears very jubilant."
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.21.18). It was spoken by the //gopīs// when Lord Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma entered the forest in the autumn. The //gopīs// spoke among themselves and glorified Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma for Their pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.87
description: Reciting this verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ran toward the sand dune as fast as the wind. Govinda ran after Him, but he could not approach Him.
text:
> ei śloka paḍi' prabhu calena vāyu-vege
> govinda dhāila pāche, nāhi pāya lāge
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---this verse; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:calena]]---goes; [[synonyms:v:vāyu]]-[[synonyms:v:vege]]---at the speed of the wind; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:d:dhāila]]---ran; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---behind; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]] [[synonyms:l:lāge]]---could not catch.
translation: Reciting this verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ran toward the sand dune as fast as the wind. Govinda ran after Him, but he could not approach Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.88
description: First one devotee shouted loudly, and then a tumultuous uproar arose as all the devotees stood up and began to run after the Lord.
text:
> phukāra paḍila, mahā-kolāhala ha-ila
> yei yāhāṅ chila sei uṭhiyā dhāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:phu]]-[[synonyms:k:kāra]]---a loud call; [[synonyms:p:paḍila]]---arose; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:k:kolāhala]]---a tumultuous sound; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whoever; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:c:chila]]---was; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---he; [[synonyms:u:uṭhiyā]] [[synonyms:d:dhāila]]---got up and began to run.
translation: First one devotee shouted loudly, and then a tumultuous uproar arose as all the devotees stood up and began to run after the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.89
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Jagadānanda Paṇḍita, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Rāmāi, Nandāi and Śaṅkara Paṇḍita are some of the devotees who ran after Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> svarūpa, jagadānanda, paṇḍita-gadādhara
> rāmāi, nandāi, āra paṇḍita śaṅkara
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:j:jagadānanda]]---Jagadānanda Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]-[[synonyms:g:gadādhara]]---Gadādhara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:r:rāmāi]]---Rāmāi; [[synonyms:n:nandāi]]---Nandāi; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaṅkara]]---Śaṅkara Paṇḍita.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Jagadānanda Paṇḍita, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Rāmāi, Nandāi and Śaṅkara Paṇḍita are some of the devotees who ran after Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.9
description: These two great personalities [Svarūpa Dāmodara and Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī] recorded the activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu moment by moment. They described these activities briefly as well as elaborately in their notebooks.
text:
> kṣaṇe kṣaṇe anubhavi' ei dui-jana
> saṅkṣepe bāhulye karena kaḍacā-granthana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]] [[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---moment by moment; [[synonyms:a:anubhavi']]---understanding; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---these two persons; [[synonyms:s:saṅkṣepe]]---in brief; [[synonyms:b:bāhulye]]---elaborately; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---do; [[synonyms:k:kaḍacā]]-[[synonyms:g:granthana]]---compiling the notebooks.
translation: These two great personalities [Svarūpa Dāmodara and Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī] recorded the activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu moment by moment. They described these activities briefly as well as elaborately in their notebooks.
purport: For future reference, we should remember that Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī recorded the pastimes briefly, whereas Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī recorded them elaborately. These two great personalities simply recorded the facts; they did not create any descriptive literary embellishments.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.90
description: Paramānanda Purī and Brahmānanda Bhāratī also went toward the beach, and Bhagavān Ācārya, who was lame, followed them very slowly.
text:
> purī-bhāratī-gosāñi āilā sindhu-tīre
> bhagavān-ācārya khañja calilā dhīre dhīre
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:purī]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:b:bhāratī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:s:sindhu]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the shore of the sea; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Bhagavān Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:khañja]]---lame; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---ran; [[synonyms:d:dhīre]] [[synonyms:d:dhīre]]---very slowly.
translation: Paramānanda Purī and Brahmānanda Bhāratī also went toward the beach, and Bhagavān Ācārya, who was lame, followed them very slowly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.91
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was running with the speed of the wind, but He suddenly became stunned in ecstasy and lost all strength to proceed further.
text:
> prathame calilā prabhu,---yena vāyu-gati
> stambha-bhāva pathe haila, calite nāhi śakti
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prathame]]---in the beginning; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---like; [[synonyms:v:vāyu]]-[[synonyms:g:gati]]---the speed of the wind; [[synonyms:s:stambha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the emotion of being stunned; [[synonyms:p:pathe]]---on the way; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:c:calite]]---to move; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---no; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---power.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was running with the speed of the wind, but He suddenly became stunned in ecstasy and lost all strength to proceed further.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.92
description: The flesh at each of His pores erupted like pimples, and His hair, standing on end, appeared like kadamba flowers.
text:
> prati-roma-kūpe māṁsa---vraṇera ākāra
> tāra upare romodgama---kadamba-prakāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:r:roma]]-[[synonyms:k:kūpe]]---in every hair hole; [[synonyms:m:māṁsa]]---the flesh; [[synonyms:v:vraṇera]] [[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---like pimples; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:u:upare]]---upon that; [[synonyms:r:roma]]-[[synonyms:u:udgama]]---standing of the hair; [[synonyms:k:kadamba]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---like the //kadamba// flowers.
translation: The flesh at each of His pores erupted like pimples, and His hair, standing on end, appeared like kadamba flowers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.93
description: Blood and perspiration flowed incessantly from every pore of His body, and He could not speak a word but simply produced a gargling sound within His throat.
text:
> prati-rome prasveda paḍe rudhirera dhāra
> kaṇṭhe gharghara, nāhi varṇera uccāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:r:rome]]---from each hair; [[synonyms:p:prasveda]]---sweat; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---drops; [[synonyms:r:rudhirera]]---of blood; [[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---flow; [[synonyms:k:kaṇṭhe]]---in the throat; [[synonyms:g:gharghara]]---gargling sound; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:v:varṇera]]---of letters; [[synonyms:u:uccāra]]---pronunciation.
translation: Blood and perspiration flowed incessantly from every pore of His body, and He could not speak a word but simply produced a gargling sound within His throat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.94
description: The Lord's eyes filled up and overflowed with unlimited tears, like the Ganges and Yamunā meeting in the sea.
text:
> dui netre bhari' aśru vahaye apāra
> samudre mililā yena gaṅgā-yamunā-dhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:n:netre]]---in the two eyes; [[synonyms:b:bhari']]---filling; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:v:vahaye]]---flow; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:s:samudre]]---the ocean; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]---of the Ganges; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]---of the Yamunā; [[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---flow.
translation: The Lord's eyes filled up and overflowed with unlimited tears, like the Ganges and Yamunā meeting in the sea.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.95
description: His entire body faded to the color of a white conchshell, and then He began to quiver, like the waves in the ocean.
text:
> vaivarṇye śaṅkha-prāya śveta haila aṅga
> tabe kampa uṭhe,---yena samudre taraṅga
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaivarṇye]]---by fading; [[synonyms:ś:śaṅkha]]-[[synonyms:p:prāya]]---like a conchshell; [[synonyms:ś:śveta]]---white; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---body; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:k:kampa]]---shivering; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---arises; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:s:samudre]]---in the ocean; [[synonyms:t:taraṅga]]---waves.
translation: His entire body faded to the color of a white conchshell, and then He began to quiver, like the waves in the ocean.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.96
description: While quivering in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell down on the ground. Then Govinda approached Him.
text:
> kāṅpite kāṅpite prabhu bhūmete paḍilā
> tabe ta' govinda prabhura nikaṭe āilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāṅpite]] [[synonyms:k:kāṅpite]]---while shivering; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhūmete]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nikaṭe]]---near; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came.
translation: While quivering in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell down on the ground. Then Govinda approached Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.97
description: Govinda sprinkled water from a karaṅga waterpot all over the Lord's body, and then, taking His own outer garment, he began to fan Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> karaṅgera jale kare sarvāṅga siñcana
> bahirvāsa lañā kare aṅga saṁvījana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:karaṅgera]] [[synonyms:j:jale]]---with water from a //karaṅga// waterpot; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---all parts of the body; [[synonyms:s:siñcana]]---sprinkling; [[synonyms:b:bahirvāsa]]---covering cloth; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the body; [[synonyms:s:saṁvījana]]---fanning.
translation: Govinda sprinkled water from a karaṅga waterpot all over the Lord's body, and then, taking His own outer garment, he began to fan Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.98
description: When Svarūpa Dāmodara and the other devotees reached the spot and saw the condition of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they began to cry.
text:
> svarūpādi-gaṇa tāhāṅ āsiyā mililā
> prabhura avasthā dekhi' kāndite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees, headed by Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:avasthā]]---condition; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kāndite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to cry.
translation: When Svarūpa Dāmodara and the other devotees reached the spot and saw the condition of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they began to cry.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 14.99
description: All eight kinds of transcendental transformations were visible in the Lord's body. All the devotees were struck with wonder to see such a sight.
text:
> prabhura aṅge dekhe aṣṭa-sāttvika vikāra
> āścarya sāttvika dekhi' hailā camatkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---in the body; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---they see; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:s:sāttvika]] [[synonyms:v:vikāra]]---eight kinds of transcendental transformations; [[synonyms:ā:āścarya]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:s:sāttvika]]---transcendental; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:hailā]] [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---they became struck with wonder.
translation: All eight kinds of transcendental transformations were visible in the Lord's body. All the devotees were struck with wonder to see such a sight.
purport: The eight ecstatic symptoms are the state of being stunned, perspiration, standing of the hairs on end, faltering of the voice, trembling, fading of the body's color, tears and devastation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.1
description: The ocean of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa is very difficult to understand, even for such demigods as Lord Brahmā. By enacting His pastimes, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu submerged Himself in that ocean, and His heart was absorbed in that love. Thus He exhibited in various ways the exalted position of transcendental love for Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> durgame kṛṣṇa-bhāvābdhau
> nimagnonmagna-cetasā
> gaureṇa hariṇā prema-
> maryādā bhūri darśitā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:durgame]]---very difficult to understand; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:a:abdhau]]---in the ocean of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nimagna]]---submerged; [[synonyms:u:unmagna]]-[[synonyms:c:cetasā]]---His heart being absorbed; [[synonyms:g:gaureṇa]]---by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hariṇā]]---by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:m:maryādā]]---the exalted position of transcendental love; [[synonyms:b:bhūri]]---in various ways; [[synonyms:d:darśitā]]---was exhibited.
translation: The ocean of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa is very difficult to understand, even for such demigods as Lord Brahmā. By enacting His pastimes, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu submerged Himself in that ocean, and His heart was absorbed in that love. Thus He exhibited in various ways the exalted position of transcendental love for Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.10
description: Just then, the upala-bhoga ceremony of Lord Jagannātha concluded, and the devotees who had accompanied Lord Caitanya to the temple brought Him back home.
text:
> hena-kāle īśvarera upala-bhoga sarila
> bhakta-gaṇa mahāprabhure ghare lañā āila
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:ī:īśvarera]]---of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:u:upala]]-[[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---the //upala-bhoga// ceremony; [[synonyms:s:sarila]]---was finished; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---home; [[synonyms:l:lañā]] [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---brought.
