translation: Just then, the upala-bhoga ceremony of Lord Jagannātha concluded, and the devotees who had accompanied Lord Caitanya to the temple brought Him back home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.11
description: That night, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was attended by Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya. Keeping His hands around their necks, the Lord began to lament.
text:
> svarūpa, rāmānanda,---ei dui-jana lañā
> vilāpa karena duṅhāra kaṇṭhete dhariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---these two personalities; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---with; [[synonyms:v:vilāpa]] [[synonyms:k:karena]]---laments; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]]---of both; [[synonyms:k:kaṇṭhete]]---the necks; [[synonyms:d:dhariyā]]---holding.
translation: That night, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was attended by Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya. Keeping His hands around their necks, the Lord began to lament.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.12
description: When Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī was very agitated due to feeling great separation from Kṛṣṇa, She spoke a verse to Viśākhā explaining the cause of Her great anxiety and restlessness.
text:
> kṛṣṇera viyoge rādhāra utkaṇṭhita mana
> viśākhāre kahe āpana utkaṇṭhā-kāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---from Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:viyoge]]---in separation; [[synonyms:r:rādhāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:u:utkaṇṭhita]]---very agitated; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:v:viśākhāre]]---to Viśākhā; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---spoke; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]---own; [[synonyms:u:utkaṇṭhā]]-[[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause of great anxiety and restlessness.
translation: When Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī was very agitated due to feeling great separation from Kṛṣṇa, She spoke a verse to Viśākhā explaining the cause of Her great anxiety and restlessness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.13
description: Reciting that verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu expressed His burning emotions. Then, with great lamentation, He explained the verse to Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya.
text:
> sei śloka paḍi' āpane kare manastāpa
> ślokera artha śunāya duṅhāre kariyā vilāpa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---that verse; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:t:tāpa]]---burning of the mind; [[synonyms:ś:ślokera]]---of the verse; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:ś:śunāya]]---causes to hear; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāre]]---both; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:v:vilāpa]]---lamenting.
translation: Reciting that verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu expressed His burning emotions. Then, with great lamentation, He explained the verse to Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.14
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said:" 'Though the hearts of the gopīs are like high-standing hills, they are inundated by the waves of the nectarean ocean of Kṛṣṇa's beauty. His sweet voice enters their ears and gives them transcendental bliss. The touch of His body is cooler than millions and millions of moons together, and the nectar of His bodily fragrance overfloods the entire world. O My dear friend, that Kṛṣṇa, who is the son of Nanda Mahārāja and whose lips are exactly like nectar, is attracting My five senses by force.'
text:
> saundaryāmṛta-sindhu-bhaṅga-lalanā-cittādri-saṁplāvakaḥ
> karṇānandi-sanarma-ramya-vacanaḥ koṭīndu-śītāṅgakaḥ
> saurabhyāmṛta-samplavāvṛta-jagat pīyūṣa-ramyādharaḥ
> śrī-gopendra-sutaḥ sa karṣati balāt pañcendriyāṇy āli me
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saundarya]]---His beauty; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:s:sindhu]]---of the ocean of nectar; [[synonyms:b:bhaṅga]]---by the waves; [[synonyms:l:lalanā]]---of women; [[synonyms:c:citta]]---the hearts; [[synonyms:a:adri]]---hills; [[synonyms:s:saṁplāvakaḥ]]---inundating; [[synonyms:k:karṇa]]---through the ears; [[synonyms:ā:ānandi]]---giving pleasure; [[synonyms:s:sanarma]]---joyful; [[synonyms:r:ramya]]---beautiful; [[synonyms:v:vacanaḥ]]---whose voice; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:i:indu]]---than ten million moons; [[synonyms:ś:śīta]]---more cooling; [[synonyms:a:aṅgakaḥ]]---whose body; [[synonyms:s:saurabhya]]---His fragrance; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---of nectar; [[synonyms:s:samplava]]---by the inundation; [[synonyms:ā:āvṛta]]---covered; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the entire universe; [[synonyms:p:pīyūṣa]]---nectar; [[synonyms:r:ramya]]---beautiful; [[synonyms:a:adharaḥ]]---whose lips; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:i:indra]]---of Nanda Mahārāja; [[synonyms:s:sutaḥ]]---the son; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:k:karṣati]]---attracts; [[synonyms:b:balāt]]---by force; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:i:indriyāṇi]]---the five senses; [[synonyms:ā:āli]]---O dear friend; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said:" 'Though the hearts of the gopīs are like high-standing hills, they are inundated by the waves of the nectarean ocean of Kṛṣṇa's beauty. His sweet voice enters their ears and gives them transcendental bliss. The touch of His body is cooler than millions and millions of moons together, and the nectar of His bodily fragrance overfloods the entire world. O My dear friend, that Kṛṣṇa, who is the son of Nanda Mahārāja and whose lips are exactly like nectar, is attracting My five senses by force.'
purport: This verse is found in //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (8.3).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.15
description: "Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa's beauty, the sound of His words and the vibration of His flute, His touch, His fragrance and the taste of His lips are full of an indescribable sweetness. When all these features attract My five senses at once, My senses all ride together on the single horse of My mind but want to go in five different directions.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-rūpa-śabda-sparśa, saurabhya-adhara-rasa,
> yāra mādhurya kahana nā yāya
> dekhi' lobhe pañca-jana, eka aśva---mora mana,
> caḍi' pañca pāṅca-dike dhāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---beauty; [[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---sound; [[synonyms:s:sparśa]]---touch; [[synonyms:s:saurabhya]]---fragrance; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]---of lips; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---taste; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---sweetness; [[synonyms:k:kahana]]---describing; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---is not possible; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:l:lobhe]]---in greed; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---five men; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:a:aśva]]---horse; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:c:caḍi']]---riding on; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]---all five; [[synonyms:p:pāṅca]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---in five directions; [[synonyms:d:dhāya]]---run.
translation: "Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa's beauty, the sound of His words and the vibration of His flute, His touch, His fragrance and the taste of His lips are full of an indescribable sweetness. When all these features attract My five senses at once, My senses all ride together on the single horse of My mind but want to go in five different directions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.16
description: "O My dear friend, please hear the cause of My misery. My five senses are actually extravagant rogues. They know very well that Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but they still want to plunder Kṛṣṇa's property.
text:
> sakhi he, śuna mora duḥkhera kāraṇa
> mora pañcendriya-gaṇa, mahā-lampaṭa dasyu-gaṇa,
> sabe kahe,---hara' para-dhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---My dear friend; [[synonyms:h:he]]---O; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:d:duḥkhera]] [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause of unhappiness; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:i:indriya]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---five senses of perception; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]---very; [[synonyms:l:lampaṭa]]---extravagant; [[synonyms:d:dasyu]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---rogues; [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---they all say; [[synonyms:h:hara']]---plunder; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---another's property.
translation: "O My dear friend, please hear the cause of My misery. My five senses are actually extravagant rogues. They know very well that Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but they still want to plunder Kṛṣṇa's property.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.17
description: "My mind is just like a single horse being ridden by the five senses of perception, headed by sight. Each sense wants to ride that horse, and thus they pull My mind in five directions simultaneously. In what direction will it go? If they all pull at one time, certainly the horse will lose its life. How can I tolerate this atrocity?
text:
> eka aśva eka-kṣaṇe, pāṅca pāṅca dike ṭāne,
> eka mana kon dike yāya?
> eka-kāle sabe ṭāne, gela ghoḍāra parāṇe,
> ei duḥkha sahana nā yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:a:aśva]]---horse; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---at one time; [[synonyms:p:pāṅca]]---five men; [[synonyms:p:pāṅca]] [[synonyms:d:dike]]---in five directions; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭāne]]---pull; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:k:kon]] [[synonyms:d:dike]]---in what direction; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---will go; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at one time; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭāne]]---pull; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---will go; [[synonyms:g:ghoḍāra]]---of the horse; [[synonyms:p:parāṇe]]---life; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:s:sahana]]---tolerating; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---is not possible.
translation: "My mind is just like a single horse being ridden by the five senses of perception, headed by sight. Each sense wants to ride that horse, and thus they pull My mind in five directions simultaneously. In what direction will it go? If they all pull at one time, certainly the horse will lose its life. How can I tolerate this atrocity?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.18
description: "My dear friend, if you say, 'Just try to control Your senses,' what shall I say? I cannot become angry at My senses. Is it their fault? Kṛṣṇa's beauty, sounds, touch, fragrance and taste are by nature extremely attractive. These five features are attracting My senses, and each wants to drag My mind in a different direction. Thus the life of My mind is in great danger, just like a horse ridden in five directions at once. Thus I am also in danger of dying.
text:
> indriye nā kari roṣa, iṅhā-sabāra kāhāṅ doṣa,
> kṛṣṇa-rūpādira mahā ākarṣaṇa
> rūpādi pāṅca pāṅce ṭāne, gela ghoḍāra parāṇe,
> mora dehe nā rahe jīvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:indriye]]---at the senses; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:k:kari]] [[synonyms:r:roṣa]]---I can be angry; [[synonyms:i:iṅhā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---fault; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādira]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa's beauty, sounds, touch, fragrance and taste; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]---very great; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaṇa]]---attraction; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the beauty and so on; [[synonyms:p:pāṅca]]---five; [[synonyms:p:pāṅce]]---the five senses; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭāne]]---drag; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---is going away; [[synonyms:g:ghoḍāra]]---of the horse; [[synonyms:p:parāṇe]]---life; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:d:dehe]]---in the body; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---life.
translation: "My dear friend, if you say, 'Just try to control Your senses,' what shall I say? I cannot become angry at My senses. Is it their fault? Kṛṣṇa's beauty, sounds, touch, fragrance and taste are by nature extremely attractive. These five features are attracting My senses, and each wants to drag My mind in a different direction. Thus the life of My mind is in great danger, just like a horse ridden in five directions at once. Thus I am also in danger of dying.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.19
description: "The consciousness of each woman within the three worlds is certainly like a high hill, but the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's beauty is like an ocean. Even a drop of water from that ocean can flood the entire world and submerge all the high hills of consciousness.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-rūpāmṛta-sindhu, tāhāra taraṅga-bindu,
> eka-bindu jagat ḍubāya
> trijagate yata nārī, tāra citta-ucca-giri,
> tāhā ḍubāi āge uṭhi' dhāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---of Kṛṣṇa's transcendental beauty; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:s:sindhu]]---the ocean of nectar; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:t:taraṅga]]-[[synonyms:b:bindu]]---a drop of a wave; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:b:bindu]]---one drop; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the whole world; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍubāya]]---can flood; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:j:jagate]]---in the three worlds; [[synonyms:y:yata]] [[synonyms:n:nārī]]---all women; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:c:citta]]---their consciousness; [[synonyms:u:ucca]]-[[synonyms:g:giri]]---high hills; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍubāi]]---drowning; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---forward; [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---raising; [[synonyms:d:dhāya]]---runs.
translation: "The consciousness of each woman within the three worlds is certainly like a high hill, but the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's beauty is like an ocean. Even a drop of water from that ocean can flood the entire world and submerge all the high hills of consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.2
description: All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the Supreme Personality of Godhead! All glories to Lord Nityānanda, whose body is always filled with transcendental bliss!
text:
> jaya jaya śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya adhīśvara
> jaya nityānanda pūrṇānanda-kalevara
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:adhīśvara]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---to Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---filled with transcendental pleasure; [[synonyms:k:kalevara]]---His body.
translation: All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the Supreme Personality of Godhead! All glories to Lord Nityānanda, whose body is always filled with transcendental bliss!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.20
description: "The sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's joking words plays indescribable havoc with the hearts of all women. His words bind a woman's ear to the qualities of their sweetness. Thus there is a tug-of-war, and the life of the ear departs.
text:
> kṛṣṇera vacana-mādhurī, nānā-rasa-narma-dhārī,
> tāra anyāya kathana nā yāya
> jagatera nārīra kāṇe, mādhurī-guṇe bāndhi' ṭāne,
> ṭānāṭāni kāṇera prāṇa yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhurī]]---the sweetness of speaking; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:n:narma]]-[[synonyms:d:dhārī]]---full of joking words; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:a:anyāya]]---atrocities; [[synonyms:k:kathana]]---description; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---cannot be made; [[synonyms:j:jagatera]]---of the world; [[synonyms:n:nārīra]]---of women; [[synonyms:k:kāṇe]]---in the ear; [[synonyms:m:mādhurī]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---to the attributes of sweetness; [[synonyms:b:bāndhi']]---binding; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭāne]]---pulls; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭānāṭāni]]---tug-of-war; [[synonyms:k:kāṇera]]---of the ear; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---the life departs.
translation: "The sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's joking words plays indescribable havoc with the hearts of all women. His words bind a woman's ear to the qualities of their sweetness. Thus there is a tug-of-war, and the life of the ear departs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.21
description: "Kṛṣṇa's transcendental body is so cool that it cannot be compared even to sandalwood pulp or to millions upon millions of moons. It expertly attracts the breasts of all women, which resemble high hills. Indeed, the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa attracts the minds of all women within the three worlds.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-aṅga suśītala, ki kahimu tāra bala,
> chaṭāya jine koṭīndu-candana
> saśaila nārīra vakṣa, tāhā ākarṣite dakṣa,
> ākarṣaye nārī-gaṇa-mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the body of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:ś:śītala]]---very cool; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:k:kahimu]]---what shall I say; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:b:bala]]---the strength; [[synonyms:c:chaṭāya]]---by the rays; [[synonyms:j:jine]]---surpasses; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:i:indu]]---millions upon millions of moons; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood pulp; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śaila]]---like raised hills; [[synonyms:n:nārīra]]---of a woman; [[synonyms:v:vakṣa]]---breasts; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣite]]---to attract; [[synonyms:d:dakṣa]]---very expert; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaye]]---attracts; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds of all women.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa's transcendental body is so cool that it cannot be compared even to sandalwood pulp or to millions upon millions of moons. It expertly attracts the breasts of all women, which resemble high hills. Indeed, the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa attracts the minds of all women within the three worlds.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.22
description: "The fragrance of Kṛṣṇa's body is more maddening than the aroma of musk, and it surpasses the fragrance of the bluish lotus flower. It enters the nostrils of all the women of the world and, making a nest there, thus attracts them.
text:
> kṛṣṇāṅga---saurabhya-bhara, mṛga-mada-mada-hara,
> nīlotpalera hare garva-dhana
> jagat-nārīra nāsā, tāra bhitara pāte vāsā,
> nārī-gaṇe kare ākarṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the body of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:saurabhya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhara]]---full of fragrance; [[synonyms:m:mṛga]]-[[synonyms:m:mada]]---of musk; [[synonyms:m:mada]]-[[synonyms:h:hara]]---intoxicating power; [[synonyms:n:nīlotpalera]]---of the bluish lotus flower; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---takes away; [[synonyms:g:garva]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---the pride of the treasure; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:n:nārīra]]---of the women in the world; [[synonyms:n:nāsā]]---nostrils; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:b:bhitara]]---within them; [[synonyms:p:pāte]] [[synonyms:v:vāsā]]---constructs a residence; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---women; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaṇa]]---attracts.
translation: "The fragrance of Kṛṣṇa's body is more maddening than the aroma of musk, and it surpasses the fragrance of the bluish lotus flower. It enters the nostrils of all the women of the world and, making a nest there, thus attracts them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.23
description: "Kṛṣṇa's lips are so sweet when combined with the camphor of His gentle smile that they attract the minds of all women, forcing them to give up all other attractions. If the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's smile is unobtainable, great mental difficulties and lamentation result. That sweetness is the only wealth of the gopīs of Vṛndāvana."
text:
> kṛṣṇera adharāmṛta, tāte karpūra manda-smita,
> sva-mādhurye hare nārīra mana
> anyatra chāḍāya lobha, nā pāile mane kṣobha,
> vraja-nārī-gaṇera mūla-dhana"
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---the sweetness of the lips; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---with that; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]---camphor; [[synonyms:m:manda]]-[[synonyms:s:smita]]---gentle smile; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhurye]]---by His sweetness; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:n:nārīra]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds of all women; [[synonyms:a:anyatra]]---anywhere else; [[synonyms:c:chāḍāya]]---vanquishes; [[synonyms:l:lobha]]---greed; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāile]]---without getting; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:k:kṣobha]]---great agitation; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:n:nārī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of all the //gopīs// of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:m:mūla]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---wealth.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa's lips are so sweet when combined with the camphor of His gentle smile that they attract the minds of all women, forcing them to give up all other attractions. If the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's smile is unobtainable, great mental difficulties and lamentation result. That sweetness is the only wealth of the gopīs of Vṛndāvana."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.24
description: After speaking in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu caught hold of the necks of Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara. Then the Lord said, "My dear friends, please listen to Me. What shall I do? Where shall I go? Where can I go to get Kṛṣṇa? Please, both of you, tell Me how I can find Him."
text:
> eta kahi' gaurahari, dui-janāra kaṇṭha dhari',
> kahe,---'śuna, svarūpa-rāmarāya
> kāhāṅ karoṅ, kāhāṅ yāṅa, kāhāṅ gele kṛṣṇa pāṅa,
> duṅhe more kaha se upāya'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---saying this; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:janāra]]---of the two persons; [[synonyms:k:kaṇṭha]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching the necks; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---please hear; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:k:karoṅ]]---what shall I do; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:y:yāṅa]]---where shall I go; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:g:gele]]---going where; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:p:pāṅa]]---I can get Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:duṅhe]]---both of you; [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please say; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---such a means.
translation: After speaking in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu caught hold of the necks of Rāmānanda Rāya and Svarūpa Dāmodara. Then the Lord said, "My dear friends, please listen to Me. What shall I do? Where shall I go? Where can I go to get Kṛṣṇa? Please, both of you, tell Me how I can find Him."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.25
description: Thus absorbed in transcendental pain, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lamented day after day in the company of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya.
text:
> ei-mata gaura-prabhu prati dine-dine
> vilāpa karena svarūpa-rāmānanda-sane
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prati]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---day after day; [[synonyms:v:vilāpa]] [[synonyms:k:karena]]---laments; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---in the company of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya.
translation: Thus absorbed in transcendental pain, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lamented day after day in the company of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.26
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī would sing appropriate songs, and Rāmānanda Rāya would recite suitable verses to enhance the ecstatic mood of the Lord. In this way they were able to pacify Him.
text:
> sei dui-jana prabhure kare āśvāsana
> svarūpa gāya, rāya kare śloka paṭhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---two persons; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:ā:āśvāsana]]---pacification; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]] [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara sings; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:p:paṭhana]]---recitation of verses.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī would sing appropriate songs, and Rāmānanda Rāya would recite suitable verses to enhance the ecstatic mood of the Lord. In this way they were able to pacify Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.27
description: The Lord especially liked to hear Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura's Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta, the poetry of Vidyāpati and Śrī Gīta-govinda by Jayadeva Gosvāmī. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu felt great pleasure in His heart when His associates chanted verses from these books.
text:
> karṇāmṛta, vidyāpati, śrī-gīta-govinda
> ihāra śloka-gīte prabhura karāya ānanda
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:karṇāmṛta]]---the book //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta//; [[synonyms:v:vidyāpati]]---the author Vidyāpati; [[synonyms:ś:śri]]-[[synonyms:g:gīta]]-[[synonyms:g:govinda]]---the book //Śrī Gīta-govinda// by Jayadeva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of these; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]-[[synonyms:g:gīte]]---verses and songs; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---create; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---happiness.
translation: The Lord especially liked to hear Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura's Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta, the poetry of Vidyāpati and Śrī Gīta-govinda by Jayadeva Gosvāmī. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu felt great pleasure in His heart when His associates chanted verses from these books.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.28
description: One day, while going to the beach by the sea, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu suddenly saw a flower garden.
text:
> eka-dina mahāprabhu samudra-tīre yāite
> puṣpera udyāna tathā dekhena ācambite
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:samudra]]-[[synonyms:t:tīre]]---to the seashore; [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---while going; [[synonyms:p:puṣpera]] [[synonyms:u:udyāna]]---a flower garden; [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---there; [[synonyms:d:dekhena]]---sees; [[synonyms:ā:ācambite]]---suddenly.
translation: One day, while going to the beach by the sea, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu suddenly saw a flower garden.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.29
description: Lord Caitanya mistook that garden for Vṛndāvana and very quickly entered it. Absorbed in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa, He wandered throughout the garden, searching for Him.
text:
> vṛndāvana-bhrame tāhāṅ paśilā dhāñā
> premāveśe bule tāhāṅ kṛṣṇa anveṣiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhrame]]---taking it for Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:p:paśilā]]---entered; [[synonyms:d:dhāñā]]---running; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bule]]---wanders; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:anveṣiyā]]---searching for.
translation: Lord Caitanya mistook that garden for Vṛndāvana and very quickly entered it. Absorbed in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa, He wandered throughout the garden, searching for Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.3
description: All glories to Śrī Advaita Ācārya, who is very dear to Lord Caitanya! And all glories to the devotees of the Lord, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura!
text:
> jayādvaitācārya kṛṣṇa-caitanya-priyatama
> jaya śrīvāsa-ādi prabhura bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---to Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:priya]]-[[synonyms:t:tama]]---very dear; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---to the devotees.
translation: All glories to Śrī Advaita Ācārya, who is very dear to Lord Caitanya! And all glories to the devotees of the Lord, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.30
description: After Kṛṣṇa disappeared with Rādhārāṇī during the rāsa dance, the gopīs wandered in the forest looking for Him. In the same way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wandered in that garden by the sea.
text:
> rāse rādhā lañā kṛṣṇa antardhāna kailā
> pāche sakhī-gaṇa yaiche cāhi' beḍāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāse]]---in the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:antardhāna]] [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---disappeared; [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---afterward; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:c:cāhi']]---looking; [[synonyms:b:beḍāilā]]---wandered.
translation: After Kṛṣṇa disappeared with Rādhārāṇī during the rāsa dance, the gopīs wandered in the forest looking for Him. In the same way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wandered in that garden by the sea.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.31
description: Absorbed in the ecstatic mood of the gopīs, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wandered here and there. He began to inquire after Kṛṣṇa by quoting verses to all the trees and creepers.
text:
> sei bhāvāveśe prabhu prati-taru-latā
> śloka paḍi' paḍi' cāhi' bule yathā tathā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:t:taru]]-[[synonyms:l:latā]]---each tree and creeper; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting verses; [[synonyms:c:cāhi']]---inquiring; [[synonyms:b:bule]]---wanders; [[synonyms:y:yathā]] [[synonyms:t:tathā]]---here and there.
translation: Absorbed in the ecstatic mood of the gopīs, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wandered here and there. He began to inquire after Kṛṣṇa by quoting verses to all the trees and creepers.
purport: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then quoted the following three verses from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.30.9,7,8).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.32
description: "(The gopīs said:) 'O cūta tree, priyāla tree, pasana, āsana and kovidāra! O jambu tree, O arka tree, O bel, bakula and mango! O kadamba tree, O nīpa tree and all other trees living on the bank of the Yamunā for the welfare of others, please let us know where Kṛṣṇa has gone. We have lost our minds and are almost dead.
text:
> cūta-priyāla-panasāsana-kovidāra-
> jambv-arka-bilva-bakulāmra-kadamba-nīpāḥ
> ye 'nye parārtha-bhavakā yamunopakūlāḥ
> śaṁsantu kṛṣṇa-padavīṁ rahitātmanāṁ naḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cūta]]---O //cūta// tree (a kind of mango tree); [[synonyms:p:priyāla]]---O //priyāla// tree; [[synonyms:p:panasa]]---O jackfruit tree; [[synonyms:ā:āsana]]---O //āsana// tree; [[synonyms:k:kovidāra]]---O //kovidāra// tree; [[synonyms:j:jambu]]---O //jambu// tree; [[synonyms:a:arka]]---O //arka// tree; [[synonyms:b:bilva]]---O belfruit tree; [[synonyms:b:bakula]]---O //bakula// tree; [[synonyms:ā:āmra]]---O mango tree; [[synonyms:k:kadamba]]---O //kadamba// tree; [[synonyms:n:nīpāḥ]]---O //nīpa// tree; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:a:anye]]---others; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhavakāḥ]]---very beneficial to others; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]-[[synonyms:u:upakūlāḥ]]---on the bank of the Yamunā; [[synonyms:ś:śaṁsantu]]---please tell; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:padavīm]]---where Kṛṣṇa has gone; [[synonyms:r:rahita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ātmanām]]---who have lost our minds; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---us.
translation: "(The gopīs said:) 'O cūta tree, priyāla tree, pasana, āsana and kovidāra! O jambu tree, O arka tree, O bel, bakula and mango! O kadamba tree, O nīpa tree and all other trees living on the bank of the Yamunā for the welfare of others, please let us know where Kṛṣṇa has gone. We have lost our minds and are almost dead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.33
description: " 'O all-auspicious tulasī plant, you are very dear to Govinda's lotus feet, and He is very dear to you. Have you seen Kṛṣṇa walking here wearing a garland of your leaves, surrounded by a swarm of bumblebees?
text:
> kaccit tulasi kalyāṇi
> govinda-caraṇa-priye
> saha tvāli-kulair bibhrad
> dṛṣṭas te 'ti-priyo 'cyutaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kaccit]]---whether; [[synonyms:t:tulasi]]---O //tulasī// plant; [[synonyms:k:kalyāṇi]]---all-auspicious; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---to Govinda's lotus feet; [[synonyms:p:priye]]---very dear; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:t:tvā]]---you; [[synonyms:a:ali]]-[[synonyms:k:kulaiḥ]]---bumblebees; [[synonyms:b:bibhrat]]---bearing; [[synonyms:d:dṛṣṭaḥ]]---has been seen; [[synonyms:t:te]]---your; [[synonyms:a:ati]]-[[synonyms:p:priyaḥ]]---very dear; [[synonyms:a:acyutaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: “ 'O all-auspicious tulasī plant, you are very dear to Govinda's lotus feet, and He is very dear to you. Have you seen Kṛṣṇa walking here wearing a garland of your leaves, surrounded by a swarm of bumblebees?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.34
description: " 'O plants of mālatī flowers, mallikā flowers, jātī and yūthikā flowers, have you seen Kṛṣṇa passing this way, touching you with His hand to give you pleasure?' "
text:
> mālaty adarśi vaḥ kaccin
> mallike jāti yūthike
> prītiṁ vo janayan yātaḥ
> kara-sparśena mādhavaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mālati]]---O plant of //mālatī// flowers; [[synonyms:a:adarśi]]---was seen; [[synonyms:v:vaḥ]]---by you; [[synonyms:k:kaccit]]---whether; [[synonyms:m:mallike]]---O plant of //mallikā// flowers; [[synonyms:j:jāti]]---O plant of //jātī// flowers; [[synonyms:y:yūthike]]---O plant of //yūthikā// flowers; [[synonyms:p:prītim]]---pleasure; [[synonyms:v:vaḥ]]---your; [[synonyms:j:janayan]]---creating; [[synonyms:y:yātaḥ]]---passed by; [[synonyms:k:kara]]-[[synonyms:s:sparśena]]---by the touch of His hand; [[synonyms:m:mādhavaḥ]]---Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
translation: “ 'O plants of mālatī flowers, mallikā flowers, jātī and yūthikā flowers, have you seen Kṛṣṇa passing this way, touching you with His hand to give you pleasure?' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.35
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued: " 'O mango tree, O jackfruit tree, O piyāla, jambu and kovidāra trees, you are all inhabitants of a holy place. Therefore kindly act for the welfare of others.
text:
> āmra, panasa, piyāla, jambu, kovidāra
> tīrtha-vāsī sabe, kara para-upakāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmra]]---O mango tree; [[synonyms:p:panasa]]---O jackfruit tree; [[synonyms:p:piyāla]]---O //piyāla// tree; [[synonyms:j:jambu]]---O //jambu// tree; [[synonyms:k:kovidāra]]---O //kovidāra// tree; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---inhabitants of a holy place; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---please do; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:u:upakāra]]---others' benefit.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued: " 'O mango tree, O jackfruit tree, O piyāla, jambu and kovidāra trees, you are all inhabitants of a holy place. Therefore kindly act for the welfare of others.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.36
description: " 'Have you seen Kṛṣṇa coming this way? Kindly tell us which way He has gone and save our lives.'
text:
> kṛṣṇa tomāra ihāṅ āilā, pāilā daraśana?
> kṛṣṇera uddeśa kahi' rākhaha jīvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:pāilā]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---you have seen; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:u:uddeśa]]---the direction; [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---by telling; [[synonyms:r:rākhaha]] [[synonyms:j:jīvana]]---kindly save our lives.
translation: “ 'Have you seen Kṛṣṇa coming this way? Kindly tell us which way He has gone and save our lives.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.37
description: "When the trees did not reply, the gopīs guessed,'Since all of these trees belong to the male class, all of them must be friends of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> uttara nā pāñā punaḥ kare anumāna
> ei saba---puruṣa-jāti, kṛṣṇera sakhāra samāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uttara]]---answer; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:a:anumāna]]---guess; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all these; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:j:jāti]]---belonging to the male class; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sakhāra]] [[synonyms:s:samāna]]---as good as friends.
translation: "When the trees did not reply, the gopīs guessed,'Since all of these trees belong to the male class, all of them must be friends of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.38
description: " 'Why should the trees tell us where Kṛṣṇa has gone? Let us rather inquire from the creepers; they are female and therefore are like friends to us.
text:
> e kene kahibe kṛṣṇera uddeśa āmāya?
> e---strī-jāti latā, āmāra sakhī-prāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:e]]---these; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:k:kahibe]]---will say; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:u:uddeśa]]---direction; [[synonyms:ā:āmāya]]---to us; [[synonyms:e:e]]---these; [[synonyms:s:strī]]-[[synonyms:j:jāti]]---belonging to the class of women; [[synonyms:l:latā]]---creepers; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---our; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]-[[synonyms:p:prāya]]---like friends.
translation: “ 'Why should the trees tell us where Kṛṣṇa has gone? Let us rather inquire from the creepers; they are female and therefore are like friends to us.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.39
description: " 'They will certainly tell us where Kṛṣṇa has gone, since they have seen Him personally.' Guessing in this way, the gopīs inquired from the plants and creepers, headed by tulasī.
text:
> avaśya kahibe,---pāñāche kṛṣṇera darśane
> eta anumāni' puche tulasy-ādi-gaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:k:kahibe]]---they will say; [[synonyms:p:pāñāche]]---they have gotten; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:darśane]]---audience; [[synonyms:e:eta]]---this; [[synonyms:a:anumāni']]---guessing; [[synonyms:p:puche]]---inquire from; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the plants and creepers, headed by the //tulasī// plant.
translation: “ 'They will certainly tell us where Kṛṣṇa has gone, since they have seen Him personally.' Guessing in this way, the gopīs inquired from the plants and creepers, headed by tulasī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.4
description: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu forgot Himself throughout the entire day and night, being merged in an ocean of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> ei-mata mahāprabhu rātri-divase
> ātma-sphūrti nāhi kṛṣṇa-bhāvāveśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:divase]]---night and day; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:s:sphūrti]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---forgot Himself; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---being merged in ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu forgot Himself throughout the entire day and night, being merged in an ocean of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.40
description: " 'O tulasī! O mālatī! O yūthī, mādhavī and mallikā! Kṛṣṇa is very dear to you. Therefore He must have come near you.
text:
> "tulasi, mālati, yūthi, mādhavi, mallike
> tomāra priya kṛṣṇa āilā tomāra antike?
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tulasi]]---O //tulasī//; [[synonyms:m:mālati]]---O //mālatī//; [[synonyms:y:yūthi]]---O //yūthī//; [[synonyms:m:mādhavi]]---O //mādhavī//; [[synonyms:m:mallike]]---O //mallikā//; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:p:priya]]---very dear; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:a:antike]]---near you.
translation: “ 'O tulasī! O mālatī! O yūthī, mādhavī and mallikā! Kṛṣṇa is very dear to you. Therefore He must have come near you.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.41
description: " 'You are all just like dear friends to us. Kindly tell us which way Kṛṣṇa has gone and save our lives.'
text:
> tumi-saba---hao āmāra sakhīra samāna
> kṛṣṇoddeśa kahi' sabe rākhaha parāṇa"
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of you; [[synonyms:h:hao]]---are; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---our; [[synonyms:s:sakhīra]]---dear friends; [[synonyms:s:samāna]]---equal to; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:u:uddeśa]]---the direction in which Kṛṣṇa has gone; [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---speaking; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of you; [[synonyms:r:rākhaha]] [[synonyms:p:parāṇa]]---save our lives.
translation: “ 'You are all just like dear friends to us. Kindly tell us which way Kṛṣṇa has gone and save our lives.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.42
description: "When they still received no reply, the gopīs thought, 'These plants are all Kṛṣṇa's maidservants, and out of fear they will not speak to us.'
text:
> uttara nā pāñā punaḥ bhāvena antare
> 'eha---kṛṣṇa-dāsī, bhaye nā kahe āmāre'
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uttara]]---reply; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:b:bhāvena]]---think; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---within their minds; [[synonyms:e:eha]]---these; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsī]]---maidservants of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---out of fear; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---do not speak; [[synonyms:ā:āmāre]]---to us.
translation: "When they still received no reply, the gopīs thought, 'These plants are all Kṛṣṇa's maidservants, and out of fear they will not speak to us.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.43
description: "The gopīs then came upon a group of she-deer. Smelling the aroma of Kṛṣṇa's body and seeing the faces of the deer, the gopīs inquired from them to ascertain if Kṛṣṇa was nearby.
text:
> āge mṛgī-gaṇa dekhi' kṛṣṇāṅga-gandha pāñā
> tāra mukha dekhi' puchena nirṇaya kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:m:mṛgī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the deer; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:g:gandha]]---the aroma of Kṛṣṇa's body; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---their faces; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:puchena]]---inquire; [[synonyms:n:nirṇaya]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---making certain.
translation: "The gopīs then came upon a group of she-deer. Smelling the aroma of Kṛṣṇa's body and seeing the faces of the deer, the gopīs inquired from them to ascertain if Kṛṣṇa was nearby.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.44
description: " 'O wife of the deer, Lord Kṛṣṇa has been embracing His beloved, and thus the kuṅkuma powder on Her raised breasts has covered His garland of kunda flowers. The fragrance of this garland is flowing here. O my dear friend, have you seen Kṛṣṇa passing this way with His dearmost companion, increasing the pleasure of the eyes of all of you?'
text:
> apy eṇa-patny upagataḥ priyayeha gātrais
> tanvan dṛśāṁ sakhi sunirvṛtim acyuto vaḥ
> kāntāṅga-saṅga-kuca-kuṅkuma-rañjitāyāḥ
> kunda-srajaḥ kula-pater iha vāti gandhaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:api]]---whether; [[synonyms:e:eṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:patnī]]---O she-deer; [[synonyms:u:upagataḥ]]---has come; [[synonyms:p:priyayā]]---along with His dearmost companion; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---here; [[synonyms:g:gātraiḥ]]---by the bodily limbs; [[synonyms:t:tanvan]]---increasing; [[synonyms:d:dṛśām]]---of the eyes; [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---O my dear friend; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:n:nirvṛtim]]---happiness; [[synonyms:a:acyutaḥ]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vaḥ]]---of all of you; [[synonyms:k:kānta]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---with the body of the beloved; [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---by association; [[synonyms:k:kuca]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṅkuma]]---with //kuṅkuma// powder from the breasts; [[synonyms:r:rañjitāyāḥ]]---colored; [[synonyms:k:kunda]]-[[synonyms:s:srajaḥ]]---of the garland of //kunda// flowers; [[synonyms:k:kula]]-[[synonyms:p:pateḥ]]---of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---here; [[synonyms:v:vāti]]---flows; [[synonyms:g:gandhaḥ]]---the fragrance.
translation: “ 'O wife of the deer, Lord Kṛṣṇa has been embracing His beloved, and thus the kuṅkuma powder on Her raised breasts has covered His garland of kunda flowers. The fragrance of this garland is flowing here. O my dear friend, have you seen Kṛṣṇa passing this way with His dearmost companion, increasing the pleasure of the eyes of all of you?'
purport: This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.30.11).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.45
description: " 'O dear doe, Śrī Kṛṣṇa is always very pleased to give you pleasure. Kindly inform us whether He passed this way in the company of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. We think They must certainly have come this way.
text:
> "kaha, mṛgi, rādhā-saha śrī-kṛṣṇa sarvathā
> tomāya sukha dite āilā? nāhika anyathā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please say; [[synonyms:m:mṛgi]]---O she-deer; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:s:saha]]---with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sarvathā]]---in all respects; [[synonyms:t:tomāya]]---to you; [[synonyms:s:sukha]] [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to give pleasure; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---did come; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]] [[synonyms:a:anyathā]]---it is certain.
translation: “ 'O dear doe, Śrī Kṛṣṇa is always very pleased to give you pleasure. Kindly inform us whether He passed this way in the company of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. We think They must certainly have come this way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.46
description: " 'We are not outsiders. Being very dear friends of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, we can perceive the bodily fragrance of Kṛṣṇa from a distance.
text:
> rādhā-priya-sakhī āmarā, nahi bahiraṅga
> dūra haite jāni tāra yaiche aṅga-gandha
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:p:priya]]-[[synonyms:s:sakhī]]---very dear friends; [[synonyms:ā:āmarā]]---we; [[synonyms:n:nahi]] [[synonyms:b:bahiraṅga]]---are not outsiders; [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from a distance; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---we know; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:g:gandha]]---bodily fragrance.
translation: “ 'We are not outsiders. Being very dear friends of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, we can perceive the bodily fragrance of Kṛṣṇa from a distance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.47
description: " 'Kṛṣṇa has been embracing Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and the kuṅkuma powder on Her breasts has mixed with the garland of kunda flowers decorating His body. The fragrance of the garland has scented the entire atmosphere.
text:
> rādhā-aṅga-saṅge kuca-kuṅkuma-bhūṣita
> kṛṣṇa-kunda-mālā-gandhe vāyu---suvāsita
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---the body of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---by embracing; [[synonyms:k:kuca]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṅkuma]]---with the //kuṅkuma// from the breasts; [[synonyms:b:bhūṣita]]---decorated; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kunda]]-[[synonyms:m:mālā]]---of the garland of //kunda// flowers; [[synonyms:g:gandhe]]---by the fragrance; [[synonyms:v:vāyu]]---the air; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsita]]---aromatic.
translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa has been embracing Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and the kuṅkuma powder on Her breasts has mixed with the garland of kunda flowers decorating His body. The fragrance of the garland has scented the entire atmosphere.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.48
description: " 'Lord Kṛṣṇa has left this place, and therefore the deer are feeling separation. They do not hear our words; therefore how can they reply?'
text:
> kṛṣṇa ihāṅ chāḍi' gelā, ihoṅ---virahiṇī
> kibā uttara dibe ei---nā śune kāhinī"
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']] [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---has left; [[synonyms:i:ihoṅ]]---the deer; [[synonyms:v:virahiṇī]]---feeling separation; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---what; [[synonyms:u:uttara]]---reply; [[synonyms:d:dibe]]---will they give; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---do not hear; [[synonyms:k:kāhinī]]---our words.
translation: “ 'Lord Kṛṣṇa has left this place, and therefore the deer are feeling separation. They do not hear our words; therefore how can they reply?'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.49
description: "The gopīs then came upon many trees so laden with fruits and flowers that their branches bent down to the ground.
text:
> āge vṛkṣa-gaṇa dekhe puṣpa-phala-bhare
> śākhā saba paḍiyāche pṛthivī-upare
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the trees; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---see; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]-[[synonyms:b:bhare]]---because of the heavy burden of flowers and fruits; [[synonyms:ś:śākhā]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all the branches; [[synonyms:p:paḍiyāche]]---have bent down; [[synonyms:p:pṛthivī]]-[[synonyms:u:upare]]---to the ground.
translation: "The gopīs then came upon many trees so laden with fruits and flowers that their branches bent down to the ground.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.5
description: The Lord would maintain Himself in three kinds of consciousness: sometimes He merged totally in ecstatic emotion, sometimes He was in partial external consciousness and sometimes in full external consciousness.
text:
> kabhu bhāve magna, kabhu ardha-bāhya-sphūrti
> kabhu bāhya-sphūrti,---tina rīte prabhu-sthiti
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---in ecstatic emotion; [[synonyms:m:magna]]---merged; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:a:ardha]]---half; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]-[[synonyms:s:sphūrti]]---in external consciousness; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]-[[synonyms:s:sphūrti]]---in full external consciousness; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:r:rīte]]---in three ways; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---the situation of the Lord.
translation: The Lord would maintain Himself in three kinds of consciousness: sometimes He merged totally in ecstatic emotion, sometimes He was in partial external consciousness and sometimes in full external consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.50
description: "The gopīs thought that because all the trees must have seen Kṛṣṇa pass by they were offering respectful obeisances to Him. To be certain, the gopīs inquired from the trees.
text:
> kṛṣṇe dekhi' ei saba karena namaskāra
> kṛṣṇa-gamana puche tāre kariyā nirdhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---offer respectful obeisances; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:gamana]]---the passing of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:puche]]---inquire; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---from them; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:n:nirdhāra]]---making certain.
translation: "The gopīs thought that because all the trees must have seen Kṛṣṇa pass by they were offering respectful obeisances to Him. To be certain, the gopīs inquired from the trees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.51
description: " 'O trees, kindly tell us whether Balarāma's younger brother, Kṛṣṇa, welcomed your obeisances with loving glances as He passed this way, resting one hand on the shoulder of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, holding a lotus flower in the other, and being followed by a swarm of bumblebees maddened by the fragrance of tulasī leaves.'
text:
> bāhuṁ priyāṁsa upadhāya gṛhīta-padmo
> rāmānujas tulasikāli-kulair madāndhaiḥ
> anvīyamāna iha vas taravaḥ praṇāmaṁ
> kiṁvābhinandati caran praṇayāvalokaiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāhum]]---arm; [[synonyms:p:priyā]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁse]]---on the shoulder of His beloved; [[synonyms:u:upadhāya]]---placing; [[synonyms:g:gṛhīta]]---having taken; [[synonyms:p:padmaḥ]]---a lotus flower; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:a:anujaḥ]]---Lord Balarāma's younger brother (Kṛṣṇa); [[synonyms:t:tulasikā]]---because of the garland of //tulasī// flowers; [[synonyms:a:ali]]-[[synonyms:k:kulaiḥ]]---by bumblebees; [[synonyms:m:mada]]-[[synonyms:a:andhaiḥ]]---blinded by the fragrance; [[synonyms:a:anvīyamānaḥ]]---being followed; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---here; [[synonyms:v:vaḥ]]---of you; [[synonyms:t:taravaḥ]]---O trees; [[synonyms:p:praṇāmam]]---the obeisances; [[synonyms:k:kiṁvā]]---whether; [[synonyms:a:abhinandati]]---welcomes; [[synonyms:c:caran]]---while passing; [[synonyms:p:praṇaya]]-[[synonyms:a:avalokaiḥ]]---with glances of love.
translation: “ 'O trees, kindly tell us whether Balarāma's younger brother, Kṛṣṇa, welcomed your obeisances with loving glances as He passed this way, resting one hand on the shoulder of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, holding a lotus flower in the other, and being followed by a swarm of bumblebees maddened by the fragrance of tulasī leaves.'
purport: This verse is quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.30.12).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.52
description: " 'To stop the bumblebees from landing on the face of His beloved, He whisked them away with the lotus flower in His hand, and thus His mind was slightly diverted.
text:
> priyā-mukhe bhṛṅga paḍe, tāhā nivārite
> līlā-padma cālāite haila anya-citte
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:priyā]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---on His beloved's face; [[synonyms:b:bhṛṅga]]---the bumblebees; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fall; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:n:nivārite]]---to prevent; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes; [[synonyms:p:padma]]---the lotus flower; [[synonyms:c:cālāite]]---causing to move; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:c:citte]]---diverted in the mind.
translation: “ 'To stop the bumblebees from landing on the face of His beloved, He whisked them away with the lotus flower in His hand, and thus His mind was slightly diverted.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.53
description: " 'Did He or did He not pay attention while You offered Him obeisances? Kindly give evidence supporting your words.
text:
> tomāra praṇāme ki kairāchena avadhāna?
> kibā nāhi karena, kaha vacana-pramāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:p:praṇāme]]---to the obeisances; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---whether; [[synonyms:k:kairāchena]]---has given; [[synonyms:a:avadhāna]]---attention; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---or; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:k:karena]]---did not do so; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---kindly speak; [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---words; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---evidence.
translation: “ 'Did He or did He not pay attention while You offered Him obeisances? Kindly give evidence supporting your words.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.54
description: " 'Separation from Kṛṣṇa has made these servants very unhappy. Having lost consciousness, how can they answer us?'
text:
> kṛṣṇera viyoge ei sevaka duḥkhita
> kibā uttara dibe? ihāra nāhika samvit"
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:v:viyoge]]---by separation from Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---servants; [[synonyms:d:duḥkhita]]---very unhappy; [[synonyms:k:kibā]]---what; [[synonyms:u:uttara]]---reply; [[synonyms:d:dibe]]---will they give; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of these; [[synonyms:n:nāhika]]---there's not; [[synonyms:s:samvit]]---consciousness.
translation: “ 'Separation from Kṛṣṇa has made these servants very unhappy. Having lost consciousness, how can they answer us?'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.55
description: "Saying this, the gopīs stepped onto the beach by the Yamunā River. There they saw Lord Kṛṣṇa beneath a kadamba tree.
text:
> eta bali' āge cale yamunāra kūle
> dekhe,---tāhāṅ kṛṣṇa haya kadambera tale
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:ā:āge]] [[synonyms:c:cale]]---go forward; [[synonyms:y:yamunāra]] [[synonyms:k:kūle]]---onto the beach by the Yamunā; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---they see; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is present; [[synonyms:k:kadambera]] [[synonyms:t:tale]]---underneath a //kadamba// tree.
translation: "Saying this, the gopīs stepped onto the beach by the Yamunā River. There they saw Lord Kṛṣṇa beneath a kadamba tree.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.56
description: "Standing there with His flute to His lips, Kṛṣṇa, who enchants millions upon millions of Cupids, attracted the eyes and minds of all the world with His unlimited beauty."
text:
> koṭi-manmatha-mohana muralī-vadana
> apāra saundarye hare jagan-netra-mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]---ten million; [[synonyms:m:manmatha]]---Cupids; [[synonyms:m:mohana]]---enchanting; [[synonyms:m:muralī]]-[[synonyms:v:vadana]]---with His flute to His lips; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimited; [[synonyms:s:saundarye]]---by the beauty; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---enchants; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---of the whole world; [[synonyms:n:netra]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the eyes and mind.
translation: "Standing there with His flute to His lips, Kṛṣṇa, who enchants millions upon millions of Cupids, attracted the eyes and minds of all the world with His unlimited beauty."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.57
description: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the transcendental beauty of Kṛṣṇa, He fell down on the ground unconscious. At that time, all the devotees, headed by Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, joined Him in the garden.
text:
> saundarya dekhiyā bhūme paḍe mūrcchā pāñā
> hena-kāle svarūpādi mililā āsiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saundarya]]---beauty; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:b:bhūme]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---fell; [[synonyms:m:mūrcchā]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---becoming unconscious; [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the devotees, headed by Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:m:mililā]] [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---came there and met.
translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the transcendental beauty of Kṛṣṇa, He fell down on the ground unconscious. At that time, all the devotees, headed by Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, joined Him in the garden.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.58
description: Just as before, they saw all the symptoms of transcendental ecstatic love manifested in the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Although externally He appeared bewildered, He was tasting transcendental bliss within.
text:
> pūrvavat sarvāṅge sāttvika-bhāva-sakala
> antare ānanda-āsvāda, bāhire vihvala
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---as before; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---all over the body; [[synonyms:s:sāttvika]]---transcendental; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all the symptoms of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---within; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsvāda]]---the taste of transcendental bliss; [[synonyms:b:bāhire]]---externally; [[synonyms:v:vihvala]]---bewildered.
translation: Just as before, they saw all the symptoms of transcendental ecstatic love manifested in the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Although externally He appeared bewildered, He was tasting transcendental bliss within.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.59
description: Once again all the devotees brought Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu back to consciousness by a concerted effort. Then the Lord got up and began wandering here and there, looking all around.
text:
> pūrvavat sabe mili' karāilā cetana
> uṭhiyā caudike prabhu karena darśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---as before; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:m:mili']]---coming together; [[synonyms:k:karāilā]] [[synonyms:c:cetana]]---brought to consciousness; [[synonyms:u:uṭhiyā]]---standing up; [[synonyms:c:cau]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---all around; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---was looking.
translation: Once again all the devotees brought Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu back to consciousness by a concerted effort. Then the Lord got up and began wandering here and there, looking all around.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.6
description: Actually, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was always merged in ecstatic emotion, but just as a potter's wheel turns without the potter's touching it, the Lord's bodily activities, like bathing, going to the temple to see Lord Jagannātha, and taking lunch, went on automatically.
text:
> snāna, darśana, bhojana deha-svabhāve haya
> kumārera cāka yena satata phiraya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---bathing; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---visiting the temple; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---taking lunch; [[synonyms:d:deha]]-[[synonyms:s:svabhāve]]---by the nature of the body; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:k:kumārera]] [[synonyms:c:cāka]]---the potter's wheel; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as; [[synonyms:s:satata]]---always; [[synonyms:p:phiraya]]---revolves.
translation: Actually, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was always merged in ecstatic emotion, but just as a potter's wheel turns without the potter's touching it, the Lord's bodily activities, like bathing, going to the temple to see Lord Jagannātha, and taking lunch, went on automatically.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.60
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Where has My Kṛṣṇa gone? I saw Him just now, and His beauty has captured My eyes and mind.
text:
> "kāhāṅ gelā kṛṣṇa? ekhani pāinu daraśana!
> tāṅhāra saundarya mora harila netra-mana!
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:g:gelā]] [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---has Kṛṣṇa gone; [[synonyms:e:ekhani]]---just now; [[synonyms:p:pāinu]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---I saw; [[synonyms:t:taṅhāra]]---His; [[synonyms:s:saundarya]]---beauty; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:h:harila]]---has taken away; [[synonyms:n:netra]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---eyes and mind.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Where has My Kṛṣṇa gone? I saw Him just now, and His beauty has captured My eyes and mind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.61
description: "Why can't I again see Kṛṣṇa holding His flute to His lips? My eyes are wandering in hopes of seeing Him once more."
text:
> punaḥ kene nā dekhiye muralī-vadana!
> tāṅhāra darśana-lobhe bhramaya nayana"
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiye]]---I do not see; [[synonyms:m:muralī]]-[[synonyms:v:vadana]]---with His flute to His lips; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---of Him; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]-[[synonyms:l:lobhe]]---in hopes of seeing; [[synonyms:b:bhramaya]]---are wandering; [[synonyms:n:nayana]]---My eyes.
translation: "Why can't I again see Kṛṣṇa holding His flute to His lips? My eyes are wandering in hopes of seeing Him once more."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.62
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then recited the following verse, which was spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī to Her dear friend Viśākhā.
text:
> viśākhāre rādhā yaiche śloka kahilā
> sei śloka mahāprabhu paḍite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viśākhāre]]---to Viśākhā; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---recited a verse; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verse; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:paḍite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to recite.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then recited the following verse, which was spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī to Her dear friend Viśākhā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.63
description: "My dear friend, the luster of Kṛṣṇa's body is more brilliant than a newly formed cloud, and His yellow dress is more attractive than newly arrived lightning. A peacock feather decorates His head, and on His neck hangs a lovely necklace of brilliant pearls. As He holds His charming flute to His lips, His face looks as beautiful as the full autumn moon. By such beauty, Madana-mohana, the enchanter of Cupid, is increasing the desire of my eyes to see Him."
text:
> navāmbuda-lasad-dyutir nava-taḍin-manojñāmbaraḥ
> sucitra-muralī-sphurac-charad-amanda-candrānanaḥ
> mayūra-dala-bhūṣitaḥ subhaga-tāra-hāra-prabhaḥ
> sa me madana-mohanaḥ sakhi tanoti netra-spṛhām
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:a:ambuda]]---a newly formed cloud; [[synonyms:l:lasat]]---brilliant; [[synonyms:d:dyutiḥ]]---whose luster; [[synonyms:n:nava]]---new; [[synonyms:t:taḍit]]---lightning; [[synonyms:m:manojña]]---attractive; [[synonyms:a:ambaraḥ]]---whose dress; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:c:citra]]---very charming; [[synonyms:m:muralī]]---with a flute; [[synonyms:s:sphurat]]---appearing beautiful; [[synonyms:ś:śarat]]---autumn; [[synonyms:a:amanda]]---bright; [[synonyms:c:candra]]---like the moon; [[synonyms:ā:ānanaḥ]]---whose face; [[synonyms:m:mayūra]]---peacock; [[synonyms:d:dala]]---with a feather; [[synonyms:b:bhūṣitaḥ]]---decorated; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaga]]---lovely; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of pearls; [[synonyms:h:hāra]]---of a necklace; [[synonyms:p:prabhaḥ]]---with the effulgence; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mohanaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa, the enchanter of Cupid; [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---O My dear friend; [[synonyms:t:tanoti]]---increases; [[synonyms:n:netra]]-[[synonyms:s:spṛhām]]---the desire of the eyes.
translation: "My dear friend, the luster of Kṛṣṇa's body is more brilliant than a newly formed cloud, and His yellow dress is more attractive than newly arrived lightning. A peacock feather decorates His head, and on His neck hangs a lovely necklace of brilliant pearls. As He holds His charming flute to His lips, His face looks as beautiful as the full autumn moon. By such beauty, Madana-mohana, the enchanter of Cupid, is increasing the desire of my eyes to see Him."
purport: This verse is also found in the //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (8.4).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.64
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued: "Śrī Kṛṣṇa's complexion is as polished as powdered eye ointment. It surpasses the beauty of a newly formed cloud and is softer than a blue lotus flower. Indeed, His complexion is so pleasing that it attracts the eyes and mind of everyone, and it is so powerful that it defies all comparison.
text:
> nava-ghana-snigdha-varṇa, dalitāñjana-cikkaṇa,
> indīvara-nindi sukomala
> jini' upamāna-gaṇa, hare sabāra netra-mana,
> kṛṣṇa-kānti parama prabala
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:g:ghana]]---a newly formed cloud; [[synonyms:s:snigdha]]---attractive; [[synonyms:v:varṇa]]---bodily complexion; [[synonyms:d:dalita]]---powdered; [[synonyms:a:añjana]]---ointment; [[synonyms:c:cikkaṇa]]---polished; [[synonyms:i:indīvara]]---a blue lotus flower; [[synonyms:n:nindi]]---defeating; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:k:komala]]---soft; [[synonyms:j:jini]]---surpassing; [[synonyms:u:upamāna]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all comparison; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all; [[synonyms:n:netra]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the eyes and mind; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kānti]]---the complexion of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:p:prabala]]---supremely powerful.
translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued: "Śrī Kṛṣṇa's complexion is as polished as powdered eye ointment. It surpasses the beauty of a newly formed cloud and is softer than a blue lotus flower. Indeed, His complexion is so pleasing that it attracts the eyes and mind of everyone, and it is so powerful that it defies all comparison.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.65
description: "My dear friend, please tell me what I should do. Kṛṣṇa is as attractive as a wonderful cloud, and My eyes are just like cātaka birds, which are dying of thirst because they do not see such a cloud.
text:
> kaha, sakhi, ki kari upāya?
> kṛṣṇādbhuta balāhaka, mora netra-cātaka,
> nā dekhi' piyāse mari' yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---please tell; [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---My dear friend; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:k:kari]] [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---what shall I do; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:b:balāhaka]]---cloud; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:n:netra]]---eyes; [[synonyms:c:cātaka]]---like //cātaka birds//; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---without seeing; [[synonyms:p:piyāse]]---from thirst; [[synonyms:m:mari']] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---are dying.
translation: "My dear friend, please tell me what I should do. Kṛṣṇa is as attractive as a wonderful cloud, and My eyes are just like cātaka birds, which are dying of thirst because they do not see such a cloud.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.66
description: "Kṛṣṇa's yellow dress looks exactly like restless lightning in the sky, and the pearl necklace on His neck appears like a line of ducks flying below a cloud. Both the peacock feather on His head and His vaijayantī garland [containing flowers of five colors] resemble rainbows.
text:
> saudāminī pītāmbara, sthira nahe nirantara,
> muktā-hāra baka-pāṅti bhāla
> indra-dhanu śikhi-pākhā, upare diyāche dekhā,
> āra dhanu vaijayantī-māla
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saudāminī]]---lightning; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]-[[synonyms:a:ambara]]---the yellow dress; [[synonyms:s:sthira]]---still; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---is not; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---always; [[synonyms:m:muktā]]-[[synonyms:h:hāra]]---the necklace of pearls; [[synonyms:b:baka]]-[[synonyms:p:pāṅti]] [[synonyms:b:bhāla]]---like a line of ducks; [[synonyms:i:indra]]-[[synonyms:d:dhanu]]---the bow of Indra (a rainbow); [[synonyms:ś:śikhi]]-[[synonyms:p:pākhā]]---the peacock feather; [[synonyms:u:upare]]---on the head; [[synonyms:d:diyāche]] [[synonyms:d:dekhā]]---is seen; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dhanu]]---another rainbow; [[synonyms:v:vaijayantī]]-[[synonyms:m:māla]]---the //vaijayantī// garland.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa's yellow dress looks exactly like restless lightning in the sky, and the pearl necklace on His neck appears like a line of ducks flying below a cloud. Both the peacock feather on His head and His vaijayantī garland [containing flowers of five colors] resemble rainbows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.67
description: "The luster of Kṛṣṇa's body is as beautiful as a spotless full moon that has just risen, and the vibration of His flute sounds exactly like the sweet thundering of a newly formed cloud. When the peacocks in Vṛndāvana hear that vibration, they all begin to dance.
text:
> muralīra kala-dhvani, madhura garjana śuni',
> vṛndāvane nāce mayūra-caya
> akalaṅka pūrṇa-kala, lāvaṇya-jyotsnā jhalamala,
> citra-candrera tāhāte udaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:muralīra]]---of the flute; [[synonyms:k:kala]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---the low vibration; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweet; [[synonyms:g:garjana]]---thundering; [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---hearing; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvane]]---in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:m:mayūra]]-[[synonyms:c:caya]]---the peacocks; [[synonyms:a:akalaṅka]]---spotless; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kala]]---the full moon; [[synonyms:l:lāvaṇya]]---beauty; [[synonyms:j:jyotsnā]]---light; [[synonyms:j:jhalamala]]---glittering; [[synonyms:c:citra]]-[[synonyms:c:candrera]]---of the beautiful moon; [[synonyms:t:tāhāte]]---in that; [[synonyms:u:udaya]]---the rising.
translation: "The luster of Kṛṣṇa's body is as beautiful as a spotless full moon that has just risen, and the vibration of His flute sounds exactly like the sweet thundering of a newly formed cloud. When the peacocks in Vṛndāvana hear that vibration, they all begin to dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.68
description: "The cloud of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes is drenching the fourteen worlds with a shower of nectar. Unfortunately, when that cloud appeared, a whirlwind arose and blew it away from Me. Being unable to see the cloud, the cātaka bird of My eyes is almost dead from thirst."
text:
> līlāmṛta-variṣaṇe, siñce caudda bhuvane'
> hena megha yabe dekhā dila
> durdaiva-jhañjhā-pavane, meghe nila anya-sthāne,
> mare cātaka, pite nā pāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---of the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---of nectar; [[synonyms:v:variṣaṇe]]---the shower; [[synonyms:s:siñce]]---drenches; [[synonyms:c:caudda]] [[synonyms:b:bhuvane]]---the fourteen worlds; [[synonyms:h:hena]] [[synonyms:m:megha]]---such a cloud; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:d:dekhā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---was visible; [[synonyms:d:durdaiva]]---misfortune; [[synonyms:j:jhañjhā]]-[[synonyms:p:pavane]]---a high wind; [[synonyms:m:meghe]]---the cloud; [[synonyms:n:nila]]---brought; [[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to another place; [[synonyms:m:mare]]---dies; [[synonyms:c:cātaka]]---the //cātaka// bird; [[synonyms:p:pite]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---could not drink.
translation: "The cloud of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes is drenching the fourteen worlds with a shower of nectar. Unfortunately, when that cloud appeared, a whirlwind arose and blew it away from Me. Being unable to see the cloud, the cātaka bird of My eyes is almost dead from thirst."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.69
description: In a faltering voice, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu again said, "Alas, go on reading, Rāma Rāya." Thus Rāmānanda Rāya began to read a verse. While listening to this verse, the Lord was sometimes very jubilant and sometimes overcome by lamentation. Afterwards the Lord personally explained the verse.
text:
> punaḥ kahe,---'hāya hāya, paḍa paḍa rāma-raya',
> kahe prabhu gadgada ākhyāne
> rāmānanda paḍe śloka, śuni' prabhura harṣa-śoka,
> āpane prabhu karena vyākhyāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:h:hāya]] [[synonyms:h:hāya]]---alas, alas; [[synonyms:p:paḍa]] [[synonyms:p:paḍa]]---go on reading; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gadgada]] [[synonyms:ā:ākhyāne]]---in a faltering voice; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---reads; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---a verse; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śoka]]---jubilation and lamentation; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:v:vyākhyāne]]---explains.
translation: In a faltering voice, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu again said, "Alas, go on reading, Rāma Rāya." Thus Rāmānanda Rāya began to read a verse. While listening to this verse, the Lord was sometimes very jubilant and sometimes overcome by lamentation. Afterwards the Lord personally explained the verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.7
description: One day, while Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was looking at Lord Jagannātha in the temple, Lord Jagannātha appeared to be personally the son of Nanda Mahārāja, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> eka-dina karena prabhu jagannātha daraśana
> jagannāthe dekhe sākṣāt vrajendra-nandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---visiting; [[synonyms:j:jagannāthe]]---Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---He sees; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]---personally; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of Mahārāja Nanda.
translation: One day, while Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was looking at Lord Jagannātha in the temple, Lord Jagannātha appeared to be personally the son of Nanda Mahārāja, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.70
description: "Dear Kṛṣṇa, by seeing Your beautiful face decorated with tresses of hair, by seeing the beauty of Your earrings falling on Your cheeks, and by seeing the nectar of Your lips, the beauty of Your smiling glances, Your two arms, which assure complete fearlessness, and Your broad chest, whose beauty arouses conjugal attraction, we have simply surrendered ourselves to becoming Your maidservants.'
text:
> vīkṣyālakāvṛta-mukhaṁ tava kuṇḍala-śri-
> gaṇḍa-sthalādhara-sudhaṁ hasitāvalokam
> dattābhayaṁ ca bhuja-daṇḍa-yugaṁ vilokya
> vakṣaḥ śriyaika-ramaṇaṁ ca bhavāma dāsyaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vīkṣya]]---seeing; [[synonyms:a:alaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:āvṛta]]---decorated with curling tresses of hair; [[synonyms:m:mukham]]---face; [[synonyms:t:tava]]---Your; [[synonyms:k:kuṇḍala]]-[[synonyms:ś:śri]]---the beauty of earrings; [[synonyms:g:gaṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:s:sthala]]---falling in Your cheeks; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:s:sudham]]---and the nectar of Your lips; [[synonyms:h:hasita]]-[[synonyms:a:avalokam]]---Your smiling glance; [[synonyms:d:datta]]-[[synonyms:a:abhayam]]---which assure fearlessness; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:b:bhuja]]-[[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:y:yugam]]---the two arms; [[synonyms:v:vilokya]]---by seeing; [[synonyms:v:vakṣaḥ]]---chest; [[synonyms:ś:śriyā]]---by the beauty; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:r:ramaṇam]]---chiefly producing conjugal attraction; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:b:bhavāma]]---we have become; [[synonyms:d:dāsyaḥ]]---Your maidservants.
translation: "Dear Kṛṣṇa, by seeing Your beautiful face decorated with tresses of hair, by seeing the beauty of Your earrings falling on Your cheeks, and by seeing the nectar of Your lips, the beauty of Your smiling glances, Your two arms, which assure complete fearlessness, and Your broad chest, whose beauty arouses conjugal attraction, we have simply surrendered ourselves to becoming Your maidservants.'
purport: This verse quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.29.39) was spoken by the //gopīs// when they arrived before Kṛṣṇa for the //rāsa// dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.71
description: "After conquering the moon and the lotus flower, Kṛṣṇa wished to capture the doelike gopīs. Thus He spread the noose of His beautiful face, and within that noose He placed the bait of His sweet smile to misguide the gopīs. The gopīs fell prey to that trap and became Kṛṣṇa's maidservants, giving up their homes, families, husbands and prestige.
text:
> kṛṣṇa jini' padma-cānda, pātiyāche mukha phānda,
> tāte adhara-madhu-smita cāra
> vraja-nārī āsi' āsi', phānde paḍi' haya dāsī,
> chāḍi' lāja-pati-ghara-dvāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:j:jini']]---surpassing; [[synonyms:p:padma]]-[[synonyms:c:cānda]]---the lotus flower and the moon; [[synonyms:p:pātiyāche]]---has spread; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---the face; [[synonyms:p:phānda]]---noose; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in that; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]---lips; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:s:smita]]---sweet smiling; [[synonyms:c:cāra]]---bait; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:n:nārī]]---the damsels of Vraja; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---approaching; [[synonyms:p:phānde]]---in the network; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---falling; [[synonyms:h:haya]] [[synonyms:d:dāsī]]---become maidservants; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:l:lāja]]---prestige; [[synonyms:p:pati]]---husbands; [[synonyms:g:ghara]]---home; [[synonyms:d:dvāra]]---family.
translation: "After conquering the moon and the lotus flower, Kṛṣṇa wished to capture the doelike gopīs. Thus He spread the noose of His beautiful face, and within that noose He placed the bait of His sweet smile to misguide the gopīs. The gopīs fell prey to that trap and became Kṛṣṇa's maidservants, giving up their homes, families, husbands and prestige.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.72
description: "My dear friend, Kṛṣṇa acts just like a hunter. This hunter does not care for piety or impiety; He simply creates many devices to conquer the cores of the hearts of the doelike gopīs.
text:
> bāndhava kṛṣṇa kare vyādhera ācāra
> nāhi māne dharmādharma, hare nārī-mṛgī-marma,
> kare nānā upāya tāhāra
