synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāndhava]]---O friend; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:v:vyādhera]] [[synonyms:ā:ācāra]]---the behavior of a hunter; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---cares for; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:a:adharma]]---piety and impiety; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]---of a woman; [[synonyms:m:mṛgī]]---doe; [[synonyms:m:marma]]---the core of the heart; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---varieties of; [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---means; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---for that purpose.
translation: "My dear friend, Kṛṣṇa acts just like a hunter. This hunter does not care for piety or impiety; He simply creates many devices to conquer the cores of the hearts of the doelike gopīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.73
description: "The earrings dancing on Kṛṣṇa's cheeks are shaped like sharks, and they shine very brightly. These dancing earrings attract the minds of all women. Over and above this, Kṛṣṇa pierces the hearts of women with the arrows of His sweetly smiling glances. He is not at all afraid to kill women in this way.
text:
> gaṇḍa-sthala jhalamala, nāce makara-kuṇḍala,
> sei nṛtye hare nārī-caya
> sasmita kaṭākṣa-bāṇe, tā-sabāra hṛdaye hāne,
> nārī-vadhe nāhi kichu bhaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gaṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:s:sthala]]---on the cheeks; [[synonyms:j:jhalamala]]---glittering; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:m:makara]]-[[synonyms:k:kuṇḍala]]---earrings shaped like sharks; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:n:nṛtye]]---dancing; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]-[[synonyms:c:caya]]---all the women; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:s:smita]]---with smiles; [[synonyms:k:kaṭākṣa]]---of glances; [[synonyms:b:bāṇe]]---by the arrows; [[synonyms:t:tā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---the hearts; [[synonyms:h:hāne]]---pierces; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]-[[synonyms:v:vadhe]]---for killing women; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---any; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear.
translation: "The earrings dancing on Kṛṣṇa's cheeks are shaped like sharks, and they shine very brightly. These dancing earrings attract the minds of all women. Over and above this, Kṛṣṇa pierces the hearts of women with the arrows of His sweetly smiling glances. He is not at all afraid to kill women in this way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.74
description: "On Kṛṣṇa's chest are the ornaments of Śrīvatsa and the mark indicating the residence of the goddess of fortune. His chest, which is as broad as a plunderer's, attracts thousands upon thousands of damsels of Vraja, conquering their minds and breasts by force. Thus they all become maidservants of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
text:
> ati ucca suvistāra, lakṣmī-śrīvatsa-alaṅkāra,
> kṛṣṇera ye ḍākātiyā vakṣa
> vraja-devī lakṣa lakṣa, tā-sabāra mano-vakṣa,
> hari-dāsī karibāre dakṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ati]]---very; [[synonyms:u:ucca]]---high; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:v:vistāra]]---broad; [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]---a mark of golden lines on the left side of the chest of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, indicating the residence of the goddess of fortune; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvatsa]]---a mark of silver hairs on the right side of the Lord's chest; [[synonyms:a:alaṅkāra]]---ornaments; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---that; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍākātiyā]]---like a plunderer; [[synonyms:v:vakṣa]]---chest; [[synonyms:v:vraja]]-[[synonyms:d:devī]]---the damsels of Vraja; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]] [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---thousands upon thousands; [[synonyms:t:tā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]-[[synonyms:v:vakṣa]]---the minds and breasts; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsī]]---maidservants of the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:k:karibāre]]---to make; [[synonyms:d:dakṣa]]---expert.
translation: "On Kṛṣṇa's chest are the ornaments of Śrīvatsa and the mark indicating the residence of the goddess of fortune. His chest, which is as broad as a plunderer's, attracts thousands upon thousands of damsels of Vraja, conquering their minds and breasts by force. Thus they all become maidservants of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.75
description: "The two very beautiful arms of Kṛṣṇa are just like long bolts. They also resemble the bodies of black snakes that enter the space between the two hill-like breasts of women and bite their hearts. The women then die from the burning poison.
text:
> sulalita dīrghārgala, kṛṣṇera bhuja-yugala,
> bhuja nahe,---kṛṣṇa-sarpa-kāya
> dui śaila-chidre paiśe, nārīra hṛdaye daṁśe,
> mare nārī se viṣa-jvālāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:l:lalita]]---very beautiful; [[synonyms:d:dīrgha]]-[[synonyms:a:argala]]---long bolts; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhuja]]-[[synonyms:y:yugala]]---two arms; [[synonyms:b:bhuja]]---arms; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---not; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---black; [[synonyms:s:sarpa]]---of snakes; [[synonyms:k:kāya]]---bodies; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:ś:śaila]]-[[synonyms:c:chidre]]---in the space between the hills; [[synonyms:p:paiśe]]---enter; [[synonyms:n:nārīra]]---of women; [[synonyms:h:hṛdaye]]---the hearts; [[synonyms:d:daṁśe]]---bite; [[synonyms:m:mare]]---die; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]---women; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:v:viṣa]]-[[synonyms:j:jvālāya]]---from the burning of the poison.
translation: "The two very beautiful arms of Kṛṣṇa are just like long bolts. They also resemble the bodies of black snakes that enter the space between the two hill-like breasts of women and bite their hearts. The women then die from the burning poison.
purport: In other words, the //gopīs// become very agitated by lusty desires; they are burning due to the poisonous bite inflicted by the black snakes of Kṛṣṇa's beautiful arms.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.76
description: "The combined cooling effect of camphor, roots of khasakhasa and sandalwood is surpassed by the coolness of Kṛṣṇa's palms and the soles of His feet, which are cooler and more pleasing than millions upon millions of moons. If women are touched by them even once, their minds are enticed, and the burning poison of lusty desire for Kṛṣṇa is immediately vanquished."
text:
> kṛṣṇa-kara-pada-tala, koṭi-candra-suśītala,
> jini' karpūra-veṇā-mūla-candana
> eka-bāra yāra sparśe, smara-jvālā-viṣa nāśe,
> yāra sparśe lubdha nārī-mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kara]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:t:tala]]---the palms and the soles of the feet; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---millions upon millions of moons; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:ś:śītala]]---cool and pleasing; [[synonyms:j:jini']]---surpassing; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]---camphor; [[synonyms:v:veṇā]]-[[synonyms:m:mūla]]---roots of //khasakhasa//; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood pulp; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---once; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:s:sparśe]]---by the touch; [[synonyms:s:smara]]-[[synonyms:j:jvālā]]---the burning effect of remembering; [[synonyms:v:viṣa]]---the poison; [[synonyms:n:nāśe]]---becomes vanquished; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:s:sparśe]]---by the touch; [[synonyms:l:lubdha]]---enticed; [[synonyms:n:nāri]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds of women.
translation: "The combined cooling effect of camphor, roots of khasakhasa and sandalwood is surpassed by the coolness of Kṛṣṇa's palms and the soles of His feet, which are cooler and more pleasing than millions upon millions of moons. If women are touched by them even once, their minds are enticed, and the burning poison of lusty desire for Kṛṣṇa is immediately vanquished."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.77
description: Lamenting in ecstatic love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then recited the following verse, which was spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī while exposing the lamentation of Her heart to Her friend Śrīmatī Viśākhā.
text:
> eteka vilāpa kari' premāveśe gaurahari,
> ei arthe paḍe eka śloka
> sei śloka paḍi' rādhā, viśākhāre kahe bādhā,
> ughāḍiyā hṛdayera śoka
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eteka]]---thus; [[synonyms:v:vilāpa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---lamenting; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:a:arthe]]---in understanding the purpose; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---recites; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---one verse; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---this verse; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reading; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:v:viśākhāre]]---to Viśākhā; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:b:bādhā]]---obstacle; [[synonyms:u:ughāḍiyā]]---exposing; [[synonyms:h:hṛdayera]]---of the heart; [[synonyms:ś:śoka]]---lamentation.
translation: Lamenting in ecstatic love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then recited the following verse, which was spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī while exposing the lamentation of Her heart to Her friend Śrīmatī Viśākhā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.78
description: "My dear friend, Kṛṣṇa's chest is as broad and attractive as a door made of indranīla gems, and His two arms, strong as bolts, can relieve the mental anguish of young girls distressed by lusty desires for Him. His body is cooler than the moon, sandalwood, the lotus flower and camphor. In this way, Madana-mohana, the attractor of Cupid, is increasing the desire of My breasts."
text:
> harinmaṇi-kavāṭikā-pratata-hāri-vakṣaḥ-sthalaḥ
> smarārta-taruṇī-manaḥ-kaluṣa-hāri-dor-argalaḥ
> sudhāṁśu-hari-candanotpala-sitābhra-śītāṅgakaḥ
> sa me madana-mohanaḥ sakhi tanoti vakṣaḥ-spṛhām
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:harit]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇi]]---of //indranīla// gems; [[synonyms:k:kavāṭikā]]---like a door; [[synonyms:p:pratata]]---broad; [[synonyms:h:hāri]]---attractive; [[synonyms:v:vakṣaḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:sthalaḥ]]---whose chest; [[synonyms:s:smara]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārta]]---distressed by remembering; [[synonyms:t:taruṇī]]---of young women; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]---of the mind; [[synonyms:k:kaluṣa]]---the pain; [[synonyms:h:hāri]]---taking away; [[synonyms:d:doḥ]]---whose two arms; [[synonyms:a:argalaḥ]]---like bolts; [[synonyms:s:sudhāṁśu]]---the moon; [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:c:candana]]---sandalwood; [[synonyms:u:utpala]]---lotus flower; [[synonyms:s:sitābhra]]---camphor; [[synonyms:ś:śīta]]---cool; [[synonyms:a:aṅgakaḥ]]---whose body; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mohanaḥ]]---Kṛṣṇa, who is more attractive than Cupid; [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---My friend; [[synonyms:t:tanoti]]---expands; [[synonyms:v:vakṣaḥ]]-[[synonyms:s:spṛhām]]---the desire of the breasts.
translation: "My dear friend, Kṛṣṇa's chest is as broad and attractive as a door made of indranīla gems, and His two arms, strong as bolts, can relieve the mental anguish of young girls distressed by lusty desires for Him. His body is cooler than the moon, sandalwood, the lotus flower and camphor. In this way, Madana-mohana, the attractor of Cupid, is increasing the desire of My breasts."
purport: This verse is also found in the //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (8.7).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.79
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "I just now had Kṛṣṇa, but unfortunately I have lost Him again.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---"kṛṣṇa muñi ekhana-i pāinu
> āpanāra durdaive punaḥ hārāinu
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:e:ekhana]]-[[synonyms:i:i]]---just now; [[synonyms:p:pāinu]]---had; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāra]]---My own; [[synonyms:d:durdaive]]---by misfortune; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:h:hārāinu]]---I have lost.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "I just now had Kṛṣṇa, but unfortunately I have lost Him again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.8
description: When He realized Lord Jagannātha to be Kṛṣṇa Himself, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's five senses were immediately absorbed in attraction for the five attributes of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> eka-bāre sphure prabhura kṛṣṇera pañca-guṇa
> pañca-guṇe kare pañcendriya ākarṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:b:bāre]]---at one time; [[synonyms:s:sphure]]---manifest; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---five attributes; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---five attributes; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:i:indriya]]---of the five senses; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaṇa]]---attraction.
translation: When He realized Lord Jagannātha to be Kṛṣṇa Himself, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's five senses were immediately absorbed in attraction for the five attributes of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
purport: Śrī Kṛṣṇa's beauty attracted the eyes of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Kṛṣṇa's singing and the vibration of His flute attracted the Lord's ears, the transcendental fragrance of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet attracted His nostrils, Kṛṣṇa's transcendental sweetness attracted His tongue, and Kṛṣṇa's bodily touch attracted the Lord's sensation of touch. Thus each of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's five senses was attracted by one of the five attributes of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.80
description: "By nature, Kṛṣṇa is very restless; He does not stay in one place. He meets with someone, enchants his mind and then disappears.
text:
> cañcala-svabhāva kṛṣṇera, nā raya eka-sthāne
> dekhā diyā mana hari' kare antardhāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cañcala]]---restless; [[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---characteristic; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:r:raya]]---stay; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in one place; [[synonyms:d:dekhā]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---giving His audience; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:h:hari']]---enchanting; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:a:antardhāne]]---disappearance.
translation: "By nature, Kṛṣṇa is very restless; He does not stay in one place. He meets with someone, enchants his mind and then disappears.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.81
description: " 'The gopīs became proud of their great fortune. To subdue their sense of superiority and show them special favor, Keśava, the subduer of even Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva, disappeared from the rāsa dance.' "
text:
> tāsāṁ tat-saubhaga-madaṁ
> vīkṣya mānaṁ ca keśavaḥ
> praśamāya prasādāya
> tatraivāntaradhīyata
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāsām]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:t:tat]]---their; [[synonyms:s:saubhaga]]-[[synonyms:m:madam]]---pride due to great fortune; [[synonyms:v:vīkṣya]]---seeing; [[synonyms:m:mānam]]---conception of superiority; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:k:keśavaḥ]]---Kṛṣṇa, who subdues even //ka// (Lord Brahmā) and //īśa// (Lord Śiva); [[synonyms:p:praśamāya]]---to subdue; [[synonyms:p:prasādāya]]---to show mercy; [[synonyms:t:tatra]]---there; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:a:antaradhīyata]]---disappeared.
translation: “ 'The gopīs became proud of their great fortune. To subdue their sense of superiority and show them special favor, Keśava, the subduer of even Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva, disappeared from the rāsa dance.' "
purport: This verse quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.29.48) was spoken by Śukadeva Gosvāmī to Mahārāja Parīkṣit.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.82
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said to Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī: "Please sing a song that will bring consciousness to My heart."
text:
> svarūpa-gosāñire kahena,---"gāo eka gīta
> yāte āmāra hṛdayera haye ta' 'samvit' "
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñire]]---to Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---said; [[synonyms:g:gāo]]---sing; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:g:gīta]]---song; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---by which; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---My; [[synonyms:h:hṛdayera]]---of the heart; [[synonyms:h:haye]]---there is; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:samvit]]---consciousness.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said to Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī: "Please sing a song that will bring consciousness to My heart."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.83
description: Thus for the pleasure of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī began very sweetly singing the following verse from Gīta-govinda.
text:
> svarūpa-gosāñi tabe madhura kariyā
> gīta-govindera pada gāya prabhure śunāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:m:madhura]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---very sweetly; [[synonyms:g:gīta]]-[[synonyms:g:govindera]]---of the book //Gīta-govinda//; [[synonyms:p:pada]]---one verse; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sings; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śunāñā]]---making to hear.
translation: Thus for the pleasure of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī began very sweetly singing the following verse from Gīta-govinda.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.84
description: "Here in the arena of the rāsa dance, I remember Kṛṣṇa, who is always fond of joking and performing pastimes."
text:
> rāse harim iha vihita-vilāsam
> smarati mano mama kṛta-parihāsam
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāse]]---in the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:h:harim]]---Śrī Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:i:iha]]---here; [[synonyms:v:vihita]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāsam]]---performing pastimes; [[synonyms:s:smarati]]---remembers; [[synonyms:m:manaḥ]]---mind; [[synonyms:m:mama]]---my; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:p:parihāsam]]---fond of making jokes.
translation: "Here in the arena of the //rāsa// dance, I remember Kṛṣṇa, who is always fond of joking and performing pastimes."
purport: This verse is quoted from //Gīta-govinda// (2.3).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.85
description: When Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī sang this special song, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately got up and began to dance in ecstatic love.
text:
> svarūpa-gosāñi yabe ei pada gāhilā
> uṭhi' premāveśe prabhu nācite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:p:pada]]---verse; [[synonyms:g:gāhilā]]---sang; [[synonyms:u:uṭhi']]---standing up; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nācite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to dance.
translation: When Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī sang this special song, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately got up and began to dance in ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.86
description: At that time, all eight kinds of spiritual transformations became manifest in Lord Caitanya's body. The thirty-three symptoms of vyabhicārī-bhāva, beginning with lamentation and jubilation, became prominent as well.
text:
> 'aṣṭa-sāttvika' bhāva aṅge prakaṭa ha-ila
> harṣādi 'vyabhicārī' saba uthalila
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:asta]]-[[synonyms:s:sāttvika]]---eight spiritual; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---emotions; [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---on the body; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭa]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became manifest; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---beginning with jubilation; [[synonyms:v:vyabhicārī]]---thirty-three changes of //vyabhicārī-bhāva//; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:u:uthalila]]---were manifest.
translation: At that time, all eight kinds of spiritual transformations became manifest in Lord Caitanya's body. The thirty-three symptoms of vyabhicārī-bhāva, beginning with lamentation and jubilation, became prominent as well.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.87
description: All the ecstatic symptoms, such as bhāvodaya, bhāva-sandhi and bhāva-śābalya, awakened in the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. A great fight arose between one emotion and another, and each of them became prominent.
text:
> bhāvodaya, bhāva-sandhi, bhāva-śābalya
> bhāve-bhāve mahā-yuddhe sabāra prābalya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]]---awakening of all the ecstatic symptoms; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:s:sandhi]]---meeting of ecstatic symptoms; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śābalya]]---mixing of ecstatic symptoms; [[synonyms:b:bhāve]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---between one ecstasy and another; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:y:yuddhe]]---a great fight; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:p:prābalya]]---prominence.
translation: All the ecstatic symptoms, such as bhāvodaya, bhāva-sandhi and bhāva-śābalya, awakened in the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. A great fight arose between one emotion and another, and each of them became prominent.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.88
description: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu had Svarūpa Dāmodara sing the same verse again and again. Each time he sang it, the Lord tasted it anew, and thus He danced again and again.
text:
> sei pada punaḥ punaḥ karāya gāyana
> punaḥ punaḥ āsvādaye, karena nartana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:pada]]---that verse; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]] [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again and again; [[synonyms:k:karāya]] [[synonyms:g:gāyana]]---made to sing; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]] [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again and again; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādaye]]---tastes; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dances.
translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu had Svarūpa Dāmodara sing the same verse again and again. Each time he sang it, the Lord tasted it anew, and thus He danced again and again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.89
description: After the Lord had been dancing for a long time, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī stopped singing the verse.
text:
> ei-mata nṛtya yadi ha-ila bahu-kṣaṇa
> svarūpa-gosāñi pada kailā samāpana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---dancing; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---when; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---was; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇa]]---for a long time; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pada]]---verse; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:s:samāpana]]---stopped.
translation: After the Lord had been dancing for a long time, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī stopped singing the verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.9
description: Just as in a tug-of-war, the single mind of Lord Caitanya was attracted in five directions by the five transcendental attributes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Thus the Lord became unconscious.
text:
> eka-mana pañca-dike pañca-guṇa ṭāne
> ṭānāṭāni prabhura mana haila ageyāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---one mind; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:d:dike]]---in five directions; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---the five attributes; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭāne]]---attracted; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭānāṭāni]]---by a tug-of-war; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:a:ageyāne]]---unconscious.
translation: Just as in a tug-of-war, the single mind of Lord Caitanya was attracted in five directions by the five transcendental attributes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Thus the Lord became unconscious.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.90
description: Over and over again Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Go on! Sing! Sing!" But Svarūpa Dāmodara, seeing the Lord's fatigue, did not resume singing.
text:
> 'bal' 'bal' bali' prabhu kahena bāra-bāra
> nā gāya svarūpa-gosāñi śrama dekhi' tāṅra
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bal]]---sing; [[synonyms:b:bal]]---sing; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---uttering; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---says; [[synonyms:b:bāra]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---again and again; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sings; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ś:śrama]]---fatigue; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Lord Caitanya.
translation: Over and over again Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Go on! Sing! Sing!" But Svarūpa Dāmodara, seeing the Lord's fatigue, did not resume singing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.91
description: When the devotees heard Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu say, "Go on singing!" they all gathered around Him and began to chant the holy name of Hari in unison.
text:
> 'bal' 'bal' prabhu balena, bhakta-gaṇa śuni'
> caudikete sabe meli' kare hari-dhvani
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bal]] [[synonyms:b:bal]]---go on singing, go on singing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:b:balena]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:c:cau]]-[[synonyms:d:dikete]]---all around; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:m:meli']]---combining; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]]---vibrate the holy name of Hari.
translation: When the devotees heard Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu say, "Go on singing!" they all gathered around Him and began to chant the holy name of Hari in unison.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.92
description: At that time, Rāmānanda Rāya made the Lord sit down and dissipated His fatigue by fanning Him.
text:
> rāmānanda-rāya tabe prabhure vasāilā
> vījanādi kari' prabhura śrama ghucāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vasāilā]]---made to sit down; [[synonyms:v:vījana]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---fanning and so on; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrama]]---fatigue; [[synonyms:g:ghucāilā]]---dissipated.
translation: At that time, Rāmānanda Rāya made the Lord sit down and dissipated His fatigue by fanning Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.93
description: Then all the devotees took Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to the beach and bathed Him. Finally they brought Him back home.
text:
> prabhure lañā gelā sabe samudrera tīre
> snāna karāñā punaḥ tāṅre lañā āilā ghare
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all; [[synonyms:s:samudrera]] [[synonyms:t:tīre]]---to the beach by the sea; [[synonyms:s:snāna]] [[synonyms:k:karāñā]]---bathing Him; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:l:lañā]] [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---brought back; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to His residence.
translation: Then all the devotees took Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to the beach and bathed Him. Finally they brought Him back home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.94
description: After they fed Him lunch, they made Him lie down. Then all the devotees, headed by Rāmānanda Rāya, returned to their respective homes.
text:
> bhojana karāñā prabhure karāilā śayana
> rāmānanda-ādi sabe gelā nija-sthāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhojana]] [[synonyms:k:karāñā]]---feeding; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karāilā]] [[synonyms:ś:śayana]]---made to lie down; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---to their homes.
translation: After they fed Him lunch, they made Him lie down. Then all the devotees, headed by Rāmānanda Rāya, returned to their respective homes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.95
description: Thus I have described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastimes in the garden, which He entered, mistaking it for Vṛndāvana.
text:
> ei ta' kahiluṅ prabhura udyāna-vihāra
> vṛndāvana-bhrame yāhāṅ praveśa tāṅhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---thus; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have described; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:u:udyāna]]-[[synonyms:v:vihāra]]---pastimes in the garden; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhrame]]---mistaking for Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:p:praveśa]]---entrance; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---His.
translation: Thus I have described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastimes in the garden, which He entered, mistaking it for Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.96
description: There He exhibited transcendental madness and ecstatic ravings, which Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī has described very nicely in his Stava-mālā as follows.
text:
> pralāpa sahita ei unmāda-varṇana
> śrī-rūpa-gosāñi ihā kariyāchena varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pralāpa]]---ecstatic ravings; [[synonyms:s:sahita]]---with; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:u:unmāda]]---of madness; [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---description; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchena]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---has described.
translation: There He exhibited transcendental madness and ecstatic ravings, which Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī has described very nicely in his Stava-mālā as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.97
description: "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the topmost of all devotees. Sometimes, while walking on the beach, He would see a beautiful garden nearby and mistake it for the forest of Vṛndāvana. Thus He would be completely overwhelmed by ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa and begin to dance and chant the holy name. His tongue worked incessantly as He chanted, 'Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!' Will He again become visible before the path of My eyes?"
text:
> payorāśes tīre sphurad-upavanālī-kalanayā
> muhur vṛndāraṇya-smaraṇa-janita-prema-vivaśaḥ
> kvacit kṛṣṇāvṛtti-pracala-rasano bhakti-rasikaḥ
> sa caitanyaḥ kiṁ me punarapi dṛśor yāsyati padam
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:payaḥ]]-[[synonyms:r:rāśeḥ]]---by the sea; [[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the beach; [[synonyms:s:sphurat]]---beautiful; [[synonyms:u:upavanālī]]---garden; [[synonyms:k:kalanayā]]---by seeing; [[synonyms:m:muhuḥ]]---continuously; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāraṇya]]---the forest of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]-[[synonyms:j:janita]]---by remembering; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:v:vivaśaḥ]]---being overwhelmed by ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kvacit]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āvṛtti]]---repetition; [[synonyms:p:pracala]]---busily engaged in; [[synonyms:r:rasanaḥ]]---whose tongue; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:r:rasikaḥ]]---expert in devotional service; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that; [[synonyms:c:caitanyaḥ]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---whether; [[synonyms:m:me]]---my; [[synonyms:p:punarapi]]---again; [[synonyms:d:dṛśoḥ]]---of the eyes; [[synonyms:y:yāsyati]]---will go; [[synonyms:p:padam]]---in the path.
translation: "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the topmost of all devotees. Sometimes, while walking on the beach, He would see a beautiful garden nearby and mistake it for the forest of Vṛndāvana. Thus He would be completely overwhelmed by ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa and begin to dance and chant the holy name. His tongue worked incessantly as He chanted, 'Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!' Will He again become visible before the path of My eyes?"
purport: This quotation is from the first //Caitanyāṣṭaka,// verse 6, in Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī's //Stava-mālā.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.98
description: The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are unlimited; it is not possible to write of them properly. I can only give an indication of them as I try to introduce them.
text:
> ananta caitanya-līlā nā yāya likhana
> diṅ-mātra dekhāñā tāhā kariye sūcana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ananta]]---endless; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]] [[synonyms:l:likhana]]---it is impossible to write; [[synonyms:d:dik]]-[[synonyms:m:mātra]]---only a direction; [[synonyms:d:dekhāñā]]---showing; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---them; [[synonyms:k:kariye]] [[synonyms:s:sūcana]]---I introduce.
translation: The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are unlimited; it is not possible to write of them properly. I can only give an indication of them as I try to introduce them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 15.99
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation:
Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā,  Fifteenth Chapter, describing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastimes in the garden by the sea.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.1
description: Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who personally tasted the nectar of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa and then instructed His devotees how to taste it. Thus He enlightened them about ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa to initiate them into transcendental knowledge.
text:
> vande śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanyaṁ
> kṛṣṇa-bhāvāmṛtaṁ hi yaḥ
> āsvādyāsvādayan bhaktān
> prema-dīkṣām aśikṣayat
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vande]]---I offer my respectful obeisances; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanyam]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛtam]]---the nectar of ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---He who; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādya]]---tasting; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādayan]]---causing to taste; [[synonyms:b:bhaktān]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---in love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dīkṣām]]---initiation; [[synonyms:a:aśikṣayat]]---instructed.
translation: Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who personally tasted the nectar of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa and then instructed His devotees how to taste it. Thus He enlightened them about ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa to initiate them into transcendental knowledge.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.10
description: He would go to all the Vaiṣṇavas born in brāhmaṇa families, be they neophyte or advanced devotees, and present them gifts of first-class eatables.
text:
> brāhmaṇa-vaiṣṇava yata---choṭa, baḍa haya
> uttama-vastu bheṭa lañā tāṅra ṭhāñi yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---Vaiṣṇavas coming from //brāhmaṇa// families; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---all; [[synonyms:c:choṭa]]---neophyte; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---highly advanced; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:u:uttama]]-[[synonyms:v:vastu]]---first-class eatables; [[synonyms:b:bheṭa]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking as gifts; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---to them; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes.
translation: He would go to all the Vaiṣṇavas born in brāhmaṇa families, be they neophyte or advanced devotees, and present them gifts of first-class eatables.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.100
description: "The word 'sukṛti' refers to pious activities performed by the mercy of Kṛṣṇa. One who is fortunate enough to obtain such mercy receives the remnants of the Lord's food and thus becomes glorious."
text:
> 'sukṛti'-śabde kahe 'kṛṣṇa-kṛpā-hetu puṇya'
> sei yāṅra haya, 'phelā' pāya sei dhanya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sukṛti]]---//sukṛti// (pious activities); [[synonyms:ś:śabde]]---the word; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---is to be understood; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---the mercy of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:hetu]]---because of; [[synonyms:p:puṇya]]---pious activities; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---he; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:p:phelā]]---the remnants of food; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---he; [[synonyms:d:dhanya]]---very glorious.
translation: "The word 'sukṛti' refers to pious activities performed by the mercy of Kṛṣṇa. One who is fortunate enough to obtain such mercy receives the remnants of the Lord's food and thus becomes glorious."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.101
description: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade farewell to all the servants. After seeing the next offering of food to Lord Jagannātha, a function known as upala-bhoga, He returned to His own quarters.
text:
> eta bali' prabhu tā-sabāre vidāya dilā
> upala-bhoga dekhiyā prabhu nija-vāsā āilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---unto all of them; [[synonyms:v:vidāya]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---bade farewell; [[synonyms:u:upala]]-[[synonyms:b:bhoga]]---the next offering of food; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsā]]---to His place; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned.
translation: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade farewell to all the servants. After seeing the next offering of food to Lord Jagannātha, a function known as upala-bhoga, He returned to His own quarters.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.102
description: After finishing His noon duties, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ate His lunch, but He constantly remembered the remnants of Kṛṣṇa's food.
text:
> madhyāhna kariyā kailā bhikṣā nirvāhaṇa
> kṛṣṇādharāmṛta sadā antare smaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhyāhna]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---after finishing His noon duties; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:n:nirvāhaṇa]]---completed His lunch; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---the nectar from the lips of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---within Himself; [[synonyms:s:smaraṇa]]---remembering.
translation: After finishing His noon duties, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ate His lunch, but He constantly remembered the remnants of Kṛṣṇa's food.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.103
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed His external activities, but His mind was filled with ecstatic love. With great difficulty He tried to restrain His mind, but it would always be overwhelmed by very deep ecstasy.
text:
> bāhya-kṛtya karena, preme garagara mana
> kaṣṭe samvaraṇa karena, āveśa saghana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛtya]]---external activities; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---performs; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:g:garagara]]---filled; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:k:kaṣṭe]]---with great difficulty; [[synonyms:s:samvaraṇa]] [[synonyms:k:karena]]---restricts; [[synonyms:ā:āveśa]]---ecstasy; [[synonyms:s:saghana]]---very deep.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed His external activities, but His mind was filled with ecstatic love. With great difficulty He tried to restrain His mind, but it would always be overwhelmed by very deep ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.104
description: After finishing His evening duties, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat down with His personal associates in a secluded place and discussed the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa in great jubilation.
text:
> sandhyā-kṛtya kari' punaḥ nija-gaṇa-saṅge
> nibhṛte vasilā nānā-kṛṣṇa-kathā-raṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sandhyā]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛtya]]---the evening duties; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---after performing; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---along with His personal associates; [[synonyms:n:nibhṛte]]---in a solitary place; [[synonyms:v:vasilā]]---sat down; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---of topics of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---in the jubilation.
translation: After finishing His evening duties, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat down with His personal associates in a secluded place and discussed the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa in great jubilation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.105
description: Following the indications of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Govinda brought the prasāda of Lord Jagannātha. The Lord sent some to Paramānanda Purī and Brahmānanda Bhāratī.
text:
> prabhura iṅgite govinda prasāda ānilā
> purī-bhāratīre prabhu kichu pāṭhāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:i:iṅgite]]---by the indication of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]---Govinda; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:ā:ānilā]]---brought the remnants of the food of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:p:purī]]---to Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:b:bhāratīre]]---to Brahmānanda Bhāratī; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāilā]]---sent.
translation: Following the indications of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Govinda brought the prasāda of Lord Jagannātha. The Lord sent some to Paramānanda Purī and Brahmānanda Bhāratī.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.106
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then gave shares of the prasāda to Rāmānanda Rāya, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and all the other devotees.
text:
> rāmānanda-sārvabhauma-svarūpādi-gaṇe
> sabāre prasāda dila kariyā baṇṭane
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:s:sārvabhauma]]---Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by; [[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---unto them; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---unto all of them; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---the remnants of the food of Lord Jagannātha; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---delivered; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:b:baṇṭane]]---making shares.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then gave shares of the prasāda to Rāmānanda Rāya, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and all the other devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.107
description: As they tasted the uncommon sweetness and fragrance of the prasāda, everyone's mind was struck with wonder.
text:
> prasādera saurabhya-mādhurya kari' āsvādana
> alaukika āsvāde sabāra vismita haila mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prasādera]]---of the //prasāda//; [[synonyms:s:saurabhya]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---the sweetness and fragrance; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasting; [[synonyms:a:alaukika]]---uncommon; [[synonyms:ā:āsvāde]]---by the taste; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:v:vismita]]---struck with wonder; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: As they tasted the uncommon sweetness and fragrance of the prasāda, everyone's mind was struck with wonder.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.108-109
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "These ingredients, such as sugar, camphor, black pepper, cardamom, cloves, butter, spices and licorice, are all material. Everyone has tasted these material substances before.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---"ei saba haya 'prākṛta' dravya
> aikṣava, karpūra, marica, elāica, lavaṅga, gavya
>
> rasavāsa, guḍatvaka-ādi yata saba
> 'prākṛta' vastura svāda sabāra anubhava
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:p:prākṛta]]---material; [[synonyms:d:dravya]]---ingredients; [[synonyms:a:aikṣava]]---sugar; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]---camphor; [[synonyms:m:marica]]---black pepper; [[synonyms:e:elāica]]---cardamom; [[synonyms:l:lavaṅga]]---cloves; [[synonyms:g:gavya]]---butter; [[synonyms:r:rasavāsa]]---spices; [[synonyms:g:guḍatvaka]]---licorice; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and so on; [[synonyms:y:yata]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---each and every one of them; [[synonyms:p:prākṛta]]---material; [[synonyms:v:vastura]]---of ingredients; [[synonyms:s:svāda]]---taste; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---everyone's; [[synonyms:a:anubhava]]---experience.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "These ingredients, such as sugar, camphor, black pepper, cardamom, cloves, butter, spices and licorice, are all material. Everyone has tasted these material substances before.
purport: The word //prākṛta// refers to things tasted for the sense gratification of the conditioned soul. Such things are limited by the material laws. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to make the point that material things have already been experienced by materially absorbed persons who are interested only in sense gratification.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.11
description: He would beg remnants of food from such Vaiṣṇavas, and if he did not receive any, he would hide.
text:
> tāṅra ṭhāñi śeṣa-pātra layena māgiyā
> kāhāṅ nā pāya, tabe rahe lukāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---from them; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---plates of remnants; [[synonyms:l:layena]]---takes; [[synonyms:m:māgiyā]]---begging; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---does not get; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remains; [[synonyms:l:lukāñā]]---hiding.
translation: He would beg remnants of food from such Vaiṣṇavas, and if he did not receive any, he would hide.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.110
description: "However," the Lord continued, "in these ingredients there are extraordinary tastes and uncommon fragrances. Just taste them and see the difference in the experience.
text:
> sei dravye eta āsvāda, gandha lokātīta
> āsvāda kariyā dekha,---sabāra pratīta
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:dravye]]---in such material things; [[synonyms:e:eta]]---so much; [[synonyms:ā:āsvāda]]---pleasing taste; [[synonyms:g:gandha]]---fragrance; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:a:atīta]]---never experienced by any common man; [[synonyms:ā:āsvāda]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---tasting; [[synonyms:d:dekha]]---see; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:p:pratīta]]---experience.
translation: "However," the Lord continued, "in these ingredients there are extraordinary tastes and uncommon fragrances. Just taste them and see the difference in the experience.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.111
description: "Apart from the taste, even the fragrance pleases the mind and makes one forget any other sweetness besides its own.
text:
> āsvāda dūre rahu, yāra gandhe māte mana
> āpanā vinā anya mādhurya karāya vismaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āsvāda]]---the taste; [[synonyms:d:dūre]] [[synonyms:r:rahu]]---leave aside; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:g:gandhe]]---by the fragrance; [[synonyms:m:māte]]---becomes pleased; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:ā:āpanā]] [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---besides itself; [[synonyms:a:anya]]---different; [[synonyms:m:mādhurya]]---sweetness; [[synonyms:k:karāya]] [[synonyms:v:vismaraṇa]]---causes to forget.
translation: "Apart from the taste, even the fragrance pleases the mind and makes one forget any other sweetness besides its own.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.112
description: "Therefore, it is to be understood that the spiritual nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips has touched these ordinary ingredients and transferred to them all their spiritual qualities.
text:
> tāte ei dravye kṛṣṇādhara-sparśa haila
> adharera guṇa saba ihāte sañcārila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:d:dravye]]---in these ingredients; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:adhara]]---of the lips of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sparśa]]---touch; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:a:adharera]]---of the lips; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---attributes; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:i:ihāte]]---in these ingredients; [[synonyms:s:sañcārila]]---have become transferred.
translation: "Therefore, it is to be understood that the spiritual nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips has touched these ordinary ingredients and transferred to them all their spiritual qualities.
purport: Since everyone had previously tasted these ingredients, why had they become extraordinary and spiritually tasteful? This was proof that food, //prasāda,// becomes uncommonly flavorful and tasteful by touching Kṛṣṇa's lips.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.113
description: "An uncommon, greatly enchanting fragrance and taste that makes one forget all other experiences are attributes of Kṛṣṇa's lips.
text:
> alaukika-gandha-svāda, anya-vismāraṇa
> mahā-mādaka haya ei kṛṣṇādharera guṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:alaukika]]---uncommon; [[synonyms:g:gandha]]---fragrance; [[synonyms:s:svāda]]---taste; [[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:v:vismāraṇa]]---forgetting all others; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:m:mādaka]]---highly enchanting; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:adharera]]---of the lips of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---attributes.
translation: "An uncommon, greatly enchanting fragrance and taste that makes one forget all other experiences are attributes of Kṛṣṇa's lips.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.114
description: "This prasāda has been made available only as a result of many pious activities. Now taste it with great faith and devotion."
text:
> aneka 'sukṛte' ihā hañāche samprāpti
> sabe ei āsvāda kara kari' mahā-bhakti"
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aneka]]---many; [[synonyms:s:sukṛte]]---by pious activities; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this; [[synonyms:h:hañāche]] [[synonyms:s:samprāpti]]---has become available; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of you; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this //prasāda//; [[synonyms:ā:āsvāda]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---taste; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---with great devotion.
translation: "This prasāda has been made available only as a result of many pious activities. Now taste it with great faith and devotion."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.115
description: Loudly chanting the holy name of Hari, all of them tasted the prasāda. As they tasted it, their minds became mad in the ecstasy of love.
text:
> hari-dhvani kari' sabe kailā āsvādana
> āsvādite preme matta ha-ila sabāra mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hari]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvani]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---loudly resounding the holy name of Hari; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasted; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādite]]---as soon as they tasted; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:m:matta]]---maddened; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds of all.
translation: Loudly chanting the holy name of Hari, all of them tasted the prasāda. As they tasted it, their minds became mad in the ecstasy of love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.116
description: In ecstatic love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered Rāmānanda Rāya to recite some verses. Thus Rāmānanda Rāya spoke as follows.
text:
> premāveśe mahāprabhu yabe ājñā dilā
> rāmānanda-rāya śloka paḍite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---ordered; [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verses; [[synonyms:p:paḍite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to recite.
translation: In ecstatic love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ordered Rāmānanda Rāya to recite some verses. Thus Rāmānanda Rāya spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.117
description: "O hero of charity, please deliver unto us the nectar of Your lips. That nectar increases lusty desires for enjoyment and diminishes lamentation in the material world. Kindly give us the nectar of Your lips, which are touched by Your transcendentally vibrating flute, for that nectar makes all human beings forget all other attachments."
text:
> surata-vardhanaṁ śoka-nāśanaṁ
> svarita-veṇunā suṣṭhu-cumbitam
> itara-rāga-vismāraṇaṁ nṛṇāṁ
> vitara vīra nas te 'dharāmṛtam
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:surata]]-[[synonyms:v:vardhanam]]---which increases the lusty desire for enjoyment; [[synonyms:ś:śoka]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśanam]]---which vanquishes all lamentation; [[synonyms:s:svarita]]-[[synonyms:v:veṇunā]]---by the vibrating flute; [[synonyms:s:suṣṭhu]]---nicely; [[synonyms:c:cumbitam]]---touched; [[synonyms:i:itara]]-[[synonyms:r:rāga]]-[[synonyms:v:vismāraṇam]]---which causes forgetfulness of all other attachment; [[synonyms:n:nṛṇām]]---of the human beings; [[synonyms:v:vitara]]---please deliver; [[synonyms:v:vīra]]---O hero of charity; [[synonyms:n:naḥ]]---unto us; [[synonyms:t:te]]---Your; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛtam]]---the nectar of the lips.
translation: "O hero of charity, please deliver unto us the nectar of Your lips. That nectar increases lusty desires for enjoyment and diminishes lamentation in the material world. Kindly give us the nectar of Your lips, which are touched by Your transcendentally vibrating flute, for that nectar makes all human beings forget all other attachments."
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.31.14).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.118
description: Upon hearing Rāmānanda Rāya quote this verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very satisfied. Then He recited the following verse, which had been spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī in great anxiety.
text:
> śloka śuni' mahāprabhu mahā-tuṣṭa hailā
> rādhāra utkaṇṭhā-śloka paḍite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing the verse; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:t:tuṣṭa]]---very satisfied; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:r:rādhāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:u:utkaṇṭhā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---a verse pertaining to the anxiety; [[synonyms:p:paḍite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to recite.
translation: Upon hearing Rāmānanda Rāya quote this verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very satisfied. Then He recited the following verse, which had been spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī in great anxiety.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.119
description: "My dear friend, the all-surpassing nectar from the lips of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, can be obtained only after many, many pious activities. For the beautiful gopīs of Vṛndāvana, that nectar vanquishes the desire for all other tastes. Madana-mohana always chews pan that surpasses the nectar of heaven. He is certainly increasing the desires of My tongue."
text:
> vrajātula-kulāṅganetara-rasāli-tṛṣṇā-hara-
> pradīvyad-adharāmṛtaḥ sukṛti-labhya-phelā-lavaḥ
> sudhā-jid-ahivallikā-sudala-vīṭikā-carvitaḥ
> sa me madana-mohanaḥ sakhi tanoti jihvā-spṛhām
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vraja]]---of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:a:atula]]---incomparable; [[synonyms:k:kulāṅgana]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:i:itara]]---other; [[synonyms:r:rasa]]-[[synonyms:ā:āli]]---for tastes or mellows; [[synonyms:t:tṛṣṇā]]---desire; [[synonyms:h:hara]]---vanquishing; [[synonyms:p:pradīvyat]]---all-surpassing; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛtaḥ]]---whose nectar emanating from the lips; [[synonyms:s:sukṛti]]---after many pious activities; [[synonyms:l:labhya]]---obtainable; [[synonyms:p:phelā]]---of the nectar of whose lips; [[synonyms:l:lavaḥ]]---a small portion; [[synonyms:s:sudhā]]-[[synonyms:j:jit]]---conquering the nectar; [[synonyms:a:ahivallikā]]---of the betel plant; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:d:dala]]---made from selected leaves; [[synonyms:v:vīṭikā]]---pan; [[synonyms:c:carvitaḥ]]---chewing; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mohanaḥ]]---Madana-mohana; [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---My dear friend; [[synonyms:t:tanoti]]---increases; [[synonyms:j:jihvā]]---of the tongue; [[synonyms:s:spṛhām]]---desire.
translation: "My dear friend, the all-surpassing nectar from the lips of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, can be obtained only after many, many pious activities. For the beautiful gopīs of Vṛndāvana, that nectar vanquishes the desire for all other tastes. Madana-mohana always chews pan that surpasses the nectar of heaven. He is certainly increasing the desires of My tongue."
purport: This verse is found in the //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (8.8).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.12
description: After the Vaiṣṇavas finished eating, they would throw away their dishes or leaves, and Kālidāsa would come out of hiding, take the leaves and lick up the remnants.
text:
> bhojana karile pātra phelāñā yāya
> lukāñā sei pātra āni' cāṭi' khāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhojana]] [[synonyms:k:karile]]---after eating; [[synonyms:p:pātra]]---the plate; [[synonyms:p:phelāñā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---is thrown away; [[synonyms:l:lukāñā]]---hiding; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:p:pātra]]---that plate; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:c:cāṭi']] [[synonyms:k:khāya]]---he licks up.
translation: After the Vaiṣṇavas finished eating, they would throw away their dishes or leaves, and Kālidāsa would come out of hiding, take the leaves and lick up the remnants.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.120
description: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was overwhelmed by ecstatic loving emotions. Talking like a madman, He began to explain the meaning of the two verses.
text:
> eta kahi' gaura-prabhu bhāvāviṣṭa hañā
> dui ślokera artha kare pralāpa kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:k:kahi']]---saying this; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---overwhelmed by ecstatic loving emotions; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:ś:ślokera]]---of the two verses; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---makes; [[synonyms:p:pralāpa]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---talking like a madman.
translation: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was overwhelmed by ecstatic loving emotions. Talking like a madman, He began to explain the meaning of the two verses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.121-122
description: "My dear lover," He said, "let Me describe some of the characteristics of Your transcendental lips. They agitate the mind and body of everyone, they increase lusty desires for enjoyment, they destroy the burden of material happiness and lamentation, and they make one forget all material tastes. The whole world falls under their control. They vanquish shame, religion and patience, especially in women. Indeed, they inspire madness in the minds of all women. Your lips increase the greed of the tongue and thus attract it. Considering all this, we see that the activities of Your transcendental lips are always perplexing.
text:
> tanu-mana karāya kṣobha, bāḍāya surata-lobha,
> harṣa-śokādi-bhāra vināśaya
> pāsarāya anya rasa, jagat kare ātma-vaśa,
> lajjā, dharma, dhairya kare kṣaya
> nāgara, śuna tomāra adhara-carita
> mātāya nārīra mana, jihvā kare ākarṣaṇa,
> vicārite saba viparīta
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tanu]]---body; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---cause; [[synonyms:k:kṣobha]]---agitation; [[synonyms:b:bāḍāya]]---increase; [[synonyms:s:surata]]-[[synonyms:l:lobha]]---lusty desires for enjoyment; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---of jubilation; [[synonyms:ś:śoka]]---lamentation; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and so on; [[synonyms:b:bhāra]]---burden; [[synonyms:v:vināśaya]]---destroy; [[synonyms:p:pāsarāya]]---cause to forget; [[synonyms:a:anya]] [[synonyms:r:rasa]]---other tastes; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the whole world; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---make; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---under their control; [[synonyms:l:lajjā]]---shame; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---religion; [[synonyms:d:dhairya]]---patience; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:k:kṣaya]]---vanquish; [[synonyms:n:nāgara]]---O lover; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]---of lips; [[synonyms:c:carita]]---the characteristics; [[synonyms:m:mātāya]]---madden; [[synonyms:n:nārīra]]---of women; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:j:jihvā]]---tongue; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaṇa]]---attract; [[synonyms:v:vicārite]]---considering; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:v:viparīta]]---opposite.
translation: "My dear lover," He said, "let Me describe some of the characteristics of Your transcendental lips. They agitate the mind and body of everyone, they increase lusty desires for enjoyment, they destroy the burden of material happiness and lamentation, and they make one forget all material tastes. The whole world falls under their control. They vanquish shame, religion and patience, especially in women. Indeed, they inspire madness in the minds of all women. Your lips increase the greed of the tongue and thus attract it. Considering all this, we see that the activities of Your transcendental lips are always perplexing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.123
description: "My dear Kṛṣṇa, since You are a male, it is not very extraordinary that the attraction of Your lips can disturb the minds of women. I am ashamed to say this, but Your lips sometimes attract even Your flute, which is also considered a male. It likes to drink the nectar of Your lips, and thus it also forgets all other tastes.
text:
> āchuka nārīra kāya, kahite vāsiye lāja,
> tomāra adhara baḍa dhṛṣṭa-rāya
> puruṣe kare ākarṣaṇa, āpanā piyāite mana,
> anya-rasa saba pāsarāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āchuka]]---let it be; [[synonyms:n:nārīra]]---of women; [[synonyms:k:kāya]]---the bodies; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:v:vāsiye]]---I feel; [[synonyms:l:lāja]]---shame; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]---lips; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very much; [[synonyms:d:dhṛṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:r:rāya]]---impudent; [[synonyms:p:puruṣe]]---the male; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaṇa]]---they attract; [[synonyms:ā:āpanā]]---themselves; [[synonyms:p:piyāite]]---causing to drink; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---other tastes; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:p:pāsarāya]]---cause to forget.
translation: "My dear Kṛṣṇa, since You are a male, it is not very extraordinary that the attraction of Your lips can disturb the minds of women. I am ashamed to say this, but Your lips sometimes attract even Your flute, which is also considered a male. It likes to drink the nectar of Your lips, and thus it also forgets all other tastes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.124
description: "Aside from conscious living beings, even unconscious matter is sometimes made conscious by Your lips. Therefore, Your lips are great magicians. Paradoxically, although Your flute is nothing but dry wood, Your lips make it drink their nectar. They create a mind and senses in the dry wooden flute and give it transcendental bliss.
text:
> sacetana rahu dūre, acetana sacetana kare,
> tomāra adhara---baḍa vājikara
> tomāra veṇu śuṣkendhana, tāra janmāya indriya-mana,
> tāre āpanā piyāya nirantara
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:c:cetana]]---conscious living beings; [[synonyms:r:rahu]] [[synonyms:d:dūre]]---leave aside; [[synonyms:a:acetana]]---unconscious; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:c:cetana]]---conscious; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---make; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]---lips; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---very great; [[synonyms:v:vājikara]]---magicians; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:v:veṇu]]---flute; [[synonyms:ś:śuṣka]]-[[synonyms:i:in]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---dry wood; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:j:janmāya]]---creates; [[synonyms:i:indriya]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the senses and mind; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---the flute; [[synonyms:ā:āpanā]]---themselves; [[synonyms:p:piyāya]]---cause to drink; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---constantly.
translation: "Aside from conscious living beings, even unconscious matter is sometimes made conscious by Your lips. Therefore, Your lips are great magicians. Paradoxically, although Your flute is nothing but dry wood, Your lips make it drink their nectar. They create a mind and senses in the dry wooden flute and give it transcendental bliss.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.125
description: "That flute is a very cunning male who drinks again and again the taste of another male's lips. It advertises its qualities and says to the gopīs, 'O gopīs, if you are so proud of being women, come forward and enjoy your property—the nectar of the lips of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
text:
> veṇu dhṛṣṭa-puruṣa hañā, puruṣādhara piyā piyā,
> gopī-gaṇe jānāya nija-pāna
> 'aho śuna, gopī-gaṇa, bale piṅo tomāra dhana,
> tomāra yadi thāke abhimāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:veṇu]]---the flute; [[synonyms:d:dhṛṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]---a cunning male; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:a:adhara]]---the lips of the male; [[synonyms:p:piyā]] [[synonyms:p:piyā]]---drinking and drinking; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---unto the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:j:jānāya]]---informs; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:p:pāna]]---own drinking; [[synonyms:a:aho]]---oh; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---//gopīs//; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---says; [[synonyms:p:piṅo]]---drink; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---property; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:t:thāke]]---there is; [[synonyms:a:abhimāna]]---pride.
translation: "That flute is a very cunning male who drinks again and again the taste of another male's lips. It advertises its qualities and says to the gopīs, 'O gopīs, if you are so proud of being women, come forward and enjoy your property---the nectar of the lips of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.126
description: "Thereupon, the flute said angrily to Me, 'Give up Your shame, fear and religion and come drink the lips of Kṛṣṇa. On that condition, I shall give up my attachment for them. If You do not give up Your shame and fear, however, I shall continuously drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips. I am slightly fearful because You also have the right to drink that nectar, but as for the others, I consider them like straw.'
text:
> tabe more krodha kari;, lajjā bhaya, dharma, chāḍi',
> chāḍi' dimu, kara āsi' pāna
> nahe pimu nirantara, tomāya mora nāhika ḍara,
> anye dekhoṅ tṛṇera samāna
