translation: "Thereupon, the flute said angrily to Me, 'Give up Your shame, fear and religion and come drink the lips of Kṛṣṇa. On that condition, I shall give up my attachment for them. If You do not give up Your shame and fear, however, I shall continuously drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips. I am slightly fearful because You also have the right to drink that nectar, but as for the others, I consider them like straw.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.127
description: "The nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips, combined with the vibration of His flute, attracts all the people of the three worlds. However, if we gopīs remain patient out of respect for religious principles, the flute then criticizes us.
text:
> adharāmṛta nija-svare, sañcāriyā sei bale,
> ākarṣaya trijagat-jana
> āmarā dharma-bhaya kari', rahi' yadi dhairya dhari',
> tabe āmāya kare viḍambana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---the nectar of the lips; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:s:svare]]---with the vibration of the flute; [[synonyms:s:sañcāriyā]]---combining; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---by strength; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaya]]---attract; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---the people of the three worlds; [[synonyms:ā:āmarā]]---we; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---religion; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---because of; [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---remaining; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:d:dhairya]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---keeping patient; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:ā:āmāya]]---us; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:v:viḍambana]]---criticizes.
translation: "The nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips, combined with the vibration of His flute, attracts all the people of the three worlds. However, if we gopīs remain patient out of respect for religious principles, the flute then criticizes us.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.128
description: "The nectar of Your lips and vibration of Your flute join together to loosen our belts and induce us to give up shame and religion, even before our superiors. As if catching us by our hair, they forcibly take us away and surrender us unto You to become Your maidservants. Hearing of these incidents, people laugh at us. We have thus become completely subordinate to the flute.
text:
> nīvi khasāya guru-āge, lajjā-dharma karāya tyāge,
> keśe dhari' yena lañā yāya
> āni' karāya tomāra dāsī, śuni' loka kare hāsi',
> ei-mata nārīre nācāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nīvi]]---the belts; [[synonyms:k:khasāya]]---cause to loosen; [[synonyms:g:guru]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---before superiors; [[synonyms:l:lajjā]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---shame and religion; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---induce; [[synonyms:t:tyāge]]---to give up; [[synonyms:k:keśe]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching by the hair; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:l:lañā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---takes us away; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:k:karāya]]---induce to become; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:d:dāsī]]---maidservants; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:h:hāsi']]---laugh; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:n:nārīre]]---women; [[synonyms:n:nācāya]]---cause to dance.
translation: "The nectar of Your lips and vibration of Your flute join together to loosen our belts and induce us to give up shame and religion, even before our superiors. As if catching us by our hair, they forcibly take us away and surrender us unto You to become Your maidservants. Hearing of these incidents, people laugh at us. We have thus become completely subordinate to the flute.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.129
description: "This flute is nothing but a dry stick of bamboo, but it becomes our master and insults us in so many ways that it forces us into a predicament. What can we do but tolerate it? The mother of a thief cannot cry loudly for justice when the thief is punished. Therefore we simply remain silent.
text:
> śuṣka bāṅśera lāṭhikhāna, eta kare apamāna,
> ei daśā karila, gosāñi
> nā sahi' ki karite pāri, tāhe rahi mauna dhari',
> corāra māke ḍāki' kāndite nāi
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuṣka]]---dry; [[synonyms:b:bāṅśera]]---of bamboo; [[synonyms:l:lāṭhi]]-[[synonyms:k:khāna]]---a stick; [[synonyms:e:eta]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:a:apamāna]]---insults; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---condition; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---made; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---the master; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:s:sahi']]---not tolerating; [[synonyms:k:ki]]---what; [[synonyms:k:karite]] [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---can we do; [[synonyms:t:tāhe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:r:rahi]]---we remain; [[synonyms:m:mauna]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---keeping silent; [[synonyms:c:corāra]]---of a thief; [[synonyms:m:māke]]---for the mother; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍāki']]---calling; [[synonyms:k:kāndite]]---to cry; [[synonyms:n:nāi]]---is not possible.
translation: "This flute is nothing but a dry stick of bamboo, but it becomes our master and insults us in so many ways that it forces us into a predicament. What can we do but tolerate it? The mother of a thief cannot cry loudly for justice when the thief is punished. Therefore we simply remain silent.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.13
description: He would also take gifts to the homes of Vaiṣṇavas born in śūdra families. Then he would hide and eat the remnants of food they threw away in this manner.
text:
> śūdra-vaiṣṇavera ghare yāya bheṭa lañā
> ei-mata tāṅra ucchiṣṭa khāya lukāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śūdra]]-[[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavera]]---of Vaiṣṇavas born in //śūdra// families; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at the homes; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes; [[synonyms:b:bheṭa]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking gifts; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---their; [[synonyms:u:ucchiṣṭa]]---remnants of food; [[synonyms:k:khāya]]---eats; [[synonyms:l:lukāñā]]---hiding.
translation: He would also take gifts to the homes of Vaiṣṇavas born in śūdra families. Then he would hide and eat the remnants of food they threw away in this manner.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.130
description: "That is the policy of these lips. Just consider the other injustices. Everything that touches those lips-including food, drink or betel-becomes just like nectar. It is then called kṛṣṇa-phelā, or remnants left by Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> adharera ei rīti, āra śuna kunīti,
> se adhara-sane yāra melā
> sei bhakṣya-bhojya-pāna, haya amṛta-samāna,
> nāma tāra haya 'kṛṣṇa-phelā'
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:adharera]]---of the lips; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:r:rīti]]---policy; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---other; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:k:kunīti]]---injustices; [[synonyms:s:se]]---those; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]---lips; [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:m:melā]]---meeting; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:b:bhakṣya]]---eatables; [[synonyms:b:bhojya]]---foods; [[synonyms:p:pāna]]---drink or betel; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---become; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:s:samāna]]---like nectar; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of those; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:phelā]]---the remnants of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "That is the policy of these lips. Just consider the other injustices. Everything that touches those lips-including food, drink or betel-becomes just like nectar. It is then called kṛṣṇa-phelā, or remnants left by Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.131
description: "Even after much prayer, the demigods themselves cannot obtain even a small portion of the remnants of such food. Just imagine the pride of those remnants! Only a person who has acted piously for many, many births and has thus become a devotee can obtain the remnants of such food.
text:
> se phelāra eka lava, nā pāya devatā saba,
> e dambhe kebā pātiyāya?
> bahu-janma puṇya kare, tabe 'sukṛti' nāma dhare,
> se 'sukṛte' tāra lava pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:p:phelāra]]---of those remnants; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:l:lava]]---small particle; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---do not get; [[synonyms:d:devatā]]---the demigods; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:e:e]] [[synonyms:d:dambhe]]---this pride; [[synonyms:k:kebā]]---who; [[synonyms:p:pātiyāya]]---can believe; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:j:janma]]---for many births; [[synonyms:p:puṇya]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---acts piously; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:s:sukṛti]]---one who performs pious activities; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the name; [[synonyms:d:dhare]]---bears; [[synonyms:s:se]]---those; [[synonyms:s:sukṛte]]---by pious activities; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:l:lava]]---a fraction; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---one can get.
translation: "Even after much prayer, the demigods themselves cannot obtain even a small portion of the remnants of such food. Just imagine the pride of those remnants! Only a person who has acted piously for many, many births and has thus become a devotee can obtain the remnants of such food.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.132
description: "The betel chewed by Kṛṣṇa is priceless, and the remnants of such chewed betel from His mouth are said to be the essence of nectar. When the gopīs accept these remnants, their mouths become like His spittoons.
text:
> kṛṣṇa ye khāya tāmbūla, kahe tāra nāhi rnūla,
> tāhe āra dambha-paripāṭī
> tāra yebā udgāra, tāre kaya 'amṛta-sa-ra',
> gopīra mukha kare 'ālabāṭī'
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---what; [[synonyms:k:khāya]]---chews; [[synonyms:t:tāmbūla]]---the betel; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it is said; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of it; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:m:mūla]]---price; [[synonyms:t:tāhe]]---over and above that; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---also; [[synonyms:d:dambha]]-[[synonyms:p:paripāṭī]]---complete pride; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:y:yebā]]---whatever; [[synonyms:u:udgāra]]---coming out; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---is called; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:s:sāra]]---the essence of the nectar; [[synonyms:g:gopīra]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---the mouth; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---makes; [[synonyms:ā:ālabāṭī]]---spittoon.
translation: "The betel chewed by Kṛṣṇa is priceless, and the remnants of such chewed betel from His mouth are said to be the essence of nectar. When the gopīs accept these remnants, their mouths become like His spittoons.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.133
description: "Therefore, My dear Kṛṣṇa, please give up all the tricks You have set up so expertly. Do not try to kill the life of the gopīs with the vibration of Your flute. Because of Your joking and laughing, You are becoming responsible for the killing of women. It would be better for You to satisfy us by giving us the charity of the nectar of Your lips."
text:
> e-saba---tomāra kuṭināṭi, chāḍa ei paripāṭī,
> veṇu-dvāre kāṅhe hara' prāṇa
> āpanāra hāsi lāgi', naha nārīra vadha-bhāgī,
> deha' nijādharāmṛta-dāna"
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all these; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:k:kuṭināṭi]]---tricks; [[synonyms:c:chāḍa]]---give up; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:p:paripāṭī]]---very expert activities; [[synonyms:v:veṇu]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---by the flute; [[synonyms:k:kāṅhe]]---why; [[synonyms:h:hara]]---You take away; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]---life; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāra]]---Your own; [[synonyms:h:hāsi]]---laughing; [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for the matter of; [[synonyms:n:naha]]---do not be; [[synonyms:n:nārīra]]---of women; [[synonyms:v:vadha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgī]]---responsible for killing; [[synonyms:d:deha']]---kindly give; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---the nectar of Your lips; [[synonyms:d:dāna]]---charity.
translation: "Therefore, My dear Kṛṣṇa, please give up all the tricks You have set up so expertly. Do not try to kill the life of the gopīs with the vibration of Your flute. Because of Your joking and laughing, You are becoming responsible for the killing of women. It would be better for You to satisfy us by giving us the charity of the nectar of Your lips."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.134
description: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was talking like this, His mind changed. His anger subsided, but His mental agitation increased.
text:
> kahite kahite prabhura mana phiri' gela
> krodha-aṁśa śānta haila, utkaṇṭhā bāḍila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---talking and talking; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:p:phiri']] [[synonyms:g:gela]]---became changed; [[synonyms:k:krodha]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---the part of anger; [[synonyms:ś:śānta]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became pacified; [[synonyms:u:utkaṇṭhā]]---agitation of the mind; [[synonyms:b:bāḍila]]---increased.
translation: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was talking like this, His mind changed. His anger subsided, but His mental agitation increased.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.135
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "This nectar from Kṛṣṇa's lips is supremely difficult to obtain, but if one gets some, his life becomes successful.
text:
> parama durlabha ei kṛṣṇādharāmṛta
> tāhā yei pāya, tāra saphala jīvita
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:parama]]---supremely; [[synonyms:d:durlabha]]---difficult to obtain; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---the nectar from the lips; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---one who; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:t:ta]]-[[synonyms:r:ra]]---his; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]---successful; [[synonyms:j:jīvita]]---life.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "This nectar from Kṛṣṇa's lips is supremely difficult to obtain, but if one gets some, his life becomes successful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.136
description: "When a person competent to drink that nectar does not do so, that shameless person continues his life uselessly.
text:
> yogya hañā keha karite nā pāya pāna
> tathāpi se nirlajja, vṛthā dhare prāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yogya]]---competent; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---anyone; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to do; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---does not get; [[synonyms:p:pāna]]---drinking; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that person; [[synonyms:n:nirlajja]]---shameless; [[synonyms:v:vṛthā]]---uselessly; [[synonyms:d:dhare]] [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]---continues life.
translation: "When a person competent to drink that nectar does not do so, that shameless person continues his life uselessly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.137
description: "There are persons who are unfit to drink that nectar but who nevertheless drink it continuously, whereas some who are suitable never get it and thus die of greed.
text:
> ayogya hañā tāhā keha sadā pāna kare
> yogya jana nāhi pāya, lobhe mātra mare
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ayogya]]---unfit; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:p:pāna]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---drinks; [[synonyms:y:yogya]] [[synonyms:j:jana]]---the competent person; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---does not get; [[synonyms:l:lobhe]]---out of greed; [[synonyms:m:mātra]]---simply; [[synonyms:m:mare]]---dies.
translation: "There are persons who are unfit to drink that nectar but who nevertheless drink it continuously, whereas some who are suitable never get it and thus die of greed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.138
description: "It is therefore to be understood that such an unfit person must have obtained the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips on the strength of some austerity."
text:
> tāte jāni,---kona tapasyāra āche bala
> ayogyere deoyāya kṛṣṇādharāmṛta-phala
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I can understand; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---some; [[synonyms:t:tapasyāra]]---of austerity; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---there is; [[synonyms:b:bala]]---strength; [[synonyms:a:ayogyere]]---unto the unfit; [[synonyms:d:deoyāya]]---delivers; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---the result.
translation: "It is therefore to be understood that such an unfit person must have obtained the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips on the strength of some austerity."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.139
description: Again Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said to Rāmānanda Rāya, "Please say something. I want to hear." Understanding the situation, Rāmānanda Rāya recited the following words of the gopīs.
text:
> 'kaha rāma-rāya, kichu śunite haya mana'
> bhāva jāni' paḍe rāya gopīra vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---speak; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---something; [[synonyms:ś:śunite]]---to hear; [[synonyms:h:haya]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---I wish; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the situation; [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---understanding; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]] [[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Rāmānanda Rāya cites; [[synonyms:g:gopīra]] [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---the words of the //gopīs.//
translation: Again Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said to Rāmānanda Rāya, "Please say something. I want to hear." Understanding the situation, Rāmānanda Rāya recited the following words of the gopīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.14
description: There was a great Vaiṣṇava named Jhaḍu Ṭhākura, who belonged to the bhūṅimāli caste. Kālidāsa went to his home, taking mangoes with him.
text:
> bhūṅimāli-jāti, 'vaiṣṇava'---'jhaḍu' tāṅra nāma
> āmra-phala lañā teṅho gelā tāṅra sthāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhūṅimāli]]-[[synonyms:j:jāti]]---belonging to the //bhūṅimāli// caste; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---a great devotee; [[synonyms:j:jhaḍu]]---Jhaḍu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---name; [[synonyms:ā:āmra]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]---mango fruits; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---to his place.
translation: There was a great Vaiṣṇava named Jhaḍu Ṭhākura, who belonged to the bhūṅimāli caste. Kālidāsa went to his home, taking mangoes with him.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura remarks that both Kālidāsa and Jhaḍu Ṭhākura are worshiped at a place called Śrīpāṭabāṭī, in the village known as Bhedo or Bhaduyā. This village is situated about three miles south of the village of Kṛṣṇapura, the birthplace of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, which is about one mile west of the Byāṇḍel junction of the Burdwan line. A post office there is named Devānanda-pura. Jhaḍu Ṭhākura used to worship the Deity of Śrī Madana-gopāla. The Deity is still worshiped by one Rāmaprasāda dāsa, who belongs to the //rāmāyet// community. It is said that the Deity worshiped by Kālidāsa had been worshiped until now in the village of Śaṅkhya on the bank of the Sarasvatī River, but the Deity has been taken away by a gentleman named Matilāla Caṭṭopādhyāya from the village of Triveṇī. The Deity is now being worshiped at his place.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.140
description: "My dear gopīs, what auspicious activities must the flute have performed to enjoy the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips independently and leave only a taste for the gopīs for whom that nectar is actually meant. The forefathers of the flute, the bamboo trees, shed tears of pleasure. His mother, the river, on whose bank the bamboo was born, feels jubilation, and therefore her blooming lotus flowers are standing like hair on her body."
text:
> gopyaḥ kim ācarad ayaṁ kuśalaṁ sma veṇur
> dāmodarādhara-sudhām api gopikānām
> bhuṅkte svayaṁ yad avaśiṣṭa-rasaṁ hradinyo
> hṛṣyat-tvaco 'śru mumucus taravo yathāryāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopyaḥ]]---O //gopīs//; [[synonyms:k:kim]]---what; [[synonyms:ā:ācarat]]---performed; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:k:kuśalam]]---auspicious activities; [[synonyms:s:sma]]---certainly; [[synonyms:v:veṇuḥ]]---flute; [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:s:sudhām]]---the nectar of the lips; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:g:gopikānām]]---which is owed to the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:b:bhuṅkte]]---enjoys; [[synonyms:s:svayam]]---independently; [[synonyms:y:yat]]---from which; [[synonyms:a:avaśiṣṭa]]---remaining; [[synonyms:r:rasam]]---the taste only; [[synonyms:h:hradinyaḥ]]---the rivers; [[synonyms:h:hṛṣyat]]---feeling jubilant; [[synonyms:t:tvacaḥ]]---whose bodies; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]---tears; [[synonyms:m:mumucuḥ]]---shed; [[synonyms:t:taravaḥ]]---the trees; [[synonyms:y:yathā]]---exactly like; [[synonyms:ā:āryāḥ]]---old forefathers.
translation: "My dear gopīs, what auspicious activities must the flute have performed to enjoy the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips independently and leave only a taste for the gopīs for whom that nectar is actually meant. The forefathers of the flute, the bamboo trees, shed tears of pleasure. His mother, the river, on whose bank the bamboo was born, feels jubilation, and therefore her blooming lotus flowers are standing like hair on her body."
purport: This is a verse quoted from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (10.21.9) regarding a discussion the //gopīs// had among themselves. As the autumn season began in Vṛndāvana, Lord Kṛṣṇa was tending the cows and blowing on His flute. The //gopīs// then began to praise Kṛṣṇa and discuss the fortunate position of His flute.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.141
description: Upon hearing the recitation of this verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became absorbed in ecstatic love, and with a greatly agitated mind He began to explain its meaning like a madman.
text:
> ei śloka śuni' prabhu bhāvāviṣṭa hañā
> utkaṇṭhāte artha kare pralāpa kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---this verse; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]]---absorbed in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming; [[synonyms:u:utkaṇṭhāte]]---in agitation of the mind; [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---makes the meaning; [[synonyms:p:pralāpa]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---talking like a madman.
translation: Upon hearing the recitation of this verse, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became absorbed in ecstatic love, and with a greatly agitated mind He began to explain its meaning like a madman.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.142
description: "Some gopīs said to other gopīs, 'Just see the astonishing pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Vrajendra! He will certainly marry all the gopīs of Vṛndāvana. Therefore, the gopīs know for certain that the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips is their own property and cannot be enjoyed by anyone else.'
text:
> eho vrajendra-nandana, vrajera kona kanyā-gaṇa,
> avaśya kariba pariṇaya
> se-sambandhe gopī-gaṇa, yāre māne nija-dhana,
> se sudhā anyera labhya naya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eho]]---this; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of Nanda Mahārāja; [[synonyms:v:vrajera]]---of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:k:kona]]---any; [[synonyms:k:kanyā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---//gopīs//; [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:k:kariba]] [[synonyms:p:pariṇaya]]---will marry; [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:s:sambandhe]]---in that connection; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:y:yāre]]---which; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---consider; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]]---the personal property; [[synonyms:s:se]] [[synonyms:s:sudhā]]---that nectar; [[synonyms:a:anyera]]---by others; [[synonyms:l:labhya]] [[synonyms:n:naya]]---is not obtainable.
translation: "Some gopīs said to other gopīs, 'Just see the astonishing pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Vrajendra! He will certainly marry all the gopīs of Vṛndāvana. Therefore, the gopīs know for certain that the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips is their own property and cannot be enjoyed by anyone else.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.143
description: "My dear gopīs, fully consider how many pious activities this flute performed in his past life. We do not know what places of pilgrimage he visited, what austerities he performed or what perfect mantra he chanted.
text:
> gopī-gaṇa, kaha saba kariyā vicāre
> kon tīrtha, kon tapa, kon siddha-mantra-japa,
> ei veṇu kaila janmāntare?
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---O //gopīs//; [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---say; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:v:vicāre]]---after full consideration; [[synonyms:k:kon]]---what; [[synonyms:t:tīrtha]]---holy places; [[synonyms:k:kon]]---what; [[synonyms:t:tapa]]---austerities; [[synonyms:k:kon]]---what; [[synonyms:s:siddha]]-[[synonyms:m:mantra]]-[[synonyms:j:japa]]---chanting of a perfect //mantra//; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:v:veṇu]]---flute; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:j:janma]]-[[synonyms:a:antare]]---in his past life.
translation: "My dear gopīs, fully consider how many pious activities this flute performed in his past life. We do not know what places of pilgrimage he visited, what austerities he performed or what perfect mantra he chanted.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.144
description: " 'This flute is utterly unfit because it is merely a dead bamboo stick. Moreover, it belongs to the male sex. Yet this flute is always drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips, which surpasses nectarean sweetness of every description. Only in hope of that nectar do the gopīs continue to live.
text:
> hena kṛṣṇādhara-sudhā, ye kaila amṛta mudhā,
> yāra āśāya gopī dhare prāṇa
> ei veṇu ayogya ati, sthāvara 'puruṣa-jāti',
> sei sudhā sadā kare pāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]---such; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:adhara]]---of Kṛṣṇa's lips; [[synonyms:s:sudhā]]---nectar; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---nectar; [[synonyms:m:mudhā]]---surpassed; [[synonyms:y:yāra]] [[synonyms:ā:āśāya]]---by hoping for which; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:d:dhare]] [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]---continue to live; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:v:veṇu]]---this flute; [[synonyms:a:ayogya]]---unfit; [[synonyms:a:ati]]---completely; [[synonyms:s:sthāvara]]---dead; [[synonyms:p:puruṣa]]-[[synonyms:j:jāti]]---belonging to the male class; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:sudhā]]---that nectar; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:p:pāna]]---drinks.
translation: “ 'This flute is utterly unfit because it is merely a dead bamboo stick. Moreover, it belongs to the male sex. Yet this flute is always drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips, which surpasses nectarean sweetness of every description. Only in hope of that nectar do the gopīs continue to live.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.145
description: " 'Although the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips is the absolute property of the gopīs, the flute, which is just an insignificant stick, is forcibly drinking that nectar and loudly inviting the gopīs to come drink it also. Just imagine the strength of the flute's austerities and good fortune. Even great devotees drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips after the flute has done so.
text:
> yāra dhana, nā kahe tāre, pāna kare balātkāre,
> pite tāre ḍākiyā jānāya
> tāra tapasyāra phala, dekha ihāra bhāgya-bala,
> ihāra ucchiṣṭa mahā-jane khāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---the property; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---does not speak; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---to them; [[synonyms:p:pāna]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---drinks; [[synonyms:b:balātkāre]]---by force; [[synonyms:p:pite]]---while drinking; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---unto them; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍākiyā]]---calling loudly; [[synonyms:j:jānāya]]---informs; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---its; [[synonyms:t:tapasyāra]]---of austerities; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---result; [[synonyms:d:dekha]]---see; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---its; [[synonyms:b:bhāgya]]-[[synonyms:b:bala]]---strength of fortune; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---its; [[synonyms:u:ucchiṣṭa]]---remnants; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:j:jane]]---great personalities; [[synonyms:k:khāya]]---drink.
translation: “ 'Although the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips is the absolute property of the gopīs, the flute, which is just an insignificant stick, is forcibly drinking that nectar and loudly inviting the gopīs to come drink it also. Just imagine the strength of the flute's austerities and good fortune. Even great devotees drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips after the flute has done so.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.146
description: " 'When Kṛṣṇa takes His bath in universally purifying rivers like the Yamunā and the Ganges of the celestial world, the great personalities of those rivers greedily and jubilantly drink the remnants of the nectarean juice from His lips.
text:
> mānasa-gaṅgā, kālindī, bhuvana-pāvanī nadī,
> kṛṣṇa yadi tāte kare snāna
> veṇura jhuṭādhara-rasa, hañā lobhe paravaśa,
> sei kāle harṣe kare pāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mānasa]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṅgā]]---the Ganges of the celestial world; [[synonyms:k:kālindī]]---the Yamunā; [[synonyms:b:bhuvana]]---the world; [[synonyms:p:pāvanī]]---purifying; [[synonyms:n:nadī]]---rivers; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---in those; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:s:snāna]]---takes a bath; [[synonyms:v:veṇura]]---of the flute; [[synonyms:j:jhuṭa]]-[[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---remnants of the juice of the lips; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:l:lobhe]]---by greed; [[synonyms:p:paravaśa]]---controlled; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at that time; [[synonyms:h:harṣe]]---in jubilation; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:p:pāna]]---drink.
translation: “ 'When Kṛṣṇa takes His bath in universally purifying rivers like the Yamunā and the Ganges of the celestial world, the great personalities of those rivers greedily and jubilantly drink the remnants of the nectarean juice from His lips.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.147
description: "Aside from the rivers, the trees standing on the banks like great ascetics and engaging in welfare activities for all living entities drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips by drawing water from the river with their roots. We cannot understand why they drink like that.
text:
> e-ta nārī rahu dūre, vṛkṣa saba tāra tīre,
> tapa kare para-upakārī
> nadīra śeṣa-rasa pāñā, mūla-dvāre ākarṣiyā,
> kene piye, bujhite nā pāri
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:t:ta]] [[synonyms:n:nārī]]---these women; [[synonyms:r:rahu]] [[synonyms:d:dūre]]---leaving aside; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]---the trees; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on their banks; [[synonyms:t:tapa]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---perform austerities; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:u:upakārī]]---benefactors of all other living entities; [[synonyms:n:nadīra]]---of the rivers; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]]---the remnants of the nectarean juice; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:m:mūla]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---by the roots; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣiyā]]---drawing; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:p:piye]]---drink; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---we cannot understand.
translation: "Aside from the rivers, the trees standing on the banks like great ascetics and engaging in welfare activities for all living entities drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips by drawing water from the river with their roots. We cannot understand why they drink like that.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.148
description: "The trees on the bank of the Yamunā and Ganges are always jubilant. They appear to be smiling with their flowers and shedding tears in the form of flowing honey. Just as the forefathers of a Vaiṣṇava son or grandson feel transcendental bliss, the trees feel blissful because the flute is a member of their family.'
text:
> nijāṅkure pulakita, puṣpe hāsya vikasita,
> madhu-miṣe vahe aśru-dhāra
> veṇure māni' nija-jāti, āryera yena putra-nāti,
> 'vaiṣṇava' haile ānanda-vikāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅkure]]---by their buds; [[synonyms:p:pulakita]]---jubilant; [[synonyms:p:puṣpe]]---by flowers; [[synonyms:h:hāsya]]---smiling; [[synonyms:v:vikasita]]---exhibited; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:m:miṣe]]---by the oozing of honey; [[synonyms:v:vahe]]---flows; [[synonyms:a:aśru]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---showers of tears; [[synonyms:v:veṇure]]---the flute; [[synonyms:m:māni']]---accepting; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:j:jāti]]---as belonging to the same family; [[synonyms:ā:āryera]]---of forefathers; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:p:putra]]-[[synonyms:n:nāti]]---son or grandson; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---a Vaiṣṇava; [[synonyms:h:haile]]---when becomes; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]-[[synonyms:v:vikāra]]---transformation of transcendental bliss.
translation: "The trees on the bank of the Yamunā and Ganges are always jubilant. They appear to be smiling with their flowers and shedding tears in the form of flowing honey. Just as the forefathers of a Vaiṣṇava son or grandson feel transcendental bliss, the trees feel blissful because the flute is a member of their family.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.149
description: "The gopīs considered, 'The flute is completely unfit for his position. We want to know what kind of austerities the flute executed, so that we may also perform the same austerities. Although the flute is unfit, he is drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips. Seeing this, we qualified gopīs are dying of unhappiness. Therefore, we must consider the austerities the flute underwent in his past life.' "
text:
> veṇura tapa jāni yabe, sei tapa kari tabe,
> e---a yogya, āmarā---yogyā nārī
> yā nā pāñā duḥkhe mari, ayogya piye sahite nāri,
> tāhā lāgi' tapasyā vicāri
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:veṇura]]---of the flute; [[synonyms:t:tapa]]---austerities; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---knowing; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:t:tapa]]---austerities; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---we perform; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:e:e]]---this (flute); [[synonyms:a:ayogya]]---unfit; [[synonyms:ā:āmarā]]---we; [[synonyms:y:yogyā]] [[synonyms:n:nārī]]---fit women; [[synonyms:y:yā]]---which; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---not getting; [[synonyms:d:duḥkhe]]---in unhappiness; [[synonyms:m:mari]]---we die; [[synonyms:a:ayogya]]---the most unfit; [[synonyms:p:piye]]---drinks; [[synonyms:s:sahite]] [[synonyms:n:nāri]]---we cannot tolerate; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for that reason; [[synonyms:t:tapasyā]]---austerities; [[synonyms:v:vicāri]]---we are considering.
translation: "The gopīs considered, 'The flute is completely unfit for his position. We want to know what kind of austerities the flute executed, so that we may also perform the same austerities. Although the flute is unfit, he is drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips. Seeing this, we qualified gopīs are dying of unhappiness. Therefore, we must consider the austerities the flute underwent in his past life.' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.15
description: Kālidāsa presented the mangoes to Jhaḍu Ṭhākura and offered him respectful obeisances. Then he also offered respectful obeisances to the Ṭhākura's wife.
text:
> āmra bheṭa diyā tāṅra caraṇa vandilā
> tāṅra patnīre tabe namaskāra kailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmra]]---mangoes; [[synonyms:b:bheṭa]]---gift; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---presenting; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---feet; [[synonyms:v:vandilā]]---offered respects to; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:p:patnīre]]---to his wife; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]] [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---offered respectful obeisances.
translation: Kālidāsa presented the mangoes to Jhaḍu Ṭhākura and offered him respectful obeisances. Then he also offered respectful obeisances to the Ṭhākura's wife.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.150
description: While thus speaking like a madman, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became full of ecstatic emotion. In the company of His two friends, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya, He sometimes danced, sometimes sang and sometimes became unconscious in ecstatic love. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed His days and nights in this way.
text:
> eteka pralāpa kari', premāveśe gaurahari,
> saṅge lañā svarūpa-rāma-rāya
> kabhu nāce, kabhu gāya, bhāvāveśe mūrcchā yāya,
> ei-rūpe rātri-dina yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eteka]]---so much; [[synonyms:p:pralāpa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---talking like a crazy man; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking with Him; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:r:rāya]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]] [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---sometimes dances; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]] [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---sometimes sings; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:m:mūrcchā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---becomes unconscious; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpe]]---in this way; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---the whole night and day; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---passes.
translation: While thus speaking like a madman, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became full of ecstatic emotion. In the company of His two friends, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya, He sometimes danced, sometimes sang and sometimes became unconscious in ecstatic love. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed His days and nights in this way.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.151
description: Expecting the mercy of Svarūpa, Rūpa, Sanātana and Raghunātha dāsa, and taking their lotus feet on my head, I, the most fallen Kṛṣṇadāsa, continue chanting the epic Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, which is sweeter than the nectar of transcendental bliss.
text:
> svarūpa, rūpa, sanātana, raghunāthera śrī-caraṇa,
> śire dhari' kari yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta, amṛta haite parāmṛta,
> gāya dīna-hīna kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunāthera]]---of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet; [[synonyms:ś:śire]]---on the head; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---taking; [[synonyms:k:kari]] [[synonyms:y:yāra]] [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---hoping for their mercy; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:a:amṛta]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---than nectar; [[synonyms:p:para]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---more nectarean; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chants; [[synonyms:d:dīna]]-[[synonyms:h:hīna]]---the most wretched; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation:
Expecting the mercy of Svarūpa, Rūpa, Sanātana and Raghunātha dāsa, and taking their lotus feet on my head, I, the most fallen Kṛṣṇadāsa, continue chanting the epic Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, which is sweeter than the nectar of transcendental bliss.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā,  Sixteenth Chapter, describing the nectar flowing from Śrī Kṛṣṇa's lotus lips.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.16
description: When Kālidāsa went to Jhaḍu Ṭhākura, he saw that saintly person sitting with his wife. As soon as Jhaḍu Ṭhākura saw Kālidāsa, he likewise offered his respectful obeisances unto him.
text:
> patnī-sahita teṅho āchena vasiyā
> bahu sammāna kailā kālidāsere dekhiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:patnī]]-[[synonyms:s:sahita]]---with his wife; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he (Jhaḍu Ṭhākura); [[synonyms:ā:āchena]] [[synonyms:v:vasiyā]]---was sitting; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---much; [[synonyms:s:sammāna]]---respect; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---offered; [[synonyms:k:kālidāsere]] [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing Kālidāsa.
translation: When Kālidāsa went to Jhaḍu Ṭhākura, he saw that saintly person sitting with his wife. As soon as Jhaḍu Ṭhākura saw Kālidāsa, he likewise offered his respectful obeisances unto him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.17
description: After a discussion for some time with Kālidāsa, Jhaḍu Ṭhākura said something to him in sweet words.
text:
> iṣṭagoṣṭhī kata-kṣaṇa kari' tāṅra sane
> jhaḍu-ṭhākura kahe tāṅre madhura vacane
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:iṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:g:goṣṭhī]]---discussion; [[synonyms:k:kata]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇa]]---for some time; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---performing; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with him; [[synonyms:j:jhaḍu]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---Jhaḍu Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto him (Kālidāsa); [[synonyms:m:madhura]] [[synonyms:v:vacane]]---in sweet words.
translation: After a discussion for some time with Kālidāsa, Jhaḍu Ṭhākura said something to him in sweet words.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.18
description: "I belong to a low caste, and you are a very respectable guest. How shall I serve you?
text:
> "āmi---nīca-jāti, tumi,---atithi sarvottama
> kon prakāre karimu āmi tomāra sevana?
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nīca]]-[[synonyms:j:jāti]]---belong to a low caste; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:a:atithi]]---guest; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:u:uttama]]---very respectable; [[synonyms:k:kon]] [[synonyms:p:prakāre]]---how; [[synonyms:k:karimu]]---shall perform; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---your service.
translation: "I belong to a low caste, and you are a very respectable guest. How shall I serve you?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.19
description: "If you will permit me, I shall send some food to a brāhmaṇa's house, and there you may take prasāda. If you do so, I shall then live very comfortably."
text:
> ājñā deha',---brāhmaṇa-ghare anna lañā diye
> tāhāṅ tumi prasāda pāo, tabe āmi jīye"
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:deha']]---permit me; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:ghare]]---to the house of a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:a:anna]]---food; [[synonyms:l:lañā]] [[synonyms:d:diye]]---I shall offer; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:p:pāo]]---take //prasāda//; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:j:jīye]]---shall live.

All respect should be given to him, and whatever he offers should be accepted, for such devotees are indeed as worshipable as I am.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.26
description: "A person may be born in a brāhmaṇa family and have all twelve brahminical qualities, but if in spite of being qualified he is not devoted to the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, who has a navel shaped like a lotus, he is not as good as a caṇḍāla who has dedicated his mind, words, activities, wealth and life to the service of the Lord. Simply to take birth in a brāhmaṇa family or to have brahminical qualities is not sufficient. One must become a pure devotee of the Lord. If a śva-paca or caṇḍāla is a devotee, he delivers not only himself but his whole family, whereas a brāhmaṇa who is not a devotee but simply has brahminical qualifications cannot even purify himself, not to speak of his family.'

> pādāravinda-vimukhāt śva-pacaṁ variṣṭham

translation: "A person may be born in a brāhmaṇa family and have all twelve brahminical qualities, but if in spite of being qualified he is not devoted to the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, who has a navel shaped like a lotus, he is not as good as a caṇḍāla who has dedicated his mind, words, activities, wealth and life to the service of the Lord. Simply to take birth in a brāhmaṇa family or to have brahminical qualities is not sufficient. One must become a pure devotee of the Lord. If a śva-paca or caṇḍāla is a devotee, he delivers not only himself but his whole family, whereas a brāhmaṇa who is not a devotee but simply has brahminical qualifications cannot even purify himself, not to speak of his family.'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 16.27
description: "My dear Lord, anyone who always keeps Your holy name on his tongue is greater than an initiated brāhmaṇa. Although he may be born in a family of dog-eaters and therefore, by material calculations, be the lowest of men, he is glorious nevertheless. That is the wonderful power of chanting the holy name of the Lord. One who chants the holy name is understood to have performed all kinds of austerities. He has studied all the Vedas, he has performed all the great sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas, he has already taken his bath in all the holy places of pilgrimage, and it is he who is factually the Āryan.'
