synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:b:bhūta]]---this ghost; [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁha]]-[[synonyms:n:nāme]]---by the holy name of Lord Nṛsiṁha; [[synonyms:c:cāpaye]]---comes over me; [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---with doubled strength; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---his; [[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---form; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]]---seeing; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:l:lāge]] [[synonyms:m:mane]]---arises in the mind.
translation: "This ghost, however, overcomes me with redoubled strength when I chant the Nṛsiṁha mantra. When I even see the form of this ghost, great fear arises in my mind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.59
description: "Do not go near there. I forbid you. If you go, that ghost will catch you all."
text:
> othā nā yāiha, āmi niṣedhi tomāre
> tāhāṅ gele sei bhūta lāgibe sabāre"
synonyms: [[synonyms:o:othā]]---there; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāiha]]---do not go; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:niṣedhi]]---forbid; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---you; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:g:gele]]---if you go; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:b:bhūta]]---that ghost; [[synonyms:l:lāgibe]]---will catch; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]]---all of you.
translation: "Do not go near there. I forbid you. If you go, that ghost will catch you all."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.6
description: He sang and danced in ecstatic love and sometimes imitated the rāsa dance in emotional ecstasy.
text:
> prabhu premāveśe karena gāna, nartana
> kabhu bhāvāveśe rāsa-līlānukaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:g:gāna]]---singing; [[synonyms:n:nartana]]---dancing; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstatic emotion; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the //rāsa-līlā// dance; [[synonyms:a:anukaraṇa]]---imitating.
translation: He sang and danced in ecstatic love and sometimes imitated the rāsa dance in emotional ecstasy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.60
description: Hearing this, Svarūpa Dāmodara could understand the full truth of the matter. He spoke sweetly to the fisherman.
text:
> eta śuni' svarūpa-gosāñi saba tattva jāni'
> jāliyāre kichu kaya sumadhura vāṇī
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing this; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]---truth; [[synonyms:j:jāni']]---understanding; [[synonyms:j:jāliyāre]]---unto the fisherman; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:k:kaya]]---said; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:madhura]]---sweet; [[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---words.
translation: Hearing this, Svarūpa Dāmodara could understand the full truth of the matter. He spoke sweetly to the fisherman.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.61
description: "I am a famous exorcist," he said, "and I know how to rid you of this ghost." He then chanted some mantras and placed his hand on the top of the fisherman's head.
text:
> 'āmi---baḍa ojhā jāni bhūta chāḍāite'
> mantra paḍi' śrī-hasta dilā tāhāra māthāte
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---big; [[synonyms:o:ojhā]]---exorcist; [[synonyms:j:jāni]]---I know; [[synonyms:b:bhūta]]---ghost; [[synonyms:c:chāḍāite]]---how to exorcise; [[synonyms:m:mantra]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---chanting hymns; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:h:hasta]]---his hand; [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---placed; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]] [[synonyms:m:māthāte]]---on his head.
translation: "I am a famous exorcist," he said, "and I know how to rid you of this ghost." He then chanted some mantras and placed his hand on the top of the fisherman's head.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.62
description: He slapped the fisherman three times and said, "Now the ghost has gone away. Do not be afraid." By saying this, he pacified the fisherman.
text:
> tina cāpaḍa māri' kahe,---'bhūta palāila
> bhaya nā pāiha'---bali' susthira karila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:c:cāpaḍa]] [[synonyms:m:māri']]---slapping three times; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:b:bhūta]]---the ghost; [[synonyms:p:palāila]]---has gone away; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāiha]]---do not be afraid; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:s:sthira]] [[synonyms:k:karila]]---pacified him.
translation: He slapped the fisherman three times and said, "Now the ghost has gone away. Do not be afraid." By saying this, he pacified the fisherman.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.63
description: The fisherman was affected by ecstatic love, but he was also fearful. He had thus become doubly agitated. Now that his fear had subsided, however, he had become somewhat normal.
text:
> eke prema, āre bhaya,---dviguṇa asthira
> bhaya-aṁśa gela,---se haila kichu dhīra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eke]]---on one hand; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---ecstatic love; [[synonyms:ā:āre]]---on the other hand; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:d:dvi]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---doubly; [[synonyms:a:asthira]]---agitated; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]-[[synonyms:a:aṁśa]]---the fear part; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---disappeared; [[synonyms:s:se]]---he; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---somewhat; [[synonyms:d:dhīra]]---sober.
translation: The fisherman was affected by ecstatic love, but he was also fearful. He had thus become doubly agitated. Now that his fear had subsided, however, he had become somewhat normal.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.64
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara said to the fisherman, "My dear sir, the person whom you are thinking a ghost is not actually a ghost but the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> svarūpa kahe,---"yāṅre tumi kara 'bhūta'-jñāna
> bhūta nahe---teṅho kṛṣṇa-caitanya bhagavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī said; [[synonyms:y:yāṅre]]---the person whom; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:b:bhūta]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---consider a ghost; [[synonyms:b:bhūta]] [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---is not a ghost; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara said to the fisherman, "My dear sir, the person whom you are thinking a ghost is not actually a ghost but the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.65
description: "Because of ecstatic love, the Lord fell into the sea, and you have caught Him in your net and rescued Him.
text:
> premāveśe paḍilā teṅho samudrera jale
> tāṅre tumi uṭhāilā āpanāra jāle
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---out of ecstatic emotion; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:s:samudrera]] [[synonyms:j:jale]]---in the water of the sea; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāilā]]---brought out; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāra]] [[synonyms:j:jāle]]---in your net.
translation: "Because of ecstatic love, the Lord fell into the sea, and you have caught Him in your net and rescued Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.66
description: "Simply touching Him has awakened your dormant love of Kṛṣṇa, but because you thought Him a ghost, you were very much afraid of Him.
text:
> tāṅra sparśe ha-ila tomāra kṛṣṇa-premodaya
> bhūta-preta-jñāne tomāra haila mahā-bhaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:s:sparśe]]---by His touch; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---there was; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]]---awakening of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhūta]]-[[synonyms:p:preta]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---by thinking to be a ghost; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---great fear.
translation: "Simply touching Him has awakened your dormant love of Kṛṣṇa, but because you thought Him a ghost, you were very much afraid of Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.67
description: "Now that your fear has gone and your mind is peaceful, please show me where He is."
text:
> ebe bhaya gela, tomāra mana haila sthire
> kāhāṅ tāṅre uṭhāñācha, dekhāha āmāre"
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---has gone; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---has become; [[synonyms:s:sthire]]---pacified; [[synonyms:k:kāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāñācha]]---have you lifted; [[synonyms:d:dekhāha]]---please show; [[synonyms:ā:āmāre]]---me.
translation: "Now that your fear has gone and your mind is peaceful, please show me where He is."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.68
description: The fisherman replied, "I have seen the Lord many times, but this is not He. This body is very deformed."
text:
> jāliyā kahe,---"prabhure dekhyāchoṅ bāra-bāra
> teṅho nahena, ei ati-vikṛta ākāra"
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jāliyā]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the fisherman said; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhyāchoṅ]]---I have seen; [[synonyms:b:bāra]]-[[synonyms:b:bāra]]---many times; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---He; [[synonyms:n:nahena]]---it is not; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:a:ati]]-[[synonyms:v:vikṛta]]---very deformed; [[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---body.
translation: The fisherman replied, "I have seen the Lord many times, but this is not He. This body is very deformed."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.69
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara said, "The Lord's body becomes transformed in His love for God. Sometimes the joints of His bones separate, and His body becomes very elongated."
text:
> svarūpa kahe,---"tāṅra haya premera vikāra
> asthi-sandhi chāḍe, haya ati dīrghākāra"
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara said; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---of Him; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:p:premera]]---of love of Godhead; [[synonyms:v:vikāra]]---transformations of the body; [[synonyms:a:asthi]]-[[synonyms:s:sandhi]]---the joints of the bones; [[synonyms:c:chāḍe]]---become separated; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:a:ati]]---very; [[synonyms:d:dīrgha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]---elongated body.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara said, "The Lord's body becomes transformed in His love for God. Sometimes the joints of His bones separate, and His body becomes very elongated."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.7
description: He sometimes ran here and there in the madness of ecstasy and sometimes fell and rolled on the ground. Sometimes He became completely unconscious.
text:
> kabhu bhāvonmāde prabhu iti-uti dhāya
> bhūme paḍi' kabhu mūrcchā, kabhu gaḍi' yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:u:unmāde]]---in the madness of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:i:iti]]-[[synonyms:u:uti]]---here and there; [[synonyms:d:dhāya]]---runs; [[synonyms:b:bhūme]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---falling on the ground; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]] [[synonyms:m:mūrcchā]]---sometimes unconscious; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:g:gaḍi']] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---rolls on the ground.
translation: He sometimes ran here and there in the madness of ecstasy and sometimes fell and rolled on the ground. Sometimes He became completely unconscious.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.70
description: Hearing this, the fisherman was very happy. He brought all the devotees with him and showed them the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> śuni, sei jāliyā ānandita ha-ila
> sabā lañā gela, mahāprabhure dekhāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:j:jāliyā]]---fisherman; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became very happy; [[synonyms:s:sabā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking everyone; [[synonyms:g:gela]]---went; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhāila]]---showed.
translation: Hearing this, the fisherman was very happy. He brought all the devotees with him and showed them the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.71
description: The Lord was lying on the ground, His body elongated and bleached white by the water. He was covered from head to foot with sand.
text:
> bhūmite paḍi' āche prabhu dīrgha saba kāya
> jale śveta-tanu, vālu lāgiyāche gāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhūmite]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---lying; [[synonyms:ā:āche]]---was; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dīrgha]]---elongated; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:k:kāya]]---the whole body; [[synonyms:j:jale]]---by the water; [[synonyms:ś:śveta]]-[[synonyms:t:tanu]]---white body; [[synonyms:v:vālu]]---sand; [[synonyms:l:lāgiyāche]] [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---was smeared over the body.
translation: The Lord was lying on the ground, His body elongated and bleached white by the water. He was covered from head to foot with sand.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.72
description: The Lord's body was stretched, and His skin was slack and hanging loose. To lift Him and take Him the long distance home would have been impossible.
text:
> ati-dīrgha śithila tanu-carma naṭkāya
> dūra patha uṭhāñā ghare ānāna nā yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ati]]-[[synonyms:d:dīrgha]]---very elongated; [[synonyms:ś:śithila]]---slackened; [[synonyms:t:tanu]]---body; [[synonyms:c:carma]]---skin; [[synonyms:n:naṭkāya]]---hanging; [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:p:patha]]---long distance; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāñā]]---lifting; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---home; [[synonyms:ā:ānāna]]---bringing; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---was not possible.
translation: The Lord's body was stretched, and His skin was slack and hanging loose. To lift Him and take Him the long distance home would have been impossible.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.73
description: The devotees removed His wet undergarment and replaced it with a dry one. Then, laying the Lord on an outer cloth, they cleaned the sand from His body.
text:
> ārdra kaupīna dūra kari' śuṣka parāñā
> bahirvāse śoyāilā vālukā chāḍāñā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ārdra]]---wet; [[synonyms:k:kaupīna]]---underwear; [[synonyms:d:dūra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---removing; [[synonyms:ś:śuṣka]]---dry; [[synonyms:p:parāñā]]---putting on; [[synonyms:b:bahirvāse]]---on a covering cloth; [[synonyms:ś:śoyāilā]]---put down; [[synonyms:v:vālukā]]---sand; [[synonyms:c:chāḍāñā]]---removing.
translation: The devotees removed His wet undergarment and replaced it with a dry one. Then, laying the Lord on an outer cloth, they cleaned the sand from His body.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.74
description: They all performed saṅkīrtana, loudly chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa into the Lord's ear.
text:
> sabe meli' ucca kari' karena saṅkīrtane
> ucca kari' kṛṣṇa-nāma kahena prabhura kāṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:m:meli']]---all together; [[synonyms:u:ucca]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---very loudly; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---performed; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtane]]---chanting of the holy name; [[synonyms:u:ucca]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---loudly; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---said; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:k:kāṇe]]---in the ear of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: They all performed saṅkīrtana, loudly chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa into the Lord's ear.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.75
description: After some time, the sound of the holy name entered the ear of the Lord, who immediately got up, making a great noise.
text:
> kata-kṣaṇe prabhura kāṇe śabda paraśila
> huṅkāra kariyā prabhu tabahi uṭhila
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kata]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---after some time; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kāṇe]]---within the ear; [[synonyms:ś:śabda]]---the sound; [[synonyms:p:paraśila]]---entered; [[synonyms:h:huṅkāra]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---making a loud sound; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tabahi]]---immediately; [[synonyms:u:uṭhila]]---got up.
translation: After some time, the sound of the holy name entered the ear of the Lord, who immediately got up, making a great noise.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.76
description: As soon as He got up, His bones assumed their proper places. With half-external consciousness, the Lord looked here and there.
text:
> uṭhitei asthi saba lāgila nija-sthāne
> 'ardha-bāhye' iti-uti karena daraśane
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uṭhitei]]---as soon as He got up; [[synonyms:a:asthi]]---bones; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:l:lāgila]]---contracted; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---in their own places; [[synonyms:a:ardha]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhye]]---in half-external consciousness; [[synonyms:i:iti]]-[[synonyms:u:uti]]---here and there; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---looks.
translation: As soon as He got up, His bones assumed their proper places. With half-external consciousness, the Lord looked here and there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.77
description: The Lord remains in one of three different states of consciousness at all times: internal, external, and half-external.
text:
> tina-daśāya mahāprabhu rahena sarva-kāla
> 'antar-daśā', 'bāhya-daśā', 'ardha-bāhya' āra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:d:daśāya]]---in three conditions; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:r:rahena]]---remains; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāla]]---at all times; [[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]-[[synonyms:d:daśā]]---internal condition; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]-[[synonyms:d:daśā]]---external condition; [[synonyms:a:ardha]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---half-external consciousness; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and.
translation: The Lord remains in one of three different states of consciousness at all times: internal, external, and half-external.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.78
description: When the Lord is deeply absorbed in internal consciousness but He nevertheless exhibits some external consciousness, devotees call His condition ardha-bāhya, or half-external consciousness.
text:
> antar-daśāra kichu ghora, kichu bāhya-jñāna
> sei daśā kahe bhakta 'ardha-bāhya'-nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:antaḥ]]-[[synonyms:d:daśāra]]---of the internal condition; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:g:ghora]]---deep state; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāna]]---external consciousness; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:daśā]]---that condition; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---say; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---devotees; [[synonyms:a:ardha]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---half-external consciousness; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---name.
translation: When the Lord is deeply absorbed in internal consciousness but He nevertheless exhibits some external consciousness, devotees call His condition ardha-bāhya, or half-external consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.79
description: In this half-external consciousness, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu talked like a madman. The devotees could distinctly hear Him speaking to the sky.
text:
> 'ardha-bāhye' kahena prabhu pralāpa-vacane
> ākāśe kahena prabhu, śunena bhakta-gaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:ardha]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhye]]---in half-external consciousness; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---says; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pralāpa]]-[[synonyms:v:vacane]]---crazy words; [[synonyms:ā:ākāśe]]---to the sky; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---speaks; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śunena]]---hear; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the devotees.
translation: In this half-external consciousness, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu talked like a madman. The devotees could distinctly hear Him speaking to the sky.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.8
description: When He heard Svarūpa Dāmodara recite a verse concerning the rāsa-līlā or He Himself recited one, He would personally explain it, as He had previously done.
text:
> rāsa-līlāra eka śloka yabe paḍe, śune
> pūrvavat tabe artha karena āpane
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlāra]]---of the //rāsa-līlā//; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verse; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---recites; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hears; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---as previously; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:k:karena]]---explains; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally.
translation: When He heard Svarūpa Dāmodara recite a verse concerning the rāsa-līlā or He Himself recited one, He would personally explain it, as He had previously done.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.80
description: "Seeing the River Yamunā," He said, "I went to Vṛndāvana. There I saw the son of Nanda Mahārāja performing His sporting pastimes in the water.
text:
> "kālindī dekhiyā āmi gelāṅa vṛndāvana
> dekhi,---jala-krīḍā karena vrajendra-nandana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kālindī]]---River Yamunā; [[synonyms:d:dekhiyā]]---seeing; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:g:gelāṅa]]---went; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---to Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---I see; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:k:krīḍā]]---pastimes in the water; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---performs; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja.
translation: "Seeing the River Yamunā," He said, "I went to Vṛndāvana. There I saw the son of Nanda Mahārāja performing His sporting pastimes in the water.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.81
description: "Lord Kṛṣṇa was in the water of the Yamunā in the company of the gopīs, headed by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. They were performing pastimes in a great sporting manner.
text:
> rādhikādi gopī-gaṇa-saṅge ekatra meli'
> yamunāra jale mahā-raṅge karena keli
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rādhikā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---headed by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:e:ekatra]] [[synonyms:m:meli']]---meeting together; [[synonyms:y:yamunāra]]---of the River Yamunā; [[synonyms:j:jale]]---in the water; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---in a great sporting attitude; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:k:keli]]---performs pastimes.
translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa was in the water of the Yamunā in the company of the gopīs, headed by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. They were performing pastimes in a great sporting manner.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.82
description: "I saw this pastime as I stood on the bank of the Yamunā in the company of the gopīs. One gopī was showing some other gopīs the pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in the water.
text:
> tīre rahi' dekhi āmi sakhī-gaṇa-saṅge
> eka-sakhī sakhī-gaṇe dekhāya sei raṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank; [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---standing; [[synonyms:d:dekhi]]---see; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:s:sakhī]]---one //gopī//; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---to other //gopīs//; [[synonyms:d:dekhāya]]---shows; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---that pastime.
translation: "I saw this pastime as I stood on the bank of the Yamunā in the company of the gopīs. One gopī was showing some other gopīs the pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in the water.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.83
description: "All the gopīs entrusted their silken garments and ornaments to the care of their friends and then put on fine white cloth. Taking His beloved gopīs with Him, Lord Kṛṣṇa bathed and performed very nice pastimes in the water of the Yamunā.
text:
> paṭṭa-vastra, alaṅkāre, samarpiyā sakhī-kare,
> sūkṣma-śukla-vastra-paridhāna
> kṛṣṇa lañā kāntā-gaṇa, kailā jalāvagāhana,
> jala-keli racilā suṭhāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paṭṭa]]-[[synonyms:v:vastra]]---silk garments; [[synonyms:a:alaṅkāre]]---ornaments; [[synonyms:s:samarpiyā]]---entrusting; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]-[[synonyms:k:kare]]---in the hands of their //gopī// friends; [[synonyms:s:sūkṣma]]---very fine; [[synonyms:ś:śukla]]-[[synonyms:v:vastra]]---white cloth; [[synonyms:p:paridhāna]]---putting on; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:k:kāntā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the beloved //gopīs//; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---performed; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:a:avagāhana]]---bathing in the water; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:k:keli]]---pastimes in the water; [[synonyms:r:racilā]]---planned; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāma]]---very nice.
translation: "All the gopīs entrusted their silken garments and ornaments to the care of their friends and then put on fine white cloth. Taking His beloved gopīs with Him, Lord Kṛṣṇa bathed and performed very nice pastimes in the water of the Yamunā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.84
description: "My dear friends, just see Lord Kṛṣṇa's sporting pastimes in the water. Kṛṣṇa's restless palms resemble lotus flowers. He is just like a chief of mad elephants, and the gopīs who accompany Him are like she-elephants.
text:
> sakhi he, dekha kṛṣṇera jala-keli-raṅge
> kṛṣṇa matta kari-vara, cañcala kara-puṣkara,
> gopī-gaṇa kariṇīra saṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakhi]] [[synonyms:h:he]]---O my dear friends; [[synonyms:d:dekha]]---just see; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:k:keli]]---of the pastimes in the water; [[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---the sporting mood; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:matta]]---maddened; [[synonyms:k:kari]]-[[synonyms:v:vara]]---chief elephant; [[synonyms:c:cañcala]]---restless; [[synonyms:k:kara]]-[[synonyms:p:puṣkara]]---lotus palms; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:k:kariṇīra]]---of the she-elephants; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the company.
translation: "My dear friends, just see Lord Kṛṣṇa's sporting pastimes in the water. Kṛṣṇa's restless palms resemble lotus flowers. He is just like a chief of mad elephants, and the gopīs who accompany Him are like she-elephants.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.85
description: "The sporting pastimes in the water began, and everyone started splashing water back and forth. In the tumultuous showers of water, no one could be certain which party was winning and which was losing. This sporting water fight increased unlimitedly.
text:
> ārambhilā jala-keli, anyo 'nye jala phelāpheli,
> huḍāhuḍi, varṣe jala-dhāra
> sabe jaya-parājaya, nāhi kichu niścaya,
> jala-yuddha bāḍila apāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ārambhilā]]---began; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:k:keli]]---pastimes in the water; [[synonyms:a:anyo]] [[synonyms:n:'nye]]---at one another; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---water; [[synonyms:p:phelāpheli]]---throwing back and forth; [[synonyms:h:huḍāhuḍi]]---tumultuous activities; [[synonyms:v:varṣe]]---in rains; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:d:dhāra]]---showers of water; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]-[[synonyms:p:parājaya]]---victory and defeat; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---any; [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---certainty; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:y:yuddha]]---the fight in the water; [[synonyms:b:bāḍila]]---increased; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimitedly.
translation: "The sporting pastimes in the water began, and everyone started splashing water back and forth. In the tumultuous showers of water, no one could be certain which party was winning and which was losing. This sporting water fight increased unlimitedly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.86
description: "The gopīs were like steady streaks of lightning, and Kṛṣṇa resembled a blackish cloud. The lightning began sprinkling water upon the cloud, and the cloud upon the lightning. Like thirsty cātaka birds, the eyes of the gopīs joyously drank the nectarean water from the cloud.
text:
> varṣe sthira taḍid-gaṇa, siñce śyāma nava-ghana,
> ghana varṣe taḍit-upare
> sakhī-gaṇera nayana, tṛṣita cātaka-gaṇa,
> sei amṛta sukhe pāna kare
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:varṣe]]---in that shower; [[synonyms:s:sthira]]---fixed; [[synonyms:t:taḍit]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---streaks of lightning; [[synonyms:s:siñce]]---sprinkle; [[synonyms:ś:śyāma]]---blackish; [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:g:ghana]]---new cloud; [[synonyms:g:ghana]]---the cloud; [[synonyms:v:varṣe]]---rains; [[synonyms:t:taḍit]]-[[synonyms:u:upare]]---upon the streaks of lightning; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:n:nayana]]---the eyes; [[synonyms:t:tṛṣita]]---thirsty; [[synonyms:c:cātaka]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---//cātaka// birds; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---that nectar; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---in happiness; [[synonyms:p:pāna]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---drink.
translation: "The gopīs were like steady streaks of lightning, and Kṛṣṇa resembled a blackish cloud. The lightning began sprinkling water upon the cloud, and the cloud upon the lightning. Like thirsty cātaka birds, the eyes of the gopīs joyously drank the nectarean water from the cloud.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.87
description: "As the fight began, they splashed water on one another. Then they fought hand to hand, then face to face, then chest to chest, teeth to teeth and finally nail to nail.
text:
> prathame yuddha jalājali', tabe yuddha 'karākari',
> tāra pāche yuddha 'mukhāmukhi'
> tabe yuddha 'hṛdāhṛdi', tabe haila 'radāradi',
> tabe haila yuddha 'nakhānakhi'
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prathame]]---in the beginning; [[synonyms:y:yuddha]]---the fight; [[synonyms:j:jalājali]]---throwing water upon one another; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:y:yuddha]]---the fight; [[synonyms:k:karākari]]---hand to hand; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:p:pāche]]---after that; [[synonyms:y:yuddha]]---the fight; [[synonyms:m:mukhāmukhi]]---face to face; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:y:yuddha]]---the fight; [[synonyms:h:hṛdāhṛdi]]---chest to chest; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:r:radāradi]]---teeth to teeth; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:y:yuddha]]---the fight; [[synonyms:n:nakhānakhi]]---nail to nail.
translation: "As the fight began, they splashed water on one another. Then they fought hand to hand, then face to face, then chest to chest, teeth to teeth and finally nail to nail.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.88
description: "Thousands of hands splashed water, and the gopīs saw Kṛṣṇa with thousands of eyes. With thousands of legs they came near Him and kissed Him with thousands of faces. Thousands of bodies embraced Him. The gopīs heard His joking words with thousands of ears.
text:
> sahasra-kare jala seke, sahasra netre gopī dekhe,
> sahasra-pade nikaṭa gamane
> sahasra-mukha-cumbane, sahasra-vapu-saṅgame,
> gopī-narma śune sahasra-kāṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]---thousands; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---with hands; [[synonyms:j:jala]]---water; [[synonyms:s:seke]]---throw; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]---thousands; [[synonyms:n:netre]]---with eyes; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---see; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]---thousands; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---with legs; [[synonyms:n:nikaṭa]]---near; [[synonyms:g:gamane]]---in going; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]---thousands; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---faces; [[synonyms:c:cumbane]]---kissing; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]---thousands; [[synonyms:v:vapu]]---bodies; [[synonyms:s:saṅgame]]---in embracing; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:n:narma]]---joking; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hear; [[synonyms:s:sahasra]]---thousands; [[synonyms:k:kāṇe]]---in ears.
translation: "Thousands of hands splashed water, and the gopīs saw Kṛṣṇa with thousands of eyes. With thousands of legs they came near Him and kissed Him with thousands of faces. Thousands of bodies embraced Him. The gopīs heard His joking words with thousands of ears.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.89
description: "Kṛṣṇa forcibly swept Rādhārāṇī away and took Her into water up to Her neck. Then He released Her where the water was very deep. She grasped Kṛṣṇa's neck, however, and floated on the water like a lotus flower plucked by the trunk of a elephant.
text:
> kṛṣṇa rādhā lañā bale, gelā kaṇṭha-daghna jale,
> chāḍilā tāhāṅ, yāhāṅ agādha pānī
> teṅho kṛṣṇa-kaṇṭha dhari', bhāse jalera upari,
> gajotkhāte yaiche kamalinī
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---forcibly; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:k:kaṇṭha]]-[[synonyms:d:daghna]]---up to the neck; [[synonyms:j:jale]]---in water; [[synonyms:c:chāḍilā]]---let go; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:a:agādha]]---very deep; [[synonyms:p:pānī]]---water; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---She; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kaṇṭha]]---the neck of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---capturing; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---floats; [[synonyms:j:jalera]] [[synonyms:u:upari]]---on the water; [[synonyms:g:gaja]]-[[synonyms:u:utkhāte]]---plucked by an elephant; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:k:kamalinī]]---a lotus flower.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa forcibly swept Rādhārāṇī away and took Her into water up to Her neck. Then He released Her where the water was very deep. She grasped Kṛṣṇa's neck, however, and floated on the water like a lotus flower plucked by the trunk of a elephant.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.9
description: In this way, He explained the meaning of all the verses concerning the rāsa-līlā. Sometimes He would be very sad and sometimes very happy.
text:
> ei-mata rāsa-līlāya haya yata śloka
> sabāra artha kare, pāya kabhu harṣa-śoka
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:r:rāsa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlāya]]---in the pastimes of the //rāsa-līlā//; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there are; [[synonyms:y:yata]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---as many verses; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---He explains the meaning; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śoka]]---happiness and lamentation.
translation: In this way, He explained the meaning of all the verses concerning the rāsa-līlā. Sometimes He would be very sad and sometimes very happy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.90
description: "Kṛṣṇa expanded Himself into as many forms as there were gopīs and then took away all the garments that covered them. The water of the River Yamunā was crystal clear, and Kṛṣṇa saw the glittering bodies of the gopīs in great happiness.
text:
> yata gopa-sundarī, kṛṣṇa tata rūpa dhari',
> sabāra vastra karilā haraṇe
> yamunā-jala nirmala, aṅga kare jhalamala,
> sukhe kṛṣṇa kare daraśane
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yata]]---as many; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:s:sundarī]]---beautiful //gopīs//; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tata]]---that many; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---forms; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---accepting; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all; [[synonyms:v:vastra]]---covering cloths; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:h:haraṇe]]---took away; [[synonyms:y:yamunā]]-[[synonyms:j:jala]]---the water of the Yamunā; [[synonyms:n:nirmala]]---very clear; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---bodies; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:j:jhalamala]]---glitter; [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---happily; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---sees.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa expanded Himself into as many forms as there were gopīs and then took away all the garments that covered them. The water of the River Yamunā was crystal clear, and Kṛṣṇa saw the glittering bodies of the gopīs in great happiness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.91
description: "The lotus stems were friends of the gopīs and therefore helped them by offering them lotus leaves. The lotuses pushed their large, round leaves over the surface of the water with their hands, the waves of the Yamunā, to cover the gopīs' bodies. Some gopīs undid their hair and kept it in front of them as dresses to cover the lower portions of their bodies and used their hands as bodices to cover their breasts.
text:
> padminī-latā---sakhī-caya, kaila kāro sahāya,
> taraṅga-haste patra samarpila
> keha mukta-keśa-pāśa, āge kaila adhovāsa,
> haste keha kañculi dharila
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:padminī]]-[[synonyms:l:latā]]---the stems of lotus flowers; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]-[[synonyms:c:caya]]---friends of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---gave; [[synonyms:k:kāro]]---to some of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:s:sahāya]]---help; [[synonyms:t:taraṅga]]-[[synonyms:h:haste]]---by the waves of the Yamunā, which are compared to hands; [[synonyms:p:patra]]---the lotus leaves; [[synonyms:s:samarpila]]---supplied; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---someone; [[synonyms:m:mukta]]---released; [[synonyms:k:keśa]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---the bunches of hair; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made; [[synonyms:a:adhovāsa]]---a lower dress; [[synonyms:h:haste]]---the hands; [[synonyms:k:keha]]---some; [[synonyms:k:kañculi]]---as a top dress; [[synonyms:d:dharila]]---held.
translation: "The lotus stems were friends of the gopīs and therefore helped them by offering them lotus leaves. The lotuses pushed their large, round leaves over the surface of the water with their hands, the waves of the Yamunā, to cover the gopīs' bodies. Some gopīs undid their hair and kept it in front of them as dresses to cover the lower portions of their bodies and used their hands as bodices to cover their breasts.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.92
description: "Then Kṛṣṇa quarreled with Rādhārāṇī, and all the gopīs hid themselves in a cluster of white lotus flowers. They submerged their bodies up to their necks in the water. Only their faces floated above the surface, and the faces were indistinguishable from the lotuses.
text:
> kṛṣṇera kalaha rādhā-sane, gopī-gaṇa sei-kṣaṇe,
> hemābja-vane gelā lukāite
> ākaṇṭha-vapu jale paiśe, mukha-mātra jale bhāse,
> padme-mukhe nā pāri cinite
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kalaha]]---quarrel; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with Rādhā; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:s:sei]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaṇe]]---at that moment; [[synonyms:h:hema]]-[[synonyms:a:abja]]---of white lotus flowers; [[synonyms:v:vane]]---in the forest; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:l:lukāite]]---to hide; [[synonyms:ā:ākaṇṭha]]---up to the neck; [[synonyms:v:vapu]]---body; [[synonyms:j:jale]]---into the water; [[synonyms:p:paiśe]]---enter; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]-[[synonyms:m:mātra]]---only the lotus flowers and the faces; [[synonyms:j:jale]]---in the water; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---float; [[synonyms:p:padme]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---between the lotus flowers and the faces; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāri]]---not able; [[synonyms:c:cinite]]---to discern.
translation: "Then Kṛṣṇa quarreled with Rādhārāṇī, and all the gopīs hid themselves in a cluster of white lotus flowers. They submerged their bodies up to their necks in the water. Only their faces floated above the surface, and the faces were indistinguishable from the lotuses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.93
description: "In the absence of the other gopīs, Lord Kṛṣṇa behaved with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī as freely as He desired. When the gopīs began searching for Kṛṣṇa, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, being of very fine intelligence and thus knowing the situation of Her friends, immediately mingled in their midst.
text:
> ethā kṛṣṇa rādhā-sane, kailā ye āchila mane,
> gopī-gaṇa anveṣite gelā
> tabe rādhā sūkṣma-mati, jāniyā sakhīra sthiti,
> sakhī-madhye āsiyā mililā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ethā]]---here; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---performed; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---what; [[synonyms:ā:āchila]]---was; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:a:anveṣite]]---to search out; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:s:sūkṣma]]-[[synonyms:m:mati]]---very finely intelligent; [[synonyms:j:jāniyā]]---knowing; [[synonyms:s:sakhīra]]---of the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---situation; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---among the friends; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---mixed.
translation: "In the absence of the other gopīs, Lord Kṛṣṇa behaved with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī as freely as He desired. When the gopīs began searching for Kṛṣṇa, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, being of very fine intelligence and thus knowing the situation of Her friends, immediately mingled in their midst.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.94
description: "Many white lotus flowers were floating in the water, and as many bluish lotus flowers came nearby. As they came close together, the white and blue lotuses collided and began fighting with one another. The gopīs on the bank of the Yamunā watched with great amusement.
text:
> yata hemābja jale bhāse, tata nīlābja tāra pāśe,
> āsi' āsi' karaye milana
> nīlābje hemābje ṭheke, yuddha haya pratyeke,
> kautuke dekhe tīre sakhī-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yata]]---as many as there were; [[synonyms:h:hema]]-[[synonyms:a:abja]]---white lotus flowers; [[synonyms:j:jale]]---on the water; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---float; [[synonyms:t:tata]]---that many; [[synonyms:n:nīla]]-[[synonyms:a:abja]]---bluish lotus flowers; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:p:pāśe]]---by their side; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']] [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming closer; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:m:milana]]---they meet; [[synonyms:n:nīla]]-[[synonyms:a:abje]]---the bluish lotus flowers; [[synonyms:h:hema]]-[[synonyms:a:abje]]---with the white lotus flowers; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭheke]]---collide; [[synonyms:y:yuddha]]---a fight; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:e:eke]]---with one another; [[synonyms:k:kautuke]]---in great fun; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---see; [[synonyms:t:tīre]]---on the bank; [[synonyms:s:sakhī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---the //gopīs.//
translation: "Many white lotus flowers were floating in the water, and as many bluish lotus flowers came nearby. As they came close together, the white and blue lotuses collided and began fighting with one another. The gopīs on the bank of the Yamunā watched with great amusement.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.95
description: "When the raised breasts of the gopīs, which resembled the globelike bodies of cakravāka birds, emerged from the water in separate couples, the bluish lotuses of Kṛṣṇa's hands rose to cover them.
text:
> cakravāka-maṇḍala, pṛthak pṛthak yugala,
> jala haite karila udgama
> uṭhila padma-maṇḍala, pṛthak pṛthak yugala,
> cakravāke kaila ācchādana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cakravāka]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇḍala]]---the globes of //cakravāka// birds; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]] [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---separate; [[synonyms:y:yugala]]---couples; [[synonyms:j:jala]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the water; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---made; [[synonyms:u:udgama]]---appearance; [[synonyms:u:uṭhila]]---arose; [[synonyms:p:padma]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇḍala]]---the circle of lotus flowers; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]] [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---separate; [[synonyms:y:yugala]]---couples; [[synonyms:c:cakravāke]]---the //cakravāka// birds; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:ā:ācchādana]]---covering.
translation: "When the raised breasts of the gopīs, which resembled the globelike bodies of cakravāka birds, emerged from the water in separate couples, the bluish lotuses of Kṛṣṇa's hands rose to cover them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.96
description: "The hands of the gopīs, which resembled red lotus flowers, arose from the water in pairs to obstruct the bluish flowers. The blue lotuses tried to plunder the white cakravāka birds, and the red lotuses tried to protect them. Thus there was a fight between the two.
text:
> uṭhila bahu raktotpala, pṛthak pṛthak yugala,
> padma-gaṇera kaila nivāraṇa
> 'padma' cāhe luṭi' nite, 'utpala' cāhe rākhite',
> 'cakravāka' lāgi' duṅhāra raṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uṭhila]]---arose; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]---many; [[synonyms:r:rakta]]-[[synonyms:u:utpala]]---red lotus flowers; [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]] [[synonyms:p:pṛthak]]---separate; [[synonyms:y:yugala]]---couples; [[synonyms:p:padma]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the bluish lotus flowers; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:n:nivāraṇa]]---obstruction; [[synonyms:p:padma]]---the blue lotus flowers; [[synonyms:c:cāhe]]---want; [[synonyms:l:luṭi']]---stealing; [[synonyms:n:nite]]---to take; [[synonyms:u:utpala]]---the red lotus flowers; [[synonyms:c:cāhe]] [[synonyms:r:rākhite']]---wanted to protect; [[synonyms:c:cakravāka]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for the //cakravāka// birds; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]]---between the two, (the red and blue lotus flowers); [[synonyms:r:raṇa]]---fight.
translation: "The hands of the gopīs, which resembled red lotus flowers, arose from the water in pairs to obstruct the bluish flowers. The blue lotuses tried to plunder the white cakravāka birds, and the red lotuses tried to protect them. Thus there was a fight between the two.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.97
description: "Blue and red lotus flowers are unconscious objects, whereas cakravākas are conscious and alive. Nevertheless, in ecstatic love, the blue lotuses began to taste the cakravākas. This is a reversal of their natural behavior, but in Lord Kṛṣṇa's kingdom such reversals are a principle of His pastimes.
text:
> padmotpala---acetana, cakravāka---sacetana,
> cakravāke padma āsvādaya
> ihāṅ duṅhāra ulṭā sthiti, dharma haila viparīti,
> kṛṣṇera rājye aiche nyāya haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:padma]]-[[synonyms:u:utpala]]---the blue and red lotus flowers; [[synonyms:a:acetana]]---unconscious; [[synonyms:c:cakravāka]]---the //cakravāka// birds; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:c:cetana]]---conscious; [[synonyms:c:cakravāke]]---the //cakravāka// birds; [[synonyms:p:padma]]---the blue lotus flowers; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādaya]]---taste; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:d:duṅhāra]]---of both of them; [[synonyms:u:ulṭā]] [[synonyms:s:sthiti]]---the reverse situation; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---characteristic nature; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:v:viparīti]]---reversed; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:r:rājye]]---in the kingdom; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:n:nyāya]]---principle; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is.
translation: "Blue and red lotus flowers are unconscious objects, whereas cakravākas are conscious and alive. Nevertheless, in ecstatic love, the blue lotuses began to taste the cakravākas. This is a reversal of their natural behavior, but in Lord Kṛṣṇa's kingdom such reversals are a principle of His pastimes.
purport: Generally the //cakravāka// bird tastes the lotus flower, but in Kṛṣṇa's pastimes the lotus, which is usually lifeless, tastes the //cakravāka// bird.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.98
description: "The blue lotuses are friends of the sun-god, and though they all live together, the blue lotuses plunder the cakravākas. The red lotuses, however, blossom at night and are therefore strangers or enemies to the cakravākas. Yet in Kṛṣṇa's pastimes the red lotuses, which are the hands of the gopīs, protect their cakravāka breasts. This is a metaphor of contradiction."
text:
> mitrera mitra saha-vāsī, cakravāke luṭe āsi',
> kṛṣṇera rājye aiche vyavahāra
> aparicita śatrura mitra, rākhe utpala,---e baḍa citra,
> ei baḍa 'virodha-alaṅkāra'
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mitrera]]---of the sun-god; [[synonyms:m:mitra]]---the friend; [[synonyms:s:saha]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---living together with the //cakravāka// birds; [[synonyms:c:cakravāke]]---the //cakravāka// birds; [[synonyms:l:luṭe]]---plunder; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:r:rājye]]---in the kingdom of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:v:vyavahāra]]---behavior; [[synonyms:a:aparicita]]---unacquainted; [[synonyms:ś:śatrura]] [[synonyms:m:mitra]]---the friend of the enemy; [[synonyms:r:rākhe]]---protects; [[synonyms:u:utpala]]---the red lotus flower; [[synonyms:e:e]]---this; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:c:citra]]---very wonderful; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---great; [[synonyms:v:virodha]]-[[synonyms:a:alaṅkāra]]---metaphor of contradiction.
translation: "The blue lotuses are friends of the sun-god, and though they all live together, the blue lotuses plunder the cakravākas. The red lotuses, however, blossom at night and are therefore strangers or enemies to the cakravākas. Yet in Kṛṣṇa's pastimes the red lotuses, which are the hands of the gopīs, protect their cakravāka breasts. This is a metaphor of contradiction."
purport: Because the blue lotus flower blossoms with the rising of the sun, the sun is the friend of the blue lotus. The //cakravāka// birds also appear when the sun rises, and therefore the //cakravākas// and blue lotuses meet. Although the blue lotus is a friend of the sun, in Kṛṣṇa's pastimes it nevertheless plunders their mutual friend the //cakravāka.// Normally, //cakravākas// move about whereas lotuses stand still, but herein Kṛṣṇa's hands, which are compared to blue lotuses, attack the breasts of the //gopīs,// which are compared to //cakravākas.// This is called a reverse analogy. At night the red lotus blossoms, whereas in sunlight it closes. Therefore the red lotus is an enemy to the sun and is unknown to the sun's friend the //cakravāka.// The //gopīs'// breasts, however, are compared to //cakravākas// and their hands to red lotuses protecting them. This is a wonderful instance of reverse analogy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 18.99
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "In His pastimes, Kṛṣṇa displayed the two ornaments of hyperbole and reverse analogy. Tasting them brought gladness to My mind and fully satisfied My ears and eyes.
text:
> atiśayokti, virodhābhāsa, dui alaṅkāra prakāśa,
> kari' kṛṣṇa prakaṭa dekhāila
> yāhā kari' āsvādana, ānandita mora mana,
> netra-karṇa-yugma juḍāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:atiśaya]]-[[synonyms:u:ukti]]---exaggerated language; [[synonyms:v:virodha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāsa]]---incongruent analogy; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:a:alaṅkāra]]---two metaphors; [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---manifestations; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prakaṭa]]---exhibited; [[synonyms:d:dekhāila]]---showed; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]]---which; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasting; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---pleased; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---My mind; [[synonyms:n:netra]]-[[synonyms:k:karṇa]]---of eyes and ears; [[synonyms:y:yugma]]---the couples; [[synonyms:j:juḍāila]]---became satisfied.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "In His pastimes, Kṛṣṇa displayed the two ornaments of hyperbole and reverse analogy. Tasting them brought gladness to My mind and fully satisfied My ears and eyes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.1
description: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the most exalted of all devotees of mothers, spoke like a madman and rubbed His face against the walls. Overwhelmed by emotions of ecstatic love, He would sometimes enter the Jagannātha-vallabha garden to perform His pastimes. I offer my respectful obeisances unto Him.
text:
> vande taṁ kṛṣṇa-caitanyaṁ
> mātṛ-bhakta-śiromaṇim
> pralapya mukha-saṅgharṣī
> madhūdyāne lalāsa yaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vande]]---I offer my respectful obeisances; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---unto Him; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanyam]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mātṛ]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---of great devotees of mothers; [[synonyms:ś:śiromaṇim]]---the crown jewel; [[synonyms:p:pralapya]]---talking like a madman; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgharṣī]]---who used to rub His face; [[synonyms:m:madhu]]-[[synonyms:u:udyāne]]---in the garden known as Jagannātha-vallabha; [[synonyms:l:lalāsa]]---enjoyed; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---who.
translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the most exalted of all devotees of mothers, spoke like a madman and rubbed His face against the walls. Overwhelmed by emotions of ecstatic love, He would sometimes enter the Jagannātha-vallabha garden to perform His pastimes. I offer my respectful obeisances unto Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.10
description: "Mother, please do not take this as an offense, for I, your son, am completely dependent upon you.
text:
> ei aparādha tumi nā la-iha āmāra
> tomāra adhīna āmi---putra se tomāra

translation: "Mother, please do not take this as an offense, for I, your son, am completely dependent upon you.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.100
description: Both Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya sang to the Lord, who danced and enjoyed happiness until the morning arrived. Then they devised a plan to revive the Lord to external consciousness.
text:
> svarūpa-rāmānanda gāya, prabhu nāce, sukha pāya,
> ei-mate prātaḥ-kāla haila
> svarūpa-rāmānanda-rāya, kari nānā upāya,
> mahāprabhura bāhya-sphūrti kaila
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]] [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya sing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu dances; [[synonyms:s:sukha]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---enjoys happiness; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---in this way; [[synonyms:p:prātaḥ]]-[[synonyms:k:kāla]] [[synonyms:h:haila]]---morning arrived; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]-[[synonyms:r:rāya]]---both Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---devising; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]---various; [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---means; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]-[[synonyms:s:sphūrti]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---awakened the external consciousness.
translation: Both Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya sang to the Lord, who danced and enjoyed happiness until the morning arrived. Then they devised a plan to revive the Lord to external consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.101
description: Thus, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, the servant of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, have sung of four divisions of the Lord's pastimes in this chapter: the Lord's devotion to His mother, His words of madness, His rubbing His face against the walls at night, and His dancing at the appearance of Lord Kṛṣṇa's fragrance.
text:
> mātṛ-bhakti, pralāpana, bhittye mukha-gharṣaṇa,
> kṛṣṇa-gandha-sphūrtye divya-nṛtya
> ei cāri-līlā-bhede, gāila ei paricchede,
> kṛṣṇadāsa rūpa-gosāñi-bhṛtya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mātṛ]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotion to His mother; [[synonyms:p:pralāpana]]---words of madness; [[synonyms:b:bhittye]]---on the walls; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]-[[synonyms:g:gharṣaṇa]]---rubbing His face; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:gandha]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa's fragrance; [[synonyms:s:sphūrtye]]---on the appearance; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---transcendental dancing; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:c:cāri]]---four; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:b:bhede]]---different; [[synonyms:g:gāila]]---has sung; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:p:paricchede]]---in this chapter; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]-[[synonyms:b:bhṛtya]]---servant of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.
translation: Thus, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, the servant of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, have sung of four divisions of the Lord's pastimes in this chapter: the Lord's devotion to His mother, His words of madness, His rubbing His face against the walls at night, and His dancing at the appearance of Lord Kṛṣṇa's fragrance.
purport: Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī says that he has been able to describe these four pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by the blessings of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī was not actually a direct disciple of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, but he followed the instructions given by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī in //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu.// He therefore acted according to the directions of Rūpa Gosvāmī and prayed in every chapter for his mercy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.102
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus returned to consciousness. He then bathed and went to see Lord Jagannātha.
text:
> ei-mata mahāprabhu pāñā cetana
> snāna kari' kaila jagannātha-daraśana

translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus returned to consciousness. He then bathed and went to see Lord Jagannātha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.103
description: The pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa are uncommonly full of transcendental potency. It is a characteristic of such pastimes that they do not fall within the jurisdiction of experimental logic and arguments.
text:
> alaukika kṛṣṇa-līlā, divya-śakti tāra
> tarkera gocara nahe caritra yāhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:alaukika]]---uncommon; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---transcendental potency; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:t:tarkera]]---of argument; [[synonyms:g:gocara]]---within the purview; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---is not; [[synonyms:c:caritra]]---the characteristics; [[synonyms:y:yāhāra]]---of which.
translation: The pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa are uncommonly full of transcendental potency. It is a characteristic of such pastimes that they do not fall within the jurisdiction of experimental logic and arguments.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.104
description: When transcendental love of Kṛṣṇa awakens in one's heart, even a learned scholar cannot comprehend one's activities.
text:
> ei prema sadā jāge yāhāra antare
> paṇḍiteha tāra ceṣṭā bujhite nā pāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:j:jāge]]---awakens; [[synonyms:y:yāhāra]]---of whom; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---within the heart; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍiteha]]---even a learned scholar; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his; [[synonyms:c:ceṣṭā]]---activities; [[synonyms:b:bujhite]]---to understand; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---cannot.
translation: When transcendental love of Kṛṣṇa awakens in one's heart, even a learned scholar cannot comprehend one's activities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.105
description: "The activities and symptoms of that exalted personality in whose heart love of Godhead has awakened cannot be understood even by the most learned scholar."
text:
> dhanyasyāyaṁ navaḥ premā
> yasyonmīlati cetasi
> antarvāṇībhir apy asya
> mudrā suṣṭhu sudurgamā
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dhanyasya]]---of a most fortunate person; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:n:navaḥ]]---new; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:y:yasya]]---of whom; [[synonyms:u:unmīlati]]---manifests; [[synonyms:c:cetasi]]---in the heart; [[synonyms:a:antarvāṇībhiḥ]]---by persons well versed in //śāstras//; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:a:asya]]---of him; [[synonyms:m:mudrā]]---the symptoms; [[synonyms:s:suṣṭhu]]---exceedingly; [[synonyms:s:sudurgamā]]---difficult to understand.
translation: "The activities and symptoms of that exalted personality in whose heart love of Godhead has awakened cannot be understood even by the most learned scholar."
purport: This verse is quoted from //Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// (1.4.17).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.106
description: The activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are undoubtedly uncommon, especially His talking like a madman. Therefore, one who hears of these pastimes should not put forward mundane arguments. He should simply hear the pastimes with full faith.
text:
> alaukika prabhura 'ceṣṭā', 'pralāpa' śuniyā
> tarka nā kariha, śuna viśvāsa kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:alaukika]]---uncommon; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:ceṣṭā]]---the activities; [[synonyms:p:pralāpa]]---talking in madness; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:t:tarka]]---unnecessary arguments; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do not make; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---simply hear; [[synonyms:v:viśvāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---having full faith.
translation: The activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are undoubtedly uncommon, especially His talking like a madman. Therefore, one who hears of these pastimes should not put forward mundane arguments. He should simply hear the pastimes with full faith.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.107
description: The evidence of the truth of these talks is found in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. There, in the section of the Tenth Canto known as the Bhramara-gītā, "the Song to the Bumblebee," Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī speaks insanely in ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> ihāra satyatve pramāṇa śrī-bhāgavate
> śrī-rādhāra prema-pralāpa 'bhramara-gītā'te
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---of these talks; [[synonyms:s:satyatve]]---in the truthfulness; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---the evidence; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavate]]---in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam//; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rādhāra]]---of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:p:pralāpa]]---talking crazily in ecstatic love; [[synonyms:b:bhramara]]-[[synonyms:g:gītāte]]---in the section known as //Bhramara-gītā.//
translation: The evidence of the truth of these talks is found in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. There, in the section of the Tenth Canto known as the Bhramara-gītā, "the Song to the Bumblebee," Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī speaks insanely in ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.
purport:
When Uddhava arrived from Mathurā carrying a message for the //gopīs,// the //gopīs// began talking about Kṛṣṇa and crying. Then one important //gopī// saw a bumblebee and began speaking to it like someone mad, thinking that the bee was a messenger of Uddhava's or was someone very dear to him and Kṛṣṇa. The verses are as follows (SB. 10.47.12-21):

> madhupa kitava-bandho mā spṛśāṅghriṁ sapatnyāḥ
> kuca-vilulita-mālā-kuṅkuma-śmaśrubhir naḥ
> vahatu madhu-patis tan-māninīnāṁ prasādaṁ
> yadu-sadasi viḍambyaṁ yasya dūtas tvam īdṛk

"My dear bumblebee, you are a very cunning friend of Uddhava and Kṛṣṇa. You are very expert in touching people's feet, but I am not going to be misled by this. You appear to have sat on the breasts of one of Kṛṣṇa's friends, for I see that you have //kuṅkuma// dust on your mustache. Kṛṣṇa is now engaged in flattering all His young girl friends in Mathurā. Therefore, now that He can be called a friend of the residents of Mathurā, He does not need the help of the residents of Vṛndāvana. He has no reason to satisfy us //gopīs.// Since you are the messenger of such a person as He, what is the use of your presence here? Certainly Kṛṣṇa would be ashamed of your presence in this assembly."

How has Kṛṣṇa offended the //gopīs// so that they want to reject Him from their minds? The answer is given as follows:

> sakṛd adhara-sudhāṁ svāṁ mohinīṁ pāyayitvā
> sumanasa iva sadyas tatyaje 'smān bhavādṛk
> paricarati kathaṁ tat-pāda-padmaṁ tu padmā
> hy api bata hṛta-cetā uttama-śloka-jalpaiḥ

"Kṛṣṇa no longer gives us the enchanting nectar of His lips; instead, He now gives that nectar to the women of Mathurā. Kṛṣṇa directly attracts our minds, yet He resembles a bumblebee like you because He gives up the association of a beautiful flower and goes to a flower that is inferior. That is the way Kṛṣṇa has treated us. I do not know why the goddess of fortune continues to serve His lotus feet instead of leaving them aside. Apparently she believes in Kṛṣṇa's false words. We //gopīs,// however, are not unintelligent like Lakṣmī."

After hearing the bumblebee's sweet songs and recognizing that the bee was singing about Kṛṣṇa for Her satisfaction, the //gopī// replied,

> kim iha bahu ṣaḍaṅghre gāyasi tvaṁ yadūnām
> adhipatim agṛhāṇām agrato naḥ purāṇam
> vijaya-sakha-sakhīnāṁ gīyatāṁ tat-prasaṅgaḥ
> kṣapita-kucarujas te kalpayantīṣṭam iṣṭāḥ

"Dear bumblebee, Lord Kṛṣṇa has no residence here, but we know Him as Yadupati [the King of the Yadu dynasty]. We know Him very well, and therefore we are not interested in hearing any more songs about Him. It would be better for you to go sing to those who are now very dear to Kṛṣṇa. Those women of Mathurā have now achieved the opportunity to be embraced by Him. They are His beloveds now, and therefore He has relieved the burning in their breasts. If you go there and sing your songs to those fortunate women, they will be very pleased, and they will honor you."

> divi bhuvi ca rasāyāṁ kāḥ striyas tad durāpāḥ
> kapaṭa-rucira-hāsa-bhrūvi-jṛmbhasya yāḥ syuḥ
> caraṇa-raja upāste yasya bhūtir vayaṁ kā
> api ca kṛpaṇa-pakṣe hy uttamaśloka-śabdaḥ

"O collector of honey, Kṛṣṇa must be very sorry not to see us gopīs. Surely He is afflicted by memories of our pastimes. Therefore He has sent you as a messenger to satisfy us. Do not speak to us! All the women in the three worlds where death is inevitable---the heavenly, middle and lower planets-are very easily available to Kṛṣṇa because His curved eyebrows are so attractive. Moreover, He is always served very faithfully by the goddess of fortune. In comparison with her, we are most insignificant. Indeed, we are nothing. Yet although He is very cunning, Kṛṣṇa is also very charitable. You may inform Him that He is praised for His kindness to unfortunate persons and that He is therefore known as Uttamaśloka, one who is praised by chosen words and verses."

> visṛja śirasi pādaṁ vedmy ahaṁ cāṭukārair
> anunaya-viduṣas te 'bhyetya dautyair mukundāt
> svakṛta iha visṛṣṭāpatya-paty-anya-lokā
> vyasṛjad akṛta-cetāḥ kiṁ nu sandheyam asmin

"You are buzzing at My feet just to be forgiven for your past offenses. Kindly go away from My feet! I know that Mukunda has taught you to speak very sweet, flattering words like this and to act as His messenger. These are certainly clever tricks, My dear bumblebee, but I can understand them. This is Kṛṣṇa's offense. Do not tell Kṛṣṇa what I have said, although I know that you are very envious. We //gopīs// have given up our husbands, our sons, and all the religious principles that promise better births, and now we have no other business then serving Kṛṣṇa. Yet Kṛṣṇa, by controlling His mind, has easily forgotten us. Therefore, don't speak of Him any more. Let us forget our relationship."

> mṛgayur iva kapīndraṁ vivyadhe lubdha-dharmā
> striyam akṛta-virūpāṁ strī-jitaḥ kāmayānām
> balim api balim attvāveṣṭayad dhvāṅkṣavad yas
> tad alam asita-sakhyair dustyajas tat-kathārthaḥ

"When we remember the past births of Kṛṣṇa, My dear bumblebee, we are very afraid of Him. In His incarnation as Lord Rāmacandra, He acted just like a hunter and unjustly killed His friend Vāli. Lusty Śūrpaṇakhā came to satisfy Rāmacandra's desires, but He was so attached to Sītādevī that He cut off Śūrpaṇakhā's nose. In His incarnation as Vāmanadeva, He plundered Bali Mahārāja and took all his possessions, cheating him on the pretext of accepting worship from him. Vāmanadeva caught Bali Mahārāja exactly as one catches a crow. My dear bumblebee, it is not very good to make friends with such a person. I know that once one begins to talk about Kṛṣṇa, it is very difficult to stop, and I admit that I have insufficient strength to give up talking about Him."

> yad-anucarita-līlā-karṇa-pīyuṣa-vipruṭ
> sakṛd adana-vidhūta-dvandva-dharmā vinaṣṭāḥ
> sapadi gṛha-kuṭumbaṁ dīnam utsṛjya dīnā
> bahava iha vihaṅgā bhikṣu-caryāṁ caranti

"Topics about Kṛṣṇa are so powerful that they destroy the four religious principles-religion, economic development, sense gratification and liberation. Anyone who drinks even a small drop of //kṛṣṇa-kathā// through aural reception is freed from all material attachment and envy. Like a bird with no means of subsistence, such a person becomes a mendicant and lives by begging. Ordinary household affairs become miserable for him, and without attachment he suddenly gives up everything. Although such renunciation is quite suitable, because I am a woman I am unable to adopt it."

> vayam ṛtam iva jihma-vyāhṛtaṁ śraddadhānāḥ
> kulikarutam ivājñāḥ kṛṣṇa-vadhvo hiraṇyaḥ
> dadṛśur asakṛd etat tan-nakha-sparśatīvra-
> smararuja upamantrin bhaṇyatām anya-vārtā

"O My dear messenger, I am just like a foolish bird that hears the sweet songs of a hunter, believes in them due to simplicity, and is then pierced in the heart and made to suffer all kinds of miseries. Because we believed in Kṛṣṇa's words, we have suffered great pain. Indeed, the touch of Kṛṣṇa's nails has injured our faces. He has caused us so much pain! Therefore, you should give up topics concerning Him and talk about something else."

After hearing all these statements from Śrīmatī Rādhikā, the bumblebee left and then returned. After some thought, the //gopī// said:

> priya-sakha punar āgāḥ preyasā preṣitaḥ kiṁ
> varaya kim anurundhe mānanīyo 'si me 'ṅga
> nayasi katham ihāsmān dustyaja-dvandva-pārśvaṁ
> satatam urasi saumya śrīr vadhūḥ sākamāste

"You are Kṛṣṇa's very dear friend, and by His order you have come here again. Therefore you are worshipable for Me. O best of messengers, tell Me now, what is your request? What do you want? Kṛṣṇa cannot give up conjugal love, and therefore I understand that you have come here to take us to Him. But how will you do that? We know many goddesses of fortune now reside at Kṛṣṇa's chest, and they constantly serve Kṛṣṇa better than we can."

Praising the bumblebee for its sobriety, She began to speak in great jubilation.

> api bata madhu-puryām ārya-putro 'dhunā 'ste
> smarati sa pitṛ-gehān saumya bandhūṁś ca gopān
> kvacid api sa kathā naḥ kiṅkarīṇāṁ gṛṇīte
> bhujam aguru-sugandhaṁ mūrdhny adhāsyat kadā nu

"Kṛṣṇa is now living like a gentleman at the Gurukula in Mathurā, forgetting all the //gopīs// of Vṛndāvana. But does He not remember the sweet house of His father, Nanda Mahārāja? We are all naturally His maidservants. Does He not remember us? Does He ever speak about us, or has He forgotten us completely? Will He ever forgive us and once again touch us with those hands fragrant with the scent of //aguru//?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.108
description: The songs of the queens at Dvārakā, which are mentioned at the end of the Tenth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, have a very special meaning. They are not understood even by the most learned scholars.
text:
> mahiṣīra gīta yena 'daśame'ra śeṣe
> paṇḍite nā bujhe tāra artha-viśeṣe
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahiṣīra]]---of the queens; [[synonyms:g:gīta]]---the songs; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---just as; [[synonyms:d:daśamera]]---of the Tenth Canto; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---at the end; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍite]]---very learned scholars; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:b:bujhe]]---understand; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---its; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:v:viśeṣe]]---particular meaning.
translation: The songs of the queens at Dvārakā, which are mentioned at the end of the Tenth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, have a very special meaning. They are not understood even by the most learned scholars.
purport:
These songs of //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// are verses 15-24 of the Ninetieth Chapter of the Tenth Canto.

> kurari vilapasi tvaṁ vīta-nidrā na śeṣe
> svapiti jagati rātryām īśvaro gupta-bodhaḥ
> vayam iva sakhi kaccid gāḍha-nirbhinna-cetā
> nalina-nayana-hāsodāra-līlekṣitena

All the queens incessantly thought of Kṛṣṇa. After their pastimes in the water, the queens said, "Our dear friend the osprey, Kṛṣṇa is now asleep, but we stay awake at night because of Him. You laugh at us when you see us awake at night, but why are you not sleeping? You seem absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa. Have you also been pierced by Kṛṣṇa's smile? His smile is very sweet. One who is pierced by such an arrow is very fortunate."

> netre nimīlayasi naktam adṛṣṭa-bandhus
> tvam roravīṣi karuṇaṁ bata cakravāki
> dāsyaṁ gatā vayam ivācyuta-pāda-juṣṭāṁ
> kiṁ vā srajaṁ spṛhayase kabareṇa voḍhum

"O //cakravāki,// you keep your eyes wide open at night because you cannot see your friend. Indeed, you are suffering very much. Is it because of compassion that you are crying, or are you trying to capture Kṛṣṇa by remembering Him? Having been touched by the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, all the queens are very happy. Are you crying to wear Kṛṣṇa's garland on your head? Please answer these questions clearly, O //cakravāki,// so that we can understand."

> bho bhoḥ sadā niṣṭanase udanvann
> alabdha-nidro 'dhigata-prajāgaraḥ
> kiṁ vā mukundāpahṛtātma-lāñchanaḥ
> prāptāṁ daśāṁ tvaṁ ca gato duratyayām

"O ocean, you have no opportunity to sleep quietly at night. Instead, you are always awake and crying. You have received this benediction, and your heart is broken just like ours. Mukunda's business with us is simply to smear our marks of //kuṅkuma.// O ocean, you suffer as much as we."

> tvaṁ yakṣmaṇā balavatāsi gṛhīta indo
> kṣīṇas tamo na nija-dīdhitibhiḥ kṣiṇoṣi
> kaccin mukunda-gaditāni yathā vayaṁ tvaṁ
> vismṛtya bhoḥ sthagita-gīr upalakṣyase naḥ

"O moon, you appear to be suffering from a severe fever, perhaps tuberculosis. Indeed, your effulgence does not have the strength to destroy the darkness. Have you become mad after hearing the songs of Kṛṣṇa? Is that why you are silent? Seeing your suffering, we feel that you are one of us."

> kiṁ tvācaritam asmābhir
> malayānila te 'priyam
> govindāpāṅga-nirbhinne
> hṛdīrayasi naḥ smaran

"O Malayan breeze, kindly tell us what wrong we have done to you. Why do you fan the flames of desire in our hearts? We have been pierced by the arrow of Govinda's glance, for He is perfect in the art of awakening the influence of Cupid."

> megha śrīmaṁs tvam asi dayito yādavendrasya nūnaṁ
> śrīvatsāṅkaṁ vayam iva bhavān dhyāyati prema-baddhaḥ
> atyutkaṇṭhaḥ śabala-hṛdayo 'smad-vidho bāṣpa-dhārāḥ
> smṛtvā smṛtvā visṛjasi muhur duḥkha-das tat-prasaṅgaḥ

"Dear cloud, O friend of Kṛṣṇa's, are you thinking of the Śrīvatsa symbol on Kṛṣṇa's chest like us queens engaged in loving affairs with Him? You are absorbed in meditation, remembering the association of Kṛṣṇa, and thus you shed tears of misery."

> priya-rāva-padāni bhāṣase
> mṛta-saṁjīvikayānayā girā
> karavāṇi kim adya te priyaṁ
> vada me valgita-kaṇṭha kokila

"Dear cuckoo, you possess a very sweet voice, and you are very expert in imitating others. You could excite even a dead body with your voice. Therefore, tell the queens that good behavior is their proper duty."

> na calasi na vadasy udāra-buddhe
> kṣiti-dhara cintyase mahāntam artham
> api bata vasudeva-nandanāṅghriṁ
> vayam iva kāmayase stanair vidhartum

"O magnanimous mountain, you are very grave and sober, absorbed in thoughts of doing something very great. Like us, you have vowed to keep within your heart the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Vasudeva."

> śuṣyad-ghradāḥ karśitā bata sindhu-patnyaḥ
> sampraty-apāsta-kamala-śriya-iṣṭa-bhartuḥ
> yadvad vayaṁ madhu-pateḥ praṇayāvalokam
> aprāpya muṣṭa-hṛdayāḥ puru-karṣitāḥ sma

"O rivers, wives of the ocean, we see that the ocean does not give you happiness. Thus you have almost dried up, and you no longer bear beautiful lotuses. The lotuses have become skinny, and even in the sunshine they are devoid of all pleasure. Similarly, the hearts of us poor queens are all dried up, and our bodies are skinny because we are now devoid of loving affairs with Madhupati. Are you, like us, dry and without beauty because you are devoid of Kṛṣṇa's loving glance?"

> haṁsa svāgatam āsyatāṁ piba payo brūhy aṅga śaureḥ kathāṁ
> dūtaṁ tvāṁ nu vidāma kaccid ajitaḥ svasty āsta uktaṁ purā
> kiṁ vā naś cala-sauhṛdaḥ smarati taṁ kasmād bhajāmo vayaṁ
> kṣaudrālāpaya-kāmadaṁ śriyamṛte saivaika-niṣṭhā striyām

"O swan, you have come here so happily! Let us welcome you. We understand that you are always Kṛṣṇa's messenger. Now while you drink this milk, tell us what His message is. Has Kṛṣṇa said something about us to you? May we inquire from you whether Kṛṣṇa is happy? We want to know. Does He remember us? We know that the goddess of fortune is serving Him alone. We are simply maidservants. How can we worship He who speaks sweet words but never fulfills our desires?"

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.109
description: If one becomes a servant of the servants of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Lord Nityānanda Prabhu and is favored by Them, he can believe in all these discourses.
text:
> mahāprabhu-nityānanda, doṅhāra dāsera dāsa
> yāre kṛpā karena, tāra haya ithe viśvāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:d:doṅhāra]] [[synonyms:d:dāsera]] [[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---I am a servant of the servant of the servants of these two personalities; [[synonyms:y:yāre]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:karena]]---if anyone is favored by Them; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---he certainly maintains; [[synonyms:i:ithe]] [[synonyms:v:viśvāsa]]---faith in all these affairs.
translation: If one becomes a servant of the servants of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Lord Nityānanda Prabhu and is favored by Them, he can believe in all these discourses.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.11
description: "I am staying here at Nīlācala, Jagannātha Purī, according to your order. As long as I live, I shall not leave this place.' "
text:
> nīlācale āchi āmi tomāra ājñāte
> yāvat jība, tāvat āmi nāriba chāḍite'
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---Jagannātha Purī, Nīlācala; [[synonyms:ā:āchi]] [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I am; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:ā:ājñāte]]---on the basis of your order; [[synonyms:y:yāvat]] [[synonyms:j:jība]]---as long as I live; [[synonyms:t:tāvat]]---so long; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:n:nāriba]]---shall not be able; [[synonyms:c:chāḍite]]---to leave.
translation: "I am staying here at Nīlācala, Jagannātha Purī, according to your order. As long as I live, I shall not leave this place.' "

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.110
description: Just try to hear these topics with faith, for there is great pleasure even in hearing them. That hearing will destroy all miseries pertaining to the body, mind and other living entities, and the unhappiness of false arguments as well.
text:
> śraddhā kari, śuna ihā, śunite mahā-sukha
> khaṇḍibe ādhyātmikādi kutarkādi-duḥkha
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śraddhā]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---with great faith; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---all these topics; [[synonyms:ś:śunite]]---even to hear; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]---great pleasure; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍibe]]---it will destroy; [[synonyms:ā:ādhyātmika]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---all distresses due to the body, mind and so on; [[synonyms:k:kutarka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---and the miserable conditions arising from the use of false arguments.
translation: Just try to hear these topics with faith, for there is great pleasure even in hearing them. That hearing will destroy all miseries pertaining to the body, mind and other living entities, and the unhappiness of false arguments as well.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.111
description: Caitanya-caritāmṛta is ever-increasingly fresh. Continuously hearing it pacifies one's heart and ear.
text:
> caitanya-caritāmṛta---nitya-nūtana
> śunite śunite juḍāya hṛdaya-śravaṇa
