translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in this way stayed immersed day and night in an ocean of ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa. Sometimes He was submerged, and sometimes He floated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.78
description: One full-moon night in the month of Vaiśākha [April and May], Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to a garden.
text:
> eka-kāle vaiśākhera paurṇamāsī-dine
> rātri-kāle mahāprabhu calilā udyāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at one time; [[synonyms:v:vaiśākhera]]---of the month of Vaiśākha, (April-May); [[synonyms:p:paurṇamāsī]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---on the full-moon night; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at night; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went; [[synonyms:u:udyāne]]---to a garden.
translation: One full-moon night in the month of Vaiśākha [April and May], Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to a garden.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.79
description: The Lord, along with His devotees, entered one of the nicest gardens, called Jagannātha-vallabha.
text:
> 'jagannātha-vallabha' nāma udyāna-pradhāne
> praveśa karilā prabhu lañā bhakta-gaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]-[[synonyms:v:vallabha]]---Jagannātha-vallabha; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:u:udyāna]]-[[synonyms:p:pradhāne]]---one of the best gardens; [[synonyms:p:praveśa]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---entered; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---the devotees.
translation: The Lord, along with His devotees, entered one of the nicest gardens, called Jagannātha-vallabha.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.8
description: "Any day you desire to feed Me, I certainly come and accept what you offer.
text:
> ye-dine tomāra icchā karāite bhojana
> se-dine āsi' avaśya kariye bhakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---any day; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:i:icchā]]---desire; [[synonyms:k:karāite]] [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---to feed Me; [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---on that day; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:k:kariye]] [[synonyms:b:bhakṣaṇa]]---I eat.
translation: "Any day you desire to feed Me, I certainly come and accept what you offer.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.80
description: In the garden were fully blossomed trees and creepers exactly like those in Vṛndāvana. Bumblebees and birds like the śuka, śārī and pika talked with one another.
text:
> praphullita vṛkṣa-vallī,---yena vṛndāvana
> śuka, śārī, pika, bhṛṅga kare ālāpana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:praphullita]]---fully blossomed; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:v:vallī]]---trees and creepers; [[synonyms:y:yena]] [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---exactly resembling Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:ś:śuka]]---the //śuka// birds; [[synonyms:ś:śārī]]---the //śārī// birds; [[synonyms:p:pika]]---the //pika// birds; [[synonyms:b:bhṛṅga]]---the bumblebees; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:ā:ālāpana]]---talking with one another.
translation: In the garden were fully blossomed trees and creepers exactly like those in Vṛndāvana. Bumblebees and birds like the śuka, śārī and pika talked with one another.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.81
description: A mild breeze was blowing, carrying the fragrance of aromatic flowers. The breeze had become a guru and was teaching all the trees and creepers how to dance.
text:
> puṣpa-gandha lañā vahe malaya-pavana
> 'guru' hañā taru-latāya śikhāya nācana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gandha]]---the fragrance of the flowers; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:v:vahe]]---blows; [[synonyms:m:malaya]]-[[synonyms:p:pavana]]---the mild breeze; [[synonyms:g:guru]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming the spiritual master; [[synonyms:t:taru]]-[[synonyms:l:latāya]]---to the trees and creepers; [[synonyms:ś:śikhāya]]---instructs; [[synonyms:n:nācana]]---dancing.
translation: A mild breeze was blowing, carrying the fragrance of aromatic flowers. The breeze had become a guru and was teaching all the trees and creepers how to dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.82
description: Brightly illuminated by the full moon, the trees and creepers glittered in the light.
text:
> pūrṇa-candra-candrikāya parama ujjvala
> taru-latādi jyotsnāya kare jhalamala
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---of the full moon; [[synonyms:c:candrikāya]]---by the shine; [[synonyms:p:parama]]---very; [[synonyms:u:ujjvala]]---bright; [[synonyms:t:taru]]-[[synonyms:l:latā]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the creepers, trees and so on; [[synonyms:j:jyotsnāya]]---in the illumination of the moonshine; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:j:jhalamala]]---glittering.
translation: Brightly illuminated by the full moon, the trees and creepers glittered in the light.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.83
description: The six seasons, especially spring, seemed present there. Seeing the garden, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, was very happy.
text:
> chaya ṛtu-gaṇa yāhāṅ vasanta pradhāna
> dekhi' ānandita hailā gaura bhagavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:chaya]]---six; [[synonyms:ṛ:ṛtu]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---seasons; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:v:vasanta]] [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---the spring season was chief; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---very pleased; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: The six seasons, especially spring, seemed present there. Seeing the garden, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, was very happy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.84
description: In this atmosphere, the Lord had His associates sing a verse from the Gīta-govinda, beginning with the words "lalita-lavaṅga-latā," as He danced and wandered about with them.
text:
> "lalita-lavaṅga-latā" pada gāoyāñā
> nṛtya kari' bulena prabhu nija-gaṇa lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lalita]]-[[synonyms:l:lavaṅga]]-[[synonyms:l:latā]]---beginning with the words //lalita-lavaṅga-latā//; [[synonyms:p:pada]]---the verse; [[synonyms:g:gāoyāñā]]---making sing; [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---dancing; [[synonyms:b:bulena]]---wanders; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---accompanied by His personal associates.
translation: In this atmosphere, the Lord had His associates sing a verse from the Gīta-govinda, beginning with the words "lalita-lavaṅga-latā," as He danced and wandered about with them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.85
description: As He thus wandered around every tree and creeper, He came beneath an aśoka tree and suddenly saw Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> prati-vṛkṣa-vallī aiche bhramite bhramite
> aśokera tale kṛṣṇe dekhena ācambite
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:v:vallī]]---around each and every tree and creeper; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---in that way; [[synonyms:b:bhramite]] [[synonyms:b:bhramite]]---wandering; [[synonyms:a:aśokera]] [[synonyms:t:tale]]---underneath an //aśoka// tree; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dekhena]]---He sees; [[synonyms:ā:ācambite]]---suddenly.
translation: As He thus wandered around every tree and creeper, He came beneath an aśoka tree and suddenly saw Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.86
description: When He saw Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began running very swiftly, but Kṛṣṇa smiled and disappeared.
text:
> kṛṣṇa dekhi' mahāprabhu dhāñā calilā
> āge dekhi' hāsi' kṛṣṇa antardhāna ha-ilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dhāñā]] [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---began to run very swiftly; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---ahead; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:hāsi']]---smiling; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:antardhāna]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---disappeared.
translation: When He saw Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began running very swiftly, but Kṛṣṇa smiled and disappeared.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.87
description: Having first gotten Kṛṣṇa and then having lost Him again, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell to the ground unconscious.
text:
> āge pāilā kṛṣṇe, tāṅre punaḥ hārāñā
> bhūmete paḍilā prabhu mūrcchita hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in the beginning; [[synonyms:p:pāilā]]---got; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---Him; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:h:hārāñā]]---losing; [[synonyms:b:bhūmete]]---on the ground; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]]---fell down; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mūrcchita]]---unconscious; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming.
translation: Having first gotten Kṛṣṇa and then having lost Him again, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell to the ground unconscious.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.88
description: The entire garden was filled with the scent of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa's transcendental body. When Srī Caitanya Mahāprabhu smelled it, He fell unconscious at once.
text:
> kṛṣṇera śrī-aṅga-gandhe bhariche udyāne
> sei gandha pāñā prabhu hailā acetane
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:g:gandhe]]---the aroma of the transcendental body; [[synonyms:b:bhariche]]---filled; [[synonyms:u:udyāne]]---in the garden; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:g:gandha]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting that aroma; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hailā]]---became; [[synonyms:a:acetane]]---unconscious.
translation: The entire garden was filled with the scent of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa's transcendental body. When Srī Caitanya Mahāprabhu smelled it, He fell unconscious at once.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.89
description: The scent of Kṛṣṇa's body, however, incessantly entered His nostrils, and the Lord became mad to relish it.
text:
> nirantara nāsāya paśe kṛṣṇa-parimala
> gandha āsvādite prabhu ha-ilā pāgala
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---incessantly; [[synonyms:n:nāsāya]]---in the nostrils; [[synonyms:p:paśe]]---enters; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:parimala]]---the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body; [[synonyms:g:gandha]] [[synonyms:ā:āsvādite]]---to relish the fragrance; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]] [[synonyms:p:pāgala]]---became mad.
translation: The scent of Kṛṣṇa's body, however, incessantly entered His nostrils, and the Lord became mad to relish it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.9
description: " 'I have given up service to you and have accepted the vow of sannyāsa. I have thus become mad and have destroyed the principles of religion.
text:
> tomāra sevā chāḍi' āmi kariluṅ sannyāsa
> 'bāula' hañā āmi kailuṅ dharma-nāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomāra]] [[synonyms:s:sevā]] [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up your service; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kariluṅ]]---accepted; [[synonyms:s:sannyāsa]]---the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:b:bāula]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming mad; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:k:kailuṅ]]---did; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---destruction of religion.
translation: “ 'I have given up service to you and have accepted the vow of sannyāsa. I have thus become mad and have destroyed the principles of religion.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.90
description: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī expressed to Her gopī friends how She hankers for the transcendental scent of Kṛṣṇa's body. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited that same verse and made its meaning clear.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-gandha-lubdhā rādhā sakhīre ye kahilā
> sei śloka paḍi' prabhu artha karilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:gandha]]---the scent of the body of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:lubdhā]]---hankering after; [[synonyms:r:rādhā]]---Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:s:sakhīre]]---to the //gopī// friends; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---whatever She said; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---verse; [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---reciting; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---explained its meaning.
translation: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī expressed to Her gopī friends how She hankers for the transcendental scent of Kṛṣṇa's body. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited that same verse and made its meaning clear.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.91
description: " 'The scent of Kṛṣṇa's transcendental body surpasses the aroma of musk and attracts the minds of all women. The eight lotuslike parts of His body distribute the fragrance of lotuses mixed with that of camphor. His body is anointed with aromatic substances like musk, camphor, sandalwood and aguru. O My dear friend, that Personality of Godhead, also known as the enchanter of Cupid, always increases the desire of My nostrils.'
text:
> kuraṅga-mada-jid-vapuḥ-parimalormi-kṛṣṭāṅganaḥ
> svakāṅga-nalināṣṭake śaśi-yutābja-gandha-prathaḥ
> madenduvara-candanāguru-sugandhi-carcārcitaḥ
> sa me madana-mohanaḥ sakhi tanoti nāsā-spṛhām
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kuraṅga]]-[[synonyms:m:mada]]-[[synonyms:j:jit]]---conquering the aromatic smell of musk; [[synonyms:v:vapuḥ]]---of His transcendental body; [[synonyms:p:parimala]]-[[synonyms:ū:ūrmi]]---with waves of scent; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅganaḥ]]---attracting the //gopīs// of Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:s:svaka]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:n:nalina]]-[[synonyms:a:aṣṭake]]---on all eight different lotuslike parts of the body (face, navel, eyes, palms and feet); [[synonyms:ś:śaśi]]-[[synonyms:y:yuta]]-[[synonyms:a:abja]]-[[synonyms:g:gandha]]-[[synonyms:p:prathaḥ]]---who distributes the scent of lotus mixed with camphor; [[synonyms:m:mada]]-[[synonyms:i:induvara]]-[[synonyms:c:candana]]-[[synonyms:a:aguru]]-[[synonyms:s:sugandhi]]-[[synonyms:c:carca]]-[[synonyms:a:arcitaḥ]]---smeared with the unguents of musk, camphor, white sandalwood and //aguru//; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---He; [[synonyms:m:me]]---My; [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mohanaḥ]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa, who enchants even Cupid; [[synonyms:s:sakhi]]---O My dear friends; [[synonyms:t:tanoti]]---increases; [[synonyms:n:nāsā]]-[[synonyms:s:spṛhām]]---the desire of My nostrils.
translation: “ 'The scent of Kṛṣṇa's transcendental body surpasses the aroma of musk and attracts the minds of all women. The eight lotuslike parts of His body distribute the fragrance of lotuses mixed with that of camphor. His body is anointed with aromatic substances like musk, camphor, sandalwood and aguru. O My dear friend, that Personality of Godhead, also known as the enchanter of Cupid, always increases the desire of My nostrils.'
purport: This is a verse found in //Govinda-līlāmṛta// (8.6).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.92
description: "The scent of Kṛṣṇa's body surpasses the fragrances of musk and the bluish lotus flower. Spreading throughout the fourteen worlds, it attracts everyone and makes the eyes of all women blind.
text:
> kastūrikā-nīlotpala, tāra yei parimala,
> tāhā jini' kṛṣṇa-aṅga-gandha
> vyāpe caudda-bhuvane, kare sarva ākarṣaṇe,
> nārī-gaṇera āṅkhi kare andha
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kastūrikā]]---musk; [[synonyms:n:nīlotpala]]---combined with the bluish lotus flower; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---its; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:p:parimala]]---scent; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:j:jini']]---conquering; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---of the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gandha]]---the scent; [[synonyms:v:vyāpe]]---spreads; [[synonyms:c:caudda]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvane]]---throughout the fourteen worlds; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:s:sarva]] [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaṇe]]---attracting everyone; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the women; [[synonyms:ā:āṅkhi]]---the eyes; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---makes; [[synonyms:a:andha]]---blind.
translation: "The scent of Kṛṣṇa's body surpasses the fragrances of musk and the bluish lotus flower. Spreading throughout the fourteen worlds, it attracts everyone and makes the eyes of all women blind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.93
description: "My dear friend, the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body enchants the entire world. It especially enters the nostrils of women and remains seated there. Thus it captures them and forcibly brings them to Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> sakhi he, kṛṣṇa-gandha jagat mātāya
> nārīra nāsāte paśe, sarva-kāla tāhāṅ vaise,
> kṛṣṇa-pāśa dhari' lañā yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakhi]] [[synonyms:h:he]]---O My dear friend; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:gandha]]---the fragrance of the body of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:j:jagat]] [[synonyms:m:mātāya]]---enchants the whole world; [[synonyms:n:nārīra]]---of women; [[synonyms:n:nāsāte]]---in the nostrils; [[synonyms:p:paśe]]---enters; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:k:kāla]]---always; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:v:vaise]]---remains; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśa]]---to the side of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching; [[synonyms:l:lañā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---takes one.
translation: "My dear friend, the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body enchants the entire world. It especially enters the nostrils of women and remains seated there. Thus it captures them and forcibly brings them to Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.94
description: "Kṛṣṇa's eyes, navel and face, hands and feet are like eight lotus flowers on His body. From those eight lotuses emanates a fragrance like a mixture of camphor and lotus. That is the scent associated with His body.
text:
> netra-nābhi, vadana, kara-yuga caraṇa,
> ei aṣṭa-padma kṛṣṇa-aṅge
> karpūra-lipta kamala, tāra yaiche parimala,
> sei gandha aṣṭa-padma-saṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:netra]]---the eyes; [[synonyms:n:nābhi]]---the navel; [[synonyms:v:vadana]]---the face; [[synonyms:k:kara]]-[[synonyms:y:yuga]]---the palms; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the feet; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]]---eight; [[synonyms:p:padma]]---lotus flowers; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---in the body of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]---with camphor; [[synonyms:l:lipta]]---smeared; [[synonyms:k:kamala]]---the lotus flower; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---like; [[synonyms:p:parimala]]---the fragrance; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:g:gandha]]---that fragrance; [[synonyms:a:aṣṭa]]-[[synonyms:p:padma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---is associated with the eight lotus flowers.
translation: "Kṛṣṇa's eyes, navel and face, hands and feet are like eight lotus flowers on His body. From those eight lotuses emanates a fragrance like a mixture of camphor and lotus. That is the scent associated with His body.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.95
description: "When sandalwood pulp with aguru, kuṅkuma and musk is mixed with camphor and spread on Kṛṣṇa's body, it combines with Kṛṣṇa's own original bodily perfume and seems to cover it.
text:
> hema-kīlita candana, tāhā kari' gharṣaṇa,
> tāhe aguru, kuṅkuma, kastūrī
> karpūra-sane carcā aṅge, pūrva aṅgera gandha saṅge,
> mili' tāre yena kaila curi
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hema]]---with gold; [[synonyms:k:kīlita]]---bedecked; [[synonyms:c:candana]]---white sandalwood; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:g:gharṣaṇa]]---rubbing; [[synonyms:t:tāhe]]---in that; [[synonyms:a:aguru]]---the //aguru// flavor; [[synonyms:k:kuṅkuma]]---//kuṅkuma//; [[synonyms:k:kastūrī]]---and musk; [[synonyms:k:karpūra]]---camphor; [[synonyms:s:sane]]---with; [[synonyms:c:carcā]]---smearing; [[synonyms:a:aṅge]]---on the body; [[synonyms:p:pūrva]]---previous; [[synonyms:a:aṅgera]]---of the body; [[synonyms:g:gandha]]---scent; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with; [[synonyms:m:mili']]---combining; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---that; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as if; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:c:curi]]---stealing or covering.
translation: "When sandalwood pulp with aguru, kuṅkuma and musk is mixed with camphor and spread on Kṛṣṇa's body, it combines with Kṛṣṇa's own original bodily perfume and seems to cover it.
purport: In another version, the last line of this verse reads, kāmadevera mana kaila curi. This means "the scent of all these substances mixes with the previous scent of Kṛṣṇa's body and steals away the mind of Cupid."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.96
description: "The scent of Kṛṣṇa's transcendental body is so attractive that it enchants the bodies and minds of all women. It bewilders their nostrils, loosens their belts and hair, and makes them madwomen. All the women of world come under its influence, and therefore the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body is like a plunderer.
text:
> hare nārīra tanu-mana, nāsā kare ghūrṇana,
> khasāya nīvi, chuṭāya keśa-bandha
> kariyā āge bāurī, nācāya jagat-nāri,
> hena ḍākātiyā kṛṣṇāṅga-gandha
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hare]]---enchants; [[synonyms:n:nārīra]]---of women; [[synonyms:t:tanu]]-[[synonyms:m:mana]]---the minds and bodies; [[synonyms:n:nāsā]]---the nostrils; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:g:ghūrṇana]]---bewilders; [[synonyms:k:khasāya]]---slackens; [[synonyms:n:nīvi]]---the belt; [[synonyms:c:chuṭāya]]---loosens; [[synonyms:k:keśa]]-[[synonyms:b:bandha]]---the bunch of hair; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---acting; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front; [[synonyms:b:bāurī]]---like madwomen; [[synonyms:n:nācāya]]---causes to dance; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:n:nārī]]---all the women of the world; [[synonyms:h:hena]]---such; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍākātiyā]]---a plunderer; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:g:gandha]]---the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body.
translation: "The scent of Kṛṣṇa's transcendental body is so attractive that it enchants the bodies and minds of all women. It bewilders their nostrils, loosens their belts and hair, and makes them madwomen. All the women of world come under its influence, and therefore the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body is like a plunderer.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.97
description: "Falling completely under its influence, the nostrils yearn for it continuously, although sometimes they obtain it and sometimes not. When they do they drink their fill, though they still want more and more, but if they don't, out of thirst they die.
text:
> sei gandha-vaśa nāsā, sadā kare gandhera āśā,
> kabhu pāya, kabhu nāhi pāya
> pāile piyā peṭa bhare, piṅa piṅa tabu kare,
> nā pāile tṛṣṇāya mari' yāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:g:gandha]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---under the control of the fragrance; [[synonyms:n:nāsā]]---the nostrils; [[synonyms:s:sadā]]---always; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---make; [[synonyms:g:gandhera]]---for the fragrance; [[synonyms:ā:āśā]]---hope; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---sometimes they obtain; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---sometimes do not obtain; [[synonyms:p:pāile]]---if obtaining; [[synonyms:p:piyā]]---drinking; [[synonyms:p:peṭa]]---the belly; [[synonyms:b:bhare]]---fills; [[synonyms:p:piṅa]]---let me drink; [[synonyms:p:piṅa]]---let me drink; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---they hanker; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāile]]---if they do not get; [[synonyms:t:tṛṣṇāya]]---out of thirst; [[synonyms:m:mari']] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---they die.
translation: "Falling completely under its influence, the nostrils yearn for it continuously, although sometimes they obtain it and sometimes not. When they do they drink their fill, though they still want more and more, but if they don't, out of thirst they die.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.98
description: "The dramatic actor Madana-mohana has opened a shop of scents that attract the women of the world to be His customers. He delivers the scents freely, but they make the women all so blind they cannot find the path returning home."
text:
> madana-mohana-nāṭa, pasāri gandhera hāṭa,
> jagan-nārī-grāhake lobhāya
> vinā-mūlye deya gandha, gandha diyā kare andha,
> ghara yāite patha nāhi pāya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mohana]]-[[synonyms:n:nāṭa]]---the dramatic player Madana-mohana; [[synonyms:p:pasāri]]---a dealer; [[synonyms:g:gandhera]] [[synonyms:h:hāṭa]]---in a market of scents; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:n:nārī]]---of the women of the whole world; [[synonyms:g:grāhake]]---to the customers; [[synonyms:l:lobhāya]]---attracts; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]-[[synonyms:m:mūlye]]---without a price; [[synonyms:d:deya]]---distributes; [[synonyms:g:gandha]]---the scent; [[synonyms:g:gandha]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---delivering the scent; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:a:andha]]---makes the customers blind; [[synonyms:g:ghara]] [[synonyms:y:yāite]]---to return home; [[synonyms:p:patha]]---the path; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---do not find.
translation: "The dramatic actor Madana-mohana has opened a shop of scents that attract the women of the world to be His customers. He delivers the scents freely, but they make the women all so blind they cannot find the path returning home."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 19.99
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, His mind thus stolen by that scent, ran here and there like a bumblebee. He ran to the trees and plants, hoping that Lord Kṛṣṇa would appear, but instead He found only the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body.
text:
> ei-mata gaurahari, gandhe kaila mana curi,
> bhṛṅga-prāya iti-uti dhāya
> yāya vṛkṣa-latā-pāśe, kṛṣṇa sphure---sei āśe,
> kṛṣṇa nā pāya, gandha-mātra pāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:g:gaurahari]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gandhe]]---by the scent; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---did; [[synonyms:m:mana]] [[synonyms:c:curi]]---stealing of the mind; [[synonyms:b:bhṛṅga]]-[[synonyms:p:prāya]]---just like a bumblebee; [[synonyms:i:iti]]-[[synonyms:u:uti]] [[synonyms:d:dhāya]]---wanders here and there; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]]-[[synonyms:l:latā]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśe]]---by the side of the trees and creepers; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:s:sphure]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa will appear; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ā:āśe]]---by that hope; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---does not obtain Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:g:gandha]]-[[synonyms:m:mātra]] [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets only the scent.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, His mind thus stolen by that scent, ran here and there like a bumblebee. He ran to the trees and plants, hoping that Lord Kṛṣṇa would appear, but instead He found only the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.1
description: I offer my respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of my spiritual master and of all the other preceptors on the path of devotional service. I offer my respectful obeisances unto all the Vaiṣṇavas and unto the six Gosvāmīs, including Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, Jīva Gosvāmī and their associates. I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrī Advaita Ācārya Prabhu, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and all His devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura. I then offer my respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and all the gopīs, headed by Lalitā and Viśākhā.
text:
> vande 'haṁ śrī-guroḥ śrī-yuta-pada-kamalaṁ śrī-gurūn vaiṣṇavāṁś ca
> śrī-rūpaṁ sāgrajātaṁ saha-gaṇa-raghunāthānvitaṁ taṁ sa-jīvam
> sādvaitaṁ sāvadhūtaṁ parijana-sahitaṁ kṛṣṇa-caitanya-devaṁ
> śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-pādān saha-gaṇa-lalitā-śrī-viśākhānvitāṁś ca
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vande]]---offer my respectful obeisances; [[synonyms:a:aham]]---I; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:g:guroḥ]]---of my initiating spiritual master or instructing spiritual master; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:y:yuta]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:k:kamalam]]---unto the opulent lotus feet; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:g:gurūn]]---unto the spiritual masters in the //paramparā// system, beginning from Mādhavendra Purī down to Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavān]]---unto all the Vaiṣṇavas, beginning from Lord Brahmā and others coming from the very start of the creation; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---and; [[synonyms:ś:śri]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpam]]---unto Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:a:agra]]-[[synonyms:j:jātam]]---with his elder brother, Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:saha]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]-[[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]-[[synonyms:a:anvitam]]---with Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī and his associates; [[synonyms:t:tam]]---unto him; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:j:jīvam]]---with Jīva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:a:advaitam]]---with Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:a:avadhūtam]]---with Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:p:parijana]]-[[synonyms:s:sahitam]]---and with Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura and all the other devotees; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:d:devam]]---unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pādān]]---unto the lotus feet of the all-opulent Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:s:saha]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---with associates; [[synonyms:l:lalitā]]-[[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:v:viśākhā]]-[[synonyms:a:anvitān]]---accompanied by Lalitā and Śrī Viśākhā; [[synonyms:c:ca]]---also.
translation: I offer my respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of my spiritual master and of all the other preceptors on the path of devotional service. I offer my respectful obeisances unto all the Vaiṣṇavas and unto the six Gosvāmīs, including Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, Jīva Gosvāmī and their associates. I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrī Advaita Ācārya Prabhu, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and all His devotees, headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura. I then offer my respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and all the gopīs, headed by Lalitā and Viśākhā.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.10
description: People from all over the universe, including the seven islands, the nine khaṇḍas, the planets of the demigods, Gandharvaloka and Kinnaraloka, would go there in the forms of human beings.
text:
> sapta-dvīpera loka āra nava-khaṇḍa-vāsī
> deva, gandharva, kinnara manuṣya-veśe āsi'
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sapta]]-[[synonyms:d:dvīpera]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people from all of the seven islands within the universe; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:n:nava]]-[[synonyms:k:khaṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:v:vāsī]]---the in habitants of the nine //khaṇḍas//; [[synonyms:d:deva]]---demigods; [[synonyms:g:gandharva]]---the inhabitants of Gandharvaloka; [[synonyms:k:kinnara]]---the inhabitants of Kinnaraloka; [[synonyms:m:manuṣya]]-[[synonyms:v:veśe]]---in the form of human beings; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming.
translation: People from all over the universe, including the seven islands, the nine khaṇḍas, the planets of the demigods, Gandharvaloka and Kinnaraloka, would go there in the forms of human beings.
purport:
For an explanation of //sapta-dvīpa,// see //Madhya-līlā,// Chapter Twenty, verse 218, and //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// Fifth Canto, Chapters Sixteen and Twenty. in the //Siddhānta-śiromaṇi,// Chapter One (//Golādhyāya//), in the //Bhuvana-kośa// section, the nine //khaṇḍas// are mentioned as follows:

> aindraṁ kaśeru sakalaṁ kila tāmraparṇam
> anyad gabhastimad ataś ca kumārikākhyam
> nāgaṁ ca saumyam iha vāruṇam antya-khaṇḍaṁ
> gāndharva-saṁjñam iti bhārata-varṣa-madhye

"Within Bhārata-varṣa, there are nine //khaṇḍas.// They are known as (1) Aindra, (2) Kaśeru, (3) Tāmraparṇa, (4) Gabhastimat, (5) Kumārikā, (6) Nāga (7) Saumya, (8) Vāruṇa and (9) Gāndharva."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.100
description: Thus Bhagavān Ācārya, greatly ashamed and fearful, remained silent. The next day, he asked Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya to return to his own district.
text:
> lajjā-bhaya pāñā ācārya mauna ha-ilā
> āra dina gopālere deśe pāṭhāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lajjā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear and shame; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Bhagavān Ācārya; [[synonyms:m:mauna]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became silent; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---the next day; [[synonyms:g:gopālere]]---Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:d:deśe]]---to his own country; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāilā]]---sent.
translation: Thus Bhagavān Ācārya, greatly ashamed and fearful, remained silent. The next day, he asked Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya to return to his own district.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.101
description: One day Bhagavān Ācārya invited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to dine at his home. Thus he was preparing rice and various types of vegetables.
text:
> eka-dina ācārya prabhure kailā nimantraṇa
> ghare bhāta kari' kare vividha vyañjana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Bhagavān Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---made an invitation for dinner; [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at home; [[synonyms:b:bhāta]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---cooking rice; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---prepares; [[synonyms:v:vividha]] [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---varieties of vegetable preparations.
translation: One day Bhagavān Ācārya invited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to dine at his home. Thus he was preparing rice and various types of vegetables.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.102
description: A devotee named Choṭa Haridāsa used to sing for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Bhagavān Ācārya called him to his home and spoke as follows.
text:
> 'choṭa-haridāsa' nāma prabhura kīrtanīyā
> tāhāre kahena ācārya ḍākiyā āniyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:choṭa]]-[[synonyms:h:haridāsa]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---a devotee named Choṭa Haridāsa; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:k:kīrtanīyā]]---a chanter of songs for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāhāre]]---unto him; [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---says; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---the //ācārya//; [[synonyms:ḍ:ḍākiyā]] [[synonyms:ā:āniyā]]---calling him to his place.
translation: A devotee named Choṭa Haridāsa used to sing for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Bhagavān Ācārya called him to his home and spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.103
description: "Please go to the sister of Śikhi Māhiti. In my name, ask her for a māna of white rice and bring it here."
text:
> 'mora nāme śikhi-māhitira bhaginī-sthāne giyā
> śukla-cāula eka māna ānaha māgiyā'
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:n:nāme]]---in my name; [[synonyms:ś:śikhi]]-[[synonyms:m:māhitira]]---of Śikhi Māhiti; [[synonyms:b:bhaginī]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---at the place of the sister; [[synonyms:g:giyā]]---going; [[synonyms:ś:śukla]]-[[synonyms:c:cāula]]---white rice; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:m:māna]]---the measurement of one //māna//; [[synonyms:ā:ānaha]]---please bring; [[synonyms:m:māgiyā]]---requesting.
translation: "Please go to the sister of Śikhi Māhiti. In my name, ask her for a māna of white rice and bring it here."
purport: In India //śukla-cāula// (white rice) is also called //ātapa-cāula,// or rice that has not been boiled before being threshed. Another kind of rice, called //siddha-cāula// (brown rice), is boiled before being threshed. Generally, first-class fine white rice is required for offerings to the Deity. Thus Bhagavān Ācārya asked Choṭa Haridāsa, or Junior Haridāsa, a singer in the assembly of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, to get some of this rice from the sister of Śikhi Māhiti. A //māna// is a standard of measurement in Orissa for rice and other food grains.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.104
description: Śikhi Māhiti's sister was named Mādhavīdevī. She was an elderly lady who always performed austerities. She was very advanced in devotional service.
text:
> māhitira bhaginī sei, nāma---mādhavī-devī
> vṛddhā tapasvinī āra paramā vaiṣṇavī
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māhitira]] [[synonyms:b:bhaginī]]---sister of Śikhi Māhiti; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:m:mādhavī]]-[[synonyms:d:devī]]---of the name Mādhavīdevī; [[synonyms:v:vṛddhā]]---an elderly lady; [[synonyms:t:tapasvinī]]---very strict in executing devotional service; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:paramā]] [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavī]]---a first-class devotee.
translation: Śikhi Māhiti's sister was named Mādhavīdevī. She was an elderly lady who always performed austerities. She was very advanced in devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.105
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted her as having formerly been an associate of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. In the entire world, three and a half people were His intimate devotees.
text:
> prabhu lekhā kare yāre---rādhikāra 'gaṇa'
> jagatera madhye 'pātra'---sāḍe tina jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:lekhā]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---accepts; [[synonyms:y:yāre]]---whom; [[synonyms:r:rādhikāra]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---as one of the associates of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:j:jagatera]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---throughout the whole world; [[synonyms:p:pātra]]---most confidential devotees; [[synonyms:s:sāḍe]] [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three and a half; [[synonyms:j:jana]]---persons.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted her as having formerly been an associate of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. In the entire world, three and a half people were His intimate devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.106
description: The three were Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Rāmānanda Rāya and Śikhi Māhiti, and the half a person was Śikhi Māhiti's sister.
text:
> svarūpa gosāñi, āra rāya rāmānanda
> śikhi-māhiti---tina, tāṅra bhaginī---ardha-jana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]] [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---of the name Svarūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:r:rāya]] [[synonyms:r:rāmānanda]]---Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:ś:śikhi]]-[[synonyms:m:māhiti]]---Śikhi Māhiti; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:b:bhaginī]]---his sister; [[synonyms:a:ardha]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---half a person.
translation: The three were Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Rāmānanda Rāya and Śikhi Māhiti, and the half a person was Śikhi Māhiti's sister.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.107
description: After begging the rice from her, Junior Haridāsa brought it to Bhagavān Ācārya, who was very pleased to see its quality.
text:
> tāṅra ṭhāñi taṇḍula māgi' ānila haridāsa
> taṇḍula dekhi' ācāryera adhika ullāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---from her; [[synonyms:t:taṇḍula]] [[synonyms:m:māgi']]---begging rice; [[synonyms:ā:ānila]] [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa brought; [[synonyms:t:taṇḍula]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing the rice; [[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]]---of Bhagavān Ācārya; [[synonyms:a:adhika]] [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---very great satisfaction.
translation: After begging the rice from her, Junior Haridāsa brought it to Bhagavān Ācārya, who was very pleased to see its quality.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.108
description: In great affection, Bhagavān Ācārya cooked varieties of vegetables and other preparations dear to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He also obtained remnants of food from Lord Jagannātha and digestive aids such as ground ginger and also lime with salt.
text:
> snehe rāndhila prabhura priya ye vyañjana
> deula prasāda, ādā-cāki, lembu-salavaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:snehe]]---in great affection; [[synonyms:r:rāndhila]]---cooked; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:priya]]---dear; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---vegetables; [[synonyms:d:deula]] [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]---remnants from the temple of Jagannātha; [[synonyms:ā:ādā]]-[[synonyms:c:cāki]]---ground ginger; [[synonyms:l:lembu]]---lime; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:l:lavaṇa]]---with salt.
translation: In great affection, Bhagavān Ācārya cooked varieties of vegetables and other preparations dear to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He also obtained remnants of food from Lord Jagannātha and digestive aids such as ground ginger and also lime with salt.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.109
description: At noon, when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to eat the offerings of Bhagavān Ācārya, He first appreciated the fine rice and therefore questioned him.
text:
> madhyāhne āsiyā prabhu bhojane vasilā
> śālyanna dekhi' prabhu ācārye puchilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhyāhne]]---at noon; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhojane]] [[synonyms:v:vasilā]]---sat down to eat; [[synonyms:ś:śāli]]-[[synonyms:a:anna]]---the rice of fine quality; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:ācārye]] [[synonyms:p:puchilā]]---inquired from Bhagavān Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.11
description: Having seen the Lord, they all became Vaiṣṇavas. Thus they danced and chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra in ecstatic love of Godhead.

translation: Having seen the Lord, they all became Vaiṣṇavas. Thus they danced and chanted the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra in ecstatic love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.110

translation: "Where did you get such fine rice?" the Lord asked. Bhagavān Ācārya replied, "I got it by begging from Mādhavīdevī."

translation: " From this day forward, do not allow Choṭa Haridāsa to come here."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.114

translation: When Junior Haridāsa heard that he had been ordered not to approach Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he was very unhappy. No one could understand why he had been ordered not to come.

> tina-dina haila haridāsa kare upavāsa

translation: Haridāsa fasted continuously for three days. Then Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and other confidential devotees approached Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to inquire from Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.116

> "kon aparādha, prabhu, kaila haridāsa?

translation: "What great offense has Junior Haridāsa committed? Why has he been forbidden to come to Your door? He has now been fasting for three days."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.117
description: The Lord replied, "I cannot tolerate seeing the face of a person who has accepted the renounced order of life but who still talks intimately with a woman.
text:
> prabhu kahe,---"vairāgī kare prakṛti sambhāṣaṇa
> dekhite nā pāroṅ āmi tāhāra vadana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied; [[synonyms:v:vairāgī]]---a person in the renounced order of life; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]] [[synonyms:s:sambhāṣaṇa]]---intimate talking with a woman; [[synonyms:d:dekhite]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāroṅ]]---cannot see; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]] [[synonyms:v:vadana]]---his face.
translation: The Lord replied, "I cannot tolerate seeing the face of a person who has accepted the renounced order of life but who still talks intimately with a woman.
purport: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that //saralatā,// or simplicity, is the first qualification of a Vaiṣṇava, whereas duplicity or cunning behavior is a great offense against the principles of devotional service. As one advances in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, one must gradually become disgusted with material attachment and thus become more and more attached to the service of the Lord. If one is not factually detached from material activities but still proclaims himself advanced in devotional service, he is cheating. No one will be happy to see such behavior.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.118
description: "So strongly do the senses adhere to the objects of their enjoyment that indeed a wooden statue of a woman attracts the mind of even a great saintly person.
text:
> durvāra indriya kare viṣaya-grahaṇa
> dāravī prakṛti hare munerapi mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:durvāra]]---uncontrollable; [[synonyms:i:indriya]]---the senses; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---do; [[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]-[[synonyms:g:grahaṇa]]---accepting sense objects; [[synonyms:d:dāravī]] [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]]---a wooden statue of a woman; [[synonyms:h:hare]]---attracts; [[synonyms:m:munerapi]]---even of a great sage; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind.
translation: "So strongly do the senses adhere to the objects of their enjoyment that indeed a wooden statue of a woman attracts the mind of even a great saintly person.
purport: The senses and the sense objects are so intimately connected that the mind of even a great saintly person is attracted to a wooden doll if it is attractively shaped like a young woman. The sense objects, namely form, sound, smell, taste and touch, are always attractive for the eyes, ears, nose, tongue and skin. Since the senses and sense objects are naturally intimately related, sometimes even a person claiming control over his senses remains always subject to the control of sense objects. The senses are impossible to control unless purified and engaged in the service of the Lord. Thus even though a saintly person vows to control his senses, the senses are still sometimes perturbed by sense objects.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.119
description: " 'One should not sit closely with one's mother, sister or daughter, for the senses are so strong that they may attract even a person advanced in knowledge.'
text:
> mātrā svasrā duhitrā vā
> nā viviktāsano bhavet
> balavān indriya-grāmo
> vidvāṁsam api karṣati
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mātrā]]---with one's mother; [[synonyms:s:svasrā]]---with one's sister; [[synonyms:d:duhitrā]]---with one's daughter; [[synonyms:v:vā]]---or; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:v:vivikta]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsanaḥ]]---sitting together; [[synonyms:b:bhavet]]---there should be; [[synonyms:b:balavān]]---very strong; [[synonyms:i:indriya]]-[[synonyms:g:grāmaḥ]]---the group of senses; [[synonyms:v:vidvāṁsam]]---a person with knowledge of liberation; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:k:karṣati]]---attract.
translation: “ 'One should not sit closely with one's mother, sister or daughter, for the senses are so strong that they may attract even a person advanced in knowledge.'
purport: This verse appears in the //Manu-saṁhitā// (2.215) and //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:9:19:17|(9.19.17)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.12
description: Thus by direct meetings, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered the three worlds. Some people, however, could not go and were entangled in material activities.
text:
> ei-mata darśane trijagat nistāri
> ye keha āsite nāre aneka saṁsārī
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:d:darśane]]---by direct visits; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the three worlds; [[synonyms:n:nistāri]]---delivering; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:k:keha]]---some who; [[synonyms:ā:āsite]] [[synonyms:n:nāre]]---could not come; [[synonyms:a:aneka]]---many; [[synonyms:s:saṁsārī]]---persons entangled in this material world.
translation: Thus by direct meetings, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered the three worlds. Some people, however, could not go and were entangled in material activities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.120
description: "There are many persons with little in their possession who accept the renounced order of life like monkeys. They go here and there engaging in sense gratification and speaking intimately with women."
text:
> kṣudra-jīva saba markaṭa-vairāgya kariyā
> indriya carāñā bule 'prakṛti' sambhāṣiyā"
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṣudra]]-[[synonyms:j:jīva]]---poor living entities; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:m:markaṭa]] [[synonyms:v:vairāgya]]---a renounced life like that of a monkey; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---accepting; [[synonyms:i:indriya]] [[synonyms:c:carāñā]]---satisfying the senses; [[synonyms:b:bule]]---wander here and there; [[synonyms:p:prakṛti]] [[synonyms:s:sambhāṣiyā]]---talking intimately with women.
translation: "There are many persons with little in their possession who accept the renounced order of life like monkeys. They go here and there engaging in sense gratification and speaking intimately with women."
purport: One should strictly follow the regulative principles, namely no illicit sex, no meat-eating, no intoxication and no gambling, and in this way one should make progress in spiritual life. If an unfit person sentimentally accepts //vairāgya// or takes //sannyāsa// but at the same time remains attached to women, he is in a very dangerous position. His renunciation is called //markaṭa-vairāgya,// or renunciation like that of a monkey. The monkey lives in the forest, eats fruit and does not even cover itself with a cloth. In this way it resembles a saint, but the monkey always thinks of female monkeys and sometimes keeps dozens of them for sexual intercourse. This is called //markaṭa-vairāgya.// Therefore one who is unfit should not accept the renounced order of life. One who accepts the order of //sannyāsa// but again becomes agitated by sensual disturbances and talks privately with women is called //dharma-dhvajī// or //dharma-kalaṅka,// which means that he brings condemnation upon the religious order. Therefore one should be extremely careful in this connection. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura explains the word //markaṭa// to mean "restless." A restless person cannot be steady; therefore he simply wanders about, gratifying his senses. Just to get praise from others, to get cheap adoration from his followers or people in general, such a person sometimes accepts the dress of a //sannyāsī// or //bābājī// in the renounced order, but he cannot give up desires for sense gratification, especially for the association of women. Such a person cannot make advancement in spiritual life. There are eight different kinds of sensual enjoyment with women, including talking about them and thinking about them. Thus for a //sannyāsī,// a person in the renounced order, talking intimately with women is a great offense. Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya and Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura actually achieved the most elevated stage of the renounced order, but those who imitate them, accepting them as ordinary human beings, fall under the influence of the material energy, for that is a great misunderstanding.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.121
description: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered His room. Seeing Him in such an angry mood, all the devotees fell silent.

translation: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered His room. Seeing Him in such an angry mood, all the devotees fell silent.

> "alpa aparādha, prabhu karaha prasāda

translation: "Haridāsa has committed a small offense," they said. "Therefore, O Lord, please be merciful to him. Now he has received a sufficient lesson. In the future he will not commit such a offense."

> prabhu kahe,---"mora vaśa nahe mora mana
> prakṛti-sambhāṣī vairāgī nā kare darśana

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.125
description: "You should all tend to your respective engagements. Give up this useless talk. If you speak this way again, I shall go away, and you will no longer see Me here."
text:
> nija kārye yāha sabe, chāḍa vṛthā kathā
> punaḥ yadi kaha āmā nā dekhibe hethā"

translation: "You should all tend to your respective engagements. Give up this useless talk. If you speak this way again, I shall go away, and you will no longer see Me here."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.126

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.127
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also left that place to perform His noon duties. No one could understand His pastimes.
text:
> mahāprabhu madhyāhna karite cali, gelā
> bujhana nā yāya ei mahāprabhura līlā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:madhyāhna]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to execute His noon activities; [[synonyms:c:cali]]---walking; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---left; [[synonyms:b:bujhana]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---no one could understand; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhura]] [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastime of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also left that place to perform His noon duties. No one could understand His pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.128
description: The next day, all the devotees went to Śrī Paramānanda Purī and requested him to pacify the Lord.
text:
> āra dina sabe paramānanda-purī-sthāne
> 'prabhuke prasanna kara'---kailā nivedane
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---the next day; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:p:paramānanda]]-[[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---at the place of Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:p:prabhuke]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:prasanna]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---please try to pacify; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:n:nivedane]]---submitted.
translation: The next day, all the devotees went to Śrī Paramānanda Purī and requested him to pacify the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.129
description: Paramānanda Purī thereupon went alone to the residence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The Lord, after offering him obeisances, seated him by His side with great respect.
text:
> tabe purī-gosāñi ekā prabhu-sthāne āilā
> namaskari' prabhu tāṅre sambhrame vasāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereupon; [[synonyms:p:purī]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Paramānanda Purī; [[synonyms:e:ekā]]---alone; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the place of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:n:namaskari']]---after offering obeisances; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:s:sambhrame]]---with great respect; [[synonyms:v:vasāilā]]---got to sit down.
translation: Paramānanda Purī thereupon went alone to the residence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The Lord, after offering him obeisances, seated him by His side with great respect.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.13
description: To deliver people in regions throughout the universe who could not meet Him, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally entered the bodies of pure devotees.
text:
> tā-sabā tārite prabhu sei saba deśe
> yogya-bhakta jīva-dehe karena 'āveśe'
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabā]]---all of them; [[synonyms:t:tārite]]---to deliver; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---those; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in countries; [[synonyms:y:yogya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---a suitable devotee; [[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:d:dehe]]---in the body of such a living entity; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---entrance.
translation: To deliver people in regions throughout the universe who could not meet Him, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally entered the bodies of pure devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.130
description: The Lord inquired, "What is your order? For what purpose have you come here?" Paramānanda Purī then submitted his prayer that the Lord show favor to Junior Haridāsa.
text:
> puchilā,---ki ājñā, kene haila āgamana?
> 'haridāse prasāda lāgi' kailā nivedana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:puchilā]]---the Lord inquired; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---what is your order; [[synonyms:k:kenehaila]] [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---what is the reason you have come; [[synonyms:h:haridāse]] [[synonyms:p:prasāda]] [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for a favor to Junior Haridāsa; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:n:nivedana]]---he made a request.
translation: The Lord inquired, "What is your order? For what purpose have you come here?" Paramānanda Purī then submitted his prayer that the Lord show favor to Junior Haridāsa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.131
description: Hearing this request, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "My dear lord, please hear me. It is better for you to stay here with all the Vaiṣṇavas.
text:
> śuniyā kahena prabhu,---"śunaha, gosāñi

synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:k:kahena]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:ś:śunaha]]---please hear; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---my lord; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---all the Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---your lordship; [[synonyms:r:raha]]---stay; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---in this place.
translation: Hearing this request, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "My dear lord, please hear me. It is better for you to stay here with all the Vaiṣṇavas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.132
description: "Please give Me permission to go to Ālālanātha. I shall remain there alone; only Govinda will go with Me."

translation: "Please give Me permission to go to Ālālanātha. I shall remain there alone; only Govinda will go with Me."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.133

translation: After saying this, the Lord called for Govinda. Offering obeisances to Paramānanda Purī, He got up and began to leave.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.134

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.135

translation: Paramānanda Purī said, "My dear Lord Caitanya, You are the independent Personality of Godhead. You can do whatever You like. Who can say anything above You?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.136

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.137

translation: After saying this, Paramānanda Purī Gosāñi left for his own home. Then all the devotees went to see Junior Haridāsa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.138

> svarūpa-gosāñi kahe,---"śuna, haridāsa

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.139
description: "At present Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is persisting in His mood of anger because He is the independent Supreme Personality of Godhead. At some time, however, He will surely be merciful, for at heart He is very kind.
text:
> prabhu haṭhe paḍiyāche svatantra īśvara
> kabhu kṛpā karibena yāte dayālu antara
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:haṭhe]] [[synonyms:p:paḍiyāche]]---has taken up a persistently angry mood; [[synonyms:s:svatantra]] [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the independent Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---some time; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:karibena]]---He will be merciful (to you); [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---because; [[synonyms:d:dayālu]]---merciful; [[synonyms:a:antara]]---at heart.
translation: "At present Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is persisting in His mood of anger because He is the independent Supreme Personality of Godhead. At some time, however, He will surely be merciful, for at heart He is very kind.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.14
description: Thus He empowered living beings [His pure devotees] by manifesting in them so much of His own devotion that people in all other countries became devotees by seeing them.
text:
> sei jīve nija-bhakti karena prakāśe
> tāhāra darśane 'vaiṣṇava' haya sarva-deśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:j:jīve]]---in that living being; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---His own devotion; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---manifests directly; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]] [[synonyms:d:darśane]]---by seeing such an empowered devotee; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---devotees of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---become; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---in all other countries.
translation: Thus He empowered living beings [His pure devotees] by manifesting in them so much of His own devotion that people in all other countries became devotees by seeing them.
purport:
As stated in //Caitanya-caritāmṛta// [[books:cc:antya:7:11|(Antya 7.11)]]:

> kali-kālera dharma-kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana
> kṛṣṇa-śakti vinā nahe tāra pravartana

Unless one is empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, one cannot spread the holy names of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// throughout the world. Persons who do so are empowered. Therefore they are sometimes called //āveśa-avatāras// or incarnations, for they are endowed with the power of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.140
description: "The Lord is persisting, and if you also persist, His persistence will increase. It is better for you to bathe and take prasāda. In due course, His anger will automatically subside."
text:
> tumi haṭha kaile tāṅra haṭha se bāḍibe

translation: "The Lord is persisting, and if you also persist, His persistence will increase. It is better for you to bathe and take prasāda. In due course, His anger will automatically subside."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.141
description: Having said this, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī induced Haridāsa to bathe and take prasāda. After thus reassuring him, he returned home.
text:
> eta bali tāre snāna bhojana karāñā
