synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereupon; [[synonyms:ś:śivānanda]]---Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]]-[[synonyms:s:sāmagrī]]---ingredients for preparing food; [[synonyms:ā:ānilā]]---brought; [[synonyms:p:pāka]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---after cooking; [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁhera]]---of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva; [[synonyms:b:bhoga]] [[synonyms:l:lāgāilā]]---offered the food.
translation: Then Śivānanda Sena again brought the ingredients with which to cook, and Pradyumna Brahmacārī again cooked and offered the food to Nṛsiṁhadeva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.75
description: The next year, Śivānanda went to Jagannātha Purī with all the other devotees to see the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> varṣāntare śivānanda lañā bhakta-gaṇa
> nīlācale dekhe yāñā prabhura caraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:varṣa]]-[[synonyms:a:antare]]---the next year; [[synonyms:ś:śivānanda]]---Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:n:nīlācale]]---at Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:d:dekhe]]---sees; [[synonyms:y:yāñā]]---going; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of the Lord.
translation: The next year, Śivānanda went to Jagannātha Purī with all the other devotees to see the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.76
description: One day, in the presence of all the devotees, the Lord raised these topics concerning Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī and praised his transcendental qualities.
text:
> eka-dina sabhāte prabhu vāta cālāilā
> nṛsiṁhānandera guṇa kahite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:s:sabhāte]]---in the presence of all the devotees; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vāta]] [[synonyms:c:cālāilā]]---raised the topic (of eating at Nṛsiṁhānanda's house); [[synonyms:n:nṛsiṁhānandera]]---of Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---transcendental qualities; [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to speak.
translation: One day, in the presence of all the devotees, the Lord raised these topics concerning Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī and praised his transcendental qualities.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.77
description: The Lord said, "Last year in the month of Pauṣa, when Nṛsiṁhānanda gave me varieties of sweetmeats and vegetables to eat, they were so good that I had never before eaten such preparations."
text:
> 'gata-varṣa pauṣe more karāila bhojana
> kabhu nāhi khāi aiche miṣṭānna-vyañjana'
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gata]]-[[synonyms:v:varṣa]]---last year; [[synonyms:p:pauṣe]]---in the month of Pauṣa (December-January); [[synonyms:m:more]]---unto Me; [[synonyms:k:karāila]] [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---offered many foodstuffs; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:k:khāi]]---I never tasted; [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---such; [[synonyms:m:miṣṭānna]]---sweetmeats; [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---vegetables.
translation: The Lord said, "Last year in the month of Pauṣa, when Nṛsiṁhānanda gave me varieties of sweetmeats and vegetables to eat, they were so good that I had never before eaten such preparations."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.78
description: Hearing this, all the devotees were struck with wonder, and Śivānanda became confident that the incident was true.
text:
> śuni' bhakta-gaṇa mane āścarya mānila
> śivānandera mane tabe pratyaya janmila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the devotees; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:ā:āścarya]] [[synonyms:m:mānila]]---felt wonder; [[synonyms:ś:śivānandera]]---of Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereupon; [[synonyms:p:pratyaya]] [[synonyms:j:janmila]]---there was confidence.
translation: Hearing this, all the devotees were struck with wonder, and Śivānanda became confident that the incident was true.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.79
description: In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to eat at the temple of Śacīmātā every day and also visit the house of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura when kīrtana was performed.
text:
> ei-mata śacī-gṛhe satata bhojana
> śrīvāsera gṛhe karena kīrtana-darśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---in this way; [[synonyms:ś:śacī]]-[[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---at the house of Śacīmātā; [[synonyms:s:satata]]---always; [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---eating; [[synonyms:ś:śrīvāsera]] [[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---in the house of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---performs; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]-[[synonyms:d:darśana]]---visiting the //kīrtana// performances.
translation: In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to eat at the temple of Śacīmātā every day and also visit the house of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura when kīrtana was performed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.8
description: Every year, devotees from Bengal would go to Jagannātha Purī to meet Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and after the meeting they would return to Bengal.
text:
> gauḍa-deśera bhakta-gaṇa pratyabda āsiyā
> punaḥ gauḍa-deśe yāya prabhure miliyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:deśera]]---of Bengal; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---devotees; [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:a:abda]]---every year; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:g:gauḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:deśe]]---to Bengal; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---return; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:miliyā]]---after meeting.
translation: Every year, devotees from Bengal would go to Jagannātha Purī to meet Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and after the meeting they would return to Bengal.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.80
description: Similarly, He was always present when Nityānanda Prabhu danced, and He regularly appeared at the house of Rāghava.
text:
> nityānandera nṛtya dekhena āsi' bāre bāre
> 'nirantara āvirbhāva' rāghavera ghare
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānandera]] [[synonyms:n:nṛtya]]---the dancing of Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhena]]---He sees; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:b:bāre]] [[synonyms:b:bāre]]---again and again; [[synonyms:n:nirantara]] [[synonyms:ā:āvirbhāva]]---constant appearance; [[synonyms:r:rāghavera]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in the house of Rāghava.
translation: Similarly, He was always present when Nityānanda Prabhu danced, and He regularly appeared at the house of Rāghava.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.81
description: Lord Gaurasundara is greatly influenced by the love of His devotees. Therefore wherever there is pure devotion to the Lord, the Lord Himself, subdued by such love, appears, and His devotees see Him.
text:
> prema-vaśa gaura-prabhu, yāhāṅ premottama
> prema-vasa hañā tāhā dena daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---subdued by loving service; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Gaurasundara; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:u:uttama]]---wherever there is pure love; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:v:vaśa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being subdued by such love; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---there; [[synonyms:d:dena]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---appears personally.
translation: Lord Gaurasundara is greatly influenced by the love of His devotees. Therefore wherever there is pure devotion to the Lord, the Lord Himself, subdued by such love, appears, and His devotees see Him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.82
description: Influenced by the loving affairs of Śivānanda Sena, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came again and again. Therefore who can estimate the limits of his love?
text:
> śivānandera prema-sīmā ke kahite pāre?
> yāṅra preme vaśa prabhu āise bāre bāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śivānandera]]---of Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:s:sīmā]]---the limit of love; [[synonyms:k:ke]]---who; [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---can estimate; [[synonyms:y:yāṅra]]---whose; [[synonyms:p:preme]]---by loving affairs; [[synonyms:v:vaśa]]---influenced; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---comes; [[synonyms:b:bāre]] [[synonyms:b:bāre]]---again and again.
translation: Influenced by the loving affairs of Śivānanda Sena, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came again and again. Therefore who can estimate the limits of his love?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.83
description: Thus I have described the appearance of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Anyone who hears about these incidents can understand the transcendental opulence of the Lord.
text:
> ei ta' kahilu gaurera 'āvirbhāva'
> ihā yei śune, jāne caitanya-prabhāva
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:ta']]---thus; [[synonyms:k:kahilu]]---I have described; [[synonyms:g:gaurera]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āvirbhāva]]---appearance; [[synonyms:i:ihā]]---this incident; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---whoever hears; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---knows; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:p:prabhāva]]---the opulence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Thus I have described the appearance of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Anyone who hears about these incidents can understand the transcendental opulence of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.84
description: At Jagannātha Purī, in the association of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, lived Bhagavān Ācārya, who was certainly a gentleman, a learned scholar and a great devotee.
text:
> puruṣottame prabhu-pāśe bhagavān ācārya
> parama vaiṣṇava teṅho supaṇḍita ārya
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:puruṣottame]]---at Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pāśe]]---in the association of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]] [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Bhagavān Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---pure devotee; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---very learned scholar; [[synonyms:ā:ārya]]---gentleman.
translation: At Jagannātha Purī, in the association of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, lived Bhagavān Ācārya, who was certainly a gentleman, a learned scholar and a great devotee.
purport: For a description of Bhagavān Ācārya, one may refer to the //Ādi-līlā,// Tenth Chapter, verse 136.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.85
description: He was fully absorbed in thoughts of fraternal relationships with God. He was an incarnation of a cowherd boy, and thus his dealings with Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī were very friendly.
text:
> sakhya-bhāvākrānta-citta, gopa-avatāra
> svarūpa-gosāñi-saha sakhya-vyavahāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sakhya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---by fraternal love; [[synonyms:ā:ākrānta]]---overwhelmed; [[synonyms:c:citta]]---heart; [[synonyms:g:gopa]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---an incarnation of one of the cowherd boys; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]-[[synonyms:s:saha]]---with Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:s:sakhya]]-[[synonyms:v:vyavahāra]]---dealings just like those of a friend.
translation: He was fully absorbed in thoughts of fraternal relationships with God. He was an incarnation of a cowherd boy, and thus his dealings with Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī were very friendly.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.86
description: He sought the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with full surrender. Sometimes he would invite the Lord to dine at his home.
text:
> ekānta-bhāve āśriyāchena caitanya-caraṇa
> madhye madhye prabhura teṅho karena nimantraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ekānta]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāve]]---with full attention; [[synonyms:ā:āśriyāchena]]---has taken shelter of; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:m:madhye]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:teṅho]]---he; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:n:nimantraṇa]]---invitation.
translation: He sought the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with full surrender. Sometimes he would invite the Lord to dine at his home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.87
description: Bhagavān Ācārya prepared varieties of rice and vegetables at home and brought the Lord there alone to eat.
text:
> ghare bhāta kari' karena vividha vyañjana
> ekale gosāñi lañā karāna bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at home; [[synonyms:b:bhāta]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---preparing rice; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---prepares; [[synonyms:v:vividha]] [[synonyms:v:vyañjana]]---varieties of vegetables; [[synonyms:e:ekale]]---alone; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:karāna]] [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---makes to eat.
translation: Bhagavān Ācārya prepared varieties of rice and vegetables at home and brought the Lord there alone to eat.
purport: Generally those who invited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for dinner used to offer Him the remnants of food that had first been offered to Lord Jagannātha. Bhagavān Ācārya, however, instead of giving Him the remnants of Jagannātha's food, prepared dinner at his home. In Orissa, food offered to Lord Jagannātha is called //prasādī,// and that which is not offered to Lord Jagannātha is known as //āmānī// or //ghara-bhāta,// rice prepared at home.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.88
description: Bhagavān Ācārya's father, whose name was Śatānanda Khān, was an expert statesman, whereas Bhagavān Ācārya was not at all interested in the management of the state. Indeed, he was almost in the renounced order of life.
text:
> tāṅra pitā 'viṣayī' baḍa śatānanda-khāṅna
> 'viṣaya-vimukha' ācārya---'vairāgya-pradhāna'
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:p:pitā]]---his father; [[synonyms:v:viṣayī]]---a statesman; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]]---expert; [[synonyms:ś:śatānanda]]-[[synonyms:k:khāṅna]]---named Śatānanda Khān; [[synonyms:v:viṣaya]]-[[synonyms:v:vimukha]]---not interested in state management; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Bhagavān Ācārya; [[synonyms:v:vairāgya]]-[[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---mostly in the renounced order of life.
translation: Bhagavān Ācārya's father, whose name was Śatānanda Khān, was an expert statesman, whereas Bhagavān Ācārya was not at all interested in the management of the state. Indeed, he was almost in the renounced order of life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.89
description: Bhagavān Ācārya's brother, whose name was Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya, had studied Vedānta philosophy at Benares and had then returned to Bhagavān Ācārya's home.
text:
> 'gopāla-bhaṭṭācārya' nāma tāṅra choṭa-bhāi
> kāśīte vedānta paḍi' gelā tāṅra ṭhāñi
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācārya]]---Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:c:choṭa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---younger brother; [[synonyms:k:kāśīte]]---at Benares; [[synonyms:v:vedānta]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---studying Vedānta philosophy; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---to his place.
translation: Bhagavān Ācārya's brother, whose name was Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya, had studied Vedānta philosophy at Benares and had then returned to Bhagavān Ācārya's home.
purport: During those days and also at the present, Vedānta philosophy is understood through the commentary of Śaṅkarācārya, which is known as //Śārīraka-bhāṣya.// Thus it appears that Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya the younger brother of Bhagavān Ācārya, had studied Vedānta according to the way of the //Śārīraka-bhāṣya,// which expounds the Māyāvāda philosophy of the impersonalists.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.9
description: Similarly, people who went to Jagannātha Purī from various provinces of India were fully satisfied after seeing the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> āra nānā-deśera loka āsi' jagannātha
> caitanya-caraṇa dekhi' ha-ila kṛtārtha
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---again; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:d:deśera]]---of different provinces; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---people; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:j:jagannātha]]---to Jagannātha Purī; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:a:artha]]---fully satisfied.
translation: Similarly, people who went to Jagannātha Purī from various provinces of India were fully satisfied after seeing the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.90
description: Bhagavān Ācārya took his brother to meet Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, but the Lord, knowing that Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya was a Māyāvādī philosopher, could not get much happiness from meeting him.
text:
> ācārya tāhāre prabhu-pade milāilā
> antaryāmī prabhu citte sukha nā pāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Bhagavān Ācārya; [[synonyms:t:tāhāre]]---him (his brother); [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:p:pade]] [[synonyms:m:milāilā]]---got to meet Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:antaryāmī]] [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who could study anyone's heart; [[synonyms:c:citte]]---within Himself; [[synonyms:s:sukha]]---happiness; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāilā]]---could not get.
translation: Bhagavān Ācārya took his brother to meet Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, but the Lord, knowing that Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya was a Māyāvādī philosopher, could not get much happiness from meeting him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.91
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu derives no happiness from meeting one who is not a pure devotee of Kṛṣṇa. Thus because Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya was a Māyāvādī scholar, the Lord felt no jubilation in meeting him. Nevertheless, because Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya was related to Bhagavān Ācārya, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu feigned pleasure in seeing him.
text:
> ācārya-sambandhe bāhye kare prītyābhāsa
> kṛṣṇa-bhakti vinā prabhura nā haya ullāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:s:sambandhe]]---because he was related with Bhagavān Ācārya; [[synonyms:b:bāhye]]---externally; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:p:prīti]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāsa]]---appearance of pleasure; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is no; [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---jubilation.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu derives no happiness from meeting one who is not a pure devotee of Kṛṣṇa. Thus because Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya was a Māyāvādī scholar, the Lord felt no jubilation in meeting him. Nevertheless, because Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya was related to Bhagavān Ācārya, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu feigned pleasure in seeing him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.92
description: Bhagavān Ācārya said to Svarūpa Dāmodara, "Gopāla, my younger brother, has returned to my home, having concluded his study of Vedānta philosophy."
text:
> svarūpa gosāñire ācārya kahe āra dine
> 'vedānta paḍiyā gopāla āisāche ekhāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]] [[synonyms:g:gosāñire]]---unto Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Bhagavān Ācārya; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dine]]---the next day; [[synonyms:v:vedānta]] [[synonyms:p:paḍiyā]]---after studying Vedānta; [[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---Gopāla; [[synonyms:ā:āisāche]]---has come back; [[synonyms:e:ekhāne]]---here.
translation: Bhagavān Ācārya said to Svarūpa Dāmodara, "Gopāla, my younger brother, has returned to my home, having concluded his study of Vedānta philosophy."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.93
description: Bhagavān Ācārya requested Svarūpa Dāmodara to hear from Gopāla the commentary upon Vedānta. Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, however, somewhat angry because of love, spoke as follows.
text:
> sabe meli' āisa, śuni 'bhāṣya' ihāra sthāne'
> prema-krodha kari' svarūpa balaya vacane
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:m:meli']]---all together; [[synonyms:ā:āisa]]---come; [[synonyms:ś:śuni]]---let us hear; [[synonyms:b:bhāṣya]]---the commentary; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]] [[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---from him; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:k:krodha]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---in an angry mood of love; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara; [[synonyms:b:balaya]] [[synonyms:v:vacane]]---said these words.
translation: Bhagavān Ācārya requested Svarūpa Dāmodara to hear from Gopāla the commentary upon Vedānta. Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, however, somewhat angry because of love, spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.94
description: "You have lost your intelligence in the association of Gopāla, and therefore you are eager to hear the Māyāvāda philosophy.
text:
> "buddhi bhraṣṭa haila tomāra gopālera saṅge
> māyāvāda śunibāre upajila raṅge
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:buddhi]]---intelligence; [[synonyms:b:bhraṣṭa]]---lost; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---has been; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:g:gopālera]] [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---in the association of Gopāla; [[synonyms:m:māyāvāda]] [[synonyms:ś:śunibāre]]---to hear the commentary of Māyāvāda philosophy; [[synonyms:u:upajila]] [[synonyms:r:raṅge]]---has awakened the propensity.
translation: "You have lost your intelligence in the association of Gopāla, and therefore you are eager to hear the Māyāvāda philosophy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.95
description: "When a Vaiṣṇava listens to the Śārīraka-bhāṣya, the Māyāvāda commentary upon Vedānta-sūtra, he gives up the Kṛṣṇa conscious attitude that the Lord is the master and the living entity is His servant. Instead, he considers himself the Supreme Lord.
text:
> vaiṣṇava hañā yebā śārīraka-bhāṣya śune
> sevya-sevaka-bhāva chāḍi' āpanāre 'īśvara' māne
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being a Vaiṣṇava; [[synonyms:y:yebā]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:ś:śārīraka]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāṣya]]---the Māyāvāda commentary //Śārīraka-bhāṣya//; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---listens to; [[synonyms:s:sevya]]-[[synonyms:s:sevaka]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the Kṛṣṇa conscious attitude that the Lord is the master and the living entity is His servant; [[synonyms:c:chāḍi']]---giving up; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāre]]---himself; [[synonyms:ī:īśvara]]---the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:m:māne]]---considers.
translation: "When a Vaiṣṇava listens to the Śārīraka-bhāṣya, the Māyāvāda commentary upon Vedānta-sūtra, he gives up the Kṛṣṇa conscious attitude that the Lord is the master and the living entity is His servant. Instead, he considers himself the Supreme Lord.
purport:
The philosophers known as //kevalādvaita-vādīs// generally occupy themselves with hearing the //Śārīraka-bhāṣya,// a commentary by Śaṅkarācārya advocating that one impersonally consider oneself the Supreme Lord. Such Māyāvāda philosophical commentaries upon Vedānta are simply imaginary, but there are other commentaries on Vedānta philosophy. The commentary by Śrīla Rāmānujācārya, known as //Śrī-bhāṣya,// establishes the //viśiṣṭādvaita-vāda// philosophy. Similarly, in the Brahma-sampradāya, Madhvācārya's //Pūrṇaprajña-bhāṣya// establishes //śuddha-dvaita-vāda.// In the Kumāra-sampradāya, or Nimbārka-sampradāya, Śrī Nimbārka establishes the philosophy of //dvaitādvaita-vāda// in the //Pārijāta-saurabha-bhāṣya.// And in the Viṣṇusvāmi-sampradāya, or Rudra-sampradāya, which comes from Lord Śiva, Viṣṇusvāmī has written a commentary called //Sarvajña-bhāṣya,// which establishes //śuddhādvaita-vāda.//

A Vaiṣṇava should study the commentaries on //Vedānta-sūtra// written by the four //sampradāya-ācāryas,// namely Śrī Rāmānujācārya, Madhvācārya, Viṣṇusvāmī and Nimbārka, for these commentaries are based upon the philosophy that the Lord is the master and that all living entities are His eternal servants. One interested in studying Vedānta philosophy properly must study these commentaries, especially if he is a Vaiṣṇava. These commentaries are always adored by Vaiṣṇavas. The commentary by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī is elaborately given in the //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Seven, text 101. The Māyāvāda commentary //Śārīraka-bhāṣya// is like poison for a Vaiṣṇava. It should not be touched at all. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura remarks that even a //mahā-bhāgavata,// or highly elevated devotee who has surrendered himself unto the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, sometimes falls down from pure devotional service if he hears the Māyāvāda philosophy of //Śārīraka-bhāṣya.// This commentary should therefore be shunned by all Vaiṣṇavas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.96
description: "The Māyāvāda philosophy presents such a jugglery of words that even a highly elevated devotee who has accepted Kṛṣṇa as his life and soul changes his decision when he reads the Māyāvāda commentary on Vedānta-sūtra."
text:
> mahā-bhāgavata yei, kṛṣṇa prāṇa-dhana yāra
> māyāvāda-śravaṇe citta avaśya phire tāṅra"
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]] [[synonyms:y:yei]]---one who is a highly elevated devotee; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dhana]] [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose life and soul; [[synonyms:m:māyāvāda]]-[[synonyms:ś:śravaṇe]]---by hearing the Māyāvāda philosophy; [[synonyms:c:citta]]---the heart; [[synonyms:a:avaśya]]---certainly; [[synonyms:p:phire]]---changes; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his.
translation: "The Māyāvāda philosophy presents such a jugglery of words that even a highly elevated devotee who has accepted Kṛṣṇa as his life and soul changes his decision when he reads the Māyāvāda commentary on Vedānta-sūtra."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.97
description: In spite of Svarūpa Dāmodara's protest, Bhagavān Ācārya continued, "We are all fixed at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa with our hearts and souls. Therefore the Śārīraka-bhāṣya cannot change our minds."
text:
> ācārya kahe,---'āmā sabāra kṛṣṇa-niṣṭha-citte
> āmā sabāra mana bhāṣya nāre phirāite'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Bhagavān Ācārya replied; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]] [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of us; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:niṣṭha]]---devoted to Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:c:citte]]---hearts; [[synonyms:ā:āmā]] [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of us; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---minds; [[synonyms:b:bhāṣya]]---//Śārīraka-bhāṣya//; [[synonyms:n:nāre]] [[synonyms:p:phirāite]]---cannot change.
translation: In spite of Svarūpa Dāmodara's protest, Bhagavān Ācārya continued, "We are all fixed at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa with our hearts and souls. Therefore the Śārīraka-bhāṣya cannot change our minds."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.98
description: Svarūpa Dāmodara replied, "Nevertheless, when we hear the Māyāvāda philosophy, we hear that Brahman is knowledge and that the universe of māyā is false, but we gain no spiritual understanding.
text:
> svarūpa kahe, "tathāpi māyāvāda-śravaṇe
> 'cit, brahma, māyā, mithyā'---ei-mātra śune
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara replied; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:m:māyāvāda]]-[[synonyms:ś:śravaṇe]]---by hearing the Māyāvāda commentary; [[synonyms:c:cit]]---knowledge; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---the Absolute Truth; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---external energy; [[synonyms:m:mithyā]]---false; [[synonyms:e:ei]]-[[synonyms:m:mātra]]---only these; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hears.
translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara replied, "Nevertheless, when we hear the Māyāvāda philosophy, we hear that Brahman is knowledge and that the universe of māyā is false, but we gain no spiritual understanding.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 2.99
description: "The Māyāvādī philosopher tries to establish that the living entity is only imaginary and that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is under the influence of māyā. Hearing this kind of commentary breaks the heart and life of a devotee."
text:
> jīvājñāna-kalpita īśvare, sakala-i ajñāna
> yāhāra śravaṇe bhaktera phāṭe mana prāṇa"
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---the ordinary living being; [[synonyms:a:ajñāna]]---by ignorance; [[synonyms:k:kalpita]]---imagined; [[synonyms:ī:īśvare]]---in the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]-[[synonyms:i:i]] [[synonyms:a:ajñāna]]---all ignorance; [[synonyms:y:yāhāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇe]]---hearing of which; [[synonyms:b:bhaktera]]---of the devotee; [[synonyms:p:phāṭe]]---breaks; [[synonyms:m:mana]] [[synonyms:p:prāṇa]]---mind and life.
translation: "The Māyāvādī philosopher tries to establish that the living entity is only imaginary and that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is under the influence of māyā. Hearing this kind of commentary breaks the heart and life of a devotee."
purport: Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī wanted to impress upon Bhagavān Ācārya that even though someone firmly fixed in devotion to Kṛṣṇa's service might not be deviated by hearing the Māyāvāda //bhāṣya,// that //bhāṣya// is nevertheless full of impersonal words and ideas such as Brahman which represent knowledge but which are impersonal. The Māyāvādīs say that the world created by //māyā// is false, and that actually there is no living entity but only one spiritual effulgence. They further say that God is imaginary, that people think of God only because of ignorance, and that when the Supreme Absolute Truth is befooled by the external energy, //māyā,// He becomes a //jīva,// or living entity. Upon hearing all these nonsensical ideas from the nondevotee, a devotee is greatly afflicted, as if his heart and soul were broken.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.1
description: Only the most fortunate will relish the mad words of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, which mixed with jubilation, envy, agitation, submissiveness and grief, all produced by ecstatic loving emotions.
text:
> premodbhāvita-harṣerṣyod-
> vega-dainyārti-miśritam
> lapitaṁ gauracandrasya
> bhāgyavadbhir niṣevyate
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:u:udbhāvita]]---produced from ecstatic love and emotion; [[synonyms:h:harṣa]]---jubilation; [[synonyms:ī:īrṣyā]]---envy; [[synonyms:u:udvega]]---agitation; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]---submissiveness; [[synonyms:ā:ārti]]---grief; [[synonyms:m:miśritam]]---mixed with; [[synonyms:l:lapitam]]---talks like those of a crazy man; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:c:candrasya]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhāgyavadbhiḥ]]---by the most fortunate; [[synonyms:n:niṣevyate]]---is enjoyable.
translation: Only the most fortunate will relish the mad words of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, which mixed with jubilation, envy, agitation, submissiveness and grief, all produced by ecstatic loving emotions.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.10
description: " 'In the age of Kali, intelligent persons perform congregational chanting to worship the incarnation of Godhead who constantly sings the name of Kṛṣṇa. Although His complexion is not blackish, He is Kṛṣṇa Himself. He is accompanied by His associates, servants, weapons and confidential companions.'
text:
> kṛṣṇa-varṇaṁ tviṣākṛṣṇaṁ
> sāṅgopāṅgāstra-pārṣadam
> yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair
> yajanti hi sumedhasaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇam]]---repeating the syllables //kṛṣ-ṇa//; [[synonyms:t:tviṣā]]---with a luster; [[synonyms:a:akṛṣṇam]]---not black (golden); [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:a:aṅga]]---with associates; [[synonyms:u:upāṅga]]---servitors; [[synonyms:a:astra]]---weapons; [[synonyms:p:pārṣadam]]---confidential companions; [[synonyms:y:yajñaiḥ]]---by sacrifice; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]-[[synonyms:p:prāyaiḥ]]---consisting chiefly of congregational chanting; [[synonyms:y:yajanti]]---they worship; [[synonyms:h:hi]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:m:medhasaḥ]]---intelligent persons.
translation: “ 'In the age of Kali, intelligent persons perform congregational chanting to worship the incarnation of Godhead who constantly sings the name of Kṛṣṇa. Although His complexion is not blackish, He is Kṛṣṇa Himself. He is accompanied by His associates, servants, weapons and confidential companions.'
purport: This verse is spoken by Saint Karabhājana in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (11.5.32). For further information, see //Ādi-līlā,// Chapter Three, text 52.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.100
description: If I did not disclose this fact, I would be guilty of ingratitude to the Lord. Therefore, my dear readers, please do not consider me too proud and be angry at me.
text:
> nā kahile haya mora kṛta-ghnatā-doṣa
> dambha kari bali' śrotā, nā kariha roṣa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kahile]]---if I do not say; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:k:kṛta]]-[[synonyms:g:ghnatā]]-[[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---fault of ingratitude; [[synonyms:d:dambha]] [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I am proud; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---taking as; [[synonyms:ś:śrotā]]---O readers; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kariha]] [[synonyms:r:roṣa]]---do not be angry.
translation: If I did not disclose this fact, I would be guilty of ingratitude to the Lord. Therefore, my dear readers, please do not consider me too proud and be angry at me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.101
description: It is because I have offered my prayers unto the lotus feet of all of you that whatever I have written about Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has been possible.
text:
> tomā-sabāra caraṇa-dhūli karinu vandana
> tāte caitanya-līlā haila ye kichu likhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of you; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dhūli]]---the dust of the feet; [[synonyms:k:karinu]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---I have prayed to; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---for that reason; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]---the pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:y:ye]]---whatever; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:l:likhana]]---writing.
translation: It is because I have offered my prayers unto the lotus feet of all of you that whatever I have written about Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has been possible.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.102
description: Now let me repeat all the pastimes of the Antya-līlā, for if I do so I shall taste the pastimes again.
text:
> ebe antya-līlā-gaṇera kari anuvāda
> 'anuvāda' kaile pāi līlāra 'āsvāda'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:a:antya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]] [[synonyms:k:kari]] [[synonyms:a:anuvāda]]---I beg to repeat all the facts of this //Antya-līlā//; [[synonyms:a:anuvāda]] [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---if it is repeated; [[synonyms:p:pāi]]---I get; [[synonyms:l:līlāra]]---of the pastime; [[synonyms:ā:āsvāda]]---taste.
translation: Now let me repeat all the pastimes of the Antya-līlā, for if I do so I shall taste the pastimes again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.103
description: The First Chapter describes how Rūpa Gosvāmī met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for the second time and how the Lord heard his two dramas [Vidagdha-mādhava and Lalita-mādhava].
text:
> prathama paricchede---rūpera dvitīya-milana
> tāra madhye dui-nāṭakera vidhāna-śravaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prathama]] [[synonyms:p:paricchede]]---in the First Chapter; [[synonyms:r:rūpera]]---of Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]]-[[synonyms:m:milana]]---the second meeting with Lord Caitanya; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that chapter; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:n:nāṭakera]]---of the two dramas; [[synonyms:v:vidhāna]]-[[synonyms:ś:śravaṇa]]---hearing of the process of writing.
translation: The First Chapter describes how Rūpa Gosvāmī met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for the second time and how the Lord heard his two dramas [Vidagdha-mādhava and Lalita-mādhava].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.104
description: That chapter also describes the incident of Śivānanda Sena's dog, who was induced by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and was thus liberated.
text:
> tāra madhye śivānanda-saṅge kukkura āilā
> prabhu tāre kṛṣṇa kahāñā mukta karilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in that chapter; [[synonyms:ś:śivānanda]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---with Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:k:kukkura]]---the dog; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---unto him (the dog); [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kahāñā]]---inducing to chant Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mukta]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---liberated.
translation: That chapter also describes the incident of Śivānanda Sena's dog, who was induced by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and was thus liberated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.105
description: In the Second Chapter the Lord instructively punished Junior Haridāsa. Also in that chapter is the wonderful vision of Śivānanda Sena.
text:
> dvitīye---choṭa-haridāse karāilā śikṣana
> tāra madhye śivānandera āścarya darśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dvitīye]]---in the Second Chapter; [[synonyms:c:choṭa]]-[[synonyms:h:haridāse]]---Junior Haridāsa; [[synonyms:k:karāilā]] [[synonyms:ś:śikṣaṇa]]---He taught very strictly; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that chapter; [[synonyms:ś:śivānandera]]---of Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:ā:āścarya]] [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---the wonderful vision.
translation: In the Second Chapter the Lord instructively punished Junior Haridāsa. Also in that chapter is the wonderful vision of Śivānanda Sena.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.106
description: In the Third Chapter is a description of the forceful glories of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. That chapter also mentions how Dāmodara Paṇḍita spoke words of criticism to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> tṛtīye---haridāsera mahimā pracaṇḍa
> dāmodara-paṇḍita kailā prabhure vākya-danda
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tṛtīye]]---in the Third Chapter; [[synonyms:h:haridāsera]]---of Ṭhākura Haridāsa; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]] [[synonyms:p:pracaṇḍa]]---very forceful glories; [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]-[[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---Dāmodara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---made; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:vākya]]-[[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]]---impudence of chastising by words.
translation: In the Third Chapter is a description of the forceful glories of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. That chapter also mentions how Dāmodara Paṇḍita spoke words of criticism to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.107
description: The Third Chapter also tells how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered everyone by bestowing upon the universe the holy name of the Lord, and it describes how Haridāsa Ṭhākura established the glories of the holy name by his practical example.
text:
> prabhu 'nāma' diyā kailā brahmāṇḍa-mocana
> haridāsa karilā nāmera mahimā-sthāpana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---delivering the holy name; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:b:brahmāṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:m:mocana]]---the liberation of the universe; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:n:nāmera]]---of the holy name; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāpana]]---the establishment of the glories.
translation: The Third Chapter also tells how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered everyone by bestowing upon the universe the holy name of the Lord, and it describes how Haridāsa Ṭhākura established the glories of the holy name by his practical example.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.108
description: The Fourth Chapter describes Sanātana Gosvāmī's second visit with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and how the Lord saved him from committing suicide.
text:
> caturthe---śrī-sanātanera dvitīya-milana
> deha-tyāga haite tāṅra karilā rakṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caturthe]]---in the Fourth Chapter; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:s:sanātanera]]---of Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:d:dvitīya]]-[[synonyms:m:milana]]---visiting for the second time; [[synonyms:d:deha]]-[[synonyms:t:tyāga]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from committing suicide; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:r:rakṣaṇa]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu protected him.
translation: The Fourth Chapter describes Sanātana Gosvāmī's second visit with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and how the Lord saved him from committing suicide.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.109
description: The Fourth Chapter also tells how Sanātana Gosvāmī was tested in the sunshine of Jyaiṣṭha [May and June] and was then empowered and sent back to Vṛndāvana.
text:
> jyaiṣṭha-māsera dhūpe tāṅre kailā parīkṣaṇa
> śakti sañcāriyā punaḥ pāṭhāilā vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jyaiṣṭha]]-[[synonyms:m:māsera]]---of the month of May-June; [[synonyms:d:dhūpe]]---in the sunshine; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---him; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:p:parīkṣaṇa]]---examining; [[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---potency; [[synonyms:s:sañcāriyā]]---giving him; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāilā]] [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---sent back to Vṛndāvana.
translation: The Fourth Chapter also tells how Sanātana Gosvāmī was tested in the sunshine of Jyaiṣṭha [May and June] and was then empowered and sent back to Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.11
description: "Simply by chanting the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa, one can be freed from all undesirable habits. This is the means of awakening all good fortune and initiating the flow of waves of love for Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> nāma-saṅkīrtana haite sarvānartha-nāśa
> sarva-śubhodaya, kṛṣṇa-premera ullāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the holy names of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:a:anartha]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---destruction of all undesirable things; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śubha]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]]---awakening of all good fortune; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:premera]] [[synonyms:u:ullāsa]]---the beginning of the flow of love of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Simply by chanting the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa, one can be freed from all undesirable habits. This is the means of awakening all good fortune and initiating the flow of waves of love for Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.110
description: In the Fifth Chapter, the Lord showed His favor to Pradyumna Miśra and made him hear topics of Kṛṣṇa from Rāmānanda Rāya.
text:
> pañcame---pradyumna-miśre prabhu kṛpā karilā
> rāya-dvārā kṛṣṇa-kathā tāṅre śunāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pañcame]]---in the Fifth Chapter; [[synonyms:p:pradyumna]]-[[synonyms:m:miśre]]---unto Pradyumna Miśra; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---showed mercy; [[synonyms:r:rāya]]-[[synonyms:d:dvārā]]---with the help of Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kathā]]---topics of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]] [[synonyms:ś:śunāilā]]---made him hear.
translation: In the Fifth Chapter, the Lord showed His favor to Pradyumna Miśra and made him hear topics of Kṛṣṇa from Rāmānanda Rāya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.111
description: Also in that chapter, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī rejected the drama of a poet from Bengal and established the glories of the Deity.
text:
> tāra madhye 'bāṅgāla'-kavira nāṭaka-upekṣaṇa
> svarūpa-gosāñi kailā vigrahera mahimā-sthāpana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that chapter; [[synonyms:b:bāṅgāla]]-[[synonyms:k:kavira]]---of a poet from Bengal; [[synonyms:n:nāṭaka]]-[[synonyms:u:upekṣaṇa]]---the rejection of the drama; [[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:v:vigrahera]]---of the Deity; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāpana]]---the establishment of the glories.
translation: Also in that chapter, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī rejected the drama of a poet from Bengal and established the glories of the Deity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.112
description: The Sixth Chapter describes how Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and performed the chipped rice festival in accordance with Nityānanda Prabhu's order.
text:
> ṣaṣṭhe---raghunātha-dāsa prabhure mililā
> nityānanda-ājñāya ciḍā-mahotsava kailā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣaṣṭhe]]---in the Sixth Chapter; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]] [[synonyms:m:mililā]]---met Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]-[[synonyms:ā:ājñāya]]---by the order of Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:c:ciḍā]]-[[synonyms:m:mahotsava]] [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---performed the festival of chipped rice.
translation: The Sixth Chapter describes how Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and performed the chipped rice festival in accordance with Nityānanda Prabhu's order.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.113
description: The Lord entrusted Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī to the care of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and gave Raghunātha dāsa the gift of a stone from Govardhana Hill and a garland of small conchshells.
text:
> dāmodara-svarūpa-ṭhāñi tāṅre samarpila
> 'govardhana-śilā', 'guñjā-mālā' tāṅre dila
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]-[[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---to the care of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]] [[synonyms:s:samarpila]]---the Lord entrusted him; [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]-[[synonyms:ś:śilā]]---the stone from Govardhana Hill; [[synonyms:g:guñjā]]-[[synonyms:m:mālā]]---the garland of small conchshells; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---delivered to him.
translation: The Lord entrusted Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī to the care of Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī and gave Raghunātha dāsa the gift of a stone from Govardhana Hill and a garland of small conchshells.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.114
description: The Seventh Chapter tells how Śrī Caitanya met Vallabha Bhaṭṭa and dismantled his false pride in various ways.
text:
> saptama-paricchede---vallabha bhaṭṭera milana
> nānā-mate kailā tāṅra garva khaṇḍana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saptama]]-[[synonyms:p:paricchede]]---in the Seventh Chapter; [[synonyms:v:vallabha]] [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭera]] [[synonyms:m:milana]]---the meeting of Vallabha Bhaṭṭa with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:m:mate]]---in various ways; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:g:garva]]---pride; [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍana]]---dismantling.
translation: The Seventh Chapter tells how Śrī Caitanya met Vallabha Bhaṭṭa and dismantled his false pride in various ways.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.115
description: The Eighth Chapter describes the arrival of Rāmacandra Purī and how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu minimized His eating due to fear of him.
text:
> aṣṭame---rāmacandra-purīra āgamana
> tāṅra bhaye kailā prabhu bhikṣā saṅkocana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aṣṭame]]---in the Eighth Chapter; [[synonyms:r:rāmacandra]]-[[synonyms:p:purīra]] [[synonyms:ā:āgamana]]---the arrival of Rāmacandra Purī; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:b:bhaye]]---because of fear of him; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:s:saṅkocana]]---minimizing His eating.
translation: The Eighth Chapter describes the arrival of Rāmacandra Purī and how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu minimized His eating due to fear of him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.116
description: In the Ninth Chapter is a description of how Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka was delivered and how the people of the three worlds were able to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> navame---gopīnātha-paṭṭanāyaka-mocana
> trijagatera loka prabhura pāila daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:navame]]---in the Ninth Chapter; [[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]-[[synonyms:p:paṭṭanāyaka]]-[[synonyms:m:mocana]]---the deliverance of Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka, the brother of Rāmānanda Rāya; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:j:jagatera]]---of the three worlds; [[synonyms:l:loka]]---the people in general; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pāila]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---got the audience.
translation: In the Ninth Chapter is a description of how Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka was delivered and how the people of the three worlds were able to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.117
description: In the Tenth Chapter I have described how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu tasted the food given by His devotees, and I have also described the assortments in the bags of Rāghava Paṇḍita.
text:
> daśame---kahiluṅ bhakta-datta-āsvādana
> rāghava-paṇḍitera tāhāṅ jhālira sājana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:daśame]]---in the Tenth Chapter; [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have described; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:d:datta]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---the tasting of the food given by the devotees; [[synonyms:r:rāghava]]-[[synonyms:p:paṇḍitera]]---of Rāghava Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---therein; [[synonyms:j:jhālira]] [[synonyms:s:sājana]]---the assortment in the bags.
translation: In the Tenth Chapter I have described how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu tasted the food given by His devotees, and I have also described the assortments in the bags of Rāghava Paṇḍita.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.118
description: Also in that chapter is a description of how the Lord examined Govinda and how He danced in the temple.
text:
> tāra madhye govindera kailā parīkṣaṇa
> tāra madhye parimuṇḍā-nṛtyera varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that chapter; [[synonyms:g:govindera]]---of Govinda, His personal assistant; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:p:parīkṣaṇa]]---testing; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in that chapter; [[synonyms:p:parimuṇḍā]]-[[synonyms:n:nṛtyera]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---description of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu's dancing in the temple.
translation: Also in that chapter is a description of how the Lord examined Govinda and how He danced in the temple.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.119
description: The Eleventh Chapter describes the disappearance of Haridāsa Ṭhākura and how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, showed His affection for His devotees.
text:
> ekādaśe---haridāsa-ṭhākurera niryāṇa
> bhakta-vātsalya yāhāṅ dekhāilā gaura bhagavān
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ekādaśe]]---in the Eleventh Chapter; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākurera]] [[synonyms:n:niryāṇa]]---the disappearance of Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vātsalya]]---affection for the devotee; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherein; [[synonyms:d:dekhāilā]]---exhibited; [[synonyms:g:gaura]] [[synonyms:b:bhagavān]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
translation: The Eleventh Chapter describes the disappearance of Haridāsa Ṭhākura and how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, showed His affection for His devotees.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.12
description: "Let there be all victory for the chanting of the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa, which can cleanse the mirror of the heart and stop the miseries of the blazing fire of material existence. That chanting is the waxing moon that spreads the white lotus of good fortune for all living entities. It is the life and soul of all education. The chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa expands the blissful ocean of transcendental life. It gives a cooling effect to everyone and enables one to taste full nectar at every step.
text:
> ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanaṁ bhava-mahā-dāvāgni-nirvāpaṇaṁ
> śreyaḥ-kairava-candrikā-vitaraṇaṁ vidyā-vadhū-jīvanam
> ānandāmbudhi-vardhanaṁ prati-padaṁ pūrṇāmṛtāsvādanaṁ
> sarvātma-snapanaṁ paraṁ vijayate śrī-kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtanam
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:cetaḥ]]---of the heart; [[synonyms:d:darpaṇa]]---the mirror; [[synonyms:m:mārjanam]]---cleansing; [[synonyms:b:bhava]]---of material existence; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:d:dāvāgni]]---the blazing forest fire; [[synonyms:n:nirvāpaṇam]]---extinguishing; [[synonyms:ś:śreyaḥ]]---of good fortune; [[synonyms:k:kairava]]---the white lotus; [[synonyms:c:candrikā]]---the moonshine; [[synonyms:v:vitaraṇam]]---spreading; [[synonyms:v:vidyā]]---of all education; [[synonyms:v:vadhū]]---wife; [[synonyms:j:jīvanam]]---the life; [[synonyms:ā:ānanda]]---of bliss; [[synonyms:a:ambudhi]]---the ocean; [[synonyms:v:vardhanam]]---increasing; [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:p:padam]]---at every step; [[synonyms:p:pūrṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---of the full nectar; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādanam]]---giving a taste; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]---for everyone; [[synonyms:ā:ātma]]-[[synonyms:s:snapanam]]---bathing of the self; [[synonyms:p:param]]---transcendental; [[synonyms:v:vijayate]]---let there be victory; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtanam]]---for the congregational chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Let there be all victory for the chanting of the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa, which can cleanse the mirror of the heart and stop the miseries of the blazing fire of material existence. That chanting is the waxing moon that spreads the white lotus of good fortune for all living entities. It is the life and soul of all education. The chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa expands the blissful ocean of transcendental life. It gives a cooling effect to everyone and enables one to taste full nectar at every step.
purport: This is the first verse of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's //Śikṣāṣṭaka.// The other seven verses are found in texts 16, 21, 29, 32, 36, 39 and 47.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.120
description: In the Twelfth Chapter are descriptions of how Jagadānanda Paṇḍita broke a pot of oil and how Lord Nityānanda chastised Śivānanda Sena.
text:
> dvādaśe---jagadānandera taila-bhañjana
> nityānanda kailā śivānandere tāḍana
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dvādaśe]]---in the Twelfth Chapter; [[synonyms:j:jagadānandera]]---of Jagadānanda Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:t:taila]]-[[synonyms:b:bhañjana]]---breaking the oil pot; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---performed; [[synonyms:ś:śivānandere]] [[synonyms:t:tāḍana]]---the chastisement of Śivānanda Sena.
translation: In the Twelfth Chapter are descriptions of how Jagadānanda Paṇḍita broke a pot of oil and how Lord Nityānanda chastised Śivānanda Sena.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.121
description: In the Thirteenth Chapter, Jagadānanda Paṇḍita went to Mathurā and returned, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by chance heard a song sung by a deva-dāsī dancing girl.
text:
> trayodaśe---jagadānanda mathurā yāi' āilā
> mahāprabhu deva-dāsīra gīta śunilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:trayodaśe]]---in the Thirteenth Chapter; [[synonyms:j:jagadānanda]]---Jagadānanda Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:m:mathurā]] [[synonyms:y:yāi']]---going to Mathurā; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned; [[synonyms:m:mahāprabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:d:deva]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsīra]]---of the deva-dāsī dancing girl; [[synonyms:g:gīta]] [[synonyms:ś:śunilā]]---heard the song.
translation: In the Thirteenth Chapter, Jagadānanda Paṇḍita went to Mathurā and returned, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by chance heard a song sung by a deva-dāsī dancing girl.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.122
description: Also in the Thirteenth Chapter, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who by His causeless mercy sent him to Vṛndāvana.
text:
> raghunātha-bhaṭṭācāryera tāhāṅi milana
> prabhu tāṅre kṛpā kari' pāṭhāilā vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭācāryera]]---of Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅi]]---there; [[synonyms:m:milana]]---meeting; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---to him; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---showing causeless mercy; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāilā]] [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---sent to Vṛndāvana.
translation: Also in the Thirteenth Chapter, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who by His causeless mercy sent him to Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.123
description: The Fourteenth Chapter describes the beginning of the Lord's spiritual trance, in which His body was at Jagannātha Purī but His mind was in Vṛndāvana.
text:
> caturdaśe---divyonmāda-ārambha varṇana
> 'śarīra' ethā prabhura, 'mana' gelā vṛndāvana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caturdaśe]]---in the Fourteenth Chapter; [[synonyms:d:divya]]-[[synonyms:u:unmāda]]-[[synonyms:ā:ārambha]]---the beginning of the spiritual trance of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---describing; [[synonyms:ś:śarīra]]---the body; [[synonyms:e:ethā]]---here; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]---to Vṛndāvana.
translation: The Fourteenth Chapter describes the beginning of the Lord's spiritual trance, in which His body was at Jagannātha Purī but His mind was in Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.124
description: Also in that chapter is a description of how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell down in front of the Siṁha-dvāra gate of Jagannātha temple, His bones separated at the joints, and how various transcendental symptoms awakened.
text:
> tāra madhye prabhura siṁha-dvāre patana
> asthi-sandhi-tyāga, anubhāvera udgama
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in that chapter; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:s:siṁha]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]] [[synonyms:p:patana]]---falling down by the Siṁha-dvāra gate; [[synonyms:a:asthi]]-[[synonyms:s:sandhi]]---of the joints of the bones; [[synonyms:t:tyāga]]---release; [[synonyms:a:anubhāvera]] [[synonyms:u:udgama]]---the awakening of a trance and emotion.
translation: Also in that chapter is a description of how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell down in front of the Siṁha-dvāra gate of Jagannātha temple, His bones separated at the joints, and how various transcendental symptoms awakened.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.125
description: Also in that chapter there is a description of how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ran toward Caṭaka-parvata and spoke like a madman.
text:
> caṭaka-parvata dekhi' prabhura dhāvana
> tāra madhye prabhura kichu pralāpa-varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caṭaka]]-[[synonyms:p:parvata]]---the hill known as Caṭaka-parvata; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:d:dhāvana]]---the running of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in that chapter; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:p:pralāpa]] [[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---talking like a madman.
translation: Also in that chapter there is a description of how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ran toward Caṭaka-parvata and spoke like a madman.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.126
description: In the Fifteenth Chapter is a description of how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered a garden on the shore of the sea, mistaking the garden for Vṛndāvana.
text:
> pañcadaśa-paricchede---udyāna-vilāse
> vṛndāvana-bhrame yāhāṅ karilā praveśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pañcadaśa]]-[[synonyms:p:paricchede]]---in the Fifteenth Chapter; [[synonyms:u:udyāna]]-[[synonyms:v:vilāse]]---in His pastimes within the garden; [[synonyms:v:vṛndāvana]]-[[synonyms:b:bhrame]]---His taking the garden to be Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:p:praveśe]]---He entered.
translation: In the Fifteenth Chapter is a description of how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered a garden on the shore of the sea, mistaking the garden for Vṛndāvana.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.127
description: Also in that chapter is a description of the attraction of Lord Caitanya's five senses to Kṛṣṇa and how He searched for Kṛṣṇa in the rāsa dance.
text:
> tāra madhye prabhura pañcendriya-ākarṣaṇa
> tāra madhye karilā rāse kṛṣṇa-anveṣaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:i:indriya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākarṣaṇa]]---the attraction of the five senses; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---within that chapter; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:r:rāse]]---in the //rāsa// dance; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:anveṣaṇa]]---searching for Kṛṣṇa.
translation: Also in that chapter is a description of the attraction of Lord Caitanya's five senses to Kṛṣṇa and how He searched for Kṛṣṇa in the rāsa dance.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.128
description: The Sixteenth Chapter tells how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu showed His mercy to Kālidāsa and thus demonstrated the result of eating the remnants of the food of Vaiṣṇavas.
text:
> ṣoḍaśe---kālidāse prabhu kṛpā karilā
> vaiṣṇavocchiṣṭa khāibāra phala dekhāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṣ:ṣoḍaśe]]---in the Sixteenth Chapter; [[synonyms:k:kāli]]-[[synonyms:d:dāse]]---unto Kālidāsa; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---showed favor; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:u:ucchiṣṭa]] [[synonyms:k:khāibāra]]---of eating the remnants of food left by Vaiṣṇavas; [[synonyms:p:phala]] [[synonyms:d:dekhāilā]]---showed the result.
translation: The Sixteenth Chapter tells how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu showed His mercy to Kālidāsa and thus demonstrated the result of eating the remnants of the food of Vaiṣṇavas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.129
description: It also describes how Śivānanda's son composed a verse and how the doorkeeper of the Siṁha-dvāra showed Kṛṣṇa to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> śivānandera bālake śloka karāilā
> siṁha-dvāre dvārī prabhure kṛṣṇa dekhāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śivānandera]]---of Śivānanda Sena; [[synonyms:b:bālake]]---the son; [[synonyms:ś:śloka]] [[synonyms:k:karāilā]]---made to compose a verse; [[synonyms:s:siṁha]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---at the Siṁha-dvāra gate of the Jagannātha temple; [[synonyms:d:dvārī]]---the doorkeeper; [[synonyms:p:prabhure]]---unto Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadekhāilā]]---showed Lord Kṛṣṇa.
translation: It also describes how Śivānanda's son composed a verse and how the doorkeeper of the Siṁha-dvāra showed Kṛṣṇa to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.13
description: "By performing congregational chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra, one can destroy the sinful condition of material existence, purify the unclean heart and awaken all varieties of devotional service.
text:
> saṅkīrtana haite pāpa-saṁsāra-nāśana
> citta-śuddhi, sarva-bhakti-sādhana-udgama
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from the process of chanting the holy name; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṁsāra]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśana]]---annihilation of materialistic life resulting from sins; [[synonyms:c:citta]]-[[synonyms:ś:śuddhi]]---cleansing of the heart; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---all kinds of devotional service; [[synonyms:s:sādhana]]---of the performances; [[synonyms:u:udgama]]---awakening.
translation: "By performing congregational chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra, one can destroy the sinful condition of material existence, purify the unclean heart and awaken all varieties of devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.130
description: Also in that chapter, the glories of mahā-prasāda are explained, and a verse is tasted describing the effect of nectar from the lips of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> mahā-prasādera tāhāṅ mahimā varṇilā
> kṛṣṇādharāmṛtera phala-śloka āsvādilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:prasādera]]---of the remnants of the food of the Lord, //mahā-prasāda//; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---the glories; [[synonyms:v:varṇilā]]---described; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:adhara]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛtera]]---of the nectar from the lips of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:phala]]-[[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---the verse mentioning the result; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādilā]]---tasted.
translation: Also in that chapter, the glories of mahā-prasāda are explained, and a verse is tasted describing the effect of nectar from the lips of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.131
description: In the Seventeenth Chapter, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell among the cows and assumed the form of a tortoise as His ecstatic emotions awakened.
text:
> saptadaśe---gābhī-madhye prabhura patana
> kūrmākāra-anubhāvera tāhāṅi udgama
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saptadaśe]]---in the Seventeenth Chapter; [[synonyms:g:gābhī]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---among the cows; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:p:patana]]---the falling down of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kūrma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ākāra]]-[[synonyms:a:anubhāvera]]---of ecstatic emotion in the form of a tortoise; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅi]]---there; [[synonyms:u:udgama]]---awakening.
translation: In the Seventeenth Chapter, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell among the cows and assumed the form of a tortoise as His ecstatic emotions awakened.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.132
description: Also in the Seventeenth Chapter, the attributes of Kṛṣṇa's sound attracted the mind of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who described in ecstasy the meaning of the "kā stry aṅga te" verse.
text:
> kṛṣṇera śabda-guṇe prabhura mana ākarṣilā
> "kā stry aṅga te" ślokera artha āveśe karilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ś:śabda]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇe]]---by the qualities of the sound; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind; [[synonyms:ā:ākarṣilā]]---was attracted; [[synonyms:k:kā]] [[synonyms:s:stry]] [[synonyms:a:aṅga]] [[synonyms:t:te]] [[synonyms:ś:ślokera]]---of the verse beginning with the words //kā stry aṅga te//; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meaning; [[synonyms:ā:āveśe]]---in ecstasy; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---described.
translation: Also in the Seventeenth Chapter, the attributes of Kṛṣṇa's sound attracted the mind of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who described in ecstasy the meaning of the "kā stry aṅga te" verse.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.133
description: Due to the conjunction of various ecstatic emotions, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu again began speaking like a madman and described in detail the meaning of a verse from Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta.
text:
> bhāva-śābalye punaḥ kailā pralapana
> karṇāmṛta-ślokera artha kailā vivaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhāva]]-[[synonyms:ś:śābalye]]---from the aggregate of all ecstatic emotions; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:p:pralapana]]---He talked like a madman; [[synonyms:k:karṇāmṛta]]-[[synonyms:ś:ślokera]]---of a verse from //Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta//; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meaning; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---described in detail.
translation: Due to the conjunction of various ecstatic emotions, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu again began speaking like a madman and described in detail the meaning of a verse from Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.134
description: In the Eighteenth Chapter, the Lord fell into the ocean, and in ecstasy He saw the pastimes of the water fight between Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs.
text:
> aṣṭādaśa paricchede---samudre patana
> kṛṣṇa-gopī-jala-keli tāhāṅ daraśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aṣṭādaśa]] [[synonyms:p:paricchede]]---in the Eighteenth Chapter; [[synonyms:s:samudre]] [[synonyms:p:patana]]---the Lord's falling into the ocean; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:g:gopī]]-[[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:k:keli]]---the water pastimes of Kṛṣṇa and the //gopīs//; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]] [[synonyms:d:daraśana]]---seeing there.
translation: In the Eighteenth Chapter, the Lord fell into the ocean, and in ecstasy He saw the pastimes of the water fight between Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.135
description: In that dream, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw Kṛṣṇa's picnic in the forest. As Lord Caitanya floated in the sea, a fisherman caught Him, and then the Lord returned to His own residence.
text:
> tāhāṅi dekhilā kṛṣṇera vanya-bhojana
> jāliyā uṭhāila, prabhu āilā sva-bhavana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅi]]---there; [[synonyms:d:dekhilā]]---He saw; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:v:vanya]]-[[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---a picnic in the forest; [[synonyms:j:jāliyā]]---a fisherman; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāila]]---caught Him; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---the Lord; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---returned; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhavana]]---to His own residence.
translation: In that dream, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw Kṛṣṇa's picnic in the forest. As Lord Caitanya floated in the sea, a fisherman caught Him, and then the Lord returned to His own residence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.136
description: In the Nineteenth Chapter is a description of how Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu rubbed His face against the walls and spoke like a madman because of separation from Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> ūnaviṁśe---bhittye prabhura mukha-saṅgharṣaṇa
> kṛṣṇera viraha-sphūrti-pralāpa-varṇana
synonyms: [[synonyms:ū:ūnaviṁśe]]---in the Nineteenth Chapter; [[synonyms:b:bhittye]]---on the walls; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:m:mukha]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅgharṣaṇa]]---the rubbing of the face of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:v:viraha]]-[[synonyms:s:sphūrti]]---the awakening of separation from Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pralāpa]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇana]]---and talking like a crazy person.
translation: In the Nineteenth Chapter is a description of how Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu rubbed His face against the walls and spoke like a madman because of separation from Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.137
description: That chapter also describes Kṛṣṇa's wandering in a garden on a spring night, and it fully describes the meaning of a verse about the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body.
text:
> vasanta-rajanīte puṣpodyāne viharaṇa
> kṛṣṇera saurabhya-ślokera artha-vivaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vasanta]]-[[synonyms:r:rajanīte]]---on a spring night; [[synonyms:p:puṣpa]]-[[synonyms:u:udyāne]]---in a flower garden; [[synonyms:v:viharaṇa]]---the wandering; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]]---of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:saurabhya]]-[[synonyms:ś:ślokera]]---of a verse about the bodily fragrance; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---describing the meaning.
translation: That chapter also describes Kṛṣṇa's wandering in a garden on a spring night, and it fully describes the meaning of a verse about the scent of Kṛṣṇa's body.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.138
description: In the Twentieth Chapter, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited His own eight stanzas of instruction and tasted their meaning in ecstatic love.
text:
> viṁśa-paricchede---nija-'śikṣāṣṭaka' paḍiyā
> tāra artha āsvādilā premāviṣṭa hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:viṁśa]]-[[synonyms:p:paricchede]]---in the Twentieth Chapter; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:ś:śikṣāṣṭaka]] [[synonyms:p:paḍiyā]]---reciting His own //Śikṣāṣṭaka// verses; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:a:artha]]---their meaning; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādilā]]---tasted; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:ā:āviṣṭa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being absorbed in ecstatic love.
translation: In the Twentieth Chapter, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited His own eight stanzas of instruction and tasted their meaning in ecstatic love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.139
description: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu composed those eight stanzas to instruct the devotees, but He also personally tasted their meaning.
text:
> bhakte śikhāite yei śikṣāṣṭaka kahilā
> sei ślokāṣṭakera artha punaḥ āsvādilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakte]]---the devotees; [[synonyms:ś:śikhāite]]---to teach; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---that which; [[synonyms:ś:śikṣā]]-[[synonyms:a:aṣṭaka]]---eight instructions; [[synonyms:k:kahilā]]---described; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ś:śloka]]-[[synonyms:a:aṣṭakera]]---of the same eight verses; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meaning; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]] [[synonyms:ā:āsvādilā]]---again He tasted.
translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu composed those eight stanzas to instruct the devotees, but He also personally tasted their meaning.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.14
description: "The result of chanting is that one awakens his love for Kṛṣṇa and tastes transcendental bliss. Ultimately, one attains the association of Kṛṣṇa and engages in His devotional service, as if immersing himself in a great ocean of love."
text:
> kṛṣṇa-premodgama, premāmṛta-āsvādana
> kṛṣṇa-prāpti, sevāmṛta-samudre majjana
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:u:udgama]]---awakening of love for Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]-[[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasting of the transcendental bliss of love for Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:prāpti]]---attainment of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:s:sevā]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---of the nectar of service; [[synonyms:s:samudre]]---in the ocean; [[synonyms:m:majjana]]---immersing.
translation: "The result of chanting is that one awakens his love for Kṛṣṇa and tastes transcendental bliss. Ultimately, one attains the association of Kṛṣṇa and engages in His devotional service, as if immersing himself in a great ocean of love."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.140
description: I have thus described the principal pastimes and their meaning, for by such repetition one can remember the descriptions in the book.
text:
> mukhya-mukhya-līlāra artha kariluṅ kathana
> 'anuvāda' haite smare grantha-vivaraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhya]]-[[synonyms:l:līlāra]]---of the chief pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---the meaning; [[synonyms:k:kariluṅ]]---have done; [[synonyms:k:kathana]]---describing; [[synonyms:a:anuvāda]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---by repeating them again; [[synonyms:s:smare]]---one remembers; [[synonyms:g:grantha]]-[[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---the description in the book.
translation: I have thus described the principal pastimes and their meaning, for by such repetition one can remember the descriptions in the book.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.141
description: In every chapter there are various topics, but I have selected only those that are principal, for not all of them could be described again.
text:
> eka eka paricchedera kathā---aneka-prakāra
> mukhya-mukhya kahiluṅ, kathā nā yāya vistāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:p:paricchedera]]---of every chapter; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---description; [[synonyms:a:aneka]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāra]]---different varieties; [[synonyms:m:mukhya]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhya]] [[synonyms:k:kahiluṅ]]---I have repeated only the principal ones; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---discussions; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---not possible; [[synonyms:v:vistāra]]---expansion.
translation: In every chapter there are various topics, but I have selected only those that are principal, for not all of them could be described again.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.142-143
description: The Vṛndāvana Deities of Madana-mohana with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Govinda with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and Gopīnātha with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī are the life and soul of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas.
text:
> śrī-rādhā-saha 'śrī-madana-mohana'
> śrī-rādhā-saha 'śrī-govinda'-caraṇa
>
> śrī-rādhā-saha śrīla 'śrī-gopīnātha'
> ei tina ṭhākura haya 'gauḍiyāra nātha'
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:s:saha]]---with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:m:mohana]]---the Deity Madana-mohanajī; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:s:saha]]---with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of Śrī Govindajī; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rādhā]]-[[synonyms:s:saha]]---with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; [[synonyms:ś:śrīla]] [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:g:gopīnātha]]---the all-beautiful and opulent Gopīnāthajī; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:t:tina]]---all these three; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---Deities; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---are; [[synonyms:g:gauḍiyāra]] [[synonyms:n:nātha]]---worshipable by all the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas.
translation: The Vṛndāvana Deities of Madana-mohana with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Govinda with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and Gopīnātha with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī are the life and soul of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.144-146
description: So that my desires may be fulfilled, I place the lotus feet of these personalities on my head: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, with Lord Nityānanda, Advaita Ācārya and Their devotees, as well as Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrī Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, who is my spiritual master, and Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī.
text:
> śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya, śrī-yuta nityānanda
> śrī-advaita-ācārya, śrī-gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
>
> śrī-svarūpa, śrī-rūpa, śrī-sanātana
> śrī-guru śrī-raghunātha, śrī-jīva-caraṇa
>
> nija-śire dhari' ei sabāra caraṇa
> yāhā haite haya saba vāñchita-pūraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:y:yuta]] [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Śrī Advaita Prabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:s:svarūpa]]---Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:s:sanātana]]---Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:g:guru]]---the spiritual master; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:j:jīva]]-[[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:n:nija]]-[[synonyms:ś:śire]] [[synonyms:d:dhari']]---catching on my head; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:s:sabāra]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of all of them; [[synonyms:y:yāhā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---by which action; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:v:vāñchita]]-[[synonyms:p:pūraṇa]]---the fulfilling of desires.
translation: So that my desires may be fulfilled, I place the lotus feet of these personalities on my head: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, with Lord Nityānanda, Advaita Ācārya and Their devotees, as well as Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrī Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, who is my spiritual master, and Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī.
purport: Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī was the instructing spiritual master of Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī and has therefore been described as //śrī-guru.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.147
description: The mercy of their lotus feet is my spiritual master, and my words are my disciples that I have made dance in various ways.
text:
> sabāra caraṇa-kṛpā---'guru upādhyāyi'
> mora vāṇī---śiṣyā, tāre bahuta nācāi
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of them; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---the mercy of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:g:guru]] [[synonyms:u:upādhyāyī]]---my teacher of Vedic instruction; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---my words; [[synonyms:ś:śiṣyā]]---the disciples; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---them; [[synonyms:b:bahuta]] [[synonyms:n:nācāi]]---I made dance in various ways.
translation: The mercy of their lotus feet is my spiritual master, and my words are my disciples that I have made dance in various ways.
purport:
//Upādhyāyī,// or //upādhyāya,// refers to one who teaches when approached (//upetya adhīyate asmāt).// In the //Manu-saṁhitā// it is said:

> eka-deśaṁ tu vedasya
> vedāṅgāny api vā punaḥ
> yo 'dhyāpayati vṛtty-artham
> upādhyāyaḥ sa ucyate

"One who teaches others a part of the Vedas or literatures supplementary to the Vedas may be called //upādhyāya.//" //Upādhyāya// also refers to one who teaches art.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.148
