description: Seeing the fatigue of the disciples, the spiritual master has stopped making them dance, and because that mercy no longer makes them dance, my words now sit silently.
text:
> śiṣyāra śrama dekhi' guru nācāna rākhilā
> 'kṛpā' nā nācāya, 'vāṇī' vasiyā rahilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śiṣyāra]]---of the disciples; [[synonyms:ś:śrama]]---the fatigue; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:g:guru]]---the spiritual master; [[synonyms:n:nācāna]] [[synonyms:r:rākhilā]]---stopped causing the dancing; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---mercy; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:n:nācāya]]---does not make dance; [[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---the words; [[synonyms:v:vasiyā]]---sitting down; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remain silent.
translation: Seeing the fatigue of the disciples, the spiritual master has stopped making them dance, and because that mercy no longer makes them dance, my words now sit silently.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.149
description: My inexperienced words do not know how to dance by themselves. The mercy of the guru made them dance as much as possible, and now, after dancing, they have taken rest.
text:
> anipuṇā vāṇī āpane nācite nā jāne
> yata nācāilā, nāci' karilā viśrāme
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anipuṇā]] [[synonyms:v:vāṇī]]---inexperienced words; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---by themselves; [[synonyms:n:nācite]]---to dance; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:j:jāne]]---know how; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---whatever; [[synonyms:n:nācāilā]]---caused to dance; [[synonyms:n:nāci']]---after dancing; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:v:viśrāme]]---took rest.
translation: My inexperienced words do not know how to dance by themselves. The mercy of the guru made them dance as much as possible, and now, after dancing, they have taken rest.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.15
description: Lamentation and humility awoke within Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and He began reciting another of His own verses. By hearing the meaning of that verse, one can forget all unhappiness and lamentation.
text:
> uṭhila viṣāda, dainya,---paḍe āpana-śloka
> yāhāra artha śuni' saba yāya duḥkha-śoka
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:uṭhila]] [[synonyms:v:viṣāda]]---there was awakening of lamentation; [[synonyms:d:dainya]]---humility; [[synonyms:p:paḍe]]---reads; [[synonyms:ā:āpana]]-[[synonyms:ś:śloka]]---His own verse; [[synonyms:y:yāhāra]]---of which; [[synonyms:a:artha]] [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing the meaning; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---go away; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]-[[synonyms:ś:śoka]]---unhappiness and lamentation.
translation: Lamentation and humility awoke within Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and He began reciting another of His own verses. By hearing the meaning of that verse, one can forget all unhappiness and lamentation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.150
description: I now worship the lotus feet of all my readers, for by the mercy of their lotus feet there is all good fortune.
text:
> saba śrotā-gaṇera kari caraṇa vandana
> yāṅ-sabāra caraṇa-kṛpā---śubhera kāraṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:ś:śrotā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇera]]---of the readers; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I do; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]] [[synonyms:v:vandana]]---worshiping the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāṅ]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of whom; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---the mercy of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:ś:śubhera]] [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause of all good fortune.
translation: I now worship the lotus feet of all my readers, for by the mercy of their lotus feet there is all good fortune.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.151
description: If one hears the pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as described in Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, I wash his lotus feet and drink the water.
text:
> caitanya-caritāmṛta yei jana śune
> tāṅra caraṇa dhuñā karoṅ muñi pāne
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the description of Lord Śrī Caitanya's pastimes; [[synonyms:y:yei]] [[synonyms:j:jana]] [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---anyone who hears; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---his lotus feet; [[synonyms:d:dhuñā]]---washing; [[synonyms:k:karoṅ]]---do; [[synonyms:m:muñi]]---I; [[synonyms:p:pāne]]---drinking.
translation: If one hears the pastimes of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as described in Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, I wash his lotus feet and drink the water.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.152
description: I decorate my head with the dust of the lotus feet of my audience. Now you have all drunk this nectar, and therefore my labor is successful.
text:
> śrotāra pada-reṇu karoṅ mastaka-bhūṣaṇa
> tomarā e-amṛta pile saphala haila śrama
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrotāra]]---of the audience; [[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:r:reṇu]]---the dust of the lotus feet; [[synonyms:k:karoṅ]]---I make; [[synonyms:m:mastaka]]-[[synonyms:b:bhūṣaṇa]]---a decoration on my head; [[synonyms:t:tomarā]]---all of you; [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:a:amṛta]]---this nectar; [[synonyms:p:pile]]---have drunk; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]---successful; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---has become; [[synonyms:ś:śrama]]---my labor.
translation: I decorate my head with the dust of the lotus feet of my audience. Now you have all drunk this nectar, and therefore my labor is successful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.153
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇadāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.154
description: Caitanya-caritāmṛta is filled with the activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. It invokes all good fortune and destroys everything inauspicious. If one tastes the nectar of Caitanya-caritāmṛta with faith and love, I become like a bumblebee tasting the honey of transcendental love from his lotus feet.
text:
> caritam amṛtam etac chrīla-caitanya-viṣṇoḥ
> śubhadam aśubhanāśi śraddhayāsvādayed yaḥ
> tad-amala-pada-padme bhṛṅgatām etya so 'yaṁ
> rasayati rasam uccaiḥ prema-mādhvīka-pūram
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caritam]]---the character; [[synonyms:a:amṛtam]]---nectarean; [[synonyms:e:etat]]---this; [[synonyms:ś:śrīla]]---most opulent; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:v:viṣṇoḥ]]---of He who is Lord Viṣṇu Himself, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:ś:śubhadam]]---giving auspiciousness; [[synonyms:a:aśubha]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśi]]---destroying all inauspiciousness; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhayā]]---with faith and love; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādayet]]---should taste; [[synonyms:y:yaḥ]]---anyone who; [[synonyms:t:tat]]-[[synonyms:a:amala]]-[[synonyms:p:pada]]-[[synonyms:p:padme]]---at the spotless lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhṛṅgatām]] [[synonyms:e:etya]]---becoming like a bumblebee; [[synonyms:s:saḥ]]---that person; [[synonyms:a:ayam]]---this; [[synonyms:r:rasayati]]---tastes; [[synonyms:r:rasam]]---transcendental mellow; [[synonyms:u:uccaiḥ]]---a large quantity; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:m:mādhvīka]]---of the wine of ecstatic love; [[synonyms:p:pūram]]---full.
translation: Caitanya-caritāmṛta is filled with the activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. It invokes all good fortune and destroys everything inauspicious. If one tastes the nectar of Caitanya-caritāmṛta with faith and love, I become like a bumblebee tasting the honey of transcendental love from his lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.155
description: Since this book, Caitanya-caritāmṛta, is now complete, having been written for the satisfaction of the most opulent Deities Madana-mohanajī and Govindajī, let it be offered at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanyadeva.
text:
> śrīman-madana-gopāla-
> govindadeva-tuṣṭaye
> caitanyārpitam astv etac
> caitanya-caritāmṛtam
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrīmat]]---all-beautiful; [[synonyms:m:madana]]-[[synonyms:g:gopāla]]---of the Deity Madana-mohana; [[synonyms:g:govinda]]-[[synonyms:d:deva]]---of the Deity Śrī Govindadeva in Vṛndāvana; [[synonyms:t:tuṣṭaye]]---for the satisfaction; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:a:arpitam]]---offered to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:a:astu]]---let it be; [[synonyms:e:etat]]---this book; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛtam]]---containing the nectarean activities of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
translation: Since this book, Caitanya-caritāmṛta, is now complete, having been written for the satisfaction of the most opulent Deities Madana-mohanajī and Govindajī, let it be offered at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanyadeva.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.156

translation: Realized devotees are like bumblebees maddened by their own mellows at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet. The scent of those lotus feet perfumes the entire world. Who is the realized soul that could give them up?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.16

You have invested all Your potencies in those names, and there are no hard and fast rules for remembering them. My dear Lord, although You bestow such mercy upon the fallen, conditioned souls by liberally teaching Your holy names, I am so unfortunate that I commit offenses while chanting the holy name, and therefore I do not achieve attachment for chanting.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.28
description: Wherever there is a relationship of love of Godhead, its natural symptom is that the devotee does not think himself a devotee. Instead, he always thinks that he has not even a drop of love for Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> premera svabhāva---yāhāṅ premera sambandha
> sei māne,---'kṛṣṇe mora nāhi prema-gandha'
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:premera]] [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the nature of love of Godhead; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:p:premera]] [[synonyms:s:sambandha]]---a relationship of love of Godhead; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:m:māne]]---he recognizes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---unto Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:g:gandha]]---even a scent of love of Godhead.
translation: Wherever there is a relationship of love of Godhead, its natural symptom is that the devotee does not think himself a devotee. Instead, he always thinks that he has not even a drop of love for Kṛṣṇa.
purport:
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that persons who are actually very poor because they possess not even a drop of love of Godhead or pure devotional service falsely advertise themselves as great devotees, although they cannot at any time relish the transcendental bliss of devotional service. A class of so-called devotees known as //prākṛta-sahajiyās// sometimes display devotional symptoms to exhibit their good fortune. They are pretending, however, because these devotional features are only external. The //prākṛta-sahajiyās// exhibit these symptoms to advertise their so-called advancement in love of Kṛṣṇa, but instead of praising the //prākṛta-sahajiyās// for their symptoms of transcendental ecstasy, pure devotees do not like to associate with them. It is not advisable to equate the //prākṛta-sahajiyās// with pure devotees. When one is actually advanced in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa, he does not try to advertise himself. Instead, he endeavors more and more to render service to the Lord.

The //prākṛta-sahajiyās// sometimes criticize pure devotees by calling them philosophers, learned scholars, knowers of the truth, or minute observers, but not devotees. On the other hand, they depict themselves as the most advanced, transcendentally blissful devotees, deeply absorbed in devotional service and mad to taste transcendental mellows. They also describe themselves as the most advanced devotees in spontaneous love, as knowers of transcendental mellows, as the topmost devotees in conjugal love of Kṛṣṇa, and so on. Not actually knowing the transcendental nature of love of God, they accept their material emotions to be indicative of advancement. In this way they pollute the process of devotional service. To try to become writers of Vaiṣṇava literature, they introduce their material conceptions of life into pure devotional service. Because of their material conceptions, they advertise themselves as knowers of transcendental mellows, but they do not understand the transcendental nature of devotional service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 20.29
