title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.100
description: Haridāsa Ṭhākura constructed a cottage in a solitary forest. There he planted a tulasī plant, and in front of the tulasī he would chant the holy name of the Lord 300,000 times daily. He chanted throughout the entire day and night.
text:
> nirjana-vane kuṭira kari' tulasī sevana
> rātri-dine tina lakṣa nāma-saṅkīrtana
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirjana]]-[[synonyms:v:vane]]---in a solitary forest; [[synonyms:k:kuṭira]]---a cottage; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---making; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]---the //tulasī// plant; [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---worshiping; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---throughout the entire day and night; [[synonyms:t:tina]]---three; [[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---hundred thousand; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the holy name.
translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura constructed a cottage in a solitary forest. There he planted a tulasī plant, and in front of the tulasī he would chant the holy name of the Lord 300,000 times daily. He chanted throughout the entire day and night.
purport:
The village of Benāpola is situated in the district of Yaśohara, which is now in Bangladesh. Benāpola is near the Banagāṅo station, which is at the border of Bangladesh and may be reached by the eastern railway from Shelda Station in Calcutta. Haridāsa Ṭhākura, being the //ācārya// of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra,// is called Nāmācārya Haridāsa Ṭhākura. From his personal Example we can understand that chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// and becoming highly elevated in Kṛṣṇa consciousness is very simple. Without difficulty one can sit down anywhere, especially on the bank of the Ganges, Yamunā or any sacred river, devise a sitting place or cottage, plant a tulasī, and before the tulasī chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// undisturbed.

Haridāsa Ṭhākura used to chant the holy name on his beads 300,000 times daily. Throughout the entire day and night, he would chant the sixteen names of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// One should not, however, imitate Haridāsa Ṭhākura, for no one else can chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// 300,000 times a day. Such chanting is for the //mukta-puruṣa,// or liberated soul. We can follow his example, however, by chanting sixteen rounds of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// on beads every day and offering respect to the //tulasī// plant. This is not at all difficult for anyone, and the process of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra// with a vow before the //tulasī// plant has such great spiritual potency that simply by doing this one can become spiritually strong. Therefore we request the members of the Hare Kṛṣṇa movement to follow Haridāsa Ṭhākura's example rigidly. Chanting sixteen rounds does not take much time, nor is offering respects to the //tulasī// plant difficult. The process has immense spiritual potency. One should not miss this opportunity.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.101
description: For his bodily maintenance he would go to a brāhmaṇa's house and beg some food. He was spiritually so influential that all the neighboring people worshiped him.
text:
> brāhmaṇera ghare kare bhikṣā nirvāhaṇa
> prabhāve sakala loka karaye pūjana
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇera]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in the house of a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]] [[synonyms:n:nirvāhaṇa]]---asking alms of food; [[synonyms:p:prabhāve]]---by spiritual potency; [[synonyms:s:sakala]] [[synonyms:l:loka]]---all people; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:p:pūjana]]---worship.
translation: For his bodily maintenance he would go to a brāhmaṇa's house and beg some food. He was spiritually so influential that all the neighboring people worshiped him.
purport: In the days of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, all the //brāhmaṇas// worshiped Nārāyaṇa in the form of the //śālagrama-śilā.// Therefore begging from a //brāhmaṇa's// house meant taking //kṛṣṇa-prasāda,// which is transcendental (//nirguṇa).// If we take food from the house of others, such as //karmīs,// we shall have to share the qualities of those from whom we take alms. Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took //prasāda// in the houses of Vaiṣṇavas. This is the general process. The members of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement are advised not to take food from anywhere but a Vaiṣṇava's or //brāhmaṇa's// house where Deity worship is performed. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has said, //viṣayīra anna khāile duṣṭa haya mana:// if a devotee takes alms or food from the house of a //karmī// who is simply interested in money, his mind will be unclean. We must always remember that a devotee's life is one of //vairāgya-vidyā,// or renunciation and knowledge. Therefore all devotees are warned not to live unnecessarily luxurious lives at the cost of others. //Gṛhasthas// living within the jurisdiction of the temple must be especially careful not to imitate //karmīs// by acquiring opulent clothing, food and conveyances. As far as possible, these should be avoided. A member of the temple, whether //gṛhastha, brahmacārī// or //sannyāsī,// must practice a life of renunciation, following in the footsteps of Haridāsa Ṭhākura and the six Gosvāmīs. Otherwise, because //māyā// is very strong, at any time one may become a victim of //māyā// and fall down from spiritual life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.104
description: By no means could he find any fault in the character of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Therefore he called for local prostitutes and began a plan to discredit His Holiness.
text:
> kona-prakāre haridāsera chidra nāhi pāya
> veśyā-gaṇe āni' kare chidrera upāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kona]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāre]]---by any means; [[synonyms:h:haridāsera]]---of Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:c:chidra]]---fault; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---not; [[synonyms:p:pāya]]---gets; [[synonyms:v:veśyā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---prostitutes; [[synonyms:ā:āni']]---bringing; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---makes; [[synonyms:c:chidrera]] [[synonyms:u:upāya]]---a means to find some fault.
translation: By no means could he find any fault in the character of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Therefore he called for local prostitutes and began a plan to discredit His Holiness.
purport: This is typical of atheistic men, but even among so-called religionists, //sādhus,// mendicants, //sannyāsīs// and //brahmacārīs,// there are many enemies of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement who always try to find faults in it, not considering that the movement is spreading automatically by the grace of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who wanted it spread all over the world, in every town and village. We are trying to fulfill the Lord's desire, and our attempt has become fairly successful, but the enemies of this movement unnecessarily try to find faults in it, exactly like the old rascal Rāmacandra Khān, who opposed Haridāsa Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.105
description: Rāmacandra Khān said to the prostitutes, "There is a mendicant named Haridāsa Ṭhākura. All of you devise a way to deviate him from his vows of austerity."
text:
> veśyā-gaṇe kahe,---"ei vairāgī haridāsa
> tumi-saba kara ihāra vairāgya-dharma nāśa"
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:veśyā]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---unto the prostitutes; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:v:vairāgī]]---mendicant; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]]---all of you; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---cause; [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---his; [[synonyms:v:vairāgya]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---from the life of a mendicant; [[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---deviation.
translation: Rāmacandra Khān said to the prostitutes, "There is a mendicant named Haridāsa Ṭhākura. All of you devise a way to deviate him from his vows of austerity."
purport: Devotional service is the path of //vairāgya-vidyā// (renunciation and knowledge). Haridāsa Ṭhākura was following this path, but Rāmacandra Khān planned to induce him to break his vows. Renunciation means renunciation of sensual pleasure, especially the pleasure of sex. Therefore a //brahmacārī, sannyāsī// or //vānaprastha// is strictly prohibited from having relationships with women. Haridāsa Ṭhākura was strictly renounced, and thus Rāmacandra Khān called for prostitutes because prostitutes know how to break a man's vow of celibacy by their feminine influence and thus pollute a mendicant or a person engaged in devotional life. It was impossible for Rāmacandra Khān to induce any other women to break Haridāsa Ṭhākura's vow, and therefore he called for prostitutes. Free mingling with women has never been possible in India, but for one who wanted to associate with society girls, they were available in a district of prostitutes. There were prostitutes in human society even in Lord Kṛṣṇa's time, for it is said that the prostitutes of Dvārakā City came forth to receive the Lord. Although they were prostitutes, they were also devotees of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.106
description: Among the prostitutes, one attractive young girl was selected."I shall attract the mind of Haridāsa Ṭhākura," she promised, "within three days."
text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.11
description: Dāmodara Paṇḍita impudently said to the Lord, "Everyone says that You are a great teacher because of Your instructions to others, but now we shall find out what kind of teacher You are.
text:
> anyopadeśe paṇḍita---kahe gosāñira ṭhāñi
> 'gosāñi"gosāñi' ebe jānimu 'gosāñi'
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anya]]-[[synonyms:u:upadeśe]]---by instructing others; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---learned teacher; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:g:gosāñira]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---in front of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]] [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the supreme teacher; [[synonyms:e:ebe]]---now; [[synonyms:j:jānimu]]---we shall know; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---what kind of teacher.
translation: Dāmodara Paṇḍita impudently said to the Lord, "Everyone says that You are a great teacher because of Your instructions to others, but now we shall find out what kind of teacher You are.
purport:
Dāmodara Paṇḍita was a great devotee of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Sometimes, however, a person in such a position becomes impudent, being influenced by the external energy and material considerations. Thus a devotee mistakenly dares to criticize the activities of the spiritual master or the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Despite the logic that "Caesar's wife must be above suspicion," a devotee should not be disturbed by the activities of his spiritual master and should not try to criticize him. A devotee should be fixed in the conclusion that the spiritual master cannot be subject to criticism and should never be considered equal to a common man. Even if there appears to be some discrepancy according to an imperfect devotee's estimation, the devotee should be fixed in the conviction that even if his spiritual master goes to a liquor shop, he is not a drunkard; rather, he must have some purpose in going there. it is said in a Bengali poem:

> yadyapi nityānanda surā-bāḍi yāya
> tathāpio haya nityānanda-rāya

"Even if I see that Lord Nityānanda has entered a liquor shop, I shall not be diverted from my conclusion that Nityānanda Rāya is the Supreme Personality of Godhead."

synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tulasīre]]---unto the //tulasī// plant; [[synonyms:t:tāṅke]]---unto Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:v:veśyā]]---the prostitute; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:d:dvāre]] [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting at the door; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name; [[synonyms:ś:śune]]---hears; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---says; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---O my Lord Hari, O my Lord Hari.
translation: After offering her obeisances to the tulasī plant and Haridāsa Ṭhākura, she sat down at the door. Hearing Haridāsa Ṭhākura chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra, she also chanted, "O my Lord Hari, O my Lord Hari."
purport: Herein one can clearly see how a Vaiṣṇava delivers a fallen soul by a transcendental trick. The prostitute came to pollute Haridāsa Ṭhākura but he took it as his duty to deliver the prostitute. As clearly demonstrated here, the process of deliverance is very simple. With faith and reverence the prostitute associated with Haridāsa Ṭhākura, who personally treated her material disease by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// Although the prostitute had an ulterior motive, somehow or other she got the association of a Vaiṣṇava and satisfied him by occasionally chanting in imitation, "O my Lord Hari, O my Lord Hari." The conclusion is that associating with a Vaiṣṇava, chanting the holy name of the Lord and offering obeisances to the //tulasī// plant or a Vaiṣṇava all lead one to become a transcendental devotee who is completely cleansed of all material contamination.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.124

> "koṭi-nāma-grahaṇa-yajña kari eka-māse
> ei dīkṣā kariyāchi, haila āsi' śeṣe
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:g:grahaṇa]]---chanting ten million names; [[synonyms:y:yajña]]---such a sacrifice; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---I perform; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:m:māse]]---in one month; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:d:dīkṣā]]---vow; [[synonyms:k:kariyāchi]]---I have taken; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---it was; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---nearing; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣe]]---the end.
translation: "I have vowed to chant ten million names in a month. I have taken this vow, but now it is nearing its end.
purport:
If one regularly chants 333,333 times daily for a month and then chants one time more, he will thus chant ten million times. In this way a devotee worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Such worship is called //yajña. Yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair yajanti hi sumedhasaḥ:// those whose intelligence is brilliant accept this //hari-nāma-yajña,// the //yajña// of chanting the holy name of the Lord. By performing this //yajña,// one satisfies the Supreme Personality of Godhead and thus attains perfection in spiritual life. According to external vision, Haridāsa Ṭhākura belonged to a Mohammedan family. Nevertheless, because he engaged himself in performing the //yajña// of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra,// he became a regularly initiated //brāhmaṇa.// As stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:33:6|(3.33.6)]]:

> yan-nāmadheya-śravaṇānukīrtanād
> yat-prahvaṇād yat-smaraṇād api kvacit
> śvādo 'pi sadyaḥ savanāya kalpate
> kutaḥ punas te bhagavan nu darśanāt

Even if a devotee comes from a family of dog-eaters, if he surrenders to the personality of Godhead he immediately becomes a qualified //brāhmaṇa// and is immediately fit to perform //yajña,// whereas a person born in a family of //brāhmaṇas// has to wait until completing the reformatory processes before he may be called //saṁskṛta,// purified. It is further said in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// (12.1.40):

> asaṁskṛtāḥ kriyā-hīnā
> rajasā tamasāvṛtāḥ
> prajās te bhakṣayiṣyanti
> mlecchā rājanya-rūpiṇaḥ

"In the age of Kali, //mlecchas,// or lowborn people who have not undergone the purifying process of //saṁskāra,// who do not know how to apply that process in actual life and who are covered by the modes of passion and ignorance, will take the posts of administrators. They will devour the citizens with their atheistic activities." A person who is not purified by the prescribed process of //saṁskāra// is called //asaṁskṛta,// but if one remains //kriyā-hīna// even after being purified by initiation-in other words, if one fails to actually apply the principles of purity in his life-he remains an unpurified //mleccha// or //yavana.// On the other hand, we find that Haridāsa Ṭhākura, although born in a //mleccha// or //yavana// family, became Nāmācārya Haridāsa Ṭhākura because he performed the //nāma-yajña// a minimum of 300,000 times every day.

Herein we find that Haridāsa Ṭhākura strictly followed his regulative principle of chanting 300,000 times. Thus when the prostitute became restless, he informed her that first he had to finish his chanting and then he would be able to satisfy her. Actually Haridāsa Ṭhākura chanted the holy name of the Lord for three nights continuously and gave the prostitute a chance to hear him. Thus she became purified, as will be seen in the following verses.

purport:
Haridāsa Ṭhākura never wanted to enjoy the prostitute, but he tricked her to deliver her by giving her a chance to hear the holy name of the Lord while he chanted. Pure devotees chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra,// and simply by hearing this chanting from a purified transcendental person, one is purified of all sinful activities, no matter how lowborn or fallen one may be. As soon as one is thus completely free from the reactions of sinful activities, he is eligible to render devotional service to the Lord. This is the process for engaging the fallen souls in devotional service. As Lord Kṛṣṇa says in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:7:28|(Bg. 7.28)]]:

> yeṣāṁ tv anta-gataṁ pāpaṁ
> janānāṁ puṇya-karmaṇām
> te dvandva-moha-nirmuktā
> bhajante māṁ dṛḍha-vratāḥ

"Persons who have acted piously in previous lives and in this life, whose sinful actions are completely eradicated and who are freed from the duality of delusion, engage themselves in My service with determination."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.136
description: Haridāsa Ṭhākura replied, "Immediately go home and distribute to the brāhmaṇas whatever property you have. Then come back to this room and stay here forever in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.
text:
> ṭhākura kahe,---"gharera dravya brāhmaṇe kara dāna
> ei ghare āsi' tumi karaha viśrāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura said; [[synonyms:g:gharera]]---at home; [[synonyms:d:dravya]]---articles; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇe]]---to the //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:k:kara]] [[synonyms:d:dāna]]---give as charity; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in this room; [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---returning; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:v:viśrāma]]---stay.
translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura replied, "Immediately go home and distribute to the brāhmaṇas whatever property you have. Then come back to this room and stay here forever in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.
purport:
Haridāsa Ṭhākura's instruction that the prostitute should distribute to the //brāhmaṇas// all the property she had at home is very significant. Haridāsa Ṭhākura never advised the prostitute to give charity to the so-called //daridra-nārāyaṇa// ("poor Nārāyaṇa") or any other such persons. According to Vedic civilization, charity should be given only to the qualified //brāhmaṇas.// As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:18:42|(Bg. 18.42)]]:

> śamo damas tapaḥ śaucaṁ
> kṣāntir ārjavam eva ca
> jñānaṁ vijñānam āstikyaṁ
> brahma-karma svabhāva-jam

The brahminical qualifications are truthfulness, control of the senses and mind, tolerance, simplicity, knowledge, practical application of transcendental knowledge in one's life, and full faith in the Supreme Personality of Godhead. persons engaged in pursuing spiritual understanding have no time to earn their livelihood. They depend completely on the mercy of the Lord, who says in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:22|(Bg. 9.22)]] that He personally carries to them all their necessities (//yoga-kṣemaṁ vahāmy aham).//

The Vedic civilization recommends that one give charity to //brāhmaṇas// and //sannyāsīs,// not to the so-called //daridra-nārāyaṇa.// Nārāyaṇa cannot be //daridra,// nor can //daridra// be Nārāyaṇa, for these are contradictory terms. Atheistic men invent such concoctions and preach them to fools, but charity should actually be given to //brāhmaṇas// and //sannyāsīs// because whatever money they get they spend for Kṛṣṇa. Whatever charity one gives to a //brāhmaṇa// goes to Kṛṣṇa, who says in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:9:27|(Bg. 9.27)]]:

> yat karoṣi yad aśnāsi
> yaj juhoṣi dadāsi yat
> yat tapasyasi kaunteya
> tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇam

"O son of Kunti, all that you eat, all that you offer and give away, as well as all austerities that you may perform, should be done as an offering unto Me." Everything actually belongs to Kṛṣṇa, but so-called civilized men unfortunately think that everything belongs to them. This is the mistake of materialistic civilization. The prostitute (//veśyā//) had earned money by questionable means, and therefore Haridāsa Ṭhākura advised her to distribute to the //brāhmaṇas// whatever she possessed. When Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī retired from family life, he distributed fifty percent of his income to the //brāhmaṇas// and Vaiṣṇavas. A //brāhmaṇa// knows what the Absolute Truth is, and a Vaiṣṇava, knowing the Absolute Truth, acts on behalf of the Absolute Truth, the Supreme personality of Godhead. Generally one earns money by many questionable means. Therefore at some time one should retire and distribute whatever one has to the //brāhmaṇas// and Vaiṣṇavas who engage in devotional service by preaching the glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.137
description: "Chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra continuously and render service to the tulasī plant by watering her and offering prayers to her. In this way you will very soon get the opportunity to be sheltered at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa."
text:
> nirantara nāma lao, kara tulasī sevana
> acirāt pābe tabe kṛṣṇera caraṇa"
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirantara]]---twenty-four hours a day; [[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:l:lao]]---chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra//; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---perform; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]] [[synonyms:s:sevana]]---worship of the //tulasī// plant; [[synonyms:a:acirāt]]---very soon; [[synonyms:p:pābe]]---you will get; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇera]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "Chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra continuously and render service to the tulasī plant by watering her and offering prayers to her. In this way you will very soon get the opportunity to be sheltered at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa."
purport:
At least five thousand years ago, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa expressed His desire that everyone surrender to Him (//sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja).// Why is it that people cannot do this? Kṛṣṇa assures, //ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ:// "I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear." Everyone is suffering from the results of sinful activities, but Kṛṣṇa says that if one surrenders unto Him, He will protect one from sinful reactions. Modern civilization, however, is interested neither in Kṛṣṇa nor in getting relief from sinful acts. Therefore men are suffering. Surrender is the ultimate instruction of //Bhagavad-gītā,// but for one who cannot surrender to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, it is better to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// constantly, under the instruction of Haridāsa Ṭhākura.

In our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement we are teaching our followers to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// continuously on beads. Even those who are not accustomed to this practice are advised to chant at least sixteen rounds on their beads so that they may be trained. Otherwise, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recommended:

> tṛṇād api sunīcena
> taror api sahiṣṇunā
> amāninā mānadena
> kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ

"One should chant the holy name of the Lord in a humble state of mind, thinking oneself lower than the straw in the street. One should be more tolerant than a tree, devoid of all sense of false prestige, and ready to offer all respect to others. In such a state of mind one can chant the holy name of the Lord constantly." //Sadā// means "always." Haridāsa Ṭhākura says, //nirantara nāma lao:// "Chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// without stopping."

Although Kṛṣṇa wants everyone to surrender to His lotus feet, because of people's sinful activities they cannot do this. //Na māṁ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ:// rascals and fools, the lowest of men, who engage in sinful activities, cannot suddenly surrender to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. Nevertheless, if they begin chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra// and rendering service unto the //tulasī// plant, they will very soon be able to surrender. One's real duty is to surrender to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa but if one is unable to do so, he should adopt this process, as introduced by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His most confidential servant, Nāmācārya Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura. This is the way to achieve success in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.138
description: After thus instructing the prostitute about the process of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra, Haridāsa Ṭhākura stood up and left, continuously chanting "Hari, Hari."
text:
> eta bali' tāre 'nāma' upadeśa kari'
> uṭhiyā calilā ṭhākura bali' 'hari' 'hari'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---her; [[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:u:upadeśa]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---instructing about the process of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra//; [[synonyms:u:uṭhiyā]]---standing up; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---left; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:b:bali']]---chanting; [[synonyms:h:hari]] [[synonyms:h:hari]]---the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.//
translation: After thus instructing the prostitute about the process of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra, Haridāsa Ṭhākura stood up and left, continuously chanting "Hari, Hari."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.139
description: Thereafter, the prostitute distributed to the brāhmaṇas whatever household possessions she had, following the order of her spiritual master.
text:
> tabe sei veśyā gurura ājñā la-ila
> gṛha-vitta yebā chila, brāhmaṇere dila
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---thereafter; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:v:veśyā]]---prostitute; [[synonyms:g:gurura]]---of the spiritual master; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]]---order; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---took; [[synonyms:g:gṛha]]-[[synonyms:v:vitta]]---all household possessions; [[synonyms:y:yebā]]---whatever; [[synonyms:c:chila]]---there was; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇere]]---to the //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:d:dila]]---gave.
translation: Thereafter, the prostitute distributed to the brāhmaṇas whatever household possessions she had, following the order of her spiritual master.
purport: Sometimes the word //gṛha-vṛtti// is substituted for the word //gṛha-vitta. Vṛtti// means "profession." The //gṛha-vṛtti// of the prostitute was to enchant foolish people and induce them to indulge in sex. Here, however, //gṛha-vṛtti// is not a suitable word. The proper word is //gṛha-vitta,// which means "all the possessions she had in her home." All the girl's possessions had been earned by professional prostitution and were therefore products of her sinful life. When such possessions are given to //brāhmaṇas// and Vaiṣṇavas who can engage them in the service of the Lord because of their advancement in spiritual life, this indirectly helps the person who gives the charity, for he is thus relieved of sinful reactions. As Kṛṣṇa promises, //ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi:// "I shall save you from all sinful reactions." When our Kṛṣṇa conscious devotees go out to beg charity or collect contributions in the form of membership fees, the money thus coming to the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is strictly employed to advance Kṛṣṇa consciousness all over the world. The Kṛṣṇa conscious devotees collect the money of others for the service of Kṛṣṇa, and they are satisfied with Kṛṣṇa's //prasāda// and whatever He gives them for their maintenance. They do not desire material comforts. However, they go to great pains to engage the possessions of prostitutes, or persons who are more or less like prostitutes, in the service of the Lord and thus free them from sinful reactions. A Vaiṣṇava //guru// accepts money or other contributions, but he does not employ such contributions for sense gratification. A pure Vaiṣṇava thinks himself unfit to help free even one person from the reactions of sinful life, but he engages one's hard-earned money in the service of the Lord and thus frees one from sinful reactions. A Vaiṣṇava //guru// is never dependent on the contributions of his disciples. Following the instructions of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, a pure Vaiṣṇava does not personally take even a single paisa from anyone, but he induces his followers to spend for the service of the Lord whatever possessions they have.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.14
description: "My dear Lord, You can act as You please. No one can say anything to restrict You. Nevertheless, the entire world is impudent. People can say anything. How can You stop them?
text:
> svacchande ācāra kara, ke pāre balite?
> mukhara jagatera mukha pāra ācchādite?
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:svacchande]]---without restriction; [[synonyms:ā:ācāra]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---You behave; [[synonyms:k:ke]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]] [[synonyms:b:balite]]---who can talk; [[synonyms:m:mukhara]]---talkative; [[synonyms:j:jagatera]]---of the whole world; [[synonyms:m:mukha]]---mouth; [[synonyms:p:pāra]] [[synonyms:ā:ācchādite]]---can You cover.
translation: "My dear Lord, You can act as You please. No one can say anything to restrict You. Nevertheless, the entire world is impudent. People can say anything. How can You stop them?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.140
description: The prostitute shaved her head clean in accordance with Vaiṣṇava principles and stayed in that room wearing only one cloth. Following in the footsteps of her spiritual master, she began chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra 300,000 times a day. She chanted throughout the entire day and night.
text:
> māthā muḍi' eka-vastre rahila sei ghare
> rātri-dine tina-lakṣa nāma grahaṇa kare
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māthā]] [[synonyms:m:muḍi']]---shaving her head; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:v:vastre]]---wearing one cloth; [[synonyms:r:rahila]]---remained; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in that room; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]-[[synonyms:d:dine]]---throughout the entire day and night; [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---300,000; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---holy names; [[synonyms:g:grahaṇa]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---chants.
translation: The prostitute shaved her head clean in accordance with Vaiṣṇava principles and stayed in that room wearing only one cloth. Following in the footsteps of her spiritual master, she began chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra 300,000 times a day. She chanted throughout the entire day and night.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.141
description: She worshiped the tulasī plant, following in the footsteps of her spiritual master. Instead of eating regularly, she chewed whatever food she received as alms, and if nothing was supplied she would fast. Thus by eating frugally and fasting she conquered her senses, and as soon as her senses were controlled, symptoms of love of Godhead appeared in her person.
text:
> tulasī sevana kare, carvaṇa, upavāsa
> indriya-damana haila, premera prakāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]---the //tulasī// plant; [[synonyms:s:sevana]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---she worshiped; [[synonyms:c:carvaṇa]]---chewing; [[synonyms:u:upavāsa]]---fasting; [[synonyms:i:indriya]]-[[synonyms:d:damana]]---controlling the senses; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:p:premera]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---manifestations symptomizing love of Godhead.
translation: She worshiped the tulasī plant, following in the footsteps of her spiritual master. Instead of eating regularly, she chewed whatever food she received as alms, and if nothing was supplied she would fast. Thus by eating frugally and fasting she conquered her senses, and as soon as her senses were controlled, symptoms of love of Godhead appeared in her person.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.142
description: Thus the prostitute became a celebrated devotee. She became very advanced in spiritual life, and many stalwart Vaiṣṇavas would come to see her.
text:
> prasiddhā vaiṣṇavī haila parama-mahāntī
> baḍa baḍa vaiṣṇava tāṅra darśanete yānti
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prasiddhā]]---celebrated; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇavī]]---devotee of the Lord; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:m:mahāntī]]---very advanced; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]---many recognized, highly situated devotees; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---her; [[synonyms:d:darśanete]]---to see; [[synonyms:y:yānti]]---used to go.
translation: Thus the prostitute became a celebrated devotee. She became very advanced in spiritual life, and many stalwart Vaiṣṇavas would come to see her.
purport: Stalwart, highly advanced Vaiṣṇava devotees are not interested in seeing prostitutes, but when a prostitute or any other fallen soul becomes a Vaiṣṇava, stalwart Vaiṣṇavas are interested in seeing them. Anyone can be turned into a Vaiṣṇava if he or she follows the Vaiṣṇava principles. A devotee who follows these principles is no longer on the material platform. Therefore, it is one's strict adherence to the principles that should be considered, not the country of one's birth. Many devotees join our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement from Europe and America, but one should not therefore consider them European Vaiṣṇavas or American Vaiṣṇavas. A Vaiṣṇava is a Vaiṣṇava and should therefore be given all the respect due a Vaiṣṇava.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.143
description: Seeing the sublime character of the prostitute, everyone was astonished. Everyone glorified the influence of Haridāsa Ṭhākura and offered him obeisances.
text:
> veśyāra caritra dekhi' loke camatkāra
> haridāsera mahimā kahe kari' namaskāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:veśyāra]]---of the prostitute; [[synonyms:c:caritra]]---character; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---all people; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonished; [[synonyms:h:haridāsera]]---of Ṭhākura Haridāsa; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---glories; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---speak; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---offering obeisances.
translation: Seeing the sublime character of the prostitute, everyone was astonished. Everyone glorified the influence of Haridāsa Ṭhākura and offered him obeisances.
purport: It is said, //phalena paricīyate:// one is recognized by the result of his actions. In Vaiṣṇava society there are many types of Vaiṣṇavas. Some of them are called //gosvāmīs,// some are called //svāmīs,// some are //prabhus,// and some are //prabhupāda.// One is not recognized, however, simply by such a name. A spiritual master is recognized as an actual //guru// when it is seen that he has changed the character of his disciples. Haridāsa Ṭhākura actually changed the character of the professional prostitute. People greatly appreciated this, and therefore they all offered obeisances to Haridāsa Ṭhākura and glorified him.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.144
description: By inducing a prostitute to disturb Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Rāmacandra Khān caused a seed of offense at his lotus feet to germinate. This seed later became a tree, and when it fructified, Rāmacandra Khān ate its fruits.
text:
> rāmacandra khāṅna aparādha-bīja kaila
> sei bīja vṛkṣa hañā āgete phalila
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:rāmacandra]] [[synonyms:k:khāṅna]]---Rāmacandra Khān; [[synonyms:a:aparādha]]---of the offense; [[synonyms:b:bīja]]---seed; [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---caused to germinate; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:b:bīja]]---that seed; [[synonyms:v:vṛkṣa]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming a tree; [[synonyms:ā:āgete]]---later; [[synonyms:p:phalila]]---fructified.
translation: By inducing a prostitute to disturb Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Rāmacandra Khān caused a seed of offense at his lotus feet to germinate. This seed later became a tree, and when it fructified, Rāmacandra Khān ate its fruits.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.145
description: This offense at the lotus feet of an exalted devotee has resulted in a wonderful narration. Taking advantage of the opportunity afforded by these incidents, I shall explain what happened. O devotees, please listen.
text:
> mahad-aparādhera phala adbhuta kathana
> prastāva pāñā kahi, śuna, bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahat]]-[[synonyms:a:aparādhera]]---of a great offense at the feet of the exalted devotee; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---the result; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:k:kathana]]---narration; [[synonyms:p:prastāva]]---opportunity; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---taking advantage of; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I say; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---O devotees.
translation: This offense at the lotus feet of an exalted devotee has resulted in a wonderful narration. Taking advantage of the opportunity afforded by these incidents, I shall explain what happened. O devotees, please listen.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.146
description: Rāmacandra Khān was naturally a nondevotee. Now, having offended the lotus feet of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, he became just like a demoniac atheist.
text:
> sahajei avaiṣṇava rāmacandra-khāṅna
> haridāsera aparādhe haila asura-samāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sahajei]]---naturally; [[synonyms:a:avaiṣṇava]]---nondevotee; [[synonyms:r:rāmacandra]]-[[synonyms:k:khāṅna]]---Rāmacandra Khān; [[synonyms:h:haridāsera]]---at the lotus feet of Haridāsa; [[synonyms:a:aparādhe]]---by offenses; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---was; [[synonyms:a:asura]]-[[synonyms:s:samāna]]---exactly like a demon.
translation: Rāmacandra Khān was naturally a nondevotee. Now, having offended the lotus feet of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, he became just like a demoniac atheist.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.147
description: Because of blaspheming the cult of Vaiṣṇavism and insulting the devotees for a long time, he now received the results of his offensive activities.
text:
> vaiṣṇava-dharma nindā kare, vaiṣṇava-apamāna
> bahu-dinera aparādhe pāila pariṇāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]]-[[synonyms:d:dharma]]---the cult of Vaiṣṇavism; [[synonyms:n:nindā]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---blasphemes; [[synonyms:v:vaiṣṇava]] [[synonyms:a:apamāna]]---insults to the devotees; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:d:dinera]]---for a long time; [[synonyms:a:aparādhe]]---by offensive activities; [[synonyms:p:pāila]]---got; [[synonyms:p:pariṇāma]]---the resultant action.
translation: Because of blaspheming the cult of Vaiṣṇavism and insulting the devotees for a long time, he now received the results of his offensive activities.
purport: Rāmacandra Khān was a great offender at the lotus feet of the Vaiṣṇavas and Viṣṇu. Just as Rāvaṇa, although born of a //brāhmaṇa// father, Viśvaśravā, was nevertheless called an //asura// or //rākṣasa// because of his offenses against Lord Rāmacandra (Viṣṇu) and Hanumān (a Vaiṣṇava), so Rāmacandra Khān also became such an //asura// because of his offenses against Haridāsa Ṭhākura and many others.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.148
description: When Lord Nityānanda returned to Bengal to preach the cult of bhakti, love of Godhead, He began touring all over the country.
text:
> nityānanda-gosāñi gauḍe yabe āilā
> prema pracārite tabe bhramite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:g:gauḍe]]---in Bengal; [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---when; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came back; [[synonyms:p:prema]] [[synonyms:p:pracārite]]---to preach the cult of //bhakti,// love of Godhead; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:b:bhramite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to tour.
translation: When Lord Nityānanda returned to Bengal to preach the cult of bhakti, love of Godhead, He began touring all over the country.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.149
description: For two purposes-to spread the cult of bhakti and to defeat and subdue the atheists-Lord Nityānanda, the most dedicated devotee of the Lord, moved throughout the country.
text:
> prema-pracāraṇa āra pāṣaṇḍa-dalana
> dui-kārye avadhūta karena bhramaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:p:pracāraṇa]]---preaching the cult of //bhakti//; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:p:pāṣaṇḍa]]-[[synonyms:d:dalana]]---subduing atheistic men; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:k:kārye]]---with two kinds of activities; [[synonyms:a:avadhūta]]---the great devotee and mendicant; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---does; [[synonyms:b:bhramaṇa]]---touring.
translation: For two purposes-to spread the cult of bhakti and to defeat and subdue the atheists-Lord Nityānanda, the most dedicated devotee of the Lord, moved throughout the country.
purport:
As stated in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:4:8|(Bg. 4.8)]]:

> paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ-
> vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām
> dharma-saṁsthāpanārthāya
> sambhavāmi yuge yuge

Lord Kṛṣṇa appears in every millennium for two purposes, namely to deliver the devotees and kill the nondevotees. His devotees also have two similar purposes-to preach the //bhakti// cult of Kṛṣṇa consciousness and defeat all kinds of agnostics and atheistic demons. Nityānanda Prabhu carried out the order of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in this way, and those who strictly follow Nityānanda Prabhu perform the same activities. There are two classes of devotees. One is called //goṣṭhyānandī,// and the other is called //bhajanānandī.// A devotee who does not preach but always engages in devotional activities is called a //bhajanānandī,// whereas a devotee who not only is expert in devotional service but who also preaches the cult of //bhakti// and defeats all kinds of agnostics is called a //goṣṭhyānandī.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.15
description: "Dear Lord, You are a learned teacher. Why then don't You consider that this boy is the son of a widowed brāhmaṇī? Why are You so affectionate to him?
text:
> paṇḍita hañā mane kene vicāra nā kara?
> rāṇḍī brāhmaṇīra bālake prīti kene kara?
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being a learned teacher; [[synonyms:m:mane]]---in the mind; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:v:vicāra]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---do You not consider; [[synonyms:r:rāṇḍī]] [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇīra]]---of a widowed wife of a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:b:bālake]]---unto the son; [[synonyms:p:prīti]]---affection; [[synonyms:k:kene]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---why do You show.
translation: "Dear Lord, You are a learned teacher. Why then don't You consider that this boy is the son of a widowed brāhmaṇī? Why are You so affectionate to him?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.150
description: Lord Nityānanda, who is omniscient because He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, came to the house of Rāmacandra Khān and sat down on the altar of the Durgā-maṇḍapa.
text:
> sarvajña nityānanda āilā tāra ghare
> āsiyā vasilā durgā-maṇḍapa-upare
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:j:jña]]---omniscient; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---//came//; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at his house; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:v:vasilā]]---sat down; [[synonyms:d:durgā]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇḍapa]]-[[synonyms:u:upare]]---on the altar of the Durgā-maṇḍapa.
translation: Lord Nityānanda, who is omniscient because He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, came to the house of Rāmacandra Khān and sat down on the altar of the Durgā-maṇḍapa.
purport: Well-to-do Hindu gentlemen constructed their houses with a place called the Durgā-maṇḍapa for the worship of the goddess Durgā. There they generally held worship of the goddess every year in the month of Āśvina (October). Rāmacandra Khān possessed such a Durgā-maṇḍapa at his residence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.151
description: When the Durgā-maṇḍapa and courtyard were filled with crowds of men, Rāmacandra Khān, who was inside the house, sent his servant to Lord Nityānanda.
text:
> aneka loka-jana saṅge aṅgana bharila
> bhitara haite rāmacandra sevaka pāṭhāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aneka]]---many; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---crowds of people; [[synonyms:s:saṅge]]---accompanied by; [[synonyms:a:aṅgana]]---the courtyard; [[synonyms:b:bharila]]---became filled; [[synonyms:b:bhitara]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from inside; [[synonyms:r:rāmacandra]]---Rāmacandra Khān; [[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---servant; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāila]]---sent.
translation: When the Durgā-maṇḍapa and courtyard were filled with crowds of men, Rāmacandra Khān, who was inside the house, sent his servant to Lord Nityānanda.
purport: In those days, and also even now, the palatial buildings of respectable people, especially in the villages of Bengal, were divided into two parts. The inside part was especially meant for the family, and the ladies would live there unexposed to men. That part was called the //bhitara-bāḍi,// or inside house. In the outside house, or //bahir-bāḍi,// the respectable gentleman received visitors and kept his business office. The Durgā-maṇḍapa would be part of the outside house. Thus when Lord Nityānanda entered the outside house, Rāmacandra Khān was in the inside house with the members of his family. When Nityānanda Prabhu arrived, Rāmacandra Khān did not receive Him personally but sent his servant to inform Him indirectly to go away.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.152
description: The servant informed Lord Nityānanda, "My dear sir, Rāmacandra Khān has sent me to accommodate You in some common man's house.
text:
> sevaka bale---"gosāñi, more pāṭhāila khāṅna
> gṛhasthera ghare tomāya diba vāsā-sthāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sevaka]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---the servant said; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---my dear Lord; [[synonyms:m:more]]---me; [[synonyms:p:pāṭhāila]]---sent; [[synonyms:k:khāṅna]]---Rāmacandra Khān; [[synonyms:g:gṛhasthera]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at the house of some ordinary person; [[synonyms:t:tomāya]]---unto You; [[synonyms:d:diba]]---I shall give; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---residential place.
translation: The servant informed Lord Nityānanda, "My dear sir, Rāmacandra Khān has sent me to accommodate You in some common man's house.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.153
description: "You might go to the house of a milkman, for the cow shed is spacious, whereas the space here in the Durgā-maṇḍapa is insufficient because You have many followers with You."
text:
> goyālāra gośālā haya atyanta vistāra
> ihāṅ saṅkīrṇa-sthala, tomāra manuṣya---apāra"
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:goyālāra]]---of a milkman; [[synonyms:g:go]]-[[synonyms:ś:śālā]]---cow shed; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:a:atyanta]]---very; [[synonyms:v:vistāra]]---spacious; [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:s:saṅkīrṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:sthala]]---very narrow place; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:m:manuṣya]]---adherents; [[synonyms:a:apāra]]---unlimited.
translation: "You might go to the house of a milkman, for the cow shed is spacious, whereas the space here in the Durgā-maṇḍapa is insufficient because You have many followers with You."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.154
description: When Nityānanda Prabhu heard this order from the servant of Rāmacandra Khān, He became very angry and came out. Laughing very loudly, He spoke as follows.
text:
> bhitare āchilā, śuni' krodhe bāhirilā
> aṭṭa aṭṭa hāsi' gosāñi kahite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhitare]] [[synonyms:ā:āchilā]]---was staying inside; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:k:krodhe]]---in anger; [[synonyms:b:bāhirilā]]---came out; [[synonyms:a:aṭṭa]] [[synonyms:a:aṭṭa]]---very loudly; [[synonyms:h:hāsi']]---laughing; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:k:kahite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to say.
translation: When Nityānanda Prabhu heard this order from the servant of Rāmacandra Khān, He became very angry and came out. Laughing very loudly, He spoke as follows.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.155
description: "Rāmacandra Khān has spoken rightly. This place is unfit for Me. It is fit for cow-killing meateaters."
text:
> "satya kahe,---ei ghara mora yogya naya
> mleccha go-vadha kare, tāra yogya haya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:satya]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Rāmacandra Khān says rightly; [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:g:ghara]]---this house; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---for Me; [[synonyms:y:yogya]] [[synonyms:n:naya]]---is not fit; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]---the meateaters; [[synonyms:g:go]]-[[synonyms:v:vadha]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---who kill cows; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---for them; [[synonyms:y:yogya]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---it is fit.
translation: "Rāmacandra Khān has spoken rightly. This place is unfit for Me. It is fit for cow-killing meateaters."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.156
description: Having said this, Lord Nityānanda stood up and left in an angry mood. To chastise Rāmacandra Khān, He did not even stay in that village.
text:
> eta bali' krodhe gosāñi uṭhiyā calilā
> tāre daṇḍa dite se grāme nā rahilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:k:krodhe]]---in anger; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:u:uṭhiyā]] [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---got up and left; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---him; [[synonyms:d:daṇḍa]] [[synonyms:d:dite]]---to chastise; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in the village; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---did not stay.
translation: Having said this, Lord Nityānanda stood up and left in an angry mood. To chastise Rāmacandra Khān, He did not even stay in that village.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.157
description: Rāmacandra Khān ordered the servant to dig up the dirt in the place where Nityānanda Prabhu had sat.
text:
> ihāṅ rāmacandra khāna sevake ājñā dila
> gosāñi yāhāṅ vasilā, tāra māṭī khodāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ihāṅ]]---here; [[synonyms:r:rāmacandra]] [[synonyms:k:khāna]]---Rāmacandra Khān; [[synonyms:s:sevake]]---to the servant; [[synonyms:ā:ājñā]] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---ordered; [[synonyms:g:gosāñi]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---where; [[synonyms:v:vasilā]]---sat down; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---of that place; [[synonyms:m:māṭī]]---earth; [[synonyms:k:khodāila]]---caused to dig.
translation: Rāmacandra Khān ordered the servant to dig up the dirt in the place where Nityānanda Prabhu had sat.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.158
description: To purify the Durgā-maṇḍapa temple and the courtyard, Rāmacandra Khān sprinkled and smeared it with water mixed with cow dung, but still his mind was unsatisfied.
text:
> gomaya-jale lepilā saba mandira-prāṅgaṇa
> tabu rāmacandrera mana nā haila parasanna
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:go]]-[[synonyms:m:maya]]-[[synonyms:j:jale]]---with water mixed with cow dung; [[synonyms:l:lepilā]]---smeared; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:m:mandira]]---the Durgā-maṇḍapa temple; [[synonyms:p:prāṅgaṇa]]---the courtyard; [[synonyms:t:tabu]]---still; [[synonyms:r:rāmacandrera]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---the mind of Rāmacandra Khān; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haila]] [[synonyms:p:parasanna]]---was not happy.
translation: To purify the Durgā-maṇḍapa temple and the courtyard, Rāmacandra Khān sprinkled and smeared it with water mixed with cow dung, but still his mind was unsatisfied.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.159
description: Rāmacandra Khān's business was questionable, for he tried to avoid paying income tax to the government. Therefore the government's minister of finance was angry and came to his residence.
text:
> dasyu-vṛtti kare rāmacandra rājāre nā deya kara
> kruddha hañā mleccha ujira āila tāra ghara
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dasyu]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛtti]]---the business of a thief; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:r:rāmacandra]]---Rāmacandra; [[synonyms:r:rājāre]]---to the government; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---does not; [[synonyms:d:deya]]---pay; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---tax; [[synonyms:k:kruddha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being angry; [[synonyms:m:mleccha]]---the Mohammedan; [[synonyms:u:ujira]]---minister; [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:g:ghara]]---to his house.
translation: Rāmacandra Khān's business was questionable, for he tried to avoid paying income tax to the government. Therefore the government's minister of finance was angry and came to his residence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.16
description: "Although the boy's mother is completely austere and chaste, she has one natural fault-she is a very beautiful young girl.
text:
> yadyapi brāhmaṇī sei tapasvinī satī
> tathāpi tāhāra doṣa---sundarī yuvatī
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yadyapi]]---although; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇī]]---wife of a //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:t:tapasvinī]]---austere; [[synonyms:s:satī]]---chaste; [[synonyms:t:tathāpi]]---still; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---her; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---fault; [[synonyms:s:sundarī]]---very beautiful; [[synonyms:y:yuvatī]]---young girl.
translation: "Although the boy's mother is completely austere and chaste, she has one natural fault-she is a very beautiful young girl.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.160
description: The Mohammedan minister made his residence in the Durgā-maṇḍapa of Rāmacandra Khān. He killed a cow and cooked the meat at that very place.
text:
> āsi' sei durgā-maṇḍape vāsā kaila
> avadhya vadha kari' māṁsa se-ghare rāndhāila
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āsi']]---coming; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:d:durgā]]-[[synonyms:m:maṇḍape]]---at that very place of the Durgā-maṇḍapa; [[synonyms:v:vāsā]] [[synonyms:k:kaila]]---made his residence; [[synonyms:a:avadhya]]---a cow or calf, which is not to be killed; [[synonyms:v:vadha]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---killing; [[synonyms:m:māṁsa]]---meat; [[synonyms:s:se]]-[[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in that place; [[synonyms:r:rāndhāila]]---cooked.
translation: The Mohammedan minister made his residence in the Durgā-maṇḍapa of Rāmacandra Khān. He killed a cow and cooked the meat at that very place.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.161
description: He arrested Rāmacandra Khān, along with his wife and sons, and then he continuously plundered the house and village for three days.
text:
> strī-putra-sahita rāmacandrere bāndhiyā
> tāra ghara-grāma luṭe tina-dina rahiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:strī]]-[[synonyms:p:putra]]---his wife and children; [[synonyms:s:sahita]]---with; [[synonyms:r:rāmacandrere]] [[synonyms:b:bāndhiyā]]---arresting Rāmacandra Khān; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his; [[synonyms:g:ghara]]-[[synonyms:g:grāma]]---house and village; [[synonyms:l:luṭe]]---plundered; [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]] [[synonyms:r:rahiyā]]---staying three days.
translation: He arrested Rāmacandra Khān, along with his wife and sons, and then he continuously plundered the house and village for three days.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.162
description: In that very room he cooked the flesh of a cow for three consecutive days. Then the next day he left, accompanied by his followers.
text:
> sei ghare tina dina kare amedhya randhana
> āra dina sabā lañā karilā gamana
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---in that room; [[synonyms:t:tina]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---for three days; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:a:amedhya]] [[synonyms:r:randhana]]---cooking the flesh of a cow; [[synonyms:ā:āra]] [[synonyms:d:dina]]---the next day; [[synonyms:s:sabā]] [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---accompanied by his followers; [[synonyms:k:karilā]] [[synonyms:g:gamana]]---left.
translation: In that very room he cooked the flesh of a cow for three consecutive days. Then the next day he left, accompanied by his followers.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.163
description: The Mohammedan minister took away Rāmacandra Khān's position, wealth and followers. For many days the village remained deserted.
text:
> jāti-dhana-jana khānera sakala la-ila
> bahu-dina paryanta grāma ujāḍa rahila
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jāti]]---birthright; [[synonyms:d:dhana]]---riches; [[synonyms:j:jana]]---followers; [[synonyms:k:khānera]]---of Rāmacandra Khān; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---everything; [[synonyms:l:la]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---he took away; [[synonyms:b:bahu]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---a long time; [[synonyms:p:paryanta]]---for; [[synonyms:g:grāma]]---the village; [[synonyms:u:ujāḍa]] [[synonyms:r:rahila]]---remained deserted.
translation: The Mohammedan minister took away Rāmacandra Khān's position, wealth and followers. For many days the village remained deserted.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.164
description: Wherever an advanced devotee is insulted, for one man's fault the entire town or place is afflicted.
text:
> mahāntera apamāna ye deśa-grāme haya
> eka janāra doṣe saba deśa ujāḍaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mahāntera]]---of persons who are highly advanced in spiritual life; [[synonyms:a:apamāna]]---disrespect; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:d:deśa]]-[[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in which country or village; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:e:eka]] [[synonyms:j:janāra]]---of one man; [[synonyms:d:doṣe]]---for the fault; [[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:d:deśa]]---the whole country; [[synonyms:u:ujāḍaya]]---becomes afflicted.
translation: Wherever an advanced devotee is insulted, for one man's fault the entire town or place is afflicted.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.165
description: Haridāsa Ṭhākura walked until he came to the village known as Cāndapura. There he stayed at the house of Balarāma Ācārya.
text:
> haridāsa-ṭhākura cali' āilā cāndapure
> āsiyā rahilā balarāma-ācāryera ghare
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:c:cali']]---walking; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:c:cāndapure]]---in the village known as Cāndapura; [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:r:rahilā]]---remained; [[synonyms:b:balarāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācāryera]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at the residence of Balarāma Ācārya
translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura walked until he came to the village known as Cāndapura. There he stayed at the house of Balarāma Ācārya.
purport: The village of Cāndapura is situated near the confluence of the rivers Ganges and Yamunā at Saptagrāma in the district of Huglī. Cāndapura is just east of the house of the two brothers Hiraṇya and Govardhana, the father and uncle of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī. In Cāndapura lived Balarāma Ācārya and Yadunandana Ācārya, the priests of these two personalities, and when Haridāsa Ṭhākura went there he lived with them. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that the name of this village was later changed to Kṛṣṇapura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.166
description: Hiraṇya and Govardhana were the two governmental treasurers in that division of the country. Their priest was named Balarāma Ācārya.
text:
> hiraṇya, govardhana---dui mulukera majumadāra
> tāra purohita---'balarāma' nāma tāṅra
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hiraṇya]]---Hiraṇya; [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]---Govardhana; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:m:mulukera]]---of that country; [[synonyms:m:majumadāra]]---treasurers of the government; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---their; [[synonyms:p:purohita]]---priest; [[synonyms:b:balarāma]]---Balarāma; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---name; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his.
translation: Hiraṇya and Govardhana were the two governmental treasurers in that division of the country. Their priest was named Balarāma Ācārya.
purport: The word //majumadāra// refers to a treasurer who keeps accounts of revenue.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.167
description: Balarāma Ācārya, being favored by Haridāsa Ṭhākura, was very attached to him. Therefore he kept Haridāsa Ṭhākura in the village with great care and attention.
text:
> haridāsera kṛpā-pātra, tāte bhakti-māne
> yatna kari' ṭhākurere rākhilā sei grāme
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsera]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---favored by Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:t:tāte]]---therefore; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:m:māne]]---a great devotee of Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:y:yatna]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---with great care and attention; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākurere]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:r:rākhilā]]---kept; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:g:grāme]]---in the village.
translation: Balarāma Ācārya, being favored by Haridāsa Ṭhākura, was very attached to him. Therefore he kept Haridāsa Ṭhākura in the village with great care and attention.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.168
description: In the village, Haridāsa Ṭhākura was given a solitary thatched cottage, where he performed the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra He accepted prasāda at the house of Balarāma Ācārya.
text:
> nirjana parṇa-śālāya karena kīrtana
> balarāma-ācārya-gṛhe bhikṣā-nirvāhaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirjana]]---solitary; [[synonyms:p:parṇa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śālāya]]---in a thatched cottage; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---performs; [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mantra//; [[synonyms:b:balarāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:g:gṛhe]]---at the house of Balarāma Ācārya; [[synonyms:b:bhikṣā]]-[[synonyms:n:nirvāhaṇa]]---accepting alms.
translation: In the village, Haridāsa Ṭhākura was given a solitary thatched cottage, where he performed the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra He accepted prasāda at the house of Balarāma Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.169
description: Raghunātha dāsa, who was the son of Hiraṇya Majumadāra and was later to become Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, was at that time a boy engaged in study. He came to see Haridāsa Ṭhākura daily.
text:
> raghunātha-dāsa bālaka karena adhyayana
> haridāsa-ṭhākurere yāi' karena darśana
synonyms: [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---Raghunātha dāsa; [[synonyms:b:bālaka]]---a boy; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:a:adhyayana]]---was engaged in study; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākurere]]---to Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:y:yāi']]---going; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---used to see.
translation: Raghunātha dāsa, who was the son of Hiraṇya Majumadāra and was later to become Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, was at that time a boy engaged in study. He came to see Haridāsa Ṭhākura daily.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.17
description: "And You, my dear Lord, are a handsome, attractive young man. Therefore certainly people will whisper about You. Why should You give them such a opportunity?"
text:
> tumi-ha---parama yuvā, parama sundara
> lokera kāṇākāṇi-vāte deha avasara"
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]]-[[synonyms:h:ha]]---You also; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:y:yuvā]]---young man; [[synonyms:p:parama]] [[synonyms:s:sundara]]---very beautiful; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of the people in general; [[synonyms:k:kāṇākāṇi]]---whispering; [[synonyms:v:vāte]]---talks; [[synonyms:d:deha]] [[synonyms:a:avasara]]---You are giving an opportunity for.
translation: "And You, my dear Lord, are a handsome, attractive young man. Therefore certainly people will whisper about You. Why should You give them such a opportunity?"
purport: As a simple and staunch devotee of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Dāmodara Paṇḍita could not tolerate criticism of the Lord, but unfortunately he himself was criticizing Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in his own way. The Lord could understand that it was because of Dāmodara Paṇḍita's simplicity that he impudently dared criticize Him. Nevertheless, such behavior by a devotee is not very good.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.170
description: Naturally Haridāsa Ṭhākura was merciful toward him, and because of the merciful benediction of this Vaiṣṇava, he later attained the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's lotus feet.
text:
> haridāsa kṛpā kare tāṅhāra upare
> sei kṛpā 'kāraṇa' haila caitanya pāibāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Ṭhākura Haridāsa; [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---shows mercy; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]] [[synonyms:u:upare]]---upon him; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---that mercy; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]]---the cause; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---became; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:p:pāibāre]]---to attain.
translation: Naturally Haridāsa Ṭhākura was merciful toward him, and because of the merciful benediction of this Vaiṣṇava, he later attained the shelter of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's lotus feet.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.171
description: At the residence of Hiraṇya and Govardhana, discourses took place by which Haridāsa Ṭhākura was glorified. O devotees, please listen to that wonderful story.
text:
> tāhāṅ yaiche haila haridāsera mahimā kathana
> vyākhyāna,---adbhuta kathā śuna, bhakta-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---at that place; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---just as; [[synonyms:h:haila]]---there was; [[synonyms:h:haridāsera]]---of Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---glories; [[synonyms:k:kathana]]---discussion; [[synonyms:v:vyākhyāna]]---discourse; [[synonyms:a:adbhuta]]---wonderful; [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---incident; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---hear; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---O devotees.
translation: At the residence of Hiraṇya and Govardhana, discourses took place by which Haridāsa Ṭhākura was glorified. O devotees, please listen to that wonderful story.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.172
description: One day Balarāma Ācārya requested Haridāsa Ṭhākura with great humility to come to the assembly of the Majumadāras, Hiraṇya and Govardhana. Thus Balarāma Ācārya went there with Haridāsa Ṭhākura.
text:
> eka-dina balarāma minati kariyā
> majumadārera sabhāya āilā ṭhākure lañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:b:balarāma]]---Balarāma Ācārya; [[synonyms:m:minati]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---in great humility; [[synonyms:m:majumadārera]]---of the Majumadāras, Hiraṇya and Govardhana; [[synonyms:s:sabhāya]]---at the assembly; [[synonyms:ā:āilā]]---came; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākure]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---taking with him.
translation: One day Balarāma Ācārya requested Haridāsa Ṭhākura with great humility to come to the assembly of the Majumadāras, Hiraṇya and Govardhana. Thus Balarāma Ācārya went there with Haridāsa Ṭhākura.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.173
description: Seeing Haridāsa Ṭhākura, the two brothers immediately stood up and fell at his lotus feet. Then with great respect they offered him a place to sit.
text:
> ṭhākura dekhi' dui bhāi kailā abhyutthāna
> pāya paḍi' āsana dilā kariyā sammāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]] [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---the two brothers; [[synonyms:k:kailā]] [[synonyms:a:abhyutthāna]]---stood up; [[synonyms:p:pāya]] [[synonyms:p:paḍi']]---falling at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:ā:āsana]] [[synonyms:d:dilā]]---offered a sitting place; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:s:sammāna]]---with great respect.
translation: Seeing Haridāsa Ṭhākura, the two brothers immediately stood up and fell at his lotus feet. Then with great respect they offered him a place to sit.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.174
description: In that assembly were many learned scholars, brāhmaṇas and respectable gentlemen. The two brothers Hiraṇya and Govardhana were also greatly learned.
text:
> aneka paṇḍita sabhāya, brāhmaṇa, sajjana
> dui bhāi mahā-paṇḍita---hiraṇya, govardhana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aneka]] [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---many learned scholars; [[synonyms:s:sabhāya]]---in that assembly; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---//brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:s:sat]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---respectable gentlemen; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---the two brothers; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---very learned scholars; [[synonyms:h:hiraṇya]]---Hiraṇya; [[synonyms:g:govardhana]]---Govardhana.
translation: In that assembly were many learned scholars, brāhmaṇas and respectable gentlemen. The two brothers Hiraṇya and Govardhana were also greatly learned.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.175
description: Everyone there began to speak of Haridāsa Ṭhākura's great qualities as if they had five mouths. Hearing this, both brothers were extremely happy.
text:
> haridāsera guṇa sabe kahe pañca-mukhe
> śuniyā ta' dui bhāi pāilā baḍa sukhe
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsera]]---of Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---the qualities; [[synonyms:s:sabe]]---all of them; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---began to speak; [[synonyms:p:pañca]]-[[synonyms:m:mukhe]]---as if speaking with five mouths; [[synonyms:ś:śuniyā]]---hearing; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:d:dui]] [[synonyms:b:bhāi]]---the two brothers; [[synonyms:p:pāilā]]---got; [[synonyms:b:baḍa]] [[synonyms:s:sukhe]]---very great happiness.
translation: Everyone there began to speak of Haridāsa Ṭhākura's great qualities as if they had five mouths. Hearing this, both brothers were extremely happy.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.176
description: It was mentioned in the assembly that Haridāsa Ṭhākura chanted the holy names of Kṛṣṇa 300,000 times a day. Thus all the learned scholars began to discuss the glories of the holy name.
text:
> tina-lakṣa nāma ṭhākura karena kīrtana
> nāmera mahimā uṭhāila paṇḍita-gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tina]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---300,000; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---holy names of the Lord; [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākura]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:k:kīrtana]]---used to chant; [[synonyms:n:nāmera]]---of the holy name; [[synonyms:m:mahimā]]---glories; [[synonyms:u:uṭhāila]]---raised; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---all the learned scholars.
translation: It was mentioned in the assembly that Haridāsa Ṭhākura chanted the holy names of Kṛṣṇa 300,000 times a day. Thus all the learned scholars began to discuss the glories of the holy name.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.177
description: Some of them said, "By chanting the holy name of the Lord, one is freed from the reactions of all sinful life." Others said, "Simply by chanting the holy name of the Lord, a living being is liberated from material bondage."
text:
> keha bale,---'nāma haite haya pāpa-kṣaya'
> keha bale,---'nāma haite jīvera mokṣa haya'
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---some of them said; [[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]-[[synonyms:k:kṣaya]]---disappearance of all reactions to sinful activities; [[synonyms:k:keha]] [[synonyms:b:bale]]---some of them said; [[synonyms:n:nāma]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---by chanting the holy name; [[synonyms:j:jīvera]]---of the living entities; [[synonyms:m:mokṣa]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is liberation.
translation: Some of them said, "By chanting the holy name of the Lord, one is freed from the reactions of all sinful life." Others said, "Simply by chanting the holy name of the Lord, a living being is liberated from material bondage."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.178
description: Haridāsa Ṭhākura protested, "These two benedictions are not the true result of chanting the holy name. By actually chanting the holy name without offenses, one awakens his ecstatic love for the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> haridāsa kahena,---"nāmera ei dui phala naya
> nāmera phale kṛṣṇa-pade prema upajaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura replied; [[synonyms:n:nāmera]]---of chanting the holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---these; [[synonyms:d:dui]]---two; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---results; [[synonyms:n:naya]]---are not; [[synonyms:n:nāmera]] [[synonyms:p:phale]]---by the result of chanting the holy name; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:prema]] [[synonyms:u:upajaya]]---awakening of ecstatic love.
translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura protested, "These two benedictions are not the true result of chanting the holy name. By actually chanting the holy name without offenses, one awakens his ecstatic love for the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.179
description: "When a person is actually advanced and takes pleasure in chanting the holy name of the Lord, who is very dear to him, he is agitated and loudly chants the holy name. He also laughs, cries, becomes agitated and chants just like a madman, not caring for outsiders.'
text:
> evaṁ-vrataḥ sva-priya-nāma-kīrtyā
> jātānurāgo druta-citta uccaiḥ
> hasaty atho roditi rauti gāyaty
> unmādavan nṛtyati loka-bāhyaḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:evam]]-[[synonyms:v:vrataḥ]]---when one thus engages in the vow to chant and dance; [[synonyms:s:sva]]---own; [[synonyms:p:priya]]---very dear; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---holy name; [[synonyms:k:kīrtyā]]---by chanting; [[synonyms:j:jāta]]---in this way develops; [[synonyms:a:anurāgaḥ]]---attachment; [[synonyms:d:druta]]-[[synonyms:c:cittaḥ]]---very eagerly; [[synonyms:u:uccaiḥ]]---loudly; [[synonyms:h:hasati]]---laughs; [[synonyms:a:atho]]---also; [[synonyms:r:roditi]]---cries; [[synonyms:r:rauti]]---becomes agitated; [[synonyms:g:gāyati]]---chants; [[synonyms:u:unmāda]]-[[synonyms:v:vat]]---like a madman; [[synonyms:n:nṛtyati]]---dances; [[synonyms:l:loka]]-[[synonyms:b:bāhyaḥ]]---not caring for outsiders.
translation: "When a person is actually advanced and takes pleasure in chanting the holy name of the Lord, who is very dear to him, he is agitated and loudly chants the holy name. He also laughs, cries, becomes agitated and chants just like a madman, not caring for outsiders.'
purport: For an explanation of this verse (//Bhāg.// 11.2.40) one may consult Chapter Seven, text 94, of the //Ādi-līlā.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.18
description: Having said this, Dāmodara Paṇḍita became silent. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu smiled, pleased within Himself, and considered the impudence of Dāmodara Paṇḍita.
text:
> eta bali' dāmodara mauna ha-ilā
> antare santoṣa prabhu hāsi' vicārilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]---Dāmodara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:m:mauna]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ilā]]---became silent; [[synonyms:a:antare]]---within Himself; [[synonyms:s:santoṣa]]---pleased; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:h:hāsi']]---smiling; [[synonyms:v:vicārilā]]---considered.
translation: Having said this, Dāmodara Paṇḍita became silent. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu smiled, pleased within Himself, and considered the impudence of Dāmodara Paṇḍita.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.180
description: "Liberation and extinction of the reactions of sinful life are two concomitant by-products of chanting the holy name of the Lord. An example is found in the gleams of morning sunlight.
text:
> ānuṣaṅgika phala nāmera---'mukti', 'pāpa-nāśa'
> tāhāra dṛṣṭānta yaiche sūryera prakāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ānuṣaṅgika]]---concomitant; [[synonyms:p:phala]]---result; [[synonyms:n:nāmera]]---of the holy name; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---extinction of the resultant actions of sinful life; [[synonyms:t:tāhāra]]---of that; [[synonyms:d:dṛṣṭānta]]---example; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---as; [[synonyms:s:sūryera]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---light of the sun.
translation: "Liberation and extinction of the reactions of sinful life are two concomitant by-products of chanting the holy name of the Lord. An example is found in the gleams of morning sunlight.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.181
description: "As the rising sun immediately dissipates all the world's darkness, which is deep like an ocean, so the holy name of the Lord, if chanted once without offenses, can dissipate all the reactions of a living being's sinful life. All glories to that holy name of the Lord, which is auspicious for the entire world.' "
text:
> aṁhaḥ saṁharad akhilaṁ sakṛd
> udayād eva sakala-lokasya
> taraṇir iva timira-jaladhiṁ
> jayati jagan-maṅgalaṁ harer nāma
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aṁhaḥ]]---the resultant action of sinful life, which causes material bondage; [[synonyms:s:saṁharat]]---completely eradicating; [[synonyms:a:akhilam]]---all; [[synonyms:s:sakṛt]]---once only; [[synonyms:u:udayāt]]---by rising; [[synonyms:e:eva]]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:sakala]]---all; [[synonyms:l:lokasya]]---of the people of the world; [[synonyms:t:taraṇiḥ]]---the sun; [[synonyms:i:iva]]---like; [[synonyms:t:timira]]---of darkness; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:d:dhim]]---the ocean; [[synonyms:j:jayati]]---all glories to; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:m:maṅgalam]]---auspicious for the whole world; [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of the Lord. name of the Lord.
translation: "As the rising sun immediately dissipates all the world's darkness, which is deep like an ocean, so the holy name of the Lord, if chanted once without offenses, can dissipate all the reactions of a living being's sinful life. All glories to that holy name of the Lord, which is auspicious for the entire world.' "
purport: This verse is found in the //Padyāvalī// (16).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.182
description: After reciting this verse, Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "O learned scholars, please explain the meaning of this verse." But the audience requested Haridāsa Ṭhākura, "It is better for you to explain the meaning of this important verse."
text:
> ei ślokera artha kara paṇḍitera gaṇa"
> sabe kahe,---'tumi kaha artha-vivaraṇa'
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:ei]] [[synonyms:ś:ślokera]]---of this verse; [[synonyms:a:artha]]---meaning; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---explain; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍitera]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---O groups of learned scholars; [[synonyms:s:sabe]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---everyone said; [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:k:kaha]]---you speak; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:v:vivaraṇa]]---the meaning and explanation.
translation: After reciting this verse, Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "O learned scholars, please explain the meaning of this verse." But the audience requested Haridāsa Ṭhākura, "It is better for you to explain the meaning of this important verse."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.183
description: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "As the sun begins to rise, even before visible it dissipates the darkness of night.
text:
> haridāsa kahena,---"yaiche sūryera udaya
> udaya nā haite ārambhe tamera haya kṣaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura began to explain; [[synonyms:y:yaiche]]---like; [[synonyms:s:sūryera]] [[synonyms:u:udaya]]---sunrise; [[synonyms:u:udaya]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---although not visible; [[synonyms:ā:ārambhe]]---from the beginning; [[synonyms:t:tamera]]---of darkness; [[synonyms:h:haya]] [[synonyms:k:kṣaya]]---there is dissipation.
translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "As the sun begins to rise, even before visible it dissipates the darkness of night.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.184
description: "With the first glimpse of sunlight, fear of thieves, ghosts and demons immediately disappears, and when the sun is actually visible, everything is manifest, and everyone begins performing his religious activities and regulative duties.
text:
> caura-preta-rākṣasādira bhaya haya nāśa
> udaya haile dharma-karma-ādi parakāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caura]]---thieves; [[synonyms:p:preta]]---ghosts; [[synonyms:r:rākṣasa]]---demons; [[synonyms:ā:ādira]]---of them and others; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---destroyed; [[synonyms:u:udaya]] [[synonyms:h:haile]]---when the sunrise is actually visible; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]-[[synonyms:k:karma]]---all religious activities and regulative principles; [[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---everything; [[synonyms:p:parakāśa]]---becomes manifest.
translation: "With the first glimpse of sunlight, fear of thieves, ghosts and demons immediately disappears, and when the sun is actually visible, everything is manifest, and everyone begins performing his religious activities and regulative duties.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.185
