description: "Similarly, the first hint that offenseless chanting of the Lord's holy name has awakened dissipates the reactions of sinful life immediately. And when one chants the holy name offenselessly, one awakens to service in ecstatic love at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> aiche nāmodayārambhe pāpa-ādira kṣaya
> udaya kaile kṛṣṇa-pade haya premodaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:aiche]]---similarly; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]]---of the appearance of the holy name; [[synonyms:ā:ārambhe]]---by the beginning; [[synonyms:p:pāpa]]---reactions of sinful activities; [[synonyms:ā:ādira]]---of them and others; [[synonyms:k:kṣaya]]---dissipation; [[synonyms:u:udaya]] [[synonyms:k:kaile]]---when there is actually awakening of offenseless chanting; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:h:haya]] [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:u:udaya]]---there is awakening of ecstatic love.
translation: "Similarly, the first hint that offenseless chanting of the Lord's holy name has awakened dissipates the reactions of sinful life immediately. And when one chants the holy name offenselessly, one awakens to service in ecstatic love at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.186
description: "Liberation is the insignificant result derived from a glimpse of awakening of offenseless chanting of the holy name.
text: > mukti' tuccha-phala haya nāmābhāsa haite
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:'mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:t:tuccha]]-[[synonyms:p:phala]]---insignificant result; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāsa]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from a glimpse of awakening of offenseless chanting of the holy name.
translation: "Liberation is the insignificant result derived from a glimpse of awakening of offenseless chanting of the holy name.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.187
description: "While dying, Ajāmila chanted the holy name of the Lord, intending to call his son Nārāyaṇa. Nevertheless, he attained the spiritual world. What then to speak of those who chant the holy name with faith and reverence?'
text:
> mriyamāṇo harer nāma
> gṛṇan putropacāritam
> ajāmilo 'py agād dhāma
> kim uta śraddhayā gṛṇan
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mriyamāṇaḥ]]---dying; [[synonyms:h:hareḥ]] [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:g:gṛṇan]]---chanting; [[synonyms:p:putra]]-[[synonyms:u:upacāritam]]---though spoken for his son; [[synonyms:a:ajāmilaḥ]]---Ajāmila; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:a:agāt]]---attained; [[synonyms:d:dhāma]]---the spiritual world; [[synonyms:k:kim]] [[synonyms:u:uta]]---what to speak of; [[synonyms:ś:śraddhayā]]---with faith and reverence; [[synonyms:g:gṛṇan]]---chanting.
translation: "While dying, Ajāmila chanted the holy name of the Lord, intending to call his son Nārāyaṇa. Nevertheless, he attained the spiritual world. What then to speak of those who chant the holy name with faith and reverence?'
purport: This is a verse from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:6:2:49|(6.2.49)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.188
description: "Liberation, which is unacceptable for a pure devotee, is always offered by Kṛṣṇa without difficulty.
text: > ye mukti bhakta nā laya, se kṛṣṇa cāhe dite"
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:ye]]---which; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]---a devotee; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:l:laya]]---does not take; [[synonyms:s:se]]---that; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:c:cāhe]] [[synonyms:d:dite]]---wants to offer.
translation: "Liberation, which is unacceptable for a pure devotee, is always offered by Kṛṣṇa without difficulty.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.189
description: "My devotees do not accept sālokya, sārṣṭi, sārūpya, sāmīpya, or oneness with Me-even if I offer these liberations-in preference to serving Me.' "
text:
> sālokya-sārṣṭi-sārūpya-
> sāmīpyaikatvam apy uta
> dīyamānaṁ na gṛhṇanti
> vinā mat-sevanaṁ janāḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sālokya]]---to live on the same planet; [[synonyms:s:sārṣṭi]]---to acquire the same opulence; [[synonyms:s:sārūpya]]---to achieve the same bodily features; [[synonyms:s:sāmīpya]]---to live always near the Supreme Lord; [[synonyms:e:ekatvam]]---to merge into the existence of the Lord; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:u:uta]]---certainly; [[synonyms:d:dīyamānam]]---being offered; [[synonyms:n:na]] [[synonyms:g:gṛhṇanti]]---do not take; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:m:mat]]-[[synonyms:s:sevanam]]---My service; [[synonyms:j:janāḥ]]---the devotees.
translation: "My devotees do not accept sālokya, sārṣṭi, sārūpya, sāmīpya, or oneness with Me-even if I offer these liberations-in preference to serving Me.' "
purport: This verse is spoken by Lord Kapila, an //avatāra// of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:3:29:13|(3.29.13)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.19
description: "This impudence is also a sign of pure love for Me. I have no other intimate friend like Dāmodara Paṇḍita."
text:
> "ihāre kahiye śuddha-premera taraṅga
> dāmodara-sama mora nāhi 'antaraṅga' "
synonyms: [[synonyms:i:ihāre]]---such behavior; [[synonyms:k:kahiye]]---I can say; [[synonyms:ś:śuddha]]-[[synonyms:p:premerataraṅga]]---waves of pure devotional service; [[synonyms:d:dāmodara]]-[[synonyms:s:sama]]---like Dāmodara; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---My; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:a:antaraṅga]]---intimate friend.
translation: "This impudence is also a sign of pure love for Me. I have no other intimate friend like Dāmodara Paṇḍita."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.190
description: At the house of Hiraṇya and Govardhana Majumadāra, a person named Gopāla Cakravartī was officially the chief tax collector.
text:
> 'gopāla cakravartī' nāma eka-jana
> majumadārera ghare sei ārindā pradhāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gopāla]] [[synonyms:c:cakravartī]]---Gopāla Cakravartī; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---named; [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:j:jana]]---one person; [[synonyms:m:majumadārera]] [[synonyms:g:ghare]]---at the residence of Hiraṇya and Govardhana Majumadāra; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---he; [[synonyms:ā:ārindā]] [[synonyms:p:pradhāna]]---the chief tax collector.
translation: At the house of Hiraṇya and Govardhana Majumadāra, a person named Gopāla Cakravartī was officially the chief tax collector.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.191
description: This Gopāla Cakravartī lived in Bengal. His duty as chief tax collector was to collect 1,200,000 coins to deposit in the treasury of the emperor.
text:
> gauḍe rahi' pātsāhā-āge ārindā-giri kare
> bāra-lakṣa mudrā sei pātsāra ṭhāñi bhare
synonyms: [[synonyms:g:gauḍe]] [[synonyms:r:rahi']]---living in Bengal; [[synonyms:p:pātsāhā]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---on behalf of the emperor; [[synonyms:ā:ārindā]]-[[synonyms:g:giri]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---acts as the chief tax collector; [[synonyms:b:bāra]]-[[synonyms:l:lakṣa]]---twelve hundred thousand; [[synonyms:m:mudrā]]---coins; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---he; [[synonyms:p:pātsāra]] [[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhāñi]]---for the emperor; [[synonyms:b:bhare]]---collects.
translation: This Gopāla Cakravartī lived in Bengal. His duty as chief tax collector was to collect 1,200,000 coins to deposit in the treasury of the emperor.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.192
description: He had handsome bodily features, and he was learned and youthful, but he could not tolerate the statement that simply by glimpsing the awakening of the Lord's holy name one can attain liberation.
text:
> parama-sundara, paṇḍita, nūtana-yauvana
> nāmābhāse 'mukti' śuni' nā ha-ila sahana
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:parama]]-[[synonyms:s:sundara]]---very beautiful; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---learned; [[synonyms:n:nūtana]]---new; [[synonyms:y:yauvana]]---youth; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāse]]---by the glimpse of awakening of pure chanting of the holy name; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]] [[synonyms:s:sahana]]---could not tolerate.
translation: He had handsome bodily features, and he was learned and youthful, but he could not tolerate the statement that simply by glimpsing the awakening of the Lord's holy name one can attain liberation.
purport: Vaiṣṇavas strictly follow the directions of the //śāstras// regarding how one can be liberated simply by a slight awakening of pure chanting of the holy name. Māyāvādīs cannot tolerate the statements of the //śāstras// about how easily liberation can be achieved, for as stated in //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:12:5|(Bg. 12.5)]], //kleśo 'dhikataras teṣām avyaktāsakta-cetasām:// impersonalists must work hard for many, many births, and only then will they perhaps be liberated. Vaiṣṇavas know that simply by chanting the holy name of the Lord offenselessly, one achieves liberation as a by-product. Thus there is no need to endeavor separately for liberation. Śrīla Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura has said, //muktiḥ svayaṁ mukulitāñjali sevate 'smān:// liberation stands at one's door, ready to render any kind of service, if one is a pure devotee with unflinching faith and reverence. This the Māyāvādīs cannot tolerate. Therefore the //ārindā pradhāna,// chief tax collector, although very learned, handsome and youthful, could not tolerate the statements of Haridāsa Ṭhākura

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.193
description: This young man, Gopāla Cakravartī, became very angry upon hearing the statements of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. He immediately criticized him. "O assembly of learned scholars," he said, "just hear the conclusion of the emotional devotee.
text:
> kruddha hañā bale sei saroṣa vacana
> "bhāvukera siddhānta śuna, paṇḍitera gaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kruddha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---becoming very angry; [[synonyms:b:bale]]---said; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---he; [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:r:roṣa]] [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---angry words; [[synonyms:b:bhāvukera]]---of an emotional person; [[synonyms:s:siddhānta]]---conclusion; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---just hear; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍitera]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---O assembly of learned scholars.
translation: This young man, Gopāla Cakravartī, became very angry upon hearing the statements of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. He immediately criticized him. "O assembly of learned scholars," he said, "just hear the conclusion of the emotional devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.194
description: "After many millions upon millions of births, when one is complete in absolute knowledge, one still may not attain liberation, yet this ma says that one may attain it simply by the awakening of a glimpse of the holy name."
text:
> koṭi-janme brahma-jñāne yei 'mukti' naya
> ei kahe,---nāmābhāse sei 'mukti' haya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:j:janme]]---after millions upon millions of births; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:j:jñāne]]---by absolute knowledge; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---which; [[synonyms:m:mukti]] [[synonyms:n:naya]]---liberation is not possible; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this person; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāse]]---simply by the awakening of a glimpse of the pure chanting of the holy name; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes possible.
translation: "After many millions upon millions of births, when one is complete in absolute knowledge, one still may not attain liberation, yet this ma says that one may attain it simply by the awakening of a glimpse of the holy name."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.195
text:
> haridāsa kahena,---kene karaha saṁśaya?
> śāstre kahe,---nāmābhāsa-mātre 'mukti' haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura said; [[synonyms:k:kene]]---why; [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:s:saṁśaya]]---are you doubtful; [[synonyms:ś:śāstre]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---it is stated in the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāsamātre]]---simply by a glimpse of the chanting of the holy name; [[synonyms:m:mukti]] [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is liberation.
translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "Why are you doubtful? The revealed scriptures say that one can attain liberation simply by a glimpse of offenseless chanting of the holy name.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.196
description: "For a devotee who enjoys the transcendental bliss of devotional service, liberation is most insignificant. Therefore pure devotees never desire to achieve liberation.
text:
> bhakti-sukha-āge 'mukti' ati-tuccha haya
> ataeva bhakta-gaṇa 'mukti' nāhi laya
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]-[[synonyms:s:sukha]]---transcendental bliss derived from devotional service; [[synonyms:ā:āge]]---before; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:a:ati]]-[[synonyms:t:tuccha]]---extremely insignificant; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:a:ataeva]]---therefore; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---pure devotees; [[synonyms:m:mukti]]---liberation; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:l:laya]]---do not accept.
translation: "For a devotee who enjoys the transcendental bliss of devotional service, liberation is most insignificant. Therefore pure devotees never desire to achieve liberation.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.197
description: "My dear Lord, O master of the universe, since I have directly seen You, my transcendental bliss has taken the shape of a great ocean. Being situated in that ocean, I now realize all other so-called happiness, including even brahmānanda, to be like the water contained in the hoofprint of a calf.' "
text:
> tvat-sākṣātkaraṇāhlāda-
> viśuddhābdhi-sthitasya me
> sukhāni goṣpadāyante
> brāhmāṇy api jagad-guro
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tvat]]---You; [[synonyms:s:sākṣāt]]-[[synonyms:k:karaṇa]]---by meeting; [[synonyms:ā:āhlāda]]---of pleasure; [[synonyms:v:viśuddha]]---spiritually purified; [[synonyms:a:abdhi]]---in an ocean; [[synonyms:s:sthitasya]]---situated; [[synonyms:m:me]]---of me; [[synonyms:s:sukhāni]]---happiness; [[synonyms:g:goṣpadāyante]]---is like a calf's hoofprint; [[synonyms:b:brāhmāṇi]]---derived from understanding of impersonal Brahman; [[synonyms:a:api]]---also; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:g:guro]]---O master of the universe.
translation: "My dear Lord, O master of the universe, since I have directly seen You, my transcendental bliss has taken the shape of a great ocean. Being situated in that ocean, I now realize all other so-called happiness, including even brahmānanda, to be like the water contained in the hoofprint of a calf.' "
purport: This verse is quoted from the //Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya// (14.36).

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.198
description: Gopāla Cakravartī said, "if one is not liberated by nāmābhāsa, then you may be certain that I shall cut off your nose."
text:
> vipra kahe,---"nāmābhāse yadi 'mukti' naya
> tabe tomāra nāka kāṭi' karaha niścaya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:v:vipra]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---the //brāhmaṇa// said; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāse]]---simply by the awakening of offenseless chanting of the holy name; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:m:mukti]] [[synonyms:n:naya]]---liberation is not attainable; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your; [[synonyms:n:nāka]]---nose; [[synonyms:k:kāṭi']]---I shall cut off; [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:n:niścaya]]---take it as certain.
translation: Gopāla Cakravartī said, "if one is not liberated by nāmābhāsa, then you may be certain that I shall cut off your nose."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.199
description: Then Haridāsa Ṭhākura accepted the challenge offered by Gopāla Cakravartī. "If by nāmābhāsa liberation is not available," he said, "certainly I shall cut off my nose."
text:
> haridāsa kahena,---"yadi nāmābhāse 'mukti' naya
> tabe āmāra nāka kāṭimu,---ei suniścaya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura said; [[synonyms:y:yadi]]---if; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ābhāse]]---simply by the awakening of the holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:m:mukti]] [[synonyms:n:naya]]---mukti is not available; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]]---my; [[synonyms:n:nāka]]---nose; [[synonyms:k:kāṭimu]]---I shall cut off; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:suniścaya]]---certain.
translation: Then Haridāsa Ṭhākura accepted the challenge offered by Gopāla Cakravartī. "If by nāmābhāsa liberation is not available," he said, "certainly I shall cut off my nose."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.2
description: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!
text:
> jaya jaya gauracandra jaya nityānanda
> jayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---to Śrī Caitanya; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:n:nityānanda]]---to Lord Nityānanda; [[synonyms:j:jaya]] [[synonyms:a:advaita]]-[[synonyms:c:candra]]---all glories to Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:j:jaya]]---all glories; [[synonyms:g:gaura]]-[[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:v:vṛnda]]---to the devotees of Lord Caitanya.
translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Ācārya! And all glories to all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.20
description: Thinking in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to perform His noon duties. The next day, He called Dāmodara Paṇḍita to a solitary place.
text:
> eteka vicāri' prabhu madhyāhne calilā
> āra dine dāmodare nibhṛte bolāilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eteka]] [[synonyms:v:vicāri']]---considering like this; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:m:madhyāhne]] [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---went to perform His noon duties; [[synonyms:ā:āradine]]---the next day; [[synonyms:d:dāmodare]]---unto Dāmodara Paṇḍita; [[synonyms:n:nibhṛte]]---in a solitary place; [[synonyms:b:bolāilā]]---called.
translation: Thinking in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to perform His noon duties. The next day, He called Dāmodara Paṇḍita to a solitary place.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.200
description: All the members of the assembly who had heard the challenge were greatly agitated, and they got up, making a tumultuous sound. Hiraṇya and Govardhana Majumadāra both immediately chastised the brāhmaṇa tax collector.
text:
> śuni' sabhā-sad uṭhe kari' hāhākāra
> majumadāra sei vipre karila dhikkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:s:sabhā]]-[[synonyms:s:sat]]---all the members of the assembly; [[synonyms:u:uṭhe]]---got up; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:h:hāhā]]-[[synonyms:k:kāra]]---making a tumultuous sound; [[synonyms:m:majumadāra]]---Hiraṇya and Govardhana Majumadāra; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipre]]---unto that //brāhmaṇa// who was their servant; [[synonyms:k:karila]]---made; [[synonyms:d:dhik]]-[[synonyms:k:kāra]]---chastisement.
translation: All the members of the assembly who had heard the challenge were greatly agitated, and they got up, making a tumultuous sound. Hiraṇya and Govardhana Majumadāra both immediately chastised the brāhmaṇa tax collector.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.201
description: The priest named Balarāma Ācārya chastised Gopāla Cakravartī. "You are a foolish logician," he said, "What do you know about the devotional service of the Lord?
text:
> balāi-purohita tāre karilā bhartsana
> "ghaṭa-paṭiyā mūrkha tuñi bhakti kāṅhā jāna?
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:balāi]]-[[synonyms:p:purohita]]---the priest named Balarāma Ācārya; [[synonyms:t:tāre]]---unto Gopāla Cakravartī; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---did; [[synonyms:b:bhartsana]]---chastisement; [[synonyms:g:ghaṭa]]-[[synonyms:p:paṭiyā]]---interested in the pot and the earth; [[synonyms:m:mūrkha]]---fool; [[synonyms:t:tuñi]]---you; [[synonyms:b:bhakti]]---devotional service; [[synonyms:k:kāṅhā]]---what; [[synonyms:j:jāna]]---do know.
translation: The priest named Balarāma Ācārya chastised Gopāla Cakravartī. "You are a foolish logician," he said, "What do you know about the devotional service of the Lord?
purport: The philosophy enunciated by the Māyāvādīs is called //ghaṭa-paṭiyā// philosophy. According to this philosophy, everything is one, everything is earth, and therefore anything made of earth, such as different pots, is also the same earth. Such philosophers see no distinction between a pot made of earth and the earth itself. Since Gopāla Cakravartī was a //ghaṭa-paṭiyā// logician, a gross materialist, what could he understand about the transcendental devotional service of the Lord?

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.202
description: "You have insulted Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Thus there will be a dangerous position for you. You should not expect anything auspicious."
text:
> haridāsa-ṭhākure tuñi kaili apamāna!
> sarva-nāśa habe tora, nā habe kalyāṇa"
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]-[[synonyms:ṭ:ṭhākure]]---unto Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:t:tuñi]]---you; [[synonyms:k:kaili]]---did; [[synonyms:a:apamāna]]---insult; [[synonyms:s:sarva]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---destruction of everything; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---there will be; [[synonyms:t:tora]]---your; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:h:habe]]---will be; [[synonyms:k:kalyāṇa]]---auspicious result.
translation: "You have insulted Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Thus there will be a dangerous position for you. You should not expect anything auspicious."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.203
description: Then Haridāsa Ṭhākura got up to leave, and the Majumadāras, the masters of Gopāla Cakravartī, immediately dismissed Gopāla Cakravartī from their service.
text:
> śuni' haridāsa tabe uṭhiyā calilā
> majumadāra sei vipre tyāga karilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śuni']]---hearing; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---then; [[synonyms:u:uṭhiyā]] [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---got up and began to go away; [[synonyms:m:majumadāra]]---Hiraṇya and Govardhana Majumadāra; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:v:vipre]]---this; [[synonyms:t:tyāga]] [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---kicked out.
translation: Then Haridāsa Ṭhākura got up to leave, and the Majumadāras, the masters of Gopāla Cakravartī, immediately dismissed Gopāla Cakravartī from their service.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.204
description: With all the members of the assembly, the two Majumadāras fell at the lotus feet of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Haridāsa Ṭhākura was smiling, however, and he spoke in a sweet voice.
text:
> sabhā-sahite haridāsera paḍilā caraṇe
> haridāsa hāsi' kahe madhura-vacane
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sabhā]]-[[synonyms:s:sahite]]---with all the members of the assembly; [[synonyms:h:haridāsera]]---of Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:p:paḍilā]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇe]]---fell down at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:h:hāsi']]---smiling; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:m:madhura]]-[[synonyms:v:vacane]]---in a sweet voice.
translation: With all the members of the assembly, the two Majumadāras fell at the lotus feet of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Haridāsa Ṭhākura was smiling, however, and he spoke in a sweet voice.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.205
description: "None of you are at fault," he said. "Indeed, even this ignorant so-called brāhmaṇa is not at fault, for he is accustomed to dry speculation and logic.
text:
> "tomā-sabāra doṣa nāhi, ei ajña brāhmaṇa
> tāra doṣa nāhi, tāra tarka-niṣṭha mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomā]]-[[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of all of you; [[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---fault; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:a:ajña]]---ignorant; [[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]---so-called //brāhmaṇa//; [[synonyms:t:tāra]] [[synonyms:d:doṣa]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---he is also not at fault; [[synonyms:t:tāra]]---his; [[synonyms:t:tarka]]-[[synonyms:n:niṣṭha]]---accustomed to speculation; [[synonyms:m:mana]]---mind.
translation: "None of you are at fault," he said. "Indeed, even this ignorant so-called brāhmaṇa is not at fault, for he is accustomed to dry speculation and logic.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.206
description: "One cannot understand the glories of the holy name simply by logic and argument. Therefore this man cannot possibly understand the glories of the holy name.
text:
> tarkera gocara nahe nāmera mahattva
> kothā haite jānibe se ei saba tattva?
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tarkera]]---by argument and logic; [[synonyms:g:gocara]]---appreciable; [[synonyms:n:nahe]]---is not; [[synonyms:n:nāmera]]---of the holy name; [[synonyms:m:mahattva]]---the glory; [[synonyms:k:kothā]] [[synonyms:h:haite]]---from where; [[synonyms:j:jānibe]]---will know; [[synonyms:s:se]]---he; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all; [[synonyms:t:tattva]]---truth.
translation: "One cannot understand the glories of the holy name simply by logic and argument. Therefore this man cannot possibly understand the glories of the holy name.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.207
description: "All of you may now go to your homes. May Lord Kṛṣṇa bestow his blessings upon you all. Do not be sorry because of my being insulted."
text:
> yāha ghara, kṛṣṇa karuna kuśala sabāra
> āmāra sambandhe duḥkha nā ha-uka kāhāra"
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yāha]] [[synonyms:g:ghara]]---go to your homes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]] [[synonyms:k:karuna]]---may Lord Kṛṣṇa bestow; [[synonyms:k:kuśala]] [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---blessings to everyone; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:s:sambandhe]]---on my account; [[synonyms:d:duḥkha]]---unhappiness; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:u:uka]]---may there not be; [[synonyms:k:kāhāra]]---of anyone.
translation: "All of you may now go to your homes. May Lord Kṛṣṇa bestow his blessings upon you all. Do not be sorry because of my being insulted."
purport:
From this statement by Haridāsa Ṭhākura, it is understood that a pure Vaiṣṇava never takes anyone's insults seriously. This is the teaching of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu:

> tṛṇād api sunīcena
> taror api sahiṣṇunā
> amāninā mānadena
> kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ

"One should chant the holy name of the Lord in a humble state of mind, thinking oneself lower than the straw in the street. One should be more tolerant than a tree, devoid of all sense of false prestige and ready to offer all respects to others. In such a state of mind one can chant the holy name of the Lord constantly." A Vaiṣṇava is always tolerant and submissive like trees and grass. He tolerates insults offered by others, for he is simply interested in chanting the holy name of the Lord without being disturbed.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.213
description: A characteristic of a pure devotee is that he excuses any offense by an ignorant rascal. The characteristic of Kṛṣṇa, however, is that He cannot tolerate blasphemy of His devotees.
text:
> bhakta-svabhāva,---ajña-doṣa kṣamā kare
> kṛṣṇa-svabhāva,---bhakta-nindā sahite nā pāre
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---the characteristic of a pure devotee; [[synonyms:a:ajña]]-[[synonyms:d:doṣa]]---offense by an ignorant rascal; [[synonyms:k:kṣamā]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---excuses; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---the characteristic of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:b:bhakta]]-[[synonyms:n:nindā]]---blaspheming the devotees; [[synonyms:s:sahite]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:p:pāre]]---cannot tolerate.
translation: A characteristic of a pure devotee is that he excuses any offense by an ignorant rascal. The characteristic of Kṛṣṇa, however, is that He cannot tolerate blasphemy of His devotees.
purport:
//tṛṇād api sunīcena \\
taror api sahiṣṇunā \\
amāninā mānadena \\
kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ//

A Vaiṣṇava strictly follows this principle of being humbler than the grass and more tolerant than a tree, expecting no honor from others but offering honor to everyone. In this way, a Vaiṣṇava is simply interested in chanting about the Supreme personality of Godhead and glorifying Him. Haridāsa Ṭhākura epitomized this foremost order of Vaiṣṇavism. Kṛṣṇa cannot tolerate any insults or blasphemy against a Vaiṣṇava. For example, Prahlāda Mahārāja was chastised by his father, Hiraṇyakaśipu, in so many ways, but although Prahlāda tolerated this, Kṛṣṇa did not. The Lord therefore came in the form of Nṛsiṁhadeva to kill Hiraṇyakaśipu. Similarly, although Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura tolerated the insult by Gopāla Cakravartī, Kṛṣṇa could not. The Lord immediately punished Gopāla Cakravartī by making him suffer from leprosy. While instructing Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī about the many restrictive rules and regulations for Vaiṣṇavas, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has very vividly described the effects of offenses at the lotus feet of a Vaiṣṇava. //Yadi vaiṣṇava-aparādha uṭhe hātī mātā// [[books:cc:madhya:19:156|(Madhya 19.156)]]. Offending or blaspheming a Vaiṣṇava has been described as the greatest offense, and it has been compared to a mad elephant. When a mad elephant enters a garden, it ruins all the creepers, flowers and trees. Similarly, if a devotee properly executing his devotional service becomes an offender at the lotus feet of his spiritual master or a Vaiṣṇava, his devotional service is spoiled.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.220
description: "My dear sir, Your behavior is uncommon. Indeed, sometimes I am afraid to speak to You. But please favor me by protecting me from the behavior of society."
text:
> alaukika ācāra tomāra kahite pāi bhaya
> sei kṛpā karibā,---yāte mora rakṣā haya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:alaukika]] [[synonyms:ā:ācāra]]---uncommon behavior; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---Your; [[synonyms:k:kahite]]---to speak; [[synonyms:p:pāibhaya]]---I am afraid; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---that favor; [[synonyms:k:karibā]]---kindly do; [[synonyms:y:yāte]]---by which; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:r:rakṣā]]---protection; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is.
translation: "My dear sir, Your behavior is uncommon. Indeed, sometimes I am afraid to speak to You. But please favor me by protecting me from the behavior of society."
purport: While Haridāsa Ṭhākura was staying under the care of Advaita Ācārya, he was afraid of the behavior of society in Śāntipura, Navadvīpa, which was full of exceedingly aristocratic //brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas// and //vaiśyas.// Haridāsa Ṭhākura was born in a Mohammedan family and was later recognized as a great Vaiṣṇava, but nevertheless the //brāhmaṇas// were very critical of him. Thus Haridāsa Ṭhākura was afraid that Advaita Ācārya would be put into some difficulty because of His familiarity with Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Śrī Advaita Ācārya treated Haridāsa Ṭhākura as a most elevated Vaiṣṇava, but others, like Rāmacandra Khān, were envious of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Of course, we have to follow in the footsteps of Advaita Ācārya, not caring for people like Rāmacandra Khān. At present, many Vaiṣṇavas are coming to our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement from among the Europeans and Americans, and although a man like Rāmacandra Khān is always envious of such Vaiṣṇavas, one should follow in the footsteps of Śrī Advaita Ācārya by treating all of them as Vaiṣṇavas. Although they are not as exalted as Haridāsa Ṭhākura, such Americans and Europeans, having accepted the principles of Vaiṣṇava philosophy and behavior, should never be excluded from Vaiṣṇava society.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.221
description: Advaita Ācārya replied, "My dear Haridāsa, do not be afraid. I shall behave strictly according to the principles of the revealed scriptures.
text:
> ācārya kahena,---"tumi nā kariha bhaya
> sei ācariba, yei śāstra-mata haya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]] [[synonyms:k:kahena]]---Advaita Ācārya said; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do; [[synonyms:b:bhaya]]---fear; [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:ā:ācariba]]---I shall behave in that way; [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:ś:śāstra]]-[[synonyms:m:mata]]---sanctioned by the revealed scriptures; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is.
translation: Advaita Ācārya replied, "My dear Haridāsa, do not be afraid. I shall behave strictly according to the principles of the revealed scriptures.
purport:
Śrīla Advaita Ācārya was not afraid of the strict brahminical culture and customs of society. As stated in the śāstric injunctions, which are the true medium of evidence or proof, anyone can go back to Godhead, even if born of a low family. Kṛṣṇa says in //Bhagavad-gītā://

> māṁ hi pārtha vyapāśritya
> ye 'pi syuḥ pāpa-yonayaḥ
> striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrās
> te 'pi yānti parāṁ gatim

"O son of Pṛthā, those who take shelter in Me, though they be of lower birth-women, //vaiśyas// [merchants], as well as //śūdras// [workers]---can approach the supreme destination." [[books:bg:9:32|(Bg. 9.32)]] Though having taken a low birth in human society, one who accepts Kṛṣṇa as the Supreme Personality of Godhead is quite competent to go back home, back to Godhead; and one who is a bona fide candidate for going back to Godhead should not be considered lowborn, or //caṇḍāla.// That is also a śāstric injunction. As stated in //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:2:4:18|(2.4.18)]]:

> kirāta-hūṇāndhra-pulinda-pulkaśā
> ābhīra-śumbhā yavanāḥ khasādayaḥ
> ye 'nye ca pāpā yad-apāśrayāśrayāḥ
> śudhyanti tasmai prabhaviṣṇave namaḥ

Not only the //yavanas// and //khasādayaḥ// but even those born in still lower families can be purified (//śudhyanti//) by the grace of a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa, for Kṛṣṇa empowers such devotees to perform this purification. Advaita Ācārya had confidence in the śāstric evidence and did not care about social customs. The Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, therefore, is a cultural movement that does not care about local social conventions. Following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Advaita Ācārya, we can accept a devotee from any part of the world and recognize him as a //brāhmaṇa// as soon as he is qualified due to following the principles of Vaiṣṇava behavior.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.222
description: "Feeding you is equal to feeding ten million brāhmaṇas," Advaita Ācārya said. "Therefore, accept this śrāddha-pātra." Thus Advaita Ācārya made him eat.
text:
> tumi khāile haya koṭi-brāhmaṇa-bhojana"
> eta bali, śrāddha-pātra karāilā bhojana
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tumi]] [[synonyms:k:khāile]]---if you eat; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:k:koṭi]]-[[synonyms:b:brāhmaṇa]]-[[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---feeding ten million //brāhmaṇas//; [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali]]---saying this; [[synonyms:ś:śrāddha]]-[[synonyms:p:pātra]]---the dish offered to the forefathers; [[synonyms:k:karāilā]] [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---made to eat.
translation: "Feeding you is equal to feeding ten million brāhmaṇas," Advaita Ācārya said. "Therefore, accept this śrāddha-pātra." Thus Advaita Ācārya made him eat.
purport:
//Śrāddha// is //prasāda// offered to the forefathers at a certain date of the year or month. The //śrāddha-pātra,// or plate offered to the forefathers, is then offered to the best of the //brāhmaṇas// in society. instead of offering the //śrāddha-pātra// to any other //brāhmaṇa,// Advaita Ācārya offered it to Haridāsa Ṭhākura, considering him greater than any of the foremost //brāhmaṇas.// This act by Śrī Advaita Ācārya proves that Haridāsa Ṭhākura was always situated in a transcendental position and was therefore always greater than even the most exalted //brāhmaṇa,// for he was situated above the mode of goodness of the material world. Referring to the //Bhakti-sandarbha,// verse 177, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura quotes the following statements from the //Garuḍa Purāṇa// in this connection:

> brāhmaṇānāṁ sahasrebhyaḥ
> satra-yājī viśiṣyate
> satra-yāji-sahasrebhyaḥ
> sarva-vedānta-pāragaḥ
>
> sarva-vedānta-vit-koṭyā
> viṣṇu-bhakto viśiṣyate
> vaiṣṇavānāṁ sahasrebhya
> ekānty eko viśiṣyate

"A //brāhmaṇa// qualified to offer sacrifices is better than an ordinary //brāhmaṇa// and better than such a //brāhmaṇa// is one who has studied all the Vedic scriptures. Among many such //brāhmaṇas,// one who is a devotee of Lord Viṣṇu is the best; and among many such Vaiṣṇavas, one who fully engages in the service of the Lord is the best."

> bhaktir aṣṭa-vidhā hy eṣā
> yasmin mlecche 'pi vartate
> sa viprendro muni-śreṣṭhaḥ
> sa jñānī sa ca paṇḍitaḥ
> tasmai deyaṁ tato grāhyaṁ
> sa ca pūjyo yathā hariḥ

"There are many different kinds of devotees, but even a Vaiṣṇava coming from a family of //mlecchas// or //yavanas// is understood to be a learned scholar, complete in knowledge, if he knows the Vaiṣṇava philosophy. He should therefore be given charity, for such a Vaiṣṇava is as worshipable as the Supreme Personality of Godhead."

> na me 'bhaktaś catur-vedī
> mad-bhaktaḥ śva-pacaḥ priyaḥ
> tasmai deyaṁ tato grāhyaṁ
> sa ca pūjyo yathā hy aham

Lord Kṛṣṇa says, "Even if a nondevotee comes from a //brāhmaṇa// family and is expert in studying the //Vedas,// he is not very dear to Me, whereas even if a sincere devotee comes from a low family of meat-eaters, he is very dear to Me. Such a sincere pure devotee should be given charity, for he is as worshipable as I."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.223
description: Advaita Ācārya was always absorbed in thoughts of how to deliver the fallen souls of the entire world. "The entire world is full of nondevotees," He thought. "How will they be delivered?"
text:
> jagat-nistāra lāgi' karena cintana
> avaiṣṇava-jagat kemane ha-ibe mocana?
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagat]]-[[synonyms:n:nistāra]]---the deliverance of the people of the whole world; [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:c:cintana]]---was always thinking; [[synonyms:a:avaiṣṇava]]---full of nondevotees; [[synonyms:j:jagat]]---the whole world; [[synonyms:k:kemane]]---how; [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ibe]] [[synonyms:m:mocana]]---will be delivered.
translation: Advaita Ācārya was always absorbed in thoughts of how to deliver the fallen souls of the entire world. "The entire world is full of nondevotees," He thought. "How will they be delivered?"
purport: Śrīla Advaita Ācārya sets the standard for //ācāryas// in the Vaiṣṇava //sampradāya.// An //ācārya// must always be eager to deliver the fallen souls. A person who establishes a temple or maṭha to take advantage of people's sentiments by using for his livelihood what people contribute for the worship of the Deity cannot be called a //gosvāmī// or //ācārya.// One who knows the conclusion of the //śāstras,// follows in the footsteps of his predecessors and endeavors to preach the //bhakti// cult all over the world is to be considered an //ācārya.// The role of an //ācārya// is not to earn his livelihood through the income of the temple. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura used to say that if one earns his livelihood by displaying the Deity in the temple, he is not an //ācārya// or //gosvāmī.// it would be better for him to accept service even as a sweeper in the street, for that is a more honorable means of earning one's living.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.224
description: Determined to deliver all the fallen souls, Advaita Ācārya decided to cause Kṛṣṇa to descend. With this vow, he began to offer Ganges water and tulasī leaves to worship the Lord.
text:
> kṛṣṇe avatārite advaita pratijñā karilā
> jala-tulasī diyā pūjā karite lāgilā
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇe]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:avatārite]]---to cause to descend; [[synonyms:a:advaita]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:p:pratijñā]]---promise; [[synonyms:k:karilā]]---made; [[synonyms:j:jala]]-[[synonyms:t:tulasī]]---Ganges water and //tulasī// leaves; [[synonyms:d:diyā]]---offering; [[synonyms:p:pūjā]]---worship; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to do; [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began.
translation: Determined to deliver all the fallen souls, Advaita Ācārya decided to cause Kṛṣṇa to descend. With this vow, he began to offer Ganges water and tulasī leaves to worship the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.225
description: Similarly, Haridāsa Ṭhākura chanted in his cave on the bank of the Ganges with the intention to cause Kṛṣṇa's descent.
text:
> haridāsa kare goṅphāya nāma-saṅkīrtana
> kṛṣṇa avatīrṇa ha-ibena,---ei tāṅra mana
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---performed; [[synonyms:g:goṅphāya]]---in the cave; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]---Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:avatīrṇa]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ibena]]---will descend; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]] [[synonyms:m:mana]]---his mind.
translation: Similarly, Haridāsa Ṭhākura chanted in his cave on the bank of the Ganges with the intention to cause Kṛṣṇa's descent.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.226
description: Because of the devotional service of these two persons, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu descended as an incarnation. Thus He preached the holy name of the Lord and ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa to deliver the entire world.
text:
> dui-janera bhaktye caitanya kailā avatāra
> nāma-prema pracāri' kailā jagat uddhāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:j:janera]]---of these two persons; [[synonyms:b:bhaktye]]---because of the devotional service; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---made; [[synonyms:a:avatāra]]---incarnation; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]---the holy name and love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pracāri']]---preaching; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:j:jagat]] [[synonyms:u:uddhāra]]---deliverance of the whole world.
translation: Because of the devotional service of these two persons, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu descended as an incarnation. Thus He preached the holy name of the Lord and ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa to deliver the entire world.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.227
description: There is another incident concerning Haridāsa Ṭhākura's uncommon behavior. One will be astonished to hear about it.
text:
> āra alaukika eka caritra tāṅhāra
> yāhāra śravaṇe loke haya camatkāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---another; [[synonyms:a:alaukika]]---uncommon; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:c:caritra]]---characteristic; [[synonyms:t:tāṅhāra]]---of Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:y:yāhāraśravaṇe]]---in hearing which; [[synonyms:l:loke]]---in human society; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:c:camatkāra]]---astonishment.
translation: There is another incident concerning Haridāsa Ṭhākura's uncommon behavior. One will be astonished to hear about it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.228
description: Hear about such incidents without putting forth dry arguments, for these incidents are beyond our material reasoning. One must believe in them with faith.
text:
> tarka nā kariha, tarkāgocara tāṅra rīti
> viśvāsa kariyā śuna kariyā pratīti
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tarka]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:k:kariha]]---do not argue; [[synonyms:t:tarka]]-[[synonyms:a:agocara]]---beyond argument; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---his; [[synonyms:r:rīti]]---behavior; [[synonyms:v:viśvāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---believing; [[synonyms:ś:śuna]]---listen; [[synonyms:k:kariyā]] [[synonyms:p:pratīti]]---having confidence.
translation: Hear about such incidents without putting forth dry arguments, for these incidents are beyond our material reasoning. One must believe in them with faith.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.229
description: One day Haridāsa Ṭhākura was sitting in his cave, reciting very loudly the holy name of the Lord.
text:
> eka-dina haridāsa goṅphāte vasiyā
> nāma-saṅkīrtana karena ucca kariyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eka]]-[[synonyms:d:dina]]---one day; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:g:goṅphāte]] [[synonyms:v:vasiyā]]---sitting in his cave; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]] [[synonyms:k:karena]]---was chanting the holy name of the Lord; [[synonyms:u:ucca]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---resounding very loudly.
translation: One day Haridāsa Ṭhākura was sitting in his cave, reciting very loudly the holy name of the Lord.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.23
description: "You are the most neutral among My associates. This is very good, for without being neutral one cannot protect religious principles.
text:
> tomā sama 'nirapekṣa' nāhi mora gaṇe
> 'nirapekṣa' nahile 'dharma' nā yāya rakṣaṇe
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tomā]] [[synonyms:s:sama]]---like you; [[synonyms:n:nirapekṣa]]---neutral; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there is not; [[synonyms:m:mora]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇe]]---among My associates; [[synonyms:n:nirapekṣa]]---neutral; [[synonyms:n:nahile]]---without being; [[synonyms:d:dharma]]---religious principles; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:y:yāya]] [[synonyms:r:rakṣaṇe]]---cannot be protected.
translation: "You are the most neutral among My associates. This is very good, for without being neutral one cannot protect religious principles.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.230
description: The night was full of moonlight, which made the waves of the Ganges look dazzling. All directions were clear and bright.
text:
> jyotsnāvatī rātri, daśa dik sunirmala
> gaṅgāra laharī jyotsnāya kare jhala-mala
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jyotsnāvatī]]---full of moonlight; [[synonyms:r:rātri]]---the night; [[synonyms:d:daśa]] [[synonyms:d:dik]]---ten directions; [[synonyms:s:su]]-[[synonyms:n:nirmala]]---very clear and bright; [[synonyms:g:gaṅgāra]] [[synonyms:l:laharī]]---the waves of the Ganges; [[synonyms:j:jyotsnāya]]---in the moonlight; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:j:jhala]]-[[synonyms:m:mala]]---appear dazzling.
translation: The night was full of moonlight, which made the waves of the Ganges look dazzling. All directions were clear and bright.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.231
description: Thus everyone who saw the beauty of the cave, with the tulasī plant on a clean altar, was astonished and satisfied at heart.
text:
> dvāre tulasī lepā-piṇḍira upara
> goṅphāra śobhā dekhi' lokera juḍāya antara
synonyms: [[synonyms:d:dvāre]]---at the door; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]---the //tulasī// plant; [[synonyms:l:lepā]]---very clean; [[synonyms:p:piṇḍira]] [[synonyms:u:upara]]---on the altar; [[synonyms:g:goṅphāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śobhā]]---the beauty of the cave; [[synonyms:d:dekhi']]---seeing; [[synonyms:l:lokera]]---of everyone; [[synonyms:j:juḍāya]]---was satisfied; [[synonyms:a:antara]]---the heart.
translation: Thus everyone who saw the beauty of the cave, with the tulasī plant on a clean altar, was astonished and satisfied at heart.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.232
description: At that time, in that beautiful scene, a woman appeared in the courtyard. The beauty of her body was so bright that it tinged the entire place with a hue of yellow.
text:
> hena-kāle eka nārī aṅgane āila
> tāṅra aṅga-kāntye sthāna pīta-varṇa ha-ila
synonyms: [[synonyms:h:hena]]-[[synonyms:k:kāle]]---at this time; [[synonyms:e:eka]]---one; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]---woman; [[synonyms:a:aṅgane]] [[synonyms:ā:āila]]---came to the courtyard; [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---her; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:k:kāntye]]---by the beauty of the body; [[synonyms:s:sthāna]]---that place; [[synonyms:p:pīta]]-[[synonyms:v:varṇa]] [[synonyms:h:ha]]-[[synonyms:i:ila]]---became yellowish.
translation: At that time, in that beautiful scene, a woman appeared in the courtyard. The beauty of her body was so bright that it tinged the entire place with a hue of yellow.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.233
description: The scent of her body perfumed all directions, and the tinkling of her ornaments startled the ear.
text:
> tāṅra aṅga-gandhe daśa dik āmodita
> bhūṣaṇa-dhvanite karṇa haya camakita
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāṅra]]---her; [[synonyms:a:aṅga]]-[[synonyms:g:gandhe]]---the scent of the body; [[synonyms:d:daśa]] [[synonyms:d:dik]]---ten directions; [[synonyms:ā:āmodita]]---perfumed; [[synonyms:b:bhūṣaṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dhvanite]]---by the tinkling of her ornaments; [[synonyms:k:karṇa]]---the ear; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---becomes; [[synonyms:c:camakita]]---startled.
translation: The scent of her body perfumed all directions, and the tinkling of her ornaments startled the ear.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.234
description: After coming there, the woman offered obeisances to the tulasī plant, and after circumambulating the tulasī plant she came to the door of the cave where Haridāsa Ṭhākura was sitting.
text:
> āsiyā tulasīre sei kailā namaskāra
> tulasī parikramā kari' gelā goṅphā-dvāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:āsiyā]]---coming; [[synonyms:t:tulasīre]]---unto the //tulasī// plant; [[synonyms:s:sei]]---that woman; [[synonyms:k:kailā]]---did; [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---obeisances; [[synonyms:t:tulasī]]---the //tulasī// plant; [[synonyms:p:parikramā]]---circumambulating; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---doing; [[synonyms:g:gelā]]---went; [[synonyms:g:goṅphā]]-[[synonyms:d:dvāra]]---to the door of the cave.
translation: After coming there, the woman offered obeisances to the tulasī plant, and after circumambulating the tulasī plant she came to the door of the cave where Haridāsa Ṭhākura was sitting.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.235
description: With folded hands she offered obeisances at the lotus feet of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Sitting at the door, she then spoke in a very sweet voice.
text:
> yoḍa-hāte haridāsera vandilā caraṇa
> dvāre vasi' kahe kichu madhura vacana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yoḍa]]-[[synonyms:h:hāte]]---with folded hands; [[synonyms:h:haridāsera]]---of Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:v:vandilā]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---offered prayers at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:d:dvāre]] [[synonyms:v:vasi']]---sitting at the door; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---says; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---some; [[synonyms:m:madhura]] [[synonyms:v:vacana]]---sweet words.
translation: With folded hands she offered obeisances at the lotus feet of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Sitting at the door, she then spoke in a very sweet voice.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.236
description: "My dear friend," she said, "you are the friend of the entire world. You are so beautiful and qualified. I have come here only for union with you.
text:
> "jagatera bandhu tumi rūpa-guṇavān
> tava saṅga lāgi' mora ethāke prayāṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:j:jagatera]]---of the whole world; [[synonyms:b:bandhu]]---friend; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:r:rūpa]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]-[[synonyms:v:vān]]---so beautiful and qualified; [[synonyms:t:tava]] [[synonyms:s:saṅga]]---your union; [[synonyms:l:lāgi']]---for; [[synonyms:m:mora]]---my; [[synonyms:e:ethāke]] [[synonyms:p:prayāṇa]]---coming here.
translation: "My dear friend," she said, "you are the friend of the entire world. You are so beautiful and qualified. I have come here only for union with you.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.237
description: "My dear sir, kindly accept me and be merciful toward me, for it is a characteristic of all saintly persons to be kind toward the poor and fallen."
text:
> more aṅgīkāra kara hañā sadaya
> dīne dayā kare,---ei sādhu-svabhāva haya"
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:more]]---me; [[synonyms:a:aṅgīkāra]] [[synonyms:k:kara]]---accept; [[synonyms:h:hañā]] [[synonyms:s:sa]]-[[synonyms:d:daya]]---being very kind; [[synonyms:d:dīne]]---to the fallen souls; [[synonyms:d:dayā]] [[synonyms:k:kare]]---show favor; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:s:svabhāva]]---the characteristic of saintly persons; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is.
translation: "My dear sir, kindly accept me and be merciful toward me, for it is a characteristic of all saintly persons to be kind toward the poor and fallen."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.238
description: After saying this, she began to manifest various postures, which even the greatest philosopher would lose his patience upon seeing.
text:
> eta bali' nānā-bhāva karaye prakāśa
> yāhāra darśane munira haya dhairya-nāśa
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:n:nānā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---various postures; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:p:prakāśa]]---began to manifest; [[synonyms:y:yāhāra]] [[synonyms:d:darśane]]---seeing which; [[synonyms:m:munira]]---of even the great philosophers; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:d:dhairya]]-[[synonyms:n:nāśa]]---loss of patience.
translation: After saying this, she began to manifest various postures, which even the greatest philosopher would lose his patience upon seeing.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.239
description: Haridāsa Ṭhākura was immovable, for he was deeply determined. He began to speak to her, being very merciful toward her.
text:
> nirvikāra haridāsa gambhīra-āśaya
> balite lāgilā tāṅre hañā sadaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:n:nirvikāra]]---unmoved; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]]---Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:g:gambhīra]]---very deep; [[synonyms:ā:āśaya]]---determination; [[synonyms:b:balite]] [[synonyms:l:lāgilā]]---began to speak; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto her; [[synonyms:h:hañā]] [[synonyms:s:sadaya]]---being merciful.
translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura was immovable, for he was deeply determined. He began to speak to her, being very merciful toward her.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.24
description: "You can do whatever I cannot. Indeed, you can chastise even Me, not to speak of others.
text:

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.250
description: After offering obeisances to Haridāsa Ṭhākura, the woman said: "I am the illusory energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. I came here to test you.
text:
> tabe nārī kahe tāṅre kari' namaskāra
> 'āmi---māyā' karite āilāṅa parīkṣā tomāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tabe]]---at that time; [[synonyms:n:nārī]]---the woman; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---said; [[synonyms:t:tāṅre]]---unto Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:k:kari']] [[synonyms:n:namaskāra]]---offering obeisances; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---the illusory energy; [[synonyms:k:karite]]---to do; [[synonyms:ā:āilāṅa]]---I came; [[synonyms:p:parīkṣā]]---testing; [[synonyms:t:tomāra]]---your.
translation: After offering obeisances to Haridāsa Ṭhākura, the woman said: "I am the illusory energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. I came here to test you.
purport:
In //Bhagavad-gītā// [[books:bg:7:14|(Bg. 7.14)]] Lord Kṛṣṇa says:

> daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī
> mama māyā duratyayā
> mām eva ye prapadyante
> māyām etāṁ taranti te

"This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it." This was actually proved by the behavior of Haridāsa Ṭhākura. //Māyā// enchants the entire world. Indeed, people have forgotten the ultimate goal of life because of the dazzling attractions of the material world. But this dazzling attraction, especially the attractive beauty of a woman, is meant for persons who are not surrendered to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Lord says, //mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṁ taranti te:// "One who is surrendered unto Me cannot be conquered by the illusory energy." The illusory energy personally came to test Haridāsa Ṭhākura, but herein she admits her defeat, for she was unable to captivate him. How is this possible? it was because Haridāsa Ṭhākura, fully surrendered to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, was always absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa by chanting the holy names of the Lord 300,000 times daily as a vow.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.251
description: "I have previously captivated the mind of even Brahmā, not to speak of others. Your mind alone have I failed to attract.
text:
> brahmādi jīva, āmi sabāre mohiluṅ
> ekelā tomāre āmi mohite nāriluṅ
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:brahma]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:j:jīva]]---all living entities, beginning from Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:s:sabāre]] [[synonyms:m:mohiluṅ]]---captivated everyone; [[synonyms:e:ekelā]]---alone; [[synonyms:t:tomāre]]---you; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:m:mohite]] [[synonyms:n:nāriluṅ]]---could not attract.
translation: "I have previously captivated the mind of even Brahmā, not to speak of others. Your mind alone have I failed to attract.
purport:
Beginning from Lord Brahmā down to the insignificant ant, everyone, without exception, is attracted by the illusory energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The demigods, human beings, animals, birds, beasts, trees and plants are all attracted by sexual desire. That is the illusion of //māyā.// Everyone, whether man or woman, thinks that he is the enjoyer of the illusory energy. In this way, everyone is captivated and engaged in material activities. However, because Haridāsa Ṭhākura was always thinking of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and was always busy satisfying the senses of the Lord, this process alone saved him from the captivation of //māyā.// This is practical proof of the strength of devotional service. Because of his full engagement in the service of the Lord, he could not be induced to enjoy //māyā.// The verdict of the //śāstras// is that a pure Vaiṣṇava, or devotee of the Lord, never thinks of enjoying the material world, which culminates in sex life. He never thinks himself an enjoyer; instead, he always wants to be enjoyed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore the conclusion is that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is eternal, transcendental, beyond the perception of sense gratification and beyond the material qualities. Only if a living entity gives up the false conception that the body is the self and always thinks himself an eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa and the Vaiṣṇavas can he surpass the influence of //māyā// (//mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṁ taranti te).// A pure living entity who thus attains the stage of //anartha-nivṛtti,// cessation of everything unwanted, has nothing to enjoy in the material world. One attains this stage only by properly performing the functions of devotional service. Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī has written:

> ādau śraddhā tataḥ sādhu-
> saṅgo 'tha bhajana-kriyā
> tato 'nartha-nivṛttiḥ syāt
> tato niṣṭhā rucis tataḥ

"In the beginning one must have a preliminary desire for self-realization. This will bring one to the stage of trying to associate with persons who are spiritually elevated. In the next stage, one becomes initiated by an elevated spiritual master, and under his instruction the neophyte devotee begins the process of devotional service. By execution of devotional service under the guidance of the spiritual master, one becomes freed from all material attachments, attains steadiness in self-realization and acquires a taste for hearing about the Absolute Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa." (//Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu// 1.4.15) If one is actually executing devotional service, then //anarthas,// the unwanted things associated with material enjoyment, will automatically disappear.

Sahasra-yuga-paryantam ahar yad brahmaṇo viduḥ.// One day of Brahmā is called a //kalpa.// A //yuga,// or //mahā-yuga,// consists of 4,320,000 years, and one thousand such //mahā-yugas// constitute one //kalpa.// The author of //Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta// says that if one does not take advantage of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he cannot be delivered for millions of such //kalpas.//

translation: "Formerly I received the holy name of Lord Rāma from Lord Śiva, but now, due to your association, I am greatly eager to chant the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.257
description: "The holy name of Lord Rāma certainly gives liberation, but the holy name of Kṛṣṇa transports one to the other side of the ocean of nescience and at last gives one ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> mukti-hetuka tāraka haya 'rāma-nāma'
> 'kṛṣṇa-nāma' pāraka hañā kare prema-dāna
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mukti]]-[[synonyms:h:hetuka]]---the cause of liberation; [[synonyms:t:tāraka]]---deliverer; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---is; [[synonyms:r:rāma]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Rāma; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:p:pāraka]]---that which gets one to the other side of the ocean of nescience; [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---gives; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:d:dāna]]---the gift of love of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: "The holy name of Lord Rāma certainly gives liberation, but the holy name of Kṛṣṇa transports one to the other side of the ocean of nescience and at last gives one ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa.
purport:
In an indirect way, this verse explains the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.// The Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra//---Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare---includes both the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa and the name of Lord Rāma. Lord Rāma gives one the opportunity to be liberated, but simply by liberation one does not get actual spiritual benefit. Sometimes if one is liberated from the material world but has no shelter at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, one falls down to the material world again. Liberation is like a state of convalescence, in which one is free from a fever but is still not healthy. Even in the stage of convalescence, if one is not very careful, one may have a relapse. Similarly, liberation does not offer as much security as the shelter of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. It is stated in the //śāstra://

> ye 'nye 'ravindākṣa vimukta-māninas
> tvayy asta-bhāvād aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ
> āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ
> patanty adho 'nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ

"O Lord, the intelligence of those who think themselves liberated but who have no devotion is impure. Even though they rise to the highest point of liberation by dint of severe penances and austerities, they are sure to fall down again into material existence, for they do not take shelter at Your lotus feet." [[books:sb:10:2:32|(Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 10.2.32)]] //Yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ// refers to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. If one does not take shelter of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, he falls down (//patanty adhaḥ),// even from liberation. The Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra,// however, gives liberation and at the same time offers shelter at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. If one takes shelter at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa after liberation, he develops his dormant ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa. That is the highest perfection of life.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.258
description: "Please give me the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and thus make me fortunate, so that I also may float in the flood of love of Godhead inaugurated by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu."
text:
> kṛṣṇa-nāma deha' tumi more kara dhanyā
> āmāre bhāsāya yaiche ei prema-vanyā

translation: "Please give me the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and thus make me fortunate, so that I also may float in the flood of love of Godhead inaugurated by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu."

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.259
description: After speaking in this way, Māyā worshiped the lotus feet of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, who initiated her by saying, "Just perform chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra."
text:
> eta bali' vandilā haridāsera caraṇa
> haridāsa kahe,---"kara kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtana"
synonyms: [[synonyms:e:eta]] [[synonyms:b:bali']]---saying this; [[synonyms:v:vandilā]]---worshiped; [[synonyms:h:haridāsera]] [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]---the lotus feet of Haridāsa Ṭhākura; [[synonyms:h:haridāsa]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Haridāsa said; [[synonyms:k:kara]]---just perform; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtana]]---chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: After speaking in this way, Māyā worshiped the lotus feet of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, who initiated her by saying, "Just perform chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra."
purport: Now even Māyā wanted to be favored by Haridāsa Ṭhākura. Therefore Haridāsa Ṭhākura formally initiated her by asking her to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa //mahā-mantra.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.26
description: "At intervals you may come see Me here and then soon again go there.
text:
> madhye madhye āsibā kabhu āmāra daraśane
> śīghra kari' punaḥ tāhāṅ karaha gamane
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:madhye]] [[synonyms:m:madhye]]---at intervals; [[synonyms:ā:āsibā]]---you will come; [[synonyms:k:kabhu]]---sometimes; [[synonyms:ā:āmāra]] [[synonyms:d:daraśane]]---to see Me; [[synonyms:ś:śīghra]] [[synonyms:k:kari']]---very soon; [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---again; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:k:karaha]] [[synonyms:g:gamane]]---arrange to go.
translation: "At intervals you may come see Me here and then soon again go there.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.260
description: After thus being instructed by Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Māyā left with great pleasure. Unfortunately, some people have no faith in these narrations.
text:
> upadeśa pāñā māyā calilā hañā prīta
> e-saba kathāte kāro nā janme pratīta
synonyms: [[synonyms:u:upadeśa]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting this instruction; [[synonyms:m:māyā]]---Māyā; [[synonyms:c:calilā]]---left; [[synonyms:h:hañā]] [[synonyms:p:prīta]]---being very pleased; [[synonyms:e:e]]-[[synonyms:s:saba]] [[synonyms:k:kathāte]]---in all these narrations; [[synonyms:k:kāro]]---of someone; [[synonyms:n:nā]]---not; [[synonyms:j:janme]]---there is; [[synonyms:p:pratīta]]---faith.
translation: After thus being instructed by Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Māyā left with great pleasure. Unfortunately, some people have no faith in these narrations.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.261
description: Therefore I shall explain the reasons why people should have faith. Everyone who hears this will be faithful.
text:
> pratīta karite kahi kāraṇa ihāra
> yāhāra śravaṇe haya viśvāsa sabāra
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:pratīta]] [[synonyms:k:karite]]---just to make one faithful; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I say; [[synonyms:k:kāraṇa]] [[synonyms:i:ihāra]]---the reason for this; [[synonyms:y:yāhāra]] [[synonyms:ś:śravaṇe]]---hearing which; [[synonyms:h:haya]]---there is; [[synonyms:v:viśvāsa]]---faith; [[synonyms:s:sabāra]]---of everyone.
translation: Therefore I shall explain the reasons why people should have faith. Everyone who hears this will be faithful.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.262
description: During the incarnation of Lord Caitanya to inaugurate the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, even such personalities as Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and the four Kumāras took birth upon this earth, being allured by ecstatic love of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> caitanyāvatāre kṛṣṇa-preme lubdha hañā
> brahma-śiva-sanakādi pṛthivīte janmiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:a:avatāre]]---in the incarnation of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:preme]]---for ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:lubdha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being very greedy; [[synonyms:b:brahma]]---Lord Brahmā; [[synonyms:ś:śiva]]---Lord Śiva; [[synonyms:s:sanaka]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the Kumāras and others; [[synonyms:p:pṛthivīte]]---on this earth; [[synonyms:j:janmiyā]]---taking birth.
translation: During the incarnation of Lord Caitanya to inaugurate the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, even such personalities as Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and the four Kumāras took birth upon this earth, being allured by ecstatic love of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.263
description: All of them, including the great sage Nārada and devotees like Prahlāda, came here as if human beings, chanting the holy names of Lord Kṛṣṇa together and dancing and floating in the inundation of love of Godhead.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-nāma lañā nāce, prema-vanyāya bhāse
> nārada-prahlādādi āse manuṣya-prakāśe
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:n:nāma]]---the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---chanting; [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---dance; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:v:vanyāya]]---in the inundation of the flood of love of Godhead; [[synonyms:b:bhāse]]---float; [[synonyms:n:nārada]]---the sage Nārada; [[synonyms:p:prahlāda]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---and devotees like Prahlāda; [[synonyms:ā:āse]]---come; [[synonyms:m:manuṣya]]-[[synonyms:p:prakāśe]]---as if human beings.
translation: All of them, including the great sage Nārada and devotees like Prahlāda, came here as if human beings, chanting the holy names of Lord Kṛṣṇa together and dancing and floating in the inundation of love of Godhead.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.264
description: The goddess of fortune and others, allured by love of Kṛṣṇa, also came down in the form of human beings and tasted the holy name of the Lord in love.
text:
> lakṣmī-ādi kari' kṛṣṇa-preme lubdha hañā
> nāma-prema āsvādilā manuṣye janmiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:l:lakṣmī]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---the goddess of fortune and others; [[synonyms:k:kari']]---in this way; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:preme]]---for love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:l:lubdha]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being greedy; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]-[[synonyms:p:prema]]---the holy name of Kṛṣṇa in love; [[synonyms:ā:āsvādilā]]---tasted; [[synonyms:m:manuṣye]] [[synonyms:j:janmiyā]]---taking birth in human society.
translation: The goddess of fortune and others, allured by love of Kṛṣṇa, also came down in the form of human beings and tasted the holy name of the Lord in love.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.265
description: What to speak of others, even Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja, personally descends to taste the nectar of love of Godhead in the form of the chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa.
text:
> anyera kā kathā, āpane vrajendra-nandana
> avatari' karena prema-rasa āsvādana
synonyms: [[synonyms:a:anyera]] [[synonyms:k:kā]] [[synonyms:k:kathā]]---what to speak of others; [[synonyms:ā:āpane]]---personally; [[synonyms:v:vrajendra]]-[[synonyms:n:nandana]]---the son of Nanda Mahārāja, Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:a:avatari']]---descending; [[synonyms:k:karena]]---performs; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:r:rasa]] [[synonyms:ā:āsvādana]]---tasting of the nectar of love of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: What to speak of others, even Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja, personally descends to taste the nectar of love of Godhead in the form of the chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.266
description: What is the wonder if the maidservant of Kṛṣṇa, His external energy, begs for love of Godhead? Without the mercy of a devotee and without the chanting of the holy name of the Lord, love of Godhead cannot be possible.
text:
> māyā-dāsī 'prema' māge,---ithe ki vismaya?
> 'sādhu-kṛpā-'nāma' vinā 'prema' nā janmaya
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:māyā]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsī]]---the external energy is a maidservant; [[synonyms:p:prema]] [[synonyms:m:māge]]---she wants love of Godhead; [[synonyms:i:ithe]]---in this; [[synonyms:k:ki]] [[synonyms:v:vismaya]]---what is the wonder; [[synonyms:s:sādhu]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpā]]---the mercy of the devotee; [[synonyms:n:nāma]]---chanting of the holy name; [[synonyms:v:vinā]]---without; [[synonyms:p:prema]]---love of Godhead; [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:j:janmaya]]---is not possible.
translation: What is the wonder if the maidservant of Kṛṣṇa, His external energy, begs for love of Godhead? Without the mercy of a devotee and without the chanting of the holy name of the Lord, love of Godhead cannot be possible.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.267
description: In the activities of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the three worlds dance and chant, having come in touch with love of Godhead. This is the characteristic of His pastimes.
text:
> caitanya-gosāñira līlāra ei ta' svabhāva
> tribhuvana nāce, gāya, pāñā prema-bhāva
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:g:gosāñira]]---of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:līlāra]]---of the pastimes; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:t:ta']]---certainly; [[synonyms:s:sva]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---the characteristic; [[synonyms:t:tri]]-[[synonyms:b:bhuvana]] [[synonyms:n:nāce]]---the three worlds dance; [[synonyms:g:gāya]]---chant; [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---getting; [[synonyms:p:prema]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāva]]---love of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: In the activities of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the three worlds dance and chant, having come in touch with love of Godhead. This is the characteristic of His pastimes.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.268
description: The holy name of Kṛṣṇa is so attractive that anyone who chants it-including all living entities, moving and nonmoving, and even Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself-becomes imbued with love of Kṛṣṇa. This is the effect of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.
text:
> kṛṣṇa-ādi, āra yata sthāvara-jaṅgame
> kṛṣṇa-preme matta kare kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtane
synonyms: [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]---beginning from Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:ā:āra]]---and; [[synonyms:y:yata]]---ail; [[synonyms:s:sthāvara]]-[[synonyms:j:jaṅgame]]---moving and nonmoving creatures; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:p:preme]]---in love of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:m:matta]]---maddened; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---make; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:s:saṅkīrtane]]---chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa.
translation: The holy name of Kṛṣṇa is so attractive that anyone who chants it-including all living entities, moving and nonmoving, and even Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself-becomes imbued with love of Kṛṣṇa. This is the effect of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.269
description: I have heard from the mouth of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī all that Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī recorded in his notes about the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
text:
> svarūpa-gosāñi kaḍacāya ye-līlā likhila
> raghunātha-dāsa-mukhe ye saba śunila

translation: I have heard from the mouth of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī all that Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī recorded in his notes about the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.27
description: "Offer My mother millions of My obeisances. Please speak to her about My happiness here and thus give her happiness.
text:
> mātāre kahiha mora koṭī namaskāre
> mora sukha-kathā kahi' sukha diha' tāṅre

translation: "Offer My mother millions of My obeisances. Please speak to her about My happiness here and thus give her happiness.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.270
description: I have briefly described those pastimes. Whatever I have written is by the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, since I am an insignificant living being.
text:
> sei saba līlā kahi saṅkṣepa kariyā
> caitanya-kṛpāte likhi kṣudra-jīva hañā
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sei]] [[synonyms:s:saba]]---all those; [[synonyms:l:līlā]]---pastimes; [[synonyms:k:kahi]]---I say; [[synonyms:s:saṅkṣepa]] [[synonyms:k:kariyā]]---in brief; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:k:kṛpāte]]---by the mercy of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:l:likhi]]---I write; [[synonyms:k:kṣudra]]-[[synonyms:j:jīva]] [[synonyms:h:hañā]]---being a very insignificant living entity.
translation: I have briefly described those pastimes. Whatever I have written is by the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, since I am an insignificant living being.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.271
description: I have described but a fragment of the glories of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Hearing this satisfies the aural reception of every devotee.
text:
> haridāsa ṭhākurera kahiluṅ mahimāra kaṇa
> yāhāra śravaṇe bhaktera juḍāya śravaṇa

translation: I have described but a fragment of the glories of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Hearing this satisfies the aural reception of every devotee.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.272
description: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
text:
> śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
> caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:r:rūpa]]---Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; [[synonyms:p:pade]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:y:yāra]]---whose; [[synonyms:ā:āśa]]---expectation; [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]-[[synonyms:c:caritāmṛta]]---the book named //Caitanya-caritāmṛta//; [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---describes; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:d:dāsa]]---Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī.
translation:
Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.


//Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā,  Third Chapter, describing the glories of Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.28
description: "Tell her that I sent you to inform her of My personal activities so that she may share in My happiness.
text:
> 'nirantara nija-kathā tomāre śunāite
> ei lāgi' prabhu more pāṭhāilā ihāṅte'

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.31
description: " 'You know that I come and eat the offerings, but because of external separation, you consider this a dream.
text:
> bhojana kariye āmi, tumi tāhā jāna
> bāhya virahe tāhā svapna kari māna
synonyms: [[synonyms:b:bhojana]]---dining; [[synonyms:k:kariye]]---do; [[synonyms:ā:āmi]]---I; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:j:jāna]]---know; [[synonyms:b:bāhya]]---externally; [[synonyms:v:virahe]]---in separation; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:s:svapna]]---dream; [[synonyms:k:kari]]---as; [[synonyms:m:māna]]---you accept.
translation: “ 'You know that I come and eat the offerings, but because of external separation, you consider this a dream.
purport:
Because mother Śacī was feeling separation from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, she thought she was dreaming that her son had come to her. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, however, wanted to inform her that actually it was not a dream. He actually came there and ate whatever His mother offered Him. Such are the dealings of advanced devotees with the Supreme personality of Godhead. As stated in the //Brahma-saṁhitā://

> premāñjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena
> santaḥ sadaiva hṛdayeṣu vilokayanti
> yaṁ śyāmasundaram acintya-guṇa-svarūpaṁ
> govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi

"I worship the primeval Lord, Govinda, who is always seen by the devotee whose eyes are anointed with the pulp of love. He is seen in His eternal form of Śyāmasundara, situated within the heart of the devotee." (//Brahma-saṁhitā// 5.38) pure devotees realize dealings with the Lord on the transcendental plane, but because the devotees are still in the material world, they think that these are dreams. The Lord, however, talks with the advanced devotee, and the advanced devotee also sees Him. It is all factual; it is not a dream.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.47
description: The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are deeper than millions of seas and oceans. Therefore no one can understand what He does nor why He does it.
text:

translation: The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are deeper than millions of seas and oceans. Therefore no one can understand what He does nor why He does it.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.48
description: I do not know the deep meaning of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities. As far as possible I shall try to explain them externally.

> ataeva gūḍha artha kichui nā jāni
> bāhya artha karibāre kari ṭānāṭāni

translation: I do not know the deep meaning of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities. As far as possible I shall try to explain them externally.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 3.49
description: One day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu met Haridāsa Ṭhākura as usual, and in the course of discussion He inquired as follows.
