translation: Then a brāhmaṇa brought a flower garland, placed the garland on Nityānanda Prabhu's neck and smeared sandalwood pulp all over His body.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 6.97
description: When a servant brought betel nuts and offered them to Lord Nityānanda, the Lord smiled and chewed them.
text:
> sevaka tāmbūla lañā kare samarpaṇa
> hāsiyā hāsiyā prabhu karaye carvaṇa
synonyms: [[synonyms:s:sevaka]]---servant; [[synonyms:t:tāmbūla]]---betel nuts; [[synonyms:l:lañā]]---bringing; [[synonyms:k:kare]] [[synonyms:s:samarpaṇa]]---offers; [[synonyms:h:hāsiyā]] [[synonyms:h:hāsiyā]]---smiling; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Lord Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:k:karaye]] [[synonyms:c:carvaṇa]]---chews.
translation: When a servant brought betel nuts and offered them to Lord Nityānanda, the Lord smiled and chewed them.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 6.98
description: With His own hands Lord Nityānanda Prabhu distributed to all the devotees whatever flower garlands, sandalwood pulp and betel nuts remained.
text:
> mālā-candana-tāmbūla śeṣa ye āchila
> śrī-haste prabhu tāhā sabākāre bāṅṭi' dila
synonyms: [[synonyms:m:mālā]]-[[synonyms:c:candana]]-[[synonyms:t:tāmbūla]]---the flower garlands, sandalwood pulp and betel; [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]] [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:ā:āchila]]---whatever remained; [[synonyms:ś:śrī]]-[[synonyms:h:haste]]---in His own hand; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]---Nityānanda Prabhu; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:s:sabākāre]]---to all; [[synonyms:b:bāṅṭi']] [[synonyms:d:dila]]---distributed.
translation: With His own hands Lord Nityānanda Prabhu distributed to all the devotees whatever flower garlands, sandalwood pulp and betel nuts remained.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 6.99
description: After receiving the remnants of food left by Lord Nityānanda Prabhu, Raghunātha dāsa, who was greatly happy, ate some and distributed the rest among his own associates.
text:
> ānandita raghunātha prabhura 'śeṣa, pāñā
> āpanāra gaṇa-saha khāilā bāṅtiyā
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ānandita]]---being very happy; [[synonyms:r:raghunātha]]---Raghunātha dāsa; [[synonyms:p:prabhura]] [[synonyms:ś:śeṣa]] [[synonyms:p:pāñā]]---after getting the remnants left by Lord Nityānanda prabhu; [[synonyms:ā:āpanāra]] [[synonyms:g:gaṇa]]---his own associates; [[synonyms:s:saha]]---with; [[synonyms:k:khāilā]]---ate; [[synonyms:b:bāṅtiyā]]---distributing.
translation: After receiving the remnants of food left by Lord Nityānanda Prabhu, Raghunātha dāsa, who was greatly happy, ate some and distributed the rest among his own associates.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.1
description: Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Simply by the causeless mercy of the devotees engaged in licking honey from His lotus feet, even a fallen soul becomes eternally liberated.
text:
> caitanya-caraṇāmbhoja-
> makaranda-liho bhaje
> yeṣāṁ prasāda-mātreṇa
> pāmaro 'py amaro bhavet
synonyms: [[synonyms:c:caitanya]]---of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:c:caraṇa]]-[[synonyms:a:ambhoja]]---at the lotus feet; [[synonyms:m:makaranda]]---the honey; [[synonyms:l:lihaḥ]]---unto those engaged in licking; [[synonyms:b:bhaje]]---I offer my obeisances; [[synonyms:y:yeṣām]]---of whom; [[synonyms:p:prasāda]]-[[synonyms:m:mātreṇa]]---simply by the mercy; [[synonyms:p:pāmaraḥ]]---a fallen soul; [[synonyms:a:api]]---even; [[synonyms:a:amaraḥ]]---liberated; [[synonyms:b:bhavet]]---becomes.
translation: Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Simply by the causeless mercy of the devotees engaged in licking honey from His lotus feet, even a fallen soul becomes eternally liberated.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.10
description: "One can immediately purify his entire house simply by remembering exalted personalities, to say nothing of directly seeing them, touching their lotus feet, washing their feet or offering them places to sit.'
text:
> yeṣāṁ saṁsmaraṇāt puṁsāṁ
> sadyaḥ śuddhyanti vai gṛhāḥ
> kiṁ punar darśana-sparśa-
> pāda-śaucāsanādibhiḥ
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yeṣām]]---of whom; [[synonyms:s:saṁsmaraṇāt]]---by remembrance; [[synonyms:p:puṁsām]]---of persons; [[synonyms:s:sadyaḥ]]---immediately; [[synonyms:ś:śuddhyanti]]---become purified; [[synonyms:v:vai]]---certainly; [[synonyms:g:gṛhāḥ]]---the houses; [[synonyms:k:kim]] [[synonyms:p:punaḥ]]---what to speak of; [[synonyms:d:darśana]]---by seeing; [[synonyms:s:sparśa]]---touching; [[synonyms:p:pāda]]-[[synonyms:ś:śauca]]---washing the feet; [[synonyms:ā:āsana]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādibhiḥ]]---by offering a seat and so on.
translation: "One can immediately purify his entire house simply by remembering exalted personalities, to say nothing of directly seeing them, touching their lotus feet, washing their feet or offering them places to sit.'
purport: This is a quotation from //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// [[books:sb:1:19:33|(1.19.33)]].

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.100
description: Every day, Vallabha Bhaṭṭa would come to the place of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to engage in unnecessary arguments with Advaita Ācārya and other great personalities, such as Svarūpa Dāmodara.
text:
> pratyaha vallabha-bhaṭṭa āise prabhu-sthāne
> 'udgrāhādi' prāya kare ācāryādi-sane
synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prati]]-[[synonyms:a:aha]]---daily; [[synonyms:v:vallabha]]-[[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Vallabha Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:ā:āise]]---comes; [[synonyms:p:prabhu]]-[[synonyms:s:sthāne]]---to the place of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; [[synonyms:u:udgrāha]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]] [[synonyms:p:prāya]]---unnecessary argument; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:s:sane]]---with Advaita Ācārya and others.
translation: Every day, Vallabha Bhaṭṭa would come to the place of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to engage in unnecessary arguments with Advaita Ācārya and other great personalities, such as Svarūpa Dāmodara.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.101
description: Whatever conclusions Vallabha Bhaṭṭa eagerly presented were refuted by personalities like Advaita Ācārya.
text:
> yei kichu kare bhaṭṭa 'siddhānta' sthāpana
> śunitei ācārya tāhā karena khaṇḍana
synonyms: [[synonyms:y:yei]]---whatever; [[synonyms:k:kichu]]---any; [[synonyms:k:kare]]---does; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Vallabha Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:s:siddhānta]]---conclusion; [[synonyms:s:sthāpana]]---establishing; [[synonyms:ś:śunitei]]---hearing; [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]---Advaita Ācārya; [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:k:karena]] [[synonyms:k:khaṇḍana]]---refuted.
translation: Whatever conclusions Vallabha Bhaṭṭa eagerly presented were refuted by personalities like Advaita Ācārya.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.102
description: Whenever Vallabha Bhaṭṭa entered the society of devotees, headed by Advaita Ācārya, he was like a duck in a society of white swans.
text:
> ācāryādi-āge bhaṭṭa yabe yabe yāya
> rājahaṁsa-madhye yena rahe baka-prāya
synonyms: [[synonyms:ā:ācārya]]-[[synonyms:ā:ādi]]-[[synonyms:ā:āge]]---in front of Advaita Ācārya and others; [[synonyms:b:bhaṭṭa]]---Vallabha Bhaṭṭa; [[synonyms:y:yabe]] [[synonyms:y:yabe]]---whenever; [[synonyms:y:yāya]]---goes; [[synonyms:r:rāja]]-[[synonyms:h:haṁsa]]-[[synonyms:m:madhye]]---in a society of white swans; [[synonyms:y:yena]]---as; [[synonyms:r:rahe]]---remained; [[synonyms:b:baka]]-[[synonyms:p:prāya]]---like a duck.

translation: By various hints and refutations, Lord Caitanya, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, corrected Vallabha Bhaṭṭa exactly as Kṛṣṇa had cut down the false pride of Indra.
purport: Indra, the King of heaven, was very proud of his position. Therefore when the residents of Vṛndāvana decided not to perform the Indra-yajña but to perform the Govardhana-yajña in accordance with the instructions of Kṛṣṇa, Indra, because of his false pride, wanted to chastise the residents of Vṛndāvana. Thinking himself extremely powerful, Indra poured incessant rain upon Vṛndāvana, but Lord Kṛṣṇa immediately cut down his pride by lifting the Govardhana Hill as an umbrella to save the residents of Vṛndāvana. In this way Kṛṣṇa proved Indra's power most insignificant in the presence of His own omnipotence.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.119

translation: An ignorant living being does not recognize his actual profit. Because of ignorance and material pride, he sometimes considers profit a loss, but when his pride is cut down he can actually see his true benefit.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.12

text:
> tāhā pravartāilā tumi,---ei ta 'pramāṇa'
> kṛṣṇa-śakti dhara tumi,---ithe nāhi āna
synonyms: [[synonyms:t:tāhā]]---that; [[synonyms:p:pravartāilā]]---have propagated; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:e:ei]]---this; [[synonyms:t:ta]]---certainly; [[synonyms:p:pramāṇa]]---evidence; [[synonyms:k:kṛṣṇa]]-[[synonyms:ś:śakti]]---the energy of Kṛṣṇa; [[synonyms:d:dhara]]---bear; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---You; [[synonyms:i:ithe]] [[synonyms:n:nāhi]] [[synonyms:ā:āna]]---there is no question about it.
translation: "You have spread the saṅkīrtana movement of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Therefore it is evident that You have been empowered by Lord Kṛṣṇa. There is no question about it.
purport:
Śrī Madhvācārya has brought our attention to this quotation from the //Nārāyaṇa-saṁhitā://

> dvāparīyair janair viṣṇuḥ
> pañcarātrais tu kevalaiḥ
> kalau tu nāma-mātreṇa
> pūjyate bhagavān hariḥ

"in the Dvāpara-yuga one could satisfy Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu only by worshiping opulently according to the //pāñcarātrikī// system, but in the age of Kali one can satisfy and worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead Hari simply by chanting His holy name." Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura explains that unless one is directly empowered by the causeless mercy of Kṛṣṇa, one cannot become the spiritual master of the entire world //(jagad-guru).// One cannot become an //ācārya// simply by mental speculation. The true //ācārya// presents Kṛṣṇa to everyone by preaching the holy name of the Lord throughout the world. Thus the conditioned souls, purified by chanting the holy name, are liberated from the blazing fire of material existence. In this way, spiritual benefit grows increasingly full, like the waxing moon in the sky. The true //ācārya,// the spiritual master of the entire world, must be considered an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa's mercy. indeed, he is personally embracing Kṛṣṇa. He is therefore the spiritual master of all the //varṇas// (//brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya// and //śūdra//) and all the //āśramas// (//brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha// and //sannyāsa//). Since he is understood to be the most advanced devotee, he is called //paramahaṁsa-ṭhākura.// Ṭhākura is a title of honor offered to the //paramahaṁsa.// Therefore one who acts as an ācārya, directly presenting Lord Kṛṣṇa by spreading His name and fame, is also to be called //paramahaṁsa-ṭhākura.//

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.120
description: Returning home that night, Vallabha Bhaṭṭa thought, "Previously, at Prayāga, Lord Caitanya was very kind to me.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.122
description: "Being very proud of my learning, I am thinking, 'Let me become victorious.' Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, however, is trying to purify me by nullifying this false pride, for a characteristic of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is that He acts for everyone's welfare.
text:
> 'āmi jiti',---ei garva-śūnya ha-uka iṅhāra cita

translation: "Being very proud of my learning, I am thinking, 'Let me become victorious.' Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, however, is trying to purify me by nullifying this false pride, for a characteristic of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is that He acts for everyone's welfare.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.123
description: "I am falsely proud, advertising myself as a learned scholar. Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu insults me just to favor me by cutting down this false pride.

translation: "I am falsely proud, advertising myself as a learned scholar. Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu insults me just to favor me by cutting down this false pride.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.125

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.127
description: "My dear Lord, You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead. You have showed mercy to me in a way just befitting Your position by insulting me to cut down all my false pride.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.13

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.131

synonyms: [[synonyms:p:prabhu]] [[synonyms:k:kahe]]---Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said; [[synonyms:t:tumi]]---you; [[synonyms:p:paṇḍita]]---very learned scholar; [[synonyms:m:mahā]]-[[synonyms:b:bhāgavata]]---great devotee; [[synonyms:d:dui]]-[[synonyms:g:guṇa]]---two qualities; [[synonyms:y:yāhāṅ]]---wherever; [[synonyms:t:tāhāṅ]]---there; [[synonyms:n:nāhi]]---there cannot be; [[synonyms:g:garva]]-[[synonyms:p:parvata]]---the mountain of pride.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.132

translation: "Śrīdhara Svāmī is the spiritual master of the entire world because by his mercy we can understand Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. I therefore accept him as a spiritual master.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.134
description: "Whatever you might write due to false pride, trying to surpass Śrīdhara Svāmī, would carry a contrary purport. Therefore no one would pay attention to it.
text:
> śrīdhara-upare garve ye kichu likhibe
> 'artha-vyasta' likhana sei, loke nā mānibe
synonyms: [[synonyms:ś:śrīdhara]]-[[synonyms:u:upare]]---above Śrīdhara Svāmī; [[synonyms:g:garve]]---in false pride; [[synonyms:y:ye]] [[synonyms:k:kichu]] [[synonyms:l:likhibe]]---whatever you write; [[synonyms:a:artha]]-[[synonyms:v:vyasta]]---the opposite meaning; [[synonyms:l:likhana]] [[synonyms:s:sei]]---such writing; [[synonyms:l:loke]] [[synonyms:n:nā]] [[synonyms:m:mānibe]]---no one will care about it.
translation: "Whatever you might write due to false pride, trying to surpass Śrīdhara Svāmī, would carry a contrary purport. Therefore no one would pay attention to it.
purport: //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam// has many //ṭīkās,// or commentaries, following the //paramparā// system, but Śrīdhara Svāmī's is first. The commentaries of all the other //ācāryas// follow his. The //paramparā// system does not allow one to deviate from the commentaries of the previous //ācāryas.// By depending upon the previous //ācāryas,// one can write beautiful commentaries. However, one cannot defy the previous //ācāryas.// The false pride that makes one think that he can write better than the previous //ācāryas// will make one's comments faulty. At the present moment it has become fashionable for everyone to write in his own way, but such writing is never accepted by serious devotees. Because of false pride, every scholar and philosopher wants to exhibit his learning by interpreting the //śāstras,// especially //Bhagavad-gītā// and //Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,// in his own way. This system of commenting in one's own way is fully condemned by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Therefore He says, //'artha-vyasta' likhana sei.// Commentaries written according to one's own philosophical way are never accepted; no one will appreciate such commentaries on the revealed scriptures.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.135
description: "One who comments on Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam following in the footsteps of Śrīdhara Svāmī will be honored and accepted by everyone.

translation: "One who comments on Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam following in the footsteps of Śrīdhara Svāmī will be honored and accepted by everyone.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.136

translation: "Put forth your explanation of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam following in the footsteps of Śrīdhara Svāmī. Giving up your false pride, worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa.

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya-līlā 7.137
